_childDocuments_.review: The biggest plus for this game is probably the art style and animation, and then sound and music.Gameplay was good and gives you the chance in the progress of the story to getting used to combo and mechanics that gets introduced over time.But like some other comments, it gets frustrating at times when the way scaling works, especially late game is that the game throw tons of enemies at you at the same time, with save points some times annoying far from each others. Most annoying of all is if and when the save point requires you to run a fair distance to get to the enemy spawn, wasting time just running through the same scenery each time you die.Another issue that I had, but more rarely would be the way enemies work in a 2d setting in a 3d world. Some area have this issue where it looks like the enemy can be hit, but they aren't (because they're slightly infront/behind due to 3d world), and sometimes this isn't visually clear.For someone that played in difficulty 2 and cannot play dark souls (because I'm a noob lol), I think it is still fun even though i died a ton.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that while I will recommend, this is not a recommendation for everyone, and you should really consider the price for what you getting.So, the game is visually amazing. The story itself is nice and the "multiple endings" add a bit of variety to it but not that much. But boy, is the combat system repetitive.Once you unlock the finisher of Up + Light - Light - Light - Heavy you have seen everything there is to see for your own worthfull skills. The enemies don't have the same rules of engagement as you, so between reloading canon shots in sub 2 seconds or infinite combos, it can become frustrating from time to time.Doing 100% achievements isn't "ideal" per say, as in, for a few achievements you basically have one shot / no way to go back to a previous chapter, so you might as well just save scum when going for 100%, specifically in 2-3 achievements.Expect about 4-6 hours for 1 playthough, 8-12 hours for 100%.All in all, still very recommended much recommended if you buy it for a good price due to the visuals alone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting story to follow and the combat in fun, but neither of them are amazing. My objective opinion is that the game is average to above average. The combat, for myself, took time to get used to as timing blocks/parries/attacks felt as if they didn't match when you press the keys. After putting the time, I've come to understand the attacks, timing, combos, etc. and that the chance to have fun slicing and dicing though enemies, but it took me a while to get to that point. There are also some quality of life aspects that this game is missing, and for me, who was achievement hunting, it was a nightmare. If you have a level you want to replay, you have to replay everything up to that point in order to play which ever chapter. The game has some replay ability but it gets repetitive and boring at times. Despite my criticisms, I enjoyed the game thoroughly, but I can easily see someone not enjoying it as much, I would suggest trying to buy the game discounted to $10 to $15.

_childDocuments_.review: A simple but fun game if you enjoy samurai media especially content based on older samurai movies. The story is simple yet enjoyable with some choices within the game that determines the outcome of the ending. The Art design is intentionally left black and white as a call back to those older samurai films but even so the game looks beautiful, making good use of shadow and light. The gameplay also feels mostly satisfying, cutting your way through enemies really makes you feel like a skilled samurai warrior. However there are some issues in terms of poor input and  responsiveness. This mostly comes in the form of enacting combos, if you press the buttons too fast, they dont execute properly, if you put them in too slowly they don't execute properly. This means there is a very fine timing you need to properly do combos, although once you get used to it it feels great. There is also the issue of blocking and dodging feeling off, as I'll press the bottoms to do either just as the enemy attacks but they'll still hit, due to the game being structured to press these buttons at the very very beginning of attack animations rather than during them, often meaning you'll need to block before the enemy even enacts their attack.Other than that however Trek to Yomi is a fun game, it's roughly five hours long and does have a new mode to play after beating the campaign but I also wish they had a new game plus mode due to all of the collectibles they have in this game. For $20 it's not a bad deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Overall, I would actually recommend you DO NOT play this game, but I can definitely see how it can be enjoyable.If you're into samurai stuff, but it on a sale for about 10 Euros.So, you've played Ghost of Tsushima and want more. This is definitely not it, but it CAN be enjoyable nonetheless. I say *can* because I have not enjoyed it. I am roughly 70% done, but I will not finish it.That said, I can appreciate the game for what it is. The combat is all right, and you gradually get new combos. On Hard, the game is challenging, borderline just annoying at times. I don't feel that this is a system of skill as much as a system of cheese. The story is predictable and and nothing impressive, but it's all right. The voice acting is good. The music is great. The art style, visuals and environments are great, BUT I don't like the black and white style at all. Your mileage will vary depending on that.

_childDocuments_.review: is a stunning snapshot of Edo period Japan, and an ode to 1950s Samurai cinema. But it's also a terrible game.It is an experience that sees you tussle through the afterlife in search of either honor, love or, if you're like me, fury. One that see's Hiroki overcome multiple trials and tribulations in order to return to life and defeat the man that took it all from him. But almost every moment of this 4 hour long adventure is fraught with misery, for both the protagonist and, unfortunately, the player. It is a dull, predictable and repetitive slog that makes it feel like a game far longer than it is. By the end, I couldn't wait for it to be over. The directional combat is boring, and the game gives you little reason to truly embrace it, instead you can just spam the same light and heavy combos for the whole game with not much trouble, until the end that is. Weird environment puzzles are tacked on somewhere in Ch.4 and overstay their welcome for the next few. Collectible hunting just pertains to randomly placed lore entries, often hard to differentiate from the environment on account of the games artistic choices. Speaking of which, brings me to the only real thing this game has going for it. The bold black and white, almost painterly style to the levels and world. It is drop dead gorgeous and the only real point of praise. It's unfortunate really, because going in, I was desperately hoping for a surprise but reviewers are right about this one. It's a game that bounces from acceptable at best, to just plain annoying. I got it on Humble last month so there wasn't much of an investment from me, but I do not recommend paying anywhere near retail for this, and honestly I don't really recommend it at all. There are better Samurai games out there, if that's what you want. So unless you have an OLED panel and really want to flex those contrast and black levels, avoid .

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as part of a humble bundle so was pleased with the game at that price point. I would be hard pressed to recommend this at full price though.Ultimately, as others have said, the aesthetic is really nice but for me it falls down in two places:1. The combat is so random and unbalanced that when I defeated a challenging scene I didnt get a sense of accomplishment, just abating annoyance. Enemies seem to have random amounts of health, can move significantly faster than you, and are not bound by the same constraints you are (swing speed, stamina etc).2. The Yomi part of the game. Undead, zombies etc - do we need a supernatural element to every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game? I feel I would have been significantly happier if I had beaten the boss at chapter 3 and been done with it. I get that its part of the narrative, the protagonists journey to his 'balance' but it feels really tired and uninteresting. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: first impression, Beautiful style and the samurai theme is so thick and and well done here. Combat is very fun and fast, lots of really nice landscapes and city streets, full of life and conversations. Such a cool approach with the black and white color scheme. would totally recommend for anybody who likes a nice story and great gameplay
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It has a compelling story and fun gameplay. The black and white style set in feudal japan (i think) sets the atmosphere perfectly. And the story, while not beeing the most unpredictable one, serves the game realy well and doesnt feel like a second thought. Now the best part is the gameplay if you like pretending to be a samurai, you will propably love this game. The controls are simple enough but the timing and when to do which combo makes it so you still have a good learning curve. Also there is a limited number of combos which are unlocked as you progress through the story, keeping the combat interesting. That beeing said, the execution type attacks can be abused. If you do that the combat will become less interesting but you will feel like a badass dropping enemies left and right. tl,dr: very good game, gameplay can become repetitive if you spam powermoves
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game! I loved the art direction, (Japanese) voice acting and the exploration. The fixed camera while exploring was really cool, and had a great early 3d video game feeling. However, I had to stop playing because I was totally burnt out on the combat loop. All the reviewers that commented on this are unfortunately correct... as fun as the art style, exploration and (early chapter 4) story goes I wanted to see the end but couldn't trudge through the combat. I played some FANTASTIC sword combat in Ghost of Tsushima, but Trek to Yomi was missing combat depth and fun. At first, the combat was too easy and I could basically two-hit kill the enemies without any issue. But by act 4 the combat just becomes duller and enemies take more hits to defeat and there is no depth to countering, slashing, or movement. Feels like tank combat, and I dreaded combat encounters by the end. I will check out the rest of the story on YouTube unfortunately!
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful game. The history is not a big deal, but good enough to keep you engage. Th game play is fun and addicted. But the best is the environment, the black and white theme that make it look like a Japanese movie from the 80s. Is game with a lot of love, and if you like the Japanese culture you should buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi is a visually stunning yet incredibly disappointing game.The game does look fantastic, however every other aspect of what actually makes a game is extremely lacking.  The combat is repetitive, at times unresponsive and overall a chore to get through.  Around the ch5 mark I would start to groan every time a new wave of enemies appeared.  The story is basic and forgetful, the characters aren't characters they're simple nothing archetype tropes.  The 'puzzles' are so easy that a 3 year old could solve them and it's the exact same "match the 3 symbols straight in front you to those on the dials" repeated with no variation.  The English dub is also atrocious but that might be on purpose to capture the old school feeling they're going for. Overall, Trek to Yomi makes me sad and annoyed.  It had the potential to be something really good, however the underwhelming and tedious combat, mixed in with how repetitive the whole experience is, ruins what could have been.  The result is something I would never recommend playing yourself but instead watch on YouTube just to see the visuals.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: A remarkable atmospheric samurai action game.A great samurai action game with simple but very innovative choice of presentation. By making a game out of post-WWII Japanese black-and-white period drama, the result is very stunning. The right atmosphere for Japanese historical drama, perhaps.Despite its colorlessness, the game contains highly detailed graphical elements, e.g. decorative material on building, tools and utensils on tables, and even debris of ruined house and carriage. Sound effect is also great in details as crying and agony can be variously heard throughout ravaged villages. Illusive Yomi world are also well-depicted in fantastic details. Actions and blade movement are also realistic. Feel like watching an action movie.Story and choice of path may be a little bit simple. but understandable. Paths and direction in each level is also quite simple. The game focuses more on swordfight and cinematic camera angles which are considered as pièce de résistance.Good action command and sword move. Not too complicated. Not too overpowered or supernatural. Require player's skill in movement control and timing to fight on.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically give games a thumbs down however Trek to Yomi is very much a mixed review needs improvement kind of game.In terms of aesthetic the game has it going in spades, the world and area designs are great and the camera is very well done which makes for a great cinematic experience. The story is so-so. Nothing grand but decent enough.My biggest issue stems from the gameplay. It's not terrible, don't get me wrong. It's just very repetitive with little in the way of variety. Sure you get some different tools that function similarly and some combo moves that do some differing animations but overall it's very samey throughout the whole game. The other issue is that the controls feel kinda bad. For some reason I could only sprint in the cardinal directions and not diagonally. In combat it felt like I should be executing certain attacks or combos only for them to not work or not trigger properly or alternatively I'd attempt to do an action and it just wouldn't occur. It's quite a pain and really drags the game down.Another annoyance is that there are collectables and upgrades, this is typically fine however if you miss something and want to go back, you generally wont be able to. Once you beat a level, that's it. Once you drop down somewhere, that's it. It's rather annoying if you've got exploration in the game yet the game restricts so much of your access to it.  If the game had some additional QoL changes and If the controls were tighter and combat felt better the game would be fine but as it stands, I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I'm forcing myself to finish the game because it's a visual masterpiece, but this is arguably the worst gameplay I've ever experienced. Boring and repetitive at best, and completely broken most of the time.The artists should be praised while I hope the combat designer never gets to work on another project again. I have no idea how this made it past play-testing.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gorgeous work of art.  That's what you'd be playing it for.  The mechanics are decent, but repetitive.  The finishers are cool, but repetitive.  I played my first run on Ronin level, and the hardest fight outside of boss fights was the very first one.  Once you get the ability to stun and finish it's a cake walk.  Some of the bosses can be a pain, and the final fight is an absolute pointless nightmare.  I eventually beat it after about an hour and 100 tries.  I would suggest just playing it on a lower difficulty and enjoying the story and the art.  The game could've been about 2 acts shorter imo as it kind of drags on towards the middle-end.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some solid points. It does get alittle tedious at times like same enemy types/same type of waves the game throws at you. It trys to change it up alittle bit through out the game but it starts to get stale about 1/2 to 2/3rds of the game.  Then the last 2/3rds is somewhat of a chore.  But if you were to get this game for like 5$ its somewhat worth it.   Art work is solid through the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: The art direction and visuals for this game are ridiculously good. Love seeing the way the scenes shifted perspective as it went on. The combat however, was too ambitious and too inconsistent with its weird parry timings that it was just frustrating with the hordes of enemies past chapter 3. Game is best experienced on easy mode and treated as a beat ‘Em up so you can actually enjoy the visuals and get to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics and ambiance. I started on medium difficulty but quickly changed to easy as some of the fights become tediously difficult for my key-bashing skills. At this point I don't know if I will finish the game as more and more segments become difficult to get through even on easy and you are sent far back to repeat over and over. Super easy mode please? Pity because I would like to see all of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: trek to yomi is definitely a case of style over substance. the game looks great - it has a real sense of style, knows what it's trying to pay homage to (kurosawa), and pulls it off.unfortunately the actual gameplay doesn't match it. the combat feels imprecise and sloppy, there's way too many attack combos for a game this short and simple, enemy variation is lacking. the level design is mostly linear, and a few puzzles are thrown in that are so simple you wonder why they even bothered. the meat and potatoes of the game can't live up to its amazing presentation.with that said, still a cautious recommendation. get it on a good discount, play it on easy, enjoy the visuals and the power fantasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Really amazing game with very cool black-and-white design choice and varying camera angles for the game. The gameplay is also very action packed with perfectly challenging parry system and well-placed checkpoints. My one gripe for this game is in the beginning/tutorial of the game, where you're flooded with text for both tutorial and dialogue. So you feel overwhelmed and it gets hard to read everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: So beautiful it's hard to convey how nice it is for someone that just look at the pictures.You will come back to it later and replay for sure.I hope there's more of this game soon, like, another story, another character, idk, but it can't be a single experience.On the "bad" side, there is too much walking around and facing the same  guys over and over near the end to a point where you're doing the exact same thing for like 2h with little to no progress to the story.The last boss is a little too difficult but once you understand what you have to do, you can kill it faster and be over with him already.

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi is a gorgeous homage to old samurai films. While not for everyone, it's still an excellent game that I absolutely recommend. Here's why.To start, lets go over the most striking element. The visuals. The entire game is in black and white. The world, the main menu, the pause screen, the cutscenes, all of it is in black and white. Camera angles are fixed, and cannot be moved by the player manually, providing the feel of a spirit watching everything happening from afar. Even with areas that should feel dark and mysterious keep a feeling of visual distinction without sacrificing contrast. It's simply excellent.Along with that, the environments displayed in the game compliment this style of black and white fixed angles. Sweeping vistas are viewed from a far away point to make the characters feel small and insignificant, while more intimate battles are shot head on from close up, making things feel tense and claustrophobic. The locals vary from the raw wilderness, to ancient towns and places best left unsaid. It's a truly varied set of locations which is surprising, but not unwelcome.Now, onto gameplay. As stated previously, your camera is fixed and cannot be moved at will. If it needs to move, it will either move on it's own or follow you temporarily while you move across a longer area. All combat sections are done on a 2d plane, while exploration can be done in a mix of 3d and 2d movement. I'll cover the exploration first.Exploration is not what you'd think this game would do well, but it absolutely does. As your camera is fixed, you very often will see the path you need to take to get where you need to go next. However, the game hides not-so-obvious paths in the shot that can often be gone to. Heading down these paths will net you ammo for ranged weapons, lore collectibles, character upgrades, combat techniques and sometimes even save points. Even if you don't care about the lore collectibles you're rewarded for exploration, but the lore collectibles are actually very interesting as they pertain to Japanese myth and folklore, along with the main character's motivations. Character Upgrades provide health and stamina, which is almost essential to performing better in boss fights. There are also puzzles in the environment, and these puzzles never get too complicated nor do they overstay their welcome. It's honestly lovely.Combat is the other form of gameplay, and it is executed very well, but not perfectly. You have combos that do differing damage and have differing functions that can ultimately either stun or outright kill an enemy. Stunned enemies can be executed to restore health and are done with very smooth and cool animations. You can also begin these combos after parrying a blow by blocking it at the last second, or after rolling through an attack. But ultimately you'll find yourself repeating 1 of 3 that you find most effective. This is mostly the case due to 2 reasons, boss mechanics and enemy variety.Enemy Variety is sadly a bit lacking. Most enemies are one of two types, Armored or Unarmored. Unarmored enemies will die quickly if you can get in enough damage, and often will die before being stunned. Armored Enemies on the other hand will take a very large amount of hits to kill, but can be instakilled by stunning them and then executing them. The problem with this is that you never have a reason to do long, intricate chains when the same combo that will stun an armored enemy will outright kill an unarmored enemy. While some enemies do mix this formula up, they aren't frequent enough to really make you want to move out of using your favored combos and instead experiment with new combos and strategies. Boss mechanics are a bit tricky to mention without spoiling the game, so I will do it without spoilers by banging on the mechanic they rely on. Rolling. Rolling gives you I-Frames and prevents all damage while doing so. the issue is in how strict the timing is. Most bosses have very aggressive attack patterns with some attacks at the end that cannot be blocked. These attacks must be rolled through, but if you were blocking the attacks up until the point you needed to dodge then the timing to dodge it is some of the strictest timing I've ever seen in a video game. This often leads to bosses being less about weaving your blade into the enemy between attacks and more about staying out of attack range until they're done attacking and doing a fast attack. This doesn't mean they're bad or uninteresting, but it does mean that they can be frustrating due to the level of timing required, especially on higher difficulties.All the gameplay though mixes very well to both encourage exploration and make combat feel fluid. If you fail to explore, you will struggle later due to having less health, stamina, and ammo. If you fail to learn combat timings, you'll want to explore to make fighting easier. Once fighting is easier, you can make more mistakes and therefor have more opportunities to learn. It's very well executed.The story is extremely hard to not spoil while speaking of it, so this entire section will be marked as a spoiler. I will not go over major story beats or characters, but even then I think it's best to go into the story with no idea what you're getting into. It's quite short, but it's very rewarding. Anywho, either skip this below section or read through it at your own peril:Sound design is absolutely spectacular as well. The swinging of swords sounds deadly, the sound of footsteps is heavy, and all other environmental sounds just work perfectly. The voice acting is all in Japanese, and it is amazing to listen to. No effort was spared for the voice acting past the first chapter. You feel the emotions, the anger, the regret. Magnifique. The music is unobtrusive ambient Japanese folk music. It often perfectly fits the scene it's used in, so I have no complaints regarding it.Put all of this together and you have a game that tries to be something very specific and excels at it. It knows it's niche and while not everyone may enjoy that niche, those that do are sure to love this game. Get it for full price or on sale, either way you'll get your moneys worth, I promise.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: i have recently taken into the idea that all games are played at the hardest difficulty (not anything abnormal like 1 hit kills or whatever) as a first run so i did this game at the ronin difficulty which was a nice challenge to play, the game is unique and beautiful. with nice mix of mechanics that allow you to go into every situation in a mix of combinations added together as you gain new moves and weapons. boss fights are amazing and the feeling of satisfaction you get after each boss is really good. all in all a solid game i picked up on sale. well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: A really satisfying combat game. That rewards the correct combo and method rather then just reinforcing perfect parry's and spamming the best moves. The story is a bit on the side and requires some philosophical thinking. While not overstaying it's welcome. it took me 5 hours to finish my first playthrough on the hardest difficulty i could pick Ronin. Now I'm allowed to playthough it again on Kenshi which turns the game in to a 1 hit 1 kill playstyle throughout the entire game. For someone wanting some cheap fun for a few hours and that's really in to the whole Old black/white samurai movies and duals in the fields of grass. You can definetly find great enjoyment here. Also if your a completionist that like a challenge the achievments will kick your ass.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Love the art of the game, it reminds me a lot of the old Japanese samurai films. The gameplay is very basic and easy to learn, although I only managed to master the parrying at the end of the game, because all enemy types have different attack pasterns, and further down the game, it gets even more difficult to master it.The game offers dialogue choice at important events, and I wish the game allowed you to play those events again just so you could see how each choice impacts the game. Instead you're forced to play the game all over again just so you can pick different dialogues, or just watch a video on YouTube.In short, I give this game a 7/10, I would give a higher score if it wasn't for the price and how short it is, you can literally finish this game in less than 4 hours, although it may last longer if you want the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Overall nice, short game with great atmosphere, pretty good story and unique graphic (much better with color mod)  but a fight system... it so unpolished... sometimes great but most of the time is soooo frustrating. As much as i like this game i probably never come back to it. I hope for Trek to Yomi 2 with combat so smooth as in Sifu ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some amazing visuals. The gameplay is good, with simple fighting mechanics that become increasingly complemented with new moves and weapons along the way. It's a short game, but there are multiple endings, and it features an exploring/collecting element. You can choose between multiple difficulty modes, including "one hit kills".
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: What a game really well done. The atmosphere the swordsmanship it was all amazing. If you like anything samurai related or like the old Kurosawa movies this is a must play. The atmosphere is enough too sell me fighting in the rain with lighting and everything will never get old. You can also easily beat the game in one sitting like i did. overall 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Immaculate. A subtle beauty between story, visual, and game play. Very engaging and rewarding visually. As you advance, the visual delights get replaced with the pace of sword play and oncoming enemies to bring you into the realm of this world in turmoil. Every game camera shot seems to have been curated delicately, precise to a point where you do mentally escape into the world that is Yomi.Choices of paths change the story line. Truly a magnificent work of art. Sit forward and immerse yourself into this one and feel you are "the Samurai". Stunning and a Cinematic masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Giving it a recommend with a TW: all the war things. They don't soften it here, especially in the sound design.I had fun with this game. Played it on the Story difficulty and finished in 7 hours. It's souls-like on higher difficulties for those who enjoy a challenge. I did find the sound design to be a bit mixed. Great music and atmosphere, but some of the atmosphere is a bit... too much. Could have been toned down. Overall an easy recommend if you enjoy fighting, platforming and getting your a** kicked a gazillion times.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Just a heads up for what is a beautiful and a cool game - you are going to want to throw your controller at a wall sooner or later if you play this. So if you're in it for the visuals and the story, don't bother with anything else than easy difficulty.As for the visuals - they're striking. I love Kurosawa and the use of grainy, black and white scenes that employ his philosophy of constant movement in a very rich and deep frame. Combined with Japanese mythology it makes for a very interesting setting for a game. The sound design is also very fitting.But then we have to talk about the elephant in the room. The combat. I've seen people split into camps over the combat system. Some say it's complete trash and others that it's good once you master it. I believe the intent of it is admirable and the combat itself is good... when it isn't unfair and when it works it can be really satisfying. And I do respect the developers for creating a game that's old school hard in a way. But the combat system will often test your patience more than your skill. When you're being attacked left and right (literally) and the character doesn't want to switch sides for some reason and when you get stuck in an opponent's combo, and you're grinding a single scene for the X'th time you will find yourself wishing there was a skip button or something.If you've got a kink for beautiful visuals and you're a patient person - buy it.If you're not patient and you care more about the mechanics of a game - skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale and I feel like I robbed the Developers. Amazing game. Gameplay reminds me of Onimusha but way more polished. Just played for 90 minutes and I didn't quit because I was bored, I quit so I can savor it. The swordplay feels fast and deadly. The style and story are 100% Kurisawa, and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: It has decent atmosphere but the gameplay is unfortunately bad. The fighting system is unbalanced but its definitely fixable. It has a good fundament to build upon, the devs just need to dish out minor tweaks to make this a gem imo. I will give it a positive rating anyway though because i got it during sale and it is definitely worth 5€ or less in this current state.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: HERE WE GO!Not knowing anything of this game. Bought it after seeing the previews on steam. Mechanics looked amazing and for a more in-depth side scroller this game caught my attention reason why i pulled the trigger and bought it. Did not realize there were multiple endings. Started this game off on the most hardest difficulty and yes it was definitely a challenge. After completing the one of the first endings is why I am not posting this review. The game goes further into mechanics with its combo system which can also be chained and timing is a thing with this as well. I've noticed trying to attempt certain combos they would not go off unless you time the buttons perfectly. I play this with a controller on PC and  on the steamdeck and both run amazingly. Extremely happy with my purchase and looking forward to revealing the other endings!
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely mindnumbingly uninvolved. The aesthetics are nice at first but quickly make the game feel monotonous even when the game makes significant change in what it's doing, and most of combat is like a bogstandard beat-em-up/hack n' slash where you just go from screen to screen to kill 2-3 guys and repeat ad nauseum. Game is only about 4-5 hrs long but feels way longer.There's potential there but it just doesn't work out in this case.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: yes while i recommend this game i have to stress this game still has some bugs after the patches i started my first play through on hard mode the game has been fun and not really to difficult  but there is a part near the end of chapter 5 where the are so many block and perry bugs it make me want to restart the game these glitches will speed up and slow the actions you perform  ive seen these bugs through the rest of the game but they where so minor i felt like it was my controller  attaining to my blocking anyway  yes the game is pleasing in many ways  if your a fan of the samurai play it just on normal id say  as the damage by enemys  plus these bugs will cause more retrys  then most could tolerate
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This is a stock standard side scrolling action game in a 2.5D space.The visuals are absolutely stunning and it's almost like playing through an old samurai movie from the 50s.If you are new to gaming, this is great, it has all the standard video game tropes and zero innovation in gameplay. This game is an amazing in the perspective of attracting people to gaming because how it's used the visuals.That being said, if you have played your share of games, don't get this.If playing it is like watching an old samurai movie, well, these samurai movies are generally higher quality than this game, and you should just go watch these movies.The problems is that the visuals are all this game has.The combat is a bit weird and the characters are a bit clunky. There's no enemy variation past the first few levels and then you just get to fight the shiny ghost versions with slightly different move and some zombies. That all can be forgiven if the combat is crisp and responsive, but it's not, responsiveness is not the biggest strength of this game. It's still ok, the combat is not difficult to nail down, although enemy attack patterns are the same the entire game and by the end of it you are just carving through entire rooms without much trouble. It did made me feel like I was just slogging through padded areas. This game has no replay value.This game offers nothing new for experienced gamers but could be used as a great introductory for people who aren't so familiar with gaming mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, astounding sound design. Rather simple story of revenge, but well done. Read the lore to fully understand the story. Game-play can get repetitive unless you actively try to vary up your combos. My personal biggest gripe is the fact that I can't replay individual chapters after the end. I missed TWO, only TWO lore collectables and am frustrated that I need to replay the entire game again. It does have multiple endings and a new difficulty mode after you beat it once, so there's that. Received product for $10 during sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I read reviews complaining about simple combat, but I guess I just don't understand why that's an issue for a short casual indie game like this. Generally, I thought this was a fun time. The aesthetic carries a lot of weight, to be sure. In a game with such simple combat, there is a risk that the combat becomes tedious if the game drags on too long. I do think it does that here. Six chapters only, instead of the present seven, would have been better. I think they should have just cut out some of the hell levels and the game would have been much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. Beatiful AD and good gameplay, even if turning around and ranged weapons are not easy to use at first time. Sometimes it's not easy to orient yourself with the camera changes, but the viewpoints are very beautiful, so you get used to it quickly. I come back to this game every time I switch on my computer, that was a long time that I discover a nice game like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Its a stunning looking game, truly breathtaking at times. The combat is difficult but once you lock it in its not unbearable, timing and patience are the key to getting it to lock in. It is short and although there are multiple endings I'm satisfied with the one I chose and can't see myself needing to immediately jump back in.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi is game in a more loose sense of the word. While a game is not made by its visuals, some games make the most use of them and this is one of those games. Combat is more akin to a filler between set pieces or using set pieces to their fullest with cast shadows, burning buildings, or raging winds. Fights start out hard or maybe even downright frustrating until the system grows on you or the timing clicks, then it shifts from the former to nothing more than minor annoyances between you and the next line of dialogue or beautiful scene. Trek to Yomi doesn't out stay its welcome nor does it innovate but literally every area is oozing with detail and careful placement of visuals as though you're skipping from painting to painting. A scene is not complete without its sound or music and both are served in perfect abundance. While you are mostly on rails for the journey, the mix between art, serviceable sound, and beautiful music is more than enough to make up for average combat.I recommend this game to anyone with a little patience, who is a samurai movie enthusiast, or simply wanting to explore beautiful scenery while being engrossed by the sounds of winds and flutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I am almost done with my first playthrough on Ronin difficulty, and really enjoying it so far. I am aiming for getting 100% achievements too.Pros:- Beautiful art style and music to match- Combat rewards fast reaction time and good positioning- Different endings and earnable difficulty setting adds to playtimeCons:- Ranged items are not that useful- Non-boss enemies are easily taken down with any stun/finisher combo (backwards + strong attack -> finisher is easiest)- No chapter-select (even after beating the game) makes replaying certain sections a hassle without save manipulationOne thing for anyone that likes to 100% games, this game has a ton of missable artifacts and skill upgrades. If you miss something, you just have to try for it again next playthrough unless you create a copy of your save. The game is not too long, so it is not the worst thing though.Overall, for the price I am really happy with this game. I bought it for half-off ($10) but I would pay full price too.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: A great Akira Kurosawa style walking simulator with a katana that you can kill someone :)the design focus is visual art, with tons of composition and shots idea for presenting the Akira Kurosawa art style...A tribute to Yojimbo but Art contents break everything else....hmmm... besides a memorable and impressive visual art design... What else is there?Poor combat design, simple story, children puzzle, and frustrating camera effect blocks the sight of player frequently..hmmm... In general... it's a 6/10 “movie" that I can play with a controller...
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that suck you in right away. The visuals alone keep you playing, it's like you're watching an old samurai movie. The game also surprises you with some pretty cool camera angles. At one point I'm fighting behind paper partition walls and all you see are silhouettes:DI'm liking the story and the gameplay, looking forward to finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I love this Kurosawa vibe, and the gameplay was pleasantly challenging. I had some misinputs other players report, but nothing too challenging. I recommend Ronin difficulty for start, then (if you enjoy the game enough) the Kensei - it's really game changing - all non-boss entities are one hit kill (that includes you!) - this is the way the game should be played!
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric as any game i've ever played. The art style and cinematography work well.I loved every second of it. This is among my all-time favorite games.. If you're looking for a game about 4-5 hours long, with beautiful art style, different renditions of both the real and supernatural worlds, and abundant opportunities for screenshots, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi is a game developed by Leonard Menchiari and Flying Wild Hog and published by Devolver DigitalThe game offers some nice graphics and a really beautiful aesthetic, although some really ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the same. The game does suffer from some really bad glitches that I'm quite surprised were never fixed or patched in later, and it's not just me that encountered these glitches, many others did as wellThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game and a painfully average story and really boring sections of the game which hindered me from enjoying it even more than I wanted to but it's an okay game nonetheless, I guessTrek to Yomi overall, however, is an okay game to play with a lot of shortfalls and issues that only people who like an average story make like, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is an okay adventure game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning and amazing art direction could easily be a 10/10.  I have mixed feelings about the combat system sometimes it works and feels pretty good, and sometimes it is the worst thing ever that sucks the enjoyment out of the game. but do not let it distract you from everything this game has to offer.  I give it 7/10. (buy on sale if you are cautious)"Sending people to Yomi does not mean sending them to the afterlife. It means that you are sending them to Yubari in modern Japan.""Hmm...Damn bratty bandits...! !! !! Raiding villages :anger::anger: I need a sword correction... :anger:
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfecly stylish - story in Feudal Japan, presented as an old Japan black-n-white movie...however thats all it can really offer. Story itself is pretty much cliche and fighting system is badly unbalanced - extremely easy on Easy setting, while frustrating on next one - Medium, so you cant find the balance for you. One good thing is that game is very short, can be beaten over the weekend or so...
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.  The combat is good and the move unlock system is good.  You can choose your difficulty so the game isnt really hard. However, the stunning visuals make up for these otherwise ok features. The collectable system, which contribute greatly to the immersion and worldbuilding, are a standout feature. For the price, I reccomend you get this game.  It's live Seven Samurai blended with Ghost of Tsushima.  8.7/10 game!
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi was incredible! What can I say, I enjoyed the beautiful wide angles reminiscent of classic cinema - the visual art/style (Kurosawa Cinematography). In addition, short story about love, loss and vengeance. The game starts slow, but it will becomes fast-paced the more you play it, and the combat is fun and satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the visuals and story of the game. Excellent Camera angles that are really cinematic. The controls are a bit rough though- sometimes even frustrating. You really need to learn a few key combos that can stagger enemies to progress well. Overall a short game though, As I beat it in about 4.5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: The selling point of this game is its stylization as mid century japanese samurai film. It is purely black and white, with locations feeling like set pieces and all of it covered by filters that emulate film grains and various scratches and defects of aged film reel. The music uses traditional instruments and there is a japanese voice acting with subtitles to complete the illusion. The game contains collectibles that serve to explain some of the background of Edo era life and believes.  The gameplay is centered on fights interspersed with short exploration intervals. The fights are based on duelling opponents, with dodging, countering, combos and stunning. When I managed to pull it off, it looked great; however I could do only a handful of moves consistently. Even so I managed to go through the game on normal difficulty without too much frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who found the game play in Sekiro too hard this is a good alternative. I get what people are saying about the game play being too easy but it has a really engaging story and it looks great. There's plenty of katana combos added throughout the game and there's a variety of range weapons to keep things interesting. There was a few basic puzzle challenges which were interesting but not difficult and a singular time challenge (could have used more of those actually, seemed like a last minute edition to the game). Also there were a couple of boss battles that I personally had a bit of difficulty with so I did get that sense of achievement from getting through them.100% recommend if you just want to have fun slashing your way through a great story with some amazing visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game is designed to make you feel like you're playing a Kurosawa film. This is obviously the goal the game is striving towards and it achieves it really well. I love how this game looks and I'm enamored with how it sounds. The only stain is the frankly mediocre gameplay. So just be aware that this is less of a sword fighting game and more of a beautiful homage to Japanese cinema.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Although the gameplay is simple, it's a fun game to play and enjoy. I played through the Ronin difficulty and had a good amount of fun and challenge with the game. I will definitely play through it again to see the other endings to the story. If you are not into games that are short or linear then this game is not for you it's very scripted and narrow in terms of gameplay variety. there is also an English dub that you can apply if you so desire, but I do recommend playing it through with the Japanese audio for Authenticity and Immersion. If none of these is an issue to you then hack and slash away my fellow Samurai (bows Proudly and then exit's)
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this whole game in a single day and while the experience I had with the game wasn't all terrible. It was a fairly decent game at best. The game's presentation is one of the strongest elements of the game but it wasn't enough to save for its combat and gameplay. At times, I found myself repeating the same simple moves then any of the combos with little difficulty. The enemies would have me at a corner and because I can't roll by them. It made things real frustrating for me. The game expects you to use the combos, whenever I tried there would be occasions the enemy would stun lock me or not register at all. The heavy combos I highly recommend the most as they helped me during the endgame. With the exception of the final boss and another. The bosses are by far the weakest element for me. You can roll past simple movesets, parry them, or use your strong attack to highly damage their health bars.The game is divided into seven chapters and has different endings. It also encourages exploration which unlocks combos, more health and stamina. Some collectables if you want more insight on Japanese culture. I do somewhat recommend this game because its fairly entertaining for what it pulls off. You can finish this whole game in one day and its replay value comes from its difficulty settings and see different outcomes.Trek to Yomi did lived up to my expectations when I first saw the trailer and was happy that I played it.  However I can't recommend this game if you dislike short video games. For a game that's 20$, it felt more like 10$.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great at first. From the art style to the story line. But there is one bad thing about it which makes it not worth playing, the combat. It seemed okay at first but it's a bit clunky and some of the combinations cant be done. You should not get this game, maybe watch a YouTuber play it? Most of the combinations make the same result making the harder combos not worth it and making it easy to spam with the easy ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: very enjoyable game. For this kind of game all apects of it are well made. especially the fighting system is to point out. it needs some time to get used to the timing and the pace. but after some practice you will be rewarded with very satisfying and elegant samurai-duels.i am really looking forward for addons for this game and new games from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed bag. I made it all the way until the final boss on hard, and then it just went full ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Parries arent super consistent, and then half the time inputs just feel ignored, I beat this post patch. Visually it is stunning, the story and voice acting are great, but it just falls short in the polish on the gameplay. It gets really samey because there is an objectively best way to play on higher difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game in 2 sittings although it is well doable in one swoop.The combat system is unforgiving played at anything else than easy (Kabuki) level, so I suggest at least one game played in that difficulty at the beginning, because there is much to enjoy:the art, music, style, story and even the folklore descriptions of the collectibles are thoroughly enjoyable, and especially if one realizes that this game runs on Ultra even on a 9 years old PC like mine.I can't wait for the developers to upload something describing the development because it must be interesting.Also I bought it on a whim during the Devolver Sale Weekend just because I love Devolver, but last week I played Shadow Warrior and was disgusted, and surely I was not expecting this to be develop by the same studio, given how minimal and elegant it is. But then starting the second run, I noticed what maybe the reason: the original idea and probably some supervision is by Leonard Menchiari who is managing to become the Spike Jonze of videogames in my opinion (go back and check his other 2 titles if you didn't play them).So, to summarize: strikingly beautiful, short (which is a plus for me), non-AAA title capturing the spirit of Samurai classic cinema in a game that runs well even on low end PCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning!. I lost myself in the game like I was in a old Black & White samurai movie. The combat became more enjoyable when I learned new combos. I enjoyed side tracking off the main paths for a bit of exploration, upgrades and items. This has a bit of Little nightmare / Limbo presentation. Multiple choices on multiple occasions to determine a path. This probably consists of different dialog and endings. I LOVED IT! and plan on playing this again \m/
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: If God Of War and Ghost Of Tsushima had a child, this is what the game would look like.Although relatively short, the game has high replayability. The story takes you to Yomi, the Japanese underworld, where you will find your true self after being faced with difficult choices. There are several possible endings, including a secret one.The atmosphere in this game is, simply put, amazing. Reminiscent of Kurosawa's movies, the focus on Japanese mythology and the story of Izanagi and Izanami in particular is a very nice twist. The gameplay is enjoyable, unlike several reviewers who in my view are a bit too harsh I find the combat system quite good though one must get used to it.A single playthrough lasts for about 6 hours or so, relatively short but as I said there is high replayability. I strongly encourage you to give it a try, I for one would not hesitate to buy a DLC.

Would recommend if you're looking a bad-ass samurai game!  Only con I would say is the combat doesn't evolve into anything crazy or in depth but that was okay for me.  8 aikos/10 aikos
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: The entire point of the game is combat and story... The story is decent no complaints. The combat is decent at first and then gets worse. The entire roster of enemies can somehow super armor through your attack and hit you immediately after getting cut so. there's no feeling of weight to you hitting enemies but they feel like they hit like a sledgehammer. and combos the game gives either do not work at all or you can only do it once and then wonder what was different that time than any other. If they actually fixed the inputs with the combat i would like this game until then its unplayable to me

_childDocuments_.review: First playthrough with Ronin Difficulty, which is Hard Mode. This game has 4 difficulties considered it as Easy, Normal, Hard & Insane. You have to beat the game first to unlock the Hardest Difficulty which is called Kensei ( Insane ).Game is short but once you know how to combo and utilize your finisher to regen your health, then you will be fine. Ronin and Below Difficulties should be fine without using any Range Atk. Cause i only used it once or twice with Range Atk for fun. 99% of the time i was trying to use my finisher to take out the enemies because during the Finisher Animation, you will have I-Frame. That's how you beat the game and of course learn the Enemies ATK / Movement Pattern.Story is not too bad but sadly it is linear and short. Gameplay is good but it can be better of course. It is not something new to be honest, it is just old concept but implement with some new designs and that's it!If you want real challenge, straight to Ronin and then try Kensei.Overall i'm Rating It 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the atmosphere, the graphics and the story (no new "story" as it is, it was just nice to watch imo). I never write reviews for games (at least until now), but this has to be done. I make it short.Aesthetics are incredible, i personally love japanese themed games and this one nailed it (especially japanese voice acting).The map is linear, no big way around or something or big maps to explore. I liked it that way.And now the important Part, the combat. It is simple.....simple, not easy. Playing the game i noticed how i became better with the controls (which are not too complicated) and even got it how to use the combos. *Sarcasm on* Spoiler *Sarcasm off* ---> dont spam buttons....It really is not that hard to play it. On the plus side there are like a maximum of 2 fights between each checkpoints. There is not a single time i had to run like 5 minutes to get to the battle normal mobs or a boss. I love Sekiro for example and the game reminded me at bit of this game. Just get to know the game and see how easy a boss becomes compared to the first time you played the game. I do recommend this game a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so looking forward to this but sadly i was disappointed to the extent i refunded the game. No matter how visually unique the graphics was, it just couldnt make up the deficit of a lack luster combat system. There is so many game in this genre that when you are spoiled with options, its hard to recommend something that sadly felt flat to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: Before I to tell you why you should., here's why you shouldn't. This game's biggest flaw is it's game-play. The combat of this game is very under-cooked. About 30 minutes in the game gives you a combo into insta-kill finisher that works on all enemies up to the toughest of regular mobs. This makes the levels feel more like a "Run to the end" rather than a challenge. This also means that on bosses the difficulty skyrockets for no reason. A certain boss does a lot of jumping attacks that will stun you to the point where I either put the game down for good, or lowered the difficulty to the minimum. The ranged weapons also feel like an afterthought. Since you plow through enemies in a single combo they serve no real purpose.However.This game is beautiful. The story while a bit basic did what it had to do for me. The music and collectibles were fun. The whole game feels like a old cheesy movie. It's definitely worth experiencing if you're in the mood for that.In the end, it's a game to put on a shelf and experience, but not one I enjoyed game-play wise.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game, wish there was an option to load chapters as you really can't go back to a specific section without going through the game again. Also would be nice if it had some kind of "EXTRAS" menu where you could change your costume, how enemies look, have the game be in color, etc. but overall cool game. Maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Trek to Yomi

_childDocuments_.review: A example of perfect presentation and poor execution.Trek to Yomi feels like a passion project from a visual and story perspective with lots of really cool detail and dedication in the storytelling, visuals and enviorment interaction, but the mask starts to slip when gameplay mechanics show up.Combat feels stilted, there is no "flow" to fights or even the combos you can throw out, for a 2d fighter the concept of having to press a seperate button to face enemies behind you is borderline idiocy (the last game to ever do this was MK Mythologies a game not known for its design choices.) the parry/counter system is the worst one i think i've ever seen yet the game seems to intend for you to rely on it in a pinch as it restores HP.Trek to Yomi is a game i want to like, it does one of my favorite tropes of putting monsters into a grounded fantasy setting but the mechanics and controls of the game just get in the way of it being anything more than a chore to play. If Devolver gets around to giving the game a overhaul i'll gladly change this review but until then its a firm "no"

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi was a bit of a mixed experience for me, but overall I'd still recommend it. The game is absolutely gorgeous and the camera is always creating shots that you'll want to take in. This game has made me stop just to appreciate my surroundings more than any other game I've played. The story was alright. Not much else to say, its pretty simple. The music wasn't very memorable. Combat... Is weird... I think the controls felt good although long combos can be tough to perform because you cant just perform the combo all in one go, you have to wait until the animation of every attack is done which throws me off. Most fights came down to stunning enemies with 1 or 2 of the same combos and performing a finisher on them.So yeah, as I said before, mixed bag but I'd still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Trek to Yomi opens with young Hiroki honing his skills with Master Sanjuro as a tutorial. Our basic moveset consists of a two-hit light attack combo which can be altered if you hold up or down/W or S, a heavy strike, a block & parry and a dodge roll. But once we come face-to-face with our first foe, the cracks start to show. If playing with controller, you must keep the left analogue stick neutral, otherwise you'll be performing a stab. The game will buffer your inputs, but a lack of animation cancelling leads to repeated deaths - you have no choice but to commit to offense or defense. Speaking of defenses, the parry window is fairly generous, most likely to compensate for the stylistic design. Most combat arenas obscure the "glint of the enemy's blade", and the lack of any audio cues makes the parrying reliant on memorization. The introductory chapter is the most difficult in terms of standard enemies. You have very few moves, no ranged weapons, and a modicum of health & stamina. Run out of health, and it's back to the most recent checkpoint. Run out of stamina, and you'll be forced into the 'tired' state - all you can do is attempt to attack and parry. After the introductory chapter, stamina management is a non-issue thanks to the plethora of upgrades scattered around the world. As our first glimpse into the world of Trek to Yomi, chapter one does set the stage for what's to come, even if the mechanical issues appear right away.Once the main antagonist, Kagerou, wipes the floor with Hiroki, Sanjuro, and the village, we get a time skip! Hiroki vows to his love, Aiko, to protect the village of Kamikawamura from the invading bandits. This is the part of the game where the entire combat system versus non-boss opponents falls apart. You unlock a move upon starting chapter two proper; this move is  powerful. A three hit combo (light-light-heavy) which has the power to ignore blocking, stun the enemy, and consumes no stamina on the third hit. A few minutes later, we get the ability to perform an invincible instant-kill on any stunned foe to regain three points of health. While the timing to execute this unbeatable combo is tight, learning it is far more rewarding than studying the enemies' attacks. There are zero downsides to spamming this technique, and it is a shame. The 2D beat 'em up action is very engaging during boss fights, but mowing down hundreds of goons with this setup is mind-numbing. "Just don't use it then!" While that is a good point, I did run into many situations where my health bar was depleted in the blink of an eye. Whether it was multiple baddies hitting me at once, or taking damage in a unique hitbox, the number of times I  I was getting instantly killed were aggravating. Resorting to the killer combo seemed to be the only option for a ronin, which did suit my choices during the story.The boss encounters in Trek to Yomi are immune to the killer combo, thankfully. I cannot reveal much information on the fights, however, due to their spoilery nature. Just know that you will be in for attacks that break your guard, and eventually become unblockable. Spacing is key in the duels; rolling has no invincibility frames, but can get you to the opponent's back, if used on the correct move.Sporting no RPG elements whatsoever, and opting to use classic upgrades means there is no overleveling in Trek to Yomi. Your skill with the blade is all you need. That, and the unnecessary upgraded version of the 'killer combo'. In chapter four, you'll unlock a variation of the light-light-heavy string, but up/W must be held to perform it. The combo is much quicker than the standard and sports longer reach, but consumes stamina. One of the last moves earned is yet another variation of this, with even more speed and range This input requires you to hold down/S and tap light-light-light-heavy in a very specific rhythm. If you mash, the input will drop and you'll take unavoidable damage. Is it balanced? Maybe, but you should test it yourself.The dev team set out to make a streamlined beat 'em up system and I suppose they succeeded. While I did enjoy my time with Trek to Yomi, I am unsure if I will do subsequent playthroughs. If you are looking for a mindless button masher, this isn't it, as evidenced by the inconsistent handling of player inputs. If you're looking for a deeply complex beat 'em up, this isn't it, as shown by the easy access to instant-kills. Trek to Yomi's mechanics fall somewhere in between those extremes, and it works. If you take the path of ronin,  your goal should be to dispatch anyone who stands in your way as efficiently as possible. Playing on easy or normal is recommended as the combat is the weakest aspect of the game; the artistry and atmosphere of the Trek might be more than enough to keep this title out of the depths of Yomi for you, as it did for me.
