_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2:another switch.Gotta understand that this is attempting to be a soulsborne-lite.The real fun begins if you crank up the difficulty, and then REALLY pay close attention to weak spots and types of damage to use. Once you learn to parry with the sword, it becomes somewhat easier - but in order to truly flourish you'll have to explore every nook and cranny to find secrets.I feel this game requires one of those "You're playing it wrong" manuals or tutorials.Anyway - probably worth the cash. Hexen is just one of influences ,I bet Witchaven and dark souls were the others.Edit:changed my mind and switched to Thumbs Down.By the time I reached the library - I have literally completely given up and was playing simply because of sunken costs. I was steadily getting more and more frustrated after the first quest (Lighthouse), but I thought, OK, its just temporary, there'll be a payoff somewhere...No such thing.The most polished experience is the one you'll get the first hour, maybe two. The rest goes downfall slowly, but when it hits the library - it just becomes an exercise in frustration. It is visible from the airplane that no one play tested this. You simply have no tools, no weapons, no moving abilities - to stand up to gangs of enemies that go after you.I've come to a point where I simply focused on one enemy, kept slashing at it until it was dead - and then died myself. Rinse & repeat until the whole mob is done.Then, you meet an invincible enemy that follows you around through walls and hits you with AoE and hitscan attack. At this point, I have completely given up fighting as well, and just kept running through hordes of enemies looking for puzzles to solve.Astonishingly terrible design.This game is going to need a bit of a miracle to save itself. Which ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks, because there's a TON of level content in there to explore, and whoever crafted the maps is a master at his job.Whoever designed enemies and -especially- weapons - needs to go back to their real job of flipping burgers because this is atrocious.I am uninstalling this garbage because I can't be bothered at all to finish this. Would rather go watch paint dry.Original review:So, I get what its trying to be, but it'll need a whole lot more of love.I almost gave up within first 2h because pacing is nearly atrocious. Sure, you unlock your second "weapon" very quickly - but its basically a puzzle solver, so you'll spend a good 1.5-2.0h fighting most of enemies with your starter stick.On the positive side - your spells have many interesting interactions with the environment.Eventually you get a poor-ass hand crossbow, simply because you also get ranged enemies, and then you get a sword which honestly seems weaker than your staff, but it allows you to parry.You have stamina and because you can die pretty easily, there's a dash of soulsbornes feeling to it - however, dying costs nothing from what I've seen so far, and checkpoints are generious so your "punishment" is to backtrack for 10-15 seconds.It is very cool that it has inventory and hotbar system so you can pick and choose what goes on your hotbar - but then again, it locks certain things up so you can't move them.Again, the pacing issue - you can upgrade all your weapons and spells, but it costs insane amounts of gold compared to how much you earn. In my 3h play, I don't think I gathered even 1700gold, all spent on upgrading staff and sword. To upgrade your spells so that they aren't useless in combat - you need 6000 gold. I am not even sure there's enough content in the game for that price - so it might've been solved by gating how much gold you get in the beginning... but then why the damn fake shops to begin with? Either give me a shop so I can pick when and what to upgrade to manage my playstyle - or simply let me pick the damn upgrades the same way I pick the weapons.Maps are very large and quite interesting to explore, and you get a really cool drawn map to help you. However - some parts are so insanely dark that even by lighting nearby torches and boosting gamma - its still almost pitch black. Again, positive side - eventually you get a to a point where you start getting shortcuts in maps, which is pretty cool - but then again, once you use them /once/, you don't need them ever again.I had this game on my wishlist probably for 2 years, waiting for a good special to come around, because reviews were pushing me away - and honestly, the reviews were right. As you can see from my own - its a mixed bag of good and bad.Graphics are great, maps are great, ideas are great... but the way its all stitched together is, imo, a mess, and needs a good experienced game designer to adjust the gauges to make it into an awesome game.Potential is absolutely there, but I wonder if it'll be reached because if the game stays like this and just adds more content.... that's 4/10 for me.For now thumbs up because its EA.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven is a pretty significant disappointment.I enjoyed Heretic and Hexen and when I heard that there was a new retro shooter styled game coming out going for that sort of style, with some immersive sim stuff thrown in as well I was all for it. While it has the aesthetics that I was looking for, I find the rest of the game to be undercooked.Graven is divided into acts, and while the problems are already evident in the first act things don't become particularly egregious until later. There are weight switch puzzles that break and revert upon loading a save and you have to take the weight off the switch to solve it again. There is no actual save system in Graven, it insists on using checkpoints instead which just makes things more of a pain, you can't save, quit, and start back up where you left off, you need to backtrack to wherever you were from town, where you pop back everytime you load a save, a problem that's compounded by how Graven also uses a stamina meter which limits sprinting. There are places where the player can get trapped with no way out without either quitting out and being forced to backtrack or blowing yourself up. There is a trap sequence that you can soft lock yourself out of being able to solve it. That same trap sequence can also bug out and kill you when you should be safe.Really a lot of the game seems to be not completely thought out. You are given multiple melee options, but the way the game plays means you will definitely not be as effective as just shooting enemies with the numerous ranged weapons you have instead. You can only have so many weapons assigned to hotbar keys at any given time, each weapon taking up a certain amount of space on it. It's an interesting idea but you can pause at any time to move stuff around means that its just added tedium. The immersive sim stuff seems to be limited to stacking crates in certain locations to get to the occasional secret and electrocuting water to stun groups of enemies, something that only came a few times. There will be no creating elaborate staircases of barrels and crates to get somewhere early, they break from under you when you try. When you find chests of stuff, the things inside explode outward, sometimes landing somewhere inaccessible or outright falling into a death pit.The worst part is that it's not all bad. The art style looks cool, some (but not all) weapons are satisfying to use and have good feedback. There's a weapon upgrade system that adds not just boosts to damage but alternate firing modes and utility, though losing the gold needed for those upgrades on death is especially frustrating when you die from the game bugging out. There are altars that give permanent increases to max health, stamina, and mana, which is a pretty great reward for exploration. Some enemy designs can look pretty cool, although some encounters are not the best (like fighting five big damage sponge enemies that can heal each other at the same time), and the game over uses enemies reflecting projectiles. Overall, Graven's bad parts overcome the good and I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Attempted to play all the way through, but am no longer compelled to finish due to frustration.I really wanted to enjoy this as it is heralded as being a successor to Heretic/HeXen as well as '90s FPS titles. I seriously can't see this and fail to understand any such comparisons as the ONLY similarity is art style. Having play Duke Nukem, Quake, Quake II, Heretic, HeXen, HeXen II, Unreal, Strife, DooM, DooM II, and many others over the years, I never felt such disappointment as it didn't play like any of those games. As Ion Maiden (Fury) nailed this claim in every regard, I chose to give this game a chance.  Firstly, what I did enjoy or thought interesting. The art style is unique and creates a nice atmosphere which is aided by a nice soundtrack. Although looking like a dated game, it looks good and feels like it was made many years ago.  Yeah, now what I didn't like and I know, not much to like, lol. Combat is what an FPS is about and it is not fun nor engaging. When one plays say DooM or Quake or Halo or any other FPS, you can feel a comfortable loop or play style(s) forming as you get more experience with it. In Graven, it boils down to whacking almost everything with a wooden staff. I don't say everything because there are annoying flying enemies that spit acid from miles away that you can't hit with it. Another note, with almost 8 hours in, I have 4 weapons and 2 spells. Now, you might say, wow, you have that many at your disposal and only use a staff? Yes, the sword is not an upgrade as it deals about the same damage and has a block mechanic, but is executed badly. As for ranged you get a weak wrist crossbow and a crossbow that shoots rocks that functions as a shotgun, but does unreliable damage. The spells are an absolute disgrace to magic as they are the most impractical, weak, very inefficient at resource cost and killing power. The devs explained that using spells to shock water or ignite barrels to help be resourceful in combat. Alright, shocking water just stuns enemies and does little damage and you have to be about 2 feet from a barrel to ignite it then the enemies just take a minor amount of damage. So, basically use the staff for melee and crossbows for flying until certain later enemies (we will get to THEM).  Progression is another setback as one would expect from a game of the targeted period, is somewhat maze-like level design. Graven doesn't do hallways connected by arenas and tries a large map connected by different unique areas rather than level transitions and tries to make a hub from Cruxfirth and each area is somewhat reachable from that hub. However, this is a major issue as each area is not reachable from there and is an absolute pain to traverse the world because every damn time you quit, enemies are repopulated. Also, saving, doesn't even do that. You always start back in Cruxfirth. I do not understand this decision and it needs to be fixed as everyone seems to hate this or do not respawn the very annoying enemies you have created. I understand re-killing is part of the economy, but then fix it by having better rewards or lower costs or have them in secrets or actually make the combat enjoyable. Even at that, starting the game up again is depressing as you have to slog through the enemies again and again or just run and hope you don't get hit.  So, the enemies, the reason for combat and all. 90% of the time is zombies then cultists. Now, why is that bad? Zombies deal a lot of damage on higher difficulties and once you get a hang of their attacks, a few can be easily killed. However, they are thrown at you in large groups and take many hits unless hit in the head which is somewhat hard for the poor hit detection of the staff. Then the other issue is the slow clearing of enemies using a staff. In DooM, the Rocket Launcher does splash damage and high direct-hit damage, clears weaker enemies quickly. Now, I am not saying add one, but this is a problem on ALL difficulties and is worsened as you progress because enemies eventually have both ranged and melee or long reach for melee which out-ranges you and are forced to used your precious ammo. This is another major issue as melee weapons don't use ammo or mana and use stamina which is annoying since it feels out of place and is there to just slow you down or prevent you from jumping. Speaking of the weapons, they can be upgraded, but I laughed at them as the spell upgrades were the only ones that seemed worth the high cost (hint, hint, all of them are crazy expensive). So, you never actually feel any stronger as you progress (yes, I fully upgraded the Staff, Sword, Wrist Crossbow, Crossbow, and both spells) which is not good. So, the other enemies? Skeletons that have longer reach melee, skeletons with bombs and wrist bows, cultists with throwing daggers, 4-legged beasts with really bad animations that don't display attacks properly, flying acid-spitting things, armored cultists, ghosts, and some ghostly skull boss. Notice how I don't know their names or speak fondly of them because none of the enemies are fun to fight or seem unique in a game play perspective. In DooM, an Archvile is instantly recognizable as it has a reputation for resurrection demons, dealing a lot of damage when those flames start flashing, or their appearance. How about the first Skarj you faced in Unreal? Scary, dodging attacks, rushing you with movement predicting projectiles, and a Predator-inspired design?  Anyway, rambling, moving on now. As a strong suggestion, wait until many issues are addressed and I do look forward to seeing this game be complete, but it has been a few years and is looking grim. For the devs, keep improving, but the game has a good atmosphere with a somewhat there story that could improve the immersion, but it is severely held back by the most important part, the game play. Movement is slow, progression is slow, enemies are not fun to fight, and I would rather not use any of the weapons in my arsenal as I don't like them or the feel of them. Another thing, the inventory is somehow more annoying than Heretic because there are not quick-cast hot keys for items and instead everything is on a hotbar and must be selected and some weapons take multiple slots for some reason. Also, ammo counts are too low for higher difficulties (played on the 2nd to hardest difficulty first time then did various testing on others) along with a really low item cap on "Quartz Flasks". Weapons should fulfill a role in combat or possibly make spells viable as stated above, the sword is honestly worse than the staff. Spells are useless outside of puzzles or not wanting to use arrows on explosives. Make enemies fulfill specific roles in combat or seem unique. All melee enemies are the same, rush player and perform attack and later enemies just get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ range that doesn't match animations or ranged units get armor so they can't be head shot. Until many, many updates to those categories and bug fixes (yeah, quite a few teleporting enemies among other problems) are implemented, I won't be revisiting this game and I would suggest the same to you unless you want a frustrating experience. I would very highly recommend Amid Evil if you want a perfect example of a throwback '90s.

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game. It's like Diablo 2 and Quake 2 had a baby. My spatial memory hasn't been worked like this in ages. I like the old style level design, that re-uses areas by introducing previously inaccessible paths. Everything is smooth and feels like what a game should be, just enough detail for your imagination to do the rest, like the older games. Combat is a puzzle in itself, allowing the player to learn to adapt to different enemies and their weakness, which I found to be very interesting. Sometimes you have to put your mind in the developers shoes to progress through certain areas by finding ways that are not immediately obvious, but overall it was smooth sailing for the majority of the time. The one thing I would say is that after completing the game, I missed quite a few weapons, I simply did not encounter them. So I wish the developers took note of like Dark Messiah Might & Magic, where if you didn't find the new weapon, you'll find the same one in some secret area later in the game, or even in the town merchants for a price. Overall, I'd say the wait was well worth it. The team did a lovely job. I am glad to still be alive to have experienced this. I wish there were more games like this, in the same low-poly style as back in the day. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this game is shockingly bad. Honestly I don't expect Slipgate to improve any of this so I won't get into detail and just mention a few issues instead.- The save system is terrible. Slipgate, you've been doing this to me since Rise of the Triad 2013 and I just fail to understand how implementing something as simple as save slots can prove to be an insurmountable challenge for this company. And in some respects this game is even worse than ROTT because whenever you decide to quit the game and then launch it again later you get put back to the town square for whatever reason. What the actual....- This is a Hexen-esque "metroidvania-like" game that doesn't give you access to a map. That's super strange since the early access version had one and the game absolutely feels like it needs one too. Navigating these maps and looking for secrets seems to be quite complex actually and level design could even be a strong point here... if the game had a map. 3 years of early access and these hacks couldn't be bothered to implement a map for the full game.- Sometimes Graven thinks that it's Dark Souls so you have a stamina meter but a stamina meter absolutely doesn't fit the gameplay because in its essence this is just a retro shooter. In a retro shooter you obviously want to move fast and attack a lot but Graven doesn't let you do that because EVERYTHING exhausts your stamina. Running, attacking, jumping all needs stamina just like in Dark Souls so have fun listening to the "out of breath" sound effect and having to wait a few seconds before being able to perform a jump in a game that obviously has its fair share of jumping and jumping puzzles.- For some reason Graven also thinks that it's Resident Evil 4 sometimes so you have some inventory management to deal with here. In fact some weapons take up multiple slots in your item bar which means that you won't be able to bind every weapon to their respective hotkeys and in practice you can only cycle between 3 to 4 weapons at any given time. Yep, that makes this a retro shooter with a weapon selection limit. I guess Graven like to think of itself as Halo too sometimes.- This relates to the previous point but hotkeys obviously suck here. For example you get a very weak and useless kick that is bound to Q by default but whenever you want to use a healing potion you have to switch to it as if it was a weapon and "shoot" to consume it. I guess binding the potion to Q and just letting you use it instantly would have made too much sense, a weak kick that isn't even useful for quickly breaking boxes deserved its own hotkey though.- Magic sucks against enemies, like you get spells that sound very obviously powerful like burning or electrocuting enemies but once you actually try those things you end up doing next to no damage. Apparently you can upgrade the spells for a fortune later in the game but I never got that far so that feels irrelevant for at least the first few hours.Overall Graven is essentially a time waster, like the entire purpose of the game design seems to be to take a retro shooter and then ruin it by complicating mechanics that have been working perfectly fine since Doom 1. You want to run? Nope, here's a stamina bar. You need a map? Lol real chads don't need a map, get lost literally! You want to switch between weapons? Nope, here's an inventory system. You want to save your progress? Haha, go back to the town square, you loser. This is so bad that I'm just curious how products like this get made mostly because well, a lot of these issues seem to be avoidable or fixable with next to no work. Like sure, making a map would take some actual effort but implementing stamina was even a waste of work hours here, just not doing that would have improved the game's movement tremendously.Oh and of course it's a Slipgate game so it can run like absolute arse, it's full of UE4 microstuttering, the enemies are badly designed so a lot of them don't telegraph their attacks and overall the gameplay is really-really boring. But hey, at least you can pet the dog YOU PRETENTIOUS HACKS.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven, something of a spiritual successor to the Heretic/Hexen series from Raven Software, is a flawed, but nonetheless enjoyable, title. I found that there’s a lot to love about this game, but it definitely leaves some things to be desired as well. I’ll preface this by saying I played with a mouse and keyboard. Also, I did not try multiplayer. Anyway, let’s start with the flaws. - Perhaps the most disappointing thing about Graven are the bugs that remain in the game. I was able to play through the entire game without too much trouble. I had only one crash in the roughly 20 hours it took me to play through the whole narrative. However, the whole thing feels sort of held together with masking tape and I found myself making do in spots where I shouldn’t have had to. For example, I would clear out a certain alcove of enemies only to have a new enemy spawn very soon after. In another instance, the animation for one of the enemies is entirely bugged (though it’s almost scarier watching it come after you without the animations). - I’ve never seen a save system like this in a game, and I doubt I ever will again. Saving does not work as you might expect. Each of the three levels of the game has a number of quests to complete: the main quest along with some side quests. The levels change, with short-cuts opened or puzzles solved, as the player progresses. No matter where you were when you saved the game, when you reload your save, you will spawn in town. This can be frustrating in a couple of ways. Having to backtrack to where you were before isn’t great. Also, you might have to redo some stuff. Related to the above point about bugs, you may find that the level isn’t exactly accommodating to you coming back through an area a second time. For example, there was a trap that I had to momentarily deactivate to get past. When I returned to that spot after reloading my save, the trap was reactivated, and, despite knowing how to handle it, it took more convincing than I would have liked to allow me to pass again.  - The story in the game is fairly weak. You’re given a motivation for your quest, but how it plays out is not very cohesive and the connections between the levels is extremely tenuous, at best. I didn’t find myself to be very invested in the plot. - Is this even a thing? Graven was released to EA a couple of years ago and I picked it up at that time, following its development relatively closely and even reporting bugs when I found them to their Discord. It feels like a lot more time was dedicated to the first level than the other two, and this was sort of reflected in the time I spent in those levels. Roughly half of my 20 hours were in the first level. I didn’t keep track of how long I spent in each of the other two levels, but it felt like I spent the least amount of time in the third level.  - The game looks great. Textures are detailed and beautiful while nailing the look from early 3D games of the late ‘90s. Animations for the player and enemies are smooth, for the most part (except for that one enemy mentioned above). Enemies are easily recognizable, even at a distance. - The sound is very good, as well. I think the soundtrack is appropriate with some good atmospheric tunes. I can’t think of anything to complain about regarding the sound effects. The weapons sound good, hitting with an appropriate amount of oomph. The enemies have recognizable sounds, so, even if you can’t see them, you’ll have a pretty good idea of what’s seen you. I did run into a couple of bugs where sounds wouldn’t travel clearly through doorways. It didn’t happen often, but sometimes sounds from the other side of an open doorway would sound muffled. - I found combat to be enjoyable, for the most part. While I can’t be certain it applies to every enemy in the game, many of them were put down easier by certain weapons than others. For example, a run-of-the-mill plague zombie was easily dispatched by a thwack from my staff straight to the dome. Also, when upgraded, I would set skeletons (and other enemies) ablaze with my fire spell and watch them run about for a few seconds before exploding.  - Each weapon and spell has a couple of upgrades that you can purchase with the gold you collect. Usually, in the case of weapons, the first upgrade will introduce an alternate fire mode, and the second will further increase its killing potential. Spells can also be upgraded, but they are more expensive and require a special item to do so. - Related to combat is the inventory and your equipment bar. While you do get a number of weapons throughout the game, you’re limited to how many you can equip at once. You can swap out weapons at any time, but you’ll need to open the inventory and then drag and drop your weapon down onto the bar at the bottom of the screen. Your staff and spellbook always take up two slots, and you’ll likely want your healing potions at hand, as well, so you’re kind of limited to only having two or three other weapons at the ready. - Hub 1 introduces you to two spells, with a third appearing in hub 2. Unlike in most games, the spells in Graven do not do damage to enemies, at least initially. They are used for puzzles, dealing with explosive gas/crates, and hindering enemies. As you upgrade them, they become more useful in combat.  - Graven does not hold your hand. You might complete a quest and it’s not readily apparent what the benefit was. You might flip a switch and won’t be able to see exactly what that switch did immediately. Despite being there in EA, there is no map in the game, so it can be easy to get lost if you’re not paying attention. I don’t think any of this is a bad thing, but some might. So, yeah. I listed a lot of stuff and gave my thoughts on it. I enjoyed Graven and would recommend it. That said, it’s probably not for everyone. If you’re not willing to be patient and a little bit forgiving, then you might want to pass on it or wait for some patches to, hopefully, iron out some of the more glaring issues.

_childDocuments_.review: As you can probably see from the other reviews, this game has some divisive opinions. The things that are done good are well appreciated (GFX, Music, atmosphere); the things that are lacking though are what bring the game down.In saying that, I still thinks it's a good game, but it does have some strong flaws that may turn people off.The GOOD:* music, atmosphere, GFX - all of this that creates the world (especially Act 1) create a great experience* there is a satisfaction to knocking enemies across the field with a critical hit (white crystal staff)* it is not Hexen reborn, but it does have some similarities in that it hubs levels and doesn't hold your hand in explorationThe BAD(yes, there are bugs but the complaints I have, I feel they are in the game for good and will not change)* STAMINA - this game does not need it and would benefit in terms of flow without it - you lose jump height and swing time and they break the momentum when you need to either hide or "jog" away until you get some recovery* WEAPON BALANCE - I'm not a stickler for weapon balance but you start to lean into your favourites once you find them and I don't believe inventing "combat loops" will resolve this; there's just some duplication in their nature that make some redundant.* WEAPON HOLD LIMITATION - a bug-bear of mine, i haaaaaate weapoin limitation, just let me hold all of the weapons at once, I like that I can sort them in different order BUT let me hold them all; I may then be inspired to try them all to understand them betterOtherwise I enjoyed it, I'm still on the Retro FPS bandwagon and love that new stuff keeps coming out. :DHexen 3 please....

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to love...even though it took a pretty good stab at being a modern day Hexen, but I am enjoying it. Unfortunately, it is still buggy even after the 1.0 full release and a couple of updates.  I have had to restart twice due to my inventory disappearing...this was made worse by the game having only one save and a terrible checkpoint/hub save system.  This is *not* a retro shooter, this is a thinking mans game but some of the puzzles are very obtuse and honestly make little sense. It's also very difficult, which I think is p1ssing a lot of the reviewers off.  There's no Map (!!) and  even trash mobs will wreck you.  It is not for everyone.   I also think it has been abandoned and doubt there will be another patch, which is unfortunate but I'm going to try and finish it as is. Your tolerance for bugs, hardcore game play and having no map (with the levels being very large) will determine how much you enjoy Graven.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven desperately needs some quality-of-life features. The ill-conceived stamina and save systems, which drew ire from the first demo way back 2020, remain unaddressed after three years in early access. Having no means of fast travelling means when you return after a play session, you'll find yourself back in the hub and way to spend minutes journeying back despite pop-ups constantly telling the player you've reached a checkpoint, which should include an asterisk beside it because it doesn't function like 99% of other games and no justification is offered as to why.Additionally, there's a slew of other issues that diminished my enjoyment. I don't understand why you don't have access to all your weapons at once. You can, after all, just pause and switch at any time, so why limit the hotbar but allow this fiddly, tedious method?Despite promising art direction, the visual presentation on the whole is inconsistent: some of the enemies are nicely key-framed with satisfying tells that lead-in to their attacks; others move like they're auditioning for Looney Tunes, jerkily rushing towards you with no sense of weight or presence. Combat sounds alternate between satisfying booms and wimpy, even silent, encounters. The number of times when you get hit from behind with no chance of knowing because there's no indication whatsoever, not even even a squeak, exacerbates the feeling of the game being rushed out the door long before it was ready.I love complex levels that offer a sense of discovery. Despite Graven's hubs being, at times, intricate, that's not what's offered here. Without a map, a compass or clear markers that differentiate one space from another, either thematically or in terms of geometry, navigating these rambling, repeating layouts is frequently unpleasant. The frequently broken scripting ensures that missing an essential trigger on the critical path through no fault of your own is all-but-guaranteed. I encountered three hard crashes and had to restart the campaign once to bypass a progress blocker. The game defaults to a black screen whenever I tried to play in 1440p regardless of whether it's set to fullscreen or windowed mode. The only solution I found was to play in windowed mode in 1080p. I hope you fare better!Please note: I played Graven on another platform but purchased here to see if my issues were related to the platform.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the graphics, love the atmosphere, love the setting, love the music, love the voice acting, love the audio design, love the level design, love the weapons, love the enemies, love the exploration. So much to love in this game. It just makes me sad and angry that the game manages to ruin all of the good parts with the way they handle saves/checkpoints, not having a map, bugs all around the place. Acts 2 and 3 are clearly rushed and have super inconsistent enemy placements and loot availability and a bunch of unused areas and invisible walls. Some 'puzzles' make absolutely zero sense even when you know the solution and have all the clues. Some monsters are completely broken OP and impossible to fight without taking tons of damage. Looking at you act 2 sonic the hedgehog zombies and act 2 boss. It would also be nice if you warned the player that they are about to lock themselves out from previous acts when defeating bosses. And worse of all, getting out of water and using ladders is absolutely horrendous.

_childDocuments_.review: This game (More like a demo), it didn't hype me up at all... Where to even start... There's not enough content it's about two hours long even when taking your sweet time to find all the secrets. And it's not like there's a reason to find all the stuff cause the moment you find the first weapon (other than your basic staff) the game is now on easy mode. Just circle and hit. Except for minor barely even puzzle the spells do nothing (I'm not even sure there's more than one right now) and if you have a ranged enemy there's no reason to even use anything else than the basic crossbow.I'm unsure if the game is meant to be non-linear when it comes out of early access but right now, it's straighforward with shortcuts that are totally useless. It's like someone saw the shortcut from the church to firelink shrine in Dark Souls and went: ''This will suffice as good level design. Now they can go back to the start of the game to gear up.'' But there's no reason to buy anything because odds are you'll have bought everything there is in the first 20 min. And when there is a little exploring to be had, it's unrewarding. The one puzzle the game has managed to get me stuck. The puzzle is not hard, mind you. I just managed to miss a clue. That is nowhere near the thing that I need to solve. And speaking of games that are better than this. That kick button, it's another moment where the devs saw something that player loved in Dark Messiah, but didn't understand why it was fun. In this game, it does nothing. There's no trap to kick monsters in. I understand the lack of content and that maybe a lot of this will be fixed, that the combat will be more interesting or that there will be reason to explores latter on. But this was an opportunity to wow us, to get us more invested but right now, I just don't get why you would release this in that state except to make money right here and now...

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't hate this game, nor did I like it much either. Waited for it for a long time with much anticipation and the final result is somewhat disappointing. I did not buy it in early access either and chose to wait for the full release. We are several months into release now and game breaking bugs still exist so that is the first and main issue I have with it. I don't know if the devs plan to release future patches or notGameplay is janky in general with some very frustrating design choices that ruin the fun such as making you lose money every time you die. If you fall into a pit, you're never retrieving that again. There are more examples too but won't list them all. It certainly has very good level design going for it, the first Cruxfirth hub looks superb and the snowy castle hub is a cool place to be as I love me a frozen, snowy level in my games.I can't really recommend it, I feel like other players will have the same frustrating time I did. _childDocuments_.review: I bought Graven when it initially released, and had a great time with it. I think the majority of the negative reviews for this game fall under either the lack of content, or bugs and glitches. The game hasn't received any new content since launch, however a new update is expected in the very very near future. I think, personally, Graven has a lot of potential, and while a lot of it goes unrecognised, I am confident that this will be rectified in further updates and releases. The base of the game is solid, with beautiful graphics, wonderful sound design, and a great set of base features. Combat is fun, and exploration is a joy. However there are still issues, such as enemy AI, and once again, the lack of content, but that will be fixed in due time. TLDR; Game is good despite lack of content and few issues, but wait until they update it more before diving in to it.

_childDocuments_.review: The bad reviews for this game come mostly from people who bought into the EA lies and expected this to be the second coming of christ. It is not, so people are mad. To me however, who got this game after release expecting nothing I was very much entertained for the almost 20 hours it took me to complete it. It's not a straight up boomer shooter, it has inventory management, puzzles and hub towns, more like an immersive sim.So if you're looking for something like that with a gorgeous retro artstyle, give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Heretic and Hexen games, I like Graven overall, but it has some glaring issues that hold it back from greatness. This game definitely needed more time in the oven.The Good:-The art design is excellent, makes for an excellent first impression-Stephan Weyte is always a plus-Some of the weapons feel great, like the flail, ballista and peat burnerThe Bad:-Easily the worst aspect of this game is the stamina system, which kills the game's momentum especially when you're traversing these large areas trying to get to the next objective. If you really wanted such a system in the game, tweak it so that it resembles the Souls series' stamina bar that refills rather quickly.-Physics for chest loot and gold dropped from death are insane. A lot of the time the loot is flung so hard it either falls into a pit or gets stuck in walls at unreachable heights-AI is really weak. Sometimes enemies just aren't interested in pursuing you through a doorway or they run away entirely after being hit a couple of times (not counting the headless skeletons)-Ladders are a bit jank. You shouldn't be able to stick to and climb them from both sides-A good number of bugs, including, but not limited to, hard crashes that make me lose some progress, chest items falling through the world upon opening it, infinitely respawning enemies right at my position, and breakable items phasing through elevators-A number of weapons feel redundant; spells are basically useless in combat, knotted stave feels a bit clunky to use etc.Some of these issues can be remedied with patches, but others require tweaking the game's mechanics. I'm sure once they are resolved this game will be in much better shape. I enjoyed my time with the game, even though some of the combat encounters felt frustrating at times. However, it is not something I would recommend to fans of this kind of game, especially in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: The game becomes less fun the longer you play. It started out ok with gameplay and story but there are some big annoyances with the game. The first is when you save and quit you get dumped back into town and not get put at the last checkpoint you activated. This mean if you want a quick way to town save and quit its nice but for short play sessions it becomes tedious with backtracking through respawned enemies. With the large amount of shortcuts and alternate paths you open up as you go, you can end up wandering in circles trying to find that exact spot where you left off. The removal of a map system was a stupid move by the devs.While no hand holding is fine there are things the game should tell you. You can jump-duck onto low ledges that you can't normally jump on to. This would have been very useful to know and would have made getting around a little easier. Also to get out of water without a ramp sprint upwards and it effectively jumps you out of the water. Even with knowing these I still got stuck several times and had to save/quit and renter the game.I got stuck progress wise and run in circles backtracking trying to find what I had missed or where to go next and thats not fun at all. I never knew I had to break a window and walk around outside the library or other times I missed a wall colored lever or ones hiding between a desk with chair and a wall. Act 1 was maze like but the enemies were all fair for health and damage, the final boss of the chapter was a pushover. Act 2 suddenly enemies are spongy and hit for half your health. It feels like they just increased difficulty too much too fast that I worry what act 3 will be like with type of increase.A very confusing design choice that I find was pointless is that weapons can take up more than one slot of your hotbar. A thing designed for quick access to your weapons and potions gets bogged down with inventory/hotbar management. I have seen weapons take from 1 to 3 slots and makes zero sense. I have more weapons than can fit on the hotbar this is not something old retro games had an issue with.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up in the golden age of PC gaming, Graven is a love letter to one of my fav FPS/RPG hybrids of all time - Hexen 2. I've gone through the EA build twice now and loved every moment of it. The atmosphere, the world building, the combat, the graphics - everything is what I've been looking for in a retro PC FPS/RPG. I am very much looking forward to the finished game, whenever that may be.Some feedback for the devs:- save system needs improvement. I love the hardcore element of no free saves rather checkpoints, but the incredible frustration of saving and quitting to come back to needing to redo the entire whole area (case in point - my first playthrough I quit out as soon as I picked up the skull key. When I picked the game back up the next day, I literally had to redo the entire Clotted Avenues map from the start, just to find that literally the skull key is the end of the EA pretty much. Frustrating. I am the type of player who sticks his nose in every nook and cranny - there is no need for me to redo an area I have already exhaustively explored. Additionally, we're all adults here - I don't want to reinvest/have the time for something your save system should have captured). I see this is something the dev team is addressing in their next update, so kudos.- The spells are underwhelming. Again, I see this is potentially being addressed but I was hoping that spells would be more combat-focused rather than utility-focused. Why have fire and lightning at my disposal if all I can do is light a match with my flame and electrify some water? Let's get some combat fireballs and Sith-level shock spells into the mix :)- The weapons are awesome - that short sword could carry me through the game and I love the look! Peat launcher and scrap gun and wrist blades are also very cool. Love the staff and the spellbook is badass. - Game is 10/10. You guys nailed pretty much everything but the few concerns noted above. Highly recommend to anyone to pick up - you will not be sorry. Quality game with a team that knows their work. I reiterate - I cannot wait for the finished game!!! Kudos devs for making quality experiences like this for the fans - I will happily throw my money your way anytime for games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: So far this is shaping up to be a really good retro shooter that is setting itself apart from all the others in the boomer shooter revival crowd. The level design so far is great with sprawling interconnected levels that go from tight spaces to open areas and I feel it pushes you to explore the combat options at your disposal.I think some tweaks to the progression system are needed as I feel the unlocks (particularly for spells) take a while but I can give this a pass given that it's EA. I do feel the checkpoint system needs a bit of revision in places, there is one area in particular that you can get yourself into a respawn and get killed over again scenario a little too easily. All in all though I think this is shaping up to be a great game and I am excited to see the full release. I will update my review once 1.0 is released but wanted to give it a thumbs up as I feel this has come a long way since it's initial EA release and deserves to be on peoples radars.

_childDocuments_.review: I... I want to like this game. I really do. It reminds me a lot of Hexen and Heretic, which are games that we DEFINITELY need more of. Hell, we need more first person hack and slash medieval games, period. But I can't recommend it now. There's no content, simple as that. It's basically that demo they've released a while back. You've got only 5 weapons and 1 spell. And 4 missions. But that's it. The setting looks amazing, the atmosphere is great... But the game itself... No. Not worth the price now. Wait until more content is released, because this is WAAAAY too bare-bones.And they say they'll be releasing a greater chunk of the game until the first half of 2022. Honestly, I kinda doubt it. It just feels... Bare. So bare. So, please, don't do as I did and don't buy it now.As the game gets more content, I'll probably change this review. But if it follows WRATH's development path... Well, this review will remain as is for a looooong time, I feel.

_childDocuments_.review: Hexen 2's estranged cousin. The element interactions are largely superfluous and the encounter design is on the weaker end, fully running out of ideas by act 3. It's still a pretty good time. I liked the slightly more aggressive than usual puzzles and the vast but not difficult to navigate levels. Enemy types require some thought to efficiently best which is good but with some upgrades a select few weapons shine so far above the rest in doing so that you'll be playing with a rather simple rotation towards the second half (consequently making it truly a lot more like Hexen 2). I personally found this a nice change of pace as it meant the speed of the game increased a lot over time until you really blaze through the last few areas. I recommend you play on Ordained until you feel confident even if you have solid experience from other shooters.It is missing setpiece, it is missing enemy roster synergy. These are not elements that can be patched in later, so "pretty good" is likely the final potential of the game. There's some bugs and more pertinent issues as well of course, but in due time these can be ironed out so I don't care, I got by just fine. As far as a "retro shooter" goes, it's ultimately middle of the road. Not by means of blandness, but by leaning in opposing directions. The air of a compromised vision, perhaps. Still a worthy entry.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere is great. It has a very gritty look and feel which I think is one of its strongest points. It's got a medieval fantasy setting which works pretty well. It's what drew me to the game in the first place. Level design is ok. Areas can look a bit samey. I found myself getting lost a lot. I think if they improved the map screen it would help, and also use less of the same texture everywhere. The levels are also huge and you have to backtrack a lot. I got bored way before the level was near finishing, but you can't quicksave. If you quit you have to start the level again. I made that mistake once. Quest design is terrible, it's basically just a key hunt. Door locked, find key. Unlock door, reach another locked door, find key, repeat. Honestly the worst thing for me is the combat. The enemy AI is completely braindead, and circle strafing defeats every enemy currently in early access. The basic zombie enemy has a lunge attack, the giant lizard thing has a lunge attack, the armoured zombies have a lunge attack. You get the idea. Circle strafe === win. ZzzzIt's somehow positioned itself as the spiritual successor to Hexen without capturing what makes combat in the Doom engine so satisfying. Movement is so slow and there is a stamina mechanic that slows you down further. Slow, boring, don't buy.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: Looks really good, sounds good, level design is really really enjoyable, circle strafing is mind numbing, and combining it with proper weapons makes the game extremely easy, but at least not as boring as smacking everything with wooden staff. Checkpoint system is trash, respawning in town everytime you quit the game is very questionable. But the atmosphere and exploration is so good that i don't really mind. Also i have to warn you that this is NOT an immersive sim, it's straigt up boomer shooter just with a slower pacing and a little more exploration. No stealth, no multiple paths, no different solutions to problems. You just smack or shoot enemies, find keys, open shortcuts and progress.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit, I was reluctant to buy because of "mixed" reviews on steam. And they were absolutely unjustified. The game is an amazing balance between a nostalgic gameplay of the oldies, and the technical quality of new games.The atmosphere if the game is briliant, and the world is very well developed for Early Access game. There's heaps of lore to find, and slowly you get more and more acustomed to the world. The fighting system is definitely not "just swing it" as some people described. You have to pick proper weapon for situation, you have to aim and time your strikes. There are distance weapons, two melee ones, some magic to help. I know people used to having 40 guns in their backpack might feel like taht's not much, but the game is in Early Access, so I'm certain more stuff will be added. Overall I really like the game, and I can safely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Attention: I do NOT recommend this game to 100% YET. It's a mixed bag.The concept, the art style, the atmosphere of the game world, wonderful stuff. And there is definitely fun to be had with the game, exploration is rewarding, combat is decent.BUT: Early Access is a painfully slow process here, there was almost an entire year of dead silence before the first substantial content update dropped out of nowhere. People already believed the game to be abandoned, and I am happy to see progress. Because GRAVEN is really promising, unique and beautifully melancholic. It's quite a trippy experience, honestly. And I kinda love it.But in its current form, after content update #1 and during Early Access, it definitely still needs work. It needs more content and refinement. Especially a certain boss enemy in a later part of the game is very frustrating and needs an overhaul. One of the puzzles is too difficult for non native English folks, as it relies on fancy english words. And you can feel that the game systems are not fully fleshed out and polished yet.So, I highly recommend putting it on your wishlist for now. And when it comes out of Early Access and doesn't somehow get terribly, terribly screwed up in the meantime, I fully recommend it. Right now? Only purchase it, if you could accept the price tag for an unfinished (but promising) game that might be many, many months away from a full release with a lot of silence from the devs until then.

_childDocuments_.review: My original impressions write-up was more or less back in 2012/22 during the early access build, since then I have been playing the console and PC versions post-launch - I stand by my original recommendation.So what it is Graven, now that the game has been officially launched?A "Boomer Shooter" it is NOT.  In fact, comparing this game to what inspired it I fear does little justice in describing the game as well.  Whilst Graven is uses both perspective and movement from your typical FPS games, you're barely scratching the surface.  If you were expecting Heretic/Hexen, don't.  Graven has more in common with the likes of Ultima Underworld and System Shock than any of that games made with IdTech (Doom, Heretic, Hexen, Strife, etc.).  Like those games, everything (weapons included) serves a utilitarian purpose as even combat encounters are puzzles - If you seen an object you can pick up (whether weapon, tool consumable placed into your inventory or one that can be placed / thrown), you can use it.  In fact, the first quest will demonstrate my point that all objects serve as potential components to puzzle solutions.  Graven uses objects (inventory items and those in the world) very similarly to how Point'n'Click adventure games (eg. Sierra and Lucas Arts adventure games of the 1980s/90s) use objects when solving puzzles.  In fact there are puzzles that are solved simply by interacting with them.  Graven is a game that leans toward having more in common with the classic first person dungeon crawlers than any shooter.As the story and setting of Graven - You play a condemned priest in-exile whom arrives on ferry to town in the middle of a swap hit stricken by plague and encounters a cult whilst seeking absolution.  The setting is strikingly similar to games from The Serpent Rider trilogy (Heretic, Hexen and Hexen II) and the Diablo franchise.  Then there's navigation...  This will be especially irksome who are used to the creature comforts "Modern" games offer.  There is NO map.  You find your way around through careful observation of both your surroundings and journal entries as well as performing some detective work when the directions given are too vague to follow.  Graven straight up warns you when starting a new game, the game has a good chunk of  "Light Reading".  The games storytelling and world building are conveyed through both the notes and world design.Whilst Graven is largely a single player experience, there is the ability to engage in cooperative multiplayer - More minds, the merrier.  Graven from a technical standpoint runs solid across all platforms. Though, binding keyboard and mouse is a far easier time than trying to map a controller to your liking - For console players especially, I recommend control scheme "B" for anyone who prefers to keep their thumbs on the analogue sticks.If you enjoy dark fantasy CRPGs and Point 'n' Click adventure games with a gothic horror vibe, Graven should be right up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: having just finished this game's early access offering, i'm gonna recommend holding off on it. tl;dr this makes the "demo" they briefly released somewhat recently feel less like a demo and more like a "here's what we've gotten done so far."the early access portion is very short, about two hours long. only one map more than the "demo" that was put out then taken away (it's a big map, but it contains a very bad puzzle). the description says there are two spells, but i only ever found one despite feeling like i searched pretty thoroughly. the game consistently dropped blue mana i never got to use, and the fire spell was nearly useless in combat.they made the bizarre choice to, in addition to having resident evil-style inventory slots, also apply that to your  keys. the sword takes up two slots of your quickbar, and the shotgun-crossbow and rocket launcher take up three.  this means that, while you can hold all your equipment in your inventory just fine, you have to pick and choose what you want to have immediate access to. i ended up unequipping my health potions so i could have enough weapons equipped to overcome not having much ammo capacity. you can't unequip your staff or spell book despite both being rendered pretty much useless by an hour in.despite this acting kinda like a dark messiah, there is no reason to ever kick anything. you can kick anything, but it doesnt stun enemies and there are no environmental traps or spikes or whatever to kick them into. there are red  explody barrels that line the walls of most rooms, but you can't throw them around and kicking them causes them to explodealso it would be nice if you could make your character a woman. i dont need character creation, but the "PRAEST" is basically a blank slate and there's no reason why it couldn't be a woman.games are hard to make, and based on the demo and this offering i don't see how they're going to fulfill their plan of having the whole game done _childDocuments_.review: It has immense potential but its just not there yet. Maybe the full version will fix it. For the time being, it deserves the mixed rating because the game is a mixed bag. Very pretty graphics, performance that should be better, but tolerable, really good atmosphere, good level design, but severe negatives. Overall, the only reason i gave it a yes is because ultimately i enjoyed it, even if it needs work more than content.The staff is hard to use because it either hits top right of the crosshair or bottom left. 50/50 which place it hits and you can only instakill zombies if you put the location on their head. if you put the top right of the crosshair on their head and the staff hits bottom left of the crosshair, sucks to be you, you either missed or did a body hit, which takes 3 to kill a single zombie. More if the zombie 'stinks'Same for the sword except no instantkills. The upgrades for it seem cool on paper but amount to nothing because rolling chances to see if the staff hits them in the head or not still kills them faster than just hacking at them with a fully upgraded sword. It has a parry mechanic aswell but i have no idea how it works because its feedback is bad, and i keep taking damage. Jumping out of the water is completely impossible. In the final boss' arena the water will slow you down even if you're standing on a plank above said water. During a bossfight, this isnt exactly fun or fair. The starting spell you get is essentially a magical lighter. Deals next to no damage and only sets enemies on fire, and on top of that, the starting enemies, the zombies, resist the fire too. its range is about 3 meters but figuring that out is impossible based on the animation. The only way you'll know how far it can reach is by manually testing distances against a wall, or having someone tell you. Its feedback on its range is awful. Second spell, the lightning, stuns enemies for a short moment but its only like 2 seconds so you can't use it for much. It also deals next to no damage and a full mana bar wont kill a single enemy. Does it even do any damage?The stinky zombies have significantly increased armor and immunity to headbashes. Killing them is a slog before you get good weapons.The cuff crossbow works well enough but it takes like 2 hours of unpleasant and clunky combat to get to it, and while its decent it feels underwhelming with its sound effectsWhen you are low on stamina, your jump height is decreased by like 80%, which means you essentially cant jump. _childDocuments_.review: This game is at present, not fit to be sold in my opinion. Early Access is a contract between the developer, and the player. A recognition that the game will be either light on content, or light on polish, but is not SUPPOSED to be light on both. The games that stray from this unwritten and unspoken rule are the ones that tend to flounder for years in early access, and I am sad to say that Graven is exactly such a game at the moment.Common Criticisms-Save System is bad : The save system isnt bad, or it would not be, if not for the MANY game-breaking bugs currently present in the game. The odds of you having to start over before reaching the end of the EA content (1-4 hours) is about 50/50, which is are abysmal odds by just about any measure.- Game is short : This is one of those "your mileage may vary" sort of complaints I generally take with a grain of salt, but trust me when I say you will get AT MOST 4 hours out of this build of the game, only if you search every nook and cranny. A practice which at this stage, the game really does not reward. More likely it will take you somewhere ~2.5 hours to complete.Personal Critiques- Do not go into this expecting another boomer shooter like wrath, prodeus, dusk, etc. The shooting in the game is, at the moment, VERY limp and unsatisfying. The weapons are meant to get more satisfying as you unlock more variants, but at present, those variants are not in the game for the most part.- Optimization : This game is running in UE4, so if you are using a mid range or low range laptop, and assuming you can run the game because the graphics are similar to quake 2, think again. You will almost certainly not be able to run the game at a stable framerate, which hurts an already hobbled and undercooked combat system.ConclusionThis game has a really interesting art style, and a very unique look, but it does not compensate for the lack of any kind of stability, satisfying gameplay, or extremely poor optimization. If you buy this game, you are buying into the promise it holds in the future. Maybe that is worth it to you, but if you are looking for any kind of enjoyable experience in the here and now, stay away. Come back in 8-10 months, or maybe even longer.Edit: It is now more than 6 months on since the time of my review, and the game has yet to receive a single update. Literally, not one. 10 months out from release, and the paid version of the game still has less content than the demo did. This game is dead, or on ice. Either way, please do not spend your money on it.Edit 2: The game is back on an active development schedule.Edit 3: The game is back OFF an  active development schedule.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real hidden gem. I'm not gonna sugarcoat it though, Graven is definitely not for everyone. It is quite rough around the edges and severely in need of a map and better fast travel system. But DAMN, is this a good crossover of a metroidvania, rpg and boomer shooter. Gives me some serious Dark Messiah of Might and Magic nostalgia vibes, even more so as it allows you to stack boxes and sequence break some parts with a bit of finesse. Oh, and the mighty kick, while at first not quite as powerful as dark messiah's, can easily fling enemies into the shadow realm after you get a specific gem for your staff, which can be acquired fairly early on. While not as open-ended regarding combat options as Dark Messiah, Graven does let you do some im-sim shenanigans with enemies, which are an actual rarity nowadays, such as kicking them into traps, tossing them down chasms and leading them into explosive barrels.This game has some of the most satisfying old school Hexen-inspired melee combat I've experienced in ages. The maps are vast and filled with secrets and it has some truly inspired architecture and art direction, featuring quite good environmental story telling. There is some good enemy variety and the weapons and spells I've unlocked so far are sufficiently varied and satisfying to use. The spells are a bit underpowered at their base state though, but offer good utility to burn through shields and zap enemies into a stun state and solve environmental puzzles. Not a fan of the major self damage you get if you cast the zap spell in water though, as areas with water are where the spell is actually most effective versus enemies.HOWEVER, while this game can impecably channel what made games like heretic, hexen and hexen 2 so great, it also falls into some of their pitfalls. Particularly, the convoluted and sometimes obtuse level design of hexen 2 in which finding the way forward or where to use a newly acquired key item can be a frustrating chore. And because Graven has enemy respawns upon revisiting a cleared area, checking that one door you vaguely remember from 1h ago can easily turn into a wild goose chase where you end up clearing an entire area again just to find the damn door. And then you find out the item is actually for another door...I'm not a big fan of extreme handholding of many modern games that give you an arrow pointing exactly where to go at all times and have yellow paint on every interactable part of the map, but Graven steers way too far into the other direction, with vague objectives and item descriptions and frequent criptic clues for puzzles. If only the game gave you any sort of map, much of this frustration would be alleviated. And fast travel would be much appreciated. In the game's defense, you can frequently unlock shortcuts to alleviate backtracking and going to town to spend your gold, but for how crucial these are, some are far too well hidden and require you to maintain a clear mental map of the area you're in to take advantage of them.Finally, the stamina system feels like a poorly thought out and unnecessary addition in a game with massive maps that you will want to be running in 90% of the time. Also, the weapons taking up multiple quickslots when you can pause the game at any time to switch out your equipped gear is such a bad idea that adds nothing to the game other than wasting players' time... Fortunantely, there are two mods that fix these issues on Nexus mods which I HIGHLY recommend to anyone who wishes to play game and have a good time.All in all, despite its many shortcomings, I've very much enjoyed my time with Graven so far and I can safely say there is nothing quite like this on the market that I'm aware of. Hope acts 2 and 3 won't disappoint.PS: The game is a little finnicky and I've read it has a few possible softlocks, so make sure to back up your save files every now and then.EDIT: Wow, I think the game has wiped my inventory about 8 times by now. Most frequently after I got stuck in some geometry and quit to menu. You ABSOLUTELY MUST keep regular backups of your saves. THIS GAME IS VERY BUGGY, so BE WARNED! Still great otherwise, but man is this annoyingSave data is located in the folder C:\Users\*YourUsername*\AppData\Local\Praest\Saved

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Graven, even though there's only four hours of content max at the moment. The interwoven level design is fantastic, and the secrets rarely devolve into corner-checking  The retro styling really serves the atmosphere, rather than just being a gimmick. The one major puzzle had me get out pen and paper to solve it, which had me awash in nostalgia.That said, I'm not sure there's $25 worth of game here yet, and I can easily imagine people being disappointed with it as it stands. The combat is fun but way too easy--every enemy in the game can be one-shotted by a weapon you can buy very early. Also I'd guess 15% of my playtime was spent destroying crates, which is an annoying way to keep the player completely flush in health, mana, and ammo (Not sure if blue magic is in game yet--I never found the spell.) And the pillar puzzle is fun and challenging, but that's really the only puzzle in the game so far.I had a ton of fun with Graven, and it feels petty to complain an early access game doesn't have enough content yet. So I recommend it. But you wouldn't be harmed by waiting till there's more here.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried, I really did, but it's not good.  A lot of the problems I have with the game are very fixable, but I dont know if the devs are willing to go to such lengths.   - There is zero map, making getting lost a very regular occurrence.  - There is very little direction in the game, so again, getting lost and just mindlessly throwing yourself around to see if something new is found is also a regular occurrence. I dont need my handheld but having literally all of the direction be done in a journal that regularly overwrites its own notes on your goals and is often poor at telling what it wants you to do? No, I need a bit more than that.  - Melee enemies hit very hard and dodging their attacks often feels like RNG. Sometimes you can circle strafe around enemies and they'll miss you, other times they'll do an instant 180 degree turn and launch themselves at you with no warning.  - Weapon balance is terrible. The sword does barely more damage than the staff but cant seem to headshot enemies, so the staff is literally always better and takes up only 1 slot. Wrist crossbow does about as much damage as the staff does, despite being wildly inaccurate and having limited ammo. I could go on honestly, the weapon and enemy balance is a total mess. It also doesnt help that there is almost zero hit feedback on weapons and no stagger so melee just sucks in general, you'll get hit if you try most of the time.  - Level design, I dont know why the devs decided to make everything in an area look the same AND have no map. It's so painfully easy to look at a new area and think "have I been here before? I cant tell"  - Finally(though not the only thing remaining, I just cant be bothered writing more) enemies respawn incredibly fast, you can kill every enemy in a room, walk into the next room and back up into the previous room while kiting enemies and the enemies you JUST killed are all alive again. It's absurd how often this happens.

_childDocuments_.review: 2 of my absolute favorite games in the entire world are Heretic and Hexen. For so long, even throughout most of EA, this game looked and felt like it would be a decent spiritual successor to those games. But for the first time(that I've experienced) a game actually didn't improve from EA to full release, but got worse. Most, if not all, of what I hoped would be fixed or improved was not. And the Dev's even took things away(Why take away the Map???), which made no sense. Its almost as if, partway through development, they felt it was too similar to Heretic/Hexen(which is kinda the point since that was the inspiration) so they tried to change direction in order to make their game "its own thing". Except it had already pulled too much inspiration from Heretic and other games like it, so they changed petty little things which only made the game worse. Then by a certain point, they'd gone too far to turn back so they just had to release the crap pile they'd shoveled together.All in all, if you can get this game dirt cheap and have never played Heretic/Hexen, you might like this. But even then, after almost 30 years Heretic and Hexen are far better games so my best recommendation is to just go play those instead of wasting your money on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a bad game, plain and simple.1. Jank. A lot of it. Shots go wherever they please. Melee hits stun or don't. Enemy hits connect or not.  It's more of a coin toss than something that is influenced by the player. Enemies get catapulted across the terrain on object collision, making them bounce around the player. Horrible2. Game can't decide what it wants to be. They have a darksouls like respawn, except when they don't. But there is also checkpoints, but they only work during one game session, closing and opening the game brings you back to the hub again. And yeah there are limited ressources, but you can buy ammo form the blacksmith, but only with gold, which is not respawning. But you can kill enemies for gold drops, but you have to do it with melee, which costs you life and the only way to heal is either by health drops or by dying. But when you die you loose gold. And there are max ammo and health pots limits.Seemingly none of the devs has ask themselves, is the gameplay loop actually fun?! Short answer - NO!3. The game used to be somewhat straight forward in EA. You found fire, you learned about what you can do with it. Then you found electricity, found out about it, yadda, yadda, yadda. However because they seemingly ran out of ideas, they thought that it would be a thing to stretch out the time until you find those upgrades. Ironically they did not change the maps accordingly, which means if you want access to blocked off areas (the staff gets the ability to break certain structures) you have to backtrack entire maps for little to no benefit. Prior to these changes in when you get the upgrades, all of this came alongside naturally exploring the hub areas. So the EA version had a better pacing than the final product.4. Enemy design. Some of the most uninteresting things I have ever seen. There are zombies, that hit or pounce. There are lizard thingies, that can hit or pounce. There are skelly bois, that can - you guessed it - hit or pounce. But wait there is more, there are skelly bois that can shoot and vampires that can shoot. Of course don't get me wrong, a basic system, that works can still be a lot of fun, but that is exactly the problem, it is janky af. And there are so many things, which you are not told about as a player. For example why are some enemies invincible? And it is not even special enemies, but just a bunch of random zombie. Why can't they be killed? Well, have fun kiting.And there we come to the final nail in the coffin. An absolutely horrible, horrible boss design. I only fought the archivist, which the devs describe as totally optional (which is a rather bad excuse for bad design), but anyways the fight itself if pretty simple: a ghost entity that materializes and dematerializes , which you can only damaged while it is in its material form, destroy the 5 heads and you're done. However because of all the jank your crossbow might hit or it doesn't for no apparent reason. If you get close for your shotgun to be used, the boss causes a screen jiggle that messes up your aim causing you to not hit the head you aimed for and as the icing on the cake, periodically the boss will casts some type of aoe spell and even if you are outside of this circle, the lightning will still hit you unless there is a solid object between you and the boss.I could go on, but I think this sums it up quite well.Edit: Continued playing, finished the swamps and killed the tree as well as the archivist and yeah game still sucks. I did not feel joy for a single minute, level design and enemies as well as their spawn and respawn are just outright annoying, if not even insulting.

_childDocuments_.review: I get that this is an Early Access game, so its going to need some polish and bug fixes. I also know the developers pushed the first content update back to release combined with the second update, I get why some users are frustrated with this. I know development takes time and things change. I don't blame the devs, it is what it is, they're making a great game. The levels have only gotten more polished and gameplay better with each update. I love the art direction and play style is great. I really enjoyed the two new areas, though the last one felt a little short. I really liked the library, definitely need more puzzles like the sliding one.I can't wait to play the whole 3 Hubs, really excited about both the "snow" and "desert" styles.The spell upgrades finally make them deal enough damage to make them worth using. I don't think there is any enemy scaling in multiplayer, I played through it with 3 people and it felt way to easy.I know multiplayer is like beta early access. The only issue i found was that other player's upgrades didn't keep when they joined, I think they got mine instead (the other two accounts had played 0% singleplayer).My only complaint is I wish there was a harder difficulty, with 2x the enemies. I think the enemies were made easier in this update. It would be awesome if at harder difficulties, the notes with the puzzle clues would differ and be harder to find, or go to one of a few locations. To be fair, I loved getting lost and frustrated with the Hexen maps, so I'd like to get lost in Graven.I definitely recommend the game if you like dark fantasy retro fps. _childDocuments_.review: From what I understood about Graven, I thought it was going to be like some kinda Hexen - a game series that I never really could get on with, but had the trappings of greatness. A blast from the past imagining of a FPS action RPG from the late 90s, with all the trappings and care of modern FPS design! So I was stoked to play it.In this case, it evoked that retro FPS feel so well, it made me feel just as bored as I did with Hexen. It takes the mission structure of something like Hexen or Hexen II and just blows it up to the size of a sprawling overworld (which is cool!), but it doesn't really improve on the level structure or add much of anything new. Actually, it kind of goes backwards - there's no map at all, which wouldn't be that big of a problem if the level design wasn't so brown and drab and unmemorable. Combat starts out kind of fun with the improvisational dance of trying to determine how to defeat the zombies, which is fun. But none of the spells or weapons feel good to fight with - landing a critical hit requires precision, and I can't do precision when I have some giant lizard rottweiler thing charging at me, giving me no opportunity to circle-strafe it and shoot it in its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.I think what finally broke me on this game was that I had died charging through some castle balustrade after finally getting somewhere. It was after I had unlocked the gate that required the castle key. I had lost a duel with the flying one-eyed lizards that shoot acid from very far away, and ended up losing a bunch of gold. I ragequit (as I do), stopped playing for a time (mainly because Balatro came out), and when I finally came back to it, I had to figure out where the ♥♥♥♥ I was supposed to go, because the game dumped me back in the town square and didn't want to remind me what the ♥♥♥♥ I was trying to do in the first place. So I ran around the game map for about an hour before I realized I had found my path back up to the castle balustrades... and then died to that same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flying lizard that shoots acid. Cool. Well, I'm going back to playing Balatro. Have a nice life or whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't you just love when a game locks you out of previous game sections so that you cannot explore them any further? Be prepared to experience this over and over again in this game. Additionally: bad hit feedback, rather repetitive weapon design, unfair deaths and progress-loss due to bugs or crashes. There sure is a nice Hexen-Clone somewhere under the hood, but it is obfuscated by all the frustrating issues this game has. If a game leaves early access, I expect some form of polish. Hopefully, the devs will fix all these issues in the long run. This can still become a great game. Currently, I can only recommend it to true Hexen-fans. Other people, keep your hands off for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Many people fail to understand what Early Access is, and it's unfortunate because they get frustrated at the fact they are playing a buggy incomplete game, which is transparently exactly what they purchased.This game is off to a fantastic start. It's beautiful, atmospheric, visceral, and just plain fun.  The Devs already have great ideas on how to improve and iterate the gameplay.  Anyone who has an itch for this kind of first person action RPG, better keep an eye on this game.Right now there's about 4 hours of content, and the game has its fair share of bugs, which is in part why it is in EA, so players can help identify issues, provide critical feedback, that the devs can take and in turn, fix bugs, and improve the game.So if you are interested in this kind of game, and want to support the devs, or participate in the game's development, then you should buy into EA.If you are expecting a fully developed game, this is not for you (but do check back later). It's sad people don't seem to understand what EA is.
