_childDocuments_.review: If you played Hexen or Heretic games in the past you will definatly like this one!The game has really good atmosphare, every medieval-fantasy lovers should like this one.The game uses much from Heretic II story - you will arrive a zombie infested little village, but give so much more:First of all, you will have quests to open new areas, unfortunatly these are linear.Therefore you can earn some gold trough killing and looking for secret places ,you can spend these for health potion and new weapons as well.A lot of weapon are available in the game, i saw much more in previous demos, i hope they will be available later.The only disadvantage of the game that it is really hard. _childDocuments_.review: This just feels like a big mess. Here are some reasons not to play it:1: I like shootersThere are three projectile weapons at writing. small crossbow, shotgun crossbow, and peatburner/grenade thrower. You get no ammo and it takes forever to kill anything. They are all incredibly unsatisfying to use.2: I like puzzlesThere was one puzzle I could think of. It was pulling a sequence of levers. Boring, and even then the layout of movement to lever was... awful. The solution involved scrabbling around generic cobblestones searching for two scraps of paper the same color as the wood it's plastered to. It was boring.3: I like explorationYou're going to have to if you want to enjoy this game. Everything is stored in boxes, money, ammo, mana, and... that's it. There are "secrets" that give you little notifications when you find them. An easter-egg or two. but if you're hoping for more interesting stuff.... all you will find is that you wasted your time.4: Hey, maybe the lore is goodSo far it is very generic and not interesting at all. I don't remember the name of the main character at all. Despite seeing it in the inventory screen, and probably being able to recall it if I tried, I simply do not care to put a modicum of effort into learning about them or whatever they're doing in the place that they are, where ever that is. I'm not sure who this game is for.The setting is boring and done to death.Characters have all the warmth and personality of an introductory paragraph.Combat is extremely bland, with no variety of weapons or actions.Objectives are unclear and the INCREDIBLY bland levels sprawl out forever. This is not helped by the largely ornamental map.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: My original review was negative but on re-evaluation, an EA title will always have flaws. The developers responded to my points, so I have shifted this review to positive to support the title, conditional on how well the next update addresses my concerns. My comments on the original review are added in <> below.It's difficult for me to give this game a negative review <so I haven't!>, as there's a lot to like about it - BEAUTIFUL art direction, even though the graphics are not modern by any stretch of the imagination; decent combat, with many options and playstyles available to you; an engrossing and involving world, which does not have enough lore for my liking but still has enough to keep you engaged; pretty good level design, which is nowhere near ImSim territory (since levels are generally designed to be unlocked in a linear way with a single design path from beginning to end, although you have plenty of side-paths to ♥♥♥♥ around in until you find the expected path), etcetc. But there's flaws that I can't even begin to understand right now <which would be unacceptable in final release but acceptable for now in EA>:1) The enemies respawn every time you start up the game, but the ammo drops and loot don't. As a result I'm now in a situation where I have zero ammo for my weapons, and I have literally a battalion of monsters to take down. I would love to play more but this is almost a hard-lock. I can't emphasize how annoying this is enough - if you respawn during the game, enemies stay dead and even retain the life that they had when you last fought them and died. But if I reopen the game for a new session, all of them are back and there's no ammo to compensate. Which would be fine if you could _buy_ ammo, which brings me to.....2) .....you can't. At least, I have not been able to find a store for ammo. There's already a blacksmith where you can get weapon upgrades, but no ammo. Am I just missing something? If I'm not, this is terrible design already. How can you respawn enemies but not the stuff that you kill them with?3) Minor, but there's no cloud saves that I could see. I played this game on Geforce NOW, and then I played it on a Paperspace PC. I played through Steam both times, but had to restart for Paperspace since none of my GFN progress was saved on the cloud. Strange, to say the least.4) Very few ImSim elements. There's very little emergent behavior that I can see aside from some physics features, but even in those, they're limited. You can't throw barrels far enough to do anything useful, and there don't seem to be any rules or tools or RPG systems to exploit the world design, which is halfway decent. No character development, no ImSim. There's generally one playstyle, and I can't imagine in what situations stealth would be of any use.There's a lot of great ideas here. There's some decent execution, but other than that it's really questionable how these points got past the designers so far. The game is most definitely not dead, there's an update which has come out recently that added two new areas, which sound exciting but unless I can get me some new ammo I'm probably locked out of this. If the developers are reading this, any response would be much appreciated and if these issues are resolved I would gladly give the game a thumbs up, since there's a lot going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hexen Reborn! I have spent quite a few hours in Graven now and can confirm that the game scratches that Hexen/heretic itch very well and veterans of those games (especially Hexen eesh!) will be pleased to learn that the puzzles are not as confusing or esoteric. The game has a fantastic gloomy atmosphere with a retro 90's aesthetic that many of us, especially those of us who lived through that fps golden age, have come to love. At its core Graven is a game about exploration and as you find new abilities and open new paths, more of the game is revealed, the game however does not hold your hand in regards to guiding you to these new paths and the map is rudimentary. All in All Graven is a great retro experience and i recommend it to those who enjoyed the Hexen style of game play or those looking for a more Atmospheric, slow paced, retro slasher/shooter game with puzzle elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't waste your time on this. It looks like Hexen, but it's definitely not. The game is very buggy, specifically where key switches randomly reset which can soft lock you into sections.The biggest problem by far with this game is the combat, which is unforgivably bad. Even on the easiest setting, the basic zombies can one-shot you. Your weapons are effectively useless, and the "magic" weapons are bad and unfulfilling. Their version of Afrits spit acid that becomes a large area of effect attack that you just have to wait for it to dissipate, which takes an extremely long time, halting all progress. This isn't a question of the game being too hard so much as it just not working well as designed.Another big issue is the stamina system. For a game that involves a surprising amount of platforming, having to sit still and just wait while your stamina recharges so that you can jump up a set of stairs to proceed is very, very annoying. There's no need to slow players down like this, it should just be removed.Last, saving just doesn't work. You end up back in the main town not at the last checkpoint, and *all* the enemies have respawned, effectively forcing you to start over on any progress. Save your money, and just replay Hexen again instead.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, where to even begin. This game could've been so insanely good, it could've been a really cool spiritual sequel to Dark Messiah of Might & Magic, Arx Fatalis, or Ultima Underworld, but instead we get... this, a poorly realized, inconsistent, and unpolished game which does not know what it actually wants to be.One thing is for sure, it's not an immersive sim even though it's portrayed like one, it's much closer to something like a Hexen/Heretic clone than anything.Everything in this game screams unpolished and underdeveloped: The intro video is choppy and doesn't play correctly (could be a bug), the UI and text doesn't scale with ultrawidescreen resolutions, you can't turn certain effects/filters off, candles/sconces/torches can be lit but then turn on and off randomly or the fire jump between other unlit candles/sconces/torches, some barricades/spikes/fires do damage to the player character but some do not, the chairs the NPC's sit on can be destroyed, some barrels/pots randomly levitate in the air.Worst of all is the low health vignetting (the low health warning). It's downright horrendous to look at and can't be turn off. I almost never get motion sick from a game, but that vignetting gave me a headache and only encouraged to kill my character so that I could respawn with more health.The pacing needed to be improved upon too. Running around with a staff as your only weapon for the first hour does not feel good. Having a staminia meter tied to that staff weapon only made combat feel unsatisfying and a slog, but it sure didn't help that the hitboxes feel off and that stamina regenerates extremely slow either.Writing is clunky, I'm not even a native English speaker but I felt that much of the dialogue and the information in the journal flowed poorly. Except for the art direction I'm terribly disappointed with this game. It needs at least another year of polish, bug fixing, and balancing before I can even remotely begin to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest, I'm didn't enjoy what I played of the EA build of Graven. It seemed slow, and kind of boring, and I got so incredibly lost after the lighthouse that I had to search up a let's play of the game to figure out where to go next.However, a game I enjoyed far, far more is the demo for Graven. The demo had some more interesting combat, and was generally more interesting to me. It also went over the same first section of the game, but with more content, which is a fairly good explanation as to why I enjoyed the EA build so much less. What's more, it seems like the devs are planning on implementing some more features from the demo build of the game, like reverting back to the spells doing some kinds of damage. Still, the demo was extremely promising, and I hope they make the rest of the game as good as that. Also, ♥♥♥♥ these idiots that think an EA game only being a few hours is a scam, it's early access ffs, and quite frankly I'm relieved they went into EA when they did as if they made the rest of the game in the style of the start of this build, I wouldn't enjoy it.If you don't understand early access, do yourself a favour and wait until the full release, but this game is worth supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, I was disappointed. Maybe my expectations were too high for a spiritual successor to the likes of Hexen and Heretic, but while I find those old games still fun in spite of their rough edges, Graven just never quite delivers on its promises. On the Pros side of things, the art and design nails the atmosphere. The game also has a strong start in the opening act. Cons. Magic and combat never seems quite balanced though, like it is not sure if magic should be good or not, and some weapons are just awkward at best. Things seem to go increasingly downhill towards end of Act 1 onwards. My feeling is they never quite nailed what sort of game they are trying to make, spent a lot of time polishing and repolishing the start, then management said "you must release now" and so they just had to make it work and release. There are also bugs. Nothing game-crashing, but soft-lock states and unkillable enemies are not fun. Some have been patched a bit, but I feel that with the current state of the game it simply cannot be fixed without just starting over again with the assets. A real shame.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: I spent the first 30 minutes destroying barrels, and I liked it.Full Release: There is lot of things to dislike about Graven, I wish there wasn't but I have to agree with the mixed rating. There are SO MANY BUGS I ran into that irritated me so much I literally just quit playing a few times and took breaks that lasted weeks some times. Hence why I am only now finishing it, almost four months after release. Everyone has probably already said everything that I have to say but here is my personal rundown.Positives: I love the music, great soundtrack. The visuals are amazing, possibly the best (in my opinion) low poly 3D art in any game ever. Weapons are mixed, didn't care for about half but the good ones are really cool for a fantasy FPS. Plentiful resources, but doesn't seem as overabundant as in EA. Despite what some people are saying, magic is very useful in combat if you know how to use it. The hubs, NPC's, and side quests make this feel more like an RPG than you'd probably expect at times which is cool. Level design is overall very open and areas are interesting to explore.Negatives: Well bugs of course. A lot of that has been fixed at this point but there are still minor bugs everywhere you look. Stamina is really annoying, I hate crawling around in these sorts of games I want to run and jump non-stop. And in graven I don't even have enough stamina to jump over rocks when I need to. So I sit there and wait for it to painfully slowly refill. Doesn't seem like a big deal until it happens to you. Inventory is dumb, inconvenient and unnecessary and just makes you forget 3 / 4 of your stuff exists. Seriously about 75% of playtime is just backtracking trying to figure out what to do. THERE IS NO MAP which is unbelievable, this game desperately needs a map, it would make the flow of the game so much smoother, more fun, and not nearly as frustrating. The very few puzzles in the game are horrible. Clues just don't make any sense or they are extremely basic. Some enemies don't feel like they were made for your character to fight. Idk how to describe it combat just doesn't feel right a lot of the time, it's not the weapons it comes down to the stamina factor and enemies movement / attack patterns I believe. There is a particular enemy type in episode 2, and one in episode 3, that have horrible and ridiculous movement though I believe this has been somewhat improved with updates judging by what I saw from going back to hub 2 after finishing the game. Each episode is a little smaller and worse than the last, not great game progression. Essentially, the thing is, between being lost all the time and having honestly just not fun combat, Graven just isn't nearly as enjoyable as it looks. I really don't think I'll ever play it again, I'd rather watch a playthrough. But I also do not regret buying it and playing it through once. And if a sequel comes out (which I doubt) I would buy it. And I think a lot of the complaining about graven is unjustified and comes from people who's opinions are heavily influenced by youtubers and who are biased against 3D realms due to things that have happened over the last few years. One thing you hear all the time is how this game was in EA development forever, but it came out after Ultrakill and Viscerafest and has already had a full release while those two don't even have release dates yet, Ultrakill is on its path to being the next Wrath Aeon of Ruin with how ridiculously long its EA is lasting. I mean just look at the dates. The only reason people were targeting this games development was because of its publisher and development team unfortunately. Back to Graven though, it has a lot of issues, but it isn't terrible like a lot of people would have you believe. It is about a 6 / 10 and it could have been a solid 10 with some different design choices and more development time, which is kinda sad, but it is worth supporting in my opinion. Don't pick a youtuber out and let them think for you, decide for yourself what you like and what is good.
_childDocuments_.name: GRAVEN

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals and atmosphere makes this one's world a great place to explore, however the gameplay lets it down.Even though the game is clearly taking inspiration from Hexen, including the mana system and what most of its pickups look like, however despite having that game's enemy count it does not play like one. Do you enjoy walking forward, bonking a zombie on the nogging with a melee weapon, then backing up to avoid its friends' swipes? Repeat 10 times per group, in every area, every time you return as they respawn?Because that's most of what you'll be doing for the first 6 hours. The melee weapons feel bad, and the level design repeatedly makes use of water that slows you to a crawl, making avoiding damage even more difficult. Oh, what's that, still not obnoxious enough? Okay, how about a "modern" stamina system that depletes when you sprint, jump or ?But wait, what about the ranged weapons? Well, you have a mini crossbow. It takes several shots in the head to take down a basic zombie, and until later you don't get nearly enough ammo to afford spending it on the respawning fodder.The shotgun crossbow fares better, however like above, you simply do not get enough ammo to use it comfortably, and deity help you if you need to fight a bigger monster without ranged ammo, one or two hits is enough to put you at death's door.Surely the magic will save you! Well, no. See, for some reason, the first two spells you get are absolutely worthless as damage dealers. You can set people on fire, but will burn most of your mana bar taking down a single zombie with it (and it'll take +10s). Your second spell (gotten hours in) is a lightning bolt that stuns people! Great! Except it stuns them only the first time they're hit, and has the same damage problem the fire spell has.No, these two spells are instead used for burning terrain and activating mechanisms. Hexen indeed.I am now 6 hours in and  got an offensive means of using magic (a book). Hooraaaay, I finally get to use those resources they've been throwing at me for hours now. Perhaps in another 6 hours I will get to use this big brick ammo that I've been full up on since the literal start of the game, oh, to dream.The enemies are spongy, the weapons feel bad, the save system is broken (reloading the game starts you from the central hub, in a game with no fast travel), you're punished for playing the game like the fast games that inspired it and the single boss I fought so far felt like a first pass at the design that no one returned back to. If the game gets better after this point I will never know, for I am done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I see quite alot of potential with Graven in future updates, but right now its VERY barren of any sort of challenge or content. Ammo is VERY abundant, so the melee weapons lose their purpose quickly, healing vials are everywhere and negate the urgency of using healing potions. At no point after the sewers did i feel any danger from anything i fought, maybe if they made enemies more aggressive or increased numbers, or even made it more like a Resident evil game where ammo can be precious, maybe then the gameplay will feel better.Graven isnt bad by any means, the story is good, visually the game has a very old school vibe, and future updates can fix alot of the issues, but this is also a $25 game. Early access was the best choice for future development, but i hope the devs can figure out what this game wants to be before they move forward. Survival shooter or old school FPS, right now its too confused with too many elements of both. For this reason at the moment, i cant recommend this game UNLESS you want to support development. _childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game with a few very important caveats.First, this is not a standard Boomer Shooter. It has hubs, a death mechanic with infinite respawns which cost only gold, no quicksaves, central hubs, lots of exploration, and resource management in the form of limited hot bar space and various weapons/spells/items which can take 1, 2, or even 3 hotbar spaces.You need to backtrack to complete quests, find hidden items, gold, and upgrade your gear.Enemies can respawn to a limited degree if you save and quit. Saving and quitting will also return you to the main hub, which is technically a feature since it guarantees you the ability to return to town without the chance of being killed and losing some of your gold.Next, this game was another victim of top level corporate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scandal and was left abandoned and fallow for over a year at one point until the devs were finally able to get back to finishing it.So, the game is essentially a multi-act, hub based exploration game in first person, set in a dark fantasy world with excellent retro themed visuals and top notch sound work.If that sounds good, you might just enjoy Graven.If you're expecting a traditional boomer shooter? Maybe not so much.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this a thumbs down not because it is bad, but because it's something you can find better somewhere else. I got this for 5$, so my experience wasn't too bad considering that I feel like I got my money's worth, but for it's retail asking price, no, definitely not. This game feels like a kind of Bioshock/systemshock style tactical shooter, but lacks the depth needed to satisfy as the combat just comes down to whacking enemies with basic melee or shooting with little skill or strategy. no stealth, weapons are just direct pistol and shotgun and two almost the same melee weapons (I know there's more from the demo, but I haven't found the flail again yet.), and little other than combat beyond simple find the key puzzles and little else. Some puzzles aren't, but those are not fun in their own right.Now, I wouldn't damn this game just for being an inferior version of another. if a game is good on it's own merit and can be considered unique enough not be be plageristically derivative, than it still justifies itself, but by itself, it's just unsatisfactory after a while. combat complexity never grows, enemies are bare bones in how to fight them, and there's not enough satisfaction in exploration as there's little gain beyond keeping your ammo and health up. What's worse is that the magic is pointless. The first two spells you get are hardly worth it. the resources needed for them are rare and quickly depleted with regular use, but you never want to use magic regularly because it's useless. the fire spell is only good at light DoT which hardly does anything, and for lighting explosive, which can be done with a crossbow bolt just as well. The lightning spell activates machinery, just another key then, and stuns enemies. For how long? Well as long as you keep shocking them, which means that as soon as you try to attack with an actual damaging weapon, they go right back to normal. The two weapons you can't unassign from the quickslot are the staff and the spellbook, and I hardly ever use the spell book outside of needed, which is also rarely. And then there's a thin about slotting gemstones in your staff to give it alternative effects, the first of which, guess what, is a stone that allows you to break walls and doors open.................so basically another kind of key. It does something else, but it never felt different from default, so I can't even remember what it is.Overall, you can get the entire Bioshock collection for around 10$ on a good sale, and there's probably a slew of other titles I don't know about just as good or offering their own thing. Now if you want a DOOM-like shooter with a gothic fantasy and where you play as a wizard, play project Warlock. Better combat, better weapons, better exploration, and the magic spells are actually useful.EDIT: and before anyone says that this game is still early access, so flaws are to be expected, let this be seen as an explanation as to what the flaws are, and why a new player may not want to pick this game up as it is now. But considering all the complaints of how slow updates are coming, there may be valid worry that this game may not be leaving early access any time soon. Still, for me, I got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is Mixed, leaning slightly to positive) A game with great ideas but often poor execution.Graven is a Retro FPS hybrid game, set in a fantasy medieval world with magic, monsters, and a lot of running around. You play as... Mr. Graven, I don't think the main character is named, as he goes through 3 distinctive lands as he looks for his daughter. Graven is a game that I have very mixed feels on as while the core gameplay is surprisingly a lot of fun, there's so many little things wrong with it that drag it down to just a "It's a okay game" Basically, I advise to wait to grab it on a huge discount or if it's packaged in a bundle like I did!Gameplay of GRAVEN is basically if you took Hexen and made it somewhat less confusing. Each of the 3 acts starts in a hub and then branches out with puzzles to solve and progress. Well at least Act 1 is like this. Acts 2 and 3 feel a lot more linear at least in it's map design while Act 1 in Cruxfirth feels more natural with a lot of entrances and exits to different levels branching from the hub world. It made the fact that the game doesn't save your checkpoints after leaving the game a bit more fun as it gave me the opportunity to route pathways between levels. Most of the time the game does a pretty good job at trying to subtle tell the player what they need to do but if the game doesn't you can expect walking around trying to figure out what to a lot. The weaponry of GRAVEN is also a bit all over the place. You have Melee, Ranged, and Magic to use to defeat enemies and between all of them, Ranged is clearly the superior method. Melee weapons have the risk of being up close to enemies which is more of a problem because the hit detection on yourself is very jank which could cause you to lose way more health than you wished. Magic starts off pretty ineffective and you have to commit to upgrading them to make them a bit more useful. Ranged Weapons basically have none of these downsides other than ammo usage, except for the fact ammo is absolutely everywhere in this game and they provide simply a safer and more effective way to defeat enemies. As you can upgrade your weapons with the gold you can collected as mentioned before, you'd probably be spending a lot of it on weapon upgrades as even the early game weapons fully upgraded are still extremely useful even by Act 3. Speaking of Gold, that's your currency. Collected from enemies, the environment, and secrets. Which would be great except for the fact if you die, you lose gold. Which sounds reasonable but the more you horde the more you lose and since there's a lack of quicksaving it ends up enforcing you to play as carefully as possible, avoiding as many risks as possible, even if you can regain your loot unless you fell in a pit. It's a gameplay loop I had a lot of fun with but it just lacks in a lot of areas that prevents it from being the best it can be all the time. Style wise however, GRAVEN looks absolutely fantastic. While again I do think Cruxfirth of Act 1 got the most beauty treatment, which is surprising since it's basically a sewer/swamp theme. GRAVEN's use of lowpoly and pixel-y textures is absolutely used to it's advantage as all the various maps and really pretty and have pretty elaborate architecture. It gives a fantastic fantasy medieval vibe with the kind of technology that is in places in the game's lore. It's kinda a shame there's only roughly 3 main level themes cause I would have loved to have seen more environments in this artstyle. Overall, GRAVEN, in my eyes, is just okay. it has a lot of potential with a good chunk of the game flowing really well. It's just brought down with all the little gameplay quirks and jank that boils it down to just a alright experience. While the game does support multiplayer, I'm unsure if having more people to play the game with would assist in the game's other shortcomings. Like how Halo 1 was with me. Basically, I advise to pick up this game either when it's on a deep discount and you really wanna play/experience it. I struggle to call it completely bad but it is certainly not worth the 25$ in it's current state. Plus, during my playthrough, absolutely NONE of the Achievements worked which absolutely annoyed me as a achievement enjoyer.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven is a game about wasted potential.A modern Hexen or Heretic with evocative dark fantasy artstyle, a range of upgradable weapons going from fantastical to mystical, a sufficiently wide bestiary and classic puzzles, switch-pulling and key-seeking gameplay? The idea sounds great.The implementation is unfortunately lacking and much of that can be blamed on the atrocious map design. While areas are beautiful and distinctive, objectives tend to be stowed away in odd places requiring extensive backtracking- and the removal of the in-game map with the full release in light of that is actually criminal, resulting in aimless wandering to try to find whatever door the key you found opens for longer than I'd like. That could be forgiven if the combat was more fun, but unfortunately that is lacking too.Combat itself is fairly simple. Use weapon, shoot monster. Some enemies have weakpoints so you can bash them with your stick and dispatch them more easily. This is fine in Act 1, where you have a nice mix between projectile slinging cultists, burly warriors, expendable zombies and the like. The real problem comes in Act 2, where enemies are very, very durable, rush at you in massive hordes, sprint at Mach 2 and shear off a third of your health per swing. Some slow you and fire projectiles that are nearly hitscan. All do far too much damage.I'm playing on Ordained difficulty, the 'normal' difficulty. More times than I'd like to admit I'd been suddenly mobbed by chilly zombies sprinting in from outside view range like cruise missiles and murdered, and frankly, I got tired of struggling through screens reading YOU LOST 271 GOLD to continue the aimless wandering, lever and door search to continue.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;DR - Great start. Peters out after the second chapter. Still worth playing for FPS fans.First, the good. The first ten hours of the game are amazing. Sure, there is a bit of jank here and there, but it's playable jank and doesn't detract from the overall experience.Visually the game is quite impressive, the music is very on point and the atmosphere in some areas is second to none. I was having an absolute blast and Graven was on course for being my game of the year. That is, until...About half way through the second chapter I realised I was playing a cut down version of the original vision. There were less side quests, the environments were smaller and less interactive. By chapter 3 there was no doubt the dev team gathered together stray bits of completed content and haphazardly stapled them together.They clearly ran out of time, or money, or both and released what they could. The result is a game that is entirely front loaded with it's best content, sours over time and leaves a poor impression upon completion.It's a shame because the start of the game promised great things. It was *this* close to being a modern classic, but it fell at the last hurdle, cracked it's skull and dragged itself across the finish line on broken legs.Despite it's flaws I still think it's worth playing, if only for the opening chapter. Just make sure you temper your expectations going in.

It's alluded to that you'll eventually get there but take this as a Build engine type shooter with some magic elements and you'll enjoy what's here so far.

_childDocuments_.review: It was just boring. Level design looked pretty good but the core gameplay is was just not there IMO. Slow paced and combat was a mash fest. Spells and medieval weaponry were a big letdown, mana was incredibly stingy and spells were only used for puzzle solving. Some aspects of the levels were also pretty frustrating like the totem puzzle.Side note - This game is unoptimized. It's fine on my gtx 1080 but there's just simple aspects of game design that it fails completely flat. Explosions create WAY too many particle effects, leading even *me* to lag (let me remind you this game is going for retro-inspired graphics. It has absolutely ZERO excuse to be system intensive.) The engine felt slightly buggy overall and I took damage due to a bug at least once (fell through water and hit the ground, I could see potential for taking damage from other bugs (stepping on helmets makes you fly forward in some situations.)) Aside from that, i'd give this game a 2/10 in its current state

_childDocuments_.review: At present this game isn't worth it, there isn't much more content than the demo (in some cases weapons/spells and bosses have been removed) though there is one additional area and a handful of new enemies.The combat feels rather simplistic and not that challenging, the only challenge I found was getting shot from the side while attacking another enemy, but that feels rather cheap. The enemy AI is incredibly dumb and you can beat most enemies easily with simple circle strafing or sniping them with a ranged weapon. There doesn't really seem to be much in the way of defensive options which make combat interesting either, the sword can block but I don't know if that even does anything. Despite the emphasis put on fighting intelligently I don't really feel there's many options for that or much cause to do so when it's so much simpler to spam left click and circle strafe.The world and game itself have real potential, but at the moment there just isn't enough there to see if the game will live up to that potential, but I sincerely hope it does.tl;dr: With little more content than the demo, consistent bugs, and lack of a strong core combat loop I'd recommend waiting for a major update or two before buying.I'll update this review as more of the game releases, I'm looking forward to seeing what it becomes in the end.

I can just tell that this game is something I really like.The explorations feels worth your time, optional weapons in optional areas you can completly skip. The choice of putting in a spellbook whose pages you can, and must turn, It is simply awesome. Small details that add to the gameplay and atmosphere of the game. _childDocuments_.review: The game suffers a little from being neither a true immersive sim nor a boomer shooter, but it's still pretty fun.The environments are beautiful and enjoyable to explore, with plenty of secrets to find and shortcuts that loop back around to previous areas, making the world feel more interconnected and less linear.The immersive sim elements are very light and generally have more in common with something like the original System Shock than more modern games in the genre. For the most part you're finding keys, completing objectives, and killing everything in your way, rather than making any decisions in terms of how to complete your objective. But there are a variety of useful upgrades you'll usually have to choose between that can impact how you play the game, plus most opponents have a few hidden weaknesses to figure out, which helps to keep things interesting.Combat is a little odd in that it sometimes feels like it expects you to play it like a fast paced boomer shooter, but you have stamina, can't sprint backwards, and can only have a handful of weapons ready to go at a time. Additionally some enemy attacks feel a little overtuned, I'd expect to take more damage from a skeleton in melee than at range for example, yet the extremely fast and mostly silent crossbow attacks from skeleton mages seem to be more problematic than any melee attack, or even their magic attacks.The weapons all feel excellent though, each that I've found so far has its uses and I find myself swapping between them regularly. Sound design and feedback can be a little mixed but there's definitely some solid weapons, the alt fire on one crossbow fires delayed explosive bolts which are incredibly satisfying to use.This may be an obscure comparison, but overall the combat reminds me a little of a less janky Northern Journey. A weapon might feel a little weird at first, but once you figure it out it's quite effective, and that need to get good with it makes it more satisfying in the long run.I was a little wary after the game came out of Early Access due to some of the more mixed/negative reviews, but I'm enjoying it quite a lot so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven is a game I cannot recommend right now. Besides giving me terrible motion sickness, I just didn’t enjoy it I’m afraid. I’ll do my best to review the part that I did play, however, which isn’t very long, about an hour or so, but as far as I can tell the rest of the game plays out in a similar manner, just with more difficult puzzles. Once of the other reasons I quit was that I was continuously being spawnkilled by a more powerful enemy. After six times I had enough. I just didn’t like it.  Maybe I expected something different, but this is far from a game that I would buy. The game is marketed as a first person puzzle game, and in a way it is, but don’t come in thinking this is similar to Portal or The Talos Principle.The first thing you’ll notice is how sharp the graphics look while looking old school at the same time. It’s a nice looking game and it’s the thing that made me want to try it out in the first place. And then you start the game. You arrive in a boat, so you’re wondering if this is maybe some kind of open world RPG like The Elder Scrolls – which would definitely be a better fit in my opinion – but alas, it’s not. But then you accept your first quest and you start wondering again, even exploring a little, but nope, it’s still not a RPG.  You enter the rather big area below the city and there are enemies there and it quickly becomes clear that this is, nope, still not a RPG, but some kind of puzzle game set in a city. The area is filled with enemies that can be defeated, secrets to find, items to pick up and, naturally, puzzles to complete. It now starts to look more like Quake or Doom, with item pick-ups and killing enemies. And in a way it is, I guess, but it just has the addition of (a) puzzle(s). Once you complete the quest it’s on to the next one and the next area.The game has a couple of spells and a couple of weapons in Early Access, but so far all the weapons I’ve tried lack any punch. For some enemies it takes one hit, for others it can take five or six. I miss any kind of logic to it, or I might have missed something maybe, I don’t know. For spells it’s the same thing. It’s a good exercise for your hand, though; my hand is now extra muscular because of all the unnecessary clicking.I’ve already mentioned being spawnkilled by a bigger, more powerful, enemy so that’s one of my frustrating issues with the game. The other is that the enemies aren’t smart and that their attacks are more annoying than tactical. Enemies can jump – and they’ll jump a lot – making it hard to hit them. They can also hit very hard. So to balance it out you will have to find health potions from time to time. There’s no regenerating health here. It’s all very old school. And about the enemy intelligence; I had a group of 7 enemies coming at me. All I had to do it hide behind a spiked barricade and they all jumped into it and got instantly killed. I’m not sure if that’s part of a puzzle or not (I’m fairly confident it’s not), but man, the AI leaves a lot to be desired, as does the pathfinding of these enemies.One other issue is the fact that the game saves at checkpoints. I had a quest accepted, then quit later and when I got back I would be back in the city, just like the game informed me about when I first started it. Except it didn’t tell me I also had to fetch the quest again. Now, the distances aren’t that terrible and it would take just a minute or so, but I would say that that’s something that would normally have to be saved.The UI could also use a little work to make things a little easier. I saw some elements in it that left me clueless and were never explained. Sure, it’s still Early Access and it might be updated later on, but still; I found it worth to mention.Does this game have any redeeming qualities then? Yes, it gave me motion sickness so I could quit the game. Joking aside, the graphics really do look kind of awesome, with a nice mix of old school and modern graphics. The atmosphere is moody and fits the style the game is going for (a lot of dead people laying around) and the music is equally moody, which is also good. The voice acting that is there is solid and fits the theme. I had no issues here.I’m sorry, but this game is just no good. Aside from the great aesthetics this game just didn’t do it for me. Maybe you’ll enjoy it more, your mileage may vary. Given the current price it’s going for I definitely wouldn’t recommend it, but maybe if it was $10 or so, sure, give it a try. You can always ask for a refund.But if you want to play a better first person puzzle game, be sure to try out these first: Portal, Portal 2, The Talos Principle, Q.U.B.E., Q.U.B.E. 2, Antichamber, Quantum Conundrum or The Witness. These are all much, much, *much* better games. This game would just be a last resort, for when you have finished all of these and all of rest of the other puzzle games and your puzzle hunger just cannot be quenched any longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven is like that lingering sneeze that never comes through and leaves you uncontented. The game is raw as it is but second and third chapters are just a rotting corpse.A strange, inconsistent atmosphere is present in every episode, just like the game doesn't know what it wants to be.Some parts are decently made and atmospheric, most others, badly made arena/corridor shooter scenarios. Imsim elements barely woven into the gameplay, leave you with only the illusion of creativity.This game was not created to be a fast paced arena shooter yet it often floods you with quick moving enemies and throws you right into combat arenas that you have to deal with, using your sluggish and limited movement.At least the overall difficulty is somewhat well crafted by sparing you from fighting obnoxious bullet sponges, as enemy hp and damage they deliver stays the same across all difficulties, only the complexity of encounters changes.Graven is missing any form of fast travel and manual save system. I would be fine with that if it didn’t throw you back into the main hub each time you saved and quit. You would like to save the game and go attend your grandmas funeral, well too bad, next time you are back we will spawn you in some sh*thole. Games that require you to venture off the main path, explore and interact with dangerous environments, even to a limited degree as seen in Graven, should either save you in the spot you were in when you quit, resetting all the enemies, or grant you the ability to save manually. It also doesn’t help that checkpoints are straight up bugged at some points, and as I was going backwards through a level, they kept spawning enemies all around me.Blatantly bad game design decisions and uncooked content also include: a terrible stamina system, THE FU*KING SWIMMING, ladders, obnoxiously designed or unfinished enemies, unbalanced or simply useless weapons and spells, unfinished side quests (even some main quests are unintuitive at times), objectively bad boss fights and many, many more.Graven is rotten at its core, so I cannot recommend it for now or for the future, unless some miraculous revisioned version happens.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about whacking things with a stick. At least, that's the impression I got 50 minutes into it, at which point I tapped out. The stick you get in the beginning helps you crack various pots, crates, and barrels scattered around the world for health and ammo pickups - a real necessity because you need both in a hurry. Often these containers take multiple hits to break apart, which can quickly become tedious. The game introduces you to your first spell which allows you to set things on fire, and then throws your first enemy, a zombie, at you. I made the mistake of spending all my mana using the fire spell, which did absolutely no noticeable damage despite setting the enemy on fire. Back to whacking zombies with a stick. Sometimes they go down in one hit, other times in 4-5 hits. These zombies are tough and can easily take down half your health if you just stand there and trade blows with them. Thankfully there are plenty of health pickups, but it's a lot of mouse clicking / stick whacking.Just as the game started to get a bit boring, I picked up my first distance weapon, a crossbow, and a lightning spell. The crossbow is nice, it shoots fast and takes things down in a few hits, but I quickly ran out of ammo. The lightning spell was introduced in the same way as a fire spell, by throwing five zombies right after you pick it up. It's not the kind of lightning that turns zombies into ash, it's the kind that paralyzes them temporarily so that you can... you guessed it, whack them with a stick, by now a repetitive, tedious, drawn out process. Finally I ran into a new monster that took three hits to take me down and sent me to the very beginning of the level, despite multiple checkpoints my progress was "saved at" along the way. At about this point I decided it's not worth my while to wait if things get better.I didn't have any particular hopes for Graven, and I understand that it's its own kind game. It does look like Wrath: Aeon of Ruin, but I think it goes for a very different gameplay. The problem is that the introduction to the game world is boring and repetitive, and maybe that is also starts with a sewer level. Maybe things get more fun with more weapons and cool enemies down the line, but none of that matters when the first hour is such a chore, and when you have to backtrack after death. Other reviews say you need to fight all the enemies you already killed along the way. I don't know if it's true or not, I decided it wasn't worth it to find out.I think this game has potential, and after all, this is some sort of alpha build, which shows. It has a potential to be fun, and hopefully that will be unlocked in the months to come. I'll check back in a year I think.

_childDocuments_.review: I am recommending Graven for the atmosphere, The retro style graphics, mixed with a cool, medieval/ gothic art direction makes for great exploration. If you look at something like Hexen or Amid Evil, which is what this game reminds me so I can't help but compare, we have such cool weapons in those game. These games make you feel like a bad ass. Hit feedback and all that is better than the Phantom Fury demo but not by much, most weapons don't feel impactful at all etc.What finally put me off of the game was going into act 2 which is essentially just a recoloured swamp world with the exact same style of buildings and gameplay and I'd just had enough by that point.I would say wait for patches to really iron things over but given that half the dev team got sacked I wouldn't expect too much out of it for the time being.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon the first impression, the game has very strong Hexen / Heretic vibes. And it's not just the visually similar potions, weapons and the overall atmosphere, it's also huge locations with various secrets and shortcuts, general combat feel and exploration.Of course, Graven also takes some things from other games, sometimes it reminds of Thief, sometimes of Quake. But in general, this is an homage to shooters of the 90s, however, it's not a "boomer shooter", it's a slower paced, more methodical game, where you are rewarded for exploration, curiosity and wits.However, as you move forward, the game becomes progressively worse. Act I has tons of content, including many optional quests and various secrets. It is obvious it received a lot of love. But Act II is already worse, and Act III is so bad I wish it wasn't even in the game. Thankfully, Act I is about the same length as the latter two acts combined.The same goes about bosses. They are all bad, just huge dudes with lots of HP. But the last one is especially bad, it reminds me of Half-Life's Nihilant. The fight and the ending is so unticlimactic and smudges the great impressions of the first part of the game.Then, the game has so many strange design decisions. There are checkpoints, but when you exit the game and load back, you are back at the act hub. It's not so bad in the first two Acts, but Act III is empty and huge, and this point is put very strangely. Besides, you need stamina to run, jump and attack with melee weapons, and it runs out pretty quickly. And thus this makes walking back even a bigger chore. Why is stamina even in the game, I have no idea. It seems it's there just to annoy the player.The same goes about UI. It has limited number of quick slots, so you can't equip all the weapons you have. And it later acts, when you have many weapons, but ammo runs out quickly, you have to open the inventory to swap the weapon in a quick slot. It's not hard (the game pauses when you open the inventory), just plain irritating.And, of course, there's no minimap, which is a rather strange decision since the locations are huge, you have to backtrack a lot, and even though you unlock shortcuts, it's easy to get lost. And it has nothing to do with game being an omage to 90s shooters: the majority of those had mini maps.Still, even with all its flaws, I recommend Graven, because there's very few modern games like this (but then again, I grew up playing Doom, Heretic, Quake, Half-Life and Thief). But get it on sale and after patches: I had to restart because of a few game breaking bugs, and since it entails running back from a hub area, this makes the issues Graven has even more noticeable.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was going to rate this game thumbs down and call it a walking stick-wacking simulator.Then, I realized that you actually have to read in this game, and those explosive barrels actually have a reason to be there other than making a big boom!Now we shall call it--Hexen 2 Advanced, without the crazy puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: A Bundle of Gaming JoyI recently dove into the Steam bundle featuring Graven, Wrath, & Ion Fury, and what a ride it's been! Let me share my experience:Graven's Flagellant Mode Fun: Starting off with Graven on flagellant mode was a bold move for a first-timer like me, but boy, am I glad I did! The thrill of navigating through its challenges while enjoying the buttery-smooth Unreal Engine gameplay is an absolute joy. Kudos to the developers for delivering such an outstanding experience.A Unique Blend: While some may try to categorize Graven into familiar genres like Puzzle, RPG or FPS, I believe it's in a league of its own. Its distinct gameplay mechanics and immersive world make it truly unique.A Contrast with Wrath: Comparing it to Wrath: Aeon of Ruin, where you move like a praeterhuman killing machine (totally rocks btw) which does not take fall damage, Graven takes a more human-like approach with its stamina system and movement mechanics. This adds depth to the gameplay, requiring a blend of patience, strategy, and quick reflexes.A Roguelike Mindset: Graven demands of me a roguelike mindset (there are no procedurally generated levels in game), where every move counts. 'Diving' into dangerous areas and pulling back when you need healing, supplies or upgrades. It's not just about twitch skills; it's about strategic thinking and careful planning, making each victory all the more satisfying. Overall, diving into Graven has been an absolute delight. If you're looking for a game that challenges you in all the right ways while offering a truly unique experience, look no further. Graven delivers, and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried twice to get into "Graven", but although I liked the atmosphere that reminds on "Hexen" & Co., I failed twice to experience real fun with the game. Equipped with a staff, a pseudo-inventory (devs, tell people they only get a few armor points in the HUD when buying that expensive armor - I searched the forums for an answer to the bug that it doesn't appear in inventory!) and some mana crystals, you try to figure out what to do first, and where. As this might be the easy task, navigating the world isn't because of a total miss of compass or even map. And - as beautiful as the levels might be designed - every corner basically looks the same - in the cellar, in the town, in the swamp, everywhere). Fighting enemies might become easier with new weapons, but in melee, our character is overpowered even in the second difficulty. One shot by a zombie - and there are hordes of them -, and you bite the dust. The 'magic' in the game seems like a puzzle-solver - I got his 'flame' spell that basically does nothing but inflaming barrels. Using it to fight an enemy ... well, try to fight a werewolf with a match and you know what I mean. Overall, the game felt non-motivating, with a sword I found and tried to fight that neverending swamp-zombie-horde and died like twelve times, losing all my money, and no hint where to go next. I mean, you can of course give it a try or two, but in the end, I thought that playing "Hexen" another onehundredandone times would be more satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Very very good.For context i've been on a historical tour through some older games while reading Masters of Doom (about John Carmack and John Romero creating Doom and ID Software). The reason i mention that is because before playing this i've sunk 40 hours into Doom 1993 (and then even more in the source ports). I've been through Quake, Kingpin (Reloaded).  I found that doing this actually reset my palate. I'd gotten so used to modern visuals and games that i was struggling to appreciate them anymore. It was all so generic and dull.I really haven't felt interested in any modern games since this. They all feel far too bloated and over-complicated. I crave the simplicity of the older games.So coming to Graven with this mindset i'm already loving it. It feels like the perfect progression for me. It sits in a spot that feels like an old classic while also looking and feeling like a modern take on the old classic. Both visually and in terms of gameplay and story.I love the art direction. It's got atmoshpere. It feels authentic and immersive yet retains an oldschool charm. A bit like what Boltgun did visually. Super crisp visuals with atmospheric lighting and detailed environments yet at the same time refined and pixelated. It's gorgeous. It's oozing with atmosphere from the visuals and audio to the voice work and story.I'm not super far in but have replayed the opening a few times (i tend to do this while i learn a new game before i get going) and i can tell that i already love it.It doesn't hold your hand at all. The maps take a while to figure out at first but then once you have you can zip around them really fast (either to revisit secrets or on a replay). The combat feels chunky and fun even with the starting weapon.I'll update once i've got further along but so far i'm really enjoying what this game has shown me and i can't wait to have some time to sit down and go through it fully.

_childDocuments_.review: Never has burning piles of plague-victims been as satisfying.Played this three years ago with an early, bare-bones demo and saw enough in the game to buy it. It's dark, grimy, and bleak with fun game play including light puzzle work, melee and ranged combat, secret area hunting and what seems like a few story points right now. Overall, for this GenXer that first played Heretic when it was still shareware, I am satisfied. Just dive in, wreck stuff and explore. Will it change your life? I certainly hope not. It's just a game. Will it entertain you and enrich your gaming vocabulary? I think so. It is NOT without its flaws and there are things that I hope the devs address (but it seems as of July 2024 they have quit trying) but Graven is really cool thus far and I am having good fun playing it. _childDocuments_.review: Somethings before you dive in my review:*I didn't finish the game, i've only played through the first act and the very first 10 minutes of the second one;*I didn't try the coop (for lack of friends with the game).*I waited until the game got released to play it, didn't try it through the EA.Graven is a beautiful. moody, atmospheric first  person adventure game, more similar to (but not the same as) Hexen 2. It's clearer and easier to navigate. The maps are full of secrets and interconnected, keeping things interesting. The weapons are cool and upgradable, though the game suffer from the issue of 70% of your arsenal being composed of different kinds of crossbows.My main issue with the game is how buggy the game was on release, with a lot of things being fixed in the first couple of  patches. The thing is, everytime i get a problem, it's something that people haven't reported yet or that the developers don't know how to fix. I've lost all of my inventory once, but kept the game progress. The second, and worst issue is that the game crashes at the very first 10 minutes of the second act when i need to go through a door and that issue hasn't been solved since the last time i've played, meaning the game is unplayable for me at the moment.If i could give something between a yes and a no for the game, i would. There's a lot of potential there, but the way the games have been handled by the publisher left the developers exhausted and the games unnatended (Wrath and Phantom Fury are in the same place).I'm giving it a thumbs up because people should experience it, but i can't say anything about two of the three acts of the game. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game... I really did. I bought it in early access over a year ago.  It had a number of bugs and issues back then, which is fine, but as a long time 3D Realms fan and reading about the game, it was something I wanted to support and hoped it would improve on before the full release.  Last month, I watched Zlimbratski's review on the game -  - and it got me psyched up to sink my teeth into this game.  Unfortunately, after many many hours on the first chapter I can not recommend this.  First, a lot of things other people complain about do not bother me so much - the stamina (I kind of like the realism that if you are tired from running, you can't jump high!), the lack of a map (again, adds to realism), the constant crate and barrel smashing.  A number of other things has turned me off - the sudden respawning of monsters for no apparent reason, the respawning of my character after dying into situations of instant death, and how quickly and easily you can lose everything because of this!   Like I mentioned earlier, I enjoy realism and this game has it some areas.... but then I go through a large area and kill every single monster, depleting my ammo to almost nothing, and then I turn around to go grab gold or ammo dropped near the beginning, and suddenly EVERY SINGLE MONSTER I JUST KILLED HAS SUDDENLY SPRUNG BACK TO LIFE.  What the hell!  At least put the ammo drops back that I picked up... but no, they don't.  This has happened numerous times.  And then the most crushing thing is you find yourself surrounded with a bunch of respawned flying acid-spitting creatures around you, and of course they have IMPECCABLE AIM, and nail you before you can switch to your crossbow - so you die and lose a huge chunk of gold that you were saving to upgrade your fire and lightning powers.  You choose to respawn because you don't want to go back to the beginning... and you respawn on the pools of acid and die immediately, losing even more gold.  You choose to respawn again, because surely that is a better choice than starting at the beginning, and this time you avoid the pools of acid, but are met with an army of skeletons with crossbows who also have perfect aim, and they nail you from all sides and kill you almost instantly, just as those acid-spitting f**kers from above are shooting at you too.  You respawn... and again die immediately in a pool of acid.  You respawn again, and this time you avoid the acid and can take out a couple skeletons with lightning and fire... and then when you check your inventory you realize that the 3,000 gold you had saved has now dwindled down to less than 1,000, you get so mad you rage quit.  *ahem*Anyway, it would be nice if they could implement a few things:1 - Instead of respawning all creatures in an area, maybe just a handful at a time2 - More care should be taken with our character respawning after death - like how about not dropping us in a pool of acid?  Or maybe starting off invincible for five seconds to avoid hazards?3 - I like that we can recover some of our gold after dying - but can we not have it stuck up in trees or on the side of cliffs that we can't reach?  It's hard enough to build up savings, let alone lose it like this.  Or maybe implement a safe in town for storage?Anyway, I'm taking a break from the game - many things to love about it, but will check in to see if there are improvements on some of these things.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven got it's first update a year later... Well, I'm not disappointed ! To finish the entire 1st chapter (at least I think we got the entire first chapter?) it took me about 10 hours because I took my time explore the area.If the 2nd and 3rd area are this big, the game promise a lot of enjoyment. I'm in a hurry to see more weapons and more spells along with rings and gems for your staff. The level design is fantastic, weapons are a blast and to think that more is to come is pure bliss ! Everything is somewhat interconnected and you keep finding new areas as you explore and unlock areas.We also got the co-op update which works pretty well, still a few bugs left but nothing that will stop you from enjoying the game.Everything about the game screams hexen but the level design is way better, the graphics are amazing and the animations adds quite a lot.It's still an EA, you can feel it at times but I'm sure everything is going to be fixed overtime. The current state of the game is already worth it but if you want to wait, keep an eye out because this game is by far the best heretic/hexen-like game we ever got. If you long for those games, do not hesitate !The only complain I could eventually have right now is how you do not find new weapons/spells or equipment after reaching the first half (or even 1/3rd) of the first area. There are 2 weapons hidden and you can still upgrade your weapons but it's costly (and for a reason, especially spells since they get so insanely powerful). Not a big problem but you keep exploring hoping to find some new toys and nothing shows up for so long. Pretty sure there will be plenty more to discover in the future but right now I could kind of feel a lack in that area.

If I unlock no vsync I get 200+fps, so for now I'm using vysnc w/ unlocked frames and its smoother ~144fps with less framedrops, minimal fan noise.I still have to move to a new area upon save load to remove the bug 60fps cap.)Pros:- Amazing art/atmosphere- Music matches levels well- Excellent level design (I'm ok with no map, it makes me observe environment, like OG souls games)- Shortcuts are well placed- Exploration rewards are quite satisfying- Weapon upgrades are fun- Combat while a little clunky is good and environmental tactic options are plentyCons:- Some treasure rewards still shoot into the walls/ ceiling.- Spawning in the city when you resume a save is tedious    (I backtrack to the city before exit to memorize my recent shortcut path)- I feel some puzzle solutions are arbitrary based on the hints. _childDocuments_.review: PLEASE READ THIS BEFORE PURCHASING:I recommend waiting for a full release before purchasing and playing this game. Why? Because updates to this game create soft locks that force you to create a new save. Taking a step back, this game used to delete save data every time you uninstalled it from your computer. I would keep it on my computer at all times for this reason, and months ago when one of the first major content drops came out, I was super excited that I got to go straight to the new content without having to play the intro sequence for the fourth time (at that point, including the demo). However, when I loaded the game up, it warned me that the update might have messed with certain parts of the game, and when I got to an elevator that was necessary to progress, it simply didn't function. I immediately uninstalled out of anger.A few months later, I was ready to give the game another shot. I started a new save and progressed an hour or two, but I had simply played the intro too many times and got sick of it very quick. I uninstalled it again.A few days ago, I decided to give the game one last chance to impress me. I had seen all of the major updates and all the cool new enemies, spells, areas, etc. To my surprise when I loaded it up, my save data was still there from the last time I had played, and when loading my save I did not get a warning that my game might be corrupt from updates. I was so excited that I was finally going to get to play the new exciting parts, and it was going great until after I beat a boss in the Archives. The area right after the fight was soft locked- I was not able to hit enemies, they would not hit me, I was not able to pick up the necessary key to progress, and I was even able to phase through some doors that were closed.I absolutely refuse to play up to this point in the game AGAIN. I have played through that sequence so many times and it is absolutely tedious. This is because of some other complaints I have with the game:-The areas are very big and very confusing.-Unrewarding exploration (No cool items, just health, mana, and ammo pickups. Rings seem to no longer exist early game, unless I simply overlooked them. They used to exist in earlier versions.).-Enemies are either extremely easy to kill by circle strafing and aiming for the head or snipe you with projectiles you cannot dodge most of the time and do massive damage.--The game will explain very little to you so you will just have to hope you explore exactly the right spot to find the item you must have to progress (this isn't necessarily bad, but it is infuriating if you are like me and have played through the areas many times and cannot remember exactly where you need to go OR if you typically like games to tell you exactly what to do with map markers).-Every time you launch the game, you are spawned in the city hub, losing considerable amounts of progress each time you save & quit. To get back to the point you were at last time you played, I hope you remember exactly what you were doing and exactly how to get there. Enemies also respawn.-I'm honestly not sure if this game will ever be finished. The last news update on the game was Jan. 11, and it wasn't even an update on the game as much as it was an insider look on how the map was developed.I could go on and on about my frustrations with the game. I want to love this game so much. I just cannot be bothered to play the same boring first 3-5 hours yet again. My recommendation is that you:1. Play the game co-op (I have never tried it so I cannot say whether the co-op mode is actually any good or not).2. Put a day aside to run through the game in its entirety. This game is not worth playing if you cannot play it through it one sitting.3. Simply don't buy it. Wait for a full release if you can.Edit:Don't even get me started on the puzzles. You will probably just end up looking up the solutions the same way most of us probably have. There's even a "simple puzzles" option in the menu, lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to give this a shot again to see if anything has changed or been improved - TLDR: my opinion is the same. The game is still incredibly aimless, repetitive in the wrong ways, etc etc. See below.--A frustrating try-hard of an FPS with faux RPG elements. The gameplay is pretty bland overall, and so is the audio at large. The more I play, the more complaints I have...Let's start with the enemies: on an easier difficulty, their health seems unnecessarily large for the so little ammo given. Even more terrible is that the damage they deal is extraordinarily OP.Then, the checkpoint system: a completely broken save point system that doesn't bring me anywhere near the last "checkpoint" that popped up. Even worse, I can't save on a whim like every other RPG and/or FPS, AND EVEN EVEN WORSE is that enemies respawn. Thanks for nothing: you're literally tripling the amount of effort for absolutely no payoff.So, you'd think with all of that, there would at least be a cool story or something to push things forward. Guess what? Nope: the directionlessness and abstract levels don't help. There's a complete lack of goals within the terrible architecture of the levels. It's baffling how bad it is, and how you're consistently bogged down by swampy water (SO SCARY).And ffs, I don't want to spend most of my time clubbing boxes and barrels to death like Donkey Kong in order to get mana or arrows -- this is excruciating.As for what seems to be a bug: I think there's this expectation or mechanic to use explosive objects frequently. Unfortunately they're very touchy and very glitchy - I've seen them explode into other rooms, or even trigger other explosives without any warning. In fact, just by moving them around I've made them explode, just for me to die... oh so fun!TLDR: You force me to waddle around in the terrible levels by constantly restarting them, fight off black plague zombies and monsters with little weaponry, and aimlessly wander about with little story to move things forward in any compelling way.This game is absolutely terrible. Go play CULTIC or something and you'll actually have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: GRAVEN is an odd title.It boasts superb level design, sounds great, looks incredible and has a lot of interesting mechanics. The game is, at the moment, only held back by the lack of a proper teleportation back to the hub, uneven difficulty which leads to loads of trial and error and tedious navigation due to the bizarre removal of the map.While navigating around is easy enough due to the outstanding level design, the backtracking becomes an issue when you are out of resources and need a quick fix back in town, leading players to '' return to the main menu '' and hop back in the game to get back to town in an instant.Having a map with some baked-in checkpoints that you can fast travel to once unlocked or having the traditional '' town portal '' would be a no-brainer to make this game much more fun.While some weapons are overtuned (the book that shoots sheets, once upgraded, melted the first boss in seconds) and some other just plain suck (the sword and the writ), the game offers a lot of interesting tools of destruction to play with.Overall, GRAVEN has enormous potential. It is gorgeous, fun, dark and incredibly fun to play. But as of now, its being held back by head-scratching design decisions.Devs, please consider fixing the following :- Spawn players with full HP, remove the gold loss penalty, but make death a teleport to the nearest checkpoint.- Remove enemy spawn unless players die or move to another area.- Add the map back. It's important to find those gated hidden secrets.- Buff some weapons. Don't nerf, just buff.- Add a mean of fast travel or teleportaton to remove the immersion-breaking quit the game mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven is less a boomer-shooter and more like Hexen 2 with a checkpoint system. You'll be hunting for keys, solving puzzles, and fighting your way through tons of enemies. It's a game that really punishes mistakes, can be pretty maze-like at times, and still feels incomplete.Overall, I'd say it's a 6.5/10. It's not awful, but it's hard to recommend without caveats (I'd give it a Mixed if I could). There are a lot of design decisions that feel half-baked and hold the game back. Magic is really only for puzzles, one of the weapons has a permanently dirty scope (seriously, was this even play-tested?), the stamina system only makes the game worse, and the inventory management seems like it came from a time when the game had more depth. This game really feels like they were going for an Immersive Sim, gave up, and released it as-is.While I still had fun with it, I think the average fan of the genre (what genre even is this?) won't enjoy it. The artists did a fantastic job, but pretty much everyone else dropped the ball.

_childDocuments_.review: After its announcement at Realms Deep 2020, I was extremely hyped for Graven! The atmosphere, the presentation, it was all top notch! That much is true for this early access version of the game as well. How it plays though is a whole other story. First of all, Graven is not a high octane action game. It's more moody, slower paced, and focused on exploration. That already might not make it some people's cup of tea. You'd be forgiven for thinking you were in for a different experience. The game is basically advertised as another boomer shooter, even sold in bundles with games like Ion Fury, when the two could not be less alike. The first couple of hours are a slog; you hit enemies with your stick and use your spell book to solve puzzles. The latter unfortunately never becomes useful in combat, which every player I've read reviews from found just as frustrating as me. But after getting a couple more weapons, and enemies become more varied, the game starts hitting a sweet spot. At its best, you're exploring amazing environments, finding secrets, and killing enemies by utilizing your arsenal of melee weapons and medievalized versions of shotguns and grenade launchers. At its worst however, Graven becomes one of those "where the ♥♥♥♥ do I go?" kind of games. Even though levels are large and detailed, there is only one path forward, so if you miss a door, a lever or a cog somewhere, your next 20 minutes will be about combing through the entire map to try and find that one little thing you missed.Also, whenever you decide to save&quit, the game puts you back in the starter area and repopulates all the levels with enemies, even resetting scripted spawn-ins. Basically, it punishes you even more for losing your way, and since there's already a fair bit of backtracking in the game, the issue compounds over time. You do have a journal and a map, both essentially useless: the map doesn't show you where you need to go first, or label most landmarks, and the journal only gives you the outline of what you're doing, locations or hints are sorely missing. They're more for flavor than anything else, but as a player you are in dire of direction.I wish I could recommend Graven. I love the world and unique take on a fantasy themed FPS (very distinct from Hexen or Amid Evil). When it gets you in the right groove, it's actually pretty enjoyable. But with all the getting lost, and replaying parts of the game over and over again, all the good points slowly fall to the wayside. There is already plenty of content here, and with the slightest adjustments and polish the game could essentially come out right now, but the developers seriously need to reconsider their design philosophy and some of their core mechanics first.
