_childDocuments_.review: So, I played this game from the very beginning. For those who don't have time or don't want to read much, here is my brief review: the game has seen many improvements over the time, and now it's totally playable and enjoyable. However it still has quite a few details that need to be polished. I would only recommend it for hardcore fans of the genre (Heretic, Hexen, Quake I, Daikatana, etc.). If I was to give a score from 1 to 100, I would give it a 70.OK, now for the details of what I've found:1. The hotbar system is quite a hassle. The staff and spellbook are bound to the bar, but they are mostly used for progressing and secrets, for combat there are better optinons. Why can't we replace them in the bar and take them out when we need them, like any other weapon/potion? 2. Also in the bar, the assigning/removing items is very orthopedic. can't we just mouseover the item and press the corresponding number to assign it?3. Who the heck thought that it was a good idea to remove the map? Older versions of the game had it, why remove it? It would be a lot more useful that the "Character" screen, that doesn't give any useful info. If not a map, then at least some waypoint system... some visual cue... an objetctive marker... a compass... I don't know, something to know where you are supposed to go.4. The journal screen is fine, just the text is too large, or the notebook is too small, so you have to be constantly scrolling to read the latest entry.4. In the bindings menu, it would be nice to have the option to assing two keys to the same action.5. In the bindings menu for the controller, can we get to assign hotbar items or menus like the inventory, notes, etc? I end up with 2-3 useless buttons in my controller.6. Less cryptic descriptions (e.g. we are never told that potions can be thrown, and their thrown effects are never explained).7. The gold lost by dying on Flagellant is WAY too high. Maybe nerf it and add a health/mana penalty?1. What's the purpose of the secondary attack of the staff? Apparently it pushes back enemies, but the effect is too low, the speed too slow and I see no difference when upgraded with the iron tip.2. The kinetic stone is cool, but costs way too much mana for what it's worth.3.  The short sword's 2nd upgrade, bloodlust... I see no difference whatsoever, neither in damage, nor range, nor speed.4. The discharge spell, when fully upgraded, no longer stuns enemies, they keep moving and attacking while convulsing. The "ball lightning" is also very erratic.5. There's a bug with the fully upgraded Inflame spell wih the zombies: they become inmune to it.6. What does the wirt of subjugation secondary fire do? It's completely useless.1. Those pesky one eyed, bat-like creatures... they snipe you from 1000 miles away and tear through your armor, and without armor you are very vulnerable. And if you are out of cuff arrow bolts, you're done for. Maybe nerf their damage?2. There's a bug with the metal collar cultists: if you stun them with Discharge and then attempt to get close to finish them they still attack you with their magic projectiles, which hurt a lot.3. Don't you think it's overkill to put those explosive throwing skeletons so early in the game on higher difficulties? I died like 3 times between the Lice Slough and the Brine Muskeg because of those f**kers.1) The achievement for getting all the shrines activates when you get the 1st one.2) The achievement for breaking 10 projectiles with the crystal candellabra doesn't workI think that's all I have so far. Like I said, good game for the fans of the type, and good work so far. I will continue pending of the patches and playing it once a while.I hope this review proves useful for anyone. Cya.

_childDocuments_.review: You know what? Screw this game.I have rarely seen a game so much at odds with itself, where the bad parts will constantly make you question if you want to go on despite the excellent parts, until eventually making you leave disgusted by the insanely off-putting decisions of the developers.What finally broke me:Got locked out of a ton of content because the game couldn't be assed to tell you you walk into a point of no return and automatically advances you to the next chapter upon beating the boss. Just so unnecessarily frustrating.Almost everything in this game is either good to excellent or bad to terrible.Let's start with the good:- The atmosphere and everything around it (graphics style, sound effects, soundscape, effects, writing) is possibly the best I've seen in a retro-styled FPS. If it is possible to do better than Graven in this regard, I don't know how.- The sense of exploration and rewards you get for it are excellent. Secrets aplenty with the best of them being hinted at, too.- Level design is truly well done. Again, it'd be hard to do better.- Almost every weapon is incredibly fun to use and upgrade.But the bad, man... the bad:- No map. And the levels are both open and HUGE. It has nothing to do with handholding, either, nobody wants a perfect map, but just SOMETHING to help you navigate roughly. There isn't a single good reason why a game like this shouldn't have a map.- Inane save system, truly abhorrent. When you die, you lose some gold and respawn at the latest checkpoint. Okay, fine. But when you "save & quit", any sane person would expect you to continue from where you left off.  But nope, instead when you launch the game again, you start from the hub - and have to spend minutes to get back to where you were, with all enemies respawned. What the actual f*ck...- Stamina system. Just why? A stamina system adds nothing to a game like this. This ain't Dark Souls, not even close.- Trash quick bar & inventory system. Some weapons take three (!!!!!!) slots in your quick bar. You are constantly in your inventory, moving weapons or potions in and out so you can use them. Oh, and being in the inventory pauses the game, so there is really no point to this whatsoever, the ONLY thing this does is waste your time.- Combat is often janky. Especially melee is mostly made pointless by enemies sliding or even teleporting around regardless of their animation state. And melee damage is incredibly dangerous, parrying with the sword cannot parry everything, so why would you ever do melee unless it is some stray easy enemy? Projectiles often get stuck in mid air, too.- Bugs, glitches, getting stuck on geometry. Despite a few years in early access, the game still feels like a beta sometimes.- THE GAME AUTO-ADVANCES YOU TO THE NEXT CHAPTER WHEN YOU BEAT A BOSS. No more exploring what you missed, side quests bye-bye. And of course no telling you accidentally walked into a point of no return.If the devs just got out of their own asses and added a rudimentary map with notes, fixed the save & quit, removed the stamina system, not auto-advance you to the next chapter and made all weapons just take a single quick slot space, this would easily be an 80% game despite the other issues that wouldn't be so easy to fix.As it is now, stay clear of this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Graven is a perfect example of a competently made game with a lot of potential completely undone by an incredible array of poor design decisions. It feels like the game doesn't know whether it wants to be a boomer shooter or an immersive sim so it kind of tries to be both and doesn't do either very well. It has the environmental reactivity and interactivity of immersive sims but many spells aren't very useful in combat. The level design is bland and tedious with weird interconnections that seems random and progression relying on finding hidden keys spread across the map and solving tedious puzzles, not to mention the insane amount of backtracking. Ammo/mana is scarce and mana levels seem to fluctuate for no apparent reason, so there is a focus on melee combat which isn't good, particularly because even the weakest enemies have this insane leap attack that makes it difficult to hit them without taking damage. Enemy design in general is annoying, especially those things that are basically cliff racers from Morrowind but with the ability to spit poison at you. It also has the enemy density of a boomer shooter so you have to tediously melee a ♥♥♥♥ ton of enemies. From what I can tell there is no map or even a compass so you cant tell where you are and you aren't always given clear directions or instructions in journal entries when taking quests. The game also has the worst quick bar I've ever seen because for some reason there are items that take up MULTIPLE QUICK BAR SLOTS if you decide to put them there. Acquiring new weapons and spells is painfully slow and some of them are even hidden, with none of the ones that I found in my time with the game being fun to use either. The game also doesn't allow you to manually save and has a monetary penalty for dying along with respawn and checkpoint systems that are confusing and don't seem to work properly, especially when you reenter the game. The cool art style and atmosphere dont matter when the game is just fundamentally unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I 'finished' the game. Definitely do not buy this in its current state. Act III is incomplete and a buggy mess. The game will softlock and prevent you from making progress unless you kill yourself in a specific location of the map (which the game punishes you for by depleting your gold btw). And because of the game's odd safe system, you can't just 'load' a previous save either if you get soft locked.I played the early access demo, liked where it was headed and was really excited when it finally hit 1.0.The level design and atmosphere are really well done  and the developers clearly took a lot of ideas and inspiration from immersive sim games like Thief, System Shock, BioShock and Dishonored, along with the art style of games like Heretic and Hexen. There is a a clear sense of art direction and the levels overall feel wide, expansive, and fun to explore, if sometimes a little empty. I love imsim games, I loved Heretic/Hexen, so naturally I really wanted to love this game.The game does NOT do a good job of telegraphing to the player where they need to go next or what needs to happen to progress - I spent an inordinate amount of time running around in Act II trying to understand what to do after I hit a certain point. This isn't fun. There also is no map you can access to see where you've been and where you need to go still. While the game doesn't need quest markers, having a map with the names of the different areas/places would go a LONG way in improving a player's pathfinding experience.The puzzles can be confusing as well, and the clues provided seem half-baked and inconsequential.The game falters heavily in its combat. It feels underdeveloped and unbalanced in a multitude of ways:-Weapons don't have satisfying sounds/impacts/animations, and they constantly feel like they don't do enough damage, even when upgraded-Melee combat in particular is tricky. When blocking with the sword, attacking enemies will oftentimes seem to hit 'behind' your shield's hitbox, thus making blocking pointless. They'll also randomly teleport behind you after you've hit them.-Enemy attacks difficult to gauge as they don't telegraph their attacks, and will often switch between being completely braindead to swarming you in seconds-The enemies also dish out a disproportionate amount of damage compared to how weak your weapons feel. Some of the late game enemies will deplete 50% of your health in one hit but they can tank an insane amount of damage themselves before dyingThe combat system feels like they wanted to make a boomer shooter first in the style of Heretic/Hexen, but then midway through development decided they wanted the pace to more closely match an imsim-style game, so they weakened the player and weakened the weapons but kept the enemies how they were.Also, the game has a very odd save system. There are checkpoints strewn about the playable area and if you die, you will respawn at your last checkpoint. But, if you quit the game and come back, you will spawn at the central hub again and will be forced to retrace your steps through the area all the way back to where you were. It can be frustrating and it eats up a ton of time. I can see having this save option available for, like, the highest difficulty possible, but for every other difficulty level it would be nice if the game simply loaded you back up at the last checkpointUltimately this game feels like it was created by highly talented level designers who wanted to create a thoughtful, grown-up tribute to both boomer shooters and imsim games of old, but otherwise didn't have enough time, budget, or knowledge to make the rest of it work well. I really hope that over time either the devs and/or the modding community can update this game with more bug fixes and gameplay re-balances, because this game has a TON of potential

_childDocuments_.review: First off I really love the idea this game sells. The look, feel, setting and walking speed all remind me of great games from the 90s. So that part is totally on target.What really surprised me is the state of the game in early access. I finished the content in under 3 hours for what is a lot more than the price of a movie ticket in my area. Much of that time was spent searching for some area or door to progress the game which is very extreme in this game. Sure old games had you find keys for doors, but this game actively hides doors from you without telling you where they are. Really frustrating!The combat is currently a complete non-starter. Every enemy can be defeated in the same way: Spam attack and side-step (A and D). That's it. Lastly there is a _really_ hard puzzle half way through the early access game which totally kills all the momentum the game built.Early Access has it's space in games and on Steam, but this game isn't much more than a vertical slice of gameplay at the moment. I suggest waiting until it's on sale for pennies or they have added an order of magnitude more gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- Combat feels nice and splatty (I feel like "weighty" is the term that's in vogue, but this is more splatty).  Weapons so far are all well done.- Use of magic as strategic control is fun, hope to see more options.- Unique atmosphere.  Really looking forward to more biomes.- The puzzles I've found have been pretty fun to solve.  Careful exploration and note-taking are rewarded.The Less Good:- Map design is pretty confusing at times.  This feels intentional, and while the exploration aspect is fun, there are some times where I'm doing a lot of backtracking because I either found a key, and don't know where the door is, or vice versa.  There is a map, but not the most helpful.  While I enjoy hunting for secrets and having options to explore, there are times where I think I'm missing the critical path.- Once you master the circle strafe, the combat gets pretty easy, at least for some of the enemies.  Dying doesn't seem to respawn enemies, so there doesn't seem to be any penalty for death.- Not a whole lot of character progression yet.  The game is more in the style of a Half-Life, so I don't expect too much of this beyond weapons, but something to add some depth to the combat would be nice.You may love or hate it:- Graphical style is unique.  I love it, makes me feel like I'm playing a game I would have gotten grounded for playing in the 90s.- Old-school sensibilities on things like health and mana (pick-ups rather than recharging).  Be prepared to smash barrels and explore to find money and mana.All in all I'm enjoying it.  If you think you'll fall on the love side of the love it/hate it stuff, I recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: So first and foremost: I DID not receive this for free. I am not paid by 3D Realms or anyone else for this review.What do I Think? It is awesome. I have waited on the ball park of 20-ish something years to play a game that gets the atmosphere and the nostalgia right. Now please understand that I know that this isn't finished. I firmly get that. I will be writing another review when It is finished. Now on to the good stuff.The movement is good, it is snappy and receptive. I genuinely put this early access through its paces. I have been coming up with new and inventive ways to move throughout areas faster and faster. It almost (not quite there) has the movement down like Monolith's Classic: BLOOD. By I say almost, its almost to that point where if I bounce just right I can move with speed and precision most of the time. There is some hangups I ran into, and I think that it is mostly just up to like edges getting caught up like a old watch with bits hanging out. Just needs to be smoothed. This was in areas where there were no enemies it was was mostly on down hill textures. The Weaponry Is really solid. I like the nice touches of differentiating when and which damage to use on what enemy to be most effective. For example: Living plague victims can get wrecked by the short sword, but take more than a couple hits from the staff. On the other hand, undead get bonked by the staff and are a pain with the sword. Makes an old gamer happy. The magic whilst limited, Is pretty awesome. Unique thinking outside the box and not making it just straight damage is a interesting choice. I like what the developers have done. The ranged options are pretty great too from what I've been able to ascertain. The explosives hit that sweet spot. The Environment is something that every dark medieval era could learn from. I say this because too often, it is either too cheery or there isn't enough in the environment to give a proper sense of dread. I like this and it is worth picking up just for the scenery alone. I enjoy the water mechanics that Graven gives but there is a bug that if you sprint to swim fast near a certain landing next to a sewer grate/waterfall, the game thinks you are running instead of swimming and will almost certainly kill you with no knowledge of this bug beforehand. It happened to me a couple times and It almost killed me twice.  My Suggestion? Buy it. It is worth the money. It is a great play through and from the work I've seen, It will only get better. I saw this game a while back through by someone in the U.S. Department of Special Corrections and I saw the gameplay and said i'll wait and See how this plays out because I'm a 90's shooter type of guy. As soon as it was in early access, I snagged it. So Happy. Early Access Review: 9.8/10 (Because of the almost death bugs)

_childDocuments_.review: If you do buy this DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE..On Sale ONLYIt's fun but VERY jank or it came out of EA a little to early..The save system feels consolitis , you can only save when you quit and exit the game.You also always start back in town..You get in area check points so if you die,  you don't start the map all over, but they punish you with losing gold ( and now you just drop that gold... hope you died somewhere you can go pick that up )The stamina system is only bad for exploring but only for about the first map ( for me at least  I found a few of the character upgrades )..The inventory system feels bad with it's a limited weapon slots and the first 2 taken up by your staff and mostly environment puzzle spell book ( if I can just go into my inventory at anytime and change what I have equipped  WHAT IS THE POINT of this)Upgrading items USUALLY means they do more damage, have more utility.. not hereThe upgrades feel BAD with a few exceptions and then the later in the game you go weapons don't seem to do enough damage..The weapon upgrades are mostly 1st upgrade is a right click ability and the 2nd is usually now not only do you need ammo for weapons you use mana every time you shoot.In order to upgrade spells you have to do side quests and what you get for that just feels BAD, mana is consumed WAY to fast, you can pick up 5 mana at a time when it takes 3-4 times that to do anything useful or you can waste your upgrade weapons/spells money for mana pots..that you can also throw for grenades? Yes, some enemies do drop them but I only found them in a certain areas of the end of ACT 1 and ACT 2 and it doesn't drop reliably enough.I've found some fun but know that going in this is NOT polished but at least for know they are trying to fix it....it's just slow going..edit after beating the game..In the games current state I cannot say anyone should get this..This has some very fun parts but way to many head scratchers..When you beat an ACT boss, you are instantly teleported to the next area..I went from Act 2 end boss surrounded by lewt and healing, beat the boss, showed up in Act 3 with 6hp..VERY frustrating..The worst for me was the Act 3 enemy that does not look finished..It does not walk towards you it slides on the ground like it's on wheels, then when it dies the rocket in it's pocket explodes and OFF IT GOES..If they fix most of the issues I will update this but know that if you do get it's VERY frustrating..I can see a good game in here somewhere under all the rush this out syndrome...

_childDocuments_.review: It takes six hits to kill the most basic enemy with your starting weapon. The first spell you get, lighting things on fire, is specifically noted to be bad for combat. You soon get a wrist crossbow that can take them out in three hits and is much more time efficient and safe. The second enemy, the big hulking beasts, take seven crossbow bolts and are so dangerous in melee that I don't trust the second spell's stun to keep me alive should I decide to try to lock them down and smack them with a melee weapon. The wrist crossbow has a max of 32 ammo. All the above factors led me to repeatedly run back from the lighthouse area through the available world sometimes as far back as the lice slough to pick up more crossbow bolts. This behavior massively dropped off once I got the short sword and could kill zombies in melee without it taking forever allowing me to conserve ammo.I understand the desire to make the early game feel like you're starting with nothing in a dangerous world but you need to consider that players will optimize the fun out of a game given the opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: When the game was in early access, I thought it had a lot of potential, so I bought it. Unfortunately I'm disappointed with the final version, the game still feels unfinished after so many years of development.For example, the developers promised to add a map, which didn't happen, and that's a big problem for a game like Graven with a large levels. The old games Graven refers to as Hexen always had a map.Also disrespecting the player's time is the need to always return to the starting position of the hub after finishing the game, so the area has to be traversed unnecessarily repeatedly. Just everything still feels unpolished, enemy AI is unimpressive, controls are clunky (although the game has controller support, it lacks the weapon wheel) etc. Furthermore, I encounter a lot of bugs even in the final version.The prolonged development and semi-complete final version of the game gives me the impression of an amateur product that does not match the basic qualities of a commercially released game.The world of the game has an impressive atmosphere and I still think the game has the potential to be decent, but the review must unfortunately be negative until at least the biggest problems of the game are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: NEWWell, goodness, I am glad to see a new update. Can't wait for the full game!(old)It has been a good while since any concrete word from the devs and any updates to the game. Even if it's a buggy level or a new enemy with unfinished AI - we need to see the game is being worked on. The full release of Graven was supposed to be this year. I hate to say it, but I am losing faith in this game and suspect this will be another crowdfunded, lackluster piece of vapourware that never got off the ground and was finished by another studio 10+years in the future.As of now, what I feel is me and a lot of other people bought an expensive demo of the first map of the game.This review is by no means a stab at the dev team. I think they are hardworking and responsible people. I do not know what is going on in 3drealms, but someone set the goals and workload too high for the team to manage in time. If it's about funding, same answer: goals were set too high concerning funding.I know it would crush the dev team and the players if this never got off the ground, but as the development and game is right now, I cannot in good faith recommend anyone buy it.(OLD)Played the demo and really excited for the full release.As 3drealms has shown a roadmap to the game's final release, I encourage you to show support if you are interested in "Boomer Shooters". The devs have shown in their recent patch that they can perform efficiently to address issues presented by the community.Still, I'll add: Buyer Beware. This is early access, not the finished product.A lot of issues have risen that were not in the demo.-sound in cinematics skips and pops in an ear-tearing fashion-strange frame-drops and stutter in various places-game doesn't save your graphics settings (sometimes it does, but then forgets the others)-obnoxiously long loading screens between areas (e.g. cruxfirth -> muskeg)-who thought up with the bizarro world save system? The current system doesn't add anything or make the game more difficult, it just forces me to restart the unfinished quest and go through the same area/baddies with the weapons I had acquired earlier from said area and baddies. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this by saying steam really needs a middle ground option for reviews, the game isn't awful, nor is it amazing, its in-between and that's... fine.GRAVEN is a first person """immersive""" sim with roots dug in by Deus Ex, System Shock, you name it, I don't think it delivers on that in its current state, and going by the roadmap presented on the steam page currently, ever. It's a fantasy game where you play a priest with access to magic, melee weapon/s and ranged weaponry, in the current build there's a handful at best of the full arsenal, two spells, three ranged weapons and two melee weapons, there's also only four quests which comes to my next point.Graven is currently only offering a decently sized map and quest chain that takes just under 2 hours to beat, which for a game asking for £19.99 isn't great, I get that it's early access so content will be missing, but 3DR's commitment, or lackthereof doesn't do much to persuade me otherwise, Ion Fury and Wrath, especially Wrath has struggled in their early access runs, little-to-no content, lack of updates, it's all pushed out at once and made the early access feel like a glorified paid demo, which if that's what 3DR wants then label it as such, not early access with roadmaps upon roadmaps which so far have both failed, GRAVEN's only had a single update in the 3 months its been available.Moving on, I came into GRAVEN negative, I didn't enjoy the demo, and hearing that the demo had more content than the early access build rubbed me the wrong way, I was reluctant to even buy the game in the first place, but I was surprised that I found myself enjoying the current build of the game, the combat's clunky, I don't think ragdolls are fitting for the game's graphical style, it makes everything feel *off* loses any form of weight something would have, and the lack of any gibs on enemies makes that whole system feel weird when decapitating an enemy to just walk into their head resulting in some huge blood splatter would be more fitting for something with actual gibs, not just a random blood explosion and... nothing, ignoring that, I found myself enjoying exploring the current map, finding the handful of decent secrets, two of which opened up permanent shortcuts, it made me want to keep going to see what I can find, there does need to be an incentive to go secret-hunting, I don't think healing items should be 'locked' away behind secrets, because I ultimately just gave up searching as a lot of the secrets weren't interesting to go searching out for, and with the current checkpoint system death is literally meaningless. The level design in the two areas, currently Swamp and Castle, were well designed with decent enemy layouts and a genuinely interesting look to them, even with them being generic fantasy areas, the artstyle's pretty eye-catching. Overall, I'm mixed, I found myself enjoying the game and it definitely needs work ASAP, but its a step up from the prior two games 3DR have released in this psuedo-retro lineup (Ion Fury and Wrath) it feels like an actual game one that has a genuinely neat future if 3DR can just sort out their early access management.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, my thoughts on Graven. I'll make it clear that, straight out of the starting block, I like this game. I like the style, the atmosphere, the intertwined levels; Early Access Graven has showcased a 'Dark Souls vibe' to it that I can't help but enjoy. I know this style of level isn't to everyone's tastes - the overlaying of paths/shortcuts could be a turn-off for some.However, for me, this EA release has shown me enough of Graven to look forward to its final form. That, to me, is enough. There is something sinister going on in the game world, and I do want to find out more.Now - things that I would weigh in on:The writing. I will have a bias here, due to what I do for a living, but someone has thrown in words they've seen in a dictionary and liked. I'm all for this, but a lot of polish is needed to make the writing shine.Combat. Combat in this game is a lot of the same; this is an EA release, and I am hoping we get more variety outside of step back/strafe then attack.Clarity. I had no idea I had finished all the content on offer. I spent a good hour wandering around looking for what I'd missed (at the instruction of an NPC). No - once you reach the library, EA is over. The random key required to access a door in the hub world isn't in the game yet.Weapon location. Just take them out of the Blacksmith shop for now; you find them in game. However, I also accept that this is EA and maybe some people haven't found them yet. The weapons do feel nice, though; I like the weapon feedback and design - looking forward to seeing what else we get and what spells become available.Music. The mixing on the music seems a little confused at times - activating combat music when there are no enemies, etc. I'm sure that'll be fixed.World design. Simply recommend some smog in the sewers and make lighting the torches important as a light source in dark areas! I'd love some rain/thunder effects thrown in too. I'm also hoping there'll be more faces (voice acting?) and accessible areas (such as some of the houses) in the hub world.Boxes/barrels. They are EVERYWHERE, allowing you to stay stocked up with no worries at all. Maybe they'll change the drop rate here. Now, blue mana.... why is it in this release? It does nothing.With all that said and done, I have high hopes for this game (I really enjoy Wrath) and look forward to the next update! Keep going, guys - I do feel like this game could be a real winner.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying it so far. I'll just go through the pro's and con's.Pro's: -Amazing atmosphere. Feels like another Hexen/Heretic game. Levels looked lived-in and then subsequently destroyed. Enemy designs and towns look good too.-Nice contiguous open world. Filled with secrets that are fun and not too hard to find. You can revisit areas with new powers to unlock more stashes-Weapons feel good. Smashing stuff with your staff and slashing enemies with swords feel nice and chunky. The shotgun ranged weapon thing has a really fun alt-fire -Runs like a champ 98% of the time. That's to be expected. Gonna try it on some Ryzen integrated graphics soon-I wanna buy drugs from that boat guy in the beginning and I hope he shows up again at some pointCon's:-Levels are a little confusing. It's a throwback to how a lot of these games were made. There's enough hints to get you though.-The first ranged weapon could already use a rework. It takes 7-8 shots to take down even a basic zombie. Maybe 4-5 with headshots. You can only hold 30 bolts so you're always better off with a sword and saving them for flying enemies.-I'm stuck on the third level puzzle. Not really a big deal but the hint I found wasn't very helpful.-Kinda wish the townspeople would do or say more. I get they're just filler NPC's but they could do more to help with the atmosphere.Overall, it's WAY better than Wrath and much more fleshed out. Definitely get this over that game. It's EA so changes are coming but what I've played so far is already worth the $20.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: 2 years in, Graven is still very much "whack boring zombies with a boring stick" simulator. Changing my recommendation, I guess it'll be always a shovelware title in my Steam Library and nothing else, it seems. Pity, the graphics feel really unique and cool.Original review in 2021:I don't know how to rate Graven. On one hand, it has cool lowpoly visuals that actually look really good, atmospheric music and feel. The worldbuilding seems to be promising, with level design, puzzles and everything.On the other hand, it's a pretty lousy start of a classic first-person shooter. I played this for an hour and all I really did was whack zombies with a stick. Each one takes about 5 smacks to go down and there was about hundred of them. So all you do is circle strafe. This is totally unsatisfying, if not to say incredibly boring. I learned 2 nearly useless spells and got a crossbow with extremely confusing trail particles. Still boring. Booooring.Classic first person shooters would  do that. Blood gave you a crate of TNT just 3 meters from the game start. Once you blew up the first zombies, you knew that this'll be an awesome ride.Duke Nukem 3D gave you an RPG the moment you left the roof of very first map. Hail to the king, baby!Heretic introduced Ethereal crossbow, a super satisifying alternative to a staple shotgun of those games just a minute into the game. And gauntlets to zap everyone, with heavy bass sound. Splash! Groans! Blood and gibs! COOL.You blew stuff up left and right, ripped and roamed. That's what I'd expect from a game like this. Not watching my ammo count.This terrible design makes "Graven" feel like it was one of those Japanese horror games with a revolver and three bullets and running away from zombies rather than blasting them to smithereens. Like Resident Evil. Except it's not Resident Evil. It's a retro shooter with no "retro shooter" part implemented.Why??? Why do you artificially limit satisfaction of playing a video game, dear developer? Just add difficulty levels and more enemies for those who want to feel ultra hardcore. Don't ruin a promising game by bad, needless overdesign.I simply wonder why all those neo retro shooters won't let player have any . Same problems exist in Ion Fury, Amid Evil or Dusk. Why? Perhaps you should play the real classics over again, and start taking actual notes?I  that developer thinks "oh, no, we meant magic to be used as utility only, it was never supposed to kill enemies, anyway. See, our game is super sophisticated and clever like this".  It's dumb as hell. From what I see, it's a retro shooter. Not survival horror simulator. Don't force your game into something it will never be. The lackluster AI, the whole retro feel, being niche already -- it's a beginning of a  shooter, plain and simple. So make it into one. You can either make a great retro shooter, or you could add niche design that'll just confuse and annoy people and never get anywhere. . If you're going to add a fire spell, it'd better make entire walls of it, like that firewall launcher from Rise of the Triad. Screw the tactical combat, nobody's going to buy Graven for that precise one bullet Rainbow Six or Swat4 experience. Seriously, nobody, ever.Old games gave you a ton of tools. Right away. And no, it wasn't bad or "too casual". It was .All the potential is there, but the feeling is not. I'm going to leave thumbs up, but I'm staying quite skeptical.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time playing through the game, but I have a hard time recommending it. I think this game deserves a rating towards the upper end of "mixed" here on steam, so I'm giving a +1 with that in mind.First of all, the game is a buggy disaster, especially in co-op. If you can't handle that, do not play.The implementation of co-op feels extraordinarily tacked on. Co-op players have no progression of their own, and instead get a carbon copy of the host's inventory each time they join the game. However, once in game, their progress is independent for that session, though it will be reset once they leave. Additionally there are many glitches, and at least several puzzles which could be bypassed with multiple players, and one puzzle which required the host to perform the solution alone for seemingly no reason.Looking past the glitches and co-op issues, the game is genuinely enjoyable (usually...) and has some neat ideas. It is very front-loaded in terms of design, so the first act is the most fleshed out, but the last half of the final act is a huge slog.Also yes there's a stamina system, it sucks and should be removed, but it doesn't *always* get in the way, and I was able to ignore it a majority of the time.If this *looks* like a game you'd enjoy, then you probably will, but wait for a sale. Co-op players should expect a rough time.

_childDocuments_.review: A movie can be "So bad it's good" but can a game? This is the question Graven seeks to answer.Heavily inspired by the Hexen/Heretic series, Graven is an RPG/Shooter hybrid with horror themes from the venerable 3D realms studios (the guys who gave us Duke Nukem 3D). This game is still in early access at the time of writing and it shows. Graven has alot of jank, but also alot of heart. - The enemy AI is currently atrocious. The foes in this game easily get stuck on the environment and often just run in the wrong direction. Sometimes they don't notice you at all even when your right in front of them. Other times, they can be found clipping through walls. In my opinion, this is currently the main flaw of Graven.- By cleverly stacking barrels and crates, the player can easily get out of bounds and achieve epic, game breaking sequence skips. (please don't change this because I LOVE IT)- IMO the inventory system is pointless and should be scrapped. just let me select weapons with the number keys without having to bother with a hotbar, like God intended.+ The graphics are pretty nice and the atmosphere is excellent. Character models look good even if the animations are a little rough. The art design is consistent.+/- The sound design is acceptable. It adds to the spooky atmosphere but i don't really have much else to say about it. It's fine.+ The level design is actually quite good (only occasionally confusing). Graven has big, open levels connected by a central hub (much like Hexen). Progressing through a level opens up shortcuts that make things alot easier on return trips. Something like a "town portal" spell would be a welcome addition.- The checkpoints are pretty wonky. Sometimes enemies gather at my current spawnpoint and kill me as soon as I respawn. The placement of checkpoints is inconsistent with some of them only being a few feet apart.- A million minor glitches. too many to list here. I haven't encountered any that are game breaking.In it's current state, Graven might not be worth the pricetag (pretty normal for early access TBH) However, with alot of love and care, this could wind up being a really great game. The developers just need to iron out the rough spots. Im excited to see the finished product. (assuming it ever actually gets finished....)

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like the third location and 1.0 were shipped out well before they were done. Plenty of minor bugs in the game throughout all locations (enemies walking in mid-air, mana refusing to regenerate, etc) not to mention in-game mechanics working incorrectly. As an example; I was unable to buy ammo for a weapon due to my inventory being "full" despite no indication of capacity or ammo requiring said capacity. The checkpoint system has spawned me in incorrect locations at times or even caused my death by re-spawning me next to enemies. These problems, you can encounter throughout the game. However, the third level is where things really go downhill. The level is huge and EMPTY. For a game based on secret hunting, it felt like exploring was actually a detriment due to how little was outside the beaten path. Overall, I am saddened, I enjoyed the beginning greatly but it failed to capitalize on the core elements of its gameplay, overall failing to create a cohesive story OR a consistently enjoyable gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: "At its very core, I don’t think Graven is a bad idea. The game is essentially Hexen 3 and that’s cool. The problem is that most of the design philosophy here is so rooted in 90s mentality that it forgets all of the advancements made over the last 27 years in crafting levels or balancing combat encounters. DUSK wasn’t such an amazing game because it copied Quake and called it a day. New Blood looked at all of the titles it loved growing up and bettered them. You know, that and DUSK actually works.At some point in the future, I could see Graven becoming pretty decent. It will never be a new age classic, but with polish and certain segments actually getting finished, this could be a fun enough game. There’s even a co-op mode, so that could be neat. Until then, however, I’m not sure I would recommend anyone play this. It simply isn’t in an acceptable state."Full Review on YouTube:

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, what a disappointment this game is currently. I have followed this game for over a year after seeing a very interesting teaser trailer. I really enjoyed the art style, the protagonist being a priest of sorts, and the hints at immersive-sim style gameplay. However, after playing this game for a few hours I feel I understand where the developers are going and I have many gripes; and a few positive things to say. TLDR:Performance: runs well, with some strange EA issues that are easily fixed. Gameplay: WAY TOO MANY BOXES? Strange design choices (see below)Puzzles: decent, but one stopped my playthrough completely. (totem puzzle wtf)*Overall: I feel cheated and this game is NOT fun currently.**booting up* When I booted up the game I was frustrated to find that the volume was incredibly loud and there were no options to adjust immediately, this seems to be a trend among games lately (or perhaps always) and it is truly frustrating to get your ears blasted to smithereens! Easily fixed though. The game also booted up in windowed mode which was odd. I adjusted the screen size and it worked well, but when I hit a certain resolution (I think one of the 3000 x ???) it opened midway between my first and second monitor. It was positioned in a way that I couldn't hit apply and had to force quit. Upon opening it was better. These are all minor issues solved quickly, but looking back it was kind of apt foreshadowing.*opening scenes* I was very excited to be in a new world with such a grimy, cool, fun atmosphere. I began doing what I saw in the trailer, killing boxes. Although, for some reason I had no magic yet and the trailer did. At first I was pleased to find a lot of interesting items in them. Then I realized the magnitude of boxes and breakables on the dock alone. It was staggering. I spent the first 10 minutes or so just breaking boxes because the min-maxer in me thought I might need these items, or that something special could be hidden! Nothing special here, just repeat items and a strange looting system that is my first major gripe with the game. There is absolutely no scarcity because there are pickups EVERYWHERE. However, breaking boxes can be slow and very much NOT fun. Monsters do not drop anything currently, so all pickups are from boxes alone.*combat* After awhile I entered in to my first areas of combat. I was disappointed to find this happened before I got any magic and was using a staff only. The staff is pretty weak. The combat at this stage has no blocking, so I thought it was a very shallow experience. Soon after I found my first magic spell! Oh, I was excited. Further excited to find that it read like an immersive-sim. The first fire spell is used to light items in the world on fire. Cool! It wasn't really useful in combat at all, but it felt fun to finally find a spell. Little did I know that for the next few hours there would be no spell additions. There are no levels in this game. There is no experience. Other games lock strong spells behind levels, for instance, but this game seems to lock them behind game time. Later on I discovered a blacksmith. Because I had gathered so much gold from boxes I purchased a sword. This sword was much stronger than the staff, and it had block too! I was beginning to think this game had all the things I was looking for. Later on I noticed that the combat coupled with the movement speed felt really off. It feels fun, but in a DOOM kind of way. I did not expect this, nor desire this, from this game. I was hoping for more of an RPG and unfortunately this feels, and is intended, like a fast-paced slash-em-up/shooter. This leads me to one of my other issues with the game, and/or the current stage of the EA. EVERY WEAPON PURCHASABLE FROM THE BLACKSMITH IS GIVEN TO YOU FOR FREE IN GAME, QUICKLY. This caused me to feel like I wasted a lot of gold, but also made the game feel disorganized. Was I meant to hold out and get these for free? Why can I  buy them early. No I cannot pick them up to sell, or something. They are just wasted if you already have the item. Really poor design choice.I quickly found that the movement speed was so fast that I could speed past all enemies with no consequences. I found that combat was pretty easy, especially after finding my sword, and that there were zero incentives to actually engage in or kill enemies at all. No experience, no loot, and in fact many areas do not require me to clear an area to progress.*puzzles* The core of GRAVEN seems to be puzzles. The combat can be ignored, skipped, and is in general pretty simplistic. Especially when one does not have much magic spells. These puzzles so far are not that difficult. There are standard tropes like a door won't open until you find a lever, one area where there is a pressure plate that you need to set a treasure chest on, etc. However, this is where the game completely broke down for me. There is a section about 1.5hrs in where you reach a large totem pole type of structure. It has 3 stones that make it up. There are approximately 5 sides to each stone. Throughout the level there are two pieces of paper with several symbols on them. The first paper is easy to find and practically given to you. The second one is on the floor in a room that has no purpose besides for the paper and easily skipped. It took me probably one hour or one half hour to discover I was missing a page. However, after finding the page I could not complete this puzzle without google. The given shapes seem to hold almost no bearing on the final outcome. This puzzle apparently makes sense to some, but through my eyes, even after seeing the puzzle finished, there is no logic that I can connect. My inability to solve puzzles is besides the point though. The true tragedy here is that the pacing of the game, despite having no meaningful magic spells at this point, was decently quick. It felt fluid to get through. This puzzle stopped this game in its tracks for me. I had killed every monster, traveled in circles numerous times, and even after finding the piece of paper I missed? Still the puzzle was not able to be completed. What a shame. *Misc.* The graphics here are fun. They have a good style and the character animates really well. The sound design feels good. The general aesthetic feels good and fits. There is one gripe that I'm not sure where to place. It seems that if you leave a zone for some time, enemies respawn. This confused me a few times because I thought I found a new area I missed, but I hadn't. This is somewhat minor, though, but where it really is bad is how the game chooses to save/load. Upon saving your inventory and items are saved, but your position is not. You restart in the town square. The game tells you this very early, but the problem for me is the respawning enemies. If you were a combat purist before and killed everything because you felt you should, well let me tell you. If you reload a game you will truly know how it feels to not give a ♥♥♥♥ about the combat or enemies. I loaded this game up interested in solving the totem puzzle previously mentioned, but upon loading into the town and making my way to the zone I was in previously, BEGINNING enemies had respawned. Every enemy (and even a door was shut that required a lever that I had previously opened) had respawned. This completely killed any hope I had for this game for me. This just makes zero sense to me. As previously mentioned, I see no real reason to engage in combat. The game gives you the tool (SPRINT) to avoid combat. Enemies seem to get uninterested after some time. The design choices seem to push you toward ignoring combat, but if that were the case, why respawn the enemies? Not to mention it makes the game feel cheap and arcadey. There is NO immersive-sim to be had where enemies that were in the very first dungeon you enetered respawn at every play through. This design choice sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it's early access and there's a lot of work left to do, but so far Graven is doing well at what it's setting out to be. What this game is, is Heretic 3 without being able to get the naming rights to calling the game Heretic. The problem with drawing the Heretic comparison is that many gamers haven't played Heretic 2 to understand why this ultimately feels like Heretic 3. So most people are going to see the Heretic title get thrown around and they're going to think "Okay, this is a boomer shooter that plays somewhat like an updated version of an old DOS classic I'm familiar-ish with." But if you really haven't played Heretic 2 then you're not going to understand how the gameplay of H2 was so drastically different from Heretic, but that this game really makes sense as H3.The developers are leaning very heavily on this understanding of the evolution of Heretic in order for players to get why this game claims that heritage. In fact, they even go as far as starting the game at a dock (both Heretic 1 and 2 did this) after a Half-Life inspired boat ride, but they also model the health pickups after the blue vials and pink bottles of the originals. I imagine that the full game will include weapons that feel more closely related to Heretic's weapons, even if the models have to remain "inspired"-looking. If that's the case then we will be in for a treat.Anyways, the game has all the regular problems you expect from an Early Access game and if you're considering buying it now then you need to just accept that it's not a full game. I see negative reviews that I feel aren't entirely fair for a game that's really aiming at a pretty specific audience to fully grasp it's roots and inspirations. So things like wimpy AI or enemy design are both intentional and things that are going to get improved upon over time.If you have a rough idea of what Heretic 3 probably would have been then this is your game. Just bear in mind that you really have to have played Heretic 2 to understand. If you've heard "Boomer Shooter" get thrown around and are expecting a fairly one-dimensional fast paced shooter that hearkens back to the days of Doom, Doom II, Duke Nukem, Heretic (obviously), et al, then you're probably going to feel let down. Unfortunately, I think you'd be missing out of an otherwise solid experience with that expectation. But, again, if you can see the design vision for this game, you'll love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm treating this review as a feedback for the early access version, so have that in mind.!Spoilers for the game ahead!The game enchanted me with the very first trailer with it's retro graphics and atmosphere. The idea of setting and gameplay were very promising. I've played many oldschool FPS and immedately I have noticed similarities for games like Thief and Hexen II. When I put my hands on the EA, it started great and went down from there. Thinking 3d Realms I was expecting polished expanded level or two like in case of Ion Fury, and I got that, except the polish ended after the first hour of gameplay. I got the feeling that the game is in state of crisis, the developers don't know exactly what it supposed to be - should it be more immersive sim with some enviormental puzzles or just a retro shooter? We talk with a few npcs at the beginning of the game, they even send us for a quest or two, but after that it's just a boring key hunt in latter parts of a level. The game broke me when after finding the key to a library it wouldn't let me progress because there were something to find in the level. What to find? The hell I know, because game says nothing about it. Nor the quest menu. I went back to give the game one more chance and after looking thoroughly I found a secret passage, that led to... the section of the level that I has been to before many times. A pointless shortcut! I gave up. So concluding my frustration I've pointed out my problems with the demo:1. Starting game with limited resources, no mana and small amount of health is good! The problem is there is so many resources laying around the game immedately allows you to stock up.2. Why are we collecting blue mana when we don't use it at all?3. Game sequence breaking - the door to a sewer at the beginning of the game should be locked with a key that town guard give us along with a quest instead of wooden boards that you can break and thus explore the whole place without concrete goal what to do there (I did that)4. Too many empty and pointless buildings. I don't want to explore a new and hard to find place just to find few pieces of ammunition or gold that I can find basically anywhere else.5. Why do we respawn at the beginning of the level when we exit and then come back to the game? This is so annoying, especially that every unlocked shortcut is closed again that we discovered during a quest, but didn't finished it before exiting the game. So what's the point in shortcuts at all?! I say less checkpoints (stacks with a skull and a crow) and ability to save and reload game at them.6. The fire spell was very promising - solving puzzles, clearing the cobwebs, lighting ene- NO. It's USELESS. The lore says that undead are straying from the fire. Haven't noticed after lighting every unlit lantern, just a waste of time.7. Why do blacksmith sells weapons that we can pick up later in the level? What's the point in gathering money then? What about some armor?8. Latter parts of a level are barren and empty. There's a tower with plenty of bolts for an arm crossbow. Thought that there will be some tough enemies to fight. Nope. Empty.9. There is a part of the level where the door require a key to open. The key is sitting next to it on a edge of a slope. I had hopes that either the ground will crumble beneath my feet into a swamp below after picking it, so I would neet to trot my way up fighting monsters along the way, or some enemies would spawn behind my back. None of that happened which was a wasted opportunity.10. The lighthouse quest - what is the point of it lore-wise? The game says it should bring some change regarding the undead banging to the gates near the town hall. I thought - Nice! It will allow me to open that gate and go to a different part of the town when the undead scatter! ...nope. Nothing changed lore-wise. Instead, somehow, you gain access to new sections of the map through sewers that were sealed off by the town guard before! So who went there to open the back entrance for you? Am I overthinking it?!11. Enemies - too much enemies that are too easy to outmaneuver and kill. Should be more projectile-based enemies, or enemies that react to your attacks by stepping back or to the side. Also - to "balance" the enemies, the devs decided for them to deal staggering amount of damage when they finally hit you. Uh, no. That's not how it should work. 12. Keyhunt - first of all - why? The latter portion of the level in the demo is being convoluted and there are points where it's really easy to get stuck, becuse the game didn't gave you enough hints on what to do or where to go. Big contrast to the beginning of the game.13. Breakable walls - the game gives little to none information about certain gates that can be destroyed after acquiring an item allowing you to break them. Then sends you to go and find those pesky barriers in earlier parts of the game for some unnamed reason, hindering your progress. Mind that the games that Graven takes inspirations from had those design problems as well back in the day. I hope we evolved as a devs and gamers alike to make those flaws nonexistent in modern games.This was my very first review on Steam, made in good faith and intentions to help in delevopment of the game. Thanks for reading :)

_childDocuments_.review: I tabbed out of my game to type this review, that's how bad it is.Fundamentally it's a good game, if you like Hexen and Arx Fatalis and the like you'll likely like this game.But whatever you do, do not buy it in it's current state, it quite simply is not finished and not enjoyable.The problem is the game is so buggy that a good chunk of the things that should work don't. In addition the puzzles at times are so obtuse that you're left wondering if the developer had anyone other than themselves sit down and play the game to figure out if their puzzles made any sense whatsoever. But the real killer is the bugginess combined with the obtuseness. I simply DO NOT KNOW whether my puzzles are bugged or I'm just not following the developers harebrained logic. I only really realised that this was commonly happening when I tried to do the slide puzzle and the pieces started sliding OUTSIDE of the puzzle but it's been a recurring theme throughout the game.I never know when I'm missing something or the game is bugged, so frequently I've had to look up online the solution to a puzzle only to realise the game isn't working as it should. There have been times when the game is working as it should but the solution is so dumb it's understandable I thought it was glitching.Do yourself a favour and wait like half a year or more to see if the devs actually fix their game, then consider this review a positive one. I get the feeling this game might have been forced out of EA by someone other than the devs, that's me being charitable to the devs because the game is good other than it being an extremely frustrating experience due to the bugs.Some other things to note: The performance gradually degrades to the point that it becomes unplayable, like there's a memory leak or something. You have to restart your game every couple of hours to get your performance back. _childDocuments_.review: Boy, this game has some issues...It feels like it's being rushed a little, which is quite odd for a game that has been in open development for so long. Yet it seems a few more months of that wouldn't have hurt.My experience is completely twofold - on the one hand, the combat is quite enjoyable and addictive, and the general design, athmosphere and lovecraftian overtones are excellent.On the other hand, the whole thing was still quite buggy and seemed to have cut obvious corners everywhere I looked, which broke the immersion and the fun every few minutes. Not to mention that you CAN'T finish this without a guide - which is hilarious for a game where there are no puzzles to solve. You just can't finish it, because you don't know what to do, again and again.Bugs I encountered:- getting my savegame corrupted TWO times, having to start the whole game again each time (I quit and saved, next time I clicked Continue my character is in the starting village, the play time is set to 0:00:00 and all items, quest-items and weapons are gone. The journal is still filled in and the items are missing from the game world, so yeah - no way of fixing this.)- items disappearing when trying to drop them, but there was a wall / earth hill in the way- pressable floor board glitching out, especially when previously activated and later loading the game and/or returning there- crushing walls not reacting to there pressable floor boards correctly in a trap room, these floor boards vanishing once I placed a metal barrel on themDesign flaws:- while traversing levels I always run out of stamina and then can't jump, meaning I have to wait on every minor step in my way for half a minute for it to refill- (especially in the first act EVERYWHERE:) triggers not being pointed out - so you fulfill a quest, then have no idea where to go and have to backtrack the whole level multiple times in hope of the shear luck to find that SINGLE ONE DOOR that now opened.- journal entries not being helpful AT ALL (this also got a little better in later acts), nor telling you ANYTHING plot related- journal entries revering to "This is..." without having ANY indication what is referenced, because the entry was generated a few minutes to hours earlier- journal entries sometimes just add one or two new sentences without indicating which, so its your duty to scroll all the way down each time and read everything AGAIN just to figure out the few lines that are new.- The plot being... not even remotely clear to me. I read every single text I could find, yet they were always so cryptic and littered with different special culty names / references that I never had a clue what I was actually doing.- end of acts aren't telegraphed (except the last one), so you could stumble in (as I did) without knowing and never finish your open quests for that act- no going back to previous chapters to finish remaining quests- weapons that were, as far as I could tell, absolutely useless - even when upgraded: triton and morning star- all staff gems being, as far as I could tell, absolutely useless, except for the white knockback one- no fast travel, so you have to traverse the same paths over and over again- no in-level save locations, so that you always have to walk to where you left off after quitting and continuing- no clear visual distinguation between usable and unusable doors- the whole get-the-machine-working-puzzle of chapter 2: it IS no puzzle. It is: "You need these parts, but we won't tell you. And they are all DIRECTLY HERE, so IF you know you need them - because you looked it up in a walkthrough - then there's no challenge." You literally pick things up and then put them down again. Then you press levers in ... SOME ... order. That's all just pointless, needlessly confusing-to-handle busywork."Why do I recommend it nonethesame? Don't know. It's charming, and could be made REALLY good after a few minor tweaks and updates. And even now it's already enjoyable, albeit in a kind of love-hate kinda way.So there you go.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Hexen Heretic hardcore fan, I like this game but to those that didn't play any of Hexen/Heretic Series, this is probably not a game for you.  Hexen 1 and Hexen 2 are very different game. Although both are from the same series, Hexen 1 is action-combat + puzzle solving while Hexen 2 is mostly puzzle solving. Certainly there is combat in Hexen 2 but not as much as Hexen 1. Graven is more like Hexen 2 than Hexen 1, so if you are looking for Hexen 1 style, then this is probably not a game for you. Do I enjoy the game? Yes, because I'm a hardcore fan of Hexen 2. I just hope Graven's combat is more engaging and have more interesting spells. Do I endorse this game? It's a tough question. I kinda lean more towards to Yes? or maybe No? hahaha I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: Big potential...but flops hard. The theme is great, the graphics look appropriately old school and grimdark but man the gameplay is such a hot mess. And the level design is horrendous with zero to no help. Naviating menus and inventory is a pain and there is no good way of managing the hotbar. Game forces you into melee combat but FPS melee is notoriously bad and it is exaggerated by the animations and whacky hitbox. Since it takes the "souls like" approach to save, but has just one central save system, you cannot play this game in bursts. You have to stick your ass in the chair and hope you can figure out where to go before you inevitably have to quit the game. And then bam. Back to the starting location, with  none of the resources refunded but guess what...enemies have respawned. And the magic system is nonsensically nerfed with the mana depleting faster than you can blink. Why? Maybe there is a great pick up later on into the game that really overhauls your mana pool. But I had absolutely no patience to find that out.Still a cool concept though. If 3dRealms can fix a few issues, give some much needed quality of life changes I might try again but for now. It is a no recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game with some issues, but one of them being the biggest. That being that I am unable to finish the game. Not because it's difficult or anything, but because I am unable to trigger a boss fight after you complete The Gorged Dunes mission which lets you into the settlement in the area that is blocked by a magical barrier.The art style is phenomenal, the combat and weapon design feels great, the atmosphere is amazing, but I was physically unable to finish the game due to an, apparently, frequent bug preventing me from progressing though the story in the third act of the game.The first act is great, but the second act is rough. The enemies are unbalanced and the areas are confusing.The third act was even worse, not in layout (it was better than the second act, in my opinion) but in how buggy the game is here. When you pull some of the levers, you are unable to see what's changing which leads to a lot of confusion when you go out to look when you might not have been paying very close attention to the environments previously. The same levers change orientation when you exit and resume the game later so you're not sure if you have to pull the lever again.Even with those complaints, I was mostly enjoying the time I spent playing this game so it's unfortunate that I can't finish it. Maybe I'll pick it up again if this bug ever gets patched (I've seen some people saying you just quit the game and launch it again to magically appear in the city, but that has not happened to me), but as of now I'm abandoning this game and can't recommend it as of now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it, but could use a few QOL features. The lack of these features doesn't make it a bad game, it's actually a good game with flaws, many of which were fixed with a patch in the first few days after release. If you're used to playing indies you can typically overlook this and power through, but if you're not, you're probably one of thousands of players who dive into every game expecting perfection and will be pissed. This game is like fast food or your neighborhood diner, not fine dining. Walk in with that expectation and you'll find it rewarding.Good:1. Action pacing is unique. Starts as a survival FPS, kind of soulsy, but generally you're circle strafing and meleeing and trying to keep your health up. Go back and get explosive barrels when you see them. Spells blow but have their uses (fire can quickly blow up all the barrels so you can loot easy.) No spoilers, but by the end it's full on boomer shooter, but frankly with way more options. Sure, not all of them are optimal, but I ended the game really only ignoring maybe 3 or 4 tools, but using the other 8 or so?2. Exploration is rewarded. This game has a lot of secrets and unlike some much bigger games many of these secrets are worth it. Most of them are gold, but gold is relatively scarce so you're happy to find it. Holding E will pick up loot by the way.3. It's well written and monsters are mostly well balanced. I usually hate boomer shooter storylines but this one was fine. A little convoluted and sometimes too wordy (lol, "Palimpsest") but pretty fun and engaging enough.4. Gameplay is good but hard if you're expecting to rush in and win with dexterity alone. Stamina is kind of an issue early on but as you find shrines it becomes no issue. Stamina is more like extreme fatigue - once it's draining, then your attacks will drain it but if it's not draining then they won't?Bad:1. Buggy. Might be resolved but you can get stuck in a foot of water. There are little ways out of stuff, like you can sprint jump out of deeper water, or just save/load warp home but there are some goofy things going on. Gold gets stuck in walls. Enemies can sink into levels. Sometimes this works in your favor, like when a miniboss got trapped in a wall. 2. Loadout is unbalanced. You can do a lot of stuff with what you're given, but some of the items really are just trash. Of the items I ignored, some of them were for good reason. By the time it's a boomer shooter, do I really need a slow and vulnerable melee weapon? I don't know. Maybe on the harder difficulties you really do need to resort to it but at that point the balance issues are probably magnified. Normal mode was fine.3. Collect-a-quests are repeated. I don't need to find 3 gears 3 times in this game. Especially when you don't have a map. I don't think the lack of a map is game breaking, but it can become incredibly frustrating when I need to find out what I've missed. Some of the required areas and items are pretty obscurely hidden, which means check everywhere. Exploration being rewarding is a double edged sword when I need to explore extensively to continue.4. Lost or dropped ideas and poor level pacing. It's pretty apparent they released this game before they finished everything they wanted to. You get a lot of mechanics that seem like they're going to be used in puzzles or in a metroidvania sense but you really don't end up using them much. They exist as a puzzle mechanic for like, 1-2 puzzles and then you never do it again. The last act straight up has dead zones (some you can get stuck in) that look like they were intended as content but then forgotten, and some NPCs that don't even have dialogue. The devs were probably going in a lot of directions here and it shows. Ironically, some of the later trap areas could probably be resolved using these mechanics but aren't solvable that way.

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing a boomer shooter, but i watched some on Youtube. By the looks of it, Graven is a much more nuanced game, with metroidvania elements, so kudos to devs. Loved Act 1 setting, i decided to play the game because of it, as i am a fan of dark fantasy. Unlike many of reviewers, i really enjoyed 'return to hub' system, with enemies respawning in smaller quantities so that you can replenish resources and also not run around in empty locations. Enemies and combat are okay, especially throwing dudes with kinetic crystal. What was very unexpected - difficulty. I ended up playing on difficlty level 1 out of 5, because even on level 2 i was constantly dying. I have never experienced such problems with games before. Also, 3-slot weapons make you constantly switch them in inventory. Seems excessive to me. Other than that, i find Graven very enjoyable for this particular genre.P.S. Having said that, i am definetely never playing boomer shooters again. Yes, it looked interesting on screenshots, but after 30 min of gameplay the fascination wears off and it becomes just painful to the point of 'Why the hell am i wasting time on this? It's not an arthouse game, it's a very simple shooter with hideous graphics and design'. But i'm just venting, sorry, it's my take on the whole genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Game that starts really good with a nice art style that invokes nostalgia of past 3D games quickly turns into a slog.Congratulations devs - you made magic boring. That is an achievement. While the Steam capsule portraits main protagonist casting a spell, it is really useless to use spells against the enemies. To an extent it is possible to use upgraded fire spell in the first chapter but it will not work on the basic enemies. So we revert to staff. Spells? Spells are only for puzzles. I wonder why spells then? Why not some device instead?Congratulations devs - you made melee combat boring! While we have staff as our initial weapon, we gain a sword as well and several types of crossbows during the gameplay. So the priest that we might thing is supposed to cast spells and occasionally use spells - no! It quickly becomes a shooter game which is totally normal and expected role for a priest to slide into.Chapter transition - it is horrible! So I just finished the chapter 1 and I didn't knew that I am about to fight the boss of chapter 1! OK - deal with it. So I defeat the boss and there is a cutscene which immediately puts me on the map for chapter 2! Wait a minute - I had few unfinished quests that I wanted to finish! Nope! This is most disgusting way to transit into the next chapter without asking player if player wants it!Map - map is NEEDED for the game like this. Levels are nicely designed but very convoluted and quite big! So often player has to revisit places over and over in attempt to check if something is missed. Map - map solves it. And there are some fans that say map is not needed - good for you if you don't need a map, don't use it. There is a myriad of players needing a map!Difficulty - it is TES4 Oblivion all over again. Enemies increase difficulty based on how many other enemies you kill. It is well known as the worst leveling system but here we go again. In Chapter 1, I had all my weapons maxed except useless spells - spells are 100% useless against the new enemies, new enemies hit hard, real hard ans swarm player real quick. So in chapter 1, I have found only one eldrich feather and upgraded flame spell. My lightning spell could hit only one enemy in chapter 2 to stun and other swarm me quickly and kill in 1 or 2 shots. Btw if there was a pillar to increase health in Chapter 1, I have missed it because I got only mana and stamina ones and game pushed me in Chapter 2 without asking.I bought this game while it was in early access as I saw post on reddit and thought it might be interesting. I regret it now.
