_childDocuments_.review: I like the art, I like the setting, I like the story, but the main gameplay loop was not for me. It feels legitimate to warn others: it is based on REPETITION of ATTENTION, MEMORY and TIMING SKILLS. This is like learning to perform card harder and harder regular card tricks with a timer, and there is not a lot of room for mistakes, and be certain that if you don't like the first 30 minutes, it will only get worse for you. If you love it right away and only wish it gets more complicated and challenging, be my guest as I pour you French wine. Otherwise, too bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: While I've played a lot of roguelike deckbuilders and some online CCGs, I never had much familiarity with traditional playing cards. But after playing a ton of Balatro, I picked this game up after looking for more card-related games. It's really excellent! The cheating techniques start off relatively simple and escalate to a delicious level of complexity making them really satisfying to comprehend and execute correctly. I was expecting this to be more of a MKB type game and I was somewhat surprised by the game's recommendation to play this with a controller. But as you keep playing the game the reason becomes clear -- the game is as much about executing the cheats with stealthy dexterity as it is about understanding the sequence of cards and how to arrange them. On a gameplay level, the satisfaction of executing some of these cheats is comparable to executing a series of successful parries in Sekiro or notes in a rhythm game.I was also really surprised by how good the story and atmosphere was. It puts you smack dab in the middle of the 18th-century France. The setting is impeccably realized with great art, witty writing and good music. There's a ton of eye-popping drama and some surprisingly funny art and dialogue. I found myself giggling a lot in many scenes.As an experience the game far exceeded my expectation and I recommend it highly.P.S. I really liked the difficulty curve of the tricks, but it can sometimes be frustrating to repeat an entire sequence of trick repetitions after messing up one step. One solution for this is to quit to the title menu if you know you messed up in the middle of the trick. It will let you repeat the trick if you go back into the save without loosing too much progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I wish I liked it more. At the end of the day the game comes down to sequence memorization and not making any input errors while under pressure. It's fun learning multiple card cheats that seem to reflect real life strategies, but ultimately I feel like this game wastes a lot of time due to not following any sort logical probability. If I screw up a cheat and deal the Comte two kings instead of two aces and I deal the mark a pair of twos, I lose the hand. If this happens to be once the stakes are high and I can't afford to cover the minimum bet, that means I go back to the world map and have to do the whole sequence over again.If you screw something up in a cheating method, you usually have to walk through the entire doomed sequence until the hand is lost and start again. I don't mind being punished for mistakes, but I'd rather the punishment be swift instead of my time being wasted. When you're better off hitting alt+f4 and booting the game again instead of following through there's something in the design that's off.I like the story and the art design, the music fits, and I really like the premise but I feel that the gameplay doesn't live up to what expectations I built up from seeing the first trailers. I enjoyed the minigames that are involved in the various cheating techniques but by the end of it they started to either feel repetitive or frustrating. One errant card dealt and I'm often left walking away from the table and sitting through a handful of load screens and dialogue before being able to get back to the game.I'm glad I bought the game and to clarify my positive rating, for me it's somewhere around a 6.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark is a game set in historical France, following the story various con artists who are out to run scams and unveil a conspiracy that is happening in the upper ranks of the kingdom. For this, the game teaches you quite a lot of scams you need to employ and execute correctly and includes some quite dangerous and risky games (and other scenarios) in which you need to win money and get the information you want before your opponents get suspicious.Visually, I am completely impressed with this game, I honestly didn't expect that much when buying the game, but I found the art style and level of polish quite impressive. The game has tons of unique animations and feels very lively and well-designed and it's really good at creating unique atmospheres for about every place you visit and the soundtrack was amazing too!The narrative starts rather simple, but as you progress through the story quite a lot of unexpected things start to happen and the story went from being engaging enough to keep playing to me finishing the whole game in a day because I wanted to know how the story would shake out.The narrative told is also a really immersive expierience, where getting the information you want feels very earned and the story knows how to build tension. I also really loved the idea of a mute protagonist, because it felt like the writers genuinely explored how a character like that would exist in the world and it wasn't just a cheap gimmick to explain why the game protagonist didn't have speaking lines.As a smaller criticism I felt the game sometimes communicated some controls in a rather unintuitive way, which never really was too frustrating, but it took me quite some tries to get a few things right, like e.g. I only understood how sword fighting was supposed to work after 4+ attempts. And I like that the game offers you a tutorial for these moments so you arent killed 4+ times in the story (as death isnt just a "try again" state), but this creates another problem, which is, that you expierience a constant feeling of "Still Being In The Tutorial". This isnt as bad as it sounds, but after a while I grew a bit exhausted of learning more and more techniques (there are 28 techniques to cheat at the game, which you get introduced to through the entire story), and I genuinely would have sometimes wished for the game to only have ~15 techniques, with more of a focus on "getting better" at the techniques and improving your interaction time with them, since some of them felt a bit one-off and gimmicky (or even if they didn't, while I liked almost all of them, I just found them to be a bit too many, you literally get the achievement "Complete All Tutorials" when there are only TWO games left in the story).But what I really liked is that, even though the game throws a lot of tutorials at you, it never just hands you the answers while actually playing or is otherwise patronizingly giving you hints - you need to be smart and fast and adapt cryptic hints and shuffle cards to fit the order of these cryptic hints and that honestly felt really good, because while I wished there would have been an additional chapter or so after you are finally done with the tutorials, you weren't REALLY in the tutorial anymore and the game would at times get really mean (i mean that affectionately)I especially loved the techinques that forced you to think on your own part about a strategy to improve them and execute them as fast as possible and I think the combination of all available techniques made the games feel like pulling a con really was a bit of luck, a bit of logic, a bit of forsight, a bit of strategy and a bit of dexterity, and you always also had to look out for your opponent and I thought that the game really was just right when it came to difficulty for me. I still felt like some techniques that were more QTE-based really didn't feel very accessible or incredibly fun to me - I am not in any way physically disabled, but i still struggled with the hand-eye-coordination / exactness the game wanted of me, so I feel like a person who might actually have some impediments when it comes to controlling games will find some sections quite frustrating.But generally I found the game and the mechanics (especially in combination with the story) really enjoyable and I felt like I was in that one type of anime where every conflict is solved by winning at card games and everyone in the universe just adheres to this rule without question, the jobs were never too easy to pull or too hard and I was super hooked on finishing the game. And I wholeheartedly loved the last 2 games where the stakes are super high and you need to pull of the biggest con you did until that point. And that is to say that while I think this game has some minor flaws, I want to empathize how much I loved playing a game that aimed (and very often succeeded) to be so full of innovative mechanics, I really wish there were more games that would do stuff like this instead of adhering to more well-known formulas.tl; dr: Card Shark is quite an unconventional game in a lot of ways, and I really enjoyed it! All of that innovation in mechanics comes with some rough edges at some points in gameplay (especially a lot of tutorials), but I still generally think that the game tried to handle these problems as gracefully as they could. If you think that sort of game is for you I can really recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a really great promise. The movie "Barry Lyndon" by Stanley Kubrick is indeed my favorite Kubrick film.BUT - the game falls woefully short of its vast potential. It *really* is nothing more than a glorified QTE-fest (Quick-Time Events, push button X, Y, A, B quickly). You need to complete various QTE's in succession, or fail the game - with permadeath. Even on "easy mode" ("Dilletante" difficulty), it's harrowing and frustrating. I can not in good conscience recommend this game, which is a real pity. If the game was based less on "dexterity" (QTE, though I would posit that true "dexterity" is only appraised in VR), and more on brains - it would be interesting.Pros: I like the art style and the music.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has astonishing art and a well-made story line! I thoroughly enjoyed the funny moments between characters and the main character feels full of life. If there was more game to play, I would definitely play it just to squeeze a little more time enjoying these silly little painting friends interact with each other! If you're interested in this game, I'd personally say it's 90% worth your money!That said, some big improvements could be made -1. Make a practice mode! I'd love a place to practice specific techniques in to get the controls down, especially when going for the "don't lose any games" achievement.2. Make a chapter select for completed files! Once I'm done with one run, I'd like an option to go replay specific chapters to see the different choice option dialogues!3. Make the ending more easily re-playable! I don't want to replay the ENTIRE game to see what an ending looks like. That's hours of repeating game play to slog through for one ending.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:The variety of strategies available is unexpectedly fun to learn and master.The visuals.The story provides an interesting setting and motive to improve your skills.CONS:The player is often limited to specific methods of foul play during each mission, which can be disappointing at times.The winnings earned from each game are almost only used to play more games. (Except during specific events)Dying in the game has little to no consequences when playing on normal difficulty. (Which is a shame, since cheating death itself in a card game sounds like a thrilling way to escape the fate of your own making.)Some cheating methods are criminally underutilized while others can overstay their welcome.The suspicion bar (AKA, the SUS-Meter) often betrays the opponent's depiction in the story. (For example, you can pass a card in front of a mirror for 0.000001 seconds and the meter will jump, while holding one half of a riffle shuffle for four seconds too long will not gain any attention.)

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark is okay. Mid as they say. I wouldn't recommend buying it until it gets some polish and re-releases as a "definitive edition" thingie.The game has nice art, music, and atmosphere. It's easy to immerse yourself as your char and just go with the flow.The bad points:1) Death is kinda handled badly. If you're gonna propose a Perma-death feature in a game about taking risks, but then make you grind narration boxes to get back up to your point of progress, you gooberd up. You can't fast-forward narration. Animation. You have to painstakingly re-do the entire game. It made me just quit instead of retry. Especially since this was my first mistake in a, what I would consider, low stakes environment. It was shown to be the "grind money" area (barn). Sure if I messed up when people with guns and swords were standing at the table, fine, but in a stable? With some easy cash? Just yoinked me out the experience so hard.2) Controls feel finicky. The game in the end is just a dexterity check. Every trick is about doing stuff as fast as possible. I didn't feel like a smart rogue, I felt like I was playing Cooking mama on expert. "shuffle the cards, jog 3, index, shuffle again until done" The game rewards speed over mastery, and punishes you with death. I can count the times i was "thrown off guard and had to think on my feet" on a single finger, and that was when the ship was moving so the board moved.Maybe this comes up later but having the opponent also cheat and you being able to notice and counter said cheat would've felt amazing. Especially if unprompted. What if my cheat didn't work at a location but if I go back and look CAREFULLY at the animation I can see their hands revealing information being passed on while I was dealing? Stuff like that.3) Pace. The game's pace feels very disorganised. Alot of tutorials and learning of new tricks and not enough time playing around with the tricks. Doing the same trick over and over and learning a way to get better at them is rewarding. A monkey-see, monkey-do repeating and moving on to next tricks for 12+ tricks in a row gets old fast. The only trick I "mentally evolved" at was the one where you have to remember which 5 cards you picked. Imagine that but then they suddenly add a player to a table, or remove one. All in all, fun experience, worth checking out on a rainy wednesday, but not something to buy right now or you'll regret passing on.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot, but the methods of cheating can be a bit tricky sometimes and when you go for a little bit without playing it you easily forget everything and the instructions aren't enough to let you go along.Nevertheless, it's a really interesting game and I enjoyed it a lot. It infuriated me and made me frustrated af which is not something most games can do (that's a good thing). The art is just incredible and I really like the two main characters as well. _childDocuments_.review: Great little hidden gem. Let's you cheat at cards using the real tricks used by card sharks back in the day. It is fully possible to screw up a cheat, and sometimes even possible to recover from a screw up! As a fan of magicians this game tickled my fancy greatly, and let me live the fantasy of being a master of slight-of-hand.The story is engaging but not outstanding. At certain points I became quite lost about individual characters motivations, but I think that was intentional. Would only recommend the game if you find the gameplay compelling, because I don't think the story will carry the game for you otherwise. Overall though I personally rate it highly!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark certainly left me feeling swindled...The visuals are gorgeous, the music exceptional, the writing sharp. I just wish the gameplay loop didn't suck so bad.Behind the vignette, Card Shark is a repetitive set of overly convoluted mini-games that is plagued by a complete disregard for "quality of life" at every single turn.A lengthy tutorial before almost every section, unforgiving gameplay, rewatching unskippable cutscenes every time you fail, unclear puzzles where if you guess the devs' intent wrong - you start the entire level over, literally no support for creativity or fidning alternative solutions (you have to do tricks exactly how the game wants - it doesn't actually have a deck simulation going on), etc...I like text-heavy games, I like challenging games - but this one tested my patience far more than my skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to love about this game but it has three fundamental flaws that overshadow everything else: 1. The inputs are EXTREMELY janky and unpredictable. Some of the minigame gestures can't be done consistently with the mouse due to lag (e.g. 3 card monte for money and some of the signalling cheats) and others can't be done consistently with the controller (e.g. the false cut). I've been alternating this game between my laptop and my Steamdeck so I can have the most predictable controls for the right gambit but it's maddening.2. You can actually get stuck with no way to progress the story and no way back because of a single save slot. I've had this three times at different places. I could sort of overlook this if the gameplay was smooth and satisfying but see above. It's disheartening to have to start from scratch again.3. The pass/fail nature of every single cheat is unrealistic and takes away the magic. When you, say, mess up a stacked deck in a round of cards, the storyline shouldn't grind to halt and your character shouldn't die all the time, just let us lose the money for the round and play again, as you would in real life... as long as the marks don't have a full suspicion meter, the game should just continue as normal with no one realizing that the cheat messed up a move. Instead, the game goes out of its way to punish you for every mistake with repetition of sequences and lost time.It's a diamond in the rough that works hard to do justice to its premise but falls short because of the above, especially the input problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game with a pretty exciting system for cheating at [unspecified card game]. However, instead of leveraging that system to produce an exciting and player driven challenge, it is used to set up quicktime events that sideline a story. The story, though interesting, carries that interest only through moments where every hour a new character shows up and adds an extra twist to the narrative with little character depth, and pretty much no player agency. Even at a 50% discount, I felt a little 'cheated' of the depth of the experience.---(A bit more on the gameplay)Unlike many of the negative reviews, I found the controls to be totally fine. The gameplay is great, especially in the sections where you set yourself up to sneakily shuffle the deck to be dealt exactly how you need it. I was just waiting for the moment that the tutorials would end and I would find myself making the calls on how to win.At one point in the game, you are given access to a repeatable challenge that can give you money. This is intended to help players who might've lost a few times to recover the funds necessary to continue the story. However, these repeatable challenges also gave you agency over which cheating strategy you used!Then, 5 hours into playing the game, I get an achievement "Complete the last tutorial of the game." and I am so excited for the game to finally start! And then, 30 minutes later, it ended.As I played I realized two extra things: the deck is rigged to make your strategies work every time if executed correctly, so there is no value in trying to 'make a hard situation work anyway in a creative way'; and the game only checks if you executed the steps in the strategy correctly, so there is no value in creating good hands in ways the game did not intend.If [unspecified card game], was defined more fully, and the game allowed to play with a truly random deck and with real player agency, then such a "gamemode" would probably get as much interest from me as the 5-hour tutorial (with story attached).

_childDocuments_.review: As a magician, this game is amazingI will be a bit afraid of revealing the secrets to layman, but this game is doing such a great job to make the slight of hand into an actual way that you can play with.I understand that the tricks and slight of hand that show in the game are those you can easily find in Youtube or anywhere, so this should less harm to the community of magician.But indeed, the music, the way to play, are all making this game as an Art.If you were a magician, I will highly recommend that you should try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very unique genre-less experience.Technically it's a card cheater simulator. It does most of the job for you but it never feels like you're just doing quick time events, it's all very tactile and connected to what you see on the screen. I don't want to say more except that I think this game should be played with a gamepad. If you are worried about the stress of doing card tricks it is indeed stressful, but the game is benign, and if you switch to the low difficulty it will even offer you a free win if you're having problems, so you will never get stuck.There's also a story and presentation, and they're all delightful and authentic. It is a Picaresque novel and authenticity is only tarnished by forced entries by famous historical figures which feels cartoonish. It short and nice, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark is nothing short of a masterpiece.♥  ♣  ♦  ♠  ♥  ♣  ♦  ♠  ♥  ♣  ♦  ♠  ♥  ♣  ♦  ♠  ♥  ♣  ♦  ♠When I first began playing this game, I thought it was just about cheating at cards; I was surprised to find swordfighting, great dialogue, a beautifully orchestrated soundtrack, and a handful of different endings.The storyline, while simple, delivers powerful twists and surprises. The soundtrack matches the intensity of the moment better than any other game I can think of, seamlessly changing to compliment the current scene. When "Cour des Miracles" by Andrea Boccadoro started playing during the fight with the King of Thieves and the twist began to unfold, I realized that this game was unlike any other.This game doesn't give you much to keep track of aside of the deck of cards you set out to manipulate, and I believe that is one of the key reasons that each wager you make becomes increasingly stressful, intense, and invigorating as the suspicion of your opponent slowly increases with each passing second.I haven't had this much fun playing a game in a long time.Well done, Nerial.I'm excited to see what the future holds in store.11 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: A game reveals card cheats and tricks, with a neat historical fantasy story and wonderful early music.Card Shark is not about deck-builder and earning powerful cards, but to learn and cheat in regular poker games back in the renaissance. By expertise in poker, player helps Comte saint-Germain to reveal the truth of a missing lover and son of King Louis XV. That is, the gameplay can be divided into 2 parts: travel around France to join high class poker games, and revealing/seeking truth and schemes that change life for both of them. These two parts are executed and integrated well, a pleasant for whoever enjoys cards or storyline or both.For card cheats, you'll learn regular tricks like to move, cut, shuffle, swap a single, multiple cards or a set, but there are more like giving hints using a traditionally fan, and the way you hold a glass and how many time wiping the table etc., I've never thought of any. There are 28 tricks in total and the first 2/3 are easy to master, however, the later ones are challenging, but I find the difficulty is well balanced, and you can always practice in the carriage if you are having a hard time with opponents, especially in higher bet the suspicious time boosts fast. The story is well written and made as a game, I won't give it away but at the very beginning, a brief line is given "It will teach you to turn a beggar into a king", which is very true. Player was once a nobody in a tavern, picked by the comte and taught by cheats is no coincidence- everything is not a coincidence like the winner in the poker game. I enjoyed how the story was unveiled, plenty of betrayal, mystery, lies and surprises, then truth came out after layers of lies, at the end the game let the player make fate.Upon finishing Card Shark I can't help thinking of Inscryption. I won't put them in the same genre - one is of a strategy card battle and the other is of regular poker cheat. Also, Card Shark has a clear historical fantasy story, yet Inscryption is too mysterious even at the end so many questions are unanswered. Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game about cheating at cards. Though I'm not sure on how accurate the story is and avoiding potential spoilers, if you like French history and also learning new tricks I would very much recommend this game. It does need to be noted that this game is not a card game itself, it's a game about cheating at cards. You do not actually play out the hand of cards. Game play flows nice, mini-games are fun, I feel like I'm learning card tricks (and I'm able to replicate a handful of them without further research). I like the story, and I think the game offers some good replay value. There's three difficulties, and I feel like anyone can play this game because of the three settings. Noting my own personal bias: I've been looking forward to this game since I saw the reveal trailer live. I also really like card games, so learning new card tricks is something I enjoy. I played with a controller, but mouse works just as well if you ask me. TL;DR: I like the story and highly recommend this game to anyone who wants to learn card tricks. However, if you're looking for an actual game of cards, this is not what you're looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: In one sentence:"Narrative Simon Says puzzle game"I really enjoyed my time playing Card Shark- it's a story based game where you learn card tricks and perform them. You never actually play the card game so don't expect that. If you enjoy practicing a routine of "do this this this that and this" on the fly with a fun story, then you will enjoy this game.If you aren't a fan of learning a static trick, I wouldn't play this game as you would find the gameplay boring. The sounds and visuals are quite good. I will say that if you aren't hooked within 2 hours then you'll know if this game is for you or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark is a delightful enlightenment in history of 18th century France and card/board cheating for me. It gives me an utterly novel experience and reminds me of some other indie games that have amazed me like CupHead, Kenshi, RimWorld, ChronoArk, SuperMeatBoy.Pros: 1. The oil painting or crayon drawing stick figure art style is enchanting. And though I barely listen to the classical music, I'm obsessed with the piano, harpsichord and fiddle in card shark. They are beautiful masterpieces.2. The learning curve is smooth. The feedback of gambling is great, and I just hardly say no to any gambling parts of any games I've ever played. 3. Nice scripts. I like this story of political struggle, betrayal and growing up.4. I was addicted in cards several times in the past, i'm interested in almost all board/card games. I love techniques in this game especially the last few, like tricks in comte's backup and erdnase special, the one that injogs and outjogs synchronously.5. Stanley Kubrick movies seem attractive, thanks to this game for letting me know about Barry Lyndon.Cons: I must say, though it's tense and thrilling to execute even simple techniques, the gameplay is a bit repetitive and boring. 1. So-called magic or cheating tricks is just a loop - "you learn some techniques and a trick that puts them in a sequence, and you practice". You must practice subtle fingerings hard rather than some simple QTE(quick time events) for memory or APM(actions per minute) test.The gameplay is not fascinating enough, maybe there is other choices better than mere qte? It diminishes satisfaction of executing those stuff under pressure.2. The rule of the card games, the details of the games and hands aren't presented, which is a pity for me.3. I reckon that there is some overlap among the 28 methods.4. Bugs. A Chinese display bug. Another one was encountered after explaining the suits and JQKA early in chapter 1 - I was stuck on the overlooking table scene.5. Rehearsal can't be skipped, sometimes clicks by mistake are annoying. And maybe the tutorial could be simpler or optional. It's more enjoyable to reason out some steps of those techniques intuitively.This is the first game that I've ever completed through entirely in English, except for online ones like LOL or those I didn't complete like Caves of Qud. I'm convinced that only play game in its original language can get the original flavor after this experience, and I'll play all those whose original language is English in English thenceforth,  thanks to card shark.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Devolver Digital don't miss. That is something we should have learned after exploring motels with dead Russian mobsters in them. Though, this time, this game isn't about senselessness in general, it's about the art of cheating.As with any true art form, there has to be some philosophy to act as the guidance and foundation of our actions. No technique is not without its proven history, no legend is not without its fantastical backstory.Card Shark explores cheating as an art, a philosophy, a way of life for those bum ass 1800s smelly French people that truly had nothing else to do with their boring lives. As such, the "card games" you play in Card Shark are as empty as the delightful NPCs hobbling around town.Modern day cheating is a lost art. Cheat codes are a relic. People are too scared/lazy of downloading game trainers because they run the risk of running into HotMommyMilkers.mp4, a computer virus that transforms a gaming PC into a vector for NFT ransomware.I'm gonna show you my dirty hands, wayward reader. I cheated in Card Shark. I needed to see what would happen if you had beaten the game on the highest difficulty - The Con Man. A difficulty that delets your save file if you die. Perma-death, if you will.I employed various techniques. Note taking. Hiding my mistakes by quickly returning to the menu. But the most egregious of them all was save-file manipulation, because it's just another basic Unity game after all.Normally, I would be pretty dismissive about these petty achievements. But since this was a game about cheating, I thought it'd be fitting to do it to a stupid Card Shark.Cheating is all about precision and execution. A single misstep and the illusion fades. At low levels, it's addictive eye candy. At the highest levels, it's using Sand Attack on fate herself. But how does that translate to gameplay?Well... Card shark is essentially 100% QTEs. But don't let that deter you. Its QTEs are more intuitive than any big budget AAA movie-type games (Heavy Rain, The Quarry, Until Dawn, Detroit Become Human).This is a game that requires you to memorize techniques and the execution of all 28 card tricks. If you make any mistake, you lose the card round. Fitting, because it's bad practice to teach you that it's okay to make mistakes. If you were of nobility and you found out that you were being swindled by a Card Shark, would you not be angry?Casual indie critics often point out that Card Shark's biggest flaw would lie within the dialogue choices. But this is no flaw. In fact, the illusion of choice is one of the game's greatest sleight of hands.The only point to be made about cheating is that it's a literal hell of a tool to manipulate the odds. That's it. When you cheat, you expose yourself as an inglorious dishonorable French fart. You're sacrificing everything for a simple manipulated result. A life-threatening gamble for the sake of a little peace in your mind or perhaps the world as a whole.The spectacular finale of Card Shark made me feel empty and sad. Its classical edgy writing had kept me intriqued from beginning to end, yet I couldn't help but feel cheated at the end of it all.Trying to cheat a stupid basic Unity game lead to absolutely nothing. The illusion of choice produced a few more entertaining lines. Note-taking significantly helped demystify complex cheats. Manipulating saves lead nowhere as there was no achievement, no glory for beating the game as "The Con Man".At the end of the day, did I cheat myself? Or did Card Shark teach me an honest lesson in cheating? Could there have been more to Card Shark? Could there have been an achievement for beating the game on "The Con Man" difficulty legitimately? Nay. Because this is a simple, stupid, basic video game made in Unity xdOkay Nerial, you got me fair and square. Card Shark is a phenomenal video game when you take it all in. It will stand as a masterpiece of card games without any legitimate card gameplay. From the harmonious soundtrack to its gorgiously astute presentation, from the QTEs to the elegence of sharp and tasteful writing, I don't need to explain any thing else.In conclusion, you  to play Card Shark.Score breakdown:(base 5)+5 gameplay: Tense QTE action, harder than any David Cage video game+5 presentation: Subtle Cutthroat Consistency+5 soundtrack: Elegent Modern Classical Remixes+5 writing: Definitive proof that 1800s France smelt like a gamer convention

_childDocuments_.review: So we get a lot of card games on Steam, but I’m pretty sure this is the first one where the actual card game itself does not matter - and in the most brilliant way possible.Having not played the demo prior, I was under the impression the game was going to be some sort of deckbuilder with a unique art style. That latter part is still true, but the game itself is actually about cheating in a card game. In fact, throughout the entire experience, you never get to learn what card game is being played - just how to cheat at it.This takes the focus off of mechanics you may already know from existing card games and instead places all emphasis on learning and executing various sleight of hand and other tricks. You’ll be shuffling decks while maintaining cards in a specific order, using multiple decks while keeping track of potential duplicates, signaling to your partner using a variety of creative signs, and using the smallest of marks to know which card is which from the back.The difficulty does not come from how good your opponents are, but rather your ability to keep up with the numerous tricks introduced as the game progresses. You’ll learn one, and then in a few matches learn an evolution of that trick and so on until it is this very complex thing with a bunch of steps you’ll need to have memorized.This is a double-edged sword. The complexity and depth of the tricks when layered on one another is cool and very satisfying when pulled off successfully, but it’s also very frustrating to pull off all the tricks correctly and then make one small mistake or even misclick in the final round that costs you the whole thing. All the animations, dialogue scenes, and stuff really gets old when you’ve seen it more than twice.This is obviously a game developed for controller and it unfortunately shows in some ways when using keyboard and mouse. A lot of the inputs are just joystick movements mapped to mouse which don’t always feel right and I frequently found myself misinputting despite how few actions there are in the game.Once you do get the hang of it though - there’s a lot to like here. Bunch of cool tricks to learn, places to visit, and the game does a good job diversifying its gameplay over the course of its runtime. You’re not just cheating at a card game, but also learning how to flick cards into a hat, how to flip a coin and guarantee the result, and even how to duel with swords.When it is just card cheats though, it’s still some good stuff, although not quite perfect. While evolving previously learned tricks is cool, the game treats them as entirely new tricks each time, so of the 28 you learn, only a handful are entirely unique on their own. The rest are simply combinations of other tricks into one or a previous trick with one small change. Honestly, it’s a little bit disappointing.It took me about five hours to clear the game and get each ending. Granted, I am still missing 19 of the achievements so there is a bit more there to do for completionists, but nothing to really flesh out the experience after you’ve given it a good playthrough - it is mostly linear with just a handful of different endings that you can simply reload to achieve.The story is a bit basic, sure, but engaging enough to keep the experience going. There’s not a whole lot of filler here, it’s straight to the point, hits all the main story beats, and nothing more outside of the occasional bit of comedy. Great effort all around there and similar things can be said about the art. It’s incredibly stylized, colorful, and looks great at 4k.4k 144fps, no drops, no crashes, no freezing, none of that. I did have an issue where I managed to softlock myself and prevent further progress, but I notified the devs and they were able to quickly fix the issue.Card Shark is one of the most unique indie games of the year. Taking the focus off of the card game itself and placing it all on cheating in said card game makes for some very cool gameplay, with a bunch of neat tricks to learn, minigames to partake in, and a story to experience that is surprisingly not bad. It’s not perfect and suffers from some disappointing design choices, but I can’t deny I had a good time with it and would recommend it.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr I had no idea what this game was when I bought it yesterday. After less than 24 hours, I've finished it and will be replaying it. I LOVED this game. It combines timing, memorization, and technique with a choose-your-own-adventure feel within an overarching story. I played with an Xbox controller really smoothly on the normal mode. There are times when I lost because a trick was hard to pull off, and other times, you're meant to lose for the story. Overall, though, this game does a really good job at teaching you fundamentals which later become larger cons. I'll be playing this again on hard mode, making some different decisions to see where the story takes me, as I still have about 20 achievements to unlock! I haven't sat down and played a game completely like this since Return of the Obra Dinn. 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: It was a miss for me and might be for you but I can see its appeal. Story Rich wasn't a lie but it should at least make me feel more engulfed in this story. You get multiple choice dialog options that have 0 impact on the game. I thought we were over with fake dialog options. It's a game of memorization and quick time events which was fun at the start but quickly got boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Truly an impressive feat of game design. I hope that people don't take for granted how difficult it must have been to smooth out the mechanics of this game. Great concept, but really formidable execution. It manages to find the knife's edge between too simple and too complicated, and keeps you in that spot for the whole ride. At the end I feel satisfied and wanting for more at the same time. Graphics and presentation are original and masterful. Controls are well thought out- but it is important to note that it was designed to be played with a controller and I'm sure that using m&k objectively diminishes the enjoyment of the game. It's still great to play without controller though. The techniques presented in this game are pretty much all real, which adds to the fun. There were a few times where the explanations/instructions were a bit obtuse. But I think this was one of the hardest things for them to achieve- to succinctly describe each gambit.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are great and the music is nicely themed but the gameplay is just a mess. The controls are very loose for something that wants you to play on a timer and one mistake could cost you loads of time replaying sections of the game. I also find it odd there was no on screen prompts to remember the directions to rotate and move the stick for different suits and values. Taking a break and coming back to the game is a mess and restarting like I did takes ages because there is no real skip feature on dialog.TLDR: Better controls and some quality of life features could make a world of difference.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very unique. It teaches you how to cheat and con with playing cards to discover the truth about people and their secrets. The game visuals are stunning and a feast to the eye. Music can get repetitive as the game lacks variety in that but its not an issue as the music is pretty catchy. Every trick performed in this game can be used to cheat in real life. 7/10This should be an 8/10 but trick number 24 gave me a headache and it lacked a proper tutorial so I'm removing 1 because of that. Otherwise, fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I really was interested in this game way back when the first trailer was shown. The idea of using card tricks to profit seemed really interesting and the artist style was very unique. I still think this game would be fun to people with better memories and patience than me, but I have neither of them these days. Every time I messed up a prompt or trick in the tutorial, I would get frustrated as to why I need to continue when I already screwed up, unable to start over without going through it all.I wish there was a neutral review; this is the best I can do. I played on normal and haven't looked at the lower difficulty, but I'd have to complete the tutorial on the day I was already on and it was a doozy. There really should be a way to reset a hand in the tutorial or start a day over if it isn't in the easy difficulty. Perhaps if steam would let me have more time before refunds were no longer allowed I would be more willing to see if its easy enough. I have doubts with how much memory you need even at just the first area you can go to and how one mistake loses a whole hand.My ADD infested goldfish like brain can't handle this. Perhaps one day I'll come back after the game gets tweaked and if I see the easy difficulty is enough for me to handle. The thing that broke me was being told I'd have to remember the cards I palmed for the 10 min bet area.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: The most fascinating thing about Card Shark is that it's a card game where you don't even know what game you're playing. The only thing you're concerned with is cheating.All the tricks you'll use in the game are actual card tricks and cheats you can try in real life, which is incredibly interesting on its own. The story, set in France during king's Louis XV monarchy, does a good job at tying together all the stages and basically takes you on a tour of 18th century pre-revolutionary France.Special props to the sound track, which is amazing and fits perfectly both the historical period and the mood the game sets.It playes perfectly on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game with a perfect combination of beautiful art, amazing music, intriguing gameplay, and compelling story. The theme of 18th-century France sets the perfect background for the card tricks to be played out without hampering the progress of the story. The game has multiple endings, and players will be rewarded with an achievement for completing each of them.That being said, there are two points I don't like about this game. There is a feeling that the game is not 100% refined and the devs have neglected their products. First, the game is still having 2 bugged achievements since its launch in 2022. I spent multiple playthroughs to fulfill their requirements but none of them unlocked. In the end, I had to resort to 'external' method to unlock them. It was quite annoying to spend a long amount of time trying to go for the achievements only to figure out they were bugged. The devs were informed about this problem on steam discussion and discord, but no measure was taken ever since. It's a shame that the vast majority of players cannot complete the full house for achievements of this game due to the bug dating back to its release.Second, sometimes the game skips the cutscene entirely without the player's control. In my very first playthrough, I did not get to see the final cutscene revealing the twist of the story because the game just casually skipped that part. I only realized I had missed that scene thanks to my second playthrough. And in my later playthroughs, other cutscenes in other parts of the story were skipped, making the story somewhat awkward and incomprehensible if someone was playing it the first time (e.g., the main character plays card with a new character or the main character appears at a new place without any context given).Overall, Card Shark is a solid game that ingeniously combines historical theme and card tricks. Yet, the game is not without flaws. There are some minor, yet critical errors here and there that prevent players from fully enjoying the game. I would still give it a 8.5/10, and I hope the devs will soon fix the bugs to provide better experience for future players.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with nice art and a charming story. The goal of the game isn't to win, but to cheat in order to get a desired outcome. I would describe them not as quick time events, but little mini games with the cards. Some of the can get a little complex and complicated. There are a few that took me more time to practice than others, but overall this was a very unique game using mechanics that I had never seen used in this way.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so badly to like this game, but it left me more frustrated than satisfied. If you truly don't care about endings, give it a play. If you do, I don't think it's worth it.Art and music: phenomenal.Gameplay: often buggy but generally pretty fun, except that failure is often punished just by making you go through a tedious checklist of scenes rather than raising the stakes in any meaningful way.Writing: Oof. So the dialogue is good, but the story is... not good. It builds a really interesting premise (intrigue, a chase, romance), but ultimately builds to a series of rushed deus ex machinas, followed by a "multiple choice" ending that ignores all choices made and lessons learned. In vague terms (I'll still use a spoiler tag), Additionally, the ending suffers from the games tendency to punish failure with boredom, since its margin of error is nonexistent.Beautiful, frustrating game.One more specific example:
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Fun games challenge the player, let them train and then succeed with enough practice and skill...but Card Shark is increasingly demanding and always unforgiving. Just as I had perfected one trick in one scenario, another overwhelming set of tricks was revealed, and often combined. I just could not get in the balancing act of remembering what I was supposed to do, minding the opponent's awareness and trying to make some coin, time and time again. After 3 hours, restarting whole scenes because I screwed up one step out of 10 was just not fun anymore.I suck at cards, in game and real life, yes, but Card Shark could have fun if it rewarded creativity, or improvisation, rather than mechanic perfect memory. (What about allies? Sound hints? Second chances? not restarting everytime?!). A pity, I was intrigued by the characters and the conspiracy.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This is like a Celeste, extremely precise inputs at extremely precise times, but with added pressure of a ticking clock! Unlike a Celeste there's not an option to quickly and easily try again. This really needs a story mode difficulty; I'm very intrigued by the story but I just can't make it through.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes charm. The art style and music are fantastic, and the concept of learning multiple different ways to cheat at cards in 18th century, French high society is great. The game play is basically a series of mini games and QTE's, but the overall presentation is so great that you can feel the stress of not wanting to screw up and get caught. I used a gamepad since that's what the game recommends, but I saw other reviews mention the keyboard controls have problems, so keep that in mind if you don't own a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game! I think the coolest part is the techniques you learn to cheat in card games all appear to be real and useable! They definitely require adept slight of hand but you really feel like you are learning a very interesting and under-the-table skill while you play through this game. I highly recommend using a controller. It feels very right and tactile moving your thumbs on the analog stick to do slight of hand tricks. Game took me about 6 hours to beat, but there are alternate endings and a new game plus. I'm sure I'll feel the desire to play such a satisfying game again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite a new experience for me, challenging and full of tension. I find the artstyle to be quite charming, and the concept of this game is interesting enough.The storyline of this game is a bit lacking as the others might have said, it could have more weight added to the plot and less in flat conversations, but alas a neat one.Playing this game with gamepad instead of keyboard is proved to be harder and less accurate. The ui is a bit glitchy, and so are the inputs.If there is anything to be improved for this game, it should be the ui, controller inputs, and storyline. Overall amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but the gameplay amounts to memorizing how to do different quicktime events. The art style is fantastic, the story was fun (for the amount that I played), but the gameplay itself lacks the complexity and nuance that you would expect in a game about cheating at cards. The biggest bummer about this was when I messed up one of the cheating sequences and knew how I could fix the situation. I did what I thought would fix the deck so that I would win and still was told that I lost! It's a very unforgiving game where you can spend minutes at a time playing out a quicktime event that you failed on the first or second input. I really hope someone else tries this type of game and gives it the type of gameplay system that it deserves, or that the developers come back and release an update fixing the (very fixable) issues with this game. Who knows? Maybe I'll give it another try some day. But right now I feel disappointed with how this game turned out.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played. Fun, unique, atmospheric, immersive, and you never know where the game will take you even if you cheat! A 9.5/10 for me! The only thing that would make it better is more diverse ending choices but perhaps that's the point? You cheated the game so the game cheats you! Enjoy everyone this game is one for the ages!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark is an original game that is worth your time, even if you are not a gambling fan. The individual pieces of gameplay may be essentially quite simple (visual novel and mini-games), but they are so aptly married and combined with the witty and phlegmatic writing, they make for a very addictive game that will keep your interest until the credits roll.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This game won't be for everyone but it's super unique and it really resonated with me.The game loop, at its core, boils down to the following pattern: small tutorial for a new card minigame (contextualized in the setting)  -> card game where you're asked to cheat using the techniques the game just taught you -> repeatThe minigames heavily abstract the card mechanics involved but are still fun to learn and master (it feels a bit like a less goofy WarioWare in execution) and the tricks tend to build on each other as you progress. The story is also enjoyable, featuring a number of twists and turns and featuring characters inspired by real life historical figures. The dialogue in the game was well written and presented in a way that was easy to read.I don't think I should say much more as a lot of the game's charm comes from experiencing it firsthand, but if the above tidbits have you curious, I highly recommend giving Card Shark a shot. There's nothing quite like it!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting concept that just does not work as intended.Doing small tricks and scams works fine for the majority of the game, but in the last chapter, you have so little time to think, you really don`t even have 3 seconds to check if what you did is correct in an entire scam. The timer moves way too fast, and unless you know every trick by heart and every card placement variations on the top of your head, you are going to lose a lot. Not to mention, you WILL HAVE TO GRIND the money to come back to the main campaign and just try again for one round (you need to win three times in a row to pass one game). Not to mention, even tho the game has an RNG system built into it, it can totally destroy you as well, giving you impossible combinations. Also, it happened a few times that I did everything correct in a round, and still lost in the end. Truly unbalanced and unpolished mess from time to time.It really did deserve some patching up, that obviously did not happen. But again, I had fun for the most part, but I cannot recommend this game to anyone.3.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: i like it a lot, the artstyle and the whole aesthetic is great, but it's become literally unplayable. the controls have always been a pain in the ***, but it now got to a point where i things just don't work at all, no matter with mouse or gamepad. i am looking forward to finishing/replaying this game when it gets better, will be updating this review later.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: "The Card Shark's Assistant" would be a more apt title for this one. I don't think Card Shark nails its unconventional idea of making you feel like an ace cheat largely because the gameplay itself is little more than Simon Says, following QTE's and other minigames at the whims of the REAL card shark, your mentor.The gameplay often felt like a slog, but for me I found enough enjoyment in the non gameplay aspects of this game that I still reflect on it fondly. It's got an unmistakable aesthetic that really gives you the vibe of 18th century France.Unless you have a particular fondness for the subject matter (card tricks), then I think this is a title worth playing despite its gameplay and not because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cool game if you can just . The art is so beautiful, the story is fun, and there are some really amazing sequences (that you play once per run when you get them right). I was able to play through the whole campaign across just a few sessions -which is ideal to me- but even in that time I forgot like half of the card tricks. A lot of my issues crystalize in the little side racket to boost your money reserves. It's the only table you can play without getting set into working on new cheats or progressing the story when you win. It has a fun ensemble of archetypal (and not historical, which is rare in this) characters who all look distinct and have personalities that make them a joy to swindle. However, the ideal interaction I slipped into with them was a sort of smash and grab, since the rate that suspicion increases makes longer games a waste. I'd sit down, up the bet a ridiculous amount, choose the easiest/shortest of the three random cheat options I was presented with since that tends to gain the least suspicion, and leave after one huge win. There's an option to lose hands, whether on accident or on purpose, to lower suspicion. I had hoped that would make a hustle longer than 3 hands possible, but it wasn't and I never got to just play with a gameplay loop that felt unauthored.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark, a game that I wanted to love but it was just too frustrating for me. There are a lot of tricks to learn and the game does not do a great job in explaining the mechanics of each one, let alone remember them after you've learned 10 other different tricks. And let's not forget those tricks that are very similar to each other but with very slight differences and you just have to guess which one you have to use based on a name that's not descriptive at all. Oh, and you get them wrong? Do everything again. Story was interesting but not enough to carry the game and make me ignore my issues with it. I just wasn't having fun after 3 hours. I believe that with some QoL updates this game can improve, but I just can't recommend in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I have to think the Alliance is going to frown on this...Jokes aside, this is a phenomenal game. From the POV of a magician, what is demonstrated here (so far) is really great. I'm amazed at how well the gameplay mechanics have captured the feeling of pulling off sleight of hand. As someone who has to do stuff similar to this a lot, it draws up the same amount of anxiety from wanting it to go successful, the mental agility of remembering multiple things at once and the satisfaction when you pull it off without a hitch.I hope this piques peoples interest in magic and sleight of hand, because it's an exciting fun world. This game showcases the beauty of magic that not many people get to see or experience, the method and the technique, so it's a very rare peek behind the curtain.The only negative, that I'd concur with people is that sometimes the "QTE" and actual mechanics can become tedious, but I can't imagine the sleight of hand mechanics being any different. Be thankful it's not super true to life and the tutorial isn't several years of being in your room performing into the mirror...Also the artstyle is gorgeous and the music is excellent... All in all a really unique, innovative and educational experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games I've ever played. The art style, the atmosphere, soundtracks, witty humour, hilarious and dumb faces of the main character... Overall creating a unique concept.But the game is not for the casual gamer. It'll test your patience and your ability to withstand annoying QTE sequences. It took me 18 hours to beat it when there's an achievement for beating it in 2 hours.I spent roughly 10 hours remembering and practicing the tricks just because I sat on the game for too long and forgot everything.Even though I was overwhelmingly disappointed with the ending I got, a wise man once said the journey is more important than the destination. So for that reason I give it a solid 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I am sorry to say, but I do not reccomend this Game.I admit, from the Trailers I imagined something a little different, BUT in the first few hours in the first Chapter, I actually had some "fun" and was intrigued how the story would move on.The biggest problem for me lies in the Gameplay and Controls.First of, the Gameplay: This is a Game that seems to be only about Quick Time Events and Button Presses at the right time without them needing to be quick. Also it is about memorization. There is nothing else to it.Yes, you can walk around sometimes, from left to right and back, but this is not Gameplay.Dialog Options suggest that you have Dialog Choices, but in fact the outcome seems to be always the same.The biggest problem I have - and this is why I stopped playing in Chapter 2 - are the controls. There comes one "Card Trick" that is so fiddly and unforgiving in the Controls that even after 10 tries I couldn't do it.I knew what had to be pressed and how the "Trick" worked, but the controls wouldn't do what I would input.9/10 times it failed to do what I pressed. With a brand new XBox One Controller.And for that price, I can't say I reccomend it. I will not be able to finish the Game because of that.There are a few pros, the Art Style looks nice and the story can be engrossing. Also it is pretty chill WHEN it works. But this is not enough for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark is a unique, creative and masterfully executed concept about a conman.You are taught various tricks and have to execute them in stressful scenarios. At the same time, you get to experience a bizarre yet intriguing story that goes perfectly hand in hand with the gameplay.An absolute must play for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I accidentally stumbled upon this game thanks to the Steam discovery queue, and boy am I grateful that I did. This little hidden gem was a delightful 8-hour experience. If you enjoyed Papers, Please, then you will enjoy this game. If you live for the opulent XVIII century aesthetic, you will fall in love with this game and wish for more. And if you want to learn how to cheat in card games, .I cannot recommend Card Shark enough. Please give it a try and see if you can make a fortune without getting caught.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Sounds fun up front, but the gameplay is ultimately very repetitive and limited. You learn a QTE trick ("press up then down then A"), you do it 2-3 times, you're done with it and move on to the next one. No room for creativity or adaptation. Spends more time teaching you a trick than you end up doing it.The story itself is actually pretty good, the art is good, shame about the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Really like the game but the controls are too sensitive and there is no way to change sensitivity in game. I made it to the first baths mission and I literally cannot do the trick because the game thinks when i place one false card down that I want to insert it into my deck right after. d pad has the same issue where the very very slight off center input on a controller is read as  going right instead of staying center. Like moving the thumbstick all the way left and letting it fall back is a right input.And no my controller works just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I like the story, the setting, and the general *idea* of Card Shark so far, but it has a LOT of technical problems that need to be fixed. Some of these elements are so bad it makes me wonder if the game was playtested at all before it was put on sale.In Card Shark, you are a mute boy in mid-1700s France who becomes the disciple of a traveling conman. Each level consists of learning a new card scam (or a variation of an old one) and then playing them out in QTEs. As these become more elaborate, they shift from QTEs to memory games and quickly clicking through menus on a timer. For example, the first game has you simply look at an opponent's cards while pouring wine and then use a QTE to signal their suit. This is okay, BUT it is severely undermined by easy quality-of-life updates. First, there are no instructions after the tutorial. It's a game ALL ABOUT SIGNALS and there is no way (in game) to look up the signals after you learn them. There's a glossary for each of the scams, but they only describe the *techinique*, not how to actually do them in game. There's even a button that says "controls" but that only states what imput you use to make the signal, not how to make the different signals themselves. This means you basically have to play the whole game in one go because I guarantee you will forget these techniques between LEVELS, to say nothing of between play sessions.  Also, you can't play the tutorial again after learning the technique for the first time. So I hope you memorized it perfectly and/or wrote it down. This is doubly insulting because there are nearly 30 scams to learn and each has different QTE controls you are expected to memorize after being shown once. By the way, your victims get more suspicious the more time you take. So if you hesitate to remember what the controls are for a scam, it means less money for you in the long run. But here's the thing, that doesn't inspire me to commit these scams to memory. That tells me to pause, write down how to play each scam, and then call upon it while paused. That is the opposite intention of the story and gameplay. It not only cheapens the experience, but could be fixed instantly with a button that explains signals and another that allows you to replay tutorials in the overworld menu.The triple insult comes later on where you need to string multiple scams together. So you might need to stack a deck in your mentor's favor, then remember all 5 cards, use QTEs to signal number of cards and suite unrelated to what you just saw, and then recall all 5 cards that you picked the first time while scrolling through an entire deck. The only advice for how to do this is "use memory tricks." They don't attempt to teach you any and you can't proceed until you learn the trick. On top of this, if you mess up at any part during a tutorial there is no way to restart. Another easy quality of life update. If you mess up in part 1 of a 5 part scam, you need to either play the whole thing through again or Alt+F4 and restart. I do not know which is faster.  With aggressively bad bugs, bad tutorials, bad menus, and a game that requires undivided attention and memory, I can't recommend Card Shark **in it's current state**. Maybe after a full 2.0 patch this might be worth it in 2-3 years.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most creative gMamew I’ve ever played, with an incredible story and atmosphere. The ambience and mechanics are fantastic and while it can be completed in only around 8 hours, it’s still some very fun 8 hours. I highly recommend CardShark to most people who love story games  with clever mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and exciting to play, and has a really neat visual style. The card tricks are essentially small mini-games, requiring you to make the right move with the right timing - a type of gameplay I normally wouldn't en joy that much, but which fits the story so perfectly that I had a great time.The story is well-written too, with plenty of interesting characters and an exploration of class and identity. Set in a time of vast inequality, you lie and cheat your way through posh salons, daring to see if you can be more than you were.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the game for 2 and a half hours, I am in act 2 currently. So far the game is very enjoyable, it has an interesting story combined with fun elements of cheating and con artistry. Sometimes the controls can be annoying, but I really think the characters and environments are beautiful, forcing me to keep playing. The tricks can get difficult sometimes, and with the time limits it can get stressful trying to finish a trick, but I think that adds to the satisfaction of conning and opponent with only a second left before you would lose.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: One of the rare game where I started getting legitimately mad that the annoying gameplay kept interrupting the story. I'm giving this a recommend despite the fact I really did not like it. Definitely not my cup of tea but I can't deny that it isn't charming and well done. My big like is the story. I really didn't care to begin with which made this a real slog to play but I got sucked it and it's actually a rather well told tale with a lot of Tudor's style historical intrigue and twists. My big dislike is the gameplay. I'm just not a fan of 25-30 different yet very similar minigames to begin with and the frustrating way in which they're taught. A lot of techniques were taught in a very controlled environment which made learning the process easy but come gametime I realized that I clearly didn't get the the principle in practice because something like changing seating order would throw me off. The game was very good at making me feel dumb about shuffling until I learned to ignore the deck altogether and just follow the card positions at the top of the screen.  Losing is also annoying because you have to play a minigame to cheat death and start the level over at the very beginning skipping thru previous tutorials and dialogue again. This lead to me spending a lot of time doing this game's version of save scumming and just quitting to title screen every time I messed up to always keep myself at the start of my last best hand. I happily accepted the ending where I didn't cheat at cards at all because I was exhausted (despite it being a short playthru) and couldn't be bothered to learn yet another technique. Great story, great looking, mostly well made. Clearly not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really great game! Though to clarify, it is a bit buggy at the time of writing. I ran into a couple of buggy moments, like where the game broke sequence and confused the next tutorial with the previous one, or the controller stopped working when I click on the screen by accident. Aside from that, the only real issue I have with it is replay value. Unless you want to scam people out of their money and clean house, or just achievement hunt, it doesn't feel like there's a lot to go back to unless I'm mistaken.(This part will be antiquated in a bit I'm sure)The game does one thing great, by marrying the gameplay with the narrative, where you grow and learn with the protagonist himself. It's a feeling I cant describe but it really got me invested in my playthrough! It was fun story to get into (without spoiling).The gameplay itself is another beast entirely. It is pretty cool to learn ACTUAL card cheating techniques in this game, injogging in particular. Though while it is a series of muscle memory and actually paying attention to what cards you're dealing with, it can be easy to mess up under pressure. It is easy to catch a few deaths along the way, I've only died about 5 times by screw ups rather than being surprised.All and all, great game to buy, and if the story doesn't grab you, the variety of card sharking skills on display should at least teach the players something cool!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and the music of this game is incredible! The concept of the game is simple at first, and learning what you need to do isn't all that difficult. The game quickly picks up, however, and you need to make sure that you're paying attention. I love all of the focus that this game requires, it is really good. Also it is very funny and has a lot of great dialog!
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I love card games, and after learning how to do magic tricks with cards when I was 9, I always bring a deck of cards with me everywhere. This game can show you how to really stack a deck in real life, not just in game. It is explained clearly with visuals and I now have new ways to manipulate a normal deck to do magic tricks (or a game of cards if I ever need to).Game music is very nice, it fits the game perfectly, visuals are really nice, I love the artstyle they went with, gameplay was confusing at first but once you get it its super simple, you only need to use the mouse, no keyboard and it can be described as just a bunch of quick time events. Of course, that can also be considered a bad thing since you dont do much else than quick time events. I still enjoyed it tho since most if not all card tricks are based in real life tricks I could perform after seeing how they worked (with practice, they are complicated). Story was super interesting, it has different endings in the end and the story has its share of twists and turns to keep you wondering what will happen next. It also knows how to go from being just a chill game of cards to sudently you are fighting for your life. That reminds me of the amazing death mechanic! When you die, you have to play a game of cards against Death to cheat them into bringing you back to life, otherwise your safe file gets deleted. It also has difficulty settings to make the game harder or more difficult, so you can set it to whatever you want. Playing this game not only gave me a wonderful experience but it game me more knowledge to do magic tricks, do card cheats at games with my friends and explained how real life cheats at games work so that I would be able to recognize if an opponent is cheating or if an opponent is stacking the deck for a magic trick. I would suggest card players and non card players to give it a try, since its simple and super interesting
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: What other game presents you with the opportunity to actually try to cheat Death?Simply put, this is a marvellous game. The mechanics are beautiful and the escalation in card shenanigans is surprisingly robust. The care and attention to detail in this game is superb. For example, there are 52 achievements, each with a different card face. I can't think of a better way for that to be.I encountered a game breaking bug. Travelling to a new location, I was told that my execution of the technique was incorrect (despite getting it perfect multiple times). After a short while on the support boards, in the FAQ it was revealed that by using control + shift + 9, you can revert to the start of the scene or travel back to the map. The only criticism I have of this game is that these troubleshooting features are hidden from the player base. Which is very small compared to the joy this game sparks.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Unironically, this is my game of the year. The puzzles are engaging and not too repetitive, and the game makes you feel like you have really done a good trick when you succeed. It has elements of being "educational" (sort of in the vein of something like Cooking Mama) and does deliver in giving you a couple of neat tricks next time you want to cheat at go-fish or whatever.The story falls a little flat in the end -- but I like that. Wouldn't say it's a game you'll play through multiple times, but for a single afternoon, it's very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming game about stealing money from the French, accompanied with surprisingly well-written dialogue and characters. For better or for worse, I found myself extremely fond of the Comte. Beautiful art and animation, with varied and interesting gameplay. It makes you feel smart for memorizing and pulling off the various tricks the game teaches you. I only wish that we could replay the ending without having to play the entire game over again. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Card Shark makes you feel like a con artist. if you'll be precise and think fast you can swindle even the most intelligent rich ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But be too sloppy or reckless and you'll pay a visit to death. Learning new card tricks is really fun especially because they can be used in the real world. The game also features an extremely unique art style that looks gorgeous and music that is an absolute joy to listen to. Both of them set the unique vibe of the game. The game also features an intriguing story about 18th-century France that will make you want to keep playing. On the steam page the developer promised a game "where you’ll need to play your opponents better than you play your cards", and oh boy do they deliver.sadly there are no sharks in this game so I will have to give it only a stab in the belly out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like $20 is a bit much tbh, like, it's a good game, but I didn't really feel like my $20 was all that well-spent by the end, especially with its very low replay value. Granted, I personally don't usually replay any game once I've beaten it, but Card Shark really feels like a game I just wouldn't be able to return to and enjoy very much. That being said, it is a pretty enjoyable experience first time around for what it is, just, maybe get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Card Shark

_childDocuments_.review: Swindling and scamming are somethings that I have apparently become known in my streams for, but this game showed me I am but a small tadpole in a sea of Megaldon with the tactics and art forms that are displayed within Card Shark. I will never be able to play cards with anybody ever again, the game was very indepth perhaps too indepth I really struggled to understand what the explanations actually meant. However, the story was very well done and unexpected especially the secret ending where the German Ludwig comes in at the end and steals you away as his own, and sends you to Switzerland to manage the casino. That one was a real twist I didn't see coming. Chat went WOW! Also there were a good amount of KEKOUIs and LULOUIs to be had throughout the game. And there was also one MEOW.
