_childDocuments_.review: Edit: BENJI!  Please clap.I purchased this at launch expecting an old-school feel srpg, and that is exactly what I have received.  I can give you the pros very easily, nice art, nice relatively unique take on the triangle combat system, no broken weapons, and changing on the fly helps pick the best weapon for the job, I am playing on the hardest difficult, as I like challenges, and it is very very well balanced.  I had to restart only when I made foolish mistakes, which is nice.  The character art is well done, as are the levels and combat animations.The story isn't... unique so far, but I don't want to be harsh on it as I haven't experienced it all, obviously.  I read all the dialogue between characters and was pleasantly surprised by the differences between personalities.  With some small companies, it is obvious the characters are written by the same people, and while that may be the case here, they did a good job (so far) in making them at least have their own goals and opinions about things.  Also, kudos to the team so far for proper grammar, indie games can sometimes really fail in this department and it drives me bonkers!Now, the few negative things I experienced.  1) there isn't a lot of help navigating the controls for example, I received the rank up screen, but nothing said I needed to press the glowing promote sign at the top, I thought it was just artwork, so I was mashing buttons (I saw this in a negative review, but don't think its worth putting a thumbs down).  2) I have accidently pressed "enter" during enemy combat to have it completely skip, don't get me wrong, great feature, but maybe a "are you sure you want to skip to your turn", as its almost instant.  3) Not game-breaking, but theres a weirdly large amount of loading screens in this game, it just seems like, especially with a game that is low-graphics, there wouldn't be a need for so much filler and feels a bit like poor programming. 4) this is completely personal, but, the level of diversity so far at three hours is.. lacking, hoping that improves (again, personal preference).All in all, I would recommend this, and plan to, to my friends who are fans of srpgs.  Its extremely impressive for such a small company and for a first game.   Way to go guys, keep up the good work!Edit 2: Upon completion of the game, I can make a final comment saying that I continue to recommend this game.  It has a lot of great qualities, art, dialogue, characters, etc... One note I will make is there is no "catch up" system if you don't use a character for a few maps.  Similar titles, namely Fire Emblem Path of Radiance and Radiant Dawn, has an out of combat leveling, most characters just become fodder, and if they are too weak... you just hope you can do the 1-4 damage required to kill an enemy to try and level them up.  Lastly, the story lacks, but, its fine, just don't expect a jaw dropping experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Had fun with this game and is prompt you to continue playing. The characters are fun and the class works well. The option to advancing the class makes you look forward to actually fighting. However, i wish it had not the need to different weapons or if it is a mechanic to make it special, do not make upgrading it so exp and let us have scenarios to earn money else alot of money is spent upgrading the wrong items.  Also sometimes the conversations are too long for my liking. Anyway is a fun game and you really need to know your character's strength and weakness to go with the classes strength and weakness as well. Rate it 8 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game just now and WOW!! I had been searching for something to fill the Fire Emblem void and this game was it!!!!!! Although some of the systems I still have no clue about, the characters, art, storytelling, and familiar gameplay were all so welcome!! The game is really quite well done for being of "lesser quality." It's like the A-tier of the B-tier if that makes sense. There are little things I wish I could have such as wishing a "restart level" in the pause menu but the workaround is decently fast and it didn't really affect my experience with the game!For what it is and what I was searching for - a 9/10 for me!! Thank you Sword & Axe!! Would love a sequel~~~~
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Chapter 2 and I has a few things to say.While I do recommend this game, there are pros/cons that I can list off the bat:Pros:+ Animations/Art: WOW! Pixel art combat is what I missed in Fire Emblem and Dark Deity delivers here. Characters are designed cleanly; no complaints here.+ No Tutorials: Although this is a controversial point, the fact that I'm left alone to explore and understand the mechanics of the game myself is a breath of fresh air. I hate hand holding and I hate unskippable tutorials. Thank you Dark Deity.Cons:- Battle transitions are non-existent: Combat feels like a whiplash after the combat animation. It feels so unfinished just seeing the combat screen and then without warning, BAM, back to the map overlay.- Voice Over: I thought this game would be fully voiced considering gaming standards, but a few quips and "oohs" and "arghs" in between kind of let me down. Maybe sound files are too big? I dont know, but it's sort of a disappointment.- UI: The lack of "plinks" when traversing the menu just feels odd; like the game wasn't completed or someone forgot to add them. It feels too janky just having immediate response when I click a button w/ no indication other than the sound of my mouse click.Overall I would compare this game to Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance, but without the polish. I would love to see the dev team look critically at some of the critiques made and either make a new patch or take this info and build from this into their next game. This team has potential and every moment to screw Nintendo over and play a game where the game devs ACTUALLY CARE about their audience is always a W in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the hell out of this game. After finishing up all of FE:3H I needed a new game like this. I love the unique take on the genre and the story and characters are enjoyable and fun. In addition this game has loads of replayability with the built in randomizer, adds a fun extra element of chaos to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game at this time, it's just too buggy. I was hoping after four months it would be in a good state but I guess I was wrong. Let me run down the list of bugs I've come across:Units randomly becoming unselectable in battles. Nothing I tried fixed this.Controller will randomly stop working. The KB+Mouse controls are workable but this is still the type of game I'd rather play with a controller.When upgrading weapons it only gives the price for the first weapon and copies it across to the other four.Voulge is misspelled Volgue. I mean I know it ain't a common word but if Diablo II could get it right 20 years ago...One of my characters has an exclamation point in the bonds menu, but nobody is available to increase the bond with. At first I thought it was because they had a bond with a couple of other characters who later left but when they came back the mystery bond is still there.Damage numbers in the battle animations don't match up with the battle forecast or the damage actually dealt. I've seen this most often with animations that hit multiple times where it'll do for example 3 hits of 3 damage but the forecast and the actual damage dealt is 8. This is minor and visual only but it just reeks of a lack of polish.I also have gripes with the gameplay itself, the weakness system is way too complicated. You have to memorize armour types and weapon types of every class unless you want to spend a minute every turn just checking their stat pages. You can't even really use logic to try and figure it out because electric is good against chainmail because it's metal... but electric is bad against plate mail because it's... metal?Dodge is also absurdly broken. I'm playing after the patch which supposedly rebalances it and it's still completely overpowered so I don't even want to imagine how it was before that.The weapon system also has some issues. You get to pick between four types of weapon when making an attack, one that's strong but heavy, one that has high crit, one that has high hit and one that's a balance between the other three but also more often than not the lightest weapon. Since weight affects speed and speed affects both how much you can double and your dodge rate, the lightest one is far and away the best option 90% of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: For what this game is trying to achieve, I think it's quite good for a first try by the team involved. I bought this because I needed some FE in my life after not getting a smidgen from E3. I can say I've scratched the itch somewhat with this game.The characters aren't as boring as others in the review section seem to say, they just don't match up to what you may come to expect from other series. As of writing this I'm on Chapter 5 and I like several of the characters in my party; though not all of them are interesting, many have quirks that can be appreciated given context via support dialogue. I do agree with another reviewer that said supports take up a lot of time between maps; however, this has always been an issue for modern FE games where supports are more commonplace. I'd much rather have the option to have many supports than none. For being the first game of the sort the development team has done, I'd say I'm quite impressed. Not only by the characters and story, but also by the gameplay. It certainly borrows a lot from the FE series, but it stands alone in many aspects that make the gameplay unique. I recommend giving a try, while acknowledging this game isn't supposed to be AAA-comparable.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Worth your time if you're looking to scratch that Fire Emblem itch. Deep combat system and plenty of class options. The music and combat animations are also pretty good, as is map design. The story is passable, and most characters are likable enough, although some are pretty well-worn tropes. The way weapons and armor work is far different than FE and took a while to grasp, but the depth it adds is worth your effort to understand. The UI is a bit clunky and some of the characters need rebalanced, and the battle save doesn't reload for me if I exit the game. Minor complaints in an otherwise stellar game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it a lot so far.  The daily QoL patches are helping already.  Combat calculations are more complex than FE, but the death system is a lot more forgiving too so it balances.  I really like the weapon/armor matchups and how they tend to make sense from a realistic perspective to some degree.  Bond conversations have been mostly very good so far.  I'm a little worried about having to specialize into specific weapons, since I really like the versatility of the early game
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hate this game, but I also think there are better titles in the genre asking for less money on this platform. I think that the sequel to this title looks promising, but I can't in good conscious recommend this iteration. I think this game has a lot of great ideas, but it is grossly inferior to the series it clearly takes inspiration from. The item interface is tedious, the storytelling quality vacillates between droll exposition and breakneck character development that happens off-screen, and the maps are overly large without much intrinsic strategic depth, the way damage is calculated against armor/class feels almost completely arbitrary. Worst of all, however, is that the game does not divulge anything about its unique systems, nor does it tutorialize its gameplay which makes your first attempts at character building feel like you're gambling. In a game where experience points are their own finite resource to manage, it becomes frustrating when you invest into characters only to find out that the build you selected is effectively non-viable without significant luck in how your character gains stats.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the effort and passion of the Dev. team, and I really enjoyed the game before Chapter 10. However, Dark Deity really has a lot of problems needed to be improved.First, the game balance is really terrible. Some classes are way too good, while some classes are way too terrible, if you choose the wrong class in LV 10, the character will become totally useless in the entire game. (For example, a character can deal 0 dmg to almost all kind of enemies.)Moreover, the enemies are too good. I can understand if the Boss or some Named Characters should be much more powerful than our heroes, but why all the enemies units are better than ours? (Ironically, Boss or Named Characters are not better than the other common enemies.) The DEF and FOR of the enemies are incredibly high, sometimes with an incredibly high attack dmg too. Also, the amount of the enemies are enormous, for example in CH 19, we are surrounded by two tiles of enemies from both side, and we need to break through them, and get ALL OUR UNITS to get to the escape point. One critical hit (which is incredibly high) would ruin all your effort, and this is very frustrating.Second, maybe the DEV team knows that it's too hard to play when the enemies are too powerful, so they generously give some powerful units to players after chapters. It should not be a problem, the problem is the level of these units are usually much higher than ours, even if we have farmed a lot in the previous chapters. We can only use 14 units on each maps, so it should be more satisfy if we can glow up a powerful team by ourselves, instead of just giving us powerful units. (Some of them even just join us with bad reasons, like an unknown stowaway priest in the ship??)The Aspect shared the same problems too. We don't need to do anything to gain the Aspect, they will just be given to you automatically. Maybe I missed some special Aspect, but after I finished some chapters (precisely 2 of the chapters), I gain a lot of Aspect without doing anything. Third, the maps design are bad. The heroes traveled many places, each places have different maps, but there is no real difference at all. The maps just changed the appearance, but there is no actual use. No matter we are in the forest, in the temple or in a town, they are just the same only some of them are confusing. Sometimes if you are careless, you will miss a path or misunderstand a path easily.Of course there are some good advantages in the game, like most of the characters are adorable, some chapters are really well designed (I like the doppelganger and dragon chapter), and as I said at the beginning, I can feel the effort and passion of the Team, they did not just want to reproduce Fire Emblem, they want to make their own remarkable Dark Deity, so they tried to add different feature in the game. I won't recommend the game, but if the Team make another game in the future, I will definitely support it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, look, I was gonna type up a big review tearing this game apart for every little thing but I don't have the energy. I beat it on Deity, using all the characters I like. It's just not very good. Maybe the devs will fix bugs, jank, and tweak balance stuff in a way that doesn't put most of the impetus for making the game fun on the player, etc, but at present I just can't recommend the game and I'm heartbroken and exhausted as a result of that.If I hadn't received this game for free, I would have refunded it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot wrong with the game. _childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game a lot. It is pretty similar to being just another Fire Emblem clone, but the characters are spunky have pretty decent development. The story is engaging enough. The one thing I have issues with is it feels like there's way too many loading screens. In between "cut scenes", between battles, between chapters. Always a loading screen. If there's bound to be loading screens, at least make them thematic, maybe? But it's always the same stuff, which is boring. The loading screens also end up making everything feel rushed and kind of "mushed together" simply to push the story along. It'd be nice if there was some form of choice in at least some parts of the game (outside of the class advancements ofc). Outside of that it's everything you'd expect of a Fire Emblem game or Advanced Wars game with a touch of differences here and there. The last thing I have an issue with isn't necessarily the game itself, but it's the massive push of advertising I've ended up seeing as this "daring take on the RPG genre". Well played considering the amount of sales it's garnered, but it's so overbearing that all you see are ads when you attempt to look up information about the game. Whether it be about a bug or just how to do a specific thing as some aspects aren't explained out to you very well if at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Devs asked for an early review, so this is it.I've been anticipating this release for a long time now. To say I was excited is an understatement.However, that excitement isn't enough to overlook the severe lack of polish from an actual gameplay perspective. Controller support is spotty at best (within the first map, I've found multiple screens that don't work with it), and if you've played any turn based tactics games in the past, there are several features that will be missed (such as the ability to tab through enemy units.) There are several mechanics that simply aren't explained anywhere, or explained at extremely awkward places. For instance, the Ranger has the ability Haste. It's only *after* you select Haste, and select an ally to use it on that it states what it does. For each damage type, it shows what the modifiers are against different armour types. However, you can't see the inverse, you're just supposed to infer it, I guess. Trying to deduce mechanics is not what I want in a strategy game personally. Unfortunately, I think too much of the budget went towards the paint and not enough on the actual game. Things like voice acting shouldn't have even been considered with the game in the state it's currently in.This is currently not worth $20, not even close honestly. The very positive reviews are coming from an absolute rabid fan base.I'll be refunding after leaving this review. Don't think I'll bother checking it out later. My faith in the QA/Development team is simply nonexistent, and the fanbase too toxic.Had they called this a beta, and had they not requested reviews, I might be inclined to be more lenient.

_childDocuments_.review: It was good for a while. I edged my level ups all the time from the start. Put plenty of XP upgrades into accuracy, again and again. I planned routes. Carefully planned fights. Some levels were taxing, some were tough but doable as long as you were careful and didnt mind the deaths of some of your team (they respawn after the battle with a deduction from a random stat, nothing too serious)... Ive had a few of my team level up to 30 so I can get the advanced base builds... Then I got to chapter 18.Everyone on my team misses constantly. The enemy 1-hit kills most of my team. Its awful. I cant believe other people can beat that level. When I do occasionally get a hit, the amount of damage is laughable, bar one Conjurer. I've checked some guides and there's no mention of what I haven't done. I do not understand where I have gone wrong, and its too late to go back to the start and really overdrive my XP levels. It really sucks. A lot of time wasted.

_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I heard about this game's reputation and decided to hold off from playing it for the longest time. Now that the dust has settled and several patches have been pushed out, I figured "Okay. Now seems like a good time to give this game a chance"Unfortunately, I don't think this game is worth playing.Bear in mind, I am only reviewing it based on the gameplay. I haven't read any of the cutscenes, so for all I know, the story could be what makes up for the game's short comings. However, based on what other people have said about it, that probably isn't the case.The biggest issue with this game is that it is very slow. Enemies have enormous HP bars, and your chance to hit is astonishingly low. You'd think this would make the game difficult, but the enemy AI doesn't seem especially competent even on the highest difficulty, which is what I played on. They sometimes attack units who are not vulnerable to dying, or can outright kill them easily. Low accuracy applies to the enemies as well, so there really isn't any urgency when fighting them. There came a point where I was fighting a boss that only had a 1% chance to even hit me.The lack of permadeath compared to Fire Emblem is not necessarily a bad thing, but the punishment for losing a unit during a battle is basically a slap on the wrist. You lose a single stat, which only serves to make battles take longer rather than making them more difficult. If I were to rebalance this game, I think I would have had enemies be a lot more dangerous, and make each playable unit more unique and impactful. That way, if you lose someone, you lose a valuable resource, and cause a snowball effect as the current battle becomes more difficult.Anyway. There's a lot more problems I could cover, such as the sound design, but you get the gist. If what the creators' said is true and the game was built in such a way where it is hard to fix these problems, then I guess I can understand why it came out the way it is. However, this still makes me wary of whatever games they make in the future. Hopefully, they can prove my cynicism wrong though.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: A game of pros and cons that is able to take the mantle of "Fire Emblem like" and surprise me at times.Play if: You enjoy top down turn based games that are all about countering what stands in your wayDon't play if: You are looking for a Fire Emblem clone that will let you take the logic of the weapons triangle and armor is weak to magic. This game has a much more complex system of who is good against what.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is a fun turn based game and it's great value on sale but some battles are long and code error crashes after a lot of effort make it not worth its full price. It's also completely linear which isn't something I normally mind too much. A well crafted story with interesting maps and enemies is something that can often be preferable to the modern obsession with open world gaming and, for the most part, DD succeeds in this but the dialogue is often overly wordy and clicking through it - even when you WANT to hear everything that is said - can become tiresome after a while.There's no doubt it's a fun game and were it not for the crashes its other weaknesses would be well outweighed by its strengths so without them this would have been an easy recommendation even at it's full price. As is, DD remains a great buy when on sale but I can't give it a full endorsement. However, it's currently 75% off which is an absolute steal and even at 25% off it would be a fair buy. So this is another of those where I would have preferred to have been able to give a more neutral rating but the bugs towards the end are fairly numerous.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: So after beating the game of heroic mode, and about to start a hard mode campaign I will say that this game can, and will infuriate you at times. Because there are certain maps that are not in your favor at all if you try to do the slow approach. In which you are then punished by the enemy for having to "rush" to the end. The other problems I have with this game is that once you reach the 14 map character limit, you will then quickly be replacing all the units you've used up to that point with the new ones that the game just gave you, because they are higher level and thus are way more useful, because otherwise the enemy will two hit kill your older units if given the chance. Also some of the maps are just a hard level check on you.That being said though, I did enjoy my time playing the game. Even with all the loud yelling I sometimes did at it, or some of the harder mission that pushed me to my sanity limits. It does heavily inspire itself from the older Fire Emblem games, and while it is not a 100% comparison, it does what it takes well enough for it to scratch the itch that I was having for a new Fire Emblem-esce game. I do wish that the bonds actually were important to the game in some sense, or that there were secret missions you could unlock if you did a certain goal, so that it could add a little bit of replayability. Or that the characters wouldn't be completely replaceable once a new unit shows up. The other main flaw this game has is that the story is very lacking in feeling emotions. By the end of the game I really could care less about everyone but the main character. Everyone else I really had no attachment for.So to end I would say that I would recommend this game to people who really like Fire Emblem type games, and for people wanting a fun game that does challenge you. I would not recommend it to people who do not like Fire Emblem games, or people who do not enjoy unit strategy games. It was well worth the price of admission for me, and I would rate it as one of the more enjoyable indie strategy games (Such as Banner of the Maid) 8.25 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral option I would pick it. However there is not so from a general gaming perspective, I would not recommend this game.If you're a fan of the Fire Emblem brand of strategy RPGs and want something new to scratch that itch definitely pick this up when it's on sale. Barring some significant updates I would not pay more than $15 USD for this game.Pros:- Large Roster- Customizable options such as random recruitment order, random classes, and random stat growths for fun runs after you initial playthrough.- Nostalgic pixel art and animations for fans of the GBA Fire Emblem games in particular- Decently lengthy campaign.- Interesting middle ground between permadeath and casual play where a unit will face permanent stat penalties if they die on a map, but are still able to be used afterward.Cons:- Buggy. Units will sometimes "ghost" in the map meaning enemies will end up being untargettable for a turn, or your units will warp between positions randomly. Not frequent, but very frustrating when it happens.- Music cuts in and out very jarringly between combat and the map. I assume this is a quirk of the game being made on Gamemaker.- The writing is actually just bad. Sorry, but neither the story nor the characterization is interesting or coherent. It reads like a bad teenaged fanfiction author. I can tolerate tropey narratives, or very stereotypical rehashes, but the writing in this game is just an actual mess.- The balance is pretty terrible. Some maps will jump in difficulty pretty wildly.- The combat systems are poorly explained, and lack proper documentation in game, again likely due to Game Maker limitations.- UI and menus are also a pain to navigate. The downsides to Game Maker really make themselves known here.Overall:If you were a fan of GBA Fire Emblem games and spent a lot of time playing through modded versions of those games, and want something in a similar vein, this game should be a decent fit. If you like just going through the motions of a strategy RPG then this game is probably a good fit.The game feels like it was made by a single amateur dev, but then again there are real gems out there such as Stardew Valley that were created all from scratch by a single person. Hell there are even some GBA Fire Emblem mods out there that are more polished and well put together than Dark Deity. This game fills a niche that isn't commonly catered to, especially on PC, and that's probably the only reason to be interested in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: So just beat the game on normal difficulty last night. It's a good game, definitely heavy GBA FE vibes, and the artwork is fantastic. Story wise it's pretty ok. The creator is definitely a Wheel of Time/Cosmere/Robert Jordan/Brandon Sanderson fan. And the beginning feels a bit rushed in that you don't really get to know any of the starter cast very well before the new characters start showing up. Very frequently I would forget who was who.Gameplay-wise, it differs in a few key areas vs FE: weapon triangle is different and based on armor the units wear e.g. plate, chain, etc. Interesting spin imo. Class choices are interesting, but the strange part to me is that, for each of your 6 base classes, there's 4 options for level 10 promotion. For something like Ranger (bow starter class) you have 2 bow options and 2 sword options at level 10, but the characters sometimes have only bow/quiver art on their in-game portrait art and very often the stronger play is to go swords at level 10 for class skill and growths. This hurts in another way since now you have 0 projectile damage for 1/2 the game + you have even MORE melee units - just a weird feel to it. Lastly, almost every new character that you get comes in over-levelled and gives each of them a pre-promote feel. There are no Ests in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: The weapon system is lame. You get tokens to upgrade instead of experience on the character. You upgrade your character, then he gets left in the dust by the new higher level version of him who gets assigned to your team between every battle.What does the bond system even do? If im going to spend 30 min clicking around through lame dialog, can it at least show me how its helping?Why does every turn based RPG rely on dodge to make later battles harder? Eventually a game will come out with an interesting game mechanic that makes combat harder without just having the higher level enemies having 60% dodge. This game isnt it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is a game that touches on some of the best aspects of Turn-based Strategy RPGs like Fire Emblem, but also has so many issues that seem easily fixed.To begin, the art style for characters outside of combat is great. I only wish the in-battle sprites were a bit more tailored to each character rather than being so identical aside from hair and clothing color. Map and battle designs start out relatively well, but quickly get repetitive or just plain oversimplified. There are plenty of enemies to fill the space, but most missions feel like nothing more than "Take your giant mob of people this way and murder everyone in your path". I feel like a lot more could have been done.I'll note that there's one character who is nothing more than a fountain of internet memes who both looks and sounds like he's the main character of a teenager's edgy fanfiction story. Every other line of his is just a reference, which is extremely jarring especially when he offers no plot significance whatsoever.CLASSES, oh boy. As much as I LOVE the way promotions are handled in this game (being able to promote to any of the 4 options regardless of your original choice) I found myself sticking to one or two promotions for every single character because some of them are just SO PAINFULLY BAD. I mean who in their right mind would choose +1 range to pushing another character over extra movement AND increased crit chance per square moved that turn? I had a character with a consistent 80%+ crit chance and he was invincible. Huge missed opportunity here. I think the system itself is great, just done very poorly in terms of balancing.Aside from one track, the music never really caught my attention. No epic music to listen to during tense battles or anything. I'd have just as good a time with the sound turned completely off, and that's coming from a musician who loves the audio aspect of games more than most.TLDR: Despite my complaints, I really did enjoy the game. I like what was done here and have high hopes for improvements or patches (which the developer seems very quick with so far), but in its current state you'd have to be chomping at the bit for FE-inspired games to pick this up. Still, it was fun for a single playthrough. Might give that campaign customization tool a try. For $25, it's not like you're burning through your rent money if you're willing to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: For how cheap it is right now, I definitely recommend if you're a fan of Fire Emblem. This is an entertaining homage to the Game Boy Advance generation of games. That being said, it is missing a lot of polish and looks like it was made from a group of fans. Starting from the first mission, I was confused why all allies and enemies were facing the same direction. I noticed a sequel is going to be released this year, so I'll definitely support them with that. That being said, I hope they make a lot of improvements and be more Fire Emblem friendly in all aspects.Edit: After playing more missions, it is evident that the game is filled with bugs. Not sure how they remained in the game after so many years. A character's hair changes color at some point, then it randomly changes back to the original color with no explanation. Then the mission I just completed, it changed again. The big bug I've ran into is what I would describe as a "ghost" of a character that you can't select. Sometimes it was due to them dying, other times I just couldn't select them at all and had to end their turn. Quite annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty ambitious entry into the FE clone world especially on the PC market.  However there are a lot of things to consider as strengths and weaknesses before going in and buying as I did. I am on the fence about regretting my purchase, normally I would refund games like this but I wanted to give it a fair chance because I know FE / FE style games take time to explore mechanics properly.Lets start with a few pros: *Artwork - Very professionally done artwork no designs really fall behind when it comes to characters, everything is nice and clean. ( Some of the sprites could use a little work though for combat animations to make characters feel more unique) *Animation - I feel needs to be mentioned on its own. There is an extreme attention to detail when this team tackled the animations. They captured the FE style combat animations perfectly and did a great job making each classes attacks and crits feel unique. *Class variety- There is a lot of good departure from the usual norms in games like this and it gives you the illusion of diversity...however this falls short for a few reasons.*General Game feel - Feels very similar to FE games but something is a bit off.Cons : Weapon Triangle ( lack of ) : None of the counters make any sense at all, You have different weapons / damage types that are good/bad against specific armors. In practice what this means is you never are really sure if a unit should be engaging another unit unless you just try out every unit on all the enemies because things that would normally make sense like say magic vs beefy armored guy doesn't always ( and often doesn't ) mean an advantage. With enough time I am sure one could learn this system, but its very flawed in that it is too convoluted up front to make much sense to a new player. Especially one coming from FE with expected rock paper scissors.Bugs : Heaps of nasty bugs from characters not being able to be selected on your turn to disappearing UI / obscured UI. Not to mention the bugs associated with "pushing" other characters around which causes their sprite to violently shake until the next turn or until they move. Also I swear something is off about the calculated hit %'s but I have not bothered to test.Upgrading weapons : Neat idea on paper but ends up really feeling unrewarding , no longer do you have the FE style preparing for your enemy, you just sink your money into one or two weapons on each person and hope that those weapons give you the best results. Class Diversity : In games like FE ,classes... especially promotion classes had distinctive flavor and play-style to each of them. Here you have tons of classes that all sort of feel the same more or less, despite their different sprites and unique passives not enough thought was put into making them really feel different from each other. In this case maybe quality would have been the better route than quantity. Also promotions are instant at level 10 without any way to see what the best promote for the character would be stats wise so it is very easy to end up bricking a character by not having remembered their strengths.The maps: They start out simple enough, but fairly quickly they become hectic swarms of enemies that prevent you from setting up any sort of real strategy aside from reloading saves to see how your dice fare or changing starting positions on the map over and over to get the best results.Story / Character development. :  Since chapter 2-3 I no longer read any dialogue, all the bond convos I skipped over as well as I didn't care enough about any of the characters to read it , unlike say in FE where these were fun ways of exploring the background of your favorite characters.I could go on, for every good thing the game offers as a FE clone it has 2-3+ things that could be brought up as major flaws in the design / mechanics. I think its probably the best you are going to find for PC as far as FE clones go currently, but still has many problems that really hold it back as a game. Unfortunately when you build a game based on another, it will inevitably be compared to that game harshly. The unique mechanics this game offers do not make it stand out as its own game in a good way. All in all 20-25 USD might not be a lot, especially once the bugs are squashed but its worth knowing these facts prior to purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is a decent fire emblem - like game but thats about it.I'm actually surprised this isn't an early access game due to how unpolised it is in it's current state.List of some issues I'm having,- UI has a lot of issues, such as when promoting, the 'promoting button' is just text on the top right corner of the screen and I couldn't figure it out for a long while. - Alot of the sprites look like they were ripped from GBA fire emblem games and just painted over. Gives it a very fe rom-hack vibe, which tbh isn't a good vibe imo.- Map sprites all face left for some reason, I guess it's a design choice, but I really dislike it.- The maps themselves are pretty ugly and confusing, I was pretty early in the game and there were portals and it was difficult to tell which portal leads to progress just cause they were all so similar in color, which btw sucks to be color-blind.- Character art and sprites do not match at all, imagine being a super busty mage lady in character art and then suddenly your battle sprite is just flat. I guess it was too difficult to make individual sprites for each character.-It's generic fire-emblem style, the differences really needed a tutorial or something cause the game doesn't explain anything.-Promoting units is confusing since you can't see the actual changes that happens stat-wise, it just tells you a basic description. -In battle the numbers at the top doesn't indicate whether the attack twice. It gets really confusing since some animations do multi-hits. -So many loading screens, I'm already tired of looking at angry looking king talking to guy and 4 kids doing training and I'm not that far into the game.Anyways, they really need to polish the game a lot more cause these small UI problems and lack of tutorial is annoying. Until then, just skip this game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the GBA era fire emblem games, i have to say that i picked up this game solely because it so unashamedly shows the inspiration it took from those games: the blue/red movement tilesets, the pixel animations, the level-up screens, the attack animations - everything shows very clearly where the idea for this game came from. My only hope was that they managed to capture well what makes those games fun.And man oh man did they capture what makes those games fun.The supports, the combat that starts off very tactical and then slowly devolves into a kill-fest where you toss your overfed allies into hoards of enemies and watch as theyre all torn apart, the beautifully animated attacks - it just  it. It even does a lot of things better than those games, such as the weapon system which is a lot of fun to play around with, as opposed to fire emblems 'just give everyone as many silver weapons as you can afford,' being able to support as many characters as you want (which, unfortunately, was only added after the GBA era), the increased freedom in promotions with cool skills, built-in stat pages showing peoples growths and how their stats change upon different promotions, the unique combat skills for each class, built-in randomiser and stat/growth sliders for replayability - all things that are a very welcome addition to an already great line of games.That said, there is one major issue with the game, one that many other commenters have already noted as well: this game has an extreme lack of polish. It is riddled with weird bugs and jank. Characters will occasionally move a tile to the side while its not your turn (i glitched a character off the ship during the sea level, which obviously wasnt intended, as my character could just run around on water killing off all the sea-borne enemies), enemies being rerandomised upon reloading a level, promotion pages just straight up showing a completely wrong description for the skills you'll get, some weirdness with the save page (some other reviewers have mentioned a lack of a battle save - there actually is one, its just extremely easy to miss. Its automatically made and can be found by clicking the 'battle save' button in the load screen).Frankly, I'd been holding out hope the developers would come around to fixing these issues, but it doesn't seem like this'll be the case, as they seem more focused on making other content, such as the dlc, the switch port, and simply other game(s).I still recommend the game, especially if you're a fire emblem fan, as it really does scratch that itch, despite its flaws, and it really is just a lot of dumb fun. However, the recommendation does come with a warning that you'll have to be willing to look past the lack of polish for this otherwise great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall:Worth playing for strategy rpg fans, with more emphasis on the strategy part. Has some unique ideas on how to create class, item, and skill systems which are in some cases more interesting than those in fire emblemPros:- Interesting class system, with flexibility in upgrade paths that keeps character uniqueness.- Half-ish of the skills alter play patterns, like mixed weapon types, increase heal range, healing on crits, etc. They can be combined to create some interesting architypes- Deep wounds system instead of permadeath keeps a pretty good reason for keeping units alive, but it isn't quite as punishing as permadeath, so it's easier to keep going after losing a few units.- The story seems pretty solid and the characters seem decently well written for those that appreciate writing- Aspects are a really nice take on legendary weapons/items. There are like 30 of them, they have a wide variety, most include trade offs (like lose dodge to gain defense), and they are freely tradeable between units. These allow for quite a bit of interesting build customization and should improve the replayability- It's pretty fun to optimize units. One example, take a really weak unit, stack a bunch of crit and then use an aspect which swaps power and crit, and then that unit attacks for really high damage despite being a low strength unit.Cons:- Weapons lack variety. No effects, just different stats.- Weapon upgrade system is weak. There is a single upgrade path, upgrades only grant stats and sometimes make you slower (by increasing weight), and the game doesn't give enough upgrade tokens to really experiment- A lot of class and personal skills just change numbers around, rather than alter the play patterns. Maybe half of the total skills. They are generally powerful, but they're mostly uninteresting- The game has a lot of percent-based buffs (like power +20%), which benefits most from optimizing a few stats instead of getting a high average. This makes it more difficult to take advantage of the class system flexibility

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review, I want to preface it by saying I ADORE this game already. It's got fun dialogue and fun gameplay. It's also the first time I've really seen a Tactical RPG finally take into account the different kinds of armors.However, there are many things I have qualms with involving this game. First, the music is incredibly repetitive. This is easily solvable by simply turning the music to 0%. Second, this game has some odd quirks with its UI. Some parts look clickable but aren't, and some menus can only be closed by either pressing a specific key (e.g. you can only progress past the battle summary menu by pressing enter), or you can't use keys to exit it (e.g. the escape menu can't be closed by pressing escape again). Overall, though, this doesn't detract too much from the game, and I think it's incredibly fun despite how little time I spent playing it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Though a fairly obvious first game (as far as I can tell this is the developers first game don't be surprised if I'm wrong) it has enough genuine potential and fun game-play to justify purchasing it for its asking price (at time of writing that would be around $25, I got it for around $19.99 due to a sale) if the most recent E3 left all you fire emblem fans disappointed I'd recommend giving this one a try. Just be aware that while its a fun game, its not going to be another three houses. (I'd personally put it a little below Fire Emblem Blazing Blade) and keep an eye out for the quality of life fixes that are likely to be put out as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of Fire Emblem. Normally I don't write reviews but i feel this one needs a quick tid bit. It was very enjoyable at first and then progression sped up very fast and the difficulty curve increased dramatically. There are way too many characters, and the fact that they all travel together but you only can use half in some huge maps is ridiculous. I like the concept and the characters are very likable but I think the execution in the tactical genre failed as well as story writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game, and a pretty solid fire emblem clone, however it needs more polishing. I understand having to release this game during the E3 hype, but ultimately this game would benefit alot more from polishing. Alot of the maps, (4 to 5 in particular) are just giant squares with nothing in it, or massive hallways with nothing happening. The lack of clarity during battle is confusing, such as the advantages and disadvantages of different weapons, leading to me just using the most upgraded weapon to kill most anyways regardless of weapon advantage. The lack of terrain advantages like forests and forts is also disappointing for a strategy/fire emblem clone, and the pacing of the story is tad rushed. It's not all bad though, I love the class lineup, the sprite work is beautiful, and the story is pretty solid as well as the characters, adding a lot of replay factor. There were also a lot of chapters that were really fun despite the map design, and its always fun having a character you built up from the beginning nuke everyone in their path (though i do wish for a bonus exp system similar to path of radiance if i want to use specific units).Ultimately, Dark Deity is a solid tactical game and a solid fire emblem clone, but it CAN be better. I've seen the developers already fix initial bugs and issues. Hopefully later on they can add more replayability, fix a lot of the maps (especially the mid/late game), make it more clear with some of the systems it has, and make it more enjoyable. I have faith it can be better :)-Franzie

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity calls back to the GBA era of Fire Emblem, and sadly doesn't quite measure up. The Story is underwhelming. It's not merely derivative, it lacks even decent plot hooks to justify the party's involvement. At least when the bad guy blows up the main character's hometown I know why he's fighting. The lead protagonist is maximally generic. Stick a slightly self aware tone to him and he'd be a stock parody. The rest of the writing lacks impact. For a game with Dark in the title, this title is pretty meek to do anything dramatic. Even the Villains get a soft focus. Do you love when a story tells you that one note evil bad guy had some crappy thing happen to them that should make you feel bad? This is the anime cliche for you. The cast balance is spread far too thin across the narrative. When everyone gets a word in, no one stands out. While the old Fire Emblem formula of only having a half dozen units truly matter in the plot had its issues. this was an over correction in the opposite direction. The character design has it's ups and downs as you'll easily in other reviews. Vesta might be the silliest variant of boob window full plate girl I've seen in years. Tactics: It's a counter attack heavy meta. Units with life recovery, heavy damage mitigation, or tanks (in both traditional and blink flavors) will generally be much more reliably potent than anything else. To the game's credit, most Units are decent to good, and only a few truly suck. With the ways the game flows, no unit's offensive prowess on your turn will match the ability of the enemy's phase to feed your top performers kills. You also get a lot of units too soon, although that plays more havoc with the aforementioned narrative than it does with the game difficulty. Credit where it's due, turning the clerics from fragile units armored only in their misbegotten faith to decent DnD-esque clerics who can smack occasionally in melee is a neat alternative to babying them in classic FE until they finally promote. The real issue is the game's lack of elegance. FE has minimal mechanics that lead to addicting variation. Advantages in battle between units are few and powerful. Dark Deity has a way too many small inconsistent bonuses spread across the field that you're never really quite sure what they all mean until you actually see the battle preview screen. The fact that units' mutual advantage/disadvantage isn't shown on the map without clicking on the enemy unit in question doesn't help. Granted, with no item durability and unit deaths being a debuff rather than outright perma-elimination means you can afford a more cavalier attitude, but I prefer system clarity whenever possible. Maps: The maps are pretty blah. To the dev's credit, some of the more egregious examples have been reworked. Still, the dozen variant goals of the maps rarely meaningfully translate to the turn-by-turn. There's a few good ideas here and there, but generally you're either attack sweeping across a field or defending/surviving with slight wrinkles. The lack of any terrain tiles beyond walls is a hard obstacle to overcome. System: There are still some stage crashing bugs. I was able to reboot enough times to get around it, but it is something to be aware of. QoL features are a bit lacking but improving. Subsequent campaign runs give you some excellent setting tweaks, but some standbys are surprisingly absent. Turning off combat animations turns them off completely, so you're left 'surprised' after the enemy phase about how much health everyone has. The FE standby that showed damage taken while skipping the sprites feels necessary for a game from the 2020s. The game does have a battle save now, and the system isn't especially lethal since death only results in stat loss, but still, for those truly perfectionistic tacticians out there, it's pick your poison. Overall, this is fine, but as unmemorable as the soundtrack I haven't bothered to mention. A sequel, especially one captained by an experienced writer and bolder narrative and map choices is something worth watching for.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played up to Chapter Six so far, so I'd say these are my initial impressions. As a huge Fire Emblem fan, this game fantastic and satisfying. It reminds me a lot of Wargroove with its more simplistic style and battle format. There are significant variations from current Fire Emblem iterations though. I am really enjoying the weapons system so far. Each class seems to have an inherent set of four weapons that all have different focuses. There doesn't seem to be any weapon durability or limit to how many times a unit can heal. The combat map is pretty simplistic and so far, the goals of each chapter have varied from "rout enemy" to "last x amount of turns" to "beat chapter boss." Pretty standard.The supports are pretty good as well. The game is not fully voice acted, but the small voice blurbs are enjoyable all the same. There seem to be a good mesh of characters so far, and I'm excited to see who I can recruit in the future. As the game has advertised, there are a large variety of classes. I've only promoted a few units so far, but the promotion tree looks promising. Each class can learn new skills and have different advantages, which are a bit lost on you in the first playthrough. Mostly because I'm not sure what to anticipate coming up. I'm excited to min/max later on, though. Something I didn't particularly like, and something I think this game could draw from Fire Emblem, is the ability to highlight a specific enemy. Y turns on enemy range, but you cannot select a specific enemy to have their range darkened or highlighted specifically. Another note is that occasionally, hovering over a character brings up a popup, which can sometimes obscure other important information on the map. I'd like to have a chapter restart button too, just for convenience. Looking at my playtime vs. progress so far, I don't think this game will have the playtime of say, Fire Emblem 3H. However, one thing I did notice was the ability to randomize recruit order, character growth rates (or something like that), and other various aspects of the game within the game options itself. I can see randomized runs being a very large factor in replayability later on. I can't wait to finish my first playthrough and do a randomized run, once I have fully learned the systems and characters of the game. At the current 20% off, I'd say it's a definite buy for Fire Emblem-like fans. The art is cute, the music is pretty good, writing is decent, and it is an overall great first impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is a game inspired by Fire Emblem and have some alright to good character designs.The class tree is actively interesting and enjoyable to see as the class tree is much like Fire Emblem Sacred Stones, except everyone a rookie class upon acquiring them. I am on chapter 10 and so far the story is just alright. The supports in the game are enjoyable as with any game like this it allows the player to see what the characters are like and how they interact with each other. The weapon triangle is interesting and refreshing and it does matter to an extent as there is a character like Cia who can kind of make the weapon triangle of sorts meaningless. But the weapon triangle is focused on what type of damage that class does. The type of damage range from slash, pierce, blunt, arcane, fire, thunder, light, etc. and each one has a type of armor they have an advantage against ranging from Plate, Leather, Chainmail, and Robes. So far every weapon type has an advantage against 2 armor types and a disadvantage against two armor types.Another interesting thing about the battle system is that everyone has 4 weapons ranging from Damage being Red, Accuracy being Green, Crit being Blue, and Balance type being Yellow. You can upgrade each of the 4 weapons to have them do more damage, have more accuracy, have a higher crit, or less weight. Promoting the class keeps the upgrade if you were curious.Downside though about the game which is bothersome is that there are still some bugs that need to be tweaked. One such bug is going to the main menu and hoping the game does not crash. Another bug that I just ran into was in Chapter 9 or 10 where you have to defend for 8 turns. 8 turns pass one of my characters died and suffered a permanent minus 4 or 6 in hp, I pressed escape hoping for the menu to pop up so I can press main menu but it crashed (to be expected). Boot up the game, press battle save and I am now on turn 10 of the map. Press next turn and it is now turn 11. Chapter continues. Now the game has had from what I've seen 13? updates to fix bugs and the like so far. In my opinion the game is interesting mainly for the gameplay because the game does have a randomizer which is something I was not expecting, but considering how this is Fire Emblem inspired it is to be expected as the fans of the game to do randomizers of Fire Emblem 6, 7, and Sacred Stones primarily Sacred Stones. Overall I'd give the game a 7/10 primarily because of the bugs that I have encountered while playing the game. One such bug that I encountered that I have just remembered is having my characters being absolutely smirfed. Now, I don't know wth I did or how it happened but it did. I don't remember pressing anything in the randomizer option but it could also be a bug. So if you team has like 18 or so health when you start on normal difficulty then I'd recommend to restart.

_childDocuments_.review: Over all Dark deity is a solid SRPG that pulls a lot from earlier entries in the Fire Emblem series. Although at first glance this may seem like a clone, there are stark differences in how it plays out that will keep you interested. If you remember older SRPG games fondly, this game will likely hit home for you both in its familiarity and novelty.There have been some bugs that have sprung up since launch, but the dev team has proven themselves to be dedicated to maintaining and perfecting the game they have already given so much love and care to. This being their first release, Dark Deity is not perfect, but it is promising and well worth the purchase. If you want to see more games in this style and genre then show some support and give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few 16 bit style "Fire Emblem" type games on Steam.  This is probably the 2nd best one I have played (Vestaria Saga is my tops).  This game gets a lot of things right:  The combat, nice variety of characters, good voice acting (although limited), character interactions, nice progression system, good character artwork.   The downside is probably the lack of original objectives.  Too many maps is just a battle of attrition. They occasional mix it up, but most battles is just wipe out the other team.  Also, the in-game sprites are lackluster.  I will still give this a very solid 8/10, and a must play for Fire emblem fans.  I think Vestaria Saga (both 1 and 2) are better gameplay wise, but Dark Diety is a solid contender, and I have the sequel on my wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty I'll make this quick: it's like a mix of old school (pixelated graphics) and new school (bonding conversation system) Fire Emblem. Weapons are unbreakable and each unit has four types to choose from, which they can change between on the go during battle. Each weapon tends to focus on one specific stat (like power, accuracy) or a balance between all. Weapon tokens can be purchased and found to upgrade each character's weapons.Is there permadeath? No, but there is a Grave Wound system. Depending on what kills your character, they receive a permanent reduction in one of their stats.Each unit has a class, which can then be promoted to one of three different specialized classes when they reach level 10 and 30. You are not restricted to a certain branching path when you promote, so you have the freedom to choose whatever when you reach the last tier.The combat is engaging and the story is pretty solid too. There is a big cast of characters and they can be pretty fun, even though the main character is a bit lame and heavy on the hero-type trope. Do I recommend this game? Hell yeah I do, it's solid tactical combat in a retro package. If you want a fuller, more detailed professional review head on over to  because I don't want to sit here all day and type this out lol
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: So, Dark Deity, a game I was REALLY hyped for and after the recent E3 presentaion form Nintendo, I was even happier to see that it just came out! I am a huge fan of SRPGs like Fore Emblem and the Saga games, so I will use them as a comparison point, yet I woun't hold this game to the standard those series' have. That would be unfair, seeing as they have alot more resources. I have played the game up to chapter 8, so some of the points I will make may get adress during later stages of the game.Yet the game has some big problems form a regular SRPG perspective. Some of these may be personal problems I have with how the game is designed, but some of these are just general problem that either are the way they are by design or need to get adressed in the near future.First off, I'd like to praise the game a bit.The gameplay itself is really fun. The weapon system, having 4 different weapons at your disposal, each with a different stat allocation, is a fresh take on the gamepaly loop. On top of that, the way you upgrade those weapons, with tokens ranging form level 1 to level 4, complements this system very well. It lets you choose which way you want to gear you characters towards.Another good aspect about the game is the way the story integrates the characters you meet along the way. Up to the point I played, each side character gets a good amount of story moments, not beeing just religated to support hell. Seeing as the roster of character will only increase, this may change over the span of the game. Yet the stuff that is currently there is nice and entertaining. While I'm on the characters, I can say that the current cast of units is fun and interesting. They aren't the deepest of characters right now, but they are just fun to use, with their supports giving them a good few options for character interaction. My personal favorites are characters like Cia, Elias and Garrick. The voice acting, altough in the style of Fire Emblem Awakening (little expressions and short voice lines), helps them out alot and so far, every VA did a good job of giving the characters life.Now that I have showcased some good points about the game, I would like to highlight the probelms that exist within the game.The biggest problem I have with the game is the UI and how the game presents the player the information they need. Alot of the gameplay mechanics aren't explained to you. The armor and damage type system, similar to the weapon triangle in consept, giving certain classes advantages against other classes, isn't explained to you at all, making you guess at first why some character have a red or green arrow and why not. After some time, i figured it out on my own, but not getting told about such a crucial mechanic seems weared to me.This leads perfectly into the biggest problem I have with the UI, the fact that you can't inspect the details of you opponents equipment. During the early stages, a good amount of enemys use axes/cleave damage, yet without having a character of the same damage type yourself, you can't see what stats their weapons have. On top of that, you can't look at what a item held by your oppnents does. During the second chapter of the game, one of the bosses holds an item called a "hot bean juice". Seeing as all items up to that point have been healing items, I assumed that it too would just be a strong healing item to insentivise you to go and merc him. Turns out, it's a speed stat boosert, which really frustrated me after not being able to optain it, because I wasn't able to read its description and plan accordingly to optain it.Another problem that exists is the way menus and battle forecasts display themselfs and function. Using a controller feels somewhat weird, because alot of menus aren't designed around it or don't feel like they were. Double confirmations, choosing the wrong menu or option, not being able to move the chamera because you switched to the next character (R1 on my PS4 contoller) and the way trading and the inventory works. If you choose a menu, it sometimes feels like you didn't actually choose it. This happens alot during inventory management and choosing support conversations. This may be a personal problem of incompentecy.Lastly, I want to talk about the lack of polish this game has. I may be nitpicking here, but some things just look janky and unfinished.The character portraits are all really good looking and the artist did a really good job giving each one a destinct look. Sadly this doesn't reflect well into the battle animations. For example, Sloane's battle model looks really of. Her hair looks like spaghetti or something, I initially didn't recognize her. Another example would be how Sophia looks in her portrait in comperison to how she looks ingame. I know that not every character can get a unique animation for each of their classes to perfectly represent them, but alot of the class sprites are just one simple colour with no real details or special look to them based on their gender. Fire Emblem hadgender specific differences for each class, maybe a ponytail or different clothing altogether. It made each character and class look unique among themselves, but here everyone just looks the same. I know with the amount of classes, this may seem like alot of work, but it just feels like alot of work has been put into stuff like character art and voice acting instead of thing like the animations, which you will be seeing throughout the whole game.The animations themselves range from good and ok to boring and forgettable. I know I said I wouldn't hold this game up to the standards of the GBA FE Games, but over the years, alot of independent animators have shown that it is possible to create cool and interesting looking animations for these types of games, which makes me even sader to see that the animation just feel boring. They don't feel like poweful blows are being exchanged. They lack the visual bravado and feedback that the older sprite based animations of older SRPGs provide. This lack of polish can also be seen in the Duelist's crit animation. So, for all the people with OCD out there, this one is for you! For you see, if you look at the right shoulder pad, the moment the character jumps to the opponent to strike them, a lone brown pixle (in Cia's case) remains there until the character finished his or her attack and returns to the default position. And while we are on the topic of the Duelist, why is the Duelist, who, judging from the battle animation and map sprite, uses a rapier, a SLASH DAMAGE type class. This is probably gameplay and balancing related decision, but it feeld weird to me.I'm sorry I got so negativ and nitpicky towards the end, but I really like the game so far, but so much of the expirience gets bogged down by the obvious problems that exist, some that I haven't even touched upon, like the lack of different generic enemy character and class art. (Why does the Barbarien use the Cleric/Mage character art?)I have alot of fun with the game so far, and will definetly play it through to the end, so im sorry if things will change troughout the game.I know didn't touch upon the balancing as a whole, but to be fair I am only at the beginning, so I can't really say alot about it right now, just some things. Your characters all feel useful and can all contribute, yet the fact that chapter 4 has mages with extremly high magic, that could two shot nearly everyone that isn't a HP tank, AND have a chance to crit is kinda not really fun to be honest.Right now, I am going to recommend this game ONLY to the core fanbase of SRPGs, people who know what they get themselfs into and are ok with some jank, because the core gameplay of an SRPG is fun.Sadly, for everybody else, who just want a good starting point for the genre or are more accustomed to the newer Fire Emblem games, I would recommend looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Early impressions so far, really. This game was hailed as a new take on Fire Emblem, and I have to say outright that they succeed on injecting some new ideas into an old game type. PROS-It definitely scratches a strategy RPG itch, with a style that few games follow. If you want it, it's here.-Once you get pasts the polish issues, the game is surprisingly engaging and fun, and the ideas that they have implemented are ones I would be interested in seeing in future SRPG games-I was not a believer in the "choose whatever branching class you want" path the game took. I personally like my characters to have one track, like older Fire Emblem games. However, the ability to customize your team is a lot of fun, and the variety on tap here is very fun. Meanwhile, characters still have a niche to fill, thanks to their starting classes dictating what branches they can pursue.-Character designs and voice acting are very interesting, so far. I like them a lot, but your mileage may vary here.-Excellent campaign and difficulty adjustment options. Having access to randomizers and growth mods is a very interesting include that should really be in all games like this.NEUTRAL-Story so far (getting on 10 chapters in) is fine. I'm not expecting this to be Genealogy of the Holy War. I find the characters engaging enough to build my own through-narrative, though, so they've nailed the flavor that most Fire Emblem games achieve-Music ranges from very, very meh to surprisingly decent. "Low budget" definitely comes through on this one, with so many of the tracks feeling thinly written. I haven't run into anything too memorable on this front, which is a shame. -Combat isn't as transparent as Fire Emblem, thanks to the weapon advantage system lifted from Warcraft 3. Each character does a certain kind of damage (say, slashing...or fire) that deals more damage to certain types of armor and less to others. It's set as a % bonus, instead of a flat one like Fire Emblem would use. This can make it quite tough to figure out if your character is in too much danger, and you have to "feel" it out a lot more. I don't mind that so much, since I don't play these games that carefully.-The high growths in this game are turning my characters into monsters on hard mode, kind of like what can happen in Fire Emblem Awakening. I don't know if this will make the game a cakewalk later, but I dig the old-school stingy level ups that make the vanishingly rare perfect level up something to really celebrate. Another one of those "your mileage may vary" things that might not affect the overall game experience.BAD-Polish and user experience leave a lot to be desired. I won't dwell on them, because other reviews cover these polish issues to no end. Yes, you have to click a lot. Yes, the battle animations cut back to the map in a very jarring way. Yes, there are plenty of unexplained mechanics. I'll be quick to point out here that I don't think that lack of polish ruins the game. It's a bit disappointing, because games like Stardew give us a sense of what an indie game COULD be. As long as you don't go in expecting the "Stardew of Fire Emblem" games, there is a lot to sink your teeth into and enjoy. I think it's a no-brainer for Fire Emblem fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game and 100%'d it a few weeks back, gave my thoughts some time to ruminate in my head. Brutally honest opinion is that it's just "okay". The game honestly isn't bad and has some good ideas, it even has a bit of a charm with its very well-written character interactions and support conversations, but it has about as many flaws as it does things that it excels. In particular the weapon versus armor match-ups, the replacement for the weapon triangle, is far more convoluted and not always clear. Still had plenty of fun, but didn't find myself overly hooked in like how Fire Emblem titles tend to grab me.I would recommend the game still, and to not go into it with too high of expectations, and would genuinely love to see a follow-up game from the devs down the line to polish up the bad and expand upon the good. I think there's a lot of potential here, and it's great for a first attempt by an indie studio to where I'd say it nearly even succeeds at going toe-to-toe with Fire Emblem, but it comes up just a tiny bit short. I'd argue to be any harsher when comparing the two is a bit unfair, considering that one is made AAA studio with years of experience and titles to expand upon and the other is a passion project by a fresh studio, but a lot of the criticism in those critical reviews are still valid.An enjoyable title regardless of the bad, as long as you can appreciate the good.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty hyped for this game all things considered but it simply did not live up to expectations closely and i can't bear to play a lot more.Firstly the mechanics and strategic elements in the game aren't really explained, the ability for each class is not explained till after you try to use it, so you don't even know when you can use it in the first place. The story feels rushed and they say characters names as if we know them already and sometimes brush over an introduction.Secondly balancing. being as one of the ways they advertised was Tiktok I knew ahead of time balancing wasn't going to be all that important to them as they said something like "it could take away the fun of the game if its too restrictive" and I agree with that. But restrictiveness is not the only thing needed for balancing, the one i had a problem with being the sheer lack of care for the power output of the players characters. It's either not enough and takes 3 characters to take one down, or just 1 character to do almost all its health in one attack, i.e ranger in chapter 2 doing like 19 damage to one enemy. or in stage 1 and 3, where one character could blitz through all the enemies like they are nothing, stage 1's being the mage and stage 3 being the LEVEL 9 CLERIC they just give you, that for the first few enemies takes 0 damage from their attacks, while others you have could just die outright. he also hits for like 13-17, and the spear girl they give you can hit 15x2 in a turn, killing any enemy like that.Another balancing issue is the simple fact of characters being to frail. rouges are practically known for being pretty frail fighters so its not a surprise they won't be damage sponges in many games, but the rouge in this game can't even live long enough to get back to a healer, I had her in the back as to just not get destroyed and she got jumped by a single enemy and instantly wiped.The pacing is very off and inconsistent, the story is shaped oddly and in stage 2 two characters show up in the bottom right and to my knowledge simply aren't explained at all, and it makes me think I could get the same experience, or even a better one playing fire emblem on the game boy advanced.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I don't feel compelled enough to write a review.  However I loved FE games and this is what drew me to buy this one.  The game play is very similar to older FE games.  Not being able to truly grind was a bit annoying, but not that big of a deal.  What had me very annoyed with this one, was the bugs, and the lack of a save feature.  First the bugs.  When promoting at first I could see how a units stats were affected by the class change.  Once I hit the third promotion this just stopped.  I can still see the percentage changes, but not the actual numbers anymore.  As far as the lack of a save feature, the maps can be a bit long.  When trying to level my units, it was not unusual for a map to take an hour plus.  At one point I sunk in over 2 hours on one map, because I could not save and come back.  This day and age it seems a little strange not to have this feature.   So the game is very close to an FE title, but needs a bit of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a Fire Emblem clone, same kind of weapon triangle, very classic classes, unoriginal characters and story, issues in the story telling department (after about 8 hours of gameplay, I'm not convinced it's getting better)...BUT, great visuals; animations, although sometimes jumpy, are amazing and satisfying; maps are fun and enemies aren't too dumb; even though the story is basic, it's efficient (don't tell me FE stories are original, they aren't).Overall I would recommend if you like SRPG, it's a good choice, and basically a fix until the next Fire Emblem comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy the older fire emblem games where you don't have training maps to level up your under-used units and you have to manage experience appropriately so all your important units level up, this game is for you.  TLDR: The strengths of the game are the combat and the customizability of the units.  The weaknesses lie in story, characters, and some map design.Pros:+ Gameplay is very similar to old school fire emblem+ Different unit upgrade paths allow for lots of customizability and replay potential+ The weapon system is really interesting, especially for classes that can use physical and magical weapons such as dragon knight and astral seeker+ There are quite a few different map objectives other than "Beat all enemies" or "defeat boss", although by the end of the game most of them become "defeat boss"Cons:- Story is meh- Character development doesn't really happen- Support conversations are long and drawn out, and most of them don't matter at all- Some of the maps, particularly towards the end of the game area really uninspiringI mean, in general it's a $20-30 fire emblem style game that plays similarly to the older ones in the FE series.  If you're looking for a story/character driven game, skip this one.  If you're looking for a relatively quick strategy RPG that makes you think about promotions so that you have good ability combinations, this is definitely the game for you.
