_childDocuments_.review: Stellar game. fun classes, good cast of characters, and good writing. Good genre-savvy from the deveopers as well, Making your gold reward on maps without turn limits determined by how many turns you take helps incentivise against going slow and overcautious, and the penalty for units "dying" in the field being injuries that take a point or 2 off your characters stats is a fair punishment that I much prefer to permadeath (that like many people just means I am going to just restart the map if that happen) that you see in other games of this kind. Also the healthbars for characters in combat being health potions that gradually empty until the glass breaks (and how it breaks depends on the attack type your unit has) is a really neat visual that I thought deserved a shoutout. Overall a great showing from this new studio, hoping they have lots of success here and very much look forward to what they do in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I like the idea of this game, I can't recommend it for a couple reasons. First, and most importantly, the game did not receive sufficient play testing to produce a polished game. Some of these things are minor (such as a random lowercase letter on a weapon name or a typo in dialogue), but some of them are dramatic and frankly should have been caught. One level is a showdown with a recurring villain, where the aforementioned boss just stood there and let me whack him each turn. Second, I think this game tried to have too many characters. Most levels add at least one new character, and many add several. They try to share the spotlight, which only manages to water down the actually interesting characters. Additionally, the relationship component of the game feels a bit too generous as to how many characters build relationships and how quickly. You'll have 10-20 new bonding conversations between each battle, which led me to skip most of them. Finally, everything feels just a little more sluggish than I want. Admittedly, I'm the type of person that turns off battle animations halfway through most games, but Dark Deity had me turning them off on the first level. The animations look fine, but they are all just far too slow.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, if you're into fire emblem (especially the older ones) you'll enjoy the gameplay for sure. The game is worth buying no doubt about it.TLDR: Great game, great art, weird music and sound design in some areas that are surprisingly awkward and unsatisfying (Most of them personal preferences).Animations in combat are smooth and satisfying, very reminiscent of those classic fire emblem animations hold up still to this day.Gameplay is interesting and progression is satisfying with all the classes available and all the optional choices you have to change up progression and enemy classes.There is one thing that bothers me alot and it's the music/sound design. I don't know whether the tracks are just inconsistent in quality or the sound mixing is a bit poor, or perhaps both. There is some great tracks in the game, but some, particularly in battle are weird and out of place, either not upbeat enough or just totally unfitting for combat, the jump between combat music and battlefield music is really jarring as it is instant instead of fading in and out.The only thing holding this back from being a true gem in the genre for me is this as it feels a bit messily done which is a bit of a shame when everything else is so beautifully crafted.When trying to mimic classic fire emblem, you can't skip out on a big part of those games, which is the satisfying and memorable soundtracks in and out of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Intro:The game is mostly everything I expected it to be so far. I'm only on Chapter 6 after about 6.5 hours of taking my time to enjoy the Bonds and do the story on Normal (Hero Difficulty I believe). I overall enjoy the game a lot, and there are a few things I'd like that comment on for pros and cons up to the point I'm at:PROs:- Many of the characters are likable and easy to grow attached to, especially Sophia who deserves the world.- The story so far is nice, but may be hit-or-miss. So far it feels a little cliché, but it's not bad by any means if you are okay with the typical "teens go to war against evil".- While some quality of life things are missing (suspend data which is being added soon and keybind changing) and there are some bugs that need working out, the team is very on top of fixing and tweaking the game. Within two days they did two pretty noticeable patches to fix some things which is not bad for a team of only a few people. The team was very proactive on fixing and changing stuff during development based on fan input, so I expect they will continue to do so with future patches.- Sprites, animations, and character art are all great and the maps are pretty decent. Some maps have been somewhat lackluster while others are more detailed and pleasant to look at. There is no 2K/4K resolution, but in my experience, that is fine even on a 4K screen since it is all pixel art. - Gameplay is splendid for the most part. Many skills are fun, the four weapon categories are cool, and the game has some creative takes on class archetypes. The Grave Wounds system is amazing and really does seem like the best alternative to Permadeath (it lowers one of the defeated unit's stats by 10% based on the type of damage, so a magic attack killing someone might drop their fortitude/magic defense by 10%, or it could drop their magic damage instead). It adds weight to just letting people get defeated without making you feel like you have to restart to keep your precious glass cannon or rewind time to save them and replay part of the map. - Custom difficulty/randomizer built in.CONs:- Some bugs and lacking some quality of life things like suspend data, keybind changing, and 2K/4K resolution. They are really active with adding things and fixing bugs.- The weapon/armor system is a tad hard to learn and calculate. Instead of a Weapon Triangle, your damage is damage type vs armor type, and the calculating can be hard. They tell you the percent differences if you hover over the weapon types, but the math is hard to predict when you also have to calculate it with defense/fortitude (physical defense/magical defense) as well. They do at least have arrows over sprites that tell you if you are at an advantage or disadvantage.Conclusion:I would recommend it if you are interested in SRPGs or want to try one, though it may be a tad hard for people who are unfamiliar with the genre. The forums are helpful and the tips tab just got rehauled into a tutorial tab, so that makes it a little easier to learn some of the game's unique features and takes on the genre. It's definitely going to get better as time goes on with all the patches to fix some bugs and add features people want, so definitely wait if some of the missing features I mentioned matter a lot to you (though they may be added shortly after this review since they are so fast to release patches). Also, while the team is very open about being huge Fire Emblem fans and that the series is the main inspiration for this game, I would definitely not look at this as a ROM hack or a clone, as there is a lot of creative liberties taken with the FE formula to make this game stand out a bit. I've seen a lot of people expecting almost every FE feature to be in this game (reclassing, grinding maps, and romance are examples of things they said they aren't planning to add), as well as those expecting things that most SRPGs don't do in my experience (autosave every turn or save whenever you want so you can save scum). TLDR; - If you go into it expecting a decent SRPG and not the next Fire Emblem game, then you will enjoy it. It has a great cast of characters, a pretty okay story, and a really dedicated team running it and constantly adding features and fixing bugs here and there.- If you are expecting this to be the next FE game, maybe watch someone play a bit of it before you buy it. It's a good game, but all the FEtubers who called it "the next Fire Emblem" might have set some unfulfilled expectations for some people because it is quite different in many ways and the devs have tried to avoid calling it that to my knowledge.

_childDocuments_.review: God this game is good. Saw it announced at E3 yesterday, then I heard that it was released today and I immediately bought it, 100% captivating.Obligatory "Fire Emblem clone" comment, because yes, this is a Fire Emblem clone, but there's nothing wrong with that. This game brings original mechanics, characters and story to the age-old formula that we know and love, making it feel fresh instead of like something new. I have been hankering for the aesthetic of the GBA Fire Emblem games, and Dark Deity delivers on that front, made with modern technology that help to get rid of some of the tediousness of playing the aforementioned older Fire Emblem games. Tl;dr, yes it's a lot like Fire Emblem, but it's original enough to be considered its own thing.The artstyle is absolutely immaculate. Having characters drawn in great detail to contrast their pixel art battle sprites is a wonderful juxtaposition to have. Not only that, but characters and environments are all drawn in a visually distinct way, no two look the same. The first two thieves you get, Cia and Brooke (I had to mention Cia here somewhere as she's currently my favorite character), have similar personality traits that come with that thief moniker, but the aesthetic choices made in their designs help them stand out from each other. It's that typical fantasy RPG-style of aesthetic that just works. Tl;dr, pretty art good.What I love about Dark Deity is how it combines elements we know and love from games all over the timeline of gaming. The Fire Emblem formula mixed with more traditional and diverse RPG-style aesthetics, in addition to a unique weapon system and beautiful animations, makes this "Fire Emblem clone" stand out amongst it's relatively few peers. If you like Fire Emblem, but have had enough with Fire Emblem, try Dark Deity.And I hate to do this specifically, but I have to warn that this game is not peak-professional quality. Typos, bugs, and clunky menus among other things are present throughout Dark Deity's presentations. Long loading screens are an unfortunate product of the game being made within Game Maker, and can serve to bog down the playing experience for those who are less patient. This all being said, the game is well worth dealing with these lacking "professional standards" that we have come to take for granted. What the dev team did with this game is an incredible feat, given the resources and limitations that they had to work with, so a long loading screen here, or a typo there is peanuts compared to the passion and love which this game clearly embodies. Tl;dr, Game Maker stinky but it's well worth it.One more shameless Cia mention because I adore her <3

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfull Game, since i am a big fan of the fire emblem series, i was looking for another round based strategy game, and now, after i played it completely through and got all achievements i have to say, that if you are a fan of said genre, you should definitely give this game a chance.to start with the good things, i needed round about 50 hours to beat the game once on the highest difficulty. the game gives you 30 characters each with different personalities, stat growhts and a unique passive. every character can get promoted two times with a choice of 4 classes per promotion. every promotion has different passives and different changes in the characters growth rates, that combined with  weapon upgrading and choosing equipment gives you plenty of options to make your own team. Even if you dont like spending time on reading whats gonna be best for the character, you have the option to pretty much customize the difficulty of the game, even with something like base stats modifiers (i left my settings on standard with difficulty on deity).The game has bonds, its pretty much like the supports from fire emblem, two characters having a conversation, so you can learn a bit more about the characters, which is something i personally love, because it just gives a bit more depth to the world and characters.The winning condition on the map are not always to just kill everyone, sometimes you have to stop enemys from reaching something, or survive a certain number of rounds which as well is something that just gives adds a little bit of variety. It has a battlesave as well, you can just exit the game, it automatically saves for you, and in the lower left corner of the load game menu you have a little battlesave icon to just go back to where you quitThe game has a few weaknesses as well, there are a few characters that are simply just better than other characters, and some of the characters dont really have that much of a reason to join you, but just stay with the group anyways. But even with that said, dont just dump a character because some people say they are bad, i personally just like elias, and even though he is considered pretty bad, he was really strong and usefull in my run, so just try the characters you personally likeI as well did run into the one or another bug, like a character being shown on a adjacent field, but the movement range still was like the character would be on the right postion.But these "problems" really are just minor things that dont take the fun out of the game, like i said it is a wonderfull game, i would recommend everyone to give it a try and i am looking forward to Dark Deity 2

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I jumped in on Deity Mode immediately, so my reviews may not apply to lower difficulties. Second of all, I'm gonna compare this several times to what it seemingly draw inspiration from, Fire Emblem, but I'll try to keep the comparison to a minimum.So, what's good about this game?+ Better challenge than 3DS ~ Switch era Fire Emblem entries (except for Conquest, obviously).+ Somehow made an open, large empty map works. I'm talking about the supposedly controversial chapter 19, of course.+ Combat system is great; I can imagine saturated class choice would lead to bad times, which is good since it prevents one-class supremacy.+ Some musics are great, especially the pre-finale chapter one.+ Battle animations are pleasing to see, just lacking a bit in term of impact feel.+ The game is imbalanced, but that's just what a game should be IMO. Balanced games are in general, boring as heck.+ The replacement for permadeath is an interesting idea, however...(see the section below)+ It blew my expectation from Fire Emblem fan perspective, but that might be because there are no actually good FEs for the past decade save for Awakening (on hard mode) and Conquest.So, what's bad about this one?- Permadeath doesn't exist despite the large cast given and the injury system doesn't do anything other than take off a very insignificant amount of stats. This takes away the challenge by a huge chunk.- The last couple of chapters are absolutely horrible. They're not challenging at all.- The story is forgettable, I don't even remember why we're fighting in the first place half-way through the game.- Only a few of the characters are memorable. With a large cast, one might say that's a natural outcome, but I beg to differ when I remember every single name and class from FE titles after beating them once.- I did praise the game for being imbalanced, but it could use more broken stuff on the enemy side to add more challenge.- Deity Mode could've been the Normal Mode. Not gonna lie, braindead moments can be found a lot in it.- Enemies should've been made to be able to utilize Chain, Disarm and Phase as well. Them not being able to feels unfair.- Battle BGMs aren't exciting or properly portray a fight.- Controls are bad, especially with gamepad. I never thought the day I complain about control in an SRPG game would come, but alas...- Bugs, crashes. I had almost two hours wasted just because it crashed three times near the end of a certain chapter.- Inventory management isn't a part of the challenge, a missed opportunity/potential IMO.It gets 7/10 from me. Definitely an impressive first game for the team, just ruined by rushed release that resulted in bugs and crashes roaming in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty fun game so far. It has a couple of flaws, but if you're looking for tactical games in the vein of Fire Emblem, you should check this out. My only big frustration with it is the lack of experimentation. Your characters can change their class at Level 10, but you're locked into whatever you choose until Level 30, when you can change again (and your choice there is permanent). They really should include the option to switch between classes whenever you want but in case they never add that, I'll give you some advice. Whenever you have the option, choose the nimble, dexterous classes. Evasion tanks are by far the best tanks in this game. Similarly, when you're picking the weapons, accuracy is more important than damage.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like people are expecting a bit too much from this considering it's the first game the developers have made in this style.Yes there are a couple issues and depending on what level of Fire Emblem experience and enjoyment you're coming in from, this could really impact your view of it. Fire Emblem is my absolute favourite series so I went into this with high expectations but tried to keep them realistic considering. The music could be updated in my mind, I'm not a huge fan but it's by no means awful to listen to. Just feels a little off. The levelling system is EXTREMELY generous. The majority of my stat ups are 5-6 stats per. That's not necessarily a bad thing but if you're used to be absolutely screwed over by RNG/FE level ups, this is going to make you feel indestructible.  The weapon/magic/armour triangle could have been described a little better. The controller support feels a little glitchy, there are a few issues I'm finding with navigating maps (mostly for accessing menus, chapter requirements and using items within the maps), I can't seem to see my units stats when I'm promoting them (which is only a small annoyance) and then the cursor is ALWAYS in the top left of the map when every chapter starts. These are small things though, they're not going to turn me off the game as a whole and I find the good outweighs these by a lot.It reminds me of an earlier Fire Emblem story wise (I get major Sacred Stones vibes) and the artwork is beautiful. I find myself liking the personality of almost all the characters (Sorry Lincoln) and I'm enjoying the level up/promote system they have going. I am actively enjoying this game and it's helping with the tactics itch. It's the absolute closest thing to Fire Emblem you'll find on Steam and I'm thankful for it. I've been eagerly waiting for this since I found it on Kickstarter so when I finally got my code I was through the moon. It's what I wanted, what I expected and I can see these developers making more and improving from this. This is a first game. This isn't the 13th+ instalment of a long-standing tactics game - it's a new series and you need to take that into consideration going into this. Fire Emblem didn't have absolute winners for each game they released, so try not to write this one off and give it a shot. I'm looking forward to more games from this studio in the future. I paid WAY more for Langrisser and enjoyed it significantly less. The price point for Deity is extremely fair. _childDocuments_.review: I got the privilege of designing the logo for Sword & Axe LLC, and getting to work with the development team showed me how dedicated they were to perfecting the game. So far I've placed about 3 hours into the game, and coming from a background of enjoying Fire Emblem games, this one lived up to all the hype.I see complaints existing about a lack of tutorial for this game, but I was extremely surprised by the intuitive nature of the game. The point and click combat, the chess-like attack patterns, and support roles of the different characters was exceptional and considering the game was made by such a small team,  how could anyone not see the tree that has bared such fruit? Great job guys, really.Now for constructive criticisms, I have no qualms so far. Relationships in the bond conversations are the heart of my joy when playing, and the system that plays into developing these bonds on the battlefield are clear as day. The only critique I have actually, is a strange bug that I know could be easily resolved with the game coding by Chip; that being when I enter into full screen mode my audio disables.Overall, I really enjoy the game, and expect the fun to continue as I slowly but surely near its end. I definitely recommend this to friends, and am gladdened to see three of my colleagues already owning the game - even before my recommendation and without their knowledge of my involvement. Solid job boys. -Draco

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a true Spiritual Sibling to Fire Emblem on the PC!Made for fans by fans. it has an amazing soundtrack and very nice looking character art.It switches the formula a little bit, so it's not a straight up FE game with the serials filled off. Every character has a type of armor that is better against certain types of damage. And every class has 4 weapons that can be upgraded with tokens that can be bought or dropped by the enemy. Power weapons are good against low defense or lightly armored targets.Accuracy weapons are good against dodgy targets.Finesse weapons have low weight so they are more likely to double and also have high crit rate so they are good for Units that have high luck or other crit boosting skills.Balance weapons are usually middle of the road in terms of accuracy and power, but they are usually very low on weight so they are likely to allow your Unit to attack twice and tend to have better accuracy and power than Finesse weapons.2 tiers of promotions, meaning a 2nd and a 3rd class with 4 classes per tier. This adds tons of customization to each character and already oozes replay value. Do you go for a full Horse team or do you spread your classes out to cover all your bases? Do you go for tankier classes to turtle maps or go for glass cannons to live dangerously? You decide!No promotion items needed. As soon as the character reaches the max level for the class you are offered to promote right then and there. Even mid-mission.No permadeath. Characters get "injured" and are out of the mission and also get penalized in one stat if they are struck down. I still reset if that happens due to not wanting that character to lag behind on combat Exp for the remainder of the mission but it makes it so you don't have to reset if you are about to finish a long mission and get an unlucky critical.No grinding. Classic FE style. You get a story mission, then intermission to upgrade or shop if there's a shop available, then checkout "support conversations" which are called Bonds in this game, save, check out your Units and then on to the next mission. You'll have to make due with what resources you have as you go along.I have two nitpicks in regards to the graphics:1.- Class sprites only have one body so both your male and female cleric will look the same, the only difference being their head which, admitedly, is different enough so you can recognize them. Having a male and female body for the sprite would have been great.2.- Map tiles look a little low detail in regards to the sprites, but battle map backdrops are very good so it's not really a detriment to the graphics.Outside of those two nitpicks, I only have good things to say about this game.TLDR: If you are a fan of the Fire Emblem series, it's a must buy. If you are a TRPG junkie, it's a must buy. If you kinda liked games in the genre or RPGs about warfare and such, then checkout some gameplay videos and see if this is up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to start by saying that this game is actually pretty fun, and if you enjoy turn based strategy games like Fire Emblem (you are going to hear a lot of Fire Emblem comparisons) then you should defiantly give this game a try. The sprite work and character art is very good. While this game does borrow inspiration from Fire Emblem, it has its own unique "weapon triangle" in the form of armor and damage types. The class progression system is pretty good and gives you plenty of room to customize your party how you like. Characters also don't die permanently, instead accruing wounds that lower their stats if they fall during a mission. I think these systems work to give a really good new player experience to people who haven't played other role playing strategy game before, while also giving fans of the genre something new.Positives aside, I do have several complaints. 1: There is no tutorial or in-game manual on game mechanics. I get that older games in the genre didn't have in-game manuals, but this is 2021, you need to have a manual to look mechanics up in. 2: Limited settings. The GBA FE games had more options, such as having combat animations only on your turn. 3: There is no way to skip enemy phase. in the earlier missions it isn't a problem, but when you are against 50+ enemy units it starts to take a while. 4: Probably my biggest gripe, the controls. I don't know if this game was designed with controllers in mind, but on mouse and keyboard it is pretty rough. sometimes you miss click and fumble your turn, other times you cancel your move multiple times before it actually registers. Having been said, I don't think this is a game that the developers will abandon. There is obviously a lot of care put into this project, and I do believe that they will fix the issues I have had at a later date. I enjoy it and will continue to play it through the summer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Now I did say recommend but I think it depends. The story is meh, if you're a big story person, it might be tough to get through. It's boring and predictable so like I don't really remember what happens but I could probably tell major story points by how generic it is. The characters are alright, they stand out enough that most aren't forgettable. There are supports like Fire Emblem where characters have nice side convo that give them more characterization. Tho tbh I can only really remember one.Now the really good stuff is the gameplay. Even if your a story/character person first I would still implore to try the game for the gameplay. First everyone character has their own passive ala Fire Emblem Fates/3H and each class has their own passive, actions and abilities. Every class has four paths with two promotions each and the cool thing is you're not locked into a path. So like if you chose the top path for the first promotion, you can choose the fourth path's final class on your second promotion. This leads to a lot of choices for you to build your units as you have all these passives to combo with. But wait there's more! In the game you'll get special items that have their own passive, each character can only one but it gives you a lot of leeway on how to build your party. Each class has a weapon type and armor. Each weapon has a damage type so lances are piercing, hammers are bashing or whatever and magic has it's own thing and each armor has it's strengths and weaknesses against each damage type. It's like a more advanced version of the Fire Emblem weapon triangle that adds more depth to combat. Also each character hold 4 weapons, each one with a specialization. There's a Power, Crit, Accurate and Balanced weapon and there are special coins used to upgrade these weapons and because of the limited supply, you choose how each character would upgrade their weapons. Do you invested completely into one weapon or have a more balanced arsenal for that character? Dark Diety really gives a lot of options when building up your party which gives the game a lot of replay value and that's besides the fact that there's a built in randomizer in the game in case you wanna spice it up. It's really fun.TLDR, MEH STORY AWESOME GAMEPLAY YOU SHOULD TRY IT PROBABLY

_childDocuments_.review: When you play a Triple A SRPG like FE, you get used to a certain level of polish. Normally, this comes at the cost of a flawed gameplay design or a detached story that doesn't feel part of the game itself. This game piqued my interest as soon as I saw it and got hooked despite the lack of polish. It has the core gameplay loops and mechanics that keep you engaged with it, something games like FE Birthright/Revelations lacked. It even offers more diversity in classes and these have very well thought out skills that affect decision-making in the game and have the potential to create very powerful characters with the right decisions, and this is what's awesome, the game doesn't give you OP units with OP skill combinations, you have to work for it. But complementary to the gameplay, I look for engaging characters and an interesting story, which is harder to present and to shine brighter requires further more polish. Sure, it could use a LOT of quality of life improvements, but for an indie release this game is giving me my money's worth and more. Kudos to the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many folks who have written reviews about the game, I'm a big fan of RPGS like Fire Emblem, Dragon Age, etc. This game definitely felt more like a Fire Emblem game, but I also liked how it differentiated itself and had some interesting mechanics. Here are some likes/dislikes. Most of it is spoiler free/vague enough, but also limited to the first couple chapters.Likes:Nice Quality of Life Differences from Fire Emblem:-Each unit comes with four weapons that can be upgraded. It takes some getting used to, but I liked not having to manage a bunch of weapons and being able to eventually get powerful weapons by the end of the game. Spells had cool animations too.-I actually liked the damage/armor advantage system. While the game could have a better tutorial on this (more below) I did appreciate how the game didn't just copy and paste a weapon triangle system. I do wish that advantage mattered a bit more since I found myself getting through the game on Hero difficulty pretty well without worrying about it that much.Graphics/Gameplay/Music:I enjoyed the art style and the overall characters and animations are fun. Spells are clearly better animated than weapons, so the game could work on that, but overall the animation and artwork is really nice. Music is also generally nice and has a good fantasy/rpg vibe for the genre. Story/Characters:This might be controversial since I feel like most people didn't seem to like the story/felt it had its plot holes. I will say that for an indie game and given the amount of hours I put into it I genuinely enjoyed the straightforward story. I also liked the additional fantasy elements. It reminded me more of Lord of the Rings about midway through or so. I also really liked the "Bond" conversations. Dislikes/Things to be Improved:-Minor bugs: I generally managed to beat the game with little issues. It's my understanding the developers are continuing to update and fix the game, so I don't want to be too harsh. The only bug that was game breaking was chapter 22 when I fielded a certain unit. Otherwise, I just had random things like the "push" command pushing a unit awkwardly or my cursor not being able to select my unit because it was a space away even though I hadn't moved it there? Again, minor things but I still was able to finish.-Class Balance: While the game lets you play around with classes and has a branch class system where you can pick from four options after your unit reaches two level thresholds (or promotions), I found that certain classes were clearly more superior/better for certain units. The class system definitely needs some overhaul, but I find this is also a challenge with recent Fire Emblem games like Three Houses. Part of the issue comes with certain classes having both 1-2 range and also higher movement advantages with little penalties.Crit/Crit Avoid: I wanted to bring this up as a subsection of class balance. In this game when a unit crits it does 2 times damage. Since there is no crit avoid this means that crits from enemies and your units can happen (quite a lot too). While it makes the game a bit more interesting, I found that early in the game and toward the end enemies would sometimes have an uncomfortably high crit chance. Luckily if they can't hit you, they can't crit, but I still thinking having crit avoid would make crits happen less often. Then again, you need to be able to crit especially to do enough damage by mid to endgame, so I'm not sure how that would need to be balanced out. -World Building: While I liked the straight forward story, I found that by the end of the game I just wanted to know more about the characters like the different races. I like that the game is replayable, but I think the challenge with having such a large roster of characters is that they each come from different places, and it's hard to actually visualize what those places are outside of bond conversations. Maybe having more maps (of the world itself including places we don't get to see), or slowing down the story a bit more at relevant plot points? I also just wonder if the game either needs a sequel or a prologue to further flesh out the world and what will happen next with the characters.-Chapter 1 either needs to be a tutorial or there should be a tutorial prologue: The game is really not beginner friendly. Even having played Fire Emblem like games I found myself confused about the advantage and weapon upgrade system at first. I eventually I read into it more, and it made sense but I still think it would be helpful if the game asked you "Want to know about how to attack? Advantage? Level objectives?" It would just make the game more accessible especially to newcomers to the genre. Difficulty: A bit Uneven but mostly easy (I played on "Hero difficulty") once you get the hang of it. Since none of your units can actually die but instead can get wounded and lose stats, I didn't find myself struggling in the game. There were some maps that were certainly harder than others, but I think that's because enemy AI may be rushing you vs. you drawing them in (bait and attack strategy). The maps I also found more enjoyable were more boss focused ones and ones that had a unique gimmick. Early game is generally pretty good with mid game having some challenging maps with endgame going fairly smooth since at that point most of my units were pretty strong. I personally think games like Fire Emblem need more competition, and I enjoy indie RPGs because they still are able to have their own creativity and flare. This was a fun game, and I look forward to maybe trying it out on "Deity" difficulty. There are characters that I'd like to try out and others I'd like to give a second chance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great tactical RPG that ramps up methodically and, on Deity mode, presents a considerable challenge that is satisfying and entertaining. At first, I wished there was some kind of free battle component so I could grind it out and stomp through the campaign, but not having that actually made it that much more important to take advantage of opportunities to level within the fights. Several chapters required multiple attempts to get it down (I think Arrogance took me the most) and having to play them out perfectly was a very rewarding experience.The aptitudes/classes make it a very interesting game to try and optimize all the right people, and many of the battles require you to set up formations and think strategically about how to proceed, or stand your ground. It's not a game where you can take one OP character and slam an entire army (although Monroe came close). The story isn't bad, but what I loved about the game is the complex balance of character aptitudes, classes, weapon types, and battlefield positioning that was required to successfully complete it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think the game is bad in anyway it's just not polished enough in certain aspects that can really hinder the overall enjoyment.  Lack of explanation of the games mechanics, new players are left in a daze in regards to what the four weapon types do and which upgrade path suits which character.  Not being able to look at your character's status when at home base is a nuisance, lack of quicksave feature mid battles forces you to commit, awkward item management while at base, look at how fire emblem gba does it and you'll see where this one falls short. But the biggest sin by far, the primary reason I'm writing this is that if you press start, the go to main menu option is present in the pause and it does not ask you are you sure, so if you're on controller and you press start and x by accident, you're thrown to the main menu and all your progress is lost. _childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity has been giving me the Fire Emblem fix I've been missing since I finished with Three Houses, and in that sense it seems to be doing exactly what the creators set out to do. The combat is everything you'd expect out of an SRPG and oftentimes even deeper than you'd usually expect due to the various abilities and weapon types you can switch between, all of which have a notable impact on strategy. I do have to warn here though that some of these systems and intricacies can be a bit poorly explained - I've played many similar games so I picked up on them fairly quick but for those new to SRPG's I suspect there would be a fairly steep learning curve. If the devs can get around to tutorializing these features, I think it would greatly improve the game's accessibility. The story thus far as I've played seems adequate but nothing spectacular, however the characters (which I personally find more important in these games) are quite good and have interesting support chains.All in all I'd strongly recommend this game for Fire Emblem and SRPG fans, but while I do think newcomers to the genre can enjoy Dark Deity as well I'd warn that they might have a difficult time with the mechanics until the devs can include a comprehensive tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary - Enjoyable, but repetitive and with issues:Story - 5/10. Interesting but hard transitions make it difficult to follow.Gameplay - 8/10. Combat is fun, but repetitive.Characters - 6/10. The starting 4 are fun and dynamic, and it's only downhill from there.In short, the game doesn't do anything new or innovative and there are definitely bugs I've encountered, but if you enjoy TTRPG's, I'd definitely pick up this game on sale. Review:I picked up Dark Deity via the Kickstarter and just now got around to playing it on my Steam Deck. It plays very well on my Steam Deck and would call it a good choice for the platform.The game's characters are interesting, at first, but end up coming off flat and one dimensional. Some of the characters just show up out of no where and apparently no one in the party has no issues with random tag-a-longs. The overall story is strongest for the starting 4 (Irving, Garrick, Maren, & Alden), and believable for a few others (Monroe, Ford, Lincoln, Bianca, Sara, & Samara) but then breaks down with some, looking at you Faust.The combat is the core of the game and it is fun and engaging. It's simple enough to pick up, but can have tricky parts that keep maps interesting. I have encountered a few bugs, with characters being able to end turns in spaces that are already occupied, or just plain won't respond to commands and I have to skip over them completely for the rest of combat. The magical aspects are fun to equip, but you won't end up swapping them around much at all. And leveling the weapons is simple and intuitive.Some of my biggest gripes come from what appears to be a very disjointed story. It's told in distinct chapters that have little to no transition between them. There is very little background explained about the world itself or even the main antagonist. It makes many scenes feel very disjointed and rushed. They tout this story of "magical aspects are being stolen and we have to stop it or the world will be destroyed!" but then quickly veer off of that. In the end, I think that there are too many characters, most of the uniqueness ends up being fairly pointless between them, and because the combats limit your party size to 14, when you have 30+ characters, you'll literally never use some of them because you can't keep them leveled with the party.

_childDocuments_.review: let me start by saying I have been a backer of the game on kick starter since May of 2020 At its core there is a decent SRPG  with fresh mechanics that will still feel familiar to fans of the genre in Dark Deity However there are some pretty glaring polish issues with this game and I'm honestly surprised it launched in this state.  The menus just straight up feel bad to navigate with a controller, there is information you just cant view with a controller in the camp menus that you can with a mouse and its pretty annoying. There are also no sounds with clicking through things in the battle menus.The maps are just kinda bland to look at. They kinda have a storybook aesthetic which is made worse by how broken you can make your units so early. I'm playing with 100% vanilla settings, and 5 chapters in the maps are completely trivial. The starter mage you get is so powerful he can solo maps because he just gets 33% life steal for free at his first promotion. The damage type vs armor type ( which is literally not explained anywhere in the game btw ??? I had to go to the discord and find someone to explain it) just doesn't matter which is wild because again, im 5 chapters in. Getting your units to feel powerful is half the fun in SRPG and when  they  just become God slayers 5 maps it leaves you with little motivation to play the rest of the game.  It feels like game balance was a complete afterthought. The visuals are nice in terms of battle animations for spells but archers and melee units just have the same generic sword/bow/lance/mace attack for all 4 weapon types which feels omega bad. Speaking of the weapon types they actually don't matter because your mages one round anything with the balance spell so there is no point on using anything else. If you are even a casual fan of games like Fire Emblem, Advance Wars, Shining Force, Final Fantasy Tactics, Fae Tactic, Fell Seal etc. Then you are better off just playing one of those games. If you have played all of those and are just dying for a new SRPG to play I recommend the FireEmblem 8 Rom hack Vision Quest lol. which I can say with certainty you will have a better time with plus that's free. This game should have really come with an early access tag because it hardly feels finished. some balance patches, UI fixes, map updates and I could really see this game being a decent. SRPG.  Will those things happen? probably not but one can dream. Side note, I am so upset that this game even has voice acting when there are so many more issues that 100% should have been addressed first. I really feel like they spent way to much time/money/effort on making sure things looked good instead of just making a good game first, and then adding all of that stuff later but thats just me idk.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the game once on Hero difficulty with no custom changes. This game is basically fire emblem with little differences but that's what I enjoyed about this game style and genre. The game play is really simple, move character from point A to B, defeat all enemies and survive to the next chapter. The spin on this game that is different from regular fire emblem games is that you don't lose characters when they are beaten by enemies. Instead they lose permanent stats which can later affect them throughout the campaign. With that aspect in mind I had to be mindful of who to prioritize more so and pick and choose a balanced team. Not going to lie though, I found myself using 4 healers just to make sure my guys don't die and since the maps get larger and larger and there are more units versus ours you need at least 4 healers. Overall, I really enjoyed this game and will play on Deity difficulty with some custom changes as well. If I the development team were to make sequel to this game I would say have areas where you can grind for levels like how fire emblem has. That way you level up units that you want to use or so you can buy the upgrades and stat boosters. A way to balance that would just be in between each main story chapter you are able to do 1 or 2 side missions (maybe use it as a way to build character development, relationships, etc). Or just have stat boosters in the shop be limited so that if you build up x amount of gold you can't just buy 20 +2 strength and give it x unit. Just food for thought.

_childDocuments_.review: ✔ you control a lot of fighters at once - after a couple of maps it's 10 and then it gets to 15+✔ a lot of classes with upgrades (although the differences aren't that big - more about mechanics later)❔ when a character gets defeated in combat they can still be picked later, but with permanently lost stat. At first I hated it, but later I realized that it doesn't matter❔ bonds - essentially there is a lot of dialogue between each pair of your companions (doesn't influence combat). And since there are 25+ of them it's actually A LOT of dialogue. Unfortunately I stopped caring soon, because I couldn't get attached to anyone ...❔ complex armor / weapon rock-paper-scissors mechanic - bad UI and lack of other mechanics in the game doesn't allow it to shine✘ UI - why can't I easily see exactly how my weapon type interacts with enemy armor type? The little red/blue arrow is not enough as it can vary wildly. Or better yet - show the expected damage that I could do to each enemy in range✘ moving to the next group of enemies with your 15+ guys is a pain ✘ randomness combined with low hp pool -> characters can die in one or two hits.. or not. You cannot predict it so it's up to the (thankfully stupid) AI. Even how much stats you gain on level-up is random✘ actions/attacks available to each characters are extremely restrictive and boring. Everyone has range of 1-2 tiles (except some very specific classes, which can get +1). Yes, this means that an Archer can shoot what looks like maybe 8 meters with a bow (but not 4 meters - that would be too close). I didn't encounter any area of effect attacks. Each class has a special ability, but they are very underwhelming (except priest's Heal). For example mages can teleport... but only a character that is next to them and only through reflection symmetry of himself - so from touching them on their left to touching them on their right. There seems to be a strong aversion of letting characters do anything interesting on the battlefield✘ there are also no interesting interactions when it comes to positioning - no attacks of opportunity or flanking✘ side-based turns - first you move all your characters and then AI controls all enemies✘ in most maps the enemies just wait for you, even when you are killing their friends✘ there isn't much customization (you can slightly upgrade weapons in linear fashion). The only things there are are class upgrades (which are alright) and every character can equip one Aspect (very important for the story). Aspects can have such amazing perks as "enemy you hit is marked and receives 10% more damage". Keep in mind that you mostly kill enemies in 1-3 hits so it changes nothing. Or 10% chance that you will do 150% damage - it's basically never useful, but the game loves its RNG✘ there are way too many characters that are introduced. They are always higher level than your guys and you should use them, otherwise you will be outleveled quickly. So unless you pick your favorite characters soon after their introduction and focus on giving them kills they will be outcompeted by the new guys✘ story is generic and boring - I couldn't get into it even though I tried for the first couple of hours. Then I skimmed it all. At least the dialogues aren't awful✘ scaling is broken, at least on medium difficulty level - I played something like 2/3 of the story and the Mage I focused on became an untouchable demigod oneshotting everyone (disregarding advantages completely) while everyone else was average or next to useless. It was somewhat amusing getting there, but why should I even play the last 1/3?✘ most disappointing dragon fight ever

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have flaws, but its fun to play. One of those "one more battle" games you dont see as often these days. A fantastic tribute to fire emblem, shining force, stella deus, and many other classic srpgs.Lets get the main flaw out of the way....The map designs are not very good. Its REALLY hard to see what is what. Chests and such are very hard to spot because they blend in with the maps scenery, for example. I hope this gets addressed in some future patch because it can get very annoying.The voice acting is top notch. I find it amusing and a little irritating at the same time that an indie game like this can have A+ voice acting, while mega corporation developers like Tecmo Koei have either no english translation in many games (Orochi) or just garbage voice acting (Dynasty Warriors 9). Take note Koei, THIS Is how you add great VA's!The story is decent. There are a ton of characters and I am only in the 5th battle or so. The designs are fantastic, each with their own voice and personality....And they are varied enough that everyone will eventually have a party they like. You can even randomize who-joins-and-when which is a fantastic feature, giving the game a LONG replay value!The graphics for the characters in battle are great. The animations in combat are more then I was expecting. You really can tell this is a labor of love. Every character also has multiple promotion paths, so you probably wont play the same game twice on replays. Weapon upgrade are done with a nice mechanic as well, as instead of finding different weapons, you find weapon tokens which let you upgrade one of several weapons on each character giving them stat boost, but after so many upgrades, the weapon will change into a higher tier new one. This mechanic is great!The gameplay is much like most SRPGs, where you move each unit and attack enemies or heal ect. However, each character has special actions as well. For example, rogues can disarm an opponent for X number of rounds, others can chain them in place so they cant move, or some characters can push a unit one square and so forth really boosting the strategy element. There is also a friendship system. So far I havent seen any optional grinding battles. I hope they are in there but so far its been chapter to chapter....Music is passable. Typical themes for a tactical game.So overall is it worth it? Oh yeah.Despite its shortcomings, it really does feel like one of those old classic games that you just cant put down once you start playing....The game is well made, and you can tell someone really put their heart and soul into making this.Strategy RPGs are rare enough as it is, sadly. And some of them end up being not worth you time, but sometimes you find a gem in the pile of rocks. Like this title.With the success of Fire Emblem 3 houses becoming the highest selling srpg of all time, and the major success of other srpgs it is time for this genre to grow and solidify itself as a common genre in league with other popular genres . And this is a great sign that this will come to pass.If  you are a fan of oldschool srpgs, this is one you dont want to pass on.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend and continue it but it has some issues that has me dropping the game.1. Controls: I'm guessing the game was meant for controller because mouse and keyboard felt off.2. Death penalty system: If you lose a character during battle it get a permanent stats debuff like -1 Defense. Congrats your character that was probably already lagging behind the rest now has less experience and will die even faster in the next mission where you'll fight even stronger enemies. Also there's no saving during missions so you can easily lose 20 to 30 minutes of progress.3. The weapon system: Each character has 4 weapons with slight different stats regarding, power, accuracy, crit and wt. Which seems pretty cool at first but it means that every turn you spend most of your time comparing each attack for what's best at that moment. Which slows gameplay to a crawl. Also it feels weird for a realism standpoint, just imagine an archer fumbling around with 4 bows strapped to hit body switch between them for every shot.The biggest problem is probably the pacing, the game is slow to play even compared to other tactical RPG's and incentivizes either loading a lot or playing very slow and methodically.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Fire Emblem fan I always get excited to play games with similar gameplay. So when I had some money for Christmas I decided to use it on this game which had been in my wishlist for awhile.In terms of recommendation I wish there was a way of saying recommended for a certain type of player, but not others.If you are after a well written story with well written characters then I’d suggest skipping this game. I found the writing somewhat all over the place, like they tried to link together several different story ideas instead of making one flowing and cohesive story. This personally didn’t bother me as if I enjoy the gameplay I tend to be forgiving towards a games writing.In terms of gameplay, I haven’t tried the hardest difficulty yet. In these kinds of games I tend to play the normal mode over easy or hard. I found the gameplay during battles straight forward and enjoyable, it scratched that FE itch. The class tree system was an interesting variation, although I feel it needs some work refining and making all routes viable. Supports were reminiscent of gba era. The weapon level up system reminded me of suikoden’s and punished me for trying to level everyone early on instead of focusing on a select few. In terms of visuals I liked the sprites and portraits, but I felt the maps could use some work.Overall I felt this was a solid first attempt and I hope the devs will continue to support the game with some patches to fix some of the issues the community is having. These days games often live and die on how supportive their developers are of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to go into detail about what I like and don't like about this game. I will also compare it to other games of similar SRPG fashion.First off, this game looks amazing. It has a nice aesthetic and the U.I. is pretty great. If you are a fan of Fire Emblem, you'll love how it plays and sounds. However, there are a few major differences between Dark Diety and other games of the same nature. I will now begin to break down the review into different parts.<Mechanics>This game tries somethings that either work really well in this genre, or don't work at all.You'd expect some weapons to work better on certain enemies, but in reality they don't work as you'd think.For example, magic barely effects an armored unit and rapiers don't either.Pro:Each class has it's own unique four different weapons that you don't have to equip or will break.You can cycle through them during combat and upgrade them with tokens you buy or earn throughout the game.Con:Some weapons all share the same appearance regardless of what they are called and don't swap images.There is no equipping or no durability which may be a turn off for some people who like these types of games.Pro:Combat is fun and you can feel the weight of the movements and animations. Maps are small and the enemies are generally challenging. But, sometimes they can be a bit overwhelming especially with reinforcements. Some units are better than others. Another neat fact is that you can class change the moment you get to the level needed.Con:You cannot save in the middle of combat and your characters get perm. debuffs for falling in battle.This makes your units that die, more and more useless overtime as you don't have a way to level them up outside of the story. There are no side quests like in the Falnarion Tactics series or bonus EXP that allow you to gain extra money, exp and items on the side.<Story>The story is something that some people may enjoy, however I do not. It's not exactly terrible, but it's not memorable or great in any sense. That being said, I have yet to finish the game and am still playing it.Pro:The characters look appealing and you have many different options on how you can randomize the story and customize some character introductions in the order they happen which is nice for people who want a bit of a surprise.Con:There are way too many characters. I'd understand if these characters were meant to join the party as background guests that bring nothing to the story on purpose and are just units for combat. Then I could get behind that idea. But, no. These characters are all meant to bring something to the plot albeit terrible and are mainly just lost in a sea of faces.I don't remember pretty much any character and I don't feel anything for any of them. You get like 2-5 characters every map (Chapter) and it's all too much. Like in this one map, I got 3 characters just introduced for the fight and then after the fight was over, two new characters joined me. All of them have virtually no screen time and are horribly under developed. The main character is also uninteresting.Conclusion: 5/10While it's a visually appealing, fun game to play. It's story and content are lackluster for the price. The story is quite boring, the "plot" gets lost in a sea of forgettable faces. Although it has a bonding system between characters for extra chats like in Fire Emblem. It doesn't make me care about the characters anymore than I already don't.Other games of this same genre do certain things better such as the Falnarion Tactics series. But, this game isn't terrible and it's worth buying on sale to enjoy for the game-play. I barely suggest this game as positive.My final verdict is neutral.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is the indie Fire Emblem we've all been waiting for. That's the simplest and, in my opinion, best way to describe it. I have completed one campaign and am currently playing two others (one Deity mode, and one reverse recruitment mode) so when I say this game is good, I feel that I'm justified in my words. The character designs are top tier, the maps have varied and fun objectives, the innovations to the class system allow for a great variety of builds and styles, and the armor vs damage type system, while confusing at first, allows for some strategic decision making that Fire Emblem craves. Finally, the bond conversations are incredible. The amount of depth packed into these conversations blew me away, and added an insane amount of characterization to the party. There's strong discussions of philosophy, right and wrong, the purpose of ones life, and more, and that's saying nothing of the ways character play off of each other to both strengthen and subvert their character archetypes. It's fantastic. There are some low points as well. The game launched in a very buggy state, although Chip and the dev team have been running overtime to get everything fixed up and implement requested changes, so there's little to fear here for new buyers. The music and sound design is a bit of a mixed bag. Some battle and map themes are excellent, and had me wishing I could change what themes play when. This is because some of the themes are very lackluster, and can kill the mood of a map when they suddenly start playing during battle scenes or player/enemy phase transitions. Finally, the story is...fine. There's a standard FE style plot where we see our heroes sucked into a grand plot that could destroy the world, and must gather the MacGuffins before the bad guys to save the day. That's fine, deserving neither praise nor critique. The story is a device to drive us through different settings and battles, and that's all it needs to do. But there are hints of a grand world with deep lore that we catch the barest whiffs of through dialogue pieces, and it's a shame we don't get to see more if it. Ultimately. Dark Deity is absolutely worth the price. It's a game with very high levels of replayability and experimentation. The community has been fantastic, and the dev team clearly put their heart and soul into the title. If you have even a passing interest in Fire Emblem, Final Fantasy Tactics, or any other strategy or RPG titles, check this one out. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played a lot of Tactics RPGs, including most of the Fire Emblems (including ones you need language patches for) this  game seems to be made as a tribute to the 2D Fire Emblem games in a great way, and not in a way thats a copy either. It takes the tried and true formula of them but adds a lot of little quality of life improvements and new systems that build on those in a different way than the newer 3D Fire emblems. The QoL improvements mainly being ways to randomize your campaign and after battle stats to help better evaluate your units. You have familiar bonds system and promotion system as well as fun characters and weapon types. However the first major change is that instead of a weapon triangle you have a weapon and armor system where certain weapon types are good vs certain armor types. It seems to be each weapon has a type is very bad again, kinda bad against, kinda good against, very good against. This actually changes up the combat consideration a bit. Second is that instead of buying weapons that degrade, each weapon type (slash, pierce, blunt, fire, etc) has 4 variations that change up power/crit chance/accuracy/speed and don't degrade. Instead of degrading you can upgrade the variations of the type, but so far it does not seem like you get tokens to full upgrade every variation all the way. So you have to make choices (at least early could change later) on which of the types works best with the stats your character has gotten up to that point. This is also something I think is a positive change from the weapon system of fire emblem. Then there is the promotion system, I have only gotten the first promotions so far, but each class seems to have 4 paths they can go down instead of the usual 2 of the older fire emblems and all of them actually seem quite good and fitting different playstyles. Each one adds 2 abilities to the class, and each characters (not class) comes with their own passive as well so you can find ways to make their passives work with the class passives. Overall the first 3 hours have been very enjoyable and have scratched that Fire Emblem Itch. There are a few issues with the UI but once you get use to them you barely notice it in my opinion. The story so far has been better than expected and the characters have been on par with Fire Emblem characters and have distinct personalities and the typical fun banter expected in these types of games.  I would overall give this game an 8/10, and recommend it to anyone who enjoyed the old Fire Emblems.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: while this review was written before the 1.5 Recurve update, pretty much everything I said before still applies.)When Dark Deity was first released, it made a lot of noise in the Fire Emblem community. However, the overall perception seemed pretty negative, one of the major reasons being that the game was full of bugs, many of which are game-breaking. With that in mind, I decided to wait until the dust has settled. When the game was on sale again two months later, I decided to give it a try...... only to find that there's still bugs in this game! I saw various graphics glitches during combat animations. The autosave feature didn't work correctly for me. That doesn't bode well, considering that even just two chapters in, I'm already running into so many bugs. I also heard that some skills still don't work correctly. At least when the game first released, the devs were diligently releasing patches every day. But over time, they became less frequent, despite there still being issues, giving the impression that the devs have more or less "given up" on this game. At least the bugs aren't too serious. A bigger issue for me was performance. The game lagged like crazy the moment it started. I had to turn down the resolution to the lowest setting for it to be tolerable, although it still ran slow. Admittedly, my computer isn't up to par by modern gaming standards, but it can still run all Fire Emblem games up to and including the 3DS games no problem. So why would a game that's barely more complex than the GBA games run so slow? I can only imagine there's serious optimization issues. At least the UI is straightforward and intuitive. I heard people using controllers had a hard time, but I had no issues with a keyboard and mouse. Although I don't like how if you turn animations off, you have no idea how the battle went. Why can't they have a quick animation with little HP bars, like in the Fire Emblem games?The story is a mess. It's so bad that I would've preferred no story, than wasting my time on one that's not engaging at all. The main issue is that every part seems to be written individually, and there's hardly a transition between them. You go from being conscripted, to fighting bandits, to having an encounter with the villain, to finally fighting the war, , doing various quests, fight a boss that randomly has a gorgeous portrait, slay a dragon for no reason, then fighting the war again, and then some random person in your party suddenly decides , and at that point, I just gave up trying to care. The characters and the world are introduced too quickly for you to be invested in it. The bonds are great though, on par with FE support conversations, and gives the cast some much-needed depth. Kind of a bummer that bonds don't give combat bonuses though. (This is where I overanalyze game mechanics. Skip it if you want.)The mechanics are overcomplicated for seemingly no reason. The beauty of Fire Emblem lies in its simplicity. Damage = attack - defense. Hit rate = accuracy - avoid. Factor in weapon triangle, supports, skills, and terrain, and you can calculate the numbers ahead of time, and form a plan accordingly. This is not the case in Dark Deity, where the mechanics are not only too complex, but also not transparent, so it's pretty much impossible to calculate numbers ahead of time, which is bad for a supposed "strategy" game. Your accuracy and evade is multiplied by a "map factor", which starts at 4 and decreases to 1.6 in the later maps. But the game never tells you it's doing this. Your damage output is multiplied by a percentage that depends on weapon and armor type. The percentage makes it very hard to calculate in your head, not to mention, there's 9 weapon types and 4 armor types, meaning 36 values to memorize. But it gets even worse- there's also this thing called mastery, which improves your advantageous matchups. By how much? The game doesn't tell you, and the real formula is so complex, it's impossible without a calculator. Normally, when an overly complex mechanic is present, it's used as a band-aid to prevent a cheese tactic or something unbalanced. For example, it's well known that "dodgetanking" is very powerful in many Fire Emblem games, so it's easy to imagine that the diminishing map factor was an attempt at mitigating that. And yet, the irony is, lategame dodgetanking is far more powerful in Dark Deity, than in most Fire Emblem games! Overall, game balance is pretty bad (though to be fair, not that it's much better in Fire Emblem). Dex is pretty much a god stat, as it affects both accuracy and evade (and by significant amounts), to the point where it almost singlehandedly dictates which characters/classes are good. I also don't like how there's no crit evade in this game, so every attack has a chance to crit (which only gets worse over time). Even without permadeath, this makes every fight needlessly stressful, and frustrating when it does happen. The devs added new mechanics to distinguish it from Fire Emblem, though it's debateable how well they're implemented. Although there's 4 choices at each promotion, some choices (like Strider) are far and away better than the alternatives, while others (basically anything that uses axes) are borderline unusable. Most of the time, there's 1-2 options that are clearly better. (I also don't like how so many class skills rely on RNG.) The same can be said about the 4 weapons everybody has. In theory, you get to choose between different weapons, but that only applies in the earlygame. Once you start upgrading weapons, you'll be using exclusively that, and then it's not interesting anymore. (There's also the fact that new recruits start with unupgraded weapons, which is annoying.) If you're experienced with Fire Emblem, you know that speed is the best stat, so yellow weapons are the best in most cases. Green weapons are a good backup weapon for securing finishing blows. Blue weapons are good for some specialized builds, otherwise you're just gambling. And red weapons are just trash most of the time. Have fun never doubling, getting doubled yourself, and missing half the time. (end overanalysis)I really wanted to like this game. As a Fire Emblem fan, I'm always on the lookout for similar SRPGs. And I try to cut small developers some slack. But I just can't. This game is barely playable. It has every flaw imaginable: bugs, resource-intensive, bad story, overly complex and opaque mechanics, unbalanced, and too much RNG. The story and the sheer number of bugs in particular, is so bad it's comical. The only saving grace is the clean UI and the bonds. 3/10EDIT for 1.5 Recurve update:The update changed nothing. Don't believe a word of what the patch notes say. It's the epitome of overpromising and underdelivering. The "localization" is a joke. Just look at all the complaints about poor grammar and broken nonsensical sentences. I wouldn't be surprised if the devs just threw everything into Google translate and called it a day. I don't know how many bugs they fixed, but they sure introduced new ones. Just go to the forums and see how many people are experiencing bugs and crashes. The game has not been more balanced. The accuracy rework changed very little, aside from inflating numbers on the status screen. If anything, the disparity between high and low hit/avoid only got bigger. As early as chapter 3, there are enemies that are so dodgy, even green weapons have ~60% change to hit, while your innacurate units have <20%. Previously, those numbers are at least 20-30% higher. How is that acceptable? Meanwhile, dodgetanking is still a thing, and still capable of soloing maps. This "update" feels like a desperate, last-ditch attempt to milk some more money.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is good, but it doesn't have the grinding that makes these games fun for me, so it's not my cup of tea. If you like tactics games, you'll like this.I know this may be a bit... petty. And a lot of people won't agree. But I really like grinding characters in games. I want to be able to use any unit whenever I want, but if you get bad level ups, or end up disliking a unit and want to go back to one from earlier, there's no way to catch them up. You have to stick with a team, and I'm not a big fan. Give optional grinding maps, then if people want to get OP, they have that option, and the people who will complain about it making the game too easy can just ignore the feature.And for those who say "just use the easy difficulty", that's not the same. There's a difference between the satisfaction of knowing I grinded my characters up to that point, and the enemies just naturally being so easy that there's no sense of accomplishment.Maybe I'm just looking too hard for something closer to Fire Emblem or Disgaea, but I really wanted to like this game. I love the art, and the gameplay itself is fun, I just really miss that feeling.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big believer in the malleability of standards, and I'm also someone who winces whenever I see someone insinuate that any reviewer who likes the latest gamer scapegoat must have either been paid off or clueless. All that being said, anyone who insinuates Dark Deity is a well-made game either has no degree of discernment whatsoever or has something to gain. The problems are so readily apparent that it is simply not arguable that the game is anything but heavily flawed. The only thing that can be argued is the degree to which these flaws damage the game. This is, sadly, the only lens with which I find this SRPG interesting to discuss. This is not a game with any well-implemented ideas. It does have, on the other hand, a varied selection of bad ideas, with some being good concepts done wrong, some being bad concepts done worse, and the bulk of it being unfinished if not outright lazy.On the most defensible side of things, you have ideas that I can see the merit in, but did not pan out well at all. Being a fan of permadeath, I did not like the death system at first. Hitting 0 HP means that unit is gone for the map and takes minimal attribute penalties--but after a few hours of play, I began to like the idea of such a system. It significantly reduces a player's desire to mash the "reset chapter" button at the slightest inconvenience, seeing as, providing the player plays well, these attribute penalties will occur very rarely and mean next to nothing, while still providing memorable divergence from the player's default state of play.The problem with Dark Deity's take on this system is that deaths still mean next to nothing even in excess. This is partly because the game gives you an absolute glut of units and deployment slots, allowing you to always have extra space for units that do nothing but act as meat shields (this is outright optimal on certain escape maps) and partly because these attribute penalties are so minimal that even if accrued by one of your core units, there's no reason to care. The penalties should have been a lot more substantial than they currently are, and there probably should have been an additional penalty for death on top of this.Another interesting but badly executed idea is the weapon system, where all units have 4 unbreakable and untradeable weapons that can be improved through upgrade materials. One weapon focuses on raw power, another on crit, another on accuracy, and the last one is supposed to be a balance between the three but in practice seemed to be anything but. The main issue here is that Dark Deity borrows from Fire Emblem's rather bad stat system, where doubling through speed (lowered by weight) is essential for both offense and defense and therefore, high weight weapons are a poor choice unless you can mitigate the weight or consistently keep that unit out of enemy attack range (i.e. archers). This results in an upgrade system where upgrading anything other than your low-weight accuracy-focused weapon (and maybe balance if your class has a good one) is a strictly worse option, with the only exceptions being archers and the one or two classes that have weight mitigation.This is several orders of magnitude worse than Fire Emblem's weapon mechanics, where even if the poorly-considered stat system led to bad weapons and occasionally outright bad classes, these bad options were at least never demanding of any valuable resource. In Dark Deity, not only are certain weapons strictly better than other weapons, but the game asks you to spend limited resources on such weapons, thereby allowing inexperienced players the chance to screw themselves over while giving experienced players no actually meaningful choice. This could have been partially mitigated by giving fully upgraded weapons some sort of ability that exists outside the purview of raw numbers, so even if the player decides to upgrade down a strictly worse weapon path, they at least get something unique out of it. As is, it's simply a choice between good bundles of stats and bad bundles of stats.The death system and the weapon system are, in spite of my criticisms, the only parts of the game I can actually see the merit in. From here, it gets nearly indefensible: we have the ideas that are simply and obviously bad, and should have/would have been vetoed by anyone on the design team with experience in the SRPG genre.The most obvious of these is the weapon vs armor mechanic, which I refuse to believe anyone actually understands or fully accounts for during play. The gist of it is that every unit has an armor type, and certain weapons gain a bonus or penalty against these armor types based on the unit's Mastery stat (How is this bonus/penalty calculated? We'll probably never know, it's that poorly explained). If this system wasn't bad enough on the face of it, the bonuses and penalties granted by it are percentage based rather than additive or subtractive, meaning it is practically impossible for anyone that's not a math prodigy to calculate exact damage during any given enemy phase.It would actually be partially misleading to call the bulk of Dark Deity's design decisions "bad ideas", as for the most part, the majority of the poor decisions stem from the culling of good ideas present in other SRPGs. For this reason, it is difficult to distinguish what was a calculated and bad decision and what was just simple laziness. The omission of terrain modifiers is particularly suspect.The laziness here is what really gets me, and makes me think that my take on all this is actually fairly generous. If this was yet another badly designed SRPG with a toothless narrative, I wouldn't even be writing this review, but Dark Deity is so blatantly lazy, bugged, and outright under-cooked that I cannot fully rule out the possibility that this was a game designed purely for clout and networking purposes. The developers of Dark Deity led a massive advertising campaign, incessantly and aggressively engaged in publicity stunts with SRPG-focused youtubers, hired some of the most well-known voice actors in the industry, and we still ended up with a map that looks like Add onto all this the fact that this game was suddenly released without any warning after no Fire Emblem title was announced at E3, and the red flags become nuclear sirens: I am almost certain that this game exists purely so that a small group of amoral techies can worm their way into the industry by boasting "Hey, my first game was a #1 best seller on Steam with acclaimed voice actors, hire me". I really hope I'm wrong on this, but even if I'm not, the game still frankly sucks.
