_childDocuments_.review: I was lured into this game by the promise of a modernized Fire Emblem like experience but was let down by the lack of charm and immersion that made me fall in love with this games inspiration. The game plays like an unceremonious DnD homebrew that the DM just cant quite wait to be over and done with. To specify, the best summary disappointment I can provide rears its ugly head when your first unit reaches level 10. You bring your new favorite unit into position, kill that bandit, you watch your exp reach the the level 10 threshold, then you get a pop-up screen that forces you to pick an evolution for that character right then and there. That's it. No animation, no special chime or tune, you don't have to find an event/item/certain time to promote your character. It just happens with no lead up and is over as fast as the pop-up can close. As if by gaining enough experience you pull an entire new set of armor/weapon/horse out of your backpack and slap it on. This isn't the only unceremonious quirk I take exception to, as the transitions from completing the combat portion of a chapter to the story portion of another is not a gentle process nor always a sensical one. I didn't care too much about the end of the battles  until I reach about chapter 7 or 8 where you have to fight a large number of enemies and defeat a specified number to advance. Much like the my previous quip the stage suddenly and with no lead up, ends. For this example, once the specified number of units were slain a pop-up score screen appears and we are on to the next bit of story. This really hit home on this particular chapter as it was quite easy (So we can avoid any tit for tat, I play on deity), the specified amount of units to kill was less than half the enemies total, there was still some loot I could have gotten from the guys in the far back, and On a similarly disenchanting note, the graphics and other assets need to be polished up and tuned. What you may notice first about this game is that the background pixel art for the combat portions of the game use very basic and poorly lit tiles. While I do understand that making assets can be difficult, you spend a great deal of time looking at these particular pieces of art and they do not look nicer the longer you have to look at them.On stranger note, there comes a time in an automated animation cycle where selecting a child's head to put on a mans body is not quite accurate. As the characters start out in their level 1 forms, they are quite well represented in their combat animations. As you progress through the game and your characters get promoted their in combat models also changes, great! Well it would be if the models weren't just a head of that character stapled to a different body each time. The most jarring profound example is perhaps the young mage of the party. The only true mechanical departure from this game and the Fire Emblem series is the exchange of the weapon triangles for static damage and armor types. I do believe one of the most charming and immersive combat portions of the FE series was the ability to use different weapons when available, decide if you want to use the limited durability of a specific weapon, and make tactical decisions based on what weapons you have equipped at the end of your turn. most of those choices are removed here. While each character does get 4 different variants of the same damage type that have slightly differing stats, , I just wasn't happy with my choices, or lack there of.This game could be great with more polish.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a slight thumbs up.Before playing this game, I was deep in Vestaria saga; which was one of the most frustrating game experiences. Both Dark Deity and Vestaria are inspired by the Fire Emblem games, and both have problems that are on opposite sides of the spectrum. Vestaria saga was convoluted, and super duper hard; to the point where one of your dudes could just be one shot by a low lever enemy.Dark Deity has the opposite problem -- it's super, super easy. There's also no permadeath; yet you still have a ton of dudes added to your army every chapter. I felt games like this had all these extra team members, so you could play on even with permadeath. But with the team never growing smaller, and so many of them similar in style; it gets repetative real fast, and the stakes and pressure just isnt there.If only I could find a game somewhere in the middle of Dark Deity and Vestaria Saga I'd be in heaven.If this ones on sale, and you dig Fire Emblem, give it a go and have for for a few hours. But don't expect to be drawn in for the long haul.

_childDocuments_.review: After replaying this game, I have come to enjoy it much more. I am not sure what the devs changed since 2021, but I will say that it is a lot more fun than it was a few months upon release. Reviewers have problems with this game that are either outdated or are due to their own inability to adapt to new mechanics. By reviewers, I mean Fire Emblem fans.It is a well known fact that Fire Emblem fans are monkey-brained individuals. I will state some of the more common complaints I have seen in the reviews and express how I feel they are incorrect or not applicable.This is  There is no weapon system, it runs on armor classes. and if you hover your mouse over the icons at the top left, you can see the % modifier you have against certain armor types. It is for this reason that I highly recommend  having more than one of the same class.Fire Emblem fans are too used to the weapon triangle that they cannot comprehend another strategy game having a different type of advantage system.  As I said earlier, this game has armor types that will take extra damage depending on the enemies' attack type.These types are: Slash, pierce, cleave, crush, projectile, arcane, fire, storm, and holy. Each of these categories will determine how much damage you deal depending on the enemy's armor type, ranging from -10% to +40%. A green arrow will be next to an enemy if your unit has a +% damage modifier, and red if you have a -% damage modifier.  This is where every Fire Emblem veteran  Just because you see a green arrow, does not mean that the battle is completely stacked in your favor, and a red arrow does not always mean you will get stomped.For example: Irving is a unit with Plate armor and Slashing damage who does major damage to Leather and Rune Cloak armor types. Another unit Alvin, has Rune Cloak armor and Arcane damage and deals major damage to Plate and Chain armor types. If they were to fight, even though Irving would see a green arrow next to Alvin because he does major damage to those with Rune Cloak armor, the playing field would be leveled since Alvin does major damage to Plate armor. Unlike the weapon triangle system, this  effects the damage modifier. Hit rates and damage reduction will  change depending on attack types. Hit rates and dodges are effected by the stats of your weapon (accuracy, weight) and the Dexterity stat. A unit facing a red arrow enemy will not always do bad, it just means the damage they do will be reduced by x% amount.Weapons each have different stats that change upon upgrading them. Some get heavier but more accurate, some gain extra crit rate but no power. I believe the stats on the weapons vary by class, since some strength weapons at +4 would have 12 damage and 1 accuracy for a Slashing class, but have 12 damage and 0 accuracy for a Crushing class. The weapons you use are completely independent from the armor system. They effect your hit rate, dodge, crit rate, and flat damage output. When it comes to upgrading them, I recommend buying 4-8 Tier tokens per chapter, since the stat boosters are simply not needed and healing items are littered throughout maps in enemy inventories. I personally upgraded the weapons of units that I felt were lacking in a certain stat so that they would be able to keep up. Speaking of keeping up...This is . Contrary to what the Fire Emblem elitists preach, bases are  over growths, both in Fire Emblem and Dark Deity. In fact, growths also do not matter, and setting up your army around them will sour your experience. Dark Deity is a game that encourages class diversity and spreading out exp. Any unit you decide to train will be good against whatever armor class they have advantages against, and skills should  be top priority when choosing classes. When new units join your army, they should be around the same level as your top few units, not so far ahead that you start benching others in their place. In my first playthrough, I got to the dragon and the dwarf that joined me was a full 5 levels ahead of my best unit. On my second playthrough, (both on Hero difficulty) he was around my 5th highest level unit, and I already had lower-level units that could fit his role better than he could.In my first playthrough, my Fire Emblem-tainted brain made Garrick an Archer since it was a class I was familiar with, and it essentially rendered his personal skill of crit dmg +15% worthless. In my second playthrough, I made him a Drifter since it came with skills that garnered towards high crit rates and high crit damage. Also, just because you choose a certain class at level 10, you shouldn't lock yourself into that class's Stage 2 promotion. Look for the class that gives you more skills that benefit your build.I made Sloane a Magician and promoted her into a Wizard since she was really fast but lacked defense, and it gave her two great skills that increased her magic damage and paired nicely with her other skills. In my first playthrough, both Maeve and Garrick were Archers, and Elias, Bianca, and Iris were Adepts. I chose these class pathways with no thought for their skills and damage types, and it created 3 units that all excelled against the same few units but got demolished by the rest. As we know, Fire Emblem fans are brain dead. They are all too familiar with using units like Sigurd and Seth to solo their games, but they become raging children when they cannot do this in Dark Deity. The game frequently has groups of enemies with different armor classes and damage types, so 1 unit usually cannot take on an entire group by themselves.I rarely encountered bugs while playing until the last few maps. Units would be shown in one spot but be selectable in another, and it would prevent other units from attacking or healing. I never experienced the bug until the map where you open the gates to the final castle. Also, any Fire Emblem game besides 9 and 10 would be rated 6/10 or below if people actually accounted the story in enjoyment. Conquest is one of the best entries in the series even while having the worst story of all of them, and 90% of players skip through New Mystery of the Emblem's story. This game's story is most definitely better than both of those, and anyone that says its story being bad matters does not truly care. Eat dirt you little story-obsessed-but-not-really freakazoids.If you had any of the problems above or made the mistakes I made in my first playthrough, I heavily recommend trying the game again while keeping what I said in mind. Classes and skills are what matter the most in this game, and diversity is rewarded and should be prioritized. Even if they have green arrows, check enemy weapon types to see if they do increased damage to your armor type. Spend money on Tier tokens, as stat boosters and healing items aren't necessary in the long run.Also, the chapter unanimously considered to be the worst in the game, Chapter 19, has been greatly changed and is now fun. I noticed that in the final chapter, the final boss just ended his turn instead of attacking me after I surrounded him. Granted, it was the turn before I killed him that he waited, so I'm not sure if it's a bug......but why is Bianca GAY? That has to be a bug. Overall, I would rate this game 7.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect too much from the game going in, but much to my surprise there's a surprising amount of fresh vision put into it, that it's easily the best PC Fire Emblem I have come across!-Story-This is the weakest link, the lore and meta narrative is serviceable, even intriguing at occasions, but often times feels very sluggish and transitions between chapters at times is really jarring. These sections get way too long winded at times, especially if the bonds between units have to address the main events from chapters. There's some really good character development to be seen the closer you get to the end, but a lot of the bonds between units often times lack real drama, and even the tension half the time is very superficial, it can be hard to get invested. If you are more about the banter than gameplay, I would suggest intentionally picking characters that will poke and tease others, it makes the bond conversations way more entertaining.-Gameplay-Now this is where the game really excels! Now you have to consider not just weapons, but what armor everyone is wearing. How different passive skills interact with actions, or other units, should you mix promotion paths, or further develop one focused path? would a special class action come in handy when direct combat won't help? The fundamental mechanics are so diverse and potent that the same approach or unit composition might not work so well in the next chapter. Chapters have a variety of objectives, so it won't always be routing a set of enemies. Essentially what Dark Deity brings to the table is actual strategy, which I found often too lacking in Fire Emblem games!-Production Quality-I'm blown away with the music quality especially! Notes almost perfectly convey what is needed in every situation. Character design is great, not just the conversation sprites, but especially the smaller pixel versions of units are very impressive! I really like all the idle animations at play! It's also worth noting the promotional stuff you see here in store have the old backgrounds, which look way worse than the current updated ones, all the same backgrounds are okay, but I gather this isn't per say for lack of skill in the area, it's more a limitation from the game engine 'Game Maker'

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for all Fire Emblem fans. I got tired of the new FE games because of all the junk you have to do between battles. Dark Deity plays like the FE games I fell in love with. Those GBA games were peak FE for me and Dark Deity captures that same magic. It can feel a little bit janky to play but I couldn't care less. This is the game I have been looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: This is effectively a simplified version of classic Fire Emblem games. Each class has exactly four weapons that don't break but can be upgraded, and the bond system is simplified. I love it. Plus, there's no forced tutorial, which I love. I've played enough games like this to know how to play, that the game doesn't force me through a pointless tutorial is a HUGE boon IMO. The story doesn't take itself too seriously but is still engaging, and the set save points have a very quick recap when you start them, which is awesome to have that very brief reminder after a day away while I was at work or what-not.The music and voice work is good. Not amazing, but good. I listen to it more often than not. The animation is simple and delightful. So yeah, great game, highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like this game but it is just not finished. Menu UI is awful. And most off putting to me personally was the music. The entire school is being drafted in what seems like a terrible event but the cheery town music just keeps on playing. Bandits are attacking and the cheery town music just keeps on going. Just not the right tone for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Game lacks terrain types, the map design is terrible, its all empty spaces and corridors. The UI isnt any good and the gameplay lacks depth.No patch will fix most of these problems, the sprites and artwork is good but that cant carry the game, at the end of the day the gameplay is bland, unit customization is very good even compared to 3Ds era FEs, but units lack identity (you even get to choose the prepromotes classes the moment they join). Even as a very vanilla FE-like game the armor/weapon type mechanic makes calculating damage very difficult and you have to guess how much damage you will actually do/take, this isnt helped by the weird % damage boosters in the game.Dont buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. If you're as big a fan as I of the older Fire Emblem games for the GBA then this game is right up your alley. It's challenging, the characters and classes are really cool, and the mechanics and features make for a great game in the turn-based strategy RPG genre. I 100% recommend this game to fans of any game in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Difficulty spike comes at around Chapter 10. It has the progression style like classic FE, so if any unit falls behind, they will kind of stay that way, since level difference is pretty huge with how battles are designed without anything designed for the player to really get to set up. You're shunted into the fray on most maps with an incentive to finish quickly for more gold. Gold management seemed really shallow to me, It was a chore trying to keep most units up at a matching scale with the enemies who grew in levels and gear very early in. This was especially evident when given a new unit who while matched the level jump, joins without upgraded weapon skills, so they really don't come equipped ready to play without spending thousands of gold you hardly have.Character designs are a solid plus, and the dialogue is pretty well tailored from what I was seeing. (Though the story moves unrealistically quickly in the first 10 chapters.) I'm giving a negative review mostly in that the normal mode seems pretty unbalanced since there's very little way to play catch up with units. and new one's joining needing hand holding as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity its a fun tactical rpg with simple plot inspired by FE games,  any fan of the saga will be atracted. Character portraits and battle sprites are well done and show a lot of detail.The OST its good, but i think most of it don't "fit" the setting or the environment of the game.There are only a couple of songs that really stand out, especially one near the end of the journey. We have some flaws which most of them are in the bug department, nothing game breaking but sometimes annoying. Also as you keep advancing in the game, the map design falls in the quality, making some of them feel "empty".I hope that you guys keep working for future installments, because this game has a lot of love poured on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a solid Fire Emblem style tactical turn-based game. The overall story is fairly okay and easy to ignore if it doesn't interest you anyway. The character designs are great both in-battle and during the visual novel style talking parts. Some of the level designs are a slog to get through which can be frustrating and time consuming but overall it's a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've run out of Fire Emblem games, this is a good substitute.The weapon/upgrade system is interesting, and the branching class paths are cool (but it is hard to tell what will be good ahead of time). The varied options for each character will make this worth replaying.It would be nice to have terrain effects and the accuracy/evasion calculations be explicit, and it is difficult to manage how the 9 damage types each interact with 4 armor types to be able to correctly position units for the enemy phase.Also, there is a Windrunner class and a Cosmere magic school, for those to whom those terms mean anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: FrickenMoron and Atreus basically said all the points I have against this game, so I'll just consolidate them here.- There are no UI sounds at all. No sounds for moving the cursor, selecting an unit, the unit moving etc. I honestly wasn't sure if this was a bug at first, but it seems this is by design? It really gives the game a beta-build feel.- The music is.... not good. It just lacks character. There's also weird mood whiplashes where cheerful music plays at scenes that are supposed to be sad/tragic for example. (my own note; music continues to play over the turn transitions, so you get very grating noises where the turn transitions play through the music and it just sounds terrible.)- There are no explanations on the games systems. I only realized in the third mission that each character has four weapon types available that focus on different stats. (There's a 'tutorial' but it's really just text boxes, and it badly explains mechanics. Also, I don't quite understand why they felt a need to have every character have four options for combat at the start.- There are a LOT of loading screens. Like, this is supposed to be a GBA style game, and the game is so poorly optimized that we need hard cuts to loading screens just to load new backgrounds and portraits? We aren't doing anything graphically intensive here, and this is on a Solid State Drive. I almost thought I was playing an online game where it was checking in with the server every scene.- The story feels very bland and I have literally no idea who anyone is. In chapter 1 we meet "sword guy with older brother", "bow guy", "healer girl" and "magic kid". That is LITERALLY all we get from them, but we're supposed to be invested. Why dump 4 characters, plus a teacher, plus an older brother, plus them two companions of the older brother, on us in the first four minutes? Then drop in two OTHER characters in the next chapter's pre-fight scenes!?-No Borderless Fullscreen option hurts. This game, again, does not look intensive, but we couldn't develop a borderless fullscreen option for seamless alt-tabbing? Again, this game needs some optimization done to it.This feels like an Early Access game, yet it was Kickstarter'd and is not being sold as Early Access. Here's hoping it gets updates to make it better, but for now, I'll have to tell my friends to hold off on buying. Which is a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm really enjoying it! Echoing what a lot of people have already said there are definitely spots that need polishing up (better tutorial, sfx issues) but early impressions are definitely positive.Coming from history in Fire Emblem, I love the iterations I'm seeing so far. The wound mechanic is a clever way to keep the stakes high without grinding your run to a halt like in FE, and I am an absolute sucker for branching classes. The weapon upgrade system is super cool...now that I understand it. It took until I had access to my menu a few levels in to understand how it worked, and until then I had been working under the assumption that it was a weapon triangle of some sorts. There are still a few things in the stats and menus that I'm not clear on but I'm guessing they'll present themselves in time.I'm playing on Heroic and the difficulty is good, so as long as it keeps this pace with a few curveballs here and there, I'm satisfied. That said, tactical games like this kind of live or die by their difficulty scaling, so here's hoping it doesn't peter off before the end game.All in all, I'd say if you like Fire Emblem or tactical RPGs this is absolutely worth your money and time. At the bare minimum, wishlist it and keep an eye on it, because it's got a rock solid foundation and with a little QOL love I think this game will stand shoulder to shoulder with the likes of Fire Emblem or Wargoove.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Don't usually review games, but wanted to give my thoughts to the team behind the game as well as anyone interested in playing it. I backed this game on kickstarter and I have been following along as well since then.TLDR: If you like Fire Emblem, you'll probably like this game. It does have flaws, and certainly some things are not polished, but the core game is fun despite some issues.I am on Chapter 12- which I imagine is halfway through. Playing on the hardest difficulty with base settings.Pros: Class Fantasy- there are lots of different branching paths for classes, and with individual character traits it makes for interesting combinations. Some do feel better than others, but mostly feel balanced to situation.Combat Animations-They bring me back to the GBA days of fire emblem, and they are very well done. Some of the attacks feel that they even have a little oomph behind them. Magic is especially cool looking, and I have a couple of favorite critical animations that I watch every time.Map Design- So far I feel that there is a lot of variation in level design. A lot of maps feel different in scope and make me think a little more than usual on who to send where, even though I still don't have a good grasp on what is better (more on this later).Combat- The hardest difficulty does feel hard, if a little unfair, but not like NIghtmare plus mode in mainstream Fire Emblem. I do see ways for adaptation in tactics after I beat a chapter to where I could have done better and not lost troops in some ways.So So:The Characters/Support conversations- These have not been bad by any means, but some feel almost awkward in context. it doesn't help that the music during support conversations so far is the same, really upbeat tune that almost distracts me from the conversation. I will say that most of the characters don't feel like they are "the grumpy one" like we have gotten a lot with modern Fire Emblem. However some of the writing/dialogue seems odd coming from certain characters. Additionally, if I had not known some of the character bio's from the discord, I would have no context to their dialogue. Having those lore bits in game would probably help players who are new, but I even found myself having to go back to the discord to look at the previous bio's to understand what these characters were doing and who they were. There is not much context given in game (So far).The controls- I have been playing on mouse and keyboard, which to say the least has been a bit clunky. The cursor seems to click at random times, forcing me to hit back and reclick in combat. I have lost a couple of turns to this what I think is a bug? You also have to click several times to get things done in combat. For example, if you click on an enemy to auto move to it, you then need to click again on its space and another time to start the combat. It feels clunky which sometimes detracts from the experience.The Story- No spoilers here, but some of the decisions and story beats don't really make sense to me. Things escalate very quickly at times, and I find myself really questioning the characters decisions. It almost feels at some points that I straight up missed a entire cutscene or lore dump. Like I am missing context, when I have read every bit of story thus far. It just feels a bit out of place sometimes. Certainly not bad so far, but it is not cohesive.The Wounds mechanic- I have not restarted a chapter, which the game wants you to not do as if your character goes to zero they instead get a wound which permanently detracts from their stats. it is a interesting system, and it is even based on what kind of damage did you in. But there is not a way I have seen to see what wounds a character has (would be nice to see and maybe even remember the chapter it happened) and the text only shows up once during battle. Additionally it kind of cheapens combat in some aspects-like there is not a lot of consequence to losing characters over and over again, which makes me feel like I can just throw people in and do as much damage as possible. I do hope the devs introduce some sort of option to make death permanent (or at least like 3H where they participate in story but they can no longer be chosen) or some sort of system where after a certain amount of wounds you cannot participate in the next battle. Sometimes my mage goes down and looses strength several times, when it is already 0, so other than xp I don't feel punished for misplacing them. One other thing about this, and I am unsure if this is oversight or not, but when a character gets to 0, it plays sad music and shows text as if they are dying, like in Fire emblem. Its a bit goofy when they are not dead and they just get a minor wound. Some sort of text signifying retreat would be more appropriate.   Cons:Music choices- This has been one of the more frustrating things so far. The music is not bad in a vacuum, but when something dark or tragic happens, I am often confused by the jingly tune that sounds like I am in a jrpg magic shop buying an item. I don't mind if it were repeating often but it matched the mood. The worst of these instances are during the support conversations, where no matter what the music is light and upbeat, and the story cutscenes, where again even if the worst possible thing just happened the music is so happy and upbeat. These songs do have place within the narrative so far, but they are not appropriate in other places. It sounds like they do have some more dark or somber music within other places, and I wonder if that could not be applied to various bits of the story in which it would match. Lack of information- The developers are working on this, but I figure at least for now to put this out there for anyone on the fence. Across the board, there is a severe lack of information. The game has a small tutorial tips in the menu, but it does not explain the vast amount of mechanics and terms. Unlike fire emblem, not every menu you can click to view more of an explanation, and early on this amounted to me guessing what might be good or bad. Combat sometimes can feel like a guessing game, and I honestly still am guessing about what is better where. There seems to be a weapon triangle (Square?) system like in fire emblem, but I usually end up hitting whatever does the most damage. Some aspects of the UI are also confusing at first, and I have encountered a couple of objectives that were not clear in what I was to do. One mission has you defend an ally, who can also be used in combat, for 8 turns. I accidentally moved her into range and she got obliterated, which I figured would make me restart. But it did not and it seemed I just needed to survive for that long. Another you are tasked with defending the health of a objective, but there was not a great explanation on which enemies were dealing damage to the health bar. I mentioned it earlier but I also feel I am missing a core chunk of information about the story/characters as I question decisions they make. I say this in context that I have played every Fire Emblem game made, and some of them it was a bit of a guessing game. But the lack of information did not feel like this game does sometimes. If you are someone who has never played a fire emblem game, you may find this very confusing at first.Overall, as someone who kickstarted this game, I am very happy with the outcome so far. There are a couple of things that I wish would be different, but the core loop of the game is solid. I hope the Devs can take all of the feedback, continue to work on the game, and learn from it in their future projects. I would recommend this in a heartbeat to anyone who loved Fire Emblem or turn based strategy games at full price.  Despite my gripes with some aspects of the game, I have continued to play and welcome the idea of future content for the game or more from this dev team.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool indie SRPG, very reminiscent of GBA-era Fire Emblem but also with its own interesting quirks and systems.Pros:- The artstyle is very colourful and unique, and the spritework and animations are very well-done, I really like in particular how the health bar is destroyed depending on the attack that landed the killing blow, as well as the hand-drawn maps and backgrounds.- The strategy gameplay is very fun, and is a refreshing mix of familiar systems (for anyone who's played FE) and new mechanics to make approaching combat interesting. The grave wound system, replacing the infamous permadeath system, adds some interesting depth to weighing up risks.- The characters, in FE-inspired fashion, are colourful and interesting, and very fun to fight with as well. The bonds, while they don't have any gameplay benefit, are still very fun to read.Neutral:- The plot is fairly standard so far. and the writing. while very humorous and sometimes 4th-wall breaking, doesn't take itself super seriously. Not necessarily a con, but it depends on what you're looking for in a story.Cons:- The tutorials feel somewhat lacking, and is also not great at explaining the advantage system, which is it's own mess. Thankfully the chart makes it a little less confusing, but thanks to the UI arrows you don't need to think about it too much.- Bugs are definitely better than they once were, but it's not 100% polished yet. While it's just a nitpick, I do find transitions between scenes to be too quick and jarring.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the game in a 5 for 5$ bundle. I've had a lot of fun playing the game. I wouldn't spend more than 5$ on it though. It feels like Fire Emblem: Sacred Stones in a lot of ways. Before you buy: there are a lot... and I mean A LOT of map bugs. I can't tell you how many times I've had a solid strategy only to be ruined by a unit getting stuck in limbo, not being where the map says they are, or some how getting glitched into a wall/another unit. What I liked: similar feel to an OG Fire Emblem if you need an itch scratched that FE: Engage didn't. There are some really cool classes too. What I didn't like: BugsToo many units for a game without perma death (and no way to grind maps to level people who fall behind)The story is generic and full of anime troupes (wait... maybe I like that!?) The bond system feels pointless, though I like the writing in the bonds better than the actual story writingWorth getting on sale around 5$ if you got a scratch to itch. I wouldn't buy it full price.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial impression of this game was extremely negative and I believe this is mainly due to the game simply being unfinished and a huge lack of playtesting. IF this was in early access right now I would be much more gracious but the fact that the developers consider this to be finished is a very bad sign. I really wanted to love this game because I love the GBA Fire Emblems but this feels like the developers had no idea why people loved those games so much.The game has apparent glitches and polish is clearly missing. The tips menu forgets your sound settings and changes the SFX volume to max while you're on it. You can't inspect the stats or gear of enemies. The first boss cannot move (traditional in Fire Emblem games) but you are given ranged units in that battle and he has no ranged attacks. Meaning he literally cannot fight back. How on Earth did that get past playtesting?The game throws so much information at you with no explanation of how it works. All FOUR of your starting characters each have FOUR weapons and the differences between them are not made clear (atleast in the first hour). Character abilities are not explained, Liberty has an action called Phase but I can't select it and nowhere does it say what that does. When you get the Rogue in the second battle if you move him next to an enemy you'll see he has the Disarm ability but it doesn't explain exactly what that entails nor anywhere on his info screen does it say he has this ability.In the first hour of playing this game felt like discount Fire Emblem made by a team of college students who released the game before it was ready in order to capitalize off of their E3 hype. It doesn't do anything unique to separate itself from Fire Emblem making it look like a sad imitation instead of a true spiritual successor and I genuinely hate that. I wanted to love this game but I just can't recommend it in the current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game! It was a fun experience, it scratched that Fire Emblem itch for me. It feels low-budget, but it also has a small price so you get what you pay for.The good:+ It's a Fire Emblem clone, same art style everything. If you like that, you'll like this.+ Some cool character classes+ Pretty good pacing+ I thought the maps were good. Not too big, not too small. Had chokepoints and everything to control the flow of battle.+ Art style was fine+ Character progression was cool+ I like how characters permanently lose stats when they die. It's punishing enough so you worry about keeping your characters alive, but not so harsh that you feel like having to restart the game once they die.The meh- It's a Fire Emblem clone. If you do not like Fire Emblem, this is not for you.- Some UI was a bit unclear. Unable to check victory conditions once the battle has started- You get a ton of characters, but can only use half. The once you don't use get no xp, so they just rot away. I would've liked to experiment some more with rosters, but the game discourages you from doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. My first playthrough was blind on Deity mode. This game is a lot easier than most FE games. Most chapters, including late-game chapters, can be easily cleared first try without needing to reset. If you've played FE games before, play on Deity to give yourself some semblance of a challenge.Dark Deity is way easier than most GBA games on the hardest setting. Comparable to Awakening Lunatic. Only slightly harder than 3 Houses Hard, way easier than Maddening.Worth the money at full price if you love GBA FE, otherwise it's very good on a sale.Pros:+ Good character designs, some very entertaining support conversations+ Large variety of weapons and attack animations+ A lot of classes (although not all of them are equally viable)+ Built-in "mod" features like item/character/stat randomizer, customizable difficulty+ Fundamentally works pretty well as a FE clone, the formula just works+ Good progression pacing; both you and the enemy get stronger at a respectable rate+ Never feel starved or cheated out of exp or gold due to exp curve and generous drops (even when experimenting as a new player)+ Trinket system has more depth than the simple stat-boosters in most FE games+ Lose a random amount of a random stat when a unit "dies" instead of permadeath, allows enemies to be very intimidating while saving time and frustration+ Fully flexible class progression - 4 paths for tier 2 class, then you can pick ANY of the 4 corresponding tier 3 classes later (i.e you can pick tier 2 archer, then pick tier 3 myrmidon/fast sword user)+/- No weapon triangle, instead there is a new armor vs damage type system+/- Weapons are not stored in inventory and don't have durability, instead every character has 4 permanent, upgradeable weapons with different stat spreads. Also means there are no weapons with unique traits like Armorslayer or Levin Sword.Cons:- Questionable class balance especially with respect to the armor system, basically certain combinations of stat growth/damage type/armor type are extremely bad (slightly alleviated by flexible class progression)- Maps are pretty bad to look at, artistically far worse than any GBA FE, not a huge deal if you're here for the gameplay anyway - Clear bugs, like enemy attack range being displayed inaccurately when there is too much terrain- Could not give a ♥♥♥♥ about the story- Random weird inconveniences, like sound effects from certain weapons being extremely loud compared to others- Like Returnal, no in-battle saving
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read this review you should know I'm a Fire Emblem Loser. I've played all of them and somehow still love the series.Good:- Animation: They were so good. Honestly better than the GBA Fire Emblem animations. Best part of the game by far.- Character Art & Music: Very Anime! I'm a big fan.- Voice Acting: Made the game feel higher quality than it actually was- New Ideas: I like how the game punishes you for letting a unit fall in battle. The debuffs probably should have been more sever tho. The way weapons worked was also neat. I hope it's expanded upon.- Maps: There were a handful of very fun maps. I really liked the tree house and the palace. Bad:- Story & Characters: Kind of a bore for me. I think the fact that the writer probably had to spend writing 30+ support conversations really had an impact on the rest of the story feeling just sloppy.- Too many characters: In Fire Emblem you receive a ton of units because you might need them to replace dead units. In this game you can't lose units, but still receive like 30 characters. The new characters are generally  better than your old ones as well. It was very annoying when you had been training a unit up but a new an improved version shows up like 2 chapters later. It also kinda irked me that you got to choose their class every time they showed up. It really took away from that character's personality.- Maps: Very uninspired. I enjoyed the variance in quest objectives but the maps never had anything to keep the players on their toes. Some of the maps felt like cop outs as well. The dragon and second to last level are two good examples.- Bugs: Good lord this game needed more development time. The bugs were almost game breaking. Sometimes enemies would be able to attack from across the map without telling me. Enemy attack ranges don't update when you move a character or defeat an enemy. There are some tiles you can't hover over without the game crashing. Sometimes the game would forget that I had a ranged weapon, so I had to stop moving the character, switch the weapon, then go back to attack. This game needed way more play testing.Overall:I think if this game was as polished as it's battle animations screen then it could have been great. Unfortunately the rest of the game is a far cry from that level of quality. All that being said, I'm excited to see what comes next from these developers. I feel like with some experience under their belt they could put out some real banger SRPG games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with Dark Deity. I think there are a lot of good aspects to this game - the combat is well done, the animations are clean, and the sound effects are satisfying. The class system enables making cool builds with your characters, and the aspects are cool as well. If you want a fun tactical game and don't care very much about the story, then this is a great buy. If you care about the story, well.... the story is bad. The characters are kindof dumb, and the dialogue is cringe. If you want to scratch the fire emblem itch but don't have a switch, this will do the trick. Overall pretty good, i'd say 7.5/10, but only because i don't care about the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Why would you make the open command replace the attack command without a confirm option. Now my unit is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dead because I pressed a to check a damage range.On a more serious note, this game has a lot of issues. It can definitely be enjoyable, but the quality is questionable. Here are some examples:Poor balancing: In chapter 6 on the middle difficulty 1 random enemy archer has 11 power, the next one has 24. Big gaps between the same enemy units is common and makes it impossible to get a good feeling for how much damage an enemy might do to you.Frequent bugs: The attack range indicator of the enemies doesn't update after they move which could easily result in the death of a unit if you forget to update it and think your units aren't in danger. There is also a very common bug when giving units movement commands where a unit both is and isn't selected at the same time. It's very minor but just reflects the lack of polish this game has. The displayed damage is also frequently inaccurate.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a re-skinned Fire Emblem. A very antiquated SRPG format of move units a few blocks then attack, move attack, move attack repeat. There is no real strategy involved aside from resource management in regards to exp. The strategy is rotate your units to make sure the one with the lowest amount of exp gets to attack next. That's not strategy and it's not fun. There is no real team compositions and unit synergy. You can change units class, you can bond units with others, but all party comps are viable. Each unit has a unique trait or ability, some are clearly better than others. This is the closest thing to a wrinkle this game has, and makes you consider who you might want to take into battle, but again, it doesn't really matter in the end. Story is beyond derivative, you play as a group of mercenaries, you fight bandits and kingdoms. I really wish more SRPGs would try and do something different and devs would have an imagination. This is a team doing the bare minimum to make an SRPG. Went through, checked all the boxes. Zero creativity or imagination. Nothing new, nothing fun. If you are looking to shut your brain off, move units and attack, and have your memba berries tickled, then you are the target audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is a turn-based strategy game in the likes of Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics. After a short conversation, you immediately get into your first battle to test your skills in the genre. As there is no tutorial, it's up to you to find out how everything works. Battles are turn-based. You can move and attack, heal, use items, or other abilities such as disarm and a few more. Every character has their basic attack and one ability. When attacking enemies, an animation will pop up and you'll see their attacks.At first, battles will seem easy and simple but as you progress in the story, battles will get harder, and more tactical. Although heroes just have one ability, their basic attack changes with their equipped weapon. Every hero has four weapons and while they don't differ in looks, stats are different enough to bring more depth into battles.After every move in a battle, heroes will gain EXP. Leveling up will raise their attributes (HP, Strength, etc.). At levels 10, 20, and 30 you can choose between one of four classes. The new class will give your hero new weapons, a new or improved ability, or attributes changes. Much like in Fire Emblem, your heroes will strengthen their bond over time. In fact, their bond will strengthen when nearby in fights. This unlocks dialogues between them in the camp. Speaking of, every few chapters, you'll have the possibility to get into your camp. You can check your heroes, their inventories, buy items in the shop, upgrade their weapons and read the dialogues between heroes.Most items are there to heal your characters in a battle but there are also some which will give upgrades to attributes.Upgrading your weapons makes their stats better. They will do more damage, have a higher accuracy or chance of a critical hit.     Dark Deity offers something most Fire Emblem fans are missing on PC. While this certainly doesn't reach the quality a Triple-A game does, and some QoL features are missing, the turn-based battles are tactical and challenging enough to warrant giving this a try if you're into TBS - even if you just want to skip all dialogues!
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to give this game a chance because I had an itch for a trpg and this one looked good despite being made by a small group.PROS+The sprite work is great, the units and the different attacks based on weapon looks amazing.+The weapon/armor system is kinda complicated to remember in the middle of the game but I personally like it.CONS-Massive amount of missing QoL changes. (Quick option to restart a map, put character faces next to the dialog boxes, icons for items, etc)-Story goes at lightspeed. You are killing bandits at one point, blink and then you are a war criminal for both sides in the conflict.-Weapon system is awful on the enemy side. Massive amount of enemies with strong weapons with low acc means that 1shots with no counterplay because unlucky hit and crit rolls happen more often that you'd think.-Soundtrack is either decent enough or stock music level, there is no in between.-Gameplay wise the maps feel really boring, could have use a lot of work on this part.- A lot of maps dont have any bosses which feels lame and if they do they are most of the time really weak or not coded properly. (Range1 only bosses who doesnt move so you can easily kill him from range).-AI problems like enemies not wishing to attack or reinforcements that dont move unless an enemy is at range, so they also block the way of other reinforcements for free.-Crit is either broken or not displaying the chance correctly. Game saying you have an average 30% chance to crit yet going multiple maps with less than 10% kinda broken.-Some attacks take waaaay too long. Why do some spells have like 3 times the attack duration compared to other ones?TL: DR = Not worth it at the current moment. Keep an eye for changes because I do feel the game does have potential to be so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: When Nintendo fails to announce a new Fire Emblem at E3 in 2021, Dark Deity scratched the itch left in the aftermath. Sure it's different here and there but Fire Emblem games already have huge variance from one entry to the next. One thing this game does that Fire Emblem doesn't is adding in an in-game randomizer adding to the replayability. And while it may seem unfair to constantly compare this to Fire Emblem or maybe you don't know what that is, the game is just a solid tactics game that is worth picking up regardless. Two thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: The power scaling towards the later half seems to completely jump out of the blue. In one chapter I seem to be doing completely fine, and I was even really enjoying the characters and story. All of a sudden it felt as though all of the enemies pre-maturely classed up, and outscaled my characters. Chapter 19 specifically has no cover, requires all of your characters to escape from being completely surrounded, and nearly all of the enemies are extremely powerful with final tier classes.Looking back at how I played, I did squeeze a lot of exp out of the enemies they allowed me to, although many levels ended with turn limits instead of allowing you to farm the exp you so obviously needed. Even on chapter 18, you receive two new characters that start at level 26, which was a lot lower than where my other characters were at that point, and in the end of that same chapter, you receive a character that is level 30. I do not understand the choices that went into these last couple of chapters that I played, and I feel unable to play through a game that I was genuinely enjoying up until this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to give this game a good review, instead I'm giving it an "Meh" one. Why? Well, if you like the Fire Emblem series and the other games in the genre, you'll get about the same for the most part. But if you don't, then I suggest you avoid it.From a tactical standpoint - the battles are interesting at first, and then they're a bit repetitive and feel like they're purposely designed to have at least one annoying quirk. What's frustrating to a point is as your party grows, making the choice for the group composition is an endeavor of balance. You can never have enough ranged, melee and healers in the way you NEED to have them and down the line, some battles are going to tick you off with how you get railroaded.The artwork is okay, though one of the healers looks like a little girl. But the more pixelated look of fights was annoying on my 21:9 screens.The story is the story, I feel no attachment to it. The characters don't help it, I think I like maybe two of them so far the rest feel like they're as forced as can be. The artwork for them reminds me of some middling level anime; not bad, but not striking either.The spoken dialogue....some of it is decent - just don't expect A+ voice acting. But when you have A interacting with B, the one word comments that are to keep the written parts going is useless. I'm halfway through the game though and I'm leaning towards uninstalling it because of the flow of combat, the loading times (I have an I9 12900, Win 10 on an NVME, and 128GB of DDR5 and it's still SLLLOOOOWWW) and that I have no attachment to the story. Bottom line: Recommended only to fans of games like this, so that's why I hit the recommend it button -but I will say y'all got more patience than I do and I have a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently on chapter 4, and I enjoyed the first two chapters because it brought FE nostalgia from the GBA days. I really wanted to like this game, but little negatives things added up that made the experience more frustrating and less engaging. I can't really recommend this game because after a few chapters I already feel like I'm better off playing something else.The good:- Graphics are gorgeous. It's a modernized and updated version of what GBA FE would've been if they kept going. The sprites are well animated, and I had never any inclinations to turn them off. They provided a great amount of visual enjoyment whenever they played. The map sprites also look great.- The illustrations are also beautiful. Characters portraits have a great amount of detail.- The token system is very interesting. A straightforward but simple way of upgrading character weapons, once you get used to it and understand it.- Also no durability! No more pesky breaking of your favorite weapons.The bad:- Bare bone tutorial that is very lacking. You are provided such a small amount of information in this game. The meaning of stats when leveling up, weapon advantages (or what even triggers the match up), and even the backstories of your characters are never explained. So much critical information is never brought up in this game and I found myself having to look up why weapon advantages happened in a certain way. The token system above is also never explained. You're just expected to figure it out. So much of this game is just figuring out basic game mechanics that should've been included in a tutorial.- The story is so confusing. Characters appear on the screen with little explanation. Then the game plows through and expects you to make peace that some rando just joined. Most characters never have any depth to them. They're just eccentric strangers you have in your armies, at best. You're never given a reason to care for any one or why you should form a connection with the characters. - Quality of life is missing in a lot of places. Little things like being able to use stat-boosters outside of battle maps are noticeably missing.It looks and sounds like Fire Emblem, but it lacks the depth and polish of one. No permadeaths in this game, so do what you will with that. I haven't had a unit die yet, but it may mean that you could experiment with builds. It could also mean that you use everyone as cannon fodder while you only invest in a few characters you like.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh really the only good thing I can say about this game is that is made me rediscover the Fire Emblem Romhacking community. Seriously don't bother wasting money on this and try some of the stuff on FEUniverse instead.Lets talk about the maps. First off devs lied lol. Kickstarter claims to have "zero route maps!" Lamo guess what one of the very first ones end up being . You have incredibly boring, bland maps that are flat planes which encourage turtling and nothing else. Played on "normal." Any "time pressure" is pretty much entirely in your mind. The thing that broke me was a "prison escape" map that implied you should hurry since they'll be executed!!! Except...nothing happens on the map and if you take your sweet sweet time. oh sure game says that finishing faster gives you more gold, but I have zero feedback on what "fast" is or any difference on whetehr Turn 10 vs 13 clears actually help my wallet that much.The gameplay systems are needlessly overcomplicated too. What the ♥♥♥♥ is "Mastery" actually doing? The strength of FE is that the math is fairly simple and straightforward without stupid % stuff getting in the way. And dont get me even started on the stupidly intricate weapon type vs armor stuff. About as useless as weapon triangle while being 100 times more complicated and difficult to remember.And oh gods don't get me even started on the story and writing. You have the stupidiest excuse plot ever, a protagonist everyone treats as the next coming of Christ for no reason whatsoever (oh hello serious military man, you're just gonna verbally ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this guy because he's knows you have to fight enemies to beat them?) that is blander than a typical silent protag while somehow also being more morally reprehensible than Corrin durring FE Conquest. I actually didn't realize how awful this guy and the cast were until reading an analysis since the writing made my eyes glaze over that much

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I've played this game for 4 hours on what looks like normal difficulty. So,I'm probably qualified to talk about the game after 7 chapters.Even with upgraded weapons on early levels, you either have garbage accuracy or you do no damage. Literally once battle mages start appearing on the enemy team you're going to contemplate suicide because you're going to need 2-3 people to take them out. The only saving grace you have is that Bianca is op af.Map layouts are alright if not just kinda basic, but not terrible. The controls are really weird, like how sometimes when you click attack sometimes it will highlight a random enemy that's within range, and sometimes it won't. The problem with that is if you just want to check the damage or accuracy of your weapons, you might just click the one that's already highlighted causing you to confirm your attack, which isn't always helpful. Don't use a gamepad even if you're used to playing fire emblem. It is incredibly uncomfortable, so just use the mouse. Even though you can use asdw and the arrow keys to move the camera, only the arrow keys will let you select weapons which is really weird if you're right handed.You basically start with 4 weapons on each character, and you'll only have maybe 1 good weapon and if you're lucky a decent high damage slow weapon. I like that the side characters actually show up in cutscenes after you recruit them, something that most fire emblem games don't really do. Also, the animations are very reminiscent of the gba fire emblems, which are probably the most fun to watch. I would say the animations are not as good as the fire emblem gba game animations, but they're more enjoyable to watch than most of the other fire emblem battle animations. I'm done playing this game, but I don't think the game is terrible. I just know that I'd rather just replay old fire emblem games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is fine enough as a spiritual successor to Fire Emblem. Although it does not really stand out from the other Fire Emblem games, the difficulty in developing an RPG like this is commendable. That being said, the game was not released in a completed state. Knowing this, I held off on playing it for half a year. At the time of writing this, my current playthrough has seen two major patches with graphical overhauls and major balance changes. Had this game been marked as an early access title, I would not be writing this, but in light of this game being marketed as a completed product I would not recommend that most people play this until it is done receiving major patches.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Fire Emblem like game, with some interesting ideas of its own. Take's more inspiration from the older NA releases of Fire Emblem from the GBA than anything after Awakening.Combat system with many different types of attacks and armor types can be a bit to get used to, but its not too hard, especially given the nature of other strategy rpg mechanics. It ensures no one is able to face tank the entire stage, as something will actually hit with some damage, even trying to evade everything will eventually need to be careful, because plenty of enemies will actually match your speed.Plot is sort of decentralized from the 'main' character, with almost every character you use having plot relevance.Support conversations range from memey for characters that are clowns with each other, to learning quite a bit of the backstory and motivations of the characters. Overall, quite solid, though if you are expecting waifu sim, this is not that.The relic system can do some really funky things with stats and such. Invert crit chance for damage, turn magic stat into defenses, plenty of absolutely silly things that can happen.No side missions to grind, which means that you need to be somewhat mindful of who gets experience. I didn't have any particular issue with levelling, though I did have to sideline a few characters for later characters because the growths were not kind. But no character is pre-premote style bad, so everyone you find is at least supposed to be worth using.Game has great randomizer options, which are always really interesting with games like this.Given Fire Emblem games are not, and almost certainly never will be, available for PC, if you like them, this should be quite enjoyable. If I had one ask, it would be another set of tier 2/3 classes for each base, to help give just a bit of balancing out to each of the attack types. Bolt being exclusive to a tank mage, and an adept upgrade to try and all in magic is, rough, crush not existing on non-heavy armor units, another projectile option outside of ranger, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: To get this out of the way, even as a statement you've probably heard a lot of times already: If you like Fire Emblem, you will almost definitely like this game.This game has a decent chunk of problems, primarily the large amount of bugs and glitches. Some can be relatively minor, like audio playing at the wrong time, and others can lead to restarting entire chapters, like the combat forecast displaying the wrong damage, or being unable to select units in certain situations. While these bugs certainly do bring the game as a whole down quite a bit, it's also definitely not enough to where I wouldn't be able to recommend the game.Other than the bugs though, this game does have some noticeable issues. Characters lack development, the story can't really be called anything above decent, although enjoyable, some animations feel unfinished, and the UI feels like it isn't quite finished. In fact, I think that's a solid way of describing this game; It feels more like a game at the very end of it's early access cycle more so than it does a fully released game. My speculation was that this game was rushed out to ride the hype of E3, whether it was ready by then or not. The inconsistent gameplay systems, unfinished animations, and myriad of glitches lead me to believe this is simply an unfinished product.All of that being said, the majority of my major gripes with this game will eventually be solved with future updates, and as a whole, this game is a blast to play. I've played through a decent chunk of FE games, and I can say for certain that this game has some of the most fun maps to play through compared to any FE game, as well as the most fun animations and classes by far. Map design can be hit or miss for this game, but I'd say 70-80% of the maps are very fun to play through while others are poorly designed, and sometimes downright unfinished. At the end of the day though, getting through those underwhelming maps is 100% worth it for the fun you're going to be having for the rest of the game. I really can't overstate how fun this game is to play, how fun customization is, and how satisfying maps can feel to challenge and overcome.TL;DR: This game feels unfinished with lots of glitches and it leaves much be desired, such as the UI design, story, and character depth, but the gameplay, class system, and animations make it worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10 highly recommend for GBA Fire Emblem fans. needs improvements but highly fun game. If any devs is reading this please read at the end for some constructive criticism. I never really liked the 3D Fire Emblems animations that came after the GBA games, I always found the Gameboy advance games the best in the series the animation was awesome and full of color, their critical damage animation was something I always looked forward too.  while the 3D animation feels bland and lifeless. With that being said, this is what I love most about this game the animation is inspired by such games, however some of the animations are straight out copied from Fire Emblem: Sacred Stones like the Mage and Arcanist has the same animation minus the book. I sure hope they add new animations later on. One of the strongest suits of the game for me is the Armor and Damage system, it’s not like Fire Emblem were there were only 3 weapon types in a triangle where one weapon was strong vs one and weak Vs another here the system is more robust there are I think 9 Damage types, Cleaving, Pierce, Slash, Crush, Projectile, Fire, Holy, Storm and Arcane while armor types were Leather, Plate, Magical Cloak and Chainmail.... now some are weak Vs another and each class is very varied in Armor/Damage so you have to think very thoroughly how you will engage a target by taking those into account which require more thinking than Fire Emblem which I really, really like. For example, you may have a Defender class unit that has Plate armor and Damage type Slash, while his Attack is better against Leather armor, the armor is weak against magic so a Defender can deal lot of damage to a unit with leather but if the counter attack if Arcane it will also take a lot of damage…  now if it was enemy unit with leather and pierce its safe to say the Defender will mop the floor with this type of enemy, this is represented in game by letters from least effective to most effective F, E, D, C, B, A and S.Another strong point over Fire Emblem is that there are more promotions. Fire Emblem for example the Recruit class had two choices Knight or Cavalier then from there it would advance into advanced classes if you choose Knight then you could choose from General and Great Knight when you had a Seal to promote them. Now on Dark Deity each starter class has 4 promotions to choose from a level 10 and at level 30 another 4 for a total of 8 Unit per class, and you are not stuck into a linear promotion you could choose from. for example, Ranger can go to Archer Class then Sniper if you want a dedicated archer unit, but lets ay your Archer you want to promote into Green Knight which is an advanced class mounted anti-mage archer so you mixed one strength into the other weakness, your Ranger class heroes will never play the same neither since all of them have a unique skill that correspond to their character. For example, I found Elias to be a good Gale with a high critical weapon that supplements his unique critical skill he glasses canon that can kill units in two critical continuous strike or you can promote him into a Reverie so he becomes a tank unit. I heard as a thunder lord he pretty good too. Each class has also a special action Healer do Heal, Mages do Phase, Archer do Haste, Warrior do Push and Rogues to Disarm they are abilities that affect the battlefield. Push moves enemy units, Phase moves Friendly unit, Heal well pretty clear what it does, Haste makes a friendly unit move again I think, Disarm that can lower weapons abilities.Also one last point over Fire Emblem is that there is no Permadeath but Grave Injuries instead that when a character “dies” instead get injured and faces a permanent injury that lowers randomly one stat of that character… still annoying but I like it depending on the penalty Ill either keep fighting or restart the level.Now for the weak points that to me need improving. Number#1-The strongest aspect for me in the game is the 2D battle animations, however some of these animation are straight out copied from  the GBA version of Fire Emblem I know the Mage, and dragon rider animation are straight from the GBA version of Fire Emblem: Sacred Stones. I think they need to change them might get them in trouble. Another problem I had was that the Defender class and its upgrade class has the same animation… that was a big letdown for me since the promotions of the units for the battle animation is something I look forward too that the one I noticed IDK if there are others.Number#2- Linear story, I would like if they copied  Sacred stones and other similar games where there are some side quest were one can grind some of the unit’s that need leveling up with each level I can only choose so much and some units fall behind and there nothing I can do about it.Number #3- Lack of tutorial or in game encyclopedia, there lot of info on the game and there are tons of things I still don’t understand like the weapon choices yellow, Green, red and Blue, or the effect of weight or mastery to name a few.Number#4- Weapons animations, there are 4 weapons o choose from yet when one chooses it there no difference in the animation unlike the Mages were they have 4 different spells to choose from and they can keep upgrading them and they look different each time, I know it as lot of work  it even more frustrating there a weapon named Javelin yet it cannot be throw. Number #5- Level spacing promotions and promoting later- The leveling up to second classes too fast I can’t enjoy the class one animation, from 10 to 30 it feels like forever, maybe level class 15 then 30 this is more my personal taste. But one thing I really disliked as many other was that if a units leveled up and needed to be promoted it need to be promoted on the spot, literally putting me on the spot since now I wasn’t prepared for such a promotion and I need to promote randomly since I can’t compare my other units to see what need to be filled in my war party…. maybe one unit with Chain armor? Or maybe I need a unit with Fire attack damage? Or maybe I need a unit with Hack damage? I have started my game 3 times because I made a wrong choice early in game by choosing a class to a character that doesn’t quite feel right or I needed a spot to be filled just let me promote later on at the campsite. Since I can’t see the class advancement tree before I promote them I didn’t really know what to promote my future character too.

_childDocuments_.review: Just played through the game and this will be one of the few games I'll rate, just goes to show how much I liked it, it deserves to be discovered more, not sure how my review will help with that but who knows.Many draw obvious comparisons to the Fire Emblem series, while definitely inspired by it, calling this a FE clone would be a disservice. The only direct ideas used are the support system to deliver character lore in an engaging way and showing the battle results as an animated scene. I was not a backer of this project, but found this on my own, not sure if that allowed me to enjoy this game more, not having any expectations or promises for the game to live up to.Next I will list topics and elaborate on them, that were interesting in the game to me in my brainstormy random way:Weapon upgrading is it's own system entirely of having 4 different types of weapons trees with different stat focuses for each character, weapon stats also differing between weapon types. While certainly limiting compared to FE, not being able to carry and use magic, bows, swords, lances etc on one character, I think it adds to the challenge a bit, and solidifying each character a role, that you chose for it.The weapon triangle is expanded, though it's more of a weapon against armor triangle now, so that each weapon type is effective to two different types or armor and ineffective to the same amount too at varying degrees, which is interesting, albeit a bit confusing at first. Also much more logical, why was a weapon more effective against another weapon? You don't strike the enemy's weapon to deal damage, but the armor, so thematically this makes much more sense.Character classes are where the most drastic customization comes in, picking a different class can wildly change the way the character can be played. For example from picking up a mount, magic caster brandishing a mace and abandoning his spells or later on using both magic and melee weapons. This is where the most drastic customization happens.Eternal aspects, items that each character can have one equipped at a time, which can also change the way the character plays very drastically. Thinking of ways to use them and equipping them on characters was very enjoyable. The aspects range from swapping stats, draining all of one stat to boost others and more complicated buffs etc. For example, swapping defense and strength, draining all luck and distributing it to power, dodge and true speed (advanced stats, that are boosted by normal stats) or boosting counterattack damage by 25%. My favorite aspects were the ones which drained all the magic and gave 10 of both defenses, having made mage into a melee character who didn't need magic, making it a proper tank, or boosting dodge by the amount of strength, making a berserker also very hard to hit back.The sheer amount of characters is astonishing, and one should be able to easily find a favorite among them, being able to deploy 14 characters for most of the game, into battle at one time, and the game having twice as many characters. The art and pixel art of the characters is sublime, for the most part. I think I may have nightmares about the Sniper class' stretchy arms straight from The Incredibles.People seem to hate on the story, but I enjoyed it, it was unpredictable enough with enough exposition to the world and the powers at play for to make sense. It certainly felt like an adventure, with stakes at play.The game definitely has a lot of replay value, not being able to use basically more than half the roster each play through, needing to use characters in battle to unlock support conversations and then the modifiers and randomizers that you can use to customize your campaign. I came across a few bugs, being unable to target two enemies in one level, the game thinking they were presumably in a different spot. And the battle forecast sometimes showing different numbers than when the battle scene shows once you are locked in battles. But that was few and far between, so I did not lose my trust in the number, it did keep me on my toes from taking risks that would result in characters surviving with 1 hp should all go as planned though.The battlesave feature was added during my playthrough and is certainly a great feature to have, to avoid some frustration of RNG destroying you. Though this was not that big of an issue, as even if your characters were defeated, they'd only get gravely wounded, which would randomly decrease one of their stats. Though depending on which stat, it could be quite bad too.The game does lack a little bit of polish however, from UI, overall explaining of mechanics, and a visual way to see the weapon armor triangle, just remembering it isn't very viable in the current state, at least it shows when you hover/select an unit to which enemies the character's weapon is effective against. Trade and the in game support abilities were not very necessary, at least for me. Didn't help that I would only choose Trade by accident which would freeze the game for a few frames. The game also freezes when a chapter is beat, instead of gracefully declaring the battle was one and continuing, but that's quite minor.Difficulty can be a bit steep at times, due to the game not having any way to farm exp, once a chapter is clear, it's off to the next harder one. Partially to make up for this, the game gives you one/two new quite high lever characters every few chapters until you have the whole roster. Using these units is completely optional after you get them, and are not required to succeed in the game. Using them may help, but using and growing the units you like and want to use is still very viable. You may have to let your lower level characters to snatch some kills of low hp enemies, but isn't that the done thing in any game where you want to keep your characters all leveled up anyway. Having a way to farm exp would make the game a lot easier, if that's an issue, there is always a difficulty slider. Though, I am not sure if that can be changed once the game has started. I think the difficulty is fine, as the characters cannot permanently die, just get gravely wounded and retreat. Overall this is a solid recommendation from me to anyone that loves a good turn based character builder, with excellent customization, great characters and a good story. If you can put up with the occasional minor inconveniences and figuring a few things with the game offering minimal support, then you can't go wrong with this one.PS. This game was my go to as a "bit more casual turnbased unitbuilder experience" when I needed a break from FE, during my FE 3H hard mode playthrough, made me think a few times that "man I could just be playing Dark Deity right now" instead of this suffering.

_childDocuments_.review: While this is a positive review, it is sadly a hesitant one. Now, most of you want to know if it scratches the FE itch: It does. I'll make a quick pros and cons list:Pros:-The character art is amazing-Likeable characters(although more lore/story/side-story would be REALLY nice for most of them. -fun gameplay-varied classes-magic animations rock and most animations are very pretty-cool builds, not all of them viable but still fun.-there's apparently a post-game challenge mode, havent seen that yet, but its definitely a plus to be able to do(correct me if im mistaken)-decent balance and nice with an in-built randomizer(although you can't randomize your own characters classes)Cons:-Most maps look...not very pretty. Some do, I've encountered like two so far, out of like, 12? That one effed up clock where you recruit Cia and Elias still haunts me.-The bonds are INCREDIBLY short and do NOT flesh out characters as well as you would hope. Many side-characters just don't talk, like, ever again. And there's not even permadeath so what's the reason?-Janky story. Not bad, just a little bit of a blur and pretty typical from what I've seen so far. Even with potential twists, I'm not sure there would be a major payoff. The writing that DOES exist is pretty good and characters don't feel like they "blur" into each-other when talking.-all the physical weapons look the same. its only class-dependant, which is too bad, since all the magical classes have unique weapons for all tiers.-menus are a bit jarring, zoom out from battle is not very smooth.-little bit buggyAs you can see, while there are a lot of cons, not many of them are MAJOR, but it's enough to irritate you a little bit. dark deity delivers everything that it promised to deliver, however, it's execution was flawed, not damningly or majorly, though. It's still a good,fun and also pretty game. It's a fun experiece, but do note that it probably needs a bit of fine-tuning before fully being the best version of itself.
