_childDocuments_.review: Tl; dr: I can only recommend this game to fans and lovers of the series, who absolutely need a new Fire Emblem or strategy game. I recommend everyone else to wait until there are more patches or a decent sale. First of all, I would like to mention that I have supported Dark Deity via Kickstarter since the very beginning, and have followed the development with growing enthusiasm. The game is obviously a game by Fire Emblem fans for Fire Emblem fans ... A more or less tribute to the old FE GameBoy parts. The characters are colorful and different and the pixel designs are wonderful. All characters look unique and are well designed, but there's more to it than that. Everyone has their own conversations with each other, which they can have with each other during the breaks. However, they always have so many of them that you quickly loose the overview and thus at some point you lose the desire to follow all of them. Here one would have preferred to go back to the origins of inspiration in order to limit all conversations.Unfortunately, the game has many other problems as well.- The game does not have a tutorial or a classic weapon triangle. Instead, there are different types of armor, which are never really explained, which is why you only orientate yourself to red and green triangles from the start so that you know who has an advantage over whom. - Another problem is the amount of characters that you get at the beginning. You get so many new units that you often don't know whether you should use any of the previous characters or rather the new units with a much higher level and better base stats.- Due to the new "Gravewound" system, units no longer die, but instead they lose an stat value in a skill (depending on the opponent). The idea sounds good in theory, but the average growth rates are so high that at the end of the day it doesn't really make a difference and therefore doesn't matter. - The sheer number of loading screens is absurd, there are 4 of them before the first fight. - Unfortunately, the game is quite facet-free (most maps are empty and listless). - The story is confusing and jumps around more than a raver on speed. - There is no special terrain that can be tactically included, another reason to think further than to put a tank in the middle and block everything doesn`t exist.- Even on the "highest" level of difficulty you can play blind through the game and receive all achievements ... If not, some bug prevents you from doing it. But you have to admit that the developer has been working hard to fix bugs and blemishes (of which there are plenty). Still, it has to be said that everything seems like the game was only released to take advantage of the E3 hype. It would certainly have taken another 1-2 months in development to become what we had hoped for, a homage to the classics of our childhood.

_childDocuments_.review: So lets talk for a moment. I'm going to use Fire Emblem as my base for evaluation here. (A series that most tactical rpg players have played and is still ongoing Rip FF tactics.)First things first grid based tactics are involved, Bonds are included, weapon upgrades are included, and finally at the start of the game you have 3 options for difficulty. (I chose Hero because I have some experience)Basics out of the way lets see what I have found in my first hour of play. There is some semblance of a weapon circle (Red,Blue,Yellow,Green) Although I myself am unsure of how it applies, This is a bit confusing but easy to deal with if you look at the stats and damage while preparing for damage. This part is neither a pro or a con. A pro to the weapons is that they take the Gaiden/SoV approach where weapons do not break, to balance this out you upgrade weapons with tokens that are gained by level up and purchasable.An undecided factor I have for the weapons is that 4 chapters in I do feel a bit of a gap between my damage and the enemies. This I'm sure will scale but if you expect to go through the game upgradeless or without spending some gold you might struggle, but this feature makes sense to balance out not breaking any weapons.Overall The characters I have met are fun, the story is a bit slow but seems like it is trying to build the world up, I would recommend playing this game if you have a scratch for a tactical rpg, it shows that love was put into creation and the fights do have their own fun flair with swapping between 4 weapns.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, I enjoy the advanced tactical approach you can take in using certain weapon types against certain enemies for a better effect. Power, Finesse, Focus and Balance. Power is what is written on the Tin, high damage with little to no chance of critically hitting; effective for getting that good damage without risking much. Finesse is the critical hit king, this is the high risk high reward weapon, use this at your own risk of doing 8 or 20 damage. Focus is your high accuracy less damage poking tool, safe and easy for killing that enemy that keeps living against your mage with 1 hp and you just want him gone. Balance is the jack of all trades, middling damage accuracy and critical chance, usually you will use this if you want a good clean hit with the benefit of having a better chance of dodging the next incoming attack. Yes the weapon you use will make a difference in whether or not the enemies will hit you back, there is so much depth to this system it is insane. I'm not a game reviewer but I did pay the full price for the game and I can tell you now, it is definitely worth it for the depth alone, not even mentioning the story. Only downside to the story is the massive exposition dump at the start (it gets better, trust me.)

_childDocuments_.review: 10% Gameplay, 10% Fighting the Menu Boss, 80% Dialogue- The menu navigation in this game (on a controller) is just about the worst I've seen - Mouse is so-so.- The gameplay is alright, but very basic even compared to Warsong/Langrisser 1 which is 20+ years old at this point. - There's very little strategy above rock/paper/scissor. - The graphics are very jarring. Jumping from pixel to sharp anime sometimes both in the same scene. I get what they were going for but.. it's too much of a disparity.- Their "live broadcast" to hype the game is a pre-recorded loop. Very disingenuous.- The 'voiced' characters are actually little soundbite quips in between text dialogue... of which there is a LOT. Not a lot of words but a lot of short sentences flipping back and forth making the dialogue take 100x longer. Multiple characters on the screen lighting up and darkening.. it's very hard to smoothly follow the conversation.- The inventory and equipment system is simultaneously very basic and very cumbersome.- The leveling system is an insult to other titles that have done it better. Most of the options seem superfluous or actually worse. Seems more like filler than goal.- You're thrown characters so quickly you don't form any bond with them. Yet, the Bond system in the game expects you to care about hours of clicking through dialogue between multiple characters you know nothing about. There needs to be a hook for people to even want to go into the menu or know anything about who is who. It currently just feels like button you need to press because the game told you to.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this immediately after playing Fire Emblem: Engage because I wanted to keep scratching my srgp itch. Boy, oh boy, Dark Deity scratched my itch and more. It also has a better story than Fire Emblem: Engage, which is saying a lot, because the story is nothing special in Dark Deity. Shots fired.Dark Deity is not a polished game. There are bugs, things are janky, it's under-tutorialized, and I think some things are unnecessarily hidden from the player, but hot dog it's a good time once you wrap your head around the battle system by doing some reading.Characters and story are interesting enough, sprites and battle animations are absolutely beautiful (brings to mind the GBA Fire Emblems), and the combat is surprisingly complex. For srpg fans, for GBA Fire Emblem lovers, for people OK with a little jank, and for people OK with doing a little reading to figure things out, I highly recommend this game. I am very much looking forward to Dark Deity 2.

_childDocuments_.review: It really is similar to the older Fire Emblem games. This review is currently only based on the first 7 chapters with multiple play throughs of each (approx 8 hours of play) The graphics are a bit mixed, the character portraits are very nice, but the spirites are retro and a bit crude (it takes some practice to recognize your characters). The background of the battlefields are also retro, but better handled, nice details like tents, archery targets, etc.The combat is fairly simplistic, but not in a bad way. Each character can move, then attack or use their special command. The various classes have a damage type and range and a single command they can do (clerics heal, mages teleport allies, archers can boost allies movement, etc). The damage types each get a bonus and penalty against certain armour types, and each class has a specific armour type. The bonuses aren’t crazy (unlike fire emblem with its x3 damage), it’s in the 10-35% range, so it matters but not so much that a single attack from a slightly higher enemy is likely to kill you (although a couple might).Each character also has a special passive skill, so that two characters of the same class will play similarly, but not identical.They also have 4 weapons each a balanced one, a high damage one, a high crit one, and a high accuracy one. You get upgrade tokens as loot sometimes and you use those to improve your weapons separately, You can eventually upgrade all 4, but it makes more sense to focus on one or two. This means that you will have a high crit archer and a high damage archer for example.There are also restorative items, and the rare permanent stat boost items.Level ups result in random rolls of each stat and each either increases or not. The rates seem fairly good, so even though some levels are better than others it’s not as extreme as Fire Emblem (zero increases being common in many FE games). Although I felt pressured to repeatedly save and reload for “perfect” level ups in FE, I’m content to accept level ups in DD (at least so far).Upon reaching level 10 you automatically and instantly upgrade your character's class to one of four advances classes. These all have two new skills, might have a different attack range and type, and different armour type. In addition the rate of various ability parameters going up increases for some score and decreases for others. This can be enough to change the character's role significantly. A cleric (melee healer) can choose to upgrade to a heavily armoured healer, a healer who can heal at range and has magic attacks instead of melee, a healer who has a magic attack that drains life, or a mounter healer who applies a long-acting heal over time and has better mobility.There appears to be a third tier of classes (call them ultimate classes), they might be available at level 20, or perhaps a higher level. They appear to be independent of previous choice, but I can't be sure yet.

_childDocuments_.review: What if an indie developer took inspiration from great titles like Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics? You'd have Dark Deity! Scratches the SRPG itch deeply with a slew of features that will keep you coming back. You might be missing some of the polish that you see in the bigger SRPG franchise games but the core gameplay experience is rock solid and developers are engaged in quality of life updates. PROS:+ Faithful SRPG gameplay with unique spins on various systems that give the game its own flavor. There's a lot to say here from the weapon and armor system giving a sort of bi-directional rock-paper-scissors to grave wounds giving character defeats more impact, but the bottom line is there's plenty of crunch if you like that but the systems can be engaged with at a more basic level and still be satisfying+ Deep customization options for replayability, including enemy class/weapon and stat randomizers and several difficulty adjustment avenues+ Classic SRPG story elements with a bit of Final Fantasy flair+ An engaged developer committed to pushing quality of life updates and acting on player feedback+ Great sprite-work and character artCONS:- Still a few bugs to squish and QoL changes to be made, but they are being actively addressed- The map art style looks better in full screen than it does in some of the thumbnails but it still isn't quite for me- The plot may feel a bit breakneck or tropey depending on your experience, though personally I felt right at home as a long time JRPG fan Overall Dark Deity is a great pickup for the price, and even more so for turn based strategy and RPG diehards.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game mixed if steam allowed it.First, I find game interesting and I'm looking forward to what devs do with the sequel, but ...There is just something about about difficulty of this game that makes it unfun. Hero (medium) is too easy while Deity (hard) have enemy stats so bloated that game feel super reliant on hitting dodgy hit rates or enemies missing.Enemy damage is crazy, archers can oneshot your speed based units all through the game and physical tanks can't tank anything. Later on enemies get so hard to hit that maybe 3-4 of your units can land a hit with 50-60% hit rates. Low dex units (clerics, tank warriors etc) can barely hit any units.Enemies HP pools are huge, at the beginning it didn't bother me because I could focus threatening enemies and position to survive enemy phase ... it changes when enemies start to get dodgy, then you can't reliably plan anything. If enemy had 2 out of those 3 stats bloated: dmg/hit rate and dodge/hp then I would be fine, but 3 just doesn't feel fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Fire-Emblem-like, and if you like Fire Emblem, you may or may not like it.Most of Dark Deity's changes to FE's formula are convenience driven. Weapons don't have durability. Advancing in one support conversation doesn't lock you out of others. Death merely reduces your stats, rather than permanently removing a character.At the same time, you have an unprecedented level of strategic customization for your army. Every character has four potential upgrade paths. Every character also has four potential weapon types you can upgrade and switch between. Stat-boosting items are featured in the between-mission shop, as are weapon upgrade tokens, and both are expensive. With the right choices, you can make any character shine.Unfortunately, this is where my praise starts to stall out.Because there's less clunk to manage, Dark Deity's missions tend to be much more centralized around having strong characters. Even in early missions on normal difficulty, enemies hit HARD. You have lots of tools to try and mitigate this, but at the end of the day you'll still reset a lot. Losing stat points is better than losing characters---but losing stat points might as well mean losing characters when you need every possible stat point to stay competitive.At the same time, the writing is only okay. There are some nice flourishes, and the overall tone and style are fine, but I didn't feel pulled in. I think this is because the setting is just...sort of standard fantasy. There's some nice politicking, and there's a ferret named Butters that steals every scene it's in, but otherwise the world is a little flat.Ultimately, Dark Deity feels good when you're making good choices and tanking waves of scarily high damage enemies with a few overtuned units. If that's something you like, you should get this game.If you play FE more for the plot than the combat mechanics, you may want to wait to try this on sale.Overall, I've been enjoying it, and I'm definitely curious to check out other games from the developer.Edit: In the temple in chapter 14, one of the chests is bugged and gives infinite Jars Of Milk. These are a +2 DEF item. So if you can hold out until chapter 14, you can make a few units that can keep up with the game's wild attack pacing.2nd Edit: I'd thought it was just my potato computer, but it turns out the loading screens are bad even on a modern rig. So, a second caveat for this game: the loading screens are like 4 minutes each. No idea why. There shouldn't be anything graphically intensive or mechanically complicated that's being loaded.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of GBA-era Fire Emblem, this game will scratch that itch. At the time of writing I'm still early in the game, but I'm loving it so far. While it follows the tried-and-true tactical RPG formula, it has streamlined several of the systems that you may be used to, including inventory and weapons. I've spent far too much of my life fiddling with inventory, so, for me, it was a welcome change. Overall, if you're a fan of the genre, you know what you're getting into and the gameplay is going to feel like you expect it to.As for looks, it's a bit hit and miss. The character portraits are all beautifully drawn, but the some of the sprites aren't quite doing it for me, and the over-world map is a little muddy for my taste (an extreme quibble on my part). That said, I think Dark Deity's visuals capture the spirit of those old Fire Emblem games, and it feels incredibly nostalgic to see a game like this being made today.Can't comment much on the game's writing and story yet, but it's getting more fun as it goes. The support dialogue between characters has been a treat so far, and should always be a strength in this sort of game. So far, so good.

_childDocuments_.review: Having plenty of fun with this. Got it very cheap in a bundle, and for that it's been well worth it.The gameplay is good, though there's a little bit of UI polish needed. Just little things like how to choose a different target, you have to both highlight them and press A - why isn't highlighting them enough? Another is that it does save during battle, but this can only be resumed by a small button in the bottom right of the "Load" menu without a timestamp. The art is always super, so a shame the UI isn't to the same level.The levels are punchy and fun, and map design is varied and pretty good - sometimes letting you have a big force, other times splitting your team, etc. This is one of the most important parts of a tactics game, and here they're on par with Fire Emblem, and leagues ahead of Wargroove and some other indies.I really like some changes from Fire Emblem, in particular how all characters have 4 choices of weapon/move to give different risk-reward choices on many individual attacks. Sometimes you'll choose a lower damage move for a guaranteed hit, or a risky crit in the hopes of finishing an enemy one turn quicker. These weapons don't degrade, and generally stop things getting too routine.The writing is good! An interesting story around troops dealing with the king making foolish decisions, with a few jokes but nothing that breaks suspension of disbelief.There's slightly too many characters. I have to spend effort remembering who came from where and grew up with whom, or else just skip the character bonds entirely. Luckily they're optional with no mechanical impact. It also means that inevitably some characters can't follow you into battle, which makes less sense in a game without permadeath. In general, it might have been better if they edited it down to 15 characters instead of 30. Frequently, the newest joiners will be as high or higher than your top levelled fighter, so inevitably you leave characters you care about on the bench in the name of better stats. Also, levelling seems truly randomised, meaning that sometimes a character just doesn't get the Dex to hit things accurately... and if they die in combat and take a -2 Dex permanently, they're going to stay benched. I think I'd rather they died - for the drama!I'm not sure I'll finish this game to 30 hours, but I've had at least 10 very fun ones being sucked into this story and combat. Some smaller issues, but honestly still a standout effort for an indie tactics game.

_childDocuments_.review: A good, simple, fun tactics rpg with no frills.I'm not a fan of the story, it's all a bit silly and there are plenty of pop culture references and the like that keep you from getting invested, but the characters are pretty charming in their design and simple personalities. The roster keeps increasing, often giving you a new character (or multiple) every map up to the final few battles of the game. Good variance of classes and unique abilities for each unit as well.The penalty for a character getting knocked out during a map is a small decrease to a seemingly random stat, which is an interesting feature that doesn't force a reset upon losing a single character, causing some interesting choices and encouraging riskier plays. I'm playing through on the hard difficulty, which I find challenging but not frustrating or unfair. I imagine the normal and easy difficulties are appropriate for newer players or people looking for a less difficult experience. I like the music as well, and never ended up muting the game and playing my own music or a podcast as I normally do.The only real negative I can think of are the multitude of bugs. I've only encountered a few minor bugs, such as characters getting stuck on walls and shaking back and forth violently until being placed on a nearby tile on a subsequent turn. Though from the other reviews I can see bugs are a big concern, including some of the game breaking variety.It appears that the devs are making fixes on a semi-regular basis, and putting out DLC as well, so I can only imagine the game with improve in quality and substance over time. Overall, I have no problem recommending Dark Deity!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I have now beaten the game. I will say the tier 3 classes fix some of my issues below about combat. Also, map design / boss encounters in the last five chapters are actually fairly fresh takes that were a joy to play. Seeing these made me see the potential for the entire game, but having to go through 22-23 chapters (the majority of the game) to get there, was rough. I was very much looking forward to the game and I should say, for a first attempt it's ok. However, this game feels exceedingly unfinished, as though it was rushed to release at E3. 1st, you have no time at all to get invested in the world before you're expected to learn more of characters through supports (bonds), I don't know anything about the kingdoms or this world, how they interact, anything beyond what the between chapter scenes tell me. To give an example look to Path of Radiance, you have something like 6-8 chapters before the game even lets you support your characters because it's making sure you know enough about the world to understand the characters. By then you know that a laguz that says human or a beorc that says sub-humans are racist or at least ignorant. Focusing on that understanding of the world lets the player pick up on subtely of conversation. Dark Deity doesn't even bother. The only other issue with bonds is that it's completely unclear as to how many supports are allowed per character from the start (you can figure this out through play though). This is by far my biggest issue with the game. 2nd, my second biggest issue with the game is every chapter having a time limit. This isn't strictly true, but a large majority have a time limit restricting them. Those that don't overly-incentivize fast play by reducing chapter rewards based on turn count. Even chapters with non-time limit conditions often have some odd condition that either is a time limit in essence or is so awkward that you forget about it and trigger the condition out of nowhere. 3rd, UX/UI experience is fairly bad. A splash loading screen between every transition seems completely unnecessary for a game of this visual quality (which don't get me wrong I enjoy the visuals). In addition, playing on mouse and keyboard is a fairly odd experience, I can't count on both hands the number of times I've done an unintended action when I was attempting to do another. Edit on UX/UI: Not being able to save mid-chapter (at least not that I've noticed), is a poor choice, you might lock your own players into an hour long fight where they can't save their progress if they need to go somewhere. If you save at the start of a chapter after making your battle preps, the game should save after you've made the preps not always load you to before. Also, every chapter you are given your top X (depending on chapter deployment allowance) units in level, even though you don't necessarily want to use those higher level units, basically by halfway through the game you'd only have characters you got introduced in the last three chapters in your party. The game should try to remember your most used if it's going to try and force any units on deployment.4th, while I don't mind too much, combat balance is pretty much non-existent. If you stumble into the classes that are broken you'll have an easy time, and if you pick the wrong ones, you'll ruin a character for the rest of your run. Before I continue on combat, a disclosure, I personally stopped playing at Chapter 9 so maybe these issues get alleviated later. Giving your non-magic units no access to 1-2 range weapons makes them awful in an enemy phase heavy game. In addition, I ran into 1 (seemingly?) non-magic unit the enemy had access to that I didn't (the trickster). I stopped playing because the enemy had flying units that I had no ability to access by that point in the game without heavily over investing in 2-3 units instead of trying to maintain a decent size team (around 11 units). This wasn't the first time it happened, but it was the most eggregious due to those flying units being on terrain I couldn't access. Edit on balance: Having nearly every archer in later chapters capable of one/two shotting any member of your party from full health (sometimes without a crit) is an absolutely awful balance decision especially considering the large number of them in some chapters. In addition, for some melee units 1-2 range is available by going into certain classes, but only the highest tier of class. 5th, there is a complete lack of clarity of information in the game. Should I spend my money on weapon upgrade tokens? Or stat boosters? Could you invest in a weapon to its highest level and it turn out awful? While I'm extremely familiar with the genre and could get around, if you're new to it, don't even bother with Dark Deity. 6th, unfortunately the UX/UI, balance, and clarity issues I've seen done better in some less wholesome FE-esque games of around the same visual quality. SS for example. I'll probably pick the game back up later on to finish and update this review, but for now it has left a bad taste in my mouth.A few spoilers below to help you if you've read this and decide to keep going with the game./spoiler 1st, make sure you don't put any magic possible units into melee, you'll be limiting their ability greatly. 2nd, there don't seem to be any doors or chests that require something like a thief to open, so don't put those units into the thief class it's near useless compared to the alternatives. 3rd, the enemy in the game as mainly learned the lesson to keep the units magic so all of your army needs to be able to resist magic pretty much all of the time. 4th chapter 19 is probably the worst designed map I've ever seen in any fire emblem esque game including fan mods /spoiler

_childDocuments_.review: Game is decent but I wouldn't recommend it.  Feels like a poor man's attempt at making a Fire Emblem clone.  Game makers clearly missed on a lot of game design concepts.  They leaned in heavily into luck too.  So expect to see units faint from bad luck rolls every now and again.  Balance is really poor here, Some classes/ class sub types are insanely good and others are trash. The best tank you'll have is a thief because dodge tanks are far superior to any armor/magic armor since tanks only get 1 of those but dodge ultimately protects you from both.  Level design needs a LOT of work.  They tried to make levels interesting by putting you in different situations. Some with lots of chokes, some levels that are open.  That shows some overall good choices from developers, a shame they chose to use way too many choke based levels which are just a huge slog to go through since you can only ever make 1 or two attacks a turn. Unfortunately the AI stupidity kills any level layout plans and need for real strategy.  99% of enemies are stationary until a unit of yours enters attack range, and then the pod of units wakes up and attacks.  Enemies also almost always attack weak/low health units as first priority,  then seemingly the unit they will do the most damage to regardless of hit chance.  Honestly completely random would be better then the current setup.  The good is the artwork of the character overall designs.  Characters look good, fun, varied, and interesting.  Props to the artist there.  The bad art is the sprites.  I don't think they are very good.  Animations are nice and special effects for attacks are cool. But the overall design and look of the PEOPLE sprites leaves me really wanting more.  Story exists.  It's pretty cookie-cutter fantasy DnD/generic fantasy story plot.  Rag tag group finds an evil plot and has to stop it.  Dialogue is solid overall.  Is it great, no. But there are certainly worse offenders out there.  It's a bit too talky with uselessness but props to the team to at least try and give characters depth and personality which is something few games with so many characters try to do.  The stories you learn from bonding characters shows a lot of effort from the devs, a shame they didn't put that effort into game play design and mechanics.As a total experience this game feels lacking.  Worth it on extreme discount but certainly not worth the full price. Too many levels feel like a slog to get through.  With so little strategy needed all your main failures or 'mistakes' are just luck based.  A crit here, a few missed attacks there will be the only things that make you rethink the plan, and even then the plan is the same, bum rush your way to the objective.

_childDocuments_.review: Things I like a lot about the game:Elias is Ryu from Street Fighter as Blaze class using Fire Dart can critical into a blue Hadouken!Main characters are not over powered causing difficulty even in normal play. Their clear weaknesses are low accuracy vs rogue classes requiring the use of more accurate weapons, and low force causing death from magic.Players can choose any class advancement they want for a character despite it being not efficient. For example buff Battlemage class for childlike Alden or Plate Armored Guardian Maren. (I did not do this yet, but the thought makes this game exciting!)Needed quality of life changes to Dark Deity to make it even better!Create a status called "Most Used Weapon" or highlight the most used weapon, so new players know what weapon to upgrade because there is various weapons and various characters that causes decision paralysis. For example I get decision paralysis from choosing class change. I want to min max stats and it feels like I am taking a test. My way around it was to make the characters look like their picture to calm my minor OCD always pick the best option. A highlighted weapon would make me use up my 40 saved tokens, so I get through the game faster. Please lower the level requirement of class changes because players fight higher class enemies that are lower level than the characters and that they are using. I do know my suggestion causes exponential power creep, but this incongruency is unsettling even if it does drive up hype to get to higher levels. When I got to level 20 I was disappointed that double the first class change level 10 was not enough to change again. I do know I have a problem leveling everyone equally, that's how I played Pokemon. (Tip to new players majority of classes have utility skills to get to higher levels without the risk of fighting.)Story Transition in from Chapter 11 to 12 was slightly confusing. I do not want to spoil it, but other players will know what I mean.Minor needed changes:Conjurer should have Chain Armor to resist FireAcolyte should have Rune Cloak Armor to have weakness to Holy.Priest should have Leather to be resistant to Holy.Crusader and Paladin should not be vulnerable to Holy (do not get me wrong I like the plate armor) unless this is was intended for the enemy. Should just make special rule all undead, and evil vulnerable to holy damage.Give lighting have higher accuracy vs Remove bug where your unit becomes untargetable by your left click because the code misplaced the pixels. _childDocuments_.review: Its trying to be like classic FE games, but completely streamlines most of the mechanics, stripping away the tactical depth that makes those games interesting and fun.For example, there is no inventory management aside from healing items and buff items. Each character automatically carries 4 weapons of only one type that they always have access to and never break. Red/power, blue/criticals, green/accuracy, and yellow/speed. So combat is less about preparation and equipping the right units with the right items, and more like a puzzle that solves itself. You can just scroll through each weapon as you're deciding which one to use on that particular enemy and look at the stats. There will always be an objectively right answer. For example, if the yellow one is the only one that lets you attack twice, you will usually pick that if the damage adds up to more when multiplied by 2. If the blue, green, and yellow ones have two attacks, and your hit is close to 100% on all three, just use the blue one. Its not challenging while also being tedious. They should have had units able to equip multiple weapon types (and set up weapon ranks) with things like "spears counter horses, swords counter infantry" etc. That would have actually been tactical, instead of just juggling random numbers. This also makes the weapon upgrade system very frustrating. You just get "tokens" that you can spend to upgrade each character's weapon colors individually. This even carries through each of their class upgrades in case the weapons change. But this just further makes everything feel streamlined and generic. Also, it makes it very hard to pick which color to upgrade. You kind of need all 4 colors to be upgraded, since the best one is really going to depend on the situation. And then on top of this, the weapon triangle is very confusing. You have an "advantage" or "disadvantage" system that seems to be somewhat loosely based on armor type vs. weapon damage type instead of the classic swords > axes > lances > swords system. I was never able to figure this out through and it always just seemed kind of random which units were bad or good against others. Sometimes advantage or disadvantage would matter a lot, or sometimes it wouldn't matter at all. There is an in-game manual, but it explains this aspect rather poorly.The mission design is very boring. Most fights are open arenas with very few terrain features where the objective is just "kill all". It makes fights turn into mindless, slow slugfest where the best strategy is to deathball all your units into a pile to protect the squishes and then proceed methodically. Healers get infinite uses as well, so there really is no reason not to play slow and boring, especially when the enemy outnumbers you 5 to 1 and will easily pick off your weakest characters immediately, giving them permanent injuries that reduce their stats. And don't forget the UI. Its clunky. Most things are based on mouse but then randomly some will be keyboard. For example, the weapon scroll. You have to use the arrow keys, even though everything else about attacking requires using the mouse to click. Because of this, combined with the fact the game doesn't have a tutorial, I didn't even know there were different weapon colors until a few missions in. Lastly, the story is pretty bad. You get recruited to fight a war, but spend a bunch of time goofing around fighting bandits and rebels. Some wizard shows up looking for an "aspect" and then disappears. Is this explained? No. Now back to fighting a war. There is no sense of pacing and getting the player used to the characters. Which are also pretty dull. Their main dialogue is mostly juvenile and expository. There are supports, but they're all things like "What's up, oh you like beans? Cool. Bye." For a game that focuses so much on the visual novel aspect (even to the point of having beautiful portraits of characters) this is an odd choice. Skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I want so badly to give this game a good review. It had beautiful animations, a decent story, interesting and diverse characters, and a nice variety in classes. That wouldn't be too bad except there is no way to grind levels so you are stuck with whatever experience you can glean from the maps. A huge improvement to this game would be the ability to replay maps so you could evenly strengthen all of your soldiers. Really, the only way to succeed is to dump all our your time and effort into just a handful of characters. I really want to be able to grind experience and money. I get that maybe this was a deliberate  choice by the devs, but I think it is a bad one. It lowers the play time since you can only do each level once, and contributes to the issues I have already mentioned. I am going to put playing this on hold until replaying maps is available. If it doesn't happen then I won't be playing any further. It just stopped being fun.

_childDocuments_.review: (A precursor to the full review- after the 1.5 update)I wanted to try the game again after the major 1.5 update to see how it is, but after playing through it again, I can't say it's any better. Things are still very unbalanced and buggy. The enemy range indicator is still often wrong and buggy. I had a character on the river map get stuck and not be able to move for the rest of the map. They said they changed it so the sniper is supposed to be able to attack from 3 range without being countered- but it isn't actually changed, they still get countered at 3 range. On the protect the ship map- I've played that numerous times and I still have no idea how the ship damage works (I think it might be bugged?). Chapter 18 randomly has insanely dodgy enemies. Classes will never be very balanced when the 1-2 range is inherit in the class, 1-2 range will always be better; especially with the self-healing classes. Having no stat caps and stat boosters always be available to buy is practically begging you to make god-like characters. Imagine fighting Ashnard in Fire Emblem PoR and he has a 1% chance of hitting you. That's how it is in this game, the bosses are pathetically easy and it is still really easy to make unhittable dodge tanks. Chapters are also very short, you can easily beat the game in 8-10 hours without even trying to speed run or LTC (skipping the boring story). There really isn't much strategy in this game at all! So yeah, I don't recommend getting this game. Since it was just announced that Vestaria Saga Gaiden: The Sacred Sword of Silvanister is coming out in 2022, I again recommend checking out Vestaria Saga I: War of the Scions- its a much better game then this one and its cheaper! If you want a more in-depth review of Dark Deity- read the review below.(Edited- After I beat the game a second time on Deity Difficulty.)I found Dark Deity to be a somewhat fun but flawed game- and I would only recommend it under certain circumstances. I am a big Fire Emblem fan and had been eagerly following the development of this game for a while. First, I will quickly mention a few of the positives. The character art, other background image art, some of the characters, combat animations and the Fire Emblem-like experience the game provided were all pretty good. However, there were a lot of flaws and things I didn't like about the game. First of all, the story is pretty meh. It starts with potential but seems to meander-things happen kind of randomly, there isn't really enough backstory, most things aren't explained well and instead of your team being a part of the world - the whole world seems to revolve around them. The world also seems very empty and boring. They are very much reactionary rather than proactive. I think the game would have benefited from having more dialogue/explanations between stages and an info menu that gave additional (but optional) information (like the Tellius FE games). I also didn't like the weapon system. It is pretty tedious- and not in a good way. Upgrading the different weapons is also a pain. In addition, this weapon system really locks you into using only characters that you can afford to upgrade. It's hard to drop someone that you've upgraded a lot and start using someone else instead. I would have preferred a more traditional FE weapon system (with or without weapon usage). It seemed like the developers changed the weapon system just to differentiate the game from Fire Emblem- which would be fine except I think it is much worse. In relation to stats, having no crit avoid in the game leads to very high occurrences of crits. In addition, having no stat caps means you can make 1 or 2 godly characters that can easily carry through the entire game (even on Deity mode).Character recruitment is weird. Every new character you get is almost always a higher level than everyone else you have, which makes it very difficult to use a lot of the early characters. If you try to use a majority of the early cast, too many will fall behind. This encourages you to just always use the new characters. (Especially since EXP can be fairly limited). Bonds were interesting to read but I wish they had some kind of benefit-bonus. After reading them once- there isn’t any incentive to read them again.One MAJOR problem I encountered was that classes are not balanced very well. Some classes are just way better than others. The good classes can trivialize the game and the bad classes make it really difficult. Each tree seems to have at least some good/useable classes but also many poor ones. The ranger tree is also the only tree to have no class with any 1-2 range. In almost every instance, classes that are 1 range locked are less useful than the 1-2 range classes. (Also for Snipers- 3 range skill- It seems weird that other ranged units can counter.)Another problem I found were with the glass cannon classes. Archer classes that use the power weapon have very high power and accuracy (and some mages fall in this category). In some stages of the game, I found it difficult to deal with these in large groups. The AI doesn't worry about keeping soldiers alive and can throw these at you with little regard. My best dodgers would still get hit often (for high damage) and high defense units would get doubled and still take massive damage because their power was so high. It feels like a bit of a balance issue as most other units are hardly any trouble at all. The Aspects (items with some kind of modifier/bonus) are also unbalanced- some give insane bonuses and others are very underwhelming. I also found that bosses generally were very easy. Basically what differentiated them as bosses was having an extremely large health pool. On some maps, the units guarding the boss were much more difficult enemies than the bosses themselves. Another problem were the maps. Too many of the maps seemed to be large wide open spaces. It makes it difficult to use different strategies and certain classes. It also makes many chapters seem bland and many of the maps just blur together. No terrain, forts or other things makes them feel lacking. No map combat animations is also disappointing. I think the game has an okay playtime- but 28 chapters can be a bit misleading because many chapters are very short. Another thing I felt was weird were random difficulty spikes. I played through the game on Hero (and then on Deity) difficulty, most stages were pretty easy- but for some reason there would be a random stage here and there that was way more difficult. Having a more consistent difficulty curve would make it more fun.I also encountered more bugs the second time through. The enemy range indicator doesn’t refresh (which is annoying) and often displays it wrong when there is water. I also had an enemy who I couldn’t target, and could move on top of- only for him to run through my troops and kill someone I had in the back line. I also found some typos in the bond conversations.The steam recommendation system is pretty basic- yes or no. I went with a "no" but in some cases I think it might be worth it. If you have any Nintendo Systems- I would recommend any and all FE games above this. I also think Vestaria Saga (available on Steam) is a much better game (it's also cheaper). If you have played all the FE games to death (I'd say I have)- then I think this game could be a fun experience to play through- Though I would definitely wait for a sale). I'm a little disappointed with having bought this game at launch (I bought at $20 when it came out), and I would have felt better buying it at $10 or under. I think it is too flawed to recommend buying at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Deity is filled with game-breaking glitches such as my cursor not showing up and me not being able to move or have my units attack enemies. A minor complaint is not being able to choose between classic and casual mode. Instead of when your unit dies, it isn't gone forever or comes back, but its stats are weakened. This does not support the player to get better but to take shortcuts and to kill off their units all willy nilly. At least with casual mode, it made it easier for newer players to get into FE but still allowed them to play on harder difficulties. Which has none of the benefits of either choice which you got from the FE games. Another complaint is the lazy map design found in throughout the game but especially in chapter 19. It's literally a fricking square with lines of enemies lined up on each side. I could make this design myself in Microsoft Paint. The lazy map design and the game-breaking glitches are that the game was rushed to release around E3 2021. I played through all FE 3H and most FE Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light. This game should have taken some ideas from three houses, such as the five divine pulses and bookmarking levels. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game as a long time fan of the Fire Emblem series, but its riddled with bugs and extremely poor UI and UX. I will say I love the art and the gameplay itself is quite good, but small things such as - doubles not appearing in the combat screen on the damage display, - numbers not always adding up when getting hit by weapons that strike multiple times per attack, - choppy transitions from combat, attack previews not updating on hover but rather on press (which can lead to an accidental attack), - music playing over music (during the new phase notifications, it should really be sound effects because of the layering), - not being able to preview inventories when deciding who to trade with in the base, - and questionable pathfinding algorithms for when you go right into an attack instead of moving into one, only placing you at the top or bottom of the enemy character if possible, when it should be placing you at the nearest possible point.It makes it much harder to enjoy. These things don't actually break the game but its the little things that would make this game appear polished, but in this case the lack thereof makes the game feel very clunky, and incomplete. I have also experienced a bug where using the R button to switch to my next available character, it selected them and didn't let me deselect, or move, meaning I had to throw away a chapter 20-30 minutes in because of a bug, simply unacceptable for a bug like this to exist. I don't think I can comment much on the story, as with only 3 hours playtime at the time of writing, I have a lot to unfold. But I'm afraid it is going to be lacklustre at best, that is, if the game will allow me to keep progressing through it.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like in this game. If you're a classic Fire Emblem fan it's definitely worth picking up. There's a robust and interesting class and weapon system that keeps things strategic and interesting.However, while I do recommend the game that comes with a lot of caveats. It's VERY rough. I've run into a lot of bugs, a couple of which have forced me to restart chapters. Controller support is iffy - it works but it's finnicky to get it to do what you want. The animations and character sprites are for the most part very nice, but there are still bugs with them (for instance using certain magic in melee range doesn't shift the spell animation over) and there is very little if any difference between male and female sprites resulting in most characters having the same kind of bulky unappealing build. The character art is passable but not professional quality, and the writing/story is extremely long-winded, convoluted and yet full of predictable cliches that make it feel like a fan project. The Bond conversations in particular are VERY long and while they occasionally say something important about the lore, could easily be trimmed down without losing anything.All that said, I do like the game and for what it's worth I've been having fun with it. It's worth picking up if you like the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Fire Emblem-esq GameTLDR (1-5) Story ☯ 4Music ♬ 3Gameplay ⚔ 4Difficulty ☠ 5Bugs § 4Game time / Length ۞ 4Price $ 5The Review:If you have played Fire Emblem, you will instantly feel welcomed into this game. Dark Deity is easy to pick up, and easy to play casual. A full run is 25 - 30 hours of the game. Its story is engaging, and there is a decent sound track to bop along too as you vanquish enemy of enemy. The variety of abilities, weapons, and classes is great. The accessibility of the various weapon traits is something I loved about the game. Every class has the ability to hold 'in a sense' four weapons at once, each with their own characteristics.The game has no side quests. No optional 'level grinding' maps. So if you run into a hard encounter that you have to repeat several times, there is no option to power up before retrying. Having said that, unlike FE games a death has a penalty to one of your stats instead of the character dying outright. I did find there was a lack of 'hover descriptions' in some of the windows. When selecting new abilities having a hover explanation of the Stat would've been very helpful.There is a lot of replay-ability here as you can adjust the game rules to your liking at the 'new game' menu, and it can create some very funky outcomes, ranging from tragic to godlike. I couldn't play an entire run on a random stat new game as It was game breaking... in a fun way though.Overall, it's a great game for a great price, and am very excited to see what the creators do with the announcement of Dark Deity 2 coming in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of games such as Fire Emblem, Final Fantasy Tactics, Tactics Ogre, etc. I already knew this was going to be a good game. I backed it when it was in its Kickstarter days and it does not disappoint. The combat is nice and fluid, having four different weapons to choose from for each character gives many options on how to kill enemies efficiently. Do you need raw damage? Use red weapons. Want to make sure you hit the enemy? Use green weapons? Do you want a balance of both? Use a yellow weapon. And then there's blue, which give higher crit chances.Besides that the character's art both sprite-wise and portraits are fantastically made, and from the bond conversations I have gotten so far as of beating chapter 4 I can tell that these characters have good chemistry together. While I haven't gotten to class changing any one unit yet, the idea of having four options without the limit of a branching tree forcing only two is great. If you didn't like your choice for the 2nd class, you can choose one of the other three options for the 3rd tier class, you aren't stuck with it. The story so far has been standard, but I can already see that things aren't as clear as they seem to be. I do wish that the introductory portion had a bit more worldbuilding as far as the various countries go, as it really only at first focuses on the two countries at war. Also, for the two maps so far with a time limit, I would have preferred if the bosses were mobile at the tail end of the chapter instead of just being stationary. It doesn't give them much impact as bosses if they can easily be ignored because of time constraints on the player. Another thing that I think would help is maybe letting stat-boosters be used during the preparations, unless I've somehow missed how to do that I would have to wait until a chapter began to use it.All in all, I would recommend this game to anyone who loves a good tactical game with a nice story and neat mechanics. Since it was released today I'm sure more reviews will be coming in here about the game. The developers actively encourage you to leave reviews and are very open to public opinion. Let them know how they've done and I'm sure the game can become better than it already is, Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: Dark deity is a fantastic nostalgic game that is worth the price and time  to go through ! The art and characters are great and the interactions are very entertaining and the motley crew of characters that this game brings together is great ! The game play is memorable to anyone who has played a tactical rpg and the classes - promote system is a great idea however my main cache about this game is balance.There are some serious balance issues and sure there are MANY ways to play but FEW ways to win. Balance IssuesThe game has several characters you can choose from however often times those characters and classes are replaced by characters with superior level and stats. usually if you are lucky you can hold onto about 3 characters from the first half of the game if you keep them fighting and scoring kills to gain XP. Late game the 3 level gap is insane and if you bring any NON armored / high defense character its a liability to get one shot or killed within 2 fights. This game  needs replayable scenarios where you can get underleveled or underpowered characters up to snuff otherwise half your roster will be sitting on the sidelines as the gap goes from being able to bring characters in who are 5 levels below to if they are 3 or 2 dont even bother. Stat boosters5000!? gold for a measly +2 for a stat? i don't think so, maybe 500 to purchase could be reasoned with but 9/10 times i sell statboosters when I pick them up, you can arm your team with so much with that 5000 gold. More special commands/ BuffsAnother thing that would support the game would be buff commands and more support abilities. Certain very bad level designs  Some levels are very small with very few points to move through ( choke points) you can litteraly park a tank with food and a ranged dps behind him and they will sweep everything hoarding all the XP where tons of characters need. level 18 is also a nightmare where you get a new ally and you are forced to pick battle mage because its sheer luck that the NPCS outside the first two who are suppossed to attack you swarm you and kill you before your team can reach said player.RIGHT WEAPON / RIGHT CLASS / WRONG LEVELIt is very annoying when you invest in characters and give them very high gear and that gear gets trumped by raw level advantage.  The game also punishes death by permanant stat reductions and if you are lucky it will get rid of something you dont need but try taking 9 hp from a tank or 4 str from a dps. If those characters are already behind you are double screwed and you will have to restart to try to preserve themanyway thats the most glaring of the balance issues , I know I focused on them a lot but it comes from a place of love and serious desire to see these developers and their game get better and be sucsessful ! good luck on the switch port ! I hope nintendo fans will get to enjoy this game as much as I did !
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game as an homage to Fire Emblem. There is definitely fun in the emergent gameplay of combining synergistic abilities from promotion as well as Aspects (equipment) that can be quite powerful when in the right hands, and the writing and style is pretty decent. They gave almost all the characters really good growth rates that can be altered by class choice to shore up weaknesses so you can use almost anyone if you like, though it's often easier to use later units as they will be autolevelled with their class growths to a higher level than your current units. EXP gain is very generous though so it's easy to baby anyone you want to use. Instead of permadeath you have stat loss on death which is not too bad if you end up losing a unit you don't care too much about since then you don't have to reset, but you do feel a sting if it is a unit you do care about.The game is really buggy though. Several times my battle save disappeared and I had to restart the chapter from the beginning. If you start from battlesave too many global counters reset, kills, damage dealt etc. so some classes that rely on ramping up with additional kills lose their power halfway through the chapter due to this. Also, Adepts if you send them to their full move quickly after they have been displaced by another ability will often just freeze in place and you can't do anything but wait with them, plus you lose all the movement for that turn. Pushing units often causes them to glitch out.There is also some UI weirdness. Blue tiles are interactive - that means they could be chests or arrive tiles. Why not just have a chest there which would be way more obvious? The weapon triangle substitute is pretty hard to parse so I just found myself relying on checking if enemies had a green or red arrow before sending my units in, and I have no ideas what the F to S rating system is for and I've beaten the game on Hero so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my most anticipated games of the year and it does not disappoint! The weapon/upgrade system is so much more interesting than other games in the genre (also no arbitrary equipment durability!). The character progression system is so engaging and unique. It feels really meaningful to advance to the next class and you can really specialize your team the way you want. This game has a LOT of optional conversations between units as their bonds increase. Based on playing Fire Emblem: Three Houses I kinda expected these to be pretty bland but I was surprised at how well written they actually are. Several have actually made me laugh and the rest are just as engaging! I can go on about how well crafted this game is but I'm sure you can tell how I feel about the game. I can not recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to recommend this game, but I can not.  The game feels like a good Fire Emblem clone at first glance but when you get into the details of the game it falls on its face.  The plot is a good sleep aide it is is so bland.  Balance feels good at first but becomes tedious in the second half of game.  Fights become hordes of enemies with extremely high speed and dexterity stats so chances to hit become abysmal, even with high accuracy heroes and weapons.  Another issue of balance is the leveling.  At first you build a team of heroes and you become attached to them as they are involved in the plot but as you move on through the game there is not enough chance to level everyone to keep them relevant in the battles.  Too soon your favorite plot drivers are so under level vs enemies that they are ineffective and even liabilities in fights.  To balance this the game gives you a steady stream of new heroes that are appropriately leveled so you just rotate randos through your fights to progress the plot.  The other option is to focus on a small handful of heroes and grind through waves of enemies with only a few over leveled heroes, like most Fire Emblem games actually!  Had the game offered some type of arena to level heroes between fights it would feel better and most fire emblem games offer some type of side quest or arena for just this reason.  I would get the game if you are a big fan of Fire Emblem and it is on a large sale, otherwise pass.  Good attempt but just not good enough to be memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is a fun Tactical RPG that plays just like you'd expect as a fan of something like Shining Force. I don't really have a lot else to say about it,mechanically the game is solid.Spritework is pretty great and outside of spritework I'm pretty sure nobody expected anything other than anime art style from a game like this anyway so I guess that's fine.Only negative thing I have  to say about the game is that the story is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dreadfully written. It's basically written like a below average quality young adult novel with everything from nobody respecting their superiors in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ medieval military, characters talking back to the king with no respect and nothing bad ever happening as a result. This is because these characters are about as well thought out as your average TTRPG character, basically they're all given one personality type like carefree or quirky and they will never break out of that, even when doing so should realistically be the only way to avoid flogging or straight up field execution.If you're here for a story then just leave but if you're like me and you're here just to play a party based tactical RPG then this is pretty damn solid one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people like to compare this game to the gba fire emblem games, but I think a better comparison would be to Fire Emblem Three Houses. The design philosophy for both was to throw a bunch of customization at the screen without regards to balance. While in Three Houses that made for your own units interacting with the enemy in different ways, in Dark Deity most of the changes change how the enemy react to you, which unfortunately makes it so that there's no room for strict strategy or planning. You just end up throwing hard counters at each other, which is fun at first but it doesn't make for the best strategy rpg experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Absolutely beautiful graphics, overall. I'm not generally the biggest fan of the typical fantasy anime art style, but when it's done well, it works... and it's done well here. Also, the color palette is so vibrant, I just love it from the very first screen when you start a new game.- Character sprites are awesome- Can see an xp bar when selecting a character in combat. This one's hugely helpful in deciding who should try for a kill.- After battle statistics are nice to see- Combat is generally fun, and seems to be the correct level of challenge for most of the game. Late game has some issues, below.- When you reach the level to promote, you just promote. There's no delaying promotion to gain more stats, no stupid items needed, no games you have to play with promoting. And the classes are pretty awesome if rather unbalanced.- Certain characters are really growing on me unexpectedly. This rarely happens for me, so it feels like a big deal.Cons:- The game is essentially 98% plagiarism - Music sometimes becomes a bit dull and loses "momentum" in combat. Other times, it doesn't seem to match the mood of the cutscene. Also, it's too repetitive overall. Or maybe it's just not good enough to be as repetitive as it is.- Characters don't speak their lines, but instead make cringey monosyllabic noises. Pick one or the other, fully voiced or not. Don't make me listen to grunts and gasps.- Characters don't feel original; I feel like I've seen all the characters a dozen times before, with different hair colors.- Characters with boobs usually have boobs that are so big that it's just silly and cringey.- Can't seem to save or suspend in battles. Some kind of autosave would help the crashing issue.- No option between battle animations completely on, which are too long, and completely off, which looks ridiculous because nothing happens at all. There should be an abbreviated animation that plays on the main battlefield, like other similar games have. (If there's one idea DD should have borrowed from similar games, it's this)- Game hasn't explained any of the characters' special abilities yet (or anything at all, actually), which feels very odd because there's literally a tutorial mission. What's the point of that mission then?- No info about stats, how damage is calculated, etc. I need more info.- Weapon switching is rather annoying. The game doesn't explain it. Once you figure it out, you're spending half your time in combat switching weapons repeatedly between the 4 each character gets.- Clicking through the bond conversations is extremely annoying. And is there a limit to them? What benefits does it give? I don't know anything about it because the game doesn't tell you.- I NEED MORE INFORMATION- Later in the game, your heroes either need extraordinarily high speed or fairly high defenses to avoid being oneshot by frequent enemy crits. Since over half the heroes in the game don't get either, their survivability options are very limited and they're probably useless in battle unless protected from all enemy hits.- There are still crashes. The random spell animation option seems to crash the game when it tries to load an animation that it can't, for example. Because I can't change any options after starting a game, my Deity difficulty save is now bricked.- Edit: patches introduce a *lot* of new bugs and crashesThe positives outweigh the negatives, mainly because of the lack of competition.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far! If you like Fire emblem or similar games, please check this game out.If I might add one thing that's different from FE and that I like, it's that there is no permadeath, instead replaced by permanent stat losses should a unit fall. While this makes the game a little easier, I like that from a story point of view, your whole crew is still involved after their initial recruitment chapter instead of just the main lord and his 2-3 friends, meaning they pipe up from time to time in the main story line. This, coupled with some supports being chapter-gated, feels like your army is always chatting between themselves about (mostly) recent events in the game, making the whole cast feel more alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished my first playthrough on the "normal" difficulty and let me just say it was a wonderful experience. Let me start with all of my pros. The cast of main characters are all super well put together and i found myself loving most of them and loving to hate the others, along with some key phrase voice acting you can really feel the characters come to life. The combat of Dark Deity is reminds me of the old GBA fire emblem games but with some unique and interesting mechanics, such as promotion tree/skill combos and the aspects (in game items). Lastly the chapters were all good and i didnt find myself overly frustrated with any specific one although some i did have to restart with a different strategy going in. There are some downsides to the game but to me they are mostly moot in comparison to just how fun the game is. It would lag a little upon special screens like clearing the map or promotions. A couple times my character would be messed up and id have to go back and redo their move. The game isnt very well explained, although there is an in game tutorial and most frustratingly there seem to be some key chapters where you just feel under powered and others where you feel a bit overpowered.However some of those issues can be fixed with future patches and some can be fixed if you just choose to make it harder to suit your own difficulty liking. There is a customization button when you start a new file and you can change your stat gains and the enemies so make it crazy or keep it simple whatever floats your boat. I cannot wait to play through this game at least 2 more times as i want to beat the hardest difficulty and do a more crazy custom run and i hope the future updates fix the minor gripes i have. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: the combat and strategy-battle parts are fine, and the art and animations are great, but the characters are very generic and the dialogue is poor, and the inter-character relationship-building is meaningless with regard to the game, it's just a reading exercise, which might have been merely tedious with good characters and dialogue, but as it is there's absolutely no reason to engage with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: This game was wonderful to play, a genuine delight and a love letter to the classic Fire Emblem series. 10/10 8/10 loved it but there were so few voiced scenes it was hard to really appreciate it. 8/10 Nothing groundbreaking, just another JRPG heroes must stop bad guy, it doesn't go into intricate details too much outside of cutscene's but the characters do have rich backstories and are really well interconnected. 9/10 The mechanics of evolving your class and mixing and matching feels so fresh, since an rogue can do way more then just be a thief, assasin or even a fencer. Once you get your tier 2 you can also get a tier 3 down the line and change it into anything you want, it's really fun once you get there and for the combos it just felt right.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% not worth full price, I got it on sale and have played up to chapter ten so far. It is an amazing game right as you start, but the more you play the more you see the shoddy cracks. There are almost no options in the game at all, much less key bindings. Which would be fine if the controls were all mouse based but there are button prompts that you HAVE to use space and keyboard. To be fair isn't the biggest deal, it just comes off as early accessOther than that the game itself takes forever to load and the only way to restart a fight is to exit the save and reload from before the fight started. There is a battle save button but I haven't figured out how to use it yet lolThe story seems deep and polished just translated/interpreted poorly in englishAll in all the gameplay is REMARKABLE its just some of the clutter on the UI side that ruins the polish a bit for me. TL;DR 6/10 If you intend to only play with a mouse9/10 if you don't gafWould highly recommend waiting for a sale as 25$ seems reaaaallllly steep for something that needs a bit more work

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so weirdly inscrutable.  If you're here, you're no doubt familiar with the weapon triangle from Fire Emblem.This game has...a weapon thing-which-was-not-meant-to-be, a non-euclidean polyhedron.  I've got a couple dozen hours in the game and I still have absolutely no idea how to interpret advantages and disadvantages.  Every class has four weapons and an armor type.  They somehow all interact with each other.  I have no idea.Sometimes the game tells me a character has an advantage over a target enemy, and then the battle-prediction infographic tells me that if I engage I'll get absolutely demolished by the "disadvantaged" enemy.  I have no clue.I've attempted to read explanatory guides.  Still absolutely no idea what is going on.Anyway, long story short, if you're looking at this game and you haven't already checked out the alternatives, do yourself a favor and pick up Symphony of War or even Banner of the Maid.  Both of those have fun mechanics which make sense.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Dark Deity as a part of a bundle. As a Fire Emblem fan I was curious to try it out, and it kept me engaged for a few hours. The story and characters were dull to me, but the gameplay was at first interesting (I played the intermediate difficulty). I really enjoyed the idea of upgrading weapons and the different armor types/weapon advantage.However, I feel like the game suffers a bit when it comes to balance, map design and number of characters.1. The game's balance was allover the place, the level ups always gave a lot of stats, which meant that having a character die and lose 1 or 2 points of 1 stat didn't feel meaningful. The excessive amount of skills also made the enemy phase especially unpredictable/difficult to strategize around.2. The map design felt uninspired. Some of the maps such as the aqueduct fell cool, but most other felt like you were just killing everything in your path. The lack of terrain/other design elements to make the maps play different from each other also hurt the game.3. The number of characters was just too high and the fact that any character can promote to any classes within it's base class, including characters you just got, make them all feel very similar. Especially in a game without permanent death, it felt pointless to have this many uninspired characters. In Fire Emblem, having many characters can add to re-playability, but here since all characters are good and all are same-same and it makes little difference whether you raise characters or replace them by recent additions, it doesn't feel like there's much of a point to that.Overall, it's not the worst game I've played, but a few design choices let it down.
_childDocuments_.name: Dark Deity

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game extensively in the last week, and had a wonderful experience. That is not to say the game is perfect: it has some core gameplay flaws, and right now it is full of bugs and QoL problems.If you want to try this game, you have to keep in mind that it was developed by a really small team, with limited resources and experience. What they delivered is an incredible achievement for a first time product, but you will be disappointed if you are expecting a polished experience like Fire Emblem games deliver.Still, if you are willing to overlook those problems, you will find a bold game, full of personality and love. Some ideas feel refreshing in a genre that has struggled to innovate in the recent past, while others fall flat and just add an unnecessary complexity to a game that was already supposed to be about strategy.The good things:Character artwork is awesome, and they are full of personalities. The story is good overall, although some points feel rushed. The class system is really fun and engaging, and when you pair that up with personal skills, the weapon and aspects system, you get tons of customization options. The built in randomizer also fits perfectly with these customization options, allowing for great replayability.The bad:Bugs, bugs and more bugs. The testing strategy was deeply flawed, and they should have release it as an early access or made a public beta. Underestimating testing is a clear rookie mistake, and I'm sure the team knows this by now, and they are doing their best to fix things daily, but the backlog right now is huge. More extensive testing would also allow for more diverse feedbacks, and maybe releasing the game as early access would be a nice way to raise money to invest in more polishing, like the map sprites and sound design. The advantage system also feels bloated and even after beating the game twice, I still don't have a full grasp on how it works. It should be reworked and simplified.My veredict:If you love strategy RPGs, play this game. There is a lot of gold here, and the experience feels refreshing even if you have played all FE games out there. If you are not willing to deal with bugs and a game that feels unfinished, you should wait a couple of weeks, since the developers are pushing updates in a timely manner.

_childDocuments_.review: Crash heaven, chapter 5 locked as it crashes after you win. Also, part of the fun is to take you time to trial and promote your characters..........well, actually the class system is rather straight forward, no multiclass possible and no real "skills" or "spells" really, just rock paper scissors with different bonus and animations for the different classes.
