_childDocuments_.review: Note: This game is NOT a metroidvania. This is a 2d action platforming game. Spoilers will be marked.Review update as of version 1.4 - Original launch review below.Feels good to flip the review to thumbs up. Map looks MUCH better.Would still like to see a way to view how many powerups you have/are missing.Spells feel a LOT better. Gilded enemies feel good because of spell rebalancing.Dark mirror changes are cool, the gameplay feels more fluid now because you dont get interrupted every checkpoint.I like the change to how Moonhunger occurs. Doesn't lock people into a harder difficulty if they are already struggling. Honestly feels like the devs fixed almost everything in my original review. Very pleased, great job!=====TL;DR - It's ok. I didn't particularly enjoy due to what I feel are balance and design issues and some soft-lock bugs.=====I beat my first playthrough completely on moonhunger, and I did not enjoy. I did a 2nd playthrough entirely on the gentle moon, and it was a bit more enjoyable.  You cannot clearly see room/path borders so making sure you have explored thoroughly is hard because you need to have good memory as you cannot rely on the map. There are also limited powerups that you NEED (like damage) but there's no way to find/track them, or see how many you have.It's also a terrible negative feedback loop where if you die on the "easy" difficulty, you go to hard mode.Because moonhunger boosted enemy stats spells felt like they were terrible. Cost is high, damage low. But you HAVE to use them on gilded enemies.and because of the above, gilded enemies felt awful to fight, especially if you have to fight multiple and/or ravenous ones at the same time. The whole secondary weapon system seems whack. A temporary weapon that you lose at checkpoints? It has a one time bonus you lose when you die? Whack.  I encountered a couple soft locks, most notably the final boss. He just stopped doing anything and I had to force quit.Softlocked on an NPC who when I talked to them, no dialogue played and I had to force quit. Seemed to stop all progression for that npc too Game feels very very parry-spam heavy. Makes the combat feel shallow/repetitive.Boss fights felt challenging and definitely where I noticed myself improving at the combat.For better or worse, bosses seem to punish parrying so it broke up the normal feel of combat and made it more dodge-y.Always a fan of charm/accessories/customization options, though I didn't like that some of the strong ones broke on death with limited supply.Art style is coolFinally, I personally enjoyed the demo and was quite looking forward to this game. Perhaps thinking it was a metroidvania misled me, because I love that genre of game. This game not having metroidvania elements was a bit disappointing, but changing my perception to it being an action-platformer I think is much more fair to the game.Overall can't say I'd recommend, but I hope the devs can polish the game a little and keep making games, would like to see what they make next.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen here, you primitive clayborne…Perhaps you’ve heard of the complaints about the combat and the parry system... but fear not – they both evolve as the game goes on. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer : This is just my personal opinion you are free to disagree. The game looks very beautiful. Animations are slick and smooth. Atmosphere it builds is very moody. _childDocuments_.review: From the atmosphere, and the art, to the smooth and easily understandable combat.  I played this game twice, a rarity for me.  The glaring spelling and grammatical errors were, for a pedant like me, quite annoying and made it hard to take the story seriously.  However, I can see the effort that went into the worldbuilding.The combat is clear and readable; I've never had such an easy time parrying in a game.  The animations together with the sound design made every weapon swing feel hefty.  Only very rarely did I find myself cussing at the game instead of myself (for failures in combat) because frankly, the game is very fair.Just by looking at the enemies, I found myself instinctively understanding how they would work.  Thank you to those that designed their move set and art.  The difficulty of the enemies was upped in every area and it felt quite natural.The boss fights were a great amount of fun.  As soon as you understand their moves, and muscle memory kicks in, some do become somewhat trivial to defeat.  In my second playthrough, I defeated almost every boss on the first try without needing to switch out any amulets or witcheries.  I'm not sure if this is a negative or positive, just something of note.I felt the art in the cutscenes didn't work as well as it did in the actual gameplay and dialogue moments.  But that may be just my opinion.I didn't find myself using too many different witcheries but I enjoyed trying out most of them.That being said, the game isn't flawless.  The story's use of amnesia didn't feel clever; it felt like an excuse to have the main character learn the plot alongside the player but it never felt very meaningful.  The glaring spelling and grammatical and typing errors (there's a point where the dialogue's font has an inconsistency, and Adelinka is called Adelina on multiple occasions) were more than a mild inconvenience.  This isn't meant to undermine the real work that was put into it but as a writer myself, I found it very hard to ignore.  It's difficult to get invested in the characters when I can't stop imagining the writer stumbling over the keyboard; it's immersion-breaking.This is a damn good game.  The mechanics are fun and weighty.  The animation and art are smooth and atmospheric.  Nothing felt out of place (except for the spelling).  This is more a letter of praise to the developers than an actual review, I feel, but yes!  I recommend this to anyone that doesn't mind a challenge and enjoys 2D side-scrollers.  The atmosphere is Gothic, dark and brooding, without becoming tiring.  Each area has some reoccurring visual assets but overall feel distinct enough that I never had a problem in finding my way.What a lovely gem.  I must be biased because this is the kind of game that I've been looking for.  I want to thank my friend for recommending it to me.  Great find!  Mind you, I've never written a review before but this game deserved it.  Thanks to all involved.  I hope to see more of  in the future.  I'll be keeping an eye out!  Adelina and Adelinka are different people!  Obvious, looking back on it... but, that solidifies my point on the inconsistent spelling and grammar.  You need better writing-consistency if you want the player to take better note of your lore.

_childDocuments_.review: Moonscars is cool! I didn't know what to expect when I started other than a metroidvania with a cool atmosphere. STEAMDECK COMPATIBILITY: Super smooth, a few hitches here and there. There will be bad frame drops if there are a ton of particles and enemies on screen, but there are only 3-4 encounters within the game like this. I would say this is a safe pick for SteamDeck.STORY:+Flavorful dialogue.+Nothing feels tagged on. The game does not overstay its welcome.+-In Dark Souls, there are a lot of vague quests that you can miss if you don't get an item here or there, this game has those too. -Gonna be honest, I don't really fully get the story. I beat the game and am still left scratching my head, but there are not enough mysteries to draw me back in for a second play-through. COMBAT: +There is a pretty intense learning curve early on, but after that, the game hits its stride and nothing felt too easy or too hard. +Simple basic combos with a lot of parrying and dodging mixed in. Parrying chances are nicely telegraphed and lead to satisfying kills. +Spells are fun, but cost a lot. I wanted to use a lot more of them, but I ended up sticking with two. There were definitely a lot of varying options for spells+Charm/Trinket system really lets you make something akin to a build,EX: parries that heal, slower but take less damage, spells cost less. +Simple but effective enemy variety. +Special Weapon system was great, it never felt overpowered, and every-time you get to a new save-point your special weapon is changed, resulting in a fun way to spice up the game-play.-A few areas had way too many enemies, and made combat feel like a chore.-Flying enemies are a pain and force you to use a specific spell through the whole play-through.-Could have used one or two more bosses, there really were only about 7 bosses, with one being a repeat. The few mini-bosses that were there became common enemies in late-game, I completely forgot they were bosses. EXPLORATION: +The world was really fun to explore!+Felt more like a Dark Souls experience with the exploration, where pulling a lever may open a door to a previous checkpoint. The world consistently wraps back into itself in a satisfying way. -Movement was fluid and good for platforming, but some platforms are placed in a way where you don't feel like you can reach them. -If you attach the "slow movement" charm, there are important areas in the game you cannot reach with this trinket attached, resulting in some heavy confusion. -Simple aesthetic areas, none of the areas truly stood out barring one--The one area that stood out was due to how they play with the lighting, and it was fabulous to see, but it shows what they could've done more of.OVERALL:I really enjoyed my time with Moonscars. This really scratched the itch of  Souls-like while also giving me the fun of a Castlevania game. I definitely think this game is worth the money despite the short play-time. If it doesn't seem worth the money at twenty bucks, it is absolutely a must-get on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed this game but it has some flaws.Let's start with the positives:The visuals. You can see the screenshots. Enough said. Music's alright, similar to Blasphemous. Story is interesting and you get to piece together things when you progress through the game. Exploration is pretty typical metroidvania stuff.The game has a mechanic where you get bonuses for your character if you kill enough enemies without dying. If/when you die, you will lose these bonuses. This rewards good play and is a pretty cool idea.If you die with enough of these bonuses the game buffs the enemies - you can get rid of this by beating a boss or using up 'Gland' currency which makes it a non-issue, and I didn't find the buff to be that noticeable. Ichor/mana mechanic allows you to cast spells and heal yourself, which is implemented in a way where you can have 'spoiled' Ichor after using it, which can't be used for spells, only for healing. This encourages aggressive play and was something new I haven't seen from these types of games yet.You also have a special attack weapon that you get to choose multiple times throughout the game. It encourages experimenting with all the weapons but I felt most of them were quite slow to be viable in combat. You can use these combined with a dash to have a nice gap-closer. You can again use the 'Gland' currency to roll new special weapons if you really don't like your current one but it changed often enough where I didn't see the need for it.Then the negatives: Basically all the bosses are really easy. Even the combat in general is easy, except when the game throws multiple enemies at you, which is not a great way to put difficulty in your game. It does make for some fast-paced moments but I'm not a huge fan.Most enemies only have one attack combo they do over and over again, sometimes they have a ranged attack too. There are not that many new enemies to be seen after the first 2-3 hours of gameplay which was a bit disappointing.Some questionable design choices of which I want to highlight a couple (these are quite nitpicky but someone's gotta point these out):The map doesn't allow you to zoom out for some reason - annoying in a metroidvania game, the markers on the map are huge too.It's genuinely hard to tell which amulets you have equipped once you have many of them. You have to select an amulet to check the names of the items you have equipped. Also why do multiple tiers of an amulet stay in your inventory if you can't even sell the inferior versions at shops. It's just needless clutter, maybe make the better versions replace the worse ones. With spells it's implemented that way and it's fine.If you select an amulet to equip and then try to cancel the selection, it throws you out of the pause menu. Why?This can be viewed as a negative or a positive but the game allows for a ton of cheese strats. Hitting enemies through the ceiling, spikes on the walls or ground can be used to kill tougher enemies instantly, even .In summary, I'd recommend it if you're really into the visual style and wanna experience the story. The combat is easy, especially the bosses, so if you're looking for something difficult, this might not be it.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania with some fantastic pixel art. It doesn't do much to redefine the genre, but everything in it works together well.Controls are great, parrying is very responsive with clear / fair cues, platforming is pretty minimal but done well when it's required. Despite the game kind of having a "hardcore" appearance, combat as a whole is definitely on the easier side, with the game having some good adaptability if you want to make it easier or harder for yourself (both in world state and in the accessories you can use). The bosses are not particularly difficult but all offer some great visual spectacle and are excellently designed fights, mechanically speaking. One negative I have is that enemy variety is fairly lacking, with very few enemies being introduced beyond the first zone or two. Fortunately, it's a pretty short game so that doesn't really hit you too much, but it is disappointing to go to a brand new zone and fight basically the same enemies you've been fighting all game. Special weapons also felt generally underwhelming, and I honestly didn't find myself using them outside of very niche scenarios. Your character gets access to a bunch of spells (you can equip two at a time), and each has a good utility case so you won't feel like you've "wasted" points leveling them if you find one you prefer. That being said, there are some which have much more usefulness overall. Sound design and score are top notch, with brooding ambiance as you traverse the castle, and sinister boss themes to rally you on that "this'll be the one" attempt.The game has definitely benefited a lot from post-launch support, and I feel it's very well worth the full price. A lot of the early negative reviews / criticisms include elements which have been fixed by the developers (Moonhunger, much improved map showing upgrades / collectibles, different cue for unparryable moves). I did not encounter any visual nor gameplay bugs throughout my playthrough, and was able to achieve 100% in just under 10 hours. Can't wait to see what comes next from Black Mermaid!

_childDocuments_.review: In Moonscars, you play as Grey Irma, a warrior made of clay on a mission to find her creator, the Sculptor. Spoiler alert: the Sculptor is probably hiding because he knows how many times you’re going to rage-quit before you even get close to finding him. The game’s motto should be, “Die, Retry, Repeat,” but it feels more like, “Die, Cry, Repeat.”The combat is as fluid as a river of molten lava, and just as deadly. The enemies are as merciless as a cat with a laser pointer, and the bosses? They make you wish you had a cheat code for invincibility. Each encounter is a dance of death, and you’re the one with two left feet.The art style is a beautiful blend of gothic horror and claymation nightmares. It’s like someone took a Tim Burton movie and decided to make it even creepier. The story is as mysterious as a locked diary, and just as frustrating to decipher. But who needs a clear plot when you have the thrill of finally beating that one boss after countless attempts?In conclusion, Moonscars is a masterpiece of masochism. It’s perfect for those who enjoy a challenge, have a high pain tolerance, and don’t mind yelling at their screen. 10/10 would recommend, but only if you have a spare controller or two.

_childDocuments_.review: I got platinum in this game a little while ago, and I only went for it (77 collectibles ) because I loved it. I must first admit, I'm in a abstinence crisis ever since I finished Blasphemous and fell in love with Metroidvania genre, and this one was a nice little trip to feel the need that I have.  The ambiance of the game together with it's art, focusing on a three color pallet (black, white and blood), do make a very interesting atmosphere which match with the lore of the game's region - a desolated land where the fierce but gentle gaze of the moon lies eternal, result of hunger, war and death.  From it's beginning to the last cutscene the game is poetic and philosophical, rising up some discussions about it's own lore that got me off guard a couple of times. But in the start it could be a little rough to get it all and follow most details because everything is just thrown on you.  The combat it's very simple, but pleasant. There's a nice amount of shenanigans you could learn and make some slightly different play styles, I can't say much about how diverse build making can be, because I did only used a couple of them that got my attention from the start.   But after all the fights were indeed a very enjoyable part of the experience, once you got the rhythm it just feels natural and fluid. The enemies have some diversity and are awesome to kill, but the bosses... . All of them feels unique, since the first one who is a very pleasant surprise. They great design and movesets, have heavily importance to the story and to your character, some of them can be hard, and after all that's what I like, a good challenge.  It's a indie and simple game, that you can't expect too much, but a quick adventure and a very nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game since the combat system is actually challenging and discourages button mashing but there are a lot of things that make me cannot recommend this game at its current state:- After talking to any NPC, you can not directly move horizontally if you've been holding down the analog stick, and you need to press any other button before being able to move. Why is this a thing? - Once you've progressed far enough you'll get an upgraded dash. The input for this skill is not nice at all as it triggers when you 'hold' the dash button. When I first fight a boss, I'll focus at its sprite to learn its moves. Inevitably this sometimes make me not tap the dash button, but instead hold it for almost a second. What happens next? The MC winds up the superdash animation and got stuck in animation. (I get that if the input becomes a double tap, then button-spamming players will experience this inconvenience but surely there is a better way than locking it to the i-frame button.)   - There have been 2 instances where I got stuck in a room with enemies because one of the clays do not spawn an enemy. I know that this is a bug, but when you've been lost for a while due to the map being very hard to look at without touching a save point, then you just lost a lot of progress. The 1st time it happened made me go 'oh well' but the 2nd time just made me disappointed. I'm not going to comment on the story because I only made it to  so far before getting tired of the game. The art is fine, but I hope the map can be visualized better because you would need to memorize spots (because there aren't clear 'nodes' that shows possible paths.)Hopefully the devs can make the game less janky because as of right now, I can not focus on what I think is the fun part of the gameー its high-risk, high-reward combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Moonscars is a solid 2d souls-like game that I very much enjoyed playing. However, it does have some interesting design choices that may / may not dissuade you from playing it all the way through.Pros:- Amazing graphics and visuals. The scenery is beautiful and the animations are pristine. Moonscars was nothing but addictive eye candy.- Soundtrack is pretty good with some nice, eerie atmospheric tracks as well as cooler and heavier boss themes.- Combat was fluid and fun to master, with plenty of different spells / witcheries to experiment with.- Story was a bit confusing to piece together, but it was an enjoyable one nonetheless.Cons:- Parrying. The telegraphs for enemies parriable attacks in not as consistent, and sometimes you will parry and just miss the auto follow up attack because of weird spacing.- Secondary weapons are a very fun part of the game, but it feels like you're getting punished if you find one you like. When you switch to a different weapon, you get a bonus to health or ichor. But if you choose to stay with the weapon you've been using, you get nothing, and if you already had a health or ichor bonus and stick with the same weapon it gets removed.- Spell costs get very high when you upgrade them, which on paper sounds fine, but when you actually use them you see that you only get to use 1-2 charges at most sometimes. This wouldn't be so bad if the meter wasn't also tied to healing.- Healing is tied to your special meter, but when you use your special meter, it leaves behind this Blue Ichor in its place which can also be used for healing. Unfortunately, healing drains your normal special meter first  it starts to use the Blue Ichor. This makes it a bit frustrating to use these mechanics together. I believe this would be a much better system if it this was reversed.Neutral:- Short-ish game. While I enjoyed 100%ing this game, it only took me a little under 14 hours to do so, which was over the course of 2 playthroughs.- The Earrings were a bit annoying to find because they are tied to a mechanic known as Moonhunger. Moonhunger occurs when you reach high spite levels from killing enemies, and then dying when the moon icon on the top-left has red glow to it. You can only see these earrings when in Moonhunger, which isn't too bad, but the major problem with this is that Moonhunger is automatically cured when you kill a boss. I found myself having to just kill myself after killing a boss just so I was able to get as many earrings as possible. (This was mainly a personal pet peeve because I went for 100%, but if you're not going for a completionist playthrough then disregard this point).Moonscars was a very fun game. Even with all the negative criticisms I had, it didn't hinder my overall enjoyment, and I would definitely recommend it if you aren't bothered by the slight grievances I had. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play a lot of 2D games, but I like this oneThe visuals, animations and music are great. Enemies are challenging but fun, and there's a great variety of them. _childDocuments_.review: This game is great despite some of the negative reviews I've seen complaining about certain things that are skill based (aka a skill issue), though there are some things i can agree with but most of it is because i can tell half these people don't play as many Metroidvania games as i do. So i will go over both the positives and negatives by an experienced Metroidvania player.A Warning to New Players as this Review will have SPOILERS for the Later Game.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------     Positives: The main focus of this game is the Combat that is very apparent when moving through the Outskirts to the main Castle, the combat feels nice to play and isn't too punishing (at the first half). The Animations are great and the Special Weapon Previews heavily remind me of the Skill/Attack Previews in Castlevania Lords of Shadow. The Artstyle of this game is Very reminiscent of a Classic Castlevania game.The Parry System is one i see many complaints about but the thing people never realize is yes the Red Blink is an Indicator as to an attack you can parry but it ISN'T one you parry as the blink happens for a Successful Parry you need to block Last Second as most games have as a parry it's Not GRIME where you instant kill enemies by blocking with your head and having an easier window of performing said parry, personally i find the Parry system in this game to be completely fair except for it sometimes not registering attacks from rapid strikes (like the weird tentacle enemies in the lower castle).The music is very Atmospheric and fits each area very well.A complaint i often see is the use of Witchery's being mandatory to kill most enemies that's not the case as i use the main sword the most the only time i ever needed to use a witchery was during a boss fight (usually the doppleganger witchery) to give myself a larger window to heal and the first one (one that's mandatory) to break barriers.I see a mix bag on Etelag's (the cat) quest as it's one you can apparently fail? i never failed it as i go out of my way to explore to find mirrors and collectibles that i'll never use so i'm more bias on this one as i didn't see much of an issue with it besides locking you out of a mirror temporarily.The bosses are a fun fight though some seemed a little easier than others for the phases (my only issue with the final boss)     Negatives: As i mentioned just above with the bosses there's no reason for the Final Boss (Second Phase) to be easier than all the bosses and tougher enemies prior as his attacks did less damage, easier to parry and dodge and easier to get hits on.The part that irks me the most was the Earths Bowels area (East) as it has the Flying enemies with Shields now i understand that by this point you would have other Witchery's to deal with them easier but i always decided to run with Scimitars and slowly bleed them to death since the standard bolt was practically useless on them since they were always a 45% angle above you so you couldn't hit the with that witchery unless you get on an elevated platform then cast (something that isn't present in the later portion of the bowels).Another issue i had was the lack of Enemy Variety as the late game you would expect new enemies per area but the Castle Apex has all the enemies from the Outskirts with shields and higher Damage what happened to the bomb enemy in Depths why is that enemy only there and nowhere else in the entire game? each area needs more enemies for variety as once you know how an enemy works you kind of know how to deal with them for the rest of the game defeating the existing challenge with learning new attacks and patterns.One of the other things that annoyed me a bit on the later portion was the way the Apex and Bowels were handled with enemy damage and health, what annoys me is when you fail to make something harder naturally so decide to use the same enemy and just increase the damage and health 5x and give it armor while being the same enemy like i mentioned above.And don't remove Vendor NPC's without giving a second means of getting their pre-existing Stock as i had my inventory filled with memories that i couldn't use for 500 powder each because the NPC for it dissapears.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Now one of the things you'll probably see on this review is my hours i'll tell you readers now i have 10-11 hours in this game  the reason it says 5-6 is because i lost connection to steam a couple times so it just stopped tracking hours i have 100% the achievements in this game i'm working on grinding all the bone dust to unlock every witchery.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my recommendation for this game come with a great BUT. I unlocked all spells, found more or less all gems, reached maximum life and magic power, did all sidequests and uncovered the entire map but i did NOT finish the last boss. This game comes with a great art style and Sounddesign that together make for a weighty impacting experience.The developer also sat down and cooked up an interesting variety of gameplay elements. There is: A witchery tree to unlock quite a few spells like poisonous attacks, homing missiles, shockwaves etc.Gems that give various stats boosts or special conditions like gaining Magic Energy on being hit.Bone amulets that give similar effects like the gems just much more stronger and they get destroyed when the player gets defeated and respawns.The Moonhunger status that comes up after the player has died a few times. This status can be alleviated by the player via a currency that is also used in shops and upgrades but also can intentionally be summoned by the player. It is essentially a Bloodmoon that strengthens enemies in damage and life but also the XP that they give upon defeat. Special Attacks/Weapons that take longer to execute and can have extra additions like causing bleeding on enemies or refill your magic, stuff like that.The Gameplay overall is a bit janky.During exploration Spike/Trap placement had some really dickish moments that made me roll my eyes but for the most part were entirely fair. Similar with hidden secrets. I never felt that they were unfairly hidden and discovering them was fun.Sidequests were also relatively short and well done. Some could simply be fulfilled by playing the game, basically giving some interesting story bits or gems as reward.Oh yeah and there is a dodge... it is a dodge, it is there and it does what it says.Combat feels scrappy, brutal and like an unforgiving brawl where you fight with tooth and nail. Partially this is because it is well... no quite balanced or polished. The parry is a mess. Enemies have a red glint in their eyes that flares up as an indicator when it would be best to parry. This works well for the starter and the straight forward enemies. But for many of the enemies it varies heavily by type when to actually parry, based on their position and/or the attack they are executing.For some I was repeatedly wishing they did not have the red glint because it was too distracting from the actual indicator that helped with parrying their specific attacks (which can be their attack animation or their distance to the player or other factors). Overall it made parrying quite janky.The parry also takes FAR too long, which is a repeating problem. The same for example counts for the Special Attacks. They are beautifully animated but take far too long to execute and if you actually want to hit anything with it you will have to just accept that you will cash damage in the process.This is however where the scrappy feeling comes from that gives combat an interesting feeling.There were also a few bugs in the game the worst of which was that an important collectible was missing or not indicated on the map (which they should be on a bloodmoon). But I had nothing strictly technical like the game crashing or slow downs in the frame rate.Unfortunately there are some design decisions that are, well not great. For example, when fighting enemies you can gain five levels, each level gifts you a choice of three upgrades, like 10 percent increased critical hit chance, Spells cost less, etc. Problem is that if you die you loose all of these levels and the associated boni. That feels bad at first. Then you realize that it is limited to five levels, which isn't really that much and which also means you are NOT getting rewarded if you survive much longer then usually.So you learn to just ignore these Boni at first. But then it becomes annoying again since you  to choose these five boni anew every time that you respawn and then subsequently level back up. You also won't have them really for the last boss so why the whole thing is there in the first place is a bit baffling.The other issue is the aforementioned last boss. The first phase is still actually fun to figure out, It has the usually last boss bs like homing attacks and, before you figure out how to deal with it, a onslaught of enemies.Unfortunately the first phase also has an element of luck. The spawners can spawn either what I would call summons. Those are enemies that pop up, do one or two large attacks and disappear again, which means you were lucky. Or they PRECISELY spawn THE EXACT enemies from the overall game which I would describe as the most janky. In this case you were unlucky because they can also spawn WHILE you have to deal with the homing attacks or a wave of chasing tentacle spikes. It is quite ridiculous how precisely they choose these for the boss fight.     Now it is possible to best this phase and I got as far as being able to reach the second boss phase quite reliably, depending on my luck.The second phase is basically a jumping puzzle and consists of the player mostly jumping over and over and over and over evading a veriety of spear and spike attacks and then landing some hits on the boss, maybe. There is not really time for healing nor for more elaborate attacks. It certainly won't let you use special attacks since they just take you too long and you can't dodge out of them. They will simply get you killed.Overall the boss just felt not great to fight and relatively unfairly hard. The second phase basically takes out any sort of real fighting and just made me stop.Now, despite these issues, why do I STILL recommend this game? Because for at least 21 of the 26 hours I played I really enjoyed myself. Combat felt hefty and of a difficulty that felt great because you often scrapped by evading death in the last second or finishing an encounter with only a quarter of life left.I also really enjoyed the atmosphere of the world, the music and the somber feel amidst thundering and crashing encounters with enemies and bosses.Its a okay game with overall more good qualities then flaws. I am looking forward to see what the team learned from this and how they implements feedback and their experience in their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: If not interested in details - check the last paragraph.Moonscar's setting, music and ambience are incredible, however I feel like the game is missing something. Although that opinion might be based on my unforgettable experience with Blasphemous. I get that the Moonscars is a different game, however as I said, I felt it was missing something, maybe a bit of "horrendousness"? The game's climate seems to aim at a poetically dark, depressive, full of sadness, reaching its end world and I feel some aspects made it stray away from that. Fighting is definetely one of the best parts of the game, feels smooth and intuitive. Looking at the game's usable resources, I think that Bone Powder becomes pretty useless very early in the game. Once I checked out every Witchery, I chose two and sticked with them until the end of the game. Ended up with 30 glands too, choosing not to use them as I did not feel that would bring me noticable bonuses.I will not talk about the difficulty, except i found it challenging and not too irritating, even after dying in the same place numerous times. One thing I found really annoying though, was the fact that the equipment menu was disorientating. For example once I equipped the necklaces (gemstones/bonestones w/e you'd like to call them), later I couldn't find which ones were equipped, as they were not highlighted in any way. (They all look pretty similar too, literally everything in the menu is in the same colour.)I generally reccomend playing moonscars if you like metroidvanias, the plot is interesting and the quests very souls-likish (you might have a hard time completing them without a guide) and not absolutely boring. The climate is great (with a little piece missing), fighting is fun and rewarding. Resources could be made better (imo). The game is challenging, but not annoying. _childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and really loved it. was looking forward to the full game. but right now I cant recommend it to anyone who doesn't hate themselves. Pros: animations and backgrounds are fluid, and the story had me curious enough to keep going.sadly the cons are more or less everything else. the combat gets boring very quickly with you dealing with enemies is much the same ways (until later where it gets worse ) your ichor skills (magic) cost so damn much that they were never really an option for me in combat. on top of that, they cost EVEN MORE to use as you upgrade them, further de-incentivizing using them. your base combos never change, and 3 bosses in, i havent gained any new world traversal skills, making me question why its being called a metroidvania. I could also talk about how the parry system is inconsistent at best with the reward being more or less the same as if you had simply dodged the attack and at worst, attempting it gets you killed. on top of that, the game seems to have its worst frame rate drop RIGHT before an enemy attack goes off, so sometimes if the parry mechanic doesn't kill you, the lag does. I could ignore ALL of the above by the way, if it wasn't for my last issue. the blood moon. this mechanic is the one that made me decide to put this game down for my own sanity. your world's default state is the gentle moon, your standard difficulty. dying from anything for any reason activates the blood moon. during this, you suffer from moon hunger. what does that do? it makes enemies hit harder, have more health, more aggressive, and you take more damage, deal less, and heal less. the 'trade off' is supposed to be that you earn more money in the blood moon, but as we previously discussed, money is useless if its for upgrading a magic system i wont even use. the only way to cleanse the blood moon and return to normal difficulty is to spend glands, a resource that is limited and can instead be used to buy VERY helpful items from an npc. so you are torn between suffering through the bloodmoon to save your glads for an item that might help you turn the tide, or spending your resource to get the game to return to default state. a state that will disappear if you die again. I found myself stuck on a boss that I couldn't kill on normal and was getting ANNIHILATED by on blood moon. i could only watch helplessly as my store of glands started to dwindle after so many failed attempts, knowing eventually i'd have none left and i'd have a bricked file where i couldn't progress. eventually the anxiety of this got to me and i just set it down. I think the blood moon as a mechanic isn't bad, but it should be a CHOICE. punishing suffering players by making the game harder, feels cruel and doesn't feel like a fun challenge. so right now, I cant imagine anyone who isn't one of those 'git gud' people enjoying this. save your money until it gets some balance changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's pretty good. It's no Ender Lilies, but it's got solid combat and movement, so the core gameplay is fun. Not only do you lose your currently equipped special attack, but you have to fight a clone of yourself in order to get it back. This happens EVER SINGLE TIME you find a new checkpoint. It gets irritating REALLY fast. Not only is it annoying and tedious, but it dramatically slows things down for basically no reason. I wish there was a way to mitigate this, like by paying Glands or something so that you didn't spawn one every time. But whatever, I guess we deal with it.Bottom-line, a serviceable addition to the collection of games like Ender Lilies, Unworthy, Vigil: The Longest Night, and so forth. Not the best of that crowd, but not the worst. Worth checking out if you really love the genre like I do, and the price is spot on.

_childDocuments_.review: Moonscars is a 2D hack and slash RPG with a low-graphical presentation, likely inspired by Dark Souls and the like. The competent combat and aesthetic may set it apart for you in the giant pool of Soulslike inspired games.It is gloomy, it is dark, and it intentionally looks ambiguous and low quality to create an atmosphere where the beings in game have recognizable shapes but are… off in a creepy way. The music is made to fit the atmosphere (dark/gloomy).Tl;drSoulslike.Better defined as a platformer hack and slasher, where you navigate various maps, defeat monsters and bigger monsters. Resources you collect in the world amount to a currency lost on death (Bonedust), a rarer currency used to give check-point based buffs or remove the death penalty (Glands), and then permanent Health, Magic, and Power upgrades.You can equip two spells and three accessories that modify your character in specific ways.Bonedust is used to purchase things from merchants, and to buy SPELLS at checkpoints. One accessory allows you to spend bonedust to power-up your spells. Glands are used to buy even better accessories, grant temporary buffs until you activate a new checkpoint, remove the death penalty (Monsters are more sturdy and hit harder), and allow you to pick a secondary weapon without fighting a mini-boss.There is slight randomized progress in the form of Spite Level and Special Weapons, the former gained from killing enemies without using a checkpoint and the other by slaying a Doppelganger. Doppelgangers are spawned every time you activate a new checkpoint, and must be defeated to claim a special weapon.Special weapons are slow, but powerful attacks that apply unique debuffs to your enemy. More importantly, however, is that landing blows with special weapons generates more mana to cast spells and heal compared to your basic attack.Healing is done with a dedicated button, which is good. Healing uses the same resource as your attack spells, which is good. Using attack spells does not limit your healing, despite my implications of such. Healing limits your use of attack spells. The game explains it better. It’s a good system that compliments itself by encouraging the player to find a rhythm of attacking, spell-casting, and healing.The spells are necessary, to an extent, in the game to damage Gilded enemies and a certain boss who suffer very little damage from your attacks otherwise. There is a dash dodge and a parry that also must be mastered to successfully defeat Gilded enemies without headache.Tl;drSoulslike.The world is dead or dying, you are made of clay and Ichor (God’s Blood), and you need to find the Sculptor to… do things. And there’s a lot of clay monsters in your way. Go kill them.Except Sweet Wanda. She kills you. A lot.The game is intentionally cryptic and vague as the characters relate the story, and they all have their own goals and intentions for the character you control. There are sidequests to expand upon the world’s lore and history, but it's ultimately unnecessary to do them save for the resource advantages they give. There is only one ending to the game, as far as I know.It's Soulslike, I could be wrong about there being a singular ending.IT IS A SOULSLIKE.For twenty bucks.It pulls it off. The combat is engaging as long as you use your whole kit of dodging, parrying, and special attacks. The Ichor(Mana) system of the game is the innovation that I appreciate in the combat system, as it encourages you to be aggressive with your magic but allows you to heal even if you whiff spells. It has lore and secrets to sniff out if you really want more story, but for twenty dollars it's a good SOULSLIKE.

_childDocuments_.review: is a Metroidvania with Souls-like elements. The story follows Grey Irma, who is not the Chosen Undead, but a Pristine Clayborn, which is technically different, and trying to find her creator, Zoran the Sculptor. There are no dialogue choices, but not counting , the logic is fine. The game discusses the topics of free will and self-determination. There is minimal character customisation and it is limited to combat. The health, Ichor (mana), and damage increase linearly when finding the upgrades on the map, certain modifiers can be chosen as one progresses and lost on death, while the spells have to be bought with Bone Powder (“souls”). There are 3 amulets, 2 spells, and 1 special weapon to have equipped simultaneously. Though, nothing stops one from changing the amulets and spells between battles, the special weapon can be changed only at the Mirrors (fast-travel and checkpoints) or upon defeating a boss. While there are few bosses, each of them feels significant and has a background story, with the dialogues building up the boss battle. One of the most notable aspects is the healing system - Grey gains Ichor to spend on healing or casting upon attacking foes or getting hit, so there is no hard limit on recovering one’s health and it is possible to travel and fight for long before resting. The game saves the exact position on exit, so it is possible to continue between sessions without the need to backtrack to the nearest checkpoint. Another important aspect is that the combat difficulty and rewards from the enemies increase the longer one keeps going without dying, though it caps at 5 passive abilities and it is doable due to the healing system.  The highlight of a Metroidvania is exploration and in  is enjoyable and rewarding - most of the traversal abilities are available from the start, the controls are rebindable and responsive, though the rewards vary - there are above-mentioned stat upgrades, a few quest items and keys, some amulets (better ones can be bought from the merchants at the hub), and a lot of little piles of bone powder. The only issue is the second unlockable traversal ability, Super Dash. It takes some time to learn from what distance it should be activated to successfully get over a chasm. The pixel art and almost monochrome visual style is gorgeous and readable at the same time. The animations are fluid and expressive. The soundtrack fits the game and does not distract from it. There is no VA outside of the opening and ending cinematics.The only issues I have with the game are the design of the side quests - the triggers are really obscure or time-limited.Overall, it is an enjoyable action game.

While satisfying, once I perfected my parry timing, every enemy became a pushover other than the bosses. However, these boss fights were still fun and engaging, so I really don't think it's a huge issue for a game of this length. In fact, I think the reward of easily dispatching almost any enemy that challenges you is deserved if you manage to perfect your timing within that estimated 8.5-hour period.Also, a warning to any completionists out there: you will need to play the game twice to 100% it due to some story choices, but by the time you beat it the first time, the second run will be much easier.Overall, I really loved this game and would highly recommend it to anyone interested in Souls-likes or pixel graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and honestly, for the first few areas, I really did!  The artstyle is unique, the animations are fluid and nice.  The combat is fun, and manages to be one of the few games that gets the parry feel down right.  But as I get further in, it becomes increasingly apparent that the devs ran out of ideas.  The same few enemies are reused over and over and over and over and over again, with the only difference being bloated hp and damage.  It gets to the point where you've fought everything so many times that combat becomes more of a slog than an interesting experience.  The secrets quickly become meaningless, as most are just this games equivalent of souls, which can only be used to purchase a few charms and some spells, or glands, the other form of currency that can be used for charms or various temporary upgrades, as well as ending the blood moon.  You rack up so many of these so quickly that even losing everything at death doesn't feel all that meaningful.  The main issue is that every combat encounter past a certain point is just enemy spam.  Put a few massive enemies together that can kill you in a few hits, add in some smaller enemies that are nearly impossible to distinguish in the mob, and some flying enemies, too, cuz why the ♥♥♥♥ not?!  It's just tiring.  The story is very intentionally vague and esoteric, a trope that is honestly getting more and more tired the more I see it used.  It has an interesting basis, but my god, the whole "confusing for the sake of being confusing" is just old at this point.  Who are these characters?  Why should I care about them?  No answers are given other than "this is my best friend, ignore the fact that we have never interacted throughout the game."  Everything just turns so... bleh.  I just can't bring myself to care about it.  Even the environments start blending into each other, which isn't helped by the color palette of the game being black, white, red, and some washed out blues and greens.  I don't know, man... Definitely disappointing.  I'd say maybe pick it up on a sale if you really love metroidvanias and are itching for another one.  Not that great if you ask me.

_childDocuments_.review: I imagine most other reviews will reference Hollow Knight and Bloodborne, and they'd be right.  Take the combat, movement, and spell system of Hollow Knight, and then give it a much darker, Bloodborne-style narrative.   You'll uncover lore as you progress, which you can choose to immerse yourself in or not.  There's some light roguelite mechanics in addition to the familiar charm (amulet) system, which make way for fast paced combat that doesn't leave you too disappointed if you lose a few fights.  I always appreciate when roguelite mechanics tie into the narrative, which I think they did a nice job of here.My first save file took me less than 10 hours to clear, so while there may be more to sink your teeth into elsewhere, this game felt like it achieved its overall goal of being an excellent gothic 2D action platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Moonscars is a deeply flawed game and one that I absolutely adore and celebrate. The art style is a painterly impressionism but with the dark foreboding tones of romanticism. It's breathtaking.It's probably one of the best written MVs I've played, if not outright the best. Very strong LoK and BR2049 vibes. The themes of meaning, being, existence, creation, and freewill are explored. It doesn't always stick the landing but it never falters too hard either. It keeps you very much engaged narratively.The gameplay is a mishmash of genres like some Darksiders game. The basic nature of it is very much like a very tiny SOTN - fairly linear yet sprawling environments to explore with lots of secret upgrades for those that seek them. Nothing in the game is Metroidesque, there is no non-lineary, sequence breaking, etc. The game wants to tell a specific story and it wants you to experience it in that specific way.There are soulslike elements here like corpse running, xp as currency, difficulty fetish, dodge/parry heavy gameplay. I would specifically compare the difficulty to CV3 USA or CV68k - it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tough. However, you can craft builds quite easily that let you manhandle the game, so to speak.Beyond the soulslike, there's also the roguelike elements - lots of significant bonuses divided up between gameplay elements. Special weapons upgrades offer rotating bonuses on weapon swap. Killstreaks allow you to stack additional bonuses. I think I had up to five at a time and it makes you strong; however, you lose these on death. You can even choose what enemies drop. Lastly, there's also a CV2esque mechanic: dying with stacked bonuses triggers a world state where enemies are tankier, deadlier, and way more lucrative to kill. This can easily be alleviated with an item.Yes, this is a Soulslike Roguelike Metroidvania from 2022 that is only 10h long. Of course it pushes zero gameplay boundaries but the writing, art, and vibe alone are where the game is at. It does those best and if you wish to play this game then do it for the writing and the art, nothing else. _childDocuments_.review: below, copy-pasting a review from a forum where I write those sometimes: is a pixel-art, grimdark soulslike metroidvania(?). With this being basically me favourite genre of games, I had very high expectations for this. Unfortunately, the game mostly fell flat for me, although it does deliver decent entertainment in some key areas.To not sound overly negative, I'll start with the positives. The main one, which is also the reason why the game got decent amount of attention, is its absolutely gorgeus artstyle. Mostly 3-color pallet of black, white and red, paired with some incredibly fluid animations works perfectly for this genre and conveys a great atmosphere.Combat against regular enemies is also very well design, you have many offensive options and the game encourages (and rewards) you for seamlessly switching between all of them. It feels great to land attacks, parries and spells on all the foes the game throws at you.I liked the story as well, it is a bit less cryptic than your typical soulslike, but all the usual themes of decaying kindgomds and death are there, as well as some other interesting ideas.Unfortunately, this is where my praising ends. My biggest issue with the game comes from its biggest diversion from the standards of the genre - namely, its implementation of roguelike-ish mechanics. As you go kill enemies, you get continuous levels of upgrades, that are lost on death. Additionally, on death there is a decent chance that the game will go into "ravenous moon" mode, making enemies hit harder and have more health. Basically, you are rewarded for not dying more than in other soulslikes and punished for death more than in other soulslikes. This creates an awkard gameplay loop, where for a while you're just cruising, snowballing into a powerhouse and making the game extremely easy. Then, when you finally die, it becomes much, much harder. Fortunately, there are some ways to remedy this, but they are mostly tied to limited consumables. Overall, it just feels like a bad design for a soulslike.Exploration is also lacking in my opinion. I hesitated to even call it a metroidvania - yes, there are movement abilities and ability gates, but these were planned in an incredibly linear fashion. Sure, you can "preview" some areas earlier if you want, but you will be stopped very quickly - the overall progression of the game is completely linear.The level design seemed cool at first, but it got very repetetive very quickly and by around half of the game I was already bored. There are some secrets, but they are not exciting - this is tied to a very limited character progression/customization, I understand that this is not an rpg, but you need some way of rewarding exploration other than one of 2 ingame currencies.Finally, my feeling on bosses are rather mixed. There's not many of them (I counted 7, with 1 reskin) and I wouldn't necessarly call them "bad", but they are just designed in a way that's not my style, with tons of adds, projectiles and AOE attacks. I understand that designing a fair, but challenging straight duel can be difficult, especially with parry window and reward being very generous, but what we got just isn't doing it for me.Despite all the negativity above, I still had a decent amount of fun with the game. It's not bad, it just tried very hard to be different than others in the genre and, in my opinion, all those diversions were not succesful. That being said, big part of my disappointment came from my high expectations. If you're looking for a pretty game with great combat and don't mind overly punishing mechanics, Moonscars might be for you. From me it's a .

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better Metroidvanias I've played recently. Thickly atmospheric, steeped in cryptic-yet-captivating lore, gorgeous to look at, and terribly fun to play.Gameplay-wise, there is quite a bit of focus on enemy encounters and bosses, which is precisely where the game's design shines. Combat feels gratifying and fast: with combos, spells, dodges and parries.There is an interesting amount of customisation, as well: several "Gemstones" can be found throughout the world to complement your play-style; and killing enough enemies without dying grants a selection of passive boons, which are particularly useful against bosses. Special weapons may also be acquired by defeating some foes or conducting rituals at checkpoints: these lend some variety to your moveset while also building up special effects on foes, such as damage-over-time or slowdown.Unfortunately, I feel as though the game is a bit too short for the genre: I clocked a bit over 15h for a blind playthrough with around 90% completion - I didn't feel like scouring the map for special collectables. Enemy variety does also takes a bit of a nosedive in the endgame, making this final stretch a bit repetitive - although the final set of bosses more than makes up for it.Overall, the most criticism I can give to this game is: I wish there was more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: An easy 8/10 recommend for me.Story seemed very cryptic and difficult to understand at first, but it becomes gradually more clear, and I liked the way it went and the twists along the way.I appreciate the art style a lot. It falls behind Blasphemous a bit, because it also has beautiful pixelart and detailed animations, but lacks the vibrant colors and backgrounds. Still, I think the animations are more impactful here.Music was very fitting. Wouldn't listen by itself most likely, but really added to the atmosphere, and I would say the game is very atmospheric and easy to get immersed in.The most important point is the gameplay. I would say moving was pretty satisfying, but not much platforming challenge. The map is "open", but progression feels very linear. The thing that kept me playing was definitely the combat. Not many bosses in the game, but the selling point are all the mob encounters. When you get in the zone with witcheries, secondary weapon and normal attacks, charged attacks, jumping attacks and parries, you get into a sort of satisfying rhythm that reminds me of sekiro somewhat. It's also very, very brutal and punishing. Losing focus for one second in a crowded enemy encounter is death, but you also recover from being near death very quickly with the hollow knight-like healing system. I have seen many people call the combat "clunky", and the enemies "repetitive", but I just simply didn't feel that. For the record, I also played the entire game under ravenous moon, the extra challenge was fun.I really hope black mermaid makes some more games, I'm sure they will learn a lot from this already great game and make some more great stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent souls-like metroidvania on the same level of quality as Blasphemous.Pros:+ Pixel art is great, dark and brooding, with muted earthy colours contrasted by the vibrant reds of the blood and your character+ Combat is extremely satisfying. Unlike others in the genre (e.g. the abysmal Tarnishing Of Juxtia) your attacks *can* be interrupted by healing / dashing / jumping and vice-versa+ Fast-traveling, again unlike the atrocious one in Juxtia, is implemented from the beginning of the game and is actually useful and easy to use+ Enemy design is varied and and in tone with the dark environment around+ Full key rebinding is implemented (has to be mentioned since many devs nowadays deny this option)Cons:- If I had to pick one negative, it's the story. It's a rather crude take on the Creation that has a rather uninspired ending following a straight path with only one (small) twist near the end- Still story-related, there are a couple of characters you meet on the way that can either die or be saved by your actions. The problem is that it is never made clear which ones can die and which can be saved, and how to do that precisely

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit skeptic at first, there are just too many mediocre games with janky cinematics, metroidvania and souls-like structures built in; but if you like any of the aspects in this genre, do give this one a shot. The art direction is great, the music is moody and non-interfering and the overall level design and control scheme are respectively intricate and responsive (and yet at times infuriating!). There are going to be obvious comparisons to Blasphemous, but I can assure this game does not ride along the coattails of it's indie cousin well earned fame. Where Moonscars really shines is the story. Grey Irma as a character works really well as a player surrogate, the excuse for discovering bits and pieces of the fairly convoluted worldbuilding using dialogue and events made me feel like I was a bit of an archaeologist,  or a detective in a crime scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite metroidvania I've ever played. I think the closest comparison I have is Blasphemous, but this game overall is much more cohesive in game-play and world design. Interesting characters and the mysteries of this world make you want to learn about the story of the world and your character Grey Irma. The aesthetics and themes in this game are immersive, making the whole experience enjoyable. The music is fitting for the environments and never too distracting. The backgrounds of the maps are layered well, giving you a feel for its grandiose environments in the way it moves. With regards to movement, it feels smooth which further enhances the enjoyability of landscape traversal. In terms of level design, there's a good balance of map hazards as well as hidden secret rewards. Though I wish there was more verticality to the first map/area.I think what makes this game so good is the smoothness of the game-play. In terms of combat, the enemies are well balanced, with regular enemies being able to kill you if you aren't paying attention or just spamming attacks. The special attack is highly underutilized in my opinion though, as the damage is not nearly good enough to use consistently. You end up spamming dash and light attack and this is usually good enough to get rid of most enemies. This is a viable strategy since most of the enemies are fast attacking. If there were more slow and heavy hitting enemies that required you to use this heavy attack, then it would see more use. But at the moment, the big enemies are also quick and don't deal enough damage so you end up just spamming them with light attacks and dash. The difficulty is fair, though there are times where it feels a little monotonous due to a lack of tougher regular enemies. The boss fights so far have been good, though I wish there were more of them. Overall, worth the time and price

_childDocuments_.review: Moonscars is a great soulslike action-platformer with satisfying combat, sprawling level design and gorgeous visuals hampered by some technical issues & odd design choices as well as rough translation at times. These small issues aren't enough to detract from what is at it's core a game with such solid pace and action that it's hard to put down. So much so that i beat the whole game in 3 sittings, which is very few since i tend to need breaks from games every 2 hours or so to take a breather. The game often reminded me of blasphemous in the best possible way, and while it doesn't quite reach as high it's still a good game worthy of your time. I hope i can convey why in this review.Let's start with the combat as this is the foundation upon which any action platformer is built. The combat almost feels as great as blasphemous at times, even surpasing it in some regards like animations. The core combat is incredibly good with regular attacks, heavy attacks, special attacks, magic, dodging and parrying all woven together into an exhilirating dance of death. The parry especially became my go-to for most enemies, akin to blasphemous' parry, which while generous (especially compared to something like grime) still required good timing to execute properly. When it does work though you can riposte with a satisfying heavy attack which deals big damage and knockbacks enemies. This can be used to knock enemies into the many spikes sprinkled about thoughtfully in most combat sections. A big contribution to this smooth combat are the mindblowingly well animated attacks and dodges from not only the main character but enemies & bosses as well. Never before in pixel art have i seen such great animations for the characters attacks, they flow over into eachother perfectly and really give combat the feeling of a dance rather than mindless slashing which many other soulslike fall into.The balance is also just right. It's not stupidly hard but it ain't easy either, the game is challenging and sometimes pretty hard which makes it all more rewarding in the end. The challenge comes from fighting the multiple enemy types in different combinations. Enemy designs and attack patterns are also very well designed, with each enemy having one or several different attacks that vary enough to keep you from falling into the same pattern. The attack timings are ever so slighly different so that you always have to be on your toes to dodge/parry. These enemies, while few in variations (about a dozen or two) are combined in different configurations throught the game. It's really impressive how no two combinations felt similar, requiring me to adapt on the fly. The bosses also follow this design phylosophy where each felt distinct and unique with many different attacks that are all fun to dodge and a spectacle to behold thanks to the great animations.The level design while mostly linear at the start really opens up in the mid/endgame with multiple zones to go explore. Each zone is also filled with different pathways and shortcuts that seamlessly loop back on eachother after a while, which is the hallmark of great level design imo. While there's only two forms of ability gating i think that the game is still metroidvania-ey enough to be counted as one. The overal map is a joy to explore thanks to it's great level design on a micro & macro scale. Each zone is also distinct visually, ranging from gardens & caverns to ruins, castles and cathedral rooftops. Here again the game reminds many of blasphemous in the best possible ways. I'd even go as far as to say that i think that the visuals themselves surpass the fine pixelart from blasphemous, not in terms of designs but purely in a visual sense.The careful and deliberate use of colour amongst the greys and blacks elevates the pixelart to where it almost feels like brushstrokes off paint that were then pixelated afterwards. Add to this some stellar lighting and fog effects and you have a gorgeous & memorable aesthetic worthy of being framed and placed in your living room. The sombre visuals go even better with the melancholy soundtrack that more often than not is more ambient than it is prevelant. This may sound like a bad thing but i found both to work in tandem to create an immersive & beautiful experience that pulled me in for several hours at a time. Sadly this immersion got broken several times by some technical issues (which i'll get into later) and some rough translation in the dialogues. The writing (or it's translation?) left much to be desired, often being obtuse, weird or outright confusing. This made the story hard to follow as well as create several moments where items or mechanics were unclear such as the spite you acquire by killing enemies, which is somehow tied to the cycles of the moon. These mechanics while not only poorly described feel counter intuitive. The spite is your reward for playing well, giving you powerups as you rack up kills, however dying not only takes these boons away but also makes the moon more red, making enemies more powerful. Thus you're rewarded for playing well but then punished harder for failing? (On top of already losing your 'souls' until you reclaim them, as well as being sent back to the last checkpoint). This mechanic was supposedly integrated into the story but this was unclear.The technical issues also hamper the experience, it's not so much bugs at it is frequent stuttering which can happen at any time but most often during combat.  This often made me take damage i would've otherwise avoided and in some cases even cost me my life. This was all the more frustrating paired with the death system. These lag spikes also caused me to fail some jumps at times, especially when using the super dash you require over halfway through the game. This dash allows you to acces several new areas but actually made the game much less fun. You perform this dash by holding down the dodge button, however if a lag spike occurs at the same time, the game while count it as being held, even if it was only pressed for a short time. As the super dash has a windup animation and an ending animation, this caused me to take a lot of unnecesary damage and made combat much clunkier than it was before. There's also a handy equipable item that reduces damage taken at the cost of losing some movement speed. This is fine except for the fact that it also affects the super dash, so that you can't make the jump (as well as other normal jumps) without going into the menu and unequiping said item. You can then go into the menu again to re-equip but if you then fall (due to lag or otherwise) you'll have to do this process AGAIN. This often led to moments of frustration that did significantly hamper my experience.In the end the negatives aren't enough to detract from the smooth and satisfying combat that is prevalent throughout most of the game (if it doesn't lag out). The odd design choices such as moon cycles and super dash speed aren't that bad all things considered and the stutters can be fixed as well as additional optimization work. It's not a perfect game by any means but the core gameplay and presentation are so good that i'd be a shame to give this game a pass. It's an easy recommendation for any action platformer/soulslike fan that isn't afraid of a challenge or anyone looking for a game with great combat. Well worth the price and time investment! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm only a few hours into the game, so this is an early impression review I'll probably go back and elaborate on later. The game has been pretty cool so far! The combat feels very nice and works very well, and my criticisms are relatively minor. I also like how dense individual areas are for what you have to explore. I think at each mirror I've unlocked 2 or 3 shortcuts forward (for a total of like 3 to 4 paths forward from a mirror). To comment on difficulty, this game is pretty hard and also not very nice to you if you die. I was fine through the first area until the first boss but now in the second area I'm dying a lot (curse all the ranged enemies). In terms of how often I'm dying and distance between like "checkpoints" (either new shortcut or new mirror checkpoint) the difficulty in the second area is lining up with like Sekiro for me (there's no rhythm parrying in this game though, this is just in terms of death count and distance between checkpoints). I have two points for constructive criticism right now:I think the game is punishing enough on death between the blood moons and losing the spite bonuses I'd personally prefer if we at least got to keep the weapon special attack bonus. Especially since the parry timing varies a lot between enemies and there's quite a bit of trial and error that naturally leads to dying. Losing the weapon special attack bonus after one death with no cheapish way to get it back especially hurts, and unless you're a pro at this game you're gonna lose this bonus quickly all the time.For my second one I'd actually rate this as a design flaw. Thanks to other reviews I've seen it's possible to lock yourself out of being able to cast a spell if you upgrade it too much since the ichor cost increases per upgrade. I've had to hold back and intentionally not upgrade any spells yet due to this. I really think there should be some mechanic to address/prevent this. I can think of: Add Ichor upgrades to the spell skill tree, add ability to refund a spell upgrade, have the spell automatically downcast to the previous level(s) if your maximum ichor is too low to cast it, add explicit labels for your maximum ichor and the ichor cost of each spell, add a warning that the upgrade will push the spell past your maximum ichor, and I'm sure there's other ways I haven't thought of.But anyways two minor gripes and otherwise having fun so far! I'll update this further when I actually get farther in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this was an excellent Metroidvania worth all the time and money spent on it. The combat is amazing, the boss fights are outstanding and extremely fun, the art is gorgeous, and the game is challenging but very rarely feels frustrating. The best thing about Moonscars is the combat. You have most of Irma's abilities right at the start, and it's extremely fluid to use a mix of dashes, parries, light attacks, heavy attack, and magic to flit around enemies and in and out of danger. The game presents you with a skill tree of magic abilities you can unlock and upgrade as you play, as well as a bunch of amulets you can find and purchase that provide various buffs. It's a fairly simplistic customization set but does allow you to tweak the combat to your style and to adapt to the levels around you, which in a couple places is a near necessity. The bosses are extremely fun, most of them I beat within a couple attempts but the harder ones required more time to figure out the attack patterns and how to perfectly dodge. Other comments complained about the run backs, I'm not sure if the game was patched but for no boss was the run back even worth mentioning, the longest one took about 7 seconds from respawn to arena.The art is stunning as well, with the gorgeous low saturation pixel art style persisting through the game. The animations are smooth and visually pleasing and really make the game pop despite the low color art. The music is good and while it never feels lacking its not one of the shining features of the game. The story is good in my opinion. Ultimately Moonscars is not a story game and if you're looking for a game that gives a story in a clear way with lots of cutscenes and the like, it's not that. The story takes place in a ruined medieval world that has been destroyed by some calamity in which the "clayborn", some form of artificial life, turned on their human creator and humanity in general. As you play through the game you learn more about the events leading up to the game and the characters involved. Not everything is answered and it's told in a way that really makes you piece it all together, while you're left understanding the whole story at the end it does leave you wanting for more to be fleshed out in the world. The concepts are fascinating and I would enjoy more games in the same setting, but really it is not a story game. The game isn't perfect. The mana system is incredibly tight until the final quarter of the game and as such magic feels like a pretty pointless weapon to use except where it is required. The spells feel powerful and satisfying but you can use them once every few fights and then you're waiting again. Additionally, a lot of the spells feel like graphically different versions of themselves and the variety is a little lacking. The amulet system has the same problem, where you end up using about 4 of the whole collection plus 2 that help a lot in specific situations. The rest aren't worth equipping because you end up considerably weaker without the best amulets equipped.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugged to no ends... Avoid at all cost, there are no more updates it seems and the game is filled with bugs among other things. The maps allows you to get out of bounds for some reasons and then you do not die, you're just stuck there... Only possible option is to restart a new game -_- Sometimes quitting and restarting works but where I'm at, nope !The game has some frustrating mechanics, too many flying monsters when air combat is not great at all and many abilities are just made for ground combat. The story is confusing, not interesting and you quickly want to dismiss it because it's not clear and you don't understand what npc are talking about most of the time. (a story about flesh and clay, a sculptor which you try to find and his cat because you forgot everything). NPC are also annoying calling you "poor thing" all the time.There are other strange mechanics with the moon and enemies but it's all too confusing! Also, you do not feel like you really gain powers, when you "level up" you only gain new powers which aren't all that great so each time you die and said powers cost wayyyyyyy too much, they won't allow you to cast them much. You gain strength by getting orbs scattered here and there but the entire system is not great at all and there is also a small level up system which you have to start all over again each time you die.Your "build" mainly consist of 2 powers, one special attack which you can randomly change and 3 amulets among a plethora you will find... said amulets don't feel great either safe for a few (at least to the point I got before I got stuck out of bound)All in all, it's pretty sad, animation is great, music sounds good (depressing souls-esque kind), sound design is also good, the combat generally speaking feels good and there are some great things about the game, you can feel the love that was put in during development. Unfortunately, all those good parts are quickly erased each time you get frustrated by one of  the above.
