_childDocuments_.review: Hard games are fun because they build up to being hard.  But, for this game, 20 minutes in you have every button of the controller being used with basically no space to practice your combat moves or abilities.  Here's a fireball, here's one wall to try it on and we're going to run you out of ichor immediately so you can't practice it again until you've killed a bunch of stuff.  Here's a SUPER slow to build up attack, but you get no practice with this one, so figure out how to use it on your own.  Oh, and we're immediately going to start throwing swarms of enemies that contain mobs that can take 50% of your health if you don't parry perfectly or dodge every other attack.  And when you die, watch your resources disappear.  It's just 2D darksouls, because everything needs to be punishing and darksouls lately...Death is punishing, resetting from death is boring, the fights are boring as while you have ten buttons only three actually do anything useful most of the time but sometimes you'll need to figure out how to get a forth PITA to use button in there.  Oh, and don't actually attack the mobs or they'll attack back and hit harder than you because you can't parry if you're in an animation.  Go forbid you get into an attack chain (because you think spamming attack is fun but we don't want that here...).  The game piles on and on and even lets you break your build the bad way so you can no longer use ichor abilities... Beautiful art, looks fun in the trailers but that's because all of the trailers are perfectly timed.  I gave it some time, took a break came back to it, but ended up putting it down quickly three times as it has really fundamental game design issues.If you want to play a fun version of this game (and you haven't already) with better art then pick up a copy of Ori.  It's very hard, but not punishing, and it's also very satisfying when you complete something.  Death is expected often but you restart near where you last died and you get to try again and again quickly so you can learn quickly.  More so, the rooms you get power ups in are designed to show you how to use them and give you a space to practice with them instead of just one enemy.  It also builds slowly so you have time to learn how your powers work together and has rooms specifically built to teach you to start using abilities together so you get a nice natural progression toward good muscle memory.This game has none of that and so it will be loved by a very niche hardcore crowd that will be very loud about how everyone else is wrong.  But, it will still be terribly designed. So this, this is just mediocre at best.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a lover of Metroidvanias then this game is for you.  Presentation: The pixel graphics are just absolutely stunning and the music has a kind of sombre feel to it that fits the tone of this game very well. Combat:  The combat can be challenging some times but it is for the most part absolutely fair so long as you are competent at dodging and parrying.  Parrying is a must in this game as Grey Irma, the protagonist does not do a lot damage by default at least not at the beginning.  By parrying an enemy's attack that can be parried (they'll glow red) Grey Irma will do a devastating counter attack that will either completely destroy or significantly reduce an enemy's health.  In my opinion the window to parry an attack is fairly reasonable so even if you're not very experienced with such mechanics you should do OK.Criticisms:  I think that Moonscars is fairly short for a Metroidvania.  Even though that I was taking my time I still managed to platinum the game within two playthroughs which was just over 24 hours game time.Another downside is that there is no new game plus which is a shame as it would have been nice to play from the beginning using abilities that you can't get till mid or late game.All in all I'd give this game a 4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: Hilariously, the bad reviews seem to be a "get good" issue. I'm normally not the person to be saying something like that but it's truly the case for a lot of these reviews. Let me tell you, Moonscars is not as difficult as Blasphemous,(giving you something to compare it to)  so I have no idea what those people were thinking coming into this game if they liked soulslike/metrovania type games.I'm about 3/4's through the game and I have to say this is WELL worth the money. There's nothing to fancy going on here but if you were itching for a Metrovania rogue light ( I say rogue light due to the buff system, as you kill more enemies you get to choose a buff such as crit increase or health power increase etc , this resetting as you die) this is the game for you. The story is interesting and the dialogue is organic. A few things that I wish were better. They parry system feels a bit to difficult to use, so most of the time I felt dodging and character overlapping helped evade attacks more often than parrying. Ichor (magic) should be expanded on. It actually feels good to use when your able to. You have to balance using Ichor for magic and healing, and while Black Mermaid did a pretty damn good job balancing these out. I feel that maybe spells could have cost a little less so you could use them more often. Even if that means lowering the effectiveness. Only a few spells felt worth using. Enemies are pretty quick to attack you once in range and your spells have a limited range to them  and have long cast times so I felt the most bang for buck was using poison blade and doppelganger spell. Most projectiles just didn't feel worth it has you had to stand still for a long time to cast and dealt subpar damage.Sound track. As someone who writes themselves, I was hoping for something more than atmospheric music. I would 110% bet if this game had a more memorable soundtrack to it, it would feel way more immersive, memorable and personable. If you're someone like me and loves soulslike difficulty games, this will be right up your alley. It's not the most difficult game, it takes some practice to get the pace and memorize enemy attacks (no more than any other) but after you do, the combat feels very rewarding.Hope Black Mermaid further expands on the ideas here for their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: So my initial review of Moonscars was basically a giant neon sign to the effect of "releasing a game without controller rebinding options is a bad idea" for which I received so much hate I actually turned the comments off. Slow clap for the Steam community and a solid ♥♥♥♥ me for trying. If you're wondering where all the jester reacts came from, it's because some people are so insecure in their opinions that someone saying "I loved everything about this game but had to refund it because it didn't have accessibility options" is the same as saying "I hate this game and everyone who played it is a dumb pleb with no taste and probably jerks of to MLP porn"Anywho, now the devs patched in controller rebinding and I can confirm I enjoy the game. Bit of an anticlimax really. The art is fantastic, and the atmosphere is the tops. It's oppressive, bleak, nihilistic and overall a joy to hurt myself with.The story is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ impenetrable, but I'm pretty sure it's supposed to be. But who cares about story when the atmosphere is this good. I would say there are maybe too many mechanics all interacting, but then again it all feels pretty optional. I was two bosses deep before I realised you could upgrade basic spells, and three bosses deep before I figured out how to equip charms. This isn't really a bad thing tho as it lets you chose how invested you personally want to be in the details of it all.I feel like me enjoying Moonscars was pretty inevitable tho, as it's just Salt and Sanctuary with a teeny bit of Blasphemous sprinkled over for flavour. It certainly does enough to feel original and the combat really rubs me up the right way. Smooth, impactful, intuitive... uhm, probably some other buzzwords marketing types like. Dynamic?In summary, this is such a classic example of one small oversight letting down a whole project. I would have loved for this to be my day one review, but I am happy the devs cared enough to go back and add this feature. Y'all did a great job on this one and I'm so happy to see it live up to the potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I sometimes bounce off of 2D Soulslikes (Salt & Sanctuary, Grime).  This game gives you infinite wall jump and air dash right out of the gate though, which was promising.  The combat, controls and movement all feel good.  Knocking or luring enemies into spikes is very satisfying. The level design is also fun, with large enough areas containing different little ways to go.The biggest issue for this game is a sin it deliberately committed by painting everything in black/grey/white/red.  Oppressive to look at, and you always feel like you're in the same place - areas inevitably lack character and variety as a result of this decision.  This colour scheme also applies to the inventory screen, making items difficult to distinguish from one another.When you open your map, you are always forced to move your cursor out of the way, it impedes your vision.  I had to read some dialogue here and there to understand some of the games systems - some of which felt unnecessary.I felt like I could have continued playing, but can't see how acquiring more spells and abilities or exploring more areas that look the same could in any way get me past the things that are holding the experience down for me.I'd leave a neutral review, but considering it didn't work for me, fairest is probably not too. _childDocuments_.review: It was an ok game for me. It has some good and bad thingsThe grafics are just beautiful, this painted like pixelart in the animations, the pixelart in the areas overall, just amazing. Combat is kinda meh to nice, with many enemys it can be hard t stay alive at times, yetyou got a bunch of tools to work out how you deal with them. And attacks have indicators, also showing you if you can parry them. It´s also not too punishing since healing is superfast and the way to heal you can also get really easy, on the other hand that makies bosses quite easy since you can realy much just heal against them 90% of the time.Speaking of, enemy variety is nice, the game isn´t that big so you don´t need a ton of enemys. They get stronger in later areas, gain shields and through another mechanic get sometimes stronger. Some are easier while others can be quite scary to run by.Bosses are a bit hit or miss. Tbhere are several spots where you thing "well I wait for the double jump". But then you get it: The upgraded dash needed for those things. Even tho it feels a bit weird to use it helps travveling through the map quicker and it´s not just the "get double jump now explore" ability with I like.Since the game is short I would wait for a discount but it´s worth a try. It didn´t had me fully hooked all the time but it was still fun. 10h for I think a 100% playthrough not all achievementsEdit: Last areas music really hits good with the atmosphere, nice one there.And I wish that you could sort your inventory, looking on every charm reading what it does isn´t that niceAnd the second last area is a bit arena heavy wich is a bit boring

_childDocuments_.review: Ended up beating the game on console, but I figured I could give a useful review anyway. Overall, it was a pretty fun game. The combat is straightforward, what it was advertised. Some enemies are harder to dodge than others, but they're all doable. I will say though, I felt the difficulty was a bit imbalanced. If you're playing with a full moon (the default), the combat is a bit too easy. I'm not a pro myself, but by dashing correctly, I easily beat all the bosses (except the last two) on my first try. There's also a limited variety of enemies (a dozen, maybe two), so it can get a bit boring. By the end of it, I forgot about dodging and just dashed/jumped over enemies. That being said, if you die I'm certain conditions, you'll get a blood moon. This makes enemies (and the game) a lot harder, to the point where even common enemies can two-shot you, even with damage-reducing buffs. You can get rid of the moon sometimes, but you have to use limited resources to do so.The story itself was pretty interesting, but complicated. It uses a lot of made-up terminology that it doesn't explain right away. One thing I'll say, when the game hints that you can sell *certain items* to *a certain woman,* do it. It'll give you lore about the game. As for the game itself, it's fine overall, but there are a few things that can get annoying/could've been better. For example, there will be mini-cutscenes with NPCs giving dialog, but instead of walking on/off screen or moving when they "preform an action," they just stand still, talk, the screen fades to black, and they disappear. Other than that, the game will prompt you to interact with some things sometimes, and well, sometimes it'll do what it's meant to, but sometimes it won't. And not in an "I can't interact with this/I'm missing something," kind of way. More in an "it says <Press X to talk>, I'm pressing X, but the character won't even grunt and dismiss me, it doesn't work. Also, be cautious about advancing too far too quickly, specifically when it comes to sidequests. Some disappear if you accidentally kill a boss too soon, so be cautious about area-specific quests. Try to fully explore an area before you fight its boss.All in all, it's a fun game, cool story, decent gameplay, but there's a reason it's not winning any Game Of The Year awards. You can definitely have fun with it, but don't expect Super Metroid or Symphony Of The Night level metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game.  Combat overall was fun, but enemies are very repetitive which got tiresome by the end.  Similar magic/healing as hollow knight, in that you generate mana through hitting enemies and then use it for spells/healing.  Bosses keep you engaged but are pretty easy, didn't die to any of them.  Story was interesting enough, it was pretty unique and clear enough to follow while still leaving some things vague enough for theorizing.  In terms of the metroidvania aspect, the game is fairly linear and you only get one significant upgrade throughout the game which is a movement upgrade that lets you access a couple areas previously inaccessible, and that upgrade isn't really usable in combat so the combat at the start of the game is the same as the combat at the end of the game.  The game had a minor roguelike element in that as you killed enemies you'd level and choose an upgrade out of 3 options, up to I think 4 or 5 levels, and these were lost on death.  There was also a system that encouraged you to swap your secondary weapon from time to time, this was mildly annoying because you get benefits for swapping weapons but I really only wanted to use the weapon I liked.Overall I say the game is decent because the game does combat, platforming, and story all fine, but it doesn't do anything particularly good, so while I had fun with it it's not something I would replay or that will stick in my memory years down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: A great game with really good feeling combat, nice visuals and art and a good story. Would totally recommend it. I hope the developers get around to bring us more of thisGood things:- The Combat is the main star of the show here and it feels really good. If i had to compare it to other games it feels like something between dead cells and blasphemous, though a lot more like dead cells, which i personally love. No contact damage with enemies makes the combat feel great and allows you to just to in, though certain enemies do get harder to fight the closer you are to them. Enemies have clear attacks that show you with either a red or blue blink if you can parry them or not. So while things get a bit hectic with a few enemies around, theres never a feeling of chaos. - Bosses are also very fun. Especially the last bossfight was a highlight for me. They all are very fair without any attacks/moves that cant be countered.- The Story is nice. Its being told pretty directly so you wont really miss it. It dips into some pretty deep topics that were quite enjoyable to think about. Personally i feel like there is potential to flesh out some motives more like the clayborn and humans, their flaws etc. Giving the players more choice to act on their morals and thoughts about the topics handled could be great, but its understandable that it would be a lot of effort and time. - Backtracking for doors or obstacles you previously couldnt do without some ability is super nice, since these things get automatically marked on the map, without any need of manually placing markers. A much better system than giving the player only the ability to set custom markers (which you can still do) and expecting them to write down somewhere which marker means what or something the like. While the map isnt huge anyway, its still a neat feature i enjoyed- The playtime of around 8 hours feels pretty good. Things dont get stale, but if it took more time, some more enemies would have been needed. Personally i like shorter games as well that can just be finished in a week or weekend if youre really into them. This is just a solid package for a good price and it doesnt drag things out.Neutrals:- The game isnt super difficult. Ive died a bunch of times but especially if you keep it at the default difficulty, its really not awfully hard. The nicely telegraphed attacks might contribute to this but i never found it to be stupidly easy either. Healing is quick as well, so even in most combat situations you can sustain yourself a bit. This is somewhat offset by the fact that you cant take a lot of hits (at least on the harder difficulty). The situations you cannot sustain yourself are pretty spicy and appreciated. Personally i think i would have enjoyed more of these situations where enemies are plentiful and dont allow you to heal. Though this is very much a personal preference. - Most of the music and locations arent overly unique. There are spaces that look stunning and areas are clearly different but i suspect you dont have the same uniques in areas as in other games like Hollow Knight or Blasphemous. I think this works for the setting the game goes for, which is the reason i dont note it as a negative. Though i do feel like this area has more potential. Areas like the Apex and the Depths are pretty cool. More of those perhaps! I think theres also great potential in creating memorable moments in the story and supporting them with great music. Whats currently in the game isnt bad, i just think theres potential to make things even better.- The roguelite spite bonuses (gain a bonus with enemies killed, loose on death) are interessting and speed up combat but you will feel a bit worse when you die. Its not an issue where you need to grind up levels before you fight a boss, so thats good but i felt this system was nice but perhaps a bit lackluster. In my opinion it could be great to have it be optional but the more perks you choose, the more enemies you fight or the harder they get. You dont just become stronger but combat becomes more intense. I feel like this could suit the game well if executed nicely. Bad things:- There are a lot of doors that you need abilities/witchery to destroy. But only some of the witchery can break doors (projectiles) whereas others cant (like decoys, summons). This leads to either always changing abilites or just keeping one ability that can break these doors always in a slot. I would love to see these things to just become doors that cost Ichor/Mana to open instead of being tied to an ability. Theres many cool abilities and this just reduces you basically to one slot of free choice which i think is a shame cause the abilities are genuinly fun and different. Though this is way better than the way Blashpemous 1 handled that, where you had to switch relics because you only have 3 slots and theres no logical reason why they couldnt just all be active since they do not grant any advantage in combat.

_childDocuments_.review: It's short and conсise experience deeply rooted in its restricted palette and grim aesthetics. I'm not a fan of the overused "dark" setting, but it works surprisingly well in this case with the characters interesting enough to not skip dialogues, and the plot having a nice and original enough twist on basically the same old story.The combat is pretty good with several specials and many spells to choose from all bringing some slight variations to tactics. That being said the progress balance, though, is pretty bad: starting ok, then difficulty spiked considerably to end up being none at all in the late game (though I didn't use some items that are meant to spice it up a little bit). The bosses (in the original release being pretty hard and at times very frustrating for me) got nerfed with later updates so that even me (generally just not good at games and especially in metroidvanias' boss battles) killed almost every one of them on a first try.With some polishing and bugfixing brought to the game with the later updates it's now more user-friendly (though, I've still encountered some minor bugs and haven't got one achievement (the cat one) due to NPC not spawning in its place) and overall smoother experience. Definitely worth a purchase if you've got around 10 hours to kill and are in the mood for some map-exploring in the glum and dreary world.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Level Design: The feeling of the map, secrets, different kinds of parkour elements are great. They are some weird jumps but everything is beautiful and well designed. 10/10Enemies: Very verstaile range of enemies but some has some has annoying moveset and all of them repeat their kind of cycle of movements. Like: Jump Slash->Slash->Jump Slash->Slash and no other moves(For one enemy). Even if you are infront of them they still do the jump slash. And Sometimes some enemies think or maybe it's the special effect of the stronges ones but sometimes after a moveset cycle went down there is no "rest" between the cycles and just kills you because all the other enemies have a 0.5-1sec rest between their cycles. 6/10Bosses: The worst part of the game sadly. Bosses doesn't have much health and have limited moveset but now in a big space so you can easly dodge most of them or just stand in on place so they miss you. Positive thing that the hitbox is very good and when there is an explosion or other effect it doesn't randomly damages you.Unfortuntly they are still boring and you can just tank and heal you way to victory.The Only good boss (For me) is Sweet Wanda. 4/10Collectibles: There are many collectibles and one of them can only be collected when you died and didn't defeat a boss or healed yourself at the mirror. Beside that they are many different kind and they are good and fun. 9/10Gameplay: Very Solid while you have limited moveset in the way of only the sword 3 light strikes and one big if you hold down the attack. They feel great and look good and are very fluid. You have spells which are good but not necesarry only in special cases.The Special attacks do look cool but they are slow, they can deal some good dmg but I haven't really used them beside the Harpoon because of the range. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Not a Blasphemous substitute by any means, or any of the hard-hitting titles in the genre for that matter, but Moonscars is an engaging package. It doesn't shake up the genre with new mechanics -- it has all the trappings of current Metroidvania type games: 1. Fluid Combat: Light & Heavy attacks are topped up by a limited stock of Special Weapon Attacks that you can brandish after chaining a couple of attacks. Aerial juggling is somewhat possible allowing the character to attack two time in the air (which can be used as a movement tool) There is decent dodge and parry mechanic, guided with color coded animations for Parry-able and Unblockable attacks. 2. Decent Character customization: Your combat set is augmented by accessories and spells, ranging from Projectiles, Traps, Summons, Damage-Over-Time Effects and the like. The game has several currencies you can spend to give your run a bit of a boost until you kiss dirt. The "Leveling" mechanic is pretty unique as it grants you some select-able buffs, however, once you've hit the cap an in-game difficulty mode is flipped on -- monster become stronger (though this could have been a bigger challenge if certain patterns changed) but with the benefit of dropping more currency.3. Chiaroscuro Art Style and minimalist sound production: the game has a pretty good art direction playing on Blacks, Whites & Grays only broken by streaks and highlight of Red from Clothing and Gore. There is little to say about the music -- gloomy, foreboding, it's pretty mellow with the exception of boss fights. 4. Story: Nothing to write home about, really, it's your typical Humans-Playing-As-Gods-Gone-Wild. Think of it as a dark fantasy take on Cloning, maybe. I don't know. It gets confusing who's who and what's what. Again, nothing to fancy or off the beaten path. Would probably say get it on Sale, pick it up if you've already bathe in the guts of other titles under the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, waiting for the second part!!! If you liked the 2D Castlevania and Metroid, Bloodstained, Ender Lillies, Vigil, Dandara, Enderand, HunterX, Haiku The Robot THAT'S THE GAME FOR YOU!It's not so difficult like Blasphemous, Hollow Knight and Salt and Sanctuary and as for me this is a HUGE PRO!

_childDocuments_.review: The story is cryptic but you start to pick up what's going on as you progress through the game. I sure as heck didn't know what was going on, but it started to click together a bit as I went through. The one thing I did not like about the story telling was how dark it was and the text was difficult to read. Maybe that is just me.Not gonna lie, the game is hard. It's unforgiving. I spent a good half hour working one of the bosses, eventually kicked their butt, and then immediately died from some trash mobs that weren't even moon starved in the next room. It has a Dark Souls mechanic where you lose all your collected bone powder when you die, but you can pick it back up if you manage to get back to it (unless you die on the way). The parry mechanic only works during specific cues, and many attacks force you to dodge... yet if you can land that parry, it makes the fights so much easier, especially as there is a trinket you can equip that will assist in getting help back if you are successful.When it comes to magic, I think people will tend to pick those that fit their play style and keep with it. I played around, and only one spell seems situation based (needed to get through walls), but I tended to keep with the Chain Boulder for flying enemies and Poison. Using a decoy or a doppelganger for a boss can give you valuable time to learn their attack moves.You need to explore and you need to think: the map will open as you go along but it does NOT show collectibles or tell you where you haven't been in those open space and does NOT show secrets (far as I can tell). It doesn't hold your hand. I spent an hour lost because part of the map opened and I assumed I had already been there. Whoops. As difficult as it was at time, I enjoyed it. It just goes to show that you are a clayborne: you were made without a choice, and yet you delve forward in search of the truth and learning what – who – you are.*** I do want to note that since I saw it in one of the first negative reviews: if you get stuck somewhere on the map, open it and there is a button shown in the upper right corner that will automatically teleport you back to your last warp spot. You don't have to restart the game.*** Oh, and you need to take off the Stone amulet to use Super Dash once you get it (you're too heavy if you have it equipped)
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: Nice metroidvania with retro taste in pixel art, in a super dark setting. If you like dark atmospheric environments, this is for you. _childDocuments_.review: Recently played Ender Lilies because I wanted to get back into Metroidvania games, and this one stood out to me because of the artstyle and combat seemed interesting. Once I started playing I was instantly hooked. There's solid depth to the combat: weak attacks, charged attack, aerial attacks, downward smash attack, a choice between 5 secondary weapons that can be switched out throughout your playthourgh, and a decent selection in skills as well. Parrying an enemy grants you iframes and you hit multiple enemies making rewarding and the response it quite good. The challenge is managing your ichor (mana) because with this you heal and also use it for your skills, it fills up as you hit enemies. So if you're getting hit all the time you need to know when to heal and when to go on the offense, although the game pushes towards aggressive play. Character customization is quite plain, you put on a few pendants that can push towards a certain playstyle, but it's straightforward. If you've played Souls games, the questlines are just like it. I would've liked a couple more bosses for sure, but for how short the game is it kinda makes sense. I loved playing Megaman games and this one does justice for the genre, overall I'd give it an 8.5/10. I recommend it to anyone seeking a challenge in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled upon this game when it was first released. I can really appreciate the effort coming through to round out and improve the game after community feedback and major patch updates. Great job devs, this is a special game. This is exactly what I love: high risk-reward parry-focused tight-fluid-precision combat.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s hard to stand out in the enormous crowd of souls-likes that came out in recent years. Your character is responsive, the animations are super smooth and the combat flows impeccably. Plus, it’s got a distinctive art style and the enemy and level design can hold their ground. If you've got a few hours to spare, Moonscars is well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is similar to Blasphemous, but I’d say it leans even more into the Dark Souls inspiration than Castlevania. Dark, moody, and gorgeous to look at.About the only thing I’d say was not too great about this game is the story. I began the game knowing nothing about the story, and I finished the game knowing very little. I guess that’s remarkable in itself..Either way, I thoroughly enjoyed this game and I recommend it. _childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and short. Really good combat. Nice dashes and parry's. Wasn't super hard, felt challenging at times but I had very few deaths. I think people talking about it being really hard didn't realize that when the moon is ravenous enemies do much more damage or they just weren't clicking with how to play.Accessory slots are a bit too limited. Your limited to 3 and I stuck with more crit damage and get ichor upon taking damage the entire time.Healing is like how you do it in hollow knight but very quick and snappy. Hit stuff to get ichor, use that to heal. But you don't have to choose between magic and healing which is awesome. Using a spell leaves the bar with tainted ichor and you can still use that to heal. Leveling up a spell does make it cost more to cast and there isn't a way to reverse. I purposely kept a few spells low level so they stayed low cost. Honestly I liked this game way more than hollow knight.It's not a perfect game by far but it was 15 hours well spent.Spite mechanic is interesting. You get buffs for killing more enemies without dying. but I basically stuck with trying to get the same combos each time. It might be better if you could just fully choose what you want rather than picking from 2 random choices. FYI the heal option for it is single use and still counts towards the max spite level so it's a pretty bad choice most of the time. But you could save it for an emergency I guess but like there is also a 25% extra heal, so like that made more sense to me to get.Regarding spite, don't feel like you need to grind each time you die. It will come naturally as you explore. While it is a nice boost, the healing boost is probably going to be what you feel the most and I usually got that with level 1 or 2 which is super quick to get back.It's metrodvania but there's really only one ability that you learn to progress. Everything else is basically a key. There really isn't much hidden or anything in the way of upgrades. Most of the time I found a secret wall it was just some bone dust (souls/xp) The actual health, ichor, and damage boosts are all stuff you'd find just casually filling out the map and there isn't really a reason to backtrack unless you want to get the earrings for a quest/item which are only available during a ravenous moon. The map layout is decent and marks everything important automatically. The map loops back on itself nicely with shortcuts too.If the cat wants milk and you want the achievement for giving it to him do it in the order you find him. I somehow missed the milk the second time he asks thinking it was elsewhere and did the 3rd area he asks first and then was unable to give the milk in the second area he asks for it.There are 2 areas that specifically go against previously established rules for pits and spikes. Normally a fall has ground below and spikes don't instant kill. There is an area late game and one early where you just die and it looks like there could be stuff below.Being able to toggle more spells would be nice. You can only hotkey two at a time. Being able to freely swap secondary weapons would also be great. I only really liked the gauntlets and hammer. I guess the point of some of this is to encourage playing a little different and to shake stuff up but your gonna find your favorites with everything really quick and likely stick with it.Story is super confusing at first but evens out and makes more sense later. It's not the best story but I guess it works enough. I understand it more than most dark souls games at least.Overall if your into short metroidvania style games this is really solid if you can forgive some weird but overall un-harmful game design choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Still fun, despite doing its best to not be fun. God awful controls. Clunky unintuitive UI. Auto climbing ledges/ladders-where every single other game I've ever played with these have you press up before the character would do so. One of the worst ladder climb animations I've ever seen lol. Annoying dialogue style and word choices. To ramp up difficulty, the only change is how much health and damage enemies do, with later enemies able to 2-shot the player. _childDocuments_.review: Introduction:Ladies and gentlemen, space explorers, and cosmic wanderers, get ready for a mind-bending journey through the universe of emotion with 'Moon Scars.' This indie gem takes you on a breathtaking trip beyond the stars, blending deep storytelling with innovative gameplay mechanics that leave an indelible mark on your gaming soul.Graphics and Atmosphere:Moon Scars delivers a visual feast, inviting players into a celestial dreamscape where stars twinkle like distant memories. The art direction is nothing short of stunning, with each celestial body and alien world exquisitely crafted. Whether you're floating in the haunting beauty of a gas giant or soaring over the jagged terrain of a lunar landscape, every frame feels like a piece of cosmic art.Storytelling:At the heart of Moon Scars is a narrative that pierces the veil of space and time, exploring themes of loss, love, and existentialism. You assume the role of Alex, a lonely astronaut on a mission to recover his shattered memories scattered throughout the cosmos. The storytelling is both poignant and surreal, weaving a tale that challenges your perception of reality and leaves you pondering life's deepest questions.Gameplay:Moon Scars introduces a novel gameplay mechanic - gravity manipulation. As Alex, you have the power to control gravitational forces, altering the environment and solving intricate puzzles. This ingenious mechanic adds layers of depth to the gameplay, making every moment of exploration an intellectual delight.Emotional Resonance:The emotional depth of Moon Scars is its crowning achievement. As you navigate through a universe filled with memories and metaphors, you'll feel a profound connection to Alex's journey. The game masterfully uses its mechanics and storytelling to tug at your heartstrings, reminding you that, even in the vast emptiness of space, the human experience is universal.Sound and Music:Moon Scars' ethereal soundtrack is the sonic equivalent of a wormhole to another dimension. It's an auditory masterpiece that perfectly complements the game's otherworldly atmosphere. The haunting melodies and celestial soundscape immerse you deeper into the narrative, heightening the emotional impact of each revelation.Conclusion:Moon Scars is not just a game; it's a transformative experience that transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming. It's a symphony of art, storytelling, and gameplay that leaves an indelible mark on your gaming soul. It will make you contemplate the universe, your place in it, and the memories that define you. _childDocuments_.review: Nowhere near as hard as its reputation would suggest, and I personally really enjoyed its mechanics with the exception of losing your spite levels upon death, since all that means is you farm spite levels again before a boss if you want to be fully prepared which doesn't really add depth and another progression layer should have taken its place. Other than that I love Moonscars and it feels excellent to play.I especially enjoy the ichor mechanic with how it encourages spell use mixed in with melee. I also enjoy a lot of the perks you can get and how they can interact to make powerful builds, or give you abilities like a second dash in a row which even works mid-air. I wish levels had more interesting loot to find more often, since most items you pick up are tiny amount of the game's currency.Moonscars seems like it is a lot better now than when it first released, and I admire the devs efforts to update it with meaningful changes and additions. Please consider playing it, especially if you enjoy Blasphemous.

_childDocuments_.review: A short, challenging Metroidvania with a grimdark aesthetic, and art style to match... Moonscars is an o.k. game.I read a lot about the brutal difficulty of this game, and while it's challenging--with a particular toughness from midgame and onward's enemy combination of aerial and ground foes--it's... really not that bad. I'm a veteran of the game type, and this is easier than a Souls game. I actually died (unintentionally) very few times throughout the game, and you're given tools to deal with the various challenges. While Spite levels are a little tedious to grind, I ended up misplaying on the final boss and dying, and just finishing the game at 0 Spite levels (getting one in the final battle), and without the Statue Gemstone.This is a very short game, around 8-9 hours. If you really don't care about achievements or side quests, you can likely do it in 7, even semi-casually. I finished at just over 9 hours, but finished some side quests, including the big item collection one.Like most games of the genre, with a high a difficulty, this has a PARRY system. It was kind of annoying at first, but the game explains what attacks you can parry. There's a few that you can parry outside the system and still work. Parrying is semi-forgiving and fairly responsive, so you just need to learn the timing with practice. Once triggered, even against multiple enemies, you're invincible for the full animation, and you can equip a Gemstone that gives you substantial chunk of health on trigger (and Ichor on hit). I never used it on bosses or doppelgangers, though, favoring dodging--which also has very responsive i-frames.The 'special weapons' system is flashy, but most of them aren't that helpful. I am playing after the addition of the Scimitar, which is pretty useful for a couple situations, but overall they weren't integral to gameplay. Likewise, there's a pretty expansive spell set that I used maybe a quarter of. Some of these likely would've been a lot better than what I rolled with for the game.There's also a big equipment system of Gemstones/charms, that you can equip up to 3 of (with some category restrictions). These modify and cater to your playstyle, buffing any facet of gameplay, be it offensive or defensive. These are the most impacting on gameplay, and they can get very powerful when stacking them towards one particular function. There's even 'fragile' ones that are stronger, but break on death, though you can acquire additional ones with some resources.--------------CriticismThe writing is... odd. While the story isn't anything wild--being akin to other games I've played, even in this genre, the thing that irked me the most is the painful vagueness of a lot of the explanations, and the dialogue of the main character. For some reason Irma changes her dialogue structure at random. It can vary from character to character she interacts with, or sometimes even in the same conversation. Given the strange and stilted way some characters talk it comes off like a localization quirk where words are missing in a sentence, and then not a few sentences later. I don't have a game to compare this to off the top of my head in that regard. I think it's just a mild lack of consistency for having the characters speak with an archaic bent to their dialect.If you walk away from this game confused about the overall plot... I wouldn't be surprised. As I mentioned, the vagueness is annoying. Things make a little more sense later, and some of the story elements become more direct, but at the end of the game I came away wondering why it's called 'Moonscars' after completing the main story. Though the moon is emphasized as a pretty big presence, I found it to be pretty insignificant in the actual lore of what was going on, rather than just the current events. Maybe I missed something, since I completely biffed The Cruel Queen questline, so I don't know if that held more significant about it.The artstyle is neat, but sometimes it's a little too smeared or messy in appearance, and I feel like some potential details in scenery can get lost. While I didn't have much trouble with finding secrets because they do have a distinct appearance from their surroundings, there were instances where finding vertical and corner secrets, especially behind foreground obstructions, was a bit too much. Hell, there was one I didn't even know about at all until I accidentally saw it in a video guide when I was lost about something. I found myself jumping into ceilings holding Up more than I would've liked, just guessing, and always wondering if I missed something in the foreground scenarios.There should probably be a trigger at the end to simply reveal all of the Earring icons on the map as I had to look up a detailed online map to find the last one, which was off in a detached, floating area that is otherwise impossible to know even exists with the rest of the map explored.One minor gripe with Parrying is that there's armored enemies later that you have to parry first, and then hit with a Witchery (spell) to break the armor. They're immune to damage until it's broken, but not stuns. The gripe is that there's no way to tell the armored ones apart from non-armored, and you can't always reliably break the armor before parrying the charging soldiers. This just slows you down, since Witcheries are pretty slow in my experience with using them. It's a minor complaint pretty late into the game.------------------Overall, the story is serviceable with some interesting elements, and the gameplay is solid. If you really like the grimdark aesthetic, and don't want a very long game, this might be for you. As far as the collections go, it wasn't a terrible grind for the Earrings. Most of them don't take too much effort to get, and the fast travel is good.If you do find the game too challenging there's a sort of "Easy Mode" through the Statue Gemstone. It will slow your movement and attack speed a little bit, but massively reduce the damage taken. I used this when doing early Earring collecting, specifically, since that can only take place on a red moon, it's not required to beat the game at all. I do get the concerns about it nerfing incoming damage too much, but I can promise you that dying is still very reasonable under a red moon. (It is required to remove this for making the Super Dash jumps later in the game, as the speed reduction impacts that. Otherwise, go nuts.)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Worth checking out, especially on a sale. A bit short at around 10-12 hours, but I've paid more for shorter and worse games. Combat is decent enough, but the bosses are by and large a bit too easy and spells are perhaps too powerful. They kind of break the game, and I wasn't even using any charms that enhance them. Spells are also annoying to swap between, you can have two equipped at a time and have to navigate the menu to swap them out, meaning I couldn't be bothered even trying new spells after the first few. Aerial enemies are annoying to fight, at least until you unlock the Chain Boulder spell, but the problem remains that aerial melee "combo" is ineffectual and annoying to use.You start out with a lot of regular metroidvania tools such as a dash and wall grab already unlocked, which I'm a bit split on. On one hand it's kinda nice and the game gets going pretty fast, but on the other hand it means there isn't much sense of progression other than increased hp/mana/damage numbers. As a result, the game feels fairly linear and there isn't all that much to find by going back to previously explored areas with new movement tools. I don't mind too much personally because I think backtracking and exploring is a pretty overrated aspect of metroidvanias, even in games that do it very well like hollow knight, but it's something to keep in mind if you like that kind of thing. Spells do require unlocking and I guess it's kind of on me that I mostly ignored them, but there also wasn't really any need to use more than two or three different spells, since they're all exclusively used in combat which as mentioned is already a bit on the easy side. Secondary weapons probably should have been permanent unlocks that you can swap between at any time, the current system for them is kind of clunky and doesn't exactly encourage experimenting with different ones.Story is fairly good, but it's hard to say anything concrete about it in a review without going into spoilers.The game has sort of a rudimentary leveling system where you get xp from defeating enemies, level up and choose one of three buffs that last until you die, and you can have up to five of these at a time. I wasn't a huge fan of this system, losing a full set of buffs is annoying, even though leveling up again is a reasonably quick process. One of the possible buffs is increased mana efficiency while healing, and this buff feels more or less like a tax because without it, healing takes an absolutely insane amount of mana in the late game. I also imagine that players that struggle with the boss fights might find it very annoying to lose the buffs to their first death, which increases the difficulty of the fight substantially unless you grind up new buffs, which is not advisable.Worst part of the game is probably the sidequests, because they almost require you to use a guide to complete. There's one that requires you to canvas the entire map for 77 collectable items, but they only show up after a certain point in the game and when a certain condition is met, which makes it extra annoying and you will have to do a lot of tedious backtracking if you choose to try to gather them all (I didn't). Another quest, where you're supposed to repeatedly find an item and give it to an NPC in most parts of the map apparently breaks if you do the zones out of order. Unintuitive sidequests kind of come with the genre I suppose, but like the pointless corpseruns back to boss fights, they're not a good part of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a hardcore Soulslike player. I appriciate good challange but will definitely pass on all the bullshittery that comes along with it. With this out of the way I can say that Moonscars is good and worthwile game. It is top notch on so many levels... Artstyle, story, worldbuilding, gameplay... Love it, despite  typical storytelling way of "You know nothing, deal with it, maybe we will explain everything later" (even despite some basic facts should be known to the character from the very start). _childDocuments_.review: INTRODUCTION:i'll start this review saying that you should not expect too much from this game. I say this because i have seen some review saying that this game is "too simple" or "repetitive", And this is said from people who liked the game. I think the reason behind this disappointment is that this game, especially in the beginning and the mid game, looks too good for what it actually is, and i say this in a good way. This game looks and feel like it's made by a team of dozens of people and with a decently good budget. But it's actually made by more or less five people, so they had to cut some corners, especially in the end game (of which i'll talk later). Despite this, i still think that the developers managed to deliver a complete game with a fun and challenging gamplay.To recap, I think this is a really good game, just don't expect a masterpiece, because it's easy doing so in the beginning.THE GOOD:the combat system is preaty simple, but that doesn't mean it's not fun. i especially love the parry system, which is very intuitive (when and where to use it) and rewarding, both in a gameplay way and in a dopamine way.I don't want to talk about the combat system too much because i don't want to spoil it for you. The only two major thing i am going to say is that, one: in this game you don't have a lot of health, so you die very easily if you are not careful, this is balanced by your ability to heal using icor, which you can gain by hitting and killing enemies. This makes for very intense fights, which i really enjoy.The second thing i am gonna say about the combat system is that it gets harder as you go on without dying. The game spawn's stronger enemies with bigger rewards, this makes for a dynamic difficulty, and the rewards make you want to keep your not-dead streak. In my opinion, they could have make the change in difficulty more extreme, or at least to cap at a higher point, but still, it's still a nice touch to keep you on your toes.The story and the lore is very interesting and original. It managed to keep my attention throughout the whole game. If you like dark fantasy and souls-like lore, i think you are really gona like it.And last but not least, the art style... i mean, just look at it, it's gorgeous!THE BAD:As i said above, the game is made by very few people, so they had limited resources and time. This is unfortunately very clear in the endgame, were the developers copy pasted enemies from previous areas. This plus the fact that you have probably discovered all the combat and exploration abilities a while ago makes for a bit of a repetitive experience, this is especially emphasized by the early-mid game experience, which gives you a lot of new enemies in a relative short period of time.While this is unfortunately very sad, i personally don't think this ruins the experience of the game, it all depends on whether you like the combat system or not, if you do, it's still fun, just not as fun as the previous areas.I THINK YOU SHOULD PLAY THIS GAME IF:-you like metroidvanias, but you don't need extremely new systems to enjoy it-you like pixel art-you like dark fantasy world and souls like lore (it's more dialog based here but you know what i mean)-you don't mind short games (about 20 hours)-you like hard games

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quite decent metroidvania. It takes inspiration from the likes of Dark Souls, Hollow Knight and, perhaps, Blasphemous. For the most part, the game has very nice combat mechanics. Enemies hit hard, but most of them aren't damage sponges, parrying (unlike what I've seen said in other reviews) is quite intuitive, and spells are beefy enough to speed up combat against tougher enemies. The balance is a bit iffy at points. For instance, most special attacks (slow attacks made with special weapons) deal pitiful damage for the risk, particularly when witchery (this game's name for spells) deals higher damage, and Ichor (MP) is rather easy to recover. Otherwise, the game is short and intense. The exploration is very straightforward, for the most part. I did very little backtracking. Most of what you find is Bone Powder (this game's souls), but equipment and permanent upgrades to health, damage and mp are also spread about. The equipment system consists of three accessory slots, which seem to be overlooked by most people having difficulty with bosses, as they allow for different kinds of builds.As for issues, my biggest gripe is some late areas, which have many enemies who can only be damaged by spells. I suppose it's one way to make the game challenging, but it just felt obtuse and restricting. It also made later bosses feel disappointing, because a random mob in the way could be more of a threat. The story is also odd, possibly a case of inspiration gone wrong. The basic gist is that a fella called the Sculptor created artificial beings, the clayborn, to deal with a revolt. The clayborn went out of control and he made perfected creatures called Pristines to eliminate the clayborn, but had ulterior motives. You play as Grey Irma, the last intact Pristine. There are many twists and turns, but most characters feel irritating, there is not a single person who is straightforward. Every line is a suggestion, a hint, or a piece of the puzzle. By the end, I was mostly uninterested because it felt more like an attempt to be opaque than a story. Luckily, the game is fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I think that if you liked games like Blasphemous and Unworthy, you will probably like this game. I did not finish every side quest, but based on how they look, I'd expect it to only take another 3-5 hours to wrap those sidequests up.I think the first 80% of this game felt better than most combat-focused metroidvanias I've played, but the final 20% or so highlighted the above issues and left a middling taste in my mouth. _childDocuments_.review: It's stuttery on my system for some reason but also the game itself just feels arduous to get through.Instead of feeling like i'm overcoming challenges with worthy foes, it feels like i'm manipulating irritating encounters to present themselves more favourably to me. Like jumping over and dashing through enemies to convince them to line up properly while simultaneously kiting and prioritising the annoying flying enemies.When the moon is angwy the game becomes genuinely difficult and exacerbates the issues. You have to flawlessly execute running around like a weirdo instead of flawlessly execute hectic combat. The spite system is a joke overall, i don't understand the incentive. Why would I take a series of borderline inconsequential buffs in one life to permanently inhibit the rest of the playthrough until I feel like wasting a gland on fixing it? The game isn't interesting enough for the moonlight secrets to be worth it, and none of the upgrades interest me at all so the increased currency drops don't seem cool either.I played with angwy moon for a little bit before the first boss, and all the enemies were doing so much damage it was crazy so i just assumed the game was super hard, but when I was losing patience with the boss I decided to sacrifice a precious gland to make the moon chillax again and then i beat the boss on the first try. So the damage scaling on angwy moon is completely unreasonable. There is no reason to engage with the spite system. But even without angwy moon the game is hard in a boring way. The map design just drags on and on and on, with enemy positions feeling spammy and not well considered. I'm sure the late game combat and controls will be good but the early game impression is very poor, good metroidvanias can sell themselves without the upgrades but this one just doesn't. The jump is low, the ladder positioning is stupidly precise, the wall climb looks janky, The special attacks are just way too slow and aren't useful enough to use which makes it feel insulting that the game thinks killing your doppleganger to get it back is some cool story feature. Ichor is a resource that is more efficiently used on healing than spells considering how many traps or horrible enemy positions you might be facing in the future. And the parry glitches out on some enemies.There isn't much of a soundtrack to speak of in the early game, the story is like next level cryptic, and the sound design is average. The vibes are there and the potential is there but it doesn't do it for me. I will continue giving it chances but I don't think I'll binge it like I have others. I got addicted to hollow knight, blasphemous, islets, tunic, ender lilies, haiku, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10It has a lot of "indie with a budget" qualities but is overall a solid metroidvania. Don't expect Hollow Knight, the contents are very limited.I see a few reviews complaining about the difficulty but the game feels relatively easy for me. There are some tough bosses but the thing about the game is that you don't run out of healing. You can just smack enemies to regenerate your ichor gauge and use it to heal yourself. The ichor gauge regenerates quickly as long as you are landing blows so as long as you are not getting hit twice as often as you're hitting enemies, your health shouldn't budge. It can feel too generous at times but I feel that the bosses remain challenging in spite of this so it works out.Also for an indie title it manages to keep the mood and settings stable. No quip, no fourth wall breaking dialogue. There's probably not a lot of stories to tell in the first place but the dialogues are very engaging, each character is a bit nuanced and the dialogues are very well written. I probably would have skipped all the dialogues in this game because they are inconsequential, but I didn't because I felt engaged.The level designs are okay. The game is not open-ended (you travel through biomes in a very linear fashion and even within biomes, where you go is more or less fixed) but the layouts are sufficiently complex to travel through without getting bored. Enemy variety is quite poor, you see all of them maybe 1/3 through the game, but they serve their purpose. Loot is bad and doesn't feel rewarding (you just get currency items)Character customization is terrible. The only thing that really feels impactful is your special attack, which is effectively 1 move that can't be used in the air. Spell choices don't feel meaningful and are just filler. There's also the temporary currency drop buff, which is meaningless because currency are (more or less) only spent on meaningless upgrades.Overall I was satisfied with the game. If you're expecting another Hollow Knight/Ender Lillies, you won't find it here, but there are so many bad metroidvanias on steam this deserve a call out for being one of the good ones.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 for me. I really enjoy these kinds of dark metroidvanias. Blashphemous, Vigil, Death's Gambit, Salt and Sanctuary, Hollow Knight etc. So I had to play this one just because of the art style. There's a lot of good stuff here and I think with some tweaks, perhaps a sequel or a high content filled DLC could be great. First, the art style is pretty solid. It's very Blasphemous inspired, dreary and dark, but it's a little too restrained to be as memorable. Nothing especially creepy or morbid, rather more of a 'gothic' feel. Lots of shades of gray and black and brown and really, very little else. I think that it's pretty cool but perhaps a bit monotonous. Some kind of snow, water or grass would have helped give it a little more pizzazz. By the first or second hour I was feeling a little underwhelmed by how every new land looked nearly identical to the last one in terms of color scheme. Still, I did like the art style in general and again, just a shade or two extra would take it from good to great.The gameplay is decent. First off, this was a pretty easy game for the genre when compared to the likes of Hollow Knight or Blasphemous. It's more akin to Vigil in terms of difficulty. You'll definitely have a few struggling moments, but once you get through a boss or two you'll catch on a bit and it becomes fairly smooth sailing. The customization options were pretty bland; you get a sword, you swing the sword, they die. There's a strong attack, weak attack, 'special' attack and two magic slots. No armor/clothes. You won't use the magic much at first, and probably wouldn't at all honestly as just clicking the simple attack button with an occasional special attack does the job 90% of the time, but the game literally makes you use it near the end to kill about 70% of the enemies. I found this to be a hair irritating because, well, the magic is also how you heal. That, and the attacking magic is pretty much an attack. Throw rocks at them, shoot a little magic wave at them, do an AoE at them, etc.  When you're spammed and locked in with 4-5 enemies that all kill you in two hits and you can only use magic to hurt them, which is in very finite supply and takes a moment to load up...it's just a bit unnecessary. I think that the spamming/locking in with enemies was meant to be grueling or demanding, but it came off much less Bloodborne difficult and much more Dark Souls 2 difficult. Rinse and repeat, drop down, oh look I can't escape, boom, 5 enemies. If I played a drinking game for every time I was in that situation every 30 minutes I'd be a dead man. Still, it's a trope of the genre if nothing else and it is to be expected. I just didn't expect it to happen as often as it did. The bosses were a decent challenge. If you ignore exploration and don't upgrade your weapon/magic/health like I did for the first half of the playthrough you'll think that the bosses are especially punishing. Once I realized that error however, I didn't die to a boss again. A lot of people complained about certain bosses in the reviews but they must be new to the genre. If a boss kills you in 2 hits, you're probably not ready for them. I enjoyed the boss fights. There's an otherwise decent selection of enemies, the usual suspects: Basic attackers, shield attackers, flying projectile throwers, mages, creepy/crawly spider things, etc. I thought that it was a decent variety. The story was...fine. I don't know, I tried to follow it the best that I could but it was one of those 'intentionally vague' stories where the protagonist is meant to be confused and well, I was confused. Even in the end I feel that I get the gist of it and that's about it. I could explore more I'm sure but it just didn't appeal much to me. The worst part of this game is the audio. No sound cues for enemy attacks, super bland soundscape rather than a soundtrack, very little voice acting, etc. About 15 minutes in I took my headphones off and turned on some of my own music. A good soundtrack can make or break a game, and it doesn't get much more bland than this one. It's like they went to Fiverr for the soundtrack and overall sound design and spent a cold $15. If the developer comes across this review, please for the love of God, spend that little extra for a good composer. Overall this game is about what I expected. A pretty fun, reasonably challenging experience with a cool art styling and bare bones, if effective, combat system. I'd play a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid action platformer, but not quite everything it could've been.At its core Moonscars is a very satisfying action game with a light sprinkling of metroidvania and some soulslike thrown in. The aesthetic is lovely, the bosses are fun, and the story is a little more interesting than the usual "plague/curse beings the world to ruin" soulslike formula. I'd say the game's two strongest points are the combat and the aesthetic. Everything looks and animates beautifully, with weighty, meaty animations that lend the combat a lot of punch. Your basic melee combo is quick and snappy, aerial attacks have you hang in the air for the perfect amount of time, and charge moves feel incredibly satisfying to line up and land during openings in enemies' attack patterns. Moonscars also has probably the best parry I've ever used in a game of this type. Unlike some action platformers where the risk is too high for the reward, the parry here is forgiving enough to feel viable and the payoff is immense. Yet it isn't so easy that it muscles out your dodge, requiring different timings for different attacks in a way that forces you to learn each enemy's parry windows before you can reliably counter them.There are a few other interesting systems in Moonscars that make it stand out, most notably a Souls-esque world state change that occurs every time you die, spawning more challenging variants of enemies to up the difficulty in exchange for more currency and collectables to spend on upgrades. This optional hard mode is easily reversed with a common consumable item, making it a very organic way to adjust the difficulty to your liking. There are several fun little quirks like this that help to break up the formula, though none that really break the mould in a massively meaningful way.Despite having a solid enough core for me to recommend the game to anyone who likes challenging action, Moonscars does unfortunately have a lot of rough edges. None of them are major, but they do hold the game back quite a bit. For one, at the time of writing this review there is no option to rebind the controls. Attack is bound to the Square/X button, while your dodge is bound to the Circle/B button. Since you can freely cancel attacks into a dodge, you want to be able to use these two inputs in quick succession, but with them bound to opposite face buttons you have to move your thumb every time. The parry is bound to one of the triggers, which would have been a logical place to put the dodge as well so that it could be chained together with attacks without requiring the player to move their thumb. This might seem like a minor complaint (and it by no means makes the game unplayable or anything), but it bothered me a lot at the start, and felt like an unnecessary hindrance to the controls throughout.The game's level design, as well, is a notable weak point. The starting areas are fairly fun and varied, with stage hazards and gimmicks working to spice up the combat, but as the game progresses it begins to rely increasingly heavily on combat rooms that lock you in and force you to fight enemies in mini-gauntlets. You'll often have a corridor or an elevator to traverse, maybe with a platform or two to climb, then you'll be thrown into another combat room with a slightly different configuration of enemies. The combat is strong enough that these are still fun, but the level design feels very uninspired as a result. There are almost no meaningful platforming challenges despite the game having fairly good aerial mobility and a decent wall jump. Enemies in the late game don't tend to be placed in interesting patterns that take advantage of the level design because the game relies on straightforward combat rooms instead.The game has a metroidvania-style open world and lots of little secrets to uncover, but progression is very linear, and backtracking mostly serves to uncover missed secrets or visit a few key NPCs for sidequests. There is only one unlockable ability in the game, and it isn't used regularly enough to have a transformative impact on the way you revisit old areas. The game's currency system, as well, feels underutilised. Currency is your main reward for exploration, yet it can only be spent on a few vendor items and new spells. You'll notice I haven't mentioned the magic system before now, because it's really not that impactful most of the time. Towards the end of the game you start facing enemies who only take substantial damage from magic attacks, which feels like a very heavy-handed way of forcing the player to actually use their spells. If it hadn't been for these enemies, I would've barely touched the magic system. The melee combat just feels so good and functions in such a versatile manner that spells aren't necessary in most situations. This makes spending your currency on spells feel rather underwhelming. I never really felt like my currency was valuable, because there were so few things I spent it on that had a meaningful impact on my gameplay.I could probably type a lot more about the various nuances and nitpicks in Moonscars, but at the end of the day it's a fun game that feels like it was a little rushed. Everything's there, and it all works well enough, but it doesn't feel as rich and fleshed out as it could be. Perhaps with another year in the oven the game could've gotten some more interesting level design, a couple more iterations of the magic and character progression systems, and some quality of life features like rebindable controls.It's a fun game. It's worth your time. The action is great and the presentation is slick. But it's probably not going to be your game of the year. Credit where credit's due, though, for a very small dev team this is an impressively realised crack at a platforming soulslike. I would love to see what they're capable of with a little more experience, iteration, and dev time on their future projects. Moonscars shows enough of an understanding of the fundamentals of good action platforming for me to be excited about what they do next. It's very possible that if they come out with another game in the same vein it'll end up being something really special.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game you play if you want a relatively quick, fulfilling Souls-like experience that doesn't get too complex or difficult. It'd be an excellent gateway to more challenging games like Dark Souls, Bloodborne, Elden Ring or whatever the elitist kids are playing these days.I think parts of the story may be a little lost in translation (literally), but it can be pieced together with a (worthwhile) second playthrough or some YT videos or a wiki scan or whatever. Not as opaque as other SoulsBorne-type games, but there's still nuance and thought-provoking elements.I got everything worth getting on my second playthrough, no guides, and I'm not a very good completionist. Give it a play now, or wait for a sale, you probably won't regret it either way.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: Superb indie metroidvania/soulslike with a grim dark setting and and awesome pixel art look.If you liked blasphemous give this game a try, the combat feels impactful and satisfying, the bosses and enemies have an amazing design and the story is just as cryptic as a souls fan can hope for.looking forward to the next project of black mermaid, definitly one of my personal top 10 games of 2022
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah this game has truly been a blast and I'm REALLY curious to see where this story ends up. The combat is quick and engaging. The spells are kinda just whatever to me. The enemies are challenging but not mind numbingly frustrating. Still alot of that vague dark soul style story telling, so the story might not actually matter in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A tough but addicting game that I finished on the steam deck. Performance was great apart from the odd stutter here and there.  Game itself has a great art style and animations, combat is fun. The game is tough, the spell and secondary weapon mechanics could be tuned a bit to make them more worthwhile to use.Overall I would recommend it, but not for those easily frustrated!
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Blasphemous and Hollow Knight, you'll probably enjoy this game!Extremely atmospheric, gorgeous pixel art and tight combat and platforming mechanics. The entire game feels oppressive in a very satisfying way, and its a relatively well polished experience too.The combat is hard, satisfying too. It takes some time to get used to the mechanics, timings, enemy behavior, every encounter can be deadly if you don't pay attention and fight accordingly, but it never feels unfair. You have the tools to overcome all challenges but achieving that is your full merit of executing it all properly!Boss fights are also very good. They feel badass, imposing and also test the limits of what you have learned.The only bad things I feel in this game are a few mechanics and designs that just don't feel properly refined like the rest of the game:- economy and the red moon: I'm good regarding the challenge but the price to pay to stabilize the moon is way too high considering how rare glands are. Besides, more resources to spend is always good so what's the point? It doesn't make much sense but doesn't get in the way of the fun, it just really feels "charming" given the context of the game but entirely pointless given the mechanics, as a player I do want to maximize my rewards anyway.- shielded flying enemies: I like that they don't stagger easily and are a nice improved challenge overall but they really overstay their welcome. I'm not entirely sure I'm missing a witchery to defeat them or if this is intended design, its just a problem of them being absolute damage spongesOverall a great game anyway! Loving it so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: I can only recommend this game if you are ok with a grueling challange.Moonscars kind of shifts between a satisfying action game where you weave attacks, dodges and parries making you feel like a master of combat and then there is the portion where your normal attacks no longer cut it.At that point you spent most of your time saving up ichor for your witchery spells to even scratch most enemies. I felt this part to be the weaker side of the game as it turn the combat from interesting duels into long battles of attrition.I did encounter some bugs but I only had to restart the game once or twice to get past those.In summary: Moonscars is a good game with some flaws, would only recommend if you are willing to put up with some frustrating challanges.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: this review finished the game in about 11 hours without 100% i think im missing like 5 achievementscontrols feel really nice and responsive on keyboardi have not experienced any bugsnice visuals obviouslymusic is mostly moody and immersive/atmospheric so you wont find any songs you will listen to outside the gamedifficulty is challenging and keeps you on the edge of your seat so thats a big plusgood enemy varietyi cannot comment on the story sadly, that alone is on the peak of being subjective (i personally liked it altho that wont tell you much)i can think of a two gameplay designs i don't like and that is the spells you unlock, most of them feel useless and not practical and when you dont kill your doppleganger you cannot interact with people in the world or atleast i could notalso an upwards slash would be welcome to deal with flying enemies more easilyi look forward to playing upcoming expansions for this game if there will be any

_childDocuments_.review: * The battle system is almost as good as blasphemous but i am still not convinced.  * I'm looking forward to the greatness of story for a game such this, yet it didn't offer a great one. * I crossed some bugs. * Game is too short. It has small content.* Music is not that interesting.* I hate the maps, it doesn't even show the location name.* You always fight doppelganger every time you find new mirror.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really into metroidvanias but this one got me. Nice "comfort" features and i really like the graphics. Can't use my right arm for mouse & keyboard atm cause it's broken, this game saved me from a few boring hours. Plays perfectly well with controller  :) Adelinka "quest" is a bit too much imo as it needs too much unnecessery backtraveling.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonscars

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly want to balance out the negative reviews - yes there are some issues, but I think it can all be fixed fairly easily. In a nutshell: it's very enjoyable as a souls-like action game, with fairly well designed interconnected paths, while overall progression remains linear. Don't expect super in-depth exploration. Enemy variety seems ok - not great. The combat feels good (cool idea to add spikes everywhere to push the enemies into) and the art/athmosphere is great. I think the issue lies into some mechanics that don't seem very well tuned - I've only played a couple of hours but so far it feels like there is no real incentive to use spells (except on some breakable walls/elite enemies), due to their lack of damage on regular enemies, and their cost. The doppelganger mechanic is pointless in my opinion (why having to fight yourself every time you activate a portal to get your special weapon back??).Overall I'm enjoying my time with this game, even though yes it's a bit linear and some mechanics need fixing IMO. There is a lot of good here too, and it's fun.
