_childDocuments_.review: I think my favorite part of this game is that they built it with original appeal in mind (the original director returning makes it even better). This means that its built to be not only played, but beatable using the classic play style of a lance/dagger, and four directional shooting. All of the broken magic upgrades are optional, and are only included to broaden appeal for newcomers and lessen frustrations when you want to practice areas you struggle in. Things like the extra weapon capacity were my favorite because it didn't take away the intentional sting of losing the knife, but it made it so you wouldn't have to farm in a clearly action focused series. Another great addition was semi-random spawns for enemies and gold armor with the set stage layout. This felt like a good fit since the appeal of GnG (for me at least) is mastering the game rather than chasing high scores or getting a strategy down through muscle memory like a lot of arcade style games. There is still a scoreboard, but it's clear that wasn't the focus thankfully. It only enhances those moments when you earn extra power since its never a foregone conclusion. The only complaint would be the reuse of ideas from older games in the series, but even those feel significantly different thanks to drastic level changes, moving stage layouts, and the genuinely great visuals that make threats and platforms more clear in their behavior. Maybe this is more of a personal observation, but the improved visuals seemed to have allowed the level designers to make this one of the most ruthless platformers you'll play. You are constantly being barraged with unique encounter after unique encounter. While enemies may be reused, their positioning and combinations with stage layouts, numbers, and other enemy types never leave a dull moment or time wasted trying to overcome the demon hoard. If you are a fan of this genre or well-crafted action games in general, I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: Most times when I play an extra hard game for NES / SNES, I usually let some things slide, as I know the game is from a time when people still didn't fully grasp game design, so they put some mechanics that now seem a little unfair.But when they make a revival of the game that uses those broken mechanics to be "classic hard" and make the game unbearable to play, I'm not as kind.I didn't like to play this game. Maybe if you're a fan of the series you'll like it, but I'd rather play Dark Souls with the Donkey Konga bongos than play any more of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: Ghosts N Goblins Resurrection is a remake featuring remixed levels from both classic arcade games "Ghosts N Goblins" and "Ghouls N Ghosts" that is, for the most part, pretty faithful to the original games.The returning levels feature brand new sections that keep things fresh, even if some of them are pretty annoying. Jumping feels off compared to the original games (though that may be just me), the lives system has been replaced by a checkpoint system, and a skill tree was added allowing you to unlock spells for your character to use in combat.The original games were tougher than nails, and even though some of the changes in Resurrection make it easier (Including a super-easy difficulty option that lets you respawn like you're playing a Lego game, but prevents you from getting 100% completion), you're still gonna die. A LOT.The game is honestly pretty fun and charming if you can get into it, but if you're gonna play this at all, you must understand going in that it is likely going to be very hard, very brutal, and in multiple occasions unfair.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: If you're fan of SNES Super Ghouls 'n Ghosts, this game will be a frustration. _childDocuments_.review: Much better than the original game due to the new mechanics like the skill tree and the rebirth banners. The base game is very short, about 5 hours, but there is more to do if you are into it.However, mind this:*Gameplay Spoilers*- Make sure to pick the correct spawning option after dying. The default option takes you to the beginning of the area while you usually want to go back to the last rebirth banner you've reached.- The game does not reward you that much by exploring other weapons. After you get the dagger, don't even bother breaking any other chests since you actually risk grabbing a bad weapon by mistake.- Jump mechanics are still designed to be bad as in the original to make the game more difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: I've cleared the Megadrive Daimakaimura and the CPS1 Daimakaimura with no cheats. I've been close to clearing Chohmakaimura on Super Famicom but the last boss is very tough. So, I was anticipating this release but, unfortunately, it's broken. Many old games had a perfect formula and creating sequels is tricky. Mostly, things get added with, it seems, the philosophy that more is better. More characters, more levels etc. Well, this is not true. The PSP makaimura game was badly designed IMO. Too many enemies and the game was simply not fun. Well, this is more of the same. The enemy spawn rate is ridiculous and makes it a chore to play. Pacing is what made this series great and this game is a mess. If you agree with my view, save your money or buy something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this? No in fact I recommend you stay away from it. This is only somewhat pleasant at lower difficulties and for older fans of nostalgia. It's like playing Strider 2014 but without any of the excellent controls. Go buy that game instead. In fact you get the exact same Snake-Sky boss, from the exact same company. I still dont know why I bought it.Things that need to go away/be implemented:- Arremer invincibility frames, he is practically invincible 95% of the time- Projectile limit on screen (this is a relic of the NES hardware that does not need to be copied)- All non sword/knife weapons are totally useless and even detrimental to you- Grabbing a non sword/knife with only 1 weapon slot can destroy your stage progress- This game needs a baseline double jump from the start and at least 2 weapon slots immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game and difficulty settings. The game brings back memories and surprisingly never gets old. I thought it would, thinking a repetitiveness of the same old stages with little changes.   Wrong! You have two maps to choose from for every stage, mixing it all up. I played this literally as a kid with low gaming skills so I expected very little in the amount of stages the game has to offer. So far Im working on the 3rd long stage, with each having 3 different enemy backdrops/characters to each stage before fighting the main boss.   There are 4 different difficulty settings and I started out with the 2nd highest; Too hard for me at the moment, so I reverted to the 3rd in difficulty. With that being said, the 3rd difficulty is the sweet spot. Not too difficult, nor easy... Its perfectly challenging/entertaining.  I have read one negative review when the total reviews where at a total of 19. The solo negative was quoting the game as being dull. That had me having doubts for this game, being old and all. Im GLAD I didnt allow that solo negative review get to me. After 20 minutes of debating, I pulled the trigger.  This game is a MUST for your library addition! You wont regret it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: Am I in love with the style?  No.  Do I think that it does everything possible to honor the incredible art direction of the 16 bit era games?  No.  Are there a few too many nearly impossible sections that make playing on Legend difficulty a masochist's paradise?  Oh yes.  But these are nitpicks ultimately.  This is especially true for the latter point about the difficulty.  It is much much harder to design a game that is both very hard and very fair when you are forced to include multiple difficulty levels, and when you add the magic system to that it becomes a nearly impossible task to make a game that is still somewhat challenging even after getting all the buffs.  Even acknowledging its flaws, I can't imagine how you could call yourself a fan of platformers and not enjoy the hell out of this, especially the bosses.  There simply aren't enough of these being made right now and I haven't found a better one lately.  We should all be thankful they didn't ruin another great platforming franchise by making it a metroidvania like they did to Strider.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy a challenge and I like this series. But this game is designed just be as unenjoyable as possible for the sake of frustrating the player. _childDocuments_.review: This game sure feels like Ghost 'n Goblin game. That's natural because it's directed by Professor F who's also producer of Super Ghouls 'N Ghosts. The jumping mechanic is as simple as you get like in Ghost 'n Goblin. You can't alter the height and trajectory of Arthur's jump at all. If you get used to any game with better jump mechanic , you're most likely have hard time to play this game or even any of Ghost 'n Goblin. The arsenal is supposed to be balance. Not the sensible kind of balance that can be depicted as symmetrical balance with same weight on both of its end. No. The "balance" is chaotic, like a stable condition of a goat doing handstand on your head while you crouch on rocking chair and juggles 5 balls at the time. The problem with weapon that flies in straight line is you only restricted to 4 basic directions while the enemy's aim has flexible degree that usually follow your position.   Thus i strongly recommend bow weapon. I finish this game with less hour gameplay than Cuphead. Not only because the main content is shorter but also thanks to those Banners of Rebirth. You die a ton but they quite generous with the checkpoint or at least in "Knight" difficult. They also ditch the live system and gives you unlimited try instead. As long as you reach Banners of Rebirth, you make good amount of progress. I also like to say that the boss section is noticeably shorter than Cuphead's. Either you defeat the boss faster or you die to the boss faster. :pMy score: 6.2 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: What hurts most is playing a game with potential that ends up being badly designed. I put in 6 hours to not be able to beat the first level. You might think that over tuned difficulty is the crux of my critique but that actually isn't the case. I have spent far more embarrassing amounts of time beating even more benign challenges in far more difficult games. If anything it's the opposite, because once you "get" the strategy necessary to beat something in this game, it is fairly easy to do, as the controls are pretty simple but rather it's the unfair design that  necessitates constant trial and error.I knew I didn't want to continue the game when I got to the plant ambush in the first level where 4 carnivorous plants ambush you and give you no space to move. After enough attempts, I looked at a guide and saw that the real strategy to beat this **** of a section was to individually spawn every plant by itself by triggering their arbitrary triggers and effortlessly take them down.That's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There isn't any strategy, no catharsis, no "click" moment, you just have to beat the game at its own incompetent design. Many times in difficult games you have "how the hell was I supposed to avoid that?!" moments that give you the ability to look back and say "AH-HAH!". Even if you have to look at a guide, it actually makes you respect the game, because you learn of a new strategy technique or way of playing that you would have needed to succeed. Something, that tells you that the game is built around you becoming better and indirectly informing you that if you had been a better player, you would have been able to figure it out. Now that's rewarding.On the other hand GnG just throws bs encounter one after the other to deliberately tire you out, so as to keep its old school difficulty.I actually had high hopes for GnG and wanted to experience many of its unorthodox systems. The rigid jump arc that necessitates that the player think ahead instead of reacting to obstacles is actually something that really intrigued me. Yet the issue was that in reality the game was designed not around thinking ahead, but of exploiting the game's patterns through trial and error to succeed.I wouldn't have minded knocking down the difficulty from Legend to something lower so as to find a comfort zone, but the difficulty settings have clearly been made as an afterthought, merely increasing how many hits the player can take. Lower difficulties should prepare players for the eventual higher ones, not give them extra free get out of jail cards so that they don't notice how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ certain parts are.I actually came out of this game wanting to play something with similar controls and mechanics, but not with the obnoxious design of this game. Now that's certainly something I haven't experienced with many other games lol.

_childDocuments_.review: If game is hard but fair, then the game is fun.but this game is not fun. because it's NOT FAIR on every aspect.Developers should see Cuphead (and Sekiro) how to make a game that hard but fair.Definition of "fair" is if you know what incoming to hit you , you can react to avoid if you fast enough.  (Please check Sekiro & Cuphead as I said, both games are extremely fun because you take control the game when your skill is good enough)But not in this game. The boss attack is going to land on you and you know that but NO ANY POSSIBLE MOVE THAT YOU CAN DODGE the attack, you are running too slow, no dash, no double jump, no drop down to lower level. you just struggle to jump fwd (faster that running) away but still take a hit, or just get barely lucky enough to avoid on some rare occasion. Furthermore, another example of how not fair is, when you see the floor head is clear & safe to jump to, you jump forward, then the ENERMY IS SUDDENLY SPAWNED AT THE LOCATION YOU ARE LANDING TO then take a hit, SERIOUSLY?  Don't tell me to gid gud, I know i'm gud enough that I've got all achievements for both Sekiro and Cuphead.And playing on lower difficulty just feel empty.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the 80s arcade Ghost n' Goblin. Scrounging 1 litre coke bottles as a young kid to exchange for another 5 minute hit of gaming at the Fish n Chip shop was standard practice on the way home from school and this title cleaned several beaches from glass bottles.Salvation from living like hobo came with release of versions for my trusty C64 and later also on my Amiga (I think). With some hacks and no needs to sacrifice coins we got good to clock through this title.Fast forward a couple of decades and I was excited to see this re-release popping up in my feed.I must say I was pretty excited and thought the graphics where a nice blend between the 8bit look of the past and a more modern title.But then the game started and the animation and controls are like WTF!This thing is absolute garbage at an outrages price of A$45-Wait until its $5 dollars and even that is on the high side. However, at least at this price point one could argue that the controls/animation are "true" to the original.This was a missed opportunity to revive the franchise with some modern mechanics and better interactivity / animations.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, my first impression was good, even great, taking two hours to reach the first checkpoint in the Graveyard level on Legend difficulty.Then, I found out that when you revisit previously-cleared areas to hunt down the collectibles you've missed, the game punishes you by erasing any progress you've made on any checkpoints (or levels) after the area you've returned to. This is such a baffling design decision that I feel like I got ripped off paying 20$ for this game, when they're asking people to pay 40$.It's a real shame, too... As a huge fan of the original GnG games, this had major potential for me. Don't get me wrong, I'm a die-hard and I'm going to keep playing it, but I really can't recommend this to anyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing the original game in the 80’s and had it memorized front to back.  Needless to say, I can appreciate the nuances and love that went into creating this game. Sadly, I found it underwhelming.  The art style of the game in particular was not what i expected. It looks a bit flat, similar to an illustrated pop up book with some sections even looking  a bit drab and uninspired.  I was hoping for something closer to Rayman Legends visually.   Also, textures are very inconsistent. Even the key which you receive at the end of each level looks blurry.  Overall, this feels more like a parody of the original with a new coat of paint— and the paint job looks a bit cheap. Will recommend to hardcore fans of the original games but newcomers should wait for a deep sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm a huge fan of the series, going back to the NES port, there are some pretty poor design choices in this game. In every death (which is very common in the game) you have to choose the checkpoint again and again, making it absurdly tiring. NG+ is a dark version of the game with bad art direction, losing the game's bright colors and making it not pleasant to look and play.  Even the character's movement is uncomfortable by today's standards, it could be improved for life quality (for example, you can´t even jump or cancel when climbing a ladder), giving a general feeling of a game that doesn't value the player's skill. I thought it would be a game to be played many times, but it became a tiring and unpleasant experience much sooner than I thought.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: I was pumped until I played it.  I typically like remakes, but I believe Campcom missed the mark on this one.  If you liked Super Ghosts n' Goblins on the SNES, then you will probably be disappointed with this remake.  As mentioned in other review, no double jump.  But besides that the controls feels off compared to the original.  Kinda like you are pushing the stick, but it feels slower than the animation.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom sure s*** the bed. On paper this reboot of a challenging classic should've been a sure hit. I'm no stranger to the series, with both Ghouls'n Ghosts on 16-bit systems being among my favortie games. I'm fond of the new artistic direction and the game provides content in spades with a boatload of new levels and collectibles. Yet, from the get go, it manages to annoy more than to challenge, the main issues being overwhemingly high spawn-rates and random enemy patterns whose, coupled with the stiff controls the franchise is known for, are making the progression between each checkpoint a true nightmare even on the two easier difficulty modes.Fun is relative -sure!- but, as far as I'm concerned, there's not much fun to be had with these Ghosts and those Goblins.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT Ghosts N' Goblins. Do not waste your money if you are like me and grew up playing the original or Super GNG and are hoping for a worthy carrier of the torch, Arthur is PAINFULLY slow compared to the originals, but the enemies are just as  fast. This takes all of the difficulty of the originals but none of the skill-based gameplay and simply throws a clunky Arthur to a mess of enemies and projectiles with somewhat recognizable skins and areas. I wouldn't have thought a modern translation of this game could actually handle WORSE than the originals, but they somehow managed to make everything about controlling Arthur more frustrating and less responsive. Save your money and get an emulator if you're craving some nostalgia, because this dumpster fire of a cash grab won't scratch that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of hard games, I think they are my favorite types of games, those that push you, those that kill you and demand that you come back, not sorry, but better. But when a game is difficult and not fair that's where I draw the line and say no, this isn't difficult, this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.To clarify, I only played on legend difficulty, no point in playing on lower difficulty as the game loses its sole point: being difficult. This difficulty is senseless. It's unfair, unfun, and straight-up cheap. I have never played a more aids game than this.Enemies. Do. Not. Stop. Spawning. That is insane, stuff keeps coming at you from every direction, you die in two hits and no matter how far you have made it, you go back all the way to the checkpoint. Okay, so how do you defend yourself? You attack enemies, you are a knight with weapons. But there's a single viable weapon in the entire game. The knife. This isn't a joke, you have to get the knife. Every other weapon in this game is so bad, that's virtually impossible to play the game with. Now that is appalling. What kind of design is that? It's like the game actively trying to sabotage you.Okay, what about magic? it sucks. It sucks on a gigantic scale. You need to charge a spell before you can use it for like 5 seconds, in this game, seriously? Enemies spawn in the air, beneath you, above you. You jump and an enemy spawns in the air killing you. Real Ninja Gaiden vibes. Furthermore, once Arthur jumped, you have no control over him, once you jumped, your fate is in the balance of the RNG. It's clunky and outdated. I think they were trying to emulate the Genesis versions, but there, enemies did NOT keep spawning AND you had a double jump to mitigate that.All in all, your sanity isn't worth this game. It's frustrating and blood-boiling. What really kills it for me is that it's not about getting better, mastering some abilities, or focusing yourself and gathering your strength, patience, and will, which is why I play difficult games, no, it's about just keep trying and trying and trying and trying and trying till you FINALLY by some miracle get to the next checkpoint. What a nightmare of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: After nearly a decade away, Ghosts ‘n Goblins makes a return – and this time also on PC. I’ve played a lot of the classic, difficult NES games, but this series has somehow escaped me thus far and that is the perspective I will be reviewing from.For those unfamiliar with the series, Ghosts ‘n Goblins is one of those side-scrolling action platformers infamous for its difficulty level. As in, it’s quite literally considered to be one of the hardest video game series ever created. Resurrection is no different, but underneath that is actually a pretty well-made game.The mechanics themselves are very simple, but the levels are very creative to make up for it. You’ll go from the classic cemetery full of zombies to a frozen wasteland with demons flying all over, and then somehow end up riding a dragon into the clouds. These levels often introduce new mechanics of their own and some even offer multiple paths to go through. There is a nice sense of variety there and the mix between platforming, combat, and boss fights is well-balanced.There are some problems here core to the design of the game regardless of what difficulty you play at. Never is it fun to commit to a jump only for an enemy to spawn where you’re landing before you can even react. And no, it’s also not fun when an enemy spawns right on top of you when you’re just moving normally. These examples are both based on the game’s RNG enemy spawns – a form of fake difficulty that honestly shouldn’t be receiving defense from anyone.The difficulty is much better off when it isn’t relying on RNG – which fortunately is the majority in this game’s case. Tight platforming, hordes of enemies that can easily knock you into the void, and boss fights with some truly challenging attack patterns – it’s not an easy game by any means, but it is a fun one for those that are up to the challenge.There are four difficulty levels and each allow you to take more hits as you go down. You can even adjust the difficulty mid-stage just for that stage if you’re really stuck at one part. To be honest, I would probably not recommend this game if these features were not included. I have no shame in admitting I played on squire difficulty. This makes the bizarre RNG design choices a lot more bearable and allowed me to actually enjoy the underlying game for what it should be – a fun platformer with a nice sense of challenge to it.Even on that difficulty though, I still had to retry segments over and over – it is not like the challenge is completely lost. Still, Legend difficulty is there for those that want the classic experience. I tried it, but I simply don’t have the time to put up with it.This is a 2021 2D platformer that retains that same stiff movement and controls that you would find on most NES games of the day. Little to no movement while airborne, slow character speed, floaty jumps – it’s all there. To some, this might not be a problem – it might even be a positive – but it’s something I didn’t like about NES games I played then and still not something I am a fan of now.As for the graphics and music – both are fine and I really don’t have any complaints there. The graphics are a bit stylized and the animation is definitely not the usual, but it doesn’t look bad. The music is actually a lot better than what I was expecting and I enjoyed the variety offered there.On the performance side of things, the game immediately shoots itself with the 60 fps cap. This is easily a game that could benefit from an unlimited fps option, but it simply doesn’t do that. It is at least a stable 60 fps and I had no issues playing through the entire thing at 1440p.Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection, although incredibly difficult, is a fun enough 2D platformer for those into the genre. It has some nice level design, some simple, yet effective game mechanics, and difficulty options that actually make the game playable by modern standards. It doesn’t completely shed some of the problems of its older counterparts, but I did have a good time with it and would recommend it if you can catch it on sale.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this a fair crack, but it seems there are many flaws in the level design (e.g. failure to signpost where the player needs to move/jump) and stupid "surpriiiiiiise" traps that will likely kill the player without warning - oh ho ho, so funny. No it isn't.Also, the ceaselessly spawning enemies irked me no end because the pace they respawned was relentless (I know the earlier games also had this but it seems like the respawn rate here is faster with more enemies) and, oh what's this? The game gave me a new weapon that I had no clue how to use properly immediately before a boss fight. :-\Next level, ice platforms. These sometimes collapsed under the player's feet. Not a problem you might say - games have been doing this since the early 1980s days of Manic Miner on the ZX Spectrum (and probably earlier) where collapsible platforms looked different to normal ones so the player has fair warning. Not in G N' G Resurrection. Oh no, the collapsable ice platforms looked the same as solid ones, and they would break immediately when walking on them sending the player plummeting to the platform below or death. That got old very quickly.At this point I gave up - there are tonnes of other platform games that are more enjoyable that don't metaphorically slap you in the face every 10 seconds.It seems that Capcom put all their G N' G Resurrection development budget into hiring amazing artists, programmers and musicians to make a beautiful looking and sounding game, with super smooth gameplay.  After that, I would speculate that the money ran out so Capcom gave the last ¥100 of the budget to some random they dragged off the street, showed them a video of the original games and told them to get cracking with the level design!Very poor. Very poor indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: GnG is a series of action platformers that started in the mid 80's. It was a big influence on early Castlevania, and it has a similar combination of brutal difficulty combined with simple, deliberate controls. Likewise, the series features a cute, comical horror aesthetic. In its heyday, the series spawned three titles - Ghosts 'n Goblins, Ghouls 'n Ghosts, and Super Ghouls 'n Ghosts, along with various spinoffs, before long going dormant.Resurrection beautifully updates the look and charm of these old games with an updated soundtrack and storybook graphical style I personally love. The stages are all 100% new, though many are directly reimagined from specific stages in the first two arcade games. True to form, Resurrection is also ridiculously hard... way harder than any of the old ones, in fact. In terms of game design, it's a major step down from the two Ghouls 'n Ghosts titles, but better than Ghosts 'n Goblins. It tends to favor overwhelming the player with excessive numbers of enemies and other threats, and often feels like a parody of how hard people THOUGHT the old games were. It's kind of too bad, because the levels have so many awesome ideas and dynamic elements that the mass onslaught of enemies isn't really needed.While Resurrection is in some ways uncompromising, it does also contain various modern improvements. There are 4 difficulty levels. On its face, Legend is most similar to the old games' rules: 2 hits and you're dead, and only 1-2 checkpoints per level. But because the levels are so long and difficult, I would argue the 2nd hardest difficulty (Knight) is the closest approximation of how hard the old games were, giving you 3 hits and extra optional checkpoints.Arthur's magic spells have been vastly upgraded. Some of them are absurdly powerful, and they're no longer tied to wearing gold armor or having a specific weapon. These spells, along with some other helpful abilities, are unlocked by finding Umbral Bees, then using them on a skill tree. One skill finally let's you carry 2 or more weapons, solving the series' decades-long "unwanted weapon" problem. Thank god!Even the series' infamous "you have to beat the game twice" mechanic has been revamped: The 2nd loop presents you with radically-altered "Shadow" variants of the games' 7 levels, effectively upping the game to 14 levels.Overall, I'd strongly recommend Resurrection to fans of the series, or of action platformers with this combination of tough gameplay and simple controls. Yes, the game's approach to creating difficulty is an issue. But the game has so many other strong points, and enough options to temper that difficulty, that I'd still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Good graphics & music, 2 player mode is cool.It's main problem, as it has been extensively addressed, is it's difficulty level. I can understand it tho. The game was made to be hard and challenging, and since I'm a bit of a challenge monger I stuck with it until I had all achievements. It is not as unfair as many people claim it to be, game can indeed cheap shot you, but advancing it is not a matter of "luck" as mostly everything in this game can be made easier by using the right strategy/spells/weapons. If you are a knife caveman that believes "half of this game's weapons are useless", you will indeed struggle and seek for excuses for your own shortcomings. Regarding weapon selection though, I do think there could be a way to choose with which weapons you want to start a stage, since farming the layout you want for your next ordeal is not even challenging, just time consuming and adds nothing to the experience.Also, as a personal rant, I feel Arthur in this game runs WAYYY too slow....However, despite understanding the devs choices for difficulty, I was still going to downvote this game when I was done with it. Why?BECAUSE IT IS STILL TOO HARD.I played most of the gng titles, especially the old ones as this game's catering more to the more classical style of gameplay was what drove me in. I managed to beat them with moderate effort and will oftenly replay some them for fun, but this? This is a step above; as I said, it is WAY too hard, so much so that it doesn't feel like a genuine gng experience imo, it gives me ptsd. Legend difficulty has laughably sadistic checkpoint spreadout, so much so that I had to bite the bullet and decrease it to knight when I played and I STILL think it is way harder than any earlier title."Skill issue"Even if it were so, my skill was still sufficient to enjoy the other titles so my point still stands: This one's difficulty is overdone.However, in the end I still gave it a thumbs up. Why?Damn, you unlock so much cool and silly stuff after you beat this game I've forgiven it. So there. Long story short: If you like to rethink your strategies and complement your skill with efficient gameplay, this is the game for you. If you are a bruteforcer meta***, this game will annoy you much more than it should. Just don't play it on legend, frankly they went way overboard with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Every game this legendary deserves an epic makeover treatment on a scale as this.  With more and more super-realistic first-person shooters out there every year, It feels great knowing that some programmers still acknowledge and respect what computer gaming is all about.  This game is art.  Just as my early "Command & Conquer" games were recently revamped with upgraded graphics and music to look spectacular on my 48" HD monitor, someone did the same for another big chunk of my childhood.All the original artwork of this game is intact.  The characters, the music, the story.  (...the difficulty.)  Plus, they combined all the elements from the original with its sequel "Ghouls & Ghosts" into one game.  You can beat it rather quickly on easy, or to see even more levels you can spend the rest of your life trying to beat it on hard.  Worth much more than I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece of self-loathing and torture, where each little victory is a grandiose triumph over devious game design. The word "cheap" doesn't even come close to describing the perils that await you here. How many times will you die before clearing a single stage? 50? 100? Each step you take could very well be your last. True, I beat this on Legend without magic, but even with hand-holding, this game is no joke. _childDocuments_.review: The game being on sale for $11 I picked it up again. Initially when I first got it: I couldn't play it because of my display problems. Having ditched the 4kUHD television (4k is overrated anyway; it's very taxing on a CPU and GPU and if something you have works, it works..As expected, the game is hard: This is a G&G game; so whining about the difficulty, is like complaining that milk is white or a liquid. I've heard a lot of people complain about this game and that made me want to try it, even more. :) Of course, knowing the history of this franchise, in order to actually FINISH the game; you're gonna have to beat it more then once and on the highest difficulty. That's the way the franchise has always been, since the 80's.I don't mind the art style actually--the thing I have noticed so far; is that the movement animation, seems stiff, particularly with jumps. The music sounds good, the game is very vibrant, the controls are easy to pick up and play: there's even a two-player mode. I just got into it, so I'm scratching the surface: but if you're a fan and you're less cynical then I am (in general) You'll probably enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lives up to its predecessors in terms of difficulty.  Granted I started off on Knight mode, but man there can be little to no room for mistakes.  This game plays as great as the others and the talent tree is a welcomed addition!  Very different, but has good chemistry with the game.  If you love the series, you will definitely want to add this to your collection.  It's a nice side-scrolling game and you're able to choose either the Ghosts 'N Goblins levels or the Ghouls 'N Ghosts levels.  Be warned as they are tougher than they used to be, especially with the new mechanics.  There are four difficulties so if you want to take it easy, the option is there.UPDATE:  I went for 100% on Knight Mode and I don't think I'll be doing that again anytime soon lol.  If I have anything to criticize, it's the means to obtain certain Umbral Bees, especially in the harder modes.  I love the system itself, and it's fun collecting the bees, but to find them in chests while wearing gold armor and not dying, let alone not taking any hits...it's pretty rough to say the least.  Any future GNG games to be made with the Umbral Bee system, I would say don't put them in chests.  Other than that, I still love the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think if you played the other GnG games from the past this title will have something for you! Very interesting what I have seen so far. Kind of like putting Ghost n goblins and Ghouls n ghost in a blender and creating something "new". Many things are very nostalgic yet new and fresh at the same time. One of the best remakes I have played these past few years IMO. Right up there with Battlefront 2 (2017) and Hydro Thunder Hurricane. This is not "really" a review from me, I might review it some time later.New Ghost N Goblins Resurrection - Full spoiler review.Ok it has been awhile, but as I said before I would eventually do a full review of the game. This review will contains pretty much everything I liked and hated about the game, and as said. SPOILERS AHEAD!!!From the get go, I chose the upper path which is more catered or modeled around the original Ghost N Goblins game (the bottom is Ghouls N Ghost).    As the game starts you hear this swirling air sound that sounds kind of like something you have probably heard before late at night.......highways.........factories..........motors, engines, etc etc.As soon as you cross that first checkpoint the music kicks in and BAM!  It puts you right back into the world of Ghost N Goblins.  I heard the classic original theme and the big crows diving and cawing  and it was almost like that moment Han Solo had on TFA where he enters the Millenium Falcon after many years away and says "Chewie............we're home!".  I don't know if this event about conjured a tear of joy or just the sheer frustration that is Ghost N Goblins lol.  But ok, "member berries" aside on with the game.Capcom essentially took that familiar frame of artwork from the old NES game and made it like moving graphics.  I thought at first this game might be cheesy because of it, like an old Newgrounds FLASH game or something, but its actually brilliant how it worked out.What they did was basically give the world of GnG the Mario treatment.  And all of the classic characters are back and much more detailed now.As I said before, it is really like they took many classic things from Ghost N Goblins and Ghouls N Ghost and put it all in a blender and made something new yet still very nostalgic feeling.Of all the new and original themes, I really liked the intro theme where you choose new game or saved game. It is very haunting and yet beautiful as many really good GnG themes from back in the day were. There is also a very Tim Burton / Danny Elfman sounding theme I liked a lot.And now.........we come to the 1000 pound gorilla in the room...THE DIFFICULTY - Wow..........................just...............wow...........................Capcom....what were you thinking?   This game.............this game is harder than Chun Li's nano-diamond infused pantyhose.     Perhaps............one of the hardest 2d side scrollers of all time?  Granted there are OTHER difficulties (mostly for just 2 player coop party purposes surely).....but if one wants the true ending and all.......and to do this game RIGHT.  They have to play it on the hardest difficulty.  And asking a Ghost N Goblins game (which were already quite infamous for their tediousness and difficulty) to basically give all it can, is probably NOT VERY SMART for anyone to do.At the Legend difficulty things just became incredibly time consuming and difficult.  Just laughably difficult lol.  But...............it brought a gamer out of me that I had not seen probably in 30+ years.   But times are different now, and I'm more like the "old slow" Arthur from Ghouls N Ghost when the sorcerer smited him and he became old for a little while, and he threw his lances so slow and jumped so slow etc etc...I can't prove this.......(like dynamic Zombies in level 1), but I kind of think that first level is a percentage tougher than the rest of the levels of the game in some way.  That and I think the 3rd level is meant to break you. I think if you get past it you can win. Now it is just a matter of time and study for you after that point.I did not even fool with the umbrel tree the first play through, I kept it as old school as possible.There were times in the second play through I can kind of agree with a comment I read on Steam about how things got a little cheesy with the forced magic usage.  And then there is the third play through.  See what I just said? A third playthrough? It was during this third play through that I learned (that it was even more impossibly difficult) that the player must complete all of the "hell holes",  that they might get access to fight the last last boss, and get the TRUE ending.Ok......I do not agree with this. Capcom just broke a cardinal rule of the Ghost N Goblins franchise, and that is it ALWAYS takes two times to win (TWO times, not more or less or special objectives). And it was usually some kind of magic weapon that had to be used to win. A magic shield, or magic plasma beam or something.- Hell holes -  I think the concept is new and decent, and offers a "warp zone" kind of mechanic to the gameplay (as a reward for a hellish battle), but again, I disagree with it being some kind of new requirement to fully win the game. One can still play through and win Super Mario Bros even if they don't use warp zones.- Magic use - We got to see a bit of this with golden and bronze armor from Ghouls N Ghost and Super Ghouls N Ghost, and that connected the magic to the armor, (lose your armour? lose your powers!) but now Arthur can himself cast magic learned from the umbrel tree. The golden armor is still around though (when you are lucky enough to find it) and enhances weapon speed and stuff.  But now his magic use to me, gives the game a Megaman type of quality and feeling. Different powers for different situations. But there are different CHARGE times to reload. Some familiar abilities here like the phantom clone, and the lightning.   And some new transfiguration abilities like turning things into stone or frogs, or you yourself turning into a large boulder and mowing through enemies for a few seconds. And others like....- Armor bearer (a magic)- I really like this one, the ability to cast UP one level of armor.  If he is in undies? SILVER ARMOR...............If he is in silver armor? GOLD ARMOR (which itself now allows Arthur to take one hit and just go back to silver armor), but the thing here.......this ability is all for nought IMO because it takes like 2 minutes or so for Arthur to charge his powers back. During which time he can't use any other magic. And it becomes kind of necessary in the second playthrough and beyond.  But that is how it works, after each magic use there is a recharge period that varies depending on what was cast.- resurrection ability - This is cool when it happens, but I think even now I have only seen it a handful of times. Making it kind of useless like the armor bearer.- umbrel tree - this is where you unlock and learn the magic abilities based on how many of the blue umbrel bees you catch during the game. If you are on a new stage and catch 2? You can go right out of the stage and back to the main menu and to that tree and maybe you can unlock more?  Don't forget you can also sell back to the tree to possibly get things you could not normally. So there is many strategies here...- Red Devil / Aremeer - Trying to fight him is basically impossible now on Legend difficulty.  He CAN be beat, but its not reliable hehehe.  In some silly way it was like an exaggerated child hood fear (for me like 10 years old) running from this thing because of his speed and aggressiveness. Then in time you learned his patterns and met him head on. I couldn't really find a pattern here to fighting him.  Maybe it is just me or maybe its very very deep algorithm. Maybe he should be the main boss of the game?    hahah    And speaking of main bosses...- No individual boss themes - I thought from Ghouls N Gho

_childDocuments_.review: I want to point out something that's probably obvious just from looking at the screenshots, but this game has an amazing art style and I want to give commendations to the team who worked on it. You guys made something beautiful here. Thank you.As for the gameplay, it sure as hell is Ghosts 'n Goblins since you'll be failing over and over again hoping to progress a little bit further the next time. It's what makes victories all the sweeter, as rare as they may be at times. There's other difficulty options to make things easier if you want to go that route, but if you choose to be a purist and go for the Legend difficulty (which the game defaults to), then buckle up and quit yer whining when you fail. I think some people tend to play these games as an attempt to flex, soon realize the game's not as easy as they imagined, and then complain about it rather than sucking it up and playing at a lower difficulty to get better at learning things. I'm playing on the Knight difficulty because I ain't too proud, but want a nice taste of what awaits me when it takes away the little help I've got.This is a great intro to the series, and a must have in your library if you're an old school fan (but I probably didn't need to tell you that if you're the latter). Oh, and screw the Knife. Fireball all the way (j/k).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of the entire series, and so far I must say I'm impressed with this game entirely. I see aspects from every edition blended together.   At the same time, it makes itself harder, and even easier as well.  Minor examples - (Harder) Enemies are faster and have more varied attacks. Easier- Your armor isn't completely lost in 1 hit,  making the game  less punishing. The game also allows you to reduce the difficulty and has more frequent mid-point spots.  But fortunately, you don't have to use them to preserve the original experience. It's very good at a blending of the originals - seemingly all of them.     I Definitely recommend this for any original fans.  People used to easier platformers probably would want to skip this one, however.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a long time fan of this series since a kid back when I first saw it at the front of my local Wal-mart on a cold January night back in 1986. Thought was actually a little spooky as a child but fun none the less. A few years later I come across the second in the series at my local mall and would later purchase an original board for that came more than 20 years later. Owned both e Genesis and Super Nintendo carts and nes one as well. Now playing this for the past few days I realize why this series won't die. The endless challenge is frustrating yet rewarding at the same time. This game was Dark Souls of its day and it still holds up. This new version has all the tough game play of the old games plus has bonus incentives to keep you coming back for more. I have heard some of the veteran players complain bout the graphics. I on the other hand think they help to modernize the series while still honoring the past. This style of game is not for all but it is very satisfying if you have the patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghosts ‘n Goblins Resurrection is a reboot that brings the beloved Capcom franchise back to life and into the 21st century. Paying homage to Ghosts ‘n Goblins and Ghouls ‘n Ghosts, the latest entry combines the franchise’s action platforming gameplay with storybook-like graphics and challenging new obstacles. The game follows the valiant knight Arthur as he runs, jumps and battles his way through eerie stages set in the Demon Realm, a demonic fantasy world. Brave knights will need to proceed with extreme caution as terrifying dangers await, including familiar enemies like Zombie, Skeleton Murderer, Pigman and Red Arremer. Ghosts ‘n Goblins Resurrection is a nostalgic, yet fresh adventure that welcomes back its faithful fans, while introduces a new generation of heroes to challenge one of gaming's classic series.

name: Big Mutha Truckers 2
detailed_description: Big Mutha Truckers 2 begins with Ma Jackson being taken into police custody for tax evasion. The only way she can win her case is by hiring Cousin Jacob, the most 'fancy-talkin' legal fella' this side of Booger's Canyon. Players will be challenged to raise the cash needed to bribe jurors to let Ma off by trucking, trading, wheeling and dealing. The go-anywhere, any-time philosophy that was utilized in the original Big Mutha Truckers will be expanded for Big Mutha Truckers 2 with additional routes, hidden shortcuts, and the ability to drive numerous vehicles. Players have the freedom to deviate from their route and explore the highways and back roads to whichever city they decide to visit. In addition, the trading process will be extremely streamlined, with more focus on the on-road action. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: More streamlined than the first title. Good for arcadey fun, not as in-depth/simulated as the first one. Also, bring the first one on Steam!This is another time where I wish Steam had a numeric rating system or at least a "no positive or negative" rating to truly show how I feel. For context, I played this game a lot when I was a youngin' and I got back into it a few years ago with my OG Xbox copies. I since got a download of the first game and bought this second one. Spoiler alert, I prefer the first one.The first game was a redneck trucking simulator where you had to buy and sell goods in different cities, challenge fellow truckers to races, and complete random missions at the bar in order to get enough money to buy your ma's company and beat your brothers and sisters. There were 4 drivers (a 5th secret driver you could unlock on NG+), memorable characters and settings, a decently sized map, serviceable driving, a comedic script and radio (it wasn't Monty Python funny but it had some legit chuckles), overall the game was a charming little sim that wasn't too deep, but didn't try to be. It was a balance that favored aesthetic a little more and it worked out well enough in its favor.BMT2 doubles down on the hillbilly arcade aspect of the last title with mixed results. The writing, while a lot of people complain about it, isn't all too bad, in fact it's on par with the last game. The map, while more detailed also feels significantly smaller in size. The game as a whole also feels weirdly smaller, with small details such as a 5th driver missing, main menu being static images, missing entering/leaving the diesel animations, less radio songs (tbf there was very little in the way for music in the original), no more custom truck symbols, they essentially hyper-emphasized so much details in some areas and completely ignored it in others. There's also new types of supplies to sell (including new illegal substances) and new missions/encounters, which are a welcome change of pace. The story is more or less the same, except instead of earning money to buy the company, you're earning cash to pay off jurors for your ma's legal case. The story works and the characters you meet are interesting enough to feel acceptable.The driving, to be blunt, is an extreme downgrade from the last title. The last game was slower, could withstand more damage, and overall felt like driving a truck. They try to make the game more fast pace but it ends up coming across like a bad Crazy Taxi clone as the physics are completely screwed e'ery which way to Sunday and the handling just feels...weird, like you're not hauling a big ol' trailer. The changes may help during missions when you're driving cars, but the truck itself just feels wrong to drive, and with the way the new timing system works, instead of selecting an optional race to earn extra money, you HAVE to choose a time to get to your location, which ranges from Truck Me Tenderly to Truck Me Harder, and the game expects you to get away from the BS "revamped" police system or drive the worthless hobos around as the game Trucks You In The Cornhole.The game is also weird in technical aspect too, like the textures feel EXTREMELY crunchy and the game overall looks worse than the first one. Also, the steam overlay doesn't work properly for me, which is slightly annoying. The audio levels are also all over the place.Overall, the new casino games, gallery features, and new missions aren't enough to fill the whole left in my heart. It's fun, but I would much rather prefer the slower, weighty driving as opposed to this simplified arcade wannabe. This is a good starter to introduce someone to the games to and by no means is it a "bad game" per say, I just feel the arcade route doesn't work on a concept like hauling trailers across the land to get your ma sum cash.It is normally on sale super cheap and you can still get some enjoyment so I GUESS I'll recommend it, but your enjoyment of this game will really come down to what you wanted to see out of the series, the over the top zany moments placed through an average trucking trip, or the ride itself to be the zany moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Dreadful, this is much worse than the previous game. The handing of the trucks is awful, especially when trying to complete the 'parking challenge'. _childDocuments_.review: What a piece of sh*t. Apart from outdated tech (1024*768 max res), bad controls and lack of content & care, the game simply is the worst in terms of progression through the story.The game at minute 15 plays exactly the same as at minute 400: you buy low and look where to sell high, making a few 10,000 bucks at a time - if your stuff doesn't get stolen during unfair mini challenges on the way. (You will need millions of $.)But there just aren't any upgrades to buy, having more money in the bank doesn't allow you to invest more to make more profit per trip. It's a horrible grind, driving the ever same  routes dozens of times.The side missions inbetween are sh*t. The world and the roads are boring, uninspired and paths leading off the sides are only created to be used during the side missions. All characters in the game are offensive tokens/tropes, which I don't really mind but they're not executed in a funny way. Neither does the game have any redeeming nudity. The almost nude pretentious hipster hippie girl is a plus but they should have followed through with their sex sells marketing strat - or should have left it out.Any money the publisher has spent went into the "All right now" music licence and any effort the developers have made went into the creation of one of the radio stations that features  funny interviews (kudos to the voice actors on that one). And you will spent at least half the time in menus - which is something I really don't understand as it makes the game worse than the prequel.  (and not the good kind of sucking)

_childDocuments_.review: Big Mutha Truckers 2 begins with Ma Jackson being taken into police custody for tax evasion. The only way she can win her case is by hiring Cousin Jacob, the most "fancy-talkin' legal fella" this side of Booger's Canyon. Players will be challenged to raise the cash needed to bribe jurors to let Ma off by trucking, trading, wheeling and dealing. The go-anywhere, any-time philosophy that was utilized in the original Big Mutha Truckers is expanded in Big Mutha Truckers 2 with additional routes, hidden shortcuts, and the ability to drive numerous vehicles. name: Drawn to Life: Two Realms
detailed_description: The quirky Raposa and your drawn hero return in Drawn to Life: Two Realms, the next installment in the beloved franchise! You again take on the role of the Creator, unlocking the mysterious connection between the two worlds, and creating a Hero to save them both! A brand-new Creation Tool expands the creative possibility with millions of colors, unique stickers, templates, new hero animations. Unlock additional Stickers to further customize and save out your unique Hero looks via the new “Outfit System”. The story continues! Now that Mike is awake, a new human world is revealed. Travel between the Raposa and Human towns to uncover the mystery of the shadow and save Mike and his friends. The full cast of Raposa return, along with brand new characters to interact with! Use the Book of Imagination to enter the mind and challenge Townspeople, Enemies and Raposa to resolve conflict and defeat the shadow. Utilize and place dozens of unique toys to score points based on your own imaginative solutions. Take control of your Hero and jump, spin, and ground pound your way through over 100 unique challenges! A true continuation of the series, brought to life by many of the original developers. Enjoy over 50 new music tracks from the original franchise composer, a lush 2D world from the renowned original sprite artist, and continued story presented by the original Executive Producer of Drawn to Life, and Drawn to Life: The Next Chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: 11 years later, I see this.You better believe I bought it instantly.I had long given up hope for a continuation. This series was part of my childhood. I still listen to the prequel soundtracks to this very day. To be able to experience this world again is all I could ever want.-----------------------------EDIT: Here's the deal: Is it the same gameplay as past titles? No. It's more Mario Maker-esque and puzzle-focused. There's still some drawing element but not as much as before.Is it the same universe/story? Yes. The story continues years after the quite downer ending of Drawn to Life: The Next Chapter. Is it still good? Although the more negative reviews make valid points, I'm not gonna let that stop me from enjoying what I've been deprived of for a decade.I am 100% fine with a mellower experience after the prior title's dark and uncertain ending. Honestly, I'm just happy everyone is okay. I don't mind the shift in gameplay direction (I already like puzzles and Mario Maker). Plus, the dialogue brings a smile to my face.
_childDocuments_.name: Drawn to Life: Two Realms

_childDocuments_.review: It really hurts to write this seeing that somehow a new Drawn To Life games comes out after what seemed to be the end of the series for more than a decade. However I write this as a fan and someone who has played the previous games (and the spinoff) to death. This game is not that great. It does many things well but what is true to Drawn to Life is missing. An adventure platformer that utilizies drawing to create things in those levels. Pros:- Absolute gorgeous pixel art, I may be a fan of the drawn art from TNC but this is quality stuff- The OST is amazing and definitely worthy of re listening to. - Optional content to play and earn more rewards for cosmetics- Appearances of the previous villages, if nothing to them was a nice feature- Not retconning any of the previous story for this game (I thank the devs for not taking away anthing from TNC and its ending) Also their transparency in reading things from the fanbase. I can tell they do love the games and what it offered. That's about it from what I can say was good/great about the game. Now about the cons.Cons- Story is bland, forgettable, with missing beats and emotional connection. The first DTL we learn to connect with the characters Mari and Jowee. However this game tries to do the same but fails, there's no clear threat that impacts the village/town that the characters can grow from. Everything is loosely connected and feels half baked and rushed. -Characters feel very bland (this is a repeating theme), especially the new ones. None of them stand out or have anything unique about them, nor are they present for majority of the time. - The core gameplay are puzzles, not a majority platformer with enemies, equipment, some puzzles, and bosses. I feel like this is a slap in the face to people who liked the previous games. It's akin to making a spinoff title and slapping a DTL 3 on it.- The levels themselves are just boring, you'll find some of them incredibly easy or incredibly hard. Not only that but they are bite size short levels. Some levels can last literal seconds. This means almost hundreds of levels in these extremely short puzzle areas. All of this combined with the main gameplay makes me have the sneaking suspicion that this was a mobile game solely, and happened to be ported to Steam and Switch. - The way you enter levels themselves have is just a popup, whether this is a good thing or bad thing to you is your opinion but I believe there is nothing adventurous about it. There's no door to open for new worlds because there are no worlds or physical levels to enter. You have the two villages, and that's that. It kills any tone the game wants to have because it never progresses out of that area it's in. - There is barely any actual drawing in this game, sure you can make your hero and some things in the villages as decor. That is it, you can not make things within the level and use them. This is so mind boggling because the themes of all the games was creation and this game lacks that- Zero bosses, also kills any sense of adventure or progression  (if there is one I will change this)I don't know what to think, I'm not disappointed because I was never anticipating another game.  I feel like this game is for people who like puzzle games but not actual DtL fans. If this was labelled as just another spinoff then I wouldn't be writing this. I know the devs are passionate but I question their ideas when making this game. If you're a DtL fan, don't bother with this game. Buy the OST though, it's awesome as always
_childDocuments_.name: Drawn to Life: Two Realms

_childDocuments_.review: Change is scary, y'all. This game isn't the same as the previous generation on the Nintendo DS. If you're looking for a true continuation, wait longer. Gameplay, it's a repetitive sequence where you would go from point A to point B, dig into someone's mind for 3 areas of puzzle platforming, then get rewarded with a few dialogues of the story. Rinse and repeat.Two Realm's music is amazing, like the previous games. The original composer of the series, David J. Franco, is responsible for making these tunes so damn catchy, so seeing him back isn't surprising.Story-wise, I honestly don't have the energy to sit down and endure the gameplay.Overall, the game delivers on what it was promised. A puzzle platformer with amazing music and some type of story that might continue with the earlier games. I, however, don't recommend this game at this price. The Mobile version is far cheaper, so you should probably go for that instead of the Steam version. I recommend watching the developer gameplay streams to see if this really interests you, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel mixed but positive about the game. I kept my expectations in check since it was announced and never expected anything closely similar to the DS games, coming from a decade-long hiatus; as I've said before, that's a fairly unreasonable expectation. The new direction with puzzle-based levels is interesting, though not a bad move on its own. For what it's worth, I think these levels are better than DTL1, though less memorable and far more repetitive (I still can't get over the issues in the first game's level design); though, these levels are a larger step down from DTL2. I think they could have improved this formula by removing the timer and introducing a bit more of a platformer-focus into the level design, even if it retained that puzzle aspect. DTL1&2 felt like exploration, while these levels felt like tasks. The biggest issue I have with the game is the optional challenge levels. There are some significant difficulty scaling issues with some of those levels, especially if you're going for a three-star bonus in all levels like I am. All around, a few of the levels need to be far less challenging. Bosses would be nice too, please. please... :)I had minor annoyances with the day/night cycle animation, the fact you can't customize keybinding, and the overall lack of drawings in the Village. The story is nowhere on the same level as the DS versions. I don't think it's terrible; it's just not fantastic. As someone who really got engrossed in the story for the first two games, I feel a little "meh" about the storyline. Still, I appreciate that there's something there; it's not soul-less like some people feared, at least not in my opinion, and it does add to the previous entries.The music and graphics in the game are fantastic. Far better than either of the DS games, in my opinion, especially in music. I just wish there was more to see! This is, of course, subjective. I understand that it's hard not to be excited over a new installment to the series after so many years. Still, I feel like it should have been evident that this wasn't going to be the continuation many of us dreamed of. Though it's heavily attached to the original storyline, Two Realms can stand on its own. For that reason, I'm more compelled to judge it on that basis. For the price I paid, I had an enjoyable experience. There are issues in this game, but if it receives patches like we're expecting, many of those will likely be resolved. If there ever is a future game, I just hope it improves on the Next Chapter (Puzzles are nice, but I miss the adventure and story-focus!), with smaller sprinkles of what Two Realms attempted to bring to the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Drawn to Life: Two Realms

_childDocuments_.review: WHERE'S THE BOSSES????The game so far (almost 3 hours in) has just been a constant feeling of "HERE COMES A BOSS, HERE COMES A BOSS" and then it's just another uneventful chain of short puzzle levels. The gameplay is essentially -- play 3 short puzzle stages, then sit through 5 minutes of dialogue, then repeat. Also, somehow my character manages to always be facing AWAY from people during any conversations at all. The biggest entertainment of the game is laughing at it with my friends, but I would definitely drop it within minutes if playing without an audience to complain with. Nothing feels consequential at all. All this game has done is make me want to play the first two games again and stop playing this. If you're a fan of the series, you're better off waiting for a plot synopsis to pop up on the wiki to read. This is not drawn to life. This is Yawn to Life. The ending of the second game was awesome, and this is almost an insulting afterthought.ALSO: Who thought it would be a good mechanic to have you move painfully slow on the world map, and place "speed boosts" around to gain a temporary reasonable walking pace? This adds nothing to the game besides making travel in an already slow paced game feel like a slug coated in epoxy resin crawling on a carpet floor of epoxy hardener. Use your money to rebuy the second game, or if you want something new and exciting then roll a ten dollar bill up and see how far up your nostril it can go.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're here, you're likely a Drawn to Life fan. There hasn't been a new game in 11 years, so you might be tempted to impulse-buy this. Buyer beware: the game's divisive even among fans. If you're interested in this and haven't already played the old DTL games or scribblenauts, I'd recommend looking at those instead.Two Realms is what it says on the tin: two realms. You can explore two lovely pixel art hubworlds filled with cute little characters and buildings all done in a style that's highly reminiscent of the old games while still having its own identity. Unfortunately, once you've seen the two hub-worlds, you've seen everything.The basic gimmick of drawing your own hero is present, and you do get to draw lil' decorations in the hub worlds, but there is nothing else to draw beyond that. There is no exploration beyond the "two realms", the gameplay is contained entirely within what's called "imagination battles", each composed of a set of "platforming" challenges.In the game's main story, these battles are typically 3 'levels' long. The first two levels are essentially bite-sized introductions to new mechanics, and the third level lets you place the enemies & misc. yourself. The meat of the game is small puzzles where you place the enemies in the right way to progress.You can try this game for a spin and see if you like the "imagination battles". 2 hours is more than enough to know whether you'd enjoy this or not. If you don't, you can refund if you wish since this is the whole game. It's extremely easy to softlock yourself, and you might get stumped since the game doesn't properly explain all the mechanics.So, there are no bosses, no drawn-to-life style levels, no wings, no weapons. The game's essentially a stripped-down version of scribblenauts except you're limited to a few toys rather than any word you can think of. What if we don't care about the gameplay, what if we just want the story? Well, it's nothing groundbreaking.The story is, once again, a very scribblenautsish thing in the vein of using PHENOMENAL COSMIC POWER to solve mundane issues. Also, there is very little character development, since the hero solves everything for everyone.However, the plot does respect the previous games' endings. What we discover over the plot is the aftermath of Mike's accident, and I think the way they handled  was fitting. I'm still glad Drawn to Life came back at all, though in a- experimental form. The gameplay will certainly alienate old time fans quickly, and I don't think it's fun enough to pull in newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: Drawn to life was perhaps the most influential game of my childhood , behind its childish artstyle and seemingly innocent narrative lies a story of tragedy and suffering aswell as trauma, the original two installements drawn to life and drawn to life next chapter ( drawn to life wii edition is not officially cannon and as such will not be taking part of this discussion) were pieces of art that although had relatively repetitive gameplay shared a long narrative with emotion and actual care put into it , the story of the first game takes a much simpler approach since it is the starting point of the series and as such most likely did not have the full scope fully layed out although the pieces were there , you come to learn that the world you inhabit which is the world of the rapoza is the creation of a boy in a coma , you dont fully yet understand the reason for his existence in it but you learn that the villain of the story wishes to keep the boy in the coma as to allow himself and his fellow villagers to continue existing since waking him up would lead to the destruction of the world , its not the darkest or most philosophical of concepts but yet it is something that can be understood and appreciated expecially given the target audience , the second game improved a lot more on this formula and presented multiple different themes alongside its story aswell as the progress of mikes situation and pain , we learn that his parents died in a horrible car crash , his sister has half of her face disfigured from the accident and spent the entire time next to his brother in a hospital bed praying that he would wake up , the ending was touchy although bittersweet , the boy Mike finally awakes to the joy of his siter , and we see a final moment in which the two main rapozas from the game series stand side by side giving us a sense of closure , it was far from perfect but yet it had heart,  and then this game came out , not only retconning the world of the rapoza being the coma of the boy , but also removing the physical damage that Mikes sister had sustained from the car crash , it also completly changed how the gameplay of the game works , making it honestly feel like nothing more of a glorified phone game , which it was in the end given the fact that this game released onto the phone market, i dont expect you to care about what i have written previousely but i cant give a positive review to a game that would spit in the legacy of something great , it feels as if the developers did not care for the previous lore and story and simply wanted to milk the franchise further.

_childDocuments_.review: I uh, this is uh... Look, It's just, not very good, it's very unpolished, very bland, and the art-styles dont work well together. The art is nice, it's really really good, but the characters and backgrounds feel like they were made by two different people. Not only that, it's missing the entire whole thing that was great about drawn to life, making your own drawings for platforming, and objects, that stuff was really really cool and fun. This is just a really boring and bland platformer with nothing special about it. I really want to like it, I really really do, but, I can't recommend this game. It's got a lot of effort put into it, it's just, not very well done, there's no invincibility frames, dying means you gotta go back to the mario maker screen thing, and click play again, it's not even a drawn to life game, it doesn't feel like a drawn to life game. _childDocuments_.review: While the art is beautiful for the most part, and the music just so-so, I can't say there's anything quite redeeming about this game. I really, really wanted something of substance to be in Two Realms. I'm a fan of the Drawn to Life Series, having played both DS games for years and years, and I've become a part of the speedrun community for the Drawn to Life games. I've even participated in an interview with Jeremiah Slaczka, the creator of the original DtL games. So I got Two Realms, nervous about the quality of the game. Drawn to Life: The Next Chapter (DS) came out 11 years prior, so this new company continuing an old series was something to worry about. And my worry ended up being correct:Sprites sometimes don't animate. There are text and grammar errors in the game and even the main game. There's constant layering issues with the player and sprites clipping under or over landscape and overworld objects. There are countless and innumerable glitches and bugs and gameplay issues that make it so some levels REQUIRE you to cheat because of other glitches impeding you. Even the level design sometimes required cheating or glitching to make it doable. To 100% the game is extremely time wasting and laborious and repetitive, and sometimes isn't even possible because of poor coding and glitches and achievements not being received even once the requirements are met!The story is slow, repetitive, and never goes anywhere. This game is supposedly canon yet there are many discrepancies between this and previous games. The gameplay with how the character moves in and out of levels makes me feel like this is an entirely different game that's just using Drawn to Life's story, characters, and elements glued on because they knew that other game would be bland otherwise. I wanted this game to be good. Thousands of other people wanted it to be good. But this is just a sad, disgraceful stain on the Drawn to Life series history, even worse than that of the ii game and Spongebob spin-off. The worst part is this is an improper and insufficient way to introduce new fans to the franchise. Please, play the original DS games and support 5th Cell.
_childDocuments_.name: Drawn to Life: Two Realms

_childDocuments_.review: I played the originals when I was a kid, and when I saw the game I didn't hesitate to buy it. It looked good, graphically improved and nostalgia got the best of me. Turns out, it is not developed by the same team, 5th Cell. So all the essence is gone in favor of dull mobile-like gameplay that would even bore me out back when I was a kid. Even the character creator was underwhelming, you would think that 10 years after the original the character creator would be more advanced, have more features. They didn't even have tablet support for pc. Am I supposed to draw with my mouse? And in console with a game controller? This game was made specifically for the DS, if you make a sequel for other consoles, don't you think that maybe it won't work as well if you don't optimize it?TLDR: don't buy it for the nostalgia if you played the originals, not the same team, boring gameplay
_childDocuments_.name: Drawn to Life: Two Realms

_childDocuments_.review: The developers say it's a "True continuation..." This feels like a mobile game spin-off. The hero creation tool is pretty good, but much simpler than the previous game. No extra limbs, body shapes, color palettes or any cool stuff like that though. The stickers are lame and don't match your character. The biggest offense to me is that...you don't draw anything except for your hero and a few overworld things. No weapons, enemies, obstacles, platforms, vehicles, anything....So yeah, if you're expecting the platforming from the previous games you won't find it. There are no weapons or bosses, every level is a small puzzle with some light platforming. Sometimes you have to place the enemies to reach the exit, but there's not really any depth to it. The art and music are really good, at least...? I enjoyed seeing all the old raposa hanging out around the village. Couldn't care less about the human characters.It's not a bad game, but if you're a Drawn to Life fan there's no point in playing this. It doesn't do anything interesting with the characters and story. If you want a cheap and cute puzzle platformer, this game is for you, I guess. (It's cheaper on mobile, by the way...)

_childDocuments_.review: As a big drawn to life fan this game does not deliver.Maybe I shouldn't act entitled because who ever saw a third game coming?But it's like, why fix/change what isn't broken? If you enjoy small puzzle games built for mobile then this is for you. Maybe it should've been advertised as a spin-off rather than DTL3.Visually it's still great.Musically it's still great.
