_childDocuments_.review: Stop reading other negative review and give this game a chance! It is totally worth it! At the time of this review, I only got like more than 2 hours playing, but wait and see, I will hit 100 hours soon to prove that the positive reviews are correct.I have been losing interest in single-player games recently - Most of the games I am playing now is co-op and multiplayer, which make me feel connected with others and less lonely. However, this game for sure will keep me engaged with single-playing habit for awhile now. It is a beautifully crafted world with relaxing music, cute characters, simple storyline, amazing scenery and atmosphere - I totally immerse myself in this lovely world of Evertree. I am a fan of Stardew Valley and My Time in Portia back - that somehow explain why I am hooked with this game so easily. After a long day working, this game helps me fully relaxed and chill before I go to bed.Basically, you can do anything that you want in this game without any pressure. You can build your own village, explore the whole wide world, collect stuff, go fishing, catch bugs, etc. - the game leaves all the possibilities and choices up to you. Some notes that there is no combat system in this game (well, if you want to fight monster or bad guys, there are many of games out there to choose) / also there is no multiplayer or coop system in this game at the moment (which is a big shame for me, this game can become a wholesome experience with others). _childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It's not your average farming game as you'd expect, so I'd recommend getting some information first if it's a game you'd enjoy. Many people may feel like the things you do are repetititve and they're right - basically you do the same things every day:Improve your little towns, hire people for your towns (if they aren't full), create seeds, plant those seeds on the big evertree so worlds can grow from those seeds (the worlds change with the seeds you create) and then visit your worlds to get rid of the "corruption" by planting and growing plants, getting rid of corrupted plants, helping the animals on the islands out, and so on daily until the world is "finished" - which means cleaned from the corruption.So basically you visit your worlds everyday and do those tasks again and again. Surely not everyone's tea.While working on your worlds you'll get loot, which can contain decorations for your town, "ingredients" for your seeds, walls for your town's houses etc. From chests you can sometimes even get hairstyles and clothes. Sometimes there's some puzzles, too.It's the perfect game for when you want to chill out, as there's no stress to do anything. It doesn't matter how fast or slow you work through the worlds. Some worlds are really beautiful, others are weird or even funny. There are many things to discover which is motivating to keep on working.You can befriend the animals you meet on the worlds and adopt them and take them with you to your towns or put them into one of the nature zones found between your little towns, where they can live. One little detail I really love and want to point out is the ability to change the plants, the grass and the trees in your towns. So when you visit worlds and gather things like fruits there. Or nuts from smaller bushes, you can take them with you and you can use them in one of your towns to change the appearance. So for example, if I find a funny looking bush that I want for my town, and it has some nuts on it, I can gather one, take it to my town and change the plants appearance to resemble that bush that I found on my world (feature unlocks after a little bit of playing though).So you can really make very different towns, even with blue grass, pink grass, mushroom trees and so on. There's a lot.I picked it up in a sale and it was very worth it. The standard price is worth it imo, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like Harvest Moon, with some Atelier and No Man's Sky tossed in. It offers all the rewards of real life gardening, but more accessible, you get to see something grow under your tender love and care.  Then you love it, let it go, and start planning for something new.First, the visuals in the game are gorgeous. Sometimes all I will do is explore to take pretty pictures. The music is beautiful and calming. The game play itself is very fun. And there's SO Much to see and discover. You can tell that the creators and artists, etc, put thought and passion into every detail. Can’t stress enough how absolutely stunning the visuals are. The way they managed to capture the changes in lighting at different times of day, and how it's an all-encompassing mood. You can actually see the lighting creep across the ground and show the angles of the setting sun. And when the night starts to hit and the aurora borealis sky meets up with the fireflies and neon lights of the towns? I'm in awe every time.Nothing felt generic or rushed. The story is incredibly deep, which I did not expect going into the game. The detail of the pastel-esque digital drawings have so much life in them that show the events of the story even when the images are static. It makes me want to bust out my digital drawing tablet every time. And ahh, I love the dialogue between our sweet parents Coppertop and Book! And all the little details into their family life. Also, the humor in the game is delightful. (Those cheeky Everkids!) And since the biomes make the game virtually endless, you don't have to start a new game to find something else to do.You'll also work on restoring the various towns that were at the foot of the Evertree. You'll be able to build new buildings, take in new townsfolk and assign them places to work, and even customize the various buildings and place various decorations. You can even mine, hunt for bugs, adopt various critters, and even go fishing. There's no combat, and you can't die, so it's a pretty chill experience.You are free to do what you want, at your own pace - if you give it time, and the right mindset, this game teaches you the joy of following your heart and whims in the moment.  Would you like to catch a lovely fish, carry it into your beautiful custom lit and decorated town, marvel at the beauty of it all, then throw that floppy wet thing at annoying Tammy who told you that you work too hard? Well that's what I just did anyway. :PExploration is rewarded with real quality, and sometimes a bit of silly - I found something amazing in a cave I never would have found if I didn't try to jump into water I probably shouldn't have and landed on a lillypad.  Also a tree gave me my favourite hat!The mood is perfect - the way the music and visuals swell my silly squishy heart while I'm progressing a new seed, or simply cuddling my new pets, sometimes leaves me in a puddle of warm fuzzyness.At the ends of several long days, it has been a comfort to immerse myself in the worlds I helped create. To me, this game represents three important and much needed things:  creativity, kindness, and hope.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy game with a variety of tasks you can focus on or delay as you like. The core loop is repetitive but the variations you encounter within each type of activity make up for it and keep things feeling fresh. For example, the World Seeds randomly generate locations with a different look and feel although the core tasks in each location are the same.The game incorporates - gardening, pets, city building, and very light platforming/puzzle solving to advance the major plot points.The story reveal is mostly predictable from the start of the game, so you must really like the core loop of either too-easy town management or gardening -- this is important! You MUST like the gardening/cleanup and/or town management elements of the game enough to like repeating it. Otherwise the game will just be a boring slog.Despite the procedural generation to make every playthrough "different", there's not much point in actually playing through more than once.Encountered only one serious bug so far, and it's an annoying one -- when you collect an achievement, the game might lock up with no inputs recognized. So save your game before picking up achievements. Don't rely on Autosaves since you don't really know how much progress you'll end up rolling back with an autosave.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I have some mixed feelings about it, I recommend Grow: Song of the Evertree wholeheartedly. The environments are stunning, and the gameplay is quite relaxing. My biggest complaint (if it can really be call that) is that the worlds are procedurally generated. I loved the previous game that the developers made, Yonder, mostly because of its exploration aspects. I adored wondering around the different biomes, finding all the little secrets. Grow also has exploration as part of the game, but a lot of it takes place on the worlds you make, and at least, personally, I've never been a great fan of procedurally generated environments. That being said, I saw in the reviews that some people actually love it! So, this is just a very personal nitpick. I'm already super excited to see what the Prideful Sloth team makes next!

_childDocuments_.review: 47.3h (based on the in-game clock, 100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (8 achievements). No. is a game where you build a village and restore a world. You'll have to plant and water trees to turn barren lands into lush greenery.- A lot of activities to do- Freedom to build the village however you want- The gameplay cycle is too repetitive with nothing new to add- Animation cutscenes are too long, especially when petting animalsIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 has great-looking visuals. It's always nice to see how the land that you tend to be something beautiful after you are done with it. The change was done little by little as you tend to it daily, making you appreciate it more, especially when you do it for the first time.There isn't much to the story. You'll get a piece of a story of what happened after you collect the fragment in each region, where you'll get a few sentences about it. You already know what you must do at the beginning of the game, though, and your objective won't change from there. That being said, the storytelling was done well. I like the artwork displayed during the cutscene, and the words that were used at that time were brief and easy to understand.The game was divided into two regions: the world seed areas and the town areas. In the town areas, you explore the island to find some puzzles or points of interest. The world seed areas are the area where you can gather the essences needed to build buildings for the town and restore the barren lands into greeneries.The town areas are divided into several districts. You can only explore the first district and the area surrounding it at first. That being said, there are still a lot of areas to cover to explore, with some optional secrets here and there.One thing that you must explore in the town areas is the vault, where you must solve some puzzles to receive a fragment. The puzzles are very easy to solve - you mostly just have to walk. However, reaching them might be another matter. Some vaults can be tricky to reach, although it won't give you issues as long as you explore everything that the game has to offer. You can build anything in the town. You'll be given a plot of land and it's up to you how to design the town. You can put on decorations, place some buildings, and even customize the walls and add decorations to that same building. The latter makes it easier to distinguish one building from the other. Some buildings will give you additional items that you can buy, although money can be an issue at the beginning.It's hard to get money at the beginning. The same goes for essences, the currency you use to build buildings, actually. However, you'll be able to easily get more as you progress - I even got more money than I needed by the time I finished the game. The essences are another thing since you still need to work for them - you can only get them by harvesting items in the world seed areas, but luckily, you won't need them that much. Residents are lifeless. Some residents will come to live in the districts, and you can tend to their issues. Sometimes, they will ask you to finish a quest, sometimes they want you to talk to them. I find tending to their needs to be useless. The quests are recycled from a list, and finding them can be problematic - sometimes they won't even appear in the area that the game points to. It's just a waste of time.You can put a world seed into a seed planter to turn it into a new world. The world that comes out will be randomized, but the essences you can harvest from it will be predetermined based on the essences that you use to create the seed. In this area, your job is to turn the barren lands into lush greenery.There will be a set of actions that you can do for the land each day. You'll clear weeds, plant seeds, water plants, and sing to make them grow. Do it for a few days, and a new area will spawn. This cycle will be repeated three times until the world is fully healed. You still can harvest your hard work before the world is fully healed, though. As new areas open, old areas will be healed and fully grown, allowing you to harvest anything that was in it: fruits, nuts, rocks, fish, insects - you can even chop the trees to get wood if needed. All of these resources can be converted into essences, which can be used for your town building needs.Insects look too similar. Some insects can be rarer than others, but it's hard to spot them in the wild. It feels as if they are only different in name due to the randomization aspect. Luckily, the same doesn't happen to fish.And that's everything that the game has to offer. Despite the randomization, I didn't find a lot of variations. In 6 world seeds that I had fully grown, I saw the same patterns used several times. Heck, I even found the same puzzles and caves in it. I'd rather have the game omit the randomization part altogether if the variation is not this many.I finished the game in 47.3h. My Steam playtime was shorter because there was some offline playtime caused by my internet disconnection. I had fully grown 6 world seeds: 5 perfects, 1 not. The game can be finished faster if you don't fully grow the world seeds, though. That's where the grindy part of the game comes from.The gameplay loop is too repetitive for my taste. It might be fun at the first few worlds, seeing the world grow with your own eyes. However, there is nothing new added to the mix, and the animation where you are taking care of the animals and flying is taking so much time.As for the difficulty, the game isn't difficult at all. You might have issues keeping up with the daily task if you have a lot of things to do, but there isn't any deadline and you can always finish it the next day. That's if you ignore most of the residents' needs, though. It'll take forever if you decide to finish their needs and do whatever else you have to do.I don't know why, but the game crashed a lot. Luckily, autosaves are plenty. Also, there is no bulk sell option. I had to use an auto clicker to sell 99 of my items to save my mouse from breaking. is a good game that overstayed its welcome. It might work as a very short game, although sadly, it decided that it's a good idea to make 6 districts with nothing new to add to the gameplay, forcing you to repeat the same thing 6 times. You'll get everything that the game has to offer within the first few hours of playing the game. Since I got bored playing it, I'm afraid I couldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited for this game, but once the intro ends, it was instant disappointment.The character creation was absolutely appalling. The very first thing you see is the word "gender" (immediate red flag when inappropriately associated with character generation) followed by the symbols for both male and female sexes as well as a third made-up sign that just gives you another female-sexed character that looks a bit nerdier. Why this was added makes no sense, and should've just been left out. The "sliders" for various options don't actually slide, and you have to guess where to click in the hopes of seeing the various options. There's also a tab with a bunch of shapes that are presumably meant for body shape, but you can't actually see what they do because of the clunky outfit.But let's move past this huge opening disappointment and onto the next. Your only companions in the beginning are a book and a cauldron who each make one basic sound every time they "speak". Perhaps this was to save on budget, but it really gets annoying fast. At the end of the little Q&A infodump (or when you've had enough of the noises), you're given your "alchemical tools" - which are just a bunch of gardening supplies - and it's off to restore the "worlds".I'll be perfectly honest here. The graphics are MOSTLY cute, and the music isn't bad, but everything else just falls flat. It's a very mechanical gameplay that reads more like a cheap copy of the Harvest Moon franchise with far less effort put into it. The language in this universe apparently lacks any form of gender, with EVERYONE being referred to in the neuter, including the protagonist. One would think they could have taken the time to at least incorporate the concept of gender into the text so kids who didn't grow up speaking a genderless language such as Turkish could understand what's going on better - especially since the overly simplistic gameplay and cartoony graphics seem aimed primarily at kids.There are also bugs in the game that can be frustrating (and a last straw for some) that seem unlikely to be ever fixed.So when you consider the bugs, overly monotonous gameplay, lack of gender in the text, and insultingly terrible character generation, this is one game that is sure to disappoint. Perhaps one day some intrepid modder will come along and fix all of these problems, but until then, don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is filled with creativity. The worlds you grow can look so nice, so unique, it is just nice to see.Sadly, this creativity is untapped.  The buildings you can build are just meh. You can decorate them, but the options are really limited, and the way you get decorations is full RNG. So, to decorate a city in one theme, is nearly impossible.The city building is really empty. The buildings has no real functions, so you can just build a city with only houses in it and it will still generate you "money". The residents you get are random, so it takes a lot of time to get the kind you want (for example one who's dream job is a shopkeeper).And the bulidng limit just worsens this part. You are already limited by the terrain, but you can only build a certain amount of buildings. And this goes to decorations too, which makes your cities really empty. The game has a lot of puzzles and dungeons in it. And, it shows that this game is intended for all ages. They are really simple and fast to solve - clear. These are the two biggest issues with the gameplay. Everything takes time in it. Too much time. More than what would be reasonable. And it is really repetitive. Growing worlds is always the same chores. Again and again and again. It easily overshadows the creativity behind them, with how boring it is.And this is true to the main storyline too. Unlock a city, go to a dungeon, solve a puzzle, reach 100% happiness in said city, repeat. This has problems too. Because you can't create nice looking characters. Only boring or ugly ones. And the choices are really limited. Later on you get a lot of extra outfits and accessories, but still not enough to fix them.Nothing more than you would expect. Cartoonish graphics, which looks nice overall, but there is nothing outstanding in it. Just what you expect.Sadly, there are bugs in this game. Not working generated puzzles, graphical glitches and i even managed to find a game breaking bug, which could only be solved by starting a new game. How nice.As with the graphics, it is just there. If you turn them off and listen to a podcast instead, while playing, you will notice no difference, since there are no voice acted lines. Just ambient sounds and some music.There is some, but not too much. And it is really easy to predict. They did a really big miss here.There are some interesting characters but, they have only some minor roles. And after it is over, they have noting to say anymore. Even those who you think will be integral to the story... well they are not. They are just there.There are multiple races and an interesting world that the devs thought up. It has a lot of pontential in it... but we learn almost nothing in the game. No codex entries, no expositions, just what is absolutely neccesary, to understand what is going on.There is no replay value in this game. You can just infinetly create new worlds (until you get bored), rebuild the cities any time, so there is no point for a reset. And the story... well that does not worth it.They had a great idea, they had the creativity to support it, but they missed ther mark and it became, sadly, a bad game...

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to not recommend this game because the world itself is beautiful and this game had one of my favorite character hats I've ever seen before (Cat ears with a bubble wand and when you run bubbles form which is amazing) however, the game is extremely repetitive and the whole gist of the game is to clear an area of the land, move in villagers, complete objectives to get the town up to snuff until the next area, and while clearing that area, you explore different seed worlds to get materials. To get all of the achievements you do this loop several times. It was fun/cute the first two times. The rest of it started to feel like a chore. _childDocuments_.review: A beautiful charming little game.If you're looking for something that doesn't require too much thought and just want to relax, Grow: Song of the Evertree can't really do you much wrong. However, Don't expect anything complex. Outside the simple growing mechanics, You'll be completing a checklist in each town and then moving on to the next.There is plenty of customisation options for both your townies and buildings. Tons of wall paper, decorations, hairstyles which is shame because, they're all just purely cosmetic and have practically no impact on the game outside the stat boosters and even then. They seem to make little difference outside levelling up villagers to meet level requirements for the town check list by the time I hit the last town, I barely even cared what I was picking.I completed it 22 hours, However, Near the end it felt padded and repetitive. It probably could have gotten away with a town less or two.For Steam Deck Users:It's worth it's Verified status. I played it from start to completion on my Deck, I played on the highest settings and for the most part it stayed at 60FPS and occasionally dropping into the 40's. A great little game if you're looking to kill 30 minutes on the go.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game, relatively simple to complete the main storyline. It's a bit repetitive; while there's a moderate amount of procedural generation in fine details, the broader strokes are pretty same-y. There's two basic type of critter to tame - dog and cow. The world seeds have some similar elements - there's a third iteration "big flat plain" that annoyed me because it was harder to divide the restoration tasks up into easier chunks, and it procced four or five times out of the eight world seeds I planted.Honestly, I suspect I played the game the wrong way. I found one of the "perfect world" recipes early on, and stuck to making the known recipes, which meant I was able to get every element with just seven world seeds (and one of those was, strictly speaking, unnecessary). If I had experimented more with the alchemy recipes, I think I might have had more variety.And that's the real core of this game. Don't go into it planning to rush. You can do that, but it won't be all that fun. Take your time. Experiment with "wrong" alchemy recipes. Kit your districts out to the nines. Have a critter companion for every home (I don't know if you can actually do that, btw, there might be limits). Follow the Magic School Bus mantra: Take chances, make mistakes, get messy. In other words, have fun.One of the best parts of the game for me was finding all the little hidden things, whether they had some practical purpose, like the Leapgate, or were just a fun easter egg, like the two warring cults. It really encourages you to explore, in a way that iron or gold chest #8465 just can't do.Some things I wish the game had (perhaps in an expansion or patch?):1. A way to move villagers from one district to another. If I want to make the Islands district my shopping district, it's a bit annoying that all the villagers I'm getting there want to be ranchers, while the Plains district keeps getting residents that want to be hairdressers.2. Refining the procedural generation to not block your ability to actually interact with some objects. On several of my worlds, I was unable to actually interact with several types of tree, as the hitbox became too big, preventing my character from getting close enough to chop or shake it.3. More variety. As I said above, there's really only two types of critter: dog and cow. The details might differ - one dog might have antlers, and a cow might have a bear's face - but their behavior is the same in every way. There's really only two or three types of caves that spawn. Etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually enjoy farming-style games, but this game is more about growing your world seeds rather than farming and selling crops. Either way, I find Grow: Song of the Evertree to be extremely addictive. Grow has a good gameplay loop between managing the towns at the Evertree, and taking care of the world seeds you're growing. Every world seed has its own special fruit, bugs, fish, and animals to collect, and the best part is - you get to create the world seeds yourself from essences you've harvested. This can lead to some really beautiful, or really cursed worlds depending on which essences you choose to mix.Managing the towns is also more fun than I thought it would be, reminds me a lot of the Wiiware title My Life as a King but without the dungeons, for the 2 other people who played that game lolGrow is very well polished, I didn't come across any glitches during my playthrough and I am the type of person who will try to glitch my way through walls and geometry and stuff like that. It has the feeling of a game made by a professional team, it almost feels like it could have been a late Gamecube or early Wii title.In summary, I definitely recommend Grow: Song of the Evertree because it's charming, addictive, relaxing, and a lot of fun. I recommend this game to people who like farming games, simulation games, and games which allow you to customise a lot. Games I find it similar to are: MySims, My Life as a King, Spore, Animal Crossing, Harvest Moon.

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing, So much exploring to do with huge replay-ability potential as each game is different (Except the story line) I like having a baddy to defeat (Thorny hedgerow) but no fighting, and get rewarded for being helpful and doing positive things. Sometimes you just need a break from wielding a staff and smiting things. The art style is wonderful. The music is really nice.  Easy to play with either keyboard or controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I get the strong impression these folks make games purposefully for depressed adults who want to taste childhood joy again, and they absolutely hit the mark with that. Plenty to do, and varied enough that the repetitive parts don't feel annoying.Beautiful. Soothing. And the writing has genuinely made me laugh aloud several times. Would be a great game to get for your child, but it's complex enough to be absolutely enjoyable as an adult too. Also; you get to cuddle the fluffy fae dragon thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

But then I became "un-lost" and played for another 50 hours before I got to where they were talking about.This is a fun game (the fishing is annoying), but after reinvigorating 4 districts, the repetition becomes painful. _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game that really scratched the itch for a relaxing experience that also has some level of depth.The town building mode doesn't feel lackluster, or like an afterthought. Exploring Alaria is rewarding and interesting. I love discovering the areas littered around the world. I also appreciate the ability to take things at my own pace for the most part and just enjoy the game without being rushed through everything.It's just beautiful to look at and thoroughly enjoyable to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying the game's beginning and gradual introduction of new elements, and would quite recommend it as a zen title, but then got hit with a reproducible, reported bug that crashes the game every single time when you claim a certain in-game achievement for a reward. I can probably keep playing past that point by ignoring that claim (and saving before trying to claim any other), but the fact is that the developers apparently abandoned the game within 2 months of release, leaving behind these critical game breaking bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 highly recommend so far. I've had troubles putting the game down, similiar to how I felt when I played Stardew Valley for the first time. It has the farming/tending aspects of a farming game, but on a much chiller scale. You don't have to do pesky things like refill your watering can, you just run around and water. You don't really have to worry about making profit when you're re-vitalizing a dying world. If you don't complete a task, nothing negative happens. If you don't water your plants one day, it's cool you can just water them the next day.It's very satisfying to complete an area of your island. There's a whole town building aspect & an endlessly huge world that I've barely scratched the surface of at 5 hours. There's decorating. There's alchemy. There's cooking. There's fishing. It's like Animal Crossing, but with significantly more to do & more space to explore.Music is beautiful, art style is gorgeous. The scenery is beautiful & the creatures are ridiculously cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest and say I bought this purely because it was on sale and I was bored lol. But in the first hour of playing it, I can CONFIDENTLY say that this game is a must. If you love anything Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing with TONS of in depth story line that gets you hooked, I 1000% guarantee you'd love this game. The art style is divine, the graphics are smooth, allows for individual personality, has a 10/10 story line, hours of gameplay so you can take your time, and the best of all, they are inclusive to non-binary//Gender fluid//LGBTQ+ folk! BUY IT <3
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is very sweet and clearly handcrafted with love, the actual game loop is just very tedious and boring. There's no real freedom of movement - you can't swing your hammer anytime, only when standing in front of a hammer-prompted object (and even then, sometimes your character whiffs). The act of tending to a growing world is just... by... holding a lot of buttons, and madly tapping others to equip the right tool. Over and over. The base building aspect is very cute and fun, but it wasn't worth suffering through daily tedium of the world seed aspect for me.Like, you don't even get to choose what to plant or where to plant it. There's just plant spots and a generic seed bag. Most times you destroy a rock, a new seed spot appears. And then you have to swap to your seed bag spamming through the wheel. And then to your watering can. Now hold the button to water. Repeat this like 20x a day. It's just not... fun.But I feel bad saying that because the game is otherwise super cute. The sound design is fantastic, the models are adorable. But you can't even meaningfully interact with your flying mount! It doesn't follow you around, it barely does anything... you can pet it at the roost area but that's it. I'm pretty sad about that in particular, because the model is so soft and the design is so cute, I wish I could have more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a laid back game that I am enjoying almost as much as Stardew Valley, but for entirely different reasons. This is a huge, explore-your-world game, with some not too difficult puzzles (at least to where I currently am), cutesy but very detailed graphics, and almost no pressure.  If you like games like this, you'll probably love it.  It incorporates almost all of the casual game styles.  I love foraging, collecting, and hoarding items in games, so this is right up my alley. The relationships are forced and very shallow, but I understand the game not focusing on those. You are there to explore, build, create and nurture. No stress at all.  I suppose I can see how this would be boring for goal driven  gamers, or gamers  who like high tension games.  This is not me at all.  I hate timers, permadeath (except for roguelikes), and...well, consequences. I game to relax.  This game is ideal for relaxing, and is very easy to get sucked into.  I've had it for a grand total of 4 days and am already almost at 30 hours.  I also have caught myself not going to bed until 3 or 4 am.  I love the worlds and Essences. I love breaking down items and discovering which weird items make what Essences.  I love creating almost any world I want from Essences and growing it myself, and collecting everything I find.  I REALLY like having an inexhaustible backpack, because I hate to not have at least 5 of everything I discover. Your main teachers are a little annoying, but bearable. The Everkin are adorable, especially the Everkids, but their home is so so confusing. It took me forever to navigate it. There are some amusing jokes, and lots of pop culture winks. I don't care so much about town planning, but it's not so onerous it can't be done.   The difficulty level is turned way down on this one, and that's how I like my relaxing games.  I'm not even that worried about finishing the game right now because there's so much to do/see and so many worlds to make. I actually have the opportunity to discover EVERYTHING eventually.  That's rare in most games, unless you like the torture of being an completionist.  (Katamari ruined me for completionism.  It haunts me. )Don't expect this game to be something it's not.  This is a highly enjoyable, stress-free game that is sorely needed right now.  It offers hours and hours of creative, serene gameplay, but be prepared to have  lots of repetitive tasks, almost all the time.  If you find that zen like I do and can zone out on it, then you'll love it. Otherwise.....I'd look at some live play and see if it makes your frustration level ratchet.  This, in my opinion, is a truly fine game of its type.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Crossing meets No Man's Sky. Very cute, a tad repetitive but in a comforting way. Incredibly wholesome. Also, inventory management is just not a thing, you'll have to live with chaos. All that said, I am still playing this game daily, well after 100%. It's just so lovely and soothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Does this have an in depth story and exciting cutscenes? Not really, especially after the few hours. Does it do what I want it to? Absolutely. This gives me the same calm monotony of MMOs or farming games once the story is complete, but without the stresses of approaching deadlines. _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Save often. It's not bad but it can crash randomly. I haven't seen a pattern since it's happened to be only twice.It's a good game for just relaxing and wanting to zen out. I'll update the review when I play more!EDIT:So I've played more. I'm honestly neutral about it. I will warn you, you will not like this game if you want to progress quickly.IT'S EXTREMELY tedious, although it's meant to be that way. Also, I should clarify that you don't do any city building on the worlds you create (at least not that I have ever seen even looking at the wiki).Your city building is reserved for the "main zone". It takes 9 days approx in order to fully revitalize a world if you go there and complete the clean up tasks every single day. Also, in terms of creating your own worlds, I'll note that it took me approximate 3 hours to unlock the feature to start creating worlds.And for better or worse, the worlds appearance is still random (asides from traits assigned to it from the essences you use) . I don't have a problem with this but I do question some visuals. Why does my "elegant" princess biome world have trees topped with poop emojis???I won't deny it is nice tending to the worlds and watching them grow from a barren land to something lush and alive.And again, there are the hard crashes I experienced which never got patched, and it seems Prideful Sloth isn't maintaining the game anymore. My verdict is.....Buy it when HEAVILY discounted.It has the issue of being big as a late with the depth of a puddle to put it bluntly. I won't say ocean because to be honest, the worlds you revive are pretty tiny.I got the game on discount for $10 and that's all I would pay for it honestly. But at the full price? I cannot recommend the game even though I'll keep playing it to relax. I will say this is a good game for children, and I'm sure that was the target audience. But again, wouldn't spend more than $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: While I am reviewing it positively, it's more of a neutral recommendation.Pros:No real time constraints.Randomly generated islands gives at least some variety.Village building is highly customizable.No needlessly difficult steam achievements.Can save anywhere, and it regularly autosaves in case of the rare crash.Simple and forgiving mechanics.Cons:You're hand-held through damn near everything you do. Every time there is a new non-randomly-generated puzzle you come across, the game slowly pans across the entire length of the room, showing every part of the puzzle and where you need to go. Every time, no matter how simple or braindead the puzzle is. When you enter a new resource island that still isn't fully completed yet, the game will always pan over the most recent area, despite how obviously visible the "problem" areas are normally. This very much feels like it's made with young children in mind, who need to be shown everything they need to do every time. Every time there's any "main" story stuff that needs to be done, the main side characters will not shut up during the day until you do it, despite there being a pinned mission for it. The hand-holding is my main complaint of the game, and I almost gave it a negative review because of it, because of just how obnoxious it gets over time.Human villagers almost universally look bad. You can customize them to an extent, but it still looks awkward.Despite the randomness, there's only 2 real critters: dogs/dog-hybrids and buffalos. No other animals really exist despite the vast differences in various plants in all the biomes you can make.I enjoyed it enough to finish the game and get all the achievements. I spent a fair bit of time trying to "perfect" stuff, but I eventually realized it's just not worth it. Harvested resources eventually become pretty useless, and the main currency you collect eventually is just 99% daily passive income.If you're looking for a casual time waster, or possibly a safe game for a child, this is it. If you want something with deep mechanics, looks elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful. Both adorable and sweet as well a fun.I can't express enough how much I have already enjoyed this game. 18 hours in and I still feel like I am nowhere near the end game and the fact I can create so many world seeds in which all new worlds will be different is reason enough. The animals that are mishmashed together is another reason I can't stop creating new worlds as well as just how beautiful and cute everything is.Pros- Every plant pulled, fruit harvested, rocks broken, seeds planted....etc, all feels like it has a purpose and makes it so much easier to grind and collect.- Customization of areas is fun. I love making each individual building unique.- Building "decoration" to further customize is always a positive in my book.- The soundtrack is relaxing and makes it easy to lose track of time and play just for the music.- THE EVERKIN ARE THE MOST ADORABLE CREATURES EVER. (Please make a plush for real life)Cons- Not 100% in love with the decoration and building limits in the town areas. I really wish I could put as much as I want.- Wish that you could move new residents into every area so everyone can have their dream job (I feel like if you are creating a better world you should be able to have a Utopia)- Not a huge fan of no maps I tend to waste a lot of the day walking around and not being able to really have more that 2 world seeds going, manage those, finish quests, and explore within the time allotted.- Out of all of this the fishin mechanic sucks, takes forever to catch fish and not really sure if the reeling in even works or has a trick to it.In all honesty I recommend this game, it was an impulse buy after seeing a youtuber (Raptor) play like 15 minutes of the game on youtube. Even bought it on release day without knowing. Just had to have it.Bring on more crafting games that involve even and inkling of alchemy.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Grow: Song of the Evertree is a fantastic game. The setting is fluffy and friendly but the story is well done. The central message is that you should take good care of your world, not exploit the natural ressources but rather restore harmony and balance with respect for the beings around you. While making a real difference regarding the ongoing destruction of nature in our real world can be quite hard at least in this game everything is possible.There is no combat and it takes a while for things to change so it feels like a real investment and a slow process. You can gather many different ressources and extract their essence to create new pocket-worlds within the tree. This is quite exciting because it is surprising how the new worlds can look like. The customization options in the various districts of the city you are rebuilding are great and you can invest many hours "to make things pretty". There are extremely cute creatures to discover, my personal favorite being the so-called everkids. There is no pressure and you can finish everything in your own pace so it is not stressful at all.The controls are a bit clunky and it takes a while to not get stuck and find your way. But the main principle of the game is engaging and makes it easy to overlook the few bugs that will hopefully get fixed in future patches and updates.Overall I rate grow with  and recommend it to everyone who enjoys relaxing games like Animal Crossing.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second play-through (First time on Nintendo) and it is just as good as I remember it. I have been enjoying it just as much as I did the first time, which is a rare case for me. I usually get bored very easily.One of my favorite things about this game is that it's really unique. There really isn't anything to effectively compare it to. The developers did a good job putting something out there that's different, but still has all of the elements that make cozy games fun like tasks and customization. It's so fun being able to contribute to growing worlds around you. It is single-handedly up to you to literally grow each world from scratch. You start with the corrupted bare-bones, and through your work on the tree every day, you can grow everything into a luscious, highly inhabited world.Another thing I really like are the graphics. They are so cute and unlike anything I have ever seen in the game. They really contribute to the ethereal and whimsical feeling of the game. The characters sometimes have off-the wall outfits and it's fun to see how everyone changes over time.All in all, Grow: Song of the Evertree is a must-play for anyone who loves cozy games. It's laid back, yet still has so much to offer in terms of captivating game-play. The game changes so much as you play it, and it's so satisfying to watch it come together. Give this one a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not just calming, it's meditative. It's the kind of game that I've been waiting for for a long time, and the execution is even better than I'd expect--really, it's just adorable, and the mechanics are enjoyable. I was a little nervous about getting this game originally due to the reviews (one in particular of a user encountering glitches to the point of feeling that the game is unfinished), but for what it's worth I personally haven't encountered any noticeable glitches yet. I've only played on Steam Deck, so I'm not sure how the game fares on PC, but I can say that it plays perfectly on Steam Deck. It really is a pleasure, and the controls feel smooth and natural.I'll give a disclaimer right away, this game is not going to be for everyone. I suspect many people will find it repetitive or even boring, and I'll expand on that further in a bit. But if you enjoy the process of building up a dilapidated area into a flourishing wonderland, this game will be right up your alley, and the procedurally-generated mini-worlds that inhabit the larger game ensures that you will be able to scratch that itch to your heart's content. It's a bit mindless, but in the best way possible, however much sense that makes. In spite of being a laid back and chill experience, it maintains the feeling of accomplishment and dopamine hits that come from gaming. There are achievements, some rudimentary crafting mechanics (when it comes to making new worlds with the components obtained from sprucing up previous worlds), and some collecting elements as well. I think a game like House Flipper or (to a less degree) PC Building Simulator might come close to the type of experience it provides. Although it follows a storyline, it technically has infinite replayability as you can continue to craft new planets for as long as you care to."For as long as you care to" is a significant caveat here, as I mentioned earlier that this game could easily feel repetitive or even boring to people who are not into these types of laid back "cozy games." As I said earlier, it feels game-y in its mechanics with plenty of dopamine hits, but it's not particularly challenging. It's very casual. I suspect that the intended audience for this game will know who they are, I just felt like it was important to include this disclaimer for those it applies to. To everyone else, I think you'll love this game! Especially now while it's on sale :)

_childDocuments_.review: The lack of negative reviews is disturbing. And the amount of people comparing this to things like Stardew Valley or My Time At Portia sound like bots, tbh. If you go into this game with the expectation that it's ANYTHING like those you're going to be very, VERY disappointed.I have no idea what people are on calling this a "farming sim" in any way, and the city building aspect is so shallow, the world is the definition of "big and empty" with the space between areas seemingly exsisting to pad out game time. _childDocuments_.review: First, this is fundamentally a kids game. Which is fine! There's no violence. The stakes are low. There's a couple of funny jokes and lots of cute animals.Second, the game is like 20% too long. At first I was drawn in by exploring all the areas I unlocked, but as the game progressed, less and less secrets were revealed. Everything seemed frontloaded. Third, just because a game is for kids doesn't mean it needs to be simplified to the point of being trivial. The townbuilding is what I was looking forward to the most and it is just totally barebones (...but still enough to keep me engaged, I'll say that much). The unskippable camera zooms on every aspect of gameplay were pretty annoying too. Fourth, it is fundamentally weird for a game about ecological disaster to warn you about the dangers of taking more than you need in the tutorial, and then encourage you to....harvest everything in sight, all the time, forever, with zero consequences. It's not unique to this game, and is endemic to the genre, but it's something that continues to irritate me in "environmental" games. I would recommend this game for family play, or if you are comfortable bailing after the first few hours. I would not recommend this game with absolutely no qualifiers.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a wonderful game, i absolutely love it!It's relaxing, soothing, cute, bright, fluffy, soft and squishy at the same time.Who doesn't love cute and tiny creatures that you can tummy rub?! The game is a simulation type game where you create new "worlds" to nurture and grow.While doing so you attract folk to your starting habitat that you need to keep happy by providing housing, jobs  and do some small quests. The one thing you have to mind is the people who you allow to stay in a house, be mindful off the job preference as you need to be able to build the location for them to work at (e.g. temple build comes around your 2nd plot and a hairsalon build comes around your 3rd plot).There is no rush, you can do as much as you like in a day or slack of and just relaxe and take in the view.The game is beautiful and fluffy, so wondering around is a day well spend :)

_childDocuments_.review: Ammendment: Not recommended if you care about completing the story or unlocking everything. The "puzzles" to get to the next area are awful, especially the mid-game platforming one in the forest area; I literally got trapped in that one with no way out but through or reverting to an older save file.It's fun, but it doesn't feel like a full release and needs more polish before I can recommend it in good conscience.Relaxing and fun at the same time, the big thing that distinguishes Grow is creating your own world varieties and seeing how mixing different traits affects the results. For example, I have a creamy world and a sparkly one as well as a frozen one, all with secondary traits.The main story dialog's so fun that I don't want to give spoilers. It reminds me of GlaDOS in Portal, but without the tone of trying-to-kill-you-politely.The menu music is excellent such that I purposefully linger on the menu, which only Civilization IV has done for me before.When collection starts getting tedious because a world's fully developed, the game lets you hire a helper who collects stuff for you.My main feedback for the developers is that conversations and quests with generic NPCs need a lot more variety to make the townbuilding feel real. (Does everyone love dressing bugs in formal attire of all things when they want a bug?) The lovely quirkiness gets diluted a ton when everyone's saying the same thing. Also a very large percentage of dialog that's over-the-top complimentary or rude. Just saying that they don't feel like talking would be enough.Also, could phrases of the menu music be integrated into the game itself instead of the almost non-music "song" to represent the Evertree's song entering the world? It doesn't even have to be in the character's voice or language to fit with the lore, but I fully expected something musical to be the "Song of the Evertree" and was disappointed. You have such excellent source material to work with already.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Grow is a adorable and comfy game for any age that combines 'Citybuilding Sim', 'Open World Exploring', 'Farming Sim' and 'Puzzle Platformer' in a beautiful and individual scenary. The Story: After the first introductionary story you're pretty much left on your own. The rest of the story is mostly told through cinematic throwbacks. You ain't gonna play this game for its stunning and interactive storyline, but there is some explanation to why you there and what happened at last.The Citybuilding Aspect: You can create your own villages within areas as you wish. You're able to customize your building with many little perks and can let your creativity flow with many design options. I did find the limitation of 20 building per area fairly low. I ended up having a lot of open space and either villagers with no work or no homes for any more villagers. I would love an additional perk to extend that limit as soon as you finish the main story to fully focus on this part. Also I found the balance of gaining money exponentially too high. For the first 2-3 areas I've been really struggling with income but after that I was constantly on the high end and could literally speedrun the other areas.The Open World: The game redeems everyone whos looking around strange corners or trying to climb a rather unusual mountain. Around any corner you may find a secret place or treasure. I found the exploring part a lot of fun, though the world do be fairly small, so for each area you will get to see everything in a good amount of time. The Evertree (Farming): In the beginning this looks fun and gives you something to do, while your villages are growing, though by the time it gets rather repetitive and annoying and really unnecessary. This part is not essential for the progress of the game, but it might be interesting to some people to discover some new worlds and species with it.Puzzle Platformer: The storyline is driven by little puzzleplatformer challenges you have to solve. I found them fairly easy to solve, but still each time there was a unique idea behind it, so it was always something new to figure out. For those parts though I'd wish to skip the tons of cinematic overviews of the rooms you enter. For me this ruined the flow and also the exploration part.Special Tip: I found mining and minerals to be most effective for the everlings and I had good experiences just using that to buy my wanted elements.Overall I am super happy with this game and don't regret a single second in there. It was super relaxing, interesting and adorable.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, relaxing, but tedious game.Grow puts you in the role of the last person who can hear the song of the Evertree (hence the name): a young apprentice out to save the tree from some evil vines. To do this, you plant world seeds up the tree, which produce randomly generated patches of land, which you then have to maintain by pulling weeds, planting seeds, removing debris, etc. You're rewarded for this with things to help you build towns down on the surface. You can also explore the surface, finding secrets and caves with more stuff for towns. And so on.Grow is one of those games where you need to be in the right mood to play. There's no combat, no conflict besides the main story, and you live your life building lovey-dovey towns and watering plants. The town building is quite fun, the exploration is enjoyable, and the world lore is well thought out. The music is decent and really builds the atmosphere, and the graphics are solid. It is a nice game to play.But, pulling weeds can get a bit monotonous. I found the gameplay on the surface to be fun, but the gameplay up the tree to be dull. It works, only if you don't want to think, just to relax and enjoy the mundane parts of life.I'll also note a big pet peeve of mine. At some point in the game, you have to enter these shrines to find pieces of the song. These consist of some small platforming puzzles that are relatively easy to complete.The problem is the game stops you with cutscenes on how to do it every time. For example, one shrine starts with two columns with slots in them. The cutscene shows you the path to an orb on the left, then an orb on the right. Alright, I can do that. I get the orbs, put them in the slots, and a door opens.In this next area is another two slots. Cool, so there must be two orbs to find. A cutscene stops you from exploring and shows you how to get the orbs... okay, I get it. I do it, a door opens, and the next room does THE SAME THING. A cutscene showing how to do the puzzle.It's like the game assumes you're an idiot, or a child. But even then, I think children can figure out how to complete these puzzles once they've done the first part. These shrines hold your hand to a frustrating degree.But other than that, fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much and am so glad I bought it because it is so good. If you have ever played Yonder it is very similar in a way but also very different. You look after multiple worlds you build yourself from "essences" and depending on the type of essences you use the worlds will look different. Along with this you look after and basically build your own town from scratch much like animal crossing, using essences gained from the worlds you grow. (Also you can pet the cute animals and take selfies with them which by itself is a 10/10)It is incredibly addictive and has a lot of stuff to do which feels very rewarding once completed. I highly recommend this to anyone that enjoyed playing Yonder, animal crossing, stardew etc...
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Only just released but the graphics on this game is very pretty, reminds of the Yonder trailers.  In short the tree has died due to people neglect, the wither or dead roots have taken over it and people have left the town, now as the only person there with the help of 2 characters, help put the tree back to life again and set up the town for people to return, while slowly pushing back the wither.  So much to do and difficult to work out what to do next, always keeps you busy........minor glitches but they are being fixed in next patch.....all in all a fun game to play......parts can be tedious but then again what game doesnt have those moments......
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so wholesome and lovely.  The music is really lovely and soothing, and there is no voice dialogue that can be jarring to a game like this.  You create a whole world and make it grow, with several journeys for you and your townspeople to go on.  It is very inclusive with several genders and configuration options for your character at the start, and the dialogue is very kind and compassionate.  This is a game that adults and kids will love to play over and over, since from start to finish, it is procedurally generated.  I highly recommend this to anyone wanting to relax and enjoy a stunning game. No fighting or violence in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Hm, it is kind of a gardening simulator, where you pull out or cut down weeds, plant beautiful flowers, water them, and sing to them to make them grow - in a world covered by the all-encroaching Withering. Sounds strange, but it is a fantasy world after all.You are an apprentice, living in a house together with a talking book and coppertop, and you have a dragon to ride. The rest of your people have fled the land, when the Withering destroyed their town and covered the whole land (and the large Evertree). But now your job is to revive the Evertree and destroy the Withering. Small creatures, the Everlings, help you, and tell you how to catch bugs or fish. So you run around with your axe, watering can, sickle, hammer, camera, fishing rod, insect net and seeds and work on the land to make it beautiful again, while you follow the story and talk with its cute inhabitants. Bring back the humans that fled the land, experiment with magical essences, and restore the old town around the Evertree to its former glory. Great soundtrack (I love the title song), ultrawidescreen support, gamepad support.A beautiful, relaxing gardening simulation in a fantasy world. There is always something to do, new things to discover or new creatures to meet.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty disapointed by this game.I really enjoyed their previous game, Cloud Catcher Chronicles. But this one fell flat for me.I haven't played for that long, but the game seems a bit boring and repetitive. It's just clean up the tree by smacking rocks, pulling weeds etc. Do this for several days, yay tree restored. Ok and now? Next tree.The same for the town district. Build X buildings, X decorations, find the song fragment, restore harmony, Done. Now? Next district. The story is ok, but not amazing. There were barely characters I cared about and they weren't very expressive. The everkin are cute, but also not super helpful.The previous game, technically maybe even had less content. But I really liked the roaming aspect of it. Wandering around from place to place, talking to people, doing the little quests and crafting. And wander on, or wander back to check on farms etc you built all around the place. This doesn't have that. Here you have a house and that's where you go back to. It just didn't do it for me. Usually I'm all about these types of games, and I don't always mind the repetition so much. Maybe this just missed some soul that the first game did have for me. I don't think I'll continue with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, but I just can't. I actually really enjoy games about cleaning up and fixing things, so I thought this would be a good fit, but there's just no point. Past the first island that you grow and clean up, you're making more randomly generated islands that need to be cleaned up and repaired for...no reason? In the beginning you have daily quests to fix up the starter island but eventually it's just "Do whatever". Then, there's the town management section, which plays like a completely different game. This is almost entirely unconnected to the island growing and improving part of the game, and it's a lot of waiting for more townsfolk to show up, even if you've built plenty of extra houses and job buildings. There's just not enough of a direction towards an end goal, and the core gameplay isn't compelling enough to play just for the sake of doing it. But hey, at least it looks pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually a big fan of games like this, farming and exploring etc. And I do really enjoy this game, but some of the game play does get a bit monotonous. Even though it doesn't really matter when you have to start a new day I do miss the ease of playing for as many hours as you want in games like Animal crossing without having to go to sleep. But you get a lot longer day time in this game than I have experienced in others and with the help of your flying companion  you can easily return home quickly. The game is fun and relaxing and you can find yourself playing for many hours at a time, but the contsant planting watering smashing chopping etc to grow your seed island does get a little tedious and I do recommend not trying to grow more than 2 at one time as you will easily lose track of how far you are in each island and there isn't enough time in the day to get to more than 2 seed islands and complete each one. But overall I am enjoying this game and I would recommend it to others who like these types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could just give this an in between thumb.   Some elements of this were super fun in the beginning, but became a grind later on, so I just can't totally recommend it, unless you get it cheap and have nothing better to play.Pros:  -It is very cute.           -In the beginning it is fun to collect resources and combine them and complete little islands.          -You are only going to die if you fall into the water.          -It was oddly satisfying to decorate the houses with "wallpapers".          -You could probably let a kid play this and they would be content just growing little islands and have fun.  I have some reservations about the story line, but there was nothing inappropriate that set my mom-alarm off. Cons: - The story is a bit weird and I ended up later just letting the cut scenes play while I went off and got a snack.          -The village job system was bewildering and hard to keep track of.  I muddled through enough to progress the story.          -The game was oddly taxing on my PC resources and I literally had to run a cooler to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy farming/life sim games, this game delivers. I'm only 15 hours in but I have to say it keeps surprising me and I'm thoroughly enjoying the story line so far. The only thing that's stumping me about the game is how to take adopted animals out of the storage, which really isn't the biggest issue. Other then that it's a lovely go at your own pace kind of game. I'd compare it to a mix of Ever Oasis on the 3DS & really most farming sims. The graphics blow me away, and I adore the character designing system in the beginning. I look forward to playing the rest of the game and expanding more worlds on the Evertree itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: a relaxing but incredibly basic game with half baked art direction that was abandoned 3-4 months after release. there are still game breaking bugs present. lots of promise in the beginning and certainly a relaxing game to play with a bit of visual variety, but it feels like 1/4th of a game. there is so much diversity that is hinted at with all the different types of essences that you can use to make your worlds, the promise of new things to overcome in your towns, but after the first few hours or about the first 3-4 tree worlds you finish, you have seen literally every interesting thing this game has to offer. they just did not finish it. you can get to the end of the main "story" sure but the game play progression is just not there and the actual impact of that story is negligible to non-existent. could've been great, as it stand it is somewhere around a 6 if you like the farming/chore simulation type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I liked mixing up weird concoctions and seeing what worlds would grow, and was often delighted by the results.  Even by the worlds with the... fleshier themes.  Objectively speaking, those are horrors that my Alchemist should feel bad for unleashing upon creation. She regrets nothing. The game has a few bugs and unfinished feeling areas, could really, really benefit from a compass or more precise guidence tool, the item distribution seems badly balanced, and the clothing options are weirdly un-gaudy considering the eye watering things you can do to buildings... but by and large is a just a nice soothing game to play. I like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played this game too much yet, but so far I think I can fairly say it's pretty good. The game sort of reminds me of MySims which I played a lot as a kid. The main objective is to revitalize your mini worlds, gather items and turn them into essences, create new worlds, and expand your town. I love seeing the different worlds you can create and I like turning the worlds into something pretty. If this doesn't interest you much and you dislike repetitive tasks then the game might not be right for you.The game isn't perfect though and there are some negatives. First of all, I dislike that you have to be in the exact right spot to perform an action, such as pulling a weed or chopping a tree. Secondly, I think it would be nice if we had an encyclopedia or something and it was easier to tell what items we haven't collected yet. Also, where to find certain items we want. The biggest negative though, is that I can't play it for too long because it gives me motion sickness even with mouse sensitivity lowered.Overall it's a very enjoyable game with beautiful graphics, fun game-play, and an interesting story. I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very relaxing and is not like your typical management game. There's always something to do each day, always something to tend to, always a new town to build etc. And I enjoy it for those aspects, but once you really get past your last town, there really isn't that much for you to do besides find some ruins to explore. The game doesn't have anything for the "end game" or after you've completed most of what you're supposed to complete. I also feel like it's very limited in the amount of NPCs you can really talk to. In the game there are only 3 NPCs you can talk to and have some sort of relationship with, which is not at all a lot compared to games like Stardew and Portia. Decorating your towns houses is also not as fun, as you're limited in the amount of decorations you can use for the houses and there isn't an easy way to get decorations over and over again (meaning sometimes your houses will just look plain silly lol) You can't decorate your own house or change the outside of it either, which is pretty disappointing considering it looks like such a shabby place at first. And is pretty open and empty as if it'd be the perfect place to decorate things. Other than all these negatives, if you're looking for something to turn your brain off too and just play while you zone out, then it's perfect I recommend. But if you're looking for a very deep, and pretty good management game and rpg like Stardew or Portia, there's nothing really here with the story. Which is a shame, because the game has the potential to be a great game just like those two and uniquely different. But there's just no effort put into the NPCs or the building mechanics. The only thing that seems truly fleshed out or the puzzles for the ruins and the whole "cleaning up a world" bit that becomes pretty useless once you've made all your towns and all the residents are happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game was like a hot cup of tea on a cold winters night. It was the perfect combo of cozy, adventure, puzzle and town building without the stress. The art style is adorable and all the little creatures are just too cute. I had a lot of fun creating world seeds and seeing how it would turn out. Also ended up being one of very few games I actually completed 100% and my first perfect game on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't get into this. Seemed disorganized. Not a lot of joy in running around to water and sing to plants that are spread far and wide around the map from one another. Why can't I have everything in one location or exactly how I want it? I didn't bother seeing if this changes over time. Wasn't able to determine if I was playing a farming game or some kid-like questing game, with fishing, and petting farm animals with seemingly no real benefit other than being a pointless filler to tack on some playtime. The only thing I liked about this game is that I was able to name my mount after my BF, and use the game as a LARPing outlet for riding him around... with extreme limitation. You can not control your mount.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I usually play Farm Sim games and while this one isn't farming, it is kinda God game plus city building game. Its very easy and would be suitable for a child. The puzzles are not hard, there is no combat, and the graphics are great. Personally, I love how gender is a non issue here. Girls can have beards, boys can have pigtails and non-binary characters exist in a state of peace with everyone. Its fun, slow, and easy to put down/pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, short-term game and I completed my towns and maxed out my cash within a week. Oddly enough, there is nothing interesting or needed to buy after the 7 towns are completed. The  world building aspect of the tree is unbelievably cool and I wish this part of the game went deeper: it would have given me weeks of experimenting and fun if that part was more developed . I would have loved it if the 24 essences actually had 24 different themes/attributes that I could have played around with, instead of the 6 basic biomes that encompass the 24 in the list. Like, no matter how much "watery" or "sparkly" essence you put into the mix, you only get "frozen" qualities. Add "lively" or "dreamy" essence and you get silly princess shoes or neon pinwheels in an otherwise beautiful world. Those world seeds were my favorite part of the game.This game was great for a week but it could have been excellent for many, many weeks if it has some long-term things to do.Update: I am now making the worlds out of each biome family and that is interesting. I've made 3 biomes ( 12 worlds) so far, so that has given me another week of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is visually quite lovely. The storyline is simple, but I really think it works well. There isn't anything overly demanding and nothing is timed. You truly can take things at your own pace without worrying about maximizing efficiency.  As a bonus, you can easily allow children access to this game without fear. I would say 7/8 and up is likely alright as long as they can read well. My children saw me playing and they created their own files.  So it is definitely an appealing game for kids.There is very little challenge wise. A few exceptionally basic puzzles but the game makes it fairly clear how to solve them. Like I said, more relaxing than anything else.There seem to be a couple minor bugs. Tailor shop accessories do not function at this time during customization, but that is a tiny issue. If you want a game where you feel like interacting with npcs is rewarding, I don't think this game offers that. Even though there are a few interactions with required npcs, I personally felt my children may enjoy the interactions but I felt they were very...zelda-esque and not necessarily in a good way. I did enjoy managing my towns and tending to them, but animal crossing interactions this is not. Honestly, this is relaxing, beautiful and requires very little brain power. I was listening to documentaries and tending my world seeds at the same time. Worked very well.For the record, the music in the game is quite lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: TLRD; Animal Crossing for very young kids, but too frustrating to be appealing. Quit in time for refund.I waited until this game was on a big sale to try it and ended up refunding it anyway. I so badly wanted to like it going in because it's a cute idea and the artstyle was neat, but it's legit Animal Crossing for absolute babies. I know it probably wasn't made for someone as old as I am, but I enjoy easy, pretty games sometimes; I have hundreds of hours in New Horizons. The character creation menu is limited and options on sliders aren't labeled in any way and your two options for voice in a game about songs and singing are high pitched or low- points for a 'they' option for gender though. The dialogue can be genuinely funny, but that's undermined when they discourage you from exploring or figuring out anything for yourself because they remind you in a large text window what your objective is every couple of minutes. The areas are huge and that's good, but they're also easy to get lost in which is bad because there's no map of any kind. I can't find a way to access a current quest menu to ask the game where my quests are after not pinning them because I was busy catching bugs and ignoring quest npcs since they gave me a bug net and fishing rod miles before I met the people who teach you how to use them. The button that pings your areas of work needing to be done only seems to work on the little gardening islands, so that didn't help either. It let me plant something in a 'nature preserve' for most of my money and then didn't tell me that removing the plant wouldn't refund the money, which I needed to do a main quest. I only put a little over 100 minutes in before I had too many little things that made me not want to keep playing; set a timer if you want to try it out yourself because you'll know if you can tolerate the issues the game has.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the incarnation of lucky 3. Whatever it is you will be faced by doing it at least 3 times. You want to tame a critter?Pet it 3 Times for 3 days.You want to grow your world?Tend to it 3 times for each of the 3 areas.You want to clear a shrine?Clear 3 parts with similiar objectives.You want to fell a tree or destroy a tree?Hit it in most cases 3 times with your tool.Honestly the start felt kinda frustrating due to this constant repetition, especially as I always had to repeat everything 3 times, I would have appreaciated if it weren't that biased to the number 3.However the game is very simple, straightforward and definetely amateur friendly. At some point you will also have the chance to change your daily cylce a little which will decrease the constant repetitiveness, but in the end you won't get around the grind. I honestly started the game due to the music from one of the trailers and I'm a little dissappointed that I heard that specific soundtrack relatively seldom, but the music was still decent overall. This helped in just laying back to relax while playing the game.In the case that you just want to lay back a little and enjoy a grind with some simple village building then this game may be something for you.And for all the achievement hunters, all the achievements are really simple and can easily be finished by just finishing the story line. It took me 20 hours to finish the game and I could have probably finished a few hours earlier by just sleeping faster as I usually used the whole day and night to grind and farm everything I may need and it also took me a while to efficiently increase the happiness in my districts.
