_childDocuments_.review: Negatives- Boring plot, found myself skipping cutscenes whenever I could- VERY bland and repetitive character design - Most characters look the same with very little variation. Not helped by few (and unflattering) clothing choices. Large selection of hats though.- Awkward/unfinished character animations -E.g. when the character lands from a jump or when they are floating with their umbrella.- No option to sell your items in spite of building loads of stores.- Repetitive gameplay.- Too easy.- The vaults you have to find to get your world seeds are not challenging or engaging in any way, they just drag the game out.- You can (achievement wise) 100% the game without completing the story.- The game overall seems unfinished, which is very sad because there is definitely something interesting here that just needed a bit longer in the oven.Positives+ Non-violent (for the very most part) gameplay. There is no combat in this game, the closest you get to violence is when you have to smash the corruption in your land with your hammer. I thought this was a good choice for this kind of game.+ Very visually interesting worlds you can build with your seeds. You can tell the developers had fun with this.Overall thoughts. I did by no means hate this game. It just needed more polish and a bit more consideration for other mechanics in the game apart from the city building and seed maintenance aspects. It was clear they wanted to include a few more things. Romance (It unfortunately just felt very awkward) and I assume breeding your flying mount ? I also kept waiting for something to happen for me to actually start farming anything there are crop plots right outside your house or even get the option to sell any of my items to get more Myora.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew within seconds it was by the fabulous people who created Yonder. The style is unmistakable, as is the lovely music and atmosphere. Very easy to just have the time go past as you play. Pluses:  First and foremost, this is the first game where I've been given the option of the player character being female, male or non-binary. Brilliant.  Hair, glasses and facial hair seem a bit uninteresting, but you get the option of a hairdresser and tailor in the town, plus you find fresh looks in the wild. It leans heavy on exploration and wonder. There's a lot to encourage a player to actually use the camera feature.  There's fishing and bug hunting, but it's very forgiving to clumsy players. So far, with only one world completed,  the puzzles are a mild challenge, but finding some of the hidden locations requires some creative thinking. Creatures are adorable. Trees and rocks look like Dr Seuss plushies. Even the bugs look cuddly.Minuses- (Setting aside the bugs that are being hotfixed)  I wish there was a way to mute the constant cooing/grunting from the Book and Coppertop. You deal with the characters all the time, and I end up hitting mute when they're tutorial/info dumping. Ugh. A few elements like the alchemy and town people could be better explained at the start. The Land of the Everkin is strangely washed out, and finding where you are can be tricky. First game in a while where I wish there was a minimap. Lastly, minor quibble, I wish there were more skin tone options in character build. Been a bit glitchy the past few days, not sure why, but CTD is a pain. At least you don't have to go to extremes to save.Overall: Very well worth it. Prideful Sloth do lovely work.

_childDocuments_.review: A strange game. It feels like it's made for small children, but it has a huge amount of items and aspects that would be beyond the very young children it seems to be targeted toward. The dialogue is downright boring for anyone above the age of 7, though the idea behind the story is very compelling. It's attractive in a cartoon-y kind of way, but the character models are lumpy and move strangely. The management of town districts is simultaneously too easy and annoyingly micromanager-y. It lacks quality-of-life when it comes to inventory management or accessing information, but the game is so casual I guess it doesn't matter?I LOVE the concept. The idea of creating and growing these little seed worlds (that you create) which give you the supplies to build up and revitalize an abandoned city is a fantastic and sensational concept...but none of it seems to...matter. The massive amount of "items" are essentially randomized and not particularly distinct from each other. The seed worlds start to blend together. Rinse and repeat.The game left me cold and yet also left me inspired and wanting to do so much MORE, which was ultimately even more disappointing.I wish I could give it a neutral review. I'll definitely keep an eye on the developers future projects and I hope this game "grows" this particular combination of gaming concepts in the industry.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say. This is the one of the most beautiful, outstanding, heartfelt, visually stunning, fun, and pleasurable games I have ever played. I play a lot of games, a lot of mainstream games at that, and while yes, some are great (No Man's Sky for example) - it's just that this one in particular wraps up so many positive aspects into one emotionally beautiful journey that it's hard to not see it as top notch. I feel like I stole this game @ 22 dollars. You can tell the work on this was from the heart and meant to be meaningful to all who play it. I'm a 49 year old mom and I bought it for me and my 16 year old daughter; we have so much fun and we play it side by side. It has so many lessons in it that are interwoven into a game format, I mean even the opening song (look it up on youtube) speaks volumes to the integrity and meaning put into this game. I do not ordinarily play this type of game, but I'm so glad I got this and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is the pleasant, beautiful fix that I needed after Stardew Valley and animal crossing. with elements of Dark Cloud's premise of rebuilding the world- you enjoy the gentle day to day the way you would with any cathartic casual game. Grow actually surprised me a couple hours in when I found out you can design your own worlds. the level of exploration and identifying of wild life become infinite with that premise, and the more unusual the world you create, the more different of creatures and flora you see. You create and decorate your own towns, choose who to add to them, and enjoy the pleasant beauty of the world as you unlock new areas, work through not-too-frustrating puzzles, and learn more about Evertree and its history.ConsIt doesn't have the detailed NPC's that Stardew has, although there is a friendship and relationship plot in the game. to be honest, I stumbled through it as it seemed underwhelmingly simple. The game has monotony in it. you create a schedule each day of pulling weeds, planting seeds, and aiding townspeople. the con to this as anyone who would play this game would be looking for that pleasant cathartic repetition is that unlike star dew and animal crossing, you don't get to pick what or where you grow, which is unfortunate given the title. There is no challenge to this game. although not technically a con, given the casual genre, I can comfortably say a toddler can play this with joy and no threat of loss of any kind. this may even be a pro to some.

_childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary game, maybe the best of its kind I ever played. Which bears the question, what exactly is its kind? Strictly speaking, it's not a farm game, because the 5000th carrot gets you nowhere. Strictly speaking, it's not an adventure game, because the scripted contents only highlights key moments. Strictly speaking, it's not a manager, unless you have ever played a manager, in which you don't hunt for resources, but for base products, which may or may not yield the resourcces you need. And I haven't even started to talk about what you need the resources for, which is a basic city builder. Well, village builder. Important is this. Starting with this vague description means doing the potential buyer a favor, because while playing the game, one has to decide for oneself, which aspect to like best in this farming-adventure-manager-village-builder. Only one thing is for certain. If you hate games without killing and instead puttering around so relaxed that even the cat on your keyboard cannot phase you, then this game will not be your cup of tea.Which also means, that likening the game to My Time At Portia is silly. After two or three tasks in what feels like the tutorial stage, I never ran into time pressure again (though I'm far from being done yet).On the other hand, just not having pressure doesn't mean, that you don't have plenty to do. Very early in the game, that may not be obvious.So, what can you expect? The basic game play loop is, you plant a "world seed", which gives you a parcel of land. That land is tainted and has to be cleansed and filled with flora and fauna again. In the process, you snatch up samples, for instance a type of fruit. This fruit in its current specific form is worthless. Instead, your alchemical equipment distills it into one so-called essence out of a break-down list procedurally generated for this one specific fruit. With the help of the essences, you can build a village in several steps called districts. And while you are working on that, you can invite dwellers, which need basic accommodations with upgrades, a job, the occasional little quest, and other dwellers, they like to live with. At the same time, the very same essences allow creating new world seeds.And I guess this is, where it gets a little complicated. I have read some negative reviews, and it is pretty obvious that people miss the point of a new seed. Since you will find that some essences are currently plentiful and some are rare or non-existant, the natural thing to do is to pick a sum of  fifty necessary for the seed from those essences, you have lots of. Don't do that. Ever. A seed creates a "world" (as a matter of fact a tiered patch) which in turn yields two outputs. Lots of what you invested in it, plus a list of (random?) five "rares", which you can see when pausing the game while on the patch. What that means is, if you make the mistake and get your seed essences from the big stacks, all you guarantee is bigger stacks (which are in and of themselves useless), actually only profiting from random chance. This means, try insteadf to come up with ones you desperately need (supposedly in batches of ten or fifteen). That may be complicated, because trade is relatively difficult. Worse, you may need to hold back on some new building type, because only the seed will give you, what actually keeps you trucking. Choosing the optimal essence combination, which is right for your current point of your individual playthrough, is a major fun factor. As it is a guaranteed letdown, if you blindly choose your combination from some knucklehead's list-of-the-bestest-seeds on the net.Now that we have the basic game loop, two urgent warnings. Don't rush recruting and figure out, what is replenishable and what is not.Don't rush recruiting means that good skills alone don't make a valuable dweller. Try to make up your mind what you want to build. Then find dwellers, that bring the right skills. Ideally, they may think of what you need as their "dream job". Remember, there is no rush whatsoever. (On a side note, supposedly there is a way to boost a dweller's skills with upgrades, but I haven't found that yet.)Replenishable finds in the seed worlds dictate, how you guarantee that you get more back of what essences you invested in. Remember, a find's essence break-down list is what counts, not the find itself. (On another sidenote, it is hinted at, that one can ruin a world by overfarming non-replenishables. I won't risk that, because it's thoroughly unnecessary.)Of course, this is a review, not a guide. Then again, I thought that giving you a basic concept of the game keeps you from having false hopes or falling into one of those demoralizing beginner mistakes. This being said, Grow is a delight to play. In a way, it is a successor to Yonder in spirit, except that in Grow everything is better. If anything, Grow is Yonder on serious steroids.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is about the life-giving tree, which for a long time brought harmony to the inhabitants at its roots through a "song". One day the song "fell apart" and people didn't hear it anymore. Soon the tree was taken over by a wilting tree, and they all fled, except for one young alchemist, who now sets out to restore Evertree to its former glory.Grow: Song of the Evertree is a multi-faceted game. To spoil it there is gardening, city building and exploration. You plant seeds to build the worlds you cultivate, and that provides you with resources. You then use these resources to build city regions and attract residents. To make progress, you must then find a piece of the song, return it to Evertree's heart chamber, and then, if your citizens are happy enough, you can fend off the wilting and expand your city.If that sounds repetitive, that's because it is. It compensates for the fact that there is so much to be done. You often wander off to your worlds in the branches and watch the same ad absurdum planting / watering / hammering animation, but nothing compels you to do it every day. You don't need to work out a routine, you can go out and mess around with every little project you have.It's a fact that there are so many interactions when it comes to progression that it takes a long time to get old. Maybe you want to spend the day maximizing the city's potential. Perhaps you prefer to complete tasks to keep your inhabitants happy. There are even goals you can complete to earn different rewards. Much of the game is so rewarding, and Grow: Song of the Evertree is oddly well-balanced for a game with so many individual mechanics.City building, for example, is highly customizable. Not only do you have a lot of control over its layout, almost everything can be decorated with a variety of paints and signs. You can even put a mustache on all your inhabitants, I'm not going to stop you, and neither is Grow: Song of the Evertree.The gardens you build on Evertree's branches are also something special. You create seeds by mixing different alchemical elements, and the world is created from this combination. At first I only got plain but colorful woods but then I started getting weird stuff like a world where eyeballs were moving everywhere. The number of possible combinations is insane, and I wonder what's inside this algorithm.The search is also not hunchbacked. Each area of the city you explore contains a short dungeon that is perhaps less ambitious than a typical Breath of the Wild dungeon, but is at least comparable. They each have their own puzzles and themes, and while the design can be confusing at times, it blends well with the rest of the game.All of this is done in a sunny aesthetic. There is a lot of work to do. You can adopt creatures from your worlds, and earning their trust is accomplished by rubbing your belly and scratching your chin. You can also take selfies with pets, which doesn't give you much other than the warmth inside.If you want to get technical skills, a bit of a fight awaits you. There are things that go around sometimes that you have to hit with a hammer. However, they don't attack you, and hitting them causes them to dissolve and release an insect caught in their goo.Grow: Song of the Evertree certainly hits beyond its weight class. There is a lot of content, and while most of it is extremely solid, there are some sharp edges, but they don't detract significantly from the overall feel.However, you will definitely see them. While the game's graphic style stands out with its vivid colors, the animation is a bit rough. There is a lot of clipping and a lot of awkward moments. If you jump from a high place, your character will open the umbrella to protect yourself from getting hurt. However, if they do so while carrying the item, the umbrella will simply pop out of their hand, hanging in front of them in a way that would be completely useless.There's this romance mechanic in the game, but I don't know why. Technically speaking, you can build relationships with any characters, but there were a few that popped up as frequent quests until they admitted I was attracted to my fabulous self. It may be sweet, but a little undercooked. It just happens out of your control, and doesn't really lead much beyond a rather mundane storyline.For that matter, the only characters with any real depth are Copperpot and Book, your two alchemical companions and tools. The dialogue is often quite pleasant, even with random villagers, but I never felt like getting to know any of them. Maybe that is beyond the scope and the whole storyline is an optimistic environmental message, but I think I would feel more drawn into the world if there were people living in it to connect with.Grow: Song of the Evertree to my own surprise, is a game that luring me with relax and freedom, constricted only by day/night in game cycle. Amazing Game!

_childDocuments_.review: Grow: Song of the Evertree - it's a pretty unique farming/town building sim/sandbox/open world hybrid.== Pros ==*Graphics are well-done and the visual style is nice.*Gifting items (including hairstyles, contacts, and face paint) to your townspeople have them actually change into what you gave them which is pretty unique.*Tons of essences and items to discover.*Many quests to complete.*Town building is reminiscent of Dark Cloud (townsfolk have specific requirements).*Fast travel to move around quicker.*Worlds you finished can be returned to the earth, allowing you unlimited worlds you can build.*Interact with animals and set up various things in Nature Reserves.*Photo and selfie modes to take screenshots.== Cons ==*No minimap, or stationary map. You have to always call on your flying pet to see where you are in the world, and even then it doesn't help because it's so small.*You're forced to sleep once it hits night.*If your character falls in deep water and you don't jump right away, you'll be forced back on land in what appears to be a random spot when you're in the overworld. When in a cave or other instanced area, it resets you to the very beginning or end (if you completed it).*Can't customize the main Alchemy building or surrounding area (or at least, I haven't unlocked it yet).*Limited buildings and decorations you can place in a section.*Gameplay can get repetitive, especially when you have to clean up the worlds every single freaking day.*There's a lot to do, and some things can get pretty confusing or be difficult to complete at times.*This is a personal con for me, but I can't stand the "cutesy" eyes the main character has or the "frolicking".*No fast fall - falling from a long height forces you to parasol all the way down, which can take a long ass time.*Even if you own a decoration, you still have to a pay the main currency to place it in the world, which seems pretty stupid.All in all, check out Grow: Song of the Evertree - it's pretty chill!

_childDocuments_.review: It's good for casual play also child-friendly. A wholesome game without combat if you had  a bad day with work or pandemic lock-down.So I didn't like Yonder much but this game is really good. Everything's improved in value.There's some motivation, a creative world with lore. I love the regrowing aspect of the game and making the area green bit by bit. (like in Regrowth mod for Minecraft)Sure there's grind but that's just the genre. You have your routine and then there's exploration.You pull weeds, you water plants, you sing to trees.You collect and serch for materials, you hunt treasure chests. You get a bazillion of items.You commision buildings and switch the townfolks around.Graphics are nice and candy-colored, game crashes on highest setting though.Music is good with some vocals too, sfx took some hints from Breath of the Wild.Nominated for "SIT BACK AND RELAX AWARD"While the day is timed, nothing bad really happens if you take more days apparently so you can just play at your own pace. _childDocuments_.review: A little rough around the edges but charming and chill management game with lots of exploration and some platforming puzzles thrown in for variation. Lovely, colorful and comedic, with a hopeful environmental story. Creating and tending to you own worlds is fun and rewarding. New mechanics are introduced every now and then quite far into the games play time.I have 3 complaints:1) When you, say, wanna pick nuts from a bush situated close to a tree, you will often auto connect to the tree to shake it, due to the hit boxes overlapping (or so I assume), and the bigger hit box for the tree reaches farther. It can be a bit frustrating. Same with talking to characters standing next to something you wanna interact with. You'll end up starting conversations when you wanna open a chest for instance.2) Sometimes the dialogue boxes cover characters faces, but it's not a huge issue and only effects immersion.And the biggest issue, 3) is that it's rather easy to get stuck in scenery and behind map sections when exploring nooks and crannies, something which is encouraged during game play, so save often and EVERYTIME before going to explore more thoroughly. The game will otherwise likely auto save you in a compromised position, and you'll have to load the most recent manual save you've done.Overall feelgood!

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't your typical farming sim. You play as an apprentice alchemist, who is trying to stop their world from becoming overtaken by the wither. To stop it, you craft world seeds out of essences to grow new worlds on the branches of a giant tree. You tend to these worlds by cleaning up and restoring nature and planting plants. Its kind of cool, because the seeds you plant are infinite, and you don't choose what to plant. the types of plants that grow depend solely on the type of world seed you plant, and its interesting watching each world change from a barren wasteland into all sorts of crazy biomes through your efforts. Thats only one part of the game however. The other big part of it is town building, and you can use the resources from the worlds you cultivate to help in that endeavor, and help keep the people living there happy. Never have I played such a satisfying and relaxing game before. Like others have said it can be repetitive, but so can a lot other farming/life sims. The fun of this game for me, is seeing what crazy world seeds I can brew up, and getting to know the townspeople that move in to my town. The devs have also managed to make the "busy work" in the game extremely satisfying, and I think a big part of that is the brilliant sound design. The music is also S tier. this is well worth the 25 dollars it costs.

Build houses and buildings like a tailor shop where you buy new clothes, a bakery, a flower shop, library, and MORE! You can customize everything! The walls, the roof color, the outside of the buildings, the town itself. It's so amazing, you can meet new villagers that wanna move in from humans to alien looking villagers! The diversity is amazing. Did I mention you can have a 3rd gender option !?!? Customize your character into the perfect body shape, no longer just skinny, chubby, or in between. Now there's about 9 body types to choose from! Choose your pronouns too! There are many they/thems in the game as well! My favorite villager perfers they/them pronouns. This game is just wonderful and I will always hold it dear in my heart. Zeeka!

_childDocuments_.review: My 4 year old daughter's favorite game. With very little help she was able to finish it. She doesn't speak or read English and this game required very little of either to enjoy at least with a little bit of support. Finding a suitable game for her was very difficult. Almost zero violence and no consequences for failure. Possible to play in short sessions. Good controller support. Plenty of exploring, solving simple mysteries and puzzles, building, decorating, garden work, teaches a little bit of discipline. Cute theme and characters. Requires doing some boring work so that she could collect items for the more interesting activities. A perfect fit for her. She thoroughly enjoyed it and with a tear in her eye said she'll miss it when I explained to her that the game is probably ending soon once she was unlocking the last 2 villages. I think she felt something akin to the feeling of finishing a good book so when it ended and the game allowed her to continue she was able to put it down feeling sad but satisfied. Not a flawless game but highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I was recommended this because it has town building mechanics similar to the Dark Cloud games, and I enjoyed the developer's first game, Yonder, even though it was pretty unfinished. I assumed this would be better, more fleshed out. I was wrong.The best part of the game is the world creation. The environments are beautiful, tending to them is very meditative. The story is cute, your tutorial NPCs are charming mentor figures. But once you complete the first seed, progressing the story is relegated to extremely tedious "dungeons" that will see you traipsing through dozens of identical corridors hoping to find one of three puzzles, and the only purpose the world seeds have left is generating resources for town building.Except... most of the town building does nothing. Aside from a handful of story characters, who have very little dialogue, most of your townspeople are randomly generated, and repeat the same few lines over and over again. They have stats that suggest they're better at working at certain types of buildings than others... but most of the buildings don't do anything, so juggling which villagers are assigned to what is literally pointless.The gardens don't produce resources. The bakeries don't sell anything. The flower shop sells keys, for some reason. You're grinding away at your seed worlds to produce resources to build buildings that don't do anything for villagers you don't care about. It's depressing. It's a checklist. I'd actually rather be at my day job.I'd accept this as "charmingly over-ambitous" from a first-time team, but... this isn't their first time. This has more of the same problems Yonder had, and from a studio that bills itself as "micro-AAA", it just isn't charming anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unfortunately disappointing as a whole.I went in expecting to be able to do a lot of customizing for my town, create fun worlds with different things to do in each of them and have meaningful interactions with my villagers. This was anything but that.This is going to be a bit long as I've completed the game now and gotten all achievements, but I think this should give you a very good idea of what to expect from the game. Maybe this'll be your cup of tea, but it definitely wasn't mine in the end. I did enjoy the first 10 hours or so, but after that the game becomes a chore of doing the same thing over and over, until you get to see the end of the story and get all of the town unlocked. Here's a couple things I had issues with: I'm not sure if this one was a time constraint, budget or out of pure laziness, but unlocking a new district shows you the same cutscene every time. Progressing the story shows you a nice little cutscenes with some of the story, and then you get the same short cutscene of the tree every time. It would've been nice if the town area cutscenes represented the are you unlocked, and to actually see the tree growing bigger and taller after every step of the story, rather than just getting the same visuals every time.  You are limited to 20 buildings, 20 decorations and 500 miscellaneous (paths and walls for the most part). Things like trees, a flower or a bush (yes, one single flower or bush counts as one of your 20 decorations), lamp posts, etc. - I would've expected to be able to place many, many more objects down to make the area beautiful and to my liking. This isn't to say that the towns aren't pretty - The game does a great job of making everything look very nice and peaceful. However, given the amount of decorations the game throws at you, 20 is not nearly enough to make a themed area or to fill in all empty spaces.There is also the issue of all buildings and decorations having a square hitbox around them - This means you can't put flowers or bushes right next to a house, for example. You'll always have some kind of gap and it just doesn't look great. I can understand having the hitbox for the building itself, but leaving the gap around it seems like an odd decision. Customizing your town areas and spending time decorating clearly was not an intended focus of this game. There are a total of  seeds in the game, other than the one you begin with. You can also make strange seeds with essence combinations that don't go together, but from what I saw in my play through they just generate a mostly empty world that has nothing to do in it.Perfect seeds don't seem very different from a seed of the same world type that isn't perfect - I tried a specific biome without making it perfect and it's pretty much the same, minus one building that spawned only on the perfect one. The majority of the time you'll spend in this game will be on worlds you grow from those seeds - You pluck weeds, grow plants, break stacks of bricks (that somehow keep coming back every day?) and.. that's about it? You keep doing it until the game says your world is ready to finish growing, go complete it and then you can just completely ignore it if you want to. You can get some of its resources passively but they don't have much use. I also encountered issues where completing certain activities on those worlds just didn't register on the checklist of things to do, which made it impossible to complete the list of tasks. I also fully completed it on two worlds and either it didn't register for Book's achievement, or I'm misunderstanding what it means by "Complete all discoveries in an area". There isn't really any meaningful dialog for any of them. You'll get requests from them for items, find something they've lost or customize their house, but that's about all there is to them. Some you can have a "relationship" with, but it doesn't go much further than having a very short event with them, hearts floating above their head and then it's never mentioned again for the rest of your play through.: There isn't much to explore in this game - The town area has a couple side-areas like caves and story "dungeons", (for lack of a better word) containing puzzles, but don't expect much more than that. My initial impression was that exploring was rewarded with chests containing items, however even toward the end of the game you just keep getting the same kind of stuff out of them, even the highest tier of chests. I never felt like it had been worth my time to do the puzzles.During the story "dungeons", you will be constantly shown nearly, if not the entirety of the area with cutscenes. You don't get to explore and figure out the puzzles yourself - Everything is shown through cutscenes, so you end up knowing exactly where you need to go and what you need to do. I'm not sure if the target audience for this game is young kids, but this took away a lot of the fun for me. Not that these are particularly difficult to begin with, so I can't see a kid struggling with them either anyway. You also can't skip them as far as I know, so you have to just sit there and wait until it's over. Looking back now I suppose I could've just not looked at my screen, or gotten up and came back after a minute but I really don't think this was designed well.There's also a weird design choice when it comes to jumping - Sometimes your character will stagger/stay in place for half a second when they land from a jump, which can be really annoying in the few jumping puzzles if you're expecting to jump right as you land. For me it was jarring and not a particularly enjoyable experience.: This just recently released and the developers have already released a hot fix patch, so I'm sure they will be fixed given enough time, but there are quite a few bugs at the moment, some that can even lock you from progressing your save.At the end of the day this isn't a bad game, but there isn't much to do. Maybe my expectations were too high, but overall this was a rather disappointing experience past the 10 hour mark. If the things I've listed aren't a concern to you, by all means buy the game! You're likely to have a great experience if you can look past those. For me they were little things that built up over the play through and ended up being annoying as I repeated the same actions day after day.

This is more like a coloring game where you are presented with a picture to fill in, and the process of doing so is exceptionally grind-y busywork.The town design aspect of the game is better in that you can choose where to place the buildings, but the map is designed in such a way that it pretty much predetermines where most players are going to rationally place each structure. Bakeries, inns and other commercial establishments will naturally be placed around the predetermined town squares which can't be edited, while houses will be placed further away. _childDocuments_.review: *EDIT* COMPLETED GAME  *EDIT*Let me preface by saying that I love this game, but I don't recommend it for most people.  The magic the trailers delivered, the game failed to follow up on.  That is my biggest regret.  This is not My Time at Portia, or Stardew Valley.  Get that out of your head right now.  This is Powerwash simulator ecosystem edition.It is tedious.  70% of the game is tending to world seeds, which amounts to plucking plants, cleaning animals, breaking rocks, planting seeds, watering them, and singing to them.  Essentially button mashing that can be mindlessly done.  The remaining 30% is a bit of exploration and mostly city management.  Game loop is the same throughout.  Get city to 100% happiness, unlock new area, get new song fragment, unlock more world seed planters.  Rinse repeat ad nauseam.  There is no replaybility here as the game is virtually on rails, while attempting to deceive you into believing it is not.  There is little in the way of 'progress', as in don't expect a tool evolution or to get 'better' at anything.  There are certain perks that unlock that speed up a couple of activities such as watering.  Definitely useful but the achievement isn't marked as increasing watering speed, so its more of an unexpected bonus than something you actually strive for.  Unlike say SDV where you can grind for better tools.  You are actively pursuing something and it feels good to achieve it. That being said, this game is magical and soothing.  The closest parallel I can draw is powerwash simulator strangely enough.  This game is almost like a form of therapy.  While I love it, this game disappointed me.  It is not what I expected.  This might be my fault as the trailers and gameplay truly looked magical and I got my hopes up.Edit: Easily 13 hours of my playtime is pulling weeds.  I'm beginning to lose my sanity.   I might not be able to stomach finishing this. I finally started unlocking some of the 'end game building enhancements' and guess what all they give you is 'additional myora' which I've had an abundance of since District 3.  This has been a huge goal that I've been striving for throughout my entire gameplay and its more of a useless resource?  This whole game is hollow.Every district is the same. Nothing changes in the city development. Nothing changes in the seed world management.  It's literally like they designed the game, realized there was not enough content and just copypasta'd it 7 times.  My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined.Final Edit: Finally completed the game.  Play time at completion 21 hours 15 minutes.  Absolutely nothing changed through the end.  :'(

_childDocuments_.review: The once beautiful and bountiful land of Alaria has been laid to ruins, the previous residents having ignored The Evertree’s - the guardian tree of this land - warnings of overusing The Song and draining the land of Myora; and so The Withering grew with a vengeance. Huge, destructive, and thorny vines constantly pulsating, growing, and bringing with it, a purple fiery wind that has forced every living thing to run for their lives and abandon this land… except for you; the last Everheart Alchemist. Take on the task of becoming the Evertree’s caretaker, growing seeds on its branches to push back The Withering; retake lost districts and rebuild the towns, and find the Song Fragments that were either stolen or lost to restore what never should have been broken.I liked playing Grow: Song of the Evertree, but I absolutely refuse to give it a positive review. First of all, this game is abandoned, second, it has so many bugs it should still be in Early Access; and third, it’s unfinished. I went through so much trouble just trying to play the game I purchased I cannot in good conscious let you go without at least a warning; this game was literally unplayable for me. 4-ish hours in I ran into a bug, which I assume was cause by a duplicating dialogue box right before the issue, in which I would start the next day completely unable to move my character. I did everything, uninstalling, reinstalling, verifying my files, updating my drivers, bug reporting, emailing the publishers (who were EXTREMELY UNHELPFUL and basically told me since it was abandoned I was SOL), and even making an entirely new game to no avail.  THAT IS NOT OK. Also, growing worlds and caring for them is one of the big draws about buying this game, you can craft as many as you like and they are all different.. except they aren’t? All worlds with a similar type look the same with a different generated name and similar generated animals, such as Icy worlds all have the same trees and bushes; and every world, regardless of type, has the exact same fruits and rocks available, except they are recolored and have a new name. All the animals are similar, either medium dog shaped or large mammoth, and they only variety they have is what color they are; and it gets old fast! By the fourth world I no longer had any interest in doing anything, because I’ve seen it all before! Even bugs and fish are not an exception.You cannot adopt anything in game without it crashing! You can’t even accept any rewards related to adopting without the game absolutely freaking out; the critter center is broken. There are also other specific rewards that cause your game to fail, I found it’s better to ignore any completion reward entirely, or save your game before you accept any. There are invisible chests, missing items and functions, and even an entire storefront. The Community Gardens, which I suspect is where you were supposed to be able to purchase housing decorations like flower boxes and mailboxes for your community, is inaccessible. There are things that look like they should function, like the Juke Box in the diner, that don’t, and there are missing items or unfinished idle animations. NPC’s use invisible items, eat invisible food, and some dialogue boxes, don’t have any dialogue? It’s genuinely a mess. Also a small gripe, inventory management, please? Rocks, fish, wood, bugs, and plants all go in the same inventory and they are not organized by type, rarity, nor is it possible to fix it yourself. What determines their place is what you obtained first, so it’s just, a huge mess! And what, you can buy things for Myora but you can’t sell anything?? I thought Myora was the currency but according to the wiki, “It’s the source of all life” so how am I even using this to buy anything…

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, first of all, I like this game. It's cute and clearly has a lot of love put into it, but personally, I wouldn't recommend it.The positives are outlined well by the other reviews so I'm gonna skip over that and just get straight to the point; this game is boring. It doesn't start as boring, but the more you play the more mundane and stale it gets. At the beginning you get more quests, the subplot with your childhood friends plays out, it's interesting and fun. But as soon as you get to the plains things just... stop. The only quests you get are "ask Builderkin to repair the docks", "look for the song fragment" and "restore the harmony to the region", rinse and repeat. Yeah sure, you can also do sidequests for your villagers, but they're just boring fetch quests that don't help it at all. Special encounters however are fun and interesting, but they hardly ever occur, which is so unfortunate since I really like some of the characters. The story is interesting and not bad at all, yet the sluggish gameplay kinda ruins the flow of it. Speaking of gameplay, that one is probably my biggest issue with the game; the core gameplay (creating seeds, growing worlds, take care of your town) is INSANELY unrewarding. You get nothing from completing a world and releasing it. You get nothing from catching bugs and fishing. You get nothing from exploring caves. A few materials and a crumb of Myora maybe, but is that really a reward? Especially once you reach the forest it's practically worthless to even go exploring since you get all the Myora passively from your town overnight. And that's the glaring issue I see in this game, and the sole reason why I would not recommend it. Sure the game is very well made and packed with love and care (and a few hilarious glitches, but that's not a big issue to me) but there is... no content. After ~24 hours of playtime I feel like I haven't progressed at all, even after unlocking the zones and creating a bunch of world seeds, there is no feeling of accomplishment or anything for that matter. After getting a zone to 100% all I think is "meh finally" and move onto the next one, which is such a massive pity for a lovely game like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. This is exactly the kind of game I've been waiting for since I beat My Time At Portia and have been desperately searching for other games in the genre. -The aesthetic in this game is incomparable. The artistic direction is unique, fantastical, nice to look at, and charming. I love the biomes (They're all unique and stunning to look at) + I love the clothing (only complaint would be I wish there were more shirts or maybe a clothing dye system? But I don't care enough when you look at the full product). One design thing I don't really care for are male faces in the game? They all look kinda weird, but thats my personal taste.-The characters are charming and interesting, and I appreciate that there are unique NPCs with dialog and even history with your character. I appreciate that they added the friendship/romance aspect, because that's something i really enjoy in these games even if it's just a little afterthought (which it doesn't feel like in this game. It feels like the characters are actually interesting and compelling.)-There's a LOT to do in this game. I love that you can manage towns, do fetch quests for NPCs, create world seeds, clean up those worlds and watch them come to life, ect. The progression feels really nice, and where it COULD be repetitive and boring, it really doesn't feel like it. I think it's actually more rewarding to see everything come together rather than feeling like a chore simulator. THe dungeon runs are all unique and fun (my only complaint here would be that it's all a bit handhold-y and I don't appreciate that but I can understand its importance for its target audience so whatever.)-The progression in this game is expertly done in my opinion. There's always something to do, there's always an interesting story beat looming around the edge, and it feels genuinely satisfying to get things done. They tap into that goblin completionist part of my brain really well between the sky islands, the towns, and the book of achievements.-There is endless customization in every aspect. It might seem overwhelming to some? Maybe? But I really liked it. This game has a nasty habit of getting me glued to it for hours micromanaging every detail of my town to make it pretty or have the perfect animals in my nature reserves. One thing I wish that was tweaked here is that I wish that houses and job sites were separated for easier management, but like with most of my complaints with this game it's a minor aspect and I don't really care that much. Overall, I am really pleased with this game. It's definitely a gem; a breath of fresh air and addiction for me that I haven't had in a new release in a year or so. I would highly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of the genre in general, and anyone who likes a relaxing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Grow is a combination of gardening/farming sim and townbuilder with exploration and some light puzzles. It is charming, zen, and relaxing. I am in love with this game! I love the alchemy mechanic that lets you create world seeds from various ingredients. You never know exactly what you are going to get each time you mix up a batch of world juice. Granted, you know that you'll get trees, flowers, bushes, some dog-like critters and some cow-like critters but... it's always different enough that I find that I have favorites. For instance, I created a world last night that caught me completely by surprise. The entire world is covered in giant, blinking eyeballs. It's kind of disconcerting... and really, really cool! The gardening/farming side of things can get a little grindy, but it's no more grindy than any other farming sim. You know the drill: pull up weeds, plant seeds, water and wait for everything to grow. But, that's part of what I like about it. I find that whole play cycle of tending to my worlds incredibly soothing. The music is relaxing and I'm just puttering along, making my world pretty. The town building is fun without being stressful. Your buildings are categorized as "food, well-being, production, etc." and every citizen that you attract and house has a numerical score for each category. They also have dream jobs where they would like to work. So, you just match the numbers to the category and try to put people where they want to be. People will also have quests for you, like "bring me a bug from [this world]" or "I could use a new outfit." Stuff like that.Another fun part of the town building is just the decorating part of it. Placing buildings where you like, customizing them, and putting decorations out is oodles of fun. At first, it seems like you don't have a lot of variety of wallpapers and stuff, but that will increase as you get your general store where you can purchase paints/wallpapers and as you complete more and more tasks in Book. (The same thing goes for hairstyles and clothes for your character. Once you build the hairstylist and tailor, you'll get more items to use to dress up.)So far, the puzzles are very light. The ones I have done have been very easy to figure out. Which, again, is fine! I'm playing this game to relax, not to have to particularly challenge my thinking skills. (Though, I will admit that the jumping puzzles gave me problems, but not because they were hard to figure out. I knew what I needed to do. I am just absolute rubbish at jumping.)I'll close out this review by saying that if you loved Yonder, you will love Grow. It's very much in the same vein. Explore, grow your worlds, enjoy your time and just... be.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a lovely game. It's a non-violent experience that has a lot in common with farming games, but it also has some light town management content. It is very task-oriented, so you probably already know if that is the kind of gameplay you enjoy. You can control how grindy it is, to a degree. If you create new seed worlds rapidly, you might find yourself overwhelmed by having to tend to each world. So just take it slow, focus on building your town and discovering new essences, and you'll find Grow to be a relaxing, charming game. The writing is clever and the characters are endearing. There are light puzzles here and there, and the world rewards exploration: there are caves, hidden chests, all sorts of things to find. At just under 14 hours I still have a ways to go. I think the world (the real one) needs more games like Grow: Song of the Evertree.

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but running into annoyances with every single step.- There is no voiced audio, every character just makes a forced noise when their dialogue comes up. The book in your house sounds like you are watching porn with its ooOOhh, AAhhh, aAAhh with every click. It is your main guide so you will be dealing with it a lot. There is no audio option to mute this mess. I'd rather have silence instead.- The controls are designed with controllers in mind. Mouse controls are a mess. Maxed out mouse sensitivity barely makes a difference in camera turning speed. Rotating with a keyboard also feels like trying to gyro around with a joystick.- When you turn while walking/running, the character tilts like you are riding a motorcycle. Hard to believe in this day and age you can butcher a walking animation.- Pulling out weeds is a button mashing system. You need to press E 5x to pull out a single weed. There's a lot of weeds. Holding a key would be nice. A single press even better, not trying to break my keyboard here. Oh and the weeds grew back the next day. Trash building leftovers also re-appeared waiting to be torn down again. The chore continues.- When catching bugs, you can't run and swing your net at the same time. You have to stop, play swinging animation, then run again. Needless to say it is very painful to catch stuff this way as you have to force a bug's collision with something so it stops moving. Forget about catching flying stuff when you can't swing in midair for the same reason.- Trade windows won't show you prices. You have to pick what you want to sell first and the amount of it, exit back to the dialogue and only then will you find out how much the total is worth. Not an easy way to find out how much each unit of each item is worth huh.I've played both Stardew Valley (half the price) and My Time at Portia (fully voiced and more polished). Both of them feel like a better experience both in terms of storytelling as well as gameplay mechanics. So far this game feels like a repetitive chore. Will give it a bit more time, but certainly watching the 2h refund window.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for... forever. I remember seeing it when it was first announced, and getting all excited and shoving that bad boy into my wishlist.When I finally got it, I came in with high hopes, and little to no knowledge about what the game was about, except for the brief description that was provided to me at the store page. I don't even think I really processed much about the art style, life was hectic, and the only thing I knew about this game was that I wanted it. I think I was sick when I first picked this game up, so I was looking for a good distraction in a new comfort game. When I loaded in for the first time, I honestly just sat there and marveled on how beautiful the graphics and animation style was. The music was absolutely perfect and fit just right with the world. It made you believe that you were really trying to help save the Evertree yourself! When I showed my friends the game, one of them described the art style as "something from Wizard101," which was one of my favorite games growing up, so no wonder I gravitated towards Grow: Song of the Evertree! The music is all original (if I remember correctly), the animation style is smooth and charming. This world is whimsical and wonderful and everything I look for in a comfort game.I love the customization style of everything, I love the town building mechanics, and of course, I absolutely adore the Everkin. I always keep an ear out in my town to listen for when they come and go! The puzzles are actually kind of the perfect difficulty for a game like this. They're not too tough, but they're good enough to make you stop and think for a second. It's always a treat to see how my world grows and shapes itself every day.I haven't finished it, and I'm honestly not too sure how close I am to finishing it (I honestly don't want it to end for quite a while), but this is a game I could sit down and just enjoy myself for a few hours at a time. Its cute, creative, and absolutely a wonderful concept and I am so very pleased that the devs blew my expectations out of the water.As for complaints, I honestly have not noticed any quite yet, I don't think I've progressed far enough to where that would be an issue. I'm seeing that some people have had some issues with bugs, but that's about it. The only potential (and I say potential, because it could be a story thing, but I don't know) bug I can even think of would be that the Everkin builder over by the ruins isn't popping up for me, but that's it.I'm greatly enjoying myself with this, and I look forward to seeing what else it offers!

_childDocuments_.review: | Summary |This game is a lot of good clean fun. The visuals are beautiful, the story is entertaining, and the gameplay is relaxing. There's a few bugs during the initial release, but there's an impressive amount of polish to this game.This game was amazing and well worth the money. It took me nearly 60 hours to complete the game, which is a ton of enjoyment. There's some things to do for "end game" but I personally will not do much now that the game is done. There is little replayability for me personally.I very much hope they make a Grow 2 with more features and a bigger end game.| Comparison |I only played Stardew Valley for like 30 minutes before deciding I didn't like it. I love Grow: Song of the Evertree. So they're similar, but liking one does not mean you'll like the other. I believe both have farming, decorating, and social interactions. But the way these happen is very different with Grow being more of a beautiful story. Stories have an ending.This game is like Farmville in that you plant and farm stuff for resources and decorate your town. But that's where it ends, as Grow is more of a linear game with a soft ending. Grow is also way more interactive and beautiful.| Positive |+ The game is beautiful in all areas. The designers were very creative and its impressive how they were able to keep a clear aesthetic that doesn't ever diminish gameplay.+  The UI is clear and easy to use. I was easily able to setup my gamepad (Razer Orbweaver 2) and play fluidly. I believe it would have been the same on the keyboard.+ You are pretty free to do whatever you want without any consequence. You can't die, you can't lose progress, and you can't fail. The only consequence you can experience is a minor loss in efficiency, but even that is mitigated well.+ There's only a bare minimum requirement for each aspect of the game, so if you don't feel like doing one aspect you can spend just a few minutes on it then go do what you want. But...+ If you really like an aspect of the game, you can dive into it further than is required. You are rewarded for doing more without being required to do so.+ The developers are VERY engaged on social media. I interacted directly with some on Discord and saw work arounds within hours and bug fixes within days. The Discord community for this game is pretty great.| Negative |- There were some bugs during the first week of launch that prevented people from progressing the story, lost progress, and crashed the game. These were mostly fixed within the first week.- The first 10 hours or so of gameplay was very smooth and beautiful, but then bugs started popping up in later gameplay indicating that pre-launch QA was above average but focused on early play.- The game objectives get repetitive at the midway point. After the initial tutorial objective, all other objectives are almost exactly the same thing but in new locations. The saving grace is that there is a stacking benefit to finishing each objective.- There's some time gating on objectives (new residents) which feels fine the first few rounds but gets annoying towards the end of the game.- There is no significant end game objectives. That said, you can still mindlessly complete minor objectives which is relaxing and beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem and a massive improvement from the previous game I played from these developers.  well worth the time and money if you enjoy these types of game and although not a difficult game by any means, its charming, relaxing, and rewards you for exploring this gorgeous world and for going outside of the "achievement list".This game is "like" several others in some respects but also different from everything I could relate it  a good way. The game isn't perfect by any means, I found myself wishing for a few things here or there, but honestly was surprised how much I loved this game and how easy it was to go just "one more day".  Kept playing long after I got 100% on the achievement list (roughly 20-25 hours playing casually) and even as I unlocked all the zones and crept up on 30 hours of playtime, I was still surprised to find secrets, hidden bits of story, and things to find in the main world alone. I could easily spend another 10 hours just seeing what kind of world's get generated from the world seeds.Here are a few +/- that I found:If you're still reading - thanks! The only other thing I thought was odd... Not good or bad.. was the types of buildings for each district. Houses and inns were required to attract people to the district, but outside of that, it didn't seem to matter what buildings were in the district. In my first district I built out buildings like a typical city manager, start with food, then production, before switching to services and then finally creativity. I STRUGGLED to get my people lined up with the right job, happy, and the harmony meter filled... My next district i built buildings to suite my residents "dream jobs" but from what I could tell there was no negative impact if there were no food or service buildings in a district. I could have all creative buildings and create just as much happiness. The game isn't exactly clear on what each building brings to the town (other than what they sell to the player). There is a direct correlation to upgrading buildings = more happiness which means more currency produced but it didn't seem to matter what buildings were actually in the town to move the progress bar. A little odd at first... but in my "meta roleplay" I figured I could treat each district/zone just like that - a market district, a farming district, etc. All in all, highly recommend the game, especially if on sale. If you're looking for combat or a challenge, this one should be a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating of Game: 8/10 | I bought the game during a sale for 10% off at $22.49USDTLDR: The game is pretty worth it to buy if you have an inch of a feeling for a farming simulator game like Stardew Valley with less of the grind, and lingering feelings for various games such as Hat in Time or My Time in Portia or another city builder.| I am writing this review with 7.5 hours of gameplay |STORY: [8.75/10] /Warning May Contain Spoilers to Some People- I strive to make it a general summary/ Like most farming games, your objective is to battle the unknown evil force through cleaning up your farming area, rebuilding, forming quality relationships with your town/world/city's inhabitants and possibly romancing them, etc. General farming sim feels- however, I will say this one has a very unique lore background a lot different than other farming sims. It has really good artstyle. Make sure you are watching and have time to watch the cutscenes when they are happening real time, because it can scroll through very quickly on the text if you haven't set up your options before creating a game.GRAPHICS: [9/10] I am running this game with a 1080GTX at maximum setting. I am not having any noticeable issues with the graphics. They are stylized and cute, and the world design is really great. Gives a whimsical feel.GAMEPLAY: [8.5/10] The game has a very relaxed feel to it. One thing that is interesting to pay attention for is the timed day spans seem to vary at where the day progresses and where it isn't progressing. Make sure to look to see when you are being timed, and when you aren't. If the clock isn't there during a part in the story, or in certain areas, you can take your time to do tasks.  This can make the game feel relaxing at times, and rushed at other times, because when the time is actively going through, it can be pretty quick almost at times.You don't have to, for the most part, balance lots of resources which is a VERY nice take. You don't have to deal with 100 different kinds of seeds when you are planting on your worlds, and you don't have to fill up your watering can. You just switch around on your wheel, or if you are playing a keyboard the key designated for that tool. At times this can be very relaxing, especially with the amount of time you have to perform certain tasks. However, for the most part the game is very relaxing, but the lack of strategy when actually growing your worlds with knowing and planning out resources to plug in can feel lackluster, and start to feel monotonous and grindy.MUSIC: 9/10 The music is wonderful, I really like the title screen song. It was very well done. Most of the sound works perfectly. However, I do notice a bug- when you are exploring the areas where you are building your town. Sometimes when you get a bit close to certain blocked off areas, the sound will almost take on a muffled feel. And that's fine, that's part of the design. But I think the menu/HUD toggling sound effects also become muffled which makes the design they are trying to implement come off as buggy and disconnected.OTHER NOTABLE POSITIVE SIDES TO THIS GAME:+the game is great to sit back and relax to and get a cute little bite-sized story from+if you want a farming sim and city builder and have an itch to find the next best one to play like me, you will enjoy this one+if you appreciate a wonderfully whimsical like feeling in your games, then you will enjoy this game. The artists and video game designers did amazing world design and lore design on this story IMO+the devs are supporting planting trees in our real world, which was enticing for me to invest in for only $20. I garden irl, and I really love planting trees and plants to help give back to our world as well as recycle. Why not support a cause while you're at it of adding this unique gem to your growing collection?+ The devs were responsible for creating Yonder, and the publisher 505 were responsible for publishing titles like Death Stranding which I enjoyed and was very story rich. They seem to both have a good stack of games they have took part in.++++CONS++++Like I said before in my gameplay, at times it can start to feel grindy and monotonous and other times tedious. I still don't think that it takes away from the game in the long run if you want to sit back and enjoy a game for all of it's positives. ++++++CONCLUSION:+++++++buy the game, its 100% wurf

_childDocuments_.review: Grow: Song of the Evertree combines town building, cleaning, growing plants, petting animals, alchemy and exploring dungeons in a charming and relaxing game. By mixing essences like ice, water, dry etc, you can create unique worlds in the branches of a huge tree called the Evertree. In these worlds, you need to clean rubbish, plant seeds and water them to make them grow. When your world is fully grown, you'll get fruits, materials and animals that you can sell for credits, which you need to build your town at the foot of the Evertree. The more houses and shops you build, the more people are coming to live in your town. You need to keep people happy by completing quests and providing them with a job that they like. The game is very casual friendly, as everything you need to do is explained very well. You'll constantly get new objectives to keep you busy. There are also many (hidden) dungeons to explore, where you can find unique items. Despite the fact that there are lot of things to do, the game is a huge checklist with lots of visual customization options. It becomes rather repetitive after a while because you're repeating the same tasks over and over again without any actual challenge. But no doubt you'll have many hours of fun before that happens. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines multiple themes.It is a puzzle exploration game similar to Yonder: The Cloud Catcher Chronicles.It is a game with gardening/farming and resource acquisition, similar to other farming games like Stardew Valley.It is a game with a lot of Animal Crossing like features, such as the towns and the villagers and the designing of them.What it does seem to do is combine the three smoothly and seemlessly into a unique and enchanting world with magical technology and a large amount of exciting and delightful stories and lore to enjoy.The game is endlessly playable and replayable, even if the main story ends the game will endlessly provide quests, tasks, and content, using procedural generation and randomly generated worlds to explore and villagers to meet. There is no end to the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very simple, very lovely, but chill game that I really enjoyed when I just needed to calm my brain down a bit.It's definitely (as negative review say) somewhat repetitive, and lacks for a proper map but I enjoyed the beautiful graphics and general well constructed game - that said I was ready for it to end when it did, as growing worlds in particular is rather chore like.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: AS YOU TRAVERSE THE MAP, YOU SPOT AN EASY JUMPING PUZZLE, WITH NO EXPECTATIONS YOU MAKE IT UP THE HILL, YOU SPOT A CAVE TUCKED AWAY IN THE CORNER OF LEDGE, AS YOU ENTER YOUR FIRST LAVA MAP, YOU HEAR OMINOUS SOUNDS DEEP WITHIN, THE CAVE IS LIT WITH BURNING RED SMOG, YOU CANNOT INTERPRET THE MUSIC AT ALL, NERVOUSLY YOU MAKE YOUR WAY WITH CAUTION AROUND THE NARROW PATHWAY, THE SOUNDS GROW LOUDER AS YOU APPROACH THE END OF THE CAVE, YOU SPOT A GROUP OF NEW NPC MODELS- WELCOME TO THE YODELLING APPRECIATION CLUB!D O Y O U L I K E Y O D E L L I N G ?WTF.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Game!!I've had a niche that has been needed filled ever since the Dark Cloud/Dark Chronicle series and this has come the closest to filling that. I look forward to the next game from this studio because this will go down as an all time favorite. Thank you so much for this game that I will continue to enjoy and love.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice, soft game that I think a lot of people will like. It's technically a farming game, but without the annoying parts like relationships and crop management. You've got an infinite seed bag, infinite water, and a nice long day to spend making your world better.Also, you can save and quit at any time, making it great for casual players!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was worried that this game was TOO cute!!!However, the gameplay, quests, puzzles, caves, locations, town-building and the romance (yep, there is an element of that) made the game compelling. A wonderfully thought-out and constructed game.There are a few issues: no mini-map means it is sometimes hard to work out where to go; a couple of the quests where you need to jump, platform style, made it tricky for me - being older, my reflexes can be a bit slow at times. However, with perseverance, and strategic saves, I did finish them.My other quibbles are that there is no way to delete saved games - the only way is to overwrite them;also, there is no way to load a saved game whilst in play - you have to exit then load.Well worth a try, recommended if you want to escape the harsh realities of life, or just want to relax. Oh, and the music is good too.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a little while since I've opened this game, but I played it for about two weeks straight with a lot of interest. This game is cute and fun, and there is always something to do. I love the building/managing village aspect, and I love creating different islands. The only downfall I would say is that it gets repetitive. I plan on going back to this game eventually (I had a baby, which is one of the reasons I stopped). I hope there are future updates that add some more content. I will say I'm not a huge fan of fishing, but that's minor and would not turn me away. If you are looking for a cute management/farming-ish sim, this is a great game to check out!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really relaxing and entertaining. There is a lot to do: gardening, bug hunting, fishing, city management, exploring, all in a peaceful environment enhanced by the colorful art design.Although the game mechanics have been designed to be accessible to young children (the puzzles are very simple, the city management is relatively minimalist, ...), Grow: Song of the Evertree remains a fun and quite addictive game in the tradition of Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a high rating so badly. I really do. But it does not run. I got it to run perfectly for 2 hours, then just spend 30mins trying to stop it from freezing and crashing. I've removed all of my controllers, my double monitor, changed my resolution, and nothing. There is no more support from the devs. Unfortunately it's not a workable game no matter how much I really enjoy the gameplay itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Nicely designed, and the amount of grinding you need is just right. Recommend this game to anyone love games like Stardew Valley but is tired of doing repetitive works. The scenery, music and puzzle solving part are kinda similar to a combination of Stardew Valley, Legend of Zelda BW and My Time at Portia.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game by Prideful Sloth. I bought this after enjoying their previous game, Yonder, and found Grow to be quite enjoyable as well. While it seemed a little hand-holdy in the beginning, I realized that there was no tutorial and that was instead incorporated into the early game stages. I will admit to being time-stressed at the start, until I understood that the clock stops when your character is in their home base, and in "Else-where". Time runs when you're in the main game helping people, or harvesting/repairing worldlets. Again, a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Underdevelopped. Purchased asset animations. Frequent crashes/freezes + no auto-save. Simple and repetitive to a fault. Becomes pure tedium an hour into it. Development is abandoned. Very little variety of animals, trees, shrubs, etc. Complete, uncontroled randomness in animal colors, villager look, etc.Seeing as this is a pattern of underdevelopment, then abandonment, might want to avoid the dev altogether.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, WHAT. This game is stunning. I saw this game on a Facebook Ad, and added it to my wishlist. I did not know what to expect, as I like to be surprised with these types of games. This game is absolutely GORGEOUS and seems to have a lot of content so far! I love games where you can catch bugs/ fish/ craft. Overall, this game truly scratches the itch of adorable collection games!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, this game is just adorable.Wanna be a he, she or they? The devs got you covered.Wanna build a cute town? Actually a task you need to do.Wanna care for adorable little garden worlds? Yep, a core necessity.It's a calm game, where you can progress at your own pace.A fluffy dragon with dragonfly wings as a fast travel system? Yep, present.Did I mention that it's adorable?
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I recently purchased this game because it has everything i am looking for in a life sim game and than some. Building the worlds to exploring and caring for them have captivated my attention. iv'e spent about 20 hours playing the game in the three days that ive had it. the story is interesting and the style of the game is so cute and easy on the eyes.As a fan of Classical music the music that plays in the background is so soothing, as i play the game ill come back and update the review but so far i am thoroughly enjoying the exploration. They game really encourages the player to take their time and doing what you want to do at your own pace, which is quite refreshing.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I have 11 hours into the game. Have to say this is the most frustrating game I've ever played.  I know I have spent at least 8 hrs totally lost.  There is no compass, no map of the area you are to see where you are supposed to go... for example go find a certain person.  Can't see past the huge houses that are suppose to be small houses. Asked to place decor that it won't let you place. Do the same things over and over again. Inventory full of certain items, they don't tell you how to sell them. Eventually you stumble across what you need but that could take days.  Residents ask for things you don't have and no idea how to get.  This game looks very different but it needs a lot of work to make it nice. Yonder was a relaxing game, this is not. Disappointed.  They encountered a problem, they don't want to post this.The straw that broke this camel's back was the vaults. Inside the vault you are to find a certain stone which will draw back the withering on the mainland. Inside you are expected to be a mind reader... literally. You get one short glimpse of a view of your area. Your inside a huge place often surrounded by water on all sides.  They raise and lower the water, spin you around in circles and expect you to find some unknown item and place in in another unknown place.  I was trapped inside for hours on end.  There is no hope except luck to get out.  Often falling into the water and they revive you and throw you up on a platform in the middle of this place just to try again.  There are no hints or clues and the Discord group can not possibly help you at all.  So, farewell and goodbye.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Yonder, you should like this one as well and there is more to do ; explore, build, GROW and solve puzzles, all with a friendly ecological touch. The game is relax, but not as much as Yonder though there is no fighting and the music is beautiful. Good for kids (8+) and adults alike. There is even a reference to poutine, if you know where to look...What I like :- Character customization like in yonder, but better (could use more eye colors and the hair looks like ballons).- Town, building customization ; plus you can move and delete freely.- Helpers.- Beautiful music.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is my first ever negative review.If this game had been released as early access and was being updated, I'd be happy with it.  But it was released as supposedly a complete game.  What we got instead was something full of game-breaking bugs at every turn.  Just take a look at the bugs thread on the forum - page after page of people running into constant crashes and other issues that are completely ignored.The game also hypes up the idea of growing a huge variety of astounding worlds.  In reality, there are only 6 world types.  Six.  In the entire game.  Spore had much, much more variety than this, and that was released 14 years ago.It's unpolished, full of bugs (both inconveniences and game-breaking disasters), and completely lacking in the variety that's supposed to be its primary draw.  Do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: So, an amazing friend of mine gifted me this game. I was a little skeptical of the game because it looks like something I would love and then it didn't at the same time because of what I've seen. I've played for about an hour and a half and I am completely in love with it. I am so thankful to my friend for gifting me this game because it brings so much joy out of me! All in 1 he of gameplay? That's rare for me. If you love Alchemy, Building, Farming, Adventures, and all the fluffy little creatures, THIS GAME IS FOR YOU!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a refreshing change from killing zombies and looting trash! It's a unique take on pocket worlds and the game is actually pretty huge. AND for first time in MANY years, I am actually finding myself emotionally invested. New creatures I find are so darn cute I could DIE!
