_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute game that is well suited for unwinding after a long day. If you like town building and finding secrets this game is packed with it. The only minor spat I have with it is that growing worlds quickly takes a back seat to everything else.PS. I was not prepared for the romance options for the story npc's and was flabergasted when I accidentally romanced Oleander.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite simply a beautiful escape from reality.  It has absolutely stunning visuals - from the shadows of the fish in the rivers to the colour schemes,  it's pretty much perfect.  I "completed" my world in about 35 hours but have kept on playing because there's still more to do - more worlds to maintain, more people wanting items.  The seed creation is genius - we went mad trying to recreate the "essence" of coffee, or a meat pie, or each family member, and I was astounded to see the variety and aptness of the worlds we created.  For instance my daughter ended up being a "strange seed" in a world with nothing to do but pat animals.  This could not be more accurate.Definitely family friendly, good mix of sandbox and quest.  Had only one early frustration where I had to find an item that wasn't unlocked until later, but the fact I didn't restart and instead spent hours working until I found a way around it speaks to how engaging the game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10The combination of bugs and really weird design choices, both cosmetic and game play, really dampen the experience,If you like repetitive actions in a relaxing environment, it's great, charming, buggy jank with many hours to enjoy.I love it conceptually, but then I got soft locked twice and lost hours of progress while trying to redeem a quest. That's been pretty much the experience with every single mechanic. Everything is just enough to get the gist of it done and then left at that, without any polish. I love it on paper, but then I look and I'm looking at a villagers eyes going haywire while I'm standing in my fish hat clipping through half the floor while the camera is practicing acrobatics. Catching bugs and most of them end up inside an inaccessible wall.Couldn't pick up any fish I caught since they all ended up on land?Trying to float up with an umbrella in a wind draft that doesn't quite give enough lift, falling into a small pond and respawning halfway across the island randomly.Still a good time, just go in with middle expectations
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game (50+ hours) and I really enjoyed it. It is cute but it is the music that steals the show. I loved the music!It's not repetitive if you create perfect seeds where each world is unique. Just google the recipes and you will be good to go. Overall I really loved this game and just could not stop playing. I didn't encounter any bugs and controller support was great.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A bit repetitive. However, it is a cute and relaxing game. Easy to play through without giving too much thought of what to do. Achievements are simple to get if that is super important to the player. Supplies getting is an easy tactic as long as you pay attention to where you can locate it. Making a strange world seed: Half Water/Half Dry + Half Warm/Half Ice This worked the first try for me. Most of the things I found online did not do the trick.Again, very cute and sweet game. You can cuddle with so many cute little animals!I got it on sale. Not sure I would have bought it off sale. Still, a super fun game if you are in the mood to farm a little and create your own town.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up because I tend to play a lot of world simulation games and it was on sale. Very good casual game, and it doesn't feel similar to other world sims that I've played. It has a unique feel, and lots of content. Occasionally the puzzles get a bit repetitive (ex. grab the ball and put it in the hole 1000x), but it's always more fun than trouble. Most of the time, there's constant progression and new material to work with. It feels like I've been playing for much longer than I have, and I can easily see myself marathon-ing this game by accident.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the first 2 hours, but unfortunately the game just never evolves beyond that. Once you've fully grown your first world, completed the first dungeon (with some passable but dull platforming) and built your first precinct to 100%, you've basically seen all the game has to offer - 'unique' items, pets etc are just reskins of old ones.The game will still appeal to a certain kind of person who wants to switch their brain off and just play a relaxing game for an hour every so often, but for someone looking for more progression as you play, there are much better options out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game! I enjoyed the complexity of the quest system and being able to create my own village and handling the villagers, etc. was an A+ for me.  After a point things felt a bit more repetitive, but I played 40+ hours which is enough to demonstrate that there's a lot of good content. Graphics are pretty good and stylized, but not mind blowing and I would've maybe liked a bit more diversity in the village environments.  Overall though, I'd give it a solid 8.5/10 as it's given me a lot of fun and joy.And I see there's been some updates so now I'm going for my second playthrough :)
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.So bored. The farming genre, for a lack of a better term, has grown like crazy.  There are so many different takes on the idea.  Grow: Song of The Evertree, has the player replanting the world to beat back an encroaching darkness, and singing to plants.  It sounds good and it’s certainly popular.  I just can’t figure out why.  So much of this game just feels like chores and not the type that is fun or interesting.  Instead of building towards something, you’re just told to grow plants, farm them for items, and eventually build a town, but everything is so monotonous.  Admittedly, I’m early in the game, but I went back after an hour to play more and I gave up a second time because I was so bored.Pick this up if... honestly, if there’s nothing else.  Maybe this is the type of game that doesn’t work for the first hour review, but as always I ask if the first 90 minutes of the game are so weak, why not cut those out, or improve them?   The thing is while playing the game I started thinking up a list.  Slime Rancher, Stardew Valley, My Time at Portia, Graveyard Keeper, Forager.  Even the soon-to-be greedy Dreamlight Valley all of these games have great opening hours that get players excited for the rest of the experience.  Grow, just feels like it’s chores upon more chores.  I’d rather play any of those six games I mentioned. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: so much better than i anticipated! i appreciated that there was a playable non - binary option. very small gesture but sweet. i had never played an open world game before that was this cosy. it's very colourful yet soft with the old timey architecture, nature and cute animals to interact with. my best animal friend, has to be the cutest dragon i've ever seen. there was a good balance between the organisation in the crafting of the towns and the exploration so i got to choose what i wanted to do based on what i wanted. i'm a big fan of being a collector in games and there were many different items to collect including the underlining purpose of the game to collect all the songs and take them to a place where they belong. crafting worlds based upon essences i had extracted was a beautiful way to show my creativity. this game made me feel so happy :)
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Everything is adorable. Buying and expanding my town feels satisfying and I don't have to wait ages to do so. Taking care of my little worlds is relaxing and lets me zone out a bit. It could feel a little grind-y but I like listening to an audio book or podcast while I do that part of the game. I love that there are strategy puzzles every once and a while. Overall a fun relaxing game, perfect for weekday evenings when I am tired or weekends when my kids are around.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game, but really unpolished at the underlying design level. Of the game's two core gameplay elements - growing worlds and building towns - the world-growing quickly loses any purpose (by the end of the game you can have 14+ worlds active at a time, but by time you finish growing your 4th you already have significantly more *stuff* than you'll need for the rest of the game), and the town building centers around filling the place up with happy, productive townies, but the actual town building goals that advance the game can largely be achieved with only 4-5 people per district. Also, not a sandbox game, just a game with a lot of procedurally generated rubber-stamp content.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most adorable and fun farming/city sim game in ages. If you liked "My Time At Portia" or "Stardew Valley", this game is a wonderful unique mash-up of the two. The animation is cute, the customization (female, male, or non-binary) is truly customizable, and the sound design from the music to the ambient noises is spectacular! If you're looking for a fun, relaxed game to play, this is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute setting with some genuine humor and a familiar but comfortable narrative about restoring balance to the natural world. It has some neat ideas about what that looks like, and some rough edges that make me wonder if I'll be able to finish it, in spite of liking the essence of what it is. I could have sworn to you that this game was a (very polished!) early access title, and am a little bit surprised to find out, coming back to the store page, that it isn't. But overall, if you like this kind of game, there's a very good chance you'll enjoy Grow.The characters, music, artwork, and premise are all inviting and charming. Book and Coppertop, and the EverKin, are especially well-imagined characters.The gameplay is for the most part straightforward, although this game suffers from the phenomenon you occasionally run into wherein a game tries to hold your hand much too firmly in some areas, and in other areas fails to provide you any information at all, leading to a lot of forum browsing for information. I was going to say that I think these issues could be cleared up by QA with some outside players, but having realized this game isn't actually EA, I'm not sure if that's in the cards.I've completed the first 'chunk' of stuff to do, and opened up a new district, and suddenly the comfortable rhythm I established feels a bit less comfy -- there is an overwhelming amount of stuff I could be doing, but it's all the same stuff as before...just *more* of it. I found myself logging out rather than diving in. I'm not sure if it's the time limit pressure of the day/night cycle (very thankfully they've omitted the 'energy' costs with actions present in many of these games), the amount of time it takes to do the chores on each world seed, or what, but it suddenly felt a bit more like a grind than a satisfying path to progress.Overall I really like what this game is trying to do, and wish it was possible to iron out some elements that feel a bit unbalanced/unconsidered/underbaked. But if you like this kind of game, regardless of the annoyances, I think you'll enjoy a lot of what you find here. By all accounts it does those things better than Yonder before it did. If it succeeds, maybe we'll see another lifestyle game in the future, even better than Grow, as the dev studio continues to fine-tune the formula.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game but I encountered some sort of menu bug after adopting my first pet. Seemed like I finally got around the fuzzy menu/pet achievement bug it still corrupted my save. I try to pull a weed or do ANY action and it soft crashes. Really discouraged over trying to get past these crashes and I saw chat about others having their own crashing battles. I have decided to just not play it. Sux.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I think the reviews saying this is a "chore simulator" are pretty accurate.  You don't get to decide where to plant things or what to plant, you just show up and are told exactly what to do and where, you walk up to the thing and push the button they tell you to; if you're looking for a game that's low-key, saccharine sweet, and relaxing, then this game is great!  There's a "city management" aspect to the game as well, but it's almost purely aesthetic.  The "world creation" aspect is very shallow.  The "worlds" you create are little more than small platforms with some plants and animals, your "crafting" of the world changes very little other than the color pallet.  The dialog is bad, the story is extremely generic and feels like it was written by a tumbler tween.  This is a "press F to hug your friends" game, and if you're into that, then definitely buy!  But this is not Stardew, it's not even in the same genre, it's like Spiritfarer but less creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: The good: It is a chill experience. No enemies, no time crunch.The bad: it is VERY clunky. If you want a no brain game where you can spend some time cleaning up magical islands, want to fish or catch bugs this is your game. If you want more I would look elsewhere, like Portia or Sandrock or even their upcoming game (that looks really promising).
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Gra jest naprawdę ładna, ma fajny klimat, jak ze starych gier i filmów, mam na myśli, ile razy można zobaczyć książkę z twarzą? Stworzenia są urocze i uwielbiam odkrywać skarby. Wciąż uczę się niektórych mechanik i będę aktualizować swoją recenzję.Od tej złej strony: Czasami przedmioty przechodzą przez ściany i nie możesz do nich dosięgnąć, więc zbieranie przedmiotów jest złe, latają wszędzie, więc jest 20% szansy na to, że przepadną. (Odkryłam, że robienie niektórych celów zwiększa zasięg podnoszenia, więc to pomaga.) Nie masz mapy, na którą możesz spojrzeć. Nie wiesz, gdzie dokładnie jesteś, i nie możesz sprawdzić, gdzie byłeś, a to trudne, gdy poszukujesz skarbów. Rzeczywiste cele powinny zostać przerobione, jest to mylące, ponieważ niektóre z nich przypominają bardziej osiągnięcia, a inne są jak zadania, więc trudno jest wiedzieć, jak progresować, również esencje? Nie wiesz, jak zdobyć konkretne i możesz utknąć przy zdobywaniu, i musisz spróbować zgadnąć, jaki przedmiot ci je da. Ścinanie drzew też trochę przeszkadza, ponieważ musisz być pod odpowiednim kątem, zwłaszcza przy dużych drzewach. Niektóre skrzynie są trudne do podniesienia, dla kogoś z talassofobią prawie niemożliwe jest przejście przez wodę lub nieskończoną ciemną dziurę, która bardziej przypomina niedokończoną część mapay. Game is really pretty, it's got some nice vibe i get like from old games and movies, I mean how many times u saw a book with face? Creatures are lovely and i'm always hungry for treasures. Still learning some machnics and I will update my review.From bad side: Sometimes items go through walls, and u can't reach them so picking up items is bad, they fly everywhere so in 20% chances, they stuck. (Found out that doing some goals it increases range of pickup so maybe this will help.) You don't have actual map you can look on. You don't know where exactly you are, and u can't check where have u been and that's hard when you treasure hunt. Actual goals should be reworked, it's confusing because some of them are more like achievements, and other are like quest so it's hard to know how to progress, also essences? It's so bad you don't know how to get specific ones and you're stuck at getting them and you have to try to guess what item will give it to you. Chopping kinda bugged too because you have to be at the right angle especially with big trees. Some chests are ****** up, for someone with talassofobia it's almost impossible to go through water or infinite dark ******* hole which looks like it's an unfinished map.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable little world and story. The game does feel a bit repetitive and empty after a while. Only a few NPC's matter and each village area you build is going to be more or less the same, changing very little after you built it in the first place. I appreciate the limited space requiring you to plan what sort of stores/services are available in each town, but so far there's not really a need to interact with your small villages after finishing them off for the story to progress... The tree areas are neat looking but they do get repetitive as well. The story itself is simple and predictable but that's fine. I wish we got to know more about the different races. One of my favourite moments was learning about the robot-looking people's masks. I'd like more of this please. Maybe the ability to recruit someone to help you fix the islands so it doesn't seem like you're the only reason this entire operation functions with no outside input. All in all its got good bones though I think it needs a bit more filling in terms of villager individuality and interactions and tree island utility during growth. P.S. Remove the "Grow" part from the title, it makes the title feel so clunky and harder to remember. I always ended up calling it Evertree or Song of the Evertree in conversation anyways
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying that this game is pretty decent, and I enjoyed a lot of my time spent playing it. The graphics are nice, and the world management is pretty fun for a while.I've enjoyed my time in this game so far, but I just can't bring myself to give it a positive review. I love the grindyness of games like stardew valley, mostly because it feels rewarding in the end, but this game doesn't really give you much in the way of rewards except giving you more of the same stuff to do. Village management started out pretty cool, but the building limit in each of the districts seems too low and there isn't really enough space to place as many buildings as I want. Also having multiple "districts" doesn't really make much sense to me, since they are all exactly the same, just with a different design layout  depending on how you place the buildings. The puzzles in the game are fun, but you aren't really given much chance to figure it out for yourself before the game starts bombarding you with hints or dragging you into a cutscene showing the layout of a puzzle after each step (for example the cave puzzles). The game also seems to have a lot of bugs.For an indie game, I would say it is very good. I put a lot of hours into it, and enjoyed the graphics and the story. But the more I played, the more irritated I felt at how slow my character was, and not to mention how little time there is in each game day, considering you have to manage multiple "worlds" and a bunch of different districts with citizens who have needs. The game feels kind of incomplete, and very repetitive. I don't regret buying it, but I just don't feel like I could give it a good review either.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really beautiful game, both visually and the story! The bright colours and adorable surroundings make it a really relaxing and enjoyable game to play.  As you try to restore the land, you will meet interesting characters, catch bugs, go fishing, help the town and it's people, and often talk to a book and a big glass jar, lol. Overall, I'm really enjoying Grow: Song of the Evertree.  It's a beautiful work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about five hours in, and enjoying Grow. It is so similar to Yonder that I was feeling nostalgic, and carries the same whimsical (without being too silly) and childlike wonder feel. If you like a game that is casual and wholesome and focuses on helping and improving the world, definitely try this. If you liked Yonder, you will probably love this, as Prideful Sloth really seems to have carried the best forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is delightful - I've never played Animal Crossing but I have friends who are serious hooked on that game. Grow seems to be a lovely blend of Animal Crossing, Slimerancher and Stardew Valley all in one. It's gorgeous to look at, has so many options and things to do. I was looking for a game that is just no pressure twee, and this definitely fits the bill. First of all, well done with the score! What struck me most is the game story - they've found a way to weave the music score into the game in a way which is so reminiscent of listening to Peter and the Wolf, I was immediately going on and on about it to my also-musically inclined husband, who sat and listened with me for a while.Also - I give a respectful nod to the character list. When I was a kid, the 'Non-binary' option didn't exist in games. Heck, games insisted they didn't need to put women in games because women didn't play them! A lot of hard work is paying off, and I am glad to see that, slowly but surely, representation is expanding. I don't have only a 'funny afro' to a slightly au-lait skintone if I want to play a non-white character, and I can finally be 'they' in a game for the first time. I got a bit emotional, but then the whole game sort of plays like that to me. This is the kind of game I would have wanted to play when I was (cough) a bit younger than now. Now I will say this - because everything is so shiny, flashy and urgent, you are going to want to DO ALL THE THINGS. I saw about midway in the game would get overwhelming in a hurry if I tried to do everything at once. No you do not HAVE to have five seed worlds going at once. No, you really don't need to unlock every district as quickly as possible. Pace yourself with this game and you will be fine.Well done, developers, for making the game I hope a lot of people can see themselves in, and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. Its super cute and the story seems quite nice. Nevertheless its just not fun to play. The daily tasks are very repetetive and annoying. Also, those daily tasks are the only thing you really have to do in this game and I just cant bear myself to do them. In addition to that it really feels like a mobile game, because you usally just press a button and wait. What I also dont like is the character editor. There could have been so many potential. You can only pick one face for each gender. I think it´s quite awesome that you can be non-binary though.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Grow: Song of the Evertree is an impressive game full of colors and graphics! The storyline is interesting, and I really liked the craft of houses and the creation of a settlement. Every day interesting guests arrive with their abilities. By the time I lost only 3 hours, but it already captures adventure and invites you to help heal a wonderful tree, where I'm sure there will be new and interesting settlements.I rate 10 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: The core game play of the game is fun, assuming you like the farming simulating and town building and such (and if you don't why are you considering buying the game?). That and you don't run into one of the major bugs in the game that require you to restart the game, reload a save, or start the game from the very beginning again. If this is something you'd rather avoid... wait till they're fixed.If you are someone who does not like having their hand held, however, this game is NOT for you. Book and Coppertop, the two main NPCs in the game who run you through the basics in the beginning, never let up. You're always going to get commentary from them on everything you do, be constantly reminded that you have to do things you'd rather do later, and be asked to do things for people you'd rather not interact with. Coppertop will even prevent you from sleeping too early which doesn't seem so bad until you encounter the bug that makes the clock display turn off and time freeze.The NPCs that join your town range from your average person to socially impaired jerk-offs and while you can choose who you build housing for and who not to for the most part, the game does force you to take NPCs who are just as annoying or even more so. Not only do you have to build these guys a house, but you also have to build them their favorite work place and assign them there (even if you have NPCs working there you like) and do quests for them. It can get rather tiresome and the random quests from the NPCs who are randomized aren't much better. 2 of the 3 NPCs I've had to recruit this way, I'd rather punch in the face than help and the rest I haven't met, because I keep running into bugs that freeze the game, give me a black screen, stop time, crash the game, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Let's play this out reasonably; If you have this big flying creature who can teleport you FROM anywhere to a specific two spots on the map that you've already discovered, and one of them is where "Coppertop" is, why do you stop the player from calling "Kazumi" (I think is the default name) by pressing "M" blocking the map with Book telling me to stop asking for a flight and speak to Coppertop first. What is so important that she needs me to be there? Can't I say "Later, I'm busy."? Coppertop is NOT in front of me while I'm discovering the newly opened area, and I'm lost amidst the branches with no access to a map, because Book is being bossy. Not good programming. Reduce the number of shrubs you give, or increase the amount of decorations you can place in an area, by the end of the game it's full and you can't sell it anywhere that I know of. Unless there's some special house I have to walk into to sell shrubs?? I can't turn them into Essences?? I can do it with everything else I collected. Is it GARBAGE? NO!Next problem is when you've got time to hop around on floaty circles of wood chained to a cavern poolbed full of water, it might be nice to re-introduce to "progress-save-spot" mechanics to the tiled parts of the floor that were in-between the switches you had to tromp your way around. No? You want to make a kid do the ENTIRE MAZE WITHOUT A SINGLE MISTAKE?!Oh, I know, teach the kid to swim, and make it fun again, they would be swimming and hopping onto a lillypad and falling over a waterfall. Oh, that's right. No one thought to make the water an object that could interact with by the player. Sure you can run around in some spots, but swim? No, you've decided to kill everyone who gets in the water too deep. Yuck.Raise the floor and let the kid walk around? No, you'd rather kill the poor idiot who thought he could hop reliably from wood disk to wood disk that sinks no matter what  -- waterlogged wood? Really? No logic here.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game intrigued by its promise of growing a world.  The oddest bit of design choice happens at the start: the game starts off feeling very hand-holdy and there were no real meaningful choices, rather a lot of repetitive chores, to start you off.  Once the game actually opens up, it began delivering on its promises and turns out to be an enjoyable experience.  It feels very rewarding to turn a barren land into lush gardens, and to flesh out towns to encourage people to move in.  It feels like there are a lot you can do, and the fantasy of the player actively restoring and growing the game world is well done.I do wish the core "chores" such as chopping down corrupted weeds or smashing rocks or planting stuff could feel more rewarding.  Perhaps this part of the game will open up at some point, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and I will keep playing it for quite a while.  The randomly generated worlds give it a great deal of replayability.  The only issue I have with the game is one many players have complained about: no map!  There is no in-game map to help find things or keep everything strait and it can be very frustrating.  It's not a complete deal-breaker, though, and all the other great features make up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for comfy you found it.I'm editing this because after a few more hours I realize that I hadn't said nearly enough. What seems like a cute sandbox game at first turned out to be deeper and more interesting than I initially thought. This game is positively enchanting. It's adorable. I'm enamored. Seriously. From the little conversations that your weird housemates have randomly to the interesting mechanics around generating new areas for resource and the clever way that all ties in. All the attention to detail helps this game avoid the soullessness that other sandbox games tend to have. There's an older dude in my town and I noticed he goes to bed earlier than everyone else. If that wasn't just a coincidence then I am honestly impressed. Little touches like that breathe life into games. Honestly bravo. Just wow. What a pleasant surprise this game has been. It's clear that the focus was fun and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A friend told me about this game and I absolutely love it!The design is very pretty and cute, you get interesting plants and animals to interact with. I also adore the characterdesign and the best part of it is that this game does not care about gender norms. You can choose between male, female and enby, huge shoutout for that. The soundtrack is beautiful, the story very sweet, interesting and as a human who loves gardening, I had so much fun to watch everything grow and envolve. There´s a lot to discover and the puzzles are easy to understand but entertaining to solve anyway. I was looking for a calming game to play without the pressure of time in this not-so-calming times and after work when I just want to relax, and this game is perfect for that. I could go on and on about the things I love in this game but NO SPOILERS so lemme just say Im a huge fan of this game and of the everkin. I want ten of them in my own garden. More games like this please!Jack
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: For buying this on a whim (and based off of other gamer's reviews tbh), it was my absolute pleasure to be shocked by how much thought has been put in such a cute and almost childish-looking game. Definitely more here than meets the eye. I'm 20 hours in and I still have a lot of things that I want to do and that I'm excited to discover. Well worth the deal that I got it for. Nicely done.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely in love with this game so far. I do wish that tending to the world seeds would get a tad quicker as you progress, but the diversity of the world seeds, creatures, and materials makes it fun to tend them to see how the world will grow. Building the cities, assigning townies to jobs, and customizing everything is also a fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game with my Humble Choice games and decided to play it the moment my games unlocked as I was in the mood for a silly little farming sim to just pass my time on. Did it meet my need for a silly little farming sim? Absolutely. Did it also give me so much more than just a farming sim? YES. There are so many little hidden gems in this game and I actually love the storyline as well. There are neat little puzzles around the world/worlds, adorable and strange little critters you can tame and pet, many caves to explore, people to talk to, places to decorate and lots of towns to repair. I've also found that it is quite an inclusive game. I absolutely love that there's no time limit on completing quests or taking care of your worlds as I find that games that add the time limit can often add a level of stress I'm just not quite looking for when I jump into a simulation game such as this one. Would I recommend this game to everyone? Not necessarily as you can see from the other reviews, but this game keeps me entertained and allows me to move everyone and do several different things as well as look at lots of cute creatures and decorate my little towns.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: In general I really enjoy the game loop and the game plays well on the deck. Game is a chill farming simulator with some platforming elements. However the game has a game crashing bug when the first pet is adopted that has been present for over a year and there is another bug when collecting a reward from the book. There are various workarounds so you can play after the game crashes. In my case I had to let the game sit and wait for night to get off the tree before I could resume my game. I will recommend this game once game breaking bugs are patched.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Flawed but chill game, looks good, gameplay is alright, controls can be a bit clunky. The world-creating/gardening part of the game was fun at first, but completely lost its charm when I realized that they're all randomly generated copies of one another with a different coats of paint. Working on them becomes almost completely meaningless if your goal is to progress the story, they're just resource farms and nothing else. At least you can pet cute (or ugly, depending on what the randomizer picks) animals once you've taken care of a world for long enough..?The city building and management aspect works well for the most part, except a lot of the building areas are so narrow that placing some of the larger structures becomes quite challenging. It can very quickly turn into playing tetris with the buildings just to fit everything you need.I binged the entire game in about 3 days and the gameplay loop definitely started wearing thin near the end. The game introduces a bunch of stuff in the first 3-5 hours of the game, you'll be unlocking new things left, right and center and then you do the same things for the rest of the game. I feel like it really could've used something to spice things up around the 2/3 mark.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Stardew or other life sims you'll know about what to expect. It's a cozy and solid game.My main criticism would be that it lacks a fair bit of polish. Things like your character only being half animated when holding a tool. Positioning to get an interaction prompt can be fiddly. Or trying to interact on the move both stops you and looks awkward. Some transitions, in cutscenes or otherwise, are a bit rough. Some sounds cut in or out suddenly.It's a cute game, but it could benefit from some refinement too.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: More than recommend! This game is revolutionary. I don't even know where to begin. This is one of those once in a lifetime games that comes around. It's so different from anything I've ever played before. Basically, this is kind of like a fantasy farming game. I put this one right up there with titles like Dragon Quest 11 S, Trials of Mana and Tales of Vesperia. Just to clarify, this is not a review. This is only my personal opinion and recommendation. Difficult to explain here just how fantastic this game really is. What really is hard to believe is the fact that it's so cheap. This is EASILY better than MANY games on Steam that I've paid $60 for. They could sell this game for double the asking price and it would still be a bargain. It's one of the most beautiful looking and fun games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. 1000% recommend. It's sooooo much more than just farming. There's so much to explore and find with secret areas, dungeons, the Everkin realm, all the little areas you unlock, build, design, customize the buildings, decorate, increase your friendship with tons of villagers, plant new seeds on the Evertree that turn into worlds. The worlds themselves even grow larger as you tend to them. Some of them even grow caves to be explored with plenty of loot to be found within them. Time does not pass while in the caves, so you can go into them and gather all those resources for alchemy without any time passing. There are many different buildings to unlock for your villages, it's just great. There's so much stuff I could mention and this game deserves much more love than it's gotten. Grow has become one of my all-time favorite games and even after nearing 50+ hours of play, there is TONS of content yet to unlock and things to do. There are special little events that will pop up with certain villagers that add more depth to their character and make the game a little more interesting. I'm probably missing hundreds of great features about this game but one thing is for sure: if you pass on this one, you're seriously missing out on something special in my opinion. I love Grow so much, I bought it here on Steam and on the Nintendo Switch. Anyway, if you're on the fence about purchasing, you shouldn't be. You will love this game once you see what it's all about. A vast, beautiful fantasy-type farming/exploration/town building game that will wow you with its art, gameplay, music and overall experience. One of the best games ever put on the Steam store. Trolls that know it's true will just laugh or leave a stupid response. Haters are gonna hate!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I was surprised how good this game was because I found it a bit childish and simple at first. I am glad I stuck with it because it turned out to be really good. I enjoyed the town building part of the game the most. The part where you have to look after a biome every day gets annoying after a while but at least it lets you ignore that part if you want to. The game is easy and the puzzles are quite simple but do require some effort to get them done. Overall a very enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Grow is kind of nostalgic in the fact that it feels like Dark Cloud but without the dungeon trampling. I'd call it a much more relaxed Dark cloud. While the taking care of the worlds get a little repetitive. Only so many times I can pull evil weeds before I need to take a break, it has it's little charm. Enjoy the different people you can meet in town. Like customization in the game and the fact of getting the creatures I enjoy. Enjoyable if you just want a relaxing game to unwind after using all your brain power with work and more harder adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game but unfortunately didn't enjoy it. It's a mix of Genshin (exploring), Sims (village builder and villager management), and animal crossing new horizons (in terms of game play). But it kinda took the fun parts out of all these games? _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a fun and relaxing time! Not a lot of challenge, and the challenges are pretty easy. But that's what I love about it, I'm not stressed when playing it. It can get repetitive, but I honestly don't mind that either. Everything is adorable too! And it's so much fun exploring the world and finding hidden items and places!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I like how the game always has something to do.  You are always making progress and seeing the progress in the world as you open more areas, growing your towns, and bringing life to your wolds that you make with alchemy. The only problem I have is I wish there wasn't a cap on how many decorations and buildings you can have in your towns. Maybe there is a way to increase the limit that I am not aware of, but as of now I do't know. Other than that I am really enjoying the game,
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool game, lots of things to do. Sometimes too many things to do in one day. The only thing I did not like is that more people arrived in the towns then you actually had room for. I thought they would just migrate to other towns but they don't. They just wander around with a big "give me a home" over their head. Making the seeds are fun. I wish there were more then 6 different types of worlds. The strange worlds give you cool things and you can delete these seeds as soon as you plunder the land. Its a good story though, and there are many cute items you can decorate with.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the character models and scenery design. I found the game play relaxing as there's no timer, you can end your day as you wish without being a walking simulator. The controls are smooth and easy to pick up for anyone.What I didn't like and the reasons I don't recommend:- The tutorial was painful, asking to do things which are relatively obvious and shouldn't need "hand-holding".- Some things can be harder to find and should have been in the tutorial, such as the exit gate (that's one use the "find work" option WOULD actually be useful for!)- I would prefer an actual map of an area to find what I'm looking for instead of summoning the flying mount, summoning it should be exclusively for moving to areas you would otherwise not be able to access.- The play can be motion sickness inducing, really needs a slower frame rate or option to slow- I found the npc's dialogue unnecessarily excessive and dull - The lore and characters are dull- The game activity is very simple, repetitive and not very rewarding- I loved the music to start with, but it quickly gets repetitive and irritating - it needs more variation/tracks.- The game crashes after a few hours.- Town building to switch up the activities of growing the song tree is unrewarding as the people and buildings do nothing. It's too simple to be considered aesthetic decorating.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple with a nice dash of complexity to keep you addicted. I have had to force myself to stop playing this game in order to try out some other titles I have recently purchased, because it is so easy to get lost in the game loop. This is more a town builder sim than a farming sim since you don't actually grow any crops. You do grow 'worlds' and can gather unique items from that world to grow more worlds or grow your little suburbs, but overall that is more than enough to keep you engaged.There is a clock in the game, but it only runs when you are in your towns and on your 'worlds'. If you go inside your house, a cave, or visit the Everkin, time freezes. Allowing you to take your time in those places without feeling rushed. It also helps provide ways to pause the game in case you have to step away suddenly. The games saves often as well, so if it crashes or you have an issue with power/your PC you won't loose too much progress.Any complaints I have about the game are very minor. I've noticed that my citizens are putting up axes, carts, or clotheslines outside their house's box. This has led to some disappointment where I think I had things places nicely only to find such items blocking the prebuilt path markers. I also feel a little dissatisfied with how the Everkids work. It would be nice if they could be tasked with specific jobs on the world, like gathering bugs or fish versus nuts and fruits. The time between harvests is fine, but I wish I could influence what and how much is found just a little more. It would also be nice to have a little map that I can access without calling my flying friend just to see where I am at in relation to other locations in the game. I found myself accidentally exploring in circles and missing large areas of the map.A slightly bigger, but still small issue, is getting essences for creating some of the perfect seeds. I'm stuggling to get Cute, Mushy, and Spongy essences. This was mitigated a little with the sale of essences in Everwhere, but some essences just seem tough to acquire in the beginning (which I know is meant to fuel experimenting with seed creation.)
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Baby's first hypercasual, ultra-cozy, kitsch-drenched and rather uninspiredly lore-infused alchemy sandbox city builder. You'll probably keep coming back for the evertree part, though: Mixing new world seeds, tending to the new areas of the tree and seeing them grow into different biomes with a wide variety of proc-gen species, plants and minerals is actually really satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. I just finished the story and there's still so much to do! I loved Yonder so I was excited to play this and I'm so glad I got it. It's charming, the visuals and soundtrack are stunning, and it's such a relaxing game! It's fun to experiment with world seeds, not knowing what type of world you'll end up with, what type of plants you'll get or what cute little creatures might inhabit it. I highly recommend checking this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely wonderful in every way when it comes to relaxing games.  The music is great,  it's very serene,  the dialog of the many characters is witty and entertaining, and all around its absolutely beautiful.  The gameplay is very smooth as well. If you're a fan of games like the original harvest moon series before they split/rune factory/ or maybe even a little bit of Slime rancher then this game is 100% for you.  There's no combat but there is you effectively battling an enemy by creating wonderful new worlds by restoring the environments with trees, plants,  and much more. 10/10 I highly recommend.  May I also mention that the photo mode in this game is absolutely great as well for you photographers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say good things about this. It's beautiful beyond anything. It's charming. It's quirky. But it's a chore. The main gameplay loop is cleaning an island to watch it grow. Which sounds kinda cool, and watching it grow is cool. But it takes several days to get there, and a hell of a lot of mindless button presses. It's so close to be amazing. But it's not a system you can ignore, or slowly partake in. I don't mind monotony in games, but it feels like 4 button presses just to plant one shrub.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted this more than it gave me.The main idea of the game is nice and cute - save the tree through harmony within the villages. First question: why can't the tree have harmony without a village of stupid humans?? Okay, lets say it is a ... different... tree and can't have harmony without humans. You get to create seeds by collecting stuff from different worlds and mix the essences together. But you have to collect a lot of stuff and nowhere to see what you already had (and destroyed). You also need the essence to buy buildings for your villagers - to create harmony. the maximum amount of essences needed per village is 260, those are very mixed though. Nonetheless, you will end the game with over 200 essences of some sorts and less than 10 of others. Second question: when i have a currency to build worlds, why would i use them for a building? seems like a waste to me, with all those humans not being happy about their jobs which you gave them because they requested them. Kinda confused? I was, too. If a villager wants to be a hairdresser and I specially build a Hairsalon and offer them a job, why can they be unhappy two days later?   When I play a game with main feature "collecting", I want a sticker book or smth where i can mark off my findings and get rewarded for a full collection. So all possible world seeds, the wood, stones, fish, insects all within one book and as reward you get a... special building part in the middle of the village where villagers of different villages can interact?! Or small trees to help the big one recreate? whatever, i never felt special since reaching 100% harmony of first village. Why do I need to feel special? Hello, they requested me to regrow a freakin evertree and i am the only one who can sing songs to make it happy, I am a special person! Soon I learned only to go harvesting in the worlds, no need to complete them. no need to answer the requests for villagers, cause they can't get mad and don't go away. No need to return to a world 3 times after completing it to tame the final animal, cause a 100% research rate won't do anything good for you. No need to go to the ever-village bc you can harvest everything in the tree. No need to grow new seeds, cause with 5-6 well chosen worlds you can harvest every essence you need. Why do I have 31h of playtime when I'm not happy with this? Bc I wanted all the achievements and I felt this one has much more potential that it was expressing. So yeah, If you are content with a game thats pretty much wasting it's potential on repetiveness, this one will be right for you. Oh, there is a book but it only marks off quests and you don't even need to complete them to finish the game. and as reward you get costumes or tapestry - things you already own plenty from. There should be a way of completing 100% of the game (and an achievement).
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: It's not too hard to explore and also not too difficult to manage the precincts as long as you're not a perfectionist going crazy about fulfilling every single possible desire. The story is melancholic and sweet and the animations of the critters are very cute indeed. It's like less elaborate Animal Crossing and will suck your time if you need to relax a bit. Even someone with bad reflexes like me can handle the tiny bit of platforming required.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to love this game because as you can see it's beautiful and the 4 hours i spent was great until i came across a bug that won't let me progress any further and looking through the discussions a lot of people have had the same issue along side other breaking bugs, so with that, I honestly cannot recommend this game. The developers have left this game to go dry so I wouldn't bother wasting money on something that isn't going to be fixed even on sale. I'd suggest buying another alternative game like Yonder, Portia or any other type of relaxing farming, role-playing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, cute, colorful game to just unwind and relax with. While the tasks can seem repetitive or monotone at times, they're actually all part of the whole - let your mind go - experience that this is. It's sweet, simple and lifts the mood. Has good crafting and exploring elements to it, the story is interesting and the characters goofy and adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: is not a bad game, for me is a big step back compared to yonder.my little son liked seeding, watering, singing and the bouncing mushrooms, but my son is barely 4yrs old.the game cicle and the story are boring, drawings are really cute.buy it to play with your little children. if your child is not so little yonder is better.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The colors are fun. Everything is pretty much adorable. If you're looking for a relaxing game this is it. With the ability to create worlds, building towns, completing quests and improving your own skills, there's plenty to love. With the regular monthly updates it just keeps getting better.Personally this game helps me destress, and collect my thoughts about the day. The game play isn't overbearing. But if I want I can spend a great deal of time upgrading my buildings and interacting with the towns people.There isn't a lot of in depth interactions. Everything is very one sided. And it feels a little.. ambiguous. Like I'm not certain which conversation options will lead where.Overall I love this game. This visuals are stunning. Controls are smooth. This game still has a little ways to go. But I cannot tell you how excited I am about it. I'm thrilled For the developer.Good job! Keep it up! You have a fan for life.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game just yesterday and already have 8 hours of playtime. I can't remember the last time I loved playing a game for the first time this much as I do this game. Finally something  a little different from the usual games, relaxing, and just up my alley. I love creating things, I love buiding something up, I love town building, I love developing something new. It's exactly  everything I always dreamed of.I honestly am already l ooking forward to Grow 2, but  I doubt it's even being developed. This game is still very new. It's just that good, that I'm already dreading finishing it and then never feeling the same again and never finding a game that matches up to the amazing gameplay this one have.I bought it on sale, but it's surely worth the full price. _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute,cozy and unique game. I went into this having no idea if I would like it, honestly think I got it with a humble bundle but it really ended up surprising me with how well made it is. Being able to essentially have endless content with the seed mechanic if you really wanted to was nice. _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A simple, casual management game with a shallow story and repetitive game play.I'm always on the hunt to find a new game to fill the void that Stardew Valley left, and I can definitely tell you that this game has NONE of the charm that made Stardew Valley great. The story is so basic to the i didn't even realize I had accidentally started a relationship with one of the two other characters you can talk to. It's like the developer was scared to say the word "love" or "date". The gameplay at first seems expansive, but it quickly becomes repetitive and grindy when nothing new is added between areas other than a new color scheme to do the same repetitive tasks in.I honestly don't know how this game has such good ratings because it feels like a game made by an overprotective parent for their 8-12 year old child. Nothing dangerous, nothing emotional, nothing challenging.  Maybe this would be fun if I was younger or had a kid of my own, but as it is, i can't recommend this game for anyone over the ago of 14.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: At the same time I liked this game but at the same time I found it little bit boring. Visually this game is stunning and the world  around you makes you feel calm and relaxed. Music is nice and story is 8/10. I think gameplay was repetitive at times and too easy for my liking. Building cities and making people happy was so easy that most of the time I only had to build couple buildings and everyone in the city was happy. There were nice little tasks from people that lived in your town but they never really brought any depth to the characters and in the end I didn't really care that they were there. Also somehow everyone kinda looked the same and even though you changed hair or clothes there were so little amount of options that they looked the same anyway.  + Nice to look at+Stress free game+Little secrets around the world+Cute characters- Too easy - Repetitive gameplay - Shallow characters- Not enough customization options for buildings or characters even though it was big part of the gameplay I can't say I don't like the game but it wasn't as good as it seemed like at first when I saw reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

Choose the layout and style of your city, manage villagers & play a beautiful story. 4. _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really fun, laid-back, peaceful, relaxing, non-violent, chill game. You play at your own pace. There is no rush or worry you'll miss stuff. Super wholesome. Lots of secrets to explore, lots of stuff to do. You feel like you are making a real positive difference in the world. The story is really good. Exploration is encouraged and very rewarding. Elements in place to make sure each game is unique; no two players or save files will have the same experiences. 11/10 would highly recommend to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good! I strongly recommend it if you are someone who likes Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley. You can manage a village or grind out worldbuilding, like I did. It's really satisfying to see an island you made transform from a lifeless wasteland to a lush, beautiful place. Each island is unique and interesting, especially since you can make them yourself with alchemy.The animals that spawn in the islands are unique to you! They, like everything else about the island, are influenced by your alchemical ingredients and are really cool! I have screenshots of a few of mine.Last thing I'll mention: The character customization is really nice! There are nine body types to choose from and you can choose to be non-binary! As someone who uses they/them, it's really nice to see this being incorporated in games. The only flaw with the character creator is that it is lacking in hairstyles and facial features.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by saying that this is the first review I have ever written for a game. I got this game on launch day and have only been able to sink about 18 hours into it but I have have LOVED every second of it. It is such a peaceful and BEAUTIFUL game. Often now, have I been stuck in photo mode taking pictures of beautiful worlds I have planted or just the home world in general. The game also runs great and I have yet to run into any major bugs or glitches. The replayability is absolutely there and getting to make your own custom seeds with a plethora of different attributes is also a rewarding experience as you watch them grow and tediously tend to them. There's also puzzles to solve, dungeons to delve, and towns to build with all the random npcs in them that you not only get to build relationships with but get to choose housing for and assign jobs(after you build the workplace of course). You can also fish, mine, cut wood, adopt animals, and catch insects. At first I will admit that I thought the game may be a bit too childish for me in the beginning but then it opened up and I was sucked right in. If you're a fan of games like Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, and My Time At Portia, you will love this title!
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy as heck. Strains my low end, several years outdated laptop. The town builder and the world growing halves of the game feel like two separate games stapled together. Hate the Find my X quests as the object either never spawns or despawns after night and the quest giver doesn't have any other interaction until you find X. That means no gift giving, no talking and no changing their look. Rest of town builder is fun trying to find the optimal amount of housing to jobs to max out everyone's happiness/stars. World growing is my preferred half. Running around and performing different tasks to nurturing a world, while repetitive, is a game play loop i quite enjoy. Did have a world grow INTO the Evertree though, I could run through the tree to tend to the rest of the world and only put up with it because that world was so different from the pervious worlds I had grown. 6.5/10 Good for a few hours but there are better farm sims out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent choice if you want to waste time and relax as you play. Sadly, it's not for me. I went into this game thinking it's like Stardew Valley or any other farming sim game, but this game is not. This game is more like Animal Crossing and more for a casual audience where you play around 30 minutes every day. So while I don't like this kind of game, and will refund it, there's nothing glaringly wrong or broken with it. I would recommend it if you are only looking for a casual game where you can waste an hour a day or so playing.In the short amount of time I played, I already feel like I've completed the full game loop. You wake up and go to the island where you grow things. You take care of the debris, water plants, collect produce and then you go home or visit the village. You collect essences from your islands while you take care of it and can spend it on the simplified village management sim the game introduces to you early on. Although I was just introduced to the village in my game, I can already see where it's headed. I'm guessing, the goal is to grow the village and expand it, while eliminating the wither at the base of the Evertree. After managing the village is over with, you go home and sleep. Then the cycle repeats. Each day loop takes about 10-15 minutes, but I expect the time to increase as you expand the village and unlock more islands.I think the main selling point of the village is the idea that you can customize everything in it. As I progressed through the early game, I earned a TON of cosmetic items. Things ranging from new player hairstyles, to different types of wallpaper for houses were given as rewards. This is why I feel that the game is very similar to animal crossing, because you're allowed to design a unique town with your own flair to it. However, this is also why I lost interest in the game; I don't enjoy spending time designing and planning how and where I put things.The best aspect of this game is the atmosphere and the music. The game is very bright and cheerful, the colors are vibrant and the music, although simple, completes the overall feel of the game. As I went through the opening, funny quips in the music and sound design really add life to some of the characters you meet. Overall, I can see that the devs made great choices in this aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Currently refunding this game until more bugs have been fixed/are not game breaking. This game has a lot of potential and is beautiful, even when being lazy and playing on a laptop. I love that the graphics setting for below low is "my hardware is on fire".It's been a week of the game not being playable without completely starting a new save file. If this was in alpha or beta, I would find that acceptable but not for a fully released game. I've reached out via the forums, bug report, and 505 support ticket but have yet to hear back. My game is currently stuck after the game where it wants me to do a certain action, advanced saying I had the resources when I didn't and will not complete that building, or even place buildings I do have the resources for. The only way to even get out of that menu is force exiting the game. Upon getting back into the game, my last save was after the resources were spent but the game will not let me do anything else in game and will only flash going to the build menu where it'll get stuck again.I'll happily re-purchase and try again once issues like this are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: CONS: individual town and world navigation is a huge pain without a mini map. It’s incredibly easy to get lost or turned around even in the beginning of the game. At 4 worlds and 4 districts, I still get lost easily and have a difficult time finding things. It can be a bit frustrating especially when you're not really allowed to explore at night. It can get a little repetitive, but if you're a completionist, this game will keep you busy.PROS: I really like the concept of Grow, and the art is adorable. The alchemy is a fun, but grindy task. Town building is also fun, but be warned  that there is a building limit per district! You'll end up having to delete buildings if you're not careful, wasting essence in the process. At this point, I'm playing to discover the art and see what all of the "Perfect Seed" worlds look like. I probably wouldn't have played this if hadn't been for a Humble Bundle gift, so I'd be cautious and read more reviews if you're thinking of buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

I'm sorta excited to be one of the 'first' people to play it, so I can actually go around and tell people to play it (but not in a gate-keeping or elitist way) :DAmazing world and character design.Yes,  you can pet the animals.A LOT of content - town-building, taking care of nature, character customization / accessories.Also, you can make your character NB and I think that is just neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game to get lost in and relax. You'll be creating random world seeds, and then clearing them of their taint while at the same time farming them for resources which you need to make more seeds and provide buildings and decorations for your citizens. A great balance from farming resources and then creating and managing a large city as you play. You're putting down buildings, assigning citizens to houses and then assigning them to jobs.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I made the mistake of running round trying to look after too many worlds and doing everything at once.  You can do 2 or even 3 seeds if you want but I've learned to just do one world seed and spend the rest to the day trying to help the villagers, even if at first I can't afford or do much for them.  It takes awhile to build up the points and everything this way but worth the extra time in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, but it becomes a rehash of the same thing about a third of the way in, although just in different environments.Basically, you do stuff on an island seed.  That could be tend plants, pet creatures, clear debris, etc so that you can get access to plants or rocks or wood to break them down into essences.  You need essences to build stuff in your towns.  Each town is pretty much the same thing, although there's little variation.  Each seed is basically the same thing, just reskins and they gives you different essences.There's a little bit of an overarching story, but not much.  It's not a "deep" game.  It's a very relaxing, go at your own pace type of game, but I would definitely recommend.  It just got boring after about 25 hours in.  I was about 2/3 of the way "done".
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down my favorite relaxing game! I have been looking for tears for a game with a calm atmosphere, a wonderful sense of exploration, beautiful scenery and a place to call home. Grow: SotE give you that! With a deep city management aspect and STUNNING and huge world, it blends together in a truly relaxing game. So so SO much customization to your character, your houses, vegetation and citizens!Many city management games, farming games etc can feel stressful because you have a ton of stuff you need to do each day and the more you expand the more things you need to keep up with. Grow let's you work as hard or slow you want. You are not at all punished if you just wanna take a day exploring caves and finding secrets.The story about the Evertree is brilliantly told piece by piece throughout the game and it actually has a beautiful message.A game that gives you SO much to do, so much to explore and after many hours I keep finding new things to be mesmerized about. I simply can't stop playing and this is a game world I truly can relax in. I have found the game I was looking for for so long. Thank you <3
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful story, beautiful world, beautiful music!In this game you embark on the adventure to restore the Evertree and save the world from the withering. You can split your time between building the city (unlocking new districts as you progress the story) and creating new worlds on the Evertree.There are LOADS of different things to do, befriend the people who will begin to inhabit your cities, create love interests, befriend animals, catch fish and insects, participate in festivals etc. There are a lot of different quests and tasks for you to complete, some will even grant you perks.There are also MANY customization possibilities both when it comes to your villagers and the worlds that you can create, I was very fascinated about all the different possibilities and outcomes. Some worlds were super beautiful, others downright weird xDI loved spending time exploring the city districts and discovering some of the many secrets hidden all around, whilst finding out what happened to the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I will agree with the other reviews of this game. This is repetitive, kind of boring. Half the stuff isn't really explained, there are too many things. No inventory management (like filter etc) so it's just a jumble when you try to find something. Some animations for the characters are just... weird? The two fingers touching appeared too much for my liking. The temples were boring, there were unexplained sentries you had to avoid. There is like 7 towns.... which is 4 too many. After the third time, the third dungeon I was ready to be done. I actually haven't finished it, because even though I'd love to see the ending I can't force myself to play another hour or two of tedious and unimpactful gameplay. Building stuff doesn't really impact your gameplay, there's no skill involved. The main gimmick is that you can sing to the plants and animals when you heal the things in the sky.. It doesn't even have a tune! there's just a sound effect like a small sound wave. The animation for a lot of things are too long (going into and out of maps etc.) and the fact that even when you have the item you need to pay "money" to place the item just makes the start of the game longer that it needs to be....The story? Kind of fun, the world lore is nicely built. I LOVED the drawing mural when the tree "speaks" to you, they were really well made. The animation for the tree growing was funny because it looked like a ps1 animation but it felt more endearing than anything else. Finding notes made me thing of magical melody, but there are a lot of things that would need a lot of work before I'd play something from this dev team again. There's love in it, but a lot of it feels like filler and I would have loved it if it was tuned a little better.I would not recommend this game unless it's below 10$ and you like repetitive tasks.
_childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun, gentle, excellent, entertaining game.  Kid friendly.   I liked the fact that one can play this game at their own speed.  I love all the little hidden treasures.    The only thing lacking is that as the world expands, it would be really great to have horse, or horse like creature to get around with in towns.

_childDocuments_.review: People who gave negative reviews in this kind of games are used to violent, adrenaline pumping and run-of-the-mill kinda games which I am tired of. I have played both Family Computer and outside games in my childhood with other children, so pretty much I have good gaming wisdom.Hear me out!In my college days, I mostly played Dota 2 and other competitive games. _childDocuments_.name: Grow: Song of the Evertree

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot. I like the graphics and the gameplay. I like that you get to build your towns however you like and that you can choose different decorations for each house. I love the idea of putting different elements together and creating random worlds from them that you get to care for and that you see grow.I love that you don't HAVE to care for your worlds or villagers. If you don't feel like it, explore or do other stuff all day long. There is no time pressure whatsoever. My only gripe is that it does get a bit repetitive after a while. You get up, go to your town, build houses and decided where to house / employ your new villagers, fly up to your islands, weed, water, plant stuff, go to bed, rinse repeat. You do get to explore the lands in between, which is fun, and there are a few other things you can do, but after I was about halfway through, I started to get a bit bored. Not enough to stop playing, but it wasn't the full enjoyment I had hoped for. So overall, I would say, if you like this style of game, grab it, but perhaps wait for a nice sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, straight off the bat, I really, really dislike the aesthetics.The game looks good, it does, but the player model is... bad. Really bad. On par with My Time at Portia bad.It's a really bad case of butterface, weird body proportions, plastic, static hands that are waaaay too big and arms waaay too long.
