_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game where you modify the level geometry in order to advance. You carve out things that stand on your way and add missing things. It's presented through intuitive mechanic where you make photos and then place them in front of your sight and everything becomes just like if what's on the photo is actually there.Technically the way this system works is very impressive. The engine modifies meshes in runtime, automatically filling resulting holes in geometry.There's nice learning curve and interesting variety of puzzles: from the ones you'd breeze through to the ones that would make you feel like you've done the impossible, if you stay on it long enough, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanic is incredibly impressive for a few minutes, but it feels like it never hits a stride. Only two puzzles felt 'good' to me though your mileage may vary. This feels more like under-explored mechanic than well balanced.The story comes across as clichéd, and it becomes even more confusing when you attempt to connect the mystical elements in the ending. I can't help but think that the experience would have been more enjoyable if they had focused solely on the puzzle aspect, removing the unnecessary voiceovers and attempts at profundity. I suspect that in another 10 years, this topic will feel outdated compared to other outstanding titles in the same genre. However, I believe that maintaining the same theme but transitioning to a "show-don't tell" approach without audio could have significantly enhanced the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Viewfinder was a wonderfully refreshing puzzle game. I only spent three hours with the game, but every hour with that was simply terrific. _childDocuments_.review: Viewfinder is a fun short innovative puzzle game taking me just under 6 hours to complete as an experienced puzzle gamer. I only was stuck on a handful of puzzles for more than 5 minutes but crucially never felt the need to reach for a guide. The freedom to rewind and experiment with the rules and physics as new mechanics are introduced was fantastic. Physics glitches did occur from time to time due to the nature of the game, but I never suffered any major technical issues with the game.Ultimately while I wished the game explored more of its interesting side mechanics in each associated hub world and overall had a longer length, I did enjoy my time with Viewfinder. If price is a factor in your decision, I would recommend picking it up on a sale, where it has regularly now been 25% off. I’d give Viewfinder a 7 out of 10 (Very Good) and would love to see a level editor/additional content added in future.

_childDocuments_.review: Viewfinder is mechanically creative – Super Mario-like in that most of the puzzles aren't particularly challenging as much as they are showcasing interesting ideas. Only a few puzzles gave me pause, several made me feel clever, and there were a couple instances of tickling mind-bendery. I didn't find the story to be particularly compelling, and some of the dialog was grating to the point that I wished I could skip it. Its most egregious quality is how emotionally exploitative it is. The story forces you to make what is intended to be a morally gray, or at least morally complex "choice" and then twists the knife in a way that I found pretty tasteless – an emotional cheap-shot that you'll find has some people tied up in knots if you search around. (Spoilers below)I do recommend it generally, I just...bleh, elements of the story and that ending are kind of a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I... Hesitated on reviewing this game due to thinking it's an insanely novel game with things I really like, but there are 3 major flaws that just sour the experience.Let's start with the positives:1. The MechanicsGenerally very creative and abstract, allowing for probably thousands of dumb roundabout solutions, I ended up doing a lot of random stuff for fun and the game allows you to generally thanks to being relatively lenient on how you decide to solve puzzles.2. The VisualsBeautiful. The different styles you encounter throughout the game are something to behold. There's some polish missing here and there, mainly with some level transitions (most notably the lack of any when exiting a level), but nothing major.Now for the Negatives....1. Story kinda just sucks.Yeah this was probably the most frustrating part. The game establishes itself as a classic dystopia torn by global warming, not inherently bad but the really predictable plot built off of it is, and the cliché ending didn't help.2. Repetitive and lack of much challenge.Whilst I do appreciate the do-it-your-own-way nature of the puzzles it also ends up with difficult levels being hard to make, and the hardest levels I had throughout the whole game were just because I missed a piece, and that was just frustrating. Unfortunately, this lack of challenge is paired with a repetitive game, almost every puzzles feels like it's introducing a mechanic again and again and very often it ends up with the same solution to tons of levels.3. Short and sweet but WAY overpricedI'm all up for short and sweet games, linelith is still one of my favourite puzzles games, difference being it lasted 2 hours but cost 3 euros, this game with only 5 hours costs 25 euros, It's pretty, sure, but a much more adequate price tag would be near the 10-15 euro mark.In Conclusion, one of the most creative games I've seen visually and sometimes mechanically, but ruined by a price tag, repetitiveness and a generic narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been almost a year since I played the game, but I'll write the review based on what I can remember.Viewfinder is one of those first person puzzle games that have unique gimmick: taking pictures and then placing them back into environment. The thing is that all the objects in the picture transform into physical objects. You can for example by reorienting the picture make a makeshift bridge out of it (store screenshots have actually screenshot of that). Nice feature is that you rewind time, so small mistake doesn't mean that you need to replay the whole level.It manages to add new things along the way, like non photographable surfaces and making power flow between to points in various ways.There's plenty of optional levels, but for me they got bit frustrating, though some of them have refreshing ideas how creatively use the game mechanics to make puzzles. Didn't feel like playing them all.Final level is bit annoying with the time limit, but luckily it can be turned off.Still, while Viewfinder has faults, Viewfinder is worthy addition of to group of many vaguely Portal like puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: What if there isn't just one simple solution? An impossible problem requires an impossible answer.One glance towards Sad Owl Studio's newest game Viewfinder elicits similar technical confusion and wonder compared to games like Antichamber, Superliminal, and The Witness. Its primary mechanic, reality distorting photographs that can be placed anywhere to create platforms and new environments, is a sight that never grows stale throughout the hours of puzzling the game has to offer. Much of the puzzle work here is extremely unique, tasking players with literally thinking outside of the box in order to power the teleporter out of each level. The game is divided into solitary stages, connected by a hub world. While the hubs don't provide much purpose, it was nice to not be just continuously shoved into the next level. While most of the game skews on the easier side, there are a few legitimately tricky puzzles that required a bit more trial-and-error to figure out. Some puzzles I felt leaned a little too much into "breaking" the level, but that also felt in the spirit of the game's design. Viewfinder has no problem introducing new mechanics right up until the very end, and I wish there was more time to spend with some of these ideas, mixing them with earlier ones, and posing more brutal challenges. By the end, there are a few headscratchers, but nothing that will stump you for very long. Viewfinder wants you to not only be thinking about its creative challenges, but also thinking about its spaces, its characters, and life outside of the game. Frequently, it poses very pressing questions about the state of our known reality, and there are several shocking moments that elevated the fun, peaceful gameplay into something that carries much more weight than it seems. This is the most successful I've ever seen a puzzle game implement a narrative that actually matches the genre's themes and ideas, and they only get stronger the further you get into the game.I really enjoyed my time with Viewfinder. The graphics and art design are simple, but pleasing, and SOS has no problem switching it up when you least expect it. The accompanying music has a lower-key ambient feel that stays out of your way, with a few more noticeable tracks entering in the hub world and key story moments. There are also fully voiced characters in phonographs and memories scattered across the levels, and none of this blew me away, but the writing was serviceable enough to keep me interested in hearing everything being said. The story was as surprising as the mechanics, and it only left me wanting more. If you are a fan of any similar titles in the FPS puzzle genre, you are going to need to check this out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game, I deeply enjoyed it and honestly it was a nice soft fun. The story is compelling and interesting, the emotional beats are well crafted, the companions aren't annoying and all in all it was a nice experience with plenty of easy "aha!" moments that make you feel like the smartest person alive.Do I recommend this game? Unfortunately, I just can't recommend it as a puzzler. At $32.85 AUD it is staggeringly overpriced for what you get, which is a game that's barely 3 hours long and fumbles the capacity to be truly brilliant as a puzzler. This reminds me more of a Naughty Dog game, where the actual gameplay is not challenging to better allow yourself to be immersed in the world and the story. That's totally fine for a linear story telling game, but when Viewfinder is tagged as a Puzzle game (and steam is comparing it to games such as ) you'd hope that the puzzles would be the forefront of the gameplay not the story. The puzzles (even the optional "challenge" puzzles) are easy. Really easy. Your biggest puzzle sometimes is trying to figure out where the exit teleport is so you can actually do the simple step to reach it. This is really such a shame, because this game had everything going for it to be a challenging perspective warping puzzler and I just don't think it delivered aside from one or two levels which introduced fresh and exciting concepts but never expanded properly upon them. I feel like this is half a game, that I just finished learning all the mechanics and I'm right about to start applying them and then the game is over.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game going into it. The systems and mechanics for the puzzles are excellent and offer a lot of promise. But it feels the game itself barely scratches the surface of that potential. So much of the gameplay involves little more than building bridges to reach areas, or navigating around obstructions, while the potential the systems offer allows for so much more. Each of the game's unique systems rarely, if ever, interact with each other, and it's always very telegraphed to the player when they're to be employed. I would have loved it if the developers had simply allowed themselves to explore the potential of what they'd created more, but instead what we're left with feels so very small and surface-level.

name: Please Fix The Road
detailed_description: Please Fix The Road is a colorful, minimalistic, laid-back and casual puzzle game in which it's probably not hard to guess... you're fixing roads! In each level you have a specific limited set of tools that will help you get all the cars, boats, trains or animals from their point A to point B. The mentioned animals include, of course, kittens, dogs and... pink llamas! You are able to manipulate multiple tiles at the same time. You can insert, destroy, rotate, copy, swap, raise, lower, push or move different segments of roads, rivers, paths or railroad tracks. The game combines elements of many other logic games into a nice minimalistic experience. Your road repair doesn't have to be beautiful, it just needs to get the job done! So please... Fix the road and have fun! Your mom will like this game too!

_childDocuments_.review: Please Fix The Road is a puzzle game where the player must complete roads, rivers and paths to allow cars, boats and animals to reach a flag. Each puzzle takes place on a landscape divided into a square grid, and you can destroy, insert, rotate, push, swap, and change the height of tiles.Unfortunately, while I’m a fan of many puzzle games, I didn’t really enjoy playing this one. If Steam’s review system had a neutral option, I would have selected that. This isn’t a terrible game, but I never really had fun, so it didn’t earn a positive rating. My main complaints are that the UI design is bad, and the puzzle design feels too restrictive.Some of the icons which indicate the different actions look very similar to each other, so its often unclear which specific actions are available to use on each puzzle. After a while I adopted a tactic of whenever I started a new puzzle I’d quickly use all the moves on random tiles, not trying to solve the puzzle, just so that I could clarify which actions I have to work with, then I’d reset and start again. I really think the game would benefit from having some words underneath each icon that say “push”, “swap”, etc, to make things more clear.I also found that on some puzzles, the camera angle makes judging tile elevation (high ground, slopes) more difficult than it should be.Each puzzle forces you to use the available actions in a specific order. For example on one puzzle you might have to destroy, then insert, then rotate. On the next puzzle you might have to rotate, then destroy, then insert. There’s no logical reason for this, its just an artificial limitation that is applied to each puzzle.If we could use the actions in any order, we might be able to solve the puzzles in a variety of creative ways, but being forced to use them in one specific order meant that I often felt like I had to solve puzzles in the least efficient way possible just because the developers decided that was the solution.This is especially true on some later puzzles where one or more actions seem to be provided as red herrings. The solution doesn’t require all the actions, but because you can’t skip the ones you don’t want to use, you’re still forced to use them on random grass tiles.I received a free copy of this game as a gift from my work colleagues.

_childDocuments_.review: , originally a flash game from 2014, is your average road-building jigsaw-like puzzler with above-average presentation. the goal is simple: create paths for all the cars (or whatever else, including animals) to reach their destination. little do they know they're only gonna explode when they arrive. it's fun and the . they do get old eventually and make level reset take a while as well, so a toggle for them would be appreciated. (10 were added after release) unlocked one by one for the most part, but some award an extra unlock that can be used to skip ahead a bit. levels provide . so instead of finding the next piece or step to continue the road, you have to figure out what to do with the current one. they're all visible on the bottom, size and orientation are indicated by white squares, available amount by blue dots.other tiles include bombs and a hand to get rid of stuff in the way, copy-paste, rotate, swap, slide and elevation modifiers. as good as they look,  and all the clutter is in the way of puzzling, but it can be reduced. and , especially without level rotation to assist in the matter. all the mechanics are introduced on the first 40-odd levels, then it's just iteration after iteration.the game  for everything except placing and rotating tiles (if applicable). rebinds are coming at some point and controller is also supported, didn't try it. the tutorial at the beginning quickly shows you the ropes. move the currently active puzzle piece with the mouse (or more awkwardly with the arrow keys), place with left click, right click puts it down if it can. , holding the mouse wheel or wasd pans the camera (as I said, no rotation here either). mouse wheel or +/- zooms, clicking mouse wheel or space toggles between full zoom in and out.  and an axis flip option wouldn't hurt either. if you get stuck, a few per level with a short cooldown after each. 'f' and 'h' replaced tab as a hotkey, it wasn't a good idea for to alt-tabbing and shift-tabbing reasons. also, , as they don't simply place the current piece where it should go (which would require checking if so far everything's shipshape), but . it also means they can only help with the first few steps and once a hint is used, the level can only be reset completely from level select, as it only goes back until the hint otherwise. not a big deal but needs some getting used to.excellent and varied presentation, . pretty good and similarly diverse soundtrack, though a skip track button would be nice, they're not all winners. settings cover the basics and are available while playing: separate volume sliders, windowed mode with resolution options, graphics detail and decoration density sliders, plus one for controller vibration. no on-screen level numbers yet, but the level select icon brings up a list that shows where you are, good enough. the list should be more condensed though, to 5 pages instead of 15.it's a well-known and oft-seen concept executed competently, providing a generous amount of content, functionality and quality of life, though it could use a bit more of the latter. I hate tile-sliding puzzles, so when that mechanic came on, I lost a considerable amount of interest, but it's still .

_childDocuments_.review: Lately I've been in the mood for very light and relaxing puzzle / builder games and I thought Please Fix The Road (PFTR) would be right up my alley. The very charming diorama's shown in screenshots, jazzy soundtrack that oozes class and initial 15 levels of the game hide a very tough, tricky puzzle game. PFTR is a game where you get 160 beautifully rendered diorama's, with a "something" (cow / car / ...) that needs to get to its destination. The roads to that destination are obviously broken and you need to fix it. Unfortunately, this is not like MineCraft where you can put blocks in any order you like. The player is given a certain amount of actions (pushing blocks, adding blocks, destroying blocks, reversing blocks, rotating blocks...) and you have no choice in what type of actions you can pick from a list. Furthermore, not only can you not choose your actions, you have to do the actions in the very specific order the developer intended. This last tidbit is where my mounting frustrations came from. The game becomes difficult in a hurry. At around puzzle #20 I needed to start using a hint, at puzzle 40 multiple hints, and at around puzzle 70 my confidence started to crumble as I needed to skip puzzles because I couldn't figure them out even with all hints turned on. Speaking of hints, this game does have a pretty helpful hint system, which will solve partial steps of the puzzle for you, both decreasing the amount of steps needed to be solved by you and allowing you to see more of the game. This is partially a complaint and partially a comment but I really don't like how little creativity is allowed for the puzzles. The developers seem to be annoyingly aware of how many ways their puzzles can be beaten because almost every idea I had ended up becoming invalid because it would take one action too many, or I was blocked by a flag or a car. The direct route or the most seemingly obvious move was never, ever the solution in this game. In most puzzles there is ZERO room for error or misplacement, and in a game where you have to calculate so far down the line where you're going to put certain blocks it mystifies me why there aren't other mechanics available where you can quickly swap out blocks to verify and experiment with loose ideas, without needing all the undoing and waiting for animations. So you have trial-and-error-based gameplay, with quite a bit of waiting around. Not the greatest combo.The difficulty is all over the place as well. Sometimes some puzzles are these nice relaxing brain teasers, others made me want to barf. One time I ran into a hilarious, hopefully unintentional mistake by the developer where puzzle 93 was switched around with puzzle 24. At other times I'm working with a team of theoretical physicists how to solve puzzle 68 but then you have puzzle 70 which I completed in less than 20 seconds. This happened so frequently that I'm internally debating if this was intentional or not. I understand that, when you've been developing the same game for years you assume that players will just pick up on certain teachings but that's unfortunately not how gamers' minds work - at least not in the span of a couple of hours. For some reason this game makes my computer think it's running Red Dead Redemption 2 for how hot it gets. I've had 4 hour sessions of Elden Ring where my PC wasn't running this hot, so I don't know what's happening under the hood.Aside from all this, it cannot be overstated the passion that has gone in this game. It's funky, sexy soundtrack especially reminds me of a mix between Greed Corp's and The Pedestrian's soundtrack. The graphics, ranging from the choice of colors to the tiny models to the variety of supercool level transitions all look perfect. I very much enjoy the option of turning off chromatic aberration. This is topped off with a very pleasing and very functional UI.I'm a bit bummed out I didn't enjoy this game more. Perhaps it requires a certain type of thinking that I'm just very bad at. I thought quite a while if I'd recommend this game or not. A neutral option is unfortunately still impossible. Yet after a while of debating I can say that this is one of those rare cases where I will recommend a game despite the complaints I have. - First of all - and most importantly - this is very much a puzzle game - and nothing else. The building elements are the puzzle mechanics and they aren't there for casual playfulness. The Steam tags are a little misleading in that sense.- PFTR is also priced appropriately. It's not suspiciously cheap nor insultingly expensive, which invites a broader audience to try out lesser known games. - The game was also being played by somebody who doesn't really like puzzle games all that much, and the game did hold my hand up to puzzle 115, which I think is proof of good design. Not "Valve-good" design but good design nonetheless.- Even when the game was being a frustrating nightmare at times, it's sheer charm and beautiful presentation kept me playing way past its refund period. Massive props for that. - The developer is also quite welcoming to pirates, and as somebody who had to choose between food and video games at one point, this is a huge plus. - The developer is active on the review section and isn't being a dirtbag when facing some criticism. We need more of this in the indie space.

_childDocuments_.review: Many modern puzzle games have begun to transcend their humble (and somewhat mundane) origins. The artistic endeavors and stylistic choices they contain now can often be as important as the puzzle gameplay itself. While the AAA industry has little to show in this genre, indie developers are regularly making puzzles much cooler than they have any right to be. While I still wouldn’t call myself a fan of the genre, I can’t help but try more of them out because of the wonderful designs they showcase, and Please Fix The Road does that as good as any I’ve played before.Abbreviated Review: There’s something about these strange little tilt-shifted, miniature-looking, diorama games that appeal to me. Please Fix The Road puts you in front of a platform of land floating in a void providing an almost god-like perspective on the puzzle. The goal, of course, is to fix the road and get whatever vehicle or creature is on one end to the opposite end to capture a little flag. There may be more than one road to be fixed and more than one entity that wants to travel upon it. Often, they’ll even intersect to complicate things more. However, the task is always the same. You use your abilities and problem-solving skills to repair a busted path to victory.These abilities start pretty straightforward – destroying plots of land and adding ones with functional roads. This simplicity doesn’t last for long. Soon you’ll have the power to pick plots of land up and spin them around, swap one selected area for another, or pick them up entirely and move them to another location. When combined with the rest of your magical earth-moving/creating powers, you end up with a pretty robust arsenal of options for solving puzzles. So many that, at times, I would forget which one of these actions the icon represents.You don’t get to use them at will though, each level presents a specific set of tools you have for that road repair endeavor and that’s all you have to use. You also have to use all of them in the order presented. That means there is basically only one resolution to a puzzle – the one the developer intended.Given the singular solution to these puzzles, or at least the one intended, reminds me of that scene in Avengers where Doctor Strange is looking into the future to find a path to victory. Every time you start a level, you have dozens of potential paths you can take with the tools you are given and virtually all of them accomplish nothing. Only when you start with the correct initial steps does it become clearer what is necessary to rebuild the road. Early in the game, it’s generally not too difficult to accomplish this, but as you progress, the challenge is always figuring out what the intention is from the start.To address this, each map has a hint feature that will give you, at the very least, the first move. Even if there were something like ten or more moves, once I was able to establish what the intention was for the puzzle, it became far easier to solve. However, after I was about 50 or 60 levels into the 160 available, I found that most of the puzzles I encountered had such convoluted starts that I couldn’t tell what needed to be done without a good bit of trial and error. This seems to be the intention for the game given how easy it is to reset as well as undo and redo your efforts, but it mostly resulted in using the hint system as a crutch – which took some of the fun out of it.For me, there’s a pretty delicate balance in puzzle game difficulty. I’m usually not too upset if the game is a little too easy, but still satisfying. Yet, when it’s too difficult, I quickly lose interest even if it appeals to me in other ways. Please Fix The Road has an exceptional visual design and some pleasant music that reminds me of Sim City (which is great). It also has a breadth of mechanics that allow for some intriguing puzzles that feel distinct even though they all essentially have the same goal. But it’s just not really for me.That doesn’t mean I can’t see the value in this game though. For people that have more patience than I do (that’s probably the majority) and those that want puzzle games that don’t hold back, this is an excellent choice. The game is extremely polished and the little bit of magic that comes from completing a level and seeing the cool animation is reminiscent of that little instance of joy you’d get when completing a game of Solitaire and seeing the cards bounce around. Despite my interest fading halfway through the game, I still think it’s worth recommending because it is well-made, reasonably priced, and good fun when you’re smart enough to solve these tough puzzles without leaning on the hints – which I can only hope one day I will be.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game at first but after 50-60 levels I realized I'm just mindlessly exhausting all available hints before even thinking what to do - and decided to accept that the game isn't for me.The game is done well, no arguing there. I do however have the same problem with it as with a ton of other puzzle games - they start fun, but then the "difficulty" ramps up by making the levels convoluted in a really bad way. Like here you get a fixed set of moves that you must do in a predefined order. Such a move could be destroying a weird tetris shape worth of blocks or rotating a patch of tiles together.Problem is, by stringing together multiple such weird moves you end up having literally millions of combinations of things to do with them. I don't understand what I'm supposed to do so I sort of randomly go through some options and learn nothing. It just feels to me like I'm supposed to mess around until the puzzle solves itself. For comparison, in Picross genre or Hexcell-like games you solve puzzles one bit at a time but here you need to grasp the entire level at once or you won't solve it at all. I don't like that.Additionally:- Level transition animations are great, too bad you end up skipping them anyway- Pretty graphics only hinder gameplay information- Hint system doesn't give you "hints", it just undoes all your moves and then shows the first correct move (even if that's exactly what you did)Anyway like I said it's a problem I have with many similar games. Like, here, have a set of moves you must do, now make them somehow fall into becoming the perfect solution and work out in the end. But how do I reach that solution? I can hardly make any deductions or split the puzzle into smaller chunks or anything? I don't know. I'm not good at this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: TyposI really hate to give this game a bad review because it’s so charming and beautiful. But at the end of the day it’s a puzzle game and a lot of the puzzles are poorly designed. For the first 25 levels or so the puzzles are painfully easy. A level will introduce a new mechanic and give you a pretty simple puzzle to learn it and then the next 5 levels will be basically the exact same concept without building on it at all. After this section you get to the sweet spot around the 20s-40s ish here there are some really great ones. When I was playing these I found the game the most fun. But at the end of the 40s and onwards the puzzles just skyrocketed in difficulty. While the sweet spot levels had elegance and clever tricks, solving these ones just felt like trying to solve a rubix cube. You don’t get the “Aha!” moment I think a good puzzle has. It almost seemed like the developer just started at the end, shuffled a bunch of tiles around, and called it a day; leaving you to figure out the highly specific 12 step process needed to find the solution. While there are hints which can help you out, a good game shouldn’t need you to use a hint on almost every level. I think what happened is the dev wanted to have enough content in the game to last more than 3 or 4 hours. And this came at the expense of quality. It's tough to design 160 good puzzles. It’s a real shame because the mechanic of this game offers so much and there are some truly creative and engaging puzzles in here and I’m sure there are more great ones in the 100 levels I haven’t played, but because there are so many puzzles that don’t offer the same I can’t give this a positive review. This game could be great if it was only 40 levels long.TLDR: There are some really great puzzles but most of them are either way too easy or way too hard. Look at the global achievement stats for this game before you decide to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to casual puzzler games, the genre has been mostly flooded with games that are hyper-minimalist abstracts that are highly repetitive and derivative. Please Fix The Road shows how far a little polish and life can go. The graphics are smooth and cute and there's a lot of nice little details to maps and animations. They get you up and running fast and you'll pretty naturally get right into interesting puzzles. I'm especially a fan of the game sort of luring you into some common types of traps early, encouraging you to get comfortable with experimenting and re-trying. It also has nice QoL things, like gamepad, mouse only and M+KB support, plus a simple set of options that nevertheless cover the important graphics quality and resolution options. While I'm not far in yet, I'm also encouraged by the 150 levels. Given how things are going, it feels like the right amount of levels to get your value and really see everything without the game letting the cult of replayability/"value is in playtime" drag on into mediocrity. Big fan so far, especially at the price point. If you like things like Dorf Romantik and other calm non-timed puzzlers, give it a look!
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: It looks good but after ~40 levels/minutes I don't find it entertaining. I feel like a toddler putting squares in square holes. The problem is the predefined order in which you put the level together which makes it simple and not fun. It might be that without the guidance the game does not work but then it needs some redesign.This game has a case of Dorf Romantik - looks great but the gameplay is too basic. I should have listened to the trailer where all the quotes revolve around how good the game looks and no word about how fun it is to play.The blurb also says my mom will like this game and that is not the case.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck.Complete masterpiece of a puzzle game. I spent hours on Independence Day listening to fireworks and playing Please Fix the Road and had a great time. This game has style, in its music, art, and puzzle design. The visual transitions between the stages are very enjoyable to watch, and the music is a jazzy mix that has an impressive number of tracks. Not to be outdone, the puzzles are the meat of any puzzle game and of the 160 roads being fixed the first third feel like beginner, the middle was challenging but still relaxing, and the end of the game ramped up to quite the struggle, with the last ten levels removing the hint assistance!! 10/10 puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: "Please Fix the Road" features cute isometric graphics and lovely transition animations between puzzle layouts. Despite its charming visuals, I found myself getting bored quickly as there wasn't much to keep me engaged. I wish I could love this game, but it ultimately fell short in maintaining my interest.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: not a bad game at any rate but a bit underwhelming.the solutions to the more advanced puzzles don't have the elegance I would like to see in a puzzle game. there's no symmetry or pattern emerging. sometimes you are given moves that don't seem necessary, unsure if they are meant as a red herring, for other solutions, or both.graphics are pretty but sometimes too busy and it makes terrain elevation quite hard to read which can throw a wrench in your plans.in the end the game is a small disappointment for me
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: The animations look nice and in theory, the concept for the puzzles looks great, but in reality, the weakest point of this game is the levels.Well, yeah, you are fixing the roads, but the result is usually that you have messed up the world - you start with a nice-looking plot and you end up with the screwed-up one. Sure, it doesn't have to be beautiful, it just needs to get the job done, but that's not satisfying. Maybe it should be in reverse, you start with a messed up plot and you need to get it back to normal, but maybe it's just my OCD :PThere are too many game mechanics too, it's difficult to remember all of them just by looking at the icons. There are also too many levels and not enough achievements. It felt like a grind and when the hints ended on the last levels, I felt helpless.Did I mention that the animations look nice? They do, but that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game way before the release date. The idea is great. Mechanics? Too. But god this game is so unreadable. I can't distinguish anything because it's so cluttered with unnecessary stuff. Height is also very hard to distinguish. All and all I'm struggling with the visuals even with lowest detail setting on. What suppose to be a perk that makes this game stand out from others, for me it's a huge blocker to fully expierience the game. That's why Tetris is so approachable game - its ascetics don't interfere with a game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle game about making paths for cars, boats and even llamas.Pros:+ Challenging puzzles and satisfying controls+ 150 levels - a huge amount of content for the price+ Transitions between levels are mesmerisingCons:- It's insulting that the game wants me to use hints for taking too long. Stop it game, I'll work it out eventually!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Please Fix The Road is a head-scratcher, but never so hard that you can't work it out. It takes conventional tile-placement mechanics and constantly turns them on their head, making for constant surprises, an fresh novelty in each level. This is a game that will be hard to put down and suck you in for hours.The game has already received an update since, but please check out my Let's Try video for gameplay:
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to write a negative review, but PFTR has issues.The good:- the game is very prettythe bad:- the pretty graphics make it hard to distinguish tiles- there is little variation in the puzzles- the iconography is unclear, what action, what shape, etc., are easy to confuse- the result of any action is a little opaque, you have to take an action and undo to see the result- the difficulty is all over the place
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Tiles have to be manipulated or destroyed in a predetermined pattern and in a fixed order dictated by the level. There is an undo button. Patterns are designed to throw the player off, as they often only have to be used partially, greatly increasing the challenge. Imagine a square tetris shape of four bombs which is only meant to be used to remove two tiles of the level instead of four.About a third of the way through I started using all the available hints as it became devilishly difficult to "see" the solution in the tiles making up the level. Hints are available up until the final ten levels - the achievement for 100% completion requires solving them without hints, so I stopped there, bowing out in shame trying to salvage what little honour was left by stoically refusing to copy solutions from a video guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Ticks all the boxes for a polished indie puzzle game in 2022. There are many  moments to be had with over 150 well-designed puzzles. A lot of care went into the controls and interfaces; it never feels clunky and when you start the game up again you're right where you left off. And an awesome, varied selection of songs to go with it.Most importantly, it respects your time with a clever hint system that helps you get  far enough into that tricky puzzle where you can then figure it out on your own.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Great casual puzzle game. The puzzles are just right in difficulty for me. Not too challenging, and not too boring. If you get stuck, you can use the hint button and it will do one step for you to nudge you in the right direction. I like the visuals of the game- looks clean, cute, and aesthetically pleasing. My only gripe would be that it's a bit difficult to tell the difference in elevation sometimes, but you can zoom in to make it a bit clearer, so it's not so bad. The music is chill and nice too.Update: The levels do get more challenging around lvl ~75
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Please Play This GameSuper polished, charming, and easy to play. The puzzles can be challenging but since there are only a few possible moves at any turn you can brute force solve them if you get stuck. This is great because you never really feel overwhelmed by a single puzzle. New mechanics are introduced every couple puzzles so there's a lot of variety.Guessing 15-20 hours of gameplay based on me being about 35% done at 7 hours played.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Gets brutal after 30.  It has a very nice ramp up where it introduces each of the different puzzle mechanics and gives hints on the kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the designer is going to do to you.  It gets to a point where you just have to put down your controller and come back in a day because it has a habit of locking your brain.   There is a reason why your not penalized using hints.Seriously, the presentation is excellent, moment is smooth.  Using either the controller or the mouse makes no difference in the handling of this game.  Its worth 10 bucks if you want to torture yourself with a good set of puzzles.Now I want to see them make a sequel to Nes' Lolo: Hellscape.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Does not work well with steam deck. Certain controls seem to not work right, like literally not being able to place certain tiles, and the somewhat strict method of choosing what tile to place is not great. Can't say much more than that at this point.I hope this is fixed at some point as I'd like to try this cute-looking puzzler again, but for now I am going to refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: I might be bad at puzzles but this game is good! To start the visuals are delicious, I love the level transitions. The puzzles are tricky as well. You must plan ahead and see the solution, can't brute force your way through the bigger levels. Also, it has a lot more tools than I was expecting. It's not just placing blocks but blowing them up, copying them, moving them, rotating them, and plenty more.Full thoughts,
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Overall seems like it'd be a decent game but it's difficulty to really see anything because the game is overly bright and the colors over-saturated. UI is entirely graphical with no tool-tips either which is a pretty big no-no imo. I enjoy what I've played game-play wise, but it's hard for me to even play it for more than 5-10m settings because it hurts the eyes and gets frustrating trying to solve the puzzle on a level you can't see well.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Hate to say this but I had to issue a refund. The graphics are charming and atmosphere is relaxing but the "difficult" -tag doesn't describe how much of a mess the gameplay feels like. I personally struggled greatly to visualize how the upcoming moves should've been used.My head is straight up incompatible with this one...
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle game with plenty of levels, so it's well worth the price. The hint system is great -- you aren't punished in any way for taking a hint, so if you really get stuck, just use one. You could easily look up a guide if you wanted to, so there's no point in tracking hints anyway. Note that there are no hints for the last few puzzles, so you're probably going to use a guide eventually, but until then you can play with minimal stress. Enjoy the ride!
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning game. But I don't think the developer really know how to make the game .Like, why take away the control in the middle of a very first level just to introduce the undo-redo-reset buttons? This everywhere to be seen UI/UX should be the humanity common knowledge by now! Also, by take away the control and force players to push that buttons instead of just completing the level, it make players doubt themselves if they did something wrong. Very bad first impression.And the puzzle part is ... somehow missed the sweet spot. Players are given a list of tiles to place on the board. However, those tiles must be placed in the given order. That's fine. But why lock the subsequent tiles so players can't select them to overlay on the board and get the puzzle overview at all? By unable to visualize the board clearly (this game treat tiles with different height differently), sooner or later players will place a lot of tiles, just to find out that the final tile (that they can only plan where to place in their head) is wrong and has to reset the level. This is annoying rather than fun.Apart from the graphic, I'm not enjoying this.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. It's enjoyable and relaxing. I like that some of the levels are solvable in more than one way, and the progression system is steady and interesting.The only downside to this game is the soundtrack, which is terrible, but it's quite easy to play your own music in the background, so this doesn't really affect gameplay at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like it could be a nice casual game, but it doesn't work for me.  (Ubuntu 22.04 linux,  Nvidia Gforce 710 with 1 GB, AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6 core with 16 GB RAM. Should be adequate for casual gaming)  Takes like two minutes to get through the opening credits, and then I can scroll but nothing else works.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to really like this game, but it has no controller support or steam deck support and even mouse/keyboard controls are a little out there. It was really hard to like this game when it kept not letting me play or even control the game correctly- then if you take too long it; it pities you and does the puzzle for you which was really frustrating. :"") I still think the graphics are really pleasing and the game itself looks nice, but the controls were so frustrating that I am returning it.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, Fun, ChallengingThe learning process of the mechanics are gradual and intuitive. The game doesn't tell you how a mechanic works by instructing the player to do a certain move using a pop-up. Instead, they'd made it so to progress through a level you'd have to use the mechanic to solve it, which I admire in a gameThe later parts of the puzzles involves thinking outside of the box and a lot of foresight which is fun if you love problems like chess puzzles but might be frustrating to some people especially when the solution involves some obscure move that is vital to the success of the processI'd recommend if you would play this to try to avoid using any hints before actually trying the level as it might hinder your performance in later levels. Do note that the final 10 levels disables hints so you're on your own for those ones (I mean, you can just watch a walkthrough but then it defeats the point of playing a puzzle game right?)Finally, Thank you for Sleepy for gifting this game it is fun <3
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Concept looks interesting at first, but becomes monotonous pretty fast. Adding to this cars that get ejected from the board and explode, surely for the "crazy" factor but for a peaceful game appears quite weird moreover for a game where we have to fix things, it makes the whole thing not appealing to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute, simple puzzle game. Some of the puzzles are very satisfying to solve, but it is very hit or miss with each puzzle because it feels like there is exactly one solution, and you either see it or you dont. Then you press hint until you see it. There isn't much you can do to work it out or even to tell if you are on the wrong track.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Not really what I was expecting. You must perform specific actions in the exact order, there is no flexibility. Your only choice is where on the map. Many of the actions take you away from what you need to do to make the solution longer, so you must subvert them. It is like Tetris, where you have no control over the next shape, but you must form an exact layout at the end and it only goes together in one way. You essentially have to replay the steps the author took, but in reverse. At least you didn't have to race the clock. I didn't find it very enjoyable or relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended – 7/10This is a pretty nice, casual feeling, puzzle game.  Each puzzle is a cute little space in the city, country, etc…that has you modifying the road layout to get one or more things from point A to point B.  To do this, you are given a fixed set of moves.  You must then use these moves in an exact order to complete the puzzle.  As you progress, you are introduced to newer moves and longer move chains.  This increases the difficulty as it allows for more complex move combinations and requires more planning.I will say that as I got towards the final quarter of the game, each level started feeling more like trying to solve a Rubik’s cube and not something I could just casually sit down and solve.  Maybe others will see things differently.  The other issue I had was that some of the move pictures looked very similar and I would constantly mistake what each move could do or how it behaved.  This became more irritating as the number of moves increased or the solution required more abstract thinking.Overall, the game is good for what it is and I’d recommend it to anyone who likes puzzle manipulation games.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game good? Yes. Is it an amazing, unique, and mind-blowing experience? No. Basically what you see in the trailer is exactly what you get: manipulate tiles to get cars from Point A to Point B. Easy to pick up, gives good vibes with a nice jazz soundtrack, and an overall chill game. If you're willing to spend the asking price for a casual puzzle game that'll keep you busy for a few hours, go ahead and get this.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: For the price there is a lot of content. The puzzles are hard, cool mechanics, and the levels are beautiful. Around level 100 I felt all done with the game. I was struggling to get through them without using all tips and I just wanted to be done with the game. Sometimes the tile snapping, especially when rotating pieces, feels really clunky. 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: As a fellow unity dev this game is both inspiring and just beautiful to look at. It does so much with so little. It's a very simple puzzle game, but it presents everything with so much style. I particularly love how the lighting changes between levels so that things are constantly being switched up, and you never get your retinas burnt in from looking at the same bright background for hours.The developer is also a sweetheart from all the online interactions I've seen, they are far too nice XDBuy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very chill games that exudes serotonin upon level completion. I am about 40% of the way through and can say that it's definitely earned it's $5 from me.The devs are super responsive to feedback to the point where they are using YouTubers as testers and adjusting difficulty curves based on the footage. Level 17 was very complex early in the game. By far the hardest level I have seen in the game so far but they have since updated it to make it fit better within the curve. You can follow my play through of the game [ ] HERE! [/url]
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game with great graphics and interesting gameplay.The thing that could (by some people) be viewed as negative is a lack of "break" between levels - there is a immediate jump to next level after finishing one. It may be overwhelming and lead to a feeling of "it is too much of the same".Also I think on some levels it is not immediately clear what are the heights of particular blocks, but with the undo/redo feature it is not a much of an issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics and level transitions. Pretty much all of the puzzles have very satisfying solutions but it is not easy by any means.Perhaps worse performance than I would expect... It runs smoothly on my relatively powerful gaming laptop but it causes substantial spikes in CPU temp. This game may not be for you if your CPU can't handle the load.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous presentation, I love the smooth transitions between levels. The puzzles have also been pretty good so far.I'm having trouble with level 38 and I think the hints might be broken for this specific level, using them all seems to put me in a position that makes it impossible to finish (or maybe I'm just dumb).
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

_childDocuments_.review:
Please Fix The Road is a colorful, minimalistic, laid-back and casual puzzle game in which it's probably not hard to guess... you're fixing roads!

In each level you have a specific limited set of tools that will help you get all the cars, boats, trains or animals from their point A to point B. The mentioned animals include, of course, kittens, dogs and... pink llamas!

You can insert, destroy, rotate, copy, swap, raise, lower, push or move different segments of roads, rivers, paths or railroad tracks. The game combines elements of many other logic games into a nice minimalistic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Please Fix The Road

name: Jet Kave Adventure
detailed_description: FEATURES Master the jet-fueled platforming It won’t be easy with your clumsy caveman’s movements but try and do your best! Jetpack through 36 colorful levels Roam the amazing side-scrolling landscapes riddled with hazards and rich with secrets. Smack and whack 30 types of enemies Fight a variety of prehistoric beasts and bosses using your trusty bone club. Experience breakneck flight sequences and boss fights Soar across pitfalls, smash through rocky walls, and defeat the most terrific enemies using your continuously improving skills. Challenge yourself in ARCADE MODE Try the exciting arcade-like experience, where you have a limited number of lives, and getting to the checkpoint no longer replenishes your health. Plus, extra lives can be bought only between levels so if you lose them all, it means a good ol’ Game Over. It’s tough but fair. Reach the top of the leaderboard Take part in Time, Collectible, and No Damage Challenges, and compete against other players to get the best possible high score in online rankings. Find collectibles and upgrade your gear Return to the time when seashells were the only currency and collect as many of them to enhance your strength. Enjoy the unusual Stone-Fiction setting Whether you're ready for it or not, the fate of your island now depends on you. So put on your jet-fueled device and start your adventure in a world where the Stone Age and science fiction collide. Collect various achievements Some of them may seem odd, but they are all fun! SUMMARY: Jet Kave Adventure is a completely historically inaccurate yet highly entertaining 2.5D adventure platformer. Thaw out your inner caveman and join the skill-based action! Your name is Kave, and you’re the chief of your tribe – or rather you were until now. Banished by your own people you stumble upon… a jetpack! The device turns you into the only caveman who stands a chance against “the alien invader” – a rather unlikable guy from the sky who’ll readily kick off a disastrous volcanic eruption just so he can repair his spaceship. Begin your quest to save the whole island and prove your worth to the tribe!

short_description: Jetpack through the prehistoric world in this Stone-Fiction adventure platformer. Enjoy challenging boss fights, flying over pitfalls, smashing through walls, knocking out enemies, and manipulating objects as you halt the alien threat once and for all.

_childDocuments_.review: consists of four worlds, each with nine levels (36 in total); introduced throughout are a variety of platforming mechanics, a total of 30 types of enemies, different challenges and gameplay styles as well as a selection of boss fights. This all works together to provide a gradual (but very noticeable) increase in complexity and difficulty, making the game progressively more challenging and ultimately satisfying.Jet Kave is an exciting and varied game, mixing genres and gameplay to help the game continue to feel fresh despite the undeniably repetitive nature of platformers in general. Whilst it remains challenging throughout, it lends itself to a more casual style of play whilst also providing a range of ways for players to challenge themselves and add difficulty if desired. A single playthrough is relatively short but replayability (and additional value) is provided in a number of ways, especially for the more skilled and competitive of players.In conclusion, Jet Kave doesn’t do anything particularly original or reinvent (invent?) the wheel but it is a well made 2.5D platformer, with smooth controls and varied gameplay that I’d happily recommend to fans of this genre!My full detailed review of jet Kave, where I discuss, gameplay, mechanics, narrative and styling, is available at .

_childDocuments_.review: My first review (in 450+ games owned), I have decided to give this game a thumbs up to give the developers their due (seeing as it is so overlooked). It is a well crafted and thought out game with a few flaws, but clearly a lot of soul and effort has gone into the game. A few fixes may make the perfect sequel, or who knows possibly they can update the game to achieve this within this game. This game is a fun 2.5D platformer that the PC community can benefit from. There are not a ton in that category that compare to the DKC games, and as a huge fan of those, I would wholly recommend this to everyone, so long as they are not looking for a challenge comparable to DKC Tropical Freeze or the like. It is a more chill game that is a wonderful time to play and not stress on that level. The level design isn't perfect, and occasionally there are frustrating moments where the pathfinding is unclear, but otherwise this is a nice game to play for those who enjoy 2D platformers with a sense of progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice platform game. I like the theme and surroundings, it is nice to watch, to move, etc. But, the game is sometimes more difficult, especially with bosses :D And frustrating in some moments, when you have to jump, jump and jump again, up. These 2 things are the only disagvantages, but game - as a whole - is perfect, funny, relaxing. I like it! And for that price, "do not take it", don´t you :D

_childDocuments_.review: My initial impressions of the game were extremely good. Felt like a combination between rayman, crash, and donkey kong country. It wasn't perfect but overall it seemed very good and visually was pretty great.And then I continued to play.......After about the 3rd or 4th stage the flaws started to show until I finally just quit around the 9th level.-The movement while relatively smooth, and offering a lot of options, just feels a bit sloppy.-The cooldown on the boost ability is way too low and it just feels goofy to be able to dash costantly and negates most other movement options when going for speedrun times.-The glider and vertical jetpack sections were horendously bad, as noted by a couple other negative reviews.-Level design is highly repetitive and they start to feel like copy pastes very quickly-Combat feels weightless and enemy design is overall pretty bland. The first boss fight is laughably bad......and you get the point, overall just not very good. Its far from the worst platformer, but with so many great platformers on steam, your money and time would be better spent elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Kave Adventure

_childDocuments_.review: A simple and well-made 2D/3D platformer that excels in what it is trying to do - just be a platformer. As Kave, you jump and run through 36 levels, all with their optional challenges and things to find. The game controls well and the gameplay itself is fluid. You also have a futuristic jetpack with hover and boost abilities.A few weaknesses hold this game back from being truly great, though. One weakness is that the game's controls, while reliable enough, have problems with collapsing platforms. You have to jump from the very edge, else the jump will either not be executed or you only make a slight hop, which can kill you even with the jetpack if you're not careful - this was clearly an oversight, but it happens often enough to be frustrating and worth mentioning. Some levels also have a kite section that, frankly, controls terribly. The optional challenges are also annoying - while it is easy enough to complete all 3 in the first few levels (finish in a certain time, find all seeds in a level, do not take damage), it gets very frustrating in later levels when damage comes from all directions and the few control issues come up more often. All that considered, though, if you are looking for a simple and straightforward platformer, Jet Kave Adventure can definitely hold your attention and should get more recognition than it currently has.

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing this game featured on FanTheDeck and looking at its wonderful DKC inspired visuals, I had high hopes for this one. Unfortunately, poor controls and repetitive gameplay lead to an experience that I cannot recommend to anyone even on sale.Visually, the game is very impressive with detailed 2D/3D environments and nice lighting effects which are appreciated more and more as you play. The prehistoric themes mixed with alien technologies creates for stages that tend to only be eclipsed by larger studios/publishers on the surface. Story-wise, the game is a bit of a mishmash of ideas but with the lighthearted presentation it's totally fine. Most 2D platformers aren't really known for their story elements anyway and some cutscenes are cute and well animated. Audio-wise it's fairly standard with a soundtrack that fits the themes and in-game effects that are tastefully done. But gameplay reigns supreme here, and this is where it kind of falls apart...This is for the most part a basic 2D platforming experience. There are some obvious Donkey Kong Country influences in the level design with some collectibles littered throughout. However, collecting doesn't hold the same weight here and there aren't any real alternate paths or secret side levels to speak of here. Don't expect something like Kaze and the Wild Masks, Yooka Laylee and the Impossible Lair, or Marsupilami Hoobadventure here, it's more standard 2D platformer than heavily inspired DKC-esque platformer outside of visuals. You start out with a club to attack and soon gain a jetpack which is a nice addition. Collectibles can be used to upgrade the jetpack, club, health, and more incrementally and that helps a bit, but there's one big issue with gameplay. As mentioned before, this is a 2D platformer. What aspect needs to be nailed in this regard -- jumping. Sadly, this is a dealbreaker with Jet Kave Adventure.Jumping has a peculiar weightiness to it and what's even worse is it is fundamentally broken. On falling platforms (of which there are many), your jump will almost certainly fail to execute, in spite of pressing the correct button to do so. Whether this is an issue with momentum or colliders or something else, it's broken to the point that it simply isn't fun to play. Imagine playing a platformer that intentionally misfires jumps at random. Unless it was a meme, you likely wouldn't play that game anymore. Well, that's what it's like playing Jet Kave Adventure, particularly when you do not have your Jetpack.It's unfortunate because without this dealbreaker, I could say it would be a decent one to try. But I can't and unless that is fixed which is unlikely given the game was released over 2 years ago, it's a game that I simply cannot recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Putting a jetpack on a caveman's back certainly sounds like a good setup for a lighthearted platforming action game - and Jet Kave Adventure takes this ball right from the start and runs with it. With beautifully crafted backgrounds, lame-ish animations which however fit the caveman theme very well, and a surprisingly fluid gameplay, the game starts very strongly, and as our hero Kave gets most of the abilities in the first few levels, there's a lot of fun to be had from dashing through the levels by chaining moves together. After the first 5 levels or so, the game looks brilliant. Then stagnation sets in, because in the remaining 31 levels, there are new enemies and new environments, but hardly anything new gameplay-wise, and there are also no creative challenges to make you try and use your abilities in different manners. There are upgrades - all of them go for quantity (longer club reach, more jetpack fuel, more lives, etc.), and nothing whatsoever to change the gameplay.Oh, I beg your pardon, there ARE some new things: there are chase sequences, which are woefully bad, there are the inevitable boss fights, which are horrible, and there are some flying minigames, which are downright atrocious. The horizontal kite sequences are the worst, it doesn't really take too long to get through them, but that time gives the player an ample insight into how horrible it can be at times to be a caveman...To be honest, this duality confuses me. The base gameplay mechanics look like that they are created by people who understand platforming very well, while the minigames / boss fights / chases look like a hurriedly added afterthought by a producer who understands numbers, not players. All in all, the 6 hours I spent with the game were mostly fun, so I can recommend it, but be warned - at the most unexpected moments, you'll run into segments you won't enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty ok pure platformer.Very nice visuals and music.Works with checkpoints that are correctly placed.Unlimited retries that does not oblige to come back to the main menu.Funny creatures to deal with, it even improves the more you progress.Typically, the 3- levels are nicer than the previous.What is missing is variety. You find an alien jet pack at the beginning and that is pretty much it. For some inconsistent reasons, you will be able to upgrade it a bit at a shop but nothing new to find on your way beside shells to be used for money. She takes sea shell at the sea shop... Short cinematic are slow and not very funny or even interesting. The universe is supposed to be funny and while some creatures are, that is pretty much it. Your character never is. This character won't become a mascot or something like other in the same genre became (Mario, Crash, Sony, Rayman... to name a few). He will be forgotten once the game finished.Gameplay and mechanics will be pretty similar from the beginning till the end. The game does not invent anything.Some levels flying vertically or horizontally also proves it. A bit boring since it is that not inventive. More mechanics and animations would have typically been more appreciated in these parts. Bottom line, more average that something else but also good visually.Between the demo and the 90% of like today, no reason to not give it a try for who appreciate the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably one of the best I've ever played. It joins together modern graphics and old-school platforming. Gameplay is extremely fun, with interesting mechanics. Enemies are original and well designed, atmosphere and ambience are awesome, and boss fights are challenging but not frustrating. The overall difficulty is well balanced, to the point that I would recommend this game to kids who are approaching platformers for the first time. Jet Cave Adventure is almost perfect from every possible point of view, so don't miss the opportunity to play this absolute masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review:
Jet Kave Adventure brings everything you love about 2.5D platformers. Enjoy the skill-based action, challenging boss fights, clever secrets and thrilling set-pieces in a game where the Stone Age and science fiction collide.

Meet Kave, the jet-powered caveman. A has-been chief banished by his own tribe, he stumbles upon… a jetpack! The device turns him into the only prehistoric man who stands a chance against “the alien invader” – a rather unlikable guy from the sky who’ll readily kick off a disastrous volcanic eruption just so he can repair his spaceship. So begins Kave’s quest to save the whole island and prove his worth to the tribe.

_childDocuments_.review: The last fighting game I was into was smash bros melee, so it was a bit of a stretch for me to shill out $60 for this.  However, it's super fun!  I practiced one character on arcade for a while and then started playing in online matches which are a blast (and much more approachable than I was expecting).Similar to smash bros, every character has a basic kick and punch and then a special set of slashes (GG spreads them out over 4 buttons rather than 2).  There is a grab to break shields (like smash) and burst move to break combos.  Aside from that there are ~4 special moves per character and an ult.Once you know this its pretty easy to learn one character well and start recognizing the ~5-7 cool moves other characters can do.I would say as a guy who is basically new  to fighting games; its fun, approachable, pretty self aware (one characters ult is where he slams a wheelchair into you shin) and kicks ass.  I would rec!  probably 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I keep on switching between Xrd and Strive. It's really tough because they both have different mechanics. All I can say is I keep on going back to Xrd just because the gameplay is simply much deeper and exciting. Strive's motive to slow down the gameplay by gutting the combo expression is to appeal to casuals. It's not like Xrd or previous entries were really that difficult to pull off chains. Graphics and sound is great, just the fighting can easily become stale and repetitive for my taste. This might sound like a stretch, but the rhythm reminds me of a faster/stylish Samurai Showdown. The reason is because Strive implements a calculative fighting approach, and if you land a hit you can deal lots of damage. Counter-hits seem like a big deal, as it opens you up to chain combos, while corners can be devastating; this means that hard reads and positioning are important. This is practically a SamSho-style way of fighting in a Guilty Gear skin,Despite my gripes, I would still recommend to check out, especially if you're new to fighting games. It's a beautifully made game and learning characters are easy to pick up. It's a keeper for me to support the devs. Maybe it'll grow on me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit late, but I hope this review can be helpful to someone even though it took me so long to finally write it, in spite of buying the game on release. As a long time fan of Guilty Gear, I never wanted to write something like this, but at this point it's become clear that my grievances are not merely originating from that of growing paints of a series moving on to its new iteration.I've always considered GG my game. Some people have Tekken, many have KOF, others have SF, but GG was mine. I never took to the others in the same way. I never spent hours in training mode, I never spent hours playing on Netplay. I'd learn them on a basic level and play at locals, but when it came to playing a game I wanted to play, it was always GG. I went out of my way to learn, study and stress the systems and mechanics, some which weren't even readily available on dustloop. It's what I loved about fighting games, and what I loved about GG.Every character was unique, and even if I thought I might have perfected a character for a time (which was never actually the case), there was always a new one to go to and dissect. I lived for this, I loved discovering new things and improving. Hearing someone say, 'How the F*** did you do that?" or "That's the first time I've ever seen X" always provided a dose of dopamine that kept me going. The appeal of fighting games for me was learning and mastering systems, and implementing them in the context of mind games in a 1v1 match.I won't say Strive doesn't have this, but it's greatly diminished. Things feel homogenized to a detrimental degree and the sheer variety in the characters feels like it's taken a nosedive from AC/Xrd to Strive in a similar way it had from SFIV to SFV. I don't have the drive anymore. The drive to experiment, the drive to improve. I don't feel like Strive provides me enough interesting avenues to progress in my play to drive me forward.I am by no means the best player, I am not even claiming to be a good player. What I am claiming to be is a player who wanted the room to experiment, learn and improve, which Strive does not appear to offer me. The sheer variety of options AC/Xrd offered you are not to be found here, and the move away from frequent Okizeme to neutral marks a deep, tonal shift away from classic GG which I can't reconcile. I don't want to get into the weeds of mechanics and deviations, since it's all largely preference, but as a GG player for many, many years, I can't seem to meet the game half-way to enjoy it.  I've really tried, and I'll continue to try, but as every character releases and I hope one vibes with me (after being alienated by my prior 3 main characters (Sol/I-No/Baiken), I've come to realize that no character is going to magically reconcile the issues I have with the game.Will some like it? Probably. It's a competent game. But it's not GG. It's not my game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great online netcode. Almost feels like I'm playing offline. Great mechanics as well, Roman Cancel is a joy to use and the supers feel great to land. Loving this game, pick it up if you want to support a company who embraces great netcode... unlike some companies.Update: The game's balance feels like the devs don't know they want their own game to play. Characters are constantly changing to the point their kits, while the same, function entirely different, albeit some characters are getting new moves as well. The new mechanics feel like they didn't add too much depth to the game. Wild Assault feels more like a bandaid fix to a bigger problem, which is character conversions in neutral or even just to be combo filler. Some characters do not even need to use wild assault in their combos, which is nice, as I do not like the mechanic anyways, but kinda leaves the mechanic feeling hollow in their kits. Burst was changed as well, now being full screen, which seems kind of egregious and an obvious attempt at nerfing a specific character, but it's also a change that affects the whole cast in one way or another. Overall, I don't recommend this game. I'd recommend Granblue Rising or even an older GG. I do like the game, but it's been hard, as the direction the devs have headed is sort of bland at times and they seem confused as to their idea. I'd recommend the devs take a step back from the game, re-examine it, and find the exact way they wish the game and its characters to play. If I gave it a rating, I'd have to give it a 5 or 6/10.

Is it still worth buying? Yes because once you finally get into a good lobby, you will be treated to an amazing fighting game and great introduction into the genre.
