_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay has a nice game mechanic that restricts how much you can zoom out. The developers got the max zoom out camera distance spot on as I was always spinning my mouse wheel thinking, if only I could see a little further... Thankfully there are skills your mountaineer can acquire or start with that lets you see further for a limited period of time to get a better idea of paths to take.Regarding the price of Insurmountable, don't ask yourself if it's worth the asking price on steam. For Indie developers, I prefer to use the following method. Evaluate if you'd like to see more games for this developer and pay the price of the game so you can support their next game development.With my first impressions (and a glace at the steam achievements), I'm hooked. I want to try Mountain 1 again to get a better result so the next two climbs will be injury free. Replay value is no problem as the steam achievements set a goal to climbing all three mountains with each of the adventurers - something that is likely to require multiple attempts... for each mountain... for each adventurer skill set... with each random event encounters.My first impressions:Diving right in with minimal instructions, I chose to start as the Adventurer and stumbled my way up Mountain 1 (of 3 currently).  I picked whatever event happened to be on my way. I surprised myself when I summited the first mountain after using that last oxygen tank that I'd picked up in an earlier event. My initial thought at that point was, 'huh, that wasn't too hard'... and then reality set it as the game advised, 'congrats - now make it down to the safe point over.... there.' With the summit at 7200m-ish, I was still well into the 'death zone'. Movement above 6000m uses up the oxygen resource as time passes, this also includes when sleeping when trying to recover energy.This is when I learnt that juggling the oxygen / energy resources was a bit harder that I was expecting, especially now that I had to factor in keeping some in reserve for the decent.My character ending up collapsing from lack of oxygen about 500m above the death zone. I've added yet another body to add to those that seem to litter these dangerous mountains.For my second attempt (same play session), I chose the Scientist. This time I'm armed with the knowledge of needing to keep a careful watch on my resources and ensure there is reserve for the decent. I lucked into having the warm nights random event for this climb which meant I won't be losing body heat as much if I slept out in the open without a tent or in a cave.With some careful route selection, I managed to summit and climb back down out of the death zone just as my oxygen was running out. Energy and body temp resources were now quite low, and my exit point was tantalisingly in sight. My currently selected route showed that my energy would be empty for a most of the time walking to the exit and I'd need a ridiculous amount of luck to make it.To reduce that risk, I had a short sleep out in the open to recover some energy, but this let me with my body temp with only a sliver left. Clicking on the exit tile showed I'd be crossing some dangerous terrain and would be on zero energy a few tiles before the exit. I confirmed the action and watched it all play out. A few rock slides, a cougar and a twisted ankle had me on the edge of my seat as I read the various results. Then my little mountaineer crossed into the green exit zone and I was advised I gambled on my life and won!However, the injury meant my future expedition attempts on mountains 2 & 3 for this character were compromised. Specifically because I now have a 15% increased movement penalty due to that twisted ankle I suffered on the decent. Hmmm, I should probably try that again.. uh-oh, I'm hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: The game is all right. I had fun going up the mountain once. I didn't like that after I died and started a new game there wasn't any sort of progression feature to make my next journey different or less difficult. No added gear. No bonus stats. No customization. Nothing. You start from scratch each and every time simply choosing from one of the three locked in "classes". I just thought to myself, "Every trip is going be like this?" In a rogue like game you really need some way to tip the scales in your favor in order to keep a feeling of progression going. This game doesn't have that and I imagine repeated plays that end in permanent death will likely quickly start feeling hopeless for most people.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very decent, but it requires more work.Edit: Be careful with this purchase because the biggest flaw in this game comes out past 2h mark.I started the game Normal mode and made it up all three peaks first try. Hard mode unlocked so I continued with the same character and died 23 times in a row. (the difficulty gap between normal and hard needs to be reworked a bit)The difficulty skyrocketed by multiple factors. All your base stats suffer more (ex -0.5/h oxygen normal and -1/h oxygen hard). Random events tend to have more bad outcomes when you click the same choices. You need to manage additional bar - sanity. Normal mode I managed it too, but it suffered the least of all stats and I made it up all three mountains hardly ever buffing it. On Hard you suddenly need to worry about 4 instead of 3 factors and sanity is imbalanced both how it constantly slides down and how hard it hits when its down. You only have 25 health total and one sanity event took out as much as 7.9 health. You simply don't gain enough experience to choose enough perks to counteract all the loses and you hardly have enough time to search the base of the mountain for oxygen before you start going bonkers unless you buff sanity, but then you'll freeze your arse off or suffocate because you've ignored other perks. Big problem -> This game needs to help me out here as it has the fatal tendency to wipe all your progress when your character dies and you restart Hard mode every time with zero equipment at the bottom of the first mountain - I made it up the second mountain peak a few times and died on the way down, but I always restart at the foot of the first mountain. Your character needs to learn a bit every several attempts in a row when you die. For example, start with perks, or if other players wish to be hardcore give a choice whether to select starting perks or not, increase the number of perks per number of deaths. This isn't fun to be dead all the time and not having made any progress. After Hard mode, there is even harder Expert mode and I seriously don't want to know how that goes because I'm betting all the events will be out to punish you so there won't be a point of exploring.I'm going to select a different character, go through Normal mode and try my luck with the Hard mode again, but I hope the game balance gets readjusted and new features added.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to boil this game down to its basic elements, it would be a game of Preparation, Decision making, and RNG.You'll prepare yourselves with finding gear along your trek in the mountains, gain skill points to help improve your ability to survive and traverse the mountains, there are also temporary perks that can either last a few game hours or for the mission from experience gained from events that occur during your journey upwards.You'll have to decide on how to spend your limited resources and balance their usage to keep them from being depleted. Your health, stamina, body temperature, even willpower. As you get higher, you'll have to manage your oxygen as well. Time is also an important resource that needs close management. Even if you have plenty of time to make choices when game time is paused, your stats will deplete as game time flows. There are numerous routes to take with plenty of points of interests to make a detour for, but there is no benefit without risks. How you choose is up to you.Finally, events will occur along your trek. Some offer promise of supplies, gear, or replenishment of stats, often with a cost. Others can deplete your stats and give nothing in return. You might be able to exert some control over how the dice rolls, but outcomes of your choices in events are entirely at the mercy of the RNG.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential, it's pretty laid back if you're looking for a basic game to chill with, but it gets old fast. Not a bad game if it's on sale and you want a low mental energy game to have, but at that point you might as well play dorf romantik or thronefall.

_childDocuments_.review: Allright I reached a point with Insurmountable where patience invested in the game would not be rewarded with enough fun. I made my climb on the lowest difficulty and went all the way to the final peak. It is important to understand that this is not a bad game, regardless of what I am goind to critizies. I played for 10h and those where fine. I do believe however that this game is not exeptional either. For me its stuck in the vast ocean of games your are going to forget about  after beating them. Games that evade you memories and will feel familiar but you cant grasp your old experience times after beating them once. Lets head up the moment and talk about the rights and wrongs. For me I came to term with three Problems that I had with the game. But I wanna mention three good things aswell to give a little contrast to the negativty I am about to unleash. Starting of with the first major problem on your way up the insurmountable mountain. Immersion, the game and its event killed all immersion for me. While we have a funny and simple story the world building makes no sense at all. At the beginning I am told you are alone on this island and the mountain. But I managed to meet quite a few people ranging from strangers to foreeigners. I am ok with the later being natural inhabitants of this island but the amount of other climbers met is ridicules and only topped by the amount of old theethless ladys sitting in front of a shady and worn hut in the middle of the death zone. The game focus its interaction on other people you meet, rather than on your own journes that you walk. Each Event you can discover has a limited amount of varation and they repeat quite often. So the old hag in the deathzone happend way to often. For a risky trip with your equipment and your very soul to protect there are way to many people chilling on this mountain. To much for me to bear and I lost my immersion early on. A good thing worth mentioning is that the dialogs and events are well written. Its clear that the author of this little story knows how to use words. To be fair the story is what kept me playing till the end otherwise I would have quitted pretty early on. Sadly there is no real ending. So many question left unanswered and I dont understand way it needed end so upruptly. Only real disapointment. The rest is workable with.Second flaw for me is within the gameplay. The basic gameplay loop is build around preservation. You got four important stats to managed and if you fail the game will drain your actual health until you die. On normal difficulty its quite impossible to get in a dangerous situation where you are forced to walk in critical state. I only was forced on way up the final peak. This problem might be solved by playing on a harder difficulty which I might wanna do some time in the future. But there is curtain something hiding in the shadows that propably will still be a problem on higher difficulty. That being the absense of a deep layer of complexity. The gameplay resolves arround planing your route and then respond to any action. Those action can be a discovery, a random event of incoming danger, trading or meeting a stranger. Escpacially the random events that either can hurt you depening on the choice to make have no influence outside of said event. The interaction with the level is tied to pop ups. An event blocking a path, for example the collapse of an icy passage, drain some stats but you can continue on without every rerouting. On top of that as long as you maintain your stats nothing searious is ever going to happen. As you only die when your health reaches zero and with events costin rougly 1/20 of your health you need to be stupid on the normal difficulty to die. For what I´ve seen the difficutly adjust only the drain rate of your stats. You run out of energy much quicker, lose temperature faster, sanity breaks faster and O2 is breathinkly fast used up. This will forcefully put you in a difficult spot of entering critical state much ofter. This is a lame way of adding difficutly. I wished for changes in terrain or level. Like mention a avalanche forcing you to acutal route out of the way instead of having a pop up. Or a local storm obnstruction the map forcing you arround or suffer through. The game has a tabletop map and you draw event cards thats all. And this type of simple mechanic made me lose my fun pretty quickly. Atleast they good some outside effect going on. Some missions have route choice where you can choose between serveral obstacles. Obstacles like a spooky route, where haunted by fear your sanity breaks apart quite fast or a stormy route where energy use is increased by a lot. Those things give a litte varation to preperation. They heavily influence the items to take with you. But they happen to rare or are to small to have an influence att all. Which directly leads us the third problem.That being mission design. Three main peaks. The first is the tutorial, the second is more or less a revelation and the last marks the end of you playthrough. Inbetween you have side mission. They exist to serve as a grind for points to level up the climbers and points to invest in better group stats. Groupstats are useless. 10 Point for 0,1% energy consumption. Stuff like that. You need way more you can earn in all of the run to matter. The climber however have cool effect. Abilities like crafting an Item are a nice addition to the game. Its fun to be stucl in the deathzone without O2 and magicaly be able to craft a new O2 Bottle. The problem is that the side mission are a drag. They are repetive and boring. The vary from reach the peak missions and find X Amount of anomalies. The first type is ok. Climb up the peak and than get to the final extract location. The do coontribute nothing to the story rather climbing for fun while find anomalies is the worst type. You need to climb around the mountain on the search for a special tile. You must do them in order and you cant choose wich one to do first. On top they are hidden and need to be tracted with a scanner. Essentially pressing "free cam", lock arround and move in the dircetion with the most beeps. The first side mission have three anomalys the last have five. They are boring and drag the game on. I dont understand why they didnt add points of interest as side mission. Location to discover or secrets to track. Why not climb all the way up to a labratory or military base to maybe find some information or equipment. Why not make a mission that rewards you with a new better item to use after discovering a stash. You even can make some side mission specially design for one of the three characters to justife the reason why the game wants you to use this sepcial characters. Instead of telling you to do it with this one or you are not getting the extra points. Where is my freedom of choice. At the end i skipped some side mission because I grew tired of them. I wanted to see the conclusion to the plot and kinda expected that not doing them wouldnt be of negative influence. I was right. You do them for more points thats it. To get this to an end. I feel this game had potential. Even though this is version 2.0 and I barely have memories of the first itteration before the big changes. I know that the story used to be different. You kinda had three story. One for each character and they tied up at the end. Part of their journey is left behing on peak two. But i feel like the left behind the potential and made a playable ok version of the game. My hope is other developers get inspired by the potential to make there own version of roguelite mountain climbin game. This type is unique ind this game is intersting. I just fails to stand out enough.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting game with thoughtful strategies and frustrating decisions.Accessibility is better than most games (can be played with just a mouse, much of the color coding is colorblind friendly, and there are a wide variety of pacing options).Save features make punctuated gaming a breeze and total time for each mission is long enough to be engaging but short enough to fit a busy schedule.My preferred strategy, once I got the scientist, was to start with a tent, boots, and herbs, wander around below the death zone while power-leveling through research and crafting, and then basically yolo my way to the objectives only really being mindful to sleep as needed and shovel mind-altering herbs into my face.Regarding all of the comments I'd previously read about a lack of "realism" from people claiming to be experienced mountain climbers: You just haven't climbed high enough to make it through your first time loop. You'll know you've gotten to that proficiency level when the world's hexagonal grid tiles are revealed to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of potential here with Insurmountable. Unfortunately, because this game is not in early access, I will treat it the same as any other fully released game, and for that reason, I would not recommend buying it in its current state. I've beaten the game on my second attempt, and I won't be playing it again until the game gets a few QOL updates. I'll name a few that I'd need to see in the game to play again.Being able to exit an event to observe surroundings and change gear without the event disappearing - Nothing more frustrating than getting to a cave only to realize you forgot to wear your gloves.Add more to the story - I'm not sure why this game isn't early access. If it was, I would say, "I can't wait to see what they add to the story", but as it is a full game, I will judge it as such. STORY SPOILER More events - The replayability of this game is hindered by the amount of repeating events. Would love to see more events to flesh out the game.Force the player upwards faster - The game is very easy if you stay at the base of the mountain collecting everything you need. I'd like some kind of reason not to just hike around the bottom. Maybe some external force affecting sanity  (A call of the mountain requiring an increase in altitude per hour perhaps?)All in all, with some effort, this game could gain some wonderful replayability.NEXT DAY EDIT:A huge thing that I'm not sure how to improve would be just how much gear switching there is. It really makes the game feel too Min-Max heavy. I hate having to change my gear to cross two pieces of ice. And If I choose to skip doing this one time, when I die 10 minutes later from a lack of energy, I get frustrated at the game and myself, wondering if I would have made it to the next cave if I had JUST changed into crampons.

_childDocuments_.review: Insurmountable is a mountain climbing strategic roguelike that is super unique and a one of a kind experience.The game starts off by having you select one of three different climbers that all have different starting bonuses and equipment and then you choose the mountain you are going to be tackling.The game then puts you at the foot of a mountain that is made up in a hex grid type style and tells you to climb to the very top.There is a decent tutorial explaining all the different mechanics but overall you have 5 main stats you need to worry about.First is your sanity which can get lowered by supernatural events or traumatizing situations like finding the dead body of another fellow mountain climber. You also have your energy which is super important because this is what you use to actually move around. And you use up more energy the steeper the climb is. So if you are going between two tiles that are the same height it won't cost that much energy but if you are having to scale a 3 story difference in height between two tiles you are going to have to spend a ton of energy.You also have your body temperature which gets lower the colder it is especially if the weather gets crazy bad like a snowstorm starting.You then have your oxygen which only really matters once you get super high up in the mountain in the “dead zone” where there isn't enough oxygen so you cant stay super high up for too long.And of course you have your health in case you fall during an event or get attacked by wild animals or things like that.So all of these are super important to balance because one if your health gets to 0 you automatically die, but the other ones if you get them to 0 there are massive side effects.So like if your sanity goes to 0 you start hallucinating and hearing things that can cause you to make major mistakes that hurt you. And if you can't breathe because you have no oxygen that is obviously bad. Same with the energy and body temperature. So you start scaling these mountains by trying to find the best route and there are also a ton of random events scattered in the mountains that are represented by these tokens.They all pop up these impressive looking art pieces and have a ton of dialogue describing what is happening and most of the time you will have to make decisions that impact the outcome.These are one of the coolest features about the game but I will say that after getting to the second mountain about an hour and a half in my game time I already started to see repeating events.And the events that repeat aren’t even randomized. Some games will have multiple randomized outcomes from a single event to make it even more varied if you get the same event multiple times but this game doesn't seem to do that. The game definitely needs more events considering this is a huge chunky of the game.The other huge part of the game is that you can actually level up your climber by gaining xp from events. And every time you level up you can choose an active or passive perk that fall into a couple different categories. So on my Let’s Play series of the game I kept taking a ton of perks that where focused on climbing at night time.So I would try to rest up which let you regain some stats by spending some time sleeping during the day and then would just try to make as much progress as I could in the middle of the night.And the actives you get are on cooldowns so some of them you can only use once a day but they would make you run extra fast for 2 hours in game time.You also can find a bunch of different equipment like different boots, hats, climbing gear and more that all give you passive bonuses to different activities like a climbing pick that lets you less energy climbing steep parts or a hiking stick that helps you walk faster on flat areas. I like this a lot the only problem I have with it is that it is wayyyy to tedious to constantly switch between the equipment. Because technically the optimal thing to do would be to move one tile and then switch equipment on what is the best for the next tile, move that tile, and then change equipment but that's not fun at all so I tended to just keep the equipment on I thought was generally better. Maybe if there was an auto switch mechanic where if you had the equipment in your inventory space it would automatically use the better gear you needed.And the only other complaint I have with the game is the camera. The camera is a little bit janky and kind of locks and glitches sometimes because I think its tied to each tile and its super cool to zoom in sometimes and get cool shots but some of the time it can be wonky. Nothing too bad just something I wanted to mention.The devs have released an updated that added a handful of new events and made a couple fixes to the camera but I don't think they solve my issues entirely.So overall Insurmountable is a genuinely enjoyable experience mainly because it is super unique but I will say I dont know if I could see myself playing the game past a couple of hours. I think if they add even more events, make a couple of changes to the gear mechanics and camera it would be a lot better but its overall a fully launched game its not in early access or anything.So if you think its worth it for a couple of hours of really awesome unique gameplay then I would say definitely go for it but if your wanting something with more replayability I might hold off unless its on sale or anything.And if you love Roguelikes and Roguelites as much as me then follow my  for more reviews and videos about them.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy review to write.  I've scaled one mountain and then died in the descent.  I've played for an hour, and so I believe I could refund now if I chose.   But of course I won't refund this.  Despite not providing everything a true mountain climbing simulation could possibly provide, it provides not only enough -- but what is crucial: a real sense of challenge and accomplishment.   Some people have mentioned that some events might repeat themselves.  I'm surprised now to find that I simply don't care if they do.   The events are part of what must be taken into account.   They are simply one part of the puzzle of survival.  Even the smallest mountain was sufficiently large that path choice becomes a real part of the game.  I don't know how much "replayability" this has -- but I'm guessing one could play this for much longer than one might initially think.    My first partial success took an hour, as I mentioned, and it didn't seem at all tedious.   To the contrary, it was genuinely interesting the whole time.  The developers have a winner here, in my now even more humble opinion.Edit after the second expedition:  I have reached the summit again.   But this time, making some wiser decisions, I manage to continue much farther.   Relief comes when I finally get back down below the death zone.  My oxygen-starved body begins to recover, but it is still struggling.   Optimism is valuable, but must be tempered.  Indeed, I narrowly escape an unexpected death even as the base camp begins to seem attainable.But then a miracle happens: the sun emerges and a gentle snowfall begins at the same time.   Around me the very air seems to sparkle, as I trudge into base camp, my  long ordeal drawing to a close.  I only wish I could listen to John Denver as I walk those last yards.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent and highly original game. The visuals and atmosphere are wonderful, haunting and at times breathtaking. I love rogue-likes/lites  but I find that not enough is being done with original applications of the genre. Insurmountable does something genuinely new and original with this very relaxing and enjoyable strategy/survival/ path-finding affair.  Simple to grasp, but involving and intense whilst at the same time being a really chilled out gaming experience. Performance wise it's excellent,  I'm running it on "High" settings on a low end gaming laptop ( 1050m/3550h/16gb ram) and having a very smooth time of it with this game. The music and sound effects are rather understated and perhaps the least interesting part of the game, being rather quiet and unobtrusive, but they are no means bad.I'm not going to go into the ins and outs of the game-play, it's better discovered on your own, but suffice to say that it all works beautifully, to the degree that as a whole package I consider this to be well worth the asking price, yet the devs are promising a patch at the end of the month with more random events etc.Now I will say that this is not, in any way a fast-paced game, so if you're looking for one of those turn based games with the dynamism of a real-time game, this definitely isn't it.However, if you're looking for something different and something immersive but with a nice relaxed pace to it then this could be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: "A Mountain of Potential, Buried by Poor Design."Insurmountable had the potential to be a truly unique and engaging climbing game, but unfortunately, it falls short in several critical areas. The most glaring issue is the camera, which is simply horrible—one of the worst I've encountered in any video game. It constantly gets stuck at awkward angles, making it nearly impossible to navigate the terrain effectively. This is especially frustrating in a game where precise movement and planning are crucial.Equally problematic is the pathfinding. Your character frequently takes inefficient or outright bizarre routes to reach a destination, often leading to unnecessary backtracking or dangerous detours. This not only breaks immersion but also adds an infuriating layer of difficulty that feels entirely artificial.Adding to the list of disappointments is the lack of atmosphere, which is crucial for this type of game. A climbing game should immerse you in the environment, making you feel the isolation, the tension, and the sheer awe of the mountains. However, Insurmountable fails to create any of this atmosphere. The visuals are bland, the sound design is lackluster, and there’s a general absence of the environmental storytelling that could have brought the game to life.These issues combine to create a highly unenjoyable experience. Instead of feeling the thrill of scaling daunting heights and overcoming nature's challenges, you're left wrestling with poor controls, erratic navigation, and a dull, uninspired world. The game’s concept is fantastic, but the execution is severely lacking.If you're looking for an adventure game that will test your strategic thinking and climbing skills, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. Insurmountable, in its current state, is more of a test of your patience than anything else. Save yourself the headache and skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: You are one of three mountaineers of differing disciplinary fields on an “uncharted” island. With a common penchant for being easily riled up into believing there’s an award or claim to fame sitting at the top of them summits! Whether it will pay off eventually is another matter, as they aren’t gonna climb themselves, are they? Didn’t think this through- did you now~ This rock-climbing simulator isn’t all just muscly or brain dead, at least not until your oxygen runs out… It is driven by your judgement, resource management and ability to map out a path before actually committing to it! Yes, it is a numbers game for the most part, as you’ll soon see for yourself. Where you have to keep a keen eye on your . But it is like having a partial formula or with the variables missing… The latter being the most important and sole determining factor to a game over.They take the form of events which could nab you precious consumables, waste your breath for nothing or maybe come into some clarity. There exist other climbers, inhabitants, corpses and even ghosts, so the story goes. Although the ascents feel out of your control with the randomized mountain layouts; there is still constant forethought such as deciding on a character class with specialized perks, which route to take with the handicaps listed out, the skills thereafter to pick up and develop. That’s excluding the buffs-debuffs that come and go!Each mountain lasts up to half an hour and there are three to qualify for a win! Multiply that by 3 characters, premature cockiness and deaths, it could take up to 20-30+ hours. And I’m not even done, but perhaps that’s the brilliance of it. Isn’t the journey meant to be a gauge of how much we can put up with? Normal difficulty already let me taste the burn and lactic acid- I shudder to think how miserable or contented I would be on the remaining two difficulties where the experience gets literally too draining~1) Plot your own points, instead of using the default trajectory…2) There’s an “invisible” stat; luck! Frozen into your periphery are the loyal Northern Lights, the rows of stony-icy terrain that stack and dip out of your field of view… For a game that doesn’t have much to look at in real-time as well as lacking animations, it is breathtaking! The events- which range from familiar, unexpected to the occasionally rare sighting never cease to keep me both grounded and tempted to pursue the end of the thread! The way scenarios are vividly and engagingly worded accounted for half of my attention. The other is always focused on not making a slip-up, so to speak!And the sound design rests somewhere between paranoid and clingy with unnerving howls, groans and cracks giving way. To music that instill false hope and divine intervention especially when near events or finding out you’re so close to the top! The striking of the climbing axe also slowly becoming permanent ASMR. It has all the feels just waiting for you to grace your presence~ Visualize a person trapped between  and  with the worst possible outcomes in each becoming reality. A struggle against nature, a searching of purpose and proving oneself… While it is true the main plot points get buried under avalanche or put on ice with each attempt’s triumph, the journey however repeatedly gets overwritten each new climb! New shadowy figures, strangers to betray and hands are lent to you. And the composed, survivalist self you were can be gone just as fast along with the wind as well~What better perfect metaphor of life is there than the literal act of climbing a mountain, reaching a dead end and to having to go back down? Or to totally lose bearings!? Boy, let me tell you my first fruitful climb quickly spiked in despair when I overlooked one major detail; the trip back. So, before you think it’s just balancing stats and brain freezes, it pits you against the powerful, brick wall of “consequences”! Oh look yet another redundant event? Surely the outcomes are unchanged too? WRONG!I am convinced more and more that morality can also be symbolized as a “mountain” where you think you have principles one moment but then it plunges down when you resort to heinous acts like stealing someone’s lifeline thereby condemning you to hell. A concept that you never believed in until seconds away from a permanent blackout. It confronts you with questions like why should you get to live at the cost of others? You could leave it behind, but it catches up with you at a later time and is all you'll obsess about.But it is unmistakably more motivating than it is depressing, although everything is at odds with you. The merciless weather, distrustful beings, yourself, voices inside and so on... Pushing through is the ultimate test of self-worth! A greater appreciation of life, death and everything in between. You think it led to "nothing"? Are you sure absolutely positive about that~  You’re not the only one getting all sorts of crazy the further you climb. The camera is also a victim or is it… a culprit? Especially when you’re encased between tall walls or in a crevasse! Trying to shift it to gain some perspective becomes a bobbing contest where it collides with the surroundings. But there is one good thing, it really nails some claustrophobia into you~ For every mountain overcome, you unlock a life-defining trait that you can choose between when starting a new run. However, one thing that consistently nagged at me was how the equipment or loadout was always the same. Logically speaking, like who would go on a potentially life-threatening mission with just one canned food!?Also, the single run per playthrough means you always have to see things through… Harsh but respectable. However, same can’t be said of the forced progression; tougher difficulties unlocking only after completion of “normal”. And that’s for every role so a minimum of 6 successful climbs is needed to get to the “Bear Grylls” level~ x It could’ve been a feature I suppose- but one of the icons indicating points of interest was obscured by the terrain.~ Saving is still one big snowy blur to me… For instance, when exactly or how!~ At least 3 save slots would have been best. Not for save-scumming but so three characters’ stories can be alternated…Climbing roguelike simple to grasp but mastery is knotty. Stunted progression notwithstanding; does wonders to your endorphins! The way up is truly eventful and so are the downs keeping you going~ If you like to undertake a colossal, breathtaking and semi-realistic challenge involving mountains. If you love to take all of what mother nature has to offer; both good & bad, coming out of it renewed and more survival-savvy. This is one personal hurdle that you simply must climb over~

_childDocuments_.review: Insurmountable is an exploration simulator about mountaineering. You have a character, a few items and you climb the mountain in front of you. There are points of interest on the map (more on those in a minute) but otherwise you're picking your way through various terrains - some of which are more dangerous or harder than others - slowly making your way past obstacles to get to the summit.There's really just two parts to this game. The first is base camp, where you level your alpinists, choose a few pieces of equipment (your carrying capacity is woefully limited) and there's a bit of a story there. Frankly, the story was a throw-away for me. It didn't make much sense about being stuck in a temporal loop and some amulet. You go there, read some text, level up skills, drop a few pieces of equipment into your character sheet and pick your next climb.The climbs are the majority of the game play. The mountains are not truly beautiful because to identify the terrain you can walk on, the textures look a bit like rabbit pellets turned on their ends. The areas you can't go look much more natural. But I understand why that was done in order to distinguish various approaches for the player. So while not a visual feast, the graphics are decent enough especially if you love mountains like I do. The sounds and music are nondescript but not annoying. No voice over work for the few lines of dialog which suits me just fine.  You explore to find various paths and hit points of interest on the way. These can give buffs to your 5 main resources - energy, sanity, warmth, oxygen and health - or they might give you debuffs. You might get items, have an encounter with someone else or so forth. It's a bit random and while there are varied events, you quickly see the same ones over and over again. You're often looking out for caves so you can sleep someplace dry, or a prominent point to recover your sanity or just looking for a treasure chest to get a piece of gear that might help you conquer this climb.The entire time those resources are getting depleted. Energy is the primary stat here because if you have no energy then you're not climbing. Health is the critical one because if that hits zero then it's over. I rarely had a problem with O2 or Sanity (except the final climb where I had to keep watching that stat) and when it got cold I found someplace to get out of the freeze. There's a day/night cycle and weather is a factor too, so climbing at night in bad weather is really going to sap your avatar pretty quickly.Once you've completed your climb (or for some missions found all the points you needed to hit), it's back to base camp for a bit of leveling and selecting your next climb. That's the game, folks.As such, this game doesn't have a ton of depth. It's more of a game to chill to and explore with rather than beat. There are 3 difficulty levels (Normal, Hard, Insurmountable) and I played on Normal without coming close to failing on any climb. it was all kind of easy, and though getting myself into stupid positions was the cause for concern from time to time it was easy enough to right the ship when I made a bad move. There are a handful of downsides/wishes:(1) The camera can be annoying as hell. In general it's fine but you can't really zoom out enough to get a total overview. That's probably okay since it would make it too easy to plan your climbs. But occasionally it zooms WAY in when you're about 1/2 up a steep wall and you actually can't see more than about 5 feet in front of you. You can rotate the camera around but then it's facing in a direction you're not interested in. It needs some work. It wasn't a problem in every climb but there were a few times I had to make moves almost blind until it would reset, zoom out and let me see where I was going.(2) It only took me 8 hours to beat the game. My played time is 8.7 hours and that's with me eating dinner and taking my daughter to school. At $25, that's kind of pricey. (3) Your avatar can't carry much to start a mission but then can fill up a backpack while you're out there with no problem. I guess that's to keep it challenging - after all, if you could take all the gear with you then climbing would be a snap - but it seems rather illogical. (4) There's apparently no random mode. I don't know if the maps are hand-crafted or random since I haven't started a 2nd play-through. But there's just the campaign and that's it. I'd love a random map mode where you get $x to buy equipment, you can use one of your avatars from your campaigns and set a height of the mountain you would want to scale. Then have the game auto-generate a mountain and start climbing. I have no idea how difficult that would be but I just want a climb mode.The verdict on this is pretty easy. If you're not interested in the subject matter - mountains, mountaineering, climbing, exploring - then avoid the game. If you're born with that mountain goat gene and there's not much better than seeing the sunrise from the summit of a mountain then get the game. But get it on sale since $25 seems a bit steep for what you get. I purchased it at 50% off and that seemed a bit of a bargain. _childDocuments_.review: First things first - I enjoyed this little game a lot. It is challenging and you have to constantly consider your decisions. Do I climb up to a point of interest which is out of my way in hope of getting a boost to my stats or maybe find a useful item, or do I conserve my strength and wait for a more easily reachable reward? You have four stats which you need to maintain: Energy which is used for climbing, Body Heat which will decrease in cold weather, Oxygen which will decrease at high altitudes, and Sanity which will gradually decrease as you go. There are ways to replenish all stats but you need to manage them closely.The story I did not really care too much about. It's there to give you a reason to climb a mountain, but it is quite obviously the game play that will draw you in. As you ascend higher and higher the difficulty is gradually increased. At one point you will need oxygen or you will pass out, the higher up you go the colder it becomes, etc. I have spent 25 hours and have completed the game on the normal difficult with all three characters. Basically, I have spent 1 day each on them. Only when you have completed the game with a character are you able to choose a higher difficulty setting - but only for that character. Each characters has a few different starting skills which gives you a slight difference in how you approach the game, but I mean slight because you will mostly rely on the skills you choose as you level up. As you discover points of interest you will receive experience points and when enough has been earned, you get to select one of three random skills/talents. Some are passive and some are activated with a cool down. There are enough skills available to make it interesting to play the game through 2-3 times, allowing you to experiment a bit and choose a different approach each time. In addition, you will find gear and consumables which will make your ascent easier. With that said, it can be a tad tedious to constantly swap between your snow boots or your walking boots etc. every time you are about to scale a particular kind of cliff.This game has kept me interested up until now. It will most likely feel very repetitive at this point so I will give this game a rest. I picked the game up at £15 and as mentioned, it gave me a solid 25 hours of enjoyment which is pretty good considering it is such a small game. I will probably come back to it later on and give it another run at a higher difficulty setting, so I would definitely say it is value for money.I would give it as solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice roguelite(-ke, depends on the difficulty level) about climbing mountains (with some sci-fi elements), in which I spent WAY more time that it deserves, but nonetheless is quite good.The gameplay sequence is to climb a randomly generated map of a mountain (with some basic forms, so its not possible to get a non-passable level) in a form of hexes with different types of terrains, using resource management (you have 5 resources, sanity, warmth, oxygen, energy and health), and interacting with encounters. _childDocuments_.review: A unique game.  It seems like a basic point and click, until you realize you need to do some resource management to achieve your goals.  Inevitably, you'll hike and climb a few different terrains; snow, rock, and ice while managing four attributes that affect you; sanity, heat, energy, and oxygen.  You'll need to keep these above zero to ultimately survive.  Along the way, you'll encounter a lot of events, some random and some marked on the map.  Some of these provide tangible rewards, while some don't.  It's a risk vs. reward system, which I think is cool, but definitely could be better.  Completing each mission will net you experience based on the events you encounter and team upgrades.  Some experience is specific to classes and skill trees.I think it mostly appeals to folks that either climb or hike.  That said, as an avid hiker and novice climber, there are some unrealistic scenarios here.  While, it mostly works (because it's a game and not a sim), I think there are some things it needs to improve upon.Some QoL things:Ability to mouse over terrain to see what your you're on - ice is supposed to be blue, rocks = gray, and snow = white - though sometimes it's not apparentGear is mostly useless - you get 4 slots, face, hands (gloves), other hand (tool), and feet.  Take instance the feet slot; crampons are good for less energy use on ice.  There's heavy boots for saving energy on stone terrain.  You can only wear one at a time.  Though honestly, you should be able to wear crampons or show shoes with hiking boots.  Then there's your tool slot; You'll find a climbing axe which is good for, duh, saving energy for climbing.  But, then you'll have a hiking staff which is good for using less energy on flat terrain.  Again, pick one.  You'll find fur gloves for holding in heat.  Climbing gloves for decreased energy on all terrains.  All of these items will have 2-3 others that, again, do different things on different terrain or effect your attributes.  It goes on.  In theory, these are valuable, but in Insurmountable, these are nothing but filler items because of how often the terrain changes.   To have to go into your inventory at each change of terrain is an unrealistic expectation and ruins any kind of immersion.  Also, considering that when you stop, you stop in the middle of terrain, so I'm not quite sure when you'd have to switch anyway (before that terrain or when you stop?).  Speaking of unrealistic, the story is interesting... (I won't spoil it)Ability to rotate items so you can fit more items in your backpack.Speaking of backpack.  It also amazes me on how unprepared you're allowed to go out.  While you have a backpack, but can only carry a couple of things to start, based on weight.  However, I don't know anyone that would set out on mountain summit with zero food.So, Insurmountable is fun enough and you really don't have to manage your gear if you don't want to, but you really should be min-maxing.  The only things you really need to manage are your attributes and keeping them from getting to zero, although the few times I've gotten to zero energy, my character just goes to sleep and wakes up with 30-40% energy (yes, you gain energy without eating).  Don't get me wrong, I didn't expect it to be a survival game, nor did I want it to be.  I do feel with what's there and just a little more accuracy as to what it's try to portray I think it can be a solid foundation for something bigger and better.Even with it's faults, it's a unique effort and I do like the game.  And, I do recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Probably worth $20 players who want something a bit slower paced (though it may get repetitive after a few successful games). Pretty high quality for what it is.So let's deal with the elephant in the room right away. This is basically a game about pathfinding. That's it; that's pretty much the whole game. Sure there are items to use, and abilities to trigger, and random events to make decisions on; but the fact is the real meat of the game is planning your routes. The built in pathfinder optimizes for the most DIRECT route, not the BEST route, so while you don't need to select each hex in your route, you'll get much better results if you plan your route rather than letting the game do it (for example, climbing up a sheer cliff to the hex next to you might use all your energy for the day, but taking a longer route with more gradual steps to the same point may only take a tiny fraction of it). The possible boredom this could create is somewhat alleviated by having to balance multiple resources (5 in total, only one of which can kill you), since you won't always be optimizing for the same thing; but be aware that this is pretty much the game's core mechanic.That said, there's some rogue-ish elements too. It's a permadeath game, so once you die your run's over and it's time to start over. Most of the meta-progression comes from player learning rather than in-game unlocks, though each character (3 total) can unlock a more difficult mode by completing the game (I've only completed on normal so far, so not sure if there's a drastic change when playing "hard" or "insurmountable" difficulty.There's also consumable's and equipment to find to give passive or one time effects to the resources you're managing, there's also a very basic and unnecessary "inventory Tetris" system (seriously devs, unless items are odd shaped and/or you can rotate them, just limit the number of items we can carry and you'll get the same effect).There's a bare-bones story, each character has different reasons for climbing, and the "mysterious island" angle seems to be more of an excuse for some of the stranger events to happen and for you to be on your own rather than as something interesting to actually discover (though again, only 6.9 hours in so far).All in all it's a fun game for the right situations. Haven't gotten in deep enough to know whether the harder difficulties offer anything other than a more punishing experience, so the only potential downsides I can see are the slow pace and possibly repetitive game play loop.Also: Runs out of the box on Linux via Proton, though the achievements don't seem to work (might be a game bug rather than a Proton bug).EDIT: As of 2.0.7 it no longer runs with Proton. I can get it to launch by adding PROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 but if you are susceptible to photosensitive seizures DON'T DO IT!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm within reach of the peak on my first climb on the first mountain and I have no idea if I will make it either tomorrow or the next day. My sanity, oxygen and warmth are good but my energy is low and my tent is only good for one more night in the danger zone of high altitude. The ice cracks beneath my crampons. The wind plays a Siren song in my ears. I think I can reach the peak but will I make it back down the mountain or will my corpse be just another discovery for another solo climber?I bought Insurmountable after getting bored of the usual multiplayer games with the usual trolls ruining everything for everyone and desperately trying to upset anyone; and I am very glad that I did. No guns. No zombies. No trolls. Just the sound of rockfalls, wind and creaking ice ... and the thump of my heart when I run out of energy.  It may not be for everyone but if you've ever enjoyed watching a film or documentary about mountain climbing while thinking 'I'm never doing that those people are crazy' even as you enjoy the scenery, or if you fancy a more meditative game, then give it a try. After playing it for the first time yesterday I even dreamed of mountain climbing after I went to bed. Now that's good value.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun survival game where you attempt to climb to the top of a mountain while overcoming the elements and dangers that the environment throws at you. You can come across things such as mountain lions, other mountaineers or maybe you start hearing voices echoing in your head from your lack of sanity. Once you reach the top, you must descend back into a safe zone before attempting the second and third mountains respectively. Collect loot on your ascent to help you overcome the dangers that await. This title offers a very high replay value, since the mountains are procedurally created with ever changing environment from, terrain, weather and randomly generated events. The only issue I have thus far, is the events that come up. After your first couple play throughs, you will know each event and how to get the most out of it. I hope the devs add more events to help keep things fresh. Other than that, great game upon release. Keep up the good work.

I decided to return it rather than risk investing hours into it and pass the return time frame, then find out the game was in fact broken.Evidently people have been complaining about this error for months and the devs have been unable to fix it or explain it, just telling everyone to go to their Discord. _childDocuments_.review: INSURMOUNTABLE is a turn based Strategy Mountaineering game from Developers ByteRockers' Games who already have a few well received titles under their belt.In Insurmountable you get to pick from just 3 characters, each has their own set of bonus attributes, equipment and limitations; but essentially they all move the same way on the mountain.  There are 3 Mountains in Insurmountable and each one has 3 routes that you can pick from.  To unlock mountains 2 & 3 you need to have successfully reached the summit & returned safely from the mountain before it at least once.The mountain is represented as a 3D Hexagonal peak which reaches pretty high up into the sky, to move you simply click on a tile that you want to move to and click a second time to confirm.  Each step you take towards the summit has either a positive or negative effect on your energy, warmth, oxygen levels, overall health or even your sanity.  Sanity is an interesting choice, replacing the more obvious food and drink option we normally see in games.  There is a night and day cycle and time is recorded in the bottom left corner, every action you take increases the clock and whilst it is possible to climb at night visibility is often dramatically reduced.  Each day’s weather is also represented here and ranges from normal to stormy weather, the character you selected and their equipment will dictate which of your vital stats are affected first and by how much. As you progress further up the mountain you will find numerous special tiles, if you reach them safely they provide a written encounter or experience of some kind.  This could be dead mountaineers, dangerous animals, camps, old shacks or even long forgotten supply crates.  Each time you have an encounter there is an opportunity for an event to occur where you choose the course of action; however every action has consequences, usually this will included time taken (thereby progressing the in-game day) energy and warmth (especially if it is a cold day).  Sometimes these instances will reward you with additional supplies, tents (which have a maximum number of uses), food for energy or perhaps warm clothing or equipment that can help you transition certain terrains quicker, my personal favourite is the flask of tea, well I am an Englishman afterall.These encounters are not always positive however; sometimes you will sustain an injury from them or worse.  Any injury you sustain stays with you for a period of time and slows down your progress (which is represented by more time passing on the clock for each tile you move).  It is worth exploring these areas especially when below 6,000 feet (I’ll explain that more in a minute) as you can get XP points that allow you to level up your character from 3 seemingly randomly selected perks, not all of which are injury free.  Level up enough and you can unlock new perks that help you transition the mountain more quickly or more safely.The second most dangerous aspect of mountaineering is the terrain itself, hidden fishers, falling rocks or even landslides.  As you choose your route you will often come across dangerous tiles, there is no guarantee that these tiles will be harmful for you & you can sometimes pass them without incident, the adventurer character even has a perk called careful steps which allow you to pass by these dangerous tiles without incident for 4 in-game hours; like all perks there is a long cooldown period before you can use it again.But the most dangerous item on the mountain is oxygen, or lack thereof.  As soon as you climb above 6,000ft you are in the death zone, and as the name suggests the entire time you are there you are slowly asphyxiating, unless of course you are lucky enough to discover an oxygen mask along the way…pretty essential that you do.It a beautiful game, with great character animations and is a lot of fun to play, my only real gripe is with the stats section at the bottom which gets in the way of watching the animation and often trying to look around for a safe route, it would be great if it was perhaps collapsible, and if I could have one thing added it would be animations for falling rocks, landslides or even falls into crevasse with the map shape actually changing to reflect these events.Insurmountable is a fantastic single player experience which has the right gameplay to potentially one day evolved into a MP game, but even without any of these suggestions implemented it is great fun to play and challenging enough to be rewarding too.INSURMOUNTABLE is a genuinely unique & engaging gaming experience.As I climbed to the summit of my first mountain I joked about `what if I had to climb back down afterwards lol`.  Then, I had to climb back down afterwards, without my oxygen mask, or my tent and zero provisions....Level 1 is tough!I like that each mountain climb experience is unique, I like the artistic style and animations & I enjoyed the challenge.I might suggest that the main centralised menu be collapsible or moved over to the right so that it doesn't obscure the animation and path-finding, but other than that I have no complaints (except for the person who hit me round the head when I wasn't looking!).Bug free, stable and basically faultless, but I do question why we set off with ZERO provisions?  Seems a little irresponsible?A few tips & things to note from my limited experience; o Tents only last 3 sleeps! So use caves whenever possible (be wary of smelly ones!)o Be wary of other peoples tents!  NEVER go in them uninvited.o Cold is seriously a killer...I found a few fires, but they never warmed me!  Why is that?o Don't be in a rush, plan your assent; especially when above 6,000ft.A really enjoyable strategy title that literally packs a punch!

_childDocuments_.review: This game “could” be really fun, but I refunded for the following reasons.__________________________________________Story – The magic time loop is stupid. I should have free movement of the camera to move it around and see ahead to plot my course.  You can’t even control the cameras with the wasd keys and can’t rotate with q & e. You manage oxygen, sanity, energy, and body temperature with randomly generated scenarios to deal with, all with varying and sometimes unpredictable outcomes. Excellent game for fans of the survival genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a great time with this, I'm a big fan of survival games and mountaineering is not a game mechanic you see often.Issues:- One event popped up (the tattooed man) and the text was replaced by errors. My friend also had this issue.- Within 20 minutes, I was already seeing duplicate events - the first mountain took me 108 minutes - I feel you shouldn't be seeing duplicate events in that short a time.- The first peak is unreasonably difficult. I had significantly less issues on peak 2 and 3, where 1 was a disaster on all three runs I've done so far. It's an incredibly steep climb, and I didn't have a single oxygen event on all three runs. Yes, I had better equipment on peak 2 and 3, but it feels like that wasn't taken into account for peak one. If you can do peak 1, then you can do peak 2 and 3.Interesting and challenging, balancing the different gear and I like how different routes change your experience. It feels a little thin maybe, needs some fleshing out. I do like how if you do events, the stories continue for more events, creating little stories. Also how each of the three types of climbers have unique text and motives, makes things more interesting and you'll try them all.Enjoying it, it needs to have a bigger selection of events or a setting that the same event can't trigger in a certain timeframe but that's my only real issue. Recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I find myself saying this a lot, but I wish Steam had a neutral rating. Since it doesn't, I feel like this falls more on the negative side for me. Insurmountable is like playing a game of hopscotch up a mountain with occasional events that you can see coming with a triangle/exclamation point or a floating logo. You have health, oxygen, warmth, sanity and energy meters that you have to sort of manage. You also have some light inventory management and basic character upgrades. The game is supposed to have hundreds of events, but in the two or three mountains I've done, I've had at least two of the same events on each run.Don't be fooled by the screenshots on the store page. some are misleading. Only the ones that have the hopscotch hexes are truly representative of what you get. I'd love an actual mountain climbing game, but this is more like a moving a piece on a gameboard.In the end, this game isn't horrible, but neither is it in any way actually good. I got it on a flash sale for quite cheap, but I wouldn't even recommend it at the price I paid.

_childDocuments_.review: A good surprise, simple decision making, resource management.Some people are complaining about the camera, but I think the game is supposed to be that way, since one major aspect of climbing is choosing the right route. Thus, low visibility makes it harder to choose and that is the part that makes the game immersive. Well at least for me, so I think it's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful and surprisingly chill game.  The core is managing your 5 innate resources - Sanity, Energy, Body Temperature, Oxygen and Health.  Each are depleted in different ways and different rates.  Choosing the correct path up (and back down!) the mountain is crucial.  Coupled with an in-game reason to repeat the mountains (with modifiers) it also has some meta progression between climbs.  It is turn based so easy to pick-up and put-down while waiting for appointments or the like.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable game that was a nice change of pace. Something of a puzzle solver as well as inventory management and whilst I understand some of the complaints about the camera angles I felt that it aided the challenge by limiting visibility and forcing  some 'guesswork' on the part of the player. I felt this was in keeping with the mountaineering theme.The ending itself left me with more questions than answers.Overall I would recommend this to anyone who is looking for a somewhat more sedate puzzle game with an interesting, well-presented style.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Insurmountable has fairly unique gameplay and is generally pretty fun, but it soon grows repetitive. Thankfully, there aren't  many missions to grind through (and really, most of them are optional, if you don't mind losing the chance to gain more XP). Also, I found the default difficulty level to be very easy, contributing to my eventual boredom. But it's a decent little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Insurmountable is a game about big decisions. You’re climbing a mountain, an ascent governed by a harsh simulation. Walking is done one tile at a time, click by click, fighting mother nature through text vignettes. Often to your character’s detriment. It’s a game full of metaphorical card draws and coin flips -- but one where every crossroad affects your journey.At the foot of the mountain the story is always the same. You’re full of optimism. You have plenty of resources and oxygen. You take detours just to explore the scenery. I mean, who knows what’s hiding in that nearby cave? And at this stage, the stakes are minimal, with rewards that are potentially high. Like finding abandoned gear. Or points of interest that reinvigorate you, giving you an even better head start. Sure, you’ll expend some warmth and energy to pursue these things. But it gives you more flexibility down the line. Because the further up you go, the more slippery it gets. Terrain takes more time to climb. Weather gets harsher. Bone-breaking hazards pop up everywhere -- each element slowly depleting you. Meanwhile, all those reserves you previously saved up? Gone.The challenge is all about juggling resources. To that end, Insurmountable is very transparent. Choices always have a visible outcome -- good or bad. And if it’s unknown, you always have the choice to ignore it and continue your journey towards the summit instead.Recommended if you think you’d enjoy climbing stacks of hexagonal tiles.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I've played the game long enough at this point to give a  fair review. Honestly, I didn't expect the game to be as entertaining as it was, I'm not usually into the top-down style along with the restriction in movements but I was pleasantly surprised. The game is quite expansive and every map has a slew of interactions that will keep you occupied for a while. It's a good challenge without being punishing, and overall a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Great nugget of a game! I worked through the main campaign in about 10 sessions of an hour, which doubled up as little zen moments. On the lowest difficulty it's harder to fail than to make it (didn't even came close to failing once) so don't be afraid to start it out on the middle one at least, if you're not just looking for a very relaxing playthrough.Very atmospheric and pretty. Such a grand sense of scale when you're at the bottom of one of the mountains.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool gamification of mountain climbing. Feels sort of board-gamey. It's not a realist survival simulator, if that's what you're after, but there is a lot of fun resource management gameplay to be had here.  Strongly recommend you change the keybindings. I find left ctrl to be much better for camera movement than holding down the middle mouse button.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: It's certainly very far from being a finished game. but the potential this game has for story telling and rpg like decision making, as well as a stand alone survival experience are very promising. I'd be very interested to see where it goes in the future. Is it worth picking up in its current state? I think so. more to support the finishing of this game than anything. although you will probably get a good few playthroughs out of this game as it stands, you certainly will need to keep in mind its not finished yet, to not let certain details bother you
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after playing this game for a while, I can say that it's fun, I had a great time playing it and it's enjoyable, however, I also must say that it's not for everyone, and I can understand if someone says that it's boring.In one sentence: Is a good turn-based game, but don't expect it to be as addictive as X-Com or Phoenix Point, however, it's very enjoyable and different from other games.The game story is... just ok, don't expect something similar to The Witcher or similar, you better concentrate in the game itself, it's challenging, makes you wish to play a bit more, do you know the sentence "just one more turn"? well, you got the point. Give it a chance if it might be your type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:- Graphics, animations and UI have a high quality feel to them.- The gameplay elements and epecially the resource meters are simple enough to immediately understand (unlike other management and strategy games).- Clear and meaningful numbers also help with making decisions without just guessing the outcome, i.e. the game is fully transparent in what will happen. There are sill random events (especially negative ones), but they feel very fair and only make you rethink the next step instead of screwing you over completely.Neutral:- There are 2 unlockable characters and a whole skill tree, but I could finish the game before unlocking any of it.- You can't do anything while moving, so even at the highest speed it's a lot of waiting, then thinking, then more waiting. The game demands my attention to make decisions, but if I didn't watch a video while playing this, I would fall asleep.- The events feel unfinished and cheap. The text promt tells me about a camp, so I would like to actually find a camp by looking at the surroundings (a tile that is actually there on the mountain, not just an icon) and interact with a person sitting there.- Each mission usually has one especially difficult thing (e.g. less oxygen), but at least on normal difficulty there are a few level-up awards which completely bypass said difficult thing and remove all challenge.Negatives:- If this wants to be a rougelike then it actually needs to have the gameplay loop and content of a roguelike. This game doesn't allow dying and repeating the same thing until you succeed. Instead, dying is something you try to avoid at all cost and so you will probably finish each mission on the first try.- The story is bad. It tries to set up a time loop mechanic, but with the lack of content and the fixed missions it just doesn't make any sense. In a way, there is too much story which dilutes the pure adventure of climbing a mountain, but also there is too much gameplay (time) which dilutes the story of breaking out of a time loop. The devs should choose one of them and stick with it.- The camera controls like a CAD software, which works most of the time, but it's not fun, especially when it requires finding the anomalies in what is not even a proper first person view.- There are ads in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: I have really been enjoying this game! I like the challenge to see if I can take on the mountain. The only glitch I have ran into that tends to be a pain is when I am climbing an event pops up! Then I am stuck in this climbing pose and the only way to keep going is by pausing the game for every movement. It has happened twice in the 12 hours I have played so far. Other than that which is a quick fix, its awesome. If you like to use strategy and being challenged, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I decided to do this review because of the 2.0 update recently released. I completely changes the whole reason for playing this game.I followed it before release and bought Insurmountable shortly after it's initial release. Played it a couple times and it was everything it purported to be...and quite enjoyable. The devs recently introduced an update (how often do you see a version 2.0 without being sold "Game 2" from any developer?) that totally shakes up the metagame, the story and (for me personally) the whole reason to play it.Basically the game went from three individual climber's reasons for summiting various peaks (think Vertical Limit without the Bill Paxton [R.I.P.] ...meh...) to a Philadelphia Experiment time loop story a la Devil's Pass. I LIKE IT!As for gameplay, the same hexagonal, vertically varied game board and real-time, strategic decision making exists but now the carried over skill and item aquisition matters more and you get to plan for following climbs with the experience you've gained.I would have gladly recommended this one before and I certainly do now.!
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: This game provides pleasing challenges that accurately gamify mountaineering complex multi-part route and equipment decisions ; helps even veterans organize everyday-carry kit with a variety of mindsets ... very psyche'ically healthy to encourage always "Mount the challenge!" too, dialectically progressive :)
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very refreshing game in the rogue-lite genre, like a fresh cool mountain breeze. It has both tension and calmness/zen feels to it. The game's events are what grab you early while the planning and strategy at the higher difficulties reward you for staying around. The soundtrack and sfx soundscape compliment the game quite well. It's an enjoyable experience well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: While game play is similar across all character classes, the nuance in the abilities you gain, and equipment you find, brings a fun element of strategy to hand. I really enjoy the level design, and the rules around stats, and movement seem well balanced. I do find the encounters and events to be repetitive. I hope the developers consider adding more variety into the game, at some point. Overall, simple and fun. Just challenging enough to make that third and final peak an accomplishment.
_childDocuments_.name: Insurmountable

_childDocuments_.review: Finished a full adventure after 5 hours.Got a headstart because I watched a pair of youtube let's play before buying the game.Recommend.The atmosphere of the game is slow and relaxing. (Some may say too slow).The far landscape is gorgeous when the weather is clear.The whole concept and gameplay is good and well executed.I hope to see more unique events/items/other added. Replayability is quite limited at the moment. I'm not surprised to see some comments refunding after 2 hours, there really isn't a lot. ---TIP: The highest a climb, the dramatically more energy it consumes. It's more economic to climb gradually over 3 small blocks, than to climb a single block 3 levels tall.TIP: It's probably a good idea to collect some events at a low altitude when there is no pressure for heat/oxygen/energy, the extra items/XP will be much needed later.TIP: Clicking the mountain top will highlight a short path from the current position, that is a good way to find a heading and avoid dead ends.TIP: On the third mountain, the game concludes when you reach the peak, you don't have to get back to the bottom.

_childDocuments_.review: very, challenging game to play i think, and that was on normal. your actions accumulate and can kill you or make you survive.not an action packed edge of your seat game like some. but i really liked that about this game, i could chill with a beer and play at same time.  fantastic game, really enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely puzzle game with some rpg elements. Simple to play, but not easy to complete a full 3 mountain run. Relaxed but engaging game play. A great brainteaser to relax into. Graphics look great, no bugs. Highly recommended if you want a chilled but thoughtful experience.
