_childDocuments_.review: +32 hours spent in the Demo briefly available in late June 2021, which is important because it means I already knew what I was buying into when I pre-ordered this. In my opinion another Demo should be made available, because it's much better for everyone - including the Devs - than playing 1.9 hours, claiming a Steam refund, and leaving a negative review.It's  to properly assess a game of this depth and detail in 1.9 hours.So what is CoG? It's much easier to say what it , so let's start there.This is not , which is okay since it never claimed to be, and was never intended to be.The majority of negative reviews have been left by players basically looking for a spiritual successor to GOC (a relatively simple & undemanding 1998 game about highly aggressive, warring Prohibition era gangs, but given the limited scope of the game it was great fun all the same), or perhaps something similar to the recent  but which, unlike that game, is actually fun to play...The problem is, these players never looked closely enough to see that vicious, unrelenting gang conflict is  what  is about, , so in their disappointment they left extremely unfair negative reviews.What this  is a Tycoon style business management & logistics simulation in a suave, stylish, sophisticated gangster suit. You are  supposed to be some minor street thug looking to make his name in the local underworld, written in blood.In this game you are essentially  in his formative years, having just set up  and planning how best to make the most of the boundless opportunities offered by Prohibition. Of course it will involve some bloodshed, for such is the nature of this highly profitable & competitive business, but  ever as a last resort. Blood is expensive, and too much of it is distinctly bad for business: this simple historical  is an element of realism almost always conveniently ignored by most mob games, but in  it is paramount.Don Corleone would most definitely approve.In summary: if you're looking for mindless mob violence, look elsewhere. If, however, you're actually looking for a deep, intricate, challenging recreation of the Prohibition era underworld,  may well prove as ideal for you as it is for me.Edit:I feel it's worth adding that in just the few days since the game's release there have been multiple game updates. In addition to the obligatory minor bug fixes (and I do mean minor - game crashes or ruined saves are  something we have had to worry about) there have been a substantial number of UI and mechanical improvements made, most obviously derived from player feedback and suggestions. The devs are clearly listening and are dedicated to improving the game, as their hard work over the past few days demonstrates beyond any measure of a doubt.If you're interested in the finer detail of this game, feel free to check out my comprehensive :

_childDocuments_.review: After a lot of time playing through the game I simply cannot recommend it. There is a ton of potential here, but what seems like it could be a deep game at first, ends up being difficult to control and ultimately shallow. The overall approach where you are a small timer building a bootlegging business is neat and the way that the game uses favors and reputation has potential. In practice though it leads to repetitive game play. Favors for example lead to these chains of repetitive conversations where you don't actually have to do anything but click a few times and then drive to the next guy, ultimately resulting in lots of people who are willing to buy your product. The police for me, after several days of playing, seems to be either a huge pain or trivial, nothing in between. Rival gangs are either unstoppable when you meet them due to their having guns compared to your bat or are complete push overs after you get guns with one mobster with a gun able to nearly always pick them off one by one. To top it all off, you don't seem to truly have any affect on places. Supplying them with product doesn't lead to anything happening, aside from maybe the police eventually being interested.The game does have some fun points:But those fun aspects are completely overshadowed by the pain points which I found to be:Overall, the game has a lot of potential and, in some ways, reminded me of the game series Patrician, but ultimately I find that it falls short of being truly engaging. I found myself frustrated just as often as I found myself excited. Far too many areas need more depth, from interacting with the police, to setting up your businesses, everything seems to be buried too deeply in various menus and be only superficial. Given all that I would say to steer clear of this game for the time being, especially at a $30 price point.The good news is that the developer does seem to be continuing to add things to the game, including UI improvements and the like. I will keep an eye on things and update my review should any of these improvements add to the depth of game play or smooth out the user experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So I rarely leave reviews, but I feel that for the ones who don't like it there is a fix. Anyone that says this game is just driving around, do one play through using cheats. _childDocuments_.review: The game had potential but has huge drawbacks crippling its replayability. Consider purchasing only during a steep steam sale. I won't dive too deep but I'll list a few things that have made me bored of playing the game, and having just purchased numerous DLC's for this I am leaving my spiteful review as it sort of falls in line with what others have complained about over the past few years. 1.) Crew sizes are limited, you'll be capped on the amount of employees and foot soldiers you can hire. 2.) Expanding fronts is a very tedious and slow going process, with one block expanding every 4 turns or so. The city is massive, and you won't always be able to break even on expenses for that particular front as some blocks simply have no businesses for income to be generated, so you'll end up having to drive down there and make payments to keep the territory under your control - or lose it altogether. With limited crew sizes, you're now having to do the money deliveries yourself or change up the complex scheduling of your own delivery drivers. It's tedious micro that doesn't need to be in there.3.) Discovering more businesses willing to purchase a particular alcohol that you have the infrastructure of producing in high quantity. This was difficult for me, and ended up creating a bottleneck. The game wanted me to expand in different avenues of alcohol production like Gin & Bourbon, but again - I'm capped on the managers and delivery drivers I can hire for that particular industry without bottlenecking my own beer production so why bother? All in all decent tycoon game, but has many pitfalls. The 3d aspect was a bit unnecessary, many buildings look the same and the city feels kind of hollow at some points, and I would have been fine with isometric 2d visuals provided the game could have more content and complex data visualizations of charts. The revenue chart isn't that appealing to look at.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of organized crime stories and 4X games, I was very pleased to find this little crime tycoon gem on sale. The gameplay is mostly management and decision based with your concerns revolving around supply and demand and influence, but the real fun comes from crafting your own crime narrative. The developers have given you a lot of tools and room to roleplay and create your own criminal empire story. Are you content running a protection racket in your neighborhood, recruiting local thugs to help lean on store owners? Or will you try your hand in bootlegging, manufacturing your own liquor and managing speakeasies? Or maybe you prefer gambling ventures, running card games, taking bets, and shaking down debtors? Do you have higher ambitions in politics, maybe you want to influence candidates and push legislation? Uh oh, looks like you forgot to renew your "donation" with the police and so they've raided one of your speakeasy operations and cleaned your coffers to compensate themselves. Now you need to go to your relative/connection and help sponsor another immigrant's passage so they can smuggle in more of that sweet Whiskey for your speak easy, and maybe you can help them find a job in your operation too. All of these mechanics are part of City of Gangsters. Some features are available through their extremely reasonably priced DLCs. That's the pitch, now the pros and cons:Pros: +Lots of fun crime enterprise mechanics to play with and fun events to keep you on your toes, like police, rival gangs, politicians, and store owners. Plenty of gameplay options to play your way and narrative directions to go in here. +The game is really good a facilitating your needs without making it too easy. Like if you're a cider bootlegger, but you don't have a place to sell some Gin you recently just "found", that's ok, you just need to put it in your truck and talk to some store owners in your territory and start calling on favors so they can grant you access to new contacts that may specifically buy your new inventory. You'll rarely struggle to find what you need, but you may struggle a little to get it by having to do a favor or a task, that's perfectly fine.+There are some really great narrative details here, like the immigration/smuggling scheme I described above was something I experienced that allowed my Scottish gang to import some high grade whiskey that sold well and offered up lots of crew members. Those kinds of things really flesh out the game and make it feel like your experience is unique and the gameplay is catered to your playthrough decisions.+The option to automate delivery routes and collections is a fun management tool that can help ease expansion and adds a lot to the game.+Great setting, music, and minimalist art style really help immerse you in the role of a criminal leader.+You can really build and foster relationships with the local business owners and expand your influence through fronts and favors. They'll become your contacts for weapons, new business opportunities, learning new skills, and facilitating new business partnerships. The favor system is interesting and a great way to expand your influence like a real Don.+Extremely reasonable DLC prices.Cons, Suggestions, and Room for Improvement:-Some of the gameplay elements only really scratch the surface of the narrative options. This game has the potential to be the Crusader Kings of crime tycoon games, but it needs a bit more decision making in the criminal capacity. Killing, for example. You can only kill other gangsters and hoodlums by landing on the same space as them and having a combat encounter, but I would like the ability to call for executions, either contracted out to another gang or hoodlum or delegated to a crew member. For a relevant example from my game, I encountered a store owner that was actually the relative of a local hoodlum I had previously killed in an encounter, so he had a super high negative opinion me from the start and refused every interaction, there was no reasoning with him to join my territory, no favors I could call on to improve his opinion, and no way to even do business with him. So why can't I threaten him to make him leave, or have him killed, or break up his business with a fire bomb? That's what a criminal might do. Another example is vehicles and crews; if I have a delivery truck that seats 2, why can only one guy can ride in it? You should be able to have crew members double up and ride together in a vehicle to cover each other and double up on tasks to reduce the time or steps necessary to complete a route. Also some more "family" elements would be awesome, like designating successors, maybe marriage and home management (even the Don Corleone had a house compound), though one of the DLC's does offer the option to customize an office, which is nice.-Repetitive prompts. Store owners will regularly ask for favors, which is how you earn favors in kind, usually in the form of a cash loan or some start up materials. But oh my Godfather, the repetition. I was so sick of everyone asking for the same loan for $1k to "save the family farm!" 20 people in a row had the same request. I was in Atlantic City, yet all of you have family farms that need saving? All 20 of you? Shouldn't someone be asking for a loan to help out their degenerate gambler family member? Or maybe ask me to break up their competitor's operation? Or maybe just ask me to teach someone a lesson or facilitate a business partnership? Nope, everybody wants to save the old farm. I couldn't tell if it was a bug or just a lack of diversity in early game prompts for favors, but there needs to be a bit more diversity of store owner quest and favor prompts. I'd happily offer the developers 100 free prompts based on crime stories just to see them included.-Crew interaction: Another unfortunately shallow mechanic is the crew. You find and hire crew members as you progress and grow your empire. You can assign them to management positions, pickup or delivery routes, or you can personally control their movements and actions, but you can't really interact with them at all. They have no side plots, no conversation options, no individual struggles or dilemmas, they don't ask you for favors (though that may be in another DLC). They have traits, sure, but the negative ones rarely ever come into play in any meaningful way besides being a limitation. Say, for example, my casino manager has the traits of being Cruel, Vindictive, and Strong, it would be interesting if that actually impacted his position. Like maybe he enjoys roughing up the gamblers excessively over minimal debts, and now he's hurt a politicians son, broken his leg, that could be a prompt for the choice to send him away, have him switch to another operation, like collections (but that could piss off the politician), or you could let the politician exact some justice, or maybe you could decide he's a mad dog that needs to be put down. Those would be great crime management options... but you can't do any of that, you can only assign him to his job and his tasks. So I would love to see more crew elements.-No way to take over an already occupied territory. If I go to a new location and find a hoodlum causing problems, kill him, I can't just take his territory, I still can't even work with the store owners and opening the door to new areas can be pretty difficult, but that may be more realistic; it's easier to kill someone than it is to take over their enterprise.All in all, I love this game and will support the developers with the hope that they will keep adding more to this solid foundation. There is a lot more to love here than there is to hate, and the stuff that bothers me really amounts to more of a wishlist than a s**tlist. If you love crime tycoons, gangsters and mobsters, 4X games, management games, or just want to do some crime boss roleplay, this game is a fantastic affordable option that is worth your attention. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect metaphor for how much micro-management and boring time-wasting must go into real organised crime. Al-Capone himself would have chose prison over playing this abomination. ✔️ Basic customisation options.✔️ Art style is okay, Procedural generated maps.❓It's a attempt at a genre that is not commonly made so I'll give the dev's some props. ❌ Micro-management hell. This game is 100% ONLY micro-management. Want to start making beer? that's a 15 step process. Second resource needed? another 30 steps. Car can only hold 5 oranges? Lol Add more steps, This is the whole game, nothing more than a very long, drawn-out process and the more you play, you'll simply do this process forever with different resources.❌ There is NO thinking in this game. AI about to attack your Territory? Game Tell's you exactly where and when. Simply put someone there and your safe. Police raid coming? Game tell's you where and when. Simply don't go there that turn.❌ NOTHING IS INTUITIVE, Making ANY resource & selling it takes forever is increasingly boring and tedious. ❌ "Combat" is a joke. It literally boils down to "have a higher attack number?" Press attack and they die/run away. How can a game focused around gangsters and violence have so little thought put into it? ❌ One soundtrack in game. Enjoy hearing it forever. ❌ Territory/AI conflicts are frustrating, and not even remotely fun or engaging. AI Walks into your land that you've spent 20 hours setting up a route in? Time to restart all over again. Accidentally closed the popup? Time to reload.❌ No multiplayer. ❌ Overpriced and under-developed, Like real organised crime ... avoid this trash.

_childDocuments_.review: is a gang management game. The objective is simple: take over the criminal underworld of whatever city you are playing in. You can take over Detroit, Chicago, and Pittsburgh. In addition, prohibition has just hit, giving you and other like-minded gangsters a prime opportunity to make some cash selling illegal booze. So while the beginning isn’t that challenging, it quickly ramps up as you spread your territory.The core of the game revolves around cash, just like real life. You need money to pay your crew, buy upgrades, fix your cars and trucks, take over new territory, and buy supplies. When you first start off, you are selling homemade beer, cheap wine, and moonshine. Then, as you take over more turf and do more favors, you unlock the premium stuff and can start bringing in real money. Of course, you have to find someone to sell the alcohol to since it is illegal and all. Selling booze can be one of the game’s biggest determinants. Sometimes you need to travel way too far to sell your stuff, and you end up wasting turns.To buy new buildings and get new alcohol productions going, you will have to expand your empire. First, you pay a business that likes you to act as a front for you and your illegal activities. From there, you can also convince the neighbors to pay you protection money. Of course, they won’t like this, and the cops will take notice, but the income is reliable and steady. While  is a solid mafia management sim but the combat holds it back from greatness.- Huge amount of variety- Gameplay is smooth- Good pacing- One background track- Quickly overwhelming- Characters feel very blandDISASTER | BAD | MEDIOCRE | OKAY | GOOD |  | AMAZING | MASTERPIECE

_childDocuments_.review: This is not "gangster crusader kings" but it is pretty "meh". Automation is clunky, combat is RNG with very little you can do to impact it, you drive around filling your warehouses mostly and you get frustrated after a while when your competition keeps shutting down your fronts.It's difficult to figure out what a manager does and very quickly you will start to need to automate deliveries. Except automation requires a lot of attention and micromanagement. They need money in their trucks, they can't just "buy all" or "sell all" since their truck will tend to fill with one good or another over time.It's just not a good game right now. With some more engaging gameplay and QoL upgrades to automation it might become it. Good luck finding a truck dealership.The concept of corners, fronts and businesses has a lot of potential, but i feel more like a delivery boy than the boss of a budding crime family.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the concept of this game. But I can't recommend it because the RNG aspect is too hardcore. Each time you play, aspects of the city are procedurally generated and it gets frustrating because you end up with bridges to nowhere, dead ends and huge deadzones that are generally just ugly.Additionally, even though there might be someone in the city selling your resource, good luck finding it. If you don't *start* with an infinite free supply of a tier 1 ingredient, you might as well restart the map. It's entirely possible to just not get any of the resources you need to start.Also, I really don't like how the game handles certain things. If you want to drive across the map, it can take months. And expanding territory is annoying because unless you get a nice grid area, you might just not have any good options near your starting location. It would be really nice if you could choose your starting location, and initial setup too.All of these problems are fixable, and I do occasionaly retry this game, so I'll update this review if I do, but I can't recommend this game in the current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is NUMBER ONE if you are a Godfather, Boardwalk Empire fan, or just a fan of Gangster/Mafia history. The great thing about it is how you can take over parts of the city, and structure your outfit just like a Mafia hierarchical structure. I'm a fan of the Godfather and Sopranos, and I like order and structure, and this game has it. Selling booze isn't the only thing you can do, you can run gambling houses, extort, loan-shark, and get into turf wars with rival gangs and outfits! This game is a 9/10 (not a full 10 because the game has a endgame timer, but it lasts so long, you'll have time to beat the game, I wish you had a unlimited time option, cause I'd love to run it forever!!!).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of games with an ecconomic component, and I think I've found my next weekend killer - CoG is an absolutely wonderful game that looks to be getting even better over time. the procedurally generated elements and multiple different valid play styles (focus on one product line? on your own speakeasies? on variety for ease of sale? on territory and passive income?) make the game infinitely replayable. the unique social system the game is based on is the heart of a broad and successful approach to make the game roleplayable - there are some mechanics that you learn to deal with better over time, but I mostly just do whatever I would irl. various mechanics give the game a satisfying air of challenge - achievements feel real, and when struggles pay off you feel powerful and accomplished. _childDocuments_.review: I was hoping this game would fulfill my desire for a spiritual successor to Gangsters: Organized Crime which was first released in 1998.  Unfortunately it is not cut from quite the same cloth.  City of Gangsters isn't a bad game, and I would give it a "so-so" rather than negative review if that were an option, but it does not offer (within the refund limit) a compelling or engaging experience from my perspective.Major complaints are: a clunky interface, somewhat clunky controls when controlling more than one vehicle, lack of automation and flexibility for buying and selling goods, opaque combat, music that does not fit the theme, and a generally ugly aesthetic.  Sometimes building signs stack on top of each other in certain camera rotations, and there isn't any kind of compass so sometimes it's hard to tell which direction you're facing.  Sometimes double-clicking will perform a move action when right-click is the default for this.  Is it possible to set up a route to buy and sell resources?  I don't know since I skipped the tutorial to experience as much of the game as possible in two hours.  Early game weapons don't seem all that different, and it doesn't seem possible to kill somebody with a knife because you will be incapacitated by their fists.  The music is kind of a happy bumbling-along sim-city track that isn't bad, but where's the 1920s swing jazz and piano?  The game is also very brown, even the wealthier parts of the city.  I love pixel graphics but I just am not digging the aesthetic.Those are all very specific complaints, and I am willing to bet that the game gets more fun as time goes on if some of my complaints about the mechanics are resolved through ability unlocks later.  I do like having various resources to trade and produce, but production is limited and tedious.  What might be nice would be even more limitation on the goods you can buy and sell in the beginning: why do I need to see quests and buying options for barrels and bottles when all I can produce is moonshine with stoneware crocks?There are plenty of good qualities to this game as well, and you can probably read about those in other reviews, but I personally found it more tedious than fun, did not like the look or sound of it, and hope I get my refund at 2.1 hours.  If not, maybe I'll play it again, but for now I am going to try to reinstall Gangsters: Organized Crime.Update 1: 7.5 hours inI have played for another 5 hours so far and am now very familiar with the automated routing system...it is also very clunky.  Maybe the biggest problem I have with this game now (besides it being ugly) is the lack of analytics...I can't tell how efficient my routes are at all or really what each individual gang member is accomplishing each turn.  There doesn't seem to be any way to cancel quests, so when I get something I really shouldn't have agreed to do, like give some person $1000 for an unclear reward, it just takes up the entire side of my screen.One more word about the game being ugly: it is almost hard to look at.  There is a certain zoom level that shows each corner and only the relevant businesses, but you can't really see your people, so you have to zoom to the cluttered level to give any orders.  Everything is just dull brown...I get that it is going for the 1920s sepia tone look but it just looks like a bunch of square barf.  Nothing at all on the map moves...it would be great to have some little squares with heads bouncing along on the sidewalks or maybe other cars just randomly driving around to make it seem less dead.Is this early access?  I will keep playing to get deeper understanding (for the people) but for now my negative review stands.

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations were subverted and while this isn’t usually a negative thing, I pictured City of Gangsters like a potential revival for the organized crime strategy subgenre. That was a target placed rather far compared to what the title I’m reviewing today managed to aim in the end. COG has been published by Kasedo Games and it is developer’s SomaSim third Steam release to date after “1849” and “Project Highrise”. With their experience, I knew that the simulated economics will be spot on, yet I certainly hoped for the underhanded aspects to organized crime to be branched out more. It isn’t a spiritual successor to 2001’s “Gangsters 2”, a title still nowhere to be purchased or played on modern systems.“Another cog in the murder machine” as a song by My Chemical Romance mentions. COG is the acronym used in the game’s executable icon but it weirdly fits into the sentence I previously mentioned since you’ll be roleplaying an integral part of a bootlegging machine that eventually formed the influential Commission also known as Murder Inc. While not the same love letter to the “Boardwalk Empire” series like Kalypso’s Omerta, COG manages to simulate in-depth the bootlegging aspects of the Roaring Twenties in the United States. Time for a little history lesson. The National Prohibition (Volstead Act), 18th Amendament of the US Constitution came into effect in January 1920. To simplify matters to their exact absurdity, the seemingly good intentions of certain self-righteous politicians and members of the civil society paved an almost literal road to Hell. By banning the legal production, distribution and consumption of "intoxicating liquors", the Prohibition opened the proverbial floodgates of illegal booze which in turn funded the American Mafia and the entire US underworld regardless of member ethnicity. Street hoodlums became affluent gangsters overnight and they were aided and abetted by corrupt US officials which took a significant part of those profits. Blood money funding political campaigns is just the tip of the iceberg. By the time Uncle Sam realized the disaster and monsters it had enabled, it was obviously too late. The Volstead Act was finally repealed by the 21st Amendament in December 1933. Alcohol was no longer a hot commodity, but the mobsters had all the spare cash they needed to look towards new profitable ventures such as legalized gambling, real estate, fine dining or the classical “waste management”. Legal fronts to more nefarious activities. Investments made possible by those 13 years of Prohibition.If you actually expected a proper story from COG, you may have to settle for what I’ve written above as the template for the randomly generated campaign maps found in-game. There’s no New York, Boston or Atlantic City at the time of this writing, but you can indulge your bootlegging fantasies in other iconic cities which marked the Prohibition era such as Chicago, Pittsburgh, Detroit or Cincinnati. The East Coast may be a future update while the locations currently present are focusing on the Midwest portion of USA. You'll roleplay a character you’re free to customize in name, portrait and social background, this including the various traits crucial during gameplay. The Midwest was the target of the last immigration waves towards the United States from Central and Eastern Europe, so veritable melting pots were formed in the aforementioned cities. I really liked how the dev team handled this portrayal, since organized crime went beyond Hollywood’s typecast for poor immigrants of Italian or Irish descent in the early 20th Century. Unity Engine is powering COG to the best of its ability given this particular voxelized approach towards the game’s visual style. I enjoyed “Gangsters 2” or “Chicago 1930: The Prohibition” in 2D sprites, I am not going to complain about the 3D aspect of the assets in City of Gangsters. If all you want is shallow eye-candy, “Empire of Sin” will gladly provide just that. COG is fine from a graphical perspective, serviceable for its strategic subgenre and it scales perfectly to higher resolutions without any glitches, bugs or crashes in sight. You can even disable the HUD for proper screenshots of those maps you’re slowly corrupting.There’s no voice acting, yet the soundtrack keeps things from getting stale, even as those few in-game songs play in an infinite loop. Jazz is an acquired taste, I know. Those instrumentals fit the title’s simulated era like a glove and authenticity matters in this case. You can mute them and listen to whatever you want instead, even better if you have your own jazz & swing playlist running in the background. Can’t go wrong with Bing Crosby,  Benny Goodman or Django Reinhardt.Sandbox Bootlegging Campaign would describe COG’s core gameplay, since you won’t be able to properly emulate the dark deeds of Al Capone by just making and shipping the illegal alcohol from point A to B. Drinking oneself to death on booze of dubious quality isn’t the only vice which was catered by Prohibition-era gangsters. You had “earnings on the side” from prostitution, gambling, protection rackets and shylocking (usury). COG only simulates bootlegging in all its complex glory, while merely dipping its toes in minor hustles such as extortion and low-stakes poker sessions you may only participate in. It’s paramount that you complete the tutorial and keep a close eye on the game’s encyclopedia long afterwards. There are a lot of gameplay mechanics you will have to learn through the “hard way” RNG will deliver them. Seed generation for the maps can deal you lousy starting conditions and my advice would be to rinse and repeat until you notice a proper resource infrastructure for at least one commodity right from the start.I’ll up the ante and propose you focus on brick wine or moonshine from the get go. They are the biggest return on investment for a neophyte bootlegger struggling to stay afloat. Financially speaking, you’ll face at least the first two years inching very close towards “bankruptcy” and ironically, there are no loan sharks to prevent that. You expand your influence by gaining new street corners with the help of fronts you must establish. Make it a priority to also offer and enforce your very own protection racket on any small businesses within your territory. You’ll need that extra cash once you notice the weekly wages of your subordinates. A week is an in-game turn and there are over 650 turns in a campaign. Plenty of time to subjugate an entire city. Make sure you keep the patrolling cops happy. Having a truckload of booze confiscated alongside your dirty cash, will hurt infinitely more than a bribe or two.I really wanted to enjoy and rate this game more, but even its comprehensive economical aspects pale once you realize that the combat is as simplistic as a bunch of static images checking your stats to determine the outcome. Perhaps it may get fleshed out in the future, it really needs an overhaul there. Good luck establishing automated supply lines, it’s gonna be an uphill battle to form an actual bootlegging empire across the map.+ Steam Achievements.+ Complex economic simulation.+ Replay value through randomly generated assets.- Underwhelming combat section.- No Steam Trading Cards.- No storyline per se.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this is simply the best high-command strategy game about the mafia. Xcom is nice, but not as a mafia game, so Empire of Sin is not as good an option. This game is a masterpiece

_childDocuments_.review: Showing my age a little here, I was a massive fan of Gangsters: Organized Crime back in the day. Since then, I've been waiting for a game which replicated that experience and brought it up to date. This game is not it. However, it is a fun and engaging management sim with a 1920s feel. I've played nearly 150 hours (although probably about 1/4 of those are just leaving the game on in the background while doing other things) and I'm not bored of it yet. The game focuses on resource management. The idea is to set up supply chains to produce illegal booze which you then sell to businesses or through your own outlets. The police, other outfits and local thugs provide the obstacles which can be overcome in diverse ways.Pros: - The game looks and sounds nice.- It runs quickly; there are no long delays between turns.- There is an excellent variety of illegal booze to make and sell.- You can set up quite complex routes with many conditions to really optimize your booze production and selling.- The developers are very committed to the game, and updates come regularly. They just released a patch with a random city generator that really boosts replayability.Cons:- Other outfits aren't as much of a challenge as they could be. Once you reach a certain size, they tend to just leave you alone, and you can safely ignore them until you want/need to take them out.- The local police will bust you if not paid off, but the FBI equivalent don't do much at all. On my last playthrough, I had an agent pass through my whole territory, and nothing happened.- The missions and flavour dry up in the mid to late game, and things get rather repetitive.Overall I'd give this game 7/10, and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys management sims.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, but it has a lot--and I mean A LOT--of unnecessary clicking.  Everything you do will send you through menus and sub-menus.  You will make 100s of sales and purchases in this game, and each time you will go through about 4 menus to do even this basic and crucial action.  Even saving and quitting has a couple of extra clicks.There is more mouse clicking than a 2002 RTS game!The clicking is so bad, I almost gave this game a down vote, and I would submit that all the clicking is what caused some reviewers to  feel that the game gets tedious as it goes along.  It would feel a lot less tedious if there wasn't so much GD extra clicking.

_childDocuments_.review: Great bones to become a game that can rival Gangsters Organized Crime. The small development team is engaged and active on comments and social media and it feels like they want to create something special. The game is getting a lot of attention through patches and DLC. A solid  mafia game has been missing since the original gangsters. It would be worth developing the characters more (more faces, abilities and outfits). It would be great if you could rename your characters and if they had their own tech tree. It would be great if you could assign muscle to fronts and pay to have a couple of goons protect some valuable locations. AI needs to be more difficult. It would also be great if you could put a few gangsters in one vehicle as opposed to having them all drive in separate cars. For such a small dev team, they have done quite a bit of work. Hopefully the community continues to support them and the game can become a cult classic.Cheers,The Tea Tiger =)

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game but it's not worth it.- Becomes tedious and boring very soon, just a couple years in.My dislikes in no particualar order- After some expanding, new buildings prices skyrocket - from $1k to $8k. I understand this from game design perspective, but it doesn't make sense realistically. Why suddenly everyone who has a business proposition, offers it 8 times more expensive than the ones you made a deal with already.- Upgrading a business deletes all improvements you installed, you'll have to install them again at double price.- There are tons of generic events you can attend, which cost from $250 to $400 and reward you with: relation boost with a random person who dislikes you, or random mission to deliver 70 units of random booze in short time (5-6 weeks) to a random location - if you have it producing, it probably takes you 8 weeks to brew that much, and there's a high chance you don't produce that booze and have to fail the mission (and to remove it from quest log you have to travel there, which may be at the other side of city)-  your crew works either on delivery, or manages a business. Crewmember that earned enough promotions becomes a captain and can qualify to position of accountant or intimidator. Accountant require them to _both_ have produced 500 units of booze, and have been sold 500, which means you have to move your manager into a car and have them deliver booze while their skills go to waste there. Intimidator also have weird requirements: vandalize 5 businesses, forgive 5 gamblers (what?) and something else I found to have my most intimidating captain to lack.- other than building space, a bottleneck for your production is stoneware crocks: you can't reuse the ones you sold, and have to buy new ones at various cafes.- some improvements to production make more booze out of same amount of ingridients, which includes crocks. meaning you can brew 30 crocks of booze using 25 crocks and sell that. I don't mind, but makes no sense.- your buyers always require the same type of booze. Meaning if you produce moonshine, and a business nearbuy wants beer and wine, you'll never be able to trade with them until you open a production of those. Makes little sense with how thirsty everyone is in prohibition era.- you can open a gambling house for $3.5k, then you have to keep $1k in there for possible winnings, and then you get measly $60 profit per turn. Quite a pointless waste of money, but it seems to be required to make one of you captains the intimidator (eventually)I tried to keep playing, but I lost myself trying to gather the bottlenecking stoneware crocks around the city, trying to gather money for next business, and just got bored to death

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters, which could have been an interesting foray into a criminally underutilized genre in gaming, quickly devolves into nothing more than a never ending daisy chain management simulator, with little depth and next to no style (unlike the era it's supposedly set in). Things go from bad to worse as one quickly realizes that neither the poorly thought out and implemented UI (which manages to be simultaneously clunky while at the same time not displaying enough at a glance information) nor the actual supply automation mechanics themselves are up to the challenge of running anything beyond a modest empire at best. "Combat" doesn't even warrant mentioning, as it's nothing more than a single obfuscated RNG roll with bonuses added to it by the weapon you have equipped (weapons are in a linear list, with the ones lower down being objectively better in the damage potential statistic).City of Gangsters, put simply, is an offer you SHOULD refuse.  Do yourself a favor and buy, and read this carefully as it was FIRST and is a DIFFERENT game,  Omerta: City of Gangsters instead,  as it's better in all regards and focuses on game-play and tactical decision making rather than an endless treadmill of micromanagement.What a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: I can say this game is interesting.  However, it is also boring and tedious.  The delivery system is all kind of messed up at the moment, so you're left doing everything manually.  Which. is. the. worst.  Navigating the talks with each store front to buy stoneware crocks and bring it back to the base may seem fun at first.  But when you need to go to 5 stores per turn, it gets REAL old REAL fast.  I have like 10 achievements that belong to only 2-3% of players, and I can see why.  I have a lot of patience and restarted/reloaded my games several times to make up for the poor procedural generation giving me nothing to make alcohol with or nobody to sell my alcohol to.  Finally got on a good run, I'm taking over my part of Chicago, I took down a rival gang by taking out 3 of their leaders trespassing in my territory and having my cop buddies tip off the feds on them twice.  I'm having a good time.  But the deliveries do not function correctly.  It takes 2-3 weeks (turns) for my guy to drive down the street, pick up some goods, and come back.  He should be making 3 of those trips PER turn with his action and movement points.  Given that, I fell behind by a month or two in supplying my operation, and now I'm trying to figure out how far I have to go back to reload to save it. But that's when I realized, I didn't really want to.  I did not want to use 3 different people in 3 different vehicles all manually, each going to 4-5 places per turn all click-by-click.  Trying to remember all the routes, all the stores, when their stuff resupplies, how much money to put into which vehicle, etc.  If that was able to be automated, and the person was as efficient in the automation as it is to do manually, THEN it would be fun.  I could focus on late-game things like growing MASSIVE territory and supplying HUGE neighborhoods with multiple types of alcohol.  But I can barely keep 2 types of alcohol running while keeping everything straight in my head since deliveries are messed up.  I have 3 different supplies to keep supplied to 2 different operations and then 2 different delivery routes depending on which alcohol I have on hand.  It's a LOT to not have any functioning automation available.  TL;DR, until they fix deliveries, this is fun until you need to automate things (about an hour in).  Then it is no longer fun (which automation is one of the most fun and satisfying parts of any resource management game).  They don't even teach you in the tutorial how to do deliveries.  It's a fundamental part of the game.  DO NOT BUY until this has been addressed and this review changes to positive.EDIT:  Oh, and that's completely glossing over the fact that this game has like 0 gangster/mob gameplay.  It's an illegal alcohol management game.  The most gangster things you'll ever do is pay off a cop and fight other gangsters on corners.  And that's it.  0/10 gangster/mob value

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, but you need to come at it with the right frame of mind. It plays very much like a board game. There are a handful of balance and QoL issues with the game; however, the developers have shown a keen interest in addressing these issues with a series of patches.The gameplay centres primarily on controlling you and your gang members in producing and distributing illegal alcohol. So logistics plays a major role. Combat is downplayed in the game, although it does exist. While the game gives you a final score at the historical end of prohibition, you can continue to play the game afterwards (much like most Civ-style games that declared a winner after a certain turn limit).All in all, if you're on the fence, the price point is reasonable, and the developers are very responsive.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept plagued by bad decisions after bad decisions and bad implementations after bad implementations....For example, it's pretty  much unheard of to make a x4 turn based strategy game with no adjustable difficulty levels/sliders/options.  If you feel the game is too easy, too bad and if you feel the game is too difficult, well, once again, too bad.*** While you can chose your character's name, sex, nationality and starting skill, the character traits are randomly assigned once the game starts.  You can have up to 3 random traits.  No kidding, I've spend over 4 hours starting new games until I ended up with a character and starting location that I wanted to try my luck with.  This is such a letdown.  So many others games let you create your character prior to starting a game just to avoid this particular setback.  Not them. *** - Fixed in patchGoing hand in hand with the unremarkable character creation is the character relationship status with the rest of the city.  This is the most original aspect of the game but it definitely needs a lot of adjustments to the formula to actually make it fun on a consistent basis.  "You gotta know a guy..."  to get anything done and building relations and getting favors and meeting new people can be very exciting if you get lucky enough for the random game seed to be balanced right.  I've started games with my circle of friends being right next to me and I've started games where turn 1 was pretty much game over because all my friends and people that I could ask for favors and introductions were across the city and and it would take 30+ turns to make it there assuming that I didn't get killed on the way.  The maps suffer from the curse of the 4x gameplay.  Each seed is randomly generated and you can have the awesome luck of having the game start in a great location with resources that could be put to use immediately or you can end up spending half hour or maybe even more exploring the immediate area before you realize that it's game over and you need to start a new game.  Think of starting a Civilization game in the frozen arctic...  It's playable but you're not going to have much fun with it...Another major issue that I have with the game is the repetitive grind.  At first it is a lot of fun exploring and finding out who's buying what and finding a way to get the resources moved to and from them but after 20 hours of playing this game I am so F-in burned out on the grind that on this fact alone I can't recommend the game.  Sure, eventually you can push past it but you'll pull all the hair out of your head before you do. Yet another problem that should be addressed by the developers is the restraints that the game puts on your "family".  The size of your organization is determined by the size of your territory.  In my opinion (and this is just my opinion) this is a very stupid concept.  I can spread out like a virus, be completely broke, have a very limited number of connections/favors but have an army of thugs because of my large territory.  Now you can have a well-oiled machine, organized, focused, rich but small in territorial size and because of that territory size, you can't hire any muscle.  So in another words, the only strategy that the game truly respects is that of the ZERG.  Small but tough is not much of an option.  This emphasis on the ZERG pretty much goes against the "keep a low profile" aspect of organized crime so once again, until they patch and fix this issue, I personally can't recommend this game.  But just because I don't appreciate a ZERG strategy, it doesn't mean that you might not either.  Overall, even though I can't recommend it in it's current state, I do like the game and I will keep a close eye on it in hopes that future patches address some of those issues.  If those issues are resolved, I will change my review accordingly.  In it's current state with it's current features, this game is a $10 to $15 vallue at best.EDIT:  I have close to 40 hours in the game now.  Until the game addresses and fixes the broken random map generation features such as resource distribution and points of interest, the game is  broken for the most part, creating a complete fun killer.  Visiting the dentist is more appealing than sinking another minute in this pile of broken mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon starting a new game, you will be able to choose the settings for your game. The settings on offer to you are Scenario - Map (Chicago, Detroit and Pittsburgh), Nationality, you have the option to choose your characters Nationality from the following options, English, American, Austrian, Canadian, Danish, German, Hungarian, Irish, Italian, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Polish, Russian, Scottish and Swedish. If you can decide which Map or Nationality to choose there is a Random Value Die which will give a random scenario.    Next you can choose your character's Name, Gender (Male or Female) and a Starting Skill. You can also choose to hit another Die which will give your character a random name etcetera. The Starting Skills you have on offer are, Getting Territorial, Hooligan Respect, Natural Mechanic, Nice Building You’ve Got There, Organising Crime, Protection Rackets, Respect for the Law and Street Brawler. Each of the skills will give you a bonus of some sort, such as Street Brawler will improve your outfit’s prowess with non-firearm weapons, increasing their damage and chance of successfully landing a blow. Once you’ve decided on your game's settings selecting Start will begin your game.    The game starts on the 1st of June 1920 (first turn) and before you get in to creating your criminal empire there’s some information on your current situation. You only have a few quid to your name as you arrive in the city, however, you have family there and they run a small business. It’s from this place that you will branch out in to the neighbouring areas as you spread across the city.  The neighbourhood and city are split into blocks, on one of the corners is your safe house. This is your relative's legit business, however, there’s room in the back to get a not-so legit business up and running. There is also a storage room where you can store your resources and cash. To help you start you will have some resources to sell which will bring in a few quid. What resources you have are random for each game you play, but you could have something like Home Brew, Brick Wine, Cider, Barrels of Fruit or other items.  Your little bit of the city is indicated by a blue area, this to begin with is your area is the corner of one of the blocks within the city. From here you’ll need to expand, the city buildings are colourless, like a Fog of War. However, as you move from corner to corner of each new block you will reveal the nearby buildings. When you reveal the new buildings, some will have an icon above them, these icons will display the type of business you can find there. Moving to a new corner will require a Movement Point, revealing a buildings business will cost you an Action Point. Once you have used up your action and movement points, you will need to end turn, each turn lasts Seven Days.  As you reveal new businesses, you may be able to trade with them, although sometimes they might not like you. This could be a problem if they don’t like you and you want to expand in their area. To get around this you can have a resident have a word, with the residents on other blocks and businesses. This will require a Favour from one of the residents which are already onboard with your expansion. There are other Favours you can call upon as you progress, although be careful with your Favours. Some folks only have one favour while others have four or more. Be wise with your favours, the resident with only one favour might come in handy more than those who owe you more favours. It's a good thing to get your residents to spread your good name, this will allow you to expand into new corners and be able to buy and sell with new residents who wouldn’t normally deal with you. You can find out how you stand with the residents by clicking on the icon above their building. It will tell you how many favours they owe you, some information about them, you can also buy and sell from here along with other things. You can also select the Chat icon which will show you who that resident is friendly with. Also here is how good a relationship is between you and the resident. To take control of a new block corner you will need to be in good standing with the residents there. Next you will need to set up a front in one of the businesses. This front will collect money from the other residents each month and are now under your protection. You can also may be able to start a new business in the back of a residents building. You will need to unlock new skills where you can create new resources, you can find these being offered by residents and are indicated on their icon above their building. Keep an eye on the icons above the buildings as they will let you know when to collect your cash, if the residents know someone who could be of help to you, whether or not they know of a building for sale so that you can create a new business from premises.  As you expand, you’re going to come under the microscope of the law, hooligans and other crime crew who don’t want you stepping foot on their territory. You can bribe the law but if they don’t and they are sniffing around one of your businesses then you won’t be able to collect cash, resources while they are close by. You can may be use the hooligans and other crews to do some dirty work for you but you’ll need to get the on your side. If you don’t then they can attack you especially if they find you trying to do business in their territory.  If you do get into a confrontation with another crew, you can Initiate Attack mode. This will pit your crew against another crew, some information will let you know the strength and health of both yours and the other crew along with The Target and Method of attack. The method is the type of weapon your crew will use, you can choose which weapon if you have multiple weapons. You can also choose which target to attack if you have multiple targets. Once you’ve decided selecting the fight button will play out the fight. You or your enemy will then have the result come in which is either good or bad. You don’t want to be roughed up or worse but if you do suffer some damage and lose health you can visit a place and stay while your health recovers. you can choose which weapon if you have multiple weapons. You have until the end of Prohibition (December 3RD 1933) to establish your fame and establish your Legacy. If you can reach and maintain three goals then you’ll become a famous businessman or community leader. However, if you can reach and maintain six goals upon Prohibition ending then you will become the stuff of legends. There are four categories for your legacy goals, Fame, Connections, Economy and Competitors. Each of the categories have goals which you need to complete and maintain if you want to become overall boss.  Positives  + Nice graphics + Enjoyable game + Challenging + Steam cloud + Has achievements + Has cards Negatives  -  Camera angles frustrating at times -  HUD gets in the way on right side of screen  It’s the 1920, the dawn of Prohibition, you arrive in the city with nothing but a few quid in your pockets. Can you change your status, wealth and become a legend of the Prohibition era before it ends? 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Just wanted to start that I haven't played the game for 80+ hours. I have a tendency to leave my computer on when I am away. It is more like 20+ hours.City of Gangsters is a tycoon management game where you play as a bootlegger at the start of prohibition. With a small amount of money in your pocket and big ambitions, you sow the seeds that will create your criminal empire. The biggest issue with this game is that you come expecting a very in-depth crime simulation and that's not really what you're getting. The main gameplay loop in this game is that you will be managing and growing a bootlegging empire. However, to do this, you must gain connections and socialize with the people around you. The first thing that might stump new players who haven't played the tutorial is that they will find that no one wants to buy/sell anything. This is when you learn that the most important thing about this game is who you know and, more importantly, what they can do for you. Selling Illegal booze is... well... Illegal. And no one is going to openly buy off of anyone. You need to gain trust and also prove you have a quality product and the only way you can really do that is by doing tasks for people OR meeting people through mutual friends. The social system in this game basically determines what you can and cannot do. You can't expand without having someone close to you who would be willing to open a front for you and that requires a close connection. You also can't find many buyers without having people tell you who is buying what and you can also find that a lot of people have connections that could prove important and valuable in your expansion.Now that you have some buyers, now it's time to brew. There are a lot of different beverages you can make for the public, from hard cider, to bathtub gin. These products all have different prices and demand. You might find that hard cider is the most popular drink in the neighborhood and you'll have to meet the demand to make the most bank and maybe you'll find that just the next block over, there's a large demand for wine. Every playthrough will be different and there is no "cheat" booze that you can universally use. However, as it stands now, there is a few beverages that are way too costly. For example, bathtub gin is incredibly expensive to and often comes out as a loss in profits. These minor problems are a common theme with this game. It's really small things like that which add up. Now that you have booze for your buyers, you can now sell it off. Now this process at first is going to be incredibly tedious. However, as your empire grows, you'll be able to afford more people to help automate the process. Your crew will vary and each individual will have a set of skills that will make them better at a specific job. A crewmate can either be a manager at one of your operations, making it run more effectively; A deliverer which basically goes around buying or selling the goods you need for your operations or muscle, who basically are just characters who don't have any specific task and usually are going to do the tasks that everyone else doesn't have the space to do. Muscles will most likely be your soldiers during a gang war or the ones who do the tasks for NPCs.Now while all of this very fun, hence why I am recommending this game, there are some major problems with this game that makes the "mixed" score very fitting. The most glaring issue is that this game has a bad UI and it gets frustrating when you get lost in all of these menu options just to do very simple tasks. The UI finds you clicking way more than is necessary to do tasks that in any other game would be done in 1-2 clicks. The UI has probably THE worst notification system ever because it doesn't notify you of anything of an importance. The amount of times that I lost tons of product because my bribe with a police officer wore off is insane and I am never notified of it. It's even worse, when sometimes the police will arrest one of my guys AS SOON as the deal is over. And when I say soon, I mean on the same turn. I shouldn't have to lose possibly thousands of dollars worth of product simply because the UI doesn't know how to notify me.There's barely any diplomacy in this game at all when it comes to rival outfits and for a game that praises itself for it's social simulation, you can barely do much with an outfit outside either ignore them or destroy them. This game barely let's you speak to the rival outfits, never mind make deals with them. For example, I went to war with a rival outfit. After a few months of fighting, the outfit leader asked to meet in a neutral spot. I sent a guy over and he was attacked. At first I thought this was a clever ploy by the outfit to try and kill one of my guys but no, when I interacted with my attacker in an attempt to strike back they were offering me peace? They attacked me and then asked if we could have a truce. It's small stuff like that which seriously takes me out of the experience. I was expecting very rich choice when it comes to dealing with outfits and gangs but your option literally just comes down to "ignore or kill".You'll also find that it is incredibly frustrating to automate things in the game. For example, you can only talk to people if one of your guys are in the corner that the person is on. On paper, this sounds a like a good way to add a little immersion but in practice it's incredibly cumbersome. Because that often means I have to take someone else out of doing their task to simply talk to someone. I understand the reason behind this choice and I'd be okay with it if I had to have a guy come over to bring the items they need for the task or to collect the reward, I'm totally okay with that because it makes sense. But to simply talk to the person? Phones existed in 1920, it would be very easy for someone to extend their disbelief in believing you're calling someone on the phone to discuss business. You can still have it so that you still need to send a guy over to deliver the goods or collect payment but to have to derail everything for someone to ask me to do a task that I may or may not do? It's cumbersome. There's also a weight system in this game. It makes sense for cars because cars can carry so much but for operations/warehouses it can be tedious because if you reach a weight limit in one of these operations, it can derail your entire operation. It means that you'll always need to have a guy on stand by to check the warehouses to make sure you still have space to make your booze. They did kind of alleviate this with a recent update that allowed you to extend the space in your operations but I would much prefer if they introduced a menu that allows you to alter things in the game so you can turn off and on the things you don't like. I would be fine with an Iron-man mode of sorts that requires you to play with default settings to get achievements but a lot of my criticism would be negated if there was an option to turn these things off. After all that, should you get this game? I personally say you should. This game is a seriously addictive experience and you'll have tons of fun playing the game. The Devs are very good people and they have put out many updates fixing these problems. I wouldn't be shocked if much of my criticism is outdated within a few months (and if it does, I will make sure to edit this review). There are problems but I feel it extends from being a small team of developers rather than the development team being bad designers. It's a good tycoon game that in a few months may turn into a great mobster game and if you're willing to look past the flaws, you'll have an amazing gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A painfully tedious game, quality feels like something you would see on Newgrounds or Kongregate in 2012. If you're not absolutely married to the prohibition/gangster aesthetic, try out Caravaneer 2.  It's a fraction of the cost and is similar in concept: you're a merchant running trade routes, managing production facilities and it actually has a real combat system, unlike City of Gangsters. This game boils down to micromanaging little faces on your map around the city for hours on end. The incredibly limited options at your disposal when it comes to interacting with the city is an unfortunate reminder that not all game dev teams are equal, especially the smaller ones. If you wanted to expand the toe-deep shallow content of the base game, be prepared to open your wallet to get through some DLC paywalls.I have been looking for a worthy heir for Gangsters: Organized Crime and alas, this was not it.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't your standard mobster shoot-em-up game. This game is about thriving and surviving in an american city during the prohibition era. You'll learn how to brew beer, wine, cider and even champagne and spiced rum.But first, you'll need to acquire territory and get your hands on some buildings to house your operations. The best way to do this is to build a casino and extort some poor, indebted patrons into granting you a building owned by their relatives.   Bribe the cops, buy politicians and occasionally fight with rival gangs. You have quite the arsenal at your disposal, including Winchesters and tommyguns. City of Gangsters has some in-game achievements that allow you to become a celebrated and famous mobster.The music in CoG (upbeat mysterious instrumental jazz) is so good I didn't even want to tune in to a radio station :)  If you buy this game I strongly recommend you buy the expansions for a few bucks more as they ad a lot of content, maps and even mob factions. Addictive and fun. A management game with a twist.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would recommend this game if you enjoy turn-based management games, mobsters and if you're patient enough to learn the game. I'm having a blast. It reminds me of Omerta: City of Gangsters (2013). I've put in 137 hrs and am still trying to conquer my first map (AC) the 'right' way. It seems like the developers are putting in good work on the game and, I guess, it's ok to spend a few bucks on new content to support the continued development.I think whats missing is turn based strategy during combat like Omerta: City of Gangsters has. Enhancing character customization during up-leveling with the idea that I may have to use this person to fight in a specific way would really enhance the experience imho. _childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on gangsters management, but not quite the Gangsters: Organized Crime (1998) of olde. With a surprisingly deep logistical system in place that feeds your illicit businesses, this might appeal to players who enjoy games like Rise of Industry more than those that loved Omerta or Empire of Sin. To be fair, I'm still relatively new to the game, and I haven't gotten to experience the mid or end-game content just yet. So far though, the early game seems to be primarily a logistical experience as you explore the map and open up new locations. There is a complex relationship system that you can exploit using favors to gain relationships, items, or business opportunities, but overall it feels a bit clunky in terms of how many clicks it takes you to get what you want.Gang vs. gang combat so far also seems a bit lackluster, with your characters being directed onto another enemy gang member to engage in a random dice-roll fight. At the end of the day, I still think this would be a recommendation but with a caveat: you should be a person who doesn't mind following logistics chains and ensuring your supply/demand is balanced properly with automated delivery routes. If any of that sounds boring, this might not be the game for you.(Received Steam key for Youtube content)

_childDocuments_.review: So, I was on the fence about this game.  I like the idea and concept it's going for, and I  think there's an opportunity here for this to grow into a much better game. As it stands however, I simply cannot recommend this game at the price I paid for it. With a 25% discount I grabbed the Deluxe edition for about $27.  Based on the percieved entertainment value the game currently has, I would put this in the realm of tabletop/board-game titles and would consider it at around the ~$15 price point or ~$20 if you absolutely love resource micromanagement like ANNO but are willing to sacrifice all the nice graphics, movement, real time flow, and etc and exchange it for a turn-based clicker game.  Graphically it gets the job done, but don't expect high-end graphics here or much of an evolution in your business or buildings as they expand or grow -- they largely stay the same.There's a lot of great stuff here.  The maps are procedural and there's workshop map support so the opportunity for continued play is pretty much limitless.  Sadly, it just isn't really that fun.  As has been mentioned in other reviews, the game is a resource management clicker game, and not really a crime or gang game much at all.  You will do pretty much clicking all game long.  From making products, to moving products, to selling products, and everything in between.  Click.  Click.  Click-click.  Shift+Click.  Click some more.  Click... click... .  The setting is neat and again -- the idea is pretty cool -- but it isn't fun to just click and read and click and read and rinse and repeat for eternity.  I really wish there was more involvement here to which I would refer to the devs to look at Weedcraft Inc.  A similar game but one that allows you to take more of an in-person role in the creation of what you sell to run your business.  Things like actually being a part of the brewing/making process... making custom beverage recipes and what not.  It would go a huge way to breaking up the monotony of endless clicking and having everything automatically done in the background by turns and RNG. In the end, I just felt pretty disconnected from the game.  I never felt like a kingpin crime boss ruling the streets -- I felt like a courier, making endless rounds of a town and clicking on every business I could endlessly repeating the same processes of making new connections, buying materials, selling where I could, and so on.  The opposing AI didn't feel very smart and never did I feel that I had a "fire under my rear" to make me sweat or worry.  Perhaps multiplayer where you could go against other human gangs and not just AI would help here, but even then it's still just a clickfest against other people in a clickfest.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game a big thumbs up but I can't. I love the genre and the gangster theme. The has some great potential but it's just not there yet. While playing I never got really hooked and I kept thinking about other older games that did it right like Port Royal 2. I know not a gangster game but a really nice supply and demand simulation with some fighting elements. So after about 30 hours of this game I dusted off the old PR2 and spend my time playing that.What's wrong with City of gangsters in my opinion is some minor stuff I can get used to and not that big a deal like the weird controls and the repetative graphics . Where the game falls apart is in the gameplay. It's too micro managy, i couldn't finish one thing before being forced into another thing. I felt like I was always a step behind, or too slow with expansion and progression. This feeling of lack of control made the game frustrating instead of fun. The biggest frustration is when you finally have your 5 corners and the enemy drives up and shuts down your front. For some reason there is no defense and you can start all over again for the enemy to do the same thing again. So you think well then I have to go destroy that outfit so it stops but you can't because you don't have the muscle because you don't have the territory.The start of a game is too slow, and when you push through that it gets too overwhelming once you have a bigger crew and multiple businesses. Managing the supply routes is impossible because you can't figure out how many action points it costs your driver to do stuff and you can not see the production rates of other businesses. And if by some miracle you get it right, the driver levels up and he has to many action points so it all goes too fast. Not to mention the insane delivery setup menu where you have to load and unload every single thing in a new step where the focus keeps popping back to your first shop so you keep scrolling around the map trying to find the business you where just 1 second ago (This is actually bad programming and they should fix it).Like I said at the start of my review, I really want to give this game a good review but it does't deserve it because it really isn't a fun and addictive game but the main reason I dusted off a 20 year old game and played that instead. So unless you can get it at 75% discount I would not recommend buying this game

_childDocuments_.review: It's not the most entertaining game. Kinda had lazy written all over it. The map and icons are over whelming to look at and discern, you lose track of key buildings you need to access because it just gets lost amongst the hundreds of others. I got this game hoping it would expand upon Omerta: City of Gangsters, and it did; the problem is is that is not a fun game like Omerta was - there is a severe lack of atmosphere. No voice acting, Dreadfully un-amusing map, graphic features, and art design. It's fun for for the first few hours, but, when you realize how one-dimensional the gameplay is, it loses it's appeal. It builds from Omerta in how the maps are vastly bigger, and you can more intensively employ a growing list of crew, each with their own shipping routes of cash, booze, and other contraband, which has it's charm but loses that charm when buying resources for your manufacturing operations is more of a chore than first expected. You have to buy the same item from multiple stores, and there's never a constant amount in each store, and there's almost never enough; So, when you automate your crew to pick these resources up, your forced to pick between either going by too many stores to make sure you bought enough jars for your homebrewed beer or keeping the route short and risk having your production screech to a halt becasue your guy wasn't able to find enough of the jars - this would be easy to do if i had more control over my crew, but the automation lacks the versatility to effectively do this. There is nothing else it offers. There is no combat. just a simple 3-click menu and if your stats outweigh that of your oppenent, you win - it's very lack luster. The music is mundane. There is no story mode, just endless sandbox, which gives little to no incentive to play. A lot of "new" features are locked behind DLC but i doubt they would do much to revive this game. The Police and enemy gangs do almost nothing to impede your progress, so long as you bribe the police, they are harmless. Even when you encroach on other gangs turfs and attack their members, they do not actively hunt down you or your crew, thereby leaving you no dynamic form of gameplay. The vast majority of this game revolves around a helf-baked route making system to automate a prohibiton empire. There is an extortion system where you can shake down store owners for protection money, but there's no incentive other than to claim more territory that you need to build your back-room oprations in. The game doesn't change much as you progress, there is no strategy involved, since the AI doesn't so much to challange your tactics as a threat to the livelihood of your crime family as much as it serves merely as an inconvenient obstacle that you can just leave on the backburner until it's to time to expand your empire, then you could attack them whenever it's convenient to you.  You can see this game as an unfulfilled vision of the devs to build a long-lasting top down tycoon style game. The fun goes away very quickly and although it does have some value as being an orignial take on the top-down tycoon series, it falls too short of being a game that is fun to play, hard to master, and just having a sense of character that so many others in this genre have achieved and is not worth the 30 dollar price tag. The devs are talented but it seems this game suffers from a lack of a centralized vision and does little to make for where it lacks. Buy this at half-price. tops.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays like a mix of Gangsters 1 and Gangsters 2. It's got a lot of the depth and management that G1 had, and the real-time environment G2 had. Unlike G2 though, CoG is flexible with how you can use spaces, and expansion isn't just endless drive-bys (though I do kinda miss those).A few tweaks could certainly be made. It's got a sliding cost scale (like Heroes of Might and Magic level creep) where new buildings etc cost significantly more as you grow. I guess this keeps you and the AI from building sprawling empires with dozens of buildings (which probably helps performance), but it feels really artificial.Some expansions could also be made to the game info. Like better info on what the difference is between different sorts of cars. More depth in areas like policing, courts, jail, etc (like G1) would also be amazing.Even so, CoG has more depth than any other prohibition era gangsters management game since G1. SomaSim definitely understands the genre. Hopefully they can take the depth further with expansions or a sequel.
