_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for over 8 hours after purchase and am not sure at want point it is actually supposed to become fun.The random spawning of your initial operation, supplies available near your starting area, and purchasers of products you can produce seems to set you up for failure more often than not with what you can realistically access in the early game.  It took me more than a dozen spawns to finally get one that was even remotely viable and since the game keeps one continuous rolling save it seemed like a miracle.Even after hours of expansion, hiring 3 other gangsters to automate delivery and supply routes for my operation as well as handle other random tasks, the game was still just clicking around trying to complete random tasks.  More often than not the rewards were either recipes for booze I couldn't produce or even sell, or it was free supplies of booze that nobody wanted to buy anywhere around.  What a prize!As soon as I expanded to a second building and was about to setup a second operation to make beer (the only other booze I could source from one single available business and sell to only one other different business) the rival gang from several blocks away that I had never even talked to immediately came into the corners all around my main operation, started wrecking shops, and attacked my crew.Multiple local cops showed up because of it arresting all of my gangsters, a huge chunk of my product/supplies, and the majority of my money.Now I'm pretty much back to square one after an entire day playing and asking myself why...when...when does this game become fun?Click and Drive Simulator 3000 is a better title for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a ton of potential. I hope the devs work on adding in more complexity and much more depth. It would be nice to see the development head into a Gangsters: Organized Crime (G:OC) 1998 like game direction. The options to do so and the potential is there that's for sure. Some things that could be added since the potential is already there:-A legal system with depth and options to bribe DA's, Judges, Mayors, snitches. Jail time possibilites for not dealing with active cases or hiring the right lawyers/paying off the right people-Options to organizing hits on civilians or business operators (whom may have snitched on your operations or saw something they shouldn't have), lawyers, judges (working on active cases involving your organization or employees), mayors, people of influence and many more-Opening more illegal business and legal business of different kinds other than alcohol operations ( gambling dens [could be added to upgrading the speakeasy], numbers rackets, prostitution operations, gun running, counterfeit money operation presses, loan sharking) endless possibilities to list-The robbing of banks and other businesses-Different illegal and legal routes to income, other achievements, and much more-Multiple routes and ways to clean dirty money-Kidnapping other outfit members, judges, civilians, and so on. With options of extracting information or other things useful to your needs or missions-Too many to list :)A MAJOR PROBLEM I've come across is the DIFFICULTY. The game is way to EASY in it's current state. What is needed: -AI needs to be tougher, more intelligent -The police need to be tougher-Bad choices of location and store fronts of illegal businesses should punish you in game with law enforcement raids and or other outfits discovering these locations and punishing you for poor decisions-FBI implementation needs a lot of work as well and needs to be more difficult and complex. More of a threat regardless of certain bribed officials and so on-Hiring of different types of employees for your outfits (lawyers, accountants (used to audit business and clean dirty money), political advisers, construction contractors, immigration officials, legal business operators-Extremely good gangsters that you are able to hire should be more rare. You can easily find a hood with good gun skills and give him a tommy gun and run the table on rivals due to the simplicity and non challenging AI. Make them harder to acquire and make the AI much more difficult by having more numbers, options, and or intelligence-Slow down the ease and speedy progression by making things more difficult and complex (I've been playing around with random generated maps and maxing out the values of rival gangs, police, and hooligans to 200% but that still doesn't make it much more challenging) -The AI needs a lot of work. In it's current state there is zero challenge at all. Needs more difficulty, depth, and complexityI could go on forever but overall the game has a TON of potential and a dev team whom seem to care about where the game goes from here. For City of Gangsters only being in a 1.1.2v (1.1.3v) state the sky is the limit. But much more needs to be added into the current game for replay value. My only hope is the devs take this game to level of depth and complexity it deserves with all the intended features working and functioning as meant to be.There is so much possibility to add to this game in way of business, management, and strategy. Again the sky is the limit as they've seem to have left open all options. I'm excited to see what the devs do with the game and have really enjoyed playing it thus far. Hopefully the game will reach it's full potential which is very possible. A good game which has the potential to be a small cult classic to the dwindling numbers of us who remember great titles like G:OC from 1998. This game isn't and won't be for everyone but if you take the time to learn the game, enjoy business/mafia management sims, then this could be a great game for you. I own the Deluxe Version of City of Gangsters and have thoroughly enjoyed it myself thus far.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game. It feels too narrow. The NPC's all say the same stuff. It feels repetitive to talk to them over and over again. The video in the store and the updates under development made it seem like a deep simulation game. But in reality it doesnt feel that way when I play it, it feels too simple and it gets boring quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Its a bit fun, but one does struggle with complexity and repetitive tasks. The supply chain is really cumbersome and the game doesn't go far in terms of automating steps. Partially due to its round base nature, which as a game mechanic isn't totally understandable. After a few hours I got bored, even with all the DLC I don't think there is much more depth to the game - quite unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far not a game for everyone. Hot damn is it the game for me though.Basically if you are looking for a slow burn, micromanagement, make your own story gangster game then this is exactly for you. It combines RPG, Turn Based Strategy, and Business Tycoon style gameplay fluently together forming a game that makes you feel like you are running a bootlegging business. That being said, it is a VERY slow burn. This isn't Omerta or Empire of Sin. You play on a massive map with incredible detail on every turn. You have to really take your time, check things over, and make sure that you have considered all of your options on what to do or make sure that you fully read the text boxes of what you are doing. Overall: Personally this is the gangster game I've been waiting on for a long time, so for me its a high 9/10 if not a 10, but its pretty bias leaning into a very niche style and theme of game.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: I spent 3 hours micro-managing all my deliveries, and pick ups. Love the game, but there should be a bonus for buying from a store where you now have increased loyalty. They should offer to deliver direct to you, meaning you can free up you own men, and also make the game feel more populated. I found in late game I was getting everything delivered to a single warehouse, then it would be taken from there and given out to where it needed to go. I also believe that it would be good, instead of having a shop ICON over the shop itself, that the icon should be in the centre with the other corner shops on that block. this would make late game easier to navigate. you already do this when you zoom out. More shops on blocks, and never none. this just basically makes a road block I feel.More ways to make police happy... Also more policeOther gangs are not really a threat and just annoying.Cars need to be able to have more men in. its annoying when you have to move an army of men but due to treats the all travel at different speeds. maybe they can all get in a 4 door car and the best drives.other than that, it scratches that ADD itch in my brain

_childDocuments_.review: It's strictly a logistics game, the territorial stuff is basic and there are no other rackets other than selling and producing alcohol... you can carry out hits etc and it's very simplified, basically a bunch of modified dicerolls depending on weapon and skill levels, which I am cool with but it may not be ok to others. If they added more ways to make money, more quest variety and maybe more weapons and territorial strategy it would be really solid.But yeah, its basically a ups simulator, which I am ok with, so I give it a tentative thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Tried this game out as I've been trying to find a crime management game to play and whilst I was hooked in it for a while, it slowly started getting tedious later down the game. Pros:- The management layout is really fun and I've had a lot of fun figuring out how to start up new booze businesses which crept into getting a fully Luxurious Casino.- Fighting off other territories are fun as well, so long as your map doesn't pair you with 3 other outfits to fight against at the very start.- I very much appreciate the way automation works, however it could be better.Cons:- The overall UI and map could use a lot of work. It's quite clunky and overfed with information, quite a lot of them you won't need in the future. Though there are certain features that allows you to navigate through what you want to find, I would appreciate it if I don't see a gazillion of unused parked car icons and also if my notification bar would stop spamming me with people indebted to me (because there will be a ton of them when you start levelling up your casino).- Automation on gambling collections would be great. Collecting debts is quite good at the start however it becomes horribly tedious once you get near hundreds of people indebted to you. It also stops your casino from racking up a lot of cash if you don't collect them, hence you can't just ignore it.- Hiring new people and getting new skills are a pain because it's all through RNG. It becomes even more painful at the start since your characters are not fully established and there's not a lot of steps and actions you can do.Overall I feel that the game itself is good if you're into micro-managing games, this will definitely be a good game to try out. As of the time i'm writing this review, it seems that the devs are still working on this game so I hope they are able to update the game further.TLDR: *Points finger* Game is good, but it could be better!
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Be aware of what you are getting into! This game is not for everyone. More like a turnbased Crusaderkings but with a little less "flavour" (even though it's there in a decent amount. I would wish for a little more different faces and all around a tad bit more unnessecary details - even though the day and night cycle and seasons including snow are lovely so far) and a bit more business management in a big city mafia type setting instead of feudal europe, than anything else.A lot of negative reviewers seem to haven't been aware of that and base their verdict on their taste and don't review the game for what it is. The pricetag is a bit steep but fair nevertheless, the content packs sadly seem kind of necessary for a "full" experience in my view, therefore i recommend to pick it up as a package on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, really fun. Compared to some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gangster games that have been released these past few years, this one really doesn't try to be those but instead creates it's own genre of logistical gangster games. This ticks most of the boxes I love, however they could still fill in the gaps with political positions, a mafia hierarchy, and possibly more. However, the potential in this game is incredible, and I can't wait to see it in the future and it's journey.The replayability is also huge, everything regenerates when you use a new map completely and you can have an all new playstyle. This'll overall improve as the game proceeds. Otherwise, this is an extremely fun game that I've now spent the entirety of day 1 and early day 2 of release playing through my first playthrough.Definitely recommended to buy, if not for what already exists but what is to come. The devs have proven themselves competent in game-making (looking at their track record) and if they really put in enough time, effort, and good updates this game will become a gem amongst gangster games.Overall, 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only management game I've ever really gotten into. There is an initial learning curve, but expanding your operation is immensely satisfying and I'm having an amazing time.The scope is a bit limited -- the game is mostly about managing logistics, but is occasionally punctuated by well-coordinated violence. Still, if you look at my hours, I've found a lot to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the ideas here, but the implementation regrettably falls far short of being fun past the first couple of hours, after it turns out that what you see in those first couple define the rest of the game too. I appreciate and understand that it is set up as a tycoon game, but after 8 hours at it, a better label would be 'beer delivery boy'. An entirely undue amount of your time will be spent driving alcohol to customers, who may only want a small amount of it, and occasionally asking about potential new customers.The random map generation leaves a lot to be desired too, and the difficulty of the game varies really wildly based on it. Finding basic resources feels like it shouldn't require upwards of ten turns.The base here is sound enough that I think the developers could probably address and remedy the problems, but until such a time, I can't really recommend it, especially not with the time commitment it requires.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: going into this i already knew it was more about logistics management than gangsters but wowie. on the bright side i think a lot of the base mechanics are pretty good, albeit underdeveloped. the idea of corners is great, i think the turn based style actually works well, the idea of having all the characters interconnected and trading favors is all great, the buildings system is good (but should be much less random). BUT, i think the problems start to show themselves when you try to look deeper. for one there is a massive lack of information accessible to you, for example, there is no way to tell how you actually get favors other than vaguely getting them at random when you have a good relationship with a character, when you buy a car or weapon, it doesnt tell you any information about it and when you have them they sometimes dont even. the second biggest problem is how limited the other gangs and police are. enemies can barley be interacted with, the player literally only being able to attack them or truce them (in which case they will ask you to pay obscene amounts of money for the truce regardless of how much a war is going in your favor). enemies will randomly decide to destroy your territory or attack your people half way across town when their territory is not even near yours, police will just randomly decide to arrest your people taking away anything they had on them. and for some god forsaken reason, if you dont bribe police when someone is arrested, when they are jailed they still take up a character slot (which are already extremely limited) wasting the slot for literally half a full game length. lastly, the activities  you can do are also, you guessed it, very limited. you can either extort people, which requires you to mind numbly go to each corner you own asking for money (this cannot be automated), or automating a booze network, which i think is decently done, but still very clunky. no loan sharks, no smuggling, no gun running, no union or political things to mess with, no drugs. overall, this game can be summed up in one word, underwhelming.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: This is an ok game, but I will not recommend it considering the price and because 90% of people who see the title will be mislead.It's a business management game, with a main focus on logistics. The mafia part of it is just for flavour, you can attack a rival mobster in a single click to decide the outcome, but that's about it.For me personally I don't mind the lack of combat. The issue is that it doesn't feel thematic enough, I don't imagine myself running a criminal enterprise, or feel any pressure from rivalry (this isn't a difficulty problem, it's a gameplay problem).I'm not sure if the devs can make the game feel more real or not but as it stands, it's a No.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters is exactly as it is described here on this store page; a trading and resource management sim based around specifically the bootlegging aspects of prohibition era gangs. You will know this game is for you if, like me, you are OVERJOYED to see there is no shoehorned combat in this game. Complaints of early game tedium are valid but much like starting a new game of Factorio, you have to start out doing things for yourself. You quickly gain the ability to hire people and it opens up automated trade routes similar to Anno and the loop is very satisfying once you get up and running.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After couple months of not attempting to replay it anymore due to the crashes, tried downloading it again and play a new game, had loads of fun but crashed at the 6-7 hour mark, usually right at the time of it saving, so I suggest anyone that plays this should save often which I do but at some point it will crash and you will have to start over at a certain point, the irony is that it crashes as it saves. Really liked this game...spent about 160 hours+ on it which is way above my average with games in general. Then it started crashing all the time, re downloading it didn't work and sometimes the game functions just flat out stop working (Not able to complete conversations with characters or selecting buying/selling) Re tried it loads over the months but still would crash randomly. Would keep playing for sure if it works normally. Will recommend it for those into resource management with a hint of combat.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  Very impressed with the level of detail - number, types and upgrades of booze operations available, crew progression and traits, the favors mechanic, etc. I was hesitant to purchase it at first because it seemed to me to be more of a booze simulator rather than a gangster simulator.   I enjoyed Gangsters Organized Crime way back when and was looking for something similar.  I went ahead and purchased it on sale and wow I am glad i did!  There is plenty of gang on gang violence to be had as well as the ability to damage the store fronts of uncooperative shop owners to help them see things your way.  Many of the reviews complain of a lot of micromanagement. This is true so if you don't prefer games like that then probably best you stay away from this.  However if you are like me and don't mind some micromanagement do yourself a favor and get this game, you wont regret if you are looking for a solid 1920s prohibition era experience.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Building a gangster empire should be fun and exciting, and yet this game bores me to tears. The tutorial drags on forever and isn't helped by its text heavy nature--would investing in a narrator really have been out of the question? Given this game's regular asking price, I find that hard to believe.Clearly the budget was blown on art and making the maps huge...which with how threadbare the gameplay is, I struggle to understand why. I don't get the impression this was playtested. It's just not fun. The gameplay loop is tedious and uninteresting. Had the tutorial not taken me nearly 3 hours to get through I'd have strongly considered a refund.UI is also kind of a mess and not very well designed. It's a sad and poor showing for SomaSim, especially since I really enjoyed Project Highrise (their previous title).

Crew members can't be delegated to handle more mundane tasks such as material procurement or "protection" collections.Would love to see this company make another generation of this game in an RTS style where the focus becomes more macro management as the organization and territory controlled expands.

_childDocuments_.review: Love & HateI first got this game when it got released in 2021, From what it was to what is now is night and day.The Management is less to be desired, early and mid game its perfect but the end game bump is just annoying. Constant upkeep and micro-management just kills continuing a game after the 10 hour mark.  The Devs said the delivery and shipping system is meant to be flawed for "realism" but it kills all flow of gameplay.The storage on building fill up in no time, Its not even in the players control, its more like full of one or two items and it cant produce anything, then you resort to having a building just to store all items for another building, and that without saying how building prices are exponential. Profits are very linear. My suggestions is have limits the player can control for each item in the building.For the Casino, I like the idea and how its run but coming after 5 debters each turn make is a hassle. The Debt system is a great off put for acquiring buildings. Maybe have a second role in the Casinos as debt collectors and let the player choose what outcome for what they want, like Cash only mode / Credit increase, Land Acquirement or Alcohol and Favours.For the rival gangs they seem to be sticking to there own land and not coming after the player besides asking for help with there war, and to destroy a rival gang is too easy just find mob boss and kill him them poof there all gone. maybe adding a power struggle into the game like one big gang after the leader dies turns into smaller gangs that can fight for control of there old land.Theres a lot more i can say for this game, i have so much faith in the devs for this based off of there other game. I want to love this game because its a culmination of alot i like it management games. Im gonna keep a close eye to this game still after 80+ hours playing because i know it will get there and you should too.Love,Some Random with option
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: A business management game where you play bootleggers during the Prohibition.  It tries to sit between management game and RPG kind of like Crusader Kings 3 does, but there's actually very little roleplaying, so really you're just playing a management game entirely through moving pawns around the map and navigating dialogue trees. I can see the start of a cool strategy/RPG blend because there's relationship gauges, ways to get people to owe you favors, and relationship mechanics between characters, but it just doesn't do all that much with them since there's no story or events to hook them to. Like if you hire a business owner's relative to join your gang, their relationship with you will go up, but that's the beginning and end of it. You won't have friendships form, or be betrayed, or have your character get married even though there's a lot of opportunity for that kind of organized crime drama in the game. And on the other hand, there's the management side, which I said is managed pretty much entirely through dialogue trees. Mostly I just find myself driving back and forth between places selling booze and buying ingredients to make booze. It ended up feeling boring.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: After watching the game play by The_geek_cupboard, Pinstar and Drawing_pin, I was invested in the game play and style. This turn based game slows down the management aspect of the management sim so they you can attend to various issues, sales and requests at your own pace rather than being overwhelmed. while this game is enjoyable and I have played it to near completion achievement wise there are a few bug, glitches and issues as any game does, for instance I had an issue where the upgrade screen overrode the escape function and constantly showed the same upgrade screen despite clicking off to attend to a level up. The limitation of the four door sedan being unable to encompass at least 1 additional muscle seems a little odd but may be in place for balancing reasons. Finally I feel the COG encyclopedia is a little hard to navigate and doesn't flow well for new players attempting to figure out the next upgrade or missing prerequisite to proceed such as the speakeasy requiring the player to have at least 1 tier 2 operation. Overall I enjoy the style, speed and mechanics if a little shakey and look forward to future updates and expansions by the developers. Overall If you like a slower paced management sim this is highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game stinks on ice. It's more suited as a bus company simulator than a gangster game. I way overpaid and thought in time I would like it, but it goes nowhere and is more work than play. The turn based feature kills this game, and the fact that enemies come out of nowhere to give you cash suggests the developers know this. Without the freebies the game is unplayable, and while I can even enjoy paying a bad game, this isn't one of them. Pay no attention to my hours, this game has literally put me to sleep, and I just left it running. And more than once...
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game while it does have it charms. I have probably 20-30 afk hours on this minimum but 50 hours in I'm still far away from finishing a game as it's on a timer.Sure you do get playtime for your $ but what you actually do in this game is extremely limited. You can setup automation (routes) for your people to buy/sell pick up/drop ressources and automate production. The rest you select your characters and move them around buying and selling and moving products. The gang, war, combat whatever you want to call it is extremely limited.Capturing one street corner at a time is extremely limiting and eventually just breaks the flow. Not sure if it's meant to prevent you from capturing and steamrolling too much but the game is way to easy anyway.Killing other outfits requires 3-4 NPCs to kill and that can be done with 1-2 characters properly armed and systematically jsut going to each character and launching combat, sure, using all action points and injuries may slow you down but when you are done, you are done. 4 kills and you cleared out an entire crime family, taking over or breaking their fronts is useless.This game seems to be lacking so much gameplay wise that unless you are an optimizer, supply line freak, there's very little here for you. Sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters is a bootlegger simulator based in prohibition era USA, You start as a fresh immigrant in a family members' backroom growing your criminal empire by relationships, force, racketeering and of course bootlegging.The game is engaging as you start from your small corner of your chosen city and spread across them map corner by corner. There are plenty of beverages to brew with several tiers of increasing value(with increasing complex production chains) with the DLC there's politics and gambling too.You have ti deal with rival outfits, small time corner hoodlums and of course the coppers and the bureau of prohibition.CoG is a diamond in the rough, there are a few problems with automation, the clunky UI, tooltips are sometimes completely unhelpful and the AI isn't strong but despite this the immersion is great and if you can stand the late game micromanaging you'll have a lot of fun with this game.Another game where i'd love to see a polished sequel perhaps with even more criminal endeavours.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: There is almost never-ending strategizing needed to play this game. Being impulsive and beating someone up  is fun, sure, but you will be better off making some connections, paying off the police and driving around the city to see who has what to sell and buy.  The hardest part seems to be getting people to join your outfit and work for you, but once you have some men and women, you can plot a route on which they can buy materials and sell your booze. Meanwhile, you can negotiate with your brain or your brawn to help the family make some do ray mi.I can play the game for a couple of hours nightly and stay engaged.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: When you get too big it gets annoying and I cant build more because I am dealing with all the micromanaging. Also whats the point of having a repair truck building if I cant automatically repair my trucks there. Could there be an option to build a basement to increase storage. Could there be an option for my guys to big up all the alcohol i have in the building and sell it, it gets annoying when you have to select each 10 + liquors to be delivered. _childDocuments_.review: Good Game especially in early game. If you get good at it, you can really get the cash flow up which means you invest more, which means each turn becomes so complex to manage. As a result, I was never able to finish to prohibition before my empire became so big each turn would take 20 minutes of planning. I don't think you need all the expansions. Base game should be enough.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky as hell.If you enjoy clicking 5 things to get to what you need- multiple times a turn - on every character every turn - from your first turn to your last turn - this is your jam!Outside of that, it's also overpriced for what you get and needs a lot of work. I'm definitely glad I didn't try it before the 1.2 update because I can't imagine how bad it was before it reached the current state of development.Entire mechanics don't matter. Heat doesn't matter - if you're doing anything the cops will be all over it - so the existence of the mechanic is moot because you WILL end up paying off the cops.The clunky trade automation is moot without paying off the cops as well. Your people are too stupid to avoid them in high heat areas, so you'll pay off the cops or you'll pay the feds to botch investigations, or your crew will be in prison constantly and not doing their trade routes anyway.I like this type of game, and the beginning of the play through before it's just not worth how many clicks it takes to get through a turn is the best part. Eventually maybe it won't be a game about setting up clunky routes and toughing out the terrible UI - to get to a late game that's only about setting up more clunky routes and swapping crew around 5 clicks at a time - but right now it's just a mess.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: So here's the thing: this game is fun for the first bit of a play-through but you eventually run into a ridiculous amount of tediousness that can only be dealt with via a cumbersome "delivery"-type system. Couple this with the rarity of being able to buy buildings close enough together, but especially with auto-produced resources, that you're not running all over the place just to get the supplies needed to make even the simplest types of booze and you've got the most micro-management game on the planet. It's close to being a really fun game, but it gets absolutely killed by its tediousness and required micromanagement.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem. Quite a dry game (no pun intended) in the sense that it's heavy on management and light on "action", this is however by design and well understood. The mechanics blend together nicely and immersively and the DLC adds fair enhancement for the amount paid. If you enjoy heavy resource management then this is simply a must-have. It combines the Civ "just... one... more... turn..." addictiveness (and lack of time pressure) with Rimworld levels of "OMG what is this spawn?" (for better or worse) with train/transport simulator game levels of management of your logistics routes. My one cautionary note would be that the early game is a bit hit-miss, on some starts you can be scratching your head as to how with optimal play you're supposed to get things going, but for the types of player who this game should appeal to the most, they would either recognise this and start a new spawn quickly, or embrace the brutality of the bad start.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game as it seemed interesting, and it is, just not in the right ways. The game's extremely chance-based and you might end up starting over a few times just because you're put in a position that's impossible to even start off from.I've got 6 hours into the game and had a territory taken away without any sort of fight taking place, so I reloaded the game to a point before that happened, but the territory is still gone. Now I no longer have the will to continue playing at all.Only buy on a massive discount, if you do it at all. It's not worth the regular price.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It's a short burst of fun at the beginning but will become tiresome because there is a frustrating lack of information that prevents planning for the mid to late stages of the game. Starting out as a small time boss means that there is a lot to discover about running your criminal empire - sadly there is almost no help in finding out what the next level of booze is and how to unlock it. So many traditional methods for finding this information (a game encyclopedia, an online wiki, etc.) is absent of any actual details that it becomes frustrating trying to advance and develop your empire. This causes the gameplay to stall as you grind for more knowledge about other booze, where to sell it, and finding the materials to make it.What's even more upsetting is that this is clearly a game design decision that eschews reality - why would a bootlegger not know about all the available alcohol in the country or region and hope to one day become more than a backroom beer brewer? Isn't there a hope to be a respectable whiskey distiller who runs a nightclub speakeasy? Like, there are visible achievements listed for running a dining hall/supper house/eatery but nowhere is that knowledge documented in-game or out. If it weren't for the achievements, you wouldn't know about the late game stuff at all.On top of this is a reputation system that doesn't seem to represent reality - as a bootlegger bringing liquid joy to the dry masses, I am apparently unknown to everyone outside of a 1 block radius of the bars I operate. The Police know and constantly raid them (unless you pay them off every dozen turns or so) but even "advertising" your gin joints does nothing to inform people or build a relationship. You can be the literal only gang in town, having murdered dozens of other mobsters to build an empire that spans the city but Barbara the grocer still hasn't heard of you and needs some money to trust you. Intimidation means nothing and having 2 notorious hitmen visit her means the same as an accountant trying to buy apples.The end result is a game that struggles to be more than a grind with no ability to plan growth because you won't have access to the knowledge of finer alcohols, better bars/venues, gang member leveling improvements (or what the next stages of a trait develops into), etc. The game is operating in a deliberate lack of detail and seems to want players to grind instead of play.I recommend skipping the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10: Great idea for a game, but the ultimate lack of direction and defeating of every other gang makes  a snoozefest. May very well be the only management game in which ol' Il Pallino scaled-back his gang activities near the end for the sole sake of making the turns go faster. The review would have been a four, except that a gambler managed to hit the jackpot despite the game inferring there was a 0% chance of this happening.The turned-based tedious nature of  can be described as the following: First the player feels powerless starting out for the first few years only able to make one low quality variety of booze, then once the player flips the difficulty curve, the player is stressed trying to get supplies to illegal booze manufacturers due to all of the new buildings the player is either likely to accumulate through either their gang's Accountant or citizens who owe gambling debts.  puts too much emphasis on the business side of running a gang by making combat limited and enemies flawed by often ignoring gang wars. (In the last gang war, the members of the opposing gang didn't try to seek out ol' Il Pallino's gang members, they just went about their business as usual.)The graphics are on the simple side, but the brick buildings do create a nostalgic feel that transports the player back into the 1920's.The sounds are all perfect for the game with the exception of the music. The music encountered is on the very tame side of 1920's Jazz music, and only helps to make the player even sleepier than what the boring, repetitive gameplay provides.The idea of allowing gang members to become officers is a good idea, but the requirements for an Accountant are flat out annoying! While it isn't difficult to switch out managers in a building so that building improvements can be (instantly) purchased, it sure is stupid and annoying! Another requirement is that a would be Accountant needs to produce one thousand units of any sort of alcohol. This is problematic because on ol' Il Pallino's first playthrough, he decided to make an aunt an Accountant because she already produced a thousand loads of liquor, and whenever he needed this Accountant to run a scheme to acquire a new building, this gang member had to be pulled out of her building assignment and put into a car.Some players may appreciate the fact that racism and sexism do not exist in , but there's bound to be a player who resents the idea of seeing a woman in the 1920's driving a delivery truck like a man and mowing down enemies with a Tommy Gun like a man. (Note: Ol' Il Pallino believes that there are women tough enough to drive big trucks and fight IRL... Even some that are heterosexual!) Ol' Il Pallino personally felt like Blacks should have at least counted as a different ethnicity since racism was very much a thing in the 1920's. (Even outside of the southeastern United States! Irish and Italian gang members receive bonuses for dealing with other people of their own ethnicity, but do not have to put up with the same discrimination and hate that Irish and Italian immigrants in the United States experienced in the 1920's.)On the issue of gang members, they have more in common with teamsters than criminals... Unless maybe a gang member is selling booze to a local business or is extorting a business to agree to pay to belong to a protection racket. Otherwise, gang members are frequently going to be purchasing legal products to supply their illegal operations.The traits that gang members can have are often complimentary to each other, and can make a gang member either ideal as a soldier, explorer, teamster, building manager, or booze retailer. Sadly, the same cannot be said for the three traits that the main character has. The player has to pick a description that contains three traits when the player should be allowed to just pick whatever the heck traits they find most useful.Corner Hooligans are interesting in a way and provide a unique challenge, but can be annoying. Corner Hooligans interested in business will "find" stuff to sell to the player which is usually of use, but after awhile, offers for crowbars, baseball bats, and cars can be annoying. business-minded Corner Hooligans can be paid $800 to join the player's gang (if enough space for a new gang member is available) which is good, because Corner Hooligans start out beyond the first level, which will be necessary when the player is looking to make high-end booze. (More on that in a minute.) Corner Hooligans interested in brawling cannot be removed through non-violent means. Ol' Il Pallino tried using a favor to increase relations with such a Corner Hooligan and then paid that Corner Hooligan to attack a rival gang, but the elevated relationship level meant nothing in the end. Of course, Corner Hooligans can all be killed, but everyone is related to someone on the map, and one of those people could be someone the player frequently does business with that the player will lose as a buyer or seller. The resentful person may even be a police officer who the player will be unable to bribe for the rest of the game who's beat may just happen to be where the player has a gambling house.The experience system for building managers is messed up. Building managers only earn experience after a batch of liquor has been made. This works alright for buildings producing low grade crap, but the player can forget about leveling-up managers overseeing the production of high grade booze.The biggest gripe, is that the only incentive to make lots of alcohol is merely for chasing achievements. Once these achievements are earned, there's no logical reason to continue aggressively earning money. (A sign of a poorly made management/tycoon game.) In four decades of gaming, this is the only time ol' Il Pallino can remember a game in the same genre where the player will scale back their operations for the mere sake of finishing the game.Far from a good game, but ol' Il Pallino is set on trying to sweep all of the achievements. If the player doesn't have Asperger's as bad as ol' Il Pallino (or lots of good music to play in the background) the player could potentially die of boredom.(And hopefully not the last words of Il Pallino!)This review has been provided independently by an admin at .This game was gifted by a friend.Email contact@dnbmedia.co for requests & promotions.

The game is perfect those who wants to flex their logistic brain instead of running around town gunning down everyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know what to find of this game. It had me intrigued before it came out but it has not been able to quite live up to my expectations. Basically City of Gangsters is a game which just revolves around having a set amount of resources and money (which is actually pretty hard to get by sufficiently) in order to make illegal alcoholic beverages. You can then sell these products to people around the city in order to gain respect, favors and money. It does not really evolve much further than that. There is an occasional rival nearby which can try to attack you and prevent you from buying and selling the products you wish. You can then try to scare them or kill them in a rather unsatisfying form of combat. During combat (or rather, before you attack) you select which weapon to use and who to attack (not that there is any form of multi-person combat) to then learn how many damage you did to the other person. This is not at all satisfying. To be honest, it feels as if this game is some kind of interactive novel that is missing pages and details about basically everything. I won't be playing this game anymore until some major updates and expansions have come along.

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining management game by a very responsive developer featuring a colorful time in American history...prohibition. It loaded up fine, and at 76 hours in I've found no bugs. The release version features 4 cities in which to build your empire....Chicago (of course), Detroit, Pittsburgh, and Cincinnati.  All of them are immense, literally hundreds of corners to take over in each. The game has weekly turns, and last from June, 1920 to the end of Prohibition in 1933, although you can keep playing. The best I've done so far is 12 corners by the one year mark.  The forum features a thread with some excellent starting seeds.I would highly recommend this game as well worth the price. It will hold your attention with tons of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: OK so while I do recommend this game it comes with a BUT! It is a decent game, good amount of options for making illegal booze (the main theme, it is during prohibition after all), you can build a crew and level them up to suit there roles better, take over turf, start gang wars, pay off the cops, etc. BUT...If you are looking for deep strategy, real time game play, expect it to be similar to Gangsters: Life of Crime, or have modern graphics, well then it probably won't be for you. The main theme is you start with a bit of old booze and a backroom in your uncle's business. Generally the business will produce one of the main ingredients you need to start your first bootleg operation. So goal one find people to buy the existing booze and make enough money to invest in a bootleg operation in the back of your uncle's business. Next goal is to find enough people selling mason jars (known as stoneware crocs in game) to package the booze from your bootleg operation. Once you have a supply it will start producing bootleg booze every 4 to 7 weeks/turns (depends on the type). OK so now you have a booze supply and know who to sell it too, so next plan is to expand your turf. Goal 3 find "friends" in good business locations that owe you a favor and let them know you want them to operate as a front for you. This will cost you some money, but once done you can start to extort other business on the same corner for "protection" money. This part is key since to expand further they need money and that money comes from the protection fees paid by others. Any money not used up is saved for you to pick up at your leisure. And that's pretty much it you are off and running. You will encounter lots of missions/requests from business owners they are how you will learn new skills, gain special vehicles, etc. You will also encounter the police who you can build a relationship with and eventually pay off. And you will encounter local thugs that are causing trouble, as well as organized outfits that are competitors to you. Cooperate or fight, the choice is yours.

_childDocuments_.review: first of all this game is not "violence" focused. if you're looking for action or fights, CoG does not really deliver. Fights are just a tool to take care of competition or create problems for your rivals. it is not the main focus of the game. you can play the game without killing anyone. More than anything this game should be named as City of Bootleggers / Bootlegging Tycoon, but here we are. The game is more like a illegal business tycoon sim, and nothing similar like Omerta or Empire of Sin.That being said the main focus is to make money and the expansion of your territory. It has a heavy business/management feel to the game, where you are required to be smart in your choices to invest in the product you want to sell, and make choices as who to sell or buy from to gain the most benefit. Selling your goods not only gives you money but gives you reputation with a shop/company. The reputation give you favors, which you can exchange it for other things that will help. This is all done as a bootlegger in prohibition era. Also the supply chain aspect of this game can start rather simple, but once you diversify your product sold, it will be quite complex. There is the idea of expanding your territory. You can extort businesses in your territory for protection money as an extra income, but it will never be enough, so it is safe to say that making and selling alcohol is main money maker.However there are other bootleggers (AI) also trying to make money this way and how you deal with the competition is also another part of the game. You can sic your muscle and kill them. You can intimidate them or pay off cops/hooligans to harrass them. Otherwise the main focus is just to grow / maintain your cash flow. While you can go around killing people, it can turn a lot of business away and it will impact your money making. Businesses will not buy/sell to you if they don't like you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a great resource management game, though it is a little rough around the edges. I really love the setting and the progression -- starting with one building and a small cache of illegal booze, you must build yourself an empire. By mid-game, you're running with a proper crew in a sizable territory. Many of your crew will work deliveries, making sure your production buildings have what they need to produce booze. Some of your other crew will manage the buildings, perfecting their craft so they don't need as many resources or so they produce more booze. The rest of your crew is probably your muscle, protecting your deliveries and fronts or aggressively attacking rival crews. While all of this is very fun, it also gets very repetitive. By mid-game, you'll probably start to get bored and want to start over. You'll have so much money and your only option to spend it is to invest in things that will make you even more money. That sounds fun, but in the end, you don't really feel like you're working toward anything.As for the "rough around the edges" I mentioned earlier, the game seems unoptimized despite the scope. Many of the cities or ethnicities you can play are specialized for one kind of booze, yet it's completely random what your starting legit business produces. (Usually, you'll have a legit business that produces something useful to making booze -- like grapes for wine or apples for hard cider.) In addition, you'll often find yourself placed in a part of the city with absolutely no nearby access to universal resources -- like no pipes or bricks, which you need to upgrade nearly all buildings. That kind of roadblock means you'll have to spend a lot of time sending your people across the map to buy and deliver items everyone needs. And you typically don't learn you're having that problem until you've spent a few hours building your starting area, which can feel like you've just wasted a lot of time.I don't mean to bring up these problems to dissuade you from buying the game. I mean it when I say it's a really fun resources management game. I just think everyone should have as much info as possible before they dive in!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like turn based strategy games like Civilization games, but based in the 1920's during the prohibition, then this is definitely the game for you. The graphics are simple but fun. It keeps you sucked in and involved because, at every turn, something is bound to happen. You need to stay on your toes if you dare to compete with the other Outfits who have that same entrepreneurship, ambition, and drive as you do, to give you that leg up, on the competition. I bought this game and I'm glad I did. This game has so much packed into it! Pay off the cops so they look the other way as you build your Alcoholic Empire, hire new muscle, managers, delivery people, mechanics, and rank them up as you go about your business learning the tricks of the trade! What are you still doing reading this! GO BUY THE GAME ALREADY AND SPEND HOURS OF FUN ENJOYING THE PURCHASE YOU MADE!!! I KNOW I AM! Goodluck!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking for a prohibition era crime sim/management game for the longest time and unfortunately this attempt is not the answer for me. I play Paradox games and this is a menu heavy nightmare for me. I cant get into the repetitive dialogue which is required for every single transaction. Buy/sell should not require as many button presses as it does. I could see this being fun if I were more interested in the RPG elements as the game allows you and as a game mechanic forces you to get to know the characters you interact with. Personally, I would rather take over the city than continually help my cousin by catering his birthday parties for JUST ONE more person to sell to. Not the worst game out there and if you don't have any problems with what i just described you could have a good time. Not for me.

All in all, a great game. Happy bootlegging!Edit 6/4/2022They added gambling now so you can you have your own poker room among other betting vices. But the combat is lacking and the cat house is non-existent still. But still a good game, just don't expect "gansters", it's simply not. It is however still bootleggers.

_childDocuments_.review: I got it on sale for ~$12 and it's worth it for that much. However, after 50 hrs it's getting pretty redundant and the economy system is a little jacked up.  I don't know if I'm  gonna finish a play  through at this point, because the  turns keep  getting  longer, and the prices are getting outrageous early in the game. I'm about 170 turns into one game where I've pretty much saturated the market for brickwine, and cider. I haven't  made a bootlegger yet, but I wanted to make different alcohols, as there  are a lot of beer and sparkling  cider places around. So I made a sparkling cider op and then decided to open a beer spot. Together they cost about $20k just  for the property! What's next? Is it gonna be $20k to open another beer place? It gonna start costing 6 figures? Why is the housing market jumping 10x where it started 3 purchases ago? Also Charging 5  movement  points to drive thru a new block is overkill and doesn't make much sense. Each turn is supposedly a week; so  it takes your character(s) a week to explore  2-3 blocks? A person  could  crawl on their hands a knees  and get further than that in a day.  I understand  they use it to pace the game, but it's  too  much, considering  the lack of available distributors. It could  take you a 3-4 months to find someone that  sells  what  you  have.... I'm 50 hrs in on  one game and haven't even seen half the map  yet! I have  6 drivers, still no time!

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun. Challenging at times, but fun none the less. Figuring out how to get Canadian business started up can be fun. How to remove a rival without damaging future business opportunities can be quite challenging. Ex. I took down a female gangster who had one family member. However I never looked at that one family member. That one family member had family members that controlled over a third of the malt supply in the city. Do I need to say how big of an "oh crap" moment I had when every dealer I went to for several districts all said we don't want to deal with the likes of you? It took me about a half an hour to figure out how it came to be. I was mad enough I started a new game. It can be worked past but it is not easy to do and it takes quite a bit of time and tracking down known associates of each one to get them to recommend you and earn the favor levels back high enough to do business again. This game does not forgive screw ups easily, your rivals only need one good chance to take you down. Thinking is required to play this game well. Sure you can just kill everyone off. But they all have family and friends. Actions have consequences. There are other ways to get the same result but not have it point at you. You just have to figure it out and, in some cases, wait for it to come available as an option. How to talk to your people could be a bit more obvious. It is on their player id page at the very bottom is a tiny speech button you can push. So if it tells you to talk to so and so about doing this job that is where to look. Took me a while to find where to look. SCHEMES TAKE FOREVER AND A DAY when your captains do them. Like as in over 20 turns to acquire one new business with my accountant. Be prepared. But yeah, its a lot of fun, but it can give you a good challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't decide if I like this game or not.So what's there is good. You have somewhat well rounded production chains, you have tons of weighty decisions to make with a limited number of resources and actions per turn and you have decent rewards for actions done. The core of the game is accumulating favors from people that you then cash in to get something. You have a decent chance of accumulating a favor with any positive interaction, and you can spend favors on tons of things.The game is also primarily a management game. Combat is sticky and honestly kind of unrewarding, and as much as this is a hot take I think that was a great decision. Early combat is hand to hand, so fights mean everyone gets hurt and it doesn't really solve your problem. It's better to intimidate and talk people down. The management is also great with gang members being either operatives or managers. Managers have some a significant on the businesses they manage and operatives roam around with a million things to do between balancing your needed resources, doing missions, running errands, exploring, and occasionally even fighting. The core gameplay loop, that is interacting with your duders and doing the tasks is solid. So the problem is balance and variety. I would say a lot of parts of this are horrendously balanced. Here are 4 ways of making money:1.) Casinos: To get a casino you need a skill that lets you build one. This takes time to get, as you'll need to do a number of favor missions to get it. Then you need to establish the location, get a manager, build each individual game in the casino (The size of the casino dictates how many games you run, the lowest level is like 4-5 games), and then keep a minimum amount of cash in the casino. The casino kind of acts like a bank, in that it's mostly a place to keep funds that can then accumulate value slowly. At the lowest level expect like $100 a turn with 3 games running. I would say that you're probably going to need 100 turns at that rate to pay back the probably $10,000 it costs to start the casino. You'll also need to go track down people that run up too high of a debt in the casino, which gives you money or goods to sell usually. All of this takes at minimum like 8 turns to make, with 2-4 turns per game added.2.) Liquor production: Get a building. Now build in that building, a liquor still. The still then needs resources, get resources. Now you've made the liquor, sell it to shops. Shops accept varying amounts per commodity sold, which isn't labeled at the outset. So when you go to sell something, you then figure out if you need to go other places or not. Randomly, you'll find some place that will accept 100s of cases of liquor. The low level liquor returns like $8-12 per item, with resources needed from 2 source buildings. If you're smart you've built your first building on one of those source buildings so you only need 1 recipe item to be bought from elsewhere. That usually is going to run you about under 100$ per load of liquor produced. So you're making around 4k per load every 5 or so days. Tier 2 liquor requires tier 1 liquor and a whole other list of things, but sells for about $20 per commodity item... and so on and so fourth.3.) Foreign Liquor from contacts: Favor mission pops up with the random german baker that is in your territory. He asks for $250. You actually don't have to give him $250, you can give him less and it just impacts how much foreign liquor you get. For every favor you have with this guy, he'll give you between like 10-20 commodity items of liquor that sells for 20+. Take that to a place that buys it and get $2000.4.) Extortion: Set up a front in a legitimate buisness. Get that front to expand your territory by paying them a small amount. After a few turns they do, and you can go extort in that new section of territory they expanded to. Now, repeat. This pays out about once every 4 turns, under 100 per front. You could with a great map spawn have 5 fronts cover 20 corners, which would mean about $500 per 4 turns. TBH this isn't cash you use in practice. I use it as petty cash my operatives can get on the way to do something else.Options 1 and 2 take multiple turns to do. Option 3 takes 1 turn and about 5 minutes. Since Option 3 is more map dependent and random though, you may get like 3 people in your territory that give you liquor like this, you may get 20. It really kind of undercuts any need to go into liquor production when it's such a quick and easy payout.So you have easy money that can be made like that, and extremely fiddly money that can be made besides that supports a greater network of items.This is all... Fine. Ish. But, what I described is also the entirety of the crime you can do. Produce Liquor, open casino banks, favor cash items, and extort money from businesses by growing your territory. So it's a newish game, the devs are continuing support, etc. etc. but the first new mechanic, Casinos (The banks I mentioned earlier) were a DLC. The volume of things not covered here makes this a problem. There's no prostitution, no real smuggling outside of favors, no need to clean money, no selling of arms, no stealing, no real interaction with other gangs practically speaking, and while I could keep going here I think you get the point. Will all of those be dolled out in DLC as well?So in scoring I'm docking 1 point for balance, 1 point for variety, and 1 point for the Monetization model. I'm hesitant about dropping it lower, because honestly I do enjoy this title greatly... but it's closer to a 6 than an 8 for me. A lot of promise, it's far better than a lot of gangsters games to come out in the last 2 decades, just... it's not sticking the landing.Overall score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a good game. Very micro-managey and very booze-centric when it comes to crime. _childDocuments_.review: As a kid, I spent hours with Gangsters: Organized Crime.In a ray of naive hope, I saw Omerta: City of Gangsters as a return to form, to be sorely disappointed.I was incredibly excited for Empire of Sin, to be badly let down again....And from the swamp of sadness, came City of Gangsters.A very challenging, but rewarding game, where you feel like an actual Don, running an empire, collecting 'Protection Money', managing Speakeasies and 'whacking' your enemies.This is easily the best Mafia strategy game since gangsters, no question.

_childDocuments_.review: In the spirit of the original GANGSTERS (1998) by Hothouse, this mafia operations SIM is fantastic!  Plan your mafia dirty work, then work your plan with the team and/or family you recruit into your operations.  From finance decisions to what booze you should hustle, you build your mafia empire over time.  The ability to auto-distribute, as well as modify automation on the fly, with assigned routes makes it easier to focus on "the dirty work" rather than the day-to-day maintenance and upkeep of resources.  The different skills and attributes for all characters is good (and hopefully will expand), and the relationship building needed to build a large, mafia social network is exceptional. The Kasedo game team continues to work many of the bugs and kinks, as well as detailed descriptions of the patches and how it impacts game play.  I believe the team will continue to do so as they have proven responsive throughout the release so far.  A MUST for any fan of SIM and/or Mafia style games.

_childDocuments_.review: To start this is just a business management game with very little to do with gangsters.Took me a few hours of painfully maintaining supply of 3 different types of booze before I even realised there was an automated delivery system. THANK GOD ! I was sick to death of buying crockpots. Oh no wait, the deliveries system is massively broken so now Im forced to do it all manually. Its effort trying to remember which stores sell what, theres a handy UI feature that highlights which stores sell various supplies, HOWEVER as soon as you move to one store its removed. I have to go to like 4 or 5 shops per turn to get yet more crockpots, having to turn this feature on 3 or 4 times is just tedious. Same thing happens when you then need to sell resources.I can barely manage the small operation I have now, theres no chance Ill be able to when I expand.The games fun for the first hour or so, then it fast becomes tedious. _childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting little niche title with some potential, but I have to stress that it is immensely tedious.The 1920s era gangland setting is interesting, the art style is quaint, the music is thematic and it has all the elements of a tycoon/4x game for people to enjoy.  However, getting any of those elements running is a MASSIVE factor of RNG.First of all, your start location being randomized is a crapshoot.  You may spawn in a location with the ability to produce booze that no one will buy.  You may spawn in an area with no easy access to materials to make booze.  You may spawn without the ability to make booze in the first place.  That's just a hard reroll.Then you have elements like police and rival gangs.  If you spawn in an area with 2 police precincts, that's a reroll.  If you spawn in an area with a hostile gang, that's a reroll.  If you somehow manage to hit the jackpot and get a start that isn't terrible, you might not get a good spread of businesses to use as fronts.  That's a reroll.There's just too much RNG inherent in this game for me to recommend.  It's not fun to reroll constantly for a viable start, or to play through only to find on turn 100 your little empire isn't going to make it.  This is not fun, this is not challenging, it's just numbers.

_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: Game's great. It's not for everyone, it's a business/logistics sim more so than a strategy sim, and combat plays less of a role than resource management. Which obviously is not what everyone is looking for in a game about gangsters. You into micromanagement? If not, then maybe pass on this.But if you're into slower-paced (it's turn-based, so you have plenty of time to min/max), micromanagement games, this'll probably do it for you.The game's also surprisingly deep. And hard. Its' relationships, favours, profit and automation mechanics are all something you need to keep in mind, all while defending your territory from rival gangs. There's always something you forget, which ends up biting you late into the game. Like unknowingly killing your local beat cop's sister, because she happened to join a rival gang that you've been at war with, and now your cover from the precinct is gone, and you're getting raided every few turns.I will say the early game (before you control 5 blocks and hire your first crew member) can be kinda dry. You're just opening up the map, starting to build relationships, getting a sense of what your starting business logistics will be, and trying to run a profit off a single basement bootleg. But like I said, plenty of people are into the lots-to-think-about-slow-pace-every-turn-counts-numbers-are-fun stuff. Like myself.One flaw is the beginning tutorial covers how to do things, but not why, or when. And since the game's so mechanically dense, if you skip the tutorial you're bound to get frustrated. The game doesn't hold your hand. There are some , though.My only real con against the game (beyond having a steep learning curve and thin tutorial), is that SomaSim put out DLCs for only 5 of the core available nationalities, which means those 5 will always have a [sometimes small] advantage over the other , and incentivizes the player to always pick one of those 5. It's never an OP advantage, but it's notable.If SomaSim put out a new DLC that gives the other nationalities the same attention as the first 5, I'd buy it in a heartbeat.Also kind of wish we could add whichever DLC systems we want to whichever map we want, but they're locked to their own specific maps. Which isn't a huge deal, but what if I want to play with  DLC systems at once? Can't be done.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is strictly a business management sim, and a really good one. The negative reviews are either from people who bought a game without paying attention to what they were buying, or who don't like the dice-roll heavy RNG aspect (which is fair). City of Gangsters delivers exactly what it promises - a business management board game about the prohibition era, and is engaging, thoughtful, and has a ton of variety. The only real downside I can call out is that there's a lot of RNG in how good your starting location/setup are, you can start with phenomenal resources and connections and get rich right off the bat, or you can languish in poverty for 4 years before getting a start. I've had fun with both kinds of start though!Here are some facts to help you determine if it's for you:Turn-basedIncredibly abstracted combat, no visible violenceActor-based - you control a number of individual actors that move around the city in limited fashion each turn. For example to sell moonshine you need a crew member to visit the place it's stored, pick it up, drive it to someone who will buy it, and unload it.Wide variety of starting conditions but chosen randomly - you should be ok with either playing the role of a struggling startup with nothing to its name, or re-rolling new games until you get a good setup.Very Boardgame-yRNG-heavy - you cannot always get the best outcomes or options and you will have to adjust your strategy based on your luck. The upside here being that there's no one build order/strategy that you'll return to every time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be brilliant but right now three things are holding it back. 1) The combat  - violence and force is an important part of any gangster game.  Here it is deeply one-dimensional and underwhelming.  So much more could be done with it.2) The micro-management seems endless and becomes just a grind -  And I'm someone who likes 'grindy' games! 3) There isn't enough depth in general - you can bribe the police but what about local politicians? Diplomacy - what about being able to set one neighbouring gang against another? The cloak and dagger side of things?  What about illegal trades other than alcohol? - Robberies? Heists? Prostitution? So it feels a bit bare bones and repetitive right now but COULD be amazing with more work.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I was buying a Mafia/Mob based strategy game, instead found myself playing a 1920's courier simulator. The main game-play loop is transporting one resource to a location in order to access another resource which you need to produce a third, etc, etc. There is nothing about this game that particularly feels like running a gang in Prohibition era America, in fact I would have mistaken this for a run of the mill business management game if it wasn't for the text telling me I doing something apparently illegal. Expanding your territory is a similarly boring process too, whats more you are expected to make all the collections as well which means all you play time is spent on micromanagement. I felt less like Al Capone and more like a milkman making his rounds  Part of the problem Is down to aesthetics, its a very bloodless game, combat is very unimpactful and I was left feeling it was rather perfunctory affair. I didn't expect much from the games graphic, this being an indie title and all, but the cartoonish art style betrays the setting, there is none of the grit you would expect from a game called City of Gangsters. Not every game has to be a blood-fest, not every game about crime has to emulate GTA, but when the subject matter IS violence and vice it seems strange at how coy the developers are in depicting it, a better title would have been Bootlegger cus that's all you do.

_childDocuments_.review: To quote a friend: The thing I like most about CoG is that there are a dozen different answers to the question "What should I do next?" and the design lends itself to lots of emergent narrative moments that play into the prohibition-era gangster motif - like maybe you're short on cash that you need urgently when you suddenly remember one of your bootleg operations or fronts you've been neglecting so you swing by and discover a whole trove of money. Or maybe you spot a friend some money so their uncle can open a new cold storage business, then they find a locked storage closet in the basement and you get them some crowbars to crack it open and you find an old stockpile of hundreds of casks of moonshine, literally more than your warehouses can hold - so much that it stops production of your actual business operations because there's nowhere to store the products, so you need to have a big-ass fire-sale where you drive around the entire city unloading truck after truck of moonshine.What makes it cool is that none of that is really done through dialog or the player being told much about it, it's direct interaction with the (abstracted) mechanics. That makes it a great game to tell and hear stories from. It nails the feel of the role and the time period, it just doesn't do it in flashy Hollywood ways. It's not The Godfather, it's just the story of some person in the 1920's getting rich bootlegging moonshine.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game. I downloaded it when it first came out and really enjoyed the first few hours. However, the Delivery system was a source of a lot of frustration. I wanted to create a perfect delivery route that would allow everything to be exactly on time for production, but I found it impossible. The game was unclear how long it took for NPC's inventories to restock, requiring several turns of experimentation. The timing of deliveries seemed inconsistent with the mechanics of the rest of the game, as my delivery driver would only make one stop in a turn despite theoretically having more movement/action points. If the delivery system were improved to be easier to use, I would 100% recommend this game, but as it stands I can not.
_childDocuments_.name: City of Gangsters

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters is a game about selling booze in 1920s America. It's not about shooting people in the streets, nor about a number of other criminal ventures. It's possible to fight other gangsters, it's possible to do a bit of racketeering and you get to shark some loans if you get an appropriate mission, but that is largely window dressing. This game is about selling lots of booze and getting as rich and respected as possible before the prohibition is lifted.While this single minded focus may put a lot of people of and I hope to see criminal ventures expanded, I enjoy building and optimizing supply lines, building trust with the locals, placating officers of the law and steadily expanding my business. The one thing that holds the game back in my eyes is the randomisation of the maps and starting conditions. A good seed will pose interesting challenges and provide you with the means to overcome them, but a bad seed might leave you bored and without apparent challenge just as well as it might present you with an insurmountable cliff for a starting challenge.Example I: I started the game close to the border of a residential and an industrial district, with a business generating malt syrup, the knowledge to make homebrew beer and stupendous amounts of businesses around to sell beer to. I could not conceivably sell enough beer to meet demand, there were 3 suppliers of malt syrup within 2 blocks of my HQ and lots of social connections between the NPCs guiding me from one customer to the next. There was basically no challenge at all.Example II: I started the game in an industrial district with a business producing furniture and surrounded by nothing other then garages and car dealers with not interest in either my starting supply of booze nor furniture for several blocks and next to no social connections between the npcs in the area.Such a start might be fine for a challenge run later in the game, but it's hardly conventionelly fun.My currently ongoing game instead started in a mixed area with pockets of NPC who knew each other, a starting business that provided resources to start brick wine production and moderate interest in said product around the neighbourhood. Enough to get me started, but certainly not enough to carry me through the game. I had to hustle for other types of booze, use the social mechanics to open new markets and everything clicked into place to make that "just one more turn" game that kept me up well past any reasonable bed time.I think the game would benefit greatly from certain brakes put on the random generation and make sure spawns meet certain conditions, to more reliably create the kind of interesting game the last example provided me with.Because frankly I see two types of negative reviews here atm: Those of people who had vastly different expectations, and those of people who probably got served a position as described in my first two examples.Either way: City of Gangsters to me is a good game most of the time and a great one at the best of times. It just needs its greatness to be made more reliably accessible and could benefit from loosening the focus over time to include more types of businesses.
