_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr The game is a good deal on discount but no longer in development so buyer beware (I got it for 9 USD). it is mildly entertaining for those who enjoy economy building games. It suffers from some poor design choices I outline below, I was hopeful developers would continue to expand the gameplay and rebalance stats, but they posted in the discussion that they are no longer developing this which is a real shame.I came to this game based on other reviews comparing it to Gangsters: Organized Crime (which I loved growing up). It definitely has a lot of these elements in play, and there is considerable depth but the game needs to me modded heavily for playability. I believe with refinement in the stats, better manual/guidelines, and some additional gameplay elements it could be a great game. Right now it suffers from a the following in my opinion:1) Very poor information on profitability of different enterprises and basic game mechanics (gambling, booze , territory etc.), in the game it is very difficult to figure out if something will make you money before you set it up and play out many turns. As others have commented, you will restart your game often at first when you realize your booze/gambling venture is a waste of time. You essentially have to trial and error with punishing costs to time/$ if you change your mind. This means a big time suck just to figure out how to play. Other players have put together spreadsheets to help guide you in this, but they are incomplete, and can be out of date with current versions. 2) Needless complexity, there are simply way too many options in terms of different liquors, beer, wine, supplies etc. The tiers of production are good, but they should be significantly consolidated (we don't need dozens of different kinds of alcohol!) for ease of play. Ditto for the supply chains. It makes micromanagement of supply runs a nightmare in mid/late game. Additionally the complexity in booze options brings little variety to the game. Meanwhile, there are no other businesses to get involved in, racketeering, prize fightings, brothel, counterfeit money, theft and smuggling are absent. Also buying legitimate businesses should generate income as well. 3) The % increases in cost of everything as the game progresses makes the mid/late very grindy and tedious. Its a cheezy mechanic on developers part. 4) The AI is very passive and easily beaten, I found one of the more profitable things is to attack another outfit, get a truce request from them (for $$$) and break the truce (for no apparent penalty?), rinse repeat. 5) The cops mechanic is dumb and tedious. Basically you have to bribe them continually or they will wreak havoc on your business, the heat mechanics are pointless because if you do not bribe cops they will harass your team not matter how careful you are within a few turns of the game start. Its essentially a required cost every 6 months or so in game, and adds little interest or variety.6) The gambling houses are fun to set up, but again very little info on how best to make money with these, and you can find that you lose a HUGE amount of money setting these up and watching customers win jackpots. 7) Expanding territory is janky. Basically you set up a front but it can only expand 1 square in any direction, but the streets are not perfect grids, so some fronts only expand 1-3 squares, while others 4 (you learn through error, this is not made clear at all). The result of this is your territory expands in a funny inorganic way as you only put fronts on spots with 4 square expansion options. I think this could be solved mostly if they allowed fronts to reach 2 squares in any direction.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 8/10 - Nothing groundbreaking, but very stylistic for which they deserve credit. Sound: 3/10 - Good quality but repetitive and annoying in the manner of most 4X games. Can’t play it with the sound off, but distracting with it on. Gameplay: 6/10 - This game could be SO MUCH MORE THAN IT IS! Very frustrating and hopefully the devs work on it. Value: 7/10 - $20-$25 depending on where you live. Nice little game for not much money. However, with DLC included value drops to 2/10. DLC content is forgettable and largely flavor in an already over-flavored game. Overall: 6/10 - Get it if you love this genre, but hold off on the DLC until you’ve played it through once. To compare this game with the classic pinnacle of gangster gaming, Gangsters (G98), it’s easy to see where the developers of City of Gangsters (COG) got their inspiration, but there are some mechanics in COG which are inferior to the original. There is more Micro than is necessary which bogs this game down. In COG you are constantly building and modifying trade routes to buy and sell, or running around to your various fronts to collect protection; G98 allowed you to give broad orders like “Export” and “Collect Protection” in a certain territory and then the AI would use its best discretion to fulfill those tasks. Gang members in this game have zero autonomy which makes you feel like less of a crime lord and more of a daycare worker. COG is somewhat compensating for its lack of strategic depth by relying on tactical gameplay. However, the AI is tactically weak so you can roll enemy factions fairly easily by killing all their hoods in the early game. Even in the later game, you can show up in their territory with 3-4 hoods strapped with guns and pick off the enemy one-by-one after they scatter. Safe houses are not actually safe because the AI cannot hide inside them. One of the great pleasures of G98 was getting a 5-star bomber/stealth character, scouting out the enemy safe house and throwing a bomb through their window and killing their boss and whole crew. In COG you just drive around shooting people for a couple turns and that’s it. What I really enjoyed about G98 was the intelligence gathering aspect of the game where it would take many many turns to surveil, plan, and execute a hit on enemy personnel, where in COG you can just drive into their territory and shoot everyone you see until their faction collapses. Enemy territory in COG is largely unguarded because of the scarcity of characters, making your movements mostly unhindered. Ideally, the devs of COG should add a mechanic that allows you to guard businesses in your territory for a set price per week, and this defense provides a level of damage to enemy hoods entering your territory. The lack of any gang members besides the leaders and their main lieutenants makes the game world feel very empty. Because of the way this game handles your gang as just a handful of folks being micromanaged, the scope of the game feels very small, though it plays out in a large territory so the game itself feels clumsy and at odds with itself. You can see that the game wants to be big, it just doesn’t know how to get there yet. Unfortunately the devs are focused on mostly flavor DLC, and packing more mechanics into the same already-overwhelmed world of micro. One of the greatest game designs of all time, Civilization, was so successful because it understood how to automate so much minutiae. There’s no reason for players to spend 5 minutes building a delivery schedule with 20 stops when it should be a simple order of “sell wine in this territory” and “buy wine making supplies in this territory”. Overall, COG feels as though isn’t sure what it wants to be. It tries to blend a strategic layer with a tactical layer, but this would be better done in a manner like XCOM and Total War with distinctly separate formats. Instead you have the strategic and the tactical mechanics bumping into each other on the same layer, both getting in each others’ way. Still, it very much has a “just one more turn!” vibe to it which will keep me up at night to a surprising hour if I’m not careful. 6/10, temper your expectations and don’t expect it to be the masterpiece that was Gangsters: Organized Crime.

_childDocuments_.review: I have read the descriptions of the game and looked at the video blogs, so I didn't have the expectation some folks have about this being some kind of massive organized crime sim. It's not, it's a bootlegging business sim and on that level it works well. I think it's rather unfair to criticize the game for being what the devs have always said it would be. The tutorial introduced a lot of stuff and frankly I think it overwhelmed people. My advice would be that once you finished the hand-holding part of the tutorial, quit and go start a regular game. A regular playthrough lets you proceed at your own speed. This allows you to focus on the game concepts at a more relaxed pace. That's what I'm doing now and I'm enjoying it that way. The game has got a lot of fun ideas. The way you influence people through family and friend networks is very clever and makes for an interesting game mechanic. Each member of your crew can have different and sometimes unusual characteristics. The game is a business sim, but by limiting the number of actions and driving by each person you control it becomes important to know which gang member is good at which action. And overall the game just has a lot of flavor.One important detail was given in an answer to a question I posted to the devs. I asked about procedural generation of the map and their answer was:  This is a really cool and nice touch to the game. The current game I'm playing started me close to the river and so I was challenged to expand with less access than the tutorial, but it's a fun challenge and heck, if you don't like the map you got, roll up another one.So overall I'm giving the game a thumbs up. Lots of good content, no crashes or glitches, and perhaps just a few minor bugs which no doubt will be ironed out soon. A very enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Although similar to the Gangster mobile games that took the internet by storm in 2018, City of Gangsters is entirely different. Developed by SomaSim and published by Kasedo Games, this game has proven itself to be an addicting management tycoon.GAMEPLAY  - At the start, new players can choose between starting up a new game themselves or using the tutorial mode to do so. If the tutorial mode is selected, a pre-made character will be created and the city chosen for the player. If a player chooses to foray into the game on their own, however, they can choose between not only a multitude of cities, but nationalities for their character as well.At the beginning, the player will have a singular aspiring gangster in the game, eager to claim as many corners as possible. This game takes place around the time of the prohibition era in the United States, meaning alcohol is both a very illegal and very lucrative business. The player must build up their reputation and gang through selling such illegal substances, collecting more members as they go along. Players can expand territory through setting up fronts with business owners- something that requires a good reputation with said owner. Reputations can be improved through interactions with owners and use of favors between mutual friends.  Rival gangs can lurk in the player’s territory, ruining their fronts and eventually stealing back corners. In order to avoid this, players can engage in combat with enemies. The combat in this game is fairly simple. If an enemy is at full health, the most a player will do is half their health. A player can then attack again to kill a rival and loot their stash. The gameplay, all in all, is focused on management. Players must manage money and resources as their gang expands, making sure each of their underground breweries are properly supplied. Money and brewing supplies must be in warehouse storages, otherwise production will halt. As the player’s gang expands, they can set up delivery drivers to go to shops and sell alcohol. They can also set up an automated delivery service, so a gang member will deliver and buy supplies on their own.  City of Gangsters does also include a sort of obstacle to the player in the form of policemen. However, it should be noted that officers are fairly easy to avoid and don’t play as big of an obstacle as they should. The most they will do is prevent a player from doing business with a shop the cop is parked in front of. Otherwise, they do little to pose as a proper threat. Interestingly enough, the game also provides a fun leveling up feature. The more a particular gangster does, the more experience they earn, which allows them to level up in a particular skill. Whether it be in driving, brawling, delivery, or brewing, a character can increase a singular proficiency by one level each time. Players can also level up breweries and commit to new businesses with individuals. FINAL THOUGHTS  - City of Gangsters proved to be a wonderful and enjoyable surprise. The tycoon was developed in a way that always kept me hooked. That isn’t to say, however, that there is no room for improvement. Moving forward, I think the developers need to focus heavily on making the policemen in the game a bigger threat. As the game stands now, they are more of a nuisance than anything else. Additionally, I think it would be a good idea to look into implementing multiplayer gameplay. Creating and running your own gang on your own is fun, but if you could do that with a friend? It would be spectacular. All in all, City of Gangsters proved to be an addicting game that any tycoon enthusiast would thoroughly enjoy. It’s simple yet captivating gameplay is sure to have any average gamer pouring hours into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: For a long time I have been waiting for a game in the style and with the quality of "Gangsters: Organized Crime" (1998). Therefore, I was very pleased when I heard about this title.But to take away the hope of all like-minded people directly: This game is no "Gangsters: Organized Crime". But it's still not bad and definitely exudes a similar charm.What it's all about is quickly clear: to make as much money and criminal fame as possible during Prohibition. For this we have numerous possibilities, which we can and must constantly extend in the course of the game by so-called "competences", since the constantly rising prices could not be handled otherwise. The AI-controlled traders seem to have a variable, though quickly transparent economy based on supply and demand. It is a pity that the processes behind this are not explained well. The tutorial is limited to things that anyone who has ever played a computer game will quickly grasp, but explains little of the game's own mechanics. For example, how the demand of the traders arises, which seems to depend on a fixed value and on whispering pubs and smuggling in the area. In addition to the interesting setting, there are entertaining resource management facets. We have to buy ingredients, deliver them and be careful not to get caught by the cops. While at the beginning everything is done manually, the syndicate grows at some point and you can work with automatic supply chains. At the same time we have to defend ourselves against other syndicates and small gangs of thugs.So all in all, it's very multi-layered, but there are also some weaknesses that I keep shaking my head over while playing: the difficulty level is ridiculous, enemy gangs (have only met 2 so far) are mostly very peaceful, expand quickly at the beginning, but then stagnate soon, so that overrunning is possible without any problems. The police mechanics are too simple and at the same time unwieldy: once a year you go to the policemen and bribe them, then you can smuggle, kill and do whatever else in front of them. I would have liked to see much more interaction here. Maybe not every policeman is bribable and then you have to get them out of the way in a different way... But this possibility does not exist in general. Combative interactions are only with other syndicates and gangs of thugs.In addition, the management of the supply chains is very unwieldy, because you can see where what is bought, but you can't see their route, so adjusting the routes is extremely cumbersome.So in a nutshell:Pro:- Setting- Atmosphere- Freedom of action- constant advancement- Interesting relationship network of each characterNegatives:- Difficulty level too low / not adjustable- Unclear management- Few interaction possibilities with the policeConclusion:Great game, with room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: A game for the mature mafioso. It's a pleasure to finally have a mafia game that illustrates that the day to day of organized crime isn't shootouts in the streets, but the daily grind of picking up cash from protection rackets, collecting on debts, and using your net of "a guy who knows a guy" to exploit opportunities for some quick and easy ill-gotten gains. This isn't a "side of gangsters" with your tycoon game, this is organized crime presented in a realistic way. It's always been about business.I'm hoping the developers will release more DLC covering the fertile ground that still remains unexplored. I'd like to see more diplomacy between rival gangs, like the ability to have a "sit downs" and hash out deals for territory or exclusive rights to rackets. This could easily go in a Crusader Kings direction, seeking protection or joining up with more powerful gangs, or ruling over smaller outfits and making sure they pay their cut to the boss. Family council meetings to solve grievances. Made men. There is a lot here and tremendous potential. But City of Gangsters already does a fine job at doing what it does without all the extras I mentioned. I haven't explored even a 20% of the first map of Chicago, and I'm still a bit lost in a sea of skills and rackets I'm still clueless about. I started with brick wine deliveries on the down low, and recently opened my first "store" in a tobacco shop, where with the right phrase you can get yourself a few bottles. Next it was the numbers, always a go-to for an enterprising gangster. No more credit. Pay up or I start breakin' things. I'm sure one day I'll get a proper speakeasy set up and running, but I've got two Czech gangs moving in on my territory right now, and one of them is eyeing my Deli "front" I've had up since the beginning of prohibition. I hired an ugly bastard with a bad temper and a .45 to watch for now, but I'd rather play nice and make money than go to war. War is bad for business. Recommended and hoping for more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of historical themed games and strategy, I was interested in this game immediately.  I didn't love the art style at first, but thanks to the steam autumn sale I decided to give it a try and I am immensely glad I did.  This game has a wonderful balance of business strategy and that "just one more turn" addictive gameplay.  As soon as I intend to quit, I have to play "one more turn" as I try to grow my Prohibition era booze business.  I appreciate that there's many different ways to pursue the game and, as yet, there does not seem to be an obvious "meta" to exploit the game mechanics.  A lot about your save depends on the people you meet, the places you go, and the way the map unfolds.  I played through the tutorial and am still on my first actual playthrough when I hit my 20 hour mark.  Considering the price tag on this game and the fact that there are unique elements to each of the cities (even in the base game, not counting two DLCs and regular updates), this is really something special.  I even joined the game's discord to talk with others about game strategy and further suggestions.This is a game that I always dreamed to play.  Each gameplay mechanic from violence to making alcohol to deciding how to engage with every NPC you meet... every action has a consequence.  It's really a game about building a network and learning how to use the people around you to get the things you need to maximize profits.  At the end of the day, the game measures success in "legacy" and I think that's a perfect perspective for a gangster.  It's not just about kills or even stacks of cash; it's about power, control, and having other people remember your name in the era that you lived and dominated.This is a definite recommend for me.  I am eager to keep playing and supporting the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT 'Empire of Sin' (meaning, don't expect this game to be something other than what it is)I've been prompted to review by the mixed feedback received so far. There are certainly some issues with City of Gangsters but it's well worth a look and many of the issues being raised by negative reviews are either being addressed by the Devs or can be circumvented within the game as it stands.The big plus for me is that the Devs are very active and the game is being constantly tweaked with QoL improvements. A few of these should probably have been fixed before release but it's still very playable and their proactive approach to player feedback is a lesson to some larger developers.I've played every Gangster game since the original Gangsters and for me this new offering from Kasedo comes closest to the spirit of that old classic than anything since. This game is primarily a business and human management sim. That's the sweet spot for me since you can automate the micro managing by setting up automated deliveries and your treatment of everyone does have consequences in game. If you whack some rival gangster or smash up someone's shop then he/she will have friends/family in the game somewhere and they will react accordingly. It would be interesting to see surviving family actively conduct a vendetta against you but the game remembers your actions and you'll have to work hard to ever do business with them again. I'd like a few more options for interactions with NPCs, police especially, and many of the missions feel very similar but if you approach the gameplay with a business management headset then you'll appreciate the diversity that it offers - where to set up that next business for maximum efficiency, should you create a speakeasy now or will you struggle to keep it properly supplied, can you guarantee a regular supply of apple juice to justify creating a hard cider operation, who do you need for your crew - another driver, a brawler, a manager, should you hire the person with 2 good skills or the friend of that NPC you're hoping to build a relationship with ...  If this sort of decision making is your thing then you'll probably enjoy the game. If you're still on the fence then check youtube for playthroughs (eg: The Geek Cupboard)There are shortcuts to avoid excessive clicking (eg: Shift click takes you straight to buying/selling) and as mentioned, setting up deliveries helps avoid the descent into micro management that this game can easily become. It can feel repetitive at times but that's usually when you need to take a step back from micro managing your businesses and instead delegate tasks to automated deliveries. Remember - you're the boss; let someone else deliver stoneware crocks to your new brewery

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoy this Gangsters themed logistics sim. If you want lots of combat and fancy graphics I'm sorry to say you won't find it here ( combat is more of a means to an end ). I do like the simple graphics myself, but then I am an old fart.What you will find is an underrated gem - starting out with nothing but some booze in your uncle / aunt's backroom, you spend your early turns building up your cash to open up your first backroom production. You must pay attention to the resources available with the locals and produced in your starting building ( usually part of ingredients to make a certain type of booze ).One of the cool things I like about this game is that you have no idea what anyone near you is selling or willing to buy until you explore - even then, if they don't like or trust you, based on how you interact with their family and friends, you may never find out. So it does pay to be a true Mafioso and not go in guns blazing all the time.  Also, the maps are HUGE.You develop relationships over time with business owners, using this and favours they owe you to open up opportunities for buying and selling, missions and introductions to unknown business owners who may be useful to you, based on what you already hold, produce or use in your production. It's extremely satisfying when all of your turns and turns worth of saving, planning and scouting pay off and a business becomes self sufficient with the delivery system in place - you don't even need to collect your own money at this point, have one of your goons do it for you!So, as mentioned, the delivery system - essentially pickup/collection routes that you can create to save you from having to manually go and pick up your booze and sell it around town yourself. I eventually had multiple delivery drivers, some auto-buying bottles, crocks etc for my production, others picking up the booze and selling it to designated customers around the map and others yet moving T1 products to another of my buildings to either be sold or used as input for higher tier alcohol.Developing your businesses is quite fun too - there are optional upgrades, depending on the many many skills that you can learn by using your favours and completing missions from characters across the map. Did I mention the maps are HUGE? Every building ( or just about ) has an interact-able character for you to extort, buy, sell, learn skills from, give you missions etc etc.Okay, so the negativesCombat is very basic, really it's just a means to an end and as long as you outnumber the opponent you will be fine. There are interactions with other gangs beyond whacking them, like deals not to take over territory within 3 tiles of eachother etc. I felt like diplomacy was something to be worked on in an update that never came.Unfortunately when it comes to conflict, the options beyond killing all of the enemy outfit are limited in variety and practicality - shutting down their territory expanding 'front' buildings does next to nothing, really it's much less hassle to just wipe them out at the source.By the time you get a good few strong illicit buildings up and running you'll be swimming in money and able to wipe out any other gang with ease, pay off every cop etc. The mid-end game is where the game does fall short, with the amount of characters and businesses under your control becoming unmanageable somewhat. I would have really liked some sort of 'delegate' system where your captains could be given neighbourhoods to manage for you as under-bosses or something, this would have been awesome.In summary;An underrated turn-based gangsters themed logistics sim, missed a few tricks that you can't help but feel would come with further patches and development. If you are a fan of the gangster theme and enjoy managing logistics, you definitely want to pick this up and make your own mind up. Personally, I'm crossing my fingers and toes they are working on a sequel because nothing else has ever come close to my ideal old-school gangster game.7.75/10

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters is unlike any other game I've seen, a great rarity in the often derivative world of gaming.  It's turn based, strategic, and centers around resource management and networking with NPCs, so it's not for adrenaline junkies and those with short attention spans.  But for fans of thoughtful strategy games, it's first rate, and definitely worth a try!The game is set in America in 1920 as the 18th Amendment and the Volstead Act prohibiting the sale and consumption of alcohol come into effect.  This is the era when gangsters like Al Capone and bootleggers like Joe Kennedy (father of the future President) made their fortunes.  Your goal is to create an illegal booze operation and carve out your own share of that lucrative and illegal market.The game centers around building logistics networks- finding discrete places to produce your illegal hootch, finding the ingredients and containers to make and package it, and finding the thirsty customers who will buy it, all while avoiding the law and fending off rival outfits.  Along the way you'll discover technologies that allow you to produce more sophisticated, and lucrative, forms of alcohol.  These will require more ingredients and a more expensive production facility, making the game more challenging as your network of connections and resources grows.  You'll also assemble a crew that will help with the production and distribution, and they'll provide invaluable support when you run into rival gangs and things inevitably get violent.  These episodes of violence are somewhat rare, though, most of the game is about buying, transporting, and selling things.  It's fun, but if you're looking for a blood-soaked mafia game with a high body count, this probably isn't the game you're looking for.One of the things I quite like about the game is the network of connections and acquaintances that are generated at the start that you'll have to navigate in order to be successful.  During setup, the game populates a new city with a number of families of different, historical ethnicities and simulates their marriages and family formation for several generations.  The result is that the businesses you encounter will be run by people who have brothers, cousins, friends, and aunts they can introduce you to as your booze empire grows and spreads.  Help somebody out, and their sister two blocks over might be more inclined to support your efforts.  Beat up the wrong hooligan, and suddenly one of your key suppliers might refuse to do business with you.  It's a key part of the game, and adds a lot to the experience.This game isn't for everyone- it's turn based, and rewards meticulousness and attention to detail.  You'll spend a lot of time exploring new parts of the city and looking for the connections that will give you the resources and customers you need.  You'll spend considerably less time dishing out beatings and making people sleep with the fishes.  Also, it's made by a small, indie development team, so it doesn't have some of the size and polish that bigger game studios lavish on their games.  The devs have already shown tremendous commitment to the game, however, making numerous patches and updates in the few days since launch.  One of their more impressive feats, IMO, is revamping the resource overlay in response to player feedback so you can look for multiple resources on the map at the same time.  That patch, their fourth since launch, dropped Friday, just five days after the game came out.The game is original and unique, and has become one of my favorites.  If thoughtful management sims appeal to you, definitely give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: This isn't a city-builder. It might LOOK like a city-builder, but be aware that it isn't a city-builder or even a city-sim at all. This game takes place in a pre-built city, where you expand your influence and conquer the city around you, making it much more of a , so take note of that.Pros: #1. The map is gigantic. It'll take you a couple of days to conquer it all.#2. Very different from anything I've played beforeCons: #1. NO Voice Acting and lots of reading#2. $30 is too much imo. $20 would be better, seeing as how basic the game is.#3. Basically 80% of the game is you transporting resources from one place to another#4. It's turn-based... I just feel like combining a 'city-sim' with a turn-based game is a no-no. City-sims are better off being real-time. I guess this game is almost more of a 4X game than anything else really, due to it being turn-based and you not really building anything.Fans of Tropico, Anno, City Skylines, etc. will perhaps find the 'expansion mechanic' weird, since you're spreading through the city like a plague, instead of actually building stuff. On the whole, this is a borderline recommend from me... It's not worth $30 imo, due to almost everything in the game being very basic (the graphics, no voice acting, the cinematics, etc.), but it's a good game, albeit an expensive one, and I can't NOT recommend a game simply for it being a bit over-priced. So it's a recommend, but only just. _childDocuments_.review: This is game is not Gangsters : Organized Crime.I really loved G:OC, but it would be unfair to compare both games.City of Gangsters is above all a game of resource management in the context of the Prohibition: it is therefore a matter of programming production chains, selling alcohol, defending and increasing one's territory. It's not a combat game. That being said, the graphics of the game are unique, many small roleplay elements add to the immersion: the city, generated procedurally, is populated by interconnected people, like in a Crusader Kings game. If you kill someone's brother, so and so will hate you and refuse to sell you or buy products. It's a game based on connections, you have to get favors to learn new skills, open front shops, discover new resources, obtain weapons or recruit gangsters ... and many more. The game is revealed gradually, and there is not one unique way to discover new things. A game could last a long time : I have almost a hundred hours on my first try, because I take the time to optimize my travels, my routes and my connections.The game has some purely ergonomic flaws: we do not always have all the information at hand. Like the old games, you have to guess or suppose the effects of certain traits, certain actions and sometimes you remain a little in the dark: why so and so refuses to open a front business, when he owes me a favor? and that he likes me? Ha, it's because he's religious!Rivals are more passive obstacles than real threat, and I enjoy it that way. It's a chill game with a good ambiance.

_childDocuments_.review: City of gangsters is a superb implementation of what real life gangster evolution might look like Video REVIEW : Helped out and encouraged by your aunt you're quickly going to be thrown into an ever expanding world where street corners dominate and dictate your standing within the community.  Prohibition has landed you a real money spinning opportunity but there are other opportunities you can expand into if you desire.  Over time, with good planning, your loyal crew and the regular payments from those under your protection, you should have enough spare cash to give back to the community and gain more loyal support which permits expansion.Every shady business venture needs to have a front, a cover a way to legitimise all of that lovely cash and that requires property purchasing.Once you own property you'll need to think about back room alterations and sourcing ingredients to make your produce.  Keeping in with the friendly local cop helps to keep things sweet and as other small-time gangsters move in you can choose how best to utilise them, or get rid of them....!The game offers up some excellent micro-management opportunities which can then be handed over to a Manager whilst you focus your time on expansion, corruption, production or ALL OUT WAR!Every single aspect of this game impresses me, the fact that your car needs to be serviced regularly, that you need to learn how to drive a truck & even need to source raw materials to build, then allow enough time for construction.This is not a wham bam thank you mam kind of game, it requires thought, planning and daring if you want to make an empire worthy of note...and an empire it will be as the map is HUGE!  So many corners and so little time.Having to re-select my character's car every time I perform an action is frustrating and unnecessary.  I would like my character to remain the selected character without me needing to click the each time.Honestly my ONLY Gripe with this game is the unnecessary click it has you perform; Select an option > (pop-up: are you sure you want to do this?) click yes and Yes!  The game UI could be streamlined a lot more reducing the number of clicks required by 50% and I am NOT Joking!I would also like to see a lot more variety in terms of shops...how many Florists do we actually need in one block??Ultimately I really like this game and be WARNED it is addictive as heck, my first lets play (mostly tutorial for 2 hours) just zipped by without any real issue....well there was this one gang member who I beat into oblivion about 5 times but he still wouldn't let me buy a baseball bat from his crew....even after I worked him over with a flick knife!

This is still a fun game if you're into resource management, and the developers are doing good on making the game better through patches and add ons (love the custom map and start on mods), so it is still a recommend but with an asterisk in there for some minor issues

Absolutely no role play tools. Good game play, but it's so grindy that it makes the game feel linear. Weird limits, like how fast you can expand territory / how many people you can recruit (maybe this is just preference, but I like the games where you can choose to risk it all and then get slapped down for flying too close to the sun).I like it, it's a decent game, but if you're buying this because it's in the simulation genre, you'll be a little disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game, but it is not a perfect representation of the mob or this time period. I really like this game but there are a lot of things in this game that are just not very realistic. For example, the number of women in a gang or as a business owner, or cop is very unrealistic for this time period. yes there were some women in gangs back then, and a few were even the boss, but not near at the frequency shown in this game, also it was basically unheard of for a woman to own a business back in those days, and I don't think any women were cops back then. Not trying to be sexist, that's just how it was back in those days. Another thing that is not very realistic is how mixed the neighborhoods are for ethnicities. back in those days people of same ethnicities tended to group together in their own neighborhoods. there may have been a few in the neighborhood that was not of that ethnicity, but the overall neighborhood was mostly of that certain ethnicity. It really seems that for simplicity they just randomized everyone's gender and ethnicity. this may make it easier to develop characters, but it gives a very unrealistic feel to the game. Also the combat isn't very realistic. I once went to fight a woman hoodlum with 2 men. my main character had a revolver. the woman roughed up my men pretty good and the woman survived. it seems to actually kill someone, you need to bring like 3 guys to actually get the job done, which is not very realistic as long as 1 guy has a gun. The quests are good for establishing relationships and getting things in return, but it is a bit too much sometimes. Much of the time I am so busy trying to run my business that I have no time to do any of the stupid quests which just keep coming in like a game of WOW! sometimes there are some silly quirks in the quests like they need an item that they themselves sell. so you can literally buy that item from them and then just give it back to them for the quest. All in all this is a great game and I enjoy playing it a lot, but it would be nice if the things I mentioned would get corrected in order to have a more realistic feel to the game!

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters: The Adventure of Building a Criminal Empire[Introduction]City of Gangsters is a strategy-based game that immerses you in an adventure of rising through the criminal world. The game succeeds in drawing you in with its strategic decisions and elements such as relationships with other gangs.[Gameplay]City of Gangsters' gameplay revolves around strategic and tactical decisions. It offers an experience that combines city management, resource management, and tactical battles. To progress in the criminal world, you need to determine the right strategies to control businesses and compete against rivals. The gameplay can be immersive, but for some players, the tendency to fall into repetition can make it monotonous.[Graphics and Sounds]City of Gangsters' graphics successfully reflect the atmosphere of the criminal world. Detailed city and character designs create a realistic and dark ambiance in the game. The stylized graphics give the game an aesthetically appealing look. However, some players may consider the quality of the graphics and the lack of visual details as a disadvantage. Sound design enhances the game experience. Detailed sound effects like street noises, gunshots, and vehicle engine sounds immerse the player in the criminal world. The game's music is also used in harmony to support the atmosphere. The sounds provide a more immersive experience for the player.[Conclusion]City of Gangsters offers an addictive experience for players interested in the criminal world. While its gameplay is based on strategic decisions, the tendency to become repetitive may bother some players. The graphics and sounds enhance the game's atmosphere. In conclusion, City of Gangsters can be a choice for players who want to test themselves in the criminal world.Rating: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun seeing your little one corner hooliganism turn into a liquor and money making machine. It scratches the same itch of civilization but in a more niche application. Mixes a little production game, city sim, grand strategy, real time strategy. The notes that I have are small in magnitude and do not ruin the experience. They are things that interrupt my flow while playing for an extended period. Here's my likes:I have yet to win a game and I'm always able to improve my method with each game. It's exciting to edge closer and closer to a building upgrade, or pushing into a neighborhood and seeing your influence grow one corner at a time. I appreciate it being turn based so I can really look at where the other syndicates are pushing, or revise routes. It's nice having some options for how to interact with the businesses and other syndicates but not so many choices you're paralyzed. The dialogue has become a blur at where I'm at hour wise. Not a lot of variety after the initial couple trees of dialogue which is fine. I'm playing the game to build my criminal empire, not date the entire city.I appreciate having an in-game wiki! Not requiring a two screen setup to understand what the flip is going on and how I get the next gadget is refreshing. A tech tree of sorts just laying out the different qualities of each item, average market price etc. The tutorial is worth playing. The story of the immigrant getting set up in a families back room is grounding as far as how small you do start to how big of an operation you can become. It also exemplifies that it's really interpersonal relationships that are going to make or break your enterprise. Now for the room for improvement section:The route making process is pretty refined. When selecting the who what why when how it will show you on the map which businesses are available for what you're trying to do. What I would like to see is a simulation of how the delivery/pickup will go. Where does my character spend most of their time? Are they improving or harming our relationship with each delivery? If so, how much per delivery? Should I upgrade action points or movement points when they get enough XP? Show a delivery history that tells me me how many goods have been moved over the course of ten turns or something. I don't want to follow my drivers around as the turn is starting when they're driving around the map. On the notification bar, it would be nice to have a turn stamp in case I haven't removed a notification from previous turns. There's been several times where the urgent front message has spooked me by not removing it as I took care of the problem the turn(s) previous. I don't like the 'another settlement needs our help'. Example is all of the favorable businesses give the exact same type of mission when they show that a mission is available. I spend time running around seeing if any of the are steals of a mission ($500 for a new building is a notable one) or if they're asking for money in exchange for basically nothing but a relationship bonus for a business that I almost have max relationship with. I can imagine it being a mod where you opt out of certain missions you just don't want to ever do.It would be nice to see how much of a given good is supplied/demanded per turn by businesses and your production facilities,and if your relationship can change that number if it's a business. Spending movement points to figure it out adds tedium and disrupts the flow chasing down where I can reasonably source goods. An example of something that I like in the game already that speaks to what I'm talking about it shift+click to get to the trade screen quickly. Expansions on that sort of thinking would be useful in getting to the information that I need a little faster. Adding custom missions, of your own, say building a winery or something, that keep track of how many of each required good are in that building's inventory. In the overlay screen you can favorite certain goods, but you cannot un-favorite them, so if you mark it and have favorites toggled, you will ALWAYS see that good on the map. If you're not careful it makes your map look very cluttered. Adding specifics towards the benefits of certain character promotions. Yeah they're a better brawler now, but by how much? Does it change with each rank I put in? Some things are a little goofy like it costs an action point to scope out a building and you need at least one left in order to ask about trading and find out what goods they offer.All in all it's a great game even with it's quirks. Highly recommend.I got this game as a gift, but the $10 price tag seems very reasonable for the content. $30 is a bit steep from what I've been able to get out of it so far (~30hrs).

_childDocuments_.review: I hung in there for 8 hours, hoping the game would get better....not!  The game is so repetitive.  The screen gets full of all kinds of big and little icons. The tutorial is actually quite good and covers a lot of the key points.  Clearly, doing 'deliveries' with a gang member is key to the game.  The 'delivery' process is nothing very creative and is quite old school of moving things up/down, rather than point/click.  Also, the 'delivery' can pick up goods, but you just don't know if the goods will be available in the quantity you want/need, so this really messes with any calculations you might attempt.  Eventually, I found the game to be just boring.  I'd get my money back, but I've played too many hours.  So, now this game will just sit around and likely never be played again.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is "meh". My Recommendation comes from the pure potential this game has to be something truly great.TLDR; the game needs multiplayer for the repetitive Relationships/Missions/Favors mechanics to hold the weight they need to. Everything in the game is entirely predictable and bland once you figure out how things work. The only way I could see them leaving the mechanics the way they are and having a perfect game is if they added a true sense of unpredictability and competition via PvP. If we could hold a 6 Player Outfit + 6 NPC Outfit lobby, the game would have the replayability of Civ VI.Here's an explanation:The way you navigate towards your success in COG works on three basic premises which are: Relationships, Missions, and Favors.Any interaction with any NPC results in creating a connection between you and them. Those NPCs also have various connections of their own whether it be through family, friends, police, small troublemakers, or other Outfit Dons (or any combination thereof). When you start out, you have family and close-by relatives which have a direct connection to you as the player. But since they also have their own Relationships, the clear way to proceed is to lean on their connections in the form of a . Which is where we start to notice a very simple formula and leads us to how the mechanics of Favors work.Favors are just that-- favors. Need to increase your Relationship Level with a certain shopkeeper and gain +1 Favor? Just ask your Aunt. Need to possibly find a weapon to take care of local Troublemaker? Spend 1 Favor with the Shopkeeper and gain +1 Pistol. Need reduced Heat in your neighborhood and don't have the relationship level with the local police to succeed in a Bribe? Ask the Mechanic to put in a good word with Officer Miller. Need a Shotgun? Ask Officer Miller. He doesn't have one? Wait a few months, and then ask Officer Miller again. Need another Shotgun? Ask Officer Miller. He doesn't have one? Bribe Officer Bates and then ask Officer Bates. Don't have the required Relationship Level with Officer Bates? Ask the other Shopkeeper to put in a good word.And I think we can see how this is getting stale...Missions act as you doing favors for various NPCs in your city so that you can increase relationship levels, earn Favors with said NPC, and unlock new items to buy or sell. Which leads us to buying and selling items (the crux of the game). When you first meet certain Shopkeepers, you may or may not be able to see everything that they're selling or buying. Sometimes, you will have a (?) symbol in the "Sell" and "Buy" rows. The (?) means the goods for sale may be illicit. So how do I discover what lies behind the (?)'s..?You guessed it, I can increase my relationship level with said Shopkeeper through my mutual connections who owe me Favors OR I can do a Mission for that Shopkeeper. The problem with Missions are that it's very transparent in which Missions will lead you to what you're looking for and which won't. It's pretty much safe to assume that anyone begging for Brickwine because they "heard through the Grapevine" that you had some and heard people want more will result in them becoming a permanent buyer of your product. Deliver 30x Brickwine and Vuala! Said Shopkeeper is now a loyal customer. For instance: Let's say my Outfit produces Grape Concentrate in my legitimate business (which is procedurally generated) for me to produce 45x Brickwine/4-turns in the backroom. I need Buyers. Where and how do I find these buyers if they're not already present on the map? I run around to different Shopkeepers who are offering Missions and look for the specific Missions that I know will result in a Buyer. What if I'm looking for Counterfeit Wine Buyers? Simple: start a Counterfeit Wine operation and then look for the Shopkeepers who "heard through the yard" that you have some. ez. ******The problem with all of the aforementioned is that the Relationships/Missions/Favors (RMF) mechanic works the same through every aspect of the game. If I want to gain access to a local Troublemaker so I can solicit businesses in their 1x1 territory yet keep them as a barrier between me and another Outfit, all I have to do is increase my Relationship Level with said Troublemaker through RMF mechanics and then ask that Troublemaker if I can solicit his businesses. It's really that simple. The whole entire game; regardless of what it is you produce or are setting out to achieve, is Relationships, Missions, Favors. And although the game might offer some variation between producing certain products and playing a certain way, there isn't much to do once you get past turn 300 or so. What you've been doing on turn 300 is roughly what you will be doing on turn 500. What you were doing on turn 300 is, in essence, what you were doing on turn 30.What would make this game blow-up is a re-launch with a Player vs. Player mechanic being added to the game so that the RMF mechanics can be used as a tool for Players to get the edge over one another on the map. The Relationships/Missions/Favors mechanic is just too stale to keep me coming back and a PvPvE mechanic with up to 6 Player Outfits and 6 NPC Outfits to start would be the perfect thing to bring spice to an otherwise bland game once you hit the 15h mark.

_childDocuments_.review: City of Gangsters is good at what it does, which is being a prohibition resource management sim, but it seems as though people are having a hard time reading the description of the game BEFORE they bought it. Its not a "Mob simulator", nor a Mafia type game. you make production chains and sell goods, trying not to get caught by the cops or killed by rivals. A lot of people are getting hung up on the name, when they hear "gangster" they think it should equate to hit squads, and other larger crimes etc, and i can understand that, but the game never sold itself as an Omerta clone, its more like the show "Boardwalk Empire" and it always came across like that, but of course, you would have to read the description of the game to have come to grips with that it seemsbut all that said its not perfect, some of the criticism is quite fair, there are some odd bugs, after i took over ten corners it seems that every store owner was begging for money to pay off a bad loan or because their cousins farms were under threat of foreclosure. It can get a bit boring if you were expecting "Empire of Sin" and got this, but at the end of the day that doesn't really seem like a fault of the game, but of the inability to read literally two paragraphs that describe a it.TL;DR Good game, people need to learn to read.

The devs are a small indie team, but determined, and also just generally a friendly bunch. _childDocuments_.review: Can tell I am really gonna enjoy this game. There is a deep complexity that I can tell I've hardly scratched.Primarily, it's a logistics and business building/investment game. There are confrontations but they can be minimized and/or avoided until late game (this isnt an action game. Combat is RPG/RNG based). This game is about building a successful and efficient bootlegging/speakeasy/smuggling/extortion racket. Wise investments of money and personal favors & relationships takes a lot of thought and planning. It's good to know what your future goals are. Do I extort the business next to my warehouse that only sells bottles? What a silly business. Seems like a good idea on turn 1 but when turn 100 comes around you realize you need those bottles to brew your newest creation? Turns out the bottle shop you smashed up up was ran by the mother of a huge Irish family that owns half of the industrial buildings on your side of town - and now they all hate you. You'll have to cash in favors and pay for an Irish community center if you want another shot at working with them. Should have picked on the coffee shop owner with no friends...

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on City Of Gangsters for a while now. I actually am a huge geek for the 1900-1950's. But if not the war's, my attention is always on the prohibition era. When I saw this game, I actually was put off by it, it looked interesting, but I didn't know what to think. But when Steam had the big Demo event, I gave it a shot, and boy did I like it. A management game in the 20's and 30's, mixing in gangsters and alcohol!  You should know that I actually own a 1931 Ford Model A Sports Coupe! I plan on getting a Denix Tommy Gun replica, then a nice suit and fancy shoes to complete the gangster outfit! I'm also an artist, and I draw comics. A lot of them involve car's and ideas from this era! So this gives me ideas on comics about a young man, down on his luck either coming across and joining a gang, or starting one of his own. This game is really chill. It's slow, but it can be entertaining! Just slowly growing your gangster empire, and exploring the randomly generated maps! Lots lot's of people around, to force into submission and to pay you, or to win over with favors, and or selling illegal items too. I like this game a lot, and I think that if your willing to give it a shot and put some time in you'll probably like it too! I got tired of it after a while, but I am going to jump right back in when ready. It actually makes me want to go drive my old Model A. Just for the hell of it!

They're less than useless if you need a soldier or a leg breaker, which is the steak and potatoes of the early mobs.Edit: After almost 150hrs of it I can't give this a thumbs up anymore. _childDocuments_.review: Allow me to get one thing out of the way. If you want to play another game, go get that game instead of leaving a negative review because you were expecting a different game. If you were expecting something different, then read first the game description and then leave feedback accordingly. Otherwise, the game works, the graphic are nice, some improvement would make it easier to enjoy it more like for example the odd way of turning around the camera and some expansion in the future can be done easily given it is solid already. And if you find the game expensive, get another job or a different one, or simply find another hobby.Now, with that said, it is a game based on prohibition in the 1920, essentially alcohol was made illegal and just like anything made illegal, there is always a way around it. Prostitution never changed, loan shark never changed either, casino, money printing and so forth, it was and still illegal today, alcohol was a different story. And yes some mafia outfit may have had their hands in some of those activities, but seriously alcohol would have been hotter commodity to have sell around. So I have no problem with the game focusing on that. Matter of fact I find it fascinating the way it was done, that you need to have and/or find contact(s) in order to move the good, but also to get the basic necessity  to get it off the ground.And yes it will take some time to understand the mechanic but even at the time of this review, I managed to get one business off the ground without the tutorial, so the game is well done.  One thing I actually like is the size of the city, the design even though cartoonish works so well. The only complaints I will make is the dialogue need to be redone a little bit because sometime there are no way out of them, other than closing that dialogue window. The camera turning around need some improvement too, it makes no sense you need to use 3 button to spin around. I wish too you could have a top down view instead of the always 3/4 view, simply because you have to click on a lot different places and sometime either you will lose your vehicle or simply the business you wanted. And then you have to turn around a few times to get it done, it is a pain but I'm sure easily fixable. I have a difficult time with the idea of corners but it makes sense with the way the game was designed.Personally I like it. There are many reasons to like it too. And there is a lot of room for DLC too which I know will be coming sooner than later and that is perfectly fine too. I don't work for free, why should the developers then, simple logic.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR , the focus is completely different, but it is a very nice booze  (it’s important to note that this is a tycoon game, not a violent mafia sim) set during the prohibition era with a heavy emphasis on relationships and a good dose of RNG.City of Gangsters is a turn-based game where you play as a budding entrepreneur trying their hand at making and distributing illegal alcohol in the prohibition.In City of Gangsters, you start out as a young man or woman arriving in your city of choice (from, as of now, 4 cities – Chicago, Detroit, Pittsburgh or Cincinnati /the last is only available as part of the deluxe edition/). The game being set during the prohibition, naturally, you decide to go into some kind of illegal booze distribution. You start with an amount of one or two of the several kinds of alcohol featured in the game (such as hoe brewed beer, brick wine or hard cider) and try to sell them to appreciative buyers. Then you use the profits from your first, free batch to fund the building of a backroom operation, something that makes alcohol for you every few weeks, provided you have the necessary ingredients (malt syrup, grape concentrate, apple juice, stoneware crocks, barrels, etc.) in stock. Then you use your wealth to expand your influence in the area, spending money on charitable causes to earn the respect of citizens living in that area.Being a newcomer to the big city, you will only see a very small portion of it, basically, only your owned corner and a few stores where you have a good relationship with the owner. Two factors (complementing your booze business, which is the core aspect of the game) come into play here, exploration and contacts.Exploration is a large part of the game – the maps are very large, so you will have your work cut out for you throughout the game to discover every corner, turn by turn, using your crew members’ Drive and Action points. New locations may bring new opportunities, such as a new place to buy your ingredients, sell your stuff, or get a new quest or challenges – there are both street gangs, who are content to stay in their area but will protect it and also cause trouble in the neighborhood (if you befriend them, they can also prove to be somewhat useful assets, though), and rival outfits, who, just like you, are out there to conquer the city.The other important aspect is . As you accrue relationship points (by doing business with the given person, doing a favor for them, being talked up by a common acquaintance…), you incur favors, which can be redeemed for things like getting introduced to a new potential buyer, getting a good word with someone else, being offered a new crew member, etc. Relationships are also important because even stores that buy illicit booze won’t buy from you until they trust you, i.e. have some relationship points. Watch out, though, you can also lose relationship points – maybe that hooligan you murdered was on good terms with some of the big buyers of your booze and now they won’t even talk to you anymore.Then there is the police, members of which will raid corners generating much “heat” (activities such as selling alcohol or vandalism generate heat), searching and/or imprisoning anyone who deem “suspicious”, so you have to take note of where they are – unless you’ve “convinced” them to look the other way.The game has no one single end goal. Instead, the game ends in December 1933, when Prohibition ended. By that time, you should have collected at least 3 stars, awarded for various milestones (being the single top producer of booze, having the biggest territory, having many shop owners owe you favors at once, etc.), or 6 if you want to be considered a legend.*The core loop of producing and selling alcohol, scouting new areas, expanding to those new areas and dealing with hooligans and rivals works very well, making it a very enjoyable game.*RNG is king – the starting seed (which you can see and set, so you can play the same game again if you wish) determines almost everything in the game, so each playthrough will be different. (Of course, that also means that some starts will not be as good as others.)*Attention to historical details – while RNG determines the low-level layout of cities, their high-level appearance does reflect the real cities they are based on. Also, ethnicities in each city and their ratios are based on real-life census from the era.*Also, the cities’ buildings are very nicely drawn.*The 3 (4 with Deluxe) maps provide a nice variety, with each having something unique.*The game is quite nicely polished, especially for a brand new release, with attention to detail and the various parts working along very well.*That said, there are some quality-of-life features missing which would be welcome to have*No historical figures – you won’t meet Lucky Luciano or Al Capone in the game. Everyone is procedurally generated.*This game is purely about distributing booze, so there are no other illicit activities one might associate with gangs (gambling, prostitution, illegal fights, etc.)*Doing the same things over and over again can get tedious.*The lack of a clear, single goal might be deterrent for some players.If you like business simulations, you will most probably like this game. It is quite nicely put together, with a lot of attention to details and the setting is good.If you are looking for a game simulating the seedier parts of running a gang, this game is probably not for you. You may still enjoy it if you like tycoons, but it’s not a “darkest side of the mob” simulation.

The game is also not made to be a sandbox, meaning there is a certain period of time which you can keep playing or intended to play (the Probation Era), but you are able to continue playing the game afterwards like nothing has changed, though what I described above already pushes you set the game aside after a while. I understand that it is move for financing the game studio, but as a player, I am not happy with it. Despite all this, I would recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, but at the end of the day it doesn't really respect your time. It takes hours to build up and capture territory in some areas, and you can have hours of progress wiped out in a single turn with no chance to do anything about it, simply because you "discover" a new competing outfit which can wipe out hours of work as soon as your next turn loads. The AI seems to constantly have every advantage over you, and if the RNG isn't in your favor then you're always falling behind the AI as you fight off multiple outfits, all of which are stronger than you and have better weapons. This game has no difficulty scaling and no way to change how this game scales income, which is ultimately the problem. Generating income takes soooooo long, the AI can just steam roll you while you wait for money to trickle in. The end result is that this feels like a treadmill going slightly faster than you can keep up with. Eventually, you know you are going to fall off, so do you stay on it for another 3 hours and wait until it happens, or do you just get off before you waste all that time? I think this game could be so good, but if you leave it up to RNG whether or not a given map is even going to be feasible then you're not really doing your players any favors. There's a lot here to like, but I can't recommend this unless you really don't care if you spend 10 hours trying to make progress and then lose it for no reason. If I wanted that I'd go play Dwarf Fortress.Edit: I played the game to completion, but didn't enjoy the last 15 or so hours. Once you get enough guns, the AI isn't so difficult, but it also doesn't really seem like ti serves as anything more than a source of irritation. You can't really do much constructive with it. Ultimately, the treadmill feeling only gets worse. Your income scaling never really gets to a point where the game feels fun, it just feels like you run from expense to expense while constantly being almost broke if you didn't intervene to fix the problems that arise with the automated routes.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't love thumbs-up thumbs-down, as that loses a lot of nuance. Overall, I think this is a very good game and certainly worth the price I paid for it on sale. I give it thumbs-up. My review is based on a single game that I'm playing without any DLC, and which I started as a tutorial. I've seen reviews are mixed, and I think that's in large part because the game is pretty particular in terms of intended audience:Who this is for: if you like strategy, logistics, exploration, resource management, and some light roleplaying. If you like trying to find how things connect, how to keep your businesses supplied and making money, this is a game for you.Who this is NOT for: if you're looking for a shoot-em-up or more intense roleplaying. It's also not like, say, Suzerain: there's dialogue, but it's on a somewhat basic level and tends to repeat from interaction to interaction. Combat is there, but you find yourself trying to avoid it when you can. The Good, Bad, and Ugly:Good:- Very deep simulation. There's a lot to keep track of, a lot of little tricks to figure out, and decisions can have unpredictable consequences just like in real life. Did you totally waste that punk who was holding down that one street corner you really needed, then were really happy to get to raid his hideout and take his stuff? Well, turns out he was the best "in"/connection you had to somebody else who was really important later on. Oops. There's also this sense that the game is hiding a lot from you. Normally I'd say that's annoying, but a big part of this game is exploration, and you get a satisfying sense of discovery as you piece out the world around you.- There are a LOT of turns, so a lot of play-time. I've played through enough of them to notice that there's clearly a beginning, a middle-game, and an end-game. There's a potential to really get sucked in, "one more turn", a lot like Civilization. - Replayability seems to be pretty good, though again I'm only on my first game.- I grew up outside of Chicago, went to school in Pittsburgh, and am from a Polish family, so it's nice to see all three of those things represented in the base game. Bad:- While the street plan of Chicago looks about right, and there are several neighborhoods about where they should be, it doesn't look like the street names line up with what they are in real life. I'm also having trouble finding things like The University of Chicago, and I'm playing on the South Side. - The soundtrack  is kind of monotonous, with one song on an infinite loop. I wish this had something like the "Omerta: City of Gangsters" soundtrack instead. - There are times when progress is slow, and it feels like certain missions are pretty much mandatory if you're going to advance. You also start to see the same mission popping up in different areas of the city at the same time, and it would be nice to have some more variety there.Ugly:- It's sometimes hard to know what skills are actually valuable and when. - Sometimes the encyclopedia isn't as informative or comprehensive as it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I have 422 hours in the game.Its basically a business sim, focused on prohibition era alcohol production and distribution. If that aspect is interesting to you you will probably like this game. If you want a lot of combat or if you want to delve into other criminal enterprises you will probably be disappointed. Combat is a definite weak point for the game. And I would say the mechanics discourage combat. It basically boils down to a roll of the dice; i.e. each character deals a random amount of damage based on what skills/weapons they have at the time. Then assuming you aren't killed you have to spend several turns recovering.The alcohol production is where the game shines. You can produce a number of alcohols, at various tiers of complexity. And you can set up fairly complex automation systems by assigning your various crew to delivery routes.I really enjoy it. And if you want a game focused on the business of prohibition you may as well. If you want to be a "bad ass" criminal, you may not.

_childDocuments_.review: Well.... First of all, this game is very good. The pace from the start is a bit slow, because you don't have any characters to use yet, but that will change. This is one of the best trade sims I ever played. The "gangster" angle is not that good, though, mostly it is background color and small things like you can bribe a policeman and shoot another gangster. Still, in my opinion, this is mostly a trading sim. It's a very entertaining trading sim as well. Here are a few of the major flaws, that you can choose to ignore if it suits your playing style:There's a couple of totally unreasonable money sinks that absolutely kills the game when you reach some kind of success. Each building costs more and more. My 17th building in game cost 150k, wheras the first cost around 1k. This is of course completely unreasonable. Same thing goes for establishing territory, the cost escalates (although not as quickly) to make it almost unplayable. [Luckily, there are two user-made mods named "Cheaper Buildings" and "Profitable Corners" in the forums which fixes this.]Other than that, the most notable unfixed bugs and cons are:- Most custom maps don't generate correctly, they create a quarter-sized map with lots of errors such as missing goods, railroad never reaches the city, it ends in the forest.- The micro-management increases steadily and soon you drown in it. You can automate transport routes, but the "quit if full/empty" switch does not work properly. Also there are no way to automate tasks and skills of the automated plant managers you have, although they do level up.- Most DLC:s are more or less just cosmetics. My personal favourites are New York (politics), Atlantic City (gambling) and the Irish (cooler colors).Now, all that being said, I've spent some 800 hours on the game and I'm still playing. As I said, this is probably the best trading sim I've ever played. I love the game. I only wish the developer, who has openly abandoned developing the game further, would spend some more time. If the worst bad stuff was fixed, this should be such an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 hours of n00bing my way through the game trying not to look up online help, here is my review:short version: Game has way more to it that may appear, but could use a little interface work.Longer Version: First Mafia strategy/economy/RPG? game in over 20 years that I am aware of. Super stoked about this!This game has hidden depths that are easy to miss because instead of giving you specific + or - numbers it will often be like this: Character is strong (strong means they can fill trucks more easily and fight better). And then that is it, doesn't tell you extra damage or accuracy numbers, or if loading a truck better means it doesn't count as an action. I don't even know I'm too busy having fun to figure it out. EDIT: Between how you choose to play and the RNG random elements you may not see the variety in missions or requests available, ex: you may get see requests for bats and crowbars and cash to go on a raid of some sort, or you may see no such requests at all. Maybe its because the people you know have a trait that prevents them from offering that mission, or the person you do know doesn't like you enough yet.There is also some discrepancy in how hotkeys and controls are set up compared to many pc games. Ex: its very common in a game when in a screen with a list of options to choose from that the number keys will correspond to the list on the screen (like if you are presented with several dialogue choices so you press 2 instead of moving the mouse over and clicking it). It would be really awesome to have this game, i don't think its possible to change the hotkeys for this but i haven't seriously looked (i am too busy being addicted to this game). It sort of feels like this game was made primarily for a tablet for pen play, its always awesome when a game can be played completely with just a mouse though (the only thing you'd miss out on is custom names for things)Gameplay wise with the random elements of map generation (this game has map seeds!) and RNG stuff, its a bit difficult to nail down a vibe for pacing. You may spawn in a map with no nearby rivals and spend a dozen hours wondering why combat skills are so pointless, only to suffer greatly when an enemy gang finally does roll over and start wiping you out because you focused everyone on economy and nobody on combat. You may start a game with a resource production you won't be able to make use of for hours, or you may have a great money maker in a building that produces half the requirements on its own. Each turn of the game is 1 week and the game is about 13 years long, and the further into the game the more you will probably want to slow down. I haven't looked up how good other people are at this game, but i would be shocked if someone could run a good game without knowing the map seed before hand in less than 10-20 hours. This feels like a looong game and i am totally into it. Apparently it even doesn't really end, its just that when the date rolls over to the end of Prohibition after about 13 years you can no long get achievements and maybe also not be able to officially achieve any remaining legacy goals. So the game can go as long as you want!On the technical side I haven't experienced any bugs or crashes as far as I can tell. The game also seems to have built in mod support and workshop, but I am too busy playing this game to be bothered looking any up yet.I think I paid full price and I am loving it, needs a little interface and info display work though. Free dlc is always awesome, although i don't think I've attempted any of those yet. Perhaps the games greatest pitfall is the combat, it has some depth from a variety of character traits, and some strategy in choosing where/when/who to involve. But there isn't anything to watch, no spectacle for people that may require combat animation of some sort in their games. This is about all I can say before I have to get back into itI'd give it say 7/10-1 interface and info display-1 no combat animation-1 some of the background ambiance noises (easy to mute and cover with your own music)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot like Civ to me: I put it down for weeks at a time but if I sit down to play a game, that's what I'm doing for several hours a day for the next few days, and the "one more turn" mentality is strong. I'm not sure if that's what its like for everyone, but if the idea of that doesn't appeal to you in the least, this game may not be for you. The game is one of micro, then macro, management: you start as a small time gangster, having a small supply of booze right after prohibition, and the space to make a way to make more. You have to hustle to sell your stock to get some seed money, find regular spots you can supply (and get supplied from), and take over corners to earn more territory (the businesses in your territory can be convinced to buy some extra insurance from you, if you know what I mean, but you can sell to people outside your territory, as well, as long as they aren't in a rival's territory. Gang size and number of operations are also tied to territory size). There are a lot of clicks necessary to get anything done yourself, but it is possible to set up delivery routes once you know what you're doing, eliminating the repetitiveness and allowing you to focus on the bigger picture. There are a few things missing from the game (I'd love to see some form of the Commission, for instance, where you can form alliances or deals with major rivals, or with other major cities), but all in all it is a solid game. I didn't realize it was done by an indie team, and I am very impressed. 4/5
