_childDocuments_.review: Well it's that time of year again, isn't that right? The spookiest month of the year where at the end, we go to other peoples houses for candy, and a trip to the operating room because of razor blades. The month also gives me an excuse to marathon spooky games, or movies, a tradition of mine that I started last year. And, since I'm hot off of watching all of Cyberpunk Edgerunners, I thought why not start off my horror game marathon with a cyberpunk horror game? That's exactly what The Observer is.So, is it good? Yes, I'd say so. Although like with every and any other game in existence, it's not perfect. I'll get my complaints out of the way first, and I'll start off with explaining my problems with the graphics options shmasm whatever you wanna call it. The graphics themselves are beautiful, no doubt, I played the game all the way through on ultra with ray-tracing and a solid 120 fps. Now, usually when I boot the game again, it's not capped to 120 fps, as my RivaTuner shows it running above that limit. While an fps above 120 sounds dandy, the reason I kept it at that limit is because I have a heavy workload gpu, and the unlimited fps that would go at least over 250 by the way, along with the ray-tracing and ultra settings at 1440p, not even 4K, would crank my gpu to 80 degrees. Thank god I had the RivaTuner monitoring. Also I had many, many stuttering issues across my 8 hours with the game. Luckily that's pretty much the only issues I've experienced, I didn't crash at all while playing, so that's good.Now, what's The Observer anyways? What's the story? Well I mean, you could always look at the Steam page...But I'll tell you anyways. Well, sometime in the future a very nasty war between two different sides of the world left each other in shambles, so much so that a Polish corporation took the reigns. If it couldn't get any worse there's the nasty Nanophage plague. The year is now 2084. You, the player, take the role of The Observer himself, Daniel Lazarski, who by the way is voiced by none other than the legendary late Rutger Hauer. Dan travels to what I can describe as the crappiest apartment complex that acts as the games' main liminal space, as he looks for clues and answers to figure out the whereabouts of his son, while uncovering a killer that is loose in the building which is on lockdown.Now what I can tell you is, that horror is subjective. This game may scare you, it may not. I'm not usually scared because I'm absolutely cold, and it takes the worst of the worst vile real world garbage to actually scare me. The events throughout the story itself, I wasn't able to clue it all together, but I think maybe its one of those things that is better just through pure speculation, an outside looking in thing if you will. I wouldn't say it's bad at all really. But, it's also not very engaging. While there are times when you have to avoid some kind of threat, these are very short lived and very few of em happen. Can't help but feel too that the acting seems just a bit off for some reason.Gameplay itself is fine. It's like a walking simulator with a hint of detective work. Collectables in the form of mugshots(?). it is what it is, you'll have to try it yourself to see if you like it or not. I sure didn't mind it all that much. That's pretty much all I've to say about the game, pretty solid experience from my point of view. I'd highly recommend it. This has nothing to do with my review, but I thought I'd make mention of it here. I can vaguely remember the day during the summer of 2019, I watched Blade Runner for the first time. The movie with it's visuals, themes, world, and the soundtrack, easily made it one of my top 5 movies of all time, and it was my introduction to the genre of cyberpunk. In a cruel ironic fate or twist, literally days after within the same week of watching the movie, it was announced that the actor in the film who plays Roy Batty, Rutger Hauer, who also voices Daniel in the Observer, had passed away at the age of 75. This man delivered one of the most memorable, chilling, and emotional monologues I've ever heard in any media. So, rest in peace Mr. Hauer, your memories and the impact you've made will not be lost in time like tears in rain. <3

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Cyberpunk genre, one of the key aspects of it is nailing the aesthetics of its world. The harshness and grit displayed with every loose wire and cable, the degradation of the apartments and almost anarchic state the residents live in is on point. And the body horror is up front and center, many of the tenants you see having signs of a hard lived life and losing much of their physical selves to genetic and cybernetic augmentation. The side stories themselves are interesting, with the well lived in apartments hosting a strange array of cases to explore and interesting dilemmas to interact with. Some cases even come with choices that, while not having a grand effect on the world, still feel personal as you investigate and utilize the most interesting mechanic of delving into the minds of others. These themselves are their own vivid scenarios, allowing for unique visuals that wouldn't otherwise make sense in such a gritty cybernetic world. The main story is intriguing, hitting strong and only ramping up in intensity, confusion and horror as we delve further into what Daniel's son was doing in such a decrepit place. With such a story-heavy game, it's no wonder the game-play itself is more of dressing rather than the main meat, with not many interesting mechanics to play with, no combat or major puzzle solving and only light stealth sections spread a fair bit apart. The environment and stories are engaging enough that first and possibly second play-through will help ignore this, but it is a game where replay-ability is low outside of achievement hunting.The weakest element to me was the scares of the game. When it attempts to intentionally startle you, it feels cheap: loud noises screeching at you, objects flying suddenly, bodies rapidly approaching you in inhuman ways. All of it strangely feels forced in, as the genuine dread and horror of the apartments themselves feel stronger. From the realization of the one room with the "fun" dolls and the animal in the basement, to the dread of something stalking around you but you're unable to ever really see it, only hear it occasionally, and then to your own psyche breaking as each observation into a mind drags out fragments of your own past and mingles with the memories of others. The horror and dread of the game's setting and story outweigh the otherwise weak scares it tries to give.TLDR:The story and side stories are the strongest points of the game, each giving interesting and horrifying realizations to the cybernetic hellscape that is Observer's world. Aesthetics are nailed to the letter, visually stunning, beautiful and ugly in all the right ways. Voices all range from fair to the lead voice actor himself, Rutger Hauer (Rest in Peace), and the audio is all kinds of juicy goodness. The gameplay and scares are the weakest aspects, with the former being simple clicks and minor stealth segments and running around from place to play, and the latter using every cheap tactic it can from screams to objects flying to things jumping at you suddenly. If you can tolerate relatively meh gameplay, the story, main lead and atmosphere carries the experiences from beginning to end!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite a ride. The beginning of it was more investigation / thriller getting more progressively horror and cerebral towards the end. There is a bit of a twist in terms of the main story too that is nicely weaved in with the killer the protagonist is hunting. The gameplay was straightforward as there is not much to the investigation mechanic besides scanning objects. Most of the focus is on the scanning and piecing together or finding the next piece of an investigation, so there is no challenge from hostiles. There are parts where you enter the minds of certain characters to piece together details needed to progress the story. These are self contained segments that are more experienced and have slight interactive moments. They become more and more intense as the game progress, which suggests the protagonist is losing grip with reality. This is a nice immersive element that makes sense given the details the game presents.The setting is mostly contained within a building and some underground segments, but even so it doesn't feel old or repetitive. There are enough parts that take you within dreamscapes, so in that way the building doesn't feel stale or restricting. The side quests are also memorable and the general foreboding mood makes the game consistently creepy. There is no escaping the dread of the world in this one as everything we see and read through the lore texts found throughout the game paint a traumatized society. The theme is definitely cyberpunk but with none of the glitzy decay seen in other media. All the hallmarks are present: augmentation, technological escapism, corporate control, questions around humanity and identity. The delivery and execution was unique, and the ending will stay with you for a bit, especially if you were exploring and trying to get as much of the lore as possible. If you are a fan of cyberpunk, this is a game to definitely play.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a very fun game. Excellent mystery, interesting setting, and gameplay that reminds me of Amnesia and Soma (in a good way).The reason this is a negative review is down to some questionable messaging on the topic of transhumanism. I'll explain in detail but if you want to play totally spoiler free stop reading here, because the game is still somewhat worth playing.To summarize my concern, there's a plot involving the topic of transhumanism, which for the sake of this discussion I'll define as unnecessarily modifying your body to either improve it or as a form of self expression. A critic of this in game makes an argument many might find familiar by saying this will hurt impressionable children in some nebulous way, and a spokesperson responds by comparing this to arguments made against transgender people in the past (our present).I feel this is a great comparison, and it's interesting to see a story where someone who could be seen as transspecies/otherkin gets to realize their true self. The problem is, in the context of this story, the critic is sort of right. Every single transhumanist character in the main story (I did not complete the side quests) is not only malicious, but very specifically predatory in some way. The writers addressed a dangerous stereotype, then played it completely straight.Yes it might be petty to be hung up on a relatively minor element of a video game's story, but cyberpunk as a genre is meant to explore these themes, and I feel it's important to think about what a story says if you're going to make piece of fiction so focused on its story. In hindsight I'm genuinely unsure if this was lazy writing and the creators thought the little interview about transphobia was a good defense of transgender people and transhumanism as a whole, or if the critic was meant to be right and this story is meant to say that these things are harmful.In either case, it's a major blunder that misses the entire point of the genre it explores. That's why I have to make this a negative review despite overall liking the game. I've not played anything else from Bloober, but I hear this is an ongoing issue they have when it comes to similar topics like mental illness and drug addiction.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty much a playable / linear book, you go from place to place, discovering more about the plot, there isn't really puzzles (some very basic ones like "find the password") and no danger (only very few / specific parts), which makes it be much less scary, as you don't have anything to avoid. Considering all of that, it would be a fine game for me personally, even if I really would prefer to be challenged. However: - one of the doors was supposed to be locked, but when I pressed against it, it snapped into being open, just to suddenly close again after I walked away a few steps, I was even able to enter the room, the door closes and you can't open, luckly I was able to load a save before that.- I had to interact with a screen, but it had a white glow so intense I was unable to see anything and had to replay a long section from a previous save (mind that it is pretty much all autosaves, so if I had done something else, I wouldn't be able to return to any saves)- Sometimes after scanning things, they stay on your screen, needing you to scan something else to try making it go away.- I got locked out of a certain optional part, because the cable I was supposed to connect nocliped, making me unable to grab it, and I didn't have any saves with it in the right place- I was unable to finish an optional quest the "regular way" because the thing I had to interact with simply wouldn't allow, requiring me to instead google the password to progress with it.Given all that, I even checked if the game was still being worked on to fix issues, but I didn't find anything on that. So I find it very risky to play it, even if it is a fine game when talking about gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very bizarre game and not in a good way. It's very confused and all over the place in terms of what it's trying to be. If it had been pure cyberpunk and ditched the horror it would have been a lot better. The cyberpunk stuff was interesting but the horror was awful. It was actually embarrassing. I can now see why (despite loving Blair Witch, my only other Bloober game) Bloober's horror games are hated. My god, it was so, so bad. I'm in awe of how bad is was, it really is something to behold. Literally screaming in your face, throwing things at the camera, begging you to be scared when its just obnoxious and irritating. Its about as scary as a two year old throwing a hysterical tantrum and just as annoying. If anything its taught me to stay far away from their other games. If you want an instruction manual on how to not do horror then this is perfect.I had to force myself to finish this game. Sadly I had gone over the 2 hour limit so I couldn't refund. The only thing that stops me from entirely regretting the purchase was the cyberpunk setting, story and the detective work. Though it is very disappointingly linear, your choices don't matter nor does talking to the residents. That's the only good thing I can say about it and even then it turned into a criticism.  Honestly, it isn't worth buying. Just consume other cyberpunk media instead. It isn't worth it for the terrible, obnoxious jump scares and embarrassing attempts at horror, it just spoils the rest of it. I was left angry and frustrated instead of scared or immersed each time they felt the need to ruin their own game. Don't get this, even on sale. If its ever free I guess there's no harm then if you just focus on the cyberpunk and detective work while trying to ignore the rest, if that's even possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Observer is a cyberpunk first person horror game that understand the genre and uses it to enhance its narrative and atmosphere.We play as a police detective in search of his son, last time seen in a apartment lot. We would have to move through it, looking for clues and asking questions to the residents.The game narrate its story through well written dialogues and its environment. With excellent art direction, it's fill with details and every prop is carefully crafted so that it fits with the style. A very good use of lighting emphasizes the horror moments and creates a heavy atmosphere that comes to a full circle with it excellent sound design and soundtrack.Another aspect that is important to bring out is the performance of the late great Rutger Hauer and the residents of the building, that give life to the world.In terms of mechanics, the game doesn't introduces us to nothing particularly complex, most of the time we will only walk around, asking questions and interacting with the environment. This can feel a bit underwhelming considering that the detective aspect of the game plays itself in a very linear fashion but it compensates the lack of complexity with scenes that play with the environments and uses its limited mechanics to create interesting moments for the player to resolve.The level design also invites us the explore and this leads to different side missions and backtracking that ads to the experience. This sometimes can fill detached from the main objective and its themes but give the oportunity to tackle other aspect of the genre better than most other games.One aspect that I think it's important to mention is that the game is not very well optimized. Though sometimes you don't notices it, the game has stuttering problems and very low framerates (20 sometimes) in particulare scenes. And the directx12 version, necessary to play with RTX, is (in my case) completly unplayble in any graphic settings.In conclusion, I think that Observer it's a great horror game and a good cyberpunk one that undestands its genre and uses to narrate the story, with excellent art direction and well written dialogues though sometimes can fell a little bit underwhelming in its mechanics but that it compensates with scenes that stick with you.

_childDocuments_.review: I still really despise the way they handled the release of this, but god, this game is just incredible. Bloober Team is really in their element here. If you liked Layers Of Fear, and you have any interest in cyberpunk media, you'll absolutely adore this. It's SUPER impressive to me how they managed to adapt that kind of gameplay/narrative format to such a dramatically different setting. Also, this game puts the Braindances in Cyberpunk 2077 to absolute shame.Haven't finished the game yet, I'm about 18 hours in right now, but I'll update this review if my feelings on all this stuff end up changing. There are some stealth elements that come into play later in the game, and I'm hoping those sections don't ruin it for me since I'm particularly averse to stealth games, but thus far it's been pretty carefully executed and largely auxiliary to the rest of what's going on the game, and I'm really happy about that. I'm glad the stakes haven't been too high for those aspects of the game yet. It's also really friendly about not setting you back if you fail--in fact, some of my progress actually remained after a game over, meaning even if you stumble over it repeatedly, it doesn't actually become a chokepoint. Really really good. We'll see how that holds up for the remainder of the game, but I'm feeling really optimistic about it thus far!Just... OK, here's my big gripe, and it isn't about the game itself, just the way they rolled it out. if you do another remaster like this, please give owners of the original game more time to take advantage of the discount. Even if it's only like a month or two extra before the deal expires. That's all. There should have been a Steam coupon (even if it expired quickly) so we actually got notifications about the discount. I didn't even hear about it until it was too late to take advantage, meaning I had to pay 20$ extra for a game I already owned most of. And I check Steam daily, bare minimum. I felt so actively burned by the whole thing that I almost didn't pick up this version. That's all. I've never had to go through the process of releasing a game on Steam though, so maybe this is all easier said than done.The game itself, though? God. One of the most visually breathtaking things I've ever seen, and one of the best games I've played in ages. So incredibly excited for what Bloober Team does next.

_childDocuments_.review: Revisiting 'Observer: System Redux' recently brought back a stark contrast to my experience with 'Cyberpunk 2077' from a couple of years ago. When I played 'Cyberpunk 2077,' it felt like CD Projekt Red missed the essence of what I personally seek in a cyberpunk universe – the atmosphere of Night City and the tone of the main story just didn’t hit the mark for me. This, of course, is a personal preference, and I understand it might not be the case for everyone. But compared to my playthrough of 'Observer' three years ago, and again now with the System Redux version, there’s a clear difference. 'Observer' immerses you in that dark, gritty cyberpunk world, something I found lacking in 'Cyberpunk 2077.'Rutger Hauer's voice acting in 'Observer' stands out remarkably, adding a depth that’s rare in video games. It’s a poignant reminder of his talent, especially knowing we won’t hear more from him. The game isn’t flawless, though. The fisheye lens effect and the restricted FOV admittedly do add to the atmosphere and give off a sense of claustrophobia that adds tension to the gameplay, but I would have appreciated the ability to turn some of those features off, as they did make me feel some motion sickness from time to time. Also, the way the audio was mixed, even after turning SFX down to 50%, the atmospheric sounds still drowned out the voices of the characters from time to time. That being said, I would consider these to be minor issues that did not keep me from enjoying my experience overall.My biggest complaint would have to be the game’s genre shift towards the end. Going from an intriguing psychological, detective story to a standard B-psychological horror game, felt rushed to me and was somewhat disappointing. I was really digging the detective aspect of the game, and that's actually what originally drew me in and set 'Observer' apart. i was let-down when the developers threw that aspect of the game aside and traded it for a tonal shift that didn't feel appropriate to me... Despite these downsides, I still greatly enjoyed the game; enough so that I've played through it twice now. 'Observer: System Redux' has made a lasting impression on me. Unlike many other games that fade into obscurity, 'Observer' stays with you, refusing to 'fade away like tears in the rain.' It’s a unique and haunting experience that leaves a lasting mark. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty much a walking simulator. This can be a hit or a miss for me. Personally, it was a miss. _childDocuments_.review: It was easy to see the evolution from Layers of Fear to this game, Observer; a lot of tropes and mechanics carried over, but some significant improvements to story telling made Observer rise above, offering a game with plenty to enjoy, even if there were a few issues along the way.The acting and voice overs, atmosphere and creativity was great. The game essentially takes place in a single apartment building, but you get a sense for what the wider world would be like, and the contents of the building serve to show hints at what life is like.  The game is a series of crime scenes that you use two different types of scanners to collect clues - biological and mechanical - until you've uncovered enough evidence to take a trip into the head of the dead guy, in which you experience significant portions of that characters memories and experiences, essentially to explain who the person is, some brief background, and ultimately what lead to their death. My main complaint with the game is these extremely disjointed "inside the persons head" experiences are so over the top, and so filled with effects and warping around, it actually gets in the way of the story they're trying to tell. There were times I reached the end of the experience and hadn't really picked up on anything they were trying to tell me because the effects and psychedelics was just so overwhelming and overdone. I think a bit of subtlety could've gone a long way, as it was, it kind of felt like the developers were trying to hard to be "out there" and the story got a bit lost behind it all.Overall I think the game had a lot of personality and character. I'd be interested in replaying it again in the future to see if I can find more info, and maybe understand some of the story I missed the first time. It would also be interesting to make some difference choices to see how it affects the outcome, even though I always have trouble making choices I don't agree with in games.Good game. A real trip.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing impressive, but it offers a little bit more than your average walking simulator. You have multiple vision modes and they seem to cause a strain on your body after prolonged use which is pretty cool. One thing that I cannot really get behind are the controls for interacting with things being trigger by default. Also opening doors is just plain awkward in that game. I would have liked it if the visions were more needed for progression than they seem to be.There is a lot to unpack with this and the game does well in doing so. It may fly over a lot of peoples heads what is actually going on and to be fair I am probably one of them. While an enjoyable experience as a whole, there was a lot of abstract concepts that made it hard to follow and make me just feel lost. Where the story had its challenges the visuals more than made up for it. The game was a visual flex. I may have had no idea what was actually happening, but I knew I had to run or just look at the pretty shapes. There are a lot of interesting and trippy visuals accompanied with this game.The voice acting was good and did what it achieved to do. It didn’t leave a lasting impression for normal dialogue. For the more trippy aspects, such as the building moaning or anything else in the dream state.. Hats off! The sound effects were also well done and added to the cyberpunk vibe.The game was a bit more surreal than I thought it would be, with a lot less people in it as well. There are like 2 people you ever talk to face to face which gives the game an empty feel. That said, it was in a lot of ways what I came to expect from the game. It was an enjoyable experience that may get another run later on down the line. A good game for anyone wanting a visual roller coaster in a cyber punk setting.

My only gripe was I did manage to accidentally tunnel the main story quest and beat to game far too soon and ignore the many other cool things do go do \  solve, whoops.  But I will be going back to do do them someday on a fresh game.10 \ 10 Will replay and try different endings.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a slow sci-fi, cyberpunkish walking simulator type of game where you play the role of a detective searching for his lost son. I found the writing for most of the side quests and some of the main quest in this game to be excellent, and reminiscent of shows like Black Mirror. It is some of the best writing and delivery of narrative I have ever seen and the narrative exploration remains as the best part of the game for me.However it is not without flaws and I personally found some of the memory jacking sequences and a few of the puzzles to be a little lacking. I didn't find most of the things in some of these memory sequences scary at all and just served as an obstacle to getting to the narrative as it didn't really add anything to it in my honest opinion. I also found some of the puzzles to be a bit annoying as there is really no clear design to a few of them, such as the one where you are exploring the hotel in the past. It's not really clear what you're supposed to do or why. I did figure it out but it does ruin the pacing of the narrative a bit in my opinion. Others seem to like these sequences so I'll chalk it up to a difference in personal preferences.I did find the actual ending to be unsatisfying as well. It felt a little too long and like some of the game play elements were added in to pad the length of the game. That said, I still enjoyed the game and I highly recommend it, due to the strength of the writing and delivery of narrative. It's not perfect but nothing ever is. If you guys like narrative driven, gritty sci-fi, this may be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is HIGHLY underrated. It's probably my favorite cyberpunk game of all time. I feel like the genre really lends itself well to body horror, and this game amps it up to 11. It's basically a walking detective sim that takes place almost entirely in an apartment building. The atmosphere is amazing. I feel like the developers really cared about putting as much detail as possible in this place. All the cases are interesting, and there's really no clear cut "good" outcome from your decisions. This is definitely not a feel-good game. The world is just so dark, and the more you learn about the characters the more depressing each one is. It's even a bigger bummer now that Rutger Hauer is gone. His performance is great in this game even if it feels very wooden at the start.The dream sequences are pretty good, and some definitely blew me away the first time I played the original game. I think they cut a little bit from some of them for the remaster which was good. A few of them went on too long (or at least felt that way during my playthrough of the original release). I was able to wrap up just about everything except the tedious card collection in just over 9 hours. Probably a bit longer if it's your first play through the game.If you haven't played the original then definitely pick this up. The lighting and details are a huge improvement even though I loved how dark the original game was. Even if you have played the original I thought the few dollars I spent for the redux were well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Needs more Polish"Cyberpunk horror from Poland? That's not a combination you see every day!Having finished the game now, though, that might be for the better. The Observer puts you in the boots of a mind-jacking future police in 2083 Poland, a country ravaged by cyber-plague, crime and megacorporations controlling all aspects of life. Standard cyberpunk affair, then, and the protagonists ability to invade minds to aid his investigations gives a lot of potential for interesting narratives, horror and visuals.The game does make the most of its engine and art style, catering plenty of imaginative visuals both in the real world and the various minds you explore. Flashing lights, holograms, glitches and more are everpresent, often to the point of overwhelming and inducing headache in the player. The world-building and art style both strive for excess, which can be hard to process.In the realm of audio the game doesn't fare nearly as well as in the visuals. Most of the voice acting is delivered in a laboured and stiff manner with many of the voice actors seemingly unconnected, unaware of how their counterparts delivered their parts. There are also several child characters who's voices are delivered so clearly by adults that it just starts to feel weird with how many child voices the game decides to have. As seems to be customary with Polish games the protagonist is also written as a deeply unpleasant person for the most part, with a personality swinging to and fro, often taking time to engage people in conversations just to annoy and anger them for no gain or reason.When it comes to the meat and bones of The Observer, the game itself, there isn't much to see. The vast majority of playtime for me was spent walking around, looking at things and exhausting pointless dialogue trees with characters I could not even see. The rest of the game consists of entering codes to open doors, scanning things for bits of information (looking at them, but while pressing a button), plugging cables into sockets and reading. Puzzle solving is relegated to a tiny sliver of game-play barely even worth mentioning. The game implies there are further mechanics available, such as a drug the protagonist must collect and use to stay sane and grounded in reality, but based on experimentation with this mechanic it doesn't actually seem to exist beyond a few visual quirks and a really annoying message the game blares at you if you fail to take your medicine in time.Lastly there is the horror. This is a horror game, right? Sort of? Well, at least according to Steam, but I didn't experience much horror here. For the most part The Observer just likes to play loud noises at you and flash jumpscare visuals in your face over and over again. Sudden changes in the environment, bright lights, sudden darkness, at least three occasions where a pidgeon flies into your face... it's all the cheapest scares you could put in your game that, for me at least, didn't do much. The only moment I felt something was truly horrifying and scary in the game came in just minutes before the end of the game, and the experience was swiftly nullified by the flat, ambiguous ending the game dropped on me.Beyond the main story the game offers an array of side quests, though with these I feel I must warn any potential player. The side quests all seem to end without any impact on anything. In fact I feel like none of the side stories actually resolved in any way, rather ending with the protagonist deeming they had seen all they neede to see, shrugging and walking away. Case closed.Playtime: 7+ hours (A single playthrough)Ratings (1-10)Visual: 8Audio: 7Story: 3Gameplay: 3Overall: 4

_childDocuments_.review: The game's narrative is a standout feature, plunging players into a gripping cyber-noir detective story. You step into the shoes of Daniel Lazarski, an Observer, who is part detective, part hacker, and tasked with investigating gruesome murders in a grimy, post-apocalyptic Krakow. The story is thought-provoking and densely layered, delving into themes of identity, technology, and the consequences of unchecked power.Visually, "Observer: System Redux" is a treat for the eyes. The remastered graphics take full advantage of modern hardware, creating a dark and atmospheric world that feels both futuristic and oppressive. The attention to detail in the environments and character models adds to the game's immersion, drawing players deeper into the dystopian setting.One of the game's defining features is its use of psychological horror. As an Observer, you have the ability to hack into the minds of suspects, uncovering their darkest fears and memories. These sequences are deeply unsettling and create an atmosphere of unease that lingers throughout the game. The tension is further heightened by the superb sound design, which includes haunting ambient noises and a chilling soundtrack.Gameplay in "Observer: System Redux" is a mix of detective work, exploration, and puzzle-solving. The detective segments involve scanning crime scenes and interrogating suspects, while the hacking sequences transport you into surreal and nightmarish mindscapes. The puzzles are well-designed, offering a satisfying blend of challenge and intrigue.This remastered edition also introduces new content, including additional story elements that shed light on the world's lore and provide a more comprehensive narrative experience.While "Observer: System Redux" offers a compelling and immersive journey, it may not be for everyone. The psychological horror elements can be quite intense, and the narrative is deliberately paced, focusing on storytelling rather than action.In conclusion, "Observer: System Redux" is a dark and captivating cyberpunk thriller that excels in storytelling, atmosphere, and psychological horror. The remastered visuals and additional content enhance the original experience, making it a must-play for fans of dystopian narratives and psychological thrillers. It's a thought-provoking and unsettling journey that will leave you questioning the boundaries of technology and the depths of human consciousness.

The game's cyberpunk world is beautifully realized, with intricate details and stunning visual effects that help to transport players into a dark and dangerous future. The game's soundtrack is also exceptional, with hauntingly beautiful music that perfectly complements the game's atmosphere and tone.Another standout feature of Observer: System Redux is the game's storytelling, which is complex and thought-provoking. The game's plot is a twisted and intricate web of lies, conspiracies, and personal demons, all of which are masterfully woven together to create a deeply engrossing and engaging narrative. The game's characters are also well-written and well-acted, with each one bringing their own unique perspective and motivations to the story.Overall, Observer: System Redux is an exceptional game that combines stunning visuals, immersive gameplay, and thought-provoking storytelling to create a deeply engrossing and satisfying experience. If you're a fan of Cyberpunk or horror games, or if you simply enjoy games with rich and complex narratives, then Observer: System Redux is definitely worth checking out.Overall Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply personal and disturbing masterpiece. In fact, both "Observer: System Redux" and "Layers of fear 2" are somehow the end of the psychedelic, labyrinthine and nightmarish concept of videogames that defined Bloober Team's early stages. Not exactly Walking Simulators or Haunted Houses, but at the same time definitely not action-oriented, they make us walk and go deep into their characters (and worlds) pain and suffering. What makes them special, compared mostly to their follow-ups ("Blair witch" and "The Medium") is that there's nothing streamlined or easy about them. Some users might find Bloober's early games confusing or pointless, but that only indicates how personal and subjective these games are ("What remains of Edith Finch" comes to mind, but with all of its ugly parts and none of the beautiful ones). Even if "Blair Witch" and "The Medium" also deal with long journeys, both corporeal and psychological, they're more mainstream both in concept and execution, so the experience is not as rewarding (for some users will be much easier to grasp).Observer: System Redux is expertly crafted and designed. It's more an experience of loss and destruction, filled with fun puzzles and disturbing images, than an action-packed adventure. That's what makes it special and unique. Not for everybody, but highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what I think, when I hear Cyberpunk. Dark, dystopian climate, harsh and brutal futuristic world. Full of strange people, and even stranger events happening around you. You cannot be sure, who is living next door to yours. Maybe it is normal person, or serial killer? Who knows?Despite the fact that the game is relatively short, there is a very interesting vision of the futuristic world. An interesting story and the issues that you will have to solve along the way, make you want to end this game in one long session. Great job from Bloober Team!

_childDocuments_.review: For real cyberpunk experience this is likely among the best you can ever find, the vibes are there and the tension the grimy dystopian and depressing world of man and machine and virtual world blended into a twisted mind warp if there is one. It's less a detective game but more a dark, semi horror exploration of this fascinating world.The Good+ Interesting premise with its blend of old world detective noir, with cyberpunk dystopian environments.+ The plot is an interesting one, nothing new but with the vibes and ambiance its gritty, mysterious and pulls you in.+ The world building within the apartment as well as when you connect to the mind of the virtual world is well built and the graphics and sounds adds to the overall experience.+ The mini games are an interesting distraction to the main story and quite enjoyable.+ The use of the game mechanics like investigation, hacking and mind dives are not the best use of its capabilities and turns the game at times into just a linear walking sim, which is unfortunate.+ Some of the creation, scenes and themes are quite gory and frankly eldritch, combining both techno and biological fear triggers in many cases.+ The achievements really make you work, and I'm not too gung ho to get 100% for this game, some of the bar is too high to be worth another playthrough.The Bad- Generally there's only a single living being you interact with, with the exception of residents behind locked doors which you talk through the vid phones, the rest are dead.- Most of the exploration and mind investigations are more linear and at times fall back on jump scares than anything, yet it does create great atmosphere that it doesn't get too bland and boring.- Finding the collectible cards in the dark atmosphere and monotones environments can be hell, and most are missable so without a guide generally you won't be finding them all for sure.- The investigation part is a bit weak and at some point you really can't back track to find things you missed early game, so its a pain.- There are some glitches when i find i am stuck in an infinite loop and can't progress.-  The flashing lights and strobes as warned may not be user friendly to some gamers, be warned. Even I felt it at times.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to try this game and delve into a character portrayed by Rutger Hauer. The setting of the story is interesting: dystopian Krakow where the protagonist somewhat resembles Rick Deckard from Blade Runner (the irony isn't lost on me).However, in a sentence, I would describe this game as a nauseating door simulator.The movement of the first person perspective is delayed and had involuntary motion, which even to a seasoned gamer who loves first person shooters causes nausea within minutes. Especially crouching is awful, awful, awful. Combined with the camera zooms when interacting with things, on this point alone I would not recommend this game to anybody of the human race. 🤮On top of that, the visual effects of glitching and speckles over integral UI elements and the world itself is in its own right headache inducing and frustrating when you are trying to read something.It should also be pointed out that the game is not accessible to a broad audience due to extremely dark graphics (even with the gamma set to maximum) and subtitles not displaying with spoken English audio.Then, the interactions in the world. These are needlessly complicated, like opening doors and closets, drawers, cabinets. I have lost patience in trying to position myself in such a way that the door can be swung open in the right direction with the right amount of force (because otherwise it bounces back and closes again).The story is interesting at first, but becomes convoluted to the degree that you will find yourself randomly walking around the tenement building to find the room you overlooked. The place is so oddly constructed that you will constantly lose your orientation, and combined with the nausea factor, will have absolutely no fun in doing so. After all, in the end, almost all the interactions are through doorbell conversations, which truly tests your patience.Incidentally, the voice acting is lackluster. Not because Hauer isn't a good actor, quite the contrary; much of the dialog is a conversation between two people, and it's plainly obvious that the voice recordings were not done together.The game developers appear to have acknowledged that the game is slow-paced, and have added an extremely frustrating game element of needing to administer medicine on a periodic basis.While I loved the art direction of the world that is created and the character you play, I am very sorry to say that this game is just woefully underwhelming and downright unpleasant to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely dystopian cyberpunk noir horror story what else is there to say. You play as a cyborg "Detective" aka Observer who is trying to find his son or more what is left of him in a slum apartment building full of suspicious people and freaks. You have a main story and many small side stories that can be done or totally ignored. The good type about this apartment complex playstyle is that you dont even know sometimes what belongs to the main story. If you just ask questions and do interrogations with neighbors you will eventually do side quests without realizing it. The whole story feels truly authentic and the conversations have a very deep meaning behind it so you must be a bit intelligent to understand it fully. Graphic is pretty and I highly recommend to play with raytracing on, because reflections will only be visible while on.Spooky elements are common but you have enough time to explore and no time limits so you can just walk around freely in the areas. Many information is hidden so it is highly recommended to search the rooms for both Visual and Body components. Lazarski aka yourself can use a body/blood analysing gadget by pressing "Q" and a visual/machinery analysing gadget by pressing "E". With your middle mous button you can use your intercom which will show you your current information and the possibility to use drugs if you have high blood pressure or instability with gadgets. It is possible to die so you should check the intercom whenever your character feels weak.Altogether a really good game with an impressive story and nice visuals.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This team has some very talented environmental artists, some scenes are pretty stunning. It is a decent horror/sci-fi adventure/puzzle/walking-sim game, which borrows themes and aesthetics from sources like Ghost in the Shell, The Matrix, Cyberpunk (the tabletop RPG), Blade Runner, Alien. The puzzles are all right.The game relies too much on cheap jump scares though (the same team made Layers of Fear), so if you get it I hope you enjoy screeching noises and threatening shapes rushing at you constantly. The relentless grimness and misery of the single apartment building the game takes place in, and the horrifying fate of almost every person in it eventually makes you feel numb. I think they should have added some normality and everyday life into the scenery as some contrast. But what ultimately made me turn this into a not-recommended is the painfully bad dialogue, full of action movie cliches and non-sequiturs. I would genuinely not have been surprised if he had said "Damn...just one day away from my retirement. Just my luck huh" at one point. The voice acting by Rutger Hauer as the player character is often monotonous and bored, like he feels it is below his dignity as an actor to read this script. Unfortunately I think he is right.

_childDocuments_.review: The plot is interesting with surprising developments. But the gameplay is so monotonous that I regretted buying the game. Cheap jumpscares. Enemy encounters are poor, the game fails to create a tense atmosphere, I guess the developers' idea was that the more abstract the better, but in this case I don't think it worked. Too much surreal and symbolic elements that, even justified by the context, make the storytelling boring.Do you know the saying "don't tell the story, show it"? It is difficult to understand the story when half of what is shown is abstract and the other half are scattered fragments mixed with visual and sound noises such as glitches, screams, white noise, etc...Another thing that bothered me was the apathy of the protagonist, who, faced with his own loss of mental faculties and his sanity hanging by a thread, acts like "am I going insane? Nah, it must have been the wind".However, the game also has its positive points beside the plot, for example the possibility of making decisions with moral conflicts, and secondary stories that are worth exploring by reading emails and talking to tenants.

_childDocuments_.review: Observer: System Redux serves as a remaster and a "definitive edition" of the surreal cyberpunk horror game Observer. I should mention that System Redux is NOT a sequel of Observer, it's the same game with a few additions. You play as Daniel Lazarski, a detective voiced by late actor Rutger Hauer, the antagonist in iconic cyberpunk movie Blade Runner. The game not really linear and has some light RPG elements, as you can free roam in the hub area (up until the point where you have to go to the attic), it has sidequests, and also offers dialogue choices. Like their previous game Layers of Fear, do not expect a traditional mystery game with this one, as things get weird often.For new content, there are 3 new sidequests, 7 new levels of the Spiders minigame, and a Blade Runner reference. There are also some updated mechanics, such as the ability to load older saves and view collectibles from the main menu. The graphics and lighting are updated to look better, but it is costly in performance. You might want to reconsider buying this if you have a weak PC. It would be better if Observer: System Redux is packaged with the original one since that one is considerably lighter on performance. Sadly, there are still some bugs on this game. Some collectibles do not appear, you can access the basement early, and the shrine cables from a new quest is buggy. Luckily, it can be bypassed by using a walkthrough to proceed to the next part of the quest. I personally think cyberpunk horror is a cool but underutilized genre. There are just so many possibilities with that one, and Observer is one great example of cyberpunk horror. It's a different take from the usual existentialism or transhumanism theme in cyberpunk media. For me, it is Bloober's best game so far. Definitely one of the coolest cyberpunk games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: A master pice worth playing: nice graphics, atmosphere, scenes, ideas, narrative.There is no combat. The only action involved requires a bit of stealth and patience. Puzzles are mostly about finding or deducing a code (to open doors), but there are also about finding the right order/combination of paths (v.g. an endless room; persecution...) or combinations of locks (v.g. light switches), and moving/connecting objects (v.g. a tv, computer, animal...). Reading logs is encouraged to help you to deduce access codes (e.g. finding and using a certain name, book etc) and to understand the main story and tenants'.It is easy to complete the main story without an online walkthrough, but if it is needed there are tons available.P.S. Redux is worth if you haven't played the original; you played the original long ago and you liked it; or you are a huge fan of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Observer: System Redux is probably one of the most unique psych-horror games I have ever played...the dream eater sequences are truly mind blowing. In this game you play as a cyberneticly enhanced detective who gets a call from his estranged son and goes out to investigate. These are my pros/cons of the game:+ story is intriguing from start to finish and will keep you glued to your seat+ character development is very well done, and by the end the protagonist is well rounded+ game is approximately 7 hours in length with the fat trimmed; likely 10+ hours if you pursue side objectives+ game encourages exploration through intrigue but outside achievements no actual rewards (aside from world building which I enjoy)+ game will make you question reality and will have you on the edge of your seat going "wtf did I just experience"+ the scenarios in the game are well thought out and do tug on your emotions- only negative I can think of is when you access the mission log, the text would be slightly difficult to read because they were going for the bladerunner cyberpunk feel and added that screen tearing effect to add to the vibe. Its honestly not that big of a deal and this is nitpicking. I would definitely recommend this game and will likely replay it again probably closer to Halloween or when I get that detective/cyberpunk itch. Like I said before, this is a unique experience that will hold your attention and be hard to forget.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this to you but I can't. The first half of the game is actually really fun, the puzzles while sometimes very obscure are satisfying to solve, and the world building is phenomenal. However, around the halfway mark the story takes over and it's super convoluted. Some game mechanics are super buggy and you will be running around interacting with everything only to come back to what you interacted with first and now it magically works. Get this if it's heavily discounted. Can be fun for the right person. But definitely not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much to say about Observer System redux, I honestly don’t know where to begin.I’ll start with a simple statement:  I love this game!Observer System Redux is an immersive, atmospheric, story based, exploration based, puzzle based, crime scene investigation based walking simulator.  There are many side quests to find, many areas to explore and collectibles to uncover.  It took me around 8 hrs to finish the game my first time through.This game is a trip. The immersion level is off the charts.  It’s setting and ambiance are imaginative, unique and profound.  The Cyberpunk setting is perfectly executed in terms of visual fidelity and artistic design. The presentation is simply wonderful.  Yes it’s super dark but the colors ‘pop’ and overall is a visual feast to the eyes.  Visually the artistic design is just so imaginative, it really blew my mind.  Sure the game takes place in an apartment complex… doesn’t sound too imaginative, does it?… but the game goes everywhere.  It takes the viewer on a wild, David Lynch inspired ride.  You’ll find yourself in many David-Lynch-esque set pieces, constantly being surprised by what the game throws at you.  It keeps you interested.  In fact, I would go so far as to say that ‘Observer System Redux’ is one of the most interesting games I’ve ever played.And now for the  negative.  Performance wise, the game can be a little choppy during its loading sequences.  There are no loading screens but you can tell when the game is loading a new section by the way the game stutters for around a second.  It happens quite often but but compared to what the game does right, it almost feels silly mentioning it.  When the game is running, it runs buttery smooth.If you like immersive, story based, moody, grim, cyberpunk experiences, you’ll love this!!
_childDocuments_.name: Observer: System Redux

_childDocuments_.review: This game was insanely good and has easily made it up there with some of my favourite games of all time. A really unique cyberpunk mystery. This game was trippy as hell though, don't think i have ever said wtf to myself so many times playing a game before lol. There was a couple of bugs but nothing too annoying or game breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: RIP Rutger HauerThis is an incredible experience. As a lover of all things Cyberpunk, I had to pick this up once more (completed on XBOX at release). From just a visuals perspective, this game nails the aesthetic. Moody, dark, and grim, this is a glimpse at a dark cyberpunk world following a terrible nanophage. Nothing is glamorized, here. This is a setting that is not ideal for the future! But it feels real. The story is incredible and very, very tense. I jumped a lot in this game. Yes, it is horror which may through some people off (I wouldn't have minded a peaceful mechanic like SOMA to be honest!), but it's worth all the clenched teeth.Rutger Hauer is incredible. His voice sounds like smooth granite in your ears as you play the game. I could listen to him read an encyclopedia. He's the king of the cyberpunk genre and I'll resist a Tears in the Rain comment (though the game itself doesn't resist mentioning it either))  ).Ultimately, a wonderful experience to add to any game collector who loves the story driven, "walking simulator", genre. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Mindbendingly awesome, I dont want it to end. If you want "bang bang" run/gun off the mill gaming, this is not for you. If you want amazing, atmospheric storydriven cyberhorror with themes from neuromancer, ghost in the shell, akira and Bladerunner - this is what you have been waiting for. I adore it - but im not going to be able to sleep tonight.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game. It's hard to bring words to this thing. I'm still trying to digest it, to let it seep into my psyche, let it take over my body like the Nanophage plague. I..It's an EXPERIENCE unlike any other I've had in gaming. Observer IS dystopian. It's Uncomfortable. It's wet. Nasty. The visuals are striking and horrific...and ABSOLUTELY PERFECT. I loved the dread I felt with this game. The way the game is crafted, visually...it's rare to be able to look at something on screen and be able to engage your other senses. You can FEEL the oppressive world in which Chiron Corp RULES. You can smell the rot and decay of trash, of mold slowly crawling up the walls, and to an extent, your character. The technology is betraying you, failing, the sparks flying and dripping with the rain and leaking roofs. The smell of burnt and charred plaster, the pools of blood and smell of ozone is UNREAL, yet familiar. A murder mystery, plain and simple, that leads to the dark corners of a horrible, nightmarish, cyberpunk future of dystopian hymns and dirges. At one point, I had to put the game away. At a certain point, it affected me so much that I had to step away for a few days...and that has never happened. It was great to come back and dive into this nightmare.  The soundtrack really sets the mood, too. I dare say this is *the definitive cyberpunk experience I wanted*. This is up there with my all time favorite games, Edging out Silent Hill 2 by only a small margin. HIGHEST RECOMMENDATION.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent on almost all front.I enjoyed getting lost and talking to the residents, finding all the passcodes, and uncovering the smaller narratives between residents. Seeing how they economised time effectively with gifs when talking to them, jerky object movements and glitch to act as animation when making the game. Sound design and its correlations to visual audio disturbances throughout was excellent. I think they caught that players get lost as at one point the menu screen flashed go to apartment such and such.I felt like they wanted to cover and integrate every cyberpunk storyline which hindered it or made it needlessly sprawling for the main story especially with the jumps to new locations which would stretch out. I reckon the monster walking around needed to only be that. I got caught once near the end by it multiple times, which just made me go ergh reload, reload,reload,reload. Its simple presence throughout the game didn’t detract from the experience of fear at all. Very enjoyable game overall though and up there as a favourite.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing story driven narrative games for a while and Observer: System Redux does bring a fresh breath of air in this game category. Its world actually feels like living in Cyberpunk dsytopian era rather than just having the tag line of being a cyberpunk game that so many other games do in this genre but not actually relating to it much. Main story arc was pretty good and its side quests were equally good because all of these quests kept me curious to find out what was going on in each of these cases. I couldn't grab few of the achievements as it seems they are triggered only if some of the items or objectives are to be found in sequence. But otherwise solving each case and grabbing the achievements was fun. Variety of mini games in dream sequence was quite good, but some of them are pretty hard as well, like Adam's mind mini-games and achievement associated with it on scoring 3K. Game is mostly linear but unlike other narrative games this one has actually some gameplay elements rather than just pressing random buttons that flash on screen or QTE.Game runs smoothly 90% of time even on 10yrs old PC at medium graphic setting, but it still has some game breaking glitches which could totally ruin your playthrough if it occurs during important events as it doesn't have manual quick save option. One glitch I found was during Helen's dream sequence whrby if you left the mini tv behind the door would lock and you will be stuck in loop of going to nxt stage area but warping back to locked door. Second game breaking glitch was in the sewers after unlocking a locked door upon operating a big switch box opposite to it. Once you enter through the gate, passed through some pipes and as you walk towards a tunnel with a big door infront, there is sometime "UE-4 Tokio file lowlevelfatal error". In my case after hours of trying everything from downloading DX11 to checking graphic card updates and manual settings ingame, what worked was clicking the game file check option in STEAM. It found 1 file was corrupted, re-download 9 GB of file and after that only I could proceed ingame. Sometimes interactive objects related to the case would be stuck in the walls or floor so you would have to re-load the last auto-save and hope it fixes the glitch. So my advise, make a copy of "SaveGames" folder (ObserverSystemRedux\Saved\SaveGames) anytime you think important event is about to begin.Apart from these glitches, rest of the game is pretty good and I enjoyed it a lot, had some jumpscares too. In the final arc both endings were super satisfying. Rarely game will have endings that make sense and also makes the gamer happy. Overall, I would definitely recommend this game if you enjoy good story and like solving cases. Rating: 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating mind bender of a game, not what I usually play but I felt like a change! Admittedly, I found a lot of it hard to follow but I was able to piece it together here and there near the end.Observer is a narrative driven, text heavy game told in a cyberpunk dystopian future, with clear inspiration from sources such as Blade Runner that shape the weird and wonderful world you find yourself in. Additionally there's a huge aspect of psychological horror where nothing ever seems quite right, as if reality is tearing itself apart and curdling with your worst nightmares that only get worse the further down the rabbit hole you go. Its slow burning, somewhat of a walking simulator, but you can interact with most things in the world.You find yourself in an apartment complex after receiving a strange message from your son, only for it to go into lock-down with no means of escape (sounds familiar...). You play as Daniel Lazarski, a detective, but not just any old detective, you're part of a special neural branch known as the Observers who have advanced ways of investigating crime scenes, gathering evidence and even breaking into peoples minds as a form of "Interrogation" to forcefully relieve them of information, regardless of whether they are dead or alive.As mentioned, its quite text heavy, I don't usually play games like this or anything that may require you to read reams of information so I did skim over a LOT of information in favour of a speedier playthrough but for those who like to get fully immersed and like to appreciate everything a game like this has to offer, then you could definitely get lost in mountains of theories and discoveries, especially since the game isn't just a straight forward single story, as there are additional investigations you can do that uncover the horrors going on just inside that complex alone.The whole game is just insanely strange, but in a really good way...it's a shame my brain isn't big enough to fully appreciate or comprehend what is happening but it was still brilliant to play and by the end I was able to get enough of an idea as to not feel like I came out the other end with nothing.It's thanks to this game that I also learned of Rutger Hauers death, very unfortunate but a fantastic actor and he did some great voice acting in this too. Rest in peace Rutger!

_childDocuments_.review: it takes a lot to make me feel good about spending 30$ on a ~10hr walking sim with some stealth sequences. But Observer did it. I recommend this game without reservation to any and all fans of the cyberpunk genre. The phrase I kept using to describe this game to my friends was "Bladerunner meets Silent Hill" it's gorgeous, it's fun to play, it's very scary and spooky, it's compelling, it's atmospheric, and Rutger Hauer's performance is one of the best in video game history.

_childDocuments_.review: Next gen upgrade of a cyberpunk horror from a few years back.Pros:- Impressive visuals with ray tracing- Unique art direction, retro-futurism rooted in Polish communist aesthetics- Finely-crafted environment of a slum tenement building located by Plac Matejki in Kraków- Good world-building through side-quests- It's a Polish Bladerunner- Accurate vision of a future where you didn't invest in Eastern PolandCons:- By-the-numbers cyberpunk story somewhat lacking in fresh ideas- I guess music is kind of there, but it's never noticeably good- Mind hacking sections feel tedius due to lack of interactivity, for the most part being a walking simulator that drags on too long- Not very spookyOverall, it's pretty good. I'd recommend getting it on sale where it's at a price you feel comfortable paying for a niche 8-hour indie game.

_childDocuments_.review: this was fantastic. the story is well done, everyone has a past and the country has some serious recent history, but youre never bogged down in exposition. actually, you could miss all of it and stay on the main path. my favorite part was off the path, exploring this slum building and checking every door and corner shows how detailed this really is. even the childrens books get more deranged as you go. the scenes are creatively scary, theres one in an office turning a radio dial i thought was beautifully done. i dont expect much more than neon signs and robot prostitutes when its cyberpunk these days, its great to see theres still people who can make something great out of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good. But I expected more from the game. I want to describe what I did not like. I did not like the fact that this game did not bring anything new in terms of describing the human consciousness. All ideas are old. There is no deep description, at least from the point of view of science fiction, how consciousness is arranged and how it works, whether it is reflex, and so on. Existential questions are not dealt with in depth enough. In terms of genre, The Observer falls short of Ghost in the Shell as a work of fiction. At the end of the game, the developers deliberately make a logical error in the game scenarios of the behavior of one of the main characters in order to add artistry to the plot. I can’t say what kind of logical error we are talking about, because on this is built just do the whole essence of the game, its logical meaning.  In terms of plot, the game is weak, but worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: A walking simulator with horror elements and confusing pseudo-psychological nonsense.Don't get me wrong, the story is really good--once you start understanding it. Unfortunately by the time the plot becomes clear, your character's perception of it becomes unreliable.Movement is painfully slow, and there are sections which slow you even further, which makes the map feel three times as large as it really is.The purpose of Synchrozine is unclear: it's obvious you need to use it after an interrogation because you get an audible warning, but other than that the sync meter doesn't provide any useful information.And most damning of all, it's not clear when the main plot will lock you out of all the subplots until it happens, which means the ending sequence can have flashes of "memories" of sub-cases you haven't actually resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting alot from this game but it was surprising good with its dark aesthetic and atmosphere. The visuals and good voice acting of the cast create an immersive experience which draws you in. While the gameplay is the standard walking simulator format of Bloober with some interactive elements, and the puzzles are straightforward, the real draw is the rich world-building.You play as a detective with the ability to dive into people's minds, trying to locate your estranged son who contacted you out of nowhere while unraveling a conspiracy in a dystopian slum (filled weirdos) and discovering the various horrifying things unfolding in the building. The plot is intriguing but cryptic, requiring you to piece together the story through various themes and interactions. The first half is fairly chill but the story picks up pace and goes wild towards the end. The side quests and interactions with the tenants add depth bringing the world to life with its dark, cyberpunk vibe. Everyone that you meet in this game is flawed in someway and has their own unique story which I really liked. The ending was unexpected and leaves room for potential sequels.The game had lots of  flickering lights/glitching effects, etc  that made me nauseous, and frequent crashes with ray tracing(No crashes on DX11). Despite these problems, the experience was enjoyable and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really good time with this one.  It’s a very interesting game with a solid story.  There is no combat in this game, as you are a detective who tried to solve the murder of his own son in the distant future. You investigate clues and interview people door to door in his apartment complex.  At times it is pretty funny, but most of the time it’s pretty darned grim.  The gameplay will stay with me for a long long time, it is super original and the graphics are absolutely breathtaking.  It also has puzzles you must solve, some of which are pretty difficult.  I would definitely recommend this game, especially if you love cyberpunk and sci-fi.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the old version about two years ago and I've played for one new game+, recently thinking about have one more NG+ in this version. I would say this is the cyberpunk I really want, absolutely one of my favorite cyberpunk artwork. This game really get the kernel thinking of the word "cyberpunk": abuse of technology, dehumanize, unlimited power of the corrupted cooperation / government. We don't always need mega buildings, Japanese food or something like that to represent cyberpunk because those are just something floating on the shallow surface, those are just one way of some cyberpunk artwork used to illustrate their world. In my opinion, cyberpunk can be a wider idea than those stuff we usually see on internet pop culture, Blade Runner or Ghost in Shell are excellent works but it doesn't mean they are the template of cyberpunk. Things like Observer, or an old manga called BLAME! are also another fantastic way of expressing the cyberpunk. So, if you want to try something hard core under this topic, you can't miss this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to games from Bloober Team I'm very sceptical, because all their games I've played so far (namely Layers of Fear 1 and 2 and Blair Witch) have been mediocre at best. Observer doesn't deviate much from Bloober Team's known horror walking sim formula but it has some cool little bits that slightly elevate it above the other mentioned Bloober Team games.Observer is set in a dystopian cyberpunk future of 2084 and you play as detective Daniel Lazarski (personated by Cyberpunk cult actor Rutger Hauer), who is looking for his son in a deranged apartment building and stumbles upon some gruesome murders. What sounds simple at the start, gets more and more confusing and in the end the story conclusion doesn't really make much sense. The muddled narrative is accompanied by very simplistic gameplay: You explore the building, interogate the residents through their apartment doors, deal with a few puzzles and scan the environment for clues how to solve them. Very rarely, maybe three or four times during the whole game, you have to traverse through an area with patroling enemies by using simple stealth tactics, nevertheless the main gameplay focus is clearly on the story and atmosphere and exploring the detailed environment. But while the Bloober Team gameplay formula is simply a matter of taste, the couple of gamebreaking bugs I encountered are an inexcusable and embarassing nuisance that really shouldn't happen in a "Redux" remaster: At one or two points the game seemingly failed to trigger certain events which prevented progress and required reloading a previous save state. Apart from that, the game runs silky smooth on highest grafics settings.   What Observer lacks in storytelling and engaging gameplay is compensated through its presentation: It's dense Blade Runner-inspired atmosphere and cyberpunk style are carried by rather detailed grafics, decent sound, voice acting and music and fancy visual effects. But note: If you are epileptic, stay the hell away from this game.Generally, Observer is just another so called "horror"-walking sim, but thanks to it's distinct cyberpunk setting it belongs to the rather enjoyable titles of this genre. Despite this, even hardcore walking sim fans should bring at least some affinity for Sci-Fi and cyberpunk and shouldn't have too high expectations in terms of thrilling horror and terrifying jumpscares to avoid disappointment. _childDocuments_.review: It's more Cyberpunk than the game by that very name. _childDocuments_.review: Observer was flat out amazing! A dystopian cybernetic fever dream. Cyberpunk done right. Truly a masterpiece in presentation and extraordinary technological craftsmanship (redux version is a step above).  The development teams hard work is on full display and has worked to further immortalize Rutger.. I highly recommend people buy this game immediately. Then if you want more detective Hauer watch Split Second. Sure hope the team can revisit this world again sometime.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited about this, as a fan of both Rutger Hauer and detective walking sims. When researching the game online I saw plenty of reassurance that it was just a crime-solving walking sim with no enemy encounters. Sounds right up my alley!Well, there are definitely some enemy encounters of the hide 'n' sneak variety. There aren't many, they are quite easy (despite sluggish controls), and it's mostly relegated to the dream hack sequences; but if this is a deal breaker - which it pretty much is, for me - I would rather warn sensitive players than downplay or pretend it's not there.The game also put me off in a few other ways: there's no real deduction to be done, just basic clue hunting. This was a disappointment given the detective-centric marketing. The end of the story goes into rather stupid territory and many of the plot points (including the optional cases) are just edgier-than-thou scenarios that don't really explore anything. There sure are some lovingly detailed slum environments though.Speaking of which: the aesthetic is heavily overdone at times, especially during the dream hack sequences. It's headache inducing and noisy, both visually and aurally. Those sequences can be very difficult to navigate as a result and I hugely preferred the meatspace segments to the cyberspace ones. Pathfinding through the labyrinthine, claustrophobic apartment complex was a personal highlight - I even completed most of the optional cases (although I didn't finish one due to a bug; the subject matter wasn't worth retrying after a reload).When all's said and done, I did enjoy some aspects of the game and I appreciate what Bloober Team were trying to do. There's clearly some talent on display here, if not taste. But if you're looking for a monster-free deduction game, this ain't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Observer: System Redux

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible journey out of the mind and into the ether. What starts as a fairly routine crime investigation slowly dissolves into chaos and digital nightmare. Extremely detailed, visually resplendent and artistically expressive, this game is visceral and evocative. The late Rutger Hauer gives one final performance in the genre he helped start in films; this time in a media that is ever prescient to the core of the cyberpunk ethos. A great work by a team of dedicated professionals.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, first of all  this is a real cyberpunk:)They say that cyberpunk is dead and it is Post-Cyberpunk time, where nearest future is not so dark, corporactions are not so bad and so on.We are having lots of hollywood style cyberpunk (or post cyberpunk) games with an overabundance of pathos and epic. Mos of them, erm, just games with epic and futuristic setting.But this one is a real golden grail!  And its not about how it is dark and gloomy - the biggest plus of the game that it feels really  natural and organic.The second big advantage  is "gameplay".  Actually it better be called "expirience".  This is a good example of a Video game as an art form. In most of games  gameplay mechanics are in the foreground. I mean it is really difficult for person who is really not into computer games to interact with all artistic filling of a game. You need to think at first about mechanics (character upgrade, weapons and e.t.c) and only if you able to maintain it you could interact with some deep staff like expirence or idea.Other games pretend that they could give you reall expirince without extra\distructing features, but in act they are empty due to lack of conflict. For example(but its just my opinion), The Layers of Fear of the same studio hava some issues with that: you do not feel really affect while you travelling throught the game. You will meet no reall obstacles or threat on your way to thegame final, so you feel sometimes uninvolved.But Observer is an ideal example of experience transaction! You feel threat, fright and interest. You feel involved, you are envolved!So really recommend for all classic cyberpunk lovers and those  who want to see a  games as an art :)

_childDocuments_.review: Observer is a sci-fi detective game set in a steam punk style atmosphere. The story is about finding who possibly murdered your son and various other killings as you progress through the game. The game play consists of taking scans of blood samples, electronics, interrogation, and following trails to find leads to help your case. While at first it seems like a fully fledged detective game it starts to throw all that away a little over half way into the game. The game then turns into a complete mess of wandering random rooms and hallways that seem completely out of place and serve no purpose to the story. It feels like a bunch of people all had different ideas and they threw them all together with no rhyme or reason behind them.The story is also an incoherent mess that no longer made any sense towards the end. I’m not entirely sure what they were going for but if confusing was it than they nailed it. What started off decent enough unraveled quickly towards the mid section of the game and all was lost as you wondered what was happening.The main protagonists voice acting was terrible and flat sounding. It really took away from the game listening to him get upset about something but it sounded like not a care in the world was given to even try to sell that scene. The other voices in the game were decent so it was rather odd they had such a bland lead role who sounded like they didn’t even try.This was one of the few games I was so glad it ended so I can be done with it. 5/10
