_childDocuments_.review: (As of 11/3/2022, this game has received updates to squash the more troublesome bugs within it. While I don't think the game has reached a flawless state, I do believe that enough of the annoyances have been resolved that I can comfortably give this game a passing grade. The original negative opinion follows below.)The Short Version: The Long Version: I'm a nice guy, right? I mean, you can look at my review history and see that I'm very stingy when it comes to not recommending games. If there's a game I feel on the fence about, I'll likely give it a pass because hey, at least I had some fun right? I'm not pointing this out for internet points, I'm pointing this out because I need you to fully appreciate what it means that this game was able to frustrate me enough to vote against it.This game should've been a slam dunk for me. I like retro games, and the idea of a lite simulator where you work to slowly convert some dilapidated laundromat in a rundown part of some nowheresville town into a flashy, neon-filled arcade with 35 games sounded like a great way to blow a weekend. The games that you unlock for your arcade are mostly parodies of classic games from the 70s and 80s; simple, single screened games that you enjoy for a few minutes at a time before moving onto something else. None of them would be worth buying as separate products, compared to the games that they're riffing on, but having them all together allows them to become greater than the sum of their parts.  Because the game doesn't allow you to have all of the games at once, but instead makes you earn them through running the laundromat and arcade, it creates a compelling gameplay loop where you're always oh so close to your next skill upgrade, or new arcade machine, or building renovation that you'll be compelled to play just one more turn/in-game day. You'll rarely have a moment to idle; there will always be more clothes to wash and to dry, coin hoppers to empty out and put in your safe, broken games to fix and (in-game time) daily challenges to complete. You'll do it all to work towards the moment when you'll be finally free to just play the games whenever you want, however much you want.The game is ambitious, I had fun playing it, and I really wish I could just recommend it and move on, but I cannot do that in good conscience. I cannot do that because throughout the time I've played it I was constantly subjected to bugs, and not the ha-ha let's flick roaches off of the game's circuit board minigame. This game is full of actual, unintentional bugs that spoil the experience the more you find them. Trash items that you can't pick up despite the game wanting you to. The car that you earn randomly disappearing from the game until you restart it. Control errors in the videogames. In-game challenges being impossible to complete because the score tracking your progress is busted. Audio clips being cut off before they can play in full. Messages in the in-game email repeating multiple times, spamming the inbox. The game failing to properly return to the menu upon saving and quitting, forcing me to Alt+F4 out. Just a bunch of stupid little annoyances that aren't necessarily game breaking (so far), but are just too overwhelming to be ignored. It's death by 1,000 cuts. Maybe I'll come back to this review and make it a positive one, if this game reaches an acceptable state. Until then, my advice is to stay away and hope for a long list of bug fixes to come. If this studio wants the PC audience to beta test their game, they should be paying us, not the other way around.Not Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another case of Steam needing to add a mediocre/moderate rating. This game is not terrible by an means but its not generically good either.Its biggest issues are inconsistent game design, inconsistent characters, and esoteric progression.I managed to play over an hour of this game but it felt like quite a bit longer--------Story----------You are a 19 year old girl working your fathers laundromat after dropping out of college for a business degree. After seeing how much money the arcade was making you request to invest more into it but your father denies it because 'laundry' is the backbone of the community.  Your sister who did this before you helps you achieve your plans for expanding the arcade and proving your father wrong.  ---------Controls--------Felt terrible where it mattered. Most of the time you won't notice any issues with the controls except when what you are looking at isn't being selected. An example would be emptying the hopper (coins) of an arcade machine and then being forced into playing it instead.The office computer is also terrible, its hard to tell what you are clicking on because the mouse pointer has two points. Further interacting with the computer is usually just very tedious I don't have anything nice to say about it.--------Performance----------I had no performance issues. There are not many entities on the map at any given time so I don't imagine performance will be an issue for many--------Graphics-----------Nothing to complain about. I personally enjoyed the small nods to 90's culture but you could easily say this was from any modern time period with little effort. You are building an arcade... most arcades have looked the same since the 90's with the only thing changing being the cabinets----------UI------------Frustrating. The game loves to cover 2/3s of the screen. Pick up trash? The trash gets scaled up to take screen space. Laundromat task needs done? Your arm takes up a 1/3 of the screen. I found this to be very frustrating once the objects and tasks started repeating.The PDA menu was nice however.-------Game Design--------Inconsistent and more often than not poor. The game presents itself as a management game...which there isn't much of even over an hour in. Arcade games provided come into 2 categories significantly worse version of a classic or over complicated mess  I personally despised the 'Blockchain' arcade cabinet for the latter issueWhat makes the game design poor? It conflicts with 'purpose'Your purpose as provided by the game is to run a laundromat. The arcade games are to pass time while working at said laundromat. The only benefit they provide you is more popularity(and therefore more customers) as well as some money from others playing it. Whats more is your progress is not preserved when you get called away to work on things in the laundromat. For the first 40 minutes you will be relying heavily on 'S Ranking' the laundry activities to get money. Anything less than an 'S rank' yields significantly less money. The only thing that lowers your rank in those activities is the amount of time it takes to complete. Meaning that you may start a game but you will probably never get past the first or second level if you are focusing on just money.This wouldn't matter .... if you didn't get quests that required you to play said arcade games.Which gets into the biggest inconsistencies.After some progression you will unlock 'to-do list' from your father which....includes playing arcade games. Completing these tasks yields you an alternative currency to get personal and shop wide upgrades. Move faster, see farther being the simplest of them. The to-do list usually includes 3 unique versions of the following:Play x arcade cabinet for y timeComplete maintenance (pick up trash, clean up gum, etc)Achieve score or feat in an arcade gameThe issue is 2 of these are not achievable without ignoring the laundromat entirelyTime in the game is set to 1 in game minute is 1 real life secondWhen it says play a game for 5 minutes it really means play a game for 5 in game hours. The worse version of this task is 10 in game hours or almost the entirety of your shift if not more.Many of the 'Achieve feat' version of the tasks can in some cases be unachievable.So you can pick one or the other, make money to buy arcade cabinets or arcade expansions.....or upgrades. The quality of the upgrades vary substantially and can even be .... very bad. One of the upgrades makes it to where less trash and gum spawn... but cleaning it up generates you money....so you are spending money....to make less money.Some of the most important upgrades are ridiculously expensive for how needed they are to be able to make money from the laundromat AND the to-do list. An example of this would be another employee to help with the laundromat tasks.Whats more is its your father telling you to play these games....who wants you to manage the laundromat?---------Progression---------Feels bad man. There is no indicator telling you what the next goal is. Early this isn't a problem. You have expansions and arcade cabinets to buy....until there isn't any left because you are waiting on story progression to unlock the next set. What causes the story to progress is not well telegraphed or marked. -----------OVERALL-------------There are some people that will love this game. A lot of care was put into it. Each arcade cabinet felt different from the others.If conflicting game design crippled this game then the inconsistent poor progression was a quick stab to finish it off. Its worth picking up on sale to try, or at full price if you are sold on it by the trailers. Otherwise I would steer clear and keep an eye out for more games from the developers in the future. I can't emphasize enough how much care went into each gear of this machine. Its just all the people working on it were not communicating so the gears just don't fit together.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of retro games, and this game takes them up a notch.Playing on the steamdeck, I've had a great experience. It's able to run at 2560 x 1440 at about 45-60 fps no problems (45 fps is present when outside the laundry, inside, you get a full on 60 fps no dips) docked mode.Portable mode of course works like a charm.The game itself is awesome, it features a simple-like management of a laundry, all to get money to buy arcades for the back, making even more money with those. The laundry part is actually pretty cool, simple yet fun... just go around picking up trash, put clothes in the washer then the dryer, clean... It's not too bad, but can get repetitive.Before it gets repetitive, though, you'll have racked up enough money to have a fair amount of arcades in the back + a room expansion. At that point of the game you can pretty much leave the laundry part if you wish and solely focus on playing the arcades, which can give a hefty amount of money.The arcade games are simply GREAT. So far they all remind me of old games, but they all have some kind of twist and look different... for example, a pacman like game, which looks like GTA and has some different gameplay mechanics, like having a second chance to escape when you get caught. They are super nice, all and all, they feel like WarioWare style minigames, but with more depth.The UI is amazing, graphics, optimization... there's nothing else to say besides buy this game if you're interested in retro like arcade games, since this game won't disappoint one bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Not a huge fan of work simulators, but the arcade theme and being able to transform the laundrymat into an arcade kept me going through completion of the game. But in the end the game feels empty, and I regret the time I sunk into completing the same grinding tasks over and over to get there. Positives include a few good games that are actually fun to play, the theme and the story is decent for what it is. The negatives are the grind, and it is a long one. I know it's the theme but doing laundry is so tedious and it's constantly interrupting you as if you start to play a game and actually start to enjoy playing. You'll have to ignore the laundry and get a bad grade or you'll have to abandon the game. Midway through the game you'll unlock the ability to grind a second currency that can unlock upgrades that will reduce the grind a bit. The problem is if you play normally (there are some ways to get more of the gold through scamming the system) you'll only have enough gold to unlock a few of the unlocks. At my endgame state I had less than half of them despite focusing on completing the objectives. The biggest shortcoming are the games themselves. Some of the biggest most expensive games are absolutely unplayable with the current interface (looking at you table football), the physics of Billiards is broken, air hockey looks right but again the interface kills it. Darts is an absolute slog, will take most of your day to complete a game, DDR, which should be perfect with a D pad, is somehow one of the most boring games there. List goes on and on. Then there are the other games, there's often just little things that don't feel right in them; I think it's because they're basically clones of classics, so you KNOW how they're supposed to feel and any changes in that are impossible to ignore. Bomberman is so simple, but the bombs don't chain, you'll just be walking and get randomly killed often by absolutely nothing. Street of Rage had some work put into it, the art is cool, but the strikes feel empty and you'll just be better off cheaping the enemies with less risky attacks like spamming jumpkicks to get through them. Racer Chaser is pretty much impossible to get through without getting hit and having to run to your next car, but it's not that hard and just becomes tedious, Fruit crush won't let you drop the tiles fast so it gets pretty slow, Space race sim is really boring, how hard is it to just program a simple race game with no powerups?Communists from Mars, woodgal candycrush, Zombat, Bugai are all pretty fun.Strike gold is decent but the control is still a little sloppy and the bricks bug out all the time not falling or behaving as they should. Line terror had so much potential but you move slower than any other game of that genre ever created ruining the fun. Gravchase, Blobs, UFO, meteor, pong, tree choppers, Atack vector all behave as they should but they're so simple you're not going to want to sink a lot of time into any of them. No one wants to play Dino jump on the PDA, please don't make us play that, especially to hit a high score. So not everyone will like every game, but there are real shortcomings on some of them (as I've tried to outline above). The problem is that the game's earning potential is based on how many goals you hit in that game and how often you play it so if there's a large percentage of games that suck then you're not going to be playing them, then they won't earn much, and that in turn translates into a longer grind. Just play the games you don't like? That's extra grind too. Either way too much grind and not enough fun. There's also games that were obviously in development, but aren't included in the game. If they didn't make the cut or you're saving them for DLC fine, that may just be the way things are. But don't show me the games front and center on the title screen every time I boot the game up and tease me into thinking that they're part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot stop. This game is so wonderful! I even enjoyed the laundry parts! Having something on a time that you could work with chores and daily tasks was just so pleasing to my ADHD brain. The arcade games are amazing. Stack Overflow has consumed me. The only thing stopping me from scoring higher is sheer time spent to get that high. Blockchain is so neat! It took me a bit to figure it out, but I was hooked once I got to it. The only thing I have is maybe have the objectives on some of the games a bit clearer for those unfamiliar: pool, darts, some of the other arcade ones. The music is so cool and nostalgic. I LOVE the art style. The chores have lots of reinforcement to keep me engaged and looking for more trash so I can be radical and throw away my trash bag. Sometimes it's the little things with reinforcement that really tickle the brain in self-soothing ways. This game is my happy place. Any chance at end game we could revert and get some of the laundry machines back? (or maybe I haven't made it that far yet...)Overall, a wonderful game, a wonderful team of developers to interact with, good vibes all round.Also, GERALT AS DAD!? Hell yeah!

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise certainly isn't a bad game. It has good things going for it; such as a quaint coming of age story, fun classic gaming and 90's references, and good vibes. But I can't honestly say that I found any of the individual arcade mini-games on offer all that fun. There is a certain addictive grind to the progression in the game, which can be satisfying. But none of the games on offer are ones that I would enjoy playing if this were simply a collection of arcade mini games. The sim aspect is bare bones, just enough to have a few knobs to fiddle with. Overall I think this is a decent game with a lot of heart and good ideas, but doesn't execute on any of them as much as I'd hoped. I spent about 30 hours playing through the campaign until the story came to a conclusion, and I didn't feel any desire to continue playing any of the arcades, even though there were a lot more challenges to complete and upgrades to unlock. A+ for art direction and sound design. I just wish the sim part was deeper and more interesting, or some of the games were compelling enough to keep playing on their own merit.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The very basic concept is a neat one, but feels varied between uninspired and poorly considered.The intro is great, at least, and lends itself well to what they were hoping to achieve with the time period being referenced, as does most of the designs thereafter. 90's-ish, with a helping of 80's carry over. The problem is that after this visual splash I still have to play the game, and things start to go awry almost immediately.First, the laundry element is done away with very quickly. By all accounts, the laundry chores should be abandoned quickly in favor of playing arcade games and building up the arcade portion of the business. The problem is this: why even HAVE the laundry element in the first place? The story still could have worked (earning your father's trust) without including it at all. It's not particularly enjoyable, distracts from the main draw, I imagine that the idea was to give a reason why you, the player AND the character, would not want to continue with these chores; but to deliberately make something repetitive and ultimately dull is not the way to put one's best foot forward.The arcade games themselves are a mixed bag. Some of this may well be subjective, of course, in terms of general taste, other issues are less subjective. Chaser Racer's camera is abysmal, pulled too close to make for meaningful avoidance of the police. Strike Gold is rife with glitches and bugs, most notable of which is a regular occurrence where bricks that SHOULD fall do not. Air Hockey, in which the paddle moves so quickly that its control is haphazard in a way that fails to be enjoyable. By contrast other games are very well done through and through (Stack overflow being a personal favorite).The management is minimal, to say the least. Play games, make money, achieve goals on each machine that require a significant amount of grinding. Repeat. It does the unfathomable by turning the arcade games into a chore. Most arcade cabinets are unavailable until the player expands the arcade, which requires more grinding, still, just to earn enough money for an expansion of space that carries with it VERY little customization. The loop becomes so repetitive that it becomes difficult to enjoy the games AS games, but just a way to push through to the next objective, and all in service of an arcade that never once feels like one of my own making.. The grind and the repetition far outweighs any enjoyment that could come from the arcade games themselves. This, especially as so many of the games are gated off from the player until they slog through the repetitive loop.

_childDocuments_.review: its pretty alright. the main premise of the gameplay is balancing chores and playing arcade games together, and then gradually becoming able to spend more time using more arcade machines and slowly letting the laundry aspect fade away. the story is okay, although it might hit too close to home for some people.i would like to talk about the arcade machines specifically. besides warioware, i have not enjoyed an experience yet where the goal is to rapidly switch between games with wildly different objectives for multiple rewards. the strongest mechanics of arcade paradise are the parts where you complete machine-specific goals that permanently enhance the money it generates per hour, and then the daily tasks which give a unique currency that you spend on permanent establishment upgrades like a slower flow of time, higher capacity garbage bags and automatic money collecting. these both combined to make for a pleasurable gaming experience where there was always something to do on the horizon for all types of gamers and skill levels.that being said, some machines are far better than others. people like to organise them by tier lists so that is what i will do as well in no particular order:S tier - Line Terror, Gravichase, Graffiti Ballz, Vostok 2093A tier - Zombat 2, Video Air Hockey, Attack Vector, Space Race Simulator, Knuckles & Knees, BugaiB tier - UFO Assault, Woodguy/Woodgal Jr, Thump-a-Gopher, Stack Overflow, Slime Pipes, Shuttlecocks (Pong), Meteor Madness, Hustler, Cyber Dance, Woodgal's AdventureC tier - Bomb Dudes, Championship Darts, Blockchain, Blobs from Space, Communists from Mars, Jukebox, Strike Gold, Table Football, Racer Chaser, BarkanoidD tier - Fruit Crush, Air HockeyF tier - Toad and Turtle (literally unplayable)Didn't play much - Woodguy Golfthe only ones you need to read into are the S tier and A tier, and then be wary of D tier and F tier. B tier and C tier are okay but not groundbreaking. i liked line terror and gravichase in particular because the former captured a horror game atmosphere perfectly and was intensely skill based with a little rng to keep things interesting (even if lots of people hate it), while i enjoy the latter just because i liked playing super hexagon, and gravichase is very similar to super hexagon and i am biased. graffiti ballz and vostok 2093 are just good, fun games that can keep you entertained for a very long timei could see the appeal for fruit crush and air hockey but i just was not feeling it, i felt that *video* air hockey was much more fun. toad and turtle is literally unplayable, it is a frogger game except you can actually fall into the water for unknown reasons because god hates you, dont even bother. woodguy golf didnt entice me that much i guess, idk.overall i think the BIGGEST strength of this game is that it caters to all gamers of all skill levels, and you can appreciate the feel of being able to play more games over time while your adult responsibilities fade away. even if lots of people dont like the beginning of the game where laundry is intensive to do, i enjoyed it i guess.  there is something for everyone here. just a shame that there are so many minor bugs scattered around, if only the devs did one last big patch up before they took off to their next projects.by the way, remember to check the video settings and adjust them according to your preferences. i felt that the base game's default settings were far too bright, but thankfully you can turn that down.

_childDocuments_.review: After enjoying the demo and hoping the game would pick up after a few days, I was sorely wrong. I bought this ignoring the warnings from other reviews talking about the gameplay loop. The main gameplay involves going back and forth managing loads of laundry. Collecting as they come in, waiting for the wash to be done, waiting for the drying to be done, and then setting them on the table to collect money based on how fast you did it. That means the game will punish you if you don't do the laundry fast enough. If you want to maximize your rewards and get more games for your arcade (the main selling point of this whole game), then you have to do this menial task as efficiently as possible. Doing the laundry as efficiently as possible means you have absolutely no time to play any of the arcade games in any decent capacity.The save feature is one that frustrated me the most, though. You cannot pause and save in the middle of the day. Every time you save and exit, it ends the day and stops you from earning any profit. Laundry gets stuck wherever it was before you saved, making every single load a failed one. The game, for some reason, wants you to save right before you have to leave on the bus for the night. It's honestly a little maddening there's no better way for saving progress.The arcade games, what little I could play of them, are genuinely fun! It's just a shame that the game inherently discourages you from playing it's main selling point by punishing you with menial labor.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you really like retro game remixes this game gets really repetitive really fast. Even once you are making money and can ignore laundry you get stuck with a list of chores and a daily time limit, so you only play the cabinets for a handful of minutes at once. If you want to actually progress, the game even tries to make you play specific ones almost all ingame-day, as daily quests.Some of the games at the beginning are interesting creative remixes, but I felt the games got worse the more cabinets I ordered; Eventually it back-peddled to two-button tree choppers, etch a sketch nightmares, and lame four direction shooters with bad graphics. I lost interest at that point.Overall there is a lack of polish and just endless bugs. The UI is buggy, when ordering cabinets some are hidden "between pages " and it can be very difficult to order all cabinets until you figure out that you can scroll the browser using keyboard keys instead of the mouse (also buggy). The PC in general is a UI nightmare, with terrible cursor, buggy windows, strange clickboxes, and other frustrating things. The games themselves are equally buggy, one example is a game where you can shoot but holding down more than one direction key makes you shoot in weird directions depending on which two are held down; I would often find myself shooting backwards. There's the racing game where curves in the track gravitationally pull you towards the edge regardless of speed, feels bad to play. Games where enemies spawn on top of you or are hidden by bad camera positioning. Freezing menus, bad hitboxes, etc.Just lots of frustrating bugs and a lack of polish. Tries to do everything at once and fails at most aspects in the process.

_childDocuments_.review: Synopsis: Your father hires you to manage his laundromat, which you find rather stale and boring, and dream of converting it to a hip arcade business.It is a fun game, although it is somewhat grinding. Each day, you have to clean out the trash (and every morning when you open, there is fresh trash that needs to be taking to the dumpster)You are responsible for washing and drying the clothes in a timely manner, for the biggest bonus, as well as playing maintenance when the toilet clogs (which seems to happen every other day).There is already a small cluster of video games in the back room, which you can also play, but as it interferes with your duties, except smaller bonuses when you finish washing/drying your customers clothesAlso the coin 'hoppers' need to bee emptied on a regular basis, and stashed in the safe in your office, which can be used to purchase more video games, after you unlock them (by grinding and "quests".Again the fact that you can play the video games, is a cool feature. But don't expect any 2022 graphics, as this sets place in the 90s' and the games are mostly side-scrollers, but it's still cool.Like I said, it is a fun game, if you don't take it too seriously
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Part business management, part laundry simulator and part mini-game collection, Arcade Paradise is an absolute treat.You take over an old laundromat with a few arcade machines out the back and slowly upgrade the arcade part while making more money and completing challenges in the games.The game are new takes on old arcade and home console games, I didn't expect to be playing a match 3 game in 2023, and a lot of them are really good. There is the odd stinker in there, which fits with the arcade theme, and that's okay.The game has a fantastic vibe, and quite a touching story, I'd really recommend that you give it a go.Steam Deck Note: Plays amazingly on deck, which made up about 75% of my time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for about an hour, and while it's okay so far, the pacing feels a bit slow. I'm hoping it picks up as I progress. My main issue, however, is with the saving system. Most players will likely finish their session after completing a day and taking the bus home. The problem is that whenever you quit the game, it ends your entire day--even if you just started the day. In short: it ends the day, saves, and quits every time you exit. It's confusing why they didn’t adopt something similar to Stardew Valley, where the game only saves after you go to bed. Since most players naturally stop after finishing a day, this design choice is baffling. It’s an odd system and frankly kinda discourages me from playing further. Giving this a hesitant thumbs up, only because I shouldn't give a negative review with my ~1 hour of play.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of grinding, sims, and arcade games, Arcade Paradise was a near 30 hour dopamine mainline. The progression is super satisfying - watching the business grow physically and financially was all the incentive I needed for several blurry-eyed late nights of pixelated nostalgia. Between the awesome art style and insanely addicting gameplay loop, I cannot recommend this title enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is a labor of love filled with time wasters.The best comparison to this game is probably Coin Game but with more story and world building.The attention to detail while also nailing the vibe of different machines really drives this game home for me.I'm a sucker for well polished games and this has to be one of the best games to come out of a dev team this small.To be fair, i use this game as a time waster (watching vids or podcast in the background etc.) but quickly stop everything else to tune into the story and progression the game shows me.IF YOU NEED A GAME TO PLAY PLEASE GET THIS. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Oooph, A lot to say about this one. A complete love letter to anyone who grew up in the 80's and 90's arcades. Nearly all your favourites have had there take made on here all wrapped up of the era teenage angst and pop culture references. I've completed the game but I think It'll be a while still before I 100% complete it. Since I be a pirate I'll break me thoughts into aye's and nay's.Aye!:- 35 cabinets of nearly all your favourites; Arkanoid, Bust-A-Move, Frogger, Dance Dance Revolution and more. All lovingly remade in tongue in cheek references. It also surprisingly includes versions of Air Hockey, Pool and Darts. - Swimming in 80's and 90's nostalgia. Hearing the old dial-up noises when you booted into the computer set me back to the heady years as a kid browsing the web on my aunt's win 98 PC.- Nails the grimy arcade feel, all the way down to pulling off bubble gum from under the tables- Engaging Story line mixed with earlier teenage angst and rebellion although if not a little on the nose.- A lot of effort went into the games, some of them are well thought out with multiple goals, Other's not so much. - Value for money. 35 Cabinets minus the Jukebox for £16 is a good deal, I got it for a tenner on the recent sale. If you're into 90's arcades, A very good purchase.Nay's:- The Launderette; If you're picking up to play it as a launderette management simulator. You're going to be sorely disappointed. You will be cleaning up regardless of the stage your in, It basically has the one mini-game of washing and drying and using the funds to build up the real centrepiece - the arcade.- To Do's & Goals; Holy hell are some machines more easier to do then others and some of those goals are down right cancerous. The amount of times I've been sent back to Zombat II to get x kills with Y weapons is annoying. Especially when it asks to do it with a mini-gun in a single life.- Arcade management; There just isn't much to it. As long as your maximising your income on the machines by playing with the settings once and completing associated goals. They will ♥♥♥♥ out money, The game tells you that you can park less popular games with more popular ones. I didn't really bother. I just plonked machines in any random old space.- It gets repetitive, with the goals and to do's. It can wear you down pretty quick, especially when it's being an ass with more of some of the nastier goals/to do's.  My arcade is done but I'm only half way down on the upgrades mostly because I just didn't like half the tasks.Couldn't give a cannon shot:- DLC. I'm reading a fair complaints that some of the newer machines should be free and I'm probably gonna take a broadside for this; The game is £16 full price. You get a lot of machines, I think you get a lot of bang for your buck. If you loved the game, support the dev buy a few cabinets. They're not all that expensive, if not. Don't. Vote with your wallet.- Bugs. Outside the ones I crushed when fixing my cabinets. I didn't run into any. I don't know if the Dev's did a big sweep but I don't see any of the issues others are experiencing.ConclusionIf you're into 80's/90's arcade nostalgia. This is the game for you, set on a back-drop of growing your own personal arcade and a decent story to go with. If you're expecting to play the laundry side more or wanting more from the arcade management. You may want to rethink your purchase. 8/10 Gold doubloons. A treasure worth collecting with the rest of your booty.Just for the Steam Deck users:Played through the entire thing on my steam deck. 60FPS. Very good battery life, no real slow down. If you're looking to pick this up to play on your deck, your good to go! It fits well!.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The worst of mobile business models now on PC!Laundry simulator semi-idle game. In the first 4-5 hours 80% of the game is loading washing machines and collectiong trash. The reward is buying arcade machines that can play very simple mini-games (most suck). But if you play them, the laundry will lose money (even though it's narratively implied that you shouldn't neglect the laundry and your dad keeps tabs on you). And you need the money to buy more arcade machines. At this point you have about 4-5 machines.You can expand the arcade area, but it costs a lot of money i.e. lot of time meanwhile what do you do? Play reskinned Pacman?Also, it feels like half a game, as half the arcade machines are in DLC and the game shoves it into your face from the beginning that these are the machines you don't have access to.If you want non-ripoff nostalgia, buy UFO50 or Atari50 instead.PS:Originally the game used the arrow keys. People complained that WASD isn't supported (it's easier for the 3D part of the game). Now WASD is supported but the arrow keys no longer, even though for many arcade games it would be preferrable. Making both work isn't rocket science in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve only put about 3 hours into this game, but so far it’s simply too slow and not catching my attention.It’s polished and has a great retro look, but cleaning the laundromat is probably the most fun I’ve had in those 3 hours. The arcade games aren’t fun to play and there’s just… so… much… waiting while I manually do people’s laundry—which, by the way, isn’t at ALL what laundromats do?? Plus there are zero interactable NPCs; instead what the devs chose to do is implement a cool polygonal effect that make nearby people disappear when you get too close, but that choice makes the game feel disproportionately smaller and empty and, in a big way, deflates that feeling one might get when their empire grows in any other simulator game. Who am I making this arcade empire for, if not to see people enjoy the games and pump in quarters?Watching something like Supermarket Simulator, Internet Cafe Simulator, or even that weed game makes this game feel so empty and pointless. It was a relaxing few hours, but the lack of any real, impactful feedback killed my momentum quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is a wonderful trip where you build up an Arcade in the 90s. Over 35 playable cabinets that are very well made wait for you. They vary between decades of arcade history between the 70s-90s.The only thing i dont really like are the DLC's even if they are not necessary at all. I would prefer a Story DLC.. who knows!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I've expanded the arcade twice and its filling up nicely with machines. Absolutely loving it. Seen some reviews mention bugs and game not running right, can say I've not come across issues like this whatsoever. The nostalgia is real, the soundtrack is awesome. Get the jukebox as soon as you are able. 10/10 fore this type of game. Best Laundo/Arcade game out there!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise manages to make playing arcade games monotonous and feel like a chore. Additionally, the main sim portion of the game is more basic and less developed than any other sim that I've played. There's very little customization freedom, besides choosing which predetermined location to put an arcade machine and selecting it's difficulty/cost. If playing knockoff arcade games, with worse graphics and mechanics than the originals, are your fetish... this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: You do laundry and gradually build up an arcade, exactly what it says on the tin and a predictably good game to wind down with. Low key, low stakes, and while you won't love all the arcade games, you will love at least two. If there's a creative mode where I don't have to do the same damn chores over and over and over and over again I haven't found it yet, but man would I appreciate just being able to walk around and play the games. Also, side note, if you're expecting a Sims-style arcade builder like I was -- this is not that at all. More of a visual spreadsheet manager, but it's fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: So... Yes, its everything you see.. Laundry, Trash, Clean, Play... Trash is a bit (gas station sim) appears everyday by the truck load, but you get money for picking it up. I dont see why people are complaining about it... If you come into this KNOWING you have to do laundry... I mean come on lol, then you are gonna enjoy it. My favorite game is the pacman/gta LMFAO its pretty much the only fun one right now IMO. I think Im on Friday first week, my only gripe is figuring out when to start the last load. I seem to always go over the closing time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

You just won't bother to do it. - Too busy raking in that console $$$$.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I saw this on an episode of Game Grumps and had one of those "I NEED to play this" moments. But I waited for it to go on sale before I picked it up.This game is right up my ally, along the lines of those silly low-stakes sims like Supermarket Simulator. It's absolutely my guilty-pleasure genre. I'm 20-ish hours in already and I'm thoroughly engrossed. I've seen a few of the reviews and I generally agree with the pro's and cons. The arcade games are fun and I'm getting a kick out of their knock-off brand. Micro-managing the cabinets hits that sweet spot of being complex enough to dive as deep as you want yet doesn't punish you for focusing on something else for a while. Balancing the wash with the goals and daily tasks sets a nice pace and keeps things moving. The story and background lore is engaging and I enjoy the humor in all the little interactions. The music, jukebox and in the games, is excellent; it's already stuck in my head.The biggest pro for me, as a matter of taste, is the nostalgia factor. I used to live for these arcades as a kid, and an arcade sim wasn't something I knew I needed until I had one. There's something intoxicating about slamming a song down on the Jukebox and then diving into an arcade cabinet for the next 5-10 minutes. That being said, there are areas that could use a bit more polish. Interactables often feel disjointed, sometimes requiring finding just the right angle to work, which can be irritating when you're trying to quickly pick up trash or empty the machines. Some games can get janky, the worst offender being Hustler (Billiards) that I've found, which is really hard to play on keyboard, the camera isn't the best, and the physics feel inconsistent. TL:DR, it's worth the money, but if you're on the fence, wait for it to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great game! The music in amazing - I love the playable arcade games and how they are original but still retain a characteristic of 80/90's arcade games. I love the tasks and doing the washing and the games make you feel so good when you slowly rid of them to get more games.10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: this game makes the most mundane tasks fun, and almost makes me want to do chores in real life. (almost.) it's not without its problems, but the game is so good that most of the problems are hard to notice.my biggest issue (and this has been a problem for months now) is that the cursor isn't completely accurate as to where you're pointing; sometimes it'll aim at your feet when you're looking straight ahead, sometimes it'll aim *behind you* at something else entirely, and sometimes, despite being on top of, or a foot away from a piece of trash/hopper, the hoppers or trash aren't accessible. i reported this as a bug, but i recall their FAQ saying something to the effect of "we know about this problem. *it's annoying, right?*" which lead me to believe that this issue was purposefully left in. that, or programming an accurate cursor is very difficult. i don't know, i'm not a game programmer. (i do know that making games is extremely difficult, however. so who knows why the cursor isn't 100% accurate)aside from that, a majority of the games are very very fun, with my favorites currently being woodgal jr, zombat, attack vector, and wack-a-mole, and least favorites being stack overflow (the noises will make you wish you were deaf), video air hockey, and pool/billiards (they don't control very well. which is a bummer because i like playing pool)if you're thinking about getting this game but you don't love the idea of doing mundane tasks, get this game anyways because it really makes doing laundry and picking up trash fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is a casual but satisfying management sim soaked in good feeling and ‘90s vibes, but it’s also a story about finding success in what you love in life. Though there are some missed opportunities and the customization options are limited, the quality of the roster of playable arcade cabinets, the attention to detail, and the striking audiovisual presentation all go to make this one game worth cleaning up your act for.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting a simple little sim about running an arcade and while I got that I don't think I was prepared for just how much I was getting.First of all the story has these beautiful 80's/90's MTV grunge art that really pops. The entire game is a love letter to the time period. The story is about your father giving you his failing laundromat to run and as you go through it you discover the relationship you have with him and your sister. I was far more invested than I ever expected to be in the story of an arcade sim.The gameplay has various parts to it. As you run the daily operations you need to put clothes in the washer, the dryer, and then put them aside for pick up. Clean gum off the various surfaces, collect the coins from arcade machines, clean up trash, and if you have time left over you can play the various arcade machines. The games themselves are a ton of fun retro arcade games with everything from 'Barkanoid' to an Pac Man game with GTA graphics. As you make money you can buy arcade cabinets, expand, complete challenges in the arcade games for coins, buy upgrades for running the business, and unlock more story.I found myself hooked to this little gem and it's great.There is so much here for the money
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a MEH rating.The concept is awesome.  Running a laundry to create an arcade.  The FX are decent enough, first person is nice, and playing the games is awesome.My beef comes from the insanely repetitive laundry part of the game.  The grind is just too repetitive after a while.  Trash, Wash, Dry, Done.  It occupies most of the gameplay.  Maybe later it gets better, but not sure there's enough depth if they took laundry away completely.I can't remember what day I'm on, but I don't think I can bring myself to play anymore.  Which is sad for me, cause I want to advance.If you are OK with grinding out money over and over doing repetitive tasks, then you will be OK.  Just too much for me.I can't really recommend it at the moment.  Need to add more management stuff?  Perhaps let the customers do their laundry and you help them fix the machine?... The customers come in and stand around, that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Shallow management and buggy, uninteresting arcade games make this a hard pass.The majority of my time was spent doing laundry for the customers that disappear if you get too close to them.Weird to have a business game where the only customer feedback or interaction is a % bonus/penalty if you picked up enough trash that day.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game.I really, *really* want o.But I can't.First, none of the arcade games list their controls. Does this racing game have a 'brake' button? Who knows! I certainly don't. How do you access the shop in this shooter? No hints. Additionally, the game has a habit of freezing, which I could look past if it didn't happen while I was attempting to break a high score for story content in a very fast-paced game.Third, there is story content locked behind the worst cabinet in the game, not least because it's the one most likely to give you RSI. I shouldn't be risking carpal tunnel just to play your arcade management game.Overall, trying to get good at any of the cabinets in the game will inevitably lead to frustration due to the lack of polish. The DDR-alike is so poorly matched to the music you'll have a better time playing with the music disabled. The top-down shooter's hitboxes are just strange, and it's almost impossible to actually get into the shop. It's also clear that keyboard controls were an afterthought, and a particularly late one at that.

You cannot upgrade the laundry side - like actually filling up the vending machines, upgrading the walls, floors.. etc. I know its about making a business with the game cabinets but you should at least be able to make the front business look more presentable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of management games, from running a computer repair shop to managing a dinosaur theme park even being the director of a hospital, so when I played the demo for Arcade Paradise, I put it in my wish list immediately. The video games in the backroom were okay, but I was waiting for the laundromat and managing of the arcade because... well, I have no life, okay. The managing portion of this game is fun, but I do not believe that is this game's purpose. Controlling the laundromat and arcade are story driven and will proceed forward on their own, as long as you provide money. The story is a pretty good one to me, except that it might possibly hit a bit too close to home for some of us. No, this game's purpose is an ode to the arcades many of us grew up with, and it has done a fantastic job of that. The laundromat is as disgusting and repulsive as any I've ever been forced to be in, in real life. The drudgery and annoyance of doing someone else's laundry is real. The arcade looks very similar to ones I used to hang out in before I got a real job; not as dark, not as crowded, but almost as noisy. A neat feature to implement would be the ability to place multiple of the same machine down; I remember facing an entire row of the same popular machine (Space Invaders), and all of them occupied.The video games, however, are outstanding. With out exception, every game I played I was bad at and didn't get, until I played it several more times, just like I always was in the... unspecified time range I grew up in. There are enough similarities to the real games, plus the excitement of seeing a new game in the arcade that you've never seen before to make this easily a "just one more turn" kind of game. You will quickly pick your favorites, and want to play them over and over again, but you can't! You've got that annoying laundry to do because at the beginning that's how you get your money.The goal system is a great idea; there are daily goals to earn pounds to buy things to upgrade yourself, and machine goals to make a given cabinet more popular, and therefore generate more cash, with which you buy more cabinets. The daily goals seem to be focused on a few specific games, rather than all the games in your arcade; it would be really nice if we could have "play game-x for 5 minutes" for every single game you own at some point or other.  The upgrades you can purchase range from the 'useless' (to me, the shoes) to the 'can't live without' (Assistant Manager's Assistant). Something that might be interesting to see would be a buy back or trade in system for these; I want my money back for those shoes, or put them toward something I'm going to get use out of!There are a few minor glitches here and there, but most of them seem to have been cleared up with the latest patch. There are still some, but the developers/publishers seem to be listening to the fans and following the forum here. For that, I am extremely appreciative; it makes it feel like we have a voice. I would really love to see a DLC with a bunch of games the developers wanted to add but couldn't!This game won me over from the management side to the playing video games side, easily; now every time I play it, I just ignore managing and head straight for my favorite games (Blockchain, Attack Vector and Stack Overflow; but really the list keeps growing).This will be a game I keep coming back to over and over again, and I can't recommend it enough. This is a must-buy!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have any real life experience with arcades, but I have played these sort of "simple" games over my childhood (35 now), so I didn't have a nostalgia factor going into this.Wishlisted this before launch, but it took me all this time to actually get around playing it. But boy was this fun! There are a lot of things to improve upon, but the core of it is great. However the main thing I will take from this game is the soundtrack. It's so good. Loved the jukebox, though would like some quality of life updates on that too.BE WARNED THOUGH: There is a major bug that may make you be "stuck" for an extended time unless you realize what you are doing wrong. When meaning to scroll the websites, using the scroll of your mouse often breaks it. Use WASD to avoid this. I'm not sure if you can use it again the same day if it glitches out, but it should be fine the next day.Also, be careful if you get anxious over a father character berating you regardless of doing well.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most underrated games to come out in 2022. One of my favorite pastimes is going to one of the local laundrymat locations and playing the few arcade games they have, and this game perfectly emulates the experience. Love the mini games too. I've even found myself saying "SYSTEM SUBJUGATED" whenever I'm done unclogging a toilet at work.If you like arcade games and simulations, you'll definitely not want to miss out on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Weird controls and visuals that gave me a headache immediately. It's a couple of generic knock-offs of a few basic arcade classics, with the most shallow shell of management and like 3 basic tasks constantly pulling you away from that machine. you're bouncing between a few hollow gameplay loops, and the switching doesn't enhance any of them. I'ts an arcade game collection that doesn't let you relax and play, it's a management sim without much to manage. It's got charm, they put effort into it, but I can't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I love retro-style games and actual retro games from the 80's and 90's, but I admit I was slow to pick this up.  I was excited about a game letting you build up a classic arcade, but the whole managing a laundromat thing made me hesitant.  I thought it would be another "simulator" game.  This game went on sale and finally gave it a go.  Seriously! I'm impressed!  This is more fun than I expected.  The game is set in the 90's.  Yes, you have to manage a laundromat but it's fun too.  You get paid for doing literally everything.  Taking out the trash, doing laundry, unclogging the toilet and even picking off gum earns money.  Then use that hard-earned cash and buy arcade stuff!  And doing the laundromat job has video game mechanics too.  (Just play it, you'll see.)  Best of all, when you order new arcade cabinets, you can actually play them.  At the end of the day, collect the money from them.As you advance through the game, your arcade becomes bigger, your tasks become more challenging, and you can get upgrades to make your job easier.  To tell the truth, the laundromat part of the game is satisfying.  I've read other reviews.  I'm not the only one that thinks this.Fun retro-style game!Customize your own 90's style arcade.You can actually play the arcade cabinets!Laundromat part is fun too.Upgrades to make gameplay better.Good ol' capitalism.Nostalgia.Sometimes using the office computer can be difficult.  Trying to scroll through the menus to order new arcades, upgrades and other things can be difficult.  You should be able to use the mouse and scroll wheel, but I found it's easier to use W and S.  Sometimes it can be laggy.  The game doesn't really show that you have to press spacebar to reply to messages and emails.  So if you have a message, just start pressing stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad. I feel like I have been taken in.I did the laundry - every day - trying to always speed me up / get high scores. Even when my side business of arcade machines was taking off, I still did the laundry, as dad asked, to prove him I am worth his love. Even if customers vanished as soon I approached them (doubting the realness of the world around me), I still did the laundry. Even if I got tons of things to do (collecting the changes, putting money in the safe, ordering new arcades, cleaning the toilet, reaching high scores in the mini games, etc), I still put some time in for doing the laundry.After 8 hours in, I got it. There are no rewards. Nobody will come help with that laundry thing. Nobody really cares about what you are doing. Nothing will change, every day will be the same, the only variations, aestethics. And those games you play on arcade machines? Just (limited) clones of real ones. Rip-off.This game is just stupid. I am stupid having played it for so long (where's my pay check?). I am stupid having thought it would lead to something. Developers are stupid for having made it (I think they spent a lot of time on it, it feels very polished, but it lacks what makes games fun).
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game on release but micro transactions for each new cabinet... No thank you!Main stream developers have gone this way to the lessening and hollowing of gaming and if small developers are now starting to go down this route as well then it is indeed a bad time to be a gamer. Once bitten! I will not be in a rush to buy a game from this developer again.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise by Nosebleed Interactive and published by Wired Productions is a fantastic game, conceptually speaking. In practice, bugs, crashes, unbalanced difficulty, inconsistent grind, lack of quality control on some of the arcade games and a general lack of polish in the places where it matters most, hold this game back from being an absolutely top tier experience in practice.Perhaps the game will be fixed in the future, but I don't see any recent update announcements on Steam. And if what I see here is what I get, then it's a damn shame and deserves a thumbs down, even if only for wasting an absolutely brilliant idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The game is OK.  if you like 90s style vid games, you might like it.  the gameplay loop is ok. wash clothes, pickup trash, maybe have a cpl hours per day to play games.  save $, buy more games, repeat.  only 2 or 3 of my 7 games are very fun.  theres probably more fun ones. but not gonna grind thru psuedo pac man levels to progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I like the overall intent of the game, but at every single stage, it seems like they made efforts to make the gameplay as clunky, obnoxious, and difficult to use as possible. And, once the "new game" shine wears off, it's incredibly shallow, to boot. I tried hard to like it. But I can only try a needlessly repetitive task so many times before I get sick of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like gas station sim but with super fun mini games and you don't actually have direct customer feed back. The mini-games, as super fun actual games. The song remakes are hilarious if not fantastic on their own. Great graphics style, and low resource usage. Plays for many hours on the Steam Deck on a single chargeHas some minor bugs but nothing game breaking. Interested to see where it goes and what all gets added in the future. 100% worth the buy if you enjoy 80's neon nostalgia and job sim games with a grind. What these folks really got right, beyond the game, style, and fun factor, is the pacing. Every job sim game is super chaotic at a point. This game can be, if you choose for it to be. But there is no negative if some days you just wanna chill and take a slower road. Makes it a great game to be entertained and relax with. 10/10 on design and implementation. 9/10 over all, needs res fixed on Deck and needs some small bugs squashed.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, fun, and competently contrived nostalgic journey, towards building your own Arcade Paradise.The games themselves are as legitimate as the ones they're inspired by, and well worth the price of admission on their own.The music is well produced, and very fitting, but an option to add actual real world songs from the time period, through the player's personal libraries, would have blasted this tasty cake into orbit.As it stands, this is as close to perfection as it gets, in a criminally underexplored genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a grind of down time, or tedious chores.EDIT: The dev says that the "chores"  are part of the early game. I get that. It's still tedious, repetitive, and not enjoyable to me, hence my review.A game needs to be "fun" from the start, or else I lose interest. I don't want to sink hours into some game to only find out the later game isn't my thing as well.Give the game some things that will catch my interest right from the start. Give me more things to do other than just operating a bunch of laundry machines, and clicking the exact same buttons for hours before getting to what is supposed to be the whole point of the game: operating an arcade.If this sounds critical, well, that's the point. But I hope that it is constructive as well. I'll try it again at some point to see what it is like now.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: For all the Gen-Xers out there who loved going to the arcade, this game will be a big dose of nostalgia.  The time Management is fun but not punishing.  The Arcade games are generally pretty enjoyable to play, and aren't complete knockoffs of well established arcade tropes, and generally at least bring some new gameplay elements to the table.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to play a game within a game within a game? No, it's not , but it makes me think of recursion, and within this game there are definitely stories within stories that make the value for money go sky-high!Tedium? That would be your own fault, and the laundry is a joke (to be vague 🔐) + I praise the developer for wrongfully advertising their game — rather as work than play?!9.1337/10 — Extra fun with/against friends! Some arcade games really deserve to be released stand-alone!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It is an average game of grind this and that, it has minimal fun. The early grind is decidedly boring, it does get better with time but only just. The controls are straight forward if a bit clunky. Perhaps with time this could be a bit better but as of now it is about 75% as far as worth goes 5-10$ game, good for a couple hours of fun. I wish there was a neutral recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you are enjoying a game but have to stop playing to go to work or do some chores? Isn't that the highlight of your day? These devs seem to think so, since that is the ENTIRE gameplay loop here. Start each day coming in to work to clean up piles of trash. no matter how clean you kept the store the night before it seems throughout the night the shop turns into a homeless shelter.Load washing machines with clothing, plunge a toilette, pick up gum, pick up trash, take trash out, take clothing from washer and place it in dryer. Then when you can find a couple mins play some bad knock offs of classic arcade games. All so you can scrape together enough cash to select another generic arcade game or shop upgrade.Rinse and repeat. It may turn into a fun arcade management sim at some point after purchasing enough upgrades but I am not willing to sit through the hours of boredom required to get to that point.Why have the boring laundry feature at all? Why not just allow you to manage and customise an arcade? The only reason for the laundry bs seems to be to support whatever weak af story they are trying to push. Like doing laundry and playing bad games? This one is for you
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Decent games, decent "loop" on the laundromat sim. Weirdly characterless graphics in the world, all the humans look like Poser people. Shines once you get the Jukebox after a few hours. Overall a bit like if the Game Center CX games sacrificed game quality for a great 90s mise en scène.Many things need refinement... some buggy games, some wonky hitboxes on cabinet coin boxes. The story eventually takes a weirdly depressing turn which I simply "alt f4'd" out of.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It takes too long to get to the good bits where you just play arcade games every day.  It's a game I quite enjoyed, but I also found to be monotonous at times.  I just wanted to play some arcade games, collect my quarters, and call it a day.  The laundry aspect is just... boring as heck.  And it goes on forever.Still, I don't think there are many Arcade Shop simulators that have really managed to pull off as much success as Arcade Paradise has.  It really is a good game, once you get past much of the annoying aspects.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun arcade games. There really isn't a machine I dislike, they're all enjoyable. A lot of remixes on classics and some unique games as well. The unique ones for me are some of my favourites. Especially Blockchain, as soon as I figured it out it was very addicting. Also the progress being saved on a lot of the machines is super helpful. The story is more involved than I expected, I quite enjoyed it and was surprised at some events taking place. The nostalgia feel and look is flawless. There's a schedule to your day, but no stress behind it, you can really just do whatever you want throughout the day, even if that's absolutely nothing. Let your machines all break and stare at the floor morning to night, no worries. I personally can't do that, but the option is there.There are bugs, but that's to be expected with so many different types of games and the devs are very clearly working on fixes on the regular. There are small wishes like the ability to control the jukebox while in a game, and maybe a way of highlighting trash easier (thru an upgrade maybe idk) since the carpet is fairly dark and some trash is clear or minuscule. I also wish you could accrue pounds easier. I beat the game and have more money than I know what to do with, but barely any upgrades or music.Having said that it's a great game to pick up and play, even after completion. Had tons of fun playing multiplayer games with my kid, and getting the goals on each machine is a fun long term... well, goal.  Having the to-do list is a great way of getting me to play games I haven't in a while, and I often keep playing games even after finishing the tasks. The music is surprisingly catchy. I've been humming choruses while doing chores at home, and not even realizing it's from this game. _childDocuments_.review: So after more time in this game, and reading a developer's response to a negative review, you really don't need to do any of the laundry out in the bins in the laundromat part of the arcade. It's basically just extra money to help you get started, cause like the message I saw from the dev "You can actually make more money from the arcade machines than the laundry if you focus on it." and you 100% can. I've been having more fun, and been making more money just focusing on the machines. Do the laundry if you want some extra money, but don't expect to do a lot of gaming while those are going on. You only have 3 minutes between each cycle. I feel like if it was actually LONGER. the balance between doing laundry and trying to do the game's goals, wouldn't be that bad. So just play the game how you want in the end, as there's no upkeep. No real way to lose the game, which is kinda something that I wish the game HAD. Like maybe just a harder option or something. Other than that, it's kinda dumb you can play the machines where ever you want, like in the laundromat, or just in spots you select instead of preassigned positions. Some of them, like the ones in the corner, or in the middle look so weird, and I wish I could fix them cause they're canted in such a weird way (like the video air hockey table, like wtf is that angle? Why can't it just me STRAIGHT?)TL;DR: It's a fun little tycoon game, but it's very base level. Barely any management elements, it's basically you playing arcade machines to get people to play them, and upgrade the arcade. You can't interact with people, so it feels like a ghost town really. Also don't expect ANY customization of the walls of your arcade, they're already furnished...

_childDocuments_.review: Did your childhood have trips to Vegas where you got to play in the arcades? Or a pizza place with a really rad selection of games? Maybe the local comic store was so fun because it had those machines you loved? Did little you dream of making your own place where you could play games all day and get paid for it? Yeah? Buy in. The game starts a little slow, and I need to tell you: Ignore, the freaking, laundry. It's not Laundry Paradise, it's Arcade Paradise. Follow your dreams, get some passive income going and enjoy the games. The game has a few story misses, but overall: Lovely, and lets you play out your childhood fantasy of your own arcade to help make people happy. Plus, anyone who's on your favorite game gets de-rezzed the second you get close to them. Man, I wish I got 60 bucks every time I took out the trash. I'd have the cleanest place on the western hemisphere. I will warn you that if you play this game for too long you'll develop a strange compulsion to fire up The Witcher and have Geralt take a long walk off a short pier.

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy first person camera, way too slow progress, locking behind the ability to simply sprint under 4 hours of playtime, this game isn't really worth it. I think I got this in some bundle for pretty cheap, but looking at the price on Steam both on Steam sales and MSRP I could easily call this a rip off. I feel like they have stuff going, but it's not...great. The retro-inspired games are at best, good mobile games and nowhere near the quality of good arcade games. If you can get it for under $5 I'd recommend. Also I think I'm way too jaded for the optimistic and like, joyous ♥♥♥♥ this game tries to pull. Also like combining the thing that makes money at first (literally doing CHORES) to playing the arcade games and you need to focus on the chores instead of getting to do the remotely fun stuff.Also like, on the subject of monotinus tasks in games, it really just does not work in this type of game. It works GREAT in horror games where the you get sucked into the mundanity, but here there's just nothing going for it, if I'm taking out my actual phone while playing a game because I have to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wait for 2 minutes and if I go start an in game arcade machine I'll have to leave before the arcade game becomes fun, it's just...not worth it.EDIT:-also really, microtransations on minigames for an already kinda overpriced game?-i said this already but I want to reiterate, if the main way to make money in an ARCADE sim for the first 4 hours is to do Laundry, then maybe something should be redone.-the "sim" part is lacking as well which makes me wonder what this game is trying to do. If it's a sim go full out and let me do more than just 2 different settings with 3 options and moving around the cabinets.TLDR: too shallow, too boring, too expensive, but has potential that I didn't talk about enough because I'm too fed up by the mundanity.

_childDocuments_.review: Work simulator where you need to try to turn a laundromat into an Arcade.  Sounds pretty trite if you ask me.But oh boy... was I wrong. This game has had me sucked in for a good 10 hours so far (sorry work and school). The menial tasks of loading laundry into a washer, waiting, loading it into a dryer, wait, then unload and drop off for a paltry sum of cash sounds mundane. But the main antagonist sees life as I think a lot of us do.. as a weird game. Everything from removing gum from surfaces, taking out the trash, and even loading and unloading the laundry is all based as mini-games. you ask? Well from the beginning the laundromat houses a few misplaced arcade cabinets in the back of the laundromat. But low and behold .So then you begin the task of raising money from both sides of the location, adding new machines, expanding space, and all the while each arcade cabinet is a game in itself. In this one title you are effectively picking up numerous video games. Backed by an awesome Synthwave, Vaporwave, Darkwave, and other 80's nostalgia, this game raises the question "What if YOU could make an arcade and enjoy your job?".I'm hooked on this title already, and I simply saw it on Opera GX as a new release. But I was like I would LOVE to have an arcade (a la 80s style). If you enjoy titles like Viscera Clean Up Detail or other "Work Sims". This title is something special. Even if all you wanna do is play arcade cabinets all day made for the game and listen to the aforementioned music. I can't wait to continue expanding my arcade and maybe eventually rid myself of the laundromat.Edit: spelling corrections.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played just under an hour to get a first impression and while I want to love this game so bad, right now it just feels like a lost opportunity. I don't really understand why it had to be such a pivotal part of the game and if so I really wish it could have been something more entertaining (substitute the laundromat with a pizza place).   There are other little things that don't really make sense such as why the laundromat is filthy when you arrive in the mornings even though you left it cleaned up etc. You can tell they put a lot of love into the arcade games and while I don't mind the grind aspect of making money to buy and improve my arcade, I just hate that you do it in such a boring, uninteresting place. _childDocuments_.review: This game is quite charming. The aesthetics are retro, and I love how the place changes visually as you get further into the game. In terms of gameplay, at first I thought it was going to be one of those more mundane simulators where you put laundry in a machine and the tumble dryer afterwards, but nah. You're given the choice for how you want to approach each day. Just slave away with the laundry machines? Go for it! Or you wanna grind out the arcade machines in the back? Sure, why not?I like how there's noticeable progression. One of the first games I had grinded out was Racer Chaser and it quickly became an absolute money maker, giving me a hopper full of 250$ just about every day. It's cool that playing the games doesn't only serve as a fun side thing to do, but also actively provides them with bonus income due to rising popularity as well as bonuses from the different goals you can achieve at them. I also enjoy the soundtrack and general sound design, and how everything is gamified.Overall, I'd say I'll give this game a solid 8/10 so far. There's a lot to do, but no pressure to get it done.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so surprised with how much i enjoyed this game. I had so much fun running the laundromat while trying to earn the money to buy new game cabinets.
