_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is a great game if you enjoy progression and seeing numbers grow. Once you are in post-credits, there isn't much more to grow with. A few bugs here and there, but it was a great time nonetheless.Arcade Paradise, once I got done with it, makes me think of Nosebleed's other game, Vostok Inc. That game blends shmup gameplay with incremental game mechanics (Think Geometry Wars mixed with Cookie Clicker). Arcade Paradise is actually pretty similar to that, where you have 2 or 3 incomes, one of them being the laundry can be steady profit at the start, and the other being arcades that will get exponentially more profitable over the course of the game.There is something therapeutic to doing the laundry part for myself. That's just me though, you'll either like it or don't care for it. That won't be the actual focus for long though, because you've done the numbers and the arcades will make more profit. I did like juggling between doing the laundry in between playing the arcades, getting a few more goals and to-do list objectives finished on the games being done so they become more profitable. You'll want to focus on the to-do list because it will give you a secondary currency you save up to get very useful upgrades, especially a certain one that makes collecting profits from the machines automatic. There may be a point where you choose to not do the laundry nor no longer go for S-ranks because the arcade generates way more profit.The games themselves, for the most part, are all good quality. Some would have an odd bug here and there (and some more than others) but can all be played decently. Using your favorite modern twin-stick controller is highly recommended. The highlights of the game selection for me are Woodgal's Adventure (Bejeweled clone), Zombat2 (Twin Stick Shooter), Barkanoid (Arkanoid with an adorable doggie), Woodguy's Golf (if you like golf games that is), and the Whack-A-Gopher game. A lot of the fun and novelty of this game is discovering what games are in here and how they play like, plus seeing how much money you can get from them.As far as actually customizing an arcade goes, you can only really place machines at certain spots... and that's it. The actual management part of the game is very lite, and the main focus is the arcade games themselves. You can't change decorations or add odds and ends here and there. I would've liked to add a fan by the DDR machine, because I can relate to how hot and sweaty DDR players can get (I'm sure the NPCs that digitize away would appreciate it). For you achievement hunters out there, do know going into this game that it gets pretty grindy. As of the most recent update on 9/7/2022, I was able to unlock the last few achievements I had been bugged out of.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Really recommend this game!Showing results for Very nice looking game, the games in the arcade are all playable and all machines have different goals to fulfill in order to get more profit out of them. You play as a character beginning your life in the laundromat business and from there your adventure begins, slowly but surely.Very fun Simulator for sure and if you like retro arcade machines this game is for you, graphic are pretty nice and the game run very smoothly to. There is even a story in this that is very interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it, and loved every single second up to the end.   Is there grinding?   Yes.  Lots of it, but the progression from laundry grunt to arcade owner feels the exact amount of grind. You won't have time to play the arcades at first of course, and it's up to each player finding a way to balance work time and play time. Sounds much like real life maybe??? Of course!  And, as far as I felt, it was the intention.  Maybe people who didin't like that grinding and had trouble finding that balance felt annoyed for this metaphore for real life...  and it's understandable.   But there are ways to get to that balance...  and eventually, midway to the game, you'll find yourself doing more playing than laundring.  Not for nothing there's a PDA task that reads "Do not perform any laundry task today." as a way to SHOW you there's life beyond laundring.  :)The Arcades feel right... some more than others of course (Fruit Jam is hedious... Stockpile is wonderful) and there will be a game for everyone.  Yes, they are simple... some don't even follow the "arcade rules"... but it wasn't the point of this game to make an Arcade Simulator and portray FULL arcade games from beggining to end...  though I hope someday developers allow Workshop Modding and lets us add our own games, emulated or from scratch.  If that happens...  this would easily become the greates game of the last decade.  :)Anyways...  if you have the patience and enough nostalgia loads to see above the laundry grinding and follow the intended game progression as it is and not as a nuissance, then you should give this game a go. If you are seeking for instant gratification... move along and go back to your Fortnite kid.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting a ton out of this title when I picked it up. Sure, manage a arcade was the thought but holy cow, I wasn't ready for what was in store. You can really tell how much of a passion project this was for the dev team. From all the small details in the arcade to the complete bonkers amount of depth to the game. It seems like everything was really handled with care. I was not prepared to see that every single game is playable... Not only that but they are fun! The story line is heartfelt and got me invested. The arcade expansions provide a game loop in itself and the goals... don't get me started on the goals. I NEED TO FINISH THEM ALL! lol. This is a gem of a game that shouldn't be missed. I Highly recommend you give this game a try. You are in for a treat. I give it 10 Woodguy jr. axes out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratched the right itch for me. Its been a pretty fun sim/management game and unlocking the new arcade games is always exciting. There is a grind but the only thing I would recommend for anyone playing this game is to realize you dont have to do the laundry after a while as you will make way more money back in the arcade.  Also, the soundtracks on this game are god tier!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Call it a mostly-thumbs-up. Managing the arcade is fun, the aesthetics are spot on, and it really evokes that vaguely early 1990s feel. Simple chores like cleaning up and doing laundry even add to the chill-out factor of just hanging around doing stuff and watching the numbers go up. It does what it does well enough to be worth recommending.But there are caveats. Many of the games are clones of existing arcade classics and mobile games, but worse (pixel art that doesn't behave like pixel art, slow play, clunky controls). There's not a lot of customization of your arcade beyond game placement. Many of the goals and tasks are way too difficult to bother with, especially if you don't like the game in the first place.So if you're forgiving of jank and not expecting an all-killer-no-filler experience, it's pretty okay.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is barely a negative review, while I really like this game and think it has the potential to be a 5/5 game, this game is mired with bugs and poor balance to such a degree that I cant give it a positive review at the moment.Arcade Paradise is a super cool game about running an arcade (and laundromat) and slowly expanding it, It gives me nostalgia for something i barely experienced, its always cool to finally save up enough cash to finally expand the arcade and see what cool new games you can buy and a lot of the games are fun or cool twists on older games of the era. You also progress faster bu playing the games you buy and completing challenges, which in turn makes them earn more money, rewarding you for engaging in every aspect of the game which goes along with daily tasks that give you a special currency used for upgrades like faster movement or extending the day so you can do more. Unfortunately, the game seems to front lode the game with the cooler cabinets, after about the halfway through the game, i found myself rarely getting a good new cabinet or getting something that after playing once i never wanted to touch again. for instance, I understand why Shuttlecocks(pong) is in the game, but why would I ever want to play pong, there are multiple games like this, tedious or just not fun to play, but to make them earn a reasonable amount of money, you need to play them and complete challenges, it really turns into a drag after a while.To add to that the balance, for lack of a better term, on the challenges is all over the place, some you can do in one or two plays on the cabinet, while others take far to long to grind out, add the grind to bad controlling cabinets like pool, darts or Foosball makes it painful to boost their value.Speaking to the balance elsewhere, you get 3 tasks everyday to do various thing, like get a certain score in a game etc. giving you a second currency (pounds sterling) to buy upgrades that help streamline or improve the experience. You get 15-20 Pounds per completed task, which seems fine in the beginning, but towards the end of the game, you are still only earning 15-20 per task, while most upgrades cost 300-600, with only a few cost 50-250. It takes way to long to get these things and as previously stated, you get more cabinets that aren't fun, which means you will start getting task for the new cabinets, with the difficulty or those challenges being all over the place, some easy, some way to hard and to make it even worse, they are random and cant be changed, its a massive grind.EDIT: Ok so, I still have a lot of issues with this game, the upgrades are way to grindy and a lot of them are bad while others feel necessary, and at maybe 50% of the cabinets are bad/boring. BUT, When looking at my time with Arcade Paradise, i did still have a fun time with it, all things considered.TLDR. So, if you can put up a fair amount of playing and grinding games like pong, arkanoid etc. then i think there's a very cool game here you will enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for a little over a year now and it's been worth the wait! All the arcade cabinets I've unlocked so far are so varied and each unique soundtrack sets it apart from its neighboring cabinet. I love how it turns even the most mundane things into a mini-game, cleaning the toilet, laundry, trash, and debugging are all an intuitive mini-game that adds that much more replayability for me. Well done devs! I'm so glad I stumbled on this game and I can't wait to see what's next!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING!!I have been waiting for this title to be released for some time now and safe to say it hasn't disappointed so far!Im only just passed 1.5hrs in so far and absolutely enjoying every minute of it!.Can I see myself getting lost in this for some time? YES! (may need to call in for some sick days)The only con i have with the game is the people who come into the laundry/arcade, the way they fade out like a glitch and disappear when going near them slightly takes you out of the game BUT its only a small gripe and i'm assuming this was done for performance reasons!So if you ever want to move out from your mums basement, learn how to wash and dry your own clothes all while sneaking a game in between loads then this is the game for you!!HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, this game really is a wild ride. That tagline of "rags to riches" rings true as you go from desperately clamoring together money, washed clothes, trash, and chewed gum to having a bustling arcade full of games that you can play, a retro aesthetic, and peace of mind with the "quality of life" upgrades.Where the game is a menial chore from laundromat owner on one end, it comes out as a REALLY fun arcade business simulator on the other side.Some of the arcade games were quite easy to meet the goals for, others are near impossible, but I had so much fun digging into all the minigames. This really was a labor of love, and it's a shame that more people don't know about this game. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Delve into the realms of dirty clothes, retro video games, parental gaslighting, and sibling revolt as Ashley, the Business major dropout who got punished into management of her father's old business. Forced into a daily grind of laundry loads, gum removal, toilet plunging, and picking up after the mysterious stranger who leaves discarded bottles, newspapers, and food wrappers behind every night after she closes the store, and all this without being able to wash her hands... ever. Her only release from this hellhole is to revive the forgotten video arcade in the back room. Earning enough to unlock new upgrades such as renovation, more cabinets, games, and even a jukebox over time. Despite Ashley's inability to remember the office safe's combination, she manages to get it open every night, making the player wonder why she didn't set out as a bank heist specialist instead. Things I'd love to see in the sequel (and there will be a sequel):- Laundry and Arcades are all about coins and the owner's love/hate relationship with them as the source of both income and frustration. I'd like to see the monetary system converted to quarters and make the business of collecting and hauling the quarters and clearing jams in the machines part of the game.- More RPG elements. Arcades are a people business, and though there's plenty of emails and chats in the office computers, customers are more like background art in this game. - Vending machines are shown in this game but you can't interact with them. That's another profit stream the player could manage.- The most unrealistic thing about this game is a laundromat where no machine appears to ever break down, get overloaded, or overfilled with soap. Customers can grow impatient and territorial in a laundromat, and I was hoping for some chaos  from them even though the focus of the game is on the business in the back room.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review by saying that I have played 80% of the business simulator genre, and had Arcade Paradise on my wish list for about a year!What a disappointment!Unfortunately, Arcade Paradise suffers from an unsatisfying gameplay loop, a lack of content and no real personality after the opening sequence.The game starts promisingly- We get an incredible MTV Style animated video to kick things off and it had me sufficiently excited to get stuck in! Then we have a small tutorial- teaching us how to wash clothes, pick up trash and unblock the toilet- the graphics are pretty good and the visual style is very pleasing to the eye- so far so good....And then we start to "play" for real.Day 1: Enter the shop, pick up trash-unblock toilet-wash clothes-decide to try an arcade game (this one is a mash up of GTA and Pac man)-cannot finish game of GTPAcman due to laundry commitments-it reaches 11pm already and it is time for bed...No problem I think to myself, its early days, I will forget about the Arcade for a few days and grind some laundry until I have enough money to hire someone to help me with laundry while I play games out the back.And that's it. that's the whole game...Pick up TrashUnblock the toilet or stand around awkwardly watching washing machines spin while trying to occasionally squeeze 30 seconds out of a terrible air hockey rip off.there is no balance- 1 second = 1 minute game time A wash/dry cycle takes around 3mins in game hours each (so 2 x 3min) There is no possible way to have a complete or even satisfying arcade game in between the time it takes to wash clothes so therefore you have a choice- do I want to earn money today or do I want to play a mediocre clone of Dr Mario.I am no stranger to grinding in games- as a matter of fact i rather enjoy it- but the problem with Arcade Paradise is that there is not enough satisfaction, fun or content to be had in the running of the Laundromat portion of the game to justify Grinding out the machines with hard work- and the machines themselves are not enough fun to justify skipping work to play them anyway!I must also add that in my short playtime I experienced several bugs, the worst of which made the game freeze on start up, and also noticed that trash can spawn in places you cannot physically reach!So, to summarise , I love the premise and can see the potential in the game, but right now it feels lifeless and very very boring - to the point where i cannot force myself to wash clothes anymore because i don't care enough about the arcade games available to want to play them. Visually one of the better looking simulation games but I feel that 3 hours in I have seen absolutely everything the game has to offer on the business sim front and it is charmless.TLDR: 4/10- Looks great visually but ultimately very boring and lifeless with several game breaking bugs and the most unsatisfying gameplay loop i have seen from the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for August 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before September 5th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Laundromat simulator.Arcade Paradise might be where the game eventually gets, but early on players are running a laundromat, having to wash and dry clothes for money, and able to play arcade games in the back while waiting for the machines to finish.  Over time earning money will let players expand and I assume play more games.  Having to mix time between the laundromat and the arcade machine is challenging, but hopefully, that isn’t as much a part of the title.The downside is the games aren’t the deepest, and even the few games that are surprisingly deep at the beginning don’t work well in the one to two-minute range players have to play them.   There are also 8 games available as DLC, the total price of those titles is almost as much as the base game as well.  While there are 35 titles contained in the game, immediately seeing a hand held out for more money always rubs me the wrong way.   Also, some of the games are a bit “meh”, so I’m not sure if the ones I haven’t played yet will be amazing.Pick this up if you love the simulator genre and old arcade games.  There’s a lot of work that went into this, and I’m curious how much deeper the game goes, but I’m not sure how long this one can keep my attention.  Still, the idea of running an arcade is one of those things 90s kids always wanted to do. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I used to go to the arcades all the time when I was a kid, so this hits just the right nostalgia buttons for me. It's not really an arcade management game. More like a celebration of arcades of old. You can play an of the arcade  games you buy for your arcade and I think that's where the real draw is. A lot of them take clear inspiration from many old games, like Pong, Pac-Man, Missile Command, etc. The quality of the games are hit and miss, but there are a lot of gems there. There's a decent challenge to most of them.It's fun to see the little details of the arcade change as you slowly upgrade it, too. The story isn't bad, with good voice acting. Honestly, once I played through to the story conclusion, I didn't feel as inclined to do a 100% completion of the game. Your mileage may vary on that.Still, I enjoyed it. I think others might, too, as long as you don't go into it expecting a deep arcade management simulator and more of a narrative-driven game with a lot of arcade throwback minigames.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, Now i can continue to avoid washing my own laundry IRL and wash other peoples laundry from the comfort of my desk. 10/10 would wash clothes again!All seriousness if you like the sort of Vaporwave/Synthwave style thats making its way through youll love this game. So sit back and just play some old cabs and an enjoy the late 80's/90's feel of life.I will say my only 2 points of negativity would be 1. the computer when buying the cabinets the scroll wheel sometimes skips multiple pages making you think you've gotten all the cabs. Use the arrow keys to by pass this issue, but still i would like to scroll.2. Please either add a small reticle or something to make Trash picking up a little easier. _childDocuments_.review: I rarely ever feel the need to write reviews about games, but this game has given me hours of enjoyment. Yes you have to work for your goal of getting an arcade but it does come. The laundry part isn't even that bad. Once you unlock your to-do list, you can start having a reason to play games for a little bit in between laundry loads and as you play, the laundromat becomes less and less of one of your concerns. The game does a great job of making the work you put in feel rewarding and I'm really happy I ignored the few negative reviews I saw. If you grew up going to old school arcades or are an arcade enthusiast, you'll really appreciate the amount of detail they've put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this for anyone wanting to play a collection of different 1980s to 1990s retro arcade games for a dozen or so hours, as it is so light on management of the laundromat/arcade that there's no bankruptcy possible.   This is a relatively relaxing and calming game for me, though I wouldn't call the vast majority of arcade games casual in terms of difficulty.  It gamifies the laundromat aspect and you are able to game in-between laundring, wherein upgrades become available to shorten the laundry and increase the gaming.  I'm glad I got in a Humble Choice bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Not to be rude to devs, but, when I played this for the first time, the whole premise was very innovative... You're in charge of a laundrymat and you get the brilliant idea of having a retro room where clients can wait for their clothes to dry out... Your dad is against it and does his absolute best so that you fail (as most trash dads do, mine included).Anyways, let's go straight to the point: your task is simple, micro AND macromanage your laundrymat... How you do that? Cleaning out garbage thrown around by your customers, pull out chewing gum plastered in your chairs, do the laundry, wait for the laundry to wash, take it out of the washing machine and put it into the dryer, take out money from the locked coin dispensers in the space reserved for laundry and on each Arcaded Machine and finally put it into a safe in your office. Sounds simple, right? No, it's not simple, because in between all of those things you're TASKED to testrun the Arcade machines in the back by playing them and I mean really playing them... like reaching highscores, beating games, doing cringy challenges in a wannabe pacman game, that kind of stuff! Now, I wouldn't be mad about having minigames inside the original game, but I am... One because you've literally got NO TIME to care for the Arcade machines when you have to keep your clients doing their laundry satisfied and two because these minigames, most of the at least, are trash. Too bad you can't fix how buggy Race Crasher is, which is a Pacman clones... I understand, licensing is an issue here, but I would've loved to see ACTUAL retro games in the cabinets, like the real Pacman, or Galaga, or frigging Master Blaster for all I care... Instead you get a bunch of new "Arcade games" never heard of before that are a MESS, to say the least.Other than that, you can use your money to buy new "crappy" Arcade cabinets, upgrade your laundmat as well as create more space for more Arcade cabinets. Your father will be increasingly mad about how you're turning his renowned laundmat into an Arcade "garbage bin", as he calls it. Thing is, and I agree on this, videogames sell more than frigging laundry, dad! Even the to-do list and chores you do around the laundmat when you're not gaming on your Arcade cabinets get tedious after a while... Two weeks in and you're already sick and tired of collecting socks on the floor, collecting money from dispensers, and taking out chewing gum from the toilet seat...It's a , I somehow had lots of fun with it the first time I played it, now to me it seems just flawed beyond recognition. The thumbs up is for nostalgia's sake, other than that, the game is horribly boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Set in 1993, during that transition between 80s neon to 90s grunge, this simulator captures a era lost to time. Starting with a Laundromat with a few arcade cabinets you expand and build a arcade business. Every arcade machine is a fully realized mini game, with goals to encourage you to complete to have them make more profits.Yes it is a bit of a grind, and I am not a fan of the save system, with no separate files and where if you quit the game it automatically ends the current day.Overall I have loved it, from the asthetic and theming, to it scratching that itch for management sim with tasks and bits of busywork.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: There is just something about a simulator with a lot of heart that gets me. Arcade Paradise does a lot of things, all relatively well.Arcade Paradise is:-A business simulator-A love-letter to 90's arcade culture-A bunch of mini-games in a trench coat that (miraculously) feel like one cohesive whole-Sometimes frustrating with inexact controlsAside from fairly satisfying arcade games, my favorite thing about Arcade Paradise is that it is chock full of so many delicious details: the pattern of the arcade carpet, the wear and tear on the laundry machines, the old computer in the back office, the gum you have to clean off of the equipment. If you enjoy business simulators, arcades, or laundry, I would recommend trying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: What makes a game fun? It's a difficult question to answer. However, Nosebleed Interactive seems to have a very different idea of fun than me!The game revolves  around you managing a laundromat with arcade cabinets in the back. You clean up trash, put laundry in laundering machines, put washed clothes in dryers, put dried clothes on a table, remove gum, empty hoppers (coin mechanisms) and clean toilets. You make money while doing all of these which you can then use to buy extra arcade cabinets.Does all this sound fun to you? Yeah, to me neither."But, you're representing the game wrong! You're supposed to be playing the arcade games while the laundry is spinning!"Ah yes, the arcade games. OK-ish knock offs of existing classics ... but every time a dryer or washing machine is done, your hand (with watch) pops up to remind you it's done which not only distracts you, it blocks part of the screen. What a blast it is to try and play a game to constantly get reminded the tedious job of emptying & filling machines is to be done!I mean, the idea isn't bad and sure you end up getting rid of the laundromat in the end ... after hours of tedious grinding to get there.It's also such a wasted good idea that is poorly executed. Instead of you starting in 1985 or so, you start in 1993, well after the arcade craze had died down massively and the Playstation was close to be released which pretty much killed the arcade cabinet industry. Yet half the game seems to be 80's themed, the other half 90's themed. Nosebleed, what on earth were you thinking?There's also so much that could have been done better. The 80's vibe (or 90's vibe) isn't there. There's no music that fits either era, the TV is some early 80's style and just shows a test image, you can't stock candy or soda machines (or remove the coins), you cannot interact with any visitors, etc. Another grave sin is that the game refuses to let you run the game in the background to pass in-game time. It will pause it no matter what you do. On top of this are the technical problems: rebinding keys is extremely buggy - some keys refuse to be rebound and the on-screen prompts show the original keys. The FOV is also extremely low and almost made me nauseous which is very rare -  I've been playing FPS games since 1993 and it's been a long time since a FPS made me nauseous.Does the game have positives between being a good idea? Well, the graphics are OK (but not on par with the way better New Retro Arcade which hits the retro vibe a million times better) and the arcade games are decent. Other than that? It's just no fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting arcade sim bogged down and hindered by Laundromat chores.  I get they needed a way for you to make money in game to buy new arcades and slowly build up your collection but the tedium and border sets in quick. The mini games are fun in their own right but you hard get any time to focus on them even with the upgrades unlocked.  The issue is some of the challenges to get the upgrades are interrupted by the watch reminding you to swap stuff from the washer to the dryer or from the dryer to the collection table. Also what kind of laundromat makes the employee's do everyone else's laundry?! every one I've been to is self serve and again takes me out of the fun of managing an arcade when I have to wash Tim, tom, bob and sally's undies every couple minutes.  If you like a reallllllyy dull slow burn/grind, this is probably down your ally. If not, there are better management sim games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Game(s) of the YearI love the super nostalgic vibes.Most arcades in video games fart in your face and say "Here, 2 of these are playable, the rest are coincidentally "out of order". Here the WHOLE arcade is playable. Which is cool. I love variety. I love that all the games are really old school arcade games, just re skinned.Also I like the story and the idea of starting with a tiny a** arcade and then the arcade overtakes the laundromatALSO the laundromat chores is just "casual gameplay" that nets you extra $"Is the DLC worth it?"Yes. _childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to give this game a negative review, but considering what this is, I feel like it just barely misses the mark. I realized very quickly what the game loop is all about. Doing laundry, cleaning the shop, making money, buy an arcade machine. Rinse repeat. Sure, the goal of it all is to get the arcade machines so you can play them, but I just feel like that isn't enough variety in gameplay.Initially I got the impression that this game had more simulation/survival mechanics based on the preview videos, but that's not the case. It's honestly just a bunch of minigames you try to unlock by doing the same few repeating tasks around the laundromat.  On the surface, the game looks beautiful, They nailed the retro aesthetic, and I haven't ran into any bugs in my couple of hours of play time, so that was nice. I just wish the devs would add more to the game to make it feel more alive, and have more things to do. Maybe have a research mechanic to make our own custom games. Maybe let us have another way of generating revenue. Hold tournaments for customers, let them win prizes. Maybe have a separate area for a kitchen for food and drinks to sell, and hire staff. The list can go on forever on stuff the devs could add. It was hard to figure out if I liked this game or not, because I am a fan of everything in the game, but it just feels lacking, and repetitive. Also, when I'm browsing Steam and trying to decide what game I want to play, I always get a little excited when This game comes across my screen, but then I immediately remember why I haven't picked it up again. It's one of those games that you can get very excited for very quickly and see a lot of potential in what it could be, but then get deflated with the reality that it's just a bunch of minigames with chore mechanics in the way that get stale very quickly. I also feel that the $20 might even be too much for this game being that it's mainly just buying minigames since that's the end goal.I really want to like this game, but the game has been out long enough to see the direction the developers are going with this game, and the above listed wishes seem very unlikely. So if you're looking for a collection of mini games that you have to unlock by grinding a few small chores over and over again then this game is perfect for you. If you're looking for a TRUE 90's arcade simulator with depth, then you may need to look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on my 40-50 hour playthrough to the end of the game.What starts as an intentionally tedious simulation of doing people's clothes in a laundromat turns shortly into running an arcade. Your job is to make that transition happen. This involves playing the arcade games, each of which have Goals, just small achievements that are specific to that game, and the more Goals you get done, the more the machine earns. This, in itself, could take up 20-30 hours of your life easily. Thankfully, the more you play the arcade games, the more money you earn from them. You can customize the layout of the arcade games, and this is actually relevant to the money you make, as putting less popular machines near highly popular ones gives a bonus to the lower popularity machines. That, and it's just nice to have a choice of where your machines go. This isn't one of those trash simulators - this game has tons of polish and care put into the game, be it the quite good soundtrack that has electronic/rock/rap songs, the artwork and posters in-game, or even the story and writing that I honestly didn't even expect the game to have. Absolutely recommend if you have any interest at all in retro arcade games - all your favorites have been pretty well replicated (or in fact, made even more interesting) in most cases. Even after beating the game, there's still plenty of reasons to keep visiting your games.Also, to the people annoyed about laundry - here's a hint: Just stop doing laundry. Seriously. Just don't even do it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: First off: Yes, I do recommend this. Quite a bit. Some of the arcade games by themselves would most likely be worth the price of admission, never mind *all* of them.I see this game being compared to "sims" (Gas Station Sim, etc) quite a bit, but I really think that's an incorrect impression. The game is a bit of a trojan horse, in the sense that where it starts and where it goes are very different (this actually fits the meta-narrative quite well, for what it's worth).In the start, you're basically forced to deal with the laundry side of the business. It's boring, but decent money. A tip for newer players: You're only graded on the wash/dry speed from when you put in the load, so if it's close to closing time, save them till tomorrow for more cash.After some time, you'll start growing the arcade, until it eventually eclipses the laundromat in cashflow. One of the semi-early space upgrades makes it clear that you now have free reign to ignore the laundry completely, and I suggest you follow that advice. Passive income from the arcade, especially with a few popular machines (clear their goals if you like the game) rakes in the $$$. That cash buys more machines, which make more money, etc. You can literally sit and stare at the wall for each day, only emptying the hoppers and have infinite cash.However the obvious thing to do at that junction is start playing the arcade games. As I said at the start, many of them are incredibly good, and they cover a wide array of genres. Some of them even include progression mechanics (basically impossible in a real coin-op) which allow you to gain power/abilities over multiple play sessions. I came to look forward to each new machine I unlocked.So, I really have to say, this is not a sim. There's no real pressure, you basically make money by doing nothing (eventually). Sure, you have some chores (trash cleanup, machine repair), but the game devs set them up so they really don't get in the way much. If you force yourself to keep doing laundry when you don't have to, and thus are constantly interrupted in the arcade, I really don't know what to say to you.There are a few annoyances. Upgrades use a secondary currency, which is only gained by doing daily challenges. The payouts on these are incredibly stingy, so it can take a while to get anything. Most of the "annoyance reduction" is under there (less trash, more time in a day, not having to empty the hoppers yourself, etc). Some of the challenges can also end up on games that you don't like. However you can always just wait (or skip) to the next day and get new challenges, so not too big of a deal.The larger problem is the additional jukebox tunes are also under the secondary currency, which means you're really not going to be getting any of them for a very long time. Given how good the default set of jukebox songs are, that's a real shame.Overall, don't go into this expecting a sim. It's really a couple hours of laundry, followed by endless days of hanging out in a sweet arcade.Edit: Forgot to add - Most of the games play just fine with a keyboard, but many of them are better with a gamepad. A few (like pool) are near impossible to play without an analog control. However I had many hours in before I even plugged a gamepad in.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Warning?For a $20 game this is pretty damn fun. I am currently anywhere from 10-20 in game days in, and the game just keeps getting better. From the small management of the arcade consoles, to the little chores you have to do, the game doesn't stop impressing me. You also gotta keep in mind that you're paying for somewhere near 15 or so other mini-games, on top of the main game experience. The small daily quest you receive are super cool, and I love that almost every thing that you do is tied to some form of mini game. I would also suggest buying the DLC that the game has because it brings in some extra cabinets, and from the 3 or 4 I can own currently, I do enjoy them quite a bit. Something else to toss in is the NPC's that are scattered around the shop just kinda disappear as you run into them, and it's pretty damn funny that I can basically kick people out lol.I will say this game does have some problems though. Certain daily quests that you are assigned have been broken for me, which kinda sucks because these quests are supposed to help you get some good upgrades, and I cant because it will not progress further. Another gripe is the watch system. It goes off quite a bit, and I dont really mind it, until im already finishing the load its reminding me of, or playing a game. I've had experiences where I was in the middle of a challenge for Zombat 2 or Racer Chaser, and the watch blocks 1/4 of my screen, which in turn makes me get caught or die from something I couldnt see. Or in the Stacking Game (I dont remember the title) the undo button doesn't work. All small things, but stuff that messes me up nonetheless. BUT! Even though this game might have downsides, it is far better than what I expected. 8.5/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: I was NOT expecting to enjoy Arcade Paradise this much. It's a game that completely flew under the radar for me. I actually discovered it when Nintendo dropped a trailer for the Nintendo Switch version of the game and got it on there. And to answer a quick question about the game on different systems, the performance is just as good on Nintendo Switch as it is on PC. Arcade Paradise has you running your dad's laundormat while he's away working on business ventures in other countries. You play as a character named Ash. Ash wants to make her dad proud of her accomplishments running the laundromat, but she also is a huge gamer and wants to convert the laundromat into a full blown arcade. In comes Lesley, Ash's sister, who works at City Hall and can "bend the strings" to help Ash expand her underground arcade business, and here you have a full blown adventure game inside an arcade game collection inside a laundromat simulator. Running the laundromat is a lot of fun. I personally LOVE doing the chores of washing clothes, drying clothes, picking up trash, unclogging the toilet, and pulling gum. To be completely honest, I wish we could do more like scrub windows, vacuum, mop, and fix the vending machines/TV's. The chores remind me a lot of Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing, and there's a cathartic, therapeutic feeling when cleaning the place up. Devs, if you could consider more chores! While waiting for the laundry to get done, Ash can play the arcade games. Playing the arcade games and achieving the goals the games ask you to accomplish actually increase the cash flow of each game, thus giving you a huge incentive to playing them. The game also has a "to do" list which fills itself with randomized daily missions like "do no laundry at all", "do 5 loads of laundry all at the same time", or "get a score greater than X on this arcade game". So even if you do get all the goals done, the daily to-do's give you lots of replay value to going back and playing those machines. I would definitely compare Arcade Paradise to Animal Crossing. Ash is determined to expand her business. Talking to Dad and Lesley really help the story, I find myself eagerly wanting Ash to succeed and achieve her dreams. This game really pushes the ideology of hard work and being able to work hard and play hard. I think what also makes this game fun are the quirks. Laundromat patrons "fade and pixelate" into minecraft looking people and then fade out of existence when walking too close to them. Trash spawns in the most random of places. Newspaper headlines are super random. There's a lot of fun goodies to be found when playing the game. Overall, I'm still working through Arcade Paradise, but I am LOVING what I'm seeing so far. I also stream the game on Twitch and being able to roleplay and chat with others while running the laundromat side of things is a blast. I cannot recommend this game enough. It's relaxing, chaotic and fun all at the same time. Did I mention this game takes place in the 90's? AND that you can use a PDA?!?! God, I miss those. Thank you so much for developing this game, I can't wait to continue my way through arcade paradise and make Ash's dreams come true.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun, well thought out sim game. It is a bit buggy but as of writing it's been out for like 2 days so that's not a huge deal, game is still super fun and every bug so far has been easily fixed by saving and going to the menu and coming back in to a new day. Just some minor issues like certain pieces of trash not being able to pick up or being extremely difficult if they spawn in certain places, or some hoppers being very hard to access like the pool table, or some machine placements make them hard to reach, also some of the physics in the games are unreliable, pool and the ball launch/pop game the lines don't track super well. Slightly larger issues are one area layout cuts off access to a washing machine early with a metal laundry basket you can't use, again not a huge deal because by that point in the game laundry is really not important anymore, I only wanted to use it once during a quest before I realized there were more behind me. The last major bug I've found was when I first purchased the whack-a-gopher game the gophers didn't load properly and the game was unplayable, but this was fixed by returning to the menu and coming back in. None of these have been huge issues and I've just found ways to work around them, the game itself is amazing and I've binged my way through most of it in about 2 days, pacing can be a bit rough as the game has no organic downtime but it can be paused, so again not a big deal, just be prepared for hours to go missing from your nights. P.S. I've read many reviews on the game annoyed at the laundry loop, the game like MANY others does start with a grind, if you focus on the arcade you can end this VERY quickly, the arcade quickly outstrips the money you can make doing laundry and then you only have to do it for tasks for upgrades. Once the arcade is expanded it also becomes quite a bit more customizable as far as layout, very few machines are stuck in place. The upgrades are a bit grindey themselves but since the challenges also improve your game popularity and keep you playing different games, they really just give you something to do for the 15 minutes or so your arcade makes money throughout the day with a bonus at the end that makes the game easier. FOCUS ON THE ARCADE IN THE ARCADE GAME AND YOU WILL BE LESS FRUSTRATED WITH DOING LAUNDRY

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. So, this is one of those games where I wish there was something between "recommend" and "not recommend". It's enjoyable but only to a point. There are many puzzling design decisions that the devs made here.You're a kid who runs his father's Laundromat (your father is away overseas) that has an arcade in the backroom. You make money by washing and drying people's clothes and from the arcade machines.The fully playable arcade machines are based on real games and are very very good. A lot of care and love went into creating them. There are two pools of money that you have - US dollars and Pounds. The USD is for buying arcade machines and the pounds you get by completing "to-do lists" daily. You get three tasks to do each day to earn pounds. You can earn up to 60 pounds a day if you complete all three. Most of them involve achieving certain things by playing the arcade machines. Here's where the problems start - the to-do tasks are not easy, you're lucky if you get two of the three. AND, you are so busy doing laundry tasks during the day you have almost no time at all to spend playing the arcade machines. You can, and ignore all the laundry, but then you lose that laundry income. And on top of all this, the upgrades are EXPENSIVE so it will take quite a while to get even basic upgrades, and I think I'll lose interest before I get any of them. For example you can't get another employee until you amass 600 pounds. The fastest way to do that means completing all three to-do items everyday for ten days. Nearly impossible to do. It will take much much longer. All the while you're just washing and drying washing and drying, and desperately trying to find a few minutes here and there to play and learn the games.That's my main problem with the gameplay loop in this game.Also notable is the annoying feature that when you quit the game you can't in the middle of the day, because quitting also includes a mandatory "end the day". So again you lose income if you have to quit the game before the end of the day.The washers and driers never break down, which seems odd to me as well.All the garbage appears overnight. Not realistic but not a big deal. But it's inconceivable to me that during game design meetings no one said "hey let's just make the garbage appear randomly throughout the day, just like we do with the dirty laundry baskets.". That is simple to do I'd imagine and makes much more sense.The early 90s atmosphere is great. The laundromat looks great and is very detailed.I want to like it and I'll continue to play but at this point (8 hours in) I think some simple balance changes could improve it a lot. I want the darn upgraded safe that opens quicker but it's 450 pounds so it'll be a while yet. Funny, I'm supposed to be physically in the USA and it's extremely easy to get loads of USD but I can't upgrade the safe without British pounds, which I can only obtain from father by doing daily tasks in the arcade (which father doesn't even approve of!!)... Sigh..

Per day you will get about 500-600$.All in all, this game is for probably the first 5 hours a cleaning and washing simulator.its very repetitive, wich i dont like.If you like repetitive and slowly progressing games, this would be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely call a game "bad", but this is pretty bad. There's already several loooong negative reviews describing all this game's problems - very lengthy, yet articulated better than I ever could. So I'll leave my review short and sweet:It's unfun as a management sim, as a game compilation, and as wish fulfillment. Gameplay is so monotonous and chore-filled that it somehow manages to play like a bleak parody of adult life, despite being named "Arcade Paradise." As fun as the presentation is, once the novelty wears off, there's little left to enjoy.It does have its charms though, and many people enjoyed it. While I personally found it unplayable, it might be your thing. Just be aware that if you don't like the first 2 hours, it'll only get worse. (In my opinion, at least.)

_childDocuments_.review: Originally wishlisted this and followed since 9/21/21 and was excited to buy and play on launch day. I just spent over 4 hours playing through the beginning and it's not quite what I was hoping for. Firstly, it should be called Laundry Hell instead of Arcade Paradise, because you spend most of your time running loads of laundry and cleaning up trash laying around every morning the laundromat opens. Speaking of that, how do you leave the building clean at night and come back to trash every morning? Must be some dirty rats in the building.  Stupid. The arcade games are just o...k. It's cool that you can buy different ones but the cash required to do that from your office is quite the "do the dirty laundry" cycle ad nauseum. You can play the games and just empty the hoppers and collect money that way, but it's an even slower grind. The game got marginally more interesting once to-do lists gave tasks, but some of those were downright impossible like "do 15 loads of laundry" you get 13 done and then run out of time for more laundry to spawn. Overnight the to-do lists reset so you can't work on them through multi-days. There some somewhat clever minigames like a toilet plunger cleaning and throw the trash into the dumpster hitting a bullseye and there is this PDA that's kinda cool to look at and navigate around, but this game is just too much laundromat sim and not enough arcade. Again, the arcade games do have a bit of a retro feel to them, but none of them really caught on. The Pac-Man like game with cop cars was sort of a cross with Rally-X and Pac-Man ... all these games are inspired by some other (better) retro game you love. This game isn't worth $19.99 on Steam, sorry. To my retrogaming friends, just look elsewhere. I didn't refund this, but probably should have.

Gamers have only been complaining about that for about 20 years now though, so I can understand them not knowing we hate that...But all of those complaints pale in comparison to the real issue. _childDocuments_.review: This is a gem. A chill game where you can slowly build up a collection of old school arcade cabinets, and build your dream arcade. The arcade games themselves are deep games where you often can upgrade stuff like a rogue-like, and slowly progess through them. This game is pretty grindy though. Depending on how you earn your money, it will probably take you between 25-35 hours to complete the story and finish your collection, so keep at it, and apply yourself!This game is a niche mix of a casual management sim and an arcade game mix and I love it. And the story was engaging, albeit pretty infuriating.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Quick edit a little ways in cause I see some folks complaining about being interrupted by laundry - focus on growing the arcade part of the business, laundry is such a small part of your income you can actually totally ignore it after a while. My morning routine is to throw on 3 loads of laundry, clean garbage, empty hoppers, finish laundry, and then spend the rest of the day gaming. It kicks ass.Also the later arcade games are amazingly fun/=====================================================================I think this game might be genius...The vibe is pure 90s like when I was a kid. The arcade's soundtrack is full of loving parodies - more than once I was like "Hold up is that Technotronic? Oh no it's just a perfect recreation."The arcade games are a mishmash of familiar favourites with fresh visuals and cute storylines. All of them are well worth spending time with, even if it means missing a laundry timer. The more you play the games, and the more challenges you complete, the more popular and consequently more profitable the games become.Our gameplay loop involves throwing loads of laundry into machines on 3 minute timers, picking up garbage, performing minigames to throw out trash and clean gum, and emptying the cash hoppers. There's lots to keep you busy without feeling overwhelming - there are no penalties for not doing a great job on the laundry besides a lower cash reward for the work.In short, the game has lots to do, an unbelievably comfy vibe, and a real hit of memory lane for we who were kids in the 90s. I really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really on the fence about how I would review this game.  Unfortunately, it's going to have to be a thumbs down from me.But let's go over it:The Pros:I REALLY enjoyed the first 25 hours of this game.  It was great building up my little laundromat slowly but surely into an arcade that people like to come and spend their money at.  I enjoyed the mundane laundry tasks quite a bit, and then also slowly shifting to not need to do any laundry and letting the profits of the arcade take over.  It was fun buying new games and seeing what they were like.  There are some REALLY top tier arcade games in here - mainly Blockchain, even though it took me forever to figure out.  Once I did figure it out, it became super addicting. I also really like the character and aesthetic of the game, where ever single task becomes a minigame with fanfare and scores.  I can S rank laundry! I can S rank taking out the trash!  everything you have to do is very fun and rewarding.  The 90s vibe is very nostalgic to me as well as I grew up in the 90s.Now onto the Cons:Once I beat the story and started grinding for all of the achievements, this is where the cracks under the paint really started to show.  There are countless bugs in here, and they range from mildly annoying to borderline infuriating.  The Electrical Engineering upgrade which is supposed to stop machines from breaking down either does not work at all or the difference is so minor that I am mad that I spent any money on it (money which I needed to get all the achievements) - please devs, fix this.  Beyond that, I encountered glitches with just about every single cabinet.  Some of them render the games unplayable at times which only served to frustrate me further when trying to grind out the final achievements.Summary:The first 25 hours are great.  If you are a completionist like me, you will hate every single moment after the credits roll.  Some of the achievements are just so grindy and not even remotely fun to try and get.  Passing out 10 times in the arcade?  Okay well after I have done literally everything in the game, this boils down just standing around doing nothing until I pass out.  So I am just running the game and staring at my phone waiting for the achievement to pop.  Oh, and fully upgrading your ship in Space Racer?  The grind to get this done is atrocious.  This game is fun for 5 minutes max, and then becomes an absolute chore for the remaining 2 or so hours that is required to collect all the currency for the upgradesTo the devs: I see what you have all done here, it is mostly fine work, but very rough around the edges.  The price point is fair here, but the amount of bugs to me feels inexcusable.  I am pretty sure I like you as a developer but please patch all the bugs, and I may consider changing my review.EDIT: I am changing my review now because the devs seem devoted to fixing many of the bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Judging by the number of players on SteamDB, it doesn't look like Arcade Paradise is successful at all but I bought it on a whim in one of the recent sales for $15 and am having a very hard time putting it down. There are a couple of genres it falls into but mostly it can be probably categorized as a time-management sim as your day is bound by the workday and there are tasks to complete before going home.The story is that your dad lets you run his laundromat instead of having you work at his meat packing factory. You'll start out your journey doing laundry and picking up trash but almost immediately after doing a good job, you'll get a key to the "backroom." There you'll find a few arcade machines and an office with a Windows 95 themed computer (complete with the Maze screensaver running).As time progresses and work days continue, dad stops paying attention and you're starting to pull in cash primarily through the arcade. You and your sister work to expand the space available while ordering new cabinets from a reseller through the computer. You're able to rearrange the space and adjust game settings to get them more profitable (put really popular games near less popular ones to increase output, change difficulty and cost per play to maximize hourly income).That alone may make for a fun game if you're into business management though it's a bit lightweight, but what makes it special is that each and every cabinet is playable, and just about every one is based in a real, old school title.For example, Barkanoid is a Breakout/Arkanoid clone, Cyber Dance is Dance Dance Revolution, Bugai is Puzzle Bobble/Bust-a-Move, and Line Terror is Qix. Each game has unique goals to complete which increase the game's popularity (thus increasing money output), and because this is based on old arcades, many of them have online leaderboards that you can view through your palm pilot. They're not all winners, and some of them, like the Qix-clone, could be tweaked to improve them (it is just too slow in movement),I'm roughly 22 hours into it and will probably see the credits for the main story roll soon, but I understand you can keep playing afterwards. There are also some DLC cabinets, which I thought was a little silly when I started playing, but am honestly considering picking them up now as they aren't very expensive and one is based on a real Steam game partnership (Kung Fury). Overall, I highly recommend giving it a shot. On sale it was $15 (US) and I think that was probably the perfect price.

_childDocuments_.review: - The game ran at a buttery smooth 144 FPS and maximum settings (1080p) despite not having top of the line equipment, which is quite good to see in a time of so many games coming out unoptimized. Granted there were some small hiccups but they were rare so it's in the realm of 0.1% which isn't exactly the average. - Going into this not being a 90s kid, I couldn't exactly point to the accuracy of the things being shown such as words like ''tubular'' but from what other reviews are saying and my own personal experience with other people from that time period, this game definitely appeals to the nostalgia of some, though that can be a double edged sword, which I'll speak about later on in this review. - The pacing for getting the new arcades felt reasonable, ( getting a new machine every 1-3 in-game days depending on the price) though that's more so for the fact I made the early realization that the grading for the laundry doesn't start until you actually pick it up from the arrival desk, making the strategy to wait for 3 baskets of laundry to show up before putting them all to wash at the same time, giving you way more time to actually play the arcade games rather than just waiting for the laundry part to end to play at the end of the day. - The meat and potatoes of this game and I have to say they've done a good job of recreating classics from the past, though some may have gone over my head, which may explain why I don't really like a lot of the games, though that doesn't mean they're necesarrily bad, they're just not for me. - The audio is a bit of a mess when it comes to every corner of the game, from the laundromat service to the arcade, most notably the jukebox. First off, when you enter ''King Wash'', if you stand by the door when it's open, you won't actually hear anything as you have to pass a certain threshold for the backround noise to start, which, after a few hours of play becomes annoying, because even if there's no machine running, you still hear one running every so often in the sound loop that was used for that area. The same can be said for the arcade but it's less noticeable there.There's also a radio that can't be found in the laundromat, and the TVs don't function, so I wouldn't know where the sound is even coming from, which is a constant trend in these audio problems which is ''backround'' audio instead of ''spacial''. The only exception to that is the arcade cabinets which play their little jingle when you get close and dissapears off as you get away. Unfortunately I cannot say the same thing for the Jukebox, which is even worse than the backround noise of both. Once you play a song on the jukebox, it will play on the global audio of the game, so whether you are in the arcade, the laundry section or even outside, you'll hear it at full volume. - While I was praising the game for its smoothness and graphics, the texture quality leaves a lot to be desired, and for things like the board where people have their ads for missing dogs or little tidbits of information which are fun to uncover. Those at least should be given the light of day with some better textures, since I doubt the glasses upgrade would make me able to see them better. - There's never any bills. - While the games are up for personal preference in terms of quality up to a certain point, what's not exactly hard to miss once you've noticed is the awful arcade cabinets a lot of them have which can do away with the nostalgia glasses rather quickly, not to mention that they're even on the starting machines you get. Here's my findings as I've started to notice them: - Video Air Hockey (VAH) has 2 joysticks on each side alongside a whopping 8 different buttons. 1 for the boost alongisde one joystick would've sufficed, maybe 2 buttons if you wanted an additional function but 8?! - Strike Gold which even though is a one player game, it's setup like a 2 player game, even with singleplayer/multiplayer buttons like the overlay, which funnily enough is present on VAH but not the buttons.- Racer Chaser has a wheel and a joystick in a configuration which suggests a shifter, but I don't exactly know why a Pacman movement equivalent would need a shifter, not to mention playing Pacman with a wheel would be atrocious. It also doesn't concide with the fact you can shoot ''notes'' while on foot. So in the end, the cabinet should just have a joystick and 1 button, which is something that I'd say for a lot of the other machines, so I'll avoid repeating it ad nauseum.- Woodgal's Adventure alongside others is a game which tracks progress, and like Space Race where you upgrade your vehicle, considering it's a token based machine, how would it know which player plays it and keep tabs on everyone's progress? I know there are ways but they're never shown, and a game centered around arcades should at least try to be somewhat accurate. Speaking of accuracy...- Cyber Dance is actually quite good when it comes its arcade cabinet mimicking DDR, but I've put its place here because the game is flat-out just bad and it deserves its own section here. First of all the notes barely align with the music, and if they don't I have to painfully press them off-rythm to get a perfect, which defeats the point of a rythm game. The music, compared to the good soundtrack is surprising to be honest, as the game has a decent selection of interesting songs for the jukebox, yet the ones in Cyber Dance seem like the ones thrown in there that didn't make the cut. -  One issue I have with the forced placements is that they don't make sense. Why would the dart board be next to the dance pads, giving it no room. Why would one of the chairs and table set be by the token machine where people are most likely to head first? Maybe some of these problems would be alleviated if you upgrade your arcade all the way but, I don't see why presumably permanent placements would be in such odd locations. - I don't see why you are collecting money from the arcade cabinet hoppers when there's an exchange machine at the entrance. Wouldn't you collect the money from the exchange machine and just the tokens from the cabinet hoppers when they're full to refill the exchange machine? You'd probably need to do the same thing for the laundromat tokens. The game comes from a good place but unfortunately misses on a lot of things which may make or break the experience, though I'm not here to rain on anyone's parade, if you like the game, more power to you. If I could've added one thing, it would've been different sounds for collecting the coins from the arcade cabinet hoppers ( 3 most likely ), meaning the more you waited, the more tokens would drop out, which is quite satisfying.  - The game's all right but I wasn't a fan, if you like playing arcade games, though granted not from the 90s, give The Coin Game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of it as a All-You-Can-Eat buffet, not a full course meal.  Arcade Paradise is a business simulator where you take a old, worn down laundry mat with a few arcade cabinets, and slowly convert it to a fully fledged arcade. Early game progression can be a slog, where you will be spending most of your time doing laundry, taking out trash, removing stuck gum wads, and collecting cash. These mundane tasks are sugar coated as mini-games but this early point in the game will filter a lot of people, but for those who can push through it will find a addicting game-play loop for the rest of the time. Maintain the business, complete goals & To-Do tasks, play the arcade, boost popularity, collect more and more cash, buy upgrades & arcade cabinets, repeat. Ultimately, you are encouraged to play the arcade. Its how the game progresses. Having goals for each cabinet was a smart way to keep a sense of progression and the feeling of beating a cabinet. The arcade games are copycat titles of instantly recognizable games we know and love, and there are a lot of them here. You will have a lot of choices, play the ones you like, avoid the ones you don't. Most of these games are simple, providing ankle deep complexity, but turn out to be the most addicting to play. My favorites were: Zombat 2, Woodgal Jr., Hustler, Attack Vector, Gravichase, Striking Gold, UFO Assault, and Knee & Knuckle.For those who love arcade games, this one is for you. I certainly had my fun here. I look forward to Nosebleed Interactive's future titles! Pick this one up during a sale.Great on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions of Arcade Paradise, AKA Laundry: The Game, Game.I absolutely adore the overall presentation, it makes all the chores "gamey" to where even unclogging the toilet or unsticking gum from random places is incredibly satisfying. Achieving S Rank on each chore activates my deepest lizard brain functions.So far performance is just fine, running it on Steam Deck at 56-60fps with default settings. Though it feels like the game is slightly zoomed in to where some text is cut off and resolution options are locked at 720p. So just a heads up for the Deck users out there. But overall its super playable, just had to figure out some of the stuff the game is trying to tell me on my own, it's worth it though.Haven't dug into actually playing the machines yet, because dad is totally on me for making sure the place is clean and laundry is done on time. But I do recommend working in a Laundromat, good money, and i do recommend Arcade Paradise.

_childDocuments_.review: Im giving a negative review just for how the main character sets up some arcade cabinets/pool table/Foosball/couches. Really? The character deserves to fail for how some of those are just haphazardly placed. Ok cool, half the couch back is 3 feet away from the wall while the other half is against it just fine. rectangular room with rectangular pool table? lets place it at an angle. Dont get me started on the Foosball table. But really, 90s charm mixed with "parents are always wrong and dont understand" (I Cringed when the mc complained how her dad didnt take her business degree seriously even though she didnt do more than 2 years of college and dropped out, and the dad said the meany mean mean thing of "half a degree isnt a degree".) mixed with bare bare bare bones sim elements that you can literally ignore mixed with arcade game knockoffs and a banging soundtrack. Its not a bad idea of a game, but you spend like majority of the game with the laundromat (that according to the developer you are supposed to ignore, even though it is a major element of your arcade for like 80% of the game and you get tasks to do stuff with it.) that is a chore and does nothing except get you money only slightly faster. Honestly I wish the sim element would have been deeper so I could of had a good mix of laundromat and arcade, but nope the MC's main goal is to get rid of anything that reminds her of her dad. If the laundromat was supposed to be ignored (literally you could do like zero laundry and beat the game) then why have it? But at the same time the game tracks your laundry income and all that (even when its gone) so is it supposed to be ignored or was it just a bad element that didnt stick that we are now being told we are not supposed to do?The arcade games are... fine. If you enjoy older arcade games and have nostalgia for 80s-90s arcade then you will probably like it. I dont have that so it didnt add any style points for me. Would have loved a good street fighter like fighting game or something but there really isnt anything like that. Love that they have ddr-like games, but they are so barebones that I was kinda disappointed. Banging soundtrack. Absolutely would just turn on the game to play songs on the Jukebox and do something on my phone. I literally spent all of the money meant for upgrades on all the songs first. If anyone tells you this is an arcade sim, dont believe them. Or dont trust their opinions on sims. Literally you can change none of the settings of the games (cost, difficulty, location and these are the only fidgets you can bobble) and still make absolute bank. It FEELS like a sim, but it isnt. straight up you can just turn the game on and stand there doing nothing and get farther in the story and make a ton of money. and the dialogue... if you still hate your parents and/or think they dont understand then you will like it. Kinda cringy at times. The Dad is made out to be a bad guy who doesnt understand and this is the MC's last chance or she will be FORCED to work at the MEAT PACKING plant (I didnt understand this point? like she could just NOT work there. Get of job somewhere else). Main character acts like she knows everything and dad knows nothing (honestly opening an arcade is a RISKY venture, so i understand the dads attitude of just do the laundromat stuff. Its safe and laundromats will always be needed.). Main character gets free job where she has to do basically nothing, illegally does a bunch of stuff to expand the business. (it blames it on the sister, but the MC should know about ordinances and such to run the business she wants to run... I mean didnt she go to business school...), gets bailed out from a friends investment and learns nothing ( and doesnt fix any of the stupid placement of objects). She ♥♥♥♥♥ up royally and still finds a way to blame it on the dad even after he covered all the legal fees and made sure she didnt get in more trouble.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope you like doing laundry.It's not exactly the 1983 movie "Joysticks" but it's as close as we're going to get. You'll be spending most of your time jockeying washing machines and dryers. Meanwhile you're trying to steal away some time to play the games in your ever growing arcade that you're trying to build with the money. There's no pressure here to succeed. You can do it all at your own pace. As for the games, well most are inferior rip-offs of other arcade games but with a real lack of depth. Some have a bit of a twist on the formula they are ripping off, and some are just ugly to play and control. None of the games are really a stand-out unfortunately. It could have been interesting to have actual licensed arcade ROMs in the game instead, but then that would have pushed the price of this right up. Similarly pinball machines are conspicuous by their absence. And look, no skee-ball? No ticket games? No prize booth?It would have been nice to have people around the machine cheering you on once you get beyond the high score on any game - but this too is missing. So are games competitions in the arcade.As far as the management sim aspect of this game, it needed to have more realistic expenses (rent, electricity, repair costs, extra people on payroll, daily expenses, vandalism, coinbox theft, etc) as all the money you make just gets ploughed straight back into the business without any profit taking. It's still fun for most of us over 40 who grew up in arcades. Now we get to re-live those golden days that will never ever be coming back - thanks to the evolution of mobile gaming, internet, and all the predatory game design practices that have ruined good game design. That's not to say that arcades weren't predatory either, but you at least required skill to get past the magic two minute limit that most arcade machines aimed to send you to "Game Over" by. Why some of these games seem to have saved achievements is a bit odd, but it at least fits with the concept that you'll be unable to play them without distraction, and have to return at a later time to complete them.There's definitely room for improvement with the overall experience, but it still kept me going for 30 hours, plus there's still plenty of achievement trophies to get, so your mileage may vary.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a job simulator with mini-games essentially. Some guy wrote a book report about why he doesnt like the game and I feel like he simply approached it wrong. The game wants you to balance playing games and having a job because you essentially have 2 revenue streams, doing laundry and playing games. There is a bit of strategic approach you can take to this due to how the game is structured. Your arcade cabinets will overtake how much money your laundry makes very quickly into the game, basically by the time you buy your 3rd cabinet, which is very early on. So if you just want to play the arcade games, you literally can just ignore the laundry and not really "fall behind", this game can be played casually as well, there is no "Oh I need to pay the rent by day 5" mechanic, you just hit milestones and the game slowly opens up more and more.There are some negatives to the game, it has a small amount of bugs. Nothing gamebreaking or unplayable and it certainly isnt on the level of a bethesda game, but it isnt as polished as it should be. Also you cannot modify the look of your arcade at all, so if you are wanting to play this with the expectation of being able to change the colors of the walls or the floor, its not possible, the most you can do is move cabinets around and some cabinets are hard locked into certain spots which is actually quite annoying.Still though I do recommend the game, figuring out how to min-max your income is fun and.. I mean this game essentially has ~30 minigames in it. its certainly worth $20.

_childDocuments_.review: After Getting to the point where I can say that I have "beaten" the game I can say that if you are into simulator games where you manage a business this is the game for you I do have some Pros and Cons from my time playing that definitely could influence someones choice to purchase the game.  • The balance between trying to balance the laundry and the arcade portion can feel satisfying and give the game that sort of challenge that always gives you something to do.• The arcade games themselves are fun and makes you want to play them more than the laundry part. they are all well designed and have good play feel and never feel like they are just cobbled together to fill slots• The optimization is good I'm not playing it on the best computer and it maintains a good FPS the entire time • Good use of particles and effects that don't feel too over the top and only serve to add that little bit of feedback that keeps things more engaging•The Laundry portion of the game gets really old really quickly on the other hand that is the point  . The game could benefit from an upgrade that makes the laundry interactions faster could be a huge benefit.• Picking up litter and gum can be a serious hassle after you expand the arcade portion as some of the trash blends into the black carpet making them impossible to see. This could be mitigated by adding an upgrade that highlights trash or just make the trash more visible• Some of the arcade games can be frustrating when it comes to trying to accomplish the goals for each cabinet some goals just seem to feel like they were added to pad out time and make you play them more just to get them done. I get that the goals are important as them increase the popularity of the cabinet but some goals just seem either too hard or arbitrary.•There are some issues with using the mouse in the computer menus (which you use daily in game) The mouse cursor is some pointless cursor that is shaped like a hand making the metal horns gesture which makes telling what part of the cursor is the part to click with hard. This could easily be mitigated by adding an options menu selection for a basic cursor or even add custom mouse cursor optionsI can wholeheartedly recommend this game in its current state for its current price if you are into simulators that give you an amazing 90's feel that has fun arcade games that keep you engaged.
