_childDocuments_.review: From Laundry to Legendary – A Weeb’s Guide to Dishonoring Your Famiry! (Disclaimer: This Game Has No Actual Weebness)Have you ever dreamed of opening your own arcade, surrounded by the nostalgic glow of CRT screens and the sweet sounds of pixelated victory? Well, my fellow weebs, Arcade Paradise is here to make that dream a reality! (Just a quick heads up – the game itself isn’t actually weeby, but hey, we can still pretend, right? 😉)So, here’s the setup: you start off with a rundown laundromat, courtesy of your dad who thinks you’re going to be folding clothes all day. Little does he know, you’ve got bigger plans – like turning this place into the ultimate arcade paradise! The catch? You start with absolutely nothing. Zero arcade machines, nada. It’s just you, some washing machines, and your cunning ability to slowly transform this laundromat into a gaming haven without your dad catching on. 😎💸At first, you’re just stuck doing laundry, which sounds boring, but it’s all part of the master plan. You’ll be pocketing the extra quarters and using that cash to sneak in your first arcade cabinet. From there, it’s all about juggling the mundane chores while secretly building your arcade empire behind your dad’s back. The thrill of upgrading your space, adding more machines, and watching your arcade grow is seriously addictive. It’s like you’re living out an anime where the stakes aren’t about saving the world, but about building the best hangout spot in town without getting busted. 😂And let me tell you, the satisfaction of turning that boring laundromat into a neon-lit, coin-filled arcade paradise is chef’s kiss perfection. The mini-games on the machines are retro bliss, giving you that nostalgic hit while keeping things fresh and fun. Plus, the whole sneaky aspect of doing it all without your dad knowing adds this extra layer of excitement. It’s like being a secret agent, but instead of saving the world, you’re just trying to build the coolest arcade ever.Overall, Arcade Paradise is a total win. It’s got that addictive gameplay loop, a charmingly rebellious storyline, and while it’s not weeby, it’s got plenty of retro charm to keep you hooked. If you’ve ever wanted to go from zero to arcade hero, all while keeping your dad in the dark, this game is for you. Dishonor your famiry, embrace the neon, and build your very own Arcade Paradise! 10/10, would totally recommend to any fellow weebs out there. (But remember, the weebness is all in your head this time! 😜) Now, back to doing laundry... and plotting my next arcade expansion... 🎮✨

_childDocuments_.review: My best memories of video-game arcades are - probably - not the same as your memories of the arcades. Mine date back to before they became the haven of the younger set, back when the arcades were often attached to drinking establishments and the games themselves were aimed more at young urban professionals than at oily teens. By the time the arcades had transformed into the darkened lairs of the adolescent, I had already abandoned the hobby for computers. So I've never really felt that much nostalgia for the arcade as it is popularly remembered.Still, I was willing to give "Arcade Paradise" a chance, because it's overall framing story looked interesting, and it had a certain visual flair to it that appealed to me. And in these regards, I wasn't disappointed. The game beautifully captures the feel of trying to transform a failing launderette in the 80s into a hoppin' arcade palace, machine by machine.  Between it's surprisingly realistic visuals where you do your 'real world' chores, and the retro-visuals of the arcade remakes, the game looks good. I was really digging the story too, of a young manager who - with a love of the arcade and a desire to improve the business despite an obstinate boss - struggles to prove his acumen. It's just a shame that so much of the game revolves around, you know, actually playing the arcade games.Because while the early parts of the game revolve around slowly earning money - both through the launderette and arcade machines - to buy new arcades, place adverts, and generally grow the business (interspersed with arcade-like takes on daily chores, such as plunging the WC or tossing the trash into the skip), later parts of the game demand that you play and master many of those arcade games you've been buying. And, quite frankly, most of those games just aren't worth playing. They're cheap reproductions of better-known arcades (albeit often with some clever skins; Pac-Man gets transformed into a Grand Theft Auto clone, for instance) that lack the excitement of the originals they are emulating. Add into this an annoying time-limit and I'm left with little incentive or desire to keep playing the arcades... except that if I don't, you can't progress.All of which meant that, five or so hours into the game, I lost all interest in continuing. I admit it; I never finished this one. I wanted to, and perhaps had the game offered other ways to keep going - a secondary method to continue without wasting time on the arcade games themselves - I would have persevered. Maybe had I a more intense relation to classic arcades, I might have made the effort. But it didn't, and I didn't, and so - not without some sadness - I walked away from this game. It's a clever idea, well implemented, but it demanded a dedication to 8-bit arcades that I just didn't have.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is a decent game with an identity crisis, but the devs will insist that's kind of the point. They took obligation, tedium, and progression that comes with a simulator and combined it with the freedom, nostalgia, and goofiness that comes with an emulator.The game starts with a focus on the former and very little on the latter; you're effectively running a ghetto laundromat owned by your overly disappointed father and there just happens to be a few arcade cabinets in the back. These cabinets were purchased by your sister in the past as an attempt to boost revenue and provide customers waiting for laundry with some entertainment. Makes sense. You spend most of your time doing laundry which is about as exciting as it sounds, picking up trash, and waiting for clothes to dry. After checking the hoppers -- the coin holders in the bottom of the arcade cabinets -- you discover they were racking up significantly more cash than the measly laundry grind did, and that's where the story really begins.As you slowly pivot away from laundry and expand the arcade, your responsibilities start to grow. Every morning you'll come in, pick up trash, take trash to the dumpster, rip some gum off a surface or two, empty arcade hoppers, deposit cash in the safe via a small mini game, check/pursue daily tasks, and if you're lucky, unclog a toilet. Arcade cabinets will also regularly break and require a bug-squashing (literally) mini-game to fix. On your PC, you'll check email, chat messages, order new arcade cabinets, and purchase quality of life upgrades.The aforementioned daily tasks require anything from playing a specific game for 10 real world minutes, reaching a certain score, and/or killing x amount of enemies. Three tasks are generated every day at random and each offers a small reward in the form of an upgrade currency. There's also a clock ticking at all times, counting down from the moment you open until the bus ride home. While you can buy an upgrade that slows down time, this just adds to a sense of urgency and general time management.If that sounds like a lot, that's because it is. You're constantly moving from one task to the next, until you decide to put your foot down and just play a damn game which is when you'll be bombarded with alerts and intrusive animations that literally block your view of the game you're playing. Games don't really save your progress either, so a quick detour to unclog a toilet means coming back to an Insert Coin screen.This is where the game's identity crisis comes in but don't take my word for it. Read the description. It's all about the simulator. They literally don't even mention PLAYING the 35 games available. Then in the exact opposite direction the recent blog post is a showcase of the arcade games you CAN play, which is all about the emulator. These games even have promotional materials, branding, and their own unique personalities complete with a recurring character/family (e.g., Mario, Sonic)  in several games.There's a dichotomy here and while the devs and/or loyal fans may argue this is by design, I'm going to argue that this design isn't chocolate and peanut butter, it's oil and water. Imagine sitting down at your PC, flipping on some neon lighting, blasting some synthwave while sipping a Capri Sun, and launching an 80s game emulator. Then, just as you're getting into the flow your mom crashes through the door and insists you take the trash out. And you're like first of all mom I'm 40 how'd you get in here but more importantly, ok, fine; thanks for killing the vibe. You take the trash out, return to your desk, and you're finally on that last level you've died on countless times when suddenly the doorbell rings and it's someone trying to sell you solar panels for your house. You politely turn them away by slamming the door in their face and rush back to your desk, needing a quick bathroom break. You flush and the toilet overflows. Great. After a quick clean up you rush back to your desk and strap in then halfway through another run your computer bursts into flames.Is this fun? Did someone think this was fun?So, here's my hot take; I think someone on the dev team really wanted a first person arcade emulator, and someone else really wanted a sim with heavy micromanagement, and it shows. Neither system is polished or particularly fun because the other is always vying for attention.That being said, there's a lot they did incredibly well; sound design is borderline flawless, graphics and art direction are on point, and even the writing/story is done pretty well. Optimization is solid. Bugs are present but mostly hidden behind specific conditions. And you can't argue with that price point, either.Regardless, lets put all that aside for now and just focus on the arcade games. Are they good? That depends. First of all, they took a roguelike/lite approach here for sure. I'm not a fan of the genre mostly because I don't think punishing mechanics are a good substitute for content or substance, but I also appreciate a good challenge so I see both sides of the coin. Speaking of which, that's the problem; the lack of coins. While some may argue, and they 100% will, that arcade games were challenging so a rogue/souls approach is accurate, you're missing the bigger picture. Arcades prioritized profit over fun. You could circumvent every difficulty spike with another quarter. Boss has too much health? Pop in a quarter. Friend kicked your ass in Mortal Kombat? Pop in a quarter. Wizard needs food, badly? Quarter. Does any of this sound familiar? Almost like a pay to win business model based heavily on microtransactions? Almost like, I don't know, they padded content in the TMNT beat 'em up game by tuning the difficulty to Give Us Your Money? The point is, this is not a fun model, it's a profitable one. I'd argue padding content with difficult spikes was a solid approach as long as you could circumvent those spikes by dropping cash to continue. If you remove the ability to circumvent difficulty with quarters, you just designed 35 mini games designed explicitly to piss people off, especially those lacking twitchy reflexes and high scores in Super Meat Boy. Like I said, it depends, but while the games can be fun, most of them just annoyed me even if I did manage to "beat" most of them. I appreciate that it's unreasonable to expect every arcade game to be Breath of the Wild, but depth has been replaced by pain, and pain isn't fun without a workaround. And without saved progress or checkpoints, walking away from a cabinet mid-game is a forfeit.And for me, personally, the difficulty in the games just kind of adds insult to injury. The game doesn't know what it wants to be and even if the devs do, I disagree with the approach. That's not to say that with some proper tuning this game couldn't almost immediately warrant a hard recommend from someone like me, as the bones are certainly there, but something's gotta give. Either lean into the sim side by adding decoration options, layouts, events, and expansions, or allow the player to slowly creep away from the sim side of things with more significant upgrades and turn the arcade into an self-sustained playground with more cabinets, depth, and rivalries. Maybe both. Either way, I respect the team's ambition combining genres, but they don't compliment each other, they compete. There is some obvious overlap systematically speaking where it's obvious the goal was synergy, but it misses the mark and feels a lot more like compromise and/or sacrifice.EDIT: Beat the game. Want to support the devs and recent patch, although I stand by the points mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: Another nice game for neon arcade chilling out. Beautiful interior, a lot of games. The cabinets aren't the real MAME games and it's unlikely that it'll be possible to mod it into something like the NRA. There's a good and bad side to it:Good: Some of these games are quite fun, and some are inspired by popular arcade games you'll easily recognize if you're into these things. You can play real arcades in CoinOps or RetroArch or even NewRetroArcade, here you can check out some indie arcade games, which fit well into the entire game's atmosphere.Bad: Obviously, these mini-games can't really be at the level of 80' arcades, which were basically an analogue to today's AAA titles, and in most cases the investments in such simple by today's standards games were more than in this whole game. So yeah, if you compare these to your usual MAME game, the graphics are cheaper, and the game is shorter in content. But again, that's understandable and I'm not in any way implying that these games are bad, they're absolutely great for game-inside-the game, man i've seen much worse.Another significant design difference in real arcade games and these is their difficulty. Sure, they've quite challenging, but for MAME arcade punk they're too easy. You see, the arcades of 80' are very different to today's games "arcade" tag, not only by the quality, but in difficulty. You couldn't just sit at the new arcade cabinet and beat it even if you're good. Because such cabinet won't be profitable. They were designed in the way that you should spend a lot of lives (=coins) before you "git gut" and beat it. In case of the in-game arcades, you can "git gut" very quickly, because they've quite simple. With the couple of machines I literally had to lose intentionally because I could play forever otherwise (the future race, and vostok), could take a better place on leaderboard, but what's the point of such competition.What was kinda unexpected from this kind of game is that you've forces to work at laundry for at the beginning of it, and slowly building it into an arcade. It's fun and kinda meditative, but only if you know what to expect. After playing other games like NewRetroArcade or Coin Game, I've expected everything to be available from the start or shortly after it. Maybe devs should include a "sandbox" mode in the future, so people could taste the arcade if they want, and then go to story mode.The performance of the game is very good. It surprised me that the game worked well on my old laptop with everything maxed out. (840M GPU). After completing the game and buying everything, the things I would like to have in this arcade to be more relaxing:1. Disable litter and toilet problems. At this level of profits, hiring a janitor is logical. 2. Slow down the time even more. To the actual time, maybe. Because at this point, you don't really need money and, therefore, time compression.3. More machines. At the moment, there is some free space (slots) left in the arcade. But I've heard rumors that some of the machines are still in development, so they probably reserved this space for these.Whle I have some mixed comments as an actual arcade fan, the game's great, it is very well-made, so get it if you into this kind of things. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: So this caught me by surprise because it wasn't what I expected going in. Though that's probably on me not watching trailers or reading much about the game before diving in. It's got a bit more of a story to it (pretty basic, serviceable I suppose) where you inherit a laundromat and you slowly convert it to a gaming arcade. You get to play each of the machines you buy for the arcade, many of which seem to be cheap imitations of other older arcade games. So a lot of the 'game' revolves around getting this business going, which is a fun enough distraction, but gets quite samey very quickly, and quite early on found it difficult to enjoy the arcade games because I was constantly being pulled away to do menial tasks such as empty the dryers. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a playground.The overlying game is all about managing a video arcade - specifically, turning a laundromat into one. It's certainly not a *deep* simulation, but it's not supposed to be. Every aspect of this game is designed to be fun. If you're into micromanaging and statistics and the like, you can do that as you run your arcade. But, it's also not necessary to progress through Arcade Paradise's endgame. Every game you add to your arcade is playable - in fact, the more you play them, the more money they earn for your business. The majority of the games are fantastic - and even the ones that aren't great are still pretty good.This is just a great, fun game. You can't go wrong with it.

_childDocuments_.review: My insane 45 hours on Steam (100% achievements), combined with 29 hours on XBox (only 30% achievements), should speak for itself as to the danger of this game. It's the perfect balancing act of playing games and micromanaging your own personal business. The story feels a bit forced, though has some genuine moments and serves its purpose, but that's hopefully not what you came here for. So... how are the games?Arcade Paradise features a TON of "classic" arcade titles, really a bunch of knock-offs, or parodies, of more popular titles. Part of this is likely to dumb-down the more complex titles to be more understandable, especially considering you'd need to master most of the games, each with VASTLY different play-styles, save for a couple that are essentially identical. (WoodGuy & WoodGal) Among these titles, I found quite a lot of favorites; Zombat 2 is a hecktic twin-stick shooter with a variety of weapons, Stack Overflow was a stressful but rewarding puzzle game, Strike Gold was a competent Mr. Driller clone, Line Terror is Qix but with more anxiety, Bugai is your Bust-A-Move clone, and Blockchain is a FANTASTIC original puzzle game that I'd totally play outside of this title. Barkanoid gets an honorable mention as it's just Arkanoid, but with a dog; perfection.The visual presentation isn't much to look at, definitely not turning any heads at this title, but there was a clear art design and the arcade feels cohesively chaotic, as though the machines don't match each other, but feel like they belong in an arcade. Don't know if that makes sense or not. The retro-neon arcade room is simple but perfectly facilitates the machines, and I'd definitely go to an arcade like that in real life, definitely been to worse ones.The music is kinda a mixed bag. All of the Jukebox tracks are by just the same few people and it feels like they REALLY stretched to make the OST. Whilst there is some great music, there's also some duds, but they range greatly in genres and styles, allowing you to just mix it up a little as you go on. Definitely considering that Soundtrack Double-Vinyl. The games themselves mostly use stock music, and the tracks sometimes don't repeat properly, making the generic stock music even more grueling after repeat listens. Little tip, I turned my music off after about 30-40 hours so I could play my own instead.Overall a really fun time, greatly addicting as you expand your arcade, and well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! You can really feel all the love for arcades that went into it. The arcade games are fun and varied. The story isn't particularly in depth but it was enough to have me invested and wanting to see how things would turn out for our main character. Sometimes the laundry part of the early game can feel a bit repetitive but as you upgrade your arcade it is no longer is an issue. So if you enjoy the arcade games but are disliking the laundry management parts, I'd encourage you to push through!

_childDocuments_.review: ...a not to be classified simulation! Review & CritiqueThis game is not evene close a serious business management simulation, but neither is it a pure arcade game collection! It is something between and this is exactly a problem here! I can understand people who say that they can't recommend this game, because there are really some reasons for it!You will have to invest several hours in the game before you can play and enjoy some different arcade machines! The arcade games are a kind of reward for the very monotonous work in the laundry shop, but there isn't much time to play them in the first “xx” hours! The laundry is getting smaller and the arcade shop is growing over time, but you always have to do some things again and again and again... what is not really funny!- Really authentic 80s-90s vibe- Good graphics and sounds for this kind of game - Many arcade games that I played in my youth... like “Line Terror“ ;-)- Possibility to play with friends- The Jukebox is a really nice thing to have here, when you like „covered“ music from the 90´s (focus on electronics, beat, dance and rock, luckily less pop^^)! Bad is that you can chose / play only one song at time... - The Story is ok but nothing special- The Minigames, collecting trash, cleaning the toilet, scraping off chewing gum, debugging arcades, collecting money, and doing laundry are fun... a few times, but get annoying later!- Challenging in many many ways^...^- I had no lags bugs or crahes... very rare these days!- Overall a bit to much grind / repetitive actions- Game focus could be much better and more clear- Some arcade games are not really „polished“...- The second in game currency does have its purpose... but I didn't really liked that idea^^ ;) (insider)You really need a gampad for some arcade games....are all working but they are very often not easy to get and they are more acrade game focused than business simulation focused! I accepted the challenge and made them all but i wouldn't do it again to be honest, because it was sometimes really an hard grind and not allways fun!The balance between the growing arcade shop simulation and the arcade games themselves are ok in the first gaming hours! Later it would be nice if you could really concentrate a lot more on the different arcade games, but no... there are still other things you have to do!My in game bank account is bursting with money, but nooo i cant have an employee...? ...for collecting the junk?? ...removing chewing gums?? ...for cleaning the toilet?? ...for debugging my arcade machines?I can only have one very expensive employee to collect my money in the endgame?! These “Minigames” are fun a few times... then they start to get really on your nerves... more and more... until you hate them! Do you want your game to be more fun, than change this points asap! I would never buy a dlc because i know that i have to play these annoying minigames another x or xxx times...!It is clear to me that someone put a lot of love into this game and I really appreciate that! It is a good game when you like the 90´s and arcade gaming, but you need much time and strong nerves to reach an “arcade shop enjoyable state”.Greetings & glhf anytime!

_childDocuments_.review: My knowledge of the '90s is somewhat limited, but playing this game unexpectedly fulfills a nostalgic longing I didn't know I had.Sure, this game has its rough spots, but if you're seeking AAA perfection (whatever that means in today's gaming landscape), you might want to consider investing in a retro emulation experience instead, as you won't find that level of polish here.But.. despite any minor flaws- and reading a collection of positive reviews- I'm convinced this isn't a tycoon game you should overlook, especially if you revel in scratching that nostalgic itch. _childDocuments_.review: This game is basically overdosing on nostalgia. Its honestly brilliant for a pick up and play type game.The music, setting, theme.. it takes you back to literally being a kid playing stupid pointless arcade games just to beat high scores and compete with yourself to burn hours of your free time.The laundromat tasks start off a little heavy, but you can neglect them pretty quickly and focus on earning alot more from your arcade - playing more games, completing more goals on individual machines nets you a higher earning per day. Ignoring laundry tasks has no penalty other than earning less per day (but its not significant after you get a few arcade machines on the go!)The story parts aren't overly complex, but do give a nice addition to the theme, and play the whole "moody teenager story" very well. This is alongside the business slowly developing into a massive, bad-ass, retro arcade - taking about 12 or so hours to complete.The "arcade management" though, is easy to neglect. It feels like the games weak point - e.g. I don't think anyone will care about what cabinet goes where, or how much it costs to play.. its oddly detailed here, in a game that feels has its strong-suit in being a more casual game than overly complex.. Management-type game addicts, (or control freaks) will not find their itches scratched well here.For me though, playing through this game has been awesome. Its such as casual game. In a setting where yes, the arcade games are basic.. but they are plentiful, varied, and are highly addictive if you're a high-score/goal/achievement chaser.This is without a doubt a game I will keep coming back to for a little poke about every now and then. Its a game heavily  investing in nostalgia, that in a few years, I will get nostalgic about... 100% Recommend!Side note: you can pick this game up online for an absolute steal...

_childDocuments_.review: When i pick myself up a copy of this it was like i step into my dream job owning a Arcade front. Well in Arcade Paradise that pretty much what you do. You start out drop out as a college student who then go to work for big rich daddy in one of his old crappy laundromat business which later on you will  manage profits, pick up gum and rubbish, do the laundry and keep the arcades in good condition and then turn it into Arcade Paradise yes it does feel bit of chore until you get rid of all the laundry  machines and turn it into arcade paradise. but it is suppose to be simulator game however it doesn't go too serious on the simulator element. that not bad thing it pretty much works with this type game. not only do you purchase arcade machines you get to play them as well and a lot of them all have that arcade feel back in the 80s and 90s. I felt like i was a kid again playing this arcade games as lot of them are reference to some of the great arcade games we ever had. some of the arcade games actually have rouge like element too. now the point of this is turn small laundromat in a arcade business to do that you have to reach your goals so you can expand the business and get more arcade machines. money managment to this game is the key but like i said it doesn't take the simulator element too serious. You also can spend your money on tracks, power ups and tool to help you further increase your reach to complete the goal for expansion. the story of the game is pretty good. you will get alot of voice mail messages from your dad and yes his voice is the same voice actor that play as Geralt from the Witcher. there pop reference that reflect in the 80s and 90s and it just feels like i gone back in time. I highly recommend to get this game and get the dlcs 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I try to do reviews in a way that would bring forth new information. So if you read the other reviews and you're still on the fence about buying this, this review is for you. I know you see the thumbs up, just know that I'm being unbiased, and that's just my opinion of the game for me.Pros- A drastically large amount of content for playing a bunch of minigames (Apparently there's 35 of them not including DLC you can buy if you want more). - Missions for each cabinet that range from easy to difficult and each cabinet has their own difficulty settings.- The cabinets are inspired by other games and the feel they give out is reminiscent of they games they're mimicking.- Achievements that actually take time to get so it gives a bigger sense of accomplishment.- Content that keeps progressing throughout the game. I'm over 10 hours in and still continuously unlocking and finding new stuff.- Other reviews kept complaining about having to do laundry, but you can just ignore it once you progress far enough to  (I unlocked it about two hours in, but I was grinding for money which ended up being a waste of time since laundry is the worst income in the game)- controls are GREAT! Even with controller support.- Tons of ways to play this game from floor design to micromanaging the cabinets, and unlockables/upgrades that change how the game works. Cons- The game is buggy sometimes, and it gets frustrating. Weird things happen that make you not be able to progress in cabinets causing you to start over. This isn't that bad because they're all minigames, but it's still annoying when you're on a good run and things stop working like they should.Game crashes and either erases your day or forwards you a day from when it crashed after you reopen it. You have goals for each cabinet and sometimes they don't give you the completion when you achieve the goal ESPECIALLY in your daily to do list.- The DLC (Which is weirdly sold per cabinet and expensive for buying one minigame) doesn't let you progress in the main story. I get they were trying to make DLC be it's own thing for people that finished the game wanting extra content, but the game wouldn't have a balance issue with them existing even though you can buy them very early in the game.- Highlighting an item can be stupid hard. Trying to pick up a sock off the floor? Naw, you're getting the laundry basket that's behind you OR you can't highlight it no matter how hard you try. You have to adjust your screen and not look anywhere near the object to get it sometimes. You can add a crosshair, but it just confirms the item's hitbox is off. It's not as bad as it sounds most times, but it is pretty much every object in the game.- I found the storyline cringy. I skip storylines most of the time so it doesn't bother me much.I got this game on sale, so I already feel like I got my money's worth, and I'm going to continue playing it. This game does get repetitive, but the feeling of achievement and progression outweighs the the repetition getting boring for me. I hope this info helps your decision making. If you're still not sure, watch CaRtOoNz play it. He does a series of long videos on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game!  The biggest criticism seems to be that it overstayed its welcome, which all games eventually do.  For me this occurred after 40 hours on the steam deck, after the story was completed.  I loved the tension of “I’m in the zone on this arcade game but I’ve got to go put some laundry in the drier.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more unique game collections I've seen out there, with a rags-to-riches framing device of running your own arcade by building it from a laundromat. I had a great time with managing the place, getting new games in, and really appreciated the attention-to-detail and humor of these arcade titles. The soundtrack is full of bangers, too. Arcade Paradise is an underappreciated gem! 9/10 it has some odd pacing towards the middle, but I thoroughly enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Good concept but not very well executed. The games aren't very fun and you're constantly interrupted from playing them due to having to do wash events where being even a few seconds late drastically cut rewards. Even without the pop up notices for washing and drying you don't receive notice for when a new basket of laundry has arrived to start so you have to constantly recheck. The most fun game is a jump one on your pda and unfortunately it's the only one that freezes time so you can't even use it while waiting for something else. Overall just not very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, albeit a bit too grindy for my taste. The main loop is: gain money doing chores, play some arcade games to increase a passive money multiplier, invest money in new arcade games, repeat.It doesn't feel perfectly cohesive - the chores often interrupts gameplay and the end-goal is ignoring the chores to build up an arcade store. After around 4 hours of gameplay the chore part is still prominent and it feels like it's not going anyway anytime soon.I feel like it could be enjoyed quite a bite if it was taken as a cozy game, I was expecting a bit more "management" out of it but I guess it comes at a later stage.Up to the point I've been playing, some arcade games were cool but most of them didn't feel exactly right, even janky at times.I would not recommend it for its full price but it can be easily purchased at a discount, either on Steam or as part of bundles.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: “I was there, Gandalf.”  This game perfectly nails a surprising range of eighties cultural tropes.  I am particularly impressed with the genre-perfect novelty tunes.  Contains skill-based games where one must practice to succeed.  And simulated clothes laundering.Humor rating: Three out of five whoopee cushions.  Descriptions and dialogues are frequently amusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Ignored laundry to play video games.  Thank God I don’t do that in real life :^)Management aspect is actually quite shallow, it’s a very simple business management sim.  The laundromat is quite boring since there’s not much to do with that side except pick up trash and move laundry between the washer and dryer (which feels very tedious) but fortunately you can ignore the laundromat part when the arcade starts pulling in more money.  Once you get enough cabinets, figure out the best placement, play them and complete some goals within them to boost their popularity, you’ll get to knock down some walls in your father’s laundromat to expand upon your snazzy arcade carpet empire and spend your days playing NotOutRun… and maybe plunge the toilet now and then.As for the games, there are many cabinets to collect and most will feel very familiar.  They’re hit or miss, they’re arcade games so they’re expectedly not very deep, but they serve their purpose.It’s not great, I found myself getting bored sometimes but it’s a nice “play while doing something else” game.Oh, there's a shoegaze achievement complete with a MBV reference.  Good stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: An addictive series of mini games tied seamlessly together. For a simulation game, I was blow away by the great voice actor and storytelling, and the absolute banger of a soundtrack.Most of the mini games are based on the classics with a twist. If you like a game with a bunch of tiny objectives, then you will love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say this game rocks, it will keep you hooked if you give it the chance it truly deserves. I see a lot of reviews complain about the arcade games not being real games, they are clones, parodies, etc, they are great and most play great. They managed to create their own little brands and characters that you wish were real, well they are that too. The game does not do everything perfect but that is okay. The game really plugs you in and takes you out of the real world, it is a feel good game, you get lost in it, time will fly by while you live the Arcade dream. What I really hope for is a sequel. I can think of so many things I would love to have for a follow up game, more customization of the buildings aesthetics, the ability to hire and manage different employees with varying quality and skills. Managing the bills, such as electricity, water, rent, etc, to give it an even more real experience. There are so many things they could do in a sequel, but yeah this is the game, and for a first it truly is a gem. Sometimes I wish I could move some of the unmovable cabinets, or straighten them out on the floor, the ability to store cabinets and games away. None of that is a big issue, but found myself constantly thinking that to myself. I would totally recommend this one to anyone that loves the Arcade vibes, classic gaming, score grinding, it is a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly addictive to me, but you might not feel the same if you haven't lived through the 80's or 90's actual arcade era. Nostalgia is real. The simpler arcade games (pong for example) are quite true to original counterparts but the modern/complexs the ingame arcades become the more simplified they are. Not necessarily a bad thing though.The manager side of the game/story is a bunch a mini games (laundry, cleanup, repairing) which are ok, but not the main focus of the game by far. Laundry side of the game you can ignore entirely after the early game and it is literally removed completely at end game.Not sure if there even is a way to replay the game? But if so not that much replay value other than arcade machine placement and micromanagement of their settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: this game is fun. you're stuck in some arcade tycoon limbo universe where everyone disappears when you get close. laundry piles up from the ether. you scavenge every cent from the coin hoppers, even while people are using them. turning into coin goblin, managing prices and doing laundry (or not). interesting idea and fun loop. i DO NOT like the fact that the game will basically auto budget things for you by telling you what budgets work best.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but as it is right now, I can not recommend it due to all the technical issues as well a some bad design decisions that plague this game. I will continue playing it though, as I am just riding a nostalgia trip, but here is where my issues start.1. If You're old enough to get a nostalgia trip out of this game, You are also probably to old to unlock all the achievements in the games that are dexterity and reaction time based. Even some of the narrative in the game is hidden in beating and racing for high scores with your clients. If You are not a fast paced super agile gamer god, You may miss out on some of these things entirely and there is no way to cheat or skip your way out of it. Not only that, but you will also mis out on "premium currency" that unlocks all sorts of things that make this game easier, so it's not just punishing for players that are not agility and reaction time oriented, but also punishes them AGAIN by locking the things that would make their life easier behind their own mechanical skill level.2. My sedcond massive issue is the camera work checking steam forum only ensured me that this is a common issue that most people experience and there exists no fix for it. What is going on exactly? The camera is skipping across the entire screen, sometimes making you do a full 180 turn just because it jumped. It happens randomly, mostly in the laundry area and it is extremely confusing and nausea inducing. It seems to be less of an issue for controller players, but again, if you are old enough to get a nostalgia trip from the whole arcade theme, you are also most likely a mouse and keyboard player. Even in the pause menu where you have the PDA device, the stylus part jumps all over the place because the game does not seem to know where your coursor is at any given moment and it's a complete jumping mess.3. The laundry part - the game never really tells you what to do with that part of the game. At some point you will reach income levels where laundry income is negligible compared to the arcade income, but the game never tells you if you cna igonre it or not, will you still be getting customers without the laundry part or not? will your popularity drop? There is no hint about it whatsoever, so you just keep on doing that absolutely horrendously boring chore of moving baskets around just because you never know if your arcade will shut down without it as well or not. If you're an older player whtat suffers from mechanical skill issue, You will also not have all the arcade achievements unlocked to boost your income even further, so the laundry still seems like something you need to be doing just in case.4. There is no way to save your settings it would seem or it is just bugged, or only limited to a controller (not sure, since it never gave me any prompts). No matter what I change in the settings, it all instantly resets to default. If I do it in game or in the main menu, it never saves my changes. It is super infuriating because the default FPFV is set to 45, which feels like playing a game while looking through a roll of toilet paper and I HAVE A ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ULTRAWIDE MONITOR! The ultrawide resolution may also be the issue with the messed up jumps in coursor and camera movement, but since the game does not even allow me to save any settings I can not tell if that is the case. All I have is the default tunnel vision that I can not adjust, change resolution, can not swhitch between true full screen and windowed full screen, nothing, because the whole settings menu ignores any changes and just does its own thing.Holy hell this game is a mess. Yet, it still is enough of a nostalgia trip to keep me playing and the visual side of it is also super fun. It triggers every neon arcade bone in my body the right way, so it's even a bigger shame that it's just completely broken mechanically.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: After 63 Hours of Playing this i can say the first impressions aren't that good with the sense you don't have full access to the PDA or PC and the fact the game gives a sense of "you have to do laundry, clean trash, clean toilet, clean gum! you just gotta! when in reality if you literally just sink all your efforts into the arcade machines, the hopper profit pays for itself. especially with the video hockey table at the beginning of the game, the cab placement can be weird sometimes and the progression definitely feels weird but the most positive thing i can say about this game is the music selection, secrets, and the games. by the time you reach end-game and follow the story, the characters and story feel relatable when it comes to family matters. but the arcade games with the music OST is some pretty awesome stuff and i can see the devs put alot of time and effort into making alot of really awesome arcade cabs just for this game with some great music to boot. all it's missing now is VR and i can only imagine how awesome it'd be to be playing in an arcade in VR with games, neon and great music. also as of the time of writing this, i'm currently waiting to see what the devs do with the game next and VR would be cool.edit: Bro they made it VR like a week ago :nosebleed: i can't wait to play this sht in VR once i get a VR headset!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a game of mini games. Its fun but the game progress is too linear for me, buy a couple arcade cabinets and extend arcade. Rinse and repeat. I just completely stopped doing laundry a couple of days in and found daily tasks tedious. I did enjoy how your time spent on arcade cabinets actually affected profitability and that every cabinet was playable.unfortunately the controls for the arcade games are sometimes difficult to handle (especially Billiards). I still chose a positive review because it was entertaining, not a badly made game, and there a plenty of games to play. I wouldn't however suggest this to someone looking to run an arcade business as the only real choice your given is which of the few cabinets available you'll spend your money on.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: A "simulator" type of game that's actually really good! The day cycle can be somewhat slow on the beginning but once you get the arcade going the day goes in a flash! The production value on this one impressed me a lot, all the arcade games are well done and they just kept coming! There is little focus on management but it means you get more time to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. In the first part of the game though it was pretty boring as one person stated. The laundry mat was just boring as heck. But as the story kept evolving and everything came into light. By the end I had a deep seeded hatred for her dad. He was just a *Beep* anyway the story line was pretty good. for what is was. It did give me some feels as in feeling sorry for the girl. And hating the dad lol. I wanted to hit him really really hard. heh that is good storytelling right there. I waited till I beat the game to post my review. And I got to say the game itself is good. Though the beginning is quite boring but as you grow you arcade and build onto it. And start playing the many many games it has. It got quite fun. I was astonished how many games they actually have. And all of them work. It gave be quite the nostalgia for the 90s I was in my teens then but it did hit the right feeling for the most part. The only game I seen missing was a mortal kombat clone and street fighter. But for the amount that was there They were quite fun. I liked the game so much I bought all the DLC for it too. So I had everything and had a blast playing most of them. Like with any arcades. There was games I liked and did not like but there was quite a few that was really fun.Now then lastly I will talk bugs. There was a few here and there. Esp with one machine in particular. The one with the Olympic games. For some reason the hopper where you would take the money out was a PITA to get to. That machine was hard as heck to get the money. Also there was alot of buggyness with the computer GUI and the mouse not working right in the office. I had to press W and S and space to select stuff instead of using the mouse itself. Other then that there was some glitches with some of the stuff on the side of the building where you would toss your trash. The bags on the ground and some of the other stuff on the ground would pop out of existence when you got close to them. Lastly the game itself was really good. The voice acting and stuff and the music etc. Was quite fun to listen to. The dad was a jerk though. I really hope that there is a part 2 of this game. With even more stuff added. Maybe even be able to buy a apartment and decorate it. too. I can tell this game will need more end game stuff after you got what you wanted. And beat it. There def needs to be end game content. This is a great game and I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. 20 hours to full completion (without DLC) and I've enjoyed it more than any other game I've picked up in the last couple of years. The starting basic gameplay loop of doing the laundry is a touch tiring after a while but as you slowly build up your arcade and get some arcade machines you really enjoy and some great songs on the jukebox (HIGHLY recommend getting this as early as possible, the music is great background for the rest of the gameplay) it really becomes a great time. Great gameplay, a decent story, great arcade games and music and if you find a particular part of the game monotonous or you dont want to do it you just dont! Lets you mix and match all the stuff you enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I recently went to an arcade that I remember as a child being filled with games like Rampage, Street Fighter, Cruisin' USA, Time Cop, etc etc. What I found walking around was a pile of gatcha games and maybe TWO older racing games. I left without playing anything, went home and looked at my arcade cabinet build. Arcade Paradise got me right in the nostalgias. Each cabinet pays a homage, both for better and for worse, to many oldschool, and several current arcade-style games. It delivers the atmosphere that many of us "older" gamers remember, and was genuinely a game I found myself thinking about when not playing, which doesn't happen to me often anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Nice atmosphere, style and story. My only wish for the game, is that it would have been a bit more fun to have more roguelite progress introduced to the mini games. Like the upgrades in Space Race Simulator / Vostock 2093, inventory in Woodgal's Adventure or the level unlocks from Bugai! Really liked those machines and ones like them.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The game is simple and very repetitive, but some of us folk like that, and then add in nostalgic music and old game cabinets and for me it's a winner!   No game crashing bugs and it runs super smooth on highest settings.  The DLC is pricey if you want it all but it's not required to enjoy the game.  Overall if you can get it on sale for 20% or more I'd purchase it if you like 'Tycoon" type games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is the type of game where you hope for a remaster at some point. The bones are great. It has a fun, silly gameplay loop, the writing is nice. But there are a bunch of bugs, the mouse and keyboard controls are pretty bad, and frankly all the in-world art is pretty ugly. I had a good time with it, but hopefully it does well enough to get the polish it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wasn't expecting to like this as much as I did.  I am an 80's and early 90's gamer, but not really an arcade gamer per say.  We didn't have tons of money to spend on arcade games...I'd rather save my quarters and buy one I can keep, after all.   BUT that doesn't mean I didn't enjoy the sites and sounds of arcades.  And this game seems to have nailed that!  WHY did all those arcades have the carpet with the weird shapes on it?!  Who knows!  I always guessed to hide spills.  And the beeps and boops of the various machines going off chaotically...absolutely love it!I wish there was a REASON to continue to operate the laundry.  At a certain point, you realize that you might as well just ignore the laundry completely...and that point doesn't take long.  The arcade quickly outpaces it...but there is no reason to continue to do it at all.  I may have enjoyed the laundry being some sort of requirement somehow...an annoying deterrence from your goals that you eventually manage to work your way past What I was NOT expecting was to be pulled into the storyline.  The story is VERY cliche, but...I found myself invested none the less.  To be honest, I'm not even entirely sure why.  The voice acting is good, sure, but....I think at the end of the day we can all appreciate the story of someone who takes a leap of faith towards their dream job and manages to actually make it.Anyways, if you enjoy mini-games themed after classic games and a light touch of business management, give this a go.  You don't have to be GREAT at the mini-games to move forward...by spending time playing the games and achieving various goals you will boost the arcade's income and easily progress through the story.And if not....well, there are no time limits within the game so feel free to take your time and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and unique, but very quirky (and not always in a good way).Game starts as a pretty slow, monotonous burn. The motivation for progression is entirely based on reducing, and eventually overcoming, that monotony. Most cabinets are clearly inspired by real games; inspirations are a mix of real cabinets (Qix, Asteroids, Missile Command), or arcade-like games (Candy Crush, Super Hexagon). There are definitely hits and misses, but that's true of the source material too.Sadly, in-game balance can be all over the place. Each cabinet has its own goals, and the game gets more popular for every goal you complete. Most are just enough to stretch you into learning the game, but some are super easy and some are absurd. The extreme examples are Empathy and Smoke 'Em (granted, both are DLC). I cleared the Smoke 'Em's goals in my first round by accident on mouse+keyboard. Meanwhile, I'm not sure I'll ever complete a single goal for Empathy. Certain goals, like the dance machine note count or Space Race Simulator total distance, aren't hard just extremely time consuming. Its frustrating to order a new cabinet and not know ahead of time if you'll have it at 3/3 by the end of the day, or struggle to get it to 1/3.Then there are the daily objectives; each day you're given a "TO-DO" list, which rewards secondary currency for upgrades. Most are pretty achievable, but there's a sore lack of variety; the game's given me so many UFO Assault to-dos that I can't stand playing that cabinet anymore, meanwhile my Stack Overflow cabinet is gathering dust.However, the core experience of this game is very unique, and simultaneously delivers on a multi-game package, a business simulator, and an interesting (if light) story, all in one. If you can ignore the rough edges, 8.7/10, would recommend.(But skip the Empathy DLC for all that is holy)
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game, bought it for the minigames stayed for the story. It's surprisingly heartfelt and charming watching your arcade grow as the MC develops their relationships. The environment was absolutely amazing, the music, the arcade machines, even the street outside the arcade are all fantastic. The subtle changes that happen alongside the bigger changes when you upgrade, amazing. Also really enjoy how the arcade games are challenging but not frustratingly difficult. Great game. 10/10

Love that you can play on everything in your arcade and really make it your own.Graphics are beautiful with a real 90s arcade feel. Very few negatives. _childDocuments_.review: first off ignore my hours played I play offline(my achievements can clear up any doubts)This game is an absolute masterpiece and super chill but it doesn't dump all the games on you at once like capcom arcade stadium. it is quite literally an arcade you build from the ground up making each new cabinet special as you have to make an arcade npcs wanna visit to buy more.it has an overarching story which hit me in the feels like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ truck but the finale was so satisfying but theres plenty of other things to keep you busy from daily chores to layout and pricing management. theres also highscore battles with npcs as well if like myself online fixtures arent your jam.

_childDocuments_.review: A very entertaining game filled with many games you will be familiar with if you've spent any time in a 90s arcade.The progress is kind of linnear with your choices not mattering too much.Can get a bit grindy. In fact some of the goals and achievements are SUPER grindy so if 100% is really important this will annoy you.But have to say it was a fun experience getting through this game and the amount of different games inside the game make up for any nitpicks.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: If you play all day, nothing gets done. Thanks for the valuable life lesson, Arcade Paradise.Before getting to the fun arcade bits, there's a laundromat to run over a non-essential background story about daddy issues. It's a cute nod to starting small and investing time and money to grow, hard work and perseverance, but it all becomes highly repetitive and mundane after only a few in-game days.Everything is a mini game on its own: wash endless loads of laundry, pick up trash, unclog the toilet, clean up gum, collect coins from machines, repair those that break down. Again, cute a handful of times, not 100x. Automations or helpers are not available until somewhat late in the game, and even those don't completely eliminate the tedium of shallow management tasks built on repetition.With enough time, you'll earn enough cash to start improving the arcade lounge and the laundromat business will slowly take a backseat.Most arcade cabinets are clones of classic or popular titles from decades gone. Some machines are fairly impressive in their thematic inspirations or reinterpretations of the original game mechanics. All have great retro visuals and sounds. A few would be fun to see developed in extended versions, but a good number are cheap knockoffs only worth playing a handful of times, perhaps more if you intend to complete their associated challenges.These simple challenges include scoring points or playing a number of times to earn a special currency. Completing them improves the popularity of your machines, in turn increasing revenue and allowing further expansion. Having a new machine delivered always feels good.Many games have terrible controls and most have pretty questionable physics, in many ways true to the originals, but some are actually pretty good, and all have a certain charm that emanates from their retro quality.None of the cabinets are built for longevity, though a few include permanent upgrades that make them worth revisiting. By the time your retro emporium reaches its final stage, you’ll be about done playing its vintage replicas.Check emails, chat with your sister, order new machines online, buy additional 90s inspired tracks for the jukebox, purchase expansion permits. Management tasks are reduced once the arcade business gets going and eventually you'll be playing games all day.Recommended to fans of chip tunes and pixel graphics, or anyone old enough to have fond memories of the 90’s.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: If I'm being honest, it's right on the border between a thumbs up or down for me. I got it included with my Humble Choice and I had some fun with it, but I would likely be kinda bummed out if I paid full price. Pros - -Has that late 90's, early 2000's punk vibe that brings a lot of nostalgia and a lot of the graphics and character designs remind me a great deal of like the early 2000's classics like Tony Hawk (This is probably the main reason I give it a thumbs up-A large assortment of good music that you can play through the Jukebox, with more being unlock-able, though it can kinda get lost in the background-While not much in the way of voice acting leaning into the whole Gerald of the Riviera bit was amusing-A large assortment of games. Some better than others but at least half of them are pretty solid retro-style games.Cons - -There's not necessarily a tutorial. You learn the basics over the course of several in-game days. That being said, each day is a long time and you are chastised for ending a day quickly. It feels like the first hour of the game you are just doing laundry and picking up trash with maybe two arcade games. It's not the lack of tutorial that gets me, it's that you play SO LONG before actually getting what feels like a solid arcade.-Lots of busywork. At first it doesn't feel so bad and you are SORTA left off the hook from doing much after a few HOURS of playing, it gets to be an annoyance, especially with reminders constantly going off on your watch. -While not necessarily a con for some... this game doesn't really fill one genre, instead it half fulfills two separate game genre's. It's a business sim where your only choices are where to place the arcade games and your revenue is based off of how well you play the games and how much busywork you do. No other customization. But it's also a game where you are expected to enjoy retro video games... but it can feel diluted or forced because you need so many specific tasks in each game to earn more money and your alarm is constantly going off.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are old enough to have set foot in an arcade (or have been to one of the recent arcades that have started to spring up everywhere) then you totally get the vibe: neon colours, classic rock vibe, etc.In this game you run a laundromat because your dad thinks you are a lazy slob. As you progress through the game you gradually turn more and more of the laundromat into an arcade until ultimately running a full fledged arcade.Despite being a business sim, there's actually very little actual business simulation. You clean messes, debug the games when they crash, and collect money manually from the arcade games. Gradually you can automate most of this process through completing challenges given daily and using those rewards to unlock perks. The main part of the game is to buy and play arcade games. The arcade games are pretty fun and are themed around popular arcade games (although other thank pong and frogger they are reskinned to look different). Overall good and fun game if you grew up around arcades

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation is solid. It certainly sells the vibe that it's going for, with serviceable visuals on par with House Flipper.There are many negative reviews citing the low maximum FOV of 60, but I didn't have much trouble here. I kept it at the default 45 as it helped me focus on the cabinet in front of me. A low FOV just sort of makes sense with the kind of gameplay on offer. That being said, the maximum should be higher to help out folks who are sensitive to FOV.Arcade Paradise features some interesting twists on well-known arcade classics, like a Grand Theft Auto meets Pac-Man game that I found kind of neat.Unfortunately, this game hinges entirely on your level of nostalgia for arcade games, of which I have very little. Gaming has come a long way in the past several decades, and it's increasingly difficult to justify spending much time playing Air Hockey or Bejeweled so that I can unlock Solitaire or whatever when I have Baldur's Gate 3 and Hollow Knight competing for my attention.There is a bit of management busywork on the side since you're also operating a laundromat. Between arcade sessions you'll be picking up trash, loading washers and dryers, and unclogging toilets, none of which is terribly engaging but does add context and variety to the experience. I can't really say that I had actual fun during these segments, as the management minigames are even more basic than the arcade games they unlock.If I hadn't gotten this in my monthly Humble Bundle, I never would have bought it. Understanding that I'm obviously outside of its target audience, I'm going to leave a thumbs up because I'm sure this game will resonate strongly with people who are actually interested in an otherwise very solid arcade simulator. If you're not absolutely fascinated by the prospect of playing retro arcade games, I don't think this game is going to do much to sway you. Frankly, I could go the rest of my life without revisiting Pac-Man again.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Accurately replicates the special frustration of being pulled away from your video games to go do chores. I'm considering that a feature instead of a fault. To start, you do have to do some 'laundromat simulator' activity. However, soon you'll be greatly rewarded for completely shirking your duties and will happily be knocking out To-do list arcade objectives and heading home at 2pm. It takes a mercifully small amount of time before the most intrustive duties become optional. There is little to no actual arcade management. It's definitely not 'arcade tycoon.' You just clean the place up every day and then try to achieve arcade gameplay-based goals, and the better you can do, the more money your machines make.The arcade games are all pretty fun in their own way and you have to learn to do well at them to progress. A couple of them are pretty brilliant and had me genuinely interested in getting better at them.However I do find it criminal that you have to clear _one hundred_ battles of Woodgal to clear that machine's goal. Blech.

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10Well.. what an odd game this is. The games aren't exactly very good (although some people like them for some weird reason), the game preaches anti work drone/force due to repeating menial tasks yet throws a bunch of menial tasks at you all the time like having to clean up and do washing if you want more money. additionally, the story is super anti fatherhood. someone clearly had daddy issues when writing the story. the weird thing is the main character is super entitled too. the dad gives her a way to create her business and she never even thanks him for it. She just refers to him as a terrible person. the way they forced the dad character to be evil was weird as heck also. for some unknown reason he just doesn't want you to create an arcade place lol. he ignores your research that proves an arcade place is more profitable just like an evil Saturday morning cartoon step dad. Obviously this has to be present otherwise people might suspect that her dad is actually the good guy who tries to teach her business responsibility and tries to provide an actual bloody whole business for her to learn how to manage it. She lies, deceives her dad but it's all good because SHE'S the good guy cause her dad didn't listen to he that one time lol. don't get me wrong, her dad not listening to her is dumb, she was right in that one and he was wrong but she is also a massive entitled brat and the game tries to show you in the story how the father is wrong but never cares to show you that the main character and her sister are entitled twits. Despite all of these problems and more... the game is still super addictive.. :/ working to get that new arcade machine which you're hoping is actually a good game with good mechanics is super fun! wanting to know how the story turns out is also really addictive and giving you tasks to perform in the games to make them become more profitable is an absolute stroke of genius.That's why this game gets a 6.5/10 it's good enough to keep you hooked but a lot of the times you could be playing actual retro games that are way more fun than this. if the games where better made and instead of giving you the laundry mat backstory, converting it slowly into less Landry mat and more arcade place and clean up duties  if you had to upgrade your arcade place to new buildings and a deeper more rewarding management simulation then  this would have been a much better game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: While I think this game has a few issues, I keep playing it. Ultimately, this is a 'Recommend', especially if on sale. I first played this game on a Luna+ trial account, and ended up buying the Steam version when it was bundled with some other games on Humble Choice.Another reviewer said not to look at it as a business management sim, and to appreciate it a a collection of mini-games. For me, I find much greater appeal in managing the laundromat and building up my backroom arcade more than the mini-games. I enjoy spending time moving laundry baskets from washer to dryer to earn money to purchase the next arcade machine, while passively letting the coin hoppers fill up throughout the day. The arcade has a nice retro aesthetic which adds a lot to the appeal. You can also purchase an old-school jukebox for the arcade, which allows you to change the BGM for a few minutes. I like the synth-wave tracks, but most of the jukebox songs are electronica tunes that seems more appropriate for a 1990's rave simulator.Once you start building up your arcade room, the game encourages you to spend more time playing the arcade games, at which point which you can ignore the laundromat with no penalty, other than miss out on potential revenue. Yet, I'm still moving laundry baskets around and watching the timer count down until the load is done.The mini-games are mostly hit or miss, with more quite a few more misses than hits. One mini-game is a slower-moving version of Qix, for example. I'm not sure anyone needed that in their life. Another is a Timberman clone, which is as basic as it comes in terms of gameplay. One of the better games is a simple match-3 game.Where Arcade Paradise really excels is in the visual and audio appeal that evokes the feeling of managing an old-school arcade, with a decent laundromat mini-game as the backbone of the experience. This game has a lot of style and lets us know that there is great potential for an arcade management sim in the video game space. I hope this game paves the way for a more refined successor in the future that can build upon these ideas and include some more compelling set of arcade mini-games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish there was a Neutral recommend button. I love the concept of the game, but the execution is a bit of a hot mess. For one, I really didn't care for the "story" of the game. The family dynamics were so one dimensional and stilted that it might as well have been set up in one of the arcade cabinets. The father who is obsessed with you becoming a respectable adult through hard work and dedication gets mad at you for exhibiting hard work and dedication simply because it wasn't in efforts towards the laundromat. This despite the fact that you've already proven yourself to be an immense financial success. Even after you  he still chastises you. This is entirely contradictory to his singular defining characteristic which really bugged me.Second, cleaning up the laundromat and having a strict clock really detracts from the main game. I know the point is to ultimately eliminate the laundromat and just have an arcade, but it feels so half assed and burdensome.Third, the achievements are unnecessarily grindy. Cleaning up 100 pieces of bubblegum when you only get ~3 a day is just disrespectful of my time. What's worse is that the buff you can buy to limit garbage ALSO limits the amount of gum that shows up so I had to deal with cleaning up lots of garbage and the toilet to just get my daily quota of gum. On that note, the toilet has disgusting and unnecessary visuals which is a big minus in my book. I want to play with managing the arcade not cleaning a ♥♥♥♥ filled toilet. In a game where the people blink out of existence when you approach, you don't need everything  to be "realistic" to this degree. Same goes for cleaning the literal bugs out of the cabinets.All that said, where this game really shines is the actual arcade games. There's enough love and attention to detail in these games that makes most of the issues I had just melt away. They also added some interesting twists to core mechanics of the old classics that at once pays homage to the original while providing a truly plausible alternative version that might have existed in another universe.However, there was one thing that really REALLY bugged me about a lot of the arcade games, and that was the fact that they held progression. This confused me at first because many of the games seemed impossible to beat in a single session, then I realized that when I went back to a cabinet that my progression had been saved and I picked up right where I left off. This was completely tone deaf to me because the entire point of an arcade game is that you start from scratch every time. That every new player has all the tools available to them from the start and everyone is on an equal playing field. What we ended up with is a whole lot of grindy mechanics that have no place in an actual arcade.So final verdict is a recommend, but just barely. Do better in the sequel!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real love letter to arcades of the 80's to early 90's.  An absolutely stunning amount of playable games are included.  Not all of them are perfect, but many are just a lot of fun to sit back and play.As a simulation, the game is not particularly deep.  There are things you can do to maximize your income, but it's hardly necessary.  You could adjust the difficulty and price of games, adjust their position to try to line up less popular cabinets next to more popular cabinets so they get a little bump in revenue.  You can also play them to complete objectives on them and give them a boost in popularity that way.  In fact, simply playing complete games will boost the cabinets appeal as well.  But at the end of the day, as long as you actually do make sure to collect the cash from them, you'll have plenty of money to continue to advance the story.  Of course, keeping on top of the laundry helps a lot, but that's more "time management" than simulation.And there's a decent bit of story here.  Enough that by game's end you will care about the arcade.  It feels like a personal investment.  It was an enjoyable experience.  Mechanically, you purchase available cabinets until you can expand, at which point more cabinets become available.  Rinse, repeat.  Though the game is not well balanced.  As said, even with minimal effort you can rake in the money.  Which is bad for the 'upgrades' feature which uses a separate currency.  Which is given out in far smaller, more limited amounts.  At the end of the game I hadn't even purchased half of the options.As for the arcade games themselves, it's a mixed bag.  There's a lot of knock-offs and clones here, of varying quality.  Some of the games can be remarkably good and fun.  This game's Asteroids clone, for example, tries to improve on the original with a few added features that I enjoyed.  One of my favorite pass times turned out to be the digital Air-Hockey that you start the game with, even when I obtained a 'real' Air Hockey table.  The arcade version had a better viewing angle, only went to five, and I'm sorry to say the computer cheats in the 'real' version with a hitbox larger than the graphics for his paddle.  In fact, other than the dart board, I found all of the 'real' tables to be some of the worst games of the bunch.  In particular the Pool table, which was among the worst I've ever seen - which includes old Flash games.That's not to say all the games are bad.  I have some favorites.  There's a fun quick arcade game in Woodguy Jr., a simple high-score pass-time.  I'm a fan of the puzzle game Stack Overflow.  Zombat 2 was a perfectly suitable example of that style game, something that could have worked in actual arcades.Games that couldn't though were ones with upgrades - though Zombat 2 somewhat qualifies as once you buy a weapon, it can start dropping from enemies randomly.  In particular, Vostok 2093 is very... not arcade.  Insanely easy with a lot of upgrades of mixed value that is more of a time sink than a challenge.  And while not all the games are "cheap knock-offs", some - like the digging game - I found to be riddled with bugs and had a cheap feeling to them.The inconsistent quality of the arcade games included though doesn't put me off on the game as a whole.  There's more than enough content in here to enjoy even if a few of the games don't sit well with you. They may not be as brutally difficult as actual arcade games - most of the time - but you're here to relax and waste time anyway while managing your empire and swapping loads of clothing from one machine to another.  The game is absolutely worth playing, and I'm curious to check out the DLC myself.  I would have liked a little more control over the arcade, being able to set the theme and the like, rather than just "where to place the cabinets", but that's fine.  Again, this isn't mean to be some serious, spreadsheet manager simulation game.  It's more casual, laid back, have fun and enjoy the story.  One begging for VR support to wander the virtual arcade.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game in a Humble Monthly Bundle, and was immediately intrigued. I assumed it would be some sort of management simulator, and I suppose it is, but only barely so. The real enjoyment I received from this game was observing and being part of the awe that comes with simply being IN an arcade. This is a love letter to early gaming in the best way. There are over 30 game cabinets to unlock and place as you grow from a tiny laundromat back room into a full fledged arcade. I was not prepared for the fun story attached with the growth. And not just fun, but well written and emotional at times, too. Although it did take me too long to realize that I didn't need to continue to do the laundry side of things after a while. :)Most of the games will be replicas of old favorites, including a few new ones thrown in for good measure. Most do not have a lot of depth, but each one is, I feel, a great representation of their respective genres.Overall, I had an absolute blast with this game, and I cannot thank the developers more for it.
