_childDocuments_.review: You know, the very first time I ever played an arcade game was when I was very young at a grimy laundromat very much like the one in this game. Arcade Paradise starts as a great realistic laundromat sim that allows you to use the laundromat profits to transform the business into a profitable arcade, starting with just a few old machines in the back, and expanding into a full arcade. All of the laundry/maintenance actions are little mini games that keep it from getting too droll, and is somehow immensely satisfying. The arcade games are each playable mini-games, quite a few of them even have a co-op mode! If you enjoy multi-tasking time management sims as well as mini-game related titles like Mario Party, this will be sure to catch your attention. You can play all of your own arcade games and it's actually encouraged, as the arcade game will set in-game goals for you and increase it's relative popularity if you play it enough. They're remakes of some seriously classic arcade games as a tribute to video game history. I've got personal favorites that I go back to! You are given enough business stats to entirely customize your arcade cabinets and turn it into a booming entrepreneurial dream, you control the layout of your arcade and everything else down to the game difficulty and how much to charge. If you like mini-games you could be immersed in this for hours, otherwise it's still very satisfying just playing a day at a time and building your routine. If doing the laundry feel boring, then don't do it, go play games in the back until the laundromat closes.  Definitely recommend checking out this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games of all time, it's basically a collection of arcade games inside another whole game, and I can't possibly recommend it more. I think no matter what your interests, you'll find many (very addictive) games you enjoy in the cabinets you purchase for your laundry arcade. The progression from a tiny closet space with a couple of machines to a full arcade is pretty crazy, the vibes are off the charts, and the story that rolls along with it is actually very emotional and packs a couple twists you might not see coming. This is certainly a hidden gem of a title and more than worth a spot in anyones library, I could've payed $60 for this and still felt like I got my moneys worth and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Well this game when I played it in early access was really good I had almost no issues. After playing it for some time i left for a while I came back. First 5 mins into the game I ran into 2 bugs. 1 that locked me inside the arcade with a laundry basket in hand and the door being shut behind me and would not open until i quit the game no matter what I did. And 2 the hand animation constantly breaks for picking up and loading the laundry. I love this game just the bug where I got locked inside the arcade with no way out as my watch was beeping non stop to tend to my stuff was maddening.Overall game is still very good I just wish the hand bug wasn't still happening now even in full release. It just sits static and stretched out on my screen until I pick something up or play a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Oddly satisfying. You get to do crap tasks and play games in order to grow a crap business into an arcade. The growth is the satisfying part. Once the laundromat shrinks enough, you get to play games and manage all day. Growth is a grind, but it's at least fairly accurate in that businesses don't grow from garbage to bangin' overnight.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Good laundromat sim and a better arcade sim (non-functional snack machines notwithstanding) with a satisfying gameplay loop and a staggering number of legitimately fun mini-games (which are complete games in their own right). Despite long since having "beaten" the game (i.e. fully upgraded the arcade and completed the store) and still boot it up regularly just to play the arcade games. Even the wood-chopping ones! (Highly recommend the Snood-like Bugai, Breakout-meets-dachshund Barkanoid, OutRun-by-way-of-Star-Wars-podracing Space Race Simulator, and the deeply weird and highly-addictive Blockchain.) The soundtrack is excellent as well (several of the radio and jukebox tunes are legitimately catchy and sometimes I play Space Race Simulator just to listen to the music).
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: lOTS OF GRINDING IN THE BEGINNING BUT ITS AN EASY GAME TO PICK UP AND LEARN QUICK. then YOULL HAVE TO DEVISE A STRATEGY TO GET WASHES DONE QUICK FOR MORE MONEY, KEEP THE SHOP CLEAN AND EXPAND THE BACK ROOM. eventually THE IDEA IS TO GET RID OF THE LAUNDRY AND MAKE IT AN ARCADE ONLY.7/12/23 UPDATE.  Got all the games now. Controls still suck. Have to use a mixture of keyboard/mouse and game controller. sETTINGS DONT TAKE THE UPDATED CONFIGURATION AND W A S D DOSENT ALWAYS WORK OR ARE POORLY ADAPTED TO THE GAME.SOME GAMES JUST SUCK SOOOOOO BAD THO. GRAVICHASE IS COMPLETELY UNPLAYABLE. SEVERAL WOODGUY GAMES. THOSE LAST 7 SECONDS AND SUCK. THE PAC MAN/GTA MASHUP OF RACER CHASER COULD BE BETTER BUT THE CONTROLS ARE NOT AS RESPONSIVE TO PLAY. THE DANCE GAMES ARE UNPLAYABLE. NO CONTROL OR KEYBOARD WORK. THE PINBALL IS MUCH TOO FAST TO BE BELIEVABLE OR ACCURATE. MABYE AN UPDATE WILL HELP?
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun experience. I've always enjoyed the atmosphere of arcades and this game felt quite unique for reliving the life of playing in an arcade, but virtually. The game is a bit slow and tedious after a while, and some of the controls for some of the games are a bit clunky or inaccurate, but that didn't ruin the experience for me.Only thing I'd suggest is some tweaking of the controls, like for example: changing the controls for Vector Attack where pressing a direction snaps the cannon to the direction you want to shoot instead of needing to rotate all the way around. And tone down the sensitivity of the Pool Table game. Other small improvements would be appreciated, but those 2 are the ones that I found to be a bit frustrating.I still recommend this game, even if you don't play all the way through, it's definitely worth taking a look at.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun way to waste a bit of time. I'd personally wait for a sale though. While it was fun to play a bunch of arcade games within the game, it would have been better more focused of the management. Have a bunch of games you don't necessarily get to play, but have to constantly be switched out for new games to keep up with trends.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is a light Simulation Game. You run an Arcade in the Back of a Laundry at first. The day to day involves picking up trash and unplugging the Toilet and occasionally fixing the Machines. You can do Laundry too. I call this a light simulation because they don't make you Pay Electricity costs.The Arcade Games are the Star of the show here. there are Facsimiles of  many Popular Old Arcade Games like Pac Man and Space Invaders  Arkanoid and  Frogger and they offer quite a Few DLC machines to buy if the Base Game's Arcade Machines don't quite do it for you.I prefer to play this Game with a Controller. The Arcade Game Controls seem more Responsive VS a Keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise- The only game where peeling gum off is enjoyable.9/10 game. A few bugs, but they can probably be ironed out. The only two noticeable ones are a zombie hand when you take clothes out of the dryer, and some trash being in spots that you can't access like under the dryer machine's door.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game, surely a must have for any arcade game nostalgia fans. The gameplay is basically a "tycoon-lite" thing where you show up at the laundromat you own, clean it up, start some laundry, then play arcade games in the back for achievements that boost your in-game income. Go back and change the laundry every once and a while, rinse repeat. The core of the game is arcade playing, I do with they'd expand the tycoon and laundrymat management aspect though. There is the foundation of a wonderful tycoon game here too. Right now the tycoon aspect is more of a window dressing for the arcade machine gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very nostalgic, it brings back a lot of memories from old Arcade machines and games played when I was younger. It is an amazing simulator with a slight back story to it, and honestly it might be the simulator out there and the most underated one. Not sure why many people haven't come across this game, but this on path or better than Streamer Life Simulator, both are amazing, both should be tried out. I would recommend this highly if you enjoy simulator games like myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I love the retro aspect of the game. I was amazed at the office. I was surprised how accurate the game play is on the arcade games. Chores get a little hectic but as you gain upgrades time management becomes easier. Collecting coins from the hoppers can be a bit frustrating but I think there is an upgrade for that, which I haven't got yet. All up Arcade Paradise is loads of fun, full of nostalgia and a nice change.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a very good game, with some flaws.  The collection of minigames is mixed, but nicely varied.  You'll find some games in there that are truly a delight to play, (Zombat, Blockchain, and a few others), mixed with some great takes on existing arcade games (including their takes on Missile Command, Mr. Driller, and Space Invaders)...mixed in with some games that are just much clunkier versions of existing games (such as their takes on Qix and Frogger, both of which are severely bugged.)The story is passable, a good excuse to keep progressing, though it does have some disturbing moments of outright parental abuse that clash against the otherwise light tone of the gameplay.Overall, while I wish they'd fix a few of the bugs with individual games, and fix a few of the bugs with the overall gameplay mechanics [such as random daily goals that can literally be impossible to complete due to story progression], I quite recommend the game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: So you run a Laundromat that had a few arcade machines at the back and you use the Laundromat to expand the arcade and you can make money by doing the laundry for customers and throwing out the rubbish to the point your arcade makes big money.The best part is that you get to play the games you brought and there is a nice range of them for you to play too.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Just an awesome game. Not all of the machines are the greatest (like every arcade), but you'll have fun trying them all and finding your favourites. The story is kind of interesting, and certainly holds the whole thing together. But don't buy it for the story, buy it for the glory of old-school arcade gaming. Who knew emptying coins from machines would be so much fun?!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This one is kinda weird. It is dripping with nostalgia for a time I honestly do not remember, but adore anyway - Anemoia is the term, apparently. The devs clearly love this game, and to an extent, I love it too. It has a character of it's own and captures the 90s feel perfectly (at least, what I think that feeling is). However, the bugs really are a major letdown. I can usually  look past the bugs in games (I adored Cyberpunk even at launch) but this game is propped up by them to an extent that I cannot. Weird controls that feel unnatural are throughout, like in the air hockey type game, arrow keys instead of mouse? Just bizarre. If it wasn't for these bugs, I would consider this a hidden gem. It still is - like I said, kinda weird. Still really like it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: (Summary below this text wall)I really enjoy this game. For some reason my play history says I've only played this for 15.6 hours, but I've played it for much more, having started over once. I've about 21 hours in actual total, and I find this game rather chill. I recommend however, don't treat it as a "simulator". I've seen many people online see the game and assume it's a simulator, whereas this is much more of a management sim than anything. The game starts rather slow, but as you acquire more arcade games and upgrades, you get to spend more time playing arcade games. The game pushes you to play specific games by having you complete single time goals, like get 200 points or upgrade your player to the max, as well as giving you daily to do tasks which are like mini-goals. This is great for most games, save a single one I do not like (we'll get to that in a bit). The 90's aesthetic of the game is also wonderful, calling back to a time I barely remember. Making money isn't hard after a point and it really begins to just feel like 90's Arcade Simulator. The to-do tasks also reward a separate currency (Pounds sterling) that you can use to buy upgrades like faster shoes, to an assistant that collects cash from the machines for you.The worst part for a lot of people are gonna be those first two or three (or was it five?) hours where you're saving up to get enough money to make the arcade more profitable than the laundromat (oh yeah forgot to mention that, your players dad put you in charge of a laundromat) but once it is more profitable you pretty much just spend time playing arcade games (or do you? No spoilers in this review though). That's the first negative point towards the game, but it didn't really bother me that much (I've heard people online complain about it though). The issue I have the most with the game thus far is the goals for a VERY specific arcade cabinet: Zombat 2. This game is a zombie shooter and is a direct sequel to another Nosebleed title from what I've heard. The issue with the game is it is downright ridiculously hard. Like, you can change the difficulty of the game from the arcade management and it will still be hard as hell. Sometimes the daily to-dos for multiple days will tell you to do crap in Zombat 2, and I find myself just skipping it. This leads directly into my next complaint, sometimes it will give you the same daily tasks multiple times in a row, which depending on any cabinet in the game can be just frustrating. I don't enjoy having to do 5000 points in Stack Overflow daily (and I LIKE Stack Overflow).Oh also, the soundtrack is great, it does a really good job of capturing the 90s.In summary:+Great 90s Asthetic+Really well made arcade games+Funny plot+It's also a laundry sim+Stack Overflow keeps me up till 4AM everyday now+Good music/Really slow start/Somewhat odd upgrade system/+Goals and Daily Tasks-Zombat 2-Those times daily tasks repeat-Occasional lack of instructions on how to play a game (Specifically, Championship Darts)-Any task that requires you to play something for 5 minutes (Though, this can be fixed with an upgrade)
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game. If you ever played Arcade Craft, its like that mixed with Laundrymat simulator, except you can play the arcade games you post in your store. Most are simplified 80's style arcade games with a small twist to make them new/unique. Well worth the MSRP, but if you can get it on sale, its a steal. Plus, the developers are adding new cabinets to expand your arcade, so it just keeps getting better.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rather charming title in gaming. It's a sort of 80's/90's tale of an underdog's rise to glory whilst also giving moderate insight as to what a small portion of what the arcade industry looked like, with that portion being the most recognizable, the arcade itself. The key points that I liked about the game is the charm and atmosphere surrounding the in-game world, some of the arcade pieces (I.E. the cabinets and other things one might find in an arcade), and the soundtrack. However, there are some things that I wasn't a big fan of, those being the aspects of the arcade pieces that I didn't like, the overall kind of clunkiness of the game, and the fact that the story is a little lack luster and that there isn't a whole lot to do after the story is finished.I'll start off with the positives, firstly with the atmosphere. The theme of the game is superb to put it lightly, it's this sort of stereotypical retro aesthetic that is really appealing to me. With the bright and colorful environment and NPC's (specifically their clothing), the machines themselves, and how the story plays out.Next I'll discuss my next topic,  of the arcade machines and what I like about them. Most of the machines are quite fun to mess around and play with, and it feels a little exciting whenever you buy a new machine and wondering what it will be like. One of the key mechanics that I like about the cabinets is the intuitive nature of them, where the cabinet(s) gets bonus popularity when you achieve any of the preset goals that come with each machine which encourages you to play each of the machines that you buy, and that you need to fine tune each of the cabinets so that you can maximize the monetary output of the machines.Lastly is the soundtrack. The soundtrack is amazing and features a lot of great tracks. There are more or less two kinds of tracks in the game, punk/hip hop tracks which are incredible, and retrowave tracks that can be either great or kind of lacking. The in-game music really helps to sell the theme of the arcade that your character runs, as the hip hop fits best with the character you play as (that being a rebellious young adult), and the retro giving the place a certain mood while playing.In spite of all that though, there were a couple of things I didn't particularly enjoy. As you've probably noticed that when I was listing off the positives of the arcade pieces I would only ever say "some" and that's for a reason. That reason being the fact that a number of the machines are not fun all together or get stale and boring after only a short time. Secondly is the overall sense of roughness while playing. One of my most hated was the decisions with just about all of the more physical arcade pieces (the hustler table, a.k.a. pool, foosball table, and the actual airhockey table), as all of them have what can only be called the worst camera angles in all of gaming history. As it seems that the devs wanted to show off their "impressive" 3-D graphics and put the camera at isometric angles on all of the table based pieces which makes it a ♥♥♥♥♥ to see anything while playing. I mean come on, the actual airhockey table is awful compared to its virtual counterpart, all because the virtual one is top-down while the physical one is a crappy isometric angle. Besides the camera angles is the gameplay, which feels a little slow and stiff, it isn't the biggest problem in the game (and it's probably because I played on controller) but it should be pointed out none the less.Thirdly is the story, which isn't the greatest. I won't give any spoilers but I will say that it isn't all that great. As there is not very much interaction between characters besides chat messages, e-mails, and voicemails, and that no other NPC's can be interacted with. Although, the story's lacking-ness fits in with the theme of a chessy underdog's rise to fame. Then again, once the story is finished there's not much else to do than try and get all the achievements and to get all the upgrades and items you can. What I would've liked to see is a more realistic approach to running the business and your character's life, like if there was taxes on your purchases and property, or if you could see more of the city the game is set in or at least the character's home and you would need to manage your person on top of the arcade.All in all, I would say this a worth while purchase and I would highly recommend this to anyone. Although there are problems, many of them can be ignored since they don't harshly impact the experience and that it was made by an indie-developer so they might not have had the resources to make the game perfect, except for the bad camera angles, that was just straight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Anyway, get out there and make your arcade a paradise.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Honest review of this game: I like most of it. At it's core this game is a bunch of minigames inside a basic business sim. The first part of the game feels really tedious and the interruptions between doing "chores" and actually playing the games are frequent, but as you progress along the interruptions become less frequent and by the end game are still there but much more manageable. Some of the games are pretty great and I have a good time playing them even though they are simplistic in nature. Some offer rogue-like progression and some seem well made even if they are just a quick concept. Others, however, are frustrating to control and the goals seem out of reach to me, not because of the difficulty of the gameplay concept but because of they janky, unpolished controls on many of them. I think a lot could be done to fix them. For example, the Qix clone is really clunky on some lines and doesn't let you move smoothly and often gets caught on lines you can't see. The original played much more smoothly. Pool is nearly unplayable for me as there's no fine tuning your shots and you can't even see the end of the table sometimes.  Darts has frustrating RNG that doesn't matter if you line everything up perfectly it will just sometimes screw you making a 6 dart out seem an effort in just dumb luck. There are other games with similar issues but there are many games that are just flat out fun and you'll have a good time playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgia, Greek for that old, familiar pain. Some of my happiest childhood memories come from video arcades with my dad and my brother. This game, for whatever flaws it may have (and they are far too few to be of any concern), gives me a little bit of that back. The pain is indeed old, but so very familiar. And for that, I give thanks.Lots of fun little games reminiscent of a simpler time, some enjoyable if on-rails business management, and a story that feels all too familiar for far too many of us. And, of course, that soundtrack...I loved it. All of it. Recommended with great enthusiasm for anyone who remembers that time or just loves arcades and everything in them.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful. A tad slow at the start, and a tad to much time spent doing laundry. Would be nice to have the laundromats music seprate, AND have a few more tracks in the laundromat. The arcade itself has plenty of different music. Some of the arcade games are suuuper lame (UFO game!), some are really good. If your even remotely interested in arcades, this is for you.Weird hope that theirs a laundromat zombie defence DLC in the future, as the newspaper talks about zombies a lot. Like, at night, you build simple defenses, and shoot some zombies, to protect ur laundromat OR just skip and go to bed.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: All the arcade games are awesome. If you’re a fan of indie arcade games you get a ton of interesting options that you really feel like you earned them. Building and watching your arcade grow is rewarding. No wrong way to play. Awesome experience. Got on sale but would recommend at full price. Great work devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Although i'd recommend this game there are certainly issues with the finishing touches and some bugs that persist but given the depth of the content its more than forgivable. its got a killer soundtrack that's both nostalgic yet still modern feeling and an array of classic arcade games reinvented, if not simplified.  but if you don't enjoy retro games or care for the late century nostalgia then this one isn't for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off as a management game; slowly building up into a proper arcade from a laundromat 'gifted' by your father.Good arcade games, but the pressure for management tasks is relieved only in mid-late game with proper automation and management reduction upgrades. Task pressure was a bit of a distraction while pursuing high scores, but it did help give bonus to management with in arcade game achievements.Would do laundry irl while managing a laundromat's laundry and arcade again.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, overall a pretty chill and it's amazing the amount of depth in all the mini games. The developer obviously had a fun time going through all the classic arcade games and then putting a unique spin on them for this. There are plenty of things to unlock to keep it interesting for a significant amount of time
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely and novel game, a mix of management, mini-games and story / progression with a really authentic 80s/90s video arcade vibe. It's not all about washing other people's smalls and cleaning the toilets, although even that can be surprising fun! Tons of little details and Easter eggs for old-skool arcade game lovers
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true love letter to the bygone area of the western arcades of the 80's and 90's. I was expecting a more simulation/management style game originally but in the end I was delivered this wonderful treat that had every cabinet be playable. It captured the atmosphere of what some of the arcades were like at that time. In the end this game delivered a really great experience where I ended up doing nothing but playing their tributes to classic arcade games. Hopefully they will add in more games and a bigger place, and hopefully allow us to do mods for the game ourselves. This is definitely worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest.  There isn't nearly as much Management Sim as I thought there was going to be, but in exchange there was way more mini games!  Every single arcade cabinet is playable!  They're simple games, but playable!  That's awesome!  I only have two major gripes about the game.1. The challenge side stories are easily brought into impossible status for new players.  You start to compete with 2 NPCs on specific cabinets and you can easily ♥♥♥♥ yourself over if you do too good too quickly, because the NPCs will always beat your score even if you can't.  The longer story against Sam I couldn't finish because I couldn't beat my highest score at a certain point and had to give up.  That was a bummer.2. There are two music based cabinets, one you naturally unlock and one that is buy-able DLC.  Neither will have you typing notes to the beat or melody of the song.  Almost all typed notes are off beat.  It's feels bad, but is still playable if you learn to rely on sight rather than rhythm.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing value for money. It’s like one of those 100-in-one games you’d get as a kid but actually fun. Very satisfying to upgrade yourself and the arcade and watch the money roll in, making your work day easier every shift.You don’t even have to do the laundry part if you don’t want, but even that is gamified. Earning all goals on a machine is incredibly satisfying and actually earns more players for that machine.All around very satisfying gameplay and around 40 games (including DLC) inside a really fairly-priced job simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Was very excited to play this ever since I saw gameplay of the demo.I have to say that the controls for some of the games are a little wonky/ probably not made to play on PC. (I got stuck at some point only making money through laundry/ the arcades that I had because I tried to control the ingame PC with mouse instead of the keyboard and missed a few arcades I could buy to reach the next point in the story).I think there are still some issues to fix, but it's already a great experience and I also enjoyed the story that went along with it!It felt like the right level of difficult to me and I'm grateful that some arcade games required multiple tries rather than a high skill level to complete the machine's goals.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: You start out earning income by maintaining a laundromat that is owned by your in game father.  You use the income to build up the arcade in the back and eventually work toward converting more sales toward the arcade revenue.It's actually a lot of fun managing a business and working toward the goal of making it more enjoyable and adding more to your arcade library. I enjoy the creativity in the game as well as the music and the retro vibes. If you want to take a step back in time to what it was like to work in the 90's or 80's this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mix of empire building and arcade gaming. You build your own arcade where all the arcade cabinets are fully playable. Most of the games are heavily inspired by the classics, with a few arcade games that seem to be completely original. There's a decent plot and it’s all wrapped up in a late 80s early 90s aesthetic.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I have been sucked so deeply into this game. Who would have thought that you could tell an endearing story around owning a laundromat and building a secret arcade within it. Everything about this game is excellent. The repetitive loops give way to advancement that has an emotional connection. The arcade games within the game are themselves really well done too. The music is also amazing. The sound design is overall well done. Copies of popular 90s songs have being re-imagined for this game. I thought I was hearing was Nine Inch Nails Closer, but it was something else completely, and I dug it! This is one game you absolutely must try. I give this one a standing ovation.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It is a quality game for what it is, however, there is not a lot of room for creativity within the game itself. You are pretty well locked into what can go where with only minor variances of it, and no matter what you do you have to keep the laundromat going. It's good for about 15 hours of game play tops before it just becomes a repetitive grind and starts to lose its interest. Many of the games you are forced to play are very poor quality clones of very old games. Buy it when its on sale and it's good for a bit of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: A game about taking out bags of trash and playing video games.  It's a basic business simulator with decently fun arcade games, many of which directly pay homage to classic arcade games.  Nice unlock system and progression that keeps you wanting to play as you expand your arcade and game selection.  There's a ranking system depending on how well you do menial tasks like achieving an S rank for doing laundry fast enough.  Very fun, worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly at first I thought there was no way this game could be fun, taking care of a laundromat, picking up trash, and of course battling the toilet. After accumulating a handful of machines and upgrading Kings Wash I can say that this game is worth playing. The mini-game like tasks you do around Kings Wash, for me, has yet to get tedious because it makes trying worth it by giving more money the better score you get. The Arcade games are super fun and the game gives you a plethora of different "classic" arcade games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing that they finally made a game where Landry Detergent can do his Laundry.If you enjoy games such as "Gas Station Simulator." You are in for something special!I really like the idea behind this game, help out at your family laundromat with your end goal being to have the best arcade in town. It's a simple concept but takes time to achieve. Remember that patience is a virtue and Rome was not built overnight.Never had so much fun unclogging a toilet or picking gum off a chair!I plan to spend more time making this old laundromat into the baddest arcade anyone has ever seen.The graphics are nothing crazy but get the job done and the music has such a solid 90s influence.The humor is relatable and funny, I assume many of us (definitely not all) have gone through that stage of our lives where our parents think we'll amount to nothing. But as I always say, "the gamer always wins." I refuse to ONLY run my family's laundromat, my arcade makes more money!9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far.  Lots more to do with the arcade settings than with the laundromat part.  People wanting a laundromat simulator may enjoy it at first, but one does get pushed to increasing the size of the arcade.The mini-games have been good—they remind me of pico-8-styled games, but a bit more graphical.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Fun quirky little game, if you ever played arcade games like Asteroids, Pong, Pac Man, Frogger (and the list goes on). But you now want more but in videogame format? Here you are.Rise from your dull life at a laundromat and convert it to a arcade.HOWEVER, a critique is that some of the controls for games are a bit ... wonky. Fun time burn.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun game! I've always dreamed of an arcade management simulator for years, and I'm glad it's finally come to fruition. Slightly disappointed that some of the arcade machines advertised in the marketing were DLC cabinets instead of part of the main game, but they're only $2 each, so it's not much of a deal to me.All-in-all, amazingly fun game, and I would definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to take a lot of time to really make sure I played this game well to do a proper review. While the game does have occasional bugs, like the Woodgal challenge emails executing at the wrong times, sound muting temporarily, arms going wonky very rarely, and some cabinet game bugs (which I find fine because what arcade game didn't have bugs), this game is not only surprisingly fun with it's repetition but the narrative is something I did not expect. It's a story that keeps you engrossed in this game while literally just taking care of a buisnes in a fun way. Not to mention the music is boss! Overall, I give this a 9/10 and highly recommend this nostalgic romp through the 90's.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: If, like me, you enjoy building something this could be a fun game. I certainly enjoyed it. It's nice to slowly increase the size and number of cabinets in your arcade. There's a story. Bit hit and miss maybe, depending on your tastes. Me personally, I enjoyed it enough. Either way definitely not the star of the game. Those are the arcade cabinets, each of which are their own minigame. They are all pretty simple, but there are so many there will be some that you enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: First found this game by watching a friend play it and i have no regretsThe game starts pretty boring but i ended up having a great time playing all those spoofed Arcade games while trying to make more money to get more.The arcades are pretty fun, the game isnt that demanding of you and all you have to do is work forward for when you'll have more time to beat up your highscorei recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent progression system, really rewarding management experience, just enough depth to keep you coming back, but not too much as to put off players new to management sims. Great graphics, great soundtrack, and pretty good minigames too. This is a great game to sink hours into, or to throw on for a bit when you're home from your real job. Great work overall, looking forward to seeing another DLC pack if there's one on the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: A good game for the price, but in need of some bug-fixes for the office computer and some of the games. For the record, I'm playing with a keyboard and mouse, on Win11.For the office computer: desktop links don't always open when you click on them. Email is especially egregious, but none are exempt. Scrolling lists of items on sites like ArcadeMania and the Upgrades store is tricky. If you scroll with your mouse wheel, as I did, you will end up missing purchasable items since the scroll jumps too far in one direction or the other. I spent several weeks in game waiting for the next story beat, only to discover that I had arcade games left to buy. I would never have noticed if I hadn't tried scolling the ArcadeMania list with my keys instead of the mouse.But that opens another issue: when you use your keyboard to navigate the office computer, the mouse pointer on that screen jumps all over the place. It's apparently trying to "snap" to clickable links, but then the link might not respond to being clicked on, as noted above. Even worse, the "exit" key - the key you use to exit out of the computer or any of the games - may stop working, and won't start again until you quit and restart the game.As for the games themselves, they mostly work out alright. The only two I've had trouble with so far are Blockchain and Zombat 2.Blockchain doesn't appear to follow its own rules. According to the "How to Play" instructions, drop numbered blocks into a line, and build a line of a length matching the number shown in a given block to eliminate that block. For example, if the  block shows a seven, you must build a line of seven blocks to erase that block.Not so. I've had many lines of sufficient length to erase certain blocks, and yet they remain stubbornly not-erased. I'd love to have some clarification here.Zombat 2's issue is that I can't enter the shop for anything. Directions say to use the space bar, but that doesn't work. Nether does the "interact" key, or the three "fire" keys.Like I said, these aren't game-breaking issues, but they are noticeable and annoying. Hopefully a patch for some or all of these will be coming soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: "Overall, Arcade Paradise is an incredibly fun simulation game that has the perfect balance between performing menial tasks and arcade fun. Its arcade games are addicting, and the fact that you can enter and exit the arcade machines with zero load times is an impressive feat and not something I’ve encountered before. In the end, I’ve decided to give the game a 9 out of 10, I really enjoy the game and feel it deserves a high score. It’ll definitely please fans of arcade games but I will admit that it’s likely not a game everyone is going to enjoy but as a fan of arcade games myself it’s definitely my kind of game."Full Review:
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it was a positive experience but it's not without it's annoyances. My two biggest gripes were:1. The upgrades took so long to achieve that by the time I could afford the ones I needed, the story had moved on making them useless. I still had 3 upgrades to go by the time I finished the game and I didn't even touch the musicjammers.2. The washing was so obnoxious and disruptive, it made getting the 3 items on to-do near impossible some days to the point where I simply neglected the washing. Some days I breezed through the to-do's making the days feel long or it took so long to get through some of them with so much washing, the day didn't feel even close to being long enough.On a side note, one of my to do's one day was to leave before 4. I left at 3:55 and Dad was up my arse about it. I guess it was a reminder that they're painting him as the bad guy in all of this. So I felt a compulsive need to stay and not leave early on days when the to-do's were done well in advance of closing which got boring. Anything that annoyed you in the game could be bought as an upgrade except for someone to come and do the washing. As an homage to arcade games, I did spend an awful long time washing clothes. I didn't really need the reminder on who the bad dude was.The cabs were generally pretty good. Although, that UFO game though can suck a giant ♥♥♥♥♥ and I never got the hang of Blockchain.The ending was beautiful and satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: HUGE HUGE HUGE CAVEAT: Every single "physical" game is garbage. Foosball, pool, anything with actual physics blows. I really thought I'd do every game's challenges until I got to the physical games. Heck even the dancing game's stepmania/ddr ripoff can't match the song's beats to the steps properly. You want knockoff dig dug? Galaga? Weird tank game? They've got it. Some of these games are love letters to the originals, others are more like "oh shoot I guess we have to have that huh?", looking at you "whack a mole with the worst imaginable key layout"Here is a perfect example of lack of polish. You have an upgrade to RClick to zoom. It's to "help find garbage better". Yeah hey. Guess what? You have games that use RClick and don't disable that feature. So if you're using RClick to brake in your Fzero ripoff? You ZOOM IN.When you play pool, the instructions to place the cue ball obstruct....15% of the table, all in the top right corner. Really needed about another month's polish and feedback to make a good game great. Still worth it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: So I'd say worth a buy, and worth sticking through the bit slower times.First I came for the arcade style, stayed for the family drama. I like that this isn't just an arcade business simulator, but you have an actual story going on while this is happening.There are a surprising amount of games within this game, some are better than others. Some i've actually played for at least an hour. There are also some good songs you can unlock in the jukebox too. Little jems from small artists you would have never heard from. I'm really glad I got this game, and I'm sure you will too.Oh also I saw the Game Grumps play this which is why I bought it. To bad they will never know how deep the game goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It might just be me, but it is insanely addictive. The story is quite 'meh', but the arcade games with metaprogression are quite fun. Some of the 35 games are awful copies of each other... Woodgal Jr and Woodguy Jr is the same game. Air Hockey, Video Air Hockey and Shuttlecocks has exactly the same gameplay. Unlike other games, at the  time of writing, Zombat 2 has no coin-retaining option, so getting the 200 and 250-coin weapons are impossible. Even so, there is something about the ambiance that keeps me coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Jam Packed with goodness and as addicting as candy, but much sweeter! most sim-career games where you open up a new business or start a new career are just kind of annoying and outstay their welcome with gameplay loops that don't feel rewarding or interactions that just sour the experience, but this game just makes EVERY aspect fun! with a tonne of original arcade games, all playable (and each having unique challenges to encourage you to try every one of them), a bunch of work tasks that are gamified to a very endearing extent, and most importantly a story that just grants so much wish fulfillment. I think that if you don't BUY this game, you should at least watch your favourite youtubers PLAY this game because it's just lovely!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. One part management sim, one part vintage gaming nostalgia. There is so much to like here. The game starts with you taking on the management of a laundromat in which there is a back room with some dusty old games. Each day you make money by doing the laundry and playing the games, so you can buy more games to make more money. Eventually (rather quickly) the games begin to make more money than the laundry so you can abandon that altogether if you want and focus on the arcade. Each game is a playable take on actual old school games, and each is quirky and fun in its own way. Highly recommend this game to anyone who likes management sims and old school games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It's good but it's too short and pretty buggy. Hopefully the bugs will be fixed and they add a DLC or something to make it longer. Oh yeah, I'd with there was a way to easily reset the game, because I went into the appdata folder for the game, deleted the files, and it still didn't reset it, so I'm stuck in the post-game, and can't replay the main story, so enjoy that the one time you get to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I love arcade classic compilation games, and I love janky simulator games...and this game is like both rolled into one. Plus the "late 80s/early 90s" soundtrack music is awesome! There are two forms of currency...money (made by the arcade machines and laundromat) and pounds sterling (made by doing daily "quests"). I do wish there were more things to spend money on. Money can only be spent on new arcade boxes and occasional arcade space upgrades...and it becomes an overly-abundant resource very early in the game. Pounds sterling is the main grind for permanent upgrades. Great game for the price though overall!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Not only was this a chill game, but it has a great soundtrack. All the mini games are...OK. I was most excited about the beat em'up only to find it a bit lacking. I'd really like to see a sequel with some things fleshed out. Maybe a bit more management. Not so grindy on the goals to make money for upgrades. I got all the way through the narrative on very few upgrades because it seemed the more you had the less you had to do. Everything started to automate.All in all it was a great game and I can't believe I put as much time into it as I did, but once I started I got hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who plays a TON of management/simulator/tycoon style games, this game is WAYYYYYY too grindy early on. It's very tedious, the machines take too long, and you end up just doing literally the EXACT same thing literally every single day. If they change this, then maybe I could recommend it at the pricey $20 tag.Also for the love of god, let the player look all the way down. Being limited by how far down I'm allowed to look is by far the worst design choice in this game, and totally unrealistic too! I seriously can't think of any possible reason for this other than to prevent you from being unable to see your legs, and I hate when games do this.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It's just what you'd expect, with a little story that acts as the backdrop to your success.I look forward to more cabinets and games, even if it's DLC.Some of the goals are ridiculous, though. Straight up bad.  I hope Nosebleed is getting enough feedback to help them tweak this part in upcoming updates.Love the game though, and there's an absolute ton of creativity here - from original soundtracks, games, even how every aspect of the game is a game within itself!  Creatively fantastic and I love the aesthetic.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, talk about a labour of love. It may be a cliché phrase but it thouroughly and accuratly conveys the amount of blood, sweet and tears that must have gone in to making this game feels as fun to play as it is. Not just in the arcade games themselves but also the graphical style. Loved the soundtrack too. The story is suprisingly engaging too, not something I though I'd say about an arcade management game! If you enjoy arcade /retro games this gem is well worth your time & money.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game slotted nicely into my 'super chillout' calendar after I beat Power Washing Simulator. It's honestly a very unique and relaxing experience throughout - though I haven't beaten it yet, I've dropped a good 20 hours in. Watching your arcade grow from one or two rusty old machines to a thriving neon hotspot is great - and the variety of games that have been coded/designed for the setting is striking.Absolutely worth checking out if you need a game you can just turn on and chill out after a hard days work! Everyone will have their own preferred arcade cabinets and I find myself weirdly curious where the story is going.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this got addicting quick! Who new running a laundromat could be so fun! Basically you run a laundromat  completing chores and doing your WASHING earning you extra cash so you can buy more arcade games. Then you  play the arcade games to complete challenges making them better thus increasing their profit. If you complete tasks from your Dad you can earn a different currency which will allow you to upgrade things making your quality of life better!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have the same arcade nostalgia shared by so many. Sure, I spent many evenings in the bowling alley arcade as child, but just watching my brother play! It didn't click then, or maybe they just didn't have the right games. Regardless, even without that nostalgia, I love Arcade Paradise. The plot actually touched a nerve of mine around the climax, and even if it does not for you the emotions were conveyed incredibly well in those scenes.Beyond that, I dare say any game that can surprise me with having things I expected not to like and turned out to love is a winner, much more so when it is a full series of mini games. The management aspects are a little light for the genre, but the blend between it and playing the mini games is part of what makes it special. Not to mention how great the music actually is. 100% consider the soundtrack bundle. It is too much of a shame to miss out on.Absolutely give Arcade Paradise a chance if you are interested. I won't pretend the games doesn't have hiccups still, especially as you progress, but they are being patched and both the present and the future look bright.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Randomly checked out a Drae video today and saw this game in it and I just had to buy it, the tussle between doing laundry and making guaranteed cash, or waste my life away on little arcade games was not the fight I expected to have with myself, but here we are. From pulling bubble gum off chairs, to throwing away the trash, to unclogging a mega dump this game turns everything into a very satisfying mini game and I would highly recommend anyone to check out this little Indie Game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I overall really enjoy this game only 1 criticism I have is doing the space racer is really straining on the eyes to where i cant play it more than a few min. and even after adjusting the graphics settings to try to make it better. other than that ive had a couple pieces of trash in the arcade i wasnt able to pick up. This has been a ton of fun and would definitely recommend to anyone who gets a kick out of management games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun but I think it needs a lot more polishing.The mouse-keyboard controls seem to have gotten some rework since the closed beta but they're still bad.Some of the Arcades need some bug fixing too I think.So far I've encountered 2 Arcades that don't work for me.Line Terror takes away lives despite none of the Terrors being anywhere near me and Stack Overflow sometimes let's me pick up crates but I can't but them down and using Backspace (which is supposed to be Undo) doesn'T do anything. Other Arcade sometimes have issues too. Like Zombat 2 which doesn't let me enter the shop sometimes.Considering that playing these Arcade Games is somewhat mandatory it really sucks when they don't work.The concept is really cool and it's fun when things work. But it doesn't so it's not worth the money in retrospect.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Good game while watching videos/streams.Graphics arent impressive. Found the exact Laundrette in the game "Daymare: 1998" in chapter 4. It´s a small part of that game, which explains the undetailed graphics when copying. A bit disappointed considering the play space.The games on the arcade machines are fun. There surely is a game for everyone to enjoy.The story could be told more interestingly. Feels a bit empty.Very repetetive. Doing pretty much the same thing every day with minimal changes.I cant recommend it for 20€. About 10€ would be more fitting in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing trip down the neon lined memory lane that was the 80s & 90s at arcades. Very well made mini games at each cabinet, although some are buggy, but not to the point I'd call them "game breaking" and could easily be patched to polished perfection. I will say this game is not perfect. As mentioned before some mini games have bugs, some cabinet goals will reset(bug), for some it can be hard to figure out how to progress beyond a certain point.But the weakest aspect in the game by far, is the story. At the end the father goes way out of character and  It honestly made no sense and that's when I realized... someone on the dev. team might have some daddy issues. Again this is definitely worth it, especially if you grew up in the 80s/90s, just try to enjoy the games and tune out the story for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-35+ Mini-arcade games that are a ton of fun to play with challenging goals and achievements. -Management Sim is light - No real fail state; easy to keep progressing.-Polished visuals and audio; really feels like being in an arcade.Cons:-Laundry stuff drags on for far too long-Constant interruptions to trying to complete challenging game goals-Super long (and boring) plot sequences that pull you away from the arcade -Lots of bugs. As of this writing I am unable to finish the 'toads' once game due to game breaking bugs... let alone try for any goals on it.-Very strange hit-boxes for items; very easy to click things you don't mean to.-Little 'post-game' content besides finishing the game goals? seems like the game just kinda trails off at the end...
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews for games but this one, I feel warrants it. It's kind of rare these days, but this game is exactly what it looks like and what the creators sell it as. It feels like a 90s arcade through and through. I was actually surprised by how many fully fleshed out games there are with so many different mechanics and systems! The aesthetic is spot on, the soundtrack is amazing, and while the story is essentially just a glue to hold together your reasons to be building a laundromat into an arcade(it really doesn't need to be anything more) it still has a pretty nice undertone to it. The graphics of each game are phenomenal, which is impressive to me considering just how many different styles of art they implemented for each arcade cabinet! You can definitely feel the love and care oozing out of this game from the devs that made it.I definitely think its worth at full price if you're an arcade fan even in the slightest.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Love simulation games and miss the arcades I grew up in so this game is perfect for me. This game has fully sucked me in and my need to set high scores has been driving me nonstop even after finishing the story. Some small bugs at the time of writing so 9/10 overall.10/10 if I include the happiness of finding the Hexadecimal Achievements related Easter Egg
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game but I also have a few issues with the game. First off, the Daily Challenges. Some days those challenges include tasks like, picking up gum from the walls and such, but when I take a look around I can only find like 2 of the 3 pieces the task is asking to pick up. I mean I spent an hour looking around for said gum and couldn't find it anywhere. Or at times it will ask me to get a certain task done from an Arcade Machine that wasn't even purchased yet.Now the Arcade Machines are fun. Like seriously fun. It's creative the way they will turn around some of these games into knock-offs but it works. Some of the stations I feel are a bit bugged? (like Cyber Dance being extremely off beat on all three of it's songs or Stack Overflow not responding to commands and being somewhat laggy) But it could also be part of the charm of the machine to make it feel like its rigged to get money from you (or piss you off)The interactions of Player NPC's trying to beat your scores are fun. (I hate Sam and them beating my Woodgal Jr high score every time)The whole managing both sides of the business from doing laundry, finishing goals and tasks to make your Arcade Machines more popular is perfect. Though I feel the upgrade you can purchase to "slow down" time so you can spend more time on the games and finish said tasks and goals doesn't help much. Still feels like time is passing by pretty fast.Overall this game is a lot of fun. I haven't stopped playing since I got it just a few days ago. You build your own arcade out of the remains of a run down laundromat. And the concept and features of the game are almost perfect. Really makes you feel like you are running an Arcade of your own. Wish I had the money to start my own Arcade, maybe someday, but in the mean time this game fills that void in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lot of fun. It's a love-letter to old video game arcades, and plays as a combination of chore-core, a slight management overlay and a large amount of retro-style mini games -- a few  which are janky and finicky, but most are of really good quality and a few are quite brilliant retro-games in their own right.A strong recommend from me, and in particular for anyone who likes old arcade games and retro games.  The game isn't perfect, and if you don't like chore-core or having to juggle time between competing goals, the first few hours of the game might feel a bit frustrating -- although the game is forgiving and you can't really fail it; it's just a question of juggling which way you want to earn money and sometimes having to focus on progressing the story over playing the mini-games you want. Just finished the main story line of the game, and have about 30 hours of playtime put in so far. I'll probably put this on the back-burner for now as I've been playing it a bit much over the last week, but I can definitely see me going back to finish some of the goals in the mini-games. I might even hunt down some of the achievements, which I usually don't bother with.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was a teenager in the early 90's, this game hits me squarely in the nostalgia. I miss arcades so much and hope they make a comeback. Until then, I'll be playing this to get my fix. Excellent music as well and the arcade cabs are a lot of fun. I hope they keep adding stuff, but even if they leave it as is, it's a pleasure to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviews have said, the laundromat side of the game will interrupt you playing the arcade games. This never bothered me however, given that this game is first and foremost a management sim. If you want to just play arcade games, this isn't the game for you. If you're looking for a chilled out sim game with some arcade minigames though, I've been having a lot of fun with this :)
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I personally really love this game, I am a fan of other types of sim type of games and typically love taking the time to immerse myself in the environment I'm in. I also enjoy business sort of games like the old Roller Coaster and Lemonade Tycoon games and this definitely gives me that feeling. Doing laundry to make money feels like work just as it would in the real life, but seeing new machines show up the next morning and seeing the backroom expand is such a rewarding feeling. The arcade games themselves are the main focus as you will be playing them and finishing their cabinet specific goals to bump up their popularity to earn more cash and most of the games I have played are quite fun. Zombat 2 (twin stick styled shooter) and Vostok #### (A Galega ship game) are my favorites so far. Keep in mind that the studio has made a ton of arcade cabinets so how in-depth they go vary, such as Vostok having only 4 different enemy types and such. There are also times where the games aren't to great if you had experience with other games that turn that activity to 11. For me, the pool minigame (called Hustle(r)) is not too great after I had a lot of experience with a game called Pure Pool on Ps4. I wouldn't expect the highest quality of games of the irl nature but they do okay.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Always liked the idea of sim games more than I actually enjoyed them but this one I like.  The sim aspect of it is decent enough but the arcade games themselves are actually very fun to play.  The whole atmosphere of the game puts you in a good place and I find its a great game to just chill out to.  If your interested I say give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best games I've played in a long while. One thing to note before I begin is that if tedious tasks, and long wait times to progress both you this game might not be for you. However if you do have the patience the game can be a lot of fun if you're into retro style games. On top of the arcade game play the story plays out really nicely and Ashley feels really relatable given the circumstances the game gives about her. Towards the end certain parts really had me moved for this game, and I hope that this kind of genre of game continues to expand.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The story is much better than I would have expected, and the gameplay (even doing laundry!) is surprisingly engaging, with the game motivating you to go around playing all the different games. The games bread and butter, of course, is the 35 games (well, 34 and a jukebox) made for your virtual arcade. Some are simple mini games, some are basically clones of classic games like Pong, Space Invaders, Missile Command, Frogger, Bomberman, and Bust-a-Move. Some are solid but generic examples of classic genres like twin-stick shooters, brawlers, racing games, and shmups, some are enjoyable representations of other arcade attractions like pool, whack-a-mole, and darts, and then a few are legitimately original games with clever concepts, like Racer Chaser (sort of a combination of Pac-Man and Grand Theft Auto) and Blockchain (a very good and DEEP puzzle game that has a bit of a learning curve but is really worth the effort). I really hope there are DLC games I can get later, because I would love to add some skee ball or maybe a light gun game. I've spent a lot of time in this one already, and even having accomplished almost everything, it's still fun to just hang out in my arcade and play some games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is fun.There was a time where I've wanted to work in an arcade, or even own one myself, as a way to keep that dream of arcades alive in the modern days. And this game lets me experience just that. Playing them is a blast, too.The arcade cabinets are pretty simplistic (but tough) in what they offer for different types of play and levels, but they're a joy to play nonetheless. It's also great to see that popularity with games boosts over time as you complete goals and visiting them often.I also find myself using the laundromat at times. With my arcade continuing to expand rapidly and putting in more games, sure the laundromat may be redundant to use when you reach a certain point, but the extra money is often worth the hassle.Earning Pound Sterling is a drag, however. Some of the To-Do tasks can be a bit too challenging, and the rewards are kind of slight, at best, so getting the necessary upgrades to make yourself and your arcade better and better (and adding more music into the Jukebox) can get fairly grindy sometimes.10/10 Great Game and Time CapsuleEdit, 12/15/22: It's been 3 and a half months since this review, so I figured I'd send an update and still recommend Arcade Paradise. With new updates means there are now more cabinets to check out, and one of those is Kung Fury. For those who remember the short film and game that came with, you know.If you don't, Kung Fury is a short 40-minute film that pays full homage to 1980s tropes and turns up the cheesiness level to 11. I suggest you watch this film and see for yourself. The game that came with, for a time it was free, then came with a price tag (which is still a really good deal!), and it was a classic arcade-style game. Easy to learn, but hard to master. And now it's in Arcade Paradise.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the better and more polished "simulation" games I've played. It was fun to play and the time management aspect seems just right. The arcade machines are really nice - the art work and sound design for them is cool and the nostalgia of going to the arcade as a kid in the 90s hit me hard. The only difference is that I could actually play the arcade machines this time! The story isn't bad for a simulator game either. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The definition of a passion project. The devs executed their vision on this game pretty much perfectly. I've never played a game that has captured the ambiance of an arcade like this. Hustle so you can make your dreams come true.It's the little things - every cabinet is meticulously designed. The sound work is fantastic. Yeah, just get this game its a vibe.Pro tip - get the slow down time upgrade as soon as you can, this game is made better at a leisurely pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this a 50/50 if Steam wasn't so binary.It has tons of bugs, but is playable to the end. It's alright. Not bad. Not worth the initial price point, but clearly a lot of work went into it by a select few people. So I respect it. Played it to the "end."There isn't a lot to the game on a macro level. Grind away money from one "day" to the next until you can afford enough for the next expansion by filling up your arcade. 4 Expansions later, "the end." A lot of "fluff" was put into the game for the environment, which is really well done, but that came at a cost of macro mechanics. People are calling it "grindy" and it *sort of* is, but compared to a laundry (heh) list of other games, it's not that bad. Could've been much worse to pad out run-time.Without the padding a game like this would last about 6-8 hours. 10-20 isn't bad, but it's definitely padded out. This should've released at a $10 price point.The biggest "benefit" the game has going for it is that the arcade games you can play are plentiful. If a larger company released this, they would've released fewer arcade machines on launch with day-1 DLC.Plenty of things to enjoy here and appreciate, but falls flat in some respects to the benefit of other respects.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Was doing laundry at home and playing a videogame... about doing laundry and playing videogames.Mind. Blown.Seriously though, I didn't really like some of the early cabinets available, but once you get a game in your arcade that you enjoy playing, it's a lot of fun. Laundry is an annoying task that gets in the way, just like IRL.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game in a loooonnnnnggg time where I first started playing it, I was smiling from ear to ear!It reminded me of the all the fun and grandeur that comes along with visiting and playing games at the arcade!! If you love arcade culture, arcade history, and arcade games in general, then this is a must have! Definitely (in my opinion) Indie Game of the Year!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: After a bit of a slow start, I'd resigned myself to a bit of a brainless loop of doing in-game laundry between emptying coins from a handful of backroom arcade machines. Suddenly, though, I found myself opening that backroom door to period-accurate arcade floor carpets and neon lighting--and I was hooked.With only a handful of hours in the game, I do find myself struggling for time to balance the laundromat gameplay and actual GAME gameplay (often needing to abandon arcade game runs after less than a minute to attend to laundry in the next room), and I do wish the best parts of the game weren't merely hinted at through item unlock descriptions that you'll access later--but the aesthetics and tone are on point and I'm already considering the long-term ramifications of my arcade layout in my head between games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna say I've really been enjoying this game so far. It's nice coming to a chill game like this especially after stressful days at work. I only have two points of criticism- The game sometimes feels a little unstable when in loading up after the start screen. I've had a couple of crashes during the load screen. Twice after getting the pool table the game didn't load the world geometry correctly. It resolved itself eventually.- Respectfully - I'd revisit the pool table game play. It feels impossible to take gentle shots. Even gently pushing the analog stick or mouse forward seems to deliver a full power shot.  Additionally, the lamp will sometimes completely block the view, especially when the cue ball is near a corner hole.Other than that, the game is great, and I enjoy all the other arcade games I've unlocked so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Pros Its fun to grind and have to work to turn the Laundromat in to an Arcade. The Arcade games themselves are fun and engaging, some are really difficult and require time and skill in order to beat them.Being able to see scores of people around the world or closer to home is great, really makes you want to get the best score possible on some of the Arcade machines.Being able to manage your Arcade machines and adjust the difficulty and price in order to get the best returns and bonus is like a puzzle in and of itself and fun once you crack it.I love the music in the game and having the jukebox and being able to control the music is great.ConsThe story feels like you have no control and are railroaded in to a single path.Really makes you HATE a certain character. The Daily Goals are sometimes completely unobtainable  e.g do no laundry all day, but then have in the same list, do 7 baskets of  laundry or have four machines running. The Arcade machines do not have their controls on the machines and they don't come up when you play the game, requiring you to have to search out the controls on your Tablet which is annoying and the controls page is not in depth and does not tell you how to play the game beyond the basic controls.Which can leave you in the learch ( I still don't know how to summon Wood guy in Attack Vector ).Overall I recommend this game and i give it a 4/5 Stars
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: was fun for the first few hours, then the game becomes extremely boring and tedious.  the only things you "manage" in the arcade boil down to buying machines, picking up trash, doing laundry, and unclogging a toilet every 2-3 days.  im also not a fan of how the npc's fade away when you get too close, it gives off a very lonely and deserted feeling to the atmosphere.this concept has a lot of potential, but completely missed the mark.   one can only hope that there are dozens of updates planned for sooner than later.  Until then, I'd wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, I loved every minute of playing this to completion.  I'm an original arcade rat, from the golden age of the early 1980s, and the atmosphere and attention to detail in this game are tremendous.  The graphics and sound are really well done and genuinely transported me back to the 1980s/90s.  The idea of running my own arcade in a first-person 3D world is a dream come true, something I never thought I'd really see in a video game, and now that I've seen it, I want more!  The game loop is seductive and highly entertaining, with every bit of progress feeling earned and a lot of eager anticipation built up for the next goal.  Every time you get to expand your arcade or buy a new game, it's a charming experience that just makes you want to play "one more day".  The arcade games within the game are more like mini-games - don't expect the next Galaga or Joust - but they often recall the classics of yesteryear, in clever ways, and are mostly very well done and appropriately nostalgic-feeling.  Several of them are quite good games in their own right.  All games have goals to reach that make them worth playing and mastering for further rewards, and collecting them and exploring them was easily the funnest part of this game.The game is so good that I'm giving it a high rating in spite of it having released in a pretty buggy state.  That alone would have brought a lesser game down, and I wish they had polished things up some more before release.  We could have waited a little longer.  But none of the bugs are game-breaking (read the discussion forum for common solutions), and the quality of the game simply overcomes the annoyances in the end.  As long as they keep patching the game, this shouldn't be a concern as time passes.  This game is tremendous fun and a clever twist on the simulation genre.  Highly recommended, and an absolute must-have for anyone who lived through this era and has fond memories of it.  This game brings those memories to life once again.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, proper nostalgia trip for me (who used to hang out in arcades as a kid).Some interesting game mechanics and good balancing too which I did not expect.And the actual arcade games themselves are cool and fun to play, you can tell there has been plenty of attention/time spent on each one.Quite enjoyed the background story too.Overall I am a lot more impressed than I expected
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: 1.) Would I recommend Arcade Paradise to people who want to have some fun and blow off some steam in a casual management/arcade sim?Yes,2.) Would I recommend this game to people who are chasing achievements or who pride themselves on completing every goal presented by a game?Yep! The devs have continued to squash bugs and ensured that every achievement is now attainable. The game itself still has some tracking bugs internally, but they are being worked on.3.)Have the devs been active in fixing the reported bugs and issues as of September 16, 2022?Yes.4.) Does this arcade management simulator have a fun game loop?Yes, it keeps you engaged and like many other time-management sims it offers the options to increase your efficiency and/or delegate some tasks to the AI. But it could offer even more options for the latter.8.) Is the management portion of the game engaging?Yes, to an extent. There are ways to increase profits/# of people playing the games through the setting of specific options so min/maxing is seemingly possible. But the in-game economies exist only to make sure you can upgrade your arcade and your character. Money is never going to be a problem, you don't have staff to manage or pay and most of the tedious tasks remain yours to do even at the end of the game with all the upgrades. There are tangible in-game benefits to doing the tasks, which gives them a purpose. Eventually I'd like to see the player reach the point of being able to kick back in the office and play the games without being bothered by the day-to-day if they so choose.9.) Are the arcade games fun to play?Yes, usually, but this will come down to personal preference of course. Some are boring, some are maddening, some still have issues with their controls (at least using M/KB like me--I haven't tried a controller),
