_childDocuments_.review: I loved how this game flowed from start to finish.  I have seen some reviews commenting on how much time you actually have to play the arcade games but I personally had no issues.  The game does make you work hard for a while in the beginning, but once you start making progress it feels more like an accomplishment than a stepping stone towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR laundry is annoying at start, but a great compilation of retro game remakes once you start making money.It's not often i will buy a full priced game on here, i prefer to wait for sales. This however caught my attention given that you can actually play the games in your arcade (and actually need to to help them earn more money). The whole laundry operation gets a bit tedious at the beginning, but it builds up money for the arcade and once that is up and running you can just forget the laundry exists altogether. As for the games, i am a huge fan of retro games and the games in your arcade are basically old school retro games. you will find clones of pacman (with a new spin on it) qix, digger t rock (nes), outrun / rad racer, dance dance revolution, space invaders and many others. if you are a fan of retro games, you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The variety in the playable arcade games and the kick-ass faux-90s soundtrack, make this one easy to recommend, particularly if you grew up loving arcades. A lot of the 35-ish arcade games are genuinely enjoyable knock offs of classic arcade games, and I spent quite a bit of time playing a couple of them outside of things the game was encouraging me to do.  It's not a perfect game, I ran into quite a few minor bugs at launch, mostly regarding daily tasks that didn't register correctly, and the daily tasks also vary wildly in how difficult they are to complete, with some of them seeming nearly impossible. This is not a huge game breaker, but can be annoying.I saw credits at the 22 hour mark, and had a good time for almost all of that time, particularly as you get farther into the game and have more time to play the games, and the time management of the laundromat is a bit less frantic.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ton of fun. I love the arcade machines and the amount of work put into it. Looks great and all the arcade games that were made are also really well done. Also love the over-the-top effects added to the basic choirs. If you want a chill game with a weird 80's vibe I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Wow, just finished and loved it. Shocked how it actually made me feel emotional at a few points, that was a pleasant surprise. The dedication at the end is very moving.Great retro business simulator. The music, vibes, sights and sounds all gel. The humor is on point and the whole game is a love letter to the 80s/90s and arcades. I was shocked at how innovative and fun the takes on arcade classics are, like combining GTA with Pac-Man. I'm 5 hours in and totally hooked. The endorphins when you get a new machine are firing for sure. The gameplay/ growth mechanics are pretty ingenious as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't put this game down since release- I have to see it through, build my ultimate arcade, and see how many To Do's (individual game challenges) I can complete.I was quite happy at the start just doing the laundry and keeping busy, but it became after a couple of "days" in-game that I could make way more cash with the arcade side, and thankfully not doing the laundry after a while really doesn't matter.I thoroughly recommend this game, it's repetitive to start with, but hey working in place that has "Grind" in the title should indicate what you need to do in order to succeed!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:  And 20 hours in, I'm done.  There's a plot twist midway through.  A plot twist that absolutely ruins what little goodwill I had left for a game that had been getting increasingly tedious and grindy for the last few hours.  Because you know how you make a job simulator worse?  By forcing the player to work an even more meaningless and grindy fake job, just to be able to return to their original fake job.Sorry, no.  I'm sure the developers thought they were being clever, but it's just hit a level of deliberate annoyance that I'm not willing to put up with.**********************************Insert usual wish about Steam having a sideways thumb, because this gets a resounding "meh" from me.  It's not terrible, but it feels like it should have been so much better.On one hand, the presentation is nice, and has a lot of polish.  I love some of the little details, like the Scott Pilgrim-esque 8-bit minigame popups for doing basic chores, like treating toilet-plunging like a fighting game.  And it is addictive in a zone-out-and-do-chores way, good enough for killing an hour or two at a time.  Plus, some of the arcade games have clever concepts or ideas.But it's got three big problems that I don't think will be addressed in patches.1 - The core gameplay loop is incredibly shallow.  You open the store in the morning, do chores, make money, play games to kill time, and buy new games.   Occasionally you have to save up to expand the arcade.  That's all you do.2 - The "management" side is shockingly scant.  Literally all you can do is change the price/difficulty of games to minmax their profits, and the game tells you outright how much money each combination will make, so there's no experimentation.  And you have some limited ability to move some cabinets around.  But that is IT.  No financial management like bills to pay.  No advertising, aside from a single buy-once powerup that improves your popularity.  No competition.  No employees to hire.  You can't even change the design of your arcade or add\change other elements like furniture.    (And at 13+ hours in, if any of these things are there but still haven't unlocked, it's taken WAY too long.)3 - Most of the arcade games are only so-so.  Many have pretty glaring design problems.  Like a potentially clever one mashing up Pac-Man with early top-down GTA games has an absolutely terrible semi-isometric camera that's locked to the north, wrecking your visibility.  Or a DDR-style rhythm game that, for some reason, doesn't play high-energy dance music - making it very hard to find the beat.   Or an Outrun-style racing game that's just unforgivably boring.Also, while this is in grumpy-old-man territory, there are so many anachronisms.  The game feels like it can't decide whether it's invoking the 80s or the 90s, so it just mashes them together uncomfortably.  And some of the arcade games have really out-of-place modern designs, like a twin stick zombie shooter clearly inspired by Isaac rather than Smash TV.All in all, I can tell the developers really tried with this one, but it doesn't feel like they tried hard enough.  Aside from the nice presentation, every individual element comes off as feeling lackluster and undercooked.  If you really just want a chore-and-arcade-game simulator, it accomplishes the basics, but don't expect anything more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of stuff here for a pretty low amount, but it's more like a mile wide but and inch deep kind of situations. All the gameplay elements, mini games, management, building up the arcade and the games themselves are fine but not great and don't really capture what made games like the original packman as addictive as it was. Then again, there is a staggering number of games so it may go over differently, especially give the existence of a pool table for some local multiplayer pool. Biggest gripes beyond the pretty low depth of gameplay is the upgrade system, which is quite the grind and not satisfying to do. The objectives themselves, too, are random and range from painfully easy to day wastingly hard. Didn't regret my time but didn't fully finish the game either5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: There is something oddly satisfying and relaxing about making a mini-game out of collecting rubbish, pulling chewing gum, unclogging the toilet and doing other people's laundry. While neglecting my own laundry that is piling up on 'that' chair in the bedroom (you know the one).Just as the guilt slowly crawls along your back to whisper "Stop" in your ear. You are freed and given some respite to play arcade games that will give you the much desired 90s nostalgia! No arcade cabinet is boring, they're all unique in their own way and offer an variety in flavour in regards to gameplay. There is surely an arcade cabinet for everyone here. This game goes way beyond being some "multi-pack arcade game" that we see too frequently, as it offers a wonderfully special story alongside that makes you warm towards the protagonist.Kick back and play some arcade games or relax and unwind while washing other people's clothes! Also, check out their discord server there is an awesome community that's around this game who'll gladly offer help / tips and tricks!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I played the snake arcade game inside a beat em up arcade game inside of the arcade managing game, i kid you not. On top of that, I played an intergalactic puzzle game where you travel the world dueling characters from the different arcade cabinets around the world, but when i got to japan i fought against Grey Fox..GREY FOX ! 10/10 BEST GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting to play 3 hours in one sitting with this game. I had to force myself off of this game.First of all the basic game play plot.You are a teenager in what I assume is the mid to late 90's, and your dad has left you his old run down laundromat business. You have to do all the chores of this business to keep the income running it, this includes keeping the premises clean and tidy, loading and unloading washers and dryers, and unclogging the toilet. Everything gives you some form of income and most things involve a simple mini game, keeping the game moving at least.All while this is happening you are secretly trying to develop a successful arcade business despite your dad not liking the idea, you then have to expand the area around the laundromat to increase space for your new arcade machines.You get to play the machines yourself and the games are pretty fun, they generate income each day you are in the premises and you have to empty the coin boxes from time to time, to get the income.Its a laid back and well made game, I haven't found any real glaring issues at the moment with it, but then I am taking my time and just enjoying the casual game play. Sure it has the same similar assets as most other Unity made game of this style, but don't let that put you off. I took a gamble on this game and I enjoy it a lot.Highly recommended for those who like laid back business management sims.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: decent management system that doesn't bog you down too much.a wide variety of entertaining arcade games.and a surprisingly good story without being overly complicated.if you like classic games, you will find hours of entertainment even after the storyline is complete.and remember, a paradise on earth can't be built in a day. but it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game is boring. The progression is way too slow. In the start most of your time is waiting around for laundry to wash/dry. Nothing to do in-between the wash cycle or dry cycle. And you'd better be paying attention to that wash/dry cycle because if you're a few seconds behind your reminder that whichever cycle is done, you just dropped from a S rank to an A rank or lower. I was doing the to-do list and missed a wash cycle by 30 seconds. I ended up with a C rank. So I was doing what the game wanted me to do but got punished for it via a different in-game mechanic. How stupid is that? Maybe the down time for the game would be better if there was a banging soundtrack I could jam out to while waiting for that next load of laundry to dry but even the music sucks in this game. It wants to be 80s/90s but it's not. They either picked free music to add into the game or they added in music from a local band who's stuck in the 90s. It's not enjoyable. There is no notification that a new load of laundry has shown up to be washed. Just turn the camera around randomly and sometimes there's a new load and sometimes there is not. There should be something, anything, to let you know. Especially when in the beginning when your main source of income is the laundry and if you let the laundry sit for too long, the rank goes down which means your money goes down. I can't recommend this game. It's just far too boring and there is far too much down time in this game. The pacing is too slow and off. There is nothing in this game that makes me think about it while not playing therefore making me want to play it. Most of the time I forget I even have this game installed, that's how boring it is. I would highly suggest to wait for this game to be free or 3 bucks before your purchase it. It's not worth anymore than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Life sim? Work sim? Fun sim? Yeah, it's kinda' all three.I legitimately love this game, from doing laundry to trying to increase the popularity of my arcade games, all the way down to playing the arcade games themselves. It's a weird but magnificent combination of game play loops I seriously enjoy.Part resource management, part retro emulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute nostalgia simulator. You mostly just complete simple chores, collect cash and invest that into arcade machines, that you can place in the back of your laundrette to earn even more money... You can also play every arcade game for yourself, so this game has kind of a two-tiered nostalgia going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise perfectly encapsulates a retro arcade from the golden era. The mixture between laundromat and arcade sim, while gradually expanding your arcade and cabinet collection is welcoming and unseen amongst steam's library of games. Arcade Paradise is a very enjoyable experience if you have the time to throw at it, as while it is a bit grindy it's grind pays off in the immense satisfaction that comes with each arcade expansion.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game has definitely got some interesting gameplay. Interesting take on a arcade sim game, as much "fun" as it is, it can be quite tedious at moments (especially in the beginning), also if you're not good in the mini-games and you get objectives which you just are bad at it, it can be frustrating. Also the focus is more on the arcade (makes sense because of it's name), and not a lot on the laundromat. It would feel more interesting if you could upgrade the laundromat as well, upgrading your machines, maybe also the snackmachines. There is a lot of potential in making this game even better than it is now. I do hope they will add more things to keep the game interesting. (more games, more minigames, more chores, more ways to make the game a bit less tedious) For now the game has enough to keep you going for a while, especially if you're into 90s nostalgic gaming. But it feels like it has missed some awesome add-ons. Also certain UI "bugs" are still there, so you might encounter some irritation. But all in all, this game is a pleasant sim game. But really can use some improvements & add-ons. I do hope they come. (there are no plans announced for future dlc/updates/...)
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific game! Finally an experience that allows you to not only run an arcade but you can also play the games. Laundromat + arcade = a good good time. The only problem is the amount of bugs and glitches I came across that hindered the experience. Once they've figured those out, it should be smooth sailing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I've always enjoyed these kind of sim games, but I usually will play and grind for about a week and then get kind of tired of the monotony and quite playing. This game DOES get monotonous pretty quickly in the beginning, with the constant laundry and trash pick up. But if you stay with it and earn enough cash to start buying better arcade cabinets and upgrading the shop, it gets a bit more fun. I enjoy the game more as a relaxed, time killer, wind down after work kind of game. Not so much as a daily player or something I can get real lost in. There is somewhat of a story line in the game, the premise being: You play as the "black sheep" of the family and your father unloaded a failing, piece of crap laundry business on you that he pretty much forgot he even owned (not sure how you forget you own a business). Your sister used to help run it and left a couple of arcade cabinets in the back room. After you see how profitable the arcade cabinets can be, you get the bright idea of making it an arcade/laundry business. The rest of the game is earning money from the arcade and the laundry business to expand them and buy new/better equipment and games.     The arcade games are pretty cool and well done. Many of them are pretty humorous or satirical. Most of them are spin offs of classic arcade games, a few being a mash-up of a couple different games. For example: there is a game you get right off the bat that is a mash-up of PacMan and GTA 2.  It's really cool that you can play every single game available. You are able to place the cabinets where you want, even having a strategy of placing lower earning games next to higher earning games in order to attract more players to the former. Change the prices of every game individually and a few more customization options. I have yet to unlock all the features in the game after being about 3.5 hours in (not sure why steam says I've only played for 58 minute).    All things considered, I feel the game is absolutely worth the price. Even as a collection of fun arcade games. If you enjoy these kind of sim games, arcade games, time management games or anything like that - you will most likely enjoy this game. It's well done, low on glitches and can be pretty funny at time! I would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I usually see these "management simulator" games and am intrigued. But when I buy them, they usually just aren't fun IMO. This is an exception. It nails the dopamine hits correctly. There's a frantic, yet solid feel to the game. It is not perfect, sometimes the hit indicators are off and it's difficult to perform tasks which is frustrating. Also, the pacing in the early game is a bit slow. The soundtrack is incredible, the games in the game are mostly good, though nothing spectacular. The atmosphere is top notch, and the look of the game is great. it's a terrific love letter to 80's and 90's kids. It really makes time fly as well. This game can and will make you lose track of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off a bit grindy and the laundry component does get boring quickly but the general concept and arcaade is good.Needs a bit of work polishing bugs, balancing and adding a bit more to the management of the arcade.At the moment all in all its worth your time, particularly if you are old enough to remember arcades like this.Time will tell how much extra the devs put into this game. With a bit more refinement / work it could be amazing, whereas at the moment it's merely "pretty good" :)   A solid 7/10 for me in it's current state.Talking of bugs..... none of my machines have ever broken in 8 hours of play.  Is that normal?  .... Ah after writing this they started breaking! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game. It's very consistently designed, which is rare and it also offers something different. I'd actually compare it to Hades in terms of design consistency. Everything just works. The music is amazing, the gameplay loop and setup works, the visual style is great and some of the arcade games are legitimately fun (I'm looking at you Stack Overflow but ♥♥♥♥ that UFO game). Only thing I wish they told me is that time stops, if you're at an arcade machine at 2am. Income is tied to machine progression goals and playing on a machine but in the course of your daily chores you hardly have any time. Getting to a machine before 2am allows you to finish the progression goals for that machine and take how ever long you want.I still wouldn't recommend it to everyone, as the gameplay is light management (basically doing chores, pressing the action button) and arcade machine clones. But if you're a fan of well designed games, great style, high scores, arcade games or doing menial task I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game and an homage to the past. The nostalgia is extreme, yet the content original. Anyone who was a teenager in the 80's and 90's will love this game, and as a bonus the developer has neatly encapsulated stylish design with a love of the subject matter. The cabinets feel legit. The games can be simple but many have layers of complexity that DO remind me of the coin-eaters of old. If you love the look and feel of a classic arcade, don't wait: buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Right i have been Playing 12 hours so far.To start with you will have no time to play your arcades because you need to money to but more cabs to increase the income of the arcade, once you get passed $600 a day profit on your arcades just forget about the laundromat and have fun with all the games and doing the goals to increase profit of the machines.10/10 love the game and you will too if you like old arcade games!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only at 2.5 hours but I keep asking myself "why am I still playing this"? Lol. Kinda hooks you to go through the grind to get the next fun pay off. I love the idea and I like the game. I want the DEVS to ADD adding snacks and drinks to the machines (and clearing their hoppers) and changing the damn watch beep noise! Thanks! May update later in to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Paradise is a simulator where you're put in charge of a laundromat that happens to have some arcade games in the back, and you slowly turn it into a full-on arcade, purchasing more games and expanding the space until it becomes the talk of the town.Words cannot express how happy this game makes me. From the ambience of both the arcade and the laundromat, to the games themselves (which you not only CAN play, but are HIGHLY INCENTIVIZED to play), I just can't get over how much fun it is to explore this game and play around with all of the things it offers. I've played other arcade-based sims in the past and all of them just miss the mark of what I want in this sort of game; not Arcade Paradise.This game is fantastic, and I've only had it a few days. I can't wait to see what else it has to offer!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: As a 90s kid that truly misses the arcade culture of the time, this game scratches the itch. All of the games I've unlocked so far (13) have been fun in their own ways. The simulation side of things is very light. There's no upkeep costs so there's no way to lose, just progress slower. It's really more about enjoying the atmosphere and chasing high scores on your games.Dealing with the laundry in the early game can be tedious for a bit but it can easily be ignored as early as the first arcade expansion. By that point, your time is better spent chasing goals on your arcade games to boost their popularity and profit.The daily chores can be a little buggy. It's often difficult to target and pick up some trash items. The daily to-do list can be a little too challenging until you unlock the time slowing upgrade. (I understand the dev team is working on a patch to smooth out the rough edges) Overall I've been having more fun with this game than anything else in my library.Laslty, I want to share some praise about the audio in this game. The team really worked hard in that aspect and it shows. Everything from the digitized fighting game call-outs when you're facing off with a dastardly piece of gum to the authentic feeling chip-tunes (including, what sounds like a Ghost cover in Blockchain?). I recommend you take a moment and just... stand in your arcade, soak in the sound of all the different games fighting for your customer's attention. At that moment, the illusion is complete. You feel like you're standing in a real arcade, with just enough doctoring to keep the audio chaos from becoming a cacophony. Do buy if:You just want to enjoy the feeling of hanging out in an arcadeYou have a fondness of 90's aestheticsYou enjoy old-school arcade gamesYou want to replay all of those old games, mostly with a clever twistYou find satisfaction in the sound of a hopper full of quarters being dumped into your pocket.Don't buy if:You're looking for a deep and challenging management sim.Neon signs offend you
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what else I can say about this game. I am absolutely in love with it. I've been playing games since I was a kid in the early 90's, this is my #1 favorite video game of all time. The one issue i found with a certain game was fixed the next time I logged on.The team made a game that rewards the player for EVERYTHING!! The soundtrack is great, the vibe is immaculate. I did not hesitate to re purchase this on the Switch when I saw it on the Nintendo store, that's how much I want to play this game. I can't wait to get my friends over to enjoy some amazing arcade games. RDR2  and The Last of Us took a step down after years up top for me. I'm even considering getting the logo added to my tattoo sleeve hahaha.Thank you Nosebleed for making this grown man feel like a kid again. 20/10 go buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: The first part of the game where you need to work the landromat can be a bit boring, but if you manage to keep it up until you sell all those pesky washer and drier the game loose its boring side and everythings beging to be fun.I really enjoyed this game, it still needs some tweeking but for the most part its great.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: This game fills the voids of every other arcade sim/tycoon game that has come before it. The laundry element can be a bit of a grind but you make some cash so it's kind of a wash. The way that the game makes nearly every aspect a minigame is fresh and fun, I never thought plunging a toilet could be so satisfying. Then you have gaming inception with some pretty awesome arcade games to play. This game can get a little chaotic but it seems they realized this and gave you a reason to try to get your to-do list completed. My only qualms are in the resolution issues that are present in the game. When you try to run at 720p (See steam deck) some visual assets are outside of the viewable area. This was replicated on pc. It seems that the dialog boxes etc don't reposition from where they'd be at 1080p.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: STOP OPTIMISING THE FUN OUT OF THE GAMEEDIT( I still think its a fun game and it is worth the asking price, but those dlc are FAR to expensive for what they are and I am frankly shocked how far the other way this developer went in terms of value, the standalone game, is chocked full of value, but the dlc costs nearly 20% of the price in some cases, for a singular cabinet. Ridiculous considering the number that come with.)Its really good, but if you are spending every second you can doing the laundry you are going to find the game extremely tedious, its boring cause you aren't supposed to do it more than a few times, and its not even that profitable once you have a few machines and you have done some goals,How about try this... imagine you had a room full of fun arcade machines, and a few baskets of laundry that literally no one actually cared if you did. Would you do the laundry then? Only if you were out of your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Good stuff - Not perfect - room for improvementThe gameplay loop turns into a incremental progression game quickly, which some people love and some hate.I'm on the side that likes it, but i wasn't expecting it from the start, imagined the game would have more with managing the arcade.As it stands, the first week you spend mostly doing laundry work and cleaning while sneaking in a few arcade games here and there.From the 2nd week you probably have enough arcade machines to turn a profit only with cleaning up the place and making certain machines popular. During this time you've also probably unlocked upgrades to purchase both for your arcade and for yourself and can set some daily goals for yourself.The highlight of the experience are the playable arcade games, at which you'll need to get good at in order to actually raise their popularity. This might annoy people who are strictly into the management aspect and weren't ready for leveling up their arcade skills IRL.Issues:My biggest gripe is that there are random bugs like unable to pick up certain pieces of trash, like crushed cans on a windowsill. Or in my personal case, playing on the SteamDeck, it says it's verified.. and sure. It runs well, however it's in 720p and the interface elements such as the laundry pop-up or the text when you get the tutorials go outside the screen you can only see half of them. The game offers no option to resize or reposition the UI.I've even tried outside of the game to force it to run in 1080p, hoping to downscale the rendering in-game. However when launching the game it's still running in 720p and i don't have an option to change that.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: In a market of tons of "____ Flipper" games, this one really stands out and expresses itself differently. The aspect of having full playable minigames inside of the game each with full save capabilities is awesome. Thoroughly recommend this game to people who love old retro arcade games and ignoring doing the laundry.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of retro games. Just the collection of retro inspired games alone makes this game shine and well worth the money. With the 90's style arcade/laundromat management added it really brings the atmosphere to life. Are there bugs? Sure, but most of them are fairly minor which can't be said for most AAA titles at launch that go for 3 times the price.The majority of the arcade games have a leader board and some of the games have a saved progressions system so I can see myself coming back to this game for a while. I still have a lot more mileage for the sim side of the game but I am already hoping for some additional DLC that adds more games, features, and possible customization options.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Basically you run an arcade, but instead of a high focus on management its more of a collection of period accurate inspired games that you can dunk on whenever you want. There's challenges associated with them which increases your arcade's popularity, which gives you more money, which means you can get more games. Now you start out very humbly with mostly a laundry mat and some arcade machines. I'm telling you now doing laundry after a certain point is a waste of time. You gain more popularity the more you yourself play the machines, which again gives you more money, way more money than a full day of focusing laundry. Don't be the laundry guy. I'm number 12 on Space Race Simulator, and i'm proud of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: You'll see alot of people here complaining about the laundry being boring and the loops being uninteresting.  This game does hold your hand a little tightly as you progress and there is a point where the laundry gets annoying.  Play through that, you'll thank me later.  It doesn't take that long (~6 hours) to get to a point where you make more money from the arcade than from the laundry and then you can safely ignore the laundry part.  This game is about a collection of mini games and playing through those to make your machines more valuable and get more machines and more games.  Its a blast.  Its not perfect but they did a great job rebuilding the great games of the 80's and 90's without flat out copying them.  I highly recommend you ignore the nay sayers and give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how 30 hours of my life pasted by playing this, but here we are. I have seen the credits, bought all the machines, played for several in game days afterwards to work on goals and layouts, earning around $12,000 a day and right before this review I even unlocked the 60 goals achievement which is only .1% of people have.This one is a slow burn, it takes a while before you're able to focus more on the arcade games then on the laundry but I don't think it's a bad thing. Didn't take me to long before I had more machines, was making more money and I averaged around ether buying one new machine or upgrade every day with a couple of the later ones needing two.I didn't grow up with arcade games and more used to modern ones, but most of these were fun enough to sit and play though to unlock one or two goals for extra profit, however a few of the them like Gold Strikers, required way to much of your time for game play that wasn't all that fun if I'm being honest. The other one that didn't so much have bad goals but was just unfun or to complex to play for me was Blockchain, which is a shame seeing how it's mentioned more than any other game in emails, I just didn't get it but puzzle games are my weakness so don't take that to serious.My biggest complaints have to be with the controls for some of the games. your PDA and computer are hard to use with just a mouse (thankfully WASD work well enough but some issues with scrolling still happen in all the windows), and the games like darts and table football or nearly impossible to play and I just left them alone after a few trys. Outside of a few games glitching and being unable to work, those were fixed with a restart. The third level of Frogger games is entirely broken and lets you walk on the water, that's the biggest bug and it's a useful one so at least it didn't ruin the game.I should also mention that the daily quests you get don't reward nearly enough currency, and have you going back to play the same games over and over again even ones you have all the goals finished for. Even a good five or six days after the credits the only upgrades I've managed to afford are the shoes, glasses, bigger trash bags, and less broken systems, and I'm one hundred more off getting the assistant because a lot of my games max out a couple times a day making me stop to empty everything single game out. If anything needed to be overhauled it would need to be this system, make it give more points and have it be smarter about making you play games you are still trying to get goals for, so you don't feel like your time is wasted playing a game for ten mins that you already have maxed out just for ten points of currency when you need three hundred for an upgrade.Still happy I played it, would recommend to anyone that isn't afraid of a grind.85/100 and can easily be a 95/100 with some bug fixes and a better upgrade system.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly did not think i would like this game as much as I do. What I saw on the steam page looked like a collection of bootleg arcade games but later it popped in my feed again and figured id give it a try. Overall the games are tons of fun, not all ofcourse because they cover a very wide range of arcade game and some are not to my liking but overall tons of fun and tons of selection. The game does have a few bugs that still need to be worked out such as some of the items of trash are impossible to grab, the coin hopper is sometimes hard to access to empty, and one day my car just dissapeared. Some points of the game can feel rather grindy like the upgrade system, but all in all very great game. Highly recommend the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: As well as being a love letter to the 1990s arcade, Arcade Paradise is a game about work-life balance, and also the balance between different kinds of work: the work you do to survive, and the work you do for love. Like all management games, it’s inherently about capitalism, but in a way that’s both pricklier and gentler than the satirical, be-the-machine emptiness of clicker games like Vostok Inc. This one’s about how to live within the system, and how to use it to build something beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Great game just needs a few adjustments and bit of extra content. The wash cycle and dry cycle is too short and doesnt pay enough. Extend the timer so i can play the games more than 2 mins at a time, some of the to do list challenges means i have to neglect the laundromat and lose nearly all the cash bonus. There should be some extra steps to some of the cleaning jobs; like make me use a dry cleaner of stain remover or something to freshen up the constant loop that doesnt change from the very beginning of the game. There is no customisation, seriously? let me renovate the laundromat with better machines and choose the style and theme of my arcade please. This is my biggest gripe right now and makes the game a little disappointing at the moment.The game is good and i do recommend it but it just needs that extra bit of spice to make this good game into a great one.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: YES AND NO! It takes a real grind of non stop doing laundry to buy anything. Needs more customization of laundry mat to make that part of the game interesting, lets be able to change the floor, walls, upgrade washers and dryers. Also we should be able to customize the arcade room more, not just have what you buy and thats it. The game has a very empty feeling, NPC's kept glitching into pixels when getting closer.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game, you spend your day doing menial tasks that don't take much energy, you have time to play & order random arcade games, and other humans disintegrate into polygons when you approach them. Your only social interactions are via phone messages & instant messenger.This isn't an Arcade Paradise. It's an Optimal Introvert Workplace Paradise. Hiring managers, take note.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this so far, although from a management sim perspective making money is ridiculously easy, but there is still plenty of fun to be had.It's really nice to use my GCOM Arcade Stick with this game, only a bare minimum of keybinding configuration was needed and except for the 'enter' key which I have been unable to figure out how to re-bind it was all handled from the in game options. What I was particularly pleased with is that the Arcade Stick works great for the FPS elements of the game (in combo with the mouse) as well as for the arcade gameplay which feel far more authentic with the stick.The in game graphics are nice, and there are some good retro touches. I will update this review later after a few more hours gameplay but so far it's good fun and well worth the £15 price tag
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for a while now, strangely for the reason that I used to work in a launderette which also had arcade cabs back in the mid 80's :-) I have to say this really does bring it all back to me as I also used to help the owner in deciding what cabs to get! Nostalgia is a wonderful thing!As for the game, I love it, it runs perfectly, controls are good both joypad and Keyboard/Mouse, graphics are ok, no ray-tracing here :-) but they have that 90's feel, and suit the game perfectly.I can't wait to get my launderette upgraded to a shiny arcade...Well done devs on giving us retro gamers a sim game that seriously does take you back to those days.Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: I've only put in a little over an hour at the time of this review but what I've played I really enjoyed. Most of the reviews talked about what the game is. If you grew up in the 80s/90s, I think you'd appreciate this more than it just being an arcade management sim genre. Reminds me of being in Clerks like Randall at the video store, ignoring responsibility to play games instead of watching movies. This game just hits all the right nostalgia and game play notes for me. The arcade games I have played are all well made too and worth taking time to enjoy them.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Basic first-person arcade management simulator. Think of it like the game ThrillVille, where the games you put down are actually playable. Story's pretty much teaching a teenager responsibility, which feels right for a management sim. Games within are primarily akin to other real-world games of the 80s and 90s era. Leaderboards, at least for the first half of the game, currently consists of scores made during the closed beta; some might be unreachable, however aren't hacked. On Steam Deck, it's fully playable, but you might have UI scaling issues, so it's advisable to set the resolution back to 720p before transferring the save to the Deck. Favorite Games: Blockchain, Gravichase, Vostok93.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly 5 hours put into my first play-through and I must say, this game is absolutely amazing and very polished for an EA title. From the 80's/90's themed soundtrack, to the nostalgic adventure of growing up going to a laundromat to play an arcade game... I can tell you right now that I'm not going to get enough of this game. With over 35 arcade games to collect (I've only played 6 of them so far) you'll not want to stop until you play them all (my favorite so far is Zombat 2). There's also so many upgrades not only for you as a character, but for your machines and the laundromat. They also split up the in-game currency between what you earn running the laundromat and what you earn playing the arcade machines through "daily tasks" (in-game days). the money you earn running the laundromat is used to purchase more machines and the money you earn from completing dailies are used to upgrade your gear, hire help, and run ad campaigns for your arcade which in turn brings you more money.... I could go on and on.... WITH JUST 5 hours played! Sheesh!The developers are also super awesome and friendly on their discord and has made their launch very smooth with instant feedback and info! As if you find any bugs or just want to throw out a suggestion they're there to take it in and respond.Listen if you're a sucker for nostalgia, you like synths and arcades, and you've always wanted to own and manage laundromat/arcade combo... GET THIS!!! The $20 is well worth the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

_childDocuments_.review:
Welcome to Arcade Paradise, the 90's-fuelled retro arcade adventure. Rather than washing rags for a living, you decide to turn the family laundromat into the ultimate arcade. Play, profit and purchase new arcade machines, with over 35 to choose from, to build your very own Arcade Paradise!

Take the laundromat business made up of dull chores from washing clothes to throwing out the trash, and turn it into a booming arcade with the coolest games in town raking in all the money!

Over 35 arcade games, each fully realized with its own gameplay, stories, missions and high scores to set! Inspired by 3 decades of gaming, from early vector games right up to the 32-bit era.

Insert a second coin and play against a friend in a number of co-operative & competitive arcade games up to 4 players locally.
_childDocuments_.name: Arcade Paradise

name: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus!
detailed_description: Enter the #1 Psychological Horror Experience! Welcome to a terrifying world of poetry and romance! Write poems for your crush and erase any mistakes along the way to ensure your perfect ending. Now’s your chance to discover why DDLC is one of the most beloved psychological horror games of the decade! You play as the main character, who reluctantly joins the Literature Club in search of a romantic interest. With every poem you write and every choice you make, you’ll charm your crush and begin to unfold the horrors of school romance. Do you have what it takes to crack the code of dating sims and get the perfect ending? Now, the original mind-shattering DDLC experience is packed with tons of new features and content exclusive to Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! Doki Doki Literature Club Plus Features: 6 new Side Stories about friendship and literature, totaling hours of new content 100+ unlockable images including new game art, wallpapers, never-before-seen concept sketches, and more 26 total music tracks, including 13 all-new unlockable songs by Nikki Kaelar, plus special guests Jason Hayes and Azuria Sky A built-in DDLC music player to unwind with your favorite songs in a custom playlist, or loop a single track forever A high-fidelity visual upgrade with all artwork now in Full HD (1080p) Meet the Literature Club! Sayori – Sayori, your childhood friend, begins your story by recruiting you to the Literature Club! As a daydreamer full of positive energy, Sayori’s greatest passion is to deliver happiness to others. Natsuki – Natsuki tries to act tough, but her cuteness can make it hard to take her too seriously! She might be willing to warm up to good listeners who can respect her love for cute things. Yuri – Yuri, the quiet bookworm, reserves her passionate side for those who can more deeply understand her enigmatic mind. Monika – Monika, the superstar President of the Literature Club, will keep you on track for a perfect ending. Monika is always there to give you a guiding hand, both in literature and in love! This game is not suitable for children or those who are easily disturbed.

_childDocuments_.review: About 20 minutes ago, I finally achieved 100% completion on this game and i am still grinning. DDLC has been such a major part of my life since it was first released for free in 2017, and then when plus was released in 2021, and to finally be able to say that I have gotten the achievement that only 8.7% of players have is such an amazing feeling. Thank you DDLC for raising me, this game will always have a special place in my heart

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so freaking awesome, if you've played the original and liked the characters and want to get to know them better and see them interact with each other more than I highly recommend playing the side stories in this game. The side stories feel meaningful and don't drag on at all. Doki Doki Plus doesn't at a whole lot on the horror side of things but does present you with a little mystery which is quite fun to unravel. It also comes with a lot of options to customise your Virtual Computer ( your PC in game) like a bunch of really cute wallpapers and promo art. This game gave me another excuse to replay doki doki literature club and I had a blast with it. With all the bonus content, artwork and even some new music tracks this game feels like a love letter to Doki Doki Literature Club, and I wouldn't have it any other way.

_childDocuments_.review: Its very hard to write a review for plus, without it going one of two ways:1. You just review the original game2. You just review the new contentI think its easiest just to tell you to download the original free version, play it, and ask yourself "do I want to pay $15 for a slightly shiner version of what I just played, and a few hours of extra side content?"If yes, get Plus, while OG story has zero changes (beyond 1 missing easter egg) the new VM interface, its side stories, and brand new secrets are a treat for fans of the game.If not, Plus is just gonna leave you feeling like you wasted your money on a game you could have just played for free.I really loved OG and I felt the $15 was worth it, this is only a recommendation to fans of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really think it's worth $14.99, but there are some cool new additions.The biggest thing that was added was the virtual desktop. This was made just for the people who play with gamepads or on console. When I first played the game, I had no clue that this existed.  Oh yeah, all of the new bonus content is on the virtual desktop, including the 6 new unlockable stories, soundtrack, and bonus gallery (of which you can set as your virtual desktop wallpaper).The base game remains mostly the same with a few minor changes in dialogue and extra moments.  Depending on who you write poems for in the base game, you can unlock 2 out of the 6 bonus side stories, mostly revolving around one of the girls. These feature cool new art and music and they tell the backstory on how the literature club was formed. I found these stories to be sorta dull and oddly paced, but at least you can gawk at the amazing new art for it. The music player is your standard old music player. You can add tracks that you heard from playing the game into a playlist. I'll probably never use this but it's a neat feature, nonetheless. And the bonus gallery contains backgrounds, images from the game, wallpapers, poems, miscellaneous art and even concept art. You have to unlock these by going down certain paths and doing certain tasks in both the main game and the bonus side stories.The achievements in this game aren't really that difficult to get. So, If you're a completionist or an achievement hunter...good on you, I guess.If you want to see the cool new art and see how the literature club was formed, then yeah this game is worth a purchase. But if you just want to experience Doki Doki in it's raw form, then I suggest playing the free version and try it out for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of meta-fiction, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus gets my seal of approval. It adds more content and secrets than found in the original game, and I was especially a fan of all the side stories which I found very relatable to me. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah I paid money for a game that is free in reality and has the same features. But do I care? No. I believe when a team of passionate developers pour their hearts and soul on a super quality game that sticks with you for years and years and years, the least I could do is give 14 bucks for such a well delivered project, despite the fact that this game was literally EVERYWHERE on the internet. This game BROKE THE INTERNET! And it's still going on for over 7 years. Countless viewers on YT I think at this point 100M+ views on popular YTers video, it just has to be, hundreds of mods, countless of fandoms and beautiful artworks, HELL EVEN MY BEST FRIEND WHO WASN'T A GAMER BY ANY STRETCH OF THE IMAGINATION JUST RANDOMLY PLAYED IT WHEN IT FIRST RELEASED, and of course he loved it. I tried to avoid playing this game for so long because unfortunately I did get spoiled thanks to youtubers thus ruined my immersion but without them, the game wouldn't be as godly popular as it is and I'm so glad we've walked upon this path. And weirdly enough I rarely ever play indie games, and when I do it would be the best of the best, and this game barely even has any gameplay mechanics. That should speaks volume. And thus, this game remains in my top favorites, I can even go as far as to say this game has more of a "voice" you could say and a soul unlike soooo many Triple A games nowadays. This game is so accessible to almost virtually everybody on this planet, that in a way it brings everyone together. If you told your friends about this, they'll instantly get hooked. After that, you'll have plenty of new conversations and thoughts brought from this game. This game questions reality, it is very thought-provoking, it brings new topics of discussions about psychologies and among other things.So what else did I love about this game? I did say I was spoiled, but I'd lie if I said this game didnt' scare me in the slightest, because there are times where I didn't look at the screen and lowered the games' volume.The poems is incredibly well written.You can't talk about DDLC without bringing up the instantly recognizable music, of course!The bright, colorful cast of characters, each of their own unique personalities as well as their thought process, and their determinations. Hell, even the faceless main character is so likeable and has his own interesting set of thoughts and dialogues. That is, before the cast turn to something completely different the more you play.The meta, the fourth wall breaking, the fact that you can delete files in the game to see how things play out is incredible and something I didn't even know that's possible.The clever script and masterful writing. I was shocked how things turned upside down after the second act, and it only gets more insane from there. You would recognize that the MC is slowly losing response and awareness the more you stick around and that horrific scene, and that's for a reason in the ending, and that is one of the most memorable things that just glued into my brain.The unique illustrations is an absolutely beautiful, even masterful at times. Sometiems I find myself dazzed just by looking at the backgrounds.Together with all of this you create an emotional roller coaster of a game, exceptional story telling, everything that I said so far you'll NEVER FORGET because this game surely did impacted me for better or... worse! Thank you Team Salvato. Thank you Dan Salvato. Thank you Doki Doki Literature Club!

_childDocuments_.review: "Yeah its pretty good." - Me, Oct 24, 2017 for DDLC (My first review on Steam)And it still is. The new stuff added is great, the new music especially, and the side stories serve well as bonus content that isn't there for the normal game. Compared to the original version on Steam back in 2017, this is basically the game in a professional suit, looking snazzy for a job interview. It feels like a full on game that could (and should) be released on consoles. But that's where I feel it took a bit of a weird issue for me.Yes, you can't mess with game files in this one like you could in the original release. Sure, means it can be put on consoles and is more accessible, but certain "easter eggs" you cant do until either 1) you finish the game or 2) not at all (like looking at the character files in a hex editor and whatever) but I feel its kind of pointless to argue about that kind of stuff.DDLC is also those kinds of games where you cant exactly "re-release it" and have it have the same effect since "if you've played it once, there's no reason to play it again," but the long period of time that passed between the original release and this one helps a bit with that, plus there's the Side Stories and the new music as extra goodies.Personally, I think the original, 2017 release is a better option on PC just cuz... you can do all the crap you could want to on it. and its free, as well. Doesn't mean this release is *bad,* cuz the extra content is great. But if you somehow are playing it for the first time, the original release might be better. Monika: After Story is also a really cool mod to check out if you care, too. It's a bit weird, but if you wanna hang out with Monika way more then go right ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just on my second playthrough of this game (my first being on PlayStation when it launched), and the sheer amount of emotions this game still gives me after first seeing it almost five years ago is both commendable and incredibly hard to believe. Laughing at this game's cuter dialogue for one moment and still managing to tear up during scenes I've seen at least 50 times just a second later is exactly what I love about this game. Seeing the sheer amount of lines that foreshadow the future events of this game is also fun and spine chilling.Sayori herself is such an immense bundle of joy, which makes her all the more pitiable, relatable, and lovable character when you see her struggles. She genuinely feels like a real person to me at times. Her tale was one I desperately needed to hear and learn from, so even to this day I look at her way more fondly than any person should about a fictional character.The poems are also a very pleasant an inspiring read. They do a very fantastic job of alluding to the later acts without making their contents too obvious just as the usual dialogue does, but even detaching them from the game entirely they have some incredibly neat symbolism. The poem "Bottles" in particular still floods me with emotion ever time I read it.This is simply my favorite game ever made. I wouldn't go as far to say it saved my life, but it greatly changed my world view and I genuinely believe it's made me a better person. Reading the poems also really inspired me to tap into literature as a hobby, and maybe eventually a career? I hope so.I know a completely spoiler free playthrough of this game is nearly impossible, but if you're one of the lucky few to get that experience, I couldn't recommend it enough. You're strapping yourself in for a wild ride of emotions, and quite possibly one of the greatest visual novels ever made.I hope to see you at the literature club!Sayonara~

_childDocuments_.review: Depending on your current mental health status, the main game can either be thrilling and fun with its scares, or genuinely disturbing and uncomfortable. I'm in a very good mental state right now so I found the game delightfully evil (but still shocking at parts), but if I played this a few years earlier I might not have been able to handle it. Think very carefully before playing this and look up the content warnings to see if the game is safe for you to play, especially since there are two onscreen suicides, one of which requires you to not skip over for 100% completion. With that out of the way, is Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! worth buying? In my opinion, yes. The main game is great, of course, but the side stories are genuinely wholesome, with important messages on friendship and supporting those with mental health problems. It also makes the whole game more tragic and engaging; these are girls who did have a genuine friendship that got torn apart as soon as  entered the picture. This is a game that will affect you long after you played it, and has become one of my ultimate faves.

_childDocuments_.review: Expanded upgrade of the free version and it is absolutely worth your money.+ Decent art+ Great price for the quality+ Fresh approach to the genre- Some fonts can be difficult to read - Occasionally hard to tell who is talking- Can't take screenshots without text box- New UI system somewhat ruins part of the experience ☆★★★★★★★★★ 9/10 – GreatI played the original free version and I loved it. All my praises remain the same, I won't just copypaste all of that but if anyone is interested, my original review can be seen here: Back then I was (and I guess I still am) astounded by DDLC being such a high quality work despite being free, and when I learned of Plus being released, I had no problem paying for it when I knew it would be great quality. I must note that I purchased this back in July 2021 and then shamefully just let it sit in my backlog for ages due to being busy.I struggled a bit with thinking how I'd talk about Plus, as it's not a remake/reboot of the free game but just an expanded version. The devs themselves seem to be gearing Plus toward returning players rather than wanting to keep it fresh, considering that the menu of the game pretty much spoils a gameplay element immediately for you. Even so I would like to keep my text as spoiler-free as possible since there are still completely new people finding this game and I firmly believe DDLC is best experienced when you know as little about its story as possible. The visuals have been upgraded to be in full HD, but the art itself remains the same (no character designs/poses have been changed, the backgrounds are the same, etc), so I honestly don't see a reason why Plus couldn't be listed as a DLC expansion to the free game. Perhaps there are differences in the more technical side of the game/its files that required Plus to be its own product in the Store, but it just strikes me as odd. If that had been an expansion DLC under the original game, then returning players could've purchased it and immediately jumped into the new content instead of being required to replay the entire story. It's not exactly a huge bother, but it just occurred to me as I was going through the motions of the slow first hour and half of the game, during which I could not skip dialogue as according to Plus I'm playing for the first time. In any case, to anyone wanting to get into DDLC I would suggest for them to simply buy Plus to get into the full experience immediately rather than play the free version to its fullest.As mentioned above, I feel that the new UI somewhat ruins the gameplay element, but again, Plus is clearly geared toward people who have already played it before. I'm a bit torn on the UI, it feels immersion breaking and I personally didn't enjoy  The only positive side to the UI would be that it makes some parts of the late stage story easier for people to proceed with. It wasn't exactly difficult in the free version, but it was a bit tedious, and I can certainly understand some players would just think the game was over before it actually was.Speaking of, the story has stayed the same in Plus but with few expanded scenes. The story was excellent when it was new and it remains excellent now, the characters are engaging and it's a fun read. The plot takes quite a while to kick off in its fullest, which might annoy some people but I enjoy the thorough character building before the actual plot takes over – it really let's you get to know the characters. Some might also complain that the game gives you a trigger warning about some of its contents, but I consider it a good thing. It may spoil a little bit, but it's better option than just blindly punching someone who may have thought they were getting a very standard VN.I've seen some people lament the fact that even despite a Plus version, there still is no option to pick your main character's gender. I can understand the disappointment and I always welcome games including the option to choose which one you'd want to be, but I personally am not upset Plus didn't have it. This is simply because the story (or specifically one character in it) requires for you to be playing as a guy in order for her story to work – . If you could play as a girl, then this character's entire attitude and her whole story arc would've needed adjustment and it would not have been the same.Plus also comes with six side stories, which are standalone pieces focused entirely on the relationships the girls have which each other. Together they provide a lovely insight to their characters and the length of side stories is more than expected, making the stories a very welcome surprise. On the other than great deal of the side story content seemed to be focused on just the relationship between two characters, so it felt unfair they got so much extra screentime while the other two got little less focus to them. Some of the moments also became borderline preachy in how syrupy the girls' dialogues were to one another, but overall the side stories were still welcome addition.I guess Plus did disappoint me a bit since the same problems that I had in the original are still present and there's one major new issue as well. The five characters still all have the same speaking font/color, making it easy to lose track of who said what – specially in scenes with more than two characters interacting with the player. Many visual novels avoid this issue by assigning unique dialogue box colors for its main characters or other ways to highlight who is talking. There also still isn't any “easy text” function that you could use to help you read the poems (meaning the ones you are actually supposed to be able to read) made by the girls with really ornate handwriting styles. Seeing both of these still exist in the upgraded version did annoy me more than when I was first faced with them in the original game. Additionally Plus has a really, really infuriating problem that you can't take screenshots without the dialogue box/user interface. You are able to hide the UI with mouse 2, however the press of any button at all will bring the UI back immediately – meaning that you pressing your designated screenshot button makes the UI pop back and ruin the shot. This is such poorly implemented thing that it genuinely did get me a little more mad than I have any sensible reason to be over visual novel screenshots. You can later view unlocked scene artworks in the gallery without the UI, however taking a screenshot in there will immediately minimize the picture. It's just a mess. Some people have found workarounds, but this really shouldn't be necessary and that's why I'm complaining about it.In my mind I had already deducted one star from my rating for Plus because of the screenshot issue, but ultimately the bonus episodes earned that star right back so that's why my score is the exact same as it was for the free one even though I seem to be complaining about this one much more. Still absolutely more than worth the base price and I'm happy to have paid it because they really did create a great visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: So, let me get the obvious complaint out of the way first. (SPOILERS!) Because this game was for the Switch and other consoles the file deleting gimmick doesn't work anymore. Also, this is a way to sell the game with more content to justify a price which I think is a really nice way to go about it. It's not too expensive either. I loved the expansion to the characters and it made them feel like more than tropes. Not only that but it makes you realise how much the events of the game affects the girls and their relationships with each other and not just the player. I like that approach, it's fresh but remains faithful to the characters. I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate to give a negative review because the main game is absolutely brilliant, but you can get that for free. If I'm just rating the Plus features, then it's a no from me.DDLC is known for being a psychological horror, but you won't find any of that in the side stories. I found the first part of the main game, before you get into the "real game," to be painfully boring, however well-written it may be. I loved it once it got good. The side stories just feel like more of the boring stuff I waded through at the beginning because I knew things were going to get good... except that this time, they never "got good."It seems like a lot of people like the side stories, so... if you like the first part of the main game before all the psychological horror elements, I guess you may like them. If not, they may not be your thing.To be fair, I never really cared about the side stories in the first place. I only bought DDLC Plus because I wanted the game in other languages, so I don't regret the purchase. But I imagine most people are buying it for the side stories, so that's the perspective I'm writing this review from.

_childDocuments_.review: Doki Doki Literature Club is an absolutely incredible experience. It's well-written, it's terrifying and unsettling, the meta level of narration is extremely unique and fun to watch, and it's all wrapped up to look like a cute anime girl dating sim, (this isn't necessarily a plus, but it's not a minus). There are a lot of different themes present in the story, and it does a good job in getting you invested in its host of characters before slowly devolving into its horrific final form.Initially, it starts as you'd expect an anime dating game to start: you're the boy next door, your childhood best friend is walking with you to school, and you join an extracurricular club together, where you meet new people and make new friends, getting to woo the lady of your choice via the poems you write. DDLC does a great job in placing you in that environment and slowly introduces each character to you through dialogue and your assignments. You start to feel comfortable in this new clique you've found, and probably develop some favorites as well.As time goes on, your relationships with the club deepen, and you start getting a little more into the romance side of things. Your focus starts to shift between club activities and extracurricular time spent with your favorite member. Just as you start to form a more intimate connection, the game is instantly flipped upside down by *that* famous scene, and just like that, you and the main character are both cursing yourself. If only you could be given another chance...It's on this second chance that you really start getting messed with, and DDLC introduces scare tactics that are seemingly unintended upon your first play, maybe a corrupted file, a visual glitch, etc. and you question where it's going with this. As you play longer and longer, you experience more of this, realizing it's not a mistake, and your unease builds as you start to notice tension/misgivings in the group. There's a strong feeling that something is wrong, but you keep playing, hoping to push past it and maybe fix everybody's problems.I think Team Salvato did an amazing job in evoking all of these different emotions; they chose the weirdest avenue possible in order to subvert expectations and ended up with a one-of-a-kind game that is put on a pedestal as one of the best horror games to date. On top of that, this entire original game is free; the Plus version released afterwards, adding side stories, higher native resolution, and behind the scenes extras. Plus is definitely worth the pickup for the simple fact that the game deserves your money, but also all of the added extras are icing on the cake to an already great experience.Cinematic playthrough here:

_childDocuments_.review: I'm conflicted about this game, as a huge fan of the original.This re-release has ZERO new horror content, nothing, nada. The new secrets added are pretty lame too, there was a lot of potential in a virtual computer setup but it all went pretty underutilized. However, the Side Stories are EXTREMELY good, they are essentially a full-on 6-hour prequel to the original, with the cute visual novel aspect played completely straight.I loved the original DDLC for its mix of cute well-written characters, horror and meta content. Those were the THREE things that I loved about it. But for the new release, only the first aspect was expanded on, which is disappointing overall for a "Plus" version of a game, especially for 15 bucks.The ending of the Side Stories left me pretty satisfied though. The writing is wonderful, heartwarming and extremely cathartic, especially for characters I've wanted to see more of for a LONG time. They are arguably better than the original game. "Trust" and "Self-Love" are particularly great, cant recommend them enough.Overall, $15 is probably too much and set my expectations way too high for this game. Personally I would've just released the Side Stories as DLC for the original at around $6-10 max.If you buy this, only do it for the cute dokis and not for anything else. Buy it full price if you are a fan of the characters, if not, maybe wait for a discount.Sayori is best.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic psychological horror game! The horror in this game really hits hard as the build up is done excellently and really effectively. _childDocuments_.review: A new operating system is introduced within the game (virtual machine). This system allows you to launch DDLC, and the main storyline remains largely unchanged from the original version. Additional content such as new CGs, side stories, and songs are included within the virtual machine. However, these additions do not significantly contribute to the main storyline. The entirety of the story takes place within this virtual environment instead of directly on your PC. Consequently, when deleting "*.chr" files, you no longer need to navigate through your local computer files; instead, you interact with files within the virtual system. This alteration somewhat diminishes the immersion and sense of reality. Therefore, while DDLC remains an excellent game, DDLC Plus falls short of expectations.Somewhat disappointing.Most positive reviews seem to come from fans. If you haven't played it yet, consider trying the free version of DDLC for a potentially better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much to say, the good old DDLC stayed the same in this Plus! editionThe Side Stories were a really nice expansion, they added a new layer of personality to each Doki, to the point where when you replay the vanilla game you can feel the difference within the characters themselves and it's great. Sure, the stories themselves felt a bit rushed but they were straight to the point nonetheless and really enjoyable alongside the new, lovely soundtracks and CGs. While it's a bit sad that the file manipulation part is now virtualized and not real like it was in the og game (in order to respect console users), the expanded lore built around it, with multi universe, virtual machines, sentient ai etc. was really clever, well thought and intriguing to unlock and discover, really enjoyed every bit of the data collection (also, that teaser for Project Libitina right there c: )Though, the Italian translation needs a revision, there are quite a few errors here and there that ruins the immersion a bit sometimes9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A bittersweet (As Sayori would say.) story taking place in a high school literature club. I am glad I avoided any and all spoilers about this game in the four years it's been out because my experience would have been hindered by the knowledge of what's to come in the story. If it's your first time playing Doki Doki, please do not look anything up about it and just play it. Now, if you've already played DDLC, the plus version adds in a few heartwarming "prequel" side stories that show how all the girls met and became friends with another. So, if you played the original game, there's still something new for you to experience in the plus version.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely think that DDLC+ has caused me to gain more humanity. On the surface, it seems like every other remaster in that it only features some bells and whistles while also adding things to make it compliant with consoles as opposed to just being a PC release so it features a virtual desktop where you can mess with files and such there. What it also features is a mail system where you receive emails from various fictional characters who seem to be the ones who created this virtual desktop (called the Metaverse) and they speak about the game and the characters within DDLC in a very cold, clinical manner, less like people and more like subjects. This leads into a piece of lore that says the DDLC game is itself a virtual simulation as well as the unlockable side stories being a different one, but all this did was convince me that these characters are real people who are stuck in a situation that they don't deserve to be in. Seeing Sayori struggle with much more realistic depictions of suicidal depression, Monika trying to not let herself get too full of herself as the club president, Yuri attempting to actually make friends while struggling with intrusive thoughts, and Natsuki struggling with an inferiority complex which manifests in a confrontational attitude which is spurred on by some really toxic friends, seeing all of this makes playing through the game just to unlock pictures, wallpapers, and other unlockable goodies so much harder because I'm just a random person, an unknown entity that tears apart this group of friends by existing in a virtual space where they can only date me, and only 3/4 of them can.But it's why the Happy Ending hits so hard. It's Sayori taking control but thanking me for trying to give everyone a fair shot, spending time with everyone. She could see the power imbalance, as could Monikabut she could also see that I tried my best to spread myself to all of them, even if it was stressful and was initially rewarded with pain and heartbreak and terror. It's a genuine thank you for trying to keep some peace in the club because if I played normally, I would have torn these 4 friends apart.This game is really something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to preface. is a phenomenal game that is completely worth your time. It is a game that will leave a lasting impression on you long after its relatively short runtime finishes. I would wholeheartedly recommend the experience to anyone ever, if emphasizing a little  incessantly that it's best experienced blind.However, this is DDLC And given that you're reading a Steam review, that means you were more than likely planning to play this game on a computer. Therefore:While trying my absolute hardest to not spoil the experience, I will say that DDLC+ is, for the most part, the same game as the original with extra content. However, many of its changes, while unavoidable for a multi-platform game,  worsen the experience and rob the game of most of its impact, and the extra content, while nice, does not make up for it.If this were a review for a different console's version of the game, I would (begrudgingly) be more forgiving of it. However, you have the opportunity to go play the original  So I implore you. . It's literally free and it runs on all the same stuff Steam does. If you're determined to give money to the developers, you can buy this later or get the Fan Pack for the original.
