_childDocuments_.review: At this point we're far enough past the launch of the original game that saying this has horror elements isn't really a spoiler. Especially considering how explicit the game is about this on first boot now.DDLC+ is brilliant and I absolutely love it. The original game is fine, I like it more for what it tries to do than for the characters as each feels somewhat like a stereotype, not fully fleshed out. Also Yuri is the worst.The added content through this rerelease is great, each character gets one on one time with the other characters and due to taking place before the main game they talk about things that don't concern their deep love of the protagonist. Their feelings are explored, what makes them who they are and I felt things. One could even say I enjoy having games make me feel things, they even managed to make me not dislike Yuri anymore.DDLC+ is a game you should play, really. _childDocuments_.review: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus was released in 2021 as a console supported re-release of the game ‘Doki Doki Literature Club’ originally released in 2017. (This review will be a continuation of my last review on DDLC.)At first, when I purchased this game I thought it lacked content. It wasn't until I dug deeper into the array of additional easter eggs and images that I was proved wrong. If you are a fan of the first game and want to dig deeper into the lore then I would suggest you play this game.The game is now accessed through a simulated faux-desktop. At your desktop you have a number of options: files, wallpapers, mail, side stories, pictures and music. All of which are unlockable from playing the base game.The aim is for the player to gain as much ‘data’ as possible. By collecting all the data you will obtain all achievements. Along the way you unlock images, wallpapers and also the ‘Side Stories’ ; these are the most noticeable new element added to the game. The side stories reveal more about each of the four girls present in DDLC. There is a disclaimer however that the side stories are“not canon to the main story”. The email function explains the purpose of the game. We find out there is another name for the base game, which is VM1. We also learn that there is a VM2. If you thought VM1 had dark themes then VM2 will blow your mind. We learn that in VM1 the game creators have given Monika a heightened conscience to see how it affects the game and see how she reacts. This results in her deleting Sayori, Natsuki and Yuri out of jealousy. When you reset the game through the files function it says ‘Monitor_Kernal_Access] ’ which is how Monika got her name. Moni from ‘Monitor’ and the ka from ‘Kernel Access’ Monika. This also explains why her name is the only name in the game that doesn't sound japanese. An email titled ‘Issues caused by unprotected memory’ states that “My best guess is that memory being freed from VM2 isn't getting zeroed out, which technically gives VM1 access to it”. This means something horrific when you look deeper into the lore of VM2. Monika has memories of VM2 while being present in VM1. We get a picture that VM2 is some sort of cult-like reality where people are experimented on to find their “third eye potential”. People are theorizing that Sayori, Natsuki and Yuri are the ones being experimented on and Monika is a nurse in this reality, in VM2. Also it seems likely she will be called ‘Marla’ here as the email about VM2 aka ‘Project Libitina’ reads “Monitor Adjacent Runtime-Level Access” This would explain why monika asks for our help. At one point in the game she ends her poem with “delete her” she is making this in reference to Yuri who is becoming evermore unhinged by this point in the game. Then a box appears saying “please help me.” and we have no choice but to click ‘ok’. This could be in reference to many things but after the poem asking us for help with deleting Yuri I feel that's what it is referencing. I mentioned before why she might be deleting these characters files. I said she might be jealous, however with this new found information about VM2 it could change Monika’s ulterior motives entirely. Motives could be far removed from any jealous attack that the last game has given Monika a reputation for. We know that Monika is very smart and this is shown throughout the game; she writes in a mature way, she changes the game files of the game, and it is even theorized that Monika has found a way out of the game. We know she is able to access memories from VM2 and that could very well be why she wants these character files gone because she doesn't want to see any more harm coming to these three individuals, her friends. There is an email that reads “Monika’s meddling is less clumsy than we think” all I can say is that I don't think anyone should underestimate Monika. Monika knows not to speak about VM2 because in the third chapter of the game she begins to speak about the book Yuri was reading but then stops herself, as she knows better than talking about the book with us, as it is about the world of VM2. This reaffirms how clever she is. How she knows she is being watched. This also impacted her attitude when Yuri and Sayori died because she doesn't want the game makers to suspect anything. She wants them to believe she wants attention from us the player, Insead of what she really feels, that she doesn't want her friends to be experimented on. This game breathes new life and lore to a game that was released 4 years prior. I highly recommend it!  { Thanks for listening } <3

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game that is very well thought out and executed.  It is easy to judge a book by its cover. The allure of cute anime girls with promised psychological horror is attractive for weebs and horror fans alike. Both elements are what originally drew me to the base game. When ddlc+ was released I was delighted to learn that knew content was added to a game that I had previously enjoyed. Though it had been a while since I had played, I could only remember the main plot points. My second play-through of this was lacking compared to the first since the main story had not changed. But, I decided to dive deep and really read into the content more this time around. I've unlocked all of the poems and am I working on completing the last of the side stories with plans to 100% the game. I've sat rereading the same poems for over an hour. It is so satisfying to read more into the poems and try to understand what that character is trying to express and how they express it. A deeply satisfying experience for me. This has got me considering reading more poetry. While I overall do recommend this game for anyone who is looking into, I also understand that it isn't for everyone.In an unexpected place, where one searches for anime on the front cover and a horror synopsis on the back. A story of literature and self expression emerges out of the reach of anyone who judges a book by its cover and puts it down.

On the case of DDLC Plus! having enjoyed the base game as much as i did i absolutely LOVE this add-on, the side stories are so emotional and i feel every bit of what the characters feel from the pain to sorrow and the happiness that they conclude in, they are very well written stories and give you an understanding about the friendships between each character and how they came to understand each other. _childDocuments_.review: I was pretty late to the Doki Doki party and didn't play the game until the beginning of 2021. Shortly after completing the story, this version got announced so when I got around to playing this, I skipped through a lot of the main storyWith that being said, I view the main portion of this game to be its side stories, which make Doki Doki Plus a far more enjoyable experience for me personally. The original games story was fun and cool, but for me, that's all it was. Was just fun and cool. Plus however, brings a story that personally impacts me on levels that I never imagined it would. Feeling like every other line written in this game, I could relate to with what I'm currently going through in life. Feeling like Dan has secretly been watching how my lifes been playing out in the past year while writing this. Many times I almost cried, due to how impactful the story was.Trust was a story that started off fun and ended with me almost crying. Respect was a story that was filled to the brim with lines from Natsuki that sounded like the same ♥♥♥♥ I've been saying for the past year and Self-Love was the sweetest, most relatable side story in the game.Overall, a running theme in this game for me was relatablity, something that no game I've played has been able to pull off as greatly as Doki Doki Plus did. Doki Doki was a solid 7.5 from me, a pretty enjoyable experience that I didn't think I would have (visual novels aren't really my thing). But Doki Doki Plus is easily getting a 9/10, maybe even a 9.5, depending on how I'm feeling. I can see this game entering in my top 10 favorites of all time after some reflection.So to Dan, even though I was late to your game, thank you. Thank you for the emotional journey you brought me on.

I saw the happy doki doki game on the front page of the Steam Store. I was actually going to pass it by as just another visual novel I didn't care about when I noticed it had been tagged "psychological horror." I mentioned it to my boyfriend as I was finishing the purchase and installation, telling him about what I assumed it was and that I hoped it would be an entertaining time waster.I launched it and got into it. Despite the glaring warning screen, the game seemed really normal to the point that about halfway through the first "run," I was getting a little disappointed. It was well written and thoughtful and the characters were engaging. It didn't seem "so bad it's good" -- it just seemed "good." I immediately fell for Yuri and courted her with my magnificent, expired poetic license, choosing the the best words for my poems... "Suicide," "Lust," "Massacre," "Contamination," "Entropy." Wow. Why can't I fix this. Maybe it'll be okay.It was not okay.End.I noticed this wasn't the end of the game, but I needed to step away to settle down. This game is probably my favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played a quite a few games over the years, some great, some not, but there are a select few that for me have really scratched that itch, that leave me feeling really glad I played it. This is one of those games, a deceptively innocent façade, a seemingly simple before seen concept, and then before you know it, drops the act to really sell one hell of a unique narrative.Doki Doki Literature Club is deceptive in its storytelling, and for someone like me who loves a good story full mystery and secrets, it was right up my alley. Yet it was the way in which it presented this narrative that grappled my interest. The front of a seemingly innocent visual novel of romance was as far removed from its true intentions as it could have ever been, but it is the contrast between its disguise and actuality that make it work so well.The storytelling was only further fuelled by the meticulousness of the dialogue, the tone setting of the music or lack thereof in cases, and of course the beautiful artwork that didn’t hold back even when things got graphic.Beyond its artistry, there isn’t much else to it, game play mechanics are simple and the running time isn’t tens of hours, but that’s a good thing. It gives its focus where it needs to, it paces itself to hit all the right notes at all the right times. You can tell time and effort went into making it what it was, because there is no filler, there is no deviating from the main path, it is true to what it wants to be, and that is what makes it work so well.On a final note then, Doki Doki Literature Club is a diamond among coals, a small narrative journey that questions the morals, that leads you unknowingly into more than you came for. I can honestly say I enjoyed my time with it and I would give anything to have something like it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why I haven't reviewed this game yet but I will do it now. Spoilers for newcomers ahead!If you like the original game and want more story and post-game content, play this. It has a whole bunch of stuff that automatically makes this the definitive way to play the original game, while also providing the aforementioned new stuff.This new stuff consists of things like a music player, a whole gallery, customizable menu screen, and the main thing, which is the side stories.The side stories are the main thing that separate this and the original game, as they are totally new with custom music made for them. These side stories serve as an "what-if" Monika hadn't had her MONItor Kernal Access. These side stories really allow you to connect more with the characters in the game and allow you to see them when they aren't with the MC. They also have really good messages within them that can be applied to you're own life. However, I personally just like seeing the character being sweet with each other without having Monika tampering around. It's a nice refresher after you play the main game again.The main game is basically the same. You just play it normally and do you're thing again. If you are new, the basic gameplay is talking to the girls in the club, showing them you're poem, and designing a poem to their liking by choosing favorite words. The main thing to get from replaying it is the music in the music player and images that'll go in the gallery. Now, their is a personal problem I do have with how they added the original game. For some reason,they completely got rid of the whole thing that made the game interesting, being the fact that you have to check the files to see changes happen. In this version of the game, it instead creates a fake file folder for the game inside of the game itself. This, in all honesty, is kind of disappointing. It also kind of ruins the whole cool factor about the original game, that being the fact it would actually add files to you're PC. Not to mention the ending requires you in the original to delete Monika's file off you're PC, which is pretty cool. I can only assume the reason they removed files changing or needing to be removed outside of game was to either stick with the theme they had going for this DLC, or because of some sort of issue with doing file changes that caused them to not want to replicate it for the DLC. I do, however, still enjoy the game despite the unfortunate removal of those features.The additional content for this game is pretty nice and gives you the motive to replay the game multiple times to gather all of the images and tracks. Most of the stuff you get is things relating to characters, events, or places within the game. Some of these will include the CGs, backgrounds, concept art, and other cool developmental thingies. I do like one in particular as it finally reveals the appearance of an previously never seen character. I won't spoil as it'll ruin the surprise. Now, if I we're to say one semi-bad thing about these collectibles it's that some of them are EXTREMELY RNG. One of these in particular has a 1/64 chance of appearing at all. Luckily, I got this one on my first few tries so I didn't have to try it over and over. However, for someone else, this may take hundreds of times to get as it is completely up to RNG to decide whether you get it or not. The key I would like to tell you to getting these is to make sure to try everything! Don't leave any stones unturned. I also would recommend not just passing the music player off as a fun extra. It will come into play at some point. Just make sure to play all the songs you get for a bit.Overall, I really loved this game and I will definitely replay at some point in the future. It serves as a great DLC, and in my opinion, the definitive way to play the game today. If you don't wanna spend $15.00 for whatever reason, just go play the original. It's completely free to play on Steam and other platforms. The downsides to this game are the fact that it does that a while to get to the spooks, which may not be for some people. It's also a visual novel so you're going to have to read a lot of text. Theirs also the internal file system, which I personally don't like that much. And of course the RNG unlocks if you wanted to unlock everything. However, these issues aren't that game killing in my opinion and don't really matter if you're used to visual novels, or are just a casual player not looking for a 100%. Anyway, that's all I can think of writing so I'll be going. See ya'll later.And remember,It's Just Monika<3

_childDocuments_.review: So, to try to be a little more informative than most of the reviews here, this new version of DDLC is essentially the game exactly as it was, but put in a virtual desktop and with added side stories as their own, separate thing. If you were here for "the #1 horror experience" there isn't anything more for you if you already played the original.DDLC *PLUS* is really about the side stories, which are all very, VERY good.They're heartfelt, and come across as very genuine, personal interactions. Every club member gets their spotlight; they have their own struggles based on what you know of them from the main game; and the way they learn to work past them with each other, and how they learn to accept one another is...really great. Almost makes me sad this isn't a full fledged, traditional VN.(Also, the game is not that long, most of those hours were just listening to "Dear Sunshine" on loop.)
_childDocuments_.name: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus!

_childDocuments_.review: To me, what really sets DDLC+ aside from the original/free version is the addition of collectible items. I love DDLC in all its forms, but these really provide an incentive to explore every nook and cranny of the game; to replay until you've found experienced possible glitch or occurrence. $15 may seem steep to some, but the content explored both through the side stories as well as through the other items found on the virtual "desktop" the game takes place on makes it absolutely worth it for any player. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Depression jokes aside, this is one of the games that I think did the best jobs in effectively metaphysical 4th wall breaking, and emotional storytelling of various dark themes such as self harm, abuse, etc. in a way thats subtle enough to make the player at unease and not disrupt the flow of the game too much, and well written enough so that it translates perfectly in a unique, subverted visual novel-psychological horror experience to make the characters feel more 'real' and their interactions more meaningful; all of which surprised worked as well as it did.Still, don't play this game if you want second-hand depression. I made the mistake of playing this game when my mental health was at an all-time low.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I was going in blind, but I guess enough accidental cultural osmosis around the key moments slipped through that I was ready for a lot of the twists. So it's commendable how, with the crux of the game being around shocking the player with unexpected (and disturbing per the content warnings) events, I am still thinking about what Doki Doki Literature Club manages to do with its characters.Monika in particular is fascinating beyond the common place memes you'll see referencing this game. The remainder of the cast are delightful as well, designed so each player will probably develop their own favorite similar to actual dating sims. I think the Side Stories added to this paid-for version help even more, just extra context for the lives Sayori, Natsuki, Yuri, and Monika could have lived. There's a lot of comforting dialogue in there that hopefully other players can relate to, or use as guidance in their real life. Delightful stuff from Team Salvato, PM may have died for this but what a worthy cause.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game were a food, it would be a delicious blooming onion, fried golden brown but with a spot of rot at it's center. So many overlapping layers of complexity that 'meta' doesn't go far enough to explain the mind-trip it takes you on. And just when you think you've found the final layer, BOOM, more layers. As delightful as it is disturbing and unexpected. NOT for younger players or those who are easily upset by heavy topics. Go in blind and just play through once as you normally would and then look for help on the more hidden aspects of the game later if you need them. The only part I disliked was the RNG (random, low-probability events) needed to reach 100% completion, but even they weren't too terrible. A solid 9/10 for me. My only question is, when do we get the next installment...? My Third Eye is eager for more.

_childDocuments_.review: It's back! DDLC is back with everything that made it great in the first place and much more.This re-release of the original game offers the OG experience with full HD graphics and several quality of life improvements, namely the VM that allows you to reset the game at the click of a button instead of physically having to reinstall it on steam, localization in a lot of different languages, achievements (FINALLY!), a lot of collectibles and secrets, and a built in music player with old and new tracks alike. But where DDLC+ shines the most is in the side stories: 7 new storylines that take place in a different timeline and massively expand on the backgrounds and the personalities of the 4 protagonists. Just these side story alone are enough to warrant the price imo, they offer hours of amazingly written stories that make the girls truly feel like actual people, and deliver a lot of really powerful moments. On top of this, if you are anything like me and are a fan of what Salvato did with the first game; with the scavanger hunt for hints about Project Libitina: you are in luck, cause this game expands on that whole thing like CRAZY. Seriously, I don't want to spoil stuff but HOLY MOLY THERE IS A LOT. Honeslty for only 11 euros, this is a steal, the original game was already worth that pricetag and we got that for free, so... What are you waiting for? Go buy it! You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent psychological horror game. No jumpscares, no monsters, just f̶o̶u̶r̶ cute girls, just writing poems, Just ******.It takes a while to get to the horror parts of this game but I'd say that's what makes it good. It gives you time to be immersed just enough so that when things start to go sour it will hit you hard. The writing is excellent. Very subtle yet powerful. I don't know what else to say without going into spoilers... you don't have to like literature to enjoy this interactive horror story.  Happy thoughts.As for a comparison with the original version that came out a few years ago... There are a few side stories to enjoy, images and music to collect but the base story is pretty much the same. You also no longer need to dig around in the actual computer files. There is now a pretend Operating System when you "exit" the game. Makes it a bit easier for some less tech savvy players I suppose. That is also where you can access the extra content such as music, poems and images.TL;DR: New players, if you like interactive stories and crying then get this game. People that played the original: if you're a fan and you would like some side stories, wallpapers, poems etc, then you'll like this version.

_childDocuments_.review: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! is essentially an expanded version of the original game from 2017. It features the original five hour long visual novel, six new side stories totaling around three hours and some extra things like CG viewer and music player.The original VN is split to two acts with the first act being your generic dating sim and second taking a heavy focus on psychological horror. The first half is rather weak with its stereotypical characters, uninteresting setting and unexciting events. However it gets better and the second act still four years is later one of the best experiences I've had with videogames as a whole.The side stories take place before the events of the VN when Monika started the literature club and focusing on how the initial characters joined the club. In other words it gives context to the main story's beginning and more importantly depth to the characters, which is something the first act failed to do in my opinion. The side stories are definitely more interesting to read through than the first act, but if you were looking for more of the stuff featured on the 2nd act you will be disappointed.I would recommend this if you've already played through the original VN and are looking to get to better know the characters or just want to support Dan Salvato. If you haven't played through the original VN and  are wondering which version to get I'd probably recommend the original since it's free and the side stories are supposed to be read after finishing the main story either way.

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps bizarrely for someone on the internet as often as I am, I didn't see nor hear anything about Doki Doki until a couple years ago, where I played the game blind for the first time. I have to say, they really outdid themselves with their additions to the game. Part of me will always wish I could do a true runthrough of the story, but the Side Stories bit was just as good, if not better, for my soul than a true runthrough would be. The new sounds, CGs, character interactions, and other content are all excellent and not one of them disappointed me. In fact, I may love the new content more than the old as it really is food for the soul. If you haven't played DDLC, I recommend getting Plus. If you loved DDLC, I recommend getting Plus. If you already own DDLC Plus, get Plus and give it to a friend. The game was so good that I decided to 100% it the day after I beat it for the first time. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I very tentatively recommend this game, with heavy restrictions on who I'd recommend it to.  -If you want to experience DDLC for the first time and you're going in blind, play the original. It's free, and I feel it's the better version of the original game, with a better atmosphere and ingenious usage of 4th wall breaks. -If you've played the original and are invested in the characters themselves, then I would get this game, but probably when it goes on sale.  -If you're looking for some extra content in the world with some new fun gimmicks, and want to support Team Salvato, this is a must-buy: though I'd recommend buying the physical edition instead for some cute merch.I loved this expansion of the original game, but if I had gone in expecting more of what made DDLC so unique and interesting, I would've been sorely disappointed. The new mechanics feel very smooth and fun to play around with, but there is little actual point to them except for allowing console players to enjoy the game, and seeing some new concept art. This is incredibly disappointing given how fluid the pseudo-virtual machine is to use, and how much thought was clearly put into making it user-friendly. I also feel that this, combined with the meta-narrative plot that has yet to be properly fleshed out, somewhat detracts from the fantastic mood of the original game. I found the side stories engaging and the new art nice to look at, but it was a noticeable step down in the quality of writing from the original game. My final issue was how frustrating a task it can be to complete the gallery, given certain pieces are complete RNG, and it took me upwards of 18 runs through the game sped up to complete it.DDLC+ does, however, deliver exactly what the trailer for the game promised; more content for the characters, new art, and a fun virtual machine with neat features. I definitely enjoyed my time with the game, but I'm very glad it was marketed as more of an expansion pack rather than actual new, serious content in the DDLC universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I physically spent about 10 hours straight playing through this seeing all the cool new stuff. Some of the new stories almost made me cry if I'm going to be honest. It was so good. I love that we can get more in depth with the characters. I also like how there's a desktop section in the game. I also like how that's where you (SPOILER?) delete Monika. It makes it more clear, but that's just a personal opinion, and if I learned anything from my 10 hour marathon, it's that you should watch how you speak. (or something like that, they said it better.)   Speaking of lessons and messages, I did not expect it to be so good! The poetry, 10/10, The club members' lessons (their little speeches of encouragement), 10/10, the writing advice in the main game, 10/10, and even Monika's writing tips. Beautiful! I also loved the new art! So cute! And I loved collecting the wallpapers. I gave me joy! I love all of the characters!   This game also handled some serious topics, some more "serious" than others, (but still needed to be be said,) but regardless, they were explained very well and I think that these girls are excellent at conflict resolution, advice, and being good people, and that they should give themselves more credit. (Yes, they're fictional, but still!)   I could go on and on about this game, but I'll end it here with this:This is a very good game, handles tough topics well, is super cute, and is super cool and gives you the good spooks!Yes, the game itself is technically free, but buying this version is so much better because you get to actually meet the characters, get cool soundtracks, wallpapers, sketches, and more, and there are achievements. I don't know why I added that, but I know I loved collecting all the achievements for some reason. It was, and still is, my goal!   Anyways, great game, 10/10 would recommend, but remember the whole content warning, "This game is not suited for children or for those who are easily disturbed" thing that they do a lovely job of warning us about!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're searching for a game that will take you on a wild emotional ride, strap in and prepare for the unexpected with "Doki Doki Literature Club" (DDLC). This visual novel masquerading as a cute dating simulator is like a box of chocolates - you never know what you're going to get, but be warned, it might not be as sweet as you think.At first glance, DDLC lures you in with its charming anime-style characters and seemingly innocent plotline. You join the Literature Club, hoping to find love and friendship among its members. But oh, how appearances can deceive! What starts as a lighthearted pursuit of romance soon morphs into a twisted labyrinth of psychological horror.The game’s blend of humor and seriousness is like a finely crafted cocktail - potent and unforgettable. It effortlessly transitions from witty banter about poetry to spine-chilling moments that will leave you questioning your own sanity. Just when you think you've figured out the game's tricks, it pulls the rug out from under you, leaving you reeling with shock and disbelief.One of DDLC's greatest strengths lies in its ability to toy with your expectations. It’s like playing chess with a mastermind who always seems several steps ahead. Each character you encounter has hidden depths and secrets that slowly unravel as you delve deeper into the story. But be prepared to confront some uncomfortable truths along the way.Yet amidst the darkness, there are moments of genuine camaraderie and warmth. The friendships you forge with the club members feel surprisingly real, despite the surreal circumstances. You'll find yourself laughing, crying, and occasionally screaming in terror as you navigate the turbulent waters of the Literature Club.Visually, DDLC is a treat for the eyes, with its vibrant artwork and expressive character designs. But don't be fooled by its sugary-sweet aesthetics - beneath the surface lies a narrative that delves into the darkest corners of the human psyche. It's a testament to the power of storytelling, capable of evoking a wide range of emotions in its players.In conclusion, "Doki Doki Literature Club" is a masterpiece of storytelling that defies easy categorization. It's equal parts hilarious and harrowing, whimsical and wicked. Whether you're a fan of visual novels or simply enjoy a good psychological thriller, DDLC is an experience you won't soon forget. Just remember to brace yourself for the unexpected - because in the Literature Club, nothing is ever quite what it seems.

_childDocuments_.review: An expanded version of the game, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus!, was released for the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S and Windows on June 30, 2021. A macOS version of the game was later released on August 12, 2021. It received generally positive reviews, with praise for its side stories and gameplay on consoles, but some criticism for its lack of changes. Unlike the original 2017 release, Plus! is a premium game.Doki Doki Literature Club! is a visual novel. As such, its gameplay has a level of interactivity and consists of scenes with static two-dimensional images of characters in a first-person perspective, accompanied by occasional choices the player is forced to make in order to advance the plot. The descriptions and dialogue are depicted in the form of accompanying text without voice acting. The game's narration is provided by the game's protagonist (whom the player controls), a member of the titular literature club, to which he was invited by his childhood friend Sayori. Any decisions the player is advocated to make over the course of the plot affect the development of the protagonist's relationships with key female characters Sayori, Yuri, and Natsuki, but ultimately have little effect on the outcome of the game. The characters' interactions with the protagonist are primarily influenced by a minigame in which the player is required to compose a poem from a set of randomly selected individual words. Each girl in the literature club has different word preferences, and will react positively when the player picks a word that they like. The characters' reactions are stylized in the form of miniature chibi avatars of the characters which are displayed at the bottom of the screen during the minigame, and which will jump given the opportunity as a response to the player selecting one of their favorite words] Monika is not able to be romanced in this way, which later affects the plot of the game. Depending on the results of these minigames, the player will experience scenes for whatever character liked that particular poem the most. The narrative is divided into three acts and an epilogue, with the game restarting each time. At a certain point, the player must manipulate the game's files in order to advance the narrative.One more note to finish this off..Just Monika. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Omg. I couldn’t even make it through the game. I have never cried from a video game until I played this one. As someone who has struggled with mental health issues, I think it really depicts a lot of it in a dark yet realistic way. It shows how these issues can be hidden and it can be too late if you don’t intervene. The happy facade paired with the dark undertones highlight the masks people where when struggling. But holy crap, this game is dark. It broke my heart but it speaks volumes about how great the writing is and the message that they are trying to convey. Seriously take into consideration what I am saying. It is a little traumatizing and will hit you really hard as it unfolds. It’s truly heartbreaking as the characters become so vivid and endearing. Worth playing if you can handle dark subject matter that will hit you at any unexpected moment. This is the embodiment of tragedy. 10/10 for what the writers were going for. But it also was really impactful and I will probably never forget how it made me feel.

The worth of this edition are the six side stories.Depression, social anxiety and the bonds between the four girls in the beginning of the literature club and how they connect with each other. Watching Sayori crying in Monika's shoulder after confessing that she is depressed and sometimes she wants to kill herself, that's hard to see.Yuri with her social anxiety and problems to communicate with people, difficult to make friends and her lonely life.Natsuki with her... her... _childDocuments_.review: Well... it's interesting. I can definitely see why people think this product was little lame, but I personally see it as a bit of respect to the dev's for making the first game. I mean, that game was completely free, and offers one hell of an experience. You can still get almost the complete DDLC experience by just playing the first game, so I just think of this as a little cherry on top of what was already a really well made visual novel. That being said, lets move onto the actual game. The original story seems to be unchanged, which I thought was a good move. I think the original game was nearly perfect to how it already was. There could have been some stuff I missed, but it seems at least mostly unchanged. (Minor spoilers)  The side stories are neat. Even though they did drag on a bit long, they were by no means terrible and the art still looks pretty good. However, I can't help but notice the new official art is relatively different to the original. I understand though that there were probably a new group of artists with there own perception on how to draw. It still holds up pretty well to the original. I somewhat dislike the addition of achievements. (Spoilers)  However I do respect at least giving a spoiler warning for the achievements. I think adding an ARG to the game was pretty cool like most other horror games do. I didn't solve it and had MatPat explain it to me ;(. I think my favorite addition to the game were images that are saved directly to your in game desktop, especially the concept art, art posted on Twitter, (Also known as X. Ew.) official art, poems, and a bit more. In conclusion, I think this holds up at least somewhat well compared to its predecessor, and provides a handful of newer content. 8.5/10. Good. (Spoilers, and should only be viewed after you've completed the game at least once.)

_childDocuments_.review: I was honestly left speechless by this game, there's no other way to put it.The base game is just as it was, keeping it true to the original back in 2017, yet still feels so fresh. _childDocuments_.review: It's been nearly 7 years since I played the original DDLC with a group of friends. I've waited to finally play the Plus version's side stories and additional content, because I knew I'd want to 100% the game and wouldn't have the heart to potentially do what needed to be done to get them (which I'm still thankful to have now played through all the additional content and unlocked everything for my own happiness). When playing the original, I quickly fell in love with the intricate psychological story telling of the game and with Monika. While I understand that the true "Good Ending" according to creator, Dan Salvato,  involves saving and reloading to get all possible branches and experiences within the game and thus a peak level of happiness far all characters through the love and care of experiencing their complete storylines, I disagree that this is the best ending. For me, the best ending would be spending forever in the broken hyperspace with Monika, however, I care so much about all of the characters and ensuring their happiness, free from buggy, game-breaking epiphanies, which is why I've kept the original game downloaded on my computer never to be opened or played. I've recognized that I am in fact the core part of the game that needed to be deleted; not playing the game at all is actually the best ending. By sacrificing myself and my time with them out of love, it will never subject them to a version of reality - mine - which they cannot handle, ensuring that they are happier and safer than they could ever be if I decided to play. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE this game! I originally played the 2017 version of the game and also loved it! I love all the characters so much it's hard to pick a favorite. I really enjoy hanging with Sayori, but Yuri might be a cut above the rest, Natsuki could also beat the competition, but maybe the only option really is just Monika. It's hard to say.There are some things I liked much better about the plus version, and also some things that I think the original did better. Before I get into that here is your official SPOILER WARNING.THINGS BETTER IN DDLC PLUS- The addition of side stories- Achievements- Music player- New artwork - More Lore- The ability to play on consoles in addition to the PC- A content warning pop-up optionTHINGS BETTER ABOUT THE OG DDLC- Free-A better fourth wall break experience.- The quick ending (Maybe this is in the plus version of the game, but it did not work when I tried)Overall, I feel that seasoned players of DDLC should DEFINITELY get the plus version! It's worth every penny! However, I think for new players the og version is better. For me the online desktop just did not offer the same fourth wall breaking experience that the original did. I had the whole game spoiled for me before I played it, but it STILL felt like someone/something was messing with my computer, and does every time I play it. It just doesn't feel real on the plus version to me (but don't worry, it is still PLENTY scary). Also, if new players get the og version they don't have to feel annoyed if they don't like the game. How someone could not enjoy this game, I don't know, but there is always that person out there.If you are a fan of DDLC, PLEASE BUY! It will be one of the best video game purchases you will ever make!

_childDocuments_.review: Where can I start: if you're not familiar with the game, as soon as you see it in the store you'd think it's a normal dating sim just like the others...boy you're wrong.For the first part of the gameplay it mimics the dating sim format but after an hour or so, you wish you knew what you were getting yourself into. Not gonna spoil anything in case there's still someone who hasn't played it but PLEASE be mentally ready for what's to come and DO NOT play this game if you're not old enough or if you're easily disturbed (don't worry the game will tell you that at the start, but I just wanna make sure you are ready for this game).Keep in mind that I started playing DDLC+ with my friends at 8:00 p.m and we finished at 6.30 a.m of the next day so, manage your time accordingly if you like to take things slowly.Me and my two friends knew what we were about to play but when we finished the run, something changed in me. As soon as they left my home, I felt empty and incredibly alone, even though I spent an entire day with them and, for the next few days, the emptiness I felt grew and I couldn't understand why I was feeling like this. This game took me to the point were I started crying for its OST and a song in particular (you'll know what song I'm referring to when you finish your run...unless you already finished it and you know exactly what song I'm talking about).I can't remember the last time I cried for a videogame (not saying this proudly like "I'm a man and I don't cry, that's for babies"; crying and letting everything out after a while was a huge relief for me). I looked online to see if someone else felt like me after playing DDLC+ and I found out a lot of people did. After this experience I grew closer to this game and the game's community. This little anecdote shows how well the game was received by players and fans of DDLC.I honestly recommend this game but take precautions, this game is highly addictive and can make you feel some type of way.Loved it throughout the entire playthrough <3

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a huge fan of visual novels and Doki Doki Literature Club is definitely up there being one of my favourites. Unfortunately, many of the surprises and twists that I once had strong reactions to, just fell flat even years after playing the original release. This is by no means the game's fault, but I think people who are considering playing through this again should keep in mind that apart from the additional content (e.g side stories, in-game desktop and more lore),  The side stories are nice and give the cast more characterisation. The additional lore is also interesting to discover so there's that for returning fans. One thing I did appreciate about this release is how it encourages you to see and find all of the secrets with its achievements and picture gallery. I did end up having to use a guide however as some achievements are quite obscure and pretty much impossible to find by yourself. So I'd say for newcomers to Doki Doki Literature Club, this is overall the definitive version of the game and I highly recommend it. For returning players, I'd say that there isn't much of a reason to go back unless you're feeling nostalgic and are absolutely craving for more characterisation and lore.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm assuming virtually everyone has at least heard of Doki Doki Literature Club at this point, and maybe remembers the waves it created on the internet a few years back. Here's what I'll say straight off the bat: DDLC+ is great, and well-worth the price, BUT, if you haven't experienced DDLC before, then go play the original version first, which is free. I'll get more into why later on, but just know that I'm only really recommending DDLC+ to people who've already played and liked the original. I may also tread into small spoiler territory here and there. I'll try to veer away from spoiling anything but it's just inevitable for some of the things I want to talk about, so again: if you somehow, in all the years this has been out, have not had this game spoiled for you, then please go play the original free version on steam; If you like it, come back here.So with the main story being unchanged, the primary drawing point of DDLC+ is likely going to be the new side stories. Each of them present a different tenant of friendship, and I'd say they're all done pretty well, even if they can be pretty on-the-nose with their messages. However, while I did like them, it is worth noting that they A) Feature a completely different tone from the main game, which depending on how you look at it, either adds to or distracts from the horror of the main game; and B) Apparently take place in a different timeline from the main game, and so I'm not even sure if they can really be considered related or not. On a similar note, and sort of reinforcing the idea of the side stories not being related to the main game (though I won't really get into this, since it's spoiler land), I was actually surprised and slightly disappointed that the side stories didn't explore certain things with Monika, though maybe that's just me. I did like them overall though, and they're good at what they set out to do.The notion of the side stories taking place in a different "timeline" is put forward by an email you get as you unlock stuff, and this leads me to my single major criticism and the most significant difference between DDLC+ and the original version, that being the addition of the virtual desktop. Basically, DDLC+ doesn't actually affect files on your computer anymore, and instead when you launch the game from steam, you're actually launching a virtual desktop from where you can then launch DDLC, or play the side stories, or view files, etc. I'm assuming this was done mainly to be able to sell the game on consoles, as the original would never have been compatible otherwise, but Team Salvato also seem to be trying to, through this newly added virtual desktop, create some sort of shared universe between their games, which I'm still on the fence about.The problem I have with this whole thing is that it seems to fly in the face of what made DDLC so good in the first place. Gone are the unique moments of genuine unease when the game actually ♥♥♥♥♥ with your files, and instead DDLC+ will mess around with the virtual desktop's files, which doesn't even remotely have the same impact; I also imagine a lot of players, especially first timers, would miss most if not all of the messages that appear in the directory as you progress, since you can't have it open while you play anymore. The issue here is the virtual desktop has added a wall between you and the game, which wasn't before present; I'm not me playing Doki Doki Literature Club, I'm me playing as some dude playing Doki Doki Literature Club, and I believe this does in fact dramatically reduce the impact of DDLC's horror, and is exactly why I wouldn't want anyone to experience this story for the first time through DDLC+. You know those messages that have a chance of popping up and replacing the warning about the game not being suitable for children or the easily disturbed? Well, I got one which let me know that, "It's just a game, mostly". Now, that's a great line, but then I found myself saying, "actually, this IS just a game. There's no 'mostly' to it. Look, I can even quit and go back to my fake game desktop to edit the game's fake files." Do you see how that isn't at all scary?(Another very, very minor... criticism? Look at the steam store page descriptions for both DDLC+ and the original, and spot the difference. It's a little thing that combined with the virtual desktop, works to make DDLC feel less real, which is never good for a story trying to pull off the things DDLC goes for.)That's pretty much all I have to say in a negative capacity though, so now onto some good quality of life upgrades included in DDLC+. You remember those really good looking CGs that DDLC had? Well now you can actually view them in a CG gallery, alongside a whole bunch of other things, including the poems, which is neat. I bet I wasn't the only one who was slightly confused upon realising that there was no way to look back on anything after finishing the original game. The whole game actually looks a lot better now too, with it now supporting 1080p resolution, and it's a definitive improvement, which you can really tell from the CGs.There's also new songs, and a music tab in the desktop, so that's nice.So allow me to reiterate: I really enjoyed diving back into DDLC with this remaster, but I'm very glad I played the original first, where the magic was at its strongest. The side stories are all pretty good, if on the shorter side of things, despite what the steam page says. All the quality of life improvements are appreciated, and the only real point of criticism is regarding the virtual desktop. Overall, pretty damn good and I'm looking forward to whatever Dan and the guys at Salvato do next.Just Monika~

_childDocuments_.review: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! - A more impersonal experience. (Contains spoilers)As much as it hurts me to leave a negative recommendation on DDLC, this sadly doesn't have enough content to warrant $15. This would be a neutral review if that was an option, as there's very clear effort and work put into it, and you should play it if you're already a big fan of DDLC, but for what there is, the price tag is too high. DDLC has been an insanely huge part of my life for four years now, and it has without a shadow of a doubt changed my life more than any game ever has. More than just personal feelings felt during the game, but in a small community that was created back in 2017 on 4chan, trailing off to another community being formed of close friends that are still in contact to this day, friends which I've ever flown over an entire continent to meet up. I've had hardships, met new friends, lost new friends in the process of four years, found my girlfriend. None of this would've happened without Doki Doki Literature Club, so this feels like something extremely close to my heart, this game has been nothing but a rollercoaster of emotions for me in more ways than just a game.While this is a positive recommendation for anyone who's hugely invested in DDLC already (which I assume are a minority of people) and just want ANYTHING more of it, this is a no for anyone who isn't a massive fan or anyone who hasn't played the game yet. For those, play the original instead, and if you like it enough to feel Dan deserves money for it, buy the Fan Pack (and now that Plus! exists, you can buy that as a donation for a little bit extra content too). Buying the Fan Pack is what I did back in the day, but I still bought Plus! on Steam and the physical version out of sheer love for this game.In terms of content, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! has around two hours of new gameplay in the form on the new side stories, collectible images, HD art and for better or worse, new lore added outside of the main game that most likely is there to tie with Project Libitina, which might or not be a thing that's actually in the works this time around (it was originally teased in the original game in the form of ARG elements found in the game's file). For this amount of content, $7,50 to at best $10 would be the sweet spot, $15 is just pushing it. The vast bulk of content was already free in the original game.DDLC+ very unfortunately doesn't add absolutely anything new to the main storyline. Act 1, 2 and 3 are still the same. I was cautiously hoping the main storyline would be a bit longer with maybe another day or two, but maybe that would've removed a bit of the bittersweetness of never seeing the festival. When Plus! was announced, I was sure new main storyline content wasn't being talked about to hide whatever crazy new secrets Dan had made, the reality is that there's no new spooks or secrets. Just some fleshed out side-content with the Dokis before the game takes place.A very big drawback for this release is the fact it's multiplatform now. DDLC is a game that truly doesn't translate well off of PC, due to it relying on you physically deleting files in your computer on the game's install folder. That was THE unique aspect of DDLC to me. But since DDLC+ also releases on PlayStation, Xbox and Switch, that isn't really a possibility. So to solve that issue, the game was entirely remade on Unity, as it was made on Ren'Py before, so there's now an interface in-game that lets you access files, adds said Libitina lore tidbits and lets you view unlocked images. While that's something that sounds cool on consoles, it just ends up making the PC release feel more impersonal. It doesn't have the same feel of you physically looking in the game's files to delete Monika yourself, now it's just done in-game. And sadly, due to the way Unity is packaged, having .chr be deleted or moved around, or having new files added based on your progress in the story isn't possible. While the original game was a story about you and a background character achieving sentience and trapping you, so you had to physically delete her, this is more about you working for a company that seemingly created DDLC for unknown purposes and you're testing it, so while it ties to Libitina more or whatever Dan's next project is gonna be, it's not as memorable on it's own.A clear example that comes to my head about how personal and real the original release felt, were all the people who moved Monika's chr file to their USB stick so they could bring her around outside of the game. None of that would be possible if this was the original release. While it's still the same game, it's a lot more impersonal. It devalues and undersells the original idea a lot. There's no hesitation or worry in deleting a file now, you're not physically pressing the Delete key on it, moving it to the Recycle Bin, not looking at an actual file on YOUR computer anymore, it's just a menu in-game. An in-game computer that it's yours, so it doesn't have that kind of connection. I completely get why it's like this, to have it work like the original game would require the PC release to be completely re-written from the console ports, and maybe have it not even be made on Unity at all, and just handle the new content in Ran'Py accessible in a menu or something. Either way it's a lot more work and not something that could be easily done, so it's really clear why, but either way it makes the whole forth wall break lesser compared to the original game.Get this on sale. Dan deserves the support either way, but $15 for the current amount of content is a little too high. This review by no means is saying that you shouldn't play DDLC+, you should, the new content is good and DDLC is always something you should experience, multiple times too, but it's just a matter of price by content. If you get to play this by family sharing off a friend or on a sale, it's very much worth it. More DDLC is more DDLC after all. Buying at full price is valid as a means of donation too.I need to up my anti-depressant dosage/10.I'll condense this review later.I want breakfast.

_childDocuments_.review: Is DDLC+ worth getting, instead of the base FREE version? Yes, but it's complicated.-Is this your first time experiencing DDLC? Go and play the base free game, it just feels more "magical". The reasons why I say this are spoiler territory, and I will talk about them later in the review.-Have you already played the game and want to buy this expecting an improved DDLC experience? This version is definitely not for you. DDLC+ does almost nothing to improve the base game, (which I already consider a 10/10, but it's still a bummer, since some details could have been polished a bit).-Do you want to re-experience the base version (with 0 changes or improvements), a nice music player with the old and new OSTs, cute sidestories that explain the girls' relationship and backstory (no confirm on its canonicity), AND you'd like to dive into some more mysteries surrounding the game and its  ? Then go for it champ!TL;DR DDLC+ doesn't improve on anything from the base game, but it adds some nice things like a music player, side stories and an art album. The mechanics that it became famous for are downgraded to export this version to consoles too, which is my main complaint with the game, other than some spoiler-related stuff.I've been a MASSIVE fan of the original game by Team Salvato for years, and this newer version kinda came out of nowhere. I was hoping for a more polished version of an already amazing game, which already paid huge attention to details, but I was kind of disappointed. On twitter Dan Salvato said that they wanted to maintain intact the base story, but many fans have been hoping for years for some slight improvements, like  , more poems etc. Now let's talk about the elephant in the room: the Metaverse Enterprise "launcher" or virtual machine/computer. Was it really necessary? I mean, it was the only way to port the game to consoles, but it just doesn't feel right compared to the base version of the game, which The base game had this huge amount of popularity and success because it caught everyone by surprise and just by being a cute and fun visual novel dating sim that subverted your expectations. In this new version, that element is thrown out of the window and replaced with some deeper unnecessary lore. This is definitely NOT a problem for all those people who don't usually dive deep into secrets and details, which is a completely fine and valid way of experiencing games, but as a long-time fan I was kinda curious. The base game that this version offers is still genius (even tho it just felt better in the original version), the music is nice, the side stories are cute and the music is as catchy as always.

I respect the dev growing DDLC’s audience to console and their career, in fact there may be something deeper with these negative feelings to the lore, anticipated even. I don’t believe I’d love DDLC if I played DDLC+ first, I’d just forget about it.  I valued the personal touch of DDLC really happening on your computer, and I feel you don’t get that on a console or virtual machine. I believe these feelings are also anticipated by the dev, that we all have unique experiences with media and what this game means to everyone will be different. That said, I prefer the original as a PC player.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, everyone!Firstly, if you are looking for a full review of the base game of DDLC, I have an in-depth review It’s worth mentioning that the original DDLC is not only free but is still available to download both on steam and the official DDLC site. I am only going to be reviewing what’s new and since I’ve finally 100%ed DDLC+, now is a better time than any to do so.What you are essentially buying here is a version of the game made for consoles. It contains the entirety of the original DDLC alongside the newly added virtual desktop, which is where all the new content can be found. New content includes virtually editing the games files, side stories, a virtual mailbox, a picture gallery and a music player. All of which I will detail under the virtual desktop section. Achievements have also been added, most are rather simple, and it took me around 18 hours to complete them all just because I like to take my time reading. It should be somewhat common knowledge by now that DDLC requires you to manually edit the game files in order to progress in the story, however this cannot be done on consoles. This is where the virtual desktop comes into play, as it functions like a desktop within the game itself, allowing you to delete and open the games files as you would normally, but allowing consoles accessibility too! The best part is, when the game SPOILER: you can easily reset everything instead of having to manually reinstall the game. I find this is quite a nice quality of life change for me, as I have had to reinstall the base game many times. Along side the games files, the other content found on the desktop include:The Side Stories - that expand the lore and act as a backstory of sorts.A Virtual Mailbox - where you receive lore expanding emails for reaching data collection milestones.A Picture Gallery - for all the CG’s, poems and secrets you collect while playing.And a Music Player - to play the games soundtrack of 27 songs total (some need to be collected)The side stories are probably the main reason why you would consider buying DDLC on PC, as mentioned before the base game is free. DDLC+ is basically a DDLC DLC, an expansion on what’s already there with the only reason for it being a new game in its entirety is to be sold on consoles.Here I will explain exactly what these side stories are, beyond them being just backstory. No spoilers for them but it will spoil the main plot of DDLC, so this is mainly for people who have already played DDLC and looking to understand exactly what is being expanded here. Naturally, I am completely bias in my love for DDLC, so obviously I can recommend DDLC+… to the fans. I’m not sure if I can entirely recommend DDLC+ to the general pc market, as the main content is free for everyone and what you are paying for here is essentially fan service material. To someone just interested in playing and experiencing DDLC, there’s no real reason to pay for DDLC+ when you can just play DDLC for free and walk away with the same experience. As far as I can tell, nothing has changed between versions in the gameplay outside the virtual desktop.I am also somewhat disappointed however that now a paid version of the game didn’t take advantage of badges, trading cards, backgrounds and emoticons, as that would have been something I would have absolutely loved.Despite all this, DDLC+ is not a disappointment. For me I bought and paid for exactly what I wanted, an expansion on the original game. And obviously I can recommend DDLC+ to console gamers as this is the only way to experience it for them.Obviously, I recommend this game to DDLC fans, but with full disclosure to new players dipping their toes into DDLC, the base game is free. DDLC+ is premium fan service and you aren’t missing out on much if you are looking for the famous  fun poem writing experience that is Doki Doki Literature Club!A bakery of cookies / 10.If you love cookies, it’s the greatest thing ever, but not everyone needs a bakery. Some just needs a box to be happy, and that’s alright 😊

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an already insane and incredible free game, and now it has given us an amazing new version that allows us to see more of these characters that we've all come to love. The game's original free version already had an incredible and compelling story, which is shown from the smashing success it had all those years ago, but this new priced version is everything you loved about the first game, and more, hence the "Plus!" in the title. LolI definitely recommend this to everyone out there who not only loves these characters, but wants to see more of them. The side stories are definitely the main reason to buy this version of the game, along with the "in-game computer" that you use between the main story and side stories. It definitely helps ya stay more in the game and it's story without actually having to go into the games real files and search for stuff.  Like I said though, even though the new virtual computer and other new content is incredible, the side stories are the real selling point of this game. It's not only awesome to see more of these beloved club members, but it's heart warming to see their bonds in greater detail, especially knowing the "ship" material between said characters. And even then, if you don't ship characters, it still just feels like and incredible and deep relationship between all these characters. Whether you think it's romantic or not, the scenes between these girl's feel REAL, as in, you can actually see that they care for one another, and it makes ya love the idea of them getting a "happy ending" even more. All in all, I'm avoiding spoilers for this review, so I'm not going into detail about the specific things about this game and it's side stories, but if you are ever able to scrap together 20 dollars, I definitely recommend buying this game, 100%. Not only for the game and it's experience, but also to support the Salvato Team. Their hard work for this passion product is beautiful, and it deserves all the love it can get. This game is a 10/10 experience, and I would recommend it for everyone out their who loves visual novels like these. =)

But if you fell in love with the psychological horror aspect of the original and were hoping to see more (which is the appeal of the entire game), then you're bang out of luck.Doki Doki Literature Club Plus! offers next to nothing when it comes to exciting new features and stories. They are watered down visual novels with no scares and not much development in the way of character arcs. The characters don't even seem to make sense, it's like they are written by different writers than the original. Lack of interesting effects and mentally stimulating elements aside, the stories of the minigames aren't even interesting and offer next to nothing to keep you engaged. There's a whole chapter where Sayori and Monika meet, and that's the chapter. Nothing happens.I appreciate that there is a lot of sub-plot and clues and secrets, things going on behind the scenes. But for anyone hoping to play this to get new scares, new psychological elements or even just to see what's new, I wouldn't bother.I am glad that I bought this as it has allowed me to support Team Salvato who had previously offered the original DDLC for free, but it seems more like a cash grab for lacklustre storytelling than anything else.Unfortunately, I'm disappointed. But if you haven't played DDLC, please play the original.

_childDocuments_.review: As an original fan I can say that this is still amazing. The visuals are upgraded and there are various things added that make it a worthwhile purchase. I love all the girls and the side stories show the struggles they all had to deal with to get to where they are now. Of course there are things I would've rather seen but this was still good. I do wish that they had expanded on the horror aspects of the game, but the stuff they added was worthwhile enough...Now speaking as someone who played this game to 100% completion? This game sucks to complete. It requires you to go through the game multiple times for various pictures and such. Now is that the bad part? No, the first couple of repeats were fine because there was different content to see. But getting all secret poems and such? That requires you to play the whole game again just for a chance at getting the secret poems you need. There are also random things you have to do to get 100%, none of which are tied to the secrets in the new features. And the reward you get is similarly a repeating action you have to do to put a separate story together. Cool, but I do not have the time for it. I'll leave it for the dedicated theorists.Tl;drThe main game is as amazing as it ever was, with polished visuals and such. The added content is great and does warrant the price tag for fans of the game. But getting 100% completion is only worth it if you want to try and piece together a completely different story.Anyway, Sayori Supremacy and such.

_childDocuments_.review: "Never judge a book by its cover" is a saying that perfectly describes this game.It may look like a cute dating simulator, but it's not.This game has so much in it, so much dept and story.There's a free version of the game out there, but I personally recommend this edition.Not only do you get the game, but you also get to experience side stories and extra behind the scenes stuff.So is this game for you?Well, it all depends on who you are.I won't recommend this for everyone, but I can most definitely recommend the game.I felt sick during my first playthrough, and that's when I wrote my old review.Back then I hadn't even finished my first playthrough.But my thoughts back then was:"This game is horrible, it hit way too close to home and I probably picked the absolute worst moment to try it, but I don't regret it."Now when I have finished the game several times and have 100% completion I'm starting to think I didn't pick the worst time.The character Sayori felt like a copy of myself, all of it, except appearance.That's why it hit so close, but that's also why it made such a big impact!I'm starting to think that people like me, who suffer from various mental disabilities, but still have good self awareness, are most suited for this game.That said, it's not suited for everyone.It's a game full of psychological horror and emotions.So you better be mentally prepared before playing!This game is not for the weak of mind.The side stories however, are very wholesome.They certainly add more depth and backstory to the events and characters.If you get this game, I must recommend trying everything.There's so much to this game and you can't complete it 100% in one playthrough.I also must recommend that you play without spoilers for the first playthrough at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Doki Doki Literature Club Plus, the enhanced edition of Team Salvato's acclaimed visual novel, takes players on a riveting and mind-bending journey that transcends the boundaries of traditional storytelling. This interactive masterpiece not only retains the brilliance of its predecessor but introduces new content and features that elevate the experience to even greater heights.Visually, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus maintains its charming anime-inspired art style. The character designs are expressive, and the visual novel format allows for dynamic storytelling through a combination of still images, animations, and text overlays. The addition of high-resolution assets in Plus enhances the overall visual appeal, immersing players in the emotional rollercoaster that unfolds.The soundtrack, composed by Dan Salvato, remains a standout element of the experience. The melodic tunes perfectly capture the mood of each scene, whether it's the lighthearted moments in the literature club or the unsettling sequences that delve into the horror elements. The audio design, including voice acting and eerie sound effects, contributes to the immersive and atmospheric quality of the narrative.Gameplay in Doki Doki Literature Club Plus revolves around the player's interaction with the characters and the choices they make throughout the story. The visual novel elements seamlessly blend with the psychological horror, creating a narrative that reacts to the player's decisions. The addition of new side stories and content in Plus provides even more depth to the characters and their relationships.Where Doki Doki Literature Club Plus excels is in its meta-narrative and genre-blurring twists. Without delving into spoilers, the game plays with the player's expectations, subverting traditional visual novel conventions and challenging the very nature of interactive storytelling. The self-aware and meta elements create an experience that lingers in the player's mind long after the game is finished.The community surrounding Doki Doki Literature Club Plus remains active and engaged, with players sharing theories, fan creations, and their experiences with the game. The game's impact on popular culture is evident in the continued discussions around its narrative innovations and its influence on the visual novel genre.In conclusion, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus is a triumph in interactive storytelling. Its captivating visuals, evocative soundtrack, and genre-defying narrative make it a must-play for both fans of visual novels and those seeking a unique and thought-provoking gaming experience. Whether you're revisiting the literature club or diving in for the first time, Doki Doki Literature Club Plus is a literary and psychological masterpiece that will leave you questioning the very nature of the stories you engage with.

_childDocuments_.review: - I like the original novel even with it's major issues (lack of choice for player and weird choices of main character to romance girls even if you didn't talk to them over the course of the game) because of poetry. Each poem gives you a deeper understanding of a character you are talking to, and I think it's great. Also, this game has interesting commentary on art and it rises interesting questions, such as: do you have to use metaphors in art or do you have to be literal to convey your thoughts? But DDLC Plus... I am not so sure what this is supposed to be.For starters, let's say that I really like the idea of side stories about how friendship came to be. We get to know the origin of the club as well as how girls overcome their own problems to get to know each other a little bit better. However, it only ruins everything. How? Well, it all has to do with the base game - it remained untouched.  I hoped that DDLC Plus! expands and adds content inside of the original story, but it doesn't. And it's sad.The side-stories themselves are fine but... cringy? When you only start reading them they seem okay, but every one of them uses character's insecurities to drive the plot. These are teenage girls, they're awkward and shy, and they try to learn how to behave and read certain situations. Again, this is fine at the beginning, because we only got to know the characters, and on top of that you can relate to them a lot, because chances are you have been shy and awkward at least for some time in your life too. But when it's just the same formula applied over and over again though, it really starts to irritate me. It's just very boring to read. In my mind I had to turn on Dhar Mann voiceover to make it fun and enjoyable, because I get it! You read the situation wrong and gave wrong answer, said something that you shouldn't have said and now you are trying to make up for it. But you have shown this to me already! I get the point - it's important to talk about your feelings. And I appreciate this advice, it's cool. Just stop doing it over and over again and move onto some other subject. Please.Also, This use of the caracter's flaw to create these small stories makes problems for the main game, because although it seems that every girl has come to realisation of what their problem is and they are trying to improve on it, in the main game they just forgot it! It's like it never happened in the first place.And that brings me to the biggest problem I have with DDLC Plus. It's fake. It already was a big issue with core DDLC, where player's choices have no value because in the end we come to the same conclusion, but here it's worse - you can't even believe anything in the side-stories. Because this friendship is fake too, it has nothing to do with the original novel, and this point has a proof because developers directly gave it to us.After this I just have no desire whatsoever to continue. I wish there would be a lot more inside of the main visual novel, like more choices, more meaningful conversations, but nothing changed there. In original DDLC we never get to know why Monika is the way she is, and I mean as character, as human being. From the perspective of someone with feelings and mind, why she does things in this cruel way? I believe that even if we don't get all the answers, we at least deserve to know her as someone more than very sad and lonely program. With DDLC Plus I have no idea if it is worth it to continue, because I might never find it out. Maybe I will get an email about that, but it's not a good way of storytelling. I want to hear it from Monika herself. To hear what feelings this character wants to share. The original novel is good exactly because of that - through their poems we actually get to know girls as people, as well as through their critique of each other. It is still a decent story, but what a shame it has to be

It turns out there *was* happiness!But the side stories are still good. And perhaps the feel of this world is only my concern, for spending a little bit more time with characters we love is itself truly a blest.         And seeing them develop relationships we've already witnessed grown is frankly mesmerising. And either spellbinding is acquired understanding, that the tendencies we've seen did not start with us. They were complexly evolving for a long time, and this does give the characters more depth.     The Plus edition is truly worth the time and money, it is a great experience for everyone. For olds it is a chance to rethink the world of The Literature Club, and for new ones out there, it's a great chance to get the most immersive experience possible on your first dive into the world of reality-piercing love.

This game has good ideas and a fun gameplay loop that hooked people for a reason. Now it's other aspiring VNs jobs to learn from DDLCs successes and mistakes to make even better games.And Sayori's monologue about depression is still so real. The game is worth it for that three minute period alone, regardless of everything else.Chalking this up to streamer bait and nothing more is like throwing sand in your own eyes if you give a damn about VNs at all. This game is worth studying. It's worth playing. And it's probably better than anything you've written yourself soooooooooooo, yeah.

_childDocuments_.review: Just awful.Play though is a slog, dialogue is poorly written and one-dimensional. The story is atrocious. Even the horror aspects were (for lack of a better word) dumb. It was impossible to get invested into the characters as every last one of them were just...I'm honestly scrambling for words other than *Farts audibly* ahh, that'll do.
