_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express is a stylish beat ‘em up with a myriad of action-packed scenarios to please both fans of the genre and newcomers alike. As protagonist ‘Babyface’, you play through 41 levels in a quest to stop criminals taking over the city. There is a decent story here, with plenty of twists and turns, but it’s the combat that will leave its mark. The game’s very enjoyable, and surprisingly deep, combat system takes a while to reveal itself. You start with off with a basic set of moves which can be upgraded through a skill tree once you’ve accrued points from completing levels. This skill tree allows you to customise your move-set however you see fit. You may want to spend all your points on melee attacks, upgrading your parry, or buying new bullets for your secondary weapon (once you obtain it). I enjoyed the slow drip feed of new moves as it kept things interesting and allowed me to master each ability before spending more points. Before long I was stringing huge combos together in brutal balletic fashion – similar to the Batman Arkham games, Sifu, and even the cartoon brawler, Bloodroots, in some ways. The levels themselves are mostly varied – you fight through typical city locations - from nightclubs and kitchens to sewers and train stations. Some levels mix things up completely – for example, early on, you are involved in a speedboat chase that plays out like a vertical twin stick shooter. And the 40+ levels will take some time to master. Expect frequent deaths and restarts (luckily, checkpoints are generous, and there’s three difficulties, making things accessible to all). There’s plenty of reply value, with each level offering up set challenges on a second play through. And as per most beat ‘em ups, there’s a combo score system, with those elusive ‘S’ ranks there to test your mettle. Many will compare Midnight Fight Express to Hotline Miami – and with good reason. It has a similar top-down perspective, albeit isometric, bitesize levels, a pulsating electronic soundtrack, and extreme violence – yet it has a far deeper combat system, and far more customisable options and things to unlock. For Steam Deck owners, I can confirm the game plays beautifully ‘out of the box’ at a rock solid 60fps. I don’t know if the game will be ‘verified’ at launch – but it should be! For achievement hunters, most achievements will come from playing through the campaign a couple of times; getting an S Rank on all 41 levels is the toughest challenge here. There are some drawbacks. The game is very linear. Levels are small, and there’s nothing really to do, other than fighting from point A to B. The story can occasionally get in the way of the action, breaking up the flow of the game – although this can be skipped, or turned off entirely on repeat plays. And MFE doesn’t really bring anything new to the table. Yet, what it does, it does well. There’s nothing quite as exhilarating as taking down a room of enemies with a dead fish as a weapon. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Take the illegitimate lovechild of John Wick, Daredevil, Batman, Jason Bourne, John McClane, Jacket, Biker, Rama and Inspector Tequila and what do you get? Babyface... or in other words, you, the player CharacterMidnight Fight Express is a love-letter to all sorts of action media mentioned above and an insanely addictive and fun experience. The Fighting system is heavily influenced by Batman's Arkham series and Sleeping Dogs, with counters, grapples, disarms, throws, dodges, light and heavy attacks, finishers, as well as throwing environmental objects and using enemy weapons. You are quite literally a very lethal version of Arkhams Batman in this, breaking wrists, spines, necks and noses left right and center. And though the combat can seem a bit simplistic at the start (tragically, the game has a rather weak start by only giving you the light and heavy attack, being able to throw stuff and a dodge-roll), as soon as you unlock more abilities, it quickly spirals into you becoming a walking death-machine. In one clean swoop, you can disarm a guy by countering him, use his weapon to break his neck, counter another guy, throw your weapon at that far-away prick shooting at you, then grabble the first you countered and smash his head into the pavement, before punching another guy two times and then shatter his spine via a SUPPLEX. Added to that, you get a gun with recharging bullets, which all have different effects that you can unlock and a rope pistol in late game that you can use to pull enemies close.Basically, at one point this game plops you down in a very small elevator filled with heavily-armed goons that all have machine guns. You slaughter them all in a few seconds if you know what you're doing... and it's glorious.And if all of that wasn't enough, the game is very generous in its difficulty customization, offering different pre-sets, as well as allowing you to set a custom difficulty, changîng your own health, changing the enemy's aggression, turning counter-notifications on or off, enabling tips and even disabing checkpoints if you so desire. Now, to be entirely honest, while the campaign is a lot of fun, it is on the shorter end of things; depending on difficulty and if you immediately replay levels for unlocks and to get S-Rankings, it might take you between four, five, six maybe eight hours, more or less, depending on your skill-level as well. What the game makes up by that though is the ability to easily replay levels with all of your skills unlocked, while also offering a rating system, based on your combos, your hits and how much or little damage you took, with a bonus for completing a level without dying. This, combined with challenges that unlock clothing/customization for your guy and companion, as well as optinal Perks that you can unlock, makes it easy and very enjoyable to replay. The fact that the aformentioned gameplay-loop is, as I said, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, also helps a lot with thatThe Story is servicable, but understandably takes a back-seat to allow you to jump into the carnage. You have options for disabling all mid-mission dialouge, as well as the ability to fast-forward through cutscenes, so if you don't give a damn about the story and just want to murder, kill, maim and destroy, then the game happily let's you. That's not to say the story's bad or anything, it's servicable and does it's job, but isn't anything special.Very big reccommend from me, even at full price, since this game and the developer deserve all the love they can getOh and do please play this game with a controller. Like I said, this is very much like Sleeping Dogs or the Arkham games, you'll WANT to play this with a controller

_childDocuments_.review: Yes but...there's a lot that hurts it in my opinion.The actual combat is incredibly fun--feels a bit like an isometric Arkham game and the depth gradually grows as you play. Really feels fantastic to fistfight against six or eight enemies.Then the gimmicks start showing up and it just grinds that fun to a halt.Guns feel out of place and force you into a lot of dodge rolling.  Then there are enemies like the slashers that not only have annoying combos but they can attack so fast and CANNOT be interrupted by any of your attacks outside of a thrown object or your side arm (which you don't get till later on) that interrupt the flow, especially if your gun is on recharge.  These wouldn't be so bad but they interrupt the fun, its more annoying than challenging.Oh, and (some of) your finishers and every one of your grapples can be interrupted--skip the grapples entirely.The chase sequences aren't bad but they don't feel very responsive--they feel shoehorned in and in my opinion? Overstay their welcome.The gunplay gets a bit better when you've gotten use to it and more enemies drop them but...look, I signed up for a brawler and while an occasional gun is nice to mix it up, I'm really here to break arms, kneecaps or jam knives into the eye sockets of a bunch of no named thugs.  The brawling and hand-to-hand combat is fun as hell, that's what I want more of and the game has an absolutely nasty habit of interrupting my good time with something nowhere near as enjoyable.It's like eating a chocolate chip cookie that has a single raisin in it, or having a make-out session with an incredibly attractive person only to suddenly stop to do five minutes of algebra in between lip locking.Why would you do this?  Why?Its not awful it can be amazingly fun--but gods, those rough spots are freakin' rough.I'd nab it when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express is a game I was very much looking forward to ever since the Demo came out a while's back. When it first came out I left by far the longest review I've ever written on Steam to the point that I had just found out that there's an actual Word Limit on this platform which was mildly enlightening for me to find out. My review was a non-recommendation short of going on sale as I felt at the time there were a lot of criticisms I had for the game that kept its best potential and fun from shining through. Ever since then the dev had gone to work patching through just about every single criticism I had line by line, which that alone I find extremely admirable and a commendation on their character which would give me grounds alone to recommend the game for the work being put in. The game is a brutal isometric beat-em-up with a lot of influence from games like Batman: Arkham Asylum, Sleeping Dogs and Hotline Miami. It is fairly challenging but also extremely satisfying to fight the whole way through in this game, especially as you get a better understanding of some mechanics, their usage and utility along with how to approach certain types of enemies. When the game initially came out this game was EXTREMELY rough starting from the 4th level onwards, and in a 40 mission game excluding the intro this was a mixed bag to get through after all that. Not helping things is that the upgrade system gated off certain abilities until a certain level was reached, and upgrade points would only be acquired from finishing levels for the first time. The game very quickly fell in to a habit of throwing waves of extremely durable enemies with short wind-ups and also always had at least one person with a gun who would have a very itchy trigger finger. This painted the encounters in a way that made them extremely frustrating and genuinely unfun at quite a lot of points as it felt like the worst aspects of Hotline Miami were beginning to rear themselves in what is ostensibly a 3d beat em up with health bars. Since the patches, this has been toned down and in my opinion the enemies are now perfectly reasonable to deal with on Normal and Hard with Realistic basically being a challenge difficulty to begin with assuming you've gone through the former two at least once. The less useful abilities were buffed, you can pick your abilities from the trees to your content so long as you have the points and you can even turn some of them off entirely if they don't suit your playstyle. I would highly recommend for your first run that you play either Normal or Hard and don't worry about the challenges for that first big run, though they have also toned down some of the more aggravating/unreasonably difficult challenges in this case as well, so a majority of them would just be acquired during regular gameplay.Moving on from just what's been patched and discussing the game prior, this game is absolute joy to play and has some amazing mocap work with executions, counters and combos that will stick with you for a while. Absolutely hats off to NoiseCream as well for the phenomenal soundtrack that helps keep the tension high and the action a treat to watch. While the customization system could use a couple of additions like hairstyles/beards and some more varied jackets/pants, it is still extremely fun to mix and match with along with the fact that you have the ability to play as any enemy or boss you've encountered throughout the game (Though for bosses you will likely have to finish at least 4/5 of the level's challenges).The gameplay will include your standard Arkham/Sleeping Dogs punching/holding moves, grapples, prompted counters, executions, finishers and environmental finishers as well. The two additions to this that can be toggled off completely are a self-reloading Magnum that has not just a regular bullet loaded in but 5 other utility bullets once it is fully upgraded and a grappling whip that can be used for not just disarming, grabbing and swinging but also to trip up enemies with one yank. I can't thank the dev enough that if needed you can turn off the latter abilities and let you play it as a regular brawler, but they are still useful abilities if you make actual use of them to go with.Some of the highlight levels of this game are The Restroom, The Airport, The Aeroplane, The Construction Site, The Elevator and The Lobby. These may not have as many hazards but these are such nice knockdown drag-out fights across entire maps that they're not only extremely fun to batter fools around in they're a visual treat. The exception mainly being The Airport which is one big homage to No Russian from Modern Warfare 2, being able to simply walk in an elevator and batter Makarov and his goons to death with your barehands is next level badass and funny. While this is also a gun heavy level, the gunplay is short and compact after the patch and now isn't as much of a constant hazard plaguing the level design, which makes this level and all the other more gun heavy levels all the better. Which works perfectly because the gunplay is just about any John Wick fan's personal fantasy, especially once you have executions, its quick, snappy and just as brutal.I will say there are still a couple of levels that still make me a bit aggravated, The Fight Club in particular having by far one of the worst finales of on any level between the overly tanky bikers and bikes exploding at random, and The Graveyard full of zombies is still a bit of a pain to get through given how one and done their unblockable grapples can be. These are at least easy to get through if you're in a hurry and you only need to get challenges done once across all the difficulties if you really need to. However these are also few and far in between a lot of very entertainingly actiony levels to go with, and are still all the more palatable after the work the dev put in patching this game. The game is very set piece heavy in order to keep the level to level fresh, which does help in its favor as you will be seeing an extremely wide amount of enemies and hazards coming for you. While the story is decent enough for what its trying to accomplish and I do look forward to seeing what happens next, the gimmicks is what can help break some level of monotony to things now. You won't just be fighting street thugs but cops, mimes, hooded cultists, special forces, leather clad subs, aformentioned Modern Warfare villains, pirates, zombies, priests and more. While these would have been overkill beforehand, the balancing is done in to make it decently enjoyable approaching the game your way and coming out with your hands bloody. While this review is a bit shorter than my initial review, I see this is a result of the good of the game being so easy to recommend without being overtly exposition laden for things that the players looking to play this game would be able to figure out for themselves as well. I wholeheartedly endorse and recommend Midnight Fight Express as it is a labor of love from the dev and an extremely fun beat em up that I look forward to seeing what the dev does with it going from here!

_childDocuments_.review: A worthwhile purchase if you're a beat-em-up fan. I'd say it's a steady 4 outta 5.BE ADVISED: YOU CAN UNLOCK THE ABILITY TO COUNTER ENEMIES WITH WEAPONS, and I would do so very early in the game. There's a lot of reviews here of people complaining that they just had to dodge around for most of the fights. I could see the game going that way if you weren't prioritizing the "Counter" and "Finisher" skill trees. This isn't a "play it your way" kind of game, and I agree the skill tree should have been much more linear to help solve this problem. If you put all of your points into Combos and Grapple before looking at Counter and Finisher, you're going to struggle. Just ignore those "I had to dodge a lot" thumbs down reviews.If you're wondering how this plays, think isometric My Friend Pedro, or maybe even Sifu with guns. It's not about the 1st time you play a level, it's about the 12th time you play it after coming back to it with some helpful upgrades and a better idea of how to exploit the enemy variants or take advantage of the weapon set for that level. Every level has several special challenges that unlock cosmetics and gameplay mods, so if you like a game with some replay value this one's solid.The story could've used some voice acting so you don't have to stop and read text boxes all the time. Reading lines from Droney while my combo timer faded away got very old (you do get the option to skip the story elements after you beat the level once, but it was still kind of a drag when playing levels the first time). At least that Noisecream soundtrack makes up for it. It's like they just told him to pump out every banger he had in reserve, and he delivered.It's not Streets of Rage 4 or Sifu levels of amazing, but it's only one tier down from those I think. If you like knocking dudes around like John Wick or chasing leaderboard scores, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this, because the demo and the first like, half of the game are mostly a ton of fun. It reminds me of Die Hard Arcade which is a game I don't think I've ever heard mentioned in the wild outside of my friend group but we loved it, spent way way too many quarters on that thing. The problem here is, the fights are dynamic and fun and challenging, and then they just keep throwing more and more "exceptions" at you that you have to do X specific thing or else. And then more and more and more and MORE enemies armed with guns, which largely force you to interact with the game in a completely different way.I would be ok with the, to be honest, kind of lame "minigame" levels like the Jetski if the other levels were just the brawl-tastic fun of the first few. The balance isn't even strictly bad, it's just the guns aren't fun? They're just guns. The enemy shots do a significant amount of damage that you can't do anything about besides dodge and disarm, and eventually you are running into almost the entire room is gun guys. And when you have the guns... they're just guns. You shoot the dudes but you can do that in SO MANY OTHER GAMES. It's not special here, but the hand to hand and environmental weapons ARE special, and it's baffling why the dev would distract from that, and even FORCE YOU AWAY from the absolute best aspects of the game. Basically it's a very fun hand-to-hand brawler where the first few levels take place in Britain and the rest take place in the rural US where you're more likely to come across a gun than not. I'd honestly rather just replay the first few levels than finish the last few, unless the game suddenly takes a turn back away from guns, but the disappointment is strong enough where I might do neither (actually that's not true, while offline on the Deck I did play the first like 4 levels a BUNCH of times, but now I might not go back to revisit them).

_childDocuments_.review: Solid beat 'em up game. Ton of customization options for the main character, the only notable exception being the character's gender. The combat's pretty fun, though not without a bit of jank and a few redundant mechanics. Combat is generally quick and snappy, as you jump from enemy to enemy pulverizing them into the ground before leaping onto the next one. I rarely felt the game was "unfair", though there were a few annoying levels in the mid-late section that had me dying over and over. Thankfully this game takes a page out of Hotline Miami; it just takes one button press to be right back at a checkpoint, no loading times involved.While this means it's easy to get back into the action after failure, the game has quite the narrative focus, full of short dialogue boxes and mini cutscenes. This does feel at odds with the gameplay, and I found it hard to pay full attention to what was going on in the story when you're switching gears constantly, so to speak. It wasn't *too* intrusive for me though, and when replaying levels, you have options to automatically skip all dialogue/cutscenes.This only took me about 5 hours to beat, but there's a good amount of replay value, with challenges for all 40 levels unlocking unique skins and new "perks", cheats/modifiers that change the way the game works at the price of disabling challenge progression. Since you can upgrade the player character with multiple new skills along the way, revisiting earlier levels to improve your time/score becomes much easier, as all player upgrades can be used in earlier levels. I do wish you could activate multiple cheats at once though, since combining infinite ammo with explosive bullets sounds like fun. All in all, it's a solid beat 'em up. The story is creative, to say the least, and lends itself to giving you wild encounters for fast, frenetic brawling and gunplay, against a surprisingly diverse assortment of enemy types. The soundtrack is great too, and really fits the hyperviolent nature of the world, and your place in it. I had a lot of fun playing through for the first time, and I'm sure I'll have a lot of fun replaying levels to clear the challenges, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit as of 10/29/2022The game's great now!  Previously, I'd written a strongly worded review at the time of the game's release for the many flaws in the game's combat.  I'm happy to say that Jacob Dzwinel, the developer, took the negative reviews the game was catching and made lots of very welcome changes that fixed nearly every flaw I and many others were critical of!  I will leave the old review below, but in short, hitbox issues are fixed, grapples are fun and work now, and many special enemies stopped being so spammy.  You can now use your entire kit reliably.The only criticism that remains is how the special revolver works.  It still switches to the next bullet type after you fire the one you choose, meaning you may end up in a Benny Hill reenactment as you run from your foes trying to switch back to the bullet you used previously.  It's also still bound to the finisher button, so expect that bullet switching problem to be really pronounced when you waste a shot trying to perform a finisher.  My suggestion would maybe to have the finisher action be the strike+counter buttons simultaneously?Anyway, having started over and played to the end, I had a blast and can safely recommend this game now!  Huge kudos to Jacob, the reviews were still in the positives before the fixes and he could have just taken that and called it a day.  He refused, and now the game is greater for it.  Check it out!----Old, mostly obsolete review below----It looks like a complex brawler with deep, reactive mechanics on the surface, similar to say, SIFU, but right up until about level 8 or so, that's when the cracks in the fight system start to really show.  There's a number of defensive and offensive abilities to unlock along the way, but unfortunately, several encounters are structured rather poorly to the point where the majority of your unlocked kit is dis-incentivized completely, in favor of just hammering the punch button and dodging all over the place.  Grapples are worthless.  The game claims it will only work when you've broken down an enemy's defense meter, but that's a lie.  I've had broken enemies break out of grapples instantly, I've had enemies with no defenses at all break out of grapples instantly.  If grapples do end up working, most of the animations are too long and you can be hit out of them, even during finishers.Many of the most effective moves are executed with the same button as a special revolver you unlock later, which can lead to wasting a useful tool and waiting for it to cool down again when all you meant to do was use a finisher.  The revolver itself works like ass because once you fire your bullet type of choice, the stupid thing switches bullet types for really no reason, and you have to switch it back to the one you just used to restart the cooldown in the middle of a fight.Enemies react inconsistently.  I mentioned that the game incentivizes spamming punch and dodge earlier because in many situations, you'll be faced with a special, highly damaging enemy, or map element that causes instant death.  These elements ignore the grace period granted by counters and finishers and can kill you quickly, so the only option of course, is to spam your movement.  Of course, this doesn't always work either, as some enemies seem to just have active hitboxes merely where they stand.  Perfect example is, someone could be throwing an object at you.  Your only course of action when too far, is to dodge.  If you dare dodge into them, they still have an active hitbox on their otherwise wide open body, and you'll be sent ragdolling to the floor for that special enemy to kill you.  Some enemies just are randomly given an instant shove ability that leave you stumbling for 1 or 2 seconds, once again, getting you killed by the special.Now, this game clearly sells itself on being an adrenaline pumping, fast acting brawler, and the soundtrack sells that incredibly well to boot (It's very good, in case you're wondering).  There's just one problem.  That flow is completely demolished, because before and after every single fight encounter, the game screeches that experience to a halt to wrestle control from you and tell its story through god awful dialogue, mostly through your drone companion that believes himself to be the most hilarious person in the universe.  Now, there is an option to disable the dialogue entirely, but that doesn't fix the fact that most encounters still yank control from you to pan over to enemies now silently conversing or just doing bad guy stuff, and it's completely un-skippable if you haven't completed that level first yet.  Only when you re-visit levels can you "fast forward" these control stealing moments that, mind you, still steal control from you.  This can be quite the aggravation for the kind of gamer that wants to complete a level right away with a high grade at the end of each level, and much of that involves consistently high combos, no deaths and completing challenges.The game's pretty new, maybe there's plenty of patches on the way to fix a ton of the janky, flawed combat, but as of now, this one gets a no from me.Oh and in case you missed it, the soundtrack is still great.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It was definitely worth the wait :)Gamescom 2021 track is called "Lock In".If you watched one of Gamescom trailers, they didn't lie. That's exactly how the game looks like when you play itStory-wise it's not that great. You play as Babyface, a sleeper agent woken up by a mysterious drone. Gangs are going wild out on the streets are you are going to stop them. During the story you learn more about Babyface, the person controlling the drone and the person responsible for unrest in the city.If it comes to graphics - they are really nice, nothing to complain about. Blood looks great :)Gameplay is really enjoyable. Light and heavy punches, parries, dodges and 2 more moves unlocked later during the story. _childDocuments_.review: Listen, this should really be a "neutral" review, because honestly I don't want to give them a thumbs down.However, the base game doesn't have much meat on its bones. I'd say 6 to 7 hours tops, but there's higher difficulties, highscore hunt, challenges to unlock different cosmetic items, all of that is more than fine and justifies the 20 dollar price tag, even though gameplay, story, graphics, everything is kinda basic.Best thing about the game is the pumping soundtrack (IF you like that sort of music, otherwise just skip this one, because without music it's not an enjoyable experience) that really doesn't skip a beat in any of the levels, at least up until 32/40, which is where I'm at right now.Basic gameplay starts out really good, an isometric brawler with an at first intriguing plot, short and adrenaline fuelled levels, a plethora of varied enemies, some okay bosses ... but then slightly before the halfway mark the game begins to seriously drag. It's not that levels get longer, but many of the fights are just gruelling, mainly because of either unblockable attacks, constantly blocking enemies or guns, guns, guns. I can't overstate how many guns there are in a BRAWLER game. Some enemy groups consist almost exclusively of people with guns, all moving away from you and 1 or 2 shotting you, even in the midst of other enemies, meaning you're pretty much ♥♥♥♥♥♥, unless you have some luck and can grab a gun yourself to dispose of the biggest threats.Then the game starts introducing enemies that are outright immune to anything but explosives, i.e. grenade launchers, which are only carried by other goons, enemies just start killing you instantly, bosses even more so. Then there's the "harvester" boss, and I will refrain from saying anything about that cancer of a boss design.After each level you get a skill point. Nice, too bad that about half of the skills are basically unusable and the other half are pretty much vital to your survival, so too bad if you've picked the wrong one, especially since you only see what the next skill in the tree is AFTER unlocking the previous one... and of course you can't respec. You can - for some inexplicable reason - DEACTIVATE an unlocked skill, but you do NOT get a skill point back. Baffling design decision. Since you can beat the game without any skill you're never really hard-locked from progressing, but like I said, some skills are just useless, while others trivialize most encounters.For example you have a dodge roll, which is very important, that can be upgraded to perform a haymaker at the end of said dodge roll. Too bad you can't aim the skill in any way, shape or form, so 9/10 times you will just hit air. This is the case for pretty much any movement based ability. They're crap, unless you're somehow god tier at using them ... and even then the other skills are just plain better. Like "grapple", which instantly grabs an enemy and kills them outright with only 2 skill points... Later on in the game you also get your own gun that can have various different bullets in it. Too bad that switching between those bullets incurs a LENGTHY cooldown period, making the different bullet types practically useless, especially since they reset after a death. You also get a rope gun, which might just be a better grapple ... you also get various different block counter abilities, and for the life of me I still haven't figured out what the difference between these 4 or 5 moves are. Funnily enough you are immune to any damage when you perform a "finisher", which you also have to unlock via skills. Too bad that all these cool abilities can put you in a situation where you die afterwards, because you're out of position after a 3 second animation ... I really wanted to be more positive, and the foundation is here, it's just that they somehow stopped developing and testing after about 10 out of the 40 levels. Enemies repeat themselves, just have different names, mostly, or are downright irritating, like being surrounded by 10 women with rope guns ... who want to rope you in, but only make you invulnerable for the duration... levels are full of instant kill mechanics (helicopters, snipers, rocket launchers...) and the few chase levels are all pretty terrible. The guns lack impact and depth, but are so prevalent you basically are forced to use them. At least death just means a quick reset to the last check point, which is mostly fair. The story devolves into bull crap and there's so many speech bubbles in each level that I'm wondering if I'm playing a brawler or an RPG ... you don't need a lot of story here, but if you do make the player read so much text, at least hire an author to write something that isn't 4th grader level. The music keeps me going, but the rest is just a chore now ...

_childDocuments_.review: My pros and cons with midnight fight express.Pros+ Fun and addicting game. It's like streets of rage but having the cool combat style of batman arkham series or sleeping dogs. + Good amounts of upgrades for your character which makes the combat even more fun and gives you a lot of more cooler moves at your disposal.+ A lot of variety of weapons and guns that can be used during fights.+ Good amounts of customizations for your character. From the skin color, to hair color, to the tattoos, and even the clothes, hats, pants, shoes. there are a lot of choices to choose from for you to buy or unlock.+ I like that they add a playground or a training mode that allows you to create your own scenario and gives you options to just mess around in the game.+ Every level aren't that long and can usually be done in 5 to 10 mins which is good for shortburst play or when you're playing on the go.+ Enemies and gangs do have a lot of varieties which keeps everything fresh. Which also forces you to change strategy and adapt to the situation.+ Soundtrack is great.Cons- Storytelling or dialogue interrupts the pace of the game at times.- Difficulty will just ramp up to max in the last remaining 10 levels and a once really enjoyable game will suddenly turn into a really frustrating slugfest. Everything you've learned from the early parts of the game like combos, parrying, counters, grappling, well just throw all of that combat mechanics away to the dumpster because those are almost completely useless on those levels. The last few levels have been generally reduced into a roll, punch, roll, punch, and roll some more soulslike survival type of game. When it comes to enemies some of them really needs some rebalancing, like for example gun wielders which are particularly the most annoying of all since it's hard to determine whether they're going to shoot or not. There are also some enemies that can do their unblockable attacks really fast and some that can also counter your attacks which is another really cheap way to ramp up the difficulty. Also don't get me started with zombies/robots and how easy it's for them to just lock you up in place and you can't do anything about it but wait for your inevitable death. The last few levels aren't even a beat em up game anymore because the dev just decides to fill the last 10 levels with dozens of gunners, goons that spam their unblockables, goons that can stunlock you, and bosses that can 1 hit kill you thus turning it into an insanely frustrating last level experience.- Graphics might not be for everyone.- Some of the level's layout will block your view. It wont be a big deal at the easy parts of the game but it will become really annoying once you reach the difficult levels.Overall midnight fight express is a fun game for the most part, but it's unfortunate that the late game difficulty would just makes you want to smash your keyboard or controller to the floor out of frustration. After I've beaten those hard parts I'm not even interested in replaying those levels anymore and I just want to be done with the game and move on to the next. Still I would give midnight fight express a thumbs up because the game is still mostly an enjoyable and fun experience for me. I know people complain about the vehicular levels or even the gimmick levels like the harvester or helicopter part, but I do find them cool. This is a 7/10 game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The city needs a hero and he appears right now. Midnight Fight Express is a new high-speed beat 'em up that offers the player a wide variety of combat combinations, a good arsenal of a wide variety of weapons, variable difficulty and many side challenges that give the game replay value. The game is divided into 40 separate levels, which can be replayed at any time with various modifiers. Not all levels are perfect in terms of game design, but most are definitely enjoyable, and some are just downright amazing. Combat movement feels incredibly smooth, which is almost the main trump card of the game, combos from various techniques are always exciting, the seams between switching techniques are not felt, you seem to weave a long thread of movements, weapons and accelerations. Unlocked skills also do not spoil the game, not incredibly strengthening the protagonist, but complement the overall action, weaving new components into it. The only thing I think is that the cool scorpion grappling hook could have been given earlier in the game; it opens too late when you are unlikely to radically change your move set.The visuals in the game are peculiarly minimalistic, it's a matter of taste, but the animations of all actions are luxurious. Music strikes the rhythm, making the heart beat faster. As for difficulty, I would advise you to first try out a couple of levels on normal difficulty, and then immediately switch to high in order to feel a challenge to your abilities. It's not so deadly here that you die with one hit, but it makes you feel the need to move quickly more strongly and requires the use of all the gameplay tools that the game gives you. During the whole game, 4-5 bugs were met, several times I got stuck irretrievably under the stairs and in the booth, and a couple of times the key point of the level did not appear after clearing all the enemies. And, well, there was a very strange thing when, upon obtaining an achievement, the game began to lagging a lot until the very end of the level (I don’t know if this is a problem on my end or if it’s a game problem). The story… Whatever it is, you hit your enemies in the face for the sake of a ghostly goal, that's the whole story. Everything is revealed a little closer to the finale, but we do not play such games for the sake of the Lynch plot.Midnight Fight Express is a good game that will allow you to relieve stress and disperse the blood in your veins. Adrenaline movement through the gloomy back streets of the city, where you are not welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express is a fantastic Hotline-esque brawler that forgets what makes it great.The game's heart-pounding core of pummeling between counters, takedowns, and weapon/terrain usage is unfortunately scarce in its 40-mission runtime, which is frequently interrupted by gluts of gunfire, clunky setpieces, and other flow-breaking nuisances like tons of bland dialogue/micro-cutscenes, being forced to start each level from the menu instead of being able to play continuously, and idling for enemy reinforcements.You will almost constantly be broken out of the excitement of mastering a set of enemies or a new upgrade with rude awakenings of janky instakill vehicles, shootouts with ranged enemies that have no visual indicators, and going on scavenger hunts to find weapons to kill nigh-invulnerable elites with. The game's pace goes from The Raid to The Room in a heartbeat, often holding you hostage in the latter until you figure out what the game wants so you can go back to playing it.This isn't just a few problem levels either, from Act III onwards the game includes ranged enemies in almost every wave, and includes ranged-only waves at least once a level, and by the time you're familiar with the tools to handle ranged enemies you're introduced to the  which ignore or actively punish using them.This is further frustrated by the game's controls struggling to keep up with its mechanics. This doesn't just mean the long, awkward pauses after certain actions that refuse most inputs, but also the game's contextual inputs constantly fluctuating: Try to rope gun an enemy? You'll grapple someone nearby in the opposite direction. Try to fire off a life-saving revolver shot to stagger an enemy? You'll trigger a wall takedown in the middle of a crowd. Want to pick up that shotgun? Sorry, one of the 20 pillows was closer.I would recommend this game in a heartbeat if it simply didn't have half its levels, as so many of the game's best fights are jammed between things like Helicopters and Queen of Scorpions.To put it bluntly, I look forwards to seeing what this developer comes up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:Dr - Great game. Awesome soundtrack. Fun gameplay. Tons of levels. Worth buying.Midnight Fight Express is absolutely fantastic and has cemented itself as one of my favorite beat-em-up games of all time! The fighting mechanics are stellar - allowing you to seamlessly alternate between fist-fighting, using melee weapons/guns, kicking/throwing objects laying about the ground, and grappling. In essence, this game is basically the best 'John Wick simulator' on the scene right now! Midnight Fight Express also boasts a fun parry/block/dodge/deflect system that will feel instantly familiar to those who have played the Arkham-series Batman games. You'll read about this in many of the other positive reviews and I mirror the sentiment: The music in this game is exceptional. I normally don't give two hoots about videogame soundtracks but this game boasts the first one that I've actually considered buying for personal listening - it's just that good! Of course, I won't because I'm a cheapskate...but I'm at least tempted and it's the thought that counts...right?My only real complaints about Midnight Fight Express lie with the character customization options. The game boasts a fairly large assembly of tops/bottoms/gloves/headgear to choose from but many of the options don't mix well together and some options only have a single viable counterpart (unless of course, 'unstylish dork' was the vibe you were chasing). Moreover, you can only customize a male character and can't give him any facial hair/body type traits (you can *technically* play as female/fat/bearded characters but these have to be unlocked as either playable enemy types or unlockable challenge characters). All things considered, this is a very minor complaint against what is, otherwise, a well-made game and I really hope that more customization options can be added as the game matures. *pro-tip: you can only unlock new moves by beating levels so beat the campaign first (to unlock the full roster of moves/actions) and THEN go back and replay levels for challenge completion. It'll be much easier that way and, frankly, it's just more fun to have all the moves at your disposal than to try and complete challenges without them (source: just trust me bro).

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if you had a game that is designed as a melee brawler. Now imagine if 2/3 of the way through you're suddenly introduced to an enemy type that counters melee attacks by automatically grabbing you for over half your health. Imagine if this attack staggered you, meaning they can chain stunlock you until you die if you don't frame perfect roll on wakeup (this is a melee brawler). Imagine being forced to rely on the game's half-baked gun mechanics. Imagine if, for the rest of the game, its been doing a sort of 80s action-camp "criminals have taken over the city" schtick and these are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ zombies for some reason.That's the experience playing this game. A very fun and satisfying brawler for 2/3 of the game until the devs decide they need to make the game "hard" by introducing an enemy type that negates your primary attack moves and basically your entire tech tree. Absolutely insane decision (not even going to get into the less annoying but still very badly designed environment-reliant guys who will only die to explosion damage) that has 100% flipped me from a game I'd recommend to anyone to a game that I'm not going to touch again. My only regret was hitting these guys an hour past the refund limit.

_childDocuments_.review: Top down isometric beat 'em up best played with a controller. The story is pretty nonsensical casting you as a sleeper agent for a criminal overlord. In addition to standard fighting, there are also a couple of vehicle levels that aren't bad, but nowhere near as satisfying as the fighting. And the fighting does feel really good. Remember the fighting in the Arkham Knight series? It's similar. There's also about a hundred weapons. Like bottles you can throw or break over someone's head. Clubs, knives, guns, fish, etc. They all wear out too, so you can't wield one for too long. Each level is scored based on your style (kill multiple ways), time, did you die, etc. I easily beat it in a few hours, but would absolutely play a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a nice atmosphere and feel to it, but the gameplay and progression is designed by an utter moron. I would love to recommend this game because off the bat, it was nice, simple, fun. But after a few levels it showed its hideous true face:Every level you pass awards you with 1 skill point which you can use to unlock a skill in the 5 skill trees!2 of the trees are unlocked later in the game, you can only see the next available skill while the rest remains hidden (The "trees" are almost as linear as you can get.) and if you got a cool looking skill only to find out it's utterly useless? Tough luck buddy! No refunds! Not to mention I had to disable some of these for some missions because they repeatedly got me killed. (Yup, something you need to spend resources to get has you be worse off than without it.)In order to artificially attempt to pad the gameplay time, the creator made it so that every level has 5 challenges that you can see/attempt to complete ONLY on your second or later playthrough of the level. 1 is to get an S ranking, 1 is to get 10 golden teeth and 3 of them are some specific things to do during the level. Most of these level-specific ones are a pushover, but there are some that are annoyingly specific or dependent on how well the physics system slept last night. And remember, even if the challenges unlock and you did everything it's asking on your first run: "Too bad! Didn't count!"Well, what do these challenges get you? They get you some cosmetics and perks which allow you to activate special modifiers for a level you've beaten already. Stuff like unbreakable weapons, being ungrabable by enemies, infinite ammo, spawning in with a weapon instead of empty hands, yada, yada, yada. Sounds like a great reward to help with those pesky challenges, doesn't it?! Of course it doesn't. Enabling ANY perk disables your ability to complete ANY challenges within the mission. So you have to pain yourself through the challenges in order to receive something that doesn't do anything apart from letting you faff about in a replay of a level when by the time you get a lot of these you'd be happy to never see those levels again.And of course lets not forget the fact that there are finisher animations of variable duration! Don't worry, the enemies are programmed to stop attacking you while performing a finisher. But of course time doesn't stop so if you get particularly "lucky" and get the longest animation as an execution in the cargo crane section or next to a live grenade, hope you love restarting and playing through something 50 times because the stars didn't align the last 48 times and when they did on the 49th, the game bugged out in such a way that you needed to restart the level or even the entire game.The game is good as an arcade/score chaser/time trial game. But quite literally everything tied to actual gameplay is a redundant tedium that rewards you with the opportunity to faff about in the game. (And I wish I was joking...) If your incentive is to get achievements or be a completionist and unlock everything the game has to offer, you will probably want to scratch your own or the developer's eyes out after a shorter-than-expected while.If you're fine with playing a game, ignoring things like achievements or challenges, you'll probably have a good time with this. But if you play with a goal in mind, your best bet is to avoid this game like the plague.

_childDocuments_.review: This game features smooth dynamic combat and makes it the game's selling point. It is a fun top down brawler which for the most part gets it right. The moves were all mocapped to provide a smoother experience, but one gripe I have is on level 30/40. Upon stumbling on the final quarter of the campaign we are introduced to enemies that will instantly parry you without any indicator, punishing you for the pre-established pattern that the game wanted you to get into- beating up people without hesitation. They overall slow down the rhythm of the game and force you to play passively. Playing on the hardest difficulty only makes this more frustrating.Guns in this game can prove to be troublesome at times with the awkward dodges that feel too long yet too short at times. On harder difficulties the guns tend to chunk out a substantial amount of health and some levels are just riddled with nothing but guns.Similar games that feature this kind of combat are Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor and Batman: Arkham City. Those games capitalize on the combat system they've implemented and do not force you to slow down as a result of a few measly enemies. I like this game, sure, but due to gimmicks like this- the game feels more of a chore than anything later on.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. Has a great foundation, the introduction, playground, menus, and first set of levels were good. Then more and more poorly thought out and executed mechanics are added until the combat just isn't fun anymore. It seems the further you go in the game, the more the fights become about chasing down backpedaling, gun/explosive welding enemies or whatever cheesy mechanic the latest enemy type introduces. Did I mention that this game introduces multiple new enemy types every level? The AI really struggles with combating you properly, and can be really frustrating. The developers also seem to really like the "untouchable enemy shoots at you while you fight the ads" and "dodge the big unblockable heavy attack" tricks, which can maybe be fun a few times, but come on. The game allows you to unlock new abilities, but most of them seem very situational at best (minus the parry tree). I also found it had very little real challenge and I was playing on the "Hard" difficulty.I initially liked the story direction because of it's tongue-in-cheek nature. However, (like the gameplay) it REALLY goes downhill after the first set of levels. It really feels like a 14 year old took a sharpie and wrote stale memes all over the script. After a certain point, every story beat is just "Hey guys! Remember Big Smoke from GTA: SA! Remember the memes?! How about Fight Club!?!" The original content seemed fun, so I'm really disappointed it's so reliant on those things, instead of standing on it's own as a media property. In short, I wish that this game chose to refine and add depth to it's foundational mechanics, instead of adding filler on top of filler over them until you can't see them anymore. If you REALLY are thirsting for a martial arts/beat'em up style game, and have already played other (better) games on the market (e.g. Sifu), then I'd say maybe try it, since you may find it more palatable than I do.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in around 5 hours and I had lots of fun. The game shines brightest in the first 20 levels when enemies arent too obnoxious and you can try combos and different weapons here and there. The art style is great and the music is probably the best part about the entire game. The levels feel unique enough for me to beat the entire game especially the different settings and movie/game references made me smile a couple of times. Any bad parts ?The kind if different levels where you are on a boat or a bike or a truck are all very boring. I dont know why the developer felt the need to completely abandon his fighting system in those levels and have a stupid gun section. Guns in general are a big problem. When your opponent has guns they are practically useless especially when you are in a certain range where the ai cant decide wether to shoot or run towards you. When you yourself have a gun for example an assault rifle you have 25 ammo which is enough to kill 5 people which will give you another gun from a corpse. Later in the game this will lead to levels which can be beaten without punching anybody and just collecting guns. So overall the gunplay feels great and powerful but guns make the game way too easy. The elevator level. If you played through the game this will resonate with you. Later in the game there is an elevator level where the fps was horrendous for me with corpses activated. Not only that but the developer thought it would be funny to throw 5 security guards in a small elevator all with guns where you have to land 1 punch and then roll for 10 seconds before being able to land a second punch. This is not fun. It is very obnoxious.The skill tree is a very interesting design choice. One of the most fun parts the grappling hook gets unlocked way too late into the game for my taste. It also takes you playing though the entire game until you have all the skills unlocked. I dont like this since there are many cool skills and mechanics that could keep somebody from quitting the game too early. I would have loved to have all the skills unlocked midway through the game so I could have carved out my own playstyle or something. Overall I think this is a fine game. Not a great game. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express is an isometric beat em' up game developed by Jacob Dzwinel and published by Humble Games (of the Humble Bundle site I believe, good for game key deals); I didn't really know anything about this game until a buddy of mine (shoutout to my dude Gage, love ya dweeb) who threw the trailer at me. As a huge fan of Hotline Miami and games like this, I immediately liked what I saw and gave it a wishlist before forgetting about it for a while. My buddy Casey picked it up around Christmas last year for me and I went in blind, and I was pleasantly surprised. The Plot is a simple one, you play as a dude named Babyface who is woken up by a strange talking drone up in a random apartment with no idea of what's going on; only the urging from the drone to trust him and take down the city's criminal organizations as they're enacting a plan that could doom the fate of humanity. Truth is that's really it, there are some twists and turns here and there but it mostly just feels like an excuse for the gameplay, but basically fight your way through waves of dudes to take down the Boss-On-High's criminal lieutenants while in-media-resing inside of an interrogation room as you recount your story for two detectives, Agent Smithman and Agent McCloon (which both come off as parodies of Agent Smith from the Matrix and John McClane even if it's in name only). I guess that's one thing I will mention is that it's definitely parody and homage based; you'll see references to stuff like  For the most part these are fine, though I feel like in the back of my mind it's a little jarring if you're actually trying to take the plot seriously, but for the most part I wouldn't take it seriously as the game doesn't really either, it's just going from set piece to set piece beating people up. Speaking of, the gameplay.The gameplay is pretty solid, repetitive sure in the beginning but definitely solid. If I could describe the gameplay (and game overall), I'd say it's a combination of Hotline Miami, Sifu and the atmosphere of My Friend Pedro. You go from place to place, picking up weapons, throwing them, doing combos, dodging and trying to manage your crowd while coming off as cool as possible. For me, it definitely worked enough to make me invest my time going into the challenge mode to replay all of these (though to my detriment as some of them tend to get really frustrating, like a level where you can't get hit by pepper spray once even though sometimes the stun animation doesn't even render and it's in enclosed spaces). Sometimes there would be glitches too where I'd beat all the enemies and then it wouldn't spawn in but I think that was because during the end I was god-modeing it to get the challenges done, I also think a restart checkpoint system would be advantageous to this effect just in case but for the most part it works well. Doing these challenges get you rewards like new props and enemies to fight in practice mode, cosmetics to create your own character (which you can do basically as soon as you get out of the tutorial I believe?), certain cheats for repeated runs, etc. Again to me the ease of challenges at the beginning give a lot of incentive to go through them, though keep in mind some of the later ones tend to be really frustrating and mind numbing. Keep in mind you get new abilities as you advance, like a 3D printer gun which regenerates ammo over time and can be great for parrying or removing certain enemies from play or a rope gun which can drag enemies to you amongst other abilities (though you get it a bit later in the game) and helps give a bit of combat variation. If I were to name a least favorite level it would be  but otherwise are for the most part decent if not challenging, especially the levels where . I guess to finish it off, the gameplay is good, and when it REALLY connects you feel like a f u c king god, or the human equivalent of that being John Wick or something; if you're in the mood for a good beat em up with variation it's a definite recommend.The graphics are rather minimalist as it understandably focuses on gameplay flow but it fits with the overall atmosphere, the environmental art design looks good and all the objects you can use to fight look like they fit in. No voice acting as far as I'm aware and the soundtrack is by a guy named Noisecream and by god did they do a fantastic job at the soundtrack that is immersive as hell in your murder spree, continuing the sort of synthwave (best I can explain) vibe that Hotline Miami, My Friend Pedro and The Hong Kong Massacre did to great effect. And that's basically what I could compare this game to, the love child of all of those games and it's a pretty solid title that'll take up your time if you're REALLY invested in it as I was these past couple of days (minus a few headaches). If you're into beating the s h i t out of people and don't care if the story takes a bit of a backseat I can definitely recommend for the full price it's asking, also get the soundtrack too it slaps.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hesitant yes.  The fighting is pretty solid and lots of stuff there.  The Gunplay...while is necessary is less fun.  Any vehicle type sequences are definately not fun.  There are also a couple sequences that were just pure torture.The hand to hand is where the game shines.  I love hitting things.  So any game that allows me that is my prefered style.KB&M - I am hesitant to comment on.  I went with default settings and wonder how much of my frustrations were because keys were not intuitive.  Game demands fast reations most of the time and the defaults didn't seem to work for me.  By the time I realized this partial acclimation had already happened and I was loath to change mid game.  I think this is more of a me problem coupled with age and my reaction speed is definatly slowed (and I get some sort of hand spasms after intense sessions (unlike in Skyrim for instance)(I got them bad in Absolver).  The Gun play is servicable, but hardly a joy.  It seems like it fights you where the H2H play is very smooth.  The secondary weapon while useful, takes some getting use to.  The pickup guns are sometimes more trouble then they are worth.  I would often pick up and immediately drop, Find I couldn't shoot (because enemy was close) and generally I hated having to use them.  I was resentful that the enemy never ran out of bullets, hit with every shot and could pick up guns dropped by others at a greater range than I could.Vehicle sequences are mechanically fine, but I resent them due to long history in gaming.  I always hate these sequences.  They are frustrating because I don't feel they add anything to THIS game in particular.  They are not a joy and I did not have fun.  I have no control over speed. HATE THAT and yes there is one in this game as well.Overall I didn't regret my time spent but ....I just don't see myself playing long term. Also, the dialogues do not negatively affect the dynamics of the game, only adding variety to the process of killing the next batch of enemies. I recommend that you carefully read  between levels. The story itself is interesting, cute and, which is very important to me personally,  There is quite a lot of conervatism in it. There is no Woke-agenda or anything like that. I think it is a meta-modernist story.I highly recommend this game to fans of the bitmap genre and other games where there is an emphasis on melee and complex combo attacks. _childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express Review: Punches, Guns, and Drone-Fueled MayhemRating: 8.5 out of 10.0"Midnight Fight Express" is a stylish, action-packed ride through a city drowning in criminal chaos. You step into the shoes of "Babyface," a mysterious fighter dragged back into the underworld with only a cryptic drone as your guide. What follows is a relentless brawler that mixes cinematic flair with fluid combat mechanics.The High-Impact Combos (Pros)+ Thrills from the Jump: The game wastes no time, throwing you straight into its frantic, blood-pumping action.+ Satisfying Combat Mechanics: With fun, responsive controls, there's plenty to master—yet the learning curve never feels punishing.+ Customization Galore: Leveling up to unlock skills and gear keeps progression fresh and rewarding. It's like building your very own John Wick simulator.+ Intense Soundtrack: The music syncs perfectly with the chaos, making every punch, kick, and gunshot feel that much more impactful.+ Quick Hit Gameplay: The short levels make it a great pick-up-and-play experience. Ideal for when you have just 10-15 minutes to spare.+ Isometric Delight: The isometric perspective suits the game's blend of tactical combat and brawling madness, offering a cinematic view of your destruction.+ Endgame Elevation: While the midgame can drag a bit, the final stages ramp up the action, throwing new enemies and level types into the mix. It’s a satisfying payoff for the grind.The Bruises (Cons)- Weapon Overload: Sure, using a chair or a gun to decimate enemies is thrilling, but weapons are so ubiquitous and overpowered that hand-to-hand combat often takes a backseat. Great for winning; bad for variety.- A Bit Too Easy: On normal difficulty, the game feels forgiving, with only a handful of challenging moments. It’s more power fantasy than punishing brawler.- Midgame Repetition: Around the 12-15 level mark, the gameplay loop starts to wear thin. New enemy types and level designs help, but pacing might push you to take a break.Verdict: Sifu Lite Meets John Wick"Midnight Fight Express" is the perfect game for when you're short on time but still want to feel like an action movie star. It’s fast, fun, and flashy, offering bite-sized bursts of adrenaline. While the midgame repetition and overpowered weapons might soften the impact for some, the overall experience is undeniably entertaining.For less than $10, it’s an easy recommendation—especially if you want a "Sifu lite" experience with a touch more guns and chaos. Whether you’re looking to play through the whole story or just smash through a level or two in between life’s obligations, "Midnight Fight Express" delivers the goods.

Stuff like this is more important than you might think – you really don’t want to deflate all the gravity from the situation with utter clownery every 5 minutes in your hardcore ultra-violent bass-pounding bloodbath. Pick a tone and stick with it, if you want to make River City Girls – just make River City Girls.Oh, and in the end game kinda have a gall to ask as to take the dramatic bits seriously.This game has no dialogue mode hidden in the options and I’m inclined to recommend it. It is far from ideal solution, but, you know, lesser evil.The gameplay is really fun tho, the game has that much needed umph when you smash faces. I read a lot of gameplay grievances in negative reviews, but they are either not so bad in my casual scrub normal mode or the dev just fixed them all. Like zombies for example – yeah, they are annoying, but it’s just one not very great gimmick level out forty of them.I eat it up with gusto in almost one sitting, so the game must makes something right, trash story notwithstanding.===============================================The bike level legit physically hurts my eyes tho

_childDocuments_.review: On your harsh journey through 40 different locations in the city, you will encounter many dangerous guys. Nearly every level features a new type of enemy, which is nice because it keeps you from getting bored beating up the same dudes over and over again. Some of them are strong and will punch, slice or shoot you. Also, there are some bosses who will want to stop you on your furious journey. To beat 'em all, you'll need to learn and master various skills that you can unlock by completing levels. In the beginning, you can use light and heavy strikes, later on, you can learn how to grab and throw someone, combine moves to create nice combos and much more.Your fists are not the only weapons you can use, you will also get two gadgets – a revolver with special bullets and a rope, and just as the enemies use different items, you can use them too. From simple melee weapons like a wooden plank, or baseball bat to lethal ones like a knife, axe or cleaver to firearms like a pistol, a SMG, an assault rifle and even there is a rocket launcher. There are also lots of items on the ground that you can pick up and throw or kick in someone's face.There are some hidden Easter eggs or references to other games, movies and more in the game that you may miss on your first playthrough, but you can replay levels to find them, complete challenges, try a higher difficulty or increase your score. I highly recommend replaying all the levels as you can unlock nice character customization options and various perks that make the game harder, easier or more fun.There is only one thing that bothered me during my playthrough – the cutscenes and speech bubbles. On the first playthrough, it is very annoying because the game is fast-paced with a nice soundtrack, but after a short fight you get a cutscene that introduces a new enemy type or a speech bubble that you have to read (there is no dabbing), so it spoils the flow. It would be better to tell a story and present new enemies differently. After completing a level, you can choose to skip these, but it only fast-forwards instead of skipping them entirely. I enjoyed the game more when I checked this option. Levels had better flow with "skipped" cutscenes and dialogues.

_childDocuments_.review: John Wick Simulator. Midnight Fight Express is an adrenaline  filled rush of a game that has you beating, grappling and shooting your way through hoardes of enemies as you attempt to take down a kingpin crime villain whom has taken over the city. The martial aspect of the game is incredibly satisfying and all well put together. All of the choreo is great. As you progress through the game you get skill points which allow you to get new moves and abilities including parries, grapples and finishers. You are also able to use a variety of weapons and objects strewn throughout the levels and on enemies. All of these also have some great execution moves and all feel generally satisfying to use. Each level also typically adds some variety either being through different weapons, enemy types, hazards and even a couple of vehicle sections. Whilst the vehicle levels are a bit sparse, they're fine overall and don't take too long to get through but just add a bit of variety. The best part about the variety in the game is that the game is filled with curveball enemies. There's your average thugs, poisonous cannibals, Swat teams, assassins, Pirates, all sorts. They really went balls to the wall with the variety and it works quite well overall. Additionally, whilst not something I have dabbled around with yet, the game has a lot of optional content to add some replay value. There are challenges in each level as well as attaining a high ranking, a global leaderboard (Wish I could also set it to friends and region)  and gold teeth that can be collected. You also have a variety of cosmetics that you can either unlock through said challenges or buy through acquiring money as you play. There's also a hard and ultra hard difficulty for those that want even more of a challenge. Some of the reviews on here generally complain about things such as enemies having guns or certain sections of the game becoming unfun but honestly I cannot disagree more. Yes, the game gets more difficult with time and yes, there are enemies with guns but the game also gives you the tools to deal with them. By the end of the game where more enemies are more heavily equipped I was able to dodge around, whip weapons out of people's hands and throw dudes which made the ranged aspect of enemies largely nullified. I will say some areas are a bit more difficult than others but the game is rather fair in its level of challenge and difficulty as the game progresses so long as you adapt. Additionally death is just a quick checkpoint reset so it's not frustrating either. In terms of the story and writing the game is decently done. It's not anything groundbreaking as it is generally a revenge plot with a couple of twists and turns that you can figure out reasonably early on. The writing is however rather enjoyable with a plethora of references to a variety of things such as Mortal Kombat, Fight Club and even Popeye. The writing is daft and keeps the tone a little lighter. Again, a common complaint is that the talking interrupts the flow of the game but this is why you check the options menu. There's a means of disabling it. As for the aesthetic and sound side of things. The sound track is stellar with thumping electronic and metal beats really adding on a layer of brutality to the games punchy and crunchy sound effects as you dispatch and slaughter your way through your enemies. I wish the guns sounded a little more punchy as they generally sound weaker than your fists but otherwise most of it is done well. Visually the game doesn't have much flair with models being identifiable but having no real overall stand out style. Everything looks to be of an acceptable quality however and again the actual choreo and animations really shine. All in all I cannot recommend this game enough to anyone who watched John Wick and wanted a game where you felt like just as much of a badass. It's a solid entry from the developer and something worth checking out. I look forward to what they produce next.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express : By Triple FStrap on your knuckles and prepare for a wild ride through the criminal underbelly of a nameless city. "Midnight Fight Express", a 2022 indie gem, throws you headfirst into a brutal ballet of brawling. But beneath the surface of bone-crunching combos and environmental takedowns lies a surprisingly deep combat system and a narrative shrouded in intrigue.The story starts with a bang, or rather, a drone strike. You awaken as Babyface, a tattooed amnesiac with a knack for violence. A mysterious drone named DRONEY informs you the city is under siege by a criminal syndicate, and it's up to you to stop them before sunrise. The narrative unfolds in snippets between levels, piecing together Babyface's past and the motivations behind the city's takeover. While the plot itself is a pulpy blend of action movie tropes and light conspiracy, it serves as a decent framework for the real star of the show: the combat."Midnight Fight Express" transcends the button-mashing stereotype of classic beat-'em-ups. The combat is a meticulously crafted dance of offense, defense, and environmental awareness. Motion-captured animations bring a level of fluidity and brutality to every punch, kick, and throw. Dodging, parrying, and countering enemy attacks become second nature as you weave through throngs of thugs.The real depth comes from the combat styles you unlock. Each style, like "Secondary Gun" or "Rope," introduces a unique set of moves and combos. You can chain basic attacks into devastating finishers, juggle enemies in the air with well-timed throws, or disarm foes and use their own weapons against them. Experimenting with these styles and mastering their flow is immensely satisfying.The levels themselves become an extension of your combat repertoire. "Midnight Fight Express" doesn't shy away from environmental takedowns. You can hurl enemies into electrical boxes, launch them off balconies, or use parkour moves to gain the upper hand. Improvised weapons like pipes, bottles, and even severed limbs litter the environment, adding another layer of tactical choice to the brawls."Midnight Fight Express" is a visual and auditory treat. The comic book-inspired art style pops with vibrant colors, and the character designs are full of personality. The soundtrack is a pulsating mix of electronic beats and synthwave that perfectly complements the high-octane action. Every punch, kick, and bone crack is accompanied by a satisfying sound effect, further emphasizing the brutality of the combat.While "Midnight Fight Express" excels in its core gameplay, there are a few aspects that could be improved. The story, while intriguing, feels underdeveloped. The enemy variety, while decent, could benefit from more distinct fighting styles in later levels. Additionally, the single-player focus might leave some players yearning for a competitive or co-op mode.Despite these minor shortcomings, "Midnight Fight Express" is a knockout. It's a love letter to classic beat-'em-ups, offering a modern take on the genre with its deep combat system, environmental integration, and stylish presentation. If you're looking for a game that will test your reflexes, unleash your inner action hero, and leave you wanting more, then "Midnight Fight Express" is a must-play.
