_childDocuments_.review: Update: The developer has fixed a lot of the issues in my initial review, and is a lovely individual.Enemy balance has been tweaked, there are less guns, some of the more impossible challenges have been removed. Skill progression being locked behind levels has also been removed. Some of the enemy design still sucks, and bosses (especially the final boss) have problem moves. There have been a lot of quality of life fixes, such as the ability to throw back thrown items instead of having to roll. Overall, I think the game is much more worth the asking price now, although there still is a lot of issues with the game's general level design. Definitely buy on sale, and buy it full price if you're willing to put up with some frustrating parts.Original Review Below:Overall a pretty fun game, but multiple balancing issues, especially in the latter half of the game, make it hard to recommend right now. My first play through was on Realistic difficulty, which you honestly should avoid until you get all the upgrades on a first play through on a lower difficulty, so YMMV.It's definitely worth its asking price and it is really fun when it works, but enemy design and level design is really spotty throughout the game, and it makes it a little hard to recommend at launch until some areas are fixed.- Enemy attacks are seemingly unparryable at random as enemies have very similar animations for parryable attacks or they have nearly no windup animation at all. -A lot of enemies are have way to much armour as well as unparryable moves. The longer into the campaign, the worse it gets. The latter half of the game feels like just spamming dodge roll in order to survive rather than a smooth brawling experience.-The last third of the game practically dumps brawling and throws enemies with guns at you the entire time. Gun enemies are infuriating to fight since they will practically always hit you unless you're spamming roll, and they have incredible accuracy. meaning you'll probably get shot through a crowd of melee enemies you're fighting. This is much worse on realistic difficulty when you have no health regen, making it just a matter of time before you die to bullets.-Some enemies are just completely unfun to fight. One enemy that shows up in the last third of the game has pepper spray with ridiculous range that stuns you for a very, very long time, making you completely stop fighting and makes you practically a free kill. Large enemies also spam an unblockable ground pound that seemingly knocks you down at random, sometimes even after you dodge roll which ruins the flow of combat.-Level design is spotty with stage hazards that show up constantly. One level has a motorcycle that periodically chases you and will almost always kill you instantly if it even grazes you (at least on realistic difficulty). The motorcycle also explodes if it hits a wall, and the hitbox is at least twice the size of the actual explosion effect. Many of the other stage hazards throughout the game are simply a variation of a instant kill zone that is periodically marked with an X for you to dodge. It happens frequently enough to get really stale.-Skill progression really, really sucks. You only get one point for each level you complete, meaning you have to beat the game in order to get all the skills unlocked. Crucial skills, such as parrying weapons while you're unarmed are locked behind a level gate, meaning you can't even unlock them until you beat a certain level, even if you spent the points towards unlocking them. These level restrictions also don't appear until you far enough into the skill tree to unlock them.-Some skills are just garbage. The entire grapple tree is nearly useless since stopping to grab one person lets the rest of the group get free hits on you, and the grapple system only works on enemies with broken defence gauges (which are invisible on realistic with no other indicator). Throwing enemies with skills is also terrible since getting hit during the throw animation, which is ridiculously long, cancels it.-Completion isn't very fun or intuitive. Optional challenges to complete for extra content in the form of cosmetics range from something you would do in the level on a normal play through to challenges that require you to meander and farm a very certain condition for a long time due to random circumstances, such as waiting for enemies to kill each other with friendly fire. Random pickups of golden teeth that can drop from enemies are also random, and may take an upwards of 5 to 6 replays of a single level in order to farm 10 teeth pickups per level.-Bosses suck. They will instant kill you with nearly unreactable moves constantly, and practically every single boss is just a variation of an existing enemy type with infinite armour and all unparryable attacks. Bosses are usually also surrounded by regular enemies, which will usually also spam unparryable attacks to spam roll through. The final boss is especially awful to fight, as they have a full screen ranged attack that has nearly no telegraphed start up that always kills you instantly on realistic difficulty. -Story is pretty forgettable, especially since it's entirely delivered through text boxes. Your companion Droney, has the tendency to simply annoy you with way too much filler text to skip through, which really slows down the pacing of the game, and only serves to make players skip the dialogue as fast as possible to get back to gameplay. All in all, when you are fighting through regular enemies you don't have to dodge roll spam through, and you've unlocked most of the skills in the game, Midnight Fight Express is a genuinely gorgeous and fun experience to play through. However, I don't think it should be necessary to complete the game once in order to have the full experience, and the multitude of smaller issues adding up make it a slog to play through the first time. Hopefully these issues are addressed, because I genuinely do love this game despite its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a bopping soundtrack held back by pacing issues worse than Dragon Ball Z. The passable combat is constantly broken up by cut scenes and dialogue for a story I wish I could care about. There is a "turn off dialogue" option that only somewhat makes up for this as you are still interrupted by a cutscene every time you enter a new room in the level.If you want to try a no death run, you will have to sit through a loading screen and then every cutscene again upon restarting a level.Outside of the terrible pacing the combat is pretty flawed. Hotline Miami kept combat quick and brutal as everyone died in one hit. This game is more like Arkham in a sense that you mash the attack button and pray your character locks onto the guy winding up to smack you for half your health. Sometimes you get it, and sometimes you don't. The skill system the game offers tries to give you some more options in combat but they don't always work and sometimes you just have to accept that your character targeted the guy with nothing in his hands while the guy with the shotgun just blasts you in half. Enemy health can turn combat more into a chore in the later levels and on higher difficulties. I honestly am not sure what balance they were going for here as the music makes me want to play fast and brutal but the combat rewards more patient play.This last point is minor, but it really added to my confusion, the tone of the game is all over the place. All presentation style will tell you they're going for a really gritty ultraviolent feeling as you witness criminals executing innocent civilians in the streets. Then it turns out the criminals are called "Bozos" backed up by women in bunny girl outfits with knives. You fight them off with plungers before going to a game dev studio where you fight off a swat team with pillows and nerf guns.I'm splicing some levels together here but I witnessed all of these in an hour of gameplay and I'm completely confused what tone the game is going for. Maybe this specific blend of humor is lost on me.Overall it pains me to say I would probably only consider getting this game on a sale and even then I only recommend the soundtrack. I hope the devs learn from their mistakes and make an even better game next time, because they're pretty close to having something enjoyable here, it's just not quite there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game a while ago when that Indie showcase event was up years ago. I never got to play the demo, and I got this through last month's Humble Monthly. I'm honestly glad I didn't pay full price for this wasted potential of a game.I don't think I've ever seen something with so much potential crash and burn because of so many terrible design decisions. I may get flamed for this, but I really cannot overlook the bad in the good in this. If this really was made by one person, then the little successes the game has is to be commended-the melee takedowns look very satisfying to pull off and look just as painful, but that is a pittance compared to the myriad of questionable design decisions, that it feels like the dev took design advice from the back of a book they found in the washroom.The story is also absolutely abysmal, where the comparisons to Hotline Miami are surface level at best, it is by far a Hotline Miami 2 situation where the creeping and overuse of guns kills the experience, even worse than in that game, it's almost as if none of the lessons that should have been learnt were applied here as well. The game also suffers from overexplanations, where Hotline Miami worked due to its story that had to be found in the background, Midnight Fight Express explains too much, and while it tries to go for a tongue in cheek tone, it's just not my style. It's also not very cohesive in its referential stages, doing it because of "wouldn't that be cool?". It's also very obvious there was no one else to veto the stupid and questionable decisions story wise and gameplay wise. I don't know what to make of the tone. One minute you'll have an organ harvesting scheme, then you'll be having a pillow fight with video game devs. The game makes a Fight Club and a Hotline Miami reference in the same level, while simultaneously being one of the worst levels to get through, with suiciding bikers constantly harassing you, making it hard to get an S rank. This is just one of among many in the game's later half, where it feels like the 40 levels were there as a number to accomplish, and not because all of them were hand-crafted to any kind of coherence at all. When the story has you fighting people from the norm (Ratmen, zombies, and robots???), it becomes an absolute chore to play through because often, these enemies are not fun to fight, or requires you to only play one way to get through it. This would be fine as far as game design goes, if this developer knew how to do escalation right.What do I mean by this? The way this guy likes to escalate things, is often, by instakilling you in certain levels in tight spaces. If this were like Hotline Miami where everything oneshots you and you also oneshot most things, it would be fine. But you can take a certain amount of hits, and when the game forces you to do conditions that would make even a child question why the game is so baffling in its usage of raising the stakes, it makes you wonder, if the game could have been better if there were someone to just say no, instead of putting something that seems cool, but with worse executions than influencer live events. It is just not satisfying at all to play these parts.Remember those zombies I was talking about? That's a good level to talk about how the stakes are "raised" in a frustrating way. These zombies will instantly grapple you and take a chunk of your health away (They used to instakill, so that doesn't surprise me), while leaving little room to run away if surrounded. Not only does this narratively break from the flow (No, the fact that the Big Bad has his hands in literally everything, from creating ratmen to investing in the occult to the stereotypical robot uprising to cull the herd type-BS, is not an excuse for the game's narrative shortcomings, for crying out loud, even the Popeye enemy was admitted as a lazy enemy type put in, that's the level we're working at), but it also creates an awkward level running around for guns to shoot zombies, breaking the usual flow of working through arenas to fight through. And then they never show up again. Every time the game decides to do a reference or just put in stuff they think would be cool, it almost always results in a piss poor level to play through because the level is not designed well enough to compensate for the game's overall frame. For a game that rewards variety of moves, these levels almost always force the player to play a certain way, another failing of Hotline Miami 2's gun-centric levels, which are also common here too, where disabling the goons with guns is a top priority. This on top of the arbitrary challenges, makes the game even more frustrating to do at certain points.The challenges are also just some of the worst things I've ever seen in a video game in recent memory. Do not get this game if you are an achievement hunter, as I honestly felt myself breaking down and am contemplating not going through with finishing this pile of dung heap. Some of them are so hard to do when taking into account the design decisions, that it really feels like a cruel joke on the dev's part (Don't get hit by pepper spray in tight corridors with bad enemy placements is the reason I'm writing this, honestly) Please don't waste my time with not only terrible design decisions, but also terrible conditions to "completing" your game as well. (Edit: The death counter stopped at 250, so I had to grind the 250 other deaths in one sitting. If you're going to put in pointlessly grindy achievements, at least make the counter work...)The music is fine, but considering it's all only from one person, and not a combination of songs from different artists like in Hotline Miami, they couldn't do that much to stand out compared to that. It's not my style, but maybe it'll be to others liking.I don't remember being this angry at such a game with such a promising frame. The house looks stable, yes, but it's no better than a house of cards when you account for the dev's inexperience of escalation, the myraid of references because they didn't know how to make an original story to compensate for it (even when it is, it's not that great), the poorly executed design decisions, and frankly, the Jesus skin has more thought put into it, with the nails in his hands, than some of the levels in the game. Just how? I would seriously ask the dev to learn more about how to make a more satisfying game as a whole before releasing that supposed DLC of his, or another game in general. I'm usually very mild mannered in my critiques, but this game has made my blood boil in the short amount of hours I've tried to play this compared to even some other games, and that's saying something.

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun at first, but then I realized that there were 40 levels of this game, which just felt way too much.Imagine that you're playing a Batman game, but you ONLY have the combat, all the time. You just run from place to place and there's more combat. Sure you get new skills from time to time which spices it up, but about 1/3 of the game I unlocked everything I was using. A problem with this game that funnily enough Elden Ring also faces is that I would've liked to have less levels and made the game shorter but create more varied gameplay.Another problem this game has that's exact same problem as another game is that you really enjoy the fun melee combat in the beginning but then later in the game, just like in Resident Evil 5, the enemies start equipping themselves with ranged weapons. This results in you having to dodge constantly and sometimes even getting shot from an enemy that isn't even on your screen, making it absolutely impossible for you to dodge that bullet, this is what really made everything way more boring for me and I had to use a way more boring and strange play-style to counteract these types of enemies.5/10. Would've gotten a higher score if there were less ranged enemies ( or none at all ), and if the game was shorter but had more varied content.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. I understand the need for a "Mid" rating now.   I LOVE games that throw everything at you, test your reflexes and reward your skills by making you feel like the baddest man alive. Games like Sifu, or The Batman Arkham series, where you're constantly surrounded or facing a horde of villains, dodging, parrying and fighting until you're surrounded by the ailing bodies of defeated bad guys...  Sadly, this game doesn't quite nail that feeling. It's funny, goofy, violent and almost nails that feeling of rhythmic fights that require you to adjust your focus and be aware of your surroundings. For me though, the controls are a little too un-intuitive to make the game feel good. Holding the Left stick in a certain direction while parrying for certain skills doesn't quite work for me. The aiming/locking onto of enemy characters is rough too; I never quite know exactly what's in my sights for a weapon throw or firearm.   The abilities you can unlock are neat, but the execution is a crapshoot. Sometimes I'll pull off a rolling uppercut, sometimes I roll too far and punch a stationary couch because the punch pops off at the end of your roll, not when or if you press the attack button near an enemy. Run and slide? Sure... sometimes. Finish off an enemy with a cool grapple move when they're low health? Yeah! Well... Maybe. It's far faster to just press the left shoulder button and finish them off when the prompt shows if you have the ability. Pulling off the cool moves you unlock just feels like a hassle. The enemies don't make it any easier with how they move, roll, can have unclear AOE attacks (Molotovs, Heavy enemy jump attacks... you know who you are), or janky indicators for their attacks (Looking at you Train Level).    If the interaction of attacks could be a bit more ... i guess, sticky might be the word? I feel the game and combat would flow better. Too often i feel like I'm focused on one enemy, he ragdolls a bit and get's out of range, and I'm punching air, or I try to get a hit on a different enemy but don't properly get a good "lock" on them and punch air too.    The concept is great, and having gunplay thrown in seemed like a recipe for a good John Wick-like experience, but the execution is just not polished enough for me. In fact, the aiming issues with melee are amplified when trying to use firearms. It's hard to tell what you're hitting too, since the firearms (save for like... the shotgun I suppose) don't have much punch to them and the indicator is a tiny dot that dances from one enemy to another.   I'm almost 20 levels in, and while they're bite sized and fast, I honestly don't know if I feel like finishing the game. Going back to earlier levels with my unlocks is the coolest I feel because there's the right amount of enemies, firearms are less plentiful and you can actually go ham with melee fights. The one thing that pushed this game into the recommend side is the soundtrack, which will fire you up.. just wish the gameplay matched it. That, and the hope that updates are made and the gameplay is tweaked a bit, because it's almost there....

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a stellar button mash and parry beat-em-up that, for some strange reason, seems to continuously forget what makes it good. The punchy motion capture is nowhere when the game demands that you fire a gun from the back of an on-rails vehicle for a level, or face enemies that can only be defended against by using an entire arsenal. The gunplay isn't particularly good, it's the same control scheme you'd see in a thousand games like this: one trigger to aim, one stick to rotate your character. It's satisfying as a way to solve a problem in a pinch or to kill with flair, but the gameplay suffers hard when it insists on making you a sharpshooter instead of a brawler. What could be one of the easiest recommendations you could ever make in terms of "casual beat-'em-up you play an hour or so at a time of" really falters because it seems to lack confidence. If I want to play a bunch of Midnight Fight Express, it punishes me with disappointing levels meant to break up the pacing. If I only play a little Midnight Fight Express, I'm eventually going to stop on a level that doesn't feature any hand-to-hand combat and never pick it up again. I don't feel like I'm being rewarded for wanting to play more of the game.Other than that, though, it's really good. The motion capture and moveset feel impactful, and the progression keeps replaying levels for challenges fresh by offering new approaches as you advance. The actual meat of the experience is extremely enticing, and it instantly became a go-to game for me after first playing it. The issue is mostly in the surrounding content. The humor is very "one-person development team with more ideas for mechanics than content" in the sense that it's all references that are more or less flat. Midnight Fight Express can't trust itself to provide a convincing evil chef, so instead you fight Cannibal Jon Favreau. When it wants an interesting gang to throw at you, it sends The Warriors, or Grove Street Families, or the cast of Hotline Miami. Not every character or arc is a reference, though, and the game is at its best when in these scenes. One of my favorite levels is the Game Studio, where you engage in a mandatory pillow fight with a crew of vague game developers who are having a wrap party on a game they've been crunching on. There are some interesting turns and a memorable boss at the end, all of which were original and all of which SHINED. The reference enemies stand out even more thanks to the inclusion of hidden "special characters", who have a line or two of dialogue that consists either of game lore or attempts at humor, some of which are funny! It's bizarre that the original dialogues are in the collectibles and the references are in the main cast. There are also several characters and pieces of dialogue that feel questionable racially, but hey, at least the music is killer. Midnight Fight Express is a really fantastic experience when it lets itself be. It lets you chokeslam people to death. It has an unnecessary amount of flaws, but there's a tremendous game underneath all of it. Despite everything I said, I think there's enough good here to be worth a try, but it's the type of game that you just wish was a little bit better.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat-em-ups are a rare sight these days so whenever something comes out it's a novelty. MFE offers a rather simple system to pick up, not straying far from the bamham formula (light attack strings, a heavy attack, contextual finishers and a grab), adding a couple of utility items to it: a gun (which can fire a variety of bullets with different effects, such as paralysis, electroshock or knockdown) and a rope (which can bring enemies closer, used to get closer to enemies, disarm them, etc.). Once all skills are unlocked and you have a solid grasp of the mechanics, you become the main coreographer of an action movie, being a better John Wick game than the official John Wick game itself, also courtesy of the very well animated and satifyingly vicious finishing moves (especially the ones involving guns). On top of everything there's a great electronic soundtrack by Noisecream, with a track for each level, counting up to 48 tracks including the menu and non combat music.Unfortunately this is far from a perfect game and the first problem I have with it is quite apparent: it lacks a distinct aesthetic. The isometric view can work with a low poly game, but it unfortunately lacks any sort visual flair. The UI, while functional and very readable, is very forgettable.The single biggest missed opportunity is the lack of a level editor and modding. While the game offers some replayability by having extra objectives and S-ranks to achieve (giving you extra customization options), a level editor would allow this game to retain a playerbase for far longer, giving the players the opportunity to recreate iconic movie scenes, or stretch the combat systems to their limit. Overall it's a 7.5/10, at full price it may be a bit eh, but on sale it's more than worth it. Should the dev add modding support and a level editor in the future its retail price would be 100% worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not trying to poopoo on the creative elements of the dialogue in this game, but I think it takes away from where the game really shines; kicking truckloads of ass to the tasty tunes, man. The combat's good, that's the mainest thing.Noisecream backing you up with the OST does an amazing job of propelling you to the frontline and psyching you up with these tracks, making you all cocksure and soooo ready to stomp ass indiscriminately, but you just get bogged down in the constant conversation, words words words, then *oh no* there goes your combo meter score. There goes your tattoo money. Enjoy your F rating and learn to speedread, idiot. So I turned off dialogue (and it's nice this is an option) after about 20 levels, and it was so much more enjoyable, but I felt I was missing out on the off-chance it was a dumb joke that I loved. I'm glad I turned it back on towards the end because it actually goes somewhere with the story. Turns out to be not so bad,  and this is all super opinionated, ymmv. Maybe I'm just a ♥♥♥♥ or too high-brow or a snob about comedy or whatever, but y'know I get it if people hate the story the most because it's 80% stupid and interrupting here. The jokes that landed I loved though. They're in there, I swear. The game's good enough for 20 bucks all day, totally fair. Good amount of content, 40 stages, some are short. Replayability is speed-killing through stage unique challenges, posting up on timed&score leaderboards, and racking up cosmetic unlocks. Do you wanna be Jason? Do you wanna be Jacket?  Do you wanna purge, like that guy in the movie, "The Purge"? If you wanted to recreate that bus scene from "Nobody" and play as Bob Odenkirk, this is the game for you.Cool stuff here, Poland. I looked forward to this one for awhile now. Thank you, Jacob Dzwinel.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: My only real complaint is the final boss. Perhaps it was because I didn't have the right skills equipped, but even so, fighting a single enemy shouldn't take this long.Other than that, this is one of the finest action games I have ever played. It really captures the feeling of being a proper action hero. Martial arts, guns, vehicles, and tons and tons of violent takedowns. I'm honestly surprised not more people have made a game like this, because it just seems like a gold mine. This game was a blast from start to finish, and it was very much worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: The dev listened. Everything I had a problem with had been addressed in the 1.01 patch that was rolled out recently, so everything I complained about below just pretend I said the opposite.Except the knife guys, they're still nonsense.- Old Review -First, before butthurt virgins start giving me some free 🤡 points, please leave a comment explaining how I'm wrong. No, seriously, please do. I want to actually enjoy this game and if there is something I'm missing, I really want to know.Fundamentally, this is a game that has a lot of potential for creative and cool fisticuffs. And then the enemies in the game take a fat steaming dump all over that potential.Enemies will attack you with guns like they're in a third person shooter and not a brawler. They'll freely walk out of your swing range and dump their magazines into you, even if you have the long range strike skill unlocked. Dual wielding knife enemies swipe away at you with fast, unblockable, armored flurries that make you roll constantly, and who also block constantly block your hits. You can only reliably grab people when you've already pounded on them which defeats the point of grappling them. There are so many unblockable attacks coming at you at once you find yourself rolling all over the place like it's dark souls. You can mitigate it with an upgrade, but not nearly enough.Even without dealing with the worst of the enemy types, regular fights have their own dumb problems. Enemy attacks are all about magnetism: they will either skate across the ground in a split second to smack you in the back of the head, or they will just swing open air. What the Arkham games (a clear inspiration for this) got right was always making it clear that you're about to get hit by having the enemy travel while he's delivering the punch. It looked goofy, but it worked as clear communication to the player. Here, the travel and the punch are both instant. Even if the counter icon fades out, you might still be in the enemy's magic teleportation circle.Ultimately, you're almost never completely sure whether it's safe to start having fun with your moves.Enemies also have an aggravating tendency to shove you with a 1 frame push move that leaves you staggered for a full second if you just happen to get close. In a game that relies so heavily on magnetism to make blows connect, it's all too easy to have your character get punked because the combat system's automation and spotty targeting made you brush against another enemy on your way to attack someone. Getting passed around like a $20 hooker is not uncommon.So much of the game just feels awkward. Dodges travel too far, attack ranges for both you and your enemies seem inconsistent, it's hard to tell when you're allowed to do anything you want to do when trying to flex.All it takes is a little tuning and enemy balancing, and I think it would be my favorite game to come out in a hot minute. It's got everything I want as far as options, it just needs to be a game that lets me use them.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks to be inspired by such video games as Hotline Miami while people also state that it has some Sifu influences.After playing it, I personally disagree with that assessment. Sifu has methodical combat, where it's important to learn your character's moveset and to remain patient and tactical, particularly on harder difficulties. The biggest similarity is mostly in the form of kung-fu, where you can notice the player character using Wing Chun and some other forms of martial arts. But this game is easily brute forced just by button mashing whereas Sifu is much more punishing if you don't know what you are doing. You don't really have to nail the mechanics here unlike with Sifu. You even have a "rage" meter where your character will automatically enter into a mode of combat where your attacks are super powered enough to completely disintegrate the heads of your opponents. I do like the blood and gore. But there isn't really any strategy to the combat here until all of a sudden the game tries to force tactical combat and completely executes it incorrectly whilst destroying the pacing. You're often outnumbered and it's very easy to just go about using your newly acquired abilities to tackling each challenge without too much difficulty. Up until around the last act of the game, act 3. This is when the game starts to get obnoxious as it begins to introduce new enemy types that either use long ranged attacks (think rocket launchers) or an enemy that is only vulnerable to explosive damage, resulting in the pacing becoming completely slowed down as you now have to find the right type of objects and weaponry to defeat these enemies, and not all the time are these objects (like explosive barrels) even nearby, or if they are, it's entirely possible you throw it or shoot it at the wrong enemy type because the aiming isn't great, almost to the point that it doesn't really exist and you just throw or shoot at whoever is closest to you.This nuisance of game design is compounded by the fact that many maps have insta-kill mechanics that will ruin your run and your fun. If you get caught in an animation that shows your character parrying or using a finisher ability, the game punishes you with these mechanics by getting shot by an off-map sniper or having a grenade detonate at your feet before you can escape the animation sequence. There is one particular boss, the Scorpion Queen, who cannot be engaged with CQC despite this being a brawler game, because she'll instakill you if you get too close. So you have to maneuver around her while fighting henchmen and wrestling the firearms from them instead as that's the only way you can reliably damage her. This is such an oddly designed fight for what the game is supposed to be. You've spent all of that playtime prior to this encounter unlocking new kung-fu abilities and learning how to master them . . . only to have it all nullified by this single boss fight, and you completely lose trust in the developer to know what to do next. That's just one of many bad designs here that really ruins what otherwise could have been a really fun video game for just senseless violence. There's 40 total maps/missions and I got to about map 20 before I started to get bored and wondering if the game got any better only to see it gets worse. But, again, this is a brawling beat 'em up type of video game that, for whatever reason, uses gunplay at the same time to the point that you wonder if you're supposed to be a gunman or a brawler and the guns that the enemies use just ruins it.The character controls like he is drunk as well. I don't know if it's because I opted to play with a mouse and keyboard (I'm a PC gamer, not a console game) whereas it's recommended to use a controller instead, but the player movement just felt really clunky and unresponsive. It's one of those games where you have to make sure to keep your reticle where you want to attack because your character will attack wherever you are aiming, regardless of your movement around the map. But sometimes if I wanted to walk/strafe left, it seemed like my character was about to fall over from too many shots of whiskey. The movement is just really weird sometimes.From a completionist standpoint, I don't like the 'challenges' system. This unlocks only AFTER you've beaten the level for the first time, resulting in you having to replay it multiple times in order to complete the full list of challenges. This is usually collecting ten gold teeth (randomly drops from enemies), getting an S ranking (which you get from just replaying the level until your XP bar goes up a letter grade) and three miscellaneous objectives such as completing the level without dying, beating it in a certain amount of time, killing enemies with explosives, etc. Ultimately, the idea here is to try and force you to replay the same level multiple times just to pad the total time played of the entire game. This is a cheesy tactic to get players like me to spend more time than necessary beating the game. To make matters worse, some of these challenges cannot be immediately completed because you need to unlock a specific skill to, for example, disarm guns from people. You have to revisit these maps later on once you have the necessary abilities unlocked. The biggest issue with the challenge system is with the controversial nature of the aforementioned act 3 maps. I'm pretty sure there was one challenge where you had to beat a map in 3 minutes, but you'd spend 30+ seconds alone just trying to kill nigh-invulnerable enemies. Once again, it ruins the pacing of the game and isn't really a "challenge" so much as it is just tedious and unfair. The problem with this design idea is that it makes the game boring if you are not hunting for completionist status, but also tedious if you are. The game offers very little to more casual players except going from map to map, aimlessly beating up dozens of bad guys. To that point, it's perfectly fine, but you'll probably beat the game in around or even less than six hours if you aren't trying to 100% the maps.I do like the easter eggs. The game makes reference to such cultural icons like Popeye the sailor man and there's an enemy type in the earlier stages that are basically the Saints from Saints Row. I also like the character customization options. There's a variety of clothing that you can purchase to customize your character. You can even play as the bosses you defeat, or if you do the challenges, you get access to special skins/costumes. There are female characters you can play as, for example, for all of the people who like playing as chicks. The soundtrack is also great. I would almost rather advise people buy the soundtrack for $8 instead of paying full price for this game as I don't think it's worth it full price. I don't want to fault the developer as I'm going to assume it's probably just that they are inexperienced, but that is how the game evolves from the beginning: increasingly more and more bad decisions and ideas and an obvious lack of playtesting that it does seem like this developer is indeed inexperienced. And that's fine if so, we all have to start somewhere, but for any future titles I hope they learn and improve rather than remain the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express was developed by a Pole, Jakub Dzwinel, with the help of Super Alloy studio from Los Angeles, responsible for fantastic combat animations in the game, created with the use of motion capute technology, and the composer known as Noisecream.Midnight Fight Express is a dark darker, brutal and technically complicated game. The plot may not be very revealing. We play as just another lonely hero that uses his fists, legs and other objects found along the way to beat, kick, break fingers, jaws and bones, stab, cut throats, slash, stab, shoot and blow up a very colorful and diverse menagerie of sixty-nine types of enemies. All this takes place over the course of a single night, during which we will have to tear through forty different locations, from dirty streets, criminal lairs and a brothel, to a construction site, a shipyard and an oil rig, and ending with exclusive clubs and a secret laboratory. Each of these locations has its own atmosphere and interesting bits referring to various games or movies. Incorporating into it are also 3 stages in which we will be driving a vehicle and shoot more than fight hand to hand, which is quite a nice change.The core of Midnight Fight Express is brutal and spectacular hand-to-hand combat, both with fists and with a hundred of various types of weapons, both melee and firearms. In addition, there is a large tree of gradually developed combat skills, which has its in-game  justifications. As a "sleeper" agent, we must remember how to fight, from simple combinations of fast and strong blows, through more complicated counterattacks, and ending with spectacular "finishers". In addition, while completing stages, we will get access to a revolver that slowly regenerates ammunition and a grappling hook, which can pull enemies towards us to get a serious beating. Thanks to this, we get as many as forty different abilities, which, if we do not like our choices, can be changed between stages. This feature is sometimes useful, but all the abilities will be unlocked after one playthrough.After completing each stage, our game is scored. As in Hotline Miami, it is not so much the speed of getting through a stage that counts, but the style in which we do it and the variety of fighting techniques used. This is what this whole bunch of skills and weapons is for, so that the fight won't become boring. Killing someone with a knife, a cleaver or a crowbar will look different. We can beat someone up with a board or a stick, but using an axe will cut enemies in half. On the other hand, with a gun, we can simply shoot an enemy or bring him to his/her knees with a few kicks and then perform an execution. It will not be easy however, as our opponents are not ordinary pushersovers. Although not particularly difficult in the first few stages, over time they become better armed and resistant to blows. Proper use of the unlocked techniques and a very careful and tactical approach to who to defeat first or even hit him a few times to prevent any crushing attack against us is crucial in this game. Mindless button mashing won't do much good here. On top of all this, there are also interesting obstacles in some stages, such as a sniper in a helicopter, a crane trying to crush us with a container or other gimmicks that twist the gameplay and make one think about their actions all the time. Finally, it is worth mentioning a dozen or so bosses in the game. They are quite original and each has their part in the story as it unfolds. Some can be defeated with standard punches, but some need to be neutralized in other ways. It was also a very good idea to add the Playground to the game, where one can polish their fighting skills with any opponents they choose, without having to go through individual stages. On the other hand, to get all the collectibles and complete all the challenges that reward cosmetic items that allow to customize the character you play, each stage will have to be completed multiple times, which is a very tempting prospect with such excellent gameplay. The only minor drawback in the whole system is binding shooting the revolver and finisher under the same button/key, which means that sometimes instead of crushing someone's head against the wall, we waist a bullet, which could be useful for fighting another opponent.Graphically, the aesthetics are closest to an animated film or a comic book. The characters are not built of a large number of polygons, but by their appearance and weapons, one can easily know who they are dealing with and adjust their combat tactics accordingly. All the motion and combat animations are incredibly smooth and look really fantastic. Likewise with locations. They are really well designed and perfectly reflect the atmosphere of the places they are meant to represent with the right textures, furnishings, lighting and other details that make them very convincing. Moreover, in many stages there are characters who will explain some bits about our character or what is happening around in the game world.The sound effects are generally well made. All the blows, the sounds of broken bones and defeated opponents sound very convincing. The only thing I didn't like was the effects of firing several firearms, especially the shotgun. They could be much louder and have more oomph. The music in the game is as fantastic as its combat system. All thanks to 47 fantastic tracks were composed especially for this game by Noisecream. They are largely very aggressive-sounding electronic pieces that fit perfectly with the gameplay taking place on the screen and complete the atmosphere of total carnage.The only complaint I have is with the presentation of the story, which the game tries to convey to us through dialogues. Unfortunately, there is quite a lot of text to read for this genre of games. In addition, dialogues also appear between individual battle arenas, which slows down the pacing. It is a pity that the publisher Huble Games did not spend more money and commissioned the implementation of dialogues in audio format, which could be played in the background and would not distract us from the consecutive fights.Summing up, if you like games where dead bodies pile up in droves, where you can feel like a real killer beating up on all kinds of thugs, but at the same time you are looking for games with a more complex combat system than just hitting two buttons over and over again, then Midnight Fight Express is definitely the game for you. For all the other, give it a try as the game is not pulling any punches.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game with a handful of flaws ranging from relatively minor to pretty major.  I enjoyed my time playing, but there were a lot of issues I encountered with the general game design that I feel could have been greatly improved on.When the game is working well and isn't fighting itself, this game is a blast.  The animations look great, the combat feels good, and it's just generally quite good.  However, it makes a couple of interesting choices that damage the experience.First off, you have to unlock the Arkham style "press button to counter enemy", even though the tutorial tells you how to do it (unless I interpreted that wrong).  This ability is basically necessary to have a good time playing the game, and while it is technically the first unlock you can get (meaning you can have it as soon as the second level), it's still optional, which means if you're like me, you upgraded other things first.  It felt like a weird choice in a game that clearly relies on that style of gameplay.Speaking of the unlockable abilities, they all felt a little bit useless to me.  You'll see it in other review, but grabbing enemies is basically entirely pointless because as soon as you grab an enemy another enemy will sucker punch you.  The unlockable moves all had inputs that felt unnecessarily complicated or just difficult to remember during the fast-paced combat.  It's not like the moves were fighting game level complicated, most often it's just "hold up or down" while doing a move, but so often during the combat I was so focused on the fight that I couldn't recall specifically "ok, its hold down during this move to disarm the opponent".  Maybe I'm just dumb.  I also wish the game had chosen to go with the gameplay style of "button for light attacks, button for heavy attacks" because it chooses "hold light attack button to do a heavy attack" and it makes heavy attacks feel slow, cumbersome, and hard to get off when you need them too.  This speaks to a greater issue with inputs in general, I found myself unable to pick up weapons when I needed to, my character would sometimes throw away guns that still had ammo in them, etc.The game has a habit of introducing mechanics that go against everything you've just learned but also doesn't provide you with an effective way of dealing with.  Many of the gimmick enemies are just generally more frustrating to fight rather than interesting.  There's also occasionally a lack of consistency, like some enemies who flash red mean that they're gonna do an unblockable attack (which you need to dodge) but with some enemies, you can attack them to knock them out of that state, while others are just invincible during.  Many enemies who do these unblockable attacks will just chain together unblockable attacks one after the other (like, literally as soon as the previous one ends they start a new one), meaning you can't do anything for a couple seconds but roll away from them, which brings down the fast-paced fun of the combat.The final boss breaks the code of "other enemies won't attack you while you're parrying or finishing an enemy", and will randomly just blast you while you think you're safe because the game has taught you that.  The motorcycle/jetski/whatever missions are all fine, they feel like unnecessary padding on a game that could have just been straight brawling.  They don't do anything offensive but they aren't particularly interesting either.Overall I find myself kind of torn on the game, it feels like it was envisioned to be a sort of general fighting sandbox that got dragged out into a full game, and it has the problems associated with that.  I had fun with it and I think a lot of my frustration is that I feel aspects of the game could have been a lot better if some different choices had been made.  I wouldn't be writing a review this long if I didn't feel passionate about it in some capacity, so that's to the game's credit at least.  And the final thing to mention: narrative wise I was really pleasantly surprised, the ending was somewhat of a fizzle out rather than an explosion, but the build up and the way information was slowly revealed was really quite good.Ultimately, I'd recommend the game, despite the perceived shortcomings I had with it.  Like I said, when the game isn't fighting itself, it's truly a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: After someone gifting me this game I have been able to replay it with access to the newest patch, full disclosure, it was the developer of the game, I have not been paid anything, I have not signed anything, just gifted the game to give it a retry.And I am very glad he did, I probably wouldn't have re-bought the game on my own due to personal circumstance, but after going through the first 10 levels again, I can confidently say that a lot of my previous complaints have been addressed.Some things which haven't changed would be the plot, and while I haven't completed the game and talked to all the hidden characters, I can make a well-educated guess that the actual back-bone of the story is the same (at the minimum), which is, in my opinion, hilariously goofy, and while it ain't not Othello, neither is most of the other spectacle fighters currently on the market, and it's clear inspiration from various action movies leads to an enjoyably dumb, if a bit cliché, story, but that's not really what we're here for.However, the combat systems have had some changes and tweaks in the name of flow and enjoyment, such as finishers being (mostly) safe to use (exception of if you start it while another enemy is winding up an attack, which is fair to be punished by), as when performed, all enemies not in an animation will momentarily back off, giving breathing room and a reason to use them, even if they don't kill.The massive decrease in enemies performing uninterruptible attacks is also very welcome, it seems this has been done by both reducing their overall frequency, and removing this status from a couple of attacks, such as the dicers, and enemy type that before was a chore to fight, as 2 hits would provoke them to hyper-armour through your combo, and force you to dodge, but no more, as, while they still have the unblock-able status, and hit fast for high damage if they do catch you, on their own they will no longer swing out of your combo.These two changes on their own enormously improve this games in-combat flow, as the player now actually has an opportunity to perform free-flow combos, and the enemies won't just stand there and take it, if there's several on you they will still gang up on you, but you now have a chance to fight back and put pressure on them, and are no longer reliant on a few tools to prevent these problems.The player has also become less reliant on dodging, as it is now possible to parry throwables which makes the whole game-play less reliant on the old tactic of dodge, throw, dodge, throw that the original release of this game was chock-full of, especially in the later stages.Overall, the improvements made to this game have been great, and I'm actually excited to be playing it again, in a state that feels much closer to what its contemporaries are at (such as Sifu, Arkham series and Spider-man PS4), while still keeping it's own identity of being an over-the-top action film with a mostly forgettable plot, containing fun, flowing combat, aggressive and brutal take-downs/finishers, all topped off with a pretty good pulsating synth-wave soundtrack, to bring back memories of mama's home cooked Hotline Miami.To the Dev, if you're reading this, good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ job, you're most likely a better man than I, and you should be proud of being able to take criticism as well as you have.

A lot of re-skins but it's a beat-em-up. That should be expected and not a problem for most. A lot of unique enemies though. As the levels went on, I never personally got bored with what the game threw at me.Story is meh but interesting enough. It's every  scenario. They put a lot of effort into the back end with writing and jokes. Some of the memes are pretty stale but the devs made what they wanted to and that's cool enough for me.As of writing, It's only been a couple days since this came out. I liked it enough to no life and I'm at least gonna keep playing till I finish the challenges. The game can be pretty hard though. I have only completed this game on the hardest difficulty, as of writing. Realistic. I would not recommend doing this unless you are a masochist/loser like myself. Some of these fights SUCKED (I sucked/user error). But damn if it didn't feel good beating them.For 20$, you could do a lot worse. If you like arcady beat-em-ups that reward patience and understanding of its mechanics, you should definitely pick this up. Looks nice, feels nice and sounds nice.last thing though. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for December 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 2nd, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Brawling through a lawless city.Midnight Fight Express does a lot of things right.  The start of the game has a pumping beat, the combat feels tight, the levels are well laid out, there are challenges for each level, just a lot to do, and the idea of a fast past brawler can work.  On paper, all of this is a good idea and in-game everything feels very polished. The only problem is nothing ever really feels like it comes together.  Nothing is bad, necessarily, but there’s just something that isn’t as exciting as each of the parts individually, and instead of a bad or a great game, it’s just average.  The music becomes repetitive before the first hour is up even with different stages, the enemies change but not enough, there are upgrades but it will take many levels to earn them all and they don’t change the game as none of them will be required and the only thing that challenges unlock is cosmetics, that don’t affect the gameplay, at least that’s the story we’re told over and over again.  Again, nothing bad, but my excitement went down over the first hour, just as it did the last time I played this. Pick this up, you want an interesting case study in how a game just fails to come together, or just want a beat-\em-up game for a while.  Sadly that’s all this is, and it’s a shame, but I will say this, with everything that works here, I’d be interested to see if this studio can turn it on with another title that meshes a bit better because the framework is here, just something is missing. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who has S-ranked every level and completed every challenge in this game, I can say that the game is addicting and fun to play, but the difficulty and pacing is unfortunately all over the place and makes the game constantly jump up and down from fun to incredibly frustrating. The combat is really fluid and satisfying for the most part, but unfortunately later levels get progressively filled with gimmicky enemies with ridiculously annoying attacks, such as the bikers in the level "Fight Club".The game also suffers from Manhunt syndrome, as in, it relies way too much on firearms towards the later half, almost completely switching away from being a beat 'em up game and turning into a twin-stick shooter with a tight camera.That said, however, the soundtrack by Noisecream is fantastic and the presentation has a lot of charm. It is a fun game when it embraces its brawler mechanics and gives you fair enemies to fight. I do think 40 levels is a little too long for what kind of game this is, though.Reccomend to buy it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed the development of this game on Instagram for months and REALLY wanted to like it, sadly, while crystal clear in its influences, it sabotages itself in achieving almost all of what it seems to want to do most. There are technique based brawlers like Sifu, and flow-state games like Hotline Miami, both trendsetters for their own strengths. The scoring system makes clear that Midnight Fight Express wants to be a flow-state game (rewards for clear time, kill variety, no deaths, etc.) but CONSTANTLY interrupts with the most inane dialogue, and predictable story beats you can read from a mile away. I found myself desperately hoping for 45 uninterrupted seconds of play without being forced to acknowledge something, skip small talk, or being kicked into a menu, but to no avail, making the first play a slog. If only the game would get out of the way and let me play the game itself.Without a controller, movement is slippery, unintuitive, and takes some mental recalibration. 'Up' moves you on a North East diagonal, and from 1/4 of the way through the game there will be periods that require you to dodge-roll almost constantly. This makes recognising a weapon you want to pick up, and smoothly obtaining it from a cluster of dropped weapons, a completely different matter.The reason we pay for these experiences is to feel like an adaptable, unstoppable badass that thinks on their feet to win; and the game seems to recognise this, in theory, with a skilltree of contextual moves and a variety of different counter opportunities. But in practise, much of the combat devolves to directional button mashing and rolling, and many of the skills are either automated finishers, or single-target moves that are untenable in the large-group settings the game loves most. I don't feel like I'm making intelligent positioning decisions, I feel as if I'm most successful (and subsequently rewarded) when gaming the game itself, and cheesing my way through; which completely undermines the reason I'm playing in the first place.I WISH that I loved this, and what's worse is that I don't know know how these issues could be patched (beyond story-mute options), as it's beyond difficulty multipliers, it's game design decisions. I genuinely wish the developers all the best and can't wait to see what they come out with next, but I can't honestly recommend this experience over any one of the dozen other indie games I'm surprised by every other month.

_childDocuments_.review: I learned in school to do the positiv first. (Conclusion in the final paragraph)This game is fun, it really is. There just is something satisfying in beating up people in a frenzy of concetrated rage and gore while blasting the awesome music.The maps are designed perfectly for you to just turn of your brain and unload on the enemys to get that sweet combo going and while youre at it why not use the new moves you just got from the skill tree to beat up even more people, but in style.I also quite like the design of the enemy your facing, the game will nor bore you with the same paint over and over again. You will beat up normal criminals, rat people, Knife enthusiast or pirates. In every level you will find something new.I also quite like the fact, that the game gave you the option for to customise your character.So why do i take dislike in the game?  The game appears as the 3D successor to Hotline-Miami with its brutal combat and fast paced action, but its far from it, the pacing just is not there. In Hotline-Miami you can play fast, because everything dies in one or two hits, MFE on the other hand takes no time to introduce punching bags that slow you down and force you to mash your buttons until they finally go to the ground. Then they introduce the next special enemy with high damage and powerful combos that forces you to focus your attention on it until you defeat it, to bad that most of the special enemys are also punchingbags that counter your special moves and quick finishers and give you no other choice then to hammer the attack button until their shields break. Generally speaking, the combat is lack luster and unrefiened. It presents you with a lot of ways to deal with your enemys, but it takes no time to confront you with enemys, where the majority of solutions do not apply. Whats more is that, later in the game, the new enemys are just recolored versions so the game while appearing fresh does not really add anything impactful to the gameplay, which is a catastrophe since the only real challenge of the game is dealing with different enemys.Moreover, I dislike the way the game handles cutscenes. The mission starts with a cutscene and ends with a cutscene, but also uses cutscenes in the middle of the mission every time you enter a new room and to introduce a new enemy. This tired me out the most, since the new enemy is just a recolore and brings me no information but is not skippable. There is an option to skip cutscenes one you replay the mission, but that only fast-forwards them. The cutscenes interrupt the gameplay so drasticlly that i never felt emmersed into the action and could never really dive into the gameplay.On top of that, I am exteremly confused by the overall design of the game. It appears gruesome and distressing with depictions of for example dryed out corpes that, if not for the low-poly graphics, would remind me of the pictures of CC Ausschwitz and criminals killing civilians in the middle of the street. But the game calls the enemys Bozos and later in the game you will enounter people dressed up as cats wanting to see your guts spill out.The Developers probablly were not quite sure what the game should be and it is overly noticable.All in all I do not recommend this game, its fun at first but progresses into a tedious butten masher with no depth what so ever. The enemy provide little to no variation and the overall experience of the game is tiring. The cutscene will regularly rip you out of your flow and the general aesthetic of the game is contradictory. Instead of buying this game i would suggest buying Hotline-Miami, its better in every way and I guarantee you will have more fun with it then with Midnight Fight Express.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since there's been a game like this out (Shredder's Revenge was a nice surprise.) Beat-em-ups are far and few between, and unfortunately, this is kind of a good example of why: they're not easy to make. On it's face, this is a fun, fast paced brawler, but the problems start showing almost immediately. There's very little control in the game, and it mostly feels like a button-masher, more than a fighter. After the first level, the shield/invulnerable/uninterruptible enemies start to pile up, and since there's no pause build in between attacks, you mostly just roll around on the floor, instead of using any of your hard-earned skills. Sifu suffered from a lot of the same problems, with weak indications in terms of guarding and breaking. The game really takes a hard nose dive around level 14. Fighting goes out the window, and is replaced with guns. From 14 to level 40, it's pretty much just a crappy twin stick shooter. On top of that, it starts throwing a hopeless amount of invulnerable enemies at you. It has a really bad habit of putting you up against a problem, and not providing you with a solution. The level called Fight Club challenges you to use ground finishers on enemies that literally can't be knocked down. It's the kind of game design choices that really speaks to a lack of testing. I think a little bit of tinkering with the timing and pacing could make this pretty good, but right now it feels like a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: John Wick, The Raid: Redemption, Atomic Blonde, Hotline Miami, and Batman Arkham Asylum all walk into a bar and respectfully nod then raise their glasses silently at each other, all while a DJ is playing some absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bangers that sound like they came straight off the Aim to Head Mix youtube channel.The result is a game that is my taste in action media to a tee, but has some kind of odd difficulty spikes near the end of the game, which at this point is pretty much par for the course for most brawlers. Then again, I only have myself to blame for picking Hard difficulty on my first playthrough. It does make me wonder how viable realistic difficulty is, since there were some parts of the game later on that didn't feel as playtested, such as the  and a mission where there's a lot of glass doors and you smash someone's head into a face scanner, and the NPCs all have trouble walking through the glass doors.Outside of that, this game's great. _childDocuments_.review: The game looks cool in the trailer, but if you expect something as challenging fun as hotline miami, just replay hotline miami.If you must try it though, get it on discount.I only played through this game out of spite, because I wanted my moneys worth and I'm quite disappointed.Yes the game is around 8h long (I replayed some levels), but there are incentives to replay levels to unlock things.However I can't be bothered to play through the same level again and again doing some wacky challenges that would want to make me rip my flesh off my face out of frustrating, since playing through some of these levels once is already too much, just to get a tatoo or a perk that enables big head mode.To be honest there are actually many good aspects about the game and it has a lot of pontetial, but the flaws make me not recommend it.Playing the game on a keyboard, as you often do when you play a PC game, is already a challenge. If you don't like playing with a controller, this should already scare you off. Then there is such a thing as too many actions mapped on the same input. When you hold a weapon and there is some object laying next to you, there are 3 things that can happen when you press Q. You either drop your weapon, kick the object next to you or you kick the object and then drop your weapon.Also when you point your cursor towards an enemy, there is always a chance that when you attack, your character does a weird cartwheel to a random enemy you didn't mean to attack.It often breaks the flow of the fight and ruins the cinematic appeal.Finally my last gripe before I leave this review behind is that the bosses have no climax. There are always henchmen spawning in that distract you from a potentially epic fight with the big bad dude. What's worse is that sometimes these henchman tank too many hits, shoot you from across the screen or just end up making your character cartwheel around the room - exposing you to damage - and while you are already there you get locked into a finisher move on top of a grenade that blows you up and makes you start the whole fight anew. Oh and don't get me started on the bloody combine harvester, that level was completely unnecessary. So yea the bosses often feel like secondary objectives.I guess I kinda enjoyed the story though and the game can shine in the looks and animations.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a review before, mostly because I never felt compelled to. But with this game, I feel I have to as a credit to its service. It is truly fantastic, if you are the type of person that can withstand a little bit of monotony. Once you complete the main story line you have challenges and achievements to go for, if that is your cup of tea. Personally, the game feels very reminiscent of Sleeping Dogs style combat, it is obscenely well thought out and choreographed. The animations and mo-capping are quite phenomenal in my opinion, but I may just be simple. Combat is seamless and very rewarding and fun to master, there's plenty of moves and attacks to throw, and even a large variety of weapons. All in all, for 20 dollars this is one of the funnest games I have played in a long time, it's like if you take Hotline Miami's play-style and direction, and combined it with the Sleeping dogs and Mad max hand-to-hand combat system. Brutal and visceral attacks and attention to detail. Truly a wonderful game to experience for everyone from casual to serious players. if you just shoot through the main story on normal or hard, expect to have about 4-5 hours of play time. Assuming that you don't do challenges, try harder difficulties, or get caught up on some of the harder fights. All in all for a full completionist you are looking at somewhere in the 30-40 hour range.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with really cool first 15 levels that is unfortunately then completely ruined by bad enemy design not tailored to the gameplay. Add on that the challenges that have some bs here and there. Let me explain :You have a long, slow dodge and a parry that can also act as a small, unreliable dodge. The game at first lets you think that the parry will be used a lot when it's really not. Because the further you go into the level, the more you have to use the long dodge that breaks any sense of rythm in the fight. Now why is that a problem ?Because the game FILLED with these kinds of enemies further into the game. You can't dodge some huge strings of attack and you certainly can't attack them. So you have to wait for them to be done and then put in some punches. This sucks, the fights gets way too long and frustrating because of that and it's not difficult because the enemy is challenging, it's difficult because you have to be so patient at some point you can't take it anymore and do a mistake.I'm not one to turn down difficulty, I love te souls games and more recently SIFU was a treat. But this kind of difficulty is just bad design, it's not hard it's just not fun. I'll try to push a bit and continue playing but i'm at level 20 and it's getting more frustrating each level

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a nice artstyle and really nice flowing melee combat.The story is a nonsensical mess, stuffed with mishandled jokes and poorly placed memes.It also interrupts the flow of each level massively but can be turned off in the options which is great.The music is a nice selection of high energy tunes that fit the brutal melee very well.The targeting system is very inaccurate and switches through enemies seemingly at random at any given time. A bit of tweaking there would be greatly appreciated.None of these negatives is an actual dealbreaker though.And then someone decided to add guns...They are, in my personal opinion, the absolute worst thing that could have been added to the game.They completely break the melee flow, feel unsatisfying and downright cheap to use, and are a nightmare to fight against.Once there are multiple gun wielding enemies at the same time it becomes a game of luck. Bullets cant be avoided (the dodge roll sometimes having I-Frames and sometimes not, seemingly) and there is a massive lack of feedback that you are even being hit.Throw in a bunch of enemies that only use unstoppable attacks that must be dodged which cant be interrupted and you have just gone from a hilariously entertaining brawler to the limbo of: "Reload until RNGesus is with you"Which is a damn shame because I really want to like the game and when its at its best, it is so easy to love it.Unfortunately it isnt half the time.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: literally hours after i posted this review (though likely not because of it since this is a recurring topic in reviews) the Brother Hood's grenades ate a fat nerf, this is what i mean by "hold off until patches come out" at the end of the review lmao, keeping the review as is until other stuff is fixed but changing to a recommendation just for the responsiveness to feedbackIt's a brawler made by someone who has never actually played a brawler in their life--I could write you a long review going into the good (of which there's a lot!) and the bad (of which there's far more than good honestly) but I honestly think the best summary of why I don't recommend this game right now is that blocking enemies are immune to options that exist in the beat 'em up genre specifically to  blocking; if an enemy has an armor meter? Get ♥♥♥♥♥♥, bucko. It'll shrug off your grabs and heavy attacks like water off a duck's back; the only option you have is to hammer away at it with basic attacks while it beats your ass with impunity because that armor meter is a second health bar that grants super armor on top of the super armor all enemies after the third level have anyway because every enemy type introduced after the Muscle has uninterruptible basic attacks.Throwing weapons is... It's just broken. In your hands it's a joke option that wastes frames to accomplish absolutely nothing. In the AI's hands it's a devastating zero-risk extremely high-reward option that will knock you out of any animation, including the supposedly invincible ones, and will instantly end your combo if you've got one going because it's a knockdown. If it  connect, you still have to deal with the entire second of slow-mo the game has to indicate the incoming thrown weapon; that ♥♥♥♥ gets old fast and you very quickly learn to immediately beeline for any enemy carrying a throwable weapon just so it doesn't slow the game to a halt.And the thing is, the AI doesn't  this advantage because every enemy type introduced after the first three levels (in other words, right after the demo ends, funny enough) is broken in its own special way that usually involves the aforementioned "every single enemy type in later levels has super armor on its  attacks" thing: Dicers in the restroom level have fast, multi-hitting slash attacks. Crazies in the Train Station level have that but they will also pounce on you if you get a single dodge-roll or more away from them. Brother Hood members in the Slums level can throw out grenades that have basically zero indication and, like any other thrown weapon, will interrupt any animation; half the reason I got agitated enough with this game to finally write this review after weeks of thinking about it is because I kept getting hit by grenades thrown during a finisher animation.Guns are another problem. They aren't telegraphed, they either fire very quickly or do insane amounts of damage (the sawn-off shotgun in particular is guilty of this, as is the harpoon gun that thankfully only appears in the Oil Rig--the latter specifically is a one-hit-kill), and the AI keeps its distance from you if it's got one so you have to actively chase it down.Environmental hazards are just awful; every last one is some flavor of cheap, whether it's the crane at the Dock not pausing when you perform a finisher (being punished for using finishers is a recurring theme) or the motorcycles in the Fight Club stage that will knock you out of even "invincible" animations, do massive damage repeatedly on hit, and that home in on you while you can't do anything about them because they're paired with an onslaught of enemies you have to focus on and their drivers can only be shot down with guns picked up from enemies (this encounter is the other half of the reason I got aggravated enough to write this review!), they're just ridiculously unfun.This all sucks, because the combat is enjoyable! It's Sleeping Dogs on steroids (at least until you get the godawful revolver that you can't turn off even though it's functionally useless thanks to its overlong cooldown and being bound to the finisher button), but the encounter design is just unbelievably bad. The latest patch fixed some of the problems MFE had at launch so I have hope that it'll change for the better, but as things stand... I wouldn't say spend your money on something else, just hold onto it for a bit and see where the patches go.
