_childDocuments_.review: The blood-stained mark that Hotline Miami left on the video game world still permeates that unmistakable smell of iron nearly 10 years to the day.  Fast, frenetic combat in tune with a double-bump of cocaine for a soundtrack and all the style you could ask for when tasked with murdering dozens of people in the fastest time your senses can handle.  It’s a trip for everyone involved, providing a contact-high to second-hand developers who managed to walk by and get a hint of what was happening.Throughout the past decade plenty of heavily inspired projects toted the scene: Katana Zero, Superhot, Ape Out, soon to be Anger Foot.  Most spinoffs of the speedy formula find their own style while keeping the pace at its intended 4th gear, but others have kept the high-score, high action foundation and molded it into their own form.  With 10 years of studying the original and the expansion of the AA indie titles becoming more common, can the Humble Games published Midnight Fight Express tackle the genre in a fresh and intense style?Waking up in a daze, handcuffed half-naked in an interrogation room, a man known only as Babyface is peltered with questions from a duo of wise-cracking cops.  They refuse to believe Babyface’s story: a past member of the criminal underworld stripped of his memories with only a mysterious drone with knowledge of his past yearning him to stop a citywide takeover before the sun rises.  Prolific names are dropped alongside the seediest of the city’s underbellies, testimonies brought up by the soon-to-be guilty, and it’s all wrapped within the web of memories foretold by a man without any.  Babyface only has one reason forward: who is behind the drone, and who must he move out of the way to find out?Midnight Fight Express may be an original IP, but you’ll immediately feel the inspirations it pulls from from the get go.  Peppering in the combat gameplay of Sifu and the Arkham series, providing the combo-style “I can perfect this” range of Hotline Miami, to the absolute ridiculousness of its plot like it was a sequel to Hardcore Harry.  The action takes place from an isometric view, allowing an all-angles view of the ever-changing battlefield, and boy you’re gonna need it.But before that, let's talk about the customization, because this blew me away when swapping between levels.  Babyface has a multi-tiered skill tree slowly recovering his abilities to whip ass, which also provide an easier discourse to run earlier levels.  For the aesthetic connoisseurs, there are a ton of unlockables to customize your own Babyface.  Hundreds of different clothes are available for purchase, money being earned by how well you do on each level, and each enemy is available to be the main character after defeating them.  It’s a really cool touch to really personalize how badass and/or ridiculous you want to look.  Pillowman takes top honors without a shadow of a doubt.When you traverse through the campaign’s 41 levels, Babyface forever faces an uphill battle.  Each battle pits a ring of fighters for Babyface to dismantle equipped with an arsenal of tap and hold one-button combos, to QTE parries, to various grapples, dodging, and more weapons than you would expect.  No joke, almost anything that isn’t bolted to the ground can be used as a handheld weapon or kicked/thrown to decenter a man’s sense of gravity.  Each level contains a few rooms of these encounters with an added layer providing either a rewarding challenge or a merciless difficulty spike, no in-between.  Once the level is over, you’re provided a grade based on your points earned via combo length, kill variety, and completion time.  Money is given, skill points are doled out, skins are unlocked, rinse and repeat.The pace on each level is multiplied infinitely by the ridiculously good soundtrack.  Each level is provided with its own song and the slew of synthwave, darksynth, and cyberpunk melt over each level like a coat of neon wax.  Your heart will be pumping as the tunes combined with a perfect run shoot serotonin directly into your forehead and will have you pressing for more.  But this serotonin boost is provided if, and only if, you can hit that perfect run…because Midnight Fight Express does everything in its God-given power to stop you from doing so.With titles built around light/heavy attacks and an emphasis on parrying/reading enemies, the ability to recognize incoming attacks is paramount to not only making a smooth fight sequence enjoyable to play, but almost necessary on a balance level to allow a firm but fair experience.  MFE provides you with half of these options.  Parries are highlighted with a button prompt and a bright outline around the character: perfect!  Enemies that are about to throw a chair in your general direction are highlighted with a button prompt and a bright outline around the character: perfect!  Enemies with a literal gun pointed at you are given no prompt and will shoot after a 2-3 sec delay whilst circling you away from the fight and run you about a third of your health per shot: not good!  The lack of prompts for some of the hardest hitting enemies is comically bad, especially when firearms play such a large piece of the pie in the later stages and will provide you with plenty of avoidable deaths when the headcount starts to get higher.The combination of multiple moves on one button can be frustrating as well.  The default binding for your finisher (LB on an XBox controller) is the same button as your recharging magnum bullet for shaky situations.  The amount of times I’ve fanned the hammer after mistiming my finisher prompt because the enemy died too fast is a number higher than it should be.  Some combos don’t feel like they proc correctly at times either, most notably with the rope tool.  There’s a lot of unlockable moves with the rope that are provided via combo presses, but I had a ton of trouble making any of them really work, so the rope was used mainly as a stumbling move to combo starter.Some of the big set pieces cause stumbles more than jubilation.  Taking on multiple enemies while an attack helicopter plugs away with a gatling gun or grenades, or keeping your combo meter alive while shipping containers zoom through your battlefield are intense to witness and prepare for.  Unfortunately, with the previous issues stated, it’s yet another layer of work that becomes too overbearing and causes some immensely frustrating situations.  It all compounds onto itself to make an experience where you’re supposed to be near-unstoppable become an experience where you just want to stop playing.But the most egregious parts came from two of the later bosses.  I’ll try not to spoil anything but one boss becomes a rolling environmental one-hit kill and your goal is to blow up said rolling death machine.  You’re given a gun and an explosive barrel to combat the boss but those weapons are guarded by ever-spawning enemies and the rolling death machine can crush your only ways to kill it.  This process is repeated 5 times and if you don’t hit everything just right, it just runs you over and you have to do it all over again.  And why.    Why does the final boss have a one-hit kill?  What a terrible, terrible idea.I really loved Midnight Fight Express on its surface level.  There’s a ton of things to do: high scores, challenges, collectibles, and all the customization I adore in any game.  The soundtrack contends with the best of them and I’ve been routinely adding tracks to my daily listen, and when the game is hitting on all cylinders it is a fantastic experience.  But the sinister urge to one-up itself with unbalanced set pieces while battling head-shaking omissions in its battle UI compound to provide one of the more frustrating and downtrodden experiences of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Could have been good. The game uses the Arkham/AC/Mad Max/Shadow of..., combat system, yet it completely misses what makes those systems great. It's not fun when 100 unblockable enemies rush into the room and constantly spam attacks. It hurts the game tremendously to have enemies shoot you while you're fighting ublockable attacks. Some enemies react to getting hit, some don't, some enemies can be countered, but if you do then you're stuck in an animation you'll inevitably die during. Locking moves behind a skill tree only exists because they felt it has to be there, it only gimps you and leaves you unable to deal with certain enemies if you picked the wrong skill before a level. Unfortunately for every bit of this game I like, there's equally horrible mechanics to hurt it. Could've been really cool to feel like an action hero but the game just has you rolling all over the floor getting cheap shots where you can, in-between ublockable attacks and people shooting at you. Solid 4/10, don't pay full price for this if you're going to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: While not a completely bad game it definitely has it's issues. The gameplay is like an almost top down version of Sifu for anyone who has played that. Each level is only 2 to 4 minutes long. There are 40 levels.  It's a good thing each level is as short as it is. It can get repetitive. The game devolves into spamming the punch button a lot. Doesn't really give you good incentive to use much of the the other skills you unlock. The game really shines with unlockables. There is lots to unlock here in the base game. The main character can be customized quite a lot. Big praise for the amount of unlockables and replayability.Where the game falters and fails big time is the dialogue. This game does not have any voice overs for the dialogue but it is some of the most cringe dialogue for a game I've come across in quite awhile. Every character in the game comes across as written by an edgy 16 year old or what a teen would find "badass". The dialogue is laughable to get through at times.  The story is very basic from what I've experienced. Having said all that the game plays competently and is not a bug filled mess. I've yet to come across any in my 4 hours. Kudos for that. I would say wait for a big sale if you really want it and don't get this one for the story cause it's rough. I want to give this one a thumbs up but I can't. It wears out it's short welcome quickPros• Lots of unlockables• Soundtrack• Generally bug free•  Gameplay is serviceable• Each level is only 2 to 4 minutes long and invites speedrunningCons• The dialogue from every character. The game thinks it's "cool" and way more funny than it actually is. A lot of the lines from the baddies you come across are maximum cringe• The story is just kinda there nothing interesting.• While the gameplay is serviceable and the mechanics work like they are supposed to, the gameplay can get repetitive if you try to play in large chunks. This is not too bad because each level is so short but with the terrible dialogue and basic story the gameplay doesn't carry it much at all after that.• You are constantly coming across new goons to fight which the game promptly tells you by flashing a big "INTRODUCING whatever their name is" across your screen bringing the action to a halt every few seconds.

_childDocuments_.review: + entertaining for every moment you're in the game+ presentation combines hard hitting music and gameplay alike+ lots of unlockables+ score chasing incentivizes replays+ perfect for DeckMidnight Fight Express is an isometric brawler beat-em-up in the same vein as Hotline Miami but takes cues from some other games, such as the Batman Arkham titles with its combat mechanics. It has a loose narrative and story which is peppered throughout the game, typically bookending levels. These tidbits of dialog or exposition serve to justify the locations you travel to but don't really present a super compelling narrative.The game is divided into forty levels, each of which typically will take anywhere from two to five minutes to complete. While levels are very short, they have excellent replay value: you might replay a given level four or five times to complete the challenges within and get the best rank you can. The game isn't terribly difficult, however, at least on normal difficulty, with 100%ing a level with an S-rating being pretty easy to accomplish in most levels in only a few attempts.The standard gameplay loop is going through each level to then improve your repertoire of attacks (such as adding grabs, grapples, finishers, etc), and to raise money for character customization. The customization is not super indepth, it boils down to basically just clothing, but there many options to choose from, allowing some granular customization by way of dozens of different helmets, shirts, pants, boots, and more.Level design is extremely varied: toilets, metro stations, city streets, clubs, factories, and so on. Most levels are distinct from one another, with only a few level themes being repeated, even if they're different physically. Levels are also built with finishers in mind, with many of them being contextual. For example, proximity to a sink, or a railing, or train tracks will influence how combat pans out, making each level play out differently.Presentation is really fantastic, with the combat being extremely fluid and well choreographed. The isometric view works great here, making the game feel like many little dioramas connected together with John Wick-esque combat. The graphics are not tremendously detailed but it doesn't take away from the game and infact, it suits the lower-fi aesthetic very well.The soundtrack is also super fitting, being a mix of drum-and-bass and techno. It's super energetic and fits the gameplay. Each level has its own track and is mixed well to repeat throughout. Some levels are more mellow, some more punchy. Great care was given matching tracks to levels because the way it's paired works so well with the gameplay.I'm super impressed with the game so far and am having a blast trying to reach higher and higher in the leaderboards. It's easy to pick up and play, but engrossing and gamified enough to want to play levels ad repetere. It's hard to put down because it's just simple fun: beat up bad guys and rack up the high score.Runs excellent when cranked, even with max TDP dropped down to 10w. However, irrespective of graphics settings, I can't get the frametime graph to remain level. While framerate will say 60fps, it does look the tiniest bit jittery because frametimes are not perfectly 16.7ms.Experience on the Deck is also great. Controls wonderfully and the music is not hampered by the small speakers. It's almost like it was made specific for the Deck with how well it plays and feels.No support as of writing. A shame because I can't imagine where the experience wouldn't be enhanced by having a much wider birds-eye isometric view. It's free real estate to show off more of the levels.No issues whatsoever hitting my monitor's framerate ceiling of 113fps on an R5 5600X, 32gb DDR4, RTX3080 system. Exceedingly smooth experience playing the game at higher framerates and experienced zero technical issues.  A really nicely optimized game.

_childDocuments_.review: At the beginning this game was great because Noisecream carried it, then the challenge rules and inconsistent combat got worse and worse, most notable that I have encountered thus far:In mission 2, one of the challenges is disarming a boss and using their own gun to kill them, however, at minimum, you need the level 4 parry and counter, which, at minimum, requires 4 levels to already be completed in order to get the ability and do the challenge.In mission 6, one of the challenges is to kill 5 special enemies with firearms. Of which, only 3 of these firearms spawn, the enemies that you need to specifically kill spam dodge roll(invincibility) the moment you bother aiming at them with a firearm, not only that, but they don't typically die in one hit, so you have to specifically keep them alive and then lower their HP(of which they can hit each other and kill each other, denying you kills) and not only that, you can't even keep the gun. It has a durability meter so if you drop it to save it, the enemies can PICK IT UP and USE IT ON YOU.Not only that, but building up to around level 6, you get taught mechanics of the game of which some enemies out-right ignore. Almost all times that an enemy throws an item off the floor at you, you can grab it mid-air and throw it back. Some enemies will INSTANTLY throw them at you and INSTANTLY deal damage.The gun aim in this game is horrendous as well. Sometimes you can be aiming perfectly at an enemy and still miss at point-blank range. There's quite a few inconsistencies such as when throwing an item at an enemy that jumps into the air, sometimes your thrown item will miss at no fault of your own, since you have no control of where the item actually goes after thrown.Another inconsistency is when enemies charge up attacks outside of your parry range, you attempt to parry (because the button is lit up) and once you press the button, they're right outside of your parry range. Do you parry the attack? No! The enemy manages to warp over to you and hit you anyways. Very frustrating. It should be that if the attack can't be parried because it's out of range, make it red! Make it so that you must dodge it! Don't even bother giving me the prompt to parry if it's not going to work!Before I forget, doing a 180 makes your character, well, do an animation and turn around. I can't even begin to count the amount of times where I think I would normally instantly change direction(since it's not actually a 180 I am doing), hold sprint, only for my character to dance around like he has a mental deficiency before finally sprinting in the direction I want to go.Noisecream carries this game. Go buy the music track and never touch the game. I've already sunk time into it, so I'm likely going to finish it 100% with Cheat Engine since some of the challenges are a crock.

_childDocuments_.review: The highly anticipated video game, Midnight Fight Express, initially appeared promising on paper and in its meticulously curated promotional trailers. However, upon closer inspection by its players, it becomes clear that the game falls short of its hype. Rather than offering unique and engaging levels, players are left with uninspired, generic gameplay. Optional objectives that lack coherence or purpose further diminish the overall experience.The game's combat system is especially lackluster, with an overreliance on the dodge-roll mechanic that constitutes a staggering 70% of the fighting. While the use of voxel graphics and recycled assets may be forgivable to some degree, it is impossible to overlook these significant shortcomings that mar the game's quality.In light of these considerable flaws, one must question whether the game truly warrants the time, money, and effort necessary to engage with it. Despite its potential for success, Midnight Fight Express ultimately disappoints, failing to deliver the smooth and satisfying gameplay that players desire and deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to say I like the game, I really would, because presentation wise, it does everything right. It is almost entirely carried by its score, and some of the animation work is excellent. Perhaps I was mislead by another steam review, calling this a mix of Sifu and Hotline Miami.The game would greatly benefit from a Sifu-like "avoid in place" function, which would allow you to (with strict timing) avoid heavy attacks without greatly repositioning with a roll. Perhaps this is unlocked later in progression, but not early enough to where I was able to unlock it before getting bored.I played in hard mode. This may have been the reason for an exceedingly great number of armed enemies capable of heavy attacks. Rolling to avoid such attacks interrupts combat, as it moves you much too far away from enemies. Useful for repositioning, but a terrible way to dodge most attacks thrown your way, (as, again, most enemies start out armed, and will pick up weapons dropped by their defeated companions.)If you are unbothered by what I am describing, or it seems like an overly technical nitpick, do not be discouraged. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'm going to get this out of the way in this review by ranking this game an 8/10. It's a solid game by many metrics, the combat flow is really good. And you normally have several options in a situation to tackle things. As you play the early levels, you'll come to appreciate how things run.Notice how I said previous levels. The game has a couple of underlying issues that can make the game a slog to get through. The main contender amongst the worst things of this game are things that break the flow of combat. Normally this is done to make scenarios interesting. Not all things are created equal however, you can be finishing a target and be interrupted because an enemy decides to use one of their "special" moves. Or a map gimmick whose timer pauses doesn't pause for this specific move and you die from getting your head blown off. The second aspect is gun enemies. Gun enemies in this game sperg all out over the place and fire at regular intervals. There is no telegraph to when they'll fire, they'll just keep firing. This makes dealing with them a pain in the ass and trying to avoid damage of groups of gun enemies is borderline impossible. They'll clip you anyways.It's things like these that stop Midnight Fight Express from being a great game, there are some questionable design decisions. But if you do enjoy the various references, beating people to a pulp, and a variety of techniques to experiment with... then this game does look appealing. You will be reminded of its negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a good ass beat 'em up with straight-forward controls and a comically large amount of unique enemies. Seriously, it feels like every level has a new faction in it, and they all want to beat your ass. It's great. As my hours played shows, a full run without going out of your way to get all the different conversations and collectables will be like 5-6 hrs. Soundtrack is awesome, yeah, but not really memorable. It's the aggressive, synth-infused modern indie action game protag's playlist, composed pretty damn well by Noisecream who was always influential in this new Hotline Miami era of fight tracks. Make no mistake, I did like the tunes, but none of them really stood out to me like similar beats did in Hotline Miami or Katana Zero or that. Animations are pretty great for the fighting parts (the only parts that matter), and apparently they were mo-capped by an actual guy according to the store page so that's cool. It definitely looked and felt like it.Story? What about it? It's serviceable, I suppose, basically just a mishmash of 80s techno-dystopia flicks (ie Escape to New York), Hotline Miami crib notes and a post-John Wick revenge narrative that, thankfully, doesn't get too caught up on the 'why' that Babyface is wiping out every shoplifter in a 7 mile radius. But that's not the focus now is it? I enjoy that it's unvoiced though, so I can do my own accents and voices for the many, many different sociopathic criminals you'll be scrapping with.So yeah. Does everything it's supposed to do, though a longer run-time is always appreciated. The game certainly stands out, but in the current state of indie action games, it's sometimes unclear how much it stands out. 9/10 :)) (also please make a sequel if at all possible and go even harder with the cyberpunk aspects I'm a sucker for that)

_childDocuments_.review: A very simplistic game about beating up droves of punks and goons in flashy, bloody and extravagant manners.  When I say simplistic, I'm actually down-playing it a tad. It's VERY simple. It won't rock your socks off, it doesn't have a genre-breaking mechanic, or story. Hell, you can tell which parts were stitched through in Unity from some of the animations. However, the game knows this, and never wastes time in putting you where it matters. Again, nothing ground-breaking, but some neat animations, and gadgets make it satisfying to sift through the 50 (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) levels in here. A crown jewel that deserves a mention is Noisecream's OST. It's downright infectious, and turns what would probably be a mid top-down beat 'em up into an exhilarating fight pretty much everytime. It's quite a godsend. Although you might see these as way too mid, there's a kicker: This game was built from the ground up by one simple polish guy. It makes the scope and accomplishments of this game take on a greater height, to me at least. If you seek a simple, yet good "pass the time" game, are looking for background footage for your Youtube commentary vid, or are enamored with assaulting and beating up people (in videogames, of course. haha.) This is a solid pick.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game. I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to let off steam or some kind. Play it if you find yourself in one or more of these situations or feelings:- You lost a job- You don't have money (tightly connected with option above)- Your neighbor is getting on your nerve- You see some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ on TV reality show who has one digit IQ but somehow is famous- You lost a wager while betting, you needed someone to score just 1 goal so you get big money- You have a colleague who sabotage your work- Your professor didn't let you pass an exam , because he clearly doesn't like you- Your "friend" calls you only when he needs help with something- Your internet is working like ♥♥♥♥ for days, and ISP is not sending people to fix it- You wanted to eat sweets but there are none in the house, and nobody is working on Sunday afternoonIf there is anything similar to this just start the game and beat someone, I think games like this are very helpful in managing stress of any kind. No matter what people say about violent games, they can still help but only if played correctly and in normal scenarios. It is also cell shaded graphic, so it is not so much hard to look at compared to some other. It really reminded me of Ruiner which I enjoyed playing as well. I really like the short levels on this one, and high replay value to grind some achievements. There are no bugs that I found or any other problems except sometimes strange controls behavior when rolling. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Best John Wick simulator on the market. Very fluid combat with fun mechanics. There's a surprisingly large amount of content and the story supplements the game well. The game is filled with endearing references and great set pieces, many inspired by other media. Even the soundtrack has some nods to other games or movies.My only gripe is that a few of the challenges are a bit tedious and require you to go out of your way to complete them — for example the Ratboy's toxic vomit one. Also the keybind for the sprint slide are a bit awkward on a controller. Hold A and press X at the same time isn't very ergonomic.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: ​I got Midnight Fight Express out of a Humble Bundle and I'm glad I did because I doubt I would have given it a shot or even heard of it otherwise. It was a pleasant surprise for sure! This is basically a beat em up version of Hotline Miami with a killer soundtrack and a fun story. There was also some fun humor throughout the game. The dialogue with any bad guys were almost cartoonish villainy or even just silly humor.The gameplay is really tight as is the animations to go along with it. It kind of plays like the melee combat of the Batman Arkham games with a wide variety of weapons. They had some silly weapons like a paint roller or pillows but also your typical weapons like knives and pipes. The one thing this game had that I feel like most games like this don't have is guns. You don't get to reload so pick up and unload your gun at your targets, then throw the gun at your next target. The animations are also really fluid and it's really fun to accidentally perform an environmental take down, it feels really fluid and natural. My only real complaint about the combat is that you carry a gun at all times with one shot you have to recharge and to use it is the same button as the finisher button. Often times, I went for a finisher and it would waste my shot instead because I wasn't in just the right spot to perform the finisher.​Every level has a theme and particular set of enemies. For example, you'll find thugs in a sewer level or bouncers at a night club level. The enemies for the most part feel the same but do have some small differences in how they attack. My main issue is sometimes they try to get a bit creative with the levels and it just makes them really frustrating. There are some levels where you ride a vehicle and it changes the feeling of the game too much. Also some levels have hazards you have to avoid while fighting and it just feels overwhelming and frustrating. For example, there's an early level with a helicopter shooting into a train and you have to avoid the helicopter's guns while fighting enemies. There are a few other instances like this throughout the game and none of them were fun, they were all just frustrating.The game overall was a lot of fun though. It's short and sweet. You'll probably finish it at around 6 hours. I did find it hard to play in long sessions but each stage can be completed anywhere between 3-10 minutes. It's a great game to play in quick spurts. It's definitely worth your time though even with the issues aside.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a solid base when it comes to the combat system. It's versatile yet simple, giving you a breadth of options to flow between at a fairly quick pace with a huge assortment of unique weapons and enemies to fight against. I wish this game was more polished and well thought out to bring that kind of gameplay to a satisfying endpoint. It's unfortunately marred by some janky controls where direction in navigation is unintuitive or trying to switch between fighting and shooting has you swinging aimlessly at the air for example, or that it's attempts to streamline every control into a few buttons is poorly accommodated resulting in grappling close up targets when you really want to use the long-range hook, which is also ruined by the bad auto-aim system that affects the gunplay too. There are far FAR too many show-stopping cutscenes and dialogue that interrupts the pace in a game that should be consistently fluid and fast, with no option to skip as far as I know. The writing therein offers nothing of value on top of that, it's full of cheap homages, which on it's own isn't intrinsically a bad thing but when constantly shoved in your face and paired with the rest of the writing's ineffectual attempts to be funny or provide context as to why anything is happening falls flat the game play starts to feel sidelined to an annoying degree. Why is it constantly wasting my time? Levels will sometimes bring out new frustrating gameplay elements that are counter-intuitive and unexplained. Enemies parrying and counter attacking with no telegraphing, or a slow moving motorcycle that sweeps the level to damage you while you're caught in a big group of people unable to really do anything against it until by luck, it crashes into something and explodes.I really did want to enjoy this more but the poor series of high-level design decisions is a significant drawback to the overall experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Fast dynamic gameplay with cool looking animations. Fights aren't boring and are sometimes quite of a challenge except of the flamethrower chef boss in which fight u have to wait until his flamethrower runs out which stales the game a little bit. Soundtrack in some scenes is so perfectly timed that you can get goose bumps from it. 4h main story gameplay with additional content like challenges, collectibles ect. There are also some references to other games which is quite cool. To sum up it's a nice quick game that u can finish in one run that really can give u that DoPaMeIn

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid Hotline Miami style game. The combat itself is pretty simple but feels nice and fluid. The ranged combat however really doesn't feel great and enemies have no indication on when they will fire. The style of the game is decent and the soundtrack is really good and fits well.The story is okay for a game like this but nothing to write home about. Some of the dialogue can be funny but I found a lot of it to be really cringey and trying too hard to be edgy. There are also a few filler levels involving vehicles that shouldn't even be in the game, they are bad. The game is at it's best when it get's a little weird with its enemy design and leans into the melee combat. Overall it's not bad, and if you want something similar to Hotline Miami then this could be a quick fix.6/10

I would say the combat is like the old Assassins Creed system where you punch a bit and counter at most but either way it feels right. The finishers are awesome and really makes you feel the impact and the brawl. Skill tree is fun to unlock since you only need to complete the levels and abilities are fun to do. But there is a sin that this game keeps doing while you are playing it.I wanna say that while improving and bringing new stuff to the table in beat em ups and hack and slash games is good, if overdone, it can overshadow the other fun stuff you already built yourself. Every 3 levels there is something new added, whether is a new type of enemy or a new mechanic that takes you by surprise... and then it gets a reskin and it appears every other level, and also is bigger.Im talking about guns, yes. There is a point in the game when guns are just everywhere; from pistols to smgs, to assault rifles to shotguns, to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ miniguns and rocket launchers. And let me tell you, these guys are the most trigger happy enemies ive ever seen in higher difficulties. And thats OK.But what is NOT OKAY (and here is where the rant starts) is the hell that the guy making this game was being held at gunpoint; [spoitler]Graveyard.[/spoiler]It is almost the last drop for me, since I still have most of the game still. And this is where the thing I said earlier comes into play. In my eyes, it seemed like having the idea of trying to make more interesting stuff  to the game would make it more fun, it basically forgot what made the game fun in the first place. With guns I guess I can give it a pass, since things in the story get more and more heated. But with this? I cannot. To add salt to the wound, the  do not behave like the normal enemies, and their  (which is the only thing they do aside from walking (and sometimes running)) is that is a grab, that does not have cooldown, and that they can chain it while you are in the ground. Plus, to 100% with is challenges, you have to PERSONALLY hit them with your HANDS instead of firearms, plus with a machete, which yknow, you have to get close and ultimetly die in their arms trying to hit them. Fun, right? (I 80% it anyway, im not too eager to go back for the golden tooths.)But either way, it is a great beat em up and im happy playing it, just that, it makes me hit some big rocks on the ride. _childDocuments_.review: Starts really strong, but becomes quite weak by the end. Every level brings something new and fun. But by the end sometimes balancing feels unfair and moveset becomes so big that you are not using half or more of it.But it is very fun at the begining, when enemies don't have OP weapons and you are happy to unlock and use every new move. _childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Think Hotline Miami like violence with Sifu like combat mechanics and Katana Zero like levels of badassery. This is the closest thing to be an action movie star from the 90s. The parry mechanics are well designed. The variety of moves are really high and you get to use lots of environmental items (pillows, bins, bats, knives, etc) as weapons. The story starts fairly generic but then it becomes quite interesting. Also, the level design is really good. Fighting on top of moving trains, a plane, the underground, a club, a graveyard, the rooftop of a skyscraper. The variety of environments is top notch.The game is nowhere near as hard as Sifu or Katana Zero but you can make it if you want. There is also a nice level editor if you want to design your ideal combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express is an adrenaline-pumping joyride that’s got me hooked! After nearly 9 hours of gameplay, I can’t get enough of the sheer frenetic energy this game brings to the table. It’s a wild mix of everything we love about fighting – imagine the best bits from action movies and top-notch game mechanics all rolled into one.The fights are Insanely intense. Every punch, every move feels so satisfyingly crunchy. About the challenges – this game doesn’t hold back. It’s the kind of challenge that keeps you coming back for more, pushing you to get better with every round.This game also has plenty of unlockables! There’s something addictively rewarding about unlocking new skills and move sets, making each victory even sweeter.The mechanics are top-notch. Smooth, responsive controls make every move feel like second nature. It's that kind of gaming experience that just clicks.All in all, Midnight Fight Express is a knockout in the fighting game genre. It perfectly blends the best elements from movies and games we all have watched, played and, to this day, love. Serving up a thrilling, action-packed experience with a solid storyline, awesome mechanics, and enough challenges and unlockables to keep you addicted for hours.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game I received on Humble Bundle this month with a moderate to low expectation of having any fun with it. Humble Bundle games can be big hits or misses but this one had a solid 91% positive reviews on Steam so I decided to give it a whirl. After about eight hours (a good bit of that was idle time in the main menu so realistically 2-4 hours I’d say) I finished the game and unlocked the entire progression tree. I can say that  this game was 100% worth my time and I can see myself getting another couple of hours out of it now that I can go back and try to “S” rank levels with all the skills unlocked. Seeing the $20 price tag on Steam makes me hesitate slightly but given the fact that this game was created by a single developer, Jacob Dzwinel, I would toss my concerns aside to just encourage you to give the man his well-earned money. As per most of my reviews, I’m just going to talk about some of the stuff that stuck out to me versus the standard array of game mechanics reviewers tend to speak to.Not a very creative first category but a necessary one to discuss when talking about . This is the real bread and butter of the game as it will encompass ~95% of your time while playing. I can wholeheartedly endorse the finely tuned, well thought-out mechanics this game props itself up on. At first, the game felt a bit sluggish to me (I was initially ignoring the well-given advice and tried on mouse and keyboard) and after switching to controller I found that was 100% a personal problem. As you unlock the basic dodge (via tutorial), parry, heavy attack, and combos the game starts to really shine. All of these unlocks take approximately 15 minutes to come about so the game doesn’t waste too much time before getting you its most important tools.The fighting is great. It is a well-crafted, intricate gameplay loop that clearly had been thought out and thoroughly tested by the developer. The hit feel heavy, the rage mode feels solid, and the finishers/parries make you feel like you are the main character which is exactly what I was looking for. Its fun, the animations are all great, and I am happy to report that this part of the game knocked it out of the park. Just, don’t be me, play it on controller from the get-go.I was somewhat surprised to learn that this game incorporated firearms, but I figured they would be rather rare from what the tutorial made of them and that, considering this was a  game, I wouldn’t see much of them. I was quite wrong about that, and I think this is one of the two areas that  starts to slip a bit in. Firearms feel pretty good but they miss the mark for me when using them. First off, large crowds of enemies wielding firearms is rather annoying to deal with and can screw up a pretty fun flow the game has going for it until you get the  There is a weird glitch(?) that occurs when you shoot and enemy in quick succession where the “lock-on” you had disappears for a split second and causes that second/third shot to miss. This, especially when firing into a crowd of enemies, is frustrating and had me avoiding firearms for most of my playthrough. If this was intentionally added to make firearms less OP, I guess I can see the argument. I just think that guns in this game, at the volume that they appear, messed up the flow of the game for me a bit.My biggest gripe with  is the inclusion of the “alternative mechanic” levels. Out of the game’s 40 missions, I think only 4 (maybe 5?) of these levels are anything besides the core gameplay fighting loop. However, I never enjoyed these missions. They’re the equivalent of a mid-2000’s mandatory turret section developers seemed to love, and those just never hit their intended mark for me. In particular,  fight was just infuriating and poorly paced. One bad level obviously doesn’t come close to ruining this very pleasant experience for me, but it’s evident that this level didn’t receive the love that many other better areas of the game did. For me, many of these parts weren’t difficult, its just that I found them as a slog I had to get through to get back to the gameplay. Overall, really doesn’t ruin the experience, just wouldn’t recommend adding them into some sort of sequel (and I certainly will skip them on my replay). Awesome game, evidently a labor of love from developer Jacob Dwiznel. $20 is a bit steep but honestly if you even remotely enjoy fighting games, give the man his money, its well-earned. I look forward to any future work that this developer is planning on releasing and really have enjoyed my time with .

_childDocuments_.review: It is a pretty good fighting game in the spirit of Hotline Miami. It is not as forgiving as you can take multiple hits and have checkpoints. Levels are relatively small and you can finish them generally in couple minutes without dying. Fighting feels good, melee weapons hit hard and finishers got meat behind them. Guns were pretty wonky, and game gets filled with them later on, but you can survive quite well trusting your fists. As others have stated, they are not the strong point of this game.Soundtrack isn't memorable but gets you pumped enough to feel the rhythm. Story is completely wacko and skipped most of it. I think the dialog moments generally broke the pacing. You get skill point after each level that you can invest into couple trees for new moves. For achievers, levels have ranking system so you can replay earlier levels again for that S rank. Overall quite solid experience.Will not recommend the game, though, because of couple technical issues.If you don't face these issues and are looking for a nice action package, I can recommend this. For me, they were enough to turn thumb down.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall i definitely enjoyed 100%ing it.the challenges were a good way to spice up the experience chasing s ranks and special criteria even if some were more difficult than they needed to be but that just made me feel more like john wick when i did get them done. the combat is fast and mostly responsive parrying punching and stomping through the city with the only issue being activating rope combos and selecting which bullet type to use on the fly being un reliable and clunky.the music is fantastic at making you feel cool even if most of the tracks blur together by the end of it.the story is what it needs to be with fun set piece missions and references galore ,i did feel like it was padding making me play through it 3 times for the achievements since the hardest didnt unlock the trophy for the lower difficulty.for a budget title it packs a punch and does not take itself too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent John Wick vibe game with arkham style combat mixed with Hotline miami style gameplay. There is a ton of awesome easter eggs/ references that have you enjoying the game the whole experience. There is a ton of content for multiple playthroughs and lots of fun enemy types. The only con i would say is some boss fights can be a bit too easy or too hard. That being said good game and decent story. Solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hotline Miami: John Wick EditionPretty much everything about this game is super solid. Simple to control but hard to master combat. Combos and takedowns with Gun Fu that really make you feel like John Wick. A KILLER OST by Noisecream which slaps everytime. Despite being short has a ton of replay value with several challenges to do with 40 levels. Customizing your agent with the either super cool or stupidly goofy items you get from said challenges.The only negative things I'd have to say is game can be a bit wonky, softlocking while using photo mode one time and such. Plus the story is fine enough, not good but it's goofy enough to where you stay along for the ride for how wacky it is. Plus the keyboard controls kinda suck, listen to the devs and use a controller. Other than that it's been super smooth sailing.This game is very much worth your money!!! Full priced or on sale!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I am currently, at the time of writing this review, about 3/4 through the game's levels, and I'm having a blast!I saw someone saying that the game gets ridiculously tough near the end, but I can't say I've had the same experience, so far!If you like the John Wick movies, and you like to beat people up and kill them in creative ways (in a videogame!), then you'll probably enjoy this game!A few nitpicks I have is that the game can feel really chaotic and fast at times, where you just can't keep up with what's happening, there IS a button that slows down time and shows you objects you can use to fight back, but there's already a lot of buttons and combo inputs to keep track of, and it's just too much for my brain to handle I think. Also some levels throw a lot of enemies with guns at you, and it can be hard to consistently dodge them without spam rolling around and praying. As far as I can tell, there's no warning when an enemy is going to fire their guns, and bullets are 'hit-scan' in this game, meaning that bullets have no travel time and hit their mark as soon as the gun is fired.Gameplay: 4/5Music: 4/5Story: 3/5 (still not done with the story, so it might be better or worse than a 3/5!)

_childDocuments_.review: Want to feel as bad@ss as john wick? Then this is the game for you! For an example, You'll empty a handguns mag and then proceed to toss it at an enemy while immediately punching another. Almost everything around you can be used as a weapon just as john wick does. Its probably one of the best hack and slash/ beat em up games I've ever played. looks great, plays great, and is just a solid game all around. Babyface has a good amount of customize-able clothing options as well that just adds to the fun. My babyface is rocking a bag over his head, no shirt, sagging jeans, and duck slippers, all while killing baddies with speed.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best fighting games I've ever played.  Criticism of the game being too hard is valid.  It is indeed a hard game - you have to invest the time to be able to unleash the huge variety of moves at the right time, but when you do, it is so satisfying.  My only quibble is that the other enemies stand back when you grab a bad guy.  This wouldn't happen in real life.  But I guess the developers thought it was necessary or some of the levels on the toughest difficulty level would be too hard for even seasoned gamers to complete.   Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled upon this game completely at random, so I had no expectations going in.As the main component of the game, combat is very polished, complex and fluid, leaving quite a bit of room for experimentation. The upgrades make a major impact on combat (no +10% damage upgrades to be found here :) ) and what I have noticed is that there are a ♥♥♥♥ ton of finishers, to the point where I am certain I have not seen them all yet. I enjoyed the story a lot, and I like how the game manages to make room for humor and absurdity without ruining the dark overall theme. All these things, along with the phenomenal soundtrack ( Noisecream's finest work, in my opinion) make for a really enjoyable experience. Still, there are some parts towards the end where the pacing is completely broken by some gimmicky enemies and one particular boss fight against a certain agricultural machine.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: As promised, this game delivers great gameplay with great motion capture.Gmaeplay wise there a lot of different attacks I can hardly memorize all the inputs (it's not complicated inputs, but it's pretty situational and mostly a way to boost your score).The game is quite short, I finished it in more than 5 hours, I had some difficulties in some level playing in normal but otherwise it was smooth sailing. The level design is really great though, there are a lot of different environment, so it doesn't get stale at all.There is some replayability, with a difficult mode and also challenges you unlock once you complete a level for the first time.However, my mains issues that keeps this game from being a great game in my opinion are :- The music : the most boring ass synthwave I ever heard, it feels like everysong is the same, I can't even remember one of them. Hotline miami, which is for me a reference in terms of video game soundtrack, would take risk and the songs being used in each level would contribute to the atmosphere of the level.- The dialogs : The game has a ♥♥♥♥ ton of written dialogs and cutscenes, and you have to go through them before advancing to the next fight. I had the game in French so maybe the translation was a big miss in terms of how the message should have been delivered, but all of them were trying a bit to hard in being funny and It was just pointless.- The story : those dialogs are here because the game tries really hard to force the story onto you, by tring to hype you up by creating artifical suspense, but it becomes annoying past a point.The (single dev) behind all this game put in amazing work, and the game is definitely worth to be played, but it feels definitely very inequals in some aspects...Hope this review will help him in his future projects :)

_childDocuments_.review: Fun brawler for at least one play through and has an awesome soundtrack. Only complaint is the gun play is not the best when playing with a controller, since there is no targeting reticle (but there is one when playing with mouse & keyboard), so kind of have to guess what you're aiming at until a dot pops up on the target. _childDocuments_.review: "Brutha♥♥♥♥a, do we look like we give a ♥♥♥♥ about your family?"  -some dude who just wanted to talk his bro about ScrabbleIt's the good ol' Arkham combat loop, but the setpieces are a bunch of bite-sized levels instead of an open world you can freely explore. Also, there's no stealth shenanigans. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like fighting games/brawlers etc., you can't go wrong with this one.----And now to the stream of consciousness-gibberish part:This game is the closest you are going to get to the Hotline Miami feeling (so far), which in itself is a feat and worth the purchase, in my opinion. It can also hold its own, but obviously a lot of the aesthetics and game mechanics are derived from earlier, more successful titles (think Sifu + Batman Arkham series + Hotline Miami). Soundtrack is great, but.. ..there are no downtimes. I would expect the game to alternate between the high-adrenaline rushes of killing sprees and laid-back, comfy chill out zones - which is, in fact, something the devs DID try to implement by providing the player character with an all-accompanying drone that talks to you, acting as a side-kick. It does work out in a way, but the music doesn't acknowledge when you are doing what, which ends up with you trying to understand what the drone is babbling about while the bass is pumping and all you want to do is play and NOT stand there listening to a NPC. The controls are a bit too overboard for my taste. Overly convoluted. You have to press ALL the buttons on your controller (I can't even imagine how anyone would be physically able to play this on mouse and keyboard) and at the break-neck speed of a Hotline Miami game. Also, some moves you can counter, while others are un-counterable, which is just stupid. And you can't even block. In a martial arts CQC (close-quarters combat) game. Definitely not a decision I would have made.The art style is a bit too simplistic I feel. Sure, in a game like this graphics are about the last thing you'd look at, but I think the artworks you see communicate a different mood than the asset-flippity reality of what the game ultimately looks like. The world building suggests a cyberpunk-esque society and near-future setting, but if it wasn't for the drone telling you this face to face, it would hardly be noticeable. Too much visual noise is bad, especially in a game as fast-paced as this one, but a wee bit more of 'The Ascent' or 'Gamedec' would have been nice. All in all, it's not too bad, but seeing how Hotline Miami worked so well because of how the music integrated with the graphics and presentation as a whole, I fail to understand why the devs would try to cut corners budget-wise on this end. If the game had more of a style of its own, it would surely have sold better. My opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express has a really solid combat system and utilizes its theme, limitations, and pace well. The demo offers a good chunk of what this game is about. You get to see what the fluid free flow combat has to offer on a surface level, as well as how the progression and story levels work. So I suggest give the demo a go, and decide if you want to purchase the game. Although, this game is also on Xbox Gamepass, so if you're already subscribed, Midnight Fight Express serves as a nice small dish on the side on there too.In this 6-hour game, you play as "Babyface", the most wanted fighter going after the main villain "Boss". You can fully customize your character, the only restriction is your gender. Playing through the story and completing challenges unlock new cosmetic options. Most options are based on the style of the game's cover, pretty random and rebellious looks. Pretty random, that's what this game theme is. The story's overall arc is rather cohesive, but the events that are presented level-to-level are pretty effing wild, therefore offering a lot of variety in mood and tone, gameplay differences, and memorable encounters too. From Hotline Miami-like assaults on hotels and mansions, to gang warfare, a sci-fi lab, a resurrection of zombies and rat mutants, Midnight Fight Express is a ridiculous action movie that only lacks the downside of a movie - that you can actually play it.MFE's combat system is oddly well-designed. I chose to use the word "oddly" because even AAA games like the Yakuza games and Sleeping Dogs have satisfying and cinematic combat systems, but somehow are not accommodating to every fight in the game. MFE throws you against hordes of angry bad guys. Each fight you fight a room full of people, most with weapons that can make quick work to put you down. You feel like a badass sweeping through rooms after rooms of dudes. The control is responsive and doesn't tie you down to slow animations or special effects. It focuses a lot on fast combos and target-switching. One of the earliest abilities you can unlock allows you to fly across the room to hit a dude further away. The enemy AI's are also aggressive and encourage you to either commit to constant target-switching, or perfect defense in a form of parry and its variations, such as fast or heavy parry punish, disarm or push, etc.The game also shells you a constant barrage of new enemy archetypes or slightly different variations in each level. There are 69 variations of enemies in this game. All of them are quite distinct and behave differently in gameplay. The capabilities of the bots are also impressive and manage to prevent the game from being a button mash. Weaker enemies are easy to kill but they sometimes block and have unblockable moves. Special enemies like the Muscles, Dicers, top-Ninjas, etc. appear often and can shake up the fights intensely. I also like how enemies on the later levels are different combinations of earlier enemies as well, making them stronger but not feel like a wrench thrown into the gameplay loop.The brutal animations of the attacks and finishers are also what make the combat so addicting. They are easy to trigger, give the player i-frames, and make enemies back off a bit during the animations as well.The skill tree progression system is also well designed. At the end of the game, you will eventually get enough points to buy every skill. The fantastic addition is the toggle option for each skill you unlocked, making self-imposed challenges easier to set up, as well as giving the option to disable button prompts that the player doesn’t want.There is also Playground mode where you can test your combat skills and interactions of the game’s sandbox. There is also an endless wave option for you to bash heads in indefinitely non-stop. Nothing really beats that.7.5/10 a solid beat-em-up game with silly story that doesn't overstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read this: I only, and i say strongly, only recommend this game on a sale, and I mean a good one. For all this games good parts, it has some very clear flaws that makes it hard to give it a full recommend, but if the game is cheap, you can look past its flaws. Now, Midnight Fight Express has several upsides. Great music, fun combat, plenty of good stages, a really good start and end, as well as a story that I enjoyed. Its not Hotline Miami caliber storytelling, but its pretty damn close. The Animations are also top notch, and watching people's head explode after shoving them into a wall never gets boring. But, when this game tries to stray from its formula, like its vehicle sections, its out-of-place Church section with instakill enemies or introducing targets that are a pain to kill without certain skills, it starts to fumble. When the challenges become not about skill or ability but pure luck and deeply frustrating, it stumbles. The middle portion of the game especially suffers from this, and I do believe that you could have cut the 40 missions down to 30, and nothing of value would have been lost. Again, as I said above, I do recommend this game if it is cheap. Otherwise, do yourself a favor and watch a LP on YouTube first, and only then buy the game at full price if you can get past this games flaws. I do hope the developer makes more games in the future, since he clearly has talent. He just needs to focus on what he does best.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable fist fighting power fantasy.I had never head of this game when it was given to me, and I wasn’t sure what to think of it. However, 30 minutes into it I was already enjoying myself.Midnight Fight Express is an isometric fighting game. You play as Babyface, a former member of the criminal underworld lured back into a life a crime. Your mission against impossible odds is to fight your way across the city to prevent a citywide criminal takeover.The story is a bit bland. It’s like an old 80s action film, kill the bad guys until they are all dead. A few little twists and turns along the way but nothing major. Midnight Fight Express is mostly about the game play, a modern beat-'em-up with over-the-top violence. You can use weapons, knives, swords, batons and guns as part of your arsenal. You can also use environmental objects as weapons, such as chairs, boxes which can be kicked and thrown at enemies. After each level you can upgrade your character with extra moves and abilities, making you more powerful. This is where the main fun of the game happens. It’s kind of like Doom Eternal where you are the most feared and most powerful entity in the game, and nobody can stop you. By the time you reach the end, you are the ultimate bad ass ready to stop anything that stands in your way. There is also good replay value with challenges for each level unlocked after completing them. The game should last around 8 hours on hard mode but that’s ok. It’s an intense fast paced game. Any longer and you would feel burnt out and exhausted. Midnight Fight Express is a fantastic game that has an engaging game play loop. It sounds and looks fantastic, with a visually interesting art style. I’d highly recommend it!Game rating 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A mostly solid beat em up that makes me miss the olden days of Streets of Rage and its many rivals/copycats.You play as a walking set of murderous hands capable of channeling the spirit of any and every movie martial artist ever. Moves are brutal and the ragdolls make the effect hit all the harder sometimes, various unlockable abilities let you unleash more flavors of hell and once you start getting a few down you can easily become a whirlwind of fists and feet and the occasional random flung object.The levels actually feature a nice variety of mixed gameplay at times with chase sequences, sniper battles and gunplay seamlessly mixed in. The game drip feeds you new enemy types almost every level along with a massive variety of weapons which never seem to be useless.You also get a nice amount of character customization options with so many options it'll make your head spin. A very smart choice because your default character looks like Zuckerbergs avatar in the Metaverse.Add to this replayable levels and challenges not to mention mutators to make things that little bit different gives the game some massive replayability.Cons: sometimes inputs can be spotty and ive seen many people complain about heavy frame drops in certain situations (though it hasn't happened to me)Sometimes guns just won't work when you are close to a bad guy for no real reason.lastly some of the challenges are indeed just over the top tricky or hard or have various caveots that aren't mentioned. (Things like shoot X amount of bad guys with guns but your gun or using gun executions don't count for some reason)These however are small things and unless you are a completionist they shouldn't get in the way of your enjoyment of the game

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a fan of the whole beat'em up genre but honestly, I like this game. A lot. It makes me feel as if I'm some sort of retired hitman bent on destruction after my dog was shot by some wannabe upstart but in this game you're just an amnesiac and you get a flying companion called 'droney' who provides more funny than helpful insights. Enjoyed the story quite a bit, especially when it dived into the silly with references galore. Loved how the game tries not to be repetitive by adding a new mechanic of "moving while pointing and shooting" for an entire level 3 times. The first few couple of times were quite fun and refreshing but after a while it kind of gets repetitive when you're trying to complete challenges. The challenges are a mixture of "putting your hand into a blender willingly" or "licking a frozen piece of metal at 0°C". The former is difficult, messy, and something your mother would kill you for if she finds out while the latter is easy and painful. Not to say I don't like challenges but come on, passing a level where you have to avoid pepper spray from 7 different security guards who, mind you, are mostly behind groups of 4-5 men and one of them is waiting his entire life to pepper spray you at the end of a cut scene. Closest thing to feeling like a sexual predator at that level. Combat was surprisingly easy to pick up and strangely got even easier after the addition of a certain tool from a gang with suspiciously familiar purple clothing style and a stupidly difficult challenge about a harvester at the end of the level. Though to be honest, there had been a couple of times where I wanted to put my fist into the my poor screen, just like that fat clowny bloke at the metro station, after going through all 40 levels over and over again. I mean, I went for 100% so what was I expecting right?The music is genuinely sublime, it brought the feeling closer to that one scene where the retired hitman rampages through a club looking for the man that off'ed his dog. Never felt a cooler moment than that. Side note, there's a pretty nice reference to that one music video where three cats strolled into a club and fight broke out. Overall, pretty enjoyable if you're playing for the sake of it but if you want to get 100%, you better have the patience of saint and dexterous fingers.P.S. The elevator level is the perfect place to get murdered a bunch of times to get that one achievement ;)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best brawlers of 2022! I cannot comprehend the fact that a small indie studio can develop such a nice combat system, where you can be styling on enemies with awesome mo-capped animations created by none other than Eric Jacobus, who made some really cool "Tekken In Real Life" videos awhile back. It certainly feels like you're inside a modern-day action movie reminiscent of films like "John Wick", "The Equalizer", and "Nobody". If you're looking for a game that best captures this feel, definitely give "Midnight Fight Express" a try. The story is a complete cluster♥♥♥♥ with levels that can sometimes be serious or goofy. Aside from the obvious comparisons to "Hotline Miami", "Midnight Fight Express" has the same element of "mystery surrounding your actions revealed as you progress".  The only variety in enemies is their cosmetic designs, as they pretty much have the same movesets, but they're just reskinned and very few are truly unique. For a game that's 5 hours long, it's worth picking up and it definitely won't disappoint with its' smooth beat'em'up gameplay and level diversity.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Its a shame, I want to like this, and for the first few levels it was pretty good.  Sound and music are great, and the actual animations are really well done.  You can really feel the blows when you put someone down.The problem is the combat feels totally random.  You get instances where the enemy attack is clearly telegraphed, and others where you get instantly hit without the chance to react.  Ive had instances where I get randomly shoved and it causes me to die, and others where an enemy has grabbed and thrown me off the map without any chance at all to react.  I always seem to be flailing at some guy across the screen instead of the guy next to me.  After coming from games like Sifu and the Batman series, it feels janky and totally unfair.The other problem is the constant amount of waffle.  Every time you clear a screen, the next one you are bombarded with speech from the annoying drone.  The game encourages you to repeat levels, but then doesn't have the option to skip these waffling scenes, only fast forward them.If you just want to switch off and rampage through and enjoy the cool animations and sound id say wait until a big sale.EDIT:Having played a bit more I can see some of the difficulties come from enemies attacking other enemies that hit you instead.  The combat isnt perfect, but its less random than I initially felt.  The throws that come from the big enemies appear to be punishment for trying to attack a big guy who has his block up, so actually you can react to this.  I would say its a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible beat 'em up, specially if you enjoy movies like John Wick or The Raid.The combat is somewhat simple, but thanks to this performing attacks and fighting multiple enemies at once is really satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a number of incredible ideas, the levels are zany and diverse, the story is silly but well-paced so it ends up being fun, the customization of the character is off the charts, there’s tons of replayability and the game also has a fantastic combat system that gets more complex, brutal and satisfying as you upgrade your skills.So why am I giving it a negative recommendation?The game is buggy, not as a whole, frankly I played the game pass version at launch at it was way buggier and unbalanced than this version, but at its core… The game has balancing issues when it comes to the difficulty, it’s not that it’s hard, it’s frustrating, and this gets exacerbated by a strange combo system that doesn’t really explain in a clear way how to maintain it; it simply mentions that you have to be diverse with your attacks and not get hit, but this becomes extremely difficult when you’re getting swarmed with multiple enemies that only have guns at the middle of the game; this scenarios don’t provide you with a situation were you can be diverse with your attacks, because if you use some of the guns your enemies are using the game penalizes you for lack of diversity, but if you stop using the guns that your enemies are using and simply focus in using your fists and experiment with the different combos that you have, then the game punishes you by shooting you in the face…This is the core problem of the game, it has incredible ideas but a contradictory design philosophy, so every time I’m having a blast, disarming enemies, stomping on them, and building up my instinct meter (something you get if you don’t get hit that gives you a bit of a damage boost and later lets you perform special moves) I also have to deal with the brutal difficulty balancing.The game does offer options in the form of a customizable difficulty selection, although I wish this was more complex and offered more customization opportunities. So far you can customize your health, enemy aggression, damage indicators, instinct bar, and some hud elements. But there are few options here to make the game truly easier, with only the first two of these settings letting you have more health and lower the enemy aggression, for example. The rest serve as a way to make the game even challenging, disabling damage indicators or even turning off the instinct power altogether.I’m really sorry I’m giving the game a thumbs down because what’s good here is great, the customization is fantastic, the humour is hilarious, and the combat system is extremely diverse and satisfying, there are even executions that you can perform with different weapons and even environmental ones that are extremely diverse. I just wish the devs wouldn’t have “bank” as much into the notion of challenge, and instead focus more in the aspects that make the game more enjoyable.The game has received a couple of patches since its release so it’s clear the developers do care about heeding the players complaints and issues, mine right now, personally, is the fact that the game doesn’t save my custom difficulty settings after each game restart, instead defaulting my values.I truly hope the developers keep fixind, and adding stuff to the game, given that it’s truly a fantastic experience at its core, I just wish it didn’t have the type of bug I describe in the last paragraph, and instead added more options for folks like me that want to feel like an overpowered monster whilst toying around with the amazing customization.The gore is also great by the way…

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:+ Great "Game Feel" (It's FUN to play)+ Soundtrack kicks ass+ Levels are short but plentiful, so you'll never be stuck long but have plenty to play+ Challenges are genuinely challenging+ Huge weapon varietyMID:+/- The writing is campy, which people may or may not enjoyCON:- Cutscenes and dialog are not truly "skipped" on replay, it's instead a jarring fast-forward effect. It'd be nice if a way could be found to make replays uninterrupted, but it seems the game is just made this wayI was sold on MFE when I saw the first trailer. I then played the demo, and it lacked a certain "feel" I can't describe... But the 1.0 release seems to have fixed whatever that problem was. I've loved losing myself to the music while playing on Realistic, going for additional challenges, high scores on the leaderboards (I felt great getting a couple level's scores to Global Top 5)The flow of fights, the impact of fists, the mess left behind after a fight... It makes the game more than the sum of its parts. Highly, highly recommended. Don't want to drop money on it? It's on Gamepass as of this writing! _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Probably my favourite beat'em up so far.Cool music, great action and great levels.The story is also quite nice and I've enjoyed looking for extra characters to talk to around the levels.It's challenging but not impossible, so much  so that's probably the only game that I've tried to complete fully (only one challenge is missing, if somebody knows how to complete the church in 50 seconds, please, let me know ).People complains about the weapons, and I can see why. The first time you face them they feel overpowered, but after a while you'll figure out the level and how to use all the moves, and it's feel great to go through waves of enemies in a few seconds.Here's some of the issues I had with the game:- Sometimes, while fighting an enemy, you will pass through walls in rooms without an exit. Quite frustrating if you don't know how to spawn them.- There is only a masculine customizable skin.- I'm surprised there is no The Bride skin from "Kill Bill", nor a yellow tracksuit from Bruce lee :)Anyway, these are all minor complains. _childDocuments_.review: The game is great, I love it, obvious recommend. The combat is fun and makes you feel like an overpowered cracked up discount red hood murdering your way through an entire city. Some moments are absurd in a good and/or funny way, and every fight is enjoyable to a degree. Certain fights and enemies also test your skill and/or competency at the game in engaging, hectic, or fun ways.There are some drawbacks, like how the vehicle sections are boring, guns sound weak sometimes, and the "heavy bois" enemy are kinda BS.The bosses are a 'lil bit of a mixed bag. Sometimes they feel too easy, and other times they feel a lil' basic, but they have their own gimmicks and such to make a neat 'lil character, plus there are a few that give a challenge if you're not prepared or if you rush in thinking you can fight god.BUT LEMME TELL YA SOMETHING ABOUT A PARTICULAR BOSS.Something that'll spare ya your sanity.Something so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, that I opened up steam IMMEDIATELY after the fact to write this review.The Scorpion Queen boss is something that will hurt you personally. You can call me bad all you want but trust me, if you don't know what to do, you'll have a bad ♥♥♥♥♥♥ time.Possibly the worst ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss designed by mankind.So when that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ farming tractor with the blades shows up on your screen, HERE'S A TIP:(1. Whenever you see explosives to throw, throw them at the boss when no enemies are there. If there are enemies, you'll auto throw at 'em. Don't risk throwing them when enemies are about to spawn.(2. Hug the bottom of the screen and be ready to dome any enemies holding gun via the secondary revolver you unlock earlier in the game. MEMORIZE where the gun enemies come in.(3. Stun the enemies with the gun, don't waste ammo on em, and unload your gun on the boss, regardless of what kind of gun it is. BE SURE TO DODGE THE ENEMIES ROPE ATTACK, PAY ATTENTION. You will get killed regardless of if you break out of it or not.(4. If you aren't able to get a gun and use it whenever they pop up during the fight, just throw yourself into the boss, die, and restart the fight. There's only four times when enemies spawn and after that the boss speeds up and kills you, it's unavoidable.Some of you will thank me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a superb beat 'em up.. It feels a bit limited at first, but you unlock skills quickly (one per level), and things get much more interesting fast. Strikes, combos. parries, counters, grapples, throws, melee weapons, a LOT of guns, disarms, brutal finishing moves that vary per attack/weapon type, and more become available.Similar to Sifu in some ways, I gotta say I prefer MFE. It doesn't look that pretty but the gameplay feels great. This is essentially a John Wick simulator- put in more than hour or two and you WILL feel like a badass/monster. You will also die hilariously.  I am actually kinda liking the story so far, although it isn't really necessary, and scenes can be skipped on replays.And replay is an area where MFE really shines; every level has numerous goals to achieve after you've completed them once, including tracking your best time/score and leaderboards. I haven't finished the game yet (very close now), but I have already replayed some areas many (20+) times. The fights never come out the same way twice, partly because I want to use these cool skills I just got. Things can get chaotic and you'll definitely die to things you can't anticipate, but it never feels terribly unfair with short levels and generous checkpoints.Seriously, if you like beat 'em ups, you need to give this a try. There's also lot of gunplay involved, and a handful of vehicle levels, and a wide array of enemies. I am addicted.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, good supplement for Hotline Miami if you search for something like that.However last boss is horse***t, talking about the bloody insta kill laser, rest of his moves is fine but I could not beat him for 3 days until I finally cheesed with rope spam and stun lock.The game is fairly easy even on realistic difficulty, I finished it in one go as when you die you respawn at previous checkpoint.Storyline? Dunno, I do not play games like this spiritual successor to Hotline Miami for storyBut I could easily spot references to other titles which this game just drips with and I loved all of them, pillow man, The Fans, No Russian from CoDMW2 and waaaay more.The game is really good and I would not change anything about it besides this bloody last bossfight.
