_childDocuments_.review: Ultra violent fast paced Massacre 'em all. Close to excellence.Far is the time of the first Double Dragons and its blinking dying enemies before seeing them disappear from the screen.Here you chain and combine dozens of techniques. Use environment elements, grapple, brutalize, finish, execute, sometimes humiliate close to hundred different types of enemies. This along 40 shorts but intense maps while using a large variety of weapons or your fists and kicks.Big up to the brutal knife stab in the throat and breaking toilet sinks with heads (or the over way around).2 maps are turning into shoot'em up. One of them, the motorbike scene is more painful than exciting.Another one, stuck in an elevator is also not a success. Requiring to roll dodge all the time to avoid to get shot in the head at the first standing up occasion. Not fun.Last boss is also frustrating.The other maps are good to excellent.Enemies and gameplay vary constantly. Same for the maps that always bring new things including different environments and configurations.The number of challenges and bonus or cosmetics to acquire offers a great replayability with different play styles.This is definitely a Git Gud game. You can improve all the time. And play all your tricks but not all the time and not against every characters. You need to compose.What is to regret is, some weapons should instantly stop an enemy action but does not. Stunning some with electricity for example only works if the enemy did not start his/her combo.You may use enemies as shields but there is no real option for that. And since the game is already very detailed, seeing a next opus where pushing them against each other really affects their moves and balance could be a real plus.Acquiring a S rank in every levels can be quite challenging. If you expect to unlock all the achievements, you may have to spend some time and nerves on it. Good luck!Cosmetics are varied. Some are really funny. The main character is a male. Except some few complete panoplies, you wont play a character close to a female look that you can customize. If you cannot live with it, better not buying this game then.The interface is somptuous. Till the options to hide the chats and/or auto skip the cutscenes before replaying a map.Pay attention however with this option. Some NPC are to be discovered to discuss with them (not mandatory). Finding them all rewards with an achievement. But if you find them replaying while skipping the dialogs, you wont be able to read what they say and this is a one shot only. You wont be able to make them talk again later without restarting a full new game.Reading all the chat boxes is probably the most annoying part. It breaks the pace of the game during the first playthrough of a map. It may become a little annoyance. But you can quickly skip them if you are not interested into reading. Voicing this would have been so much appreciated instead. The music is also many times not good. A bad easy lazy hardcore techno/dubstep. Including in these genres, there is so much better outside than what we are provided with. More variety of genres and so, atmospheres, would have been appreciated here as well.The audio is definitely not the strong part of this game.The references to video games, movies, comics characters and pop culture in general are numerous. This is great and sometimes really funny.One did say here in the reviews, this is a Statham simulator. There is something of this indeed. This remark is funny and thinking about that, I would have preferred a story like Crank better than the one proposed. It is not that bad. But it could be less "serious" or pretentious and more stupid fun instead. Especially when the chat boxes with the drone becomes annoying for a story you do not care much about.The game should have been completely serious during the fights. This is not always the case with some karate/wing chun moves. But completely crazy fun on the story. Crank is definitely the best reference that comes to my mind to image my thoughts. That are those details that separate this game from excellence.I have encountered very little bugs. A couple of cosmetic ones, particularly some pants let's show pieces of legs of your character through the fabric. Barely visible in game.The very first interface propose to press any button of your controller to access the main menu but only works with keyboard. Then the controller will perfectly works all the time.The coding of the game seems definitely clean. The interface and its options, the animations, the playability, the general absence of bugs... all is great on that side. A very good UX and a very good work.To conclude, if you like the genre and you are not afraid to see your reflexes challenged, just go for it. You should not regret it. Remember, it is extremely violent. It is a concentrate of pure fun arcade.Bravo to its dev(s).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is packed with good content. Fun setpiece levels, a shockingly emotional story despite it being intentionally campy, and fun as hell core combat. Not to mention the 40 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tracks by noisecream. One for every level. For the vibe it seeks to hit, one of 80's bloody rampages, it nails it.It has one flaw, just ONE flaw that dumpsters what would have been a cult classic otherwise. And that's the enemy designIn short: Enemies have three kinds of attacks. Normal attacks, which can be parried easily. Grabs, which can also be parried, and unblockables of many varietys, which must be dodged. The problem comes from the fact that many enemies with exclusively unblockable attacks also have super armor, aka they can't be staggered or interrupted under any circumstance. That absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the flow of the combat. One moment you are ripping through goons, flowing between counters, grabs, and special moves, using the enviroment like jacky chan. The next - suddenly it's dark souls, just constantly dodging and poking at an enemy until it eventually dies of a thousand jabs because you simply cannot do anything else.Some levels are great! Almost no ♥♥♥♥♥ enemies, unblockables saved for rarer bashes and tougher enemies that can be staggered. Some levels are awful, full of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemies that you have no choice but to use enviromental attacks or just sit around for your gun to reload. And those really, really, REALLY drag down the game. This triggers what i cause dodgeroll syndrome, where you are forced to just roll around on the ground like an hedgehog. Excabated by gun-wielding enemies. They are actually shockingly fun and cool for a brawler, because you can disarm and use the guns with tight gunplay, even doing john-wick style gun takedowns. You can close the gap at a certain range with a long-ranged attack, even auto-dodging bulets when doing so. Unfortunately, the range on that mechanic is just a LITTLE too short, forcing you to dodgeroll towards them, then they step away and you end up rolling between 10 guys with guns like a pinball. And as a fun bonus, some enemies can randomly counter your attacks and do massive damage. Do they do anything that indicates they can do that? No. Do they do it consistantly? Also no.Is it still worth playing? Absolutely, especially for the price. The encounter design sucks, but the level design, music, story, action, and setpieces make it a fun campaign to burn through anyway. It just reeks of missed potential, it could have been in the leagues of hotline miami, but it fell short.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough review for me. I understand that I have under five hours in the game of playtime, but I've almost completed the campaign and I've unlocked most of the abilities at this point. I feel like I have a pretty good handle on the combat system.The first act of the game is great. It focuses on street fighting and feels like a direct homage to beat-em-ups like Streets of Rage and its ilk. It does a good job of introducing you to the mechanics in an intuitive way, even through the constant "INTRODUCING THIS F**KIN' GUY" every time you encounter a slightly different looking enemy shows up. If you like that part of the game, then that's good. It never goes away. Ever. It's seriously in at least every level, sometimes showing up multiple times in a level.The gunplay is introduced in the first act, but it's sporadic and infrequent enough to feel unique and brutal. But this doesn't last. As you progress through the game, guns and gunfights become more frequent and that is very unfortunate because the gun mechanics in the game are not great. The aiming system is serviceable but doesn't feel very good, especially when you're surrounded and trying to focus on enemies that can actively shoot you. It's a shame because the game feels really good when it focuses on the street fighting and the brawls.Boss fights are a mixed bag, but as you progress further in the game they become more trial and error annoyances rather than entertaining challenges. Without spoiling anything, one boss fight is literally a DPS check with an unseen time limit that once you hit it, you just die. You can't do anything about it but die and start over. That's just bad design. I understand what it's an homage to, and that's cute and all, but it's a badly designed boss. There's also a bit of a problem with making the controls more complex than the game really warrants in the heat of a battle. You can learn all the controls and the situations in where they're useful, but the reality is when you're surrounded and fighting off enemies that all require their own specific mechanics to defeat, you're not going to actively be using half of the abilities you get. There's a handful of abilities that are almost required, but for the most part a good number of them you'll generally forget you have them.All that being said, I genuinely enjoy the game and think it's a fun take on the beat-em-up genre with some cool ideas and genuinely funny easter eggs. Clearing out a room of thugs without getting touched feels amazing, pulling off John Wick executions feel great, and punting randomly items from the ground at enemies to throw their aim off before beating the crap out of them never stops being fun. There's a lot of good things the game has going for it, which is why I can recommend it to fans of the genre.Just be aware the game has absolutely manic level design, frustrating enemy mechanics that show up out of nowhere then never show up again, trial-and-error boss fights in the later levels, and wonky gun mechanics. If you keep all that in mind, and don't frustrate easily, then you'll be in for a relatively solid adventure.Edit 09/07/22: I forgot about this. Another thing that I think detracts from the experience is the constant interruptions by the drone companion and the panning cutscenes that show a simple conversation or literally just show a group of enemies. It really breaks the flow for the sake of light expose. I understand they're trying to tell a story, but I feel like it's done just fine with the interrogation scenes and the constant interruptions between (or sometimes during) fights are a bit of an annoyance.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta leave a quick review for this one because its amazing and deserves some praise.Basically if you see "John Wick simulator" or Hotline Miami comparisons it's for good reason. The game is basically Hotline Miami but with brawling mechanics. So it loses the intricate level design of HM (and the one shot aspect), but instead adds a massive array of combat moves at your disposal to dispatch enemies in the most stylish John Wick fashion possible: anything from fancy kung-fu, weapons, counters, parries, finishers, grabs to kicking enviromental stuff at your enemies.I've seen Batman AA comparison but those are stupid, because you have a lot more complexity and freedom at your disposal and the game is not a casual one where you just press 2 buttons for attack and defend like a pleb...I've seen people say that later levels (I'm only about half way through myself) add too many gun/unblockable enemies into the mix and idk if that's true, but from what I've seen, you have plenty of ways to counter everything.One criticism that I do agree with is that a lot of your moves(like grabs or finishers) are TOO SLOW for them to be used in the chaotic mess of combat, especially when surrounded, so I would love a patch to make them a lot faster/usable in some way.But yeah, it's an ABSOLUTE BLAST to play this game. Highly recommended. Hope to see more from the devs because this is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you enjoy the visceral nature of a game such as Hotline Miami but want to have a John Wick experience mixed into it then you should get this game as I'd rank it at a 9/10Midnight Fight Express, a game made by one guy who must've watch a bunch of action films like John Wick or the Raid Redemption and played games like Hotline Miami to have come-up with this idea of a game. As you can see as of this recommendation it paid off in spades and is engrossing with its combat and aesthetic. Let's start off with brass tacks though and break this down.Combat/Gameplay:By default it is recommended to play on a controller as it revolves around high movement and mobility along with crunching your enemies skulls. Mouse and Keyboard is doable but you'd have to constantly move your mouse to have the player character face your opponent, although it makes shooting sections very easy. Controls out of the way the actual gameplay is rock-solid with chaining combos and moves to quickly and effectively beating the various enemies in the forty levels in the game. Complimenting this fast-paced combat is a combo counter and a timer that invariably affects the end result of each level by giving you ranking, each level has an unlockable that can be earned with each success you have in each level goal. This is typically cosmetic customization pieces for the player character but you can also earn characters skins that range from standard enemies to bosses to special characters.Story:The story of Midnight Fight Express is reeking of Action B-Movie and it's pays off with various homages to pieces of media from gaming and film. To put simply though as to remove the love letters to various inspirations this game takes it's a action thriller through and through, enjoyable simple and linear from start to finish.Graphics:The graphics of this game are much like it's story as it is simplistic and akin to a graphic novel but in a 3D interactive space. I'm not sure how to classify it in terms of fidelity but in terms of artistic direction it is astounding on how it goes from urban city to industrial docks/workplace to then more clean and sterile environment so seamlessly and flawlessly. Though it may not have fine details in things with texture-work the levels are made well-enough that going through them on repeat is of no real problem.Cons:A problem Midnight Fight Express really has it arguably it's length but it's designed for subsequent replays to undergo various challenges. An actual compliant however is the balancing of enemies and even balancing of weapons as I notice that enemies more often than not stagger the player character or somehow evade your attacks when your in the midst of a beatdown, weapons such as guns don't have any sign of them being used until you hear a gunshot and enemies that are equipped with twin machete just don't break guard as easily and can shred through your health without giving you a opportunity even on normal difficulty. Lastly some moves don't seem to work such as grapple tackles as you can't attack the enemy you pinned.Extra Notes:- This game revolves around you replaying the game to earn cosmetics pieces/skins, and of course the want to earn a high score/time. You have the option to make a gif of your best (or worst) moments in game after every level and you can take photos in game if you so choose.- The soundtrack of this game is superb as it always hypes you up to fight faster and aggressive, I'd even probably say to go nuts with trying everything at your disposal as you can just go absolutely ham with environmental attacks or weapons that you get off enemies.Final thoughts:Midnight Fight Express is a 9/10 game in my books as it executes its ideas in gameplay very well, though there could be some balance fixes and the like overall it's amazing for a game made by one person. So if you want to see what it feels like to be the Jacket from Hotline Miami without the limitation of one-hit death or want to feel like John Wick being hunted down then go for it and buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good in small bursts, an indie brawler that starts out very finicky and is kind of a nightmare for those with OCD to not have green checkmarks on everything, Midnight Fight Express is perhaps not the next big thing, but it's pretty damn good.There are 40 levels, with each one being about 5 minutes or less, but you'll be spending most of your time trying to achieve S ranks and unlocking the challenges so you can buy/wear new cosmetics for your character (clothing, tattoos, enemy skins). One outstanding thing is the quality of the mo-cap animations considering this is a one-man dev team. The artstyle's good, the soundtrack is bomb, the sound design is good, and the level design is great.I think the addition of voice acting would be great, there are a few hitbox bugs here and there that could be tightened up, and the game looks great  but not so much in picture mode. I wish you could add a beard to your character, but that'd take away from the name Babyface.The story is serviceable but I think it'd hit harder with voice acting, the dialogue boxes that pop up feel like a nuisance without it (just a personal preference). All in all a very solid 4/5 game. [F**k that zombie level and f**k that last boss though] The biggest gripe I have with this game is the tanky enemies you fight that are highly resistant to grapples, counter you without you having a chance to counter straight up telling you to use guns or throw things rather than punching them, or ignoring the punches you throw at them. These enemies are literally a brick wall, until you learn you can cheese them with specific mechanics.

When you get you really good, I recommend trying it without having the button prompts appear; don't worry the game is super lenient if you miss the counter and doesn't put you in some missed or locked animation BS; if you miss, just go right back to punching or maybe grab them.  The telegraph is pretty easy, if the enemy runs up to you give the counter a quick try, if you see them wind up before an attack give the counter a quick try. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best brawlers I've played.  Between dodging, countering, weapons, grappling, finishers, focus, and the two permanent weapons (pistol and rope dart) there are a good number of systems at play.  So much that, by the end of the game, you will probably rely on the handful of moves you prefer.  Animation is silky-smooth and satisfying.Good variety in enemies and settings; whatever kind of mood you're in you can probably find a level that fills that particular action movie itch.There are also a number of what I consider bonuses: style rankings, customization, playground feature, activate and deactivate unlocked skills to control how the game plays.  Story is there; nothing memorable, but I did appreciate having something to drive the movement between setpieces.The balance and pacing gets a bit wonky later in the game; certain fights are unforgiving and actually not much fun, but then the game goes back to being amazing.The gunplay is also not on the level of the melee combat, and the two don't always interface well.Even so, there's no game quite like it.  Closest would probably be Redeemer.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the combat, love the customizations although it might need some more work in there, the story is great, has a good twist to it. The music is absolutely incredible, the levels have a lot of variety, cool weapons, awesome abilities and finishers.But there are problems with this game that need immediate fixing:In level 8, the certain types of enemies such as Ratboy and Crazies (Female) attack too frequently and can kill you in one strike. The grapples don't work often. Only rarely have I been able to pull off a grapple move. Even having the grapple rope didn't do any better. So the grapples need fixing. Moving the character is sensitive, needs to be turned down a notch, the aiming is a bit off. It needs to bee more accurate, the button commands are a bit delayed. Using perks should not disqualify me from completing challenges. Leaderboards and scoreboards are fine but when I'm trying to complete a challenge that requires me to use a perk, it should count as its completed. Some of the challenges can't be completed without the use of perks. Until this problem changes, there's no chance of 100% completing the game. P.S. Next time you make a Final Boss. Don't make him so cheap and unfair just because you want the game to be played longer.So far the game is still playable and worth the enjoyment but those flaws need to be fixed in order to make it a much better game.

_childDocuments_.review: Midnight Fight Express is a fun, fast-paced high-octane brawler with a few notable issues. Let's get the bad out of the way first.1. If you're ever in a situation where there's more than one enemy with a gun, it will be difficult.2. Enemies that dual-wield melee weapons can kill you very, very fast.3. Some foes just don't stun much and are a bit of a chore.4. Grappling enemies, while satisfying and suitably brutal, isn't that useful.5. You're not invincible during finishers.Other than that, the fights are fast with some seriously painful looking animations and just the right amount of brutal impact. (To say, a lot.) You really get the feeling that Babyface, the protagonist, is the kind of guy who can turn somebody's chest inside out with his bare hands, which contributes a lot to the game's appeal. Seriously, some of the finishers had me momentarily ruminating on how thoroughly dead the poor bastard on the receiving end was. It is a level of brutality that can sometimes approach Hotline Miami tier, and I mean that in the best of ways. Speaking of, this game feels inspired by Hotline Miami in a lot of ways - the fast-paced combat, bumpin' electronic soundtrack, and the "be-quick-or-be-dead" style of gameplay, (Which also feels a little Arkham-inspired, with the constant punching and pressing Y ((on an Xbox controller)) to counter) where you can use pretty much anything not nailed down as a weapon. If you can't pick it up and swing it, Babyface will automatically throw (or kick) the object into the nearest enemy's face, which produces a very nice crunch when it kills someone. Speaking of sound, while the game does use plenty of stock grunts and screams, and you will hear sound effects repeat fairly often, there's enough of a variety for it to not be grating, and the sound of Babyface's fist breaking somebody else's, ahm, face, is incredibly satisfying. Some of the guns sound a little weak, but the guns aren't the focus, here. The soundtrack, made by a guy who calls himself Noisecream, is excellent. Perfectly fits the mood.The locales you find yourself in are plenty varied. (Even if some of the environmental hazards can be a bit annoying.) City rooftops, metro stations, sewers, slums, office buildings, subway tunnels, airports, as are the enemies you fight. While they're TECHNICALLY mostly reskins, the roster changes up every five or so levels (often less) so you'll always have fresh faces to break. From your run-of-the-mill thugs, to crazies, sewer-people, cultists, pointdexters, dock workers, smugglers, security, bikers, mobsters, gangbangers, police and S.W.A.T. units, there's always a new type of goon who needs a couple bones broken, and that isn't even an exhaustive list. Plus, there's the occasional vehicle chase to mix things up, and while they don't control perfectly, it's nice to have a change of pace every now and again.Character customization is good. There's a nice variety of clothing to pick from, mainly, hats, shirts, pants, gloves and shoes. You can also get tattoos, which you probably won't see unless you wear short sleeve clothing, but the extra options are very much appreciated.Skills are interesting. You start out fairly weak, but quickly unlock the ability to parry and counter foes, break enemy guards, grab and pummel them, use the environment for finishers, and more. I won't spoil it.The plot is there. It's not a paragon of writing quality and originality, but it's not nonsensical and serves as a good rationalization for doing what you're doing. Basic rundown is: Criminals are gonna try to take over the City of Tomorrow. You're a sleeper agent and ex-criminal named Babyface. You get a drone shoved under your door who activates you, tells you about the whole "criminal takeover" thing and practically shoves you out the door. You then proceed to start kicking ass and don't stop kicking ass until the sun goes up.All in all, while Midnight Fight Express does have its occasional irritations and a few petty issues here and there, it's a great experience I can easily recommend. It's not ALWAYS great, but when it all comes together, and trust me, it all comes together more often than not, it's a fun, fast-paced beat-'em-up in a similar vein to Hotline Miami, and if I'm comparing a game to Hotline Miami in order to compliment said game, it's safe to say it's a pretty damn good game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast to play. However, just know some of the enemy's mechanics could have you grasping at straws to pull off abilities and combos. I feel enemy super armor and uninterruptables should be toned down or the player should be given an ability to regain health or increased defense the higher the combo. Also, guns every now and then versus having 16 enemies with guns coming at once would be better. I still had a great time with the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mostly here because I like Noisecream who made the OST. For the gameplay  it's essentially a harder version of sleeping dogs with alot of new skills added. I say its harder but this is the kind of game that gets easier as you gain skills. For example, there are too many un-blockable moves that happen early on. Only until mission 10 can you unlock the ability to parry weapons which drastically improves the feel and difficulty of the game. I'd hope they change the requirement since you could essentially unlock it at mission 3 in the skill tree if it weren't for the unlock requirement.-sometime later there was re-balancing updates for the better
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Intense Beat em up game, with kickass music and satisfying combat. It has great visuals and smooth gameplay ( Few fps drops on certain levels, but nothing major), and a good level design. Some levels cant get frustating if you are not used to the control scheme, but if do, its a fair and engaging game.Highly recommend this games, however i am biased for it because i just love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible! The soundtrack is great, the combat is just incredible, and the overall design is just amazing. I've only played 14 out of the 40 levels and I already have 3 hours of game play. With additional bonuses and a playground mode. This is a fairly hard game (or maybe I just suck) but, I imagine with the three higher difficulties it'll be to your desire. Also there are some hilarious moments in the game. However, there are some moments (especially in PC) were the movement is close to action/combat and make you do moves you didn't want to. Either than that I can't stress enough how great this game is. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: This game has plenty of weird design choices, it ended up frustrating me more than making me enjoy the game. Enemies become more frustrating to deal with as you progress through the game. Too many enemies with insta-kill attacks, unblockable attacks and gun spamming so you're forced to dodge roll most of the time. Doing cool, flashy finishers/ combos punish you more than rewarding you because enemies can still hit you during these animations. A skill tree ended up being useless because the requirements doesn't make sense in most combat scenarios. There's also a level that forces you to use guns because the enemies OHK you.It's not a beat 'em up game I expected it to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action games I've ever played, a combination of john wick series and jet Li movies. The background music is absolutely amazing.However, it gets little harder to play in the latter half of the game since players need to dodge constantly and its hard to do some perfect combos.  For those who want pure action game experience, the monsters and robots seem a bit of redundant.Hope there will be more DLC in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten the story I can recommend this to anyone who enjoys arkham style combat or Hotline Miami. It's a non stop action beat em up that I feel is the closest to John Wick the game and I am already excited to go back and revisit levels to get the S ranks and challenges done. It's got a great core combat system that carries the game and if you're the kind of person who likes to master a system or mechanics you'll enjoy this game. Also the soundtrack ♥♥♥♥♥♥ slaps.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Does anyone remembers Jackie Chan Stuntmaster on PS1? Yeah, this game is a love child homage of classic beat em ups with current gen twist and the sweet SWEET sounds from Noisecream. Absolutely loving the game, it's fair and tough, makes you replay and learn to get better and rewards you lavishly for a devilish playthrough. So much love and respects to the dev for making such a dope game the likes of which was much much needed!
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was disappointed by the combat and its lack of variety and felt that there were too many enemies that I had limited interaction with, enemies with weapons felt especially annoying due to me being forced to eject myself from close range as soon as they took a swing. However, the more I played the game the better it got as the skill tree slowly allows the player to engage with its incredibly satisfying combat system. Game slaps hard
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie titles of the year. Great combat, banger soundtrack, good story and really fun setpieces with fun enemies, references, and overall high writing quality.The only two cons are that there is no voice acting, and that there is an annoying glitch where if you unlock an achievement your fps plummets into the 10s/20s. It can be fixed easily by going into a loading screen, which usually means you need to restart the level, so it can suck when on a good run.The game had me grinning ear to ear on my first playthrough and has a ton of replay value thanks to its challenges and unlockables. It is an actual steal for just 20€10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with good combat mechanic! It took inspiration from Sleeping Dogs, Hotline Miami, and Batman Arkham Series. I totally recommend playing this game if you're interested in beat 'em up games.- Great Story- Great fight mechanics- Many features like the Playground mode and doing challenges like replaying missions to get the best score which benefits exclusive items you can unlock and when you collect all 10 gold tooth in each missions. - Variety of weapons to use from- Challenging and fun- Learning new fighting skills take practice which would give you time to get used to.- Guns like automatic guns aren't actually automatic since most of them fire semi faster but they deal great amount of damage but I can totally understand why the creator made it like that which would probably be overpowered for the game if the guns had real life stats.That's the only cons I can think of so yeah. Let me know if anyone can find another one in the comment section.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Rating of the game: 10/10+ Fix the achievement bug where the player's framerate drops and they get an achievement in-game but have to restart the level in order to get the achievement via steam which is disappointing cause you're not able to be in your last checkpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: Great addictive beatem up, slick combat even with Keyboard and Mouse make for an enjoyable game be it attacking with weapons, melee or scenery props.Replay levels with new skills to get better scores and a sandbox "playground" to test out weapons/combat on enemies before you try them out in the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately it wasn't fixed since the demo. Unpolished and flawed combat, probably fun if you dont care about combos, score and rating, but if you want a fair experience this game is just not it. You cant delay item throw, so you will accidentally damage yourself with explosives or get hit by an enemy that ran too close to you while you were picking it up. Some enemy attacks can be interrupted by hits while others cant and there's no visible difference in it, at least on realistic difficulty. I can't just drop a combo and instantly throw my weapon, sometimes character just continues to punch enemies. On realistic difficulty it says "enemies will constantly attack you" or something like that. So why these dudes sometimes just stand in front of me for five seconds without doing anything when all I want is to parry them? Perfect block is very easy to do but the timings are weird, you have to block as soon as attack animation starts instead of doing it right before the attack hits me like in other games. Your combo meter can ran out because enemy is knocked on ground and you cant hit him until wake up animation is finished, otherwise it will just knock him out again. And those are just the problems from the first levels.I hope this would be fixed in the future updates. Maybe I'll try it again sometime and change my opinion, this could be great game. Animations are cool, skill tree change your playstyle dramatically and guns feel nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot like My Friend Pedro, except in this one, you punch more instead of shoot guns, also this is in isometric view. Like that game, your protagonist has amnesia, and your talking to a drone instead of a floating banana. Both soundtrack was made by the same person. Both games also have this feature where you can save some awesome moves you did in game, in a form of a GIF.It's best enjoyed in small bursts, rather than powering thru the whole of it. It's a fun brawler, regardless of what you think about the story, or lack of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: We didn't get the last martial arts game. Sadly that went to Epic exclusivity (although I forgot the name). Well, luckily we got this blessing right here. You want brutal combat while head banging to a wild "go hard" soundtrack?? Look no further. Although to be fair I died a few times. Head banging and fighting don't mix. But mileage can vary!Tons of items to unlock, a healthy chuck of levels, easy restarts if you need. Multiple layers of difficulty that can be fine tuned to your liking. Even a training area with as little as one to as high as endless waves of enemies. They can spawn with nothing or all sorts of weapons. So if you need that time to get yourself on point, you got it. This game truly has a lot to offer. I say try it out if you like John Wick (Did I just use a movie as a purchase point for a game? YUP!). Wheres the suit in the unlocks? I truly wouldn't be surprised to find one, or see it added (hint hint devs). But man this game can get you jacked. My veins are throbbing and all I did was squeeze my controller while a beat the ever living ish outta people! Two hours is PLENTY time to know. Now, I have to add a negative. Hate to do it, but I have to. I saw one other review call this out and I experienced it too. If you are using a controller, something feels off about the controls. It did all actions but felt off. Not instant. Not so slow it ruins it, but slow enough to cause some hiccups. Granted I started working around that, but still, I hope to see it addressed. Also even if you alter your button layout, the game will still treat the buttons as they were. I altered dodge roll to B. This is an issue because it is also mapped to continue. So every time I move along dialogue, I dodge. Kind of annoying, not gonna lie. Finally! Red attacks. You know the ones. Cannot parry, have to dodge attacks. I usually do not have an issue with them, but in this game, way too frequent when facing certain enemy types. Killing the flow of the fighting. I dodge, hit once, have to dodge again, hit once, have to dodge again, and dodge again to finally dodging again. I haven't beaten the game or unlocked all the moves. Maybe something down the line will give me an edge with those, but so far, a whole lotta rollin.  But all in all I am having a blast! I have a big a back log right now but I will be throwing this on soon! Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best games I have played in a long time. Its like Hotline Miami on steroids. The story is alright, but due to the incredible gameplay, you can look past it. First of all, I want to mention this game can get pretty difficult with bosses and environmental hazards. So as long as you are up for the challenge I think you should buy it. It has high replayability with 40 levels and to master and get rewards, you have to play each one at least 3 to 4 times. Not only that but it has a playground mode where you can spawn enemies and weapons and fight as long as you want. The combat is incredible, with environmental finishers, grappling, a large variety of melee weapons and firearms. The animations are all amazing aswell. I think the only thing that could be added to improve the game is maybe some mod support with custom maps as the playground map is always this debug map. Overall though a very great game 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Midnight Fight Express

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put Midnight Fight Express places you in the role of a sleeper agent where the city you reside is in trouble due to various gangs hurting the innocents, it is YOUR job to encounter those gangs along with your drone and teach those bullies a lesson using your fists or literally anything at your disposal in the game world such as a knives, chairs, trashcan, baton, guns and so on. I have only played a couple levels so far but man this game is going to be fun to play as the graphics and music are great and help get that blood pumping. Yes blood and gore can be disabled if it bothers you but in this game it is awesome and the take downs are well done.After you finish a level you can compare your rating score and time with other players on the leader board and then you can further customize your character and assign skill points.  Finally I have been playing Midnight Fight Express on my PC using a Keyboard & Mouse without any problems so not using a game controller and having zero issues.

detailed_description: STORY OF SEASONS: Pioneers of Olive Town + Expansion Pass Set This set includes the STORY OF SEASONS: Pioneers of Olive Town game and its Expansion Pass featuring 14 sets of DLC. This expansive bundle will enhance your life on the farm even further with new characters, costumes, and more! ◆ Additional Outfits • Pete and Claire's Overalls • Yuto and Naomi's Hoodies • Henry and Holly's Western Attire • Animal Attire (Protagonists) • Animal Attire (Marriage Candidates) • School Uniforms (Protagonists) • School Uniforms (Marriage Candidates) • Yukata Set (Protagonists) • Yukata Set (Marriage Candidates) ◆ Sub-scenarios • Olive Town Mystery Files • The Legendary Sprite Dance ◆ Marriage Candidate Expansion Packs • Windswept Falls Expansion Pack • Terracotta Oasis Expansion Pack • Twilight Isle Expansion Pack * The protagonist outfits will become available once you have completed the town development request to build the salon. You may then commission the outfits from Karina. * All protagonist outfits can be worn regardless of gender chosen. * To change the marriage candidates' outfits, select 'Downloadable Content' from the title screen, then enable the outfits in the 'Apply Downloadable Content' menu. * Marriage candidate outfit sets are not available for marriage candidates added in the Expansion Packs. * The sub-scenarios are small sets of quests, events, and outfits that are separate from the main game's scenario. * Marriage Candidate Expansion Packs are based on past titles in the STORY OF SEASONS series, and include a new area, 2 townsfolk, and 2 marriage candidates each. About the Game Build Your Farm From the Ground Up! Welcome to Olive Town, a peaceful community established by your trailblazing grandfather and his friends. Now that you've taken over his farm, it's your job to carry on his legacy. Plant crops, raise animals, build relationships, and get to know the residents of your new home in this brand-new entry in the STORY OF SEASONS series! Cultivate Your Farm, Cultivate Your Town Tame the wilderness and build your farm from the ground up! Gather and process materials to fulfill requests and improve Olive Town's infrastructure, upgrade tools, or commission new outfits and accessories. A Farm of Endless Possibilities Clear the land, repair old facilities, and place new ones wherever you see fit. Level up your farming skills and craft a variety of decorations and facilities, from fences and automatic feeders for livestock to sprinklers for crops! New Adventures Off the Beaten Path Finding Earth Sprites while exploring your farmland may lead you to mysterious, fantastical lands such as gardens where the seasons never change, an island in the sky, or even the inside of a volcano! There's Always Something Going on in Olive Town! Participate in local festivals and watch the town come to life! Get to know your neighbors better with over 200 unique events, and you may even find love with a special someone!

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate doing this, because I'm a huge SoS fan, but ultimately, I'm not going to recommend this game, even after the 1.1 patch.  Note:  A lot of my time playing this game was the Switch version.  While the Switch version had massive FPS issues, this version does not, I rarely had FPS drops, but there was a lot of pop ins, especially in Stonebreaker.  Get this version if you really want this game, runs smoother.Here's some positives for this game:Animals - This is probably the best version of taking care of the animals of any SoS game.  Instead of feeling like a chore and needing a spreadsheet, you click on the animal, wash it if needed, get it's products, and you're on your way.  Done.  Sadly, the breeding system from the Mineral town remake rears it's head, but it's not nearly as bad, as it takes only about a week for the animal to give birth and you can still get their products during pregnancy.Character customization - Really well done here.  There's only a few hair styles that were recently added for end game, but everything is there at the beginning and you can change up later in game.Farming - It's about on the same level as any SoS season game.  Sprinklers make your watering can useless way too early though.  No more fertilizing crops, what you get is what you get, throw the crops into a seed maker, and boom, you get your high quality crops.Decorating your farm ala SoS - Meaning that you can hoe the ground wherever you want to plant crops.  You can make a variety of different pieces of furniture for both inside and outside and decorate your 3 farm areas.Events - There are a lot of events with not just your bachelors/bachelorettes, but all the townsfolk. Returning characters - It was nice to see previous bachelors/bachelorettes, and all their events are well written.Skill levels - Ala Rune Factory.  I really liked this, and liked that when you leveled, you'd get more items to craft or unlock new moves or reciples.  Or you can chop wood/mine better (Upgrading your tools will do that too, but leveling your skills definitely makes it easier as well).Sprites - I like the sprite system a lot.  You can unload the sprites into the bigger ones and get items based on which one you want to focus on.  I also like how you can unlock the 'special areas', it makes me want to go out and just collect them.Sigh, and now the bad:Boring Olive Town bachelors/bachelorettes - I think this is the first SoS game where I had no interest in any of the choices given to me, there has usually always been ONE bachelor that I've ended up liking.  None of the bachelors were interesting and most of them came off as really boring and shallow, which even with the patches, didn't really improve the characters all that much (I'm basing this off of dating all the bachelors and marrying Daemon).  A big problem is the heart events cut off really suddenly.  You'll be talking to one of them, and the scene just ends.  Save for a couple of scenes, the heart events with a majority of bachelors didn't feel romantic at all.  The only Olive town bachelor that had okay done romantic scenes for the MC was Jack, and I've seen all the male events, including the DLC characters.  The DLC bachelor events don't have this problem (They don't cut off suddenly, and all three bachelors seemed have romantic feelings for the MC), which I'm assuming before the DLC came out, they fixed up the events for them due to backlash.  But the problem is....DLC characters not implemented well - I was very disappointed overall with the DLC characters.  I was really excited for them after none of the Olive town bachelors clicked, and Raegar and Ludus were bachelors I married in their respective games.   None of the DLC characters interact with the Olive Town crew, they don't go to the town, they don't attend festivals unless you are MARRIED to them (If you're dating them, it won't work, tested this with Ludus).  And the story of how they ended up there was...  meh.  It's even more disappointing, because in one of Ludus' event, he and the MC go to Olive Town.Makers - There's too much of a reliance on Makers.  In past SoS games, they had makers, but it wasn't to this extreme, and it takes up a ton of space on your farm, and it looks ugly.  Why couldn't they do it like in SoS on the 3DS where the makers are put into individual buildings?  Even though you can make up to 10 items now, it's still not enough, especially when you need 200+ bars to make a large maker.  Not to mention, having to put up a ton of boxes to house all these items....Pail and puddles - This was a interesting idea but overall just adds clutter.Lack of calendar events - What reason was there to get rid of the crop/animal festivals?  This has always been a staple of the SoS games, I cannot fathom why they took this out.  Save for completing Lovett's requests, there is no reason to breed animals or get your crops any higher than 6 (The max level you can get after field upgrades).  The events we get are boring and shallow, there's a romantic festival and a mini game festival for each month, that's it, no valentine's, no new year's, no cooking.  Heck, Mineral Town has more events than this game!'Harvest Goddess' does nothing - A spoiler, but this game's Harvest Goddess is a waste, her design is wonderful, but she is absolutely wasted.Lack of dresses - Seriously, why are the majority of clothes pants???  There were a ton of outfits even in A New Beginning, from both pants and dresses.  Heck, even the recent new outfits are freaking pants!  And there were a ton of outfits in Trio.  There are a few that I like, but there's not much variety.Story is way too easy to complete - It is way too easy to complete the main story quest.  On my first try blind, I completed it in Winter 1.  On other playthroughs, I could get it done as early as Fall 1.No reason for money - I haven't done the recent end game content, but money is way too easy to obtain and there's nothing to really spend it on unless you have bad RNG with the rare wood and ore, and even then, at level 9, you've unlocked the area where you can farm for them.Spawnrate on farm is too high - I don't know why they didn't give us an option to turn the spawnrate off on your farm, especially when it comes to end game.  It makes customizing your farm a chore, and there are some squares where you cannot put items on, but something will spawn there.  So that one spot will always spawn ugly grass or a puddle or tree.Museum - Absolutely pointless and not done well, you can't move fish/items once you place them either (Heck, you can't even see the fish beyond a shadow of it).  Keep this to Animal Crossing, it's implemented way better.Soulless Marriage and no pregnancy event - Did they do this to keep this game E?  Marriage is a contract, you sign a contract and that's it, no hug, no kiss, no nothing.  It's the most unromantic marriage I've ever seen in any SoS/Rune Factory game.  And there's no pregnancy event, even for straight couples.  They really should take a hint of how Rune Factory 5 is handling both straight and gay marriage.Quanity over Quality - Yes, there's a lot of events, but what's the point if they all are short or don't add much to the characters?  I'd rather have less events, but they add to the character and mean something than 100 small events that cut off suddenly.Horse is pointless - I get my motocycle before I can even get the mats to restore the stable.  Bad customization of your house - They should've done this like they did with SoS.  You can put furniture in your house, but it's very limited, and you can't put down rugs until the 4th upgrade, because there is no room otherwise.  Why even have this feature if you can only customize certain parts of your home?All in all, even with the patches, this game feels very soulless and very unfinished.  Get the 3DS games or stick with stardew valley, at least SDV can be modded, or get FoMT remake

_childDocuments_.review: So I do recommend this game, but with a bit of an asterisk because there were some weird game design decisions that went into this.Off the bat I'll say if you enjoy farming rpgs then this'll be up your alley. It doesn't do anything too unique but the gameplay loop is pretty satisfying, so I think if you want something to scratch your farming game itch, this is it. However, I do think we've all been spoiled by Stardew Valley so you may leave yourself wanting when interacting with the characters and advancing the game.One thing I like is the skill system and how huge your farm is. You can unlock more areas of your farm, which in turn unlock more things to do, more mechanics, and more critters. You unlock new buildings by repairing the ones on your farm, and you unlock new animals by taming ones you find. Every first animal you get is free, and you can buy more afterwards or apply a breeding kit when your ranching level is high enough.There are little forest sprites that unlock mini-games and reward you with various items in-game by progressing and setting free more of their kind. I enjoy this kind of progression and "beating" the game also allows them to help you out more, cutting out some of the game's grind so you can focus on what you want to focus on.Relationships and characters are my favorite part of these types of games, so the lack of dialogue variety and interaction was definitely disappointing for me. The characters can be entertaining and their cutscenes are fun, but they don't have that much depth. I went for Iori, who is polite and sweet, but his "gimmick" is that he's from overseas so 90% of his dialogue is about that. The characters don't go through many noteworthy arcs, but I'll at least say I enjoy the variety of personalities here and that you feel like a part of the town rather than dictating what happens (e.g. there are some dating couples in the game, plenty of parents and family friends, everyone has people they like to hang out with)The biggest downside to this game to me is unfortunately a big mechanic: the machines. I'm no stranger to processing machines especially in Story of Seasons games, but the fact that you can only place them on your farm and there is no dedicated building for them takes a lot out. The grind is extremely real when it comes to the machines, and they slow down the game and don't look very good on your farm. I would have fewer complaints if there was a shed.Similarly, you can't place chests in your house, and decoration areas are only in specific parts and extremely limited. There's not much joy to be had in decorating and it's one of the weakest parts of the game (coming from someone who loves customization).Overall, I think this is a pretty solid game overall and I've enjoyed the time I've played it. I got my money's worth and there's still a lot I can do in the game, though I wish more time was put into giving the characters (especially the bachelor/ettes) more development, and I wish the game was a bit more organization friendly.p.s. You should turn on the option that zooms in on the characters' faces since otherwise it's pretty hard to see them

_childDocuments_.review: As much as it pains me, this is probably the first Story of Seasons title that I have to honestly say I cannot recommend.There are some cute things about it, and some of the heart of the series is there, buried way way down in there, but honestly this feels like Story of Seasons is trying too hard to take My Time at Portia elements and falling so flat on it's face that it tumbles right over a cliff.First and foremost the balancing in the game is atrocious. Day 2 of Winter Year 1 and I had already beat the town development "main" story. Winter 23 of Year 1 and I was married to the bachelor of my choice. The only major story milestone left for me is to have the kid (which I have read ahead is an adoption thing regardless of hetero marriage status or not and that moderately irks me). After that it's just little completionism, which at the rate I smashed through them in year 1 I don't expect will take longer than the last Year 3 achievement.Compare this to the previous SoS game (which wasn't a remake), Trio of Towns where I was well into year 2 or 3 before I beat the main story, let alone got married.My second biggest complaint is everything is just kind of pointless. There are no harvest or animal festivals (and seriously, what kind of SoS or HM game DOESN'T at least have a harvest festival). Crops and Aniimals exist solely as money farming, there is no other reward for putting any effort into them other than a mild to moderate boost to the value of the product. You feel no attachment to the livestock or even your pets because the are just literal cash cows for you. Pets serve no purpose other than to be cute, you don't even really need one for the in game pet festival because you can rent a pet and still win 1st place.The Makers system is insanely annoying. There are just too many of them, and there's little to no variety in the product they make. You would think if you put milk, goat milk, or buffalo milk into the cheese maker you would get cheese, goat cheese, or buffalo cheese respectively, but no. You just get cheese, no variety to it at all which is a MAJOR downgrade from Trio of Towns. Ultimately there are more maker devices to make less products that previous titles did with fewer Makers.Another major nitpick I had was you can't be a pretty girl. Seriously. The female body type is just a boy's body type with a slightly more feminine posture. Even in the obviously female clothing the female body is boxy and flat as a washboard. It isn't until after you get married and unlock the wedding dress that you can actually have a female body shape like almost EVERY OTHER FEMALE NPC IN THE GAME. Care to tell me why the female body shape clearly exists but the Player Character is somehow denied a feminine body until after you wed and save up the ludicrious amount of money to afford the wedding dress for your closet? And I haven't even touched on the fact that there are no additional hairstyles that you unlock throughout the game (again, like previous titles). The long hairstyles are massively underwhelming and most have wonky physics because they are just a flat plane of hair, so all through the game I kept hoping I would unlock new ones as I progressed but it never happened.The villagers and the village itself all feels pretty flat and lifeless. The characters seem to have little to no personality outside of their relationship building cutscenes. Heck, I didn't even remember all of the villagers' names until 20 or so hours in, they're so forgetable. The removal of the 2d art for talking to people was also a MAJOR mistake on the developers part. Story of Seasons has always had beautiful and very charming illustrated artwork, and this is even present in the game in the bios of villagers in the game menu, but they just decided to take that aspect out for some reason, and it massively hurts the charm of the game and the feeling of appeal that the npcs have. Even the "chat camera" that they have in the game that zooms in when talking doesn't come close to comparing to the 2d artwork of previous titles.Basic quality of life features feel virtually nonexistent. There is no item sorting AT ALL, and the game encourages you to hoard resources, so this gets to be a massively un-fun time sink very quickly. There's no customization to the actual design of your house or farm features (again, like Trio of Towns....I'm going to reference this one a lot because frankly I felt it to be the best title in the Story of Seasons lineup to date). While the tool bag feature is nice, actually pulling tools out of the tool bag is cumbersome and gets to be a pain after a couple of months in game.Over all, everything about this game feels like a dumbed down, inferior version of previous Story of Seasons titles (not counting Friends of Mineral Town, as that is a remake of a very very old title and can't be held to recent game standards). They abandoned what they are, a farming game, in the pursuit of I am not even sure what. I can only hope that with the next title they return to their roots, until then I'll finish up with the milestones of this title and return to my (currently) Year 6 game of Trio of Towns.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was Thanos’s life before he got his head chopped off. I went into PoOT with a lot of reservations, but it might actually be one my favorite Harvest Moon games yet. I feel like there are a bunch of things to do, but everything can be done at your own pace so you don’t feel rushed nor do you feel held back. It has some bugs and issues, but not anything worse than any other HM game.Honestly, it’s a decent game. Not the best in the series, but still fun. The patches have addressed a lot of issues on release. If you’re remotely interested, just get it. Probably on sale. The expansion pass is not the best, but the marriage candidates from the dlc have some of my favorite interactions in the game.Despite it’s flaws I’ve really enjoyed it. My wife has been loving it too and we’re both gonna save money to buy a copy for her boyfriend seeing as the price is not so bad on sale.And in my opinion the only reason some people say it’s disappointing is because people have unrealistic expectations and keep on comparing it to the previous tittles and Stardew Valley. _childDocuments_.review: If you've played any farming sim you already have a basic idea if you'll like this game. However, as much as I was a die-hard SoS/HM loyalist for basically inventing the genre - Stardew Valley ultimately really perfected a lot of it - that makes going back to these games a bit harder. I am a much bigger fan of SoS graphic style over SDV so i do lean towards the 3D games more often. Things about PoOT that I enjoy: -Graphics-the time loop feels pretty good, it doesnt move too fast or slow. -the fact that your basic tools have a separate bag so you can gain a few extra bag spaces early on when you fill up fast. -Character customization is NOT locked to gender - and you can marry any eligible candidate -Most upgrades are available immediately upon purchase so you dont have to wait -Foraging has a secondary benefit of increasing the seed options in the general store (I think this is a really cool way of increasing their stock) -you find and tame animals in the wild - which leads to you being able to purchase them from the animal shop later. Though in the early game the taming consists of just pressing a button once, the concept is cool. -Multiple Mines which makes finding specific ores easier AND an improvement from earlier SoS titles (specifically the SoS not XSeeds HM titles) where they had mining 'nodes' this game has an actual mine to explore which was something i really missed on the 3DS titles. - there are a ton of acheviements and ranks in game to achieve which is really fun for me - cooking lets you pull directly from the fridge which is so handyThings I dislike: - the Egg Hunt festival is a cut-scene. Esp after HM64 and SDV i loved hunting eggs around town and it was really disappoining that it was a cutscene AND i couldnt choose to not play with the town children in my first year (you have the option to play with other villagers but i did not have any friendships very high so i didnt try so i know you CAN play with other villagers but I wish i could have told the kids no as well) - your farm debris grows back almost crippling fast. and while you NEED the resources because you can't plant wood trees yourself, it is difficult to make significant clearing progress when it all just grows back so fast. I suspect this gets worse as your farm grows as well. - a lack of 'mixed seeds' and tree seeds. I loved how SDV gave you mixed season seeds from random foraging, and the tree seeds allow you to make a tree forest as you see fit. both things this game lacks. - not being able to hold a button on the controller to perform multiple hits with tools. ONce you start to upgrade and have hte Charge Hits I can see why this is not an option but early game its tedious to mash B over and over - if you play with a controller I find it weird that 'B' is used as the accept key most often, but not all the time so i am frequently hitting A, and accidentally trying to clear placed items on my farm, and then hitting B when i actually need to hit A and closing menus. I BELIEVE this can be changed but it's a bizarre initial set-up - while I do like that you can customize the outside of your farm - it is also fairly limited with where things can go, and the grind system everything locks into is not .... as aesthetically pleasing as i'd like. AND you can't place makers on top of paths which is making my farm look a bit of a weird way (and my understanding is i can't place my makers inside of any kind of shed/building so i'm stuck with them being outside)  and this is a downgrade from SoS on the 3DS where you had buildings and a sort of infinite ability to craft in them. (though most makers can do about 10 at a time so its not bad at all)- despite the cooking getting it right - you cant craft anything else from storage. all makers and crafting menus only work with your inventory - the crafting screen does not show you which items are 'new' which can be confusing when you level up and dont know what you just got (sometimes you get a pop up about it but not always) - you can't organize your chests automatically. if you want them to look any kind of way you need to do it manually which i loathe. Even though my dislikes list may be longer - it is a solid game to buy on Sale (i dont think it is worth full price if you're a fan of SDV over SoS in general) if you've ONLY played SoS games than I'd agree it is probably one of hte best games in teh series (though I am partial to Tree of Tranquility as being one of hte best XSeed/Marvelous titles even if graphically i dont like it as much as the Chibi styles of modern SoS games) ultimately its a solid game, runs well on PC and has a lot to offer - but I do think its more worth buying on Sale than Full Price. Additionally - there is a new(remake) coming soon if you're on the fence that game is likely to be better as it is a much loved game from the past.

_childDocuments_.review: You're probably here because of Stardew Valley (if you aren't, go buy Stardew Valley). Yes, I'm well aware that Stardew (SV) was a Harvest Moon clone, and therefore a Story of Seasons clone, but it's just better.If you are here because you've already played SV, and you're looking for another game that will fill the void, Pioneers of Olive Town (PoOT) does the job. In fact, there are things that make it better, including visual updates and improved tools that allow you to manage a large farm without spending half your day pulling up crops or managing animals, and unlockable farm zones so you don't have to dedicate your whole day to an equivalent of the "mine grind" that exists in SV. There is also less stress and more options to farm key materials without having to deal with any real combat. And you can grow crops in winter!But there are plenty of things that just aren't as good, including slightly more limited romance options, frame-rate issues during varied weather or on larger farms, the constant and frequently overbearing farm clean-up (you'll see what I mean), and most importantly a much steeper price tag.If you haven't played SV, go play it. If you're looking for another game like Stardew and haven't played My Time at Portia (MTaP), go get that. If you have already exhausted both, and you're looking for a visually more pleasing game than SV that plays somewhere between SV and MTaP, PoOT works well, as long as you're willing to throw more money at it. Just don't expect any surprises. And once your farm is big enough and you start unlocking more of the latter content, do yourself a favor and save your game beyond the auto-save, because you may get black-screened loading between zones and it's almost a deal-breaker if you've already done a lot that day.So do I recommend PoOT? Sure, if you've already played SV and MTaP and you're looking for more (because this genre can be quite addicting). You will literally be buying a game that lands somewhere between the other two, with slightly less heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Story of Seasons game made it to Steam (hurray!) == Pros ==++Large area of farm to utilize/place buildings.++Can own both a dog and a cat.++Decent amount of townspeople to interact with.++Unlocking skill upgrade by leveling up things such as mining, cooking, and fishing.++Museum where you can donate treasure, fish, and photos of animals.++Money is easy to come by, even on the normal difficulty setting.++Animals are practically given to the player for free by taming them in the wild, allowing you to have a cow, alpaca, sheep, and horse at no cost.++Sections of the farm can be unlocked by collecting the required materials, or paying a flat fee.++Many different items to collect.== Cons ==--House decorating is severely lacking and borderline nonexistent. You have a very small amount of space to work with, despite having a large interior.--So. Many. Damn. Makers. Seriously? There's at least 10 different makers in the game, all of which takes many in-game hours to process goods and it's not worth the effort, despite almost all recipes relying on it.--Townsfolk have generic personalities, and almost all of them are boring or overly personified. --Crafted cooking dishes sell for LESS then the raw materials to make them.--Trees, stones, puddles, and grass respawn at an astronomically fast rate - so fast it is almost impossible to have a completely clean farm unless you spend the entire day farming and place objects or plant things in every possible square.--Some heart events and cutscenes end abruptly, or don't even feature your character's participation at all.--Festivals and events are so bad, it's not even entertaining. It just feels like a waste of the day, as some of the events feature a low budget cutscene, or a generic, boring minigame. There's only 8 events in the game - 2 for each season.--Once you place an object in the museum, you cannot rearrange it.--One of the best things about the series is having several new people move into the town after certain requirements are meant to spice up gameplay. Pioneers of Olive Town has a whopping...1 person move in throughout the course of the game (two, if you marry a certain character, and not including DLC).If you're looking for something that plays similar to the old Harvest Moon games (A Wonderful Life, Magical Melody, Save the Homeland, 64, Friends of Mineral Town) then keep looking, because this Story of Seasons entry is pretty disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome in new installment of Story of Seasons Franchise (Before it was called Harvest Moon until Natsume and Marvelous made decision to split up, while Marvelous os the original developer studio based in Japan and Natsume was ONLY publisher for USA and Nintendo was Publisher for EU) in this title you focus on ,,pioneering'' in practice that means you get your farm after Grandpa's death (ofc as usually you do...except the last games on 3DS that intro was different) and your ,,Motorcycle'' is broken. You stop before Olive Town where Mayor stops you and wants to help to repair your Motorcycle. You decide to renovate your old farm with everything what is needed to. But opsie! Whole Olive Town is in cycle of refusing new Tourists and you are the one who will help bring the beauty of Olive Town! The ,,Pioneers'' means that you renovate your farm in way of Pioneer. So you instead of ,,build'' new barn you renovate it. As all ,,facitilities'' you do renovate when you unlock another place on your farm by the time being. There is coming the choosing ,,difficulty'' which you choose ,,Seddling'' which is for new players or for players like me who prefers ,,to relax and not feel to grind nosense numbers like in Stardew'' . I must admit, the ,,easy'' mode feels very easy for Story of Seasons title. I was used to very big grinding always. So i was suprised how this was taken this time. I would not say it's a bad thing but you will finish main story of Olive Town pretty quickly, it's possible in two seasons, even earlier. Which is bit ... idk how to feel about that. Let's go back to farm organization, in this title devs removed tools for livestock (Idk why?) so you only click on Cow, milk her with your hands and pet her. That's same with all animals which is bit weird. Cuz we needed in previous titles specific tools and so on. Second thing are ... yes MAKERS! That decision was the worst for the game. I don't understand the needs from developer's studio why the hell we need maker for every items separated. For example if you want make Yoghurt, you need to craft and place on your farm specific Maker and then when you need specific maker for every time you want to make. You have like 50x makers on your farm and you run out of the space very quickly. I would say, if they made special building for these makers, it would have been better idea. (I feel like Marvelous did not have enough time to solve the makers idea and were pushed to leave it at this state sadly. ) The characters in Olive Town feels very nice after the updates in 2021. The camera option which was added later after launch on Nintendo Switch was game changer (So you don't need the character portraits, as half of fanbase complain about it...i don't see the need of it, when they are fully 3D rendered and modeled with emotions tbh) . So i would say 8/10 for characters, some feels less funny than others and vice versa. It's not the strongest title with story but still it does satisfy for Story of Seasons standards. There were worse titles with characters, if you played previous installments of course. Let's look on graphic side of the game, i feel like some places does deserve more details such as trees or flowers to be surrounded etc. Still don't understand the locked place where you enter Olive Town (thought there would be place in endgame for our Farm as extension of kind of some place for some story but looks like it was scrapped). The expansion pass....idk how to feel about it still. I like they did bring back characters from previous games. But makes me sad that you need to travel to islands to visit them. They don't interact with Olive Town in any way. Which is bit bad decision. I though we would get visitors from the Islands and some new foraging items on the Islands and mayhap some more interaction so you would feel more motivated to visit it more often. I feel like it's okay expansions but could have been done much much better. + Cute Town+ Soundtrack is very nice to listen to, very relaxing. Specially Summer and Winter season music+Character customization + Diversity (you can marry same gender as your character's gender) + Cute graphics + Donating things to Museum+ Request Board + Characters are funny, actually- Lack of decorating place in your house- Can be bit repetive at times, if you don't know what you are doing or not have goals- Main story feels short compare to previous titles- Some textures are not fully HD on PC. (Rushed port?)  Im giving decent 8/10. Why? Because if you did read about the development of this title, then you would now that the game did suffer in organization and had chaos in behind of screen. Basically main Producer did leave Marvelous and started studio Hakama and revived Rune Factory Franchise and was left to new studio. And pretty much you can see the rush and so on. I feel like they will learn from this lesson and deliver us in future again the nice and good quality SoS games. They need some time. (Yes i defend them....but if they did not care, they would not even patch the game with feww content updates....)) So overall the game has it's decent issues but still it does deliver the classic Story of Seasons gameplay filled with nice cute cutscenes and decent soundtrack. If you are new to Franchise, buy it on sale. If you are veteran and still deciding to buy it or not. Give it try or wait for discount as well. I hope you will enjoy your time in Olive Town! ♥

_childDocuments_.review: Years ago, I have played "Harvest Moon Friends of Mineral Town" (GBA), "HM Island of Happiness" (NDS) and "HM Sunshine Islands" (NDS), so I had high hopes for this one.Compared to those two games, the town seems lifeless, no meaningful conversations with the NPCs - a dead like town and  the lacking personality of the townspeople is disappointing. The heart events mostly have a comedic purpose and lack depth.The game also lacks difficulty, you already own the brush for your livestock, same for the milking machine and trimmer. Neither can they get sick or die. Cooking recipes are already unlocked and show the needed ingredients. No more waiting until someone upgraded your house or tools - no more planning ahead. This game feels like a combination of "My Time at Portia" and "Stardew Valley". - Why do we need so many Makers? Mayonnaise or Butter Makers could fit perfectly in barns or coops (by default in the games I mentioned before, but not possible here). Also, they worked at an instant - no waiting time until something got processed.- Wherever I wanted to relocate a building I wasn't allowed to fit it on a wall, but trees and stones seem to be able to re-spawn there just fine. How the farm can be decorated, however, offers a lot of options.- There are only 2 town events each season, which also lack creativity. Where did the animal events disappear to?- Appraising at the museum takes ages, please do not make me collect stuff for a museum, especially when the museum doesn't look appealing at all.- Why isn't it possible to place a chest/storage box in my house? The decoration space in there is very limited.- The 3 extra islands (Expansion Pass) offer 4 new NPCs each (2 of them are new marriage candidates), which aren't visiting your town at all.Honestly, there is no need for Quests. Bring back rival marriages and collectables (mussels, specific grass, etc) on the town's beach or woods. Even the harvesting goddess isn't present anymore.Overall I wouldn't recommend the game if you are used to the older games, even for nostalgia. It just doesn't cut it. The port, however, is very good. (Great controller support!) The gameplay (how to use tools, interact on your farm) is smooth and loading times are low. Which is also the only thing that keeps me playing.

I'm glad to see that they brought back the characters from the old games, but the problem is if you're married to the DLC characters. They will be excluded from the town events. You won't see your spouse or any other characters in there. Like they're locked in their islands. You also can't do anything in the islands.
