_childDocuments_.review: So look, I love the Nintendo Switch. It's a great little device despite its hardware shortcomings. I'm currently playing The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD on the thing, and it plays at 60fps and feels fantastic.But like many 3rd party titles, Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town plays horribly on the Switch. From the moment you boot it up it struggles to maintain 30fps, and the more you build up your farm, the worse the game buckles under its own weight. Walking through town was a frame pacing nightmare at launch (they've patched it up so its not quite so bad now, but it's still an issue). It feels just terrible to play. I bought the Special Edition for the Switch -- the one that comes with the town map and the plushie -- and I was utterly disappointed with the game itself due to the terrible performance.And here we suddenly get a stealth release of the game for PC, and after playing it for nearly 3 hours I can't help but feel like the Switch version shouldn't even exist. The PC port runs at a solid 60fps (and can even be set to play at 120fps, where I assume it also performs fine, I couldn't test it because my TV only does 60hz). I've unlocked and run around the second section of the farm, and there are no frame drops thus far. There's also zero frame pacing issues when walking around town.I've seen other people complain about the game crashing, but so far I've had no issues with that either, if I do I'll update this review.The gameplay mechanics themselves take the classic Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons gameplay and begins to augment it with the sort of stuff that games like Stardew Valley have brought to the genre. There's a lot more in the way of crafting and using machines to create new items/consumables, but the basic loop is what you'd expect from a game in this genre.The inclusion of the new chat camera is really nice, particularly since they dropped townsfolk portraits from this game (a major criticism at time of release), although it doesn't always work. If you're standing too close to a wall or any other sort of geometry, the chat camera fails to initiate. Hopefully they'll patch that over time.If you like the Story of Seasons franchise, skip the Switch version and pick up the Steam version. If you simply must play it on a handheld device whilst laying in your bed, well, the Steam Deck is coming soon, isn't it?

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with story of seasons (or Harvest Moon) and Rune factory. I loved them. So I was really happy finally having enough time to play PoOT. I read the reviews beforehand and knew I couldn't be too euphoric going into it. So I prepared myself for an okay game with some questionable mechanics. However, though I desperately tried to like the game, not even the blur of nostalgia could save it for me.Here is why:The farm has a very strange layout. It consists of three islands that are round and each has a section of beach. This design makes it incredibly difficult to divide areas sensibly; strange gaps or alleys remain because stables or other buildings always have to be at a distance from the edges of the island.The farm becomes littered incredibly quickly. I'm fine with new rocks/grass/trees etc. spawning, but the sheer amount popping up on the islands every day is outrageous. You never have the good feeling of having cleaned up your farm. Especially because ponds that have been cleaned simply become dirty again.You cannot upgrade the buildings on the farm (except the house), making small stables completely useless once the larger ones are unlocked.Decorations in the house can only be placed in designated areas; furniture cannot be added to the majority of the house. Nothing can be placed on a carpet either.All products need makers to produce. However, each product needs its own maker (e.g. fabric made from wool and fabric made from grass) and only 10 versions can be ordered per maker. This means that half of the farm area is taken up by makers, since there is nowhere else to put them other than in open space (not in the stable, not in a shed, etc.).Items are only automatically pulled into the inventory if there is still space. Once they are on the ground, they must all be picked up individually.The NPCs are uninteresting, unloving and unnecessarily mean to each other. I've never been so annoyed about the in-game birthday in a game of this type! The NPCs literally said, ah, today is your birthday, I should have gotten you something, but I didn't. Deal with it. Whatever sad childhood memories the developers have, I don't think a farming game is the place to process them...The main story is to turn Olive Town into a tourist town. We achieved this by improving the streets twice, the lanterns and the town hall. A new shop is coming to town and a new NPC. That's all that's happening to the city. It took me until mid-autumn of the first year to finish this “story”. After that, there are still “projects” that you can complete, but the rewards are not in the slightest worth the effort.Additionally, the city and really the whole area available is tiny. The city has two streets and a tiny forest that is just big enough for a pond. You can't even cut down the trees there. You can unlock more areas (e.g. a field that always has a certain season, etc.) but because you are teleported there and there is no connection to the farm, everything still feels extremely squashed.The museum is incredibly tiring. You find the treasures in mysterious bags that you first have to have identified. This means you can't sort out useless items when you find them in the mine, but have to take them all the way to the museum, where each one has to be put through the identification loop one by one. For fish, unlike treasures and animals, only a shadow of the classification is displayed, so you cannot see at first glance which fish have already been given away. And the great photo feature that is advertised in the trailer is only useful once for each of the wild animals and you can't even keep all the photos because the camera only has space for 10 photos. Furthermore, you have to put everything in place before you know what's to come, so you basically can't have a nice sorting unless you completely spoil yourself beforehand.I could go on, but I'll end my rant here.TLDR: For way too many reasons, just don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Please note, I played this on the Nintendo Switch, I did not play the Steam/PC version.If you like Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley, you will very likely enjoy Story of Season: Pioneers of Olive Town too. You run a farm you inherited from your grandfather (seriously, why is it ALWAYS your grandfather) and learn to farm, fish, mine, craft, cook, and harvest wild goods. You become as the only person (for some reason) who can save the sleepy town's economy and increase the tourism by completing simple gathering quests. SoS is a spin-off from the Harvest Moon series so the adorable art style is very similar. As in both HM and Stardew, you also can build relationships with the townsfolk, get married to one of the several romance options, and have kids. I frequently find myself saying, "okay, I'll play just one more day" as my real day keeps slipping by. Things I like about Olive Town:- Gender doesn't matter, all romances (5 males, 5 females) are available regardless of which gender you choose.- Lots of relationship cut-scenes. One for each heart level, regardless of if it's a romance-able character or not.- The graphics are adorable!- Finding and selling new produce in the wild makes them become available in the stores.- Getting your first of each type of livestock free by taming it in the wild.- All hairstyles and colors are available upon character creation, and once the salon is unlocked, you can change those whenever you fancy.- The simplistic fishing mini-game.- The cute wildlife. I get excited every time I see one of the adorable foxes run by, and the camera is a nice touch.- Cooking lets you choose the specific items you want to use instead of auto selecting for you.- The relationships screen has a notepad about each person, which adds more detail the higher relationship level you obtain with them.Things I DON'T like about Olive Town:- Although the townsfolk have their own personalities, they are... lacking and overall uninteresting.- Inventory issues. Your inventory fills fast, then you end up with chests you built everywhere to store items you need to keep.- No fighting. Though they have "baddies" in the later mines that you can bop.- Lack luster museum. Items get placed on designated pedestals, which is fine, I suppose. I would have hoped that the fish you donate would at least have more visually appealing displays. though.- Trying to plan your farm layout is frustrating as most items are 2x2 squares, and the traditional setup for fields is 3x3, if you want to take full advantage of sprinklers. This makes it hard to make things efficient and still visually appealing.- All the "maker" machines. So, so many maker machines. You basically will end up turning your farm into a factory as you end up spending most of your time just running to each machine to refill them with resources, then take those resources to stuff into another machine to make something else. Since there are multiple grades of each resource, you need multiples of each maker machine to be efficient.- The crafting menu. Everything is shoved into one menu, with no way to organize or limit it to what you're looking for. There is no indication of which items you've previously made or what's new to your list of options. (It does tell you in the cooking menu, though)- How quickly nature takes over your farm. Resources are a must, but it's discouraging to have to chop trees and smash rock every single day to have your farm look nice.

The game punishes very little for your mistakes or bad choices: you can never lose FP and there's no hated gifts, you wont's lose stamina for swinging your axe wrong so no stress here. _childDocuments_.review: Still has the Harvest Moon formula - farm crops, raise animals, marry and start a family. The whole game screams cute and cozy. The Good:What I love is that there are a lot of events with all of the characters (not just the marriage candidates) which is great, simple storytelling. Just like typical farm sims, it's really hard at first but absolutely satisfying to see the eventual empire you can build. There's also an "easy" mode that makes the grind a little faster if you're into that.The Bad:The crafting / maker element has been heavily integrated and the game now somewhat circles around it - you might need to sacrifice a bit of your farm land to place makers all over. As compensation, the game gives you additional portions of land though during the end game, where they function as pseudo greenhouses.The Ugly:The probably most annoying thing is the constant clutter that spawns on your farm. You will continuously have to clear out trees, rocks, weeds every 3-5 days if you want to keep it tidy. The intention for this is to have unlimited resources available to the player. You can control spawning by adding paths all over you farm, which is something you might want to do little by little. During end game, when you're able to block areas from spawning clutter, the game gives you areas where rocks and trees spawn quickly, with rarer materials.Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town will definitely not disappoint fans of the series - this will give you a lot of game time especially if you play on normal and want to accomplish all the game has for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel weird posting this without having beaten the game, but I also feel like I might never get there so here we are. This game just feels like a big step backward for the series. I know Mineral Town is a remake of sorts, but it is just so much better than Olive Town, never mind other titles in the daily life farming genre. As I have yet to beat the game I will refrain from judging characters and dialog here but I will say that so far it hasn't been particularly amazing. My big gripes are with the actual farm. Without putting down flooring everywhere you will be inundated with weeds and saplings on the daily to a frankly ludicrous extent. Having renewable resources is nice but it's too much. Part of the fun of these games is having an aesthetically pleasing farm layout, no? The other major gripe is the "makers". Who thought it would be a great idea to make players give up 1/3 of their farmland (although you do get *plenty* of land to work with) to uni-tasking crafting machines that take a ridiculous amount of time to process materials thereby necessitating even more of them? I hate them so much. Another smaller annoyance are the sound effects. Most are tolerable but listening to my avatar grunt every time I place down a tile of flooring made me mute the game. Listening to the museum girl go "Ooohhhhhhh" for every single thing I wanted her to appraise made me want to kill her. Also the water bucket sound.So yeah. It's playable and if you're desperate for a farming game and don't want to replay something like Mineral Town or Stardew or whatever, and have $40 to blow then I guess go for it. _childDocuments_.review: I played this on the Switch and enjoyed the game.  However, the issues pre-patch with makers, dialogue, performance, etc had pushed me away from the game.  I ended up putting the game down at around 75ish hours on the Switch because I just couldn't take it anymore.  I ended up buying the Steam version with the Steam refund option in mind.  That said, I must say WOW they fixed all the things I had big gripes with!  The game is running at a solid 120 fps on PC.  I have zero stuttering issues and loading into new areas now takes but a second or two instead of a minute plus.  The new chat zoom option fixed the issues with portraits for me.  Yes portraits would still be nice, but this zoom option has fixed the issue of always staring at the back of NPC heads.  The last big thing was dialog with the NPCs being bland.  While this is not 100% fixed, it is vastly better than it was.  I'm actually interested in what the NPCs have to say now.If you are interested in a farming sim, this is a great one to try.  It's not as hugely engrossing as Trio of Towns or Stardew Valley, but there's tons to do.  This is not a groundbreaking game in terms of new features, but the features that are here work well and are fun.  It would be nice if there were more festivals and more of a reason to level up crops and animals.  However, game is still fun regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: This is almost exactly what you'd want and expect in a classic style Harvest Moon game.  I've got a couple of gripes, though.  Your character has a ridiculous jalopy head compared to all of the other characters, which makes them look like they've got some kind of disease and makes all of the hats look like crap.  Minor customization options and outfits aside, you don't look as good as the NPCs.  Actually, the scale of a few things is kind of weird, because the cows are absolute behemoths.The narrative themes are definitely geared towards fairly young children, which I suppose is kind of expected for a Harvest Moon game, but being constantly reminded that I'm playing a game designed for the competency and emotional maturity of 10 year olds stings a bit.  Stardew Valley could be a little dark and dreary at times, but overall struck a better balance with the characters and dialogue.Your crafting options appear in the menu in the order that you earn them, rather than organized by category or in preset positions, which makes it very frustrating if you're trying to find a specific option.  Where the hell is my thread maker?  Why is it between the fishing bait and the fodder piles, rather than having all the machines grouped together?  Why is a suction pump between fishing nets and the butter maker?The farm map is a bit irregular, and your ability to place objects/machines and customize it feels messy and unsatisfying because you can't go right to the edge, group things too tightly together, or do anything with slopes.  This is another area where Stardew did it a lot better - placing machines and customizing your farm was much tighter in Stardew, and there were really obvious areas that you could designate specifically for that purpose.  That feeling of messiness is compounded when weeds and trees crop up everywhere every day - between crops, between machines, and in the fenced-in areas of farm buildings.  My strategy to deal with that was to pave 80% of the map with mortar and stone, leaving just a few wild areas so that I had places to farm the various kinds of wood and grass, but having my army of a dozen animals out grazing on a sidewalk feels a bit... Lame.  But it's either that or hammer down trees literally every day.Despite all that, I've put an embarrassing amount of time into this in the week that I've had it, and am routinely up until 4am playing it.  It's a marvelous time-sink.  8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to mark this game down after almost 50 hours of game play, but I honestly cannot recommend this to people when they can simply play older harvest moon games and not to mention stardew valley. My first major problem: the series has devolved. The new 3D paintjob is not enough to cover up the shallow mechanics, the grind, and the robotic NPCs. For first time goers, this will be a very good game experience, until you get to the part where you need orichalcum. DO YOUR SELF A FAVOR AND GET A TRAINER TO GET INFNITE ORICHALCUM END GAME. Thank me later. For Harvest Moon veteran like myself, this game will draw out your nostalgia but then disappoint you.I want to talk about the Original Harvest Moon: Friends of the Miner Town on the GBA. The reason why that game draws me in in the first place, and continue to do so until today, is because the NPCs actually have good stories behind them, and they at least act like humans who can become angry, sad, jealous, etc.Many recent Harvest Moon titles have improved so much mechanically, but they failed in creating interesting characters in town. Olive Town suffers that problem big time. Every single NPC has a big azz smile on their face like they are the happiest people on earth. Nobody has any problems. Nobody is conflicting with anyone. No personalty, no character, no development. Mechanics can only carry you so far in this type of game. It is the attachment to a human like NPC that is the key to make players love the games.Friends of the Miner town succeded at that with flying colors. Stardew Vally failed in that department, and this game didn't even bother to give their NPCs stories. I know the downmark for this game is not very fair, but after 50 hours of game play I can only feel a void. A crave for a better time that I can't get back.

_childDocuments_.review: What is Story of Seasons: Pioneer's of Olive Town?Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town or "SoS PoOt" as the internet refers to it as is a Marvelous production following the division between Marvelous and Natsume over the desire for Marvelous to want to do in-house translation through X-Seed and Natsume losing a major series they helped promote in the West (as Harvest Moon.)PoOT was released in September, 2021. Developed by Marvelous and Published by XSeed. Gonna call the Franchise here "Harvest Moon" out of habit and a reluctance to put "SoS" or "PoOT" every time I want to reference the game or the series. -=-=-Note-=-=-This might be overly critical, but I'm a longtime fan of the franchise. So I'm going to be nitpicky. I won't excuse it or deny it. I want these games to get better over time. That means pointing out things I don't agree with. -=-=-Gameplay-=-=-Consists of your typical daily chores on your Farmstead. While not the largest (or the most easily navigated) terrain to work with, it has it's quirks. As a "Pioneer" you are able to expand your allotted territory by fulfilling various tasks such as making enough Lumber or Stone to produce various pieces of infrastructure (like bridges) to enable navigation. You can also use them for rebuilding worn down structures you find in the field. Where you can then move them about as you please. Which is a nice touch.The UI is slick and polished. The Tool bag as a separate inventory for storing your tools with a quick swap in and swap out is a feature I never knew I wanted till this release. Don't need your tools? Well, put them away and open up that space for other things. No more running back to a chest or a storage crate!The autosave is generous when it comes to routinely keeping tabs on your progress and the ability to save anywhere is such a huge plus. I'm tired of the days, with these types of games requiring you to save at the start of the day because sometimes you're just not able to complete a day to get there, so you end up either compromising a day because you need to save to attend to other stuff or quitting prematurely and losing anything you've done for that day. It's a welcome, and desired feature.There's a handful of Skills in this game and some worthwhile perks for leveling them up. It's nowhere near the number crunching, "bigger number" gimmick that is Rune Factory, but it's nice to be rewarded for hitting a particular milestone with a reduced stamina cost for using tools or new things to build. Your skills DO dictate whether or not you can Water, Seed, Plow, or Mine over a wider area over time and I like this change. Upgraded equipment simply reduces the stamina drain each tool has instead. Unfortunately there's a few glaring problems with this Story of Season's release. I'll list them below. 1. The Makers. These tiny automated production facilities are the most frustrating things they've added to the Formula. Sure, they produce things like Lumber, or Ingots, or Cloth over a period of time, but to get the most out of them: you'll need a whole field dedicated to these things alone.There's 19 of them. So knowing which ones do what is also important. I made a dedicated field and a storage chest to make some sense of, and have some control over, these dumb things. Yes, there's the "Giant" variants, but they take a while to unlock (I was at the 38-40 hour mark before I got the Giant Metal Maker.) They take up more space, require significant more resources to make, and produce more at once. While it feels useful, it takes so long to unlock that it doesn't feel worth it. Incidentally, there is also a Crafting Tab, which allows you to make most things instantly, but not the materials you need to make more advanced things. So you can make the makers on the spot, anywhere, but you can't manufacture the materials to make better things on your own. What a strange stopgap. I'd almost rather have a workbench or a dedicated room. 2. Decoration. There's no way to turn or rotate anything. So you can buy things like shelves or bookcases for your house, but you can't turn them to face the walls. They're always facing the camera. This is a big oversight. Decorating your house is such a joke. They're also limited to set slots. You can't overlap objects (like stone pathways and Makers) which means you'll have to clean the area around those annoying Makers every day as an additional chore. -=-=-Story-=-=-Misplaced Ambitions. (My third point.) The Story very much isn't about what you do. Only that you're helping the town become a tourist location. Which is antithetical to the whole Harvest Moon inspiration of getting away from the big towns and cities and enjoying a smaller, quieter life in the countryside.I just couldn't get behind this. It felt like a betrayal of what I expected. Which was the aforementioned smaller setting. While you might be instrumental in making that possible, it often has nothing to do with what you're doing. You turn in a collection of materials (like you would in Stardew) and magically they translate to increased improvements to the town. Somehow. I "completed" the story because objectives were tied to it, but I wasn't invested in what was going on, nor the plights involved. It existed, but I wasn't really engaged by it.As for the Bachelor's/Bachelorettes: I find it funny that there's no flag in the game that cuts you off from seeing events from other potential marriage candidates when you're already married. That and you can feed your chosen one the same item over and over again, day after day till they love you. I feel like that system really needs to change. I get why it's a thing, and I know it won't appeal to everybody, but some realism might be a change of pace in this genre. -=-=-DLC Notes-=-=-The Expansion Pass adds some characters from other Story of Seasons games into the mix, and a few outfits and quests. Some are unlocked by story progression. They are NOT added to the default town, but exist on tiny islands of content you'll have to go to via the boat next to your house. So you'll have to remember to go there to interact with them. -=-=-Comparisons to Stardew Valley-=-=-How does it compare?If you've played Stardew Valley, there's a lot here that is going to feel familiar. Museum, Town Development, Character Customization, etc. Stardew Valley is still clearly superior. -=-=-Final Thoughts-=-=-The story (on Seedling) is pretty brisk and straightforward once you get rolling. There's not much difficulty to it, but I really feel like Seedling is the ideal way to play. Yes, you can argue that the normal difficulty might be more rewarding at the end of the day: but is it really worth 600% more effort to get there? I don't think so. All in all, it's a fun little farm sim with some charm. If you like Story of Seasons, or the early Harvest Moon games. It's on par with past entries. If you're looking for something in the same genre as Stardew, but doesn't quite live up to that standard: this'll scratch that itch for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge HM/SoS fan so I was really excited for a Switch/PC release of the newest SoS game. I'm going to break it down into categories. I only made this because I have a lot of opinions on this game and no one to vent it to so enjoy :)==============Graphics:==============The game looks alright, I will say I do enjoy the clean look of buildings now as opposed to seeing them on the 3DS but honestly, I don't even think Tree of Tranquillity or Animal Parade looks bad. One hair just looks as if they stretched out a single shape and slapped a crappy hair texture on. Still, the faces look fine and the game doesn't look ugly and the lighting is nice I just expect a little more out of Story of Seasons when the 3DS town in Trio of Towns and SoS looks so nice and it was on such an inferior machine.==============Characters & Town:==============I used to almost exclusively play the games for the bachelors/bachelorettes and I loved interacting with them and giving them gifts to eventually give them a blue feather and I have to say this has got to be the worst game for bachelors/bachelorettes. I am personally on the side of portraits when you speak to a character and removing it just feels so strange. I honestly never noticed Animal Parade’s lack of sprites but when I play PoOT it just feels like something is missing. It could very well be the boring 1-dimensional characters or just missing the nice drawn art to accompany the model. (There is an option to have the camera move into the characters to see their faces and it does help but still, just doesn't hit it for me)The townsfolk feel for the most part fine and I love the wide range of races as well as the fact you can marry whoever but great strides like this need to also be implemented with good character writing.One of my biggest tissues was how small the world felt. Without the extra DLC islands its just two main areas, your farm and the town. it feels like they mashed together all the old areas in previous games just into your farm so you didn't need to explore but this concept makes your daily life playing incredibly boring and i found i had nothing else to do by mid day. Keeping everyone in one place isn't the issue, its there's no feeling of exploration of this town when there's only two places to explore.==============Gameplay:==============Crafting:-------------------This game seems to be very inspired by Stardews success as makers have never been in the series (New Beginning had crafting as well but it wasn't to this degree. Also ik makers have been in the series I just meant crafting ones) and it's not great.Crafting isn't the bad part it's how tedious and annoying makers are. I bought this game right when it released on Switch and I haven't touched it since as the 1 item max was probably the worst mechanic I've ever seen. This has been fixed to 10 max now and is honestly a godsend to my mental and my farm space.The farm this time has constant upgrades that you can pay or get materials to expand and it's fine, I think the only item I find stupid is the bucket and how quick little ponds create on my farm. Farm & Farming:-------------------The farming and animals are the biggest thing in this game though and it's sad to see how dumbed down it's gotten. No longer do you need a milker or shears, your character magically just shears an alpaca with their bare hands! If they made two difficulties you'd think the normal would have these actual difficulty spikes.The biggest thing about my farm I hate is paths, you can create paths but they're very picky about where they can be places so I cant have a nice path that leads all across my farm and just have it in specific fields, and nowhere near the entrances of the building. Crops are the same and honestly, there's not a lot you can screw up in regards to that.==============Overall:==============This game just feels so lifeless and dull. It's great to see the game get updates to fix these issues like DLC bachelors/bachelorettes not being able to join festivals but it's just an unmemorable SoS game. I have decided to go back and try Trio of Towns out again because I have been missing that Harvest Moon Feeling when I play. It doesn't feel like i'm actually a part of this town and I want to take part in their events if the characters are dull and the events mean nothing. This is no hate to it being made on Unity as I think the Gen 4 remakes are nice(yes I know it's buggy) but this game on the engine just feels lazy and not creative especially since this game was developed either entirely by another company or co-developed and it's pretty apparent. I'm hopeful for the next Story of Seasons game and hope that they make but this game sadly isn't one I can recommend to people as it just doesn't have enough to offer someone to introduce them to the series. It's really sad too since SoS has also exclusively been on Nintendo consoles.I will still play this game and maybe my opinion will change more but I have enough hours on steam and on Switch to decide that this is one of if not the weakest games in the SoS/HM series.

_childDocuments_.review: As of 10 hours of gameplay everything is really solid. The core aspects of farming, gathering, fishing, mining, woodcutting seems okay. The aspects that could use a little work are the grinding nature of refining materials to upgrade facilities and tools. As you progress through the game, there's an exponential increase in the required materials needed to repair/upgrade facilities. This is poor design imo, locking content behind time needed to refine materials instead of thinking of another way of progression. Another aspect that could use some work is the amount of random crashes; I've lost about a total of 2 hours due to crashes. I would play through a whole day only for it to crash at the most random moments. Some locations where I crashed are entering/exiting the chicken coop, entering random npc buildings, at the start of cutscenes , and also when I .Overall it's a great game, but the game crashed frequently enough to warrant a downvote.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game for 180 hours, all harvest moon, story of seasons, and pretty much any farming game in existence... I'm not impressed. I have many complaints if I compare this game to more recent farming games as many of the newer farming games have great features this game lacks. I will instead focus on the problems without comparing to better games. First of all, the challenges are few and far between and are hugely difficult to achieve without much reward. This makes the game mostly repetitive tasks and waiting for your machines to turn ore into bars etc. Then on top of that, the seed maker machine is so slow at converting your crops into seeds that it takes a week in-game to get 10 crops converted. It's ridiculous and makes it pretty much irrelevant, which means not being able to grow higher quality crops and therefore better quality food. Which makes Lovett's food challenges impossibly difficult. My biggest complaint- there isn't enough storage space. I pursued upgrading my home to the max just to have more fridge space only to find that it's not even close to enough. So, I built chests to hold all my crops and food supplies... only you can only place so many items even if you have the physical space. And it's not enough. So there is literally no way to hold each item in the game. Even if you only hold the max quality on each item (and not multiple qualities) you can't come close to storing everything. I've never come across this problem in a farming game and it's so frustrating I just can't finish the game. If I could back and start knowing what I now know, I wouldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful installment of the SoS/(true successors to the original harvest moon games post-natsume IP split) that is a joy to play. Not to mention it has updated QoL aspects like multiple item hotbars, light automation, streamlined UI/UX, support for key bindings and quick inputs. Like the trailers suggest, you also get to customize your farm's building placements and the like. Its better than the previous harvest moon titles that attempted this base building mechanic. The only downside is the lack of customization options for the home, with barely any space to put in your furniture in a single allotted corner.Everything else, is your oyster. The town life is pretty cool, with a myriad of town events and character stories. Some of them do feel like they are padding out the writing, but considering there's enough of them to last over 4 years of in-game time, which is 16 seasons and excluding the character cutscenes, I can see that there was plenty of effort put into making the town feel alive and fun. Just a shame that some characters feel flat because of the usual stereotyped pigeonholing, but its not necessarily bad character design... but rather predictable if you play enough of these games.Also, the point of the game is to play it YOUR way. You can hyper optimize within the first year to the point you burst past the town development goals and unlock the true endgame... randomized quests, farm decor/minmaxing and living your life your way.Is the price steep? Arguably yes... especially if you didn't get the game with the season pass which came with the DLCs included. I do recommend getting it while on discount (I say this for every game on steam), but even at 30% its reasonable. Lets face it, if you're reading this review, chances are you are a very niche type of player that enjoys farming sims like Stardew Valley, Harvestella, Rune Factory, Story of Seasons, Harvest Moon, Innocent Life, Coral Island, etc... You also most likely have played these games before and are looking for another life sim. I've sunk over 80 hrs on 2 separate playthroughs, and the game still drip feeds new content in end game like new animal types and lategame optimizations well into the 40hr mark. I'd reckon that in a single playthrough, to get max optimizations you would go well into 60 hrs, and thats excluding fully building out your entire farm to look like a paradise.If what I'm saying isn't enough to push you over the edge, remind yourself this is a cozy game that will happily wait for you to come back when you're ready. It may be a while until you feel like playing, but like most SoS lifesim games, down the road where you just want something chill. Its sitting in your library waiting to welcome you back with open arms.God I love these games.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like one of the best Harvest Moon games I have ever played.I discover something new every couple of days I play this game, and there is so much content in this game that it's absolutely amazing. It's worth playing for an extended period of time.The game is also quite relaxing, and gives the player a wide variety of ways to enjoy the game and the days, while keeping true to the farming genre by focusing on the value and importance of the farm.Plus, with the addition of implementing a skill mechanic, the player can gain perks by focusing on their favorite skills. There is also plenty of ways to aid the player, like a wonderful Rewards system at the Town Hall which rewards the player with useful things for accomplishing achievements and progressing in the game.I'm really enjoying this Harvest Moon, and it has to be in my top 5 favorite Harvest Moon games ever made that I've played, and I've played almost a dozen of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Amidst the reviews I read here and outside of steam, I was doubtful but I am so glad I gave this game a shot ! I couldn't put it down... I grew up playing harvest moon (SoS series) and for me, this game feels like the old HM game. T_T I am not a fan of the remakes tbh.. for me, the appeal for SoS game is the new adventure, new life and town to explore, new townspeople to meet and create memories. Last game I played a game in the series was Trio of Town and it was too much for me lol. For PoOT, I like how small and intimate the town is, nowadays farm life sim games tend to offer SO MUCH stuff that it can get overwhelming and grind-y. This game lets you breathe and chill. I like how you can customize the farm but not excessively. I like the townspeople and how so far the cut-scenes I uncover, really brought back memories of those wholesome candid moments and slowly learning about the townspeople and becoming part of the town. The farm and town layout is very conveniently tied together. Olive Town is breathtaking though, the seaside is perfect ! _childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: PoOT is a great addition to the Story of Season franchise. Instead of a farmland in the rural area/mountains, you get shipped off to a farmland on an island where you help to develop the town and make it a tourist-worthy location that cruise ships would like to dock at. There are a lot more customizable options that make the game very personalized for players, and a lot of portions that you can unlock and develop so it feels like you're really building on the gameplay for hours of fun, until it gets too repetitive.Pros:- Customizable character appearance for your MC at the beginning, and later you can change their looks once you've unlocked that part- Lots of farmland, with 2 unlockable areas for more space- Additional unlockable farmland areas with one of each of the four seasons for forever planting- A wide variety of crops and fruits to discover, and lots of animal varieties- Plenty of decor, accessories, machinery to build (instead of buy)- Changing the look of the town through story progression/development- Unlockable in-game achievements that award you items- Daily in-game quests that give you money- Customizable house and furniture layout, and having more than one pet- Lots of fun characters and interesting conversations- Once unlocked, magical sprites gift you items almost dailyCons:- TOO MUCH variety of items and crops. There are so many machines (some crops or goods go through 2-3 product transitions that need 1 machine each transition) and not enough space to accommodate them all, even with the expanded farmland. You also have to keep building storage boxes to store them all.- Farmland layout is weird, and you have ponds that crop up out of nowhere and make placements of barns, crops, etc very difficult- Not enough in-game storage, even with bag upgrades. Refrigerator also doesn't have enough space, even with the upgraded space. Connected to the issue with the game having too many items, and too many varieties/levels to each item- Complicated time management (due to the game having too many additional places, getting around is a challenge)- Limited variety/quantity of items you can sell  in the shipping box per day- Relationship progression here with villagers and marriage candidates are much slower even with constant gift-giving- Game has an animal you can ride, and a motorcycle, but placement and number of machines and buildings makes traversing through your farm hard, and your "mode of transpo" pretty useless (at least for me)- Museum (one of the added items for completion through collecting) displays cannot be altered or customized once items are placed- Magical sprites don't help you with your farm chores, which would otherwise not have been a problem if the farm wasn't big, and you didn't have a lot of animals and cropsSummary: Interesting new angle to the franchise, and the customizable portions do make it a fun play. There's a great story, and the animation and music are amazing. The characters and dialogue are fun too. Sadly, SoS tried to give the game too many additional things, that sometimes the game gets really repetitive and redundant in a not good way. The Harvest Moon franchise is supposed to be repetitive because of the farming aspect, but because PoOT has so many things you can do, it sometimes feels overwhelming. Too much to mine, too much animal products to collect daily, too many crops to harvest, too many unlocked areas to go to, etc.Great game especially if you love the franchise and farming sims, but buy it on sale. And don't bother spending on those added costumes since there's a lot of free in-game outfits you can naturally unlock.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit leery of this after sos- friends of mineral town on PC was so disappointing- but I am a sucker for these and harvest moon. And when I saw the water buffalo and hydroculture plant? I was sold. Novelty wins again. (turns out the goats are my absolute favorite animal in the game. watch them hop around and try not to squee)I really really enjoy this game. It hits a sweet relaxing spot and I feel like I can go my own pace with it. I like what this game was trying to do. Is the museum as polished and user friendly as Animal Crossing? No, but it gives you something to work on beyond the main story quest and helps extend the game play a bit. Are the characters as exciting as Rune Factory 4? No, but to be fair I never enjoy the making of friends/romance in these types of games. RF4 is unique that I do like the characters personalities. Is the crafting as enjoyable as stardew valley? No, the amount of makers needed is absurd. They are also redundant. I have a powder maker to make certain spices, a seasoning maker to make other certain spices, a condiment maker (which i feel like is another kind of seasoning?), and a mayo maker just for eggs. Is mayo not a condiment?? These makers also take up a ton of room, and you can't hide them away in a shed if you don't like the look. They also don't process very much. That said- these aren't horrible additions and i feel like they enhance the game. I bought sos-fomt for the pc and it was so boring. There wasn't really any story or variety to activity. I keep forgetting I have it tbh. But this game has a lot to work on aside from just straight up farming/ranching. Unlocking new areas, animals, buildings and craftable items keeps things fresh. The care of animals is probably one of the best features- I hate having to use a milker then swap to a brush. It gets old fast. Here I can just click to milk/brush/pet which makes getting through the tedious elements quick, plus you can unlock an autofeeder fairly early and place it in any coop/barn size which I LOVE. I did have a major issue where I couldn't harvest anything from the ground- so most of my hours are played without being able to farm or use chickens- as I was trying to unlock an endgame skill that would hopefully resolve that issue. But it turns out I just needed to lower my graphics settings and play in a small window and I can actually harvest. So I started over and its even better now that I can farm.

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember the wonder I felt playing the original Harvest Moon on the SNES, Back to Nature, A Wonderful Life, Hero of Leaf Valley... all fun experiences. The split with Natsume happened and I didn't exactly get on board with the Story of Seasons games for DS and whatnot. Still, I got the Friends of Mineral Town remake. Didn't care for what they did with so many of the characters so it went on the backlog.Decided to get Pioneers of Olive Town though as it got rave reviews and... well, here we are. I actually wish Steam could add a neutral option to the review process as this game has some good points and a lot of negative ones that make it middle of the road rather than a solid recommend or a decided no go.Olive Town has a certain charm to it. The character models are well made, the music's okay and the farming areas are nice. Some interesting ideas are included, such as learning new recipes by eating at the local cafe or diner and unlocking craftables if you level your skills or the town up. The town changing for the better as you complete resource requests is also nice. There's minigames at the festivals and such... and you can move farm buildings around easily. The resource variety is also good and you can get some for free by spending time managing earth sprites at their village. Tool upgrades not needing days to complete is handy. Also, the Spirit is an interesting character that could have been so much more... But alas.Olive Town feels really shallow. There's no other way to describe it, bar the wide as a swimming pool and deep as a puddle analogy. Especially when taking the DLC into account which accentuates the issue with the townsfolk by putting past game marriage candidates into little bubble islands. Dialogue focuses too much on the festivals and has little to no variation otherwise. And while festivals can have a little minigame like launching a barrel, it's usually just that and a different dialogue line from the attending townsfolk. The Egghunt being a cutscene though is insulting.Likewise, you used to need to talk, brush and milk cows with tools. Now you just pull milk out of their nose and scratch their buttocks by hand, removing a layer of interactivity. Same for the Alpacas, sheep, rabbits and so on. While unlocking new areas by gathering resources or money may seem fun... its a slog through the game's stunted way of progression. If you want a town upgrade and it lists multiple resources to deliver? Just need one of those. Want to get rid of boulders and trees? Silver ingots are a must have. Upgrade your tools? Well, good luck. You need resources that have to be unlocked first through slowly getting enough resources to get to the area. Stamina drain is a massive issue too while having the lower tier tools and no upgrades. Spot a critter wandering in the wild? You need to repair the barn/coop/hoopla building first.Aside from the resource slog there's also a distinct lack of care that was put into the camera. Certain critters (for the museum) only appear on/near trees in area x at time y in season z. But spotting a beetle/bird too late will make it fly off. You can't freely turn the camera unless you go into first person mode via the camera and then waste hours trying to find one that hasn't been scared off. The mines are also a point of gripe. You just get these semi-random little rooms that you have to find the next ladder under a rock in. Or a pitfall later. Breaking rocks, rarely finding a seam against the wall or a dig/gem spot on the floor and having to whack/avoid punk moles means even with good tools and upgraded stamina getting to the bottom of the second and third mines isa major speedrun challenge. NVM that you need to hit lvl 36+ for Orichalcum.Draining is probably the most aggravating skill though. Grab a bucket and drain away puddles for clay/etc., ponds for random resources/museum donations/medals. Or drain lakes with a pump. All very slowly. And the random finds have to be appraised one by one at the museum. Given how fast even a fully upgraded bag fills though and how you are still going to get more junk than something nice this is a massive chore. And don't get me started on how many tree sprouts, weeds and puddles appear every day.Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town could have been a great game. But it falls far short, especially compared to the now many indie-game competitors. A personal gripe as well is that some of the more interesting townfolks are not marriable, nor do the dlc characters integrate into the game proper. It's not all bad, but I cannot recommend it unless you really want it and while it's on sale. Otherwise its too tedious  and shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has several broken features that are a result of very poor quality porting between the Switch and PC. Harvesting is completely broken. If you're not standing on the right pixel at the right angle, you can't harvest crops or forage for items. In some cases, there is just no way to harvest anything. It will give you the option, execute the animation, but nothing happens. Sometimes the item will disappear but you will notice that the prompt is still there and you have no item in your inventory. Leaving and returning to the map will cause the item to become visible again on the ground where it already was. The single, primary operation of the game is dead in the water. If you check the discussion boards you will see that this is a commonly reported bug and has been since it launched.  Additionally, the movement controls are laggy and unresponsive. It sometimes takes several hits to get a movement to respond or to execute an action properly. I don't have this problem in other more demanding games or other programs that I run on the same machine. I don't recommend buying this game until or unless they fix this because the game rather quickly becomes unplayable as a farming sim.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played close to 70 hours so far, and earned 80% of the achievements. I have played enough to say, I'm 100% sure this game is worth buying. My initial review is still how I feel about it, but I wanted to point out it is a fantastic game after all this time played.Pros:+Farming is awesome+Upgrading tools, house, and farming buildings is great+Progression system for skills is fantastic+Dating, marriage, and child system is good+The game looks beautiful, I love the art direction+Mining is very enjoyableCons:-Town is too small-No options for exploration, which sucks-Dialogue for the townspeople is terrible, they often repeat same lines-Festivals are awful, especially compared to My Time at Portia-Museum is horrible, especially compared Animal Crossing:New Horizons-No multiplayerI still recommend buying the game on sale. I think it is one of best life/farming simulation game I have ever played. It is worth buying.My Original Review:I am new to the Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons games. I do really enjoy life simulation games like Animal Crossing:New Horizons, Stardew Valley, Littlewood, and My Time in Portia. Pioneers of Olive Town is more comparable to My Time at Portia, then any of the rest I have played. Like My Time at Portia, this game has a big focus on building things. If you don't like that, then maybe buy the other Story of Seasons game instead. Stardew Valley was inspired by the Harvest Moon series, so it is very similar as well. This game is sort of casual, but does have a grind to it like most life simulation games. From what I have played so far, it isn't anywhere close to as grind-y as Stardew Valley. I know many reviewers complained about the time going by too fast, but I don't think it is bad at all. It reminds me a lot of the days on My Time in Portia. Not too long, but I'm not rushed like Stardew Valley. My verdict so far is the game is worth buying. I wish the city was bigger like My Time at Portia and there were more exploration areas, but the farming and ability to upgrade things is very good. I usually just spam my way through dialogue in most life sims, so that isn't a deal breaker for me. If you love Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia, you might as well just buy it now. It is 100% worth buying on sale, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the genre has been reinvented about 5000 times there is a certain simplicity of execution that Story of Seasons excels at that makes it a much comfier game to me than Rune Factory or Stardew. This game is arguably less mechanically complex than even the GBA entries but that often works to its benefit. It doesn't become a micromanagement business simulator which I think, for as fun as that can be, goes against the spirit of the original game on SNES. It's just a game where you inherit a farm, build it up, and ultimately establish a relationship with largely two dimensional NPCs (For what it's worth, I do think the characters are more interesting than most of the other games, but they're far from complex individuals with wants and needs) I did quite a bit on switch already but I don't remember if it even has simple things like fertilizer, you just plant crop and wait for crop and the level is based on how often you interact with crop in a rune factory-esque level up menu.My main critiques is, some events really feel like they were gonna be playable and they just aren't, the easter egg hunt is a cutscene. Also there are some tremendously cute characters like Beth, Angela and Patricia who aren't romanceable, but that is part of SoS's ongoing mission of being a milf cuckold simulator which is charming in its own right.Despite considerable ease of use introductions like almost immediate access to Sprinklers and backpacks, I think this is the game that is closest to bringing me to the same feeling as the original SNES game. I don't think this is worth a full 40 dollars or anything but 15-20 it's an easy recommend. It runs way better than it did on Switch and fulfills a niche that other casual farm sims have long worked past. I bought the season pass this go and the expanded areas don't seem worth anything, unless you really want one of the bachelors or bachelorettes or the costumes or it's a considerable sale I would skip it.If you want interesting characters with a lot of personality, You can't go wrong with any of the Rune Factories. If you want a straightforward farming game and don't have Mineral Town that might be your first go to, but if you're coming from Mineral Town or just didn't jive with the frankly cryptic progression of that game, this one is excellent. Also Reina is cute.

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a neutral review option but weighing the pros and cons, I think I'll say that this is one of those games :get it if you can live with the cons Pros: * I do not mind the style of the characters, I actually find both the player character options of hairs/clothes to be amazing and a lot of the NPC's have very adorable designs. * Variety of animals to raise is quite nice too and the same goes for the variety of flowers/vegetables that can be grown in each season. * Fishing is quite fun and not too tedious, actually enjoyed it. Cons* Tedious: the crafting mechanic is so horribly tedious and is quite messy: gathering resources, managing the machines etc etc just felt like something I dreaded rather than wished to engage with. And it feels like that defeats the entire point of the game. * I personally HATED that because of the tedium of constantly needing to harvest a ♥♥♥♥ ton of resources there was always an army of tree sprouts, weeds and boulders all over my farm. Personally I like to try and keep my farming areas a bit cleared up so this drove me nuts. Would have much preferred if there was some way to decrease this or prevent it from sprouting at least outside your front door. * The events/heart events/festivals are really shallow. I personally enjoy having to fight a bit to woo my bachelor/bachelorette of choice but it felt like there was no real chase/wooing, I was more or less handed whoever I choose. Also wish that they had allowed the NPC's/romance options to be a bit deeper, I enjoy a fluffy happy fantasy as much as the next person but from my farming sims I would enjoy a bit more meat on the bones so to speak. I can't accuse the game of being a bad, it works for what it is, it just so happens that what it is was a tedious mess for me. I restarted several times and had to force myself to play for over a year, something I've never had an issue with in other SoS, Harvest Moon and other farming sims. If you're not bothered by a fluff piece with some slightly tedious game play, the game can still be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing I can salute the devs of this game for is the absolute unhinged audacity to ask for 40 euros for this shallow, lifeless puddle they think their players are worth to play in. Yikes. Imagine you sit down at your favorite restaurant. You order your favorite dish. It now sits in front of you. Unfortunately, all the components are so undercooked, the chicken just clucked at you. PoOT is like a dull and lacking version of other well-known, amazing fam/life sim games. It makes one wonder if ConcernedApe (SD Valley) or Pathea (My time at... series) are these brilliant one-in-a-generation geniuses or if devs of games like this are just lack any care about their games being an undercooked meal. Controls - Reeeally weirdly done. Sometimes hard to navigate. Is this some weird, unfinished port from handheld consoles?Characters - For the most part pretty meh, even all the bachelors. Lifeless, one dimensional. Completely pointless to have romance in the game or building relationships tbh. It adds nothing of value.Calendar events, festivals, etc. - I... I don't even have words, what a lackluster filler. Farm space - Pretty, but cleaning puddles, growing trees, herbs, grass, weeds etc. every day otherwise your farm turns into a complete mess is a head-scratching game design. (Who thought this is a good idea?)Story - I held back on this aspect but it's very obvious how empty it is. For 40 euros you should not be able to finish the game before the end of the first year. Museum - Tragic design all around. Don't even get me started on the whole appraisal of items and the absolute pain you must go through. (No, but seriously, who actually thought this is a good idea???)Organization of items - Just another tragedy you should not put your players through in farming sims lol. Who comes up with these things?! How even?!!Decorations/customizations - Please explain to me why I can craft/buy a ton of furniture if I can't even use most of it, since the area I am allowed to decorate is so small? Why can’t I turn them? Why I can't put stuff on crafted floors, or rugs? Why I can go to a random vendor and spend 500k on furniture I can at most shove up my a** since I am not allowed to use it at my house, while my house is a barren shed?! I wonder what kind of discussion happened when deciding how to design all these things because it seems like there was none. Like... how some of these things were green-lighted? Did no one on the dev team ever experienced a sim/farm/life game ever before? Were there no test players? :D What is going on here? Let me repeat, this game costs 40 euros... Now imagine that Stardew Valley is 14 euros. Trust me and spend your money on devs that actually care about their players and their gaming experience. This ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game so much. It just feels so good to play, especially how tactile the actions are and how effective their corresponding sound effects are. From the reviews I've seen it is understated how much they nailed the feel and sound which I think is very important in these kind of games where the game loop revolves around repeating the same kind of tasks over and over again.Being able to hold your charge while you move then demolishing everything around you just feels so good, this in my opinion is one of the greatest addition to the game, and I hope the series in general.The art is just lovely, I'm really digging the aesthetic, I'm currently using the Sakuna outfit and it just looks gorgeous to play with.The gameplay is fantastic, there is so much to do and added  QoL compared to SoS: FoMT. I'm really glad they adopted some of the interesting features/QoL of modern farming sims most notably Stardew Valley. I'm currently in the first week of Autumn and I'll say the progression feels good. The progression tier works surprisingly well, when you get your upgrade or level up your skill it is very noticeable how the pace of your resource gathering change. I believe the game has enough things to occupy you but not necessarily overwhelm you, with regards to the things you can do it lies in the middle of FoMT and Stardew Valley. Stardew personally felt a bit daunting since there is so much to do that It gives me this feeling that I'm missing out on things not to mention how big the map is, in comparison this game has less things to do though it feels really compact and I think it's pretty clever how they did it. Foraging, mining and woodcutting are all done inside the farm, the town and other locations are all one loading screen away. Personally I think that is it's greatest QoL .I've still yet to reach endgame and I'm really enjoying the game so far. I can't speak much about the characters, I keep hearing how they are the worst in the series but from what I've seen I assure you that is not the case(although it is understandable since they have to patch new dialogues when it released on switch, this version wasn't what they got). They certainly have their charm. If you grew up with FoMT I think you'll like the characters just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: For those of you who were on the edge of buying this game, so was I.Let me tell you that the patches that were made to this game turned it into a gem. I am enjoying the new map layouts and farm life. The added museum where you can donate collectibles, the range of crops, ranching, building up your home, and socializing with townsfolk gives there much to do. I do not find myself skipping any days unless the carpenter is closed and I am being impatient. The only con that many SoS/HM lovers would find is there being no social portraits for the townsfolk to better register their emotions and looks. I can agree that I miss this aspect of the game too, but it does not ruin anything for me. The added zoom in camera function from the patch was a great addition to make up for this. It obviously, is not a *great* replacement, but it does help. Online I saw a bunch of people complain about the 'thousand of makers' -- the processing machines for goods. It is the same mechanic used in Stardew Valley! It is not a horrible system at all. Typically in the past, games they would be added into the game as building upgrades and now they made them loose machines so you can move them closer to where you want and spend less time processing items (..I guess?). The point is, there is plenty of room for your makers on the farm. It would be nice if you could place them inside buildings, however!My favorite aspect of this game is the social aspect. I enjoy the new characters the most and always hope I find more. It does seem there are secret characters later on, however I can't say how many yet. With SoS clearly growing with each title and learning from others, I do hope they continue to work on this aspect the most because it seems the one that typically grows the least in this franchise imo. tldr: Highly recommend buying the game. Haven't skipped days, makers are fine, sad about character portraits.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game. I was a fan of the previous Story of Seasons games - especially Trio of Towns on the 3DS. The things that made that game a wonderful experience were completely gone in this title. TLDR; I'd recommend playing any other SoS game over this one. If you still want to try, wait for it to go on sale.Now for the novel version...What does this game do well? The graphics are cute, there are a good amount of customization options for your farmer, and... that's about it imo. The villagers/neighbors you have are extremely bland. They don't offer any conversation or personality that feels meaningful. They're boring and almost a chore to talk to. Perfectly fine if you're someone who doesn't care about the social aspect of these games, but as someone who does? It really bummed me out. Especially coming from their previous titles where each character felt fleshed out and engaging. Having multiple favorites and trying to decide who to marry is part of the fun! Here, it's mostly about "which NPC is nice to look at sometimes?". Whoever thought forcing the player to fill up their farm with a million small machines for crafting was insane. They're a migraine to work with and keep track of. It would have been fine if these machines were the first thing you unlock and then work towards a building where you can mass produce... but no. It doesn't happen. Cluttered Hell is your new farm name. Your presence in the game, like most other "newcomer to town" sims, is supposed to have an impact. I guess it does? Kind of? You slightly alter the way some things look, but not in a way that stands out. Pretty much the only change you'll notice is the addition of the hairdresser/clothing shop upgrade. Nothing else makes you feel like you actually made a difference. I don't know how they go from something with so much heart and memorable moments to mindless, repetitive game play. It's like the dev team lost interest in trying to make something immersive and settled for the bare minimum. Disappointed and hoping they learn from the faults of this title for their next entry to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge improvement from previous titles in terms of new features and quality of life changes. If you've played the old Harvest Moon and Story of Seasons, this game will feel a bit different. Much of the mechanics seem to be inspired from Stardew Valley, which is quite interesting considering the fact that SDV was inspired from the old HV/SoS.Skill leveling is great for motivating players to unlock new things as they play, giving them a sense of passive progress. Community projects are awesome, but there's only a few of them.; these make you feel like you're contributing something to the town's improvement and tourism rather than just focused on your own farm, and I wish there were more. The crafting system is fantastic and adds more depth to the game, giving the materials you collect more purpose than to just be thrown in the shipping bin. There are however, too many machines and makers, which can't even be placed inside buildings, whereas before these mayonnaise makers, butter makers, etc. came built-in inside the coop and barn. Now your only choice is to place them outside and it makes the surroundings ugly. There are plenty of exterior decorations, giving you the freedom to design your dream farm the way you want, especially now that you can move your coop, barn, and other farm structures around. Interior decoration on the other hand is really disappointing; the areas you're allowed to decorate in your home is very limited compared to how spacious it is, and the worst part is, you can't place storage boxes inside. Furniture can't be rotated, limiting creativity. Allowing players to decorate the farm is a step in the right direction, but it's a bit restricted at the moment. Some tools in the past such as the brush, milkers, and clippers are no longer needed to perform the action, which makes it a lot more convenient. After repairing the coop, barn, etc., a nearby farm animal can be tamed to keep for free, giving you a decent head start. On top of all this, the mining system has significantly improved and made mining easier and actually fun now. Relationship building is still a huge part of the game and is part of what made this type of farming simulator unique; there have been improvements to the townsfolk's dialogues but most of them just cycle through the pool of lines randomly regardless of your friend meter. I believe it can be done better.I love Story of Seasons and want to see it improve even further in the future. Pioneers of Olive Town has been the best one for me so far. The pacing is much calmer and it's been very relaxing to play, suits casual players. Would recommend this to anyone, especially those who have played previous titles and/or Stardew Valley.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game at launch but when I saw the reviews I waited quite some time before picking it up. After all the patchwork I can safely say the game is ready to be played and enjoyed. It's quite a bit shorter, smaller in scope, and less challenging than most of the others I've played. The only spike in difficulty in this entry comes from resource gathering, mostly in the form of things called Makers and having extremely high thresholds for things like the final house upgrade. It feels artificial like they were purposely trying to force longer play times. The town and folks are great but you quickly realize how extremely tiny it all is. This game has a lot less festivals than I'm accustomed to and I wish there were more. It also leaves out certain staples like the Hospital, Church, Library etc, which would have helped make the town larger and give you more marriage candidates. I was hoping for a next gen experience but this wasn't that. It's great, but it isn't filling. It leaves you wishing there was a lot more. I beat the game in year 1 in the first quarter of autumn, and did all the dlc side quests by year 2 spring. The game is short man. The Rune Factory games on Wii are still far deeper and more complex than these new SoS games. I'm really looking forward to their next adventure on Steam and I hope they step it up a bit. This game was pretty rough at the start, compared to how I know the series. It's still better than stardew valley and a hell of a lot prettier to look at. They just need to keep pushing the bar and take the series to the next level. SoS/RF will always be my jam.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game from the long standing Harvest Moon series(there was a split between Story of Seasons and harvest moon officially due to copyright issues, Story of Seasons is actually the "real" Harvest Moon; just see Story of Seasons; Friends of Mineral Town which was a remake of the GBA game and originally named Harvest Moon)They took a lot of pointers and features from Stardew Valley and made it their own.  Just like Stardew, you have skills that you level up to 10, unlocking craftable items and bonuses as you do so.  It takes quite a long time to do this.  However due to the mechanics of the graphics and farm layout you cannot create as easy or as aesthetically pleasing a farm as in Stardew.  Everything seems worthwhile in purpose in this game, there are tons of event/cutscenes as your friendship with the townspeople progresses, even eating at the diner is necessary later to unlock more recipes to cook.  This is one of those games that is a joy to 100% achievements if that matters to you.  It is probably the best official Harvest Moon game I have played, I did not think there would be one as good as the upstart success of Stardew Valley, but here we have it in the flesh, my bros and sisses.  Anyhow I do recommend if you liked HM, SV, Portia or any other farming sim, this one really hits the sweet spot and is a real gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I think farming games like Story of Seasons really have been tainted by the idea that everything has to be a automation sim. In earlier games, I pick up chicken eggs, and I put them into the shipping box and I am done.      In this game, I have to pick up the eggs, craft a mayo machine, and then build 3 (it takes forever to make mayo) and then after a few hours I can put it in the basket. Why do I have to do this? Because mayo goes for double or triple the money than just shipping the egg. It's boring and it drags out a simple task.      I found it really annoying that all of the fun things I like are automated. I upgraded my watering can because I like to do the little slide and water the plants in the morning. However, very early on you can craft sprinklers. Okay so I don't have to water the plants anymore.       I also really liked feeding the animals on rainy days, there's something- oh wait. That's automated to, with the help of an automated feeder. Automated fishing. You can unlock sprites that gather materials for you in the background. So what exactly do the developers want me to do in this game? Just run back and forth between crafting machines? It's very confusing. The game is slowly stripped away from you as you level up.  Well, I guess you also spend half your time cutting down trees, the wilds constantly grow back into your farm at an insane rate and the only thing you can do is put road down. And it just looks ugly.  This low effort art style might have worked back when this series was on the 3DS, but on PC the aesthetics in this game have no excuse. It's really lazy, the visuals look worse than the PS2 titles. It's somewhere between a crappy phone game and a bargain bin GameCube find.   But there is something here. I really enjoyed some of the music pieces and it still feels really good to farm and interact with villagers. The setting of Olive town is interesting, there is just no life outside of the event cut scenes.  There is no art when you talk to villagers, you just stare at their boring models (If you turn the option on.)   There are so many features in this game they contradict each other. At some point you get access to a motorcycle but the game wants you to repair a horse barn. Why would I trade 40 hp for 1? lol. I love the Story of Seasons franchise, I grew up with this series and it's one I flee too throughout the course of my life. But this one has no identity. No soul. Please, for your next title MARVELOUS try harder!

_childDocuments_.review: I truly wanted to like this game.  I played it on the Switch, but as the game progresses, it freezes continually for 1 to 2 seconds.  As I was streaming the game, the freezes were noticeable by my viewers, and they're VERY annoying.  So I bought the PC version, hoping it would be better, and I started over completely (which is a serious pain by the way).  The PC version has bugs!  The movement commands are not customizable, making for awkward movement, and the mouse clicks randomly cause the game to shift to the background, meaning you have to click the taskbar to get it back.  There also doesn't seem to be a way to change the window size from full screen.    Documentation on how to do things is also spotty.Please fix these issues!  It really could be a much better game.  It has a lot of potential, but the technical problems are really stopping me from enjoying it.  A few additional suggestions:1.  More time is needed during the game day, without an automatic reset at 2am.  2.  Finding Orichalcum Ore is way too difficult for a game of this type3.  Machines for seeds don't keep up, making it really difficult to handle production4.  House decoration is way too limited, and furniture choices are also too limited.5.  The amount of time it takes to keep areas clear is way too long and eats into your already limited time to complete tasks during a game day.  6.  The weasel things in the mines of area 3 after level 30 are almost impossible to kill.  7.  Fishing needs to have more varieties and/or a guide.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this better than the remakes that are coming out? There is some fun to be had for sure if you enjoy these games. It's not as boring as the older games. I really wish Steam had a middle of the road choice. I enjoy some of the quality of life things like being able to strafe. I did wait for a hefty sale. Here's my cons:*There is no reason to leave your farm other and going to the shops/museum/town hall (requests). There's an entire forest to the north with lake. However, there are no in-town beach foragables and no forest foragables. Everything is on your farm. Why leave?*You can't actually do much during festivals. Mini-games are something you do with sprites, and festivals are still mostly cut-scenes. I want to hunt for eggs myself!**The addition of "makers" is just an annoying way of crafting. This is one thing they took from Stardew and should have done differently. I don't want machines covering the entire farm, especially when this is the only area forageables spawn. Yes, you can sell items and new seeds show up - this is cool, but this eliminates a huge part of what I find fun.*You can't cook in batches. This is very annoying. *After all this time, being able to craft from chests should be mandatory in any new game! I'm sure I have a few more, but I expect I may get bored by the second year as I have with the previous SOS games. I'm not saying there aren't positives, but these are things I wish I new before purchasing.
