_childDocuments_.review: I was never able to play any of the Harvest Moon games when I was younger, but when I first picked up Friends of Mineral Town, I was hooked on the series. I bought the base Pioneers of Olive Town on the Switch, and decided to buy it on Steam for Christmas. The FPS is smooth as butter and everything looks great. I play with a PS5 controller and everything is very responsive.People criticize that everything is very automated; to an extent, it is, but *some* of that automation is optional. Do you like watering your crops every morning? Don't build any sprinklers. Do you like going and feeding your animals on rainy days? Keep your fodder in a chest or keep your animals in a not-upgraded facility to bypass the auto feeders. The harvest sprites can gather some materials for you each day, but what they bring back is random to an extent, and you're really just better off gathering whatever you need yourself.I will say I am a little disappointed in the rather flat characters and the fact that DLC dates can't come to festivals, but it's not really a game-killer for me personally. I love that gender doesn't matter at all except for having a child; I can wear skirts and dresses as a male character or chaps and pants as a female character. Townsfolk don't even refer to you as the gender you pick at the start, except for the one line the mayor gives you in the beginning when confirming your gender. Character customization is great with no gender-locked features, including voice and the way your character stands. I like the fact that the fatigue system is gone from FoMT, you don't have to buy 50 kitchen tools to cook meals, and you can remove all trees and rocks without forced tool upgrades (yes it takes more time, but it's still possible). I love that I can work out in my field in the rain without worrying about fatigue; I feel like I have more options than just being forced to go to the mines if I want to do literally anything on a rainy day. It's so much easier to raise your max stamina now: you buy stamina upgrades through the Harvest Goddess shrine and you get a couple through some minigames, as opposed to FoMT where you had to pray you could dig them up.I do kind of wish I had the option to put makers inside of buildings for the sake of convenience, but it's not a huge deal to me. I can just place my mayonnaise makers outside my coop, my butter, cheese, and yogurt makers outside of a cow barn, my yarn makers outside of a rabbit/sheep/alpaca barn, etc. I can understand where some people dislike the clutter with so many makers, though.All in all, I think it's a great version of Story of Seasons that took a little inspiration from Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing New Horizons with the specific crafting/land maintenance elements.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this, but I'd wait til its on sale. If you're a fan of the genre, then you'll enjoy this game. However, its no where near as polished as Stardew Valley which is embarrassing for a known video game company and says a lot about Eric Barone. Stardew Valley isn't perfect but the more I played this game, the more frustrated I became. If you wanna know more, read on.  You're extremely limited in placing furniture until you fully upgrade your house. You can buy a rug and bring it  home only to find it doesn't fit anywhere inside. You're left with lots of open empty spaces. Your house is full of these weird long display shelves which makes it look like a museum littered with dumb little items on display. I currently have the second to last house upgrade and can only hang TWO objects on  my walls. There's so much garbage that spawns all over the place every day. I absolutely hate it when it rains in this game because your farm is littered with puddles (and small ponds for some reason) which you have to use a bucket to get rid of. You must use a sickle to clear the hundreds of weeds. So many useless forage items. So many makers. There are over 40 of these things. They take up so much space. They're so slow. A huge portion of your farm has to be reserved specifically for all the makers you'll have and unless you're a completionist you'll probably only use like 6 of them. The crafting is such a grind. You need 20 orichalcum ingots for the final house upgrade. I spent like 15 mins in the mines, made it to the last level and came out with 6 ore which is enough for a single ingot. You do eventually unlock an additional area to mine orichalcum but it refreshes every few days and barely makes a difference. You can also buy them for 50k (or 40k depending on if you're playing on easy difficulty) an ore if you're made of money. I was hoping once I unlocked the Harvest Sprites, they'd make the gameplay a little less tedious like in previous games. Unfortunately, all they do is give you random items. They don't do anything useful like clear your farm of weeds, or water/harvest your crops, or collect items from your animals.

_childDocuments_.review: Best story of seasons I've played so far. Best graphics, best gameplay, and you can really feel the progression. Nearly 9 hours in and I'm still in the first season of the first year. There's so much to do and you'd get the feeling of not wanting to miss anything.          The game will not tell you what to do (it's a harvest moon game), rather it will give you hints on what you CAN do. Occasionally, the Mayor or a random NPC will come to visit you every morning to hint you on what event is coming or what Olive town is planning. Dialogue is good and the NPC's personalities are consistent. You can easily identify who's who from the first interactions. You can really feel the progression of the game because of different dialogues based on what events are to come. As you progress and help the town folks, even the town itself will change -- their shops, the color of buildings, the town mascot, and many more that I haven't experienced yet.           I'm still 9 hours in, but I can confidently say that it's a good, modern, and casual harvest moon game that you can pick up whenever you feel like dozing off after a work day or a mentally taxing school work.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played both the original Switch and the Steam versions of Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town, I am thoroughly impressed with how Marvelous has responded to feedback and criticism. This commitment to improvement gives me even more hope for future Story of Seasons releases.While the Switch version had its share of issues, I'd like to focus on the positives they've achieved with the Steam version. Firstly, while I understand the frustration about the lack of character icons, it’s worth noting that many beloved Harvest Moon/SoS titles, such as Tree of Tranquility, Animal Parade, and A Wonderful Life, also did not have these icons. I do appreciate that Marvelous then added a zoomed in version to the Steam version. It definitely adds another layer of immersion, but again, character portraits are not in EVERY HM title so I find it weird this was a main complaint. Speaking of Animal Parade, I find it disappointing to hear negative comments about Pioneers of Olive Town. To me, this game feels like the most authentic successor to Animal Parade we’ve had so far. From the art style to the city layout, it strongly evokes the charm of AP. Fingers crossed for a future SoS: AP release!Addressing some common criticisms: I’ve seen people say the characters are bland and the city is lackluster, but I strongly disagree. The characters are endearing, and if you don't initially find someone to your liking, the DLC introduces some delightful new characters. The city itself is charming, and I love the quests that allow you to improve it. There are plenty of cutscenes, ranging from romantic moments to scenes that develop the broader story, making you feel deeply involved in the characters’ lives.Compared to the other SoS titles, Pioneers of Olive Town offers many quality-of-life improvements. It maintains the heartwarming essence of Harvest Moon games—something that, in my opinion, sets it apart from other titles like Coral Island or Stardew Valley. Despite their appeal, nothing quite matches the unique storytelling and feel of a Harvest Moon game.I highly recommend this game. Supporting Marvelous means we’re more likely to see more remakes and new entries in this beloved series, which I know many of us are eagerly awaiting.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who has played a Story of Seasons game before knows the plot of Pioneers of Olive Town: an enterprising young 20-something escapes the bustle of city life and takes over their grandfather's old, dilapidated farm outside of a small, rural village that's struggling to keep its inhabitants entertained. To turn things around you grow crops, raise animals, talk to the townsfolk, and repeat. Pioneers of Olive Town isn't trying to change that, but it adds a huge amount of land to manage and crafting mechanics to work with, and that fleshes out that familiar loop into a full, pleasant take. For those of us who have been playing Stardew Valley non-stop for the last five years, it’s a much-needed refresh.Pioneers of Olive Town is stuffed with things to do, and while the seasons pass rather slowly, I was surprised at how much I was packing into a day – as well as how much more I still wanted to do at the end of each one. At any given point you're working toward rebuilding a structure, clearing a new segment of land, planning another excursion into one of multiple mines, saving for the purchase of a new tool upgrade, trying to finish a quest to develop the town, and trying to get the cute girl who works at the museum to come take a walk on the beach with you. It’s pretty standard stuff for the most part.The most dramatic differences separating Olive Town and prior Story of Seasons games are the materials and crafting systems, and the sheer scope of the farmland you have to clear. The former borrows heavily from (surprise!) Stardew Valley, teaching you new crafting recipes as you level up various skills like mining, fishing, and logging. This includes a number of recipes for machines that will convert materials into other materials, such as wood into lumber or ore into bars.It’s a hassle to have to fuss with machines instead of all the other, far more fun bits, like exploring the enormous farm I'd inherited.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: IMHO the best "official" Harvest Moon game ever made. A modern, vibrant update to one of the most loved casual farming sim series ever made. Expensive, but oh so worth it.I bought the game with the expansion pass, so my view is a bit skewed due to the volume of cut scenes and story branches that are offered even very early in the game.The game world is lush, vibrant, and seems very much alive. The NPC's are varied, cute, and there is definitely a lot of them to get to know, even in the base game. Thankfully, you can accept and fulfill commissions straight from the community board, 'cause I'd hate to chase them all down. They all have their various routines. Life goes on on with or without you, and there's nice touches like going to people's houses in the evening, and seeing the family sitting around the dining table having their evening meal.Cut scenes are well done, and very numerous, but that might be because of the expansion pass, I'm not sure. They range from light-hearted to darkly foreboding. Would love to talk about the later but want to keep this spoiler free as much as possible.Hard to say more than what is already written by others. For me it's very faithful to the series, but moving away from the 2-D pixel art into a more lush 3-D landscape and all the growing pains that come with it. It still has all the magic and charm, and is very much go-at-your own pace. Which you really need to do because there is so much to do in the game it can seem quite overwhelming if you push through it too hard. Just relax, enjoy the journey and steady progression at your own pace. It's truly the best way to embrace all that the game wants you to experience. I absolutely hate the idea of spending $50+ bucks for a friggin' video game, but it's now almost 5am, I'm totally exhausted, but can honestly say "yeah, it's worth it". I don't regret spending that one bit,  and hopefully you won't either.

_childDocuments_.review: This is both a yes and no kind of game. Polished but lazily assembled npc interactions, empty questline - this installment feels particularly half-hearted.  The farm keeps you busy, the game is easy to play and has a few fun features but I feel it's mostly a grind and lacks the charm of older titles - the main problem I have is the questline but also lack of fun details, including festivals like cooking. Despite being advertised as "freedom to do what you want", this game actually feels more limited than older games that had more of an open world.  Olive Town feels sterile and  lacks more complex gameplay and attention to little details that made older HM games so nice but there are a few fun features. CONTROLS / TECHNICAL: - Good music (weekend variations are great, especially autumn and winter) and sound effects BUT seasonal maps are no longer as beautiful / detailed as they used to be. I love changing seasons in older games.- extensive customisation options  with lovely colours  BUT female character is too flat-chested for me and I can't get the look I want. The only piece of clothing that looks any good is the wedding dress. EVENTS / CHARACTERS-  it’s great there are heart events for every level and 6 hearts are "friend events" (easier to avoid seeing romantic events you don’t want)  BUT characters are boring, lacklustre and not lovable. I don't  really have any bachelors I want to marry as a straight girl. There might be a lot of events, some of them are nice, but I just don't like any character, unlike in previous games where I had three or more favourites. Ralph's okayish and Ludus' events are nice but the lines aren't as lovely as they used to be in older games, and I'm just not feeling it, in fact the lines are limited and feel generic, with a few minor changes for every character.  instead of a BD dinner,  you get  a lazy greeting line. I do like that raising hearts extends beyond marriage but it's pointless when I don't enjoy it. It feels as if bots assembled the lines and that's it. They definitely cut corners on interactions in this game. -Clemens and Lars should have been eligible bachelors. Especially Clemens. And I like special marriage candidates but there none here (unless we count expanssion pass characters, but that's lazy) At least Beth and Lars are  a little cute. - lack of reverse proposals and dating is no longer a commitment. I'm also not fond of divorce but at least it's more like "reset" feature. That's okayish. I still prefer "change generation" mechanics instead (see Animal Parade)- Villagers are just as lacklustre as the marriage candidates - they may be diverse but they don’t have backstories or lines that would make them fun. It's boring, a lot of them are simply unlikeable. They no longer care if you run around in typhoons - a little detail that added  warmth to the bonding. I miss it. - I like romantic festivals but they are too short and there are not enough fun festivals like cooking. There's little use for your quality crops. Moreover, after 2 years in game, the festival announcements should change. They stay as if doing them for the first time - that's a problem here because they come to your house with elaborate speeches, unlike Mayor Thomas who kept things simple so repetition was acceptable. Here, these lines should change in year 2. - Wedding and child event are so so in this version. I prefer trio of towns standard - that was great.ACTIVITIES:- time flies sufficiently fast for there to be a challenge to the daily grind- many clothes to craft BUT they are as neutral / boring as they could make them and it's annoying. Only the wedding dress is worth crafting. It's the only piece of clothing that I'm happy with.  The updated clothes aren't nice for me, either. I want a dress. - mining is ok. It tries to mix mining points and traditional mining. It's not difficult but the  baddies in mines will drain your stamina so it adds a bit of challenge. I find it mediocre. I prefer either mining points or mines like in Friends of Mineral town. - camera returns from animal parade and here it combines critter catching and wild animal taming. This is one of the fun things about the game.  But shouldn't there be online features?  -I like the requirements for wild animals, It helps build the farm. -  it’s nice that cooking takes time, the dishes are quite nice. I still prefer assembling kitchen. I hate the laziness of this game.- The farm is nice, with lots of things to do but the world is hermetic, not as open as older games used to have, exploration and foraging are limited. Mounts are gimmicks, there's nowhere to take them. But I like the fact we start in a tent and get to scoop water from puddles - finding treasures is fun. I love new flower crops. - there is little flexibility with how you decorate your house. You really can't do much. Even pasting a map on the wall requires you to remove the fireplace. You can't put items on TABLES and you can't add more countertops! -I like using the upgraded tools andf the skill tree..- Fun reward system for titles and the titles are fun.- You gather earth sprites and manage them, having them help gives you freebies and sprite coins that you can use on items in sprite shop – some of them (like 10-star seeds) are useful  but I miss harvest sprites and harvest goddess. - You will unlock a spirit who live in the forest shrine. The shrine spirit will give you special blessings like unlocking gardens, raising stamina – this is nice. - special places to go when you unlock earth sprites, mostly places dedicated to gathering material and improving skills – I like that. Some are places with minigames. - The seasonal gardens are nice, the memory minigame is annoying here. Again, lack of exploration is a bummer. -I like quest board quest systems but here I don't like the characters so I'm not very compelled to do them. In fact, all characters could just be non-existent. I find them boring and mostly unlikeable.    - the gourmet quests must have been a last-minute addition, at least there's some use for all the high quality crops and dishes....because there's no cooking festival. - the premise about grandfather and pioneering promised something heartfelt BUT the main questline turned out to be empty- a tourist town, really? With golden tiles? That's not what harvest moon has always been about. - No long-term objectives like in older games. All in all, I can't say it's my favourite HM game. The writing lacks  the charm or sense of fun of the older games, a lot of features have not been thought through. It's the least likeable of harvest games I played. Even Harvest Moon: A tale of two towns was better (lots more to explore) and I wasn't fond of that one because its characters are just as forgettable as here. Well, HM games have always been uneven, not a single game does things 100% right. They either rush things or don't think things through, letting the series become a money grab, nothing more. I will not be so quick and eager to buy the next one. At least I can enjoy in peace and quiet all the better titles which are on console. I'll keep them forever., especially Trio of Towns. This title is pretty with some fun features but annoying in ways that made older HM games so lovely and enjoyable.  Fortunately, there are worthwhile indies out there, and old hm games where characters and activities are great from A to Z and make me want to spend time with them. Here, I just want to finish the achievements, uninstall and forget.

_childDocuments_.review: If you still have a 3DS go get Trio of Towns its still arguably the best "current" gen SoS/HM entry to date as this still has some teething issues much like the transition from A New Beginning to the first Story of Seasons titlted entry, if you are a veteran of Stardew Valley the Makers in this iteration should feel eerily reminiscent of what you are to expect from this game, just be thankful that they didnt use SoS' crafting mechanic and broke down the makers from that game into individual components, yes its a farming sim that mixes a bit of Stardew Valley, and Animal Crossing into the mix much like the 2 games you are given the option to freely decorate your farm as you see fit, much like Story of Seasons which based most of the building mechanics from A New Beginning your farm is your decorating playground. If you bought the Expansion pack of the game when I refer to Story of Seasons the people from Terracotta Oasis are from that game (Marian, Giorgio, Raeger and Iris). My only gripe is that the logic from both SoS and SoS:3oT are already there (namely a "free build mode") honestly it could benefit from that or being able to expose the blocks in your farm that you can build on (Trio of Town does this unlike the previous entry), if you are still hellbent on buying this game the main content is a bit lackluster much like "SoS1" your main job is to revitilize the town at least unlike SoS1 you arent forced to become a jack of all trades a master of none, as the questing system is based on Trio of Towns yes at least the townsfolk arent requesting items from you of a certain quality and quantity (this is precisely an issue when it comes to fishing) and would make requests that more or less be off season (a common example of this would be asking for 30 8* Sashimo Smelt in Summer), the only more specific requests comes from the resident gourmet Lovett but even his requests arent that much demanding assuming how much investment you have put into your farm and isnt really timed (provided you can get high quality ingredients, fishing is once again an issue due to RNG and inventory management and is a good enough of a cook you can do his quests easily kind of rewarding as well) but does have a little guess work at times. Also there's also my issue with the shipping bin once again an issue if you have laid nets all over the farm area you will get over loaded with items ASAP, the only thing that is helpful in this case is that they will only disappear if you sleep but the fact the townsfolk have no hated items yes you can even gift them a lowly junk from the farm and they will happily accept it so.... what better way to trash excess items but to give them to the villagers if you really want to trash items the mines are the better choice.Also this teething issues might be the result of long time SoS/HM Producer Hoshimoto Yoshifumi stepping down to prop up Neverland Co 2.0 AKA Hakama so we can get RF franchise back

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from someone who played the original Harvest Moon back on the SNES nearly 25 years or so years ago, I have liked being able to be a bit more industrial with my farm. Unlike more recent versions where you are given a tiny strip of land with limited options, this game gives the options to truly customise your land and choose how you want to make farm. While this does get a bit unruly when trying to harvest 1k+ crops on the same day, game does advance allowing for alot more automation and shortcuts than previously offered.That said, it's not without it's cons. The makers being placed everywhere are a pain to manage, previous comments upon having one building automating all of them (a factory perse) would have been a better way to go and interactions fall a bit flat (comments from spouse are doubtfully any different from that if the person wasn't married to you). The lack of being able to put things sideways and i'm still unsure why tourist don winter clothes but the locals don't during colder months...Finally it is a bit short, I got to the end credits twice within my first year and i've calculated 100% achievements will come likely midway through year 3.However this game is a bit of a change of pace from earlier games which focused abit much on story as a whole and I hope they keep on exploring and growing. A more polished version of this game alongside some more animals and a bit more story would make this one of my Harvest Moons/Story of Seasons of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Stardew Valley is strictly better.The game doesn't allow you to just hold down a button to continuously perform any of the many repetitive tasks that are the core game play loop (watering, hoeing, chopping trees, crushing rocks). There are other similar, very basic quality of life features missing.The DLC adds new villagers, but it adds them to a different zone you have to specifically travel to, so you never see them unless you go well out of your way. At most, you might want to get the one DLC pack with a new NPC you're interested in, but there's no reason to buy the rest of them.The villager dialogue alternates between boring and ridiculous (not in a fun way, a boring way). One of the major quest is some kids blackmailing you into letting them help you investigate a "ghost" (that part is fairly cute). Then, to progress the investigation, you need to get the kids yogurt. Because the kids, who aren't actually helping, want some. No. Just, no. The worst part is that the writing for the kids is some of the best in the game. Most of the time they're charmingly childish, which means the plot I just described is a high point in the game. How did a company with decades of experience making these games, many of them fantastic, make a game with worse dialogue and plot than a one man indie-studio?

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played  a  game since "A Wonderful Life" on Gamecube alongside the PS1 version of "Friends of Mineral Town" aka "Back to Nature". However I couldn't get this nagging mental itch of returning to the series out of my head recently, that is until now.  By the way the whole Natsume/Marvelous Inc. debacle ending up in a business 'divorce' then ultimately leading to the series changing its name is interesting, but I won't talk about that here. Getting back on topic I have to say that Pioneers of Olive Town just hits the spot. It's like the sensation of living abroad for a long time then getting to eat some comfort food that reminds you of home. Maybe its the gap from since I've last spent time with this series, but I think this franchise has generally moved in a positive direction from when I last played. Pioneers of Olive Town while not as deep as Stardew Valley with its gameplay options or cumulative amount of content still retains that irreplaceable  Story of Seasons  'vibe' while adding a lot more variety relative to the older classic games. I specifically mean having enough tasks you could be doing during a day without feeling totally overwhelmed. Although there's always some milestone or goal you can be working towards which keeps progression and the addictive gameplay loop going.On top of that I think Marvelous Inc. has learned quite a bit from Stardew Valley as well as Animal Crossing and incorporated a lot of gameplay ideas from those titles here. I can't speak for the release version of the game since I wasn't there for the aforementioned launch issues, but as it stands right now in 2023 Pioneers of Olive Town is a surprisingly good farming sim especially if you can get this on sale. The only slightly disappointing thing for me is that this game lacks dedicated character portraits for the NPCs, something I think would have added that bit extra to the game. Not that the characters are designed poorly mind you, but previous games had them and showcased some beautiful artwork that contrasted well with the overworld models.Anyways if you've missed the  Story of Seasons franchise you can safely come back and get that comfy 3D farming fix here with Pioneers of Olive Town.

I wish there were more character customization options, and I have always disliked that you look like a child even though you're of marrying age but all around it's a nice cozy game i'd happily play through multiple times.

I mean you can see the screenshots, nothing to write home about.If you came for the farming aspects and building your dream farm, it's what you could expect from a farming game. So the farming aspects is good as always. I always get addicted to these kinds of games, so, yeah. Also, I thought I would be able to decorate the town, but that's not something you do here. The town does "change" but you can't pick and choose. Most of the stores and establishments are already there when you start. You should just play their 3DS game "Harvest Moon:A New Beginning"? that had like the whole decorating the town and your farm, they had way more stuff there. Also there's like 2-3 ponds on your farm that you can't get rid of, so you gotta decorate and work your way around those.The story was something I really don't remember myself. All I remember is doing quests, that would show me a few cutscenes where people are like "yay, a new lamp post!" and that's about it. Sorry I don't remember much.Now, the romancing aspects...uh..I only saw the boys "heart" events(I don't know what you call them these days) so I could only speak for them. To be blunt they suck. _childDocuments_.review: Having only played one Harvest Moon/Story of Season game (Light of Hope), I was pleasantly surprised with this one as it was most certainly less grindy than LoH. Experienced in farming sim games, I took to this one like a duck to water, so it was easy to pick up and get into from the first moment I loaded it up. I played it for a week straight, sometimes 10-12 hours per day, and finished the main story, got married and fully upgraded the house.I love the artwork, the visuals during the cut scenes, and just everything about the game. I still haven't gotten into actually decorating the farm the way I want as I do with other games, so that's the next plan. If you're a fan of the series, or even this genre, I urge you to pick this up if you are on the fence about it. A definite "must play" in my book, and a new update, 1.1, is right around the corner.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, PoOT is not a very good Story of Seasons game. It is a Chinese sweatshop version of Story of Seasons, where 90% of the gameplay revolves around an endless cycle of grinding for raw materials, feeding them into a million different maker machines and waiting for them to churn out the processed materials you need to upgrade stuff, go to sleep, and repeat the next day. There's ♥♥♥♥ else to do because although the town and game world look pretty, they are small, empty and soulless. The townspeople don't even have a portrait when you talk to them. Their dialogue also starts repeating a few days into the game, and even when you do get new dialogue or heart events, these are some of the most generic, boring heart events yet. I don't know what this was, Marvelous, but you gotta get your ♥♥♥♥ together for the next game, because it seems to me that when you're not remaking one of your decades-old classics, you've forgotten how to make a good Story of Seasons game altogether.

_childDocuments_.review: I've owned this game for a couple days and managed 18 hours, I loved it so far but already have managed a few opinions.CONS:Dialogue - The dialogue is very repetitive when you're running around town trying to talk to different characters or spark a conversation with your love interest. One of the things that would've made this game very complete for me would've been in depth conversations where you're able to chat with them and choose different responses and have long conversations.Character - Characters seem really flat, they all have their own typical persona of being the witty character or the bad boy, or the cheerful type, but then that's all there really is to them, I wish there was more in depthness to them. It's fine if you leave it up to your own imagination but if you're not a very imaginative person these characters definitely fall flat, especially with there repetitive dialogue.Love and Friendship Progression - Building love and friendship is very repetitive, you simply talk to the character and gift them something of their liking every single day and build up their hearts until you're able to do events with them and actually get with them. This wouldn't be so bad if the conversations were more in depth. It gets very repetitive trying to level up friendship and relationship levels with them. I really hope this is improved.FARMINGWeeds and Grass - They grow back a lot and can be a pain, though I suppose thats the whole point of farming. I do wish there was some sort of in game item that could be sprayed on the grass to avoid that from happening or a setting to adjust how frequently weeds grow.PROSThis game is absolutely fun and there always seems to be something to do. You never run out and can take your time progressing and falling in love with the characters. The graphics and overall aesthetic of the game is to die for and really is what I found so attractive of the game in the first place. SUMMARYThe game would be perfect if it weren't for the cons listed above, specifically the ones listed above the farming ones. If they come out with another one I really hope they fix whats listed above because then I would love this game even more!

I can´t clear my farm, I can´t leave it nice and clean, there´s ALWAYS something growing everywhere and full of trees in no time. So tiring!! _childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town - is a "cozy life" game in which we play the role of a farmer who lives in a mysterious forest, he runs his own farm and more.Things that I liked:+ Interesting idea for a farm - It's cool that you made a farm and a forest in one. At the beginning, our farm or forest is quite small and this can be increased by asking the builder to build a bridge or remove an obstacle (as long as you have resources or money). While exploring the forest, you may come across: better trees, new animal species, new places to fish, new resources to collect in the forest, new caves, and the like. In the forest you can also find ruins of the buildings of the previous owner of this farm, which you can repair and use.+ Tasks and interesting rewards+ Great and easy character creator - in addition, at a later stage of the game you can change all the physical features of your characters.+ low requirements and energy-saving graphics (because it's a Nintendo Switch game after all).+ A lot of skills to learn - there are over 12!+ game friendly for everyoneThings that I average liked:> absurdly small city - It's nice that the city is small, but if you look closely you can see that the city is too small! Why is the playground called a park and the park a forest (which is smaller than our farm)? Why are the forester's hut, fisherman's hut and sanctuary too close to the city? This doesn't suit players!> little content in DLC - it's great that there are new NPCs, it's great that you can take part in new tasks, it's great that there are new areas and it's great that there are new outfits for players and NPCs and is that not enough? Unfortunately, definitely yes! Why are there no new things to obtain in new areas, such as crops, gemstones, fish, recipes for new dishes and the like? Additionally, these new NPCs as marriage candidates do not have the outfits from the DLC that have the NPCs from the base game.> mini games with Sprites - This is wasted potential. It's nice that we can play mini games with Sprites, but the rewards are quite small. Sprite coins (which can also be obtained in the village) and a one-time increase in maximum stamina? Why are there no unique items that can be obtained in mini games?> musical pieces - the music itself in this game, e.g. during the current season or while staying in the city and the like, is fine, but when it is, for example, a meeting with Ralph, the music becomes unbearable. I really can't listen to this music, it sounds more like an "action" game than a "cozy life" game. Fortunately, there are a few bits of unwanted music and they are quite rare.> choice of difficulty levels - in my opinion this is absurd and another wasted potential. It's okay to speed up the game with this option, but when you say that this option makes it easier to play, you are unfortunately wrong.Additionally, this option is not refined, for example: plants do not grow too fast thanks to this option or animals do not reproduce too quickly.> lack of automation and help in Barns and Hen Houses - there is automation in almost every game, but there is none here, apart from sprinklers and automatic feeders. The player has a huge farm, a lot of animals and has to obtain animal by-products on his own. For a player who has a lot of animals on the farm, it may be time-consuming. Why can't you build an automatic collector or hire someone to do the work for you? Fortunately, there are no penalties for not caring for animals for at least one day or more (I checked).Things I didn't like:- no multiplayer- the idea with Navi-Sprite - we players like it when we discover new areas and secrets on our own, to have the impression that the entire map is suitable for the players, but you preferred to go a different way and instead of making a standard, typical map like most in games, you you did the simplest thing that looks like it was taken from The Sims 4. I'm talking about forced teleportation using Navi-Sprit. I don't like this idea, the player has the impression that he has teleported several dozen kilometers away from his farm and again the player has the impression that this area is too small for him, and in addition, like Fisher's Island, apart from fishing (that are unique to this area) area) there is nothing else. And I know that this game is specially made for the Nintendo Switch, but I know a game that you probably don't know, it's The Sims 2 Castaway for PlayStation Portablet attention. It may not be your typical "Cozy Life" game, but it does it a lot better and it's rewarding to explore the areas. How can you so lazily ignore a typical standard map! A very experienced studio, but such a lazily made map!To sum up:This is not a perfect game and I thought for a long time whether to add it to positive or negative reviews. I played for quite a long time, I was looking for additional activities that the game offered, you can see that they tried their best, even though the game looks like it was their first production, I managed to create a dream character, the game will no longer be supported and is it worth the price even though it is an experienced studio? Ok, I'll spare it to you. I will give this a positive rating and ask you (if you are reading this) to come back to this game. Make an update that fixes your mistakes because this game still has some potential and not that you will make more games. Because honestly, I like this game and I want more updates to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I don't review games until I've beaten them, but there's not a whole lot to "beat" here so I'll just go ahead and start talking about my thoughts at the point I'm at, which as of writing is early in Fall 1.I'm overall not very impressed with anything Story of Seasons: Olive Town has to offer, and it's really disappointing that that's the case. This is my first Story of Seasons game so any adjustments from previous games are lost on me, my main comparison here is to my time in Stardew Valley.The first biggest thing to me is the customization of your farm. For one the farm is absolutely massive which itself is an issue, but much of this massive space consists of tiles that you cannot interact with at all. No tilling for growing crops, no placing down paths or lamps or farm facilities, just weird oblong shaped terrain that limits the amount of usable space and makes creating aesthetically pleasing farms more difficult than I'm willing to put in effort for. Every time I think of an interesting idea for my farm, I'm denied by being too close to some edge or wall that won't accept path.What can go in these empty spots, however, is all the garbage that spawns on your farm every day. It's impossible to keep your farm clean without wasting half your day clearing out the trees, weeds, puddles, and random crap that pops up. And a lot of that random crap is kind of important, as there's no way to plant your own basic trees or grass to set up a sustainable farm for them. So you basically just have a lot of encroaching nature making a mess of the place and you can do nothing to stop it, and you're encouraged to let it go so you can get the resources you need to expand.There are also a lot of systems that I just don't fully understand. Seed makers seem important but they take forever to process seeds, which feels like it makes them very inefficient vs. just buying basic seeds from the shop. Makers in general take up a lot of space and are very obtuse about telling you how much is ready to collect at any given time, but are all absolutely required to continue progressing your equipment and building up the town. Except the essence maker I guess.Speaking of the town the NPCs all look very diverse... but when interacted with have basically nothing to say, especially when there's an upcoming event. Maybe getting more of the "special events" with them will flesh out their characters more, but that takes a lot of dedicated talking and gift giving to start getting those, and gifting especially feels obtuse and pointlessly expensive. Basically the NPCs all look pretty nice but feel like they have no character outside of their designated "type" which makes interacting with them less interesting than an Animal Crossing New Horizons villager. I could probably go on for a while about all the nitpicks I have, but those are probably some of the bigger issues I have with it. Will I keep playing? Probably. Would I suggest this game to anyone? Likely not, especially when Stardew exists which costs less, looks better, offers an overall better experience, and supports mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town is a delightful farming simulation game that exceeded my expectations. From its charming characters to its immersive game play, this game offers a truly captivating experience for new and seasoned players.One of the highlights of this game is its beautifully designed world. The picturesque town of Olive Town is brought to life with stunning visuals, vibrant colors, and rich attention to detail. Whether the rolling green fields, the bustling marketplace, or the serene riverbank, every location feels alive and brimming with personality.The game's cast of characters is equally captivating. Each character has a unique story and personality, from the friendly townsfolk to the potential love interests. Interacting with them adds depth to the game and creates a sense of community and friendship, making every day in Olive Town feel special.The farming mechanics in Pioneers of Olive Town are incredibly satisfying. From tending to crops, raising livestock, exploring the wilderness, and foraging for resources, there is always something to do on your farm. The gameplay is easy to learn but offers enough depth to keep you engaged for hours. Adding new farm animals and crop varieties adds further excitement and variety to the experience.Furthermore, the game introduces numerous activities and events to keep you entertained. Whether it's participating in festivals, fishing, cooking, or even mining for precious gems, there is a wide range of activities outside of farming. These diversions add a welcome layer of variety and make every day in Olive Town feel different and exciting.The level of customization in Pioneers of Olive Town is exceptional. From designing and expanding your farm to decorating your home, countless options exist to personalize your surroundings. Whether you prefer a quaint countryside aesthetic or a modern farm, the game allows you to express your creativity and create a space that truly feels like your own.The developers have also done a fantastic job listening to player feedback and continuously updating the game. With regular patches and improvements, they have shown a commitment to enhancing the player experience and addressing any issues.In conclusion, Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town is an outstanding farming simulation game that captivates with its charming world, lovable characters, immersive game play, and extensive customization options. It offers a delightful and addictive experience that will keep you returning for more. Pioneers of Olive Town is an absolute must-play if you're a genre fan or simply looking for a game that will whisk you to a peaceful and fulfilling virtual farm life.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons is a very relaxing and simple farming game where you are not rushed to do anything. Letting you do whatever you want at your own pace. For me, I managed to complete the main story line on the last week of Fall. So not even a full year passed. However there is still a lot of end game stuff to do that I am still working on.The Farm is broken up into three sections that you are able to unlock later and get new and better resources from. You almost never have to worry about running out of resources as trees, rocks, and grass grow back WAY to fast. Even in places you rather they not grow back. Though it is a pain to get all the way to the end, mounts help speed things along. Each zone you are able to plant seasonal crops, get new buildings and craftable items, go into mines, and place buildings down for chickens, cows, goats, sheep, and rabbits. Though you are able to place down quite a bit of items on your farm, the restrictions to where you can place them can be tricky. If the land slopes just a little, you cannot place anything on that tile. Crafting machines are annoying since they take up 4 units where they could easily take up just one. Meaning you are going to need to set aside a large area just to craft resources.The Town layout is very simple to navigate and find where everything is. I quite enjoyed the town design, the shops, and "most" of the villagers that you interact with. The town has a lot of diversity to it, making it feel like everyone is welcome.Your house is probably the most annoying part of the game. You start off in a tent which can be upgraded to a tier 3 house. Tier 1 and 2 for the house barely give you any room to place furniture or decorations. So I just ignored decorating until I got the house fully upgraded. The final tier finally gives you a lot of room to customize and place down items, but you are unable to rotate furniture. I can't understand why this is not a function in the game... Really the only thing I enjoy about the house is that it allows you to have multiple pets. Cats or dogs.Overall the game is simple, easy, and enjoyable. Something you can sit down, turn your brain off, and relax with a bit of comedy from some of the villagers.

_childDocuments_.review: Pioneers of Olive Town is a bit different when it comes to the Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon series. This game very much feels like a weird hybrid of Story of Seasons mixed with Stardew Valley, and I mean that in a good way. The game has very adorable graphics, even if they are a little awkward at times, and I have the funnest time playing it. My biggest praise about this game is its cooking system and Lovel's challenges. Those were so fun to do, and it's nice to an expanded cooking system in a farming sim styled game. The game is hardly perfect with me spending much more time than I'd like try to pick up items or harvest crops. I also have an issue with you how you have all this customization for the farm, but it falls flat because the 3D graphics are awkward for trying to do that... The farm can become overwhelming cluttered because everything just grows back, and while that's nice to needing materials, it can get out of hand if you aren't able to cover everything with pathways to prevent as such (which is a LOT of materials and time to do), and that's not including all the machines and farm buildings. But I digress. These are just a few nitpicks that don't take away from how fun the game is!If you like games that are very much about growing crops and plant trees, building stuff, cooking, having a family, a little bit of customization, and light mining, then this game is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very cute game with great graphics and if you like Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia, you will surely enjoy it. The only issue I have with this game is that it is way too grindy. It takes basically all day to just do the same chores every day and there are way too many machines/makers that clutter up your farm. I wish there was a building to put them all into to make it look less ugly with all the machines standing around. There are just too many that are too specific. In the end you spend all day re-filling the machines and putting things into chests as there is zero automation and no sorting system. It leaves very little time to go exploring and mining for resources or just talking to villagers. The way My Time at Portia handles this by letting you own a Warehouse eventually that automates processes is much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Generally an enjoyable game so far, similar to other Story of Seasons games and Stardew Valley, though in my opinion, lack depth in a few aspects. Gameplay is fun most of the time, the town is lively and interesting. The only thing that put me off is the concept of Makers ( which is basically machines that turn your resources into products). Though it simplifies the production aspect, it feels boring to see multiple machines that look almost identical to each other ( really they are just boxes with a logo on top to tell you what product they produce). This makes customization of your farm more neat and tidy, but so uninteresting to look at. Also, the time to produce products on those machine is so long I feel like the dev did that on purpose to prolong a kinda short game. In short, if you want some quick fun for 1 or 2 weeks, this is a game for you, if you;re looking for a game with more customization and an in depth experience, then I suggest going back to the good old ones or wait a bit longer because this year is going to be farming sim heaven : )))

_childDocuments_.review: I will begin by saying this game is a grind. Something that could be done in two steps, for instance, could take three or four. This can feel a little frustrating at first if  you're like me, riding the wave of nostalgia and looking for that good ol' Harvest Moon fix. But in my experience this feeling faded quickly the more I played. I began to enjoy that there is always something to do and that there is no longer a big pause at the "end" of your duties (you know, when you'd hit the hay at 2pm because even with more hearts you couldn't do anything). This has quickly become my quiet hyper-focus game, where I can satisfy my brain with organization and steady task flow to fulfill that need to constantly be on the move. It's also very relaxing, both in ambiance from the music/nature and the simplicity of the life your character is living. So, if you're looking for a game that doesn't take up a lot of space, has cute design, decent graphics and provides an ever-growing list of tasks to do, to keep you busy this is the game for you! I highly suggest giving it a try :)

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!!! I think it's a great mix between Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, and Animal Crossing: NH. It's got a good pace for the story line and the days.  I like that there is so much to do.  It's not like some games that you play for 30 hours and it's practically over. I've played for 70 hours now and there is still so much to do. I've had a hard time looking for Harvest Moon like games that I liked and I think this game took that concept and added so many other great ideas that worked from other games and made this masterpiece. There are a few things that are annoying but overall it's definitely worth what I payed for it.Pros:+Farming is fantastic (lots of different crops & flowers, sprinklers help a ton, get a seed maker so you don't have to buy seeds)+Animals are cute and plentiful both for the farm and pets (You find some of them for free in the beginning so you don't have to save up to buy them. Loved that! There are many different dogs, cats, and special pets and you can have more than one as you progress.)+Very spacious farm and can move most buildings that are on the farm if you don't like the placement.+Cooking (lots of recipes and there are cooking challenges that have some nice rewards.)+Mining is fairly easy, not too many annoying enemies (moles that come out the ground) getting in the way like Stardew did.+No wait time for tool or building upgrades (That was something that really bugged me with some games is you had to plan on your tool being out of commission or wait for the barn to be built, but you don't have to wait on this game.)+Doesn't end too fast. (I know I've said that earlier, but it really is nice that it's got plenty of game to play and doesn't get boring after a few hours.)+You can increase your max health.+The marriage candidates were great and diverse.+I like the characters, dialogue, and plot. It's cute and fun. (I know some people were complaining about how few characters there are and how repetitive or goofy some of the dialogue is but I thought it was good.) If you have too many characters it's hard to befriend them or get around to talking to all of them. I think it was the right amount of people. As far as the dialogue goes, it's clean, wholesome, and not too serious subject matter. Both children and adults can enjoy. We don't have to be bombarded with serious adult responsibilities or relationship issues in every game we play.  That's what makes this relaxing.Cons:-Grass, puddles, trees, and stones spawn too much. It's impossible to keep the farm clean.-It's kinda hard to keep any money in your pocket, especially in the 1st year. Although, I may hoard too many grown crops.-So many makers that take too long to make anything-Not much town to explore. I wish some more of the town improvements expanded the town. But it's not bad as is.-No elevator in the mine or anything to get down to pre-explored levels quicker without hurting yourself.  It takes me most of the day to get to the bottom of one of the mines (which is where a lot of the gemstones are) Then you have to start all over next time you go in. -So many items that need to be stored, not enough storage.  I mean you can make tons of storage boxes without using too many resources, but having to have a place for those boxes somewhat close to the house and keeping track of what's in what can be a pain. I think the reason it piles up so quickly is how many levels there are. Maybe if there was just 3 stars instead of 10?-The decorating portion of your house is ridiculously small even though it looks like you should have so much more house to decorate.Overall I really like it. Actually, I rarely write reviews for anything, but I liked this so much I felt like it should be recommended.

Played SoS: Trio of Towns on my 3DS as a teen and loved the heck out of it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is great overall but has some areas to improve. This is now my favorite 'Harvest Moon' game. (Magical Melody is my 2nd, HM64 3rd)The Pros:* Crafting system* Unlockable areas are meaningful* Pretty much every avenue of revenue is good (some require more or less effort)* Camera mode and full 3d environment enhance the visuals dramatically* The graphics are better than other 'harvest moon' games* The game keeps you occupied for MANY hoursThe Usual:* There are some bugs here and there, but no more or less than your average game.The Cons: * Accessibility features are implemented at a minimum. Compare the controls of stardew valley to this game, and stardew simply blows it out the water.* Graphics COULD be improved even more. I'm thinking more animations for smoother player movement and special effects could have made the game even BETTER!---SPOILER ALERT---* The baby system is nonsense. You find a baby in the woods instead of getting your wife pregnant... I understand the baby in the woods thing makes sense for non-binary, but it makes no sense for traditional couples. On the same token, animals have traditional births but wives do not? Makes no sense. If we are going to add non-traditional game content, that DOES NOT mean remove traditional game content.(IE: Add a choice at marriage, Are you a non-traditional couple?)

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Harvest Moon fan, I love this series. Yeah so the name changed but the nostalgic feelings have not. I found it very cutesy and relaxing. No feeling of being pressed for time. The town layout is nice and convenient. There are different stores to explore and areas, especially with the DLC. There are lots of different crops to grow and easy access to mines. With DLC there is a boat right next to your house to travel to DLC islands. A sprite eventually stations next to the house for convenience as well. Crafting is inexpensive when you do it yourself as long as you have patience for labourous collection. I am 16 hours in and only a few days into Summer of the first year and I am still finding it very enjoyable. The festivals are not as interactive as some games but this is a harvest moon game (the old HM not the one with the current name but crap graphics), so they are very much on par with older versions. There is a wide variety of bachelors/bachelorettes, once again especially with DLC: different looks, interests and personalities. I would definitely recommend this game to my fellow HM of old followers. Thanks for an enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Is Pioneers of Olive Town perfect? No. The game has a number of minor flaws that come together to damage the overall experience. That said, I'd give it a solid 3 out of 5 and recommend it to anyone who has enjoyed other Story of Seasons/ Harvest Moon games or games like Stardew Valley.The Good:Fun characters to get to know and a nice setting to explore and enjoy.Nice variety of activities from fishing to mining, farming and ranching.A number of nice simplifications, some might consider it dumbing down, but do you really need a brush, shears, milker, etc clogging up your inventory?Enough novelty from other SoS games to make it feel unique while still having that solid SoS feeling to it.The Bad:Too many makers take up too much space. Did we need a condiment maker solely for vinegar, olive oil, and soy sauce? Couldn't that cover salt, pepper, and sugar to? Yarn and thread makers? Cloth and textile makers? The list goes on, and each one take up a bit of space.Different stars of crops, fish, animal products, EVERYTHING with stars, doesn't stack. One star different of the same crop? Different stack. Gets really annoying with the next big con.Limited shipping container space? Who thought this was okay? Why? I'm guessing this was overlooked in testing. The fact nothing stacks also makes this so much worse.Too many barn animals, not enough coop animals. Rabbits in the barn? Why not put them in the coop? Then you add brown cows, gray alpacas, gray rabbits, black cows, buffalo, I haven't even mentioned goats or sheep yet.Middling:The town development projects feel a bit too easy to complete. By the Autumn of your first year you'll probably be almost done, at worst. You can easily complete them all by the end of your first year.The town development projects feel a bit too... nothing, with little real changes or benefits to the player. I know it's about helping Olive Town, but give us more than a clothing store and salon, and one new character.Olive Town is a little small. Not that big of a deal, but there are hints (looking at you roadblock sign on the mountain) that it could have much more.Like I said, not perfect, and those flaws could turn off some people. Overall I do recommend it though. Full price, maybe not, but definitely if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been really enjoying this game for the past few days since I started playing it. But I've found that it can be incredibly tedious compared to titles like Stardew Valley (it's going to get compared to Stardew Valley at every opportunity so may as-well bring it up)In my opinion, Marvellous have seen what they did with Stardew and said to themselves, we can do that too! Just not as well which is a shame because honestly I love most of the farming sims they put out. But I'll go into more detail/ First lets cover the good stuff. 1. The graphics are lovely and really fit the style they were going for. There are a wide range of diverse characters who all have their own purpose in the town. 2. The addition of sprinklers has made the farming aspect a little less tedious3. You can now level skills and unlock rewards for doing so. 4. Customisation of your character and ability to make new clothes which I love! The not so good1. The makers are incredibly tedious, you have to click on each one and select the amount and then run it to get them to start and you will need A LOT of makers to make any semblence of progression towards the end game buildings. Also you can't place makers on top of paths which I only found out after I placed a whole area down for my ingot makers. 2. I now hate when it rains because of the puddles I have to clear whenever it does. I woke up one morning to find 2 puddles in my cow pasture which I had to clear and it's just annoying. 3. This game was clearly not made originally for the PC and it shows in the UI. When you want to turn the volume down you have to spam your mouse button until it reaches zero. For some reason some menus require you to right click to back out of them and some require you to press E which makes no sense. It's a small thing but just gets annoying. 4. The customisation of your farm needs to be fixed. You can't place anything on near bridges or the edge of any land which means I can't get a lovely path leading from my bridge to other parts of my farm and it really annoys me. I actually looked to see if anyone modded it as I am desperate to make my farm look nice. 5. NPC's have like 5 lines and my husband Ralph keeps telling me how great Beth is at her job and it's just innapropriate and needs to stop xD6. I thought the sprites might help with farming but they don't, you just go to the earth sprite village every so often and they give you stuff. 7. I wish there was a way to stop things growing in certain parts of your farm. I'm a bit tired of clearing new trees out of my animal pastures. I think all this can be improved on with some updates, I'll might still play it but at the moment it's just so grindy trying to get the stuff for the final buildings. I've still enjoyed the game though so I can recommend it :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun to play. I like the design. I'm not too bothered by the lack of portraits, but it sure is a big change. There are many quality of life changes like no longer needing a brush or milker to care for animals.The feature of this game is mainly about Makers. That means, most of your efforts will be spent in gathering, mining, logging, crafting, manufacturing, and refining materials. Cooking spends in game minutes, usually 15. I don't think it is as complex as SOS1, but it definitely has its own charm. I wish they could have added factories where you can place makers since a 2x2 object with 1 tile edge padding takes up space.Farm edit is not as extensive as the first SOS, but it's alright. I like the Farm size. You basically grow the area by "pioneering". You may gain access to new areas by buying them or by providing materials that you can gather from the previous area. Basically, you need more farm area in order to produce more because makers, barns, coops, and crops occupy land. Oh, and some farm facilities you must "repair" in order to access rather than buy. The first few farm animals are free as well. There are a lot of stuff you can get in this game without relying on money.There are other special areas that will be made available as you progress in the game. It's not many, but I think that's a good thing in itself. I won't have to go around a whole mountain or valley like SOS 1 just to meet with Elise who owns an orchard in the mountain and lives in a villa with its exclusive loading area. Everyone is usually just in town and your farm is just around 3 plots of considerable land area with special areas to visit.Overall, I think it's an SOS game with a different taste. I like it the way it is.And Linh best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 8/10, I want to be able to marry like all of the unmarryable candidates, and would give 10/10 if the cutscenes were more elaborate in terms of animations and choices in dialogue that actually affected things.Also, DLC: 5/10, felt like cash grab, characters and locations added nothing, but job board stuff was pretty fun.To start off, I love this game. After playing a good number of games since Harvest Moon AWL, I can say that this one has the most long-term playability outside of the relationships. Having so many skills to level up (that gave you things that aren't just "better stamina!") and so much to perform in and do and goals to meet really makes my gameplay experience awesome and I drown in the satisfaction it gives me every time I sit down to play. As a mostly-completionist (no, I will not marry every candidate just to complete), this game makes me very, very happy. As for things I would really like to see from the game, I have mostly comments in the social aspect and town aspect. ***BIGGEST GRIPE: I want to be able to choose my sexuality!! Really, just have a prompt that asks if you like boys, girls, or both. I don't like playing a straight or gay character and having everyone just assume I'm in to everyone. Moving on...I love LOVE that actual tourists show up: But they have a terrible case of cryptid-face and I think could use dialogue improvements. Villagers in the game, while I really love how most of their dialogue actually sounds like human speech as opposed to an army of robots, are not super interactable outside of clicking on them a lot. They don't even change outfits! Heck, Tree of Tranquility did that. Anything to breathe just that little bit more of life in to the characters (but I looove that everyone gets cutscenes! Definitely fleshes them out and makes them feel special!) Also, I want the current marriage candidates to be involved in more general goings-on cutscenes to make them feel like I should even care about them. Which leads to my next point...I want to marry Jacopo. He is so relatable, he is in every cutscene (even some of your love interests' cutscenes!), and I am just. So sad. If ANY DLC official or not comes out where I can marry at least him (though I also want Beth, Lars, and Clemens to be on the table Beth is just so damn CUTE), I will pay dat money. Which leads me to my final point...I was not impressed with the DLC. The characters and the extra islands are useless except to drag money out of people who just want to marry their favorites again in another town. The islands offer literally nothing but weird colonies of what feel like aliens on another planet that you can't interact with and have no bearing at all on the town. Big boo. As for the mystery files, it was veerrryyy hoky and I would LIKE to see my character interact with someone OTHER than Mikey and Cindy for once, but the overall goals made me actually use the job board and the idea itself was cute. Also, doing things for the Harvest Sprites (tho they are FREAKY) was fun. Overall, the DLC gets like a 5/10, saved only by the mystery files (I wasn't really in it for the outfits). Hope this helps, thanks for reading and IF YOU MAKE THAT DLC I WILL BE HERE JUST SAYING

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly great, a nice edition to the story of seasons series. This is the kind of game you can sit back and relax playing after getting tilted in some other competitive game. The core love interest are of varying personalities so you certainly have room to pick a favorite, some of their events can be a little dull depending on your taste but when you think about it, this is a small town you're helping develop. That said, it isn't without its faults here.* I wish the main storyline had more bearing or more challenge. I recall in other games how they told you if you don't earn x amount in two years the town will be taken down or how fully developing character relationships will save the town. It's a little boring that you could complete the main quest without much effort* The DLC love interest are basically a pet. They have no interaction with the town, its people and they dont participate in events I'd like to see Raeger in discussion with Mitsuki about cooking or Neil talking to Ralph about animals or at the very least be with my spouse watching fireworks and lanters. Olive town is trying to attract tourists right? Why not the inhabitants of the other islands? Hopefully they add this in an update, otherwise there wasn't really much of a point to them. It is a good game, at base but has so much more potential and possible story to add. I commend the SoS team for the excellence of this original title and hope for more.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoy this game, Story of Seasons PoOT has a lot of interesting mechanics. The different makers can add up and sometimes be alittle overwhelming. I have played Games like this since Harvest Moon AWL, I can say as a whole the games have grown and gotten better, This new take on repairing the town and your farm are nice and add to the purpose of the game. This game really gives you alot to do which is nice as sometimes just farming and visiting villagers can get repetitive. The size of your farm is great it gives you lots of space to move your buildings around and expand your farming space. You can do alot of interesting this with the layouts and its quite satisfying. If you have enjoyed theses games for years or are new to the series I feel you will find great joy here.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a fun and cute little game that is great if you're looking for something relatively mindless and cheery to spend some time with. It's not without flaws, however.The great:- lighthearted atmosphere and style makes it a great chill game- simple mechanics lets you turn off your brain and just relax- the villagers are cute, although it's sad that my favorite (beth) isn't romanceable- easy to track and achieve goals makes it feel like you're making meaningful progress from the get goThe not so great:- the menus for both donating to the museum and appraising an item at the museum are awful and actively deter me from doing that entire mechanic- the tool bag is an excellent idea, I only wish there was a quick way to return items to the bag without having to grab it and drag it back to the bag every time- the placement of items feels a little weird and makes it hard for me to lay out the many lumber machines I have in a way that doesn't look haphazardOverall it's great fun, I'm still engaged with it and will keep playing it. There's just a few things I'd love to see improved mostly from a QOL aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: STORY OF SEASONS: Pioneers of Olive Town

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big SoS and HM fan. I like that they've gone a little outside their comfort zone with this one, but while some things are an improvement, others didn't work for me.Pros:-there are no "disliked" gifts so you can play the game without having a wiki open-you can romance everyone. EVERYONE. Same sex marriage? Yes. Harem playthrough? You bet. (You can only marry one person and you can't divorce them, but that's fine)-I like the rebuilding an old farm aspect (like Stardew, yes), and i think the range of animals you can have is super nice-being able to upgrade your town gives you more to do than just romance and farming-you can easily sink a ton of hours into it. if you like farming sims, you'll definitely get your money's worthCons:-character stories are often lack-luster. While you CAN romance everyone to see their stories, you'll find yourself uninterested in a few characters if you're like me. I wish these characters had the depth of the ones of Rune Factory 4-i little too much grinding for resources and managing your manufacturing devices. feels a little to management simulator heavy than farming sim heavy-no character portraits. bring those back please (turning on chat view does help a little, though)overall, it's a fun game and besides the little gripes its very fun. I haven't come across any glitches so far. everything runs very smoothly

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful and relaxing game, great to play after coming home from work to unwind from stress.Also, THE ANIMALS DON'T DIE!! So you won't have to worry about your first ever animal dying and have to watch a sad cut scene. There's NO depressing factors in this game whatsoever ~ just cute animals & happiness. If you played harvest moon a/another wonderful life on the GameCube, this game is similar because it has mining and you can find artifacts. It's also a lot like animal crossing with fishing and having a museum that you can donate stuff to. If you're hesitant on buying this, don't be and just get it. You won't regret it, I promise. It runs great on PC, and you'll get A LOT of hours into this game. I'm almost 10 hours in and I'm still in Spring. (No, I never paused the game for a while either, these are strictly gameplay hours)I never pin games to my task bar, but this game I had to. It has a cute little buffalo as the icon. Everything about this game is so cute and friendly, JUST GET IT!!

_childDocuments_.review: 6.7 hours in my first sitting, can say that i quite enjoyed it.It feels a bit "empty" with no voice acting though, but that might just be because it reminds me of My Time At Portia in ways, and that has voice acting.The game is basically My Time At Portia meets Stardew Valley...except it's Harvest Moon, apparently. Edit after many more hours in:Negatives:I must say though that the house decorating....is attrocious and they should be ashamed.The placing is so damn limited it is infuriating, and you cannot even place things ontop of other Floor based things, like, got a new rug you want to put under your table? well tough ♥♥♥♥, you can't...yea that is Really stupid.And i don't mean the Starting table that you cannot move no no no no, i mean under a Table YOU placed yourself, chairs, bookshelves etc etc, it's either those OR a rug, not both.And on the outside if you want to have your farms and Makers (those that you use to craft certain things) are so far apart that it just looks weird and takes up needless amount of space and is infuriating when trying to add a Fence around your animal coops and you gotta fence around the entier damn building...yea it looks dumb.There is absolutely no point in building a Stable to get a Mount, since your Bike will have been repaired before you even gotten around to bothering rebuilding the stable...not that you need a mount to begin with anyways, the island is tiny (unless the path above the town that i haven't unlocked yet opens up the map to 3 times the size...but i doubt that)The cow is WAY too damn big, like, my god it is twice if not three times your size!Yes i know cows are big in real life, but jesus! come on...Every single store has it's own Closed day, which honestly is infuriating and makes absolutely NO sense.Every day of the week, 1 - 2 stores will be Closed for whatever reason, and it's just stupid.I am not saying that it's unheard of for some stores to have a certain day of the week to be closed, but ALL of them on the isle??? What even.But besides those gripes, i do enjoy it.The game has A lot of room for improvements, like the character creation, like, c'mon, really?And i cannot wait to see what becomes of it.Edit: Nothing came of it, they left it to Die...

_childDocuments_.review: Creating friendships one stone at a time, as I barge in people's houses at night while they're having their dinner, then giving them presents from the stones you mined earlier, happily accepting it with no complaints as if it was normal. then doing it again the next day. Yeah, If only building relationships in real life is as easy as giving stones or grass daily. Jokes aside this game is fantastic, Story of seasons PoOT is a game you will enjoy if you simply love the farming sim genre. The game is very grindy but rewarding. The story is very simple, the characters are well designed and the music is very relaxing, with the exception of character events, The music played during those events is amazing. Although I was a bit let down by the DLC, aside from adding new characters and new marriage candidates, they add nothing new to the game. It would have been nice if the DLC added something that is unique to the place like a game mechanic or items and live stocks or such that can only be found with each DLC. Overall I would still recommend it if you love this series.
