_childDocuments_.review: The game is good quality and while it's a little expensive, I believe it's worth it. There are a few things that I don't really like about the game which I will mention, but overall I think the game stands its ground against games like Stardew, Rune Factory, and Harvest Moon. Some positives about the game:- Great graphics. A very cute 3D game with bright colors and adorable characters!- Ability to personalize. The main character that you control can be male or female, and you choose what they look like.- Farming mechanics. Great mechanics and feels heavily like Stardew,  - Diverse characters. There's all kinds of characters and each one feels different from the next. - Decent story events. The story (Or at least the events that happen that seem like little stories) is cute, but not exactly intrusive or entirely necessary. You aren't forced to finish a story line to get into the next area like Rune Factory, but instead it's more like pleasant little events that give you something extra. Now to things that are lacking/could be improved:- Machine timing. The machines you get are relatively balanced, but oh my word the Seed Maker is by far the most horrendous out of all the others. It takes 23 hours to make one set of seeds. Now I would understand that if you had an extremely valuable crop inside, but I had potatoes, which are one of the cheaper crops, in the seed maker. I think that while this item is quite handy and useful, it takes a while to even receive it and also get the items to make it. It was extremely disappointing when I saw how long it would take for just 2 bags of potato seeds.- The roads. The roads are adorable and cheap, however I would like to be able to place the makers on top of the roads, and have it act more like a floor so that way you can avoid grass and puddles making a mess of your machine area.- The regrowth of items. Trees, grass, and rocks pop up at random in the spaces. While this is handy in some cases, it's also very annoying when you are trying to have a clean looking farm. It would be far better if trees dropped seeds which could be planted just like your specialty trees, and other trees would grow around these planted ones instead of appearing out of nowhere. Same with the grass. Rocks could show up around the mines as they do now, and not around the farm again seemingly out of nowhere. This would give people like me the satisfaction of having clean farm areas with spaces to grow the grass and trees. - Outfits/hair/facial features. While it's super awesome that there is customization, the selections of hair are fairly limited and so are the facial features. The outfits have a modest amount of variety but I would love to have more. While I'd like to have more variety, this one doesn't matter too much as there's enough styles for almost anyone to find at least one style that they like. While there's a few things that could be added/changed to make the game more satisfying and pleasing to the eye, the game as it is now is fun and enjoyable for those who enjoy a calm, peaceful farming game.

_childDocuments_.review: 11 hours in and I'm enjoying this game. I have played a lot of farming and simulation games on different consoles so I have been quite interested in this for some time. I also did a lot of research as per reviews and I saw some comments about the lack of good dialogues or script for the NPCs as you develop your relationship with them. But overall, it's such a fun, and creative game where you can customize a lot of things especially when it comes to your farm and character (which I really love).Pros:•Customization•Variety of every stuff (animals, pets, etc)•No pressure when it comes to collecting cut scenes and developing relationship with NPCs as it is alright if you're too busy with farming or fixing your farm•A lot of opportunities to earn money other than what's within your farm•I like the random cut scenes of the townspeople•Time does not pass on most cut scenes (other than festivals)•etc.. (there's too many stuff I like to list at once)Cons•There's no new dialogue when you get closer to NPCs (especially Bachelor/ettes) I really love talking to the NPCs everyday when I see them having new dialogues every time we get closer like in other titles (FoMT Gray, Cliff, and Mary/Marie blushing gives me life)•Too much reliance on makers (machines where u put stuff to turn them into another type of stuff e.g. egg into mayo, clay into bricks)•Too many types of makers (you probably realize by now i don't like makers that much)So far, these are the things I noticed. But these are just my personal opinion and I am enjoying the game. So have fun!

_childDocuments_.review:
Inspired by tales of their grandfather's pioneering days, the protagonist decides to pack their bags and leave the hustle and bustle of big city life for the frontier in Olive Town. 

When they arrive, they run into Victor, the town's mayor and their grandfather's old friend. He brings them to the old farm, which has been reclaimed by nature over the years. Determined to breathe life back into their grandfather's dream and follow in his footsteps, the protagonist rolls up their sleeves and gets to work. 

Olive Townwhich is just a stone's throw away from the farmis a port town built on the tip of a peninsula. It might be a quiet little town, but it is home to a whole host of unique characters. And while the townsfolk get by well enough in this picturesque seaside locale, a little more tourism never hurt anyone... 

The long-awaited brand new entry in the original farm/life simulation franchise, known in Japan as Bokujo Monogatari, makes its debut on Nintendo Switch, bringing players more freedom than ever before to shape an untamed wilderness and customize their farm down to the very tile. A new cast of marriage candidates, a town that grows and thrives along with your farm, and a request system highlight the new features, all while retaining the core elements of the STORY OF SEASONS series. Finding Earth Sprites while exploring your farmland may lead you to mysterious, fantastical lands such as gardens where the seasons never change, an island in the sky, or even the inside of a volcano! 

KEY FEATURES

-Cultivate Your Farm, Cultivate Your Town
Tame the wilderness of the peninsula and build your farm from the ground up! Gather and process materials to fulfill requests and improve Olive Town's infrastructure, upgrade tools, or commission new outfits and accessories.

-Simple Mechanics, Deep Gameplay
Greenhorn farmers can rest easy with the return of Seedling Mode and Normal Mode. Veteran players ready to create a bustling farm of their own will find familiar features and facilities with new twists on classic gameplay elements. 

-A Farm of Endless Possibilities
Clear the land, repair old facilities, and place new ones wherever you see fit. Level up your farming skills and craft a variety of decorations and facilities, from fences and automatic feeders for livestock to sprinklers for crops!

-There's Always Something Going on in Olive Town!
Participate in local festivals as the town comes to life with over 200 unique events! Get to know your neighbors better and you may even find love with a special someone among them.

name: Actraiser Renaissance
detailed_description: ABOUT Actraiser combines 2D platforming action (Realm Acts) with a City-building simulation (Realm Management) in the ultimate battle between good and evil! Featuring the soundtrack that sent shockwaves through the gaming world when it was first released, composed by the legendary Yuzo Koshiro - now remastered! Help humanity flourish by playing as the Lord of Light and their loyal angel in a world beset by evil. NEW FEATURES Remastered 2D graphics present the game in beautiful HD 15 new music tracks, as well as re-arranged original tracks by Actraiser composer Yuzo Koshiro! New stories, expanded action and realm management gameplay, additional action stages, an all-new realm, and a new, powerful boss! Auto-save and difficulty levels Realm Acts: Strategically cast powerful fire, ice, and other magic in these 2D action stages. Humans return to reclaim the realm after you conquer these stages, allowing you to begin cultivating your settlements. New magic that was not available in the original game has been added along with the ability to dodge. Players can also attack with upward and downward motions for a more dynamic action experience. You will need every new trick in your arsenal to defeat stronger bosses at the end of the new action stages. Realm Management: Help humanity flourish by cultivating your settlements and offering guidance. Use your miraculous powers to summon lightning and trigger earthquakes to remove obstacles such as trees and boulders that impede the growth of your chosen. Play as the Lord of Light's angel and use your mighty bow and arrows to drive back the evil monsters that prey on your people. Protect your settlements from enemy raids in real-time strategic battles. The placement of your forts and timing of your miracles is key to achieving victory in these engagements. Experience all-new tales of humanity's struggles to overcome their flaws and failings as they learn to love one another and together grow stronger. Altogether, these new scenarios amount to more than twice the story present in the original. Explore the vast new realm and enjoy building your settlements for longer than ever before! The original Actraiser composer, Yuzo Koshiro, has re-arranged all of the iconic original tracks and added 15 new tracks as well. Players can listen to the original music or switch to the re-arranged versions while playing the game. Tired from protecting and raising your villagers? Then just sit back, relax, and enjoy the tunes. © 1990, 2021 QUINTET/SQUARE ENIX CO., LTD. All Rights Reserved. © YUZO KOSHIRO

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing ActRaiser for 29 years. I bought it in summer of 1992 when the game store didn't have any copies of "Final Fantasy II" and they said ActRaiser was also a role-playing game. It became one of my favourite games of all time. I've beaten the game, I don't know, let's say 50 or 75 times over the years.  I'm writing this review to say that ActRaiser Renaissance is an  remake, and I strongly recommend it to anyone who is considering it.I see a fair amount of criticism on the forums here and elsewhere online that the game "looks like a cheap mobile port". I think that's quite uncharitable. The visual style they chose for this remake is weird: it's borderline claymation pre-rendered graphics with intentionally stiff animation. It looks like Killer Instinct, or an alternate universe Sega Saturn game. The 3d models have gobs and gobs of pixel shaded lighting on top of them, and there's a weird pixel shimmer. The Angel model in the sim mode's head is too big and it looks offputting. Further, the first enemy you see in Sim, the scorpion bat, looks bad.These first impressions are deceiving. The Master animates well, the backgrounds are excellent looking, bosses look great (though in widescreen, they're a little smaller than you remember!). There's a beautiful trail effect, like Alucard's cloak in SOTN, that follows you. There are tons of environmental effects everywhere. The maps in sim mode look almost like Heroes of Might and Magic or Hero of the Kingdom, both excellent visual references. Magic is great. I grew to love the weird way enemies over-react to being hit, again like something cheesy and mid-90s. The game is updated with a gorgeous intro video, and the Sim mode has tons of extremely high resolution, expressive, anime portraits and backgrounds, giving the game a bit of a visual novel flavour.I really think if you're wondering "should I buy this" and your reservation is "I didn't like how it looks in a screenshot or trailer", I think you should put your reservations aside and buy it.As you may have gathered from the reviews, store page, or watching video, the developers of ActRaiser Renaissance have added a third game mode. The game is now roughly equal parts platformer, town-builder, and tower defence. The tower defence mode is basic, but it does grow to be challenging over the course of the game. In sim mode, you collect resources from buildings, which you use to construct defensive fortifications. In addition to the defensive fortifications, you control hero characters. Initially, in Fillmore, this seems a little boring and overwhelming -- there's a lot of tower defence, and it doesn't really seem that interesting to start with. But in later areas, as you gain access to more interesting terrain, multiple heroes at once, and you get to understand enemy weaknesses, the tower defence mode grows into its own. Each area has 4-5 tower defence segments -- I'd maybe cut one of them, but besides that it doesn't feel like there's too much.Sim Mode is completely overhauled with extended story and character segments. In addition to all the key plots of the original game (which are present, more or less), each region has a new hero character who has a unique story. A lot of the original game's plot around doubt, faith, and human tenacity is expanded. Where Marahna always had a plot about people leaving the church to worship an evil religion, you now see their doubts grow progressively and meet the priest of the evil religion, who seems like a deceptively nice guy. This version of the game makes clear that Humanity cannot see God or the Angel, which is great.Most of the new story is interesting, and there's vibrant dialogue and localization (thanks to John Crow and Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, both Final Fantasy 14 veterans). I will say that the hero characters being centered minimizes a few of the segments I found poignant from the original game, in particular Northwall's Reincarnated Lovers and Kasandora's Man in the Desert. They're still there, they just feel a little overshadowed. The order of events and how the areas connect is slightly different to allow for some of the story changes.Sim mode also now has quests. Throwaway events from the original game are quests; beating the tower defence waves are quests; hitting various development goals are quests; and finally, re-playing action sequences (btw you can replay action sequences now) are quests. This has a nice bar-filling structure to it. I'm a little bummed that the rewards are kind of crummy, but it's still fun to complete each area.Finally, when sealing monster lairs you now play little mini Hammer Bros. style vignettes where you go in a cave, kill some enemies, then kill a monster spawning blob. This occasionally involves rematches with Act 1 bosses. Love this addition, more action!Action mode is greatly enhanced. Every single level is ground-up remade, typically with various differences and departures. Overall I would say the levels are at least as good as the original (Northwall 2 and Aitos 1 are worse because they eliminate some interesting mechanical elements, everything else as good or better). Movement is fun, and the Master has a much broader skillset -- you can dash attack, backdash, ground pound, uppercut, and combo. Jumping still has good commitment like the original but you're overall faster and more mobile.There's a great mechanic starting in Fillmore 2 where the more enemies you kill the more you power up, ending with +100% attack, +100% magic, and a free revive.Every level now has 3 hidden scrolls that add to your max MP (which is now a MP gauge, rather than a charge system). Each spell has a different MP cost, and the spells are totally redone. The new spells are: fireball, ice on the ground in front of you, Magical Stardust (nerfed, no longer able to instantly kill every boss), healing, AOE damage ball, and a holy spell that seems to do almost nothing. Some enemies have weak points, some enemies are weak to magic or physical damage. Overall the balance is much stronger, there's no longer any one hit kills on bosses.Bosses tend to have more interesting patterns and more moves. Aitos 1 and Tanzra are the only boss I feel is worse than the original; all of the others are more interesting. The hidden post-game boss evokes Hollow Knight.The game has all of the original songs in both SNES and arranged mode. Second, the game has an entire extra soundtrack worth of music, and each of the new songs has both SNES and arranged versions. Some of the new tracks are as good or better than the original soundtrack. The arranged mode music is a little too rock and roll, bordering on Castlevania -- I would have preferred more symphonic arrangements, but worth a try.There's no way around this: the sound effects are worse. They got rid of a bunch of iconic sound effects. I'm sad. It's not a deal breaker, but it sucks.There's post-game content which unlocks a 7th area -- this has interesting tower defence and sim mode but is burdened with an incredibly stupid, bordering on fan-fiction plot and dialog. Bummer about that, but the new action act and the new post-game boss are both great, and the score for the new action level is among Koshiro's best.Professional mode is replaced with a level select score attack mode, which scores you based on time, lives, enemies killed, and items collected.  For 100% completion of the main game on normal, it took me about 14 hours, add 60-90 minutes for post-game. It's a longer, meatier game.ActRaiser Renaissance does not replace ActRaiser. But it is a new, fun take on ActRaiser, well worth it for fans and newcomers alike. Long live Quintet, now and forever!
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original two Actraisers, I'm a little conflicted, but I'm gonna go ahead give this a cautious thumbs up.Does anyone remember when Gameboy Advance games attempted 3D models or attempted to make 2D sprites look 3D? That is what Actraiser Reinassance looks like. I personally love that kind of stuff, but I feel like I'm heavily in the minority here, so your mileage may vary; look at gameplay footage of the game and decide for yourself.If you've played the original Actraiser, you've played this. There are very few differences outside of some movement options in the sidescrolling sections,  and realm simulations have tower defense and upgrades and similar concepts like that. This is very clearly a budget title, that could have used more time in the oven, but I'm enjoying myself regardless. If you're unsure, use the steam refund thingie.Edit 9/24/2021: Changing my framerate to 90 fps somehow got rid of the screen-tearing.Edit 10/03/2021: Finished it tonight. This game was very clearly developed for mobile devices first, then ported to home consoles and PC second, hence the low res. But I'll be damned if I didn't enjoy every single minute of it, and I'm not really one for tower defense games. The last part of the game was so challenging that it kept me playing it through the night.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Like so many others, I was shocked and amazed to see that Squeenix had, at long last, given us a new Actraiser. It's been far too long and all I can say is: totally worth it. 100%The game was clearly designed by people who enjoyed the original and knew what could be fleshed out for a modern take. There are more action scenes and there is an expanded moveset similar to Actraiser 2 (I know a lot of people hate the sequel, but it has a lot of good ideas). More importantly, the simulation sections are massively more involved this time around. You have champions to command, and the tower defense scenes add some real tension. It starts off easy, but don't get comfortable - things get hairy quick.The action sequences are fast and the controls are precise. Things have been changed up a little so fights are more interesting. The music and sound are perfect.Downsides? Well, some of the assets are a little chunky on a hi-res display. Probably a result of being developed for the Switch, I would guess. On the upside it supports a huge variety of resolutions and even high frame rates! Also the master only yells "ha!" occasionally, rather than on every attack. An oversight, but a forgivable one. :)Overall, this update is so perfectly matched to the dreams I've had I'm not sure that this isn't a vision cooked up by my brain as I shuffle off the mortal coil. But if you're sharing this delusion, than definitely buy this game. You'll love it too.

_childDocuments_.review: Bear in mind that I'm writing this as someone who played the original game on the SNES, and played through it (and LOVED it) multiple times.PROSThe same base game is there, it's cool that you can switch between the original soundtrack and an orchestrated one.The magic system is revamped. In the original, you could only use a spell so many times, and once you were out, you were out for the rest of the level. In this game, you have a standard MP meter, so it can refill and you can keep using magic.While they're mainly there for tower defense (see the CONS section), I do like the addition of legendary heroes. Their stories are neat and do add to the overall plot.CONSGraphics are supposed to be improved, but they come off as rather "muddy". There's no benefit for those with ultrawide screens, it very much feels like this was meant to launch on mobile phones, and was ported to PC as an afterthought. I'm playing on a 5140x1440 monitor, and there was an opportunity to make something really beautiful. Instead, it feels like graphics from a couple generations ago.Addition of quests. Again, this should be an improvement, but feels like something tacked on to extend gameplay time, but done in a very boring mobile-game way. For example, one of the quests is to kill a specific monster in the first level a few times...but it only appears once, so you have to replay the level over several times to complete. In the original, you could only play through a level once, which gave each level a lot more impact. In this release, you can replay them over and over, which lessens the impact. I never thought I'd get tired of ActRaiser levels, but I did with this release.You now go into monster lairs to kill monsters, rather than the citizens of the world doing that. It messes with the overall feel since the whole point is that you're building up the world so that it can eventually fend for itself.There is an insane amount of text/story included that wasn't in the original. So much that it starts to droll on at certain points. I love flavor text and when plot elements are expanded, but it went overboard.LOATHEI can't stand the tower defense portions. The worst thing about it is that even after clearing a town of monsters, the tower defense portion will still activate after being in a town for a certain amount of time. If you lose, well, you have to do it all over, and it's very easy to lose some of them, and you can't perform any town interactions while the tower defense portion is active. It really detracts from the pacing. This is supposed to be an action/sim game, not an action/sim/tower defense. This was really poor gameplay design, and frustrated me to the point where I got to Aitos (town 4) and (at this time) just kind of gave up.SUMMARYIf you've never played the original, and you like tower defense, chances are good you will probably like this version. But it's very difficult to call this superior to the original. I'd honestly recommend the original over this mish-mash of concepts.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: ActRaiser for the SNES is one of my favorite games of all time, and I've replayed it in its entirety more times than I can count. Renaissance is a pretty good remake, with some new mechanics that I found quite interesting, as the "tower defense" sections and having to come down and fight for sealing the lairs. It's close enough to the original to respect the sensibilities of old timers like me, but the new twists are welcome IMO. And there's a New Game+ of sorts, with a new continent that did not exist on the SNES original.Is it a perfect remake? Hell no. Square botched some of textures and assets so badly that it defies belief. It seems pre-rendered as in DKC for the SNES, for instance, but with lower quality assets that look horrendous at a distance, and downright unacceptable when zoomed in. How come a studio this big do such a crappy job?Despite the graphics, I still recommend it.  It’s a unique gaming experience and the gameplay spot on. If only Square did it justice with the visuals…

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I played the game offline on my Steam Deck, so even though I logged about 16 hours in order to finish it, including the new extra stage at the end, it says I played it for just a few hours.Well, this one was a shot of nostalgia. I remember loving the original Act Raiser for the SNES and its mix of 2D side-scroller hack & slash and "Populous"-lite city building. I also found the story about playing as a sword-wielding god and his angelic attendant in a fantasy medieval world pretty interesting and sometimes even surprising, like the time I shot a bolt of lightning on a whim at my own temple and the people apologized for their selfishness and for trying to deceive me by keeping stuff from my offerings and they gave me some extra materials.So when I saw there was a modern remake I had to try it. Well, I'm not disappointed. It's pretty much the same game but better in almost every way, with updated graphics, game mechanics, more story and even a third game mode built around the idea of defending your settlement from invading monsters. When I started playing it I just wanted to see what it was like and intended to play the first 2D level and unlock the city builder section for the first region and leave it at that until I finished the other game I'm currently playing. Almost four hours later I found myself about to fight the final boss for the second region and I hadn't even noticed how long I'd been playing.My only complaint is that the settlement defense sections are too repetitive and they come up too many times in every region. Less of that would've been more. Otherwise, I had a blast playing it, remembering similarities with the original and being surprised by the differences.

_childDocuments_.review: It could be the nostalgia drip straight to my heart that biases my opinion so far. I'm enjoying it, a lot. The original was pretty simplistic, so is this. There are monster sieges now on the town where you direct a hero, establish forts and palisades. It's a neat addition that I hope is not alone. Combat took a little getting used to. The keyboard bindings are a little wonky, but it's pretty smooth once you get them sorted (probably should be using a controller anyway). You can adjust the music to play the classic versions and I almost cried. The updated music is also welcome. I'll try to add more when I'm furtherI don't have a ton to add, it was great. Bonus, unexpected content and fun all along the way. Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Tough call, i had fun going through most of this "reimagining" of the original game, but man did they drop the ball on some aspects of it. It's a lukewarm recommandation at best, berdering a noThe Goods : - Music's amazing AND it comes with both original and remastered soundtrack- The "improved" combat is a lovely tough. A couple more moves, magic is treated entirely different, allthough fireball is basically OP and the "crystals" to give you buffs is a nice touch. - Artstyle is an interesting choice, allthough not perfect everywhere, NPCs look varied and have their own distinct styles- Added an extra settlement which add some content. Nothing major ( was expecting they might take the opportunity to set up Actraiser 2) but it closes the story more naturally than the original.The Bads : - Magic is outright OP. It Gives I-Frames and deals massive damage. Won't lie, most boss went "Spam Jump Slash + cast fireball". The spell variety isn't interesting either. - Way too much redundant text. Every. Single. Settlements. You go through the SAME exact dialogue whenever your people attempt to close a monster lair or whenever you're in between text, the angel says the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing. I got it the first time y'know- Not enough Action phases, too much settlement "waiting for sh@t to happen". Game could've used all new "3rd acts" in every level. AIn't like they didn't come up with "new" stuff anyway. Instead, you just are mechanically forced to wait for "ressources / food" to generate (randomly) to complete quests or repair / upgrade forts.- Price is  steep for what's offered. Got it on sale for that reason The Uglies :- You all know what i'm gonna say. Those redundant, painfully boring settlement raids. Might've been an interesting concept on paper, but damn they messed up. Your heroes are never strong enough  ( not even sure how the devs thought making hem level 20 would even be remotely fun., 20 some hours in, game virtually finished ? my highest hero is level 12... ). You "could" sit there and wait for random raids, but even then it,s about as interesting as watching paint dry There is no "tactical" aspect to it since your fortress positioning doesn't matter and makes little to no sense, especially since you cannot entirely choose where to drop your defenses ( predetermined spots on the map) sometimes leaving wide open areas undefended. Miracles are worthless in that mode, never really dealing enough damage to actually change the tide of a battle and the cooldowns are a problem.AND, more often than not, you get stuck with hordes of flyers (thus limiting you to certain range heroes) and most of said monsters are magic resistant (downgrading your hero selection to 2, Allonso and Taia being outright MVPs) - The fact that most of your hours played are spent in settlement mode, which feels much much longer than the original SNES version, yet feels less rewarding in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Actraiser on the SNES is one of my all time FAVORITE games even until this day. It's got an all-time great soundtrack, and it's mix of god simulation + platforming action game are STILL super unique. To me, it stands out as something amazing and way ahead of it's time.Now here, we have a "modern" take on the classic... and well, in my opinion, it's a hard miss.My biggest gripe is with the largest change to the game. I can get past the pre-rendered main character, (and I actually really like the new overworld graphics and some of the boss and background graphics in particular), but the changes to the simulation part ruin the game for me. It's a classic change of "fixing something that wasn't broken". What am I talking about? In other reviews I've seen people casually say that they implemented a tower defense mechanic into the Angel town-simuation sections. With how the game actually plays, (I'm up to Bloodpool's second boss), I'd say they REPLACED the angel town-simulation sections with a tower defense mini-game. They left the ability for you to kill stuff with the angel, but honestly it doesn't fit alongside how the tower defense plays out gameplay-wise. It's now more akin to having an on-screen angel pointer then it actually accomplishing anything defensive itself. (You can't fire arrows with the angel during the tower defense mode...)The story is now INCREDIBLY linear, to the point that fans of the original will know all the story beats (which is fine), BUT ... the individual sections of rebuilding the towns are now full of drawn out exposition, with a weird focus being put on the Tower Defense characters and NOT your God-player character. They feel more like the stars of the game, not you, (who is the actual GOD who breathed life into the people and is doing the majority of cleansing the planet of the evil).It's a fine line with remastering this type of older game, I know, but I also feel like they could've changed how the maps are developed by the player and the town you're helping. With the tower defense mechanics they added in mind, the maps feel a bit half-baked FOR the added mechanics (if that makes sense). They feel smaller then they should be scale-wise, too.I also don't like how after you finish an action stage proper, (not the monster lair fights but one of the initial stages + the boss stages), they don't show your energy leaving the master's body. It's a small nitpick, but it'd happen on the original and when I don't see it happening here it feels wrong somehow.If you're a die-hard fan, I'd say buy it on sale. For full price - (and this is coming from a fan of the original like I said) - I'd pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about Actraiser: Renaissance is definitely . .  . a choice, that's for sure. Yet another perfect example of a game that Steam's Recommend/Don't Recommend review system is ill-equipped for because it's very much in the middle. The game has a pretty interesting art style since it uses pre-rendered 3D models turned into 2D sprites, the technique that made DKC look futuristic in the mid 1990s, and which conveys a kind of nostalgic tone today. The remastered music is also great and a definite positive as Actraiser always had some of the best tunes on the SNES. And the 2D action stages are honestly really great. They're not exact copies of the original game's but more "inspired by" them, with altered layouts and enemy placements. They work really well with a revamped combat system that has you taking advantage of i-frames to succeed too.What really hurts the game though is the big new addition of Renaissance: the tower defense mode. It's something that makes sense to add to this game conceptually, as the original already had you building towns with roads which you could reasonably expect would be the paths you'd build a tower defense around, but the whole sub-game is wildly inconsistent. Flying enemies ignore paths (and thus towers you've built), the buildings you have to defend change constantly (and you have no direct control over where they get built by your civilization), and you have no way of knowing where enemy spawns will appear beforehand so you really can't plan any kind of reasonable defense in an invasion until you've failed. It's just an exercise in either it being too easy or frustrating because of its myriad inconsistencies and lack of options. While some may not like the additional visual novel like reams of dialogue with a bunch of new characters acting out little morality plays that come with the tower defense mode additions, I felt they were bearable. This is a non-denominational pseudo-Christian Manga after all, such wholesome triteness actually fits the games theme. But the incoherent gameplay of these sections is just a painful slog to get through, and really feels like it was added in to pad the game's overall run-time a frankly needless amount. Still, the action stages are really good, the music is the best it's ever been, and it's always been fun to play a god game where god decides to kick demon @ss and take names. I enjoyed the game's positive elements enough to get over and deal with the interminable tower defense crud, but I'm not sure everyone will be able to do so. This is a very tepid recommendation as a result.Of course, the greatest sin Squeenix committed with this release is that the game wasn't named Actraiser: Resurrection. Come on guys, get it together! That's so obvious.

_childDocuments_.review: Fell in love with the game after second glimpse (Right now finished Fillmore). You will need some time to appreciate the effort behind this game. They mostly managed to get the spark of the older quintet games. But i can't agree with the action part that you have to start first so your first impression will get disturbed before you can enjoy the game:Action: 6/10It's clunky, the sprites are extemely ugly. Imagine Nintendo DS or PSP sprites only big. ACTRAISER ALWAYS HAD AMAZING SPRITES (!!!!). That sprites they really hurt in action mode! Also sometimes your character will not react for a looooong time after taking a hit or an animation like an down+attack was played --> Then he will run uncontrolled somewhere. Pro:- Intros when getting introduced to a boss. They are great! Like the encounter with the centaur.- The crystal system is cool. Cons: - faster than Actraiser 1 but still clunky. They could have kept Actraiser 1 action mode with HD Sprites and do some changes to the levels like they did and it would've been better than this. - missed a lot of opportunities here. --> Spark of the master rising up after killing a boss is missing. He is only lending a physical body, no ;) ? Or Bloodpool when you kill the Manticore: Why didn't they make the clouds from the sky go away and let the sun come through? Would have been a great addtion to the whole setting: Cleansing, light and dark, resurrection and this all goes in a loop thing. - IMHO: Action is a little bit worse than Actraiser 1 but way worse than Actraiser 2.  Simulation: 9/10Pro:- A LOT OF FUN- A bit cringy but in an acceptable way- Towns and map look fine. - It has got the things that made Actraiser 1 great. - Mission system will help casual gamers enjoy the game (but there's less space for exploration)Cons:- Once again: Sprites of angel (Not the drawn one) and demons when fully zoomed in. Again there is some HD resolution missing- They did not explain how to build blockhouses properly. You need to "build Fort" and press "(R1)-button"MUSIC: 11/10 !!!!YUZO KOSHIRO !!!!!!!!!!!!! THERE'S NOTHING MORE TO ADD!!!!!! If there is a master out there sonically, it's him!!!PLEASE BUY THIS GAME AS THIS MIGHT BE AN OPEN DOOR FOR MORE QUINTET REMAKES! IF THEY EVER DO ACTRAISER 2: ADD SIMULATION MODE (though the town already exist) AND PLEASE KEEP THE Actraiser 2 gameplay, with sprites from Ariga Hitoshi. Thanks

_childDocuments_.review: I played <cutscene> the original <cutscene> and don't recall <cutscene> quite so many <cutscene> interrupting cutscenes. Every <cutscene> action you attempt to <cutscene> take is impeded by <cutscene> them. Most of these <cutscene> cutscenes are irrelevant to the <cutscene> gameplay and only add <cutscene> flavor. They don’t <cutscene> prompt you to interact, the scene simply <cutscene> fades to black and villagers <cutscene> play out some VN <cutscene> dialog. I cannot <cutscene> stress how frequently <cutscene> this happens. And it <cutscene> totally ruins the <cutscene> experience.Outside of the constant interruptions, the “remaster” tries to preserve some aesthetic during the side-scrolling parts, but frankly just looks like @#$%&!. I’m running in 4K, and the grotesquely pixelated difference between the world map and action content is jarring.Another change was the addition of a hero and tower defense mechanic. This was not in the original and significantly alters the flavor of gameplay. The construction of defense towers actively competes with growth of your peoples as it occupies space needed for housing, but graciously informs you exactly how much growth you lose when placing. Also, defense towers can only be built in select places that appear to have been arbitrarily chosen by the developer. This eliminates the tactical benefits of placing them in most cases. As early as Bloodpool, you’ll notice that there is zero capacity to protect the northern part of the map due to all placements being southerly. The heroes are useful, but the controls for switching between them are awkward. You are awarded scrolls which are used to leveling up the hero units. I questioned this at first because they seemed to serve no other purpose. Why not just apply the experience to the hero directly? Then the villagers started demanded fixed amounts of these scrolls as part of their (linear) quest completions. In essence, you’ve been given a resource that serves one purpose, but you cannot safely spend because of random demands for them. Thanks…The controls in the map are, in general, awkward… mixing the LB/RB controller functions in randomly and leaving stuff in the A/B/X/Y space dead and functions you need often are buried under nested submenus.The last gripe is the addition of a different skin for the angel. This “special” outfit is a toggle option in the menus and turns the little angel into a imp (or succubi if you prefer) but this only applies to the cutscenes. The overworld sprite will continue to be the angel making this feature the ultimate why bother.If I were to recommend this game, it would be rather weak. The only real draw is the nostalgia of it. That’s why I’m here, but that nostalgia fades quickly. I soon realized I was playing a pastiche of the original and not a remake or remaster. The game is ultimately meh, and as such I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a middle rating other than thumbs up or thumbs down.  So, Actraiser is one of my favorites from back in the day, and I still play it from time to time on emulators.  I was pretty excited to see this pop up and bought it with little research.  I have to say pass on this one, unless it is a sale or you are a completionist.  Basically this is very mobile gamey.  It would probably be better played on a mobile system rather than on Steam with a controller.  The tutorial pop-ups get old, harvesting resources is a tap fast kind of mini-game, and the tower defense minigame that they added is a chore.  Also this suffers from the same v-sync issues as the Final Fantasy pixel remasters.  tl;dr: Pass unless it's on sale, or just buy it on mobile.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sad "no".The game does some things right - re-making the old SNES gameplay is quite well done. The action stages at the beginning and the end of each area are very similar and play well. Even including the flaws of the old version - If you're not playing on hard difficulty, you can just ignore all strategy when fighting most bosses and just rush them spamming attacks i/e.But the really bad flaws are in the added stuff in the simulation game parts and they are many:- They tacked on mini-action-stages for every monster lair you close. Those are short and really boring.- The succession is streamlined, only allowing you to close monster lairs once you've progressed far enough through the story elements. In the original, you could just close them up as soon as you were able to reach them.- You often get interrupted with story-elements and quests in such a a rapid succession it's really annoying. The original had that in some parts, too, but it's way worse here. The quest system tries to expand the old storyline but the way it is done it rips you out of gameplay constantly.- The tacked on "Raids" on the settlements are really bad tower defense games. iterrupting even more.- The Heroes and their stories would be kind of okay, but they're mostly used for the raids and have little other use aside from adding even more interruptions.There's something good, too - the soundtrack, it's the old SNES melodies remastert and modernized, and it's very well done. Not as good as "Act Raiser Symphonic Suite" (It you're into the music, look that one up, it's amazing), but still very very good.If this game had a classic mode, where all the new aspects are left out and just the classic parts in modernized form, this would be money well spend, but the way it is, it's mostly one thing: Annoying. I'm now going to play the old original to make the sad go away...

_childDocuments_.review: Note; This is a day 1 immediate reaction. Thoughts could change as I play more but this is as of finishing the first city. Also rewrote some parts that were confusing even for me to read!Let's get the negative out of the way, graphics. They are pretty rough. If you see the screenshots and don't like it then yeah, you won't enjoy the game. Personally I don't mind because I'm not one of top of the line graphics, but I can understand those complaints.Let's talk positives. Side scrolling levels are remade and expanded while retaining the feel of the original, music is redone and redone well with longer tracks from the original artist so they fit right in. The city building sim mode got the most attention. In addition to the original game’s features, cities now get raided by monster hordes from time to time that require tower defense elements to come into play. Most of the defense comes from forts and towers you build, the Angel that shoots flying monsters normally cant intervene, but you do have a hero human you can move around the board to handle groups of monsters head on. You can use your miracles to throw lightning and the like on creeps but there is a cooldown on them and high MP costs so they are not effective as a primary defense, more of a last ditch effort thing. Outside of raids, when sealing a monster lair you play a more active role. Instead of just watching your townies seal it themselves like in the original, you go down and play a quick little action stage to seal the deal. I would have preferred a little more to these stages, perhaps a puzzle to solve in addition to monsters to fight, but as a source of variety they get the job done. The game as a whole seems like it will be significantly longer, I took 2 hours in fillmore and while I drag things out spending some time lightning bolting my people's mud huts so they would rebuild them into better houses that hold more followers, in that same amount of time I'd be in the middle of Act 3 in the original. If my views drastically change, I'll update them here. So far I'm pretty impressed with what they've done.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr review: Get on a discount. Actraiser Renaissance is a reboot, not a remake. Not the same game and definitely missing the magic of the original. Not terrible, but not as fun or good as the original. Its another game that needs a rating between 'yes' and 'no' because its just OK.-------the tl;dr stuff-----Totally would be worth buying 100% -IF- they included a port of the original which should be very easy to do and they didn't do it. Actraiser has stood the test of time; its a 30 year old game that's still fun to play. And this brand new Actraiser game isn't so much.Don't set your expectations too high. Actraiser Renaissance biggest problem is it's a reboot and not a remake. I disagree with anyone who calls this a 'remake', its just too different from the original. The concept still works: Renaissance feels like a fresh new unique idea that is fun to play. And as stupid as this sounds, the simple little civilization management aspect of the original game was the best and most meaningful part about it. But Squenix messed it up! They changed and added things to that part of the game that don't quite work and get in the way of enjoying it. Its extremely disappointing! This game is lacking the talent and know-how of what made the original game work. Renaissance feels like an imitation.The only thing it gets right from the original is the soundtrack, which, for a SNES OST is just ok. I really don't get why people keep saying it had a great soundtrack.As far as imitations go, Sega published a bad Actraiser ripoff called SolSearaph a few years back. And Actraiser Renaissance appears to rip off that game! In the original Actraiser, you grew your nation until it became strong enough where you guided them to a portal and they would close it themselves. In this remake, you now have to play a short, pointless, and annoying platform stage to get rid of it, just like in SolSeraph! I really don't like this change at all! The platforming bits in Actraiser aren't its strong point!Another change that sucks is originally population = experience. The more pop you had, the stronger you were. And there was a puzzle element between the nations where you would need to do something but weren't quite strong enough to do it forcing the player to grow another nation and come back when they got stronger. One of those things was using earthquake. Earthquake rocked the whole map and destroyed the low pop shanties which would be rebuilt as better houses increasing the pop limit. Everything I just described was changed in Actraiser Renaissance. Population is largely irrelevant since EXP is now determined by faith earned through completing quests. But you're still encouraged to grow pop by destroying shanties once the nation has advanced. So, destroy them all using 1 earthquake, right? No. Earthquake now effects a tiny area. This is so much different than the original... And it sucks!The more I think about this game, the more I rant about how it gets wrong what the original did right.Playing as the angel has changed too. In the original game, each monster that came out of a portal was a threat to you or your people and you needed to kill them right away. It also felt more like a distraction to keep you busy as you waited between building cycles as your nation grew. I haven't played too far into Renaissance, but so far each portal releases 1 easy to kill monster per cycle and it bumbles around for awhile before it does anything. Renaissance makes the angel part of the game feel like an annoyance.Renaissance also adds an RTS to the nation building part of the game where your nation gets raided by monsters that your people need to fight off. This too is not that fun, somewhat annoying, and not well thought out. It feels like it happens too often too. As the angel, you can't shoot the raiding monsters. You can only hit them with spells. I haven't played far enough, but I've heard people complain this new minigame gets very frustrating later in the game.The absolute worst thing about this reboot is has that terrible Japanese RPG video game habit that appeared 10-15 years where there's WAY TOO MUCH TEXT. Lots of it is irrelevant. In the original game, each nation had scripted story events that were short and meaningful. They only reached out to you when they needed you. This reboot has the game get interrupted what feels like every 5 to 10 minutes for needless dialogue with half of it being people wanting to kiss your ass because you're God. These excessive interruptions really do hurt this game a lot.All of these issues might be because Squenix had Sonic Powered develop the game. Sonic Powered, an obscure developer known mostly for weirdo train/airport sim games on handhelds...Oh, so the platforming bits in this game.... Like the original, they're weak. But.... BUT! Actraiser Renaissance does them better than the original! It got that sort of rightOne last comment I'd like to make is that somehow, in spite of what the trailer shows off from the game, Actraiser Renaissance has a tendency to be visually unappealing. Its hard to explain. But if I were to try, I'd say its not ugly, just that sometimes it looks like cookie cutter cut and pasted 3d clip art.In spite of all that I've said here, the game isn't bad. It's just bad when compared to the original. Which makes picking a yes or no difficult. I'm leaning more towards no though.I wouldn't encourage buying this at full price. Get it at a discount
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I love the original SNES game and have completed it many times over the years. For those unfamiliar with it, ActRaiser is a game that marries 2 types of gameplay: side-scrolling action gameplay, where lands are liberated from the forces of evil, and top-down sim town management gameplay, where the world is rebuilt and repopulated. This is a remake that consists of a relatively faithful reimagining of all of the content of the original game, as well as quite a few additional elements.The parts that are carried over from the original game are implemented competently, albeit with pretty significant caveats. The side-scrolling action sections are completely reimagined in a way that attempts to capture the spirit of the original level layouts. In these sections, the player now has attack combos (where the original had a single attack animation), backdashing, and several attack moves with invincibility frames. The gameplay and level design is fairly well done, but it's simply not as tight as the original. The biggest problem with these sections is that the graphics consist of low-resolution pre-rerendered art. The maps tend to have poor readability and it often isn't obvious whether something is an obstacle or not. Furthermore, the internal framerate is pretty bad and does not feel like 60fps even if the game is running at or above 60fps. Altogether the presentation is poor because of the visuals.The sim parts are also mostly faithful at their core, but come with a lot of new additions that really detract from the original. The biggest addition is that of named "hero" characters which are similar to those seen in mobile games, complete with exaggerated anime art style and simplistic, cartoony dialogue. These hero characters not only beef up the script, they participate in a newly added mandatory tower defense mode, which is terrible.Each map in the sim mode has several tower defense sequences. The problem with them is that they don't have a proper game system. The enemy pathing logic is mostly nonexistent and the spawn points can be absolutely anywhere, and there are no discernible paths that you can expect them to go on so there is not a systematic game design for this element that you can learn or become good at. The towers you can build are very limited and 1 of the 3 types is a fortified gate, which sometimes the enemies can just go around, and other times not. There is no consistency. The enemies might go straight for your base, or just be weirdly attracted by 1 random tower. The game also expects the player to put down barricades in real-time while this goes on. A major issue is that the towers and barricades can only be placed in pre-defined arbitrary "slots" that have no rhyme or reason whatsoever for their placement. Giant gaps simply cannot be defended.Another problem with the sim parts is the simplification of some of the quests. A quest system was added where the player has to meet certain requirements, and the reward is typically exp for the hero characters. However, the "real" quests from the original game are greatly simplified. For example, in one quest, you are supposed to figure out where to use a certain item. In the original, it's entirely up to you to determine where it should be used, whereas in the remake, the location now just lets you press the A button on it, which then lets you choose the item to use. Another example is sharing technology between civilizations. In the original, it's up to you to bring certain technologies to other nations, whereas it's just automatic here.The sim parts now also have many more interruptions compared to the original game, and it's a real drag on the flow of the game. Combined with the tower defense segments, ultimately the sim parts feel very heavily padded.The map visuals in the sim parts are decent but the heros look like the generic ones you see in mobile games. Overall, the serious visuals of the original are compromised pretty severely in this remake.The real standout of this remake is the music. Yuzo Koshiro did a great job with the soundtrack, which consists almost entirely of compositions from the original game that have been completely redone. This feels like the only part of the remaster that is of premium quality and artistry, while everything else tends towards mobile game quality.Why a negative recommendation: almost all of the work done on this game detracts pretty significantly from the original. The original has tighter gameplay and level design and a more consistent art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is a burst of welcome nostalgia, with a few new features to fill out what was originally a pretty short endeavour. There are a number of things that I really like about the remake, and a few things I wasn't too particularly enthused about.Pros:- The remade music is absolutely gorgeous, and the new tracks in both 16-bit form and remade are fantastic.- They added a bit more depth to the action-platformer portions of the game by fleshing out the combat abilities and doing some tweaks to the mechanics that simultaneously make the content harder and also easier than the original. Overall, it felt good to play.- The addition of heroes and their personal stories was a really neat addition, in my opinion.- Overall, the experience is very faithful (no pun intended) to the original, and I think anyone who was a fan of the original would be at home here. It's hard to know whether a newer player would enjoy as much, as some portions might be a bit stilted or slow paced, but I think there's some substance here for everyone.Cons:- Apple gathering quests are quite possibly the worst aspect of the newly added side quests. You have no control over whether Apple or SP Potions spawn, and it is very frequently the latter, meaning you could be mindlessly looping in circles for a good 5-10 minutes while waiting on apples to spawn. Just tedious and boring, really.- "Kill X monsters" side quests are the 2nd worst aspect of the side quests. Normally it would incentivize going back to the action-platformer levels in the game as a secondary objective while you hunt down the Max MP boost scrolls, but if you were particularly attentive at seeking out the secrets, chances are you don't need to make more than one return trip per level. This wouldn't be terrible, except these side quests are usually set up for 2-3 return trips to complete, which is just unnecessary filler, really.- The pseudo tower defense content would have been quite good if it provided any sort've insight whatsoever as to what to expect. Instead, you go in blindly without any idea of where monsters are going to attack from, nor any indication what forts/towers might be best suited for what you're up against, and by the time you know what was good for a particular siege, it might not apply to the next one anyway. On top of that, fort placements are incredibly restrictive and limited, so it often feels like you're surviving the siege in spite of the system and not because you've mastered it. Ultimately it just ends up being trial-and-error to find out what works and what you might need. Pretty fun content but with bad execution.- The dialogue in the game comes across perhaps too preachy for my tastes at times. What is fundamentally a game rooted in some form of Christian/Catholic mythology never really came across too overbearing in the original game, but in this remake it's perhaps a bit much.Overall, I am pleased with this remake and happy it exists. It was developed well enough that I don't feel like I would instead prefer to play the original, and while it certainly has some weak points, scratched my nostalgic itch sufficiently and I'd love to see the same love applied to Soul Blazer, Illusion of Gaia, and Terranigma, perhaps!
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry I really tried to enjoy this, I loved the original Actraiser back in the day. However this one just does so many things wrong to be enjoyable.First off lets talk about the graphics. For the overworld sim sections, the graphics are fine. But the action stages.... this may be the ugliest graphics I've seen for a game in over a decade. The graphics only get worse the higher resolution you try to run the game at as well. The game also has choppiness issue at higher framerates, running the game at 144fps in action sections can result in projectiles disappearing and other interesting anomolies. I could almost deal with the bad graphics as the action stages are fun enough, the combat only changed slightly to make a more fluid combat experience.... what I cannot deal with is the civilization sim section. The original kept this part sweet and chill, it knew exactly what it wanted to be and got it right. The remakes sim section is an endless string of boring tutorials/dialogue and when its not doing that its doing extremely dull sieges and lair raids that are completely uneccessary to the game's pacing. I really tried to not be judgemental about this and keep an open mind. but after the 3rd boring siege and samey lair raid and the realization that the whole game was going to be like this I just turned the game off and went for the refund button. I get some people think the Tower Defense is fine, but I absolutely hate it, and if they were going to expand any part of the game I wish it had been the action stages.If you even look at this game, wait till a massive discount. This remake had all the markings of a great one, but poor decisions lead to an experience much worse than its original.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original as a youth, you'll love this. It stays faithful to the original and yet builds upon the rather simple game with new mechanics. We all know the best part was the original soundtrack, and it's here  but fully orchestrated and in most cases, extended versions of the original, which is real nice. If you want the original 16-bit soundtrack, you can turn that on too.2 issues: with the extra content, the RTS part where you build your cities, is CHOCK FULL of constant interruptions. Seems like every minute and a half someone is bugging you for something making it rather tedious, even though I generally liked this part of the original, and the new twists are fun. The second point is that screen tearing is a thing. It's pretty bad. I have a 3080 and tried MANY different combinations of settings but found that if I set it to cap at 120 FPS and VSYNC ON (I know doesn't make sense) but it stopped the tearing for me. Price? Worth it to me, mostly for the nostalgia, but if that's not your reason for buying this, maybe wait for a sale.
