_childDocuments_.review: Did you enjoy Actraiser on the SNES? Do you enjoy tower defense and don't mind if the sim section is sort of easier, while the platforming is way better and there's a deeper, more interesting story added to all of the areas along with a bonus area once you've beaten the usual ones you've beaten a hundred times before?You should buy this, and play it. Buy it, play it, and review it well.Also, the new music? Good!
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: You wake up when your alarm goes off, and check the time. You've got two hours until you have to be at work. You get out of bed and attempt to put on your pants only to be forced to defend your bedroom from a host of monsters in a tower defence mini game. You vanquish the fiends and put on your pants, only to be attacked by another horde of monsters upon reaching for your shirt. Another tower defence mini game. You finish getting dressed and attempt to leave your bedroom only to find, you guessed it, another tower defence mini game waiting for you in the hallway. You defeat it, and attempt to make it all the way to the bathroom to brush your teeth and yet more tower defence mini games await you.Does this sound tedious? Repetetive? I've just explained how the gameplay loop in ActRaiser Renaissance plays out. Like in the original SNES game you begin a world by entering Act 1 and fighting through a side scrolling action stage. For the most part these are in tact, but with a new leveling mechanic which honestly seems somewhat unnecessary. A trend for this remake. You beat the boss and unlock simulation mod, which many view as the big reason the original SNES classic is so beloved to this day.Unfortunately, the devs have adopted the strategy of attempting to pad this out as boringly as possible. Every single time you close a monsters lair you have to enter the lair for a "action stage" which lasts less than a minute and provides next to no challenge what so ever. It is filler. Your reward for closing the lair is a tower defence mini game. Every. Single. Time. To make matters worse randomly your town will be attacked by RNG tower defence mini games. Which means you're looking at no less than five or six of them per area minimum. It gets old extremely fast and makes the game a chore to go through, and this is from the perspective of somebody that considers the original one of his favourite games of all time.To justify these mini games you get heroes per level, and there's a new leveling mechanic for both heroes and the master that gives you additional SP for miracles (casting lightning and the like). The problem with this is that having more SP means nothing when you've got no monsters lairs left and you're sitting there waiting for the people to gift you SP increasing items at random and it could be several cycles before they even bother. So you're just sitting there watching and your town doesn't get demolished as you desperately hope somebody gives you the ability to pour a little bit of rain on something.It's not all bad. The music remaster is fantastic, even if some of the songs don't seem to play when they're meant to. There is even new music, which have been demastered if you choose to use the original SNES soundtrack. The graphics are pleasant as well - although the player character sprites seem to oddly not match the rest of the game in a slightly jarring fashion.Frankly you'd have a better experience playing the original while having the soundtrack for this game playing on youtube in the background. I cannot recommend it. It's a struggle to get through, and even with my desire to finish it due to being a fan of the original I can only play it in very short patches. Square should be ashamed of themselves for what they've done to my boy.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Actraiser Renaissance is a must play for any fan of the original. Way more than just a visual upgrade, this is in many ways a new game built upon the foundation of this classic from the SNES era. While it covers all of the original story beats and gameplay, it expands upon them with new characters and heroes, who are utilized in defense of raids that attack each of your settlements. This meshes well with the original gameplay, as does the quality of the writing for this new content. You can expect to spend 2-3 hours in each area now, whereas the original game could be thoroughly completed in a total of 6, so this is a much longer experience. The music--both the rearranged tracks and new originals pieces--is excellent. The game as a whole is a bit of a harder sell to someone without the nostalgia, as the combat is intentionally rigid, but it too is more complex than in the original, with new mobility attacks and a backstep with invis frames. Overall this is a very pleasant surprise from Square Enix, and it's nice to see Quintet on a title screen in 2021. I hope you'll support this! Maybe we'll see new versions of Soul Blazer, Illusion of Gaia and Terranigma if we're lucky.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to give this game as much of a chance as possible before writing any kind of review. I did end up finishing the story mode and saw the credits. I agree with a lot of people in that they really nailed the music with this game. It's really an incredible sountrack. That's pretty much where my praise will end with this game though. I hated the tower defense elements from the start to the end. It's very frustrating, drawn out, difficult, annoying, and just unnecessary. At first, I thought that adding tower defense to the town building was smart, and seemed like it would blend really well into the city building. A match made in heaven. But you are forced to complete a minimum of SIX of these sections PER village. If you fail, you must start the invasion over, and these can go on for like 10 - 20 minutes. It feels like they last forever and they are not fun. It's fine that they experimented here and there and tried to change some things for a modern age, but in my opinion, the changes they made were never for the better. The one exception to this being the collectibles and the crystal shard collecting in the sidescrolling levels. I really think they took an all-time classic game and crammed it so full of extra crap that it feels worse to play than a mobile game. It was important to me to support this game, though, because I DO want them to do a proper remake. To me, this isn't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: So, Actraiser Renaissance is not what I expected. This game is far more than an "HD Remaster," this feels like an entirely new experience. The stages felt somewhat familiar yet new enough to be fresh. I'm in love with it, and think it is well worth your time. Not to mention all the changes and additions to the city builder sections. There's so much more going on than before with the sieges, and having to build up and actually fortify the cities.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Competent, and could have been great, but there are silly tower defense sections added to the sim mode, as well as manually having to fight the lairs instead of your people, which end up ruining the sim mode. The original game had a very solid flow of hard action into relaxing simulation with an even mix of both, with the switching between the two mixing up the gameplay for a whole that was more than the sum of its parts, but the various additions to sim mode make for a game that's just go-go-go-go-go at all times with no relaxation or downtime at all, turning the game into less than the sum of its parts.If this would have been a 1:1 remaster with just the better sound and graphics, it'd be an amazing game, but as it is, there's no reason to play this over the original unless you *really* like mobile tower defense games. Almost good, but ultimately a swing and a miss, and yet another shoddy SE port.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Actraiser Renaissance is a good remake.Going more in depth;Graphically it isn't amazing but works, the weakest part is the player character sprite, considering some of the art provided it comes across as a blurred mess and lacks the sharp appearance seen elsewhere, most of this is likely to accommodate the Switch release but again its acceptable.Gameplay, this is split across 3 sections, Action, Town-building(Sim) and DefenceActionYou will begin and end each zone with a an action section where you have access to a basic combo, an aerial attack and down strike along side a backwards dodge giving you a decent core of attacks.Most enemy projectiles can be deflected and certain attack have invulnerability allowing you to be very aggressive.Later this skill set is augmented with magic providing ranged attacks and healing, these primarily function as a means of safely thwarting Bosses but as a limited resource you need to consider how best to utilise it.SimThis is where you guide your people, defend them from monster lairs and "encourage" them to upgrade.Help your people expand by clearing terrain, shoot some monsters trying to eat them and pick up resources.progression here is linked to quests making it less of a passive experience and more objective based.This is where the breaks in gameplay really are and you have control when to trigger quests, events etc.DefenceWhile linked to the Sim this feels distinct enough to separate, essentially your towns will be attacked and the majority of their defence is down to your people, this works via some defensive buildings placed in Sim mode and the local hero.You never feel like you have enough defence to really secure your town so it is vital you use the local hero to close gaps and your magic to prevent them being overwhelmed.This mode starts off feeling pretty brain dead but ramps up and can easily give you a game over if you aren't paying attention.The gameplay evolves steadily, new mechanics are added to the Sim and Defence modes while the threats you face in Action mode grow forcing you to dip more into your magic to claim victory.The RPG elements of levelling allow you to take your time and gain an extra level or 2 before taking on a particularly difficult challenge.Music, I personally love both the classic and remake versions, I have not felt the need to switch to the classic versions as the new ones are true to the originals while having more complex arrangements. I may be a biased source on this and your mileage may vary.Should you buy it though?I paid the £25 price tag happily but that is as a fan of the original.If you feel like that is enough for a 12-15 hour(10 if you rush) experience from beginning to end then yes.For the Metroidvania crowd, while I expect you would enjoy the Action sections you would be crying for more so unless you are looking for city building and tower defence to fill in the rest of the experience, you may wish to wait for a sale.For gamers at large...Actraiser was an oddity mixing action and town building, with the town building being shunned in the sequel to try and reach a broader audience, I can think of few games like it a none bare this remake that I would consider the same, I say you look up the original, watch some gameplay, if your response is "seems interesting but too simple" then this is the game for you, it is an evolution of that core.For me, I hope that this game finding success, leads to more Actraiser because I want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I write on steam - but I feel like this release deserves support.While many of the usual critique-points are understandable, e.g. the constant tutorial messages during the first strategy-stage, or the slightly  weird-looking render-optic of the action stages- as a whole the game ist great. It gets realy good from the second stage onwards. The gameplay loop becomes very addictive and calming, even though it is just pretty basic action and tower-defense strategy.Much of that is due to it's simple charm, great atmosphere, and more than anything else thanks to the great music from yuzo koshiro. No matter if you choose the modern or classic SNES versions of the songs - the Soundtrack consists of fantastic and catchy compositions that pretty much carry the game.I would defintetely recommend this game to any fans of retro-gaming that have nostalgia for the 16-bit days.Your first impression might not be the best. But if you give the game some time, you may find yourself being charmed enough to forgive it's minor flaws
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: is a remake of a SNES game ActRaiser and while it looks and sounds pretty it somehow makes the game worse than the original. While I have not played the original, just from basic research I can see that everything I hated about the game could be attributed as something the remake tacked on. Yet there were parts I liked. And all of those could be attributed to the original game concept. There is something seriously wrong here when I would seriously have a better time just picking up the original game rather than play this. What is even the point of Renaissance other than looking pretty?You play as, quite literally, God and one of his angels. Your divine presence cleanses the land of evil enough for citizens to start making a town. Eventually they meet a strange out-of-lace hero who lends them their aid. Monsters strike and evil is back with a vengeance. Through your guidance, the hero becomes a devout follower and leads the citizens to a victory. Yet the last evil is far too strong for anyone but God to defeat, and so you must strike down the final boss in his lair. Repeat this for every continent. However, there is an overarching story where there is a grand evil orchestrating all the other evils in the continents. In the post-game, there is yet another mysterious force as well.It's a simple and repetitive story but serves its purpose well enough. Some areas have better stories than others. I particularly liked the snowy area. There is often some pretty interesting themes in the stories as well, such as the balance of god acting on behalf of his flock versus leaving them alone to let them deal with their own problems. Or even how power may wane when faith wavers. So while the basic structure is repetitive each story is different at least. That said, the way the story is told is WAY too wordy, drags on, and just overall could be 10 hours shorter.There is SO much dialog. Even in the first area it felt like the citizens and angel were harassing me every 5 seconds. It’s immersion breaking and the opposite of relaxing. It’s just annoying. Sometimes the dialog is interesting but more often than not they could have just kept their stupid prayers in their pockets and let me handle things on my own.  Apparently the original game was far more streamlined and wasn’t as obnoxious with the dialog.For the most part, the game looks pretty fantastic. I like the overworld for the city building sections. The visual-novel like art of the cutscenes is nice. The 2D side scrolling section are a nostalgic throwback to SNES and arcade games. I can generally tell where I’m supposed to go, what is destructible, what will hurt me, etc. The game doesn’t really commit any sins. Presentation is certainly it’s strong suit. Even the music is pretty epic, with triumphant music suitable for the heaven’s conquest. I’d say my one gripe is I really dislike the “chibi” art for the angel. But that could also be because of the angel is involved with a lot of the parts of the game I hate.So there really is like 3-4 games in one with how many genres this game blends. It was honestly a drawing point – I thought a city builder mixed with a 2D side scroller sounds dope. It is pretty nice. I don’t really have any complaints for the 2D Side Scroller part – it’s pretty good. It’s dated at times and starts out way too easy. But it definitely picks up in challenge at times. It’s a basic hit and run hack and slash kind of thing where you watch the enemy movements and hit when it’s safe. There’s also magic you can use (which makes the game WAY easier) and enemies may have different weaknesses to such.Now for the city builder – this is where the cracks form because for some reason the remake decided to pad the hell out of it. I already noted the dialog problem – that’s one issue. The other major issue is the addition of tower defense sections. Just, why? I’m usually a fan of tower defense, hence I got the game despite the warnings. But these are just not good. Not well designed. Difficulty is all over the place. Some maps are frustrating hard unless you know exactly where to place towers and heroes. Others are laughably easy and can be solved while napping. But worst of all – it’s just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring. There’s level ups for the heroes which I was excited for. But it’s just stats. No skills or customization. There’s only three different towers. They can be upgraded, so yippee I guess. But here’s the kicker, the first one you get, the gatehouse, kinda sucks! Just spam the towers that actually shoot things. Heroes will be the main DPS, but the problem is they can’t be everywhere at once. Hence, need towers to help – especially with annoying as ♥♥♥♥ fliers. Fliers absolutely ruin the tower defense sections and are the bane of my existence. Wind spells help against them. Arrows also help, but there’s just so many and they love to just go around taking out farms. What’s really annoying is when you get a magician. I love the magician character and she is powerful but then the game introduces magic shields. Now for the rest of the game many enemies will resist magic!! Yay!! Including fliers!!!God, these sections suck so much. And they’re required to get through the game. Several times per area. And they often destroy all your ♥♥♥♥ so then you gotta slowly build up resources to rebuild everything again. There’s just so much pointless downtime for no reason but to pad out the game. And you can’t even AFK! Because the game will spawn random enemies to attack the town you’re supposed to shoot down with the angel. So much for a relaxing city builder in between the fighting 2D action scroller sections. The original had the pacing right. This game is just non-stop throwing crap at you, even when the pace is slowed to a crawl.Game worked fine.Operating System: Windows 10Processor (CPU): Intel Core i5-3570K CPU @3.40GHzGraphics Card (GPU): NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070Memory (RAM) 16 GBDon’t do it. It’s not worth it. It just drags on and on for what seems like centuries. I apparently played it less than 20 hours but it felt like 40! And even those less than 20 hours were too long and I wish the game was shorter. Apparently the original was! Seriously, just play the original game if it seems appealing at all. The remake does nothing but actively make the game worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: The game has it's ups and downs. Bottom line is the original is better.The original looks better, isn't bogged down by mobile gaming culture and bloat content.Whats good?------------------It's fairly faithful to the original, it would have been amazing if it had not added anything.-The music is of course, good.-The combat flows better, though reads worse.-----------------What's bad?------------------They added bloat to an already long game. An example, you get given a kill x amount of such monster quest in the first area. This monster appears near the end of that act and you need to kill it 10 times for more stuff for another feature.-The tower defense game is boring, annoying and takes up time that could be spent playing the game.-It uses 2d sprites made from 3d models, but with so few frames things can be hard to read.-The visual contrast is often low, it's harder to see certain things than it needs to be, slimes in the castle for example can completely blindside you. -The bosses need much more visual clarity, the manticore often projects a gigantic hurt box way beyond its sprite and it's quite persistent, as an example. The Minotaur reads like a teenager made a boss with 4 sprites.-Tutorials. Oh my goodness, get to the first town and you will be stopped every 5 seconds of gameplay for the first hour. The original had a fair bit of stopping and starting, but nothing like this.Should you buy it? On a sale perhaps, but not at full price. Play the original if you want to have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm... the decision if I should rate this positive or negative isn't an easy one. Actraiser Renaissance is a game that makes me feel conflicted about itself a lot, and quite honestly: I was about to just throw a coin if I go positive or negative here. XDLet me start with the positive sides of the game: * It is Actraiser! No really, the moment I saw there is a Remake I just had to try it out... and I usualy don't do Remakes. But considering the Uniqueness of Actraiser and its place in my heart, I just had to give this blast from the past a try, and I don't regret it: The Nostalgia is very real!They did a good job in bringing back the original world, both with its realms as well as with its action sequences. I always found myself excited to see what they did with that next realm that I still remember from the original. * The graphics: It's one of those hate it or love it things, I guess. A lot of people see the graphics of Actraiser Renaissance as negative point, but I personaly consider them a strong positive point. It has a very unique style, which needs some getting used to, but then both the Characters as well as the animations are quite likeable.I personaly enjoyed the use of parallax, some lighting effects (underbrush light in the woods, moonlight in Bloodpool Castle, etc) and the love for detail in some animations (like the blowdart-guys in Marahna). I think the graphics are not "bad" or "cheap/shody made", but are a stylistic choice which is well executed in itself. * The new music: Yeah, it rocks (a bit too much for some). I agree that it would fit Castlevania more at times ... but overall it is enjoyable. They even included the original soundtrack, so you can listen in comparison, if you like. Nice move!And if you really dislike the new music, you can just play the whole game in its Retro Music.If I have one gripe with the music, it might be the  feeling flat and less impactfull than in the original game. But meh, maybe thats just me and my heart shrivelling to an unfeeling plum in age or something. ;) * Mini-Acts:In Renaissance you dive into the monster generators to destroy them yourself in a small mini-mission. I think those are actualy a fairly fitting addition to the base game.Now the So~and~so: * The bonus realm. Which is a great transition to ... ... the bad things: * The Tower Defence. No really: I was considering if I should put it as good or bad point, as I think it is fairly well done, actualy, with a decent challenge on Hard Difficulty. So ... why am I rating it bad then?Well, I believe it does not fit the game.Don't get me wrong, I am a friend of diversity. I can enjoy Tower Defence Games, I like heroes and cool characters, I like cameraderie of Anime Characters with deep bonds ... but I am fairly peculiar when it comes to sequels of game series.I think a good sequel has to think hard about whats the "soul" of the game and has to design the game mechanics around those. Expand on strengths and uniqueness of the initial artistic vision.Well, Actraiser Renaissance didn't do that (from my point of view). It mostly put on a lot of make-up on a timeless classic and added some game mechanics "by the book" with little real inspiration. Tidy, yes, but kind of soulless.The Tower Defence in itself is well executed as game mechanic, no doubt, and it was interesting/nice to have an additional gamemode on those maps you still remember from the old Actraiser. But what does it change in the ~meaning~ of the game? In the original we have that world with pious inhabitants, which wouldn't dare lay a finger on forests or any other creation of their beloved god. They toil and try to live on any inch of land thats given to them by their creator and you get to like and love them for it. But in Renaissance they immidiately learn the most important human characteristic: Waging war!Suddenly those demons and devils, which beforehand were as untouchable to them as the rest of creation, become tangible opponents (even though they wouldn't border fighting anywhere else than at their towers and gateposts).I don't know, doesn't feel like Actraiser to me. * The Heroes:Same thing as with the tower defence. I ~liked~ them. They are well done Anime Characters, somewhat cliche here and there, but certainly they have their charms. BUT what is it they do with the overall story? They shift the focus on those toiling people to themselves. Not to mention how we directly control them (enforcing our divine will on them). Not something I believe a benevolent good god of light would ever do. In the original everything you do you have to do indirect with your miracles, and I believe there was quite some meaning to that. So ... while they were certainly technicaly well executed and likeable I do not believe they ~fit~ to the soul of the original game. I mean, alright, maybe seeing them as "prophets" or something makes the direct control alright (you do also directly control the angel after all), but still.... * The Quests:Quite honestly the worst change they did to the original. They put everything you can do neat and tidy into a Quest List.In the original you had to ponder how you can effectivly change the world for your flock. You had to listen, think, experiment a bit, go back and forth between realms and try to find interaction. I think, while less efficient, tidy and direct, there was meaning to that as well.But Renaissance is pretty much the "Checklist Simulator - God Edition". You are clearly told, what your godly duties are and have to work them step by step.  - check.  - check.  - che... wait, what? * Progress, huzzah!So, what else do we have as new exciting game design by the book? You guessed it:  Hunt Quests. Each realm will issue some "kill [number] xyz"-quests to make you revisit each act at least twice. So: In the original you had to descent in times of dire need and could only manifest for a short time, so the whole thing got some weight and meaning. In Renaissance you are the divine exterminator for your people. But hey, there are also other exciting quests! Like "collect x apples", quite a few times! Oh, and if you want all the achievements, you can always farm scrolls for some hours with "light" variants of the Tower Defence Mode. Whatever would any game be without farming? Surely too short!.......Ah well, and thats it. I hope you get why I feel very conflicted about my opinion for this game.Ill still give it a thumbs up though, because: Actraiser!No honestly, as I said initialy, the nostalgia was good for someone who enjoyed the original, and I can clearly imagine those who did not play the original enjoying the game aswell. And like I said before, the game mechanics itself are executed tidy, no doubt.

_childDocuments_.review: i think this is the best possible way they could have honored the original game while staying true to the spirit of it. i don't think it is perfect by any means, but to those who were fascinated by actraiser in the past, i strongly believe this game has a lot to offer. for everyone else, it's a maybe.i really don't share a lot of the complaints i've tended to see, as i personally thought everything about this was a neat little update to a classic game and had no objections to their additions. the art style of the platformer stages, which i recall having been somewhat maligned at the time, did not bother me while making my way through the stages. but i often feel that slightly less detailed or idiosyncratic graphics are somewhat interesting. it's like it came from an alternate version of the 90s or something.the rest of the character art is very pretty, anyway. the town building aspects are made more difficult with the inclusion of additional monster attack features and a tower defense-like aspect that requires you to hold off increasingly more harried sieges by greater and greater armies of demons. i felt like it did a good enough job of varying the objectives and offered a nice chunk of gameplay to do before you're allowed to go smash things in the platformer stages. additionally some characters are added which not only give some context to the plight of the humans inhabiting this world but also serves to grant the Master (and your mission to defend the townspeople with him) more weight and meaning.it can certainly get a little repetitive or stretched out, so in that sense it's not perfect as i definitely recall struggling to maintain my attention towards the end to finally get the game completed. generally when I think about games from this era, what i am looking for is a more tight and snappy experience that allows me to replay it and improve my skill. this takes a different tack, it instead offers what could conceivably be a modernized and fleshed out version of the game. it's almost like it is a version of actraiser that is bolstered by years of glorification of what was honestly a rather simple game. and that's for better and worse, depending on your outlook. i'm glad that i played this as i honestly expected it to be underwhelming when it appeared seemingly out of nowhere a few years ago. it does stick in my memory, it does have sick yuzo koshiro music, and imo i don't have any great ideas about how it could have been done any better. but i do wonder what those with no expectations would think. a retro platformer with RTS/tower defense/town building aspects is just a strange thing to consider, but i wouldn't shy away from telling anybody to try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a hell of a lot of downsides to it compared to the original on the SNES. The new music is easily the highlight of this version, with the very first theme of Fillmore being absolutely tops. Every other new addition is either a needless or unfortunately BORING addition.Being forced to go into each individual monster lair for at max 60 seconds to attack some glowing warts and then a giant glowing wart? In every new area, you are being held hostage by the storyline, somehow being too weak to drop into the next monster lair that's exactly the same as the previous ones. Only by arbitrarily sitting around and waiting for materials to drop and building defense buildings for the tower defense sections can you advance the storyline and get clearance to kill the next monster lair.Tower defense sections are horribly designed. I've never seen a tower defense game where you randomly can't build defenses in certain areas, yet in this game that's the second most damning thing that happened to me. I have screenshots of where you can place wooden barriers to temporarily stop monsters from going up that path, and there are constant times I just couldn't place any down on one section of road, giving the monsters free and unrestricted access to their goal.The number one annoying part of the tower defense sections was the randomly changing lose conditions. You can have anywhere from 1 to 4 lose conditions. Lose your temple, hero of that area gets defeated, all workshops destroyed, or all farms destroyed. You have zero control over where your workshops or farms are built, so it is INEVITABLE you're going to lose multiple times thru trial and error as you stumble your way thru the attack waves and finding out where the enemy teleports in at and acting accordingly. You may very well have to completely destroy your city and reroll the locations of where the farms/workshops end up, since some enemies can fly and nearly instantly destroy those buildings.If you can deal with the tower defense nonsense, the game is fine. The music kept me going but I absolutely couldn't recommend this to anyone who wasn't already a fan of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: It didn't scratch the nostalgic itch for me.The new mechanics doesn't make you feel like a god saving the people.Instead it makes you feel more like a person desperately trying to battle to save the people so they can believe you are a god. It's added difficulty but not in a good way as it's just more tedious requiring to do things I really don't want to do because I didn't do this in the original. Maybe if the option to turn off new mechanics would've been good. I've sat this down and not picked it back up in months.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR -- If you played and loved the original Actraiser on the SNES, this version will probably break your heart. I really, really, really wanted to love this game. I loved the original SNES version. I tried to roll with the new things they added, but I just can't do it anymore. I'm just not enjoying it. It's painfully un-fun after a while. I can't recommend anyone buy this, especially at full price ($30 USD is a bit much for what is essentially a worse version of a SNES game from 1990). The whole thing feels like a cash grab, and the only part that feels like any love was put into it is the remastered soundtrack. Everything else is pretty hit-or-miss (and mostly miss, sadly).--- PROS: ---- Remastered soundtrack is legitimately well done. Plus the option to hear the original soundtrack is great too.- Some of the graphical updates do make things look better (the world map looks quite nice for example)... but some do not.--- CONS: ---- The biggest one by far is the same one almost all others have complained about -- the horde settlement defense parts of the sim portions are truly awful. Boring, annoying, and repetitive busywork. This part was never in the original Actraiser and it was a terrible, terrible decision to add it to this remake. No one asked for this. Just a few points that make this part awful:   1.  The pacing is incredibly slow and boring,    2.  The cooldowns and wait times for SP for casting "miracles" is way too long during raids, leading to frequent lulls in the action where you're just watching baddies pummel structures while your heroes and defensive structures do whatever they do, and you do... basically nothing but wait.    3.  During some raids your miracles barely do enough to change the pace of the battle, if anything at all (even when they are highlighted as "effective" against the enemies you target).    4.  There's little to no real strategy involved in how you set up your defenses either. The predetermined placement spots for different defensive structures seems super random and frustrating (e.g., the game just flat out would not allow me to place anything defensive in the northwest section of Bloodpool for... reasons? Not even a lowly palisade. Nothing. ).  As a result, you often end up in the position where something placed ends up having zero strategic value during a raid, and you can't change it.     5.  These raids also happen way too frequently per settlement and seem to serve little purpose other than to drag out an already too-long city-building portion.- They added way too much filler content to the city-building, in terms of lots of dumb "quests", all the hero stuff, and accompanying dialogue. I honestly stopped reading most of the new dialogue because it's uninteresting, repetitive, and again way too frequent. The original game had a good serving of dialogue in the settlements, but this is a bit too much. The quests are just another form of bloat. They add pointless busywork to the settlement building (e.g., "build 5 workshops" --- sure but you can't explicitly direct your citizens to build workshops, so this quest is kind of meaningless. You just point to land squares and hope they build the thing you need.). - The pacing of the game really suffers as a result of all the settlement bloat, and it feels like it takes entirely too long to get back to action sequences. They tried to patch this by adding the "descend into a lair and destroy the spawner" schtick, but that gets repetitive too and just isn't all that fun to begin with. It's an ok idea, but it's executed really poorly here. - For some stupid reason the devs didn't bother to update the controls and general mechanics of the action portions. They added a couple of rudimentary little gimmicks like "renaissance actions", but they are forgettable and entirety of action sequence gameplay just feels "off" and very dated. Basically looks like they slapped a coat of paint on the same exact game from 1990. Contrast this with the way the devs of Streets of Rage 4 updated the controls, combat, and looks of the SoR game format and it's like night and day. SoR 4 plays like a dream and really feels like a modern take on a beloved game from the 90s. Actraiser Renaissance most definitely does not.- The new graphics are kind of bad in a lot of places, especially during the action sequences. With all the design choices and methods available, they for some bizarre reason decided to make a bunch of the assets look like cheap 3d models that came straight out of a Rare game circa 1998. Most monsters look straight out of Killer Instinct, and that is not a compliment. Their animations are similarly cheap looking and stiff. If you can get this at a steep discount (I'd say at least 70% off) during a Steam sale and you're curious, feel free. Otherwise, avoid this one and go play the original SNES version if you want to actually enjoy Actraiser.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original Actraiser on SNES, and this just doesn't hold a candle to it. The original did have occasions where a cutscene would interrupt what you're doing, but this version takes it to the extreme. There is also a ton of unnecessary padding. Originally the citizens would seal a monster's lair themselves, but now they just hold it open so you can go in to deal with it...usually in a minute or less. They also added in a tower defense minigame, which at first seems cool...but you have to do it at least 3-4 times in EACH area. It loses its appeal real quick. _childDocuments_.review: If you've ever been a fan of the SNES (Super Nintendo) game ActRaiser you will find this remake as a pretty good remake. Obviously the art-style has been updated, but the game also offers a lot more game play features that, in a way, actually add a lot to the city-building element of the original game. The greatest additions have been to the in-between battle stages, the city building part. First each region you build in has a distinct looking people, structures, and quests. Each region also introduces a new "hero" character that has their own plot develop as you build up the city. These heroes are useful for the second major addition to the city building part: the tower-defense mini games. To progress through the plot you have to deal with periodic raids by demons towards your town. During this time your city cannot develop, nor can you build additional major defensive structures. However, you can use  your hero to help defend the city, and also use your god-like powers. These mini-games can sometimes feel very repetative, however, they do offer a fairly challenging experience. Placing the correct defensive structures, and getting the hang of the best heroes and powers to use against the monsters is key. Side-quests also come into play in this game, and they further give you opportunities to enhance your main character's HP and MP, in addition to their level.As far as graphics are concerned, while the game has a major update to the original, I do feel like the game's Art-Direction was a bit lack-luster. The character sprites and animations usually are extremely well rendered, smooth, and high definition, sometimes very realistic. However, the backgrounds tend to be very static and sometimes extremely jarring. Specifically this becomes extremely noticeable in stages like Aitos Battle 1, where the backgrounds look like an early 2000s 3D Render, without any kind of movement. Meanwhile the characters are extremely detailed, beautifully rendered. On the other hand, other stages like the first one, is rendered out beautifully with nice atmospheric effects. The platforming element of the game is more enhanced. There are now bit of RPG elements included such as the amount of damage your doing, which can be modified by collecting crystals through killing monsters. Other elements are more attack movements, making it feel more action-orientated. However, just like the SNES version, there is still this odd weight to the character movements, which are easy to dismiss but sometimes become very noticeable. Difficulty wise the game is very balanced. I never felt like it was too easy, nor was I ever overly frustrated. The only thing that sometimes is missed is that mini-bosses, and major bosses may have weakness in when you can hit them, or even to the types of magic attacks you use against them. However, this is poorly conveyed and kind of has to be done through trial and error. I found one boss in particular annoying hard to fight because I was dealing so little damage to it - to discover that it was meant for the player to hit the head. Some magic is utterly ineffective and some is super effective, and what controls this is often difficult to figure out except trial and error.PROS:-An excellent example of a remake that has is true to it's original game's spirit, gameplay and direction.-Characters and Monsters are beautifully rendered and visually enjoyable to look at.-The Music is just absolutely gorgeous. 10/10 here.-Very good gameplay mechanic additions to the town-building element of the game, that keeps to the spirit of the original.-Expanded the story lines and immersion of the townfolk and heroes. (Now each culture looks distinct)CONS-Some background art is just jarring. Sometimes no consistency in it's direction.-Tower-defense mechanic is too frequent in pushing the story forward. -Movement and animation seems a bit sluggish - however not too much.-Some things are kept in the dark, without a visual signal what works and what doesn't.-No real replay value.NEUTRAL-Town building follows the same blueprint each time, with little variation, which is exactly like the SNES game. There are some improvements here: crafthouses produce resources needed for the forts and towers, and farms produce food and mana pick ups which are also very useful. But there is no means to control the ratio of farms to craft houses, and population is determined by the amount of farms. Overall, definitely a step in the right direction, however, could have used a bit more of player input.-Each stage has 3 permament HP/MP upgrades which you can find. This is a great addition to make you want to explore, however, if you move from room 1 to 2 there is no way to move back. Forcing you to miss the powerups with no way of getting them unless you replay the stage from the beginning. Which you can do even if you beat the stage.Overall:If you liked the original. If you got some cash to spend an want to relive the nostalgia with a VERY SOLID remake, this is a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: The initial impression of the 3D models may be off putting but you get used to it. This is how Remakes are meant to be done imho, updated gameplay with additional content like new characters, story lines, quests, boss fights(which are pretty easy on standard difficulty, just get to your Max Mana Crystal buff and spam magic spells at the right time.) I'm essentially at the endgame at 14 hours but there are still things to do in the various villages/cities if you revisit them. The City Manager part is still sorta automatic and doesn't really explain how to get certain things going so its a lot of waiting/experimenting to reach certain milestones but you can finish your objectives pretty easily without much worry. Its the endgame stuff that can take time. But for the main game its really solid outside of some frustrating battles where you essentially have to redo your Turret/Fort layout, not being able to build or move them during raids is a bit annoying but its not a deal breaker, and you get the resources back if you demolish them so its pretty forgiving.Overall I have to say its a solid game and you could do a lot worse for 30 bucks. But if you want to wait for a sale, go ahead, its not like you have to rush to play any game these days. But gets my approval.Edit: To 100% this game, you do sorta have to leave it running on city maps to get attacks to trigger so you can max level your heroes. I'll probably get around to doing that on a chill day.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes the new sidescrolling art looks like rejected assets from "Getting Over It with Bennet Foddy", but underneath its Actraiser and I had this game 30 years ago (good lord...) along with Pilotwings, Zelda A Link to the Past and Super Mario World for Christmas 1991. The music is great, the art  ....loads into vram correctly....., and the gameplay is classic Actraiser, I could have done without the tower defense mode, and the constant tutorial pop ups every 10 seconds in Filmore (I feel like it wasn't like that back on the SNES, who knows... maybe its "modern game design" creeping in).I would wait for a sale to under $20 if you're not a diehard fan, otherwise its Actraiser in a new coat of paint, and a re-orchestrated soundtrack (along with the option to use the original one).

_childDocuments_.review: When you look at the 2021 list of Game of the Year nominees then look back at this game, there's no reason why ActRaiser Renaissance doesn't belong. Square Enix took what's arguably a top 10 best SNES game and improved it.The soundtrack goes from a 10/10 to an 11, the gameplay is so much better thanks to new combo moves and content. The graphics are... Well, different, but they work in my book. The story is expanded via the introduction of new lovable characters, and even the bosses have some personality now. The new Tower Defense mode is fun to play in my opinion, but I understand some players dislike it, which is fair. And the extra content gives hints of DLCs which I personally can't wait for, even though I suspect they will not be made.In short, this game is my personal GOTY 2021 and there's no competition. Is it better than the original? I'm not sure. It's definitely easier, as I only died 4 times in Normal difficulty. Is it the most fun I've had this year? Yes, absolutely.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr 8/10 some hiccups but a good experience overall so farI played the original on the SNES and almost completely forgot about this game. I have a lot of fond memories of it, and was surprised to see it on the Nintendo Direct. Lo and behold, here it is on PC as well!As of this review I've completed Fillmore (chapter 1) and Bloodpool (chapter 2).Thoughts so far: Hits the nostalgia boner, hard. Overall gameplay feels much smoother and less clunky than the 1990 SNES version. Overworld is still the weakest part of the game (imo), and the Fillmore sections are over-tuned. I failed a few village sieges in Fillmore, but utterly destroyed them in Bloodpool. The difficulty curve is all over the place.The side-scrolling part was always my favourite part and it feels right at home, if a bit easier than I remember?The story has been improved, which albeit didn't take much to improve on. More characterization of the Angle and the citizens of the world, and the introduction of the new aforementioned village sieges during the City building part helped change up the most boring part of the original.The start is *very* boring. There's a lot of down time while waiting to get MP back, and feels like Fillmore could have used more time in the oven. Bloodpool felt much smoother of an experience.Overall my experience has been quite enjoyable and a massive trip down memory lane. I think it's worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I didn't like this game at first.The graphical style kind of irked me, the screen tearing was terrible, but most importantly the newly added stuff to the Sim portion of the game was really annoying and unnecessary padding. However, it gets better as you get further in. The game stops slamming you with constant tutorials and leave you to your own devices to speed things up and the tower defense stuff gets better as its painfully slow and easy at first, but by the time you get to Kassandora, it gets pretty challenging and engaging. The graphics even get better strangely enough. Soundtrack is awesome but that shouldn't be a surprise to anyone familiar with the original and the composer Yuzo Koshiro. Some bits like the monster lair mini stages just continue to suck, onyl getting slightly more challenging and not any less annoying. Also some of the boss difficulty and such is painfully easy. But Im actually enjoying it a pretty good bit now. Not the ideal remake for me but it should please most fans of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: The remake I never thought I'd live to see.I have fond memories of playing 'Soul Blazer' on the SNES as a kid, of which 'Actraiser' is its spiritual prequel. The concept of combining platforming and city-building is so weird, and yet it works. 'Actraiser Renaissance' even adds a new tower defense segment, so now you've got a game that's 3 genres in 1. It's a real treat for anyone who was a fan of Square-Enix back when they were just Enix and Square.'Actraiser' has you controlling a Judeo-Christian God-like figure who, along with your trusty cherub servant, is tasked with restoring the world after it's been devastated by (essentially) The Devil. Gameplay alternates between "Ghouls n' Ghosts"-esque 2D platforming and a "Sim City"-like world-building section. In the midst of the latter, your followers will occasionally come under attack by monsters hordes. This is where the most divisive new feature of 'Actraiser Renaissance' comes in: Raids.Before getting into the controversial stuff, let me touch on the improvements that most people can agree on: The lush new graphics and expanded orchestrated score. There's just no comparison between the remake and the original. Some people have qualms with the new anime art style for the characters, but honestly it didn't bother me. And if you prefer the original 'Actraiser' soundtrack, there's an option to toggle that too. The difficulty in the platforming segments has been increased, but so has The Master's abilities. You can pull off special moves and combos that were not present in the original game, and Magic is actually now slightly overpowered. Your character can increase their maximum HP and SP just like before, but now you can also increase your attack and magic power by collecting Crystals dropped by enemies.The city-building segments are where the biggest changes in the remake take place. You'll still travel from country to country constructing roads, buildings and using your Miracles to help along the way, but now there are Quests. Your followers frequently beg you to solve whatever problems ill them at any given moment. Answer their prayers and you'll get experience that'll allow The Master and his Champions to level up. Champions are brand new characters in 'Actraiser Renaissance' that act as a sort of liaison for the populace of whichever realm you happen to be in. Their backstories are rather uninteresting and their dialogue trite, but they do help out in Raids.Raids are the new tower defense game mode. As mentioned earlier, your population will come under assault from monster armies from time to time. Curiously, the angel is forbidden from assisting in this game mode even though he can attack monsters outside of Raids. It's up to The Master to construct forts and use Miracles to repel the invaders, who will attempt to destroy your fields and factories and, ultimately, your temple (automatic game over). A lot of reviewers are complaining about this mode. While they do get dicier in later parts of the game, I wouldn't say they truly frustrated me until the post-game content. The enemies are always the same and always spawn from the same areas of the map. Even if you fail, you can retry the Raid as many times as you want and adjust your strategy and units accordingly.'Actraiser Renaissance' is a pleasure to play, introducing a lot of new depth and variety with extra features and an expanded storyline, while still retaining the feel of the old game. If anything, it might be a little TOO faithful to the original title. But my only real complaints are the repetitive, long-winded dialogue and the difficulty in leveling up your Champions due to a lack of random Raids.Here's to a 'Soul Blazer' remake in the near future!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like ActRaiser Renaissance, as it makes an admirable attempt to add more to the original ActRaiser. But ultimately, one of ActRaiser's greatest strengths was its tight pacing, and that is completely gone here. This adds copious amounts of extra content, but none of it is particularly interesting, and it just slows the game down.I also have mixed feelings on the new graphics, which are sort of charmingly ugly, like a collage of cutouts from a magazine. I really want to like it, but then I keep getting hit by grey on grey spikes that blend in with the background. The new level design is adequate but not great - there are quite a few enemy setups that trap you into getting hit. I do like the new sword attacks, but I just can't bring myself to play more knowing I have at least a half dozen tower defense sections to go.This game is very close to being good - there just needs to be less of it.

Also, most of the map secrets are gone or turned into quests you can't fail.The new story bits are semi-interesting.Conclusion, play it for the hack n slash parts.  Wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: i dont know what they were thinking making this in the 90s for a snes but this game rulescity builder, tower defense, 2d side scroller? insane combo. no idea who thought it was a good idea for that console, but they decided to remake it for something that can handle more than the snes can and its good. its really good. play this game
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: While I did love the original, adding in an extra layer of story and characters that shouldn't be there to pad it out was a bad choice. The Tower Defense portion, plus the added going into monster spawners is so forced and off putting that it just destroys the pace of the game and there to just give the new unnecessary characters face time. The fact you can't just get rid of monster spawners as you wish like before is a major detractor as well and a big mood whiplash. In the end it is what it is, but I can't really recommend this game to people who played the classic game. If you're new to this series, enjoy it for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the original Act Raiser on SNES / Super Famicom then you're going to like this for sure. They added onto the original with additional city building elements, and a tower defense mode, which, thinking back to the original, is a perfect and creative extension of the original game model in sim mode. It feels natural to be there, like it could have been in the original game, nothing feels out of place to me. Some of the comments are complaining of graphics issues, I am playing at 2560x1440, no frame-cap, vsync off, GSYNC monitor and I have no tearing / FPS drops / stuttering, so for me it's a win. Square-Enix, we've been estranged for a while, you almost made me hate you a few times, but if you keep making games like this I think we can fall in love again.Update: Getting a bug transitioning to the first boss from the save screen in Bloodpool Act 1, currently unplayable.Update 2: Set FPS from unlimited to 60 and the bug stopped, what would happen is the MC would enter the screen, fall into the blood and keep running endlessly. It looks like a race condition in the code tied to FPS. Can't recommend this game until they fix silly bugs like this.Update 3: 240 FPS limiter seems to work without any bugs. I'm running the game on an RTX 3080 so perhaps they just did not play-test on higher-end hardware. I'm going to toggle back to recommend, with the *sigh* of I wish they would have done a better job at QC, and I hope they patch it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's...fine. I was a huge fan of the original. The action sequences feel worse to me, and they definitely look worse. The graphics for the action sections of the original still hold up, this won't. It's the opposite for the sim sections. This looks and plays much better. _childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This is a $30 port of a mobile phone game. Which about 80% has faithfully transferred over with no hitch. The problem is the 20% that pretty much ruins the entire experience.What made it over faithfully and works as intended:- The music- Sound Effects- The Story- The Graphics Interface- The backgrounds (the ones very far in the background)- Some of the particle effects- Core game mechanicsThe bad:- Character Sprites- Level art- Boss SpritesMany people would say the issue is because of the 3D pre-rendered art style. Those people would also be 100% wrong. Pre-rendered sprites has been a staple of the industry in that parts of a sprite is saved on the data and re-assembled. The issue is not the art style:The screenshots of the game look much better in the store page when in the preview mode and not full screen. It gives the impression that the art assets will scale up to match such an image when the game is running at full screen. Which is understandable for mobile phone game, as not everyone is going to be willing to free up a lot of space for a single game on their phone.Which is just very confusing that the developers would release the PC version of the game with identical assets as the mobile phone version of the game... as like mentioned previously all the other graphic interfaces do scale properly and it only makes the experience of playing the game more jarring as the GUI pops out even more over the lower pixel density art assets.So at this point, I think that either the developers were rushed to get the game to market and messed up the code of the game to not trigger higher resolution assets, or that one way or another higher resolution assets were not included in the build of the game that was sent to Steam.Its pretty obvious to see compression artifacts in the sprites, which reminds me of the game Blaster Master: Overdrive... But that game was limited to WiiWare and capped to 40MB... so it is hard to understand why this game at almost 4GB cannot have nice looking sprites.The terrain you walk on as it looks like home brew from the early 2000's, and this lower resolution assets just really hurts the action part of the game and a bit of the sim-mode too.Again, fans of the game might be able to overlook the graphics of the action part of the game and enjoy the game for what it is. There is a good game underneath it all, but I would not see an average person putting the work to get to the point that they will forgive the poor presentation.But for $30, and being published and co-developed by Square Enix... There is a lot left to be desired.I cannot in good faith recommend this game to the general public in the state that it is in... Hopefully the developers fix this as this would have been the perfect game to spark interest in the series. I am sure it looks great on a 5" or 8" screen... but the sprites look terrible even on a 25" one.If they do I will update the review.

_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I have very fond memories of playing SNES in my room on quiet weekends. Actraiser is one of those great memories, and one of the best SNES games. I've played through it a good handful of times, and enjoyed every minute of it.Now we get the remake of it, and I have been hesitant to pull the trigger because of a major change in the game. But I did get it with a hope I would still love it. I didn't. And what ruined it? That new feature:Tower defense. The game looks "nicer" by looking horrible and off in movement. That is fine. The SNES is still amazing looking even though it is so graphically outdated due to its age. It still holds so much life to it. This looks like a mess. But like said...that is fine.The side scrolling action is a little boring. The first boss is an absolute joke. The idea of descending into the monster lairs is actually interesting...until you find out it is over just as quick as watching the game load to get into the lair.The top down city creation is....not as good as the first. Locking monster lairs based on population just makes it drag way too long. The arrow has a weird curve to it. Sometimes it helps...other times though it made a straight shot miss.Then comes the tower defense. I never liked strategy games like this. But even if I did...it feels so completely out of place, that the whole flow of the game just grinds to a halt. I just sat there watching as enemies just poured out, waiting for SP items to replenish so I could smack them with magic...weee.Here is the 100% truth here: if you ever played this on SNES and have fond memories of it....do not touch this version. if you want to play this game again....take another route. I am not saying to do anything illegal...just don't do this version. If you have never played Actraiser and want to start...I recommend doing the same steps I just listed for those that have played it. I just hope I can wash my mind of this version so that the Actraiser legacy is not tarnished.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I suggest purchasing this immediately, with several Caveats:You were a huge fan of the original (as I was) and miss the simplicity and joy of what that Game provided.Oh, right. That's only one caveat.It's a big one though - Actraiser was a huge part of my childhood and the trip down memory lane was worth every single penny in this case. If you're new to Actraiser, and if you're going into it expecting something on par with modern 2D Action/Platformers / God Sims - you'll be disappointed.If you want a decent game to spend some time with, wait for a sale.If you were a fan of the original, you should play this and love it just as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often we get a de-make calling itself a remake, but every few years it happens.  What surprised me the most, however, is they managed to take an elementary yet polished Quintet game & make it look, feel & play worse than the original.  Remember the early super nintendo title Actraiser?  Too bad, now it's a graphic novel that's also a freemium-grade tower defense simulator!  To whoever bashed this together (the credits were only like 10 names long, which is wildly inappropriate considering the original credits should have been included), the short script of the original wasn't an oversight or a hardware limitation, it was BY DESIGN.  Not to patronize the player, but to let them discover things for themselves.  Not to be a party to tribalist disputes, but to hear the occasional prayer from the NPC's worthy of godly action.  There were a lot of design/themes in the original carried over from other Quintet projects in the original that were bastardized or outright ignored.  Granular HP/SP display to truly gauge a feel of progression rather than just seeing a number in the corner then seeing them bleep out in order after the boss & give you extra points.  The fact that town leveling wasn't only held back with triggers, but gave you additional SP as you grew.  The population summary screen that told you when you hit max population.  The sky palace UI that made you feel like you were using Windows 95 in Nintendo 92.  Now, everything has it's own EXP bar, even the buildings.  I had hoped the additional content post-game would redeem it but then the 2nd to last raid happened & I was all '& that was actraiser'.   On the graphic novel aspects.  Sure, the script is TERRIBLE, throwing ye olde engilishe at thou art savior inconsistantly & occasionally (often) throwing in a non-denominational prayer or scripture at you, but they went fringe weird anime on the artstyle.  FRINGE WEIRD ANIME.  Every town sequence felt like I was watching one of those japanese cult god animes the youtubers dump all over, but this was LAZY.  Singular frames occasionally animated on the xy axis, nothing more.  I'd like to remind all of you this used to be a mode 7 game with plenty of groundbreaking effects.  This is a game where you can tell upfront that they blew through 80% of the budget on the opening sequence, & renting the orchestra.6/10 the soundtrack was barely (BARELY) better than the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to anyone who is a bit nostalgic, but if you're only used to modern games, this might not satisfy you at all.The mechanics are a bit clunky for a modern remake and i would wish for a lot more quality of life improvements, especially for the "building mode". I often waited for a long time until the angels mana replanished or resources popped up and felt like wasting time, instead of actually playing a game.The platforming-parts of the game are actually quite good and fun, but even here you can feel that they tired to capture the old nintendo-feeling, instead of making a nice experience for new players. (games like blasphemous or dead cells show, that it's still possible to get a good retro-feeling while using new elements and mechanisms)Overall I still had a few hours of fun and would say.. it's not really good, but more a "yes" then a "no".

_childDocuments_.review: The Actraiser Renaissance is pretty awesome.  I played the OG Actraiser game years ago. The gameplay and graphics are really good, it stays true to everything from the original. They have revved it up with a more in depth plot, so you end up having a more involved story line where you can connect with the characters a little deeper than in the original game. One main example I can think of is that when building your town, you periodically have extra quests you must complete. There are enemies trying to destroy your temple, so you have the task of placing fortifications around. You also have a hero to help your defense. Both are new elements that didn’t exist in the original. It has a little bit of a flavor of a strategy wargame thrown into a quest based kill the monster type game.The graphics are really well done, it stays true to the original enemies, dungeons, bosses, over world map and so on. ￼I’m a fan of anime. I love how they have made all the characters in that style. I think it really adds to the overall feel and aesthetic of the game. A big plus to me… they have kept the old music 🎶 it’s just so much better now. Remastered, but just like the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, here's the thing...This remake is really good, could be a good standalone game and is... some of the graphics are weird though, like it was a PSP or VITA game during development and changed teams... but that's ok.  The music is great and there are story and gameplay refinements that are excellent.But it's not the original Actraiser.Ok, The action stages are excellent outright - a flatout improvement over the original.  You get combos, the magic system is refined and there's even a nifty mechanic where after you cast a spell your melee attack also deals that element for a short time... I like it, I hope they keep this in the Soulblazer remake.The problem/non-problem is the SIM stages.  The art is great and the story is more verbose (which is good for these days, but bad for the old days where you just wanna play), but the biggest sin in SIM mode is you don't really have any personal agency since the sealing of monster lairs is handled by quests... plus, the plot revolves around not having to overly rely on "God" to handle your problems; leading to some serious Ludonarrative Dissonance where in the original your people were a LOT more self-sufficient and the few things you do as a God could almost be shrugged away as coincidence/natural occurance... made you really feel like a "Hidden Mover".However, they counter this structured format by catering to the strengths of structured levels by adding siege battles where your towns come under attack... which is really cool.  I like it.  But at the same time there's a ton more dialogue/script...  to put it another way, in the OG Actraiser you could beat the entire game in about an hour, and in the remake where you can do the action stages EVEN FASTER, the SIM stages take several hours EACH, even when skipping all text (which I did start doing by Kasandora).  In addition, the 'secrets' you would solve in the original are now spelled out for you via quests removing some of the fun/mystery.But... it's good.  This is as good as I could hope for an Actraiser Remake.  The changes I don't like aren't really because they are bad, it's just that they are supporting modern gaming sensibilities.  Some of the stuff in this game would NEVER fly in the SNES days just like a game as short as the original would never sell for AAA prices nowadays...  so all things being equal, both versions of the game are exactly what we needed.

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game. i always wanted to play its OG version but never had a SNES... my cousin had it, but our grandma never let anybody play his systems. finally, thanks to this remake, i can see wat i was missin.. n its great.pretty easy on normal mode but thats cool for a casual playthru. classic 2d platformer action on one half, cool city builder on another. controls feel responsive, i like new tech that was added(option to turn off for a more classic feel is a great bonus), new music sounds great(option to play classic snes tunes was another great touch), new graphics look pretty good. its an addictive game. it feels great to help a community grow n watch em thrive. it feels great to smite evil so our ppl can live peacefully. game simply feels great. highly recommend. i recommend it so much, i bought it on steam even tho i already beat it prior... so i can enjoy it fresh all over again.
