_childDocuments_.review: This is not merely an HD remake of Actraiser, but almost a reimagining. All of the old elements are present, yes, but so are a lot of new ones. As someone that loved Actraiser back in the day, I initially cringed at the presence of a tower defence minigame during the settlement building segments, but the more I played, the more I began to appreciate the way in which they had expanded the vision of what Actraiser is. They absolutely understood the "spirit" of the original. Now, that original was no short game, but this reimagining is truly epic, and despite my initial feelings, I've come to absolutely love what they've done here, and lets face it, despite the way that some might complain, few would go back to the original Actraiser now that this is available. The platforming sections are particularly fluid and fun in this incarnation. I can only encourage purists to persist and newcomers to get ready to experience one of the most memorable games ever created for the first time. Here's hoping that they "reimagine" Actraiser 2 as well, but that seems unlikely, since I'm one of the few that loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful remake of the SNES classic. I've played past Fillmore into Bloodpool on my first play and am absolutely engaged with this charming remake. They really have done an incredible job of bringing the classic back with a modern take. Keep in mind, this is basically a straightforward remake of the original that is very faithful to the core mechanics. If you're looking for something super complicated, this isn't it...but for fans of the original Actraiser, it's a very enjoyable game and worth the buy.There are several useful additions to the original mechanics. The graphics are a welcome upgrade and have some great effects. The action graphics are a bit blocky but I see what they were going for. It works for me...and they've added some very cool effects to everything to include the character, backgrounds and magic effects. I especially like the backgrounds in the scrolling portions. The town building portions look great and are quite well done. I love watching the little characters run around. I enjoyed the town building and especially the sieges which actually have some depth in how you lay down your defenses. It's not Civ but it updates the original's gameplay without getting too complicated.In addition, the character art is really good and varied for each town. Of special note is the incredible soundtrack which was always ripping...the action track is pure nostalgia with an updated sound. Good stuff and if you don't dig it, then you can switch the the SNES OG soundtrack in the menu.  I'd have to say thus far that it's worth the price for anyone who was a fan of the original. And if you're not old enough to remember, you could do worse. I think it was mainly made for fans but it certainly still has major appeal. Good job!------------***Oh and a tip with the screen tearing some folks were complaining about...take off vsync and crank it to Unlimited for FPS. Immediately eliminated all of the tearing for me.***
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: The second game that I played on my SNES was the original Actraiser and I was instantly hooked. Actraiser Renaissance contains a lot of the old game, but is nonetheless very different from its predecessor. This could be a problem for everyone hoping that Renaissance will satisfy their trip to memory lane. For everyone that has never played it, this is a great game and I recommend it. It's still an action platformer with a city builder element, but with quite some changes.The music got an upgrade. But if that is too much for you, you can switch it back to the snes versions. I like the upgraded music a lot. I would even dare say that was the best upgrade to the game.The game has gotten a graphical update and the lord of light has some new moves. You can now dodge attacks by dashing, making the game almost too easy. The bosses also move very differently from the original. I found the game very easy as the original was more about recognizing patterns and moving accordingly and now you can just dash or spam magic.The city sim part of the game is also very different from the original. You can still place the roads yourself and wait for your citizens to build the houses, farms and workshops. However a tower defense and hero system are added in Renaissance. The heroes basically add more story to the game and are used in the tower defense part of the city builder. In the original the city sim was also more "free". You got to choose which lairs you wanted to close and you didn't have to worry about farms and workshops being built. In renaissance however, everything is dictated by quests. While they are not too hard to complete, they make the game a lot more linear. For example, lairs can't be closed whenever the player feels like it. A quest to close the lairs has to pop up first.- nice new graphics- lairs are now mini games, that you close with the lord of light- new moves for lord of light- new magic powers- bonus act and realm not in the original- special mode is nice, but still easy even on divineThe only cons for me really were the newly added monster raid system and quests. In general I feel the quests, monster raid and heroes were added to add more content to the game and make it last longer than it should have. The acts are easy and short and the city sim could have been shorter if it wasn't for all the hero dialogues and monster kill quests. But I guess that might be my bias for having played the original. I do recommend the game as I did enjoy it and I loved the upgrades it has gotten.The monster raids are annoying sometimes, as you never know where monsters will be coming from untill you actually get raided. This means that towers might be ill-placed. in some levels the monsters just chew away your towers and defenses like they are nothing or you are stuck with a weak hero. This happened to me in Marahna. I had to play all the other realms first to even stand a chance in the Marahna raids.The problem I have with the hero system is the amount of dialogue and text it adds. The original already had the problem that every event triggered a dialogue. In Renaissance however, I spent most of my time clicking away the hero dialogue text and angel text. The city sim could be improved by removing or disabling a lot of the hero dialogue and angel text. Though interesting, I felt the amount of text was just too much.There are so many quests that are just about defending the city from monsters. And outside of quests there are also randomly started raids, which you have to do. They are easier and also required to level your heroes, but that makes it feel like a forced mechanic. Why not just leave out the defense quests and have more randomly occuring raids.Lots of quests, where you had to kill monsters in the acts, felt useless. Play an act 2 or 3 times to just kill 12 of a certain type of monster, while the act only contains 6 of them for example. The only reason for completing quests is to level your heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mixed bag but overall I recommend it if you're a fan of the original and curious to try it out, but if you never played the original and wanted to skip it, you wouldn't be wrong to do so.I am a big fan of the original ActRaiser. This remake changes 4 things besides the updated graphics and music and I think only one of them makes it actually any better.1) The good one: The plot. It adds hero characters to each level and I think that's a great addition. It fleshes out the plot in each one which sometimes is thoughtful but at the very least is interesting.2) The sieges. I hate the sieges. While it's nice that there's something different to do in the city aspect - you have so little control over where you can place buildings, either the AI does it for you, or you are abitrarily restricted on where you can place things like gate houses. And there's just too many of them, over and over again in the plot and then also just if you take too long doing the city building aspects3) The "side stuff". What I mean are the extra quests and I'm also throwing in the little spawner dungeons. They're just padding. Between the city telling you to collect 10 fruit when you have no control over when fruit spawns, to the boring and pointless spawner mini dungeons you have to do while sealing monsters lairs. There's just no point to any of it and it does nothing to help the game.4) I think the graphics are great. The new nationalities they gave each of the nations is a wonderful touch. The updated music and slightly updated moveset is also great. The change to the way levelling works is a bit underwhelming though.Overall, it's fine, is it better than the original? That's a hard thing to say. In the end, I don't think so. The original's graphics and music may be old but it was also a tighter overall stronger experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: What could have been a really good remaster/remake of an SNES classic is instead marred by an attempt to expand the games runtime by inserting a bunch completely annoying and unfun tower defense sections between story quests. The result IS a longer game.. but one that I ended up really having a hard time picking back up as each chapter only makes the sections less and less tolerable.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Woke up this morning and discovered one of my all time favorite games got a remake. It's not a remaster either - it's a proper remake with new gameplay mechanics and a totally different artstyle that just scream 'Castlevania'. It adds tower defense mechanics, expands on the story and adds several characters, and also tightens up the action sequences. It looks like some kind of upscaled GBA game - I love its quirky art direction which just screams '90s'. The music is some of the best around - completely orchestrated with the option to use the original soundtrack from the SNES. I don't have any complaints. Summary 9/10 - God go chop, angel go pew pew. humans go scamper scamper scamper.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid remake of the first, bringing us the platforming/town duo with today's graphics. I played through the game and had a blast with both portions. The tower defense sections were interesting and made the town portion more enjoyable. Overall, if you've played the original or want to get into Actraiser, this game is a great bang for your buck. Only (minor) complaint is that your model on the platforming sections looks low resolution or has a bunch of aliasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I was starstruck when I saw this announcement, it was so surprising, not only because I loved the game for SNES, but when a game like ActRaiser gets a "remaster", it opens the door for many more.Doubt grew quickly that this game is any good, besides the soundtrack, which is superb again.It is apparent that this game originally would have been a phone game. Graphics scale horribly, everything looks spongy and muddy, it's awful. Gameplay wise I cannot see any nuance of what used to be here.A free of charge phone game would have been a nice treat, a half assed 30 bucks "remaster" butchered into pc format is a joke, or an insult, depending on your viewpoint.I have never refunded a game on steam for the decade I'm using this platform......until I bought this game.If you really want to get into this game, you'd still have to buy a SNES and an ActRaiser cartridge.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: You are a god that cleanse evil and help humans to prosper in order to kill the big bad guy, originally a SNES game.There's side-scrolling action phases, where you cut demons and stuff.Then you have a lite-sim-city phase where you protects your believers while your guide them.Nice :- Graphics are not too bad if you don't dislike the "fake 3D" style.- Actions phases are as solid as the original, and spells were rebalanced.- The building phase is comfy even if still a bit shallow.- Magnificient character art.- Remastered musics are pretty good.- Added some story fluff and some backgrounds to the new characters.- There's some new end-game content.Very based :You must force the humans to upgrade their old homes by smiting the ever-living-hell out of them.Bad :- They added a tower-defense like phase during the building parts. And honestly it barely works. I see what they tried to do with it but it's just mediocre and quite the pushover after the 3rd world, mechanics makes barely sense.I loved the original, and I enjoyed this one quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: OK, that game is ugly, with prerenderd CG's just out of the 90's. But if you can go past its looks (and survive the initial hour of quasi-uninterrupted tutorial), you'll find a solid hommage to Quintet's original blend of a god-game and an action sidescroller, which expands on the formula in many regards and manages to throw a lenghty storyline in the mix as well.Cherry on top, legendary composer Yuzo Kojiro is back at the helm to revisit his work from 30's years ago and provide many new tracks in both orchestral and SNES style.An imperfect, flawed game that grows on you and ends up being surprisingly engaging if you give it a chance to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the original Actraiser on SNES before and was really addicted to it at the time. Simple, fun gameplay with variety between the city builder and the 2d platformer action sections. What this game has done is take a really excellent SNES game and remastered it into a really excellent PSX game. If you liked the original Actraiser, this one will not disappoint. If you haven't I definitely recommend Actraiser: Renaissance. Lots of fun for a reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game when I was younger, must have beaten it a few times.  This version looks beautiful in comparison.  It is updated for today while keeping the classic look to everything.  The one gripe I have is the tower defense modes.  I am not a huge fan of tower defense games, and more than half this game has become a tower defense game.  Every map has you going through about 5 tower defense battles and they can get hectic.  It would probably be better if they would give you a run down of the mobs that are coming and what their weaknesses are so you can prepare and strategically place towers better, but they give you no advance information.  You get thrown into it and have to wing it.  The good thing is if you lose, you can just restart the fight, or go back to the map to better space out your defense structures.  It is not game over and reload your last save.  If there was some option to reduce the number of these fights, or maybe a game mode to eliminate them, I would enjoy it much more since it would be closer to the original game.Otherwise, it is a solid game that stays true in many ways to the original game that came out 34 years ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Actraiser Renaissance is a whole lot of poor design choices rolled into one in an attempt to modernize the game. Instead, it slows it down immensely and tacks on a lot of down time needlessly. The first action sequence features a ton of plaques to read. I was ready to read a little needless background lore. What I got instead was such great tutorial moments such as "Press the jump button to jump." or "Press down to crouch and avoid attacks." I guess I'll be able to replay those stages, though, should I forget how to jump or crouch along the way. Then, when you reach a checkpoint, you'll know it because it's a physical point in the game that breaks up the action rather than just a place where you respawn upon death with a feeling of "oh, cool, I don't have to do that one part over again." You don't need to spell it out. It just needs to be. This is the gaming equivalent of taking pictures of your meal. Don't do it. Just don't. It's pointless and just shows you don't know how to just be in a moment. Simulation mode has went from a nice little break from the action that was sorely missed in Actraiser 2 and turned into an absolute chore that makes me not want to play the game. For instance, the Master's level is no longer attributed the number of followers that the villages gain. So, why the hell am I burning down my villagers houses and crops? Maybe I'm not far enough in for populations to be relevant, but being forced to complete a bunch of quests to advance the story has needlessly extended playtime. I don't care about their faith. I care about their numbers. How dare you fetch quest me with this crap!Villagers are no longer able to seal monster lairs alone. You have to go in and physically hack away at the lair's core. Why do these villagers have no agency? Moreover, why the hell are a bunch of goblins hanging around in a Blue Devil's nest? Don't they know Blue Devils live there? Progress in simulation mode, which used to be non-linear, has become linear. Perhaps later stages will allow me to pick and choose which lairs to destroy first so I can eliminate the problem, but I have a feeling that they won't. Then, should I decide to end the problem by destroying the lair, I get rid of an easy source of SP points that then bottleneck my terraforming progress. The original would restore some SP between building sessions, so we're slowed down even further for no good reason. Then there's the other additions of tower defense and village heroes. Wow, what a slog! Maybe at higher levels it will be interesting, but right now it's just adding spots to bottleneck the flow and using the Master's abilities as a failsafe. It's not fun. It's not hectic. It's just there, multiple times per village, slowing down your path to progress. The hero needs directions, just like all the villagers, because they are lost without religion and cannot function. I just don't get it. It's bad enough that the graphics are some amalgram between pixels, polygons, that motion blur from Symphony of the Night, and the CGI from the Donkey Kong Country. How do you add so many frames to a walk animation and manage to make it look lifeless? It just looks bad. It looks like a project by a bunch of amateur developers, which I suppose may be what Sonic Powered is, but this game just deserves better. It doesn't need to be more than it was. It could have easily passed with hand drawn art with the same stilted animation. Bosses have new mechanics. I guess that is an attempt to fix old design of boss gimmicks, but adding some rocks so I can jump over a charging centaur who can't turn around when someone is hacking away at him from behind doesn't seem modern. It's just adding a new wrinkle to old design that somehow makes it feel out of touch with what made the game special. Want to modernize it? Have the centaur stop trying to shoot lightning while being chopped to bits. I guess that's why we have new mechanics in the up slash, down slash, and back dash. So, way to bring us up to the late-90s all the way from the mid-90s. All you need now is some bad voice acting by people who clearly weren't voice actors.I've been let down by my nostalgia getting in the way of my decision-making in the past. I'm impulsive and love Actraiser. I love the remakes soundtrack. That's honestly the only positive thing I have to say. A soundtrack that was among the best of the Super Nintendo era managed to not be destroyed in the process of modernization. Everything else? It's just a shadow of what it once was. I just don't get who the target audience is.This game sucks. I just can't believe how bad it sucks. If there's a way to place the new soundtrack into the SNES game, someone just make that rom hack. I'll gladly pay $30 for that. This, though? This is some mobile-level garbage that just took a dump on my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: There are two types of successful remakes: those that capture the essence of the original game, but don't change much, and those that take the opportunity to expand and improve upon the original.This is most definitely in the second of those categories. It effectively preserves the unique multi-genre gameplay of the original, then combines it with new characters, adorable angel dialogue and slightly higher challenge more appropriate to modern, adult gamers. The dialogue is tasteful, yet appropriate. You do get worshipped by some, tolerated by others, and your existence denied by yet others. There is quite a lot of dialogue, but it makes sense for the world, as you are hearing the prayers of an entire civilization. People talk/pray/complain a lot.They seemed to take all of the small elements in the original game, like the hero in Fillmore, and built them out into more developed people, with stories, flaws and backgrounds, like those in actual mythology. As for the action and challenge, I played on normal difficulty, as an avid Metroid player, and I only died a few times during Acts.If you're looking for more aggressive retro platforming challenge, I'd probably play on Hard. I felt like Normal was a better pick for me simply because - your character is an actual god, and should have power to match. That's part of the fun of these games to me, so I tend to select a difficulty that I believe most represents an appropriate ratio of power between the character and the world.Another area that was added on was a tower-defense mode. I love tower defense games like Sanctum, Dungeon Defenders and X-Morph: Defense, so if you like those, you will probably like those mini-games. Once in a while, there's a semi-cheesy battle, where the enemy does something unexpected like send all fliers without hinting that is coming, resulting in a loss. However, the game is respectful of time and lets you reconfigure your setup and retry as many times as you want without losing progress or resources.In general, if you enjoy grandiose stories, real-world mythology, platforming and/or civilization building, this would be a good pick for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: The release of this game is a surprise to say the least. As a fan of the original, this is more or less what I would have expected from a good remake.The gameplay of the original has been expanded in several small areas. It's as if they looked at the original and thought; "how can we make THIS aspect more interesting/less frustrating." This goes for the action stages as well as the city building sections. The game is just thicker in content than the original, and none of these additions really seems unnecessary or unwelcome.The original composer, Yuzo Koshiro, is back with a vengeance. The entire original soundtrack has been remade with an orchestral score, and the original soundtrack is available in case you prefer it. And, as a welcome addition, all the new content that called for new music means that he also wrote 16-bit versions of the new songs to stay in the style of the original soundtrack. It's really a rare treat.The one big gripe that I've heard about the game is the graphics. They've been compared to something akin to a cheap mobile game. And to be clear; I 100% agree with this assessment. I can see where love and care was put into this game. It feels, and sounds good. But, it definitely doesn't look good. The models for environments and creatures seem really slapdash and uninspired.In spite of it's graphical shortcomings, I think this game is fun as hell, and it warms my heart. I have been hoping for many years to see the unique gameplay fusion of Actraiser to see a resurgence. And, I'm happy to say, this delivered.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: All the nostalgia from the original title, plus a few extra elements that spice it up.  The only complaint about the new elements are that there are too many sieges, adding too much of a RTS/Tower Defense element that is fun a little bit, but it becomes a major time drain in terms of the game's pacing.For those who never played the original title; this title blends multiple game elements of hack and slash action, then a town building sim element, and now a bit of tower defense.  The difficulty scaling is legit, with Easy being very Easy for people looking to chill, and harder difficulties for those who want a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: A lovingly crafted and faithful remake of the cult classic SNES game.  It took me about 24 hours to complete all main and side story content, which is reasonable for the $30 price tag.  The core gameplay is more or less identical to the 1990 original, with some well thought out additions.  The sidescrolling action segments feature some improvements from ActRaiser 2 as well as a few other small tweaks.  The realm management is fleshed out with tower defense/light RTS gameplay so you have more to do than just fly the angel around.  There is an entire 7th realm after completing the original areas, which has been well executed.The music, of course, is sublime.  Yuzo Koshiro is one of the best living video game composers and he has not only rearranged the original soundtrack but also added new tracks as well as extending a few of the originals.  To make things even better, all the new tracks and extensions were composed for the original SNES soundfont and then rearranged, so each track on each version of the soundtrack is a stylistic match with its fellows.The art style seems to be divisive but I have no qualms with it.  In cutscenes characters follow a fairly typical and inoffensive modern anime style, some are better than others and I suspect that to be due to using a few different outsourced art studios for the game assets.  In game everything is pre-rendered 3D objects converted to sprites, which I think works wonderfully for this project.  It's a nice in-between of the original 16bit sprites and modern 3D graphics.  Each realm, with the exception of the new 7th one, has unique buildings and townsfolk.On the technical side, the port is good.  There's all the usual options you'd hope for on a PC release including fps limits, independent audio sliders, and a decent array of resolutions.  I had no crashes during my playtime and performance was always solid.If you didn't enjoy the original ActRaiser you probably won't like this.  If you haven't played the original ActRaiser $30 probably seems a bit steep, go play the first one and then decide.  If you've played and enjoyed the original ActRaiser I cannot recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game. I really wish. I love the original with all my heart, and I still prefer playing it rather than the remake. The reason is simple: pretty much everything they added detracts from the experience rather than improves it. The graphics, well, I don't love them but I see how this is an improvement to most people. But the lukewarm (towerish) defense gameplay? Nah, that's just something nobody asked for, or needed.Only the music is dope, but that's not quite enough to make me tell you to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: The retro remake from the SNES era returns!  Overall does it do the original justice?  It does!  New overall on graphics, music (even the option of original snes music), extra content and re-polishes.  Perhaps the two biggest changes is the character development and siege mode in the Sim mode.  Siege mode is a mini game that plays like an RTS.  It's a nice addition.  The only negative thing about it, is they throw more than there should be.  Perhaps 3-4 to would be nice vs 4-6.  It was the only hardest thing of the game.  The action stages are well done and are just as challenging with a few twists and turns.If you're completistionist that content is back as well from the original as well as bonus content, which I found a pleasant surprise. I hope they bring back the rest of the series such Soul Blazer and Illusion of Gaia and the long OVERDO release of Terriaminga.  7/10.  Very worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of an old SNES game. I think the remake is well done. I give it a B. The city building is very enjoyable and has good graphics. It also has a story and cute drawings of the people. They have added a tower defence mode which could have been better because there is so little to do for the player. You just need to know which enemy type spawns where to put the towers at the right spot. Another thing they've added is a hero for each area. The only thing that felt really off was the cowboy with the pistol. It just didnt fit the era of the game to have a pistol.The platforming parts are fun and the controls are nice but the graphics are a bit mediocre. They lack the style and charme of the original game. The music has been remastered and has a great quality. There is even an option to go for the original music. Very cool. I'd say this is not a perfect remake but a very enjoyable one.

_childDocuments_.review: Played trough the game and i'am a bit dissapointed.Graphics look really bad above resolutions of 1080p, at 1080p its borderline ok.Its definite not made for larger screens to play the game on.Compared to the original the difficulty got toned down very much so in that area everybody can enjoy the whole game without much trouble but if your looking for a challenge your at the wrong place.Bossfights are the old ones from the classic and 1 bonus boss.Theres 1 bonus area after you beat the final boss of the main game so theres a bit of new content so thats a decent new addition.The Soundtrack is great so no complaints in that area.The sim section of the game is very boring cause you just build up automaticly then raise a level burn everything down and vice versa till you reacht max level. You have a little customisation with the defense towers you can build but overall its not very strategic.Platforming sections are lackluster compared to some other Metroidvania like games available on Steam like Dust an Elysian Tail or Blasphemous or Bloodstained.If you'r a Actraiser fan you can get it now but for everyone else i dont recommend you to buy the game at full price.Its far too much compared to what you get for it, 10 bucks would be OK but not 30.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original ActRaiser to death and this game feels like a love letter to such fans.Graphics are reminiscent of the 3D models of Fire Emblem 11, which may turn some people off, but the chunky cheesiness of them is something I dig.Updated OST is absolutely phenomenal. If you don't like orchestral stuff, you can go back to the SNES version's soundtrack whenever you want from the menu!Gameplay has been updated. In the 2D Action segments, your melee options have expanded to include a three hit combo, DMC-esque Stinger stab, upslashes and downslashes, the works! Bosses are a lot spongier now to compensate, and that's a bit of a drag.The sim portions add more cutscenes, dialogue and even a full new tower defense mode! I was expecting to dislike this mode, as I loathed SolSeraph, but I was honestly enthralled the entire time. It's juuust tense enough from the get-go to get you invested, but not too tough where you'll be regretting not starting on Easy.The way to increase population has changed. The point-based system from the original is entirely gone and population is now entirely dependent on the amount of fields you can fit into one town. Population no longer affects your levels however, so it's mostly just important for completion's sake/getting the achievement for 3500 total population.This may not be worth the full $30 perhaps, but as a die-hard ActRaiser fan, I was more than happy to support the series and I'm VERY happy with what I was delivered. Can't wait to play more!
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: The game is Actraiser 1, but better in each aspect.The storytelling is a lot better!The visual is beautiful and original (it reminds me of Saga Frontier, SNES Donkey Kong, etc).The music is greatly inspired from the first game, but of course the quality is a lot better now.There are new gameplay elements such as monster raids which adds depth to the game.If you are open-minded, I'm pretty sure you'll like this new version of a classic!However, if you are upset because the game is a bit different from what it was, don't make a tantrum, don't buy the game, and replay the first Actraiser again.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Staring a new game will then let you name your character, the Lord of Light. Next you can choose the games difficulty, Weak (Enemy Strength Weak and Acts Lives - Infinite), Normal (Enemy Strength Normal and Acts Lives - Five) and Hard (Enemy Strength Formidable and Acts Lives - Three). The games difficulty can be changed at any time later in the game by visiting the Sky Palace.  You awake from along sleep to find Angel, your humble servant wishing you a warm welcome after sleeping for so long. She explains that while you’ve slept, your powers have waned and that without your presence to guide your people, monsters have ravaged the lands, scattering the people far and wide. Tanzra, the Evil One is behind the spread of evil throughout the lands. Currently your powers can’t rival those of Tanzra, however, you can regain your powers through your people's faith in you.   To restore your powers and rid the lands of the Tanzra evil you will have to guide your people, allow them to thrive and prosper. This will bring praises from them allowing you to grow strong enough to take on the monsters and Tanzra. You begin in the once prosperous verdant lands of Fillmore, where you will first come down from the heavens and clear out the evil which lies in the shadows. This is Act 1 and it will go over the basics of the game, attack, jump etcetera, you will have to make your way through the Act which is a side scrolling platform, control your character defeating everything in your path until you reach the end and the waiting Boss monster. Defeating the boss will then allow you to progress onto leading your followers, allowing them to build their community and fend for themselves.  There are two Acts per region, the Act 2 will unlock after you have guided your flock enough, allowing them to fend for themselves. Like Act 1 you come down from the heavens to take on the monsters and Boss in order so that you can move onto the next region. There are also some monster spawns which spew out monsters and will attack your people and destroy their hard work, fields, houses etcetera.   These monster spawns can only be accessed when your people have progressed enough. They are similar to the Acts where you will make your way through a side scrolling underground base of evil. While there isn’t a big boss for you to take on there is however, a Spawner. This is revealed after defeating a number of smaller spawns, defeating the Spawner will close off that hole in the ground and your folks will praise you for your good deeds in ridding the land of the constant attacks.  To defeat the monsters in the spawns and the Acts you wield a sword which you use to cut down all those before you. You can also dodgy attacks by backstepping, this will make you invulnerable briefly and may help to protect you in a tight pinch. As you progress you will also unlock new Magic, these will cost Magic Points in order to perform said magic. As you will probably lose some health and have a need to replenish your magic points, scattered at various places you will find small statues of silver and gold. There is also a bigger statue of yourself which when you pass will greatly heal your health. The smaller statues are of your little helper, Angel, these can replenish your health and magic points. You will have to strike and destroy the statues so that you can collect the items which they drop.   To have your people grow and expand into a thriving settlement, you begin with a humble temple. From here you take control of Angel, who flies above Fillmore and other regions as you unlock them. From your humble temple you will have Angel lay out where you would like roads to be built. You can select up to eight squares as you plan where you want the road to go at a time, sometimes there are obstacles which will block your path.   As you create new roads your people will start to settle down and start tending the land, building houses and will start producing resources such as Wood, Food and Mana. You can use these resources to help build structures like the Mage Tower, Gatehouses and be able to upgrade them. Angel can collect food and mana to replenish any which you have used.  As you’re the Lord of Light you do have a few heavenly powers which can help in the removal of the obstacles in your way, like trees and rocks. The heavenly powers (Miracles) you possess are Devine Lightning, Soothing Rain, Glorious Sunlight, Heavenly Winds and Restless Earth. Each miracle has multiple levels and will cost a number of Spell Points to perform a miracle. Not only are these miracles good for clearing a path but they come in very handy when your settlements are under attack.  From time to time you will have to protect your settlements from Hordes which wish to destroy what you have built. Using your heavenly powers won’t will help keep back the enemy but you’ll run out of spell points long before the final wave of monsters attacking you. To help keep back the enemy you can build things like Fortresses, Mage Towers and others which will help protect your growing settlement.   You also have the use of Prophesied Heroes once they turn up. There are six heroes with different abilities, your first hero is Philotas, a warrior who you can use to attack and protect where ever you put them on the map in Fillmore. When you move onto the new regions you can recall previous heroes to help you in the defending of your people.  In the settings there’s options for Background Music (Renaissance or Classic), Background Music and Sound Effects Volume Sliders, Message Speed, Brightness, Screen Mode, Resolution, Frame Rate, V-sync, Language (English, French, German, Chinese) and Key Configuration (Controller, Keyboard and mouse).  There’s a lot of chat in the game which isn’t bad but at times it’s annoying. Just when you think it’s over and you go to plan something or defend the oncoming monsters it starts with the chat again and again. This becomes really annoying when you just want to continue on with the game.  Another problem I had with the game is when controlling Angel and there are monsters attacking, I found that moving and trying to aim at monsters around the screen a little bit awkward at times. The only other problem I had with the game was that at times the text chat would freeze for a few seconds before continuing, not a big problem really. Overall, I’ve enjoyed playing so far, I like the graphics and the story.The game was reviewed on Steam (PC) and is also available on the following platforms, PlayStation 4, Android, Microsoft Windows, Nintendo Switch.Positives   + Nice graphics and artwork + Good story  + Controller support + Steam cloud + Has achievements  + Has cards  Negatives   - Text chat can be annoying - Moving and aiming Angel can be a bit awkward  - Text chat freezing for a few seconds  As the Lord of Light, guide your people so that they can rebuild and expand in to a thriving community, praising your greatness as you deal with the evil, which has spreading across the lands. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original, but it looked interesting so I gave it a shot. And I might keep playing after this review, so maybe I'll change my mind.First off, even if my complaints were resolved, I still don't think this game is worth more than like $15. It could be a fun distraction while you listen to a podcast or something, or just a nice relaxing game to play to unwind at the end of the day, but there's just not a whole lot going on here. It's okay, but it's not good. Get it on sale or not at all.Good:-I like the new character art-The music is listenable-The angel's dialogue is amusing enough that I tend to read it-They have several different game modes that kinda break up the monotony of doing any one of them too much-Each of the new regions gives you a new start with slight variations in gameplay and art. Very slight. Biggest difference is the art and dialogue. But at least you get to keep moving instead of trying to perfect your town forever.Bad:-Controlling the angel in town is a little unreliable. I can't consistently get him to face and shoot where I want, even with some really generous aim help. This gets to be really annoying when enemies start being able to light your town on fire.-Each of the elements of the game feels half-baked:--The platforming feels like it still needs a bit of polish. Not very responsive or fluid.--The town management is extremely minimal. You can't pick what to build, for example. You can upgrade by destroying a building with lighting, and the villagers rebuild with whatever tier of building you've now reached. Other than that, you just clear up tiles with whatever spell and watch the game play itself. It's weird to me that a major part of town building is just annihilating things with lightning, and watching everyone rebuild.--The tower defense is not fun. I'd prefer to just remove it entirely. The game limits where and what you can build, expecting you to make up for lousy planning and placement by moving your heroes around and casting spells to kill enemies. Problem is, there's nothing interesting or satisfying about it. It's extremely phoned-in. You don't even know where the enemies will come from. Not that it would matter, because you won't be able to block the right roads. It's just not fun. It's already feeling like a chore that I wish I could skip. I went to play it again, thought about the tower defense, and chose to write this review instead. That's how bad it is.--Pet peeve: You're playing as 'they' because even though the art for your avatar is pretty clearly male, the game doesn't commit to you being male and it doesn't let you pick. They they they they they.

_childDocuments_.review: Not usually a big fan of strategy games but this one definitely takes the cake out of it. Enjoyed it even though I got this mainly for 2D platformer. Glad I picked this up, because this apparently has been released for ages and this happens to be a remake of the original. So glad I didnt miss out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna give this one a thumbs up based on the fact that I have no nostalgia for the original as I haven't played it, but so far I've found a lot to enjoy about it as a rather simplistic city builder game with some hack and slash on the side. The one negative I'll give it is simply that it refuses to get out of your way long enough to just let you play the game when you first start out. _childDocuments_.review: Actraiser , the original game was a unique creation of it's time which combined both platformer action and city building in one game and now there is a Remake of this game which is kind of faithful to the original vision.Visually the game got a very nice presentation , the soundtrack is amazing and the new remastered soundtrack make it even better.the whole game goes in 3 phases , platforming , building and a new Tower Defense like strategy mode.The platforming section is a bit easier , look aesthetically pleasant even if a bit dated technology wise.the action is much faster then the original game. You Earn magic spells that hit pretty hard and tend to be a bit overpowered at times. The controls are responsives and it's overall very enjoyable but each levels tend to be too short.building is having your angel kill the monster while you clear the land from obstruction and telling the villagers to build roads , each villages will eventually build their own house , farms and workshops as you progress and gain faith. After a while you can then clear each monster spawner closing the gap to the next Platformer phase. There is no real challenge in this part but this is still pretty fun to do.the Defense strategy part is not that great and I don't know what they where thinking.It's not hard and actually fun for the first few worlds then later on it's just start being random and inconsistent in the way it's made ... the whole thing is a trial and error in which combination of towers and heroes are gonna allow you to survive the next level. It's not even challenging , just feel like you get your ass kicked once in a while then comeback with a different strategy and win very easily.this whole mode should called puzzle defense because that what it's feel like.overall I still recommend the game because both platforming and rebuilding villages is fun as you discover the stories for each of the different heroes that you meet in each land that you're gonna save from Evil , the defense mode feel like that ''meh'' another battle to do when it's happen but don't completly ruin the whole experience in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I really did-- I played so much of the SNES original and loved it; I loved the mix of action platforming and city building. Actraiser Renaissance tends to have both of those, but it's not the main focus of the game by any means-- if you play this game, expect to spend the majority of your time in a tower defense sort of game. You'll have to do DOZENS of them for each area, and it's... not exciting. It's tedious and cumbersome and just not fun.Nostalgia alone cannot save this game, even if its soundtrack is a delight to listen to-- skip the game. I wish that I had stopped before two hours so that I could have gotten a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mediocre version of a great game.The graphics went with pre-rendered art for the action and overworld scenes and art stills for characters. Some folks think it's ugly, and while I can see that, I think it works. This game clearly wasn't made on a huge budget and it gets the job done.Sound design is definitely a mixed bag. They got the original composer to do another take on his decades-old work, and while the music itself continues to be fantastic, you can tell he was kinda phoning it in. Several tracks take obvious cues from the Actraiser Symphonic Suite album that's as old as the game itself, and music repeats. A lot. Fillmore's Act 1 music is rousing and memorable for the first stage, but it kinda loses it's novelty when it's in *every single Fillmore lair AND act 2*. And what music that's completely new is forgettable.And that brings me to my biggest complaint: the changes to gameplay. All of it just feels so unnecessary. They gave your godly avatar combos and aerial attacks, while also making every single enemy in the game take more hits to defeat. The very first foe encountered is defeated in one hit on the SNES original and takes several hits here. Same goes for the first boss, who is notably more durable. It elongates the fights in a way that I don't think is meaningful. And while they changed the way magic is used so it's a more reliable form of damage, in practice you'll be using it the same way you did in 1990, spamming your best spell to pummel bosses into submission.All of the above is just in the action stages. The changes in the sim mode... Eesh. The angel now has homing arrows, making combat in that mode even more of a non-issue than it was in the original. And the tower defense mode very much overstays it's welcome - it lacks depth while simultaneously being frustrating at times because of the lack of options, not to mention it gets in the way of building the town since you have to sacrifice space for defenses. And it's so frequent! If the horde battles occurred once per town it would be an event and likely more interesting, but as it is you're going to do dozens of battles in sim mode before the game is over and you'll have seen everything they have to offer by the time you reach the second town. I get what they were going for but I don't think they pulled off the execution.Also I think the characters talk too much, even compared to the original where they interrupt you every 5 seconds, but that's just me.If you've never heard of or played Actraiser, by all means, check it out. It's still a very solid game at the end of the day. But for anyone who's played the original, just go play that again instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: A great example on how to make a remake. Renaissance does an excellent job of bring the original SNES games action and town sim into a modern era with new graphics, classic and remixed soundtrack, and expanded story that makes you feel more immersed in what was a somewhat bare-bones world before. The new artwork is great and the story telling is actually quite deep. Everything reads like a positive psalm with the writing really showing some great character development and overall storytelling. Which is good as all the new characters do little gameplay wise. The story is the only way you will interact and learn about the characters and their backstories. While the graphics do look good, some have levied complaints about how the actions sections look. I guess if it can appear a bit 'smudged' in a way, but at the same time, I don't know, it just works for some reason imo. The new art for the town building sections is great though. No longer do you have copy and pasted assets in all the lands like the original. Now every land has it's own unique culture, buildings, and followers. It's such a small thing, but the diversity in the followers does wonders to make the world feel more real and lived in. I didn't really care for the new tower defense mini-game stuff they added. I guess it gives you something to do while you're building the town and it's really the only thing that justifies the existence of the new heroes gameplay wise, but it felt more annoying than fun. It would have been neat if we could have played as the heroes in some mini-act instead of getting the tower defense stuff, but whatever I guess.The game can also be a bit... wordy. Though I think the new writing is great I would get very annoyed sometimes as it felt like I couldn't play for even 5 minutes before someone would interrupt me with more story. I guess those are minor complaints though for what felt like an overall great game.End game grind is total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ though. Getting your heroes to level 20 is a load of ♥♥♥♥ forcing you to just sit their with your thumb up your ass as you wait for monsters to come attack you. It's a shame that the least fun element of the game, the tower defense part, is the part you'll spend the most time playing, especially if you want those level 20 heroes. Just hours upon hours just sitting there like a dumbass waiting for the attacks for what feels like drips of EXP with each attack. THANK GOD I am not judging this game based solely on end/after game play because it would have been an instant thumbs down if it was. For the experience and gameplay as a whole it's good and worth it's price. Sadly, for those who want all the achievements the game turns into a dreadful bore and time waste. Someone in the forums said it ONLY takes 6 hours of grind to level up everyone to level 20. I don't believe that because I'm pretty sure I've spent more than 6 hours doing this and I'm still nowhere near done.Edit: I just found out this game is on mobile phone. Same game, same quality, cheaper price. In other words, SquareEnix is charging PC gamers more because we invest more in our platforms. I got a graphics card that cost more than the phone and mobile game controller needed to play this game combined. Wow, I honestly feel so ripped off. Moving this to a thumbs down even though I do like the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Filled with SNES nostalgia, just like the original with better graphics.The sidescroller fighting is perhaps the "worst" part of the game and even that is fun.while playing a god and doing miracles for humans so they can fullfill their faithful worship to you is amazing.Overall I give this a 6 of 10, there are definatly better games out there, but it is cheap and fun. _childDocuments_.review: To the point==================Actraiser in name only, this is more of an exercise in how long you can endure awful tower defense mechanics. If you're expecting a faithful recreation, skip this one for sure.+Cleared on Hard mode+Good Stuff================- It sort of scratches that Actraiser itch since this isn't a very common genre of game with a bunch of random ideas thrown in. There are parts of each portion, like the side scrolling, town building and yes, even the awful tower defense, that I enjoy, it's just that the glaring flaws of each mode are a huge turn off.Bad Stuff==============================- So in this version the gameplay was changed to have tower defense segments, where the enemies will spawn and try to attack certain objectives, which you use the heroes in the story to defend against.It's hard to describe how annoying this system is, it's both incredibly slow and incredibly unbalanced. You'll have enemies that take all your forces working nonstop to injure that do 50% of a structures health in a single hit. In these kinds of fights you need to adopt a strategy of trying to dump all damage/spells/units possible while letting everything else burns, it makes the mode incredibly unenjoyable.What's worse then that? Oh you have to do it at the MINIMUM of 5 times per settlement? This is not including random horde encounters, which start appearing when you destroy all the monster spawners on a map.The whole system is incredibly persistent, it almost makes me think Square thought this mode was fun or was trying to pad as much time as possible.- The 2D sections have some of the jankiest hitboxes you're going to see in a modern game and it's inexcusable for a company as big as Square Enix even if this is so obviously a budget title. The funniest thing is it works to your advantage half the time, keeping you safe from enemy hits or making it easy to dodge harder attacks. Other time's you'll be getting hit by something that looks to be the size of a baseball with the hitbox of a hippo.- You cannot control how fast buildings spawn things, this can lead to feeling like you are waiting forever for a resources or food spawn, especially on the smaller maps where you can only have 3 factories active at any given time.- This title takes anime ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to a whole new level. I like the characters even if they're pretty damn one dimensional but my GOD does this game interrupt you every 5 seconds to hear them talk, or for your patrons to come and request something from you. It drags teh pacing of the game into the mud.- You can't control where your faithful build things, which is annoying for 2 reasons. One, if you happen to have a "protect all farms" siege mission, but your followers build them all in a cluster across the map away from your very limited towers, well you can move the towers and demolish the town in the process or you can play the map on hard mode and the aforementioned elite enemies ♥♥♥♥ on your farm one by one.The second reason is that towns can only reach a max population if the buildings are laid out " correctly" meaning the AI will place them as optimally as possible but if it can't it won't tell you and you'll be stuck with a lower population. Only way around this? Nuke all buildings on the map and hope they do it right the next time.- Even if you want to play smart in tower defense mode, you really cannot since the placement of towers/gatehouses etc ii seemingly, randomly constrained for no reason.The towers you can place are limited by town size but say you want to move a tower right next to a farm that needs defending? Can't do that since the game has decided you can't use that square for some reason.To note, this is a little different then trying to place these towers on a house since it will just demolish the house which is easy enough, but what I am saying is that there are major choke-points on a map that you can't use because the game decides you can't put a gatehouse there. Just an incredibly bizarre choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and a slow start make it hard to give a try, especially when you adore the original. Will confirm once you get Fillmore going the game clicks and it feels like Actraiser. The added tower defense sections and putrid graphics make it hard to stomach but you get used to it. The added mechanics are fun and the combination of townbuilding and action stages is as charming as ever.

_childDocuments_.review: This comes from a person who played the original as a kid, and previously bought this on Switch.  I know my time in game is short, but I already played it before.Okay let's start with the obviously bad parts:- The cute cherub baby angle from the original is now a crossdressing (wearing a skirt and baby doll top) feminine boy.  I don't know the age of the character because this is a Japanese made game and their art style has different representations, but let's just hope that he has at least turned 18.- The side-scroller portion's graphics looks like it is from an off brand late N64-PS1/early PS2 console.  It doesn't even have Gamecube level graphics.  Seriously when you break the rocks it looks like the original Banjo-Kazooie, the level of pixelation is uneven, and in general each art asset looks like a different artist made it in a slightly different style.- The Narration portion is from any romance text based-game and it could have been made in an old version of RPG maker.  It is just very generic.- The Sim (city-builder) version looks like any other mobile game ported to console than ported to PC.  It is just weirdly off-putting with the giant baby head on the angel.- The graphics are honestly really bad overall.- the controls are also pretty clunky, but to be honest the originals were pretty mechanical since it was made early on the SNES, and if you saw the others games made around that time by the developer of the original Actraiser they weren't any better than the controls for say Gauntlet on the NES by Tengen (Atari's NES games alternative name).- The dialogue between EVERYTHING is a bit much.  I mean there are so many times when there is just pointless banter to increase word count it makes me literally groan out loud.  The good parts!:- The controls I will mention are actually NOT worse than the originals, you have extra attacks which are sorta silly since you have an over-sized attack box (easily hitting things below, behind, and above you).  I mean seriously neither this nor the original are difficult games.- They added a lot more depth to the sim portion, and if you are like me and you have ever red-lined the game and played the Pal version (with a difficulty selection easy, normal, hard where easy is American, normal is American 2nd play-through hard, and hard which basic goblins/bats take three hits), or played a translated original Japanese version where you can only get more mana in the sim portion by killed monsters... over and over... it was terrible.- The levels are different, and far worse in my opinion, but my opinion on them doesn't matter since they are probably just fine and I am way to old to be writing a review about how they slightly changed the way levels are laid out.TL:DRIn general anyone who is a fan of Actraiser, and wants to expand their interaction with this classic series has little other choice since Actraiser 2 is pretty terrible.You can also check out:Soul BlazerIllusion of GaiaTerranigma...and if you can handle the early 3d era...The Granstream SagaSoul Blazer, Illusion of Gaia, Terranigma are called the Quintet trilogy and follow the same theme as Actraiser where you are going around fixing all of humanities problems (kinda sorta).  They are play a little differently, but if you want to imagine what happens after everything goes to garage after you retire at the end of Actraiser than Soul Blazer is basically you coming back and fixing  up that mess too.Anyway take it or leave it.  It is your money.*edit*Jeez, I just realized I paid $15.99 for this - ON SALEDon't buy it off sale, just add it to your list and wait for it to drop to around $5.00 or play it in the return window and send it back if you can't handle the new Sim portion.I play with both controller AND keyboard & mouse.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the back and upfront the original Actraiser is easily in my top 5 games of all time. So i'll be speaking from a bias on both the positives and negatives first.I'll give the short review first: I recommend it. It still needs some polish overall but the nuts and bolts of a great game is in here. The game was clearly on a small budget and it shows. With the proper funding, time, updates, and attention this could be a truly epic remake if given the time and love to do so. I don't love the "mobile feel" of the game as it reminds me a lot of the ghouls and ghost remake that came out recently. However, there is enough here to like once you get past the initial shortcomings. I'd say its a C+ game overall. I'd love to see the team get a proper budget like the trials of mana remake for a sequel but we'll see if this sells well first.Side Scrolling gameplay:The game itself does a lot of interesting new things that builds on the old game play. For example, instead of just being able to do a standard standing, jumping, and ducking slash. You have the ability to perform a standing combo, uppercut and downward slice as well as perform the ducking slash with the added bonus of having the duck position be a defensive position causing you to take less damage. However something feels missing, and I think its the jumping. Don't get me wrong the jumping is a little easier to control, what I mean is at the height of a jump from the original you would have a downward thrust where the master would hold his sword back. I'm not sure if it can be updated later on but adding that would make the controls feel new while also maintaining the faithfulness to the original.I like the addition of going into the monster pits in order to stop the spawners. Although I haven't beaten it yet it is a nice addition to be able to play more times with the master instead of the standard 2 level acts. However, unless they shake these up I can see it getting annoying.I do also like the fact that the levels are a little different from the original, they feel a little more fleshed out while maintaining the originals integrity.One thing that is very noticeable is the bloom effect in filmores first side scrolling level. It's legitimately hard to see at points. The master is glowing and there is a glow through the trees. It needs to be toned down specifically. This is a more negative thought overall but the sprites don't do it for me. They have a sort of cheap mobile phone feel to them as I mentioned in my short review. Like the Ghost and goblins remake. The look is gonna hurt it overall as I feel a lot of people will see it and say "wow that looks like it'll play cheapilly". It's a little late to change this now but that  could easily have been changed earlier on in production and if by chance a sequel is green lit please take the time to get nicer looking sprites or models.The Backstep function is nice and my god the arranged music is beautiful. I shed a tear hearing the soundtrack.Overall the sidescrolling needs some polishing. The nuts and bolts for the gameplay is fine but the aesthetics hold it back.Simulation mode:I like the angel sprite and I like how each area now has a more fleshed out story with champions. I love the fact that there is more of a strategic mode because of raids and the options for forts and towers is awesome.I do not like having to wait to attack monster forts. That is annoying. Plus it was always cool in the original game to check out the other lands and fight them at my leisure. Being level locked out seems pointless other than to arbitrarily keep you in a specific area. I get it, there are more resources and what not but I think you could still craft the game around this and balance it out.Why does the angels shots arc? I always feel like i'm gonna miss every time i shoot even if i charge my shot. Keep it simple.What I did love and will absolutely sound hypocritical is the new simulation mode features, having the waves of enemies is a cool idea and adds more things to do while in the simulation mode. The fact they made these tie into the story is also pretty neat. The map overall looks fine but like the sidescrolling the models are just pretty bleh looking.Misc: I think the new art style is okay. Very final fantasy-esqu. I would have prefered the old christian gothic artstyle but new look is fine for what it is.Music = God tier (literally and figuratively)Overall for the game: It would have been easy to just do a one for one remake but the team attempted to do something a little bit more. Whether it was time constraints or budget they should have been given more of what was lacking. Their is something truly special here. As it stands the game is about a C+ however if given the proper care and with sufficient updates this could really become something special as a standalone or potential franchise rebirth. Give it a shot if your even slightly interested. You wont be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: As aside: Square Enix really needs to make the "pro mode" like the original ActRaiser had it. All platforming and bosses. The movement feels fairly good and the attacks are interesting if a little basic. I feel it's an improvement over the original game in mechanics but the levels do not really stand up to the original. The sim needs lots of love to really be enjoyable at all. There is too much waiting around for SP to pop up from the fields. And it is Inexcusable that the game just lets you sit there FOREVER until you figure out you need to destroy your own cities homes and stuff to get the population up... just not fun. The variety of things you can build is really low. I wish there was more.  The graphics are OK/meh for what they could have been. Yuzo as usual does a good job with the music. I wish there was VA but it's not entirely necessary. if you're a big fan of AR, get it, but otherwise, I would pass.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is a QUINTET remaster. The mere fact that this game exists is a tremendous blessing for a certain cult fanbase.The obvious bias aside, is the game good?Short answer: Yes. Long answer: IT COULD HAVE BEEN SO MUCH MOREIt's obvious that a lot of faithful effort was put into remastering this game. From including Yuzo Koshiro's amazing soundtrack and accompaniment to the astounding artwork given to the many characters, menus and intro cutscene. People put their sweat and tears into this, and it shows in that regard.HOWEVER. There are obvious hallmarks of "mobile game syndrome" visible in certain sections of the game. Which is both a tremendous shame, but understandable to a degree. Actraiser is the most popular in it's home region to the east. In that region, PC Gaming is not the reigning king, but mobile gaming is. I can understand everyone's frustration on this matter, as I wish too that we could have seen a different type of aesthetic in the gameplay sections for enemy and character design. On that note, the game bares resemblence to that of certain GBA titles which utilize pre-rendered screenshots of 3D models for animation and gameplay. It is functional, and befits the game in it's art direction, though there were quite a few who voiced their unhappiness with this direction. For me, I came to appreciate it more once I'd completed the 2nd act of Fillmore. Sure, it's different, but it works.Gameplaywise, the game shares the hallmarks of the original. Action segments & City building segments. Rennaissance tosses in a new tower/hero horde defense gameplay mechanism, which again sees mixed results from players. I personally could do without the "final" encounters, as they feel more like a constant gimmick of me moving hero's to and fro. It's a segment I could mostly do without.The added spawner fights are fun little tidbits, but don't match up to the proper Act segments. I suppose they were placed in due to the large addition of the horde defenses as to keep the action segments appearing more frequently. But all that aside, the deliverence is there. It's actually there. We have refined combat mechanics from the action segments which now allows a few more moves such as upward slicing jumps and downward slams, as well as a backstep mechanic to dodge attacks. Magic still feels good to use and it's a joy to shred through the stages and reclaim your divinity by leading your people.The game is a lot longer due to the nature of the horde defenses. I'm currently on my fourth region at around 11 hours (time of writing.) It's been an experience to relive this in the format it is presented in. The game was announced to have extra content towards the end and thus, once I've reached it, I may revisit the review to continue my thoughts on the matter.Now that I've finished the game at a total gametime of 27,5 hours (including bonus content at this point) I can say that this game is definetely well worth the money. I even took the time to revisit the classic and the amount of faithful redesign placed into this is truly admirable. If it weren't for the somewhat tedious tower defense segments, I'd have this game easily ranked in my top ten. I've yet to nab all those achievements so I think I'll be revisiting this game for quite a while still. That means I'll easily have more hours than the game's priced at if that's how you measure your games.I'm elated that this exists. And I hope it is merely a sign of more Quintet games to come.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing feeling to wake up and learn that one of your favorite childhood SNES games was remade and you didn't even know it was happening.I'm still in Fillmore but so far I'm loving this. It's a brand new game, a true remake. Everything was rebuilt, expanded, and changed. The graphics, sound, and music have been remade to be more modern and it all came out great!So far the core of the game seems to be in tact but they've changed a lot around the core mechanics of the game.Some examples:- The first level is the same theme, look, and feel but the layout is completely different so it's basically a new level. The boss is the same boss but with a different arena and similar mechanics.- Playing as the angel is similar at it's core but a lot a changed or been added. _childDocuments_.review: In anticipation for this game, having seen it on the Nintendo Direct, I immediately played the original game. Pretty good. Combat was a little clunky, but I assumed the remake would fix this. I give the original game a solid 8/10. Definitely fun, will play more.This game was so boring I almost fell asleep multiple times while playing it. There are stretches of the game where you could straight up beat your meat for a while and still probably be alright. 90% of the game you spend in the overworld, much much more than the previous game. And oh boy the overworld. Awful. Two major problems here.1.) The new music. It just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ drones on and on. The remixes of the original music (the original songs were bangers btw) are sub par and make it sound like generic ambient fantasy music. 2.) The sieges. Legitimately the worst part of the game, and ironically the part of the game that made me buy it in the first place. They take forever and they're just boring. Multiple sieges spent just watching the hero character slowly plunk away at a group of enemies that stand no chance against him. Then when the boss gets there, you watch him even more slowly plunk away at the boss. Then the boss kills him, moves away a little bit, and the hero character immediately respawns and you repeat the process. Over and over. Until you die of boredom or finish beating your meat. The worst part about this though? Every aspect of this game feels like it was designed to be a mobile game. I kept waiting for ad windows to pop up asking me to buy in game currency. I think the most obvious place where the mobile game aspect rears its ugly head is in the visuals. Even at 1080p the visuals look like they're too low resolution for my monitor. HD my fat ass. You know what makes this game look HD though? Playing it on a very small screen. Kinda like a mobile phone. Weird. I can't believe they had the audacity to sell this game for 30 dollars. The anime png's that represent the villagers and the cherub and whatnot just hang on the screen. They didn't even bother animating them. They didn't even bother cheaply animating them with Live2D or anything. They simply slapped pngs on the screen and called it a day. That'll be 30 dollars plus tip. This isn't even an "Old good new bad" scenario. I had no attachment to Actraiser before like, 4 hours ago. I played each one for about 2 hours. The old one and the new one. And while the old has problems, being a side scrolling action game from 1990 (Super Castlevania 4 wouldn't even release for another 2 years), I can't seem to find a reason to play the new one. I guess you can attack while descending your jumps. Cool, I guess they fixed that problem. Great. Thanks. I could go on but nobody's gonna read a novel. Game is bad. Don't charge people 30 dollars for your mobile trash. Kinda pissed at Nintendo for featuring it in the Direct tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about being the good guy, side-scrolling and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the bad guys.This is a game about defending the weak from cowards.This is a game about being a man, a real man.This is a very good game.Actraiser was always a very good game, and it is again.This is a game that exudes love, and triumph, and struggle, and catharsis from start to finish, in regular beats. It does that, and it excels at that. Because of that emotional loop that coincides with gameplay loop, it just *feels* really damn good. There’s a strangely intimate element to it as well, one we very seldom get these days; and just for that alone the game is great. But,I don’t know if I can recommend this to everyone. It is not for everyone.I mean, I do, because I legitimately feel like the game is not only fun, but it can enrich your life. If you’re paying attention, if you meet it halfway, if you welcome the master into your heart so to speak, this game will kind of add something to you (I know it sounds weird, but I’m not gonna pretend this isn’t the case just because it might make you uncomfortable to hear it, I apologize if apology is required);  but I accept that most people that are still playing video games in current year are only here to min-max something, or they’re chasing the new souls-like that a tryhard streamer has told them they have to like, or they’re trying to sublimate some primate need to dominate others that they can’t get in their everyday life. The point is: you won’t find that here; you will find a video game here. It is one that delivers a fun, genuine experience of the medium of games at a level of honesty and purity we just don’t really get anymore. It’s nice.This game is a love letter to the old days, it’s really just a true video game. It is not a status symbol, it is not designed to give you a false sense of superiority over your fellow man because your cartoon soldier shot the other guy’s cartoon soldier faster and more accurately. This is not a football for fat kids title. There are no sweet drops of epic loot that you need to cancel plans for, or make spreadsheets to determine the best days to farm for. There is no live service element to this game.It’s just a very good game. It’s refreshingly sincere.In its original form Actraiser was always an odd duck. It was similar to a lot of games at the same time, but superior to none in each respective field. And it balanced that so well that it distinguished itself for it. In design it was symphonic in its constituent elements.It makes you feel things.I’m not ashamed to admit that Actraiser was the first time I personally got an answer to the old question “Can a computer make you cry ?” when I was a kid.In its current form it holds up, and delivers more of what its progenitor had. This remake has a visual novel that wraps itself in the old formula perfected by additions and QOL improvements. The old formula is here, but is now polished and honed to perfection in its current form. Fans of the original will notice that the original game is all there, better than ever and just the same. They will also notice that it has wholly another game’s worth of content that it has been bolstered with. New fans will find a genuine wholesome call-back to the old school with a lot of current genre generation filigree in design dressing up the edges of the experience.All this being said, I cannot truly recommend this game because I don’t know what everyone is looking for. But if this finds you, maybe give it a chance, at the very least it is a thing of sincere and humble beauty.I realize that’s not what everyone is looking for, but maybe someday it will be. Not for everyone all at once, I know that’s a silly idea…that’s not what I mean.But maybe right now, for you, the person reading this, maybe this is the game you didn’t know you needed right now.That’s how it found me. That’s how it found me again.And, honestly, I feel like I am kinda better for it.
