_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the games I really wanted to enjoy this winter. As someone that played the daylight out of the original on the SNES to the point that I had the action stages and simulation sections down to a science, a remaster with some potentially new aspects really appealed to me. And from what I saw in reviews, most of it looked very well done.Then I got the game and started playing. Or tried to anyway.The content looks good, minus the tower defense portions which are widely viewed as distracting at best, but for me that's only because I don't like tower defense gameplay. I do however, like a mix of action and simulation content, which this game has in spades. Unfortunately the current iteration of the game and its client in particular detract greatly from what should be a wonderful spiritual remaster of a cherished classic.As I wasn't able to get far into the game before I experienced enough issues to request a refund (at great angst), I can only comment on what I experienced with regard to that aspect. The action scenes appear to be  based on the originals. But that's where the similarity ends. Monsters take on average three times the number of hits to kill and despite you having a new set of moves to work with feel somewhat cumbersome compared to the more direct approach the original ActRaiser took. I could forgive this as being a new artistic direction if not for the fact that the action areas are now broken up into "segments". I found the segmented stages to be immensely immersion breaking to the point I actually started disliking them. Add in boss battles that take ages due to them being meat shields now and the action portion quickly loses its luster.The simulation portion looked very nice graphically. And I actually liked the change in the angel's appearance. Bonus points for Square Enix finding an appearance that lets the  decide what the angel is, be it male, female, or non-binary. Whether that was the intent or not, it ended up being a refreshing bit of mental player agency. But being constantly interrupted to the point you could be preparing to press a button and be hit with yet  NPC dialogue was unbelievably offputting to the point of being incredibly pedantic. Less interruptions and more action during the simulation stages would have been greatly appreciated here.But the nail in the coffin for me wasn't the content changes. It was the game client itself. During action stages, there is a motion trail effect that is used to hide what appears to be some unfixed faults with the Unity engine and you cannot turn this effect off. The original did not have it and it actually triggered borderline nausea for me, to say nothing of throwing my timing off. It's one of the "features" I dislike in both Castlevania: Symphony of the Night and Record of Lodoss War: Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth. Visual distractions such as these impact perception more than developers seem to realize and being able to disable them would have been welcomed.The client also suffers from significantly annoying technical issues such as fullscreen defaulting to 720p and the user having to manually bump it back up to 1080p+. There is also entirely nonfunctional vertical sync (vSync).. It plain doesn't work from the in-game option, as evidenced by the excessive screen tearing during vertical panning even with the option turned on. I was able to partially remedy this by disabling the in-game option and forcing it via the nVidia control panel instead. On top of that is the inability to hide the mouse cursor. Unlike the macOS mouse pointer direction that can allow for hiding it in the upper right corner as a last resort, the Windows cursor is always visible. The game client does not hide the cursor at all. Ever. Even when you're using a controller as I was, the cursor was always onscreen, breaking immersion.So for now, I have to pass on this game and sadly can't recommend it. Not for the content, but what was done  the content and how the game client does, or in many cases, does  function. If Square/Sonic Powered can fix the underlying technical issues (and hopefully lessen the number of NPC interruptions during simulation mode), I'd be willing to give this another go. But as is, I can't justify spending good money on a broken client that also induces nausea with seemingly no real accessibility options built into the game to get around that issue.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ActRaiser from the SNES but through a modern lens.  While the story remains familiar, the specific path to get there (through design tweaks in the side-scrolling battler, tower defense added to the city sim, and additional/reworked story beats) has changed for the better in my opinion.Additional thoughts:  -Combat is harder but more varied-All enemies/bosses have learned some new moves -You can still cheese through battles with the use of Magic-You can swap spells at any time in a level-MP is less-restrictive and acquired differently-Side-scrolling stages are replayable and there's benefit to doing so-There's some bonus side-scrolling action when sealing monster lairs-There's an option to switch between classic and remastered soundtracksIn all, whether it's your first time playing or are feeling nostalgic (and don't mind castlevania-style character art), this is worth your dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: Dating back to the first run SNES games of autumn of 1991, Actraiser is one of those amazing classics very few have ever played.  So I was ecstatic that Actraiser was given a highly-unexpected remaster.  If only this remaster was worthy of the original.  Sadly, it is not.  The graphics and sound track are well done, but the gameplay has seriously suffered.You play as a god figure who has awoken to free your devout believers and save the world that is overrun by evil monsters.  The first part of the game is a 2D side-scrolling arcade-action game of fairly standard platforming fare.  Upon victory against the stage's end boss, you move on to the god-game civilization building phase where you give guidance and protection to your followers as they build a new city in the wilderness teeming with demons that would see you and your faithful undone.  Once your city is established, you descend into another 2D side-scrolling level to vanquish evil once and for all — for that realm.  And you will do this for six different realms.The original Actraiser was simple in execution, but excelled where it mattered.  Graphics and music were groundbreaking (for the day).  The side scrolling action was competently developed with challenging levels and boss designs.  The god-game city build phase isn't overly complex but kept you engaged with both guiding and protecting your followers.This is where Actraiser Renaissance breaks down.  The 2D side scrolling portions are not challenging at all.  In places, they are outright stupidly easy.  The god game mode suffers from "more is not better."  Now demons can invade in earnest in a tower defense minigame.  Ugh.  The inclusion of heroes muddies the whole god-game theme while also being integral to the awful tower defense minigames.  The angel servant is given more personality — albeit an unlikable one (he's now  who sucks up to the boss while arrogantly throwing his weight around others).  And the story is expanded, but done so with more (interruptive) cutscenes, which actually makes the game a more jarring experience.An hour and a half was all I needed to know to get a refund.  Which is disappointing, because Actraiser deserves better.  Not necessarily "more", but certainly better.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the look and feel of the action part of the game and even the city build-part is still enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original I would NEVER have expected this game to suddenly drop out of nowhere. This is like a deluxe version of the original actraiser. Vastly expanded gameplay and story, tons of attention to detail. Cute art. Amazing Yuzo Koshiro remix OST. Clearly a labour of love. I love the 32-bit looking visuals. Like a upgraded actraiser port for PSX or Saturn that we never got. It's also great how they modernized the side scrolling stages by giving the player more abilities while keeping the oldschool flair intact. Really enjoying the idea of unique hero npc and the town defense gameplay addition as well. edit: Almost 5 hours in and I just finished bloodpool. They found the right balance between keeping it oldschool and fluffing it up.Hits all the right notes for me.It's a cerebral piece about transcendence, civilization and the divine.It is a total rennaisance piece of software in the literal definition of the word.It also got cute angels and witches.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Wonderful & heart felt! But only for some. The story they added really keeps you interested and the game as a whole is fun in both RTS & Side-scrolling modes. You need to give it chance to grow on you b/c it's following a recipe laid down from the 1990's but the improvements ARE MASSIVE. And the only draw backs are the lack of higher quality 3D models but will play/look fine on Steamdeck sized screens & 1080. I recommend giving this game a play through b/c it's a great way to get a new look on our lives from a different angle than you may have expected. I'll admit, the original game changed my life after beating it due to the new perspectives it puts you in as a kid.Long wind review:Music is very reminiscent of the original game and sticks very close to the scoring, Bravo. You can even tell the first song got a lot of love. Later areas could have gotten some new scores, but they did mix up a bit. The places and plot points seem perfectly updated. I just love it! I've been re-falling in love with this game due to the remaster and I can't recommend it more. My only complaint is the lack of higher resolution textures on anything bigger than 1080. I have a 2k and 4k monitor and and boy does this game look outdated immediately. I set it to 1080 and have been enjoying it with a controller. I also wish they'd enhance some sprites so they don't look so bad. But I guess compared to the old game, this is no matter what, just plain better. Just look at an old youtube video and you'll see why lol.Spoilers?Later in the game I had a few Monty Python moments with the Giants all falling down like cheap cardboard cutouts! LMAO. They also kept calling a Giant Tree a Mountain! lol. This stuff is pretty hilarious how much they kinda left it in the old school ways of developing games. I mean look at those elbows, arms and shoulders on some of these monsters! It's like first time modeling! LOL This is such a serious game, yet this stuff is all over the place. I'm not sure but I think it's adding some charm lol.Here's to hoping they continue the story with a better 2nd game than the original 2nd game. The original 2nd game only had side scrolling and no city building.Wishlist for next game:-World exploration, and more places.-Sending champions on quests to level up.-More building options that impacted defense more.-More Strategy-more cool music.-seeing your people make more statues of you & weave them into story.-Having your champions help you in battle side by side and having them be in awe of your glory.

_childDocuments_.review: Posting this review at 11 hours in.Actraiser for SNES is probably one of my favorite games on that system.  So it pains me to say no to this recommendation.  11 hours in and I have barely done any side scrolling yet.  I'm in the 3rd area so that means i've done a total of 5 or 6 platforming sections. (they did add these very tiny stages to close the enemy gateways but those take literally a minute each).  And when it comes to the platforming/combat it's not great at all, it feels VERY janky.  Has a total different feeling than the original.  Character model is ugly and the art style they chose is not appealing, it looks like a mobile game.  The bosses do look cool, I'll give them that however they are super easy.  By the time you get to a boss your character is powered as you will see when you play you power up in the stages as you progress and by the time you reach the end your dude is super strong, you can just mow over the boss with ease.So what does that tell you?  The overworld sections are LONG.  Which I normally wouldn't have a problem with because I love city building games but unfortunately added tower defense to the building sections.  They did not need to do this.  I do like the hero's added. (there's 1 from each region) However that also comes with a cost... and that cost is the dialogue/mini stories they added for each region as well.My God... there is A LOT of dialogue.  I was painstakenly reading it trying to give the benefit of the doubt but there is a lot, I'm at the point where I just wanna play the game so am starting to skip it because of how much there is.  If you are a diehard Actraiser fan like I was then I'd say get it because there probably will never be a true Actraiser again but be prepared to understand it is not like the original.  If you are a new person who never played Actraiser and are just wondering what this is, I'd say dont' waste your time.Pros:-Music-Overworld looks cool-Bosses look cool-City building is fun.Cons:-Janky sidescrolling/combat doesn't feel good-Platforming sections are just very bland and boring.-Minus the overworld the artstyle is ugly (looks like a mobile game)-Tower defense game added-Ungodly amount of dialogue added (just skip it or you will be reading for hours)-overworld sections will be 9/10 of your gametime because of the tower defense modeSorry but I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I've played Renaissance for 2.5 hours at this point, it started off pretty good. The graphics are nice, I like the new music (albeit not as much as the original OST), there were some neat new moves added to the action platformer segments. My big issue (like many others it seems) is with the new 3rd piece of the game which is like a tower defense fight that plays out during the town building simulation phase. For starters it feels shoehorned in, like they just added it for the sake of adding something new to this game. These fights are so painfully slow and there is no kind of indicator to tell you how long they will go on for. The tower defense stuff also bleeds into the simulation aspect as you have to build and position forts, gather materials, and listen to countless dialogues and explanations that really muddy the experience of the sim aspect. It hurts me to be harsh on this game, I was really looking forward to playing it and I love the original ActRaiser but I cannot deny the disappointed feeling I have surrounding the game and feel like I have completely lost my drive to continue playing as I know there will be a million more tower defense sections and they ultimately dominate the amount of time you will spend playing the game. Go play the original any way you can instead.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - just the wrong mixture or annoying and boring - avoid this gameFull of poor design choices, depressing inanity, constant nuisancesome interruptions, banal dialogue and shallow time wasting, this ActRaiser remake is vastly inferior to its predecessor in every way. _childDocuments_.review: It actually pains me to not recommend this game.  I loved the original and wanted so badly to love this.  Is it a bad game?  Not really, but it is a remake of a truly great game and fails to match the original much less improve on it.The controls are clunky, no more so than the original though.The city building is very similar with a few minor changes, unfortunately , all of those changes are for the worse.  For example, having 3 levels of each miracle adds nothing to the gameplay.  Having to constantly collect materials from farms is annoying and adds nothing to the game.  Earthquake no longer effecting the entire map is a questionable decision at best.The levels are good, but not much different than in the original.  The mid-map 'levels' of killing the spawner are not levels or even boss fights, they are just annoyances that i would skip if i could.  repetitive and dull.The town defense mode that was added to the game is clunky and not fun.   It's not awful but it's more a chore than anything else and if i wanted that kind of game i'd buy one, there are many good TD out there and this is NOT one of them.Basically other than being a little prettier it is a cluttered up version of the original game with nothing GOOD added to it and plenty of mediocre to bad added.  If you are going to remaster or remake a good game , IMPROVE IT or be faithful to it. Don't throw poorly designed trash into it just to say you added something.5/10 at best from a game that, even decades later , is a 9/10 in the original form.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, and 2, and still own both and play them once in a while on my SNES. I was so excited to see this game remastered, and was blown away by the art style. _childDocuments_.review: + one of the best soundtracks in gaming remade+ action sequences are fun- first 30min pretty much covers everything- interrupts you frequently with banality- a real eyesore to look at- doesn't evolve past 90s designActraiser is literally a "god game", in that you play as the canon Judeo-Christian God and tend to your congregation of followers while also smiting evil and heretics and fiends. It's a bit on the nose but I loved it back then and still love it today. I still can't believe that flew in the 90s, even if it was obfuscated in the western release (and in this remake, too).It's divided into two parts: city building, and action sequences. The latter don't amount to much of your playtime, I'd say they take up maybe 10% of the game with the biggest focus on the city building. It lacks granular control in that you don't place houses or farms or anything, they just appear opportunistically if you meet some criteria like your city is a high enough level or roads connect to it.I can't say it lacks complexity when the original did it this way, too. In fact, the remake adds tower defence into the mix. But the original dealt with limitations that this remake doesn't have. I'm glad the sidescrolling sections feel great to play and the levels are designed super well, about as much as the original was at least, but the city building could have been overhauled a bit to fit modern sensibilities. It just feels very barebones and dated.Control over the game is wrested from the player way too frequently, sometimes with dialog cutscenes playing rapid-fire one-after-another with next to no refractory period. This is especially true early in the game where it would be rare to go a solid minute without being interrupted. It does let up later on but just a touch.It doesn't help what you're bothered with is often copy and pasted from previous interactions. Finish a new quest? Most of the time a generic boilerplate message thanking you will play, and it's a message you'll have seen dozens of times as you play the game. Why did it need to be a cutscene, bookended by loading screens? A little popup dialog in the corner "hey, thanks for that" would have done the trick.The graphics are pretty bad. You can zoom in to marvel at your cities and they're markedly low-res and blurry, almost like they were blown up to fit the resolution. It doesn't fare much better in the action segments, where it's as if all objects on screen are pre-rendered blurry messes with canned animations. Ironically, a technique like this I might have expected on the systems contemporary to Actraiser's original release in the 90s, not for a 2021 title.I'm writing this review after only finishing 5 of the 7 cities because honestly, if you play the first 30 minutes, you kind of get the gist of the entire game. Not many new mechanics are introduced after the first city. I'm having fun with the sidescroller action segments but more than anything I'm frustrated and annoyed with the city building segments. I could have written this review after the first hour but wanted to see if they really added nothing of note and I was unfortunately correct in my assumption.As a big fan of Actraiser, I'm pretty disappointed. To be fair, what we got was fine: it's Actraiser after all, but what could it have been if more care was put into it? It feels lazy and the effort doesn't feel in reverence of the original but rather something quick and to meet deadlines. It feels like a mobile port and possibly was.At 6w max TDP, maintains 60fps throughout with no dips. Controls well on Deck. Supports 16:9 only, so it will letterbox a little. Turn v-sync off in game; with it on, it felt very jittery despite frametime graph showing consistent 16.7ms.

_childDocuments_.review: A downgrade from the original in every way, except for the updated OST. If you have never played the original ActRaiser before, you would be doing a disservice to yourself by allowing this pitiful remake to be your introduction to the series.Keep in mind, Square Enix has their name on this title. There is no excuse for it to look and play like a mobile game.Pros:+ The new OST is a fantastic re-imagining of the original score+ The hand drawn art in the menus and during character dialogue is gorgeous + SOME of the background art in the 2D platforming stages is highly detailed Cons:- Conflicting art styles make the experience feel disjointed and slapped together (it looks like a mobile game, and an old one at that)- Runtime is shamelessly extended by persistent cutscenes, tutorials, and other pace-breaking interruptions - The new siege mini game (tower defense mode) could have been a nice addition, but it is overused and can even occur randomly, furthering the issue of pace-breaking game additions- The 2D platforming sections are the "strongest" part of the experience (still not very fun), but these sections only take up about 5% of your play time due to the runtime padding- Character models often clash with their environments, and their animations are clunky- Gameplay loop is not satisfying due to constant interruptions Final Thoughts:Ultimately, the team behind this remake focused their attention on the wrong areas to "modernize" (I am being generous using that word). It tries to be so many things, (A platformer, a building sim, a tower defense game, an RTS, and a JRPG) but it ends up failing in every category. The game did not need hand drawn menu art, more cutscenes, a tower defense mode, or leveling systems. It needed a new coat of paint with a consistent art direction, and to follow the formula that made the first game a cult classic in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: If you told me that in the Year of Our Lord 2021 we would not only be getting a remake of Actraiser, but that it would also be really good, I wouldn't have believed you.  Yet, from completely outta nowhere, here we are.  This is the best kind of remake: one that takes everything that was good about the original game and builds on it in logical ways.  The action stages are still as tight as ever, but with more offensive and defensive options, making them more enjoyable.  The city-building segments aren't as much of a chore, thanks to brand new mechanics (tower defense!) and adding actual characters and objectives that breathe a lot more life into this world you're trying to rebuild.  Add a solid aesthetic upgrade reminiscent of late SNES/early Playstation rendered graphics and an improved soundtrack with great new tracks from the composer himself, and you have an impressive reminder that yes, Square-Enix does put in a lot of effort for its fans sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: So this remake/re-imagining of the classic Act Rasier on the snes is decent. The graphics have had a big improvement, they have added new content, the music was remixed and updated, and they even added a new  type of gameplay to the mix, a number of base/tower defence sequence to each region. A lot has been added, but it still remains a very basic game, just like the original. They also nerfed the difficulty by a substantial degree. I played on normal and that felt far too easy for me. I'm not all that great at the original, so seeing normal being this easy was a bit of a let down, but with the added abilities and different types of sword swings, it made for a enjoyable playthrough nonetheless. I think the biggest downside for me was all the extra dialogue. Normally expanding the world and the characters would be good, but what they did here was very basic and I often found myself wanting to just skip it and move onto more gameplay. The worst offender is the angel companion. He is nearly unbearable as a religious zealot. I know the original was censored and the master was supposed to be God, but the angels portrayal here made me want to root for the enemy or have the villagers burn him at the stake more than once. He's just not a likeable character when you are an atheist like myself. I'm sure he would be fine for those more inclined to the christian persuasion. All said, a lot of the dialgue with the new art just screams budget visual novel with it's vibes, and I'm not much into that myself.The gameplay is fun and I do enjoy it. I'm glad I played the game, problems and all. However, there just isn't enough here to warrant the price, wait for a sale if you plan to pick this up as you just don't get enough of any type of gameplay to satisfy.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a solid MAYBE. I feel the price should be cheaper for what it is and some of the added stuff should have been left out. The additional grind quests aren't all that either...grinding over an act so I can kill a couple of typhoon pigeons is not fun.Also, some of the quests that were needed to be completed in the old game are now optional, IE: I didn't have to bring music to soothe discord or deliver herbs to cure the plague.As for the side scrolling platform bit...it was okay, just remember things being harder...especially Firewheel.Overall though, it was fun to romp over the world again.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! Where to begin? If you want to experience nostalgia from one of the best games on the Super Nintendo, this isn't it. They took the frame of the original, added content without improving the elements that made the game so great in it's time. If you want to play Actraiser, just go back and play Actraiser. This one is absolutely not worth the money, and was developed by a company that seems to have most of their experience in creating Japanese train simulators (Sonic Powered).1. They added "heroes" with poor/uninteresting character arcs that seem to be relevant to the end game, with absolutely no relevance to the end game. Each one is just a weak anime trope.2. Rather than expanding on the psuedo-RTS element of Actraiser, they instead introduce a tower defense mini game that often requires a lot of prep and proper placement of towers without knowing what creature types, or from where these creatures will be coming from. Due to the mechanics of this is can result in you losing simply because you don't know whether to target land or flyer enemies, or if they will be resistant to magic or physical attacks prior to setup. If you had a rough idea of where the enemies would come from, or if you were allowed more towers you could at least prepare for this prior to the mini-game.3. Now when you seal a monster spawner you have to descend into the spawner to destroy the spawner. The spawner will spawn enemies while you try to kill it. This is fine, except at later stages in the level it will also include the boss from the opening scene to that level, so that you're fighting the monster spawner, monsters, and a boss all at the same time. This was obvious content fluff rather than creative level design. The level was a base room with recycles creature from that level. Tedious.4. There are NO people of color in this game. Each level is obviously based on a real world culture of some type. One level has "Egyptians". They're white. One level has "Indians". They're also white. The only NON-white character was some blue ice-elf looking character. This game represents an entire world of people, and they're all white??? Just shameful.I played through this just so that I could write this review and tell you that there  are no redeeming qualities to this game. I will never touch anything from this developer again, and I really hope that someone develops a spiritual successor that breathes new life into this classic in the manner that it deserves, and not what is obviously a cash grab for an aging IP.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited to see this remake come out. i loved the original Actraiser on the SNES and was just telling someone about this awesome god game i used to play when i was young, only for me to find out about this rerelease a week later. I scooped it up recently and .... I regret it. Unfortunately they added Tower Defense segments to this game, and there are a lot of them. _childDocuments_.review: is another Unreal Engine take on an earlier premise, in this case being the early 90s SNES platforming / God game.  The story is mainly about how Judeo-Christian monotheism is good as hell and everything else is sus.- Stages are still level-capped to ensure that you don't enter them too underpowered.  Look, if I want to play this game in Goblin Mode, that's between me and God, and I am God, so that's between me and me.- Build mode is so much slower as what you're allowed to do in any given moment is dictated by story progression and logic checks.  You can't just wipe out every monster den immediately because you want to and **** them monsters.- Replicated some flaws in the name of authenticity, both to the game and belief systems generally.- They've added a tower defense thing.  I haven't played a tower defense since  so I couldn't tell you if it's good or bad.- There's also a little mini platforming / enemy rush thing in between acts to jazz it up a little.- Spells are more focused on the tower defense aspect now and less on the building.  Earthquake now levels everything and not just the stuff at the lower civ levels.- Music by the GOAT, Yuzo Koshiro- Sort of resembles  games now in that you can pick up crystals and they'll count towards in-stage bonuses.- Story flows surprisingly well from the original source and expands on what's already there in interesting ways.The core game is still fun although if you're the achievement hunting type, there's twice as much game after you complete the storyline and you'll spend most of that idling in wait of more tedious sieges.

The new graphics, I don't necessarily like because it looks just slightly off to me. The new music isn't necessarily bad, but definitely different.The game is very... cyclic. You basically go through a very specific cycle now: Increase pop to unlock next quest. Do quests to unlock the next lair. Enter the lair for a timed platformer run. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm more of a "neutral" vote edging on yes.  It's actraiser, mostly intact but they made some WEIRD choices in the update.   I'm enjoying it but after a few hours kinda wish I'd waited for it to go on a serious sale and half kinda wanting to just turn it off and play the SNES one.1. The original was HARD, and the levels felt long.  This is mind numbingly easy and the levels feel considerably shorter, many bosses so far haven't even been able to hit me due to the incredibly OP up and downswing combos and the ridiculous iframes you're given.  2. Unnecessary grind quests, seriously, they add nothing to the game, hunting down and "kill 10 of monster x" that was in an old level I'm already done with, and there's not even 10 IN that level, it just padding and NOT fun3. in the SNES game your villagers had some semblance of fending for themselves by sealing monster layers, and they felt like they themselves got stronger as the game went on.  In this you have to do a weird minigame version of a bossfight for every lair that's stupidly, almost insultingly easy, you can literally walk up to the thing and just mash attack to win...4.  There's a weird lacking of animation and animation quality in the graphics, lots of little touches like the master leaving the statue and returning to the sky palace are gone, even the monster and boss animations are really weird and stiff.5.  Things feel less impactful, the old system of your stats in battle being determined by how well your cities are doing is gone, replaced by simply finding 2-3 collectables in each level, which you can reply to pick up ones you missed.6.  In the city building phase you have auto-aim now, which is pretty awful and tends to shoot wide of things if they get too close, it's far less frantic with far less danger, the monsters are pretty much no threat.7. the spells don't really vary anymore, things like earthquake are just a more expensive lightning and pretty much everything is just AOE damage.8, the interface sucks. There's a of relying on "hold and tilt" controls9. the graphics resolution is bizarre, the game "supports" higher resolutions in the menu but anything about 720p it's just upscaling...but not even cleanly upscaling, the backgrounds upscale allright for instance but the master and the enemies become blurry messes, it's like all the artwork was drawn in different resolutions.  It's bizarre but it means the game literally looks better if you leave the resolution at 720p and let your hardware upscale it.I'm definitely still enjoying it overall, it's not a BAD game, it's just somewhat of an "ok" game that I wouldn't put this much into if not for the nostalgia, and oddities like the resolution, controls, auto-aim, and severely nerfed difficulty make it fairly clear it was developed entirely with mobile in mind and them releasing on pc was an afterthought.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty clear the leaders in charge of overseeing the development of this application do not play side-scrollers.The controls sort of get the job done, but let's talk about the way the character swings his sword for example. It's imprecise, to describe things mildly. This feels like something that might work for a mobile title. I just did a quick online search, and what a surprise, this is also a mobile title. Jumping and moving in the side-scroller sections feels off and it's the opposite of fun. It doesn't help that the frame rate is a complete mess. I managed to improve the frame pacing issues slightly by using Nvidia settings to set the "Max Frame Rate" to 50, "Monitor Technology" to GSYNC-Compatible, refresh rate to "Application-Controlled", "Triple Buffering" to On, and "Vertical Sync" to On. Digital Foundry briefly covered this frame rate / frame pacing issue. Basically, Square Enix has been releasing ports created in the Unity Engine that have an absurd frame rate issue that every amateur developer would spend a little effort to resolve unless they were in such a hurry that they did not care about how the game plays and feels to the player. There is a setting in Unity called "Fixed Timestep." The default value for this setting is 0.02, which means the camera will update 50 times each second when it's attached to a 2D "Rigid Body" such as the player character. If the camera updates 50 times per second and the game engine updates 60 times per second, the game will stutter. Casual observers might not notice how this results in a less than smooth experience, but they will have far less desire to come back and play the game when this is happening.Many players will not realize this is the reason they stop playing the game. It might seem fun at first, but many gamers are not aware of the fact that this is why they keep coming back to play some games, and have no desire to come back for more on other games. Square Enix ports are unfortunately building a bad reputation, although some players (such as myself) will keep coming back because the original versions of these old titles were great. Square Enix, if you continue to release shoddy ports, it will be impossible for new gamers to gain an appreciation for these great games. Fans of these ports might still occasionally recommend these ports to first time players, but it will be far less frequent over time, and you will be missing out on a huge opportunity to sell these ports repeatedly for decades! The potential loss in sales will be exponential. The company financial leaders and stock holders might have no idea how much they are missing out on profit they could have gained by building a great reputation and consistently creating great ports of their classic games. Serious gamers will understand this. Casual gamers won't realize this, but it will be the reason that they will or won't come back for future titles! Casual gamers will not realize that Square Enix could instead increase their standard of quality, and they would become dedicated repeat customers! Casual gamers will hear about each new Square Enix port, and think, "I don't get why people care so much about these games." Instead, casual gamers could think, "Hmm, another port of a classic Square Enix game, I had a great time with the last one." Casual gamers could become excited about each new Square Enix re-release. Again, Square Enix, you might have no idea about how much future profit you will miss out on if you don't start increasing your standard of quality for every re-release! The exponential potential is massive! Your sales and profit will increase far beyond your goals and expectations!Screens generally have not updated at 50 frames per second since the 1990's in parts of Europe. 60 fps has been an industry standard for decades, so it is absolutely absurd for a massive publisher like Square Enix to publish a title that doesn't fully conform to standard refresh rates. Maybe these titles passed their weak quality assurance program, but most play testers won't be able to tell you that the game plays in a way that doesn't feel good. They will just tell you about what bugs they can find. This is why professional User Experience analysis is so valuable. You need a professional User Experience team, and you need to set your standards with this in mind. Again, this frame rate problem is an issue that every amateur video game developer learns early on. It's an issue that many casual gamers don't realize prevents them from coming back as repeat customers, and it's an issue that will increase your future sales and profits exponentially, but only if you recognize it and increase your standard of quality to address it!The Final Fantasy Pixel Remasters have the same issue, and it is unacceptable for Square Enix to try to sell games without resolving this issue.Frame rate aside, the side-scrolling sections in this game are truly awful compared to the original game. There is frequent text in the game, telling the player how they are so great and their followers in the game worship them. This was a minor aspect of the original game, but in this new version it is vastly expanded. As players who enjoy video games, we would feel great every time our character gets a little upgrade, if the game already plays well. Scrolling through text about how great and godly we are, and how much our followers appreciate what we've done is a complete waste of time, and could feel like a slap in the face to gamers who understand what makes a good experience. This demographic of gamers is extremely important. If you waste their time, the negative financial results will not be immediate. They will be exponential though, and happens over time. If you or the leaders of your company don't understand video games in this way, you will be very confused about why your some of your sales start trending in a negative direction. The gameplay in this game is just awful, so terribly awful. Steam Users: You could grab the original game using a PC emulator. It would be missing all of the 'expanded gameplay' in this new "Renaissance" title, but it would be a much better experience, especially with save states. Even though controls in the original Actraiser are a little janky, the gameplay is much more precise than this mobile attempt. Three hit combos are nearly meaningless in this new title because of the way they were designed for mobile controls and because hitting the enemy is a completely different experience. Hitting the enemy in the original was about precisely lining up the trajectory of your sword with the location of the enemy per pixel. Hitting the enemy in this new version is about sort of being close as the game calculates many other factors behind the scenes so that a player on a mobile device can tap the section of their screen that indicates the attack button, and then the program compensates for the fact that playing on a touch screen is imprecise and a completely different control.Please Square Enix, please. Hire teams who understand what makes good gameplay for all future ports. If the people in charge of the company who will create the ports are not passionate about games and can't explain what makes gameplay  and User Experience feel good, find another team to do future ports of your beloved titles! Design each port for PC and console first. Then, and only after you've made a great experience for gamepads, port the game to mobile. Or, just create two separate versions for mobile and Console/PC. Do the research. If you create ports and re-releases with a higher standard of quality, people will continue to buy them for decades and all ages,If you are not a passionate gamer, or don't have a passionate gamer as an advisor, you will never understand how negatively it affects your future profit and sales if you don't increase your stand of quality and user experience (which is often unrecognized) for ports of classic games.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say, I wasn't expecting Squenix of all companies to release Donkey Kong Country on steam, but i'm glad they did! It's an all time classic. It stands alone without replacing the original....jokes aside...Yeah, this game is pretty damn ugly. But don't let that scare you off. There's a lot of good here. The soundtrack is stellar. Each track is longer than the original, with new sections where it otherwise would've just looped after a bit.Level design isn't a rehash. It has nods to the original, but it's mostly all new layouts. If you play on hard, the difficulty is a fair but punishing retro romp that demands perfection. Of what additions are made to the side scrolling gameplay, it's all positive. Still simpler than what a modern game might have, but ends up leaps and bounds above the original (or even its all action sequel!)The town sections may be where some fans may turn up their nose. I was a fan of the additions, but the added complexity doesn't make it any deeper, there's just more buttons to press. The tutorials are a bit heavy handed and the dialogue can get a bit wordy, but the brand new characters are interesting and welcome in my book.There are added tower defense ish sections, which make the time between action stages much longer than the original. I again recommend playing it on hard, because things can get pretty tense and require you to really have a good idea of what you're doing. It could be considered a pace killer, so if you don't care for these additions you just might hate this game.Overall, I feel Actraiser was loved for the pure simplicity of its 2 modes and the ways they contributed to a greater experience. Adding too much complexity hurts the general appeal of the game.If you don't mind longer town sections and want to immerse yourself in the flavor and story, I can recommend it to you with no hesitation. If you come for the action, consider staying away.

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair, I only played it for twenty minutes but am already very sick of this modern take on the SNES classic.Overly cluttered aesthetics aside (which is personal preference, though felt quite off-putting), most disappointing is the game play being interrupted several times for mini tutorials on aspects of the game which could easily be inferred. There's additional dialogue which does nothing but slow down the game. There's additional breaks going back and forth from reading dialogue and narrative of the people and angel character to playing, and if that isn't enough the pacing is then absolutely destroyed by not allowing the player to jump in to segments without first going through the tutorial and, of course, peppering the game play with needless breaks from the city building aspect for mini games (within mini games -- INCEPTION!) invented for this version which completely negate the narrative of the scene they're intended to augment. The side-scrolling segments seem to be extended and, at least in the first level, was broken into several chunks which, when juxtaposed against the original SNES game was one short to medium length segment with no tutorials and no breaks. The length of the level is so different (IE padded) in comparison the music has an opportunity to repeat itself, which it seldom if ever did in the original. All the jumping around, invented scenes, padding and hand holding seems rather infuriating.All that said, this is just one person's opinion, one who positively CHERISHES the original. This may be more to another person's taste, it's all down to what you expect from a game and personal preference, and my experiences lends me a certain level of expectation I don't feel the game met. It may not be that way for everyone, but in saying that, NOT RECOMMENDED. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played ActRaiser 2 when i was a young kid on my dads SNES. Seeing this game washed me in nostalgia.But this game is not ActRaiser 2 or 1.This Review is basically a sort've walkthrough of what you should expect if you buy this game.  it's mostly about the gameplay and how the gameplay loop is. Only spoilers are names of some characters, nothing story related.Anyways, I don't recommend this to anyone even people who might be nostalgic for ActRaiser. This game just isn't it.I get it, I understand why they added this kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tower Defence and resource/town management. It was to force you to put more hours into the game so you wouldn't just plow through it within 2 hours and refund. Let's Begin.Act 1 of Fillmore, a stage that takes maybe 2 minutes to complete, nothing is a threat. You get to Centuarus and he's simple to fight. They give you a Back Dash, new upward/downward attacks, you're fast and if you're clearing the Act of enemies, you gain a damage buff, 20%, 50%, 100% + a 50% HP revive if you die. Trivialises the game immensely. So Centaurus just charges from right side to left. you got a platform, he charges and then slows down to a stop, animates forever that he's about to do something and you just jump over behind him and deal approx 40% of his HP while he casts lightning from his spear to his front.Villagers love you. This is where the game decides that your time is not precious and you end up playing this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tower Defence, instead of ActRaiser. I like TD games, but this ones just boring, it's tacked on to stop you from beating the game too fast and refunding. You manage the town and show them where to build. But you have next to no say in what is built. They will build a house, farm or Workshop in scripted slots. You play as the Cherub, named Angel in this segment of the game which is practically the meat and bones. Enemies will spawn from holes in the earth. 1-2 shot the enemies, get SP which is needed to use Miracles, use Miracles to destroy trees or buildings, which get rebuilt by villagers and upgraded if possible. You need to wait on monsters to spawn and Farms for SP. Food is also spawned from Farms, but one or the other. Workshops give materials to upgrade Towers/Gates and build better houses when Community Lvl is higher. You're limited in how many Gates and Towers you can have up at a time. They share a limit.Hour Glass on top the of the screen runs out, it becomes the next day and people build and you get SP/Food/Mats. You're literally at the mercy of this timer, stealing your real life time away. Quests are just checklists. Like Build 2 Gates, gather 7 Food. Gotta deal with those Holes in the earth i mentioned earlier. After about 20 minutes of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around with this village, you finally get to play ACTRAISER THE GAME YOU WERE EXPECTING. You get in the Cave, destroy the Spawner sacs to spawn the main Spawner. You spend probably 20 seconds in this 2 screen length dungeon. BACK TO THE TOWER DEFENCE/MANAGEMENT MODE. You progress a bit, and the town finally gets attacked and the game turns into a bad TD for a segment. During TD mode, you can move Philotas, a hero for your cause, to where he is needed to attack. the Cherub comes up with zero excuse why he can't shoot his arrows to attack and just watches. Philotas has taught the town how to build Gates and Towers, which are the only defence/offence options besides Palisades. They can only be placed in scripted slots. they also take up a slot a house, farm or workshop could've been. You can use miracles on enemies. Enemies come out of portals that spawn in different areas of the map, you'll end up killing them quickly by sending Philotas to fight while you are waiting on the mercy of farms to give SP if you want to clear the TD mode quicker, as miracles are a huge source of damage.The last wave is mentioned by the Angel and you're back to Town Management.About an hour is spent and you've played Act 1 for 2 minutes, fought a Spawner for 30 seconds at most. Wasted basically an hour on waiting for SP because you HAVE to blow up houses with Miracle Lightning in order to upgrade them, while also waiting on Material drops from workshops in order to upgrade said houses, sometimes you get Food over and over at full HP instead of SP, same goes for materials sometimes its Palisades unless you're capped on them.This is literally the game right here im not even kidding. You spend 90% of your gameplay being the Cherub, waiting for the SP drops and monsters to spawn for small SP gains when you kill them and the further you progress, the more expensive things get to upgrade and the less Holes in the Earth you have that spawn enemies. So you're going at a slower pace.Destroy more Spawners, wait for SP/Materials to upgrade because Quests demand certain Population requirements.Okay, finally after about 1 hour 45ish minutes of gameplay, we got lvl 3 Gates/Towers, Philotas is lvl'd up a bit too. You do the final TD of Fillmore. Its not at all challenging. Philotas gives you Fire Magic! You tell the villagers its time you got off your ass and fought for their safety. Time to fight the MINOTAURUS!Act 2 is now available, you finally get to play ActRaiser and clear a 3 minute dungeon. which you again, just melt enemies and blaze on through, no challenge. Minotaurus is at the end, and since i just got Fire Magic, why not use it. You shoot the fire ball and it hits him multiple times for chunks of his HP. He throws his Axe and its like a boomerang. He charges at you. Thats the fight. He dies in 20 seconds or less if you were killing things along the way to get that damage buff, and why wouldn't you kill things along the way?Act 2 ends, I see that im missing some scrolls(collectible) each Act had up to 3 to find. I went and took the alternate route i seen in Act 2 and got the scroll i was missing. Town is saved, Philotas gives me a magic stone to summon him in other towns TD.Now move on the next town, Bloodpool. Now instead of using Lightning miracle to remove trees i had to remove Marshes with the Sunlight miracle, which cost more SP, so longer waiting between uses.The games loop has just repeated. Time to do all the same things i just did with Fillmore but with Bloodpool.Act 1 of Bloodpool, its longer than Minotaurus' Act, not much more challenging though. The Boss actually killed me on my first attempt but that was only because i was going for all the scrolls on the first run if possible and the water is poison, you take damage when in it.  I explored til i was low HP and thats why i died to the Chimera. He's not as much of a pushover as the others, actually can be dangerous because he's mobile and ranged. Kill more Spawners after waiting in the management mode, like we did in Fillmore. Finally after multiple TD mode sections, you play ActRaiser again for yet another short, short burst. 4 minutes tops to get through Act 2 and kill the boss.I Still had 3 more Towns to save, ♥♥♥♥ that.After I saved Bloodpool from  Zeppelin Wolf, I Saved and closed the game to write this review. Save your money. This game is 10$ at most. The YES recommendeds have got to be high on nostalgia. I honestly feel ripped off. Like... not even 20 minutes of real ActRaiser gameplay throughout this 6 and a half hours i played.

_childDocuments_.review: Billed as a remaster of the SNES cult classic, Renaissance is actually more of a full-blown remake, adding numerous new mechanics, a redone soundtrack (with Yuzo Koshiro returning to update all the tracks) and a visual style oddly reminiscent of an early PS1 game - CGI models turned into sprites are the pervading graphical element here.  The sidescrolling action stages give you slightly more of a moveset to utilize (tip: your down-slash gives you a crazy amount of invincibility frames), while the city building is much more goal-driven, giving you numerous milestones to hit and occasionally having you defend your settlements in a minigame that feels like a cross between a tower defense game and a real-time strategy.  You set down forts and barricades to slow enemies while moving around hero units to engage them, and when things get too dicey you can also utilize your god-powers (formerly just used to clear terrain for your cities to expand) to deal damage and slow down enemies.  It does have a few strange technical issues - I saw an awful lot of screen-tearing on the PC version, and turning on Vertical Sync in the options didn't seem to fix it; however, turning the framerate setting to Unlimited did.  But even with those, it's a pretty solid update of a well-regarded SNES title, and worth a play for old and new fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: A begrudging thumbs up, because there's a lot they got wrong...However, I appreciate that the remake was made at all, want to encourage companies to revive great classics.  The good:  Beautiful art, beautiful music, reasonably tight game play, and as such, does justice to the original.  Having to clear out the monster spawners in action mode was a nice break from city management mode.The bad:  The city management aspects of the game were extended with some tower defense game play, that doesn't work very well and is more annoying than fun.  They took out some the "inter-city" puzzles, where like you had to develop or discover a tech in one place, then bring it to another to help their city proceed.  The cities are just completely isolated levels now.  There's no sense of developing a whole world, and no puzzles; you are on rails the whole time.  Having to "get permission" to wipe out a lair also took away a sense of freedom of play.  There is waaaay to much chitchat from the angel and the towns people; like at times it's hard to get stuff done because you keep getting dragged into (what becomes) tedious dialog scenes.I want to encourage this kind of work, but honestly I'm more likely to dust off the old SNES than ever play this again.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of the SNES  game, it has it's ups and downs from the original SNES game. The music is orchestral reimagining of the original chip tunes, which is a plus in my book. I feel that the city planner gameplay was better on the SNES, mostly because I felt like after 10 minutes of the city planning phase it became nothing but the defend the town phase (which is 4X longer) had just begun. I like the monster spawner  levels to break up the flow. The siege levels are a bit odd to start with, but I overall like them. I recommenced it to any veteran of the original, but don't think it is always gonna be better than than the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Controller TIP: Disable steam input, then launch the game.I was pleasantly surprised to find a ton of improvements and additions to one of my favorite SNES games growing up. Graphics look good. Action in the side-scrolling map plays good and feels good. There's more places you go fight in now. There's a tower defense system while you build and upgrade your civilization. The TD is not as bad as others say. I enjoy it. You also get a hero who helps you in those tower defenses. The music is amazing and you can switch between the new and the classic. My favorite part: There's far more story and character development going on. Your angel from the original game is an adorable effeminate shota with a lot of personality. I can't get enough of him. I wish this was also all voice acted.

_childDocuments_.review: ActRaiser is a unique blend of city-building and platform game. It is a remake of one of my favorite SNES games. The original had some of the best music of any game of that era. The core gameplay has been preserved in this new version, with the addition of new graphics and a few new features.Although there are some improvements to the new game there is a clear lack of polish missing that the original had. The new music is not good and has a completely different feel. Luckily you have the option of using the old music. The platform game graphics don’t look aesthetically pleasing as the 30-year-old version. On the platform side, the game has been made slightly easier. The level design was mostly kept the same. Instant death traps like spikes and pits were removed. The boss fights have been completely redone. And there are some interesting new spells added. Some of the old spells are less effective as well.In contrast, the city-building portion has been made more challenging. You can’t just destroy all demon portals at the beginning of a new city. The biggest improvements to the game are the new characters and story elements. This was my favorite part of the new game. I actually enjoyed seeing the story play out and meeting the different characters. There are these new tower defense challenges that progress the story.  In those battles, controlling the heroes feel clunky, but I did still find them fun. Maybe it’s just nostalgia, but I did enjoy this game. With more polish it could have been a great game. I am hopeful that the release of this game leads to a more refined sequel with modern gaming standards in the future.I recommend this to fans of the original game and those seeking a unique gaming experience, ActRaiser may still be a worthwhile choice, as long as they are willing to accept the limitations of a SNES-era game.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the SNES version, mainly because I WON.More than 30 years ago I had Actraiser on the SNES but never managed to beat the last boss, so when I found out that there was a remake, was this my chance to put right a 30 year wrong? The game got off to a bit of a shaky start, at less than the 2 hour mark I hit a tower defence part that I didn't enjoy so tried to refund through Steam - but fate said otherwise, with Steam rejecting my refund due to me having the game for over 2 weeks.With my fate decided, I played on. I can't remember the original exactly, but the basics were that there were a number of lands that you as a god needed to help. First you would enter the land and defeat some monster in a 2D scrolling slash-em-up before the game switching to a kind of light weight civilisation type game where you would help the people build and populate the land, using your "miracles" as necessary to make the land more hospitable. Once you had made significant progress in helping the people develop, you would fight a final boss of the land before moving onto the next land where your help was needed.This new version keeps to the formula more or less but also introduces a tower defence type section. Rather than just help the people develop their lands, you now have monster attacks that must be defeated to allow the game to progress. This is a pretty good addition and now makes the game a combination of 2D slash-em-up, civilisation and tower defence game rolled into one.Although I can't remember exactly how the last boss played out some 30+ years ago, I do remember fighting it on a platform section where in this game, it wasn't the same so although victory was eventually mine, it doesn't feel like I've beaten the part that originally stopped me. Maybe I'll get another chance in 30 years when the remake of the remake is released....
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the original game on the SNES. Super Nintendo Entertainment System. lol, mouthful. This was one of the best games out at the time. This remake is everything and more that you could have wanted from the original 16 bit classic. Not only did they remake an original but added just what was needed. Tower defense, characters, more story context, beautiful HD 2D graphics, a sublime remake of the original symphony sound track. Its a wonderful nostalgic throwback to the original. Bravo! ;)

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty awesome remake of Actraiser, overall. The stages feel like they play much easier, and the hero has more abilities and attack options. Moreover, spells now draw from an MP pool instead of being disposable; scrolls found in stages increase your HP/MP permanently.City building has more to it also. I found this part both fun and frustrating. Fun because there's way more quests, and monster spawner disposal is more involved. But frustrating in that your citizens are sometimes complete idiots and will build loads of workshops and not fields while they're starving to death. On one city, I had to literally destroy every building and force them to start over correctly just to get my population up enough to complete a quest.The addition of heroes and siege battles was pretty fun most times, but I really wish they had done more with forts. You should really be able to build more than are allowed, and the placement of gatehouses is foolish and leaves holes in your defense everywhere almost no matter what you do.Still, a really fun game. Oh, and the remastered soundtrack is great too. Recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it, so I wouldn't say it's terrible, but if you're looking at this then like me, you're probably familiar with and nostalgic for the original SNES game. While this game does have pretty much all of the content of the original, there is a ton of stuff that is added, and to me it all felt like filler added to justify the price tag. There is far more story than the original, but I didn't find any of it compelling. You are constantly interrupted while flying over the town to reveal the next story point, and after the first two towns I just skipped all of it. It was annoying. Lots of other reviews I read mentioned the tower defense gameplay of your towns being raided, and yeah, it's tedious to the point of being frustrating. Lastly, all the elements of this game feel adequate, but that's all. I'd have very happily played this without the town raids, but some other part feeling like it was just a bit better.

_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Alright to preface, I've played the original Actraiser before on the SNES with full completion.After playing this here are some of my main criticisms of the game, most of these criticisms are linked to the God simulator portion of the game. Firstly, the addition of the "tower defense" segment compared to the previous game all in all I don't believe that this was a poor idea simply poorly executed considering how this portion of the game is overall slow and sluggish  with zero indicators for how many waves of enemies the player must defend against with the addition of slow paced enemy and player hero movement. If I were to change this I would add a wave counter to indicate how many more portals open so the player knows how much longer the battle will take and also a way to adjust in-game speeds so they don't simply sit there with thumbs up their ass.Secondly, the spell mechanics I.E. lightning, rain, sunshine, wind, earthquake yada yada each of these plays their respective roles in specific areas within the game point is previously in the original the earthquake spell would effect the whole map and destroying structures and thus quality of life for the player without needing for them to wait and destroy several areas to re-raise population as the civilization level rises thus this segues into my 3rd point.. If anything it would've been preferable if the leveled spells portion only effected the tower defense segment of the game. Thirdly, the simulator "collectibles" such as the mana potion, food, barricades, and materials for the love of god who thought that making the player manually collecting these was a good idea coupled with the fact that they DESPAWN. Thus a tedious cycle of waiting and watching for mana potions is created when the player clears out all the monster nests and is trying to raise the population levels.Lastly, the removal of secret items and offerings in the god simulator portion *SPOILERS*  Thus removing player incentive to interact with the world other than "destroy villages only when civilization level is up", now you could argue that kind of game design is gatekeeping but they simply could've included other collectibles in it's place such as buffs to THE TOWER DEFENSE SEGMENT. Now onto the positive changes, They made better characterization exampled with the "heroes" a thing which are a welcomed plot point compared to the original bare bones narrative of the original in which comprised of sparse interaction of the player as a "god" and the villagers and solving their problems. This change brought somewhat nice interactions between the mortals as the game progressed, if anything main gripes were simply some of the "filler" dialogue which didn't add much to certain portions of the game. However there was a downside to this with the addition of the ANGEL CHARACTER, overall hated this characterization of the angel as they consistently griped about mortals being mortals compared to the previous iteration in which they were more so of a background helper character.Besides this, animations are a bit ♥♥♥♥ with stiff and robotic movements, prime examples being the villagers and animals in the over world section with them practically t-posing. Graphics are decent enough for things like 2d character portraits and splash arts however game craps out when it comes to stage design and monsters. Can't complain too much about those since this game did have a limited budget F square enix for not giving them the budget for it though.TL:DR Tower defense portion sucks, offerings and secrets removed bad, magic system needs changes, quests could be better done, new hero characters good narrative choice.If played purely for the combat portions then the game itself is decent enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why there are so many hating on this game. The old Act Raiser, while nostalgic and fun at the time, was simply was lacking. Especially in today's standards. Pretty much everything has been improved. Like others have said it is not a remaster. It is a remake. A pretty good one too. You can expect to find a lot of what you used to know improved, some things added and a few things removed. Nearly all positive.Imo, those that are complaining are either complaining just to complain or only viewing the old Act Raiser with rose-tinted glasses. Compared to then and now nearly all of the changes make sense.I only have 2 complaints:A lot of times when a monster spawns a cut scene will take place. Interrupting your engagement against them.Some of the sieges are just overwhelming. Almost requiring you to lose at least once to learn the patterns of the enemies. While losing a siege is pretty much little time lost. It is still somewhat frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I just rage quit Actraiser.  OMG there are just so many freaking INTERRUPTIONS!!!  WOW.  I started getting upset after a little while but then I actually got mad enough to just start skipping stories and cutscenes...The game is great, is Actraiser alright, but its got so much new crap tossed in that my expectations were kinda offput.  I expected to be in bloodpool by now but Im still in Fillmore.  I have seen like 100+ cutscenes and heres the thing - it always happens when Im just about to pick something up or shoot an enemy.  Its freaking painful and aggressive to the point of actually being aggravating.  To the end that I actually just rage quit playing because I just want to play the freaking game without it telling so many stories.I really hope they someday add the original or something to this because Im not so sure this new version is for me. _childDocuments_.review: Man I really love the hell out of this game but I can see it being kind of a hard sell and a pretty niche product.For fans of the original game, there's so much new and updated here at times it feels like a sequel rather than a remake, for people new to the series some of the old school elements may be a turn off, and I can definitely see elements of the sim/tower defense portion of the game be frustrating for everyone. However, I found all of them to be well put together and super engaging. Although the master in the challenge acts is way more mobile and feels a lot better, enough of the combat is still retained that positioning and a thoughtful plan of movement is still just as needed as in the original. Although I wasn't sure I liked the new graphics, they definitely grew on me and I find them very endearing now - and the boss intros are super awesome. I also love the new character designs, and the new designs for each of the locations and the followers in those areas is fantastic. I loved the new heroes and their associated stories, and although the tower defense portion of the game was my least favorite part, it was still fun and I enjoyed finding the right design of forts and hero pairings to pass the challenges. And of course, Yuzo Koshiro's remade soundtrack with a bunch of new editions goes above and beyond - and the option to toggle back and forth between the originals and the updated (including the brand new tracks done in the original style) is super neat. Would've liked to see the same option for the graphics, but that'd be asking a lot, especially at the price point.In terms of negative feedback my biggest complaint is definitely in tower defense - the limitation on where you can place forts and the fact buildings are semi-randomly built sometimes requires you to lightning a building over and over until a farm is built in the right place. I also wish there was some better way to grind levels in the end game than just sitting around waiting for raids as it kind of turns the game into an idle game. Additionally, in the last area, because the enemy makeup and starting hero are random, you can sometimes get screwed with enemies that your only current hero is useless against. I also wish the behavior of enemies was better explained - you do pick up on it over time, and I'm not asking it to be all laid out from the get go, but I wasted most of the early game expecting to have to wall my temple off with gatehouses which is definitely not the right strategy. I also wish there was something in the challenge acts signifying the i-frames of the upward stab and backstep - again, you learn this and for fans of the genre it's inherent knowledge, but considering the amount of i-frame abuse needed for bosses in harder difficulties it'd be nice to cue new people into. Finally, the camera in some areas can be the worst enemy, as there are a few blind drops that look like pitfalls but aren't, and some falls you'll end up in spikes or an enemy that you would've been able to see if the camera just panned a little lower when you were on the cliff overlooking them.Overall, man what a return for the series, and I will be over the moon if Actraiser 2 gets the same treatment.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my Top 10 on the SNES.  Bring introduced through a friend, I honestly have to say I might not of thought to pick the title up on my own to check it out.  Very different back then when looking into games.  Hype was all word of mouth and the articles in the monthly magazines.  But once I played it, I was hooked.So now we come to this.  And though I can admit that I'm enjoying it, some aspects of it just don't jive for me and some are just plain annoying.I think the tower defense, while not terrible, is not something I enjoy.  I understand that the city building of the past was a little bland, but I almost feel as if I've stepped out of the game at this point.  Actraiser is now over there....and I'm over here doing something else.  For others this might be a welcome distraction and a new twist that's welcoming, but I liked the older style of city building.  The Hero thing is directly connected to all of that so I feel about the same.  Though I do like the expanded dialog.  It makes the world feel a but more fleshed out.The biggest gripe I have about the game really is the constant interruptions.  It happened in the old one, but as I recall, never at this frequency.  Our cherub has been replaced with a little angel girl who is up in your face so often she's taken on the roll of over obsessive girlfriend.  The game tasks you with something, the screen fades, you go to do said task only to be halted and get more dialog.  Needy doesn't even begin to describe the characters in this game. For me, all of this has caused the 'Civ' aspect of the game to fade into the background.  There are so many distractions now you can't take the time to casually enjoy whats going on with your little people below you.At this point, I only have 4.5 hours invested.  Not that long, but I feel that the formula will not deviate all that much as it did not in the original.But even so, I'm enjoying it.  I like the look and feel.  I don't mind the mini battles in the demon lairs.  I think the characters are interesting (even the angel to a degree) and the reworked soundtrack is very well done.I would say I do recommend  the title.  I think it will have a little something for all players new and old.  Not a bad remake by any means, just a few minor gripes.

The story has been expanded and the music is awesome. My one gripe is some of the boss fights are too easy. So if they make some challenge with the tower defense part so be it. _childDocuments_.review: I own the SNES Actraiser cartridge, but my console died many, MANY years ago so I've been limited to playing the emulator version. It's really just not the same. It's one of my all-time favorite games, so finding out there was a... I guess "re-imagining" of the game, had me very excited.The music is incredible. The art style threw me at first, but after a few minutes of playing I was used to it. While I've only played it maybe a few hours now, there are a couple of things I don't like:***Sort of Spoiler Alert***   The side banter in this game is downright infuriating. At random times when commanding the angel, you're interrupted with irritating blather text from the angel and whatever characters are located on the map that you're playing in. It's annoying, it's pointless and frankly, if I didn't see a fraction of this back-and-forth chit chat in the SNES version, why would I need it now?    I don't care about it at all. I have skipped a huge majority of the game's story text and I still know what's going on, because there's a quest that tells the player what to do. I know the game will appeal to newer players who haven't had the chance to play the original (seriously, if you can find the game or rom of the original, play it), but the game really isn't that complex and deep.Secondly, the sieges. They were fun at first, but by the time I reached Kasandora, it had me worn out and the new elements of the game have become painfully predictable:1: Kill some demons2: Build some houses3: Siege!4: Kill some more-5: Siege!6: Kill s-7: Random siege!8: Build some more-9: Siege quest!10: Deal with more stupid text that can be skipped 11: So on and so onEnough already! I get it, you have to level up your "hero," but I realized the Siege quests aren't an immediate requirement, so you can take some time setting up your defenses before dealing with it. It really shouldn't have to come to that. In the end, I think if it goes on sale, sure give it a shot. But as a full-price release, I'm sorry, but this just doesn't do it for me. I'll finish the game, but the content they added onto it really stripped away much of the fun that made the original game what it was for me.
