_childDocuments_.review: First off: IF you are a 1990 SNES ActRaiser purist, then this game is not for you. There's no insult in that statement; rather, it's just a statement of fact from a person who played and loved the original some 32 years ago, himself. It is not simply an upgraded, graphically enhanced version of ActRaiser. It has some elements in it that were not in the original (heroes, the addition of a tower defense element, and additions to the story line). as well as changes and additions to the music when Yuzo Koshiro was asked to redo it for this reboot of the game. If that's the case, then so be it. We're all allowed to have our own opinions - something too easily forgotten, these days.That being said, and as a person who has played the original and loved it, I also enjoy this version. No, it's NOT an HD version of the original. In some ways, I believe it's better. In some ways, not so much. I'll briefly touch on each so that anyone reading this can make their own decision, but first I want to address something I've seen kicked around different forums - the idea of this being "woke," or The Master looking androgynous or the angel being a boy who looks like a girl. My answer to that is a resounding "Not NO, but HELL, NO!" I am not an authority on Japanese culture or animation, but I do know that they tend to make male characters look more effeminate in their features than Western cartoons do. The Master is still, very obviously, a male with long hair. The angel is called "he" and if anything, looks like a little boy with longer, straggly hair, akin to what would have been seen many years ago. I believe those who are calling this version "woke" are, frankly, looking for something that isn't there. As with anything, YMMV but as someone who detests the PC and "woke" movements himself, I'd be the first one to agree were that the case but I don't, and it isn't.The animation, play style and music are top notch. Although I miss the plainness of the music from the original ActRaiser, thus far the improvements made in this version do not detract from it and, indeed, flesh it out and make it even more beautiful. Play style and animation improvements shouldn't be a huge surprise, considering how gaming abilities have improved in 30+ years. It's smooth, it looks superb, and the monsters come to life like never before.  The story lines are fleshed out, and I do like the addition of the story lines of the heroes, as well. It makes the world that much more alive, as the heroes aren't just cardboard cutouts. As much as can happen in a game, they grow and you see it happen.What I don't like about the game (though, thankfully, not enough for it to ruin the experience for me) is the emoti-face animations used constantly for the angel and the people at different points and the tower defense aspect of it being such a crucial part of the game. Yes, it does add an interesting dimension beyond "Fight the monster/build the town/raze the town for better buildings/fight the big boss," but it also seems intrusive sometimes. Some variation would, perhaps, be in order - a town that doesn't have invasions, or something like that. However, as was said, it's  more believable in that Tanzra isn't likely to just sit back and watch you keep winning - that evil being is going to start fighting back, and hence the invasions.I haven't finished the game yet, but thus far I am very pleased with it and would recommend it to anyone who enjoyed the original. At least give it a try for yourself and give it a chance. Any review, whether positive or negative, is just a collection of opinions of someone who has played it. Ultimately, only you can decide for yourself - and so you should!

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a REMASTER of the original Actraiser. It is a reMAKE. Gameplay has been reworked, and it is a different game. _childDocuments_.review: First things first.  yes this is the same game that was on Super Nintendo.  But it has some noticable upgrades.  The 16 bit graphics aren't even an option in the menus that I could find.  It does have Game Controller support, which makes it feel and control much like the the 16-bit game we all remember from back in the 90's.       Square/Enix has added some layers to this game however, I'm not sure that's a good thing or not.  where as before you could just use the angle to protect your community as is grew,  now there are periodic raids of monsters that attack your towns.  If you weren't prepared for them, they destroy your town and temple and game over, load your last save.  The raids have a Tower Defense game type feel.  Which isn't bad except that the progression of the story is now laced with these raids preventing you from using the "letting your Civ's grow a little more to give you that extra edge" type grind for power.      As a player who enjoyed replays, I kinda liked finding the loop holes that break a game and make you Over Powered.  The Raid system has closed many of these loop holes.       Over all I am enjoying the nostalgia and Remastered graphics and audio.  I hope it dosen't end here at the first Act Raiser.  I hope they remaster and release the sequel "Act Raiser 2" which also featured on Super Nintendo.  Lastly I hope they Take the whole thing a step farther after that by creating some sort of Act Raiser 3 with like multiplayer and more quests both for Angle and for the Lord Of Light.  Never hurt to dream I guess...

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent remake. Expands upon previous, sometimes subtle, plot points. It is a longer, more dense game. The "Act" levels are much more fluid. The simulation mode is expanded, with a new "Settlement Siege" mechanic. It takes a bit to learn how to manage forts and increase your civilization efficiently. Once you do, it's extremely fun. I have a lot of nostalgia for the original, but this game can stand on it's own. The nostalgia factor is a nice cherry on top. Replayability is good: once you learn more mechanics, it's fun to restart from the beginning and really utilize them. This is a solid 8/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the original SNES game then this is a worthwhile game to pick up, especially if its on sale.The battle segments have additional QoL elements that make you feel more powerful and in control: you now have different types of attacks and moves, plus, you swap you magic spells at any time instead of being limited to pre-selecting one before entering the level. You can also use your spells in the air, something you couldn't do in the original.Also, the addition of the crystal power-ups (introduced in the second act of the first area), reward you for taking the additional risks of going out of your way to kill more enemies, while taking minimal damage, as opposed to just brute-forcing you way through the level. So its like another mini-game/challenge in itself.The sim portions of the game are more dynamic. Sealing monster lairs now lead to a min-battle stage, instead of just having the villagers do everything automatically. There's also the added element of monster sieges, which is like a pseudo-tower defense, which requires a more active usage of your entire repertoire of miracles.I ran into a few minor issues that slowed my progress in this first play-through. First its hard to replenish your SP after you've sealed all the monster lairs, making it harder to demolish lower level structures to replace them with new ones. And second, the population density is determined by the houses, but the maximum population is determined by the farms; that can trip you up if you're coming from the original game like myself, making the last stretch of the first area take longer than it should've otherwise.Overall, I'd say so far so good; The combination of old-school nostalgia plus the added game mechanics means that I'm just having fun. Enough so, that I was compelled to write my first game review ever.I'd give it a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played the original Actraiser on the Super Nintendo Entertainment System, then you know what you're about to get into. Actraiser Renaissance is a love story for our nostalgia of this epic tale. You are the Lord of Light and you must rid the land of an ancient evil. In doing so, you allow humanity to thrive. You must also take humanity by the hand and lead them into a new age. You must take them through different levels of habitats, from shacks to mansions. You must build the confidence of your people to allow them to defend themselves from evil, and not have to solely rely on your assistance.There are aspects of side-scroller hack and slash, these are the moments when you come to the planet in physical form and fight evil. Then you have this top-down section where you play as your assistant, Angel, and you further guide humanity in how to develop their community.If you have played the original, they have added new content that was never a thing. First off, they added legendary heroes. There will be a legendary hero in each village to assist you. This give more story line to the game. They have also added, what can best be described as a Tower Defense mechanic. Every now and then, either a quest will prompt a siege or it will be randomly activated. In these events you will be responsible to guide your legendary hero to fight for you as Forts that you have established will fight off waves of bad guys.Also, if you enjoyed the original title... they completely outdid themselves on the soundtrack. They have epic orchestral remakes of the original classic songs... but if you happen to miss the originals, you can either choose to have the original music play from the option menu or listen to any of the music from the provided music player.There are too many titles from my childhood that I wish would get this treatment. Again, if you loved the original, or you're into action adventure side scrollers with a little bit extra added in, this is your game!!

_childDocuments_.review: I received the original Actraiser for Christmas back in 1991 as a present from my aunt for the Super NES I also received that Christmas. It's one of my favorite games of all time as I've never played anything quite like it again and I played it when I was young enough that it's part of my nostalgia group. This game is not as good as the original Actraiser let's get that out of the way up front. The graphics are arguably worse than the 16-bit graphics of the original and some of the new game mechanics unnecessarily over complicated things. In spite of those things the game is still a lot of fun and close enough to the original that it's still a unique experience compared to anything that's been released in the last 20 years. _childDocuments_.review: GRADE A+. Its a Classic SNES game that i thought no one else had played or remembered, except me. Actraiser was a 2d action side scroller with tower defense and City building mechanics that came out on the Super Nintendo system. It was one of the games i got with my SNES and it was way ahead of its time. And here it is now, all these years later remastered and in the flesh and its still so good.Actraiser Renaissance's developers were not content with just re-releasing the game as a direct Rom port on steam; this is a meticulous remastering that elevates the original SNES classic and showcases it to modern audiences. From its original genre-blending gameplay being polished up to its technical improvements, it's a masterclass in modernizing and remastering a beloved classic.The core of Actraiser Renaissance lies in its unique blend of side-scrolling action platforming and 4X-inspired city-building combined with tower defense. You play as the god Almighty, and descend to the earth wielding your celestial powers to smite enemies in dynamic 2D levels, then Ascend to the heavens to build your fledgling civilizations. And defend them from the forces of evil in tower defense battles. This constant shift between action-oriented combat and strategic resource management creates a unique gameplay loop. Both for is time and now.The developers have not only put a fresh shiny coat of paint on the visuals. The 2.5D newly remastered graphics showcase the charming detail of the original art, while the revamped user interface streamlines city management and combat controls. And the original soundtrack receives a divine treatment, with Yuzo Koshiro's beautiful reorchestrations and new compositions breathing fresh life into the game world. And with the inclusion of extra post game content. This is the Best version of this game that exists. As well as totally worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge ActRaiser fan, this game has exceeded ALL my expectations! In fact, it's so good that I bought it twice! () That's how good ActRaiser Renaissance is. The music, the graphics, the character artwork, the writing, gameplay, everything is practically flawless.I say practically because honestly, my only complaint about the game is that there's no way to speed up / fast forward time when you're stuck waiting for materials, food, or potions in the city building Simulation parts to complete certain Realm Quests... which ends up being such a recurring issue that honestly probably added a few hours of padding to my clear time. If there was a way to fast forward time like there was in SolSeraph, this game would be truly flawless in every way.Speaking of SolSeraph, Renaissance borrows a lot from the spiritual successor to the original ActRaiser: Tower defense, combat within monster lairs, and healing magic, to name a few, and does most of it better; especially in regards to the pacing of each siege, the wait time between sieges you can't opt out of, being able to opt into the story based sieges once you're fully prepared, and various palisades. The additions of Champions also helps give it a more hands-on approach than its spiritual predecessor. There's only a few things Renaissance does worse in regards to Tower Defense - namely fort placement being too rigid. While I appreciate it being grid based, you're not allowed to just place forts anywhere you see on the fit - only specific spots. Also the vast majority of enemies are resistant to magic, making Magehouses useless for the majority of the game outside of one or two areas in the game.I know some people complain about the addition of Tower Defense to this game, but honestly, I found it to be very fun and exciting once I got use it, especially on Hard Mode. Speaking of Hard Mode, I found that difficulty to have just the right amount of danger required for me to take enemies seriously and approach them with skill, strategy, and caution instead of just tanking them like I would in the original. However, there's also a Normal and an Easy for those that'd like more forgiving and accessible gameplay.I could sing praises about ActRaiser Renaissance all day, but instead of reading this, you should be playing it and enjoying it yourself! Here's to hoping we get DLC or a sequel! If they remake ActRaiser II, I hope they add the city building aspect to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked ActRaiser on the SNES. Both japanese and english version with their varying difficulties.The music's good. Magic system's more usable but ironically the best magic on the snes version is now the very worst.I'm not a big fan of the new additions for the sim part of the game. Tower defense is not my preferred genre and this isn't even a good tower defense. It just feels like padding and grinding to stretch the time needed to beat the game with zero impact in the end game. _childDocuments_.review: Played the original Actraiser back on the SNES back in the 90s and played it again from time to time with emulators.This is a fairly close remake of the original. The design of the side scrolling levels are slightly different in layout but are still very familiar to the original. The music is also updated but you can still listen the original music.Additions to the game that were not in the original game include a tower defense style gameplay within the town building simulator part of the game. Each town has a unique champion of sorts with unique attack types and bonus such as short range physical attack with a bonus to attack power to other champions and fortifications. As you progress past the first area, you can summon champions from completed areas to help with the defense of new settlements.The game also includes a new settlement that was not in the original game with a new "secret boss" at the end of that area.Negative criticism for the game usually are about the visual design of the "god" character and the implementation of tower defense. The game's story line often has you drawn into dialogue with your worshipers quite often. This breaks up actual game play into what feels like very small chunks.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not let people dissuade you from purchasing the game. The game does have a lengthy start (about an hour) but after that it slowly stops holding your hand. _childDocuments_.review: (Friend of mine gifted this to me :D :D :D )Absolutely fantastic remake of the original Actraiser from way back when, with a remastered soundtrack from the original game's composer, Yuzo Koshiro! The bad stuff out of the way first: The graphics suck, they look like a crappy mobile game, although this *was* released for Android and Apple as well as Steam. But aside from that, it plays almost just like the original, with a few cool additions like more attacks and a powerup system based on picking up crystals. And that's just for the platforming sections--the original Actraiser had a city builder/simulation thing going on, and that's been MASSIVELY beefed up, with a tower defense type game added in as well as characters to use in those tower defense segments, all of whom have their own stories and development, which massively beefs up the original game's plot. Fantastic work, I REALLY hope this encourages Square Enix to do more remakes like this, hopefully with better graphics. This is an 8/10 remake, easily a 10/10 if you don't mind the graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: , I've read the bad review about the game not running well and I am here to tell you...They are right, but also that it isn't as bad as they say.  You see by default the game is locked at 60fps and any game running at that frame rate should run smoothly, but I noticed like many others that there was jittering and screen taring.  Pretty unacceptable for 60fps, but if you unlock the v-sync and have a high hrz monitor (mine is 144) the problem absolutely disappears.  It has been a long time since I played the original, but I do not remember such a long and boring tutorial.  Even if it was in the original game it didn't have to be like this.  I appreciate the visual novel style story telling cut scenes, but in the early game there are too many of them.  Imagine you get a visual novel cut scene explaining the objective and then the game tells you how to do that, but before you get a chance to try it the game pulls you away again for another cut scene and tutorial before you can try it out.  It shoves a lot of information in your face without much chance (if any) to try it out.  It is poorly paced and annoying, but it probably gets better after the first stage of the game. Other than that I truly like this remake of the game.  The combat feels classic while still being updated.  The bosses feel more like a battle that I can fight instead of memorizing exactly what their pattern is or using some trick to cheese them like in the old days.  If you feel betrayed by updated features and combat added to your precious 90 classic than this might not be for you, but if you are a fan of the original and like to see a beloved classic updated to be a new experience than I would defiantly check this game out.What else can I say?
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing, I beat the main "original" campaign and I find myself in some unexpected yet welcome post content.I enjoyed Actraiser back in the day. Never owned it but rented it several times 🥰 . Playing this gave me several moments of "well *that's* new!" and for the most part they were welcome moments. My first taste of this new game was discovering little new abilities in the action stages (the up and down attacks and backstep). And then I absolutely fell in love the new depth given to each land's development owing in large part to the new heroes. And I really dig the new tower defense mechanic! But this is all from the perspective of someone who's played the original game. I gotta temper all my gushing here; Actraiser is a jack of two trades (well, now 3 I guess--side-scrolling action, city building, tower defense), and is reasonably competent at each. I can't say it's ever been an expert at all of them, even now. But I think the story narrative tying all this together makes it more than the sum of its parts. Complaints are few. There are points in "sim mode" when you're just flying around with the angel waiting for things to happen or spawn. And then there's some frustration when you're waiting and the wrong thing or resource appears. "No, not spirit points, I need *apples*." Or, replace apples with farm vs. workshop because of population problems. Another complaint would be there are a couple of busy work missions towards the end of a land's quest line where you have to revisit the action stages to kill a number of a certain monster. I guess yeah maybe it's fun and okay to have an excuse to go back into them (esp if you haven't found the 3 collectible scrolls), but it got a little tedious, esp when you didn't meet the quest requirement in one pass. Final quibble is the levelling up of the heroes. You get these scroll things to level them up, a handful after completion of almost every quest.. I kinda wish leveling them up was more interactive. Like, select different super moves, or drop points in a different specialization? I dunno. Overall, my criticisms don't really hurt my enjoyment of this game. I thought this was a fantastic remake, and I think newcomers will find a good buffet of different play styles and charming characters here.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Actraiser is a game from my childhood, and I absolutely love it.  I've wanted a sequel on modern platforms for over a decade, and it's nice to see this got the treatment.  I do own a Switch, but spend far more time on my computer and figured this was a better platform for me that I won't put down for the 'next console' later.This game has some flaws to its remake.  The tower defense happens too often, and it isn't particularly fun.  Not horrible, but it slows down the pace and extends game time with just a little fun the first couple times.  The mini dungeons in each city building monster's lair are laughable - I haven't had to redo one.  Maybe they're good practice for someone who is less accustomed to platformers.  It's nice that they fleshed out the lives of your villagers and made them unique, but there's just too much dialogue every 5 seconds.  The platforming art could be better - I'd rather have had 3d models with in-engine lighting because the prerendered stuff looks a little jarring against the scene.  I liked that the original gave you more agency over which section you played next - this makes it very linear and "you have to go to this level now".  It's not like going to Marahna Still, the platforming sections are still fantastic.  They're not the same layout as the original, but they feel right.  Same goes for your character - they added new attacks, but it feels reasonable.  The boss intro gives you a little glimpse on their attacks, which is a fair warning rather than having to die a few times to see what you're up against.  The city building itself feels pretty good, minus the constant interruptions.  The redone music is absolutely superb.  It's amazing that the original composer, Yuzo Koshiro, was able to get on board with this.I hope they make a legitimate sequel to it, and correct some of the things that marginalize the original game's greatness while keeping the good additions.  There's no need to make it in the same world - take a page from Final Fantasy and give us a new world layout, dungeons, bosses, etc.Overall, it's worth playing for $30.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original ActRaiser for the SNES several times and loved it because it had one of the best soundtracks and it was one of the better looking games during the console's early years.  Also, I had never played a sim game until ActRaiser, so it introduced me to that genre.  However, the original ActRaiser was not without its flaws.  It could have been longer and the overall difficulty was too easy.  Actraiser: Renaissance attempts to address these issues while preserving the appeal of the original.  It succeeds in some ways and fails in others.  + The same wonderful SNES soundtrack is available but you can also listen to an equally great orchestral version.  - It fails big time with its graphics.  I'm not sure why they decided to use such low res textures but they look terrible on higher resolutions and there is also screen tearing.  The original game looks much better.  + You can adjust the difficulty setting at any time.  - The angel interrupts you too much with cut scenes and this gets very irritating.  + There is a "Special" mode which is basically an arcade version of the game that cuts out the sim portion and has a high score system.  I haven't played it a lot but it's fun so far. - The new tower defense system is very barebones and could have used a greater variety of structures to build. +  The story is more detailed and has new characters, but it still preserves the original plots.  I liked what they did with Northwall and Bloodpool the most.   - Some of the extra fighting moves you can do with your character are questionable.  The dash forward ability is powerful but it usually ends up hurting you if you try it on a boss, which is why I used other techniques.  Magic is also OP and it trivializes a lot of the boss fights. Please keep in mind, however, that I have only played this on Normal difficulty so perhaps Hard mode fixes these problems.  + Branching paths and additional powerups via crystals make the platforming sections more interesting. - They nerfed the giant Skull monsters that spawn during the sim portion.  They used to charge your angel if he got close and they seem slower than they used to be.  +  You get an entirely new world to explore once you beat the final boss of the original game.+ Instead of your followers automatically sealing monster lairs, you get a mini platforming portion that involves killing a spawner. + The angel is funny sometimes, especially at the beginning when he makes fun of the dumb mortals you have to guide.  +  Destroying all your hapless followers' homes with lightning NEVER gets old.Overall I'd say this is a faithful remaster of the original.  It adds many new and interesting things and it manages to preserve what I liked about the original.  However, I will caution that the tower defense portion plays a significant role in this game, so if you aren't into that you might not enjoy it as much as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing Actraiser on SNES as a kid. This version does an excellent job of recreating the fun parts of the original and adding in some new features that complement the others nicely.  However, there are some things like the tower defense and the addition of the side-scrolling portion to close the monster layers that I could've done without. Regardless, this is a fun re-make of a classic game. I love the updated art and soundtrack. I highly recommend it. 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is three steps forward, one step back compared to it's SNES counterpart. This review will assume you've played the original Actraiser and enjoyed it.The Good: -More stuff to build that is up to the player's discretion, such as defensive towers and gates that help you fight monsters.-The amazing OST using modern instruments. -Getting mini-stages when destroying a monster's lair.-Better graphic than the SNES version, obivously. Though TBH, they're not as nice looking as they should be, especially the action stages sprites.-Shooting arrows in the overworld feels good.-Little Quests you can do after you've completed a region.-More moves in the action scenes!The Neutral:-More story! This is good at times, but also slows down the game's pace. It's kind of a mixed bag of a feature. The story is not as good as it should have been considering how much more of it there is, but it is serviceable.-There's a new defense aspect to the game where an army of demons attack your settlement and your people mostly have to defend themselves (you can help with miracles). This adds a lot more to the game, and the quality of this mode is... Okay. Again, this slows down the pace. Some people want their game to be longer, some don't care for padding. I like this feature, but it's addition isn't objectively "good" like some of the 'good' features are.-Champions are a new addition to the game. They're mostly decently written and likeable, but steal some of The Master's narrative thunder. I like them overall, though some felt a bit too anime and didn't fit in well with the tone/style of Actraiser in my opinion. They REALLY should have used Christian Bible characters for inspiration instead of Fire Emblem.Bad:-Some aspects of human management, like when you are allowed to destroy a monster's lair, is more linear than the original. This was done to service the story, and I must say, I do NOT appreciate it. The addition of forts probably makes the game less linear than the original all things considered, but still.-The action scene 'leveling' system where you gain power by defeating enemies and collecting crystals (until the end of the stage). This makes players run around the stages killing every.single.little.baddy to ensure they're powerful enough for the boss. This was a VERY poorly thought out mechanic and it hurts the experience.Altogether a better game than the SNES original and a 'good' game on it's own merits. Worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I have heard this game is on Mobile for cheaper, but to be honest, I love this game. I love the writing, as it feels like the writers both respected the games story and yet still kept it full of quick yet prudent information. The early game is a tad bit on the overbearing side with tutorials, but those for the most part go by quickly and to be frank the original was made back on super Nintendo, it makes sense to keep folks up to date. The art for this game is frankly lovely, with the only weak points being the warrior of light(IE the swordsman on the cover) whom has a gba 3d models ripped into 2d sprites quality image. As someone who grew up through the early 2000's I honestly was not bothered by this, but felt it needed mentioning. The additions added here honestly are all pretty much welcome as they just add small additions onto the already solid base game from way back when. I know this is a mobile game ported over to all other systems, but to be frank, it is still worth your time. If not now, then on a discount. This is Actraiser as you knew it, just modernized.

_childDocuments_.review: Actraiser 1 was one of my favorite games on the Super Nintendo and I'm excited that someone at Square Enix loved it enough to put this much work into a remaster. Sol Seraph was a disappointment because it leaned too heavily on the tower defense aspect. 30~ years after the SNES version, Renaissance captures what made the first great game but also shows it's age. Graphically - it looks similar to Bloodstained. It doesn't look bad, but I would have prefered a bit more color in the platforming sections. I wouldn't agree that it looks "mobile" as others have claimed because I think mobile games would probably use much more contrast that I think the game could have used. I'd almost say those sections are almost Dark Souls like in how flat the color pallate is. The City Management layer looks great though, I really like how the graphics came across there. My biggest complaint is the addition of anime characters that speak for the villagers opposed to the more western style that the first game had but I did like how they used the opportunity to really try and flesh out a distinctive style for each city. Music - I was in awe through the first act because the music just transported me back to being a little kid. It wasn't just a higher quality version, but an updated one that keeps the melodies and takes it to another level. What was a great soundtrack before is just made even better. When 'Birth of the People' started playing in the City layer I lost it. Just a beautiful score. Only complaint I could make is that I wish they extended the pieces in some ways because the tracks are fairly short and you'll hear them looped a lot. The only remastered version I didn't like was for 'Offering' because i felt like the new version was a bit too lighthearted while the original had sort of a serious vibe. Gameplay - I always thought the original game had a nice platforming feel that was a bit distinct. It wasn't as stiff as Castlevania for Nintendo where you couldn't do anything once you were in the air, but opposed to Mario or later Castlevania. the control of your character was stiff. I'm glad they kept that in this game. However, I can understand if it's not to everyone's liking. Additionally, they added in a tower defense minigame that sits alongside the City Management layer and feels very natural. Along with this they created a hero for each of the cities that has a unique fighting style for the tower defense and has a story that wasn't found in the first game and again really fits well. Both of these were very positive additions because although I'm not a fan of tower defense games, they weren't particularly difficult and connected with the rest of the game well. Story - The classic story beats are still here and Summary - For fans of the original this stands as a beautiful remake of the classic game that younger generations could get into. However, the game also shows it's age in many ways. Despite the additions the City Management layer is fairly shallow, and the platforming is also pretty simple, as is the tower defense. That said, the beauty of Actraiser, is and was, that it's a game that combines two genres. If you're a fan or the original title then this should be a must buy for you because it will bring back great memories. If you're a new fan looking to get into the game then please do, but be aware that it won't hold up to modern games with similar elements. Overall, like a peasant praying to the gods for deliverance, I keep the faith that this title will inspire someone in the new generation to give us a bounty of games of it's type.

_childDocuments_.review: I am the not-Judeo Christian Islamic God that is out to save the world from my arch-enemy not-Satan, also known as Tanzra in this new remake of classic game from the 90's, now on PC with glorious graphics that look like they came from a handheld gaming device from the mid 2000's to mid 2010's.Pros:Same game underneath all the new stuff they added.Can expand the size of your miracles so you can destroy more of the homes of your worshippers to get them to build better homes and fields.3D graphics in a 2D gameNew additions to the game like expanding the storyline for the different regions of the game in having unique npcs that are legendary heroes on top of your townpeople having their own portraits. Now the people from the desert region can stand out from the people that live far up north or in the start town.Face lift for your character, enemies, and the angel.Cons:Graphics look rough and came from the 2009 or 2011 on a handheld gaming platform.The town defense segments are tedious and not that much fun.Side quest that have you kill a number of a specific enemy are annoying. I don't like revisiting previous stages just to kill 15 lizard men or 6 skeleton dragon warrior things.Can't name your character God or YHVH. This sort of censorship could of stayed back in the 90's but then again, this game ain't a Steam exclusive and I wouldn't be surprised if devs are simply following rules from other platforms that aren't on the PC.Your mileage may vary in the appearance of your character who looks like some sort of "bishounen" and the angel looking like something out a of a anime themed mobile game.Overall, if you're a fan of the original game, I say give it a shot but otherwise it may not be all that appealing. I recommend getting the game on sale because spending $29.99 would be ridiculous for many and I paid that price simply because I enjoyed the first Actraiser and even its less well-received sequel. And the tower defense aspect of the game feels too frequent, and it doesn't make much sense in why you have to rely on the special hero NPC to save the people when the devs could of made the player be more involved in letting the angel be able to shoot arrows. Maranha will literally be a pain with its first tower defense segment.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the original. It is probably one of my most played SNES games. I was really excited to see that this game was getting a remaster. That said, I would give this game a neutral rating if I could. I love the updated visuals and soundtrack, but I absolutely hate the tower defense mechanic that seems to have replaced the city building portion of the game. And even while building you are constantly being interrupted by the people telling you something new or presenting a new quest, like the game is trying to rush you through it. Overall, I would say I've had fun with the game so far, aside from the tower defense bit, but I would recommend waiting for a sale before buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really good remaster / remake of Actraiser. I've played 4.5 hours straight and the only real fault I have is that "Normal" mode is too easy for someone who's played the SNES version. Hard mode is firm but fair (so far).Edit: I found a second fault - screen tearing on default settings with vsync enabled. _childDocuments_.review: A good homage to the SNES classic, with beautiful music and expanded gameplay. You can no longer just straight up cheese some of the bosses, and the added tower defense elements were unexpected and add additional play. I'm grateful for the difficulty setting, as I'm not very good at the action stages, and in the SNES original I had to use a Game Genie to get through them.The major downside is the vastly different resolutions of all the art assets, which range from barely noticeable backgrounds unless you pause, to the absolutely horrible scaling of the player character in action segments. I would've expected at least that last sprite to be tested to look acceptable on such a common resolution of 1920x1080. Having pre-rendered graphics was definitely A Choice, but I can't imagine why they didn't pre-render at least a few important graphics at differing resolutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, but if I'm being honest I think I thumbs up it because the nostalgia factor is so high. The levels, the music, everything is ripped straight off the SNES version of the game, which is fantastic. The tower defense stuff they added is... a little bit random, but ok. If this was a movie I would say it needs editing. It is very - VERY - unusual to play this game for more than 40-60 seconds without the game interrupting you for something. Any quest that you get starts with the angel interrupting whatever you're doing and telling you people are praying and need you. The game then forces you into the temple, where there's a pre-set dialogue for each city of the people confirm that they are, in fact, praying. Afterwards it pops up a quest log, you select the quest, and it does an introductory dialogue between you and the people, and then the quest dialogue. This then leads to a quest summary page where it tells you what to do. If you're unfortunate to have satisfied the quest requirements already (obtain 500 resources for example) then the moment you go back into the game you'll be approached by the angel.... telling you people are praying, and sending you to the temple.... The people will then confirm that they are in fact praying, and then there's a quest window where you can turn in the quest.Aside from the interruptions I think it is really fun, but the interruptions are enough that you can't play it for long stretches at a time because it gets aggravating.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this remake. Would recommend, especially if you enjoyed the original. I could still see myself playing the original sometimes when I miss the pixel art and the original action/ platforming mechanics. If I'm more in the mood to re-experience the story / the sim mode, this will be my go to version to play from now on.PROS- The remixed music is spot on. Such a good soundtrack.- The sim portions are better in the remake than the SNES version by a mile. - Brings new life to the story with visual novel like dialogue scenes and new characters.- New RTS/tower defense style protect the city from enemy raids mechanic in the sim mode.- Now you need to enter the monster lair and defeat the core when your people are trying to seal a lair.- There is new postgame content. Including a new area to guide a new kingdom, a new storyline, and a new final area / boss to challenge.CONS- The action sections felt better to play on the SNES version. Just my opinion, but the SNES version's levels and bosses just felt more clean cut, well balanced, and polished. Remake isn't bad though, just not as good for those parts.SIDE NOTE- either a minor change or possibly a mistake? They used the music for 1-1 again in 1-2. The 1-2 music comes up again in another level where it is supposed to be, so its in there. Not sure if it was intentional or if it was an oversight.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the perspective of someone who have played the original once the whole way through, I really enjoyed the remake.Admittedly my first impressions was a bit uncertain at first with the 720p sprite resolution that is glaringly pixelated in the action sequence - after 12 hours or so, it doesn't bother me as much and I think it carries a certain retro charm that I can totally appreciate.A lot of the game feel was preserved quite faithfully from my memories of playing the SNES original - with the slightly dated but still responsive platforming, animation frames that felt very much referenced from the original (for better or worse) and the sometimes cheap but cheeky traps in enemy placements.As to what has been added, I really enjoyed the new story content and the new characters that I have met so far are fairly likeable. Personally see it like additional seasoning to the core narrative structure of the original game and they don't overstay their welcome. What I really love is them really giving each locale very diverse costumes and some semblance of unique cultures. The newly added realm (tower?) defense segments is a welcoming addition though do expect it being more like a mini-game which isn't particularly deep or offer room for creative alternative solutions.Definitely recommend completing it. :)(* p/s: The soundtrack rocks! :p And also am probably biased because I'm a Falcom junkie and the composer Yuzo Koshiro also done the Ys 1 & 2 soundtracks. Also can't help but feel the game does have that nostalgic and wouldn't feel too out of place putting it side-by-side with Ys 6 :p)
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: I have quite enjoyed the game so far, I've progressed most of the way through unlocking the regions in the game, and completed the second acts of two regions. For the most part it's a great game that I've enjoyed quite a bit.If there is one thing they could do to make the game better, it would be removing the tower defense mechanic that they shoehorned into the game. It cannot be overstated how bad of an addition it makes, it breaks the flow of the town-building, adds no lore, and takes an inordinate amount of time to do it. They also interrupt town-building progress half a dozen times for it, and then proceed to spawn randomly infinitely after you finish the last one you're forced to do. I have absolutely abandoned the first town just because I don't want to do them anymore. They're not fun. It is genuinely that awful of an idea, the person who thought of it and the person who gave it the green light should both be fired, blacklisted, or just give them the back alley treatment with a colombian necktie, whatever it takes to make sure these sieges never see the light of day again.The Heroes could be completely cut as well because their only function is in these sieges, but they could just as soon be left in as lore characters that serve no mechanical purpose.I also have mixed feelings on the action sequences thrown into sealing monster dens, it's a departure from the original where they make a point of saying that your followers have sealed the monsters' dens on their own, whereas now they're totally reliant on you as their god to do that for you as well. Mechanically speaking it's just okay, you're thrown into a small arena and destroy a monster spawner. take it or leave it I have no real strong opinions beyond noting that it changes the lore to make humans even more useless.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some rather ugly side-scrolling level visuals, Actraiser Renaissance is an extremely fun remake of an SNES masterpiece. Even if you haven't played the original, give this a shot if you enjoy side-scrolling action games.The town building segments are more fleshed out. They take longer, for one. They also have new defense segments. Throughout the segment, you place defenses, such as gates and ranged attack towers. During these defense segments, enemies spawn across the map, and you place small barricades and direct a small number of hero units to push back the invaders. It's an enjoyable distraction from the main focus of the game, though these defense segments occur too often in the story for my liking.Side-scrolling combat has been fleshed out, magic now has an MP cost instead of 'each cast uses a scroll icon'. You have actual combos you can do, though they are rather simple, as opposed to just a single slash you repeat over and over. Bosses are a much bigger threat, and don't devolve into just tanking hits to rapidly slash at them, like in the original. Magic is much more powerful, as well.This is an easy recommend if you enjoy or are interested in the original, otherwise you may wanna hold off if you're just curious, this is bound to go on sale sooner or later.
_childDocuments_.name: Actraiser Renaissance

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite the surprise, and I'm glad to say, it's not only a very good remaster of the original game, but it also adds so many gameplay elements, so much content, it's hard to say it's not worth it's price. The new tower-defense-ish segments are really fun, and a great addition to the game.One thing that is kind of weak in this is the action/platforming segments graphics, which are a weird style of pre-rendered sprites and backgrounds, but even that grew a lot on me - reminds me of the late 90s, and it's not that ugly in action.If you played the first game and love it, this is well worth the price. If you like action platformers and city builders, but don't know the series, it's also worth checking out. This is just a fun, solid game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was one of my top favorites back when I was a kid, was totally surprised when they popped up a remaster of it.  It's got all the best parts of the OG, but brings a lot of extra flavor to the game with War Battles, Heroes, mini dungeons, and what not. It definitely gets a boost from nostalgia, but baring that in mind, it's still a great game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: !CAUTION! Extreme bias below, may not be a subjective review.I am a old school die hard fan of the original two Actraiser games, they were and are my all time favorite games (Honestly Actraiser 2 was very weak compare to Actraiser 1) and has had a influence on my entire life, hell I got my gamertag and profile pic from this exact series. I've played through the original at least a hundred times in my life at this point, So I can safely say I may have a general understanding of what I'm comparing to while I currently play this ReMastered version.I've just 100% the first region (Fillmore), and wholly expect the rest of the game to follow a very similar route and not stray mechanically from what I've seen. It would be wrong to say this game is a ReMaster, it's not just updating the graphics and sounds, it adds new elements to it and changes old ones. Bosses have different abilities than the SNES Act, town management has special resources besides mana, there is a mini tower defence game built into it, monster lairs are basically a rip off of Sol Seraph's exact same concept, there are special hero characters, There is a boat load of new story, levels have been changed though keep a familiar overall design and layout. Uhg this is getting long, basically there is a lot of new and changed content not in the original game, so it's a rework not really a remaster, however that is fine, a 1 to 1 remaster would make a sub standard game by today's standards. It needed the bells, whistles and gadgets on top of the facelift to ensure it's still relevant.To sum things up, there is a few things I take in to consideration.1. Is it faithful to it's Original? - Yes2. Is it a Good, quality product? - Yes3. Is it appropriate for modern gaming, not just Nostalgic? - Mostly Yes4. Is it fun? - Yes5. Is it a superior game that new comers will instantly fall in love with? - No, It will seem very much like many other games out there, it will not stand out in the sea of games we have today.All in all, its worth a play through for both the oldies like me and new folk just hearing about it, $30 price tag seems a bit steep, but not overly so, $20-$25 would make it more attractive for all, it is after all advertised as a SNES Remaster of a 31 year old game. I however, will never uninstall this game from my current computer or any future PCs I will own. As stated, I am biased, I love this series and will likely play this new version at least a solid dozen times through.10/10 Totally biased and loving it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending, but only barely.  Music- Fantastic.  The update is perfect.Graphics - Really not that great.  Looks like a Unity project.Gameplay -  Just like Actraiser!  Except...Added story.  This was a good addition!Added tower defense segments.  Here is where I'm deciding to refund the game.  Its not bad, its just not for me.  I played the original extensively, and the tower defense portions feel like they drag out the gameplay.  They are NOT bad.  They're simple, and an added mechanic.  I just don't personally like it.If you've never played Actraiser before, you might really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Blast from the past! I remember the old SNES version of this game. Loved it then, loving it even more now with the updated graphics and game play.  More options than what I remember from the old version of the SNES title. With the addition of "heroes" in the game and different scenarios, makes this game a keeper. Not to sure about replay factor. Still all in all, Still fun to play and relive your past childhood. 8/10 rated by me.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love the game. Loved the original and this remaster feels more like a remake. Kept the original theme but expanded upon it, making you feel more involved with the world. I've only a few hours in but I'm absolutely invested with the changes. The town battles were something I thought I'd hate at first, since I liked the simplicity of the original, but I found myself actually sitting down and thinking out strategy to protect the little people and their lives. _childDocuments_.review: Two remakes from Square Enix so far this year, and both happen to be my top two favourite games of all time! NieR and now Actraiser. This makes me incredibly happy, especially since both work on Linux using Proton (would have been nice to have native support, but that is too much to ask). I was shocked - my jaw literally dropped - when this was revealed during the Nintendo Direct. My son, who is only 8, even recognized it and was also surprised about it. First thing he asked me this morning when he woke up was, "is the new Actraiser out?" Yes, it is. And it is glorious.It's nice that they added some new stuff to it, but I would have been happy with a 1:1 revamp, too. I'm glad to be replaying this, though by modern standards, it probably will fall short for a lot of newcomers. For me, the original game certainly feels dated these days, but was ahead of its time back in the day. This polishes it up enough and makes it a bit more forgiving, that I feel the nostalgia without the frustration. The original was always greater than the sum of its parts, and the sequel demonstrated just how true that was, being comprised solely of mediocre platforming, and none of the great townbuilding stuff. This remake expands the townbuilding, and I welcome it. More of what I loved about that game, while ever so slightly polishing the platforming to make it more tolerable than revisiting the original.I don't know if I can whole-heartedly recommend this game to newbies, or to fans of the original, for that matter. Just because it is different, and the visual changes aren't amazing (the music is nice, though, and the original music is also an option in the menu). But if you're considering it, what do you have to lose? Literally nothing but an hour or two of your time, because Steam offers refunds. So, give it a go, and see if you like it!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it and really liked what they added.  Finishing the last of the achievements is a bit of a slog but honestly, I had a blast and it was true to the original.  Most of the complaints I see would also be true or even worse in the first game as it relates to mechanics and combat.  When it comes to the additions the city tower defense game can get old but I enjoyed it and finished almost all of them on the first try on hard.  The lair batters I enjoyed as well.  As a faithful remake I give this a 9/10.  As a modern game if you never played the original it is going to be lower than that for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mobile port. No graphical upscaling was done, therefore the blurry 2d sections look horrible with an uncanny valley effect between the crisp 3d environments and the moving ms-paint bitmaps.They added in a lot of immersion breaking portions to the game. The towns now have extra scripted events that are really unnecessary. The tower defense sequences are also tedious and painful. If you do buy this game, read a guide and cheat on those. They weren't well planned or programmed.This port is not as fun as it's 16 bit counterpart.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent all around game. Not only does  it have all the elements of the original, but they added a bunch of quests and siege elements to the city management portion. The action sections are also a little better. Your avatar has some special moves, the enemies are a tad smarter, the bosses take some more work, you have checkpoint saves, and the levels are a little longer. There is some weird movement during the action sequences that is not helped with v-sync, but the game is more than playable, at least in fullscreen mode. Action and management sections also have much improved music, which is a nice touch. Or you can elect to play the original score. Please check the videos before buying this game. One guy (who apparently needs fantastic visuals) elected to not check the screen shots and videos, purchased the game anyway, then complained the graphics were no good and demanded a refund. Weirdo.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a middle of the road one. Great performance, has unlimted fps and many resolutions supported, I'm running 4k and hitting 500fps in action mode and over 1,000fps in god mode, capped it to 144.Game has a weird screen tearing issue, but weirdly for me setting the fps to 144 in the menu on my 4k 120hz display removed the tearing. My biggest issue is that while menu's are high def and so are cutscenes the gameplay itself all seems to be designed around 720p, so the models and levels look really low res, especially when up at 4k. May be a deal breaker for some and I would really love to see some 4k background and higher quality models.If you've never played the game before maybe wait for a sale as the PC specific stuff could be better, I went in since I loved this game growing up and I;m glad they made a new way to play and preserve it outside of emulation.

_childDocuments_.review:
Heaven, earth and mankind - Create and destroy everything according to your will! 
Experience the revival of the 90's classic hit "Actraiser". 

ABOUT 
Actraiser Renaissance combines 2D platforming action (Realm Acts) with a City-building simulation (Realm Management) in the ultimate battle between good and evil!

Featuring the soundtrack that sent shockwaves through the gaming world when it was first released, composed by the legendary Yuzo Koshiro - now remastered!

Help humanity flourish by playing as the Lord of Light and their loyal angel in a world beset by evil. 

NEW FEATURES:

* Remastered 2D graphics present the game in beautiful HD
* 15 new music tracks, as well as re-arranged original tracks by Actraiser composer Yuzo Koshiro!
* New stories, expanded action and realm management gameplay, additional action stages, an all-new realm, and new more powerful bosses!
* Auto-save and difficulty levels

GAME SYSTEM 
Realm Acts: Strategically cast powerful fire, ice, and other magic in these 2D action stages. Humans return to reclaim the realm after you conquer these stages, allowing you to begin cultivating your settlements.

New magic that was not available in the original game has been added along with the ability to dodge. Players can also attack with upward and downward motions for a more dynamic action experience. You will need every new trick in your arsenal to defeat stronger bosses at the end of the new action stages. 

Realm Management: Help humanity flourish by cultivating your settlements and offering guidance. Use your miraculous powers to summon lightning and trigger earthquakes to remove obstacles such as trees and boulders that impede the growth of your chosen. Play as the Lord of Light's angel and use your mighty bow and arrows to drive back the evil monsters that prey on your people.

Protect your settlements from enemy raids in real-time strategic battles. The placement of your forts and timing of your miracles is key to achieving victory in these engagements.

Experience all-new tales of humanity's struggles to overcome their flaws and failings as they learn to love one another and together grow stronger. Altogether, these new scenarios amount to more than twice the story present in the original. Explore the vast new realm and enjoy building your settlements for longer than ever before!

MUSIC
The original Actraiser composer, Yuzo Koshiro, has re-arranged all of the iconic original tracks and added 15 new tracks as well. Players can listen to the original music or switch to the re-arranged versions while playing the game. Tired from protecting and raising your villagers? Then just sit back, relax, and enjoy the tunes.

name: Ocean's Heart
detailed_description: Ocean’s Heart is an action RPG featuring detailed pixel art with a heavy focus on exploration. In a lively world teeming with secrets and mysteries, Tilia sets out in search of her missing father. Follow the trail through the ruins of a flooded kingdom, shape the future of the current world, or keep your head down and focus on your own mission in this epic retro-inspired adventure! Explore a detailed and beautiful world, brimming with secrets hidden in misty forests, isolated mountain peaks, or saltwater marshes. Every area is filled with unique and meaningful sidequests, ancient mysteries, and dangers. Battle fearsome monsters and wield various weapons and ancient magic to defeat or outmaneuver them. Search for special materials to upgrade your weapons until you're demolishing monsters who once put up a fierce fight. Gather various items throughout the world to craft potions, upgrade weapons, and expand your ever-growing arsenal. Game Features Retro-inspired action RPG with modern trimmings. A lively and gorgeously pixeled world full of secrets free to explore at your own pace. Menacing enemies and tense boss fights that’ll keep you on your toes. An exciting array of weapons, spells, and abilities. Experiment to find your favorites for every situation and foe. Unique, character-driven sidequests with heartwarming or twisted stories that expand upon the world’s lore. Foraging and crafting elements to increase your chances of survival in a nasty fight. Quirky charm and humor to keep you smiling on your extraordinary adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't review a game I didn't recommend a little, but this is about as half-hearted a thumbs up as possible.This is, as far as I can tell, a mostly one man operation, which explains why some things are really good and other things are barely passable. The art is beautiful (I love the little cloud of "KO" smoke when you kill some enemies; really good), from the animations to the wonderful backgrounds, and some of the music tracks go hard. It's fun to explore the nooks and crannies to find different things, and I enjoy that feeling of happiness when I find a shortcut between one part of the world and another.The problem is the level design and the enemy design. The problem is the game is hewing so close to Link to the Past in some parts that I solved puzzles by saying to myself, "What was the solution to this in Link to the Past?" Most of the dungeons directly try to evoke Zelda magic, and it takes me, an armchair designer who's watched videos on Zelda level design, a couple seconds to realize these dungeons are flabby and uninteresting. Enemies vary from fine -- oh, it's a Zelda bat -- to "so this is a mushroom you one hit, who makes a damage trail when he dies that keeps you from moving through him for three seconds", which is less good. A lot of the bosses in the game are just regular enemies who hit harder.The difficulty curve is all out of whack, too. The game is hard for the first two hours, as you sell resources to the bone to afford measly power upgrades and get killed by enemies who do way too much damage. But then you reach the second area, and that pretty much goes out the window: suddenly you have a half dozen fairies, more health than you know what to do with, and enemies die in one hit. And it becomes hard to find something that does more than a half-heart of damage. Top that off with the fact that it was trivial to hit the cap on healing items, and the game becomes a cakewalk for an average player (and I have never met a Zelda enemy I can't run into).I feel like this is coming off real negative. Oceanheart is fine. If you want to play Zelda, and you've played all the Zeldas, and you don't want to just randomize Link to the Past, this is a fine diversion. It's pretty, and sometimes it's funny (other times, there are some facepalm-level bad jokes, so ymmv). I don't regret playing Oceanheart, but I feel like I won't remember it when it's over.

_childDocuments_.review: More of a neutral rating than a negative one. I would only recommend this on sale. Fairly frustrating at times with its gameplay. You certainly won't be using any of those items you craft and other respective weapons you find (spear, magic orbs) are useless in comparison to sword and bow. Enemies are often placed right in front of you as you enter a room, making it impossible to avoid being hurt. Roll is fairly useless as Tilia has an enormous hit box. From a story point, it seems bizarre that Tilia can't swim considering that she's in the Navy and the world is flooded.Story is ok, dialogue is nice and the art and music is pretty. The sidequests are enjoyable enough. The map is practically useless when it comes to details. I had a few glitches and crashes throughout. Unless I missed something you get more coral for upgrades than you actually need. Bombs are hen's teeth during the first half of the game; use them sparingly. Ending is rather anticlimactic.Really only get this on sale. It's fine but there are better games in this style out there.

_childDocuments_.review: 14.8h (100% achievement, finished the game with most upgrades) No. Yes (20 achievements). No. is an action-adventure game, played in a similar style as the old  games. It offers a vast area full of secrets and side quests that allow you to explore more optional areas.- A lot of secrets to find- Side quests to keep you busy- Different weapons that can be used based on your playstyle - Map is almost non-existent- Bosses can be cheesed- It's easy to fall to any body of waterIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 clearly took inspiration from  for its visuals. There are a lot of similarities, from the square-like indoors to the nature-themed overworld. The game still tries to make some differences, though. Different areas have a different look and feel, with a color palette that is unique to them. Areas aren't square-shaped too - the screens are still connected, but they look like modern games with larger areas on each screen. Dialogues might be plenty, but most of them feel empty. You can just skim them to get the gist of what the protagonist is going to do, and you won't miss much. As for the dialogues themselves, they try to be funny with characters showing how foolish they are, but sadly, they didn't catch my interest. Part of it might be because I'd rather do some exploration rather than read dialogues in Zelda-like games, but the empty dialogue doesn't help either.If you have played any Zelda-like games,  is played exactly like that. You'll be exploring a world with a sword in your hands, slashing monsters and exploring dungeons along the way. A level-up system is implemented in the game as well, which is done through collectibles that are scattered around the world. These collectibles will be located in a place that you won't expect, requiring you to use your wits to solve them. See an odd-looking wall? Try using a bomb at it. A grass looks fancy to you? Try slashing it.Despite having an exploration as its focus, the map sucks. It only shows the general idea of the whole region, not a detailed image of how the screen looks. Heck, there isn't even a dungeon map. This makes it hard to remember most places, especially since there is more than one way to reach a certain location. Revisiting places can be difficult since you need to remember or take notes of where everything is.The game is fast-paced. However, it can be hard to dodge enemies' attacks, especially with how quick they are. Since most enemies don't have a set attack pattern, you need to predict whenever they are attacking first, which takes too much effort to do. The thing is, enemies, including most bosses, die in a few hits, giving you no reason to avoid their attacks. Some bosses might be bulkier than others, but you can always spam health-restoring items to recover your HP.Side quests are plenty. Although some areas are blocked by upgrades, others are locked until you do certain side quests. These areas are usually short, although it's still fun to explore them. The game always rewards additional explorations with either hearts or upgrades, so you'll never feel like wasting your time.I finished the game in 14.1h and spent more time looking for upgrades that I missed. Those who just want to finish the game quickly will finish it in less time, although honestly, they will miss a lot. The main story only covers some areas in the game, and you need to do the exploration by yourself if you want to get the most out of it.As for the difficulty, it's not hard at all. Bosses can be cheesed and health-restoring items are almost everywhere. There is a hard mode for those who want some challenge, although I'm not sure if the game's mechanic is good enough for it. The hard mode only adds more damage instead of making the enemies smarter, and as I said before, it can be hard to avoid the enemies' damage.There are too many instances where you can fall into a body the water, reducing your heart as a result. The keybinding also takes time to get used to. I'd rather use my sword with the A button in my controller, but the game seems to bind the sword button with the cancel button, making it hard to change the keybinding for both the cancel and interact buttons.As someone who enjoys Zelda-likes, I also enjoyed . The quality might be less from  games, but it still doesn't disappoint. Exploring the whole area feels satisfying since the game always rewards me with upgrades, and there are just so many things to explore.You are free to explore everywhere you want and progress the main quest at your own pace. There might be some progressions that are locked behind upgrades, but the same can also be said for additional areas as well - you are bound to reexplore the whole thing at some point. If you enjoy playing a game with exploration at its focus, especially those with a lot of secret areas, buy this game at a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't play many Zelda-like games on PC, but Ocean's Heart really hit the spot in terms of old-school feel, vibe and gameplay.Developer Max Mraz has created a fantastic game that draws inspiration from the old Zelda titles like Link to the Past and Link's Awakening but adds a totally fresh outlook on the action RPG genre that we know and love so much!The story is simple to understand and very light-hearted. The characters/main and NPCS' are likable, with most of them dropping hints on how to reach or find hidden items and quests.What I found extremely rewarding was how detailed and easy to follow the main/side quest logs are.As with many Zelda-like titles, the puzzles are present in many of the dungeons. Some are very easy, but some will have you scratching your head on what to do next.  Ultimately, they are not overly complicated to complete.If you're looking for a Zelda-like title with great pixel graphics, enjoyable gameplay and fun story then look no further than Ocean's Heart!   Oh and the music/soundtrack is superb as well.Also check out Ocean's Heart First 50 Minutes of Gameplay here -

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential, but it doesn't go far enough in any direction. It is clearly an attempt at a love letter to Zelda among other classics. That's it though, just an attempt.So, what's wrong with it?Most enemies don't have tells, and when they do it's either an attack from the sky or from the ground that isn't really related to the sprite wiggling. If a giant jellyfish attacks with sky lightning, you'd expect the sprite to have some electricity particles or something right? Nah, it just wiggles. Then lightning.There are three types of attacks, generally speaking.	1. Attack comes from the ground under you or the sky above you.	2. The enemy simply charges at you without any warning.	3. Big brute types have a short animation before attempting to punch you.There are many, many more types of 1 and 2. In addition, multiple types of enemies are invulnerable at points in their attack for no reason. There's no visual indicator either.Finally, there's like maybe three bosses in the game? There are 'mini bosses' that are basically enemies you've seen before but they don't really do anything special. You get several different weapons and abilities in this game. None of them matter. I mean it. Unless it's a progression based attack (Bow/Mace), you can simply ignore them.For some reason you can upgrade your sword and armor to insane degrees incredibly quickly, trivializing every fight in the game.You can also spam the ♥♥♥♥ out of your sword. I don't know why they didn't put a cooldown. You can swing before you're done swinging. This means that you can't leave yourself open with a badly timed swing, which may have introduced some kind of combat mechanics into the game.Let's say you're terrible. Death doesn't matter. In fact, you get almost all your health back when you die. Death is actually an option to healing for free.However, you should never need to die thanks to...THERE ARE SO MANY HEALING ITEMS. Like holy ♥♥♥♥, what were they thinking? You can pause and heal to full any time you want, even mid-boss fight. Let's be honest, this game isn't trying to be a hardcore souls game or something.However, even classic Zelda knew better than to let you have infinite healing. Between barely being able to be hurt, and pockets full of bread, you will only die if you stop touching the controls.You COULD go to an inn to heal. It costs a fair amount of money and WHY WOULD YOU DO THIS. Either eat from your infinite healing pouch or get killed. There is no reason to ever go to an inn.So I just got done explaining how you're a walking god, right? Well, that's only true after the very beginning of the game. For some reason, within the first couple hours or so, there are many things that will just one shot you.That's it. Just one shot. And these creatures are very easy to find in caves near the starting town. It feels just...weird? There's not much warning to them, and it's not like appearances matter enough to warn you. As I mentioned death doesn't matter it just feels really odd as a design decision.After that you're a god, and that is it's own problem.I just don't know why this is here. There's no need for it. There's no reason for it. It's clearly integrated into the game world as you can pick up crafting materials everywhere and can craft at certain locations in towns.But you're already an immortal god fighting enemies that don't know how to move properly. Why do you need to take half damage or do a number of other things that would further make the game trivial?The world looks nice, but feels bad to move around in for some areas.In particular, SOMETIMES there are ledges you can jump off. And MOST OF THE TIME you cannot jump off a ledge. There is no visual distinction, and many areas that would be nice to quickly drop from you simply can't.However, you are more than free to drop into every single puddle of water. There seems to be an issue walking onto moving platforms sometimes as well, where you drop into water instead of walking onto the platform.Also, sometimes you go through doors and an enemy hits you immediately. It isn't super often, but it's still noticeable. For the first time coming through the door, there's no way you won't get hit.There are actually a lot of dungeons. By dungeon, I of course mean a handful of rooms and enemies without puzzles or interesting mechanics. With a lot of back tracking.The dungeons are just boring, honestly. The only good one is the final one, and I'm using 'good' loosely.For a game of this style I was expecting numerous clever puzzles, and I think the only actual puzzle was at the very end. Super strange considering the number of tools available to you at the end.Christ. Stop. Less is more when the writing quality is this cringe. The non-cringe is overly explained flavor that gets boring fast.Note: I absolutely love CrossCode. I think this game was going for that kind of banter but unfortunately fell short.The plot is basically your dad leaves to do things and after SIX MONTHS you decide to do something about it.First, what? Secondly, this makes it seem like it's a big wide world. The world is actually incredibly, incredibly small. Spoilers, he's been just hanging out going around places.There is literally no reason he or his companion couldn't have come back or told someone to tell the main character what was going on. It's very, very stupid.The actual goal of the game is fine, if nothing special. Any potentially good moments are ruined by how trivial the threats are and how sloppy the combat feels.To summarize all this rambling, this game had potential but didn't live up to it. All the pieces are there, but they're assembled incorrectly. Tweaks here and there, dialogue changes, rebalancing of encounters, etc, would go a long way. This is asking more, but making dungeons actually dungeons would be also a good choice.I wouldn't personally recommend this game, even if it was free. I know that might sound harsh, but there's just too many little frustrating things, more than what I listed here, to think someone else would enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is fun, top-down adventure game that definitely scratches an itch for The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap. The game controls nicely, combat is fun and fluid, and there's plenty of content to get your money's worth.- Zelda-like- Excellent spritework- Fun puzzles- Good music- Exploration is not strictly* locked to areas in the main quest.- Getting all the achievements doesn't require 100%ing the game.* In general, the game will give you a couple areas that you can freely explore, with the rest being locked off behind items that the main story gives you (e.g. bow). The world gets bigger as you progress through the main story, without being unreasonably linear (e.g. Minish Cap) or overwhelmingly open-world (e.g. Breath of the Wild). There are a couple NPCs (or tiles) that block your path for arbitrary story reasons, but it's not  jarring.- The map is  lacking*.- Tile/sprite Z-ordering is pretty bad in some cases, with the player's sword clipping through decorations.- You're going to need to self-impose challenges if you want the combat to be difficult**.- Collecting all the upgrades is VERY difficult without a guide.- Not much replay value.* There are no dungeon maps, and the world map is only useful for showing which areas are connected.** You can carry 50 of each of the three categories of healing items (1/2 heart, 2 hearts, 5 hearts), which gives you  of healing on hand at any given moment (excluding the revive elixirs and defense potion). That's enough to fill your life bar at  nearly 19 times over. There is no delay, cooldown, or restrictions for using the healing items, and it really trivializes the boss fights.Absolutely worth playing through once, but I don't have a reason to want to play it again.If the developer comes out with a sequel with a better map and some more balanced difficulty, I would definitely buy it though!
