_childDocuments_.review: Do you like The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past?  Because that's what they've tried to recreate here.  If you enjoyed that, you'll enjoy this.  The level design and exploration is solid throughout the game.  Maps are dense with secrets.Is it as good as A Link to the Past?  No.  Sadly, the things it does differently are also why it is worse.  Firstly it adds a lot of sidequests, most of which have weak stories and weak rewards.  A couple are amusing, but they are not helped by...Secondly, the main character talks, a lot.  But you quickly wish she wouldn't.  She's lazy, apathetic, selfish, and snarky to everyone you meet.  She occasionally says something amusing but most of the time something eye rolling or annoying.Third, there's a dodge roll.  It has no cooldown, so it is slightly faster than walking.  This of course means you will dodge roll everywhere, all the time, the entire game.  It quickly grows tiring and then after a few hours you start questioning whether you really need to roll everywhere....until you get an upgrade to the dodge roll making it move even further, cementing it as the only way to travel.Fourth, they add a bunch of magic abilities and sub weapons, except most of them are useless because you either get them too late into the game to be of much use (every attack magic but lightning bolt) or it's annoying to constantly have to switch in and out which weapons you want equipped.  Also, the sword is usually better than everything, because....Fifth, instead of finding a couple new swords or armor through the game that are major game changing upgrades, you use blacksmithing to upgrade your sword and armors incrementally (as well as finding a few other armor upgrades which are always incremental).  And the small upgrades add up to make you really strong real quick.  There's honestly no difficulty to be found whatsoever in the game, you can simply run up to bosses and spam slash (which is fast and has a huge swing arc) to kill them in moments.  If you get hit, ignore it and keep slashing, then heal instantly with your endless pouch of healing items.  Bosses do not require you to use the "Big Item" you just found in that dungeon, and bosses rarely have any actual mechanics outside "slash until dead."  Remember when you had to use the hammer to break the boss's armor before you could slash it?  Or use the hook shot to pull pieces of the boss off?  There's none of that here.But even with the drawbacks, the game as a whole is enjoyable enough.  A 7/10 Zelda clone, short and sweet for a low price.

_childDocuments_.review: Story / Setting / catching the feel of a 2D Zelda game - 8.5 / 10Moving around the world - 4 / 10Accessibility / Controller Implementation - 3 / 10As much as i want to love this game, and there is a lot to like, the control scheme and movement/interaction bugs are just not polished enough to not be distracting. A little jank is to be expected from an indie title, but getting stuck in a walking NPC's movement animation repeatedly, falling off random ledges, environmental interactions requiring you to be in a super specific area to work, and not optimising for controller inputs is what made me stop wanting to continue playing. I would love to be able to change this review to a positive one, and if at least a few of these bugs are addressed i will absolutely finish the game and update my review. but as of not the lack of polish when it comes to game feel overshadows what is otherwise a very cool homage to one of my favourite game genres.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I can tell there seems to be a fun game in here, and I love the Zelda inspired aesthetic. But this is a game that needs polishing. Like, a lot of polishing. The game is translated into a lot of different languages, which is great, but when the options menu consists of languages and nothing else...well that isn't much of an options menu. When a game has pixel art style graphics, things like being able to play the game in windowed mode or having some way to control how those pixels scale to the screen is kinda important. Otherwise it will look REALLY bad on some monitors. This is especially important if there is any amount of reading in the game, which there is. On the positive note, the dialogue seems quite well written and enjoyable. I would very much enjoy reading it if the text didn't make me feel like my eyes are burning. The lines making up letters should not vary wildly in thickness. At the very least, they should be consistent between different instances of the same letter! There are also some other things that make it hard to read like dangling sentences. Again, it's great that there are so many languages, but if it isn't comfortable to read in those languages then it seems kinda pointless. It would be better to have a good reading experience in a few languages than a bad reading experience in a lot of languages. Some of the sounds are very sharp and irritating and loud. there is an option to turn down the sounds, but that also includes all of the other very faint sounds. if they're all attached to the same slider, then they should all be about the same volume.The controls feel very odd and clunky, especially if you want to use a keyboard. The keys can be rebound which is nice, but it shouldn't be a necessity.All around the game just plain feels bad to play, which is a shame because some of the mechanics seem interesting and the story seems well written. I want to like it but it just FEELS bad to actually play and there is no getting around that.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, really captures that GBA Zelda feel while having unique characters and story. I have to say, I would really love to have seen an area map in addition to the world map. Navigating can be daunting, and between only in-game signposts and a very VERY zoomed-out world map finding my way back and forth between areas leads to a lot of frustration. Given that fast travel is limited to certain areas and there being so many hidden spots & minibosses to discover, an area map (or a map-marking/notating system) would have improved my game experience. Genuinely, this game is much longer and more involved than I expected it to be, so there's lots to discover and it'll provide even voracious gamers with entertainment. Tilia's snarky responses to NPC dialogue are a highlight for me for sure. It really gives her some pep and personality and makes reading conversations engaging. I don't think I'm anywhere near done 11 hours into this playthrough.TLDR Apart from a short QOL wishlist, a fun and engaging game with a delightful protagonist!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This is one of the case where you would give a neutral review but since Steam doesn't have this option ... well I think I'm inclined to give it a positive one.WARNING: Review may contain spoilers.There are still a few minor bug in game. The most noticeable one is that if you're using a controller, when the credit is displaying, you're actually still "playing" the game, so there's a good chance that you might mistakenly save or do anything drastic since you can't see anything (they are covered by the credit).  I triggered the save by mistake to my final save file is more or less ruined... (but luckily I got everything before it).Other issues:- The controller wasn't configure correctly. You will definitely need to start the game and reconfigure it, or otherwise a lot of missing button and things were quite weird (like pressing RB/R2 to Pause).- I'm not sure if this is isolated to controller only, but if you pick up something that will trigger a dialog box or talking to someone, there's a good chance that once it's done your character will be running toward the last direction that she's moving to. This has caused a bit of issue by the character jumping into water, running into hazard etc.- And of course, I only know about this after reading in Steam community - the game way of keeping track of updates is more or less ineffective and broken... I end up way overpowered.Now, on to my opinion - I do feel that the game is a bit easy in term of actual game play, but the random falling into places when you're close to it is absurd. There are places where you may need to be almost pixel perfect to prevent falling. To make it worse - there are places where if you fall you get health deducted - but also places where you need to fall into it to go to a new area.Similar inconsistency happen on the object that you can push. There are some that you can push once, but some that you can push as many times. There's no indication. You need to fail to test it.I do like how the game deal with dying though, making casual play possible and not frustrating.Overall, still not a bad game. At the very least, developer care enough to remove the only missable (and pointless) achievement in game.

_childDocuments_.review: When looking at Ocean's Heart (OH), I thought it might make for a decent Zelda (ZA) style game. The main reason I thought this was because the trailer shows an inventory including items such as a bow and arrow, boomerang, and bombs, while the protagonist rolled around like Link. With the overworld map showing a large area to explore, I was rather interested in how it'd play out. Plus, who doesn't want to go to a dog's birthday party?I wasn't exaggerating when I said that OH is similar to ZA games, as it replicates many aspects of those titles, sometimes a little too closely. There's nothing wrong in making a dungeon-crawler game, where the protagonist completes quests and gains items to open up previously blocked off areas. Frankly, that's a rough description of many adventure games. However, there are quite a few examples of things being carbon copies of something from a ZA title. There's blue and red switches that raise and lower barriers, the leever enemy from the first ZA game, your boomerang stuns enemies, etc. I'm not the most knowledgeable about those titles, but even these were quite obvious to me. Assuming I'm not missing the reference, there are unique elements in OH, but it loses distinction by borrowing so heavily from another series. It's possible to control the game with either a keyboard or controller, and I went for the controller myself. One issue I had with the controls was movement, as it sometimes felt touchy or unresponsive. I found the 'D-pad' the more responsive choice, but it still could have handled better. You can assign tools or items to two of the face buttons, which is a handy shortcut, instead of constantly having to find a specific tool from your inventory.You play as Tilia, who lives with her father and older sister in the local tavern. It's a simple, peaceful life, until a band of pirates raid the nearby temple, causing havoc with explosives, and kidnapping one of the locals. With her father being a volunteer navyman, he's the only person in the area that'll pursue this matter, so he sets out to get more information and rescue Hazel.Several months pass, and as Tilia sets out, she finds that her father helped people along the way and was fairly competent in his quest. In games like this, that seems to be an exception rather than the rule. Another thing I appreciate, is that the pirates do research and are knowledgeable in their lawless endeavors, with many of the game's NPCs being pretty astute. There's a few boneheads, but it's balanced out with smarter individuals.The game makes use of pixels, and does a good job with them. Although the ground and walls are made up of repeating tiles, there's enough detail and variance to them that they don't look flat or like effortless copy/pasting took place. Some areas could have benefited from more background objects to change up the visuals, but that's about the worst of it. Looking more on the positive side, many areas are quite bright and vivid. Plus, many items have enough detail and polish to look smooth and clear.I didn't find a soundtrack for OH, and though different songs play depending on your location, none of them stood out as particularly noteworthy. So, as I listened to some of the tracks, they tended to meld together for me. I'd say this is due in part to how the music is based around fairly standard tempos and instrumentation. It makes decent use of guitars and has some vibes that touch on the idea of a sea-faring adventure, but none had a lasting impact on me. Similarly, the sound effects are appropriate and fit the game well, with no irritating noises that got on my nerves.🌟 Combat isn't that advanced, but enemies are legitimate threats in OH. I died quite a bit early on, and learned to look at enemies as something to treat with proper attention and effort. Personally, I enjoy that there's some challenge from basic enemies.🌟 The quest log will update as you complete portions of it, giving you a general sense of what you need to do next. I wasn't always sure where a location it referenced was though, but I've never excelled at navigation anyways.❌ Treasure and secret items are sometimes unrewarding. There's so many armor upgrades that they feel insignificant. Even after getting several of them, the weakest enemies still do minor damage. Several chests contain scant amounts of money, even later on, which comes across as stingy. I'd rather see less chests, with more meaningful rewards.❌ Many dungeons and areas that seem like they'd have more to do wind up being small in scale, with only a couple of rooms and enemies to deal with. It's fine to have a couple of short areas to clear, but I think OH would benefit from an increase in the size of dungeons. This otherwise makes the game itself seem smaller.❌ Most boss fights don't require a strategy to be defeated. With how many healing items you get, it's quite easy to spam attacks, tanking a few hits that get through, and coming out on top, while not even dodging out of the way.🔍 Plants scattered around areas won't respawn simply from you leaving the area and walking right back. However, all of them eventually spawn again, though I'm not sure at what point. It could be as simple as moving enough screens away. Either way, it'll always be possible to gather more healing items. With the weakest berries being the most plentiful, I'd use them the most frequently.🔍 OH reveals early on that you'll get the bow by the blacksmith saying he's able to upgrade either your sword or bow. However, you don't acquire it for quite a while, so don't hesitate to upgrade the sword several times, as it'll make combat much easier.🔍 Be stingy with bombs. Throughout many parts of the game, I was pretty low on stock, and only able to buy more in the late game.I find myself in a strange place with OH, because I enjoyed the gameplay, in spite of occasional issues controlling the character. That's usually going to spoil my mood completely, but it wasn't too obnoxious here. If anything, it's probably the writing that helps immerse me into the game. However, as I consider all the issues, particularly with how disappointed I was by the small dungeons, I don't think I can recommend it. Although making a Zelda-like game as a first entry into game development is ambitious and it plays well, it was also unwise to borrow so much from that inspiration. The reason being it sets itself up to be compared directly against steep competition, and it simply doesn't fill the shoes of one of Nintendo's giants. It's worth playing if you're able to separate it from where the ideas came from, yet I find myself unable to do so and not feeling a bit let down. For that reason I lean towards the negative, but think others might enjoy it more than myself.

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying the Game until I got to the Cemetery of Waves Dungeon and found a Severe Bug. You can use the Key to skip getting a Major Item you need. The Warpbolt Arrows and go straight to the Boss. If you use the key and defeat the boss you lock yourself out of the rest of the content because you need those Arrows to traverse the rest of Game. If you're going to make Dungeons with Important Items that can be overlooked, please add multiple saves so no one has to restart the game from scratch or allow the bosses upon death to unlock every door as a fail safe. _childDocuments_.review: This action RPG game has a lot of charm!So far I'm really enjoying the setting and this looks like a zelda-like adventure game with RPG elements, which is a very tantalizing combination. The pixel graphics and animation are superbly done and brings a lot of life to the game.Sound design is pretty good and haven't found anything that would make me think otherwise.My main gripe with this game is actually how the controls are implemented, especially the controls for gamepads. The controller I'm using is a DualShock 4 V2, and the game seems to have Steam Input support so it doesn't require any workarounds.However, I cannot understand why the button mappings were done in the way they are and also why the menus navigation was done in such a convoluted manner.  This is an issue for mouse and keyboard and gamepad..First of all, to open the menus you need to press L1 (traditional Start or Select would have been way more intuitive) and the only way you can navigate between the different menus is using the d-pad or the left stick. This makes it pretty annoying when you are on the Inventory page, because you have to first cross all the item slots to get to the next page. There doesn't seem to be any input to immediately cross from one page to the next, for instance using L2 or R2. Other than the control scheme that feels a bit off regarding the menuing, this game is looking quite good for a decent price!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a 6.5/10 for me, it had a lot going for it cool art style, interesting setting, and a Zelda looking gameplay. This is the only thing it has going for it, so if you want it buy it on sale.The combat is simple, too simple. I found it far more useful to use the sword for everything, the sword can attack and bounce back projectiles making the shield ability worthless. So I would just spam attack the enemy until death, in fact I face tanked the final boss.Items are a bore, and most were optional I finished the game without finding them all. Bombs are rare at the start so if you mess up you can miss a few optional items which is not bad but hard to remember where they are all at. At the end I was swimming in bombs with nothing to use it on. The bombs also have a very very long time to explode, so long they are useless in battle. Then there's the spear, I don't know why they added a spear when you have the sword, the reach is pointless as it barely adds range to your attacks.I feel like this game with a little polish could be so much better, and I hope they release a better game next time.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression of this game was "I've played this before". On its surface it's a bog-standard Link to the Past formula with many of the same types of graphics, but it was on sale and I figured I needed something relaxing. What I found out very quickly, and the reason it's kept me so engrossed, was that no, I haven't played this before, or anything like it, and it's been a humbling reminder that there's more to a game's value than having the next big gameplay innovation.Despite being relatively conservative about changing the 2D zelda formula, this game is really proud to have its own identity and originality, and takes every opportunity to show them off. And the identity it has is witty, charming, funny, and above all it just has this... quality to it that makes you feel the excitement and pride of the creator with every lovingly detailed, regional-specific grass sprite. I feel like this is a game my friend made. Not even a specific friend, just... that type of feeling. I also expected to bounce off the story but the infectious charm and skillful distribution of information/worldbuilding have me genuinely invested, though I'm sure that's much more subjective. It has its limitations, and frankly the majority of the problems feel like a consequence of lack of game design experience, which I find pretty forgivable because nobody's born knowing how to mathematically balance difficulty, perfectly place overworld terrain sprites, or account for every possible way a player could accidentally sequence-break quest triggers. Some of the more egregious issues are the abysmal default keyboard controls (personally I had to remap every single button before I could even start playing the game) and the clumsily designed and rather unhelpful inventory UI. Despite this, I feel like it does a very good job of keeping the player focused on its strengths while working around its weaknesses. You're likely to know just from looking at it whether you would enjoy this type of game or not, and I'm here to tell you that if you're looking for a low-intensity adventure rpg to really sink some hours into and get comfy with, this game is well worth your time and money. In a competitive landscape of indie games trying to come up with the next big gimmick, Ocean's Heart is a fresh breeze that brings you back down to earth and reminds you exactly why the simple things are so beloved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a top-down adventure like 'A Link to the Past' but is focused on side-quests and exploration.  The world is large and full of secret areas, and most of the story is a patch-work of small quests, with the main story being quite simple and short.  If you need demanding combat or like a linear story where the main quest takes up most of the action, this may not be for you.  I deeply enjoyed exploring, reading the dialogues, and searching for the hidden secrets.  Since I don't care much about boss fights or combat that wasn't an issue for me.  The fights are very easy.  There is an in-game method of making battles harder but even with this the fights were not tough.  Easy enough for a 9 year old and up I would say.  The controls don't handle as well as a mainstream game, but it didn't generally matter too much.  The side stories, towns, characters, and the beautiful environments made this the type of game I enjoy.  About 15 hours to complete most of the achievements but I do wander around more than most players so the game play is probably more like 8-10 for non-completionists.  Well worth the sale price I paid, around 11$ iirc.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is a great action adventure, and maybe not necessarily a must-play, but a clear recommendation, particulalry for fans of 2D-Zeldas and Blossom Tales. And since it has been developed by (almost) just a single person, it is a marvel. Give it a shot!+Interesting story that diverges from the formula of poor boy, who sets out to save the world, in its own way+Cool art style with distinct enemies and locations, that scratch your explorer's itch+Very, very (and I mean veeeeery!) cool soundtrack+The game makes it easy to keep track on main and side quests-stiff controls; you can feel that this game is meant to be played with a keyboard or on switch-there were two events I couldn't trigger; and I don't know why until now. Maybe there is more buggy stuff that I didn't come across-Items and mechanics are very zelda; which isn't inherently a bad thing. But don't expect something innovative and new; this game is a Zelda clone in its core. And if you can't deal with that, you better not touch this gameOverall:6/10 for gamers in general 8/10 for Zelda fans

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. As a fan of the older top down Zeldas, this one pays homage to a lot of it's trademarks while breathing new life to the mechanics. Controls on controller feel nice (although you'll probably have to rebind a couple to your liking), the sword hits feel satisfying, and its not too easy - you have no shield, enemies don't drop hearts, and you'll have to find food and buy upgrades to stay alive as the game gets harder. It has a nice progression and pacing for areas and monsters, and after 7 hours I still enjoy the combat. Engaging, some projectiles, but not too sweaty. Quests are fun and cheeky. Some have complained about the map but I like it, the main paths are clearly marked, and you can fast travel to major towns and not just arbitrary landmarks (I feel too much fast travel cheapens the immersion of adventure and feeling like you're out on your own). Also, YES the context button controls interactions, talking and rolling, just like in Ocarina of Time. It is clearly the influence of that mechanic. If you don't like falling into the water, try using the D Pad, not the joystick which would have caused the same problems in any other top down game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid zelda-like with a light-hearted tone.  It's not at the lofty heights of Tunic or LttP, but as a one-man effort, it's pretty decent.  The combat is a bit old-skool for my tastes, but the game is extremely forgiving, so it never feels frustrating.  On default difficulty, it's actually too easy, but the developer put in a permanent hard-mode change, if you're feeling daring (you have to go to a temple and ring a bell -- it's not a simple slider in a menu).On the plus side, it's got a bunch of items, a large number of side quests (so many!) and optional dungeons, it's very low frustration and it's the perfect length (not too short, not too long).   The downsides are it's a bit too easy, the dungeons certainly aren't LttP calibre (they're OK, just not that clever),  the controls are bit clunky, and your character has seems to have banana peels on her feet, so she is constantly falling off of ledges.  The last part is a little absurd, but it's hard to be too upset since the game is so forgiving.One thing worth mentioning: the game doesn't seem to ever point out that you can actually jump small gaps, even though there's no jump button (she jumps automatically).  At only about 40% of the way through the game it becomes necessary in order to progress, so I stumbled around like an idiot for a half hour trying to find the path before I accidentally jumped a small gap and realized it was possible.  I'm not sure who's at fault here -- me or the dev, but an audible groan was heard coming from the direction of my couch.Also, the sword is inexplicably mapped to the right most button on the controller face.  you should swap it to the left button (i.e., the square button if you have a ps5 controller) if you're American,  or it will feel weird.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with the positives:The art and music's great, I liked the personality of the main character, and the world was reasonably fun to explore the first time.Now for the negatives:As others have complained about, having the interact button and the dodge roll button on the same key leads to a LOT of irritation when you try to talk to someone and just jump off into the water. In general the movement is a bit clunky, the dodge roll seems to be the fastest way to move around but it doesn't feel great to use as a movement ability. You have a weird hop to go over gaps but it really isn't consistent whether you make it or not.The game also has a pretty horrid fast travel system, you can only go to specific ports from other ports, and due to the way they're spaced out, you end up doing a LOT of backtracking on foot to complete sidequests.The powerups in this game are a bit uninspired, a grand total of 1 of them makes your normal movement any faster, and there's a distinct lack of the common trope of "let's leave things in older areas for you to explore later with new powerups". If a powerup affects the world, you'll probably use it in the current dungeon and maybe for 1 secret, then you'll forget you have it. Most of the combat powerups are completely outclassed by basic bow and sword gameplay too, so you collect these things just to not use them. Also, damage boosting is so effective in this game that a lot of obstacles and enemies can be defeated by just pausing to heal every once in a while.EDIT: I was watching a speedrun of this game just to see what I missed, and I found out that I accidentally skipped the first spell you get in the game. Not only was I still able to cheese the one time it was required to use that spell, that meant I literally did not use my magic meter for 80% of the game. I genuinely thought there was something up with the game, why is there a prominent UI magic meter with no way to use it for almost the entire game.The UI is also a mess in this game, I find myself going back to the menu a lot to heal or swap equipment, or check the map, or check quests, and navigating across all of them is slow and clunky. That's not even including the fact that the true options menu can't be accessed from the title screen, and uses weird left/right controls instead of proper submenus. Windowed mode in this game has no scaling as well, so if you have a high res monitor, your options are fullscreen or a tiny window.This game is very much trying to emulate zelda, a LOT of the enemies and weapons in this game emulate zelda games, and while it's not completely to the game's detriment, it's kind of obvious as well. The most blatant example are the little plant enemies which look directly taken from deku saplings.I didn't love the plot of the game either, even if the mc makes snarky remarks about it, the fact that the entire series of events is caused by someone just not sending a letter home is baffling to me. The pacing is also super off, I feel like the game takes it real slow in the start, then speeds up massively and suddenly towards the ending. Combine with that the fact that the vast majority of the content is tied up in sidequests (which involve a lot of backtracking across the entire map), and you end up with a game that doesn't feel super complete unless you actively go the extra mile and try to achievement hunt, which then means you're running around the map with bad fast travel for hours.This all culminated in the negative experience that made me put the game down. After I beat the game I went back to try and do some achievements because I somehow had only gotten 3 in my entire playthrough (I did a bunch of sidequests, but apparently not the RIGHT sidequests). I spent 3 hours backtracking and getting a fair chunk of the sidequests done, when suddenly my game crashed and I lost everything after I beat the game.Just thinking about having to go back in and run around the map for another few hours to get everything done again killed any motivation I had to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Calling Ocean’s Heart “Zelda inspired” feels like a gross understatement considering how much the game takes from the Zelda formula, specifically Wind Waker and Minish Cap. While some people would call the game a blatant rip-off of a beloved franchise, I think there’s more to it than that. Mimicking what makes an established franchise great is a relatively simple thing to do, and something that many indie games try. What very few manage to capture however is the feel and design of the original series, that punch that separates knock-offs from the originals. In that sense, Ocean’s Heart doesn’t just mimic a Zelda game, but it  a Zelda game. Its pacing, mechanics, and world are all top-notch and there are a few points where the game’s creator even manages to beat Nintendo at their own game. I want to give special attention to the way the game’s world is laid out and how secrets are both cleverly-placed and almost always worth your while to find. I spent most of my time in Ocean’s Heart completely ignoring the main story and just getting lost in the world the game has to offer, which is really a sign of how well it was able to draw me in. This isn’t to say that the game is perfect. It’s not. There are a few puzzles that can trap players if they aren’t careful, some pretty major pacing problems, some cryptic puzzles tied to the main quests, and a lot of odd “platforming” sections past the midpoint that just don’t work with the game’s controls. The game’s difficulty has some bizarre scaling where you should prepare to die a lot at the start and then never worry about running low on health again past the first dungeon. I think it’s also a shame that there aren’t options for windowed mode, or better ways to scale pixels to your specific liking. I was going to play the game in full-screen anyway, so it’s not an applicable complaint to me, but I’d feel dishonest if I didn’t mention it in the review since I understand that kind of flexibility can be a make-or-break deal for some players. I would highly recommend Ocean’s Heart, but with the understanding of what you’re getting yourself into. I think it’s a well-designed, if slightly unpolished, game that offers a lot to fans of classic Zelda. Far as I’m concerned, Ocean’s Heart gets enough right that it might as well be a Zelda game to me, and I think that should really say it all. Buy at full price or on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is from your classic Zelda-like games genre, it's an action adventure with tons of exploration where finding items and solving some minor puzzles involving moving or bringing objects and helping people paves your progress and makes your journey easier, the main difference I'd say is it has a simplified alchemy system for buffs and aids that reminds me of Gothic if it was a 32-bit game. You play as Tilia a young girl with a talent for fighting and a dream of joining the Navy who is in search of her missing father which runs a bar, but is also in the Navy, who disappeared in search of a mysterious band of pirates who suddenly attacked their village and kidnapped Tilia's best friend an adventurer herself, Tilia then embarks on a journey around the island in search of clues from them and meanwhile helping people with their problems sometimes resulting in rewards that either help or upgrade her capacities be it health, offense or defense. Speaking about upgrades although the game has RPG in it's name it doesn't deal with experience points, but it does put numbers in how much offense or defense you have, much like Zelda in general it requires you to explore and find the power ups or upgrades to make things easier against monsters, hostiles or the occasional traps.The plot is ok, pretty basic like most Zelda-like games and it does try to escalate it's importance with time, it's a bit dry by itself, but the side stories and world building help carry it on, it feels like you're unveling the world more than the main plot. The classic trope of ''my dad is gone I/he need(s) me/him'' is quite old and can be tiresome at times, but that's more a matter of personal taste, it's not too dramatic and Tilia's personality is quite charming and strong with the occasional jokey moments that help you get accostumed to it. I like how her character is no Poindexter, she makes it clear that she isn't a scholar, she likes fighting, action and survival, it's just not in her personality and the story adapts to that. She does show good investigative skills though. Other characters carry themselves well too, you can get quite curious and a bit involved in some side quests because of that, it's mini well written stories inside a big one that's cool, but not as great, but it hangs itself well. The occasional jokes are good for a few chuckles and laughters, nothing too goofy, but clearly has that good cartoon vibe with a bit of seriousness for a slight balance.The design of the game is very detailed and there's variation in accordance to it's setting, there's a lot of colors and beautiful background that immerses the player sometimes. The soundtrack is good and sometimes great, it fits well for each area and adds to the wonder, it has ''adventure'' written all over it. The gameplay is a matter of taste if you like Zelda games or not, I can't say it equals the source, but it is definitely a good love letter and you can feel it with the items usefulness, similarities and movement.My main criticisms with the game are mainly three minor things that don't affect the overall experience overall: the alchemy system, the lack of a radar or treasure map to find collectibles and the sudden ending. The sudden ending is self-explanatory sometimes your pacing is good then ''bam'' the end, and you have that feeling of ''more'' that doesn't match. The alchemy system although a welcome addition doesn't feel like it does much, it's just there to look cool, but ultimately can be easily ignored, it feels like it was just a check list the devs added up, but again it's not harming anybody, it just feels out of nowhere. Finally the radar/treasure map problem, finding upgrades and power ups is easy if you have a good memory for this stuff, but when you reach end game you meet that familiar painful experience most completionists often have where you're missing a few and you scoured the entire land only to realize it was hidden in that pocket dimension inside the wall you visited so often, or your alter ego made you forget of that weird place you visited before, or hidden behind an unique action in the game. All of this tragedy could've been avoided if we had a magic stone, treasure map or Dragon Ball Radar to give us a hint that it was in that area or just straight up shows us the exact location of it, you can even put a high price for the stuff, by then people are already rich by selling the excessive ingredients you collect to make alchemy stuff, 5000 Gold is a fair price in my opinion, just saying. But like I said it's not the end of the world just because of those three things.In short, if you love Zelda-like games you'll love Ocean's Heart, it's a great game, also the game reminds me of Alundra 1 for some reason, probably the main character's blue outfit with some leather and blonde hair which is similar plus some items similarities, but at least I didn't developed PTSD trying to get all collectibles with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: A Zelda-like which accomplishes what it purports to be: a Zelda-like.It's set on an ocean, but you don't actually sail anywhere through gameplay, with sailing functioning more as a fast-travel system between ports. There are some hidden islands, though not many (as far as I found, at least). There are a lot of dungeons, most quite short, to bulk up the experience. I played with a gamepad and the controls were sticky particularly when hitting a dialogue/cutscene and (oddly) when rapidly using different weapons, the latter of which is common as this game is more combat-focused than Zelda. The combat can be kinda sloppy, though that's certainly manageable. The story isn't too bad for what it is, although it's not the most compelling or thought through (but if you're a Zelda fan, I'm sure a light story isn't much of a deterrent).All that said, the dungeons are well designed labyrinths for exploration, never leaving you too lost but rarely giving away the path either. They're light on puzzles, but the satisfaction of untangling a knot is still there. While Ocean's Heart leads with combat and not puzzles, the nonlinearity of the dungeons helps pace things so they don't become unrelenting gauntlets. The side content also adds a lot of value, with health upgrades and magic spells scattered for explorers to find. A few of the extra dungeons are actually quite lengthy, with interesting (if not complicated) mechanics to vary the experience. The story may be lacking, but the theming of the overworld and dungeons is excellent, helping the world feel more real and distinctly maritime.Overall, it'll provide a few hours of core play, plus some compelling surprises if you explore every cranny. A good effort for a solo developer. Dive in. (Well, don't dive in, since you can't swim. But you know what I mean.)

_childDocuments_.review: So... it's not a bad game. I'd say it's a casual little action adventure with flaws. Like not all of the items have descriptions and the map doesn't list every locations (I don't like to use wikis unless I absolutely have to but hated not remembering some place). The dialogue is witty and puzzles challenging enough. I finished and got every achievement in about 25 hours, so decent length. A bit too easy for combat. Typical Zelda-like fashion, you start with a sword and eventually find a bow, spear, and some magic items. But you don't get experience from killing mobs, so there's not much point in fighting most things. You can avoid a lot of encounters by dashing away the next area. A lot of boss fights to get upgrades are optional, so you can seek out challenges if you want to max your weapons... but again, it's really not necessary... If you do end up fighting every encounter, you'll have a lot of random loot to sell and buy an absurd amount of health items. I think I only actually died once or twice by the end. And that's because I forgot to stop and restore my health. For the final few bosses I spammed the 80 or so explosive candles I had never used and won fairly quickly. There's not a difficulty slider to make things more challenging. No "easy mode" or "hardcore mode" from the start, but there is a Cursed Temple area where you can ring a bell to make enemies deal more damage. Problem is I didn't know about it until I accidentally found a page for the achievement for it online. I was more than half way though the story by then. I did force me to be more careful. The enemies do more damage then but they don't change their attack pattern or use different moves. There's not more of them with bigger agro radius or something... but that's me looking for a way to make the game challenging in one respect. You could handicap yourself if you wanted and never upgrade your sword or refuse to collect the optional weapons. Speaking of weapons... at one point you can upgrade your sword to some legendary blade relevant to the story... and it gives you a charge attack... that's it? I kind expected more from the build up of the quest.  At least could have made it visually interesting. Oh well. Nitpicking I suppose.And the story... is about a pirate who wants to control the seas with some ancient lost artifact. Is there some motive beyond this? Greed to raid every passing ship? Does he want to rule the world and build some empire? I couldn't really tell. Some more backstory could have helped develop things. The side quests actually are complex. They aren't just fetch an item or collect random things style. I did enjoy stumbling into a big distraction actually more than the main quest itself. None of the achievements are missable either. So that's nice. But yeah the best part is the funny dialogue and enjoying the characters. Even if the story and combat is meh... just take it for what it is. I still recommend the game if you're strictly looking for a fun casual game to pass the time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks promising, but I won't play past the first few minutes until some glaring control issues are fixed.  - The 'confirm' and 'cancel' buttons should absolutely not be bound to in-game action buttons such as attack and dodge. There's no reason why I shouldn't be able to bind my 'attack' button to the button that advanced the text, and my 'roll' button to the button that closes menus. - Multiple buttons should be able to be bound to the same action, and multiple actions should be able to be bound to the same button. There's no reason why the button to open the map shouldn't be able to also be the button that switches pages in the menu, for example, and there's no reason why I shouldn't be able to bind dodge to both 'A' and 'LB'. This would also be necessary if decoupling 'Confirm' with 'Roll'. Trust your players to be smart enough not to bind 'Attack' and 'Roll' to the same button, we can figure it out. - Binding a menu, ie Map, to an analogue control such as a trigger and holding it half way down causing a number of random things to happen, from opening the menu, to not doing that, to causing the menu to half open and be unusable, to crashing the game. For controls that don't utilize analogue features, a deadzone of 50-70% should be implemented (by default), and for movement a deadzone of 10-20% should be implemented by default, to prevent drift.This game strikes me as one that should be in early access, because I don't know how such issues managed to make it past QC. Beyond these faults, however, the game looks and sounds very charming, and I'd like to continue playing it in the future when it doesn't control so poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:- Serious game-pad/joystick control issues that bugged me entire 16~18 hours of game play (and many other players in the reviews), basically the player keep lose control of direction to move and fall into pits or water, or shoot arrow / attack to the backward direction- Poor player guidance in every single missions/quests where the player needs to find a thing- Bad UI navigation for game-pad, basically the same control issue as above, but this time the joystick keeps altering the left-right menu instead of up-down menu items (and it can't use the D-pad!!!)- Bad enemy placement that causes players occasionally to lose HP right after entering a room just because the enemy is literally right at the door- Unbalanced enemy attack pace that keeps the player getting hurt after invincible-recovery period (can be overcome by eating LOTS of foods to compensate)- The hold attack of primary weapon (obtained in a side quest) is completely useless- The "escape" level after the Blackbeard obtains the Ocean Heart wasn't delivered to the player, I realized that I was supposed to escape after using half of my inventory- Very limited use for joystick and keyboard, even though the player literally have 24 different weapons, spells, items and so much to use, so I had to:   1. Attack with Item 1   2. Go to inventory   3. Use Joystick to navigate to item 2   4. Select item 2   5. Use item 2   6. Go to inventory   7. Use Joystick to navigate to item 3   8. Select item 3   9. Use item 3   10. Repeat- Thunder effect flashes are harmful for player's eye health, please change it from #FFFFFF to #CCCCCC or #DDDDDDBugs:- All friendly/neutral NPCs walking on the street causes the player to get stuck if they "walk into" the player, this actually gets very annoying after you get stuck for hundreds of times- Player can spam most of the secondary weapons by mashing the primary weapon button right after attack with the secondary weapon- Player can get stuck in a conversation (not sure how it triggered) where all button stops working, and the only way is to close the game
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is a good "Zelda-like."I'm a big fan of the Zelda series and lately I've been wanting to play a new 2d Zelda game. Since Nintendo seems to prefer re-releasing 2d Zelda rather than making new ones, I've been looking for some independent games that attempt this formula. Ocean's Heart is a fun game that isn't too "meta" with it's story and characters. I'm just not a fan of the references that are present in games like Blossom Tales.Even though I'm enjoying the game, it has issues. The controller bindings seem to be bugged right now with no way to remap them from within the game. It also has a lack of settings to choose from, like resolution, framerate limits, v-sync, or more importantly, accessibility settings. While I personally don't require accessibility settings, I think all games should include some. Hopefully in the future the developer will implement some of these features.So yeah, I'd recommend it and I'm excited to see what Max works on in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game looked good in the trailers and screen shots I didn't feel the same actually playing. I am a massive Zelda fan and I see the comparison but for me what really put me off were the controls, tried with controller and it would not tell you which buttons to press so had to figure out myself. I just didn't feel anything playing this game. Such a shame as was expecting to enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I love playing Zelda like games. This looked like it would be fun to try and interesting, via the trailers and game play on twitch.But the controls are a weird unicorn configuration, and the game does not have a re keybinding on all game keys, nor a restore to default button that you can use. Good luck if you set the action/use key to something you don't want.In game they tell you very little what buttons to press, so u have to figure it out, or get to options and try to make it work.I was fighting the controls form the first moment I started playing.I will circle back to see if their are any updates that fix the keybinding.Was looking forward to playing this game when i saw it, shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: 10-14h 4/10 1 No Yes, "Katharin" wrote a very nice walkthrough and an achievement guide. On astats you can find extra tips for "Fleet Feet" and "Fragile Flower" 2 on Astats No No No No No No No difficulty option NoDid I already state that this is such a lovely game? It feels like a Zelda game and I enjoyed it a lot. You start this adventure in your own small town. Your father asks you to get something from the secret hiding spot for the cafe you run as a family. From the moment you reach that secret hiding spot, everything goes downhill.. Your small town gets attacked by pirates and they kidnap your best friend. Your father is part of the volunteer navy and takes of rescuing your best friend. But what do you do if your father and best friend still haven't returned after 6 months? You go on an amazing adventure trying to find them. Very soon you get a lot of freedom to explore the world. To reach some places you might need new items, but you'll find those during your journey. You also will find a lot of sidequests that are logged in a menu together with your main quests. Which keeps things organized. There is a very detailed walkthrough on the steam guide section, which you can use to help you find the way or give you a guideline, but without it, you'll be fine as well. It is amazing that from the day of release this guide was available for those who enjoy having a helping hand. This game has a few challenging achievements, but none are missable. At the release, the game had 1 missable achievement, but the developer felt that it was going against the spirit of the game to have that achievement and decided to delete it. Which is in my mind a very good choice. This way achievement hunters can just enjoy the game before have to focus on achievements. The few challenging ones are defeating the end boss with a curse that makes monsters a lot harder, you can do this after you've finished the game. Another is getting from point a to point b within a time limit and without using a fast travel system. And another one is getting from a different point a to point b without getting damage or using the fast travel system. All are very doable. I only needed like 3 tries for the timed one to know the way and get it done. The others I got on the first try.  Apart from those you have story-based achievements and achievements like getting all the different kinds of items, doing all the main and sidequests, stuff like that. I really did enjoy this game and it is very hard to imagine that one person was able to make such a lovely game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This game clearly draws a lot of inspiration from Zelda, and it does this WELL. It manages to keep that formulaic feel without being a direct clone - and the quest system, crafting mechanics, and equipment upgrading are unique enough that this feels like a proper tribute rather than a reskin.While there are some occasional typos, the dialogue is clean and builds the characters + world while keeping the story moving forward. The combat is your typical hack-and-slash, with new items unlocking new ways to lay waste to the monsters around you.The ending, admittedly, left a bit to be desired, but overall a fantastic game. And possibly the answer to that age-old question "What if Zelda was a girl?".
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of 2D Zelda games this is just such a gem. Not very long or very hard mind you, it could do with a "hero mode" or a NG+ of some kind. The world is dense, lots to explore, lots of quests and a fair amount of metroidvania style backtracking after unlocking abilities. It took me a little under 10 hours to do every quest and get every major item and upgrade without a guide.Overall a very enjoyable experience 8/10 <3
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Decent Zelda-like, if you enjoy Zelda games you will probably enjoy this.  That being said as others have noted the game is a bit rough and it can get annoying semi-regularly.  Few specific annoyances that regularly occur: getting blocked by NPC while walking in town, jumping off a cliff when trying to walk on narrow path, and puzzles having poor timing so if you missed a window you sit there twiddling your thumbs for far longer than you should have to.  Overall though I had fun playing it, cute world to explore, couple quests are pretty funny, optional content hidden just well enough that it's fun to search for without going crazy.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Good if you are looking for a Zelda-like game - decent story and okay mechanics. The reason I can't recommend this game is it seems to hate men. Less than an hour in the protagonist is yelling at a man in a library willing to teach her things just because he is a man and that is "man-splaining". No, it was an nice elderly man in a library willing to share his knowledge of a subject the protagonist knows nothing about. I'm all for empowerment of whatever gender you consider yourself but it should never be at the expense of another gender; that is what led to problems in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: So it is not an RPG. You don't earn XP or get better and better gear. You get stronger by finding stuff. It is more of an action-adventure with light puzzle elements. But the lack of guidance makes it weird. I played for 2 hours or a little bit more and I accidentally completed a couple of quests. How or why? I don't really know. My other problem is that it is very optimized for a small screen and D-pad. On bigger screens and with the keyboard it looks ugly and controls are weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Very good zelda clone. It has customizable difficulty by finding a hidden area where you can basically enable hard mode. Otherwise the game is very easy, since upon death you keep all items in your inventory (which also means you lose healh potions you used, which leads to me constantly suiciding rather than using health items as you get full health back that way). So that system is kinda flawed and exploitable but its much better than having to redo everything. Other reviews mention bugs but I have not encountered any. My main complaint is with the map. It's not very helpful for a sprawling metroidvania-esque game to only have the continents and major city names and that's your lot. If you vaguely remember a hidden door somewhere then you will have to search the entire area by hand cause the map is not gonna help you.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I am really amazed that this is done by a single dev. Other than the ending that seemed a bit rushed. The rest of the game is on high quality and highly completed down to tiny details. There's even a mock DLC in the game that extents the fun of exploring. For a completionist, this really is a fun and enjoyable game to 100%. Totally would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I had this as a positive review initially, but after finishing the game I unfortunately have to change this to a thumbs down. It's a beautiful game with good music and some fun dungeons, but it's ruined by combat that doesn't know how to be more difficult except by being unfair. There are no i-frames, so enemies that touch you will often hit you several times, and defense is so inconsequential that even after 14 upgrades I'm not convinced it even does anything. Enemies were still routinely taking out 3 full hearts in one hit. All of that would maybe have been manageable except for the fact that consumables stay used when you die and reload, so failure is harshly punished unless you quit without saving. If you spend all your health items and then die, well, they're gone for your next attempt as well. Better go grind them back, I guess. I also have to say that the game's description implies a much more involved story than what's actually there. The overall plot is fine. It's more than Zelda, but I won't remember it for long. The real issue is that I can't imagine anyone honestly describing the sidequests as particularly engaging, let alone "heartwrenching", and if you come to this game expecting that you're going to be sorely disappointed. It isn't the worst game I've ever played by any means, but I stopped enjoying it after about 4 hours because it had just become frustrating. Might be worth a look on sale if you really want a Minish Cap-style game and can deal with its shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic old school RPG. I tend to get frustrated with a lot of RPGs near the end and don't end up finishing them because they get too complicated or difficult, but I was able to finish this one! So it's a good game for casual gamers. I'd for sure buy a sequel or additional content for this game. I plan on going back in to try to find the side quests I missed and finish those too because it's a fun game overall, even though I've finished the main quest already. Super good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Hits most of the typical Zelda clone notes without being really janky or sloppy, and the protagonist having a personality and dialogue is a nice choice. Controls are odd, however-the game didn't seem designed with a controller in mind, and even bindings on a keyboard are a bit unusual. The game could also benefit from having 8-directional movement rather than 4.EDIT: 2/22/21- Controls are now mappable, and the player character can now move/roll in 8 directions, making for smoother exploration. Great changes!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: A charming love letter to classic top-down Zelda games. I really loved the old fashioned side fetch quests and general reward to exploration. This game wants you to delve into it, and the layout of the missions makes it easy to want to immerse yourself. My one big complaint is that the story telling and character lines are a little weak from time to time. It seems like some plot points were well fleshed out, and others were kind of left as floating chatroom-style thoughts. While I wouldn't say this game has replayability, if I could play it again for the first time, I would.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Oceans Heart is a fun Zelda like that feels a lot like playing a Link to the Past.It's not super long, but sometimes the game doesn't clearly tell you where you need to go leading to the old school method of wandering around aimlessly until something happens. although you don't need to go and gather every single item. A lot of them are optional and will significantly cut down your time in game.All in all, it's a fun throwback game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nice Zelda clone, with a lot of flat humor.Unfortunately it is way too easy, as soon you gained a few heal items and increased your health-bar to a certain point.. you can pause during fights and heal yourself up completely, and even if you forget it, there is an elexir that saves you from death... and if you die, there is no real pain.. it just sets you back to the areas entrance and you keep everything you had.That said, the world is very beautyful made and never feels generic, so I kept playing anyway.Pros: - Nice handcrafted world with quite some variation and a lot to explore - Funny NPCs and dialogs - A lot of items to find -  - Pirates!Cons: - The menues are awful - You can't remove buttons as soon you asigned them.. you only can change them - Too easy - the crafting system makes it even easier and is not necessary, because you can buy everything - the potential of this game is not fully used.. Overall I enjoyed playing it and would recommend this game to everyone who likes to play an ocean-themed Zelda in 2D without sailing yourself (that would be a nice add-on).Hope this review helps anyone! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Been having a lot of fun with this. Feels like an old school zelda game. The story is interesting enough, and getting more hearts, armor, and attack power doesn't seem to be that big of an issue.My only real complaint is the controls. _childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is a great little Zelda style action RPG! It's short and sweet, but packed with solid gameplay and fun little secrets to find. It's kind of sad less that less than 20% of users have beaten the final boss, given that you can see and do everything here in about 10 hours. This is a game that starts out as difficult as it's ever going to be, then gradually becomes easier as you upgrade your gear and character. If you are having a hard time, just power through the first hour or two, I promise it's worth it. I only really had two gripes with this one. Monster and boss design is pretty unremarkable, with 90% of enemies being completely forgettable, while the other 10% only stand out for being annoying. Exploration is this game's greatest strength and combat isn't outright bad, so mediocre enemies don't really hurt the experience all that much. What did pull me out more than a few times was the script, which tilts dangerously close to "millennial writing". The dialogue tries to keep to a lite, whimsical tone, but too many characters end up sounding like either twitter users or a male redditor imitating a teenage girl. That's harsh criticism, but honestly this isn't anywhere near as obnoxious as something like Borderlands 3 or Forspoken. It just wore me down a bit towards the end, as you have to talk to pretty much all the NPCs to find clues towards the game's secrets.Anyway, great game, absolute recommend, pick it up if you like Zelda and haven't played this one yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: It is overall a pretty nice zelda-like. Considering the game has pretty much been developped by 1-2 persons if my understanding is correct, this is mighty impressive! I enjoyed the overall experience.Very nice pixel art, music is not amazing but still pretty ok. Gameplay wise, nothing fancy, just the classic 2D zelda stuff that we like, albeit a little less smooth though.The world is pretty big, with lots of different areas.Dungeons are numerous but pretty small. Good amount of items to use, though some not as useful as others. Game is not too challenging, but you can ramp up the difficulty via a curse system, which is nice.This said, the game is obviously not exempt of little defaults here and there, and when you are accustomed to polished zelda game, those get noticed. Among others:-  The map could use reworking: you cannot zoom-in/out to check specific details/area, so this will not help that much to situate you precisely, only at a very macro level. No possibility to add pointers either, so all in all the map usefulness is reduced to the bare minimum. I don't know if this is an intentional dev choice to go for more exploration but considering there are a lot of points of interest and some backtracking involved, I would rather have had something more detailed. This is something we got accustomed to in current games.- Default button mapping is kind of weird. You can remap fortunately, but still the way the different actions are programmed/binded with a specific key are weird in my opinion, so navigating through menus and such felt a bit wonky at first and need time to get accustomed to.- I had issues controler wise: "joy-con drift like" issue despite my controler (xbox360) being fine. It seems to be a common problem, which is apparently due to the engine's controller API that is buggy, which kind of sucks. This obviously degraded the experience a little bit, but not to the point of not being able to play and enjoy the game nonetheless.Then again, keeping in mind that it is 1-2 person behind this game, not a big team, I will cut the dev some slack. And overall, the game remains very much enjoyable with a lot to explore.So if you like zelda-like games, you can definitely give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: So, it reminds me a lot of link to the past. Though, I feel like most of the items are for combat, and less for utility stuff. Also, even with all curses enabled (the games hard mode) it really isn't that challenging. about 75% completion, at time of post, and I've beaten the game. So... definitely a bit on the short side. Short and sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of Link to the Past, I really wanted to enjoy this game. A little more than an hour in, I find I am unable to.The first concern was when I initially launched the game. It recognized the controller I had plugged in, but I couldn't make a language selection. I had to Alt-F4 out of the game, unplug my controller, and re-launch just to get to the title screen.On said title screen, there are no options to adjust the VERY LOUD SOUNDS AND MUSIC. I game with headphones, and set most master volumes in the 50-75% range. After I started the game, I happily found that there were now options to lower the volume in game (why is this not at the title screen?). Even after dropping both Music and SE down to 10%, they were still louder than I found tolerable.The gameplay had some minor issues, but it isn't as intuitive as I hoped. Jumping at the first beach did not fill me with hope that this experience would improve for me as I progressed in the game.Regretfully, I would not recommend this to those looking for LotP nostalgia.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Snuggle deep with you childhood in the 90s with this brilliant gem.9/10 Zelda Tribute.And as quickly as so many N64 Zelda weekends, questing complete.  Well, mostly.You like old school Zelda?  Guaranteed love.  The thinly veiled versions of Zelda monsters manage both nostalgia AND laughter when you make the connection between each pair.The slow-paced acquisition of new abilities and thus areas can be frustrating, as a completionist will find themselves retracing outlands and temples they'd rather stick a flag in as done.  On that note, the only thing that feels missing is the dungeon map feature.  The World Map is sufficient for progressing through the plot, but having a reference of which areas to write down to revisit later in the form a map would be more satisfying.Easy to play, perfectly suited sound and graphics for the genre, reasonable puzzles, never overwhelming combat.  A few bugs here and there being locked in certain dungeon rooms (saving is on YOU, hombre) is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I already really enjoy this game- it's fun, easy going, and has enough content to stay interesting. The only thing I would ask for is an adjustment to keybinding. Movement is done by directionals, and I would like the preference to use WASD instead. Otherwise, I'm really enjoying playing this game and will most likely play to completion. If you like 2D zelda games, this is a great one to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This game's inspiration is obvious, but it has some fun twists of its own. You don't get "hearts" per se, and instead you get large numbers of items that heal half a heart or two hearts when used. This makes potions (mentioned below) a lot more important. You also get heart containers from going through small challenges, as opposed to the more common pieces of heart. You don't get one-time, story-based upgrades to your weapons or armor, instead finding a lot of small armor upgrades hidden around the world and buying weapon upgrades in exchange for a piece of coral and some money. There are several kinds of potions, but these require crafting and many ingredients are only found in specific places so that's its own challenge. This is pretty unique itself, but several puzzles and enemies are pretty fun as well. Both finding out how to defeat enemies and solve puzzles and actually doing that are somewhat of a challenge but not frustrating and are super fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game. Pretty pixelated graphics, fairly simple quests, reasonably achievable achievs, and absolutely hilarious dialogue. And it has a female protag! I played closer to 26 hrs (i have a pic showing 26.6 hrs at game close) but I think the time went down due to some funky save mechanics. Oh well, didn't affect my gameplay. The game is pretty casual, and while there is no option for a difficulty level up front, there is a place in-game where you can "curse" yourself to make it harder if you want. It's listed as playable on deck bc it sometimes show non-steamdeck controller icons (I never saw any, but I played the first half of the game on PC). I will say that while I had to rebind to play on PC, I was able to play on deck with no modifications. It ran beautifully on both platforms. I got this on sale as part of a bundle with potion permit, and I'm so glad I did bc it was exactly what I was looking for. Honestly, this is worth it even at full price. I've bought 15 dollar games with far less substance than this. I'd pay 15 for the dialogue alone lol
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Refunding this one sadly :( Two in one day, feelsbadmanWhile I really love what they were going for, it's less that I love the direction this game had and more that I love what they are obviously pulling from, A Link to the Past.The one biggest complaint I have for this game is all of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialogue. I played it for an hour and it felt like 90% of my playthrough was reading stupid and poorly written dialogue, who the ♥♥♥♥ plays top down Zelda for the dialogue? I understand that it's a new IP and doesn't have the pre-existing lore that Zelda does, but it is just tedious and annoying.This makes the second problem I have even more frustrating, too, because after you get out of the mountain of dialogue, you get into a poorly optimized, poorly designed and unfun game. The controls are mapped awfully, there are barely any settings, and this all adds up to what this game amounts to: A cash grab LTTP clone that pales in comparison.I'm no Zelda fan, too so me saying that should have a bit of weight. LTTP is cool, and BOTW is fun but I don't particularly like any of the other Zelda games in the series. This is a ripping off a game from forever ago without any real improvements. Somehow in the time between LTTP releasing and now, the dev team seems to have regressed in game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This feels a lot like a 2D Zelda, but Tilia actually talks! The game is not very challenging, sometimes annoying, but overall has a cozy vibe. I have mixed feelings but I lean more towards positive.Most of the game was enjoyable, but you should definitely use a controller to play if you can. Thankfully you can rebind the controls on keyboard to make it more bearable, but it seems to be made for controllers first and foremost.The graphics are cute and coherent, sometimes you can see some seams but it didn't bother me. I especially liked the little "KO" smoke cloud that appears after defeating a human enemy.The soundtrack is very nice, some of the tracks got stuck in my head after playing.The story isn't very deep. You set out to save Tillias dad and her friend Hazel, but it just so happens you save the world as well! Overall the writing is okay, sometimes funny. It serves its purpose.On your journey you will meet some more people who will help you out but there aren't any deep conversations or anything. There are quite a few side quests, a couple of them have more than one solution which is nice. However one of them made me want to quit and give up the game. The main draw to this game is the gameplay. If you have played all the 2D Zeldas and want more, this might be for you.Exploring the world is fun, you'll regularly stumble upon puzzles or areas that you'll have to backtrack to after you got the right equipment. However as far as I can see not all items are necessary.  The puzzles aren't difficult, if I ever struggled it was because I lacked something.At times the backtracking got on my nerves. The controls are a bit clunky and Tillia insisted on jumping into the water and drowning. The enemies on the way were annoying, there is no real challenge to most of them.Combat is simple, it's easy to figure out patterns for most enemies and bosses. There is a kind of "challenge mode" that will make the enemies hit harder but it doesn't change anything about their behaviour. Most of my deaths were caused by me mixing up the attack and dash buttons.There are plenty of heart upgrades around the world. You can easily upgrade your weapons with coral ore (I found more than I could use) and some money at the smithy. Upgrading your armour at the smithy will usually require an unique material, but a lot of armour upgrades can be found in chests. This system encourages the player to explore thoroughly which is nice. In the beginning I thought it was a bit expensive but then I realised I was finding so many items that I could easily sell them to get enough crowns.There are the types of items: healing items, crafting items and consumables. If you gather as you go you'll easily reach the cap for berries and apples, but as far as my experience goes only those and bread (which is also a healing item, it can be bought in various places) are capped. I didn't really engage with the crafting system and sold most ingredients. To me the game was easy enough without using any of the craftables (except for the speed potions for one achievement). I can't say anything bad about it, nor anything good. It's just there.Overall it can be a nice experience if you are looking for something casual. Clearly this game was made with a lot of passion and love for Zelda.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this cutesy, clever A Link to the Past-esque game (except with quests). The difficulty seems pretty balanced, it may be just a bit on the tough side for most gamers. But it's a fresh breeze, and If you like similar games, you'll enjoy this one because I've not seen any blatant faults. 8.75/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart delivers a solid adventure experience with a story that's decent—not too gripping but enough to keep players engaged. While the plot may not be groundbreaking, the game shines through its fun combat mechanics and well-designed quests, which keep things interesting and offer variety without overwhelming complexity. It’s a game that thrives on nostalgia, combining exploration and challenge in a way that's enjoyable and refreshingly straightforward.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, it is so nostalgic of Zelda, and the storyline is gripping. Even the sidequests make me curious, I was eager to find out what this and that random key is supposed to open. The art is absolutely beautiful, the gameplay is simple enough yet still challenging. You have a lot of freedom to explore all the areas, and talking to NPCs can bring you side quests. It's all the things I love about rpg rolled into one gorgeous game. You can clearly tell it was made with care and love. This game has personality, and I like it a lot. ***Edit: Now that I have completed the game, I experienced the same feeling I had when I finished Chrono Trigger for the first time... something tells me I will definitely come back to replay Ocean's Heart from scratch every once in a while ( ＾◡＾)っ♡ Thanks so much, Ocean's Heart developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10: This is an excellent top-down Zelda: Link to the Past-eque action RPG.This is a great game. I'm surprised it's not more popular. If you liked the top down Zelda games (Link to the Past, Minish Cap etc), Crosscode, Death's Door, Tunic, Hyper Light Drifter et al, you will love this game. This might be the best Zelda-like on Steam, definitely top 5 at least. Fun, engrossing, not particularly difficult but not boringly easy. Doesn't explain everything to you, rewards exploration and curiosity with lots of secrets and hidden paths/areas to discover, as well as beautiful world design. As with Metroidvanias and also other action RPGs of this style, you open up different parts of the world as you gain more skills and items. And it's not just a retread of existing games, it has its own unique character with great world-building and atmosphere. Even the combat is fun (there's a shield and a roll dodge), reminds me a little of Death's Door in that sense, not quite as precise and satisfying but still very good. This is a really enjoyable game. Download it!One note: I'm playing on an Xbox-style controller and I manually switched the attack and use item buttons (now X and B, respectively). The roll dodge/action button default is is A, which suits me. The controls are pretty intuitive but you may want to adjust them slightly to suit your preferences.
