_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding take on the Zeldalike genre, with a friendly and responsive developer who will quickly address any technical issues or questions you may have. If you're hear for a very combat-oriented ARPG, this probably isn't the one for you. But if story, exploration, atmosphere, and collection are more what you look for in this type of game, then I whole-heartedly recommend Ocean's Heart. While it can be rough around the edges at times, it more than makes up for it with its charm and character that Minish Cap fans will feel very at home with. Where Ocean's Heart goes above and beyond though is in it's gorgeous level-design. This is a world you'll want to explore every nook and cranny of, and there's certainly a lot of it to see. Also the soundtrack is an absolute banger. You should give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: It would be easy to note right upfront all the things about Ocean's Heart that left me wanting, but I think that it's telling that instead of going that route, I would much rather share how the game made me feel and respond. I laughed out loud at dialogue. I tried each and every weapon out and messed with it just to see how each on fared in different situations. I got small waves of nostalgia when I saw familiar Zelda LTtP tropes (like the bushes or similar room layouts). I did my best to talk to every NPC and search every nook and cranny and I STILL haven't found everything. I loved the graphical style, the sass of our protagonist, and the overall charm that reeks from every sprite. In short, I simply loved exploring and adventuring and in this regard, Ocean's Heart does exactly what it set out to do - make you want to go a'questing! I know it's not in the cards anytime soon if at all, but I absolutely would buy Ocean's Heart 2. Take my money!People have already noted the things that bug them. Combat can be wonky (you definitely want to be using a controller). Bosses are generally lackluster. You will get stun-locked a fair bit. It's generally a very easy game because healing is ample and the puzzles are standard fare for the most part. The money system takes a minute to get used to (you basically have to sell your spoils or find money in chests and after a certain point money becomes moot). Traveling from place to place can get tedious even with the fast travel system in place. Some of the weapons have questionable utility. Does any of this take away from the experience? Yes if you're looking for a challenge and top-notch battles, but frankly, much like Zelda, that's arguably not the point. The joy is in the exploring, in the gradual uncovering of secrets and new places to see. And for goodness sakes, you're battling PIRATES! How. Cool. Is. That?Ocean's Heart is a labor of love and a darn fine one at that. It's well worth the time it takes to romp through and while the replay value is moderate at best, I think there is enough humor and meat to warrant a rerun after the dust of a few months has settled. I look forward to that.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful, well-made Zelda-like! There's really nothing to complain about here. The game follows the pattern of classic Zelda games like A Link to the Past quite closely.The good:- Feels like a classic Zelda game- Female protagonist (though in the pixel graphic style, she looks pretty indistinguishable from Link).- Crafting is a nice addition (though not well utilized, see below).- Very nice overland map design, with a satisfying amount of optional extra stuff to discover.The bad:Nothing is actively bad about this game!But here are the things I'd love to see refined or more developed in a sequel:- Some of the items, notably the boomerang and the spear, are of limited use, and I basically spent the game so far (I'm guessing I'm 3/4 of the way through) with the magic shield always equipped and swapping the bow and bombs (and occasionally bomb arrows) in the other slot. I'd love to see more clever uses for the other items.- I get that this is love letter to Zelda, and I'm here for it. However, it would be great to see some divergence from the same old lineup of items that the original games established.- Sword swings provide a generous arc when it comes to fighting monsters, but only target the square in front of you when chopping down plants or breaking pots. I found lining myself up to cut a swath of plants needlessly fiddly and a bit annoying.- I'd love to see the dungeon designs get a bit more complex and puzzly. There's nothing at all wrong with the dungeons as they are, but they don't quite live up to the richness of the dungeons in Zelda games.- I get that this kind of game is treading well-worn ground, and so much of what goes on in the story can be boiled down to tropes. Even so, the sometimes jokey style of the dialog that tries to be cute about being aware of the tropes is disappointing. Lots of indie games go this route, choosing to aim the dialog at the player with a wink, but it almost never lands well. The jokes aren't funny, and they undermine any resonance and drama of the story. It's not a huge deal, but it's basically a signal that the story isn't important. I think the game would be better served by taking it's fictional content seriously. The best would be working to subvert the tropes in fun ways, but just engaging with them at face value seems better to me than treating them as a joke.- I would love to see the crafting be a more important part of play. I personally didn't find any of the craftable items particularly fun or useful. I could have played without them and not really missed anything. Perhaps if I turned on hard mode, the combat modifying potions would be more important? But still, it would be great if making them felt like more of an accomplishment.- This is a tough one. I am often frustrated by tough boss battles, so when I say that the bosses so far have been too easy, I'm not saying that the bosses should be tougher in a pure, mechanical sense. What makes the classic Zelda bosses fun is that there's always a trick to them. Rarely can you just get your sword out and beat them down. You usually have to use the item you just found in the dungeon to exploit their weaknesses. For me, even though that means I have to die and respawn a few times to figure it out, it's really satisfying to see it work. I'd love to see that here, for the hypothetical Ocean's Heart 2. It's not easy, but it's one of the few areas where this excellent game doesn't live up to its forebears.That's a lot of little niggling points. I don't want them to detract from the fact that this game is fantastic! It's only because I love it, that I'm so focused on the little things that would make it exceptionally great instead of just really great. If you like classic Zelda games, this is one to play for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good. Very much feels like an old school, SNES Zelda game which is definitely a good thing. Music is great and the world and each zone is awesome to look at. Two things that frustrated me were the controls around ledges (I fell into the water and wasted so many healing items from falling into water repeatedly than I did from being hit by enemies) and how if you leave a room with an enemy still alive, when you come back, 9/10 times that enemy is literally standing in the doorway ready to get a cheap hit in. For the price, easily worth it as long as you know what you are getting yourself into. This is one I can see myself going back to a bunch, just like I do with LTTP.

Hopefully those issues will get addressed in time, but even still, it's worth the price of admission.A recent patch has made controls rebindable as well as improve some of the game feel. _childDocuments_.review: I love the earlier Zelda games, from Zelda 1-4. I like the Secret of mana games. This should check all my boxes but it doesnt. The first 20mins or so was ok, but it went rapidly downhill. I didnt play very long, because I just got fed up with the game within an hour, bored out of my mind. While I tried pressing on a little longer, I just couldnt, the combat, the controls and finally the music made me just quit out. Perhaps the game gets a lot better after a certain time, but I feel there are better games that is fun from the beginning without having to trudge through an "intro" that is just... unfun.At the moment of writing this (20210411) I cannot recommend this game, it might get better with patches.Pros:* Looks kindof nice* Didnt crash* Controller support without any hassle* Rebindable buttons* Death not very punishing* Separate music and sound slidersCons:* Controls feels very floaty and inprecise - I was fighting the controls more than the monster, and whose idea was it to place "Action" and "Roll" on the same button? Walk up to a door, press action but not be in the precis place you need to be to open the door? Roll away, and hope there isnt a ledge to fall off.* Combat feels just... meh* I had lots of cheap deaths - new monster, instant death due to a projectile or something, or new monster not taking damage from my sword with almost instant death - floors falling away, coupled with inprecise controls makes it a slog of dying - restart - retry* The music. Oh the music. Its grating. Areas I visited had the same music loop repeating for what felt like every 30 seconds, and the music sounds the same between areas aswell. This was the straw that made me just quit out.

_childDocuments_.review: It was slow at first, but got better.  The ending got rushed and the final boss was easier than those bosses that guard the shining stone steeles.  At first it made me dizzy and the controls were really bad.  After re-configuring them the game was more playable.  The storyline was good.  The game did take stuff from Zelda, but what did you expect.  Zelda is the best top down 2d game ever.  It's only right to emlulate Zelda since Zelda is the gold standard.  Would like a mini map per area.  Difficult to find places such as the inns.  Also, need us not to collide with moving npc.  Get stuck all the time when npc slow walks on the stairs or in the port.Found a design error: close to the end on blackbeard ship: to the left of the map where there is a treasure chest, a teleport box, and a switch that opens a path to the bigger ship/castle.  The switch only has a gap on the southeast side with moving rafts.  At first when you jump the sinking raft to get to the chest.  On your way, you must teleport. _childDocuments_.review: The game has great potential. It aims for that old-school Zelda feel, and mostly hits the mark. However, it is lacking polish; It is very easy to get yourself stuck in an area and have to reload, the ground that falls away underneath you is a nightmare to navigate, animations aren't quite what they should be and constantly remind you that you're looking at a 2D image and not exploring an interesting world. Overall, it feels like it was released before it was ready. I really hope the developer does a couple updates down the line, but I'm not holding my breath. I wouldn't buy it at it's current price, wait for it to go under $10 and don't expect to put more than 10-15 hours into it. If it ever gets updated, I will update my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun little game. I beat it in about 10 hours and really enjoyed it. I've never played the earlier Zelda's and based on the other comments and me enjoying this, maybe I should! The combat does get kinda easy toward the end but I never tried using the mechanic that increases difficulty. Might be worth trying if you start feeling overpowered. Plenty of little side quests to do and even a quest log, which I've not often seen in 2D games. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Zelda-like that's clearly inspired by Wind Waker and the top down games like Minish Cap and A Link to the Past. It's got a good heart (pun intended) and does a good job evoking the feeling of exploration those games provide. It is however a level below actual Zelda games in terms of combat and level design. Honestly the boss fights in this game are a bit of a mess, and the difficulty starts dropping off from the mid-game onward. I still recommend, since the game has great writing and music, as well as a nice overworld, but set expectations accordingly. This is not the second coming of Ocarina of Time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game, great adventure, great side quests, great story, still some sprinkles of humor and references to older similar games. As a Zelda link to the past lover, I really am so happy I could play this game and recommand anyone who liked old view from above adventure game to play Ocean's Heart.

The controls are a bit frustrating at time as well as enemy placement but the dialogue and world are fun to explore. The mechanics are generally satisfying but I do wish they made a bigger deal of finding items or making the inventory screen easier to read. _childDocuments_.review: What a lovely homage to 16-bit Zelda! The movement felt familiar and comfortable, the items were fun and nostalgic while also playing on new riffs, and the worldbuilding was thorough and engrossing. The game might be a bit on the easy side for some, but there are in-game things you can do to bring some more challenge. Regardless, I did find by the end of the game I could pretty much face-tank any baddies or bosses (including the final boss) because of the ample amounts of healing items and very forgiving continue feature.Would recommend to anyone who wants to scratch that 16-bit Zelda-like itch!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how many times this comparison has been made, but if you need a game that feels like Zelda's A Link to the Past (sans the chicken), go for it. Easily enjoyable. Not a big fan of the lore dumps you get throughout the game though XD I skipped some texts as those get too long winded sometimes. But the neat part is that you have a quest log and you'll know where to head to next. Just... as long as you keep talking to people.Item-wise, love the variety that you get but honestly you could probably make do without some. There were a handful I kept on almost 90% of the time, and the others are highly situational. But I guess that's just me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It reminded me of a cross between Zelda, Morrowind, and Secret of Evermore. I really enjoyed that it didn't hold your hand too much and you had to explore around to find what you need and remember where you've been and what you saw. And there is really good incentives for exploring, so I felt motivated to do it.I also really enjoyed the dialogue and found it very humorous. There was one moment where I was surprised by a result that was indicated by a visual effect, and then when your character is asked about it, they basically lie, but you know the truth. Loved it.The one thing I would wish for is harder bosses. Like bosses you really have to expend your resources on. But I also didn't opt into enabling harder enemies, so maybe that is on me.Overall, this game has the fairly short but really solidly done feeling that I get from Link's Awakening.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute little Zelda game starring a girl who looks up to her adventurous father. Not too complex. Not too easy. Engaging, quippy story with a worldbuilding scattered around.The variety of weapons are essentially optional because your sword can power through everything, though. It even gets a charged attack later that I forgot about until this moment. Sometimes you need range or the flail or the barrier, but that's about it.This is a relaxing, turn-your-head-off kind of game that I was totally in the mood for.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: A very good 2D action RPG offering a well-designed world to explore, a nice story and many side quests. Most game mechanics are similar to Zelda games like A Link to the Past or Minish Cap, but Ocean's Heart brings its own humour and charm. Compared to early Zelda titles, Ocean's Heart is much easier, but the difficulty can be increased in-game via its curse mechanic.I cannot agree with all these negative comments regarding controls and fast travel. Controls are typical for such games, also they can be adjusted in the settings and controllers are also supported. The game does not lack fast travel, it is possible to travel between all the available ports via ship.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is similar to the old Zelda. I say similar as in how the game plays. Story:It follows Tilia searching for her father and friend after pirates attack. A pretty basic plot that smoothly flows along. This isn't constantly in your face, and goes onward when you reach the next point.Gameplay:Plays like an old Zelda game. You have the dungeons, and finding secret locations. And you can upgrade your equipment by finding a certain item to use at the blacksmith or out in the field. Depending on the situation, certain tools are naturally better. To add on, you can find and sell items. The money used is not only for purchasing items, but for certain trades.Maps:Each map is decently large, leaving a good amount of room for exploration. You can find spells, health up, etc.Side Quests:There are many of these, which allows you to unlock upgrades as well as other stuff. Plus, they bring more life to the game as well.Boss Battles:These are pretty basic, just something you'd similarly find in old Zelda games. You can relax, but also have fun.Overall:This is a simple but fun game. A good amount of mechanics, fun exploration, a decent story, etc. It is definitely far more lively than the older Zelda games. I'd recommend giving it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is a fun indie Zelda-like. Charming, funny, beautiful, and with a wonderful soundtrack. It's not terribly long, so you might want to wait for a sale, but it's got a good-sized world to explore with secrets and goodies hidden all over the place.My only real complaint is that it's extremely easy, since you can amass a very large collection of healing items without much trouble. There IS a hard mode you can activate pretty much immediately after the prologue is over, and it massively increases enemy damage, so if you also find the game really easy I'd recommend turning that on. Even without that, though, the game is still very fun and a solid entry into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very interesting Zelda-style game. There are a lot of secret items and areas in the game. It's a challenge to find them all.The final battle is easy, even in the hard mode (cursed). You just need to upgrade your bow and bomb to high level. I only used one burlyblade potion and twenty bomb arrows to kill Blackbeard.Cons:-In order to change default controls, player must start a new game and use in-game options.-As a member of Volunteer Navy, the heroine doesn't know how to swim! Unfortunately, there is no chance for player to learn swimming in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Such a work of love! Writing and dialogue is on point, quests take suitably wonky turns, references to 2D Zelda all over the place, the amount of detail in the environment, the way the world responds to outcome of events. As an improvement for the titles which it seems to draw it's inspirations from, the story makes perfect sense and involves characters interacting in meaningful ways (being upset at each other, talking about motivations and having changes of heart about stuff that's happening). The towns and villages feel alive and vibrant but not overwhelmingly so. Some UI/control mapping stuff feels a bit dated, but that's ok. Go play!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart features excellent interconnected world design where the overworld, dungeons and caves are woven together naturally. Secrets are fun to discover, though with how wealthy the player can get, and the excess of coral used to upgrade your weapons means that late-game not all secrets are rewarding.Combat is solid with multiple weapons and spells to choose from and combo together against a variety of enemies. I especially love the energy shield weapon that lets you essentially parry things.Ocean's Heart is one of the better 2D Zelda-likes I've played, and I recommend giving it a try! Be warned however that saving is only done manually or when exiting the game, so make sure to save often so that if the game crashes you won't lose hours of progress!
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: With a main character that doesn't like to waste time beating around the bush, Ocean's Heart is a well-done adventure with a cohesive storyline and interesting sidequests. It never feels like they give you boring stuff or impossible tasks to do. It's a very fluid game with a lot of resources that require almost no grinding. It's easy to play and may feel too simple at first glance, but when you pay attention to the lore or to what the NPCs have to say, you discover a very flavorful world.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few times I find myself fully satisfied with completion of a game. I don't remember where I originally heard of Ocean's Heart, think Steam recommended it to me, but my brother ended up buying it from my wishlist last Christmas. There it sat in my library for a months until I finally found time to begin this adventure. And boy, was it an adventure. Playing this game took me back to the days when I was a wee little lad playing Legend of Zelda; Link to the Past on my grandparents SNES. Captured the same childlike wonder of explore the world, fighting through dungeons, discovering secret items, figuring out puzzled with varying rewards, and the mixed emotions that one feels when they discover that one really hard dungeon you just went though? Yeah, well if you stuck to the story quests you would have gotten x item that would have made things easier, ya dolt! XD Still, it was a real blast figuring out where to go next and what each item did to help you progress in the story. That one Its Always Sunny reference caught me completely off guard and gave me a good chuckle. The various weapons and their upgrades feel unique and fun to test out (some more than others *cough* bomb flail *cough*). Absolutely love Tilia's wit and personality, and the interactions with the various NPC's we met along the way. I think the only complaint I have with the game is how quickly Hazel just brushes aside Tilia's concerns and worries, like seriously you and her dad have been gone for months and your response is basically "Your grief isn't important right now, stopping blackbeard from taking the oceans heart is!" Regardless, all turned out well in the end, and I think I've gone on long enough with this "review". In conclusion, I'd give this game a 10/10 for its story, gameplay, puzzles, and art style. I hope and pray that Max will considering making a sequel to Ocean's Heart, or maybe another game in similar style. (Maybe this time around with some assistance from another person or two. If Max is okay with that.)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a lifelong fan of the Legend of Zelda series, particularly the 2D/top-down entries. While I love the 3D titles, after pouring hundreds of hours into BotW, and now messing around in TotK, I find myself missing some of the magic of the older entries.I picked up Ocean's Heart in hopes of hitting those nostalgic notes, and it was exactly what I was looking for.PROS:+ Great art with smooth action animations.+ Lovely music! My Twitch chat commented numerous times on enjoying the soundtrack.+ Some great humor peppered throughout. You can tell the creator, Max Mraz, is a fan of the genre.+ Fun environments that reward exploration. I'd say the exploration aspect of the game was the best part.NEUTRAL:~ I didn't mind this one, but if it matters for your gaming interests, this is a VERY easy game depending on your playstyle. Dungeons are brief - think barely larger than Shrines in BotW, and significantly smaller than dungeons in 'Link to the Past' or 'Link's Awakening'. If you're someone that likes exploring and collecting everything, you'll be very overpowered. Chat and I had some laughs when a boss would look like it might be a dramatic moment, but be finished in less than 10 seconds. There is an (optional) feature in game that can increase enemy difficulty, but even with that on, there was no challenge to combat, even on secret bosses. However, a simple solution to this is to avoid upgrading your weapons if you'd like more of a challenge.CONS:- None! OVERALL:• If you're looking for a beautiful looking game with a classic Zelda feel, this is a delightful experience.• If you have younger gamers in your life, this would be an excellent first step into the world of Zeldalikes.• I would say it takes about 12-15 hours to 100%, so the $14.99 price point isn't bad. I got it on sale at $5.99, and feel that's a STEAL.Kudos to solo dev Max Mraz and publishers Nordcurrent Labs!

The entire town is on fire and this guy who seems to be the only volunteer in town is heading out to capture the pirates and save whoever they kidnapped?! _childDocuments_.review: Oceans’s Heart is an ambitious love letter to games like Zelda: A Link to the Past, Blossom Tales: The Sleeping King, CrossCode and the upcoming Secrets of Grindea. To those of you who came to adore classic ARPGs, this game really has it all: cute pixel art graphics, a vast over world to explore, dungeons, boss fights, mini boss fights, whacky NPCS, fun side quest, a multiple of weapons, magic, catchy retro music and last but not least an intriguing story.There isn’t much hand holding to speak of though, but this is really a good thing I my opinion. You need to go exploring on your own as in the good old days. However, I could see this becoming a problem for some, but then this game probably isn’t for you anyway. In a nutshell Ocean’s Heart feels and plays much like a traditional 2D Zelda, but has its own character and qualities for sure. The controls are good (a future patch will hopefully let you assign your own buttons) and the menu system works OK, although it could be a little easier to navigate in my opinion. Likewise I would love to see mini maps of each unique location and dungeons. Further, the game has some minor stuttering, most likely due to the Solarus Engine that isn’t optimized for Steam yet. Also, while the music is really great and brings you back to the 16-bit era, it wouldn’t hurt with a little more variety - especially at special events, not just the main ones. Finally there Is really no reason to kill enemies in the over world, since they don’t drop any healing or other items.With that said, Oceans’s Heart is a true gem and an outstanding achievement from a one-man team. In its current state I would give the game 4,5 out of 5 hearts, but a future patch will most likely transform it into a full score. Either way, I will finish this one for sure. Love from Sweden.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics – 5/10Sound – 4/10Gameplay – 6/10Story – 2/10Replayability – 2/10Overall – I have really enjoyed the resurgence of throwback gaming over the years. Many games that have come out have a certain vibe that calls back to most people’s childhood and really tugs at the nostalgia strings. Many of these games are great, Fell Seal, Bloodstained, Moonlighter, etc.…Unfortunately, Ocean’s Heart is not one of these games. A lot of these throwback games feel like a love letter to games that came before it, they live in the same realm as the games from before, but bring some fun additions to the table, without ever feeling like a cheap knock off. Ocean’s Heart feels like someone was in a hurry to copy A Link To The Past’s homework before class started.  The game felt kind of uninspired and the story was forgettable and pointless. Not recommended. 🖥️ System SpecsAMD Ryzen 9 5950X | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 | 32GB RAM | 2560 x 1440 165Hz

There are many situations where simply moving into a new room exposes you to hits and damage from things you have no ability to defend from.- While the art pops and is nice, it often suffers from too much of the same, and gets boring fast.As I said during the pros portion, I feel like this game has a lot of potential, but it suffers from clunk that drags it down. _childDocuments_.review: In the very short time I played this, I encountered several issues and control bugs that render the game effectively unplayable. The big one is that, on my Steam Deck at least, any time I exit a menu or dialog box, the game automatically moves my character in the direction she's facing indefinitely, until about half a second after I press a direction on the gamepad. I played for all of about 15 minutes and that one bug alone managed to run me into enemies half a dozen times. That's the biggest issue. I checked on my PC and the bug is not there, so I'm not sure if it's a Deck specific issue, or something related to Xinput.There are several other smaller issues I encountered. Controls display keyboard commands instead of gamepad controls. The game seems to have minor haptic feedback for every step you take, which is very, very annoying. Inputs frequently double up (e.g. tapping down in a menu moves you two spaces down). Sound effects have a weird tinny, lo-fi micro echo which may or may not be intentional, but is incredibly grating on the ears. Movement is bound to the analog stick, can't move with the D-pad without rebinding things.Overall, just a heaping pile of minor issues/missing QOL, plus one huge bug means I absolutely cannot recommend this in its current state. If these issues can be fixed, it might be worth playing? I wasn't able to get far enough to make that call. I'd be happy to come back and try again if the issues are fixed, but I'm not touching this again until that happens.

_childDocuments_.review: This would be a neutral review, except Steam doesn't allow it. Unfortunately, I spent more time annoyed than enjoying myself. I finished the game out of stubbornness.That being said, absolute props to the nearly-solo dev of the game. I'd still be interested in a more polished sequel, and a number of my gripes below are limitations of the game engine, and not his design choices.The first problem is that the game just doesn't control well using a controller (I didn't try it on keyboard). There's no dpad support, the analog stick throws your character and menu cursor all over the place, and your inputs just aren't that responsive. This is an engine issue.The second issue is that combat quickly becomes an annoyance. Enemies drop nothing of value and can be a pain to fight with clunky controls, short iframes, and finicky hit/hurtboxes. Bosses don't use unique mechanics related to the tools you've picked up - they're just zergs...assuming your opening lightning spell doesn't one-shot them or they don't get stuck on a piece of terrain. Besides all of this, semi-thorough players will be practically invincible by 1/3 of the way through the game without even farming healing items. Provide an incentive to fight, or make fluid/flashy/enjoyable combat. I never needed the vast majority of the items, nor did I even use the legendary weapon since the upgraded  was vastly superior.+Save anywhere, very little penalty for death+Good quest log+Music is decent+Fast travel points+In-game way to raise difficulty after starting area+Family-friendly+8-14 hours of play+Somewhat open-world, with optional content~2D Zelda clone~Rather muted colors, dungeons sparsely decorated/colored~Only one save slot~Game starts hard, but you quickly end up with infinite health~Map isn't incredibly helpful~Can't use d-pad on controller~Controller rebind menu has user-unfriendly UI~Many enemies (incl. bosses) can be easily cheesed or one-shotted~Boomerang can't be thrown at an angle or pick up items~Rolling is fastest movement, so you'll be doing it non-stop~A few areas with full-screen flashing that you can't disable~No animation for enemies falling into water or pits~Found a number of typos and two bugs-Almost no i-frames-Frustratingly easy to fall into water all over game-Damaging boss attacks can remain on screen after their death-A number of doorways that have unavoidable damage behind them-Movement/menuing is oversensitive, at least on controller-Enemy hit and hurtboxes are unpredictable-Enemies rarely drop anything, turning combat into a chore-"Bosses" are usually minibosses that only need zerged-Can get temporarily stuck in moving NPCs-Penultimate story boss has an ear-piercing sound effectPlayed on:i7-12700, RTX3060, 16GB DDR4-3200Using PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller for Xbox Series X|SUnadjusted difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the kind of person who's very picky when it comes to zelda-likes. There's already a ton of souls-likes in the indie market and very few zelda-likes. As someone who's loved Legend of Zelda and hates what Nintendo has done to the series Skyward Sword onward, this is a breath of fresh air.Personally, I did not really like how the game started. Very little is told to the player and even less information and quest reasons. I didn't like how the game essentially gave you no cutscenes or any story related content for why the world is basically just a bunch of islands floating in the ocean. Even worse is that, there's no way to swim in a game that's so surrounded by water.This game really doesn't pick up till you get like 3-4 hours in. At which point, you can start perusing the libraries in the towns for lore info. That's not a bad thing, but when the game starts out kinda slow and buggy and frustrating it kinda makes me not really want to recommend it. Now this isn't to say this is game is bad or anything, but the way stuff is formatted and how there's barely any cutscenes really makes me kind of question how this game ended up the way it did. From the very beginning, I got this vibe that it just felt like someone plugged some sprites and basic animations into RPG maker or something and slapped this together.Regardless, I'm not going to spoil anything. The game really doesn't pick up till about halfway through. But when it does, it feels kind of like a cohesive game. There's still the issue of the game trying to emulate Zelda, but even in zelda you could swim.I'm probably nitpicking alot of these issues and the game really isn't as bad as I probably make it out to be. But this is definitely a buyer beware sort of thing. If you like stuff like Minish Cap and can tolerate some janky 2D physics, it might be fine but in all honesty just go find something else to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean Heart at first glance looks like a Zelda game, which there's nothing at all wrong with. I purchased it the minute it released because of that; however, I quickly found there are some gamebreaking bugs. I managed to softlock save ... yes, my entire save has been softlocked. (See video below)I have been gearing up for a review after completing the game; however, since I've somehow (and I didn't do anything special lol, in fact I didn't intend to) softlock my save, I'll just write up my review now.Good•	I really like the small details, like when you fast travel from location to another via boat, it shows the path the boat takes.•	The humor was top notch, it’s very subtle. “Man who takes his carrots serious” was the name of an NPC lol. I also really liked “There’s a list here in the guard’s barracks. There’s only one item on the list: Get stronger” lol.Interaction•	I really liked that you could enter houses and interact with a lot of little details.Bad•	The hitbox detection on the sword feels very wonky at times. You’ll be looking directly at something but the sword doesn’t connect. I wish it felt more like a cone attack rather than a touch attack, if you get my drift.SFX•	It would have been nice to have some vocal lines for the NPCs, even if it’s not english. I’m thinking like Midna in Twilight Princess when you spoke to her.Music:•	The music was okay, it got fairly repetitive at times. It would have been nice to get more soundtracks for, say, the interior of houses which would make the same looping soundtrack seem a little less repetitive.Graphics:•	A lot of the game feels a bit lifeless without a bit of extra polish. It would have been nice to see rays of light, shadows of clouds moving. Even a day and night cycle would have been nice. It’s just always day.•	It would have been nice for trees to animate as well as the flowers. _childDocuments_.review: So, like others have said, this game is a pretty nice homage to the early Legend of Zelda games. However, for $15 bucks, even on sale, I would not say it is worth it. To give the game some good boy points, it has good music which isn't repetitive and is actually quite creative. The composer did a great job. The graphics are ok, it certainly has some good spritework. Story is ok too, nothing extraordinary, but its a homage, not a love letter.As for the bad, the game is extremely, and I mean EXTREMELY unpolished, despite being fully released. I finally gave up after getting hardlocked in a dungeon where the idea is to use a warp arrow to switch places with a special stone. The hardlock comes into play where, if you get knocked off a ledge (and I will talk about that in a moment), you get sent back to the place you fell off from, or sometimes the beginning of the room. Sometimes, this helps for getting back to the beginning of the room when you get the treasure, but in most cases it is just incredibly annoying.Back to the ledge thing, so the game takes place in an ocean setting. So sometimes, you have spots you can hop too in the overworld and dungeons. Its pretty neat, however, the game is incredibly, and I mean, incredibly eager to make you jump, sometimes when you didn't even mean to jump at all. So you just yeet yourself off into the water because even though it's an ocean world, no one knows how to swim (sure? I guess). Other than that, you can ignore most of the monsters because they are braindead and follow very little pattern save for the bosses which can be one shot with a lightning spell you get early on, So feel free to cheese bosses which have no real puzzle to them except for smack 'em until they are dead. Overall, I wanted to like the game. The sidequests are neat, the main quest is ok I guess. But I hate how unpolished the game is, it was a struggle to get through it and I hated most of it. Also there is a quest, called Fykonos Island, that will pretty much deplete your inventory of your weapons and bombs. Sure you get your weapons back, thats fine, quests like that are a trope. Where I didn't like the trope is that another quest earlier in the game gave you enough bombs to last till death. I thought maybe I'll get all those bombs back!You do not. I guess I'm being too harsh since you don't need that many bombs, but the lack of polish still shows the oversight nonetheless. Get it if you love Legend of Zelda and clunky games, otherwise save your money and buy something else.

_childDocuments_.review: While I appreciate the ambitiousness of this game and there clearly went a lot of passion into making it, I can't really recommend it due to a number of issues that piled up while playing and stood in the way of my enjoyment.While clearly inspired by the 2D Zelda games, there are several deviations in game design that make Ocean's Heart decidedly less fun. Adding the frustrating and inconsistent spikes in difficulty that stand in the way of fun exploration on top of these issues leads me to not being able to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: An old school Zelda looking game about a woman named Tilia who's village was attacked by pirates under the flag of an hour glass. Her father follows after saying he would be back in about two weeks, 6 months go by and Tilia take up the sword to find her father and bring the Hourglass pirates to justice.  Just a disclaimer that I have played only about 3 hours and this is really a first look not a full review of the game. I wish I could play this game fully but I have so many videos planned for next week that I can’t spend the full amount of time on the game. Seeing as this may be a 5+ hour game, I hope you guys understand and latter portions of the game may differ from the review. So far, the game does truly remind me of old school Zelda games from the super Nintendo era. The quint essential old-school top-down action RPG. With its sword swing to even picking up and/destroying of pots, the mechanics are there, the only thing I’m missing is a whirlwind charge attack and that may be latter down the line. It does have some updated mechanics like the roll/dodge ability which comes in handy with the enemies you have to fight along you journey. The only issue that I have seen is from the sword and it's not really from the killing of the foes more from destroying the pots and plants around the area. The swing seems to be a wide arch for enemies but if you try to swing at a group of pots you need to be right in front of it for it to break, which feels awkward and out of place seeing the animations of a wide arch. But for the enemies So far, I have seen Birds, mushrooms, crabs, pirates, big golems, cyclopes with bombs and others, the list of enemies goes on. All I have been able to defeat them with have been a sword and magic lightning bolts and bombs, but there is also a bow and different types of magic I have yet to find an possible other equipment. Giving you a lot of variety to defeat each enemy. Throughout your Journey you will run across some puzzles most of what I have seen have been switches that open doors or sift floor panels, and puzzles that involve dodging pitfalls, I’m sure this is not the only puzzle you will encounter but it's all that I had seen so far. There are also many side quests you can embark on, with townsfolks needing your assistants some leading to money or enhancing your health which you will need in this game. Some of the side quests are simple but some have a really good side plot that builds the world, like the leader of the merchant's guild part of an embezzlement scheme. On top of all that you can upgrade your equipment to hit harder or raise you defense. The ingredients you pick up can be used in making potions, and from what I have read in other reviews forging armor and weapons possible. So much has been put into this game that its honesty amazing for the 14.99 price tag.    The world you will traverse is an archipelago with towns spread throughout. Each town has its own nice aesthetic, from the home town you came from feeling kind of like pallet town, Goatshead Harbor being a well-off harbor town, ballast harbor being the cove for pirates and others. Each one having its own design nothing feels copied or cookie cutter here they have their own breath of life. The areas outside of the towns are also beautiful with many variations in scenery from what I have seen and secret dungeons in the walls or hidden under plants something you would except from a Zelda style game.  Graphically its well detailed the enemies are highly detailed from what you can get of a top-down adventure game. Landscapes are unique around all the biomes and even the different locations can be told apart. Sound design is on the up and up, sound effects are not bad I don’t know if I would call them 16 bit because they sound more modern then that, and that goes with the music, which is great it still holds that classic action RPG feel. All in all I see this game being 5 to 6 plus hour game full of adventure and a lot of world building. From where I had to stop I had just learned that black beard is trying to control the seas with an amulet, so yea take that for what you want

_childDocuments_.review: If the creator of this game were to explain in an elevator pitch what Ocean's Heart is to someone, I would think they'd probably use the words "combat" and/or "adventure".But you wouldn't call walking around your block "adventuring". And you wouldn't call beating up on a baby "combat". And that's because, without danger or risk, the meaning of those words would be lost.By having an uncapped number of healing items that are used from a pause menu, you so dramatically undermine the risk of combat that the main gameplay features are undone. The only way you're dying in this game is if you become so bored or lazy that you forget to look at your health bar and press a single button a single time. That's not a difficulty issue, nor is it a casual vs hardcore conversation. That design choice made this flat out not a game anymore.And to be clear- a lot of games screw this up. Breath of the Wild screwed this up. But it's never acceptable for any creation to assert a reason for being in the same breath as it undoes that very reason. Because what you're left with is nothing. No reason for the creation to exist at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is a bit of a tough sell for me. It's in no way bad or mediocre, but I can't say it's great, either. There's definitely heart put into this but it just doesn't feel like enough? If you like 2D Zelda - particularly Minish Cap - you'll probably enjoy this, but it doesn't do a whole lot to stand out, especially if you're just neutral or "ah, I like these once in a while" about this style of game.The main issues with the game are that the difficulty curve is totally reversed (unless you ring the cursed bell but I gave the normal mode its fair shake, and I think having that there shouldn't be a design crutch) and there's a surprising amount of jank. You start out incredibly weak and a lot of things can even one shot you, but once you get just a few armor and sword upgrades you're not only tanking hits, but even bosses die incredibly quickly. It gets to the point that the final bosses are a joke if you've been semi-diligent about exploring, doing sidequests and upgrading your stuff. A power fantasy is nice here and there, it can be fun, but this is a bit silly and way too easy without ringing the bell.The aforementioned jank comes in with the controls and some of the more subtle things. It does say "full controller support" for I assume most Xinput stuff like your Xboners, but it doesn't feel right - not just because the default setup is a bit weird (d-pad doesn't control movement at all? what?) and I recommend changing it in the Steam Input settings, but it almost feels more like you've set it up with JoyToKey. There's so many little oddities - like how it's super easy to roll off a cliff into a pit or water versus Zelda, or how your movement inputs get "stuck" when you enter and exit dialogue, or that there's no easy way to switch leftward between tabs in the menu with one button press. Also, bombs take WAY too long to blow up. I don't know where else to put this, but I HATED that.I'm also iffy on the dialogue and story. The dialogue is going for a sort of Earthbound or (as another reviewer put it) CrossCode sort of jokey banter but it doesn't really work here - this is a magical medieval setting yet a lot of characters speak like your average Twitter or Tumblr user thinks the cool kids talk. It's such a small thing, but the fast travel character you meet says "dude" and it bothers me for some reason, like it's really out of place. The game doesn't really know how to balance this with any of the actual more serious story stakes, so by the end of the game when you face the final boss it just doesn't stick the landing at all.There was a decent amount of bad there to talk about, but honestly I finished the game and something kept me coming back, so I can't say it's all bad, either. There were points the game got a sincere snicker or laugh out of me, the pixel art is pretty nice, and the wider worldbuilding and set dressing is enough for me to overlook the less than stellar writing. I'd say this isn't a terrible game to pick up on sale and burn through for a couple nights. Hopefully the dev takes all the feedback he's gotten and makes something that blows this out of the water next time (ha!)

_childDocuments_.review: "Ocean's Heart" is a 15 hour-long Zelda-like with lots of sidequests and light customization options.  After pirates attack her island and kidnap her best friend, Tilia's father goes out to sea on a rescue mission.  Months pass without word of their safety, so Tilia sets out to find them.  The game wears its pre-"Breath of the Wild" Zelda influences proudly on its sleeve with its "Minish Cap" art style and gameplay loop: explore dungeons, collect items, fight monsters, then move on to areas that were previously inaccessible and repeat.  The game allows you to boost your offensive and defensive stats, which can quickly make it much easier to play.  There is a way to boost the challenge early in the game by making enemies hit harder, but that can be turned on or off.  My favorite part of "Ocean's Heart" was the abundance of sidequests.  They generally result in a monetary award you can use to buy consumable items and boost your stats.  They also help you to explore the game world and find hidden items akin to Zelda's heart containers and "Link to the Past's" magic spells.  Some of the best parts of the game occur during these sidequests: you can investigate an art theft during a dog's birthday party, or find a magic spell in the root system of a dying tree, or oust a corrupt merchant from his guild with the help of a guy who dresses like a squid.  Fun times.And now the bad part: the writing isn't good.  It's funny at times, but the constant self-conscious low-grade snark of every character's dialogue gets old.  There's no sense of character progression in Tilia, other than with her stats.  The lore felt jumbled and unclear.  This game needed an editor, or at least spell check.But if you're looking for your next ARPG fix, then don't let that stop you.  The rest of the game is smartly made, with plenty of hidden corners and secrets to eat up a weekend.  Try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The two games that immediately come to mind as logical comparisons are, The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, and a fellow ALttP contemporary, Blossom Tales: The Sleeping King. It should be noted that I have not played Blossom Tales 2: The Minotaur Prince, so I have no insight as to how this game compares to that title specifically. What I do know is this:Ocean's Heart is a longer game than BT but not as long as ALttP.Ocean's Heart has more meat on the bone in terms of narrative and storyline than either BT or ALttP, but it's not exactly in JRPG-territory, either.Visuals are subjective in terms of "better" or "best," but the art in Ocean's Heart is really on a different level from that of BT and ALttP.Ocean's Heart has pleasant albeit unmemorable music. Definitely not on ALttP's level. I don't remember any music from BT and I already don't remember anything from Ocean's Heart. It did a good job of setting the proper ambiance but won't end up in a VGM playlist. I do want to give a shoutout to the thunderstorm area of the game. It had the best thunderstorm sound effects and musical tension that I've heard since Super Metroid. The worst part of the music, by far, was that there is no miniboss or boss theme. It really made the fight experience much, much worse than it should have been. It almost felt inconsequential.In terms of gameplay, you get what you'd expect from a ALttP clone. It's fun, but nothing revolutionary. My main gripe is the difficulty balancing. I feel that it is too easy to max out the power of your sword and that it then just trivializes nearly all of the game, especially once you've also built up armor significantly. There is no reason to do anything other than just approach quickly, tank hits, and be spamming attack until your foe is vanquished. Earlier on in the game, this wasn't the case, but that only lasts briefly. There is magic but I never used it other than to open sealed doorways. You will your standard ALttP-style weapons, but you really just need the sword.Dungeons and Bosses were both weak in this game compared to BT and especially ALttP. Bosses suffered significantly from the aforementioned music and main character overpowering/tanking issues. They wouldn't even get a chance to do anything before they'd be dead. It was actually comical in a few cases. Puzzles were exceedingly basic and definitely not on par with either BT or ALttP. Big missed opportunities in these areas, unfortunately.Despite the Quest Log being lovely, I don't feel the same way about the map or the fast travel system. The map is pretty bare-bones overall, but it doesn't even have every area/region labeled, so sometimes you legitimately have to:-Remember where everything is (in which case you don't need a map anyway)-Wander around the whole world (brutal)-Look it up online (and this game has pretty limited guide content, so sometimes that's very much a "good luck" proposition)Fast travel was good to have, but felt like it could have used a few more spots to avoid a lot of unnecessary trekking/wandering.I know this review has turned pretty negative, but I genuinely did still have an enjoyable time with the game despite its flaws. It truly is beautiful, I enjoyed the story, and the rest was flawed but good enough. I would say it's probably a little better than Blossom Tales overall, but certainly not as good as A Link to the Past.

_childDocuments_.review: A good little SNES/GBA era Zelda clone with a lot of virtues and a lot of flaws. I recommend it and I would like to see the studio improve on what they have here, because what I see is a lot of potential that falls a little short. The level design is great, the puzzles and items are classic, the sidequests and the lore are interesting (though you have to dig a little for it). The problems: bosses fall really flat, in most cases they can't really challenge you because you can tank them by stuffing apples in your mouth while you just smash them with your sword. There isn't that classic Zelda "use the item to exploit the weak point" boss formula, and it feels anticlimactic to just have a slightly larger pirate that you have to hit a few more times at the end of the level. Even the final boss follows this formula: you just hit him with the sword until he dies. No tricks, no problem solving, just smash until dead. The game's inability to take anything seriously hurts the story. Everything is a joke. The threat of global annihilation doesn't carry any weight. That sounds bad, but the bosses and the story are a pretty minor part of the game that is generally pretty fun exploration, combat, and puzzle solving.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good indie Zelda clone that is mostly just limited by the Solarus programming language that was used to code it. It's unabashedly a Zelda copy because Solarus is a C-based game engine designed specifically to make Zelda knockoffs. So I don't count the fact that it's a copycat game against it. It also reminds me a lot of Earthbound because you spend a lot of time in towns talking to people, and a lot of the dialog is actually pretty funny and well-written. That, combined with the decent graphics and great music make it worth playing despite the software limitations. Pros:- Lots of items, weapons, enemies, etc. Relatively decent sized world, game takes about ten hours to finish.- Fantastic music, though sometimes it seems out of place- Graphics are very detailed and beautiful, though quite often feel a little bit cheap just in terms of the sprite quality- Lots of bosses, but again due to the software limitations they usually go down really easy- Tons of side quests, actually completing the side quests is the best part of the game. There's no shortage of them and many of them have multiple parts to them. There's one where you board a boat and it ends up getting attacked by a sea monster and you're stuck on island for about an hour trying to get your gear back. It's great.Cons:- Again, the software limitations. Particularly the collision detection, but some of this is just stupid stuff like a rock in the background stopping an arrow in the foreground. Also the scripting loops get screwed up if you die, and sometimes NPCs will randomly walk into walls and disappear. Nothing game breaking, the game only crashed on time in ten hours and I could pick up right where I left off.- Too easy. I mean Zelda games are easy, this game is even easier than Minish Cap. The puzzles are basically nothing, if you've played A Link to the Past on SNES you will already know how to solve most of them. And even though enemies will kill you constantly at the start of the game, unless you're in a dungeon, you will respawn on the same screen.- Healing items are overly complicated, in Zelda you just pick up hearts, it doesn't need to be that there's multiple healing items that heal a certain number of hearts, especially since you can just die to get your hearts back anyway.- Even with the quest log it's confusing to know where to go sometimes, there's no dungeon maps (The dungeons are tiny anyway), I don't even think you can see how many keys you have. And the world map only gives an approximation of where you are, which is confusing until you unlock 2/3rds of it, since you'll be wandering aimlessly.Overally, surprised at how engrossing this game was, this is the kind of game where you think of it less as a game than as a journey. I played this for six hours straight without trying to just rush to the end because I was enjoying finding the equipment upgrades and completing the side quests. Surprisingly well done for a game made with a simple game engine, and it's probably the best game ever made in Solarus.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Fun story, cool world, felt very paper mario and really scratched that itch for me. Tried to do absolutely every quest, really enjoyed it. I'm super impressed with how small the team is that made it for such a good product, and really enjoyed the secrets, the sidequests, the humor in the dialog, the character development to the guard searching for inner strength, random stuff here and there that broke up the straightforward 'go here and do this, now come back and do this' energy. Would play again. Cons: Wouldn't recommend on PS controller, had some janky moments like somtimes in the pause menu hitting right or left would slingshot the cursor as far as it could go in .02 ms so I could never select what I wanted, and sometimes I'd be hitting right and it'd send the character down and left. I'd wonder if it was my controller but I haven't had issues with any other games so not sure what to think. There's very little risk to the game. You can stop a pause a fight at any time and just recover your health if you have the items, which I had near max amounts for the second half of the game, so I was never in fear of dying or losing.Sometimes when you're near an edge you'll just slowly get dragged (or quickly dragged) into the water or into the hole and lose health. I saw no reason for that and thought it was kinda dumb. And sometimes walkways near water have walls to keep you on the path and sometimes they don't. I lost more health to my character suddenly running headlong into the water than to any monster or boss ever, and it just drove me bonkers. Between the controls and stuff like that I couldn't have any precision gameplay, just pick a direction and swing till everything runs into you and dies, pause and heal when necessary.

There's combat and puzzles, both of which are adequate but not super deep. There's just enough secrets and upgrades to get and generally the pace is fast enough so you don't get bored of the areas. Don't expect to be blown away, but if you want a good 'ol adventuring time with a style that harkens back to the SNES era, go for Ocean's Heart.

_childDocuments_.review: My recommendation is not exactly flying but i would say it is a fun Zelda-like title, that is overall enjoyable to complete. It's a very nice setting and the characters and writing is fine.It's pretty standard 2D adventure game look, but it has it's charms. I like the fast travel system and the map. There is a pretty good amount to do besides the main storyline and the combat is fine, pretty standard. Now for the negative stuff... 1: I personally feel like this is a controller game, but it sometimes doesn't feel like it was properly mapped out on it. Just to preface this by saying i played this on the switch first some time ago and got it on steam, and it controlled fine on switch but on PC it was kinda clunky. My left stick kept spazzing out when i was sifting through the menu, so i had to use my keyboard to pick items...I hate that the dodge and interact button is the same, please no.. just use any other button. Also can we just not have it so you get stuck in NPC's that are moving around? thanks.2: All the combat is easy and then gets stupid easy as you get all the upgrades. Salt candles should not be as OP as they are... You can just throw 1-2 of those at any bosses and whack them a bit and then they die. Also you can literally just damage tank anything since you get a stupid amount of health really easily and you can also just open your menu and heal instantly while the game is paused. So there is 0 challenge in any of the gameplay. The thing that takes the most brainpower is just figuring out directions, since the "puzzles" if you could call them that are easy too. Also they copypaste the same boss? mini boss? like 10 times, which is kinda lame, since there is a lot of cool designs that they do use. 3: The music and sound slider is useless. I had them both down at the minimum and random noises was still blowing out my eardrums. Just please audio balance your game. Still if you like a fun easy game, through a vibrant archipelago, go ahead and buy. I personally would recommend getting it on sale, as it's not that long, even if you do everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean's Heart is a charming game in the spirit of Legend of Zelda: Link to the Past. You control Tilia, a member of the Volunteer Navy on a quest to locate her father and fight Blackbeard, the pirate captain who is seeking a mystical artifact called the Ocean's Heart.The gameplay is typical of the early Zelda series, with a top-down perspective and wide inventory of items. There is also a limited amount of crafting that can be done with components collected from plants located around the islands. The map is fairly large and all of the locations are packed with secrets awaiting to be discovered, greatly rewarding exploration. There are numerous towns and each contains a small number of sidequests that Tilia can complete for rewards. The art design is charming and the sprites are well-designed.The only downsides are that few of the bosses in the game are particularly memorable. All of the main questline bosses feel more like glorified regular enemies rather than true challenges, though the optional bosses are very well-executed. The controls for the game are solid, except for the fact that my X360 controller was incredibly sensitive on the menus, flying through screens with the gentlest of touches on the joystick. Overall, it was a very nice gaming experience. The game will last 13-14 hours, if you complete all of the side quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Ocean's Heart

As for the snails make sure you have the right timing, and most importantly, get the right spells.  Normal mode is quite easy, but there is a hard mode option hidden within the game to make it a bit more challenging. I really liked the puzzles found throughout the game.  A solid 16 hrs game play with all achievements.  Not bad if game is on sale like when I purchased it.

_childDocuments_.review: A tight if finnicky  hack and slash a la older Zelda games, with a somewhat simple but satisfying combat system and intuitive puzzles. You get what you see, nothing less, nothing more, and really, is there any shame in that? My biggest complaints are the fact you can p. much brute-force any combat encounter by spamming ol' manslayer board, and that there's issues with positioning sometimes. IE walking over a switch may not trigger it, because you're actually a "square" higher than you should be. But eh, that's about it.  The enemy/location/Item variety matches the length of the game, so you won't find elements that overstay their welcome. The music will live rent-free in your head for a few days after finishing the game, as all good MIDI-style soundtracks oughta. So yeah. Like bird themes? Like murdering grass and trees to collect berries? Like to spam explosives and erase bosses out of existence in five seconds flat? Then give this a spin.

_childDocuments_.review: just good enough to scratch the adventuring itch, if that's what you're after. very much a one-dev project with a variety of jank in its movement and controls. i honestly appreciate the imperfections; they add an extra layer to the experience and there's a lot of heart and raw effort in here to make up for the quirks. i enjoyed learning the map and finding the hidden nooks and crannies. the combat gets trivialized by the introduction of a spammable aoe that doubles as a universal block, but it's strangely satisfying to cheese all the encounters this way. the platforming is less fun; there are some frustrating segments to navigate, but they're not long and death is mostly a suggestion anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute but slightly unpolished action adventure in the same vein as the 2D Zelda games. You play as Tilia, who goes on a quest to save her best friend (Hazel) and her dad from pirates.Has a nice mix of genre staples and new additions on the weapon/tool side, but the boomerang in particular (often a favorite of mine in Zelda) never felt particularly useful as it would just arbitrarily collide with background elements and bounce back. Also, the bombs have an annoyingly long fuse, and I don't think their instant detonation after throwing them helps either.The world is nice, although the controls sometimes felt a bit finicky when navigating around water, but while some obstacles are overly obvious in what you need to surpass them, others are vague and strangely, arbitrarily specific.Tilia is often a source of amusing witticisms, but some of the dialogue could have used another pass in editing for either typos or weird tone. Still, the game delivers a lot more in the story department than the typical Zelda game.In the end, it's a flawed but still warmly recommended game.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't read any reviews for this game and don't intend to try and argue points with anyone here, I simply want to state what I personally enjoyed about the game. I do have some bias, of course, as I am a MASSIVE Legend of Zelda fan, "A Link to the Past" being among if not my absolute favorite of the franchise. This game is not ignorant to nor is it shy about being blatant about it's influences and doesn't pretend to be anything that it is not. I personally had a wonderful time playing this game. It felt very familiar while still having a lot of it's own charm. I will say that there were times where the characters did feel a little one dimensional if not a bit too tropey, however overall the story, lore, and quests all felt solid to me. I quite enjoyed Tilias sort of dead-pan matter-of-fact humor a lot of the time and I definitely had plenty of smirks and full on, actual, laugh out loud moments with the game. My biggest gripe is that, while playing with a generic gamepad, some of the controls were a little on the wonky side. Nothing that wasn't easy enough to get used to and I'll be honest... I never checked to see if you could change or rebind keys or buttons or anything but this is a VERY minor complaint above everything else.Overall, I would highly recommend this game. I more or less never leave reviews for games... however I felt compelled to do so here because it REALLY is worth giving a shot if you enjoy the genre and the inspirations that brought this game to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Ocean Heart*Overview*When I first brought this game, I wasn't expecting such a nostalgic feeling of the old feel of Super Nintendo gaming. The influence of Zelda and Legend of Mania is evident from the time Tilia jumps off the bed. I appreciated that because I grew up in the Nintendo and Super Nintendo generation as a gamer. I love the feel of Zelda, and I thought it was a great homage to the game. I appreciate the simple straight storyline with the witty interaction with the characters. I believe as a retro game player, you don't need a complex storyline, out-of-the-world graphics, and complicated gameplay to create something lovable and memorable. This game is precisely what a casual gamer looks for in all categories. FUN!*Highlights*The game gives you a choice of difficulty from the beginning. Yet, you have to earn it, and I like that option. The curse mode can change the gameplay; how you choose to play is your choice. I, as the gamer, appreciate that option. The storyline is enjoyable enough to keep your attention and, at times, make you smile with the character. I like the combination of magic and weapons you can collect and play with throughout the game. The puzzles are not rocket science but enough to keep you engaged. *Conclusion*Rating 8.9/10I recommend picking up this game for a good laugh and some good gameplay. The play time is 12-15 hours, but if you want to do all the achievements, I think 18-22 hours is more appropriate without a guide. However, if you need or want one, an excellent guide is available, and thank you to the person who made it. If you are wondering why my gameplay is so long, I did mine without the manual, so you can see my time is double, LoL. This is a fun game, and I appreciate the developer using a woman protagonist to empower all players to play. If it had more spells, an option with a shield, and other playable characters to swap out for me, I would give it a higher rating. The game price is 14.99, but after playing, I would have spent up to 30 to 40 dollars for this game. It is worth your money, time, and effort. Thanks for a good 45 hours of gameplay. Hope you make more….

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Ocean's Heart is a delightful SNES-era Zelda-like game. Your home is attacked by pirates and your best friend is kidnapped. Your father leaves to go rescue her and stop the pirates. You, following in your father's footsteps as a Volunteer Navy Adventurer, leave home to find them and save them if necessary since they do not return after six months. The game's style is charming, the sound (both music and effects) are rather good, and the game's overall progression was quite enjoyable.One thing I particularly enjoyed was the more sandbox style approach to secondary equipment. Stuff that was nice to have but not necessary could be collected through exploration and mini dungeons. Thematically, a core concept to the game is that very exploration itself. Getting out there and helping people is what the Volunteer Navy does. You will want to keep track of where some of these obscure locations you find are as very little other than major towns are marked on the map. I had a blast going through the game and will likely be going back to finish it on the optional hard mode setting when I have time as well as polish off my few missed side quests. That said, out of the gate, you're going to have to change up your control schemes because the default keyboard controls are absolutely terrible for anyone with any history of playing games on a keyboard. Personally, I had to reset movement controls to the W (up), S (left), A (down), and D (right) buttons as well as interact/roll to spacebar and attack to E. I also rebound all the menu opening options, but that is a little less essential than the movement ones. There were some places where I felt the controls got in the way, but overall it was rare enough to be noticed but not frustrating.Of note, there are some accessibility issues with the game I feel are important to mention. Some puzzles require sound feedback to know if you are correctly interacting with the objects. If you can't hear or can't play with sound you are going to have to trial and error your way through. There were some puzzles I knew the solution to because it was provided by NPC/objects in world, but I couldn't tell if it properly clicked anything unless sound was on.Lastly, the last zone with the final boss is a seizure-warning nightmare. The screen flashes white quickly and very brightly in a muted color zone. I have no light sensitivity what-so-ever and I still found it to be painful to be in that zone. Which, since that comes at the very end of the game it would really put a damper on your spirits if you got there and found the flashing too much your you to handle. If you have bright light sensitivity or flashing light sensitivity I would give the game a pass for that reason alone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a love letter to The Legend of Zelda. Every inch of this game is lovingly crafted by the developer as an ode to the classic top down Zeldas we played on our GameBoys. This game does a lot of things right, the puzzles are fun and varied, the graphics are fun and nostalgic, the music is beautiful and variety in combat stands up pretty well. The only downsides I can see is that the main story was not that engaging (some of the side quests are very good though!) and the game in itself is relatively short. It is well worth a punt if you fancy playing something that takes you back to your childhood and in a world where a lot of games demand a lot from you, this game really helps you sit back and relax.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Decent gameplay, questionable story, excellent artwork, excellent music.Rating: 6.5/10As you can see on its Steam store page, Ocean's Heart is a gorgeous pixel art RPG that begs comparison to classic Legend of Zelda games. Coupled with an excellent soundtrack and fascinating side characters, the game world appears expansive and rich in detail. However, although the overall atmosphere and the secondary aspects of the game (i.e. side quests, tangentially-important NPCs) are well designed, Ocean's Heart struggles with its heart and soul: gameplay and story.In regards to gameplay, the influence of classic Zelda games is clearly seen in the top-down perspective on a melee-centric combat system. Now, I can't comment on how well Ocean's Heart compares to those Zelda games gameplay-wise as I do not have experience in the latter; however, I can say that the former's gameplay does have a few issues worth noting. Combat was mediocre in difficulty as you can always jump into your inventory mid-fight, scarf down a bucket of berries to heal all your health, and pop back into whatever battle you just rendered trivial. The lack of restrictions on healing items means that, at least for me, the best fighting strategy was no strategy at all beyond mashing the attack button and healing after tanking a few hits, regardless of whether the enemy is the final boss or the final boss with the Cursed Temple activated. In fact, the only time I died during the game was during an early-game puzzle section, mainly because the dash button and the interaction/action button are one and the same. Perhaps this is a quirk of Zelda-like games, but Ocean's Heart does not have separate keys for roll/dash and interact. Consequently, my attempts at interacting with something or someone often ended with the player character Tilia dashing onto an infinite hole or into the ocean, the latter in particular prompting the concerning question of why a trainee for the Volunteer Navy does not know how to swim. Despite these issues, there is at least a competent gameplay loop that, although not challenging, keeps the game chugging along.On the other hand, the main plotline for Ocean's Heart did not appear to reflect the care and attention given to other parts of the game. In order to show this, there are mild spoilers for the story in the rest of this paragraph. The start of Tilia's journey is generic on account of the burnt village, though earns a point or two in regards to the roles of Tilia's father and friend in the aftermath. However, nothing notable really occurs to the main story after Tilia properly begins her journey. Even the lore regarding the deities of Ocean's Heart and the Sea King seemed almost tangential and inconsequential, mainly because the only real reason Tilia is even in the story is because her friend and father couldn't be bothered to visit the village once in a while. Even the game itself seemed to want to end the story quickly, with the NPC dialogue immediately preceding and during the final section — with Hornigold's speech springing to mind — rushing the player towards the final boss fight. Additionally, no moral lesson is presented through the story, which would usually justify such an uninteresting story. In the end, the plot of Ocean's Heart is certainly not something worth touting.Ultimately, Ocean's Heart excels in everything that turns an already good game into a great game (namely through excellent aesthetics, music and side-quests) but lacks a strong combat system and meaningful plotline that serve as the foundations for a good game. Given some rebalancing with the combat and more care in the plot's themes and structure, this game would definitely be worth its $15 price. As it currently stands, I would only recommend buying this game if there's a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible RPG. It is definitely very much like older Zelda games, but not in a disappointing way: it feels like a unique spin on the tried-and-true formula on which the original Zelda operated. The harvesting and crafting system is diverse enough to be very helpful in battle and throughout your journey, but not so complex that you have to walk all over the islands to try to craft something very simple (although it did take me a pretty long time to encounter the King's Crown Flower). The dialogue is cheeky and fun, with the story being a perfect mix between serious and playful. The soundtrack is amazing--usually I listen to a podcast or what-not while playing games, but I have been deeply immersed in the lovely music of Ocean's  Heart. If you are a big fan of Fantasy 8bit RPGs, I would absolutely recommend buying it. Worth full price, if you ask me.
