_childDocuments_.review: As of the time of writing this, I'm in chapter 7. I'm only missing 2 achievements (get a unit to level 50 and what I'm assuming is the final story achievement at the end of the chapter). I gotta say, this game is a complete disaster. The story is nonsensical. The character "arcs" are so shallow and based on basically nothing? The combat is ridiculously easy. The main unit, Andrias, can basically one shot anything with the assassination ability. Just equip a weapon that gives you this, get behind the enemy, and proceed to steamroll maps. The perks you get with "AP" are so useless. Do extra damage when on cooldown? Assassination is never on cooldown if you last hit people with it! Receive more healing for the mounted units? It's really hard to take damage unless you purposefully get hit in the back! Once you get the higher tier equipment, all characters are at Andrias level of OP-ness. Use mounted charge from any mounted unit to line everyone up, magical force from a mage, trap caster from an archer, and that's it, I didn't even use 90% of the units because it doesn't matter. The game takes away one of your playable characters at the end of chapter 4 and at the end of chapter 6, so you have to sub in people who you've never put in before. Doesn't matter because even 10 levels down, they'll destroy anything with the right equipment, as most AP perks don't matter at all.I feel like I've played through this game as punishment for buying something before reviews came out, but I'm a TRPG/SRPG lover and the demo was so good! However, I literally feel like I'm punishing myself to finish this slog of a game. Stay away from this. If you want a good story, this isn't it. If you want good tactics gameplay, this isn't it. If you want to throw your money down the drain, then you've come to the right spot.

_childDocuments_.review: tried the demo liked it so I pre-ordered, and even with a discount on gmg I am disappointed.Problem is I finished the game in 18 hours and I did every sidequest until the last chapter when I was beyond bored of the game and just wanted to see how it ended.What´s the problem then with a game being 18 hours? It manages to be repetitive in that short time.What you see in the demo/first 2 hours is what you get.There is barely any new enemy units introduced, all the locations look the same. The demo´s "boss" units are repeated as regular units in basically every mission after a while, and there´s not really any boss fights to speak of. And even if there are "different" enemy units, that barely matters. They function the same for all intents and purposes,  I played on HARD, and just a few hours in the gameplay had gone from "run up to a group of enemy units and kill them" to "run around the entire map to gather every single enemy unit, use a CC aoe to group them up and nuke them" , what skills to use ? barely matters, positioning? barely matters. And by all means simple gameplay can be fun , but something about diofield chronicle just lacks that "oomph" factor that simple mechanics needs to keep it fun to do over and over and over.The story then? well it does have a few twists ( by few I mean exactly three) I really enjoyed, but they are to far apart , to short and mixed in to many boring plot beats that serve little point but to extend the game time, most characters are also boring, they have backstories and sidequests attached to them but again most of them feel like filler. I just didn´t care.Technically both in mechanics and in writing this game is not terrible,but I cannot recommend this at full price. it´s a MAYBE on a deep sale. there is some good ideas in this game and it had potential, but it falls well short for me.If you try it and LOVE the gameplay of the first 2 hours it might be for you. Just know that´s what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: DioField Chronicle sets out with some bold claims to introduce a new, deeply strategic, real-time battle system but fails to deliver on those claims and instead presents a quite limited hybrid of RTWP and a strategy RPG that not only lacks depth and is devoid of tactical elements but is hampered by poor balancing that ensures any notion of challenge is entirely absent even on the hard difficulty.As with most games in the genre the game is split in to two layers: Combat and headquarters which acts as the hub for main missions, side missions, party member/NPC interaction as well as equipment/ability progression.Core of the combat manages to nail down the fundamentals needed for a fun gameplay loop but the game fails to utilize this properly and runs out of steam around half way through. Rather than being fault of a single aspect in this case it is a combination of design issues, in terms of combat design: You fight the same few unit types over and over without any major behavior changes, every map is flat and linear, outside of occasional explosive barrels there are no environment factors in play and the most significant hurdle is that every fight plays out exactly the same way.In terms of progression game offers character abilities, accessories, weapons, skill and summon upgrades. Character abilities or rather perks are a very significant source of power, but the high costs make leveling feel bland as many of the perks cost multiple levels worth of points (up to 10). Sure, power wise upgrades such as "Reduces cooldown times by 30%" or "Increases critical hit rate by 20%"  are quite chunky but if you get roughly ~45 levels in the course of the 25 hour campaign (when completing all side missions) and you'll go several hours of level ups between being able to invest points - it simply doesn't feel good.Weapon, summon and skill progression in general is heavily tied to side quests which makes them more of a mandatory content. If you do all side missions once, you obtain enough points to upgrade all available skills, but summon and weapon upgrades are significantly more stingy which on one hand make you commit to your choices but also contribute to the feeling of repetition as  you'll likely stick to the characters you've unlocked weapons for and summons you've spent points on.Additionally weapons and accessories are severely limited by the amount of gold you receive, a single weapon category for example has something like 15 to 20 weapons in it but in order to gear up my team within a reasonable time frame I purchased only 4 weapons total per character that I used in my main team. While I definitely could have afforded to purchase a few more, they were never really needed and felt completely unnecessary.With all the issues regarding combat and progression it was perhaps a little surprising that the saving grace of the game  for me turned out to be the short mission duration which averages from 2 to 4 minutes and in fact in the latter half of the game rather than trying to play it as intended I was much more interested in seeing just how fast some of these missions can be beat. Due to how quickly the balancing issues compound in the latter chapters some of the characters become almost comically overpowered which prompted me to see just how much I can get away: Can I pull most of the enemies in the map at once and then line them up so a character can one shot a large portion of them? Certainly not the intended way of playing but it was fun to see just how much you can break, a silly example would be taking roughly 1 minute 30 seconds to beat a mission where the bonus goal was to beat it in under 8 minutes.So what about the narrative and story then? I think it's fair to say this continues the streak of Square-Enix titles that took inspiration from Game of Thrones, The Witcher and various other IPs that are focused on the more grounded approach to fantasy yet occasionally feature darker elements and gritty moments woven in a setting full of political struggles.There were things I enjoyed in the story, drawn cutscenes with the narrator describing various events were a highlight and in general the writing does decent job at telegraphing the bigger plot "twists", sometimes being surprisingly subtle about them and sometimes being about as subtle as a sledgehammer with others. Story and characters suffer so much from the narrative structure acting almost as a chronicle, many events happen offscreen including some of the defining moments and time skips are happening constantly. Ultimately it all ends up feeling like a rushed mess where the player isn't invested in any of the events, after all no matter how much politics, twists and turns you cram in the span of 25 hours - it doesn't matter if you struggle to even make your characters seem one dimensional while giving players no reason to get invested in any of them.That being said I find it hard to recommend DioField Chronicle as its combat is incredibly repetitive, poorly balanced and combined with a disjointed narrative that is difficult to get invested in - all that remains is a rather underwhelming take on strategy RPGs. Veterans of the genre won't find anything worthwhile here and those new to the genre have significantlybetter options to spend their money and time on.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels very much unfinished as far as gameplay goes. Many things go unexplained and the player has to figure out how statuses, etc. work on their own past the initial tutorial. Outplaying enemies is as simple as either just stunning them whenever they charge an AOE, or just simply moving your units out of the way due to the real-time nature of combat. The skill trees and upgrade systems in general feel very linear and don't add much depth to the game, past just making your characters' numbers go up. The story itself is very rushed and doesn't take time to explain things, pacing issues notwithstanding. It tries to make you care about the world, but does nothing to get you invested into it and as a result, a lot of names, story events, etc. just fly over your head with no meaning behind them.Overall, this game feels very much like a mobile game as far as depth goes, only with modern PC game levels of presentation that don't do enough to compensate for the game's faults. Definitely not worth the 60 dollar price tag, but potentially worth purchasing when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is meh. While I can appreciate what they were trying to do with letting you walk around its rather pointless and the resources would have been spent improving other aspects of the game. Normally in this genre I wouldn't criticize the graphics but its Square and they decided to charge $60 for this so the graphics are mediocre at best to bad. Now lets talk about the meat and potatoes of an SRPG. The gameplay. This game is laughably easy. Most of the difficulty is derived from having to micro your units out of telegraphed enemy attacks. Usually I'd wait to criticize this but from the info coming out, nothing is going to change. Prebattle planning that SRPGs are known for is light and fairly inconsequential. This game is probably worth a buy when its hits a half off sale if you're a fan of the genre. I might have gone recommend if this was an indie forray into the genre but its a full price game from a major dev. If you're strapped for cash you're better off waiting for Tactics Ogre Remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a thumbs up for me.First of all, it's important to mention that the developers haven't abandoned the game. There will be a free upgrade adding a new scenario and very hard difficulty.This game has received much criticism, and I agree with most of it. It is easy even in hard mode, and lacks diversity. Maybe we could have more classes, and more enemy types.But what we do get still is a very fun gameplay. The game is paced nicely, there is nothing to artificially increase playtime. What I felt really refreshing was the fact that the story never devolved into "saving the world or the universe from some ancient great evil" (which happens way too frequently in my opinion). It remained political and down to earth. There are no clear, obvious heroes or villains. Some people hated the story, but I greatly enjoyed it, and am looking forward to a sequel or DLC.Overall, the game has its flaws, but is still fun and refreshing. Play the demo, I can safely recommend it for those who like it (wait for a sale though).

_childDocuments_.review: So i wish steam had a neutral option, something that says, "This game is not terrible, but its not good either, its like a plain and dry sandwich."  Starting with the good, the maps are gorgeous, the cg work in battle maps is beautiful and the 2d character art stills are very reminiscent of old school square, so much appreciated.  The gameplay is easy to pick up and master, and the story is a good one.  It is not great mind you, more on that in the cons section.  This game has potential, it honestly had the potential to give square a new solid franchise to run with.... now the bad...The voice acting is bad, if I were to put my actual thoughts in here about it this post wouldnt be allowed to post, it is some of the worst voice acting ive ever heard.  The sad part is its not the actors voices that is so bad but the deliver, they all sound like they are whispering off a script in someones closet.  The story is classic and predictable to a fault, if you have played any of squares back catalouge then you will see every twist and turn coming from a mile away.  Its as if the dev team just played alot of old games, wrote down their favorite plot points, then tried to cram them verbatim into Diofield.  I dont mind a story being predictable, so do not get me wrong on that, when you have played as many games and read as many books as I, and undoubtedly many of the other fans have, its nearly impossible for a developer to surprise me with anything anymore, I accept that.  My issue is that foreshadowing for events to come was SO hamhanded that even a 3rd grader, who had never played a square rpg before would know what is going to happen long before it does.  The gameplay loop is repetitive in a bad way, the bonus objectives for every level are the exact same ones on every level, even on the hardest difficulty i barely need worry about upgrading anything and can breeze most levels in under 2 minutes, I just broke 10 hours of gameplay and am halfway through chapter 4 as of the writing of this, so I expect a full plat in less than 20 hours.  You will see 95% of all abilities that you can unlock in the first 2-3 hours, you will continuously be given new characters to use, characters you will never actually need to use at all or even look at once the story is done with them.  This is how i described the game to a friend of mine and I stand by it:"The game is basically a plain and dry sandwich with grade A ingredients but without cheese, it had alot of potential, and could have kicked off another amazing franchise but honestly i think it will be a oneoff"Great Job squarenix! You have found a way to let down old school fans again, if we could give out awards for companies that have gotten great at disappointing us SquareEnix would be No.1,  I cannot recommend this game, I dont hate it, and will finish it, but I dont like it either, and to me a recommendation would be me saying "This game is worth it at full price!" and it isnt, not at all.

_childDocuments_.review: DioField Chronicles is a game without a focus on its own mechanics. Since 4/5ths of the game is the partial-RTS aspect, it becomes very clear early on that a majority of the game will be slow. Once you get AOE abilities, and abuse Andrias' assassinate/ambush; there is little that can stop you. The game makes a point that you, the player, should level up all of your characters. That becomes an issue with how DioField handles its EXP system. You'll spend more time replaying the handful of side missions just to get EXP or money to get better equipment; than you will furthering the game's story. Even though you honestly don't have to.The game's story isn't told in the best of ways. Still, it has some really good and interesting world building. Something that I hope to see continued. DioField's story will give you the necessary information to go into the next storybased mission with context. Unfortunately, the comes across as shallow and could use a bit more interaction to really flesh out the entirety of the situation. Along with character arcs that although come up, don't go too in depth with who these people are. We get a decent idea, but nothing more. The ones we learn the most about are the first mage you recruit, and the first archer. And even then, we the player, don't get to see too much other than what is at face value. Unfortunately, the main character, Andrias, remains a mystery; even at the end. It feels like SquareEnix is trying to go this multimedia route with a lot of IPs nowadays, and if FF15 is anything to learn form; it's that route doesn't go anywhere. Honestly, the characters are interesting, if you want to get to know them. It's just you don't get to spend a lot of time with them. Three of the most important characters, Izelair, Lorraine, and Fredret, people we spent the entire game with; we know only a fraction about and, have spent so little time with. We get a little background and a motivation and that's it. Yet, all of these people put their trust in Andrias despite his deflective nature. It's just a hard sell. Andrias doesn't need to open up, but there needs to be more than what was delivered. It feels like we have a modern day Fire Emblem game, but none of the fully committed aspects that made people like Fire Emblem. The missions themselves are incredibly unimaginative. We have all these abilities, these beautiful-well-crafted maps, objective points, and variations of enemies/allies/troops to play with and the most we get is: Kill everyone, don't die. There's like maybe 3 missions where it's: Defend this position. Or a literal escort mission. There were several opportunities for a stealth mission, a treasure hunt, an ambush mission, or even a resource mission. All of these ideas that could have made it into play for the design that they had; and we primarily get an elimination mission. Sure, you can get creative with the kits at your disposal, but why do that when you can just send a cavalry unit to aggro all the enemies, lead them into a narrow location, and then bomb them to hell? For a tactical game, you really don't need too many ways of thinking to succeed within the objective frames they give you. Which, the objectives you always get are, 1: kill everyone. 2: don't die. 3: Kill everyone with x-time. 4: open chest. DioField has a lot of flaws. But there is potential here. There is so much that can be done. The world presented is so interesting and is far from finished. I recommend the game because if you do like this experimental style of game; it's a good buy. If you're unsure, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: What may first seem like a fairly interesting game ultimately amounts to nothing. The DioField Chronicle ostensibly has an "innovate" combat system, but it's actually just an extremely basic RTwP (Real-time with Pause) system without much depth. Middling production values and a bare-bones by the numbers plot don't help much. If you've ever played a real-time strategy game you could pause, you've probably played something with more depth. You get a maximum of 4 units (extremely basic) who you can order around and spam skills with. All skills are executed instantly when you order it and the enemy can't move during your casting animation. There is simply no further tactical depth to any of it. When you've cleared the first mission of the game, you've essentially seen all the game has to offer in terms of combat and tactical depth. The game never changes beyond that. What's even worse is that the maps and mission structure never really change beyond what you see in that first mission. Essentially, every mission plays out almost exactly the same. There are a bunch of enemies on the map, and you need to kill them. You point your guys in their general direction, and kill them. At that point, more enemies spawn. Rinse and repeat. 95% of all the mission follow this exact structure until you get the Mission Complete screen. There are a few mission where you have to defend a barricade, but even in this scenario you actually have to go after the enemy instead of defending. There are also 2 escort missions (if I remember correctly), and that's basically it. Even the final boss battle is just the exact same thing, with the boss appearing in the final wave of spawn. There are almost no other objectives aside from "Defeat the enemy".Making things even worse: the game is extremely easy. I never lost a mission and was able to complete all the bonus objectives on the very first try.The overarching story is boring, full of annoying characters and ultimately goes nowhere. Plot details are could have been interesting have been banished to an in-game codex that most people probably won't even find. Most of the overarching conflict in the game is barely detailed and you just get some hand-waved details every once and a while. The main characters are a bunch of annoying dullards who are not only full of themselves, but experiences no real growth throughout the adventure. Any internal conflict between the characters is never resolved. On multiple occasions, there is a (simplistic) discussion between characters with opposing worldviews, and it is basically always resolved with "We don't have time for this now!" after which they don't take up the discussion again. The main character on countless occasions tells other characters to "think whatever they wish" when they opine on matters, which is just about the most boring way to react in a story like this. Many characters do have some suggestions on deeper threads in their background, but this never comes to fruition.To give you an example on how bizarre the storytelling in this game is: early on in the game you get the suggestion that there are dark things happening behind the scenes of the games local monotheistic religious order (as is mandatory in every JRPG). At some point, your characters receive a letter detailing some of the horrifying allegations of what is actually happening, leading to several scenes of conflict with the church throughout the game. But, at NO point is it revealed to the player what's actually going on. It's honestly just bizarre. I didn't know if I was missing something or if the game decided it was more effective by not revealing this, but is was a strangely unsatisfying way to handle things.Even funnier, the game even tries to pull of a "shocking twist" (which had been clearly signposted for 10 hours or so) 5 seconds before the credits roll. This is not me exaggerating. If anything, it's probably less than 5 seconds. Its the most unsatisfying narrative structure I've seen in a game in a long while. In terms of presentation, I'd say the game is alright. The battle sequences have a very distinct tilt-shifted/diorama-like style that actually works quite well. Combined with some effective lighting in those scenes, I'd say it's relatively pleasant. Unfortunately, the scenes outside of combat in cutscenes and back at base look really bad. The character models, animation and lighting completely fall apart here. Many student games or single-dev games look better. The game clearly tries to make up for it with some overtly-stylistic lighting, but I don't think it works.Voice work is a mixed bag. During the battle scenes, voice acting is actually decent (except for the fact that enemy units only have 1 death sound per faction, which is actually kind of hilarious). However, back at base the voice acting takes a dip. It almost feels like there were two different directors for these sequences. For every great actor there's also a really annoying one.In terms of soundtrack, it's not really bad, but it's just lacking in variety. I think there's only, like, one battle theme? In the entire game? Either this is incorrect or the songs were so generic I didn't even notice there were multiple ones. Overall, this is unfortunately not worth your time. I came in genuinely wanting to give this game a shot, but there just isn't much here to even talk about. It's a bare-bones experience with very simplistic gameplay. Its saving grace is its ultimately short runtime.

Not groundbreaking or a rich story.Tips:Save file location directory (Win10):C:\Users\<userName>\Documents\My Games\DFC\Steam\<ID>Additional config(?) file directory (Win10):C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\userdata\<steamID>\1399080Review:The game is an overall console port that has been mentioned by some. Ray tracing, at the time of review is all but broken and should be disabled. From looking at the community around the game, one big point to bring up is no cloud saves. Due to this, do not expect play this on multiple platforms without doing some technical work to extract the save from the Deck to the PC, and vice versa.The game itself plays like a traditional SRPG, sans the grid gameplay people grew fond of in old school tactical games. In this game, everything is running in real time, but can be stopped for selecting skills, moving units, or even pausing the game. As for the difficulty, there is little to no difficulty, even playing it on hard. You do not need to grind for EXP for any bosses as your skills are so overpowered. Due to this, expect to beat the game with little to no trouble. If you do happen to die, the game has a way to rewind to checkpoints in each battle (M key bound for K+M gameplay). So even if you do screw up, you’re saved from having to redo the entire fight. No saving mid fight, so once you start a mission, expect to finish it.Overall, if you are a fan of SRPG, I would give it a go... at an extreme discount. Just do not expect a good story, or challenge and enjoy it for a new twist with the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10 - After 40 hours of gameplay and finishing the game I am adjusting my review to 3/10. The decrease is because of the story. WHAT IN THE HECK HOT GARBAGE WAS THIS STORY? I am actually convinced that the story was written by an AI or a psychopath who doesn't know anything about human emotion but regardless it has solidified in my mind that Square Enix employs some of the worst writers known to game development. I kept playing through the whole thing with this sick wonder: "where are they going with this?" I kept playing to see if the wholly unlikeable main characters would go through any kind of character development that would turn their eyes toward issues that we generally see as more moral--such a democracy, or, I don't know, having literally any empathy whatsoever. But no, the main characters are terrible through and through. The only reason the game isn't a 0 is because I enjoyed the battles. I found them satisfying. And hey, it's pretty rare these days that I play a game all the way through. But it's hardly a compliment--I played it all the way through with the same sick wonder that one watches a train wreck. I played it all the way through to see if this little baby would grow up into something great. But instead the baby was raised on bathtub gin and what was produced was the combination of a dumpster fire and a car wreck. I am genuinely angry that someone, somewhere has their dream job in game development and was paid money to write this story. SHAME. SHAME ON YOU. I can't remember the last time I was this disgusted with a story. Original review:6.5/10 -- You will either like this game or hate this game and it's all going to depend on how you feel about the unique Real Time Tactical Battle. I highly recommend playing the demo before any impulse purchase. If I hadn't played the demo at PAX I probably never would have picked this up or even known about it. If you are looking for the next great highly strategic tactics battle-- you will not find it here. If, like me, you've struggled with RTS and Tactics, you might find some real enjoyment here. This game is easy enough for me and that is a point to its credit. I find the battles to be quite satisfying-- not so easy that I stomp through every battle without challenge but easy enough that I'm not going to get frustrated a few battles into the game and never play it again feeling like I wasted $60. A few hours in and I'm engaged by the equipment, magic, skills and character options to change up my gameplay. Other notes: The story is incredibly meh. It's the same regurgitated trash we've seen in a million Square Enix RPG's. At this point it seems like they made an AI read countless hours of formulaic RPG scripts and then it just churns them out on its own. The voice acting is very well done. The music isn't going to win any awards but it's engaging. Art style/Graphics: Man they really could have tried harder to make a richer environment but it gets the job done.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a total disaster of a game. When this was announced I was pretty curious. A unique strategy game with real time mechanics, a Fire Emblem-esque story about knights and nobles and war, made by Square-Enix and potentially for the Switch too. This ticked a ton of boxes. Fast forward, they released a demo on PS5. I gave it a try and the demo pretty much cemented what was seen from the announcement trailer. Production values were immediately iffy though and the hub area felt so lifeless and bland, it was clear this was no AAA production. But otherwise I got from the demo what was promised. The actual gameplay felt a bit jank, but it was certainly unique and not something done to death so I was willing to give it a chance - at a discount. The demo also made it very clear that the game wasn't worth the full price in any way. I ended up getting a Steamdeck eventually so at about half price I got the Steam version and not the Switch version as initially planned. It runs quite perfectly on that btw, not that that's impressive considering we have PSVita graphics at best. Now here comes the actual problem. What was in the demo wasn't a small prologue of a more interesting game to come. No, the demo already covered *everything* the game had to offer. Right until the end of the game you fight nothing but the same shield guys or bow guys and they have the exact same mechanics in the last mission as in the first two missions. There are two or three more enemies (monsters, horseback riders and wyvern riders) but THAT'S IT. And those don't offer anything unique either, they just have differently shaped AoE circles you have to step out of. The missions also offer zero switch ups of the formular. There is one escort mission in the game and one or two defense missions, but that changes essentially nothing. You can take the same party from the beginning of the game and walk through the map clearing the same enemies over and over using the same 2 techniques and formations. I don't know when I last encountered such bland and lazy game design. It's a complete and utter borefest. And if you were hoping that at least the game would have a great storyline or characters, sorry but no. That aspect is really bad too. All the main characters are super unlikeable. And the plot is just bizarre at times. When it's not bizarre it's predictable and boring. It's like someone watched Game of Thrones, didn't understand any of it and tried to mimic it anyways. The ending of the game is also simply laughable.Don't even get this game in a sale. You'll waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I was definitely hooked into the game's art design. It definitely promised a lot with its art, and its "Realtime Stategy" battle system, but it fell short and ended up looking like a repetitive RTS. One of the main features of this game is the Real Time Tactical Battle, but only ended up looking like a basic form of the combat system from the heavy hitters in the CRPG genre, like Pillars of Eternity, Pathfinder, and Tyranny. What happens usually in a combat scenario is, cluster all enemies together, buff AoE DPS, make AoE DPS kill everyone. Rinse and Repeat. You can imagine how this just becomes a chore really quickly.Missions should have had more variety. Kill All Enemies, Kill Enemy Leader, Escort Important NPC, and Defend Barricade isn't enough.The story is one of the main factors that makes me feel like this is an "okay" game, but that "okay" is more like a 7 out of 10. The story needed better execution, better dialogue, and definitely more content to make everything feel more cohesive. Some of the twists in the game feel like they could have used better execution.Lastly, the game doesn't match its price, so you might want to purchase this during a sale. Accessibility: Achievements: The hardest achievement to get is to level up a character to level 50. I finished the game with a character at the highest level of 42.Gameplay: There are two main gameplay screens. One is the social interaction/hub scene, where you can talk to characters, purchase equipment, upgrade class skills or summons, etc. The other is the combat scene. It is a diorama-style scene, very reminiscent of playing TTRPGs in real life. The diorama scenes are elegantly detailed, and is obviously one of the main features in the game due to amount of enhancements that it has. Music:Story:  Lifespan:Graphics: Gorgeously detailed and beautiful artwork, but this artwork does not match the 3D models in the game. Textures aren't up to par with current triple A games despite its triple A price, since it is made as a diorama.

_childDocuments_.review: The DioField Chronicle has some pretty significant issues, but my enjoyment of the base gameplay has pushed me through to the end of the game.The writing is pretty dreadful. While there are some interesting moments and some decent (although mostly JRPG cookie-cutter) characters, any potential weight to the story is thrown away with the way the overarching plot unfolds. The majority of the story is told through pure narrator exposition in cutscenes that feel very akin to the dry exposition you get in a Dynasty Warriors game where you're just told that things are happening.The gameplay also really needs some additional variety. I would've liked to have seen missions force or reward a bonus for mixing up your squad composition and play style - they really only do this once or twice over the course of the entire game. I also think the game really needed to have some unique character traits that would've better differentiated characters of the same class/weapon type.I also do really like the overall look and presentation, but I'm sure some people will be turned away by the generic and dead-eyed look of the characters. Nothing all that noteworthy on the music front - it's totally serviceable.Hard to really recommend at a full priced $60, but it's worth considering on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am big fan of this kind of games and I really wanted to like this game. The setting is pretty great, although it lacks character personality that Three Houses had. Systems are there, interesting combat is there, but there is no reason to engage with anything.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR @bottom:First off, I'd like to say this is a beautiful game.  The voice acting is top-notch and graphics look stunning in a mix of drawn scenery and game graphic characters reminiscent of games like Legend of Mana.  The feel of the game plays like a graphic-novel style story similar to Valkyria Chronicles, but more of a narrative than in-depth story.  It feels rushed, you join and then you're immediately a respected member, why? You haven't done anything yet.  It's part of the intro and I suppose the story doesn't want to get bogged down, which is nice for pace, but feels like you get everything for doing nothing.Strategy RPG-We all know these types of games and I originally thought this would follow suit.  It doesn't.  The gameplay is real time with the "Strategic pause" style.  I'm not a fan, so take that into consideration.  I much prefer the FF Tactics approach.  This in and of itself wouldn't be an issue, however, the interface is very clunky.  In a real-time game, you can't have a clunky interface.  The amount of times I've thought I was choosing one character and instead told all the ranged to charge into melee is aggravating or thought I had the knight selected and told him to charge but then found he's just sitting on the sidelines twiddling his thumbs.  The special attack screen defaults back to the character you used it with before instead of the character you currently have selected.  You cannot change from the special attack screen to the move screen without unpausing first which then moves the battle forward until you can try to pause it again to pick the character you wanted.  You cannot move the screen to check targets until you select a special attack, and if you go back, the game unpauses.  This is a very confusing choice, this setup has been done seamlessly in so many SRPGs before this.  I know innovation is great, but only when it's good.  This game, in it's current state, is not enjoyable to play and is not worth $60.Summary/TLDR:Beautiful graphics and voice actingNice musicWe've heard the story before (Not bad if the characters are fun!)Bad gameplay/clunky interface (Makes the battles frustrating)Stiff character movements/bad physicsNot FF Tactics remake, so if you're looking for that, this is not it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Diofield Chronicle was a game I was very excited for, I told my friends about it coming out, I waited for the release date and counted on my calendar, I even tweeted when it released on twitter and was super excited. I love Square Enix games, I love strategy RPGs as they are my favourite genre of game, and I loved Octopath Traveler so when I saw that this has a new timeline strategy system and Octopath story writing, I was extremely excited. Unfortunately, the game fell flat on its face. For the first chapters I was enamoured simply by how much I wanted to love the idea, but the game itself was a bit lacklustre. I played it on the hardest difficulty as I enjoy hard games, and then even on hard, the game was incredibly easy. I never once found myself pressed for time, even when intentionally handicapping myself and playing with 2/4 characters in play, I handily beat the goal. This is because the game is not very hard and due to the new technology being used, I'm quite sure the balancing and dev teams were just unsure how to make a game like this or how it would be played. There's incredible plot holes all throughout the story that make little to no sense, there's some nods to certain storytelling tropes but they never actually develop anyone's personal story, so it makes going into their side quests very unrewarding and ultimately feels like a waste of time. The final cutscene (I won't spoil anything in this review) was not satisfying, if you're playing through the game and trying to stick with it going "Oh boy, but just think about the ending!" There is no ending that makes this game good, I too, was excited for the ending. There was no reason to be. It was awful. This game should not be £50. It is not a fully fledged game from Square Enix, Triangle Strategy which I recently also played and greatly enjoyed, is a full fledged game. Get that with the money that you're contemplating on spending on this if you like Square Enix games and want a Strategy RPG. This game feels like it was NOT "crafted by a skilled and experienced development team", it feels like it was made by College Students for their software developer course at university. This is not a fully made £50 game, it's much shorter than most Square Enix games and I believe that is because most of the content feels like it is MISSING, especially when you consider story plots and side quests. It feels like they were meant to have finished and fleshed out these characters and then they just... Never did. This is clearly a beta test for Square Enix to work out if they want to make the timeline system in future games. And I loved the timeline system! If they can get it to be balanced to have some level of difficulty and actually make it an interactive experience, it would be great! Unfortunately as is, the gameplay elements are pretty much spamming abilities until everything on the screen dies. There's no real planning, there's no "I need to commit all my resources to this one boss", you can more or less breeze through the entire game without even using summons or consumables on hard mode. If you look at guides for this game, their strategies mostly consist of using one cavalier unit to drag every single unit on the map to your allies, and then using AOE to kill everything. And repeat. That's the gameplay loop. That's all there is. TL;DR This should not be the price it is. It feels like a beta test for timeline strategies, I was very excited for this game and even that could not pull the wool over my eyes how unfinished and bad it feels to play. From story to gameplay to outright missing features.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, my biggest complaint is difficulty. "Hard" was incredibly easy and I constantly found myself wishing that the developers would provide more opportunities to test the game's strongest component: the battle system. Story is a bit all over the place BUT it winds up in that slightly campy/unintentionally good space where I think its oddities and lackluster dialogue come back around and start to work for it by the end. In the end, it was worth the time though perhaps not the full price tag. I would actually recommend this game specifically for srpg fans who are just starting off and want something engaging but not overwhelming. If I were to assign an arbitrary number to it, a 7ish would feel appropriate.P.S. Use characters you like, don't worry about who seems better. -A stubborn Izelair user.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a bit of a disappointing one. The gameplay premise is quite intriguing as a real time strategy game with JRPG elements. Unfortunately, the systems are shallow and the combat revolves around nothing more than stat checks. I'm currently playing the game on hard and have really only faced one difficult mission. Since then, side quests and easily purchasable items in the shop have made combat trivial.The only positional advantage in the game comes from attacking a unit facing backwards. This means you pretty much only need one character to draw aggro while the rest move to an opponent's rear to maximize DPS. You units also suffer more damage when being attacked from behind, but because you never really have to run away, it doesn't particularly matter.It feels like there could have been a really unique game here, but it just wasn't fleshed out enough. The demo is honestly more exciting than the full title because it's not needlessly drawn out and repetitive. I'd be interested in seeing a sequel that adds more meat to the combat and ups the difficulty, but Square Enix has a bad habit of pumping out interesting one-off games and then forgetting them and their mechanics forever.If you absolutely loved the demo and are adamant on buying this, I'd recommend doing so at a 50% sale at least. Diofield could have been amazing, but it is actually fairly meh.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art, typically well done Square-Enix backstory, entirely soulless characters and bland emotionless voicing. I wanted so much to enjoy this game, but it's particularly repetitive and shallow leading you to not care about any of the characters, not that they have much real interaction anyway. Combat is micromanagement and becomes stagnant quickly. Enemies appear out of nowhere artificially adding difficulty to missions but removing any immersion. The game looks amazing, but it's just a smooth coat of paint over a rusted interior. The conflict between the nations was interesting, the backstory, the magic. The main characters are generic stoic stereotypes and largely differentiated only by their specific weapons/skills. Their personalities could be swapped and you'd not know or care. Square-Enix has a long, amazing history, but they are riding on it to cash in on cheap shallow games like this, Various Daylife and so on. If you want to try this, wait for a sale and expect to grind out the game in spite of the repetition and lack of feeling toward any of the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game to review.  I'll start with 2 statements and then elaborate.  This is fun game that is worth playing BUT it is not a perfect game.  This is really more of a 7/10.Diofield does a lot of things well and interestingly.  It makes you think about which characters you want to focus on and spend your time.  A lot of strategy RPGs you'll tend to train up your entire army or at least a significant portion of it.  Diofield is more about making you think which characters fit your playstyle and focus on them.  It offers a lot of different ways to customize your army in weapons, skills, and super abilities, but you simply cannot do it all so you HAVE to pick and choose, which is surprisingly refreshing.  Combat is pretty fast paced, to the point where there were a couple times I honestly wouldn't have complained if it was a little slower.  But again, all good.Plotwise the game is about on par with most strategy RPGs.  There's a plot inbetween levels but its mostly exposition and recap so it can move on to the next battle.  Think even with early Fire Emblem or Ogre Battles (note I said Ogre Battle, not Tactics Ogre, which has a strong plot.)My complaints are largely things that could probably be easily QoL patched away.  Too much dialogue is unskippable.  While this isn't an issue with your first time through, even on a single playthrough there replay mission options (to grind/level your characters) and if you redo a mission you have to redo all the dialogue/cutscenes with it, which seem completely unnecessary and easily fixable by just giving a skip option.  My other complaint would be that while I do like how the game makes you focus on a specific team and there are several options to choose from that are good, there are also some options that are just flat out bad.  They're fairly obvious if you take a few minutes to actually review what all the different skills are but it still begs the question of why having those options in the first place when there are far superior options available.At the end of the day, if you love playing tactical RPGs and are looking for a new one to play, Diofield is definitely worth your time.  If you're brand new to tactical RPGs this might not be the best entry point.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually a bit surprised that the game is getting negative reviews, frankly I'm loving it. Granted I don't really play RTS or any kind of tactical games, heck I don't even really care for Fire Emblem, but I'm really loving this game. I don't think the visuals are "sub-par" at all, not sure if people just have mediocre GPU's or PC's/monitors or what. I will admit the story isn't anything groundbreaking, but I'm still enjoying it enough. The combat is...well to me it doesn't feel difficult, I'm playing on normal and I have only really restarted a fight two times because one of my units died, and I just got to chapter two. There are A LOT of things that the game has for the player to upgrade, things you basically have to grind out, collect materials to get better things, etc. I can see how that might feel tedious to some players, you have to amass gold, resources, and things get more expensive as you progress, so it feels like you won't be able to afford stronger upgrades/equipment later on. I was reading some of the negative reviews and I just completely disagree, and it seems I'm in the minority because from what I'm seeing several people seem to agree the game is mediocre and not worth $60, it's ironic because I don't even really play tactical games and yet I'm having a blast. I didn't "hate" Fire Emblem, but it didn't seem to keep my interest like this game is doing. Anyway, the visuals don't seem bad to me, I have everything on max at 1440p and it looks fine, 100-120 FPS, no lag or dips. Combat is simplistic, but the game gives you lots of different weapons, skills, units, and ways you can build your party and approach combat. I don't know what people were really expecting, some are saying the game feels "unfinished" and I'm not sure where that is coming from? Some are saying the game doesn't have a tutorial and doesn't explain how anything seems to work, which isn't true. The game does kind of just thrust you into combat, but there is a help section that explains in detail what each stat does, and what each status effect does. It should be self-explanatory in all honesty. For example, Provoke...what do you think Provoke does? Taunts the enemy. Burning, what does Burning do? Applies a DOT to the enemy. Poison? Same thing, it's a DOT. Might? Raises attack power of allies. Wither? Lowers enemy defense. I'm just saying, this should really not be hard to understand, but some people seem to be struggling with how to apply these effects, or what they do when the meaning is in the name. I'm not even trying to come off as a jerk or smart ass, it's just like a lot of people have never played an RPG or something. I'm just not seeing the complaints that others apparently have with the game, and that's coming from someone who doesn't even really play tactical based games, so maybe I'm just naive on what to expect out of a RTS or any kind of tactical genre game. I'd say the game so far is an easy 8/10 for me, at least. I've noticed one guy said the game is "laughably easy" and I must admit, as I said earlier, the game really doesn't feel hard but I don't see that as a valid reason to give a negative rating/score. Difficulty in my eyes has nothing to do with the game's quality, I guess if it's too easy it'll be boring for some people, but I guess we can't all be badasses who want a difficulty that just one shots your units if they get poked with a pillow.

_childDocuments_.review: Diofield had so much potential and saying it fell flat is an understatement. This game is worth around $20-$25 max, not the full price. They tried to make Fire Emblem 3 Houses (even with the story) and they did not succeed. Unless this has a sequel, it is a wildly incomplete story. I'd argue even then, it has a lot of problems and I'm not sure what they would do after this one. It's like everyone on the development team wanted to take part in the story line and it led to a confusing story, characters I tried really, really hard to like and overall just a game that fell flat. The only reason I saw this through to completion was because I had passed the two hours for a refund and was going to try to get my moneys worth at that rate.I was really excited with the demo and had a lot of hope going into it despite the negative reviews. After just finishing the game around 30 hours I can absolutely confirm everything everyone else has said is completely accurate. I hit Chapter 4 around 20 hours and expected the game would last longer but the final chapters are about 10 hours at best. I had started off on the hardest difficulty but where the gameplay was grindy and repetitive I cranked the volume down to casual just for the sake of getting through the game, which I'm aware could contribute to the last bit only being 10 hours but even on the highest difficulty, I'm not sure the game would have gone past 35 hours. Even on hard though, it really wasn't challenging (as long as you're using skills and checkpoints properly). I come from playing every Fire Emblem on loop so while I understand there are differences, I'm usually fine with repetitive game play and this just became too much for me. This was my first time with RTS so I didn't mind the game play, but I feel saying I didn't enjoy how repetitive it was would be unfair to some degree. It's a mixed feeling.I planned on giving this a positive/mixed review until the ending. The story line already took a lot to get started and then fell apart completely in the middle, but I had hopes the ending would at least salvage it. It did not. There were some technical glitches. Audio would bug out in parts and the story would continue but it wasn't the end of the world. Do not buy this at full price. It is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much the same as other reviews. It's not a tactical game, it's a top-down Final Fantasy RPG consisting of 4 "units" (party members) that utilizes the same summons, techniques, and archtypes in a very narrow and linear upgrade map. For much of the game I just steamrolled it on hard difficulty, the items received for accomplishing things like "Completing a map under 6 minutes" eventually became negligible quickly. I still haven't acquired a Claw or Firearm type 20 hours in but it seemingly doesn't matter. Rias, Fredret, Donavar, Izzie, Quin, Sivat, Rickles,  and Isca who you get early are all you need to complete the game rather easily; the rest of the cast that will trickle down has absolutely no meaning. The story is bland, you're mercenaries, then you're also mercenaries, and you keep being mercenaries. You start with Bahamut as a Summon and you basically just keep using him as the others have relatively no value over his output. Interesting concept,  but not thought out or executed nearly well enough.Edit: I'm pretty bored at this point, i don't know if i'll make it all the way through the game. It's fine for a game to play in between working-from-home mindlessly or something. Wait for the discount like others are suggesting, it's a nice premise that has you thinking you'll be hooked...just drops off a cliff rather quickly from the initial excitement.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it, it's a fun game so far. I don't LOVE it, but I do like it. The battle system is fun and intuitive, they did a good job with that. The skills system is also well done, and if you're into lore and backstory, there's a whole "library" system you can delve into if you're into that. Things that aren't so great, well, the main story is a little weak so far. It's pretty basic, not a lot of complexity. Similarly, the characters are also pretty 1D, and the dialogue is weak, to say the least. Hopefully these things improve later in the game, but I'm about 5 hrs in so far, and it's not looking promising. In my playthrough so far, I'm also noticing that the game is just very EASY. Most maps my guys are a good 4 levels higher than enemies, which really trivializes a lot of the fight mechanics. I think this game had a lot of potential that wasn't fully realized, which is a shame, because the bones of the game are solid. It's just missing that wow factor. I also think the game is a bit overpriced for what it is. I paid $80CAD, and realistically, I'd say this should be closer to the $60-65 range.I'd give this about a 7/10, and while I DO find the game enjoyable for the most part, I would recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with this game and do not regret my deluxe edition pre-order with artbook and soundtrack. It is a solid entry to a new IP and I fully hope to see additions soon. Short and sweet it does not require heavy grinding or microtransactions, further there are no traps or puzzles purely implemented to add hours to game time.So why the negative reviews? I believe it might be a case of the game being easy to hate and hard to like. If one of the shortcomings annoys you sufficiently it would be quite difficult to recover and continue the game because the likes are not strong enough to recover.So my hopes are with this review to give you an idea of the shortcomings without spoilers so you can best decide if the game is for you. Comments on what the price should be and 'marks out of 10' are subjective so I have not done this here.StoryThe story is enjoyable and it was a pleasure to guess motives of some characters. This is certainly not a game full of Tropey McTrope faces that scream at the main character every 5 seconds to notice their trope. There are a few plot twists which appear as a surprise.Some problems are the full story is not fully present in the main quests so if the player does not talk to people in the HQ between missions or consult the library there will be blanks (yes, the game would be awesome if this was present yet there never is enough money to do everything), the ending does set up for DLC/sequel which could leave a few unhappy and finally of some characters leaving part way through (this is not the type of game where everyone hates each other and then just one magical word by the main character has everyone dance into the sunset. You are a mercenary force at the end of the day. Further it is possible to recover from this by replaying missions for levels and money).Strategy and combatThe combat is workable, if a little bit simplistic. Even if I really try to put everything in the game's favour, the depth is only surface level. I cannot find out enough about the developer to know if this is a conscious choice or a lack of funding.Terrain does not really make a difference here and units cannot be positioned beforehand. Each weapon has its own skill set which the user can exploit. Skills can be improved by research. Every character has a weapon slot and two accessories, by end game you will have to make a choice between one or two items.There are few main classes and a lot of recruitable characters. Once you have an idea of what really fits your playstyle, or a workable squad of 4, do not expect to move out of the configuration.Expect to meet most goals with little difficulty once you have a few levels, I would argue that this is the fruit of the player's hard work. This isn't the case where enemy health grows in line with player damage so you end up doing 2 million damage instead of 2 hundred, yet all the battles take the same time. Bosses are also on the easy side in this game, yet I love it for this. Not every single game has to have bosses with 20 health bars that require 45 minutes to beat, split millisecond response times and can one shot the player.Music and soundsThe music is lovely. Absolutely no complaints and I listen to several soundtracks away from the game. The main battle theme is a bit funny, the horn guy went to town with the 'blaaaarrrrhhh' sounds. You could even say he went to war ... hahaha (yeah, not funny I know).The character voices are just passable. Voice artists and processing can be expensive. About 50% of the lines almost sound text to speech, 10% of what is left could do with further processing as it is obvious the actor is in a booth or levels have been capped.GraphicsAre we really going to judge strategy games on graphics? Maps are well modelled, the HQ is workable, characters animated well and battle scenes good.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely clunky controls that often overwrite other commands, inability to remember selected units, nonsensical control schemes that cross between asdf type hotkeys > mouse > arrow keys, some menus use clicks others use z/x/c. Story is probably the worst I've ever played. It's very hard to ignore it when a character in one cutscene asks to join and in the next cutscene it says invited or one scene says they don't trust her and the next says earned their trust.Overall game is unpolished, poor story/narration/theme, bad voice acting which constant....slow speaking.......narration. Avoid unless a major patch is applied.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: This review would have spoilers , and if you are those that minds it alot maybe read someone else's review.The combat and story settings were all fine , its nothing groundbreaking, it has a few interesting characters, most things has voice lines and its not stellar , it gets the job done , so far so good.What made this into a ok game to a not good one is that , you lose characters along the way , due to story reasons the character simply leave. Normally its fine since you can somewhat replace the unit, but the game wants you to treat them as characters , yet they ended up as units.Pile that you pick and choose one unit over the other because it has better skills that suits your build , and you tech towards them , just like every other strat game , you build around your team , now half way through the game you lose someone "for reasons" , all the tech towards that tree is in essence wasted. Then later down the road it happens again.Combat tried to be something else , but it ended up like this : group buff - group enemies up - aoe everything down.The story itself later on just simply not make sense , the identity of the unit changes within the same chapter when you talk to different characters , one day we are the king's guard , next line we are back to mercs , the next we someone do charity out of the MC's good heart ? At this point you can imagine how strange and out of place things are going to be.Every so called "mission" is copy pasta unit spawn kill things , same units same setups , same handful of maps , it goes down in quality / placement as chapters goes on , not to mention you would kill a purple dragon on a side quest, get an achievement for it , next chapter , kill the same said dragon on a different map , and the characters would go "OMG what is that !", like ... come on ...TLDR , game has serious identity crisis , it tries to be something different , but lacking in every way in the end , all the while not play coherently as a whole.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest concern with this game is the story. It feels like reading a book with every second page ripped out.The fights are decent even though they end up being very repetitive. In between you control the main character to interact with the other party members. This very sparsely used to convey information and could be replaced with a menu. Many aspects like this seem to be influenced by Fire Emblem but they are not well put together.The control schema is optimized for a controller with support for keyboard and mouse. This results in an RTS style game that feels somewhat clunky to control.The game itself has been completely bug-free for me. If you get this at a discount, do not care at all for any story and just want to play some fights with a controller then this might suit you. For me however I feel that this was not a good investment of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered this game and because I have some weird curse where every game I pre-order turns out to be yugely disappointing I did not have high hopes. I didn't touch it for several weeks after it came out because "oh but what if it's bad." I did not play 13 Sentinels for nearly THREE YEARS for similar reasons.Let me just say, this is one of the few games I've played where my gut instincts were entirely correct: I was wooed by the dreamy character designs into pre-purchasing and I went into this baby blind. What I found was a surprisingly gripping political story with an entertaining cast ranging from perfectly likable average Janes and Joes to morally gray weirdos to outright Not Good people but I ended up loving all of them in one way or another. The game is like some weird love letter to Yiazmat mixed with a little bit of FE's focus on character writing, with ASOIAF's morality tiers and cynicism. To top it off the voice acting is unironically really great for a video game and it feels weird to say that post-2015 but here we are. The deliveries were for the most part natural and did not read as "video game voice acting" 99% of the time. Maybe I'm just easily impressed by British accents, idk. The gameplay is ~fine~ and is pretty standard RTS fare with most of the strategery hinging on character movement. It's been a hot minute since I've played it but I do remember it being a little... tedious. Let's just say the gameplay is the least of what I remember about this game.As far as I know this is the only game in existence with Waltaquin (or as I call her, WaltaQUEEN) so it's an automatic recommend for her alone. I love everything about this crazy woman. I support everything she wants and everything she does. #WaltaquinDidNothingWrong.  Legitimately I think the world would be a better place if every video game had a character like her in it. But anyway~I recommend it if you like character-focused SRPGs like Fire Emblem or 13 Sentinels. Definitely was better than I thought it would be, but I went in expecting absolutely nothing, lmao. Also recommend if you like ASOIAF or other political fantasy games like FFT, FF12, or Ogre Battle. The plot's a little too convoluted and moves a little too fast sometimes but I liked it overall. A solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Diofield is an interesting concept marred with serious issues.Real time battles are fun, and can be pretty flashy - but don't have enough strategic depth to carry this title.I picked my 'fantastic four' and on normal difficulty - easily steamrolled though campaign (that becomes noticably easier as you level up and learn powerful skill synergies).On the narrative front - game is an unmitigated disaster. At high level - story might have some general direction, but never rises above being serviceable. Whole base camp section fo Diofield is laughably bad. Characters look like taken from PS2 era, with stiff animations and cheap design. VO and dialogues quality is equally bad. Bottom line - Diofield looks and feels like an indie game, that never, ever should be sold for full price.If you're interested in SRPGs - pick up Triangle Strategy - that is far superior title.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. I liked the tactical combat. It's the first time I tried something like this. I wish they could remake Final Fantasy Tactics with this type of battle system. Also the story in this game is pretty great, that was another thing that kept me playing. Very beautiful visuals with the usual Square Enix RPG elements. 8.5/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: I'm LOVING the game so far. Excellent gameplay, with a very unique RTS approach and a lot of upgrade options. The graphics looks great, with beautiful diorama-like battlefields and great use of shaders.  Performance is perfect on my RTX3080 at 1440p. RTX makes hair glitchy, though.I like how extremely polished the game feels. Especially in this day and age of buggy and unfinished games. _childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. I'm not finished yet and I might change my mind, but I'm whelmed. I find the game fun, but for a $60 Square title I really expected a lot more. The graphics are mediocre bordering on bad, the music is genre standard, I'm on hour ten and the first truly interesting thing to happen in the story just happened and the rest of the story is convoluted and a bit boring. Oh, and the first time I used the Battle Log I got a fatal error, so I guess that's one way to restart the battle. The gameplay is pretty fun and the interesting thing that just happened in the story is pretty darn interesting, but this just seems really unpolished and kind of a half-assed effort.Edit: I finished. It didn't get any better. _childDocuments_.review: I really like this game a lot, great new franchise, just wished there wasn't a reward for finishing the missions in less than four minutes, makes me feel rushed and not really be able to take in the splendor of the environments IMO. Great cast and amount of usable characters, easily one of the best new IPs for SE, my favorite developers and publishers!

_childDocuments_.review: *UPDATE*After completing every side mission and watching every cut scene, I beat the game in roughly 30-35 hours.  For those that say this has a non existent story or lack luster characters, I feel like that's incorrect.  While not super deep story and gameplay-wise, the story has a nice twist.  Some characters could be fleshed out more.  And, yes... the game is very easy, even on hard.  I never once did not complete the mission within the bonus limit and even had to die and revive on purpose to get the achievement.  The game definitely needs some balancing.  I still like the game and recommend it (though wait for a sale).  It's a 7/10 for me.  There's also a new game plus+ (enemies do not scale).  There are some hints at a sequel, but considering people are bombing it, I'm not sure that will happen.*initial reviewRTS style SRPG with tons of the latters tropes including weapons, accessories, armor, and shields.  However, you can upgrade skills and have ultimate-like skills; think Final Fantasy and spells like Bahamut.  There's also skill trees for classes that can be upgraded.  Almost like FFVII:Remake or Stranger of Paradise weapon upgrades.  Positioning can be very (and should be) tactical.  This is not so much a turn based tactical RPG like Fire Emblem, but more like a real-time with pause a la Pillars of Eternity or Kingmaker, but with quick, short burst maps.A couple of things that are annoying.  There's no cloud saves and the game goes not support ultra-wide (not sure why I thought this would, because SE always fails here).  Also, there are timers if you want to achieve special bonuses (I hate timers, but I understand that this is real-time).  Though, time does get paused when you open a menu/command.  I also have crashed twice so far, once during a cut scene and once exiting the game.  One more thing to note is that there is some X-com like clipping, aka shooting through walls.Mouse and keyboard feels a little more natural, but controller is excellent as well.  Only parts of the game are narrated, with voice being sparse like modern day aforementioned Fire Emblem.Truly recommended as this is compelling and unique.  I think Square has a great foundation here.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great with some issues, and a unique take on the RTS genre. Combat feels fresh even if it's an amalgamation of prior systems. The game feels unfinished in some aspects, and definitely could have benefited from more time to iron out the kinks or expand upon existing systems. $60 dollars for the base game feels a bit high in it's current state, but I personally don't feel bad about my purchase at it's current asking price. I would recommend waiting for a sale if this is the final build and they move on.. But if you read the pro's and con's and are still interested - I don't think you'll be upset spending full price. It's a solid concept game, with very fun combat, and I hope they expand upon it.1. Combat is extremely addictive.2. Full control of 4 characters in battle at all times. With access to 15 or so characters you get in reserves to swap in and out of the main party. (Might be off on the actual number off the top of my head but around there.) Each character feels different enough because of their passives you can unlock.3. Seamless control over all decisions and actions you assign.4. Unique take on the equipment, skill, and party systems.-Skills: All have upgrades to add further abilities or stats.-Weapons: Which all come with certain skills you have to pick and choose from to take with you into battle.-Team Composition: Lots of freedom with builds and ability to choose how you want to play. (Though one character/skill reigns dominant over everything else atm.)1. The story is hit or miss. I personally enjoyed it, but i'm weird and I like political drama. It's short and concise, but feels convoluted and bland if you don't like macro-politics. It's obviously nothing groundbreaking, but fun if you're into this sort of thing. Also don't expect everything to make complete sense. IE: Every characters motives to be understood. Took me till about chapter 3 to dig the story. 2. If you can't get into the story, the characters can feel unimportant or just there. It took me a while to get warmed up to them. There is some backstory to most characters you meet in short segments at your home base, but don't expect anything completely fleshed out. 3. The game feels like a feeler project honestly. It's obviously a side project, and feels like square isn't confident about it's decisions on what people will like. This game has a great concept and foundation, and should've felt more confident about dumping more time, money, and energy into it. It could have been leagues better.4. The balance is . By the middle of the game, enemies might as well be ants and you Thanos with the Infinity Gauntlet. This problem is even worse by the end of the game, not to even mention NG+. The weapons, skills, and abilities you have access to completely annihilate everything. It's fun at first, but hard mode might as well be kids mode. This is the biggest issue I have with the game, and imo needs to be the first thing patched.5. Some QoL UI management issues that are common place in other RTS games. IE: When opening up the skill menu in battles, it defaults to what seems like random party members or the last used(?) instead of just the current controlled character. Very annoying and definitely a "why" moment.. But things like this.6. Lastly, i've run into a couple bugs that have soft-locked the game or made certain characters freeze entirely throughout the rest of the battle. Seems to originate from certain skills, but hard to replicate.All in all, I really enjoy this game. I hope they have an upcoming patch scheduled to fix some of these issues or add content that feels like it should be there and isn't. I rate this game a 7.5/10 in it's current state, but if they give this game more attention with a patch i'd say it could easily be a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after beating the game and completing all achievements in 40+ hours. I'm not sure whether to suggest it at its current pricing because I don't believe it's on par with other AAA games that justify a price like this. But if you're like me and have some extra cash and nothing better to do these days, you may as well give it a shot and have a few days of fun. Otherwise, don't bother right now.The plot is uninteresting, which goes against my expectations for a SE game. Numerous story twists emerge unexpectedly, with no foreshadowing till after the event. The characters were average. I only felt emotionally linked to one of the characters, The Queen Waltaquin, what also kept me going and finish the game. And going through any other characters story arcs with the side missions didn't seem rewarding became a drag at that point.Nonetheless, I must add that Diofield's character portrait artwork style, as well as the aesthetics and presentation for each map before battle, seemed flawless and fresh to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is good. The 4 unit minimum really starts to hit when you start unlocking more units. I found myself in a meta of sorts with combat. Utilizing some skills and crowd control, I found fatal funneling most of the maps was the way to go. At 30hrs now, i believe and almost done with the game. Played on hard mode and it really wasn't too bad. The story is lackluster to be honest. I wanted more, it wasn't bad. However, the story wasn't something that stood out like crazy. Most of the twists and turns are seen way to early due to dialogue (but if you skip dialogue, then it might be a surprise?)Graphics are fine, to be fair its not a triple Alpha game coming out with crazy ray-tracing and human life like graphics.My biggest complaint about the game is wanting more. I really wanted to get into some of these fights and have to scratch my brain and have to think about how to take on the map. However, most of the time I just needed like 3-4 skills and kind of steam rolled most encounters. If they plan on releasing more games like this, id purchase still, but I really want more brain usage. A fun ride nonetheless. If this game is not your style, wait for sale. It is still worth playing for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I had pre ordered this game thinking that it had Final Fantasy Vibes and would be an RPG game with Strategy such as Spell Force series.As for the The game carries the artwork familiar with SNES Final Fantasy series and updated that blends in the visual sprites with artwork.The combat battles are interesting enough and allows for enough combination to be fun.There are weapon and customization items and weapon development, but it does not seem to affect that prominent on the avatars of your characters.A "coolup/cooldown" weapon reminiscent of is present which does present nostalgic vibesThe overall story is captivating although with some caveats (explained in the cons)There are very few game crashing bugs, and I only had my game stall one time in 11 hours playthrough.As for the The story is quite linear and does not allow even any options to agree or admonish the actions of people in your roster.  It would have felt more custom if there was a relationship boost earned overtime with characters (or negative) and thru dialogue can shift the story in other directions. Furthermore, there is not even the option to kick out or decline people from joining the mercenary company.The focus of the mercenary company is quite linear in line with the overall game and does not allow to pick an alignment-based choice on each scenario.  Main characters say their peace but then proceed to keep moving on as if nothing matter and condones both good and reprehensible behavior as of Chapter 3 of this writing.The maps do become tiring at some point offer no destruction of the surrounding area which would have given the game a more lived in feel.The price point for this seemed high and disappointing and for what the game delivers is warranted more of a 39.99.   If you must pick this game, wait until a summer/holiday sale when its -50%.I hope this helps with consideration of this game and I will update this review on completion.

I have only played the game 4 hours so I don't know the whole story yet.)Graphics: 6/10 (The graphics looks good, however some characters in the game looks off/weird when they talk/react in cinematic scenes)Overall, the game is good, but little too expensive for what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as tactical JRPGs go this is very meh at 60 dollars, compared to Final Fantasy Tactics Advance & FFTactics w/Ramsa and Delita. The hybrid RTS Tactical RPG combat system makes gameplay stop & go. Tactical games or RTS games have better gameplay flow than this. Mashed together its poop. The depth of combat options is shallow due to being limited to 4 classes (8 if you bother using the fake Pair Up mechanic) and all characters not being created equal. Characters of the same class fill different roles due to the abilities that have preassigned. Character who fill the same role do not grow in stats the same. Some roles are only filled by 1 character.   The story is aggressively mediocre. But a mediocre game for 30 dollars? Decent get.
