_childDocuments_.review: My expectations for DioField were honestly too high. I was hoping for a more robust experience but even with those shortcomings I still recommend the game if you're able to get it on discount.The story can lean on tropes and have a level of predictability, but the way they handle cinematics between missions can also alleviate that by only giving you the information you need. A character might be mentioned by name but you won't get any more information than relevant to the story or to their character. On the other side of that coin just be aware there will also be a feeling of missing content where the game sets you up like you're going on some expedition that might take weeks. They mention the stress of splitting your party and you think you'll have multiple missions with these 2 groups. Not the case at all. You get 1 mission a piece and a small cutscene to bring the group back together.The combat is fun. It's easy, don't get me wrong, but this is the majority of the game and it feels good to play. The abilities are satisfying to use and the weapon upgrades give you noticeable damage boosts. My biggest gripe is that you're really limited in how you combine those abilities. There isn't a huge amount of weapon diversity and abilities are bound to those weapons. You don't learn abilities any sort of way to carry them over to mix and match at will which can make you pigeon hole yourself into only using the same abilities for a type of unit. Map design is okay but gets repetitive when you start getting later in the game and do many of the side quests. There isn't really that much enemy diversity either. Bosses can be unique with different abilities of their own but they telegraph for so long that the only way you get hit is if you just don't do anything at all.The ending of the game had a cliffhanger feel to it, so I anticipate the story will be completed at a later date whether it be paid or free DLC but the bones are here for a good experience. I would just taper your expectations. This is like a 6/10 game you should by on sale to kill 20-30 hours if you pay attention to all the cutscenes. There is a new game plus mode but carrying over your levels and equipment means you can clear the following playthrough in a matter of a day.

_childDocuments_.review: An odd mix of FF Tactics and Fire Emblem (Three Houses and THAT specific style of game)Overall I would say it's got a lot of shine, and a lot of meh. Graphics are amazing, you can pretty much crank everything and appreciate the glory of DX12 and Ray Tracing, or just sit a a cozy HIGH fps. I can't say it maxes out easily, as I run a 3090, and I doubt most people playing this genre of game went that overboard on a GPU (I have it for work, NOT GAMING ffs) but it def runs great and looks great even with the graphics turned down a bit.Audio is really good. The music is fun and fitting, but the ambiance is just annoying. I turned off Ambiance, and I left it running in the background half the day and it was relaxing. _childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this if you're looking for a coherent and complete story or any character building. Hell, even if you just liked the demo gameplay (like me), don't buy it until it's on a deep discount (75% at least). I regret paying full price for this game because it wasn't worth it.There are many story threads that start but never finish. The writers never make you care about any of the characters. In fact, the primary drivers of the story are awful people. A lot of story threads are started and never finished. There is an especially egregious story thread involving one of the main characters that is never explained or wrapped up. Maybe in the next game? Going into the finale of the game, you're just dropped into the final battle with the final boss. And then you see an ending scene that made my partner and I both go, "Wait, that was it?" at the same time.I started off doing all of the side missions until I realized that none of them actually do anything worthwhile. At some point in the game, you're already trivializing every battle, so the side missions are just time wasters to pad the game's length. Similarly, the narrator repeats, word-for-word, everything that just happened after each major story beat. It's aggravating that they had nothing more to say than exactly what you had just done.

_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: DioField Chronicle is a game that is tough to love.  The one thing that it does very well is that the developers have taken their time to innovate new systems and ways to enjoy a main genre in RPGs.  The art style does leave little to be desired but the gameplay style is very addicting once you get the hang of it.  The one thing I love about this game is that you really have to consider how you approach the battles.  This isn't about navigating within a grid like strategy games of yesterday, this is real time, and every move that you consider can either lead to victory or your downfall.  I'd only recommend this to fans of strategic RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing tactics title that blends the enjoyable mechanics of a traditional grid turn-based tactical Japanese SRPG with real-time combat.  Though comparisons are often made to an RTS, this title was apparently influenced more by MOBA combat mechanics and that shows with the 4-unit squad and abilities that can be unleashed during combat.  Music is quite stellar and contributes to the story and combat sequences.  While not for everyone, Diofield Chronicle is a solid entry in the tactical RPG genre
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR- DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL OR NEAR FULL PRICE ($60), probably wait until a deep sale.Demo was decent as a showcase, so I purchased the game on release; hoping there would be more depth in the combat and delve into the story. I was wrong. The game-play started out with 60% of the tools the player would use, and by the halfway mark you've seen all there is to see. As materials become purchasable from the vendor, the weapon tree tapers off into one "best-in-slot" weapon for each class, and the characters double-up on the classes; railroading the player into a "surefire" specific 4-by-4 party setup for most battles, where you wall-to-wall pull enemies and cc'd them down.Character portraits are well-designed, but the 3d models are rough to say the least (Standard UE Run animation bugged me once I noticed it).The story is weak, with certain elements I was hoping would evolve into bigger characters based conflicts, but said characters just give-up after awhile when there is a clash of ideals with always one-side winning (Monarchy). Once you see the first hint of a interesting character conflict resolve itself by one party just dropping the subject, the companion story missions become padding.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10It's a great RTS/Tactics game for people who aren't great at RTS/Tactics games.On normal mode, it isn't hard to meet all of the objectives of every battle if you have a basic grasp of formation (ie: know to keep your ranged fighters out of melee range, to get some units behind the enemy for ambush damage, to use stun attacks to cancel an enemy's big moves) and it's not hard to meet at least some of the objectives of every battle by rushing in and healing like mad.The story is nothing to write home about, but it's still a Square Enix title so the characters at least seem interesting enough that it's worth talking to them to hear what they have to say even if it never quite turns into masterpiece theatre.Do I think it worth £50? Well, I'd rather have paid £35, but I also think I'm going to play this for longer than some games I've paid £35 for, so in a roundabout way, I'd have to say yes, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing game play for once. Sure its not amazing graphics wise or mouth movements, or a new story we havnt heard before. Its more about the game you get to play. A new tactics style RPG or live action tactics you could say. Its really something to build on moving forward. This is what most of us gamers want these days. A fresh start to a new game style. Maybe not everyone but most of us want something new in a way of gameplay not more of the same clones we have been getting for 15 years now

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:Decent strategy game for a brand new IP from SE. Play the demo first and/or wait for a sale.Combat is real-time, but you can pause by selecting your units to give yourself time to think about your plan of action. If you mess up, you can use the checkpoint system through "Battle Logs". Okay variety in skills where you can mix-and-match via weapons, accessories, and character supports but leaves much to be desired in overall complexity and even on Hard, difficulty was a breeze. Once I had a decent team synergy, I felt no reason to change my team throughout the whole playthrough as the game doesn't have a wide enough variety of enemies to warrant a change in playstyle.Story is so-so and is a fairly typical, linear JRPG with some twists here and there that don't always make sense or make for a compelling story. Voice acting is also okay, but I had several "serious" or "climactic" moments ruined by the English voice actors' line deliveries. Not everything is voiced and there are many parts that just have characters grunt, say the same 1-2 words, and many enemy voicelines are the same if they're from the same faction. I was genuinely interested in the setting, but messy storytelling didn't do it justice.There is "New Game+" but I don't see much replayability unless you enjoy the combat or try out some new builds and play other characters. It's really easy to get 100% achievements and doesn't require NG+.Recommending based solely on that I enjoyed playing the game, combat, and was interested enough in the story to bare with it. I would play more games in this franchise. I don't think this game deserves a $60 price tag and is closer to a $40 game, so try the demo first and/or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: my recommendation comes with a caviat (steam needs a middle of the road option...):the game is way, way, way overpriced; which is sadly kinda normal for Square nowadaysit's a very basic realtime with pause tactical rpgyou command a squad of 4 active characters, which you can supplement with another 4 side characters by "equipping" one member of the main squad with another char which offers slight stat-boni and some skills the "offchar" got, also the secondary char will gain exp (diminished)combat runs in realtime, but you can pause at any moment. selecting chars (all or specific chars), creating waypoints, chosing special active abilities or items will all pause the game. in essence this allows for snappy gameplay while still feeling like some tactics are needed (imagine a boss charging an attack, you pause-enter your menu and chose the right interrupt ability for example). don't expect Tactics Orge, FF Tactics and co. , but it's functional. the whole control schema is definitly made for pads, but once you get used to it, it's actualy quite fun and functional...just kinda awekward on PC.but oyu have to chose the hardest difficulty; neither balancing nor challenging encounters are a thing in this game, so even playing on normal you can just basicaly skip all the tactics, chose your whole squad, click the enemy and that's about it.when first seeing the game i was kinda enamored with it's grafical design and while in mission/combat it still holds up. it's not a fantastic looking game, but the art-style, effects and color-pallette create a nice athmosphere. however the moment you leave combat and enter the running around your HQ phase the grafics fall apart. models, enviroments and animations outside of combat are just horrific. in many instances i felt like playing some UE-asset-flip game. doesn't break the game, but it's quite questionable especialy looking at the pricing.progression works like you'd expect in these kind of games: individual units got their own equipment, stats and skills to unlock, so does your whole mercenary-company. you unlock weapon/magic, skill research along the way. weapons/items can have their own unique active and passive skills, etc. at first it looks rather basic, but the game is kinda a slow burner; once more things get unlocked you realize there's quite some build-variety here. mixing mercenary-company upgraded skills, with your active weapon skills and your 2nd chars can lead to quite unique outcomes, like having a mage who can charge->aoe-taunt->aoe-funnel->and aoe-dps a pack of mobs for example. there's quite some choice here.the plot and combat start out rather basic. melee, archers and cavalary, but soon magic and undead and monsters enter stage. which is fine gameplay wise, but the plot...dear god. parts of the plot are quite entertaining , but it's all over the place, nothing get's explained, there's no buildup, you get hammered with made-up fantasy names (no one can pronaunce these names) and the presentation leaves quite a lot to be desired. there are hand-drawn, voiced cutscenes between mainquest which are quite good, the rest is confusing, not great to look at and the VO is all over the place. some voices are pretty good, but some are just gringe on a whole nother level. as a whole i'm not surprisedas an oldschool Square (SE) fan i came to realize that modern Square is just not a great publisher anymore and most of their games are mediocre at best; which goes for this one aswell. the one thing that still rubs me the wrong way is Square's pricing policy: this is in no way shape or form a full reatil price game. for half the price it wouldn't be this bad, but looking at the price and the quality presented here i honestly question what's going at Square HQ.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I do recommend this game because I enjoyed my time playing it, but it has a lot of issues.Pros:-"Unique" battle system, a good mix of JRPG and RTS combat.  -Using skills is OP but also necessary, learning the proper combos was fun-Ability to speed up battle-Not too long but not too shortCons-Repetitive enemies there were only a small amount of enemy types in the game, they just levelled up and used more skills as the game went on.-Nonsensical/disconnected story-"Too easy" is this game easy?  Yes, if you have enough braincells to use the right skills.  Many reviews talk about how you can just spam assassination but this is not true, but the combat is easy with just the tiniest bit of logical skill usage-Lack of variety in build.  You get 12 or so characters, but they are in 4 categories of fighter and you can pair them with others to use skills so essentially the characters don't matter, you can just pick who you like the looks of on the field of battle (Outside a few that gain attribute boosts from like fighting with all women or whatever)

It's really bad design to tie the biggest DPS-er to the tank classes. I never use Mounted units because I want to use a tank along with DPS. A lot of slop from a big company. They could and should have done far better.

_childDocuments_.review: I think its an overall good game but with several flaws. It had what I would consider a good story with good characters. I really liked the voice acting with a lot of unique voices and character design. The combat is pretty unique as well and a fun and fast-paced system that takes some getting used to. Things I didnt like was the late game repetitiveness. Eventually you hit a point where you have figured out your build/team and every single battle happens the exact same way. Near the end I began to dread doing the side missions. Another big miss is the music. I think music can really elevate a game to a new level and it fails hard here. Every mission has the exact same battle music and you get bored quick of hearing it, and you will hear it a lot.Overall though, I think it is worth playing, but not for $60. I got this game way on sale for $20 and thats what I think it is worth. If you can get it for that and enjoy JRPG, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Can easily recommend during this X-mas sale (2022) for half off. If you missed the sale then wait for the next.Features a highly unique combat system with skills that actually feel like they're practicalunlike many other games in the RPG genre.Each character's unique actions also compliment others in your party so it's funto experiment with combo recipes and then finish off the enemy with a devastating summons.And you're always progressing after each battle as there's a lot to upgrade and manage.The game IS easy (as most have said) but the originality and micro-management more than make up for it.My only gripe is that the few times that the game DOES get hard it is because of attrition and you simply are not levelled or equipped well enough for the stage at hand and thus you have to grind.Grinding is where the game can begin to feel stale real fast as you are doing so in stages which you've already completed.There's no random generation of maps or enemies and you're even skipping through the same events and dialogues.Granted there are bonus achievements, per each stage, which reward extra stuff but you can usually satisfy those goals the first time through the mission.Diofield could really use a mini mission system like FF Crisis Cores.'If you can find a good discount grab 'er up; don't let all the naysayers  blind you.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fun and somewhat innovative. It's a mix of League of Legends, classic tactics games and Valkyria Chronicles if I was asked to describe it using only other games.The story is somewhat predictable but there are elements which I couldn't anticipate so I'd rate it as good.The character design is as tacky as they come and the voice acting in Japanese and English follows suit. Think Star Ocean kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ anime style but you can get over it if the gameplay if fun enough.Like other reviews stated, once you get the last tier items and maneuver around the enemies well enough, you steamroll the entire game without much challenge.Lastly, I wouldn't recommend it only because of its price. I paid Lost Eidolons 40$ CAD and it got me more than 80 hours of gamplay with 2 New Gamer+ and this one at 80$ CAD is unjustifiably expensive. There isn't nearly enough content and not much reason to replay the game.Is it good? Yeah, kinda. Would I recommend it even at 50% off? No.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like what you see, , it gives around 2 hours of content and  if you buy the game. Then you could technically still play 2 more hours before deciding on a refund. I was convinced by the demo and the game continued in exactly the same quality, no bad surprises there.What I like about the game:- amazing art direction (concept art as well as ingame designs and effects)- the UI and gameplay design. They made sure you can efficiently and easily control this on a gamepad. Can't comment on kb/m support as the gamepad support is so good I never cared to switch. At all times it is clear exactly what's going on with every unit on the battlefield, there aren't too many or too few symbols and every single one of them is polished.- once you get used to the controls and the dynamic pausing/unpausing, as well as setting waypoints on the fly, it feels like you're playing in real-time, yet have absolute precision about every decision- the difficulty of this game is mainly skill-based (until you start overleveling / overgearing, more on that later). If you're a god at microing this game will feel "too easy" at every difficulty as you will be able to avoid all threats and exploit enemies at all times. I personally dodge red and stun enemies when necessary, but had my fair share of boss fights where I was left with 1 or 2 characters standing and my heart pounding, on normal difficulty.- the story and setting is extremely generic and sometimes absurd. I list this as a pro because it seems this game doesn't try hard to be a novel, it tries to be a tactics game merely guiding you from mission to mission via some context. Most games try to disguise this fact, this game does not. Also it seems most of the characters have some low-key personality disorder which just makes it hilarious to follow their dialogue- the skill and adjutant system, although this takes a bit to figure out. Basically your characters get one skill simply by being a certain class. All other skills come from weapons (which have their own unlock tree). Via the skill tree you can only upgrade the skills provided by those weapons, you do not need to unlock them. Based on the weapon tier you get up to 3 skills + the one class skill. On top of that, each of your characters can get an adjutant assigned to them. This basically just merges two characters into one that has all the (up to 8) skills available. You can combine any classes you want like this, just to give an example you could have a tank for taunts and CC, with an adjutant capable of doing AoE damage and lifestealWhat I don't like:- By doing all side-missions you start to significantly overlevel enemies starting by act 2. It might be necessary to skip side-missions to keep the difficulty snappy.- Anime looking characters with thick British accents, I can hardly imagine something more immersion breaking (that being said, the voice acting is excellent)- The graphics are a mixed bag. Looks last-gen in most places (which is ok), but in some places they just slapped on a flat texture on the ground for an entire area and called it a day, with NO decorations whatsoever- There's this certain unit which shouts "For the Empire!" on death at full volume and the QA apparently saw no problem letting you fight 100+ of these guys back to back.- About half of the dialogue isn't voicedAbout the price tag:Initially I thought the game should be half-price or so because a lot of the systems are simplistic. But the more I play the more I realize I don't need 200 different variations of the same weapon, if they all fit in the same 3 functional group. I don't need 12 pieces of equipment if I can do the same job (picking my archetype) with 2 pieces of equipment. Even the fact that I can equip 2 pairs of shoes doesn't bother me. It's like the game designers said "OK, let's get rid all of these unnecessary complexities and limitations that do not work in favor of the game we want to create. And let's polish the remainder as much as possible". I deeply appreciate what they have done here, and whenever I think of something that could have been added to the game, I think it would have most likely made it worse by diluting the essence. Tthe game's leanness is by design, not by lack of it.All that being said, they went a bit too far in some aspects, namely the lack of audial and visual enemy variety, only half the dialogue being voiced, the lack of decorations all around. I can understand these measures to create a maximally functioning game with as little resources as possible and unlike most indie games, they definitely "saved at the right end". But then asking 60€ for it is still disrespectful. At 40€ this would have been a masterpiece.I definitely recommend the game if you enjoyed the demo and if you're looking for a distilled piece of gamedesign, without impressive yet counter-productive fluff.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: A generous 5/10. Strategy is not a word I would use here. It's sort of monotonous, and that normally doesn't bother me.Battles get repetitive and dull. Characters have the personality of an egg.Longer review: (Still not completely done with the game yet, but far along)The games story doesn't really speak to me much, nor do the characters after a certain point. I feel like we get new additions, with little more personality than their role. I can barely remember the units i USE, from how little a role they play.Some abilities didn't seem to get a proper explanation, and several events appear to come out of nowhere, with perhaps a small nod to the player about how or why it came to be. Combat itself is a little dull, and frustrating to say the least. Changing the difficulty seems to do little more than adjust damage? Which feels sort of lazy to me.Maps don't feel fun. The pause based fighting choices feel iffy at best, with the pause being inconsistent. The units don't always move where you want them to, needing to move the map around and wiggle the spot you want them to stand in. The biggest crime of them all for me, regarding the battles are that the "special criteria" are almost always:- Do it in under 6-8 minutes.- Kill everyone- Lose no one.Some missions add a little life in the form of "defend X object/person!" but those are far and few in between. What started out as a hopeful adventure, and a bit of interest, fizzled into wanting the game to simply be over, working to finish it simply so that I won't want to bore myself in the future when i inevitably forgot about why it was left incomplete. It earns a 5/10 only because I can see potential with what's been put here. But the fact that it feels like a demo that went on for too long says a lot to me...

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I really want to like this game. But after a couple hours with it it really didn't seem to get any better. My main complaints with the game are as follows:- The characters are so very dry. Like I can handle anime tropes and isekai BS, but something about the characters here was less flavorful than sawdust. I'd have honestly appreciated some more anime tropes.- Maybe the story picks up, but at least in the part I managed to play, it read like those historical accounts books you find in Skyrim.- Limiting characters to 1 class with 4 characters usable maximum in a mission was certainly a choice, but I don't know if it was a good one. The roster just doesn't seem that fleshed out, and combat gets a lil point and clicky. I don't really feel like I'm playing something, I feel like I'm watching the slowest iteration of Runescape combat with a little flash and fanfare every so often.Unless there's a serious overhaul to this, I don't think I'll be back. _childDocuments_.review: The game is an attempt by Mistwalker studios to create a Live Tactical RPG which fails. _childDocuments_.review: I'm currently 9 hours in and at this point I've played through 1 and a 1/2 Chapters of the story and have accumulated a little over 1/3rd of the Achievements.  I'm enjoying the game and I do recommend buying it if you're a fan of the genre, but I think it's fair to discuss what the game is, and isn't, so far.First off, this is not a Triple A title.  Honestly, it feels like it was originally developed for a portable system and never finished.  Sometime later they found it in the archives, dusted it off, and put it out for modern consoles/computers.  I bring this up because when you look at the game design, especially the keybindings and overall menu layout, you get the sense it was meant to be used with a controller.  Additionally, the graphics are perfectly passable but give the impression of being meant for smaller screens and less capable hardware.  The same goes for the presentation of the story and the voice acting vs subtitles.  The music is enjoyable and doesn't take away from the playable experience, meaning I keep it playing and don't have something else going instead.With that stated, this game is perfectly enjoyable tactics game done in the style of Bladestorm and other similar games.  The units fulfill multiple tactical functions, can be somewhat individually customized through skills, equipment and a sub-hero pairing system that lets you sort of combine two heroes into a single playable unit.  Combat is not rock, paper, scissors and does require you to think about positioning, routing and basic strategy.  So far I have not encountered anything overly difficult or otherwise badly designed that makes me feel like the challenge was artificially unfair.  Story wise the game offers a passable plot up to the point I've played, throwing in some political and class based intrigue.  I do like that the characters aren't all fast friends, and appear to have their own biases, opinions, etc, however the dialogue does come off stilted at times and, as mentioned before, the story presentation is somewhat limited.  On the other hand,  the game play has had me going back for just one more round a couple of times so far, so I focus more on the various battles than I do the less than engrossing storyline.Straight up - This game is not a $60 game, it's a $40 game.  You'll definitely get your money's worth at $40 and happily pass the time waiting for another title to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: First Off - WARNING: No cloud saves. I didn't think to even look before purchasing as I had this in mind for the Steam Deck. So that's disappointing.So far it seems alright. I came in with tempered expectations and so far it's fine. I am enjoying the story so far. It is a political type story with great presentation, when there is exposition it always has a overview map showing where the armies are moving and exactly what is happening. The voice acting is probably my favourite thing so far, although for some reason they went out of their way to completely scuff secondary conversations.So here is a bit of a rant about something that seems small, but they went out of their way to do this and I cant fathom why. Normally in a game it's fine if they don't want to voice act  conversation, so they don't. Minor conversations consist of just text. Sometimes games will have a generic voice line the character says when you start talking to them, then the rest of the text only conversation is silent. This is also fine. However, DioField chose to have these conversations where the character says a random generic line EVERY time a new text line is presented. So now your brain is hearing a random VA line while you're trying to read different text. It's really weird and totally immersion breaking. Back to the review, graphics are fine, nothing amazing. Gameplay is meh, seems like it will get old. Battles aren't very strategic, but the defence missions change it up a bit. Skill progression is confusing, you have to pay SP to unlock skills, but after paying for them I still don't have them, but I'll have other skills that I have not yet unlocked. I think it's tied to the weapons, but it seems weird that I cannot access the skill I have unlocked. Overall I would give it a 6/10 so far. Probably one of those games you'll get down the road on a 70% off sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a disappointment for me. The combat system is meh. It isn't terrible, but it isn't great either. The controls are the real trouble. Too often it isn't selecting the character I want, and there is no pause button unless you go into a characters menu. The issues with selecting the correct character created enough frustration for me that it made the combat significantly less enjoyable.Outside of combat the story was, in a word, bad. Nothing made sense and I had no idea what the big picture was, or why anything was happening. The main characters seemingly become very important people immediately for no well explained reason. Maybe it would have cleared up had I made it farther into the game, but there was just so little for me to enjoy in the 2 hours I played that I didn't have the motivation to continue.Graphically the game looks pretty good. It supports Ray Tracing, but if you turn it on certain combinations of AA will cause the game to look like trash. Music is pretty generic fantasy.Since the games release two months ago there has not been a single patch for bugs or anything else. Likely this game will not receive any support at all from Enix which is normal for them on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game to completion just to get the perfect completion, not because I liked it. The reason I bought this game originally was that I tried the demo and loved it. Sadly everything that was to be seen, was in the demo. Having been a fan of JRPGs and SRPGs this was right up my alley, it had potential but it fell short. So I will rate it a 2 out of 5. Something I am very sad to do, in many ways. My reasons for scoring and why I chose are below. Visuals - 1/5The characters and enemies are lovely sprites that are full featured. The backgrounds are beautiful and reminiscent of actual towns and villages. Gameplay - 0.5/5It is simple to learn but after a few maps it blends sadly. The variety is limited. Replay ability - 0/5It has none, I see no point in actually grinding once you have gotten the core items. At that point in all honesty you are just grinding to get one of the achievements. Story - 0.5/5It has some variety and negligible twists and turns but it got boring rather quickly due to the lack of interest and surface level character depth. Depth of Gameplay - 0/5This is a compound rating including the story, gameplay and parts of what to me makes an RPG. They were all lackluster, I would say for the same price you could have gotten 3 games with much more enjoyment than this title ever could. The item/weapon/armor crafting was extremely limited and this was in line of determining your skills. Thus it became repetitive a mere thought of how many skills can I spam to burst through the level. Would I recommend this game?Only if it was 20 dollars or less, it pains me to say it but it failed to be anything special or worthy of recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific strategy/jrpg hybrid with a few odd pacing issues that's ultimately worth the purchase. At this point I'm in the middle of Chapter 3 (over 10 hours in; it may say less but I played the demo) and greatly enjoying the story, the main characters (especially Rias and Quin), and the combat. I highly recommend playing on hard mode unless you are truly just here for story. A lot of my favorite moments have been devilishly decimating troops by combining map hazards with tripwires, kicking enemies out of formation, and the like. Surprisingly for the genre (moreso the RTS side), battles are brisk and ferocious, making it feel totally fine to give them another go for more optional objectives or blitz through a chunk of story at a fast clip.The storytelling is engaging and pulls a lot of seemingly unconnected threads together as it goes. The character developing is a little more uneven, where it feels characters jump from one part of their personality to their next stage somewhat awkwardly or without clear motivation as for the shift. Still, the characters are fun and it's especially entertaining to hear what your party's murderous magician, Quin, has to say.Rias, Isca, and Hende are unnecessarily hot. The portraits, CGs, and battlefields all look fantastic. The models... the animations are pretty stiff for a PC game this shiny. It's like everybody is an animated porcelain doll. They're fine in briefing scenes sitting around a table, but any other cutscene feels kinda odd and robotic. It's pretty at-odds with the excellent English voice acting -- except, like, a few weird ones? About half of Izzy's lines feel bizzarely delivered, for example, but thankfully the most important characters like Rias, Quin, and Lorraine are great). I haven't tried the Japanese v/a since the English one is so well acted.This game has been such a pleasant surprise. My only gripe with buying the Steam version is that I may have to get a second-hand box since I love the cover art on the physical editions!

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing is as it seems.This game has an interesting story full of twists but it doesn't earn any of them.  The justification of character actions rarely makes any sense, and that is probably because EVERY MISSION IN THE GAME IS EXACTLY THE SAME.  I will say that there is one escort mission that I remember, but guess what, you still just kill everything, collect the chest, and do it under the time limit.The most interesting character in the game is gone about mid way through, and it truly an emotional ride.  This made me really believe the rest of the story would pay off.  Other characters leave but then their love interest stays without any concern for the other.There is new game +, but why you'd bother I can't imagine.  There are no real tactics here, just go from area to area and hope enemies don't flash into existence behind you after you kill the last baddie of the bunch, this happens a lot btw.  I can't tell you how many times I moved my archer into a position I thought would be advantageous just for three enemy soldiers to appear around him (not an ambush, this is just where they were supposed to spawn).I enjoyed the story, but towards the end I just stopped doing the side quests altogether, the upgrades are meaningless past making the numbers go up.  In my mind I was hoping for Ogre Battle level of RTS strategy, but it's always FOUR characters against a horde of randomly appearing bad guys.Plot is paper thin too.

_childDocuments_.review: Over 70% of the trophies done so I think I'm close to the end so I decided to just put a review down now. I like the game, but there are some things I'd like more of if we ever get a sequel. I don't go looking out for rts type games so I don't play many and this was a breath of fresh air from all the other turn based rpgs I've played.Gameplay thoughts:I would recommend the game, but it does feel a bit lacking but I'll give them a pass since this is the first game of hopefully more. For instance you are relegated to only using 4 units at a time and that just makes the game feel very empty and not giving you much to do in combat. You can technically use 8 in that your unit can bring a backup unit which you can switch between and use their skills, but you are still forced to only have 4 on the actual battlefield at once. If the game had a bigger battlefield or even just let you use 2-4 times more people on the field I feel like it would have made the game more interesting. Story thoughts:Its fine, not great or terrible. Just a band of mercenaries trying to make a name for yourselves in your kingdom.Character thoughts:Everyone is unique from each other, but thats pretty much all it is. The quirks of the characters are quite noticeable and thats all I ever felt about them honestly.Cutscenes thoughts:The cgi needs works, all the 3d models just look like puppets/dolls and it feels like a disservice to the artwork honestly.Here is hoping we get another game in the series, or just something using the same engine cause I did enjoy the gameplay, but it just needed a little more oomph.

_childDocuments_.review: For transparency: I did receive a key to this through Square Enix's influencer program. However after beating the game after nearly 40 hours of playtime, I ended up buying the PS5 collector's edition because I ended up liking it so much. I had a lot of fun with the mechanics, and found it both fast paced and extremely satisfying to be efficient in, especially after maxing out the skill trees. (I think its described as an SRPG, but I've heard some people describe it as a RTS - maybe a combination of a Tactics game + MOBA)The acting and dialogue hooked me instantly, but its the subtlety in the dialogue and performance that really makes the ending stand out. There's lots of nuance and foreshadowing to take note of, which I'm excited for in my NG+ run. I wished that the music was more varied, having been composed by those who worked on Game of Thrones. The battle themes were basically all the same track except for the final battle. And the optional battles were recycled maps with some enemy variations, so it felt tedious at some points. I also wish there was cloud save so I could have grind some practice battles on my Steam Deck. The battles are bite sized, rewarding players if they beat the battle within 6 or 8 minutes. Having maxed out a lot of my skills, I was able to clear battles at around 4 minutes. So it's nice if you don't want to be bogged down by typical long JRPG battles. It's easy to be above level if you do all the main and side battles, without having to do any additional grinding.I think the pacing of the story can be a bit jarring or sudden, and I think some players will find that especially true of the ending. But I had a lot of fun taking the time to understand and even psychoanalyze the characters (especially the first/main 4) through their personality, temperament, and even battle lines which ended up foreshadowing a lot of things, which is what I enjoyed the most and why I liked the ending. As a whole, it felt like a really fun mystery flavored as a political drama told in a unique way and I loved how it all ended. I do want more, but I don't think it necessarily warrants a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but the gameplay factor needs more depht. A lot of people is saying the story and characters are mediocre. The truth is: The story and characters are far better than most JRPGs. But most of the story and the character development isnt showed in a obvious way, you need to pay attention to each little piece of dialogue to understand the characters layers. Every time the plot advances, each character comments about whats happening, and you cant ignore if want to have a full grasp of the story. And the characters arent typical JRPG clichés with exaggerated personalities and reactions. They are more like real people, they lie, they try to hide their concerns and other things from you, they insinuate... But the story has a huge problem. It ends in a cliffhanger with some unsolved subplots. In the end, is a good game with a lot of wasted potential.

_childDocuments_.review: After getting 100% achievements, here is my review of Diofield Chronicle:What the  is that ending? Where did it come from? Where was the lead up to it? Where were the hints? I did every single side quest, including the DLC content, and I still didn't see this coming. Am I supposed to be impressed and awed? Instead I feel like the entire plot was nothing more than a sham, a pointless waste of my time becoming invested in characters and reading the lore.That being said, it's a decent videogame; it's very pleasing to the eyes and ears. I was having fun right up until that blasted, ridiculous ending out of nowhere. The combat lets you pause, which is a weird design decision when all combat takes place in real time. Either do turn-based combat or do fully real time combat, don't give us the option to pause every 3 seconds to quaff a potion or cast spells. If I'm pausing every 2 seconds to relay a command then it's not real time anymore, is it?

_childDocuments_.review: There is a great game to be had here, the mechanics are interesting, the 2D art is absolutely phenomenal, and the setting is just interesting enough to keep me invested. To me, it seemed like a return to games like FF Tactics, probably my favorite game from Square.That being said, do not buy this game at 60$. This is a 30$ game, AT BEST.While the mechanics are interesting, they don't develop much beyond the start of the game. It's also incredibly easy to abuse and steam roll through the game. What you get with the demo of the game is pretty much it. And while the port is decent, there are some glaring problems like the lack of cloud saves.And though I adore the art, the actual character models are honestly quite ♥♥♥♥. They barely resemble their own portraits and don't bother even capturing the style that is presented in the production art. I get that you don't want to waste resources on a model seen from a birds eye view but the least they could've done was given the team better direction/more time to better capture the style of the concept art and make them pleasing from booth up close and bird's eye.The story is absolutely nothing that is more concerned with uninteresting politics than any personal stories of the characters in this war. I like a few of the characters, but the voice direction is questionable and makes me like them less when they are being awkward in cutscenes. The actors aren't bad, but again, the direction they were given failed them.I really wanted to like this game. Every now and again it'll remind me of the brilliance of their other TRPGs and have fun with it, but I still can't help but see how much I spent and be disappointed. There is so much potential here that they just tossed to the wayside and still expect 60 dollars for it. It's very insulting. What could've been a neat budget game for 20~$ is just a mess that doesn't deserve the money they're asking for.
_childDocuments_.name: The DioField Chronicle

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is interesting with a semi-real time system similar to Dragon Age Inquisition. There could be a little more story or character development, but it's not any less than most strategy RPGs of this genre. I would argue that the main scenario narrative is quite intriguing. The combat animation, environment and character portraits are quality expected of the Developer. Hopefully, this gets a sequel or spiritual successor of sorts where they expand on the existing ideas.Final Edit: Having completed the game, I'd say the twists are significantly more interesting than I thought. If you've actually read all of the dialogue (not that many tbh), you'd understand where these twists come from. I see that a lot of reviewers simply skipped all of the text lol. This could be setting up for a sequel after all.

_childDocuments_.review: Storytelling is very meh. Painfully obvious when conversations just exist to feed the player information. Difficulty is disappointing for a strategy-type game, even on the hardest difficulty I just run my team into the enemy without much thought and it's never even close. In maps that I can split my party for more efficient clearing I often send my sword and shield character off alone to whichever side has more archers and she clears half of the map solo without requiring any healing or input from me outside of casting a skill once in awhile.I will continue to play on the off chance the difficulty suddenly ramps up, however I am (most of the way through?) chapter 2 at this time and it is not recommended. Regardless of whether or not difficulty does increase, the first 4-6 hours should not be a snoozefest that you have to force yourself to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly a fun game. The gameplay combat is real-time, but not with "resources" like Starcraft or Warcraft. Rather, it has Fire Emblem style characters (unique characters you equip) and you control them real-time in SRPG levels. So you can think of this as a real-time version of Fire Emblem or any other SRPG. But it's nice, I have slow reflexes and this game wasn't hard by any means and the game lets you pause at any time while you select skills to use. You have a base between missions where you can unlock skills, weapon upgrades, more shop items, etc, and you can talk to your group of characters and select missions, whether it's main missions or side missions. Some side missions are generic but there's actually a lot of character side missions that have voice acting and shed a lot of light on their backstories, and they're not hard to unlock and there's no need to grind friendship or anything like that.My only criticism of the game is that the story pacing is a bit odd and I'm not posting any spoilers, but there felt like many plot threads left hanging. You also have to be very careful of the party members you use. The game is generous with experience and you have characters and a "supporting party" where you equip another character as a kind of sub-character to the main one you use, so it's not hard to get experience or levels. But a small issue is that some party members (and they're probably the characters most people will use) will leave after certain points in the story and you better hope you have a backup you were sending on missions. All I'm saying is without spoiling is if you see the story pointing towards a character leaving, drop that character and use someone else instead (or just google who leaves), otherwise you will end up wasting a lot of experience and time on building characters who end up leaving. At the same time, I do give kudos to the developers for taking risks and actually having a pretty dramatic and impactful story, even if it's not executed perfectly, and the protagonist in this game is one you'd never see in JRPGs because he's extremely pragmatic - there's no "friendship" or even schools in this game, it genuinely feels like it's set in medieval times and the plans the protagonists make are genuinely good, it actually looks like military tactics kingdoms would use in medieval times. Just be aware the game has a few faults, but otherwise it's a very fun game and the gameplay is where it really shines. It's just fun and addicting. I wish that there were actual "routes" in this game like in Triangle Strategy, like having a different final level for different characters, that would've made the game perfect, but I'm still happy with the twist ending they gave us. Give this game a try!(Thanks to Square Enix for giving me a copy of the game.)

_childDocuments_.review: Combat isn't anything new but it gets the job done and some of the skills are pretty cool. You can set up some pretty gnarly combos with the right combinations of skills and positioning.  with 8 sets of weapon skills you can have a pretty wide toolbox on every mission.  Most battles can be handled by buffing your squad, flanking your enemy, and using AOE skills on repeat.  Squenix mentions some sort of new combat system in their marketing but there's nothing new about real time with pause battles. Levels and their objectives lack creativity and are usually just about clearing the map - good thing the combat is pretty fun when you get more skills.  Every once in a while there's a VIP to kill to end the mission instead of killing everyone.  Every mission has the same two bonus objectives to not die and finish within a time limit.  Usually easy to do in most missions but it does encourage you to rush every time.  Wouldn't have hurt to mix those up at the very least.The story suggests a grand scope but the game never really shows it.  For example, your mercenary unit is upwards of 3000 (iirc) men strong at some point but there's like 3 people in the base at any one time.  Speaking of, your base is supposed to have all manner of training grounds, facilities, etc. outside of it which would have been a great opportunity to show the scale of your mercenary outfit and to immerse you in that fantasy but I've finished the game and haven't seen anything beyond what the demo showed.  There's a mysterious elevator in the base that makes me think it was supposed to be bigger.  The lack of scale is also shown in the battles which are all decidedly small despite the game telling you how big they are. "Oh nooooo a huge horde is attacking" - 6 units spawn.  Scale would probably have been better realized if characters led a squad of units of their type (say the MC leads a 10-15 man squad of daggery types) and those units fought others but it's just single characters fighting very small unit sizes of generic enemies. Battle maps are generally small and flat which makes their layouts pretty boring.  The different environment themes look pretty cool - it's just a shame they didn't put them to good use. I would have liked to have seen bigger maps with more choke points, fortifications, siege equipment to use (or be used against you), more varied enemy types, etc.  There are shockingly few unique enemy types.  Even the final boss is mostly just a generic enemy type (with an extra skill or two.)The story is fine (if muddled in some spots) and most of the characters have interesting quirks and are not just anime stereotypes.  Dialogue is sometimes awkward in regards to word choice or because the game doesn't have time flesh out why a character makes a decision.  One exchange could be boiled down to something like - char A: I don't trust you char B: why not? Char A: ok now I do.  The character becomes your squad mate so it's clear the game really just wanted to shove them into your squad ASAP and couldn't be arsed to flesh that out properly.A high point of the game for me was the world building.  Awkward dialogue aside the lore and world are pretty interesting and I'd love to see a better game carry it forward.Overall, I found myself losing interest about 3/4 of the way through but I dropped the difficulty down to casual to mow the battles down faster as I was interested enough in the story. Casual mode + 2x battle speed made the samey-feeling fights of the back 1/4 of the game less monotonous.  Deleting a group of archers with a top tier skill is always good fun.  I know this isn't the ideal way to play a tactical RPG but it did keep me having fun which is the most important thing when playing a game.  There are a large number of missions but all objectives are basically copy/pasted from a few themes (murder humans, murder beasts, murder humans AND beasts) and most of the maps are tweaked versions of a few different themed maps.Probably worth the money at a $30 price point but $60 feels like a bit too much for what is on offer. This is a janky AA game trying to pass itself off as a AAA game.

_childDocuments_.review: “An island name DioField, long known as the home of the gods, the island has basked in nothing but peace for centuries. Alas, an inescapable wave of chaos and change appears to be approaching. While sojourning in Lestershire at the Lester residence, the fourth-born prince, Levantia Shaytham, comes under attack. Amidst the chaos, Andrias and Fredret hurry to his aid, and under their courageous protection, he escapes the manor. However, they are ambushed, and Levantia is felled by an assassin’s hand. With his last breath, he entrusts the future to his friends. Levantia’s now limp hand bears the Mark of the Blessed - proof of his rightful claim to Kingship.” Eight years later in Central Field a carriage is being chased and attacked by bandits. The carriage breaks free from its horses coming to a stop, allowing the bandits to move in for the kill. Suddenly, three figures come to the rescue, dispatching the bandits and saving the occupants within the carriage. The three figures are Andrias Rhondarson, Fredret Lester and Izelair Wigan, Central Field mercenaries and it’s from here that your adventure will begin...                             There is a tutorial of sorts, you will learn as you play, windows of information will appear when you uncover something new to learn. Learning how to move to the carriage will be the first thing you do, then after talking with the occupant in the carriage you’ll go out and secure the area, learning the basics of attacking and some other stuff to get you prepared. After which you learn the identity of the occupant, a government official called Lorraine Luckshaw. She has been tasked with creating a private military unit for the Duke William Hende of the Lords Council. Seeing that you can handle yourselves she invites you to join the military unit should you wish (obviously you do).  Your first task after joining the military unit is to meet your unit's leader, Commander Yulzim Yorden at your unit's new base of operations. Commander Yorden is introduced to you by Lorraine Luckshaw, who is the general administrator for the unit. He then goes on to explain that as the unit is run by Duke Hende his orders always take precedence, this doesn’t mean that you cannot accept requests from the public. As you progress new rooms will become available to you at your base, which is a two-floor mansion, there’s no slumming here. The main room is the war room which contains a table containing a map of DioField, here you will find your missions for both the main story and side missions. Both the mission types are indicated at a location and as a yellow beam for the main missions and a blue beam for the side missions. Moving the cursor over a mission will give you some details on that mission such as Mission Name and Details, Level, Conditions for Victory or Defeat and Rewards for completing a mission. A mission will have you enter into combat, victory will be attained by completing a set of objectives, usually to defeat all enemies or to protect an area or someone. To combat your enemy, you will have to guide their movements and select their actions. You can select one or all of your units at once and manoeuvre them into position. You’re able to make waypoints so that your units can follow a path laid out by you, this is useful for performing attacks from the rear or for flanking an enemy from all sides. Using attacks from the rear and flanks will deal more damage than a full-frontal attack, it is also a bit safer as you will also take less damage.  There is no taking it in turns with each character or even the enemy in their actions in The DioField Chronicles. Every action you make takes a number of seconds and then you can perform that action again. However, juggling all your units in their movements and actions can become a bit confusing at first. Everything seems a bit clunky but over time you begin to get used to how things work. You cannot just allow your units to stay in one place and perform the basic attacks, you must be constantly on hand at everything especially if you find yourself under attack from two or more directions.  You are in charge of four units, which consists of a leader and an adjutant, however when you first start there are only three characters, Andrias, Fredret and Izelair. You will have other characters join you as you progress and it will be up to you which you choose to be a leader and which to be an adjutant. The leader will determine the attributes and skills of the unit with the adjutant adding their extra skills. You are able to edit your units prior to going on a mission allowing you to customise them depending on what might be required in the upcoming mission. You are also able to Switch Units during a mission with one in reserve up to three times if your current units aren’t doing the job. Each character has their own class type, there are a total of four, the Soldier is on the front line, the Cavalier is able to disrupt the enemy with its mobility. The Sharpshooters do their damage from distance and then you have the Magickers, who can help your allies with magic support both attacking and healing. The enemy has a detection zone around them, upon entering this zone you will be spotted and then attacked. You can maybe use this to your advantage and move your units behind your enemy for a rear attack by using the waypoints. When Sharpshooters and Magickers are selected, they will display a target area for their ranged attacks. If an enemy moves into this target area, then they will attack automatically. To perform an action, you will have to open up the command menu. Here you will find a units Skills, Items and Magilumic Orbs. This will pause the game briefly giving you time to select your action, choosing a skill will then perform that skill. Although some skills will require you to first aim in a direction that you want, once you have selected your action then the game will resume. Performing skills requires EP and this varies depending on the type of unit you have, some have more than others but you can replenish your EP with potions if you find yourself a little short. Items allow you to use potions or other items, however you can only carry one item to begin with but more slots will become available as you progress. Defeating enemies will fill your TP Gauge and has three stages in the gauge. Once a stage is filled you can then select a Magilumic Orb from your command's menu. Magilumic Orbs are special items which are extremely powerful, bringing forth a creature of great strength to help you dispose of your enemies or they might be able to heal your units depending on the type of orbs you have in your control. Positives  + Nice graphics and artwork + Multiple characters and unit possibilities + New real time tactical battles + Has achievements + Has cards Negatives  - HDR not good - Graphical errors with RTX on Help the Blue Fox Unit protect the Kingdom of Alletain on the Island of DioField against the two warring factions from the continent as they fight over the precious resources Jade. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The DioField Chronicle is an interesting RPG RTS, and has some pretty neat ideas and aspects that make it moderately fun to play. I haven't finished the game myself, it's sort've been a good "game to play on the side" every now and then alongside other games I've been enjoying. It's a game that would be good to grab on a sale, if the general gameplay looks like something that you'd enjoy.That said, there are a few things in the game that I believe are a barrier to really enjoying the game and could have been quite a bit better. Almost all of these things are tied to character growth and progression, and the issue in every circumstance is that the requirements to unlock are too high.- The game is rife with equipment and accessories, but the costs are so high compared to the gold you earn that you will either need to spend a great deal of time grinding (wholly unnecessary), or come to the realization that you're only going to use a very small amount of the available gear options.- The game has remotely interesting passive upgrades per character, but the amount of points required to unlock them are either trivial or way too much. You get (I believe) one skill point per level-up, and the passives are either 1 or 2 points to unlock, or 10 points to unlock. If you end up spending points as you get them on the cheap passives, you'll find yourself locking yourself out of the expensive passives for a very long time to come. The game offers respeccing, but it costs gold that you already barely have enough of.- The game features summons and gear upgrades, which also drain away your limited coffers, meaning that while you might have a lot of the "gem resource" required to unlock the upgrades, you'll still likely hold off on upgrading just because the gold cost is too high.Aside from that, the game on Hard difficulty is... alright, but enemy AOEs will obliterate anyone hit by them, so you need to constantly move your army out of them or stun the enemy casting it. It's not terrible, but it does tend to get repetitive after awhile.

My biggest complaint would be a lack of research/upgrade items. I don't know if I was missing some mechanic, but I earned more SP than there are abilities to acquire in the skill trees. I had acquired all the skills I needed pretty early on in the game, which is fine, but even after hitting Level 5, I quickly got the rest and it felt like the rest of the game didn't have any meaningful progression to build towards other than completing the story.Overall, I really did enjoy this and I hope a sequel comes in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game for a sale price. 20-30 dollars. It has great bones and seems like a great place to start. While this particular title will not blow your mind, the combat has enough intrigue to warrant a fully flushed out sequel or successor. The story is lack luster, and the characters are not endearing. The enemy types are few, and the maps repetitive. However the core of the game play is rock solid and very fun. It just needs more. More everything. More skills, more writing, more map variation, more combat dynamics... and perhaps less characters. I would have enjoyed just 8 characters with a greater emphasis on swapping. Maybe an injury recovery system or something to give reason to swap characters out. All that said, I still had fun playing it through.If this game does get a sequel the Devs will have a great place to start to build a true AAA game. If you think back to the first entries of the great JRPGs, they aren't that flashy or flushed out either. It is the re-iteration and refinement of their subsequent games that truly make them great. Despite DioField's flaws, I truly hope this game gets that chance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game to me was a simpler version of what Dawn of War 2 was doing in design. The game can be described as very moba/rts like. The major strengths of Diofield is the visual polish, the game LOOKS awesome. It's presentation and art style are great. The game play itself is enjoyable, it's got some issues with area targeting *depending on the ability like the cavalier charge,* but for the most part it works. The weaker aspects of Diofield is mostly it's story, majority of it's playable characters being forgettable, and the fact that the system itself can get in it's own way when it comes to diving deeper into tactics. Most of your strats are gonna revolve around 1 or 2 really op abilities and the rest is just auto attacks as a large portion of your abilities just aren't good, the issues don't even come down to high damage, it's more the fact that some abilities are just completely useless, they don't even provide a valuable buff/debuff. Another problem that I think the team might want to revisit is how crafting weapons work. Every tree has a main line and an alternative SUBPAR choice... in every respect, just straight up blatant bad design. I admit that this is one strong point I have against the game. Is the game worth it's full price? That's up to you. I was willing to give it a try because I love tactical rpgs, and for the most part I'm enjoying Diofield Chronicles so I personally have no regrets buying it. Some people may take issue with the game's difficulty because if your a veteran at tactical rpgs and your looking for a challenge like the games of old you won't find it here.

_childDocuments_.review: As it currently stands - this game is a flat 'ok'.Gameplay is very good early on but turns into a repetitive grind towards the end - the 2x speed carried me through the last chapters. There is little to no difficulty present - the game gives decent battles early on but stops innovating, boss 'mechanics' start to repeat and the illusion of variety in mission objectives vanishes around Act 2. That said, the skills are flashy and feel good to use even after the 100th time and there's some pretty satisfying combos to pull off.Story wise - it's basic and the storytelling is... 'experimental' to phrase it kindly. Points feel forced and any drama is countered by the fact that characters don't get enough time to develop - they just jump from point to point and 'do stuff'. *If* they decide to enrich it, there is a basis for a great story here but as it stands it is extremely bare bones and NOT something that will be the selling point for people.Going through everything took me around 20-24 hours, could probably get to 30 if I wanted to max everything out. A solid 6/10 as it stands and 100% NOT worth the full price tag, grab it when it goes on sale if the gameplay looks nice.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A clearly rushed, flawed game with novel core & solid aesthetics, that has real potential should they revisit and expand the formula through sequels or otherwise. There's too much wrong here to fix through mere patches or expansions.I rate it 6/10, try the demo (covers the first chapter of the game + you can carry all progress into the full game) and buy on a discount.The RTWP combat is refreshing initially. Hotkeys provide intuitive and fluid control of your party. But the game does very little to shake things up beyond the first hour or two of the game. There is no real depth in party management,  customization or combat, and there is no real challenge either. Simply put, what you see in the demo is what you'll be doing for the rest of the game.I'd describe the combat as you micromanaging an MMO party of 4 (think FFXIV or WoW) from an RTS viewpoint. With the "challenge" being distributing aggro to your tankier characters, using your skills at the best times, and manoeuvring your party to avoid AoE puddles on the ground.I use the term "challenge" as loosely as possible because the game is just... really easy, even on hard difficulty. EVERY fight boils down to "stack the enemy, provoke them with your tank, and AoE them down".For reference, I beat EVERY map in under 4 minutes first-time - many in under three or two - with all rewards and absolutely no replaying missions - except for ONE mission where I went over the time limit first time around because the game took away my damage dealer for plot reasons. It wasn't any harder, just took a little longer.The fact that abilities are tied to weapons means that the importance of party composition is also lessened a great deal. The game is easy enough that skills are mostly icing on a cake, so all that really matters is that the characters you are using have the right weapons equipped. This can also be annoying when upgrading weapons as the upgrades may not have the abilities you want.In my playthrough I actually got locked out of upgrading weapons as the game does not give you enough upgrade materials to fill out the lower halves of all 9 weapon trees - after about 4 or so chapters in the game just stops giving you low-tier upgrade materials outright, meaning any trees you haven't advanced into the latter half yet will be stuck there for the rest of the playthrough. This is annoying because there are many abilities exclusive to the upgraded weapons.But again, the game isn't difficult enough that this becomes anything more than an annoyance.The music is technically competent, that's the best thing I can say about it. There are no tracks that really jump out at you and I can't see myself coming back to revisit any tracks.The character art is quite good and the models are pleasing visually and animated well enough (albeit maybe a bit wonky in the faces).The Japanese voice acting is also pretty good. The dub, not so much (they tried, but eh).The game is pretty stable. I only encountered one critical bug in my ~20 hours of play time that required a restart, and it was no big deal as the game autosaves in missions, so I lost about 1 minute of progress overall.As far as the plot goes, game is the exact opposite of immersive despite the claims on the store page.To bullet point some things:There's a little glossary-style section in the home base that you can use to brush up on the "whos, whats and whens". But frankly the game should've shown most of these things while you were playing the game.I write so much about this because poor handling of a plot and characters is a really, really critical flaw in a longer-form story-based RPG like this, particularly one that seems to label itself as "gritty and immersive". Shorter, arcadey-er games and games where your characters are faceless mooks (think XCOM) can get away with weak characterisation and plot. But for a 15-25 hour title to have me feeling this detached from everything that is happening is almost insulting.All in all, I'd consider this a rushed title that has nice ideas and is competent aesthetically. But is flawed from a game design and writing perspective. It's worth a try, but definitely not at the premium pricepoint of £50. I personally got it for a 20% discount from a third party website - if not, I probably would've passed on playing this at release.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm definitely enjoying myself with this. Been a minute since the last strategy game I've played but I've been itching to play one since I saw Triangle Strategy and heard rumors of a Final Fantasy Tactics remake and this game definitely scratches the itch.Graphics are nice and look a lot better than the initial trailers, characters and story are kind of introduced abruptly at first but get fleshed out as the story goes on and in the sidequests, combat is a bit easy even on hard mode but I had some challenges here and there and even had to restart a few battles (also very forgiving there because there are checkpoints you can restart from). _childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it, and I eagerly awaited its release. I think the combat is fun and will have more depth as the game progresses, I'm touching chapter 3 and the mix of abilities and equipment is already enjoyable. I am playing on Hard but I wish the game had a Very Hard setting as I'm kind of steam rolling and I haven't replayed any missions.I think the story has a decent amount of depth and reading entries in the library is fairly interesting (if a little overwhelming at times) and I'm looking forward to seeing where the story goes. The addition of character missions is also nice and I'm expecting these to be expanded on further in as more character revelations occur.I also enjoy the home base dialogue with companions as they have interesting personalities and within the main story that is causing conflict, so I'm looking forward to reaching a climax point with several characters as a result. I would recommend picking this up at full price with my current experience as I'm very happy so far. If you enjoyed Project Triangle Strategy I think this is an easy buy, if you're unsure but interested try the demo and see how you feel as that gives you essentially up to the end of Chapter 1 (3-4 hours of gameplay).UPDATE:I have completed the game and wanted to added more comments to this review.I really do wish the game had a very hard mode, towards the mid-game I was able to purchase top tier weapons and started to steam roll just about every enemy and tactical situation. Using the haste ability on your party is really quite over powered - at this point the game was lucky to have me in a map for more than 2 minutes (if that).The combat lose its charm after a while as you work out the optimal play style and that ends up becoming all you do since there's not a great deal of depth within the combat mechanics and the AI isn't very threatening either.The story is interesting enough but has steam, then loses steam, regains it, and kind of loses it again. I like that characters do have very moral differences and it causes friction, but I wish more of it was on display. We get just enough to follow along and infer things but there needed to be more side conversations to support this drama, unfortunately the codex/library doesn't provide that extra context either.The ending is kind of a mixed bag but interesting enough.Ultimately, I'd be interested in a sequel or a continuation of this game type in a different setting, but I'd want to several improvements to the story telling and more or less a complete rehaul of the combat mechanics.In the end I'd have to say the game is  slightly above average and that a discounted purchase is likely a wise decision, 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun. DEMO highly recommended.The story is nothing to write home about, but that's not an issue since it's enjoyable and not terrible, and reaching teh end it get's really interesting but then it get's cut too short with weird pacing, but it's good nonetheless. The gameplay can be repetitive after a while but that's to be expected since you get what you see.The characters are fun and interesting and their skills and interactions are one of the highlights of the game. There are some generic characters but there are some legitimately interesting ones, with a particular sadistic magic caster taking the ribbon as the best character in the game for me.The missions are all pretty much the same, just different versions of "kill the enemies". But that's to be expected.I see a lot of bad reviews that it appears is that they expected this to be some sort of revolutionary RTS/RPG mashup, and and pretending that since the game is not the last cola-sip in the desert then it's not good, but that's plain wrong.This is the definition of a good game, not bad, not outstanding, just GOOD. You'll have fun, that's it, and that's not a bad thing, just not the next RDR2.Overall I've enjoyed the experience, I played the DEMO and loved it so I bought the game and I'm happy with my purchase. Some people might argue that it's too expensive for the game that it is, but I think that's plain nitpicking.Here's my recommendation: Play the DEMO, if you enjoy it (it's like 3-4 hours long) then buy the game, you get what the demo shows you.A strong 8/10. Not for everyone but that's not a bad thing. Repetitive, but nice if you want to play some missions here and some there between other games, definitely not the kind of game you beat in a single "sitting".

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mixed bag.  I do enjoy the unique battle system and think it works well, especially with a controller.  It feels like a polished and new RPG experience.   However, the maps quickly seem to become the same thing over and over.  Spawn three groups of enemies, defeat them, spawn two more groups, defeat them, spawn one more group, maybe a boss, beat them and the map is over.  It just starts to feel repetitive quite quickly. There are plenty of characters to choose from, but many of them boil down to being the same exact unit except with a few different perks that range from negligible to middling.  The maps don't even force you to shift your party around at all (at least in the ~10 hours I've played).  Would have been cool to have objectives that force you to use cavalry to get to a point quickly.    But as far as I can tell, you can basically just employ one strategy throughout the entire game. Once I found a strategy that I liked, I didn't feel compelled to change it up at all.   Taunt with the tank, AOE attacks with the mage and ranger, use assassin to clean up.  This works on basically every fight, even on the hardest difficulty.If I could give this game a neutral review I would, because I do think there is some value here and the combat is fun, IMO.  But the overall design seems to come up a bit short for me.
