_childDocuments_.review: So, just finished the game with all achievements after just a bit more than 20 hours. First things first, I won't recommend the game at full price, and I won't recommend it unless you're a Neptunia fan. I'm not used to doing reviews so I'll just list the pros and cons from my point of view (which mean it doesn't necessarily apply to you) and try to give a quick explanation about how I feel towards this game.Pros :- The overall story is ok. Nothing real new, but it's not bad either.- The dungeon exploration and design is much more satisfying than previous games. More variety of enemies too- Most of the jokes and some cameos from V-Tubers are fun- Once you get used to it the battle system is kinda satisfying- The 2D-Live is really good during cutscenes- Each character has a different weapon and how you play them will change according to that- The shops and "Main rest area" were well made in my opinion- The characters design and their dances in the minigame are cute, cute is justiceCons :- The button mapping is a mess ; I really like to have jump on A button + confirm option outside of battle but you can't in this game- Some cutscenes when you enter a dungeon for the first time and V-Tubers cameos during loading pages are very laggy- The camera distance can't be adjusted so until you get used to it, this is gonna get in the way of your fun during the battles- The difficulty is a mess. The bosses are just damage sponges but when I got to the 4th dungeon (Twinia) I got stuck against enemies I simply couldn't damage unless I used Blanc with full charge shots. However it's filled with long-range rocket-launcher enemies that deal 2 lives worth of damage with every shot. At the early-mid game you only have ~10 lives so yeah, it was pretty rough. So I abused the leveling trick (go the the 3rd dungeon mid-boss who drops 1 level-up + 1 reset enemies items with 100% chance and beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of him until you get to a satisfying level. I personnally went up to 100 in one go for the achievement and that made the rest of the game a breeze.- Already said in most reviews but the V-Tubers aren't playable except for the ones specifically created for this game. It doesn't affect me that much because I find the one we have unplayable anyway but hey, for an anniversary game based on that they could have at least let us play the most reknown / popular ones. Lemme play Shirakami Fubuki please.- 3 crashes so far so it's not completely fixed but I didn't have much issues compared to what I see in others reviews.- A lot of stuff is pretty much irrelevant. I said I liked the main rest area and I still do but a lot of shops don't provide much, the quests are generic third-rate NPC requests, the minigames aren't that fun- Talking about minigames I did say I like the characters dances in the BeatTik mode, but this mode is, well... worthless. The ideas behind it are pretty cool in my opinion but how they made it is like they saw their to-do list, got lazy and decided to put in everything while minimizing their work output as much as they could. Unless you want to watch you fav chara dance or get the achievement you won't be getting back here for funOverall I believe it is an ok Neptunia game, very chiil, kinda fun and very satsfyied about the dungeon design and enemies but it's clearly unfinished. If there is a sale at 20$ or below I'll definitely recommend to at least give it a shot for Nep Nep fans, but there are just too many good ideas with a messy implementation in the game that ruins the experience.I wanna keep my hopes up for the future but ye, as it is I definitely can't recommend this game at full price. Hopes that helps and congrats for reading this far.

_childDocuments_.review: Another year another neptunia game and for this game to be the 10th anniversary for the franchise I had a lot of hope but my dreams were crushed so fast before booting up the game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm part of the demographic for this game - I like anime, I like Neptunia, and I like VTubers.But not even that could save me. No. Nothing can save you from how poorly put together this game is.The gameplay at first seems like it could be fun. Shoot/Strike hoards of enemies. Get XP, level up, become stronger, etc etc. How they managed to ♥♥♥♥ that up is incredible. First of all it's divided between two types of gameplay - There's the goddesses, which attack with ranged weapons. And then there's the VTubers, who attack with up-close melee combat.Too bad you're not gonna end up using the VTubers much, because almost every enemy likes you knock you back to where keeping your distance is the safest option. So yeah, okay, you decide you're going to stick with using the goddesses for the entire game. If you're a nep fan, it was probably already the idea anyway. Then we move on to the equipment. There isn't any. Instead, you get "V-Cubes". These bad boys will increase (or decrease) certain stats on whoever you equip them to. Main problem? Goddesses and VTubers have different approaches to health in this game. Both called LIFE, so for the sake of simplicity, we'll refer to goddesses health as normal, LIFE, and VTubers as HP.HP is pretty much what you expect as normal from an RPG. The amount of damage you receive from an attack is dependant on both the enemy's attack, and your defense. Goddesses' LIFE, on the other hand, is a lot more blunt. You get hit, you lose 1 LIFE. (Sometimes 2, depending on the enemy.)Every V-Cube will increase your HP, but not all of them will increase your LIFE. And when you upgrade these V-Cubes, it increases the HP stat primarily. Not the LIFE stat. That one will remain stagnant for that V-Cube.  Oh, and defense is a stat too. But given the nature of how LIFE is handled, it's a stat that, once again, ONLY effects VTubers. Sounds stupid, right? V-Cubes very clearly favor one gameplay style over the rest. So maybe you fancy VTubers after all, knowing that with V-Cubes you can buff up their defense and HP so that getting smacked around isn't so bad, after all? Well, no. Because you're still gonna get juggled. Don't even think about taking that VTuber into a crowd. So maybe all of this is a skill issue, I'm willing to fully admit that's the case, because ideally what you'd want to do is swap between and balance. Although I seriously do not think there's any argument for balancing that favors using the VTubers, maybe other people had different mileage. Other complaints with gameplay that I don't have the patience to dwell on too much:- Rhythm mini-game that feels like a chore - Tutorials are a nightmare. They pop up a lot at the start, and eventually you don't take it in as well as you'd hope, leaving you to be confused.- Some features (namely the bulletin board and Video Battler) don't have adequate tutorials to make the player understand why they should use them. I still don't fully understand the second one, even after 100% achievement completion.- Those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Twitter bird enemies that shoot missiles are a pain in the ass to avoid and I hate them. Especially the bigger ones where bigger birds equals bigger explosions.Aside from the gameplay though, one of the biggest faults is the sound design. A very big problem.It's worth noting there's no english dub for this game, unlike other Neptunias. Idea Factory did state that this was a one-off, because of the amount of lines, and the VTuber licensing was expensive. (A weird reason, given that I thought the reason would be because they couldn't just dub over VTubers)So be prepared for hours of overlapping Japanese girls yelling at every single action. Shoot? Strike? Jump? Any kind of action? They talk. Also walking past monitors where VTubers will talk to you, or sometimes they'll just pop up and talk to you anyway. This game is extremely overwhelming in the sound department and I just want them to shut up. You'll likely have to mute voices if you want to keep your sanity while playing.I'd also review the story, but I actually got bored of the amount of padding in the VN sections that outweigh the rest of the game. So I ended up skipping every cutscene. I just wanted to ♥♥♥♥♥ about how much I hated this game. Please consider playing any other Neptunia game. Not this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Another year, another Neptunia game. This time it’s another spin-off, but with a unique VTuber twist.If you’ve played Cyberdimension Neptunia, Virtual Stars is basically that, but with a bit more depth. For one, it’s both a third-person shooter and a hack and slash game, of which you can freely swap between the two at any time during gameplay. Neptune and the other three goddesses are your shooters and your slashers are these vtubers created exclusively for this game (at least, I think they are). Each has their own unique skills and weapon type and there are matchups with enemies dependent on these, so you’re encouraged to swap between them to do optimal damage.I found this part of the game to be just okay. It’s Neptunia, so I can’t say I was expecting much, but it’s at least better combat-wise than what we got with Cyberdimension Neptunia – even if it does become a bit repetitive. Part of what helps this is the enemy variety. Whether that be walking troll accounts or Twitter birds equipped with rocket launchers, they’re pretty cheesy, but in the best way possible and perfectly fit that Neptunia theme.Aside from combat, there’s the loot, character customization, and light exploration elements that come with games from this series. Again, nothing too impressive there – not good, not bad, just the usual. One area it did improve in though is level design. The levels are much less boxy this time, with fewer invisible walls and a greater emphasis on platforming.I’m afraid fans will be very disappointed with how they are handled in Virtual Stars. Despite the big VTuber theme, the only ones you actually get to play as are the slashers I mentioned earlier. All of those collab VTubers from Hololive, upd8, Game Club Project, and the rest are not playable. In fact, the only real presence they have is on these virtual billboards scattered about each level. That and each VTuber has a corresponding V-Cube that you can equip, which grants stat boosts and special attack when you fill a certain meter.It is the most barebones implementation and I’m more so inclined to believe that they were included simply to sell the game rather than to add anything meaningful to it. I mean, most of the screen time for some of these VTubers is during the loading screens, so you can kinda get an idea for how weak the overall implementation is here.Then there’s the story – which follows the same trend as the gameplay. By that, I mean that it’s not necessarily bad, but it’s not good either. It’s got the usual Neptunia fluff, the constant shifting between serious and more comedic moments, and a cheesy plotline to tie it all together. The pacing is mostly fine, although it’s a bit slow to start, but it is still not something I would recommend the game for.The game took me 16 hours to clear and about 9-10 of that was visual novel stuff. It was not uncommon to kill a boss and then have to sit through 30 minutes of dialogue. I play a ton of Compile Heart games, so I’m used to it at this point, but it’s important to note for those expecting more on the gameplay side. And yes, there is a post-game with hidden bosses and other stuff to max out if you want to go the completionist route.This is the first Neptunia game to go without an English dub and Idea Factory has stated that this was due to the VTuber collab element and high volume of voice lines. I don’t mind either way, but I know a lot of people enjoy the Neptunia dub, so that’s something to keep in mind. As for the graphics and music – well don’t expect much there. Virtual Stars looks virtually identical to the last five Neptunia games and the music is entirely forgettable. The character designs are still top-notch, but the rest is just average.I was at least able to play it at 1440p, but it is obviously upscaled and the lack of anti-aliasing makes that obvious. It is also capped to 60 fps, but there are several dialogue scenes where it goes to 30 before shifting back to 60 during other dialogue scenes – it’s a little bit jarring. Controls on a controller are fine, but if you plan on playing with keyboard and mouse, don’t go in expecting an intuitive experience. They are rebindable, but I could not get the mouse to do anything other than camera control, so everything else was keyboard-bound, including the menus.And then there’s the crashes, which I unfortunately ran into several times during my playthrough. They seemed to really like happening either during a boss fight or immediately after one, before I’m able to save of course. In fact, there was one part where I had to go through a gauntlet of three bosses before the game crashed on me right as I touched the save point. The bosses are giant damage sponges, so you can see why I was tempted to just quit the game outright right then.Neptunia Virtual Stars is just a disappointment overall, even for Neptunia fans. The gameplay and level design was improved a bit for sure, but there’s no single element that really shines here. A tacked-on VTuber element, a generic storyline, and technical issues on top of that are just a few of the problems. If you’re a hardcore Nep fan, it might be worth a look, but otherwise, give it a pass – there’s better Nep games out there anyways.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, the games worth maybe 5-15 euros.- Raising the game from 30 to 60fps (from its own settings btw) completely bugs out the game. It causes aerial slam attacks to glide across the ground until it decides to stop or you swap out the character.- It's a 3rd person shooter with no fov slider making it extremely painful to use any ranged character (oh and knocking down a smaller enemy makes the lock on completely useless as you'll only shoot over them)- Dialogue comes in the form of awkward 3D models flailing about with iffy expressions and no lipsync whatsoever at times. There's also something really wrong with Neptunes expressions and face overall.- There is no english dub option and as always, there are no subtitles during gameplay so you'll have no idea what they're actually saying. Some vtuber clips don't have the subtitles translated at all. So unless you can read kanji or whatever language it is, good luck.- There is barely any voice normalization. Some characters speak sometimes extremely quietly so you barely hear them over the bgm unless you turn it off completely. And on the other hand some enemies voices will blow your eardrums out so you can't even balance it out.- Shooting causes the character to absolutely spam the 1-3 lines nonstop. There is no pause whatsoever, so when you're shooting Neps AR with the trigger held down... I'm just gonna say you'll never get annoyed by the constant spam of same lines from the older games. (And when playing as vtubers, your partner tends to just run at the enemies and get mauled down if you haven't given them upgrades. Which is bad because you can't utilize the slow free heal if you have no partner up.)- Some enemies have their attacks just be unbelievably fast dashes across the battlefield so dodging them on goddesses (which to my knowledge have no dodge whatsoever) is pretty much impossible unless if you can jump over it. And since they don't really do damage, it's easy to get stunlocked by multiple darting enemies for 5-15 seconds where you just need to wait for an opportunity so that your character can actually get up.- Keyboard and mouse controls are a mess but can be rebound--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+ The dialogue itself is still filled with understandable references + The models look nice but geometry distorts badly + Story seems interesting enough to play through once. If you can handle the 30fps lock and other various problems with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alrightI still need to play with my camera sensitivity to make the third person shooter combat feel better for a controller, and as usual the pc controls aren't great. The bossfights are supposed to have some power meter that fluctuates and changes depending on how well you dodge or deal damage to the boss, but it's been 3 bossfights of "running in circles shooting the melee enemy", and the meter doesn't seem to have any effect on me just holding the shoot button down until it's dead. The dialogue is the same as always, pretty decent, and in cutscenes they use the 3D models, so any costume changes like adding accessories or turning on the swimsuit dlc shows up in any story content without CG, which is pretty great. If Nep showing up in cutscenes wearing an astronaut helmet with some cat ears in a tron suit while bullying Noire doesn't make the game for you, not much else will. The game isn't dubbed and I've found one npc that didn't have his line translated.It's an action spinoff made by Idea Factory and Compile Heart, without involving Tamsoft like they did with Action Unleashed and most of the other brawler games, so it's the original/mainline developers going outside their normal strike zone. The combat feels lopsided, with the 3rd person shooter combat having lower damage numbers but making it several times easier to avoid damage including decent stun rates and easy to use specials; while the melee/midrange brawler characters have a bonus towards SOME enemies (randomly, so not all the bit enemies in the same fight will be weak to the melee girl, for example) that the third-person squad gets globally, shared between all units, for free.Also: 2 hp systems, movement mechanics (dash vs dodge roll + sprinting after moving in the same direction for 3+ seconds), melee/midrange has cool combo potential like knockups but there's no movelist or explanation how to do those moves, etc.As usual with Neptunia, the endgame is finding/making the biggest stat-stick item and beating enemies over the head with it, barring the arena fights in previous games where you stacked resistances, in this case the vtuber cube bonus thingies which take the place of discs. Also, so far I've found nothing good in that category besides the tutorial cube, as all the others lower my hp down to 1 and reduce my damage stat. Maybe if you stack damage into the negatives you can cause an integer overflow, like that new Borderlands 3 exploit that lets you have a rocket launcher with 70 rounds of ammunition? I'm guessing it really is just luck on the drops, though.I should probably throw in a mention about the V-tuber stuff in the game: Most of what you see of V-tubers is going to be an introductory infomercial during your loading screen (skippable, but gives a free item if you watch the whole thing), them saying thanks for the help on billboards around the map and giving you a free item for watching the billboard for a second, and rescuing them from danger by defeating special enemies on different maps. The V-tubers you play as are representatives of the genre like Nep and the rest are representatives of video game consoles, with the ones actually on Youtube and Twitch being cameos.Overalll, I'm still going to recommend the game simply because the dialogue and the Skyrim cutscene shenanigans. The fighting's at least better than Cyberdimension, which isn't saying much, but it's an improvement nonetheless. I'll come back and update when I finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: easy, boring, not worth your time. Just play VII again.Not worth the trouble of going through six cutscenes (no, that's not an exaggeration) to shoot at things for two small areas before entering ANOTHER set of cutscenes.The game is pathetically easy. Just cleared the fourth (I think?) story boss. My strategy: hold the lock-on button (which doesn't actually lock-on), hold the fire button, and hold left to strafe. That's literally it. No thought is required to defeat bosses. Abilities are pointless. The special moves (think EXE Drives of the previous games -- I can't even remember what they're called in this game) don't seem to do nearly as much damage as you'd think they should. And, despite the fact that you can quickly use EIGHT CHARACTERS, there's never really a reason to switch off of Neptune. Her gun makes the most sense being an assault rifle. Anything else is just time wasted learning how that character plays when you can just strafe + fire with Nep.The story is meh thus far. Save the world, but now we're going to shove VTubers down your throat because Product Placement. No, you won't know who these characters are unless you're *really* into the VTuber world. Maybe they're bigger names outside of the United States, but so far I've only recognized ONE VTuber.As I mentioned, the extra parts of the game and combat (the music elements of boss fights, calling in VTuber supports, ranking up(?) accessories, etc.) are just not required in order to steamroll enemies. At least as far as I've gotten, you can literally hold three buttons (lock-on/fire/left or right) and win every fight through sheer attrition. The addition of unlimited free healing whenever you have at least four consecutive seconds without getting hit makes it even more ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, how to describe this newest installment of Neptunia...for starters: it's a hybrid genre of third-person shooting but with hack & slash gameplay mechanics too. as for the characters themselves, besides our famous and beloved quartet of CPU Goddesses; Neptune, Noire, Vert & Blanc, we also have a couple of fictional VTubers too, starting with Me & You, aka "Mewtral". the 4 goddesses are the only characters that encompass the 3rd-person shooter gameplay action with Neptune using an assault rifle, Noire with a bowgun, Blanc with a plasma cannon & Vert with a sniper rifle, and each with their special attacks too.For the Hack & Slash part, You uses a bow while Me uses a two-handed sword. my guess that any VTuber you rescue will have their own unique weapon too. Honestly, I can't complain about this game as I've onlymade it passed the Tutorial level, but compared to previous Neptunia games, playing as the CPU goddesses takes some time to master in terms of mobility and shooting. So, to anyone who's played any Neptunia game or not, this will be a challenge compared to its predecessors. However, as good as it is addicting to play, I REALLY wished they used Unreal Engine 4 for this title too, just like they did for 4GO.Anywho, that's my straight-up, honest review on Neptunia Virtual Stars.Like it, love it or hate it...I leave the decision to you. I've played it for 3 hours straight,and I don't intend to refund this game. This is by far the first Neptunia game to become a shooter...and it's every anime weeb's/shooter gamer's wet dream IMHO.

_childDocuments_.review: And no, don't take it the wrong way, the game is still good, and the story is a scathing comment on the sorry state of the "AAA" game industry and how capitalism and corporations ruin everything for everyone... the problem is: the main cast already said all they could say.See, the main thing about the OG Neptunia games is that each game was an Elseworlds (no continuity). That convention, however, changed with Neptunia Victory, point at which the following games were now sequels... and alas, the moment the clock started moving, all acquired character development stuck with the characters, whose point of sale was being a quartet of goofballs; thus, ever since Victory II, the casting is progressively less dumb and less funny... and granted, while IF saw that Victory II was as far as they could ever go history wise and following games tried to move into terra incognita, they kept the continuity, and it is until now that I can finally pinpoint the problem: The problem is the characters.On Super Neptunia RPG, I mistakenly blamed the devs for forgetting to write a comedy. No, it wasn't the devs.. it's the characters that are no longer hilarious. As good as the games may be, and as good as the story and social commentary may be, I was here for the laughs, and I'm no longer laughing.I won't be trying Neptunia x Senran Kagura Nin Nin Ninja. I'd rather quit on a good note and on a game I can still say I enjoy (and between Neptunia's obsolescence and SK now lacking the Oppai Producer, I have no interest in a crossover of hollowed out shells).Unfortunate coincidence that the game is about fighting an enemy called "Obsoletia" when the franchise is  now the obsolete one. The only way for the games to continue would be if the goddesses passed the torch to the vtubers and now the franchise was helmed by Mee and Yu.Play it, and then kiss the franchise goodbye. It's been fun, but all good things must come to an end.

_childDocuments_.review: Sixth Neptune game completed... this one I was insanely curious about because of the mixed reviews. But in all honesty, I never encountered any of the bugs other people in this review section have stated exist. Nothing game breaking or frustrating happened, game ran as intended the entire way through.As for the content of the game itself, bugs not-withstanding... It's good. I can see why some people could be turned off, normal people might go insane. Maybe my ADHD, literally autistic brain helped process all the stimuli happening at once, somehow, in some odd way, but the vtuber intro videos and everything were really interesting to me (full disclosure: I really like vtubers), seeing so many I'd never known about was fun. Even if I'll never truly watch any of them but the Hololive members and a few stragglers.As for the gameplay, I really dug it. Animations were stiff and lifeless as all hell, and this game was clearly made on a budget. But you can honestly tell that the devs were having fun making something interesting. Even if that thing ended up being a very badly balanced mess of an action game with slight RPG elements mixed in.Understand, I say that with all the love I have in my soul for niche games that do not have triple A polish. There truly is no reason to use the vtuber characters that utilize melee combat, the goddesses are too good once you get an understanding of the mechanics, and upgrading with the vtuber cubes. You can honestly get through the whole game using Nep (or whatever goddess is your fave). That might be a turn off to some, as well. Obviously, it wasn't to me.The story is everything you'd come to expect from a Nep game up to this point (and maybe that's an issue some people have, but eh, I'm a sucker for this ****). I, at least, was emotionally invested enough to enjoy it. The bosses all felt samey, the enemies all felt samey, blah blah, blah. Let's be honest, nothing new to the franchise that literally reused assets for a majority of its life.In the end, however, I really, honestly enjoyed the game. Very much. I probably would not play it again any time soon, but the one play-through I gave the game was well worth the time investment. The time investment being only about 15 hours. Shortest Nep completion thus far.Anyway, if you're into niche action shooters and a fan of the series (and maybe also a fan of vtubers, or can at least tolerate seeing and hearing them all over the place), give this an honest try if you can pick it up for cheap. The game isn't truly worth it unless it's on sale. But hey, they usually are anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: EXTREMELY IMPORTANT: This game has a rendering bug since launch that will make the game unplayable by flooding your screen with graphical glitches. I don't mean it will look ugly, I mean you won't be able to see anything. Even with the "recommended" requeriments, this bug seems to be related to something else so if you have it just know that there is no fix and there won't be a patch considering how long has it been around.There's a lot of reviews pointing out this game is a cash grab after the vtuber boom, and they're correct. So I'll skip to the good and the bad.The good:There's new 3D models for each character with nice facial expresions and they are used during dialoge and even some small cinematics.Not too much recicled content from the main games. The 4 goddesses even have new outfits. (Though the game will recicle it's own enemies on pretty much every stage)It's short to beat.The bad:Controls are horrible. If you're hoping to play on keyboard and mouse (which makes sense since this is a shoter) don't even try. Not only control mapping is weird, you can't change it because the remaping menu is bugged. Even then, controls are meant for a controller, so you would end up having to use key combinations even on keyboard. If you are using a controller aiming feels really bad. Tilting the joystick makes it so the camera goes to top speed almost inmediately. I recommend decreasing horizontal sensitivity to 20% and vertical to 5%. Turning around will be hard, but at least you can aim at things.Gameplay is pretty plain. You get overpowered really fast and the balance is terrible. Playing with goddesses makes it so you only lose 1 hp per time you get hit and you can have up to 30 hits. Even then you can use items to heal. Dodging enemies is impossible since there's two kinds of enemy attacks: superfast charge at you or bullet spam. Bosses are really bland, despite having different designs for most of them, their attacks are mostly identical.Stages are bland. Despite the layout being original and not recicled from other games, the stage is basically a bunch of corridors with a few rooms to fight. ALL the items you find in chests and drops from mobs are random, so there's also not much of a reason to explore. Which makes the design of some later stages much worse, as they become a labyrinth. And to make it worse, they are a teleporter maze with teleporters that send you somewhere else without any way to know other than memorizing them.Bugs and crashes everywhere. This game crashes so often it's almost a miracle you make it from one save point to the next one. Specially when using the Beatik minigame.Story is bad. Like, actually bad. Being a Neptunia game nobody expects a good story, however I at least expect to hear some funny jokes from Netpune, some funny and nostalgic references and some comical villains. Here not only there's nothing of that, the story summarizes with "Go to the next map. Things are weird here. Do you think it's because of the bad guys? I think it's because of the bad guys. Oh, it actually is the bad guys. I can't believe the bad guys are doing bad thing." This repeats for 6 chapters of the game. Meanwhile, Neptune barely makes a few comments, with the jokes being always the same ones, Noire sometimes answers her, and a couple of times per chapter Blanc and Vert get to speak.Vtubers, even if you like them: Yes, even if you like the vtubers, you'll be dissatisfied here. ALL the guests vtubers are not playable neither have any relevance on the story. They are merely here to appear on some floating screens and to take screen space when using the vtuber attack. Which, btw, when you use the vtuber attack, it randomly selects a vtuber you have "unlocked", plays their short clip and then a random attack from a pool of 3 is done, and they are all very similar. At some point you'll stop using them because it's better to save that energy for the other special move.The rythm minigame is kinda meh. The timing feels a bit weird, as if you have to press the button way too early, and there's no way to adjust delay input. If it wasn't enough with the game poor balance, you can further break the game with the minigame rewards if you feel like grinding it. However keep in mind you can get crashes here for pretty much any reason.Overall the game feels incredibly rushed to take advantage of the Vtuber trend. Things such as having a save button on the menu that is crossed out the whole game, a section of the city that leads nowhere and the lazy way that the stages are designed... are all things you could expect from a half-baked game. To make things worse, even if you're a vtuber fan this game will dissapoint you. Probably the worst game on the Nep franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: New Review: After a hardware upgrade, I was finally able to play the game as intended. Going to keep this short to two points each.The Good: - The combat system - There is enough of a difference for people with different playing styles. The Goddesses (Neptune, Noire, Vert, and Blanc) primarily have ranged weapons or abilities, while the VTubers control and operate much like past action games in the series like 4GO and Unleashed.- VTubers - Both the original characters and the playable DLC (the OG Kizuna Ai and Towa from Hololive) retain the charm and feel of what you'd expect from a Japanese VTuber being thrown into the same universe as Nep and the gang, and it is obvious this was a labor of love for the dev team. The roster of support characters is fairly large, and includes a lot of the original Hololive founding members (o7 Aqua), and some fan favorites that were also part of Hololive at the time such as Korone and Marine, as well as a lot of other VTubing groups in Japan at the time.Meh:- Maps - The maps and worlds were varied enough, but didn't really bring anything new to the series. Once a level was completed, you unlocked a section of the map (usually with a warp to an entirely new map, but not too different than the other map) with increased difficulty, but other than mining the item boxes for rare accessory colors/variations or OP VTuber cubes, there's not much here to do to make it worth going back at least for the first run.- VTubers - While there are a lot of supporting VTubers that are not original to the game, except for Kizuna Ai and Towa, there was a missed opportunity to include other well known VTubers into the game (Inugami Korone is in the game as a support character, but I know her popularity has skyrocketed since this game was released, and she would have loved to be in the game).Bad:- Difficulty - It is a weird mix between being difficult and super easy. Once you know that you gain the most stat boosts by equipping VCubes (since you don't gain stat boosts by pure leveling alone nearly as much), the game becomes very easy. Choosing your play style also makes or breaks how well you do. I did most of my runs with the VTubers since while the quick run mechanic while playing as one of the goddesses was useful, it didn't seem the right balance for fighting. Later on you get a mechanic that allows you to basically heal and then the healing items you do get become practically useless outside of boss battles.- All The Music Motifs/Elements - This was a dropped ball. The game hyped up 'BeatTok' and the Idol aspects of VTubing as elements and it feels like a missed opportunity to incorporate it in a more meaningful way. Other than achievements, it can be completely avoided entirely and nothing is missed, though you get reminders through some dialog and some of the stats of VCubes/Accessories have specific BeatTok features. The boss fights also had a completely skippable gimmick which you gain advantage/disadvantage depending on a meter that goes along with a song that plays while fighting. Often times you just get to a point of ignoring it and wailing away.Old Review: Apparently there is a game breaking bug that happens sometimes upon starting a new game. I have tried several different methods to play the game, and got the error every time, even after doing one of the fixes that should have worked. While there are guides to address the issue, the facts are 1) the recommended fix doesn't always fix the issue and it can reoccur on a second play-through (or even just with an existing save sometimes) and 2) the devs are aware of this, but pretty much abandoned the game so release patches that would fix this save file issue (which seems to be the consensus on what causes it) won't be forthcoming. Which is sort of sad because this game has everything I would want in a Nep/Vtuber game (nep characters, hack n' slash action similar to 4GO, music/dance elements for VTuber idol culture), short of more well-known VTubers in it instead of a lot of OCs. It's a good thing I didn't purchase any DLC since this game is completely unplayable to me. tldr: Game has a number of game breaking bugs that won't get fixed anytime soon, if you're a Nep spin-off fan that also likes VTubers/idols, I'd give this a pass solely on the bugs part.Edit: After a hardware refresh (CPU was the issue, not the GPU in this case), it seems to have launched successfully and gone past the area which had black screened. What did have me concerned is after saving and quitting the game, the game crashed upon exit. Hopefully the save will be still good.

While I did have fun with the game overall, the balance was just not good enough for me to recommend it as anything more than stupid fun similar to something like Sonic 06. Go ahead and buy (wait for sale maybe, since the DLC is, as usual, too helpful) if that's what you're after, but otherwise stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: Idol Nep+Visually this game looks great. The 3d models are really good and definitely much better than most other neptunia games. The cutscenes in this game looked great. I really like the enemy design as there is a fair amount of variety in this game and the character designs are really good. +The soundtrack of this game is really good. This is to be expected in an idol game after all. I really like the different tracks of the world. I like all 4 tracks of that you can shuffle through in boss fights. It might get annoying to hear the emotional overdrive track a lot but still a great soundtrack overall.+The voice-acting is really good. Of course, the usual 4 goddesses continue to have good voice acting. The side characters and the new main characters are have some really good voice acting. I am a fan of both the VAs of mewtral. Vice's VA also did an excellent job. I really like the VAs of all the great eight as well.+As always, I really enjoyed the dialogue of a neptunia game. Nothing too surprising as they really focus on making these really goofy. I am a fan of the many Noire lonely jokes they put in this game as she is the best and it felt like they put a ton of that in this game.+Most of the characters are really good. Noire being the best remains and the other 3 goddesses are still great but dam the other main characters are good as well. I am a fan of miss pukorine herself and mewtral is such a duo. Faira and Kado are great characters but unfortunately neither are playable.+The story is ok. It's nothing new but hey it's not done poorly. Just your normal story of heroes going to different worlds and saving them one at a time.+The gameplay is just braindead shooting. I enjoyed it. You can swap between the goddesses and the vtubers if you want different gameplay. You can also build your characters however you want really with the vcube system so there is some sort of building aspect in this game which is nice.+It is nice that you can use any of the characters you want really as long as you properly build them. Maybe some characters are a bit better than others but the powercreep is nothing obvious so you can really just stick to your favorite characters.+I liked the dungeon design in this game. Not too long nor too short but it felt very substantial. The different places felt different and it didn't feel like a chore to explore every corner of each dungeon.-I said most characters are great but dam Nol and Dia are just awful characters. They are so annoying and they have some awful dialogue.-I did say the dialogue was good in normal neptunia fashion and it is don't get me wrong but dam some of the dialogue in this game is mad cringe.-This game didn't really have any difficulty spikes. I sped through this game and enjoyed it but I do wish some parts got a bit harder. I will admit the final secret boss is quite difficult but besides that it was quite a breeze.-For a game that lets you swap parties and characters on the fly, I did not feel the need to use more than one character. I solod this whole game with Noire and occassionally used Neptune with a high TKMK stat.-There is this main hub but dam it felt useless. The shops provided barely anything and the one minigame was boring.-This game crashed thrice on me...Not the greatest neptunia game but it was still fun. Very chill and short game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Goddesses and virtual stars team up to take down the Anti in the music-based hack 'n' slash game, Neptunia Virtual Stars! In a dimension called Virtualand, the virtual planets that exist within it contain an extraordinary ability to produce a commodity known as content. Of these celestial bodies is a tranquil planet known as EMO. This was the largest target of a nefarious group whose sole purpose is to destroy content created by virtual planets... Anti. Their decimation of EMO has left its citizens hopeless. Just then, VTubers, popular live-streamers from Earth, were suddenly transported to Virtualand. Because VTubers possess an affinity for creating good content, they were obvious targets for Anti, who quickly captured them and turned them into data pockets known as V Cubes. Fair, the Virtual Goddess and leader of Planet EMO, sent out a distress signal to multiple dimensions in the hopes of a miracle. Two groups received the signal - the rising VTuber stars, Mi and Yu, members of MEWTRAL, as well as the Goddesses of Gamindustri: Neptune, Noire, Blanc, and Vert. Both parties, now entering unfamiliar terrain, decide to team up to duke it out against Anti! Can they band together and save planet EMO from complete destruction?

name: Lovecraft's Untold Stories 2
detailed_description: Lovecraft’s Untold Stories 2 is an action RPG with rogue-like elements that continues the story where Lovecraft’s Untold Stories left off, taking the characters to a new stage in their fight against the Unknown, in a completely new graphics style. Loot drops of randomized gear and resources to craft your own, explore old and new procedurally generated locations, defend yourself against dozens of different enemies and face off against epic bosses! Beware, for the game is more challenging than ever before, and the tough nightmarish creatures opposing you will not give up easily! A PAINTING FOR CRAZINESS The Surrealist Artist Ardois-Bonnot presented his painting called Dream Landscape in the Paris Spring Salon of 1926. The moment the painting was uncovered, it caused a sudden riot among the public, and people screamed and ran all over the place. Soon after the exhibition, Ardois-Bonnot fell into a strange deep sleep from which no one could wake him up. Rumors abound that shortly before this attack of ‘sleeping sickness’, he was at the verge of completion of his greatest masterpiece which would change the world. 6 DIFFERENT CHARACTERS This time, you will have access to 6 different playable characters, old and new, each one with a different playstyle. The Detective, the Witch, and the Professor from the first part, which continue their fight against the Great Old Ones, and the Medium, the Veteran, and the Alienist who join the group of adventurers. CRAFTING EQUIPMENT One of the new elements that we are including in Lovecraft’s Untold Stories 2 is the possibility of crafting your own equipment. Find blueprints and resources to create and improve new items (clothes, weapons and consumables), and see how every item changes the appearance of your character. ROGUELIKE ELEMENTS The game is not pure roguelike, you will not restart the whole story if you die. Levels are randomly generated and should you die, you will have to start from the beginning of the area, with enemies and loot both reset again. Don’t forget to explore and pick up side quests in order to get as much loot and resources as possible, so you are able to progress in your main story. Fight dozens of different enemies, monsters and terrifying bosses from the Cthulhu Mythos in this intense, challenging action RPG. Ferocious beasts in the Swamps, Asylum lunatics, City thugs and the demonic creatures from the void will test your resolve to uncover the truth! Meet the 6 playable characters - 3 familiar faces from the series and 3 complete newcomers - each with their own weapons, gear and skills. Switch between them freely and pick the one most suited for the task at hand! Collect hundreds of different weapons and clothing items, or craft your own - scour every last room in a level, open every single box and get rewarded with randomized drops of gear, money for trading or resources and blueprints for crafting. Side quests are crucial - you can earn extra resources and items and get that extra bit of advantage you may need to be able to progress in the main story. Don’t forget to trigger side quests every time you encounter them, you don’t have to finish them right away, but keep them for when you need extra loot! Exploit the roguelike elements - level maps are randomly generated, as are all lootdrops. The game is not pure roguelike, if you die or choose to restart the level, you only lose progress in the current area. Use this to your advantage and if you don’t get the loot you wanted, try again!. Make use of Charms and Amulets! Sacred relics which grant strange new abilities. Find those that serve you the best and make your journey unique - but beware, power may come at a cost! Plunge into the world of darkness where every step could be your last . Balance on the brink of madness as you explore the Asylum and various other locales in the city of Arkham, Swamps, Enchanted Forest, even the Underworld and many more mind-bending locations, all in procedurally generated levels!

name: Disney Dreamlight Valley
detailed_description: Disney Dreamlight Valley Editions Disney Dreamlight Valley – Gold Edition Live your Disney dream life with this Gold Edition that includes both Disney Dreamlight Valley, the base game, and Disney Dreamlight Valley: A Rift in Time, an Expansion Pass offering new story arcs, Characters, Biomes, and a whole wealth of surprises. This edition also contains exclusive digital items. • Access to Disney Dreamlight Valley and Disney Dreamlight Valley: A Rift in Time • 15,000 Moonstones* • Exclusive Flowery Capybara Animal Companion • Exclusive Flowery Summer Cottage House style • Exclusive Artist’s Painted Overalls Costume Disney Dreamlight Valley is a hybrid between a life-sim and an adventure game rich with quests, exploration, and engaging activities featuring Disney and Pixar friends, both old and new. Once an idyllic land, Dreamlight Valley was a place where Disney and Pixar characters lived in harmony—until the Forgetting. Night Thorns grew across the land and severed the wonderful memories tied to this magical place. With nowhere else to go, the hopeless inhabitants of Dreamlight Valley retreated behind locked doors in the Dream Castle. Now it's up to you to discover the stories of this world and bring the magic back to Dreamlight Valley! Journey to Eternity Isle in Disney Dreamlight Valley: A Rift in Time, an Expansion Pass for the game. Adventure to this faraway land and utilize a mysterious new Royal Tool—the Hourglass—as you discover new secrets and uncover lost treasures. Foil Jafar’s plan to steal the Spark of Imagination, an ancient relic that holds the fabric of Dreamlight Valley together. With the help of the Hourglass, you are the key to fixing rifts in time and putting an end to Jafar’s evil plan! *Moonstones are an in-game currency that can be collected for free by performing tasks in the game or be purchased using real money. They are used to unlock the premium track of the Star Path (a battle-pass-inspired system that grants in-game cosmetic items as a player completes various tasks and missions). Moonstones can also be used to accelerate progress in the Star Path. Additionally, Moonstones can be used to purchase cosmetic items from the in-game store. About the Game Disney Dreamlight Valley is a hybrid between a life-sim and an adventure game rich with quests, exploration, and engaging activities featuring Disney and Pixar friends, both old and new. Once an idyllic land, Dreamlight Valley was a place where Disney and Pixar characters lived in harmony—until the Forgetting. Night Thorns grew across the land and severed the wonderful memories tied to this magical place. With nowhere else to go, the hopeless inhabitants of Dreamlight Valley retreated behind locked doors in the Dream Castle. Now it’s up to you to discover the stories of this world and bring the magic back to Dreamlight Valley! Discover the Secrets Of Dreamlight Valley Free the Dream Castle from the insidious grip of the Forgetting, and unlock the unique Realms of well-loved Disney and Pixar characters, including great queens and kings such as Anna and Simba. Each Realm contains unique challenges with puzzles to solve in the quest to bring friendship back to the Valley. You’ll start your adventure in the Valley, but your journey will take you to infinity… and beyond! Explore what lurks in the Forest of Valor and brave the deepest caverns as you take on challenges from iconic Disney and Pixar heroes and villains. Who knows who—or what—you might discover. Forge friendships with Disney & Pixar characters Garden with WALL•E, cook with Remy or kick back and fish with Goofy. What better way to collect, craft, and rebuild the Valley than with a friend! From beautiful princesses to nefarious villains, every Dreamlight Valley resident brings their own story arc, quests, and rewards. Meet up in daily hangouts and make friends with some of your favorite Disney and Pixar characters.. Restore the Valley to its former glory Free the Valley from the grip of the Forgetting and return Dreamlight Valley to its former greatness by making it your own. In Dreamlight Valley, you can build the perfect neighborhood that is just for you with a fully customizable layout, creative landscaping, and thousands of decorative items. Will you settle on the Beach next to Moana, or call Buzz Lightyear your next-door neighbor in the Plaza? Express Your Disney Style Bring out your inner princess, villain, or Disney bounder! Assemble unique outfits and decorate your home with thousands of fantastic items. Using the Touch of Magic tool, you can even create your own designs with Disney- and Pixar-inspired decals! With the in-game Camera, get ready to snap a sunset selfie with Mirabel, capture a culinary creation with Remy, or simply cherish a moment. A Game In Constant Evolution New content means that there's always something fresh to explore. Meet new characters in the Valley, check out the latest clothing and furniture collections in Scrooge’s Store, and complete challenging in-game events! Be sure to dream your way back to Dreamlight Valley regularly to discover new adventures!

With nowhere else to go, the hopeless inhabitants of Dreamlight Valley retreated behind locked doors in the Dream Castle. Now it’s up to you to discover the stories of this world and bring the magic back to Dreamlight Valley! Discover the Secrets Of Dreamlight Valley Free the Dream Castle from the insidious grip of the Forgetting, and unlock the unique Realms of well-loved Disney and Pixar characters, including great queens and kings such as Anna and Simba. Each Realm contains unique challenges with puzzles to solve in the quest to bring friendship back to the Valley. You’ll start your adventure in the Valley, but your journey will take you to infinity… and beyond! Explore what lurks in the Forest of Valor and brave the deepest caverns as you take on challenges from iconic Disney and Pixar heroes and villains. Who knows who—or what—you might discover. Forge friendships with Disney & Pixar characters Garden with WALL•E, cook with Remy or kick back and fish with Goofy. What better way to collect, craft, and rebuild the Valley than with a friend! From beautiful princesses to nefarious villains, every Dreamlight Valley resident brings their own story arc, quests, and rewards. Meet up in daily hangouts and make friends with some of your favorite Disney and Pixar characters.. Restore the Valley to its former glory Free the Valley from the grip of the Forgetting and return Dreamlight Valley to its former greatness by making it your own. In Dreamlight Valley, you can build the perfect neighborhood that is just for you with a fully customizable layout, creative landscaping, and thousands of decorative items. Will you settle on the Beach next to Moana, or call Buzz Lightyear your next-door neighbor in the Plaza? Express Your Disney Style Bring out your inner princess, villain, or Disney bounder! Assemble unique outfits and decorate your home with thousands of fantastic items. Using the Touch of Magic tool, you can even create your own designs with Disney- and Pixar-inspired decals! With the in-game Camera, get ready to snap a sunset selfie with Mirabel, capture a culinary creation with Remy, or simply cherish a moment. A Game In Constant Evolution New content means that there's always something fresh to explore. Meet new characters in the Valley, check out the latest clothing and furniture collections in Scrooge’s Store, and complete challenging in-game events! Be sure to dream your way back to Dreamlight Valley regularly to discover new adventures!
short_description: Explore a world filled with the magic of Disney as you discover rich stories and build the perfect neighborhood alongside Disney and Pixar heroes and villains in this new life-sim adventure game. Welcome to Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Fishing in one spot for a quest? Be prepared for the entire valley to be in your camera doing repetative motions until you get fed up and leave. You CAN gift them whatever you want, but not during Star Paths. There's no way to pin it either, so you have to remember a bunch of random items that people are requesting that day. Like I said, little annoyances, but they pile up.

_childDocuments_.review: "But just because we're finished with a part of ourselves, it doesn't mean that part of ourselves is finished with us." -MerlinAn earlier reviewer mentioned being the target demographic for this game. I'm almost a decade older and I feel the same way. I remember being six years old and renting Adventures in the Magic Kindom for the NES with my Mom. The same year, I watched the magic castle at Disneyland light up from on top of my Uncle's shoulders. I was the same age my nephew is now. I enjoy the post-mid 90's Disney movies well enough, but they just don't hold the same nostalgia for me. When you can remember The Little Mermaid, Beauty and the Beast, Aladdin, and The Lion King coming out in a five-year span, it's difficult not to be critical of modern Disney. Except for the dog in Up... he might be the best character of all time.Anyways, this game is so good that doesn't matter.I won't go on about everything I love about the game, as most of the reviews have done a great job of that already. It has that vibrant, cartoonish look of Fable or Kingdoms of Amalur, but it plays like an Animal Crossing game. So far, with almost 40 hours of play time, I've only come across a few minor issues:- I've had to force close a couple times due to my companion being stuck between myself and a doorway when trying to exit.- With my gamepad, pressing RB until you arrive at the last tab freezes the menu so that you can't go back to a previous tab by pressing LB.- PLEASE give us an option to untuck shirts from pants. I have a hoodie on at all times so I don't feel like Steve Urkel running around the valley.As you can see, these are all very minor and I'm sure they'll be patched out quickly... well maybe not the shirts. I've got a wishlist like every other player, but based on the amount of blank plaques in the castle, we've only seen a very small piece of an already incredibly immersive early access release.2022 was one of the most difficult years of my life. I'll spare you the details because it seems like everyone is struggling right now, but suffice it to say I spent most of it in a very dark place. The world at large seems to be fixed in a state of aggression and disagreement.Disney Dreamlight Valley reminds me to slow down and remember how I once looked at the world: with some optimism and positive sense of community; and that is priceless going into 2023. 100% recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cozy games, this game is quite perfect. It is literally the epitome of cozy games. It has farming/gardening, fishing, mining - all that good stuff. The villagers and quests are also all very fun, and I love the diversity of interactions you can have with them, and that they can hang out with you too. The story hits deep. If you feel like you had to grow up too fast, are scared of growing up/ adulting, or anything like that, this story will strike you deeply for sure. The only downside is Disney's greed. The game is amazing, but they did make a promise to make this game free (this promise was broken), are charging a large price for its DLC too (which even the "founders" don't get for free), and despite it being an expensive game to buy already, you still have to buy in-game currency (moonstones) to access bonus content. I can see this as fair if the game was free, but it's not, so it really just seems greedy. But if you cast aside the company's greed and unfairness, this truly is my favorite cozy game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't recommend this game enough. It's basically Animal Crossing meets Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon (or Stardew Valley) but with Disney/Pixar, and a bunch of RPG elements to keep you going. I get bored of a lot of games, but this game? There's always something to do. Tend to your crops, grow friendships (and get cool rewards/new quests), do quests, customize your entire island or your own home, dress up as a Disney Princess or Disney Villain or just a regular human being or goth girl. Speaking of the dressup, I'm amazed by how well they translated the Disney IP into this game; they seem to have had no limits - you want to do some casual Ariel cosplay? Go for it. You want a Mike backpack? Heck yeah we got that. You want horns and wings? Sure here you go. You can truly live out your Disney fantasies. It's one of my favorite games for sure (Played it for like 40 hours on gamepass before). With cloud saving, you can play on other platforms as well which is nice for those who play on multiple platforms. Honestly, I've never in my life paid for in-game items on a PC game (I did spend some on Animal Crossing Pocket Camp..), but this might be the first time. You can collect Mooncoins (albeit slow) in the game, which help you unlock the premium battlepass or buy premium shop items. You can get the mooncoins from the free battlepass as well, just by playing. The battlepass translates to roughly 13 euros if you were to buy the currency - but again, you don't need it. It's just so you can get a few extra cute in-game items. The Premium shop has items on rotation that are more unique than what you can get in the game, and their prices seem fair. They also release quite a few updates to keep the content going, including new items, quests and events. With multiplayer being added later in the year, I imagine this is a game that will keep you entertained for a long time. I can only imagine the stuff they will add in the future - there's so many untapped Disney characters they have yet to add (most princesses) and hopefully eventually they'll do something with Star Wars and Marvel as well - it'd be a true dream game when they do (jedi costumes for the Disney characters, please??). The in-game shop rotation can be a bit meh - I never really seem to get the cool items but that's similar to how Animal Crossings in-game shop worked, if you're lucky you have a good rotation and if you're unlucky you have to spend way more time getting the items you want (depends on your personal taste of course! I'm sure my shop is someone else's dream!). I hope they will add trading once multiplayer becomes a thing, so that we can get the items we really want. Another thing is that I would have loved if you could assemble your characters in a location, or call multiple characters to one location for when you want a good photo opportunity. Sometimes I make really nice areas and the characters just don't really use those areas, or they will sit miles apart from each other. So the world could be made a bit lively imo with small additions like that. In conclusion. If you like Disney and you like playing games with chill vibes.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. As you can see, I've got a lot of hours in it. It's a very basic, very soothing psuedo-farming sim, with familiar characters. It's good for when I want to do something with my hands and not think very hard. Excellent for listening to podcasts.  I've also spent quite a lot of money on it. The premium Star Path every time, both optional quest packs, tons and tons of moonstones. And I didn't really care about the microtransaction aspect of it, because it genuinely felt like the game was equally enjoyable to people who couldn't spare as much money as I could. And since it was going to be Free to Play on release, I wanted to support the company as much as I possibly could. But then the company revealed that, actually, they don't want to make it free. I don't enjoy being lied to by the people I'm regularly giving money. Maybe I'm just petty. I don't mind $30 DLC, but when you reveal that you will no longer support free updates outside of the main questline, after all that? I'm out. Sorry, but using the Sims business model isn't a valid decision when there are thousands of games on the market with your exact, very basic gameplay loop. I would only recommend this game to people who are interested in paying hand over fist for the glory of the Disney license. If you've been to Disney World multiple times this year despite living more than five hours away from Orlando, you'll probably like this a lot. Otherwise, I would suggest trying literally any other game in the Farm Sim tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Disney Dreamlight Valley, and unfortunately, the negatives far outweigh the positives. On the surface, it's a charming game with potential, but the developers' relentless focus on squeezing money out of players through microtransactions has tarnished the experience.One of the most frustrating aspects is the constant testing of players who paid to be testers themselves. Instead of genuinely valuing their input, it feels like the developers are using us as guinea pigs to determine just how much they can get away with charging for in-game content.The pricing of certain items is simply outrageous. Charging $20 for small quests is downright excessive. These quests, while enjoyable, are not worth the steep price tag, leaving a sour taste in the mouth of those who expected fairer pricing.To make matters worse, the inclusion of a Scrooge skin priced at $10 is a perfect example of how out of touch the developers are. This skin doesn't even contribute to the immersive experience as Scrooge remains confined indoors, completely detached from the magical valley. It's a clear cash grab, preying on players' nostalgia without providing any meaningful content.Additionally, the star path rewards are heavily skewed towards motifs, which are predominantly useless in the grand scheme of gameplay. Obtaining 50% or more motifs as rewards feels like a slap in the face to dedicated players who invest time and effort into progressing.Disney Dreamlight Valley had the potential to be a fantastic game, but its monetization strategies have severely compromised the enjoyment and value for money. The constant testing of players and exorbitant prices for trivial content, combined with underwhelming rewards, demonstrate a lack of respect for the player base. It's disheartening to witness such exploitative practices in what could have been a truly magical experience.Please note that I have spent hundreds of hours playing Disney Dreamlight Valley, and my criticism stems from a genuine desire for the game to reach its full potential. While I have invested my time into the experience, it is essential to emphasize that being a dedicated player should not translate into being treated as a mere source of revenue.

_childDocuments_.review: As my spouse says, this game is way better than it has any right to be. For being casual, there's a lot to do and a surprising amount of depth. It's a LOT like Stardew Valley. There's farming, gathering, fishing, friendship levels with all of the other characters, mining, cooking, and decorating your home and avatar. There are a variety of quest chains and the game is generally not picky about what order you do them in. The good: first, off, it's really cheerful. The game never makes you feel like you've failed or are doing a bad job. And the characters are.... well, Disney. They manage to be happy, enthusiastic, and supportive without triggering my cynicism. There's easter eggs everywhere. The music is a pleasant ambiance, and the graphics are pretty. When I think casual game, I think of something with very limited interaction. Here, there's a lot to do. What's casual about this game a lack of urgency. For example, crops can dry out and stop growing, but they never die and it rains from time to time. Eventually your Okra is going to be ready to harvest no matter how neglectful you are. And while there's no game mechanic like a day/night cycle forcing you to do time management, there's also no mechanic like tiredness forcing you to limit time spent on an activity. Spawn rates seem to gradually drop temporarily if you keep mining the same handful of nodes, for example, but only enough to make you a bit less efficient. Not enough to make it useless.The map feels a lot bigger than it is. Each zone has a teleporter (which you can move) but they're small enough that I often find it's just as fast to walk between them. It doesn't feel like one spends a lot of time walking from place to place. Tools don't wear out and your character doesn't need sleep. So there's nothing to interrupt you or slow you down if you just want to keep doing some activity. There's just not much in the way of time sinks or interruptions to make you stop playing the way you want to play.The quest system is broken into two parts. There are story-driven quests for every character as well as each zone, plus the grand arc. While linear in their own right, the order in which you do them doesn't seem to matter. Don't feel like rescuing Donald at the moment? Go bring back WALL-E or restore a zone's pillar. It's more or less open world in that regard. Or, if that's just too much responsibility at the moment, there's a second type of quests which are a rotating board of 8 simple tasks, such as catch 3 fish. You can let your attention deficit bounce you from activity to activity for a few short minutes at a time.The "bosses" are either tasks or puzzles. By and large the puzzles aren't too difficult and there's a fair amount of clues to help you out. The most complicated system is the cooking and the worst possible outcome is you get something other than what you were trying to make.The bad:  if you need negative reinforcement in your games, there simply isn't any here.  Pathfinding is pretty solid (I've seen an NPC get themselves unstuck by varying their direction of movement until they were free). However, your helpers can interfere with some of the bonus events. For example, a crop will sometimes give a bonus where it lets you keep harvesting it over and over for 5 seconds or so. If you have an assistant, they have this irritating habit of walking on top of the crop making a dialog open when you're trying to quickly harvest, or of leveling up and taking you to a cut scene. While very playable and with a lot of content already, there's quite a bit not yet finished. You can decorate your home, but they haven't implemented all the features, such as changing out doors. The voice acting clips are quite limited. There are clearly some missing cut scenes. Etc.It's still a bit buggy. An inconvenient timing of an NPC leveling up their friendship can break a dialog and force you to exit and come back into the game. Activities don't always trigger completion with quests. These aren't frequent, but in 30+ hours I've hit them maybe five times. So you'll notice them. And in a very few instances you can break a quest chain by completing an activity before you hit that stage of the quest. This is almost always solved by repeating the activity, so it's annoying but not game breaking.The camera is probably the largest weakness I've noticed. You can't really zoom in or out, and it tends to be a bit too close to your avatar making it hard to get perspective on what's around you. Final analysis: This game is simply delightful escapism. And if you're a Disney fan there's going to be a lot of little smiles as familiar friends, objects, and story elements appear. Clearly a lot of Love and attention to detail have gone into this and it definitely pays off. I found it neither boring nor stressful, just happy and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: New to this game and I'm pretty scared by the reviews. Quests shouldn't be locked behind paywalls, and while I'm not against a cash shop, I am against predatory business practices in an already struggling economy. It's pretty presumptuous of the Dev's to think everyone has 50.00 a week to spend on a game compared to food, shelter, or anything else more important. A cash shop is optional and should be treated as an optional thing. By optional, I mean along the lines of a catalog of paid items you can choose from. Not this Fallout 76 style 'limited run' of just a few items you *might* maybe kind of like at heavily inflated prices for a currency you cannot easily access in game. 150 moonstones per day is ridiculous for the amount of product you receive. Make a catalog and ditch the fake sense of urgency limited time things bring. If people want it they'll pay for it, you don't need to make a fake sense of scarcity. This feels like something a CEO wanted shoehorned in because 'it works'. It's aggressive and scummy marketing tactics and we aren't stupid. We notice.I think the Dev's need to look at F2P models that -work- instead of F2P models from whatever game of the moment is popular. You need a fair system for both F2P and premium players with balance to keep people happy. As it stands I see nothing but corporate greed, and that goes wholly against what the characters in this game stand for. Especially Wall-E. Players dishing out real life money to pay for a quest related to that little guy feels like some kind of sick irony against the entire message of the movie he's even associated with. Make moonstones more accessible, change the cash shop to a catalog, study current F2P games with fair models and don't follow Sims 4 and give us half a DLC for 30.00. The fact is it's 2023. Players notice when you're practicing unfair business models, make it fair. You should at least do the characters some justice and give them some respect. Otherwise the game will become trash, and you'll lose your core player base while alienating those who can't afford to play.

_childDocuments_.review: A quick summary, if you do not want to read the whole review. A VERY great game for life simulator enjoyers. Moving buildings, trees, rocks etc. is VERY accessable and super user friendly, it's also great! The characters and their quests are usually nice and relaxing and there is always something to do, so you will never get bored. There is some grind to be done, but not too much. Achieving things is really rewarding in this game!Awonderful game for anyone who enjoys life simulator games. This game is kind of similar to Animal Crossing but.. better in ways in my opinion.A LOT of the PROS are that resources respawn pretty fastly, so you don't have to wait for a day for things to respawn. You don't also need to wait real life time for buildings to be built, you just gather the money for them and boom, the building is built. Building and Moving buildings, rocks, trees etc.Another thing compared to Animal Crossing (that is if you are into Animal Crossing) is that you are able to move buildings and objects around very freely and almost from at the start of the game. It is VERY accessable and quick. When it comes to other objects, you need to gather a lot of resources to be able to craft things you have unlocked and you can buy things from Scrooges store, where as well as in Animal Crossing the store has a daily stock system.Once you have purchased an item from the store, you can always buy it again from Scrooge by ordering it instantly. The things you bought will also instantly be in your inventory and you do not have to wait real time to recieve them.Resources and GrindingDisney Dreamlight Valley definetly does need some grind to be able to get enough money for certain things, but it isn't too much grind. In my opinion it's just a right amount of grind. THOUGH some resources will take long times to respawn, so keep that in mind as you sell things because you might need some certain items for character quests.Characters, Story and QuestsWell, they are all Disney characters, what would you expect? It's really interesting to see how different characters get along with each other. The story I think is still fairly small because of the game being early access. This game does NOT get boring, though. There is always something interesting to do with the characters and a lot of quests.Some consThe only con in my opinion is the respawn wait and pattern for flowers and mushrooms, it can get quite confusing if you don't pay a lot of attention to it like myself. (this can just be me though, it's hard for me to pay attention to little things like this)Overall if you like Disney and Life simulators, this game is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: My Scrooge's shop has been broken for months and the devs only advice was to ask me if I'd time traveled.Edited to add the below: I started playing this game on Nintendo Switch in February of 2023 because I loved the idea behind the game -- it was another game in the same vein as Animal Crossing! And while I didn't really care about the Disney aspect of it, I was excited about many aspects of the game. Designing a village, gardening, the fashion elements; it was all right up my alley and sounded very cozy. However, I was not aware until after I purchased the game that it was originally intended to be free-to-play as that information was buried in the game description. I clocked about 80 hours on Switch. While avoiding Mickey Mouse's dead-eyed stare like the plague, I encountered several weird glitches with my character model and game crashes that resulted in the loss of numerous hours of progress at a time. What turned out to be the most annoying bug was the glitch I mentioned at the top of my review: my fully updated Scrooge's shop stopped functioning correctly. One day, I logged into the game and the shop hadn't repopulated the items in the window displays. A pile of coins was shown in each window display, as though the game thought that I had already purchased the items in both of the displays. I thought that was kind of weird but it didn't keep me from playing as I figured the developer team was already working on fixing the glitch (I had seen a series similar reports on the discord) and I wouldn't have to deal with it for too long. I also had hope on the horizon: I was going to purchase I Steam Deck. I had heard that the game would run much better on Steam Deck AND I could transfer my cloud save over so I wouldn't lose any progress. It sounded like a win-win.So, I bought a Steam Deck in April 2023. Little did I know, the bugs/glitches I experienced on Switch would transfer with my cloud save. Whoopeeeee!After I purchased the game a second time on Steam and booted it up, I noticed that my Scrooge's shop was still f*cked, my heart sank, and I finally decided to submit a report to the Gameloft help desk on April 15, 2023. While I waited to hear back from Gameloft, I played the game, looked longingly at the window displays in my Scrooge's shop, and eventually only started to login every few days to see if I felt a spark of joy tending to my pumpkins. On May 2, 2023, I received a reply to my support request. The body of the email that Gameloft's help desk sent to me is copied below: "Thank you for reaching out to us!Please accept our apologies for replying to you with such a delay.We are sorry that you faced this issue.Our team of developers is investigating the problem with Scrooge's Store being empty. Unfortunately, it can take some time. No worries, if there is any error on our side, they will do their best to fix this issue in the shortest time possible.Meanwhile, we'd like to draw your attention to the fact that time skipping (including changing the time on your device) may be one of the reasons for this issue.So, if you've time skipped, please return to your proper time. Then you will need to wait until your game catches up with the date you time skipped to. Keep in mind that this is not instant and will take some time for your game to catch up. Sometimes by a few minutes/hours, sometimes another 24 hours, but it will catch up.Thank you for your understanding!Please feel free to contact us back in case of any other questions or concerns."While I was annoyed that the help desk immediately blamed me for the issue I was experiencing, I wanted to be helpful when I first received the above email so I sent them a follow-up reply email explaining that I had not time traveled and giving them further details about when the issue started and on what system(s) I was experiencing it. Gameloft never replied to my response email. I also tried to reach out a second time for an update on a fix for the bug and received an auto response that the ticket had been closed. To-date, Gameloft has not fixed the bug. I ultimately stopped playing the game sometime in October due to my frustrations with a myriad of things and have only booted the game up once in the last month to see if my Scrooge's shop has been fixed yet: it hasn't. I cannot recommend that anyone spend money on a game that is this prone to frequent bugs and crashes no matter what system you're playing on; and has a team of developers (and a help desk!) that is quick to blame the player for said bugs/crashes and/or dismiss the bug entirely without resolution.
