_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Dreamlight valley is a solid attempt at catering to the "cozy gamer" crowd and appealing to the animal-crossing and Stardew Valley fans. Monetization is pretty heavy, with a battle-pass like system, as well as cosmetic only cash shop. They however have added in ways you can earn the premium currency by submitting "Dreamsnaps" submissions - so you have a chance to earn these every Wednesday - without having to spend real money on the game besides the initial purchase. They also offer paid DLC expansions for new areas and expanded storylines. Basic functionality is already in the game:DecoratingBuilding Relationships with Disney charactersResource gathering (mining, farming, fishing, etc)Cute storyline appealing to the younger Disney fan within all of usHowever the game is missing a lot of additional character and small details, like being able to customize character homes, or even interact with the decorations you place. So the game feels very surface level.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Dreamlight Valley is a relaxing farming sim that is growing into one of my favorites. It has been a super fun game. It has so many Disney references from characters, music, and decorations. This is a must-buy for any Disney fan that likes games like Harvest Moon, Animal Crossing, and Stardew Valley. Farming is very easy; it does take time but not that much. It takes longer is similar games. You can plant multiple crops at a time by pressing the plant key or button and then holding the key or button down, Some crops seem to require watering more than once, but I just got those crops. Watering is easy too. You can water multiple crops at one time. I think it is up to 8 (4 horizontally and 2 vertically), but it is not easy to water 8 at a time. You have to be at the right spot, and you will waste more time than is needed. It is much easier to water 6 plants simultaneously (3 horizontally and 2 vertically). The more you planet, the better. For you can save some crops for quest or gifts. I recommend selling some because this is a great way to make money early and late game. I recommend bringing a gardening friend with you too. Cooking is straightforward in this game. You can pick the recipe you want to use and then auto-put in the ingredients. Crafting is easy too. You pick what you want to craft and craft it.Both cooking and crafting can be done with items from any storage in the valley, so store and make as much chest as possible. There are many clothing options in the game, and you can customize clothes to make your own clothing options. As more events and updates happen, I expect more options in the Future too. The decoration options are massive, and you can make the valley how you like it. As more events and updates happen, I expect more options in the Future too. The character creator is good in this game, but it is not the best I have ever seen. You can probably make someone who looks similar to you if you choose. You can currently create an avatar for free and import it into the game when you get the game. You do not need to spend a lot of time making your character. You can change your character's design anytime while playing the game. When you start, you have very little space. Flowers will be the bane of your existence. Well playing.Fishing is very relaxing and easy in this game. When prompted to press the button, press it and repeat until you have caught the fish. I find fishing a lot better and easier than other similar games, which can be a chore to catch only one fish.The story has been great so far. I will not say anything more to avoid spoilers but know the story and side quest are long. More stories can also easily be added in the Future. They is tons of content currently and there is going to be a cool new paid. The game looks excellent. Almost all the characters I have come across have looked great, with the right animation style befitting their character. The only character I find weird looking is Mikey Mouse. It is sad to see such an iconic Disney character Animation look so odd but hopefully, this will be fixed in the Future. The map and scenery look fantastic. The colors pop and give off a Disney vibe. It runs well on the Steam Deck with the occasional stutter as textures load in. I found it is best played on PC Low Graphics Preset found under Graphics in Settings. Even on PC Low Graphics Preset, there is an occasional stutter, but it is better than higher settings. I have been doing a lot of the grinding on the Steam Deck. It runs great on the PC on Ultra High Settings at 4K, but I have a 3090 ti. It is demanding because the game has to load a lot of stuff. After all, the map is very open.I currently have the Ultimate Edition. The items are nice and cool looking, but I find the sheer number of Moonstones you get from this pack and the Deluxe Edition well worth it.Moonstones are going to be the premium currency of this game. There are ways to get free Moonstones, but you do not get much. It is currently used to unlock premium in game events.You get Moonstones when you buy the game in Early Access. You also get access to events that happen during the early access. If you like decorations and clothing items in farming games, then you will not want to miss out on these events. There are some exceptional event items as I am writing this review. You can get premium items by using moonstones to unlock full access to the events. I recommend going for the first option because it will be a grind, no matter what. Quest can also take a long time to finish depending on what needs to be done or collected.This game is a big grind to get Event and Dreamlight Duties done. As so as you finish one, collect the dreamlight and event currency because you will get a new duty to complete. This goes on forever.I am currently playing with a controller that works great for everything except for the design mode. I found that using a mouse for design mode is a lot better.Move all the fruit trees and berry bushes next to each other. Enable cloud save as soon as possible. It can save you if something happens to your save file or if you play on two different devices. I play on the Steam Deck and PC, which is very helpful.Save both the cloud save and local save before quitting the game. You can save the cloud save under help in settings.Find and collect the daily blue chest. It will give you some moonstones.Collect the event and dreamlight duties as soon as you complete them. You will get new ones as you turn in the old ones for an eternal quest of tasks.If you choose to spend moonstone on the event, I recommend selecting the first option. The second option only gives you 100 event currency extra. You will spend this fast. It can be worth it if you want to save time and get a boost but it will be a grind to get all the stuff either way, and you can get everything by choosing the first option. The first option cost 1600 fewer moonstones. The extra can be used on future events.Get rid of all the clutter in the valley and have a minimal amount of things on the ground to make it easier to move around and collect things like flowers, sticks, gems, and more.Make more chest at the workbenchBetter animation for Mickey Mouse.The ability to store flowers better or raise the stack limit to 99.A way to cook multiple of the same dish at once.Find more reviews from me on my Steam curator page:I have a whole playlist on YouTube of me playing Disney Dreamlight Valley:

_childDocuments_.review: (Got this game since first day of Early Release)First of, the biggest thing I love about this game is being able to spend time with my favorite disney characters! I would love more villains though, as those are my favorites, but they add new characteres and worlds/quests every two months!(+ events) Big Potential game with constant updates. It is a game for those who like Cozy games and don't mind errands, farming and material gathering. Especially if you love decorating exterior and interiors! It is what I love most in the game.(I'd love though if they would add emoting to our character or other ways to interact with the disney characters, like Hugs, waving back.)Not pay to win. People may complain sometimes, but so far, at least I, was able to get all I wanted/needed without emptying my wallet (I don't get EVERYTHING just because), as you have fair ingame methods to always get the premium coins needed.I like the idea of the DLCs. They add new worlds as big as the original, complete new stories aside from the main one. And this helps mantain some franchises that may clash with some people's taste, for those who don't want them in the main game. (Star wars, Marvel, Pirates...?)The only negative thing is, after so many updates and expansions to the game, it has become very buggy, way more in some platforms than others. But they are already adressing it, which is also a positive. Let's hope they can tackle all the bugs and keep them hopefully to a minimum for the future.In general, it is the game I have spent more hours on in my life so far! And I only play in my free hours after work and not everyday. Give me Randall Boggs and King Candy in game, and it will be a 12/10 for me.(for now I give it an 8/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Dislike that it has in game currency and released high cost DLC almost not long after the 1.0 launch (screams held back content to me). The price of the core game is overpriced for what you get, the DLC apparently has what  the core game is missing, which adds more credence to it simply containing the rest of the game as it should have been, making this game a rather high priced product.Core game is standard just collect -> craft -> progress while performing endless fetch quests to advance. It is a chill experience aimed at kids though so don't expect animal crossing or anything close to that. For a game where the characters should be front and centre, the game lacks character and charm and has nothing that endears you to any of the characters which given the subject matter is just weird.One of the games more annoying aspects is having to do some tasks at specific times in real time which is difficult for kids with school and people with jobs.Overall it's a fine game for kids and my 7 year old enjoys it but I suspect will grow tired of it well before the end. The in game currency, and high probability of held back content for at least the first DLC makes this game untrustworthy for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I already can say I absolutely recommend this. It is a fun game, and if you like both disney and the sims/animal crossing, you'll like this as well.Sure there are bugs, but that is not something they tried to hide. Also, it is early access, so bugs are to be expected. I, particurlarly, have not had many - only one bug in one quest that got solved after I closed and opened the game about 3 times. After that, it ran smoothly, with only a few glitches during mining gems that did not affect my gameplay at all.That said, if you're a person that is okay with waiting (something I am not), I do recommend waiting for the full, free release in 2023. If, on the other hand, you are not good at waiting, you will not be disappointed in this game - given that you are a reasonable person and does not expect a full functioning, complete triple-A game experience within a week of EA release.Also, if you do not care about cosmetic itens, the basic pack is enough. I do have the complete one, but that is only because not having all cosmetics bothers me. There's no need to throw 70$ at this game if you don't care for that, since it won't affect your gameplay in the least.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Disney adult, I personally love this game. It has the perfect mix of Disney magic and farming/crafting. All of the customization you get to do not only to your character, but to your valley and some of the best iconic characters is a great perk that I think was a great touch. _childDocuments_.review: I've played for over 200 hours between PC and Switch and here are my thoughts:Positives: - Amazing art style- Disney characters! - Frequent updates with added content - Customization - The ability to earn in-game currency instead of needing to pay real money for itNegatives: - A lot of content is locked behind a paywall (houses, clothing, pets, and other items).- Most of the "classic" characters are missing from the game.- Weekly dreamsnaps updates seem to be running out of ideas. Tends to repeat themes or similar themes. - Scrooge shop repeats items like *crazy*. There are multiple items I have yet to see in my shop. - Some of the clothing items repeat styles and have different names and maybe just an icon of a Disney character. What I would like to see: - The ability to customize ALL furniture. - The ability to delete rooms from your house, and floors.- A less controlled path maker (maybe a paint tool instead of blocks).- More hairstyles - Facepaint (free paint) - Tattoos (not super crazy but similar to Maui's, could possibly come in a Moana collection)- More makeup options

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge Disney fan by any means, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that the Disney aspect of this game wasn't laid on as thick as I thought it might be. I still have the option to go explore or decorate and forget I'm even playing a Disney game in the first place. ... In other words, I don't have Mickey in my face 24/7, which is nice. Donald's repetitive face-planting and screeching (accompanied by a train whistle) is driving me a bit mad, though. The animation essentially plays back-to-back on repeat for upwards of 15 seconds straight. Can really throw off my immersion lmaoIt's been really hard to put down because there's so much you're allowed to do in this universe. I usually find myself feeding critters, but you can also farm/garden, fish, decorate the valley, decorate your house, and customize your character/clothes. Some of the clothes are customizable, but I went into the game initially under the impression that more items would be customizable than there currently are. Minor bummer.All in all, great game, even if you're not a massive Disney fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best cozy games I've played. It did everything right that I felt was missing from other similar games. The tasks, resource collecting, crafting, quest line, everything flows smoothly and doesn't feel too grindy. The game design, characters, and Disney items are also adorable! After 163 hours I still never find myself with nothing to do. It's a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: If you like sim games and adventure games then you will find this game highly addictive. The fact that it includes many of the iconic Disney characters just makes it hard to put down! There is a lot of grinding (which I like, mindless) but since there are so many activities I just switch between them. I have heard some say they aren't a fan of fetch quests, but again in this game, it's fun! I highly recommend getting Disney Dreamlight Valley11/28/24I'm adding additional comment to my previous review. The latest DLC dropped  a week ago and it is a visually stunning DLC (Storybook Vale). There are lots of fun animals that you can befriend, quests, great items to earn through lots of grinding. I still really like this game. I just want to give all a heads up that it is becoming increasingly more expensive to play this game. I opted to buy the enhanced DLC  which resulted in a Fifty dollar expenditure. This week's "Premium Shop"....items not available to player unless they use real money is wildly expensive. If you wanted a fair share of what is being offered it will cost you more than Fifty real dollars! Mind you I've been playing this game since the beginning so I already have a few of the items that they have rotated back in (sometimes takes months for that rotation). Even so there are enough new items that I could easily spend at least Thirty-Five dollars. The competitive weekly photo contest creates a lot of FOMO and frustration for many players when they don't earn the premium currency they were hoping for.All in all even though I love the latest DLC it is chock full of bugs, many of the game breaking. The Dev's continue being responsive to issues even if they don't ultimately resolve all of them. I am regretting buying the more expensive DLC enhanced version and maybe even questioning getting it at all. I say this because I am already burned out trying to compete weekly with others in the creative competitions just to earn a few moonstones (premium currency) and this means if I wanted anything from premium shop I would have to lay down the cash. player vote on other players submissions and they can be ruthless. If you don't have the most current items from the premium shop it is going to be difficult to compete. If I had not just spent money for this DLC I may have very seriously considered moving on from the game to other games coming. As it is I will continue to play for awhile, but I won't plan on buying anymore content. I'm not sure I wholeheartedly recommend Dreamlight Valley unless you were a die hard Sims player and never blinked and eye shelling out  loads of money just to continue playing the game. And mind you Sims is a free to play game. This game currently along with both DLC's is 80 dollars and then you have that very expensive premium shop on top of that! Dev's have become stingier and stingier with free fun items as they want to push you toward that premium shop. It makes me sad.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say enough positive things about this game, it has been such a joy to play :) -Love the character customization options, plus you can change your look any time you'd like for free!-Characters all look amazing + true to the "Disney" style, and their animations make them feel more real. Plus it gives me nostalgia every time I see them and makes me want to watch Disney movies -It's easy to farm resources and doesn't give me the "grindy" feeling to get what I need for crafting or quests -You can use the shops any time of the day and not just on certain days/times!!! -Multiple elements in the game: fishing, gardening, cooking, mining, crafting, feeding critters, foraging, digging- giving you more things to discover and collect, and figuring out the best place/time/area to get certain things-Interacting with characters has a purpose/benefit; as you level them up (hang out with them more) they will give you more materials for that activity-You are not limited to daily tasks, you get new tasks automatically after completing one, so you can farm as much Dreamlight as you'd like to-Not restricted to daily stamina or time: if you run out of energy, you can simply go back home or eat food to refill it. In other games I've played (Stardew and Animal Crossing) you are limited to getting everything done before the day resets in game, which can be stressful and limiting at times-Very interesting and engaging plot: I actually get excited uncovering more memories and exploring new areas or meeting characters. Everything ties together nicely and I am excited to see where it goes!-Free content updates!!! This is a huge one, as I originally thought you'd have to pay for DLC to unlock new characters or areas-Optional micro-transactions: you can still partake in events without having to buy a battle pass. Upgrading your pass just unlocks more tasks to complete it faster. The only things you may want to spend real-life money on is optional cosmetics, but you can slowly earn the premium currency daily (and I feel like there's already enough free clothing/furniture without having to buy them with premium currency)-Very communicative and involved community management. Their team is very responsive to people's requests, bug reports, and questions. I appreciate how transparent the team is with their goals and road maps; and it is nice to see developers care so much about their players!-All of the content!!! It sounds a bit silly, but I am so used to games nowadays being released unfinished, where you have to pay $60 for DLC to finish the story later. This game is in still Early Access and there is so much to do! I only paid $23 for this game and have already played for 70 hours, but I still have characters/realms to unlock, areas on the map to unlock, quests to finish, and collections to complete. I haven't even begun to decorate my village yet-adding onto the previous point ^ how easy it is to decorate/re-arrange things in your village! You can move literally anything; houses, plants, paths, wells, items- all for free and it's very simple to do. I was originally very cautious about where I placed Villager houses, but once I saw how quickly you could move them, I was relieved. Also, you don't have to be standing right in front of something to move it, you can zoom out and place things wherever you'd like, and the mechanic is very user-friendlyThere's probably some things I'm missing, but I just wanted to review and recommend this game for anyone considering buying it. 10000% would recommend! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Coming here to leave a negative review after buying piecemeal DLC that was heavily implied to be part of the original EA rollout at some point. I picked it up because I wanted Rapunzel, more or less why I bought this title in the first place, and now I have a big "Cashgrab" feeling I can't shake from this title. I won't be buying additional DLC, and I'm shifting my recommendation for the game from "if you like Disney and cozy games" to "if you don't mind the Sims DLC model or you love one of the few base characters"Tbh, I figured this would be the case, but hoped maybe a huge IP like Disney might be able to release a game in EA without nickle-and-diming their fans. This is not the case. Expect to pay $30 for every three disparate characters for the remainder of this very very long empty roster of Disney characters that once appeared to be a slow rollout for a partially-released title.If you don't care about money, and you don't care about big-named IPs taking advantage of the EA system that was meant to support small development studios, and you don't mind keeping up with battle passes and grinds to receive the items you paid real money for, Dreamlight Valley is fine, nothing special unless you crave Disney charm specifically, but I'm still awaiting much of what was promised to me (as a Collector edition owner, at that) in the original title and now see paid DLC rolling out, so that's the current state of the game and it doesn't feel great as an early, heavier supporter.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start by saying I've been LOVING this game so far. _childDocuments_.review: I am not extremely invested into Disney and got this game on sale-- despite that, still find this game to be extremely enjoyable. I like to say this game is a good mix of the games MySims and Animal Crossing with its own little twist. There is so much to do in this game and is a rewarding grind. Would certainly consider this game a cozy grinding game. You can cook tons of different meals with different ingredients spread throughout biomes, build countless different types of furniture, buy stuff at Scrooge's shop (and changes every day), take tons of photos, unlock a good amount of familiar characters and place them in your valley, your house and the valley is completely customizable, and much more. The game starts off extremely simple but once you start progressing you will realize how much there is to discover, and it's a lot more than meets the eye! Again, I have never really considered myself to be a Disney fan and I still find myself geeking out when I unlock certain characters and the game is just fun and relaxing to play. My only "meh..." is that naturally, they do slither in some micro transactions. The moonstones or whatever they're called. Fortunately, I have never felt pressured to purchase them nor find them necessary to play the game comfortably and it doesn't get in the way of your game play. I think it's similar to a season pass where you can unlock more stuff with events they're holding and things along those lines. But I personally feel like there is enough good stuff in the game to not need it and it does not interfere with the story line or common gameplay. If you're hesitant on trying the game because you aren't a huge follower of Disney, in my opinion I say go for it anyway. It's worth it~

_childDocuments_.review: ACNH walked so this game could run. They took every critique / QoL changes that ACNH players wanted and made their own game, but Disney version.Things they had that ACNH didn't and other pros:-Bulk crafting- No wait timers for moving buildings AND upgrading buildings- Tools go in a toolbelt and don't take space in your inventory- You don't need to take resources out of your storage to cook/craft things- You have access to resources in your storage ANYWHERE on the map. - They have a "Star Path" (their take on a battlepass) that has a free track you can complete to get some FREE items. Its completely up to you if you think the EXCLUSIVE rewards are worth spending moonstones (real life currency) for.Just remember, THIS will be the only time the game will have the LEAST content. (Lion King update in the Fall and Toy Story update in late fall 2022)For an early access title, you have TONS of things to do. Many quest lines to keep busy everyday, fishing, mining, gardening, decorating, crafting and exploring.Now that I got all the good things out of the way, its time for the bad.Like I said earlier, its an  game so some quests and items are buggy.- Things are unreachable, some quest reward tracks don't give the reward they promise (one ex:  - Whenever buying some items, they don't show up in your inventory. - Problems with house upgrades making chests and items disappear- Dream shards (resource) are EXTREMELY rare to come by so if you accidentally turn them into dreamlight, then you're out of luck- Some people experienced not getting their items from the deluxe/ultimate editions(Listing bugs off the top of my head, ofc everyone experiences different bugs but these are the ones I saw on the Discord that came up frequently.)All in all, this game is definitely worth a buy for Disney & life sim fans. It will go free-to-play in 2023 if you're still iffy on it. The optimization of the game is smooth and doesn't heat up my PC at ultra high settings. I have tons of things to do and always look forward to my shop showcasing different items everyday. Its a very "go at your pace" game. You're not forced to do quests right away and have no pressure to do them. The bugs are annoying but its in EARLY ACCESS, there are bound to be bugs. 10/10 Would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Great game. Tons of content...hundreds of hours of play without spending any additional real money. Worth the price. Must be able to read in order to play.I'm thankful that I went against my fears after reading many reviews who complained about it being a game where you are constantly being encouraged to spend money.  This is far from true.  You can play this game for 100s of hours and still find more to do.  I purchased the game with the Deluxe Bundle for a bit over $40, and have played for over 35 hours.  This is a game similar to  that if I want an item I have to grind for the materials and progress far enough through the game to "craft" or "brew" that item.  Can you choose to spend real money for special purchases, yes....but doing so isn't necessary to play the game.  Some people were complaining that in order to get new content (DLC) it cost money.  It absolutely should cost more to add additional quests and challenges to a game that is appropriately priced and already has hundreds of quests in the base game.If you enjoy sandbox type games with added adventures, you will love this game.  There are so many things to do, but without the stress of "losing" if you don't it right now or fast enough. If you don't feel like accomplishing any quests, you can fish all day with Goofy, garden, and then cook amazing food that you can sell for big profit so that you can buy bigger and better things in the game or you can craft them yourself.  Or you can take the impatient route, and literally pay to play because you don't want to invest the time to work your way through the game.  But if you chose the latter, you shouldn't leave negative reviews for this game that has been nothing but enjoyable.My only complaint is that the dialog is minimal, and the majority of communication happens through text.  After playing Detroit: Become Human, it took a minute for me to adjust to having to read again.  But it's second nature now that I've adjusted.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The variety of Disney characters really adds to the charm. Originally, you were stuck with characters you may not like wandering your valley, but they've updated it so you can remove characters as you want. There have been a ton of QoL updates that have all been free, and two paid DLCs that are a lot of fun. My rule is I should get as much time out of a game as I play it. So, if a game is $60, I should get 60 hours of time out of playing it. This game has very much exceeded how much I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: You guys are doing an outstanding job with this game. Mine never crashed, but got locked-up once out 250 hours of playtime. I solved it by playing two instances of the game and shuffling between two saves, online and local. I started the game since it was in a beta release and I find it extremely difficult to put the controller down. The vibrant colors, smooth background music, and the fascinating graphics makes this game a Winner in my book! The variety of thing to do is on-point. Keep up the great work! Dave from Texas
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must-play for Disney fans. Hearing classic Disney songs in the background brightens your day and the little movie/story references in the character dialog are delightful! As for the gameplay, it's very much like a mobile game with a hint of Animal Crossing. (Though if the characters don't have any added value for you, you might want to wait until the game goes free in 2023)The quests are simple, but the game looks amazing, and I can't wait to keep exploring and seeing what they're gonna add in the future! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but OH, THE BUGS.The game is nice in general but buggy, at the point that you keep losing items because there is no way to loot them, or getting stuck at the door because you clicked when some npc was entering, with no options to unstuck but to ctrl alt del your way out leading to progress loss. _childDocuments_.review: I'm over 300 hours in now, please send help.If you've not played yet definitely start off with the character creator to get free funky clothing.Highly addictive, even considering all the bugs that hold the game back.Free with game pass so maybe try it there before committing to purchasing one of the bundles, not many people like the idea of buying an early access game and with good reason.Constant patches and updates are a blessing with a team behind the game that pays attention down to the little details, recently removing the low energy screen animation because many people disliked it.Really nice community to top it off, all around goodness to relax with after a stressful day.Highly recommend playing, even for a little while.After the toy story drop that included stitch and the Christmas star path i've slowed down a lot, finally ran out of things to keep me occupied. _childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna start with the cons. Farming is a pretty big element of this game but the execution makes it one of the most boring of its type. You have to plant every single seed by hand, which is pretty common but there is no multi-seed distribution mechanism and while I'm sure its a second at most, the bend and plant animation makes it seem like its taking forever. I'm not asking to plant entire rows or anything, but just re-using the same animation and spread that the watering can has would be a massive improvement. Digging takes entirely to much energy. I can plant and water an entire farm with less energy than it takes to dig the thing to begin with. And honestly, in my opinion dig shouldn't get to be a companion perk because its so rarely used, especially compared to something like cooking, which is vastly under utilized in this. And as much as I enjoy the cooking element, I'd happily trade the autofill option for a multiples button. You go into a mini-game-ish type put things in pot window, then have the completed item reveal. It takes for freaking ever, especially if you're making a bunch of snacks for a farm run or something. Making multiples at a time would solve this issue.My biggest complaint though is the 24 hr clock. I hate it in Animal Crossing and I hate it in this. I understand that its meant to force players to slow down and not just rush through but the devs need to understand that people have lives and jobs and its kind of a bummer to get 'stuck' only playing in the morning or at night because those are the only times you can log in.Even with all of the above, I do really enjoy this. I think it has loads of potential to be something great but even at this early stage, its a great unwind, relax game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: I should have been taking notes while playing, but you know how that goes, a lot will be missed here. After 50 hours in game, here is my initial review and thoughts.First, nothing about the game I have found can't be fixed. The game itself is fun, a great waste of time, and a way to unwind without killing every other zombie. If you need that kind of adreneline at every moment of your game time, this game is not for you.If you like the laid back games, I really do recommend this game. This game plays similar to Animal Crossing, but is different for so many reasons. I do not see it as a Animal Crossing killer, nor do I personally find it better than Animal Crossing.OK, I am going to ignore most bugs, I found nothing game breaking, although others are reporting those issues.1) aquamarine is in every 3rd quest, and it is a very rare spawn. Please increase the spawn rate for this.2) We need larger storage. I have a room full of chests. Yes, I am a hoarder. I have grown 100 of every vegetable, keep at least 100 of every fruit in stock, plus try to keep at least 1 stack of every item in stock. We have some pretty storage options, but they don't actually store anything. I would love to have a useable food pantry for mid/late game. Even the safe from Scrooge's final quest holds 2 lines, seriously.3) While it is raining, let plants soak up the water. It is really weird to have dry veggies 2 minutes after the rain stops, which has happened to me multiple times. Let the water timer begin the second the rain stops.4 Probably a bug, but has actually forced me to forcequit the game. Merlin and Wall-E are immovable objects when they are your companion. Every other character, you can force out of your way. These guys, not so much. And if they are standing in just the right (or wrong) place, and you activate the door in a sideroom, you will be unable to reach the door, unable to go into a menu, etc.5 I would love to see a better melding of different path types. Since there are less than what, 10-15 paths in the game, this shouldn't be too hard, and no matter how you do it, it would look better than no blending.6 Do not play animations for 10 seconds until after I have hit the activate, A button. Many times, I have lost out on bonuses because the companion chooses that second to level up.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not play if you have diabetes. Really, this game is so sweet and full of sticky, yucky lovely cutesy friendship that you might die.The aim is to rescue a valley full of color, cute critters and sparkles. Even the characters sparkle. By being friendly, respectful and helpful you'll bring back many well-known Disney-characters into the valley. It's basically Animal Crossing, but in the Disney/Pixar -universe.That being said, it's actually rather complex with a crafting system, crops, cooking, customizable furtinure and clothing, relationships, daily tasks and several sorts of currency. The game mechanics themselves are simple and there's enough to do. The game starts simply and teaches you the basics. You'll play the first few hours with traditional Diskey-companions, but soon after you can start to select which newer characters to help. As a minus the game really, really lays the friendship-is-magic on thick. Orbs of virtue, daily tasks that need to be done with friendship and love... Ugh. There's no voice acting as such. The dialogue is all written, and the characters utter their classical sounds/phrases. Goofy, sadly, sounds like he's about to puke, so watch out if you're sensitive to gagging sounds.    All in all after the first few hours I'm reasonably entertained and curious to find my favorite characters - so not refunding even though my blood sugar is getting dangerously high.

_childDocuments_.review: I hopped on this game a few months ago and loved it so much that I bought their Ultimate Edition because I wanted to support development and the included items were worth it to me. However with the newest update I cannot in good conscience recommend this game. As other people have stated they have introduced a ridiculously priced premium shop that has cosmetics that may or may not become available again. The newest update has also broken the game. I have experienced so many bugs that I have had to close and open the game to fix and I find myself really disappointed that they focused on introducing a premium shop instead of fixing some of these game breaking bugs. I want desperately to love this game but 5 months into early access development feels really early to be introducing a premium shop that is so over priced. Its not a good sign for the direction this game is going. I am not opposed to the premium shop but the unclear status of the items and the exorbitant prices (as others have said being about $55 per week) has not inspired confidence in the future of this game.EDIT: All my worst fears have been confirmed. They will not be releasing the full edition as F2P as advertised. And will be screwing over the players who paid for the more expensive editions by making us buy the expansion pass even though we have already given them $90. It ridiculous. The newest release update has destroyed any goodwill I had left for this game

_childDocuments_.review: - Don’t spend your money. Wait until it’s out of early access. -On one hand, this game is genuinely fun and relaxing when it works. It plays like an Animal Crossing game, only with quest lines and Disney characters to recruit to your town. Even with some bugs, I played this for days in a row and enjoyed myself.Problem is, it’s only fun when it WORKS. Small bugs are one thing, as it’s early access this is understandable. However, at the current moment there is a well-known crash issue with the game that causes players to loose all of their save data, with NO way to retrieve it. The game operates by saving either locally or to the cloud, neither of which are accessible to the player. Folks are losing tens of hours of gameplay from crashes with no solution proposed.On top of all this, buying early access doesn’t net you anything other than a couple of cosmetic items and some in-game currency. Once the game officially releases, it’ll be free to play. If I had known I was paying to be a QA tester, I’d have waited too.-- Edit --There's now apparently a Premium shop with prices more predatory that the most infamous EA shenanigans. Previously you could get furniture pieces in the Star Path if you wanted; apparently not anymore, you have to pay the outrageous Premium shop prices or potentially miss out on one-time items. Very scummy stuff, especially considering this game ISN'T OUT OF EARLY ACCESS YET.

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits your heart in places you never would expect a game like this to hit. Don't be deceived by the cute and colorful characters and trailer. This is a deeply emotional, thought-provoking game revolving around one's relationship with themselves, with childhood, and with loss.And for a game in beta, it's surprisingly robust. Some people get more bugs than others, but there's a lot more than just quests and farming here, with plenty of hours you can clock in. I was introduced to this game by a friend of mine, and then I pulled my partner in with it, and we pulled several of our friends in with us. I can't wait for the multiplayer update. We're all so excited, we even made a group chat to share our gameplay. So imagine seven people between the ages of 23 and 33 crying over Disney characters in a Disney game. Yeah. It'll make you cry. Or at least feel a little nostalgic. It's that kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, NO I don't recommend this game unless you know going in that you'll likely be spending a fair amount of money whilst playing or you have no issue with missing out on items/content locked behind a paywall. I've played this game since launch day 1 of early access, originally on switch (Don't!, it's laggy, glitches and crashes almost hourly for me and has less item capacity so you cannot decorate your valley as much as PC) I've clocked over 120 hours on both switch and PC and PC is far superior with better visual qualities, it runs quicker and has a larger item capacity than switch. It does occasionally crash but this is way less than switch plus it's still being developed and changed.The addition of the premium shop has really soured the experience for me. The prices are outrageously HIGH, especially for a skin. It also preys on your fear of missing out by including a timer for the premium shop reset when new products will arrive. So far only a handful (if that) have made a reappearance in the premium shop. There is no catalogue, some items have been causing peoples games to crash and fail to reload when purchased items have been placed, clipping issues to name a few.Alongside this there have also been two character story packs that are to be purchased with premium currency with some new quests relating to that character and new clothing/furniture items as rewards. These are also quite highly priced.With the newest addition of weekly Dreamsnaps challenges the premium currency has become part of the reward for participating. It has helped many of us to purchase at least some of the premium shop items without spending hard cash. Dreamsnaps rewards us playing the game and voting on previous entries. It has allowed us to be more creative with our valley and encourages community involvement, overall an enjoyable and welcomed feature. Originally we were told this game would go free to play but it seems to have been redacted recently. Alongside this Gameloft have also announced an expansion DLC that's almost as expensive ($29.99) as the standard edition base game ($39.99) with what we know so far as only including 2 or 3 new characters.Having purchased the game twice after discovering the switch version is rubbish and practically unplayable for me I'm reluctant to spend even more on this game when it's starting to feel like nothing but a cash grab. I will eventually get the expansion when it goes on offer but I certainly will not be paying full price.Once the character quests are done there isn't much to do except, plant and harvest crops, mine for gems and fish. It gets stagnant quite quickly. We need more mini games and things to keep us entertained, like animal crossing has balloons that float by, bugs to catch, the ability to make snowmen, people and sellers stopping by, snorkelling, visiting other islands etc. It would also be great if we had a re-sell option to sell back the multiple furniture items we don't need.I have mostly stopped playing but have been coming back for around 2-3 hours a week at most to participate in most Dreamsnaps and to complete the star-paths.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: I resisted this game for a while, but as a new mom who loves gaming but struggles to find the time... this is heaven sent! I play it on the steamdeck and it ports over beautifully. It's very much Disney's version of animal crossing or stardew valley. There are story quests, event quests, character quests etc. There is optional DLC and micro transactions, but you don't really need to spend more money to enjoy the game. There is still the occasional bug, but I find it a very relaxing game and very easy to pick up and put down if I only have a half hour here or there to play. It got me through those long nights with a new baby! There's an auto-save feature, but also manual save. Great Disney soundtrack. Some of the characters like Mother Gothel and Beast are reallllly annoying. lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent addition to the cozy gaming format so many have come to love. DDV does a great job combining successful formats from other games in the genre like Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, and the Sims, while throwing in their own "magic" pizzazz to make it feel fresh. An expanding catalog of characters offers players to relive their childhood fantasies with their favorite Disney/Pixar favs. While there are the occasional bugs, the dev team seems to be active in updating the game to make the experience better for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Parents, guardians, older siblings, please read the second paragraph below.Disney and Gameloft play on your nostalgia in exchange for a lot of money where you get: bugs that have existed since early-access in 2022, a pointless multiplayer system, time-locked events and story-lines, overly expensive cosmetic items (a choice buy o f course but still unreasonably expensive), somewhat short story-line for base game ($30 please?), and so muc- I mean, fewer things beyond that. It is a very grind-focused game that runs on real time, so if you have a strict schedule this game isn't for you (college students, that includes you too). The DLC isn't finished yet so if you DO plan on purchasing the game, don't waste an additional $30 on the DLC just yet (it was a cash grab for a bugged out story with a multi-stage-but-minimal-content update plan).For those with younger children in the household, if you DO purchase this game for kids be sure to have parental controls set up IN STEAM due to the in-game currency that is available. Also look at others reviews or watch a play-through when it comes to the content in the base game's main story-line to see if you are comfortable with kids being exposed to somewhat heavier content revolving around mental health. If you are comfortable with them playing the game, I still recommend sitting with your child to talk about the topics in the base game story and check in with them.TL;DR: Maybe it'll be a better game a few years from now, but it is a no from me.

(i have not had any myself other than the occasional camera glitch) Nothing they haven't fixed already in patches. DO NOT restart your game! I know it's hard to wait and want to move forward in the story but all you have to do is submit a bug fix ticket to the devs and they will release a fix in the next patch update or even sooner! _childDocuments_.review: I'm okay with the devs lying and making it not free to play anymore. That's great! That means no in game microtransactions right? With regular free and paid DLCs or a complete game like other paid games? NO! Not for this game :) You still have a microtransaction premium shop, paid exclusive character story quests (WallE and Ursula), and season passes on top of paying for the base game and the DLC which is a bit high price personally, but sure I get it's so they devs get paid. But wait.. they're already making money from the base game and microtransactions! This game is really a game of "How much can the devs put behind a paywall until they need shell out some free content to appease the community?"I have long dealt with Gameloft since launch of Disney Magic Kingdoms (2016), because I'm a silly obsessed Disney fan. I have been playing Dreamlight Valley and Speedstorm since early access as well. Gameloft will ALWAYS put money first, quality of life and fairness to low spenders last. They do deliver on content, though, which is why I still enjoy these games and will continue to play them. BUT I also waste my money in gachas and silly Disney games locked behind paywalls like these. (I was gifted the smallest founder edition, and bought the ultimate founders edition later, talk about a waste of money) Plus half the content of this game will be locked behind the paid DLCs. Releasing this paid DLC while keeping the premium shop in game is a bad direction and an excuse to lock content behind paywalls for an already (now) pricey and microtransaction filled game. If you're thinking of getting into the game, do not expect to get all the content in the game easily. This game is set up as a free to play game including season passes and microtransactions shops, which was the original intent, but is now purchasable with the same money grubbing practices in game on top of it.  I'm going to keep playing the game and spending all my money on it, so I know I will be judged to hell. But I am weak and the game itself is pretty fun and caters to my addictions. If you want a Disney-fied Animal Crossing with a bit of story, it's good as long as you ignore all the extra purchasable content. I just can't recommend the game as of now for lack of content and the piss poor business practices. I'll recommend the game when the microtransactions stop for a paid game with paid DLC and seasons passes.Edit: I just wanted to emphasize that they promised no matter if the game was free or paid for, that there would not be any content locked behind a paywall only cosmetics. Rapunzel is in the DLC only. They have paid for content for Wall-e. That's literally content behind a paywall. They are just liars and crappy devs. Don't listen to the people who stick up for the devs. The game itself is fun, so those reviews make sense, but the devs know how much they are milking this game monetarily and that alone is scummy.

Original Review: Plays at 60fps on Steam Deck and looks fantastic on medium settings, though I ran into a few bugs and weird issues that caused me to hard close the game. Luckily it autosaves about every 5 minutes and you can manually save whenever you want.You have to use a physical keyboard to put in your name at the beginning because it doesn't register the virtual keyboard. The game plays in real time like Animal Crossing but everything doesn't shut down at night and the city stays lively. Energy is like Stardew Valley where you can refill it with food you harvest and cook, but you can also restore it by just going home. Cooking and gardening has more value here unlike ACNH which is just tacked on. The gameplay is no more basic than a Harvest Moon or Animal Crossing game, but the quests add something extra and help the game feel like a light adventure game as well. It's arguably better than the recent harvest moon games and no breakable tools like the most recent ACNH. There appears to be no time gating, you unlock things with gameplay. For example, you don’t have to wait for your house to upgrade once you’ve paid for it. You can play the game every day for as long as you want. There is far more to do and a much bigger world than Animal Crossing.FYI, at the time of this review Ultimate Edition also gives you the Celestial Sea Turtle from Deluxe Edition even though it doesn't mention it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not looking for a game for myself. I was actually looking for a family member who I thought might like it, so I read through the comments. I noticed a lot of adult men who could not stop raving about the game. I figured if even guys love this game then it's gotta be good, right? It seemed like most everyone loved the game. Well, it turned out my instincts were right! I absolutely LOVE this game now too! And I've played my fair share of survival games where you have to craft things and farm for materials or resources, but this game takes out A LOT of the tediousness from farming and crafting. You farm and craft faster and it's made easier. You even find yourself enjoying the farming and crafting and doing all the tasks that are generally incredibly tedious in other survival games. What's most rewarding about this game are the quests and the characters. Its main story is pretty brilliant in my opinion and how it's interwoven. It's really rewarding clearing areas of the night thorns, while getting to save and interact with Disney characters we all know and love. It's also genius making this survival game with its characters and quests as the most REWARDING part of the game! I enjoy unlocking new areas. Once you get a lot of star coins, you'll be waiting for Scrooge McDuck's store to drop its new clothing line or furniture sets! I honestly wanted a game that I could relax to that's single player. There's so much negativity and toxicity online that you run into. There's many things going on in the world right now that people can feel down about. This game definitely lifts one's spirits! It's a great game to relax to as you create your own world surrounded by familiar Disney characters. There's a pleasantness about the world and the art designs that's comforting. All I can say is that once you start playing, you'll be hooked! I played early access, so of course there's still bugs that need to be fixed. Here's a few bugs I noticed: -Disney characters who mined with me were getting stuck during the mining. -Some areas had a hard time re-spawning their flowers back like in the Sunlit Plateau, until I unlocked the entire area. -When the Disney characters leveled, sometimes the game would freeze and I'd have to restart the game.-Some of the furniture I bought didn't show up when I tried to place it in my house like Stitch's TV. It was invisible!-Pua the pig didn't show up when I was rescuing him, so there should be an animation for that. I had no clue that I had earned him as a companion pet either.  The bugs are not that big of a deal, because you can easily work around them. I know it was a little frustrating to wait for a flower to repopulate but once I unlocked the rest of the area the spawn rate increased. One issue I had with the game was some of the areas like Forest of Valor and the Forgotten Land, those places were hard to walk around due to the fact that the trees make it REALLY hard to see sometimes. I hope that when they add new areas that they start making the trees taller or higher up or something. It makes it difficult to forage. And some of the quests could be more interesting. If it weren't for the quests and the characters, the game would be stagnant. I was concerned that the game might end up like the Sims, which I get easily bored with. The characters and quests make it a thousand times more rewarding. Plus, you have cosmetic items to look forward to. I didn't find the potions for mining very helpful as they don't last as long as the ones for fishing. What are some helpful tips for new players?-Keep your iron ore, rocks, and coal ore. Coal ore you need for everything, including cooking. Iron ore you need continually, you'll run out of it the fastest. Rocks can also be a difficult material to come by when you need it, so don't sell it. -Always have a Disney character with you whenever you're farming resources. For example, if you're trying to mine iron ore... ALWAYS have a Disney character with you who has mining. You'll get extra resources from them if you have them along.-Iron ore is NOT in every area. The only places you can find iron ore is in Forest of Valor, Glade of Trust, Frosted Heights, Sunlit Plateau, and the Forgotten Lands. You'll need to unlock one of these areas in order to mine for iron ore. Do not waste your dreamlight, until you've unlocked an area with iron ore. -Every time you level up Disney characters, it will unlock quests. Be careful not to level up several characters at the same time or you'll get overwhelmed by all the quests. Try to focus on leveling one or two Disney characters at a time. -The quickest way to get rich is to sell off your gems, until you unlock the Forgotten Lands and can become a millionaire by selling off pumpkins. Try to sell between 300-600 pumpkins a day when you can afford it! -If you're having a hard time fishing a specific catch, you can make a potion as a miracle fishing bait. Use it on the white circle fishing spots to turn them into yellow circle fishing spots. -The foods I prefer are Arendellian Pickled Herring, Potato Leek Soup, Ratatouille, and Fruit Cake for energy. -You can get pet companions by feeding animals in the area their favorite foods. Feed all the animals once a day in each area. Companions can be summoned by going to your wardrobe and going into the companions option. -The time of day in game is based on your own time zone. Things I'd like to see more of... more Disney dress options to buy at the store. I did like that for some of the rewards that dresses were a reward. I'd like to see a lot more content released like maybe a big expansion with more characters and quests. There's something very calming and relaxing about the game that makes you feel good. It's a very positive and pleasant experience. Maybe something to do with the familiarity of the characters by getting to help out characters you recognize from your childhood is pretty damn amazing! I could not recommend this game enough. If you want a feel good game, it doesn't get any better than this! Plus, Ursula gets to be your neighbor. Just what you always wanted, right?

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 1 (9/6/2023)With an additional hours on the game, I'd like to give a quick update.  Having already spent $70+ USD on my 2 copies (PC/switch), I was going to continue playing despite my initial review. Get that bang for my buck.  First, I want to give credit where due. The snapshot contest update does help some of the moonstone concerns. I enjoy the challenges and seeing other players creations. However, the most recent update has increased the number of crashes substantially. And I'm pretty sure the original amount of moonstones I had on my switch disappeared during a sync after saving to the cloud on my PC, as the amount of moonstones originally varied by device.  With these crashes and issues syncing, this is just for the primary location. The game teases other locations beyond, so what happens as the game grows?  I think there is still a lot of room for improvement all around, but at the end of the day, I absolutely love the story lines thus far and the plot. I still have concerns that at the end, it will still require spending bank to unlock future locations, quest lines, etc. Even with this snapshot challenge, I'm not sure that's enough to change my mind. Also, these Star Paths, will they repeat once the game goes free? Or is this content a one shot?  There are longish gaps between paths and I'm not sure I understand how this is going to scale. I have a lot of questions, but will keep an open mind. ORIGINAL POST (6/8/2023)I really wish I was writing a positive review. With over 200 hours on my steam account, and having 2 copies (steam AND switch), I love the plot of this game. It's everything I have ever wanted in an RPG, playing with your favorite disney pals. But this game is not even out of early access and the devs are already price gouging the hell out of this game. It's quickly ruined what would have been my favorite game of all time. And let me be clear. If there were later DLC after full launch, I wouldn't be this upset. But the latest special pack is 4000 Moonstones ( 5500 Moonstones cost $17.99) for a few outfits. _childDocuments_.review: It's a charming game to start, and Merlin being your first friend in the Valley is a great start. The spaces are cozy. It's great that you can make and design your own clothes, and that's one of the best parts of it. It's a nice, chill game for the most part, and it's pretty to look at.Unfortunately, the game syncs with real-world time, which means that if you're nocturnal like me, you will only ever see the game then, and several characters, including the only one I especially like, are asleep for 3-4 hours of the main time I'm available to play the game. So now the only real reason for me to play the game is not even available for most of the time I'll be free to play.Additionally, while I understand that the Ratatouille movie has a wide range of dishes, I found the kind of huge seafood fixation a little gross. It's nice there are specifically vegetarian dishes, but it also expects you to make other dishes for achievements that you might not be comfortable making. On that same note, the fishing isn't very enjoyable and the first option in your inventory shouldn't be to eat the fish, that's insane and frankly made me feel like putting the game down for good.It's nice that you have warnings for things that might upset people, but you seemed to forget about that definitely being something that will upset people that's really easy to do. The Magical World series did a much better job of addressing the fishing element, which seems unfortunately obligatory for games anymore, and it's rarely done well.The only other major problem I had with the game was that the sprint doesn't work. For some reason, a lot of games recently have struggled with controller support, I don't know why. But this may be something that just will be addressed soon. The game is in early access, and things are being updated all the time.I liked seeing WALL-E and Merlin. I'm not honestly the biggest fan of some of the movies in the game, and I absolutely hate some of them, but at least they're presented in a fun way, and more characters are being added regularly. It's easy to imagine that most people will be able to find someone to like.Hopefully the problems will be addressed. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start my review by addressing Gameloft. Over the years, I've played many Gameloft games including NOVA, The Oregon Trail,  New York Nights and New York Nights 2, Miami Nights, Hero of Sparta, Dungeon Hunter, Dogz, Asphalt, and many many more. Gameloft mobile games have a unique charm to them. Their art styles are eye-grabbing, their controls are always fluid and seamless. While most of their mobile games offer in-app purchases, they never really impend progress too much and focus more on the core experience of having fun with their worlds.When I saw that Disney's Dreamlight Valley would be developed by Gameloft, I was surprised, excited, and nervous. Gameloft absolutely knows what they are doing when it comes to offering a superb gameplay experience. However, a lot of Gameloft's "premium" games were released in the early days of the iOS AppStore. Is this game a change of heart and direction for Gameloft? Are they trying something new when it comes to diving into the world of console game experiences? Gameloft actually designed a game called "Disney Magic Kingdoms" for iOS and Android in 2016. The game was a kids-oriented theme park strategy game. Players would collect currency, expand their kingdom and use optional in-app purchases to no longer wait for actions. Disney already has a relationship with Gameloft because of this, so it's no surprise to me that they would be approached for a larger scale console game experience.So how does Disney Dreamlight Valley deliver? Is it a glorified mobile game? Does it have a nasty in-app purchase experience? Is the game going to make you feel good with happy moments and then slam you by taking your wallet?! I'm here to say, no. It really isn't at all. I'm not sure if that was a Disney decision or a Gameloft decision, but whoever is handling things and making the decisions clearly knows the experience they were trying to create, and it works VERY well with Disney Dreamlight Valley. If you are a fan of The Sims, Animal Crossing, and even Kingdom Hearts then I believe you will feel right at home with this game. Players are introduced to a intro cutscene of leaving the big city in favor of the countryside. When they arrive at their home, they are whisked away to Dreamlight Valley, a hub of sorts for all Disney and Pixar intellectual property. Unfortunately, the Valley has been overrun with thorns and other dangerous flora, causing it to be a shadow of its former glory. Many Disney characters have left. It's up to you to restore Dreamlight Valley's former glory and save the day.Dreamlight Valley relies heavily on Animal Crossing-like mechanics to drive the story forward: farming, fishing, digging, and pickaxing materials to either craft or sell for extra in-game currency. Players will spend lots of time wandering the valley in search of useful items to complete fetch quests. Successfully fulfilling fetch quests improve the relationships of your Valley residents and offer rewards in the form of cosmetics, money, and background story cutscenes. As the Valley slowly gets cleaned up, the player will also have the opportunity to warp to the former homes of the Valley residents, convincing them to return to the Valley to set up shop. Each world offers different challenges that must completed. One nice touch that I loved is that some of the worlds take place after their respective films. For example, in the Moana world, it takes place "after" the events of the film. My personal favorite world was the Ratatouille world. Getting to see Remy again was a wholesome experience, and having him move to the Valley has been a blast. Nothing is more fun than finding your favorite Disney character, inviting them to hang out, and spending the day with them.Disney and Gameloft also spare no expense at including fully voiced over characters and a wonderful OST. (Please can we get the OST on Spotify?!) The world of Dreamlight Valley uses music, sound, and voice-over work very effectively and in some cases, I've gotten choked up with emotions from just how perfect each scene is crafted in converging story with audio.My biggest critiques with Dreamlight Valley revolve around the uncertainty of the game's future, as well as the game's engine. Starting with the latter, I've experienced issues with crashing. My game also randomly goes offline, disabling cloud saving. The only way I can re-enable cloud saving is by closing and re-opening the game, thus reconnecting to the cloud saving database. I don't have a problem with that, but it happens frequently. On the PC version, my game has crashed about four times. The crashes happen randomly and I've tried uninstalling/re-installing the game. When the game isn't crashing, the experience is smooth and wonderful. As for my next critique and concern, the game's future. Gameloft and Disney are doing a wonderful job at giving the player a lot to do, and providing generous amounts of fun to be had without the issues of paid energy, "hurrying" by paying with currency, or any sort of shady in-app purchase mechanics. The only time the in-game premium currency is brought up is if you would like to purchase the Dreamlight Valley "Battle Pass" which gives you cosmetics, in-game furniture, and design motifs for your clothes.If the game's premium currency are restricted to specifically Battle Passes and Sims style "expansion packs", then I think the vast majority of people (myself included) would be more than happy to support Dreamlight Valley and it's future. But if Gameloft and Disney stray from this and start including shady in-app purchase mechanics, rest assured my review of this game will change drastically. As of right now in the game's Early Access phase, I am more than satisfied with the experience. Its been an absolute blast, and in some cases much MUCH better than Animal Crossing. If Disney and Gameloft can maintain their existing functionality and features - I think Disney's Dreamlight Valley will have a bright future ahead of it. The game is very finely tuned and polished, the storyline is crafted wonderfully, and the gameplay loop is a love letter to Animal Crossing, The Sims, Stardew Valley, and many other life simulation game farming sims. I would argue that Disney Dreamlight Valley even sets a new precedence for other life simulation games out there. Gameloft and Disney have taken many notes and I'm really happy that they have delivered an experience that works so well. Thank you Gameloft and Disney for this wonderful game and experience. I can't wait to dive more into the world of Dreamlight Valley, compare experiences with friends, and continue to help shape the community and future of this wonderful life simulation game. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first of all, this game isn't free, and for an 'Early Access' title it goes against everything which EA should even be meant for - development of the game with the help of the community. Instead the content updates are very few and far between, seemingly not too caring of what the players think (might be my biased opinion). Implemented are 'major-transaction' cash shop with multiple FOMO tactics in the form of..	1. non-recurring Star Paths (bought reward tracks for you to work through every 2 months or so) ; 	2. very expensive weekly Premium Shop (that will probably rotate items back eventually, like some actual 'free to play' games do) ; 	3. daily login bonus (that gives next to nothing to allow any premium shop items, and makes you work in even getting it) ; 	4. and a whole bunch of mechanics on different timers (discussions with characters ; critter spawns ; Scrooge's item shop ; etc.) just to push the daily interaction of players, resulting more player retention 	..and more invested the players are, more likely they are to keep coming back to see the cash shop and spend an exuberant amount of money on tiny additions.  The game itself is somewhat okay to play, but it will probably forever be in the shadow of other games in this genre. If you are (or have been) in interest of games like Animal Crossing (AC), then Dreamlight Valley (DV) can provide the same fun factor for a while - especially with its nice Disney artstyle and charm ; and also it being a new addition, bringing that 'new game excitement' that seemingly a lot of people are giving praise to this game for (them either not having better past experiences, or just delusional for what this game really is).After a few weeks in, working through the daily tasks, progressing the 'story', and finishing a Star Path, it comes apparent on how little this game actually offers and how it operates on dumb modern 'game as a service' grind. Some examples:	1. Want to craft a balloon arch to decorate a small area of a single path? Go hit rocks and gather other materials for an hour or two. 	2. Want to progress the fantastic Story? Here's 10 meaningless back-and-forth fetch quests that culminates with a group activity (concert/show/feast/..) that happens, but doesn't actually happen (fade to black - here's your cosmetic reward). 	3. Star Paths are surely there to spice up the gameplay experience, right? Nope. Just 50 additional fetch quests (most of which can be done in a day or two if you've already played the game for a while, and built up supplies, with some 'duties' that can take up to 5 days of 'discussions' to be had), that is purely forced in just to have a cosmetic pass in this game. 	4. What if I missed any Star Path items? Well that’s just too bad. If you don't have a time machine, then you'll just have to have all these digital files installed on your machine, that we conveniently locked you out of, just to punish the non-active / non-timely / no-paying customer base. 	5. Scrooge's item shop will surely have lots of fun items to decorate the island with, right? Yeah, you get a couple items every day. How about that Corner Cupboard reskin #37, or a L-couch reskin #56? Oof, you just spent 20k gold coins on a duplicate again.. well that's sad. Better go farm more pumpkins buddy.	6. At least it is a modern game, that improves on the genre? Nah.. can't have  game saves ; can't replay the story ; cloud saves are nice to transission between multiple play machines (but have made people lost their saves without proper backup system) ; lacking tons of expected 'quality of life' features (oh so many games to take good examples from) ; and my personal pet peeve - the game engine can do Ultrawide just fine, but doesn't support it (so in 8 months a dev team hasn't enabled something that probably took a day at most for a modder to do, so I always have to run this game with a 'fix'). Only thing I can praise DV for is its 'build mode', which is nice to use, but the game has limitations on placed item amounts, and just doesn't have the item variety and interactivity that AC:NH has -a 3 y/o game that has none of the predatory and FOMO tactics DV has, and is more fun in every single way. For a parent looking at these reviews, my recommendation is buying your kid a Switch and a AC:NH copy instead (or just Sims with all its major packs) - with how Gameloft will try and squeeze its playerbase, it will save you money in the long run. DV being made into a 'free' game also doesn't guarantee its survivability in the future if the Disney overlords decide to shut this project down.I've given DV a lot of my time and feedback, and I really wanted it to be better (and hopefully there's enough QoL fixes in the future to at least improve it), but I have a gut feeling that it will just stay as another milking machine. If you play this game, then seek out trainers to make the game more enjoyable ; make manual backups ; and DO NOT feed it any more money if you've already bought into the 'Ultimate' experience (something that apparently is worth a single Star Path and 1-2 weeks of Premium shop items). Do better Gameloft!
