_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking for another game that could spark joy for me again. You know the type. You buy it, download it, and pray you wont be bored of it in the next 2 days. Then suddenly its 3 months later it has an absolute choke hold over your entire life. It determines when you eat and when you sleep. Now when you're at work thinking about going home to play it or you are sitting in the public discord chatting with total strangers about the next update coming out only to realize you forgot to leave your computer on so that it would update automatically before you got home. You have a panic attack and your boss sends you home early. Thank god. Now you can fix your mistake and not miss a precious moment after the update goes live.It is early access there are bugs but the community is very helpful with work around tips. There's a ton of potential here and  while some things have absolutely been done phenomenally, there are some details that leave something to be desired. Namely some of the dress designs for max character level rewards. they look awkward on player characters and they don't move well. You can tell its a flat layer design on the dress even though it should be multiple layers that move independently. Some are done well like Moana's dress reward but ones like Elsa and Ariel are hard to even look at imo. Mechanics are smooth and the hubs are easy to use/navigate. They clearly listened to feedback people have given about games like Stardew valley and animal crossing. While this game is very different in lots of ways its also very similar in others. The writing and quest development is where this game really shines in my opinion. sure some of them are "Gather these resources" at some point but there are so many layers to every quest that involve so many characters and new/different mechanics.  I could go on forever but my crops are probably ready and Eric needs my help. JUST BUY IT!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I had high hopes for this game. I enjoyed myself for some time at first. I was able to see the potential, but I cannot in good conscience recommend this game. Right now, it is in early access and a lot of people online have held up the early access status as some sort of shield that somehow makes this game immune to all criticism. Well, it might explain the many many bugs. That's the point of early access. There will be bugs. I understand.BUT it absolutely does not make DDV a good game. There are issues, that will continue after the early acces period is over. And they will become apparent the longer you play the game.PRO:- It looks pretty? That one is down to personal taste. But they did manage to translate 2D characters into a 3D game without them looking weird, so I think they did great on that front.- There is no storage limit of items (there is a limit to placed items, but not the storage).- The main story can be played without spending more money- Touch of magic tool let's you customize some clothes and furniture. This can be fun.CON:The game feels like a mobile game.Some people might like mobile games. I like some of them, too. But just think of all the things that might bother you with mobile games and know that all of this will be present in DDV. All of it. This includes, but needs to be mentioned specifically: the horrific prices of the premium shop, with micro transactions that are beyond a rip off. Two backpacks, that your character can wear for 1500 Moonstones. (For context: the 1200 Moonstones bundle costs 4,99$ and you would still need 300 Moonstones more. For two backpacks.)Want to have a kitchen that is inspired by Frozen? That is actually divided into three seperate bundles in the premium shop. All together it costs 3450 moonstones and it doesn't even include a sink or fridge. I imagine that will be in a future bundle. But even worse: Recently they introduced quests for Wall-E that you can pay for with moonstones. It costs 4000 Moonstones. The closest moonstone bundle to buy this is 5500 moonstones for 20$ so that makes this, what... around 15$ for a hollow feeling fetch quest, and some clothes (a dress/suit, a hat with feathers, a trashcan lid for your head - yes, really- and a shoe as decor.)?15 Dollars. Let that sink in. At what point does it stop being a micro transaction and becomes a macro transaction?The storylines are usually piecemeal. You get a sentence or two from an NPC, then you have to grind or do a fetch quest to get the next piece. Sometimes the game will force you to play at specific hours of the day and since the game is linked to real time, there is no way of circumventing this. Only able to play in the evening? Well too bad, you won't be able to progress the quest.After you finished the main and character quests, the game is basically dead. You can grind for more materials if you want. Or you could try to decorate. But the way to get new furniture is luck based and you probably won't get enough for decorating to be fun. This might change after early access, but for now... most people stop playing shortly after an update cause there is nothing to do. There is more I could say. But this might give you an idea of what it is like. Please do yourself a favour and don't buy it in early access. Wait for it to be free to play later this year or maybe just skip it entirely and safe yourself a ton of money and a headache.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell no. Do not recommend. Stay far away.I wasn't there during the F2P fiasco, so not including that.This game is what I had assumed, a paid game, meaning you paid one time and play it, with maybe occasional dlc.Turns out, it's a F2P model. Has battle pass, premium shop and additional 'quests' that is locked behind paywall.Again, I absolutely do not recommend it whatsoever. Game functions on real time, a tad similar to animal crossing.As much as how disappointing Animal Crossing New Horizon was compared to its predecessor, this game compared to AC is horrid. Not including the whole garbage premium crap (also expensive).Ex. In game quest, rainy weather only spawn certain fish, but that fish is required for progress in a QUEST. it's not optional. and rainy weather is RNG. This was one of the main breaking point for me, I would be okay if it's just for collection, but to proceed in a quest?! I wanted to remove the bones & giant ice chunk, but can't due to the rainy fish related quests. I hate Animal Crossing for their stupid "extend gameplay" mechanic for crafting one thing at a time and can't skip cutscene. But this really takes the cake.Another, there is a stamina bar, you can replenish via cooking, but if you're trying to grow crops (this again, is real time based duration), it's not fun whatsoever. You can sorta get around in remy's realm(exploit). But it's still not fun at all. And the crops need monitoring and to keep them water.The characters' realm is very lackluster and sad, there's absolutely nothing else in there aside from the fact that you're there to just get the characters out. That's it.All the charm that even the disappointment Animal Crossing has, this one doesn't at all. There's no freedom in what you want to do, and instead, locked into RNG for quests that unlock important perks.

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts to give this is a not recommended since it is a rather wholesome game to play in sort of the same vein to Animal Crossing. _childDocuments_.review: Truly addicting and really fun, definitely a relaxing chill out game.I've finished all there is currently in the game but for a new player there is loads to do already and I'm looking forward to seeing what they add and what new characters are going to be added, as it's Disney the list if almost endless :DStar path can sometimes feel like a chore but otherwise the tasks are mostly pretty simple.I wish you could craft more than one food item at a time, maybe a max of 5 or something would be good.Placement of items can sometimes be a little annoying and I wish you could place things a lot closer together.But other than those few picky things I'd definitely recommend the game if you're looking for something chill to play and enjoy games that are sim like :)Update: So they added a premium shop, which seems to change items every 5 or so days and the items it sells are cosmetic, house items, decorations, outfits, hair styles and so on. The catch being you need moonstones to buy these item sets and the pricing is not good much like any other games that have micro transactions..You can find moonstones in blue chests as you play but nowhere near enough to be able to get a set of items or all 4 sets from the premium shop... So if you really badly want that stuff you buy moonstones with real money. For this reason i wouldn't recommend the game as it's just ridiculous, I knew they where adding in the ability to buy moonstones at some point and i should have known the pricing would not be good.You do not have to buy the items to enjoy the game and i would never suggest buying the items from the premium shop or buying moonstones but hopefully it's your money and you do with it what you please.They could have easily added other tasks for limited times where those items were rewards or popped them in Scrooges shop for a high gold price, you know the currency that you don't pay for.Premium shop and moonstones are a huge no no. I wish there was a mixed option when writing a review as i personally do really like the game as there is tons to do and its pretty relaxing, but the premium shop is not necessary, there should be other ways to get pretty items, like you know, quests or scrooge's shop.Ignoring the premium shop and the buying of moonstones, i would still recommend the game.Update 2: I just wanted to add some more thoughts about the moonstones and premium shop. The chests you can find that have moonstones in them now have 50 stones, the store still rotates items and the items seem to come back around occasionally that I've seen. What I really want to say in this updated review bit though is out of all the games that have micro transactions that I've played, Disney Dreamlight Valley is one of the better ones. Since playing the game through a lot of updates and star path seasons I've managed to get extra tasks for most of the star path seasons (which you unlock with moonstones, I missed one though) and buy some things from the premium store, all WITHOUT buying moonstones! I've managed to do all that because there are a few ways you can get moonstones for free!, of course you still have the chests you can find but now they also have a dream snaps competition each week and you can earn moonstones just by participating!I'm not saying that I now love micro transactions woohoo! No I still think they're not good but unfortunately that's how a lot of games are now, I'm just saying that Disney Dreamlight Valley is more giving to their players, which is surprising because, well, 'Disney' haha.Anyway as I mentioned, I've not bought a single pack of moonstones and I personally don't plan on it as I can get them just by playing, there have been certain things in the store that I just personally don't care for but if you are someone who wants it all! You'll probably have to spend some money to get it all.Disregarding the store completely though, the game is still very much enjoyable and you don't need anything from the premium shop to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game. If you are an ACNH fan or DIsney or both, this game is 1000% for you. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Disney Dreamlight Valley is a nothing sandwichThis game could've been any cozy gamer's wet dream. Instead, it's just an empty shell where a good game *could* exist, if Disney cared about anything other than milking our wallets as much as possible. I have completed everything there is to do in the game. Here's everything they said about the game vs the sad reality:- Hanging out with Disney characters is extremely bland. The only thing they are good for is assigning them a specialty. For example, if you assign Mickey's role to be mining, then when you mine an ore there's a chance Mickey will throw another piece at you. That's your entire "friendship" with any character.- The quests are laughable. Collect/harvest/craft X thing and deliver to Y character. Or even better, "go to talk to this guy". The most unimaginative, repetitive quests I've ever seen.- One thing I was looking forward to was visiting different worlds, like Wall-E's world. They're just decorative areas where the only thing you do is complete a few quests to make them come to your valley. There is never a reason to visit them again. You can't do anything, you get nothing else from them. The "worlds" are also sometimes just ONE room, like Remy's kitchen or a kid's room for Toy Story characters.- The store is built on scarcity, honestly there are very few clothing items, and they only show you a handful each day, probably to make sure you don't wipe out the entire store and force you to come back to the game every day. There's also a 20 item limit to how many decorative items you can buy in a single day, which makes no sense. If you're in the middle of decorating a room tough luck, come back tomorrow.- The clothes and decorations are for the most part incredibly bland. Considering it's Disney, there were sooooo many options better than "yellow tshirt with logo from movie" and "teal tshirt with logo from movie", are you kidding me? The Sims 1 had more complex clothing options and they didn't have the technology and resources Disney has.- The furniture is infuriatingly minimalistic. There are a few pieces that look good, but there is sooooo much fluff, for example there are 5 or 6 different items that are the same counter, but one has the door on the left, one has the door on the right, REALLY?! And they multiply that fluff by making the same set in several extremely opaque colors with no texture or detail, they're basically CUBES- The NPC interactions/dialogue are laughably shallow. Same 5-10 lines of dialogue, that don't take into account any of your previous interactions with them. When 2 NPCs meet they have one or two "dialogues", which are just prescripted nonsense- The game is clearly missing chunks of content. At the end of a big quest line you usually put together a party, and take a picture to complete the quest. The game fades to black, and I'm sure there's supposed to be a cutscene there.- The animation glitches are inexcusable for a game that's been in early access for so long. I've had the game 6 months prior to full launch, there have been no improvements. Characters glitch all over the place, get stuck in a spot while walking, teleport to a different area if you enter/exit a building. - Jack Skellington is very hard to interact with because he's so tall and the dialogue option only appears in certain camera angles. Add to that that if there are several characters around they tend to gang up on you and I've talked to Mickey/Mirabel/Remy so many times when I wanted to talk to Jack to finish a quest.- The price for premium cosmetic items is ridiculous. 10$ for a character skin, when I already paid 40$, are you mad?!- Like others have said, they have a couple questlines behind premium currency paywalls which is a massive ♥♥♥♥ move on their part- As an extra ♥♥♥♥ you, my Ursula premium quest was bugged for THREE months, they didn't even fix it at full release, they released a patch a week later, for a quest that was just "collect 10 of x", and the 10th item wouldn't spawn, it's not rocket science to fix that.This game feels like a mobile port, and I think it would have worked much better as a phone game, free to play and filled to the brim with predatory microtransactions.Do yourself a favor and play any other cozy game, there are a bajillion of them, and none are as bad as this.

_childDocuments_.review: So I would describe myself as a casual Disney enjoyer. I like some of the movies, and that's about it. At first, I disregarded this game as shovelware, but I saw a review that compared it to Animal Crossing, which convinced me to take a second look, and I'm glad I did.I've been playing Animal Crossing since Population Growing, and I found New Horizons to be a little hollow. Dreamlight Valley hits the itch that NH failed to scratch for me, as well as a healthy dose of inspiration from Story of Seasons and other like farming sims. I would describe Dreamlight Valley as "like Animal Crossing with RPG quests". You are tasked with beautifying your village, which includes cleaning up thorns (weeds), crafting and buying furniture, upgrading facilities, decorating, inviting characters to live in your town, and building friendships with them. There is a main story questline, and each character has their own personal storylines that progress as you gain friendship levels. PROS:The character creator is very robust with a lot of options, including a lot of textured hair styles and hijab clothing items. Animations feel very good and have a lot of love put into them. Gathering is really satisfying thanks to the animation and sound design. (My favorite is mining, something about the mining feedback is extremely satisfying).Each character is well-written and feels accurate to their movie portrayal, even the villains. The villains you befriend make it clear that your friendship is one of convenience, which is a good narrative conceit to have them in your town without watering down their personalities. One of the things that bothered me about NH is how sterile and saccharine all of your villagers were. Which brings me to the main story. While this game is still appropriate for all ages, I was surprised at how compelling and sometimes grim the story could be. The story and your interactions are chock full of references, but they aren't necessary to follow the plot. While the game does operate on real time, you can always progress the story, so I never felt like I had to wait until the next day to do anything interesting.NOW HERE COMES THE CONS:The game is in Early Access still, so some bugs are to be expected. I have encountered plenty, but none of them game-breaking. The dev team has been very transparent and open about the feedback process so far, so I feel confident in their ability to fix them.Most of the cosmetics in this game are very feminine. People who prefer to dress masc will have a harder time finding things they like. Most of the characters award dresses for their level 10 friendship reward, with the exception of Ariel, who offers a dress and a suit. I would like to see them add more variety in cosmetics, and maybe retroactively add options to the other level 10 rewards, like with Ariel. I am concerned about monetization. Whenever paid cosmetics are offered, there is the tendency for your paid cosmetics to have a lot more love and care put into them than anything you can obtain in game. Recently, Moana's level 10 dress was changed from her iconic red and orange to a blue palette that doesn't evoke Moana at all. Ostensibly, the reward was always intended to be blue, but this rings false when the other characters offer their iconic cosmetics as level 10 rewards. Allegedly, this was changed so that the original color palette will be sold in the cosmetics shop, which sets a bad precedent. Regardless of how it was originally intended, it feels like players had something taken away from them just to be sold back to them for a premium. I hope this is not an omen of things to come. IN CONCLUSION:Even if you aren't a huge Disney fan, Dreamlight Valley is an extremely well-made game on its own merits, and it's easy to see how much love and care is put into making a fun gaming experience that can be enjoyed by anyone. I am eager to see how the game expands in the future, and what new characters will be added. I'm happy to pay to support the devs, and as long as the devs respect the players and don't squander their good will, I'll be happy to continue to support the in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Dreamlight at launch and loved it, however, recent updates and the addition of the cash shop leave much to be desired. So while this game is very good, the cash shop is just... not great.Pros: -An amazingly made game with solid chill farming gameplay.-Lots of way to decorate your island and home.-Lots of amazing characters and outfits.-A great story.-Lots of things to do.Cons:The cash shop. The cash shop in its entirety. Now people will say they warned us about the cash shop and that you can earn those items in game from the star path, that is true. However, there isn't enough currency in the star path to get everything from the cash shop and the cash shop is constantly rotating. That means if you miss an item it isn't coming back. This may not be a big deal to a lot of people, it wasn't to me either because I played for the story. That is until I realized that now the only new houses you can get are on that cash store unless they add more to the story line. Almost all the new character outfits and forms are locked behind not just the star path but now the cash shop. I was looking forward to grinding to get the new summer outfits but nope, they are in the cash shop. The moment I cannot earn any new cool things in game and its all going to the cash shop, that shows me in order to enjoy anything new I will have to pull out my wallet. So yes, I do like this game, I just don't like what the cash shop has become. I understand this game will become free at some point but right now its not. The prices of some of the items are pretty high as well. I am okay with paying more money for things like dlc with more characters and story, but not cosmetics.If you don't mind the cash shop, yes I recommend this game. It is very good. Just be careful about that cash shop, don't spend any money on things you aren't sure you actually want.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are already a Disney fan and love playing games with a farming/crafting/sim vibe, then this game is for you.  If you're not a Disney fan then you still may find this game loads of fun just remember that it'll quickly be full of Disney characters roaming through the game.  The quest mechanics are pretty simple which is to be expected since the developers wanted to make sure the game is playable for people of all ages.  I've seen many reviews where people list their pros v cons, so I will do that here.Pro:--The graphics are pretty good. Every Disney character you unlock for your valley will look and act the way you would expect them to.  Especially if you're a Donald Duck fan.  Everytime he goes into a temper tantrum, I just smile because it's so funny.  And it's adorable to hear Minnie say, "Remember I love you!--As mentioned above, the quests you do to unlock characters and things is pretty simple.  This is great for those who are looking for a relaxing game with little thought required.--You don't just interact with adorable Disney characters, there is stuff for your creative minds to do as well.  Aside from having nearly total controle over where you place buildings and items, there is also customization in the form of a wardrobe creator.  I'm not that artistic, but I've seen so many beautiful items that others have created.Cons:-- After a few hours of play, you may become annoyed with your villagers.  There's only so many times you want to hear Maui get in your face and say, "Hey, it's your favorite demigod!"  or Ariel say, "One of these days, I hope I can be a part of YOUR world."-- Although most of the main quests are easy to complete, there are some quests that you will not be able to figure out without checking social media or the internet.  If you don't have a PC and no access to the internet, then there will be things you will be unable to do because there is no instuctions on certain quests in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game.Admittedly, I have only played an hour of it so not really enough to judge it fully but enough things irked me to have the game refunded and to leave a bad review.I bought the gold edition to include the DLC so spent just shy of £60. Base game is £34 at the time of writing.Sorry, but this game is not worth it's high price. I know this is Disney but this game should not be this clunky or glitchy to start off with. I can already tell this game has not been polished whatsoever.Real-life time sync is weird too, for someone who works and can only play during the evenings. Not to mention the severe FOMO and micro-transactions this game has. Nope, I don't care, but this is not acceptable for an expensive game especially one that is meant to work as a singleplayer. This as well as the clunkiness and bugs within the first hour of my gameplay, were enough to turn me away from ever playing this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Disney Dreamlight Valley. It is the perfect mix of your typical grindy games like Minecraft, Stardew Valley, and Sims except it has Disney characters!! _childDocuments_.review: Do you like Animal Crossing? Do you like Harvest Moon without all the stupid romancing? Do you want to be a Disney princess? If yes to all, then game is tailor-made to you. If you'd rather be a Disney prince, then sorry your costume choices are severely limited, but it's ok, you can still wear the dresses for now since absolutely nothing is gender-locked, not even beards.The game loop is pretty simple - Befriend a Disney character, maybe build them a house, then grind a bunch of materials building things to help solve their woes, then they unlock a tool perk/building/maybe just a dress. The dialogue is simple but each character is well-written enough. Your own character is pretty bold and can get some dark/not-nice dialogue choices as well (for a Disney game that lets you befriend villains anyway). Almost unnoticed in the frenzy of making everyone your best friend is a well-featured if somewher janky layout builder with tons of furniture waiting to be cataloged. That being said, it is Early Access. The game itself will be F2P on official launch but the only way to play now is by purchasing a Founder Pack. Since there is nothing currently purchasable with the moonstones aside from the Pixar season pass booster, it is hard to say if the higher-cost packs are worth buying aside from the increased amount of stones. Deluxe includes a blue gilded turtle pet and a Buzz Lightyear-themed outfit, and Ultimate has the Cinderella ball gown costume and her Prince's tux costume as well as a royal fox kit pet.And being Early Access, the game is riddled with jank and potentially game-breaking bugs. While I managed to evade all of the dreaded softlocks completing all of the current characters/quests/pixar stuff, there were a lot of scary moments where quests would not seem proceed properly or the game stopped generating gatherables or prevented me from planting crops etc. Save often while questing. Cloud save often.The thing that killed Animal Crossing was Nintendo's garbage support of the game. If Gameloft can give this game REGULAR content updates, then this game has a heartwarming little niche it can fill, assuming the Big Mouse doesn't set it up to fail like the fate of so many of their games.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly amazing game, 10 out of 10. I love many Farming/Life Sim games like this and even without the Disney branding this is probably my very favorite, which I didn’t expect. Even in early access its surprising good and has a lot of content. I was worried about grind but this game is actually even less annoying than other life sim games which are single player, to me they hit a perfect spot where I never feel that I have to jump through hoops to accomplish anything and at the same time I always feel like I have more to do. Great job.I was very concerned about the payment model as F2P games are often notoriously irritating. Either you have to do mind numbing grind or pay huge amounts and even if it is just cosmetic it can be really irritating. However so far this games F2P model is great. Even almost all cosmetics are purchasable with in game money or random free drops, the only thing you pay for are the monthly events (which are 100% cosmetic). Even then you still get access to the event without having to pay but you can only get about half the stuff on offer. Plus these events offer microtransaction money so even then you can probably get full access to probably every 3rd or 4th event for free without spending a dime or real currency.Edit: they added the shop after I made this review. It wasn't too bad but not great, overall I now give the game a 9.5/10, so still overall fantastic. Mostly the prices for items in the shop are too high, but that's f2p for you and it actually hasn't released as f2p yet, so hopefully it won't get worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game when it was early access and promised more. I've since dropped this game, as it became too grindy and unrewarding. It quickly became a taxing dump of repetitive quests (battlepass included.) Was curious to see how the game would progress in keeping the map uncluttered and hoped to see an expansion to the map.. It was disappointing to see the quick fix was to hide characters and force out a completely separate island in a DLC, instead of introducing new biomes for the overwhelming flux of randomised characters. Not to mention how most characters need their own home, woody and buzz for example. It's almost laughable. As for the main storyline, it's cut short with an extremely anticlimactic letdown. It would have been interesting to see tension and conflict between the forgotten and main character, more corruption and anger. Instead we get a lonely emo teen breakdown, pat them on the back, and have them mope around the valley. The side quests are bland. The daily discussions are too repetitive, and uninteresting. Also scrooge's entire shop mechanic is just badly thought out. It's set up to be a daily check in, but the rng is bad, and oftentimes it's just disappointing items cycling through. This game doesn't compel me to pop in everyday, unless you're someone who has copious amount of time and money to pour in. STOP TRYING TO MAKE DDV COOP. Stop adding unfun challenges like snapshot and the boutique, to make the game feel more coop. The challenges are a hassle in themselves, and the rewards honestly aren't worth it. Nor is it fun scrambling together random pieces of furniture that sync up with the locked themes. Same goes for the boutique challenge. Stick to single player.This game is horrible and somehow becoming worse.

_childDocuments_.review: First, can disregard the hours played here - I've bought this game on other platforms where I have most of my hours right now. Holding off mostly on my Steam file for a bit, just wanted to test it out some here. It has been awhile since a game hooked me as quickly and as deeply as this has. It gets compared to Animal Crossing a lot, which is a good comparison, but - and this is coming from somebody who was very addicted to the first couple AC games - DDV does almost everything a LOT better. Larger world with varied biomes, charming characters, a gorgeous style, beautiful catchy Disney music. Only thing I might give AC a tiny edge on is having a bit more varied conversations with villagers where AC villagers might even give random gifts and such.Very chill, relaxing game, amazing escape from life. I grew up in FL so made my share of trips to Disney as a kid, and this game recaptures that feeling I had as a young kid there! Only disclaimer I'd give on recommending it for all ages is that there is very little voice acting, dialogue is written, so a younger child who can't read or read well will need some help. Being early access, it does have it's bugs, but in fairness to the devs they've already squashed a number of them. And they are very receptive to feedback - for example, the update that dropped a bit before I am writing this added what looks like FPS bleedout effects when low on stamina. Grey screen with red flashes. VERY annoying, but they took note of all our complaints and said they are removing it. Right now, I have one major issue that hopefully gets fixed - cloud saves still not working well. On Steam, though I did not sign in for the cloud saves, they still appear to work the same way as on console automatically and have the same issue... from a lot of testing, if you have a fast connection, you shouldn't have any problems, works every time for me in places with fast ones. But my home connection is pretty slow and it almost always fails there. Before the update this wasn't so much a problem, but as of the last update, if there is a discrepancy between cloud and local save when starting, if you try to keep the local save, it still tries to upload it to the cloud and will boot you back to the selection if it fails (it didn't do that last part before, you could continue with the local save). What that means is, so long as you can't upload the save to the cloud, you will not be able to save your progress unless you go to offline mode and make sure not to connect during play (not a HUGE deal, but you can't open the blue chests). If you play, save locally but cloud save fails, next time you play, as it is now, you will not be able to retain that local file if online unless the cloud upload succeeds. Hope there is a fix for this soon.Game works great on Steam Deck, both regularly and docked. Hope they add achievements to the Steam version soon... that is part of why I'm holding off on progressing on this file, working on the PS and Xbox ones now to get trophies and achievements there (some of which are pretty grindy but that's fine for me). The game is eventually going to go F2P - although the devs have promised that the mtx will be almost entirely cosmetics with some DLC, and not involved in core gameplay mechanics in any way (I think I'm remembering that right).
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Dreamlight Valley

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping in mind this game is still in development it is pretty incredible. I'm thoroughly impressed with how functional and fun everything is. I've seen some games that are "complete" that don't have this level of functionality and ease of play (*cough* Sims 4 *cough*) Even more impressed with how despite being a game made by Disney it doesn't seem to be too cash grabby (yet we shall see). PROS:-Character lines are unique, quirky, and have that overall Disney charm-The art style is GORGEOUS! -The character design has a great system, is well thought out, and inclusive-The tools NEVER break-You can move/edit relatively ANYTHING in the game allowing for complete customization of YOUR village-There's a great world building aspect to the game and there's plenty of room for growth-Game play is easy, fresh, and things (for the most part) run smoothly-The story is fun, easy to digest, easy to understand-You can access you backpack, closet, and furniture ANYTIME! -You don't have to run back and forth to get ingredients to cook. As long as the ingredients are in your backpack or in a chest you can access them-The teleportation option is fluid and is a saviorCONS-The characters can sometimes be difficult to track down or have annoying/inconvenient schedules (looking at you Ursula, Ariel, and Remy)-The stamina bar can be mildly annoying. Even after leveling up I feel like I fly through stamina-Some materials are insanely hard to find or have such a low drop rate you might have to wait a while before finding stuff-Uncle Scrooge has some of the most insane pricing for items in his shop. In what world am I paying 10,000 for a backpack or a t-shirt-Some friendship quests require other friendships to be leveled up before you can access their quest. I don't believe this is specified anywhere but it would have saved me many hours of frustration if I had known why I couldn't access some of the quests-There's no option to upgrade tools aside from questing-Save EVERYTHING. I have so many chests in my village because I've been burned too many times by selling stuff. The only thing that is safe to sell is things you grow (and even then sometimes you have to bring a character 20 carrots)-Sea dwelling characters can only be upgraded through gifts or quests. Unlike the other characters that you can "hang out" with to upgrade their friendship level characters like Ariel and Ursula are stuck only being able to upgrade through gifts or quests. To me there's a huge wasted opportunity to not allow for a diving or swimming skill to get unique fish or items. I feel like there should be a way to send Ariel and Ursula to go search for stuff similiar to Moana's boat.Overall, the game is fantastic. I'm excited to see what's to come and I would 100% recommend this game to anyone who enjoys Animal Crossing or any other cozy game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: not worth it for the price. I enjoyed it (sometimes) but the fact that you have to pay $100+ just for full access in a game that has more bugs than the bottom of a log in a swamp is absurd. Stardew Valley didn't do this to us. Devs are very greedy. Ugh where do I even begin...I guess I'll start off by saying I don't actually completely this game. I have beef with it. In theory it's a super cute game and I love the customization and all that. The gameplay is fun and the graphics are as well. It's always fun running around with your favorite Disney character following you around! The music is cute and nostalgic. And the lore is actually pretty dope. It had a lot of potential.But. The game has issues. Namely the pay-wall. Originally, it was released early-access so that you could pay to play the game before it was fully out and you got a few in-game goodies if you did that. I heard that eventually, it would be free to play. I don't know if that was actually true or just a rumor. But that still hasn't happened, it's still expensive as all hell. Now before you judge me for complaining about the price, hear me out. $40 would be a reasonable enough price for a game of this size and rendering as long as you're getting, you know, full access to the entire game and updates. But of coure, that $40 doesn't include all of the extra fees that they don't advertise. It's actually a whopping $70 if you get the gold edition. It's already absurd that $40 doesn't even get you access to the full game but when you realize what you're actually missing out by not getting the gold edition, you would laugh. The gold edition makes the game twice as expensive all for three completely unnecessary bonus items. That is INSANE. Like hello??? Oh but that's not all! There's also now a paid DLC!! $30 more bucks for the DLC!!! That is literally the price of the base game and from my understanding, all you get are like three more characters and a very mediocre storyline. And more stuff to spend irl money on. If you get everything, that adds up to $100. Disgustingly expensive for a glorified life/"farming" sim. (nevermind the fact that farming is barely even an important feature in this game but I digress). BUT THAT'S NOT ALL!! One of the in-game currencies called Moonstones used to be easy to get. It was a little more rare than the other main currencies but was still very possible and not too much of a burden. Like just challenging enough to get that it was a fun challenge. And the best part? It was completely free. But no longer! Because despite being in the market for it, Disney hates fun. Now Moonstones are hella rare and limited. They have made it so that if you want any of the items that require Moonstones, you have to pay irl money for it because it's practically impossible to get enough Moonstones within the time frame that the items are available. In fact, if you want access to even some quests, you have to buy Moonstones with real money. And it is NOT cheap either. It's actually ridiculous and frankly pretty gross that the game is swarming with microtransactions despite it being a full-priced game. Like if it were a free to play game, I'd still be bothered by it, but I would understand. Truthfully, it was only a matter of time until a Disney ran game started up with the microtransactions. But it is still heartily disappointing and frustrating. May I just remind you that Stardew Valley has been out since 2016, has frequent FREE minor and major updates TO THIS DAY, and the base game only costs you $15 TOTAL. And is still profitable. And he's doing that while working on a completely new game. That's how you make a game. That's how you do it. But Disney Dreamlight Valley costs a crap ton for such little gain. OH and that reminds me, I haven't even mentioned the bugs I've encountered yet.Cost aside, there are actually other issues in the game too. There is a quest that I have been stuck on for over a YEAR (yes really, over a year) because the item I'm supposed to retrieve simply will not spawn. It doesn't exist. And yes, I am 100% sure that I didn't just miss it. I looked it up a million times, I asked other players, I tried to contact support (they never got back to me), I even stayed up late and woke up early to see if the time of day aspect of it was just being hyper sensitive. All to no avail. I literally cannot progress in the game without this quest, all because there is a bug. Ugh. I've also heard from several people that the game crashes really badly for them. For me, it doesn't crash too much on Steam although on the Switch, it is just awful. Like, almost unplayable awful. I'm really grateful that I got the Switch version as a gift from my friend because no way in hell do I recommend buying this game more than once. It's not worth it. If you're considering getting this game on the Switch, DO NOT. It is nice that it has cross-platform compatibility and that you can play the same save file on any platform. But the Switch version is sooooooo buggy and glitchy. It's seriously so so so bad.Oh also not gonna lie, it is kiiiinda weird being homies with the villains. Like are we gonna just skip over the fact that Gaston was a womanizer and the fact that Mother Gothel was a narcissistic abuser and the fact that Scar is, well... Scar? I could keep going. I don't remember if they've added Jafar or Hans yet but if they do and they expect me to be friends with those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, then I would like to have a little ~ Chat™ ~ with them. It is pretty hilarious to call Scar a kitty cat and feed him fish though.So yeah, that's my review. Overall, I do enjoy the game and I have an insane amount of hours in it for someone that complains about it so much. I enjoy and hate it in the way that many fans of The Sims do with their game. It's a love-hate relationship, leaning heavily towards hate. This game is no longer worth it for the price. Just another classic Disney robbing everyone for absolutely no reason situation. Like come on man, you are a multibillion-dollar company, do you really need my money?? Money that I don't even have?? Get out of here. I'm all for supporting the artists but something tells me that most of this money probably doesn't even go to them, much like with everything else Disney related.

_childDocuments_.review:
Disney Dreamlight Valley is a hybrid between a life-sim and an adventure game rich with quests, exploration, and engaging activities featuring Disney and Pixar friends, both old and new.

Once an idyllic land, Dreamlight Valley was a place where Disney and Pixar characters lived in harmony - until the Forgetting. Night Thorns grew across the land and severed the wonderful memories tied to this magical place. With nowhere else to go, the hopeless inhabitants of Dreamlight Valley retreated behind locked doors in the Dream Castle.

Now it's up to you to discover the stories of this world and bring the magic back to Dreamlight Valley!

name: Eternights
detailed_description: Special Edition Immerse yourself into the world of Eternights with the Deluxe Edition, including the base game, the official digital artbook, revealing insights into the development of Eternights, and the official digital soundtrack featuring over 100 tracks composed by Spencer Bambrick. About the Game Eternights is a unique blend of dating and action where players can explore a post-apocalyptic world filled with danger, love, and adventure. Save the world, and find love along the way. Face the infected One day, something, or someone, has turned humans into dangerous monsters. All that interests them now is violence and power. They are what stand between you, a cure, and the world you want. Most importantly? You’re fighting for more than just your own survival – you are fighting for those you love. Find Love The impending end of the world makes for a great conversation starter! When you’re not exploring dungeons, you can choose to spend time growing closer to a cast of five quirky and loveable characters. Explore their stories and grow closer to them to unlock unique skills and spells you can use in battle. Race the Clock Scavenging, dungeon crawling, dating…there are just too many things to do in one day, and each area has a deadline! Will you grow closer to your confidant in order to deepen your relationship and unlock new skills? Will you scavenge the wasteland for supplies? Will you grow stronger by training with your companions? Or will you ignore all of that and go to the dungeon the first chance you get? It’s up to you, but remember, the clock is ticking. Explore Dungeons These dangerous areas - known as the 'Wall' - are filled with mystery and danger. As the deadline looms, you will have to quickly overcome traps, puzzles, and dancing minigames to make it through in time. Luckily, you have your confidants by your side to help when things get scary. Animated Cutscenes There are several fully 2D animated cutscenes that change depending on who you decide to date. Immerse yourself and truly connect with the characters you are spending time with.
about_the_game: Eternights is a unique blend of dating and action where players can explore a post-apocalyptic world filled with danger, love, and adventure. Save the world, and find love along the way. Face the infected One day, something, or someone, has turned humans into dangerous monsters. All that interests them now is violence and power. They are what stand between you, a cure, and the world you want. Most importantly? You’re fighting for more than just your own survival – you are fighting for those you love. Find Love The impending end of the world makes for a great conversation starter! When you’re not exploring dungeons, you can choose to spend time growing closer to a cast of five quirky and loveable characters. Explore their stories and grow closer to them to unlock unique skills and spells you can use in battle. Race the Clock Scavenging, dungeon crawling, dating…there are just too many things to do in one day, and each area has a deadline! Will you grow closer to your confidant in order to deepen your relationship and unlock new skills? Will you scavenge the wasteland for supplies? Will you grow stronger by training with your companions? Or will you ignore all of that and go to the dungeon the first chance you get? It’s up to you, but remember, the clock is ticking. Explore Dungeons These dangerous areas - known as the 'Wall' - are filled with mystery and danger. As the deadline looms, you will have to quickly overcome traps, puzzles, and dancing minigames to make it through in time. Luckily, you have your confidants by your side to help when things get scary. Animated Cutscenes There are several fully 2D animated cutscenes that change depending on who you decide to date. Immerse yourself and truly connect with the characters you are spending time with.
short_description: Eternights is a dating action game where you try to make the most out of life during the apocalypse. Monday: Go on a date. Tuesday: Clear dungeon. Friday: Freak out! The clock is ticking!!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 7/10Edit: I see my review has picked up traction, so I've decided to flesh it out a bit more.Man... I'm really torn on this one. I'm giving it a positive rating, but just barely. Eternights is a game I feel could have used another year or two in the oven. It has a lot of great ideas, some of which are executed well, while others are a bit on the dry side. Combat is a mix of Tokyo Xanadu eX+ action mixed with souls-like dodge (and parry) mechanics.Other aspects of the game clearly take influence from the Persona series, with social links, romantic interests, a calender system, etc. Up front I'd like to say that the voice acting, for the most part, is actually pretty good!Moving on, one of my major gripes with the game is that it's just, well, too easy, even on the hardest difficulty. This is a major problem, because all the fancy social link events are meant to give you points and rank up your connections to "make you stronger", but, well, you don't really need to be stronger, at all. Dodging is extremely easy as the timing is very lenient. I don't know if this is because of my experience with souls games, but from beginning to end, I never felt like I was in danger, or even challenged. Honestly the only difference from the beginning of the game to the end is that enemies have a bit more HP, so sure, if you "level up" your social links, things will die a little bit faster, but it honestly doesn't matter.As a result of the lackluster difficulty, I found myself just spamming through days and nights by going to bed just to progress during long "nothing to do segments", which have tiny story elements sprinkled into them, where you're meant to be upping your social links and earning points to get stronger. Some of these "empty" segments are just too long. I think the longest is around 14 days, which took like 45 minutes just to jump through. I'd also complain about the game being short, but given the fact I spammed through wait periods already, I probably wouldn't have bothered to finish the game if it was 30 hours long or something. On another note, one suggestion to the dev would be to add red circles under enemies, and green under your party, because there are times you can't even tell who is who during moments where there are a lot of smaller enemies on the screen due to dark environments. Again, the game isn't hard, but I found that to be a bit of an annoyance. Beyond what I've already touched on, there just isn't a lot to keep you invested. The game starts off really well in my opinion, but as the story progresses it just begins to feel hollow and empty -- uninspired even. The demo, for instance, hooked me COMPLETELY. I was fully engrossed, wondering what comes next, and when it ended I was rabid for more. Sadly, my interest plummeted shortly after buying the full game. To me, it feels almost as if 99% of the effort went into the first 45 minutes, then the developer couldn't figure out where to go from there. Now -- the characters. Honestly I didn't feel a connection to a single one of them during any point in the game (not to mention Chani is the most annoying character I've ever endured in a video game of any genre). Chani is so bad, in fact, he doesn't even make it into the game logo/banner artwork.Speaking of artwork, I would like to add that the anime-style animated scenes (as short and rare as they might be), as well as the stills, are very, very well done. Certainly can't knock the game for those.Switching gears, I was very sad to see that you spend 99% of the time you aren't in "dungeons" on a small, boring, lifeless train, which further enhanced my desire to "omg hurry up this is lame" through everything that wasn't a fight. Seriously, the train feels like you're stuck in a jail cell. It's unappealing, dreary, and claustrophobic. Sure, a case could be made that the train fits the central theme of the game and that it's more "immersive" than other alternatives might be, but I still didn't like anything about it. YMMV.Finally, the ending -- it's a total cop-out. No spoilers, but come on, dev. You could see it coming a mile away. My final rating is a begrudging 7/10 (I was going to say 6.5, but I think that's a LITTLE too harsh). If this would have been made by an entire team, I likely would have given it a 6/10, but since this was mostly a SOLO endeavor in terms of development, it deserves a bit more. Bravo, dev. I won't pretend I could make anything like this myself. Everything starts off okay, but that said, certain story beats feel tacked on for sake of filler content, and could really have stood to be fleshed out more to make them feel meaningful and important.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I first want to say that the people that are comparing this to games like Persona need to understand that this is an indie dev, and looks to be their first game, made by just a fairly small team with one person who did a lot of the artwork, game design/mechanics, and story. So I say kudos to the developer. Having played through Eternights multiple times, here is my breakdown of the game, some minor spoilers:The main story arc is a semi-standard anime/manga/jrpg setting where the main protagonist is "chosen" and granted an ability to help thwart the big bad who is out to corrupt the world. While the main story is fairly basic, where it has heart is with the interpersonal friendships and relationships. The characters can be rather 2-dimensional. sticking to their character tropes and it's often very middle-school/high-school levels of romance with the characters, which can be cute but can also be eye-rolling . There are also some plot threads that are never fully developed, or are shoehorned in for sake of "character development".  There are multiple endings for the game, most of which play out the same with the exception of the bad ending, and while predictable, can tug at your feelings. Overall the story is coherent, with some lightness and humor albeit a basic narrative.The core gameplay is fairly typical of a jrpg, a bit bare bones, but responsive. It can be a bit tricky to pick up the timing for dodges/parries, but once you've got that down, combat is enjoyable. You're rarely overwhelmed to the point of frustration and there were times where I wished there was more combat. The one thing that was a bit confusing was the attempt at puzzles or mechanics that were pretty much a one-off. For instance, you're told about sneaking at the beginning of the game, but it's never used after that even though there are a couple of instances where it would seem like it would come in handy, but if you try, it has no bearing on the outcome of the circumstance. You also have to do a dance/rhythm mini-game twice, but then never see it again. The individual characters' mini-games can vary between being too easy, to being rng to the point of not being able to achieve a maximum score even if done perfectly (I'm looking at you Yohan). The mini fetch quests are also random at first until you figure out the layouts, and utilize the save/load states. Not everything is explained, which I'm all for games not hand-holding, but building social stats is a guesswork during dialogue cues, and is vital to ranking up your relationship with characters. I'm glad for the New Game+ which rolls over all earned stats and abilities, (and FYI, it  take multiple playthroughs to max out all abilities) but understandably you do have to still earn each relationship rank again, although all relationship perks/abilities are still usable/unlocked if you earned them in a past playthrough. One minor thing, there's no character customization or alternate outfit choices which narrative-wise is fine, just might be something for the devs to think about for their next game or even a DLC.The visuals, while not AAA, fit the tone of the game and suited the narratives well. The character models and expressions give a sort of XBox 360 Avatar (not the blue guys) vibe. The 2D animated scenes were really well done and hit a home run each time they were used, whether for exposition, for laughs, intensiveness, or emotional impact. The audio set the mood well, and has a good combat groove to it. While I can't speak for the other languages, as a sound engineer, I believe the English voiceover work was very well done, directed well, and sounded professionally recorded and edited. While rough around the edges, for the Developers' first major release, Eternights is a solid, enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all may I remind you that it's a cheaper indie title. So please go easy on Studio Sai which only has 9 members to begin with. Jae Hyun Yoo the developer of Eternights & Founder of Studio Sai mentioned that the Persona series was the reason which gave him the courage to leave his full-time job and his inspiration for developing the game. At least he was apparent about it. It's just refreshing to see an indie studio take inspiration from something other than Soulslike or Meteoidvanias games. Although there are quite a number of thematic similarities from Persona, the play style of Eternights is rather similar to that of Scarlet Nexus. This is their first ever project btw, so I'd like to give them my full support.The story starts with you (namable character) having a conversation together with your bestfriend, Chani. Chani asks you to complete your dating app bio in the hopes of scoring a date. Moments later both of you decided to watch TV out of boredom, then a news about an anti-aging drug called "Eternights" appear to which Chani finds weird. He then switches to another channel about an idol/model named "Yuna" to which both of you simp over her. After a few days Chani discovers a new dating app which matches two people through engaging personality test. After taking the test, a mysterious woman contacts you, which appears to be very flirty, asking you to go on a yacht date. A day goes by, you decided to meet with your so called "destined partner", which unfortunately at the moment you try to meet with her, the world turns into utter chaos. A blue wall starts appearing out of nowhere and people transforming to "infected". Chani tries to contact you and that you should meet up together, and before you know it, both of you get sent to a city shelter. Eternights is a balance of action RPG and a dating sim. Exploring dungeons, navigating the environment as you fight hordes of infected, solving puzzles & mini games. Improving your relationship with the other characters and finally dating. Unlike Persona, dating only feels like an added bonus for the fans to enjoy the game. Eternights? it takes it to a different degree. The choices in the game definitely counts, so choose wisely. I remember the part on the dating app where I was asked series of questions & preferences about certain things and situations. Through dialogue, you can make choices that do provide some benefits to your Social Stats. Depending on your choice, you can increase your Expression, Confidence, Acceptance, and Courage. The game control is pretty simple tho. (X) Button for attacking which then turns into combos upon successive attacks(RB) Preform a bonus attack at the end of your combo.(A) Dodging by timely pressing the A button as the red indicator appears on screen, (LB) Perform a special attack once the special gauge is full (by attacking, successfully evading)It takes some practice to successfully pull off during the game’s early acts, but you can become a powerhouse later on as you unlock more abilities.This narrative will easily be what makes or breaks your experience with Eternights. Honestly, if you don’t find yourself connecting with the characters or their cause, the rest of the game falls apart. This is mostly because they make up most of the 10-hour campaign, which is a little short, but with the option of New Game+, secrets, and missed interactions adds to the replayability. What I’m trying to get at is that there are some really strong moments of the narrative that occur during late-game Acts, but getting there requires you to really feel like you are a member of this gang who will not mesh with everyone who plays.Each party member has a social/relationship rank attached to them, including Chani, who acts more as “wingman” support by helping you raise social stats needed to advance bonds with the other characters. You can strengthen this rank by spending time with the characters. You collect White Essence to bolster stats associated with the party members by training with them or scavenging for items they require. These stats range from increasing health and SP to strengthening their abilities. Black Essence is collected in dungeons and through battling enemies, helping you strengthen your existing sword skills while unlocking new ones. You’re limited at first in how much SP is at your disposal, encouraging you to do a dungeon run in multiple phases to replenish your strength. However, you can power through later dungeons more quickly if you efficiently utilize your skills.It's not bad but not too good either. I only have few mentionable issues:

_childDocuments_.review: HUGE SPOILER. LIKE, MASSIVE SPOILER. ONLY READ IF YOU FULLY PLAYED THE GAME. Or if you're just very curious. I really need to get my thoughts out in some way because I was very much enjoying my time with the game until right at the very end. So, if you're still reading I am going into detail about the ending since this is the main reason why my opinion of the game changed so drastically. Last warning. Here I go ranting again. SO. Eternights has a social sim similar to the Persona games. You hang out with characters during the day and level them up and everyone except for Chani is romance-able. This aspect of the game was the thing that was advertised the most so I was expecting something somewhat in depth and no... It really isn't. It's very easy to upgrade your team and date your party members which makes sense since the story moves at a mile a minute. You can even date all of them. (or so I'm told) One of the few things I can say about this game with 100% confidence is that the game does pretty well on getting you attached to the characters. Or at least to the date-able ones. I'm still not sold on Chani. BUT the character stories are good enough to get you involved and wanting to know more while strengthening your bonds. With that bit of context now I can talk about the ending.THE ENDING. This disappointing as all hell ending. Right before the final boss section of the game the story has you pick the character you think is the most important to you, i.e your love interest. So, like you may think, you are locking in who your romance partner is and who will appear with you in the ending. EXCEPT. You are also marking them for DEATH. After all the repetitiveness the game throws at you, after developing your bonds and and potentially growing attached; the game kills the most interesting character to you. But this isn't the most annoying part to me which I'll get to in a second.The writing needs work. There's some great moments with the writing. For the most part, I think they nailed the humor. For the rest, I feel as though the tone of the game shifts too much and kills immersion. (Like they killed my Min) And where the writing really falters for me is The End. When your MC goes under for the operation to put his hand energy in the fudgin' cannon or whatever. Your love interest (Min for me) is bedside with you and you say "I love you" it's all very sweet. But theeeeennn Min just leaves the train?! Why did she leave the safety of the train fully knowing there are still monsters roaming about? Is she stupid?! Then I thought, "Oh, I guess I'll have to save her now." NOPE no saving. You run out and see her strung up in the air while spewing blood and body convulsing. Much like the rest of the game it happens way too quickly and just left me mad at how random it felt. Turns out Umbra like, fused with her or something. So you fight the super lack luster final boss and get a scene where Min goes to sacrifice herself to stop Umbra from within. First parallel that came to mind was the end of Guilty Gear Strive where Jack-O goes to sacrifice herself to stop I-NO from within but Sol rips her out of there and they find a new way to defeat her with the powers of all the characters working together to stop her. Although I wasn't expecting that exact thing to play out in Eternights but I was hoping to have the best happy ending where the cast came up with an alternate plan to defeat Umbra. Now I will admit that comparing an indie game's writing to something wild and complex like Guilty Gear is a bit unfair. But just because the video game is indie does that mean that other important factors like the writing need to be indie too? Does that make sense? So Min dies, Umbra is defeated, and on to the thing that peeved me the most. Everything is instantly better. All of the horrible things that happened? Doesn't matter! It's all fixed now yippee! Of course, all the people who died are still dead. Unfortunately, the Eternights Anti-Aging Pill won't work if you're a corpse. You know who's not a corpse? Min. Because after the sacrifice it's only a matter of minutes before it's revealed that your love interest doesn't die for good and Lux just brings them back after a couple weeks. Not only that, the MC gets his flesh and bone arm back. Which means losing that arm meant nothing in the end and giving up the energy in the final act was pointless anyway because Umbra upgrades and you simply grow back the energy arm. Then you get "Where-are-they-now" style text on screen about all the party members. Yuna goes back to being a pop-star but makes more time for her friends. Sia continues her research and love of science. And Chani is cool now. The last 2 hours of the game feel like a blur because of the pace of it all. Not only that, all the fixes characters get to their stories and your love interest resurrecting feel so rushed and unimportant. And on top of it all, when you finish the game completely you get a QR code. Scan it and you get a 30 second video from your partner. It's mostly there to reinforce that fact the sacrifice didn't have emotional weight. It's cute and all but it makes me wonder why that couldn't just be in the game!Overall, I feel kinda guilty. I didn't hate the game, but the end really soured all positives I had to say about it. Aside from the writing, the pacing, and the ending I liked the social sim and found some fun with the combat. If you read this whole thing I'm sorry I rant a lot. But that's only when I'm really passionate about something and indie games bring out my passion. Eternights was within my top anticipated games when I saw the trailer and now that I am finally able to play it I'm left pretty underwhelmed. I have nothing but respect for the devs for putting time and effort into a thing they love. Much like any studio that puts their name out there, there's always something to improve on. I still have immense faith in Studio Sai and I will keep my eyes peeled for any of their future projects. That is all. Thank you for indulging my rant.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more of a guilty pleasure game than an actual good game, but would recommend giving it a try to anyone nonetheless. The puzzles are actually good, the gameplay is passable (annoyingly clunky and unforgiving, but passable), the story is decent (but has some noticeable gaps), BUT the characters are where the game really grabs you.  If I had to compare it to something, I'd compare it Dragon Age: Origins, the way the characters actually have a personality.  The format of the game is reminiscent of Persona, but it def does enough to make itself into its own thing rather than a clone.If I had to, I'd rate it a 6.5 of 10, if you're the type to focus on combat instead and charge right through the game, and/or skip every skippable scene, then it drops to a 4 of 10 (I stand by my opening statement tho, it's a guilty pleasure and worth giving a shot).

Hopefully, the people who made this game get more money and people on their next project and if it's as decent as this one then I'll probably buy the next as well.

_childDocuments_.review: *Update*I have nominated this game for both the 'Outstanding Visual Style' and Outstanding Story-Rich Game' in the 2023 Steam Game Awards.Hello!I wanted to post a non-video review of this game so here we go.Gameplay/Style: 8/10Love the look and color palate. Cell shaded and good use of ambiance. Characters were distinct in appearance without being over-the-top. Enemies were on the line between grotesque and cartoony, so it wasn't too gory or violent to look at. Anime cutscenes were a plus, very good use of them.Didn't like the Animated Stills, felt a true animation would have been better for a game at full retail price.Repetitive battles could have benefited from a larger variety of animations for 'guard breaks', spell casting and additional enemy types. Larger number of foes in battles at once could make it a little more challenging.Occasionally too easy, occasionally frustrating. Autosave assists scumsaving to the point of not needing savepoints.Dying has no real cost as you often retain most of the growth after death, only to autoload to right before you die (you can often grind 'Black Essence' this way.Sound: 8/10Music and ambient sounds are great.Battle sounds are satisfying and epic.Voices are great in Korean and Japanese; English is distracting.Voices don't always sync to animations and cutscenes.Vocalized tracks break immersion, especially the one after the first wall breaks.Controls: 8/10Keyboard is more than capable.hack & Slash gets repetitive.Dodging is sometimes broken against ranged attackers, and large groups tend to make dodges ineffective.Story/Characters: 10/10Strong characterization and story.Relationships are given center-stage and the spotlight is on the characters.Min steals the show!!! She is the best character hands-down.The focus of the game is relationship building.Final Verdict: 8.5/10Loved it, but there is room for growth.Hope this indie dev continues to release full games and avoids DLC and micro-transactions. Mu purchase of future projects and my continued support depend on this factor."No need to pander, keep things based!!! Frock Kotaku!!!" -Me

_childDocuments_.review: The game’s main quest in each chapter imposes a sense of urgency on players, as they are bound by time constraints. However, players are granted freedom to engage in various activities during their free time before the deadline. Combat mechanics are rather monotonous, with identical combos for shortsword and greatsword, accompanied by quick time events. Skillful dodging can turn the tide of battle. By slowing down time and relentlessly attacking enemies, players can break their shields using special skills. The repetitive nature of these actions may become tiresome over time. Animation quality is subpar, particularly when it comes to running, which appears more akin to barbarians marching on a battlefield.The storyline is easy to follow but relatively short, lasting less than 14 hours. While it may not be highly engaging, it still manages to hold interest. Voice acting and comedic elements sprinkled throughout the game add flavor to conversations, making it more enjoyable. I pre-purchased the game primarily for the dating sim aspect, and my experience with it has left me with mixed feelings. Dating scenes can range from bland to sweet. There's a little surprise waiting Based on my review, it seems that the game may not appeal to all players unless they are avid fans of anime games. As an experienced RPG player, I rated it 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I expected to enjoy this game as much as I did when I picked it up on sale. I'll start with my overall conclusion: this is a gem of a game with admittedly a few flaws but if you're willing to approach it with an open mind, you will definitely have a positive experience.Combat is on the basic side at the start, nothing wrong with that, as long as you get the hang of the dodging mechanic(parrying is rewarding but optional) and level up your confidant abilities as you go along you will probably have little trouble till the the mid-game at least. I have to admit that starting from there the bosses can actually kick your ass(as they did mine) so unless you've got top reflexes, have plenty of experience with souls/bloodborne/sekiro/etc or are just really lucky, you will need a strategy, or rather develop your playstyle from the abilities you have and weave them together to shut down the bosses as best you can as well as learning to deal with their patterns of course. It's from that point on that I went from 'this isn't so challenging but at least it's pretty satisfying' to 'woah I'm actually have a lot of fun overcoming whatever they have to throw at me'; that's when I felt the real fun factor kick in.Of course, that's only touching on the combat aspect.When it comes to the cast, I really do feel an amazing job was done developing them even for those who came relatively late. Their bonding events touch on some interesting themes that keep you engaged but it's never the sole thing that's memorable about them, all of them have little and big things that says something about them and it all comes together to make them feel alive to the player. This is a dating sim so I had started seeing someone as a potential LI pretty early but surprising them myself I ended up seeing them as a best friend(other than your bro friend) after doing all their events and seeing how...chill they were around each other. In contrast, someone who didn't make a great first impression on me is whom I chose in the end after all the time I spent with them. If this doesn't speak to the character writing of this game, I don't know what does(I have no regrets trying to go for the bro route from the get go). If I didn't manage to make this clear earlier, it's not only about the character events, there are a bunch that happen at your hub as the days come as well as other smaller but humorous instances.What I've mentioned so far is what I consider to be the meat as well the best from this game, the plot is on the weaker side. Its structure is pretty simple and somewhat predictable even if the details vary from modern media, I would have loved if it was expanded upon or if its execution was a bit more creative. Gameplay may feel janky at times and I think I've run into a couple of UI bugs but the latter may be because of my controller. There was room for polishing for the fine details but the final product still delivers imo. Something I forgot to mention is that there are quite a few moments where the game empowers the player to think and act for themselves without relying on a tutorial, jarring at first but I can honestly admit to approving of it in the end.As for the ending, I'm unsure as of this moment of the number of variations to it but assuming it follows the same direction everytime, I understand that will not be everyone's cup of tea. However, I will say that the fault does not lie in the execution but rather many people are not willing to accept it. I will refrain from speaking more on it but I have to give my respect to the developer for going through with it.I'm not a critic or a hardcore gamer or anything of the kind, I may be stubborn in some respects but my tastes are casual and my thoughts are not special, so I will just say that I think this game's merits far outweights its weaknesses and if you are on the fence about getting it while it's on sale, don't let yourself think that the small inconveniences or the ending with mixed opinions make the journey not worth experiencing at all.i sincerely look forward to a potential sequel in the future from this dev, whatever form it may take.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very rough around the edges, with a lot of weird cuts during scenes, semi-repetitive combat (at least at the start) and is a little harder to get used to if you're used to bigger budget games.That being said, the dialogue, story and characters very, very much make up for all of that in spades. The characters are instantly likeable, and the protagonist is basically what you'd get if you made a persona protagonist x3 the degenerate (that we all are inside, let's be real). While the combat is also repetitive, the special moves and powers are appropriately anime and cool, and makes it more fun and cinematic despite the core loop of attack-attack-attack-dodge-special attack.So far it's a fantastic game, 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really not bad. It's got jank on top of jank, but it's playable jank. Attacks feel a little disconnected, but there is a discernible rhythm to it once you acclimate. A little mashy, but I feel like this is the kind of game you come to respect for the sum of its parts.The UI is bland, but it works where it needs to work. The artstyle feels the price of the game, with opportune moments of really gorgeous animated and hand drawn art work. The longer you play, the more you respect it.The voice acting is impressive and sells well above average character beats that balance the line between expected cringey-ness and actual heartfelt moments that can resonate with a bigger audience than you would expect from a game like this.It wears its Persona inspirations on its sleeve, and that's a good thing. It's pretty good.
