_childDocuments_.review: It is with great regret that I just barely cannot recommend this game for two reasons: the ending, and the price.First of all, the game is very short for the price. My 10.5 hours of playtime represents a full playthrough of the game. Technically you can get up to 3 different endings based on  but the game does not change substantially doing this, and there's a lack of a fast forward option for dialog that would make doing additional playthroughs less tedious. It's hard to justify $30 given the playtime available.Then, there's the ending. I will try not to spoil it here, but it's unfortunately very unsatisfying. There is not a lot of closure on the events that the protagonist experiences and there are still many unanswered questions about the world and the events post-final boss. I don't really feel like I "won" or "finished" the game (maybe that's what the developer was going for, but it's not satisfying to me).That being said, I have to say that I enjoyed all of the characters. Each of their personalities was enjoyable and there were lots of funny moments, cute dialog, and heartfelt conversations. Progressing along the conversations with your friends involves raising your social stats through conversation or talking with your best friend. The conversation bonuses were always satisfying, but I found it hard to target a specific stat this way.Each friend (except your best friend) also has a minigame associated with them. While I found that the difficulty for these varied wildly, they were all at least ok and gave some good bonuses. The scavenging minigame was pretty straightforward once you knew which locations had which items as well.Finally, the combat. I found the timing for some of the dodges a little tight with not a lot of telegraphing, and in particular I felt like there was a huge difficulty spike in the final sequence. Still, it's pretty satisfying to get off a nice chain of combos and it managed to be just complex enough that I felt like I was accomplishing something without struggling to remember all the bells and whistles that often comes with ARPG style gameplay..With all that being said, if you get the game on a steep sale and are willing to accept the ending as it is, then this game could be worth it to you. For me, however, I can't say I finished it feeling satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: Love in the Time of Apocalypse! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Eternights emerges as a unique blend of dating simulation and action, offering players a post-apocalyptic world teeming with adventure, danger, and romance. Developed by a small team, this game has generated a mixed bag of opinions among players, but one thing is for sure – Eternights is a daring attempt at something different.Eternights transports you to a world overrun by infected monsters, setting the stage for your heroic journey to find a cure while forming connections with five intriguing characters. The game's combat system combines elements from Devil May Cry and Bayonetta, offering a mix of excitement and challenge. While some players have praised the combat, others have found it slightly janky and disconnected, but it's worth noting that this indie gem's combat system is more about the sum of its parts than perfection.One of Eternights' standout features is its character-driven narrative, which draws clear inspiration from the Persona series. Players can choose to deepen their relationships with the cast, unlocking unique skills and spells for use in battle. The voice acting in the game is commendable, elevating the character interactions from expected cringiness to heartfelt moments that resonate with a surprisingly broad audience.However, not all is sunshine and rainbows in Eternights. Some players have expressed disappointment in the game's overall design and execution. The lack of proper character introductions leaves players feeling disconnected from the characters they are supposed to care about. The anime-inspired character designs, while functional, may come across as bland and uninspired to some. Additionally, the game's combat, while enjoyable for many, may feel unresponsive and repetitive for others.One major gripe revolves around the pacing and storytelling. Eternights tries to weave an epic tale, but the pacing feels rushed, with dialogues that hardly scratch the surface before jumping to the next scene. This breakneck pace can be disorienting and detract from the emotional impact the game aims to deliver. Furthermore, Eternights attempts to encompass various gaming genres, including action, social simulation, and RPG elements, but it struggles to deliver the depth and nuance associated with these genres.Dungeon exploration in Eternights is, unfortunately, a letdown for some players. The linear and repetitive level design offers little in the way of variety, leaving you mostly running through hallways. Furthermore, the RPG mechanics are criticized for being too linear, with skill trees lacking balance and depth. Healing spells, in particular, come under fire for their excessive cost compared to other more effective abilities.In conclusion, Eternights is a game that refuses to play it safe, offering an intriguing blend of dating simulation and action set in a post-apocalyptic world. While it has its shortcomings – including pacing issues, unrefined mechanics, and linear design – it also has its moments of brilliance, such as engaging character interactions and enjoyable combat. Whether Eternights becomes your cup of tea will depend on your willingness to overlook its imperfections and appreciate the passion and creativity poured into it by a dedicated indie team.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: Simple, but surprisingly fun and satisfying gameplay.  Neat characters as I really liked the main cast.  It feels like a lot of passion was put into the game and there's a lot of fun/interesting ideas in the game and in the story.That being said, it really feels like an amateur's first game.  If I had to sum a lot of the games problems, it mostly comes down to a lack of depth.  The game's dungeons, while interesting, especially with some pretty fun puzzles, are extremely short in both quality and quantity.  The characters, while still enjoyable with decent character arcs in their social links, end up falling by the wayside a lot as the plot tends to only focus on like 2 of them at a time (and not for long - or particularly deep - at that).  The plot, while it has an interesting premise, needed like an extra arc or two to properly set up character motivations, worldbuilding, and personal stakes as the final arc just felt really rushed all around.  While the ending is presented quite well, it's lacking a lot of the buildup necessary for it to really feel like a gutpunch, and the epilogue just awkwardly telling us what happened to the characters after-the-fact was just underwhelming.Despite my many gripes with the game, it mostly comes down to the developer's inexperience, and not terrible design decisions or extreme greed.  I'd say it's like a 3/5 game as I still had fun with it, just wish there was more of the game in like... every area.  Check it out if it's on sale and you're interested in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine jumping into a game expecting nothing but a loosey goosey anime adventure similar to your stereotypical anime you'd watch on crunchyroll or something. Not at all what I got playing this game. At ALL. This game threw me for a loop, in many ways. It is an excellent game, and I heavily suggest if you're a fan of standard beat-em-up style games with some slice of life action included in there (and some goofy ass mini games as well cus why not), this is an excellent game for you.Certainly not the best I've seen in a game, however considering this is from an indie studio, I went in with relatively low expectations and was very pleasantly surprised. If I went in with HIGH expectations, I still woulda been a very happy man. The story writing is excellent and characters actually know how to read the room, with all aspects needed in certain situations. Whether it be serious, or funny, or sad, or romantic, you name it. There is a part of the story that contains at least one of these elements. Not to mention the story is also very well written and the pace it takes is great.I saw some people were not very happy about it. Me personally, it was a nice ending. *SPOILERS CLICK IF YOU DARE* The game has a anime style. And the graphics flip flop. When you are in game, it (for me) was a consistent, 3D 400FPS adventure with good looking, still anime inspired character designs. Some cut scenes will flip to a 24fps 3D scene, to give it that more "anime" feel, and then some cut scenes are just STRAIGHT UP anime, with the usual 24fps scene and 8-12fps on different artistic side pieces in the background. The game has quite a few different graphical options to choose from as well so if you got potato PC, guess what you can still enjoy game. So it's frankly a win for everyone. However, the game still does look very good, especially if you run everything at highest settings.Sounds are accurate to what things should sound like. When you hit something with a sword, well a magical sword, guess what it sounds kinda like something being hit with a magical sword. Nothing super special about that. Music personally, was my go to for this game. The music was excellent. Final boss music, excellent. The music utilized in the end cut scene, EXCELLENT. All music fit the theme of the conversation or situation happening in the game, and all it did was add element to that conversation or situation. Very well utilized and very good in general.The game is great. And frankly, I'd say amazing for an indie game made by a small studio. After playing this, I want a sequel. Not sure if it'll ever happen, but if it does, would immediately purchase it.Rating: 9.5/10 Would be a perfect ten, however just a few tweaks to the story and you nearly have one of the best games I've played in a long time. I say this is one of the best as my personal opinion, as this is obviously not the game for everyone. But it is still very good nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I have no idea if I should recommend this or not, but since Steam gives us only two options I think it barely gets the thumbs up in this case. There is a lot to love about the game; it is extremely similar to the Persona titles in many ways and a pretty solid albeit generic dating sim. Most of the characters are fun and most scenes are really sweet and heartwarming. The plot is pretty whatever, but definitely not bad. As for the characters, the girls are all great, but the rest of the cast is almost unnecessary to the entire game except for a couple of scenes. The biggest, greatest flaw the game has is the combat and oh boy, is it a flaw...The combat is an unresponsive mess of QTEs, dodging and waiting. Most enemies will simply parry your attacks immediately if you try to hit them so your only option is to wait around so you can counter them. This adds literal minutes to each stage! The final battle is a collection of everything horrible about the combat as it showcases perfectly how unrefined the fighting system is here.A game that left me extremely ambivalent, but overall I did enjoy it. I saw no reason to hide a part of the ending behind a QR code though...

_childDocuments_.review: First thing is first. I would  get this game on a sale. I myself might pick this up for $40 but I'm sure some wouldn't feel satisfied with a $40 price tag. That being said, I absolutely adore this game! for what seems to be this indie studio's first game, look pretty great in my opinion. I really liked the creativity that was put into the visuals, attacks, combos, and how great the girls' powers looked. Most of them looked fluent while I activated their abilities and their abilities just felt great to use (especially  power). were  I felt like I had a great connection to every character and felt pulled in with their unique charm. I kept wanting more from them like more character story and lore or a game sequel (please I beg... or a similar new game). Having amazing characters is a huuuuuge plus and is why I enjoyed this game so much. I don't think any of the characters, aside from a few lines that were forced by the plot (more on the plot later), felt out of place or weird. I really can't say  negative about the characters. is good. The combat tends to be repetitive and there isn't enough strategy to it to make it  interesting but I found myself enjoying it a little more once I figured out the key difference between the use of the great-sword compared to the normal sword. The few main things I think made the gameplay worse is that there is "one" singular 'rinse and repeat' mechanic to break shields, how I found myself using the great-sword 85% of the time (because of it simply being better in most cases than the sword), the way that the difficulty is extremely easy even on max difficulty (aside from occasionally getting hit due to the weird dodge roll or the final boss), and how all you need to do is dodge roll at a specific time (which tends to be quite generous) to more or less win every fight just makes the gameplay uninteresting at times. Other than that it did feel nice to use and it was pretty responsive. The only other thing I wished for was more puzzles that were challenging and varying. Each area had their own puzzles but I felt that there weren't enough of them and that unique puzzles could've prevailed throughout the entire game and gotten more complex as the game progresses to give a sense of familiarity but also a sense of challenge. It felt like I was being introduced to a puzzle and it was almost immediately taken away from me once I found myself figuring it out. is alright. There were many weak points and a few plot discrepancies but there were a many strong parts that made me tear up, were heartwarming, or that were downright hilarious. Dialogue options were funny and interesting at most points in the game and had me smiling a lot. There were times I could call characters "mommy" or ask my best friend to hide my p*rn collection at a point where we thought I was dying. Even so, I would occasionally be interrupted with weird weak points that felt out of place or that just felt plain distracting. The part of the story that forever hooked me into this game, however, is the ending. It was a phenomenal ending and it got me in a mindset of  a sequel. I would've bought a sequel no matter the cost if there was one made upon finishing the game. There are a couple things I dislike about the game that don't make sense and got me straight up annoyed at times. One of those things are that the day counter stays in the HUD even if you depart on a mission (the day counter is exclusively there to tell you when you are required to depart on a mission). It was simply there for no reason and I don't see why they thought to keep it. Even in the final boss-fight it was in the top right corner like it always is. I don't need to know the date to fight monsters unless they're going to give me a pop quiz. If it was put into the menu in its own area then this wouldn't be a problem. I would've actually liked it having its own menu spot. Another thing is the rooms for "the gang". If I can remember correctly, when we first get on the train, you are able to physically enter Chani's room (unsure if this is correct) and Yuna's room by walking to it and interacting with the door. After the first time or two, you are never required to go to the back of the train where the rooms are. Even when more rooms are unlocked for the other characters you are never actually able to personally enter them. There are cutscenes or small story segments where you are teleported into the room but you never really  the rooms. I am really confused why they were so underused. They felt like wasted space. I'm just a little disappointed why the areas were added and I could walk to them if they were inaccessible the entire game. Another annoyance I had was two characters came into the game and were almost immediately forgotten. One was Aria and the other was Eunji. They had a small run-time and were pretty much forgotten. I didn't really feel much for them by the end of the story. If the characters weren't good, the visuals and general look of the game weren't as appealing, and the story didn't have those incredible strong points, then I could not recommend this game for anything over $10. However, since the characters are so interesting, the look of the game had me decently interested, and the strong points in the story stuck with me throughout the game, I would recommend this game any day. This will be a game I will likely remember for a long time. Again, buy this on a sale but know that even if you buy it full price you're in for a lot of laughs, fun moments, groovy combat, and creative visuals. (This is my first real review so take it all with a grain of salt. I am not trying to scare anyone away from this game with this review. This game is great so definitely check it out!)

_childDocuments_.review: A jack of all trades but master of none, Eternights is the skeleton of an excellent hack and slash alternative to Persona and other social bond-building dating sims. I recommend this game only when on sale; 30 dollars is a bit steep for what Eternights has to offer. If the game was, say, 50 hours longer and generally filled out around the edges, this would no doubt be a must-have entry in the larger "dating sim with some form of dungeon crawling" genre even at 60 dollars, but Eternights simply can't accomplish that with its resources. As an indie pursuit, it goes so far beyond expectations that it must be compared to Atlus's greats, which is an achievement in itself, but at the end of the day it cannot compete, and thus I can't recommend it at full price. Below are some more specific positives and negatives; I'll try to keep it spoiler-free, but I may have to mention some things involving the premise.The plot is paper thin, with some elements (the train that you live in for the majority of the game, for one thing) left with little to no introduction and even less fleshing out. I'm not calling for everything to be explained, as many stories are far too involved with filling in every possible hole. Eternights's problem, however, lies in that the world of the game feels created only to serve the game's plot. The introduction shows snapshots of mysterious buildings in distinctly named places around the world (London, for one). Do we travel to these areas during the game, gaining new allies along the way? No. Despite the very possible opportunity, Eternights insists on keeping its world vague, and the lore even vaguer. I expected to have some revelation in the 'lab' level of the game, which was built up to pull back the curtain on the events that kicked off the plot. Suffice to say, this expectation was not reached. I have some nitpicks about character writing, particularly with one development arc that feels dreadfully mismanaged, but the characters meet expectations set by Persona 3, 4, and 5, which are likely what you'll compare these characters to.Reading that, it might seem like I hated the story, but it's compelling in its own way. It doesn't take itself too seriously, and it knows it's not a hard sci-fi story. Strange, magical machinery appears without much buildup, but the story never dwells on any one idea long enough to make you scrutinize it too heavily (Other than the aforementioned train.) Like a good dating sim should be, it's driven by its characters, which are likable if a bit cringe-inducing at the beginning (jokes about porn magazines in a game that came out in 2023, really? Maybe I'm getting old, but this really isn't funny anymore, if it ever was.) Thankfully, if you can get past the first section of the game the characters round out nicely, even if the cast is quite small. Again, with more resources the game would certainly be longer and have a larger cast to fill in some cracks in the storytelling, but Eternights does the job well enough with what it can. Oh, and as long as you have a heart, you're likely to be touched by the ending, even if it feels abrupt considering the game's length.Moving on to the hack and slash gameplay, it feels fine, but not superb. I'm not an aficionado of the genre, preferring slower combat in the vein of the Souls games, which Eternights does like to emulate in some boss battles, with the final boss almost feeling like a knockoff Malenia from Elden Ring. It's enjoyable, but not particularly moving. Levels are a little too dark and linear but I had a penchant for still getting lost, almost like a DOOM game without many secrets. I found myself relieved when I got away from the core loop to do simple picture puzzles, but that is probably just the Survival Horror fan in me coming out than a condemnation on the main gameplay. It is likely to frustrate you at times, but it feels gratifying enough that you won't want to quit after a particularly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ encounter. It's not PlatinumGames level, but it plays well enough to keep you from wishing you were playing one of their games instead.The amount of care put into this game is visible and heartwarming. It's rough around the edges, and each element of Eternights is likely outdone by another game, but the whole is greater than the sum of its parts, leaving you with a unique experience, even if you wish there was just a little more meat on the bone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some promise, but by other reviews, is drastically over hyped. I've seen this game being compared to Persona and Dark Souls and I question if people have actually played those games. The story is very bland. There is no interest given into why I should care about the apocalypse as the main thing I interact with are people, which so far is only two "characters'. I say that, because you have Yuna, who is just tsundere waifu bait that has a decent personality and then you have... chani... This dude is insufferable. You go from him being your bro, to him worrying about your death and how he wouldn't be able to save you, to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about how you lost your arm and got a cool power out of it all within 30 minutes. it doesn't help a lot of the game is clunky and the dialogue is also clunky. The combat is also very bad. You can basically spam your attacks to win fights. No cool combos or anything. Theres a slow time mechanic when you dodge which is just broken from the beginning making you invincible to damage for a short while. The boss fights are laughable. You basically spam your attack until you charge up the "Super cool" Quick time event attack which you might have to do 2-3 times before actually damaging the boss. Also the fact that you have to wait to pull out your weapon is so annoying. The animations are also mediocre at best. Idk why chani runs like he has a stick up his a** but it's goofy and looks bad. Along with some other cut scenes and their skin looking pink for some reason. Oh brother the amount of talking is also absurd. I feel like I spend more time listening to exposition then I do actually playing the game. The game wants to give a tutorial on the little things, but when it comes to the training minigames it throws you to the wolves, wraps up the rewards (or lack there of) that you get and skips to the next day quickly. Oh and for people hoping this is different from your generic anime, the first thing that happens once you get progress relationships with your allies is you walking in on a girl changing. Stay classy weebsThe ONLY positive I can give this game is the CG art scenes that are well drawn. I am not sure why a game was made out of this when a webtoon would've been a better way to convey the story without the headache actually playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't normally make reviews so gonna keep this brief. This is a Persona-like game with some combat elements that remind me of souls genre. Dodging, parrying, and timing of attacks/combos are important elements to defeating the various mobs and bosses. Combat feels great and weighty. Difficulty seems tuned properly (currently on Brutal but a friend of mine is playing on normal and still dies occasionally). The art style is very pretty, if a bit dark at a times in some locations. The dialogue and cast of characters I have met thus far (June 7th) are both incredible. Have definitely felt a range of emotions in the short time I have played thus far. For a game made entirely by one person, there is a lot here that would seem to run contrary to that. Not to mention that the cast of VAs is on par with AAA studios. Give the demo a go if you enjoy Persona-style day cycles and social links/confidants.

There's just something special.The animated cut scenes are beautiful, and voice acting (in Japanese at least) is really good.Gameplay is fun, with fine amount of upgrades and combos, which don't get too repetitive due to the game being short.And most importantly, the characters and the story are GREAT. _childDocuments_.review: A heartfelt game with a few flaws here and there. It's easy to have an emotional connection with the characters that join you in this journey to save the world from a reality-destroying apocalypse. The writing, though a bit cliché and tropey at times, is still quite good and there's definitely some humorous beats. Combat is... okay? It's moreso that the combat was something I had to get through to interact more with my party members. I never really had the impression that I got the hang of it since the dodge and parry system seems rather finicky. But that might be due to me.The dungeon exploration part could've really used a map though. I found myself getting lost in the same type of hallways and just wanted to get it over with. I also wish there might be some hint system for which social stat your responses increase, maybe as an accessibility feature for my ND brain.The emotional pay-off is well worth it though, so I applaud the developer for trying to give a unique spin on games like this! It's clear that they wanted to experiment and it turned out pretty darn good.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Indie project with lots of good ideas, heart, and minimal but noticeable jank. Well worth the price tag.The combat is focused on Bayonetta's slow-mo mechanic and the animation lock, as well as very conditional stagger power in your character means the game plays more or less like a fast, stamina-less Dark Souls. For the Souls fans, this might be a plus but if you're tired of seeing the same bland formula for combat, there isn't much to intrigue you in terms of combat.Characters are tropey but fleshed out and well-written enough to be enjoyable.The story is as straightforward as it gets. You won't find much symbolism or subtlety but it has a lot of personality (thanks to the characters), which is all I can ask for from an indie game.Dating sim elements are simple and give important stat bonuses and moves. If your preference for character writing favors anime and JRPGs, you should find the characters lovable enough, I think. It should be obvious but you won't find a Durance or Kreia or Joshua Graham in this game.One tip to all Persona fans eyeing this game: You won't have as much time and freedom as you would in Persona, and you won't be able to max everything or any category in a blind playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to expect from this game, but I actually REALLY like it, it fills a Persona shaped hole in my life and it's really well voice acted too. _childDocuments_.review: Eternights is an amazing Apocalypse world with Action-packed Hack and Slash along with Dating Simulator elements, and believe me, the first time i read that i was as confused as you. "An HACK AND SLASH with DATING SIMULATOR elements? What did i just read?" was what i thought, but it seriously is a lot more than that, it is a story driven game that really brings an awesome story.The game world is fantastic, it is set during an apocalypse scenario in which Gods are fighting each other to take control of the world and change it forever. The "Zombie" threat is managed in a very good way, and the amount of enemies is just right. I really love the atmosphere it brings upon you, the one that makes you feel like you're the only ones left alive in a world where every single wrong choice can bring you to your demise.Really guys, Studio Sai went all out on their debut game. Eternights has a story that is very well written, it suits the world it is set in perfectly. Needless to say, the game is driven by story, so those of you that do not like sitting through dialogues to understand what is happening might have an hard time understanding it. I also sometimes get bored when having to sit through long dialogues, but man oh man Eternights really made me sit through all of them and made me have a lot of fun doing so.The characters are all amazing, they have their own personalities and characteristics and are very fun to be with (Min best girl btw). Their story is managed in a pretty good way, allowing the players to get a grasp of what these characters went through until now, and it will be the MC's job to make them feel safe. All of the confidants are (as i said already) very fun to spend the time with, and as you progress through their dates you really get to know them better and better. I hope we one day get a DLC or an Update with content related to the post-apocalyptic part of this game, as expanding the content related tho these characters would be awesome (I need more Min please and thank you XD)The BGMs... I'm no expert but brother, they were awesome. Each and every one of the BGMs really brought to life the area they are put in, the eerie ones especially brought the creepiness of exploring the once bustling cities that are now deprived of life. Sounds were pretty good, probably can be polished a little more to bring them to perfection, but i still liked them.I'm not that much of an Hack and Slash fan, but i liked the combat system in this game. I really enjoyed mixing up the skills, powers and spells with the combos during the fights, and i think expanding on the combos that you can do with the Sword and the Greatsword might help in bringing an even better fighting system to the players.I haven't encountered any major bugs during gameplay, and only encountered really small ones (Such as colliding with invisible walls on vines that are on the ground in ACT 5, while those vines are probably smaller than a centimeter.).The game crashed only 1 time for the entirety of my first playthrough that lasted around 16 hours (I took my sweet time, i know), so i think that is not that much of a problem.Keybinds cannot be changed unfortunately, and i think they should be. I had to use ICUE to change the keybinds for now, but adding the ability to change keybinds in the feature might be a good idea.Final cutscene is hidden behind a QR Code that you have to scan to watch. I think it is a fun idea, but i also see a lot of problems coming from it (people with no internet, or those that have no way of scanning it will find it extremely annoying), so i suggest adding the cutscenes into the game directly, into an extras menu or maybe by letting us click the QR code to watch the cutscene from within the game.Studio Sai really did a good job with this. I'm gonna keep an eye on them for their next releases and hope that we can be blessed with new games as good as this one. Overall, Eternights really is a good game and even those who don't really like Dating Simulator games might enjoy this, so i really recommend it to everyone who wants to try getting into this genre or that just likes the Hack and Slash fighting style. Also, i really recommend reading all the dialogues and not skipping any, the story really deserves to be read and the dialogues bring out the personality of the characters perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to what everyone else is saying here, the combat and varying game play mechanics (like a stealth section and motorbike steering stage) was arguably my favorite part. I absolutely LOVED the combat. It is different from other games I  have played and has a huge emphasis on QTEs. I love QTEs, and it was so satisfying to fall into a rhythm with enemies. It was just the right balance for me between being too difficult and too easy. Yeah, perhaps it can be a bit repetitive, but at the point in time I started to get bored is when a new game mechanic like I mentioned above was introduced. It gave me just enough of a break to come back into the next combat section re-energized. The fun in combat comes from learning different enemies' routines and predicting moves in order to have a successful combo. I was addicted to the feeling of perfectly timing my dodges. I wished more games had QTE emphasis like this game. My only real complaint is that I wish there were more of a variety of enemies to learn the patterns of. Oh, and of course the characters are amazing. A lot of people already touched on that though, I just wanted to give my two cents since a lot reviews seemed to hate the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to leave this game thinking that it was decent, but not great. Instead, I've left this game thinking it'll end up in my top 10 played this year. Eternights definitely has some jank, the 3D models look not great to say the least, which contrasts pretty harshly with the high quality 2D art used in the menus, many menus (the options menu is the most major example) look very basic and low effort, and the game had one or two moments where I had to Alt-F4, but that wasn't that big a deal, thanks to autosave. I also dislike that the game syncs graphics settings in Steam Cloud, which means that if you play the game on two seperate devices (PC, laptop, Deck, etc.) you will likely have to change your settings every time. Many of the character interactions were funny, though the game did have its share of Anime™ moments, and it failed to have serious moments hit hard, since many of them could be seen from a mile away, and others just felt... off somehow.On gameplay, it's a pretty easy game, as soon as you figure out the trick of dodge and punish. once you get that rhythm down, losing fights will be very rare, though that doesn't mean much anyways, since the game gives you checkpoints before pretty much every encounter. Very much looking forward to Studio Sai's next game, especially since they're no longer a one man team, and now have actual staff and budget to work with.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this, the game was cute for what it was, and overall, I think that Yuna was definitely the best character. To start off on a positive note, the absolute best thing about this game is by FAR the visuals. The art style is endearing and well done, especially the romance scenes. I was captivated by every single one of them, and the art direction was fantastic. Unfortunatley, this is the only positive thing I have to say right now.The gameplay was okay, about what I was expecting from an indie company. However, the writing is where the game really fell off for me. A lot of moments in the game were kind of shattered for me due to subpar writing choices and character actions. The characters were not really fleshed out, and had forced character development (if they got any at all).Even though Yuna was the best character, her writing was super flawed. The entire apocalypse premise was completely underused and undermined, treated with absolutely no gravity in any sense. There was the impending doom of 14 days, and during Yuna's like 5 or 6 heart event, she only cared about petty tabloid gossip concerning the reputation her friend, who may or may not be alive by the end of this, if the world even lasted. She used time and resources to record a PSA to play on every T.V. once the world "came back" to insist that her friend Jisoo was not actually drinking at a bar. This is just one example of the entire premise and setting not being utilized within the characters story. My biggest gripe is with the Yohan romance route. I understand this game is made for mostly straight men, but the one gay romance had the worst and most nonsensical writing of all of them. He shows up at the end of the game, and has almost no personality. They made him an immortal being, but we never learn of how he actually came to be that way, other than it had something to do with that incident involving Jace and Delia (which we still have no idea on what actually happened, or the events that lead up to that.) His psychology is surprisingly childish, despite also having this bitter distaste towards the gods (one of which he is also helping for some reason despite her like ruining his life??). We actually didn't know he harbored this until that random comment on the mural, and the fact that the gods had the mural over him and Delia.His brother randomly being a butterfly in his dreams was also a very weak point. We have known him for a very little time, and he just opened up his memories and past to us, allowing us to see his brother dying. After this, he invites us to go talk to his brother with him, for absolutely no reason. We stand there, offer him no solace. He stupidly asks his brother to "turn back to the way he was" and his brother respond with "No, I'm a butterfly now." and then turns back to himself anyways. Then, after a non-emotional 2 minute talk with him, his brother floats away for no reason.Lux and Umbra. As mentioned before, we have literally zero backstory to these two. All we learn was Lux is what makes people "people", and that only Lux or Umbra can be active at one time. The overarching plot there was entirely predictable, the whole "light is good and dark is bad" trope. Lux being the way she is, doesn't act like a goddess whatsoever. I don't even blame Delia for trusting Umbra over Lux, she was super sus and honestly I wouldn't put it past Lux to be lying about Jace actually being inside of the stone. Immature and childish, and I honestly thought just by the way she acted, that she was going to turn out to be a surprise villain. We also never once learn of Umbra's intentions, so I would assume it's just a very very surface level "I'm evil and I want to take over the world." Chani. Just a terribly awful written character. Plagued by the horny best friend trope, and not done in a "good" way. The game tries to pass him off as my "best friend" but honestly I kinda wished he just died in the beginning rather than that one random girl. Every scene with him in it was agonizing. His character writing was also way unorganized and did not flow well at all. He was my best friend, then he wanted to save my life, then he was jealous and butthurt over my powers and the fact he didn't get a power. Then he gets a power (albeit a weak one), and he still isn't grateful at all. His character jumped all over the place, it was impossible to tell how he felt about MC. I felt that at any given moment in time he would turn on us, just cus I had no idea what the hell this character was truly thinking about.]I understand this game was written by a small team, but man the writing was just so hard to get through some times. Had they hired extra writers or had more time to polish the story and character events, this game could have been something truly special. It is almost heart breaking how the writing hindered this game, especially since the premise is on building bonds with characters and social stats.I could go on and on about many many many different examples of how baffling the writing choices were, even if the game was based around being a dating sim. The lack of actual dating sim mechanics was also heavily felt, and leveling characters bonds only affected minimal aspects of the game play.The combat. As I said at the start, I wasn't expecting much coming from an indie game developer. The fact this game got released is a major accomplishment and an impressive feat in its own right. However. The combat could have been a touch more interesting. It was literally spamming the same button over and over and over. They could have added two or three different combos just to spice it up a bit, but no. You had one 5 hit combo and one 3 hit combo and that was it. For about half of the game. The support shield break was also very unintuitive and worked the exact same for all 4 characters. It just felt bad most of the time.Lastly, (though I could say so much more about many other different things), I have no problem with the ending. However I DO have a problem with the events leading up to the ending.

_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what a game! This is the best anime game I've ever played and one of the best indie games (or any game in general that I've played). The gameplay is fast paced and is extremely fun! Now even tho this is wayyy out of my comfort zone (I'm more of a platformer guy tbh) it was still extremely fun! Hack n slashing my way through enemies, having to properly time when the enemies will attack so I can dodge in time to get that quick speed boost, building bonds and relationships with people, etc, etc. Twas a good time! The story was pretty good too, nothing crazy good but for an indie game it was pretty damn good! The dialogue can be a bit cheesy at times but sometimes the dialogue choices can legit make me burst out laughing like a nut job (Like when Min says you're bad at telling jokes and one of the dialogue choices are "I laughed" was actually really funny asf lmao). The voice acting was pretty good! (The English cast, haven't heard much from the Japanese or Korean cast yet on a 2nd playthrough I will play it in Korean since the game does take place in South Korea) Everyone killed it! and some of the acting got me really emotional good job on the actors/actresses and the voice directors! The art and 2D animated cutscenes were all AMAZING! Shout out to the artist and animators! Now its not perfect. I don't think the music was very memoriable imo and doesn't really get there until the end of the game. I'm not saying the music is bad but it did not stick to me while playing the game. Another issue I have which is honestly my biggest problem with the game are the in-game animations, they could have been better and I feel like Chani got the short in of the stick here oh also minor nit-pick here but I really hate how we have to name the protagonist and not have him speak throughout the entire game, if you're going to have him speak at the end of the game then I think you should have gone all the way through with making him speak throughout the game (I literally named him Phillip because that's the name I saw in one of the trailers for him and I think most of the fandom will agree on that being his name lol) but nevertheless this is a great time. It was fun, interesting, had me invested, made me laugh a bit, and made me cry (This might be the first video game I've ever cried to) 8.5/10 a great game!

The text translation of my main language (Brazilian Portuguese) was also pretty well done.Some points of improvement:- UI/Menu navigation on Mouse and Keyboard is awful- No achievements for harder difficulties- Calendar is not internationalised (dates are always in US format)- Difficulty spikes pretty abruptly, since the enemies get faster with harder difficulties this makes some of their attacks pretty unfair and unavoidable.Bugs I found:- In the first main boss fight of the game the autosave to the second phase of the boss wasnt work and had to be manually reloaded through the menus. _childDocuments_.review: The most striking thing about this game is its writing. The writing, especially the dialogue, is funny, genuine, believable, and FULL of personality. It's incredible that a single dev can write such good dialogue while games from big studios are still stuck in the  "Marvel Funny Quips and One-Liners" writing style.Despite it being a liiiitle rough around the edges, the game is worth it for the story and writing alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: A novel feeling I get while playing a game is when a game is so genuine enough, so clearly a work of passion, that I become detached from the notion that I am playing a game- I suddenly become hyper aware of the fact that I'm watching characters written and animated by people who sat in front of a computer for endless hours motivated not by how much money the game would make, but by how much the finished product will be a game they themselves will enjoy.This is usually seen as a negative trait, or amateurish, but I find it charming and joyful. A bunch of people came together and worked their asses off for the common goal of making something, putting it out there, and being vulnerable in their influences and likes. And now I'm playing that game. And it is great.

It takes different ideas and gaming mechanics from various famous games for example Persona and also instead of turn based combat, this game is focused on realtime combat with a parry and a dodge. This all sounds fun and game but the problem is that its just the bare minimum and it feels just llittle effort and depth has gone into these elements. The game itself is quite short, which is not bad in its own, espeically for 30€, but it just feels not worth the money and the time. The same goes for character, story and out-of-combat interactions with said characters. You can date every girl and 1 guy, but all of them are one-dimensional and boring. _childDocuments_.review: Eternights is the loveable awkward cousin of the Persona franchise that provides a downright outstanding experience considering the game was masterminded by only three people. It’s a far cry from perfect, absolutely, but if you love the social side of Persona games and maybe aren’t such a fan of JRPGs (hi hello, it’s me) then Eternights can absolutely scratch an itch for you, if only for a short while.What immediately bowled me over playing the demo for Eternights was the level of cinematography being used to deliver the story dialogue. Eternights puts Persona’s static room shots to shame, taking full advantage of its 3D environments to pan, zoom, or crop in, plus using a variety of angles to keep things feeling engaging. And this doesn’t even come at the cost of proper cutscenes – the game still has those too! There are multiple animated cutscenes(!) and several in-engine ones as well. The frequency of these is definitely frontloaded to cement a good first impression, but regardless the creativity exercised by this three-person team exceeds that of a AAA studio here; Atlus had better be taking notes.The main change moving from Persona to Eternights is the gameplay of the dungeon crawling sections. Persona games are classic JRPG turn-based weakness-exploiting battles, which Eternights entirely does away with in favour of being a hack ‘n’ slash (and no, it’s not similar to Persona 5 Strikers). You have a dodge roll (with a perfect timing mechanic), a sword with two different forms/movesets, four distinct abilities, a QTE-fest ultimate, and you also can request your allies to use their abilities to aid you in combat (e.g. healing, AoE crowd control, or damage). This is the sort of combat in games I really enjoy, however the implementation here is… subpar. The genre swap was what drew me to play this game before picking up Persona 3 Reload, but unfortunately combat is the weakest aspect of Eternights. Allow me to explain.Dodging an enemy attack is dependent on you timing a button press with a prompt (warning noise + flash), instead of being i-frame or hitbox based. What this means is that if you press the roll button before or after the warning prompt such that your character visibly evades the attack, you will still get hit. What. I’m going to go as far as to say this is straight-up wrong and is never the correct choice for any game, and I like to think it’s self-explanatory as to why. You can get used to it, but this in combination with the usage of such blatant cues reduces the skill ceiling of Eternights dramatically. I understand not everyone wants a Souls-like – personally I think this game could do well as one – but I do think the difficulty here has been excessively diluted regardless.Further to combat, the perk tree of Eternights is decidedly uninspired. There’s little meaningful choice as no mutually exclusive options/branches exist, and the majority of upgrades are just incremental improvements to abilities you already have. None of the options beyond the initial unlock of a skill altered how I played the game, and the numbers changes are so small they were hard to notice. In a singleplayer PvE experience I would always expect developers to err on the side of making perks or abilities too strong as this is often more fun than the opposite, but that’s not the approach Studio Sai took. I hope in the next game there are impactful playstyle-specific choices to be made, along with better balancing in general.The final two issues with combat feed into each other: every enemy can be dealt with in moreorless the same way, and there isn’t a great amount of enemy variety. Winning a fight requires timing a single dodge roll, then you spam basic attacks until the enemy recovers, then use all your special moves that they can’t block, and then you wait for the next dodge opening to repeat. There’s no risk/reward consideration whether to go for an extra attack: either you’ve set yourself up correctly and have enough time, or you don’t. It doesn’t feel like enemies have any agency like they did in Lies of P; they never take charge of the fight – even bosses just take their punishment once you’ve dodged correctly (meanwhile  has a full combo  you stagger her). I think the critical mistake here was having a single perfectly timed dodge guarantee you a full combo – in Souls-likes you’d need to dodge multiple times to avoid the enemy’s complete combo to find an opening, or in other hack ‘n’ slashes the dodge doesn’t guarantee anything beyond you not taking damage.Moving on from grilling the game’s combat then, I’ll briefly air a couple qualms I had with the story. It’s far from water-tight; if you wanted to critically analyse it would hold as much water as a sieve. I’m not saying it’s not enjoyable, but you just have to let it happen and not think too deeply about it. That having been said, some events really need more justification: when Sia magically appears and joins your party, no one really questions her or her motives, where she came from, how she survived until now, et. cetera. The other bit I didn’t like was the ending. The game very explicitly gets you to make a choice, and if you answer truthfully, you will probably also not enjoy the ending.  I’m not sure what Studio Sai were going for with the scannable QR code post-ending either, like why not include the video in the game? Instead, I got a real life quick time event to pull my phone out and scan the thing before it disappeared.There’s a lot of tough love in this review (and I left out a fair number of more minor gripes), so I want to re-emphasise that how closely Eternights manages to capture the Persona series’ core values in spite of its diminutive team size is nothing short of a marvel, and Studio Sai should be immensely proud of what they’ve made here. With an increased focus on combat feel in the next entry, and hopefully the budget for a more fleshed out story, I am excited to see what comes next! For now though, Eternights is a comfortable recommendation from me if you like the dating sim half of Persona games and having hack ‘n’ slash mixed in with that sounds like a good time, and you’re willing to look past the rough edges. In my eyes, on sale the game is absolutely worth it for what it offers, not to mention supporting such a promising developer.

_childDocuments_.review: My total score 8.5/10 when on my scale. I really loved this game and I hope it's the start of an awesome run for Studio Kai. There are very little games that scratch so many anime tropes like this one. The story and characters have a charm that sadly made me speed through this short game. Plot/Characters: I really like how the main character is laid out. The choices though few and not overly important to the story, had me immersed as I hit on best girl Yuna. The relationship with your main bro is also great and charming. They really hooked me with in this perspective. The story is alright with obvious tropes around every corner. Gameplay/Design: I like the post apocalypse theme, the maze like environments, and most of all the rewards for exploring.(Even though they aren't very useful) The little puzzles you encounter though not the best at times make for an extra charm and level of annoyance that again really scratches some itch for me when it comes to puzzles. There are few enemy designs and for a short game like this I would have liked more variety even some random color picker for enemy clothes. Fighting SystemThis game is not hard even on expert mode. The fighting system really left me with desires for more polish. You will mostly fight repetitive waves of the mostly same melee units and the off screen shooters that mess everything up. It tries certain things like mixing the order of parry times vs dodge times but it left me wanting Sekiro or Lies of P type polish. Buy and it and play it. Even for 30 this is a great game and I'm hoping to see more of this style from them!

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved my time with Eternights. As a mixture of hack and slash combat and Persona story/side elements, there's plenty of good, and plenty of bad - good level design, tedious combat; fun characters, lots of waiting around for the plot to proceed; engaging story, occasional terrible trope usage. Overall, as an indie game, considering the scale of it, the studio should be proud of their work, and I'd love to see what comes next.Yes, the Persona influences are very, very clear - the primary gameplay loop consists of grinding through a dungeon, and then using the rest of your time between dungeons to focus on the social/dating sim elements, it's all on a calendar with pre-determined events on certain days, a split between daytime events and night events, social stats to level up to progress further in each love interest's route, etc. The implementation is pretty much what you'd expect, but that's what I wanted, so I was glad to see it. Having only four romanceable options seemed kind of small to me before I played, but given the rather narrow scope of the narrative, it ended up making sense, and I think a larger cast would have resulted in needless bloat.Combat-wise, it's standard, repetitive hack and slash. You can unlock stronger moves as you progress, but the basic combo will carry you through pretty much any standard encounter, leaving the special moves to be useful only for bosses and enemies with shielded health, requiring a specific elemental matchup to break before laying on regular moves. That aspect of the combat is pretty much the only part that requires any thinking, which is a little disappointing, because even the bosses end up feeling rote, as their gimmicks no longer really matter when you can flowchart your way through the fight. That said, I didn't get the sense that the combat was the main focus of the game anyway, so it didn't bother me all that much.I enjoyed the story - it's a straightforward apocalypse narrative, where the player is granted special power in order to defeat the evil lurking at the end. There aren't really any twists along the way, either, but the story is propped up significantly by the characters, all of whom I found charming and endearing in different ways. I made my romance choice pretty much the moment Sia showed up, but I found all four of the potential partners to be viable, which I think is a sign that a lot of thought and care was put into them. They all have their own reasons for getting involved in the story, and are all completely distinct, both in personality and backstory. The dating sim elements are easily the best part of this game for me, and pursuing the other characters' romance routes adds replayability for sure.It's not a perfect game, of course - several of the typical anime tropes throughout the story were tiresome and annoying. Chani's personal growth arc is simultaneously excruciating and lightning-fast, and it didn't endear him to me one bit. That he and the protagonist are both perverts (and that you basically have to play the protagonist this way because the dialogue options don't let you avoid it) was eye-rolling, even if it doesn't really drag the story down. As distinct and fun as the romance options are, each of them does occasionally feel a little one-note, without very much depth to their character traits. And, as refreshingly simple as the story is, I found myself with a lot of questions about the worldbuilding that basically go completely unaddressed even as you're fighting for the fate of this world - I would've liked to see a bit more exploration of those elements, possibly in wider side content. Of course, the mid-apocalypse setting limits what you can do in that regard, and I could definitely feel myself straining against those limits towards the end of the game, trapped in that damn train.On the whole, though? Wonderful game. I had a great time with it, and it's one that I wouldn't hesitate to replay in order to try out a different romance route. Absolutely worth the price and your time.

_childDocuments_.review: For an RPG game made by an indie dev, it's a really good game.Game plays similar to Persona (you have time limits and have to explore dungeons to get to the boss. You can choose return to your base within the week and do social interaction to increase your companion approval). The romance progression is really well done, they've put a lot of effort into the characters. It's not all braindead jiggly boobies; there are narratives and sub-narratives revolving around each character and the main plot (you have male romance options too). The first 1 hour of the game wasn't the best (way too dark), but get past that and the game starts to become more and more immersive. It's like an apple with blemished skin that turns out to be juicy when you actually take a bite. Combat reminds me of Dark Souls series. You need to dodge/parry, and on higher difficulty taking damage is fatal because healing options are limited. On normal difficulty, you usually take 1-2 game overs or none at all to clear the boss (that's how it was for me). Minigames and puzzles are a refreshing break from the mid-dungeon battles.Graphics and User Interface need a lot of work but understandable because this is a budget game from a really small game studio. I personally didn't really like the foggy/bloomy ambience (sometimes it gets way too blurry) so giving a -1 on that.All in all, though, I'd say this is worth the money I spent on it. RPGs these days tend to be subpar in both story and combat, but Eternights has done a marvelous job of balancing out these elements.8/10 from me, would have given 9/10 if the graphics had been easier on the eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: So I 100% Eternights and….This indie Action RPG + Dating Sim game was surprisingly more fun and emotional than I expected. I was quite invested in each confidants’ main story and backstory. The humor worked for me. Combat is smooth in most parts(except the part where the MC takes quite a while to stand up), the QTEs for the elemental attacks are generous and simple enough to not break the flow of fighting. Engaging in Persona’s social aspects(training or spending time w/ confidants & keeping track of their skill trees) and time management were neat. The mini-games from training w/ each dateable character are fun to varying degrees(my favorite is splitting cells). The linear dungeons and their progression puzzles are also simple and short that makes repeated playthrough bearable. I personally love a lot of the enemies' designs. BUT the one feature I focused the most: HOLD RT/R2 TO HOLD HANDS( I would elaborate more about this but nah, instead, I’m just gonna incentivise you to check it out by yourself ).As for nitpicks, the game occasionally crashes on PC(be advised to save often). Skipping the credits might deny the player from unlocking the last achievement where it asks you to “earn all trophies” even if you did unlock all 25/26 trophies. The direction/editing on the Escape scene in Act2 was weird, I think the scene should’ve been extended to match a natural endpoint of the OST instead of being abruptly cut. And I wasn’t a fan of the stealth sequence of slowly walking on deadly goo..In terms of neutral aspects, I wish we had a gallery for character/enemy models to appreciate their designs, I assume that’s in the digital art book, and in that case I wish I could purchase it w/o it being bundle w/ the soundtrack in the Deluxe Ed. The demand for precise dodging and parrying might not be for everyone but IT IS DEFINITELY FOR ME; I can see why a lot of reviewers complain about the game being difficult( with the demand for Almost-Perfect Dodge + Parry ) and prefer to have less fights or wish it were turn-based… but from my experience, the amount of combat is adequate, dying over and over didn’t affect me bc it doesn’t have a ranking system like DMC or Bayonetta, and the respawn points are quite generous compare to Soulslike titles, there are fights that you can run away from(except in sealed areas or Bosses), and there are no achievements/trophies about beating the game in X difficulty( so you can play Easy Mode w/o feeling the shame of being exposed as a scrub)I can’t believe people were having trouble w/ the Act 3 Bike sequence instead of the slow af “Piggyback riding across deadly goo” section, I guess everyone has their own skill issue..Overall, highly recommend playing this solid, short, and tight game w/ good replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun RPG.  Relates itself mostly to Persona and dating sims.  I have never played a Persona game but I have played some dating sims.  I also enjoy action-adventure-puzzle games like Legend of Zelda and Kingdom Hearts.  I found Eternights to be really fun, really charming, and really cheesy.The fact that it was made by a one man developer REALLY shows at some points.  Lots of loading screens, small maps (On the bright side this is good for weaker hardware!  I don't own a Steam deck but I imagine it would provide a good experience), lack of animations.  Small awkward moments happen in game play.  It's all forgiveable really but I would love to see this game with a budget larger than $2 and some spit.Like I said, it's all forgiveable.  Those $2 went MILES at the best parts of the game.Combat is fun.  I played it on normal and found it to be a little on the hard side (I beat Kingdom hearts on proud NOT critical) until I grinded up my stats and got stronger towards the end + a little bit of learning the game.Dialogue is really silly but these are young adults.  That's how they talk.  On top of that everyone expresses themselves like its a mid 2000's to early 2010's shounen anime."Calendar gameplay" is something I was not familiar with until now.  It's just a long timer that you can't really mess up unless you try to.  If you have timer anxiety, you can relax.The girls all feel like "safe" choices personality wise.  You'll like some more than others yeah, but you won't dislike any.  To me its not a problem, deep characters / writing is not the point of Eternights.  Their physical designs are all great but won't stand out.Bonus points: Features that this game has that EVERY RPG should have but a some don't. 1) New Game+ (Haven't started it yet.  Idk the details of what you take with you).  2) Separate language options for Audio language and text language (be a weeb with ENG text and JPN voices or be a normie with ENG both).Make of all that what you will.To me, I was in love with how cheesy Eternights was from the first trailer.  I pre-ordered the deluxe edition and don't feel disappointed.  It's hard to say "if you're a fan of X then play this" so honestly, just buy the game.  If you feel hesitant then wait for a sale.  Give it the money I think it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! That was so much better than I thought it would be! I can't believe this is basically made by a single person. Someone in the industry please give this guy a job!This is rather obviously a short version of Persona 5 except with the center of the story being the romantic elements. I prefer shorter games (I love Persona 5, but omg I've been literally playing it for years and I'm still not done!). This one took me about 20 hours and was just right for me. Every moment in this game mattered. It was back-to-back non-stop enjoyment. The girls are all interesting characters and you actually want to hang out with them. (But don't make the mistake of trying to romance all of them or you miss the best endings.) One of the characters is definitely 'best girl' though (but I won't tell you who) and gives a stand out performance even compared to her rather stiff competition. The action combat was actually well done. It was a sort of easier version of a soul's game. The characters that you develop friendships with level up their combat assistance powers as you get to know them better. This ties the two sides of the game together in an interesting way. I have to wonder why there aren't more games like this. There is something charming about going on adventures with virtual friends when done right like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Eldritch creature puts you under her employ through your dating profile to put the other horror that just woke up back to sleep. make friends and solve puzzles in a presently-apocalypting japan.The anime aesthetic vibes so harshly against the enemy's nasty designs and detailing that it comes back around again to vibing well again. The characters are all pleasant, well enough written to be more than just their troupe and catchphrase, and meaningful enough by the end that they each serve a decent purpose. From a game-play perspective there is a character that is more advantageous to be with than the others; due to the elemental properties of their powers and the final few bosses weaknesses, but all are fair game. The humor is juvenile and i love it. The combat clearly got the most development attention; as the enemies are all very diverse, with many attacks each, the player has many options by mid-game to fight back; though the parry/dodge system takes the most to get used to.it behaves more like a rythmn game rather than a souls-like that most are used to. With you being expected to hit the dodge button as soon as the "tell" (the sound and visual cue) is given. Resulting in first encounters with enemies being rough until you see what part of their animation is considered "too late" to dodge. Puzzles and other mechanics were very varied and all fun to solve. ball rolling puzzles, driving challenges, counting, placement, and sliding puzzles; nearly every type but a match-3none overstayed their welcome and use; and each served its purpose to divide up the non-overly long dungeons.Technical issues.Camera speed is tied directly to the frame rate; so playing above 60fps will result in an unstable and likely very slow camera. Audio issues and animation quirks are forgiveable; though what wasn't was VERY important parts of the plot having their cutscenes being skipped over requiring me to later look them up lout of game due to the vital information they contained. This happened more times than i could count; leaving me confused how we got where we are, and worst of all occurred on the final 2 cutscenes of the game, leaving me basically completely unaware of what happened in the ending until i looked it up externally.they were great cutscenes, really well animated and cutely written; but holy moly it has been 5 months, feels like this should have been high on the priority list of things that need fixing. The ending was good. I neither loved it nor hated it, though it does not heavily change based on who you choose to be engaged with, which is fine; but makes me uncertain of the NG+ inclusion.You will have enough in game time to fully pursue 2 and possibly 3 of the characters should you choose to do so and budget time wisely. Beating a dungeon ahead of time will not result in a time skip; you will always have some reason why you must wait that set amount of time anyway, and be able to interact with your buddies.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. I'm glad the developer fleshed out each character. Calendar-based story and dialogue mechanics similar to Persona. Combat is okay, though the flashing indicator to dodge or parry is inconsistent. Don't rely solely on it, else enemies with barely any time between flash and attack will dunk on you.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface by saying this game can only be enjoyed once you accept it is EQUALLY a hack and slash and a dating sim. Dont expect it to be some highly sophisticated combat focused game.This game is a straight up masterpiece. Its a short and sweet experience with:- simple combat that rewards you for playing smart and using the mechanics given whilst also being EXTREMELY visually rewarding (i will never get tired of chainsawing barriers through). Some might find it TOO simple, my casual ass finds it enough to be engaging.- puzzles which are simple and not infuriating but arent utterly dumbed down to do so.- a Cast of characters which are all utterly and terminally loveable and all of them being completely their own character without any overlap with others.- A story which in honesty is simple and short, is extremely well executed and contains all the neccessary story beats to be a complete one.- Forged bonds with characters feels so genuine and realistic and the romances are just ofjigsdogjsig adorable and cute- And a poignant ending which will make you speedrun the 5 stages of grief.The only negative i can name is the game is too short for its non-sale price tag, but otherwise BOP 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR The B-tier "We have persona at home". And you know what? That's not an insult.Pros:-It is, to quote a certain reviewer, "anime as balls". Which is both a pro and a con. Every over the top excess and silliness that you stereotype in anime, it happens here too. And it's gloriously cringe.-Given how small the dev team is, the graphics and presentation are honestly pretty and robust. Animation is good in combat too even if a bit jank in cutscenes.- The dialogue options you get to have for him are often hilarious and witty. Genuinely, made me smile and laugh multiple times at how sassy-but-stoic you could be. Incredible.-The characters are all cute and likeable in their own ways and quirks. Chani best girl.-If you're a fan of the Persona-style "Spend time and forge bonds" system, you'll enjoy it here as well.-The story and gameplay occasionally takes jarring turns into silly nonsense like motorcycle riding and Dance Dance Revolution minigames which make me laugh at the absurdity.Cons:-As said before: it is anime as balls. If you hate that style or tropes, you will cringe all the way home here.-Combat is pretty shallow. It's good for goofy hack and slash fun, but the only "challenge" is the admittedly precise timing you need for dodges or parries.-Story is nothing to write home about. Characters have conflicts and arcs that usually get resolved within 30 mins to 1 hour of them being introduced. -The story is a stop-start rollercoaster. Don't get a very clear set-up/premise, and then we're yanked from one story beat to another and im wondering where "she" got the power to create a magical motorcycle minigame.Overall, it's a light recommend, on the condition that: Me personally, after playing a bunch of thoughtful and serious games, this is the kind of B-tier cheese that makes me giggle. But if you're expecting something on the quality of Persona or with a riveting story and vast content, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I generally enjoyed the game play and story with a few pet peeves.- only one way to heal and it isn't available half the time (based on the path you chose)- very tight window for dodging- janky ass parrying- even janky-er facial animationsas stated though, it was a very enjoyable experience especially if you can get it on sale and can look past some of the bad design/gameplay decisions they made.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from a background of playing Persona, I thought to take a quick break from that. It was then I saw Eternights recommended to me on Steam. I decided to try out the demo, and I was hooked from then on.The gameplay is fluid, fun, clean, and above all, challenging. The characters are all lovable in their own ways, and knowing the English VAs for a few of the characters have worked on Persona games made me pretty happy too. The inspiration there is from Persona is pretty obvious to those who can recognise it, including Min's dialogue lines which reference Persona 5's Haru, but at the same time this is entirely its own thing.The story is written really well. The unexpected challenging parts where the gameplay isn't hack and slash, but something else, always had me on edge. The story always had me immersed such that I'd find myself up till 2am alone in the Discord vc not realising everyone had said goodnight!The ending of the game had me in tears. The usual trope of not being able to save the most beloved one to the hero is executed very well. The game does an excellent job at attaching the player emotionally to the characters, forces the player then to select the number one, and then pulls at the player's heart as the player attempts to save the one more beloved than the rest!All in all, I give this game 10/10. Definitely will play again.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, 8.5/10 imo. Buy it and support your local gamedev studio™️Fun game. Surprisingly polished for the love child of a one man development team. Does have a fair bit of jank but honestly it's endearing. The story is actually pretty decent, I was expecting a more cookie cutter plot. Sound design is nothing to write home about but not that forgettable either. Gameplay is fantastic, and reminds me of multiple games at once, including but not limited to: Dark Souls, Persona, Nobeta, Scarlet Nexus, etc. All in all, I really enjoyed it. Some parts got pretty annoying (the breathing minigame for Yuna, the part where you had to carry Min through the poison areas (clearly nobody playtested that)) but overall, very minor things that I easily overlooked. The dating sim part was also good, if a bit too janky at times. It would be much better if you could actually see the heart meters of the girls. But meh, I just finished it so I know now how it works clearly. Japanese voice acting is the best as always, however the EN dialogue does not fit it (it's VERY different), likely due to the fact that the script was rewritten in Korean/Japanese from English. Instead of localizing it for every language on earth, perhaps the budget would have been better spent reverse localizing from Japanese and Korean into separate English dialogue scripts, so that the text on the screen would actually fit what was being said. Personally, I found the Japanese 'story' and dialogue a lot more palatable than the English one, and 99% of the time I just ignored the text on the screen in favour of just listening to the characters.  I wouldn't call this one a minor gripe, yet at the same time it's something that 99% of players will not notice, so I'll let this slide too. There were a few elements that were very unique and I really liked, like how the ending worked (multiple things about it). I will not spoil it, but safe to say that even though I was expecting exactly what happened, it still managed to bring a tear to my eye. My one and only real gripe is the lack of text autoskip. There is no reason I should have to reread all the dialogue again in NG+. Just let me quickly get it done in a day so that I can grab all achievements. I'll wait to do NG+ until that drops in an update.

_childDocuments_.review: is a (comparatively) short action JRPG that puts you in the shoes of an MC that finds himself at the center of an apocalypse. With only a limited time until the world ends, you must fight monsters, bond with your best friend + some newfound companions, and retrieve a mysterious artifact that will save the world.  is a game that clearly draws from its inspirations. It tries to be a mish-mash of Persona, Soulsborne, classic JRPGs, and dating sims. Some of them don't quite land though, especially in its combat aspects. Regardless, it is still a very fun time. At least, I personally had more fun with it than Starfield as of writing. I'd say it is worth the full asking price. Though if you're on the fence, then it doesn't hurt to wait for a sale. If you've read this far enough, you'll probably find something in this game to like.
