_childDocuments_.review: For a game made by a very limited team, it’s actually solid. The DMC combat mixed with a dating sim fits decently, toss in a calendar/ trait system from the persona serious and it’s a really good entry.Likes:-Main cast is decently written, enjoyable as the game goes on-How you respond in conversations give trait points is a great idea, I like that it doesn’t say the prompt and then what it does, it makes me really think in conversations what to say-Combat is challenging, in a good way-Variety of side content is really good, mini games galore!-The combat spells and skills feel like they hit hard and are useful, it’s nice to see you can’t mash attack and just win the game. Dislikes:-Introductions to side characters and the world around are done very poorly story wise. Acts 1-3 just throws a bunch of events at the wall and it feels like none of it sticks. The world doesn’t feel believable because nothing is explained and just takes me out of the immersion. The game pushes a tragic villain but just tossing random names into the wind doesn’t make me feel engaged to care. It needs to slow down and let it cook a bit and branch out on its pacing. The world building is there, but the cement needs to dry a bit or the structure collapses on itself.-Dungeon variety on side dungeons would be nice, it’s all copy paste city scapes (park, sewers, etc)-Different execution animations variety would be nice on other sized enemies and not reused for every enemyHopes in the future:-Maybe a tad longer-Combo meter?-PLEASE ADD A GALLERY-Would’ve like more animated cutscenes-More elements or party member types, like how Yuna does healing and Min does shields, it would cool to experiment with  more. Not having Sia be the only combat spells would be nice-Swappable party? Or lowered party size?-as with shield break animations, if you could pick a weapon other than a sword, and have it be useable on the fly, I think that would spice combat flavor even more. You literally create a ton of things in the game but it doesn’t translate to combat other than sword and BIG sword(Sia is best girl)
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is fun but doesn't feel particularly well balanced in that its at times far too easy, and then suddenly far too difficult. Its a system that relies on parries and upping the difficulty only results in split second parry/dodge windows and dying in 2-3 hits to bosses.This wouldn't be so frustrating if parries worked the way every other game does it. Rather then dodging through attacks for perfect dodges, you instead have to wait for a red flash on the screen and dodge JUST as it appears. These flashes often appear before the enemy has even started their attack path meaning your anticipating the anticipation rather then the attack itself. In most games, the enemy winds up and you get ready to dodge the attack. In this game, the enemy winds up and you press the dodge button right then and there even if the attack is no where near yet. This leads to some times having to dodge at the most random of times just because a red flash is there. On to that point, projectiles are incredibly random in how dodging them works. Sometimes dodging nearby a projectile will trigger a perfect dodge, othertimes it does nothing at all.Combat barriers and quick time events are rampant here and its not fun. Stronger enemies have barriers that need to be broken before they can take damage. This means wailing on them to build up your barrier breaker bar, and performing a random quick time event to break its shield. Sometimes you have to do this multiple times and its not fun to fight an enemy, do no damage, just so that you can do the same thing a few minutes later again.The game randomly diverts from what its primarily about for sections that feel like an after thought. Example being a random motorcycle on the rails section where you press x ever few seconds to keep moving forward. It last about 30 seconds, is incredibly boring, and feels like its only there because the devs felt like they needed a set piece. Another example being the mini games, one of which being to press the buttons on your controller in a circle at a certain rhythm for 60 seconds... Fun. Lots of random stuff like that where its like "Why is this even here? This could have been a cutscene".Story is really good though and the characters are easy to root for and fall in love with. MC is likable which is pretty rare in games like this and anime appeal strikes pretty hard pretty often. Combat does get varied and fun but it takes a bit for that opening up to happen.Overall if the gameplay videos strike your fancy then yea I recommend this game. Just keep in mind that it is indeed VERY indie feeling with all the jank and questionable design decisions that comes with. Also make sure that when your doing scavenging missions, you use the steam guide that shows where the items are.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game twice already, and enjoyed every minute of it.This is by no means perfect, with combat being mostly good, requiring quite a lot reaction timing to pull off perfect dodges and parrying, and fairly good story line. The highlight of this game are characters you interact with. They did a great job making majority of the characters quite endearing as you work your to way opening them up to you. Sia just happened to be my favorite due to her dynamic personality when it comes to science. I like that they chose a bittersweet ending instead of the typical hero wins flawlessly ending. What I find funny was after the credits rolled, a QR code popped up that you have to scan to see what it is about.The dark setting where people are killed right in front of you rather brutally definitely makes this stand out from typical anime games. This game heavily reminded me of Tokyo Xanadu; pretty much a spiritual successor to that game more than Persona since this is an action combat game, not a turn based combat game. The music though of course does not hold a candle to either Xanadu or Persona, but it is serviceable, with a couple of standout tracks that you hear near the end of the story. There is a time limit to the game so you have to choose your activities wisely each day and night to get the characters' bonds higher.Be sure to talk to the little girl as soon as you are able to. I made the mistake of not doing that for several days, missing out on vital points to character stats.There are 4 characters your protagonist can date, with the option to date multiple people at once, but I am pretty sure there are consequences with that choice, which I am not sure of since I just stuck with one person the whole time.If you are interested in a game that plays like Tokyo Xanadu, then I would highly recommend giving this gem a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest, albeit short experience. It shows that the dev poured a lot of heart into it. The combat is fun, the characters are sweet and the whole atmosphere/art of the game is pleasant. Those that expect only a cheap persona knock-off are in for a surprise. Yes, it can be rough around it's edges but the quality is more than sufficient considering the size of the team. My only real gripe with the game is the ending. It felt cheap, lackluster and disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I was curious about this game ever since the announcement from the State of Play livestream that introduced the game since it reminded me of Persona, and it definitely delivers in that category. So far I didn't find a character that I dislike (but I have my favorites) and I look forward to each dialogue and confident events. Now, for the second part that makes this game Persona-like is the fact that in addition to the social sim, there is also a big part of dungeon crawling. Unlike Persona, the combat system is not turn-based but is rather closer to the one used by Scarlet Nexus (but in a simplified form). It's definitely basic, but it gets the job done, feels great to play and never outstay its welcome.Now on the technical side of things, Eternights manages to run at a locked 60 FPS at 4K on my system (Ryzen 3400G overclocked at 4 GHz / Radeon RX 6750 XT). As a small nitpick, despite its "Steam Deck Certified" status, I needed to use Proton GE to get video playback working on Arch Linux. It's certainly minor but anyone playing on Linux need this as otherwise they will miss a lot from the story. On a completely unrelated note, the game seems to only support Xbox controller prompts, which is sometimes confusing as I play using a DualSense controller.This game is definitely a highlight for me : the story is interesting, the characters are great and the English voice actors did a fantastic job, which is even more impressive when looking back at the history behind Eternights and the fact that it's the first game released by this studio. At €27 (at the time of writing), Eternights is completely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Does this game mix all the genres it is going for perfectly? Not completely.However, it most certainly is still quite a fun game to throw a couple hours at.+Characters are well done, enough to get you emotionally invested in all their stories despite the short time you'll have with them.+And I do think their comedic take on the silent protagonist was a real fun choice, and the story understands when's a good time to have a laugh at its dialogue and when it isn't, so when the story does end up taking a serious turn it still ends up effective at pulling heart strings.+Manage to get some high radar voice actors for this game, who as always have fantastic voice delivery with their works. Plus, a majority of the game's dialogue is voiced with only very minor segments that are not, which is actually fairly rare for games such as these.+For an indie project that was primarily worked on by a single dev, this is all extremely commendable for something this ambitious as the studio's first game.If there were a few cons to point out:-Game is often too dark. Which is a shame cause it does have a pretty color palette, yet in a lot of locations it is quite a struggle to tell in the dark if you're looking at an enemy or your AI partners. [EDIT:] The dev has actually addressed this in a recent update! On replaythrough it felt better, although I'm not sure how much of it is the brightness change and how much is just me getting used to the lighting, so keep that in mind.-In harder difficulties, the attack animations of enemies are sped up. The problem this creates is that the timing to perfect dodges changes with it, to the point where many already quick attacks are now far too difficult to avoid and counter consistently. It definitely should not be as 1:1 as it is now. It also makes one particular instance near the end of the game a bit of a pain to get through on Expert.Overall though, a nice game that is worth checking out, especially to help support this dev for their hard work here. While not incredibly ground breaking, it is fun enough to get me interested in anything else Studio Sai has in mind if something is already in the works.Sia is best girl btw, and that is scientifically accurate!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot I'd like to say about this game, but I'll try to keep it semi-brief.tl;dr, play the demo! At least give the game a try, and then see if you want to buy it. I recommend the game!As for my actual review;First, this game is obviously inspired by the Persona series. If you like Persona, you're probably in the demographic to really enjoy this game. Though the game still has its own distinct identity, and doesn't fall into just being a copy-cat or anything like that.As for the combat, it's not your turn-based affair. The combat is real-time, and quite fun at that. Now, I do have some problems with it that start showing up quickly. The timing on dodging some attacks (and dodging in general) seems...off to me. To the point where parrying feels considerably easier to do consistently. And on the topic of parries, there are some moves you can perfect parry, and you'll still be hit, which feels like utter BS. It was the source of great frustration for a certain boss...As for the dialogue and writing, it... Well, it fluctuates quite a bit. There's some questions that go seemingly unanswered, like how a certain drone lady knows what she does. And no one seems to question her knowledge. Did I miss a cutscene or something? How the hell does she know about the stone and the totem, and why does our train have a device to calculate how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ we are? ??????? Other times, the dialogue is...cringe. And I hate using that word, but it's the only thing I can think of to describe it. The power of friendship gets invoked, but it doesn't feel earned at all, which is why it just feels so cringe. Things are just moving crazy fast with no explanation or build-up, and emotional plot points for characters get resolved with the wave of the writer's pen.All of this might give you the impression that I dislike, or even hate this game.Quite the contrary, actually.I can safely say that I quite love this game, even though it is rough around the edges. It's a diamond in the rough, if you will. That's why, despite some points of contention, I can safely say that I'd recommend the game in a heartbeat to anyone interested. No, it isn't perfect, nor polished to the upmost degree, but the passion behind it shines through it all, and made me fall in love with it.Despite some gripes, I do love the characters, combat, and story that is on display here.I would love to see another game from this developer again, and I hope that, should they wish to continue making games, it all goes right for them. As far as a first release goes, this game has sold me to keep a lookout for any potential future games with quite a bit of excitement.So, in short, buy the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very clearly a labor of love. It is very rough around the edges at times, but in the most endearing way. One moment you'll have beautiful fully animated cutscenes, and the next you'll have rough still sketches in their place, or worse, a black screen with white text telling you what happens. The writing can be hit or miss as well, but I believe some of that comes down to the cultural and linguistic translation. Some story elements were portrayed as VERY dramatic, but seemed perfectly reasonable to me. Thanks to some folks in my chat it was explained that it was a cultural difference. Cool to learn that now but at first it may seem out of place, so keep that in mind as you play through! The sense of humor in the game on the other hand, is top notch. VERY lewd and off the wall, and I had a blast with all of it. The actual gameplay aspects are very fun and diverse! Multiple puzzle types, fun challenges to boost companion relationships, and the combat hits the ground running. While a little repetitive at times it's fast and fluid throughout. All of this together creates a game that was clearly a passion project. Anytime I found something I didn't like about the game it never got in the way of me enjoying my time overall. Would definitely recommend for folks who want a spicier hack and slash adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has many issues - the game is too short, the pacing feels off, the dialogue is often cringy and quite sleazy, the environments have little to differentiate them from each other and the list goes on. But for an indie game, even more so when it's their first attempt, it's actually quite solid. The combat is okay, one thing of note is the enjoyable flashy combos. Also, I enjoyed the soundtrack, even though I am not a big fan of this type of music, so that's an achievement in itself. One thing I particularly enjoyed was the characters. They did make me care about them (except for Sia, all my homies hate Sia.) There's also a very cool detail at the end of the game,  Overall, it's a solid game, I would recommend it if you loved Persona and want a similar experience (we really need more games like it,) but make sure to temper your expectations. It is an indie game after all.Oh, and one more thing - when you reach the end credits... Well, to quote Lux: "Good things come to those who wait." ;)

_childDocuments_.review: The demo didn't impress, but I'm glad the pre-release reviews convinced me to give this another shot.This isn't a hidden gem. It's a VERY flawed jewel, full of chips, cracks, and dirt in it, but ultimately shines through in the spots that matter to me most. Those are the characters, the humor, and the story, which admittedly relies a LOT on your feeling the connection to these characters and liking their personalities.The combat, which is usually my primary decider for any game, is decent enough. It gets repetitive, ranged enemies are a horrendous annoyance, and I really don't like the Elemental Shield system that makes targets immune until you can finally wail on them without mercy once you finish the initial rounds of being forced to engage in smashing them with foam bats and artfully dodging their attacks. I wasn't going into the dungeons to battle monsters, which is strange, and as soon as I got the upgrades that made things so much easier, I used them liberally even if it wasn't the intended way to play.This game has other flaws, as I mentioned. The stealth section is pretty obtuse and frustrating, some gimmick levels like the dance machine is explained too poorly as with the heroine's minigames, and the entire bike sequence was a one and done gimmick that could have been more exciting if it had been played around with more. The puzzles also get points for creativity and diversity but some of these had me pulling out math skills and notepads, they were some pretty frustrating stuff at times. Even the in-world justification of the last dungeon being chock full of puzzles because the CEO is a weirdo doesn't really make me excuse how they break the flow too much between the combat.Still, the important part was that it kept me going, to see what happened next, and I was satisfied with the ending I got with my heroine of choice. This is a game for JRPG enthusiasts, people that don't mind the lack of polish and content like the Persona series, and just want to connect with another group of ragtag found family in a world gone mad.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're considering this game, chances are you're a Persona fan like me, and after finishing this game I could say Eternights has sufficiently scratched that "Persona itch". The social links/confidants have superb voice acting and the characters, while tropey, are still likable.While it's still rough around the edges, particularly in the combat and locations, you can feel the passion and joy the dev put into it. Recommended, especially to Persona fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a while, it's always looked good, but THE FINAL PRODUCT IS JUST GREAT. It's almost unbelievable that the vast majority of the work was done by SINGLE dev. The most important thing is undoubtedly the plot, which is extraordinary, the bonds and romance we create are super emotional. I won't lie, I almost cried at the end. It was very bittersweet, but... then the QR code appeared after the credits... I WAS SO HAPPY TO SEE MY YOHAN AGAIN. Super original and cute idea, breaking the fourth wall, I love it.Deep bows to everyone responsible for the songs, they are beautiful.I'm really happy that the romance option with the boyfriend was included, a great nod to the LGBTQ+ community.You know what would be amazing? For an anime adaptation to be made, the material is extremely solid and we even have a lot of animation design samples as part of the cutscenes.Once again, deep bows to everyone involved in the production, I can't wait for new projects. I wish the studio a lot of success, but also a lot of fun creating them.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the reviews here for "Eternights" are puzzling.  There are criticisms about "Quick Time Events", broken Dodge / Parry systems, repetitive combat and a bad ending.  I don't think any of these criticisms are true.  It makes me wonder if some of the reviewers here actually played the game.  The action combat is robust and dodging / parrying is satisfying and intuitive when you get into the groove of battle.  The breaking barriers part of the battle system is unique in the way the mechanics work and its fun to use the powers of your team mates to break enemy barriers.  There are plenty of combat options available to you so you get out of the combat what you put in.  I found the combat responsive, diverse and satisfying.  The quick time events, that many people are complaining about... are barely even quicktime events at all.  Its only ONE BUTTON and the events are slow enough that its a walk in the park.  Its simply a cool mechanic for breaking barriers and once you've done one - they're all the same.  I don't get the complaint.  It works well and adds excitement to the mix of combat mechanics.  Also the difficulty was just right.  I really enjoyed this part of the game.The story is fine and the characters are well drawn.  Its a bit sloggy when you're out of combat but raising your stats and putting points into your build based on your social relationships is cool so its worth it.  The ending, I thought, was great.  A lot of the writing is well done  and I really enjoyed playing through the game.  The game was made by a small team and it shows when out of combat.  The scenes are janky and the story telling and edits are a bit jarring.  It didn't bother me, but you'll notice it.  The social loop, in my opinion. was the weak part of the game as days can drag on and on while you're doing the same things over and over again just to get the the next combat section.  The game ran wonderfully for me and the art design is fabulous.  The washed out, dreamy look of the game really kept me immersed in the world.  the music is okay, nothing to write home about but not bad either.  Recommended if you're looking for solid action based combat game in an anime / social relationship world which is not too long, neither is it too short.  A very nice palette cleanser of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: While rough around the edges and falling short of a more satisfying implementation of the ambitious directions that it tried to take its gameplay mechanics, Eternights has an unmistakable charm that makes it shine despite its short-comings.The endearing personalities, the tongue-in-cheek lewd humor, and the ridiculous situations they find themselves in only left me wanting more; I quite enjoyed my time with the characters and even scavenging for miscellaneous items with them felt emotionally rewarding.The combat was fun and challenging enough (on expert), executing combos felt smooth for the most part and the special attack system was entertaining to use.Definitely worth the price for me. I'd love to see an Eternights 2 some day that builds on what it already has going for it here.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never wanted an actual "percentage rating" system more for a game than for this review of Eternights. I'm definitely giving it a thumbs up/recommendation, but it definitely has issues that should be addressed.I'll start with something important, so that if anyone reading stops, they at least see this: according to the credits, there were basically 2 people that worked on programming/technical stuff. There was a third that did story related stuff, and then other roles like VAs and I imagine they outsourced the anime cutscenes, but at least according to the credits - 2 people. Any criticism I give has to be tempered with the fact that 2 people did the vast majority of the work. No matter what else I say, this game is *very* good when you consider it through the lens of the size of the team working on it.Pros:* Persona Lite. If you like Persona, you might enjoy this (or, it might frustrate you that Persona just does it better)* A story with a strong anime/romance feel. If you particularly like anime with a romantic theme or sub-theme, the story hits most of the right beats.* Combat is interesting enough.* Characters are likeable.* CGs and cutscenes are freaking gorgeous.Cons (again, primarily a 2 person team, so consider that):* Short. I got it for about $40 AUD, and I know it had no chance of being a behemoth of duration like Persona (or many other AAA titles these days), but even besides actually being short, the pacing is a bit off. You get through a few acts and it feels like things are ramping up - and you're suddenly at the extreme tail of the game.* The human models are just a bit rough. It's made more frustrating because the CG and cutscene representations are absolutely beautiful. Seeing the characters in game versus seeing their menu pictures is just disappointing.* While combat is interesting enough, it does also get a bit tedious at times.* There's a story beat that happens at the start of the final act, that honestly asks you to suspend your disbelief a lot. It actually feels lazy; there were logical ways to get the character into the position they wanted them to be in, but they went with one that required them to act in a way that you couldn't imagine someone acting in.Ultimately, I definitely have to recommend picking up the game. The few devs have shown a lot of promise with this one. If they can get more resources (people and money) for another Persona-like game and smooth out some of the issues they had with this one, I think they could legit make a game that's worthy of a 90% rating (I'd give this about 75-80%). In order to encourage that future progress - get behind them and give this one a go!

_childDocuments_.review: I guess this is more of a rave than a review.  Honestly, this is one of my very favorite games overall, and it's 100% because of how the game tugs at your heartstrings :). It doesn't have the best combat in the world, but it's certainly not bad, and the dungeon sections do a good job of integrating the combat systems into the game's mechanics.Games with fantastic combat, great stories, and exciting gameplay are extremely rare, but even with combat not being one of my favorite parts, this game has definitely found a place in my heart.  Not only does the game boast an incredible story, but the constantly developing mood/atmosphere and voice acting (Yuna and Chani were my favs) are some of the best.   Also, the fact that it was created by such a small team is just incredible, and I cannot wait for their next project!!  This game is a steal right now at 20 bucks, and to all of the Persona fans out there, this is an absolute must buy. Even if real time combat isn't your thing, I think most people can put the game on easy mode and figure out the combat system after 30 minutes or so.  I promise you won't regret the time spent!  I believe I'm about 30% of the way through at 4 hours, so I expect the game to take 12 hours or so total (I'm definitely taking my time though, as I don't want it to end!).  The game is also really well optimized, so I'm confident it'll perform well on a wide range of systems.CHEERS and Happy Holidays :)H

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely ever leave reviews, this game made me want to.This is a fantastic game. This is the concept of a game I've dreamed about since I first played Persona; a hack and slash, calender rpg dating sim, and I loved it to pieces. It blows my mind that a game this good was not only made by a small team, but that it's also their first game. It's a relatively simple hack and slash, but it's flashy so it doesn't get old. (at least for me) The active skills the companions give you add just the right amount of depth, especially if you play it on the hardest difficulty. Only wish for two things; the maps to be a bit less empty, but there's enough and you can move through them fast enough that it isn't really a big deal, and more difficult enemy AI. I couldn't care less about graphics, but I know some people do so; They're fine, good in some aspects. The character models and animations are all pretty great, save for a few odd moments that pass quickly. The monster models are all also pretty great, but they have pretty simple animations. Even the bosses do, but they also make up for it by each of them having a few flashy attacks.What really put this game above and beyond is the characters and dialogue. This game is funny as hell, and it also handles the more serious moments really well. The character's all shine, and it helps that the voice acting is stellar. I really could say a ton more about them and the writing, but I honestly just think you should buy the game. It's a steal for $30, so if you're even thinking about it, get it dude.8.5/10, it's just peak.Will likely bump it higher after I do all the other routes. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: From the demo, this game seemed really simple: A slice of life game with some combat thrown in. What I did not expect was one of my favorite games that I have played in the past year. The game has two different facets, each reminding me of different games. The confidant/social aspect of the game reminds me of the Persona series. You have to have a certain level of each stat to advance to the next rank, unlocking new abilities ranging from health up to new power ups.On the other hand, the combat reminds me of a Dark Souls like game, with the ability to roll, limited healing, and chaining combos. The "palaces" (the persona brain in me wants to call them that) are the same throughout every play through, so the secrets and puzzles will get easier.On top of all of this, the story is amazing. The ending of the game (which I will not spoil) is so bittersweet and I teared up.All in all, this game is one of my new favorites, and I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review: A captivating, emotionally charged story with satisfying combat, held back only by tons of  inexplicable menu bugs.Long Review:Eternights is a mix of daily life game, dating game, and "souls-may-cry" spectacle fighting. The art and animation is SPECTACULAR and the gameplay is really good. The fighting is all about paying attention and timing your actions (and reactions) to the queues, and how you respond to other characters changes your own characterization which affects your relationships (and your therefore your companions skills). I have absolutely nothing negative to say about the gameplay itself, it soooo good. If you like the Persona series, From Software games, and DMC/Bayonetta games... I guarantee you will like this too.But let's get one thing clear, this is a bad PC port. There are no performance or stability problems per se, but the game menus/settings are not only bare-bones, but LOADED with bugs... like an intern threw together the extra PC UI in an hour or two and never bothered to QA any of it. There are bits that are untranslated, some of the game's resolutions are mislabelled (more on that in a second), and some of the game's buttons are reversed (like Cancel and Continue both doing the opposite). Sometimes the games menu options simply do nothing - like "Exit to Main Menu". Whoops.Back to resolutions: The game doesn't support 32:9 ultrawide resolutions natively (like 5120x1440) - in fact, it only supports 6 hard-coded resolutions TOTAL - so I decompiled one of the game files to see if I could mod it in. While I did figure out how to add support for 32:9 (details are in the game's Steam Discussion forum) I also confirmed the resolution mixup is a basic programming bug due to the sloppy way the developer implemented user-selectable resolutions. For example: If you are trying to play at 3440x1440 (21:9) and the game looks awful, it's because the game is ACTUALLY rendering at 2560x1080, because the labels for those resolutions in the UI are reversed. If you select 2560x1080, the game will actually try to render in 3440x1440, which could result in being unable to play at all. Yikes. 🤦🏽‍♂️Someone could easily fix the menu issues (AND add proper 32:9 support) in about an hour, if so inclined. Really, there is no excuse for shipping the game in this state given how basic these bugs are. Cleaning up the menus and making sure the buttons actually WORK and do what they say... maybe a couple more. That's how close this game is to being a technically solid PC port. So. Close.So - I just spent a lot of time complaining about this because I want the developer to see this and fix it. Heck, I could even do it for them if they want. This is a really great game - genuinely - and it deserves more care and polish than this.It's still a recommend for me - but the settings and UI bugs in mind, especially if you plan on playing on an ultrawide monitor. Once you work around those, there's a great game waiting for you.

_childDocuments_.review: ++ Great characters++ Very good music+ Fun combat+ Nice SoL and romance segments+ Fun puzzles and minigames+ Beautiful CGs and Drawings+ Interesting story* At times rough looking in-game models* Sound cuts off between transitions* Last level can be pretty hard without Yuna-- Unsatisfying ending(s)- Some crashesThis game is a budget Persona, which is a lot of fun to play and has an interesting story and great characters.Everything gets elevated through the nice artstyle and good music, while puzzles and minigames switch up the gameplay a bit. The in-game models look pretty rough at times, additionally the sound cuts out suddenly during scene transitions, instead of fading out which breaks the immersion a bit. The last level can be frustrating without Yuna/healing, as the game sends a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of enemies your way, luckily your Ultimate instakills the harder enemies too.My biggest gripe with the game overall is with the endings: I can excuse the technical hiccups as this game is made by only one person, but the ending being this bad puts a damper on the final stretches of the game. I still had a lot of fun with the great characters, and overall I would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.Is it perfect? No. Combat can be a bit janky (sometimes you'll get stunlocked for a few hits and you're dead without being able to do anything), character models look a bit flat, and the graphics in most areas are fairly simple.However, it's . The game itself isn't super long, but I enjoyed nearly all of the characters and when you get the grasp of perfect dodging, combat feels great. The QTEs are generous in regards to timing, there's some great moments and jokes in the story, the voice acting is well done, and if you're worried about the time limits - don't be. You only need one trip to the dungeon to clear it, and even with the three difficulty levels, the checkpoints are incredibly generous and you get healed each time so it's never required to abandon your journey partway to heal or recharge.In terms of romance - things felt a little accelerated with how each one develops, but you also get moments with the characters in the main story and not just in the personal time sections. You're gender locked to a guy, and there are three girls and one boy you can date if you so choose (you are able to turn them down if you want without losing out on any unlocks). Alas, from what I can tell, there is no harem ending - there's no downside to entering into a relationship with as many of them as you want, but you're forced to pick only one for the ending.Overall, this definitely put the devs on my radar and I'll be looking forward to future games by them!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRThe price is cringe, but on sale the game is worth it.This game is a perfect example of forgivable bad aspects. The graphics are bad. It honestly looks like a bunch of free assets hastily animated by hand in facerig of someething. So the one thing you expect for the full price isn't there. On the other hand the 2d scences look amazing. A nice breath of fresh air among the poor 3d.The game is straight up stealing the concept from presona, and it is great. Because the main aspect of this copncept is good character design and writing. Yes, you only get five of them, but they are solid. Maybe a little too cringe at times but really solid. And they are unique. The actual social gameplay lacks a lot of tutorial and pushes you to go though it with true and tried trial and error method and for a fresh playthrough it is a bit frustrating (especially when you miss some milestone you want by a few inches because of lack of understanding of the systems). And yet it felt good enough regardless. The combat is wierd. It has a broken rhytm to it and the fluidity just isn't there. But once you accept it and learn some advanced things it gets easier. You definitely need some upgrades to get comfortable with it but isn't it the main point of upgrade systems anyway?The story is good. Not too good, with a few questionable aspects, but still good. The final chapter feels a bit raw and rushed. I'd even suggest cutting it out of the story and going straight to epilogue... But it's there and it is somewhat acceptable.So, 3/10 for graphics (and 2d scenes are literally 12/10), 6/10 for gameplay, 7/10 for story and 9/10 for characters for a 7/10 overall. The only question is the price. Like literally why? It is Unity and the graphics are bad... IDK

_childDocuments_.review: Alright after finishing a single playthrough in ~11 hours; BLUF: An impressive debut title from a studio that consists of 1 full time guy and like 8 part-timers - This is important to keep in mind if you read any reviews. - If you like Persona-esque social links, and are okay with some very basic action rpg gameplay, then you might enjoy this game! The story isn't mind blowing, but the character interactions are charming and had me emotional by the end of the game despite any faults I had with the action elements. There are also a couple of times where animation choice, or boss design, made me laugh or scratch my head when it probably wasn't supposed to. Still, at the launch price ($27) it's an alright time for someone with a mushy spot in their heart for character interaction - like me! If you aren't sure, wait for a sale. Long version:- Action gameplay is very basic, featuring a single real combo and perfect dodge/parry mechanics. Rock-paper-scissors style barrier elemental weaknesses force you to change up what elemental support you use or you're gonna bash your head against a nearly impenetrable wall for a long as hell time. - The overall plot of the story is okay. You kind of get thrown into things, it gets semi-explained as you go, and the conclusion is - for me at least - unexpected but doesn't offer any great explanation of things. This is okay, as having a little bit of room for open interpretation and discussion isn't a bad thing. - The game really shines in the inter-character dialogues and situations, most notably between you (the player's character) and whichever individual you are presently Spending Time with. Characters came across as believable, nuanced in motivations/hangups/etc, and there's plenty of stuff to tug at your heart strings. It is very much in the style, if not in the exact execution, of Persona Social Links - spend time with your party members to improve the stat buffs and abilities they provide, learn more about them, and decide to romance them or not. [Similar to Persona games, you will not be able to date/reciprocate feelings for a character until roughly 3/4 of the way through the game - and you need to meet certain stat requirements to do it.] Some of these interactions/elicited emotions are better than others, some are a little trope-y and might not be your speed. Still, the writing comes across as heartfelt and I truly appreciate it for what it is. - The ending itself got me crying in the club - quite literally crying - likely because of how well I resonated with the characters (I am intentionally avoiding spoilers, IYKYK). Props to the devs for the final gameplay mechanic. Not many games have the guts to force you, the player, to really let go.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made feel enough to want to write a review of it and I think that testifies that something here is working. Eternights is a raw, but cool action rpg with Souls-lite dodge rolls/parries and Persona-lite confidante/calendar system. The best way I could describe this game is "flawed, but pretty good." For those who like Persona/anime humor and aren't particular about hack-n-slash gameplay, this game is a solid pick up. Its also a decent option for anyone who liked Akiba's Trip or Tokyo Xanadu. Pros: -Best use of a hold hands button in a video game.-It manages to capture some of the good parts to Persona's writing/mechanics, including investing in characters all tied to a central theme.-When the combat is good, its very fun. -Having the party members to the side and supporting you with spells is way better to me than the character swap model in a lot of other action rpgs with focus on a party. It matches the power fantasy and fighting with friends ideas really well. -Characters have something more to them that make them a bit better than the tropes they pull from and I found myself invested in most of them. -All love interests are at least fun and there will be very likely something for someone. Sticking with four options was a smart choice for the scope of this game.-The game didn't overstay its welcome. There were a few sections that felt little bit padded out, but nothing egregious. -The comedic timing is great. When a joke lands and, especially when they give you a funny option, it really lands.-The visual novel scenes with slight blink animations and lighting are superb. Man, I hope the sequel does more of those, because it really drives home the scene or appeal of the characters.  With some parallax when appropriate, the sequel's visuals could be very dangerous.-The character models are really expressive and well timed. -The enemy designs are really good. -The game doesn't take itself too seriously and that makes the rougher edges of some of the writing easier to forgive. Its genuinely a fun ride.Cons:-Camera behavior is not conducive to some of the fights and levels. The camera isn't good enough to handle fights with multiple enemies in tight spaces or when being cluttered with enemies with erratic movements. The camera will jerk an enemy off screen or the lock-on will not work how you expect it too. There are specific leaping enemies, the hospital area, and the final fight were the most noticeable for me. It felt like I took more hits from the camera making it impossible to see a projectile more than anything else. They really needed the camera to dip behind the walls and those walls become transparent or just have most fights in wider arenas with only single enemies in hallways. This will put some people off. If it helps some other players, for certain situations in corners and certain erratic enemies I just turned the lock on off after isolating them and normally tried to kill projectile enemies first so I would take less annoying hits. Also needing to lock-on again for each phase of a boss, end up being annoying at times.-Stun-locking. Its a terrible mechanic just in any action game. There are a lot of lightning attacks where you have to mash x to get out of and many situations where you get hit 3 or 4 times being juggled between different enemies. It doesn't add difficulty or interesting decisions; just punishment for punishment's sake. You can still perfect dodge to get out of some of these situations (some), so its not like you do absolutely nothing, but it still feels really bad. I genuinely hope they get rid of that idea in the sequel and maybe consider a teching/tech roll mechanic. For a certain boss and situations with a lot of enemies chaining AOE's together, Min's ability helps mitigate the frustration a little bit. -There is definitely some "for boys" juvenile humor and the writing plays into some very normal "anime power fantasy" tropes that aren't always the best toward female characters. For a certain niches, this is intentional nostalgia and will come across as funny. For others, this will make them bounce off the game and will feel alienated by it. That is a shame, because the game does have some really funny moments in it that are still a bit immature, but in a way appropriate for general audiences and one ups the Persona series, by at least having a male romance option.-Missed visual opportunities. In Rank 6 for most characters, there are blank screens that feel like there was originally a plan to have key visuals there. And one or two of those beautiful art scenes with slight animation would have really sold those moments far more. While the models are good, they look worse when zoomed in on the dialogue boxes and the character portraits would have been just the better choice for those.-Yohan, MC, and Sia need more time and love in the writing department. For context, I maxed out most characters, but watched videos of what I couldn't do on my first playthrough. Yohan felt like he had just barely enough screen time to pull off what was needed for him, but his main thing to overcome felt rushed at the very end of his confidante and the romance felt less compelling than the others as a result. Sia referenced her issues more than we actually see her suffer through them and that's a shame because the theme of her confidante is a pretty good one. Also her character gag (chunibyo proclamations) could have been shown three or four times rather than a dozen to make her the more grounded character her dungeon makes her out to be. MC's ending contradicts the main theme a bit, because we don't see him really move forward as the other characters do and I do think it hurts the overall package a little bit.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and interesting mesh of genre. Very cool art style, if a little stiff in the animation department, especially outside of combat--which itself has a decent flow, but becomes a bit tired, as it boils down to swing, swing, swing, finisher, repeat, with the occasional perfect or imperfect dodge or parry, followed by the elemental attacks which are quick time events, which stall flow in my opinion, but are nevertheless entertaining as they have really good sound design and effects, but I digress.But honestly beyond all that, I really enjoyed having a dating sim style game that wasn't just a visual novel. Having other elements to the game with combat, voice acting and exploration makes for a much more interactive experience, and makes me want to play significantly more of it, or anything like it (I really wish there was more like this!). Plus, I'm a sucker for romance stories, what can I say?Now I went through a few of my baseline qualms in the opening paragraph, but in the interest of voicing my opinion on some areas where I think there could be some improvement (should the developer give this style of game another go, and I hope so); I wish there was more voice acting, which is a testament to the quality of the cast (English cast, for what I played anyway). As having sections of dialogue where a character's VA says a throw away one word line, and then the actual dialogue is text only is a bit off-putting and disappointing, even if it's not crucial; and maybe that's for economic reasons, I don't know, just putting it out there. Otherwise, I'd just like a little more out of the combat, a few more animations, a little more dynamic, and a few less QTEs.But honestly, I really really enjoyed the game, and I still plan on playing more of it, getting some more endings and the like. And I would absolutely love to see more of it, whether that be in the form of a sequel, or simply anything in the same realm as this game. Damn lot of fun, and very emotional; clearly a lot of vision and soul behind this title and I look forward to seeing what more this developer can do going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game, you play as an ordinary guy who needs to save the world because you were chosen. But saving the world isn’t something you can do alone; you will have a team and spend a lot of time with them. It’s not a story with groundbreaking or profound thoughts, rather, it’s a common tale about . Each member of your team will have a unique personality with their own problems but be ready for some “dirty” jokes. The twist at the ending is super cool, and not many authors are willing to take such risks. However, it would have been even better if .The voice acting is good (I played with Japanese voices). The 2D art is awesome. There aren’t a lot of them, but the ones present are well-drawn and impressive. The characters are designed with caricatures, which is okay and sometimes funny, especially their emotions. The monster design is unique and well-executed, I haven’t seen anything similar. However, there could have been more variety in the types of monsters. Each act has a unique location, but they feel somewhat common and similar, just okay. In a few locations, there are puzzles, but they are easy to solve, and the game provides helpful hints if you get stuck (at least in the 4th act). The battle gameplay might be disappointing if you’re looking for an interesting fight. There aren’t a lot of combos and abilities, they are all quite common. There are only three global types of enemies, and in the end, you will be fighting the same enemies repeatedly. However, since the game is short, you won’t get tired of it. Additionally, there are a lot of quick time button presses, which you’ll need to defeat some enemies. So be ready for this.I recommend this game if you prefer story/character-driven games where you spend a lot of time with companions, and gameplay isn't a priority for you. Otherwise, I would suggest waiting for a sale or skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: Put simply, if you are into the idea of "10 to 12-hour mini-persona with action gameplay", then you'll probably like the game as I did. I'd like to start this review off by saying there's a lot of typical anime stuff that you'd expect. This game isn't exempt from that. If you're someone who's always found anime cliches infuriating, I would just stop now and save yourself the time and effort of looking into this game.Going into this game, I really wasn't sure what to expect. The first thing I noticed was the.. Strange... 3D models. They definitely took some adjusting to, and I can imagine some people would not be able to get past them. The characters in the bottom-left corner can range from looking alright to kinda laughable. This stays throughout the game - if you can absolutely not tolerate the 3D animation in the trailers (like a few of my friends couldn't), you should probably give this game a pass.However, if you like the idea of a game like persona with more focus on the dating sim part, some action gameplay, and some likable characters, I can definitely recommend it. Obviously, it has some very glaring flaws that stand out a lot - but despite that, I definitely enjoyed my time with the game.The main appeal of this game to me was the characters. While they weren't the best written characters on earth, I still liked them and enjoyed watching them grow throughout both the game and their social links. Obviously, since this game is only 10 hours long, they won't be nearly as fleshed out as characters from series like Persona, but for the length of the game, I'd say they do a good job, even if they feel tropey at times. The voice acting is great in both English and Japanese and adds to the characters even further. At first, the story seemed a little strange and taped together to me, but as it continued, I started to get into it enough. Some people will probably think it's a little too ridiculous, which is fine. It was enough to keep me engaged with the game throughout it, and there were some interesting parts in it to me. The definite highlight of it all was the final act - one full of emotion with an ending I'll remember. I didn't expect the ending, but I'm sure you can gather how I felt if you read a few other reviews.The combat was mostly really fun to me, but there were times it was more than a little painful. If you don't like quick-time events, you'd better get used to them, because I probably did over 500 throughout my playthrough of this game. I didn't mind them too much as they weren't hard or anything, but I was not having the time of my life repeating the same four events. The final boss fight stuck out to me as strange, because it didn't really feel like a final boss fight... it felt a little BS at points, but I honestly thought there would be more after it.Overall, despite its obvious flaws, this game was fun for me, and I might come back to it sometime to 100% it. It is DEFINITELY not for everyone - you should hopefully be able to tell if you'd like it or not just based on the reviews and trailers. It's janky at times, it can be a little ugly, and sometimes it can be a little frustrating, but overall? I somehow ended up enjoying this game, and I hope that if you pick it up, you will too.Finally, Yuna is the best, and I will not be accepting any other opinions. (By the way - if you're playing through the game, have your phone or something that can scan QR codes ready at the end! Trust me!)

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights' development has been great to follow. It doesn't necessarily bring a storyline that hasn't been seen before, original plot development or art direction that breaks new ground, but surprisingly, it brings it together in a combination that hasn't really been seen before. It's like a feverdream combination of Left4Dead and Persona. But it doesn't deserve "Very Positive" for a 30 Euro game. But it could.Eternights' combat system relies on queues to counter enemy attacks and enter a high-damage slowed-time period. The enemy's eyes flash, you hit the right button, automatically evading their attack and giving yourself opportune time to counter. This is maybe the best way of translating why Eternights doesn't deserve a "Very Positive" rating, but COULD deserve one; a number of the enemies don't have the same behaviour, but instead rely on proximity of the attack - the equivalent to a spitter from Left4Dead is an example - where it's not the enemy's attack timing but rather the proximity of their launched attack towards you that you have to time. This isn't explained in the game. And for some enemies, the timing of flashing eyes or other visual queues for the counter mechanic (which you will entirely rely on to combat any enemy) are entirely mistimed. In some enemies' instances, their eyes will flash simultaneously or even a frame after their hits land. This entirely defeats the purpose of the visual queue mechanic and simply leaves you recognizing the attack patterns of the enemy and deducting yourself when to counter to engage the slow-time high-damage period. In one of Joseph Anderson's analyses a few years ago, Anderson talks about how some games supposedly raise themselves above criticism exclusively from their difficulty, and how ridiculous that sense of thought is; i could beat the game, you couldn't, therefore you don't have room to complain. Eternights is my first game in which I've seen this first-hand. The easiest difficulty of this game is unbearable for someone who's 100%d other games on their normal or expert difficulties. Not in small part due to the complete inconsistency of the single most central combat mechanic, not to mention it being entirely mistimed with certain enemies and missing from others on top of that. A game being difficult enough to warrant dying 100 times to get past its first half Dark Souls-style does not warrant it being above criticism, somehow. Making a balanced experience for any player base regardless of skills or backgrounds in the area is central to adoption, an area critical to this first-time developer.And what to say about the developer. His work and enthusiasm is fantastic. And in many ways, many of these flaws should be relevant to larger studios that failed a QA process or didn't provide enough time to squash bugs or manipulate difficulties or combat mechanics internally before release. The fact that this project is largely run by a guy doing it for the passion's sake is incredible, and a true success story.But a 30 Euro PlayStation-grade next-to-Final-Fantasy game it's not. It could be, though. I've received my refund for now, but should Eternights ever get to a point in which combat difficulty across difficulty settings and very central, basic combat mechanics - on which the player relies ENTIRELY - get smoothed out, I'd happily pay full triple-A price.I wish Studio Sai the absolute best in endeavours and hope this can become the beginning entry in a series rather than a one-off. "Very Positive" is a ridiculous rating in its current state, however.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I know this is more than I could expect for an indie title... The action part is okay, and the galgame part is fair.50% of the thumbs-down come from the poor music and sfx. All Yuna's character voice and story lead to such a poorly-mixed, simple soundtrack, and I just can't take it. The cutscenes before the bossfight are almost always weak and are badly trimmed to cut off earlier than I expected. Some bossfights use orchestral instrumentation, but it is the epic feeling that makes emotion burst when using the trick - you need large reverb or complex mixing to achieve the effect, and when you cannot, choose a rock style sound might be a much better choice. The ending track was also a large minus - poorly mixed, weak instrumentation. I am sorry to be a bit cruel to an indie team, but the audio part of the game definitely could be much better.The other 50% comes from the main plot. I really cannot say much without spoiling the story, but I really do not like the last part of the story. There are lots of unexplained things, and many cue events and twists happen just because... they happened. Why did the meter rise at last? What is the glow boy and why it shows up with Umbra? If it were not for the last part of the story I could give a thumbs-up for the game for its pure yet lovable story, but the last part does not make me cry - it simply makes me mad.I feel really sorry for not loving the game. I think the game could be far much better than it is now, but I do believe the devs can craft better games in the future, and I am still willing to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights has an enticing idea behind it, unfortunately its held back by major issues. First let's talk about the worse aspect, which are technical issues. There are horrible performance issues with FPS drops, and since this is a heavily QTE based game, sometimes it means you'll lose some of the QTE due to frame drops. This problem is further exacerbated when some of the enemies require a successful QTE sequence to be able to be defeated. So, this means that you'll constantly be moving around the arena and baiting the enemy to an area where there are less frame drops just enough so you can try to succeed the QTEs.Fortunately, the game does let you shift between difficulty settings on the fly, so if the frame drops get too bad, you can lower to easy so you can get more QTE tries. The combat itself is mostly fine despite the jankyness, there are enough mechanics to make it more or less fun, depending on how high you set your bar. The animations are actually a bit lacking in quality and it's janky enough to affect your ability to play sometimes, so you'd think that, as far as dating games go, this would be on the higher end of the spectrum, assuming that the focus is on the dating aspect, and that the action aspect is secondary, but unfortunately, thats not the case here.The romance options are not that great. I can feel the devs took their time to try and make these characters as likable as the could, unfortunately they are all very anime tropey, and most of them one dimensional except for Yuna who gets a bit more development. The game doesn't require you to actually date any of the characters, which is an odd choice for a game like this, it only requires you to "bond" with them. So dating them only gives you access to a bit more content, but the story itself plays out the same, which is woefully disappointing.I am very dissatisfied with the lack of possible endings for this game. The endings are short and don't change much at all regardless of your smaller choices. Most players will feel massively disappointed by the lack of agency it provides. It feels like the "dating" aspect of this game is not actually front and center, its just a side content. Whether you date anyone doesn't actually affect the ending beyond just bonding with them, and when you do bond, only a small part of the ending is affected. The game itself was just supposed to be a melodramatic action game, with dating on the side. So how does it fare strictly as an action game ? Poorly. The quality is average at best and subpar most of the time. Factor in the technical issues, and the game is just straight up bad.The only redeemable qualities in the game is some of the humor, which they got right, and the overall atmosphere of the game, which reminds me of those 80's trash zombie B movie flicks, which is a whole genre that I am a fan of. Unfortunately the lack of CG art in the game, which is too few and far between from what you'd expect from a dating game, and the missed opportunity to add some more violence into the mix, also was a big disappointment. The whole thing wants to feel like a Raimi movie, but it just turned out to be just another anime highschool tropey drama.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give a thumbs down on the game, because there is/was so much potential here.  Unfortunately, it feels like too much was focused in one direction vs. a more diverse game.In this, something's happened to the people around you where, after bunkering up for a bit, you emerge to find everyone turned into some kind of zombie.  There are clear inspirations from games like Persona, Zanki Zero and Etrian Odyssey.- English dub is always a good thing and while it's not always the best, I'd rather have it than not, especially since the game isn't that expensive (thus debunking the narrative that English dub is "too expensive" - it's not really)- There's a generally intriguing story under the hood here.- Fairly accessible, controls aren't blatantly offensive where it feels like they're trying to make sure every button is made use of- If you're a fan of dungeon crawlers then this game is likely right up your alley; but that's not the kind of game I wanted or expected.- no towns, no armor, no weapons, no real leveling, no real traditional RPG mechanics despite being marketed as a role-playing game.- Every dungeon is basically a straight linear corridor with fight segments - very similar to Crisis Core:Final Fantasy VII, actually.- The relationship aspects feel tacked on and not very engaging.- Absolutely NOT a fan of the "dark void" - this is for Yuma, and it's even worse in this game because some of the enemies you fight there is no such, which adds the question as to why it made sense to do it on this one character.- Early on, a character gets killed in cold blood right in front of you; but not only is it too soon for you to feel any emotional attachment, your party doesn't really react with the level of energy you'd expect them to.- Those sensitive to motion sickness might consider skipping.  In my case it took form of a splitting headache when playing on a regular monitor (didn't happen when playing handheld, which is odd).  I didn't "hate" the game, but it just feels too light, too simple.  There just wasn't enough here to really keep my attention.  Which is unfortunate because again, this looks like it really could have been something special.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to give this game a chance. Played a couple hours, and after that, every time i launched the game, i played no more than one battle before closing it because of how clunky it felt.I admit that for a one-man team game (mostly), Eternights is pretty impressive. Great atmosphere and some cool visual ideas. Nice music and voice acting. Good job on the creator for their efforts. Pulling such a game by yourself in a few years is neat.Aside from that, i just can't get myself to like the game. Combat has no in between, either it's uncomfortable to play, or the invincibility from the dodge mechanic make it boring and bland.I won't comment the story itself since i didn't finish it, but storytelling is rushed and awkward as hell.Characters are cringe and bland at best (Chani might be one of the worst starting companion i ever saw in a rpg. Dude goes from porn jokes to incel to nohomobro to "i resent you because you have cool power to show off and i don't" in less than 30mn of gameplay)The dialogues consist only of exposition, ecchi jokes and all the most boring overused anime clichés you can think of.The way the faces and expressions are animated looks super weird and cartoony, it throws me off so bad. I feel like motionless faces or 2d sprites would have been way better.I was pleasantly surprised that the game seemed to include a gay romance but if you're there for it, i have the feeling it was put there as an afterthought. Because from the few context and UI clues i got, it seems like it has way less options than the other romances available. I could be wrong tho.I think all the people praising this game as being a cool persona slash soulborne inspired game never played either of those past the tutorial/starting zones.tldr: it doesn't feel like it's worth the 30$ price tag imo and i regret paying full price for it. If you want an actual good action jrpg anime game in a modern/futuristic setting with some social aspect, you should invest 20 bucks more to go play Scarlet Nexus instead. (or get it during sales, it's worth it) Yeah, it's probably unfair to compare a big company game with a one-man indie, but trust me, you'll have a better time and your money will be better spend.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro tip to the developers: maybe make sure there aren't any major bugs in your game before charging people 30 bucks for it? Just a few hours into the game and already there's several huge issues that ruin the experience, including the screen randomly turning black during pre-rendered cutscenes. There also just a huge lack of polish all around.That aside... the game itself is just okay. The voice acting is mostly good, and the writing is serviceable. Cliche anime tropes are littered throughout so if that's not your thing, definitely look elsewhere. The UI and art style in general is very generic and lacks any sense of style, which is funny because the game is supposedly inspired by the Persona franchise - a series absolutely oozing with style and charm. The combat is honestly quite repetitive and boring, just spam the same move, break the shield, dodge, rinse and repeat.I think the biggest problem with Eternights, though, is definitely the pacing. Everything feels incredibly rushed from the get go. There's extremely little time for the characters or the player to breathe and comprehend what is actually happening and how things have changed. This is one of those games with a premise and tone that definitely calls for at least double the length of its approximately 15 hour runtime.Overall, I'd wait until all the bugs get ironed out before even considering trying this game. But even then, there's not a ton here to like unless you really need something to scratch that Persona-style social sim itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Hm. What to say that hasn't been said? This lightweight hack and slash is simple yet has charm enough for days. I found myself smiling a lot as I watched and interacted with the characters. The combat and puzzles were simple enough to grasp and challenging enough to make it a...fun challenge, even on easy (exception: the motorcycle sequence. That was stupidly hard). Especially for someone like me who is not a twitch gamer. Hardcore Souls players will likely find it pretty easy. I found the art style used its simplistic graphics very well to create an atmosphere; character models had just enough to give personality. Really, I can't say enough about how good the visuals were despite being pretty low poly. Finally, enjoyed the voice acting a lot. Whoever played Chani deserves a medal. Annoying, endearing, funny, sad...really impressed.Cons would be that it is short, and the characters, while endearing, are pretty basic. You're on rails the whole way, some folks might not like that. Also "easy mode" isn't all *that* easy. The motorcycle sequence is in dire need of nerfing. The devs could have made the love interests a *little* harder to romance, lol.Anyway, I liked it. Def worth picking up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very impressive coming from a small developer and worth the price point (approx. 15 dollars). The combat system is on mostly on par with top games in the genre, often better than some AAA titles (FF XVI).However there are some strange design choices which left me disappointed:The silent, goofy-looking everyman protagonist renders the narrative inert from the beginning. Almost as bad; it is  tropey. Every character is more predictable than the last. From a screenshot of a character, JRPG fans could probably guess who does some of the voices (who are indeed good VAs). In short, if you played a Persona game, then you already know this story.Whilst fighting mobs is fun, tougher enemies and boss fights require extensive QTEs, and they are generally quite tanky. Together, it makes a significant proportion of fights near unbearable.The design aesthetic wears quickly. While opening environments are very interesting, it soon becomes apparent that every environment you move through looks the same.More needed to be done to distinguish Eternights from others in its niche, but it's a bright start and I'm excited to see what the dev does next.

_childDocuments_.review: i've heard people saying this is like Persona and this is like Dark Souls. on face value and paper, there is truth to this, but that's about all there is. i've also heard that this was developed by on person for the majority, and while that alone is impressive, it's not the first case of a game being developed like that, so i'm not gonna give much pity just because it may be a one man show.there is a question regardless of game or book or movie or show, that if it can't be answered, everything falls apart. "So what?"two guys use a dating app to pick up chicks. so what? the world comes to an end. so what? this character died. so what? you're chosen to be the big hero. so what? this character has a strange power. so what?this game did a poor job of making me understand why i should care about anything or anyone outside of saying "this is good" or "this is bad". it could of benefitted from showing a scene or two of what these characters were up to before the start of the game, so that way getting to caring about them would of been easier.the dialogue around the characters, especially in regards to being around girls is just nothing but cringe. and it's not even a sort of cheesy, stupid but fun kind of cringe, it's painful. at times the story wants to focus on the big picture, but for the majority, getting laid is the biggest concern.in terms of decision making, the game's a one track mind. there's a moment where you have to hide from an enemy, and the game gives you a timer and a choice between hiding with the boy or the girl. out of curiousity i let it run out, and it automatically decided to have me hide with the girl. i honestly was expecting a game over screen at least, but it just chose for me. in the big awakening scene for the protagonist, i was essentially forced to agree to it instead of being able to just decline it, because it repeated the same cutscene multiple times whenever i didn't agree to be the hero. and it's not like doing it multiple times led to something changing, i was stuck in a loop until i agreed. this game wants me to be the big hero and be with pretty anime girls, because....?the combat is pretty weightless and even effortless for the most part. it's like if DMC without the weight behind the attacks and 2-4 buttons to spam, mostly on prompts. for as much as this gets compared to Dark Souls, i don't see it outside enemies being able to kill you.the story doesn't feel important. the game wants to inform the player on enough to know exposition, but not enough to understand the gravity of the situation. yeah the world is going through an apocalypse, but you're never told much of what will happen if you fail at least. and i get (well haven't you seen a post-apocalyptic story?), but for a number of them, even in anime, there was at least a clear enough line for the characters to pick their sides and fight. this feels like it's trying to do what other media has done, and that's it. a character in this game that's basically a god says that if you don't retrieve "the stone" the world will change. but there's nothing more than that. change for the better, change for the worse, change so that murder is legal, change so that the PS3 has games? there's nothing to go off of to make the player understand in story why they should care.since this gets compared to Persona, Igor in that series is a guide that gives the player the power of persona as the world will soon be destroyed in the future. you don't actually take part in helping until there's no other option and you could die. in this, it feels backwards, and also forced upon you with no clear explanation or understanding. it doesn't feel like there's much of a point if any for this story outside of "people get older and change with time, and the person you work for hates change"the animated cutscenes for what they are, are alright. and the game itself looks fine and decently appealing at times. and the music is okay. that's about all i got on that honestly.in some ways, a game about dating others and an apocalypse actually is a neat idea that you can explore around with and make something that could do what games like Persona haven't done. but this instead just feels like a game that is a collection of popular stuff in games and anime on face value. the characters are 1 dimensional, the combat is meh, and the writing isn't really fun to look at when it's paired with trying to take itself seriously. if it was a satire and fully aware of itself, that'd be one thing, but i haven't gotten that from this at all.it's not worth it, imo.

_childDocuments_.review: While I had some fun with the game I cannot recommend it for 30$. The writing is conflicting because there are scenes with forced anime tropes or cliches that painfully shift the tone of  the story. Despite this, there are character moments that are genuinely endearing and enjoyable. However, any development in the world or characters isn't further expanded on within the 10 - 15 hour playtime. As a result, the emotional beats of the story don't  leave the impact they could have left. The gameplay is a mix of social sim, RPG , and action combat. Starting with combat, it feels very unpolished when compared to other titles in the genre. There is no air movement like jumping, you cant string light and heavy attacks together for different combos, and your stuck in very rigid and jarring attack animations. Furthermore, The RPG mechanics are very bare bones in which there are trivial stat increases and some spells that are not well balanced. For example, there is not much incentive to invest in healing at all. When you die you re spawn at very generous checkpoints with full hp and no other penalty.  Additionally, healing spells cost an excessive amount of energy that could be used on significantly cheaper spells that negate damage or provide near game breaking crowd control.  The social sim is the strongest portion of this game when the characters interact naturally with each other instead of relying on tropes to standout. However, their social links suffer from the rushed and awkward pacing of the story. In summary, this game tries to do too much too quickly which leaves it feeling more shallow than it should.  Despite my criticisms, It is apparent that there was passion for this game and its ideas. I  hope that that the developers review these shortcomings because I believe they can make a better game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed opinions on this game but overall it was enjoyable enough that I would recommend it. Characters are fun and gameplay is pretty solid. Environments do their job well enough but does feel very repetitive after a while. My biggest issue though is the length. _childDocuments_.review: With a heavy heart I can't recommend.It's atrociously buggy. Let me start with my first major gripe, I can't  care that this was a passion project from a small team. I love that they made and that everything the developer had said is amazing but, it's Ui is awful whenever you have to save you can easily accidently load a earlier save, but what makes that a issue is the AUTOSAVE, it is without a doubt the worst AUTOSAVE to have ever existed so if you accidently load a old save it autosaves you right there and bam congrats you just lost 4 hours of effort (this happened 3 times) if you press a button at the wrong time popup messages will get stuck on your screen making you unable to do anything but force close and reload. Onto the characters the main character is terrible, I mean why did you have to make him look so bland? As fans of Persona each Persona character has a unique appealing look, the MC here has none he is literally what you think the most basic shonen character template would look like. The japanese are all pretty good.Brandon James Winckler's brief lines at the end are delivered well but feel sort of out of place.  Sadly some of the female Voice Actors just don't seem to be giving it their all, but the male VA are so on point having Aleks Le voice Yohan is brilliant casting (he is also Yuki Makoto's P3R VA)  You can feel the persona influence in several ways.Do you remember mementos in Persona 5? Well that's basicially this entire game. Remember in Persona  5 how you just skip days on the calender with a ton of dialogue with no control what so ever? Yeah well there is a ton of that  The Battle system works fine and is fluid. The small budget really shines through here because it feels like it. After  the accidental hours back reload I wanted to stab myself in the face for having to sit through the same slow dialogue multiple times with no speed up  basicially because the coding for this game can't handle it if anything happens slightly too fast it glitches. The dialogue is fine until you read it for the third time in a row back to back. I anticipated this game and wanted to give it a glowing review but as it is I can't. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to persevere with this one because the trailer was interesting and premise of a weeby dating sim at the end of the world amused me, but it had too many issues for my liking.It has all the standards problems I've come to expect from Japan. Cliche storyline.The combat is both too easy and frustratingly hard -- it takes very few hits to kill you, at least early on, and you have to react so fast to get "perfect dodges" that it often seemed like it was actually warning me too late. On the other hand, if you just roll around and hack and slack and forget about the whole "perfect dodge" thing it's actually a lot easier.
