_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating monotone quick time event fighting with even more obnoxious mini games.+ CharactersThe character interactions seem to be fun, but very stereotypical, in both good and bad. If this is your first anime game you wont mind.++ Graphics & StyleIt has a very comfy and pleasing 3D anime style. It's nothing revolutionary, but it doesn't need to be.+/- Story & SettingIt's ok. It honestly feels more like some semi competent story you'd throw into a hentai game.--- CombatIt sucks, really bad. It's monotone grind-fest filled with obnoxious quick time events, with parry+dodge mechanic that only works most of the time. And it's clear that even the developers thought that the combat is bad, since the game auto saves between every encounter, and refills your health when you die and reload. Aka instead of balancing and making the combat work, they just gave you infinite lives, and hope you'll bash your head against the wall until you get through. And it's not like in souls games, where you'd learn a pattern/moves of a boss, but instead repeat the same parry prompts as any other enemy in the game x-number of times and hope the jank does not hit in this time. Also the foreground and effects etc. visual clutter tends to block your view, so you can't even see the parry prompts half of the time.It's the worst part of the game, but it's also the main focus.--- MinigamesThese are annoying beyond belief. I'd rather play FFX chocobo racing and butterfly catching than these.TLDR:It's a hard game, but it's hard due to jank, not because it has tight or creative design, that needs/allows for creative approach. Just play a dating sim and a dark souls game back to back to get the same elements but actually good.My only regret is that I didn't play this in the 2 week window after purchasing it, because now I can't even refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to sum up Eternights, I would do it as follows: ok combat, good story, good characters, great dialogue. _childDocuments_.review: The game was a delightful surprise for me. I approached it with modest expectations, but I'm always eager to try an indie game, especially one that is clearly a passion project created by just one or two individuals.The story is undoubtedly the game's strongest aspect. It’s evident that a great deal of love and effort went into crafting it, resulting in a touching narrative filled with humorous moments and an engaging plot. One of the standout features for me was the freedom the developers had in their writing, unbound by the constraints of a larger publisher or imposed standards and agendas. This allowed them to infuse the game with genuine emotions, quirky jokes, and lively dialogues, all without crossing into vulgarity or childishness.Contrary to some reviews, I found the ending to be quite powerful. Many criticisms seem to stem from a preference for typical, Hollywood-style happy endings. This game defies that expectation, offering instead a conclusion that is meaningful and emotionally resonant, making the player's choices feel significant throughout the journey.There have been some unfounded claims about the game pushing an agenda, particularly the notion that it forces players into a gay relationship to unlock special skills. This is simply not true. The game does not impose such requirements, and any such perception likely reflects a misunderstanding or a narrow viewpoint and quite frankly sound a little homophobic. In fact, the game subtly discourages players from unlocking all the ultimate skills at once, as doing so leads to the "bad" ending with the main character feeling like a dumb playboy, highlighting the importance of thoughtful decision-making.Regarding gameplay, it can become somewhat repetitive after a certain point, which is perhaps where the solo development effort does shows its limitations. However, the main dungeons remain enjoyable to explore, with well-designed puzzles that add to the overall experience.In conclusion, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. It evoked strong emotions and featured well-written, charming characters that drew me in. I am eagerly anticipating what this developer will create next.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights has truly been a remarkable addition to my gaming collection on the PS5, and as a passionate trophy hunter, it has provided an exhilarating journey that I won't soon forget. Developed with a blend of science fiction, fantasy, and strategic gameplay, Eternights offers a captivating experience that keeps players engaged from start to finish.One of the most impressive aspects of Eternights is its stunning visuals and immersive world-building. From the moment I booted up the game, I was greeted with breathtaking landscapes, intricate character designs, and attention to detail that truly brought the game world to life. Whether exploring ancient ruins or navigating through bustling cities, every environment felt meticulously crafted and added to the overall sense of immersion.In terms of gameplay, Eternights strikes a perfect balance between action and strategy. The combat mechanics are intuitive yet deep, allowing for satisfying encounters that require careful planning and execution. As I progressed through the game, I found myself constantly challenged by new enemies and obstacles, keeping me on my toes and ensuring that every encounter felt fresh and exciting.One aspect of Eternights that particularly stands out is its emphasis on player choice and consequence. Throughout my journey, I was faced with numerous decisions that had a tangible impact on the story and world around me. Whether choosing to ally with a particular faction or deciding the fate of key characters, each choice felt meaningful and added layers of depth to the overall narrative.Of course, as a trophy hunter, I can't overlook the satisfaction of completing Eternights' extensive list of challenges and achievements. From mastering every combat encounter to uncovering hidden secrets scattered throughout the world, pursuing the game's trophies provided a satisfying sense of accomplishment that kept me coming back for more.Overall, Eternights is a shining example of what a modern RPG can achieve. With its stunning visuals, engaging gameplay, and meaningful choices, it's a must-play experience for any PS5 owner. Whether you're a hardcore trophy hunter or simply looking for an immersive gaming experience, Eternights delivers in spades.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem. Bought it expecting a funny cross between a souls-like and a dating sim, and I got that for the most part. It has some perverted jokes, but it plays out as if it's making fun of perverts. The only things I would add would be having some responses make them dislike you to add some realism/challenge, and the option to play as a girl. Those would make the perverted lines seem less like they're  trying to get guys to objectify girls.Yuna and Sia are pretty good characters in my opinion. They're really down-to-earth compared to Min, who kind of has a master/servant dynamic with the main guy. _childDocuments_.review: A relatively short but sweet action RPG, Eternights absolutely does not overstay its welcome. There's room for improvement, yes: there could be a slightly more consistent tone, the skill tree and the resources used to level it up could have been a little better. (Although I appreciate the attempt of a skill tree not dependent on level-ups) While great, the combat does have a few hiccups, like the very strict dodge timers. But again, it's all solid enough to be enjoyable. The only actively bad part was the forced stealth/escort mission with Min that brings the usual fast pace to a screeching halt, but even that doesn't last too long and it is for easily the best girl in the game, so it evens out. All in all: I recommend it if you're looking for a good action RPG with similar vibes to Persona! I myself am also looking forward to a sequel or similar game that irons out these rough edges!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game really got to me! It shares similarities with GHOST at DAWN, another game created by the talented developer at Blue and Red Games.I recommend this game and the one I mentioned for the story, graphics, grit, creative element and because its plain awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid game made by a small team. I'd give it a good 6.5 to 7 out of 10. Characters: A strong point of the game. I liked all of them. Most of them are pretty well written. Story: I feel like there wasn't a whole lot done to establish the lore of the world in which the game takes place, but the story is serviceable. I strongly disliked the ending, but others may not feel the same way. The major event that took place felt very contrived. Art: Anime style. Characters are pretty cool with good design. Dungeons and lighting are an eyesore.Audio: Voice acting is amazing. Music is middling.Gameplay: Social sim part is fun, but the game should do a better job of indicating which answers will raise which stat, because there doesn't seem to be any correlation and it isn't intuitive at all. Combat is kind of repetitive and gets boring after a while, but the abilities you get keep it fresh, and once you master the system it can feel really good.WARNING: The social stat progression in my game was bugged and 2 of the 4 stats would not go up no mater how many points I earned. I had to edit the save file to give myself the max stats to get around the issue. It is a known issue. The instructions to edit the save file are in the Discussion section.It's good for a 10 hour game. There is a new game plus. All stats and combat abilities carry over, but there is no new content as far as the story and you can't skip cutscenes.I do recommend, it's a fun little game. I would be interested to see more of this world (especially Aria). :)

_childDocuments_.review: A () short positive review to push the algorithm. The bar was  low going in to this, seeing that the reviews were either raving about how incredible the game was yet all I saw on the store page was anime bait for virgins. Turns out I was totally wrong, A 10-ish hour long experience with rewarding combat, well voiced and entertaining characters, a decent story and plenty of laughs. If you don't mind the art style, this is a . The combat is a pretty simple, but it has those high-skill opportunities like Perfect Dodges and Parrying so you can flex on the monsters in style. That all feeds into the Elemental Fist and Deathblow attacks which are your bread and butter of dealing big damage. I didn't get what the negative reviews were saying with the combat; there were complaints with monsters attacking off-screen, which was solved with, , using the camera, and there are only a couple of monsters which can block, and some parry, your attacks, which you'll get hit by once and learn to do better. Also, the bosses were really fun, which I was not expecting from such a small team, just learn the timings and punish. Another big thing was that the social aspects of the game have a real tangible impact on the gameplay, with each social level gaining upgrades to abilities and passives. It makes it so that the social links are worth doing outside of just learning more about a character. Overall, the monster variety was pretty good for the length of the game, and they are all pretty well choreographed to show you what they are doing, before they do it. . I'll keep story discussions brief since I don't see the point in spoiling a game you should play, especially since other reviews spoiled the ending for me, however the story is nothing ground-breaking or revolutionary. The stakes are set well in the beginning and you know your mission throughout, it's more about the characters and their story arcs which is done pretty well. Another note to point out is the stellar voice acting for the main cast, there wasn't any point where I felt that the dialogue fell flat, and it has some genuinely funny moments with your responses which were very well done. Certain aspects could have been expanded more, and bigger story moments were lacking in gravity as the music wasn't hitting those beats to give it more impact. Another surprise for me was that I actually really liked the characters, bar one romanceable partner. They show actual growth across their social links and the social aspect provides direct upgrades for the dungeon crawling, which is something not many games do and deserves praise. Overall, a serviceable story which gives room for the more important aspect, the characters. Not many to list:Now that's out of the way, here is some classic back-tracking on my negative points. The main dev team appeared to consist of 3 people, and while there were some minor complaints I had, knowing this going in I really could  care less about the issues I encountered as they clearly spent their time well in making a realistic and focused product with the limitations they had. This is a huge success from a small main-dev team, clearly a passion project made with love.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm enjoying the game. It is a diet version of Persona and pulls a lot of things from it, like SP, dungeon layout, the time limit to take out the dungeons and of course the confidants. It's not the only game it's pulled liberally from. Just did Min's training and was surprised to see the squat mini-game from FFVIIR all the way down to the beginner button press pattern. Surprised this wasn't picked up by SquareEnix. But despite the copy/paste of some of it's mechanics, there's a fun dating sim game here with some mildly frustrating fighting gameplay loops. _childDocuments_.review: I've approached this game fully expecting it to be extremely janky, but to my surprise, aside from the very beginning when I was figuring out controls/did not have any skills, I actually found gameplay to be quite good. Could use some more polish, but the foundation is really solid.Really loved the characters and the overall vibe of the game, as well as the aesthetics and visuals. The few animation pieces were stunning, too. The music was lovely as well.Once you figure out the combat, the dungeons are a lot of fun too (though you need to tolerate SOME jank, it is an indie after all).The performance was well done as well, I've played this on my six years old gaming laptop on high settings and I did not have any problems,  when most games from 2022 and later stutter quite a bit for me.I definitely recommend this to anyone who is looking for romance-oriented game, all 4 characters are really likeable. It's also super cool that there is a gay option, I can't really think of many anime-like games that have this.My only real compliants are:-I wish MC would have been voiced. He gets a few lines and he has a pretty distinct personality, VA would have really elevated him and I think this was missed opportunity. All other characters have great VAs which I think added to their charm-I didn't really like the ending (though that is subjective), but my actul gripe is that the secret/perfect ending is a QR code that you need to scan to see the video on your phone. I understand it as a work-around if developer couldn't make it in time for the deadline, but the game was released some time ago, it definitely could have/should have been patched in.Anyways, I recommend this one if the trailers seem interesting to you, I'm definitely looking forward to more from this developer! This was an excellent debut.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights is a solid 7/10 game. BUT sometimes the most interesting experiences live within the 7/10 or 8/10 games. FIRSTLY, I think you should play this game, so I'll start with the positives. Great writing, a moving story, characters that feel real and a satisfying skill tree and level up system.Next, the not so great things... The graphics and fighting mechanics are mediocre at best. The character designs are fantastic, but this game uses so many different art styles, that it constantly loses consistency in its very short run time (10-14hrs). There are very few animated scenes in this game, but even those few all range in entirely different quality... so much so they can be jarring.To be perfectly honest, I rarely enjoyed any of the fighting in this game. But I enjoyed every second of getting to know the girls and unlocking more of their stories. _childDocuments_.review: It's good. More than good. _childDocuments_.review: Usually, I'm not too fond of hack and slashes, but this game has something that kept me in it. And don't be scared by crude starting menu or settings - yes, they look kind of like someone's first game project - but hey, you can see that time that wasn't put in there was actually used better way in the game itself ;)It has its flaws: - the camera sometimes feels like it's fighting with the player, and automatic zoom (which you can't control) sometimes does weird stuff - nothing game breaking though- with my PS5 controller, I had to crank up to the max X and Y camera axis - but I saw that on the mouse and keyboard, they were pretty OK by default- I was running it on the normal diff, which only means that it might be kind of too easy for you - but hey, there is an expert mode- and of course, it's relatively shortBut damn, it does defend itself with the following:- quite good humor - at least for me- the plot is quite pompous - kind of like the last chapter in Persona 5 (I much prefer smaller/modest plots like in Persona 4 or 3) - but humor kind of saves it for me, and it's pretty interesting- the graphics inside the game and the art style itself are quite pleasing- dungeons themselves are pretty varied and unique - nothing like Mementos in Persona 5 or dungeons from Persona 4 and 3- funny and interesting characters
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: if you like anime styled games and enjoy anime tropes and characters, you'll like this. Everything outside the characters is shallow, but the game is short and you get to date waifus so it's a recommend for meFull review: I have not played a persona game before this but the concept of this game intrigued me. The whole game is very centered around its characters and dating them and id say it does that very well. All the characters get time to show their personality that feels realistic based on what they experienced in their past. It makes connecting with them feel more natural than other games that introduce a dating theme. Of course this game is very anime inspired so there are still those tropes, but as someone who generally likes anime, it didnt bother me too much. Voice acting is generally pretty good. I settled with the Japanese dub as it felt like it fit better but some of the english cast like Chani feel very emotive. The games give you the option of 3 different options (English, Japanese, and Korean) that you can change at pretty much any moment without any loading which is very nice. Outside the characters, id say story wise the game is a little weak. Theres some lore but its not told or presented in a very interesting way and is more of a backdrop to get you to meet the characters. There's some humor which may land for you (it did for me) but ultimately how much you like this will really depend on finding a character you really like.Gameplay is very simple. Outside of talking to people, you'll be doing combat in dungeons with some puzzles here and there. Combat is pretty simple and isn't too complicated. Other than matching elemental weaknesses, this is a simple 3rd person action game. It's serviceable but I wouldn't consider it good. There's maybe 5 enemy types total and there's never any strategy outside of dodging their moves with a perfect dodge then spamming your strongest moves. There's a good loop where spending time with your romance partners will let you unlock new skills and passive boosts. Most of the upgrades are small Stat boosts which won't feel substantial until late game. Since different characters are linked to a stat, your choice of who you romance will also dictate if you have more attack, defense, or health which is probably the closest thing to a build as you can get in this game. You'll increase these stats through minigames with each of the romance interests that are very inspired from other places like the squat minigame from Final Fantasy 7. Like the rest of the game, none of them are deep, but it's serviceable and loops into the main dating part of the game.The soundtrack here is very light and not very memorable. Graphically, this isn't a demanding game but ran on the Steam Deck with a few dips below 60 fps here and there. Overall, I'd say it's a good game on deck as it's simple gameplay mechanics work well for a portable game. I only had one bug where a cutscene didn't advance but reloading the save fixed it. I recommend this game if you're like me and you're going into this game to date anime waifus. The rest of the game isn't bad, but it's clear the focus of the game was the romantic partners. Nothing here is bad and the game doesn't overstay its welcome. For the base price it's a good ask and on a sale I think it's a good deal. P.S. Min is best girl

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game but I have a couple gripes with this game.- The main story. It was very bare bones and generic. For example, when Aria was introduced, she did not explain who she is, who she works for, or how she knows what is going on. _childDocuments_.review: This is a Diamond in the Rough. It starts out as one of the funniest RomCom I have seen in ages, has satisfying, but a little clunky Gameplay. It's kinda like Metal Gear Rising meets Persona, but "low quality".The most budget I think went in the Voice Over (I played in English) which also uses some Persona 5 and Genshin Voices! (I think)It lures you into the RomCom and later hit's you like a train (results vary) right in the feels, but you should not question some of the really illogical physics that go on with the Train and Momentum.Also when you see the credits keep your Smartphone with QR code scanner ready.It is roughly 15 Hours long on easy difficulty (which was plenty fun for me).And has a New Game+ if you want to see everything, which I have not done yet.At the end the Gameplay does get repetitive, and there could have been much more potential in it, but for such a small team it was very serviceable.I try to put my thoughts into Numbers:Writing: 7/10 not a lot get's explained about the world or why something happens, but it made me laugh frequently. (More silly RomCom for 80% of the game)Gameplay: 6/10 it was fun but got very repetitive and was very clunky, but I have seen/played much worse. (Tokyo Xanadu for example is imo inferior in gameplay since it feel much more sluggish and stiff)Music: 5/10 The music was serviceable, but I barely noticed it, which could be seen as good, since it also was not that disruptive?Sound: 7/10 Impact sound of effects where pretty good and where appropriate, but nothing outstanding.Enemy Design: 7/10 some of these Creatures look like straight out of Silent Hill and where genuinely creepy.Character Visuals: 6/10 generic low budget anime "bodies".Environment: 5/10 serviceable Level Design and Puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very impressed especially finding out that a very small talented team worked on it.  The story could have been fleshed out more with finer details, such as backstories, but understandable things had to be simple because of the length.  Speaking of simple, combat system definitely falls in this category as it was easy to pick up.  Running around the levels was a breeze as things were pretty straight forward with no complicated mechanics.  If you're a fan of hack and slash type games, you'll enjoy this one. I'd say its smooth as some of the combat cut scenes and animations are decently done.  Overall, the anime art style was enjoyable.Like others mentioned, the English voice acting for all the characters are well done as it definitely immersed me into the game.  I only wish the player (you) was an actual character with a voice actor, but I understand its one of those types of games (Persona) where the Developers want you to be part of the game if you know what I mean.Back to what I mentioned about the game play being simple, there were some things that could have been improved on such as tutorials for use of combat skills like breaking shields.  The screen that shows all the high ranks of skills was a bit confusing as I often found myself with enough black essence but couldn't upgrade that skill.  There should have been descriptions or maybe some explanation through some of the screen menu's for better clarity.  Overall, additional UI helpers during game play and combat would have been nice.  For example, after rolling around so much in combat, I would get lost of which direction I'm going since every part of the environment looked the same.  I would get confused of who my party members were during combat.  Some reviewers mentioned that the game was too easy which is a bit true.  As a casual gamer,  I found it just fine as I wasn't looking for intense combat systems with crazy boss monsters with never ending uses of abilities. That would have been nice but I didn't want to be bothered with more time on my hands, let alone causing more frustration.  I was more into reaching the end to see how the story turned out.  I do admit near the last half of the game, I didn't rely much on the R2 special abilities as basic combo strikes was good enough.  Definitely some game balancing can be improved there.Anyway, the purchase was well worth it if you're into this type of game play and genre. I felt connected to the characters and its story and do hope we get a sequel or even a DLC. A bigger budget to flesh things out even more to everyone's liking would be amazing :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. The game is rough around the edges but it has its own charm. I got this game while it was on sale because I was still reluctant to fully dive into what it had to offer. My main draw to this game was because it presented itself as a persona-like game. I can say that if you are a fan of the social elements of the persona series then you will love this game. Even though the game has a way smaller batch of characters you can interact and learn more about, I believe the way the game ties its social mechanic into its story does it far better than any game I have played. The actual gameplay though is relatively simple and easy to get in with minimal stat and abilitiy progression. If this game was longer than the combat would be a downside, but because you can on average spend 13~ hours to beat, it doesn't feel like the combat becomes stale. I personally think at its base price its an okay game to risk getting, but I fully believe that its a must grab if on sale.

Skill Issue is also possible.)Very enjoyable, however you will soon realize how little enemy variety (and also attack patterns) there are.While your confidants (allies) provide active skills, realistically you (or at least, I) are/am only going to use healing (and maybe shield, I never used it). Because:Speaking of dodging, this game also provides a parry system. Funnily enough, I only managed to trigger parry once, and it was accidental.There is no point attempting anything other than dodging, unless you want style points for YouTube.Speaking of style, some enemies have barriers that you have to break using your skill with a confidant's damage element.The animation looks cool, but again: lacks in variety. (Camera also shakes so much that I can't see much thing)I could count the amount of time I died in the game on the fingers of one hand, suggesting how OP dodging is.Finally, final boss fight is underwhelming. It's like fighting another miniboss.Looks Okay.I want to be clear that this is not an insult, but for some reason, I am really reminded of the facial animation of "Seed Of The Dead" (Yeah, that hentai game). I don't quite know how to describe it, but they feel "off" and stiff. I think I would describe it as "slapping emojis on faces".The buildings in the game looks... "basic". They are not terrible/ literally undecorated, just .The maps have eye-catching arrow neon signs to guide you to the next arena, navigating through maps is not difficult.Looks fine, I have nothing to say about it.Nothing to  about.Two gods fighting each other. One wants humanity and one wants domination (or destruction I forgot).Story Of:Your Average "Desperate Trying to Bring Loss Ones Back by Helping the Villain" story.Your average "Purpose Discovery/ Redemption" stories.ALL of your confidants' backstory is , and they are VERY QUICKLY (doesn't even take a full day!) reassured by the protagonist and other confidants.As a story of its type it definitely did nothing wrong, but it is definitely not a fantastic story.You know you are here for the romance. However, I must say that I feel absolutely disconnected from the protagonist's feelings. All of the romance seems to only come from the girls (and one boy), but at the same time the protagonist claims he has feelings for them too, which I cannot feel.The fact that they all have similar backstories didn't help either.~~~MAJOR SPOILER~~~~~~SPOILER END~~~Obviously, the issue comes from only having so few days for the protagonist and any confidant to get to know and feel comfortable with each other. And having 4 romantic confidants means each story are going to be short, and ultimately ineffective at convincing us that they really, really love each other.You can also date all 4 at once and they wouldn't SUSPECT a thing. Very amazing, I know. The date scenes ""suggests"" that they have sex, are the walls so thick that others couldn't hear a thing?They certainly can convey feelings/ emotions, but nothing remarkable.Finally, NO GALLERY MODE? Really? Those scenes with the confidants looks absolutely beautiful and they are so gorgeously drawn, but I cannot view them after beating the game!Other Good Impressions:Other Bad Impressions:I sounded harsh for the most part, I know. However, I am still very happy to give this game a . For people who don't care about whether an indie game studio made the game, I recommend buying this game on sale. If you like to support indie companies, then you should definitely buy it at full price,

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a game decided to be similar to Persona structure-wise.It was such a blessing playing through the days and seeing the interactions happening.The game is short, but since there's a new game+ you can see the couple differences at the end.If I were to complain about something, it certainly would be about the lack of 'bad endings'. In games like this I like to let the deadlines expire on purpose to see what happens and are the real consequences for failure. Unfortunately, even if you fail the last and most important deadline the game gives you, nothing happens. It straight up sends you back to the main menu for you to click "load game" and try again. It felt kinda bad for me not being able to see alternative endings like that.Besides what I just said above, I don't have any real complaint. Eternights is epic, based and redpilled.All the relationships are nice to follow, and their backstories for the most part are enjoyable when it comes to the point where their characters get development.Even though there was no 'bad ending' per se, I freaking loved the ending. I got caught off guard by the consequences and was not expecting them to pull THAT off. The climax with Lux's speech was spot-on. And don't even let me get started on the anime cutscenes plus the ending sequences as a whole, with the post-credit QR code as a reward for playing the game to top it all off.Combat was extremely fun to play (this is not a hack-and-slash game, if there are a bunch of enemies in the room, you WON'T win by just clicking buttons), the power-ups were good to use, the puzzles weren't repetitive (there were some one-time-only game mechanics for some parts of the game preventing it from happening), Chani's arc was pretty good, Sia is based and very entertaining, Min is so cute, Yuna is a kind person, Yohan exists, Lux's voice actor was popping off from start to finish with the way she was interpreting the character, the scavenging mechanic was so creative and such a neat way to let us get along with the love-interests.This was the first game I bought on pre-sale in my life. I was so hyped when I first saw the trailers. I DON'T regret buying in at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I have ever played and it's one of my all time favorites. It's not perfect, but it's clearly made with unending love and dedication. The characters are extremely well-written and likable, to the point that they kind of overshadow the story, but their infectious charm makes you care anyway. The combat, while being a bit jank, is extremely fun and rewarding especially towards the end. Alot of people had issues with the ending (no spoilers) but I thought it was one of the most heartfelt and touching endings to a video game I have ever played (up there with Nier Automata and CP2077's The Star ending). It's rough, it's jank, and sometimes it's downright goofy, but no game has touched me like this in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually never write reviews but I absolutely LOVED this game. I mean. I started 2 days ago and I already have 20 hours. If you do the math correctly that adds up to 10 hours a day.. Not sure if this really represents that the game is good, or just the fact that I have no life. Either way, I came into this expecting a shorter/lower quality persona-like game, and that is exactly what I got. Besides the fact that this is a hack and slash game instead of having a turn-based combat system like persona, the two are very similar. Yet, I somehow got sucked into this game immediately, and ended up liking it even more than the much more polished persona games. I now have 24/26 achievements, which I will be finishing tomorrow. (Or.. later today, considering its 3 am) Let me make it known that I not only never write reviews, but I also never go for 100% completion on games. Of course, this game is very short, which could be a reason for that, but I also just genuinely enjoy every second of this game. From the awkward conversations about tentacles to the fairly simple yet intense combat, everything about this game felt amazing to me. Now I will be honest, the ending of the game left me feeling VERY depressed and slightly confused. Overall, I would still say this is one of my favorite games ever, even considering the fact that it was kinda short. The characters were all interesting and I had a blast getting to know all of them while also raising my confidant levels for more upgrades in their skill trees. I also loved the combat and all the monster designs, as well as the story itself.I can't say for sure that everyone will like this game as much as I do, but one thing I can say for certain is:If you're taking a look at the reviews wondering whether or not you should buy this game, do it. This game is certainly worth giving a try.

_childDocuments_.review: SOMETHING SPECIAL:So there you are, searching the steam page, and wondering if you'll ever find something that you can enjoy in these dry gaming times. Then you see it. Eternights. You watch the trailer and to your surprise, there is full voice acting in it. You can't tell whether or not if it is a scam. Then you scroll down and see the great reviews about the game. They catch your eye, but they still aren't enough for you to buy it, until you read that this was made by a single person.Eternights is something special. As someone who has poured love into a craft of my own, it becomes easy to see in other's works. This game is one of those products. Made with care, a product that is finished although not perfectly polished, is still a diamond, cut or uncut.Gameplay:The action although filled with repetition is not terrible, in fact a few combats had me stumped several times. There is a skill tree system built in that is kind of like Persona 5's confidants. The better relationships you have with the characters, the more powerful you become. But that isn't the thing that kept me playing, although if bad I may have stopped. Instead it was the characters. They all feel so fleshed out, thought out and the emotions they output just seem genuine. It's hard to explain, but the longer I played the more I liked the characters. They are really well written. There were real moments where I couldn't help but just smile but what was said between characters. I even had some genuine laughs with Chani and others.Speaking of Chani. Even your typical best friend side character Chani (Who is best boy) who i thought was going to be annoying at first, really became one of my favorite characters throughout the game. His friendship with the protagonist was done just right and his struggles and frustrations are relatable.Buy this game. I can't wait to see what's in store from this developer.Gameplay 7/10Story 9/10Girls 10/10 (All girls are best girls, fight me.)Chani 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: My experience: Beat the game. Have started but not progressed in a NG+.Pros: Short Action Persona. That's basically it. It's the best non-Persona Persona game I've played (there are shockingly few) in terms of recreating the feel - it totally gets a lot of the elements correct. Large percentage of the game is voice-acted which was surprising, given the price and the fact that this is seemingly the dev's first game. The VA is also not annoying or terrible, which is honestly worthy of a thumb's up on its own for a first game from a dev. Combat feels good.Cons: It's short - short enough to be a bit disappointing, length-wise. I played 22 hours and finished. It does help it not outstay its welcome, but the ending wraps up a little too quickly and flatly. And you don't really get much to soak in, either in terms of length or content, after the finale. Some of the plot points are touched on but not really fully explored. There were a few items after the game where I was like "oh yeah, that happened... but why did they bother?" I'm not seeing anyone in the reviews with a ton of additional playtime over me so I don't think there's content I'm missing. Some of the writing gets a little pervy teenage boy at times but not to the point that you'd ragequit. Combat, while feeling good, eventually becomes a little too easy to cheese with the skills you get.Conclusion: I'd say the game is fully and completely worth it at $20 and anywhere above that it's really up to how hard you're jonesing for a short Persona-like experience. I really hope this dev keeps producing games like this because for a first attempt, it is genuinely insanely impressive. Once I started, I played until I finished while dropping other games, so there's something very much there.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game. There is a good balance between humor, horror and romance. The characters are likable enough though their personal arcs are a bit shallow. Not a knock per say, I did still enjoy them and found myself wanted to progress, however don't expect anything to blow you away. My favorite thing in this game, has to be how the handle leveling skills. You have your own skills and the skills of your companions which mainly act as support. Increasing your health, defense, attack and special attacks. Instead of grinding out monsters you grow your relationship with them. The stronger your bond between them, the more confident they become and in turn more useful. It's a pretty neat mechanic and I'd love to see it used more. It also helps that the personal scenes with them are often pretty funny or heart-warming. As for the main story, it's pretty solid. Again, not the most amazing writing, but enough to keep you engaged and wanting to push forward. I do have a complaint about combat as many others do. Although there is a nice skill tree, the combat is a bit repetitive, especially with "boss" type enemies. You quickly find the best method to beating them is standing around waiting for a dodge prompt, using the dodge to fill you gauge, and using your powers to "break" their defense, which would be fine, however some enemies you have to do this three or four times. (Assuming you don't pick the wrong power or miss a QTE.) Luckily most of the dungeons can be ran through pretty quickly, and a large amount of enemies can be ran passed without missing out out anything. I know this review sounds a bit negative, but to be honest, this is the first game in quite sometime that I thoroughly enjoyed and found myself wanting to come back to.  The characters are adorable and funny at times. The art style is beautiful. The environment is fantastic. The story is pretty unique. I'm excited to see what the dev does next to be honest. 8/10

That one might be for Horimiya fans only though.Cons:- The whole ending sequence feels rushed. Large chunks of story have no closure and frankly it ends a garbled mess. I hated the last two hours of the game, if not more.- The combat is bad. Not 'passable' bad but seriously badly designed. Both boring and actively annoying, somehow.- The whole dating sim mechanic was weird. It's difficult to explain why but it didn't really gel with the other storyline for me.- This is clearly solo developed and has ALL the limitations you'd expect.Frankly, if Persona 4G or 5R are on sale buy those. _childDocuments_.review: This game's scrappy and small in scope. It feels very obvious that the budget was $5 and a bag of chips, and the voice actors got most of the chips (the English voices are very enjoyable!). HOWEVER: It totally works. The elevator pitch is "a much smaller-in-scope indie Persona, with dodge-and-parry based action combat in place of turn-based RPG battles and monster fusion". You can tell it was made by a teeny-tiny team that knew where to put their time and energy. The combat opens up a surprising amount as you unlock more abilities, though so far it hasn't quite stopped revolving around "dodge or parry for a window of opportunity, then exploit the hell out of it"They let the cute anime girl say the F-word (i am not allowed to type it out, or Steam will censor it). Ann Persona5 would never say the F-word. 10 additional points just for that.

_childDocuments_.review: An okay game with some fun voice acting. There are definite flaws with this game but lets start with the good. The voice acting is very good, with some great moments.  Chani is definitely the best character of the game with a pretty satisfying arc.Now for the bad. Most of the characters in this game are either super one dimensional or are underdeveloped. The lead girls were the worst offenders. Yuna was your typical bland idol who was clearly the preferred girl to date by the creator. Min is just weak, and not in a good way that you think she will grow. Sia is all the worst underdeveloped stereotypes from the Big Bang Theory. These flaws undermined the main premise of the game to bond with these girls.Speaking of the dating sim aspect of this game is underdeveloped. There's little chemistry or romance. There are some flashes here and there but the busted main girls make it just not work very well.Combat is also frustrating in that the other characters are basically useless. Using them in the midst of combat is a chore and the control surface is strange to do so. They need an AI, or alternatively this needed to be turn based combat. Turn based combat has the advantage of letting all the characters shine in a single player game. The combat otherwise was pretty standard.The plot was fine. I ended up going with Sia and the main ending was typical and decent. For the price though the game is a bit short.Overall I would say pick this up on sale. The main game is about 12 hours, so the current price is a bit high and the quality doesn't make up for it. If you are a casual gamer who may not have the best reflexes, go on Easy mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Why did I love this game so much?On the surface, it's fairly flawed. The action combat is passable, the elemental weaknesses are simple, the dodge mechanics being temperamental compared to other action games, the main story is a series of "and then this happens" with many plot hooks either disappearing or resolving entirely-too-quickly-and-conveniently, and there's quite a few bugs I found over the course of my playtime with the game (dialogue and elemental attacks continuing to play after I hit pause, one of the scene skips not working, among many other minor non-game-crashing things). And I could easily see how any number of these things could turn off a player at any given point.But that doesn't explain why I love this game so much.The answer is simple - the game has charm. It has charisma. It has soul.Underneath the layers of jank, it has interesting dialogue options between the main protagonist and his 5 companions (4 romantic options + his BFF), and even introduces a handful of smaller characters to the roster as well. Some are written better than others, but they're all written very well, and you can tell that the true focus of this game is the relationships between him and the others. The game has a handful of options that not only change a particular encounter, but it cares enough to call back to these encounters as you delve further into each of the romantic interests' storylines (making a New Game+ or a second playthru actually worth doing). A great deal of thought was put into how to progress your rank/relationship with each character (their training mini-game, the collection minigame, and the scenes where they just 'spend time' together), and between those interactions and the interactions on the train itself when you're killing time between major story beats, you really see the beauty of this game shine.For a work largely led by a single developer, Eternights has the makings of a great game. You either have to ignore some of its unpolished edges, or you have to appreciate them for what they are and enjoy them. Either way, I enjoyed the characters and the gameplay loop well enough to achieve all of the trophies and it got 26 hours out of me, and if that's not a resounding endorsement, I don't know what is.Give this game a try. I hope you enjoy it as much as I did!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I had a good experience with this game. Was it perfect? No. Of course not. I loved the different characters. I loved how unhinged some of the dialogue became based off your choices. And I liked the way they ended it. It was a unique touch that broke the PC/Console to person barrier. I also enjoyed the unique puzzles and soundtrack!That being said. I feel like while the game is good, it also feels unfinished to a degree or at least unpolished. The social dynamic left me wanting more from it. Creating bonds feels very superficial. I don't know what was missing from the equation, but it was something. The combat felt very predictable and easy for most of the game, until you got to the final boss. And depending on who you selected as your love interest the final boss can be outrageously difficult. Also, the dodge timing can be unpredictable at times even though its explained in the beginning. 7.75/10Looking forward to a sequel. Will definitely play it. I just hope the next installment in the IP feels more polished

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights isn't shy about its inspirations, but that's not a bad thing. It combines a variety of enjoyable gameplay mechanics into one nice little package.The characters are all very charming, and the writing has some really top-tier moments. This aspect is where Eternights really shines.The story is simple yet enjoyable, it left a few things unanswered after one playthrough, though there is a NG+. The combat is actually super fun. It can be a little janky sometimes, but overall I enjoyed it.But really, the best part of this game is Min. You can disagree, but you're wrong. Also the main credits were like... TWO PEOPLE? Most of it was one dude. The fact that this game is as good as it is, is super impressive. As ridiculous as this is going to sound, I hope Studio Sai gets super successful so I can see a remake of this in like 10 years with a full dev team. Looking forward to seeing what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: First section is Non-Spoilers & 2nd section is spoilers (but mostly for the devs)(Explaining The Basics)-I want to start by saying that this game is amazing. -It has a deep enough combat setup to where it's enjoyable and can be explored just enough to where it isn't boring but simple enough to where you can get on whenever and flow right back into it. Whoever invented the DEATH BLOW, I just want to give you ten bucks because I got such a thrill getting it every time.-The dodging Mechanic in this game is a little tough at first, think Dark Souls but a little worse. Not saying it is bad but it takes some getting used to. Now, once you do, you will start kicking a$$ by dodging, slowing down time and beating the crap out of the nearest enemy. On the note of dodging, it can be finicky for certain bosses and attacks. What I mean is that you will dodge at the perfect time and it won't trigger or the boss will chain attack after attack on you, after your 3rd or 4th time retrying on a boss, it gets a little annoying.-There are some visual bugs, like a character will be in another room while using their ability, but nothing game breaking. Speaking of, this game is very well polished! Especially being compared to top AAA games where you turn left and...oh I already fell through the floor. Granted, this game and a AAA title are two entirely different beasts, but the expectations are still there.(Personal Thoughts)-This story is great. It is unique, interesting, and hilarious. If I could give this game an award, it would definitely be for its comedy. The humor in the story is very slapstick and they time every joke just right. The jokes don't consist of "Character said something cringy...Please laugh", they consist of witty comedy that made me and my friends laugh hysterically (Don't want to spoil it! They are worth it). -I think this game could have used a little bit more time in the oven, not because it is a broken mess, but because there were some great ideas here that weren't fully explored and that I would have loved explored more in depth. An example of this is the scavenge feature that lets you get closer to characters by finding objects they are interested in. This sounds kinda interesting right? Well, sorta. I enjoyed it until I realized we were doing the same thing over and over, but by doing the same thing over and over, you remembered where that object is and boom, you go straight to it and grab it. If you accidentally go to the wrong place? Sorry, you now have to wait a little over a minute until you can go back. The idea was there but didn't feel fully fleshed out, like a few parts in this game.-The levels were pretty interesting, I always explored which benefited me by finding more upgrade currency, allowing me to wail on people even harder. The maps though, are fairly linear. Is that bad? Not if done right, which this game does! There are little roots here and there that allow you to find more and more upgrade currency and see more of the environment, but that is kind of it. No secrets, no nothing. It is a personal gripe I have because I love to explore new environments and get lost in the world, which I did, I played for 7 hours straight and realized it was 11 o clock at night. But the thing is that, including more benefits or more knowledge, or maybe a secret event, could spice up these environments a lot more. -Speaking of levels and stuff included, the puzzles, the puzzles were great. They were simple enough to where it wouldn't take you long to figure out, and got you right back into the combat, while also being really enjoyable, especially late game. I usually hate puzzles, not because I am bad at them, but because they aren't creative enough. Most puzzles nowadays aren't even puzzles at all, they are just "Put object here to open door" or "Pull lever and woah, door magically opened". These puzzles made you think for a sec and others encouraged you to explore. Instead of taking away from the experience, the puzzles added onto it. -In summary, I think this is a great game, If you are looking to buy it, you won't be disappointed, I promise, don't go in expecting this Balder's Gate 3 experience. It isn't a game that is perfect, it has flaws, but they are so minor to where you would be impressed no matter what expectations you have going into this. I went in with minimal expectations because I don't try too many games that aren't "Major releases", but this one was a diamond in the rough that I will probably play a few more times just to 100%, because it is that fun. THIS IS THE SPOILER BITS, MOVE ALONG IF YOU HAVE YET TO PLAY (but this is mostly for the devs for certain sections of the game).-So to start off, I love this game, y'all did an amazing job! You could tell that love was put into this and I this is a game that deserves to succeed. Now, that we got we got the compliment out of the way, I have some personal gripes that could be very easily resolved with a big fix or a content patch.-Starting off...the Delia fight. That fight would have been so cool, but, the attacks are weird. What I mean by that is when you try and dodge the attacks, you don't? Or more specifically, the time stop doesn't work. I thought at first that it was me just being garbage but it wasn't entirely me. When you would dodge at the right time, you wouldn't get your time stop to trigger and you would take a lot of damage. It wasn't too aggravating because I know it is something that can be fixed, but with people with less patience, that turns what could be an emotionally driven fight, into one where it is super frustrating. -Another thing with the Delia fight is the music, it felt off and take what I say with a grain of salt, but I felt as though it could've been more intense because it was such an emotionally driven fight. But that isn't a problem, just a suggestion!-Speaking of frustrating, was the unskippable cutscenes. They are super well animated and I love them, but when you are getting your a$$ handed to you for about 4 times by Delia, you kinda stop caring and just want to finish the fight, allowing you to skip all of the cutscenes would be great and deeply appreciated. -Another thing would be to give us more together moments in this game. What I mean are moments where every character hangs out with each other and allow you to bond with everyone a ittle bit better, it would give this game that little bit of extra time with the characters to not only get more game time out of it, but would allow me to get more attached to the other characters rather than just Yuna because Yuna felt like she got more love than everyone out of the cast.-Speaking of Yuna...Why'd y'all have to take her away from me y'all suck! I'm kidding, just wanted to be relevant lol.-Another issue is the lack of voice lines during those random moments and scavenge missions. It really feels off when a good chunk of the game, including some of the side stuff gets voice lines but those don't. It kinda ruins certain parts. I don't know if y'all did it to save on paying VA's (I don't know how expensive those get) or if they were last minute additions but I think it would go a long way if y'all included those voice lines. I think it would make those moments feel more apart of the experience.-On the topic of experience, my experience with the enemies varied. The designs themselves were amazing, y'all did a fantastic job on that, but I felt there was kind of a lack of variety?  I didn't notice it until late game where the monsters I were fighting all started to mesh where they were the same monster but different skin. I think what y'all have is fine but I think if you ever do update this game with more content, it would make the combat even better -And one last time, to the person that invented the DEATHBLOW, you are amazing, I love it.-I really loved this game and I look forward to more of y'all's work in the future. Good Luck!!

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed bag, honestly. Fighting the bosses and minibosses is fun, but the combat with the grunts is mostly flat and lacks proper feedback, hit reg is also all over the place and there seems to be a slight input delay for some actions (dodging is one of them, unfortunately). The world design is pretty interesting, but the graphics overall are pretty low effort. The enemy design is the same level of bat-sh*t crazy as Scarlet Nexus. The voice-acting - or at least the Japanese voice acting is pretty good, but otherwise the soundscape and music is pretty meh. Writing is good for an anime game, but nothing special, the characters are at least somewhat interesting, but the anime tropes and bad jokes that never land are ever present. The dating part at least so far consists mostly of doing repetitive task (yes one single task) in three small locations. The text in English has a bunch of pretty confusing translations in the tutorial section which make it harder to understand than it should be. And so on.I personally find the story interesting enough to continue, but the game isn't in a state where it would be worth 30 EUR. More like 15, so wait for a discount I guess. Probably give it a pass if you dislike stereotypical anime "humor".

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game 100%.  For an indie I thought they did really well for their first game. They took hack and slash combat and combined it with the dating sim genre. You can think of it as kinda combing DMC and Persona, however its only the ideas and Eternights I think managed to take the combat and dating sim mechanics and make it its own. The soundtrack is great and Lorien nailed the ending song.Combat:For an under 20hr game, the combat is engaging enough and not too complicated. The only issue is at the beginning, Act 1 and Act 2 you have not unlocked a lot of skills so you don't have a lot of options. Further into the game you will have normal attacks, heavy attacked, and 4 different skills not to mention spells. There is also different shield breaks, which adds a bit more complexity to the game. One issue I had was besides Yuna and Act 2, you basically never need to use Yuna/Fire break. You use Sia and Min's break often. In the future the shielded enemies could be a bit more diverse.Dating:I spent 10hrs to grind social stats and Yohan route. 2nd playthrough I did all Yuna, Min, and Sia routes. All 4 characters were interesting and if this was a full VN, I would've done all of their routes. Each datable character has their own issues and as you date them, you can see them grow as a character. Each character has a personality trait that makes them interesting. This honestly made me want to have the game be longer so we could interact with each of the character's more.Others:I do wish they fleshed out Aria more as she is there but not with any explanation. Also some animations are weird like the enemy death animations. after you kill them they just flop onto the floor and go poof. It's a bit jarring. Really looking forward to what they do next.Sidenote: Sia best girl! Yuna, Min, and Yohan fans fight meh.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game.  The creator has gone and state they were a fan of Persona and it certainly shows.  The characters are certainly the strongest points of the game. Also, it is very clear that the dungeon crawl, they tried make you go back to the train to rest and finish again later, but with the fact that all your health comes back and you don't lose items that you already picked up, there is no point to leaving, unless you are trying for that no death playthrough.  The puzzles were also creative and fun, I really enjoyed doing them all.  Also, it isn't that badly priced.So, since it's a short game and if can handle a flawed combat system, I recommend picking it up.  You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: If an ending kills a game for you, don't go for this.That being said....Game's fun. The presentation can be wonky at some points, but nothing that really detracts from the overall experience in my opinion. I was kind of surprised at how well the character bond stuff was done, it felt as close to its Persona inspiration as you could reasonably expect an indie title to get. Speaking of which, the writing overall was great, the story was good even though I feel like some plot points could have been elaborated on in a bit more detail. The comic relief in the game is stellar, although that might just be because it panders to my sense of humor. I'd describe it as "unhinged."The gameplay is fairly solid, despite its basic nature. The most complex part of the game is timing your dodges with enemy attacks, which can get quite difficult as the game throws harder enemies with more health and more vaguely telegraphed attacks. There's also the thing where you call upon a teammate to attack an enemy with their respective element to break elemental barriers. The elements that enemies are weak to are easily figured out, especially since when finding a new character, you are put into a situation where the game essentially teaches you what the character is strong against. However, I am extremely conflicted on how to feel about the endgame. This kind of ending alone can ruin the experience for some players, especially with how the game is structured. I personally feel like the ending was too serious, as I remember the comedic and lighthearted moments more than the plot-important "we're in an apocalypse let's get our s**t together" moments. Just know that the ending hits your emotions hard, and this is a good or bad thing depending on who you ask.Overall, I do think the game is worth its price tag, even more so if you happen to find it on sale. If you like hack n' slash games that can be a bit mindless fun or the social elements of the Persona series and dating simulators, this is a solid buy. Just be aware of the ending being a "you either love it or you hate it" deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights.. where do I start, the game I originally called a bootleg Persona turned out to be overall a fun time, with many good aspects going for it, but with some expected downsides and jank. In short this game is about a group of teenagers/young adults trying to save the world from being destroyed while learning more about themselves and what they truly want from life. Many of the characters need to face their past and fight for the future with their heads up and we as the MC are here on a ride with them.(I wasn't going to make a review at first, but the Dev post about this game and its development, made me want to rethink my choice and add my feedback.)And now (no spoilers)The good -Characters - This is a definite strong aspect of the game, each character has their charm attached with relative good character writing/development, I haven't found anyone I disliked or someone that I couldn't understand where they are coming from, it very much hit that scratch for a recovering Persona addict in a much shorter factor.Story - Although it wasn't anything groundbreaking and the ending was a somewhat expected turnaround, it was decently paced with emotional key notes here and there, each character brought in a new view of the story with how the entire situation affected them and their personal stories were the strongest aspect of the game.Voice Acting - To be fair, this elevated the two point above A LOT both characters and story are fine on their own, but the good voice acting (I played with English VO and a bit of Japanese) really cemented it. Most lines are voiced, but not all, the lines that are not voiced are usually filler conversations during the passing days or dialogue after doing extra activities with your confidants. Overall a very good effort here as well.Story animations -  They were short and sweet, but made with good quality, I would definitely would love to see more of them, but I am happy with what we got.The Decent -Gameplay -  For me gameplay was alright, there was jank but it was playable jank. Combat itself is fine and easy to understand and master, but eventually you get in a very monotonous cycle (The final fight was for the most part just annoying) Early on you mostly try to perfect dodge, do your basic combo, fill the bar and do your QTE, later on you unlock more skills and abilities that allow you to be more aggressive and it makes the combat cycle a bit more fun.Character Design/Animations - Nothing crazy here again, but it worked well for what it wanted to achieve with its characters. Animations were often similar, and the QTE animations got stale quickly.Music - It did what it had to, didn't blow me away, it was played where it was needed. All the Yuna tracks were a very nice touch and the ending song was a joy to listen to.The Bad - UI - It does not ruin the game, but the UI could be a little better and more responsive, especially while trying to save or load your progress. I will add that I was experiencing controller delay issues in this game, I would click on something and it would take it a few moments to realise, I played both on M+K and the controller, and overall the controller even with the delay was more enjoyable to use.I had fun with this game, I will come back to 100% it later via NG+ but for now I am satisfied with what we have received from this game. Also huge props to the Dev, I heard that it was basically a single dev effort and the credits very much showcased how much work the Dev put into this game. I hope that the good aspects that really made this game work get expanded on in future projects!7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS NOT A HENTAI GAME: it is a clone of persona + Souls-lite combat ... and I greatly enjoyed this game!All the best parts of persona, but none of the warts, it is a little content lite but that makes the game comfortably bite-sized, and the ARPG combat pacing & mechanics are some of the best I have seen since Nier. Don't mistake that I am comparing this game to Nier Automata, because they exist in completely separate weight classes, as this game is true indie project from a Korean solo developer & is very bare bones ... I am taking about the first Nier (and not even the remaster: this is daddy Nier on the Xbox 360 / PS3).Rough visuals: check.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ plot: check.Character writing that steals the show: check.Bleak ending: check.Action combat that takes timing and skill: check.Borderline bullet hell bosses: ehhh ... there are some parts, but mostly Dark Souls type arena battles.Environmental puzzle dungeons: check.Not for everyone: check.Not every game has to be a 90 hour epic with an open world the size of Texas, redundant fetch quests, a cast that is triple digits in size, eye porn visuals, and makes you climb flagpoles to scout the world map. Eternights packs everything it needs into a "good for a weekend" package. It has rough edges and I wouldn't mind seeing a remaster + extended content release at some point, but first I would like to see Eternights 2 & 3.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game.  Great graphics, great story, great characters, and some absolutely intense combat.  The Dating Sim parts of the game are really focused on developing relationships with the other characters.  Developing this relationship with the other characters will give you skills to use in battle, as well as stat boosts.Gameplay: The main loop is to go through the stages/dungeons, kill enemies, a boss, all before a set time limit is reached.  When you aren't fighting you'll be busy trying to improve your relationship with your companions.  Combat: A bit Dark Souls-ish, with timed blocks or dodges followed by attacks.  Enemy patterns are relatively easy to get down, though it can be difficult when you're in a crowd.  Combat only gets better as you play and upgrade your skills and companions.  Your companions are there to help you with different attacks or buffs, but otherwise just kind've get in the way.  Level design is the part of the game that probably could have used the most polish.  While combat is highly enjoyable, the levels themselves too often consist of corridors and hallways.  The pacing, I think, is exceptional so you'll move through the game at a pace that won't have you focusing too much on the levels.Stat upgrades and skills are all meaningful and worthwhile.  I do wish there was a bit more of an indication on how much you're improving vs what you need to reach the next rank.  It's also not clear on what you need to unlock the final date with your companion until you've gotten close to the point you can go on dates.The dating sim part of the game is far more of a relationship builder than dating.  I don't think there is any way you can fail, as all of the companions are pretty eager to date you.  It's PG-13, so don't expect any lewd stuff.  The characters are well written, though I think I second guessed their interest in me far more often than I should have.  The benefits of spending time with your companions and scavenging is entirely worth it for the stat boosts.Scavenging is... Kind've weird.  Each night you have the opportunity to scavenge for an item your companion wants, or train with them to increase your standing with them.  The Scavenging part is weird because you go to the same 3 locations.  It seems odd that the group didn't come together and make a list of what everyone needed and then make one trip to get as much as possible.  It also pretty much consists of running around and interacting with specific spots to find something.  The locations typically make sense for the objects though.Graphics: The anime portions are very well done, and the characters look amazing as well.  The enemy designs are well done, and once you're good enough at combat you should take a peek at them to admire the design.  I do have a complaint that your companions will often get in the way during fight scenes, and the fact everyone is wearing similar colors means you might go after your companions instead of enemies.Voice acting: Top notch!  The level of emotion you're able to get out of the characters at all times is fantastic.Sound/Music: Game has a pretty good soundtrack, and good sound.  The ending song is fantastic, and a bit heart wrenching.It's an emotional journey, and definitely one worth taking.  Some of the best written characters I've had the pleasure to spend time with in awhile.  It's hard to put the game down once you start playing.  The ending was emotional, and really makes the whole experience memorable.  I really hope we see more of the Eternights universe.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights is very clearly inspired by the Persona series, which is best indicated by the calendar "system" in the game, improving social stats, and ranking up confidant ranks. Now, the calendar system is honestly irrelevant in this game. It is completely pointless knowing what month and what day of said month is, whatsoever at all. The only relevant thing time-wise is how many days you have before you have to beat the next dungeon, but you don't need a calendar to tell you that. Hell, the calendar will say, "1 day left" but you'll actually have another day on top of that left.Social stats are upgraded by talking to (training with) your horny homie, and by picking certain dialogue options. Now, let's get onto the combat of the game! I will be speaking from my experience of playing the game on the highest difficulty it has. It's decently done, but it's not particularly fun. It consists of you dodging at the right time, but the timing for dodges makes absolutely 0 sense, and spamming x. The enemies with "barriers" require you to use your elemental attack, which is just a QTE slog, because why not? ♥♥♥♥ should've just been an animation, not some boring ass QTE that you have to do repeatedly. The parry skill that you can unlock just sucks ass, and the only useful skills are the dash attack, and deathblow. The range attack is just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dash attack. The aoe attack is mostly pointless, since every group of enemies will beat your ass if you aren't in dodge mode, which makes using a skill pointless since you're better off spamming x. The other skill is just an eyesore, and it made it more difficult to see attacks to get the timing to dodge right.I honestly wouldn't recommend playing on the highest difficulty, because it just isn't fun. I was more annoyed with every boss, but they were never particularly difficult to beat. They were merely chores to deal with, and the timing to dodge almost every attack makes no sense. One thing to keep in mind is that the game tells you to dodge when a red circle appears, in order to pull off a perfect dodge, but that is actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There's like, maybe 2 enemies that actually works against, and the rest you have to base on their attack either being about to hit you, or far before it hits you. Hell, if you try to base your dodges off of the circle against one of the first bosses, then you'll just keep getting ♥♥♥♥♥ slapped, because the circle doesn't even appear until he's hitting you. The worst part about the combat is that you have to build up energy in order to pull off your QTE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ against bosses, and certain enemies with barriers. You gain energy by perfect dodging, and finishing your attack combo, but you have to do that 3 times just to start a QTE once. The QTE is far too long considering if you ♥♥♥♥ up even one part, then you've failed to break the enemy's barrier, and now you have to regain energy again. God forbid you accidentally used the wrong element for your QTE attack. Granted, I only failed a QTE like, 4 times throughout the whole game, but it caused me great annoyance every time. Honestly, it's just tedious.To put it shortly, the combat is action-rpg button mashing with QTE's. The dungeons and level layout of the game are very similar looking, but that's to be expected from a game taking place in a city. There's a decent amount of enemy variety considering how short the game is, and the character models/graphics look fine for what the game is. I don't particularly care about graphics anyhow, as long as a game doesn't look like complete ♥♥♥♥.Now, how about the story and the characters? The characters are decently made, but you don't spend too much time with the characters. Honestly, the game is too short to actually make you care about any of the characters. The story itself is just dull and uninteresting. I didn't give a single ♥♥♥♥ about the story whatsoever. It just kind of exists. It's your typical, formulaic, gotta stop said person/god from ending the world, who's being helped by someone who lost a loved one, and was promised that they'd be able to reunite if they help. The dialogue is occasionally funny, but for the most part it's kind of just eh. Oh, and ♥♥♥♥ the unskippable dialogue. Why the hell is that a thing?The music in the game is also eh. I almost immediately tuned it out and started listening to my own music. The original Korean voice acting is solid, though. All in all, the game is a mixed bag, but it's entertaining enough to play for like $15. I give Eternights a 6/10. It's a kind of good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Persona franchise. Do I love it enough to make a video game just like Persona? Perhaps, but this team certainly does and they went and did it. Much love, much respect. This is a small team asking for $30 though, so expectations must be set and managed. This game is rough around the edges, but there are diamonds here. In my 10ish hours, I’ve only dealt with 2 or so crashes, and some minor menu bugs… that’s it. Delightfully surprised about that. When it comes to experiencing the story itself the world-building here is abysmal and makes no sense, but I was having fun with my new glowing sword and new crush so I just went with it. Will it be the same for you? Who knows. Now that I’ve crossed the finish line I look back and nothing still makes any sense and honestly, that’s okay, the characters and combat made it worth it.As for the combat, it’s fun. A lot of the depth is pretty front-loaded. So a handful of hours in and you’ve basically mastered all the mechanics with no more roof to break higher. It's satisfying to engage with breaking shields and using special moves and will clap your cheeks in expert mode if you don’t get adept with parrying. As for the characters you have your best bro and 4 romance options. I’ve only pursued Yuna so far and I felt like it was decently fleshed out. The setting for this game isn’t exactly the most appropriate for puppy love dates but hey I’ll take my pop-star dates where I can take em. My biggest gripe with the cut-scenes in general is the cuts. These cut scenes will just end abruptly, with music and all, and onto the next section of gameplay. There are some pretty heartfelt moments that just drop off when the game decides to move on, I hope they fix that.That’s all I’ve got, looking forward to their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆Eternights, oh boy, where do I even begin? This indie game completely blindsided me in the best possible way. Initially, I have to admit, I struggled a bit with the gameplay, particularly the dodging mechanics. But here's the secret - stick with it, and you'll unlock a world of gratifying gameplay.The learning curve might seem a bit daunting, but trust me, it's perfectly balanced. With each passing hour, your skills naturally improve, and before you know it, you're gracefully sidestepping obstacles like a pro. That sense of accomplishment and growth is what keeps you utterly engrossed.However, what truly sets Eternights apart is its captivating narrative and the lovely touch of romance. The game weaves a story that not only pulls at your heartstrings but also leaves you with that heartwarming, fuzzy feeling inside. And yes, it even had me shedding a tear or two by the end; that's just how emotionally immersive it is.Let's talk endings - I can't help but wish for some DLC that would offer a more comprehensive conclusion. Don't get me wrong; the existing ending is touching, but it left me yearning for more. Maybe an expansion that ties up loose ends or explores alternate storylines would be the icing on the cake.My personal journey through Eternights had me choosing Yuna as my steadfast companion, and it led to an ending that was not only enjoyable but also had a touch of sentimentality. The character development and the chemistry between the characters are nothing short of masterful.As I eagerly prepare for a new game+, eager to explore fresh storylines with different heroines, I can say with certainty that Eternights has etched itself into my list of the best indie games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. If you have a soft spot for heartfelt stories, a sprinkle of romance, and gameplay that keeps you on your toes, Eternights is an undiscovered gem that deserves your attention.
