_childDocuments_.review: This game found it's way to me via the r/Persona subreddit, being branded as "a story inspired by Persona 3". The persona series lives in my heart, and Persona 3 is my all time most favourite game I've ever played. That being said, I have a couple of things to say about it:The story is really well done, very high quality for an indie, and one of the only stories that actually made me cry since Persona 3 (not even kidding)it's not very long (10-15 hours) so don't expect a Persona length game.You can see some inspirations from Persona, Final Fantasy and perhaps other game series that I've not played, but to call them a clone of any of them is flat wrong.While the combat is unique and fun, it's also not completely consistent. Dodging boss' attacks tends to be a lot more difficult - parrying the attack instead can help, but is just as inconsistent.While I think some tweaks here and there are in order, this game is amazing. If you like Persona, I think you will like this.8/10, definitely in my top 50 games ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights is a hack-n-slash JRPG-like with elements heavily inspired by the Persona franchise (the director, Jaehyun Yoo, openly admits the franchise was a big inspiration, and it shows). For the first time, I have been motivated to to an in-depth review of a game, so here I go. Warning, spoilers ahead!Story:Well, this part is definitely not Persona-like! In those, you're typically a Japanese second-year high-schooler arriving in a new town by train, and through various highjinks end up in a mindscape made up by the collective unconscious, and end up shooting God in the face.No, Eternights' story is honestly closer to a mainline Shin Megami Tensei game, where you the protag are living your normal everyday life, when BOOM! Suddenly some crazy apocalypse-style stuff goes down, and now the world is a wasteland infested with monsters, and bee-tee-dub you now have superpowers and it's your job to save the world.The story is pretty standard fare for a JRPG, but is considerably shorter than you'd expect. My first play-through only took me 12 hours, while a Persona game (sorry, I know I keep comparing this game to Persona, but it's hard not to) typically takes me around 100. I honestly wish the game had been a bit longer so we could spend more time with the characters. Speaking of which...Characters:The cast is pretty small, with your core team made up of six, including the protag. You're the only one doing the fighting, though, with the rest acting as support (healing, shielding, etc) and helping you out with your finishing moves on big enemies.Like in Persona games, each party member has a social link, which you can improve by spending down-time with them. There a seven ranks in each (except your best bro/wing-man, Chani, who only has five), and each rank unlocks their skill-trees further, the skills of which you can buy with either White Essence (used for support skills, earned by spending time with party members in either training mini-games, or scavenging essential resources from nearby buildings) or Black Essence (used for combat skills, earned by defeating enemies, or occasionally hidden in secret locations in combat areas).Also like in Persona games, you only have a limited number of days to do things before you have to continue on to the next plot beat, and with two time slots per day (day-time and night-time). And, I'll be honest, I don't think you have enough days total to max out all five characters in your first play-through. You see, this game also borrows Persona's social stats, which you can improve by picking certain dialogue options, or by training with Chani (which takes a time slot). And each party member requires you to max out (level 4) one of these stats to unlock their rank seven link, In my first play-through, I only managed to max out ONE stat (with several days worth of help from Chani) so I could romance the character I wanted (btw the choice to romance a character happens during rank 6), with my other 3 stats sitting around 2 or 3. I can't see a way for it to be possible to max out everyone in one play-through (or at least, without an EXTEMELY precise guide to follow). This game does have New Game Plus (which I haven't checked out yet, probably should have before I wrote this), so hopefully you can bring your levelled-up social stats into NG+ (again, like Persona)Gameplay:Like Persona (yes, I know, broken record) the gameplay is evenly split into two parts:First half: Japanese dating sim with mini-games galoreSecond half: Hack-n-slash dungeon-crawling JRPGThe first half sees you spending time with your various party members. During the day, you can improve your social link with them, unlocking more of your skill tree, and at night, you can go on scavenging missions with them, collecting various items the characters want, and earning White Essence in the process.  Also, during either time slot, you can instead train with them, to earn more White Essence. Each character has their own training mini-game, and they're all relatively challenging. Amusingly, Min's mini-game is a squats competition, and before you ask, yes, it's exactly the same as the one from Final Fantasy 7 (not sure about the copyright on that, but I hope nothing comes of it).The second half of the game is the combat. It's pretty standard as far as a hack-n-slash JRPG goes: mash the attack button to build up your combo meter, then unleash a more poweful final hit with a quick blow. Dodge roll out of the way of incoming attacks; dodge with the right timing to slow down time to allow to unleash a flurry of blows on your target. Once your elemental meter is full, go to town with a massive QTE-powered finishing move, flattening standard enemies and breaking shields of more powerful ones. Use SP for support skills from your party members; healing, shields, various different attacks, etc. I saw someone in another review compare the combat to Scarlet Nexus, and honestly that's not too far off. The combat can get a bit tedious towards the end of the game, when you encounter enemies who can't be hurt by standard attacks, so you have to wait for them to wind up their attacks so you can dodge at just the right moment, slow down time and break their guard. I played the game on Easy mode, so I don't really want to think how annoying the combat gets on the higher difficulties.Conclusion:The game was an enjoyable time, and felt worth the price of admission. If you're a Persona fan like me, and need something to tide you over until P3:Reload comes out next year, or you're just a fan or JRPGs in general, I highly suggest giving this game a go.

_childDocuments_.review: There's an age old addage, you can make a pizza so cheap that no one will buy it anymore. Personally, I've yet to find this line, but I assume it's out there. Eternights asks, Can you make Persona so cheap that no one wants it anymore? And the answer in this case is probably not. Judging from the credits sequence, Eternights was made in large part by one dude, Jae. With that in mind, this game is extremely impressive. The level of polish, the breadth of gameplay, it's all so incredibly impressive for one person to make. Compared to a giant like Atlus with SegaSammy's money behind them, the fact that this even laps at the heels of persona is incredibly impressive. The characters are for the most part likeable, the art and animation are strong at the best of times and still servicable at the worst, and the combat is interesting enough for a short game. My hat goes of to Jae, as well as the phenomenal voice cast they got for the english dub.That being said, a lot of corner were cut to make this game, and the evidence is everywhere. Scene transitions are more often than not abrupt and awkward, the combat is repetetive and shallow, and the love interests waste absolutely no time trying to get into your pants. If the game had a larger budget and a larger team, then they might have taken the time to flesh out interactions and take it slower, but currently the relationships consist mainly of the love interests telling you their problems, and then largely solving them themselves with you just kinda in the background saying you believe in them. The story moves inconsitently, with the ending coming our of nowhere at a suddenly breakneck pace, capped off by a lackluster boss fight where you don't even get to take down all of the boss's health. I'm looking forward to Studio Sai's next game, I very much enjoyed this game for what it was, but it isn't without it's flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT: This is not Persona. It doesn't play like Persona, it doesn't act like Persona, it is NOT Persona.Beyond both being anime style and having companion conversations, genuinely don't know where people get all those Persona comparisons.So that, most important, thing aside, this game is really lot of fun.MC is a pervert (he can be kind of serious, but seriously, just be pervert, it's much more fun), his best friend is one as well, there are a lot of anime tropes, but dialogue walks a good line between funny and wholesome. Some scenes of talking to girls are really nice with basically no funny comments or perversion, just 2 people talking about their lives and world that's ending.Combat is, well both simple and good, but also sometimes really frustrating.I like simple combat when it's done well. Eternights mostly has good combat, decent amount of combos, but it also has very, very, VERY repetitive bosses with too much HP.Boss fights require learning basic understanding of their movement, which is good. What's not good is that making a single mistake often ends up with losing 75% of HP because boss fights also tend to have "Multi-attacks" which chain protagonist. As in, first hit knocks back, while still in the air 2nd attack lands, knocking back again, which ends with 3rd attack also landing.Normally it's a 3 stage attack where you need to dodge 1st, then 2nd, then 3rd attack in succession, but when one lands, all land while all you can do is watch helplessly. Losing control of player character for few seconds and watching whole HP drain at once is not fun in the slightest. This is my biggest pet peeve in games and is definitely a negative here.Compare it to any Souls game where if you get hit by a boss you're definitely in trouble, but you can recover and avoid in time. You don't get control of character before all attacks are finished by enemy here. That aside, I'm enjoying my time with the game, having a good laugh or chuckle very often and liking the music beats during exploration and combat.Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, ignore my previous review on this (which was positive still but yeah), since doing NG+ for the rest of the achievements my views on this game have changed (for better or worse, idk). Let's get the negatives out the way first: - No text fast forwarding like Persona and a lot of the cutscenes just aren't skippable (some are), even if there are no dialogue options included in them. Makes replays a bit tedious, won't lie, despite a rushed playthrough only being like 5 hours. - The combat, while not bad (especially as you unlock more stuff) is still very repetitive. If you want it to feel a bit more fun, download the cheat table for cheat engine and enable all the combat stuff, it's fun. - How tight the free time is. There is LITERALLY zero room for error if you're after the full bond achivements. Waste even 1 day with an extra hangout and you can kiss it goodbye. - Previously did state the dungeon design was bland (along with the puzzles being bad, which I take back), but after replaying the game have come to appreciate them more. I mean, it's not like you can do much better for apocalyptic dungeons. They're a lot better than let's say SMT 3's at least.- The way the whole story starts off with the Eternight canisters just exploding out of nowhere. Feels cliche imo. Wouldn't mind if it was someone who went to attack those canisters to make it happen, but... yeah. Idk why it just doesn't sit that well with me, BUT, the rest of the story makes up for it really. Very good. - After rewatching the ending(s) I've come to appreciate it a lot more, I just wish there was more to that post credit scene where you meet your lover again. - Still not that big a fan of Sia tbh. Again, S-tier design (one of the best I've seen for a girl in a JRPG in recent times tbh), but still really annoys me how overdone her eccentric science nerd personality is. And her romance feels like the most unnatural one tbh, it's cool, but not the biggest fan of it personally.Other than that though... I still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it. Good story, very lovable characters (Yohan best romance, fite me), nice OST, good voice acting, better dialogue choices than Persona sometimes, the fact they even include a gay romance. Yeah, it's REALLY good. Only really let down by the negatives, so the best I can really give it is a 7 or 7.5/10 at best. Was actually my most anticipated game of the year and did not disappoint! Might not turn out to be my GOTY in the end, but still really enjoyed my time with it :)

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where most games are bloated with content, averaging around 37 hours, Eternights felt rather short seeing how it is about 12 hours or so to finish the main quest. I felt the game would have benefited from a longer story runtime, maybe about 20 hours? However, this game is made by a very small studio and I think its their first game so the smaller budget and team does explain the shortcomings. Don't get me wrong, I loved this game since I played the demo and I may or may not have pushed back other responsibilities so I could fully enjoy this game. The story of teenagers fighting evil with superpowers is not exactly a novel idea but Studio Sai has put an admirable spin on things. As I mentioned before, the shorter story does tend to wrap up some story plots rather quickly or vaguely but it's nothing too serious. The game shines when it comes to the character portrayals though, I was thoroughly invested in each of the character arcs, if you like Persona confidant style companions then this is right up your alley. The social sim aspect worked pretty well and there is room for replay ability with the new game plus feature. Even when you're not trying to romance everything with a pulse, the character interactions feel realistic like how friends would really react in some situations. Studio Sai got some big name voice actors to fill their cast and they certainly delivered, (Miyuki Shirogane as Yohan?? Count me in).The combat is pretty simple, not too much variety in your move set and I am okay with that. I didn't buy this game to learn a laundry list of combos and fighting mechanics. I would go play DMC if that was my intention. But simple does not mean easy, if you cant get the hang of dodging at the right time and predicting enemy feints, then you are going to be on a one way trip to failure town especially on the higher difficulties.Overall, I would give this game a 7/10 if it came from a big name company owing to its length and some design choices that I don't completely agree with. But considering this is the first game by the developer, this game is easily a 8/10 maybe even a 9/10. I am excited for the next game Studio Sai puts out, they have a ton of potential!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright where to start, this game overall is a really fun and enjoyable game with a story that kept me entertain all the way through and character that i fell in love with. _childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: If you were into the trailers and the demo, this game is pretty much what you'd expect. The story goes in some interesting directions and the voice acting is surprisingly really good. I've found myself interested to find out about each Confidant's backstory, but it definitely doesn't seem possible in one playthrough. The good news is that Eternights is a relatively short game that's begging for at least one NG+ playthrough for reasons you'll find out towards the end.The game is a little janky though. The text and the menus feel really barebones kind of like placeholder text/menus while the actual ones were being worked on. They're functional, just not particularly nice to look at. For the most part, the minigames are also disappointingly simple or boring along with the puzzles. The puzzles are not explained/introduced that well, but they're simple if you look up a walkthrough. Sometimes the dodge also fails to register. Most of the time, it's because I wasn't holding a direction to dodge in or my timing was off.Overall, this is a pretty good game that's "swimming in 7s."7.5/10Full disclosure: I am currently just beginning the final dungeon at the time of review.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative yes based on a little over two hours of play.If you like Persona, but with about 25% of the storyline and 10% of the production value.. You just need something to tide you over, or are just extremely bored.. Pick it up.The reason I say this is because, the plot is like a book, except you're missing about 50% of the chapters and you're just kinda left to fill in the blanks, also movement outside of combat is very clunky, the camera is kind of annoying and the environments and enemies are very copy pasted.Also it was apparently made by one person, so pretty impressive, hence the yes.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: I finished my first playthrough, and I gotta say, for an indie game (and for what it costs) it's a really good gameThe story is your tipical JRPG stuff, apocalypse and everything else, but it gets good in the final act, the combat is simple but engaging (even though it gets kinda repetitive halfway through, every boss-fight revolves around the same gimmick and the fights are not really challenging as long as you can heal (which isn't done through items, but only through an ability)The characters are okay, some are clearly more fleshed out than others, though, and some are annoyingThis game is clearly inspired by Persona (specifically persona 5), the social sim aspects are called literally Confidants and Social Stats, they are divided into ranks and unlock abilities as you complete them, some ranks also require you to fight and they're all fully voicedThe game lasts around 9:30 hours and has a new game plus but I don't know what carries over and what doesn't

_childDocuments_.review: I am about halfway into the game (on PS5) and can honestly say I am extremely impressed with how it turned out. _childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Eternights is a sometimes clumsy, pretty dorky, very charming game, and I mean that in the best possible way! I love discovering games like this, and it has become one of my favorite games this year.I am an ARPG enthusiast and that is initially what drew me to Eternights, but besides enjoying the somewhat simple but satisfying combat, I really love the characters as well. There may only be 3 waifus available which might seem too few for a dating sim, but they are each unique and fun to interact with. The dialogue and options are also sometimes hilarious and adds to the experience a lot. Overall, I greatly appreciate that the devs didn't try to reinvent any wheels and stuck with a solid design. All of the systems in the game feel familiar, approachable, and fun. Not saying that I don't like inventive ideas, but my main goal playing video games is to have fun and be immersed, and I'm always thankful for devs who focus on balancing that aspect over everything else.There were some downsides of course and the lack of experience and/or budget definitely pops up here and there, especially with some scene transitions feeling very abrupt, or animations looking awkward, but I was able to overlook these and just enjoy the game.I wanted to keep this review short and sweet and to support the devs. Eternights gets a thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. The humor is what you'd see in an anime, and the facial expressions made me laugh a lot. Combat system is simple and highly dependent on timing to fight enemies well, which was easy to do when I found the right time to lookout for. I loved the characters, none of them had anything in their personality that made them unlikable or annoying and the story was entertaining enough that I decided to just finish the game. Its plot felt like a mix of apocalypse/magical girl/shoujo/horror type to me, which was interesting to play. You're pretty much playing an anime, though one without as much censorship around a character's sexuality and relationships. I found that a really nice difference and the main reason I decided to purchase and play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe there's a QTE to hold hands with the girl.Is the game worth it though? Well, if you can tolerate the shortcomings of the game being made by a very small team, I think you'll have a good time. What I mean by the shortcomings are the combat can be a little janky, abilities might simply target nobody if you're far enough because the lock-on isn't good enough, character animations being a little funny, and the facial expressions can be a bit weird. But like I said, if you don't mind these issues, you'll love it.Despite the game having a time limit system, it is actually VERY generous. The game gives you 14 days to complete the main quest, but you can do it in just one day time and spend the rest of the 13 days bonding with the characters. You don't feel forced at all to do the main quest, as long as you know not to leave things in the last minute.The game is also very dark for some reason. I know the world is ending so people aren't putting lights on, but my god, I have to turn up the brightness scale almost all the way up to see things better.Unfortunately, if you're playing on kb+m, you're going to have a hard time. The game doesn't have mouse support in menus, and the game seems to be designed with controller in mind, with how you have to press RB + A or LT + A to do stuff, and this also applies to the other BXY buttons as well. And there's also no customize keybinds option.Personally, I find this game to be worth it on sale at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Some people will say this is a Persona game, but they really made this unique in some ways, plus the story is way better and the ending hits harder, the combat mechanics are pretty solid minus a few minor issues with dodge timing. Great game 10/10. I went for the Yohan route with no extras so I'm not sure if that changes the ending but it was a really good ending. Also the puzzles in the game are rather simple but also somewhat complex in some cases, great balance with the puzzles I think.Watch through to the end of credits for a little extra video when you finish. Credits are short, and the extra video makes more of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: Hack-and-slash mixed with time-management dating-sim.[+]   The dating portion is pretty enjoyable, the bonding events do a fine job at fleshing out the various waifus and developing your relationship to them.[+]   The combat is pretty fun, simple but satisfying with lots of flashy moves and upgrades. Although it does have the occasional jank to it.[+]   The social activities are pretty varied, they can range from: simple dialogue events, surprisingly difficult minigames, and even combat encounters.[+/-]   The 2D portraits look very nice but the 3D models can sometimes be a bit rough.[+/-]   The story can be kinda all over the place, quickly jumping from one thing to the next, but it all has an earnest charm to it. A charming persona-esque game with fun action and great waifus to date.
_childDocuments_.name: Eternights

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, it's a SOLID 9/10 for me. The main complaint I have is the game is too damn short, criminally so. I want MORE of this game and the characters. I didn't expect a game of this short of length (10-11 hours for me) to make me emotional for the ending I got but it destroyed me for a few hours after. The music is catchy, beautiful at times and impactful when it needs to be, the boss music, credits and(Small Music/Character Spoilers:)  especially. Characters are great which is to be expected from a game claiming to be a love story to Persona games and it doesn't disappoint in that regard. The dialogue is good and funny, very much like Persona games, so if you like being a smartass or a perv in those games you will certainly find it here. Combat is fun and satisfying but can get repetitive near the end of the game, I actually struggled a bit on some of the bosses on normal difficulty, having a hard time reacting quick enough to the dodge timings feeling too short or inconsistent from boss to boss and some enemies (the shooter ones especially) but some more time with the game retrying them or in NG+ on Expert which I plan to do would likely make me better at the game's combat which I don't hate at all. Sometimes though the story scenes or exposition dumps stop too soon, feeling left with confusion on what just happened or wanting more from explanation in them, but liking it overall. Usually I'm one to always play on Japanese voices when playing JRPGs or games of that nature but for my first playthrough I went English since it was actually good, the voice actors do a great job and doesn't feel inferior to the JPN voices at all atleast for me.The game doesn't stay long but it delivers an impactful story for me, one that feels very similar to (Persona 3 and this game ending spoiler) , if you know you KNOW. If it wasn't for the game being so short this is easily a 10/10. The shortness doesn't detract from the game but for me it makes it hard to give it a 10/10 realizing the potential it had if it was just a BIT longer. That would allow more room for character moments and just more immersion in the world and exploring more characters and things in the story/setting of the game to make the endings have a bit more punch to it (Not that it doesn't have that already, in fact the opposite). Despite that the first ending I got which was Yuna's hit me like a truck (if you know you know), I assume it's the same for all the characters which I will find out in NG+. Much love for this game <3

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a great time with Eternights.For all the "professional" reviews stating flat characters, I found the entire cast rather human in fascinating ways. The storytelling is sometimes abrupt, and it does move quite fast, but I like many of the questions it poses about a number of topics; I connected to this in more ways than I expected, although I do wish there were more room for these topics and interpersonal relationships to breathe.Now I'll get to the parts that made the game frustrating; I generally play games like these as a means of passing time and relaxing, so I tend to go with easy mode with that in mind. In Eternights combat does not scale appropriately to the easiest difficulty level and I often found myself dying repeatedly until I got acquainted with the flow of combat, something I didn't exactly enjoy when I intended a stress free experience. Additionally, utilizing your companions' abilities during a fight against a group can be very difficult to get right as a result of how they are laid out. There's an especially aggravating motorcycle segment that is incredibly fickle with collision detection and involves crashing into obstacles until you've memorized the entire segment, compounded by a near constant struggle against visibility throughout the game. I often felt directionless outside of some visual signposts that are sometimes lacking in clarity. Visually the game is appealing, but I would have liked more detailed character models, or perhaps a more unified blend of retro stylization to complement the models themselves.All of that aside, I think Eternights is an innovative spin on the the Persona formula and as an effort by a very small team it has a lot to offer. The humor is well coordinated with its more severe moments, and the growth of its characters is well worth the grievances that frequently accompany indie titles of this scale, but rarely does a game like this aspire to reach the same level as higher budget releases and succeed in as many ways as this one. I have a feeling whatever Studio Sai does next will improve exponentially on what Eternights does in one way or another, so definitely give it a look and support the developer for their hard work.

_childDocuments_.review: Full discloser, This is a game done mostly by one guy so i'm more inclined to be positive than nitpick. The TLDR is Scarlet Nexus but with actaul payoff for the "social links" that doesnt take it self too seriously wich makes the final act and interactions more impactful for me personally.It's not going to impress graphically, musically its competant but outside the ending song not really stand out. Game play wise its actually kinda rough, punishing reaction based hack and slash that doesnt really have much nuance ouside of picking for slow mo perfect dodging or parrying. There's a couple bits where you're suppose to avoid/run away from the enemies that are annoying but didnt give too much trouble and overall this game can be blitzed through in 6-8 hours 10 tops if you're prone to leaving a game running while afk. The best way i can say is that its charming for what it is and I hope the dev has a bright future with any other projects. If there is one thing about the writing i'll pick at is that the game's last act comes off as pretty rushed but this is pretty typical with mostly solo projects so it didnt quite bug as much as it would in a game by a big studio. I'm left wanting more and that's probably the best thing a game can do to you when all's said and done.

_childDocuments_.review: I have problems with this game's way of showing the story so far, but I do not hate it. My main problem is with your friend Chani, if you look at his illustration you can see he's thin with long hair and sleek eyes. While I haven't seen all the models yet, Chani's is the most atrocious. It's a disservice to the character. The model looks nothing like the illustration not even in the slightest. It's so weird when everyone else looks normal, but he has a weirdly chubby face and completely different eyes from everyone else. So about the story. My main gripe is with how they just do not tell you certain things. Especially the puzzles, there is no warning of them and then they don't even give you a mini pop up tutorial of how they work. The character "Aria" is the most confusing so far, as we don't know anything about her, but she just knows the whole situation? How does that make sense? Really feels like she was just pushed into your face and you know nothing about her, just to have that one character that gives you your quests. All in all it's not terrible and I will be doing all of the story to max, bc I like this and want something to pass the time. I don't know if many people would like this, as there's already discussions on the writing of the characters that people seem to dislike in the demo they put out before this came out.

One day, something, or someone, has turned humans into dangerous monsters. All that interests them now is violence and power. They are what stand between you, a cure, and the world you want. name: 9 Years of Shadows
detailed_description: 9 Years of Shadows is a side-scrolling Metroidvania by Halberd Studios. Travel alongside Europa, a brave warrior determined to enter the mechanical giant Talos and stop the corruption within before it swallows the world in darkness. Battle through tainted creatures, meet charismatic musicians and uncover the truth behind the curse that robbed the land of all color. Many have tried to venture inside the twisted depths of Talos, a dormant fortress where several civilizations have settle over centuries. And, after losing everything she held dear, Europa has nothing holding her back from attempting what others could not achieve. As a noble fighter who refuses to be bound by the curse, she must enter the castle, find the source of corruption, and return the color once and for all. This adventure is not for Europa to face alone. Inside the giant, she befriends Apino, a cute floating bear who seems to possess magical abilities that can restore color and replenish the health of his allies. He is also able to shield his companions from the multiple dangers that roam Talos’ hallways. While exploring the castle, Apino can cleanse the corruption around Talos and shoot a variety of projectiles that can destroy dark crystals and inflict damage: A fist that punches upwards when conjured. A blast that travels along a surface until collision A cyclone that returns to Apino like a boomerang. Use the elements to your advantage to travel the map dynamically. Acquire the elemental armors that were once treasures to ancient civilizations and change on the fly and unlock special abilities to traverse your way: from swimming against waterfalls to traveling underground tunnels or gliding through warm air currents. Harness the power of lightning, water, earth, and fire. Surprise bosses while you switch armors, perform strong halberd combos, and exploit your foes’ weaknesses to pave your way through the heart of the shadows. Music is all but the soul of the game. Revitalize the world while you listen to a moving soundtrack composed by Miguel Hasson, as well as soothing pieces scored in 432hz by celebrated composers Michiru Yamane (Castlevania series) and Norihiko Hibino (Metal Gear Solid series). Meet these guest composers as in-game NPCs who aid in Europa’s quest throughout the game. Music is the binding thread that combines gameplay and storytelling: collect musical notes and perform a healing lullaby to restore your health.

_childDocuments_.review: As a 'metroidvania' experience  is a fairly straightforward example. It's not too long. It's not too complicated. And to seasoned platformer veterans, it's not too difficult (with one notable exception).  It doesn't really break the mold in any particular fashion so you can't really go wrong if you just want to have a new metroidvania experience for a few days.First and foremost, the art style is gorgeous. Animations are crisp and smooth. Character design is a treat. Pixel art is on point... there's a lot going for this game visually. It is very pleasing to look at.Gameplay is relatively simple and straightforward. There's no level system to grind out and only one 'monetary' resource that I always had plenty of whenever I needed it without any excess searching.  There are a number of upgrade collectibles (of which there are just enough to complete every upgrade and it's not an unreasonable amount) though none are all that difficult to find and even the secrets are often exposed by careful study of the map- though there are no markers to determine if any given collectible has been obtained or not so you'll have to search them out for yourself.Some people have complained that combat can get repetitive. I can see where they're coming from, but it was never a real problem for me. On the whole it's not that difficult. The bosses can sometimes throw you for a loop but once you figure out  how they work you should be able to defeat them. That is, of course, with the sole exception of the final boss, who was a significant spike in difficulty and took me several tries. He did go down, but it wasn't always clear what you were supposed to do to avoid certain attacks, and the final phase is straight up sensory overload. Most of the upgrades you'll be collecting are traversal and movement upgrades, leaving this game very linear. There is almost literally no way to sequence break as paths are often locked behind traversal requirements. I'm sure some speedrunners out there could break the game, but that's not my specialty.The story leaves a little to be desired. In short it's about coping with loss, pain, and betrayal. There are relevant themes to take away but it's not always clear on why things are happening. There's a lot of worldbuilding with a whole lot of 'fill in the gaps yourself' as some questions are never answered. You won't have the world's lore spoon-fed to you, but at the same time it's not so difficult to understand as, say, a game like .  There were a few points where I would have liked some more answers (the main character even lampshades this at one point but is immediately dismissed without an answer) or a little more expounding on the relationships between certain characters so that the big reveals had more of an impact. I believe they tried to do that via gameplay but they never really go into detail as to why the mechanic works the way it does and so it just comes off as 'part of the game' more than 'part of the story'.  Also, some more expounding in the nature of the relationship between the main character and  would have been nice. I feel like that was a character that could have had a greater impact on the story but we're only given hints that the two characters are on rocky terms despite facing a number of trials together in the past.  For a game about dealing with pain and trauma the main characters seems to be very dismissive of this other character's issues as toxic despite him giving no real reason for it other than him being a bit overbearing/demanding- and not to an unreasonable degree. It's hinted that there's more to her coldness towards him, but we're only given two scenes with the character and it simply wasn't enough to flesh it out.  Also in regards to the main antagonist (real spoiler ahead);  So that's a little personal pet-peeve, but maybe that doesn't bother you as much.  If you didn't want to read the spoiler, the TL/DR is that I feel like a large part of the potential consequences of the story is glossed over and/or ignored, and it kinda bothered me.As for outright cons, well... the game can be a little buggy. Don't start to load your game and then focus on a different window or the game might not load properly. Don't dive-kick onto the edge of a passthrough platform or you might softlock yourself (happened to me twice) and for heavens sake, don't die after defeating the  until you've returned to talk to the  otherwise you'll lock yourself out of completing the quest. I had to do an entire new playthrough to get the achievement because the game auto-saves after you defeat the enemy but if you die before completing the quest it acts like you haven't beaten him yet, but he does not respawn, leaving you unable to complete it (according to the forum this is a known bug that hasn't been fixed).And because I know some out there will ask: Is it 'woke'?  On the whole I'd say 'no'.  At least, it's not overwhelmingly ideological in nature. There are some elements if you squint and look real close- most notable being some nods that certain characters are LGBT, and of the six male characters in the game one is the main antagonist, and only two really have a shred of masculinity and one of them is painted as more an antagonist than anything else despite only vague explanations as to 'why'. On the flip side none of the female characters are painted as anything but friendly, open, helpful, and competent- with one sole exception inasmuch as one of them comes off a bit airheaded. If that sort of thing bothers you, well... can't help you there, but it wasn't a focal point or anything so I wouldn't consider it overtly ideological.It's a soft recommend at the end of the day. Watch a playthrough if you're curious. The health system can be tricky to get used to but I never found it overly difficult, especially if you're good with reacting to audio cues. I'm not, so using the 'quick-heal' was almost never an option for me, but I always found a way to recover some health as long as I studied the boss patterns and personally I appreciated always having a means at my side to regain health once I got the hang of it.  None of the platforming will make you want to hurl your controller out the window. At the same time, you may not find yourself coming back to this one for repeat playthroughs. There's no speedrunning achievement (thank heavens) and there's no 'missable' items so you should be able to go through the entire game without having to worry.It's a good game to sit down, spend a few days with, and enjoy a gorgeous -if somewhat shallow- experience.  I genuinely hope to see more of this world in the future though, as I feel like the worldbuilding left enough open questions that could make for some interesting answers if explored.

_childDocuments_.review: I find the art the strongest point of the game, a lot of attention to detail, I’ve never played a game with such detailed pixel art. I’m not experienced in metroidvanias, I’ve played just a few. What I like about 9 years is that it knows how to introduce you to the mechanics while also making them challenging as the game progresses. Has a nice story with entertaining cutscenes. I personally love the NPCs and their quirky personalities. Overall a fun game with amazing art.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the video game equivalent of something like the Law & Order TV series. It does nothing great, pretty predictable, and ultimately boring.I got about halfway through before I basically fell asleep at my keyboard.If you need a basic platformer to shut your brain off that isn't really going to challenge you, then sure, this might be a game for you. Otherwise, save your money and go buy Death's Gambit or something.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Solid if short linear metroidvania game. Tries some interesting things with combat and healing, with an action reload-style timed heal and elemental modes that can pierce shields or hit weaknesses. It's a strong QOL benefit that you automatically enter the element that's needed to protect yourself or interact with the environment, but that cuts two ways since it also makes it feel more cosmetic than anything. Your element slightly affects your attack pattern, but making them more distinct and allowing players to pick one to specialize more into would have helped. Still, while I don't think the execution was perfect, I appreciate trying things. Worth a look if you enjoy this sort of game.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if it's just me but, it feels like it's trying to be a game that it's not, some of the mechanics reminded me a lot of Hollow Knight but, with a twist. I found it cute but, the health system is interesting. I bet if I gave it another shot maybe it would grow on me but, as of now it feels dull, it feels like it just took a bunch of mechanics from other games and put twists on it.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is clearly a love letter to its many genre predecessors. Its vibrant locations and snazzy soundtrack, as well as the sheer variety of its gameplay elements – and how each elemental armor is utilized for both combat and traversal – make it very easy for me to give this one a resounding thumbs up. The storyline is a bit of a letdown and I could’ve done with more fast travel options, but frankly, I don’t play these types of games for their narratives, and the somewhat tedious backtracking is hardly a deal-breaker, either. If you’re at all interested in well-made metroidvanias, 9 Years of Shadows is a game I’d highly recommend checking out.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly fine metroidvania.The art is gorgeous. The story is simple but at the same time the lore of the game is obscure. Most of the npcs you find are musicians and even Europa plays the piano at save points. Two major characters are painters. What is the importance of music and art? It fits with the theme of returning color to the world but the game doesn't delve upon it either. Europa is missing an eye. I was expecting that to come up in the story. Maybe the eye that was covered was special somehow, but it never comes into play; it seems it was simply an easthetic choice of her design.There is a character that appears in the opening cinematic and appears to have a history with Europa, but it's touched so superficially that it becomes absolutely forgettable. I can't even remember his name, in fact, and i just finished the game.I wish the map showed you where you found items and where you collected them, a la Metroid. At the end of the story I was missing a blue note and can't for the life of me figure out where unless I go through the whole castle again, which wouldn't be fun.Mechanically, I would've liked that the elemental abilities had more applications in combat, not only in traversing new areas. Other than that, it's competent; there isn't anything particularly innovative but what is there is fun to use.My worst criticism is that, for a 2D metroidvania, it crashed on me an ungodly amount of times. Hopefully that gets patched eventually.All in all, my experience is positive and this is a great first effort for the devs. I'm looking forward to what they can put out in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, there are alot of things to like about the game, but ended up being a pretty large waste of potential I thought. If you are crazy about the genre(like me) mebbe get it, there is some good there. I thought the game was gonna gonna be fantastic for an hour or so, but as far a recommending it...nah, not me.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my rather short time with the game 100% it. Is it a pretty game? Yes. Is it fairly short. Yes. Difficulty pacing is okay, but I would have liked more of a ramp up in difficulty towards the end. I'm glad this kickstarter game was able to come to fruition, as I've seen other kickstarter games come through and be a disappointment (I was not a backer of this particular game), and it appears it met most of its promises.I would call this a precision platforming game that's fairly forgiving and contains some minor metroid style backtracking, but not much. There's really not much incentive to go over the areas you already went if you were careful the first go around. In fact, there's only one optional upgrade that I remember having to map into my backtrack and it was fairly easy to snag while going through one of the later areas.I only had one crash, and I'm pretty sure it was due to a CPU voltage issue I've been having, wasn't a CTD from the game itself, but otherwise had no issues playing the game. Would have _really_ liked a way to skip boss intros, especially on subsequent attempts, and a way to skip elevator scenes or speed them up.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is a short and sweet game.  I'm pretty new to the whole Castle/Metroidvania style having only played Hollow Knight, Gal Guardians (Grim Guardians) and a few other titles outside those. I finished the game in 10 hrs with 98% because I couldn't be compelled to backtrack for 1 material to get my final upgrade and look for all the lore. I sort of enjoyed playing this especially since a friend sent me this as a b-day present.I'm beating a dead horse but everyone's main gripe is the crashes in this game. I received it after reading the recent patch notes saying they fixed some of the things causing it, so I had high hopes. The game is going to crash on you at any moment. I feel like every moment I play, I have to speedrun to the nearest save room because I'm always at risk of losing progression. Not by dying, no by the game deciding it doesn't want to work anymore. I even had it crash loading up the main menu. It's laughable. The only other bug I experienced outside of that is one that I've only encountered during the final boss whose fight is obnoxiously drawn out. Sometimes, for whatever reason the projectile attacks were invisible. How are you supposed to fight someone that uses invisible attacks? I dunno, didn't think I'd have to face that. I also encountered a black screen bug. Luckily, I navigated my way to a save room. Saved and it went away. Other than that, I don't recall any other bugs.Gameplay/Progression: Elemental armours give you abilities to travel certain terrain and bonus damage to matching affinities. The bonus damage is only +1. Not much of incentive to match affinities outside of that +1 bonus.   Your shield doubles as a mana gauge which is unique in itself. Although I never used magic unless I had to fight an enemy that could only be defeated via magic or if I was doing a puzzle. Upgrades are simple, health, armor, and mana. After upgrading my armor, I was ready to expand on my power and abilities. I was left with a +1 damage boost to matching affinities and 2 handfuls of useless currency and wishful thinking. There is very little incentive to backtrack as you've explored everything after making your round through that zone. Despite how minuscule the map is, I sometimes wished for a fast travel between the save points to cut down on wasted time. The elevator only does so much after I've rode it 30 times and I stare at the screen only for "..." to appear for 10 seconds.Art & Music: Thumbs up, listening to how the music would change in the theater with each musician you found was cool, not that I ever stuck around other thank to check off quests and make my way to the smithy.Overall: 7/10 I didn't have to buy the game. The game is too simple and leaves you yearning for more in the wrong way. There's no reason to scour the map for secrets unless you really want that 101% or you're looking for that last upgrade. The crashing and bugs don't help this game that much either. I had high hopes and was let down, can't recommend this game to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Apino (teddy bear) mechanic is very interesting. This companion serves as health shield that can be recharged and magic ammo all together, so if you spam  it you'll end up exposing your real life bars which are just two hits away from death at the early game, quite challenging versus bosses. So, although common enemies may seem easy, you'll have to watch your health not going too crazy and saving it for the bosses.For the people wondering about colors, the black and white demon encounter at the start of the game may not be the last one. Also, for me the story seems to talk more about overcoming grief and other negative emotions to be able to return color to your mental life maybe. I see it referenced by abilities and even the great music that seems to be tuned to the famous 432hz frequency.About the art, the style is quite unique with reminiscences of Saint Seiya coming from the golden armor details and also Castlevania nostalgia. The pixel art is beautifully crafted and illustrations shown in dialogues are exquisite too. I can't wait to have the artbook. Animations change pretty fluently between armors and there are a bunch of them, wow. The Mermaid one is real fun!
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: If you like SoTN, you'll love this. Movement is great, combat is great. There is only one main issue, and it's how the health bar works. Sharing your HP bar with an ability you have to use constantly is super annoying. And the "quick reload" feature sucks since it becomes a small bar above your character instead of just using the main HP bar your eyes are already used to focusing on. It's literally the dumbest "feature" of a metroidvania I've seen. Like... why? Just... why? It makes for really crappy combat situations where the boss won't leave you alone long enough to hug the stupid bear, and because you expect the quick reload to show up over the main HP bar and not above your character, it's really easy to miss. The rest is great so far.Another stupid problem: You can't hug the bear when you're in mermaid mode, which is so painfully annoying. You're trying to dodge the stupid water boss, but because your HP is tied to that stupid ass bear attack, you basically just run out and have to dodge forever until you can barely find a window to recharge. If you attack an enemy, it slowly recharges your bar, *unless* your bar is completely empty in which case, nope. Gotta hug the bear. Still can't believe this is how they implemented that feature.Also, if you die at a boss, you have to watch the opening cinematic every, single, time. You can't skip it at all. It makes getting back into the fight so painfully slow and kills the pacing.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Very Beautiful game and very easy game. (And I mean extremely easy.) Main reason is because of Apiino and his mechanics. Without him, the game sees a bigger spike in difficulty, but by then - the game is almost over. Still not hard even then.It's a great ride though and I still recommend playing it in hopes that it'll give the creators more funding to make a bigger and longer sequel or DLC to add more things.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is a fantastic game if you like the genre. I did enjoy this game a lot. It is not without flaw though, so let's get into it!The visuals of this game are absolutely gorgeous. The movement feels good, and the (melee) combat is fast and satisfying.Most of the characters are pretty interesting. The story is nothing to write home about, but it is a solid one nonetheless. The soundtrack is good, although you would probably expect something more action oriented, it still fits the game. With an average playtime of 8-10 hours, i think it has a good lenght. It's not over too fast but also doesn't overstay it's welcome. -Boss introductions are unskippable. It gets rather annoying to watch the same cutscene mutiple times if you don't beat the boss on the first attempt. -The ranged attack feels awkward to use, since it is rather hard to aim. It also drains your "light bar", which sort of also functions as your health. You may call that a risk/reward kind of deal, but becaus of that I rarely even used it unless i really had to. -Backtracking is an absolute nightmare since there is no teleportation/fast travel function. It can take ages to traverse the map if you weren't thorough the first time. -A certain change to the health system near the end of the game which i will not go further into for spoiler reasons. If you know, you know i suppose =PWhile this may sound like a complain a lot for stating that i really enjoyed the game, know that i would call none of these flaws a dealbreaker. Minor annoyances at best. Except for the last point. That was really bad.7.5/10, would recommend at a discount. :)
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Good game on the whole. Great artwork and animation though the music is ironically kind of... just there? It's not bad, mind you, but not memorable. There are some apparent technical issues which I imagine will be patched out soon enough. Control is smooth and easy to grasp and the platforming so far is actually pretty good! It's a solid metroidvania with a what is so far, at least, a decent story and accessible (but not pushover) difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this metroidvania. The graphics and music were top notch which created a world I kept wanting to return to. Gameplay was smooth, but I do feel like the upgraded abilities could have been pushed further with some more difficulty in platforming and boss fights. There were about 20 bosses, but only a handful caught my attention and forced me to learn attack patterns. The sea serpents and final boss displayed the potential these encounters had as they were tough, intense, fair, and exciting. These are only minor complaints, though, because I couldn't put this game down. 9 Years of Shadows is very good metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: First this out of the way, Overall its enjoyable, graphics are of course the highlight the style amazing. Controls are not that bad except the dash or back dash is not even useful honestly. story well is limited but serves okay. There is at least a purpose to why you should keep going. Gameplay is good, I enjoyed it. Game is linear and if not used to this type of game, great introductionThe nitty gritty. The controls can be fluid when it wants to and complete mess when it happens. The section when going room to room and switching forms is great, Dynamic and feels good to use since it has a auto function between earth water fire. The mess when combating enemies the main one the chess boss. Honestly you dont have to you can ignore the same ability damage increase but if its in the game as a highlight I have to try and its a hit or miss. The charge attack is useless, the back dash is honestly useless. the mash attack button is all you need so it gets repetitive. Story is limited like the genre usually is using only notes, some dialogue to fill the story through environment. Honestly its serviceable. I like the little interactions between the spirit, the self thoughts in the elevator, interactions through musicians that lets Europa have a personality thats actually progressing. The side characters is hit or miss, twzii is adorable, musicians and painters are there not the greatest reason but they exist, the villians have good design although towards the end you meet not villains and I guess you end up killing them???? except for 2 but the rest no impact I guess. Mentor was eluded but honestly it kind of jumped the gun in the end before the end. maybe a dialogue in between to show a progression in change of personality or obsession  so when you meet again the player goes yep guess its inevitable not like huh that escalated quickly or in a self reflection talk about her training days and how the mentor ambition was started to flare.music is passable there is a track I like as it is soothing, ambient and serves the style of game and atmosphere very well, would I call it a banger no but it serves the game and tone and that honestly is more important even though I may not play it on my own time separate from game.It it linear so honestly I would call this game easy overall, i kind of just tanked everything and rush past enemies at times. The mana and health system. hmmmm all I can really say is sure. Did it make sense, ya, did I exploit it ya, was that intended probably not. It is a cheesy system to pretty much be invincible. well until the end but it was an experimental system and it wasnt as bad that most people make it. You get use to it and honestly makes the game easy. which is probably not a good thing but game is built around it. mostly.....In the end, it is a enjoyable game I would call it a beginner to metroidvania style game play

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous visuals.Nice controls and overall gameplay feeling.But...Classic metroidvania should have at least a way to go.One option to show it is obvious, like show the global map, and the marker on an uncharted territory. Another option is to lead the player to an obvious obstacle, like a tall wall, with a way over it, and then when the player gets an ability to climb walls - they remember where to go exactly.This one - is just an open-world "metroidvania" (is it? I'm not sure still). You are free to go anywhere. Where exactly do you need to go? You don't have to go anywhere. Just explore. Go there, and then left, and then there, and jump over. Well, you have got nothing. Don't you like gameplay so far?I - don't.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I think you should buy it! I think the game excels in a lot of things: - The art: is just amazing full of colors, and original and interesting - The music: Just amazing, the best of the best - The lore: Even if i wasn t expecting to be pay too much attention to the story, it actually is a really good one. It s engaging and it really helps to get more into the game - The controls: they are extremely responsive and feel rewarding when used - The bosses, they are unique an fun, each one of them feels like a totally new battle - The map, i think is amazing and you find since the start a lot of "i need to come back later in the game" spotsOverall a great game, i do believe there is a some work to be done to the minions (refering to the normal rooms mobs, they tend to feel repetitive when you have to kill the mobs every time you cross a room).
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, but there is just one thing that straight up killed it for me. The upgrades you get are so BORING, except the water upgrade which was kind of fun. It's a damn shame because i was expecting other upgrades to be as neat, but they weren't. The rest of them don't add any change to gameplay at all. They are all just a "now you can go here" abilities. It's a shame because it's a BEAUTIFUL looking game. I got over how the HP system worked, it's whatever. Upgrades/Abilities to get places being utterly boring is the real killer IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A true masterpiece of a game. When it comes to Metroidvanias 9 Years of Shadows is a master class on what to do. I was enthralled with this game from the moment I picked it up. The gameplay is progressive but not restrictive, the backtracking is just the right amount. The map shows you unexplored rooms on the map when you return to an area if you're going for full completion. The mechanics of the game incorporate all the titles you know and love while putting their own twist on it. The story telling was compelling and the  art had just the right amount of pixelation. I got this game in a bundle and it just so happened to be the first one due to alphabetization but it was just meant to be. This gem is  well worth your time and money if you enjoy metroidvanias. Thanks to the devs and the backers for creating/funding such a fun experience.On the negative, I didn't run into any major issues other than the game freezing during the final cutscene which required me to play the boss again for the final achievement to unlock. It was an unfortunate scenario but the boss was worth beating a second time as well.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty pixel art Metroidvania with some severe difficulty spikes at some bosses/rooms (The game makes you think at times, crazy i know!?)It's fairly short and consistent in quality, you are highly rewarded for playing methodical and safe rather then bum-rushing everything due to it's unique but punishing health system, observe mob/boss patterns, learn, dodge and prosper! Story is rather mediocre and nothing special but the fluent movement and fun element swapping gameplay with the progression upgrades(Relics) keeps you interested until the end of the game.☆*:.｡.o(≧▽≦)o.｡.:*☆~
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I do not like it. At all. Visually its the most apealing but even then they chose to have a flying teddybear with you at all times that kinda ruins the rest of the aesthetic your armored warrior princess is going for. The game has the health mechanic from Skautfold Userper. That rightfully rarely brought up metroidvania where your attack and health are the same resource. So if you shoot a lot you die. So you never shoot. Just melee attack. Nice. The first drawen boss is awful. You fight him in a tiny room and he constantly bounces between walls. Apparently randomly because on my successful attempt he did do it only once. The game has a music theme, in all npcs are musicians, but the actual soundtrack is so loud and obnoxious that it drowns out the other ingame music.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely solid. Aside from being absolutely gorgeous, the story and characters were well written if a bit simple at times. The combat was a bit simple for my taste, but otherwise it was good. easy to control, all bosses were well telegraphed and fair. Overall I would say this game is on par with the likes of Unsighted or Metroid Dread. The thing I loved most about 9 years of Shadow was that they added in these little sections where Europa would monologe to herself while in the elevator and she would mention things that had happened while she was exploring the castle, additionally certain bosses have different dialogue depending on where your at in the game. Its little things like that which made this game a great experience. 9/10 would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short the game is pretty mediocre.Everything in this game is not really good but also not really bad. The visual effects, music, combat in general, boss fights and the world and story are the definition of average. Nothing stands out as great or awful. It is honestly impressive how they made a game that does not excel at anything while barely being good enough not to bore or frustate one.It's worth a playthrough but don't except anything, especially not a metroidvania. I have no idea who tagged that but game could not be more linear.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Impeccable aesthetics and music. Controls are tight, fluid, and responsive. Combat is largely fairly simple (compared to, say, Hollow Knight), but enjoyable, with boss fights being more complicated and engaging. The game has like 20~25 mini/bosses over the course of a 6-9 hour playtime, so it's rather boss-dense (which is good, here). The Gears of Erebus boss is the only one I have real issues with, in that the only  strategy I can see for it is a cheese strat (and some checking on youtube shows everyone else doing the same, ugh). The final boss is a decent spike in difficulty from the rest: it took me 6 tries, mostly due to the third phase (which unfortunately has enough randomness that it sometimes  you to take damage), while every other boss took 1-2 attempts.There technically is a plot and setting, but the game is very light on details for both, it's mostly vibes-based.Also, for some reason the Olympian Strike/Dive move (the dive-kick thing) is explained extremely poorly by the game, to the degree that the explanation is actively misleading you.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficulty spike near the end.Can't recommend it due to the final boss being basically a sudden bullet hell. Upgrades I had all, only to feel at this boss like they have done nothing at all to help.This personally ruined the game for me, I love Metroidvanias like this, but I already avoid Soulslike tags in such games because I am casual, but games that turn out nice only to make you angry after a while because the balance is crap, that I can't stand anymore in games.Seriously, game devs, stop it with such sudden spikes or use a difficulty setting as an option. Some people just want to relax and enjoy the story and atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Falls short of greatness but still a worthy entry to the genre at a good price.A Metrovania on the surface, this game shares a lot more in common with Megaman than Castlevania—both in terms of gameplay and length. No RPG elements are present. For those who like to grind and overpower the game SotN style, worry not, the difficulty is easy to mild. Power-ups aren't particularly interesting, but are fun enough. The controls are extremely tight. Superb pixel-art graphics, but a surprisingly forgettable soundtrack for a game which puts such a strong emphasis on musician side characters. Similarly, a serviceable but forgettable narrative is good enough window dressing for the gameplay. Many, many nods to genre greats—which don't really add to the experience. A clear love-letter to games loved by the developers, but one that doesn't seem to have it's own identity. Europa is a great character design, would like to see her in a follow-up where the developers take a few more risks. As of this writing, quite a bit buggy with at least a dozen game crashes on my way to clearing the game. One final crash occurred during the rolling of credits. This may be intentional rather than a bug, but often an enemy that you should clearly be able to jump over would create an invisible wall forcing you to kill it to proceed. Extremely annoying and unnecessary. I'm assuming this was a Kickstarted game, there are a lot of seemingly random portraits and statues of what I assume to be donators. That, coupled with the inconsistent art style of some of the character portraits does take me out of the game a bit. I can give it a pass for that, but I'm assuming some of these bosses were also donator-designed, given that many are entirely skippable and do not offer any sort of reward. That is a huge negative for me. At the very least they could give currency. Killing bosses for zero reward feels really deflating in a game like this. Overall, plays excellent and is short enough that it doesn't feel like it's wasting your time at any point. Worth a look just for the art alone. Hope it gets a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually stunning! Every room looks carefully crafted and inviting, particularly the Save Room! For as long as I have played it, I found the combat challenging but rewarding, and it is nice to keep track of it in the Bestiary! I love Europa and her personality, she's very relatable as a character, and the NPCs are interesting and refreshing; Apino is just the cherry on top; I liked the lullaby mechanic (though I still think it consumes too much time to perform). Finally, the soundtrack was engaging and boosted the atmosphere a lot!
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked?- The art and music were great. - Movement systems based on elements were fun.- I love Europa's style and characterization. I actually looked forward to hopping on an elevator to hear more of her thoughts.- It wasn't too long. Minus me going for 100% it was relatively linear for a Metroidvania, but I didn't mind. It didn't overstay its welcome. My big complaints? - No teleportation meant a LOT of backtracking to get items I missed in out of the way places. Had I read spoilers I would have waited to get the final movement skill before doing all that...- The final boss was kinda bad. The difficulty spike was very jarring. A lot of attacks were almost impossible to dodge with how fast these massive attacks were overlapping each other. I breezed through most of the bosses killing most of them on my first or second try. I fought the last guy probably 20+ times before I took it down. Watching older footage the boss seemed to go down in less hits and do far fewer attacks in the final phase!If you're looking for a decent action platformer with some cool style I'd recommend it. If you're looking for a 40 hour epic Hollow Knight experience this isn't it. If this is the studio's first game I will definitely keep an eye out for their next release (which I see is listed on Steam right now).
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically a very fun game with challenging bosses held back a few small issues. No teleport makes looking for trophies a chore and and finding secrets just isn't worth the time to run through the whole map with out it.Unfortunately, the story is a bit disjointed and never really comes together in a satisfying way. You meet few characters throughout the game but there is no meaningful character development and they don't advance the story. The game has lots of bosses and some were quite challenging. The art direction and music are great and work well together.I recomend it 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Looked pretty, nice music and atmosphere, however the gameplay is lacking. All of the movement abilities are restricted to their respective coloured rooms. The Active Reload makes the game baby easy from after the second boss until they take it away for the last 2 where it becomes impossibly difficult. There's only 6 types of enemies throughout the game, but it's fine becuase there's also....30 bosses. Which would be awesome if the combat was interesting and diverse enough to warrant it.  6.5/12. _childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: You'll probably see a lot of comments saying similar things, and it pains me to not recommend this game simply because I feel like it was well-made but there are core mechanics which make it un-fun.Upgrades aren't exciting, you get 4 different "elements" which change your appearance and give you a new ability (like the ability to travel through small tunnels, or float through the air) but it doesn't change your moveset. Every "element" gets upgraded 1 time and it's hardly noticeable if it really does anything.There's no fast travel, so if you forgot something, you are running all the way back.There is a huge difficulty difference between bosses and random enemies. Random enemies pose absolutely no threat whatsoever, bosses are only challenging because the heal mechanic in the game is miserable. And if you die, you go back to your last save, so if you forgot to save before a boss you might be replaying a lot of boring content.The healing mechanic works like this, you basically have a "gun" (no spoilers) that can shoot, but it's ammo is tied to your health, so as you shoot you loose health. Once your health runs out you are vulnerable, if you are hit when out of health you lose 1 of your (originally 2, eventually 4) hit points. Once those are depleted you die. Now when the health bar runs out initially you can "time a reload", but if you miss it, you have to stand still and hold a button to get it back, during which you are super vulnerable. Basically if you miss it on a boss fight you are unlikely to have a window to get it back. Doesn't matter much because for some reason, most bosses are immune to "shoot" so you're just spamming the 1 combo you have on them.This metroidvania really isn't worth your time. The nice things I have to say about it is the art and music are great, but the gameplay is frustrating and boring and the story was impossible for me to care about.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: - Many of this games' mechanics are poorly done and some are not explained at all. For example, some enemies give damage if you touch them and some are needed to be jumped and stood upon in order to advance in the game's areas that are unreachable via normal jumps. - Upgrade materials are few and far between but are absolutely necessary for upping your damage output. Without them you are at a serious disadvantage. I wish that it was not such a stark difference in damage output in between having them and not having them.- There are areas in the game only reachable via special portals that are not marked on the map but there is no way to mark them on the map in order to backtrack to find them again. Same goes for areas with sub-bosses that you need to beat in order to advance and/or obtain crucial upgrade materials. - ***SPOILER ALERT*** For a majority of the game your health is directly tied to your projectile energy and this is so badly put together it makes certain encounters beyond frustrating. On top of that, they change this system entirely at the end of the game completely altering how you are supposed to approach combat after you have in all likelihood spent hours finding a good way to utilize the ludicrous default health/projectile energy system.- I have never played a game that has had bosses and sub-bosses that are bullet spongy to such an obscene amount. It truly beggars belief.- A majority of bosses have attacks that are unavoidable which when coupled with your health being attached to your projectile energy often can create a highly frustrating experience.-The story is pretty bad, cliche and forgettable. There is really no reason to care about any of these ridiculous characters or what situations they are in in the game. If story is important to you then good luck finding one of any merit here.I play a lot of Metroid-Vania style games, and they are rarely perfect/without fault but it has been a long time since I have had such a bad time playing one. Congratulations to the developers on that accomplishment. You would be wise to avoid this if you are looking for something fun in my opinion.Had I known you need every single one of the game's currency for increasing damage output to a normal level in the final boss battle I admittedly would have had a less stressful time but I ended up beating the final boss with essentially a 50% damage output handicap. It was the antithesis of fun, to say the least, especially when you consider these bosses are the biggest bullet sponges I have seen in any game that I have ever played in my 30+ years of gaming.All that aside, good music and art style are the only positives I can give to this clearly poorly thought out game.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I could definitely tell the last 20% of the game was rushed. The first 80% of the game is pretty was. I've played a few metroidvanias but I'm no master and these bosses were pretty fine. Then the end game came. Specifically the last orchestra boss and the final boss felt very cheap. Logon had attacks with no telegraphs that you just had to tank and the final boss arena seems extremely anti fun. Overall, this game has beautiful art and music, fine enough gameplay, and a God-awful difficulty curve. I did enjoy this though.
