_childDocuments_.review: I played quite a few metroidvania after I played Hollow Knight, but consuming so many so fast burned me out a bit. After a while since the last one I played, I came across this title, and it caught my attention because of its aesthetics that reminds me a bit of the anime of my childhood, but more precisely a Knights of the Zodiac mixed with Sailor Moon, and honestly I really wanted to play it. This is a metroidvania where we’ll embody the role of Europa, a young warrior who tries to fight against the curse that has plunged the world into the shadows for nine consecutive years. Along with a furry ghostly companion, and a repertoire of powerful elemental armors, we’ll make our way through the corridors of an enigmatic castle in order to restore color to reality.The  begins as a tale, and shows us that the aforementioned curse suddenly spread at some point, sweeping away everything in its path and stripping the world of its vibrant colors. That fateful night changed the life of our protagonist forever. After the death of her parents at the hands of this evil, Europa decided to start her journey, entering the castle of Talos; this is the place where, according to rumors, the plague that took everything away from her began.Taking control of the character, we’ll wander through the mysterious corridors of the fortress while we defeat enemies and learn some of the game's mechanics. Along the way, we'll encounter an enormous monster, who will demonstrate abysmal strenght. Without being able to do much about it, she will succumb to the attacks of the unknown being, losing the encounter and her consciousness. She will barely survive, and it will be made clear to us what kind of castle she has arrived at.After recovering a little, and lamenting her lack of strength, a peculiar creature will appear before her: a ghost, similar in appearance to a teddy bear, and who’ll be key to the progress of the plot. The encounter between this specter, Apino, and Europa, will bring color back to the surroundings and will give a glimpse of hope among the shadows that surround them. With renewed fervor and a new companion, Europa will plunge deeper and deeper into the castle of Talos. It's a plot that while it has been seen before in one form or another, and is told in small parts, it lends itself to enjoyment and left me satisfied, especially because it has a nice twist, and a beautiful ending.In terms of , we'll have to go through corridors and fight against the inhabitants of Talos, all while solving puzzles and acquiring new exploration skills. Some paths will be inaccessible at the beginning, and we'll have to return to them when we eventually get the means to advance, such as the mythical double jump. However, there are also unique touches to the game, such as elemental armor, which will let us advance through different places. The grace of Zeus will grant us the electric element, and we’ll be able to cause additional damage to enemies that have an aura of water, besides being able to activate electric switches; on the other hand, the armor of Poseidon will allow us to swim and dive in aquatic areas, also reinforcing our strength against fire enemies.Each armor has its own function and attack animations, and being four in total we'll be able to see a little variety in our journey. It should be noted that all of them can be upgraded in a blacksmith that we’ll find at various points in the castle. The combat itself is quite simple: we can jump and dodge backwards and we can attack both upwards and crouching. Something I want to comment is that I was playing it with keyboard and mouse without problems, until I acquired a skill that combined the S key and the space bar, and this made me switch to controller because it was a little difficult (for me) to press both keys in the middle of the hustle and bustle, mostly because of the timing. While I know it is the usual thing to play this kind of game with a controller, I wanted to share this detail for those who like to play with the keyboard like me.In addition to the aforementioned, we'll also have the unique abilities of Apino, our fluffy companion. This curious ghostly being will grant us the power to shoot projectiles at enemies or switches, consuming part of a celestial "light" bar that will also protect us from damage. This bar will run out as we shoot or are attacked, but we can partially recover it by hugging our partner for a few seconds. Also, in the course of the adventure we'll get the ability to renew this energy completely by pressing a button at the right time in a quicktime event; if we fail we’ll have to resort to hugging, which is not so bad either. I want to mention that Apino's powers will also evolve as we find relics for him, and both he and Europa will receive upgrades to the light bar as soon as we meet the enigmatic composers: a band of musicians scattered around the castle. Some of them will have to be rescued, and they'll give us side quests to reward us later. This band will always be found in the theater, a location that we can visit in several areas of Talos, and where we can also find the blacksmith I mentioned earlier.There are several skill relics, moves and secrets to discover, but more important will be the musical notes and armor fragments, as they are necessary for both the musicians and the forger to provide us with their services. And honestly, we'll need them, as the bosses that reside in Talos are quite peculiar and dangerous, each having their own mechanics and rooms where they'll have the advantage against us. I found this section to be the strongest point of the game, as the gameplay is very important to me in this genre, and I quite liked the fluidity of the combat and controls. The  is beautiful, from the environments and pixel art sprites to the more digital portraits and some cinematics. I thought the character design was phenomenal, both of Europa and the musicians and other NPCs, and this section is the reason why I was so reminded of Knights of the Zodiac. The overall atmosphere of the castle is very well done, as the different areas that comprise it have their own artistic touches to differentiate them from the rest, from rooms where we can see the heat captured in colors, to corridors of poisonous fog. I enjoyed seeing the variety and feeling like I was exploring new paths thanks to that. The enemies are also well detailed, from the most common to the bosses, and we can find them in a simple bestiary as long as we have defeated them once.  The  is not far behind either, with various melodies according to the areas or moments in which we find ourselves in. The music itself is part of the theme of the game, and the truth is that I found it a nice and curious detail; even the way to save is by sitting on a piano and playing a short song. It’s no surprise that this section is so good, since it’s played by both Michiru Yamane and Norihiko Hibino, renowned composers that are even in-game as NPCs. The visual and sound section left me with a more than pleasant impression, and I can see the effort put into them, as both harmonize really well and make for a fantastic atmosphere; I found it beautiful, nothing more to say!In , 9 Years of Shadows is a charming metroidvania, both for its narrative and the character development of its protagonist throughout the adventure, as well as for its highly cared-for artistic elements. It has an interesting plot that develops in a very fluid way, an active and fun combat, and a challenging difficulty. I should mention that I would have liked an auto-save system after bosses at least, since I had some crashes in loading screens; this is the only thing I have to criticize the game, to be honest.  But all in all, it was a great experience with a decent length, and I recommend it to fans of the genre, without a doubt!

_childDocuments_.review: The art is very pretty. This is the singular highlight of the game and main thing that they did very well. Unfortunately, not a single other piece of the game hits this mark, let alone a mediocre mark.The gameplay is both not engaging and not challenging I would be ok if it could hit at least one of these marks. The "metroidvania" side of things is nonexistent; it's a linear crawl that you occasionally go left instead of right to pick up a pickup, and the map loops back on itself. The game gives you a damage type swapping mechanic, but frequently forces you into one armor so you can't make use of it the majority of the time. Mid-sized enemies, despite there only being a few different ones, all play the same: do some light attacks, back dash, repeat a few times. Or you can just spam bullets from afar because despite bullets using life, you can just refill the type of life it uses indefinitely without penalty. The armor transformations give you speed, but the game never actually provides segments to capitalize on that gameplay, all the transformation segments are built around slowing you down rather than expressing the movement system they built up. The ones that don't focus on slowing you down you simply hold a direction and let the automation do all of the work.The story is nonexistent, the world building is nonexistent. The game itself still has polish issues, and actual issues. The text display during CGs, including the final end of the game CG, often breaks in various ways including: Text not displaying, text overlapping other text, text displaying in the wrong order. During CGs you can often hear the character still doing things while the CG plays, as it doesn't always lock character control. The mechanic where a bullet slides along the floor frequently will either go the wrong direction, or will vanish entirely upon hitting the ground instead for no reason.7 hours for all but one achievement in this game (maximum light bar), it is very short. It's setup to feel like a retro platformer in many ways, but unfortunately lands dramatically far from that mark. I'd skip and play something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very on the offense as to whether or not I was going to give this a thumbs-up or not. And I probably don't have a lot to say that hasn't been said already. This is a very pretty game.-In excels at squish.-The story was passable.-The bosses I did like were very fun.-I did not hate save rooms placement in relation to hard bosses.-I really liked how almost all bosses had multiple phases whose pattenrs changed up in interesting ways.-I like bullet hell stuff lol.-The UI is basically idiot-proof.-Controls feel pretty tight. at least they did for me.The bad:-Many of the bosses (which are kind of the highlight of the game in my opinions) were either push-overs or very annoying to fight.-The level design didn't do much for me. _childDocuments_.review: I've really been liking 9 Years of Shadows so far, not only on an artistic / stylistic level - it controls perfectly, is imo a pleasure to play, has some nice boss fights, and reminds me of some old 2D castlevania games.The problem to me isn't about the heart of the game itself, and surely far from everyone encountered this, but to name things precisely, I had an unavoidable freeze at the , when obtaining the relic necessary for the continuation of the playthrough.I would have upvoted this game, had I not met this issue, and will do if a solution to this is found; for the time being, good luck to the devs, I believe this is some good work, unfortunately hindered for some players by some gamebreaking bugs and crashes.______Not even one day after I first downvoted the game, the devs were, amazingly quick enough to fix the issue me and some other players, were encountering - quite impressed! So I could go on with the game following that,9 Years of Shadows was indeed very pleasant to play, with many fun bosses, a gorgeous artstyle, impeccable controls, and a nice story, told in simplicity, probably making it more powerful even. A story about loss, grief, pain, and the ability to be free while still carrying the pain inherent to life.I'd have just a few minor complaints about the game:- the absence of teleportation system made it a grind at some moments, when searching for new unopened rooms, then having to backtrack all the way by foot, that was probably the most painful issue I encoountered within the game- I didn't quite get why recharging the energy bar with the lullaby gave more energy than when done with the qte ; would have found more logical that the qte would give more energy - instead of that, the lullaby recharge, giving more energy, didn't encourage to use the qte, but rather to lazily recharge more energy in a safe place- minor detail: the elevator . . . was a bit lengthy when taking it / no possibility to skip the travel scene - but mostly, I found that the "inner dialogues" Europa was having to herself could maybe have been reorganized in another way, because there were many passages where all that would be written was ". . ." heh, but nothing that important- the game was a bit too short to my taste, would have wished for a longer adventureIn spite of these points, I don't regret at all playing 9 Years of Shadows, with its irreproachable gameplay, beautiful musics and pixel art, and appreciated the emotion sifting in a subtle way from the story - all in all found it a game of very good quality, something that may give a taste of things to come from the devs, from whom I'll with no doubt be following their next works.

_childDocuments_.review: an entertaining, but flawed platformer that is wrongfully labeled a metroidvania.why it's wrongfully labeled a metroidvania:while it has upgrades that open new paths it's all very linear and you will never really have to backtrack if you simply mindful about your surroundings. most collectables are hidden behind cracked walls or just in a room behind a platforming puzzle which you have the abilities for 95% of the time. it also doesn't help that you have all upgrades around the halfway point of the game with the remaining puzzles just combining the mechanics of the previous upgrades.the good:- the art is pretty- there is thought behind the characters, but they are not given enough time to breathe- the movement abilities are very satisfying- the HP system used is a fresh breath of air, but a bit rough- enough to collect and explore to make going through areas funthe bad:- the story and characters fell a little short and can be skipped over- the elemental weaknesses are not really relevant apart from a few shields- no forward dash- the bounce is a worse version of the hollow knight nail bounce due to how it controls and isn't reliable in fights- the environment is not used enough to support the story- coins were so overabundant that I'm asking myself if there were consumables that got scrappedthe very bad:- p1 of the final boss has too much reliance on RNG with attacks that cannot be dodged in a certain chain or when you are placed wrong when he starts using them. that makes the final boss who is supposed to be an epic battle just annoying to deal with- gaia tunnels in the boss arena getting in the way if you want to activate auriel speed boost- the observatory shouldn't be absolutely plastered with art of the team/backers/friends. the whole area was just that. too muchoverall i enjoyed my time with it. I got everything, but it wasn't too hidden as I've said at the start. I would've wished for more story flavour through backgrounds and area designs. I wouldn't have recognised the orphanage as such if it wasn't labeled and the characters pointed it out three times. it feels like there were many ideas that got included but not properly fleshed out, most noticeable with the ensemble of very different, almost disconnected characters and the vagueness of the relation of some.since it's rather cheap and has enough playtime I can recommend it, but don't expect a hidden gem

_childDocuments_.review: Okay... I'll err to the positive with this one. As far as a Metroidvania goes, it's competent. Mostly more melodic tunes (think Super Castlevania IV's waterfall area, sorta piano-laden, jazz bass popping through). There's no massive power scaling going on, as you upgrade your elemental armors for small damage buffs. There's plenty of blind exploration that doesn't take long, as you aren't really encouraged to kill things... they drop small amounts of money and you have way more than you ever need since the upgrade system uses so little. Hopping over once you get the double jump about an hour in gets you where you need to go. The"Light Bar" concept is really the lifeblood of this game. It works like this: Your little teddy bear thing provides you a shield in the form of the Light bar. It can be upgraded to be longer, so more shield energy. Without the shield you can take two hits before you die, and it doesn't recharge without some kind of action. The bear can also shoot stuff, which breaks purple crystals. If this were Metroid, consider these shots missiles, and crystals are some variety of red door... there are crystal enemies invulnerable to regular shots, a crystal door to mark a boss, and crystal body parts that will sometimes show up after a boss attack string. So, using your shield to attack the boss leaves you more vulnerable; you can blitz the boss when they're open to regular attacks by firing a lot more shots simultaneously alongside your standard halberd combo, but obviously this is dangerous too if you aren't confident. Two hit deaths while shield is down caught me off-guard, which is pretty cool. To recharge the bar you need to:  - Attack enemies (a tiny bit of energy restored per hit)- Hug the bear (Most of the bar, but not all; you're immobile, can be interrupted, long startup, and if you need to get out of the way, long cooldown)- Get an ability that gives you a one-shot QTE (like Gears of War rapid reloads) immediately on being reduced to 0 energyAll this leads to a pretty interesting risk/reward cycle. You can typically safely launch all your energy into a boss when it's down, then do a cuddle to regain most of your bar before its next attack string. But your timing needs to be pretty tight, because if you hit it hard, it gets more aggressive. Bosses are usually pretty cool. They all have a gimmick, usually some variation of hopping around attacks until they throw on crystal armor or show crystals, shoot to stun it and make it vulnerable to attacks. Just like Zelda, you'll have to use your new ability on the next boss in some way. Sometimes it's stupid, like zipping into a smaller room to fight for a few minutes while a laser barrage pops up on the surface. Sometimes (more than once) you'll be doing Mermaid leaps to dodge lasers. They're often more fun than most Metroidvania bosses because of these light puzzle elements, even if it's over quick. Attacking red destructible items while fighting the boss is the way to get some extra energy while dodging, and if you end up at no shield, finding the right opening to cuddle or hitting the sweet spot to instantly recover feels pretty good.  Finally... the traversal mechanics can be fun. Instead of the usual hopping around a bunch of rooms, a lot of areas are locked away by traversal mechanics, sometimes just for initial access and others always. These include things like the mermaid and snake modes. Mermaid mode was very fun, got me remembering Ecco the Dolphin. You can jet up waterfalls and dive out, double jump into another or through a door. It's fast. The snake mode is way less impressive but usually some kind of shortcut. Sometimes you'll have to solve a bomb puzzle. It feels pretty poorly implemented but it does get you around fast. Double jump kick ability happens pretty early, letting you bounce on things and chain into another jump before kicking again. One of the keys here is that the game switches your armor to the right ability if you're in the situation to use it; if you hit water, you're in water armor. If you walk into a poison room, earth armor. Etc. You'll also chain traversal modes this way; you can leap from a waterfall as siren directly into a snake tube without pressing the form change button again. If you're outside a certain range you DO need to press it again, which is a whole thing with snake form. Anyway, it's functional, and it's a welcome change from just hopping over everything and finding some speed boots 90% through the game like you typically find with Metroidvania stuff.------------------------------The bad:Well... it's fond of wasting your time. It's kind of wearing Metroid on its sleeve a bit too much with the elevator internal monologues. You get the "I'm unsure of myself" Other M crap, all unskippable. You can't mash A cuz the text fades in line by line. This seriously breaks up the pacing. You ever feel like you want to take a longer route because the fast route is stuck in a traffic jam and you'd rather just have the sense of moving rather than waiting around? That's what this does. It's a sign the developers take themselves and the pretty boring artsy fartsy story far too seriously, I think. It's gotta show off the armor equip animation the first time you find an armor too, and says you can hold start to skip, but you can't.  Save rooms are in weird places. I don't mind this... I don't really like save rooms before every boss fight, but I'll tell you now, if you're someone who liked Metroid Dread's stupid habit of throwing a save room in your path literally every two minutes, you'll probably be annoyed with this one. Quest minibosses are typically about five or so rooms away from a save room. Traversal stuff. I know I praised it before, but sometimes it exists just to exist. Really, this is more about level design; I don't care enough about being a mermaid to go through a basically empty room, hop back and forth up two waterfalls, into a snake tube and out into the upper portion of another waterfall just to go up two squares and exit left. Enemy variety. Most enemies are palette swaps with a different attack. You get zombie types, axe armor types, catoblepas types, gun dudes... I guess when you see them you know what they are and there's not a whole lot of purpose in wasting time on extra sprites when you've got a thing you want that guy to do that roughly fits a different enemy archetype, but it really makes exploration very forgettable.Game boils down to this: Traverse simple levels with overly fiddly traversal mechanics, kill same enemies with slightly different skins, solve about one braindead puzzle every two rooms, find level up currently hidden in walls or sometimes just a text entry room, and occasionally fight a cool boss. I've enjoyed my few hours with the game, but I've got a list of other Metroidvanias I would recommend before this one... Ender Lillies, Touhou Luna Nights, Rabi-Ribi, Lost Ruins, Momodora at least. If you've played all those already, this one is a decent consolation prize for something new.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game, amazing graphics and good storyIts maybe not an amazing or escencial game for your collection, but i feel it was good enoughYou can divide the gameplay in two, exploration and boss fights:On the exploration side, you travel through maze like map zones and do some small puzzles. The enemies in here are obstacles only, easy and generic, and since there is no exp or drops there is no point on killing them if its not needed. Still, finding hidden places, getting the collectables and exploring the castle feels really nice On the combat side there are the boss fights, its in here that all your combat skill shine or fail. There are plenty of them, some easy, some hard, some that require technical skills and some other that just need to be agressive. On average the fights feel hard but fair... until you get to the final boss XDThe regeneration / energy system feels overpower at first, but as the game progress it fits perfectly with the boss fight system...The final boss battle is not that hard, but the game changes the core of the gameplay right before you face it, so mostly of your in-game experience goes to the trash, but if you take on him with a cold mind its really not that hard  (i stopped playing for like two weeks then kill it on the first try)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this, but there are just a few too many cons that outweigh the pros. Another reviewer wanted a sideways thumb and I would agree with that, this game isn't terrible or even bad, it's just held back by a few minor things that add up to give a ho-hum overall experience. Cons: - mistakes with the map- huge enemies that can only be hit while ducking and they'll move back and forth and can push you off a ledge or back out of the room, you can back dash but need to stand before and you can back dash out of the room too, resetting their damage- getting hit sometimes causes you to turn around and face the opposite direction, doesn't matter if the hit was from- non-skip-able dialog before some boss fights- lack of health bars on the bosses, they get progressively red which helps some, but a health bar would've been better- generally feeling of weakness, it takes a while to earn upgrades and even then they don't feel impactful- takes even longer to get what you need to upgrade health- the lack of fast travel is nearly unforgivable, there's a central elevator but it's not overly useful- no markers to put on the map to remind yourself to revisit an area/roomThere are some pros too:- good looking game- performs well- good enough use of the metroidvania style, at least from the upgrades aspect- good musicI'm 80% through the game according to my save and I will stick with it, but this will land in my 'less enjoyed' metroidvania titles bucket. I love the genre and didn't hate this game by any measure, but a few too many misses instead of hits.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent metroidvania with very few rpg elements, that shines mostly because of its aesthetics and music rather than any other elements. The gamplay is good, an it responds smoothly, but the thin ammount of content can make the game feel a bit empty. Overall a good game if you are a fan of the genre or driven by the aesthetics of a game. If you are not, however, there's plenty of better games in the genre around there.The Good:+The visuals are gorgeous+The music+The gameplay is good enough+The health mechanic is quite original for the genreThe Bad:-A bit short-Very easy for the most part-Very few rpg elements and progression-Low variety of enemies-Lack of items-Few skills and unlockables-Barely any secrets-A lot of underused skills and mechanics
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice casual metroidvania game. Game isn't super challenging as others but it is pretty decent. Bosses have simple patterns and it's very rare to game over. Music isn't anything to write home to, it's very generic. Gameplay is very straight forward with simple melee attacks, which is the same for all armor types. You have a range attack, but nothing out of the ordinary. Graphics are nice, and that intro movie *chef's kiss*. But other than that, it's a very simple game with simple combat, and simple bosses.There are bugs in the game, so make sure to save often when possible, especially after a boss. You don't want the game to crash on you when you go to another room, which happened 3 times during my gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little surprised by the mediocre reviews for this game. I picked it up as part of a Humble Bundle with no expectations whatsoever and was very pleasantly surprised. It has beautiful visuals and is a solid Metroidvania that's trying some interesting stuff. It's probably not going to blow your mind, but the world is gorgeous and the boss fights are satisfying (if sometimes a little too easy).Also, this game isn't Steam Deck verified, but I played it on mine and it ran without any issues.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good Metroidvania over all. The look and the music are really good! Traversing the world is fast and unique with different forms for different situations. The game is overall not too difficult which is a good thing since this should only take 6-10 hours to beat and maybe 15 hours to 100%.Rating: 7/10 - A good Metroidvania with good visuals and great music.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun distraction if you're really pressed for a MetriodVania. Nice colors, tight gameplay, the armor system is neat (although provides no real combat advantage).I didn't finish it because I got tired of the multi-phase bosses not touching me, and then suddenly wrecking me. Every fight. Despite that, that boss fights ARE cool concepts. It was fun for awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun. lots of little technical issues with misaligned text and UI not doing its job, but nothing game breaking.the art is good, the combat is a bit stuffy but passable. the exploration aspect is somewhat limited, the map folds in on itself very nicely, but there's no reason to revisit much of it. never had one of these games turn me into a mermaid before though, so that's something. the story ends a bit abruptly but it was a fairly good one. overall it aint perfect but it was worth it. some fun ideas here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: So first off, I'll say that overall, YES I RECOMMEND THIS GAME. It's a fantastic game for anyone who loves Metroidvanias, and the abilities just feel great. The graphics are GORGEOUS, the animations and environments are GORGEOUS, the controls are GORGEOUS. Only being able to dash backwards instead of forwards is interesting (and weird at first), but you get used to it, and it works with the enemy mechanics, so I'm happy.There ARE a couple of hiccups that, if addressed, would bring it up from an 8 to a solid 10 for me though: - There NEEDS to be a minimap. Pausing the action every ten seconds to see if I'm taking the right route to get to the room I want to get to gets old, really fast. A minimap would mitigate this quite a bit. - I'm not sure if anyone else is experiencing this, but numerous times when I died and hit 'continue', the game completely froze up and I had to use 'end task' in the task manager and reboot the game. It didn't happen EVERY time I died, but it happened probably about 6-7 times in a five-hour play session. It also happened when I tried exiting to the main menu.Other than those two things, I have literally nothing else but good things to say about the game. Well done, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This is the modern take on SotN that I've been looking for! Progression happens at a enjoyable high rate. I'm about 4 hours in a completely hooked. The mechanics are pretty smooth, albeit with some minor glitches here and there. The first time I loaded up, when I would died, the game would crash. The other minor glitch I saw was with the timing of some sound effects. These are extremely minor issues that do not affect the experience at all.9 Years of Shadows has been a GREAT experience so far. Gameplay is extremely similar to Castlevania SotN but does not have a random drop system. It does have many movement and combat mechanics to find to make up for this. Boss battles (and mini boss battles) are fair and come more often then expected. I'm extremely enjoying my experience, but in terms of unlockable mechanics, it seems that I'm already at about 40% unlocked, which would reflect a 10 hour game. This game has already made my list for top Modern Metroidvania titles. Will update when I finish my first playthrough.Do yourself a favor, if you enjoy the Metroidvania genre, add this game to your library! An extremely fun title with a pixl art style similar to Blasphemous, but without the gore and madness.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that likes metroidvanias but doesn't play a lot of them this game felt great, it's challenging, but not frustrating, it feels strangly-but satisfayingly- kinectic which makes it really fun to play, the combat feels well balanced between it's different attack/defence systems. On top of all, as an audiovisual product it's pretty beautiful, from the beautiful pixel art, the sound design and the aesthetic of the game felt like a love letter to the 16-32 bit era castlevania (which was a great nostalgia boost for me).All around i would say that if you enjoy metroidvanias (and retro gaming), even if you feel they are usually hard to pick, this one is definetly a must play in the catalog. Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous game with some fun combat and absolutely fantastic movement as the game goes on. The only negative I have to say is there is the very end has a bit of a skill jump due to a change in a core mechanic. It's not game breaking and I was able to platinum the game in one save file which was nice.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun game to play for metroidvania fans. It starts out easy but starts to get really challenging with the bosses. Puzzles are fairly easy to figure out, you just scavenge the room for switchs and hit them if you have the right ability. My complaints is the game despite having a decent size map is rather linear. Your paths are clearly layed out for you. You run into a room your not supposed to go yet, well its locked or you die cause of environment. So only one path to go. You acquire your next ability and well you already know that one and only room you couldn't go through before so that's where you got to go. There really just not much reason to explore. Secret rooms in the game are very easy to spot, ether the map tells you theres a room there, or you can clearly see the cracks in the walls I mean your going to go through every room along your way but there is no reason to ever go back and explore old areas other than you got to pass through to get to next area. It just lacks that exploration for me. The final boss was hard as hell but once you beat him there doesn't seem to be anything else to do. No new game plus, or anything. I am also short one achievement but looking it up it seems to be a unachievable at this moment for many people. So if your looking to 100% this you cant. Graphically the game is a work of art, it has very well done and pretty art all the way through. Mechanically it has a interesting system, you start out with 1 health point, and you eventually can get it upped to 4 meaning you can only take 1 to 4 hits of direct damage at all. But you get magic that is both a weapon, a tool, and a force field. If you get hit you take damage from the magic  bar instead of your health. Magic can be regained by hitting and killing enemies, or hugging your teddy bear companion. In fact if you deplete you Magic, you get a little bar that pops up above your head later in the game that lets you quick recover all your magic if you time it right. Pretty much your invincible as long as you have magic.Overall its fun and worth playing when it is on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is....different.I have been playing these type of games way back to the days of Metroid and Goonies II on NES. They all tend to bleed into the same style and rules. I'm not going to say it is a better idea, but 9 Years changes the formula with one bar for health, and mana...and the ability to recharge it from....hugs. Yes you read that right: hugs. Its not easy to explain, so I'd recommend watching a little of the game in action to see what I mean.Honestly I can see where this system can bring a lot of frustration, and if it does then I question how far I will go. But it is finding a way to go against the flow that plagues a lot of Metroidvania style games. So that wins it some props. This is a definite "get on sale game" though. Remember that before you jump.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game. 15 hours on record although not all of them are playing actually.The game has some design flaws. But after giving it a try I actually found myself enjoying it.It is fairly simple, simple mechanics, simple bosses, simple plarforming and simple level design.But I guess that is exactly what I needed. Nowadays I don't have so much time for gaming. An being a Metroidvania lover, having a simple game to spend an hour here or there on my Steam Deck was exactly what I needed an enjoyed. It got me hooked. Not all games need to be super complex and ask you to invest insane amount of hours and checking guides.Yes, there are other metroidvania games out there which are better. But this game is enjoyable and if you like these type of games, give it a try. You might actually like it.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Cakewalk with a pit inside of it.The game is easy, if you've never played a Metroidvania, i would almost recommend it.Why not? The last Boss. 99% of the game can be played through in about 6-8 hours, the last 6-8 will be the last boss alone, hell ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nah.This isn't a case of "git gud" or other ♥♥♥♥ like that, other people also complain about it and it really ruins the entire game imo.i have no desire to replay this game or even finish it, even after a patch that makes the final boss fair. if i didn't knew that other Metroidvanias didn't have this massive problem, i would prolly ignore every Metroidvania after this game.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me wish i new how to make games, so i could fix all the awful game design myself. The art is beautiful! But the gameplay is an infuriating combination of boring and frustrating. The health bar/ammo/shield system is incredibly unfun and irritating, and always drains almost completely empty whenever you get hit. The starting combat (i dont know if it gets better, cause im not sure i even want to keep playing) is simple and relatively solid, but gets really bothersome and repetitive when most of the enemies take about 6 to 7 too many hits to kill, and only have one or two attacks. The absolute waste of the amazing art on a game with such thoroughly unsatisfying mechanics makes my blood boil. It's like buying a Lamborghini and admiring all the sleek design work, only to find out all the engine parts were just thrown into the engine bay. What hurts even more is no dev team to my knowledge has ever gone back to a previous project to fix it's major flaws, so i won't get to see and experience all the wonderful art unless I'm willing to slog through the "game" part of the game. I'd rather look at an artbook for this game than actually play it.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Adequate and playable, easy and repetitive, linear and boring, fun and breezy. You will enjoy this if you are new to the genre and need to ease into the style a bit. I was pretty disappointed and left feeling indifferent though I did enjoy the healing mechanic, the designs of the NPCs/creatures and some of the bosses are well done. The music is great. There's bad writing too. Best played handheld probably. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, a bit on the short side but I enjoyed my time with this game. Graphics are beautifully made.It's a Metroidvania, but you'll never get lost in it. Honestly, the structure of the game feels more like a Mega Man game (where you can't choose your boss lol): short stage - followed by a boss - powerup, repeat.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This game launched along with another platformed which caught my attention and were on my wishlist for a long time. The other one was a complete waste of time and money so this one came as a refreshing breath of air which I desperately needed.Now as I love Metroidvania, this games is very good but something doesn't quite give back the same feeling as the legends Hollow Knight, Ori, Blasphemous, Salt and Sanctuary. But, nonetheless, I really enjoyed it for what it is and would recommend it to someone who finished the aforementioned titles.PROS:- The cutscenes were astonishing as well as how the world is drawn;- Loved the design and the mechanics of some bosses (chess one for example);- The progress is quite linear so you don't have to bother on missing stuff;- The game difficulty is at most Medium so it's very relaxing to play if you don't look for a challenge;- Nice different ways to progress based on the elements, my favorite the water painting and level;- Hidden scattered lore throughout the game which makes you understand a bit the history of the current word;CONS:- If there is no dialogue, please let me skip the elevator. I don't have a powerful computer to stay eons in the loading screen for some animation;- The side quests, lore wise, are not so interesting. "I lost my drumsticks". Well, good for you, I won't fight death in a cursed castle for your sticks my man... I did it though;- At one point you're just gonna skip the mobs completely cause it's not worth fighting them anymore;- No teleport between the zone;- "Fully equipped" achievement is either bugged or not worth fighting for it. I had the bar full and then I miss two things with no indication where I might find them. So not gonna bother hours for nothing.In my case, playing on laptop with controller, I had no crashes like other people complain. Maybe I was lucky.Is this game good enough to be played again? No, but it's worth playing once for relaxation and outstanding visuals. Overall: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is a solid little metroidvania. Fans and newcomers of the genre will enjoy this game. There are some odd design elements (how health and ammo are the same bar) and the lack of autosaving checkpoints in certain sections (like before bosses) is very odd. Then again, it makes the game feel more retro in a way, which is cool I guess but I would've preferred just having checkpoints from time to time. The highlights of this game for me is the artstyle/graphics, story, and boss battles. The boss battles do a good job at having you utilize your abilities. The art style and graphics are beautiful and reminiscent of GBA games. The story is also solid, with charming characters throughout it. Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed this game and recommend it to anyone looking for a metroidvania to play. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Visually it's pretty good, but that's about all. Very much form over substance. The gameplay itself is seriously lacking and the boss fights, instead of being interesting or testing skill, are almost all nuisances. The music is also feels uninspired and, at times, clashes with the tones of the environment.After completing zone G, I decided to put this game down since it felt like a huge chore to continue playing. Perhaps the final boss makes up for it and perhaps this game will be more enjoyable to you, but for me, it's not worth it. I wouldn't say I hate this game or that I regret putting time into this game... but I would say most of the 6 hours I spent on this game was characterized by annoyance.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is absolutely in the "It's fine" tier of Metroidvania.  Great visual style, solid music, plays well, doesn't overstay its welcome.  It's not too hard due to a bit of a "shield" type mechanical system for dealing with damage that it's got going on, but a few bosses required a few attempts to get the patterns down.  The Obligatory Traversal Upgrades they designed and their interplay with the elemental armor system were pretty nice and I enjoyed those.I think the biggest problem I have with the game is that pretty much all upgrades are a function of finding items or specific collectibles and spending those to buy more shield/HP upgrades or perform one-time upgrades to each armor set.  This isn't an inherently bad thing, but enemies respawn as you go between rooms and the lack of any sort of character leveling progression or item drops (outside of coins, which you get in excess) meant that after a while it didn't feel particularly worthwhile or rewarding to fight as I moved along, I just had to clear enough gaps to get to where I was going.  Fast travel options also tend to be a bit limited, which exacerbates that issue.It may not be worth full price as it's relatively brief, but it's certainly worth a look on sale or in a bundle if you enjoy the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I just finished the game! Congratulations to those of you who are good at Metroidvanias and are saying that you finished in 5 hours, but maybe take my 30ish-hour playthrough as an example of what this game might hold in store for people who are not super familiar with the genre. I had a great time, the pixel art was gorgeous, and there were lots of memorable bosses. I was initially taken in by the colorfully light-edged aspect of the art, which you can see in the promos. Little did I know going in that those edges are crucial to the gameplay, with different armor sets having different effects - the function follows the form - and the form happens to be very beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid little metroidvania, executed quite competently, and accompanied of quite good visuals and music. Don't expect something revolutionary, because this is as classic as modern metroidvanias come, but if you like yourself some classic flavor metroidvania-ing, this is a good buy. Basically the videogame equivalent of a nice bowl of your mom's stew - it's not going to get any michelin stars, but man does it feel nice and nostalgic. Not terribly long, though. Took me about eight hours, and that's with me scouring the map and also misinterpreting a very obvious signpost so I looped the entire map before noticing - I suspect a more normal playthrough will clock more like six and a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it all! Gorgeous design, interesting story, smooth controls, and bosses that are juuuuuuust difficult enough to really sink you're teeth into without going insane. And that's before we even get to the magical girl transformations. 10/10, the price this is at is criminally low, please get it.

_childDocuments_.review: I somewhat agree with others about this not being a proper metroidvania. Areas ARE gated by ability, but the path through the game is pretty linear. Backtracking SUCKS in this one. Best to fully explore an area. If you dont, you'll end up back tracking for ages for a health upgrade. Traversal is pretty boring as well. Thankfully, the game makes up for these with great boss fights every 10 minutes or so. Difficulty curve for them spikes at the end, but it's alright.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Decent story, decent platforming, decent combat, decent bosses. As a vania the new abilities you get are pretty satisfying. Main draw of the game is that it is very, very pretty to look at and listen too, and that you have a really cute mascot to follow you around. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Its a great game if you have a controller and can pick it up in a sale, its a decent game if you have a controller, dont think i'd recommend it if you dont have a controller.Its a fun (but somewhat short) game.The Visuals are stunning, the pixel-art is amazing and the importance of colors in this game make it really enjoyable to play and watch.The combat system is relatively simple (almost but not quite to the point where its boring) but does its job. _childDocuments_.review: The artwork and music for this game is fantastic, especially in the early midgame. Sadly, that is the only positive way in which this game stands out.The game reminds me quite a bit of Yohane the Parhelion - Blaze in the deepblue as it has a similar combat and poor world design as that game as well as extremely basic enemy designs. However, 9 years of shadow is 50% cheaper and each room was clearly made by a human being. Whereas blaze in the deepblue features voice acting and is more polished.Aside from the stuff mentioned earlier this game distingushes itself from the crowd with its unique shield system, which also acts as a range weapon, and reverse-parry. The reverse parry works by recovering your shield after you lost your shield if you time it right. The shield is also used as mana for ranged attacks. Unfortunately, this doesn't work that well in practice as you will alternate between being extremely strong or extremely vulnerable. This is because in order to balance out this system you only have 2hp, This all sounds crazy but in the settings you will want to bind the "shoot" action to the inputs you use for healing, parry, AND to the right side joystick button press. Thanks to a glitch in the settings it is possible to have multiple keys do the same action. After setting one key go back to the game then return to settings and select "shoot". if you did it correctly, the box that shows up should be the one with a bigger and a smaller circle, skipping the first box that was supposed to show up. just follow the instructions as normal and you should end up with two keys for the same action. You can use the same trick to add a third keybind as well.Now for the many negatives (not previously mentioned) which block the game from getting a recommendation:- the map itself reveals passages to secret rooms, regardless of the map station, removing any exploration- The side scrolling performance of the game is poor and wobbly, its an issue that shows up commonly in really old unity games, a bit unfortunate to see it here.- Some game tips still have placeholder lorem ipsum text, particularly when you get transformations- no auto map markers or normal map markers. the map stations reveal too much information in order to compensate for this problem, revealing all secret rooms and killing any feeling of exploration.- sometimes doors are not shown on the map, especially entrances to threaters or save rooms.- extremely linear except for one biome.- the LT and RT triggers are too sensitive. You are adviced to use RT or LT for transformations and not use the other trigger.- money is completely pointless in this game. The stuff you can get is determined by other resources.One last thing I have to say is that I can see that the game's problems stem from a lack of competence in regards to the programmers and the game designer. It is not a skill issue, but a competence issues. As such, Mariachi legends is expected to have the same problems with level design and gameplay as this game does.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I should send the hospital bill to this DEV for carpal tunnel damage on the last boss.I cannot complete the boss because I don't have 4 life and I won't grind for another 20 hours just to get the notes required. When I watch youtube solution for killing the last boss, I don't have the same version. After 4 hours of the last boss, the 4th phase is impossible or require too much random luck.It takes as much button press to skip the dialogs before the boss than button press to kill the boss. And you will have to do that over and over again, each time you try the boss again.Unskippable super long cut scene before and during boss fight makes the game really frustrating. Watching the same scene over and over and over and over again for 30+ seconds is painful. I cannot recommend the game because it is an unpleasant experience. Nothings matter if you punish the player with waiting over and over for no good reason. I guess this is a 3 hour game if you remove the time you take waiting and watching cutscenes.The power where after loosing all your light you have to press a button a the right time to regain half the light has to be the most negative power in the history of videogames. Not only it is useless, but it prevent you from fully regenerating the light bar. Many time you have to empty it and doing nothing else until you can fully replenish it. I wish I could turn it off.5 minutes to reach a boss that will one shot you and no save point around? This game is such a drag, I would rather work a day at the office than play that game.For me, this game is the worst metrod-vania ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This game was almost great. I enjoyed the vast majority of it, and don't share the issues many other negative reviewers seem to have. I liked the energy system and I generally didn't find much difficulty with the bosses. There were a few times I was dying and getting quite frustrated, but it turned out to be a me issue which was easily resolved. The story is pretty good and the art is fantastic.The reason I'm not recommending is due to two things: the lack of fast travel, and the last boss. The lack of fast-travel is pretty self-explanatory. There's an elevator, but it's thoroughly underused. Mostly used to access new areas when you unlock the floor later, which is not fast travel.The last boss occurs after you've gone though a fundamental change, and therefore no longer have your trusty heal ability. Instead, you have piss-poor regeneration that kicks on after a few seconds without taking damage. This makes the last boss absolutely terrible. The first phase(s) are fine; I learned the patterns pretty quick and managed to make it through with minimal damage. And then the last phase hits, and it becomes a bullet hell that you need to play perfectly (because remember, if you get hit then your health stops regenerating and you'll start to take "real" damage). This completely ruined all the goodwill the rest of the game built up.I've seen that they're going to patch the game in the next few months, at which point I may re-examine my review. They're allegedly going to change the final armor and add fast travel, both of which go to my core complaints. I hope it actually fixes the problems, because it's a damn shame that such a good-looking game feels so bad to play.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: The game felt small compared to other metroidvanias I've played.The different armors you get don't have meaningful combat differences.The swim ability was clunky to control when jumping out of water.Secret breakable walls showed up as doorways on the map.The strong attack and charge attack didn't add value. Dps is still higher when doing the basic 4-hit combo (attack while moving, then 3-hit combo). Most of the enemies attacked very infrequently. Most combat encounters involved attacking several times, dodging one attack, then repeating.The music didn't fit the theme of the castle.When I play metroidvanias, I don't want to be able to beat most bosses on my first attempt.I shouldn't get 96% game completion on my first run, especially having not revisited any areas for secrets.No-post game content.No ability to warp or teleport throughout the map.The only ability to dash or move quickly is obtained right before the end of the game.Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game. About 30% of the way into it, I wanted to stop playing due to disinterest. I only beat it because I don't like leaving games unbeaten. If you're looking for an outstanding metroidvania, pick up Afterimage or Aeterna Noctis.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a full Metroid/Vania experience this is not going to be that sort of game.While it takes some of the basics of what those games had, it only does them part way.Other things it does not even attempt to bring over from those styles of games.The short answer is this is a middle of the road game, that unfortunately does not have thedepth to really be in the Vania category.6/10  Great Vibes but lacking game-play.I lean towards YES for recommendation, but a neutral would be more applicable.Certainly I would only get this if it was on sale.-------Long Answer: Hoo boy. I really wish this game was deeper than it is. ART Direction: First and foremost, the Art and Music in this gameis actually god tier. The vibrant colours and design of nearly everything is better than most pixel art games.While most pixel art has colours that pop and stand out, 9YOS has this absolutely wonderful GEM STONE quality to it.Things radiate and feel as if light reflects/refracts/penetrates objects in a way I haven't seen before.>THIS IS THE REASON TO PLAY THIS GAME.<COMBAT: It's unfortunate that fighting monsters and bosses is so stinted. From the beginning of the game tothe end you'll find you really dont change up anything as you collect Armors/Abilities. Each Armor fights in basically the same combo style. The only one that felt unique was the first armor which is a rapid poke. From there I figured each armor would have a unique move-set that might make it better or worse to use against enemies. Most saddening this was not the case. They're all interchangeable so pick which one you like the most.Additionally most abilities you get in the game are simply for the local level traversal mechanic and, once you go through there it really just falls off. There no cool tech you could do with snake dash into heat glide, down kick into backdash.Hell, the down kick move is used for like 2 ascending sections and I never used it again.Lastly is the elemental system. God this could have been so much better. This is just aesthetic choice for the most part.Again choose which one looks the best to you.EXPLORATION: Other reviews mention this too so Ill keep this one short. Exploration is non-existent. Once you find the map for an area (I believe) it shows all room in that location; including secret rooms. Most of this game is on rails which isn't a bad thing per se, but as a ""Vania"" game it's sad this really isn't a thing. Even with all the abilities you have, there wasn't anything weird I have to figure out to get places. Heat pillar = Glide / Water = Swim. That's pretty much it.BOSSES: From recollection Id guess there's about 20 bosses in the game. Some are easier than others. Some just are annoying, others will initially appear more interesting than others. There were a few that afterwards I though were good, but could have a been great. (( If they leaned more into elements/movement tech requirements etc.)) Decent premises but lacking in anything more than spamming attacks and dodging a little bit. (More on this later)MISC: Just some final random thoughts here. - I found everything in the game except 1 Blue Note/Shield upgrade.- Upgrades //FEEL// mostly meaning less. When you magic is just a health gate, 1 shield, is the same as 100.- The magic regen system was pretty cool, I was getting good and timing all the refreshes and was able to face tank bosses,and just reset the gauge over and over. Felt rewarding for learning the timing and keeping track of where you Shield was at and how much damage you can take before expecting the refresh mechanic.- AND THEN THIS FAKKING GAME TAKES THAT AWAY FROM YOU.Good god the final boss is actually AIDS because of this. The game right at the end, takes away your refresh mechanic andgives you this slop of "Auto Regen." But the delay is so fakking long once your shield is down its basically gone.I was punished at the end for learning the mechanic and relying on it the whole game, just for the final boss to be a bullet hell. Left a bad taste in my mouth right at the end.I finished this game liking it but definitely unsatisfied, or wanting more from it.I hope this team can come back, see the reviews and make their next game better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing gameplay experience. The story is well-thought-out, the music is masterfully made.The story itself is quite nice. It is the kind of story I'd read in a book or watch in any movie or show. It was wonderful, from beginning to end, watching Europa develop and grow, in both gameplay and narrative. Then at the end, watching her be mature enough to share her strength with others (worded to be spoiler free), that was just beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: It plays good.It looks really good.It sounds really good.It's not a ground breaking game but a nice polished metroidvania with no major issues.The one gameplay related issue I have is that "currency" basically serves no real purpose, I didn't exactly go out of my way to farm and still had a big chunk of change and nothing to use it on.But some usual Qol things are sorely missing to make it a close to perfect experience.No fast travel even if you go out of your way to design the game to avoid backtracking is not good.Not having a way to skip dialog fast is not good either  EDIT: it does have one now.Having inconsistent save placement in regards to boss fights, that's annoying, a few take a bunch of time to get back to and that's quite annoying when most have a save within a few rooms, though most bosses aren't exactly hard if you're good, I can assume someone with less skills will get quite annoyed real fast.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Metroidvanias and was very much looking forward to this game when I first heard about it, but it turned out to be a huge let-down.The art is simply gorgeous - character designs are unique, and the various biomes/ areas are captivating. Music is pretty good as well; and anime fans would be very happy that this game pays homage to so many classics (Saint Seiya, Gatchaman, to name a few). However, that's simply all the game has going for it.My grouses:1. The basic premise of having a common bar for health and ranged ammunition seems unique, but turns out to be very frustrating since almost all major bosses in the game require you to use ranged attacks.. which depletes your life bar to zero, making death very easy, and common. Fortunately combat in this game is not too frantic, with some opportunity to recover and pace yourself2. Very little enemy variety - at most just 5-6 recurring enemy types with no new mechanics involved3. As can be seen from the trailers and videos, the heroine is able to equip herself with different armours. However, apart from just allowing for exploration of different areas and driving the metroidvania element of gameplay, these armours add little extra value to the game - there is no difference in weapons or combat abilities.4. Speaking of which, combat in this game is very dull.5. Conversely, the game employs VERY finicky and frustrating platform elements.6. Hideous load times.The game was smooth and I did not experience any crashes.I would say.. caveat emptor. Buy with caution.. and a lot of patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Pixel art Metroidvania is what I signed up for but it also came with a nice character story and some pretty unique power mechanics. Nods to the classics and a few easter eggs in there. hard to quantify it in a number score alone so style 9/10 music 6/10 gameplay 9/10 story 8/10 if i had to choose an element of the game they did perfectly it would be character design, the main character has thematic outfits that are as Iconic as Samus's powersuit, gravity suit, and Varia Suit. overall its a 8.5 from me and I consider myself a harsh critic.TL;DR if your here for a great Metroidvania title. Buy this one, its great.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun metroidvania for sure. I enjoyed it enough to 100% the title. What I love about this game is that there's consistently a story unraveling throughout, and I feel that is usually a weakness of some games in the same genre. Pixel graphics are great and the healing mechanic with Apino makes for some interesting gameplay. Game was awesome, solid 9/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A polished and focused game. You have to trust the devs - there are no difficulty options, not much in the way of guidance - but they generally don't let you down. Expect a lot of bosses, but with a little perserverance they can all be overcome. The exploration and abilities are satisfying but the map does take a bit of a backseat to the sheer number of bosses. Their quality is variable, but there are some very fun ones in there.Definitely a bit more boss combat-focused than some other metroidvanias, but enjoyable all the same. Doesn't outstay its welcome. The story is... passable. Perhaps it could have done with less exposition & talking, and leaving more to the imagination (I'd have actually removed all the text and left it as a mystery). I was a bit worried that the final boss would be a massive difficulty cliff, but it was just about OK. All in all, a solid effort from an indie dev.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, if not simplistic and surprisingly straightforward, Metroidvania style game with an exceptionally artistic theme and solid music.That said, I can only recommend this game tepidly.  In its current state, it crashes with the frequency of an airplane into the Twin Towers, which is to say it might not happen all the time but when it does you'll notice it and it'll change your enjoyment of things from that point onward.  There is also something to be said for the lack of enemy variety (a lot of these creatures are just elemental-specific color swaps) and how the level progression focuses more on increasing one's power than it does intelligent upgrades and weapon choices.It's not a long game - my first playthrough clocked 5 hours - but I find some of the best games in this style really don't need to be.  I imagine as I struggle to 100% it I'll put even more time into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Has good story and the movement is mostly great. However this game is not for newcomers to the genre. _childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game! Not only is the artwork absolutely brilliant, the music in this game never got old for me; the smooth jazzy lounge feel with an upbeat pace was always fun to hear. The simple mechanics blossomed into a much more challenging and fast-paced exploration and combat system that evolves with your character.  Yes, there are a few aspects that could be improved upon (for example, the near-useless currency and repetitive armor aesthetics), but the entire aspect of fluid changes between the armor sets takes the edge off of that sting for me at least.  Is it a AAA game? Not by a long shot, but if you are looking for a retro metroidvania game with an beautiful , dark, and challenging personality, try this one!

_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Its like Ikaruga and Castlevania except they screwed up almost everything that made those games interesting and fun. The speed at which the game will let you move is too slow from rotating what armor you're in to the backdashes to being able to recover your bar, and there's no way to speed any of it up. Your power-ups are limited to really just letting you explore more of the required areas but not really adding anything to the in-between; you get a glide but its limited to areas where you climb upwards or the swimming which after the main water area is mostly to just climbing upwards or the tunneling ability which I swear the game glitches out with the map and places you and appropriate rooms to go to in the wrong places/spots but beyond that is just straight line mazes. Your charged and heavy attacks reduce your damage output pretty greatly, you'll be stuck doing the same button string over and over again and you'll quickly realize you can animation cancel just by hitting up or down to keep attacking without any stops. In terms of controls though it's fine for most of it but the downward stab ends up being majorly useless for even basic utility purposes and once you get the double jump you can't even use it without double jumping EACH time you want to do it because they tied it to the jump button. The other issue with control comes in with the glide ability as it changes your attack into a burst around you which makes certain sections awkward to go through when you need to have that reach of your main weapon.Bosses and enemies fall into one of two categories - Frustrating or Boring. Either they have so much crap going on at once that it's a pain as you'll regularly have to use your one long ranged attack that reduces health to open their weak spot and then either manage to time the recharge animation or spend too long recovering your bar and risk getting hit by the attacks around you, or you can basically sit next to them and just spam away as they have like one or two attacks which pose little threat. The same combo you'll get use to with the first actual boss is the same combo you'll be using for pretty much everyone else. As far as pros go, the artwork is absolutely gorgeous, absolutely stellar pixel graphics and one of the best looking of the style. The tiny details on the outfit that changes when you swap armors are nice, and everything pops out in just the right way. It's just a shame that the gameplay itself never really gets above 'mediocre'. Had the armors had more of an impact besides being glorified keys it would've been worth it to swap between them, as it stands the elemental weakness thing isn't worth aiming for most times unless you're dealing with a giant armor enemy as even without it, basic mooks tend to not have much HP and bosses tend to not have a weakness.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: What a hidden gem, couldn't stop playing until I finished it 100%. It's not a very long metroidvania but it's really good, it's aestetically pleasing, the combat feels good and its unique HP bar mechanic was very interesting.The bestiary is kind of buggy, I personally got a boss and a normal enemy not registering in the bestiary, luckily for some unknown reason said boss did respawn and I could register it on the second kill. _childDocuments_.review: Graphics are pretty, and the controls feel good, but that's about all this game has to offer. The main issue I had is that the progression system feels very lackluster. Which is cool, but it doesn't make the armors feel special since your armor auto-swaps when you use these abilities.By the end of the game, you will be able to double jump. If you 100% the quests, you can run too. That's it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like 9 Years of Shadows. It has gorgeous art and charming character portraits. The Character interactions are few and far between, but there are some stunningly detailed pixelated cutscenes. It has a strong visual aesthetic but flops hard mechanically. The elements are fine, but the execution could have used some more work. Beyond the game not really being a Metroidvania despite having all the visual trappings of one: the game is very linear with a very clearly defined path. Good for an introduction to this type of game, but if you can't get into a place you're not supposed to be: it's not one. It's an action-adventure game at best. Some people might find this tedious, but Europa's movement is okay in the beginning but feels progressively slower as the scope of the world opens up. Traversal across Talos (the Castle) vertically is fine (via a Fast Travel Elevator), but there is no way to go from the left or right sides of the map. Meaning if you have to get from one side to the other, you have to go through 30+ rooms to get there. Four interconnecting rooms between the Top and Bottom sides of the left and right areas would have made traversal so much more appealing. Even just a pair of rooms to help facilitate this. As demonstrated in the promotional materials: there are armors with mobility related features, some of which are quite quick. You can only use these abilities when the relevant armor and environmental features are present. So you can't use them to alleviate the above problem either. You do get an ultimate upgrade to somewhat ease this burden, but it's like finally unlocking the ability to sprint than anything like the Speed Booster. A 1.5x speed boost at best. Upgrades don't really feel like upgrades. If there is a difference between the Tier 1 and Tier 2 Armors: I could not tell you. Visually or mechanically. If they deal more damage or provide better protection: I could not tell you. The ultimate upgrade implies a lot of power, but it really is underwhelming. I found it to be an actual downgrade to how the game teaches you to use other mechanics (notably healing) and does away with both. Leaving you with a vulnerability rather than an advantage. There are two last things I want to add:There are unskippable cutscenes. Every boss fight features either introductory dialogue or an introductory animation. These get old, fast. It might be only a few seconds every time (for the animations) but going through six to seven lines of dialogue is annoying either way. Please respect our time!Other than that, they force you to go through a series of Kickstarter Backer rooms between the rest of the game and the final encounter. It might feel great for the backers to have their portrait aligned somewhere special in that congealed mass of vertical rooms: but it means absolutely nothing to those who didn't participate in backing the game. Keep those to their own little rooms. Don't make them part of the actual required progression. I don't regret my time with 9 Years of Shadows, but I can't recommend it on looks alone. If you're looking for a moderately challenging, linear, action-adventure game. Get it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing art assets, which I will not be seeing any more of, because the game starts you with exactly one "defensive option": a BACKWARDS dash. Not forward, up, or to the side, backwards. I'm not even clear if it has no invincibility frames, or I'm simply falling prey to the occasionally unclear hitboxes of enemy and boss attacks. The game is gorgeous, interesting, I'm sure the story is lovely, although since it seems to be teddy bear/musical instrument/world mythology themed, I have no idea what it could possibly be. But the profound and consistent annoyance of catapulting myself DIRECTLY into an attack because I committed the crime of facing the direction I wanted to move is simply not something I want to invest more time in than I already have.

After searching online there are a ton of reports of bugs at various points that will stop the game completely. I would say this game is in Alpha phase at best. The fact that they're charging money for it at all is ridiculous.Outside of that here are my criticisms of the game for as much as I could play it.For the Bad, I will break it down into several sections: Gameplay, Graphics, StoryAll in all, I wouldn't recommend this game in its current iteration, even if it was free. Not sure how it has such a high rating. Must be a lot of frass on steam these days.
