_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so yes, I barely scratched the surface of this game. BUT. It commits three major sins almost immediately. First, the "dodge" mechanic is an igavania style back-dash. This is always an annoying mechanic, and usually (always) indicates an extremely shallow combat system with poor enemy design. And from what little I saw, yes, it has very poor, basic, boring enemy design.Two, when you die (and you will, because, again, bad enemy design combined with useless back-dash dodge) you not only are sent back to your last save (normal, acceptable) you loose ALL progress. All items, all bestiary entries, all MAP DATA.Three, the combat is just..clunky. Like, the way your character moves. There is no input buffer, which is frustrating and flat out idiotic in a game with a combo system.Sure, this game LOOKS pretty, but the music is nothing to write home about, and the look is all it has.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed on this game, but generally like it.  I had issues getting into this game initially due to the game's unique HP/MP system, but once I got the hang of it, I really enjoyed myself with it.  Which is why when things change late into the game, it almost feels like a different game.  I really was not a fan of this.  The way the map is built alongside its fast travel system felt like a great idea at first too, but the later into the game I got, the more annoying it was to get from one section of map to another.  This game has some great ideas, but doesn't execute on all of them as well as it could have.What this game DOES do well is its art and spritework.  You can tell this game draws a lot of its inspiration from Blasphemous, and in some ways, I actually liked this game more.  The vibes and mood were geared more towards my preference, which I appreciated.  I had fun, and the game doesn't overstay its welcome.  I think it's a great length!  I feel like putting in one or two more types of collectibles would have been perfect, however.All-in-all, a solid game!  I had fun!
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A very well-made Metroid/Castlevania hybrid with some light Legend of Zelda inspiration for good measure. My playthrough was very polished and ran perfectly on both my Windows PC and my Steam Deck, just make sure you play with a controller. On my metroidvania scale it's a low 8/10, but likely a high 8/10 after the next update releases.I wasn't expecting much going into this game. I had read/heard some buzz online saying that the game was good, but had some shortcomings. Little did I know the developers have been churning out some major updates since the game released a year ago to address all these complaints. New/tweaked areas, revamped artwork/sounds, abilities, performance and bug fixes, quality of life improvements, ect. have all come together to make this a really great experience. Plus, the next major update is planning to add an  and even more abilities.If I had to nail down my favorite thing about this game, it's gotta be the visual and audio design. The music in particular is fantastic without ever feeling out of place for this type of game. You will absolutely have earworms if you decide to give this game a shot. Halberd Studios, PLEASE make an official soundtrack release happen.If I had to mention a drawback, the only major thing that comes to mind would be the design of the Talos Core area. It's a small portion of the map, but it feels rushed and partially cut, with constant elevators taking you to these small rooms instead of a full labyrinth you'll see with every other area. There's also no portrait portal, no armor unlocks, and barely any secrets. It's a shame because I'm convinced this small area is the reason why a lot of people aren't huge on the elevator cutscenes. It felt totally fine and tasteful everywhere else, it's just this small area where it becomes obnoxious. It's definitely the Water Temple of this game.But that's really the only negative I can think of. At $20 this is absolutely worth your time. Hats off to these firsttime devs.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania that starts in black and white and then a demon boss dude kills you. Collect four elemental armours, then fight demon boss dude with the help of a magic teddy bear at the end of the game. Mechanically, each armour has a quality of life and a movement ability. Like, the water armour lets you walk in water a la metroid, then later you get a mermaid ability that lets you swim around. Fire armour lets you walk in fire areas, then later you can float on vents and fart boost off like... fire stuff. Pretty cool.Your laser teddy also has two functions, one which is shoot laser and the other is hugging it. The laser drains your hp bar which is also your mp bar (???) and once it hits 0, further hits will deplete your like actual life. Most of the game you have 2 actual life. Hugging restores 70% of your hp/mp. This is weird and doesn't quite work.The exploration in the game is dope. Lots of side areas with challenges to get hp/mp shards and actual life shards, as well as minibosses etc.Combat is often ass. E.g. one regular enemy attacks incredibly slowly and sort of shuffles forwards. You can only hit him in the ankle. When he shuffles forwards, you'll often accidentally touch his pixel. That'll knock your entire hp/mp to 0 in one hit. So the dude with the massive weapon's strongest attack is shuffle slowly contact damage. Another enemy shoots a red mine which shoots slowly forwards and hovers. Often, I'd defeat the enemy and the mine would just be there blocking progress for like 30 secs after the enemy dies. Sometimes it didn't even disappear at all. The mine will knock all your hp/mp off in a single hit also.Bosses are often annoying af. Loooooong phases where you just have to dodge around and can't damage it, and then a "shoot it with lasers to make it vulnerable" bit. If the boss hits you, typically you cant hug the bear until his vulnerable phase (you hug the bear to restore hp/mp remember). Then you miss the laser phase because you have no hp/mp for firing lasers, and then need to wait again. Some bosses are just fast, so they'll hit you down to 0 hp/mp, then kill you by hitting your actual life within the same attack. E.g. laser attack boom hp off, stunlock, dead. Cool. I don't think this is intended. Bosses were either nice ones where you die a couple times but learn the window to heal and punish etc. between its attacks, or complete grind-fests where you die a dozen times. The worst for me  was the second main boss. Cutscene - fight a snek. Cutscene - fight two sneks. If you die, you have to watch the cutscenes again. Ugh. I'm done with runbacks in games.I gave up on the last boss and cheated.Exploration was cool and I enjoyed going around smoothly in the late game with all my cool elemental abilities. Felt nice. But some of the exploration nodes felt a little unrewarding. Music and sound design in the game was really good. I liked the soundtrack a lot. Some songs were a jam.Despite its flaws, I would recommend it to Metroidvania peoples, and probably not to others.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just great! I enjoyed it overall, but I think its main strengths are its visuals. _childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is a good metroidvania with some drawbacks.The presentation of the game is great. It looks and sounds good.Movement is fun and controls are very responsive and fluid. Combat is rather simple and fighting consists mostly of hitting the enemy and walking or jumping out of the enemy's attacks, but feels good for what it is. I much prefer a simpler approach that feels good all around than a game that tries too much at once, but feels bad.Boss fights were mostly fun with just very few frustrating ones. A lot of people say this game is very short at 4 hours, but I don't really understand how they completed it so fast. It took me around 10 hours to 100% (HowLongToBeat says the average is around 9 hours).A negative would be the enemy variety. The game just does not have that many different enemies to fight and most are just reskins of existing ones. The elemental armours also mostly amounted to 'if enemy has yellow outline, then lightning attack'. Only some bosses in the last third made you swap attack types on the fly and made for a much more interesting fight.Another annoying thing were the cutscenes on repeat tries of bossfights. Every time you return to the boss after you die you have to click through the dialogue or watch the boss dramatically appear again. Overall the game felt very polished and was fun for my whole playthrough except for some minor bugs:The bestiary only registers your kill when you kill it melee, which is annoying for mini bosses, but you can return to the arena later to kill it again.The game froze on the last screen of the ending and I had to fight the endboss again to get the achievement (at least it was a fun fight). These were the only bugs I encountered.I would recommend buying this game on sale for fans of the metroidvania genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the good:This is a solid metroidvania game and I burned through it eagerly. I have a ton of new games to play and this one won my attention over all the others. The graphics and designs are great. I won't comment on the quality of story because I don't care enough to notice it. The music is... jazzy, if you're into that, which I'm not, but it fits the theme of the game, so I won't knock it. The combat is okay and the map system is great. There are lots of bosses, some mandatory, some optional, each with unique mechanics. The game honors the original Metroid, down to long elevator scenes where the heroine just stands there and thinks. The controls are crisp and the new armors that you get give you interesting, sometimes fun, abilities. The platforming and puzzles are engaging and sometimes challenging, and very rarely annoying.The bad: First of all, I have to mention the crashes, which is what everyone mentions, and for a lot of people, that is a dealbreaker. I did lose a small amount of progress due to the game crashing, but it wasn't a big speed bump for me. I finished the game in about 10 hours and I had less than 10 crashes, with so little progress lost that it was barely an issue for me. Keep in mind that this is still a new game, and I have faith that the developers will fix it.Now, the bad things that actually bother me:1) unskippable boss introductions. Very annoying when attempting to kill a boss multiple times.2) awkward combat. The game features a projectile (which is also your shields), which is not easily aimed. You don't get a targeting reticle, and it seems somehow completely separate than melee attacks, even though it can and should be used to kill enemies. Also, I don't see any reason for the "heavy attack" button. The heavy attack should have been worked into the light attack combo, which would have made the "shoot" button more easily accessible. (By default, it's the right trigger.)3) bosses with strange difficulties - some bosses are so easy you can button-mash through them, and other bosses require multiple, focused attempts4) No customization - there are only a few upgrades you can buy, and you don't really get to make choices with your currency5) changing armors is fast but almost pointless - you do extra damage to enemies if you're using the armor that corresponds to the enemy's color. But it's only a 25-33% difference in damage, so you'll only care about switching armor for the difficult enemies that can't be steamrolled.6) the map needs work - the map is good, but there are some things that should be marked that aren't marked. There are "paintings" that you can jump into, which are large, separate map areas, and complete mini-levels in themselves. However these paintings aren't marked in any way on the map, so god forbid that you skip something in a painting level and want to go back (and there ARE things you can miss).7) Lack of teleportation - the game features a main elevator, which is the only "teleport" feature. When you start the game, you get 2 locations, and they're both so close to each other that it barely matters. I was 75% through the story (!!!) before this elevator got additional locations. Basically, you do NOT want to backtrack in this game, it will take forever, because you WILL be hoofing it.8) I hate Apino so much. Apino is your little stuffed teddy bear buddy that joins you at the start of the game, and facilitates your ability to shoot things and solve puzzles. The problem is, he talks, and he only says one gibberish word, and it's stupid and pointless and gets old really fast during long conversations where you're trying to button mash through the dialog. There's another level of stupidity in that the main character seems to understand what he's saying as complete ideas, even though all he says is "Tzwii!" Ugh, I hate that trope. Also, a generic teddy bear? Why? I would have rather had any plushie-thing in place of that. Maybe a floating eyeball, or a frog, or a seagull. Anything would have been better. Give us some DLC skins for him or something. Idk.9) No replayability, no new game plusI definitely did not play for 18 hours. I think I left this game on pause for half a day or something. You can finish the game in about 8-10 hours casually, and half that if you're good and trying hard.  And as of now, there's little or no reason to replay it, unless you're a speedrunner.It's fun enough to burn through in a weekend, but I would wait to buy it until it's discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn’t heard about 9 Years of Shadows until just a few days before launch, so I was really hyped when I saw this. I’m playing more metroidvania style games this year, and I’m so glad that I gave this one a try. This game was not without its flaws, but overall, I really enjoyed the core experience and the awesome features that were to offer. The overall plot is about a noble warrior woman who is on a quest to venture into a mysterious robotic fortress and destroy the corruption coming from there. Sounds cool right?! – this is where 9 Years of Shadows really shines. After the beginning grey intro scene, you are presented with a vibrant and colorful world. You can tell this was a huge focus for the dev team and they delivered big time. In my opinion, the different areas were all beautiful to look at and different enough to help me remember each zone vividly. – I personally loved the story and feel of the world around you as you progressed through the game. The small cutscenes when traveling through the elevator to a new zone were a nice touch. The atmosphere really went hand in hand with the art style which made the gameplay of this game feel awesome. – the music is absolutely phenomenal. It grabbed my attention right away and just added to the overall experience of traversing Talos. I’m a huge fan of video game music so I definitely loved this part of 9YoS. – there is a lot to cover in gameplay! Combat and game controls feel great. 9 Years of Shadows has a unique combat style that intrigued me from the start. It took me a little to get use to how the main character’s shields and mana were combined. Once the pool of mana was depleted, a timing event occurs on screen and allows you to refill your bar back up. If your pool of mana is depleted and you take a hit, you lose an armor point (which you upgrade your number of armor points during the game). After I mastered this, combat felt super fluid and I almost felt unstoppable. Your sidekick (Apino) has an ability that drains your mana pool but can definitely be useful to traverse the world or refill your mana pool. Another aspect of gameplay are Europa’s (main character’s) armor sets. I don’t want to spoil anything, but the ability to switch between them based on the area you’re in, and upgrade them individually was super sick. Combat may seem pretty basic as far as different attacks go, but I think that is a positive! Like I said before, you can increase your armor and mana by collecting upgrades throughout the world, combined with coins that you get from killing enemies, then visiting the blacksmith. Lastly, questing is pretty straightforward in 9YoS but overall, I felt it was great addition to the game that helped players actually seek out optional bosses. The musicians were an awesome hub area to check progress of your character and pull the story full circle with how much progress you have made in Talos. Bosses were unique and there were quite a few of them! Some more challenging than others, but overall, I didn’t have a hard time progressing through them. – after the patches and updates I have heard that the crashes have gotten better, but on launch day I had quite a few crashes. After certain boss fights, while traversing the map, when trying to save…there were quite a few different scenarios where my game crashed to desktop. I understand it is hard to optimize a game for PC, and I’m super grateful they are working even harder to make the game flawless in performance. I don’t know if all the bugs causing crashes are fixed, but in my experience of playing the game right after release, I had to replay areas because I hadn’t saved for a long time or even replay full boss fights. Just a thing to keep in mind! – Being an achievement hunter, I was losing my mind when achievements weren't unlocking for me after my first full playthrough. Haha. They should all be fixed now so this isn’t really a negative anymore, but for some reason a few boss achievements didn’t pop for me on my first playthrough, as well as some collectable/sidequest achievements. That’s kind of why I put my review of this game off because I couldn’t 100% it until some of the achievements were fixed. All good now!Overall, 9 Years of Shadows is a super fun metroidvania at a great price. The devs didn’t try to over innovate, they created a solid experience for players to bite their teeth into. I enjoyed my experience with the game. Newer players to the metroidvania genre will probably love this game while veterans may feel like they want more from it. I thought this was a solid title and I can’t wait to see what comes next!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game. Maybe in a huge sale.It's a nice game, good art, good gameplay, cool story, however the developers had some contestable ideas that in the balance, is heavier than the good things.As you can see in the screenshot, the hud shows a blue bar and red dots (up to 4 red dots in the game), the blue bar is shield and magic, the red dot is the health. Once the blue bar depleted, you'll lose a life in one hit and to make it worse, isn't a "life tank" as you probably expect, the shield remain depleted, so in 2 hits you'll die in the most part of the game.So to get around of this issue you can get some of blue bar by killing enemies (which fills just a little bit, but can reach 100%), by hugging the bear (awn... stupid as it sounds) which takes some seconds (if you receive damage, it cancel) and only can do with the shield depleted, and by hit the quick time event (QTE) which recover a good amount of energy. This QTE reminds me the QTE on Gears Of War when you recharge the weapon.This QTE is annoying, on the first moment it's hard to get used to, it's by far the best way to recover energy. Once you get used to it, the game become a walk in a park, you can destroy everything without much issues, even the bosses you can tank most of the attacks.I was enjoying the game, even being too easy, it's cool to explore, interesting bosses, etc. HOWEVER  I hate when the game increases the difficulty exponentially for no reason.The game can be finished 100% with all achievements in less than 7 hours without issues.Just a last complain, for some reason Europa sounds like Toad in Wario's Woods when she completes a mission. _childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is a very good, night great game.It's brimming with beautiful art and pleasing music and boasts a map that's just the right size such that no area overstays its welcome. The movement is smooth, and the further one gets into the game, the better it gets. The bosses, for the most part, are rather fun as well, though the portrait bosses feel somewhat slow due to the length of their patterns. While fairly straightforward, the story is heartwarming and works well for the game. Overall, it's a rather pleasant experience and would likely be enjoyable to anyone who enjoys the Castlevania games.My only real complaint with the 9 Years of Shadow is that there is a bug where the game can stop progressing during the epilogue, which means you'll have to reset the game and re-fight the final boss again if it happens. I only had it happen once, and it seems that just giving the game more time between animations fixes the issue, but it's something to be aware of nevertheless. Fortunately, I was still able to get the full impact of the ending since it stopped for me early on.

_childDocuments_.review: I was interested from the initial trailer before the game released. I play a lot of metroidvania titles because they often complete in under 20 hours, provide an interesting story without being basically a movie, and the 2d/2.5d graphics can be appreciated better. Nine Years of Shadow is no exception to this. It provided an engaging story, a different take on equipment/abilities, and overall had some good music. The battles were a lot of fun without being too easy or too difficult; there were a few bosses it took me 3-5 times to learn the patterns. My favorite battle involved chess....man, I wish there was a boss rush mode just so I could play that battle again. This was a bit on the just under average length to complete coming in under 10 hours for 101%. I would say on a second run knowing where things are, I would probably finish this in 6-7 hours. I did end up missing a single blue note I had to re-search the world for. Regarding the map, I do wish the map coloring was a little better; I wasn't a huge fan of their choice of coloring. Being a busy adult, this is a perfectly acceptable amount of time to keep me engaged without losing me because of adulting. I highly recommend the game and will definitely play it again and do a more formal review.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr:  Worth it on a good sale.Longer:  The art is lovely and music is enjoyable, and overall traversal is fluid and quick.  The main detractor for the gameplay is having the energy bar tied to health.  It's not a good feature, and creates some frustration during combat. _childDocuments_.review: The perfect definition of a "Just OK" game. If you're a big fan of something like Metroid Fusion, then this would be up your alley in terms of linearity, and playtime (around 5 hours). The pixel art and music are nice, and sustain well throughout the whole game. The story is simple enough to follow along, but not insanely convoluted (I just played a similar game called AfterImage, and holy crap, that plot was all over the place). Not being able to skip some dialog scenes is ridiculous, though.Most of the negative reviews seem to be based on the game crashing. My game crashed twice, but both times I had Alt+tabbed away and walked away for an hour or so, so I didn't feel too bummed when I came back and everything went kaput. I think it's been patched since it first came out as well. That said, definitely save often, especially because of how unforgiving dying is in this game.Bottom line: If you're a fan of MV's, then get this game on sale. It's simply not worth it at full price. I mentioned the game AfterImage which is incredibly similar to this game, but is around 40+ hours and is around $25. This is currently $20 and is...not 40+ hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this is a disappointing decision in the field of game design and it does not live up to expectations. The main goal of "9 Years of Shadows" is to impress gamers with its beautiful music and stunning visuals, but unfortunately, this does not happen.The decision by the developers to incorporate the mechanics of healthbar with projectiles and evasion without any invincibility frames is confusing and frustrating. As a rule, platform games have invincibility frames for evasion so that players can avoid damage by rolling over enemies and not cause harm. In "9 Years of Shadows," evasion seems like a useless and frustrating activity.Despite the impressive audiovisual accomplishments, the game is ruined by poor game design decisions. This major flaw in the game design ruins "9 Years of Shadows" and makes it an unworthy title for sophisticated gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok where to start.This game is absolutely beautiful with its art and music. The game controls work well and the boss design and mechanics are quite unique and fun. These are the main drawing point for this game. The story is also pretty good with likable characters with unique designs.The length of the game usually is around 5.5 hours and the game itself has a little bit of repetitive enemies and mechanics where you travel to each section, unlock a new armor, then go to a painting to get its skill and loop that 4 times. The worse part of the game is the most commented on and its probably the combat/ final boss. The combat is quite unique with the shield as ranged damage and HP and i mostly just spammed melee due to that. Also I am pretty sure most people forget you can hug your bear to refill your shield, which I forgot for like 25% of the game which made the main difficulty. But if you do the shield refilling and the quick time for repairing your shield, it makes early game bosses just tank and hit sometimes. The final portion of the game has you completely remove this mechanic which I can see people complain about, and I can also see why the devs did something unique similar to the ending portion of super metroid. But it really does make the game completely different for the final boss and its 4 stage difficulty probably turns people off the game.Overall TLDR: 8/10+ Great Art, Music+ Good Characters and dialogue/story+ Unique combat mechanics, and exploring mechanics- Repetitive enemies, stages- Lack of quick travel for the map (though the map isnt too big)+- Final act of the game changes everything (could be good since it makes things different)- Final boss has a huge difficulty spike (Due to combat mechanic changes, and 4 stages)- Some bugginess for some mechanics (Though nothing that prevented my completion)- No idea how to fill my missing beastiary since no one online has a list

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty impressed with this game. The art and style is amazing. I'm into the vibe of elemental armors, musicians, and a floating ghost bear you hug to replenish ammo. It feels really nice to play. I'm juuuust about done with it and while I see several people complaining about the length, I'm feeling pretty good about where it's clocking in at. I'm having fun but I feel like it's done what it's wanted to do and I don't feel the need for it to continue for another 10 hours. I'm really enjoying the environmental/platforming puzzles. It's pretty basic stuff where you unlock a new mechanic then use that mechanic in a fairly linear series of rooms that ask you to do trickier and trickier things with it (eventually combining it with some of the earlier mechanics). Is it the most challenging platforming ever? No, but it's also not the easiest. I don't die a LOT but it definitely happens sometimes. And it's difficult enough to feel like you accomplished something when you're done with an area. Same with the bosses. They're not dark souls level difficult. But they're also not pushovers. I'm finding that I need to play many of them a couple times to learn how they work. Each attempt I make significantly more progress until beating them on the 3rd or 4th try. I like that sweet spot where I don't have to grind a boss for 4 hours, but it still makes me earn the victory. I do have some complaints. For the longest time, I had no idea what my health was. Maybe I'm just stupid, but it wasn't apparent to me that you could only lose health when your mana was fully depleted. (I'm sure it said that at some point and I missed it). But after figuring out that that's how it worked, I found that system to be fairly enjoyable. Finding the right moments to hug your little bear to recharge mana while in the middle of a fight required a bit of planning and was exciting to try to pull off. I also experienced some of the crashes that a lot of people are talking about. Apparently not quite as bad as most, though. I'm 6.5 hours into the game and I think it's crashed on me 3 times. Crashes are always frustrating, especially in a game with no auto save, but certainly not a game ruiner for me. I'm really enjoying my time with this one and highly recommend it to people who like metroidvania style games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have a good intention however it has a CRITICAL FLAW within its health system.HP works as follows: your health bar increases when you hit enemies with normal attacks and decreases when you get hit by enemies So far so good.You can even recover hp for 'free' by holding a button (for a given time) IF your health bar is EMPTY. That sounds neat! right? what's the problem then?well... there's a special 'magic' attack which drains your hp... This is similar to Hollow Knight's thing. The BIG issue here is: some enemies (Bosses) require you to attack them with magic attacks.. like MANDATORY!this means YOU HURT YOURSELF just to try to beat the thing! even if you avoid enemy hits, you can find yourself  on low health because of this attack system. The worst is: at some points you CANNOT even attack anymore if you miss a shot and run out of hp, and guess what, you cannot recover energy / hp either as you need to be dodging to stay alive...I like metroidvanias and I am always happy to see new games on this genre being releases. Yet I cannot recommend this oneGo play Hollow Knight, Bloodstained, Record of Lodoss War or even the great SoTN. Pass on this one

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very nice looking, and I ended up playing the game almost to the end.  I ended up quitting the game simply because I was not having any fun playing it, simply because the game mechanics are tedious and annoying.  The whole concept that the hp bar is also your ammo is implemented really poorly.  When your hp/ammo bar empties, you get a chance to do an active reload like in a Gears of War game. If you miss the QTE for the reload, you have to stand completely still for a few second and hold the right trigger to regain hp/ammo for a few seconds. If you get hit or move, you have to let go and hold the right trigger all over again.  Also, to fire your ranged attack you also have to press the right trigger.  Guess what button you have to press to do an active reload when your health is out? It's also right trigger.  This ends up causing the most common way to die in this game.  You will be ranged attacking the boss with RT, you get hit and go to zero HP/Ammo, then you immediately fail the QTE reload because you were already using the same button to shoot.  This mechanic absolutely destroys the flow of the game, and made me uninstall it.

_childDocuments_.review: As  a fan of Metroidvanias, I have been greatly anticipating 9 Years of Shadows. 9YoS  has some of the most beautiful pixel art that I have experienced (tied with Blasphemous as the art style's peak). The game controls well and combat feels great. The most interesting (and positive choice) is the combination of the main character's shields and mana. When that pool is depleted, a quick time event occurs which (if successful) can lead to you regenerating both instantly. Learning timing for the quick time event was not overly challenging and mastery of this led to feeling nearly unkillable and combat being a joy. The different armors that Europa can equip that gain her different traversal abilities (the mermaid one was easily the best) have a fantastic visual style and the armor outlines are very helpful for players with aging eyes like myself.On the not as positive side, I did have a number of crashes during my first hour of gameplay, then none for the next ten hours followed by crashes every time I died to the Reaper boss. Since the recent patch I have not experienced any more crashes but I only had about three hours left to complete in the game. The other somewhat unusual aspect of this game is is the difficulty curve for bosses in this game. To be clear, all of the bosses in this game are fun and well designed. The first few bosses were easy but the Shadow of Hope boss was markedly more difficult than anything that came before. Following that boss, nearly all of the bosses were a breeze until the late game. Do not know if this was the intent of the developers but it seemed to be unusual execution. The mana/shields combination and stunning pixel art aside, there is not a great deal of innovation in 9YoS. This is not necessarily a bad thing except that it makes it harder to stand out in a popular genre. Newer players to the genre have a lot to love here, veterans may be left wanting a bit more. On its own, it is a solid title.

_childDocuments_.review: When I installed the game for the first hour, it started crashing every 10 minutes. It was impossible to play with it. However, I decided to give the game a second chance and after reinstalling everything became much more stable.The game itself is not bad, interesting mechanics with energy, which is also your "shield". Nice graphics and quite comfortable difficulty. A great concept about a world where magic is colors and music. However, the sydet itself is rather mediocre. There are also several critical issues:- there is no normal fast travel, for some reason the mechanics of teleportation to save points is not used, as is done in all games of this genre, while there is a lot of back tracking- at a certain point in the game, the main energy recovery mechanic is broken, it changes the game a lot, unexpectedly and without warning, it's not good to do this- a very bad progression system, firstly it is microscopic, and secondly, it is not clear whether it makes sense to pump something at all, there are no sensations from pumping, there are also changes, it only affects visual effects- a very boring last boss, not difficult, but just stuffy, did not pass it, due to random attacks in the last phase, while changing something or buying consumables is impossible, since there are noneI want the developers to realize their mistakes and do better in the next projects

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine, but there's definitely quite a bit of room for improvement.For starters, there is the Spirit Bar: it doubles both as ammo for ranged attacks and as a shield, since you normally die in two hits. It replenishes simply by hitting enemies, but if it empties you have to either kill an enemy,  do a QTE or stand still and hug your floating teddy bear.I didn't found this system punishing outside of one instance, and there are also hidden notes (tip: look for cracks in the walls) that can increase your hitpoints or your Spirit Bar's length.Combat is simple, with just a few attack moves, a backstep for evasion and the aforementioned projectile.Part of the metroidvania aspect comes from the armors you find throughout the game: they're needed to enter certain rooms, activate colored switches and have different traversal tools, like entering narrow passages or riding an air current. You also do more damage to enemies that have the same colored aura as your armor, but juggling between them is never a requirement.That said, there are a few gripes I have with the game:- There's no fast travel system. This is pretty annoying, even more so if you've missed a hidden note and need to backtrack to reach it;- The final boss was quite frustrating. It has three phases: the first two are doable, but the third is a mess that's hard to keep track of between spinning blades, 4-way lasers and big orbs that transform into massive lasers. What makes it even harder is the fact that - This is just me, but I would've liked to see a different moveset for each armor. I think it would've made them more unique.In short, it's a good game, but it could've been better. Still worth to play, Imho.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10  Borderline but would not recommend. I like the look of the game and the creativity and fun of most of the boss fights.  The traversal with the metroidvania unlocks were pretty fun at times too. The big negative is the bulk of the game.  The zones you fight through for most of the game play time were not fun due to a complete lack of enemy variety and boring enemy combat.  That part of this game wore thin well before the credits.   The bad outweighs the good for me and so it just barely gets a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing music/art. Plus, the bosses have some really good designs (the chess one has to be one of my favorite bosses of any 2D I've played). Except for the final one that i got bored by how long it takes to reach the final phase and get crushed before i can start learning the pattern. The life system gives a unique flavor to the combat, which has those high-tension moments where you're desperately searching for some space to recover your shield/ammo. That said, I didn't like that many bosses' vulnerability window is tied to having enough shield remaining after some attack sequences, also the autorefill minigame is worthless when you are completely focused on combat (it also causes to waste time to start the manual refill).As far as metroidvanias go, this one is closer to Record of Lodoss War than, say, Bloodstained. By this I mean that there are some systems and design choices (also the aesthetics) that resemble SOTN, but only on a superficial level. Progression is quite linear and map connectivity doesn't change much during the playtrough.It seems like they ran out of resources or time because things like upgrade systems and regular enemies seem like an afterthought. The map and late game traversal can also use quality of life updates.Overall, it's a solid game that anyone should try just to enjoy the quality of the pixel art and music.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible as a metroidvania, but okay as a platformer.  Unfortunately there's just too many questionable design decisions.  Not a bad game, but not worth my time.The game is far too linear.  There's only ever one path forward at any time.  The game introduces a fast travel room pretty early, and then completely neglects to insert additional fast travel rooms for the majority of the game.  The color armor system is cool, but it's not implemented well enough to use on the fly reliably.  The game would've been better off with only 2-3 colors, or with a dedicated button for each color so you know exactly how to get the color you want and develop muscle memory.Enemies, levels, and obstacles are all pretty repetitive, though I liked most of the boss fights.  Most bosses have a save room nearby, but you can't skip dialogue/cutscenes, so if you die you have to mash through text boxes and/or wait through cutscenes every time.I liked the health system.  Combat, particularly the bosses, felt fast paced and fun.I feel like the game would've been better off as a finely tuned platformer instead of a metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: - Artstyle- UI- Controls- Runs on SteamDeck - Enemy varietyIt is a minor gripe, but enemies are more or less reused everywhere or are a variation of ones you have seen before. After a while they all start blending together, I just wish there could have been more, as the art in this game is really good- Elemental-Weakness systemThis system was fine, as it brought some variety to the lack-luster combat system. The problem with it is, that at 66 % of the game, there weren't much uses for it. There always seemed to be enemies weak to an element you either haven't unlocked yet or you couldn't switch your armor to, as the room condition (heat, poison, etc.) would not allow you to switch to the element you needed. - Normal EnemiesAt first, the enemies are just your standard thing: They show up, you kill them. After a while playing I realized that there is no benefit for me at all to defeat them in the first place. Granted, they drop some currency for me to spend on upgrades, but currency is not a problem at all in this game. Later on, enemies are placed as roadblocks, so I just started ignoring and hopping over them, as they will respawn anyway, as soon as I leave the room.- BossesThe bosses in this game seem to be there to waste your time and bolster ingame time. In each fight, it seemed you had to just wait and dodge projectiles, just so the boss finally starts to show his vulnerability and you can hit them. Then the whole thing starts anew... there just isn't anything to them and it's always the same procedure: Deploy Bullet Hell for player -> Show Crystal -> Crystal destroyed? Player can hit, otherwise punish the player by deploying an unavoidable AOE attack.Also, there are some mini bosses, that have a slightly different tactic to them: Throw bouncy projectile -> Run away from the player. If the mini boss is big then: Is my health low? Throw big projectile -> run away- CombatYou spam the combo-attack button, as long as the game (boss?) allows you to do that. All the enemies in the game seem to have at least double the health that they should have, so upgrades you get just seem to have no real effect. Combine that with the road-block-enemies, bosses that don't allow you to hit them or run away and the elemental-weakness system, that can't be used all that much and you get into either a spam fest or you just dodge enemies like I did.- Level DesignLong corridors with respawning enemies and at the end of them, you realize that you cannot pass, as there is a door that needs to be opened from the other side. This happened like 3 times in the game - why would you guide a player through that, if you shouldn't be there yet in the first place? Just add a second door in the beginning to block the player from entering...

_childDocuments_.review: It saddens me to see the 'most helpful' review a negative one on launch day, so I thought I'd share my thoughts after 3hrs of gameplay.Here's why you should play:Satisfying combatChallenging boss fights Sublime musicGorgeous pixel art - superb use of colourInventive upgrades - loving the mermaid armour!Compelling story with animated cutscenesSteam Deck - Rock solid 60FPS out of the box. And it looks stunning.Oh - and a cute teddy bear companionAddressing the 'issues':For those saying this isn't a metroidvania, I have to disagree. Yes, there isn't as much backtracking as is typical of the genre but upgrades allow you to visit previously inaccessible rooms and areas (so, for me, it ticks the metroidvania box).The day one update seems to have fixed many of the tech problems mentioned in reviews. I've had one crash in 3hrs (and didn't really lose any progress). Some reviewers have bemoaned the lack of save locations. I've died a few times, but have only ever had to replay a few rooms. Save stations are usually nearby boss fights. I'd recommend going back to your nearest save after beating a boss though, as it doesn't save automatically.For those on the fence, I think this could end up being a real hidden gem in the future (especially after some QoL updates).

_childDocuments_.review: (Original review after playing for 2 hours)You get a cute little teddy bear that makes ranged attacks. Buy it.===============Further thoughts after completing the game: I like this game's art style. I'm a fan of the retro feel and vibrant colors. Most of the bosses are pretty fun. Landing a hit always feels satisfying, and bosses slowly turn red as their health gets lower, which is a pretty clever substitute for health bars. The final boss was a perfect journey of "holy crap, this is impossible" to "wow, that was satisfying to beat." Regular combat is more so-so. Common enemies tend to be either nonthreatening or just annoying. You can beat a lot of them by just standing in one place and spamming your ranged attack.One thing that did annoy me is that the game doesn't autosave collectible items, so you need hike back to the last save point every time you find an item because if you die, you have to go get it all over again. Also, I recommend not waiting too long to do side content because there's a point where certain combat mechanics change, and they never change back, which makes everything other than the endgame portion needlessly awkward.So overall, this game is not without flaws but I enjoyed myself for the most part. As I'm writing this, the game is currently sitting at 71% of recent Steam reviews, which feels a bit low to me. I can understand it's not for everyone (as Metroidvanias go, I wouldn't recommend this game before Ender Lilies or Hollow Knight), but I still think it's better than the raw numbers  indicate. Give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I am always on the lookout for new Metroidvania style games, and 9 Years of Shadows seemed to have everything I really wanted, tight controls and platforming mechanics, an interesting story to keep my engaged, really good soundtrack, and some phenomenal sprite work. The armor swapping and movement abilities of each becomes a blast to traverse the levels with.The game started off for me, almost too easy, I was blitzing through bosses, finding upgrades rapid fire, until suddenly the difficulty spiked up sharply. Nothing wrong with that, gimme a challenge! As more abilities were unlocked, and I settled into the game's groove I got to the big reveal of what's going on, and got the final upgrade.... which instantly felt like a downgrade as I no longer had my powered up projectiles, or the healing mechnics that were in place for the hours upon hours of game I had just mastered. Now with only 2 bosses left in the game I'm suddenly given a completely different set of abiilities to work with that feel...ok for tidying up any items I may have missed since I can nuke entire rooms, but when it comes to bosses instead of darting in and out and being able to pick a point to try and heal if I miss timing a button press I instead need to try and play keep away with the hectic paced mechanics I no longer feel comfortable dodging, because suddenlly bosses are even deadlier than they were before. I really was loving the game up until the final hours which feel so at odds with the rest of the game, which kills a recommendation from me. I don't feel like I wasted my time, but the final portion feels so bad it's a major let down for what was a very solid game otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: Sofar i can't recommend it, the only thing it has for it by this point is beautiful graphics.The combat is horrendous if you ask me, if we ignore the boring enemies by this point I have one BIG problem, the health/mana system. You more or less use your health to cast "spells" which you can restore only when the mana/health bar is empty. But that bar is in theory a mana shield and your true health is 2 hits early game, which can only be damaged when your manabar is 0 and everytime you get hit is taking 100% or 80% of the manabar. So what do you do? You go back to a safe space and spend all your mana to cast spella on a wall so you can fill the bar to 80% again, It's just a tedious design. So did they do anything to remedy this you ask? Yes they made a quicktime event when you reach 0 mana in which you have 0.2 secs to press for restoring mana, BUT the normal recovery is better so your best way is to skip that event and heal manually.....I commend the graphics designer but the gameplay this early is really bad. And I haven't even talked about the unskippable scenes because they wanted a full reset to last save if you die design. Edit: It feels like this could be some students first or second project, and if it is I really can respect that, the more people that makes metroidvanias the better if you ask me as a metroidvania junkie. The graphics carry this game completely, the designers/programmers need to step up and really understand what this genre is all about.

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadows is a visually breathtaking Metroidvania that delivers a memorable experience with its vibrant pixel art and a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack by industry legends like Michiru Yamane. Its elemental armor system introduces variety and depth, making combat and exploration feel engaging throughout most of the game. The world is thoughtfully designed, encouraging exploration and rewarding players with hidden secrets and upgrades.Unfortunately, the game falters in its final act. The last boss is overtuned, demanding near-perfect execution that feels like a sharp difficulty spike compared to earlier encounters. Compounding this frustration is a late-game change to the damage system, which alters how combat works in an unintuitive and aggravating way, disrupting the game’s established rhythm.While these issues tarnish the finale, 9 Years of Shadows remains an enjoyable journey for fans of the genre. Its stunning visuals and solid core gameplay make it worth playing, even if the ending leaves something to be desired.Zone Score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and quick game . Took be a little over 8 hours to complete the story and about 99% of the content (missed a few secret rooms). The combat is pretty simple, Ranged attacks, a 3 hit combo normal and a heavy attack. Nothing amazing but used well enough to remain enjoyable for the quick completion time.Now to my few small gripes:-Some boss fights have attacks or moves that come out so quickly that dodging is no possible, or there is nowhere on the screen that is safe-Hitting a save point acts as a restore point. If you die all world progress will be reset to the last time you rested. While I understand why this is done it can be irritating to be 2 rooms from a save point and dying, and now you have to go through most of an area and a boss all over again.-Money drops are incredibly small and I was unable to purchase all the upgrades through just progressing the gameOverall I would give this game a 6-7/10. This is a fun game and while it doesn't reinvent the genre it at least functions. I have seen a lot of reviews about crashes but I only experienced 1 crash, and afterwords I turned off VSync and experienced no other crashes the entire play through.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, not a bad experience. The game is pretty straightforward in what you need to do.  The traditional saving can take a little to adjust to as when you die you pick up exactly how you last saved meaning you lose all exploration, pickups, etc. like it never happened, so more the realm of SOTN and Metroid.  I say that because the experience of other metroidvanias as of late keep exploration and such since they require you go claim that games essence on death.It was on the shorter side as compared to others released recently (i.e. Last Faith, Blasphemous 2).Liked the art style and the game play overall was enjoyable.There isn't much incentive in battling if you can avoid it since there is no exp leveling system and not much in terms of upgrades that only require currency that is dropped by objects and enemies, both are hit or miss and not guaranteed.  It does give incentive for exploration as hidden items are key to upgrades in tandem with currency.

Visual and art are good, reminds me with old Saint Seiya animation.2. OST are pretty good, there are several japanese veteran composers.3. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with . It is a proper Metroidvania with a fantastic balance of exploration and combat. There were not many puzzles other than using your upgrades to get to door switches, but with this game, that design worked well. I beat the game in just over 15 hours, with about an hour of that going around and getting the last few upgrade pieces.- Skippable intros/text on repeat attempts for boss fights. It killed my flow to have to click through text just to reattempt a boss. I probably watched the 30 second cutscene 20 times on the final boss.- While I enjoyed the elevator thoughts, once Europa ran out, the elevator should have just ran its animation without a button prompt.- Some more enemy variety would have been nice, but honestly I'm okay with what is here. The color outline changes your strategy up just enough that you can't just mindlessly mash attack.- I wish the game would have played around more with grayscale vs color. I love this concept, but the game only used it twice.- The music was decent, but it would have been AMAZING to add in instruments as you found musicians, making the music more dynamic wherever you went. Would have definitely made it more audibly interesting when you backtrack looking for notes.- The pixel art is ! This game has spoiled me and I'm sure the next game I play will feel bland by comparison.- The flow of control feels really good. Combat was snappy, I enjoyed the balance of ranged attack vs shield strength, and mobility was good. Even if I were just trying to run through an area without fighting, It felt good most of the time due to the simple but effective movement you have control over and the different mobility tools each set of armor gives you.- Boss fights had a good variety, and they weren't crazy punishing (with the exception of the final boss). Their attacks are readable and for the most part give you  enough timing to get out of the way. I could beat about half the bosses first try, and the rest only took a few more tries before I learned their patterns. It made me feel great as a player.I really enjoyed my time with this game and recommend it! Kudos to Halberd Studios; they put together a great title!
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! It reminisced me a lot of classic games, such as Castlevania and Megaman; and there are more references from more recent games. The soundtrack is so good, what a blast from Miguel Hasson. And what can I say for the aesthetics and art direction? it's what I like the most, such beautiful colors.I definitely recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of metroidvanias and shorter games, this game checked a lot of boxes for me.Right out of the gate, the game looks amazing, has a fantastic soundtrack, and most importantly plays smoothly and responsively (something a good amount of indie games of the genre can't tout). The plot is interesting, Europa makes for a good protagonist, and the world feels like it needs more fleshing out, something I would love to see if the devs decide to revisit this world.There are a few viable comments to be aware of- the game can be relatively easy save for a few boss fights, especially with the common enemies. I feel like the game saves this, though, but having genuinely interesting fights with varied mechanics.If I had one qualm at all, it would be that the fast travel is very limited, which really only serves to pad the game time a little bit and making what little backtracking there is feel like a chore sometimes.The devs clearly had a lot of care for the genre and the tell they were telling, though, and the game is, above all else, a LOT of fun. I can't recommend this enough if you're looking for a solid gaming experience that doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: 6-6.5 out of 10Pros- Excellent art, especially for an indie game- Decent enough story- Interesting world- Music is ok- I love teddiesCons- No way to mark or see missing collectibles at ALL- No quest markers will likely lead most to get frustrated in finding where to go- Last boss - Consistent super speed bug where things would fast forward in weird ways. Happened throughout my whole playthrough.MAJOR TIP: I don't know if a lot of people realized you could hug your teddy with RT when you run out of his shield, but you can.I think this is a decent metroidvania and the small team of devs did a great job. If you have a hankering for a metroidvania and you like teddies, then this is a great game for you. Otherwise you should likely move on or wait for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. A small metroidvania in comparison to some others available but I don't take this as a negative, personally. The art style is really nice on the eyes and the combat, although not the most complicated in the world, fits the playstyle quite nicely (Matching your armour with the colour outline of the enemy will deal extra damage, otherwise it's just hack away).Think I echo the comments of others in that there is one fight in particular that is a huge difficulty spike compared to others but even then the pattern isn't too bad to learn. For most of the bosses they seem more like a distraction than a threat, although these fights do give some exposition about the story which is nice. One annoyance I have is with one of the achievements (and a tip for anyone reading this) is that for an enemy to be recorded in the bestiary you HAVE to take them out with your halberd. One boss I just took out at range and, sadly, they weren't recorded. Just means a second playthrough is on the cards at some point I suppose.All in all, this is a game that I can recommend. Look forward to further projects the developers dish out.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a very solid metroidvania for anyone looking for something within that genre. The art style is phenomenal, though enemy variety is a tad bit lacking. There is a small amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ design with a few very small rooms with very large enemies that can cause you to back out of a room without intending to while backtracking, but overall very well laid out and easy to navigate.My overall largest criticism of the game is the health/magic bar. You have two hits you can take at the start, increasing to four at max, but your "magic" acts as kind of buffer so that as long as you have it, you wont take HP damage. When depleted entirely, you have to stop and hold a button to refill, akin to hollow knights healing. Which is an interesting idea, in theory, but not so much in practice. There are several bosses that require you to use that magic to put them in a downed state do damage, meaning you can miss entire cycles if you take too many hits. The worst of these offenders is a mid-ish game boss that, if you fail to "down" it, has an entirely unavoidable screen-wide nuke.The "upgrade" to your magic recharge is no substitute for a faster recharge speed and fails to address this issue in my opinion. If used in quick succession, it gradually refills less and less each time. All of that said, I do genuinely enjoy the game and would absolutely recommend it to anyone interested in the metroidvainias. Doubly so if you are a fan o f Saint Seiya, because , whoever designed the armor in this game was  a fan. Not that its a bad thing, they look great.Solid 8 out of 10 game. Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked how beautiful the game looked and although it could use more enemy designs its still mostly a good time. The start of the game bosses lean easy with the middle feeling like the right difficulty. The end is where I have a hard time completely recommending the game because of how hard it gets. The healing system changes to regeneration and its so slow. What should be a overall power up feels like a downgrade in that regard. It makes backtracking frustrating because you don't feel like you have enough light power and it sucks for the far off switches that require it. It makes any quest bosses you missed more difficult. I fought two bosses in this form and struggled with both. The last quest giver boss was hard, but nothing compared to the Final boss. The Final boss is multi phase and you basically have to play almost perfect. Also sometimes I took damage and I couldn't figure out from what during the fight. My best guess is some type of poison or a glitch. When you don't have many hits taking two no matter where you stand doesn't feel fair. Also tip for anyone reading the shuriken bouncing attack can be dodged on the very far sides even though it doesn't look like it. Have seen videos of people tanking the damage and took me forever to figure out. Anyway I overall enjoyed the game, but the end feels like it needs balancing.

_childDocuments_.review: As credits roll, I need to write this one. So far, this is most bland metroidvania I have played ever. It starts very promising, guiding you by hand, teaching basics. Introduces some characters here and there, mostly unrelated to the story, imo. And at some point in the game it just gets boring.Yes, competed it 100%,expected that maybe exploration and mechanics will be better... And it did not. Maybe I am spoiled by many other polished games out there, with more movement tech, better and tight controls, more planned map movement fast travel, but hey - this game somewhat lacks the kick for it.Story - generic, with kinda expected twist to the end. Maybe, if there will be DLC, it could be expanded on and writing might be better too.Combat - don't even get me started. Armor based, or element if you like it more, was nice touch. But it loses the charm once you get deeper into the game. Upgrading armors is worth it for the damage and that's it, and it scales individually. Which, considering the skill level of an average Joe, makes little to no sense to do, but then you need to really do full map exploration. It is not hard game, it's mediocre gameplay that drags this bad combat idea. More movement polishing, some improvement or dodging techniques to add, and it would shine!Bosses - here is the deal, when it comes to bosses, it feels like an asset dump. Yes, they are somewhat unique, even with some lines of dialogue. But due to how combat and movement mechanics are implemented, they are pain in the ass. I enjoy when game challenges you to risk and go for it, but here you often are more cautious, because healing is hit or miss. Of course, idea is interesting, but boy, when there are no enemies, and, as example, last boss becomes touhou in last form, then you are against time basically.All and all, there are rooms of improvement. Style and music were nice. From here I hope devs will polish and improve the game to get more people into it, and maybe speedrunners too (if there would be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ skips for dialogues and elevators dot prompts, never mind the movement even...).As Europa said - "Stupid bear."Would give it 5/10, because finishing it was not very fun experience, my appetite only grew.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most Metroidvania, Metroidvania's I've played in recent years. This is the kind of game I think of when I think of Metrodvania. It's not a Souls-like, there's no corpse runs, no worrying about content getting locked out because you did something minor and seemingly inconsequential. It's you, the castle, and a wonderful lock and key system that would feel right at home in Aria of Sorrow. Is it a perfect game? Of course not. It would have been nice to have a marker system for the map so you can remember where things you wanted to check out is. The map shows where the doors for the hidden rooms are without you having to break the wall. While there are some elevators, I would have liked a teleport system of some kind to cut out some of the excess backtracking. I would find that I had to travel through 2 different areas to get to the place I wanted to go to check for secrets and collectables. All in all this game was a fantastic experience. It took around 10 or so hours to beat, and likely 15 to 20 hours to get 100% of the achievements. If you love Metrodvanias, especially the GBA Castlevanias, then you should absolutely grab this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been really enjoying this game (I still haven't finished it yet).Overall, I'm not a hardcore Metroidvania fan. I'm more of a casual gamer when it comes to that genre (I usually get lost in the levels). However, I do like platformers and hack-and-slash games, and this game has been a smooth experience.I wouldn't call the game "easy," but probably "accessible" instead. I think the game allows you to play with different styles. You can go for close hand-to-hand combat or shoot Apino from afar to kill enemies (some of them require a specific method). And if you're running low on health, you can always hug Apino for a free refill.So in this regard, the player has the freedom to adjust the difficulty as they see fit. If you want a more challenging experience, just avoid using too much of Apino's help.The art is beautiful and eye-catching, and the inspiration references are obvious (like Saint Seiya, Sailor Moon, and Megaman), but the game has its own identity. Everything fits together seamlessly, including the backgrounds, characters, and enemies.I'm also really engaged with the controls. The main character moves smoothly and responsively, and with the different transformations, just traveling through the levels is quite fun. Switching from walking to swimming to gliding or digging feels natural and enjoyable.I've heard complaints and praises about the length of the game. I think this is totally a personal preference, but I'm a very busy person, so I usually don't have time to play long games. I appreciate concise and interesting experiences. Moreover, the game itself is not that expensive and has already given me more playtime than the length of an average movie, so that's awesome for me.I appreciate the level of care and attention to detail put into this game. You can notice the love and passion the developers have for the genre. I know this is their first game, so achieving all of this is quite impressive already.Any technical issue you may encounter (especially in the early days), I'm pretty sure is going to be addressed by the developers. I haven't had any crashes, for example, so I had a very stable experience.Anyway, I recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I am about half-way through the game, and I feel at this point I have a solid grasp of the mechanics. For this reason, I am absolutely baffled by the negative reviews complaining about the teddy bear hugging recharge system. To explain, Europa (the player character) draws her shield (defenses) and her magic projectiles from the same bar. When the light bar runs empty either by getting hit by enemies or shooting projectiles, she's open to damage and can only take two hits without upgrades to vitality. It's very risk/reward as sometimes hitting enemies with magic bullets is the only way to open them to attack. She can recharge her light bar by hugging the teddy bear (which takes a few seconds) and getting a large boost that almost completely refills the bar, getting small recharges whenever she defeats an enemy or cancels out an enemy projectile, or getting a quick, medium-sized boost by hitting dead-center on a quick reload bar that pops up when you run empty, a system very much like the quick reload/cool down mechanic from Returnal. I really have to wonder how these reviewers are playing this game, because the charge system is very similar to the one Hollow Knight, and everyone thinks Hollow Knight is brilliant. The UI is just a bit different. Just like in Hollow Knight, you have to wait for an opening to charge up for a heal or you are going to get bodied. Actually, it's more forgiving than Hollow Knight since you can technically recharge your bar without having to damage enemies first.9 Years of Shadows has the look of the forgotten Turbo Grafix/PC Engine game . It sports gorgeous pixel animations with an overall style that feels like a cross between Sailor Moon and Saint Seiya. Europa is a young warrior who travels to a castle which is said to be the source of a curse that has plunged her world into chaos, stealing both color and vitality from the land. The game begins in black and white before it explodes into glorious, beautiful techicolor. If nothing else, the zones of the castle are colorful and lively.  The main gimmick is that Europa discovers a series of mystical armors through the her journeys on top of the standard metroidvania progression abilities like the double jump. You'll be swapping the armors for both progression and battle. Some enemies are weak against certain armors so changing to the same armor color as the glowing outline around their bodies means you will defeat them faster. They also have traversal abilities. The blue armor lets you swim up waterfalls. The green armor lets you burrow through passageways in the ground and so on. Some platforming sections will have you using several abilities in quick succession.It looks the game may have been first released in rough shape as I notice it has had a lot of patches in the span of a year. I have not encountered any issues in my first four hours as of May 2024. If there is one complaint I have is that the bosses are wildly inconsistent in how difficult they are. Most of them are cake-walks. I was able to take them down on the first try. There are a couple you might die too once or twice as their patterns might take you by surprise. The exceptions are the "Shadow" bosses hidden within worlds inside paintings. These guys almost demand either perfect reaction to their attack patterns or being able to nail the quick recharges on your light bar because they do not give you much breathing room. Unless the game completely goes sideways in the second half, I'd say 9 Years of Shadows is a metroidvania worthy of playing while you wait for Silk Song. Update: After finishing the game, my impressions largely remain the same. I encountered a few projectile glitches, all of which worked to my favor. There is an enemy on in the fire zone that shoots a slow moving bullet that explodes after a couple of seconds. I noticed maybe three times there would be an instance where the bullet fired but did not explode. We have to talk about the final boss. This one is of the most baffling I have come across, as the encounter simply doesn't feel right. This is a four stage affair, and I would say that it is a fine encounter up in until the third phase. The demon king stands upright and hovers in the air, floating around the arena as you dodge death beams and a rain of glowing red caltropes. Occasionally, he will summon rivers and pillars of hot air, and you have to ride those up to the a platform at the top of the stage as to continue the fight before getting bodied by a death flood on the lower area. After a few minutes up in the air, the platform breaks and you fall back to the ground. Something about his hit box seems off. I can't tell where the damageable section of his body is and he seems to have inconsistent iframes where sometimes he is open to damage during attack animations and sometimes not. A few times I took damage when the floor gave way and fell into some projectiles that were lingering on the screen.The fight should have stopped there because the fourth phase is some BS. You are transported to a small arena where you have to dodge about five kinds of projectiles going off at once. This phase looks impossible at first. The fights that required perfect reaction to the bosses attacks always seemed tough but fair even at their most frenetic. You'd need the reflexes of god himself to pull this phase off without a bit a cheese.Because I'm nice person I will give you the trick to betting this BS phase since I had to attempt it about fifty times. Change to the red armor and crouch down next to the boss's right leg. This way you with avoid the lasers and the floor beams about 90% of the time. When the death beam triangle starts to charge, take out the red orb. One hit with your halberd should do it. Just keep hugging the leg and chopping away. Only stop to avoid the floating sigils and to keep destroying the red orb. Now it's just a DPS race to the finish line. It's a shame that the final boss felt so unpolished. Even the really easy bosses were not bad. They were just easy to read and react to.

_childDocuments_.review: Features some very very outdated mechanics and odd design choices. Hardly a metroidvania; things you go out of your way for in short linear paths give you minimal upgrades; the armor shards provide you miniscule bonuses to damage for an individual armor piece. The save system is abysmally outdated, which wouldn't be an issue if the saves weren't sparse and occasionally very far from where you're trying to go. If you die and forgot to save recently enjoy redoing your hour of mundane grinding through enemies to reach a room you wanted to go to.The bosses are all damage sponges with a few fun exceptions. Enjoy dodging the same three attacks repeatedly while you wail on them for 10 minutes. My biggest gripe, and what soured me from a generally fun game to one I didn't finish, is the final section of the game. Half of the main gimmick you've been trained and used all game, the shooting and quick heal system for your ranged attack/health bar, is replaced with a burst attack that consumes 1/4 of the bar. Your manual health reload is replaced with a snails pace auto-reload that often will get you killed to the late games spammy bosses.I couldn't make it through the final boss. The last phase rains on you with projectiles and by taking away your ability to heal yourself for a pitiful slow auto-heal, as well as removing your ranged attack and rhythm-based reload, it was too much. I stopped having fun and gave up; you win game.The music and art is good.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty excited for 9 Years of Shadows. Between the killer artwork and the clear Castlevania inspirations, I thought we'd have a major new Metroidvania. The graphics are lovely and the controls are snappy and fairly intuitive. There are some decent platforming sections that make solid use of the protagonist's abilities. But the game is insanely linear in addition to being quite short. You can return to previous areas whenever you wish, but there's practically no reason to do so as you can easily get everything there on your first go. As such, there's not really any backtracking. You get a new ability and you use it to move forward and that's about it. There's almost never more than one way to proceed either. On very rare occasions there might be two short paths forward and one late-game section actually lets you tackle a multi-part objective in whichever order you wish, but the rest of the game is practically on rails.The game had a tendency to hard crash for me with a fair amount of frequency. This often happened ten or twenty minutes after I alt-tabbed and then maximized the game again, but sometimes it would just freeze on exiting an area or trying to fast travel. In the five hours the game lasted (my playtime is higher because I left it running a lot) the game crashed at least half a dozen times. I may have been an outlier but do note that you'll have to go back to your last save if this happens to you, as the game uses a classic saving system.The level design isn't bad but it lacks a sense of place and isn't at all memorable or interesting. Areas mostly all feel the same and are mostly a combination of different traversal challenges. The game's abilities are mostly tied to armors you'll find and the game changes you to the correct armor whenever you need to use it. For instance, once you enter a hot area, you'll automatically switch to the fire armor and can't switch back. The enemy variety is tiny, with a lot of recolors. Some enemies are weak to certain armor attacks but most aren't. It doesn't matter which armor you choose, for the most part.There's a single sidequest chain but it won't become clear what it's for until the end of the game. To complete this sidequest, you appear to have to 100% the game by finding all the musicians, completing their “quests” (you go and beat one or two weak minibosses and that's it), and you have to find all of the notes that you use to upgrade your health and mana. I found everything but three of these notes, so I couldn't complete the quest. But it isn't even worth it because you can only use the reward on the last boss anyway, which isn't nearly hard enough to require it.The gameplay is fine and the MC plays like Alucard in SotN, down to having a crummy backdash instead of a real dodge. Regular enemies are insanely easy to fight and present no challenge. Bosses are also easy, but can be a pain due to artificial difficulty. Instead of having a normal health bar, you have a mana bar that governs your helper's shots and it depletes when you shoot or take damage. If it depletes you can take just two hits by default. You can refill it instantly by pressing reload with the right timing like in Gears of War or Nioh.It's completely out of place here and, when I did need to retry bosses, it was because I missed the reload window by a fraction of a second and took a hit. The bosses are very boring to replay as they're mechanically very simple and the combat has little depth. If you're good at the instant reload, the game will be even more of a cakewalk. 9 Years of Shadow is decent enough but it's a huge letdown as a Metroidvania. It can be 100%ed in as little as five hours, it's linear, filled with boring enemies, and the combat just isn't all that ineresting even if it feels alright. Buy it on sale if you just want a 2D platformer but Metroidvania fans should keep their expectations in check.
