_childDocuments_.review: I have few complaints about this game. It's vibrant, lively and it's easy to pick up on the game mechanics quickly. The gameplay is smooth, the cutscenes are very well done. The animation is amazing, the way Europa's dress seems to flow, for example, is stunning.I have infinitely more praise than gripes about this game. The art, the sound, the mechanics are all beautiful.My gripes, though, are that the game seems to crash fairly often. I'm not sure what causes it. My other minor complaint is that the text on one of the scenes when changing floors was cut off on both ends, as it was too long to fit the screen. I could make out what it was saying, but still a very minor inconvenience.I absolutely recommend this game if you're a fan of the genre and art style. I'd rate the game a solid 9/10, honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: For the first few hours, it's a fun take on the metroid genre.  The graphics are smooth, the music is excellent, and the armor sets come with interesting movement capabilities.  But there comes a point when everything starts to feel the same.  A handful of unique enemy types are re-used in every zone.   Poison zone, fire zone, orphanage zone - all the same enemies.   Every area looks visually similar, and even the platform height, width, spacing - all too similar in every zone.  The level designs simply feel like increasingly lengthy and tedious combinations of the same few ideas.I wanted to like this game, but I found it too repetitive and tedious to see through the end.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: The game is generally fun, so I gave it a recommend.  The controls are tight.  The map is good. The puzzles here and there are satisfying.  If you enjoy a metroidvania, this is a good one to pick.The downsides are some glitches, like the map won't open sometimes, some of the bosses are just bullet chaos - and too many are immune to the halberd, so you have to wait for the "opening," hit it with special weapon, and then the halberd is effective - they went to that too many times. Can't skip dialogue you've already heard. And the worst part is the lack of fast travel. There's a single "elevator" but it doesn't go nearly enough places. Backtracking is a tedious chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty enjoyable and colorful pixelart metroidvania with ability and weapon upgrades and several areas to unlock and explore.  Unless you make notes or follow some tutorial, there definitely is more than 10-15 hours of gameplay (depending on how you play), this definitely isn't too short metroidvania. I'd rather give this game a star rating (4 stars out of 5 stars) - game has a lot of good things, but also some questionable design choices which made the game less enjoyable for me. Worst part of the game was the shield/energy bar system - for me it partially ruined the flow of traversing the environment little bit too much and it also makes (for an older player) boss battles really annoying and hard, I was about to stop playing the game early on. And there is NO way to single click skip dialogues before boss battles, sometimes these are 20+ lines before a boss battle, this is really annoying. Also, between areas, elevator sequences take way to long, even though game doesn't seem to be loading anything (on a fast NVMe drive) and you can't skip this either. Story is anime style gobbledygook and it didn't make much sense to me and world building and enemy designs aren't the greatest but not the worst either. I wish the music and color themes were used better, now these felt like wasted potential.I wish devs didn't simply put accessibility in game settings with pretty meaningless options like screen shake - make it possible for more people to enjoy this kind of games by adding proper difficulty settings, even if it would ruin the game for hardcore players, "git gud" folks can anyway select the "proper" difficulty setting. I doubt casual players that don't have a controller have any chance of beating later bosses, I personally had hard time and I was using Xbox controller.Technically things worked pretty fine. Controller worked fine. I had one freezing of game to a dialogue box in 20+ hours of playing. Game does suffer from a slightly choppy scrolling, 120 FPS setting makes no difference.Despite of these shortcomings, there is a lot to like. I did 100% the game. Thanks devs - I hope we see another game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game's art can't get enough praises. Other than that it has almost just the right amount of everything, not too hard or too easy, not too long or too short. Gameplay mechanics aren't anything new (remind me alot of Shantae games)  but are well executed, feel good and fluid. Boss fights are on the easy side but they do have interesting ideas. Good to play as a chill game and enjoy the story, audio and visual. At its price, definitely bang for yo bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania is the dominant gene in most genre descriptions. That is not the case here. 9 Years of Shadows is an action platformer first with elements of a Metroidvania. I'm not going to say there's no value to backtracking, but it isn't really necessary and I found most everything on my first run through each area. The game is beautiful and I'm obsessed with the character design. The combat and platforming are tight and responsive and the bosses are imaginative, screen filling spectacles. I enjoyed every single second with this game. I can't think of a single thing it doesn't do at least competently and most things it does incredibly well. It's a standout game and worth every cent. You wont regret playing this if you're a fan of 2D platforming action with beautiful pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this one to be released as it'd been on my wishlist from a past Next Fest, but I think I had missed the demo. It checks a lot of boxes and holds a lot of promise but I wouldn't recommend it to hardcore Metroidvania fans in its current incarnation unless you can snag a discount. For more casual fans this experience is definitely worth the cost of a movie ticketTLDR: beautiful visuals and music juxtapose against a short game that could be drastically improved with better enemy AI in combatPros:-magical anime girl transformation into cool mythology-inspired armor-the PIXEL ART is very gorgeous. Seriously. The first few minutes are all greyscale but everything is colored-in after that which is perfect for appreciating the rooms, enemies, your character, and the full-screen pixel art graphics used in the elevator transitions and cutscenes etc which are all incredible-the animations for everything similarly look great, apparently they were done by one person (voltanimation on twitter)-the music is similarly very good, ostensibly because you're gonna hear it for a while but also because the game seems to revolve around using music and musicians to lift the plot's curse-Game or map progression in Metroidvanias (IMO) can be irritating because you can spend a huge chunk of the game seeing rooms and map branches just out of reach until you get a 2nd jump (or similar), this game's short length bypasses that problem with an early Air Jump. Other abilities you earn open new progression for you but this is required by the main story instead of opening new exploration options. This is a big Con for many people who are bigger or more hardcore Metroidvania fans than I am-The Shield bar mechanics hold promise, it depletes first and you won't take "Health" damage until it is gone at which point you just hug your bear to recharge. While you DO have Shields you can hit in melee to recharge it or use it to fire a ranged attack at enemies (see my last Con)Cons:-Short, the game is about 5.5 hours long according to HowLongToBeat, which feels exacerbated by...-Mechanical improvements under the hood around loading times or skipping scenes would make for a much better experience as certain things just feel too drawn out or long and don't seem to be skippable: loading screens, death animations (not as bad as Too Human tho), but my least favorite was elevator transitions. They seem to be purposefully long so that you can learn a little more about Europa, the protag, which has the added benefit of helpfully hiding a loading screen. This absolutely sucks if you're backtracking, lost, looking for some way to progress because it feels like a 15-20 second break from gameplay and it really brought me out of the action and I found myself forgetting where I even wanted to go-Enemies are pretty disinteresting, they seem to follow a very rigid series of movements and telegraphed attacks (including bosses) so once you have seen an enemy a single time you can just steamroll them-While looking for launch-day impressions, I read a comment about how you can use the ranged attack as a machine gun and if you're even a little bit good at Gears of War-style reloading, you can basically do it ad infinitum. There is no drawback to ignoring your abilities and gunning everything down
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: The best way for me to describe this game would be "Castlevania Lite." A shorter, lighter Metroidvania with more inspiration from the Castlevania side of the equation. It's absolutely beautiful: the colour palette and pixel art are super gorgeous, accompanied by a great soundtrack. The use of different armour to grant you unique abilities is a neat mechanic, making exploring the castle super fun (you can turn into a mermaid to get around the water areas!). The highlight of the game, IMO, are the boss battles: they're all well-designed and provide just enough of a challenge without being too frustrating, and beating them feels very satisfying. My main criticism for the game is the dodge mechanic. The dodge mechanic consists of a backslide, which, while unique, is awkward to use. It works with standard enemies, who have only one, easily predictable attack, but for boss fights, not so much. In fact it's very possible to dodge one attack only to land in another attack! For a game like this, a parry mechanic would've been better. As it is, I spent most of the game avoiding attacks by hiding in corners or just letting the attack hit and then regain my energy by landing a counterattack. This can be a bit cumbersome as you have a limited amount of HP (two at the beginning, four at max) and you need to watch your MP as it doubles as your shield. The game isn't too difficult overall, but a parry mechanic and maybe more HP would've helped make the game more forgiving in the early stages.  Despite my criticisms I enjoyed the game overall. It's a nice, lovely Metroidvania and the devs show a LOT of promise. This was clearly a labour of love, and since they respond well to feedback I hope their next effort can expand on what made this game great and make something even greater.

_childDocuments_.review: This games was mostly good, it had a few annoyances like I can't seem to skip the boss  dialog or intro. But honestly I feel where it falls apart is the ending. For most of the game you have light meter protecting you health, for most of the game  if you lose your light you can do a reload game to get some back and if you fail that you  have to basically estus flask in that you are basically vulnerable for a period of time as you recharge. later you lose that and it gets replaced with a really slow recharge and you just have to deal with the last boss with this change. I honestly just did not like this change of the rules at all. the game is still  one of the most fun metroidvanias except for this last section.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and unfortunately I can say I was underwhelmed. The combat felt really lackluster and repetitive. Lots of standing around waiting for enemies to attack, spamming the attack button when they are open, and repeat until they're dead. Basically happens throughout most of the game. Not a lot of enemy variety either. I was pretty let down by the armor suit mechanic. Besides the different platforming mechanics you unlock with each one, there is no real fundamental difference between them. Attacking in each suit of armor acts exactly the same, except with some animation differences. Some suits of armor are stronger against enemies that are highlighted the same color, that was about it.I'd say the art, and some of the platforming sections, were the best part about the game. The music was pretty unforgettable and the story really was not executed well. Characters felt pretty insignificant including Europa, which is a shame because I thought she could've been more interesting. I think they tried to tell some of the surrounding details of the world/story through cryptic stones you found around the castle, but it ended up just leaving me confused. Feels like there are just gaps in the story writing, or maybe I missed something. Not too sure.There is definitely some potential in some of the ideas 9 Years of Shadows has, it just isn't fully fleshed out or executed well. Wishing the devs the best. Hope they can build off of this game and come back with something really cool in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of Shadow is a quality platform adventure that embraces its own unique themes and aesthetic, but die-hard fans of Metroidvanias might find the linearity of the progression to be a little too straightforward. Most games of the genre live or die by their traversal options and their combat, and while 9YoS does the latter really well, the former rarely requires a lot of thought or backtracking. A few branching paths for parallel exploration would have gone a long way. That said, it's a beautiful game, and the controls are tight. Boss fights are extremely challenging and prove to be the high points of difficulty within the game, requiring tight pattern recognition and control discipline to overcome. My first playthrough to 101% took just about 10 hours of real time, and it was hard to put down. Give it a shot, and enjoy the visuals and wonderful characterization. This feels like a middle chapter to a larger story setting, and it would be interesting to see if it spawns any sequels.

You got the colors, many musical things and a broad variety of boss styles where i cant see any red line connecting them all buts thats mybe just me.All in all its a good fun game and if the cons are no problem for you, you should give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: If this was released for the snes, it would've been a massive hit but we are in 2023 with competitor like hallow knight and blasphemous. It just does not deliver. A lot of the mechanics in the game is simply archaic.pros:-Amazing artstyle and unique-Music and sound effect on point-The concept of music and finding musician is original.cons:-Transition between rooms from bottom to above is absurd.-Transition in the elevator takes forever and cannot be skipped.-A lot of redundancy in term of enemies and map layouts/puzzles.-Not much incentive to kill enemies.-Simplistic upgrade and very limiting.-Cannot look down.-Aiming with your range attack is painfully hard.-100% of your companion's dialogue is unnecessary.-Maps are very small and the length of the game is very short as well.-Backtracking is minimal and there isn't much secrets in the game.-Many empty rooms for some reason...-I've died way more from contact damage than bosses attacks.-The recharge/shield system is the hardest thing in the game.-Puzzles are "toddler" easy-Boss looks amazing but ridiculously easy except some end game. They are extremely pattern oriented. -Final boss takes forever to kill in comparison to anything else in the game.The concept of elemental damages has been over used in the last couple decades...For a 25$ game, I expected something with more depth for sure.Currently sitting at a generous 6/10. Maybe some stuff will be address for dlc but at the moment there isn't anything "wow" about that game other than the art.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games that runs on my laptop.Combat is fairly simple. The game has a unique health mechanic that encourages aggression/evasion, which can be super troublesome for players that aren't into getting up-close-and-personal like in other 2D action games (Mega Man Zero; Hollow Knight, Katana Zero, etc.)The world isn't as sprawling as something like Super Metroid, but that means there's little in terms of getting lost. Movement is tied to progression, so anything interesting is gonna show up when you go somewhere you haven't been. Since the world is more "concise" than "massive," this can mean you finish the game in under 8 or 10 hours.The music is great. The visuals are nice. And the controls are responsive. Other games are surely better: but for a studio's first game, it's really solid. I'm excited for more, and wish the developers the best. And am keeping an eye out for their next work(s.)

_childDocuments_.review: The main characters power system is a very cool idea. The gameplay is unique and interesting. If you wanna use ranged attacks you have to use your own "health." However the world and story are an incoherent mess of the most "this will tug at your heart" drivel. It's 10% a unique experience 90% the same pointless crap you've seen before in other indie titles. Worse so because the things you encounter make no sense. Enemy variety is non-existent. I'd recommend it to metroidvania enthusiasts like myself on a deep sale. HOWEVER I do look forward to the studio releasing a sequel polishing the weak world and story. I think with a bit of cohesion this could be something great.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I really wanted to like. There's a lot of good things. Pretty, handcrafted graphics and levels. Handcrafted is always better than procedural generation. My main issue with the game is that at least the first part of it is too linear. For me, good metroidvania should have exploration. There's also no experience points. There's only gold, but you can't buy anything with just gold. You also need limited relics. This means, if you hit a wall with a boss, that's it, nothing you can do really. Speaking of that, the difficulty can be quite unforgiving. You literally die from just a few hits. Also ranged attacks drain your life. Regaining life is relatively easy, but considering how fast it disappears, the fight can be over before you can react. Note that this review is not a hard "no". It's definitely not a bad game. Maybe I'll get back to this game later with more patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is pretty good. It's not super ground breaking or anything but it does what it sets out to do and it does it fairly well. It's fairly short only taking me 10 hours to get 100% completion. (Though I did manage to get myself softlocked and ended up leaving the game open for an hour or 2 while I tried to find cheats to fix my mistake).The combat is pretty fluid and enjoyable but lacks a lot of challenge outside of the boss fights, and even then, only a few of them pose any real challenge. The "active reload" style mechanic to instantly heal is a neat concept and was fun to use though it is incredibly overpowered. (It was even more overpowered in early versions of the game since it always healed to full every time, now it only heals a portion and heals less each consecutive proc within a short time frame and the timing also gets more difficult).The map was very expansive and diverse and traversing the map never felt too difficult. It was always clear when I didn't have a required power to progress through an area and those areas were never too far from the games fast travel room or the location where you get the required power. Speaking of fast travel, the game only has a central elevator that connects to 6 different areas. While not too bad, if you don't manage to get everything in a given area on your first run through, it will end up taking quite a while to back track as there is no fast way to navigate to older sections. The lack of fast traversal options is also mildly annoying and running across the map to find the few items I missed in my playthrough was a bit of a chore.Overall I'd rate this game a solid 6/10. It has a very well written story with a simple premise while keeping things fresh with a new coat of paint on the tropes it uses. The characters are decently interesting although most lack depth. The combat is fun to play with though it gets a bit repetitive after a while. Movement in the game feels nice but is lacking some options for faster room traversal (such as a dash of some kind, the backdash isn't great since it isn't really all that much faster and that's only if you flick perfectly).If you are looking for a decent game that has a nice metroidvania feel without being too large, then I highly recommend this game. I bought it the same day I finished it (Oct 8th 2024) and as of now it is still on sale until the 13th for 50% off so now is a great time to grab it if you have been on the fence about it.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Infinitely regenerating shield doesn't balance well with this combat system. In fights where you have enough time to regenerate your shield between attacks, you can get hit over and over without it mattering. In fights where the enemy keeps attacking and you can't regenerate, your low health and limited mobility options feel disproportionate to how much punishment bosses can take before they finally die.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable experience, it is a good game for a coulple days, maybe a week if you aim for 100% The Level Desing is a mixture of good and dumb desicions, and the lack of fast travel and mobility definetly hurst the feeling specially when none of the enviroments feels memorable, this can be due to the small but decent size of the map.The Presentation is inmaculate, the enviromental detail shows passion and love for Pixel Art and the Color is just everywhere.The combat is simple and some bosses feel like damage sponges rather than challenges, i  die least 4-5 times during the entire game, 2 of those at the final boss which is actually a good one. Along side with the looks The Music is the strongest aspect of the package, IS SO GOOD and charming, if none of the enviroments feels memorable the music sure is.The Characters, well... exist, besides Europa all of them are collectable NPCs but their presentation art is absolutely gorgeous.The Story is decent, Good guy, Bad guy, fight, lesson. Overall is good game, a good step forward for the devs who can keep the positives and improve on the negatives for new projects.7.8/10 (The music and art carry the entire game)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few pieces in but I can confidently say; My pros: The music and the art style with its color palette together makes for a great viewing experience. The game has popping colors and I think the design of the main character looks sick. The music I'm also impatiently waiting for that to hit streaming services or for a place I can purchase it. I immediately fell in love with its electronic style in the main menu and the soothing but rhythmic beats are a joy to listen to. An added bonus, the game runs flawlessly on the steam deck without having tuned any settings. Generally  on a full battery with default settings the game will run  you about 5 hours of battery life (which for a metroidvania, that's good). My cons:Not many, only thing i would say is since I'm used to playing games with a bit more stick to them like Castlevania it's taking me a minute to getting used to how easily Europa can move. So far from what I've played the back-tracking aspect of metroidvania's doesn't seem *as* much as I'd thought I'd see but maybe that's more of me being used to things like Castlevania and Metroid's level designs.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually a pretty fun game regardless if it is a "metroidvania" or not doesn't matter much.  Everything with it is great so far aside from a few early technical problems that many gems of games have had in the past.  Keyboard and mouse custom controls could use some work, I am a kb+mouse player more than a controller user and the controls are solidly designed for left hand on keyboard and right hand on mouse, I decided to try swapping this  around and couldn't adjust it too well, so instead of my usual method of using only a keyboard for fast paced 2d games, I am stuck using opposing hands to what I am used to... for the record I grew up when 8 bit computers were common and we played on keyboards and no mice, so I usually had right hand on arrow keys for directions and left hand for things like attack/jump/use.  Im stuck so far in this using WASD and changed some of my attack stuff to JKLI on the right hand, but it still feels backwards to me and although was an improvement over having to use my clunky mouse It still lead to many embarrassing deaths at the first major boss that I think I could have handled easier with better control setup on kb.  Dying is currently a bit annoying because it happens with very low health max in the start of the game and reloading takes a bit of time, so right now Im entering the second area and when I die to an early monster I have to reload in the 1st area and back through a load / transition screen to the next area again.Still an awesome game at this point just wanted to address those small issues so far.  If they fix keyboard customizing and maybe make the loading faster somehow it would be great but I think I could adapt to beating the game after a while anyway, would just be a nice bonus :D. _childDocuments_.review: This is a very pretty game I can recommend with some caveats. The most pertinent is that the game is very bare bones.  It's short, I've fully cleared the game and my total played time says 13 hours, which is probably inaccurate given that I've left the game running several times as I got pulled away to other things. It's also lacking in depth.  Every ability you gain to traverse the castle is implemented well, but besides the movement abilities the armors offer no change in combat style beyond the visual.  The water armor might have a slightly longer horizontal heavy attack, the earth might have a slightly higher vertical but these differences, if they exist and I haven't just been fooled by the visuals, are minuscule at best.  For most of the game you will switch armors only to target weaknesses, and it's only worth it if those weaknesses are on enemies that would otherwise guard your attacks or take either one hit to kill with weakness or more than one combo to kill without.Some of the narrative elements are also somewhat lacking, not because of the subject matter but more on the implementation side of things.  If you're here you probably watched the trailer, which shows a magical hero style transformation sequence in the style of sailor moon or saint seya.  Imagine my disappointment upon grabbing the first armor and getting a flash of light and finding the character equipped with the armor.  There's nothing -wrong- there, but it seems like a missed opportunity to go for some easy style points.  The creators clearly knew the genre they were referencing, as seen by the trailer, and a something as simple as the outline used in the trailer as an interstitial between the gown and the armor would have really added something.  In a similar vein, the save rooms have a piano and your character plays it to save.  Unfortunately, the music of whatever area you're in is still playing and Europa only knows the one piano jingle so they clash every time.   Dedicated save room music would have worked, or silence until your character plays.My last critique is that the dialogue is weak to the point that I don't remember a single line.  The emotions of the narrative were conveyed, but honestly I feel as though that mostly came down to the sprite work. I would still recommend the game as the visuals and music are excellent, but I can't recommend buying it at full price given the lack of depth or replay value.  I've beaten this game and, while satisfied, have no desire to play it again any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic gothic metroidvania style game.  I highly recommend it.  The movement powers feel excellent, making the map fun to explore.  The combat is engaging.  The boss fights are challenging but enjoyable.  Some of them use bullet-hell mechanics to up the difficulty.  There are also a fair number of bosses, which is great if you're a fan of big battles.  The story is above average for the genre, relying on some fantasy tropes but also incorporating enough original elements to elevate it a bit.Some of the boss fights will require multiple attempts, so I wish any startup animations were skippable, but that's a pretty minor complaint.  The game originally released with some bugs that were causing random crashes, and these appear to have been patched out.  As of this writing, I was still experiencing some glitches where projectile sprites would disappear during the final boss battle, but this was infrequent and I assume the devs will correct this as they seem quite active.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, I really do.  I can't in good conscience, however.The spritework in the game is absolutely gorgeous, and Europa, the main character, has a striking character design.  While incredibly linear in progression, the game opens up quite a bit once the third Armor is unlocked and its traversal abilities are obtained.  The different abilities are refreshing, and can make some really clean movement for getting through rooms quickly.That said, there's some bothersome design choices that really drag down the game as a whole.Combat, even against normal mobs, is really draining.  Europa has a three-hit combo quick attack, as well as a single strike heavy attack that can be chained at the end of the three-hit combo.  Before upgrades, these attacks deal single digit damage, even when matching weaknesses.  After upgrading, the heavy attack *might* deal double-digit damage, but usually only if you are matching weakness, or chain it at the end of the three-hit combo.  That wouldn't be too bad, but even trashmobs seem to have 20+ hp, so it frequently takes 3-4 full combos to kill even basic enemies, with much more required for some of the larger ones.The health system has some novelty, where you have an energy bar that functions as both ammo for your ranged attack, and a barrier that protects your actual HP from enemy attacks.  As long as you have even a single pixel in the bar, any hit won't harm your actual HP.  Once the bar fully drains, you need to activate a long recovery animation to restore about 3/4 of it, or there's an early upgrade that adds a one-shot QTE to restore 50% that gets diminishing returns the more you invoke it.  Of course, this entire mechanic gets thrown out the window and spiked directly into the trash once the final major upgrade is obtained, where instead of getting a manual recharge, you get an auto charge for the barrier with an absolutely punishing downtime if your bar gets fully depleted.Major Bosses are just damage sponge puzzles, with long periods of complete invulnerability while you wait for them to manifest darkness crystals for you to blast in order to actually damage them, all the while draining your health and resources.  God forbid you run out of ammo while a crystal is still active, since the bosses tend to unleash a massive attack if you don't break their crystals in time to stun them.  Minor bosses are just damage sponges, period.  Spamming attacks while you try to outlast and kite them.Minor upgrades are sparse.  There are three major types of non-progression upgrades:  Health, Light, and Armor.  Each type of upgrade requires its own special collectible, plus a pittiance of an otherwise useless currency.  The first Health Upgrade requires 5 of its Collectible, and even if you fully explore everything available up to that point, won't be obtainable until around the time you find the third armor.  The second requires 8 more of that collectible, and basically isn't available until just before the final bosses.  Light bar upgrades are much more plentiful, since the first upgrade only requires two collectibles, and it slowly increasing, with the last requiring four.  Armor upgrades are a flat two per, at least for the first four.  The final Armor upgrade is a game-long series of sidequests.  The upgrades themselves give a nice aura around Europa, but barely improve your damage.  Instead of 2-3 per hit, you're now dealing 4-5, so nearly double, but as mentioned earlier, enemies are such damage sponges that it really doesn't feel impactful.Level design is fine.  All the different sectors have unique looks to them and gorgeous backgrounds, but it can be somewhat tedious to traverse at times.  There's no meaningful fast travel system, and while the game's map isn't super huge, it's still large enough to make traversing to and from different areas tedious if you missed an item in a certain area.  The game is very good at telling you where to go via the environment and different pathways available, and all hidden exits are marked on the map, so even if you missed a breakable wall, you can easily locate it on the map and figure out how to get back there.  Traversal through rooms is relatively easy.  Enemy placement can be annoying at times, but there isn't really anything unfair about it.  The main difficulty spikes in the game come from the major bosses and a few of the minor ones, with an absolutely massive spike on both the last minor boss and the final one.The TL;DR of this review is there's a ton of neat or novel ideas, but it gets dragged down by some minor annoyances plus a mechanic curveball that completely invalidates the gameplay loop up to that point.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine pouring all your heart and soul into making beautiful pixel art and music just to ruin it with a core game that isnt fun.As a fan of Metroidvania's I figured this game would be right up my alley. But this game is all flashy and no actual substance. You use your own "HP" to shoot at enemies, WHICH IS A REQUIREMENT TO EVEN KILL SOME OF THE ENEMIES.You cannot regen this HP outside of 2 methods, 1) Completely running out of this HP Bar, or by melee'ing an enemy. When you completely run out, you will be given a gears of war style QTE reload where you need to stop the meter in the middle or it will fail. This "Pass" zone will sometimes get smaller making it more and more difficult to get right. Failing to get this QTE meter will just fail and you cannot use this method to regen your HP. But even so, when you DO succeed at hitting this meter, you will only be rewarded with 50% of your max HP. Which gives you like 3-4 shots before having to do this whole song and dance all over again. Not to mention that you are still only at 50% of your HP. So of course any actual damage you receive is still counting towards your remaining HP (which never seems to be over 50% at any given time). If you do fail this QTE, you need to get to cover and hold down the fire button to perform a "lullaby" which will give you about 70% of your HP but leaves you completely vulnerable for about 3 seconds. If you are hit while performing this lullaby you will just die. Thats GGs. You will then be sent back to your last save. (There is no auto save or checkpoint system) Which in some areas could cause you to redo 10+ minutes of work, just to get back to the one room you were struggling in. To make it even more annoying, you cannot melee enemies for HP anymore UNTIL you perform a lullaby. So you then turn into this fragile thing that dies in 1 hit from ANYTHING. You will need to run away and hide in a corner to avoid being sent back to your last save. Not to mention that your upgraded suits have to be toggled in combat (but not while attacking of course) Some enemies have a shield around them and will take reduced damage unless you swap to a matching suit color. But if youre already in combat it wont let you swap. (Unless you touch water, to which the game auto swaps you to the water suit. Which is perfect to put enemies that arent damaged by the water suit in a room full of water.)  So you have to move away and then swap. The entire time im playing this im just thinking to myself. This was clearly made by someone that said "Metroid just isnt annoying enough. Its too streamlined and fun. We cant have that" Everything is so annoying and obtuse. Id rather be replaying Metroid Fusion for the 50th time than play another minute of this.

_childDocuments_.review: There's an ok story here, and some nice visuals... but the game itself is pretty... meh... Worth a grab after all other metroidvanias are done... but not one I'd recommend really to anyone with anything else they might want to play. Especially given how the fights are at end game... god some of these are just ungodly frusterating and slow... Imagine something that is like the length of a boss rush, but it's all just one boss, and super stupdily slow because it's an absolute tank, it's like you're trying to beat end game dark souls 2 bosses with the ladle here... Doable but just... why... why would you want too? First, combat... it kind of sucks. You have super simplistic combat options/movesets. So it's often very straightforward what you can/can't do. And often this means instead of an engaging fight or duel of movement... it's just dodging... dodging... possitioning... positionoing... and then there's an opening every thirty seconds or whatever. Some bosses are worse, others better, but overall the combat most of the time feels rather... lacking. Several enemy attacks are also just not fair/poorly designed, with no reliable counter or ability to see coming. One of the worst is a big underwater snake boss, when it comes in from the left side of the screen in it's final phase... the red particle/visual effect that signifies it's about to come in doesn't show up in time, I've recorded myself literally dodging wthin two frames of it showing up on my screen at the very edge... and still not being close to avoiding that attack. There are just some issues or areas here and there like that. Mostly, it's not bugs though, just... not very fun or inspired feeling combat. It's reminicsant of very old school original metroidvania games, but not in a good way, since those often still felt better, with less long dodging periods where you can't even get a hit in, like this one has.Next, platforming, the ideas of different armor types that let you traverse different enviornments or stuff sounds cool... but honestly most of the traversal is pretty linear. Like going into tunnels, nothing special there, floating with the fire thing blasting up against objects, very straightforward, going through poison with the green suit, or going through water with the blue armor... all of these just directly open up a path, that's the same old same old, or give you the very basic addition of movement often pretty linear. So moving through the enviornments isn't really that fun or challenging, no careful air dashes, managing timings through hazards, or using attacks that double as movement things or wall tacking or whatever. They've got the most basics of these ideas down... but didn't push them. So overall, colorful as it becomes, exploring and movement is not really engaging or challenging, so it's just an ok here, nothing great, but not bad either.And the map and lack of good teleport or travel options end game is pretty bad, so explroing aroudn to find everything again... very slow and not very fun... one of the few games I just said screw it and went to finish it before finding/finishing everything with. So ya, not terrible or anything, arguably not ad, though frustrating/annoying with some fights to a notable degree.... but overall just not that good either. An ok to waste some time, sadly, not much more. Shame since it looked like it had good potential. Oh, and if you think it's a bad/childish story because of the teddy bear, don't, that part at least isn't an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10An incredibly gorgeous metroidvania game and fun gameplay, just unfortunately hindered by some issues.9 Years of Shadows is a game that tells the tale of a world afflicted by a curse that takes away all color, both literally and metaphorically, and a woman who decides to go into the source of the curse to try and lift it. The game stands out immediately by how incredibly gorgeous it is, complete with some incredibly well animated cutscenes, and it also plays well right off the bat too, with the character moving at a decent speed and able to attack while moving (something not often seen in 2D games). The game then unfolds as most metroidvanias do, soon acquiring some new skills and learning how to use them while also finding some areas that are blocked off until other abilities are acquired later on.Overall, the game is great and has a solid story, with the stunning art style never getting old - it always feels like playing a piece of art. It also has some very creative abilities used for both exploration and combat. While there are some common abilities from metroidvania games like double jump and air kicks, some other abilities are also completely fresh and unique, with these abilities being often mixed together and used during some boss fights in clever ways.The game starts off great, but then loses some steam after the beginning and it's where some of the issues start to appear. First, the enemies are repetitive: once you've seen some, you've seen all of them. Some enemies have some variants that shoot different projectiles or have different attack patterns, but they're still mostly the same enemy. Then there are the bosses - rather than have them present a difficulty curve with early bosses being easier and latter bosses being harder, the first half of the game instead has a sort of mix up in difficulty where some early bosses are a lot harder than some other bosses that come afterwards. I specifically remember one boss that presented literally no challenge at all - I didn't even get to see if the boss had any attacks because the mechanics for making the boss vulnerable was so easy that I was just constantly doing it and then hacking away at the boss, finishing the fight with no damage taken at all.The game is also sorely lacking in character progression, which was definitely a bummer for me. It's a short game for a metroidvania, so it makes sense that the game has no leveling up, but I was still expecting more character progression. You can find blue and red notes to improve your light bar and vitality and each armor can be upgraded once to cause more damage... But that's it.There is also one major issue during the last section of the game - in spoilers, just in case. Overall, recommended - it's a fun game that's incredibly gorgeous, but sadly hindered by the forementioned issues.

_childDocuments_.review: so the game has a few beautiful elements and runs well. so why am i not recommending it?It has a design decision that i find incredibly frustrating.your life is ammo for a special attack.so far, so good - lots of games do that.but this special attack, doesn't do high damage, just basically the same damage as one of your hard attacks.it also is required for specific enemies and boss shields.about 4 hours in now and all my deaths are due to boss battles where i am struggling with lock on for this special attack just flat out not working on boss areas that have to be damaged down to get the boss into a phase where it can actually really be damaged.So i burn down all my health, put myself into a position where i can be 1-2 shot, by design.there are of course ways to recover this life/shield energy, but it recovers much slower than you spend it per bullet, and the number of shots needed to get through boss barriers is typically 3-6 even at this very early stage of the game, this is enough to completely deplete your health bar, even with upgrades.The game has some good potential, but this one design decision keeps me from being able to enjoy it, since every boss turns into a battle with the lock on button and regeneration mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: 9 years of shadow is somewhat decent, but ultimaltely not a very good metroidvania. I do not regret playing it once, but not going to replay it in future.Your heroine explores different parts of a big castle, battling monsters and collecting stuff along the way. Each area has its own theme (fire,water,poison,etc…) and the corresponding power-up that allows you to solve the puzzles in that area and continue your journey. End of the area is usually a boss fight. Also each wing has a few optional bosses.PROS:+ very good visual style and general aesthetics. Sprites, portraits, locations, background illustrations and so on are all vibrant and top-notch;+ layout of the castle is decent, the locations do not feel samey;+ couple of interesting boss fights (mb 2-3 for the entire game);CONS:- enemy variety is not great, a lot of reskinned monsters;- difficulty is insultingly low, you will steamroll like 90% of the game. Srsly, most boss fight (with a few exceptions) you will win with 1-2 tries, regular enemies are literal trash; No option to change difficulty either (even after you complete the game);- traversal is…annoying. The castle is big and you got basically only one way to fast travel – the big central elevator with a few stops. Everything else is you running by foot, with gets really old very fast;- upgrades are meh. Just small numerical increases, nothing fancy. The plot-related powers are also kinda uninspired, ive used only the basic hit attack all game;- the game is rather short for a metroidvania. I did a 100% items run in like 7hTL;DRA game you might want to play if you are starving for a new metroidvania, but nothing really fancy besides the looks. Gameplay gets boring pretty fast.

_childDocuments_.review: Well...  It pains me to write this because I really wanted to leave 10/10 but I can't.  It gets 4/10.  It feels like 70% of the game is just flipping through the different traversal methods granted by the armor.  You change colors, attacks stay pretty much the same.  Your heavy attack changes just a little bit, you deal a little extra (or less) damage to enemies based on their element and what armor you're in.  No heavy attacks in the air, no air combos; you hit and fall.  Not special attack per armor which is a shame; I feel that was a monumental lost opportunity.  On bosses most of the meaningful damage I was able to inflict came from charging up the melee attack and getting that quick burst in but if you get clipped by any damage the charge is cancelled. Fighting regular enemies just felt like a nuisance; yes they drop money but that money is only used for the upgrade to each of the armor types.  Once all the armor sets are upgraded the money in the game no long has any use.  There's not a leveling system; the enemies are really just kind of there to be annoying, or so it felt to me.  There's collision so you can't get hit and try to ghost through them either...  You either have to either kill them or (if there's enough room) jump kick/bounce over them.  I feel like a lot of love went into the game but it just didn't have enough story to redeem the issues I had with combat.  If you miss a save room after taking down a boss...well, don't do it because you will have to go through the fight again.  I only had trouble with a few of the bosses (and there are a lot, I did enjoy that bit at least) and forgot to save immediately after I think two of them.  If you get the game on sale and know going in you're not expecting in depth combat it's not a bad game, it just needed a little something else...  I feel the creators could even upgrade it over time if they wanted to, it's certainly not beyond improvement or repair.  (Looking at you, Lost Ruins.)

_childDocuments_.review: It starts as a fun game with solid controls, somewhat mediocre but passable combat, and an okay story. If this is an early experience with the genre, it's a good start. If you have played any other games, some problems will quickly arise. They start appearing around the halfway point.The dialog starts getting boring and cringey, to the point where I was just mashing buttons until I skipped all of it. It feels like Europa has some exposition to say about every single boss before the fight, which adds nothing of value to the story.Combat never evolves beyond a couple of abilities you pick up early on. The same basic attacks are your only option throughout the game.The map is missing some key quality of life features, mainly tracking pickups you already collected or at least marking what you skipped, which makes going for 100% a drag. This is compounded by the lack of a quick travel system. The only option is a main elevator that only serves to connect the different areas together.Most of the bosses seem to only exist to pad out the game; they basically just jump around and attack in a pattern and never deviate from that. Most are just bullet hell-type bosses, and at points, it feels like you encounter a new one every 5 minutes. I do realize most of them are optional; they are only required for 100%, but it's very apparent they went for quantity instead of quality. They're usually super easy, but occasionally they ramp up the difficulty curve to the moon, only for the next boss to be a punching bag.I didn't encounter any game-breaking bugs, but I did have a couple of cheap deaths when the game would constantly give me damage for no apparent reason.

_childDocuments_.review: 9 Years of shadows is a game i feel people are being to harsh on. It's honestly an amazing metroidvania that while more linear than most, exceeded my expectations in many ways. Mostly in its visuals, the pixel art on display here is top of the line and deserves to stand next to blasphemous, rain world, moonscars and death's gambit! I was constantly in awe with the spritework and environments. Truly a gorgeous game but that alone isn't enough for a pleasant experience. Luckily 9 years of shadows also nails the gameplay!Exploring the world of 9 years of shadows is a joy, not only due to the gorgeous visuals but also because the level design is tight. And while yes, i agree the game is relatively linear and backtracking is rarely needed, the exploration is still pretty metroidvania like. With side paths for collectibles, shortcuts and ability gating. This is an area the game is critiqued a lot for, but i actually like a more focused one every now and then. What also helps make the level design fun is the diverse and extremely satisfying movement. It starts of with a basic but responsive control set but the new mechanics added on top of that are very unique and fun.The system of switching between different elemental armors or stances, each with their own moveset and traversal mechanics, was really well executed. The water armor that let you smoothly jump between columns of water was especially fun. Later areas that chain these different types of movement together are very satisfying. In part because the game quickly switches stances for you when you jump into the according element so you don't need inhuman reaction speed to quickly switch. Just direct the joystick in the right direction and enjoy the smooth platforming that while not hard, is still satisfying.In fact the whole game leans more on the easier side, especially for regular enemies. This is because the health system in 9 years of shadows is that you have a few hearts that you can only regenerate at save points and a shield bar that protects said hearts. This shield is depleted on taking hits but also when using the rather powerful magic attacks. This creates a risk reward gameplay loop where you trade survivability for damage. You can ofcourse regen this shield by channeling for about 2 seconds. For regular enemies this is easy, just go stand away from them and heal up but for bosses this is a different story.This game has a HUGE array of bosses for you to fight. Way more than i expected for a game of this size. Luckily nearly all of these are enjoyable and while rather simple, still very unique! There's even a . These bosses range from on the easy side to pretty challenging in my opinion. The final boss especially took a few tries but in the end all of them are very doable when you learn the mechanics. In fact i think this game had a perfect difficulty! Tough but fair bosses, and regular enemies that serve as a fun distraction without being frustrating. What also helps reduce frustration is that in most cases, the save point is right next to the boss room.  No annoying runbacks that are for some reason popular? 9 years of shadow uses an old school save system though where dying literally sends you back to the last save state, losing all progress. Beware of this after you killed a boss or you'll have to fight them again, learned that the hard way haha! I'm generally not a fan of this system, but since saves were right by the boss, and regular enemies were a breeze, i found this system to be quite leanient.What then remains to be discussed is the music, story and technicallity. In regards to music i wasn't the biggest fan, although it did fit and gave the game a bit of an old school castlevania vibe (the backdash as well). Story then was in my opinion rather well executed. I really liked the premise, overal story and the main character. During loading screens, which take place on elevators, the heroine took some time to ponder in an attempt to not lose courage. These moments added a LOT to the character in my opinion, and made the rather long load screens not as annoying.Still though the loading screens are relatively long and once you've exhausted all the dialogue you'll just have to sit and wait. What annoyed me more than this was the fact that boss intro cutscenes were unskippable so doing them again took you a few seconds extra because of this. Other than load times though i had no major tech issues, no lag or bugs. I did however encounter one crash right at the end during a cutscene after i had beaten the final boss. I had to force quit and thus didn't get the achievement. Luckily i had the boss down to a T so i quickly beat them again. A tip to avoid this is to not spam the next button during cutscenes or dialogues.In the end 9 years of shadows really impressed me with it's gorgeous art, fun & unique movement, varied & challenging bosses and engaging story. The soundtrack fit the game well and the technicalities worked good enough not to hinder my enjoyment. I think the quality on display here is certainly worth the asking price and worth it for any metroidvania fan. This is a rather accesible one that despite the jump at the end remains fair. The pseudo linearity could also be good for newcomers to the genre who are afraid of getting lost otherwise. The mapping system also works very well for this so in general there's no real excuse to mis out on this one. Just one of the many amazing metroidvania's that 2023 blessed us with.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful world plagued by horrific input.As compelled as I am to see the rest of the art for the game, the issues I have with the controls make that impossible. All of your unique traversal abilities are bound to the same button which makes smooth traversal (e.g. gliding into serpent form) difficult. Combat is mostly pounding one button 3 times then tapping one more, because the charge attack takes too long for most boss damage windows, cancels when hit, and a large number of bosses I fought had bullet hell mechanics meaning getting hit is very likely. The other suits don't give any visual or mechanical combat changes, except for the last one.However, BY FAR my most hated input issue is the "upgrade" to quick heal when your shield depletes. This game has a Hollow Knight healing system where you hold a button to heal. Early on you get an upgrade to do a press the button at the right time" progress bar to quick heal. It's weaker than normal healing, the bar is over your head but the uses left are on your shield bar (3 uses, each weaker than the last), it delays and/or requires multiple inputs to do normal heals, and just overall is jank. Additionally, if you get hit while healing, you get stopped (which is fine) but then there is a delay and new input required to try again. Healing is also interrupted by basically any other input. I could handle most of this if I could just disable the rhythm healing game mechanic, but you can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Reasonably entertaining Metroidvania-type game. Good points - lovely graphics and visual style, unintrusive music and a good control system plus great bosses. It's got a lot of good points but it doesn't hang together as well as many other metroidvanias. Would still recommend though!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to be able to recommend this game in good conscience. It genuinely has a lot going for it! But ultimately such an endorsement would be half-hearted at best. 9 Years of Shadows has been plagued by a myriad of bugs since launch, and although many of the more serious ones have been patched, some persist. The standout one for me was a problem where the regeneration of light (which functions as both your "shields" and "mana" equivalent resource in this game) failed to function consistently near the end of the game, making the final boss's frustrating jump in difficulty even harder to deal with. I reported this issue in the bug thread here and gave it some time in the hope this would be patched, but it has not been acknowledged in the months since.It's possible you could have a great time with this game! If you don't run into bugs, there's a lot of beautiful pixel art and impressive animations. Those alone were what sold me on this in the first place. The game's aesthetic is great, and themes of music and color play well with it. The music is beautiful, though not especially memorable. The story is just serviceable, but honestly that's fine for a game in this genre.If you're looking for a deep metroidvania, though, this isn't it. Only a couple of items are hidden out of sequence, so there is little to no reason to revisit previous areas once you clear them, which is a shame because most of your upgrades are exclusively or primarily for traversal. Combat tends to be pretty monotonous after a while, as the elemental rock/paper/scissors is purely a question of numbers with no other difference in gameplay. Major story bosses are somewhat of an exception, with most of them having a unique gimmick that makes the fight more engaging by asking you to combine traversal techniques with combat around a large arena. Unfortunately, the endgame kind of fails to bring it all together, with the final boss relying primarily on frantic attack patterns in a lengthy endurance match that is an enormous jump in difficulty compared to anything else the game asks of you.I missed that there even was a Kickstarter for this until it released, so I didn't come to it with any expectations from that, but I still came away disappointed. I hope that the devs take it as a learning experience and find success in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Astonishingly beautiful, full of heart and sound and color. 9 Years of Shadows offers a lean metroidvania experience with little to no time wasted. The art style evokes equal parts Symphony of the Night, Sailor Moon, and Saint Seiya and portrays a beautiful fantasy world in every area of the haunted castle. The game begins deceptively easy, and slowly on-boards the player with every tool they will come to have at their arsenal and bringing intense challenge shortly after you feel just confident enough to use your new abilities on the fly. As for the game's story, it features a wonderfully written protagonist, a colorful cast of secondary characters, and enough heart and emotion its in core narrative to bring it all together by the end. I was able to 100% the game in about 10 hours, and it felt like a beautiful 10 hours well spent. An all around solid Metroidvania experience with the pixelart being worth the price of admission alone, players are in for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Worth buying at full price. Everything about this game is pretty. The art is amazing, the music is at times melancholic, fast-paced, and relaxing as necessary. Each character you meet is uniquely designed and fascinating. The game itself plays like a flowing platformer reminding me of Ori and the Blind Forest smoothness.The story is okay, too. Somewhat predictable, I found. Interesting enough.This game is a boss run platformer, yes. Every boss is different. Every boss is exciting and new. I most enjoyed the fish boss because of how unique almost every boss is.But it's the story of the gameplay mechanics that REALLY bug me. I felt like "I've played this story of character power growth before, again and again" because you must collect the gods' weapons (for whatever reason) and they are as trite and cliché as it is possible to get: Zeus's Lightning, Poseidon's Water, Gaia's Earth.They don't need to be labelled this way. There's no points for originality labelling them this way. But that's what they are.It's not keeping with the aesthetic of music or colour. And the POTENTIAL of playing with colour and lack there-of is... under-utilized, I fear. I swear they started this project with a FANTASTIC idea, but due to time constraints and marketing, dumbed the powers down so that they might be understood by a three-year-old. Which I think is really too bad. We don't need another God of War.And this is what is important to me. So pause for a moment and consider: I still think this game is worth buying. At full price.At. Full. Price.True, the gameplay mechanics and general background themes are just... incoherent, like someone gathering an orchestra and telling the musicians they now have to perform King Lear. As mimes. True, you may spend hours just exploring rooms where you've been before, looking for that ONE collectable you missed.But it's worth it. Because it's just fun to play. The gameplay, despite being dissonant with the jaw-dropping gorgeousness of this game, flows so smoothly -- so well -- that I don't care about the backstory. (Well, *I* do, but it's still worth it.) The core story itself has a few twists that are separate from the story of gameplay mechanics, and they're appreciated. And since the gameplay experience is so smooth, and the art amazing, and the bosses fun to play, yes I am very happy with my purchase.Besides. It's got a teddybear that follows you around. How cool is that?
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: The game might not have all things right to fulfill your definition of metroidvania, but elements of it are there and I think it stands very well on its own.It is a very beautiful game with some challenges and a nice story which I think is sufficient for the length of the game and plays well with how the game is designed and vice versa.One major point to address is that often you only have one path to follow until you can go back to areas you have already visited. There is no levelling, you just accumulate upgrades and skills, so grinding makes no sense which is why the need for backtracking is hardly there. There are a few things you can collect only later when you achieved the required abilities, but in retrospect I can only recall a few.Usually you have to defeat a boss to progress further, but this is certainly nothing new to this genre. So decide for yourself, if this is metroidvania enough for you. It still is a wonderful game.The map design could be better, currently there is a bugged achievement which does not unlock, and unfortunately, with the current version (1.0.19) there still seems to be a chance that the game freezes, at least it did it twice on the final boss for me. Up to there, I had no technical issues (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X, 32GB RAM, 2080 Super).You might feel trapped sometimes, though, but you just have to find the right way to advance. ;)The bosses differ in difficulty. Some I had to try more than ten times, some others, especially later on, I defeated on my first or second attempt. Due to the necessity to follow one path most of the time, there is potential for occasional frustration, but to compare it to a souls-like would go to far. Maybe at points, but very soon you have an ability which makes you kind of invincible for the majority of the game. You can still die, ofc, but if you do not rush things and learn to time it, you can take a lot of hits. Which is a very interesting idea I have not seen in a game before (not sure if it is completely new, though).What you get is basically a chance of an instant or delayed stamina/shield refill. Personally, I liked this mechanism, because it makes running between save points a bit more casual but you still have to survive or your progress is lost. If you love endless dying and frustrating attempts to reach the next bonfire, maybe it makes it too easy for you. Sorry. I do not say this cannot still happen, I am just saying, I liked the game mechanics and they ease things up for you compared to how other games work.Another thing well done imho is the set of abilities. You will find different armors based on different elements and certain abilities are tied to the set of armor you are currently wearing (you can easily switch between them). All abilities are useful and feel quite unique. The feeling that you can more and more fluently cross the castle of this world is there and felt good.So to conclude, a game related to metroidvania that stands on its own with lovely artwork and some interesting mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time playing the game. It was nice to see the thematic armor and their respective upgrades, giving long platforming sections to practice it. Others were pretty straightforward, only having a 2-3 simple moves, can just bash them quickly. The late game was rather surprising, reminded me of Metroid: Zero Mission where the gameplay changed temporarily, befitting of the game story.My main qualm with the game was the lack of global mobility; however, each sector isn't too big and by late game, I was so familiar with all the mechanics and had all the upgrades, moving around was easier. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.The good/great:Not a ton of backtracking, but the actual forward progression plays out so well.  The visuals are eye-candy and for a game that the discusses the restoration of the game world through music, it has a rather fitting soundtrack -- that is to say, it is very well done.  I also appreciated the light mechanic, which allows you to utilize your light bar as a shield or as fuel for your ranged attacks -- this bar can only be filled by hitting enemies melee or hugging the flying bear.  Yes, the flying bear.  Some of the game mechanics I found a bit annoying (but nothing that'd deter me from playing):1.) the save mechanic.  Save points are spread out too far apart.  With that said, you can find a save point directly before a boss, which is welcome.  Would have been nice to save automatically after each boss fight, though.2.) I'm not far enough in the game to know, but as of the time of writing I have not discovered a form of fast travel.  The areas are interconnected in a way that should make backtracking easier, but there haven't been any actual shortcuts.  Either would be appreciated.3.) Like many others have stated, I'm rather partial to dashing.  Oh well -- not a deal breaker at all, and the movement works well enough (especially Siren form).The oh-my--God excellent (so far):1.) Siren form.  Swimming in a Metroidvania has never been more fun.This game is highly recommended from me.  I don't write reviews often, but I wanted to give the developers some props.  So yeah, props developers!

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:I thought it was very good; the story was easy to follow. The gameplay is very unique, and the idea behind switching armors is quite cool. You have to swap different armors to kill certain enemies more easily and to traverse the map. The system where your magic is tied to your health was a first for me. I am accustomed to having a limited amount of ways to heal, but in this game, you can heal "technically" indefinitely given the circumstances. I loved the system because later on, you will unlock a way to do a quick-time event to get your barrier back quickly, and for me, that was really easy to accomplish. The art style and music are fantastic, and it is always stunning to go through. The sound design is quite good; when you lose your shield, you can hear an audio cue letting you know that you have to press the button for the quick-time event. The game does not have fast travel, but it is really easy to traverse through the map without it because they implemented many shortcuts, and many areas on the map are easy to skip quickly if you need to backtrack.Things you may dislike:I will mention that for some of us, things can feel repetitive. Though the armors are different in how they traverse and fight enemies, they have the same animations with different flairs suited to their design but essentially fight the same. Many enemies get reused with a different coat of paint and some slight variance in move set, but not that great. The barrier system, while unique and something I loved, doesn't mean it is for everyone. I know it will be challenging for some people to get used to because so many people gave up on the game within the first two hours because they don't like how it feels.I hope you give it a try; it was a unique experience for me, and it's a quick play and easy to get all the achievements if you're one of those gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: The great visuals are offset by a truly baffling design decision to tie your health to your resource for mandatory ranged attacks. Combine this with the over-long heal animation that requires you hold still and you have a game that could have been great but ends up not being fun to play.Shame because there are some good ideas here. The art, designs, UI, all top notch.Side note, the attacks feel way too light and airy for a giant halberd. Hits lack impact.Personal score, 5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty game to look at, but that's about it. Feels a bit to linear to be considered a metroidvania. The combat is just not very fun and exploration isn't very good either. The elevator load times are so long. When you get all the power ups in the game, you don't even feel that strong. You're sort of invincible unless you get hit too frequently, but you don't have any cool attacks or fun movement options. Just a pretty disappointing and meh experience overall for this game. Probably not even worth it on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with some nice boss fights.Most of the bosses available are rather accessible or on the easy side, but there are a few that can be quite challenging.This is also a linear experience. The navigation is very straight forward, but there is a blue note that will require some backtracking.There's no option to leave marks on the map, so this particular blue note should be remembered for one of the achievements.Good art, pixel quality, animations, fluidity and sound.My only issue was with the cutscenes. They can't be skipped and there is a critical bug if a player tries to skip text. NEVER, EVER, try to mash the A button to skip text. It might skip the imput requirement to advance and leave the scene playing indefinitely.I had to do the last boss twice because I got stuck on an ending scene.This review was written after completing all the achievements. Overall, I'd say a 7/10.Not a bad game but it doesn't excel as one might expect from the first impression when starting.Also, the cutscenes not being skippable, the bug when trying to go over the text and not being able to leave marks on the map for reference summarize things that need to be improved in future games.
_childDocuments_.name: 9 Years of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game that's more Castlevania than Metroid, but still a mix of both. The art is drop-dead gorgeous, and the story has substance that keeps me curious about it. I still want to know more after completing 100% of the currently-available content. The bosses are all unique, and while not exceptionally difficult, you'll need to adapt to every one of them, which keeps things fresh and engaging. You gain a generous helping of upgrades throughout the game, though I think the pace of unlocking new mechanics leaves a lot to be desired. Most of the first half of the game it feels pretty hard to get around, but there is a lot of freedom to zoom around the castle later on. The castle, while beautiful and fun to explore, has some repeat level designs, and many tweaked versions of the same enemies, who generally pose little threat and don't require any strategy to defeat. All that said, the pacing of the story is great and leaves me wanting to know more about Europa, Apino, and all of the dozen or so important characters that we meet along the way.I'm not sure how much more I can say. This is a great first game with a story that I hope receives a sequel or some kind of expansion. I would like to see the studio improve their game design chops - they can clearly make something truly great, if given the opportunity.Edit: Just want to add some recognition of the developers' hard work on this game. They have fixed many of the progression bugs that I ran into and made sure that missed achievements were retroactively rewarded. Thank you for remembering your early supporters.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sucks, I'm super disappointed. Bad controls, way too many bosses without a save point nearby, piss poor health system. Your health is also your ammo? So if you use your ammo you are vulnerable to dying in two hits (you can upgrade health but it happens so late and it's just one or two hit points more). Bullet hell mechanics in some boss fights but you don't have a dodge of any kind, and your character moves like a snail. There is no fast travel, and when you use the elevators it plays a 20 second animation EVERY TIME that you cannot skip......the character runs out of dialogue after 6 elevators and you are forced every time you take one (there are a lot) to wait for her to literally just say ".......". Garbage. Enemy design is 6 enemies, just themed to different colors. Completely linear gameplay: every time I thought I had options.....it actually just came down to ONE path I could take at all times. Not a metroidvania. Platforming feels bad, the abilities you get feel jerky and weird....and they don't work smoothly when it comes to platforming during combat. Boss design is terrible......they are just platformer bosses where you wait for their vulnerable moment and the rest of the time you cannot do anything. Again.....totally some peoples' cup of tea, but that is generally not what metroidvania fans want.  Money you get can't be used by itself for anything. Same music everywhere. Someone said "I hope this developer never stops making games" and I can't agree more. Also there is no auto save, so any rooms or paths you uncover, or even BOSSES you beat will not be saved unless you can make it all the way back to a save point without dying. You have two hit points.......and the save points are not next to the bosses except for a few in the early game (which also makes you think the game is going to be reasonable and fair....so you play past the 2 hour mark and then it's garbage and you can't refund it). Save your money folks, if you want a metroidvania this ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a solid 6/10 game. Competent, well-made metroidvania, but not amazing. Overall would recommend if you like the game's art design and like boss battles in 2D platformer type games (like Blasphemous, Hollow Knight, etc.).Soundtrack is excellent, environmental design, art direction, and sound design are all good. My favorite part of the game by far is the bosses. There are many of them. I wish they were integrated into the game's story and lore a bit better like the final boss is, but their mechanics were fun to learn. Character design is fine. I like the way the overall game looks and feels. 4-5 hour play for a normal run, maybe 10-15 for completionist, although that's stretching it.Criticisms: Combat is fine, but it never really becomes deeper than light attack, strong attack, and projectile. What you get within the first hour is what you get for the entire playthrough pretty much. There are different armors/forms, but they don't change the core gameplay. Puzzle-solving is fun in this game, but it never really felt challenging to me. There's also not really a dash/dodge button (there is a backstep, but no iframes), no timing-based defence mechanism, or parry of any kind. Story is serviceable, but a bit cliche. The sidequests in the game all function the same which was a bit disappointing. Navigating the map never becomes easier since you don't get much in the ways of a teleport besides a few central points along the main column of the map. Back-tracking is a pain if you wanted to pick up rooms you missed early on in the game. Also no map markers. The system of map marking in Blasphemous and the recent Prince of Persia game are great and I wish this game had something to that effect.
