_childDocuments_.review: John Wick Hex is a hex grid strategy game that takes place in the world of John Wick and you play as the Baba Yaga himself. Most people don't think of strategy game and John Wick in the same sentence, expecting any John Wick game to be a mindless shooting game. This may be a valid expectation but John Wick Hex really captures the feeling of being John Wick and using skill and strategy to come out on top even when vastly outnumbered and outgunned.If you've ever played a game like X-Com before then you know the basics of this type of strategy game only in John Wick Hex you don't have a squad; you are just one man. You can move around, shoot at enemies, refocus, reload (if you have ammo), bandage, throw your gun at an enemy, or if you're close enough to them initiate melee combat with strikes, parries, pushes, and takedowns. You have to keep track of your health, your weapon's ammo, and your focus meter which is used to perform parries, takedowns, and dodges during melee combat. Before each mission there is a level map where you can use your Continental coins to purchase buffs/perks and stash weapons or equipment in the level. You may have to change your play style based on what perks you buy so this adds an element of replayability. At the end of each stage you can watch a real time replay of your actions in the level complete with cinematic camera angles.I won't go deeply into the story but it takes place before the films, before John met his deceased wife, and it involves him being tasked to rescue Winston and Charon from a rogue assassin with his sights on the High Table. It's not a complex narrative but it's interesting enough to keep you playing along and Winston and Charon are voiced by the actors from the films. The real meat of this game is the gameplay though. You can play in "operator" or "expedited" modes, the difference being that in operator you have all the time you want to make a decision but in expedited mode you only have five seconds to make a decision or time will start again without your input. Each mode has its own achievements plus achievements for beating the various pars on each level such as time, accuracy, weapons used, and bandages used. This provides a lot of replayability for the completionist and I, myself, beat the game three times in order to get 100%. It didn't feel like a grind and even during some frustrating areas when I was going for Baba Yaga rank on each level it just made me think harder and tailor my strategy differently. Very rarely will you find yourself in a spot that is impossible to get out of; you just have to use your head like Mr. Wick.Performance-wise the game runs fine on my potato and I encountered only a few minor glitches. The most noticeable one is that sometimes during the replays John will bug out and will just stand in one place even though you can hear the action going on as if he were moving around killing everyone. This doesn't happen a lot but it happens enough to notice. The game did occasionally freeze for several seconds but this was minor. I did have a few actual lockups where the level completely froze and I would have to restart it but the game itself never crashed or locked up. Overall these were minor things.I recommend this game if you're a fan of John Wick and you like the X-Com style of strategy game. I initially thought the price might be too steep for what you get but as of writing this I have played for 27 hours and that's more bang for my buck than I would get going to a movie. It's good at full price but if you find it on sale then definitely pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Great premise, execution needs some work.The core idea of Hex is really good, a more tactical approach to the John Wick style combat, the moment to moment game-play is really well done, the quasi-turn based combat where actions cost you time and you have to balance your opponents actions vs your own, interrupting their attacks while dishing out your own. The game forces you to be very mindful about how you approach situations, the nuances of the guns, the strategy elements are all really good, but some parts fall short.The health system, your health carries over from stage to stage, and you may find yourself at the last level (usually the most complex) and you might have no healing items left and be forced to either brute force your way through, or re-start the entire stage. You can add healing items in the prep stage, but the tutorial kind of glossed over this, so be mindful of it when preparing for a mission. The speed of the game is deliberately a bit slow which works with the idea of being tactical and methodical, but getting killed at the end of a level can make the game feel like a bit of a slog, but the core combat wouldn't work as well if it was Hotline Miami speed, maybe something in between would work really well.Some of the animations look rather janky and while i personally liked the art style, i can see why it might not be for everyone. The enemy variety needs some work, the AI is often a bit simplistic, and the janky animations kind of highlights this, with hand to hand combat against groups looking a bit like awkward teens on the prom dance floor.From what i've played so far its definitely a great concept and if you're looking for an interesting take on the genre of top down strategy games i'd recommend it (probably on sale), but the execution needs some refinement.6/10, maybe get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: i review games on steam after i 100% complete them! check out my reviews to see all the games i have completed!john wick hex is a tactics/strategy game that uses timeline-based combat instead of turn-based. every character on a level moves whenever you move along the minimal hex-based grid. everyone moves at the same pace, and each action (shooting, melee attacks, weapon pickups) has a ‘preparation’ time as well as the time it takes to complete the actual action. the story is also pretty interesting as well and worth playing for that alone. i definitely recommend this game, even if you've never watched the john wick movies before playing (like me).

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable top down shooter based in the John Wick lore. A turn based top down shooter isn't exactly the style of game I think that would capture the spirit of Wicks amazing gun-play and combat. Would have loved a FPS, but this game does have its merits. The graphics are done in a comic book style vector image aesthetic. Ian McShane reprises his role from the film and adds some authenticity to the narrative. The environments or rooms that the player must progress through do become increasingly difficult and require some proper strategy to approach, some of the bosses provide a strong challenge. Not the best Wick game they could have done, but if your'e a Keanu/Wick fan its worth grabbing.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool puzzle game set in the John Wick world.  Winston and Charon have been kidnapped, and John Wick is out to rescue them.  The game uses a neat timing model for every action.  Moving one space takes .4 seconds.  Aiming a 9mm gun takes .9 seconds.  Bandaging yourself takes 2 seconds.  The game is about making the best choices with regards to time.  Is it better to aim and shoot, or close the gap and punch him? Or duck behind cover and try to bandage up before he rounds the corner?As neat as the system is, it doesn't expand much past what you do in the first level.  All your moves are there from the beginning, and although new (tougher) enemies pop up later, you deal with them in the same way.  I paid $4 and had fun with it.  I don't know that it's worth it at the normal price of $20.  Play the first level, and if it doesn't appeal to you immediately, refund it.  The first level is a good picture of the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: If you like but are NOT a hardcore fan of either John Wick or turn based strategy games, then this game may be worth a historic low sale or bundle if you like gameplay videos online.The game does something different with turn based tactics that was reminiscent of Transistor's pseudo-turn based attacking option. In this case, time is tracked in tenths of a second, and you can see timing of enemies next single action & next attack. You should know that this is not for everyone though, as the tactical variety isn't huge like best known turn based tactics games because there's only so much John Wick can do.Between each of the 5 areas, each one with many levels, there's a few upgrades that can be selected or you can place an extra weapon or bandage in a level.Tutorial was decent and helpful.Although the cel shading style was decent and plays to Bithell's strengths, the real-time replay of completing a level is literally rough around the edges in terms of anti aliasing, some character clipping, and mostly rigid movement. Evidently the dev had to fly to Hollywood multiple times to get the studio to sign off on the game's progress, so I'm going to blame that.It is otherwise mechanically solid and doesn't have bugs I noticed.

_childDocuments_.review: JWH is a turn based strategy game, where you use a combination of pistol shots and melee attacks to dispatch your underworld foe.I'm always a little sceptical about movie tie-ins, as I'm never sure how much care has gone into the game itself, verses cashing in on a franchise - but, I'm pleased to say it plays really well.There's a few elements which are a little annoying, and perhaps the developers could have tweaked it a little, this surrounds the animation of the characters. The styling - I like, but watching the movie-esq playbacks of John Wick mincing in diagonals with a gait like he's trying desperately to hold in a poo looses all of the drama.No hitman walks like that, they'd go for a poo before they left.But a great, steady learning curve, the more I played, the less times I needed to redo levels, and in-between each level you're rewarded with a monologue by Lovejoy, Ian McShane, the human ball bag. Love it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has awesome core mechanic but it is unpolished buggy and unbalanced to the point that is sometimes unplayable. Difficulty scaling is all over the place and you are again in a mercy of RNG. Sometimes you can go through what seems a difficult level with such an ease that is immensly enjoyable. On some other occasions you wont be able to progress at all. You you will restart and restart and restart until RNG finally dont come in your favor. Spawn points are unfair. The preparation system is bare bones as bare bones go. Plus the cost of those preparation is way to high.  You can purchase one perk and one item or two perks and maybe an item. But more often than not it is just two perks and get rekt. This game have such tremendous potential that is hard to properly describe it. But in it current state is way to short and way to buggy and it gives that rushed, half baked product vibe all over itself.On positive note the story is...well in a style of John Wick classic. So...not too deep and that is how it should be IMO. The voice acting if top noch. They got Ian McShane and Lance Reddick on board and they naturally done a hell of a job in terms of narration. Of course Troy Baker in a role of main villain Hex preformed again most admirably. In short his voiceacting is awesome, as always. I guess you could say that in this current state the game is worth of trying just wait for the sale as it not worth of full price.If the devs patch it up and add additional content that yes i would most defenetly change my review from negative to positive.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and animations are, to be blunt, pretty bad which makes the replay function a bit odd and unnecessary but honestly I still had quite a bit of fun with this game. It might seem a bit frustrating, unfair or unbalanced once you get past the tutorial stages but as you learn the ropes of the game it gets easier (still had to take advantage of a glitch to beat the 2nd-to-last stage though) and it does do a pretty good job of making you feel like John Wick, even though the experience is slightly let down by the aforementioned subpar graphics and animations which is pretty noteworthy IMO as you'd expect those things to be pretty good in a game based on the John Wick series. Overall though, I like it and to be honest the only other game that comes close to this is Door Kickers and Fights In Tight Spaces so you'd definitely be missing out if you passed over this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite an interesting idea, the beginnings of good mechanics, and a cult character, the creators of the game managed to completely screw up the game.It is not possible to understand where to start describing shortcomings and where to end. Everything is screwed up. The animation is so wooden that the distant 2000s say hello to you, I was reminded of Morrowind looking at these wooden jumping battle animations. But Morrowind was limited by the resources of its time, and what’s here?!Methods of interaction with the enemy and objects are limited throughout the entire game to literally a few options, and this is immensely tedious already at the second or third level. And yes, you can absolutely uselessly throw a gun at an enemy, because Wick did that in the movie, that’s it, you won’t find much else from Wick in this game.The courage and beauty of the fighting scenes of the franchise remained in the films, believe me, there are neither beautiful fights nor the filigree beauty of a pistol master. Everything looks incredibly stupid and disgusting. You can view a replay of your twitches on the map after the level only if you are an aesthetic masochist and want to make you even more willing to delete the game and forget that you ever played it.Graphics and textures are not here. The artists claimed some kind of style, but the square faces and the depiction in general just hit the bottom. But they are artists, they see it that way.I bought this game on sale for less than $2, which I think is the most it could cost. I think I overpaid.

_childDocuments_.review: Huh! That was kinda interesting.I'm not a fan of the John Wick movies. Extraordinary physicality of the performers aside, they're uninteresting plots encrusted in additional flavour, like deep-fried vaccum or as if you wrapped the worldbuilding of Dark Souls around a really boring game.Hex, though, is interesting. Not for the story, mind - Mike Bithell has succeeded in delivering a suitably insubstantial companion narrative to the films - but its approach to modelling the combat of the films has a lot to say for itself.Hex is a turn-based strategy game, but with only one playable unit. Each action is ascribed a set period of time to prepare and execute, with actions for the player and the enemy units resolving simultaneously according to a dynamic timeline assembled from the player's next chosen actions and the actions of the NPCs.So the game is about time management and positioning, as it should be, given the subject matter. Do you have the time to draw your weapon and execute a brawler before they throw you to the ground? Compare the upcoming schedule of actions to your desired maneuver and see, no, there will be no time to shoot. However, a briefer action - a blow to the opponent's chin, perhaps - will interrupt and reset their attack, giving you the breathing space to pull your weapon and fire.And so it goes, over 25-30 levels of playing for time and managing sightlines and for the most part it's very diverting. The gameplay can be repetitive, but it's the lack of combat animation variety that damages a game with such a strong hand-to-hand focus. There's only so many times you can watch the same two combos play out before you start to resent them.There's also something of a difficulty, I dunno, *cave* that kicks in on the second last level, where hordes of infinite randomised enemies swarm you from all sides. I spent literal hours trying to finish that level and felt no sense of victory or satisfaction at outwitting a clever design - the dice happened to roll favourably on that run, and I was glad to be done with it.Note that the game contains a series of almost-show-stopping bugs, where the program continues but it becomes impossible for the player to take a further action, halting the game. It's possible for the player to restart the level and continue from the beginning, but that can be more than a little frustrating after 20 minutes of painstaking pie slicing.I should also mention that after completing each level, the player is given the chance to view a replay of their actions shot as a mini movie - which is a fantastic feature for a game like this! It's such a shame, then, that the fixed multicam presentation amounts to a chain of swivel-cams mounted to ceilings. It's about the least compelling, dynamic presentation of a level replay it's possible to imagine. However, as the game proceeds, you can see the developer starting to feel a little more confident - camera angles become lower and more dramatic, there's the occasional trucking shot. Some bolder camera placement or perhaps some more dynamic cinematic cameras (see Fallout 3, especially as they're already using a Hex grid so can quickly check if a relevant camera angle is usable) would have made all the difference in rewarding the player.So. I'm not a fan of John Wick, and I'm not a fan of hex-based grids for primarily orthogonal environments (there's some very weird, crooked paths taken by characters in this game)... but I'm pleased to say that I had a pretty great time with Hex. It won't change the world (and it desperately needed more money and time to cook), but it represents an imaginative and engaging approach to action games - and I wouldn't mind seeing more games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: this game has cool ideas and major potential, but is totally trash. the combat system is unique, but the controls are awkward and finicky. add that to the constant spam of enemies from all directions with no real sequence makes for an overly frustrating experience. you would clear an entire room only to get swarmed in that direction due to off-screen spawns and the fog of war. i really felt i was fighting the controls and poor spawn points than actual enemies. you never really feel like john wick. even the "cool" replay of the fight sequence looks like trash because of the jerky movement and bad animations.maybe if you're an absolute john wick fan this would be worth picking up, since the voice acting from ian mcshane and lance reddick are awesome. but this is an unfortunate skip from me. i really wanted this game to be good since i'm a huge fan of the movies, but there isn't anything redeeming about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on very little gameplay that I've actually experienced (with chances of me going back in being exceedingly low), it's like a poorly thought out and less fun to play version of Fights in Tight Spaces. Whereas in that game you get this sort of tacticool feeling while reenacting fights which would not be amiss in either John Woo or John Wick films (to name its two most obvious influences), here you move in a zig-zag motion throughout a poorly designed map where enemies pop into existence behind arbitrary corners and your best friend is a percentage chance assigned to your offensive actions.It also doesn't help that the artstyle is extremely unimpressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow it manages to be incredibly boring. I felt a bit (!) cool like Keanu Reeves for about half an hour, then realised how boring it must be for him to fight through wave after wave after wave after wave of idiots. Shoot them in the head, cool once (or twice, or ten times). Throw a gun at them to buy time, also cool. Kick them around first to lower their ability to dodge bullets, okay fine. At the 586th headshot and 47th thrown gun, and having to punch someone over and over before I can shoot them, yaaaaaaawn.The maps try to be different. There is some variety in baddies. Loading up with hordes is a bit of a challenge, but I got to the point in less than an hour where I really wasn't that bothered if they killed me.

Percentage hit chances and having to follow the battle timeline make it much more big-picture strategy driven and that kind of makes me feel like Mr. Wick's coach.It focuses on fun and I love the replay feature at the end of the levels so you can relive your path or carnage in one fluid go.On physical gameplay I found it more fun with a controller than mouse/keyboard

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 2nd, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Becoming one of the greatest action heroes, one hexagon at a time. John Wick Hex is a strategy game focused on taking out enemies and managing the room as your character, John Wick, of course, advances in the game and fights his way to various goals.  It may sounds and look simple, but John Wick Hex takes simplistic rules and setups and then overloads the players till they’re forced to move through the level as John Wick would, slaughtering enemies and moving from each target to the next with an amazingly fast combat system. The one thing to know is this is far more turn-based and strategy-oriented than action.  While the game is good, it’s also a bit lacking.  There doesn’t appear to be any possibility for additional attacks other than special weapons as the game goes on, and the animations are weak as is the replay of the level.  John Wick uses so many amazing fighting moves in the movies, it’s disappointing when you see the same takedown for the third time, or an unrealistic attack. Pick this up if you like strategy games.  Rather than a turtle strategy that works in XCOM you’re going to have to be far more aggressive here, but as you mow down enemies, you start to feel like a legendary bad-ass, that Baba Yaga of myth.   This is a prequel to the movie, and while some characters and faces appear, you don’t already need to have seen the movies to enjoy this. _childDocuments_.review: I'm supposed to be timing my actions around what the enemies are doing, but I just end up shooting ranged enemies or spamming the Wait button until brawlers come close enough for a takedown. The game says the bad guys have different tactics, but they all just walk forward until they're in attack range, slowly sauntering single file over mounds of their comrades' bodies into my corridor of death.I don't feel like I'm learning anything new or sharpening my skills as the stages progress, and the level layouts don't change my approach to the game at all. It's more like a turn-based brawler than a a tactics game, and a boring one at that.

_childDocuments_.review: Just repetitive and boring. Has nothing to do with original movie series. In the movie John Wick is in control. He plans ahead, he knows who are his enemies, where they are and what are they planning to do. He knows his surroundings and uses them to his benefit.In the game you just react faster, and that's it. No briefing on what to expect from the level, enemies and bosses, no resource management in advance, no use of surroundings, well, except for cover. And to add up on top of it the game doesn't let you feel in control. It just triggers enemy spawns when you are moving through particularly exposed spot just so you felt overwhelmed while heroically overcoming all the obstacles. But it doesn't feel this way, it feels like bad game design.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not easy to create a unique and wonderful experience when it comes to real time strategy, let's admit it. I am one of those who wanted a shooter (preferably fps) JW game but I acknowledge, when properly executed, a John Wick strategy could have been sick. This one clearly isn't.I am frustrated that they did not even try to build a proper cover system or add interactions with environment. Do I really need to spam 'wait' for someone to approach me so I could take them down? Or if am I just going to run and gun (though it's not entirely feasible on some levels for various reasons) what's the point of making it turn based? Gameplay elements like pushing and parrying does not make any significant move in the genre either. It's a very bland game with very few options. It could have been ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if it was not for the aesthetics and soundtrack of the game which manages to capture the soul of John Wick.The most disappointing part is the enemies would keep spawning in certain levels (e.g. Osborn). Meanwhile I do not know if it has a limitation (cuz I never survived to see its end) regardless of whether it does have any or not, it just kills the point of the level design. If you cleverly design a level chances are high I could cleverly execute my moves. But level design being so simple and narrow, they probably decided to add spawning enemies so I could not kill every single one of them before I approach to the boss, spam takedown on him and then shoot every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ piece of him. What a cheap game direction. You can create a 'hard' game with a proper level design, there's more than one examples for it. Just place them properly and let me do what I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do.Yeah, that's the John Wick we lived to get boys. It ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks.

Not sure if I'll go back and try replaying stages as expedited mode seems to be the real intent/challenge. _childDocuments_.review: John Wick Hex presents itself as a challenging timeline-based strategy game that seeks to encapsulate the adrenaline-infused choreography of the eponymous character's cinematic exploits. Released on the Steam platform, it has garnered a wealth of attention, both positive and negative.: The game's most praiseworthy feature lies in its innovative timeline strategy system. It's an unorthodox yet captivating approach to the genre, providing an interesting puzzle element. Each action, whether it involves moving, shooting, or engaging in hand-to-hand combat, takes a specific amount of time, creating a dynamic flow akin to a rhythm game. Artistically, Hex shines with its unique comic book-like aesthetics. The color palette, character designs, and environmental details capture the grim, high-stakes world of John Wick, contributing to an immersive gaming experience.: Hex also deserves recognition for its attempt to expand the John Wick universe. The plot unravels with an intriguing, albeit linear, narrative, offering fresh insight into the mysterious backstory of the Continental Hotel. Regrettably, the game's timeline strategy becomes monotonous over time. Missions often feel recycled, detracting from the otherwise immersive environment. The lack of mission variety dulls the engaging gameplay mechanism, leading to predictability.The antagonists' AI exhibits inconsistency. Enemies range from being tactically astute, necessitating strategic thinking, to being inexplicably oblivious, undermining the game's challenge and breaking immersion.: John Wick Hex falls short in character development. The protagonist's abilities remain largely unchanged, irrespective of the player's progression. This deficiency dampens the satisfaction traditionally associated with RPG elements. Another shortcoming is the lack of voice acting, which hinders the narrative's emotional depth. In a game that heavily draws from a film franchise renowned for its memorable characters, this absence feels particularly glaring.Another negative aspect is the game's reliance on camping. This tactic may seem unintuitive and reductive to some players and limits the variety of strategies that can be successfully employed. Lastly, at times, the game can become tedious. Despite its engaging timeline-based gameplay system, Hex can fall into the trap of repetitiveness, especially due to the frequent reliance on camping.John Wick Hex is a bold venture, intertwining the world of cinema and video gaming. Despite its flaws, it showcases an inventive approach to the strategy genre and pays homage to its source material through its atmospheric design and storyline. However, its repetitive missions, inconsistent AI, and lack of character progression may deter some players. This title will likely attract fans of the franchise and strategy game enthusiasts, but others might find it somewhat lacking in variety and depth.As it stands, John Wick Hex can be a thrilling, tactical dance with death, but one that requires fine-tuning to realize its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This is effectively a game made for mobile phones/devices. The full rundown is that it has the time freeze-as-you-move mechanic and direct-line-of-sight fog-of-war from Doorkickers, but you are locked into hexagonal blocks to move back and forth across (like a traditional turn based strategy/RPG).The concept of tight little levels with the Doorkickers tactical-time mechanic is really good... but Hex requires no real tactics. It's "kill everything" and "survive." Difficulty in later levels equates to overwhelming bullet sponge enemies. It is not shamelessly difficult, but it lacks depth. There is no stealthing, this just straight up slaughter like the comics/movies.Basically the experience you have in the first level remains the same, despite being able to pick up more powerful weapons. The pre-level perk purchasing is "meh" and speaks of lazy game design where it's meta-milking to make countering bullet sponges a little less frustrating.The shoot/melee tactical options when you attack an enemy, depending on distance, is also a good concept and works well enough, but the idea of speed running with minimal reaction time... that little sub menu system is not built for speed. Not unmanageable, but distinctly not refined.Otherwise... the art style leans a little too much on milking Keanu's involvement with the Cyberpunk game he was in. Voice acting has been phoned in by the movie actors.... there is some dialogue that belongs in, and only in, comic book form. It sounds cringe worthy when spoken. The story plays out as a fan service-lite experience. The story varies from "meh" to a peppering of more cringe... partly from the voice acting being a case of actors playing their character and reading a script in an empty room... effectively fulfilling a contractual obligation and collecting a pay cheque.The comic art cut scenes are incredibly lazy. Basically motion-comic movement of static imagery... and considering this is based on a well drawn comic book, the amateurish art in the cut scenes makes this feel like a very cheap franchise cash in, reinforcing that this was meant to be easily ported onto mobile phones.Ultimately this feels like a really well done student project made in Unity, wearing $$$ franchise clothing.

_childDocuments_.review: In the game, we have to fight in the style of a John Wick movie: constantly move and not only shoot with firearms, but also apply oriental martial arts. At the heart of the combat system, as in the original idea of Bitell, is a step—by-step tactic - however, it is already more dynamic. There is always a timeline tape looming over the battlefield, which records all the actions performed by you or your opponents. Only one action can be selected per turn: step, shot, dodge, combat move or reload. Any of them "costs" a certain number of seconds, and physical struggle also takes concentration points (in fact, endurance).John Wick Hex is not the best tactic in the world, but it is certainly quite original and interesting. And most importantly, both in the plot and in the battles themselves (and in the voices of Ian McShane and Lance Reddick), you can feel that special spirit and mood of the paintings about the famous superkiller that many people like so much. So everyone who liked the movie and who is not indifferent to the fate of John Wick will have to try the game without fail.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to a JW video game experience, you'd think the film series' constant gunplay format would be ripe for it.  However, the struggle quickly begins to show when you realize this endeavor could quickly become like any other third-person action shooter or rapidly devolve into a quicktime button-masher in order to recreate the epic gun-fu ballet dance you get to see when watching the movies.  John Wick Hex is an attempt to balance these two sides of the fence for an experience that emulates the source material.  The result is an ambitious attempt by Bithell Games' team, but is milquetoast at best in final production.  The result is an overhead point-and-click turn-based strategy shooter that feels like it takes elements of Hitman Go, while still having more random features than a purely puzzle-focused outcome.The game is surprisingly difficult and punishing in regards to survival in different chapters without checkpoints, but tends to be more frustrating excessive trial-and-error instead of the pure joy you might be chasing from the movies.The graphical cinematics get depressingly tired quite fast, the story is thin and fills in a random chapter of John's previous life during his time as a younger assassin, and the gameplay is not much to write home about.  Overall, if you are a hardcore fan and want to see arguably the best possible pitch at bringing the JW concept to life in playable format...you've got it right here.  Wait for a sale and snap it up.

_childDocuments_.review: John Wick Hex is a decent little strategy game, held back by a lack of budget.What I appreciate, is that there was a clear inspiration for the game play.Tons of movie based games opt to make something generic, with the hope the IP will carry the experience.But that's not the case here, and what you get is a game that attempts to put you into the mindset of John wick, and think 2 steps ahead of your enemy.Highlights-The games timeline bar does a good job relaying relevant info on your and enemy attacks so that you can make informed decisions as to how to move forward-Level structure provides both short bite sized stages, while asks the players to plan to the long haul-A decent amount of combat options.Flaws-Lack of environmental hazards and opportunities-Bosses are pathetic-Replays are janky due to stiff animations and lack of editing featuresCheck my video review for more details.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable tactical romp. BUY IT ON SALE.It doesn't play anything like XCOM if you were wondering that. Everything comes down to how long an action takes and where you are positioned. You have to manage your ammunition and your focus (think stamina) to survive the longer fights. I found the RNG to be pretty fair. All the gunfights you have should be pretty close so you usually have a good chance to hit. Positioning is again, key in this game. There are some details that sound absurd that were obviously done for balancing. (Scarce ammunition, lack of reloading dropped weapons, lack of true cover mechanics.)  I think fans of the movies will enjoy this game the most. A more casual player might prefer something faster with more explosions, but I enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on sale for $8 which is the only way I'd buy it. It's not a AAA game, which is why full retail is $20 instead of $60, so don't expect a AAA experience. That being said, the game is fun and introduces some fresh new mechanics, such as the timeline - so it's not an RTS nor a turn-based game, it's something in between, and not only does it work but it's really cool. The game play is challenging and at times seems insurmountable. There appears to be random enemy spawn so sometimes you'll get swarmed and will die no matter what. At first I thought this was a deal breaker, but after more play and trying different tactics, I realized that maneuvering, using the terrain and wisely choosing which actions and when you do them does actually pay off, and that is what keeps me coming back - knowing that if my tactics had been better, I could have won...What the game lacks is quality we're used to seeing in AAA games. The graphics are good, not great, and I do enjoy the cell shaded vibe. The sound effects are poor, all the guns share the same sound effect which is  thin and unrealistic, however the voice acting in the cut scenes is top notch. The variety of weapons is not great so far but I'm only 4 hours in to the game, so don't quote me on that one. The replay is pretty neat, although the graphics and camera angles need to be better. What I really see in this game is POTENTIAL. I would LOVE to see a sequel with AAA quality, more weapons, different loadouts, being able to earn and spend currency on new gear, etc, along with better graphics and sound effects. This could even be a team based game with multiplayer options as well. I think the creators hit on something special here...

_childDocuments_.review: the strategy and timeline system are really cool but the game just lacks polish. If there is an intended way to play its not really explained and the way that enemies feel like they're endlessly spawning in no matter what your approach is, combined with the janky animations and unskippable dialogues that play over and over again after dying and having to re-do a section just got old real quick.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game with an interesting mechanic - The action timer. It does have somewhat clunky mechanics/movement overall (I think that they could have done better with raw distance instead of hexes, but I suppose that defeats the purpose of the name.)  It's worth the buy on sale, IMO.My largest complaint though is that, despite being John Wick, you don't really get to use any of his signature fighting. There isn't any disarming of opponents, no grappling, and most importantly there isn't any grappling of a live target to use as a shield / incapacitate them temporarily while dealing with other threats.  It's an interesting strategy game, but it is most certainly is not a John Wick game.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game where you can become THE John Wick - as he shuffles around aimlessly killing everyone in his path to find this Hex guy, and kill him too. I dunno, I haven't seen any John Wick movies. Oops.If I could give a neutral rating, I would.Under all the graphical flaws, questionable game design and distinct lack of polish, there is a core of a good tactical, shooty game where at the end of the day, you can bask in satisfaction of seeing your replay Wick take out waves upon waves of enemies, mistakes and all. If you enjoy:- XCOM percentage shots, where you can't hit a guy 3 feet away.. twice- Weapons that are most of the time worst than the default 9mm because i) Wick takes too long to shoot or ii) when he does, he keeps firing even when the enemy has died (the only exception is the bullpup shotgun but that's only available in the last few stages)- Innumerable enemies being dropped on you at the most contrived places (it gets noticeably worst as the game progresses)- Constant flitting between line of sights to avoid said enemies- Being in the fairly common scenario of smacking and stunlocking two melee enemies that are too close and have too much health- Bosses that can all be beaten with multiple takedowns and shooting them repeatedly while they're splayed on the ground- Memorising enemy spawns (with their permutations) to get the cleanest run you can muster since health is persistant- AND if you're a completionist, clearing levels with minimal damage taken, minimal shots missed, enough guns picked up, ALL under a timer.Then, you might be able to achieve some semblance of enjoyment from playing John Wick Hex. If you do, I also recommend playing it on the "5-second to act" mode to make the game go by/give you a headache faster.

_childDocuments_.review: It starts good and fun, but in the art exhibit level I encountered a bunch of bugs all at once: enemies shooting me through floors/walls which is obviously pretty annoying when you have a limited number of bandages.The other prominent issue was game freezes forcing a level restart: Normally the game will pause when John Wick spots another enemy so that you can soak in the information and react accordingly. In this level so many enemies pop up that it will sometimes pause when you are in the middle of an action, locking the game until you choose an action even though you're already mid-action... It's quite an artificial difficulty escalation from the last level which seemed to work fine.I would love to finish the game if the Art Exhibit ever gets fixed, I was having a lot of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, novel take on adapting an action franchise that comes much closer to "being John Wick" in the subtle moments of sweeping into cover at just the right moment, etc, than an FPS or TPS would. The  benefits of each action could be explained or made more distinct-- I basically never used Push-- but attempts at stylish gameplay are not punished with failure (yay) and even sometimes result in a John Wick-like moment, like when I ran out of bullets, focus points and even had to throw my gun with one health left, leading to the classic "punch-this-guy, punch-the-other guy-while-he-recovers, repeat" action movie fight finisher. I felt very Wicklike.

_childDocuments_.review: John Wick Hex takes a while to click, but when it does, the game does a surprisingly good job of making you feel like the unstoppable hitman. The title follows an original story that takes place before the John Wick movies , with comic book style cutscenes between each mission. It's a decent attempt at creating an overarching plot and creates some tension, but just like the movies, the action is the focus on your surroundings to get the job done and move to the next level, this game indeed is breathtaking!

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; Worth the time but not the money. Try to get it on sale and it should be worth it.Game is quite short, gameplay takes some grinding/retring, but mechanics are interesting and soundwork is good enough. The storyline is irrelevant and sometimes annoyingly unskippable. Lack of keyboard shortcuts is a big inconvenince, given that half of the actions are spread all over the HUD. _childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: I am very ambivalent about the game. On the one hand, the game is not necessarily BAD. You click your way through the level and kill enemies. The problem is that it is very very very simple. There is only a limited selection of possible moves. You can parry attacks, hit/kill/push enemies, shoot with guns and throw your firearms. There are no real combos, special moves, interactions with objects or the environment, etc. This is one of the biggest problems of the game. The choice of weapons is also very limited. In the end, you spend most of your time hiding behind walls and pillars and killing all the enemies. Quite boring, to be honest.The story is mediocre. The art style, on the other hand, is quite nice. There is too much unused potential and the game is not very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The available moves are too basic, no combo, special move etc which could definitely dig deeper based on the movies. Kind of boring but maybe still okish for a challenging STG game since the time system is interesting. Just so much wasted potential.However the biggest problem is the sight line. Numerous time I hide behind a obstacle like a column but enemy on the directly opposite side can still see and shoot me. This is frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: First I need to preface this review by explaining that I believe the core of the action in the John Wick movies is the skill and luck it takes to pull off what John does. In that regard, this game is exactly what I believe a John Wick game should be like.Sadly, a lot of the reviews don't seem to agree that strategy should be at the core of what makes a John into a Wick. I personally enjoyed this game a lot for the aforementioned reasons but still I can see that it's not a perfect game, or even at the fullest of it's potential. It's beautifully stylized but the animations are ... unpolished to say the least, like other parts of the game (the game contains bugs, thankfully not game breaking ones). As contrast, the voice acting is amazing. Now that that's out of the way, the core gameplay loop which entails positioning and time management, as well as a bit of dice rolling, it is in fact fun unlike others tend to say. It isn't hard to learn and it's satisfying.The trailer provided explains greatly what one should expect from this game, which is why I need not say more.  Except that you should buy it at a discount because it is overpriced.

_childDocuments_.review: If it were less than $5, this would be a decently fun, bite sized, turn based game with a twist on "turns". However, this "action takes time" system seems to fall apart when it's visually difficult to tell what's going on with several enemies on screen. The replay cinematic is pretty cool at first - but the longer the missions get the dumber it looks.I still intend to finish it, and get some achievements, because I like John Wick, and I think the system is interesting (if maybe a bit lacking in variety), but I cannot recommend it at full price.EDIT: don't bother with achievements. You will hate it. Also the more you play, the more the limited move set grows to be frustrating, there's no obvious timer to gauge how you're doing in order to beat the PAR time, and John Wick misses shots he would never miss. Enemy spawns, as everyone else has mentioned gets really annoying very quickly when there are time constraints to think about and it's all RNG.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I really enjoyed this game. That being said, I understand why it got mixed reviews. The animations were a bit janky and repetitive, which also meant that the replays didn't look anywhere near cool enough to be as worthwhile a feature as they were advertised to be. I had two crashes that required me to restart the level in the 9 hours it took me to play through the main story. All in all, it feels like a layer of polish that really would have benefited the original vision of the game got skipped in the development process. Despite all of that, however, the actual gameplay underneath it all was slick, interesting and rewarding. The strategic elements made you stop and think constantly about timing and line of sight, and when you pull it off it really does feel a lot like the brutal, calculating fights in the movie. There was some variation between the missions and I found it strategically interesting and fun the whole way through. The professional voice acting, including Ian McShane and Lance Reddick reprising their iconic roles from the movies, served as a really neat glue holding the fight scenes together and making the game feel like an extension of the movies. I really wish it had been given some more time and attention to working the kinks out of the animation in order to be the truly stellar game it had the potential to be, but the flaws are mostly superficial and I still found it very much worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: John Wick Hex is NOT an action game. Instead, it is tactical combat game that casts you as John Wick shooting his way through a passel of enemies in search for... well, a story you'll have to see for yourself. The combat is actually pretty simple: you move John on the level full of dots that are representing hexes (in this aspect, it is a little reminiscent of Battletech) as you move, every move takes time, and that's "recorded" on the timeline, while your enemies also move, and can emerge from doors behind you and in front of you, or are already on the level moving about. They will seek to engage you, and you can engage them in both gunfight or hand-to-hand melee. However, keep in mind that your hitpoints are limited, and while you can take a lot of damage, you are not indestructible. You can move behind cover as necessary, and you can even switch between standing and crouching to enter cover. However, your movement while crouched is limited to rolls and that costs focus. And without focus your ability to do damage is limited. You start with a handgun, and you know John always double-taps an enemy. And even John may miss sometimes. As each enemy appears, it shows how soon they will be attacking, and that should determine your priority in handling them. Keep in mind that handgun accuracy is low, and the further way, the less accuracy. Given that John only carries one weapon, John needs to pick up weapons dropped by his enemies to continue fighting. John sometimes do get hit, and he starts with two bandages, and can pick up more. Bandage heal up John nicely, but takes time to deploy, and time he may not have. Remember we talked about focus earlier? You can regain focus by spending a turn standing. Can't do that while crouched. Focus can be used for certain close combat moves, as well as rolls to get away from enemies (or get closer). As you move through the level, you shoot brawlers and guards that get in your way. Your objective is to move to the level exit, which puts you onto the next level. Each full level has a bunch of sub-levels, and at the end of the level is a boss, which has his unique quirks... He cannot be hit by gunfire UNTIL you deplete his focus with melee combat. I can imagine other bosses have other quirks. At the second level, you get to spend the tokens for benefits at the Bespoke Tailors to add bonuses, pre-cache guns and bandages throughout the levels, to help yo survive the tougher fights. All in all, John Wick Hex is a good little fast-paced tactical combat puzzle where you need to plan ahead in more sense than one. And its expansion on the lore about the High Table, the Intercontinental, and more, are definitely welcomed.

_childDocuments_.review: A great concept that has tons of potential to build on. Perhaps a bit too RnG with the dodging mechanics which leaves the player to gamble on defense. Things like blocking the line of fire during a push could delay the enemy fire timer or perhaps focus can be used to make john perform quicker to avoid the shot clock. A bit odd that John can be shot during a takedown event (that would be a really tough shot irl). Melee combat can be exploited and cheese the game. It would also be nice if a certain movement would show a chance of being hit before executed and where you end up will. Despite these minor issues, it was a fun game

_childDocuments_.review: Gun kata, time management, movement strategy, bullet count, & more gun kata.Very cool game, with simple controls and concept, but well put together. The game is rather short, but with possible random enemy placement, and encounters makes it replayable. Plenty of room for expansion, or new chapters. Looking forward to see what becomes of it. The simplistic nature of it, is it's beauty, and will satisfy any turn-based combat fan, as well as any John Wick fans, who just want to run&gun a bit, while doing other task online. I would highly recommend this game for quick game players, and players who take their time, and those who multi task.Has a few bugs, but not game breaking. At the time of this review, it's only been out for 4 days, so there's still time for touch ups before labeling it as bugged.On a scale of 10, I would give it a 7.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't really followed along to the coverage when it came out so I went into the game fully intending to play it slow and steady, XCOM style. But the thing is, John Wick isn't a slow and steady character, even in this game. He's a relentless nightmare that his enemies can only slow down and never really stop. And when I finally realized this about two missions into Hex's modest seven-mission campaign, I did way more damage, took fewer hits, and had much more fun, even through the frustrating bits.As a game, Hex does come with more than a few of those frustrations. Not exactly complaints since a lot of the difficulty can be filed under "git gud," but things I wish were better or reworked. I wish they did a better job of utilizing spawns (and the doors in general, really) rather than use monster closets when you'd hit checkpoints in a level. I wish there really were checkpoints mid-mission. I wish magazines were more of a thing rather than an endless recycling of weapons (though I get that it's a flavor thing). Last but not least, I wish the bosses weren't reduced to just throwing them over and over until you could shoot them in the face, especially Hex himself.All that said, John Wick Hex was a short and sweet experience, with stylish visuals, music that took me back to the source movies, and a fresh take on turn-based tactical gameplay that felt like a mix of XCOM and Lara Croft/Hitman GO. I'd say it was worth the 10-ish hours if you've been feeling the itch for something different in the genre, or looking for a new experience in the universe while waiting for John Wick 4.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: Pure and simple, this is a tactical strategy game that blends melee and ranged content into a bite-sized follow-the-goal campaign. I enjoyed the graphics and coloration used because it gave off the gritty neon vibe of a city without resorting to a tired, old color pallet. The game is about destroying enemies, not a site-seeing tour. The timeline is very useful once the control mechanics are explained.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: BECOME THE BABA YAGA - John Wick Hex is a fast-paced, action-oriented strategy game that makes you think and strike like John Wick, the professional hitman of the critically acclaimed film franchise. Created in close cooperation with the creative teams behind the films, John Wick Hex is fight-choreographed chess brought to life as a video game, capturing the series’ signature gun fu style while expanding its story universe. Players must make quick decisions and choose every action and attack they make, all the while considering their immediate cost and consequences. Featuring a unique blend of strategic momentum-based combat, John Wick Hex captures the feel of the unique tactical combat from the films and blurs the line between the strategy and action video game genres. Perform well and progress in the main story mode (which features an original story created for the game) to unlock new weapons, suit options and locations. Each weapon changes up the tactics you’ll use and the manner in which you’ll play. Ammo is finite and realistically simulated, so time your reloads and make the most of weapons you scavenge on the job. John Wick Hex complements the style of the films with a unique graphic noir art design and features the world class voice talents of Ian McShane and Lance Reddick amongst its stellar cast.
_childDocuments_.name: John Wick Hex

_childDocuments_.review: I learned to speedrun this game when it originally came out on the Nintendo Switch, and have quite a few hours there. Google "Tanuki Justice Speedrun" and you can see the video there on SRC. I submitted this to GDQ 2021 and hopefully if it's accepted, will run it this year. It's a very fun, obscure platformer, and if you're into speedrunning at all - the speedrun is great. In fact, the entire game actually is clearly built (based on the achievements) around speedrunning in mind.This game is really good and the port is also very good from the Switch original. It's a kind of run & gunner platformer with partial bullet hell mixed in. There's very little RNG to deal with so beating the game will eventually involve memorizing enemy spawns and execution. You can expect probably a 2-3 hour casual playthrough on normal. The harder difficulty levels are actually quite insane. They increase enemy spawns/bosses, some level layouts and difficulty exponentially. The mechanics are really simple: you have an 8 way shot (and there's some confusion if you read the discussions about a feature called "lock position") but, it works as intended. Locking your position doesn't and isn't supposed to make you stand in one spot a la Contra 3, but it instead "locks" the last directional input you pressed - so it's entirely possible to be facing left, lock your position, run forward right while shooting behind you. This actually is a really good mechanic and makes carrying your forward momentum through stages or doing certain sections very useful buffering it in advance.There's a neat design choice where if you pause the game, your high score stops recording, which I like and am a fan of. Any score attack/difficulty achievements can't be cheased this way and just paused through.You have a shuriken you can upgrade through treasure chests that extends your range and a shield that allows you to take one extra hit (which the game is OHKO otherwise). There's a bomb meter where the more enemies you kill/damage you do, it fills up, and once the bomb meter is full you can release it. If at any point you die, you lose your shield, bomb meter (and bomb if it's stored) and upgraded shuriken and everything is reset back down to the minimal starting point. It's punishing.Overall, this game is good and I would especially grab it on sale. I tried to find a lot of bugs and glitches and there's one softlock present in the PC port that was in the Switch original. If you scroll the screen after getting to the waterfall in stage 3 up a bit, walk back left to the first rock and walk off of it, the game softlocks. There is partial controller support and I play(ed) this with a PS4 controller fine mapped via Steam Big Picture as a XBOX 360 controller.My one BIG issue, and only issue, is this game can't be windowed. IF you don't have a second display, this is extremely annoying when it comes to streaming and interacting with chat. If you don't stream at all or don't care, then this is really a non-issue. I absolutely wish this game could be windowed.Overall probably a 8/10 for me. Game is short, but the game is also good. It's even better if you approach it as a speedrun. Despite this review, I might keep my hours low and refund it. I bought it to support the developer on PC after originally buying it on Switch, but the lack of window mode makes it almost useless to me as my current setup is a 1 monitor setup ($5000~ PC/rig setup) and I don't plan to change that anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good little arcade-style action platformer. Gets pretty tough and a bit cheap in the last couple of levels, but I'm having a really good time. The controls are great and, while there were controller issues at launch, the game works perfectly with my PS4 controller now. The game took me an hour to beat on normal the first time, most of that was practicing stages 5 and 6, though. You unlock a pretty unique, challenging survival mode after beating the story, plus there are high scores to chase and two higher difficulties. I'm glad devs are still making games like these.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 5/5Notes: Personally I do believe the game is maybe a tad overpriced for how short it is, just strictly comparing to other games in the 15$ range. But as a game itself, it is very good. Only real complaint would be lack of a boss rush mode to practice the bosses.Word of advice for a first playthrough, do not bother with insane mode. You will almost certainly not finish the game, unless you are prepared to see the game over screen 100+ times. Play through the game on hard first, then move onto insane.This game is one of the most difficult on all of steam. It's only about 15 minutes long if you speedrun it, but getting all achievements would take you 100+ hours minimum. And realistically speaking you probably just wont get the achievements ever. And this isnt a complaint from me. Love the super difficult achievements, wether or not I ever achieve them.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun action platformer, but it's very tough. The last 2 levels the difficulty really ramps up.It's cool there are 3 difficulties, but when Normal is as challenging as it is it's kinda baffling there isn't a slightly easier mode available. I'm guessing it's so people don't finish the game in 15 minutes. Still, it would be good to have that option. Right now it's just Normal, Hard, and Insane. There's also only 6 levels plus a final boss level- It wouldve been great to have multiple levels per stage, like 1-1, 1-2 at least. The achievements are a masochists dream unfortunately as well.Pick it up on a nice sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Justice

_childDocuments_.review: Tanuki Justice is a hair-raising fast-paced, run & gun plat-former that follows in the style of difficult plat-former's on the NES such as Contra, Ninja Gaiden, and Mega-Man but in the vain of 90's gaming mascots such as Sonic the Hedgehog and Rocket Knight. Play alone or together as 2 tanuki ninjas who are on a quest to save feudal japan from the evil Emperor. However, the journey to stopping him ain't gonna be easy. Much like the games that inspired it, this game is a lot of fun with its fast-paced & challenging game-play that will keep you on your paws, colorful 8-bit graphics, and a catchy NES inspired soundtrack. The game is also pretty short and it won't take long to beat it, if your a pro. As mentioned earlier, this game is viciously hard and it requires precise timing, skill, and strategy to make it through. However similar to an arcade game, the game does have unlimited continues  that lets you retry as much as you want until you give up. But you start at the beginning of the level your at, thus making the game unforgiving. But it feels very rewarding upon completing each level and satisfied at the end (if your lucky). If you looking for a hard punishing game or one featuring cute & cuddly raccoon dogs as playable protagonists. Then this game is a must play for you. Just be sure not to break your keyboard nor your controller as this game is pretty mean.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell exactly what kind of game this is just by watching the trailer. Nothing changes mechanically at any point throughout the game. The game is short (6 stages plus a final boss "stage") and is geared towards replaying the stages to get a higher score or to conquer a higher difficulty setting. In terms of difficulty, I completed the game on Normal (the easiest setting). There are two higher levels of difficulty available from there, and I have no desire to touch them because Normal was challenging enough for me. The game is meant to be very challenging and is clearly designed with players who want to be pushed to their absolute limits in mind. If you watch the trailer and think "that looks fun, and I hope it's hard!" then this is the game for you. If you don't want both of those things, this is not the game for you.Other minor thoughts:Virtually no loading timesA couple of catchy stage songsVariety of environments throughoutI played with a DualSense, and the controls are good other than the "lock in place" button also locks you into moving if you push it while moving, which is not useful at all and can lead to unintentional deaths. Movement is responsive as you would expect it to be.Good game but I'm glad I only paid $3 because I got 98 minutes out of it and while I generally enjoyed my time with it (aside from some frustrations about my own badness), I don't think I'll touch it again. People who like to replay games (and who are good enough to touch the higher difficulty modes) will probably get more mileage out of this than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time platforming in this one. I like the art and music. I found that just throwing myself at the level to get a feel of the enemies and platforms was much more fun and productive than trying to pass a level on the first try. You try and get beat down and try and try and try and somehow you get through and beat the level boss and start the whole thing over again on another unique level. Infinite continues so long as you don't mind starting over at the beginning of a stage when you run out of lives. It's full of run and gun elements. I'll have more to say once I try it with my friend.Update 2 May 2021I enjoyed playing this one with my friend but I hope they add a feature over from one player. I had infinite continues while playing alone but in local cooperative I lost this feature. It was a bitter change as our experience in games like this is low. We would have played for much longer had we been given infinite continues. I play for the local cooperative experience in most games so this is always important. I bought the game I have infinite quarters and I want my free lives.
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Justice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that actually nails the "retro" design, not only on graphics but on gameplay and difficulty, yet it adds quality of life features like control/aim precision and stage select, so you can take your time to practice this game without much pressure.Character design is soo cute that you sometimes feel bad in making them explode, but somehow the bosses look so threatening and well made, I guess that's the trademark of the Aggelos creator.Music is simple and catchy, puts you in a good mood.tl;dr if you like challenging games with rewarding gameplay, this one is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tanuki Justice

_childDocuments_.review: fun title! this is a great action platformer. i like the 8bit art style, tight controls and great gameplay (unlike other all-to-common cashgrabs on 8bit/pixel games.) price is steep and it's just 22mb but i'd say it's easily worth 8-11$ so w/e. regarding the one reviewer complaining about the double jump: i had zero issues with double jump. regarding the other neg reviewer re controls: controllers are supported flawlessly, the controls are tight and all-around feel great --responsive and solid...the locking in place mechanic works as intended and is a necessary addition in the genre...you don't have to use the running/lock in place mechanic if you don't want to but the locking aim mechanic is essential to being able to navigate.

_childDocuments_.review:
Inconspicuous combination of a platformer bullet hell with cute, pixel graphics. Tanuki Justice will challenge your precision jumping and shuriken throwing skills.

Features:
• Dynamic gameplay with visuals that fit the atmosphere.
• Dozens of different types of enemies.
• Classical shurikens over the head and a giant shuriken for difficult moments.
• Playable in single or two-player mode.

Description:
Tanuki Justice is a continuous intensive action run’n gun in which you incarnate a tanuki brother and sister. You’ll face hundreds of enemies in feudal Japan. Varied environments with landscapes of all kinds, retro and fast rhythmic music, numerous and difficult situations reminiscent of good old arcade games. A gameplay both simple and rich allowing spectacular actions. Possibility to play with 2 people for even more fun. And challenges that will challenge even the most skilled players. Time will be your worst enemy.

name: After Us
detailed_description: After Us (Original Soundtrack) is included with your game purchase on Steam. Experience the stunning atmospheric original soundtrack of After Us, composed by Daniel Elms. Comprised of 46 songs with a runtime of well over 3 hours, this score captures the emotional exploration of desolation and hope that players find within the game. Play as Gaia, the Spirit of Life, and navigate stunning platforming environments in an abstract world to salvage the souls of extinct animals. Revive these creatures after learning their final fate: the last whale harpooned, the final eagle caged, the last deer hunted down, and more, while you survive encounters with dangerous, oil-covered Devourers that roam the wasteland in search of remaining life. In this emotional journey from the creators of the critically acclaimed Arise: A Simple Story , you alone can restore life to the planet. Key Features: • Gaia’s journey : the last animals have died, and Mother has used all of her Life Force to save their souls, now trapped in their vessels. Gaia’s quest is to rescue each of their souls and bring them back to Mother’s Ark. Gaia’s traversal abilities will allow you to glide, jump, and dash to explore new areas and evade deadly traps, while her special gifts will grant you the power to clear the oil that consumes the world, face hungry Devourers, and break souls free. • A vast, surrealistic world : see through Gaia’s eyes the desolated landscapes that depict the destructive relationships between humans and nature in a beautiful demonstration of abstract artistry. From dying forests to the heart of crumbling cities, through the dry seabed and polluted skies, each environment will offer new challenges for Gaia to face and will present her different versions of the Devourers’ wake of destruction as she spreads life and beauty on her path. • A story of contrasts : After Us offers a somber look at a world decimated by human impact. As you guide Gaia’s light through it and discover the causes behind the destruction, you will learn the fate of the Devourers as agents of extinction, but also agents of progress, love, and hope.

_childDocuments_.review: A week ago I was diagnosed with a terminal illness and the doctors have given me a year at best. I'm so glad I was able to play this masterpiece before I go. I don't know how many people will see this; but I recommend to you to buy this game if you do see it. Gameplay, atmosphere, graphics, story... everything is masterfully crafted. Thank you Piccolo, you have made my final days ones of joy.
_childDocuments_.name: After Us

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to give this game an awesome review but I can't. The game's visuals are freaking amazing. So many scenes in this game could be put in art books and they'd be viewed as prime examples of surrealist masterpieces. The game is ten out of ten on that basis. The only reason I kept playing so long was to see more of these visuals. The bird cage area was amazing.What does the game do wrong? Well... pretty much everything else.The game is a very artsy piece and it lacks a lot of things you'd probably expect a 'game' to have. You spend most of your time just platforming from point A to point B. That's fine as a mechanic for progression but there isn't anything even resembling a story here. Thematically, game reminds me a lot of Ori and the Blind Forest or Little Nightmares.  Unfortunately, where those games had deep and engrossing stories and good fight mechanics, After Us doesn't have any of that. The fights that there are, are very forgettable and the story is on the same basis as Super Mario Brothers: a paper thin excuse to go platform through N worlds for a few hours. The world is huge and you have ample opportunities for exploration but the games fails to give incentives for exploration so you likely won't do it. Most of the stuff you can find during exploration in the game is pointless from a gameplay perspective and there is no real narrative that the extras could provide bonus material to. The game excels at environmental story telling but without actual characters to provide some kind of hook, it doesn't land as hard as it could.I know that these guys were trying to do an art house game and more power to them but the game really needed a better player experience to sell us on continuing the game. It doesn't have it.  Visuals do not an experience create. Even a modest story like Ori and the Blind Forest or Little Nightmares could have provided fertile ground to keep the player engaged. The game feels a lot like its trying to take a page from Prince of Persia(2008) where each level cleared feels like a real accomplish and like your cleansing corruption from the world. The thing is that game had great boss fights and a very likable pair of characters to hook us into the game and keep us going. When we cleanse an area in this game, we don't feel like we're striking a blow against evil, we just feel like we're hit a checkpoint.Should you play it? Honestly, I found the game boring. And that sucks because I loved the visuals so much that I kept playing long after I was bored to tears before giving up.

_childDocuments_.review: The greatest potential to destroy this fragile planet we call "home" comes from each and every one of . The way the developers intertwined this theme into the entirety of the game is brilliant (the environment, the end level encounters and game mechanics). Explore haunting environments by either jumping, sprinting, floating, sliding or wall running to help retrieve various animal spirits that were driven to extinction by . Each location has a central theme with a new movement ability to traverse the area to reach eight trapped main animal spirits needed for the completion of your quest. Traversal mechanics can be imprecise at times as you often float over or barely miss the platform you intended to land on which might frustrate some people. The occasional combat zones are equally as frustrating as your ability to fight back are lack-luster and often results in you retreating to gain back your stamina before heading into battle again. There are many animal spirits to be found throughout the world with some easy to locate while others are easy to see but getting to the location will require exploration to discover hidden paths. The game can take anywhere between 7 to 15 hours to complete depending if your trying to find all the animal spirits or not. [8/10]If you get easily upset or depressed by dark surrealism and/or you are uncomfortable with seeing animals hurt then you may want to avid playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Yes, but with some warnings.  Read these carefully before deciding whether to pick it up or not.① If you're uncomfortable with seeing animals hurt, you might want to avoid it.  The major animal spirits in each region depict how that animal died, and it can be pretty graphic.  Details: ② The camera is rough at times, if you have motion sickness issues or vertigo it might be a bit too much.  I have persistent vertigo, and while I was able to power through it, some areas I couldn't play for long.  Examples:   When you're captured during fights, the camera will zoom out a bit and sometimes place itself inside of walls or the ceiling.  It also wobbles around quite a bit during some fights which can make sensitive people nauseous.③ The game requires the use of a controller, keyboard controls are NOT supported.While beautiful, in a bit of a gruesome way, it's overall a bit of a depressing game.  The themes of environmental destruction and extinction are very vividly on display.The gameplay is mostly platforming, overall it's on the easier side but there are some tricky areas.  These areas require tight timing or precision.  This is especially noticeable anywhere near bubbling goop, as tentacles reach out to grab you from it.  The really narrow passages between goop/oil is sometimes hard to tell where is safe and where is not.  There are a few other platforming sections where you are clearly on a platform and you still get grabbed.  One area  requires fast movement and well aimed shots of your orb to deactivate some traps.  While the checkpoints are usually pretty good, there are a few areas with poorly placed ones.  There are some puzzles but they're not usually super difficult to figure out.This is a semi-indie game running the Unreal engine, so it's not super optimized.  While most areas run decently well, there are a few areas which stutter heavily.  This is most visible in the Power Plant, since you have large puzzle and object dense regions with a lot of particle effects.  The stutters and frame rate drops are extremely bad on one of the puzzle regions.It ran well on my Linux desktop with the standard Proton and no other changes.  On the Steam Desk, you may need to lower settings due to it being not very optimized.Overall, I enjoyed it but consider the warnings carefully.Edited:  Formatting broke, just updated the formatting to be more easy to read.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's artwork is aesthetically stunning. Absolutely beautiful. A++ I thoroughly enjoyed some sections of the game, including the revelation of each vessel, but the overall gameplay mechanics gave me overwhelming anxiety. Serious nightmare fuel. I will probably never play this game again. My hands were throbbing after completing some of the more daunting aerial acrobatics.The vast majority of this game sees you platform jumping from point A to point B over unforgiving chasms of death. Miss the jump? Try again. And again. And again. If you struggle with aerial platforming games you're going to have a very bad time with this one. If you thrive under pressure and love wall running/jumping/dashing while cheating death at every turn, then this game is right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: After Us

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, this is an excellent experience: poignant, interesting, a little haunting. The sound design is relaxing and appealing. As a game, though, this leaves something to be desired; worse, it fails as a story.Like most of the animals you're tasked with rescuing, the story has a great deal of heart and very little reason. The protagonist is tasked with getting sad about finding petrified remains of extinct animals, so a magic grove can have a record of some of the charismatic megafauna while it plants a pretty monoculture. Even something as simple as giving the player the choice whether to accept the final sacrifice or not might have rescued the message from despair, but alas--there are no choices left, only seeing the hollow promise through to the grim end. The only way to 'win' is not to play.It works reasonably well as a denouement for environmentalism, but if you don't feel like giving up quite yet, this game is probably not for you.
