_childDocuments_.review: Bruh, this game is actually hard, at least on the harder of the 2 difficulties.I didn't expect this game to have such slick combat mechanics like parrying bullets for the ultimate risk-reward.As well, the mechanic of stealing enemies weapons is a well executed mechanic but parrying bullets is a little tricky when switching to all the different timings, that's why I recommend you really focus on parrying as a technique when you gain the ability to do it with kung-fu.All in all this game kicks ass from a gameplay perspective, and the setting of a rebel folk hero in Japanese-occupied Taiwan is both incredibly unique and well-realised.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful platformer that leans heavily into a comic book aesthetic. It does try to unobtrusively teach you a little bit of history of Taiwan under Japanese occupation but is a solid game, even if you don't care to be educated.We got to start with the aesthetic: the title screen is a comic book lying on a table — as you start the game, it opens up, as if to the page you left at, and then transitions to the game. When you die, it transitions back to the comic book. Every screenshot from the game looks like a print, and the story advances through a mix of cutscenes and comic book panels.The Legend of Tianding retells the legend of a real folk hero. All the buildings in the game are made from historic references, and the game offers some background for each, if you want to read it, as well as a hundred other little infos.Mechanically, the game is superb. The levels feel interesting and a pleasure to look at. The fight system that lets you steal weapons from your enemies is fresh and polished. All of the different abilities and upgrades give you more agency over your playstyle.Despite all the cell shading and nice 3D backgrounds, the framerate never dropped below 120 in 4K on my GTX 1080 — I have certainly seen simpler games do worse. There was one time I fell through the level, but it only lost me a few seconds of progress. Have not encountered any other bugs.Oh, and you can also get an achievement for listening through the most tedious song in all of gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: There are almost no games that are set in Taiwan, especially during the Japanese Empire period. This game really sets itself apart by giving us an historical setting that is almost unexplored in gaming.The developers crafted this game with care by telling a legend story of a Taiwanese Robin Hood, Liao Tian Ding, in a comic-styled graphical presentation on top of a good set of characters that speak both Japanese and Chinese, portraying some historical accuracy and in consequence giving a more immersive experience.Combat is simple but fun to play. There are some simple combos to do and it plays similarly to Guacamelee.It is a short game that can be completed in just 4 hours, but it is very fun to play.This kind of game is something that is really rare to see these days and there's probably never going to be another game like this set in Taiwan or in this historical period since the chinese government has been increasing it's influence in censoring videogames recently.It's a good game and is very cheap when it's on sale. I recommend getting it for it's unique setting and historical/cultural value.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on real history about Japan Invasion Taiwan during WWII, player controls a rebellion Liao Tianding to defend the city. The battles are in arcade style with long distance to run and almost endless enemies to fight, I can't say it is satisfying due to the uninteresting map, limited attack routine and highly repeated enemies. Apart from the battle, player can wander around several areas of the city, which is actually well restored. The cutscene is in good comic style, some conversations are insulting but fun when describing the bad guys. This game features 2 endings, if you refuse to do errand job you'll watch the default ending, which I liked - reminds me of a shocking scene in the movie The King's Man released in 2021.If you decide to spend half an hour helping and reaching to everyone, you alters the fate of your character. Both endings are reasonable.Overall, this game is a bit outdated, I rate it positive for the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very good Game.The Legend of Tianding is a 2D-Side Scrolling-Jump'n'Run Action Brawler.It is quite short but in a good way, it doesn't overstay it's welcome. Actually thinking about it, this really was the perfect time for this Game (slightly over 9 hours with doing all the Side Quests).Let's go quickly through the motions.Graphics:The Game is Hand Drawn and presented in a Comic/Manga Style. The visuals are crisp and a Game like this will hold up for centuries without anyone saying that this is unplayable because it does not look good.Voice Acting:I don't understand Taiwanese but what you can expect is typically "eastern" over the Top Voice Acting like in those Anime Series.Sound:No complaints here.Music:Some good tracks in here, I didn't dislike it.Gameplay:It's good fun if you like a brawler and it also has teeny tini (!!) hints of Metroidvania Movement. The Controls are good, jumping around and fighting is fun as well, especially when you get more abilities.Secrets are easy to find but still rewarding, there is a ton of items you can get.The Bosses are a little highlight, I think it's about 6 bosses but they are all very well designed and fun.Especially the last one which was the only challenging one, but when you got his moveset down, it is just a fun time.Story: It's the Legend of Tian-Ding...Didn't care too much.I had a few very small gripes with the Game. 1. Some Achievements need you to grind some levels over and over. Not so great.2. The translation was not always on point, sometimes I even had French translation shown up directly after the English one. And no, this was not intended.3. There was one quest in particular which seemed buggy, in the End I still finished it somehow but this problem seemed to persist for many players.Apart from a few minor annoyances, I can wholeheartedly recommend this Game, if you like a short but sweet brawler...

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic really sold me on this game, and I am happy to announce that the gameplay is there to back it up. Combat and exploration both flow incredibly well, and it makes for an enjoyable experience whether you are clearing out the levels and looking for treasure, or engaging in a much more intensive boss fight. And playing on Wanted Outlaw the bosses did feel intensive, at least compared to the levels that preceded them, but checkpoints literally at the boss room door dampens any frustration that might cause. Anyway, welcome to my Start Menu Review: What really struck me the moment I booted the game was just how beautiful the start screen is, and I could rant for days about how nice it is to boot a game and not have my ears blasted by an opening cutscene that precedes any option to regulate the in-game volume. The attention to detail is amazing, and yet it's conceptually very simple. You start with a simple desk, upon which you have an old radio, a collection of Pogs features characters in the game, and a colorful comic book featuring our main protagonist. The start menu is the comic book itself, which opens as you press Space/X. It's a beautiful integration of aesthetic and function that we see less and less of with modern games that favor a more minimalist approach to UI design. It just charms me right off the bat. Other notes? Ding-ding 10/10I really wish we'd get an option to keep Ding-ding as a costume for the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is okay. It has some things I don't prefer, but overall doesn't do anything egregiously awful and doesn't excel in any particular area that really wows me either. As a metroidvania brawler, movement and action are a little slow to my taste. There isn't any means of increasing movement speed, so you're stuck to the character's very floaty running pace. The forward kick gives you a slight boost, so I tried spamming that as a means of increasing traversal speed, but it wasn't fast enough that it was worth the trouble. Not an objectively bad thing, but definitely very dissatisfying for me when it comes to this genre of games.Action is also just okay. You get a total of 4 combat techniques and it doesn't get much more complex from there. Stringing these techniques together to make a combo is pretty limited. At most, you might string 3 techniques together, mixed in with a bit of the basic attack. There's a neat mechanic introduced with the One-Inch Punch that lets you immediately input the One-Inch Punch after a basic attack. Would have liked to see more combat mechanics like this, where there are special circumstances to make certain strings of attacks come out faster. I prefer my combat more on the fast paced side with the opportunity to string almost everything together. Games like Dust an Elyisan Tale and Odin Sphere are great examples of this where the player is really just allowed to let loose. And it's SO much fun. As it is for Tianding though, combat consists of doing a 2-3 input combo, watching the enemy crumple, and then waiting for them to get up so you can do another 2-3 hit combo that will crumple them again. It isn't very exciting to me.Which brings me back to Traversal. The best metroidvania brawlers meld both traversal and combat. Tianding makes use of its combat techniques as traversal techniques in some pretty standard fun ways, but unfortunately there's a lot of areas where it feels like just two separate things that occur in the same game. Not necessarily bad, but it does get a little wonky in certain mechanics. The worst example is the grapple hook. It occurs really rarely, and is used almost entirely only for traversal puzzles. To the point that I have to remind myself what button it is every few times it shows up. What makes this especially sad is that there already is an enemy grapple hook system. It's the sash that lets you throw and steal from enemies. It would have been amazing if these two mechanics were mixed together so you could grapple, throw, and fling yourself with enemies. And lastly, the writing and story is really just okay. I grew up watching classic wushu martial arts films, so I get a lot of the themes of where this story was drawing from. There's the female childhood friend that sold herself into a brothel, and now you're trying to buy back her freedom. There's the evil foreign colonialists, and the one single good foreigner that the main character kind of banters with comedically. And so on. They're all classic set pieces I appreciate, so I'd be a hypocrite to say they're bad. But it certainly feels unimagined. There's nothing interesting that really sets it apart, and feels more like I'm playing out an old wushu film template. It's like the videogame version of Christian Rock songs where they take a classic pop song and just replace every other word with Lord or Jesus. Which I can't stress enough isn't necessarily bad. But it's definitely not a recipe for anything particularly good. So overall, it's a middling experience. I wouldn't call this game bad, and I got pretty much the experience I figured I was paying for. But I wouldn't recommend it over dozens of other games of the same genre that do the same things but in so much more interesting ways.

_childDocuments_.review: I was curious about this game, as the graphics is very "comic style"; and the animations are also well done. The gameplay overall is the usual metroidvania, with jumps, slides and similar, to reach weird spots and unlock new skills. At its core is a platform game with complex levels and final boss at the end of the level; it is quite hard but there are plenty of save points during the level; so it is manageble. If you like a challenge you may want to try this one out, as you need to learn patterns.I am not really into that, as I like a hard game but I don't like games that basically ask you to get a second job and train for a game to learn how to beat enemies and bosses, unless you set the difficulty level for it... This game has  a base difficulty that is asking you to learn patterns, so you can't work around that unless you spend time getting better at it. If that is your thing, this game is a good game; otherwise just move on as it won't be that enjoyable I am afraid.Story is OK; very reminiscent of "hero from the people help others against oppressing category in power"; we have seen that story in many different forms so it is a re-hash of that (not sure if it is based on a known hero or what; I am not familiar with it). Sound is great, with nice voiceover and the strong part is graphics and animations, which are really well made. What lacks is the combat, which is not bad but it is clunky and sometimes miss the mark in terms of dodge, especially against certain enemies that seems to have the upperhand no matter what, unless you just jump and avoid them instead of dodge them. The unique thing is that you can steal the weapons of your enemies until they "break"; which is fun to do.Overall a solid action metroidvania style game, which should entertain people that like hard games. 6 out of 10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Got it on a sale, The Legend of Tianding is a short and fun game with a story narrative on Taiwan history during the Japanese occupation period. Its a Metroidvania game that is similar to Hollow Knight, but a lot easier. It doable to perfect this game in one single play through;-Play on outlaw mode, its more challenging though, and you have to redo the boss many times to learn their moves-Give money to beggars until they don't need it anymore-Upgrade the weapon from blacksmith and bun from chef until max-Search youtube video on where all the treasure box is located across the 4 map-Use triple jump to go on top of all buildings for hidden collectibles-On the train map, there is a bird which you need to rope off to the second bird for hidden collectibles-Use rope on all enemy types until you get their corresponding talisman, they will have a blinking light on them until you found the talisman-Use rope on all boss until they drop the items-There will be 2 instance (Li-Hong asking the farmers where the money comes from, and A-Guai to be sold away), and you will given the option to beat or trick, select beat and then reenter the location to choose trick on the second time-Defeat the final boss after all collectibles and talisman
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous 2D platform combat game with a hint of Metroidvania progression it tells the tale of what appears to be Taiwans version of Robin Hood, a thief that targets the strong to protect and help the weak. The comic book style graphics are superb and animation is smooth throughout. Combat is somewhere between Hollow Knight and Guacamelee with snappy controls and a nice mix of special moves.  Boss fights are full soulslike  nasties with patterns to learn and patience needed to prevail.The only real downside is that a skilled player can probably see everything in under 8 hours. Personally I'll take quality over quantity and i thouroghly enjoyed my time in turn of the 20th Century Taiwan.78/100

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet is the easiest way to summarize this game. Although characters might not feel fleshed out, it's still a fun and straight-forward story. It plays like a platformer/beat-em-up, with the story told from dialogue and manga panels. I expected much more basic combat, but ended up getting a bit more with combo potentials and a variety of weapons.+Stylish art style that fits the story and setting incredibly well.+Fun and theater-esque story with summaries at the end of each chapter+Platforming segments to break up monotony of brawlsNot a difficult game, however, I still felt some reward with finding secret areas and beating bosses. I think on sale, this game should be considered if you need a short break.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good action platformer. Greatly enjoyed the presentation in between the artstyle, stylized comic storytelling, voice acting, and music. Tells a simple story with questionable dialogue/plot points and is somewhat predictable but the presentation elements kept me engaged for its ~5 hour story and by the end I was satisfied.Basic combat is mostly repetitive and simple, but the enjoyment comes from stealing mechanic ends which allows the player to steal weapons from enemies. Ended up being fun in engaging players to extend their combos since each weapon is slightly different in how it hits, how it staggers/knockdowns, whether it picks enemies off the ground, and what the best direction to toss enemies in conjunction with the weapon. I was getting bored towards the very very end due to lack of enemy variety but overall felt perfect for the length. Other things I appreciate is perfect dodge system granting increased dps and absence of enemy contact damage.Game mostly respects your time. Most collectables are easy to find/obtain and you can revisit levels to find collectibles that you missed. Only major grips is that some collectibles are required to be stolen from enemies which can take an annoying amount of time to obtain if your rng is poor. Also a couple of achievements require a second playthrough to make a different choice which unnecessarily pads gametime, especially since these choices and a second playthrough add nothing to the experience.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, the combat is simple and gets the job done at all times but when it comes to the bosses it just jumps from an 8 to an 11 (that final boss was just amazing) Loved the cultural index with the collectables and even though you have to grind a bit to get the 100% the game doesn't breach the line to annoying, great game to go for all the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent brawler platformer. The mechanics are slick (especially the sash, it's so much fun using it), the art style is very cool, the story and the characters are concise and well done, the music fits the setting perfectly, the voice acting is pretty good (Liao laughing at people is especially charming. Really embodies that trickster, hero of the people fighting against oppression archetype well and lightens some pretty heavy themes), the stage design is solid, the bosses are challenging without being overly infuriating and the Wanted Outlaw difficulty is just right.There are a few points that could be improved though: 1) There are so many collectibles that the player can get a bit lost about where they could have missed one, especially when their collection is almost complete. It would help tremendously if we could see the item descriptions before they were unlocked or if instead of the regular "???" in the description, it pointed the player in a direction like "Boss drop", "Enemy drop", "Chest drop", "Secret drop", "Side Quest drop" and "Story drop";2) The objetive of most of the side quests can be a little confusing in the beginning. It took me a while to realize that what the characters wanted were, largely, for me to find specific collectible items across the stages. So, most of the time, I could already succesfully complete a side quest the moment I got it and that was a bit weird. It would've been clearer if we got these kinds of quests before having access to the stages they can be completed in and not after;3) The Glide mechanic (and Shadow Vanish too for that matter) is pretty cool. A shame we only get access to it near the end and spend so little time with it. It does trivialize some of the previous challenges but it's so cool, I wanted to glide around more stages;4) When the story panels and dialogues are automated, they pass by too fast, like during the very beginning and the ending. It would be nice to be able to control their speed on all occasions, like during the regular stages;5) Not enough Red Turtle. "The Legend of Red Turtle", when? :pOverall, it was a real pleasure to play <3

_childDocuments_.review: is a side-scrolling action game with fluid combat, comic-like art design, and plenty of Taiwanese folklore. Over 10 hours of gameplay, you can explore Taipei City, protect the poor, end the evil, and ultimately become a hero.If you’ve played  before, you probably know how the combat system works. In addition to using your default weapon — the knife — to perform a three-hit combo, you can also hold the left stick in any direction and press B to play special moves at any time during the strike. For example,  in the upward direction kicks foes into the air. The left/right one, , can quickly shorten the distance to the enemy.Besides, after stunning an opponent, you can deftly steal his weapon. Not only does this move to make him unarmed, but it also allows you to use that weapon multiple times. Personally, this move is the most entertaining one in the game. Weapons galore to steal, bringing a lot of variation to the battle. My favorites are pistols and bamboo poles — it's cool to attack someone from a distance.Each boss has its moves, which are pretty neat in my opinion. Given the long stun bars on bosses, you can't rely on the stealing mechanic. Therefore, you should observe circumspectly to dodge. However, the game’s boss fights aren’t flawless. The animations are not very good. For instance, every time the final boss unleashes a perilous attack that cannot be dodged, he will suddenly teleport to a corner if he is not there. Also, bosses have a low drop rate for collectibles, so it took me so much time to get them all.The main story of the game is simple and easy to understand, however, the way the game tells you is unique. This uniqueness starts even from the very beginning and continues throughout the game. Firstly, the start menu and cutscenes look like comic books, giving every player an old-fashioned vibe. Moreover, after you complete the chapter, a storyteller will summarize the chapter on the air in Hokkien (an official language of Taiwan). In addition, in-game collectibles are things that can evoke memories of old times. The developers did make an effort to show their culture.Overall, I would give it an 8 out of 10. Don't hesitate to give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say from the start that I'm not into side scrollers/beat-em-ups and stuff like that. The only reason i bought this game was that it gave me mad nostalgia because of its atmosphere straight from the 90s Hong Kong movies I grew up watching. They even have a train fight level!That being said, I was surprised to find out that  the game plays very smooth and even me, as a total scrub in this kind of genre, I manage to play through the levels and beat the bosses with relative ease (i'm playing on hard difficulty). The bosses especially get my praise - they're fun to fight and they're challenging, yet aren't frustratingly so. My gripe with the genre is its absolutely idiotic boss design where you have to grind the fight for hours and to remember their whole moveset to be able to beat them. Who thought it was a great idea to make the player fight the same boss 10+ times to kill it? No idea. Can't imagine anyone repeating the same damn thing a dozen of times and finding it interesting.Tianding handles the bosses spot on - are they hard? For me, yes. Do i have to spend a day on them? No. I managed to get through all the bosses so far in 2-5 tries. Which makes them challenging, but also not enough for me to want to drop the game out of frustration.The main character has several moves that he can link together, plus the ability to steal enemies' weapons from them. All this enables you to chain some sweet and fluid combos to wreck your enemies. The only problem i have with combat is that the enemies fall flat when you hit them enough times, and you have to wait for them to get up to continue fighting, which abruptly stops the flow of combat, You can still kick them with downwards kick while they're lying, but they'll get back down and you'll still have to wait.Overall the game is pretty simplistic, yet still fun. Hardcore fans of the genre might find it a bit shallow, but for a casual player like me, this game provides just enough challenge to keep playing and enjoy the plot and the fights.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Except for those moments where you're just darting around the city from one cutscene to the next, this game is a blast and keeps getting better and better. The boss fights? Oh man, they’re tough but so much fun. The controls are as smooth as butter on a hot skillet. The graphics and music? Full of personality, like your quirky uncle who insists he was abducted by aliens. And the story? It's weird, but in a way that’s totally my jam.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Tianding is a savior of sorts to the downtrodden and oppressed people of colonial Taiwan, and he will do everything in his power to steal from the rich and corrupt and give back to his people.  However, he is constantly on the run from authorities, so much so that people barely recognize him when they see him.  While the character animation in between gameplay sections leaves a lot to be desired, looking akin to a mobile game, the gameplay is a lot of fun, from kicking some bad guy butt, grabbing their billy club or pole staff, and then smacking their friends upside the head with it.  You can even pick up guns and bombs, and small talismans and other objects to help you become more effective with these weapons.  There are also combos to learn and use, and by the end of my 3-4 hour play session, I was combining moves into chain combos that were reminiscent of Smash Bros.  The story is deep with lots of little history elements and lore to be found in the items you pick up, but I did think the narrative sequences were just too long.  Like I wanted to learn the story, but at the same time I’m playing a game, not reading a book.  I had a lot of fun overall playing it, I just wish I’d gotten to play more and read less, especially early on.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty short, but solid. Controls in general are good, art's nicely stylized, music isn't a knockout but it never intrude. Combat's fairly simplistic, so if it was any longer it might overstay its welcome. Criticisms are that the translation is a touch spotty at points, the spider wire (sort of a hookshot for specific movement points) is fairly obnoxious to actually make do what you want, and the death pits in the third level are a blight. There was also two times early on where the screen dimmed into what might've been a tutorial, but no explanation actually showed up - probably something bugging out. Didn't interfere with gameplay as a whole though.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm into this. I'd give it about a 7/10. For the price you get a pretty decent yuxia martial arts story that embellishes on a famous hero from Taiwan's past. It's a pretty challenging and entertaining beat-em up side-scroller with some fun mechanics, and the setting feels really authentic as a turn-of-the-century comic book. The plot really reminds me of Wong Fei Hung stories, with a heavy dose of patriotism and colonial resistance. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have much to say about this game, other than I loved the combat and the presentation. The game takes a nice amount of inspiration from Guacamelee, with its directional attacks. It also ads its own unique flair, in form of a steal mechanic.The absolute highlight of this game are the boss fights. To me, they alone are worth the asking price. Finally, the game is set in early 20th century Taiwan, a setting not too common in videogames, which I also appreciated. My only major gripe is regarding the sidequests. Some don't give you any indication as to where you need to go. In most cases you'll just be told to go back to a previous area, and explore it again. This was a bit frustrating, because I did fully explore the first area, the sewers (the game said I found all collectibles), yet one sidequest asked me to go back there again, and I couldn't really be bothered to go through the same area a 3rd time. Furthermore, I think completion of the sidequests is also a requirement to get the true ending, but I can't confirm this, as I said, the game doesn't give you much of an indication. But honestly, I don't think you should bother with getting the true ending, unless you really love the game. Play through it, enjoy the  bosses and combat, and you'll get your money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it. Comic book style platformer. Its relatively short (took me about 12-13 hours to finish the campaign). The difficulty spikes between the two difficulty settings are quite high.As the game description explains: you play a Taiwanese freedom fighter (sorta like Robin Hood) during the Japanese occupation of Taiwan. The overall plot is to stop a big bad evil guy who runs the local police force from collecting a mythical sword. Between levels you do a few side quests. There's some replay value as you try to collect collectables which improve your stats/abilities slightly. The story is pretty compelling and full of betrayal, funny sidekicks, chases and suspense, etc. Feels like a comic book.Game play wise you are mostly doing martial arts and disarming weapons from villains and using those weapons against them (yes, these include guns and explosives but also swords, rocks and staffs).You can upgrade your abilities by collecting collectables, going to a few shops, and abilities earned through progress in the game.This game does have multiple endings depending on how many side quests you do, etc.Overall: I liked it. Fun comic style game play and a pretty good story. My only complaints: 1) for whatever reason a few (like 3-5) of the dialogue bubbles were in french instead of English. 2) the end game side missions had really neat mechanics where you had multiple ways of finishing them and they affected other side quests. It would have been neat to see this throughout the game more instead of just in the last minutes/hour of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding : By Triple F"The Legend of Tianding" is a side-scrolling beat 'em up action-adventure game that throws you headfirst into the shoes of the legendary Taiwanese folk hero, Liao Tianding. Developed by Creative Games & Computer Graphics, the game takes you on a thrilling journey through the bustling streets of Dadaocheng, Taipei, during the early 20th century, a period marked by Japanese colonial rule.The first thing that grabs your attention in "The Legend of Tianding" is its stunning visuals. The game utilizes a vibrant comic book art style, reminiscent of classic Hong Kong action movies. The environments are bursting with life, from the bustling markets of Dadaocheng to the serene temples nestled amidst the cityscape. The character designs are equally impressive, capturing the essence of the time period and the diverse cast of characters, from the stoic Tianding to the flamboyant opera singer, A-Gu.The core gameplay of "The Legend of Tianding" revolves around satisfying beat 'em up combat. Tianding's arsenal includes a wide variety of martial arts moves, from swift kicks and punches to powerful throws and grapples. The combat system is easy to pick up but offers enough depth to master, with combos, counters, and special attacks to keep things interesting. Additionally, the game incorporates environmental elements into combat, allowing you to use objects like benches and barrels as weapons or to gain a tactical advantage.While combat is the heart of the gameplay, "The Legend of Tianding" offers more than just mindless brawling. The game features a branching narrative, with choices you make throughout the story impacting the outcome and even unlocking different endings. You'll also encounter side quests and optional challenges that add variety to the experience and delve deeper into the lore of the game world.The soundtrack of "The Legend of Tianding" is a delightful blend of traditional Chinese instruments and modern electronic music. The score perfectly complements the action, building tension during intense fights and creating a sense of atmosphere during exploration. The voice acting, available in both English and Mandarin, is commendable, bringing the characters to life with believable performances.One of the most captivating aspects of "The Legend of Tianding" is its historical setting. The game does a fantastic job of recreating the atmosphere of colonial Taiwan, showcasing the cultural clashes and tensions of the time period. You'll encounter historical figures and learn about the struggles and triumphs of the Taiwanese people under Japanese rule. The game serves as a valuable educational tool, raising awareness about a period of history often overlooked in the mainstream.While "The Legend of Tianding" excels in many aspects, it's not without its flaws. The story, while engaging, lacks the depth and complexity found in some other narrative-driven games. The level design can feel repetitive at times, and the pacing can be inconsistent, with some sections feeling drawn out. Additionally, the English translation can be somewhat clunky at times, occasionally affecting the overall experience.Despite its minor shortcomings, "The Legend of Tianding" is a captivating and memorable experience. The combination of exhilarating combat, a captivating story, and a unique historical setting makes it a game worth checking out. Whether you're a fan of beat 'em up action games, interested in learning about Taiwanese culture, or simply looking for a visually stunning and engaging experience, "The Legend of Tianding" has something to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: “The Legend of Tianding” is a charming beat’em-up platformer that unfolds in the backdrop of Japanese colonial era Taipei and its surroundings. With its stunning, vibrant backgrounds and colorful graphics reminiscent of manga art, the game seamlessly intertwines fast-paced action with elements of some light metroidvania-style exploration and side-questing around the city. The narrative remains simple enough to avoid getting into the way of the combat, which I found addictive and challenging. At least on hardcore difficulty, it often took me a while to master the controls and learn the movements and attack patterns of each boss. One notable aspect of the game is the evident care the developers have taken to incorporate elements of Taiwanese culture and history in the form of authentic historical artifacts as collectibles (even though their presentation is somewhat dry). As a Taiwanese history enthusiast, I found this to be another welcome addition that gives the game a unique feel.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun action platformer with limited backtracking, great visual style, fluid controls and a fun story. There's a ton of stuff to collect, and each collectable both gives you some kind of buff, and also gives you snippets of info on early 20th century Taiwanese history and culture. The story's got a comic book aesthetic, mixed with the presentation style of a radio serial. It's really very charming. The combat is fun and fluid, and the soundtrack KICKS ASS. It's not really time appropriate, but when you're pulling off badass kung-fu moves, the blaring rock tracks feel AWESOME. The game's fairly short, but the boss encounters are all unique and memorable. Honestly, I loved pretty much everything about this game, except that a few side fetch-quests and some achievements are hooked into RNG. You gain some collectible items and most of the amulets by "stealing" them from enemies, and the drop rate for these items is randomized. There's amulets that boost drop rate, but it can still be annoying to have to replay sections over and over in order to get everything. But overall, the fun combat and fluid traversal take most of the frustration out.  Other than that, this game is great.

_childDocuments_.review: Creative Games Computer Graphics Corporation (Creative Games), successfully produced a good side-scrolling beat-em up with style and substance that you can't help but be impressed with the offering. Follow the folk hero Liao Tian Ding as he kung fus his way to defeat occupying Japanese army and on the way, experience friendship, betrayal all the in a beautifully rendered 2.5D graphics in an old-school Hong Kong comic style animation. The devs nailed the movement and moveset, giving the title character a breadth of action skills that chain with each other, with controls that feels tight and responsive, with Soul-lite combat system coupled and some genuine interesting world-building and level design.The one major complaint I have is that I wish there was more. 4 hours of basic story line play-through means that the lack of content can be a turn-off for buyers. Barring that one major flaw, Tian Ding is a good game that showcases the potential for what Creative Games is able to accomplish, and they are now on my radar. Recommended. Immediately you're going to notice the artwork. It is very reminiscent of 80s Tony Wong comics. Seeing this art really gave me some nostalgia and with it's excellent animation and rendering, it's almost like watching a comic book come alive. I've always said that any 2D game must -  - have good controls and Creative Games delivers. Tian Ding controls excellent. He moves fast and his move-set chains with each other so that your platforming reach is extended. The move-set is similar to Ori and the Will O' the Wisp, including the use of charm slots. Combat is what I would call Souls-lite mechanics with the use of Stamina bar that is limited to your special attacks. i works quite well here since it doesn't limit your overall movement, giving you freedom to dodge as much as you want. The story here is a basic Chinese folk hero story, complete with exaggerated villains, betrayal and tragedy. If you've seen old Hong Kong movies, you would know that Chinese/Hong Kong stories have very little depth. Tian Ding suffers from this, as the plot is rather predictable. If you're looking for a grand story, Tian Ding doesn't have it unfortunately but it's still acceptably good. The characters too lacks depth. There's no character development, no arc and most of the supporting characters serve only 1 or 2 function. Other than Tian Ding and maybe the main villain, you won't ever remember the rest of the cast. I don't mind it since most of the hard work went into making a good game. However, this is something that the devs could expand in their next project. The music is a mix of modern and traditional Chinese music. A lot of it are bangers but there are quite a few that I can imagine many non-Asian players might not particularly care for. However, none of it is offensive to the ear and with a little more exposure, I'm willing to bet that players will acquire a taste for it. The content unfortunately, is short. There are only 4 dungeons and while the level design for these dungeons are good, it's just doesn't feel nearly enough as other beat-em up games. The developers tries to pad this with side-quests that sends you to these dungeons repeatedly. Well, it doesn't actually work though as padded content is still padded content and doesn't hide the fact the games  is rather small. Still, since the developers got everything else right, for me at least I can excuse this one major flaw. However, you might not feel the same if you value-conscious of your money. So buyer beware. Despite that one major flaw, I'd say on the whole, the package is quite good and it is definitely a stunning debut for a new developer. The game is fun and I am eager to see what Creative Games can do with a bigger budget. If you feel like risking it, The Legend of Tian Ding is a good beat-em up game that you might just enjoy. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding is a side-scrolling beat-em-up, metroidvania-lite that I really enjoyed. Coming from developer Creative Games Computer Graphics Corporation, their freshman effort is surprisingly polished and a great first effort out of the gate.You play as the titular Liao Tianding, a Taiwanese Folk Hero, as you fight against the oppressive Japanese set in the early 20th century. The first thing that caught my eye was the comic book-style presentation, which I found to be quite effective. Backgrounds look great and the comic panel interstitials to convey the story were beautifully drawn.It’s here where really my main complaint comes in; I wish the characters were also 2D instead of 3D. It’s a minor gripe but one that I think would have made the presentation and art style more cohesive overall.Gameplay is pretty straightforward, you gain more attacks and abilities as the game goes on as well as the ability to steal your enemy’s weapons, which can introduce a bit of strategy into fights. I found the story to be just ok and the presentation of it to be a bit overly long at times considering the genre of game that is. That said, I can appreciate the studio wanting to tell their story and its certainly great to get games from places we don’t normally, like Taiwan.I finished the game in a hair under 4 hours with minimal side quests done, so this seems like one that would best be gotten on a sale. That said though, I really enjoyed my time with The Legend of Tianding and will definitely be keeping an eye on what the studio does next.

_childDocuments_.review: I started on the harder difficulty, and it only took me 10 hours to complete the game with 100% achievements, but still.. I'd whole-heartedly recommend this game to just about anyone. The characters are so fun and lovable that it's easy to connect with the characters regardless of their different race and background, and the comic book style is so well integrated with the on screen graphics that it never feels tack-on. It really does an amazing job of riding the line between real life and video game. The world just feels like you're dropped into Taiwan during the height of the Japanese occupation, and then you're battling cops and beggars with kung fu and bullets ricocheting off your fists. It's fun and stupid and ridiculous and yet amazing, it has a heart and purpose - Tian-ding is fighting for something greater than himself. There are fantasy elements to the story but they don't overwhelm the heart of the story or muddle the consequences. The tension starts low and rises throughout the story, never dropping before you reach the end goal, which is both satisfying and difficult. I'm a pretty dedicated gamer. I've played a lot of games. This the Legend of Tianding is spectacular. It isn't just a game, it's a piece of a Taiwanese art.

_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a promising start but ultimately none of the elements of this game come together in a satisfying way. The story is mediocre, with no depth to any of its characters and multiple plot points that are brought up and never get resolved. The gameplay is fine, but it's so derivative of other games (the Guacamelee games in particular) that it just feels like a worse version of them. The combat and platforming aren't complex or audiovisually satisfying enough to yield any response from the player beyond "gee, that sure was a section of gameplay I just completed." The presentation is arguably the game's best asset, but even that isn't much to write home about. the unique setting and cultural history of early 1900's Taiwan is interesting, but outside of collectible items with some text you can read after finding them, the game doesn't delve much into the history aspect, to its detriment in my opinion. The graphical style is nice, mostly carried by the early manga artstyle they use for the comic book cutscenes sprinkled throughout the game. the music is fairly forgettable and not a single track comes to mind when I think back on the game, aside from two of the boss themes. I wish I could recommend the game, as I love Metroidvanias, and I ESPECIALLY love beat 'em up games, but Tianding is ruined because of how it spreads itself too thin between all of its systems. The hub world, sidequests, and metroidvania elements sound good in theory, but in practice they just dilute a game that clearly didn't have the budget to meet those marks. If Tianding was a completely linear dedicated platformer with a more expressive moveset, or a linear dedicated beat 'em up with a longer list of moves and combos, the game would have likely turned out as a better, more tightly designed game. If you're interested in this game for any reason other than the historical aspect, I recommend just getting one of the following and having a better time with it:-The Dishwasher Vampire Smile-Guacamelee 1+2-Dust: An Elysian Tail

_childDocuments_.review: "The Legend of Tianding" is a Nintendo Switch/handheld platformer game set in early 20th Century Taiwan... while it was the last days of the Wild West in the USA, Taiwan had it's own problems and this is as much a cultural exploration of Taiwans history as a game, which adds a (perhaps niche) element to the package.Fundamentally this is a handheld platformer/beat 'em up where you use console-esque combat moves to fight enemies, and there's a fair bit of platforming as well, with the usual double jumps, dashes and other precision platformer moves needed to help move through the narrative driven game levels. There's an overwhelming amount of mediocre Visual Novel/E-book style cutscenes in this game.  So you'll spend a huge amount of time not playing the game, but clicking through endless lines of poorly written VN text cutscenes because the developers couldn't work out how to relate their narrative through the game mechanics, and decided instead it would be better to compete with reading a book for your time.  We're here to play games, not watch hours of garbage intersituals.On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Also, a special note that the 3D cel shaded graphics look really great, another fine example to demolish arguments that "2D graphics are fine"... compare any of them to this, and The Legend of Tianding is a clear winner.Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.The controls and game handling are notably very clunky and unsmooth here.  They work "okay", but it's janky and unsatisfying to play at times... and any experienced gamer will tell you, the handling, responsiveness and general gameplay feel of the control scheme must be well polished for this kind of game to succeed. PC gamers will be insulted by the demand from the developer that a console peasant children's toy controller should be used, despite this being on PC.  Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for, and must never, under any circumstances dictate to gamers how their games are to be experienced.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"The Legend of Tianding" is overpriced at $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.Unfortunately Steam reviewers aren't presented with a "Maybe" option... if they did, that's what I'd choose.  This isn't a completely bad game, but it's also not one of the best.  As always, if you read my review and you can overlook the negatives I've called out, or they just aren't important to you, then by all means go ahead and buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of Pitfall but with vastly inferior gameplay. The story was decent and I enjoyed the boss fights. Last boss fight was the only challenging one for me. I died over 20 times there even though I am used to very hard games. It was still a fun fight nonetheless. The game offers story mode and hardcore mode, nothing in between. I played on hardcore. In general, the normal enemies and boss battles were easy except the last one. You can change the difficulty at any time. There are multiple endings to go after without enough information out there on how to get them. I just happened to stumble upon the requirements for the best ending on my own and I am glad that I did. Without giving any spoilers, you need to do 3 specific side quests that don't involve any grinding. You don't need to do all the side quests like some people said. I didn't grind the levels at all and was powerful enough at the end so that's a plus.Now why am I giving it a negative? Well, unfortunately, I personally found the game to be incredibly boring. I found myself trying to rush to get to the next boss because normal enemies and the stage design were quite lackluster. The combat felt very basic and underwhelming and it was very weird to have enemies use red moves that I can't evade. Normally those moves in every other game I have played (as far as I remember) can't be blocked, so it was very confusing and I never got used to it. The music and the art of the game are nice in general. I don't think this is a bad game, there are good things here, but I also don't think it's enough to call it a good game. TLDR : It's a decent game in general with fun boss battles. Final boss fight might be too tough for some players but you have the option to lower the difficulty if your vanity allows it. I found the normal enemies and stage design below avg and not fun at all so it's hard to recommend. I didn't hate the game though so feel free to give it a shot, you might like it more than I did. Final score : 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR 8//10 action adventure game that feels like a love letter to radio novels of folk heroes, buy it on sale if you're stingy, but really give this one a chanceI'll start by saying that I'm a huge Martial Arts fan, in almost all of its manifestations. So once I learnt this game was based off a Taiwanese folk hero, I had to play it.The world building is very interesting, with a chronicler being how you access past levels to scavenge for talismans. I seen some people complaining about the game play. It's an action game that exists around a Kung-Fu fighter, that means a lot of fights.The game gives you almost all of your power moves right at the beginning of your adventure and you'll need them to defeat your foes. Ever wanted to be able to execute an One Inch Punch? Well, you can in this game.There are a lot of cutscenes in this game that are a mix of the in-game models and a comic book style story telling. I wish there were a compilation of all those comic panels, they're pretty neat.Which brings us to the graphics, they are good for a game of this type, they have the 2.5D look and are very expressive. You can tell that there was some passion and dedication when making this game. It isn't just a mindless cash grab.If you have the money, buy it a full price, or wait for a sale and grab the soundtrack too. The OST is the typical songs you would expect from a Kung Fu movie or TV show of this variety, considering the story is split in different chapters, a radio novel even (play the game and you will understand). It isn't a very long game, but you might find yourself grinding for some collectables.There is a Boss Rush mode after you finish the main story that also allows you to just roam around the different areas of the game, though you only need to talk to the writer to access the actual levels and get the collectables.The bosses are pretty balanced in the normal difficulty. I didn't try the hard one and probably won't because there are too many games and too little time to keep replaying them all.I would like to see a speedrunner try and break this game, I bet there are a lot of exploits that can be pulled.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding was one of the biggest surprises I played in the last 5 years. This game has an incredible amount of spirit, the art is gorgeous, and the storytelling is truly unique (and the story is SO good!). The gameplay is so smooth it's a solid 10. Few games are as satisfying as this one when it comes to mechanics—I can probably mention Celeste.It is also an opportunity to learn a bit of history and get a glimpse into a fascinating historical period, complemented by a charming soundtrack and a charming hero.This is truly a hidden masterpiece that deserves far more recognition. If you haven't played it yet, you're missing out on a very enjoyable game that leaves a lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very charming game with a ton of style that I mostly enjoyed. The combat is relatively simplistic, but can have some depth if you really want to engage with it and get crazy. The story isn't anything that's going to tear your heart out or have you bust a gut over how funny it is, but the characters are charming and generally enjoyable lighthearted. It's quite a short game, 6 chapters that you could easily knock out in an afternoon. My total playtime says 8.5 hours, but I definitely had a few times where I was sitting in the menu while being distracted by other things so my total playtime is probably closer to 6 hours. My only two complaints with the game are that some of the side quests are frustratingly vague, which is made even more frustrating by the fact that since this game is so unknown, there aren't any good guides for 100%ing it online. For example, there's a side quest that tasks you with retrieving some wine for the quest giver from the sewers. You might think that this is from the lootable chests that you can find, but no! It's an item drop from a specific enemy (that funnily enough, can be found later after the sewers, so you could theoretically get this outside of the sewer area). There is no indication in the game that this is how you acquire the wine, and there's a few side quests like this. So unless you happen to luck into getting the item, good luck finding help online for it. The other minor complaint is that the ending of the game feels pretty abrupt. You fight the final boss and then within 2 minutes the game is over and I didn't love how it was resolved. Overall though, I think those are pretty minor complaints. If you just stick to the main story you won't have the issue with the side quests (or maybe you'll get lucky and get the items without realising that you've gotten them). The story/characters are incredibly charming and lighthearted, and for the most part this game is just a fun romp. I don't know how big the team was, but it feels like a game made by a small and loving team that just wanted to make something special. Definitely worth $20!

_childDocuments_.review: A solid sidescroller beat em up type game, gameplay is solid, secrets provide useful passive upgrades, and fun boss fights makes a good experience. Overall a great buy on sale for a solid 5-7 hour game with a couple extra hours for 100%. 8/10 on sale, 7/10 at listed price

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding does some wonderful things when it comes to a game experience. The presence of what is presumably chinese as the main language adds to its already beautifully drawn comic art. The 3d models reminded me of Metroid Dread to a small degree and the option to replay the chapters is very handy. The game does many things when it comes to collectibles: it a) provides a tracker for each level as well as accessories to aid your search later onb) pairs the collectibles together by theme (something I didnt realize until my last collectible which was a building)c) places indicators on enemies that still hold something of importance d) has an in-game list so you can see how far along you are as well as what numbers you are missing.The gameplay is fun and varied with a multitude of weapons to choose from and the story telling is very well done. I picked this game up at a steal of a price and was certainly not expecting to be as drawn in by it as I was. It is for sure one of my favorite games of this year. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Legend of Tianding is a pretty solid game, even for people like me who dislike platforming and boss fights. There is a lot of platforming. There are a bunch of boss  fights. As usual, both suck. But what makes this game great is the charming graphics and a setting which has never really been done before, as far as I know.Liao Tianding is a depicted as a lovable rogue, and it feels good to take down the corrupt police, help the townspeople, give money to the poor, and so on. There is only a little bit of voice acting, but what is there really sets the tone, fully Taiwanese vibes. The art is great, all the nods to 古早味 classic dishes make you hungry while you play, and the controls are responsive, if a little awkward on mouse and keyboard.If you like platformers, this is probably a no-brainer, but even if you don't, it's about a billion times more fun than the latest indie platformer about depression or a dead grandparent or something. Punch cop. Eat bun. Save Taiwan.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it. The BEAUTIFUL art style, music and own-language voiceover transported me to colonial-era Taiwan. The anime-style cast was entertaining to follow, and the story was good. Combat was challenging at first, but got trivially easy with upgrades, up until the boss fights, which are still a challenge, and a definite challenge on hard mode. The structure of the game makes for easy replaying of levels/chapters to get missed collectibles, which is great, and the side quests and side stories were there, though they mostly consisted of repeatedly visiting people or fetch quests. Even a minigame was present, but it was hard to play because the cards were in Chinese or Taiwanese. The combat was nice but the game did start feeling a bit repetitive just before it ended.Overall, a great game. Could have been an amazing game if not for a few little flaws. Easy 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece. This game tells the story of Liao Tian-Ding, a hero that did exist during the colonial era of Taiwan before it became an independant country. You'll have to fight the Japanese authorities that try to mess with Taiwan as the population is poor and considered as slave. For the gameplay you'll have a lot of references from fighting games, you'll even be able to juggle your opponents. The boss fights are interesting, they have patterns with cool animations. The music is incredible, the lore is good, you even have a collection of real items from back then that the game explains.This game is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging especially on hard difficulty, but a fun game that has satysfing combat mechanics and nostalgic platform that retro gamers will enjoy (with some newer elements). But we are not playing the game for those and most of the time I found those as an excuse to take a break.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay mechanics and boss fights were much better than I expected. The visual design and comic book style cutscenes were also great. Music and story accompany all of this very well. It has a playtime of 7-10 hours depending on your playing style. I would definitely buy if they make a sequel in the future.
