_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to those pathetic haters.This game is great in many aspects. The concept of this game is simple; you are a folk hero, stealing money from bad guys and giving it to those beggars and paupers (yes, the Robin Hood concept). Regarding the fighting system, even though it is satisfying, it's still a bit too easy when it comes to fighting those underlings and too stressful with bosses. Hence, it would be better if they could adjust this balance. The presentation in this game is pretty impressive. The stories have been presented in different ways, including dialogue provided by NPCs, voice-over narration, and comic panels. You might be under the impression that the incorporation of comic panels in this game simply involves a bunch of game screenshots, similar to what you've encountered in many other games, right? Well, that's not the case! In this game, every panel is hand-drawn, creating an experience that resembles reading a genuine comic book.Now, let's talk about the most important matter of this game. I've noticed some critics expressing dissatisfaction with extended dialogues. Personally, I appreciate the linguistic elements employed in both Chinese and English (I played with the English language for my second run). Therefore, I can confidently say that these dialogues are quite enjoyable. Nevertheless, if you prefer, you can certainly skip them since, as mentioned earlier, the stories will be conveyed through alternative means as well.This is the reason why I advise against paying attention to those "unfounded critics". For me, they seem to lack literary understanding, perhaps stemming from an inadequate education.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet game! The artwork and comic-style presantation is what drew me to the game at first. The story is good, nothing out of the ordinary, a typical robin-hood type of story with some nice writing and a charming characters. The controls are responsive and tight, while the gameplay is really fun with some anime-fight moments. Don't expect souls levels of difficulty but some sections and bosses can be challenging on the harder difficulty. I didn't expect the bosses to be that good! It's boss is better than it's predecessor and it feels like each own builds on the difficulty of the previous boss. Also the soundtrack has some real bangers! As far as content goes, there is a card mini game that I only played twice cause for me it wasn't explained and presented in a clear manner and collectables and side missions that aren't too grindy (I have 7 hours and I almost 100% the game other than a collectable that's not hard to get and a choice-based achievement). All in all it is a wonderful and short game that I think everyone should give a try!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from a Humble Bundle, and it wasn't even the game from that bundle that I particularly wanted. I opened for the first time because I was bored, not even knowing what type of game it is, and I was incredibly surprised to learn that it's one of the best platform beat-em-ups I've played in YEARS. That is, when the game decides it WANTS to be a beat-em up.What I like:- The art style is GORGEOUS- The dialogue and humor are surprisingly witty and interesting- The combat is SO satisfying and zippy- Challenging without (too much) unfairness- Lots of secrets for replayers to discoverWhat I don't like:- Almost everything in between the beat-em-up levels is a fetch quest- The overworld design is clunky, slow, and bloated- Distractions constantly pop up to slow your progression to the next section of beat-em-up gameplay- Boss fights can be a little bit BS at timesAll in all, I'd give it a 7.5/10, probably. If it were able to trim down the fetch quest/overworld content and keep the actually very compelling story intact, I would give this game as high as 8.5 or 9/10, especially considering its price tag. The gameplay is amazing when it doesn't hamper itself with the overworld/fetch quest elements that break up the actually intriguing sections.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fabulous! The Legend of Tianding sends you back in time to Taiwan and lets you explore and defend the streets through creative and agile beat-em-up style combat. In addition to hand-to-hand combat, you can steal enemy's weapons to use against them! The game tells a compelling story, with captivating comic-strip cutscenes, and introduces a wide and thrilling variety of enemies, quests, and hazards for you to navigate.This isn't usually the kind of game I play, but I enjoyed The Legend of Tianding tremendously. I highly recommend it to combat connoisseurs, aspiring vigilantes, and anyone who can appreciate a well-told story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: A very neat 2d sidescroller beat-em-up about the Taiwanese folk hero Liao Tianding. Pros:- clearly made with love: the story is illustrated in comic book style, and Taiwanese history is brought to life with a plethora of collectibles, each with a description.- a variety of enemies to fight- the weapon stealing mechanic is a nice touch, allowing you to temporarily use almost any enemy weapon- good mix of fighting, platforming and boss fights- boss fights are suitably challengingCons:- some collectibles randomly drop from enemies, requiring you to grind. This isn't fun.- quests are awkwardly managed, especially if you already have the required items.- you get interrupted by mandatory fights around the village when you're trying to get somewhere, which can be annoying- some of the moves in the boss fights aren't well telegraphed: a couple bosses have a move where they put up a shield and counterattack if you hit it. This shield comes out way too fast and you can be in the middle of a combo and hit it.Minor cons nevertheless, this is a little gem of a game and deserves a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game.Everything is well done, art and gameplay. Damn, the gameplay is very satisfying.Pacing is good because you are not ask to vacum clean, like, holly molly, like ALL OTHER GAMES, where devs think they are clever and please you by asking to pick up stuff every 10 seconds, pick 100 stuff get a... skin. ALERT, rush rush, but please read this book then listen to the podcast. Have a cutscene saying that you are in a rush rush alert! Make 2 steps, dialogue "hey we need to rush rush alert". So clever... did I mention it?Here, you beat up stuff and people, get money and spend it on upgrade. Done.And that gameplay :) so good.And did I mention the gameplay?
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun sidescroller action game. The combat system is pretty good as it offers a variety of combos. There are two difficulty modes, normal and hard. Hard mode is a perfect balance of enjoyment and challenge. Each boss is really unique and memorable. The final boss is hella difficult. Small glitch with one of the side quests [the wine one]. Still, game good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really loves platformers and history, this was a great find. It's a charming story with so many historical bits in it I actually learned a fair amount about Taiwanese history during the colonial period. Mechanics are sound, gameplay is solid. It's short, but worth it. Also, I played about as much on the in-game card game Four Colors that I bought physical cards so I could play with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding is an honest to goodness good platformer.It looks and sound great, the treasures you collect teach you a bit about Taiwan (while also boosting your capacities a bit everytime) and it controls great. There's a charm system like Hollow knight that allows you to b eover charmed a bit.Combat side, it pretty neat against regular enemies, though it does have makes fights with a lot of enemies really difficult to manage. Tianding is not a very tanky man, and as such you have to dodge enemies a lot. Well unless you grind to make him able to handle a lot more punishementStory side, I can't say much. I don't know how accurate it is to the real legend of Tianding, but I from I've been able to quickly search, the story is inspired by the real Liao Tianding. With a lot more fantasy to it. I'm pretty sure there he was never in a tale of a soul-eating swordAnd now, the biggest gripe I have with this game. The bosses. They are rage-inducing. Some are almost unplayable with how fast they attack and how large they attacks are.Then we have fights that are almost designed to be as hostile to the player as possbile.Overall, the bosses are really not this game's strong suit, not because they're weak, but because they are far too fast for the game.If you're not turned down the idea of really, really hard bosses, this game is for you. Its worth the 20$
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Good sidescrolling action game in an unused settings (early 20th century Taiwan). The game looks good in action, with a nice graphical style resembling a comic-book. After the first level, the game is pretty easy, but with somewhat hard boss fights on hardcore. The game loads fast, and I had no bugs, only one system crash when alt+tabbing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding is an excellent game where you can experience Taiwanese culture through this action platformer.I enjoyed the gameplay thoroughly where the action and the platformer aspects really create an immersive aspect regarding the velocity of the legendary thief.The story is quite good, especially the mix of Taiwanese folklore and history which shows a rich cultural background. This is done through the many collectibles that allow the player to understand some typical aspects of Taiwanese culture.The graphics and music are very nice and one can enjoy the designs that resemble Japanese manga but at the same time one can find other visual influences such as some western touches (although this might actually be Taiwanese but, alas, I am not that well acquainted with Taiwanese visual media)
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game for sure, albeit very short. It's a bit strange, it's like a metroidvania in the combat and character toolkit but presented as a linear game. It works, sometimes, although I sort of wish there were most exploring aspects and less running around in town. Overall its a short but sweet story about Taiwan and Japaneze colonizers there with big robin hood theming.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: 2-D action-adventure side scroll game. Medium difficulty. I am very impressed with the artwork and storytelling style of this game. Only a few 2D games based on Chinese/Taiwanese history. The character and artwork design remind me of the 80-90 cartoon era. Though the jump and hook-grappling control is a bit janky, the game went smoothly for an action game. It consists of 5-6 chapters which you can replay and collect all missing collectibles. The level designs aren't complex like other Metroidvania games but still have some secrets to scratch your itch. Boss fights were fun and relatively easy compared to other 2D games (I mean Ori or hollow nest level). You can also tone down the game difficulty all the time when you are feeling want to.Spending 10.5 hours to finish the best ending on the first try. Recommended for 2D side-scroll gamers who love old-style cartoons and want to experience an Asian robin hood story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Legend of Tianding is a game about finding booze in a sewer. It is also a fun sidescrolling action game, but finding the booze is the main thing. At least in my mind. 4/5Pros: + Looks like an old comic book in the best way possible. It is like you remember them looking like, but actually a lot better. + Has that charming sense of adventure in the vein of Indiana Jones and a cast of memorable characters. The plot is cliched, but in a warmly nostalgic way. + It has a lively city and a ton of collectibles that detail the history of Taiwan. And those collectibles also double as upgrades. + Levels and boss battles are mostly well designed. In other words, fun!Cons: - There is a lot of running back and forth around the city when you are outside of the main levels. Not too bad, but a little tedious, because there are not many side activities besides buying upgrades. And a few boring fetch quest side quests. - There are only 4 main stages. And the backgrounds of those stages look a bit generic. - Because there is a million upgrades, the game is unbalanced. The levels feel either too easy or there is a noticeable difficulty spike. - The combat is fun, but does not evolve much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding caught me completely off guard! It's a side scrolling platformer/beat em up with some very light metroidvania elements (emphasis on the very light). The boss fights were also fun and challenging. What I really enjoyed the most was the presentation and the aesthetic. Cut scenes and parts of the story play out like you're reading manga or a webtoon. All in all, not a long game but very enjoyable! Be sure to play on the harder difficulty to get the most out of the boss fights.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable side scrolling beat-em up with silght platforming segments where new abilities open up new paths similar to metroidvania.It has got cel-shaded artstyle aesthetic which is pleasant to look at and controls / animations are tight and responsiveAlso, the old manga like art style during cutscenes are well done.The boss fights are the most challenging sections and gives immense satisfaction when finally you get to defeat them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Interessting Action-Plattformer with some neat ideas. Liao Tianding isn't just a fictional character but historic persona. I enjoy going back in the time of early 20th century Taiwan/Taipei with all the cultural influences from China and Japan.The level design is quiet ok, I somehow enjoy this weapon stealing mechanic, which is mostly known by Beat-em-ups. The boss-designs are very good. But by far the best part of the game is the visual presentation. The Art work ist just nice. I also enjoy the quality of the translation (checked german and english), which isn't a given by many games from China or Taiwan.The one thing I didn't like was running around in the City, speaking with characters I don't really care for. Felt like a waste of time until watching the credits.It's by far not the best game ever, but a solid plattformer. Got it on lunar-new-year-sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game.- If you haven't played in a while and are looking for a big game, an experience, then this is not the game.- However, if you have just finished some heavy game/s and want to take a breather, explore something new, have fun, then I'd definite recommend this game.Overall, worth playing :)PS: Really cozy art style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing comic book style art. Gameplay is fluid and well designed, with boss battles that (on the harder difficulty) present a solid challenge. One thing I didn't like was how some of the talismans are RNG drops. That makes completing one of the achievements a matter of re-running the same section of a level where the enemy who has a chance to drop the collectible over and over. This was tedious and not fun. Also, another of the achievements is one half of a permanent choice. So you have to run back through 5/6ths of the game to get that one. The story is fun and shows off the difficulties of the imperial Japanese rule over Taiwan. I really liked how you became a kind of robin hood as you looted from the oppressors and gave back to the homeless and downtrodden. Really good concept. It does take really significant creative license with the actual history of the real Liao Tian Ding (廖添丁). The historical story is less flashy, but just as heartfelt. This is a great addition to the cannon of LTD lore which has been popular and growing in Taiwan since his death, betrayed by the brother of his lover.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game that has not already been said. Probably nothing lol.  The Chinese manga art style is beautiful! As an Anime fan I found the hand drawn visuals absolutely gorgeous! The jammin music is so good. Can we get an OST release? I would listen to this music on a day to day. The combat is fast fluid and satisfying. The fact I can bounce you in the air, steal your RPG, and kill you with in mid air in one smooth motion never stops being satisfying. The fact that they build the story with culture and issues reflecting the history of japan and china in real life is amazing and makes the game hit harder. The story can get dark, it has  depth, touching on  socioeconomic problems, racism and discrimination. And the fact it is based on real life, my interest was peaked and I decided to research  history of the issues between Taiwan, china , and Japan dating back to the 19th century. I am glad I did it because it made me appreciate the story that much more. Now a game that inspires you to become more worldly and knowledgeable, that is a good game. I wish I could  give a double thumbs up because it has quickly risen up there with my favorite games. I HIGHLY recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, the combat is super smooth, the story is simple but amazingly told and engaging. This game is a very solid experience and the only gripe I have with it is that while content wise it is fine, the game is rather short. If they had added maybe 2 or 3 levels more, even with just the same content, it would have left a more lasting impression. That being said, the boss fights are amazing, especially . After you finished the game you unlock the bus rush mode, but I didnt try that, not my cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Taiwanese Robin Hood fighting Japanese baddies full of jojo references and stuff.If you like sidescroller, action games with such exploring system that encourages you to revisit old maps and do them again for loot and to discover secrets, this game is for you!The further you are in the game the stronger you get and parcour in old levels becomes more and more easy so it's gradually faster experience and you feel stronger. Also there is no issue with secrets in this game, no need to google anything - if you complete your sidequests thoroughly eventually you will get amulet that detects not claimed secret chests. Game is really well thought with its combat and progression, your choices matter, there are multiple endings to the game. Also really easy to 100% achievments.What might be a headache for some people tho is chinese dub. If you generally don't like chinese language you might wanna skip this game.Cheers
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Very well crafted game. I can tell the developers really put their hearts into it from the main menu all the way to credits and it's hard to pick out flaws.The game is not long - I got all achievements in 9 hours, but it is a memorable experience and whether I play for half hour or 2 hours I always finish my session feeling entertained and never stressed.  Despite the hours sounding short, it feels adequate; like a wise woman once said, it's not the length, it's what you can do with it.The combat is fun and well-paced, and your skills are tested in boss fights, which are challenging and very learnable.The voice over is quite a treat, listen for yourself.  I don't understand most of the voice dialog but I find the authenticity endearing.Definitely recommend this gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really, really phenomenal game. Fantastic gameplay with plenty of fighting moves, and the gimmick that you can steal weapons from enemies and use them yourself. Staffs, batons, axes, pistols, rifles, grenades. Consistently fun and the animation is really smooth, reminded me of Mark of the Ninja. This deserves all of the praise.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding is a fun beat-em up with a comic book art style. Control Tianding in an attempt to save the village from the oppressive Japanese secret police. Along the way, learn ancient martial art techniques, save the girl and be remembered as a great hero.Pros - Easy controls - Childlike humor - Story is narrated like an episode of DBZ - Casual fighting game - Good and Bad endingCons - Short, maybe 2 - 3 hours of game play - Confusing side quests - No reason to replay after obtaining the good endingNitpicks - Skills should be obtained further apart from each other - Wish there were more contentI really did get a kick out of this game, but I'd say it's highly casual or intended for a younger audience. You definitely get an old school arcade vibe when playing through the missions. Obtaining items was confusing - ultimately replaying missions where they were supposed to be found or using your sash - but that doesn't distract too much from the main game.The story is OK. It does a decent job with it's twist, but leaves you wanting more. There isn't a cliff hanger. Regardless of whether or not you complete all the side missions, all the side character stories are tied up in the end. The way the story ends, it doesn't leave much in the way for a sequel or even DLC.I'd give this game a 7/10, a deal at $10 but a more appropriate price would probably be $15
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Scores: Excellent, Very Good, Good, Bad, Very Bad, Awful.- Performance: Excellent (Solid 60fps at 1080p. My system i5 11th gen, RTX 3060 mobile)- Art style: Excellent (Like 80s comic book)- Gameplay: Excellent ( Hack and slash, really challenging bosses)- Story: Good- Sound, Music, Voice: Very Good.The only weak point are the side missions. I think I only completed one, so I got very under leveled with the final boos, so it was a really hard challenge (I got the "bad" ending, which is harder)Totally recommended at a full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is a breath of fresh air that you don't see very often, so its a nice change of paceThe art style, music is really nice too, the way the story is delivered via manga-style cutscenes takes the story forward nicely, with a well rounded combat system.-The only negatives I can think of, its that the game isn't all that clear what you need to do to finish some side quests.The UI has some issues too, the "item get" prompt disappears too quickly sometimes, and doesn't clarify when you get an item that such is the one required for a specific side quest,  however in the map section, the green side quest icon at least shines to let you know you completed one, so its got that at least.-Overall, is a solid sidescrolling beat 'em up that you should totally get if the genre is of any interest to you.-
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: is a well-made action-platformer adventure game that shines in most aspects: the art is gorgeous and unique, the music is well-suited to the action (the boss fight themes are energising and enjoyable), and the combat system (beat-'em-up with weapon-stealing) is satisfying. The player gets a good range of movement abilities and can traverse the world with a good flow.In terms of game mechanics, I would say this game mainly borrowed from  and , but that's not a criticism! It took the excellent movement abilities from those games and repackaged them into an enjoyable new whole. The boss fights in particular are both fun and challenging; I found myself wishing these bosses were playable in some way. I think they would make excellent fighting game characters.My only complaints would be about some of the side quests being thinly veiled excuses to make the player revisit/grind old levels for collectibles (although the "relive a memory" system at least offers convenient exits mid-level), and the localisation. Really, the only thing holding this game back in any way is the translation: names are inconsistently transliterated, many utterances are awkwardly translated, and the prose is littered with errors. I can overlook most of these issues, but they did undercut the gravity of certain cutscenes.All told, I had a lot of fun with this game and I would recommend it to anyone who wants a straightforward, relatively on-the-rails story experience that gives them an excuse to brawl their way through 1900s Taiwan.Oh, and on a more personal note: it's been a few years since I've played a game released in English that featured spoken Hokkien (Taiwanese). If you're interested at all in learning about historical Taiwan, the collectibles in this game are a delightful series of historical artifacts from the time period, complete with short blurbs that explain their significance.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous pulp-comic brawler with a really fresh, clearly passionate setting and atmosphere.At its core, Tian-ding is a fairly straightforward 2D brawler with some hub-world meandering and side quests; not unlike Guacamelee! 2, but stripped even further of exploratory metroidvania aspects. Its combat is simple but solid, and while I lost interest in pursuing a lot of the side fetch quests they're innocent enough.Where this shines is the truly gorgeous visuals, with a 3D/2D blend and a color palette like rough paper, The Legend of Tian-ding really nails a look that some other games only attempt to capture. The in-engine stuff is awesome, as are the comic book interludes and character portraits. As good a cel-shaded effort as Viewtiful Joe, though this goes for something a little less loud.And while the visuals are enchanting, it's the world the team conjures that is ultimately what makes The Legend of Tian-ding really worth taking note of. I'm not particularly well-read in Taiwanese history, but the way the game is so squarely set in a very specific time and place in the country's history, amidst brutal Japanese occupation, is fascinating. The game uses its copious collectibles and upgrades as bits of culture from the time (who knew the Japanese brought Wrigley's chewing gum to Taiwan!) and really flesh out the period detail in ways that I don't often see in games. But really, how often is it that games are looking to real, obscure (to some) history for inspiration?Recommended, and can't wait to see what the team does next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet video game with good combat and platforming, as well as great visuals. You can 100% achievements and items ingame under 15 hours. Stealing weapons as well as having directional control over where the mook will get flung will let you have some super-satisfying combos.If you have a sidequest that has branching options I recommend reloading after selecting one branch to see the other branch as well. This saves you a playthrough to get the next achievment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: It's a all around good game, the levels and bosses have a nice variety in style and gameplay. It also trys to add new mechanics with each level, letting you learn and improve your ability throughout. I liked the story, it does feel like a folklore tale from China. If you like plataformers you will probably like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline and combat system is interesting. Players who know Taiwan history and Taiwanese Hokkien will probably loves the story. Maps and combats are not too difficult in easy mode. But the story is a bit short, and replayability is not good. Hopefully the developer could make DLCs, or if feasible, open for mod.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: A very immersive experience in the streets of colonial Taiwan, with immaculate artwork for both the storytelling and the fighting in the style of Hong Kong comics. There are gems to be discovered for both fans of beat'em up action platformer and fans of East Asia history. I especially enjoy all the rich historical details in the streetscape, the collectibles that upgrade Tianding's fighting skills (love any story about Morinaga milk caramels), and the trailing cries of pain following enemies that I have flung to the edge of the screen with a mighty punch. Definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, that brims with style and has a simple but fun combat system. It uses absolutely gorgeous comic-book style artwork in place of cutscenes. The 3d art used in actual gameplay is simpler but still really good looking.The gameplay is a mix of brawling and very light platforming. The combat system is simple, intuitive and satisfying. I quickly got into the flow of doing combos without really trying. And you can steal your opponent's weapons to mix it up. The game is not very hard for the most part, but the boss fights are challenging and took me several attempts.The English localisation is a little rough around the edges, but that never broke my immersion in the game.It's fairly short and can be completed in under ten hours, which makes it a good fit if you don't have too much time to commit.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding is a lovely, lovely game for history buffs and sociology enthusiasts everywhere. Much like the Yakuza series, the developers are dedicated to bringing the sights and atmosphere directly to the audience in a way that is engaging and immersive. The soundtrack is crazy good and has many creative metal and math rock influences. The game is not perfect, however, and I am a bit surprised that the game has an overwhelmingly positive rating.The combat and the plot may not resonate with everyone. The combat is fun and punchy, but it starts to get old by the end of the game as there are only a few moves to choose from. The plot may seem cheesy and Tianding may lack character development, but I invite new players to recognize that The Legend of Tianding is not a story about how Tianding becomes a hero. He is already a heroic outlaw - it's part of the premise. Just like many shonen graphic novels, the spectacle of the plot IS the story. The players is meant to be rooting for Tianding as he finds the odds stacked against him.If you're a history or sociology buff, just buy the game already. If you're not, it's still a fun game. Don't go in expecting this game to revolutionize beat em ups and just enjoy it for what it is: charming, immersive, and just plain fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: This is a side scrolling action game with educational content, similar to Valiant Hearts, but with more polished gameplay.  The visuals are stylized to look like comics from the beginning of 20th century. The graphics has nice sharply outlined and decently colored look and all characters are well animated. It is really a comics book in motion. This is supplemented by period asian music and occational chinese voice-over.  Control is smooth and both fighting and movement through levels feels good and fun. Abilities are unlocked as game progresses and finished levels can be revisited to find collectibles. There are multi-phase boss fights that are significantly more difficult than the rest of the game, but managable. I played on harder difficulty, but it can changed at any time. Only problem I had was occational lack of response when trying to heal.  The story covers adventure of local Taiwanese folk hero, a Robin Hood figure fighting against colonial oppressors, in this case Japanese and local moguls. The characters are archetypes, as befitting a folk tale. The educational value comes from showing tidbits of life at that period, aspecially through collectibles and their description. These also serve as permanent bonuses for main character and objectives of some of the side quests.  Wholly recommended, it stands as a game on its own, it has a great atmosphere and it educates a little as a bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: Talk about a rush of things! This game is definitely satisfying as far as beating up nasty people goes. The levels are creative and feature plenty of bring-back for side-quests. I suggest doing a lot of backtracking for cash as well, because there are plenty of things to do with it, like getting better equipment or being nice to the beggars in the game. But anyways, play for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10! It's a great game! The story and collectibles made me want to know more about Taiwanese history and folklore. Grinding for Yen/Sen in this game is easy once you're strong enough to beat powerful enemies even in Hardcore mode. Secret areas are also well-placed and not so obvious. Only problem I have with this game is that Stamina techniques aren't that useful late game aside from evasion purposes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful surprise ! I found this game randomly in my suggestion list, and oh boy what a gem ! From the story telling to the old school art, from the nervous, fast paced gameplay to the boss design, everything is perfect ! With the historical information as the cherry on top. What I thought was a small indie adventure game is actually a great platformer that has nothing to envy from its 'bigger brothers'.One of the best surprises this year !
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Tianding

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim because I liked the art-style and it instantly became one of my favorite sidescrolling fighting games.Starting with the presentation: The game is beautiful. In-game, characters and buildings are 3D models made to look like drawings. The enemies are all distinctive, and the bosses are particularly memorable and hilariously over-the-top. The animations are clear and smooth, making it very easy to read enemy attacks. The "cutscenes" in-between levels are masterfully drawn manhua scenes.The music gets your adrenaline pumping with a mixture of rock with traditional Taiwanese tunes. The trailers on the Steam page have a decent sample, so check them out.The story is pretty simple, but there were some interesting twists in there. The game explores some heavy themes from the Japanese colonial rule over Taiwan - from civilian massacres to sexual slavery - but overall it's quite lighthearted, with the main character cracking jokes and making fun of his opponents as he tricks them. The English translation seems a bit awkward and stiff, perhaps overly literal, but I quickly got used to it.Apart from the 10/10 presentation, the gameplay is where this title really shines: the combat is fast and smooth, and it's honestly hard to find a game to compare it to. After just a few minutes playing you already start to get a feel for the flow of the fights. The controls are super responsive, and despite the game recommending a controller I had no complaints using a keyboard.The most unique mechanic is the "sash". You use it to throw enemies around and to steal a variety of weapons from them. It's such a joy to use and in my opinion is the main feature that makes the combat so enjoyable. It's very easy to chain an air-dodge into a downward kick, punch a row of enemies into a trap, then kick the last enemy into the air to finish him with the weapon you stole from him... By the end of the game all of this becomes second nature, which brings me to the last point: the difficulty.After you get used to the combat, the regular enemies become very easy to beat. By the end I was just toying with them, trying to do the most ridiculous combos I could.  The bosses, however, always presented a huge (and to me, welcome) difficulty spike. Once you learn their patterns they become easy to beat aswell, but for me every boss took several tries. I would have liked for the regular levels to be a bit harder, perhaps a larger enemy variety could help.I highly recommend this game. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend if you enjoy platformers / beat'em ups / boss rushes.Weapon and combat system is very responsive and enjoyable with plenty of combos, dashes, dodges and parries. Some bland sections and fetch missions which don't take advantage of the game strengths and which happen mostly at the beginning of the game, where the characters are presented. Even then, the comic-style visuals are remarkable and really help convey the story which, by the way, can sometimes get politically spicy and feel like propaganda, even if it doesn't really make the game less enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Tianding is a hand drawn 2D side-scrolling platform/action game, you play as Liao Tianding, a legendary Taiwanese Folk Hero. Set in the early 1900s in Colonial Japanese Taiwan, this is the type of game that instantly grabs your attention. Let's take a quick look at the official story."Based on real events, real people and real situations, The Legend of Tianding is an exploration of a place and time often overlooked and presented in the style of Traditional Chinese Manga.Battle the colonial authorities in style with a tanto, waist sash, and fast paced Kung Fu in tightly tuned technical combat. Execute advanced aerial combos, steal weapons from your enemies, use your waist sash and grappling hook to fly around the battlefield, and strike fear into the hearts of your oppressors.Take on incredible bosses like deadly courtesans, greedy businessmen, and even military leaders, each one guaranteed to challenge you with their dynamic abilities and brutal attacks."You play in the Dadaocheng area of Taipei city, as mentioned earlier, everything is seemingly hand drawn, and although in general you play in a 2D manner, moving from cut scenes and menus, you do get a 3D view for a few moments, which is so well done. Everything is colourful and highly detailed.Although a platform game, fighting is a big part of the game, and you will quickly learn new styles and attacks as you play, as well as defensive techniques. You will explore underground as well as over ground, and even on moving trains, and not forgetting some pretty tough boss battles.The first boss fight you have is against Wang, now I have to come clean here, it took me a while to figure out how to beat him, as I clearly had not been paying attention, and didn't realise that when your health bar goes low, you can gain some health simply by pressing up on the d-pad. You will find save points throughout the game which also allows you to recover health, and store 3 health teas, or soups, not sure which, but you will take a sip of those in battle, and that will give you a health boost.Playing the game which is very much drawn in a "Retro Traditional Chinese Manga" style, at times it is like playing a comic book.Find talismans (talismen??) and upgrade your character, which in turn can also change your playstyle. The game does have a Robin Hood type element to it, steal from the rich, give to the poor, etc.The GoodThe graphics are outstanding, not enough can be said about that, just glorious to see. The gameplay is easy to pick up, the character easy to control, and you never feel overwhelmed as you learn new things. The BadThe text on screen you have to read through is a lot, conversations go on a bit, and sometimes you just want to actually play the game as opposed to reading a comic.OverallThis is a really good action platformer, looks and plays brilliantly. Some great characters to interact and fight with. A good learning curve, and detailed story to be a part of.I score The Legend of Tianding on PC (Steam) a solid 8/10Originally Published on

_childDocuments_.review: As a Taiwanese, I can’t recommend The Legend of Tianding enough.A 2D platformer beat’em up game, the platform stages & the combat system are the core aspect of the game. The combat system is responsive & flows very well, with a weapon-stealing mechanic that allows you to steal the weapon of virtually every normal enemy unit (tho the weapons are of limited use.) As you progress through the stage, you also learn special kung fu moves that complement your arsenal of skills. These special moves are not only useful in combat, but are often essential in traversing the platform stages as well, especially for the optional treasure part of the game. The grappling mechanic (using the same waist scarf you use to steal weapons) takes a bit of getting use to, but once perfected it is a lot of fun to play with as well.The bosses are all well-designed as well. Playing on the hard difficulty, I died maybe dozens of times to each boss before being able to beat them, yet the experience was challenging but fun. This speaks to the excellence of the combat system once more & the variety of moves the bosses have.Beside these two core aspects, the game is also simply stunning to look at. Set in Taipei at the start of the 20th century, the game depicts Taiwan in the Japanese colonial era with a Hong Kong comic-esque styling. This is most prominent during the cut scenes, & it works very well. The BGMs also features traditional Taiwanese instruments prominently, & the mix of such instruments with modern electric guitars is a treat to the ear.There are a lot of “collectables” in the game to well, collect, & these are usually items or artifacts from that era. A short description of the items is provided, so it’s a great way to learn about that era once again, but even ignoring this, these items confer small bonuses to the character, so function as a character growth system. I think this is an excellence way to implement optional item collections. The game has two endings, & the get one of them one needs to complete if not all the side quests, at least a few core ones. By the epilogue, one can see how finishing certain quests helped ensure this particular ending, & I really love how the game tied it all up together.While I absolutely adore the game, there are a few flaws to speak of.One is the grammar, which I think can be patched up rather easily. There was also a three-letter word used to describe the Japanese by a few on the characters in game… which really needs to be fixed.The side quests, especially the less important ones, are also simply fetch quests. It wasn’t that annoying to me, but it is something that many might find bothersome to do. This also ties to the city-traversing part of the game: while the city is gorgeous to look at, it isn’t very interactive, which is somewhat a shame. There’s a bit of exploration to do, & ofc there are the side quests & a weapon smith to upgrade the weapon, but not much more. I think there are potentials here. Two particular side quests feature a “bad” option & a “good” option to resolve them, & each option gives you an achievement. In my first play through, I went with the good option, since the bad option simply seems unproductive to me, & while those options resolved the problems for good, they locked me out of the achievements for the bad options, meaning I can only get those achievements by replaying the game until those respective point of the game! Funnily enough, if I had gone with the bad options first, I simply would have been able to go with the good options after the fact, as the bad options does not resolve the problem at hand, so in a sense the achievements punish players playing smartly the first time around. I think this achievement design choice is rather unfortunate.Beyond that, the last flaw of the game is that simply could be longer! To be honest the game is of the perfect length to me, but it feels like a waste of have such an excellent combat/platforming system not deployed for more content. Hopefully a sequel or a DLC is in the work!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lot of fun.  What primarily makes it so for me?  The story is not thrown in your face with a ton of exposition, which is a common mistake games make.  Don't show me a 10 minute cinema screen at the beginning of a game, _let me play the damn game_.  Now, that right there is a big plus, but the game itself?  It's smooth and has a lot of potential for entertaining combos.  Is it the most efficient to smack a guy a few times, kick him up in the air, yank him down with a scarf then one-inch punch his butt off a building side?  Heck no.  Is it fun?  Heck yes!The story line does not, as I have heard others say "make light" of Japanese occupation of these places at all.  What it does is show both the heroes and antagonists as (cartoon versions of) real people.  It awful that a woman is held as a courtesan against her will, but that doesn't mean she forgets how to laugh and care for others!  The human condition is to try and find the best in life even when all you have is oppression.  I like how this story reflects that.

_childDocuments_.review: The Taiwanese Robin Hood. Play as Liao Tianding (AKA. Liau Thiam-Ting), vigilante of Taipei city and wanted by the Colonial Japanese authorities. Rob the rich, feed the poor, and fight for justice in the streets of early 20th century Taipei as Taiwan’s legendary outlaw. Based on real events, real people and real situations, The Legend of Tianding is an exploration of a place and time often overlooked and presented in the style of Traditional Chinese Manga. Kung Fu Fighting. Battle the colonial authorities in style with a tanto, waist sash, and fast paced Kung Fu in tightly tuned technical combat. Execute advanced aerial combos, steal weapons from your enemies, use your waist sash and grappling hook to fly around the battlefield, and strike fear into the hearts of your oppressors. Take on incredible bosses like deadly courtesans, greedy businessmen, and even military leaders, each one guaranteed to challenge you with their dynamic abilities and brutal attacks. Explore the Dadaocheng area of Taipei city as it looked like in the early 1900s Run through colorful streets, ride on a speeding train, and make your escape through dark sewers, all done in the style of a retro Traditional Chinese Manga.

name: World of Tanks
detailed_description: Command over 600 machines from World War II through the mid-20th century and prove yourself against players from around the world. Dive into the ultimate action experience with epic PvP clashes, measured tactical decisions and thoughtful cooperation in your pursuit of victory! PICK YOUR TANK More than 600 tanks and military vehicles from history’s greatest tank-building nations are waiting for you! Choose from one of five vehicle types and familiarize yourself with their unique features and specialties. Find the perfect combination of vehicle and nation that fits your playstyle and be unstoppable! MASTER YOUR SKILLS Explore maps to find the best positions for your machine. Learn to aim for the opponents’ weak spots and to hide your own. Consider opposing vehicles and their tactical roles. Use it all to develop the best-fitting strategy to be the triumphant winner! PLAY ALONE OR TEAM UP Roll out and match up with random players or organize yourself a platoon and enjoy the exciting experience of playing with friends. Whichever you choose, have fun! UPGRADE AND CUSTOMIZE Unlock new modules, pick your equipment, and make vehicles truly yours with lots of customization options. Personalize your vehicles with historical camo, custom color schemes, emblems, and personal numbers. PLAY MULTIPLE GAME MODES Play on your own or join team clashes. Strive for fame and recognition and climb the leaderboards. Create your own clan and gather a company of playmates. Take part in special events and claim unique rewards. In World of Tanks, there's a mode for every playstyle and every player! 160 MILLION PEOPLE CAN’T BE WRONG Millions of players are having a blast in World of Tanks every day. _childDocuments_.review: The game is designed well, the graphic and models look good, there is a lot of content. You can have fun with the game.Sadly the "Free2Play" design is too poor, its not a fair f2p. As a new player you start with a lot of boni and time based premium account, you have players on the first Tiers with similar strength and you reach a good progress.After some time you see the strong imbalance significantly (pay to win or grind to death/with death):- You buy new tanks and if you dont have the crew bought by gold or huge amounts of credits, you have a weak crew (less effectiveness in battle! weaker!)- You buy new tanks and you need to research a lot, later on its very slow and without research you are too weak in your Tier level (armor, cannon)- Just buying very expensive ammuniton gives you more penetration with same damage (pay 2 win, as normal players cannot really affort this better ammunition altohugh its not based on premium currency - but in fact the price makes it premium)Based on that, matches on higher Tiers are pretty unfair for many matches (unless you pay against the disadvantages directly).My last kill criteria: You have a lot of bots in the game filling gaps, which is still fine. However, there are plenty of matches where three different Tiers come together. E.g. you start with your already artificially weakend Tier V tank and then some Tier VII tanks come around and finish you with one or a few hits. You in contrast often don't damage them really due to the penetration/armor differences.A real f2p game would enable players to buy skins or maybe progress faster by having more or higher Tier tanks in less play time. But here in WoT you have so many negative effects when you reach new Tiers and when you buy new tanks that its killing the fairness and fun in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Tanks? Yup, tanks. This game is full of 'em. Big ones, little ones, real historical ones that saw production, and ones that never even made it past blueprints. And no bombers overhead looking to ruin your day! But lets be honest here. Its a SUPER fun time if you are actually playing with a team of real people (even more so if you can get them all in a discord server). _childDocuments_.review: Lots of guys are saying this game is pay to win, which it is. This happened a long time ago so I can't exactly remember if I had gotten a free premium account (they used to give those out on special occasions) or if it was around the time they started letting people get gold rounds for silver. I have played this game for a few years, and I played during a time when there was only US, USSR, and Germany nations. I remember before they split the KV-2 and the Panzer 4 tanks. So I have much more play time then what is displayed on this review.So before I explain my experience I'm going to briefly explain what "gold rounds" are. Basically it is special ammo with more armor penetration capability. You can buy them with the special "bought" golden currency or with the earned silver. However buying with silver is unfeasible because the ammo is very expensive. In conjunction with repair and rearm costs.So, my experience is thus. Once when I had gotten access to golden rounds and I decided to try them out in a match. Now if you know anything about this game ammo racking, and setting tanks on fire are extremely rare, more so ammo racking, which means to basically one shot killing a tank by ammo detonation. I must have knocked out 5 or 7 tanks each with a single shot of golden ammo. I have never ammo racked a tank before this time or ever since because I never used gold rounds after that or before. I have set a couple of tanks on fire without golden rounds but I can count that on one hand. This is just one of many problems with the game. The matchmaking is flawed, there are many features and items that give the player direct advantage and while some of this is still accessed on free accounts the expense is so high that often times you will loose cash after every match forcing you to play the lower tiers, which is not very fun. There are also silly mechanics like the spotting system which can make a tank in an open field completely invisible, you will often get shot by invisible tanks from across the map. Also you need to spend gold to remove equipment off of your tank otherwise it gets destroyed.So overall don't play this or any free to play game. Most of them are scams that create problems which they make you pay for the solutions.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is very fun to play. But it has a few problems: - If you are a casual player, you will not have fun unless you like spending tons of money on premium ammo and premium tanks. It is everything but noob friendly.- If you are a more serious player, this game can be very fun. Especially light tanks don't rely heavily on premium stuff. But be prepared to have a grind harder than Warframe to get started. Again, it is not noob friendly.- Still, with decent skill, you will get penetrated by premium spammers, which can sometimes be countered with good angling, sometimes you are absolutely defenceless. The game can sometimes be very pay-to-win, but on lower tiers it is still somewhat acceptable.- The matchmaking is unbalanced as hell. There is no rank-based matchmaker for random queues, which would make the teams somewhat balanced. You also get matched across two tiers frequently, which turns the low tanks into water guns and the high tiers into killing machines. - Some tanks are absolutely OP while others are complete garbage. Read a guide for beginners if you don't want to grind a Ferdinand with a trash gun.- The RNG in this game makes it somewhat more arcady and less competitive. Imagine aiming at someone for 10 seconds straight and then missing them because RNG wasn't on your side. This is the game you will be playing.There are some good sides to this game as well: - The graphics are beautiful. Especially for a free game, everything looks polished.- The game has mod support. You can turn the game into whatever you want with tons of mods.- The gameplay can be very rewarding if you put enough effort into actually playing good. Easy to learn, hard to master. (Except when you pay cash, but that's for the weak)- The concept is overall fun.Concluding this review, you should either start out with a couple friends who know what they are doing and learn from them or seek a clan. Otherwise, be prepared for a rough time and a heavy grind. If you are willing to pay money, it doesn't matter. Just buy a Bourrasque / Defender / LP432 / EBR 75 FL 10 / leFH18B2 and destroy enemies. But then nobody in this game will like you.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Tanks is a massively popular online multiplayer game that puts you in command of a wide array of armored vehicles, from light scouts to heavy destroyers. With its blend of strategy, teamwork, and realistic tank combat, World of Tanks offers a unique experience for fans of military games. After spending time in its intense battles, here’s my take on what makes this game stand out:Gameplay: The core gameplay of World of Tanks revolves around tactical tank combat in large, team-based battles. Each match requires a mix of strategic thinking and skillful execution, as you navigate diverse maps, use terrain to your advantage, and cooperate with your team to outmaneuver opponents. The game’s extensive roster of tanks from different nations, each with its own strengths, weaknesses, and playstyles, adds a layer of depth that keeps the experience fresh and engaging. Whether you prefer the speed of light tanks, the firepower of heavies, or the versatility of mediums, there’s something for every type of player.Graphics and Sound: World of Tanks is visually impressive, featuring detailed tank models and varied, realistic environments. The game’s maps range from open fields and urban landscapes to rugged, mountainous terrain, each requiring different strategies to master. The attention to detail in the tanks, from the weathering of armor to the effects of damage, enhances the immersion. The sound design is equally robust, with the roar of engines, the clank of treads, and the thunderous boom of cannons creating an authentic battlefield atmosphere.Progression and Customization: One of the most appealing aspects of World of Tanks is its progression system. Players earn experience and currency through battles, which can be used to research and purchase new tanks, upgrade existing ones, and customize their loadouts. The tech trees for each nation offer a clear path for progression, allowing players to specialize in specific tank types or explore a variety of options. While the grind can be significant, especially at higher tiers, the sense of achievement in unlocking and mastering new tanks is rewarding.Community and Support: World of Tanks has a large, active community that’s central to the game’s longevity. The player base is generally welcoming, with plenty of resources available for newcomers to learn the ropes. The developers, Wargaming, regularly update the game with new content, balance adjustments, and seasonal events, keeping the experience fresh. While the game does include a free-to-play model with microtransactions, it’s generally well-balanced, though some players may find the grindier aspects tempting to bypass with premium purchases.Conclusion: World of Tanks is a well-crafted and deeply engaging multiplayer experience that offers a unique blend of strategic combat and historical authenticity. Whether you’re a fan of military history, enjoy strategic team-based gameplay, or simply love the idea of commanding powerful armored vehicles, World of Tanks has a lot to offer. Its detailed graphics, immersive sound, and robust progression system ensure that there’s always something new to achieve, making it a game worth investing time in.

_childDocuments_.review: Joe and Tom met at a World of Tanks fan club. They shared a passion for tank technology and had been playing the game for many years. However, what bonded them even more was their love for fitness and a healthy lifestyle. They often met at the gym, where Tom worked as a trainer.Joe and Tom had been in a relationship for several years and were very happy together. But lately, they had noticed that their life had become a bit boring. They knew each other too well, and it seemed like there was nothing left to surprise them.One day, they decided to take a short break from gaming and working out and go on vacation together. They chose a beautiful spot by the sea where they could relax and enjoy the scenery.On the second day of their vacation, they decided to take a walk around the town and stumbled upon a local museum. There, they learned about some interesting artifacts from World War II, including tanks. Joe and Tom were thrilled and decided to take a tour.At the end of the tour, they were given the opportunity to enter one of the tanks to experience what it was like inside. When they climbed into the tank, they felt a strong sense of excitement. Their fantasies began to work at full capacity.After the tour, they returned to their room and started talking about their feelings. It was uncomfortable for them to talk about it, but they realized they couldn't hide their desires from each other. And they decided to try having sex in a tank.The next day, they returned to the museum and asked for permission to have sex in the tank. But to their surprise, they were denied. So they decided to find another tank to have sex in. However, they found it difficult to find a suitable tank that would be available for this purpose.Therefore, they decided to use their imagination and create their own tank in the game World of Tanks. They spent several days creating the most realistic tank using various settings and modifications.And finally, they were able to have sex inside their virtual tank in the game. It was so exciting and thrilling that they decided to repeat this experiment several times. And every time they played World of Tanks, they remembered their unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, don't mistake my short play-time on Steam for being inexperienced with the game. Like many other reviewers here, I've logged a decent amount from the Wargaming launcher with over 8000 battles in over 4 years between my previous and current Wargaming accounts. It's not as much is some, but I'm no newb either. Second, I'll get out of the way that this game is playable, in that it functions as intended, and has extremely beautifully accurate tanks and environments. Now that's out of the way... I'm not going to get super in-depth over all the little nit-picky things that bother me about this game. Instead, I'm going to focus a few big items that ultimately make this one of the most frustrating games I've ever played. 1. Match Making - I have no idea the algorithm that manages the MM in this game but it is possibly the WORST MM of all time. I can literally go days of 8+ hours of gameplay without getting a top-tier battle once, meaning my tank isn't the highest tier in the battle. This means there are ALWAYS tanks that can kill you almost instantly if you encounter them because they are higher levels. With battles like this no matter how good you are, you can't contribute to the battle enough to swing anything in your team's favor if your top tier tanks suck more than the other team's top tier tanks. This results in literally entire days back-to-back where you might win 1 or 2 battles out of 20. The past couple days that I played I dealt with win rates like this. On top of that I only play when I'm platooned with my brother who's a very good player, yet he loses all the same battles I do solely because of the horrendous MM. It's absurd and probably one the most frustrating things in any game ever. I'd rather sandpaper my entire body than deal with crap like this on a regular basis!2. Wargaming Greed - While this game is technically free-to-play, WG definitely has learned from the best swindlers in the modern gaming industry over the years to take advantage of all the whales and manipulation tactics to get people spending money in-game. It's virtually impossible to do anything most rounds if you haven't spent real money because of gaming structure limitations, progression limitations, and distribution of in-game currency limitations. On top of all that, many long-term players that were grandfathered in before the more egregious pay-to-win stuff was implemented are constantly there with their uber tanks, crews and equipment to kill you non-stop. Progressing is excruciatingly slow these days, but you can pay to fix that! You might be able to buy special equipment upgrades with earned in-game silver, but you can't do it for every slot and every tank because of price. That is, unless you want to pay to fix that! Is your tank crew garbage? You can pay to fix that! Wargaming has become increasingly egregious when it comes to microtransactions since I started playing 5-6 years ago. It's been a slow creep, but they worked diligently to get them burrowed in there for you!! Great right!? When I started playing WoT I used to say they were the correct free-to-play model I wish others would emulate because it was possible to moderately progress without buying anything, and they didn't shove it in your face. I even bought stuff just to support them because you could have fun and progress honestly without it. However, now it's shoved down your throat every time you click a menu button. Pay for visuals, pay to win equipment, pay to win tanks, pay to progress with Premium, pay to upgrade your crew, etc. 3. Gameplay Imbalance - Let's say you're a wallet warrior and throw all your money at Wargaming (which is what they want), and you get everything you could ever want to buy. Well, it's still not going to help all that much because the best players are all rewarded with super premium, limited edition tanks through insanely long and excruciating special events, and these tanks are virtually unbeatable to any average player that can't play this game all day. Plus, there's another a massive imbalance on the battlefield with map-wide sniper artillery that can suck the fun out of playing any heavy tank. Additionally, they've recently added wheeled vehicles which are insanely over-powered. They are fast, have high pen guns, and cannot be immobilized like normal tanks by shooting the suspension system. The fact anyone at WG thought this was a good idea is mind-blowing to me in a TANK game. As I mentioned in the beginning of this review I'm on my second WG account, and that's because I became so fed up with the game I quit a couple years ago and deleted everything. I only recently reinstalled it and was quickly reminded by the lovely MM, RNG, and microtransactions why I gave the big middle finger to World of Tanks the last time, and now the game is SO much worse than it was before. So you might ask, why do I still have it installed at all and that's for one reason and only one reason... it's one of the only ways I can regularly hang out, visit and voice chat with my bro because it's the primary game he plays. If he didn't play I'd delete the game so fast that it would make the present US currency inflation rate look like it's at a stand-still. I can't and I won't recommend this game to anyone, especially if you're easily aggravated by stuff outside of your control. Save your precious time, and save your money while it still has some value. Final Score is 3 out of 10 cartridges.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games that feels great when you're winning, and terrible when you lose. Winning, you actually get to play the game and enjoy the combat dynamic it has to offer.Losing, you're effectively forced to sit back and watch a long and overdrawn battle between a bunch of dudes with tanks, or you can leave, but you still have to wait the full duration of whatever's left of that battle before actually getting to play again, which is a huge design oversight. Grinding technologies for each different tank is a hassle. The amount of experience you get is based on personal performance; if you do well (i.e. completing objectives, dealing damage and getting kills), you gain more experience which you can use to unlock better tanks. On the flip side, this means that if you don't perform well or you die early on in a match you basically get nothing in terms of experience, meaning you HAVE to use cheap gimmick tactics or extremely powerful meta tanks in order to actually have a competing chance against other players.A few tanks have some interesting gimmicks but their reliance on real world statistics makes it incredibly tedious to actually play a game with a tank that is just simply inferior to another one because of minute differences most casual players will not even bother looking for.This is a game made for people who are absolutely hardcore about these games, and everyone else is kinda just left aside.UPDATE: I keep receiving bonus free promotional buffs that are supposed to make the game less grindy. If this is the game's attempt at bringing me back or encouraging me to play more, it's kinda sad.

_childDocuments_.review: To those of you who don't like to read much, this game is fun. (And fair).I have played World of Tanks BLITZ for years, and after World of Tanks came to Steam, I decided to give it a try. (Partially because I wanted to see if those bad reviews were correct).So, if you've played WoT BLITZ, You will see that there is much in common between these two games. Many of the same mechanics are in place, there are tanks in both games and controls are almost the same. The main difference is that WoT add's a bit more "realism" to the recipe. Here's a quick list of the most obvious differences:-  More realistic and higher resolution graphics-  Larger maps-  Larger teams. You can have 15 vs. 15 matches-  Longer overall distances, so not as much of close range fighting-  Even thou the game still gives you the same information where to shoot, it is not as clear as in WoT BLITZ-  Matchmaking can have +2/-2 higher/lower tank tier. So if your playing tier 6 tank, you can end up in match with tier 7 and 8 tanks both at the same time.And that was list of most obvious things you will see when comparing WoT and WoT Blitz. In the eyes of a totally new player, WoT is more unforgiving than WoT BLITZ. If you are not familiar with the mechanics of the game, a lower tier tank can still destroy your tank even if your tank is +2 tiers higher. The main reason for this is most likely that both games hide much of the essential information to various places. Sometimes behind menus, sometimes to games own website. This can make the learning process frustrating, because you cant always tell why something happened like it did even if it worked before.Still I would recommend this game to anyone who has any interest to playing a tank game. Even with the learning curve this game has solid gameplay and rewards you well when you start learning how to play. The gameplay itself has been tested for many years now so it works like charm. Most of the bugs and glitches, (which are very few by the way), are mostly found in garage in form of translation errors, aforementioned glitches and some update related bugs.But the most important reason of all, this game is very _fair_. If you have the skills and know-how, you will do well in the game. There is talk about pay-to-win, but compared other games I have seen, it is almost non existent. Why I say almost is the reason of APCR-ammo. It's the "best" ammo you can have in the game. You can buy it with gold which you  can get with real money, yes. But even with money to keep you always stocked with this ammo, you cant cause much trouble if you don't know what to do with it. Besides, you can get that same ammo with ingame money and with or without gold, it's expensive. So your not likely going to use it in all of your matches.The talk about premium tanks being overpowered is also more or less exaggerated. Premium tanks are specialist tanks that are mostly used to speed up your game by lessening the grind. They may have different statistics than stock version, but that only changes the playstyle. Skill is still the main deciding factor in game. And you can eventually get everything in the game for free, it's just going to take more grind. Although that grind is mostly fun.In conclusion, I have had fun most of the times when playing this game. It has had long time to cut out the edges and thus works like a well oiled machine. So if you have even a slight interest in it, I recommend you to try it. It's free after all. (Atleast if you don't get hooked).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite fun once you get the hang of it... which you'll only do after 10k battles more or less.Some might consider this game pay to win but not entirely. I'd say it's pay to progress faster. There might be some things that can give you an edge in battle such as using bond equipment but bonds can only be earned by playing.I'd like to clarify the "pay to progress faster" more since people tend to think that aspect of the game to be unfair.See, the game has three types of currency: silver credits, gold, and bonds.Silver credits is the most basic of all currency. You use them for almost everything such as buying new vehicles, equipment, consumables, etc. You earn them after battles, completing missions/events, and sometimes through gifts Wargaming gives from time to time. You earn more silver credits in battles when you do more damage, more spotting/spotting damage, doing critical hits, blocking more damage, and receiving medals.Gold is the thing people affiliate with the p2w aspect.See, gold can buy you garage slots, buy premium tanks (tanks which can earn more credits, gain more experience, and train crews faster, and can sometimes be more powerful than the regular tanks), but most importantly is buying premium account/time. See, normal accounts don't earn as much credits and experience as premium accounts do. In higher tiers such as tier 5 and up (or sometimes as early as tier 2/3/4) there will be some enemies you can't penetrate their armor unless you load "gold" ammo. Gold ammo is just like regular ammo but costs much more to fire. They're usually described as ammo with higher penetration but with lower alpha damage. But damage doesn't matter much if you can't even penetrate a tank's armor. Gold ammo is usually APCR but it can sometimes be HESH rounds, depending on the gun of the tank. Mind you, gold ammo doesn't mean you're actually using gold to fire 1 shot (it did though in the past which is why it's called that way). For the average player, gold ammo is super expensive. If you're using a tank with super weak pen on its regular ammo, you will be forced to fire gold ammo just to be able to pen the enemy. By the time the post-battle results have shown up, your profit may well be in the negative (no joke). This is why tiers 8-10 (especially 10) can be super expensive and only those with a premium account can offset the high cost of using such ammo. This is why those with premium account may appear to be having a huge advantage over regular players since they can afford gold ammo.But most people tend to overlook the other side, you don't need to load 50 gold ammo on your gun (depending on the tier and gun of the tank) every battle and shoot that exclusively. If you can do good damage every single game, chances are you'd still make some profit albeit slower than with a premium account.Bonds are special currency that can be reliably earned by playing in tier 10 tanks. Bonds can buy special equipment which can boost your tank's performance even more sometimes even turning a bad tank into a decent one.With that out of the way, let me list the pros and cons of the game.Pros:~Rewards skillful plays (you don't know how much happiness you'd feel when you pull a one last stand against the remaining enemy teams)~Nice graphics. The game REALLY looks beautiful.~Nice sound design~Very addictive (I think it's a pro, at least for me)~Plenty of tanks to choose from WW1 to even some post-WW2 tank designs~Tanks that only existed in blueprints are brought to lifeCons:~Horrible new player experience (at least from my time (2018). I believe they've improved this aspect a lot but there's more work to be done in this department)~Requires patience (if you're the type who likes fast-paced shooters, this game might not be for you)~Requires thousands of battles to at least become decent~Requires tons of resources and guides to read/watch in order to learn~Some tech tree grinds are just horrible~Has RNG in some aspect (such as high rolling or low rolling in damage, penetration, and more)~Powercreep is super strong ~Sometimes takes years to buff some tanks/tank linesBonusNeutral:~Artillery can be a deal breaker for some~Premium time and premium tanks

_childDocuments_.review: The game fun for sure but, its going to be a challenge in the beginning for new players with no prior experience and you'll have to grind A LOT, but as soon as you start learning map positions/enemy tank weak spots, any advantage experienced players had over you balances itself out. Most OP tanks are not for sale but are rewards given from events and battle modes. People think that money gets them OP tanks or its going to fix their win rate etc., when in fact it only propels you further onto higher broken tiers where if you're a new player, most likely you'll not be prepared and lose a lot. Patience and perseverance is key. The only situation where money is an advantage, is for premium days and premium tanks, it won't make you win more, but it'll make your grind easier/faster, and still let me remind you the game has lots of missions, events, and rewards that gives premium time, personal reserves(items to boost your grind), consumables, and sometimes reward/premium tanks. Twitch and Prime gaming for example, the former gives lots of missions and rewards for watching, the latter gives you monthly Items and/or tank rentals that not only are very useful, but allow you to test premium tanks prior to spending real money, that so you don't have buyers remorse if you decided to spend money to buy a tank and didn't like it later. Happy Tanking.TIPS: Focus on learning map positions/tank weakspots.DON'T WASTE CREDITS they're to a certain extent more important than gold.Grinding is hard, so be smart and do research before grinding a tank line to see if its really worth it. YOU WILL SUFFER the consequences if you don't and start wasting your precious credits.Always try to do your daily missions.Take advantage of Twitch missions/rewards (and Prime if you have it)NEVER spend real money to buy a tank, without doing a prior research on how it plays and if it fits your playstyle.Always take advantage of any premium time you have, try to focus on completing any event/mission that reward you with more prem time, and remember that prem time gives you 3 extra daily missions.Rentals are premium tanks, they reward more exp/credits, so take advantage of any and don't sell them, because even though you can't use it after rental time expires, you'll have it in the garage and are useful as extra barracks.Crew training is one of, if not the hardest grind. If new or free-to play player, focus on one crew per tank type, per nation, eg. 1 crew for american heavy tanks, 1 crew for American medium tanks, etc., you can have more later but this will help you by making tanks better/stronger because of having a crew trained with more skills and not having to train a different crew for each tank.Hope this helps new players understand how the game works.
