_childDocuments_.review: I realize my initial review, while harsh, may some good points. So, to avoid my disappoints... DON'T DO WHAT I DID!! Been playing World of Warships for years, and I made the mistake of expecting "WoT" to be a similar experience. the two could not be more different. The biggest difference is that World of Warships is a bit more traditional and/or old-fashioned in its game design. WoWs wants you to learn to play the game by just...playing the game. If you lose your ship in mission, there's no real consequences that hinder gameplay. So, for me that gives more reason to charge in, rack up hours of experience, and level up. The grind is actually FUN, in WoWs, but I realize that's NOT for everyone.WoT (World of Tanks) actually requires that you read every announcement, news, and watch streamers. It seemed really strange to me just how much the game depends on you being fully "plugged in" to the culture and fanbase to really be successful. Maybe it is a matter of taste, BUT I do not see it as a strength to require players to learn how to play your game, by relying on external sources. With that being said, this game does have some going for it, and IS VERY MUCH Worth Your Time.PROs (that are not obvious, and take time to appreciate)- Your Decisions REALLY Matter, it is rare that I play a game where your equipment loadout and gear setup have such a HUGE impact on gameplay. Really getting to know all the modification possibilities for each tank has been truly rewarding. Honestly, it's comparable to early Mass Effect and Final Fantasy, which I LOVE- Variety of Map Design and Terrain is some of the best I have ever scene in any War Game. With all the Call of Duty (FPS) clones that seem to rely on the same strategy of "build the map on a circular loop", WoT is a much needed breath of fresh air. Some Maps I really enjoyed the challenge of finding the best positions to engage different enemy types. The BEST PART is that your most advantageous position depends entirely on what tank you are in. So, there are HOURS of replay value to keep the gameplay exciting as your improve your garage.CONS (issues I still feel strongly hinder the experience from being the very best)- the costs and penalties of running matches are INSANE!! Never have I played a game that actively makes me want to stop playing. After you hit your daily missions and objectives, every match ends up costing more resources than you can win back. No matter how much fun I am having OR if I'm suffering through a losing streak, the game reaches a point when you have to stop; throwing away resources for nothing is a bad strategy, so the game punishes you for playing??? Which leads into the NEXT problem...- World of Tanks is not at all clear on what it wants players to "DO". I LOVE the DDay Event, and everything they're doing for it. It is what made me decide to stick with this game, when I was getting pretty close to fed-up. Between watching streamers, following YouTube/twitch feeds, researching tanks, grinding matches, enjoying PvE, and then dedicating resources towards either upgrading existing tanks or building new ones... what IS the intended path for players??? Yes, it's a Free to Play game, so that does justify a slightly more challenging learning curve. You want to capitalize on cultivating a culture, so there is added incentive to purchase in-game currencies and renew subscriptions.THERE IS STILL HOPE!!! I can forgive the cons, because Warging did put out a series of surveys seeking input from players about the latest DDay Event. I shared my honest thoughts, praising ALL the aspects that are dedicated towards historical accuracy and having Battle Pass rewards that reflect that level of detail! There is A LOT to love about this game, and I hope the developers address some of these issues. Please & Thank YOU

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, This will be my review of the game World of Tanks by the developer and publisher Wargaming.First thing first, my steam playtime is low, but don't be fooled by that as i have been with the game since 2014. I am not a native English speaker, there will be grammar mistakes on the review ahead.With that out of the way, i will first talk about the claims that Wargaming made on their steam trailer video. only the claims that i have something to say will be listed here.1. , this is mostly incorrect or misleading. while the tank visual models are fairly accurate and realistic, this changes dramatically once we look at the armor model of tanks, this is most likely noticeable on tanks which has a obvious weakspot in the visual model but does not exists in the armor model itself, for example, lets take the M4A3E8 (M4A3(76)W HVSS) which has a weakspot in the front machine gun port. in this game that weakspot does not exists.  2. , yes this game does feature a lot of maps, however in my own opinion these maps are not well designed and shows very corridor like passages which forces people to be specific in their gameplay, ofc map designs are a developer's way of making players play a specific way but i wish that we had more freedom than to be forced in to these situations.  3. , OK so this will be a lil bit controversial as the developers has no way of foreseeing what a player will do in a game. Aside from the obvious that a winning team will get better rewards, players are heavily incentivized for their per-player performance. this lead into a conflict of interest among a team which can ultimately lead to losing a game. eg, some players may prefer camp instead of engaging in an assault.   Ok, now that's over. What do i as a veteran of the game has to say?1. . this exists in the game as a form of "Premium Tanks" which are almost always better than the "Tech Tree Tank" (Free tanks) variants. on top of performing better than the free counterparts, the premium tanks also generates more rewards per match. Premium Tanks used to be weaker than the tech tree counterparts but still made more money, however that was years ago. with this point as well, you will see the usual powercreep that the older premium tanks experience vs the newer premium tanks. 2. . OK so this is normal part of the personal progression of players right? in the game you can upgrade your tanks to perform better, but at the cost of being unable to select the other upgrades (ie. downsides like slower reload times). however in the game there are Premium Ammo, some players may call them gold rounds as they are used to be obtainable for gold only. these ammo are much more expensive than your standard ammo, but they perform better. with how i explained earlier that premium tanks generate more currency, this in turn makes the premium ammo somewhat a pay to win item as the player with the premium tank will be able to afford more rounds than your normal non paying player. what more is that these rounds offer higher penetration values to your tank which means that tank armor is rendered moot when people can just use these rounds. so yeah your heavy tank which is supposed to be able to face weaker guns are now penetrable by the use of these premium rounds.3. , the in game vision system is absolutely wonky and certainly needs a revisit. vision range is maxed at 445m, vision range that surpasses this cap will instead make the enemy tank's camouflage less effective, the opposite is also true that you can stack your own camouflage and be literally unseen to the enemy even when fully exposed. i just think that the current vision system is pretty bad and should at least be reasonable. There are a lot of negatives to talk about the game, these are the things that are on top of my head while typing this review.Overall, save yourself the time and trouble and play another game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Publisher(s): Deep Silver, Koch Media, IGS and Microsoft Studios.Developer(s): WargamingRelease Date: August 12th (International Youth Day), 2010 (14 years ago).Genre(s): Vehicular combat, massively multiplayer onlineCountry of Origin: BelarusPlatform(s): PC, Apple Macintosh and Microsoft Xbox 360.Moby ID: 52092"Rated T for Teen (Ages 13+): Mild Violence" (Parents need to know that World of Tanks is a downloadable free-to-play online historical (mid-20th-century) armored-tank combat-warfare game where players join with friends and strangers to challenge other teams in arena-based combat. The goal is to destroy the other team or capture control points on the map. Though World of Tanks is free to play, it has an online store that sells premium items and gives incentives to purchase premium time. Communication among teammates is a large part of the strategic planning, so the potential for unmoderated language is quite high. Though the game is violent, there's no blood or gore shown; instead, tanks are immobilized, catch fire, and explode in combat.)World of Tanks is an online-only multiplayer game in which two teams with up to 15 tanks each try to win the match - this is done by either killing everyone from the other team or by conquering the enemy base. The game is officially based in World War II but this has no big bearing: some of the available tanks were made after the war and there is also no separation of nations; German and US tanks can fight side by side. Each tank has different advantages, for example artillery has a big range but slow reload times, and a damage simulation: certain parts of the tank get destroyed when damaged enough. They respawn after a short time, but the performance takes a hit. But nevertheless, World of Tanks is no simulation and is designed for fast matches of ten minutes or less.If the whole tank dies during a match it doesn't respawn and gets locked for the rest of the match - this means the player has to watch the remaining time or uses one of his other tanks to jump right into the next. The game knows two resources which are gained with every match: experience to unlock new tanks and upgrades, and money to but them. This is were the business model comes into play: World of Tanks is free to play, but experience and money progression is relatively slow. But real money can be traded for game money and experience/money boosts which improve the profit per match.Directed by: Slava Makarov

_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating game mechanics such as player controlled artillery clicking on you from across the map without direct line of sight, invisible tanks shooting at you from jokingly short distances and remaining completely invisible (no smoke or anything after firing), heavy RNG in every move you make (penetration, damage, accuracy - zero consistency), light vehicles handle like toy cars doing 90 degree turns while going 90 km/h. Most of the tanks are fake, made up, and the few that are real have unhistorical parts that they never used IRL so you are always driving some frankenstein of a vehicle. New players are at a massive disadvantage due to untrained crews that take an insane ammount of time to train, some of the crew skills are a massive game changer and are a must have, game is unplayable without them (6th sense, BIA, repairs to name a few). Grind is also frustrating: when you unlock a new vehicle you will have a poorly trained crew and crappy modules like weapons with low penetration, accuracy and damage, turrents with poor armor and engines with low power so you will have to SUFFER untill the vehicle is in a playable state. Matchmaking is also crap, a lot of the times you will get uptiered +2 tiers where vehicles have more armor, HP, damage and will simply farm you.Heavy pay 2 win elements with various premium ammo and consumables that you won't be able to afford reliably without a premium account. More and more monetization: buy premium, buy premium battle pass, buy world of tanks plus service etc... After reaching higher tiers you will need at least a premium account (preferably premium vehicles too to get that extra silver boost) as you will start losing money due to high repair and ammo costs.And the biggest issue of all: overpowered premium vehicles that never get fixed as "people paid real money for it", at most they will do is remove it from the cash shop so nobody can buy it anymore (but can still play it if they bought it before) and later add it back on some sale with a spicy price tag on top for a limited time only to milk the game even more. And then next patch they will introduce a new even more overpowered premium tank than before so you have to buy that too if you want to stay relevant, tech tree vehicles get ignored most of the time. If they do some massive overhaul (nerf) to the whole class like artillery or tank destroyers for example they will not touch premium vehicles that class so anybody who has a premium vehicle will have a massive advantage against tech tree vehicles of the same class, but they will continue selling said premium vehicles with a massive price tag when you really want to pay 2 win.Bonus fact: you can't link your steam account to your old WG account AND you can not switch accounts on a steam client.  Don't bother with this game please. It lost any relevancy it had when War Thunder came out. If you want to play a tank game than play that one as it's much better although it has it's issues too...

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Review:World of Tanks, developed by Wargaming, is a free-to-play online multiplayer tank warfare game that has successfully captured the hearts of tank enthusiasts and gamers alike. With its vast selection of historically accurate tanks, intense battles, and strategic gameplay, World of Tanks offers a thrilling and immersive armored warfare experience.Pros:Extensive Tank Roster: World of Tanks boasts an impressive collection of tanks from various nations, spanning different eras of tank warfare. Players have the opportunity to command and customize a wide range of armored vehicles, each with its own strengths and weaknesses, providing a diverse and dynamic gameplay experience.Strategic Gameplay: The game emphasizes tactical decision-making and teamwork. Players must consider terrain, positioning, and tank types to outmaneuver and defeat opponents. The depth of strategy and the need for coordination make battles engaging and rewarding.Constant Updates: Wargaming actively supports World of Tanks with regular updates, introducing new tanks, maps, events, and game modes. This dedication to ongoing development keeps the game fresh and ensures that there is always something new to explore.Player Progression: World of Tanks features a rewarding progression system that allows players to unlock new tanks, modules, and equipment as they gain experience and climb through the tech trees. This sense of progression and accomplishment keeps players invested in the game.Cons:Steep Learning Curve: World of Tanks has a steep learning curve, especially for newcomers to the tank warfare genre. Understanding tank strengths, weak points, and effective tactics can take time and practice.Grind and Monetization: While the game is free-to-play, it relies on a freemium model, offering premium tanks, consumables, and cosmetics for purchase. Some players may find the grind to unlock higher-tier tanks without spending money to be time-consuming.Matchmaking Imbalance: Occasionally, players may encounter matches with unbalanced teams, resulting in one-sided battles. This can lead to frustration, especially when facing higher-tier tanks with more experienced players.Conclusion:World of Tanks provides an authentic and engaging tank warfare experience, allowing players to command a diverse array of historically accurate tanks in intense battles. The game's strategic gameplay, constant updates, and rewarding progression system make it a compelling choice for tank enthusiasts and fans of tactical online multiplayer games.However, the game's learning curve and monetization might be challenging for some players, and occasional matchmaking imbalances can lead to frustrating experiences. Despite these drawbacks, World of Tanks remains a strong and enjoyable free-to-play title that delivers on its promise of armored warfare action. If you're passionate about tanks and crave strategic battles, World of Tanks is definitely worth trying out on Steam.I hope this review is helpful!

_childDocuments_.review: I installed this just to write this review.I've played this game since it was in beta using the standalone launcher and it has been an interesting ride. I played it a lot more during the first years after release, and after that I have revisited the game occasionally for events or when I just wanted to check in and see what was happening in the game. I have played solo and in platoon with friends. I've participated in end game features such as clan battles and played in two tournaments. I figured that with my perspective of the game and its history I can give you a thorough breakdown of what the game is, and isn't.Most importantly I should point out that this is an arcade action game. It's not a simulator, and has never aspired to be one. It has historical tanks alongside prototypes that never left the drawing board. The tanks are very varied and caters to several different play styles. The mechanics are designed for you to be able to get in a game fast and finish it within a reasonable time. The game has a fairly steady pace, but rushing in often just gets you killed fast and is of little use to your team. Patience and following the flow of battle pays off so keep your head on a pivot and stay aware of what is happening on the map. If you get tunnel vision you can easily get flanked and killed.This game is free to play, but to a certain extent. I usually say it's easy to play for free up to and including tier 5 tanks. After that it becomes more difficult and expensive by the tier to make progress and maintain your tanks. And tier 1 through 5 are fun to play, make no mistake. A lot of top players in the game still play the lower tiers as well. However end game is all about the top tier tanks. There are a few ways to get around this and play even the highest tier tanks:The least obtainable is that you acquire an ungodly amount of skill at the game so that you're gaining more than you lose from your battles over time (cost of repairs and resupplying ammo for your tanks).The second is to pay for a premium account, which will net you xp and credit bonuses as well as daily xp boosters helping you progress faster and make enough credits to afford paying the more expensive upkeep for the higher tier tanks. Fortunately Wargaming sometimes give out a couple of premium days for free so do check out that news letter so you don't miss out. The third way is to get one or more premium tanks and use them to grind the credits needed to play your higher tier tanks. Premium tanks are designed to be slightly underpowered compared to a fully upgraded regular tank of the same tier, but they cost a lot less to repair and resupply and also earn more credits per battle meaning you have to be really bad at playing them to not gain credits. Premium tanks as you can deduce from the name cost real money to buy, but fret not. Wargaming often give out lower tier premiums as part of events and similar, so if you play regularly you should definitely be able to get a few, if you want to use this approach.You'll hear people talk about premium ammo. The premium ammo used to be nicknamed "gold ammo" because it was exclusively available for purchase with real money. That is no longer the case. You can buy it with credits earned in game now and albeit insanely expensive there is nothing saying you have to load all premium ammo. I usually load regular ammo and just add a few premium shells to switch to if I encounter an enemy tank that I am having a hard time penetrating the armour of. It keeps my costs down.All in all you can absolutely have a lot of fun in this game completely free.However if you want to play end game and go up against the top players in tournaments, or join a clan and play against other clans you will be expected to have a number of kitted top tier tanks, in which case it will be hard to not pay for the game.In closing I'd like to address a few misunderstandings that float around. For example some people seem to think the game is pay to win. This is not true since you can indeed buy everything with credits that you earn from grinding. It is as I stated before however hard to play end game without shelling out (pun intended). Unless you have godlike skill.You will also hear players complaining about the matchmaker. This is something that people have complained about since the early days, back when it was sometimes an actual problem and you would be matched against three or four tiers higher tanks. Those days are however gone and the biggest difference you see today is two tiers difference. Within that span you stand a pretty good chance to still help the team. Will situations arise where you can't penetrate the armour of an enemy tank? Absolutely. Are you meant to always be able to solo every tank in the game? Of course not. Work with your team, and find a way to deal with that heavy armoured bully that you can't handle on your own.My conclusion is that you can definitely play this game enough for free to form your own opinion. Then you can comfortably choose if you want to pay or not.See you on the battlefield.

_childDocuments_.review: First: I want to like this game, but I cant recommend it AT ALL. Why?1. You can't use your existing WoT-Account. If can not choose your own Account like you can in the launcher.     Which means I cant use my acc with ~30k games.2. Its UNFAIR and PAY TO WIN: As a newbie the game won't tell you **** what (not) to do. Furthermore, certain tank lines are quite unfair in the lower tiers. You will get frustrated quite fast. on top of that there are Tanks like the the infamous "Defender", the "Object 279(e)" or the "T95/FV4201 'Chieftain'", that you'll probably not get anytime soon. Or at all for that matter. And those Tanks are VERY powerful. That are just the most obvious examples most players can agree on. But as a matter of fact: basically any tier of tanks has more or less "powerful" premium tanks that are better than their f2p counterparts (iS-3 vs. IS-3A or Defender; P.44 Panthera vs. Progetto 46; T-44 vs T-44-100; Pz. 4H vs Pz. 4/5, just to name a few). The game is not very realistic either: If you were to be playing a Tiger 1 you are more likely to face an east-german T-55A (MBT) than a T-34 or an M4 Sherman, making them not as powerful as they should be. And Im not even starting with things like Arty (I dont have the biggest problem with them but many do) or the french cars (Wheeled scout tanks that are VERY fast and have whells that can absorb 170MM HEAT-Shells).....3. Most, if not ALL postive Reviews are biased - Why? Those players have spend a considerable amount of money - more than a few hundred $ probably, otherwise you cant get any tigh-tier tanks in a timely manner. As a result, these reviewers can throw (real) money around basically without a limit. As a "normal" player however: the higher tiers are expensive - not just the tanks or the equipment - the repair costs and the credits for ammo are as well.4. This is not directly gameplay related, but WarGaming (the Publisher) is a belarusian company. Just keep this in mind if you are considering spendig any time on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was dragged into this game by a friend. The combat feels a little janky and inconsistent at times, even without the inherit RNG tied into the game. The tanks feel fairly well balanced, but matches are harder to give a definitive opinion on. On one hand, it's nice that matches will try to balance the same number of each type of tank on both teams, including by tier. Player skill level seems to be decently balanced as well, from what I've personally experienced. Opposed to at that, however, is having matches where there are tanks up to two tiers apart (by my experience so far) facing each other seems unfair. I have yet to see anything that suggests a tier 4 tank could ever defeat a tier 6 tank. I suppose that goes both ways, but as a lower tier tank, there's nothing you can do (aside from getting extremely lucky, I guess) other than trying to avoid the higher tier tanks during the match. From an enjoyment standpoint, knowing there are players you have to run and hide from or else face guarantied destruction because you have virtually no way to fight back really negatively impacts your enjoyment. Factor that knowledge in with the fact that this game is not only very grind-intensive, but that progression seems to be strongly influenced by your personal performance in matches versus whether or not your team actually wins really makes those hopeless situations sting worse. They happen somewhat infrequently at least, perhaps dependent on what tier of tank you're playing with.I would say that if you go looking to just have fun driving around in your favorite tank while shooting other tanks, without worrying about progression or taking things too seriously, you'll probably have a fun time. Landing the final shot on an enemy tank and watching them go kaboom is very satisfying. There's a large amount of different tanks, meeting the expectations you'd have from a game calling itself World of Tanks, meaning there's likely a tank that everyone from a casual enjoyer to hardcore tank enthusiast will enjoy using. Whether it be looks, firepower, nigh-impenetrable armor, or that it's simply fun to use.I would recommend anyone who likes tanks to give the game a try, and have fun blowing things up

_childDocuments_.review: Are you ready to embark on a hilariously chaotic journey into the battlefield? Look no further than World of Tanks, the game that turns your tank-dreams into reality! Strap on your spiky helmet, grab a sandwich (or two), and prepare to experience the side-splitting joy that comes with crushing your enemies (and occasionally your own teammates)!First things first, let's talk about the tank variety in this game. It's like a buffet of armored mayhem! Whether you prefer the heavy metal monsters with cannons bigger than your neighbor's SUV, or the nimble little projectiles-on-wheels that zoom around faster than a caffeine-fueled cheetah, W.O.T.S has got you covered. Who needs a starring role in a Fast and Furious movie when you can feel the adrenaline rush from driving a pixelated killing machine?Now, let's address teamwork because we're all team players, right? Well, in W.O.T.S, the concept of teamwork is a little like herding cats (armed cats, of course). Imagine coordinating a group of enthusiastic toddlers hyped up on sugar and you're pretty close. Witness the spectacle of players zigzagging all over the map, careening into each other like a ballet of destruction. Who needs a GPS when you have a friendly tank crew constantly yodeling "Turn LEFT!" while driving straight into a river?But fear not, as the game also offers an educational experience! Want to learn how to swear in a brand new language? W.O.T.S has got you covered. The chat box becomes a linguistic playground where players invent new curse words and trade insults that could make a pirate blush. Careful though, some words might even give your tank a sudden bout of self-esteem issues, so stick with the classics.And what would a war simulation game be without explosions? W.O.T.S delivers plenty of boom, making sure you're never too far away from a Michael Bay-worthy explosion. Whether it's your own tank going "boom" due to misguided driving or an enemy tank spontaneously combusting in a burst of fireworks, explosions are definitely the stars of the show.To sum it up, W.O.T.S is like a 24/7 circus mixed with a demolition derby, sprinkled with a pinch of salty language. If you're ready to embrace the absurdity, laugh till you cry, and take armored warfare to a whole new level of hilarious pandemonium, then welcome to the world where tanks rule and sanity takes a vacation. Get your battle face on because in this game, laughter is the only currency that matters!

_childDocuments_.review: So originally I wrought a good review for this game but to be honest it was because the devs give you stuff for writing reviews. Now I didn't know if the review had to be good or bad to get the free days of premium so I just went and did a good review. However, I want to change that now. This game is extremely pay to win, it doesn't hide that fact so depending on your view of predatory I don't know if you could call it that. But I will say other people will have a an advantage over you no matter your skill level if they throw money at the game. The main factor of this is "Gold ammunition" which is just better then standard ammunition in all most all cases outside of maybe one or two tanks. The reason it's called gold is because it used to require the premium currency to purchase. However, now, it only cost the non-premium currency. And at first glance you'd think this was a good change. Making something that used to cost real money that just made you statistically better and changing it so everyone can purchase it with the in-game currency would be better, right? Well, it depends, the cost of purchasing the "gold" ammunition is so astronomically high compared to the standard with in-game currency you almost have to spend real money to always use it. The second factor which is something I guess should be obvious but I feel like a lot of people don't think about. Is that because gold ammunition is now more readily available everyone uses it and the game is horribly balanced around it. Some tanks are made useless due to gold ammunition in the game due to it's higher penetration values then standard ammunition (In most cases)  it can make tanks who's whole philosophy of just being able to bounce rounds completely useless as gold will almost always penetrate. Now what I am about to say will seem like a slight contradiction to the statement above but I would say if you play the game enough you'll know the differences in the situations I am talking about. Because Wargaming knows they have this gold ammunition in the game I believe they struggle to balance their new tanks around both types of ammunition. So what you get are these tanks that are basically impenetrable by standard ammunition and in addition don't have any weak spots outside of their lower plate and the back of the tank or the weak spots are so small that they are nigh impossible to hit consistently. In these situations, unless you have gold you're out of luck. Some of the tanks that have this exact issue are premium tanks, meaning people payed real money for them. A lot of these tanks are just strictly better some of which are the best tanks in the game to no ones surprise. You could consider some to be "game breaking". Wargaming never nerfs them, so once they are in the game they are stuck in the game in the same state forever. Well what is a company going to do when they already have "broken" stuff in their game. Well release more, because they can't release weaker tanks, no one would buy those. So you have the viscous cycle of power creep slowly making old tanks which were balanced for bygone era completely useless to the new hull-down super tank with 10 degrees of gun depression that is being sold for 40 dollars. So I would never recommend this game to anyone, and for current players of this game I would suggest if at all possible don't spend another dime. It's not worth your time and it's differently not worth your money that you worked hard to get. At the end of the day it's pixels on a screen that you don't even own. Wargaming could decide tomorrow that they are taking the game off the market and shutting down the servers. What happens to your hundreds of dollars of premium tanks? Well they are lost to void. So hopefully this review will prevent at least one person from playing or spending money on this game.

Firing premium ammo in one game can consume all the profit you just made over the past dozen battles using the regular cheap stuff. There are other things that require credits like tank equipment and the vehicles themselves so if you want to progress in the game you really can't afford to spend many credits on premium ammo.The game can be fun but Wargaming are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and keep the game full of imbalanced and unfair crap. Everything would be so easy to solve, but they would rather harpoon the whales than design a fair and balanced PvP game. Their business model for all of their titles is predatory and pay to win. _childDocuments_.review: Lets break it down. 15 minute/round 1 life strategy loadout-based fps. There's inherently a lot of player investment in a single match, which isn't always - but the game tries to maximize player count - 15v15. 10 Tiers, the higher the tier, the more expensive the investment to play, the slower and more strategy intense gameplay is, the more rewarding a win is. There's no correlating player skill to tier level, often times your investment to play a match will be entirely wasted by chance. The average winrate is 47.5%, with the best players eeking out 60-65% winrate. That's a lot of losing *everyone* experiences for this game to so heavily penalize you for losing. Which ropes in the real money economy. In order to sustain a high tier profile, you'll have to continually buy gold/credits or a buy a premium tank - based on your play habits. The large per-game investment and free price makes the playerbase pretty toxic, lots of wallet warriors out to waste your time 1 match at a time, either greifing you intentionally or out of plain ignorance. Some mid to high tiers have alternative private-ish matches - skirmishes and clan wars - which is about the only worthwhile game mode to play here. I played this game from open beta in 2010 until 2018. Lots of controversies with changes made and nearly everyone i used to play with will back up the opinion it's gotten worse every step of the way. That and I cant even log into my WoT account with the Steam Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally took the plunge and got this on Steam, after many moons of playing through the official website.The gameplay is damn good fun. You're in a tank, you blow the crap out of other tanks, and your team helps you do exactly that. There's nothing too subtle here - you know what you're getting into in terms of matches. The ballistics are all calculated with a freakishly neckbeard level of detail but you don't need to be quite so weird to enjoy it (shoot something in the ass and you're usually golden).There are three main classes - regular tanks (heavy, medium, or light), tank destroyers, and SPGs or artillery. They play pretty differently and require different skills, and I'll leave it to you to figure out what that is since this is a review and not a guide.There are complaints of grind and I understand that critique in a way - higher tier tanks require a massive time investment to hit T10 from T9 particularly. Saying it's a bare grind is an injustice though - you can earn XP from all your tanks from any level to spend on leveling up that high-tier beastie; Your Tier-1 French tractor earns XP to level up your Tier-9 British Tank-Destroyer.You can very easily get a Tier-4 tank in a single day of playing. Several T4 tanks, in fact, of various classes. So after a month of gaming, when you're trying to get that high Tier tank, you have about 12 different tanks to play, all with different gameplay and tactical styles (A Russian SU-18 SPG is wildly different from a German Grille SPG, for instance, though they're both around Tier 4), and their XP all adds on to that high level tank's 'grind'. And let's face it, if you don't enjoy mad tank battles then why are you even playing??

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to say a few things about World of Tanks for the sake of anyone who has not played it before. At its core, I actually like World of Tanks. The game plays well, and a lot of attention was put into the detail of the vehicles. My problem with World of Tanks is the predatory way that Wargaming labels it as a "free to play" game. You are capable of playing the game for free to a point, but it becomes heavily incentivized that you should buy a premium account. Its a free to play game, and getting players to spend money is how they keep the servers on. I understand that, but I dont like how they force the players hand into supporting the game.The largest problem with the game, by far, is the "pay to win" aspect. You can purchase premium vehicles from the store, for real money. I played this game off and on for probably close to 10ish years, and I have watched them unbalance the game over and over with the paid tanks. Not every vehicle in the pay store is broken, but the majority of them certainly feel like they are just flat out better.The in game economy is bad to the point that you are, yet again, incentivized to purchase a premium account.Some of the countries havent had their vehicles rebalanced in years, and they have slowly become worthless (RIP American heavy line). The game honestly has one of the most toxic communities that I have ever seen and the developers do absolutely nothing to handle that.So, if you have never played World of Tanks before, I suggest you pass on it. Its a free game though, so give it a try if you are that bored. Just go into it armed with the knowledge that it starts up kinda fun and then drives that "gimme money" attitude home after about tier 5.

The only way to have a drastic change, in a game as big and successful as this, would be to not spend any more money ever until they make the necessary changes. Unfortunately, this will never happen because not everyone has the same opinions/thoughts/preferences/etc. There's only one thing you can do. Play the game, or find another.With that being said, here are the issues with this game. I'll start with the worst from the top. This game has such a gigantic RNG modifier that I don't understand why some things even exist, such as the "Red/Orange/Green" indicator when aiming at an enemy. If you know enough about this game and the tanks, including the one you're using in a specific match, you should know that your tank weapon will most definitely penetrate the current enemy's hull. Unfortunately, RNG comes into play. Even though everything lined up perfectly, your shot will magically not hit. Ricochet. Not Penetrated. Sometimes flat out go past the tank, even though neither of you moved and the enemy is point blank range. It literally kills the desire to play the game. But hold on. Here's the real problem. This was never a big issue, at least not personally, to the point that it would make you not want to play. It's as if they thought ramping this up to the max would be a good idea. I do not understand the thought process behind this. The only logical conclusion I've come up with is the fact that individual players were able to completely dominate matches with 9-10+ kills per side, and this RNG no longer allows that to happen, at least not as easily as looking at a tank, shooting, and killing them instantly. There's not a lot to say about this. The matchmaking, in my opinion, should never be different tiers. Unfortunately, what we have is a difference of 2 tiers which in turn creates a gigantic power disparity. It becomes so bad to the point that most people will not be able to do a damn thing in said matches. I'd be perfectly content if the difference was only 1 tier, but 2 is far too much. Basic & Premium accounts are basically the same, in the sense that they really don't make much of either. You absolutely need reserves, but even with reserves, it is incredibly low. We'll take it a step further. You have premium, reserves, platoon, commander contract. You are still barely making anything, and you are more often than not LOSING credits.But then comes WG's incredible system that makes no sense whatsoever. You start a match, you basically don't do anything. Not one shot fired, nobody spotted, you just died almost instantly. Win or lose, somehow you made a large amount of credits and exp. Here comes the second game, where you've had 3 kills, quite a bit of damage done, some blocked, some spotted and the game is a victory. Your credits and exp are half of what you made in the first match where you did .What does this mean? It means that not only must you spend a very large amount of money to buy gold for reserves, or reserves for real money as well as premium account, but the fact that it really makes no difference whatsoever. You will be losing credits more often than not. What choice do you have? Yes, you guessed it right. Buy gold with real money, transfer gold to credits, or buy a premium tank that makes a hell of a lot of credits every match, regardless if you do well or not. Yes, you've been reading about this in basically every review, and it's true. Premium Tanks are vastly superior to their normal tech tree counterparts in more ways than one. Whether that's stats-wise, or the potential to make bonds, credits and/or exp faster. The recent T9 Strv K is a great example of this. This has not changed and will very likely never, ever change. This is how I get to T10 fast. Play these tanks, convert their premium exp to free exp and use it to unlock tanks faster. This costs gold, but there you have it. Not much to say on this except the truth. Much like every other multiplayer game, people flat out suck. You will lose more than win, even on a platoon where you basically carry the entire team. There's barely any sort of strategy or tactics used, it's all brainless. People are so desperate to get kills, they feed the other team free kills by making beginner mistakes. Most of the time, the only hope you have is that your platoon does well enough to help your team win.What this means is that your stats will basically be butchered. You'll have a lot of toxic troglodytes saying you're trash because your win rate is below 50%. These are the same people that will rage whisper you after a match simply because you killed them or they lost the game. You can easily make sure this never happens, as there's an option in the Main Menu to disable non-friends to message you. Always make sure to report these people, as WG actually does silence them and increases the silence time an extra day each time they are silenced.Although this is all negative, I'll say this about World of Tanks.It is freaking awesome. It is infinitely better than War Thunder in more ways than one, and you will not find another tank experience like this.Would I recommend this game solo? No.Would I recommend this game with friends that will play with you all the time? Yes.Would I recommend this game if you're not using premium tanks, aside from T10s? No.Would I recommend this game if you're not spending large amounts of money, for both premium & gold? Not a chance.Overall, avoid this game if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing World of Tanks (WOT) since 2011, and I love it so much that I frequently return to have some fun. Honestly, the game was great for the first five years, but after that, I started to feel increasingly frustrated while playing itFirst of all, the game has a serious pay-to-win problem when it comes to higher-tier matches. I'm a big fan of super heavy tanks, such as the VK 45.02b, Maus, and Type 5 Heavy, but these tanks have become less fun to play due to the prevalence of premium round spammers. Gold rounds offer 1/3 more penetration than standard shells without sacrificing any damage reduction or reload time, giving experienced players an absolute penetration advantage. The so-called good all-around armor is only effective at blocking most Tier 10 standard shells, but not premium rounds. You might wonder if I'm not angling my armor well enough, but in my experience, it would require extreme skill and luck to do so. Nowadays, the mighty Maus only shines in Tier 8 games. Many map designs are not friendly to super heavies, and spawning into a completely open map with three artillery units on the opposing team means certain doom.My advice for players who want to play heavy tanks is to pick hull-down tanks with invulnerable turrets. These tanks are hard to penetrate, even with gold rounds. Wargaming has added many hull-down positions to most maps, including city maps, with building corners and debris to entertain the hull-down player and help protect their weak hulls. These tanks also have better mobility and gun depression, making it effective to camp on high ground. Last year, they nerfed the high-explosive (HE) shell, making most hits deal zero damage to invulnerable turrets. Therefore, there is no reason not to play hull-down tanks nowadays.Furthermore, I am greatly disappointed with the introduction of the cursor armor indicator. It undermines all the effort I put into studying the weak spots and armor thickness of every tank for years. Now, everyone just wiggles their mouse around at the enemy until the cursor turns green, then they take the shot.In addition, there is too much grinding required if I don't spend money on a premium account and premium tank. Relying on inexperienced crews, lousy stock cannons, and engines makes the gameplay extremely frustrating. The process of gaining XP and researching new tech is way too long and painful. The worst thing is that I lose more money to repair my tank at Tiers 9 and 10 if I'm not contributing enough damage in the battle, because my stock cannon fails to penetrate or misses most of the targets. There are many ways to make a profit from a free-to-play game, and such frustrating gameplay causes many players to abandon it halfway through.Additionally, the presence of over 600 tanks in the game that suffer from balancing issues also saddens me. The newly released tech trees always seem to have a better advantage than the old ones. Overpowered premium tanks such as Scorpion G, Defender, Bourrasque, M6A2E1, and Progetto M35 mod 46 frequently appear in most games, and the meta reward tanks such as Chieftain and Object 279 are completely broken."Speaking of premium tanks, a tier 8 premium tank costs 60 dollars, which is equivalent to the price of a AAA game. I have never dared to own one of them.There are not enough maps in the game, and I quickly began to feel that the gameplay was repetitive. Some of the maps are just not fun to play on. Although there were many good maps in the past, unfortunately, many of them have not returned.In my opinion, as a casual player, the best way to have fun with this game is to avoid playing at higher tiers, particularly tiers 9 and 10. Initially, I believed that playing at tier 10 would allow me to avoid facing higher-tier tanks. However, it turned out to be even more frustrating. In my experience, playing around with tier 3 to 7 tanks is much more enjoyable.Over the past 10 years, many good things have been removed from the game, and instead, poorly optimized new tanks have been added. The Hydro Pneumatic, Soviet double barrel, wheeled tanks, and reserve tracks didn't add much excitement to the game. In my opinion, what we need are more elements like weather and destructible buildings that can create unexpected and exciting outcomes.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot say if I recommend or not recommend the game, but here are a few insights.Strong points:•	Graphics are decent. Maps are detailed and you can feel that pretty much.•	Tank models are very detailed. You can shoot only the main gun, but machine guns probably wouldn’t help you very much in tank battle.•	The tank tree is huge, and you don’t need too much grinding to research new vehicle. Especially if you know that red is usually an enemy vehicle.But here the fun ends:•	As a free to play game Wargaming needs to keep a player base and attract new players. So, when a player is happy – he will probably buy something. But how to do that when there are ten-year veterans? Here comes the WoT balancing. If you get any better – from time to time you will be put in teams where five or more players do ZERO (- 0 -) damage. Out of 15! And you can be skilled as you want – you will lose. And even if you are a premium player – you will be punished. If you are free to play player – you will be punished even more. Ask yourself, why do even the best players have WinRatio about 68%? How it is even possible?•	WoT track every centimeter you travel. Every tank you play. If you get your first fight with enemies on the same tier and do quite well. Next battle will be against +2 tiers. And if you accidentally meet a higher tier tank face to face – usually you will not penetrate their armor. This game you are just a “meat” and that’s it. For example, play artillery a lot and very well. And every 3 battles you will play Himmelsdorf (city map where is very hard to play as SPG).•	Premium shells. Well… Just open your wallet and penetrate everything.•	What the… is “armor not hit” message? You shoot, hit the enemy. Literally see shell hitting enemy tank and game deserves you with “armor not hit” message. •	The strongest armor in the game is the wheeled tank wheels. Try penetrating them… (game engine issue).•	Premium tanks are fun. But some are just insane. For example Bat.-Châtillon Bourrasque. Take 50 euros, buy it and here you go. Medium tank with full light tank equipment and concealment. 700 damage every 20 seconds or less. When there is a sale – every battle you get more than four of them.As conclusion – game is fun. Events are interesting, including the twitch drops. But the constant punishment… each time you play you think that maybe it will be the last time and usually hold your mouse on “uninstall” button.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the most difficult to review for me. On one hand you have a great and original idea, smooth graphics and easy to learn gameplay. The game features many historical vehicles from the whole 20th century, you can decide if you want to play for tanks (light, medium, heavy), AT gun or artilery. Depends what playing style you prefer. Controling of the vehicle on the map is pretty easy as well as using the equipment. Buying equipment and improvements is something you have to learn, but it is not that hard and takes just little time. On the other hand you get often sick of the game by being grouped in team with idiots who die in the first 10 seconds and leave you against enemy with superior numbers. Thanks to the fact that there are 10 tiers (or levels) of vehicles in the game and each teir is significantly stronger than the one before, you get often grouped with vehicles from other tiers. For example you have a tier 5 tank so you may get a group where are two tier 4, eight tier 5 and six tier 6 vehicles. You start of and run into one of the tier 6 tanks, your shots just bounce form his armor. And he fcks you up on two shots... That just sparks a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ joy, right? Another thing that ruins the game is of course the "pay to win" system. This is a bit better than it was in the past but still. You cant buy stuff that will make you immortal, but you can buy things that will give you big advantage. Some of these things are optainable even for the normal players in the game, but they are hard to get and you cant use them all the time because unlike the paying player you run out of them fast. And some things like skins for your vehicle can be only bought for real money.In conclusion... The game is well made with nice graphics and content and its probably worth playing. But be prepared to get fed up by the dumb grouping system where you dont stand a chance in half of the games however you try, or get pissed by some paying kid.

The most egregious examples are here:- E25 with the speed of a 65km/h light tank and the gun of a tier 8 at tier 7 and against tier 6's in MM- Wheeled clown cars that cannot be hit on higher than 80 ping (I play from Australia so my ping is 200)- Premiums like the T-34-85M that were shadow buffed to be better than the actual T-34-85 instead of being balanced with a worse gun before- Egregiously heavily armored tanks like the Defender- APCR rounds since the start (they were paid only for about 1 year in 2010 - and effectively still are expensive enough to be)- And finally, the all poisonous and extremely toxic HE rework that rendered half the playerbase and tank pool useless. My T-44 no longer can fire the 122mm HE shell that was the equaliser against wheeled clown cars and heavy impregnable premiums, swedish hull down castles, and otherwise. They removed the one tool that was designed to reliably force players to reposition, and to hide their tracks. The new "HEsh" type HE is literally just Hesh/Heat hybrid, with no splash damage and the inability to splash the engine deck - which IRL and in game is the only method you could use at times to kill heavies that are overarmored on all sides - (looking at the Defender here)Wargaming is actively forcing the entire playerbase to load gold in order to penetrate tanks that have heavy armor. This is blatantly pay to win and no longer debatable or plausibly deniable. Since HE was such a huge piece of my kit as a medium player and brawler I can no longer reliably track players or reliably damage scouts that I used to one shot with a large caliber HE shell. Wargaming, you win. I quit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game that remains quite challenging and rewards patience.- There are lots of tank classes, tank destroyers and self propelled guns to play, research and collect.- Actual tank designs from the 1910's to the 1970's add historical interest, while paper and prototype tanks add a 'what if' aspect to the game.- Customisation elements such as paints, camouflages, decals and crew perks make for a more personalised experience.Some overall considerations when playing this game:- Learn to play at your own pace, e.g. make use of the helpful training missions and tank academy tutorials;- Play the vehicles and classes you like (it is okay to enjoy tanks, armoured cars, tank destroyers and artillery);- Ignore (or switch off) the chat trolls;- Most of all, have fun - it is an arcade game after all!It took a while for me to start getting to grips with the game-play and mechanics. After c.270 hours at the time of writing this review I am still very much learning - a few tips that make a difference as a beginner, even if these seem somewhat obvious, are:- Make the mini-map bigger and refer to it often;- Use terrain features and bushes to conceal your position as much as possible;- Take time to manually aim and aim for tracks and weak spots, for better accuracy - auto-aim can also work well, e.g. on the move;- If you are spotted, e.g. after firing, move and change position;- Angle the vehicle whenever possible to safeguard weak spots, e.g. to present 60+ degrees to help deflect hits on flat surfaces.

_childDocuments_.review: Veteran tanker here. I have about 60k battles just for reference.I SOOOO want to recommend this game. But currently cannot. I mean I guess it depends what you want out of it. If you get easily frustrated this isn't the game for you. Let me explain my biggest frustrations.1. "Wheeled" vehicles. They decided to add wheeled light vehicles to this game for some reason. They advertised them as fast active scouts that wouldn't have armor and would be bad at 1 on 1 fighting. This was a complete and total lie! They are active scouts, they are fast, but they also have magic armor so even if you manage to hit one there's about a 20% chance you'll actually do damage. And in this game there is rng, shot dispersion, and shell travel time so good luck hitting a vehicle that can turn off road at 90kph for some reason. But the reverse is also true. They have magic guns that are about 90% accurate at hitting you while they are turning and jumping over hills. Add that when other tanks are hit in the tracks they come to a stop until repaired. When these things are hit in the wheels they just keep right on going and can repair it on the move. Beyond the most frustrating mechanic I've ever experienced in a game.2. "Reward" vehicles. Wargaming in their infinite wisdom decided the best way to reward the most skilled players in the game was to reward them with the most OP tanks. We're talking tanks that cannot be penetrated even with well aimed premium rounds from most vehicles. There is no excuse for this. None, ever! If you come face to face with one and you aren't also in a one of the best vehicles in the game you might as well log out.3. Artillery. Wargaming loves their artillery mechanic. They allow 3 self propelled guns per side. So imagine how fun it is when you are playing a large slow vehicle (also known as a tank) and some person across the map that you cant see or generally hide from that has satellite view in their WW2 artillery piece keeps hitting you non stop. Every time they hit you they probably break your track, cause damage, and stun you which makes you fire slower, move slower, and not be able to hit anything. They'll fire at you about every 30 seconds and if there is multiple arties they will team up so your entire battle is being stunned or taking damage from enemies you cannot see or counter. It's really a blasty blast! Thanks another great mechanic.Things I do like the most:1. Completely original game style. I've tried to find alternatives to this game with similar game style. There are other tank games but non seem to offer the depth and complexity and historical flair that this one does when everything is going right. There's so much to learn with armor profiles on tanks, map strategies, configuration options, etc. You never run out of things to do or try.2. Its really fun with a platoon of friends. Probably the main thing that's kept me playing is when you are teamed up with your buddies and you have the synergy of a well built platoon there is a great rush when you are kicking butt.3. It's occasionally REALLY fun! When you get into a match and the tiering is good, you have your buddies on, there are no artilleries or wheeled vehicles this game is amazing. Smart play is rewarded and bad play is punished. It's nice that it's a shooter style game where adapting and tactics are more important than twitch reflexes. If the company would fix the arty, wheeled vehicles, and reward vehicles I'd recommend this 100%. But the company as a LONG history of not fixing things the community cares about or "fixing" them by making them worse.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for the past seven months, it's really a great game. While it may seem daunting at first and can take a lot to understand the mechanics, once you gain an understanding it becomes quite satisfying. There are a lot of different play styles; there are tanks that make you feel invincible when every shell is just bouncing off of you. There are tanks where you can hide in a bush and let your team destroy them without even getting spotted. You can zip around and potshot tanks before they even end up turning toward you. While there isn't much beyond PvP and hardly any end game, the real treat is trying to upgrade your skill level in the tanks you love best. To some, the game may feel grindy, but World of Tanks really does give you tons of opportunities to minimize this without spending any money. The monetization tactics do seem steep, some tanks can go for over $100, but you do not need to spend any money. Sure, a lot of premium tanks are a lot of fun, but there's enough free tanks that are just as fun as long as you look for them. The community is far from the most friendly in random battles or steam page discussions, but you can join a clan with like minded people or platoon with two of your friends in random battles. Most importantly, Wargaming may have been based in Belarus before 2022, but they have made efforts to sever their ties to the Russian economy and have donated to medical aid for Ukraine and are currently running a promotion where 100% of the proceeds (when buying the Ukraine package) goes toward medical aid for Ukraine. Glory to Ukraine. Glory to Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very interesting game. Interesting in the aspect that the developer seems to not care at all about the experience of those playing, but in taking every advantage possible to make money. This is not unique in games. However, I have not come across an example as blatantly anti-experience as this. The game industry exists to make money. But as it started, and for the most part, up until maybe ~5 years ago, developers at least made efforts to pretend that part of their responsibility in the development and then sale of a game, is to make it enjoyable. Companies seemed to at least pay attention to feedback of failed titles, successes, etc. However, once a game has a large enough following, it seems many developers decide to switch strategies and instead focus only on profit. Is it a smart business move? It can be, but it is aggravating. In this case, WOT has established a very invested player base. But this is where it gets much worse, and unacceptable in 'ethical' practice. Let's finally get into it... How did WOT end up with such a 'loyal' player base? From my observations, a few reasons. First of all, it seems as though original players had a very decent experience. The game seemed to be largely received as fun. However, it was still quite 'grindy'. As the reputation of WOT has gone from 'fun', to 'alright', to 'eh', to 'worst game ever', more and more grinding type of aspects have been implemented. Crews are a primary example. So it seems there is a large portion of players who have invested so much of their time into this game that they have troubles walking away, as many players have. But why walk away? Why is this game so terrible now? well......Premium ammo, premium accounts, premium tanks, garage and barracks slots, ridiculously expensive equipment and consumables, literally doing the opposite of player feedback, the purposely bad matchmaker, and most importantly.... RNG!I get it. The game is 'free to play' so they gotta make money somehow. Understandable. but how they do it is absolutely absurd. I'll cover the specifics, but overall, I would suggest WOT use the payment model of League of Legends where players are able to benefit from all in-game features other than cosmetic, without paying. they make their money from accelerating the grind and cosmetics. not from effectively nerfing all free to play players as WOT has done with remarkable success....So. What specifically are the issues. They all essentially stem from the matchmaker and the RNG. Aside from always being on unbalanced teams and usually not having anything close to a close game, the matchmaker places players on teams ranging 3 tiers of tanks. For example. imagine you just GRINDED through constant match losses, making next to no credits or even losing 10x more credits per match because of an RNG feature (module/crew damage), and you finally got to tier 4. Ok. now the game is putting your basic, stock tier 4 tank in the game with tier 6 'elite' or upgraded tanks. well, that's just not fair, is it. no. it is not. so not only do you NOT have the ability to penetrate those tanks, at all. you are most likely slower, lower hp, half the armor or less, etc... well why do they do this? that sounds absurd. why do players keep playing? i dont know why people keep playing, but it's obvious why WOT does this. Now, in these games, you're giving those players 2 tiers down the option of either paying for premium ammo to have any hope of damaging anything, or just wait until the next match. they use that premium ammo and they WILL lose credits. it is designed this way. why? to tempt players to pay for a premium account in order to buy the premium ammo. now another reason. people get so sick of being in underpowered tanks that they are tempted in buying premium tanks and accelerating their progression. all any of this does is purposely punish free players. Now the most obnoxious reason, RNG. I'll explain by spelling it out as if i was describing to someone who has never played the game: when you play, your accuracy is dependent on an aiming circle. the circle is very large if you move and gradually becomes smaller after you stop. to take a 'well-aimed' shot, you must be stationary for however many seconds after stopping for the circle to shrink. BUT, a game feature is that sometimes your shell will just plop out of the barrel and fall on the ground. or it will rocket off in a different direction entirely. sometimes it just DISAPPEARS! often, it'll just barely miss. this is dependent 'on chance' have fun! seriously? imagine if in any other game, the thing you do just doesn't do what you tell it to do half the time. Now another RNG feature, module and crew damage. what if i told you that RANDOMLY, you'll sometimes have a crew member become incapacitated or an equipment module break. ok, sounds like something that could happen and is something that makes it worth aiming for certain spots (even though accuracy is random, as previously mentioned) and something to add some strategy and make it more interesting. BUT! every time this happens, you can either become irrelevant OR pay WOT from 2-40,000+ credits to 'get back in the fight'. WHAT? now what if i tell you that this is probably going to happen to you multiple times PER game and you'll probably only be making  <20,000 credits per game and of that, have to pay half or more to 'resupply' ammo and 'repair' damage (if you're not using premium ammo). well. there we have it. a very obvious way to 'force' players to either pay an absolutely RIDICULOUS amount of real money to be relevant in the game (but still subject to terribly biased RNG), or simply have a miserable experience. To make it all even more hilarious, the increasingly more upset player base complains when WOT asks for feedback and WOT often does the exact opposite. it really is hilarious. They keep asking why people are hating the game, reviews are terrible, and people have stopped playing. No one is being forced to play. The game has good potential, especially for a 'free' game. But they are essentially extorting people while claiming it isn't pay to play. it seems the only reason they get any new players is their very extensive marketing and youtuber payments. but hey, they're making big $$$, so the strategy is working. For those of you who have not played and don't know the prices..... it's about $30-100 for a tank, $100 per year for premium, and will require hundreds more to buy the stuff to be relevant without dedicating your life to the game. people pay that. lots of people. ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Boy! where to start...First of all, thank you Wargaming for making me re-download and idle the game in the background for an hour just so I can leave a review, even though I have been playing this game for 10 years. Would I recommend this game to anyone starting from zero today? No, Absolutely not. It should be criminal to label this game as free to play. Its free to install. You will either quit this game or have to shell out $100s every year to stay even remotely competitive in this game. If you are ok with this, this game 'can' be fun, in spite of Wargaming trying their hardest to break it with every 'new feature' Dont think that just buying one tier 8 premium tank and some premium time will be enough even though this will cost as much as a AAA title game, and forget about being competitive at lower tiers in non premium tank. At higher tiers, there are competitive tech tree tanks but to get to those tiers on a free account, will require ungodly amount of time and to stay competitive, you will need to use premium consumables and ammo which means you will be losing money every time you play on a free account. On top of that, thanks to a massive power creep of new premium tanks, your premium tank has a useful life of a few months before a new uber overpowered premium is released and your tank becomes garbage tier. The latest money grab feature is the "Battle Pass" that you have to buy, more than once, and gives your a privilege of grinding for equipment that is not available for silver and, of course, significantly better. If your thought you could be competitive with just premium time and premiums tanks, think again. Now, at best, you can spend a bunch more cash and get the new flavor of the month tank, more premium time, battle pass. At worst, WG will force you to buy lottery tickets and gamble with your money for a chance to get a new overpowered tank via loot boxes and blind auctions. Something that is now illegal in some EU countries. Other questionable tactics this community has endured over the years are:Having your Youtube channel copyright struck if you express opinions not in line with WG marketing. Being removed from community contributor programme for expressing opinions.Having your accounts suspended for expressing opinions on the official forum. Only being able to leave feedback about upcoming changes in the most loaded questionnaire possible, eg I like this feature a)A lot b)somewhat c)very little and reading the final report that WG research indicates at least 90% of the community 'likes' the new feature. Important tank attributes hidden in the game client, having people to rely on 3rd party tools and data mining to have an honest comparison. Politics aside, the gameplay itself is very badly balanced. There are certain classes of vehicles and certain individual vehicles that are so unbalanced WG themselves banned them from more competitive modes or have to limit their numbers in those modes, yet they refuse to do anything to actually balance them. Dont worry! They are still playable in Random battles and they will farm your tiny tech tree tank and no, you will never get one.Graphics and physics are 'ok' but really not up to standard of a modern title. To summarize, this game is fun at first, addictive, you get to shoot tanks after all, you get matched against other new players or bots even, you feel like you are progressing and getting a hang of it. Then a switch gets flipped and you are thrown into the meat grinder with players who have spent 100s of dollars and treat your tank as an XP pinata. You cant beat them, so you join them or you quit. People say this is negative review 'bombing' but it is just what happens when you neglect your customers for 10 years without giving them a way to express their opinions or bother to listen to your own community contributors.

This is the most brutal thing of them all, when a new player is sitting in a completely stock tank with no upgrades and he is being thrown in a game with 2 TIERS higher tanks. Just wait for a moment when you load premium ammo on a stock tank and aiming at enemy +2 tier tank "weak" spot you get RED marker. Game design by the gods.2) World of Premium tanks. Premium tanks on the left, premium tanks on the right, premium tanks everywhere... Those are tanks that people pay 20-40+ euros per tank, so they could log in and show their dominance on players that are grinding regular Tech tree tanks. _childDocuments_.review: So this game initially is a great time waster for people who just want to grind something. 40+ hours is more than enough for me to recommend a free game, so pick it up and give it a go... But the reality of the game starts at tier 5+ at that point its up to you if you want to stick with it let me explain in a wall of tedious text.For the first portion of the game you are pitted against other new players and bots up until Tier 4 where you start getting introduced to the 2 Tier higher games meaning half the team will be tier 5 and 6 leaving you a much weaker. This doesnt sound too bad because you can just play well and win through tactics right? What if I told you there was a thing called troll armor. What this does is add areas to a tank where you cannot penetrate period, but for Tier 4s this areas is basically the entire tank while you are left unarmored. So in reality you are below worthless. You could on the other hand scout for the team but the issue with that is the higher tiers have greater spotting range and camo, since they are in the longer tiers to climb they also have equipment and crew that drastically improve their advantages further. In short you will have 0 impact in this game, 0 impact = low xp which = longer and longer times to upgrade to T5.Then you get to tier 5 its still the same problem as you will now face T6 and 7. But you can now start adding equipment to help reduce the advantages they have over you. But the troll armor will stay more or less the same, you are better off learning the tanks and their weakpoints and 99% of the time running away unless they leave a weakpoint open which rarely happens you will probably instantly die to the higher tier even if you get it. Aim is also RNG so even if you spot a weakpoint you arent always going to hit it. Even if you do you arent always going to pen it unless it is a pure weakpoint. And in tier 5 a well known thing is seal clubbers, people who played the game for hundreds of hours but stay in T5 with the T5 meta tanks maxed out ready to destroy some newer players who arent aware of all the weakpoints yet. Strategically the basic play T5 + is at the start cross as much dead ground as possible to get to a secure tactical position. Once you've arrived you then wait for the scouts who are now more comfortable with the line being further forward to start making their moves and spotting tanks in the open. This allows for the artillery to do its thing from the back lines. Once the heavies have arrived at the positions with the medium tanks they will start to crawl forward and breakthrough or camp till the enemy makes a move. Mediums try some fancy pop shots and keep the heavies flanks guarded overcoming the heavies weakness. Mediums are also open to reposition depending on how the map starts to look. Pretty basic stuff, ofc it can get a bit more complex but nothing insane. Sadly in my experience RnG and troll armor is the biggest deciding factor in the skirmishes. Most fights are standoffs that last for most the game, which makes it more like a game of hide and seek than a fast paced combat game. It can get pretty boring waiting around if that's not your thing because it will happen. Many games half the team doesnt even leave the spawn area and just hides in bushes waiting to pick off anyone who makes an advance into dead ground, and lets be honest someone has to eventually unless you want every game to time out with no action. But yeah the troll armor is incredibly bad. Some tanks are immune entirely unless you can get behind them to a tiny vent which if you understand how terrain works its mostly impossible especially when the only ones who can move fast enough to get there have lower armor. So the trade isnt even worth taking, majority of the times as I said the mediums will be there to destroy you the moment you consider it. Remember if you cant do damage then you get no xp so its pure hell, you cant impact the game and you cant increase in tiers. I would much prefer to hit them for 10 damage on an armored part than 0 at least then you get something.So there is a way to overcome some troll armor and thats premium ammo. It used to cost gold to fire which is the real money currency but now it costs high amounts of silver. For new players this isnt sustainable you need to be playing in at least T7 + to get a decent income, and too increase that more you need a premium tank. I havent yet used the ammo for obvious reasons since I only have T5s so I cant say how effective it is. But I assume some more points become available to hit on tanks that previously appeared to be immune.Needless to say I wont bore you anymore short explanation is troll armor removes alot of the tactics slowing the game down to a crawl. You constantly face seal clubbers and higher tiers which makes you feel helpless. And the community is about as toxic as one can get, their egos are so high they think camping in a game for 10 minutes translates to skill. Ignore them if you decide to play, you will only get better and they will not show don't tell.If anyone is more knowledgeable about the game feel free to correct anything I said that's wrong or give ideas on how to beat troll armor. I'm sure it will help players who decide to try the game out.

My last 1k stats are ~64% winr, ~3450 wn8, and I am ranked #1 all time on a few tanks based on their in-game hall of fame.TLDR: Don't bother with this game.It's fun...under the very specific circumstances (playing  with friends at low/mid tiers and getting the right matchmaking). But I definitely would not recommend the game to anyone, especially new players.Issues:- Extremely Pay to Win. If you don't plan on spending a decent amount of money in this game, don't even install it. You will not have a good time. Premium time is basically a must-have, as is having a few premium vehicles to farm credits with. - Extremely steep learning curve. If you're a new and free to play player you'll get roflstomped for a very long time. It will take thousands of games for you to properly learn maps, vehicles, tactics, etc. Not to mention to buy the necessary equipment for your tanks, level your crews, etc- Bad maps. Over half of the maps are pretty terrible, in my opinion. Depending on the tank you're playing, some maps are just brutal. Corridor maps for light (scout) tanks, wide open maps for slow heavy tanks, etc. It also takes them forever to release new maps. - Atrocious matchmaking. You can literally have a team of 15 players with a winrate below 50% vs a stacked enemy team. (and to think it used to be worse somehow)- High tiers are trash to play. You lose credits at the highest tier(s). You basically need to shoot "premium" ammunition, which costs more credits.- Tier 8+ is ruined by "EBR" vehicles. They are wheeled vehicles (not tanks) that zip around maps at 100+km/h, have literal auto-aim, etc.- Arty. This type of vehicle sits at the back of the map and just rains down artillery shells that stun + damage you. You don't even need to be hit directly since they have a large splash radius. Being on the receiving end of this is awful. It takes no skill to play, and there's nothing you can really do to counter it.- Incompetent devs. They are completely tone deaf to what the players want. They have a constant habit of trying to fix things that aren't broken, while ignoring the broken aspects of the game. Latest example of this is the crew skill rework, which they were forced to scrap when the playerbase revolted. This has happened countless times over the years.- Steam version won't let you use your existing account. There's so much more but I'll stop here.
