_childDocuments_.review: Want non-terrible tanks without stupid amounts of grind? Buy gold, buy good tank.Want to earn credits for gear? Pay money for premium or grind forever just trying to afford a Tier VI tank. Also, no accruing credits for filthy standard accounts.Want to earn XP for research? Grind your face off because starting out you're going to lose a lot & that nets minimal XP. Or accrue XP on a tank that's elite and convert it to free XP...for gold.Wants good cosmetics? You guessed it, gold. But you can have some ugly stuff for free as thanks for playing.There's yet another dumb AF battle pass with lots of boosters locked behind it & gues what? Pay for that separately from premium because value is not what the store is about, gtfo.Want to improve your crew skills? Train to 100% for gold, or 75% for credits, or go free for 60%.But hey, buy boosters in the shop because paying for premium isn't enough on its own!For all the P2W elements this game has, the underlying gameplay is fun. The sounds are well done and the music compliments the maps nicely. The tanks each handle differently and the different classes require you to learn their specific movement strategies. The upgrade system does give you the feeling that your tank is getting better, but it feels a lot more tedious than it needs to be. Researching new tanks after building off the fundamentals of the prior tank is actually a good idea, but going from a fully upgraded tank to a newly researched one often feels terrible because starting gear is often worse on the new tank (treads & engine make the biggest differences).But shot RNG is infuriating. Nothing feels worse than trading shots only to be the one that dies because the shot ricochets or gets absorbed by armor because suddenly, no pen for you! Sighting also is annoying because as you rise in ranks, often chungus 5000 hour has an improved equipment & crew so he can spot you from damn near the other side of the map. Have fun trying to scramble to new cover only to die midway from a tank you can't even see! Scouting a lane? Hope you like getting 1 shot because 2 heavies and a destroyer are lane camping & blast you before your sight even lets you know they're there.TL;DR - The game gets very P2W once you rise above Tier 4 & the mechanics hold back what is otherwise a good game at the core. If you are going to play, do it in small bursts.

_childDocuments_.review: This game receives a lot of negative reviews, so many might think 'if you hate it so much, why did you play it so much?', the answer is simple, World of Tanks delivers probably the best experience in the industry for driving a tank into the battle. Unfortunately it also lacks any balance and is quite literally the embodiment of pay2win logic, more than any other game. - You can load your tank with premium ammo that almost guarantees that you will deal damage (just hitting the enemy isn't enough, you have to aim to deal damage, that's part of gameplay which makes it entertaining) and has no drawbacks other than being absurdly expensive, which isn't much problem for whales because you can convert premium currency to credits. - Playing higher tier tanks might penalize you for playing without premium (you can loose ingame credits for winning the battle). - Low tier tanks experience is very bad (there's big jump between tanks of tier 4 and 5, which makes it very hard for many players to get to actual good tanks). - default 15v15 format isn't really good for teamplay and you can't adapt to the situation in battle, if you are thrown into a battle, you're done with customizing your loadout (you can end up in a battle where you can't do much. In very radical scenario, there's the possibility that you can't do anything, some tanks without upgrades can't even fight their own tier).In all honesty, it's not all bad, when it shines, it shines as bright as thousand suns and there's a lot of technical skill visible in overall quality of the game, but there are just so many confusing things that makes this game unfortunate pile of wasted potential, don't waste your time on it. This review is based on my past experiences, I am currently downloading non-Steam client just to check if anything changed, but I doubt it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had played the game years ago, and decided to give it another try. The core value proposition of the game remains the same: Strike a good balance between an arcade game and a tank simulation. WoT lands somewhat on the arcade side of things, but the tanks look great and so do the maps. There is enough there to get a WWII nerd geeked up about playing WoT.Pros:- The initial grind seems to have shorted. After a much better introduction (bootcamp) than the earlier game, you will actually start at level 3. This is definitely a plus.- The initial experience is great because of it, as you start with enough coin to make that level playable and enjoyable, resulting in a much better initial experience than before.- There is more "stuff", from missions, battle passes, dog tags, exterior options and other things, that don't seem to be core to the game itself.  (Some may find that entertaining, others not so much.)- While the start time to get into a game seems to be longer, the games seem to be a lot more balanced than before. Complete and utter wipe-outs that were quite common before, are not nearly as frequent. (I can only speak for games up to Tier V after this short time in the new version.)- Maps seem to be well-maintained and re-balanced.  The maps are also visually appealing, and I'm not nearly done exploring the newer maps.  Even if you don't like the game itself, it is worth playing the game just for driving the tank around and taking in the virtual scenery.- Teams seem to be a little bit better behaved. The older versions were notorious for people completely losing it in team chat. I saw this very infrequently. - Tech trees seem to have been streamlined.Cons:- The grind. I understand this is how the game keeps players playing and this is where the gold is being spent.  Depending on the size of the crew you  may spend around 5 USD to transfer them to a new tank. Why is this important? Because the crew training factors in very strongly in how the tank performs.  It's very easy to spend money here, just like with converting free experience. - Starting in the mid-tiers you will realize that things are becoming expensive.  You will still be able to manage with a free account, but it will become harder and harder.  Playing the game well will strongly influence your bottom line. To a certain degree you will become an accountant in a tank. - Unless you are a very good player, having a premium account may become a necessity at a certain tier, or you will have to continue playing lower tiers. (Which is also why you see a lot of experienced tankers in the lower tiers as a new player.)- It is very easy to get caught up in the wins and losses, especially as there is an in-game financial impact. The game is however most enjoyable when you simply focus on playing well. This can be very frustrating because as an average player you will only influence the number of wins by a few percentage points, because of the team structure of the game.- The game nudges the new player to higher tiers. This is not bad in itself, but it is more expensive to do so. There is a definite dynamic that a new player can "fail up" , and will be very dissatisfied.Overall my review is positive, for these three reasons:a) The game itself is free.b) It has been maintained for a long time, and that in itself should be applauded.c) It is possible to spend very little and have a good time nevertheless.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some basic issues:- Lower levels continually get run over by experienced players slinging gold ammo and using better equipment and attributes. It makes it harder to learn.- The match making is a joke. It's bad and continually creates mismatched teams. Battles of 15 vs 15 end up in overwhelming defeats (about 75% of the time in my case). These are usually 3-15, 15-5, etc... You can't really learn or impact these games. The other 25% of the game is where the fun is... Unfortunately you need to get through 3 out of 4 games to get there. It is frustrating. I've had a number of streaks of 15+ losses or < 30% win rates for a day or more. Many of these will actually lose you in game currency.- To play the upper levels you'll need to use gold ammo (which is purchased with in game currency). In order to generate enough currency to do this, you'll either need to play a lot of lower matches or purchase a tank to make it easier to make credits. Of course, you don't make much on losses and newer players tend to sit around 45% win rate.... The more experienced players will say you don't need to use gold ammo... but amazingly they use it....- The game appears to be balanced using premium ammo. Some of the players have been playing a long time, so slinging gold ammo isn't a burden because their money has built up. This really makes it difficult for new players.- The culture is extremely toxic. Chat is a constant stream of vitriol blaming everyone and their mother for their own stupid decisions. Plan on getting nasty random messages after matches. The forums aren't a lot better.The game is aging and is basically pay to win. If you just want to mess around it can be enjoyable at the lower levels (when some higher level doesn't come in to make some coin and kill a bunch of new players). If you want to progress in the game, expect to spend a lot of time and real money to get and stay at the good part of the game.I may have recommended the game 10 years ago. I wouldn't now.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Tanks is the first and only team-based massively multiplayer online action game dedicated to armored warfare. Throw yourself into the epic tank battles of World War II with other steel cowboys all over the world. Your arsenal includes more than 150 armored vehicles from America, Germany, and the Soviet Union, carefully detailed with historical accuracy. A flexible system of authentic vehicle upgrade and development allows you to try any of the vehicles and weapons in the game. Whether you prefer to exhaust your foes with fast and maneuverable light tanks, make deep breaches in enemy lines with all-purpose medium tanks, use the force of giant tanks to eliminate opposing armored forces, or become a heavy sniper with long-range howitzers, each unit type has its own advantages and can be extremely effective when operated by a true tank ace. But being a great tank commander alone isn't enough to win! In World of Tanks, it's all about teamwork. Victory is achieved by combining your combat skills with those of the other members of your team, each playing their own role on the battlefield. Just add your favorite strategy to build your own iron empire and manifest the indisputable authority of the tank! Feel the tank power!

name: Sons of Valhalla
detailed_description: Sons of Valhalla combines side-scrolling combat with base-building strategy in a beautiful pixel-art Viking Age world. You play as Thorald Olavson, a warrior hell-bent on tracking down the Jarl who burned down his home, kidnapped his beloved, and fled to distant England. Raise a warband, establish strongholds, and personally lead your troops in a grand saga of vengeance. Across the North Sea, far from home, you must first establish a stronghold from which to begin your assault. Hunting your nemesis down will take resources, soldiers, and strategic thinking. Manage a growing economy, establish siege camps and training grounds, raise a massive host, and raid neighboring villages to bolster your resources and push your enemy back. Construct and upgrade a variety of buildings to collect resources, recruit warriors, and upgrade their capabilities and equipment. Elevate your burgeoning villages into powerful strongholds that provide well-armed troops and mighty siege engines. Establish defensive structures as you push further afield – the enemy will not sit idly by in the face of your encroachment, and you can expect conquered border towns to turn into contested battlegrounds. Mercenaries such as pyromaniacs and skilled hunters exclusively available at these towns can turn the tide of battle. With limited resources, planning your expansions and upgrades is of the utmost importance to ensure you have the right soldiers available at any given time. Will you prioritize a larger army of low-tier units? Or will you seek out expensive champions to help forge your path? A sea of swordsmen will fall to enemy archers perched behind stone walls unless upgraded with shields, just as a lone shaman would be swarmed by enemy footmen if left without an escort. Lead your men in tactical combat by issuing orders and utilizing special abilities and formations. But remember – a true warrior leads from the front, so be prepared to take up your sword to fight alongside your men. Recruit a wide array of troops to fight by your side – from basic swordsmen and archers to unique champions such as combat blacksmiths and shieldmaidens, each comes with their own strengths and weaknesses. Success in battle comes from using the right troops for the right situation. Will you utilize the shaman for their healing powers to keep your troops fighting for longer, or is the rapid swinging of the berserker more your speed? Command your troops to overcome evolving situations on the battlefield – order them to fall in line behind you, to charge forward, to retreat, or to form the impregnable shield wall when under a hail of arrows. Quick thinking, positioning, and army composition all play a major role in battle. Break through the enemy shield wall and cut them down with your own blade or become a master of the bow and spear as you destroy your enemy from a distance. Fling flasks of tar and fire, equip powerful runes to embolden your troops, and down flasks of mead to maintain your fortitude as you stand with your men, protect their retreats, and lead their assaults. After a hard battle, while your warriors recover their strength at your strongholds, you can choose to venture alone into the wilderness to find treasure and harry the enemy. Siege engines are needed to take down the mighty fortresses your enemy constructs as well as protect your own. Use catapults and battering rams to smash through gates and walls, and race to destroy the enemy trebuchets raining boulders down upon your forces. You are not alone in your war of vengeance. As you set England ablaze, Odin himself supports your cause with the gift of immortality, and with strength from beyond Midgard to aid you in combat – against armies and their leaders. Acquire powerful runes as you engage in battle and place them on your belts to strengthen your troops, your economy, and even yourself. Unlock more powerful attacks, become a particularly proficient night-raider, or seek out synergies that maximize your warband’s composition at any given time. Will you focus on your melee troops’ health and stamina, your archers’ ability to dodge and fight at night, or your siege engines’ damage and accuracy? Should you fall in battle, Odin will keep you alive to fulfill your destiny – but at a cost. Runes must be sacrificed to continue your journey with each death, and your decision might force you to seek out new strategies as old favorites are weakened with lost runes. From time to time, you will find yourself engaged in single-combat – a web of conspiracy takes you from one enemy leader to another, and only you have the strength to take them down. Balance upgrades to yourself against upgrades for your troops to ensure they are able to assist you in combat without sacrificing your own ability to overcome the enemy champions when faced with a duel – especially against those that fight without honor. An alternate horde mode is available where you lead Thorald Olavson and his troops in wave-based combat that will put your Viking warriors to the test as massive armies clash under your command. Sons of Valhalla is the creation of two brothers with a passion for pixel art and the Viking Age. In-between the conquest and swordplay, we hope you will enjoy the little touches – the look of the buildings, the ducks swimming on water, your canine companion, and the general atmosphere as days turn to nights, sunshine to storms.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it in 10 hours (with the new game + content), this game is a clone of Kingdom: Two Crowns with one major change in the gameplay: you can fight and you have to assault bases. What it does well: - Pixel Art is great- Boss fights are interesting, although a bit too easy- Shooting arrows and headshooting enemies is satisfying- The runes are a nice mechanicWhat it does not do well:- Be a clone of KingdomSee, the Kingdom concept is unique and its interest lies in the fact that you are always preparing to defend. Only towards the end game, you must start counter-attacking. In Sons of Valhalla, being the offender is more important than defending. In fact, you can probably play the whole game without being attacked once if you play aggressively. The other thing that I found wasnt done better than Kingdom was the building aspect; in Kingdom the fact that you can't build where you want is a fun part of the game, and forces you to expand sometimes in places faraway from your townhall, which often leads to some issues. In SoV, you always get the same layout for a base, which makes it a bit boring.I recommend it because I think it's a fun experience, but as you may have noticed, I find Kingdom much better. if you can afford it, buy both, and play SoV first.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: Very rarely do I find myself refunding a game, this is one of those times. In its current state I cannot recommend this game. The controls are clunky and restricted, built with a controller in mind instead of a whole keyboard and with no options to make them feel any better. The balance is way off from anything that feels good to play, I found myself more than once wondering what the game even wanted from me in order to succeed.Then you have the bugs, several times I found myself wondering why my men weren't attacking or following me, only to find that they were actually dead but visually still standing. But sometimes they were alive, and just not interested in any of my orders, standing still in a field getting murdered by enemies in melee range of them.In its current state this is the most early access feeling game I have ever bought at a full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on launch. I'm a big fan of the kingdom series.The pixel graphics look great, blood and fire in particular. The music is ok, although I have a feeling I would get tired of it after 10+ hours. The story is very simple and sadly completely unexciting.First couple of hours of this game seems amazing - you have a bit more control over your troops than in Kingdom series, the idea of conquering villages on the map seems fun… till the point when you discover that on every map you have to do the same thing. Each village is the same, builds up the same, every camp has the same mercenaries. You conquer each part of the map in the same way that got boring after 4 hours. I got to map 3 just to see if there will be anything different and sadly I was very disappointed. Later in a game you get to experiment with different units but that's pretty much it. If you played this game for a couple of hours - you saw everything it has to offer.Sadly, I was expecting more for 17$ game.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to base my opinion of one game on my experience with another, but the only reason I got this game is that it looks like it takes a lot of inspiration from the Kingdom series. The short way to describe this game to me would be - Kingdom, but a MOBA instead of a Tower Defence game.A one-dimentional MOBA is what Sons Of Valhalla feels like for the most part. You walk back and forth around in your camp, gather supplies, prepare your army and then attack and conquer the enemy bases one by one.The game also features a combat system that's inspired by the Dark Souls series with invincible rolls and a stamina bar that you have to keep an eye on. I was personally more interested in the tactical aspect of the game so the boss fights felt more like chore to me for the most part. Also, having the ability to fight through enemy hordes on my own with no warriors by my side weakened the joy of the game's tactical aspect.That's the game's main campaign mode. You travel between 5 different stages and go through a simple but effective "save the princess" story with beautifully drawn pixel art cutscenes and pretty good voice acting.The game has two other play modes:1. A stealth game called "Raya's Escape" where you play as the princess trying to escape her prison, which I personally found to be very clunky to play as it doesn't feel great to use the game's default controls for accurate character movement. Also, the game froze every time I got captured and I had to restart at the tutorial so I lost my patience very fast.2. A horde mode where you have one base and get waves of enemies coming at set intervals. The fact that you can't interact with your base at all while getting attacked makes this mode frustrating. And it leans heavily on the game's combat mechanics rather than it's tactical aspects.To sum up, Sons of Valhalla is a fun, short game that mixes tactics with action in a rather simple yet enjoyable package. It leaves a few things to be desired; Maybe multiplayer co-op or PvP; Maybe a better survival mode where you're getting attacked from both directions except for just the right side of the screen; but it's definitely a worthwhile experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game on the hardest difficulty possible, not having ever played it before. It took me a little over 11 hours. Quite frankly, I saw this game on Summer Games Fest, it looked exactly like what I wanted the Kingdom games to be. Especially after seeing how far Kingdom: Two Crowns went. A Kingdom style game where you get to fight yourself and not only that, but also over the course of a full campaign. That's what I was hoping for, like a lot of other people... And like all those other people, I've been left disappointed.This was my experience with the game, playing on the hardest difficulty possible, out of the 5 levels in this game (which is already far too little for linear gameplay), the only one that was actually challenging, was the second level. Which is both hilarious and sad. The reason it was hard? Enemy healers. They get introduced in Level 2, and after level 2 are never seen again. Which is the stupidest thing ever, seeing as introducing an enemy type and keeping it there in order to make the levels more difficult would actually create much more tension and engagement. The GameplayQuite frankly, it was way too easy. I expected to start in the middle of the map, having to build my way out on both sides while getting pummeled. This did not happen. In every single map, you start on the left, and need to make your way to the very right. This removes exploration and the rewarding of it. Unlike Kingdom, there is no day and night cycle. What does this mean? Even though you get certains buffs from runes at night, enemies attack at any time and in small waves. There also seems to be little to no upscale in attacks. So, you can pretty much take as long as you want to upgrade everything and as long as you're next to your tower to keep hack & slashing away at enemy to help out your troops, you will literally never be overrun. As for buildings in this game, they make no sense. There's a whole building dedicated to only Shamans (healers), which is stupid to me. Same with archers and Blacksmiths btw. Which I guess are tank units? I'm not sure. Then the siege weapon shop focuses on both a battering ram and Catapult. I guess that makes sense. But then the barracks host 3 different unit types. Grunt? Shield Maiden and Berserker. What's the point of Shield Maiden? Couldn't tell you, they die just as fast as grunts. What's the point of Berserkers? Couldn't tell you, they are identical to Blacksmiths, working as a Tank unit. There's only 2 resource buildings in the game, Lumber and Food. Which is a shame because, if you're gonna start implementing a variety of resources... maybe add cool things that are gained by capturing enemy camps? Like an Iron or Silver mine? Anyway, overall the buildings make no sense and with 7 different unique buildings, every town only having 6 build slots is just annoying and also kinda weird given how the buildings are divided up.As for your character, you can die as many times as you want, as long as you have runes. Runes give you abilities and every time you die, you need to sacrifice 1 rune. I think you can have up to a total of like 30 runes? So the sacrifice becomes redundant by like level 3. To me at least. My character was so powerful at level 3 that the only way to die was to just stand there and take the damage. I had infinite stamina, my dodges did damage and... that's pretty much it. I could just dodge back and forth until an entire army was dead. Even the bosses couldn't hurt me. Anything I got after that was extra. So yeah, the combat and town management is disappointing aka the whole game. "But what about the story?" you ask... not sure why. I wrote this review fully by the time you're reading it. Stop talking to your screen!The story is paraphrased for obvious reasons:Ooga Booga viking guy's wife is kidnapped (And his father is killed, but don't worry, after the first level this is never mentioned again so I guess vikings mourn quick).We go to England to chase down the dude who kidnapped her! Aaaaand we die at sea. We live... We live? WE LIVE! Nope, that's Odin. We're dead and in Asguard. Odin says you are special because "reasons" so he's giving you infinite lives because (Reasons are never explained. Which seems to be a staple of this game). "Now go warrior! Fullfill your destiny!" Oki. So we high five Heimdall on the way out. Fall through the bifrost bridge because it's not up to code and we're back on midgard. (The rest of the game, everytime you respawn at asgard there is no more unique dialogue. The starting interaction is pretty much all we get.) Que intro level. It's super easy. Your old teacher is the only other guy who survived the shipwreck. He reminds you how not to die using only his walking cane. Okay gandalf, calm down. You fight your way to the right side of the map... this is literally only gameplay. You get to the boss. Viking McGee "Haha, your princess is in another castle. Also I killed your dad!" *Sticks out Tongue like a fully bearded buff 9 year old*. And you kill him. On to the next level. You get a super short intro where Brother Tuck from Robin Hood finds out that your princess is already being taken to another castle. What purpose does this serve other than making the player feel useless this entire level? No clue. Queue  the hardest level in the game because healers. You kill brother tuck, you didn't find any puppers *Sad* and next level. A mercenary.Side Note: I think there was a bear hunter mini boss in this level. I killed it, found a chained up bear, freed it thinking I would have a super cool pet bear for life like the viking badass and I am! No... the moment its free, it runs into an enemy wall and kills itself... Welp sad.Anywho, final boss, kill the mercenary who has a kink for feeding people to his dogs. You defeat him, princess is in another castle. Also you let him be eaten by dogs. NEXT LEVEL. An Obese Knight riding a horse who looks to be in pain. I don't like animal abuse so I don't see the joke but YAY. We fight our way through to him, we're in his arena. "Princess is in the final castle with the king" okay? Kill the dudes horse (It was a mercy kill). Then kill him. The next level is the last level and doesn't even have a starting cutscene like previous levels. (For how little story there is, that's practically a crime). We fight our way through. It turns out the king is not the king but it's Loki. And he's overly Flamboyant? Not sure what that is about. In order to free his daughter... Hel. From her prison... the Norse Mythology version of Hell (I KNOW, SHOCKING) he has to kill your girl and the king who's lying on the ground barely alive I guess? You fight loki. He's honestly the hardest fight in the game because he has a ranged attack. Finally you fight his daughter Hel, who you can easily defeat without being hit once. You grab your girl, escape the castle, it appears she has some kinda Loki Necklace. You get an Ominous "To be continued..." and that's it.Most prominent bugs:These bugs were a huge letdown and should've definitely been taken care of before the game released.The pathing of archers is broken when you have more than 5. Because a tower is already filled up at the front line, they'll go back to try and fill up a redundant tower further in the back of the map. Unless you're walking back and forth over the entire map not using fast travel, you won't find them.The Mercenaries you can hire up to a maximum of 3 due to there being 3 smaller camps in every full map, once ordered to attack, will always spawn on the attack when having died and rehired. This can only be prevented by ordering them to follow you and then ordering them to hold still.Units with upgraded HP sometimes spawn with their base HP and have to be healed to max.In 4 out of 5 levels, the final base had no unit buildings and was without enemies to defend it. Super Anti-Climactic.I would not recommend this game. It needed more work, forethought and care than it got.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the entire game in ten hours. If I could go back in time, I wouldn't spend money on it. I hoped it would be a more complex version of the Kingdom series of games, since I love strategy builders. But Sons of Valhalla is more of a 2D action arcade game. The building, command, and strategy aspects of the game are repetitious, and you can beat each level with the same strategy of . On top of that, the campaign ending is a cliff hanger, setting up a sequel, which I found unsatisfying. Seeing the end of the story is probably the only reason I finished the end of the game.Buy it if you like 2D action arcade games. Otherwise, skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really unsure whether to give this a yes or no. The game starts pretty fun and there's definitely a ton of potential there.However...my experience (on hard mode) was not really good later on. And by later on, i mean just on the second stage.Basically, your character is pretty damn weak, and you can kinda cheese enemies with your power attacks to kill them, but that gets tedious. Since your troops are nearly entirely useless, you have to do all the work yourself, which means, 80% of your time is spent cheesing enemies with power attacks. The other 20% is you running back home recruiting more troops, and you usually can't because they cost too much resources and you just don't make enough.So the balance is off entirely, and it makes the gameplay worse. The whole point of this game is to recruit soldiers and send them to war, but your soldiers are useless so that defeats this point entirely.I'll give this a Yes, the dev put a lot of effort in this game and it has potential. I'll revisit it in a few months and if it didn't improve substantially it'll change to a No.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it kingdom two crowns? No. It is similar in the amount of attention it takes to play the game and in that the pixel art is very pretty and also you are constantly fighting to expand your territory. I enjoy upgrading myself and my soldiers and unlocking new weapons and abilities through new buildings and runes found after defeating enemies. The boss fights are simple but fun and actually that's a good way to describe the whole game.On the down side however the story so far has been meh and I probably wouldn't miss it if they got rid of it completely. Upgrading anything takes time for some reason, even once you have more than enough to pay the costs for the upgrades the upgrades themselves sometimes take a good 2 to 3 minutes to go through and wont apply retroactively to any of your units. Also because you are limited to a certain amount of manpower that all units count towards if your units aren't cutting it in their current state you will need to send them off to die and then wait for replacements which will probably leave you vulnerable to the never ending stream of enemies. Still its roughly what I wanted when I bought it but not quite worth what I paid for it, wait for a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "I wish I could give it a neutral rating" games. I'm grudgingly giving it a thumbs up since I feel like I did get my money's worth out of it (I bought it on sale.)The graphics are really nice if you like pixel art. It's not even pretending not to steal Kingdom's presentation style, which is fine by me!The gameplay is different than Kingdom's in various ways, but also less interesting in various ways. Combat is the main activity, and upgrading buildings and training troops is secondary. Basically you go out, kill enemies, collect resources, upgrade your buildings and grow a small army, then attack and claim the next enemy position. It's not a terrible game loop and definitely works on paper, but it gets pretty grindy and repetitive.It's also missing the sense of exploration that Kingdom has, and the pacing is fairly flat - there are waves of enemies, but they're less distinct than in Kingdom and come in a  relatively steady stream. They also aren't foreshadowed nearly as effectively in Sons of Valhalla - the setting sun doesn't mean much of anything, for example - in Kingdom you're constantly racing against the sun, trying to figure out how much you can get done before night because that's when you're going to get swarmed by enemies.There are a lot of collectible upgrades for the buildings and for your character, but most of them are just buffs to stats (for you or your troops) with the occasional new combat mechanic. Nothing terribly interesting, but it's somewhat fun trying to choose which upgrades to keep and which to discard. It also has boss fights with story beats as you move between regions on the map. The boss fights literally feel a little flat as well - I was wishing for some jumping gameplay during these.I did get hooked for a couple days, though. It's a linear game, and I got about halfway through before getting bored. I might finish it at some point, but I'm not in a big rush.If you're looking for something with a different take on the Kingdom formula and don't mind grinding, it's worth checking out, at least on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of Valhalla is visually stunning, a ton of fun - thought a little on the short side. Visuals are a big seller for this. They are excellent. The dev’s passion for pixel art really shines through and there’s a staggering attention to detail around the world. The landscapes, lighting, animations - they’re all really impressive. In terms of gameplay, the easiest reference point for this would be Kingdom - though this puts a greater focus on playing the offensive. Build siege weapons and lay into enemy Strongholds, burning them to the ground. Then, build a vastly more superior Viking settlement in its place and keep your war machine turning. There’s some character development in the form of runes - and these can enable ways to play by strengthening your abilities, as well as providing boosts to your units and towns. As you go, you’ll amass a warband to pillage your way across England - and you can organise them with formations. Nothing super in-depth here. Attack, follow or form a shield wall. The shield wall is the usual go to, because it’s awesome. If enemies get too close, the front warrior will break out and push the enemy back, which is a nice touch. The campaign is the main game mode, and whilst fun and well paced, a lot of the boss fights felt a bit easy (though I was only playing on normal difficulty). Outside of the campaign you’ve got the horde mode - an endless base defence variation. Though this doesn’t utilise the base expansion and sieging mechanics of the campaign. Which is strange, ‘cos I saw those as the standout mechanics. My future wishlist involves some kind of random skirmish mode that fuses the gameplay of the campaign with the endlessness of horde mode - because currently the game does feel a bit light on content. The dev does give some hints that there is more to come, so hopefully something in that area gets added. ‘Cos right now, that’s the only thing that’s stopping me from shouting from the rooftops and telling everyone to buy this game. If you don’t care about that though, and you just want a Viking story to blast through and set aside for a while, I’d say you’re getting 8 to 12 very enjoyable hours out of this. Also there are dogs. And yes, you can pet them. Even the magic god-dogs. How lovely.Video Review - [Edit - added video link]

_childDocuments_.review: Good little side-scroller with a bit of troop management. You push though different levels taking encampments held by variety of troops depending on the location using a hero and his army while building up a base as you go along. You also unlock abilities and runes which can help buff your style of play though there isn't a huge variety.Three aspects to the game:Hero - you attack enemies with sword, use consumables and special powersArmy - You have a squad of troops to support your attacks on the enemiesManagement - You build a base, upgrade troops and collect runes which provide buffs to the hero, army and resource gainsNow to address some of the complaints which appear to be a bit overblown.1. Bugs - A lot of these have been resolved and feedback is being taken on board by the developers which resulted in buffing certain troops(like more damage on siege and improved behaviour for healers) and even moving a stealth mission out of the main campaign.2. Depth - Some people seem to be expecting a game with the complexity of Starcraft 2 on a side-scrolling video game you will be disappointed. The commands are attack, defend and follow me; don't expect the option to encircle in a 2D game, You are a hero first, army leader second.3. Grind - I don't think I waited longer than a minute for resources, you even unlock point where you can trade resources. You push with the army you have, fight a bit(you get silver from killing enemies) and than pull back to spend the resources when you have them. You don't have to turtle in the first base waiting for resources to get every upgrade.4. Length - Took me about 6 hours on normal difficulty, an opinion on this if this is too short for you money is subjective, for example I think Assassins Creed Origins was 95% filler while another mate loved every second.Overall I get the impression people imagined this to be a game where your 80% army leader and 20% fighting as a hero when its more the other way around. I was similarly disappointed too but, I didn't let it stop me from enjoying the game.Feedback to the devs would be lean into the leading an army aspect if you make a future game and maybe a unit encyclopedia.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is playable, the bugs aren't too bad (very few), and the game is what it says it is: a base building action roguelite.Buuuuut....This game is shallow. There's 5 basic levels and you rinse/repeat the same strategem to defeat each level. Build order is roughly the same, unit types should be roughly the same, enemies, albeit with some slight variation in type, die roughly the same with the same amount of effort. If you beat the first level, just know that the next 4 are beaten identically, with the exception to the boss fights at the end of each level. These too are inconsequential after the 2nd map. That's because you get so powerful that it gets really hard to die. In boss fights, if all else fails, Then, I have to address the story. It's basically just Super Mario Bros. Oh no, your wife is stolen! Where is she? Is she at the end of this level? No? Next castle? OK! At the last castle you don't even get a kiss really. While I'm not exactly sandbagging on this game's story foibles, I am using it as an example as to how shallow the game is. Everything from the mechanics to the storyline is just so utterly based. I put in my time, beat the game, got my money's worth I guess... but it's not a game I'll come back to down the road for a trip down memory lane. At most, I'll see this title in my list of uninstalled games and go, "Oh gods, not again!"

_childDocuments_.review: This is the case when you don’t expect anything special from such a small indie game, but it turns into several pleasant and meditative evenings. I found out about this game literally by accident a few days before its release and I must admit that I love these types of games: a slow, slightly hardcore 2D strategy in a medieval setting with economic management and battles.Moreover, the price of the game was a very pleasant surprise, so this is what I can say based on the results of several hours of play.Advantages:— Relaxing and simple gameplay with interesting mechanics and relaxing gameplay;— Pleasant, not annoying music;— Interesting visual effects;— Cool combat system coupled with army management;— Voiced dialogues (pleasantly surprised, from such projects you don’t expect anything other than subtitles);— Low price;— Simple, but engaging plot.Flaws:— Pixel graphics (not too critical, but I’m more of a fan of classic 2D animation, so if you like it, then it is not a problem for you);— It is recommended to take breaks, this is not a game that can be completed from start to finish in one sitting;— No multiplayer (maybe it will appear in the future?);- Low replay value: you beat the campaign once and then you can play the Horde mode, but I think it can get boring quickly;— Some mechanics are missing I guess: for example, remote training of units, tracking their number by type of warriors and etc.- The story campaign is quite short.I understand that maybe the game's cons may confuse you more than its advantages, but in this case I would say again that I like the genre and setting, and the advantages of the game once again convinced me that the purchase is worth the money, especially , if you buy the game at a discount.In addition, it has achievements, and especially for those who are achievement hunters, I have prepared a special guide that will help you unlock all the achievements in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: This desperately needs balance. Almost fully upgraded sword doing next to no damage to literally anything, including barricades. An arrow tho? Absolutely obliterates everything with no upgrades. Your units will do more damage, take more damage, and have more stamina than you. Runes make no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sense in their tiers and I often find normal runes way more valuable than rare or epic runes. The game is constantly telling me to upgrade my units to be competitive but they're already almost maxed. Now I'm raided so often i can't even produce enough units to push them back. Something is way way off here, it's a sweet idea being totally soured by a very bad execution
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, my opinion would be a neutral vote. Its an "ok" game, it has some pros and cons. It seems like it could have some potential, and I did enjoy building up my skill set, upgrades, the units, and buildings. I didn't mind the 75 wave scenario (became a bit of a joke after doing the same thing over and over) and the escape scenario was ok. I tried to challenge myself for the heck of it and beat it on hard and hell modes.My biggest complaint would probably be that 2nd boss in the game, and maybe I'm bad at it, but for whatever reason I just hate fighting this boss. It's just nothing but a fat HP boss that blocks all your projectiles and you would do little damage with the small openings you get with your sword.  I tried to even compare these bosses on hell mode, and the 2nd boss was still the hardest boss for me because I waste too much time doing little damage with low stats and upgrades. Every other boss was easily shot down with projectiles or whacked to death; it feels like a boss you got too early in the game. Just about every other boss was a joke and I easily breezed through them.Glitches, I did run into 2 situations I was confused on that made me have to stop the game: 1) Getting caught with Raya doesn't reset back to the start or a saved location, it just gets stuck there on me and I had to manually go back to main menu and start her again2) I had a funny case where I shot the whip hound boss to death and it got stuck because the boss wouldn't move to the middle of the map, so I just ended up redoing the boss fight again.The AI for your troops could definitely use some tweaking because I waste time trying to arrange for a shield, archer, catapult, healer setup for outposts and my healers always run into the front lines to get themselves killed instead of staying in the back. Shield wall always takes my archers off the outposts, and my healers aren't far enough in the back. I had weird cases when I told my troops to attack and they kept running to the next camp after one was taken over instead of defending it first.Other than possibly moving the boss fighting styles around, I would recommend giving the ability to keep your rune set for just the endless mode gameplay so you don't waste too much time with RNG shuffles and not deleting the save file after beating it. I couldn't play the game on the keyboard and mouse because it became taxing for my wrists and fingers, so I ended up playing with the controller instead despite the horrible analog aim with arrows, it was still manageable. I would say only buy the game if it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be the first to say I haven't played much of this, but for my review I didn't need to. Right off this bat, this is a new game that did not have a keyboard in mind. Simple QOL things such as using WASD to control the units in the shift menu would make this quite a bit better. The lack of forethought on this, though, turns me off heavily. I'd almost prefer the simple 2 commands of "attack or defend"That said, they do let you pet dogs, which I can appreciate them taking the time to add in. Not every game does it, but they should.It is heavily inspired by Kingdom: New Lands. And that's a fine thing. However it feels more like I'm being forced as the player to do the battles rather than creating an army and launching it forward. I don't know if it's just a slower gameplay style or what but I find myself charging headfirst at the enemy because I have nothing I can do in my base as I slowly wait for resources to accumulate. Not a bad thing in and of itself, it's just not what I'm interested in as a player.Enemies are unique and have what I can only call minibosses defending their bases. I like the concept. I wish the gates weren't such a pain to break down, making the early game a crawl, but I can appreciate it from a balance perspective.As far as the value you're getting as a game, I think $20 is a fair price tag but sadly I just didn't enjoy my time which is the biggest reason I'm downvoting. I just feel it's more a test of patience then a back and forth struggle.Edit 6/3/24 Changing this to positive because the Dev's have said they're taking the time to fix the issues. We'll see where this review lies afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me feeling mixed but I will have to not recommend it at the $20 price point.The game has its charming artstyle and the viking theme which is always positive.  Obviously ti is drawing heavily from the kingdom series in its gameplay.While the game is entertaining its hard to say its fun.  its pretty repetitive and the combat isn't super interesting.  The melee combat is basically a death sentence if you get anywhere near a mob of enemies, which makes sense as the game wants you to play by making an army.  However it seemed to fail to take into account that it was going to make you a god of long range combat by giving you multiple arrow types, fire pots, and grease pots.  You can instakill every non boss enemy by just throwing grease on them, followed by anything fire based.  Grease will also cover multiple enemys meaning mobs are now not an issue, the only thing actually stopping you being walls.So the melee in general gameplay is a bust and spamming your ranged utility basically kills everything.  So how about the bosses? Fun character designs but after the first one or two its pretty boring.  They all follow the same design as each other.  They do some light hits and the occasional big hit in much the same fashion as each other.  They have different ranges on the attacks and might mix it up with some unique boss specific gemmic but they all go down the same.  Unlock teh javalin and arrows, then just pepper them to death. Your sword doesn't do enough damage to justify the risk/reward of it when you can just hit them in the head with a javelin and chunk their hp bar.  Which only gets to be more problematic the longer the game goes on as you just get more javs and fire arrows.The rune system is interesting but a bit dull and random.  it would have been nice to destroy ones you don't want to get better versions of ones you do. Getting legendary ram damage doesn't help when I have no interest in using the ram.  The option to pick major ability runes is very nice though, but some are just worse than others.  Doing tiny rolling damage isn't going to top firing a giant arrow that pierces everyone on screen.  Also the melee rune that is supposed to swing a bunch was very random for me to activate.  I tries to do what the description said with attacking and/or moving multiple times in the same direction but it was just not reliably triggering.  Likely I was doing something wrong but the melee in the game is so dangerous who really cares.The shield blocking damage is nice and very good against archers.  However against normal small swordsmen it felt completely useless.  They attack rapidly and repeatably so a group of them would basically give no time to drop your guard and attack them.  It also lost its use against most posses since again, range spam was just the better option.  Why guard fairly quick animation attacks from bosses when i can just roll away and throw more javs.The story is fine and generic.  Save your wife with the help of Odin.  Nothing interesting and the game could have done with more development of the bosses beyond the short speach they give at the start of combat.  Spoiler warning for the rest of the game though. Last thing I want to talk is the extra content of the story of the wife's escape and endless mode.  The escape is irrelevant as a story since if you play the main game you already know the outcome, and if you haven't played the main game then why would you care.  Its a generic stealth section, the animations are cute and well done as is the atmosphere of the area.  Beyond that the gameplay is slow and uninteresting.  It adds nothing new to the story and doesn't reveal much about her character so its not worth the time honestly.  The endless mode isn't that fun.  The only thing that really saved this game was having lots of ranged options and some fun abilities, the endless mode takes that away.  Unless you really enjoyed just watching your soldiers smack guys while you do hardly anything besides plink away with your piddly bow then its an easy pass.A pretty game with a fun concept that just fails on the execution on being anything special.  If it drops to 10-15 bucks I could recommend it for people that really like the kingdom series and want combat in that type of game.  Which I feel like is a somewhat limited audience.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok, narration is pretty solid and art style is beautiful, but that's all it really has going for it. Combat is repetitive and requires no real challenge; it's just spam as many units and overpower your enemies with maxing out buildings. The excitement quickly fades once you realize this almost £20 game ends after roughly 8 hours.Choosing various builds and messing around with what does and doesn't work, well it doesn't, since the enemy spams you constantly with a near-infinite wave every few seconds, leaving you no breathing time to plan what builds you need for each outpost.I was hoping that it would be like a traditional RTS in the sense that careful planning would be the key to winning, but I found myself winning almost every time. It was just pure spam, spam a bunch of warriors, archers, and then focus resources to max buildings and boom, you automatically win, which for me was a letdown since for every second you're focusing on buildings, you're losing outpost after outpost.Unfortunately, while playing, I amassed a decent amount of pretty good runes, but even with some in my slot, the main protagonist is still extremely weak, being knocked on the floor constantly and using all my healing items in the span of a few seconds. Overall, it was just extremely frustrating.During my playthrough, I also encountered a bug. After 30 minutes, I retreated back to resupply and upgrade, only to realize the game wouldn't let me fast travel back to my captured outpost and lost all my progress, which after that is both discouraging and why I've opted for a refund
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: You have seen it before. The same re-textured and dumbed-down, slowed-down, "Kingdom Two Crowns" gameplay that adds nothing new to the table, making it more or less a chore to continue playing for hours while you wait for resources to appear so you may send in your units to capture the objectives and repeat the process. Kingdom Two Crowns was a fantastic game until the developers became complacent and simply re-skinned the same game play over and over again under the guise of creating something new with Eighties and the others, the majority of which could have been DLC. Sons of Valhalla didn't feel like the other developers' attempts. It felt worse, with less interaction. You're waiting around for so long just to receive your resources; you're not accumulating gold by interacting with the homeless and raising them as civilians or offering you activities to keep you entertained; you're literally standing still waiting for resources to appear before building units, sending them out, and sieging. It's quite bland. Yes, there are some commands for your units, using different formations, but that's not engaging enough. It's just less substance compared to Two Crowns, which should have been changed in a positive way. The gameplay is repetitious, using the same strategies, waiting, sieging and repeating the process over and over again. Not fun at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is great. This is a much better Kingdom, because here we still develop our character, something I missed in Kingdom. Our character can be improved and can collect runes, especially those that work at night - a brilliant idea. But game has one drawback. It's terribly short. I completed the basic plot in 10 hours, and I did everything to extend the game. Overall, you can easily complete it in 8 hours. The second problem is repeatability. The next maps apart from the bosses differ only in that you have one new unit. The city's development could be greater. We only have three levels of the city and three levels of building development in the city. Not too much. The same with units, only three levels of development. Very nice game world. The plot is ultimately cool too. The difficulty level is excellent, but with a small problem. Once you have developed the first city to the maximum, you can conquer the next ones by moving like a battering ram. I had a great time, but once again it was too short.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game to you? No. If you want it, wait for a sale.I played it for about 4 hours and I'm unable to continue. I feel like this game is trying to be a jack of many genres but in the end it's master of none. The combat and controls don't feel good. The interaction with your surroundings is not smooth. The story is straight up cringy and boss fights are tediously long. All in all I would say that it's a decent game. It's just not good enough to invest my time into.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, Hooded Horse, why would you do this to Yourselves with this one? My Favourite Publisher, you have just stained the banner of well sifted titles in your portfolio with this production. It is far inferior to Kingdoms series as it fails to keep interest for longer than few hours of quite mindless button mashing, slash, roll, slash, block...shoot...go replenish and over again. I have hoped for expanding the idea heavily inspired by the aforementioned but it lacks the punch, very repetitive gameplay loop, weak units, no real tactics or economy, no unit progression just expensive upgrades not really improving survivability of the hero or your troops, thus rendering you super unworthy Odin's favour :) All that makes the whole run grindy and not immensely fun. Combat and base building feel shallow, just three levels that unlock artificial caps on settlement development and unit numbers which you will be eternally spamming for the glory of Odin... The game feels defeated by its own concepts, even the rune system is off, percentage buffs (lazy idea) or extra power attacks (this part is neat) leaves you with obvious choices to spark some extra action out of monotonous routine. Sadly, I can't recommend it to people who value their time, I can't refund now but it is a good candidate to do so in my books. Also, Hooded Horse, please don't fool me again with so deliciously crafted joke :)

_childDocuments_.review: Figured I'd write a review after the first level to help this game get some traction.First, TLDR: This is quite fun and the pixel graphics and environments quite good. 8/10 overall.It's not the same kind of game, but the graphics and setting evoke Defender of the Crown, especially the sword fighting in DOTC.It's challenging to play to me. I decided to play on easy, although I usually try to play normal mode for my first go through. I kept dying on normal so I dialed it back. If you get easily frustrated, you might want to try the first level on easy before restarting the game or starting a new one and going to normal.Now the big question, value. I don't think they could price this game much differently; it's $20 in the US. I think it's worth it. If this game had come out on Amiga in the 80s it would be a total classic. I'll say what I always say, if you can afford to support smaller publishers and projects, it's good to do. You don't get as much bang for your buck as with many huge budget games, but this is a niche product.I'll update my review when (if) I finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The experience starts off promising enough with solid music, lovely graphics, and a gripping narrative. The gameplay is everything you've seen in Kingdom/Kingdom: Two Crowns/Kingdom: Eighties with a twist in that you directly control the protagonist with the ability to actively participate in battles as well as singles combat boss fights between you and the enemey commander.Where it starts to fall apart is in terms of performance, glitches, and a narrative that quickly becomes the rote tried and true guaranteed to garner attention obligatory "the church is evil and incompetent and christians are bad" sort you can't throw a rock without hitting.Not really, it's just the usual stand-in that either garners attention because of the likes it gets you or keeps people talking because of the distaste around the story.By order of the church for some unknown reason your tribe is attacked and your father killed, yoru wife abducted and taken to England where the church has her hostage but also is incompetent in their wrongdoings and loses her and all the other women in town to a brigand.Odin has seen fit to offer you divine protection in exchange for runes so that when you fall in battle Valhalla will be denied you until you rescue her. Why your wife is a macguffin the church wants is held close to the chest, ultimately your journey is about your viking warrior cutting a bloody swath through England to get her back.It is, though it doesn't do a great job of communicating what it needs from you. If you've played the Kingdom series you've played this, which isn't a bad thing since it gives you an easy way to get up to speed quickly an doesn't take long to introduce you to what's new.The tutorial is quick and doesn't throw too much at you which is a welcome change from titles that either frontload way too much information or tell you next to nothing.You'll spend fish and wood to upgrade your facilities and hire warriors, you'll conquer smaller outposts that offer the ability to exchange wood or fish for hacksilver, you'll spend gold to get upgrades specific for your warrior, and your goal is to battle your way across each map until reaching the enemy commander for your shodown.Your warrior is pretty squishy so you'll need to be careful, but you'll gain abilities to mitigate this from random rune drops.Combat is simplistic but calculatedly intense leading to you having to carefully balance trying to help your soldiers while keeping yourself alive. That said, most of this difficult goes away when you realize your soldiers are way more powerful than you so you just keep sending scads of them ahead while you just chill at base camp.Also, if you're ever in danger of dying you can run back to camp and get your health and supplies back while your troops keep fighting, then jog back over to help.Boss fights break up the usual combat experience, but their AI is sorely lacking (I spent the first fight hitless going "slash slash roll slash slash roll slash slash roll" until the boss died). Still, it's another area where SoV tries to do more than just be a reskinned Kingdom.It does it's job. It's not like coming away from Axiom of Maria where you'll be humming the tunes all day, but it's fitting medieval fantasy fair.It's not the worst experience, but do expect crashes. In addition, I experienced instances where I would trade but not get my supplies, my fishermen would just stand around not gathering fish, my troops wouldn't follow orders, and I experienced difficulty getting the game to let me pick up rune drops.It's far from the glitchiest experience I played this year, but between that and the weird performance drops it doesn't feel ready for prime time.Not horrible, but not great. On Desktop you'll experience random crashes and sporadic lag spikes, on the Steam Deck your framerate will fluctuate wildly; even at full TDP you're lucky to be in the low forties and will frequently be in the low thirties or less for a game that absolutely should not demand that much in the way or resources.The dev has pledged to provide updates to improve performance and address glitches, so these issues will likely see some attention in the days to come.It's a nay for me; the game does a few things to be more than Kingdom 2: Viking Boogaloo, but not a ton. The loop isn't necessarily bad, but it's not particularly satisfying. The narrative is rote and derivative, the maps are the same thing in different places, and your troops are so strong you don't really need to be there which in turn just makes this a glitchier and less performant version of Kingdom for the time being.Your mileage may vary, but as for me, this just made me want to go back and finish Kingdom: Eighties.
_childDocuments_.name: Sons of Valhalla

_childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews have either bloated expectations or are just a case of git gud. People see a price tag of anything higher than 10$ and expect 40 hrs of some kind of life changing experience. 20$ gets you an 8hr ish campaign and a mode that is unlimited to play as much as you want. Let's look at this games "competitor" Kingdom Two crowns. Also 20$....Hmmmmm.....Considering this is a better game, the pricing is more than fair. I love Kingdom, but the time you'd spend running back and forth in that game, is spent being a viking warrior in this game.I am playing on hard, the enemies are NOT overpowered, and you have ample time to prepare for the bosses at the end of the level. People are just bad. Dodge, use your shield, stack runes, it's really not that hard. Sheesh. I see people saying "spam does the work", when in my experience, my soldiers just hang back most of the time looking like chads in the shield wall, and I kill everything. If you're just sitting at base spamming troops that sounds miserable. Use fire pots to incinerate whole armies with your bois instead. Did you know you can headshot bosses? (fire should work on bosses but doesn't!)If you liked the "Kingdom" games you will like this, if you don't like that game play loop you won't. Simple as. Some guy wrote about how the tactical decisions are limited, but if you look at the "tactical combat" under the about page on the game, it literally lists each command you can give. So why are you surprised? The developers aren't overselling anything, they literally list everything you can do tactically on the steam page. What more tactical depth do you want? Flanking? Terrain? It's a side scroller bro. lol. This game is taking the "Kingdom" formula and stepping in the right direction.

The campaign is repetitive with basically very little unlocks (the last boss of the campaign doesn't even unlock an option?) so you end up doing the same thing over and over again.I was waiting for this for a long time, am a little disappointed in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Now finished my first run of the game on Hard and here is my Feedback:The game mechanic is straight foward, start small, start buildig your base, recrut units and capture the next base.In each small camp awaits you a mini boss, at the end of each stage is an boss battle.Since the game is more action focused, your skills to block and doge attacks are more importan than strategic planing, since you can't take your units with you into the boss battle.The stage clearing started with my playstyle pretty slow, till i got my upgrades and after that keep pushig. That felt a bit repetitive thats why i was so happy about the stealth mission after clearing stage 3. Its a nice change in the mission pattern.After that is back to main mechanic, build your base, upgrade, push for more baseOn you way to clear stages, you are able to find runes to imporve yourself or your units/buldings. Each stage has an altar where you can find a godly rune. Personaly i think there could use an little twerke since only 1-2 feeled powerful enough. strangely , you can upgrade your rune belt to carry 6 of them, but i only find 5.In all its a nice game for in between and with the promise for more conent ( and fast patches after release ) i can recomend it

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels lacking like an early access title. (But isn't)Issues:==========================================================================1. The base building feels shallow but quickly has you wondering why troops are useful as you don't really have enough cap to train many plus the upgraded units cost more cap.(swordsman = 1 cap shields swordsman = 2 cap) (Feels sad)2. Archers are a waste time and space, One healer is enough (get the outpost healer if you can save a base spot)3. Catapults suck you have to get them killed if you want to use the fire catapult upgrade which Isn't great (5 cap=♥♥♥♥) rams are the only useful anti building weapon.4. This game is in a tedious slog at the moment too much waiting around for resources.5. The base building upgrades only to level 3 doesn't feel like it's enough to be interesting.6. The enemy attack waves needs more structure at current the enemy raids are just too weak and predictable enemy catapults should do way more to damage friendly troops how they can take shot after shot I don't know.6.1 There needs to be a proper wave system inflicting terror on the player forcing you there to reinforce.7. Unlimited restocking supplies feels weird I feel like it should cost silver or something else like that. (Also that's the auto save function if people didn't notice)==========================================================================The positives:==========================================================================1. Pretty graphics and weather change effects look good (The day time sunlight is a nice feeling when the morning rolls around and before mid day be nice if there's desktop background for that image)2. Animations quality I feel have done a favour for this game the ambience of the workers, boats, insects and water animations feel like there's something going on in ones base.==========================================================================Improvement Ideas:==========================================================================1. Perhaps a morale system for your troops if you leave them alone for too long unexpected things happen. (Chance they run from enemies, steal some of your supplies, (pickpocket) accidentally damage a building etc.)2. An option to taunt the enemy for a higher drop chance of resources/runes elite enemy units attack with the wave as well.3. Blocking and fighting be locked to the mouse for directional combat with the ability to walk backwards when blocking. The amount of times i'll go to block then the character will flip around facing the wrong way.4. Attack timing could be better with a counterattack option for a crit chance would be nice. 5. More animations would certainly be great. (e.g blacksmith working outside forging, archers training at the archery range, a man sharpening a sword in the barracks, bunch of drunk vikings outside the mead hall and engineers tinkering with a piece of catapult. Just pure ambience not only for when upgrading anything or hiring units) ==========================================================================At current can't recommend but if future changes improve this game's pace and content then I'll update.Bugs suck too who knew.

_childDocuments_.review: I only played the game/completed it on the hardest difficulty.What I enjoyed:1) The Pixel Art2) The Rune System3) Most of the Voice Acting4) Burning Pots5) Expanding my base.6) Horde Mode (though I wish there were things to collect in this mode for completing up to a certain wave [new skins, unlock concept art, etc])What I thought was so-so.1) The Story. Aside from the beginning of the game, Odin and Valhalla served little purpose. It would be cool if there was progression here as the game unfolded.2) Unlike the Kingdoms games, enemies only come from the right. Not Both sides. It almost seemed like this wasn't the case in production, but they changed their minds towards the end of release. It makes sense story wise, but I also feel like it could have been more fun if they came from both sides. Perhaps at least in horde mode?What I didn't like:1) Most of the AI Units were not smart (I mainly bought archers because they were reliable at fighting from a distance while I took on everyone on the front lines. _childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth the money and feels like the beta version of a finished game. Being a side-scrolling base-builder, it's naturally going to draw comparisons to Kingdom. I disagree and view it more as a metroidvania game with elements from Kingdom. The story is laughably short. The survival mode is boring, mundane, and finishes at level 75. When you make something, it's always better to leave people wanting more, but this pushes that too far. I want a full game.===Pros===Great soundtrackFun gameplayBeautiful animation and pixelated design===Cons===Too shortRepetitive to the point it becomes boringConstrictive in how you tend to play once you "get" the system that was built===Final Thoughts===Kingdom and Kingdom Two Crowns are both phenomenal games that I've sunk hundreds of hours into and enjoyed every minute of despite their relative simplicity. I've also enjoyed Metroidvania games like Dead Cells and Sundered. This game is an interesting attempt to merge the two genres that ultimately falls flat due to the limits of the scope of the game. It's fun, but it's over too quickly and the mechanics sometimes make it boring. It doesn't have much in terms of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said the basic concept here is Kingdom with combat. This worked for me and is both what I expected and what I wanted. $20 feels good for this game considering what you get. The story isn't blow-your-socks-off-fantastic but it's not terrible either. Pretty standard "the princess is not in this castle" fare. The gameplay, as some of the negative reviews have said, can get repetitive BUT ... it's a repetitive gameplay loop that I personally enjoy quite a bit so it never bothered me. I enjoy base-building and I enjoy sieging which is the entire loop here (plus a boss battle at the end of each level). I got what I wanted from the game so I'm happy to give this a thumbs up. And it's a true indie studio so I'm happy to pay full price to support them.Suggestions ... More replayability - the criticism that there's not much replayability is valid. I'd like to see perhaps some other game modes that give us more options to keep playing (wave combat a-la Kingdom ... or something similar). EDIT: Nevermind ... start a new game and you get 2 other modes I didn't realize, including a horde mode. <facepalm>More content - More upgrades, bigger bases, more enemies, more units, etc. So much room in that radial menu had me feeling like there were more units coming that never did. _childDocuments_.review: Having played through the whole thing (minus the stealth mission) on Normal, it's a good game, especially for the price point. It definitely warrants a few more playthroughs, even if just to give different difficulties a try and experiment with build orders, unit composition, etc. Depending on how the game is maintained and updated over time (so far there have been daily updates and bug fixes, which is promising!), I might end up revisiting it for a long time to come!The main criticism I see from others is about repetitiveness and I can certainly see what they mean, but the combination of switching from having to attack, defend and build up your base and army is fun enough, for the first playthrough anyway. The variety I'd like to see more of, probably would be in the boss fights, most of which are easy to beat by simply spamming your ranged attacks (make sure you upgrade those!) and dodging a few times. That said, the bosses are about 5% of the game, so they're more of a distraction from the base gameplay, though I can see how the dev might tweak them over time, given how receptive they have been to player feedback :)The story is simple, but effective enough. The music and visuals are also designed just well enough to serve their purpose and not distract you from murderring your way through England - nothing you haven't seen before, but just right.Overall, worth giving it a try! And with a demo available (as of the time of writing) + the refund policy, you literally have nothing to lose ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give this game a thumbs up because this is a pretty excellent job for a solo developers first game. With that said, I didnt really enjoy the game, I couldnt even be bothered to play this full version longer than an hour. I backed the game on Kickstarter and even a year or two ago during the alpha, the game was the exact same. At that time I thought "Okay the game will become more complex and strategical with time, its just in too early of a state right now". Didnt touch the game till release the other day and I was pretty disappointed to find that its the same exact game. The gameplay loop turns into you running back and forth to your base to hire soldiers, waiting at your front gate or running back to tell them to attack the enemy base after they spawn, watch them die, run back to hire more soldiers until you take the outpost over and then you fight a boss at the end (I liked the boss fights because it broke the tedious loop). Besides that you just choose what building to place at stacks of woods/tools which are the games predetermined building spots, you go to the buildings weird menu and choose what upgrade to get and thats it. Thats the loop the whole game. Honestly, I really think the developer didnt have time, money or whatever to flesh out the invasion/siege mechanics.  Maybe its my fault since I expected a more strategical and combat oriented "Kingdom: New Lands". All in all im not disappointed by my kickstarter backing. Im extremely confident in this developers skills and im glad he was able to successfully create his first game. I wish Pixel Chest all the best in the future and I look forward to their future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: Sons of Valhalla will be familiar to players of the Kingdoms Two Crowns game series, it uses many of the same mechanics while sprinkling a few of its own into the mix for good measure. There is a player controlled main character with light and heavy attacks as well as a variety of other skills that can be unlocked via Runes. Runes are the games other great addition to the genre. These can be picked up at random from battle or from chests and can be slotted in to belts with various upgrades to add more to each belt.Like kingdoms Two Crowns the game also has an ever-expanding base with a variety of units you can summon from several different buildings. Archers, Warrior, Berserkers etc as well as priests and siege weapons. All of this is driven by resources buildings, fishing, and woodcutting.The object of each map is to get from the far left of the map to the far right, breaking the enemies’ bases, building newer bases, and upgrading both the player character and the various units you summon and can command into combat. The object, reach the end of level and the level boss. Here the game adds another of its main additions. Each boss your character fights alone, and although not hard some may find them a challenge, especially towards the end.Once you finish a level you move to the next and must start from scratch, taking only the runes you have collected.There is fun to be had in the game but it forgets the thing that made Kingdoms Two Crowns entertaining, the push and pull of the day time fight and hunt versus the night time defend the outskirts of your base against ever increasing enemy waves. Here there is none of that, you are constantly on the forward moving combat train. Enemies will attack but I found only if you attack them. The maps also do not feel particularly big, each map consisting of 5 or 6 enemy bases before the end boss. In all It took me about seven and a half hours to complete the game.If you are a Two Crowns fan it might be worth a look but it does not feel to have as much depth as that series, still it might be worth your time. Cannot say I did not enjoy my time in the game.
