_childDocuments_.review: Release Date: March 18th 2022Developers: Benoit Sokal team at Microids Studio ParisGenre&Topics: story-driven cinematic adventure, mechanical puzzles, long cut scenes, nazism, fascism, resistance, World War II in fictional world reminding real history, love story, very good story and storytelling.This is a spoiler free review. I’m just discussing the quality of storytelling, not the story itself. You can read my review even before to play the game.INTROI played both the first two episodes of Syberia in 2004, but the first was released in 2002; they are like two parts of the same single game. Classic point & click graphic adventures alternating puzzles, exploration and narrative cut scenes. They added no novelties or innovations to the genre. Story is good and meaningful but weird, just like many other games belonging to the same genre. Summing up, Kate Walker seems destined to be a rampant american lawyer in a society dominated by speculation, selfishness, materialism, pursuit of selfish profit. A society that has stopped to dream, to chase adventures, passions, humaneness, creativeness, ideals and values. Kate is sent by her law firm to the fictional French village of Valadilène to oversee the corporate takeover of a family-owned “automata” factory. Automata are really evolved, some of them can even reason and speak as humans, but they apparently have no feelings and emotions. After meeting Hans Voralberg (the inventor) and the automaton Oscar, Kate understands that passions, dreams, adventure, humaneness, ideals and values are what matters more in life. She decides to escape her past life (even her mom and her boyfriend) and quit her career as lawyer. They embark on a long journey to the island of Syberia in search of Mammoths; the Mammoth is the metaphor for a dream or a passion that is perhaps unattainable and apparently crazy but makes life meaningful. As you see Syberia is a game for dreamers and idealists, for those who love to travel to escape (in vain) from themselves and reality; it comes with very elegiac, romantic and poetic mood. You can see it as a hymn to escapism through video games or fantasy novels or comics or more in general through art. Not by chance the creator of the Syberia series, Benoit Sokal, was a renowned French comic-books writer (see the pessimistic noir series Inspector Canardo) who put his art at the service of video games. He died in 2021. Syberia III was his last video game; it was released in 2017, but it was not well received by critics and fans. I never played it, sorry!However lately I was curious about the fourth episode. A lot of critics and fans were incensing it! Well, now I can say that Syberia: The Wolrd Before is a truly passionate and felt tribute to the art of Benoit Sokal by the core team of the first two episodes. And I can say they surpassed the Master and developed the best entry in the series: a narrative masterpiece, one of the best stories ever told in video games, one of the most compelling narrative games I ever played in four decades! Lately at Microids they are developing really good narrative games, see Vertigo! Kudos!FROM SYBERIA I & II TO THE WORLD BEFORETWB is the same as the first two episodes? Not properly! It’s point & click no more. You can freely explore pre-rendered scenarios, no camera control, just auto-scrolling camera following your movements; graphics is very good and detailed, with pleasant Art Nouveau aesthetics, a real joy for the eyes, especially in 4K. The design of the fictional world is at-the-state-of-the-art, very credible and absolutely immersive. Even characters are well designed; maybe animations and expressions are a bit stiff, not the best, but still very good. Overall, you have the feeling to play an AAA game or at least AA1/2!! From a technical point of view the leap is huge in comparison to the first two episodes.In old episodes, puzzles were quite hard, sometimes intrusive, annoying, nonsense, too much detached from narrative, as in other old school graphic adventures. TWB comes apparently with the same kind of puzzles. Most of times you have to put Voralberg’s automata or machinery in operation. However they are less hard, I would say easy, less annoying, less intrusive; they are more integrated in narration or at least don’t interrupt the narrative flow that much. TWB introduces multiple choice dialogues; they make storytelling more interactive but have quite no consequences on the main story. That’s good, it would be bad to change the very good story! As you see, story and gameplay are quite detached, as in old school games. Story is told through cut scenes, some dialogues, few documents and your diary; we cannot speak of integration of narrative in gameplay, as in many contemporary interactive drama by Quantic Dreams, Telltales, Dontnod or in so wrongly called walking simulators (Firewatch, Vertigo, Edith Finch, etc). However there is no heavy ludo-narrative conflict in TWB. In early Syberia episodes ludo-narrative dissonance was high, not here. It gives you the illusion to have a role in the story, even if interactivity is limited to exploration, puzzles, some multiple choice dialogues, collecting some documents. Cut scenes have the main narrative role.Is still TWB a work of poetic naive escapism? Kate Walker is the same Kate Walker as ever?(continue here:
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Syberia: The World Before - the art, the music, the story, the diaries that often tell you additional info (Kate's diary was actually the diary of that detective that is following her). It does have a single autosave but if you have cloud save turned off - you can do manual copies. When you go back to the main menu it tells you when your last save was and lets you cancel if it was too long ago. The cut scenes are beautiful and slow and you can't skip them...It was what made me go back and buy the older games on Steam...There is one section where Kate is a prisoner in a mining cave where she is not in character - otherwise it is very much in character.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Waste of money. The gameplay for pc at least is terrible. Very annoying. You can’t skip anything from cutscenes to item explanation dialogues. The game is not an adventure game. It is more like you watch a movie and at some points you can interact with the movie just to wake you up. There are no riddles no nothing. Just pointless clicks here and there and walking from here to there. All are super simple and the things you have to do are all just in front of your eyes. It would be better if they indeed made a 2 hours movie instead of this game…!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Great staged game with strong emotional but also funny moments in a fascinating steam punk world. The great soundtrack carries the very exciting story, as well as the beautifully designed locations and beautifully animated characters. I had to take screenshots every few minutes. Also, I have a crush on Kate.10/10 would hop on the train with Kate again
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty much a movie with limited interaction, a lot of conversations and clips, puzzles are a bit too easy and not very challenging. But despite that, the game design, animation and graphics quality are very good, the artistic reproduction of old Europe cities and locations is excellent, atmospheric and full of details, also the music soundtrack is worth a mention. On overall I would recommend this game, a good final chapter for the Syberia saga, especially if you played and loved the old ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is an immersive adventure game that deeply touches the hearts of its players. The story is poignant and rich in emotion, offering an exceptional narrative experience. The writers have done an outstanding job in developing the characters, making each one feel lifelike and memorable. Throughout the game, players encounter numerous thought-provoking puzzles that provide a satisfying challenge while encouraging the development of problem-solving skills.However, the difficulty level of these puzzles leaves something to be desired. While they are indeed thought-provoking, some players might feel that they could have been more challenging to truly test their abilities.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Game is terrible! I don't know how people are giving this game positive reviews? I've been playing many, many video games for well over 40 years, so I basically am knowledgeable when it comes to these type of games. I played the other 2 Syberia games in this series and was thrilled to learn that this game was coming out. I even told everyone that I knew about a third game coming out. So...Here we go!!! I played the first 1.5 Hours on this game. Game lags BIG TIME! I tried this game on the lowest settings with the latest drivers and anti-virus switched off. It's horrible the way this game lags. I am running a Dell G7 gaming computer which runs everything I can throw at it and never one single problem. Ever! The engine that the developers are using is a total pig! In order to play this game you need the latest and the greatest in order to play this game. That tells me Microids is working with either computer manufacturers and/or Graphic card manufacturers to get rich! My first impressions of the game (even if there was no lagging) is this. 1) The total atmosphere of the game, including mechanics, story yelling, etc were just terrible! _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent entry into the Syberia series of games. The voice acting has drastically improved from previous games, and I have yet to encounter any major bugs in the controls (I had a moment where Kate seemed stuck, but managed to get her moving again). I'm loving the addition of Dana Roze and the rest of the cast, looking forward to figuring out the rest of their stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start my review with a word of thank you to the entire team for finishing the product after passing away of Benoît Sokal. I played all Syberia games during my formative years and it was a pleasure to continue this story. As a mature gamer and software engineer myself, whenever I think of how adventure games should look like, Syberia among few other titles comes to my mind. The emotional rollercoaster it provides to the player is impressive. Good story telling is something I truly admire and appreciate no matter the game genre. Rest in peace Benoît Sokal and thank you for creating this game franchise. It helped me realize something about my life: how it is a constant journey; how to seek sense and appreciate small things; how automata can make people's lifes better. Thank you for that.When it comes to the Syberia: The World Before, I think this was a great continuation to the story. It makes sense after finishing the game and gives hope for another sequel in the future. It took me 14 hours to finish the story with most of the side quests. I don't know if that's a lot or not; for me it was three evenings, I personally am happy with how long the game was. The plot was rich and complex to my standards. The number of locations is okay I guess. Speaking of story overall, I think the game will be a little more enjoyable for people who played previous Syberia games; there is quite a lot of references to previous events so I highly recommend to check out entire game franchise.I highly recommend to play the game with controller, it was very pleasant to play this way for me. There were maybe few times when Kate was a little stuck and was refusing to move but after a while she was able to change her location. Other than that, it was fun to use the controller to play and solve the riddles especially.A few words about graphics and sounds: this game is a true masterpiece; the attention to details is splendid. It is aesthetically pleasing and allows player to truly immerse himself into this adventure. Honorable mention for all the automata present in the game, the steampunk vibe they give is magnificent. There are quite many cut scenes in the game and they allow player to submerge in the story even more. When it comes to sounds and music, I will speak about English dubbing only: I think that the voices match the characters very well. The ambient sounds and music are well executed. I am following Inon Zur and Spotify and really enjoy his music.Performance and technicals: I played on ultra graphical settings with no issues. The only thing I was missing is support for ultrawide resolutions, it would be nice to enjoy the picture even wider, but I know it's taken into consideration now and may be added in the future. Other than that, I have nothing to add.I had a great time playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I never leave reviews on Steam but I felt like I had to for this one.The Syberia games are very near and dear to my heart and since playing the demo for the World Before I just couldn't wait for the release of the full game. What I love the most about this universe is the locations and Vaghen really did not let me down. I would love to be able to explore Valadilene, Romansburg etc with better visuals too in the future. The city sucked me right in and I really felt like I was taking the tram together with Kate all the time.There were some things that bothered me story-wise and the puzzles were little and not very challenging (unfortunately). I'm also not a fan of not being able to skip dialogue. I want to replay the game but the fact that I'd have to listen through everything again just doesn't appeal to me. OR maybe skipping is an option and I just couldn't figure out how hahaThe music is insanely good as per usual and I'm going to keep listening to it for a very long time. The cinematography of the game is also *chef's kiss*.All in all this game exceeded my expectations (especially after how Syberia 3 left quite a bitter taste in out mouths) and I urge everyone to play it ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn.On one hand I had fun playing this game, especially since I played the other Syberia game (3).But on the other hand the game was kind of boring. The music accompanied the game well and the controls were fine. Environment was very pretty. Loved the city Vaghen. Really pretty. Characters were mildly interesting.But the game felt so long because of the diaologues (and not in a good way). Halfway the story I wasn't interested anymore, so I felt extra frustrated when I couldn't skip dialogue.So I'm really inbetween. For a standalone game I wouldn't recommend, but if you've played the previous one it's a game to try.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get the game to play. All I get is a black screen. I have a Microsoft Pro 6 with  windows 10 and i7 intel chip; other games run but this one doesn't. I've tried to find help but the community post doesn't have post that addresses "does not start" or "won't start" issue. Says it doesn't exist. I verified cache. Says game downloaded and is viable. Still won't open or start. Support is terrible and/or confusing. This is the only game I've downloaded in two years because I thought it would be cool... what a headache this has turned into.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It is an enjoyable adventure game. It doesn't quite live up to the first 2 in the series but it's ok in some ways. The story is interesting up to a point, after that it kind of leaves something to be desired, not to mention it has no ending and leaves you so incomplete, clearly they were thinking of a sequel, possibly Syberia 5.I recommend it for fans of the genre but I would recommend getting it on a discount and not full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The Syberia series has a special place in my heart. Those were not only games, there were also, or maybe mainly,  experience. It is true that 3rd part was not as good as two previous ones, but the magic was also there. Now the 4rth part brings back the similar feeling that first two parts. For sure it is different kind of Syberia, but the story, graphics and music are as magical as in first two parts. What could be better? Puzzles, which in my opinion are not of a much challenge. I love in adventures games the feeling when after being stuck in some location, even for days,  I suddenly come up with solution which than seems to be obvious. I didn’t find this in Syberia 4. The other thing that the game might really use is free camera. I cant even count how many time when I played I wished I could look around just to admire the surroundings and not to be limited to fix view. This is really shame. The game is so beautiful and it deserves to be admired fully :)Just to sum up. Syberia – The Word Before is a must play for all fans of adventures games. I really, really hope that somehow the story will continue despite the fact that Benoît Sokal is no longer among us. The journey must continue :)
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A great finale(?) for the series, massively improving on its predecessor. Unlike Syberia 3, The World Before looks much better, looking rather beautiful in some areas and plays much better, with improved controls and virtually bug free. It is overall a much more polished product compared to all the previous entries.I highly recommend it for fans of the series wanting to see the continuation (and end?) of the story. Players wanting a Syberia 1 or 2 might be disappointed however as The World Before has less focus on the puzzles and is instead focused more on the story and cinematics.If you want to play this I highly recommend playing at least Syberia 1 first to get an idea of the setting but the game does give you a recap of the events at the start.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I can't describe how this game made me feel, like an ending to a play, as the curtains closed I wanted nothing more than to go backstage and continue the story! After having bought Syberia 1 and 2 in a sale some years ago, I took the time to finally play them at the start of the year and I was driven to play the whole story. At first I wanted to play the first three just so I could start this one, but I as I played through the games I found myself becoming so engrossed I had to learn everything I could from each game and once I finally managed to play this game it felt like I was meeting an old friend again and going on an adventure once more. The story and writing in this game are incredible and combined with the amazing visuals and soundtrack, this game and the previous games in the series are a must play! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: it's intensively important, for a couple of reasons. First and most important one, it's the definitive answer from Microids regarding how much they care for this franchise. Secondly, it's a continuation of the story following Kate Walker, that is going since early 2000. was somewhat disastrous, we all know that. The Prologue available since late 2020 was pretty good, but not perfect. So, where are we exactly?Well, I'm thrilled to say the true  is finally back. It's true, and I write this with a wide smile on my face since I'm a long time fan of Kate's adventure. We deserve , and more importantly,  shows a tremendous respect for delaying the game, in order to fully optimize and craft this amazing masterpiece.As you probably know (If you played the third game), Kate Walker was imprisoned, and that's how this new game starts. Since not everyone played the Prologue, a lot of things will be new. But for those who played, know that the available Prologue only covers the very initial part of the game. So much so, I'd risk and say it's somewhat of an introduction or tutorial if you will.To avoid spoilers, I'll refrain myself from touch any further details of the main plot. Instead, I'll just mention the elegant plot construction, the exquisite narrative and an absolute blast of events that follows Kate.Her personality is present, with all her remarks, commentary, and overall presence. It's a true return of the series when comes to character development. Not that the series ever lost it, but it's 2022 so you never know.The story mixes two different timelines, one in 2005 with Kate, and one from the past with Dana Roze, in the mid 30's. Both timelines work together in a smart and engaging mechanic. There's no such thing as time travel, but memories, those travels beyond any time barrier. The game does an excellent job playing with both Kate and Dana, and how they tangle together. How both timelines further connect, that's for you to find out.Gameplay is also a worrying mechanic. After the third game messy controls, we're back on a true spirit of Point and Click. Very much like the classic games, players control the mouse in points of interest, allowing Kate to move, and interact with them. If you love the originals, you'll easily pick up the mechanics of this new game.Puzzles are obviously back, and this time they are made simpler, but you still have to think and gather clues to solve them. The Voralberg legacy is well implanted through puzzles in mechanical devices, in which you'll have riddles in a old fashioned way. There is no doubt Syberia is in the new generation of Point and Click, with smooth controls, responsive behavior and a dynamic level design that conjugate a well built world.Syberia: The World Before is not an open world game, but it's smart enough to deliver a coherent placement of locations. Naturally built, such as the classics did formerly.Before we dive into the level design, I have to mention the Unity factor. It's not real news that the developers made this new Syberia with Unity. That's always a red flag. Surprisingly, I have to admit, they made the right choice. is the best looking game ever made in Unity, showcasing a fantastic global lightning, reflections and shadows. Geometrically speaking, it honors the dates and takes special attention to automaton creations, with the fantastic mark of . Locations are really charming, especially the outdoor areas, with authentic forests and mountains. Truly is a love letter for those who, such as myself, adore to see Kate into the wild.Those who played the Prologue will be happy to know the optimization went up by a lot. Loading times, and overall stability improved considerably, and if that was the reason for the delay, it was for the best. The frame rate is very consistent, even in Ultra Settings.Unfortunately, there aren't very visual options, but you can tweak Shadows and Anti-Aliasing to control performance. Chromatic Aberration is present, and I for one did not manage to remove it. Not a good thing, especially in 2022. does everything right to captivate players in a a enjoyable adventure, one where we rejoice for having Kate Walker back, fused in a timeline as a new mystery arises. A true come back in the series, and one a true fan can and will most certainly love. Well worth the price tag, for an adventure that will easily surpass the 15 hour mark.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed my time with Syberia: The World Before. Without any spoilers, you get to know Kate, her family and their backstory a lot more which was quite a fun and entertaining trip through the past and present.Compared to the previous three games, this one feels a bit different in my opinion. To tell the story, it uses more and longer cutscenes. The cutscenes themselves are very well done and add to the experience, but you can't skip them. So when coming back to an area after an event, I'd try to get a different dialogue only to be trapped and having to listen to the same thing again. Not a huge problem, just mildly annoying.Coming to this game directly after playing Syberia 3, the camera controls reminded me a tiny bit of it, thankfully the execution was worlds better (truthfully, it'd be hard to make it worse).The Syberia games and their Valadilene automatons were already very fascinating to be in, but this game takes them on another visual level with the beautiful city of Vaghen - there's so much to see and admire.Apart from one or two questionable parts in the story, this was well worth my time and I can only recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the older iterations of Syberia and loving every one of them (especially Syberia II), I was very disappointed by Syberia: The World Before. Short version? This game is BOOOORING... Itemized review:The Good:1. Overall graphics and cinematics are beautiful.2. Voice acting is okay, nothing to write home about but at least not annoying.The Bad:1. Storyline, although at times interesting, is drawn out and overall flat. The motivation of the main character for the quest is very simple. Like something from a network tv show. Could have been more developed.2. Puzzles are incredibly simple and trivial. Very little depth and they do not require much thinking.3. The companion automaton is so annoying (mainly due to its shape).4. I played the previous Syberia games on a console and the controls/mechanics were much more pleasant and intuitive. Playing Syberia: The World Before on a mouse/keyboard was a pain - cumbersome, clunky, and slow.5. Overall, not a challenging game at all. Just plain boring.This is my subjective opinion, obviously, but I got so bored with this game that I stopped playing after the third location (the Music Square). I hope the devs will make it more challenging in future editions - it would be a shame to destroy such a good franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved this series since game one. And while I love the first 2 games dearly, the last 2 have done the series good, especially this one. The story telling may be the best in the series. You play several different characters and where the story goes, how it is told, and the voice acting is awesome. Game looks amazing and and play smooth. Had no issues with lag or crashing. Ran great. If you’re going for achievements, 2 play throughs should do it. Just makes a lot of looking around. Fun puzzles, story, and characters. A must play. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely stunning game. A few hours in and the world disappears. Every frame has been crafted so lovingly, and I've got the settings on High. When I get a new computer I'll crank it up to Ultra but even at High settings this is, again, stunning. For fans that have played this since the beginning there is much fan service and it is appreciated. Think of Syberia 3 being a bridge now between this game and Syberia 2, where this one is certainly the slam dunk to carry on the original plotlines and maybe (haven't finished yet) bring closure. Seriously Microids have balanced the point and click with the 3D environments very well and having played their recent Poirot game they are on fire for magnificent storytelling, voice acting and orchestral scores. This is a very chilled experience, no COD here, no fancy RPG, just storytelling at its best.Update: Have now finished the game and possibly one of the best adventure games I've ever played. The emotional response from the story, the music and the characters voiced to perfection, just is incredible. Amazed where the story twisted and turned. Well worth every cent paid for this
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Unfortunately, the adventure game genre is a lost genre today, and that's a very bad thing. The previous game was technically quite weak, but this time the developer team did their job, at least they made the best game they could with the budget they had. I wish there was more investment in such teams and we had the chance to play these games at AAA quality. However, the new generation does not understand such games and all studios continue to produce empty, easy-to-consume games suitable for them...
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: OK i'll give you the reasons I'm giving this a thumbs down.There's a time and place for everything, and while this Syberia is an allegory for pre-war Germany they have included a Nazi film director key character in the game, specifically, "Leni Riefenstahl".Leni Riefenstahl (who died in 2003 ironically) was Adolph Hitler's personal film director and propagandist who caused untold misery to thousands.   Syberia is meant to be a charming fictional experience and the inclusion of a real life Nazi Film Director is completely distasteful and inappropriate IMO.Having said that it looks gorgeous and and may be worth the price of a deep sale.  It isn't very interesting, you just go around doing pointless stuff really to pad out the run time.  The controls are for ♥♥♥♥ and there is no challenge to anything unlike it's predecessors.If you want a nice looking and relaxing walk about with a good soundtrack then this may be for you.  I can't honestly say there is much "Syberia" about it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Good story. Mostly interesting puzzles. Far better controls than Syberia 3. Still the weird camera angles that can't be properly adjusted were at times unfuriating. I missed several important hot spots by just not being able to 'see' them from the angles the game chooses to present the scene. That's unnecessary and I don't know why it's been done like that in the first place. Overall a good game, but with still some minor quirks regarding controls (mainly camera).
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is a marvelous game with a captivating plot, beautiful graphics, catchy soundtrack, and some entertaining puzzles. Knowledge of the prior installments of the series isn't necessary, as a video summary is provided and the game works very well as a standalone experience. As an only lightly anonymized story about the persecution of minorities by the nazis in WW2 this is also a strong statement for a culture of remembrance, one that is a worthy legacy for Benoît Sokal.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This fourth Installment of the Syberia franchise is a very beautiful and well put together game. The sceneries are epic, the story is pretty good and the puzzles are not too hard.But it's the atmosphere that does the trick. I just want to move to Vaghen and live there for the rest of my life, it's so gorgeous.It's a shame the voice actor for Oscar has changed. The very characteristic voice in parts one and two has changed to a more generic British voice for this game.Despite the more negative reviews for Syberia 3, which I thought was a OK-ish game, this fourth installment is totally epic.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a visual treat. As far as point & click genre goes, this might be up there with the best ones in this genre. The storyline was very interesting and the puzzles were of various level of difficulties throughout the game, which made for a fun experience. Would recommend it to anyone who is a fan of this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: My rating: 4/5 (good)Great entry into the franchise. I was worried at first because the first part makes it look like the game has gone woke, but things get back to normal fast enough. It is more story heavy than previous games but the story is really good and had me invested. The puzzles were just hard enough to make me think without resorting to a guide. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is a must to play for Syberia fans who have been waiting for the story to continue. The game can also be played by people new to the series, but I would think the game is more rewarding if you know the main characters well.  The story is rich and fulfilling and set me, like the other Syberia games did, in a sentimental mood. The puzzles were for the most part interesting. Great soundtrack. A game to be savoured!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Really well thought out. It seems like they've put much effort in this game, especially in details like letters or little notes, which are optional to look at. I've never seen a game putting so much effort in details. Also they've handeled such a sensitive topic respectfully. Really great game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful and sad story, full of sorrow and longing with a few laughter in between.It feels good to be back in the world of Syberia, however this time the game did not bring me joy like the first one, but instead a feeling of grief and nostalgia for The World Before, even more so that my grandmother looks so much like Dana, making the story a little more personal.Another thing is that I knew everything that was going to happen because the story is so well written that you can make conclusions early and be right about it, that doesn't take away from the experience though. My only complaint being the "impossible" diary entries and a few minor mistakes here and there, specially during.All in all, this may be the perfect farewell to a franchise that's been around for 20 years...but there will always be a train.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I still much prefer the first two games...they were magical and intriguing. This has a good story but it's not longer it.... The art is gorgeous, but the story doesn't immerse or enchant me as much as the first two games did, where there was a sense of wonder and mystery, And there's too much loss and drama in this one, too depressing, to the point it feels overdone and I don't feel sincerity from it at the moment.  I read up plot synopsis and I just don't know if I'll continue this. I don't like the direction the story took since 1 and 2, which are my favourites. Also it feels regurgitated to me, rather than deepened and I find myself fairly disappointed. I love the first two syberia games with their absolute charm, i skipped the 3 one and this one doesn't feel quite right to me, But it is still a gorgeous game, absolutely gorgeous. But will not beet Syberia or Syberia 2 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It is incredibly beautiful, incredibly well told story. Cutscenes (except one) are magnificent. Visuals are truly breathtaking and facial movement of characters was done really well. It offers a lot of locations, we keep going from one place to another in a blink of an eye and puzzles are way more simpler than in a last part, so there is no chance you will get stuck. That fixed camera kinda confuses you where to go and what can you inspect but beside that the gameplay is very smooth, peaceful and relaxing. The plot itself starts kinda weird and character motivation seems week, but all leads to a very solid and satisfying conclusion. The only thing that bothers me is that we got story about real war in a real world and you created some fake group instead of nazis. You can create your own towns and even countries but changing  history like that is kinda disgrace to a victims. There definietely should be nazis and swastikas in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully made! And well optimized. Even my 10 year old PC could mostly manage the High setting. The story is captivating, the voice acting is back where it was, the music is recorded with a live orchestra. Everything about this game is beautiful. I'd say that this, along with the 3rd installment, is more like a spinoff series because they are not about Syberia but focus on Kate Walker. But if you like adventure games this is definitely for you because they don't make them this good usually.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is magnificent without a doubt!After playing Syberia 3 (with which I have mixed opinions) I had the feeling that the next game won't be better,that's why also I delayed buying this title contemplating if it is worth my time, but I was so wrong!Syberia: The World Before is such a worthy successor of the Syberia 1 and 2!I recommend the game to everybody who liked the journey of Kate, Hans and Oscar!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I am a very big fan of the Syberia Series (yes even Syberia 3!).   I even named my dog Oscar!   I cannot tell you how excited I was for this 4th installment to come out, perhaps I set the standard too high.   Whilst this game was absolutely beautiful in terms of graphics and music, I felt I was watching a sort of interactive movie... it was very slow and there is no option for skipping anything.    I felt like I didn't get to 'DO' much compared to the other games, the small amount of puzzles were extremely easy and I never once found myself wondering what to do next or even contemplating getting a hint from somewhere like the other games.   I didn't love the objectives coming up on the side, this was very different to the other games and once again made it underwhelming and too easy.    Oscar wasn't his usual smarty pants either, I really wished he made a comeback in robot form..   I was secretly hoping there would be a big twist relating back to the Voralberg family but the story did feel miles away from the Syberia magic I have come to love.    I gave the game a thumbs up because it's nice to know Kates back story and the music and visuals were breathtaking.  Overall I have to admit I am disappointed as it felt very short which I can only put down to the fact there are so many cut scenes where you are just watching and not actually solving it yourself.    I do hope they make another one and make it much more interactive and more tricky..
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. I would rather call it an interactive movie of a video drama than a game. It is a really rich and touching story.I would not say, though, that it is the same to a previous three games of the title in terms of puzzles. They are present but feels a bit different as an interaction with them looks more realistic. The scene itself moves as the protagonists move along the streets and rooms. It gives a new level of immersion. It worth trying a demo, though, as here are some weird quirks with navigation which may irritate demanding players. However they are bearable.In terms of puzzles and searching for artefacts I found this part more concise and sensible then its predecessors. I would not say that I got stuck for long to the level of going to google for a walkthrough. The complexity is reasonable.Yeah, some people would be frustrated with system requirements as this is 100% 3D game whit all the bells and whistles such as Ray Tracing, etc. It does not support DLSS, though. I played it on RTX3080 in 4K with maximum settings. Cannot say that it was always smooth, but picture is great. average FPS: 45. Downgrading resolution to 1440 is a good option for such a VGA card.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I'm saying "no" on recommending this game...I wish I could choose both. Those who are fans of the first two games will be deeply disappointed. This game is very beautiful, but Kate has gone from a great character to a very unlikable one in this game. It's depressing and nothing about it is exciting...you are basically unearthing this weird and unbelievable story based on Nazi Germany but because this is a parallel steam punk universe, it goes under a different name. Oscar is the best part of the game, but that's not saying much. I wanted to love this game and paid full price when it was released. It's taken me a long time to get through it because it is just really a boring dragged out story, not a thrilling adventure like the other two. I don't even care that Kate is now suggested to be bisexual or whatever (which is annoying because of course we can't have her just be like she was in the first two games, we have to keep up with what's hip instead). This story is just drawn out and boring and it just seems like a lot of effort was put into it (again, it's beautiful to look at) to not have a more exciting and compelling story. It's just really kind of meh.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: To tell the truth, I am not a big fan of the series, and I certainly did not like "Syberia 3".But this one turned out to be quite a nice game! Not a classical adventure game, but rather a visual novel with a few mechanical puzzles thrown here and there - and both the visuals and the story are very good! The puzzles - well, not much so.I could also complain that no manual saves are available, and no skipping of the numerous cut-scenes - the problem is that I had a lot of crashes, and thus was forced to re-play many scenes. The crashes were gone, but the way, when I have switched the graphics to the lowest possible option.Still, the overall impressions are good!Update: it well seems to be the game of 2002 now.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: After Syberia 3 and Syberia TWD demo (it contains the beginning of the game, and it's the worst part) my expectations were pretty low, but The World Before totally delivers. It starts slow, and the first chapters are rather boring, but the story quickly picks up the pace, and all of a sudden you are pulled in into it, and all you want is to know how it ends.Sure, Syberia TWD strays even further from it's point-and-click origins than Syberia 3 did, and only has so many puzzles, being more of an interactive movie than a classic adventure game. But maybe that's the reason its story is so engaging: instead of being stuck on puzzles, you are always moving forward, discovering new facts and slowly rebuilding the history of Vaghen and its automatons, and finding out more about a mystery girl who looks very much like Kate Walker (it's not a spoiler, you actually start the game and the demo playing as this girl).I would even say, visually and story-wise The World Before is on the same level as Syberia 1 and 2 back in the day, and it's definitely a huge improvement over Syberia 3 in every way (I know, the bar was set pretty low, but still). Most importantly, it is a fitting way to end Kate Walker's journey. Of course, we might still get another game in the series, but it won't be by Benoit Sokal, sadly. RIP, master, and thank you for all the great worlds and stories you created!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I havent played the previous games, but I still enjoyed this game a lot on its own. It is possible to watch a short video with story from the previous three games on your profile, I did that after I had completed this one :)A few minor downsides I could think of is that the game seem to be a little unstable regarding fps. I played on 4K with ultra settings and it could go from 30-90 wich seems alot. Didnt seem to change alot when I changed the quality settings either.Another thing is that there is a list of chapters in the continue, but you cant actually choose a save point there and have to locate and rename it manually in the save folder on your computer.No database from what I could see on what goals you missed or finished. I wanted to complete all achievement because I played blindly. I dont want to play the whole game again and I have no Idea on what secondary goals I missed. You also have to replay I think 9 chaptes if you want the betrayed achievement.I did the manual rename of save file to test it out in order to get the eavesdrop achievement. But didnt see any point in trying to get these two harder achievements (betrayed and all secondary goals) when I have no Idea were to start. Its a good game, but I dont feel like spending another 10 hours in order to maybe get 100% achievement. Wouldnt suprise me if I missed something again on my second playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! This was a masterpiece of storytelling. Every part of the story, no matter how insignificant it may seem at first, is important. Whoever wrote the story for this game knew how to build tension and mystery. It's very emotionally gripping and mature in a harsh realistic way, but it still has some of the whimsy of the first Syberia games. I highly recommend this to anyone who enjoys narrative games, or is interested in narrative games. This belongs up their with the best of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is from someone that played the first game and second game, but never played the 3rd game since I heard it was pretty bad.What did I like about this game? Well I can say it's pretty, I do enjoy the art style, and of course a steam punk world which had drawn me to the first game.  I liked that they brought Oscar back because that is one of my favorite characters out of the whole game. Kate I have to say I enjoyed her character too this time. I don't think I really liked her to much in the previous games but she seemed to have grown up a bit from what she once was. She seemed like she actually gave a damn about Oscar this time around and had passionate about what she wanted to do. People say that this isn't the same character, but I think she just went through a lot in her life, and that can change anyone. The bad (spoilers)Now onto what I didn't like about this game. You're really trying to tell me that they find a random painting in a train and Kate just decides to full fill a promise to her now dead lover,  just because she thought the girl in the painting looked like Kate??? That's the plot??? You have got to be joking. Not only that, but you then decided to kill off a gay character just to move the plot along. C'mon man, you can do better then this! This story feels like it doesn't belong in this world. In fact it feels like it belongs in another game entirely that should have nothing to do with Kate. I don't understand why this story?  I feel like they could have gone in so many more interesting directions for a plot to have an adventure with Kate and Oscar, but we get these characters that quite frankly I don't really care about. My god this story line is depressing! The only laughs I may have had in the game came from Oscar. The rest was just doom and gloom. I understand, yeah it's war, it's not going to be happy fun times, but  it just didn't feel necessary to do that in THIS game. It felt like a mess. Like this was just a filler episode. This game was also so slow, and filled with unnecessary cut screens. I could forgive this if I could skip past it but NOPE, you have to sit there and watch a cut screen for about 15 seconds. It’s not even an interesting cut scene, all it is is showing scenery. Nothing is happening. It’s like they were just trying to stretch out the game time. I’m pretty sure this game would be way shorter if you removed all these scenery cut scenes. The save feature has got to be one of the most infuriating things about this game. It will save automatically, that’s it. You can’t make separate save files at all, which means that if you miss something you miss it and you can’t go back at all once that new scene starts the next section of the game. I learned that the hard way when one of my side quest was to investigate the train compartments. However, if you so happen to look in the wrong compartment that triggers the next scene, it will save the game and you cannot go back to get your achievement. This also means that the only way to get it now is to restart the game all over again from the beginning. I will tell you right now going back is not worth the achievement. There’s probably more I can say but I’m just going to leave this here. I don’t recommend it. I recommend playing the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly loved this game and got as far as Silberspiegel Refuge (Part 2) where they have the shoot out and the game crashed. It cost me £34.99 - money wasted!So be warned yours may crash near the end and you won't get your money back from Steam! Perhaps buy it from somewhere else who will refund you if things go wrong after 2 hours or more of play.I highly recommend this game but not from Steam!

_childDocuments_.review: How did they manage to degrade the bright, adventurous and exciting spirit that was Kate Walker, into a dull, depressed, bland, cardboard cut out of "Stick a Chick in it and Make her Gay." Geez. Leave your good memories of 1 and 2 intact, or if you haven't played them yet, go make memories there instead. This game has none of the beauty, none of the charm.Examples: Old Kate meeting a gorge would have said: I need to find a way across that.New incompetent Kate, depression relieved by cheek stroke and lingering look by girlfriend. Kate triggers a rockslide. New girlfriend pushes Kate out of the way and saves her. Kate, helpless defeated voice at the gorge "How are we going to get across that", New girlfriend come on we'll find a way. New girlfriend finds a motorbike. Kate: how will we ever get it started. New girlfriend, don't worry back in my days in a band on tours, I repaired the van! Kate, maybe I could look at the bodies. New girlfriend, no need, here's a history lesson, I immediately know all about these guys. Kate ridiculously sceptical: You wanna jump over the ravine on the motorbike? New girlfriend: Of course! I make the plans. You look for keys while I repair the bike.Kate on the train. New girlfriend joins and new girlfriend finds something interesting. Kate: Erm... yeah it's ok. New girlfriend: No, Kate! Look what's right under your nose. Kate: What's fascinating about it? New girlfriend: You mean you can't see? Look closer! Kate: Sorry you'll have to be more specific, I can't see. New girlfriend: Look again, there!Kate: Okay, better Kate than I ever was. I just wasn't good enough in my own right without you. Ughh puke. They may only have 5 litres of water a day in this Siberian Salt mine, but thank god they let the prisoners have blue hair dye. Otherwise how would we know they're gay?

_childDocuments_.review: What other reviewers have said about the mechanics of the game is absolutely true. I jokingly refer to this game as "Vaghen simulator" with my friends. There's no gameplay. It's like the devs heard the critique of Syberia 3, which was too experimental in its engine, and were like, okay, the way to solve this is to remove all the gameplay elements, obviously! Not to fix them! Ha, that would be work.Furthermore, and I struggle to type this as I know I don't want to deal with the (paid?) naysayers in the comments: the story is neither tonally nor thematically in line with what drew me into the Syberia series in the first place. Another reviewer mentioned their hypothesis that this was initially meant as a screenplay for a standalone game or movie. It could have been the pitch for an emotional (if prototypical) Sundance film about Nazi Europe and generational trauma, except the writers were advised to ditch the "Morse code was 69 and the monkey was 420" twist towards the end and they abjectly refused (seriously... what?)I'm saying this as a queer Jew: the inclusion of Kate's f/f relationship (which was refrigerated and then ENTIRELY forgotten within 15 minutes of the start of the game) and her ostensibly Jewish-ish background (which was euphemistic at best) did not serve the arc of Syberia whatsoever. I'd love to write a little more about the way I personally interpreted the first two games, especially Syberia I, but I'm not sure I can do it verbal justice; to make a long spiel short, it was always a story about the old world in contrast with the new, about a young hotshot losing her egocentric sense of identity in the face of a world much larger than she ever was. To recenter the series on Kate's personal identity felt like an injustice to the awe and humility imparted by the earlier games. I'll fully admit that this segment of my review is based on personal preference and interpretation, but I just didn't like the story at all and I can't bring myself to regard it as canon. Furthermore, uh, what happened to the whole... Youkol... situation? Are we just... not gonna even pretend to address where the third game left off? Do we not even care? I mean, sheesh, I thought Syberia 3 was the epitome of cultural insensitivity, and even I'm left wishing we had some closure. The pacing of this game is beyond insane; we start off in a literal concentration camp (which, by the way, holy CRAP, WHAT), and then "one year later" that whole sequence, barely ever referencing it again despite it being the follow-up to Syberia 3's cliffhanger ending, and then we pivot hard into some slapstick bestie-turned-into-an-armadillo hijinks? If you're trying to make a game about trauma, this is absolutely not the move. Syberia 4's writing gets a clean F on tone alone.Yeah, the graphics are stunning and the music is pretty darn good. That's why the game is Vaghen simulator. It has nothing else to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: A terrific return to form! It's been so wonderful to return to this series and a stellar tribute to the late Benoit Sokal!You can tell that a lot of love was put into this point-and-click adventure. The "clockpunk" game world, particularly the architecture of the cities, is beautifully realized. An absolute visual treat, though the character models don't always hold up to the same standard. While the story told is against the backdrop of an alternate WW2, like other Syberia titles, the story is ultimately focused on a very personal scale. It's something I really appreciated and I found myself quite affected by some of the key moments in the game. This is all punctuated by a stunning orchestral score which is especially wonderful as music is a central theme in the storyline....In terms of the gameplay, I found the game especially well designed. Movement was fluid, the UI was extremely intuitive. There's even a helpful hint system to guide you if you are ever stuck. In typical Syberia fashion, most of the puzzles revolve around automatons. They were varied and rewarding, none were especially confined or frustrating. In terms of performance, I encountered no issues whatsoever on a 3080 and 5800x at 4k max settings. A must-play for old fans of the series and highly recommended for those who enjoy adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of an interactive movie than a game. The story is compelling and the graphics amazing, but there is very little in the way of game play. I would recommend this to anyone who likes more of a story than lots of game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia 1 and 2 were groundbreaking games for the adventure genre. They were thoughtful, introspective journeys, but most significantly, they had stunning visual design and art direction from Benoit Sokal. The latest Syberia adventure had me skeptical moving out of isolation and into lived in worlds, but I have to say my concerns were proven wrong. Syberia - The World Before is not only a high point in the franchise, it could well be the strongest game of all - a fitting tribute to the final game that Benoit Sokal had input in before his tragic passing.The story is absolutely phenomenal and told in a much more intelligent and layered way than your average adventure romp, and Kate Walker has never felt more engaging.Mad props though have to go out to not just the writers who elevate the living EFF out of this game, but the thought and care that has gone into both the character and environmental design which has often AAA presentation, but the detail is where this game excels. From art nouveau accents to the details of the character poses and actions as they talk, these feel like real, lived in characters and I think it is so important to really address how much work has gone into creating these elevated details in a genre that doesnt always pay to do so.Adventure games as a genre suffer when the execution is poor, and during the opening level of Syberia: TWB i was concerned it may be another error-laden mess, but i quickly recognized that the most glaring visual flaw (Dana's hair flickering and popping with aliasing issues) is, in fact, one of the ONLY technical issues.This game is excellently optimized and runs comfortably on high settings on most modern gaming set ups.In all, this is a stunningly told and executed game and it is rare that fans of long running series' like this one are presented with such a mea culpa in the form of the best installment of the franchise. BUY IMMEDIATELY.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are so damn annoying and totally detract from the story line for no good reason. Like getting out of the cemetery. Wasted about 45 minutes in wondering around that had absolutely nothing to do with the game. That was about all I could stand after 13 hours of play time. And placing tanks, submarines, and guns on the map. Who cares?!? Probably a good game for someone with more patience in wasting their time on irrelevant crap. Really wanted to like this game as I really enjoyed the first two. Just too many dumb puzzles and not enough story for me.Update:Well, a few months after quitting the game for reasons stated above, I thought I'd give it another go. It took me awhile but I FINALLY found the exit to the cemetery. Good! I'm leaving this place! But NO!! The gates close and there is some other puzzle contraption I have to solve to open the gates back up! What in the heck does finding your way out of this frigging cemetery have to do with the story?!?!? I immediately quit the game in another bout of frustration...again. If I could give 2 thumbs down, I would.To be fair, I suppose many who enjoy puzzles for the pure sake of solving them, will enjoy this game because the feel and historical ambiance is pretty great. I just couldn't integrate distraction off solving puzzles unrelated to the story into enjoyment of the game. Great for some. A buzz kill for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been sitting here for a few hours, going back and forth between what I want to say and how I should express it. To be honest, I can't put what I want to express into words. "Syberia: The World Before" has left me with an emotion I can't put into words. I'm almost 10 days after finishing the game, and I'm still thinking about it. It is breathtakingly gorgeous, with a gripping tale that will leave you wanting more.This game is the reason I thought Syberia I and II were worthwhile to play. You must understand Kate's story—not just a few minutes of a summary, which is what is presented to you as a part of this game's menu options, but her entire story. While Kate is rarely in the spotlight in the first two games, such moments set up a picture of her previous life and her problems as the events unfold. Moving on to Syberia 3, Kate's character is completely formed, and you get introduced to times when Kate expresses her views and opinions through interaction and conversation options. All of this goes over into this game, where Kate is the main character.This is why I would strongly advise going through the entire collection. I left a review for each of these games, so if you want a spoiler-free perspective on them, I highly recommend checking them out. Personally, I had a different experience than I expected based on the reviews, and I go into detail about it under each game.I wish I could travel back in time and relive this game. This game does an excellent job of transporting you to its universe andmy only regret is that I didn't get to play it sooner.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan who was slightly disappointed with the rather abrupt ending of Syberia 3, I was excited to learn of this newly released sequel (I started playing 2 years ago but then dropped it and picked it back up now).At the beginning of this game, I wasn't sure what exactly was going on or why certain characters on Kate's journey were of any importance. Yet I kept playing, simply because my curiousity and sense of adventure (much like Kate herself) kept me going and drew me to constantly peek around the corner to see what would happen next.Eventually I got more and more invested into the actual story itself and all the wonderfully realized characters I met along the way. I wanted to get to know them and their story, and I wanted to know how they and the events surrounding them all fit into the bigger picture, as Kate slowly began connecting the dots.At the end of the road, with this game's amazing writing, I felt a sense of completion, like everything had come full circle in a satisfying way, while still leaving the door open for yet more adventure, which I hope will be the case despite dear Mr. Sokal's passing and this game being dedicated to his memory. With all due respect I sincerely hope Microïds don't let Syberia die with its creator, because I genuinely believe they have something truly special here that deserves to live on.With a great script, beautiful sets/vistas, and a gorgeous musical score that sets the atmosphere and vibe every step of the way, this is an absolute must play for any adventure fan out there, with an exciting plot about following breadcrumbs to dig up the past. Yes, it is the fourth in the series, but while there are references to prior games, events, and characters, by no means do you need to have played those to follow the beat here.Lastly, without spoiling events of this game in particular, I believe Syberia is ultimately a tale about being true to yourself and always daring to choose to answer your calling.. even in spite of responsibility and the people you may inadvertedly end up hurting along the way.During your life, there WILL be people who won't understand you or the roads you decide to take, but that shouldn't deter you from venturing them. Because this is YOUR life, not theirs. So while you may hurt or disappoint people with your decisions, above all else, it is important to stay true to yourself and follow your heart.I know the saying goes, that sometimes the right choice ain't the easy choice. But while what even is "right" in the first place can be left up for debate, Syberia, to ME, wants to tell us, that sometimes you need to do what feels right for YOU, not what others tell you is right or "the sensible thing to do". Not to say you should ditch any and all responsibility all the time, but sometimes, like Kate, we need to "get away from everything" and take the train to adventure, rather than the train back home.Rest in peace, Mr. Benoít Sokal. May your work live on in our hearts forever.And to Microïds, thank you for a great game and an amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It's nothing like any game I've ever played before. The game plays as a rich story narrative in which you navigate your way through it collecting information and items. Slow in some places, but challenging enough to keep your attention and interest going as the story unfolds. I played 6 hours before getting hung up on a puzzle, which I'm halfway through. I love the scenery and details that captivate and amaze me as I move from place to place. I try to see as much as I can, but am often pulled along and miss seeing everything. Play it again
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful story told in a graphicaly beautiful game. I'm glad the story finally adressed and gave a closure to our MC's motivations and psychology. The writing, the emotions, the music is a love letter to the narrative adventure genreMy only complain would go for the 'game' itself if I may call it so. Originaly the first two games had a lot of challenging puzzles who didn't hold your hand and you were rewarded for your wits by advancing the story.Syberia 3 may have been one of the buggiest mess I ever played but at least it kept the balance this way.But here, the balance has completly shifted the other way : you advance the story in a very straight path and are occasionnaly met with a puzzle which by the way never posed any serious hurdle.Such a shame because the landscape begged to be beheld a little more while racking my brain on an elaborate Voralberg contraption.But I get it, the game was meant to be more accessible so they could put the emphasis on the story, I get it while I'm frowning upon it, since this is supposed to be Syberia.TL:DR I liked it a lot story wise, I just wish it wasn't so easy compared to previous installments

_childDocuments_.review: This wouldn't be that bad, but it's still a disappointment for someone who's played the previous games. While the technical aspects are well improved, it loses much on the atmosphere.The graphics. It's absolutely beautiful. Really.The characters. Kate goes through some interesting character development here, and even the side characters are more fleshed out than in the previous games. The creators finally managed to make believable characters in contrast to the caricatures of Syberia 1-3.The voice acting. As cringy it was in previous games, especially Syberia 3, it's improved hugely.The puzzles. There are not many of them, and they are by no means difficult, but there are some I really enjoyed solving.The length. While the game is generally slow paced which can draw out play time, it still has more content than any of the previous games.The story. While in general it's decent and flows well, there are some really cringy scenes, especially near the end, including one of the worst WW2 fight scenes I've ever seen. Unfortunately, the death of Mr. Sokal made a noticeable gap in the direction department.The pacing. Cutscenes and dialogues cannot be skipped, which is not always a problem, but when you're trying every prompt multiple times while searching for the secondary objectives in case you forgot something, it can get annoying after some time.The controls. They improved much compared to Syberia 3, but it's still a nightmare. This point-and-click style just does not go well with a fully 3D environment like this. The limited camera angles are really annoying, and it's not even so that they can avoid modelling half the room, as at times it'll just switch around.Consistency. They managed to break the timeline of the first game just so they could shoehorn Hans' creations into a pre-WW2 world. I'd excuse this one, if not for the following point.Originality, or more like the lack of that. While all previous games managed to give something new, something to keep you in awe, this one copy-pasted elements from the first game. An art nouveau style town that seems to be stuck in the '30s? Check. A university that's seen better days, where the rector asks you to fix the music machine on the square? Check. A search for prehistoric creatures? Check. You'll also be visiting a cemetery, an attic or two with artifacts from the past, and even a stamping machine.The ending. Not only did they manage to , they made another sequel hook instead of finally bringing the series to a conclusion. They are clearly out of ideas for the series so it'd be better to just end it once and for all.

_childDocuments_.review: The first three installments of Syberia, caught Kate Walker in a whirlwind of events that she had to follow, ending up being imprisoned in a Russian gulag. 'Syberia The World Before' continues Kate's story from there, allowing players to participate in Kate’s destiny, bringing her story to closure and fulfilling her fate.Unlike its predecessors, 'Syberia The World Before' tells two separate stories. On the one hand, there is the story of Dana Roze, a young pianist who is being persecuted by the Nazis with her family and who bears a striking resemblance to Kate. On the other hand, Kate, who discovers an old painting from Dana in an abandoned Nazis train with looted art and, after escaping, tries to find out who the young woman on the paining is.The two narrative strands make the game very exciting and naturally move closer to each other as the game progresses. It is a detective story, a love story, an adventure and a war story, and while there are brief moments of joy, the game is carried by deep sadness that players empathize and experience. Oddly enough, to me, it's the sadness of the story that makes this game so special.During World War II, Jews were persecuted and killed by the Nazis. The Syberia games always present a parallel world to our actual world. The Jews in this game are called Vagerans and the Nazis are the Brown Shadows. In an impressive way, the game manages to create a personal connection between the victims of the dictatorship and the player, since you get to know the people in the game. This creates intense dismay when one learns that someone has been killed by the Brown Shadows. I found this to be an impressive feat of the game.Storytelling in ‘Syberia The World Before’ is just awesome. Especially the twists towards the end of the game are unpredictable, and the whole story and the behavior of the many protagonists is always believable and realistic. In a way, the game resembles a novel that reaches its climax at the end. As a player, I find that extremely satisfying. All loose ends are brought to a conclusion and the work of Benoît Sokal, who sadly passed away last year, finds a beautiful and dignified ending. And as a bonus, the developers have left a small gap in the door, which allows a possible continuation of Kate Walker's story. It’s wonderful! - masterpiece (I am not using this term lightly)- beautiful graphics- awesome story-telling- wonderful atmosphere- brilliant music- mainly easy to mediocre puzzles, except for the very last one - clever camera movements- changes camera focus for story-telling- very good light effects- very slow paced (not for the restless)- very emotional- mysterious- moments of introspective- scary in isolated moments- intriguing- realistic background noises- mostly realistic body animations, except on stairs- very good puzzles- some puzzles have to be solved by playing in two different times in parallel- perfect mirror reflections- lovely journal- very pretty cut scene pictures- partly very funny after Oscar is back - voice acting sometimes professional, sometimes amateurish - Kate Walker is less pretty than in part 3- one broken achievement, at least for me- requires a XL box of handkerchiefs- almost impossible to take screenshots after about 1/3 of the game without spoiling

_childDocuments_.review: by Microid is a wonderful, magical, captivating and emotional adventure, all packed into a beautiful package with great visuals.I'm a long time fan of the  series of games, all the way back to the first game, both  &  were true classics in the point & click adventure genre, so when  first came out and was mostly keyboard/controller controlled and at first had an ending without any, well, ending, it was not surprised that there were quite a few complaints, Microid eventually addressed all of these, although I'll admit, I didn't get around to try  after these changes and the release of the DLC which I understand changes the ending.So when  was announced I was cautious at first, like many other fans I expect, then I played the free prologue and I was immediately hooked, it was obvious they were taking a step back and trying to go back to the classics, to the origins, so no surprise I pre-ordered the game as soon as I could afford it., which I'll refer to as  from now on in this review for short, did not disappoint, from the very first moment you start the game you can see how visually handsome it is, the menus looks really good, settings menus are well categorized and easy to figure out and set the way you want and don't get me started on the actual graphic, if you have the hardware to run it on high or ultra settings you will not be disappointed.Gameplay wise,  goes back to basic, simple point & click interface, very intuitive and beautifully designed interface makes it fluid and the controls are easy to master, certainly a result that any point & click adventure should aspire too.The camera however during gameplay does suffer from the occasional quirks when the angle makes it a bit hard to navigate, in most cases though, just go back to a previous point before the camera angle changed using the point & click interface and the camera revert back and fixes itself.As for the story,  is the first, full  game developed after the death of original writer , it is not a secret that the game was made, at least partially in his memory, as stated just before the end credits begin to role, the story itself is very well written, it is interesting, it spans over many different years from 1937 to 2005, going back & forth between events of these years, bringing enough mystery, plot twists and interesting tidbits to keep you on your toes and invested in the story the entire time.The story was just emotional enough to make some tears stuck in my throat at some points.Now, let get technical, that is, how the game perform on the technical side, for my hardware at least, which is a pretty high end gaming PC, it performed well on high settings but was a bit choppy at ultra, no major bugs encountered during my playthrough, some weird angles in some areas in some cutscenes maybe, nothing that will hinder your enjoyment, overall  runs pretty smoothly.On the down side, the game only features autosaves, there is no option to save manually, the saving grace is that it saves frequently so it is rare to loose progress and having to repeat sections.What more? Well, The game also features more than one playable character and the ability to switch between characters at certain sections of the game.Voice acting, is in par and probably better than the original two games, not the the 3rd game was bad, not at all. certainly gives the feeling of playing the classic  games while still delivering a modern, high quality visual & gameplay experience.Overall,  is a truly wonderful and very enjoyable experience for point & click adventure players, it builds on the story of the previous games beautifully while taking the story back to it's classic  style, it is visually impressive and in my opinion, could be considered a candidate for a true classic like it's original ancestors. 9/10  10/10  8/10 8/10 7/10 6/10 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this in a Humble Bundle pack and want to heartily recommend it—even for those that don't play video games. It is like watching a cinematic movie with some walking, dialogue choices, investigations and puzzles. There is no combat, but parts are harrowing. You are not the 'chosen one,' you are Kate Walker—a woman riddled with grief at the death of her mother, a woman who is searching for meaning in the past of Dana Roze—only to find find your future. The music is by Inon Zhur (EverQuest, Elder Scrolls, Dragon Age) and is wonderful. I found myself keeping the game open just to hear the various musical melodies. If you want something different than 'saving the world,' and instead a game focus on 'saving oneself,' I highly recommend trying "Syberia: The World Before."

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start, rest in peace to my fellow Belgian, the talented Mr Benoît Sokal (producer of the Syberia games).Now, let's review this masterpiece. And it is a masterpiece, if you are a fan of the point and click story-driven genre. If not, then you might just find it a good game instead.It can be very slow at times though but that's because it's telling a story, introducing and developing each character and letting you explore for bits of backstory. And boy, is the story worth it. They wrote an amazing script, created interesting characters, got top notch voice actors, added a great soundtrack and succeeded in making the game feel like an emotional rollercoaster. To the point where the ending hit a little too close to home for me and being disappointed that the game ended so soon.Graphically, the game is breathtaking. Very detailed and looks amazing on highest settings. It's no Unreal 5 but they squeezed the max out of the Unity engine and it's a beauty. From the vibrant crowded streets to the forests and mountains, almost like looking at a nice painting. Some of the characters look a bit off at times but they're mostly just background clutter so you'll barely notice. Performance was also stellar, no bugs, no crashes, no stuttering and no sudden huge FPS drops.The simplified playstyle,  there isn't much 'pointing and clicking' but a more modern 'hovering over a point of interest' (most of them being completely optional, offering a bit of extra dialogue), felt like a nice upgrade to the usual point and click style. Some of the puzzles felt like they were inspired by The Room, which actually makes a lot of sense to include these as Syberia is set in a steampunk themed universe. Lastly, I enjoyed the controller support as the game handled way better than by using the mouse.There really isn't much to complain about to be honest. Sure, it's a slow game but the environments, story and characters really make up for it. You actually give a ♥♥♥♥, which is rare for a game story these days. You could maybe complain that dialogue can't be skipped but that's just nitpicking to be honest, if you skipping dialogue then this isn't the game for you.Hopefully we get to see a fifth Syberia game as I'm interested to see how the Kate Walker story will end.Would also be interesting to see the first games getting a remaster, they've aged quite poorly and are an absolute bore to play (I came close to finishing the first game but almost ended up in a coma).Also, I love it when games are priced reasonably. This could of easily been a 60€ game. The effort, passion and love that went into this project is insane and AAAAA (♥♥♥♥ you AAAA Ubisoft wankers) worthy. Picked this up on sale and honestly it felt like a super bargain.9/10
