_childDocuments_.review: I didn't write a review for Syberia 3, I finished that game primarily out of respect for the creators who brought the first Syberia to life. While it wasn't THAT bad (the music is so memorable it carries the whole game), I wouldn't really recommend it. A few years later I was very surprised to learn that a new Syberia was in the works. I was honestly expecting only a slightly updated Syberia 3 and nothing more.WelI, I can't remember the last time a developer took criticism so seriously, learned from every mistake and reworked the whole game. Syberia - The World Before is an order of magnitude better than Syberia 3. In fact, it easily matches the original Syberia, and even surpasses it at times. The story takes a new turn, and we finally don't have to chase the Yukols anymore. Thankfully, the automatons are still there, albeit a little more subdued this time. The story is captivating from start to finish, very emotional, a little bittersweet, just the way I like it. All of this is again accompanied by Inon Zur's wonderful score, which is so good that it takes the whole production to a new level. The 3D graphics have finally caught up to the fantastic hand painted backgrounds we had 20 years ago and at times it looks breathtaking. The character models are also much better and more detailed than in Syberia 3. The cutscenes are very well directed and enjoyable. Finally, there are no illogical puzzles in this game, which is commendable.If you are a fan of the original Syberia, I highly recommend this game. I think you probably don't even need to play Syberia 2 and 3 to enjoy this one. I am very sorry that Benoît Sokal passed away during the making of this game, he would have been very proud of the final product. I hope the team delivers at least one more entry in the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? I'd say yes, from the gorgous visual presentation, great voice acting, fascinating real-life/fictional game world to the touching story about topics rarely touched in bigger computer games, this is a great adventure.In a world full of automatons (precision mechanic machines), in a ficitional (German) town in the year 1937, Dana, a young Jewish woman from the Music Academy performs at a public concert. Dark clouds can already be seen regarding the future political developments, while Dana still dreams of going to Paris for a higher (musical) education. In a parallel story, Kate Walker freezes in a Russian prison in the year 2004, forced to work in a salt mine in Siberia, when she hears of the recent death of her mother in New York. You will switch between those stories, and soon find out how they are connected. Both stories are rather dark - don't consider playing if you look for a feel-good story. It has now been nearly 20 years since I finished Syberia (and a bit later Syberia 2), and this game gives me the same vibes. A melancholic story, in a somehow recognizable and yet strange world, with not too difficult puzzles and an emotional story that leads through a number of different locations. It is a fantasy story, but this time even more inspired by real world history than the first games.The world with its automatons is based on the genius work of French author Benoit Sokal, who sadly passed away in 2021. He already designed this world for the earlier Syberia games, but it has never been brought to life in such detail and such great visual quality. It looks more like a movie where you control the main actor(s). Fortunately it is in third-perspective, so you always have a good view of your sourroundings (and I don't get motion-sick). The game is controlled completely with the mouse or gamepad. Move around, click on hotspots (there are a lot), talk to people, move the mouse in the right direction to operate things. To-do lists show your current goals to advance the story, additional information can be found if you explore darker corners. 3440x1440 works, but with black borders on the sides. All characters are fully voiced, but the texts you can find to read are not. The game is saved automatically, cloud saves are supported.Modern point and click adventure in 3D, visually stunning, with a touching story.

_childDocuments_.review: This was definitely the most anticipated game for me in 2022 - and, probably, in a few years. And now I'm extremely happy to say that Syberia is back in its full glory, and maybe even better than ever. At the same time it feels like a very different game now. Not only it is more story-driven, the story itself has pretty much changed its direction this time. While the previous installments of the game were more about bringing fantasy and magic to the world of mundane, The World Before does exactly the opposite by taking us to the gruesome reality of World War II and telling the story that is very human, touching and even hurting at some points. It's way more emotional and personal than the previous games.The gameplay takes a bit of a backseat passenger here - it's rather comfortable than challenging, so to complement the story and not take the focus away from it. Surely, there are tons of puzzles but none of them are going to have you scratch your head and there always are hints and clues nearby. I think I only felt stuck with one particular puzzle and only for a few minutes. But that's perfectly fine - the game has a proper balance of dialogs, exploration and puzzle-solving to keep the player fully engaged all the time. There are no super-long conversations here and neither there are overly complex problems. It's all done in a right proportion.The game is also very well optimized right from the start. I never had a single glitch or performance problem during my 19 hours. So the decision to delay the release seems well justified now. The team has done a great job.In my book this is one of the most well executed adventure games of its generation. It absolutely delivers on every level - the story, the visuals, the music, the gameplay. Such a great way to honor the memory of Benoit Sokal - the creator of the series, who, unfortunately, passed away before this magnificent game was released. 10/10 and a must for all adventure game fans out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia 3 was disappointing, it wasn't worse than the previous two parts but somehow managed to be more annoying and frustrating. STWB departs from the cryptic puzzles from previous games, avoids the difficulty gatekeeping and aims for the main reason to play those games: the universe of Benoit Sokal. The dreamy, nostalgic and romantic Europe that captived Kate Walker shines now in every nook and cranny, everything is detailed in a short of antiquary object porn. Puzzles are just excuses to walk around and enjoy the overdetailed scenery, full of art nouveau and tons of detail with a gorgeus warm lighting. The sense of wonder of the previous games is still there and what was previously a torturous path is now a joy for the senses and a experience that can't be found anywhere else. The music is wonderful as always, but missed the main theme of the saga.The negative reviews don't lie,  frame drops in some places, specially at the beggining and the control, camera and collisions can be a little annoying, but not being a game oriented to action, where you're going to mostly walk, watch and read, .  it's a minor bother compared to how beautiful and pleasant the game can be. It's a peculiar pace where you can relax hearing a full piece of piano or watch some forgotten movie reels, a totally different approach to the usual fast pace of videogames. And the detail level is so hight that being smaller than some open world games it feels more alive and believable. I would love to have the previous games remade in this way, easier to explore and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more of a visual novel than a regular game. Puzzles are overly simplistic and most of the interactions are dumbed down to clicking and dragging the mouse. For me, this is not necessarily terrible. I've actually enjoyed the story and characters, although I certainly wouldn't say this game made as lasting impression as the original Syberia.My biggest problem with this game - and the only reason I leave a negative review - is how utterly unoptimized it is. It uses Unity engine and I guess it's the main culprit. I am yet to see a Unity game that loads fast and performs well. So, I am running this game on 3090 and it tries to use the GPU to its maximum (even at capped FPS), which means a lot of power consumption and a lot of noise from the GPU fans. Does it need all that power? Certainly not. I've underclocked my GPU and the game ran exactly the same but still was trying to use all the GPU's power it could. I've recently played Broken Pieces - an indie game that looks somehow similar to The World Before - and it does not try to ramp up my electricity bill (uses Unreal Engine). Furthermore, I can run Red Dead Redemption 2 at 4K and 60 FPS with GPU fans barely audible.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming adventure game that blends fiction with reality. The game features two protagonists and takes place across two time periods, 1937 and 2005. It's set in the fictional nation of Osterthal that is situated somewhere in Central Europe as it grapples with the rise (and later, the aftermath) of the Brown Shadow. The aim of this game is to discover the link between both protagonists and it does this in some interesting ways at times - for example, often your character in 2005 will read a letter detailing a scene from 1937. You then play out that scene in 1937 and use it to discover solutions to puzzles back in 2005. Though there are some twists here and there, the story isn't really that shocking or unpredictable. You'll probably guess the link between the two characters way before it's actually revealed. Luckily, you don't need to have played any of the past Syberia games to enjoy this one - there are some references to other characters and events, but it's largely a standalone game. Voice acting is overall pretty good, but there are a lot of German words used throughout and you can tell which VAs know how to speak German and which don't.The gameplay is mostly walking around environments, interacting with points of interest and sometimes solving puzzles. Given all this, it's a shame the performance was so inconsistent. I experienced major lag and reduced frame rates in some scenes, even when there wasn't really anything going on to justify it. The game is not fast paced, there are no really graphically-intensive scenes and while the graphics are decent, they aren't pushing any boundaries in a way that might explain the poor performance. Seems to simply be a case of poor optimisation.What I enjoyed most was the set dressing. Most scenes take place in Vaghen, the capital city of Osterthal. Vaghen looks very much like a Germanic city with very gorgeous gothic architecture. What makes it interesting is the addition of automatons - in this universe, an inventor created human-like robots that are built to serve specific purposes, like driving a tram or playing an instrument. Many of the puzzles revolve around fixing the unique, fantastical mechanics that power these machines. I very much enjoyed the way this game blended a believable Germanic city with these steampunk-esque automatons and it was probably my favourite aspect of the game.Performance issues aside, this is a decent standalone game that should take you somewhere around 12-15 hours to complete. The game occasionally gives you some branching dialogue options but the consequences to each are typically minor, not really enough to justify more than a single playthrough. Still, worth picking up if you can get it cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fitting conclusion to Kate Walker's journey! In terms of story, character and plot after the opening section I give it an A++. My only gripes... Control when you are using a mouse is abysmal. Non-sensical. Like an old school adventure game, the character will move to where you click on the map, however the pathfinding for this is horrible, with clicks registering in completely different areas from where your cursor was. The controller set-up is dual stick (limited camera movement) so I'm not sure why they took WASD off the table when the mouse controls are so clumsy?Also--Kate Walker's girlfriend arc in the beginning portion sucked. Her involvement is dropped incredibly quickly and unceremoniously early on in the game, and never factors into the later story. Why give Kate Walker a girlfriend if you're not going to commit to the concept, or have her be involved in any for the rest of the story?Otherwise though, everything with Kate and her family was expertly crafted and engaging. The story and presentation for the majority of the game were truly riveting and a great send off for the character. Arguably better written than previous entries in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing "Syberia" ever since I was 4 years old. My dad was the first to introduce me to this amazing game, who later turned into a small franchise. I've grown with it and I cannot see myself without it. I became very dear to my heart.I just started playing the fourth (and maybe last?) part today and while I haven't explored everything yet, I've already managed to cry a handful of times, both from nostalgia and from grief. I cannot believe Benoit Sokal is no longer among us. However, I'll always remember him as the creator of the game that made my childhood better and sweeter."Syberia" never ceased to surprise the players with its graphics, puzzles and storyline. In my opinion, these are the characteristics that make "Syberia" franchise stand out. Each game takes place inside a unique universe, where the main focus is on the little details, and "Syberia: The World Before" is not an exception. The views are breathtaking and the voice acting is unmatched! I somehow wish I were able to play this game with a VR headset; although, I'm not sure if I'd ever leave such (digital) place, heh.Short update: I finished "Syberia: The World Before". Such a touchy story! The graphics, the camera angles, the storyline... Spectacular! In addition, the political aspect was something I didn't see coming, but I appreciated it a lot, because it made sense for Dana's arc.In contrast to the dark nature of events, I had a good laugh whenever Oscar was interacting with Kate. I'd've never thought he'd make a comeback, let alone as a hedgehog. Brilliant idea!However, what I didn't particularly enjoyed was how apologetic Kate acted towards Olivia in the end. Her friend didn't deserve it, especially since she had had an affair with Kate's fiancee in the first game, who later married in the protagonist's absence.All in all, I wholeheartedly recommend this game to everybody who enjoys playing story-rich games with lots of puzzles. I, personally, am thankful I can replay it two more times, because I've missed a couple of side missions by rushing the game in the beginning. Furthermore, the ending is highly "syberian-esque" and it perfectly reflects Kate's true personality and her deepest desires.

_childDocuments_.review: Seldom do I play adventure games.  However, this one has captured my heart.My first introduction to the series was in the 2000's, with the critically acclaimed original.  The animation in that game caught my breath then, as does the animation of this game now, in 2024.  The setting of this game, namely the European town of Vaghen is a place that I've always wanted to travel to in my dreams -- pleasant, stylish, mixture of modern influences and history.  The visuals are gorgeous, and so is the sound design.  I felt immersed. Some animations can feel janky, but you could tell love was put into every scene.Kate Walker is also a fantastic character.  Her faithful companion Oscar (a robotic automaton) get through many trials and adventures, that it's hearty to seem them again in this one.There is no failure scenario, no way to mess up the game.  You explore, solve puzzles, and advance the story,  It's a fantastic journey and warms my heart.  P.S. I know Syberia 3 gets a lot of hate.  I personally have, but not played through that one.  This one is like a fresh reboot.  Those who've played the past series can note the references and appreciate them, and it doesn't detract away from newcomes who have not.  Overall, I do recommend this game.  It's like reading a novel, one about loss, courage, betrayal, and discovery.  Very few games give me that good feeling nowadays.  It's on sale often on various websites, and I do recommend picking it up.Final note -- the game plays very well with a controller.  I did both the Steam Deck, and on my desktop with an Xbox.  It controls better that way than Mouse & Keyboard.  The exception (no spoilers) being a late game puzzle where you have to move an automaton.  There are arrows on the top and bottom edges of the screen I clicked on to lean the automaton forward and backwards.  It wasn't apparent you could (and how to) do so with the controller, and I actually looked up a guide.Happy adventures.  I hope there will be a follow up to this!

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the first two entries in the series. This game captures that feeling of wonder to almost the same extent. As outlandish as Kate's motivations may seem, it makes sense considering she's an explorer at heart and finds purpose in discovering her ancestry, and really has nothing to go back home too. I think the story is just as good as Syberia I and II, not to mention the game looks gorgeous.I do have one criticism though - and it's not minor. The puzzles are too straightforward. The first two games had some nice head-scratchers that were fun and rewarding to solve. This one doesn't. Personally I care about the story a lot so that supersedes this, but for those who want challenging puzzles, you shouldn't expect that from this game.I hope the series continues. RIP Benoit Sokal.

_childDocuments_.review: It is certainly a very pretty game and is better than the last instalment.  But the story is slow paced, which although it suits its subject, I think if it were a book, an editor would have worked hard on it first. It feels like it missed that stage.The ending is terribly predictable, and I think some will be disappointed. Some have said it is a cliff hanger, but it isn't, I think. It is just a soft ending.One element is definitely missing. In the previous stories, there was always this sense that Kate is being hunted.  She needs to get a move on and time is against her.  Here, there is nothing of that. She can take her time, is never in any real peril (even at the start), and has the luxury of sitting back and thinking. I quite like that, but it might not suit everyone.On the tech side, the backgrounds and the items are beautifully rendered. I love the tram. I would love to be able to explore more of the network. The characters suffer from the normal woodeness of so many games, and limbs sometimes bend strangely. But I have found that in every game I play. The emotions on the faces are not bad. Voice acting is great (which is my thing since I am a voice person!)There are a few bugs where you can get your character stuck. It is mostly to do with the way you control the character. It is not terminal, if it happens - you just have to experiment with a direction! I did find I often missed interaction points simply because I didn't stop in time!Overall I would recommend this game to any fans of the Syberia series. It is a worthy conclusion to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to do this, but Syberia 3 squeaked by without getting a "Not Recommended" review from me, simply because I forgot to write a review after I played it in late 2021.  I've just completed Syberia 4 and this time I won't put off writing the review as a way of getting around the very sad fact that I don't recommend The World Before, either.I wrote a few notes while playing, but there's not much point in using them to create a detailed review.  The game feels wrong at a basic level, and getting into the details isn't needed.I reviewed the Prologue demo when it released two and a half years ago, and after finally getting around to playing the full game, I can say that demo was an excellent representation of the game, for  better or for worse.  I was impressed by the visuals, but worried about the tone suggested by the World War II elements, Kate's sour demeanor and elderly voice actress, and the lack of gameplay in the midst of watching a lot of cutscenes or reading texts.All of these issues I identified back then were throughout the full game.  Sharon Mann is too old to continue portraying Kate Walker in the mid-2000s.  The game is mostly dark & depressing, and references mass death, including children drowning.  The only "whimsies" to be found were the often absurd motivations and decisions made by characters.  The game didn't feel like Syberia anymore.As horrible as the technical aspects of Syberia 3 were, the game felt like proper Syberia.  A lot of the negative Steam reviewers on The World Before say they skipped Syberia 3.  Well, if TWB disappointed you, go back to the previous game in the series.  TWB is greatly improved in stability and polish over Syberia 3, so you'll have to fight through terrible glitches and jank to get that more traditional Syberia experience.I didn't like how focused TWB is on telling its story at the expense of player agency, rather than being an adventure game with a strong character, story and setting, as the original games became loved for.  Some negative reviewers called this a "walking simulator" or interactive movie.  It really is more like that than a traditional point and click adventure game.The storytelling didn't work well for me.  Kate is slowly uncovering the history of the town and the girl she's looking for, but the lack of any immediate stakes, intrigue or urgency made almost all of it fall flat for me.  It was only at the end of the game that I started to feel anything, but even that was ruined by the horrific decision to make the ending another unresolved cliffhanger, as they'd done at the end of Syberia 3.The entire Syberia franchise should have ended here, but instead it will require another game, or the franchise will be embarrassed like every game or movie that ended with sequel-bait that will never get made (the ending of Independence Day 2 was so embarrassing!)Syberia 5 and beyond would have to be made without the deceased founder, B. Sokal, which is an extremely dicey prospect.  He died during production of TWB, and the team that finished the game should have let Kate Walker rest her weary soul.I know a thing or two about weary souls.  It didn't do mine much good to play The World Before.  It didn't deliver the charming adventure I desperately needed at this moment.  I'll ask Sokal if this is truly what he wanted to change Syberia into.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! Syberia has been such a journey from my childhood. I remember receiving the first game on disk. Back on my old little computer. I was around 12 years old struggling to figure out the puzzles. I probably gave away a good 30 hours on playing the first game and trying to solve everything. As a kid the puzzles were super difficult in the first and second game. The story drops you into a beautiful French town which looked slightly abandoned and depressing. As you journey through the industrial cities into what seemed to be Soviet Russia you make it to Syberia. The first two games were incredible. I am guilty of saying i skipped the third mainly due to the reviews. When i saw the 4th installment come out i didnt hesitate to buy it. I love the new touch of throwing us into the past and present. The puzzles in the game were ALOT easier than what we had in the first two games which was something i was a little upset about. At first i thought maybe i was just younger and it was harder to solve but i realized that the team at Benoit sokal made them harder. There was alot of running back and forth to complete just ONE task for Kate. This time around it felt more focused on the story and less on solving. Nonetheless , i found the game to be beautiful and emotional. It teaches a lot of life lessons. I already knew that the game wouldnt end on Kate going back to New York. She is way too stubborn and committed. I am wondering if this is truly the final installment. It would be a shame to not continue this game despire Benoit's death. Its too beautiful and i feel like the cliffhanger they left us on kind of hints at a new game or perhaps a DLC. I think there really is no point of ending the game like that if theyre going to throw Kate onto a train with Ludwig. Let's hope and see. What a great adventure its been. It makes me a little sad thinking that it may be the last one. This game has touched my heart from the very beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: Kate Walker has been my hero since the first Syberia game came out in 1999. She is awesome... smart, relentless, and brave. Plus, she has 'normal' proportions and dresses appropriately for her adventures!  She is a truly awe-inspiring female protagonist.It was with delight that I installed and began The World Before - a new chapter in Kate's life and Benoit Sokol's final masterpiece. I was not disappointed and am sad to have finished the game. It is a darker story than before with an emphasis on love and loss. Kate is world-weary and on a quest for meaning/purpose rather than adventure. The past and present are lovingly threaded together into a beautiful story that comes to a heart-warming conclusion.The artwork and music are spectacular and there are some breathtaking moments. The voice-overs are well done and the game ran flawlessly for me. It is not a perfect game. At times, I would have liked to speed read dialog rather than listening to every word and some of the cut scenes seem to go on and on. The camera angle, when combined with point-and-click navigation, was confusing at times and I found myself circling about, looking for exits in several locations. The automatic save feature is a single point in time so if you miss an achievement, the only option is a new game. This may be a frustration to those wishing to achieve 100%.While The World Before is a stand-alone game, it will be enjoyed more by those who have played the previous Syberia titles and are familiar with Kate's history. I highly recommend this title to those who still love the idea of a point-and-click adventure with well developed characters and an interesting story.

We also enjoyed the little "Escape Room"-like puzzles. Big kudos to the developers. I hope to see another installment of Syberia.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review from someone who did not play ANY the past games:Looking at the reviews(negative) Kate used to be an adventurous person that found joy in the thrill of adventure, well... she is not in this game.I don't mean that "she is gay now so not here" type of thing that I read a lot, she is cautious, depressed, uncertain, scared, and there is no problem with a character being that as long as you have a balance with other characters and we don't... The Dana Roze thing is an extension of the main character and how she learns about everything, so it is not enough... and with the whole Vagaren = Jews in WWII, Dana has a fair share of depressing moments too.I don't care that Kate is gay, what I do care is that she does not care about her dead girlfriend, between her death and the end of the game her name is brought 2x and Kate has 1 scene with her again and there is absolutely nothing else... and those 2 times you can choose other options when explaining to people... if anything, it does feel that it was not a decision made with any intent except marketing.This game, first and foremost, had a story to tell, a message to get to the public so the game cannot be hard otherwise people won't finish it and it is clear to me in the priority of what they developed:1. Graphics2. Story3. Interactivity4. Puzzles1.GraphicsThe game is really pretty and everything has a lot of care into the creation and it shows when every shot is prolonged to show the amazing graphics of a bush, a square, a rock which gets really boring, really fast in trying to get more information from the world.2. StoryThe story has the feeling of a personal story to me, and then put in a game format, since how it starts and how it ends feel disconnected from everything else, and because it is a personal story, it is incredibly short for a game, so you need a sidequest like a trip around the world for something that does not change the game or the story for that matter at all. And it certainly shows when everything regarding Dana is better game-wise and story-wise than Kate, since there was more freedom of creativity with the character, with the exception of the resistance bit, that again felt as a personal message since the characters are elevated so they can all be important and together.3. InteractivityAnd every object you pick can be rotated 3D, another trend for awhile, to show how good the graphics are.After rotating the object you can click on it for an additional information, a key after being clicked is given the incredible information of it being a mechanical key... again, a boring mechanic to show how good the graphics are.Which is a great follow up to my next point...4.PuzzlesThis game hardly has any puzzles, most of them are click, drag, click the other part, drag, click the third part, twist, etc.It follows the "our graphics are awesome" and real logical puzzles are not here, there are 2 head scratches that I found fun, the rest cannot be considered puzzles, just QTEs.This game got the bad trends of modern gaming, and I can't say that this is a bad follow up from the before games, but I can say that it is a bad and boring point & click game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Syberia 3, I was more than a little hesitant to play The World Before, but eventually worked up my courage.  The first hour to hour and a half are a slog of micro-vignettes that don't give you enough to sink your teeth into, and reminded me of the worst of Syberia 3.  After that, , things started to pick up and become very engrossing.  I played through the rest of the game in a single marathon session, and towards the end I didn't want to step away from the keyboard.While the controls are almost the same as Syberia 3, they added the ability to have the character you are controlling be dynamically directed by the cursor, which is much easier and more intuitive, and helps avoid some of the click or keyboard control jenkiness that made 3 such a nauseating experience.  There are still a couple of scenes, particularly around the Music Square in Vaghen, where the transitions are abrupt, jarring, and disorienting, as the character moves around the square, but most of the navigation is much more seamless.  It still would have been much better to give the user full control over the camera and movement like a standard first person adventure rather than this partially locked perspective nonsense, but this game was at least playable without too much difficulty.Where this game really shines is with the story, once it gets started.  It is really engrossing, and more reasonably written than any of the previous games.  Apart from the fact that , everything that happens in this story actually makes some sense in the context of the fictionalized game world.  There are some really bad modelling issues, and some of the animated sequences take MUCH longer than they really should, the story still kept me interested and willing to follow through.  Apart from , the last several hours were an amazing ride, and I would recommend it just from that experience.  Also, the way Oscar comes back in this game makes it worth the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Syberia games, despite the puzzles not always being that intuitive. However, there is a hint system that helps you figure out most of what you need to do. There have been times where I actually had to "sleep on it" before I was able to figure some of them out. I just love this whole story and the latest game has greatly improved on the graphics quality and there are some improvements to the game interaction, as well. I've read a little on the behind the scenes of the making of the game and I think the creators love the story as much as the gaming community that play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my, how grand it was to be back in the world of Syberia!  Set this time in Eastern Europe, this adventure that Kate Walker embarks upon was immersive, compelling and very enjoyable.  My word, what a difference nearly two decades makes since the first two games - two of my all-time favorite games!  The updated graphics are stunning!  And this time, Kate Walker walks and runs a bit faster than she did back then.  Not as quickly as some might have wanted, but you know,  this time it didn't matter.  I was so immersed in walking through the different locations that I wanted to take my time to enjoy the beautiful world created by Microids and Benoit Sokal.  It was well worth it.Travelling to different locations and playing as different characters in the game, both in the present and in the past, makes the game even more immersive.  It was a joy to see the automatons again.  I loved them so much the first time around and the new automatons in this game are even more beautiful!  All the tiny details look so real.  The team did a fantastic job on them.The adventures are not difficult to complete, and the puzzles are all doable.  I only sought advice for two of them.  The ending is very satisfying.  And I'm thinking, or rather hoping, that there might be a sequel at some time in the future.  If there is, I'll certainly be on board!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: it's so sloooow, the dialogs take forever because there always is a delay between the speech files, the cutscenes and filmic transitions are way to slow. the gameplay is essentially about getting the player from a to b and triggering the dialogs and even that doesn't work flawlessly. as much as I like the sceneries and the positive narration this game is very tiresome.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, I played the Lucas Arts classics and this game just doesn't have any fun factor in it. It should be titled Pixel Hunt 2022: Syberia  Basically you progress the plot by finding just the right pixel on some random photograph to trigger the cutscene that causes the game script to open the next progress gate. Srsly? A Real Game works like an electric guitar, you get to jam, the strings in any direction you want and, if it helps, just tilt the thing's body back and forth to get it to reverb exactly the way you want it to, which I saw Jimmy Page do once. This game is a player piano.  That's why Real Games are written like "Did player find a way to reach X?" Ok, advance the plot in this direction, not "did player click exactly pixel 1420 x 893, ok give the player a cutscene and lift the invisible barrier to X." In lots of places these pixel hunts were chained over the same environment requiring you to not just pixel hunt, but find the pixels in the correct order leading to far more frustration. Then you get to a fire escape, Ok, just yeet Sonic the Armadillo up there and boogie. ... NOOOOO Sit there for fifteen minutes just mad clicking the entire building edifice just to find which pixels trigger dialogue, and keep doing it until the progress gate lifts. yeah, you get a nice animation if it were in a movie or a cartoon but I'm not talking about a video game at this point. Don't buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I will premise this review by noting I didn't realize this game was a part of a series, so I started it without playing the first three Syberia games. That being said, overall I understood what was going on. There were a few things here and there which I didn't fully understand as I was missing context from the first few games, but it didn't take away from my experience.Feels like a steampunk, historical Telltale game, though unlike Telltale the choices don't impact the story outcome as much.My one complaint about this game is Kate's voice, the main character. She looks young, but her voice sounds 10-20 years older in my opinion and it irked me, but overall still a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Few games present the heart and enchanting world that is Siberia, and this addition is most welcome.  I feel as if I have returned to a real place I had missed for so long.  Depth of character, poignant story lines, breathtaking music, beautiful scenery and a serious celebration of steampunk all wrapped into one.  I dare to hope there will be a way to follow Kate on further adventures, given the sad passing of Benoit Sokol.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The game acknowledges that Kate, and the franchise as a whole, had somewhat lost their way. Then it goes and forges a different path for both. It injects a good dose of mystery, atmosphere, puzzles, and by the end a feeling of renewed purpose. Some small gripes about the controls and camera really don't take away from just how magical this adventure was. Highly recommended to fans of the series and adventure game fans in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game with a compelling story that pulled me in, making it hard to put it aside when I needed to tend to other aspects of my life.  Its storyline had a great appeal to me as I love historical stories beautifully told, and was gripping in its intensity because the piece of history it told.  The main characters, Dana and Kate,  were each fully realized as memorable  and likable people, motivating me to care about what each had in store.  The sound track was amazingly done, and I plan to buy it if it becomes available. There were high level puzzles throughout, matching the high quality of the game throughout, and the emotional involvement I had with the characters made me take care to get the puzzles right, moving the story along for me, eager as I became to reach the answers Kate sought. furthering my understanding of the story I with them.  which further enticed me me to find the answers to Kate's questions.  I hope there will be more like this forthcoming from this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I would've been happy with what I was expecting...This was so much better than I was expecting. The art direction and writing of this game surpassed anything I was expecting even after reading tons of reviews. The voice acting and adherence to the previously established Syberia universe are excellent too. I can't think of a better send-off to such a unique and captivating series (created by Benoit Sokal (RIP)). I really hope this team goes for a sequel but even if they don't I'll just replay this game every few years until I die. 10/10Edit: Got to add one more "expecting"
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a complete masterpiece. The graphics and soundtrack are stunning, but the story is completely captivating and emotional. Every bit of care was taken to ensure that it is as immersive and detailed as possible, down the angles of the scenes, the motion capture, and especially the "Introspection" moments which added such depth to the characters. This game is up there with the first entry in the series as a divine work of gaming. It fixes everything that went wrong with the third installment and is actually playable, even with a point and click interface, but is also controller-compatible. A worthy swan song for Benoit Sokal.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I haven't finished the game at the time of writing this review.I love Syberia 1 and 2. Especially 1 got to me with the styling and narrative of the game, it just clicked with me. Second one is really like a part 2, like finishing eating already bitten apple, if you know what I mean. Third one was a bit of a let down on the story side, locations and puzzles were still good and tranformation to 3D went well.Then I started to play the last game in series (so far). And I'm blown away! The idea of different timelines seemed weird to me, but it started to form awesome story thoughout the game. Once again - the game is beutifully done, visual styling fits the Syberia universe, locations are amazing, people have personality, puzzles are creative and well done... This is true successor to Syberia 1 and 2.For complete experience, I would highly recommend to play all three previous games before going into this one - there are simply too many references to miss if you haven't played them. You will get hit by nostalgia and have a laugh at some of them.I still don't know how the game would end, but that won't change my recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember the first time i stepped into adventure games on PC, it was through Syberia 2, that game made me a fan of a world of games driven by deep storytelling, narrative,  music, and extraordinary experiences. For years I was waiting for this game's successor, and finally Syberia 3 came out.. oh.. what a disappointment. It reminded me of Broken Sword Angel of Death, poor gameplay mediocre story..I felt disappointed, and thought that was the end of Syberia world on PC. About a year later, I started to jear about this game, The World Before, and I got my hands on the demo,, I had a mixed feelings, the bitter taste of Syberia 3 was causing that.. but I decided to play it when it comes out. The game really makes up for any lacking, issues, negative experience from the last game. Actually, by today's benchmark for adventure games. it ticks all the right boxes: great visuals, great story, great puzzles, great music ! and it really manages to build more deeper connection with the main character Kate Walker. If you are a fan of Syberia, you will love this game. If you are a new player stepping into the world of Syberia, this game is so welcoming that it will make you excited to play the older ones too (Syberia 1 and 2, i would still skip 3 and watch youtube walkthrough or the recap video in this game that summarizes the events ). I can easily recommend it to all adventure game players, I was also able to play a great portion of this game on my Steam Deck with no issue. My personal rating would be 9/10.. i really haven't played such games recently that made me this much excited.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The story is a great continuation from before, even though a bit unrealistic at times, but hey, for the sake of the story. . .Like when Kate and Katyushka find that old motorbike from the WW2 era. Realistically, it's tires would be flat after all those decades of just sitting there being unused; the oil in it would be gummed or dried up and gone, simply not really usable. The story goes on though. . . :PBut I'm enjoying it. And if you have all the 3 other Syberia games prior to this one and enjoyed the story, it's still a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, a must for narrative adventure lovers and for fans of the previous Syberia games. Pros+well written, gripping and emotional story that spans between two timelines, with an open ending that makes me hope there will be a sequel+really gorgeous environments and atmosphere, especially in the city of Vaghen+immersive cinematic narration. Sometimes the game feels like a movie+15-20h to complete it is really manageable, and appropriate for the quality of the game and for its price tag+a relaxing experience overallCons-puzzles are a little bit on the easy side, and don't really require much logical thinking to be solved-walking around can sometimes be frustrating, as Kate likes to get stuck between the scenery's props, and there are a lot of them really close together-unskippable dialogues and cutscenes. This is probably a design choice, as the game really likes to take its time showing how beautiful the world the devs crafted is, but it can get annoying. I wish that they at least gave the option to skip a dialogue that you've already heard.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished a "binge-playthrough" of the four Syberia games. I did play through Syberia, Syberia 2, Amerzone and the less well known Paradise, but that was when those games were new. Playing the Syberia games one after the other, made it a more rewarding experience.So, in rating Syberia - The World Before, I must of course compare it to the previous games.  And I find it superior in every way. It is extremely beautiful, the puzzles are sometimes tricky, but never to the point that one must give up. It tells a good story which wraps up the whole series. Syberia 3 tried to do some of the more advanced things that S-TWB does, but has a frustratingly complicated interface. But this time they got everything right. Perhaps I could have complained a bit still, but after muddling through Syberia 3, there really isn't anything to complain about here.Regarding the main plot, it was so obvious that I figured it out already in the introductory section of the game. Still, it manages to side track you a few times. This adventure leaves you with the same feeling you get when you finish and put down an 800 page long novel. That is not bad for a "mere" game. The playthrough took me 18 hours, which I think is acceptable for this kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics and touching story. I played it in German with English subtitles, and that was a perfect fit for Vaghen, where all the written texts are apparently in German anyway. I had not played the previous games in the series, but now I'm inspired to start working my way back through!If you like this kind of relaxing, story-rich type of game with lots of conversation and a some light puzzles, check out the Dreamfall series, especially Dreamfall Chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: My childhood is back: I played the first two games as a kid so the Syberia games always hold a very special place in my heart. I was deeply impressed with this one - it doesn't disappoint and does the original games justice as well as being more about stories and characters this time around, all while exploring new ways of narration. I adore it completely. ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Syberia since childhood with my father. Honestely, he's the one who loved the first Syberia. Later on, when he started to play second game, I've decided to give it a shot. Not even a small regret.After a decade, my father and I played the 3rd game. I've already finished both of these last two games, and I hope my father will finish it as well, because it's a whole story, which I want him to know.Since the first day we've helped Oscar to get on his feet, never ever I thought of him badly. He's a true friend, which will make us smile and hate him at the same time, because he needs a valid train ticket. And there you go, we are at the finish line, making the best ticket we possibly can, because we now appreciate the automatons.The story about Dana is spectacular!!! Tragic and painful, yet so beautiful and elegant.Now, I want to play it on English or French. I wish I had more time...I highly recommend to play this game, especially for the Syberia fans!Thank you, Benoît Sokal for everything!

_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the entire series on sale. i had known about it for decades and always told myself i wanted to play. the ratings of the newest entry had me pull the trigger. As I played through the first three, I had become slightly disheartened. First one is Amazing, the second one stayed true, but the third one drifted away from what made the first two so whimsical. This games is not only a fantastically well written/paced narrative but the puzzles and mechanics are high quality too! Most importantly (to me) its a visual FEAST. I was blown away by the set design, cinematography, mise-en-scene, etc. etc. Stick with the series so you can make it to this GEM. 10/10 for me <3

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an avid Sibera fan, but this newest development I found very disappointing. It plays like a boring movie with dull characters and bad controls. I encountered maybe three puzzles in the first two hours of gameplay. The rest was talking, walking, and swiping left to open doors.The pros: Absolutely gorgeous scenery, and I really like how you can see that little inner ring in the character's irises. Cons: I wish they spent less time on making pretty avatars and more time on incorporating actual puzzles and mystery into this game. It's infuriating how often the characters refused to run and how regularly they walked away from the point I clicked on. When there is something to click the mouse cursor disappears entirely, making it difficult to solve any mechanism with multiple parts to interact with.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pleased to share that Syberia - The World Before did not disappoint, particularly after my dissatisfaction with Syberia 3, which I couldn't bring myself to complete. While the puzzles may have been easier than in previous episodes, the compelling story and emotional undertones more than compensate for any shortcomings.It's a fitting tribute to the late Benoit Sokal, and a promising continuation of the beloved Syberia saga.

Well devs, You have made a well produced game. I thank thee.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s been almost 20 years since I played the first Syberia in 2002. The first games were really much like many adventure games of that time, with a strong story presentation in the first few hours, and then mostly puzzles to advance to the next tiny bit of story or cutscene. The excellent world building and visual design by Benoït Sokal was already there, and displayed lots of details and creativity, that was what differentiated Benoït Sokal’s games from the rest. In terms of story though, they were minimal, those games played more like a graphic novel with a short script. One of the few high quality AA adventure game of those years nevertheless, and they were indeed different from the ones that came before or after.Benoït Sokal did have some good games over the twenty-five years that passed between Amerzone and the latest Syberia. He continued evolving and improving on several aspects of his games, many of which he did with his own game studio “White birds productions” with total freedom to pursue new stories, but somehow, all those games never achieved the same type of success the first Syberia had... and still interest was going strong for a new Syberia game. None of the games released with his own studio exceeded that and after many years he had to close down. It was then in 2017 that after 15 years Syberia 3 released… the game was just not good unfortunately. Gameplay wise, and story wise. The visual design and world building by Sokal were there, but the rest of the game elements just didn’t work. You could even say the visual presentation by Sokal was, comparing it to the first two games, “uninspired”.Another three years passed and it was in the middle of a Pandemic in 2020 that a new Syberia game: Syberia 4 (The world before) was announced and in the form of a playable demo. I think many people (including yours truly) were skeptical, although the demo was certainly intriguing and it was possibly, one of the main reasons, that I've played the game and that I’m writing this review now.Syberia 4 is the absolute best by far of this series and one of the best adventure games period. The team that worked with Sokal learned of their previous experience and developed a game that is as beautiful to look at as it is fun to play. You could say the game plays “smooth” as there’s a constant “flow” of actions the player does as well as the camera that follows our character and the story the game tells as it keeps the narration going at all times, the gameplay moving and taking the player for a ride. This time, the story takes center stage. You do play your character(s) and you are first place doing everything, but everything you do through gameplay ties to the main narrative, and it is full of surprising and emotional moments. The characters are endearing and interesting and you will care about them.  But what’s more effective this time around, are the several links this fictional story has with real world events. Although this is a fictional setting, its ties to historic events (second world war) brings more weight to what is happening in game. The subjects this game brings forward though are not limited to a specific historic period and they ring true to many periods in time. It is the beauty of Syberia The World Before: their characters are faced with universal themes that are recognizable and relatable.The story in this game is fascinating and gripping all the way until the end and the game mechanics are well designed, modern and updated for the first time in years for an adventure game… it is the perfect combination of world design, visual design, character creation, game story, gameplay, music and sound design (the music in this game’s story really plays an important part). It is then sad, and almost poetic in a way, that the creator of this series, Benoït Sokal, passed away some months before the game release in 2022 without probably seeing how the final product turned out to be and how well it was received after all these years. It is also, a great send off to his life’s work and truly the best adventure game we could ever get from Msieur Sokal and the team that worked with him all these years. A true work of passion and undeniable heart put in every step of this timeless adventure. I’m not crying you are crying! This review is
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: For me, it was worth it to play through the whole Syberia series just to get the full range of emotions out of this latest entry. Gorgeous music, beautiful visuals, wonderful voice acting, engrossing story, and logical puzzles that don't frustrate all that much. This game feels like a more proper way to modernize an old point and click style adventure game series then the not so good 3rd game's attempts at doing the same thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The game succeeds at its attempt to charm the player with unique puzzles and interesting story.Even though this review is positive. I would like to provide the viewer with some discretion:- If you're a Syberia fan like myself, you should know that this game does not have the same setting and spirit as it had in the previous games. It plays it in its own unique manner, which is neither better or worse, so don't build your expectation early as it can harm your experience - play it as a new game with familiar characters.- The content of the first chapter can color you confused. Don't take it seriously and worry not as it has no actual meaning in the story that is to fall on you later.- The game in the beginning may appear so simple that it's actually boring, but difficulty will gradually increase over time, so make sure not to lose the interest on the lame first third of a game - this game is worth your time.While other reviews are surprisingly left shocked by the beauty and quality of the game, I can feel that I had slightly more blandish experience. The graphics are decent, no matter lots of minor bags. Audio design is done well in most of the scenes. The quality of storytelling could have been polished way thoroughly. Though, the game does still feel like it has been treated with a big chunk of love from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game (and its prequels), it has an enchanted atmosphere. Voice acting was great once more and I enjoyed the beautiful graphics. It is a real resource hog for your computer, my cpu was regularly at a 100% load (3900 AMD 12 core) but it brings you a very nice presentation of a wonderful game.I highly recommend this game to all fans of the syberia line of games, the only regret I have is that I finished it so soon :)
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia – The World Before is a compelling point-and-click adventure, marred by minor technical hiccups like mission objectives occasionally failing to load (in my experience). Nevertheless, it remains overall a worthy tribute to the late Benoit Sokal, delivering an atmospheric and distinctive experience that, in my opinion, expands on Kate Walker's story wonderfully.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a good addition to the four parts of Syberia! I enjoyed it very much although I didn't feel the same as while playing Syberia 1 & 2.. But it is definitely worth your time. I really liked the stitching of the past and the present. It is story rich and a bit slower pace than I would have liked
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the best entry in the series!I randomly found and played the Demo. And it was the first time I've heard of "Syberia". I got the other three games for 33 cents each and this one for the full price.If you like the Demo, you'll love the game and the whole series!But you should play them in order: starting with Syberia 1 to 3 and ending with this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game. I cried like I hadn't for a log time. The plot is aversome. Plot twists are sometimes predictable, nonetheless dramatic and surprising. Music is fantastic. Aspecialy The hymn of Vaughan, which makes me cry every time I hear it. He touches on memories and stitches the story into a whole. For me Syberia - The World Before is a perfect continuing of the Kate Walker story. The game unmatched continues the spirit of Syberia universe. As a kid I started to walk with Kate on her journey, which became a part of me. I want to say a big thank to creator of the this story for making a light of hope in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: If you are here for the story, then go for it.. if you like challenging games, then this game is not for you. I used to play the Syberia series (games 1 and 2) with my dad, and we loved that they were both challenging and entertaining. Unfortunately, the new games lost that, so I can't even find myself wanting to finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia: The World Before is a beautiful game that is more an interactive story than a point and click adventure game. Although the story is split between Kate Walker and Dana Roze, for the first time in the series it took the time for Kate to reflect on her life and her crisis, and the story was actually good with the focus on the characters than just the plot. The best moments in the game are the quiet introspections where you can do nothing and just watch our characters contemplating about their emotions and their live. The environment is beautiful, Vaghen is a fictional city that is frozen in time in 2005 as it was in 1937. It's a satisfying end to the series. Thank you Benoît Sokal, you'll be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I love Syberia 1 and 2. Those are two of my all time favorite games and hold such a special place in my heart. I was cautious going into this game because I felt really underwhelmed by Syberia 3. It didn't have nearly the same spark as the original games. I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of wonder and even feelings of nostalgia this game brought me. The story is beautiful, captivating, and heartbreaking at some points. I truly loved this game and will play it again to get the achievements I missed the first time. Probably after playing 1 and 2 again.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: you will enjoy this game If:- You don't mind clunky and slow character movement and environment interaction- You love Clockpunk setting and Art Noveau vibes- You want to enjoy beautiful views in peace and listen to what characters have to say.- You are looking for an interactive story with a few puzzles to solve- You are looking for a slow paced game, I mean it! It is slow.You will NOT enjoy this game if:- You want a lot of puzzles, difficult puzzles: puzzles are not difficult and are not many.- You want quick action/combat: there is no combat to perform, there aren't quick actions to do, this is a slow game.- You want a long game: the game is less than 15 hours or around 15 hours If completionist. Can be more hours If you just enjoy the environment and walk around observing things.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that if you are looking to play a nice Syberia type game, this is not it.  The only part of this game that felt like a Syberia game was the very end.  Thankfully, Kate was voiced by the same person as the other games but they ruined the way she looks.  They also ruined Oscar's looks, voice, personality, and charm.  There was only one likable person - Dana.The controls are awful.  If you click to move over here, you end up way off over there someplace.  If you click what you think is a certain hot spot, chances are it's not the one you thought it was.  Part of that had to do with camera angles I guess though.  Puzzles are not too fun, and made frustrating by the inventory and cursor control at times.  There are some puzzles you cannot back out of until you complete them which is a no-no in my book.The story is predictable, though it may interest some.  It didn't much matter to me.  There are numerous cut scenes that drag on just too long.  Shorter would have been better.  The scenery all felt like it was behind a haze and I couldn't enjoy it.  I never, ever felt like I was in the game walking around like I did in the three prior games.I love the first three games but this one disappointed me.  I'm pretty sure if they make a fifth game, it will also disappoint me as I am not a "Planet of the Apes" person.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece of graphic adventure, and one of the best games I have ever played. The game takes you on a magical journey through the enchanting cities of eastern Europe, both in 1937 and 2004, as you piece together the puzzles and mysteries of two lives entwined together. The game is full of stunning visuals, captivating music, and memorable characters, all created by the late Benoît Sokal, a genius of storytelling and art. His story has left a lasting impression on me, and I will never forget the emotions and wonder I felt while playing this game.If you are a fan of point and click adventures, or just love a good story, you owe it to yourself to play the Syberia series, which started in 2002 and has become a classic of the genre. Whomever does not get around to playing this series is doing themselves a Great disservice. If I ever find myself in Paris, I'll be sure to visit the Microids HQ to pay my respects. Thank you for such a wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: -  Rich and interesting characters and relationships,-  Beautiful and detailed locations with amazing atmosphere,-  Very well-crafted narrative that make you want to lose yourself in the world and learn more about it,-  No words for the soundtrack: 10/10 Had to buy the LP!-  Well Optimized: Had no problems running the game at High settings in 4K resolution.If you’ve played the other Syberia games and you enjoy them, you will certainly love this one!It’s for sure a game I will be recommending to my friends!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia - The World Before is a beautiful game. I confess I played with a YouTube Walkthrough but still was able to solve many of the puzzles without help. The game never crashed on my 64-bit Win 10 PC. I  recommend it patient players who love a good story and like to solve puzzles that are clever but not impossible.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who had never even heard of this series before, this game was nothing like I had expected it to be based off the trailers alone, but I'm very glad I decided to play it. The environments are absolutely stunning, the music is fantastic (but it's Inon Zur, so who can be surprised by that), and the story, albeit somewhat strange at times, definitely had me gripped from the very beginning. Each character has quite a lot of personality, and the way they all interact together definitely keeps you engaged. The swapping back and forth between present day and the past was an interesting story-telling mechanic, but I will say, I definitely feel like I enjoyed the historical sections more than the modern sections, mostly because the historical sections show things as they happen, and the present day ones (until the game's finale) are mostly just set-up for how Kate Walker actually learns about the past. The puzzles aren't anything too difficult, so don't expect a ton of heavily involved gameplay, but if you don't mind that, then get ready to immerse yourself in an incredibly detailed, well-acted, enjoyable adventure through the fictional city of Vaghen and its rather grim history.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this game is visually beautiful. The scenery and settings are breathtakingly beautiful, and the storytelling is cinematically directed, with beautiful camera work and lighting. It is just a joy to watch.The gameplay is OK - some exploration, some simple puzzle solving, some decision making (although I don't think how you choose to interact with the characters ultimately really changes the story progression much). It does feature timeline switching between the present day and the past, which is a bit of fun. You also get to play as different characters in the story from time to time.Mostly, it's just beautiful to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely an AMAZING game and storyline. I finished the series halfway through Syberia 2, never completing it or the third installment in the series, so I was reluctant to purchase this one but I'm so so glad I did. It has a "Previously on..." on the main page to catch you up to par with what all happened, and it very quickly engrosses you in the new storyline. It was exciting every time I would get a new cutscene, slowly unravelling more of the story. I have never been so engrossed in a game's story since the original Mass Effect trilogy. Gosh, it was just so so good. That's all I can really say. I just finished it after 20 hours of gameplay, unlocking all the achievements. I REALLY hope for another one in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing. The environments, the dialogue, the animation and voice acting, all of it was superb. For one of the very first puzzle-adventure games, from the days of MYST, the Syberia series has only gotten better, maturing like a fine wine, with all the flavour and nuance you could ask for. Though a sequel may not be in the offering, this is a wonderful end(?) to a beautiful series.

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you make a good sequel! _childDocuments_.review: Welcome in fourth installment of Syberia Franchise. Firstly i must say this game is gorgeous with it's graphics, atmoshphere, music, details. The story in this sequel is more personal touch about Kate Walker and her connections to history of her family really. Very deep emotions and good written story, Benoit Sokal went with his team back into the roots of the Franchsie and delivered masterpiece of great quality. This game i would recommend specially for players and people who likes Syberia and Kate Walker and Oscar. You will find out interesting puzzles and solutions. Some are easier some are bit more of complex but the game this time tells you advices or tips. So you don't really need to google out solutions and spoil yourself. Im happy devs improved controls and optimization of Unity Engine from previous sequel and focused on old style point and click. Microids shows that even in 2022 point and click Adventure can be amazing experience and the immersion in this game is everything. I did grow up on this Franchise so yes i really dig this game even more than previous one. (Even though each sequel has something special and charming, and i recommend play all games before playing this one honestly.) The introduction of new additional Character Dana is huge plus. It feel like refresh of The Franchise. And also it feels like new saga journey about Kate Walke. But i don't want spoil anything. You really need to play it, if you would love to know Katy Walker's personal life and her deep likes and dislikes. I do not know what should i say more really. Just buy it now, it's worth the price for 15+ hours fun or wait for discount if your money is bit tight on your waller atm.+ Story is just *chef kiss*+ Kate Walker + Oscar + Dana+ Atmosphere+ Benoit Sokal+ Soundtrack is Masterpiece+ Puzzles+ Play as more characters when story develops+ Automatons are even more fun+ Immersion, graphic, details, locations- This time nothing, really...yeah.   Im giving 10/10, why? Because devs really redeemed themselves from Syberia 3 and delivered what us players wanted, classic point and click adventures with such a nice puzzles, story and characters. I hope they will continue going this way. And...Rest in Peace and be in our memories Benoit Sokal♥

_childDocuments_.review: Kate Walker is back!What a game! I litteraly could not put it down from the moment I started, I just had to turn the page/read the next chapter/watch the next episode whichever metaphor for being completly absorbed in a great story is relevant for you. _childDocuments_.review: Syberia: The world before is just beautiful. The music blends in perfectly with the story and the visuals are simply breathtaking. As a fan of the Syberia series I was really impressed, especially since Syberia 3 which was not so good (couldn't even play it). _childDocuments_.review: Syberia - The World Before is an enchanting odyssey that beckons players to immerse themselves in a meticulously crafted world brimming with charm, mystery, and adventure. As a fervent fan of the Syberia series, I approached this latest installment with both anticipation and nostalgia, and I am delighted to proclaim that it surpasses expectations on every front.From the moment I stepped into the shoes of protagonist Kate Walker, I was whisked away on a journey that transcends the ordinary. The game's narrative is a masterpiece, intricately weaving together elements of steampunk, history, and fantasy to create a tapestry of intrigue that kept me engaged from start to finish. The characters are richly developed, each with their own motivations and secrets waiting to be uncovered, adding depth and complexity to the overarching storyline.One of the hallmarks of the Syberia series has always been its breathtaking visuals, and The World Before is no exception. Every scene is a work of art, meticulously rendered with stunning attention to detail. From the snow-capped mountains of Syberia to the bustling streets of early 20th century Europe, each location is a testament to the talent and dedication of the developers.But what truly sets Syberia - The World Before apart is its sense of exploration and discovery. As Kate, players are given the freedom to roam the world at their own pace, uncovering hidden secrets, solving intricate puzzles, and forging meaningful connections with the characters they encounter along the way. Whether navigating treacherous landscapes or unraveling the mysteries of ancient civilizations, every moment is filled with a sense of wonder and possibility.In conclusion, Syberia - The World Before is a triumph of storytelling, gameplay, and visual design. It is a game that not only honors the legacy of its predecessors but also pushes the boundaries of what is possible in the adventure genre. Whether you're a longtime fan of the series or new to the world of Syberia, this is an experience that should not be missed. So grab your coat, pack your bags, and prepare to embark on an unforgettable journey into the heart of The World Before.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. As a long time fan of this series, Syberia TWB blew my expectations out of the water. Point n' click adventure games have been an interest of mine for most of my life at this point, and this is easily one of my favorites. Syberia goes a bit more towards a Telltale/Life is Strange way of gameplay here and it is a conversion that works perfectly. Still, everything that makes Syberia unique still remains, including tons of old machine and toy tinkering that feels more satisfying than before. If you want action though or to feel constant gameplay... I mean, I'm sure you can see that this just isn't that type of game, so I can't recommend it at all for those looking for that.First of all, this game is simply beautiful. Not just visually, but the music and composition of everything just feels so scenic. From the backgrounds and character designs to the wonderful music and storytelling, I kept thinking about how this is definitely one of, if not THE, most beautiful game I've ever played. After that I feel like I can't say much more without ruining anything. Kate Walker shows more character than ever before and truly feels real. The other characters also convey an authentic way of thinking and developing to the point that I became interested in even insignificant characters and ones with low screen time.Again, I'm not even sure if this is much of a review because I feel like I can't even go into detail without ruining part of the experience. My advice is, if you're a fan of the adventure game genre, or if this piques your interest, you should just try it for yourself. This is more of a game that I felt than I game that I played. Yes, it's a grown man cry type of game, and I'm very glad I got to experience it. This is at least a 9/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start by saying that this is one of the best point and click games I've played in years. As a big fan of the genre, I was blown away by the gameplay, graphics, story, sound, and controls. I had the pleasure of playing on both the Steam Deck and PC, and found the controls to be intuitive and easy to use – in fact, you can pretty much play the whole game using just a mouse.One thing I really appreciated about this game was its easygoing pace. Although there were a few tedious puzzles, overall I found the experience to be enjoyable and engrossing. In fact, I enjoyed it even more than the new Monkey Island, which was also great.The atmosphere of the game was another highlight for me. From the music to the visuals, everything just came together perfectly to create an immersive and engaging world.Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves point and click adventures. I'm eager for more games in this series – and I have a feeling that anyone who plays this one will feel the same way!"

_childDocuments_.review: Captivating storytelling, beautiful art and music sweep you along a through a tale of love and loss, set in an parallel history covering the late 1930's to the present day.  The game plays as a historical detective  interactive fiction,  organised as a series of 3D explorable locations reachable using the network of tram lines.  In each area you explore as you search for information, repair machinery where necessary and interact with the other characters to move the plot on.  These elements are blended so seamlessly that you can live the story .Navigation around the world is by point and click, which works well most of the time, but can lead to your character looking in the wrong direction when they stop.  Supposedly one can rotate the camera using right click + mouse, but the amount of rotation seemed limited using a trackpad.  Possibly better with a real mouse.  The game played well on a core i7 laptop with 6GB Geforce 1060 graphics on Medium Settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Loved the storytelling, the twists, and the character development even the smaller characters had some depth to them. I had so much fun, and it reignited my love for these games. Everything about Kate is so perfect, she's strong-willed, determined, and adventurous, and her independence to continue down the unbeaten path. I was so impressed to see that this story revolves around strong leading ladies, Dana, Leni, and Colonel Blake as well as Kate, there aren’t too many games that are like this. It was so hard to press pause and although some puzzles were easy to solve there were a few that took me a hot minute to figure out.  Much like the first two games, it was over too soon, and I’m itching to see the next part of this story.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the franchise for a few years now and can't say enough how much I love this addition to the series. _childDocuments_.review: An incredible game.  It took me about 15 hours to complete without looking up hints.  The beautiful visuals and atmosphere is what initially attracted me to the game, but I was not expecting the story to be so good.  The story took a bit to pick up, but once it did it just didn't stop and I was glued.  The twists were definitely unexpected and heart-wrenching.  The game can be played with only a mouse and there are no "quick time events" so it is a very cozy experience.  I wish I could replay this game for the first time again, and now I'm really hoping for a fifth game in the series!  This is everything modern Nancy Drew should be but likely never will.
