_childDocuments_.review: Not too much to say. If you were disappointed by Syberia 3 and by extention scared of this game, I would say give it a try. Syberia 4 is a great game, even if I have my slight issues. Puzzles tend to be very easy (I turned off hints and still found them easy), but I'd rather have this than puzzles making me have to go and look them up. Other problems of mine would be the set up for the adventure in this specific installment, where things just happen a tad to quickly and motivations are thin at best. At the end of the day though, the game is truly fantastic. Looks great (played on ultra settings) and the OST is, imo, the best in the franchise. I never had any real technical issues either, game controls great and outside of a bug where I just had to close and open a game I didn't encounter any such issues. Characters are all solid too for the majority (minority tied to "motivation" issues spoken of earlier).Overall, I recommend this, but do make sure to play 1 and 2 first! And read a synopsis or something for 3, it really isn't worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game was beautiful. I was a fan of the first game, buying it on a CD in a store back when it came out and running it on a computer that could barely run it. I adored the second game, getting to find out what happened. Then the third game greatly disappointed me and I thought that would be it.I'm so grateful that time and love was given to this world again. I actually teared up often. I was also overjoyed Kate's original voice actress returned and I think she did so well! Unlike ANY of the previous games this also ended in a place that both made me both hopeful and curious .I WILL say, the relationship at the beginning seemed to have been forgotten through a majority of the game... which is a bit sad because that also was beautiful even if a little cliche of a way for it to end because you know it was going to happen. I don't think this game is so much a tone shift from the series but a tone shift back towards the first game which had lots of themes and imagery of some sort of post war soviet automaton region that you had to struggle to get through because of poverty and blight.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A nice game, although could be a little slow at times. Lots of cinematic interludes that you have to watch. The atmosphere is great and the story line good. First run through took me around 18 hrs. I did seek help for a few bits I got stuck on. If you like a good story, lots of puzzles and a very chilled relaxed pace, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A tale of two...When I first booted the game and played through the prologue, I was about to uninstall it and call it a day. I was upset, disappointed that the Syberia I always loved (yes, even the third episode), was gone and forgotten, with an unrecognizable Kate, clunky gameplay, weird graphics.However, I was given the advice to keep playing past the uninspired ideas, chain of absurd coincidences, voices, face design and characters of the first few hours of game.And so it happened that at about half game of boredom and yawns, it HIT ME like a freight train: that second part was a MASTERPIECE, so excellent and sublime in literally everything, that it quickly overshadowed and faded away any recollection of the beginning I didn't like.I don't want to delve too much into spoiler territory, but suffice to say that the sections set from 1937 on, THE WORLD BEFORE, with their characters, friendships, love, dreams, drama and tragedy is among the pinnacles of videogame history. Following the heart wrenching story of Dana Roze, of her Alpine Lover, the excruciating secrets of Leni, the surprise appearance of Ludwig... these are PEOPLE I will never forget, a story that can't help but bring to mind those of many other real people, with hopes and dreams, love and family, who lived during that real WORLD BEFORE, a world at war. A world where you were not granted a tomorrow with your loved ones. Stories maybe told to us by our grandparents, who think lovingly and with tears in their eyes of THEIR world before, a world that in this day and age seems more and more faded, forgotten, replaced by the comparatively silly "problems" of our postmodern societies.I didn't like the "World now" of this game (Kate and her shenanigans), but I loved the World before sections. A tale of two cities, two times, two individuals and... almost two reviews?I absolutely recommend this game to anyone and everyone. Just hang in there, keep pushing, go past those first few hours of story and character building  and you will be greatly rewarded.Now to go a bit more in depth regarding the + and - of the gamePositives:- The music is on a complete different level with any other game I have ever played before. It is simply sublime.- As I mentioned, the characters from the world before and their whole plot are unforgettable.- The adaptive triggers in my Steam Deck allowed for a more immersive experience, with puzzles and parts of the game relying on this feature BEAUTIFULLY.- The backgrounds and vistas are absolutely stunning.Negatives:- As already mentioned, the prologue + first 5-6 hours of game seems having been put there as a quick, uninspired afterthought, without much connection to the story, except for the quest "item". Too many coincidences, and stretches. The  QUEST wasn't very convincing, the whole traveling around the world for years in pursuit of a... sketch that is supposed to look like the protagonist, but it really doesn't...  An uninspired, boring Kate with a veryyyyyy slow paced story and cringy dialogues.- The auto save function doesn't let you save whenever you want, a detriment to accomplishment seekers- The movement is clunky to say the least and it looks like a 2005 game published in 2021. The faces look weird, hair and eyes are not on par with the fantastic backgrounds.In conclusion, as my personal opinion, it almost looks like Syberia 4 is made of TWO games. The world now (Kate) and the world before (Dana). The two will expectedly connect at the end, and they do it BEAUTIFULLY, making up for this perceived split of quality and plot during the game. Everything comes together, everything makes sense, and the tears WILL FLOW.I loved the world before, I didn't very much feel the same for the world now, but I will never, ever, forget the lives of those characters. Dana and Leon, Leni, Junta and Ludwig  will stay with me like no Life is Strange, no Quantic Games has ever done before.My Curator page:
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful! Simply beautiful. I have played many amazing games over the years, but no other game fits this particular description more than Syberia TWB. Benoît Sokal and Microids have really outdone themselves this time.The game runs buttery-smooth. The graphics and the art style are amazing. Ostherthal is a lovely location, whether we're exploring the beautiful city of Vaghen or its country side. I could not stop spamming my screenshot button. Inon Zur's music is unforgettable and I'm definitely adding some tracks to my playlist. The voice acting is phenomenal, which is very welcome after the somewhat-disappointing third instalment.The game takes place roughly a year after the events of the third game and is accessible to new player. The story is good and bittersweet, although somewhat predictable. It also has nothing to do with the island of Syberia anymore, so perhaps changing the name should be considered in future games. Afterall, Amerzone: The Explorer's Legacy takes place in the same universe, so it wouldn't be the first time.On PC, Kate Walker can only be controlled with the mouse. Manual movement via WASD, introduced in Syberia 3, is gone, but thankfully pathfinding and camera work is much better this time. Having said that, there have still been a handful of locations where it was hard to make Kate go into a particular hallway, due to an awkward camera placement, so I still would have preferred to have WASD movement as an option.The game has 3 profile slots, without manual saving or chapter select. I personally will always prefer having the ability to save manually, especially since the first two games had that, but it’s not a very big deal.TWB is a worthy addition to the Syberia series and I recommend it to all fans of the franchise, as well as any newcomers looking for a story-rich game with a fantastic art style.It’s really sad that Benoît Sokal did not get to see this game finished, but it will forever live on as his swan song. RIP and thank you for this wonderful journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: What I loved the most about this game is that it's simply beautiful to look at. The landscapes, art nouveau architecture and objects combine so nicely with the lighting. The characters are well defined and I enjoyed the fact that you can switch between them at times. The story is captivating, playable at your own pace with no rush at all - it's a game to admire and relax into, hence it might feel a bit dull if one is used to a different rhythm.I wish the game were longer, but given that it has an open ending, I'm waiting for it to continue in the next one.A few points of consideration: 1. the movement is somewhat obstructive on the camera angles, making area access difficult. 2. The puzzles were good, I was expecting maybe a bit more of them along the way. 3. story-wise, character going against common sense and weather conditions to perform an action.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 84 years to finally write a review of this game. Don't ask me why...I'm just lazy. Plus, I have a game downloading at the moment and need to pass time.I had originally played the prologue and was hooked from the get-go. So naturally when the full game came out, I powered through it - but in a good way! The story was incredibly immersive, the graphics were fantastic, there were a lot of areas to explore, and I overall extremely enjoyed every part of this game. So much so that when I was at work, all I could think about was coming home to play it again.I didn't want the game to end. Truly. I begged and pleaded with my computer screen to take me on the journey after the ending, but instead all I got was desperation for another game.I highly recommend this game if you are looking to fall deep into a story and enjoy exploration-type games. 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Have played the other Syberia series games so had high hopes for this one....   although I completed this game, I didn't enjoy it because it was so depressing,  Not a spark of joy in it. It was very light on puzzles but long on dialogue and cut scenes that lasted much too long.A somewhat interesting story that clearly parallels WWII - the "Brown Shadow", the persecution of the Vagens, the train with the looted art works...A love story of sorts but rather predictable... a pregnancy, a lost child, a lost love, a jealous woman.... _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly beautiful. It somewhat made me hate the real world for not being so beautiful, since the game shows how entirely possible it would be for all the world to be beautiful. But it would be churlish to mark it down for that.I've played all the Syberias, and remember loving the first two, though that was a very very long time ago; and of course the last one was appallingly bad. (I wish there'd been a better catch-up reminder video.)But this really shines. Voice acting ranged from decent to great, dialog pretty good (though clearly a translation, and rather flattened out from it).  No intensely annoying semi-humans.The plot is fabulous, with a proper epic quality. Characterisation is profoundly good. And those visuals just make one yearn for a world with an elevated aesthetic....I could sit on that tram all day....(Still waiting for a mammoth return though, or some equivalent... Their appearance through the mist remains the single greatest moment in my whole long gaming history.)
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game left me speechless...The World Before rivals Syberia 1 and 2 without question and I've been playing the franchise since the beginning. It's the return of the series we all waited after Syberia 3.The story is intriguing, emotional. It moves you. The transition between present and past is so cool. Benoit Sokal and Lucas Lagravette did a great job.The characters are very charming. Kate is charming as always, we all love her. Dana is very cute, I like her a lot. Also the other characters make you be fond of them. Characters are well written.The music is... just wow.The atmosphere of the game is FANTASTIC. It makes you feel you are right there in the game.The visuals are stunning. One of the most beautiful games I've ever seen. Makes me wonder how Syberia 1 and 2 would look like with this updated engine. Hmm xDThe gameplay is good. One thing that annoyed me here and there is the camera. There were parts where I would have wanted to change the angle. Maybe in a future update. Apart from that, everything cool.Conclusion : One of thebest games I've ever played. I can't decide if The World Before is my number one Syberia game or not. It's a masterpiece like the first two.Benoit Sokal, you will be missed !
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous game with delightful, if somewhat easy puzzles and an enchanting, if at times tragic story about finding your own footing in tumultuous times. I was reluctant to return to Syberia after 20 years, especially after Syberia 3. This game is the continuation I wanted back in 2004. Kate helped fulfil Hans' lifelong dream, but what about her own? What is hers, to begin with? The game works as a standalone story well enough, with the new playable character serving as a sort of self-insert for newcomers to the franchise. There's tons of references and wonderful callbacks to older games, though, and I can't recommend this franchise enough to anybody who can appreciate a calmer, quieter game about how important it is to never lose the spark that makes you, you.In 2002, Syberia made me fall in love with story-driven games. In 2022, this game reminded me why.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It is a gorgeous game, really , which makes it a perfect game to play when you just want to chill out. The story itself - interesting enough to keep on playing, not mind-blowing though. The game-play rather slow for my taste and I would have liked more puzzles.I haven't played any of the previous Syberia games, so can't comment on continuity, however I didn't feel like I  to know what happened in the previous parts, which I see as a plus.Generally I enjoyed it and I would recommend it to those who like slower paced games. It's just really so pretty. So so pretty!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't miss out on this. The game is also really pretty and has the series' typical whimsical style of fantastic realism and art nouveau to offer. Overall a wonderful time and a must-play for fans of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but I had to with this one. I've played all the Syberia games as they've been released and I've loved them all. They all have a great, rich story line. However, this particular one has been the best of them all!It's not just the graphics  that are beautifully done...but, the story line itself. This story could be a movie. It's very real, gives the characters a background, makes them seem more "3D". I actually got emotional in this one, and I never do with computer games!I love classic adventure games. The point and click, talk to people to figure out the next move, etc. They seem harder and harder to come by. This is it! They really did an amazing job, and the details (in every sense) is outstanding!Get this game! You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the game has been an absolute disappointment for me, for there is not a single redeeming quality to it. It's a story driven game, yet the dialogues are so bad, they could come straight out of Star Wars prequels. Dear writers - this is not how people speak. The plot is unexplainable, after a short queerbaiting that is laughably and infuriatingly cliche you are sent on a merry chase after a ghost of the past. What is Kate looking to get out of it? Even she doesn't know. But the wheels of the adventures need to keep rolling to show us a presumably tragic story of not-Jews being persecuted by not-nazis in not-Austria or Liechtenstein. It could be great if not the fact that the characters are so bland I could not care less if they would all perish as soon as they take stage. Poor Rosa has an understanding of the world of a 10 years old and I guess it could make a wonderful rendition of Forrest Gump. Alas, it was not the case.Unfortunately, the "puzzles" seem to be geared towards people of her mental facilities. In the nearly 4 hours of walking I encountered but one part that I could honestly call a puzzle, end even then it did not require too much thought from me, a man who is not particularly smart. It seems like it might be geared towards children who enjoy Bop It toys for most of the "puzzles" are about just flailing your mouse, but there seems to be no indication of that intent.The best part seems to be the visuals, but even there it falls short. You can tell that the design was a product of love, but the technological shortcomings are quite obvious - for me it feels dated even compared to the original Life is Strange. And, of course, it wouldn't be an issue if the graphics weren't the strongest part of the game - and if not for the animations.  People don't bend this way. It's creepy. It's very creepy, the uncanny valley of neck stretching. And automata made of brass should not be all flowy like gummy worms, but rather move only using joints. And, last but not least, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ controls. Steering is so frustrating with how unpredictable the camera can be. Please, just walk into that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ store without leaving it if I don't lift my mouse 0.2 seconds after you do so. The environment is fully 3D so why don't you allow me to see it? Why am I stuck in this hell of a fixed camera, unless I go a bit too far after which it rotates with no warning? Also, using items. Considering that there is no classic point-and-click inventory with joining items together, why do we need to scroll through all we have to just pick this one, absolutely obvious item to use on some part of the scenery? What's the point?I'm sad and frustrated by Syberia and it makes me question if the previous parts were really good as I remember them.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! Everything was great in the first two Syberias is available in this one, but they fix the cons: 1. You have not to walk go and back long distance to solve a puzzle. Yeah it was great, but in Syberia II it was a little bit too annoying. Now you can enjoy the game without wandering too much. But this Syberia is full of long (and unskippable) cutscenes to add the gameplay time what we lost with the less walking.2. There is no bugged or too hard puzzle. I was a reviewer back in the release of 1st Syberia and without any available walkthrough, it was very hard. But the Wold before is solvable with common sense. No "colored salmon bait" issues anymore.I was thinking what missing (because something is missing) in the World before. And it was Hans and the mammuths. The World before has a very different story. And this story is good. But we veteran Syberia-fans are really missed the chase for Hans and the mammuths.I told in the beginning this game is beautiful. And I mean not just the textures or the graphic engine. Not even just the Sokal's design. But everything: the music, the details and even the motion capture artists made a beautiful work. Well done!

_childDocuments_.review: Rife with small mistakes and awkward animations at times, but certainly still a great story and fantastic soundtrack to back it up. _childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to be offered a review copy of Syberia 4. I'm a big fan of the series and I miss Benoit Sokal terribly. I knew him decently from our respective time in the industry and he was a very underrated vet very influential person in gaming. Syberia: The World Before (thank you for not writing it as Be4) tells two concurrent tales, one of Kate Walker, the constant heroine of the series, and a new face named Dana Roze. What follows is well over a dozen over of beautifully crafted storytelling and some outside the box point and click puzzles. The entire affair is melancholic enough, even if you ignore this as Sokal's swansong. It also ends on a cliffhanger which is perhaps the most annoying part of the entire game, because I don't think I'd feel comfortable playing a fifth game in the series. This is Benoit's baby and it should rest along with him. The game is stunning to behold and wonderfully voice acted. There are some odd bits, like like analogous Vaghen for the Jewish and Roma people or the "Black Shadow" instead of outright saying Nazis. But this is an alternative steampunk-y world, and so it is a little more acceptable. I'd have preferred to call a spade a spade though, especially for younger gamers. Although newcomers might be lost if they start with this game, I do feel the majority of it stands on its own, thanks to Dana's inclusion. I would strongly suggest starting the series from the beginning. It was a work of art way back when I was playing the version on CD-ROMs from Dreamcatcher/The Adventure Company and the games still hold up today. You can also find them for insanely cheap of most systems (I have them on my Switch of all things!).This is one of my favorite games of 2022. I can't say it is for everyone, but if you care about a well-crafted story or enjoy adventure games, this is a must get for your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia: The World Before is a graphic adventure game that doesn’t innovate the formula, but replicates it almost perfectly and adds an engaging story split between two different timelines. On one side, we have Kate Walker’s story continuation from the previous titles, with her being now prisoner of a nazi group known as the Brown Shadow. After managing to escape, she will reach the beautiful city of Vaghen to follow the traces of a mysterious drawing she found in the salt mine where she was working. On the other side, we have a new protagonist, Dana Roze, a 17 year-old pianist living in Vaghen during 1937 (just before World War II) who is somehow connected to Kate through some unexpected events that will be unveiled throughout the game. The premise sounds a bit flimsy, but the quality of the story is undisputed thanks to a solid narration alternating between two timelines that makes good use of cinematic cutscenes and touching moments. Writing and voice acting are particularly convicing and really define our protagonists, while the soundtrack composed by Inon Zur further enhances the atmosphere.In terms of gameplay, Syberia: The World Before is a classic graphic adventure where we move the protagonist through different locations, talking to secondary characters, investigating objects, reading documents and, most importantly, solving logical puzzles. The game is perfectly playable with a controller like a standard adventure game, or through mouse and keyboard with a more classic point-and-click experience. While the early puzzles are short and very easy, the difficulty increases once we start switching between characters. Kate will often get in trouble and we will have to move back in time playing as Dana to understand how can we gain the necessary knowledge to help our girl in the present. Puzzles are generally very easy and guided but, if for any reason we are unable to solve one, there is an optional “hint” button that is always available and doesn’t penalize us if used. The game also features secondary objectives that are perfectly integrated within the main adventure and can only be completed before progressing further with the story. They don’t offer any extra reward, but they are often used to incentivize exploration and know more about characters and environments. Artistically, the game is rather impressive, with Vaghen being a city full of life that wonderfully mixes art nouveau with the steampunk automatons from the Voralberg industries. Many locations are beautifully detailed and simply a pleasure to explore. Graphically the game sees remarkable improvements on lighting and textures quality, with the environments being greatly detailed, while the character models appear to be more polished, despite still showing rough animations on secondary characters. Performace-wise, there are some moments where the framerate greatly suffers, which is a bit annoying considering we mostly play in closed environments and small sandbox areas with pre-defined interaction points.Syberia: The World Before marks the epic conclusion of Kate Walker’s journey and perhaps the end of the iconic saga as we used to know it for two decades, with its visionary creator, Benoît Sokal, passing away last year. Fans of the series will treasure this sequel, while new players, as well those who skipped Syberia 3, will probably find themselves a bit confused about Kate Walker’s past and should probably start with the previous titles or at least watch a recap.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who were put off by the prologue demo, that particular story is a mere splinter of a much larger picture of Kate Walker and Syberia - TWB.  I am now 6 hours in and the discovery process has been outstanding.  The graphics and VO are very good and the presentation is wonderful.  The nostalgia alone is worth the price of this game.The mechanics are very straight forward and I found that using my 360 controller was far superior to the usual mouse control.If you enjoyed Syberia 1 and 2 (maybe even 3) then I believe you will enjoy this incarnation as much as I have, or still am.  Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It is muck less of a puzzle than previous parts, but it is much more fun to play, so on average we get quite a decent game with good controls, good visuals and almost no crazy solutions.And Kate Walker`s ass in leather leggins is beyond any praise.Upd: They managed to turn a bit stuffy puzzle series into a real game with a rich story, fully developed characters, some mystery, some detective, puzzles became more logical and constrained to a clearly identifiable area.I should say it is a great work, indeed, this is a game you could consider of replaying one day as it is like a good book, you could find something else with another play and just give rest to exhausted mind and soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Glad to see this series end on a high note, as compared to what the previous entry did. The story starts with a similar vibe as the first and second instalment, with the gameplay offering interesting enough exploration in a stereotypically picturesque, old central European city, and puzzles that feel both smarter and more intuitive than they have before. This leading up to the last few hours of the game where the story really excels, and leaves a lasting and emotional impression. Increasingly good writing with human, realistic behavior and interations, leading to a frustrating turn of events and an engaging, bittersweet end to the story of both player charactrers.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The plot is excellent, though the graphics and especially - animation quality often ruin some of the game's more emotional moments, by being inappropriately hilarious and awkward. I mean come on, you can buy mo-capped animation packs on gamedev stores these days for pocket change (on a corporate scale) and those contain most animations that you need. How come they've animated the getting on and off the tram so well, but when the character is divulging yet another heart-rending story, the item they're holding is hovering next to their hand, or their eyes are locked dead-straight like a corpse. Seriously ruins the narrative sometimes.Still. Despite this crappy graphics and animation and yet another clickbait ending, the game is a good one, with an excellent plot, cinematography and environments. Only one issue with the plot is it's linearity, but I suppose if I had to choose between crappy nonlinear plot and a good linear one, I'd also prefer the latter.So do yourself a favor one day and buy this game. It isn't going to change the world, but it will change your weekend for the better, and that's what matters, doesn't it?
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is . It's everything I ever hoped a Syberia game could be. Except that the . I wish we at least had a final say in how the game concludes. But unfortunately we don't get to make that choice.But regardless of what I said about the ending it's still a must play adventure game, and doesn't even require you to play the previous two installments to understand it (there's a handy summary video available from the menu).
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Syberia and Syberia II, but sadly can't recommend this at all.Neither graphics nor gameplay mechanics have improved much since the first games. Getting Kate around is incredibly slow and frustrating. She was constantly spinning in circles or getting stuck running into a wall. Very little actual gameplay, it's mostly just hours of disjointed, unskippable cutscenes. Puzzles are uninspired and unchallenging. The plot was bland, forgettable but also somehow extremely weird. I dont know who decided , but that whole thing was just a big no from me.Most importantly, this game totally lacked the spirit and heart of the original. When I started the game, the nostalgia factor was high enough to enjoy myself. By the end of the game I was totally checked out, just waiting for it to be done. Don't recommend purchasing unless half price or less.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Slowly developping, tragic story with beautiful level design and rather easy to proceed with the exception of a few overly intricate appliances.Visitors to Vaghen should be advised, that the village and public transport in particular are not very accessible. Lots of stairs. And at the train station long queues might form as everyone has to stamp their own tickets and present them to the door automatons individually.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia: The World Before is a huge improvement over Syberia 3. For being a game made by such a small team, it looks beautiful, the music is great and the story is genuinely interesting. I'm so glad the series didn't end with that stinker of a third game. This is definitely worth getting, even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike a bunch of classic adventure game fans I’m not the biggest fan of Syberia 1, it still does stick with me as the writing and atmosphere are quite good, but man the puzzles are just bad, filled with utterly tedious backtracking. It’s the main reason why I skipped 2 as I always heard it’s got even worse backtracking with a less interesting setting and 3 was a genuinely bad game so I skipped that as well. World Before comes as a welcome surprise though as it is by far the best game in the series and a satisfying conclusion.The puzzles this time around are much better as you don’t have to do much backtracking and they are just enough of them to still feel like a classic point and click adventure game like Syberia 1. The atmosphere is just as fantastic as the original game as Vahgen has a lot of wonder and charm to it. The narrative is actually a rather personal story which is cool to see as video games tend to love upping the stakes, even Syberia 1 was more of this epic trans-continental journey. The story ends up being a really emotional one too and surpasses the original game’s by a good deal. It goes into alt-history like the previous games did but this ends up rather awkwardly done this time around by turning the Nazis into the utterly goofy sounding Brown Shadow and Jewish people becoming an entirely fictional ethnicity which while seemingly was a change with the best intentions ends up feeling tone deaf and kind of diminishing of WWII/The Holocaust. Also the game feels a little too sympathetic to the closest the game has to a main antagonist to me, but it’s not a real detriment.Overall World Before is a great conclusion and a beautifully meditative game befitting of the series' tone and themes. Definitely check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first two Syberia games, they literally shaped my childhood. It was nice to get back into the atmosphere and meet familiar faces again. The story felt a bit soapy though, and I have to say there's less magic in the game without mammoths, but I think people who appreciated the first two titles will still love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say that I was positively surprised by this game. I expected the game to be beautiful, which it is, the setting is absolutely gorgeous and stunning. However, I feared the story might be a bit bland which was not the case. The story has some interesting twists that I did not expect and certain characters will surprise you. The game has some emotional moments and some funny and lighthearted ones, thanks to Oscar, our protagonist's companion, who can be quite the fussy drama queen despite being an usually rational automaton (he is absolutely lovely). My only major grievances with this game were the fact that you cannot skip the cut scenes (this was such a major pain in the ass when I replayed the game to get all achievements) and the controls. Steering the camera or the characters can be quite frustrating because they do not always walk or adjust the way you want them to. As for the puzzles, they were not that challenging but still fun to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: What a beatiful game. Story, music, visuals - overall a great package and a worthy successor to the original trilogy.The only two gripes i had with this game were the puzzles - if you can even call them that - and . Puzzles were way too easy. No camparison to the prior entries. Like night and day. I wholeheartedly recommend this game. If you want a laid back adventure and are not put off by point-and-click games (and loads of cinematics): Try it!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I can definitely recommend this part of series.Awesome graphics, music and plot. The puzzles seem to be easier than in previous parts. Dialogs are unskippable, which is especially annoying when you acidently click something again and it triggers some especially long conversation. Character animations are sometimes awkward, especially hand which look like rigid shovels.If you come here for graphics, music and ambience, It is definitely worth bying.When it comes to game stability I have not experienced a single crash.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: So many memories from playing Syberia 1 & 2. I know I have missed a few parts but there were even a story summary of what has happened before available in the menu. The concept, story, music and classic pick and click adventure is great. I think I need to go back and play through the whole series again after I finish this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia-The World Before: Very Good, thoughtful story that draws you in. It's very easy to lose track of time, discovering the MC's overlap of time and history. The detail of the tram/train, music, and wonderful automatons are especially interesting. I wanted to continue travelling with Kate Walker. I'd follow her even on a simple tour or stroll through the city.  I think I'll see her again. Recommended. Nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this game is a romantic poet, a visually pleasing one at that. It’s much more serious and grounded than the original trilogy, and I liked the new direction. It has many quality-of-life improvements along with cleaner UI and movement mechanics that are good. It delves into new territory of racism and prejudice alongside brighter aspects such as love, friendship, and loyalty. The story has its highs and lows—the first couple of chapters and the later chapters are peak storytelling with goosebump-worthy scenes and lore, though some other chapters aren't as intense.Graphically, it is a feast for the eyes; each scene can be a screenshot. This game is the single-player game I have taken the most screenshots of—I had to stop myself from hitting the F12 key. The vibe was immaculate along with the soundtrack, especially if you are into classical music.The main negative points I can think of are the mid-story chapters, which are not as interesting as the first and last chapters. Also, the movement sometimes suffers due to the weird camera angles in some scenes.All in all, it was truly an amazing sequel—a very good game and a fine send-off to the writer of this amazing world, Mr. Sokal.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, poor performance------------------------------------As with Syberia 3 some people report poor performance despite high-end hardware, others don't have that problem at all. Unfortunately I'm in the former group. It seems the engine has problems with certain hardware configurations.   I turned down the resolution and the effects and limited the frame rate in the NVidia system settings for the game so at least the fan wouldn't blow at max speed. But even at very low resolution and settings there was no way of stopping it from being jittery, even during the credit roll.The game is otherwise a feast for the eyes and the ears. Beautiful visuals and great soundtrack. The gameplay is very similar to its predecessor. The focus isn't on challenging the player but on giving them an experience and telling a story.As for the plot, I feel it's a worthy and fitting entry in the series. While I woulnd't have minded more adventures with the Youkols in the Siberian wilderness, the change of setting to a city didn't feel forced, and anyway Syberia has always been - among others - about letting go.   Some aspects of the plot seemed clumsy, though. Vaghen is obviously Vienna and Osterthal is clearly meant to be Austria - in one scene there is even a list with names of Austrian cities that exist in reality (Bregenz, ...) that are in Osterthal in the context of the game, and yet Austria is mentioned to exist as well. I get the impression the original idea was to set it in Austria and Osterthal was an afterthought.  The way Oscar was included was quite interesting (I'm trying to write spoiler-free). However, it could have been explored more.   For me, the main deviation from the previous games is that this time Kate's mission is only her own. The promise to Katyousha is what she tells herself and others, why she's going on, but it really is for her own sake this time, rather than for Hans or the Youkols. It seems a convincing development of her character.In summary, much like when you're having your favourite dish but it contains a few grains of sand, it's beautiful and a great experience that is marred, however, by poor performance, and that makes the prospect of replaying it unattractive for the forseeable future.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: An appropriate conclusion to this series, true to the essence of the originals; nice environments, ♥♥♥♥ all else.I bothered to play 1-3 because this looked good enough to be worth the slog through some poorly-aged predecessors, but this turned out to be the worst of the lot. At least the old ones supply some adventure game design nostalgia.This has nothing but (quite) nice graphics. The story is so thin it's embarrassing, and incredibly tedious and uninteresting. There isn't a single engaging character, and all of the dialogue, frequently poorly read, is cringeworthy. The moment-to-moment pacing is S T I L L  S O  S L O W, like it wants you to pause to consider its majesty.I'd happily overlook all this if there was gameplay worth mentioning, but instead you get a single 'find the buttons in the right order' puzzle per chapter, like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ tribute to a tenth of The Room's first level.This series seems always to have been overrated, and this faithful modernisation of it has really hammered home how I shouldn't have wasted my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia the World Before - like all Microids Syberias before it is, confused but has the spirit.Don't get me wrong, this game is magical. Its beautiful and wonderfully detailed, in the world of Benoit Sokal who created this steampunk-esque alternate universe. TWB is so beautiful and a feast for the eyes and the art and music is so beautiful, it will be stuck in your head for days. However, like all Syberias before its always a 'one step forwards, two steps back'. Every single Syberia has improved on the last whether technologically or creatively - but it has also had drawbacks. Its a double-edged sword. LIke all game companies, have improved on the games each time, it also everytime makes you miss and prefer the old controls or the old movement controls, etc. After the disaster that was Syberia 3 - where they lost their way without Benoit after he passed and tried to take what he had and ran off with it a random and predictable direction that ultimately betrayed his creation - they listened and returned to the original method; beautiful character stories about discovery, adventure and puzzles. But TWB while it had better controls than Syberia 3, still was clunky in the click-and-hold system it had tried to do in 3 and you would often go in a direction you had not intended and takes some getting used to.THE MOST ANNOYING PART is the Overly Efficient auto-save. How can an auto save be OVER efficient, you ask? Well, previously Syberias had a manual and auto save function - which was useful since you had achievements that required you to do puzzles in one go and it was helpful to just 'main menu' and come back and start again. But SOMEHOW, some genius at Microids decided to do away with 'save games' and just have a super efficient auto save that, while it is a very good system, the lack of a manual save feature means that one mistake means you have to REPLAY THE ENTIRE GAME just for one extremely specific achievement.THAT same GENIUS also had the mad idea that you cannot skip or fast forward cutscenes or conversations. Which makes the above point even more annoying if you want to speed run the game. Don't get me wrong, its beautiful game but it gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tedious the third time you're forced to do things and the whole point of an adventure mystery is to discover something NEW not replay the whole thing when you know whats going to happen already. Which makes it difficult for people to make game movies of this game - which is a pity because as mentioned its a very beautiful game. Because, while ultimately the story is set for you and your choices don't really matter, you still want to know how different dialogue choices make different reactions. AND it makes sense now why there's a severe lack of guides and walkthroughs because its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tedious to replay and figure out. Most players find out the HARD WAY, which i did, how to do certain achievements. Therefore: one step forwards, two steps back. Microids is a little confused but got the spirit. While its a better game than all the previous 3, its the most annoying and disgustingly frustrating.Another thing I will note narratively, there are a lot of plot points that are left behind. Like how Kate's ex-best friend (who's being a b word in this game) cheated with Kate's ex-fiance and then married him in Kate's absence. She never admits that it might have been a factor as to why Kate left and somehow likes to poke her nose in Kate's family's affairs by taking care of her mother. Granted, that's nice but its an AITA reddit thread waiting to happen (AITA for cheating with my bestie's fiance and then taking on the daughter role to her mother while she's MIA in Europe and imprisoned in a slave mine?) Then there's the whole Syberia 3 plot which unfortunately is canon. Edit: thankfully, Microids managed to give me a solution that enabled me to get 100% achievements which is more than i can say for MOST game companies who just say 'play the game' even when there's an issue with said game they designed. Arguably, this redeems them and even elevates them as a game company that actually cares about the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Speechless & Spellbound !. words are few to describe the beauty of this masterpiece. Its more than a game only - for syberia fans its a great gift from its creater. Benoit Sokal has put his mind and soul into this game & he left this world - its an art of this game. Highly recommended to play this game. Meticulous touching details are there in the game, the music is marvellous, character emotions are captured with great ease, above all you will live this game.Thanks Microid team  - although the wait was long, yet the wait was worth it. Love it! Wondering also, who will be the next to carry this legacy of Syberia, as we miss Benoit Sokal.The graphics are photo-realistic and great. I have a G3 Laptop, having 16 GB RAM, 8G GPU, i7,.... i am playing it on ULTRA Setting with a little tweaking.... and its wonderful.The awkard mouse movement in the past franchise has been resolved. Now we also control the character by left click of mouse and moving the cursor & viola ! Kate will follow where you move your mouse....Like a good cup of brewed premium coffee, you will enjoy each frame by frame, like a sip as the in between cutscenes are marvellous as well..... we can enjoy the cut scenes (e.g. travelling in a tram - the automaton drives the Tram Kate is sitting, enjoying the ride)

_childDocuments_.review: The game's visuals are truly stunning, presenting detailed scenarios crafted with impeccable taste. While exploring the town of Vaghen, a mysterious and nostalgic atmosphere seemed to envelop the surroundings, adding a captivating layer to the experience. The ambient sounds and music seamlessly contribute to this truly immersive environment. While the game offers a compelling narrative eliciting genuine emotions, its true standout feature lies in the exceptional artistry that breathes life into every facet of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: "Syberia - The World Before" is a masterpiece that enchants with its engaging narrative and impeccable visuals.  The story is rich in emotion and depth, following protagonist Dana Roze on a journey that mixes mystery and personal discoveries with sensitivity.  The visuals are stunning, with detailed settings that transport the player to a nostalgic and magical universe.  The soundtrack, composed with delicacy, perfectly complements the melancholic and reflective atmosphere of the game, providing an immersive and unforgettable experience. _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I was like: Ray tracing in an Adventure? Are you  kidding me? Wow, the best graphical and musical presentation I have seen so far. I could almost feel the smell of snow in the mountains and I spend a long time just sitting in the train listening to the music. For me, the athmosphere and the easy gameplay is very welcome to todays fast pace games. Lovely Story. Since 8 hours I have found no bugs, enoying voices or disorientated running arround like in Syberia 3. Thank you Microids! The waiting was worth every minute. Too sad Benoît Sokal can´t see the greatness of his work. Rest in peace.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved every single minute of every Syberia episode. I never thought there would be another one yet here it is! Best played at a casual pace to absorb everything that is happening.I played and enjoyed the other episodes a while ago, TWB is even better, I didn't want it to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Have been a fan of Syberia since the first game came out. I really love the story, it's quite unique and it always has those unexpected twists. Great job for being able to capture this again in this game! I really wish the graphics (the characters features and movements specifically) are going to start improving with the next game. It felt a bit like a flashback - I was wondering if I am playing Syberia 3 again... I was expecting a bit more. I mean it has been 5 years since the last part, technologies have changed, come on guys..Quite a lot of bugs with moving around - if your mouse is at the edge of the screen - directions cannot be selected; to move around you can select only ground area - otherwise Kate is running in random directions, glitches here and there..Also, just to mention, while it might have worked well for me to pass through the story quickly as I couldn't wait to find out what happens next, this is probably the easiest Syberia I ever played. The puzzles were not much and super simple + unlimited hints (you are definitely trying to make us lazy, bring back the challenge!)Overall, I love the game itself. This is one of the most addictive and impressive stories from all similar games. Hope another part will be in the making soon! Hey, we have to see what else is there to happen with Kate ;) However, to me - it felt a bit rushed. Hope this will be something which will be improved in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the previous Syberia games and really enjoyed them, but this one... oh my it's so unbelievably boring I could not continue playing for longer than I did. I don't know how it's got so many positive reviews. The graphics are good, but the story jumps from one point to another, and then you feel almost forced to listen to or read tonnes of detail about the history of the war / part of a country, with no option to skip dialogue etc. Really disappointed, and wouldn't recommend it to anyone certainly wouldn't pay full price for it (I bought it when it was on sale).
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A story after which you will cry and maybe even beat in hysterics from the received emotions.If you are a connoisseur of deep, dramatic novels with puzzle elements, then you should definitely pass this game. _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote this review during one of the many interminable cut scenes in syberia 4: The World Before.This game, although beautiful to play and experience, is sadly duller than listening to paint dry. As a fan since the first game, a fan of its puzzles, mechanics, terrible graphics and vague story line! This iteration delivers none of these.It's like watching a film, only one with terrible hair textures and an exceedingly unlikely and weak story. Kate Walker was a great problem solving heroine, turned russian-mining prisoner-♥♥♥-lesbian (she wasn't before?). There are very few puzzles to solve. Those that do exist are hard enough to be solved only by anyone over the age of eight and without serious mental disability. The only reason I completed the game is because my partner and I have played them all through since the first Syberia, but her autism means we need to complete a game once started.Because of her neurodivergence, I was forced to 'play' through (endure) almost ten hours of drivel, with such complex actions as 'click the mouse to chop down a tree'.Still the game has not ended. I feel my soul falling into an endless abyss as Kate decides to go home to the US after all (why do we need to play through her journey home?). I feel like scooping my eyes out with a cactus might be more entertaining (and certainly more challenging) at the moment.Do not buy this unless you are the world's most uninspired person, or if you're rarely capable of solving complex tasks such as opening the fridge.-17/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: An AAA-game among poin-and-click adventures and it's an excellent example of what a good point-and-click adventure game should be. A new standard for the genre.One of the things that immediately caught my attention was the game's stunning graphics. The environments were beautifully rendered and full of intricate details that made them feel alive.What caught my attention even more were the dialog scenes. The characters often interact with each other, objects or the environment.   Not like in a genre-typical way, where puppet-like characters stand in front of each other and pretend to have a conversation.The game's story was also a highlight for me. It never felt rushed or slowed down. The scenes where Dana plays the piano are gorgeous and unforgettable.The game's puzzles were also well-designed and reasonable. They were challenging enough to keep me engaged, but not so difficult that I ever felt frustrated or stuck. The puzzles were also logical and fit well within the context of the game's story, which made them feel satisfying to solve.Overall, I would highly recommend the game to anyone who enjoys point-and-click adventure games. It's a beautifully crafted game with an interesting story, stunning graphics, and well-designed puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game was not what I was expecting, in that there were few puzzles and little "gameplay", and it was very slow paced. However once I'd settled into what the game was (perhaps a bit different to the other Syberia games), I really enjoyed it. It was a very relaxing and beautiful game, and the story was quite moving. I could see the end coming from a mile off but there were some unexpected turns nonetheless. It was kind of like an interactive film or piece of art. The music particularly deserves a mention.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: An intriguing story of love and loss during times of war and persecution, well told and presented, - the architectural artstyle is exceptionally beautiful. Character writing is very good (not entirely without some stereotypes though) and voice acting is top notch.There are two problems though:1. (minor annoyance) The camera seems to actively obstuct important objects and paths, and the mouse controls can be suboptimal at times.2. (major annoyance) Sometimes you can't pick up or interact with objects, unless a very specific thing has happened before or you have actively looked at something. An example: to start a generator, there are some gas cans standing nearby, - but you can only "look at" them until you have "interacted" with the generator and then specifically "observed" the fuel gauge (which is clearly visible anyway), - only then are you even given the option to "pick up" the gas can. So even if you as the player have figured out the solution, you can't put it in motion until you have led the in-game-character to it via babysteps.All in all, this game is about the story and not so much about the gameplay, so those two points shouldn't factor in as much, - but you should keep them in mind during your playthrough. If you get stuck, it's probably one of those two.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I shed nearly so many tears during the game and finally gave in by the end when the plot reveals itself in conclusion. The addition of the beautiful Hymn of Vaghen only makes you cry even more. Beautiful game. Syberia holds special place in my heart from childhood when I played it with my dad, and hope to see continuation on what will follow after the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: (No spoilers) Truly a wonderful game full of various emotions. You will experience something exceptional. If you like great stories, colorful characters, unforgetable soundtrack and story driven games that will leave a mark in your soul (e.g. Life is Strange), this game is for you. _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy story rich games with detailed, atmospheric, old world graphics, then you probably don’t want to miss this one. (hence the thumbs up).However, if you are anticipating a Kate Walker adventure with that sense of long distance travel into ever more remote and wonderful locations, then you may be disappointed.This is not really Kate’s story, it is the story largely of others. Kate plays an investigative role and once she is established, she travels no further than the surrounding areas of a fictitious European town.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I was so thrilled to see the new Syberia after having played the previous 3 years ago. It is a visual feast, has a beautiful story line and music, and has some interesting puzzles. It is mostly a story you watch with some interaction, rather than a classic point and click. I would have loved to have more involvement and more puzzles, but it may have detracted from the flow of the story. Highly recommend if you have some time on your hands to fully appreciate the immense work that has gone into creating this visually stunning game.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game.....and here I am sitting with tears in my eyes. What a beautiful story but what else to expect from a game from the Syberia series.This game is made with love, you can see that in every aspect: The beautiful voice acting, the automatons (Oscar!), the great visuals (love how the trams drives on rails AND water!)......it's just a game made with passion and not making profit as first priority. If you never played a game from the Syberia series...just give it a go. It's well worth your money and time!!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I played Syberia many years ago and was captivated by the adventure, so this game holds a special place in me. Grabbed The World Before when it went on sale. Overall a casual and relaxed experience. Great if you're looking for a story, beautifully crafted puzzles and scenery. I love the puzzles and especially the one involving machines & automata.On the downside, the pace is a little slow at times. It could use more intricate puzzles. Player has very limited camera control so you can't look at the scene from any angle you chose, which felt a little outdated in today's world.Despite the cons, I still recommend the game if you're looking for a relaxing game and a story to go along.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't understand why anyone thought that what the Kate Walker character needed was some psychological trauma.  I played 1 & 2, skipped 3 due to everyone relentlessly trashing on the controls, then came back to this one to find what was a charming and largely innocent game series about a woman finding that sometimes protecting a legacy is more important than business is now somehow completely different.  Perhaps the switch actually happened in 3, but obviously I can't speak to that.  The gameplay itself is very nice.  The graphics are great, the controls are only a little clunky, and the idea of switching between 2 characters in 2 time periods is great and well executed.  I could have used a lot more puzzles, but maybe that's me.  My issue really is not even story, but character motivation.  I remember Kate as a relatively neutral entity.  Very feminine and well suited to the largely gentle world and story she was in.  Now she comes across (to me at least) as a borderline sociopath who is desperately trying to avoid reality.  Which in turn makes it seem like that's how the game creators view their audience, given that you are directly controlling her through the story.  It's jarring, disturbing and completely unnecessary to the overarching story.  Dana's story was all the drama they needed.  Kate should have been the stabilizing force for the story, but I feel like she's borderline suicidal and I'm guiding her away from seeking help.  It's not a feeling I enjoy.  At time of posting I haven't finished the storyline yet, but honestly I don't think there's anything that could possibly  happen that would make up for the unavoidable choices that were made in game so far (given that I've earned 1/3 of the achievements and missed a few, I'm guessing I'm about half way though).  Despite all the pros, the cons are disturbing enough that I can't in good conscience recommend it.  This kind of subtle messaging can really damage people.  Especially if you take in to account the extreme mental health crisis that many people (in the US at least) are already trying to navigate their way through after the covid years.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely point and click adventure. Sadly the creator and lead designer Benoît Sokal passed away. Hopefully the series get another title. I like the series.It has a beautiful story meet up and downs, even unexpected twists. The steampunk Vaghen is well done and offers gorgeous views. The graphics are nice, but I had some hair lighting bugs (glimmering hair lines). There is no skip option if you click on something several time you have to listen, or watch it again. Lucky the scenes aren't that long. The puzzles aren't that hard eather. If you love the previous games  you'll love this, too. You can still play and understand it even if you didn't played the previous ones, but expect a few weird things.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: To this day I still think that few series have done such a good job with their world-building as the Syberia series, which is why I still have very fond memories especially of the first Syberia. This led to Syberia 3 being a massive letdown. In retrospect, maybe I'll give it another chance someday, but I didn't enjoy playing it at the time. Some nice nods to the legacy of the series were included, but it failed to leave its mark.The same can definitely not be said for "Syberia - The World Before". It's one of the best adventure games in recent years, its story (although the premise is pretty far-fetched, to be honest) manages to be consistently interesting and I enjoyed its message as well as the ending, which it manages to mostly stick. Yes, one could consider the finale a "sequel bait", but I've seen much worse. It's satisfactory enough and should this be the end of the series, I would be fine with it. That the story manages to be entertaining is very important, because the game definitely follows the formula "story first, puzzles second". Which isn't to say that the puzzles are not enjoyable. They're just not what you really play this game for.Three further big strengths of the game need to be mentioned. First of all the game just looks gorgeous. It presents vistas that had me spamming the screenshot key and I can't commend it enough for its fantastic camera work. You'll hopefully see what I mean when you experience it for yourself. Secondly, I really liked that this game takes its time. That way, it fleshes out its characters and its world and hits a tone that is very fitting to the story that it wants to tell. Third: The soundtrack is great. You'll hear the hymn of Vaghen very often, which would be a problem if it wasn't such a nice musical piece. Inon Zur really hit it out of the park with this one and I'm going to have some melodies stuck in my head for quite some time now.You likely guessed already: I recommend this game whole-heartedly. It's a shame that Benoît Sokal didn't live to see it being released. It's a great ending for a series that definitely had its ups and downs, but that also always had  its heart in the right place. And that's worth a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Review after 100% of achievements earned.The game's biggest strengths are the visuals and the story.  The game is absolutely gorgeous.  I was frequently struck with how great everything looked.  It was funny when the characters commented on the beauty, even though it was true.  The story is wonderful.  As someone who played the previous three games in the Syberia series when they were released, I felt that this one lives up to those while doing some great new things as well.  There was a lot of depth created for this world and this game shows more of that than the previous games.  There are lots of new characters that weren't in the previous games.  I was interested to see how every character's storyline progressed.  I loved how Kate Walker got an entire backstory and it felt true to the character.  There are plot twists that players are given enough clues to figure out long before the characters do.  And there are plot twists that come as major shocks, too.  It is a great balance in the storytelling with lots to offer everyone.With all that said, it should be one of the greatest adventure games ever, right?  Unfortunately the technical parts of the game really let it down.  I didn't so much play the game as beat it into submission.  It was just an exercise in frustration to actually make progress.  I would regularly have to click dozens of times just to get the game to respond to a click.  Then sometimes that would be made worse because the characters would start to take that action but then just abruptly stop before finishing.  The characters got stuck on the scenery all the time and I had to have them "run" many times in many directions before they could free themselves and I could progress.  Sometimes the game's process would just have an absurdly high amount of disk access for several minutes which prevented me from doing anything at all in the game until it was finished.  I have a modern computer, the game maintained good FPS numbers the whole way, the CPU hardly had to do anything, the GPU did not seem taxed, and I had plenty of memory available.  So it didn't seem like the issues were directly related to typical system causes.  I was just screaming at the game to be allowed to play.  Related to this, all of the puzzles would be trivially easy in real life - with the most difficult ones being about on the same level as tying a necktie.  But having to fight the interface to accomplish them made them way more difficult than they should have been.  I had two where the character got stuck on the scenery at the same time as getting the issue where the game wouldn't respond to clicks so I had to end the task and go back into the game to progress.I still recommend it, but it wastes fantastic visual and story highs with the technical lows.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished Syberia: The World Before and the only thing I can tell is WOW.What a journey guys...This game is a masterpiece and surely the best action adventure I ever played.I play games since I was a child (I started with Commodore 64) and there was very few games that made me so enthusiast.I play all genres, from action adventure games, to RPG and FPS, I play high budget games mostly because I don't have that much time to play all the games I would like but this game worths all the time.Amazing graphics (technically not the best probably) but the sum of the parts are simply amazing. Incredible relaxing music, I loved it and it relaxed me so much.Wonderful story, I never felt bored by it and I never wanted to close the game xDKate is such a profound character, automatons are so magic, I loved it.The only thing that made me a bit "meh" is the fact that the first two chapters was dubbed in Italian and the 3rd and the 4th not.All in all, damn this is a masterpiece, I hope that you'll have all the best luck with future chapters if any.Congrats all guys and RIP Benoit.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what the Syberia story needed to continue!Microids, the newest installment of Syberia has uniquely poised the franchise to soar to new heights, thanks to a brilliant marriage of new ideas and references to the beloved first two games.The World before gives fans of Syberia 1 & 2 plenty of reverence to Kate's original adventures, without feeling stale, haphazard, or gratuitous, and without changing her original adventure. Equally impressive is its introductions to new characters, arcs, and aspects of gameplay which I hope to see more of in the next installment.With the passing of Benoit Sokal, I encourage anyone who liked the game to give it a great review, and write Microids so that his son can continue this beautiful story.Here's some topics I and I think many others would love to see visited/revisited in the hopeful 5th installment (Spoiler warning). Difficulty of Puzzles/length of gameplay:While I was quite happy with The World Before's length, I think Syberia 3 was a bit short. It may be that I played the first 2 games while quite young, and had to take longer for the puzzles, but this installment seemed a bit shorter than the originals. I'd love to see a more expanded story, with more locations, and more complex puzzles!Exotic Locations/edge of the world/darker universe:The setting of the World Before worked great for its duplicate stories set decades apart, and made absolute sense for the setting of a WWII tale and Kate's possible return to the normal world. HOWEVER I do miss some of the exotic locations offered in the first 3 games (A tiny town in the French Alps which is half populated by automatons, a forgotten University, an abandoned manufactoring complex in Cold-war era Russia, a past-its-heyday resort which has been claimed by the sea and salt winds, a town on the edge of the Russian Tundra, a Youkal village past the edge of the world and of course the titular island of Syberia. The 3rd game, while having its faults, even had some exotic locations in a sea-side village plagued by a sea-monster, and an irradiated abandoned theme-park. As this next adventure should travel back East, I even see potential for reference/crossover/borrowing aspects from the first two games- I imagine Baltayar to be in or near present day Mongolia or China, which leads Kate back towards much of the events set in the USSR.Riding the Train/varied locations:Yet again,while the setting for the World Before was perfect for its intended story, I did like the cyclical journey aspect that the transport by train, and even the Youkal caravan in Syberia 3, added to the story. You solved whatever was wrong in each town/train station, long enough to explore its locations/people, set things right and move on. I think Kate catching the train at the end kind of lends itself to this.Darker Universe:Something about these desolate, mostly forgotten locations on the edge of the world (Nic Canton Literally says "its like she's stepped into another world" in Syberia 2) lends itself to slightly darker story lines, which I quite enjoyed and seemed a little missing from 3 &4. Some examples are the Rectors covering up the berries' existence for money, a factory manager willing to kidnap/steal oscar's hands to satiate his obsession with a Soprano, an old man trying to fulfill an impossible childhood dream of seeing live mammoths, two brothers getting eaten by penguins, a cabaret owner who isn't accepted by monks but cares for a local orphan, oscar giving his body for Hans, Helena Romanski dying after her trip to Komkalzgrad, an alcoholic pilot wanting to go to space, an alcoholic sea captain who gives his life to fight the sea monster, etc. While the World Before had elements of darkness in its story, I would love to see more of these open-ended dark parts of the world the Sokals have created.Magic/Otherworldly-qualities:I once heard a great quote about the production of Game of Thrones that "magic is at the fringes of the Universe, but the plot is focused around human nature." I think this perfectly embodies the story the Sokals have created. While so much of the plot is based on human/relatable themes, the characters seem to navigate a thin line between a mystical world and our own. Some exampled include the Youkal Shaman/mystic healing powers, the Harfang following Kate, a world where Mammoths exist on a island somehow out of reach from modern man, a giant sea-monster in a Russian lake, strange impossible birds in Barrackstad, strange impossible automatons littered throughout the universe (but in Particular Oscar, Helena's servant, and the ones in Komkalsgrad), a Russian Cosmonaut, the Youkis, a train that runs from a winding mechanism, etc.While the World Before's setting in modern day life was perfect for its WWII story, some aspects of this made it in (the part in the Russian mines, the Yetis) I would love to see this mysticism return-which perfectly matches her trip to the mythical Baltayar.Rich/complex characters with arcs.Yet again, no complaints here about the World Before, however I feel like the 3rd installment lacked in these areas. Particularly, the Youkals in Syberia 3 were dramatically simplified from the first 2 games to "Kate walker help us took took". Also, the villains did not really get much explanation and are kind of drab cliches. Compare this to the first two games, where you have a madman still presiding over an abandoned factory in Komkalzgrad who dreams of one day seeing Helena Romanksi perform, a drunk pilot who was meant to be sent into space but has spent years drinking in the ruins, a Cabaret owner who takes care of an orphaned girl, a guard on a wall who thinks a soldier's been spying on him for years, two brothers attempting to get rich on ivory, a monk who lived amoung the Youkals for decades, etc. I loved that the fourth installment brought back some arcs that were missing in Syberia 3-particularly Kate's abandonment of her mother, her losing Dan to Olivia, etc.Extra content reading/loreI'd love to see some more extended reading/extra content in the documents, as was the case in 1, 2 & 4. Some memorable examples include the textbooks from Barrackstad University, Hans/Anna's diaries, Brother Alexei's notes from the Monastary, the newspaper clipping in Syberia 2 which details Helena Romanski's death and the article about the spaceship, etc. Some of these documents shaped the universe almost as much as the actual gameplay. Another notable example is that the Harfang follows Kate in Syberia 2 for long time before it appears in the Youkal village-at first from quite a distance, but getting closer as it becomes relevant to the story. This is also documented in Aleksei's journal.Overall I couldn't recommend the World Before more, and would love to see this universe explored more in a 5th entry. I think the engine is still hot, and would love to see some motion behind it while we still original voice actors, and while the last two entries are quite recent. I'm excited to see the Syberia series go even further!
