_childDocuments_.review: Very, very beautiful game with a nice story, likeable characters, cool puzzles, and an awesome soundtrack! ^^b This installment of Syberia brings the series back to its strong roots and can probably be considered one of the best games in the series.The city of Vaghen is such a lovely place with all its cool automation all over the place!! Thanks a lot, Microids, for making this game -- it really let's me forget the downsides of the direct predecessor! Good job!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic way to return to the world of Syberia and Benoit Sokal. I played the first 2 games, and I loved them. The story, the characters, the world and the automatons, ... they were delightfully crafted and made a great impression on me. This new game is a return to all of that plus some enhancements: beautiful hiqh quality graphics and textures (some of the backgrounds are truly mesmerizing), gameplay based on a mixture of nicely integrated minigames/puzzles, the possibility of looking for extra objectives apart from the main ones to complete each chapter, adult story with time jumps and plot twists that will keep you hooked up, etc. Overall, all these details make this new game a great addition to the saga. "Syberia: The World Before" is not only a great "Syberia" game but also a great adventure game on itself. Yes, difficulty wise, it's not as hard as old-school adventure games, and the puzzle solving mechanics have been certainly simplified to make it more accessible. So, someone looking for a "classic adventure game" experience may be slightly disappointed. Not me, I really love what they have done with the updated game mechanics in general. This game is certainly a nice goodbye tribute to Benoit Sokal and his fantastic world, and I cannot but recommend it to anyone interested in playing a beautifully crafted adventure game with complex characters and a gripping adult plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia: The World Before is a positively stunning sequel to Syberia 1 & 2. The game is so well developed you can run it stand alone or experience the deep roots of the Kate Walker story.The introduction is well delivered to launch this ongoing story line. Some puzzles may seem difficult but there's hint help if you need it.  The sound track also compliments the game well.The game runs flawless with superb graphics... the story line always held my attention & curiosity... reference to the previous titles blended well into this story. This family affair is great to replay in case you missed something and is suitable for all ages. Enjoy...Microid Studio has class and Kate Walker proves it again!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of the Syberia Series since the first game and while Syberia 3 did tumble, this game did the opposite! This game is pure magic. Everything comes together here the setting, characters, story, puzzles, and what I thought lacked in the previous games is emotion. The developers here created a masterpiece here. This is the best Syberia has ever been. I'm sad to hear that Benoît Sokal passed away. I hope we get a final game in the series to finish Kate Walker's story! This is truly a beautiful game and I loved every minute of playing it! Congrats to Microids and Benoit Sokal on a fabulous game. Lets see Kate Walker to the finish line!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with a wonderful story a great sequel to the first two episodes.The set design is stunning and very immersive, the characters are interesting and varied. They could have polished the animations a bit more and the puzzles were sometimes a bit too simple, but that's basically the only critiques I have.Definitely recommended if you're into narrative games with some easy puzzles to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This was a wonderful game that fit right in with the others. I loved the story, and how the past and the present were so deeply connected to each other. Visually, this game is stunning, and the music is amazing. The puzzles were much more intuitive than the first two games, and the interaction with the objects is really cool. This was definitely worth playing! The cons were probably the controls and the length of the game. This is not a short game like the first two, and if you had problems with the controls of the third game, you might not like how this one is. Directing Kate can be frustrating at times, but nothing as difficult as Syberia 3. But while the length of the game is greater, I think it is worth it anyways, because you really feel immersed in the game. Without adding any spoilers, I was also very impressed with the ending. Everything considered, I think it was very well done, leaving it open for another game, but also giving enough closure to accept the end if they never do make a fifth one. You can play this without fears of cliffhangers!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing these games. I played the very first game on the old first XBOX. It was an incredible game. Then I played the second game the moment I could. Amazing again! When the third game was announced I was so excited that one of my favourite stories was coming back and yet that third game was terrible. I was so disappointed. This game has taken on board all of the feedback from the third game and made something wonderful. Beautiful music, lovely story, brilliant voice acting and satisfying game play! If you love the series, you will be happy to play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting much after Syberia 3, but after playing the prologue... This should have been Syberia 3 and the original should never have existed!The story is beautiful, very sweet and heartbreaking, it was like a novel you couldn't put down... A bit of hard puzzles here and there but not that hard to push you away... If this is the last game (which I believe is not) it is a beautiful farewell to Benoit from Benoit to the fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to leave a negative review, but I'm sure I should do it.Pros: good graphics; decent plot; great music; Kate Walker; Oscar.Cons: boring; literally no puzzles; painfully slow; bad camera/movement controls; some questionable plot arcs.I'd cautiously recommend it for some fans of the series, like myself, because it still has a vibe. _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the previous games I was so excited to enter this world again. I was not disappointed. The story-line was so intriguing I couldn't stop playing. Still had the same atmosphere, beautiful artwork, and fun puzzles as the previous games. The story was quite different from the other games, but it was so beautiful and heart-felt. I was on an adventure with Kate Walker and I didn't want to get off the train!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Prologue is weird and the leftovers from third game are ridiculous and just bad. Thankfully this story thread is resolved within 30 minutes and you never go back to ugliness of the Syberia 3.I don't think that The World Before is a fantastic Syberia game, if anything, it feels way more like spin-off set in a world of Syberia (even though you kinda get closure for Kate's story). There's way too much emphasis on world war 2, and the story of Dana Roze, who may or may not be related to Kate. I'm not sure if everyone would love this game (I'm still not sure how much I like it, to be honest), but I definitely feel like the soul of Syberia is here.The series is back to what it was known for - marvelous vistas and locations, magical european towns of olden days, and, weirdly, a search for someone special.It's marginally better than the third game, and I'm glad that this is how Syberia, hopefully, ends
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the first Syberia for a few hours.Then I decided to meet with Syberia series from this game due to better graphics.After seeing cringe dialogue with russian punk Katusha in GULAG, decided to check forums, what's wrong with this game.Syberia 1: Game introduces you world's lore, shows fantastic mechanic toys which seems alive. And you have that feeling like you in some taleSyberia: The World Before: Game introduces you how bad that nazis, how bad is that GULAG, and orientation of main hero.And yeah, it's... khm... not Syberia any more. So I decided not to waste my time.Also there is terrible optimization. I don't see such a great picture to waste so much PC resources.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game if you have a few hours (15 hours in my case) to spare. It's not too hard and all puzzles are solveble for most people I do think. It's clear to see the developers took great care in puting this story together. The visuals are very well done. One think I noticed for instance is that buildings, even if they do not play a part in the story have true depth. So it's not like a the stuck a piccture on a plane and call it a window. I don't think I ever seen that before in a game.Anyway, fun story, not too hard and great visuals!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. Enough said. Do yourself a favour and play all the previous Syberia games (including Amerzone) to truly appreciate the journey of one of the best developed video game character, Kate Walker. I could have written pages of explanation and information about the story but the lesser you know is better. Play all the games and you won't be disappointed.I think this game definitely needs to get a reward!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all the other Syberia games which I liked except for the one before this game, which was one of the most jankiest games i've played (and I own Cyberpunk 2077). Storytelling in this one is superb as well as the visuals. Every environment looks like art and I loved the mechanic which allows you to switch between Dana and Kate to solve puzzles. I look forward to hopefully more Syberia games in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I played the previous games and I have to say that the only aspect they actually improved are the graphics. I am rather surprised that so many people seem to like the game. Sure, it has some moments but overall there are way too many things that got worse from previous games:- The puzzles were super easy and bare boned compared to the previous games. - The story had interesting concepts, but it was pretty predictable and not as interesting or good as the story of the previous games. Especially bad is the beginning and the plot hook that gets Kate Walker on this quest. - The controls were horrible. Often it felt like the game was not recognizing inputs and especially when clicking on interactable things (doors were the worst!) it often made the character walk in a circle or to a completely different position. Also it often seemed like they added certain things only to prolong the game. I played it veeery slowly (reading almost everything and leaving the game open while being afk) and I still had it finished quickly. It has many simple fetch quests in the same area that only seem to function as a way to waste time (and the character often walks veeery slowly). If you would drop those from the game and play it normally (without reading literally everything there is), it would probably be shorter than 6 hours, which is absolutely nuts for the price of this game (and considering the overall weak story). Most ridiculous of all were the camera angles in cutscenes though. These were often simply creep shots of the main character's ass from multiple angles. Seriously, some of them were even from bushes or from behind furniture, which added to the whole creep flair. The ass was in the center of like 70 % of the camera shots during cutscenes, even when it would have made WAY more sense to show the face of Kate Walker or the face of the person she was speaking to. I usually do not care about such things, but this was so extreme and obvious that it just made me laugh and question if even the developers themselves were bored by their dialogues and decided that the players needed Kate Walker's booty in their face 24/7 to keep them playing and not lose interest.I truly hope that they will add some more interesting puzzles again in the next part but I will not hold my breath.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The story in Syberia 3 felt lost without Hans there - there was no longer urgency and focus. Thisss, this finally recentered the story back to Kate. The !!spoiler!! return of Oscar is amazing. Dana's story is amazing. This feels like the start of an amazing new story. So personal, so well crafted. This game, unlike Syberia 3, feels like Syberia. Really gives you the gut punch feelings. It is the game we waited for 10 years after Syberia 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: So much better than Syberia 3. Absolutely gorgeous, and captures the spirit of the original two games quite well. Story feels very engaging, and much darker overall.I still dislike the controls a bit, but that's just me being an old school point n click fanatic.RIP Benoit Sokal, thank you for all your work
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Payed full price, the game looks good i have to be honest, but the unnecessary difficult puzzels make this game a drag and certainly nota jump-in and have fun game, IF you are in for the story, which if i believeis the main selling angle of the game, it seems to me that they ''tried'' to make this a 3d point & click adventure game again, I thought they weredone with those......... :( The tedious interface AND not to forget everytime you alt+tab out of the gamefor a hint on the internet, you are greeted with the pauze menu. really???For such clever people this was not too obvious, anyway...I now understand why this series has not yet lifed off, it is bad dicision making and puzzles nobody wants, we want to explore!!!!!:) see ya
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a puzzle game, it's a movie that you click to advance.To be fair, I didn't realize this was part of a series when I bought it. Perhaps it would have been better received by me if I had gone into this with the other games for reference, but this still can only be considered a puzzle game by a loose definition of the term. In four and a half hours of game play, there have been 3 actual puzzles to solve and they were barely more than moving a few sliders around. I bought this on a 60% sale and I still feel like I paid way too much, as I honestly can't get past the frustratingly pointless gameplay aspect of it to experience it's strongest feature which is the setting and story.To throw in a few pros here, the setting is beautiful and interesting. The music is lovely. The story is intriguing. I just can't recommend this game for the actual gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game. Seems so much shorter, and perhaps unfortunately much more down to earth compared to its earlier parts. Amazing scenery paired with mind soothing music. Gameplay is interesting, and ending was once again fitting. Now on to some negativities. Puzzles have been made far too easy to solve, and there is honestly not too many. Character developments seem ill fitting, I was especially hugely disappointed of the lack of melancholic humor Oscar used to brighten my life with.If you love the series, you will at least enjoy The World Before.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. You don't have to play the other Syberia games to follow the story but it does help you connect with Kate better if you do. The graphics are amazing. The puzzles are difficult but not to the point where it's not un-enjoyable. The story is...it's beyond words. It was sad and very heart touching. Best story out of the series by far. Such a over all beautiful game, if you enjoy this type of genre of game then this is a must have to your collection. Just buy it already! ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely game but also quite sad.It's so beautiful, even magical in so many places. But there's also a lot of pain and drama as the story progresses.It's so very obvious that so much effort and love went into making it, it's really impressive.I played Syberia 1 and 2 some 20+ years ago and now this one feels like coming back to the roots. I wish Syberia 1 looked like this those many years ago when I was exploring Valadilene, Barrockstadt etc. :)The game takes its time, you can't skip cutscenes, you can't skip dialogs. I think this was a design choice rather than an omission. I've felt the game encourages you at every point to slow down and experience the moment.The story in the game is very powerful, it deals with themes such as the passage of time, the impermanence of things and of human life, one's aspirations in life and the prospect of failing to meet them.On a technical level, the game cleverly combines multiple timelines, it's really well done.The game feels very nostalgic in a good way, this is certainly magnified by the fact that Benoit Sokal himself didn't live to see the release of this game and that this is quite likely the last entry in the entire series.After I finished the game one night (after roughly 17 hours of gameplay in total), I couldn't fall sleep almost the entire night, I was so overwhelmed by the story and the implications of everything.I have to say I wasn't a huge fan of Inon Zur's music in Syberia 2 because to me the arrival of a new composer shifted the atmosphere established in Syberia 1. But in this game, I have been extremely impressed with Inon Zur's soundtrack and the musical choices in general.Several of the music tracks are just brilliant and I keep listening to them over and over. And it was recorded with a live orchestra and a virtuoso pianist, wow!The voice acting is great, as well as the motion capture and animations, I enjoyed it all very much. Several of the original voice actors are back once again, which is sweet. The young lady doing the voice acting for Dana Roze apparently did both the English and the French language versions, plus also the motion capture for both Dana and Kate. Very impressive!As a side note, I noticed multiple times that different characters pronounce the same words or names differently. Typically the word Fräulein (which you'll hear VERY often) and also the name Dana. Oh and the rector of the music school apparently doesn't know how to pronounce the word "automaton". I don't quite understand how such things can go unnoticed during the recording sessions.But these are just very small details. I didn't experience any significant technical issues, no crashes either, only two very minor visual glitches with NPCs throughout the entire game. I was able to play the game on my Acer Nitro laptop on the highest settings. Very nice.Overall, this is a great game, particularly if you are a fan of the series, then it's a no brainer.I originally bought the game in a sale but then a few days ago I bought the entire Collector's Edition also, because I just wanted the artbook so much! And yes, there's obviously MUCH more than just the artbook...I really miss Benoit Sokal but it's good to know that his last game turned out so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! A hymne to all Syberia games fans! A hymne to adventure gaming! Thanks to all the people that worked on this title and to the late brilliant artist and creator Benoit Sokal.The game offers a very heart-warming, emotional, touching story. The graphics are beautiful and the game definitely resembles the originals 1 & 2. The music and voice acting are beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I have played all of the Syberia games, but this is the best one so far. I love the character switching through out the game, with an enriched story, that has many twists and turns. Beautiful cut scenes/video's.Through out the series all the story's have been fascinating and I have been left wanting more and this game is the same, it's sad that the designer Benoit Sokal has passed away, I hope this doesn't mean it's the end of Kate Walker's adventures!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The most beautiful game I played in my life. I got in touch with this masterpiece by playing Siberia 1 and I had loved the character Oscar and his way of speaking in character. The ending was absolute amazing. _childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not what it used to (Syberia 1 & 2). The puzzling aspect has been replaced with just an interactive story.I mean - it is now what I hoped for, but it is still a great experience (but if you come for the puzzles and typical point'n'click riddles, you're going to be disappointed). The locations are beautiful, music is atmospheric, the story is unfolding in an interesting way (makes me think of "The Manuscript found in Zaragozza").Controls are good (and mind I played with a touchpad) - my only complain would be that mouse sensitivity does not work for all interactions the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Syberia the world before is a adventure/puzzle game where you play as 2 characters, Kate Walker (present) and Dana Rose (the past). As you play both characters you piece together how they are linked together.The story is set in the present and the past.  As Kate Walker, you seek to find information how Dana is linked to you and as you find new clues you will play as Dana that shows you the story of the past. The story is very depressing and takes place during the 2nd world war (dana) and follows through the years until the present (Kate).Graphically this game looks great. Everything from the characters to the environments have lots of detail.  I always found something interesting to look at while playing and felt very immersed. The voice acting was also great and interacting with other npc’s felt natural. The puzzles ranged from very easy to a bit frustrating or more so time consuming than the others. While the harder puzzles weren’t  overly difficult, there were just a lot of steps involved to solving them. There wasn’t too many like this however.I thought this game was great and enjoyed playing it. I really have no gripes with it other than some annoying puzzles.8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: After a not so great 3rd part is Syberia The world before great comeback to its origin. Music : 10/10Story: 10/10Minigames are not so difficult but nicely challenging. Great new ideas like switching characters etc made this game one of my favorite after a long time! Hopefully there will be more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely flawless return to form after Syberia 3's poor showing. If we're to split hairs, no-skipping of dialogue and no manual saves can be a bit punishing (especially the latter can lock you out of achievements) but they're totally minuscule in the grand scheme of things.

_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: A French game set in a fictionalized version of Austria that combines Art Deco with Steampunk so effortlessly one  kind of wonders if this might be an existing alternate reality ^^Evokes pleasant feelings of adventure games of yore (such as The Longest Journey and its sequels) where you are put in a mysterious, different world that you explore and get to know as time goes on with rather complex characters, a very detailed world, lots of machinery and lighting and sense of style that makes it look much better than it technically has any right to be (Pretty much any shot could be a postcard).The controls are partially somewhat ennerving due to fixed camera angles, the focus is more on the story than the puzzle part of adventure games, but what a bittersweet tale it is! You just can't help to continue playing to uncover more of the world, past and present (Because you switch between two characters and periods).And if that would not be enough praise, it centers around a particular topic that sadly is relevant yet again (Right-wing nationalism with all the ills it brings), the soundtrack is rather magical and you get to punch and validate a ticket (People who love public transport like me will surely appreciate this title ^^)So in closing, if you like mystery games, moody worlds and touching tales, you should give this a try (There is even a demo after all)8/10 mechanical animals
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: 20 years have passed... I recall very fondly playing Syberia 1&2 and not so fondly playing part 3, which despite many good things about wasn't worth recommending because of how awful mechanically it was. The World Before brought hope back and reminded me yet again what it was that I, and so many other fans, loved so much about the first two installments. In Syberia 3 it seemed like nobody stopped to think that moving from 2D point and click into a full 3D environment would require changing how controls and cameras work and it killed the game. In TWB Microids did think and did what I think is almost ideally what a point'n'click adventure should look like in 3D. Sure, it has it's stutters, the camera is not always on your side but once you get immersed in the game - it's NOTHING. Like, absolutely nothing. You get swept up by the late Benoit Sokal's magic and that's it. It's again that wonderful world brought from the most beautiful, childlike wonder and imagination there is.In less poetic and emotional terms, TWB is good. It has a simple, but engaging story with a few twists here and there, well written characters with voices that actually fit them, moving around in a beautiful environment. Music is very nice, stays mostly in the background but when it comes to the fore, it does so with a bang. Riddles are fun - no rubber ducky - and require more of putting clues and stuff in game together than overheating the brain. I honestly can't get over how pretty, no, beautiful this game is. Characters might not always look super natural, but everything around them, the sights, the colours... it's a feast for the eyes, truly. The demo had some trouble with optimalisation because of all that beauty, but while I have quite decent specs, my PC is definitely not the youngest and had no trouble running the full game at Ultra level details. The only graphic mishap is weird resolutions. Perhaps I have not noticed something in the settings, but there weren't enough resolutions to choose from.Are there any faults? Yeah, the game ended. Like said earlier, camera is not always your friend, but it doesn't happen very often. Game is of average length for the genre, perhaps a bit on the shorter side. Some might say that the characters are unrealistic - well, yeah, some of them are, but if that's an issue, then they probably haven't enjoyed any of the Syberia games. Like in the previous ones, they are archetypes and they tap into that sort of worldview people have when they get their hands on their first adventure stories and then grow out of. It's part of the charm. To break it down then:PROS:+ the atmosphere is back, baby+ BEAUTIFUL+ good story+ engaging characters + it's so pretty, I just can't T_T+ solid riddles+ music CONS:- camera is not always your friend- kinda shortish- there are some minor details that don't line up perfectly with plots from previous games.SPOILER SPOILER SPOILERI consider it a good thing - the ending is open enough and a great call back to first game to suggest another one might be created at some point. A beloved character comes back and you are gonna love him even more than before, trust me. There has been some commotion over how Kate was when the demo for this game came out. I'm not a fan of rewriting existing characters but I honestly... I don't think that was the case here. It's Kate, the one we know and love and if there is one thing that TWB truly succeeds at doing is showing that its' characters are human. Yeah, sure, I did say they aren't always realistic, but those things don't contradict. Kate is shown to be a human being going through quite extreme circumstances and forced - over the course of whole series, not just this one game - to reevaluate and question 99.9% of her life and the emotions she shows and connections she makes are anything but shallow or one-dimensional. It's easy to label things as one or the other, but rarely is the world so simple, is it.END OF SPOILER

_childDocuments_.review: More of an interactive chick-flick than a videogame.  The main guy Benoit Sokal died during production so I can forgive them for the game's faults.  Namely, a distinct lack of any real or innovative puzzles, a complete absence of grime in the textures outside of the graveyard, & the static hair models are just the dynamic hair models locked into place.  In their haste to make the world look 'lived in', they instead make it look like the world has a fresh coat of paint, rather than, say, wear around doorknobs, dirt accumulated on the trains, etc.  There was a distinct lack of any real tie-ins with the voralberg family, really just the 1 or 2 main puzzles you can hammer out in 15 minutes each.  Everything else is find the key, locate the combination, perform the quicktime event.  In fact, on the quicktime events, every oscar segment is literally just holding forward.  This is the only videogame on the market with not one, but TWO Introspection buttons, but it feels off.  An introspection button should just be a panning view with incidental scoring or ambiance, instead it's used to fill out the chick-flick script with narraration.  In previous entries these were two seperate things, even if they were initiated by the same boundbox.  If you're looking for a 15-hour-completionist-run chick flick on the level of Green Fried Tomatoes, this is the film for you.  If, however, you're looking for a legitimate adventure puzzle game, maybe stick with the previous 3 entries.  This one feels like it's trying really hard to compete with Dreamfall: The Longest Journey, a game that fell into all the same tropes of loss, chick-flick, & nearly exclusively 'interactive' storytelling, yet so unremembered that it won't even run on current hardware.  Once you remove about 8 minutes of the musical square puzzles, there is nothing seperating actually playing the game with watching a completionist longplay.7/10 still looked & sounded amazing.  I mean, aside from the MIDI vorelburg anthem piano (!?).  10 lines of code & a button to this/the prologue could have made this game a benchmarking go-to, hits the graphics card harder than Flight Simulator.  You can't even hit 60fps on a 3080 TI on Ultra, which makes this a game I'll want to replay in 5 years.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into walking sims, you might like this.If you expect puzzles, you should stay away.The art team did a great job.And that's unfortunately everything positive that I can say about Syberia: The World Before.The biggest problem is the lack of puzzles, and the few puzzles that are in the game, are incredibly simplistic.That's not to say that it's the only issue, but with decent puzzles it would be easier to forgive the other flaws. But let's go through them anyway;The story is serviceable at best, but nothing out of the ordinary. Which is simply not enough when there is no interesting gameplay. The entire premise of the story, and the motivations of Kate, are whimsical at best, and the stakes are super low.Despite simple controls, it's difficult to get the character to go where you want them. The camera is equally unruly.In the same vain, there are plenty of tedious "interaction". Hold down the left mouse button and drag it forward for 20 seconds to move something. Hold down the mouse button, release, wait for 3 seconds, repeat 5 times, to chop down a tree.Is this seriously what they replaced puzzles with?There are long dialogues/monologues and cutscenes, and there's no skip button. You accidentally clicked on the same icon twice? Tough luck, now you get to watch the camera pan around for 15 seconds again.There are "side objectives", which generally require you to interact with someone/something, but again offer no puzzles, only more dialogue. If you're not interested in additional exposition, they're just pointless.This is one of those games that I found so unenjoyable that it spoils my memories of the first two (I skipped the third one) for me. Were they as good as I remember, or do I just remember them through rose-tinted glasses? I hope Microids leave this IP before they do any more damage to it, and I regret giving them money for this poor effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this review then I assume you're probably considering buying and playing The World Before. As this very game is fourth and latest (but not last, I hope) in the Syberia series, you might've played all previous Kate Walker's adventures - Syberia I, II and III - or one of it, or two of them in different configurations, or perhaps you've played none.Should you expect me to advise whether to buy it or not, this is what I have to say - first, find, download and play an hour long demo version. That' how I got persuaded to buy the game, and I'm so happy there is a demo on Steam available, as I might've had ignored this game otherwise.I believe that if you're already a Syberia acquaintance, you will eventually buy it and - I'm certain of it - won't regret it. I recommend to try it even if you're not Syberia or point'n'click enthusiast, but just somewhat happened to discover this game (though there is not much pointing and clicking for those who use the gamepad, which I myself found quite comfy).This and previous Syberias offer one-of-a-kind story, characters and setting (Voralberg toys and automatons are unforgettable). The World Before is a good point both for continuing and starting your Siberian Kate Walker's adventure.In my view, you don't need to play  the previous games in the series, though Syberia I and II are classics, and it would be a shame were you to never experience them ()You should start downloading the demo now and come back later to this review if you have doubts afterwards. Still, if you find that reading this review might be entertaining, or you've finished The World Before and are here to listen what others have to say just not to part with the Siberia series, be my guest!Siberia Series holds a very special place in my heart, and not many games do to the same degree, if any.When I was a kid, around 20 years ago more or less (which was just after its release), I saw my father play Siberia. I do not remember much of it - I certainly saw the beginning, but whether I followed his gameplay from time to time I do not know.I know though that I had no interest in such games at that time, but I enjoy memories of my father playing games. I guess they are sweet because not only are they linked to my childhood, but also my dad stepping into my world of some sort in this way, the world of games I was just starting to discover, and growing more relatable to my own interests. Years later , around 2017 or 18 I bought first two Siberias on Steam and completed them with delight, and it felt all like digging out and continuing an old story that started so many years ago with my dad.This is why I cherish this series so much. Soon after I stopped gaming as I used to, went without gaming for months, with ocassional gaming episodes (mostly on PS4) and quick shots with friends. It ceased to be my passion anymore - so many new doors opened and I grew out of  extensive gaming, which was beneficial for me.This September, however, I've got a month of free time and it just happened so that I got back on Steam. I came upon Siberia 3 on a discount for a dollar and decided to buy. II knew of its existence, but due to its bad reputation I thought I might skip it and finish my Siberian experience with the second part. This is also how I came upon Syberia - The World Before. Haven't heard of it until now and got attracted not only by a promise of a fresh story, but also graphic style that reminds me of Dishonored, Telltale and Life is Storm series.Then I contemplated about the purchase for a while and happily discovered there is a demo to try out, and the rest is a recent history.In my opinion, the 1-10 scale is a quick reviewing tool which nonetheless tries to convince to either buy or give up on the product, without describing what you actually lose or get, so I supplemented my assesment with a short paragraph:I found the story well-written, overally cohesive, engaging and surprising all the way until credits. I enjoyed it so much that I'd like it and/or its continuating to be translated into a TV series or a novel. Revolves around topics such as personal journey, hope, love, regret, friendship, war, investigation, complexity of life. It is incredible yet believable and relatable. I guess its not a spoiler, but I will black it out just in case - it inspired me to The 0.5 is missing as for me some of the threads and characters could be explored in more detail and embedded within the story to make it even more cohesive experience.Trully beautiful, pleasant for the eye, somewhat Dishonored- and Telltalesque style, which I find an advantage. You will take a screenshot more than once!I found faces the issue. I loved Dana and major female characters' design except for Kate. Her face is somewhat dull and its such a shame she does not resemble Syberia I or II Kate, especially considering the possibilities technology offers today ().When it comes to male characters, some of them look decent, some unfortunately look more like unaspiring copy-paste crowd with some lifting and could use good polishing to appear credible.It also applies to facial animations, and sadly hands in most cases are frozen, with fingers without movement,  as if those of a statue or LEGO minifigure.Character designs are inconsistent and you will see both good-looking and memorable designs as well as the opposite. Fortunately, it was for me just a gameplay distraction rather than experience-ruiner.I completed the game using gamepad at all times, it was pleasant and mostly smooth. I cannot say that about mouse and keyboard, but I have a feeling that it's far better than in Syberia 3.It was decent, though it could use improvement when it comes to invisible walls, such as flowerbeds which you can skip). I was once or twice slightly irritated not knowing whether I cannot acess certain area because it is not meant to be acessed or because I have not aligned my heroine appriopriately with the way through. Despite that, just an ocassional inconvenience and not experience ruiner.I haven't played point'n'click games for a long time, so I cannot remember quality of puzzles in other games for comparison. Nonetheless, I found this Syberia's puzzles logical, giving me satisfaction of solving them (which is so important!) but rather on the easy part. There were both creative puzzles that made me feel clever and ordinary ones, which required more switching and moving stuff rather than thinking, but none were frustrating.Generally, there were no "Talk to X to pick Y and then do Z" situations, and I could freely pick up items that would come in handy later while exploring, though I remember one moment when I was able to do certain thing only after I left the location and then returned to it after the story developed ().I am happy that this game was made and that I could play it. I enjoyed the story so much that I'm actually thinking of writing its continuation, I guess just for myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is a return to form after the third entry. it has the look and feel of a classic adventure, but brand new. The visuals are a weird mix of really, really good environmental design and often awkward character models, but there are quite a few breathtaking shots. Not that different than the originals in that regard, really. Regardless, the story and its pacing are very good, with a beautiful music score driving it on. There are also some really nice multiple-character dynamics, where what one character sees solves a puzzle for the other one. I like those a lot.Speaking of which I've seen a few reviews stating that the puzzles are barely there. That it's more of a story you click through, I have to assume these reviewers didn't get past the first hour or so of the game when it was mostly exposition. There are very sufficiently difficult mechanical puzzles that will have you going 'hmm' all throughout the game. They aren't moon logic, but I think we should be past that sort of thing now. The point is, the game will engage you. It's not a bunch of dialogue choices and quicktime events.-- editAfter beating this game I love it even more. Perfectly executed ending. There's room for another game, but a lot of the last three is finally wrapped up. Microids rocked this one... sadly, without Benoit Sokal I don't know what kind of future beyond this point it can have, but who knows? Maybe it's in loving hands.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Thank God they made this one after the horrendous vomit of Syberia 3. You could kind of forgive them for the flop on the 3rd because of this release, because you can tell, there were problems and things didn't go well during development of the 3rd entry. Everything here is way better.. graphically, voice acting, story, puzzles... LOGIC even. So, go ahead... just jump in on this if you've already played the series earlier. If you haven't got to know Kate Walker yet, I will suggest to play through the first 2 series, watch a full walk-through video for the 3rd and then start this.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be called Redemption for all. For Kate Walker and for the series of games as a whole. The gameplay concept in comparison with the classic games is changing again, but this time it's much friendlier to the player. It's not a strict classic point-and-click quest, but it's not even close to a walking simulator or an interactive movie, more like a mixture of adventure + Room-style mechanical puzzles + deep exploration of the world + interactive movie. It's in that order. In this regard, everything here works like clockwork, the game mechanics are very finely tuned, so you don’t get the feeling of inconvenience and uselessness of something.The story develops in two timelines: the pre-war 30-40s, where we meet the new heroine Dana Rose, and the present, where we play as Kate Walker. After the events of the third part, she finds herself imprisoned in salt mines, from where her new path begins. The story now has a palpable new flavor, I wouldn't call it hopelessly dark or gloomy, it's more about frustration and a desperate search for something to make sense of the path you've already traveled. This creates some new sensations, which allow us to say that this part of the game really gives something new to the series of games, creating a veil of emotional maturation. Again, one cannot but say about the thing that I absolutely do not understand - the manipulation of Kate's traditional sexual orientation, known to all of us from the first three parts of the game, seems to be implicit, but tangible. What is the meaning of this - I absolutely do not understand, because all this lasts literally 15 minutes at the beginning of the game, it immediately ends and  forgotten; all the next 15 hours of the game do not affect anything at all. The plot very beautifully intertwines two timelines, constantly warming up interest with each of them and placing accents exactly where it is needed. The two main characters are equally felt as the main ones; the contribution of each of them to building the plot structure is so strong.If the game looks great, then it sounds absolutely amazing. Fantastic work with both the sound in general and the music knocks you off your feet. The very serious work with the staging of cinematic scenes, the accuracy in establishing transitions between plot scenes, and great attention to the development of characters are striking. The game is filled with a lot of interesting secondary activities, allowing you to add a sick amount of detail to the main events. In the final part of the game, I encountered several crashes from the game, which is not so critical given the presence of a large number of autosaves. The open ending here is not the absence of an end to one story, but only the beginning for something new, which is incredibly pleasing. The game managed to give a new breath to our beloved series, while not suffocating it in the arms of the desire to change everything at once. The nostalgic journey never ends, which means we're looking forward to Kate's new adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Old time fan of the series here. The story is extremely good, but the puzzle aspect is barely in the game, there are maybe 15 puzzles in the entire game, and almost all of them are extremely easy. The game plays more like Heavy Rain or any other interactive movie rather than a quest. That being said the game is amazing, it is extremely enjoyable and interesting. I enjoyed to be in the world of Syberia once again. It is miles ahead of Syberia 3, and pretty much on par with the first two games... which is very very good. I am positively surprised to get such relaxing, enjoyable and good feeling game... last time I enjoyed a game this much was probably FFVII Remake on PS4. RIP Benoit Sokal, thank you for an amazing world to run away in.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, there are few games today that can really take you in to a far off place and let you just take it all in. The story was beautiful, it's probably the best part about it. I feel so connected to her story that it brought me to tears in parts of it. She lived a very difficult life with a great deal of loss. But her gentle demeanor and her ability to stand tall and still shine despite her tragedies were very uplifting. I absolutely love steampunk, and this game delivers it very well. It's a good mix of steampunk and Victorian aesthetics. I do wish a place like this existed today. However, it's not really a game. There are elements of puzzle solving but they are few and far between. And it's very linear, but also still so beautiful. I enjoyed the experience even though it's a very simple rinse and repeat process of finding points to click on and reading what they say. I think if there were more people and things to interact with it would feel more alive. And I feel that the original game had more of that. But I have no regrets about playing this game. It was a beautiful story and so well told. I will cherish this experience forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I have reviewed, so I will make it simple.  I'm a little confused by the overwhelmingly positive reviews for this "game". The graphics are pleasant and the writing is decent. However, I can't get past the inability to skip boring cut scenes and dialog, which make up the majority of this interactive movie. If you could skip the unnecessary scenes I would probably recommend it.Don't buy it if you are easily irritated by the inability to skip boring cut scenes and dialog. The majority of this "game" is filled with cut scenes and dialog! Buy it for 2 simple reasons: 1) you like games where you walk from one long cut scene/dialog to another long cut scene/dialog, rinse and repeat, 2) you suffer from insomnia. This game will help you get some much needed sleep.

_childDocuments_.review: Played all the games since I was a little kid when they first came out. This one is fantastic. All the charm of the original 2 games with modern graphics and smooth camera work. I love the camera in this game. It's kind of semi-open world, so you'll be running around an area and turn a corner. In the old games, it would've been a fade to black transition. In this game the camera moves smoothly around the corner, making the world truly 3d. I loved the story. It gets a little weird towards the end, but its not anything out of the realm of this series' universe.  If you played the other games, you know Hans' voyage has ended and now Kate is dealing with her own stuff. The story has come a long way from the big city girl solving puzzles in rural Europe. If you've followed from the other games then this is the next step after syberia 3. If you are hoping they return to the Youkols and Hans and the mysterious island to the north where mammoths still roam free... sorry, but they have effectively left that behind. They may return to it in Syberia 5, but this one is all about Kate, her grief, and her journey to discovering her true self and her personal meaning in life.There's a lot of call-backs to the other games. If you're looking for a return to the simple world of syberia 1, this is fairly similar. You technically don't leave one huge location for the entire game, but you delve deep into the city, slowly exploring all the neighborhoods connected to the trolley system. The puzzles are sometimes easy and sometimes hurt your brain. They fixed the problem with syberia 3 and really make use of the 3d item viewing system, so make sure to look around a puzzle and think outside the box! If you played the demo of the prologue, DON'T WORRY. The demo was an early release for a reason. They fixed all the stuttering and the strange graphics so everything runs great. The time travel is pretty good. It operates on a flashback basis, so if you need something in Kate's world then you might have to go back to the past to put it there in the first place. This will only be occasional and it will notify you when you can do it.
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me! It is the perfect cozy puzzle game with enough action to keep you intrigued. The story is deep and beautiful, and the visuals and music are stunning, with lovely fall/winter vibes. I bought it on sale without knowing anything about it, but I can now say that I would gladly pay full price for it. I did not see coming the plot-twist at the end. Honestly it was better and more entertaining than some movies and books out there. I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Syberia: The World Before

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and a great sequel for the saga!It doesn't miss that steampunk and nostalgic vibe that was the Syberia 1 most distinctive feature, but its modern gameplay and more intense cinematics take Syberia 4 into a new point-and-click game standards.Set in visually stunning locations, fans of Syberia will find the great characters from the previous games and new ones, interesting and original, with a new and intricate story, not to mention the beautiful soundtrack that describe perfectly the theme and spirit of the scenes, delivering the strong emotions that carry out the most important events.Point-and-click gamers can't miss this new masterpiece in the Syberia saga.Highly recommended!

name: Elderand
detailed_description: Through the darkness and madness, promised glory awaits. Heads will literally roll in this gruesome, retro-inspired action platformer, where only the strong will survive in brutal, skill-based combat against terrifying creatures. Wield a variety of killing instruments and abilities to test your metal against towering, bone-chilling bosses. Explore a twisted Lovecraftian world shrouded in darkness and madness. RPG elements allow you to customize your battle experience to your liking, from your character’s appearance to skills, stats, and weapons. Glory and riches await those who can spill the required blood and guts to collect it. KEY FEATURES: Wield an arsenal of killing devices, including whips, swords, daggers, axes, bows, and more. From a magical staff that shoots bursts of energy to a giant sword, different weapons have different stats and capabilities, so find the ones that you enjoy battling beasts with the most! Satisfying Metroidvania-style exploration meets terrifying Lovecraftian creatures in this detailed hand-drawn pixel world with glorious gothic aesthetics and handcrafted level design. RPG elements let you customize your experience to best suit your play style, from your character’s appearance to their skills, stats, and weapons. Collect loot from exploration and fallen enemies and then use it to upgrade your weapons via crafting. Travel to the many corners of this perilous land, such as an inviting village with merchants, a forest, a temple prison, floating islands, a cursed Cathedral, and the hellscape that is Elderand itself. More than 60 different enemy types and around a dozen bosses for your slaying pleasure. Collect lost letters and other correspondence from the poor souls who came before you to learn more about the darkness taking hold of this grim land.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very very very straightforward Metroidvania.Its simple, good, solid fun platforming with, simple, good, solid fun combat.The game seems to be a bit on the shorter-end, so maybe this should be on a smaller pricepoint.Nonetheless, I simply cannot give this a bad review; it truly does show polish and understanding of what makes metroidvanias tick.It will not be your new Hollow Knight, but it can definitely be a new Metroidvania to enjoy if you are a fan of the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: The first hour was very enjoyable.  Then the game forgot it was a "Metroidvania" and pressed the "Soulslike-Platformer" button where every enemy hits you for 1/3rd of your lifebar.  You could sacrifice every stat point into Vitality or simply "git gut," but for once I want a decent Metroidvania that doesn't substitute grating difficulty for enjoyable gameplay by making bosses (and some normal enemies) annoyingly damaging.  It is not even a skill issue, it's a "Make more than 3 errors and you have to redo the entire encounter" issue.12 hours in.  Most of the achievements done.  I got to the final boss (on the "Best" Ending path) and simply decided that I had had enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: "Metroidvania" is stretching it a bit for Elderand.  There are only a handful of progression abilities to get, which mostly amount to jumping better, and the world is laid out largely horizontally.  If you're looking for a vast unlocking world with a lot of secrets to find, this one may not satisfy you.  It's better taken as a straight action RPG, though to be honest, the RPG elements aren't very in-depth either.  Character growth is extremely basic, there's not a huge variety of equipment to find, and the economy (shops, equipment upgrades, and potion crafting) is largely superfluous.All that said, though, this IS an enjoyable game with a fast pace of exploration, with great art, music, and atmosphere throughout.  Combat is simple and a little stiff, but still chunky enough to have fun with.  The difficulty level isn't high, but it's just enough to engage with, and there was never a point where I felt frustrated or stuck on a boss.  There are multiple endings, with the true ending requiring a fair few extra steps that, refreshingly, aren't too difficult to figure out.Note that you can disable the rather intense screen shake effect if it bothers you; I did.Recommended if you're looking for a light action RPG experience that won't demand a huge time investment.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK, but hard to recommend when there's so many better games to choose from. The art and enemies look neat, but the combat is really rather basic and repetitive. There's technically three development paths for distributing level up point, but you lock yourself into one if you want to be efficient. The tool to redistribute your points from melee into magic, for example, only appears very late in the game. The resources you need to upgrade gear are very limited, so you probably won't want to experiment too much.A big pain point in the game is figuring out where to go and what to do. You can't mark discoveries on the map. You don't have any visualisation for when an areas is cleared. And I also really struggled to find where the next boss is at the end.Other than that, it can be an entertaining way to kill some time and scratch your metroidvania itch, but I wouldn't recommend it above half price.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Great little indie game. Think Castlevaina: Symphony of the Night with a lovecraftian setting. Beautiful pixel art. RPG leveling, 2D metroidvainia exploration. Fun combat variety of weapons and sub weapons to mix and match. Works great on Steam deck!!Update: Warning bug encountered!!!!! There is an arena challenge late in the game(not required to finish the game,but for a 100% run it is) and it can be glitched like mine. Reloading the save file does not fix it. About two rounds in the enemies instead of de-spawning sit on the screen and walk back and fourth. You cant hit them and they cant hit you. and You are stuck with no way out and have to reload your last save. Happens every single time for me now and I can not complete the challenge. Hopefully this bug is addressed in a patch. Otherwise amazing little gem of a game. Update 2 : The Arena glitch eventually worked its self out after a few quits to the desktop and reloading. So if  this happens to you it may be just that simple to fix. Reloading the save with the game loaded would not. So I was able to 100% the game after all. Loved every minute. Great game support indie devs. Recommended if you into metroidvainias.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really tedious for a metroidvania. Lots of grinding to upgrade your items and most of the required items are rare that become uncommon with a specific item that increases drop rates. There are also a ton of items that are basically reskins of each other with minor differences stat wise. My biggest complaint is that enemies do contact damage (which shields dont block) and that your hits dont interrupt enemies at all. Even with high health/armor I couldnt just trade hits with random trash (and there is a ton of that). It was kind of interesting for a while but the grinding/repetition got really tired after 6 or so hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Decent metroidvania with some significant issues.  One of the biggest problems for me was that most things you would want to track on the world map aren't tracked (such as chests that you see but cant reach yet), and there is no way to add markers manually.  This leads to cases where you have 100% map completion but are missing many things that you "explored" the room of but have no means of tracking that something was left behind.  8-10 hour core game completion time (can get all endings with 1 save file up until the final section, then just complete the last few fights differently by reloading the save or duplicating in a different file), but the last few achievements (like grind to level 100) could easily take another 5 hours to complete.  Not worth sticking around for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: If this game came out 10-15 years ago I'd give a thumbs up.  Unfortunately with the glut of metroidvania style games on Steam and elsewhere I just can't recommend this.  There's nothing absolutely terrible about it, but nothing that stands out as great either.  Combat is decent and exploration is fairly dull and unrewarding.Some better alternatives: F.I.S.T., Rogue Legacy 1 and 2, Hollow Knight, Astlibra, Souldiers, Valdis Story, Death's Gambit, Blasphemous 1 and 2, Cathedral
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: A fun metroidvania with a reasonable enough challenge, but has a crap story with a naff ending that is both a slap in the face, and takes a turn that seemingly comes from out of nowhere. It looks pretty and I'd say it's got the best combat of this type of game. On the other hand: there are so many examples of this genre (combat, platforming and exploration) available, and Elderand never truly excels compared to the others.It's satisfying, but no more than that if you want innovation, or are fatigued by just how many games there are like this. It has Dark Souls-esque levelling up, and some neat touches to it, but there's nothing new or better than what has gone before. And in many ways I wouldn't have to think too hard to suggest titles that surpass it. Boss-battles are pretty standard fare, both in their attacks and general lack of wow factor. The narrative is okay, but not especially well-written or original, and the ending is a dire ten seconds worth of resolution that takes a massive dump on the plot.So, yes, it looks nice and is pretty slick. Though compare this to the spectacle of, ooh, maybe I'm being a bit unfair here, the Ori titles, which look stunning AND play like absolute beasts, or Deaths Gambit with its somewhat more innovative boss-battles, or Blasphemous with its weird lore and grotesque designs. Elderand ends up a jack-of-all-trades: Nice enough that I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it if you're not burned out on the genre, but at the same time there's oodles of games that either have a better story, or better game-play, or both. Obviously  if you happen to have played a lot of those titles, then this is a slightly less essential one to pick up.I did it enjoy it though, at least up until the end. Where there was a really big difficulty spike for the least boss, that was then followed by an utterly sh*t reward for my troubles with a down-beat conclusion that they just chucked in. I honestly don't recall anything they put forward by this point that even suggested this outcome, unless it was so poorly translated (or written?) that I just didn't understand it.If you ever played the PS1 title 'Apocalypse' that had Bruce Willis in it, well, the ending here is exactly the same and just as unrewarding. By then I'd had 11 hours of enjoyable game-play, so it's not like I didn't get my moneys worth, but, still.....It left a bitter taste in my mouth at how badly the narrative ended up.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: "Blood must be offered and spilled..............for only then will the truth be revealed!!"I have always loved the "METROID-VANIA" genre ever since I first played "Castlevania Symphony Of The Night" and what a game that was.................no game has (In my opinion) ever come up to that games level of excellence or brilliant level design but some have come close...........is this one of those that has??Well yes and no sadly!! The game is brilliantly designed and the rate at which you gain new items and abilities (which you can then use to access new areas of the map or get hidden gear which was previously out of reach ECT) is well paced,the enemies (especially the BOSSES) are also well designed and if you aren't careful any can kick your ass in an instant,the music featured through out is good and is well suited to the game (I love the "HEAVY METAL" inspired music which features at certain points) and the game looks great with the graphics being top notch.............what then is the issue?? Well the story sadly as,as with a lot of new games the lore,background information and actual story itself is featured in game for you to discover by finding notes,through item descriptions and what the people you meet have to say to you but not everything is there that all of it actually makes cohesive sense sadly!!Its good but just lacks that certain "WHAM-BAM-THANK-YOU-MAM" that makes it really awesome or truly memorable!!Do I recommend this game then??  Well yes as its one hell of a good "METROID-VANIA" inspired game but just know that whilst it does really well at what it sets out to do it also at the same time (for me anyway) lets itself down ever so slightly with its plot progression and story telling!!So one that if you love "METROID-VANIA" type games you will enjoy but just go into it knowing that you may feel a little short changed when it comes to knowing and finding out all the games story and history!!"You really don't remember who you are do you??...............you will learn...............YOU WILL LEARNNNNNNNNN!!"
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: While I am recommending against the game overall, it is not a "bad" game but rather a game that leaves a lot to be desired, but I don't feel like I can even say "hold off until they fix the issues" because I think the game's problems are a bit more fundamental than that.The combat is deeply flawed to the point of being mediocre but serviceable, while the sound design leaves the entire audio experience at the end of a  completely forgotten save for the timing of the "swoosh-swoosh-swoosh" of your sword, the only notable thing about the sound as I played through the game was at points feeling like sounds were , for cues for enemy attacks but also it felt like the game lacked the music to set the tone during events like bosses delivering their evil speeches. Whether the sound experience is bug or folly it was certainly not satisfying.The one genuinely commendable aspect of the game is that the art is actually very nice, though some of the animations/telegraphing certainly needed work as did enemy hitboxes as they change between certain states, since you could take collision damage from enemies who had ended their attack and seemingly took up more room horizontally in a neutral stance than they did while attacking.The game also feels like it's having an identity crisis. Instead of an identity of it's own it seems to be merely a conglomeration of influences. Very clearly it's inspired by SOTN, metroidvanias more broadly, but very definitely SOTN above all the others(evident especially from a couple of later-game homages), while also seemingly inspired by the *Souls games(and perhaps also the various 2d games inspired by them).While the influences seems obvious it doesn't look like the developer has grasped what  in those games, or rather has something of a checklist of things that are emblematic of the games that inspire them without much of a mind for making those systems work in the context of their own game.And the extent to which unlocking new things feels like it really opens up the world is incredibly limited and unsatisfying;Congratulations hero, you've found the key that opens the magic gates! Only one of which takes you anywhere new(opening the gate that ♥♥♥♥-blocked you after clearing what turned out to be the penultimate zone of the game that you cleared too early) while the rest give you rings you almost certainly won't be using!Maybe wait for a discount? Maybe wait for some kind of massive overhaul? Maybe buy it if you're feeling exceptionally generous and are really willing to give it a chance against all the advice to the contrary?Maybe buy something else instead. At time of writing, both Hollow Knight and Ender Lilies are on sale and priced about the same as Elderand, both of which will get you more than triple the gameplay time for your money with the added benefit that they are actually worth spending money on.The one silver lining is that I did not spend my own money on the game as it was gifted to me by a friend, however I must now live with the eternal shame of knowing that a good friend's hard earned money has been wasted on me.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a decent game, but it's a fairly short game at around only 15 hours for most to 100% this game. I found most of the bosses in the game fairly easy. I beat the end boss on my 2nd try, for example. I also found it quite grindy, as I felt it necessary to farm materials to upgrade weapons.. something that definitely ate up a few hours of my entire gameplay. Graphics are good, sound is good.. mechanics are alright. I'd say buy this on a deep sale, though, as the value of this one is nowhere near close to something like Aeterna Noctis or some of the better ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright.Seriously though, it's a pretty basic Metroidvania, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. It has all the common traits of the genre and isn't breaking new ground but is still a fun, quick title to play. I 100% the achievements in  19 hours and probably could have done it faster if I used a guide. The main gripe I have w this game is the map system. It's 2023, being able to pin locations on the map to remind you where things are has been a common feature in this genre for at least the past 10 years or so. Outside of that, pretty straightforward game. Didn't find the music to be that memorable but it wasn't bad either. The sprite art is nice and well done. The game play is fun enough and it's quick to beat if you don't care about achievements. No new game plus or anything like that. Recommended all in all but when it's at it's best value is when it's on sale for the amount of content the game delivers... although it's full price is pretty reasonable, it's fairly priced.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Hoo boy. I went into this game expecting a decent souls-like metroidvania and the truth is that this game functionally succeeds at being that. You explore a map, level up your character, gain loot, and fight difficult enemies, all as expected. However, when it comes down to all of the nuances and details of the game, all I can think of are negatives. Right off the bat, the combat is really bad. Dodging does not give invincibility, there is no parry mechanic, and melee combat is extremely limited. All enemies deal damage on contact, which means that you can be easily hit if you face an enemy that decides to simply walk forward. When considering all of the loot the game has to offer, there is not much variation overall. Basically, you just choose a weapon type that fits your playstyle, then find whatever weapon of that category does the most damage - there is not much reason for experimentation at all. The bosses are not necessarily that difficult, but the harder ones only feel that way because they are very aggressive and offer very small openings for you to attack them in.On top of the mediocre combat, the game has the gall to make you farm for crafting materials in order to upgrade your equipment. The drop rates are often horrible, even when you equip a certain item which increases the item drop rates.The game's story is so bland, it might as well not even be there. I know these types of games tend to be light on explicit storytelling and leave most of it in hidden details and journal entries, but in the case of this game, I found the story's premise so uninteresting, I couldn't be bothered to delve any deeper into it. In terms of play time, this game is not really that long. The only reason why I have as many hours as I do is because I spent the time farming upgrade materials for all of my gear and went out of my way to get the good ending. If you decide to spend less time on the upgrades and have no interest in getting the good ending, I think you could beat this game in about 6 or so hours, depending on your skill, which is a testament to how little there is to see in this game.Overall, I found myself not having any fun whatsoever with this game. There are other titles in this genre that easily do everything this game has to offer, but significantly better. If you absolutely want to play this game, I would highly recommend you look at other options such as Grime or Blasphemous first.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't allow you to change the keybinding for menu functions, so regardless of how you change your keys, menu buttons are the same (escape to cancel and enter to confirm).That's an automatic NO from me.Cons:- No autosave when resting- Movement is very rigid- Rigid movement + clunky combat + contact damage = over reliance on jumping attacks- Every single enemy is faster than you. MUCH faster.- Part of the clunky controls issues, if you are looking in a direction (let's say left) and you quickly move right and then immediatelly afterwards you use your shield, you'll still have your shield up but looking to the left.- Enemies are way too tanky, every enemy past the 50% mark is just a damage sponge.Pros:- Nice graphics- Nice musicAll in all there is absolutely no way I would recommend this game. Not even if it sold for 2$.I'd honestly rate it at about 3/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not super well versed in the "Metriodvania" Genre, because of this, I'm probably not the main target audience of this game. _childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I think I've played enough and I don't want to play more. I'm getting way too little dopamine from this and I can't recommend it. The game feels very dated due to the design of its map and its save system. The combat is miserable and somehow worse than souldiers. The game has some good things going for it: For example, there is actual non-linear exploration in it unlike in 9 years of linearity and the performance is excellent thanks to a VERY competent unity programmer in the dev team. The killing blow though, is the amount of content in the game relative to the game's price. 220kr is just way too much to ask for this. _childDocuments_.review: If there's a genre of games that I go absolutely ape over, it's Metroidvanias; I find even the ho-hum, middling ones to be entertaining, watching the map get uncovered, abilities get increased, and secrets get uncovered gradually; they're just games where the player feels themselves progressing. Enter Elderand, an HP Lovecraft inspired Metroidvania that may be light on plot and some more advanced elements of the genre (sorry, we just cannot get over the hump of Hollow Knight), but is absolutely competent in its own right, making for a delightful 15 hour game (or much less if one beelines their way to the end) that makes for a solid 2023 play.Elderand's got the staples; large boss fights, varying weapons and styles, the usual mix of abilities that affect both combat and act as keys, and some additional content here and there that's just an addendum to the experience. There's some quick into information before trudging forward; Elderand's map isn't exceptionally large like Aeterna Noctis or Hollow Knight, but it does allow for some minor "off the beaten" path gameplay, though it's still ultimately linear at heart, which is fine; there's very little worse in these games than scanning the map for the ONE way you are supposed to go that is tucked away in an obscure part of the map (or even worse, hidden behind a hollow wall, as does happen a bit).The same can be said for Elderand's combat; there are light weapons, heavy weapons, ranged weapons, and some spells; there's not a huge variety of builds, and I found myself really only needing 3-4 weapons throughout the game. Leveling up gives literally one stat boost at a time, so new weapons and armor really are the significant boons to one's character, encouraging openings chests and exploring thoroughly. Enemies are of a decent variety, with only some minor re-coloring, though strategies vary little in their defeat. The biomes are distinct, though without a lot of connection between them; thankfully, Elderand's fast travel system is robust, making backtracking incredibly easy (I still have not forgiven Jedi Fallen Order and Metroid Dread). I wouldn't call this game scary, or even horrifying to the degree that a game like Blasphemous is, but it's at least got a little variety.These game live and die by bosses, and they're alright in this one; fun without being super memorable. They have obvious attack patterns, and generally can be figured out easily after a run or two; I found even the final boss only repeated 3-4 moves that were easy to dodge. There are a few different endings based on one or two minor choices, but they have the most minute of differences and are not worth replays until you are a completionist. I achieved full level up, map, and all endings (one playthrough, selective save point) within 20 hours.I enjoyed Elderand, though that may be in part due to my own biases surrounding the genre; it's fun without being exceptional, and won't end up being a game I think about highly when I think of the genre, but sometimes you just need to ramp through a castle, or dungeon, or bloody...skin...place...for a little adventure. That's Elderand.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to say, pretty alright and not too difficult. I really liked the environments and boss designs.
