_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet game. Gives a lot of options for weapons, armor and whether you want to be melee, ranged or magic. Combat and movement feel good, map is simple yet fun to explore. This one doesn't do anything particularly new or exciting, but it does the familiar metroidvania mechanics well. Looks great too.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10- combat is slow and clunky- air combat is even worse and everything has knockback..... your telling me this gnat has the same knockback as that guy who takes up 60% of the screen when he hits me with his sword- hitboxes are all over the place- you can hold 10 throwing axes, only one way you can throw them in a weird arc. they wont hit things right in front of you. miss most of them. its ok thought you can buy more to miss with- saves are far apart- no guide of any kind. just wonder around until you hit a dead end, and need to come back later with a new power to get past+ mini map. not the best, but not the worst- every save point says fast travel on it but i cant fast travel? do i unlock it at a later point, have already killed three bosses- Unlocked 48% of the map before i got fast travel+ works on windows 7- default key mappings on controller are AWFUL!!!i unlocked airdash and it doesnt do anything....the only thing i can do is use the dash animation in the air but it doesnt move me anywhere in any directionunable to push boxes anymorecant push a small box puzzle where you clearly need to push a box onto one of 3 buttons but i cant get it to moveturns out if you remap the keys it ♥♥♥♥♥ up everything....setting controls back to default fixed both, but now the game is harder with these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ default controls- i guess i finished the game already...
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: This is a paint-by-numbers metroidvania with Eldritch horrors. It doesn't innovate on anything (just go with a strength build) but the game is aware of this. Personally, I'm biased toward loving this genre of gameplay and story so it was an enjoyable 7 hour experience. Elderand is competent metroidvania and I had fun throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this with I have played a large amount of metroidvanias. This one has very unfair bosses and enemies in general. The enemies are to the point that I would rather tank damage and walk through a crowd and use healing potions than fight. I am by no means under leveled, and there is even a boss that spawns one shot-able enemies constantly that level you up that I may have abused a little, and they are still tanky. For bosses, they have arenas that go past your screen and most of them have attacks that span the entire stage. This makes for  frustrating undogable attacks. Some of which do a lot of damage as they are supposed to be 'easy to dodge.' But its pretty hard to if you can't see the enemy!
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: A 'no' but barely.  It's a very ambitious title, and many aspects of it are pretty good.  Pixel gfx are nice (granted, of a certain aesthetic), music is fine, good map design, and good variation of enemies and equipment.  The problem is that the controls are so stiff the game is basically unplayable.  I gave it the full two hours to see if I could get used to it, but as the difficulty ramps us, the fact that your character moves like a robot made of lead and doesn't have knee joints really becomes a frustrating hindrance.  They tout it as having "skill-based combat" but it's a bit of a farce, as there's really no finesse involved.  It's more like a clunky 8-Bit Nintendo game:  get thrashed a few times learning the patterns, then beat the boss without even getting touched.  Maybe that was on purpose to go with the pixel gfx?  The really clunky inventory system is a bit of a head scratcher as well.  There's just too many other Metroidvanias out there that are superior in all aspects to waste your time and money playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: I give this a dislike, not because it's bad, but because I can't put it alongside the games of its genre I genuinely recommend.It's mid. Adequate. Passable. It's response enough, plays well enough. I completed it and got all three endings.Combat is very simplistic. Stats are utterly pointless. You pick Vitality and put everything into it because it's +5 HP per point, or +1 strength/dex/intelligence, which is +1 damage. Enemies have hundreds of HP. I cannot emphasise enough how pointless stats felt. Also you can't reallocate stats until near the end of the game, by which point you're already locked into a playstyle and changing just before the last boss seems silly.The entire levelling up system felt like it was added because it's expected, and not because it made the game better in any way. Same with gold and crafting potions. Prohibitively grindy and unnecessary. Instead of crafting a healing potion, just hit a few urns and one will drop after a screen or two.There IS a story, but it's not communicated terribly well. Evil cults, evil gods, some cycle going on. But it's hard to feel like I cared about anything going on.---The thing I liked most about it is how much it draws from Castlevania. It has a LOT of references. In the secondary weapons (Axe, Dagger, and Fire potion), to a lot of the enemies (a spearman who stabs up on the platform you're standing on), as well as a few later things I won't say due to spoilers.Overall this game seems confused as to whether it's a hack and slash, a metroidvania, or an RPG. It does all of it okay, but doesn't excel at any.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice platform adventure/rpg.  Doesn't try to re-invent the wheel, but everything about the game is very good.  The controls are spot on, the game world is interconnected by a series of campfires where you can save the game, and restore health and potions, similar Dark Souls/Elden Ring.  You can also fast travel around to all the campfires that you've discovered.  There are some basic stats/skills that you can upgrade as you progress.  Elderand is nothing spectacular, but it's better than most similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Seemed like a cool game when watching but there's a bunch of smallish things making it not so cool when playing- Controls. Can't change confirm button from enter and it just makes menuing such a pain. Also couldn't rebind hook for some reason.- Minimum jump height is way too high (much higher than the regular ledges)- There was a campfire room where the camera wasn't constrained (could see out of bounds beyond the loading zones), this to me indicates poor playtesting- No in-game option to disable vsync, yuckOther than that seems cool so worth giving it a try at least, maybe you won't find these flaws as damning as I did
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly competent. It doesn't do anything new in the genre, but what's there is done well enough. Combat is serviceable, if a bit basic. Not what I would recommend to get you into the genre, but if you've played all the big names in the metroidvania space and are looking for something new, this isn't a bad way to spend a dozen hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game by any means. A good amount of fun is to be had here and is a nice journey. I liked the exploration aspect of this game the most. _childDocuments_.review: The game should be a metroidvania with souls like mechanics, but in typical soulslike the enemies respawn just when you rest at the bonfire or die, here they respawn always and I mean ALWAYS. Also whenever you die you lose all the equipment you got after the bonfire, so you have to repeat, reopen the same chests again and again just to take back the items you lost. Very boring game.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy being totally overregulated, then this game is for you. Everything in this game feels so restrictive: Lack of animation cancel and input timing sucks. Press attack once, you are frozen for half an eternity - press it twice and you start to puke. Every enemy has to be attacked a certain way. So this game is either braindead easy or impossible to play, feels really slow, counterintuitive, imprisoning. If you like cutting trees with a butter knife, pooping with your pants on or enjoyed havig parents that cut your toilet paper sheets the right size for your age, then this is a must have for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game but there are basic enemies that attack way too fast for you to react to. As much as I usually like hard games for a metroidvania there's too much friction from the enemies. I can barely make any headway because the first enemy after a checkpoint completely destroys me.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Its your basic side-scrolling 2d action platformer with rpg elements. You can build your character for hack/slash or magic or both (I'd recommend choosing one or the other so you don't waste your upgrade points). And you can have two separate character weapon/defense profiles, so one second you can fight with a sword/shield and have specific upgrades, then with a press of the button use your bow and have other specific upgrades - upgrades are in the form of two rings you can wear at any given time. I was very frustrated at first that there wasn't any sort of warping ability, but that is unlocked later in the game. You can save often. And something that is really cool is that you can clear your build and rebuild anytime you want (unlike in most games you have to spend a lot of money to buy that option maybe once or twice). Controls are not the best and some things are totally clunky, such as turning around while in the air or raising your shield after swinging your sword (enemies are faster than you and this often results in a hit before you can raise your shield)... enemies are medium variable (skins are reused some but you don't notice too much). The worst thing in the game is the bees..... THE BEEEEEEES!! I played it for a couple of weeks and beat it after accidentally triggering an invincibility glitch. Perfect timing for that because I was at the point that I needed to do a lot of grinding to save up money for some upgrades I wanted. If you upgrade properly from the get-go you can breeze through this. I would never pay $20 for this game, but on sale I got it for like $7 I think, and I feel it was worth it. But then again there are some REALLY good games for $7 with this same type of pixel-art and a better map system and controls, so I guess you gotta figure it out for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Quick summary: Good game that could definitely be better, if not for the flaws and poor idea executions.Can recommend this to genre fans. 7/10 (N.B. Achievements are broken as I write this review)The game is average. Not in the bad way as in "oooh, another mediocre pixel indie garbage", no. It's kinda good. actually. The art, the atmosphere, overall controls, enemies - at first glance everything looks cool, feels cool and acts properly.The world is fun to explore. It's big and bright, though not as "HUGE!!1" as some reviews I saw mentioned. You'll spend 5-10 hours exploring to 100%. Backtracking is... Let's say confusing at best. The map marks "interesting spots" automatically and an unreachable chest, a piece of lore or a cutscene area are all marked with the same red square, which makes backtracking, well, confusing. As soon as the monsters become more or less bulky - you'll notice that controls are not that good, really. Yes, it does the job, but if you're expecting something as perfect as Hollow Knight - forget about it. How many times did I land the jump strike facing the opposite direction of the enemy? He-he.Yes, there's EXP and inventory system in game. You can level up 4 parameters, equip various weapons and armors (which can also be upgraded by Blacksmith), rings and subweapons. Cool.Even though variety of options is not that huge -still kicks the spot just right.Bosses are... okay. Can't say that I would nominate any for "Wow! That was quite a fight", no. Except for, probably, that Corpse in A Lab dude. Just because he looks far more menacing than the actual fight is.Music/ Sounds and Sound Design is bland and meh. Sorry, devs, but not a single tune caught my attention. Good QA polish - didn't encounter a single bug, though some of the achievements are broken. Some game design questions are out there, yes. Like, why the mighty barbarian who just killed a demi-god can't go through the corridor, as it's blocked with a wooden box. Or why does the potion increase pouch should be won as a Colosseum's highest tier prize? Come on, man, it's just a leather satchel :DAnyways, even though this review is a list of complains - the game is worth your money (if you're a metroidvania enjoyer). It gave me 10 hours of fun, so can't argue here. Just make sure to note that it can be frustrating and bland at some points. Cheers!(Oh, and "Reach character lvl 100" achievement? Really? Guys, do you like your players to suffer or what?
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: This game has very tight controls, interesting weapons and enemies (at least as far as I could see). But for my taste, it is too old school in its design. No invincibility frames while dodging, thus no dodging through enemies.And no staggering of enemies, which often leads to them just straight up walking into me and damaging me, while I am busy trying a combo :/I would like to like the game, it looks and feels great for the most time, but it just wasn't for me.Go for it, if you want that old school kind of kombat. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game and I have tried a Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence builds. Nothing compares to the dps of the dexterity build using bow, whip, daggers, nothing comes close to what I've tested so far. Elderand is a great game however it is short, very very short metroidvania. Great mechanics and feel and the content that is offered is enjoyable as well as the boss fights feeling challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: A solid metroidvania with few new concepts. I would recommend it to people who are looking for a combat focused game of medium length.Pros-Lots of gear to choose from so you can really customize your build.-Can reallocate stats in late game.-Combat is fun (but is far from flawless).-Reasonable difficulty through the game, can't think of any major spikes.-Solid pixel art. It especially shines with regards to visual clarity. Enemies are distinct, biomes are interesting but not distracting, and particle effects never get busy enough to lose your character.-Can have multiple save files to save-scum for achievements or try different builds.Cons-Story is a convoluted mess. I found and read all the notes and thought the plot points were interesting but it was too complex and applied with too light a touch so it didn't come together in the end.-Some boss arenas are too large, allowing the bosses to initiate attacks off-screen leading to deaths that feel unfair (the true final boss is a particularly egregious example of this).-When using an item bound to the d-pad your character moves from the d-pad input. Not a huge issue but it would be easy to avoid (also the d-pad bindings are a bit wonky, can't seem to bind anything to just the right side of it but that may be a me issue).Neutral-No joke ending where you summon a world ending eldritch being and destroy the planet.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: A souls-like metroidvania, Elderand is simple in its story and progression. The difficulty of this game is surprisingly gentle for a souls-like so it's palatable for a much wider audience but people looking for a real challenge will probably be disappointed with this one. The real problem with Elderand is that it's just way too short. The entire game can be finished within 10 hours with very few weapons and secrets which made for a straight-forward and slightly brain-dead playthrough. I was really craving something that had a variety of weapons, play styles, and viable strategies but this one left a lot to be desired in that respect. It's good if you want something short, sweet, and simple but I feel like most people who love metroidvanias want the opposite.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: To me this game feels like a Blasphemous knockoff that doesn't really know what to do with itself. The art is great, but everything else is very bad. From the floaty controls to the ridiculously bad sound effects (picking up coins at the start made me wonder if this was a flash game), it just didn't click with me. The worst sin is that the combat feels far too simplistic and that there's just no room for experimentation. There are better metroidvanias to spend your time on.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful design, and the metroidvaina aspects are fine. But the combat feels to stiff and clunky for me. Most of the enemy attacks are not telegraphed at all, which makes playing melee frustrating.  And the only consistent non-melee option is magic. Which is also frustrating, because you have to wait endlessly for your mana to recharge - because you basically need all of it to kill even one simple enemy. I woud love to rate this game higher. But the combat just makes it a slug to play for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: After having played for just about 12 hours and achieved the best ending, I have to say the game was fun/enjoyable, if a bit short. Cleared the game at lvl 60 - went 100% into strength and vitality. Finished 99.90% of the map completed (couldn't be bothered looking for whatever pseudo-secret room I missed).Having played quite a few metroidvanias and roguelikes, I'll try to summarize the pros/cons of the game.The Good:- The combat system is different, but can be rewarding (there are no dash invincible frames - it's all about positioning)- Aesthetically pleasing graphics/environment, and the soundtrack isn't half bad either.- Loading between zones as well as fast-traveling is exceptionally fast- Learning enemy attacks can give you an edge and/or help you cheese things, but they will still mix things up enough to catch you slipping or getting too comfortable- You are rewarded for good blocks, enabling you to punish the opponent (within reason)- Mobility is key, as is character/weapon spacing (both for you and the enemies)- As your character grows, enemies that were previously problematic are much easier to deal with. (no duh, right? but it's especially enjoyable when some things have a harsh knockback early on and can pose a problem in groups, are suddenly getting evaporated)- You can reach a point where you can switch up your build/stats whenever you want at a save point - allows for experimentation with new weapons/gear, should you choose to do so.-- This also works to limit replay value, as you no longer have to start new characters/playthroughs to see what 'endgame' builds look like.The Bad:- The lack of a compendium with drop rates and the like, forces you to remember what things may have dropped for you in the past.- Lack of a 'sell' function has you accumulating resources and gear that you may not need/want.-- The same goes for deleting items - you simply can't do it. Which would be a problem... if the potential weapon/gear pool was anything substantial... speaking of...- The variety of weapons/gear that can drop from enemies is quite small. Enough that you'll occasionally be surprised when something does drop, but might even see that it's damage output is mediocre vs what you're already using. Special effects are literally what makes them stand out, if anything.- Purchasable gear is whelming. Could take or leave most things, honestly. What you find will likely be better/on par most of the time.- The amount of items that drop from enemies is laughable. Both from a resource (for gear upgrades and potion creation)- The cost for actual upgrade materials is criminal. (ex. lvl 4 upgrade for most things needs 5+ steel ingots, which are 2,000 each in the shop)- Upgrades, across the board, feel... meh. Like, They're fine, and you notice the additional damage, but you could clear the game with only using a handful of melee weapons, and never touch the rest of the gear (and that's with most things being between lvls 1-3 out of 5).- Only 3 different "secondary" weapons. Throwing knives, throwing axes and bombs. (very little variety)-- Speaking of which: Bombs. Never used them, never felt the need. Nothing will do as much damage as hitting things.- Only 2 arrow types in the game (why bother?)- Temporary damage boost potions seemed like a crutch, never needed them. - Magic items feels half-baked with the initial staves lacking special attacks, so they fall short of melee options.- Lack of New Game+ mode with additional zones, weapons/gear, etc. - Boss difficulty isn't consistent. Some earlier bosses are rough because compared to you, they hit like a truck. Some later bosses are as simple as being beneath them and swinging a sword with relative safety.- The amount of zones is short of passable - it looks and feels smaller than something like Castlevania:SoTN, but also lacks a inverted/time distorted, etc. variant. Even as a somewhat artificial way to extend the gameplay time, it would have been a welcome addition.- 3 possible endings, with all being achievable on the same playthrough, provided you know what to look for/do and when.-- goes back to the replay value being meh.For $20, it's not awful. Though it may be more worthwhile on sale or as part of a bundle with it's current content.I haven't looked into anything else by the studio and know nothing about the time/effort to make the game what is is today.Would have preferred this one have some more time in the oven for the points listed above, if only to make it a more lengthy/worthwhile experience.6.5 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Classic metroidvania with a feelgood vibe. Pros:- Good exploration, lot of secrets, unlocks, the world is not huge, but still big enough - Loved the boss fights, there were some interesting ones, but not too hard (except true one)- Love the vivid colours of the game, it has a really good, atmospheric retro vibe, which i love- Character progress is good, but not great (i could enjoy more variety here, but it works anyway)- Save points are placed well, loading is non existent, overally, the game is running smoothly- Retro pixelart is very nice to look at, detailed graphics with good vibesCons:- Combat: There are some issues with the combat, but its not bad, its just not really that good either. My problem is there are some bigger swords that actually have good damage, but the hero swings them way too slow, so that way u cannot attack with those while jumping. Thats a serious problem, becouse in almost every Metroidvania u WANT TO ATTACK from the air while jumping.... if u want to do that, u have to switch to some low damage rusty trash. Second problem of the combat is the input lag. If u keep attacking, the attacks will queue, and if u want to parry, the character will swing the second attack, THEN try to parry, but that is almost every time late. The best combats in metroidvanias are the ones, where the parry is INSTANT and gets priority even if u smashed the attack button before. Thats very important. - Lore/story: i loved the overall look of the world, reminded me a little bit a 2d gothic game with the lurkers and stuff, BUT then the game were instantly filled with lovecraftian cliches and cults and stuff.... Iam so tired of these overused tropes. Just leave that public domain material in the trashbin and came up with original lore pls. - The grind: i mean... its not that hard to grind, but thats the funny part. U can do a trick actually, that u keep running off the screen and coming back - that way everything refreshes (the urns), and u can collect the same gold over and over and over again. That means, u dont have to actually fight for money, but u have to run up and down for minutes. I dont think its a good system. If u WANT grind, then u should make it more interesting, bigger challenge but bigger rewards. But if u DONT want grind, then dont implement such expensive requirements of resources for the upgrades. Still, good enough game to explore for metroidvania fans.

_childDocuments_.review: First:  View at this as a kind of mixed review (thumb is in the middle but slightly upwards). I played the Game for nearly 12 Hours and at the moment that i´m writing this review, i finished it. There were a lot of things that motivated me to continue but  also some that really frustrated/annoyed me to the point, that i thought about quiting the game. I love metroidvanias and played quit a lot of them in my life (good ones  and really really  bad ones) This one is a sort of love and hate relationship. Positiv (+) + Love the artstil. A lot of details, reminds me a lot of good old castlevania or Blasphemous/Timespinner. The designs are great and the world feels how  i would expect it from a good metroidvania. + Plenty of weapons and equipment to choose from. You can play however you wish. Primary Weapons are usually Swords and Staffs.  You can either play as a mage or a warrior but there is also the possibilty to use fast daggers and to become a rogue. Mixed builds are also possible.+ Skillsystem. You can level up and invest points in four different stats (Health, Strength, Dexterity and Magic). There is also the possibility to reset your stats so don´t worry if you screw up. An option for respecc exists later in the game. + It depends of the build but the fights are challenging and sometimes you have to repeat a boss a certain amount of times, to learn his moveset and how to dodge it. Normal enemies also require you to learn, how to deal best with them. + Bossfights for the most part were fun (more information later on) Creative bosses that look like the came out of an nightmare (in a positive way) + Lots of Loreletters to find, so you can dig deeper into the story of the game.+ Steam-Deck Support is there and it runs really smooth. Great game to play on the go. + Exploration is great. There is a lot to find and see. Also some secret rooms. Really motivated me to play further. + Multiple Endings (For Spoiler reasons i won´t go any further into this, just be sure you create more than one savefile, if you want all of them)Minus (-)(2x) -   Clunky combat-system. For the most part it works well and if you know what you are doing, normal enemys (with patients) won´t be a problem. However in Bossfights.... urgh... I often couldn´t dodge or do what i wanted to do, because the combat system reacted to slow or didn´t catch my inputs (switching weapons for example). I know i´m a kind of viking-guy (?)  and should be really fast but this nearly killed my playthrough. Not because i couldn´t beat the game but it didn´t feel good to play (and i´m always looking forward to play  metroidvanias because of the exploration and the combat). Combat however gets better with every new upgrade for your character and this kinda fixes the game a bit. Otherwise my playthrough would have ended way sooner. - Storys lacks a lot. I know what the developers intend to tell you and what role your character plays but it didn´t work for me (good concept but lacking side-characters, antagonists rather pale). Big Minuspoint also was, that i played the game in german when it released and that there were letters missing. For example everything with " ü. ä. etc"  was just left out. They fixed this later on but it kinda killed my immersion.  - Air Movement later on is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I nearly ran into an enemys attack 9 of 10 times. Maybe it is just me but it felt terrible to play.- No % for Notecompletion. I tried to find them all and had a 100% map clearing. Seems either the achievement is bugged or i haven´t got all of them. However i will never know because the developers didn´t add a list of them or a %, how many of them you already got. Same with weapons and other stuff except  the map. THIS ♥♥♥♥ IS IMPORTANT GUYS!- No new-Game Plus. Seriously i know the game isn´t that long but doing everything from the start again for one different ending? Please let me keep my stuff if i try to speedrun. - Some bosses attacked outside of my visible screen. This is a small problem and only a few bosses do this. However if you fight one boss, that actually jumps all over the place, your game ends with you not even knowing, where he/she did fire the god ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ damnit blast.  All in all i recommend the game if you are a (hardcore) metroidvania-fan, that likes the artstil & exploring but also has good nerves because of the combatsystem. If you are a completionist and want a 100% please wait until there are more guides or if they add something to track your progress.  For all other players i  recommend this game if it is on sale or to try it out for 1,5h hour and give it back to steam, if it doesn´t click with you.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played a lot of Metroidvanias so it takes a lot for one to stand out and this one doesn’t. It’s fine and fun to play but it doesn’t do anything that sets it apart from the million others. The graphics are pretty good. I really like how every area has a completely different look and feel. The enemy designs might be the best part of the game. Each area has unique enemies that stand out from the rest and fit the theme of the area very well. The boss designs are no exception to this either. The bosses are really good. The later bosses can get pretty hard but none of them feel cheap. At first they might but once you figure out the patterns and tells, it feels like your fault for losing. One of my biggest problems is that it’s hard to avoid damage. There’s no dodge roll or parry. You can jump backwards but that doesn’t seem to work most of the time. The dash doesn’t give you i-frames and you can’t go through enemies. Health drops don’t happen often enough. I can go for a long stretch trying to find the next save point without any potion drops. While having a hard time avoiding damage that can get annoying to redo everything again. Overall I had a good time playing it. I did come across the final boss with about 60-65% of the map and at level 40. It beat the crap out of me fast. I came back later with 97% map, level 51, and max potions and it wasn’t too bad. The final boss and ending felt lacking but I did get the bad ending. I didn’t feel like getting the good and best endings. They have some more bosses. 12 hours is just right for this game. If it was twice as long I would have got tired of playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's something satisfying about a game that reminds you of some of your childhood favorites while still being its own thing, and Elderand did that for me. It's combat heavily reminded me of the GBA/DS Castlevania games, and the simplicity yet complexity of that combat succeeds here in making a challenging yet fun game. Sure, the Lovecraftian story may be familiar to many and the genre does have a lot of it: but I was still intrigued by the treachery and world created here, seemingly allowing for some choice in story progression and influence without being obvious.But you're here for the gameplay, and it's simple yet effective. Great enemy variety and difficult boss battles kept me entertained throughout the game. In addition, the weapons having real weight and usefulness in certain situations helped to define my character and his fight style, without being overly gimmicky or forcing one particular “best” way. Exploring this world with it's detail in environments and typical yet fantastic creature design was a joy, and in the end it's a game that really understands the K.I.S.S. Principle (keep it simple, stupid). Granted, there's a few design decisions that do make me scratch my head, like putting the fast travel option as a trinket to find on a path that you could miss for a bit of the game, but it doesn't overshadow the core combat loop and Metroidvania experience. Many times, I say that a game needs a unique selling point to really stand out in the modern day landscape to really be a must buy in my rating system, but there are exceptions, and Elderand is one of those exceptions. It gets the core combat loop and exploration right with very few faults, that it'll be nostalgic yet new at the same time. If you love Metroidvania's, this is a must have. But even if you don't, it's still worth a strong look as it could be the introduction into the genre that could hook you. Is it on the top tier of Metroidvania's? No, it's one step under it, but being Tier 2 is still worth your time and hard earned money.

_childDocuments_.review: Elderand offers a dark, gritty fantasy world brought to life through beautiful pixel art graphics. Each biome presents a distinct visual theme, adding variety and depth to the game's environment. Characters are stylized in a unique way, deviating from human norms to fit the eerie atmosphere.Combat in Elderand is straightforward, with each weapon type offering unique qualities. Dexterity weapons enable dodging, strength weapons allow blocking with a shield, and magic weapons fire projectiles. Weapons also have status effects and special attacks, adding some diversity. While attack patterns are generally similar, nuances such as weapon speed and reach differentiate them. Subweapons, consumed on use, provide additional tactical options, particularly against flying enemies or when extra damage is needed.However, the combat system has notable drawbacks. Contact damage from running into enemies, which also knocks the player back, severely limits mobility. The inability to dash through enemies further restricts movement, making the already precise jumping controls feel cumbersome. This rigidity is especially problematic when approaching enemies for melee attacks. Combat often involves repetitive patterns of jumping near enemies or blocking/dodging their attacks, which becomes tiresome given the high health of typical enemies. Aerial enemies exacerbate this issue, requiring repeated jumping attacks to defeat. Despite a variety of enemy attack patterns, the frequent respawning of enemies upon re-entering rooms results in repetitive encounters. Boss fights, however, stand out as a highlight, offering enjoyable challenges despite the control issues. The novelty of unique boss encounters adds excitement, though one repetitive boss fight featuring three old bosses simultaneously felt like an exception.The game's balancing is uneven due to specific design choices. Vitality becomes the primary focus for leveling, as it provides a flat 5 health per level, essential for surviving the frequent damage. In contrast, damage stats only offer minor increments, leading to a strategy of evenly leveling damage and health stats to avoid limitations. Dexterity may be considered for critical hit chances. While stats can be reset, the item to do so is only available late in the game. The game isn't particularly long—I finished it in under 4 hours without a guide, despite getting lost a few times. Item and component drops are infrequent, making resource management critical. Health potions, being consumable, necessitate farming or doing without when supplies run low.The map helps with navigation, automatically noting points of interest and save points, reducing but not eliminating the feeling of being lost. The inability to add custom pins is a minor inconvenience. Traversal powers unlocked at certain milestones expand exploration capabilities, allowing access to previously unreachable areas.The story and writing in Elderand are adequate, surpassing many indie games, especially those translated from other languages. The ability to skip all cutscenes is a positive feature, enhancing replayability. The music, fitting well with the levels' themes is another strong point.In conclusion, Elderand is a visually captivating game with a dark, gritty atmosphere and a unique art style. However, its combat system and balancing issues detract from the overall experience. While the bosses and visual design stand out, the repetitive combat and rigid controls make it hard to fully recommend. Elderand shows potential, and with some refinements, it could become a standout title in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: - Good equipment type variety for the genre. Many items are craftable and upgradable which adds another subtask of material hunting. Stat allocation and weapon choice allows for some minor build diversity on subsequent playthroughs. - Combat leans in on dark souls inspiration where well timed dodging and evasion are encouraged and pacing is on the slower side.- Frequent locations to save game progress- Weapons have unique sprites and most enemies also do as well with only 1 or 2 palate swaps.- All enemies have contact damage and knockback. The amount does not seem to vary by enemy size or type.- Cannot annotate or mark the map in anyway, therefore you will need to keep your own map somehow to remember inaccessible locations. - Armor equips do not have sprites. This should have been included as there are not that many unique armors in the game and the additional art work load would have been minimal.- The story telling and world building is minimalistic and hard to comprehend. Overly obtuse lure texts which add very little to the gameplay experience due to how obscure most of the writing is.- Alternate endings depending on how and which bosses you defeat. Instead, I would have preferred a single linear path.- A handful of "fantasy walls" without clear clues that they exist.- Stat respec unlocks far too late in the game. Should have been available in the main town instead. - No New Game + or additional modes for replay-ability. Overall its a game worth playing in the genre but don't expect a finely refined gem.

Exploring an intricate map doesn't fit well with this, especially if there's no easy way to avoid the enemies while backtracking - when you dodge/roll there are no invincibility frames so you end up getting hit all the time.I also feel there are too many weapons and equipment in general. Adding an upgrading mechanic with terrible drop rates in the mix doesn't help at all.I mostly stick with it because the pixel art and art direction is pretty beautiful... Yet this is a problem as well because backgrounds often mix too much with foreground making the whole game not easily readable.In my opinion it could have been made a bit shorter experience and less content heavy, spending more time polishing the core of the game (combat and exploration) but I guess having "a bit of everything" may sound better as marketing material.If you're ready to put up with those inconveniences I feel like it's a great game to spend a few hours on.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good intro to metroidvania genre games. The pixel art is endearing and the game itself is a fun adventure that takes you across several different territories. The enemies are somewhat challenging though not much of a nuisance but the boss fights are by far the most fun and rewarding. The story leaves much to be desired and the game itself is relatively short. I think there was so much more that could have been done to give it more depth however this finished product is definitely worth trying.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: It's a metroidvania that's serviceable at best. It doesn't bring anything new to the table, which on its own isn't necessarily a bad thing, but ultimately makes it hard to enjoy its core gameplay, as the very short-ranged melee combat combined with severe damage on touch can quickly turn into an unrewarding struggle. But if you decide to continue, it has some fun ARPG mechanics with a simple character progression. Again, nothing truly groundbreaking, but the game can be recommended to anyone enjoying  pixel-art in the style of fantasy Conan the Barbarian or various viking stories.tl;drBlasphemous' poor cousin.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, waiting for the second part!!! If you liked the 2D Castlevania and Metroid, Bloodstained, Ender Lillies, Vigil, Dandara, Moonscars, HunterX, Haiku The Robot THAT'S THE GAME FOR YOU!It's not so difficult like Blasphemous, Hollow Knight and Salt and Sanctuary and as for me this is a HUGE PRO!
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: Elderand is a solid metroidvania that I do recommend. The combat is good. Enemies aren't pushovers and take a moment to learn how to dispatch, especially when multiple attach at the same time. There is decent enemy variety. The combat is tough to begin with. I wouldn't say grinding it required to keep progressing. It's the natural result of exploration, but there was a point where I had to stop trying to fight a boss because she was simply too strong. So I went off in a different direction and came back later when I was stronger. There are a variety of different weapons that are fun to use. The exploration is fun. I enjoyed figuring out how to new areas with careful observation of the map and the environments. The traversal upgrades that unlock new areas and hard to reach spots are standard for the genre. There's nothing new here, but all the parts are competently done.  The game took over 13 hours to unlock most of the map. I think I got the bad ending, though. I beat the final boss and the game just abruptly ends. There were several locations that the map identifies as 'points of interest' that I just had no way to interact with. It seems like they have some purpose, but I just couldn't figure them out. There are a lot of notes to pick up that just bored me to tears. I couldn't be bothered to read through the dusty tomes. There are probably vital clues, but I pretty much got the most fun I'm going to get out of the game. It's a good enough game that I enjoyed my time beating it, but I'm not trying to 100% it. I wish there were more hidden areas to explore as opposed to performing a specific sequence of things to unlock the secrets. The pixel art graphics are really nice. I am a big fan of this style. They're visually interesting to look at. The enemy animations are smooth with the appropriate amount of gore when they die. There are a fair amount of different locations, although nothing that hasn't been seen before. Overall, I had a fun time with Elderand. It doesn't offer anything new, but it does everything well.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: I am near the end of this game. Two more bosses left. But I got bored grinding so I have better chances of defeating them. I think this game needs to have more areas to explore and some more additional enemies to make it more interesting when grinding. If not, then difficulty of the bosses must be reduced to avoid too much grinding. The difficulty of the current boss I hope to defeat, , is quite high when compared to the others. So I think there is a balancing issue here with regards to the amount of content, exploration time, and difficulty. I haven't encountered the final boss yet though so I don't know if he's even more harder to kill.The early to middle levels are alright and I enjoyed playing. But grinding is really a must here and it gets exponentially time consuming to level up. In the later levels, I felt the time needed to grind just went too far. My character is about level 70+ now and I found there is an  when reaching level 100. So I assume I need to reach that level to have better chances of finishing the game. But I gave up and just watched  on what will happen.I tend to avoid difficult and souls-like games for the reason that I cannot complete them as normal. I have very limited free time for gaming so I prefer to not invest so much hours by repeating scenes because my character keeps dying. I just want to progress and continue playing at a reasonable time frame per game title while enjoying content without too much frustrations.Anyhow, the story is  inspired. A lot of "Notes" containing lore tidbits can be found scattered throughout the map. But I think there is a lack of structure here to make it easy to understand. Conversations with NPCs are not enough to make the story clearer. Maybe adding some key animated intros or explanations on some parts of the game will help a lot.I still can recommend this game if you can get it for at least US$3 and you are not bothered by too much grinding. I rate this game  red robed Cultists.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: A Metroidvania through and through , similar to Dark souls in a sense actually! The lore is there but instead of forcing you to participate it lets you do things at your own pace via exploration and simple puzzles.There's a solid level/build system that keeps it simple , with a little crafting and upgrading in there too.While exploring you'll find the surrounding littered with goodies to buy/find or unlock.Combat is really solid , not over the top but more than just simple and every now and then a movement upgrade adds a little bit more zest just as you think you're starting to get used to it.Neither too hard or too easy and if you're really struggling at any point during the game or simply don't want to practice a boss to beat it, you can instead opt to leave and go explore and then come back stronger which I did myself several times.Most bosses are doable on a first try which is a good thing and the builds while simple in nature allow you to have a little freedom in how you progress through them.Really solid game.The biggest thing of note, is the visuals are incredible here in Elderand , exploring and seeing beautiful scenery and mind boggling structures in honestly some of the games most enjoyable content.Big Pro's:Solid movement/CombatLots of Items Good bosses Good pacing Great mapVaried AreasGood DifficultyMultiple Endings--- It's a perfect title for the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Elderand

_childDocuments_.review: A very good Metroidvania! I won't lie, at first I almost put it down, as I found the game too hard, but after grinding a few levels (it goes fast at the beginning), I really had a blast!The game is well paced, the map is nicely designed (not too much backtracking and plenty of fast travel points), the pixel art is beautiful, and gameplay is interesting (with various styles depending on the weapons and stats you pick). Some tunes are really catchy too. The game took me around 8-10 hours to 100%, which is a plus to me (I prefer intense, shorter games, than longer but also more repetitive ones).I wouldn't be surprised if the devs were making a sequel, as they have a very solid base here. Good job!

_childDocuments_.review: I should not give this game a positive review, there's too many issues with it currently. However i believe most of these can and will get patched sooner or later, so i'm giving it a thumbs up because i'm counting on the devs to do just that. Let's start with controls as that was my main issue with this game. The block for starters doesn't work most of the time, i even had a bug where my character would keep blocking after releasing the trigger on my controler. This made me move slower, unable to face my shield the other way which lead to some deaths early on. The only way for me to fix it was to crouch and melee, then turn the other way. This issue persisted throughout my entire playthrough so i just stopped using block all together, which is bad news because the game is built around it. I had to tank and spank some bosses and burn through all my consumable healing pots because i couldn't block their attacks. During my last hours of gameplay i discovered that this issue wasn't present on keyboard, but i could not rebind my keys so this wasn't a perfect workaround. Besides a controller is better suited for sidescrollers so i sort had to handicap myself to even attempt the final bosses (which were very block reliant).Other than this mayor issue with blocking, the dodge also had a lot of input lag. Melee attacks also locked you into an animation, so with how fast enemies attack and move this led to combat that felt really clunky. These issues often made you take damage you could otherwise avoid. Since the healing items are consumables (which are uncommon early) i often found it better to skip over enemies rather than fight them. Add to this the (absolutely horrible mechanic of) enemy hurtboxes and you're left with a combat system that is frustrating as often as it is fun. The combat was fairly balanced, and i would've loved it normally, but it was really dragged down by poor controls. To add insult to injury dying makes you reload to your last checkpoint, so again skipping enemies was preferable to fighting them and risking a loss of map progress. Luckily enemy variety is very good, with cool sprites and unique attacks. The same applies to bosses, so if the issues can get resolved and combat gets smoother you could have a ton of fun with the game.There's also some platforming which worked well enough but sadly there's no ledge grapling or wall climbing (which are my favorite mechanics in platformers). The level design is serviceable but nothing that really stands out or is memorable. The map is also pretty linear for a metroidvania, there's only a few interconnected zones with most of them being self contained which is a shame. The environments are aesthetically great however, with spiraling cathedrals, sweeping caverns and ruined cities. Pixel art combines so well with bloom, fog and lighting effects and this game utilizes it almost as well as the best of it's peers. The soundtrack is bit of mixed bag however, with some good tunes that are kinda retro, but there's also some metal soundtracks which feel out of place. I love metal, and i love metal soundtracks in games but i also love epic scores, either go with one or the other, not both. There's also not much variety, every singly boss (even the true final boss) uses the same soundtrack, which gets stale after a while.Lastly there's the story, which leaves a lot to be desired. The overal setting is cool, you are a mercenary hired to kill a cult leader in a far off land but your ship sinks before reaching said land. There's more to you than a simple hireling and it is up to you to save this land from the cult and it's eldritch motives. In essence this is all very cool but the writing is pretty bad. Either some of it got lost in translation or the writing is pretty poor in general. The added notes that provide background lore are also overely dramatic and borderline cringe at times. Using only big, cool & epic sounding words doesn't make for a good read. All in all the world is pretty forgettable and the 3 endings (which i all unlocked) didn't really make much sense. I'm grasping at straws trying to tie it all together, and i read every note so i think they failed to make a coherent story here.Luckily performance is pretty good but the numerous bugs overshadow this quite a bit. Apart from the blocking and input lag issues i also had some enemies phase into walls where they could hit me but i couldn't hit them back. The whole game is a mixed bag but if they can fix the issues i really think that this is a good game. Because the enemies and bosses are unique and interesting and the balance is challenging but fair. It just sucks that i had to experience it with a severe handicap due to technical issues. If these issues are fixed by the time you read this go ahead and play the game, but otherwise hold of for a while or buy on a sale because the product isn't polished enough to warrant a full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda recommend, kinda don't. Why? Well, if you need a new game to play, or just wanna scratch the Metroidvania itch, then this game will do it for you. There's a story, but it just seems to be a typical "save the world" story. nothing really compelling or interesting about it. I actually found it really hard to follow. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. It felt inspired by Castlevania, there are many old school elements, like enemies damage you just by touching you, your dash works like in Castlevania, you don't have invincible frames like you do in many games nowadays. You can level up, and put points in the traditional stats for being a warrior, a mage or being a dexterity character. It’s one of the first times I chose to be a mage in a 2D game, and it was underwhelming, there is basically just one kind of magic, a forward fireball. But that’s ok, the combat is simple overall, and in line with the old school style the game approaches other aspects.The map exploration is very good, the map is wide, and the game is not linear. The game has an average difficulty, not easy, but not hard as well, if you focus your attribute points as you level up. Enemies hit hard, but are slow, you are expected to memorize their attack patterns and not get hit many times. The music in the game is good and upbeat, despite the grim theme, reminding us of Castlevania again.If you want to play an old school game, with a few modern elements, it is a good choice. But some old school elements can be very annoying, like you don’t have a button for the map, it’s always necessary to enter the menu to see it. When you load the game, among your 9 slots, you have to look one by one, unless you memorize, which one you are furthest in the game, there is no “continue” option. But those are minor gripes, overall I’m having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Elderand is an okay game, though I wouldn't recommend it over other games in the genre. I enjoyed my time enough to 100% it, but it's so unoriginal and derivative that I wouldn't play it a second time. It's a perfectly serviceable appetiser to whet the palate on a quiet weekend. At its core, Elderand is a fairly by the numbers Castlevania/Symphony of the Night clone. Walk forward, stab monsties, level up, ocassionally equip new gear. Repeat until the end. This core loop carries the game nicely to end as the combat is slow and chunky (in a good way). The player can't move after attacking, and there's no animation cancelling. Attacks are a commitment for both the player and the AI. This gives it all the satisfying feeling of being skill-based without unfair deaths. I'm not great at this kinda game, my reactions are too slow and I don't quite have the patience to study patterns through dying/retrying. That said, the few times I died felt fair and entirely my fault. All the enemies/bosses telegraphed their attacks well, and I never needed to grind stats to beat a tricky combat encounter. A couple of bosses were a tad rough for me, but overall the game's a bit on the easy side.After killing a few naughty lizards, the player gets the ability to level up. This is mostly the same as Symphony of the Night, though the player can assign points to 1 of 4 generic attributes. I wasn't a fan of this system. On the one hand, this gives the player some limited ability to make a build and specialise. On the other, this forces the player to commit early to a weapon type for the whole game. Attempting to be a jack of all trades just halves the player's damage output, so there's little incentive to dip into multiple stats. Just max 1 of 3 main damage stats, and take as much extra health as needed. I wish these attributes didn't directly affect damage, as I was effectively locked out of two thirds of my gear for the whole game. There is an option to respec (for free!) but it arrives in the dying embers of the game's runtime.There's not much to say about the map or the exploration phase of the game. It's okay. Everything here has been seen before, unfortunately. Some basic platforming, the most common movement tech upgrades of the genre, a few hidden secrets leading to minor gear upgrades. All very standard stuff. Nothing amazing, nothing terrible. The ability to fast travel taunts the player in the bonfire menu (of course there's bonfires) for half the game, before it's finally unlocked. This is both a blessing and a curse. The game would be far too tedious without fast travel, but that's because the layout is surprisingly linear. Sure, there's multiple paths to go down in each biome, but the critical path is completely linear. Weirdly, it doesn't feel like the game had fast travel initially. Some of the rewards for exploration are opening shortcuts to previous biomes, but these are functionally pointless with fast travel.  I had the feeling that the game wanted to be interconnected with looping paths like Metroid or Dark Souls, but it was never really built for it. There's no backtracking at least.As a final note, the most notable thing I can about this game's story is that it exists. I can confirm there is indeed writing in this game. It would also be better without it. From start to finish, no NPC has anything interesting to say and the lore is very standard dark fantasy evil murder culty shlock. Given how dry it all is, I probably would have preferred if everyone was silent. Elderand also goes down the genre-staple route of having a weird ending that's unrelated to almost anything the player does, and cutting to credits after less than a minute. I had longer conversations with shopkeepers than the ending's runtime. This is a game about the journey, not the destination.

about_the_game: Brawl it out as your favorite Nickelodeon characters in bombastic platform battles! With a power-packed cast of heroes from the Nickelodeon universe, face-off with all-stars from SpongeBob Squarepants, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, The Loud House, Danny Phantom, Aaahh!!! Real Monsters, The Wild Thornberrys, Hey Arnold!, Rugrats, and more to determine ultimate animation dominance. With unique move sets and attacks inspired by their personalities, each character has an individual style of play enabling endless action for Nickelodeon’s legion of fans. Select your favorite and then let the intense brawls begin with online and local multiplayer action. Playable characters include SpongeBob, Lincoln Loud, Ninja Turtles Michelangelo and Leonardo, Oblina from Aaahh!!! Real Monsters, Invader Zim, and many more! 20 themed levels like Jellyfish Field from the Spongebob Squarepants series, Technodrome from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles series, plus many more! Each character offers a completely different and innovative playstyle and move set drawn from their lovable personalities Battle your friends locally with up to 4 players simultaneously or in online competitive multiplayer
short_description: Brawl it out with your Nickelodeon favorites in epic platform battles.

_childDocuments_.review: Please note that I have only played the game long enough to complete a few arcade modes and have not touched the online mode.As someone who plays these types of games casually, Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl is a fun game that still has a lot of kinks to work out. Most of the characters look fantastic with moves and animations that call back to classic moments in their series. However some of them, the Avatar characters in particular, have a mild uncanny valley look to them when in motion or when next to the more polished looking characters like Spongebob.As for gameplay, it is serviceable and there are moments of pure fun casually playing as characters from my childhood. That said, balance wise, characters were not made equal. Reptar for example can easily knock out opponents at low percentages with little punishment for missing a move. Hopefully future updates and patches will make this more manageable.The roster at the moment feels somewhat small though that may be more because I am used to Smash Bros. Ultimate's much large roster. 13 different series are represented in NASB (counting Avatar The Last Airbender and Legend of Korra as 2 different series) and of them, 8 are represented by a single character. Honestly I think it is a reasonable variety for its roster size. Hopefully any future DLC will add new franchises and fill out the single rep series, instead of bloating one series with multiple characters.TLDR: For its price, NASB is a fun platform fighter for casual play. For the more competitive crowd, if you can get past the initial jank, NASB could potentially grow and be polished into something worthwhile if given proper support by the community.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the Multiversus stans and review bombers, this isn't a $50 game, but it's an absolute great timeThere's so many gameplay mechanics that you could spend hours just trying to learn one of the 22 characters (there's a couple more that are DLC but they're worth getting)The game is currently on sale for $15 with the DLC being an additional $10 and I'd recommend it to everyone at that priceYou can always join the NASB Grinders Discord server to help you find matches because yes, people do still play this game, and once crossplay is finally added it should be very easy to find matchesDon't let the visual jankness fool you into thinking this game doesn't handle like a dream, it's one of the most responsive games I've ever played as far as button inputs, just like Slap City before itWould I recommend this game over Slap City?Well, I think Slap City is easily the better deal, but it also has way less characters and not universally recognizable ones either. So up to youBut yeah, I cannot recommend this game enough, anyone saying this game is the same level or worse than Brawlhalla either never gave it a fair shot or is lying through their teeth

_childDocuments_.review: I initially gave this game a negative review after playing it for 4 hours, but I have found every time I have played it since then (10 in-game hours) that it's felt more fun than the last and I have become more comfortable with the controls. This game is a good time, though there are a few minor changes I wish were present (but I am hopeful the devs will add them soon).That said, I do have a few changes I personally would like in the game based on my experiences playing it so far:+ Characters should have a bit more intangibility at respawn because as it stands they can be hit almost immediately upon spawning back in.+ Snap to ledge (ledge intangibility is already pretty minimal as it is).- Weak down aerials on much of the cast should be modified to not combo into itself as easily (either giving the move slightly more knockback or endlag/startup time).+ Slightly faster command grabs.+ Players should have some degree of control over the angle and trajectory of his up special. As it stands, the move always only goes in what appears to be a 45 or 60 degree arc, regardless of user input.- Helga's up special should be weaker, at least later in the move's animation (strong where she starts it, weaker near the end of it) or decrease the size of its hitbox.+ A bit more ground speed and less startup time on some of her moves, like her strong aerials and aerial down special.+ Jump-cancelable grounded down special would be nice for following up on hits or mixups, and it could achieve the aforementioned "ground move speed" without changing her base move speed.+ Hitboxes on his strong forward attack needs rework. Currently, anybody inside the big ball (end of the laser) will not take damage or knockback. Would be nice if it could sweet-spot there.+ Get up attack from ledge doesn't seem to hit characters standing right at the ledge (or hits them conditionally, maybe?). I think this needs fixing...+ Give Reptar just a bit of armor on his up special so his recovery isn't completely abused by others.- Add a cooldown mechanic to his grounded down special similar to the cooldown mechanic on many of the projectiles in the game (it should take longer to use each time you use the move in succession for a set period of time). That, or nerf the damage output of his grounded down special (maybe 30% => 18%), or both.+ Give him a bit more height on his up special.- Increase endlag or startup time on his weak down aerial. Currently it can be spammed and it covers a lot of area (seems fairly disjointed, too).+ Increase flick damage and/or knockback. It's not  currently, but it's a decent finisher at ~90% (depending on the character).- Make Nigel's weak down aerial a steeper angle or slightly slower. Much of his movement hinges on this move and it can combo into itself at low percent near the ground.+ Increase pizza projectile speed and/or make it send whoever it hits at an interesting/useful angle.+ Make him slightly smaller, maybe?- Give his weak forward aerial a bit more knockback or endlag since it can be used to essentially "carry" an opponent to the side blast zones if executed properly.+ Give her more power or faster with her strong grounded attacks (she's already so bad in the air, might as well give her a gimme).- Reduce time Toph can stand on her platform. She can currently double jump, up b, set up a platform, then camp and throw rocks. Could also just make it so platform can only be made while not in free fall.+ Make her a bit smaller.- Make her weak down attack send further out or send up so that it can't be spammed as easily.+ Make him a little smaller?+ Make him a bit smaller.- Give him a bit of endlag for landing with strong down aerial, or make the move a bit weaker.Additionally, Hollow Convergence (?) is a bit laggy (possibly because of the background particles and animations), so I avoid the stage for the most part.These are just my personal change requests–I know that very few will agree with me on every aspect, and I did not touch on every character and what could be changed about them–but I think many of these changes could make some characters a bit more usable and some strategies a bit less "spammable."

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Incredibly well made fighting game. 9/10Initially I thought this game would be too casual, since the game I played prior to this was Smash Melee (which is very difficult as a beginner and highly competitive). But this game exceeded all my expectations, I didn't think I would have so much fun AND feel challenged from this game. The characters are diverse while also being incredibly well balanced. The gameplay is fast and smooth, the movement isn't difficult but learning the attacks and how to combo is interesting and allows a lot of creativity.Outside of my personal enjoyment with the game, the game's tools are great. For all the try-hards there is a trainings-mode which allows you to gather frame-data and study hitboxes. For the people that want to play more casually there are casual game-modes in which you can just enjoy the mechanics of the game in a fun environment.I hope people support this game, since the developers have done such incredible work from the beginning, it would seem like any added content for this game just adds to the awesomeness.Only deducting 1 point because of the price.There are no voice-lines or cosmetics YET, but it seems like this is going to be added once people supported the game more. I think it would've been a better approach to sell the game cheaper and sell cosmetics in game, but I respect and understand this approach as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Thought I'd go on ahead and give a genuine review on this game, I've been playing it a lot since launch on Switch, then recently went on ahead and got it on PC for a discounted price.So, Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl is a platform fighter, a subgenre of fighting games where the goal is to knock your opponents off of the stage. If you've played games like Super Smash Bros., Rivals of Aether, or Brawlhalla, those are prime examples of this genre and you'll probably get used to the gameplay very well. At the moment, there is a 20 fighter and stage roster (22 counting the post-launch characters/stages that were confirmed), featuring fan-favorite Nicktoon characters from quite a few eras. Overall, I think it's a pretty good lineup, having characters from the 90s along with a couple from the 2000s and 2010s, though I feel like maybe there could be a few more from the latter eras to get those shows some more attention, but that's just me. Still though, decent lineup. More downloadable content is likely gonna come, so I'm looking forwards to seeing what the developers bring. The game has some banger music tracks as well, and you can even download the soundtrack for free!The gameplay is fast-paced and very competitive-focused, so for fans of competitive play in platform fighters, you can definitely enjoy the style here. There's strafing, wavedashing, air dashing, and many other cool techs you can mess around with. I'm hooked on the gameplay, which is why I've been playing it so much lately. However, at the moment, there aren't any things such as items yet for casual players who would like to use them during matches, but I'm pretty sure those are in the data and will likely come in an update.There's a few modes, such as local play where you can just play matches with the CPU or irl friends, with customizable rulesets with stock battles (lives), timed matches, and sports mode, where you knock a ball into the goal. There's an arcade mode, which can get you some unlockables such as songs and badges. The online is also pretty good from my experience.One thing that the game kind of suffers in is the polish. Some of the animations are a bit choppy, and it's noticeable in certain characters more than others. The developers had a pretty strict deadline and also didn't have enough of a budget to make the game as polished as some people want it to be, so that's likely why. It has potential to improve though, definitely. In my opinion, it's not TOO bad to me, but I can understand why some people can be turned off to this. There also isn't any voice acting, which is a known thing that people aren't happy with, but then again, the game didn't have a high enough budget. It IS possible later down the line if Nickelodeon decides to help out with that, but who knows?  Hopefully they could at least use sound clips from the shows or something.For a $50 title, I won't lie, I think that's too much for the game in it's current state. I got the game on both Switch and PC with discounts, so you could try looking for those if you can. The content is a bit on the shortside and there isn't much polish. Later on if it gets enough updates, possibly it can better match the official listed price. But for now, I''d only suggest buying it if you really want the game immediately / really want to support the devs right away. If the game does well, many quality of life things could come for it which I'm pretty excited about.That's about it, overall I think it's a great game, I can understand why some people are turned off by it, but I see a lot of potential in this. Hopefully it gets a lot of support.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. But I'm currently having to write negative because the control rebindings seem to place a firm layer of interference between me and my controls.This isn't some scrub rant about how I supposedly think strafe seems weird at first glance, I think lack of jumpsquat makes the game too quick, I think fast airdash is a braindead approach, etc. (for the record, I don't think these things.)This game simply isn't smash bros, you cannot treat it as smash bros, and you need to learn these options in the identity of its own game rather than brainlessly say they're bad because they're not what you're used to. My issue also doesn't lie with any balance issues or infinites. A few have already been discovered as of day 1 writing this review, but games with infinites can be fun. People played melee with wobbling for years, there's TONS of people playing super old janky fighting games that have infinites. And even with that, the NASB devs seem aware of the fact that they exist. They will probably (ideally) proactively balance around them and/or create systems which help to mitigate them. My issue is deeper and more objective: the QoL for controls(and even in general, more on that later) in this game seems to be incredibly lacking. For context: ALL of the movement and button and interactions in this game are ENTIRELY digital. A movement/button is either PRESSED or NOT. There is no in-between. This means you're either holding forward, full-steam ahead, or standing still. You can't tilt slightly to walk. Let me reiterate the point I made in the beginning of this review: this is FINE. This game deserves to be examined in a vacuum and interacted with as a distinct identity, not lazily compared to smash. Now, with all of that being said, since this game is on PC, I decided I would prefer to play this game with a controller that reflects digital inputs rather than analogue inputs, so I ditched my GC controller in favor of a keyboard. I do not own a hitbox/b0xx/frame1 or a fight stick as they're expensive. I would love to own a frame1, but they're out of stock and I'm a poor college student. My money needs to stretch as far as I can make it.So, due to unrelated factors, my keyboard broke, I opted to buy a relatively decent slightly cheap mechanical keyboard rather than a hitbox controller. Mechanical keyboards can act as a hitbox controller in games if I don't mind going through some effort cracking rebinds that work for you. I decided to invest a little on a keyboard that will probably last more than a really low quality 20$ one. Kills 2 birds with one stone: I have a pretty viable fighting game controller and I have a keyboard that will probably last me longer than what I'm used to.And because of that decision lies my issue: this game has NO support for rebinding my MOVEMENT keys. I'm forced to use ARROW KEYS, which my keyboard literally doesn't even have - I'm using a 60% keyboard keyboard, which I decided on to save desk space. This means I'd have to press FN and various other keys in order to get arrow keys to input.This is pretty much unacceptable for me in its current state. Am I being nitpicky? I don't think so. This game is 50$ by default and 40$ on the release sale that I got it for. That's money that could be going towards a lot of other things I want and need. Furthermore, control rebinds are fundamentally one of the most important ways to bridge the gap on making players comfortable interacting with your game in a smooth way. This is vital for comfort, especially if the game's appeal is to be somewhat competitive. Not to mention arrow keys are very rarely the way many gamers control things, considering right handed people are the majority, and hitboxes and mixboxes typically places controls on the left hand like WASD in FPS games.That is my single biggest complaint with this game. Beyond that, I'm...disappointed with some other aspectsTraining mode seems incredibly barebones. I'm happy for some of the options, such as hitbox toggle, but incredibly upset over others. I want to be able to set training dummy DI, record their buttons and replay, maybe set their ledge getup options, tech roll direction, and stuff like that. Another piece of icing on the cake would be in-game frame data. The fundamental hook of a fighting game in GENERAL is getting bodied by something you have no clue how to beat, then going and watching the replay, labbing against it, figuring out how to beat it, and then performing this in matches.YOU are the one leveling up in an incredibly direct and intimate way. It's not done through a layer of roleplay in a game such as an RPG. Your control over what you do is very precise and exact, and the improvements on the path of getting good, in my opinion as somebody who loves fighting games and not RPGs, are thus more meaningful, interesting, and fun. Training mode is the CORE of the fighting game. It's not just a combo room or a techskill practice zone, even though it's incredibly good for these things. When training mode suffers, the fighting game as a whole suffers. I don't want to lose faith in this game, and I'm very eager to keep tabs on updates. For one, this game has rollback netcode, and that simply cannot be beat. Rivals of Aether and Brawlhalla are the only comparable platform fighters in this regard, and I love to see more competition and variety enter the rink. Furthermore, the systems this game has going on seem GENUINELY interesting to me, and I would love to lab and interact with them on a deeper level. But it just feels painful when the way I want to play this game seems so feasible yet barely out of arms reach due to a lack of polish. PS: I know keyboard remappers exist, but that doesn't excuse lack of in-game QoL. Not to mention keyboard remappers are incredibly long-winded to set up and trickle down into annoyance in other regards. ex. if I rebind WASD to arrow keys, and then I need to open steam to talk to a friend. i'd have to disable my remapper to be able to actually type those keys. Nothing beats direct in-game remapping.
