_childDocuments_.review: Edit (2023): Still a good game but it's absolutely almost completely invalidated by the sequel unfortunately. If you're interested in this game get NASB 2 instead. Only go for this game if you're a hardcore plat fighter fan or collector, or if you have an interest in where the series started. There are some characters, stages, skins and items that didn't make it into the second game but that game is still better than this one in almost every possible way.First off; this is a good game, but don't buy this game for full price, wait for a Steam sale or buy it on a third party website. Ludosity deserves better than the corporate greed that has been holding this game back since launch.IT FINALLY HAS VOICE ACTING, which does wonders for the charm and feel of the game!Ludosity knows how to make a good platform fighter, and just like with Slap City, it shows with this game. Mechanically it differs enough from others such as Smash, MVS or Rivals to make it worth playing IMO. It's incredibly fast paced and heavily favors offensive play over defensive play. Unlike at launch the game is now very well balanced and you can pretty much pick any character without being at a huge disadvantage somewhere. Just like with Slap City this game has some brilliant stage designs. Lots of great layouts for competitive play and also quite a few fun hazardous stages too.As far as casual content goes the game now offers items so you can really mix up your matches with some whacky stuff, especially when combined with some of the more crazy hazard-filled stages. Sports mode is pretty fun but not every stage works well with the mode. There's also an "Arcade mode" which is just a series of fights you go through to reach an end goal and unlock some extra content after finishing with each character; similar to classic mode in Smash.Online play has rollback netcode and plays very well. Supposedly cross-platform play is coming eventually too so that will be nice.Content-wise as of October 7th (with the DLC pass included) the game will have a total of 25 characters and 25 stages (22 characters and 22 stages without the pass). I think if you're looking for a good multiplayer game with friends then there's plenty to offer here. But outside of the main multiplayer there isn't much going on and that's why the game isn't worth the full 50 dollar price tag. Honestly as it is I would say the game is probably worth somewhere between 20 or 30 dollars, since Rivals of Aether, Slap City, and the other GOOD platform fighters on Steam are all within that price range.Great game made by great devs, just not 50 dollars great. Find it cheap elsewhere (literally found it being sold on another site for less than $3 USD) and support Ludosity by buying Slap City or the DLC pass at full price instead.

There is no opening or ending to the Arcade game, not story, no introduction to the game, no static image or video, there isn't even any type of acknowledgement you beat the run except for a score and some unlocked static 3D model shots...It seems there are no unlockable characters or bosses... what you see if what you get + what you can pay for in a month when DLC comes out... Weirdly enough there is already character art for Mondo Gecko from TMNT, i assumed they stripped him last minute to sell as DLC later on (very similar to Capcom practices, where they just softlocked characters and you pay money to have a small ini file changed that unlocks them)... there is already rumours that there is supposedly audio in the game for other characters as well... very sad since the game already feels very emptyThe levels are nice, but feel small, they are pretty static and the fun part about Smash is the random items and events, but none of this is in this game. If you get knocked of a level, gravity is so high that there is almost no chance to get back on the level, no escaping death in this game.The loading time is horrible, takes almost a minute to load a level, and a match only lasts a minute or two too, so you wait almost as long on a match to load as playing the actual match. This game looks amazing, but it's just unfinished, for $5 you can grab Brawlout and have a much better experience unfortunately... i whished this was better, i was really looking forward to playing TMNT vs Ren&Stimpy... but it's just boring and feels empty

Pick this up if you’re nostalgic for any of these characters, but also consider why. If there was a guy who also had that same connection I could see popping this in and throwing down, but I also could see doing that with a lot of fighting games and probably would choose one of those. There is no story mode for the characters, no 2v2 queue, no challenge maps, and a limited roster some people are pretty unhappy with but doesn't affect me personally.Also, you can tell that some of the characters were rushed.  Very similar up specials for a lot of them, some wonky animations and strange/similar move animation choices between characters, and stuff that just doesn't work.  The balance seems kinda off too, as some characters received more attention to detail and some are outright bad (looking at you patrick) even though they are fun.Good stuff though:  Gameplay is really fast and fun, music is dope, there is good variety amongst the 20 launch brawlers and the game has tons of character.As a launch product, it's a pretty poor release.  You can tell it was rushed hard for release date, and it suffered for it.  If you buy it day one, you are not getting much. If you want to support Ludosity (Slap City was awesome in EA and only continued to get better with each patch) and the future of the game with it's ridiculous potential or you just like what's there, grab it while it's $40. _childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly really fun, even if I have my gripes with it. If you're going into this expecting it to feel like a Smash-style platform fighter, you're probably not gonna have a great time with it. With the game having digital inputs instead of analog, movement is gonna feel clunky the first time you pick it up. Instant dashing and fast-falling aren't in the game, due to those relying on analog inputs to work. There also aren't horizontal aerials, though I personally don't think this is a huge issue. It's a lot of small things that can make the game disorienting when you first play it, but it's all things you can definitely learn with enough time.I do have a few complaints with the game though. My biggest one has to be the platform fall-through mechanic, where you have to press Down+Jump to fall through platforms. I totally understand how this works on paper, and I've seen it in platformers before, but in the context of a plat fighter it doesn't work very well in practice. Maybe giving players the option to double-tap down instead of pressing Down+Jump might be a good idea? Also arcade mode feels pretty lacking at the moment. Hopefully future updates can add some extra polish to the mode to give it its own unique identity. Polish in general is something the game needs a lot of currently ^^'Character diversity is another thing the game needs. Outside of a few exceptions, pretty much every light attack in the game feels really similar, especially since almost every light comes out on frame 6. Specials switch up the game a bit, but I feel like a lot more could have been done frame data-wise to make each character feel more unique and personalized. A friend of mine put it best by saying "it feels like you're fighting the system more than the characters." Because of how similar the frame data is between characters, the general gameplan for fighting every character is about as similar, which can make the game overall feel bland after a short while.Overall, the game feels more like a very promising early-access than a full game release. I'd still recommend getting Nick All-Star Brawl, though do it while it's on sale, since at the time of writing this, I wouldn't consider the game worth the full $50 price tag. The game has a lot of promise though, and knowing Ludosity, I'm sure the game can only get better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played a few platform fighters before, for reference. I've logged around 10k hours in Brawl and its various mods like Brawl+,Brawl-, Project:M etc. before their end of life cycles, around 2.5k in Melee, about 1.8k in Smash 4, and 700-800 in ult, 1k in Rivals of Aether, a few hours in Slap City.I've been super hype for this game actually, ever since I saw the mechanical explanation. While I love Smash as a series its just clear they have little to no interest in building, growing, or maintaining their competitive community, improving game play balance, or fixing issues with the netcode. So I was immediately hype for a game that seems to take a relatively fresh and unique approach to platform fighters. With its deep mechanical systems allowing for moves to cancel into each other on hit, airdashes, airthrows, and a special RPS system for smash attacks.  The release tonight took me by surprise because it wasn't even midnight in my region but I'm not complaining.That being said I've been researching it for a while prior to release and have a few issues with it but overall after playing it for a few hours I'm very hopeful for this game's future and satisfied with the product created here.The Good:- Combo game is sick, its fast, fluid, and expressive.- The character design and cast are relatively small but the game seems balanced, honestly it feels like a labour of love. (People might say "Well X character zero to deathed me!" but honestly it feels like everyone has some kind of touch of death at this point from the footage I've seen.)- The team that did this game also did Slap City. (So if you like that type of experience and gameplay you're in for a very similar experience here just with a bit more polish and a Nickelodeon face lift.)- The game is silky smooth, and the graphical presentation is honestly amazing.- ROLLBACK NETCODE!- Developers had more of an emphasis on competitive play but didn't overlook casual options  or raise barrier of entry either.(Hitbox viewer, default 1v1 ruleset, rollback, EZ-wavedash macro, etc.)- Devs also said they would support mods, so some smaller topical and other quality of life changes may happen outside of official patches, and this also gives us future potential workshop character content.The Neutral:- Traditional smash DI (?)- Plat dropping in this game is done by holding down and pressing the jump button. (I personally like this change for accuracy's sake but its a bit jarring and I can already see it taking a while to get used to.)- The game is fast. Like FAST. If you're the kind of person who can't consistently tech you might get comboed to death easily.- A unique platform fighting experience this is a "hybrid fighter" so the game is somewhere between a traditional platform fighter, and an anime fighter. (For example there is no shielding like in smash, there is instead blocking in this game. There are no high/low mixups, but crossups (left/right mixups) are possible as a result, airdashes and airthrows are possible, etc.)The Bad:- Control schemes for this game are digital so no tap jump. Its also impossible to have two buttons as the same command.- No voice acting (Bit of a personal gripe but the lack of voice acting seems like a bit of a missed opportunity for a little extra flavour but doesn't affect the actual gameplay.)- Hit feedback (in places) doesn't feel good. Alongside no voice acting, this game doesn't really seem to have much hitpause, as a result your stronger hits can end up feeling shallow on the user side at times.Overall I'd recommend it. Its honestly one of the best (NEW) platform fighters I've played in a long time and I'm looking to seeing how both its community and meta forms and develops.

_childDocuments_.review: So after only playing two hours of Nick All-star brawl, I can honestly say it is NOT the "Smash Killer" people claim it could've been. This game is textbook example of what happens when you hype up a game to extreme levels. Because it creates an expectation it will never meet. While I do like the nostalgia of some of the old school nicktoons characters, the gameplay is awkward at best, Clumsy and Clunky at worst. Pressing Jump and Down to go through a platform is to be blunt, a stupid idea especially for a platform fighter. And the stuns when you clash a move or push someone towards a ledge is also pretty dumb. I've only won my matches by pure luck most of the time. And while there were some stages that were fine, like Battlefield, FD and Animal crossing style stages were fine, some of the more gimmicky ones are painful. Worst than some of the gimmicky stages in Smash Brawl. And that's saying something. Oh and one last thing, while it was nice that voice acting is in the game because I know that was what everyone was wanting to see in this game, I found the voices to be grating and repetitive after awhile...I didn't buy into the hype, as I kinda knew it would be more on the mediocre side... But sadly, it's definitely on the lower mediocre side of things. The only good thing it has going for it is Nostalgia, Grabbing projectiles and throwing them back and the online play (when you can actually get it to work) actually plays well! And I believe the only reason this game got even some attention was two things... Nostalgic Nicktoons characters and Smash Melee gameplay. If it weren't for those, nobody would even look twice at this game. I say just play smash if you want your smash fix. However if you do wanna try it yourself, do yourself a favor and wait for a sale. I wouldn't spend more than $10 personally (I paid $20).3/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played a lot of smash and slap city I gotta say: I don't like it.All the characters feel hollow and have barely any distinct move set or playstyles. Of course some are heavier and slightly slower or lighter and faster. Some have generally longer range, others shorter but they all function essentially the same. When I'm able to juggle enemies instantly with every character by short hop neutral spamming without needing to think which buttons to press, it just shows how shallow all of the characters are. Normally in games like this I would need multiple hours to understand how each character works, how their attacks combo and what attacks can be used when. But here I REALLY feel like I can do the same buttons presses with any character to achieve the same results.I understand that animating every character takes a huge amount of time, especially with such a small team, but the animations are just so lackluster. Everything is animated so fast, no matter the character or move which just adds to the general feeling of sameness. I almost can't tell if the very still models for most of the recovery specials is a stylistic choice or just work budget saving.The game is just not fun. None of the characters capture my fightan imagination. On top of that here is my nitpick list which sour everything even more:- No alt colors- No proper double bindings of functions- No control customization for: platform fall trough (down + jump), no tap jump option, no right stick options

_childDocuments_.review: It's like street fighter meets smash bros melee. It's very fast paced. If you're not a veteran of smash bros melee you may or may not like this because it's very combo and footsies heavy. Footsies is a term to describe a normal attack to close distance or to provoke your opponent into doing a unsafe move. You also have to space a lot. That just means controlling the distance between you and your opponent well. If you don't like touch of death combos, this isn't the game for you. There's a lot of touch of death combos for every character in the game but since every character feels unbalanced, that really balances out the game. It's really fun amongst similar skill level friends or online opponents but can feel devastatingly bad to the point where you would want to instantly refund because the game feels unbalance when you play someone better than you.If you can push through the hardships and learn than you can be really good at the game. Everyones on a equal playing field right now so it's the best time to get into the game so that you can learn as the game develops instead of in a year from now when the games more popular and much more tech has been discovered.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game the moment it game out. I've been a competitive Melee/PM player for a long time, and have also played Rivals, Slap City, Icons, and other PFGs. As of now, the game is fun, but feels very lacking in some basic aspects.- There can only be a single binding for each action, so I cannot double bind shield. My muscle memory involves using R to airdash, and L to block. As of now, that's impossible.- The only way to drop through a platform is to hold down and press jump. This is extremely counterintuitive to me, and should be a togglable option in my controls.- I can't get my Gamecube controller working via my mayflash adapter, and there's no menu in the game to help me identify controllers.- I'd like the ability to invert Strafe behavior such that by default Strafe is held, and only disabled when I press the button down.- Hitboxes come out insanely quickly, are much larger than they appear, and characters seem to be able to act out of hitstun/move endlag extremely quickly.- Ever since Rivals, I thought the platform figher developer community had figured out this whole wavedashing thing. Holding straight horizontal and jumping, then pressing airdash during jumpsquat, should result in a buffered max length wavedash. As of right now I feel like on my Xbox controller if I go more than 45 degrees out I instantly get a fully horizontal airdash. Maybe jumpsquats are short and I'm getting the timing wrong? Couldn't get it to work a single time.All of these gripes aside, the game is a fun party game with functional online play. I got many games in on quick play in my first day. You should be able to judge by the trailers if this is a game you want to play.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is responsive (both offline and online thanks to roll back net code) and the characters have good movement options. The result feels very good to play. Characters move like the way you want them to, as if they were an extension of your fingers -- the game mechanic don't hold you back. This was the essence of what made SSB: Melee so good and lost in subsequent Smash games. NASB recaptures this, which makes it potentially the best Platform Fighter since Melee.I also appreciate how they've streamlined parts of Melee to make it more accessible to new players without making the game feel shallow. The game ultimately plays differently from Melee but the same satisfaction from the smooth movement and combos that Melee provided is still there.The only caveat is that the polish is not comparable to the original smash games, but the core game play seems excellent and the net code is great (seriously, roll back net code is far better than anything Nintendo has implemented). There are no major issues that can’t be improved with future patches.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial opinion of this game so far is pretty positive! Is this game the Smash Bros. killer? Absolutely not, I don't think anything ever will be. That being said, if you have previous experience with platform fighters outside of Smash (namely Slap City), then this game will make you feel right at home! This game feels very fast and frantic, which is a whole lot of fun when most of the characters feel good to boot. You can definitely tell that Ludosity and Fair Play put in some quality effort to make this game feel fun, unique, and competitively viable.There are a few minor gripes that I have (tapping down not dropping you through platforms, some moments where the CPUs just kinda... stop working until you hit them again, custom control bindings resetting between matches, and some of the characters' animations seeming noticeably rougher than the rest of the cast), but none of them are enough to stop me from recommending this game! I know that the developers are in pretty frequent contact with the community and have a general feel on what people want from the game, so I wouldn't be surprised if my gripes are eventually resolved entirely. That being said, I wholeheartedly recommend the game in its current state if you're a fan of platform fighters in general. It's a blast!

_childDocuments_.review: It's Nickelodeon's Bargain Bin Smash Bros, and that's alright.EARLY REVIEW IMPRESSIONS/IMPORTANT FACTS:No keyboard support (controller is a must, but pretty much anything Steam supports up to and including GameCube controllers can be used if you know what you are doing.)Don't listen to reviews that say there is no keybinding, it's on the character select screen underneath the character you're picking, sort of like how Smash Bros lets you enter names there, here you can change the key bindings.There is no tap to jump on the stick, which I understand some people dislike, but...This game is made from the ground up to cater to a competitive crowd. The modes I've tried had no items, and it's purely you vs other fighter(s). Online works smoothly, although I suspect some servers are having issues right now. If I set my game server to US East (which I'd assume I'm closest to being in Ohio) the match I played lagged like a typical Smash Bros match. If I set it to automatic I had smooth, fast matches.No ultrawide support, but that's unsurprising for a budget priced 'indie' title, and not many fighting games support it anyways.As far as content, arcade mode nets you concept art, the character's stage music for the jukebox, and an avatar for online. Otherwise there is NOTHING to unlock apart from achievements as far as I can tell.Gameplay is king and it's fast, buttery smooth, and fun. Feels faster than Smash Bros. Ultimate, and at times even faster than Melee IMHO. Is it balanced? Who knows, all I know is April's hit range is big and her mic attack slaps. I'm just glad she's no longer a damsel in distress, but instead a diva serving looks while slaying the house down boots mama.Just go in expecting a good ground base for a game that can and hopefully will grow into a larger and deeper game, as of right now it feels like a pretty good skeleton of a game with a solid core to build upon.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of gripes I have with this game, but that doesn't take away from the fun that I've had playing it so far.  I would def get this game at a 30-40 dollar price point (half of what a typical big release is).  I'll list all my positives and negatives below:Positives:-The game has a very recognizable cast, nick really should invest more money into this platform fighter-The game has both a competitive mode and casual modes that really alllow you to have fun no matter what type of player you are.-There's some form of customization on your online profile (albeit not much)-Online works well for the most part (I got some bad games but that might be one of our connections instead of the game), gets choppy when laggy but that's expected if the connection isn't good.Negatives:-There's simply not that many differences in some of the roster's normals that allow the characters to look unique and it gets very noticeable (which I think is very important to any spectator or player).  This could be fixed with adding distinct touches to their animations so they stand out more (or simply making the characters more unique as they get added to the game).-The game needs an overhaul in the sound department.  The hit noises are whatever, but lack of voice acting and the game's soundtrack not being very diverse when playing on stages just really makes the game sound stale.  more music and voice acting please.-The lack of alts for characters in the game is really disappointing.  Not only do they help distinguish players better than the player icon but also gives the game a little more personality.  Having a doodlebob or donatello color scheme when playing makes playing with those characters more fun than it would be as normal.-single player is barely a thing in this game.  Arcade mode is very basic (just typical round of fights with no distinction like team battles, the characters do say some generic lines but that wore out its charm very quickly since all I could think is how they could've made a rich story to the arcade more in those text boxes instead), and there's no other options except playing CPUs or seeing the extras included.-The base roster is good but there are some missed opportunities for characters that aren't there at the moment (we'll def see some of them as DLC though so I can't be too upset with "must haves" like timmy turner or Jimmy Neutron not being in the game yet).-There seems to be glitches in the game regarding hitbox detection (this may have been the rollback netcode simply not being accurate for an instance but I did find it strange seeing one of my opponents die only for them to not be dead).Again, I want to iterate I enjoy this game at its core.  But I can't lie to you and say the game at launch doesn't have problems that should be addressed in future patches/DLC to really make this a memorable experience for platform fighter fans

_childDocuments_.review: A Smash-style fighting game where you get to watch your favorite childhood Nickelodeon characters beat the everloving ♥♥♥♥ out of one another. It's just one of the weirdest games I've ever played. The gameplay itself is okay and feels like what you'd expect. There's some inventive levels like a Powdered Toast Man level where you fight on a kitchen counter on dirty dishes and inside a bowl of cereal, or a Rugrats level (I think)where you fight in a playground and can sink into the sand. Overall it's okay, but none of the characters speak or make any noise whatsoever. Michelangelo never says "Cowabunga." Ren never calls anyone an "Eediot." They just fight in complete silence. I imagine it's some kind of licensing limitation but unfortunately it makes the game feel weirdly empty. It is also literally empty of other players because I could not find any multiplayer lobbies to join and I let quickmatch run for a while and I was unable to start a match. So you're left battling the extremely unskilled AI in limited single player modes, with the only difference in difficulty being the number of lives you and your opponent get. It ends up leaving me feeling like this is a game I should have gotten on a CD-ROM that came free in a cereal box. Normally if I play a game enough to beat it, and I beat this twice, I'll recommend it, but this game is so insubstantial that I feel like I got the full tour in 20 minutes and it left me not wanting to play it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/6/2021 updateNetplay is jankier after more playing, might have to do with my own connection's bandwidth but it is still sadly better than say, Smash Ultimate's.*Recommend IF you can tolerate some jankThe game is legit fun from what I've played so far.Movement feels a bit janky sometimes but I'm still adjusting, but at the same time it also feels good to move when you can tame it, if that makes sense.Controls could use a little more customization, it's weird that you can't pick two buttons to do the same thing.Sounds can feel repetitive especially without voices, and it's especially noticeable when you get that meaty killing hit which sounds similar to all other hits; if it weren't for the announcer occasionally going critical hit you probably wouldn't even realize it. Feedback leaves a lot to be desired in this game; I don't get that dopamine hit on kills, it just feels like I'm just tapping buttons and stuff happens and I go "oh ok". The game looks and plays fine but the lack of feedback makes it hard to gauge impact/range of moves.Online is OK when it works, most matches I've played so far were smooth except for that one match where someone's connection was very potato-ey and it felt like a slideshow. Also, you're stuck starting at a screen if you queue up for (at least competitive) matches, which feels weird in 2021 when most games let you at least practice with a character, but I'd imagine that's a feature for the future since the devs seem to have a constrained budget and time-frame, and I can tell they're trying their best with what they have.The game feels mechanically put together well from what I've played so far, and I definitely like the speedier pace of the game compared to say, Smash Ultimate. I will say it will definitely take some getting used to (you have to crouch and hit jump to drop from platforms, and I hope the devs implement toggles on that type of behavior that we can set in future updates.Basically, if you're able to tolerate jankiness I definitely would say at least give this game a bit of a try.There's lots of potential in this game and I look forward to what the devs do for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think people need to separate this game mentally from Smash Bros. While there is clear inspiration from Smash Bros, the game is different enough mechanically that it can be viewed as a standalone platform fighter. Movement, offense, and defense all work differently in this game, and it takes a bit of getting used to. While being good at other platform fighters is helpful, there is still a lot to learn in this one. Smash is an incredibly polished series of games with the financial support to consistently provide amazing gameplay, music, visuals, sounds, content, etc. and I don't think it's a fair comparison.Is this game a valuable competitive experience? Yes. It is fast-paced/many buttons per second, and for those coming from other platform fighters, it may feel weird for the first couple hours (it may even feel a bit button-mashey at first) but once you get used to the movement, the game will feel a lot better and even more strategic. This game feels very fresh and I believe the development team did a great job with it. I would say the main issues is the animations feeling weird sometimes in relation to the gameplay, and a lot of the characters' moves feeling samey, but it's exciting to have a new cast of characters that each have crazy combos.Treat this as it's own product, and find some people to play this game with. It is enjoyable, and the devs have shown that they listen, so we can presume improvements will be made in the lifespan of the game, especially with the incoming DLC characters.

Though those are a wild fun time, and worth celebrating. At the end of the day, what really sells the game for me... are the developers, and their passion for the game and the genre.The fact is, this is made by a small, extremely passionate studio who are doing everything within their power to make a legendary game (despite the small budget given to them.)The free updates have made great strides toward achieving that potential. - Garfield is glorious, and we got our first villain with Shredder. (Both came with a new stage.)- We got alternate costumes (albeit only one per character).*- The game now has voice acting, as well as items!*In my opinion, the game is already fun. Yes, I wish there were more songs to cycle through during battles. I wish there were more side-modes, more alternate costumes, etc. But with the knowledge that our financial support will be used not only to improve the game, but alleviate many of these criticisms... knowing that many of these have indeed been addressed since launch... Put simply, if the game's premise sounds fun to you, consider treating it like a Kickstarter. It's not perfect, but it's a good time. _childDocuments_.review: O...kay.I haven't played a more out of place Smash clone since Playstation All-Stars Battle Royale, until Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl. I was intrigued enough to give it a try since it's Smash and the whole premise of a brawler with no blood and gore would be a fitting scenario for a kid-friendly environment such as Nick. I, quite frankly, feel there is so much incompatibility with the roster that it shows just by how they interact with eachother.Generic one-liner or in character phrases that share no acknowledgement to the other character is all you need to know to tell how much all of this was just thrown together. I still feel there should've been more characters from each show to help accommodate this. For example, if they added Dib from Invader Zim and the interactions between Dib and Zim would've had an encounter with eachother that involved brawling to continue any sense of their in-show rivalry. I would've totally been on board with things like that.I played as Shredder in my first run and I'm surprised he didn't even recognize April O'Neal when I fought her. Guys, you're in the same universe!Someone could say that it's just a simple brawler, nothing needs to make sense. I guess so, but it wouldn't hurt to have some level of immersion in this game. Especially with cartoons who can be as self-aware as they want.Now for the gameplay itself, it's just a Smash clone, what else can you say? It actually plays just as well as a Smash clone can. The animations are fluid, there is a nice level of depth in attacks and defenses with each character. There's nicely done themed stages. I mean there's some level of effort put into this, at least.I just simply can't wrap my head around the fact that, the opportunity to make a roster more interactive is such a missed mark. The difference with this game and the Playstation brawler, is how there was zero chemistry between the characters for Playstation. There were too much of a difference between each character that made them so incompatible, it's hard to think how they'd even be relevant if they had cameos in other games. It just didn't work and fell hard on it's face.Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl had cartoon characters that are so personalized, it would be a little believable for them to acknowledge eachother. Such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that has played and still plays all Smash titles(except Smash 4/Tr4sh), including PM. I STRONGLY recommend buying the game and supporting the developers that poured their heart and soul into this.That price tag seems steep for what the game offers at first glance, BUT you will forget about it the moment you start playing this addictive and fast-paced game.This game bridges the gap between Ultimate and Melee in another marvelous way similar to PM. All-Star Brawl seems a bit more easier to grasp as well to an average player, which is good accessibility for newbies,however the Skill ceiling and layers to this game is tremendous! This is not your typical Smash clone(ICONS) we have here, it's another inspirational platform fighter with it's unique techs,such as how the game handles projectiles, strafe button, air grabs, and so much more.The game features one of the best rollback netcodes I have ever experienced, as good as Slippi's(Melee Netplay). Played many players at the ping 130 and below, superb gameplay.However, rollback does not fix horribly slow internet either, so make sure your internet is at LEAST tolerable and you should be fine.All-Star Brawl handles online lobbies the best I have ever witness as well in any fighting game I have played, which is a ton, so that says a lot.You have the options to turn down the game's music volume and also the announcer(can turn him off even).CONS:-The game doesn't have much to offer for single player wise, and CPU's are complete duds. Do not buy if you plan on playing this alone.-No voices for the characters, however this may change in the future of DLC as mention by devs-No Alternative skins for characters, however this may change as well, since there is skins in the games files, so it is probably planned.-No FFA Matchmaking, only in online public lobbies. But it may not be their fault. Apparently Matchmaking for 2 more players through Rollback is difficult as Slippi can't do the same atm.

_childDocuments_.review: My hopes for the game were never high, it was bound to be at the very least a decent game with some fun nostalgia drizzled on top. It fell below an already low bar however which is extremely upsetting.I'll start with the PROs:- Character selection: A good diverse cast, some weird choices like Helga are in there, but for the most part I don't think anyone can complain about who they chose. The strong and Badass Toph and Korra, the infernal and epic Reptar and goofy-ass Spongebob.- Mechanics: The mechanics are decent, not weird enough to be cons but decent. There's wave dashing and blocking, some fun combo strings you can do. The button mapping is the problem, that's later though.- Rollback: Rollback netcode is always a plus. Nothing else to say.-Party Game: At the end of the day if you just want to play with friends, or a group of people at a buddy's place then it's a fun game, but competitively this game isn't it.And now... CONs:- Hitboxes: They are atrocious. Some characters like Korra, Toph, and Patrick to name a few have their hit boxes at the end of their full body attacks, not throughout all of it so if you're point blank your attacks will miss. For instance Korra's light attack is her punch but the entire arm extension isn't the hit box it is JUST her fist, so if you try to attack someone getting up you miss if you're too close. Meanwhile other hit boxes that are strictly someone attack forward hit from ABOVE and BEHIND. Zim and Oblina as examples can hit you from behind, I tried this on a local connection and still found myself turned 180 degrees, strong attacking in the other direction and hitting a character away from me. Even Korra who has a problem hitting up close has her side-special where she charges straight forward can you hit you if you're landing on her.- Sound Design: All of the sounds in this game are the exact same as any other move of similar use. Of course it's a LOT of work to make different sounds for each individual attack, but every sword slash sounds like ever microphone slap, sounds like ever staff smack, and so on. Only distinctly different moves actually make different sound like Toph's earthbending, April's cameras or Patrick's phone. Otherwise everything makes a general slap or smack sound. On top of that, no characters emote, half of the fun of party games is playing characters you love and hearing them say random one liners. I can't tell you the amount of times "Show me your moves" has sparked someone at a Local to try even harder cause they refuse to lose to a taunting Falcon. Meanwhile, the most I hear from Spongebob is his breath from blowing a bubble.- "Clashing": Certain attacks making certain players do random motions is infuriating. Because someone used a high attack against a low they get completely flipped? So every encounter is either one-sided (whoever attacked first) or a rock paper scissors match? Why?! Why on earth in a fighting game about timing, reaction, and spacing are you going to add an element of "oops you attacked medium into a high, flip around please!" can you see how bizarre it is? Imagine if in Smash or even other games like SF or MVC they had mechanics like this. 50/50s are a risk for reward, if you call a move out, you get a combo starter. If you're mixed up, you immediately have to be defensive or rethink options. This isn't a 50/50 or a calculated move, this is a game of RPS and if you lose randomly, you could lose all of your advantage.Grabs: Grabbing projectiles? That's fine, need some timing but that's good for anti-zoning. Grabbing through shield? Normal, sounds good. Grabbing mid-air? Uhhhh.... Wait wh-Grabbing and getting thrown at 8% and being unable to act out of grab as you fall down half way down the stage? Yaaaay.Keybindings: You cannot remap important keys on keyboard and barely move things around on controller. W H Y?Conclusion: This game is unpolished, it has a very good foundation. Built on great characters, rollback and fun mechanics. However, there are glaring issues that need to be patched as soon as possible if this game wants to stay afloat. It will never be a "Smash Killer" but it could be a fun non-Switch alternative Smash game if the devs spent more time before release or if they make a roadmap about changes that will impact some of the problems with the game. In it's current state I can't recommend this game unless you wanna get a few drinks and beat your friend's ass as Powdered Toast Man.Grabbing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty damn amazing considering that is a budget game that got rushed to meet a deadline. The roster was supposed to have 22 characters but they had to cut 2 of them for later release, probably free updates.As for the game itself the combat is incredible, it's super fast, faster than any Smash game, which makes battles pretty chaotic and anyone's game. You can very well survive with more than 100% damage or be knocked of with 50% or less depending on the attack you received. It's kinda weird to use one more button for attack instead of just light attacks and specials but it's just a matter of practice.The characters are all pretty good with the exception of Patrick, at least right now, because he has some slow moves and he depends on grabbing the opponents which can be pretty tough to do with the crazy speed of dodges and wavedashing. Don't judge this game as a low effort cash-grab Smash clone, I watched all of the devs' showcases and they clearly have a lot of passion for this project and there's more to come, which will improve more and more the experience.I've played 5 hours so far, beaten the arcade with all the 20 characters and I would give a solid 8 for now. The only real issue I had with the steam version is that my game got stuck at 1280x720 resolution and I could not solve that problem. I pretty much agree with Max Dood that this game is just like Battle for the Grid, both games have a major inspiration (Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3 and Super Smash Bros Ultimate) but they also offer some things that those big games do not have, and Battle for the Grid evolved a lot and it's getting a ton of stuff even to this day, so it's a matter of time for Nickelodeon All Star Brawl to get better and better.

_childDocuments_.review: All-Star Brawl is a pretty fun platform fighter that is really ruined by its budget. Despite carrying a triple A price tag at 50$, the game feels extremely unpolished even compared to other indie platform fighters such as Rivals of Aether, which sells for almost half the cost of All-Star Brawl.The most apparent effect of the game's low budget is seen in the game's audio. The lack of voices is quite noticeable and really causes the characters to lose a lot of their personality. In addition, another large problem is the small soundtrack of the game. Each stage only has a single song that is attached to it and you cannot play a stage's song on another stage. Since the competitive game mode only has five different stages allowed you can be sure that you will be hearing the same  couple of songs every time you play. The game suffers from its budget graphically as well. Although most of the character models actually look pretty great, many of the characters' animations do not feel smooth and some things, like throws, are not animated at all. This causes the game to feel like it's incomplete. In addition there are some weird issues such as Danny phantom appearing disproportionately large when compared to other characters such as Aang, who should be around the same size.Still, even if there are problems with the sound and the graphics, there are plenty of games with mediocre graphics that are still very fun to play. The real question is whether or not the gameplay makes the game worth buying. Personally, I would answer no.The first thing that you need to know about the game is that it is a extremely fast, hyper-aggressive, air heavy game. If you usually like to play a zoner/trapper/defensive style then the game probably isn't for you. While there are characters  that are classified as "zoners", they must still play very aggressively in order to win. That being said if you are looking for a very fast, rushdown oriented game then you will probably have a good time. The game is very centered around aerial combat and the options that you have on the ground are very limited compared to other platform fighters. In addition, the prevalence of zero-to-death combos means that there much of the game is either spent in neutral or in comboing your opponent to death.  The game is pretty much the platform fighter equivalent of Marvel vs Capcom.Now, I would like to try and go over a few of the more specific mechanics in the game and explain what I do or do not like about them. That being said, these things come down more to personal preference then the mechanics being objectively good or bad.1. AirdashingOne of the more interesting changes from smash is that characters no longer have an airdodge and instead have an airdash.  While the characters do not have gain any invincibility during the dash they can act out of the dash much quicker. The airdash adds to the aggressive nature of the game in several ways. The first is that it really increases air movement and allows for players to chase after their opponents. Second is that it decreases an opponent's defensive options within the air, meaning that players within disadvantage have a really difficult time escaping from pressure. Ultimately, the combination of these two factors causes a very large focus on aerial attacks, where you can easily string light air attacks together to get a 60% combo.2. Universal ThrowsI have a feeling that this is another result of the game's low budget, but throws in the game are exactly the same for every single character. In addition, all characters are able to "cargo throw", meaning that they can move around and jump while they are grabbing an opponent. All characters are also able to grab in the air. Universal throws are one of my least favorite aspects within the game. The biggest problem to me is that they simply are not interesting. As I mentioned before, none of the throws are animated and the angle of the throw is the same for every character, every time. None of the throws lead in to combos very well and they feel very unsatisfying to use even when they end up leading to a kill. 3. Shield MechanicsMy hate for the throwing mechanics in the game is only exacerbated by the way that shielding works in the game. Every character can shield indefinitely and there is no shield break mechanic within the game. Instead if someone shields near a ledge and are hit then they enter into a vulnerable state. I really dislike how the shields work.The first problem is that if a character is not at the ledge, then the only way to deal with them is to use grabs, which as I already stated are boring to use. In most fighting games, guards can be broken by high/low mixups in addition to grabs, and in most other platform fighters, you can pressure shields to get past guards in addition to grabs. All star brawl only gives you one option to deal with shields and it can be pretty annoying to deal with opponents who like to shield a lot. It seems strange that a game that is so focused on aggressive gameplay would decide not to allow attacks to pressure shields.Using shields also feels pretty janky as the shield lag makes it kind of awkward to do things out of shield.4. RPS SmashesAll Star brawl has implemented a rock paper scissors system to their smash attacks. If two smash attacks clash, then it can cause one player to become stunned depending on the type of attack. While this would be a rare occurrence in other platform fighters, the presence of aerial smash attacks means that this actually becomes relevant surprisingly often. Up smashes beat down smashes, which essentially means that a player on the ground has an advantage over a play that is being juggled and trying to land. However, it also means that sometimes when you try to kill an opponent off the top with an strong up air, they instead go into spin out and you often do not have enough time to punish it. The mechanic isn't too annoying but I don't get the need for it to be in the game.5. MovesetsThis is most likely another result of the game's budget, but unlike smash where each character has 4 tilts on the ground and 5 in the air, All star Brawl's characters only have 3 tilts on the ground and 3 in the air. While this is slightly made up for in the fact that characters have air smashes, the all star brawl characters still end up with a lower net number of moves. One of the biggest effects that this has is that ground gameplay is heavily neutered. Instead of having a jab and an forward tilt, characters only have a single mid attack. For most characters their neutral attack is either equivalent to a jab or a traditional forward tilt. The problem is that characters with a jab for their neutral attack usually do not have a tilt that kills, while characters that have a more tiltlike neutral attack, do not have a jab move that they can use to get opponents off of them or to jab reset characters who miss techs. Moves on the ground are usually just used to take opponents into the air.One of my other biggest problems with character movesets is that they do not feel diverse enough. Most of the character's movesets are very similar to each other, where their up attacks are just some sort of juggling attack and their down attacks are some form of spike. Since strong attacks are mostly just used for kills or hard punishes, most characters really only approach with one or two attacks (usually nair).  Combos usually are just comboing the same move together or some form of nair, down-air string. The limited moveset makes it pretty difficult to have player expression and does not support a diverse range of playstyles. Overall, I really did not feel like All Star Brawl was for me. I think the game is fun, but the large focus on aggressive airplay strayed a little too far from a playstyle that I personally enjoy. If you enjoy rushdown then you will probably have fun, but it might still be difficult to justify it's 50$ price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic fighting game utterly mired by atrocious imbalance, outright broken "mechanics" and generally being overpriced as a whole.There's very little content to this game despite the price. There's a decent roster of characters and stages, although few stages are available in competitive, but that's about it. There's no alternate outfits or recolours, or any real progression elements at all besides unlocking profile pictures and pointless gallery images in arcade. Some of those images being really bad looking ingame screenshots while others are just actual pictures you can already see ingame at certain points. In arcade mode, at the start of every level a really lazily slapped together text box shows up in which each character participating in the fight says a completely random quote from their canon; which has absolutely no relevance to what's actually supposed to be happening. Really driving in the suggestion that whoever created this didn't really care or understand the characters in any way and just threw in some cheap asinine callbacks to their lore in an attempt to appease players. It seems like the price of this game is bloated by the fact that all these characters are simply just in it; yet the developers couldn't even get voice acting for them. And despite how much nuance there is to the various characters, their how-to-play sections explicitly do not explain certain aspects of their mechanics even though the gameplay is all about utilizing the characters and their mechanics.Although the combat manages to be fantastically satisfying, fast paced and responsive it's absolutely fraught with balancing issues. Most of all the sheer disparity between the knockout potential of various attacks. There are characters who can't knockout opponents with an upward heavy attack while they are at a hundred percent damage; while other characters can instantly knockout an opponent who is at thirty three percent damage with the same type of attack in the same situation. Yet despite the massive power difference between these attacks there's zero functional difference in how difficult they are to land or use at all. Some characters are just objectively stronger, and can knockout opponents far easier; in a game that's entirely about knocking out your opponent. While other advantages may vary none of them ultimately matter when a single ordinary attack can end the game. The game also has problems with stunlocking. While players can interrupt, some, stunlocks by pressing block as they tumble onto the ground; stunlocks that keep the player in the air are exempt from this. There's no consistent or coherent way to escape an airborne stunlock, it just kind of happens by mashing the evade or downward attack button.Combat in this game is steeped in a broken, untutorialized but seemingly deliberate movement "feature" that allows players to basically simulate high ping by pressing certain buttons at a certain time. This combination of buttons breaks the flow of character movement, causing them to jolt in a certain direction and essentially teleporting a short distance on the opponent's screen. Many players spam this constantly because it not only allows them to move faster but also allows them to completely cancel upward velocity and instantly land back on the ground, cancel the cooldown on attack animations to more quickly begin new ones thus fundamentally attacking faster; and cancelling the cooldown on attack animations to trigger stunlocks that typically would not be possible due to the cooldown. It's unbelievable how much this has utterly consumed the combat system with so many players relentlessly spamming it; teleporting around the map while rapidly attacking and instantly negating their own velocity when knocked away. Yet despite this it is seemingly an intentional "feature" added in by the developers because presumably this "feature" has existed in other fighting games, likely as a glitch which was never patched due to the playerbase becoming too dependent on it to play. It transforms the game into a broken, twitchy mess of spam entirely unrecognizable as a fighting game and I don't think it's ever going to be removed because apparently a significant amount of players are fine with abusing busted movement to turn the game into a spamming contest.Fighting other players in this game is consequently often worse than fighting the computer opponents. As not only do numerous players abuse this broken movement but they're already completely dependent on the meta of each character, spamming the same attacks over and over because apparently they believe that's the most optimal attack to use so it's the only one they're going to use much of the time. Many players explicitly spam the jumping light attack on their character, and also spam the broken movement thing everytime they knockout another player almost as if in celebration; making many fights so similar that it distinctly feels like fighting identically programmed bots. Also the computer opponents do not taunt. As the developers were insecure enough to feel it appropriate to even add a taunt option despite no player with a secure ego having use for such a thing in its intended purpose. I've even heard talk of players trying to use the taunt as a way to animation cancel in order to attack quicker, because that's just how desperate they are apparently.This game provides an amazing combat experience if you can match up against a player that doesn't spam just one or two attacks over and over, abuse the busted movement to rapidly teleport or forcibly cancel their own animations and physics; or match up against a player using one of the characters that has attacks which are up to three times more effective at their purpose compared to identical attacks used by other characters. Plus it's ridiculously overpriced, with you basically paying mainly for all the cameos despite them not even being fleshed out with any progression elements or even voices.Although Ludosity once again succeeded in making a combat system which is great in a controlled environment where its numerous imbalances are not abused; it's disappointing to see them abjectly sell out and become mere pawns to another group seemingly just for profit. Although that may be understandable if it was necessary for them to survive. I can only hope they diverge from this rut of obnoxious, spam ridden fighting games and eventually return to making content that actually has some degree of artistic and creative merit as they were so capable of previously.If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .

Ludosity decided to try with Slap City, which although a great game it had appeal problems and characters that where memes at best and just plain strange at worst. That being said playing Slap City you KNEW these developers knew EXACTLY what they where doing and how to achieve it.Then this game changed the game entirely, smash ripoffs before where just that, ripoffs. They didn't get the appeal, the mechanics, the idea behind a smash clone beyond "uh throw our IP's together and have marketing come up with accessibility garbage". Ludosity said "♥♥♥♥ it now that we have access to recognizable IP's time to make Melee 2" and they DELIVERED like crazy.The game is absurdly fast, I play Melee at a decent level and this game makes Melee look lethargic in comparison. Already in it's infancy we see amazing sets, high skilled gameplay, and lots of passionate people going as fast as humanly possible doing crazy things. The game feels AMAZING to play and pull stuff off, with a few simple issues like the sticky platforms that will be addressed in time since these devs actually listen to their audience, and have been rewarded with an already fantastic community that if fostered correctly will grow like mad.And the bad news, the game lacks a LOT of polish. The normal human looking characters (basically all the avatar characters) all look VERY jarring, the animations lack a ton of polish and things look jilted and juxtaposed especially since their seems to be a lack of transition animations between attacks (which admittedly with a game this fast would be absurdly hard to do), with seemingly generic music and no voice lines nor any real one player game modes that are substantial the game needs a TON to reach Smash quality when it comes to a complete package. Although you could tell that was not the focus of the devs who spent their time crafting a super fast, high skilled, and rewarding game to play. Arguably the most important part of the game is a smash (lol) hit and with the polish this game will be one of the BEST products on steam by far. And finally, it can out compete smash, breaking Nintendo's monopoly on platform fighters that are relevant (sorry Rivals).The game is 100% worth picking up despite this lack of polish, it has a ton of room to grow with great devs who are transparent and involved in the community, and has decades worth of material to work with for more content to come. Get ready, get sweaty, and make your hands hurt.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game.I love platform fighters, from Smash to Rivals to Rushdown, almost all of them. One of my favorite ones is actually by Ludosity, in which some of these dev made this game, that being Slap City.What I love about Slap City and other platform fighters in general is the fact that you can pick it up and play it with no BS. No real need to learn anything, no quarter circle inputs and specific button combinations, just a couple buttons and tilts and boom: you know how to play the game on a basic level. Because the controls are so basic, anyone can get into the games. Which, this game does offer that as well. However, what this game doesn't offer is any kind of appeal to moreso casual players, or at least those competitive players like me who still want wants to both improve at their own pace while still just having fun while doing so. How does it not appeal to casuals and how is it difficult for competitive players to improve?-The gameplay is EXTREMELY fast as well as any character's attacks to the point where I can't even tell what's even happening 80% of the time, speaking for my best friend and gf on this as well. When we play each other, we genuinely don't know how one of us got stocked or stocked each other at times. Then when I go to quickplay, that problem is amplified by 10. I get 4 stocked so fast and don't really know how I got stocked in any of them due to the blazing gameplay speeds. -Speaking of quickplay, I'm lucky to find any games at all because it is seemingly very rare to connect to anyone after over 5 minutes minutes of searching. The game's dying already? Anyways, players in quickplay are just being better than me and having an advantage from being used to this game's pacing or come from other speedy fighters. Yes, I'm bad at the game, but that's not the problem. The problem is how does one improve on their skills if everyone they find online is seemingly god-like to their perspective? Players they find are experienced and demolish people whom are still trying to learn. Playing offline will only do so much too improve one's skill. Plus, I can't stress this enough, it's ESPECIALLY difficult to learn anything when the speed of the game is THAT FAST. Maybe I should have guarded or wave-dashed away from my opponent to avoid their tilts and combo setups? Maybe I should have charged in first, maybe I should have jumped, maybe I should have did a n-air? I don't know what ways I can improve if I can't tell wtf my opponent is doing with every attack feeling like they come out on frame 1, ending at frame 7 and with no endlag, they're able to attack again instantly, doing a 0-death on me since the very moment I get hit, I'm dead and can't D-I out of the combo with how fast every attack is. The worst part of this is the fact every quick play match is like this. You won't find anyone around your skill level if you haven't mastered the game, and you never will be able to master the game without fighting real players except the fact you simply won't even get the chance to play the game when you fight real players.-Fine, let's say I have a skill issue with this game. It's all on me or anyone struggling to get good, my hands are slow and my eyes can't keep up. I have a very slim chance of finding players within my skill level where I can learn improve. Let's just play casually. Some for-fun matches for giggles. Arcade mode? Repetitive and boring. Timed? Boring. Sports? It's alright, after a while it gets repetitive. The new items? Very good addition and I actually had some fun with this game for once, which is ironic considering I'm not one for items in Smash or other games, usually. However, that's just one way to play this game with the already very few and bland ways to play offline. Items may be fun but it's fun for only so long. That leaves...nothing else. There's no content. Compare it to literally any Smash game. 64's adventure while a bit repetitive has some switch ups that can refresh every playthrough such as race to the finish and break the targets. Same for Melee with the revamped adventure, allstar mode, event match, and the MANY different and silly multiplayer modes like Stamina, Giant/Mini Melee, One-Button Melee, and so on. Brawl has Subspace, event match and a lot of other content, Smash 4 has a lot of content, and Ultimate too. The Smash games that offers online has varied players of any skill online and all games aren't stupidly fast. Rivals of aether has good gameplay, fun side modes, and a online where you can find players with your skill level with a lot of room for your own improvement, and isn't stupidly fast. Rushdown Revolt has different ways to play and has a lot of customization options, and even as fast as Rushdown is, it's still pretty methodical, unlike this game. Most importantly, Slap City. Slap is basically perfect in every way. Great balance between speed and methodicalness, fun for casual play and has a LOT of depth for competitive play as well that isn't oppressive like Nick, as really fun offline modes and even different online modes, has a lot of charm everywhere from the music to artstyle to characters to story to basically everything, and even has a lot of well done easter eggs and references to those who are fans of Ludosity's games- I can't even say this game remotely tries to make any kind of reference or at least tiny nods to the original counterparts. Slap City is just straight up better in EVERY way compared to Nick All Stars and I highly recommend buying that game if you haven't yet, whether if you Nick All Stars or not.I love Ludosity, and knowing Ludo with their consistency in making quality games that you should totally check out, I'm willing to bet this messy game is not entirely their fault. Regardless of whose fault it is, this game is a huge disappointment with it's pacing, mechanics, and questionable roster decisions and it is clearly trying to target the competitive audience whom are disappointed with the way that Nintendoesn't listen to their competitive fans. It's fine trying to please these fans at all and in fact, I encourage it. However, they're handling this aspect by just doing the polar opposite of what Ninten is; oppressing casual players is and primarily listening to competitive ones. It's all about balance, make a game that appeals to everyone so everyone can enjoy it. Make a game where people can play for fun and laughs while people can also play to be the best.That said...please get Slap City.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 6/6/2022: Voices were added.  This was never a concern of mine.  The netcode is still awful.Majority of matches are unplayable dumpster fires that are more unstable than average ping would suggest.  Part of the problem is the ridiculously fast start up and lack of end frames on attacks.  So much stuff is practically un-reactable in real time, online makes it a completely unpredictable mess.  I've had matches full of DBZ style teleports because the entirety of air dashes are covered in a rollback.  I've been put into true block strings that only exist online, because it will rollback between a grounded and aerial forward attack.  I've went from getting a grab to already dead and respawning so many times already.  Majority of stages have performance issues that cause the game to run at a stuttering frame rate or slow motion.  Maybe all of this will get better over time as kids stop playing on wifi and people learn that bad frame rate equals bad online.  But until then, Im expecting updates for a smoother experience.Local plays fine, the game is "fun jank", but lets not kid ourselves.  You buy this for the online, to support rollback releases. _childDocuments_.review: This game has many flaws. From the seemingly poor hitreg (at least from my view) to the massive power of some characters, there is something wrong about this game.The list of characters is small, but alright. I wish there would have been more to begin with, but what you get is what you get. The issues that I have with them is more on the lack of diversity of playstyles and furthermore the lack of needing to have any real strategy or depth to combat. Players can choose to do things that are harder to use in a game, or they can use April and just use strong dash into strong neutral. The simple and cheesy gameplay really diminishes any true value from a competitive standpoint and just makes playing this game boring for the most part.I wish there was more balance in how a characters kit could be used, but alas it seems that most of the changes are tweaks over real change. On top of this the existence of combos that nearly or totally remove the abilities of the enemy are rampant and easy to execute. If someone is given the choice to use this strat vs something that is harder to do (and with less value guaranteed out of it) why would they choose the less effective one? It is not a surprise that a majority of the playerbase has left. I wish this game the best, but I don't see it getting bigger than it was on release.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game day 1 because it got MASSIVE hype from Smash players, and understandably so because who wouldn't be hyped for a Nickelodeon platform fighter? Although I ended up only playing this game for an hour and a half just testing characters' movesets in training mode, there were several things that turned me off about the game. The most obvious thing is the lack of voice acting, which is forgivable because of the relatively small budget but still makes it feel a bit lifeless. There are some very weird design choices too that make the gameplay feel unintuitive: you have to hold down on a platform and press the jump button to drop through it, unlike Smash where you can just hold down on a platform to drop through. Dash dancing is almost nonexistant and it seems like you need to press the dash button in order to make your character go anywhere. On top of that, the game feels VERY mashy and seems to reward landing stray hits much too hard, with most characters being able to take your stock with a single combo, or even just kill you at very low percents with a single strong attack.I refunded the game. It's just not for me at the moment and I'll think about purchasing it again once the hype dies down.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRNot for $50, only maybe at a deep discount especially since there's a sequel/revision already on the way. My main issue with this game is mostly the lack of varied content and "good" unlockables/replay value imo. The only thing to do really is stock or timed battles. Unlike Slap City there are no unique platforming stages or challenges for the single player mode akin to another platform fighter's "classic mode". So you are just going to be fighting CPUs in stock matches, something you can just do in the battle mode. Also, items don't appear in arcade nor have and option to appear either (at least from my experience), that's only for the battle mode which makes arcade even less appealing to go through. The only reason to play arcade is to see if you can finish a run with however many stocks you allow yourself, there's not even a unique boss/fight at the end just another usual stock battle. There is a ball mini game similar to the one in Slap City but it feels more tacked on here since there really isn't a stage made specifically for it while Slap City had a few (IIRC), plus it's not that fun to keep coming back to imo (more of a novelty rather than a highlight mode).I don't really have much to say about the game mechanics and other things that many others haven't already stated like the janky character animations, questionable movesets, or the models of some of the characters looking off. I will say though, I really liked the idea of like locking your character in one direction, sad to see it won't be making it's way into the sequel. Also, why is there no camera mode in this game, Slap City also didn't have one but I also find it disappointing that there isn't one there either. I heard it' cause some of the models are dependent on the camera but it would be nice to be able to freely look at the stages without being in a fight and take screenshots of what's going on in a match. Another thing, I really disliked how the the DLC was handled imo I think they should have all been put in as free DLC since the base game is already $50, asking an additional $12-15 for only 3 characters and 3 stages didn't sit right with me. I know I sound entitled and I probably am but I was already disappointed with the initial roster, (and game as a whole). Since there weren't alot of 2000's era characters from shows I enjoyed that I also wanted to play as, seeing Jenny as DLC rather than being in the base roster and seeing Hugh before Jimmy had me feeling some type of way. From a business perspective (having a popular fan favorite character sell the DLC) I get it but I still didn't like it.Kind of too late to suggest things that'd make this game better (imo) since a sequel is coming but I'll list some anyways with some closing thoughts. Focusing less on the competitive aspects I think would help the game appeal to more people, By that I mean more wacky and dynamic stages, more single player content that isn't just fighting someone and if it is a fight make it not boring, add some gimmicks/modifiers to it. Instead of a 1v1 each time make it 1v2 or a team battle (2v2), an item only battle or stamina or life bar fight, something to keep it dynamic. For non fights, have something similar to a break the targets or race to the finish type stage or just have a traditional platforming stage (for the PLATFORMING fighting game crazy right). For multiplayer, having other modes other than versus and the ball minigame, maybe give the ability to go through the arcade mode with another person for a coop mode, if there were platforming stages a racing mode could work or create a new mode inspired from the many Nick live action game shows. For additional unlockables, instead of just giving out renders and songs (that you can already hear on the stages) give out unique artwork rather than renders of the characters standing in a colored void. If it has to be renders at least give it some staging, include other characters (and make it look like they are interacting with each other), recreate a scene from the show, anything more than just basic renders. Something akin to trophies or stickers so that we can get bios/additional info for the characters or other things related to the shows the characters come from. Unlocking alternate songs would be cool too. I feel like since they seemingly wanted to garner a competitive scene that a lot of single player and modes outside of just fighting someone 1 on 1 aspects got neglected. It seems like the same is happening with the sequel but not as bad since there seems an actual single player mode this time but that remains to be seen at the time of writing this. _childDocuments_.review: It takes an assortment of the positive features that Melee, Ultimate, and Brawlhalla all had, and did well, and combines it into a well oiled package that has a lot of promise. It's already very competitive, although now that it's in the hands of some very good players... Day 1 balance is very obviously a problem, but a solvable problem.The speed of the game, the ease of understanding the mechanics, yet the skill it takes to master these mechanics and how satisfying it feels to play is what sets the game apart for sure.There are some issues with the matchmaking system and online play unrelated to the (very welcomed) rollback netcode. Competitive lobbies can be griefed, there isn't enough checks for connection quality on your opponent which can result in matches played at 1/4 speed from start to finish, and there have been a few disconnects that I can only imagine are people dodging lobbies or rage quitting, and I don't understand how this is affecting my player ranking.There are a few QoL changes I think should be added as well, including a proper control binding screen and player profiles to save your binding layout. As it is right now, it remembers your binding layout based on the controller slot allocated, even if you back out of the local lobby and come back later. As long as controllers haven't been swapped, or the game reset, it remembers. This doesn't work well in a party scenario; as people are learning the game and drinking or having a good time, sometimes they don't perfectly remember how they had it set up and it sucks to reset matches for that.But I get that this is sort of designed with a tournament setup in mind, and not friends having fun on the couch drinking. I don't necessarily agree with that focus, but I get that it's the target demographic.Anyway, it's good and I believe will only get better. It absolutely shouldn't be passed up if you're wanting a platform fighter experience that feels like an evolution, and not a gimmick. It feels most like Brawlhalla meets Melee, and that's something I have been wanting for a while.
