_childDocuments_.review: This is more a First Impressions thus far, mainly because I do feel like I should warn peeps about some very clear issues present in the game. When I played a bout of Arcade offline, it felt smooth, fast and fun. The Arcade mode is beyond bare bones however, there's a set of fights to play in a row, some giving you the option to swap who you fight next. For what they included I would have rather them not add anything at all - these large text boxes where the characters just say a wack line and move on is very out of place. There's also no boss character to speak of like Master/Crazy Hand in Smash.  There are no endings, no story, etc - it's literally just the win screen at the end.Moving up to the visuals, I think the game looks great overall, but guys, please, stop over using Chromatic Aberration where it's not needed or atleast give the option to turn that off. It makes the game look blurry and weird even on a 1440p display, maxed out. Animations could use a bit of work, Toph in particular, looks SUPER stiff, their jump animations almost makes her look like she's T-Posing, it looks weird. I don't mind characters having really quick animations, and most of them DO look good. Toph was the outlier for me. This game also seems to lack 'impact'. The sound of strong attacks kinda carry the game in terms of that satisfying hit, but lacking any freeze frames makes the game feel a bit floaty, almost as if everyone in this game has Steve's neutral attack from SSBU.Presentation wise, the game needs work. The game's menu brought back very vivid memories of PlayStation All Stars' Menus. It looks very basic, very vanilla, which wouldn't be a bad thing, but you can almost tell the UI was mostly designed for a smaller system (namely the Switch) and not touched up, a bit, or added a bit of flair to it. The UI in game also needs a bit of work, the %'s at the bottom are hard to keep an eye on them with how frantic this game can get. The Results Screen and VS screen were also huge misses for me. I did not like the tiny text showing the characters' name with a blank background and their artwork. Why not make a 2D Artwork of their name matching their show's logos or something? The Results screen just has a LOT of empty space I felt, I know it looks this way because it may have 4 players, but most of the games online are 1v1 endeavours. Also, boy do I think it sucks when characters only have 1 Color Scheme to them. Colors palettes are non existant in this game. If there's 2 April O'Neals in the match, both of them will wear the same yellow jumpsuit with the same hair color, I THINK one of them gets a slightly darker hue, but I'm not even sure about that one. This one I feel may have been an issue with licensing but I do think this is something that SHOULD be addressed, because just keeping an eye out on the barely visible text that can sometimes blend into the background to even know who you are if it happens to be a mirror is annoying.Stages I feel really need an Omega/FD variant to have a much wider pool of areas to fight in that aren't incredibly annoying. Some of the stages right now feel a bit buggy or annoying to play in, particularly the Powered Toast Man one, as awesome as it looks, if you, at any point get hit into the cereal, it's a complete toss if you'll just die in there or not. One time I got tapped and just insta died, the other time I got hit by a strong down attack and just sank to the bottom, didn't die and popped back up as if nothing happened. Some stages as well seem to have very tiny death zones, Catdog's stage for example, if you even as much as come into contact with the edge BRIEFLY, you kinda just blow up. Speaking of - Not a big deal, but it would have been cool to have similar animations for sending opponents sky high, like how Smash has the into the distance or camera hit KO's. I also feel like this game would REALLY benefit from having a visual mechanic that's similar to SSBU's Critical Hit screen, cause sometimes I just land a Strong Attack from mid screen, and without any indication, it just kills, either the impact is not there or there should be a bit clearer method to tell how far away people are going to fly off.As much as I dislike them too, I do think this game should have had a fully casual mode with items being usable, I actually got a bit confused in Lincoln's stage because you had moving items in the stage that almost looked like you could pick em up.I can't comment a whole lot on the online yet - but the 4 or so matches I did manage to play all felt "jumpy", similar to SFV's. I am running on a wired connection and play other competitive games and FFXIV just fine. Maybe I just had bad luck with the peeps I ran into online, but 0/4 of those games felt good to play.There's also a BIG issue with controller remapping right now too. For some strange reason, I cannot seem to map my strong attacks to my right stick, but you do get the strong hits when your character is on the ground. That was a really weird decision they kinda just went with. It would have been great to remap controllers a bit better without being forced to rely on Steam Controller settings for these.I dunno, the bit I played was enjoyable. The game has IMMENSE potential, but this feels undercooked as of launch day at least. Toph's animations look like butt, there's kind of a weird disparity between how some characters look. The Loud kids for example, look super well animated and then well, you get Toph. The presentation could definitely use a bit of work to make it look less like PSAS and more like something unique and snazzy. This game is in desperate need of alt color palettes for characters not just for gameplay visibility in potential mirrors, but also for fun! The roster to me is also a bit weird. Crazy how we have 3 Spongebob reps, 3 Avatar reps (for the love of all that is holy, please fix Toph lol) 2 Loud House reps, etc yet we have no Miko from Glitch Techs, no XJ9, no Jimmy Neutron and other very popular Nickelodeon characters. It's a good roster overall, but it's like releasing Smash Bros with Mario and Luigi, but not including Link or Captain Falcon. (PS - I am fully aware Glitch Techs is hella niche, I just want Miko in this game maaan)

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly, very disappointed with this. Was hyped ever since the reveal and was expecting a competitively viable new smash competitor. Unfortunately, that's really ALL I got, and only an average one at best and a very lackluster one at most. Buffering system, even something minor, seems non-existent. Takes a while to get used to controls (haven't yet). Arcade mode is very half-baked and features random cpu fights with cookie-cutter dialogue. Control rebinds are very lackluster. From what I've seen in other reviews, you can't even rebind arrow keys to WASD which is pretty bad. Online isn't as impressive as it was hyped to be and isn't nearly as stable as expected. Stages frequently lag and drop framerate significantly, such as the FD clone stage from Korra (even though my PC is actually fairly high-end and should be able to handle the game very easily). It seems the game was focused on making a very fast-paced, melee like experience. Unfortunately what happened is that every character feels like they have the same combo routes (up air strings, up air to down air to tech chase, forward air down air off ledge, etc.). Characters feel like they have little diversity between them and ultimately I couldn't really settle on a main since they feel so similar. The game also as next to no causal content. No items or different modes other than sports and arcade which feel like a play it once and forget about it type of deal. Game doesn't have anything going for it to keep a casual audience in mind and will likely remain pretty niche if none of the issues get fixed. There's simply a hard lack of content for the game and does not live up to it's 50 dollar price tag at all. This is not a AAA quality game, and that's ok, but it is priced as if it were a AAA quality game, which feels unfair. I KNOW this was a super low budget game and I KNOW the devs worked their butts off to deliver the best product they could, but the reality is that it simply feels unfinished and unpolished. Lack of options, surprisingly mediocre online, half-baked arcade, you name it. Not worth your 40, let alone 50 dollars after the sale. Maybe wait a month or two to see how things evolve, but for now, I'd reconsider if you are going to buy. I'm genuinely sad; I was expecting this to finally be the game I could get into. I REALLY wanted to hunker down and really learn this game. I REALLY wanted to be hyped, but it just didn't deliver. Props to the devs for trying, but ultimately the game was low budget and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. The most important part of any platform fighter, the gameplay itself, is just so polished, fast, and slick. It is very easy to start working on beginner combos but damn, can you pull some wild ♥♥♥♥ in this game. Each character feels incredibly unique from one another and all have their own mechanics as well.That being said, it has a lot of improvements to make, but considering that Ludosity devs have said that some content simply wasn't able to be finished before launch, I gotta assume Nick themselves were probably pressuring the devs to get the game out. With just a little bit more time and polish, this could legit become one of the more popular fighting games out there. It's funny to say "lol spongebob vs powdered toastman at evo", but I can see that becoming a reality if the devs continue to work on this game.Here are the main improvements I'd want to see going forward. I definitely think this game needs better controller mapping. Seriously, I should be mapping moves to buttons, not buttons to moves, if that makes sense. Only being able to have one button perform one action feels really weird, especially since literally every other platform fighter ever seems to use this system, even Ludosity's own Slap City. In a platform fighter, options are key to making all players happy, and right now, this is not the case. I also think this game is in DIRE need of alt colors. God forbid two people main the same character, watching that match, and especially trying to play it, would be an utter ♥♥♥♥ show. Some of the game's in-game animations also could use some touching up, specifically Toph looks like she suffers from arthritis. Finally, and this may just be a personal complaint, the victory screen is so bland. I don't expect smash levels of details, but something like the characters name or something zooming on screen or whatever could be sick. I feel as if most would suggest voice acting, but I can see why that may be incredibly difficult to implement. I doubt many of the original voice actors would reprise their roles, in which case, people would just be angry.I know it may sound like I think negatively of this game, but I really do enjoy it. As I already said, the gameplay is just so fun. I'm a big fan of platform fighters and this game is just at the cusp of greatness. Before the devs focus on adding more characters or stages, I really want to see them polish up the game just a bit more, because seriously, this game has the potential to truly be something amazing. Oh, and shout out to my boy Thaddeus Crews.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun alternative to Smash if you don't have a switch but playing it still makes you wish you were actually playing smash. The game mechanics are surprisingly smooth and fluid, but the game modes get stale rather quickly, and there isn't much variety. The AI gets really easy to beat after a hour of practice, and you can pretty much beat them with your eyes closed . I literally can't find anybody to play with online, for the community is pretty much nonexistent. The most fun I've been getting out of this game is through the experimentation with different characters, by seeing what kind of crazy combos I can rack up in arcade mode. The game is aesthetically pleasing, but with all the signature and memorable characters present in the roster,  they seem lifeless and hardly have anything to say. With a game as wacky as this one, you would expect to hear some snarky dialogue from the characters, but there's absolutely none of that. Overall, this is a fun casual game to kill time when you're chilling or talking to friends, but the asking price of 50 dollars is outright laughable. Buy it on sale where it's usually 10 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hyped for Nickelodeon All Star Brawl and I have to say it did not disappoint at all. I am a huge smash fan and when I heard that Ludiosty was making a Nick themed fighting game I was so happy because I loved their previous fighting game, Slap City and I am just a huge Nickelodeon fan.And I do just want to preface this review saying that this isn’t going to be an insanely in-depth review. I’m not a fighting game pro that can discuss invincibility frames and all sorts of stuff, I just played the game a ton and enjoyed it a bunch and wanted to talk about it.So first of all I have to say that the game looks and feels really good. All the characters in the character roster feel fun to play and unique from each other, though I do wish there where a couple more fighters but hopefully that will come with post launch updates or dlc.There's a ton of fighters that I personally was excited for like the avatar characters like Toph which is my main, Spongebob, Patrick, and Sandy from Spongebob, and also random characters like Reptar, Danny Phantom, Invader Zim, and more. And if you’ve played Smash bros or especially Slap City you will feel right at home in this game. There are a couple of differences from Smash like you cant roll, grabs are way shorter, and several other differences but overall it feels very similar. I even use my gamecube controller to pretend like I am playing smash.Where games like Smash to me tend to feel smooth, I would say Nick All Star Brawl feels a little Janky. And that sounds like a bad thing but it isn’t entirely negative. Like there is a slight lack of polish in things like the u.i, like you can't make different player profiles, controller mapping gets reset sometimes, the online netcode can be a bit wonky at times, there’s no voice acting, there aren’t different skins for each character even when there are duplicate players playing the same character and more.The gameplay itself tends to feel a tiny bit janky as well in terms of sometimes moves will just look or feel like they come out of nowhere, the way things combo into each other can be a little disjointed at times, but sometimes this can lead to hilarious moments. And keep in mind I am not a pro fighting game player and this is totally just a slight feeling I get from the game.When your fighting though the game feels fair, there tends to be a lot of back and forth and like I mentioned earlier each characters moves are super unique and fun to play. Invader Zim summons enemies to fight for him, Sandy grapples enemies and pulls them to her, Toph has a ton of earth bending abilities like summoning platforms in mid air, Reptar has a down smash where he breaths fire on the ground and if he hits the opponents he deals 30% damage which is absolutely insane!It feels like all the characters are OP and because of that it feels balanced but in a really good way. You never want characters to feel like they can't do much but almost every character in the game feels like they can be extremely powerful in the right hands. The maps in the game look breathtaking honestly and I love the music on a lot of them especially the jellyfish fields map, that song slaps so hard.The game has been getting constant updates that include balance changes, bug fixes, and new mechanics and changes to the gameplay which is really good because I will say the game launched in a slightly underdeveloped state but it seems to already have made a lot of progress.I do think the $50 price tag is a bit steep for amount of content in the game but overall I think it’s worth it. To me being able to beat my friends up using Tophs awesome earthbending or just messing around with all these nick characters that made up my childhood makes me so happy and the gameplay is competent and solid enough where I dont really have any complaints.I would love to see the game get updated with more fighters like Jimmy Nuetron, Timmy from Fairly Oddparents, Zuko and more.So if you are a huge Nick Fan that enjoys the gameplay of Smash Bros I think you can get a lot of fun out of this game especially if you have some friends to play with in real life. It’s got online but it’s always better playing with friends irl in my opinion especially for this type of game.And if you liked this review then follow my  for more stuff like this!

_childDocuments_.review: is cheap and generic in a way that was forgivable and even charming in Slap City, Ludosity's previous game and this title's most direct influence. Nobody expected much from the little developer who saw the platform fighter genre, dominated as it is by the Smash franchise with niches filled in by Rivals of Aether () and Brawlhalla (), and decided to make their own version (), seemingly half-jokingly the whole time. The design of Slap City's quirky and high skill-ceiling mechanics provided enough "crunch" to distract players from the game's stiff animations, unpolished visual effects, and tiny cast of programmer-art nobodies. While these defects kept Slap City from reaching popularity even within the small world of platform fighter enthusiasts, it still had a place within the pantheon as a strange but endearing not-quite-a-novelty game.But when that ittle developer put on their big boy pants, got a license from Nickelodeon, and decided to charge $50 for their $20 quirky/janky fighting game with a new coat of paint, there is an implication that the aforementioned coat of paint provides a value of around $30. Yet it's impossible to avoid noticing the cut corners and lack of content that reveal the absurdity of this game's price. I would've been more forgiving had this been a $20 download-only title, or a free-to-play game with individually purchased characters ala Brawlhalla. But since they are charging AAA prices, I'll review them to AAA standards.Mediocre models and limited animation make this title feel like an early PS2 game. Characters have no alternate skins or even palette swaps to support readability in ditto matches. UI is generic and utterly without "Nick"-style flair and aesthetic. In fact, the only UI elements that feel "Nick" at all are the giant character art cutouts on the various menu screens. The rest of the UI looks like a rushed affair with a lack of polish approaching that of a game jam weekend project.Characters don't have individual sound effects or voices. Just thump/slap/whack effects for the various types of moves that are reused throughout the roster. The only voice you'll hear throughout your fights will be the announcer half-heartedly reading through some generic reaction clips: "Wow!", "That's gotta hurt!", et cetera.Zero music tracks from the source material. Stages have one song per stage, questionably "inspired" by the TV show it's from, but the best of these are unmemorable and little more than background noise (). The worst are irritating enough to distract from the gameplay ().Barely customizable, doesn't work natively with gamecube controllers, no saving settings per-profile (no profiles at all, in fact). No tap jump option for those who aren't used to button jumping and have decades of muscle memory of pushing up to jump.This is Slap City with 90's nick themed character skins. If you liked playing Slap City you'll like this. If Slap City felt disjointed and janky then you're going to feel that way about All-Star Brawl. Not terrible, but not as good as any other platform fighter (except Brawlhalla).All-Star Brawl is a barebones affair from start to finish and does not justify its asking price. While the gameplay is serviceable and an interesting departure from the tried-and-true formula of Smash, this is a thin, hollow-feeling experience that consistently leaves the player disappointed. I won't be returning to this game.

My brother and I have been playing Smash since it came out on the N64, and this game brings that same kind of nostalgic joy. The characters are fun and wacky. The controls are intuitive and work well. The stages have some really interesting 3d effects. It is true that there is no voice acting yet (though it is planned), and the roster is limited. In spite of these flaws though, I'm having a lot of fun. If you grew up in the 90s, it's a great game that will cater to your nostalgia with classic Nicktoons

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl - a platform fighter with melee-inspired movement options, rollback netcode, and the star power of Nickelodeon characters; what could go wrong? A lot. A lot could go wrong.Nick Brawl had a huge opening debut, with every Twitch streamer on earth enamored with the fact that Spongebob, could in fact, hit that yoinky sploinky. There was an insane amount of hype during the first week - movement in the game felt smooth, and matches were quickly found, with the game peaking at 9,120 players according to SteamDB. After the first wave of hype dissipated into a ripple, the cracks in the game became more apparent. Voicelines were oddly missing from a game which derived a huge amount of its appeal (and price tag) from its star power, and character animations felt lifelessly stilted - especially when compared to Ludosity's previous platform fighting game, Slap City. Alternate skins, too, were bizarrely missing. As time went on, the player count continuously dropped, and the most glaring issue of the game became present: there was no crossplay. The lack of crossplay strongly accentuated the dropping playercount, with players (including myself) struggling to find matches in their region after queuing for 10+ minutes. It was reported by the game's art director, Diego Hernández, during a Hungrybox stream that crossplay was planned to be added by Q1 2022. It is May of 2022, and crossplay is still not here. There has been the addition of alternate skins (Dec 2021, 2 months after release), which ranged in quality from actually differentiating two people playing the same character to normal Korra vs "sparkling water" Korra. Garfield got added, which is neat, and Shredder - who is big as hell. Jenny from My Life As a Teenage Robot got announced and added on the 13th of May (as paid DLC), along with the announcement of Hugh Neutron (???) and Rocco from Rocco's Modern Life. The game's current price tag and the price I bought it at on release (forty buckaroos) is does not feel justified in the game's current state. Currently, the game feels unfinished, especially when compared with beautiful, in-depth platform fighters on the market like Rival of Aether or even the necromanced corpse of Icons: Combat Arena, Rushdown Revolt (which is free!). The addition of "haha meme" characters like Hugh Neutron over Jimmy Neutron makes me raise an eyebrow as to the current direction of the game as a whole. The game's base price should absolutely get dropped down to something like twenty dollars instead of the current strategy of it being 60% off half of the time like furniture you find on Wish. As I have seen other reviews say similarly: this is a passable, okay-ish twenty dollar game, but a terrible fifty dollar game. I genuinely hope that adding crossplay can revive this game, along with the addition of voice acting, but I cannot recommend this game in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a No recommendation FOR NOW.I was excited at the prospect of this game, even though platform fighters are not my forté.  The previews all indicated the devs know what they are doing with game mechanics and the game doesn't disappoint in that regard.  So at it's core, the gameplay is pretty solid.  It's the rest of the package that seems unpolished overall.  The presentation is pretty basic and there is not much to say about the Singleplayer at all other than a straightforward arcade mode of opponents.  Like everyone and their grandma has stated, the sound design is the biggest flaw with lack of voices and even the music that is present is generic too.  (I understand budget is the culprit, but this is an objective judgment).  They try to infuse a bit of personality with some pre-game comment boxes during arcade mode, but those are all very generic as well.  The online is decent, so if you are strictly an online warrior that loves platform fighters, then this is a pretty good recommendation, but the previous flaws I mentioned has me concerned about the longevity and size of the community in the long run.  The devs seem quite receptive and passionate about their work though, so I have little doubt that things will improve in the future, but for NOW I can't give a wholehearted thumbs up recommendation.  The game has lots of heart to it, but it will need some more body and soul to have a lasting impact.

_childDocuments_.review: Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl isn't Smash Bros. but I think that's perfectly fine.Whenever I hear things from people who say the game is dead, it's mostly because they've had set the standard to the like of Smash Bros. Personally, I really enjoyed what I played.We got decent representation of Nickelodeon media from the 90's, the 2000's and the 2010's. Gameplay is smooth and reliable control wise for both casual play and competitive play. Even the extra modes, while limited, aren't bad in execution.The main problem facing the game right now is just a lack of content, and I'm not just talking characters. Arcade can be breezed through in a few hours and there's not a lot to do outside of fighting CPUs and players online. Even if we just got something like some info about a character after beating Arcade with them or some extra costumes, it'd go a long way.Costumes are also lacking in the game, as we originally had nothing during launch. The ones we got are nice, but the lack of voices and costumes do make the fights dull and difficult to focus on, especially if it's a 4 way fight with everyone playing as one character.But I know it's Nickelodeon itself that's holding back what can be done for content in this game, as the devs have said before on the official discord, so I don't fault them.All in all, I'd reccomend getting the game, but if it's on sale only. As while this game is decent in it's own right when not comparing it to Smash Bros, it's still pretty barebones.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've played a bit of the game, making my way through Arcade mode multiple times to get a grasp of how some fighters work before attempting the online. I'm no competitive Smash player, but I find this game immensely fun to play.Here are some positives:- If you're playing on controller, the right stick preforms some of the directional button-assigned attacks. I found this immensely easier than working with three at once. Now I'm able to focus on dealing damage with the buttons, then working on KO'ing the opponent with the stick.- Gameplay is kept simple yet fun, feeling fast-paced and less mechanic-heavy compared to Smash Bros. Makes it easier for someone who hasn't tried this kind of game to get into it since there isn't a lot to take in.- Mechanics are more versatile, such as allowing grabs in mid-air.Of course there are some cons:- The right stick changes what moves it does based on whether you're grounded or not. Feels a little unintuitive to have the stick suddenly switch from doing strong attacks to basic attacks when you're airborne. Getting to choose what that stick does, no matter your current state, would be a nice change so it's more dependable. Or even keeping that and allow us to change the states separately, so now we could make the stick do special moves if airborne.- Limited control customization. Attacks can be changed via the character selection screen, but... why there? There  an options menu where most would expect them to go. Even then, things like movement keys are unable to be changed at all without file editing. A major downside for keyboard+mouse users.- Slightly buggy AI. AI would sometimes continuously fail to go through a platform, resulting in a loop until you move closer to them. Other times, they'd just stop entirely until they are hit. - Character animations vary in quality between them, making the fighters not really feel like they mesh well with each other. Some are great, while others are quite stiff.Most of my complaints are minor though, and can be addressed in a future patch. Figured I wouldn't address move issues since I'm highly unskilled to do so, and games like this aren't my usual cup of tea, so I'll leave that to those who know what they're talking about. Otherwise, I'm happy with how this game released overall, and it makes me want to work to get better at it due to how addictively fun its game play can be. I'm looking forward to what the developers do with it next.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Platform fighters I think you have to give this game a try. While when the game launched there was a ton of missing features like casual content, voices, crossplay, skins, and competitive stages. The developers of this game have advertised that they listen to their community on what they want content wise and in terms of balance changes. They have delivered on nearly every requested feature that the community has asked for since launch. as of 8/23/2022 Nickelodeon All Stars Brawl has gained, free and paid new characters such as Garfield, Shredder, Jenny, and Hugh Neutron with Rocko coming this fall. Each of these characters have come with a custom stage and almost all of them have come with one that can be used in competitive play! They developers have added secondary colors/skins for every single fighter that add hats, change character colors, add funny episode references etc.They have also added Items and Voice acting from many of the original shows cast members! My fav item is the Anchor but it is cool that all the items are stuff from each of the shows featured in the game. The game features really good Rollback netcode that makes the game really enjoyable online compared to other similar platform fighters, Paired with this really good netcode is the simple but very effective Lobby system. you can have multiple rooms within a single lobby so multiple games with different rules and such can be happening all at once! Each game can even be watched by a spectator by simply pressing spectate when the match is starting. Its really great for online tournaments if you want to stream smaller events since you can just tap spectate on a desired set currently taking place! You can even do ranked lobbies if you want to make sure those entering your lobby know that this isnt a time to mess around. This makes it so that only stages in the current ranked quickplay rotation can be selected and wins and losses effect your elo. The movement in nick since the beginning has always been my draw to this game. The wave dashing and air dashing are super smooth and more satisfying than any other platform fighter ive tried. Doing this inputs are also pretty simple and not hard since the game has macros to detect if you intended to do a wave dash! No accidental poor angled wave dashes or accidental air dashes. The game like I said is more grounded so if you don't prefer floatier gameplay you'll really appreciate the feel of nick. Dash dancing is another added feature that didnt originally exist but make sthe game feel all that more fun to move around in and when paired with strafing it makes it really simple to properly space moves. I really like this game and seriously reccomend it to anyone open to trying new platform fighters.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting conceptually but in practicality it's without cohesion. The Nickelodeon characters don't mesh well and they look very awkward and flat out strange fighting each other. The overall visual design of the game feels uninspired. It's Nickelodeon and mostly Nickelodeon of the 90's. I think it should have drawn more from the aesthetics of that. And the music is also pretty repetitive and generic sounding. The fighting is okay since it's a copy of all the most basic mechanics of Super Smash Brothers, with some depth in its own right. But the game feels empty. No voice overs, no items to add variety to a match, and not many options with what you can change in a given fight make All-Star Brawl feel very disappointing.I wish I could recommend it just for how outrageous a Nickelodeon smash brothers game sounds but absurdity alone is not enough to recommend a game. Hopefully they keep tweaking it and it gets better, but I feel like nothing will fix the off-putting juxtapositioning of these characters fighting.

This studio has brought in extra characters, added voice lines, made continuous changes and updates that the players have asked for, so I think it can still do well. Sure, it may seem like a lot paying 50 bucks for a game, so wait for a sale, or try finding a copy of this game elsewhere for a discount. Still definitely worth playing. I just got it, and wanted to see how it compared, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. _childDocuments_.review: I'll say plainly in first starting off that I've no idea as to why the hype for this title is so grandiose and reaching, the core of the material is fun in a nostalgic manner as well that it functions as a well-to-do fighting platformer but the analogue to Super Smash Bros. and Melee specific is pretty out there. Departing from that, the biggest issue is the lack of supplement available in the base game (DLC planned for future release) with the only functions being a penny dreadful arcade whose success rewards you in concept art and music; a bout with an egregious lack of customization options, and internet match-ups which are laggy but at the very least promising. Each section feels that it still resides in a pre-release Early Access phase considering how little is available to the player on install, hopefully we'll get updates down the line both in regards to content and quality of life but at standing the game is nowhere near worth its MSRP.One of the weirdest incorporations is the addition of wavedashing as one of the base mechanics but the exclusion of an actual dodge as the player's block is firmly grounded and unbudging. Another odd aspect is the rock-paper-scissors system for special attacks where specials beat out others just depending on the directional input, up beats down specials, down beats mids, and mids beat up which in turn reminds me strikingly of the MesuKing minigame from Yakuza which itself was an odd and off-putting inclusion. The movements, animations, and art styles for all the characters is a bit off-putting as well, it's understandable that combining media with different art styles would necessitate a common ground that might make some characters look off as going from a 2D design to 3D model is never easy but the approach makes some characters look bad, really, really bad. Korra, Aang, and Toph are all pretty out there which is odd considering that PlatinumGames got the design of Korra very much in the vein of the source material.The music is familiar but not exacting, everything was made with the character's source cartoons in mind but rather than being remixes or re-imaginings made to fit the soundscape of a fighting game, they're completely new compositions that don't really hold anybody's attention and instead manage to fill the background with a melodic noise rather than something triumphant or inspiring. In that same Niche is the lack of voice acting or really anything that makes the characters feel alive or personable, if it wasn't for the SFX you would believe the sound was turned off altogether.The best stage in my opinion is the Irken Armada Invasion as it's a reskinned copy of Smash's Final Destination, with some Venom in the background. I think what makes these issues more poignant is the developer calling out Nintendo for being too elitist to listen to fans.The game would be immensely worth it if the price point was near $15, but at this stage just feels as an expensive fan project.

_childDocuments_.review: While not exactly like Super Smash Bros., Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl is still a fun, pick-up-and-play fighting game that's sure to bring lots of joy to young players and adults who grew up watching Nickelodeon's amazing lexicon of shows for the past three decades. It may not have items or trophies and there isn't many game modes and nothing to unlock, but overall, this is a solid foundation to build a new series and i'm sure there will be plenty of improvements to come whether in updates or a sequel. This game was a passion project for the team at Ludocity and what they packed into all the stages and characters really show how much they love these series and characters just as much as anyone does. With the promise of updates, improvements, new characters and a strong competitive community that's set to build up, this could be the best alternative to Smash Bros for those looking for a fun platform fighting game that's sure to bring back lots of nostalgic memories! The soundtrack is also surprisingly pretty good too.

_childDocuments_.review: [Day 4 Review] Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl is truly a fighter for Smash and Non-smash fans alike to give a try.Wave-dashing is made easy and only requires to push the two buttons at the same time, not tricky timings or anything that is proportional to the weight of a character. There are plenty of new mechanics that the fighting game community are trying to discover and master. The rollback net-code is its main selling point, however the online as of right now is a little bit clunky.Facing opponents online whether it be in competitive or quick-play is jittery and the movement can be hard to read many of the times. This sort of thing is doable for many beginner players, but when your trying to hit at least 500 rating in competitive mode it becomes a mess because the movement of the game is so fast that many of the times the connection itself cannot really handle it. If you want to get around this I recommend just making a lobby with your friends that you know have solid connections and the game is quite enjoyable.20 playable fighters for a fighting game at base really is not terrible, if anything its okay since in most fighting games you only really see the top tier fighters in competitive modes (Smash Melee as an example). Sure the lack of sound and voice acting is a little disappointing but they will add it in the future, the developers are very open about there plans for the future apart from releasing information on new characters.This game has a ton of potential and I know the developers are well aware of this and will continue to surpass our expectations. Keep at it and continue to keep the game refreshing and hyped as much as possible!

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who loved Slap City, as I would consider it my favorite platform fighter and really wanted this game to replicate its smoothness and ease to pick up and play, I would have to give this game a hard pass. Ground movement in this game feels extremely stiff. Unlike other platform fighters, there's no initial dash state. Instead, you're forced into a walk animation until you pick up speed enough to transition into a run. It's awkward and makes approaching on the ground more difficult than it needs to be. You have a wavedash, but your angles are limited compared to other games. You either do a short or long wavedash and that seems to be it. It makes your grounded options feel very limited and hard to land anything other than a dash attack on the ground. You have an airdash that you can do from the ground immediately, but airdashes, like wavedashes in other games, are committal. You will only be able to act out at the end of your airdash, which also have limited angles. On top of movement feeling awkward, animations and hitboxes don't mesh together. The animations are way too fast and unclear. Many moves look very similar due to unclear startup and animations being reused between attacks. If your character doesn't have an up-tilt with a wide-sweeping grounded hitbox, good luck trying to land it. Many kills moves have nothing that telegraphs them at all. I.E. Lucy's coffin teleport move feels instant. There's nothing to indicate where the coffin will appear unlike Grenininja's Shadow Sneak. This is just one glaring example, but similar complaints can be applied to many other moves. The animation quality really hurts the gameplay, and even Slap City had good animations for being an indie game and fast paced. Character movesets are underwhelming. Move pools feel much smaller with the lack of side attacks despite everyone getting 3 aerial strongs and 2 dash attacks. There are going to be a lot of instances where you feel like your character needs an attack that hits more directly behind or in front of you. Many normals across the cast have the same functionality. They simply start and extend combos. Strongs all serve as your finishers. Specials either have their niche uses or serve as kill moves. Very rarely do  normals, strongs, and specials do anything outside of their archetype. It makes character archetypes feel non-existent with a few exceptions like Reptar being the game's big body heavy with smaller but deadlier combos. Otherwise, everyone just feels like a rushdown character. Lastly, I wasn't too impressed with the rollback. When smooth, it feels close to offline play. However, the game will stutter with connection dips, which just starts to feel like delay-based netcode. This may just be an issue on my end though. And of course, there's a huge lack of features. Training mode is barebones, not even having an option to set your own percentage. There's no hazards toggle that would make potentially competitive stages more playable in a competitive environment. Control settings only allow you to rebind buttons with no option to turn on tap jump or turn off grounded strongs on your right stick. Overall, I cannot recommend this game. This is a game I had hopes for but has too many issues to justify buying it. I'm probably wrong on certain details as I only played the game for 2 hours, but those 2 hours left a poor enough first impression to refund the game.tl;dr Movement feels stiff. Animations and hitboxes are mismatched, making moves very unclear when trying to land or avoid them. Too many moves do the same thing, making characters feel samey. The game lacks a lot of basic features and superficial polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I can not recommend this game to anybody looking for a rich competitive game. There are many things to love about the game but there is far more disappointing aspects. For starters the art style and music are awful. I can live with poor art style but music is such an important aspect in fighting games, they lift the excitement and energy of each match. In all star brawl the most exciting music is the menu music, the rest feels soulless.The next aspect I don’t like is the most important part, the gameplay. The gameplay in this game the combos are soooooo boring. Most combos are just Dair dair dair dair dair, or uair uair uair uair uair. There is little thought to put in when you are in advantage. Next is the character design. I had really high hopes for this game to have deep and complex characters like many other indie play-fighters have INCLUDING slap city, however each character in nick have such similar move sets. Mastery of a single character does not feel individual in their normal attacks. All of the normal attacks play the same role in each characters kit.Now it’s time for the things I really like about this game. I really think that the large stages are far better then what smash has to offer. The cast themselves are very iconic. The developers choice to support modding is so important and such a wonderful thing for the community. The inclusion of wave dashes is so vital to deep and complex movement. Finally this game is really great for casuals.I don’t hate NASB but I wouldn’t recommend it for the price it’s at and I wouldn’t ever see myself investing a significant number of hours into the game. All of my opinions come from many years of playing platform fighters and fighting games

_childDocuments_.review: A begrudging positive review. While I didn't think the graphical and audio deficiencies would keep me away beforehand, it does stick out like a Fairly Odd Parents episode with Poof and Sparky in it and makes the experience feel a bit, I guess tackier compared to other platform fighters (not including the big S)? From the few matches I did play, though, the feel, speed and movement of the game are all very unique, breaking out of a mold in its genre, like say Hey Arnold or As Told by Ginger. The focus on aerial offense is evident by the game's early use of spikes for quick stocks (something that was prevalent during my time playing, but may have been addressed), sending opponents down faster than ratings during a Loud House block, but the speed of the game rivals and may even surpass Melee, with fast and frenzied fights more exciting than those between Ariana Grande and Jennette McCurdy. While the game tries to appeal to both casual and competitive parties, a sort of CatDog mindset if you will, I feel this game is in a weird middle ground where younger audiences will undoubtedly get thrashed and not keep up with advanced tech, while more competitive people may find other aspects of the title lacking compared to distinguished platform fighters. Regardless, it's still a unique and funky mess of a game that's still very enjoyable and meme-able, the sloppy green slime pouring over its contemporaries in its genre, and if anything else, a love letter to both Nick and Smash.Side note, absolute ♥♥♥♥ at this game.

name: Shovel Knight Dig
detailed_description: When Drill Knight and his dastardly digging crew blast apart Shovel Knight’s peaceful campsite and steal his loot, he grabs his trusty Shovel Blade and starts tunneling after them! Meet new friends and foes, visit strange lands, and outfit yourself in your quest to keep the entire land from collapsing underfoot! Jump, slash, and dig your way down an ever-changing chasm of mystery in Shovel Knight Dig, an all-new Shovel Knight adventure! Features: An all-new presentation featuring a new Shovel Knight story! When Drill Knight and his dastardly digging crew blast apart Shovel Knight’s peaceful campsite and steal his loot, he grabs his trusty Shovel Blade and starts tunneling after them! The first Shovel Knight adventure in glorious high color pixel graphics and sound. Fluid animation, scaling, rotation, and parallax create the most convincing Shovel Knight world yet! Every adventure is different! Shovel Knight Dig levels have been meticulously crafted, then stitched together using proprietary generation techniques for infinite replayability. Jump, slash, and dig your way in an all-new direction – down! Rely on your trusty Shovel Drop, then dig through huge swaths of dirt with all-new Speed Shovel mechanics. Grow in power and wealth as you descend into the depths of the earth. Emerge with untold riches to outfit Shovel Knight further, unlocking permanent items and upgrades to your Shoveling equipment. New Knights, new characters, and new enemies abound, but fear not! Shovel Knight Dig features Shovel Knight’s signature storytelling, humor, and maybe even some familiar faces Another pulse-pounding soundtrack in a new style by astonishing virtuoso Jake Kaufman! The first collaboration between Yacht Club Games and Nitrome, pixel masters!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bummer review.  I'm a huge fan of Yacht Club and Shovel Knight and my expectations were pretty high, but this doesn't meet those expectations - Lets talk about why!UPDATE: A lot of the addressable issues mentioned here have since been fixed!  There are real improvements here, and I'm going to make another pass at this and update this review.  For now though, take complaints with a grain of salt because several have been fixed!This game is also on phones.  That's not really a problem and honestly, putting out quality stuff on phones that isn't just predatory gambling P2W trash ought to be celebrated, but it has created major problems for this title on other platforms.First, The view port is too small.  There are several enemies that can traverse a lot of vertical space in ways that feels unfair because of the restricted view port.There are a lot of contextual actions in the game.  You auto downspike against every diggable brick, and against every enemy.  At worst, it means that you are 'forced' to dig through bricks you don't want to and even at it's best, it really cheapens the platforming experience.Finally, the UI is too big.  The nice UI from Shovel Knight is gone in favor of oversized information on top of the play space.There are several elements in this game that seem in contention with each other.A lot of people rag on the insta-kill drill - I actually like this as a means to pressure the player to move - you have to really decide what you are going to spend your time on and it helps to keep a pace.  What doesn't work here is when things that move up and down and block forward progress have painfully long cycles and you are forced to give up a ton of that time, or worse.  When the player isn't setting the pace of decent, the flow of this game falls apart.The platforming feels slow and clunky.  The punch line here is that they are very close to the original Shovel Knight, but a combination of the vertical orientation and that scenarios are so much more dense makes for mechanics that don't feel like they are serving the scenarios well.Not to belabor the whole 'also on phones' bit, but the platforming is just not that fun or expressive.  It frequently feels tedious, and the view port can sometimes make it feel unfair, or like you are cheated.In the game are these books you can step on that then snap shut.  There is a tunnel you must descend by making them snap shut and then jumping into the space they create before it opens again.  If you just walk off the edge, you still hit the book.  Trying to thread that needle is miserable, and the first time I did it, I truly had no idea if you could even jump to it's side, or if there was some other solution maybe via contextual action that I missed.  This was kind of the moment when I decided this game just isn't that great.The art is great, and the game has a lot of charm in it's animations and presentation - There is polish on display here.  There are a ton of different scenarios in each level and they way they are stitched together generally makes it feel fresh every run.   Most of the platforming challenges are pretty good (with some real stinkers here and there...). Most of the bosses are generally fun and the idea of having multiple layouts per boss is pretty cool and makes the re-clears a lot more tolerable.  The game clearly has some people who care behind it.Unfortunately, the game needs two distinct SKUs.  That's really the long and short of it.  If I were to point to one thing that is just crushing this game right now, it's the view port.  Closely behind it is the platforming mechanics which are just painfully slow and clunky.  I understand why these decisions were made to make it manageable to release this both on Mobile and Everything Else, but it has come at too steep of a cost.  It's enormously difficult (and expensive) to maintain two major versions of the same game, but I think that's what needs to happen here to really bring this to the heights of other Yacht Club entries.There are a list of other strengths and problems to talk about, but I just don't think they are relevant until the very basics are fun.  Moving and Digging and Whacking a dude with a Shovel needs to be so fun before we talk about power ups or meta progression, and we just aren't there yet.--I wish the best for this game - I'll be eagerly awaiting updates, but I'm probably not coming back to it unless there are major changes to the PC/Console release.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the original Shovel Knight and was excited to jump back into this world once more. For the record, I'd say I'm only a slightly above average platform player but I was really shocked that I was able to beat the game in just 5 hours. Once I saw the credits I honestly didn't really feel the need to keep playing, which I guess should be fine for some. I think I was hoping for there to be more. The odd thing about the game is that it starts off really difficult but once you have seen enough variations and figure out which of the handful of buffs that are the best for survivability then you will breeze through the game. I spent the first three hours just trying to beat the first boss but then once I got it, I literally was able to beat the whole game on the next run without ever seeing the areas or bosses before. I know there are still some things to collect or unlock but I definitely didn't feel like there was anything of significance left to see or experience. I guess it just feels very underwhelming having spent a lot of time with Rogue Legacy 2 which took me a solid 25 hours to beat. Still, the pixel art is great, so is the music but that's kind of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Shovel Knight, but I just can't recommend Shovel Knight Dig. For a roguelite, none of the relics and boosts you find along the way seem all that impactful to the run, and the grind to unlock equally unuseful unlocks/relics etc just isn't fun. The difficulty varies wildly between stages and bosses, and runs are either super hard or super easy, seemingly up to RNG. Whether you got areas with lots of gems, whether the level came out in a way where you could get all the gears to get the bonus at the end of each stage, and if you had enough money to buy items found in secret rooms with vendors. Some of which you can find early in a run and not be able to afford anything.The game feels rather amateur and short for the asking price. I finished the game and got the credits, but don't feel any drive to continue playing to try to get the secret ending, which feels a bit too luck based as well. I just watched them on YouTube and can tell you I do not feel like I'm missing out. As far as roguelites go, this one not only never makes you feel rewarded, but never makes you feel like you're more powerful or making progress in any meaningful way other than how far you make it on a run. I honestly don't think I'd recommend this game at over $5, and it doesn't feel great to feel that way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun, and I'm enjoying it thoroughly, but there's some stuff I feel a need to clear up from other reviews for the game, stuff with people who seem to just be too dense to understand how to interact with a game that isn't identical to what which it's a spin-off of.The platforming is fun and has tight controls to the point where using a joystick won't even delay your actions enough to hurt you. Items modify how you interact with your moveset and environment in fun ways, bosses are fun and match the quality of the usual Shovel Knight boss fights, the tweaks to Shovel Knight's moveset and the possible interactable tiles in the game make for a fun dynamic that suits the level design, and the sounds and sights on display are a joy to hear and see! Meta-progression is lighter letting the game enjoy a more Arcade-Roguelike feel without hard committing, and the game rewards playing around with what seems like background details by presenting you with more secrets than you may expect!reading dialogue from NPCs helps you find hints towards greater secrets, as well as the Meta-progression elements, and a good run can last over an hour without overstaying its welcome!Let's start adressing complaints with the "Designed for mobile" accusations!"The view port is too small."no, it's not, the game is very clearly designed for wide-screen, and if you're being hit by things above you, maybe you should kill the flying enemies that pass through blocks before you descend."There are a lot of contextual actions."The only contextual actions in the game are: Digging through dirt when attacking it, and talking to NPCs with the attach button, both of which work how you'd expect from just about any platformer."The shovel-drop is forced because manually doing that would make the controls too complex for mobile"No, it's forced to make the level design harder to navigate, if it were for simplifying the controls, the wouldn't be items that use the controls that were previously for the shovel-drop in the original Shovel Knight. Being forced to dig through the dirt blocks that are over spikes is to pressure you to not stay there too long, and make collecting the treasures harder."the UI is too big"No, it really isn't, it's literally just a reasonable size, and barely takes up any space in the corners of the screen."The platforming is tedious and simple"Well someone isn't trying to collect the gems, which is something that makes the platforming require plenty of fast thinking unless you want to handicap your run with fewer items.Next, lets get to the game's lengthI'm seeing complaints about the game being too short, saying things like "I won the game after only 3 hours, and didn't care to play again therefore the game is bad"That's not how this works, this is a roguelike game, it's literally designed to be played repeatedly, with variation between runs, just because you personally don't find roguelike games to be enjoyable, does not make roguelike games bad, that's just your personal preference."The instakill saw makes me go fast! ;-;"Yes, that is the point, if you don't like it, maybe you should destroy it, because you *can* do that! But there's a reason for putting time limits even if they're soft time limits in games like these, it prevents the player from optimizing their strategy to the point of sucking all the fun out of the game by playing everything so safe that it's a slog of nothing happening for 2 hours."The difficulty seems to fluctuate wildly!"This is not an issue with the game, this is an issue with you not reading signs before jumping down the holes they mark, at the branching paths you get to see signs that mark paths with what they will have, there's yellow signs which denote neutral information, red signs that denote harder paths, and green signs that denote easier paths, these signs are not hard to see, you're just ignoring them and blaming the game for the effects of your own refusal to engage with it."How am I supposed to thread the needle with these books?"You don't. while it's technically possible, you're not supposed to do that, and it gets you killed 9 times out of 10 because that's just not how those work, but, of you stop bashing your head against the brick wall for a second and try using a different part of your base moveset on it, you can destroy the books entirely, without risking any damage!"Shrink spore secrets make you wait around!"Oooor, you could skip them if you can't enter them under the circumstances, your inability to know when to retreat isn't the game's fault, and yes, you might not have been able to plan ahead for it, but there's a reason getting every secret in an area is an achievement, you're not expected to do it often."Some items are bad for your run!"Yes, this is called balancing the item pool, sometimes you just shouldn't take an item, and of you got it from a blindbag, there's ways to get rid of it anyways."Why can't I get a God Run?!?!?!?!?"not every roguelike has to give you an occasional free win."I lose my items when I die! Why can't I have more progression between runs!?"Yes, this is how Roguelike games work, Meta-progression is a common feature in roguelike games, sure, but it's not mandatory to make the game fun."What items you get decide of your run is viable"No, that is surprisingly not the case here, all obstacles can by gotten past with no items, and the lack of enemy health scaling makes it so that you can't get terrible luck and be unable to progress in the face of a horde of enemies you can't run from, and of you want more items so bad, just look for secret rooms, those even reset the Omega-Drill to a good distance from you when you enter then, and pause it until you leave.If I seem a bit snarky to the people writing negative reviews for this game it's because many of their complaints just don't hold water, either from being based on assumptions about how the existence of a mobile port could be affecting the game design, being from someone who just doesn't care for this type of game in the first place, or plainly displaying the intellect of Wheatley from Portal 2 in how they approach problems and read obvious signage, which is to say, stupidly, and ignoring all instruction.If the signage not being big enough for you is something you consider a problem, then perhaps you just need an easier game, not every game should need to spoonfeed instructions to you or innundate you with tutorials, especially with mechanics that can be easily learned with a little bit of experimentation. Or maybe you could just learn to pay more attention to what you're doing!

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game bad? No, not exactly. The issue is that it plays too linearly to be a replay-able roguelike and therefore is far too short. Achievements only really artificially inflate the playtime. I feel if this game wasn't a roguelike it would have been a better experience. The main issue with the game being so short, only taking me 3 hours to win a run, is that it costs as much as the original collection of 4 full sized campaigns. There's just nowhere near enough here to justify the price tag. If it was something like $10 dollars I'd say sure, pick it up, but for the current price, it's just not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game for the first time. my experience has been mostly negative in ways that updates to this game will not be able to fix.My issues with the game aren't about softlocks or glitches, though the game had plenty of those at launch, lemmie tell ya. Nah, my issue with this game is that it's really, really boring. the game feels like going from level chunk to level chunk and once you learn the optimal path for each one you just repeat the same path as you encounter them. not really that engaging or choicemaking, nor does the game feel particularly random at all due to that.the metaprogression generally shoves JUNK items into your item pool, and my file that beat the game has few unlocked (the Horn smatters bosses so i always wanted it). the boss battles aren't too bad but they aren't Yacht Club's best, either. just perfectly fine i guess.interesting chain reactions/situations are a roguelike staple. for instance: issac's upgrade combinations creating insane attacks. noita's amazing alchemical disasters you get each run.spelunky's twisting caves with rube goldberg momentsthis game has basically none of those. there are a few but you generally avoid trying to make them activate as all of them hurt you or destroy items. speaking of items the key./egg systems are annoying and luckbased and the relic system often leaves you accidentally picking up and dropping the same item multiple times by accident.can't believe this game took so long to make and costs this much. i'm not a Dollar Per Hour guy at all. I prefer to let price indicate quality in construction generally. but also this game, whilst mostly just being annoying, doesn't take long to break open and beat. so it doesn't even manage to entertain in a I Wanna Be The Guy way, sadly.if you want the pros of the game here they are:good graphicsgood musicgood controlsa bit fun on occasiongame's a 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who joined the Shovel party relatively late, I quickly found myself in love with the original as well as , which is one of my favorites. Now,  is well known for trying out different things with quite the success. To witness the great diversity of our Shovel hero, we can check  or . Different formulas that somewhat worked really well. I could say  belongs in the same category. It's a bit different, but for me personally, far more enjoyable than  or . Regardless, if you have been a fan of the series so far, even its spin-offs, I'm sure you'll feel right at home with this new take.Contrary to what we're used to, this time around, there isn't an epic adventure waiting for us. No kingdom needs rescuing, and no princess is in peril. Hour hero has just fallen asleep and someone stole his bag... Yep, not the biggest quest, but that's  for you. A short and simple introduction as the game practically pushes you right into the fun.Before we jump on the gameplay, let's make one thing clear:  is a roguelike. I'm traditionally not into that genre, but I still decided to give it a try, and I'm not disappointed. Available across all systems, including mobile devices,  fits right into that category. A game you can pick up and play almost anywhere with a difficulty level far easier from previous titles, and this time we also have procedural generated levelsOn contrary to previous games, players go straight down, digging through a hole while platforming consistently downwards. In fact, you're only going sideways for secret rooms or extra loot areas. As level design goes, it will always range a bit of what is expected. Descend while avoiding dangers, and although you can't bounce indefinitely such as in , it's still possible to use familiar moves to dig around in style.Players gather loot to upgrade at the store, as it's expected from the roguelike genre. Upgrades are actually pretty standard, and the game doesn't force constant improvements, which is a relief. Sill, dying will result in a click away from start digging it all up again, in a new and unexpected environment.It's definitely a casual game, but I still found it quite challenging in some moments. Boss fights can be intense if you're not sure what to do, and one other round might surprise you with a strange placement of enemies. I also did not feel rushed to collect loot or desperate for resources to upgrade. I'd say it's quite well-balanced in that regard.Visually  sustains that familiar 2D atmosphere of the Shovel Knight brand but far more colorful. Maybe it's a pixel design choice or perhaps a completely new style, but I do have to complement the team here. It's still Shovel Knight, but far more vibrant and somehow simple for this type of gameplay. I'm more than happy with the visuals, especially across different environments.Both soundtrack and special effects are engaging as well. The soundtrack is a bit simple, especially if you go around a few runs and starts to become repetitive. I found myself enjoying the game with my own Spotify playlist while just having the special effects, which are very resemble of Shovel Knight.I have a feeling those with a Steam Deck or a mobile device can deeply enjoy the game if they have an hour or so to burn. Of course, those who find themselves really digging for glory, will appreciate the game regardless of the system. Performance is very smooth and its compatibility with Linux is over the top. No need to tweak any settings. Optimization is on-par with the previously released titles, so you know what you're getting. A solid experience regardless of where you play!All in all,  may not be the ultimate adventure you and me were expecting, however... Can we really deny a fun roguelike with our courageous hero? Probably not. After all, I do find myself deeply enjoying the mechanics, even if it's a roguelike, I have to take my hat off and show massive respect for a simple, yet quite entertaining title.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, because I can feel all the love and effort that went into it. But at it's current price it's hard for me to recommend a 3 hour experience for 25 dollars, and with no post-game run modifiers there's no replay value outside of achievement hunting which just isn't my bag.If you are a Yacht Club Games super fan and are looking for a very short, very linear, action platformer rogue-lite in the style of Shovel Knight then this is the game for you. If you're looking for something to sink your teeth into, this isn't going to be it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I really loved Shovel Knight Dig. The art and music are incredible, and there's a lot of creative gameplay ideas. The roguelike upgrade system is a little less deep than in a game like Downwell, but I've still had a great time. People are really overblowing how little content there is, but if you're the sort of player who's done with the game as soon as you see the ending it's probably not the best value for you.I think one of the reasons a lot of reviews have been saying it's really short is that it's not hard to beat the game without seeing a lot of the content. There are 6 unique worlds, and Nitrome definitely chose to add a lot of polish and replayability to each world at the expense of making more of them. And you only play 4/6 of the worlds each run, so if you beat the game in 3 hours, you're only going through the later worlds once or twice, and you're gonna miss a lot. I honestly think they should have just forced you to play every world back to back to beat the game. For really hardcore players, I've had a lot of fun competing globally/against my friends for score, but just trying to see the ending probably isn't a big enough goal for the value. The worlds have a good amount of variation; each one has a couple distinct themes and the level generation is pretty different each time.  Even after playing for 9 hours I don't feel like any of them have gotten stale save maybe the first world that you have to play every time. Having different layouts for some of the bosses was a nice addition that made replaying the first boss a ton of times more enjoyable.The gameplay is a lot of fun, with a rough moment every once in a while. There are a lot of little level chunks that use the mechanics in clever ways, like the one where . I've really had a fun time trying to collect all the gems and gears on my way down, they're hidden in a lot of cool places. You get to the point where you will recognize a few of the repeating segments in the procedural generation, but never so much that it's annoying. I guess the bigger issue with the gameplay is the generating enemies. One time the  drill was decending on me in a section that had a ton of the pink jellyfish things and it was completely impossible to get down because they would just keep bouncing me up. It's a little frustrating that your pet allies will sometimes kill trampoline creatures that are placed in the level to allow you to get a gear. But these moments are rare enough that it doesn't bother me that much and the majority of the time it's a lot of fun to run through the game.The upgrade system is pretty decent. I think on average the tools you are given feel a little underpowered. It can be satisfying to find a good situation to use the equipable abilities, especially vs bosses, but in regular levels there's so much going on that they're only a bit better than the shovel. I think the bread and butter of a roguelike is to have a tool that feels really powerful and you want to play carefully and manage the risk/reward to hold onto it, so I wish there was a bit more of that feeling with the upgrades.I can't think of a single complaint for the art and the music, it's just a treat to look at and listen to. If you appreciate good pixel art and chip music, this is almost as good as it gets.Overall, despite a few weaknesses, I think Shovel Knight Dig is a great game and worth your time. For dev feedback, I'd recommend Nitrome change the way they pace out their content to extend the game and improve the balancing for the roguelike upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw some mixed reviews but decided to buy anyway.In short: Way better than expected core gameplay.  Graphics and music are also a treat.  The biggest flaw seems to be giving players an 'accessibility' menu right from the start instead of making them earn extra health/power/etc via Rogue-like progression.  The game is quite challenging if left to default settings.I'll wager most of the negative reviews came from players who cranked accessibility to max, beat the game quickly and were left wondering where the the value is.

_childDocuments_.review: :-Nice artwork-Good music-Responsive controls-Not nearly enough content to justify the price tag-A screen optimized for mobile devices makes this game feel too zoomed in, enemies will hit you from off-screen with little chance to react and the tiny viewing area limits level complexity-Bosses are mostly a joke once you've fought them a couple times-Unlockables felt uninspired and limited in scope and effectNot worth it at full price, lacks content and complexity. _childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, as much as I love the art style, the music, and the story telling style of the Shovel Knight games, this one ultimately wasn't for me. While I do like rogue-lites, a lot of this one felt like starting from square 0 with little permanent "progression." Any upgrades to health, for example, are temporary to the run. Alongside that, there were what felt like quite a few "gotchya" style moments. Example, I snagged a glass egg from a reward, and went into a side room. Proceed to talk to the NPC... who turns into a slime and damages me before I can react, breaking the glass egg. While that's obviously learned information for the next time encountering that room/NPC, it feels like a cheap shot, and not a good one in a "haha that's funny," kinda way. There were several other instances I encountered while playing the game and streaming for friends, which resulted in a couple instances of *them* saying "Wow, that was kinda BS," without any input from my end.While I do hope this game, and Yachtclub in general, succeeds, I think it may have a narrower audience than the original Shovel Knight was able to reach.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot believe I have to say this because I absolutely adored the first game but I cannot recommend this game as of right now. Right off the bat I found a bug that can softlock you into a wall at the start of a run that is very easy to repeat and is persistent. Not only that but the game actively discourages exploring at all and it needs A LOT of fine tuning. Spores that infinitely spawn and can go through walls and follow you anywhere, the fun police drill that starts chasing you if you don't go to the next area quick enough, little to no initial explanation of skills or upgrades, not to mention how it forces you to dig through sand regardless if you wanted to or not often resulting in missed stuff or just straight up cheap deaths.Not gonna lie I was EXTREMELY hyped for this game after the disappointment that was pocket dungeon but this just isn't a good sequel as it currently stands. Do better Yacht Club come on.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is one of those games that once you start playing it and understanding it you won't want to stop playing it!It doesn't compare to the "classic" Shovel Knight games as it is a Roguelike game and a vertical one at that, instead of a platformer. The game asks you to dig your way down to the depths in search of some lost gems and your stolen bag!Sounds simple right? Yes.. And no!The game features many secrets and it isn't so simple as you'll discover to beat it in its entirity! Keep digging and winning to uncover more and more until the "final act".. You won't regret the journey!The dungeons each time are random but also familiar as they use the same presets (though plenty to keep it fresh at every run). Clever enemies, familiar and new faces and a unique story that's worth it!You can use your faithfull shovel or use magic to defeat your foes and solve this mystery to recover your bag. Why is it so important?..Except of your abilities and magical powers, you also can find within the dungeons unlockable powers, weapons, food, upgrades and abilities. Don't forget to collect all 3 cogs for the machine! You'll be needing them!Fun achievements and fulfilling! Although for some it will require a lot of patience and deaths. The game sets many challenges for you for plenty of hours if you like it but you can also set your own and triumph at your own terms!The fantastic music and vivid visuals along with the awesome gameplay won't make you feel borred not even for one second.In all my time, I encountered very few bugs that the devs are working on them and most have already been fixed. Don't overthink it.. Just go buy yourself a copy of the game and start playing! You won't regret it one bit!For more reviews, follow my curator

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for about an hour and it's pretty great. I'll write a longer review when I've played the game more, but I wanted to get ahead of the crowd. For now, I'll just bullet list the things I like so far* All the enemies you encounter feel like tools for you to get more treasure and find your way deeper into the level. It really feels like the whole game is working together as one.* The audio is wonderful. It's just what I was expecting from a Nitrome and Yacht Club matchup* The visuals are astounding. I've never played a more beautifully drawn pixel game. Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove's graphics were fun and nostalgic for some people, but for me, DIG's graphics are even more so. Treasure Trove mimicked NES/SNES graphics, but DIG mimics and improves GBA graphics which is the era I grew up in.* Digging with the shovel just feels amazing. Each slash of dirt just feels fun, I can't explain it.* The game doesn't shove its mechanics in your face. You'll be talking with NPCs and looking at images on signs, but there's no real tutorial. You'll be discovering the nitty gritty of this game by playing it yourself, but the good news is that most of that is icing on the cake. Even if you don't understand things at first, you'll be able to enjoy the game without that understanding.* the only thing that kind of threw me off with this game is that you can't stop doing the DuckTales downward thrust. Shovel Knight will always thrust downwards, so prepare yourself with that.
