_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The second DLC has finally been announced to be close to release! Took them a year of radio silence, thought they abandoned it. Will update my review once I've had time to play around with it! Hopefully those 100 bug fixes/tweaks/localization fixes are enough to make the game fun.UPDATE 2: They missed their release deadline and have not given a new estimate for when the update releasesThis game is riddled with too many problems to be worth the cost.The game is frustrating to play and countless times I found myself genuinely angry after I lost a run to something that felt completely out of my control. Sure a lot of deaths are my fault, but plenty of them I honestly believe I had no blame whatsoever for what happened.As an aspiring game designer, I've been trying to 100% this game and I've taken to writing down every problem I can find that I believe to be an objective game design flaw (since you learn a lot more from studying what doesn't work compared to what does work) and the list grows surprisingly quickly. I find something new every other session.Just to give a few examples of the biggest problems:Many hazards have no telegraph to alert the player that something will happen. Mainly applies to Flame Spewers, which unlike most games, do not have a tell before activating. Other games usually either make it flash or shoot a small puff to alert the player beforehand.This also extends to enemies falling on top of you from offscreen. It's less frequent, but still happens plenty.The 2 choices for what level to go to next are often forced, as sometimes you only have 1 option or there is no difference between the options. For example, sometimes they will have a sign at each path saying "this enemy will appear here", which implies it won't appear on the other path, but despite that it is very common for the enemy to be in both paths, meaning your choice had no effect on the outcome.It is also quite common at the end of a world for the game to only give you 1 of the 2 possible world options. Since you only go through 4 of the 6 worlds in a run, the other world won't show up later. If you wanted to go there (like if you want to unlock the armor blueprint there) you're outta luck.There is a spike variant that just instantly kills you. Drill Spikes only do a bit of damage, but Spike Spikes just instakill you. I believe that instakill mechanics in a roguelike must be very carefully used, like the Omega Saw which needs it to be effective as a "HURRY UP" mechanic. The existence of effective non-instakill spikes prove that instakill spikes are unnecessary and were probably just included because most platforms have them, and it's fine in those games. But with platformers, you get back up at a checkpoint and continue onwards. In a roguelike, you might be set back up to an hour and lose all your progress.This says to me that they didn't think about what mechanics make sense for a roguelike, but instead thought of what mechanics make sense for a platformer. This makes me wonder if it wasn't always supposed to be a roguelike, but that's just speculation.On the topic of the Omega Saw, the levels often do not feel designed around it's existence. Many level pieces force you to wait, like moving platforms, tanky/hard to hit enemies blocking the way, swarms of enemies, and that one time I fell into a hole you couldn't jump out of and got softlocked. I'm not even sure how that last one cleared QA testing.Y'know, maybe that platformer turned roguelike theory has more to it than I thought, the Saw does feel like a bit like it was placed in after the levels were made...Managing Follow Items (Keys and Eggs) can be a major pain. Taking damage drops the item in the back, and you cannot pick it up while in I-Frames. This often leads to dropping an item in a bad position which makes you take a ton of damage trying to get it back, usually leading in the death of the run. I've even had keys fall through the floor before on moving platforms. This becomes especially frustrating with the Relic Keys.Relic Keys must be purchased at the START of a run and brought to a random point in the well to open a Relic Challenge (if one even spawns, it's not guaranteed) that will unlock a relic for your future runs. This becomes frustrating quickly as it becomes increasingly difficult to find a gate as you unlock them, and as you quickly run out of funds to buy keys with.The "Email Us" button in the settings for providing feedback & bug reports doesn't work properly. I tried to use it and while I was typing my fourth word it reset back to my inventory. I think while I was typing I hit a back button but I'm not sure. Regardless, this is still a developer issue.I'm genuinely disappointed at the devs for releasing this game. There are so many flaws that I think the only way to fix the game is to rebuild it from the ground up. That's probably why the promised QoL patch and 2nd free DLC seem to have been abandoned completely. It's almost been a year and they've been radio silent for all I can find. Maybe they actually are making big changes to fix the game and it's just taking a long time, but I wouldn't bet on it.This game has definitely severely hurt my perception of both Yacht Club and Nitrome's competency as game developers and deeply confused me.Nitrome was a legendary flash game studio, and S.K. Treasure Trove was one of the most popular indie tiles of recent memory, how did they mess up this badly?At least the soundtrack is really good. Unfortunately that's all this game really has going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: What if Spelunky was Shovel Knight?Suffers from the same pitfalls as Spelunky: the true ending requires visiting the wiki, is punishingly easy to fail out of, and winning a basic ending run is maybe slightly too easy. The core is much easier to pick up than Spelunky though, and is very true to the Shovel Knight platforming style.I'd recommend the regular Shovel Knight game over this, but this is still a very enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: SHOVEL KNIGHT! The music and art is great. It ends there though...Cons: Beat it in 3 hours and there was nothing else to do. It's a rogue lite, shouldn't there be more after you beat it? Some sort of reason to keep playing other than collect-a-thon? Difficulty is the same, Nothing really new. That said, it could use a few QoL additions. A LOT of unfair deaths because the proc. gen. is bad. Boss fights are the same EVERY time with a new arena, sort of. No new dialogue. residentSleeper.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE Shovel Knight.Pocket Dungeon is also a lot of fun.But unfortunately Shovel Knight Dig just doesn't hit home.I have been excited for a Roguelike Shovel Knight since it was announced.The last couple weeks I have been looking forward to the release, buying and playing the moment it came out.It was okay.Item unlocks are disappointingly pointless.Placement of Relics/Gears/Rooms and what is inside those rooms ultimately decides how good your run will be.And the relics that you can unlock, for the most part, don't even feel impactful to farm towards.You could get a lot of gem drops and rooms, but no merchant room, or the opposite.I encountered 5 merchant rooms in a row, all without any rooms that had treasure, hence, aside from in the first room, in the other 4 I couldn't afford anything.It also feels like runs are either super hard, or super easy.You will either die before reaching the first boss, or make a full run through it all without too much effort.The first three runs I didn't even reach the first boss.But my fifth run I was good enough to finish the game?All in all it took me about 2 hours of overall Gameplay.Ultimately I felt disappointed.The game is expensive, at least when you consider the length (2-3 hours to finish, you... could... play more? Unlock more pointless upgrades? Try for the leaderboards (which already has cheaters)) and what you could get for that kind of money in this genre... Stuff like Hades or Risk of Rain 2, games that have AT LEAST multiple dozen hours of content and after that you will STILL encounter new stuff.I feel like I have seen everything after my 2 hours. Maybe a couple small enemies, a couple more pointless unlocks, meh.At least the graphics and music are great.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: Heads up, classic Shovel Knight fans, this is NOT more of the same horizontal platforming and world traversing you are used to. Definitely look in to this game first before buying, if you're looking for that specific experience again.This game is a mostly vertical, arcade-like roguelite with roughly 30-40 minute long runsI am recommending this to people that enjoy arcade-y or short run roguelite type gamesThe Good- Very charming sprites and vivid, pleasing colors. It reminded me a lot of Mega Man 7 and 8.- Polished and often amusing animations- Nicely designed and distinct themes for each area- Excellent, catchy music which has sprinkles of Sega-ish sounds that reminded me of Dynamite Headdy, Sonic 3, plus arcade games mixed in.- A lot of the same goofy, dumb humor- Tough, but not too tough- Has a good formula and feel for new content or mechanics to be added in the futureNeutral- Shovel Knight is forced to do his downward Zelda 2 type bounce attack whenever he jumps. This forces him to break certain diggable tiles while descending. This leads to many harrowing moments where you have to be very quick and sharp to direct Shovel Knight to where you need to go. I enjoy this a lot and feel like certain sections of the stages would be boring if I had 100% control over the tiles below at all times. HOWEVER, I can very easily understand that this lack of fine control frustrates and annoys people.- It isn't more "traditional" shovel knight. Definitely an understandable write-off for many, but I am fine with a new game style since I've already played a game with a similar formula 4 times, now.- The method to get the real ending is cryptic. Some people love that, some people hate it. I think they were going for the way Spelunky works, where you either curiously or accidentally come across alternate ways to do things... but I think most people casually playing this game would never know to even try getting a different ending and therefore feel like they got the full experience in a couple of hours.The Bad- Very, very short for the price. "Beating" the game only took me about 1.5-2 hours. There are more unlocks to buy and a secret ending to get, but I feel like most people will see the credits and call it a wrap.- Many of the expensive "upgrades" are useless/situational and only dilute the item pool and make runs HARDER if you get bad item RNG. I was really hoping for a little bit more meta-progression, or at least enough "good" purchasable upgrades to get multiple styles of "builds" in.- Certain enemy attacks/events/hazards can trigger nearly off-screen and it can destroy gems/gears with little to nothing you can do about it. A couple of enemies (in particular, the enemy that looks a bit like a pancake stack, which shoots projectiles into the air and they slowly rain down) have their projectiles travel across multiple screens.- There are a couple of soft lock situations that ruin a run, like un-shrinking in the middle of a shrinky-knight tunnel mid screen transition... or the exploding rocks """"upgrade"""" destroying the only way out of a side room. - There are a few spots with weirdly near pixel perfect jumping spots that make it difficult to leave a shop, or where the tiny sideways bouncy mushrooms grab you even though you don't touch them then fling you away.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a charming and fun game that is a fresh take on the original game. Players should beware, however, that the game is quite short. I am not great at soulslike games at all, but was able to beat the game in 3.5 hours. Compare this to a game like Hades where it took be about 18 hours to beat the final boss the first time. Replayability is somewhat limited, since even though every run will have unique rooms, the feel is mostly the same. The game is a lot of fun, the graphics are stunning and the music is amazing. The cost per hour of gameplay is however a lot higher than the original Shovel Knight game, and something that might disappoint some players.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: I hate the true ending's requirements because of how unbelievably RNG based it is.The fact that you have good chance of not finding the room, store, item, or later segments making you take enough damage to break an important key item, which forces you to restart the whole run is not worth the frustration. Just watch the ending on Youtube instead.This game is not worth 22,49€ even if the introductory offer comes with the soundtrack, which is one of the best things about the game.Unless Nitrome is going to fix all the major problems and bugs that plagues this game,  I strongly recommend for you to wait and see if things get any better or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: Best in class visuals, and a host of interesting mechanics, what's not to love?Sadly, everything else. There is enough content here to create an entire fantastic sidescroller, but it's wasted on a barely-mediocre roguelike. The game doesn't feel good to play, and none of the systems made me excited to replay runs. The movement is unsatisfying, the pacing is wonky, and the difficulty curve feels off.After being stuck on levels 2 and 3 for a few hours, I finally got as single run past them, which snowballed into me beating every level after that on the first try, and then beating the game. At 4 hours in, I had beaten the game, and had zero desire to do any more runs because the game is frankly pretty boring.I don't recommend Shovel Knight Dig, despite being really excited about it coming out for the several years since it was announced.I'll summarize the review this way: THIS GAME SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN A ROGUELIKE.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many people slept on this game at launch. If you enjoy classic style action platformers and roguelikes/lites, this is going to be right up your alley.The only nitpick I have is that the screen is panned a little too far down, but it's easy enough to adjust to without even thinking about it. So, sit back, grab some gems, and enjoy yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played many roguelikes, and that's not necessarily because I don't like them, I guess it's more so just that I don't like restarting games when I'm really far in. THIS however, has become one of my favorite games of all time. It's so addicting, the platforming just rules, and trying time and time again never gets old. And it being a Shovel Knight game just adds onto this amazing ice cream sundae of a game. I implore you to try this game, even if you only mildly like platformers or roguelikes. Yacht Club does not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: I would probably review this as more of an in between thumbs up and thumbs down but I suppose in the end, I would lean slightly more towards thumbs down. If it was about half the full price, I would probably lean more towards thumbs up.First, the Shovel Knight graphics and music is great! It's as to be expected. No complaints there, it certainly sucked me in early. It's really a roguelike, there are some things you can unlock but you don't really power up between runs other than unlocking the ability to find new power ups during a run and finding new armor which is the only "permanent" upgrade you can get. Unlocking things is a total chore. You collect gems on your run which you get to keep most of to make purchases. Everything is so expensive though that you'll be grinding for hours to unlock everything. I highly recommend if you play to change the Accessibility options to double your chance at gems to help the grind out.You'll obviously be digging downwards a lot with your shovel but you'll also find yourself dropping blindly further below. You could either miss a key item along the way or fall into a dangerous area and take damage just by dumb luck. With a roguelike with permadeath, there shouldn't be any reason to take damage by dumb luck. Once you learn the enemies and hazards of each stage, it just feels, OK? It doesn't feel very rewarding for continuing through each world. You never get that sense of powering up. Even the power ups you do get don't feel like you ever get that powerful.It's pretty enjoyable for a few hours but it's hard to want to keep coming back for more. At $25, I wouldn't say it's worth it. If you see it on sale for $10-15, you can probably give it a go though.

_childDocuments_.review: As to be expected from Nitrome, the graphics are absolutely stunning. As not to be expected from YCG however, is how poorly the game is designed. The controls feel incredibly clunky as compared to other Shovel Knight titles, making this platform based rogue like an absolute pain to play. Most of the time when you get hit it doesn't feel like it's your fault but rather the jank hit boxes and slow movement, on top of this, half of the obstacles you want to look out for are off screen because the game prioritises whatever is far below you rather than having the camera focus on Shovel Knight and giving you the option to move the camera up and down. This has caused me to get hit by so many things and losing runs that could have been avoided simply by being able to look up.There is also an option to turn on an auto-downthrust, which I didn't think I would need to turn on, however on controller the precision you need to execute this move is so precise meaning if you go even a tiny bit off target from pointing your analog stick directly down, the down thrust will just be cancelled causing you to get hit by whatever you were trying to bounce off of. In the end I turned the auto-downthrust option on which brought on it's own set of issues, that being that there is no way to cancel it when you jump, by swinging forward right before you hit the ground (which in the original Shovel Knight it would cancel the downthrust)  it will still magically remove the block under you, making the spikes hidden in dirt a huge pain to get around but the one time it doesn't seem to activate is if you swing forward before landing on an enemy.The game just feels incredibly unresponsive and unfinished control wise, again the graphics are eye candy and the music goes so hard but actually playing the game is such a chore. Apparently it only takes a few hours to beat to beat which really warrants the question as to why there is a 20 quid price tag, as well as there not being a huge variety of items and floor design despite being a roguelike. For the amount of content included as well as the clunky controls it just does not feel worth the money I paid for it. I will probably finish the game eventually but have no motivation to do so, it's not unplayable but again compared to other titles it just doesn't feel polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game, however  after the few hours I put into the game I find myself more annoyed at how poorly the mechanics gel together. I've had enemies hit me while going through secret areas, being forced to fall into spikes placed offscreen and a plethora of other events like this that added unnecessary damage. The original Shovel Knight controls flawlessly which is sadly something I cannot say for Shovel Knight Dig. All the fluid and fast paced movement is gone and replaced with a much clunkier version that still expects you to blaze through levels but punishes you for attempting to do so. I've played a lot of rogue-likes and can safely say this is one of the least memorable.The art is fantastic and the soundtrack is great, but as a game bearing the name "Shovel Knight" it doesn't hold up compared to it's predecessor.It feels like they had a killer idea for a mobile game that became too complicated for the platform. I loved the original and it pains me to leave a negative review but the game just isn't fun on it's own due to clunky controls and questionable design choices. I look forward to Yacht Club's next game but I just can't endorse this one.

_childDocuments_.review: fate and fortune is the most uniquely cruel experience i have ever endured, and not merely within the confines of recreation. it is a trial-by-fire that is wholly apathetic to the notion of the indomitable human spirit and thus actively tries everything in its power to break it. i have previously regarded tooth extractions higher than this sysyphean toil. never before, or since, have i observed in a game the potential to evoke such raw, primeval indignation; like that of a trapped animal gnawing at its paw, desperate to persist in the woefully indifferent world which consigned its wretched fate in the first place. the dlc has made full completion tantamount to rubbing pepper flakes into your retinas while a scooter perpetually strikes your ankle at terminal velocity. subjecting oneself to this RNG death maze pushes the border between leisure and proverbial self-flagellation to extremes previously thought impossible and just when you think it's taken everything it will unearth more to Dig from the hollowed out remains of your soul.

_childDocuments_.review: (18 hours played from a Family Share account) Shovel Knight Dig is a curious game to talk about, but the TL;DR is a cautious recommendation. As for details:There are many things I genuinely enjoy about Dig! The visuals are a great, natural extension of the original's style. The character interactions are lovely, particularly getting more screen time with Shield Knight for an absolutely charming dynamic with SK. The music is fabulous as well, and the general control scheme is easy to conceptually grasp for pick up and play sessions. Getting the normal ending is pleasantly quick once you have a grasp on what the game can throw at you, and fun to do!BUT.The game *will* sucker punch you with its game balance from the procedural generation. Some level gimmicks across the stage biomes are straight up death sentences compared to others in the same zone, and only with time and experience will you understand either how to survive them or outright avoid them. Upgrade RNG is wildly varied, with some runs through raining down loads of useful items and health upgrades while with others you only find expendable relics or one-time heals. Enemies of certain types or configurations will ambush you before you have an honest chance to react, and only with a pessimistic play style will you avoid unnecessary damage. Often there is just a bit too much going on with enemies and hazards to coherently decipher your next correct line of play.Importantly, the route to the true ending will test your patience, at least at this moment before the last big DLC update drops a balance patch to generation. It took me 8 hours of attempts to successfully achieve the true ending, mainly because the stage hazards and enemy groups will cause you to miss pivotal chances to progress the route and force you to begin again from scratch. If the game is aware that the true ending route flags are checked, some fixed items or room patterns would greatly reduce the literal trials and errors that come with attempts. As of writing, only 4.6% of players have achieved the true ending, which seems comically low, and speaks to how the game punishes players in a way that only RNG is capable of delivering.That said, I don't regret my time playing this, and I do want to try the Wish DLC when it launches! So that's a definitive compliment. Just understand that while at its heart I think this is a game made to be enjoyed, the procedural nature of this beast will tell you that you will try again, and again, for a majority of your game time.

_childDocuments_.review: + Platforming focused roguelite+ No progression outside of runs other than unlockables+ Good bosses with high number of possible different arenas for each one+ A lot of room variety, still seeing new generations even now+ Loads of clever design evenly spread out across each world+ Good Soundtrack+ Satisfying SFX+ Gorgeous pixel art+ Worthwhile true ending run- Some rooms can be frustrating / boring- Can miss cogs due to not being able to see down far enough (happened roughly 3 times in 27 hours)- Bouncing up after every pogo on a block gets tiring fastAlso Bosses can become pushovers with certain relics (although the game challenges you to beat it without them)One of my favourite roguelites next to Spelunky 1 & 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Shovel Knight Dig is the highly anticipated spinoff that we have been waiting for, for the last couple of years.  Yacht Club Games teamed up w/ Nitrome to create this fast paced, roguelight platformer.  It has a similar feel to Downwell, but w/ a gorgeous visual aesthetic and all of the tropes that you would expect from this dev team.  This game looks fantastic visually, has a banger soundtrack, and is a ton of fun.  Unfortunately, this game feels extremely light on both meta-progression as well as build variety.  It's hard to recommend this game at a $25 price point b/c it feels like it should be in early access.  The biggest issue imo, is that it actually plays similarly to Rogue legacy 2, but RL 2 has WAY more content, far more build diversity, an insane amount of meta progression, and a world to explore that is about 10x bigger.Consensus:-Middle of the Road Game (Tier 4 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  This was my most anticipated game of the entire year, so it pains me to give this score.  To be honest, I was hesitant of even recommending this game at this point.  I had my first winning run in less than 3 hrs and had another winning run an hr later.  Pretty much every run has played out almost identically in terms of which upgrades I choose, which bosses I fight, how my build plays out, etc.  Yes, there are some more upgrades to unlock and one more ending to complete, but I don't feel a ton of motivation to see it through until more content is added.  I think that this team should have released this game into early access, and added content over the course of 18-24 months, just like RL2 did.  I'm optimistic that more upgrades will be added, some alternative bosses will be added, and maybe a new biome or two in the future will be added.  If this happens, I'll give this game a better review score, but for now, I can only recommend this game at a 50% sale or better for die hard Shovel Knight fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate the fact that I cannot recommend this title. The original Shovel Knight was, gameplay-wise, meticulously crafted to be an amazing experience where the player is in control with regards to the mechanics of the game. If you died, it was usually YOUR fault. That isn't the case here. Just like in the original Shovel knight, the visuals are beautiful and the soundtrack is incredible to listen to. Each of the environments are incredibly varied and seldom feel the same. However, from a gameplay perspective, this title falls far short. Several aspects of not only the enemy patterns, but also the level design demand you take time if they don't hurt you from a non-reactable perspective (which commonly happens due to the level design), despite the fact that the character movement and timed aspect of the ever-encroaching drill arm push you forward without time to look through your surroundings (such as in the case of a game like Spelunky, albeit noticeably more rushed and less informative). The perspective of Shovel Knight is tilted downwards despite the fact that threats can still come from above, and chaser enemies can ambush you on the sides of the level despite needing to stick to the sides to discover secrets and shops, leading to further frustration. Even your ability to deal with said incoming threats is frustrating to manage, as you have fewer options to attack above your character, and the fact that you occasionally pick up sub-weapons to replace your current one (a-la Castlevania) that can commonly source from anything: random enemies, inconvenient locations, and even flying chests that the game encourages you to pick up (as a side note, these weapons do not spawn FROM the chests, if they're in there, they AUTOMATICALLY replace the one in your inventory, no matter how far away you are). As a result, it can be very easy to lose your current sub weapon, which may be key to your gameplay style due to their diversity.Finally, much of the difficulty around each of your treks down to the depths are highly dependent on what you find in shops and chests. The RNG can get a bit ridiculous, as health-increasing items can be at every shop or as scarce as water in a desert. I've had runs where I no-hit multiple levels in a row and still fail in the end due to bad item luck and occasionally nigh-unwinnable situations. There's no consistency, which makes things even more frustrating.I really wanted to like this game, but I can't recommend it as it is now.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit disappointed how the game turned out. And afterwards, once I completed the game, turning Shovel Knight into a Roguelike was not a good choice.The problem with Shovel Knight Dig is that turning it into a more fast-paced, finish on one sitting format, made the narrative and the story suffer, which for me was the best part, and the core of the game in the original Shovel Knight.And the reason for the game being more Roguelike than Roguelite was that the bosses did not adapt to the player passing through multiple times in a row and although you were able to bank your money if you died, this was only usable to buy certain unlockables, that you can then find on the runs. No leveling or taking the banked money with you to the well. There was only one permanent item that allowed you to carry an extra item that drops if you get hit. And you were able to buy armors (which I was saving up for but then the game ended). Therefore replayability took a huge hit as well.At the end the scale of the world that was built in Shovel Knight, felt that it was not used to the fullest and and was somewhat bland.I know that there is a hidden boss at the end, that I still need to defeat but this was not hinted properly at the normal ending. Instead the story just continued as if this "true" ending had never happened. It would have been more intriguing, if there was some sort of carrot to point towards the actual end, maybe fight even harder versions of the few bosses along the way down. Instead now it was directly off to the credits, and suddenly back to the camp. There should have been a better continuation to why the player needs to go again from the beginning if they failed to get the true ending. And the "normal ending" could have been left out completely in my experience.But enough of the story, the gameplay...I got used to the controls fairly quickly but the automatic downward shovel fall took most to get used to. And often felt that why can't I just enable it myself instead of directly going to that state, similarly to how it was in the original game. This often led to some cheap deaths.Then the actual hit box when the Shovel Guy swings his spade, was often janky and would not hit some enemies.There were enemies that spawn off the screen above the player and these were utmost annoying. These sort of enemies could have been heavily toned down or their spawning could have been altered since there were often narrow paths and then bunch of these flying enemies would spawn above you, including the hell blade. In these cases, swinging your spade upwards would have been extremely helpful, but leaving this out was definitely a design choice.But yes the game is hard and I actually finished the game without buying a single armor.This turned out to be quite a long rant but the positives were that I did enjoy the style of the game and the music.And they had definitely focused on the visual aspect of the game, but this isn't enough to save the game.Instead what the game heavily needs is more content in the narrative side and better world building or even more steps along the way down.Instead of a Roguelike the game could have been a linear game with well designed challenges along the way down and checkpoints or underground cities. The overworld currently felt too small and the NPCs that appeared there felt lacking.Sadly I cannot recommend the game, it was fun initially but left a sour taste at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely, this is my favorite game.  I was waiting for this game for 2 years and it stuck the landing.  The level generation is phenomenal and extremely varied, it has some of the most unique passive items ive seen in any rogue like, the pixel art is Nitrome's beautiful glossy goodness, and the music is Jake Kaufman's best work.  "Who Needs Honor '' made me cry listening to it for the first time and its the best track ive heard in an OST for a long time.  Most of the critiques of this game are not that big of a deal or just wrong with the price being the only thing I could get behind.  The forced shovel drop is a good change for this game in my opinion with certain sections of levels using the feature to make platforming more tense and fun.this game has given me the most enjoyment out of any game this year by far and Id recommend it to anyone. If the price is a bit much for you then Id wait until a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a delight. It's the kind of game that reminds you why you like playing video games. It has extremely tight controls, catchy music, and a fun yet challenging gameplay loop that keeps you coming back for "just one more run." Many have mentioned that the game is not very long, and that you can see credits within 4 hours. This is true. However, there is an elusive "true" ending which demands much more of the player. Sure, I wish there were more characters to play as, or a few more stages/variability in the design, but overall it's an incredibly tight package that delivers a very fun experience. I'm on course for the true ending and I am having a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this review short:The good: Jake Kaufman once again delivers with the music. The art direction screams Nitrome (in the best way possible), the writing and characters are charming, and the actual areas have a lot of life to them. Running through each area that first time was extremely enjoyable. The boss fights are easy but fun, and the hexcavators fit in seamlessly with the rest of the Shovel Knight universe.The bad: Relics and especially accessories feel mostly inconsequential to your run. Variety in a run, even with additional items unlocked, does not really impact how you play, and the best items feel at most a slight convenience. Unlocking new items feels unnecessarily grindy for how little they add to the game, and the constantly scaling prices for accessories and relic keys feel more discouraging than anything. The only impactful thing you can unlock to change your runs are armors, and even then, the ones I've unlocked don't change the way you play the game to a significant degree.The disappointing: This game is short. You can finish this game within the span of a couple hours if you adjust quickly to the controls, and after you finish a run (regular or true) there's very little reason to continue playing unless you want to spend the extra time to unlock everything (which doesn't feel encouraged, once again because of how much you have to work for something that does so little for your run).TL;DR: I enjoy this game, but it is not worth its price. Get it on a 40/50% discount, or hope that future updates to this game implement more depth and reasons to replay.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a fun and short Shovel Knight adventure, if you liked the original Shovel Knight then check this out! Because, unlike the other Shovel Knight spinoffs, this entry has very similar gameplay to the original. This fact is one of the game's greatest strengths as the original Shovel Knight is awesome! But, its also one of the games greatest weaknesses, as this game does not really play much like a roguelike past the surface.The game's main structure is sort of a mix between Downwell + Mr Driller. You dig your way down whilst fighting off enemies and occasionally entering side areas for shops/secrets. This structure added with the moveset and controls of Shovel Knight are fantastic and although the game is randomly generated the chunks of level blend together. The level themes are interesting enough and the soundtrack for each one (and the entire game) is kickass, although in terms of actual gameplay they don't really shake things up THAT much.As you progress through runs you will obtain upgrades, and whilst some of them are interesting, they feel more like cheats/mini buffs rather than items for a roguelike. They don't ever change your approach to playing the game, they simply make tiny alterations. The only exception to that is the relics, which are limited-use items and again, don't really shake things up all that much.The plot is OK, but there is far too much dialogue within the actual run, dialogue that, to me, was not even that interesting, I understood the general gist of the plot seconds after I started playing, I really didn't need to read/skip through the same dialogue boxes over and over. The story is also pretty cut and dry, it starts, and it ends, relatively quickly too which is odd for this game being a roguelike.And with that, we begin to see the issue with this game, the replay value is minimal. Which is quite a big deal for a roguelike. Once you've beaten the game once, there is really little incentive to keep playing after you finished 1 run, and getting to the point of beating your first run is great and will take a decent amount of time. But past that, the lack of item variety, and rather samey level generation, accompanied with a story that's already over just leads you to move on to the next game.So in conclusion, as you're making your way to completing your first run, you'll have a blast, its just more of that original Shovel Knight goodness. But past that, as a roguelike, this game has little to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Not what I was expecting. The game play gets repetitive even after an hour or two. The "upgrades" only unlock a *chance* to find an item at random during your run. The saw blade makes so you can't clear a room and have to rush, which I also don't like. All in all, I can't really recommend this game, even at 15 bucks. I'd probably be happier with the original game, even though I usually like rogue-likes. Grinding for gems doesn't seem worth your time, since you have no direct progression by unlocking items. Also the linear increase of the cost to unlock items doesn't feel that great either.The good thing I can say about the game is, that the polish of the graphics, sounds, music and game play are top notch as you can expect from a shovel knight game. But it really hurts to see that there is no rogue-lite progression like in games similar to Rogue Legacy and Dead Cells. I'm dreadfully missing these aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you looking for the next good Shovel Knight game? Well, look further, 'cause this ain't it.Good things first: Art style is great, great transition from the 8bit style, good pixel work. You'll recognize Shovel Knight controls, it feels almost like the orginal one. Music is also great, even though maybe not as catchy as in the first one.Gameplay, however, is another matter. You remember the hand-crafter screens from the first one, where in every screen there was a puprose to enemy, dirt and block placement? That's not here. The semi-random nature of the roguelike gameplay makes the placement sometimes easy, sometimes it fits just right, often it's right our infuriating. You don't even have the time to grasp a screen and stuff is happening and flying at you and then you lost a life. The nature of this being going from up to down makes it often that you "fall" into a screen and you have no time to get your bearings because by the time you grasped what is going on there you are already at the end of the screen.Roguelike nature of the game is also really, really bad. I beat the first boss and then I got some kind of gem that is used for... what? I don't know, maybe the ability to skip the first level, which I had then to pay for to unlock. And then pay for to use every time. Permament unlocks are there, but they feel so, so useless. Skip a level. Carry one more item (not the useful ones, though). Unlock a new Relic or Passive skill that can be found in the dungeon. That's it.You can find some random items in the dungeon. Relics are usables, many of them are either useless or uninspired. Then you can grab Mana or HP upgrades, which seem to be very rare and are NOT permanent, only for the run. There are also keys and eggs (and maybe some other stuff) which will follow you. Only one in the beginning, you can buy more slots. You instantly lose these if you get hit and need to recover them, which is quite annoying. Also keeping the one you want and not picking up another by accident is a pain. Nobody also tells you what the keys are for. They look different, but as far as I can tell, you can use whatever key on whatever door or chest you want. Who made that design choice? There's like a wooden key, an iron key and an ornate key but they all do the same? Characters and story are also like very uninteresting, which pains me to say since the first one was stellar in story and characters, especially for an 8bit platformer. But that's not the case here, you get thrown in the game quite literally after 5 sec cutscene and there you go.It's a shame, really. There are so many "Shovel Knight" games out there but until today, we never got a true sequel - maybe except Spectre of Torment. I'd quite wish for Yacht Club Games going back to the basics and do another one of their great platformers. All this game has done for me is that I'm probably going back and replaying the OG one.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig takes the basic structure of the original Shovel Knight and turns it into a Rogue-lite delve into the weird and wild underground, before the events of the original game. But once you do that, you discover this game is full of secrets and unlocks yet to reach.There's new stuff I like, and new stuff I don't, but if you were jonesing for more Shovel Knight content, this really does hit the spot. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings regarding this game. On one hand the gameplay is a lot of fun, but on the other it is extremely short and there is limited run variety.Shovel knight dig starts of quite difficult. I spent more than half of my play time barely getting past the first area. But as soon as I got more used to the game the difficulty fell of quickly. And it's not like the difficulty comes back in the later stages since most of the enemies are just re-skins that function mostly the same. The enemies also don't scale in the later stages so fighting enemies feels the exact same you just get rewarded way more for the same amount of work.Roguelikes thrive of of run variety. Every run is different, and this adds replayability. Unfortunately Shovel Knight Dig does not have much run variety. There are different level options but the changes are mostly visual. There are a couple of different bosses, but all of the fights end up playing out the same. Items don't really mater and you end up picking up everything while looking for more health. And the game hands you A LOT of it which means you can just tank everything.I would love to be able to recommend this game but i can't. After finishing it once there is hardly any motivation to play again. There is nothing new to see and your run is going to look and play the exact same as the one before. Maybe I would have recommended this game if it cost 5€ but at 25€ it is hard to recommend for the amount of content there is. _childDocuments_.review: (As a note, I was gifted this game by a friend. It wasn't on my radar to buy, and I haven't played a Shovel Knight game since the first one, so I'm not like a mega-fan or anything)I'm seeing a surprising amount of negative reviews here, so I wanna give my two cents and boost the game, cause while it has flaws, I'd say it's worth playing.Shovel Knight Dig is kinda like if Shovel Knight, Downwell, Mr Driller, and modern Roguelite sensibilities are mixed in a blender. If you enjoy roguelites at all, and also enjoyed Shovel Knight, you'll probably enjoy this. But I want to acknowledge some of the criticisms I've been hearing.I've seen people say the level design is bad. It's basically an assorted bunch of predesigned blocks randomly generated into a downward well. Y'know, like a roguelite. The game incentivizes you to go fast, but at the same time secrets are around every corner. At first it might seem frustrating to not be able to explore every nook and cranny to find the secrets, but that's how a roguelite works. You can't get everything. You gotta make do with what you can, because you'll be coming back soon enough. It's about going as far as you can and getting as much as you can so you can build up your arsenal for future games.Secondly, this game is quite hard. I found that it seemed pretty overtuned, but the game actually has a lot of accessibility options. You can easily turn up your max health and damage, to make it easier to tackle. Sure that might hurt your pride but uh, I think it's better to enjoy the game than continue to slam your head against a way with pride and not have any fun with the game you bought. I also saw someone complain about the constantly respawning enemies... and I do agree to an extent. They're really my one problem so far, enemies will continue to spawn and chase you, and while it's easy to deal with them, the game is about moving downward, so the camera always has you on the top of the screen. But the game is also about bouncing, so I constantly bounce into the enemies above me who I scrolled past. I think a minor tweak to make them unspawn once off screen would fix that problem immediately~And lastly, this game is gorgeous. The art in shovel knight has always been very pretty, it feels taken up to 11 here. If Shovel Knight is like, NES taken to its extreme, this feels like SNES taken to its extreme. Very gorgeous pixel art.Anyway long story short, while it's not the best roguelite I've ever played, it's worth checking out. I still haven't gotten to the bottom, so I intend to play it more to find out what's down there!

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, and addicting if you're a fan of roguelikes.A pretty packed game; the visuals are great, the level themes, for all of them being underground, are interestingly varied, the equipment and items are incredibly useful and fun, and the music is outstanding; Nothing less expected from Jake Kaufman. The level gimmicks are pretty straightforward and are well used, this is impressive when you consider the random level generation mixed in with that. There's also hidden details that you find out and take advantage of every now and then, like the water clearing out the muddy relic, and how defeating a boss while dying actually revives shovel knight and it counts as a victory- which no game i've played has done, yet it's a thing every player wants. There's all sorts of stuff like that to look out for in this game. And no spoilers, but getting the true ending feels incredible. I guess it's because of how difficult it is, but hardly any game made me feel excited for a good ending this much.In general the whole thing has me reeled in, it's a real treat for classic pixel art game enjoyers.However, it's a bummer how difficult and outright brutal it can be at times, especially since the only thing to look forward to after completing the game is even more difficult challenges, it also doesn't help that luck has a great influence on your successful runs, sometimes all it takes to win is crazy luck with the health upgrades. I appreciate how the devs constantly add quality of life changes, bug fixes and other minor features to the game, but none of them really made the game considerably any less difficult, which I don't mind myself, but this whole thing makes it harder to recommend the game to someone else. It just narrows the audience for shovel knight further. And heh, *tips helmet* as a shovelhead myself i'd say that's not too shovelful.Do I like this game? Hell yeah!Would I recommend it? Hmm..... maybe? It's a hit or miss depending on who you are, but if it hits, it hits hard, so yeah sure i'd recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game FUN? Yes, this game is fun. Is this game FAIR? No, not in my opinion. The skill curve is crazy high, and there's LOTS of interactions and moments in the game that are just unfair. In lots of places, you can get stuck in a way where you're required to take damage. In some areas, there's straight up softlocks. Never have I felt like I needed accessibility options to have fun in a game. Ever. I played all of Shovel Knight, even completing NG+,  Most relics need a rework. Some actively suck / make the game worse. Some of the hitboxes are way too harsh, like the fish. There's a room where you can ONLY get up by the fish, the fish take 5 seconds to spawn, and you probably won't be able to get out without getting hit. I feel like the camera is too high up. It prevents me from seeing things above me, LIKE COGS. That is stupid. Also, why can't you talk to NPC's by looking up, like in Shovel Knight? Why do I have to swing my shovel, every time? Why can I get stuck in a loop of POGOing ontop of an NPC, UNABLE TO TALK TO THEM BECAUSE I CANT GET OFF.I have lots of complaints about this game. It feels rushed, unfair, and has quirks that I don't like. But I like this game. This game is BEAUTIFUL. I LOVE the sound design in this game, and when I'm in a good groove, I am having fun. This game is fun, but it's rough around the edges, and unfair to people who aren't GOD GAMERS. I honestly feel this game could be fixed with a few tweaks and adjustments.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to beat the original Shovel Knight, but in terms of sheer fun factor, I think Dig takes the cake. While I hope Yacht Club Games returns to its roots and creates a sequel to the original Shovel Knight, I'd gladly take more collabs between them and Nitrome. Clearly, it's a duo that complements each other very well, indeed.Pros    Fantastic Artistic Direction and Soundtrack    Recognizable Shovel Knight Elements Make a Return    Different Environments Add to the Unpredictability and MayhemCons    Light on New Shovel Knight Lore    Some Readability Issues With In-Game SignsScore: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent addition to the Shovel Knight saga!Shovel Knight Dig is an action-platformer roguelite, though I'd say most of its focus is with its action instead of its randomization. Many of the staples of a modern roguelite are here - procedurally generated levels, permanent death, a progression system, and randomized items - but the extent to which the game runs with a roguelite mentality is a bit different than in its inspirations, such as Downwell or Spelunky. Instead, it uses these elements to support the gameplay of an arcade-styled Shovel Knight game, rather than having the randomness and huge amounts of content be its main focal point.I don't think the game is perfect, but I also don't think it's deserving of an overall "mixed" consensus. $25 may be a bit steep for those expecting a big game by sheer numbers of content with tons of different things to do, but I still had a total blast playing the game again and again to the point where I feel the asking price would be worth it, such as for going after the secret ending and tackling its other challenges (and, of course, chasing after a higher score). The presentation is also phenomenal - it's a GORGEOUS looking game with a top-notch soundtrack - and it's the other main thing that had me coming back for more.How much you put into this game is how much you'll get out of it. If you're only interested in clearing the normal ending and nothing more, this game may not be your cup of tea, as it doesn't take very long to do so (I was able to beat it at roughly the 3 hour mark).If you love arcade games, you are a newcomer to the roguelite genre, or you don't mind the roguelite elements being more of a "side dish" instead of the "main course," this game is for you! If you're a die-hard roguelite enthusiast, the game is absolutely still tons of fun; you may just have to temper your expectations a little in terms of raw content.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: I have gone back and forth about whether or not to recommend this game to players on several occasions. The Game has a GORGEOUS artstyle and I can't say that I haven't found SOME enjoyment in this game seeing as I have over 120 hours in it...The problem is that most of those hours have been made up of me revisiting the game after updates to check if any of it's problems have been fixed, and to this day the game remains as poorly balanced as it was at launch.The devs clearly have no idea how to balance this game and seem to be ignoring most of the feedback they get from their community in favour of building their "dream" experience.1. The elemental ring system is incredibly poorly designed with 90% of them being useless for nearly the entire run, at most these rings may save you from 3 stray hits, not worth using and certainly not worth making up 20% of the items in the entire game.2. The Knightmare System does not make the game any harder, only more tedious. The modifiers introduced by the system are not only poorly suited for the game but are also not linked to any form of upgrades or unlockables, meaning the only reward for throwing yourself into the mess that is this game's NG + is a distinctly less fun experience and a trophy in the hub.3. There are very few items in this game that increase your damage or synergies with other items meaning all your runs feel very similar. Those synergies that do exist are nearly impossible to reliably come across because of how diluted the item pool is with all the elemental rings.4. Book of Bomb may randomly show up in a drill capsule or an item bag and if it does you might as well re-set the run because of how dangerous it is.5. The game is not updated very frequently, with the first substancial content update coming half a year after  launch and leaving the game in an equaly bad (if not worse) state than it started in. (Though props to the devs for adding manual shovel drop and at least attempting to make the game more replayable with knightmare mode).6. In general there are not many items, shovel blade upgrades or forms of meta progression in this game. Runs will get boring really quickly.Do you want a Shovel Knight Roguelike with a high skill ceiling, tons of gameplay variety, frequent updates and a bright future? You're probably better off playing Pocket Dungeon.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of both Nitrome and Yacht Club, seeing them work together is very cool. Shovel Knight Dig gets to simultaneously benefit from amazing pixel art/animations and charming environment/character designs. The dark-toned color palette still evokes the first game's feelings very well, despite the sprites being more detailed. And speaking of the original, the soundtrack is just as great, but this time it has a bunch of fresh adaptive takes.Gameplay-wise, the roguelike mechanics allow for more replayability and present the right amount of risk and reward you'd expect in the genre. There's a bit of a lack of accessory variety, though. Foods, relics, and weapon upgrades are much more useful than elemental resistance or any other small QoL buffs that are only worth getting if your health bar is already full. An update introducing a couple more stages, new accessories, and something similar to Hades' Pact of Punishment would be much appreciated. Felt like adding a couple more impressions to this review concerning the game being on Apple Arcade and the discovery of new endings. I, for one, don't feel like the fact this game is also on mobile devices hindered its UI, camera or controls at all. Differently from what some people seemingly think, the mobile version  play in portrait mode. Most complaints relate to design choices influenced by the overall experience developers were aiming for, not the game being on mobile devices. Choosing between shovel pouncing or just jumping, for example, would completely ruin the sense of danger of many sections. It doesn't take a genius to figure out spikes buried underneath dirt (meaning you only have one chance to bounce off before taking damage) would be irrelevant if you could just opt not to bounce off the dirt. This would render the Spikeproof Sabatons almost useless, and players wouldn't even need to watch their heads.However, I do feel the alternate endings are way too ominous. There are no hints whatsoever that there are other endings to achieve after completing a run for the first time. The requirements for the True Ending are oddly specific, and we still have no idea what needs to be done to reach the other endings. Adding such content and not even briefly telling players its a thing strikes me odd.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cleverly designed roguelite with a lot of good ideas. One of my favorite things about this game is how it is forcing you to regularly make small risk versus reward decisions. These decisions are small as to not overwhelm, and they manage to introduce a level of strategy to runs not often seen in other games of the genre. The game is also seamlessly polished in its mechanics. Because of this, controls and player movement never feel like they are adding unnecessary difficulty.These things would be enough to merit a good roguelite, but on top of all of this the game has a shocking amount of really fun enemies and hazards. Every area has a distinct feel to it both graphically and mechanically. This helps runs from becoming tiring, as you are always adapting to your surroundings. I strongly recommend you give it a go!

_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: I really was in the center of whether I wanted to recommend or not recommend this game. Long story short: Art, Music is Amazing, While IMO the design makes the game not fun.Starting out I wanna say I've never played the OG Shovel Knight game so starting out, something I don't like about the game is just the general movement and input. It's floaty to accommodate you being able to jump attack shovel blocks I believe and this would all be pretty fine if the game is built around that part. To me here is where the game ruins itself. So the movement is made to one type of gameplay, for me it's like a flow type game where you have to time jumps and attacks to get more loot, you have one shot to get it right and that is cool. And this part feels great. It can get harder by preset enemies on the ground you have to avoid or move around. So far so good, if this was the game I think it would be more fun. But instead, random enemies spawn so you can't stay in one area too long or make it so you have something to bounce off to jump higher. Sounds good on paper on these parts. But in reality, these enemies break the flow mentioned above. Suddenly you have to stop or suddenly two random enemies move in a way so you can't avoid damage. Roguelikes like these are supposed to be hard, no one would say otherwise. But in games like Enter the Gungeon you always take damage cause YOU screw up or miss the window of a dodge. This game has no dodge, it's hit, jump or use an item. And here is where another problem rears its head. Hitboxes. Your “slash” is your own height and nothing more. You can’t hit upwards (Unless you get a random drop item that lets you super mario jump into blocks above). This leads to many times you take damage even if you feel like you should have dealt the damage instead. Like you jump to slash an enemy but you were just  a bit under/above and the enemy now moved into you and you take damage instead. This is something that I can say ofc all games have happen. But when it happens more often than you imagine, then it doesn't feel so good. And the game doesn't feel hard, it just feels “artificially hard”. To give an example, I feel like the game has the seed of the same feeling of movement Hollow Knight has. You know the tight timed jumping etc. But in Hollow knight it never feels BS when you slash, you slash and bounce off taking no damage. You will probably hit the enemy when you mean to and you will see that when you screw up your input you missed and the damage you took feels certified. I feel like this game could benefit from having the “slash” hitbox for enemies being bigger than you above and below. So you hit when you mean to. Will the game be easier? YES, but I don’t think anyone wants a game that is hard in a way where it’s just not fun. Like in Elden Ring when you get into a boss room and instead of a new guy to beat it’s just two previous bosses slapped together and you get like cheesy stunlocked by two guys insta killing you. That’s not fun hard gameplay, that is the “jumpscare” of hard gameplay. It’s simple, and lacks depth for hard skill based gameplay. In the later stages this problem becomes worse with more things added to the level in what feels like just jumbles with too many weird mechanics that don't feel right for the game (IMO). Almost to the point of feeling like Mario Maker levels with random damage. For example and this might be a spoiler as it's about what the different stages themes are so I'll mark it as one if you still wanna play it.  Without spoilers I'll say that something fun that can happen is enemies hitting you off screen from either below or above or through a wall. Some enemies drop a project that falls. And if you fall with it, it never disappears. Why is that a problem? Well you see if it just so happens to fall with you and hit an item be it a key or something without being too specific... the item breaks. So that's fun... I guess? Getting “deep” (far) into the game sometimes just feels like luck, where you get like damage resist rings and suddenly can just breeze through the levels no issue as you don’t have to care for almost anything. It’s like your skill of the game weighs so little over just getting good loot. The loot should help you ofc, but in other roguelikes it’s there to make the runs feel different and sometimes you can get breeze items in like Enter The Gungeon, but it always feels like you could still be able to win on fair ground and still have fun. That is not the case here for me. When you get to deeper layers without loot the game just gets no fun harder. It's so weird... I really really wanted to like this game so much. And I do on some fronts like the game a lot. The Art is just really really amazing, some of the best Pixel art I've seen. The music is great, The character design is great. Even as I said, when the game design feels right it feels good. But that's just it, it doesn't feel good all the time. As a matter of fact it doesn't for me at least a majority of the time. For me, to make this a good game, a major overhaul of the games enemy and player movement design has to be done. And I really can’t see such a big change happening. Closing out I wanna say, you might like this game, but I think looking at other reviews, chance is that you might also not like this game just as much. I'd say give the game a go and get your own opinion, maybe get a refund if you after 50 mins say not for me.

Reaching the end is not gonna take you long but the potential is there to always have a good time while launching a new run. As long as you don't expect endless grindy progression ... _childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a fun little roguelite that fans of the original will probably get a kick out of. The difficulty curve is kinda wack and the zoomed-in camera was the cause of a few cheap deaths, but overall, it's Shovel Knight goodness stuffed into a neat roguelite package. However, it does run VERY short for its price point; I was able to finish a run in about 6 hours, only a few more to get the true ending, and beyond that there's not much else to do. I'm not a "$$$ = hours played" type of guy, but it makes it hard to fully recommend Shovel Knight Dig. _childDocuments_.review: (to anyone who wants to buy this game in hopes of seeing Donovan and Luan come back, they're not here, sorry, they're planning to make a dlc tho, dunno what's gonna be in it)Oh boy, it pains me to write this review since I love the Shovel Knight franchise with all my heart, but this just isn't a good game :(I'll just list what bothered me:> the game is incredibly short, given the price> there are two endings, regular and true; reaching the true ending is absolutely ridiculous - the list of things you need to do is so specific and difficult that I feel like there's almost no way you could figure it out without looking it up> after I finished it once I didn't feel the need to explore, there was nothing that made me want to come back - it'd be better if there was a reason to keep going back into the well, like maybe instead of a campsite there could be a village and you unlock new buildings, from which you can learn some lore (that's just off the top of my head), but this might be just a little pet peeve of mine> this game is meant to be a prequel, but it barely explains the character motivations, there's little to no character development, and their personalities are just not very well explored (especially shovel and shield); the story in itself feels kinda bland, unlike the previous titlesHere's the stuff I liked tho:> graphics are pretty good, I liked the ones in Pocket Dungeon more but these are still cute> music is great, obvi> Mole Knight's design was really cool> some boss fights were fun> actually using the shovel to move around in a digging-based environment is an amazing concept> the new villains were fun and varied, I liked that you could meet them later at the campsite> those tentacles in the bag sections were really juicy, yumTo summarize, if this game was like $5-$10 I probably wouldn't have been as salty. _childDocuments_.review: Listen, I love the idea of a Shovel Knight platformer roguelike. Really, I do. Plus, transitioning to a top-down design sounds like a no-brainer for letting the shovel-drop and new digging mechanic shine. But, bottom line is, this game isn't fun.To be fair, this game has its moments. It goes without saying how gorgeous the 16-bit transition is, as well as the new characters and rogues gallery having superb designs. Plus, the true ending is very climactic and might be one of my favorite sequences in a Shovel Knight campaign, period. But, these periods of brevity are often overshadowed by run-ending bugs, poor game-design choices, and an overall frustrating journey. While the team has been doing their best to patch the sea of softlocks they've received (some of which I reported), a lot of my problems are with the game's design itself. Just spitballing a few of my complaints: - Having insta-kill obstacles appearing in every world (non-drill spikes) - Almost half of the accessories being either useless or actively detrimental - The bottom half of the screen taking up so much space that fly enemies from above come out of nowhere, - Shops not spawning for whole WORLDS due to rng - Having tight pockets of time to react when falling contrasted by having no option to backtrack - Only some bosses doing the same damage as drill spikes (2) despite needing to get close to attack them - Random boss room generation making the fight's difficulty very unreliable (either commit to having spikes in Spore Knights room each run or remove it)I get that most of my issues can be chalked up to a skill issue or something you just learn to deal with, but I'd rather have consistency rather than peaks and valleys of playthroughs. Sometimes, it's really fun if you have enough item luck and get the few broken accessories in the game. Most times, you get bent over by bad luck, with whether you win or lose feeling out of your control at some points. If you want a fun Shovel Knight game, replay literally any TT campaign. If you want a Shovel Knight roguelike, play Pocket Dungeon. If you want to sour your mood, play Dig.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this one. I LOVED the original Shovel Knight, loved every single entry in the Treasure Trove series. This game has a confused design. It expects you to play meticulously (life refills are relatively precious, keys and eggs require perfect play (they are dropped and/or destroyed when you take damage)), but then there is constant pressure to play quickly, because if you're too slow an unkillable enemy spawns in above you until you run away. The game constantly doles out cheap sources of damage (ranged enemies, enemies who actively and constantly move outside your attack range, flying enemies, enemies that suddenly appear from the foreground/background with little warning, traps everywhere that are often hard to see, traps that feel virtually unavoidable, traps that are sometimes literally unavoidable when placed in conjunction with the aforementioned enemies, etc.), but then the game requires you to choose between health and upgrades, and bars you from getting other upgrades if you drop your keys or eggs. So many of the upgrades provide incredibly minor (or even actively unhelpful) boosts that collecting money to buy them feels like a chore. As others have mentioned, it feels like it rewards luck more than skilled playing; this would be fine if the game itself was fun to play, but sadly, it's not. The spritework is gorgeous. The music, shockingly, is okay at best, despite the original Treasure Trove series being stuffed head-to-toe with fantastic and memorable tracks. The story feels like an afterthought and the dialogue is just serviceable; expect to read the exchange between the MC and the first few bosses over and over and over and over and over, because nobody bothered to write more than a few sentences of pre-fight dialogue but the game doesn't just skip these lines either, so you have to mash through it every time. It's just another annoyance in a game already heaped with seemingly intentionally annoying design choices.Every moment in the original Shovel Knight is pure platforming bliss. This feels like a cheap, soulless imitation. Yacht Club can keep my money but I will be very careful before jumping into their next game without reading a lot of reviews first.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what proved to me that Yacht Club still knows how to make video games. The original Shovel Knight was a masterpiece, and is to this day one of my favorite games of all time. Because of how great original Shovel Knight was, I tried to continue to follow the developers, but their next games were just very mediocre in my opinion and not very fun. With Dig however, I can say that Yacht Club has made another great game. I've tried reading some of the negative reviews, but I really don't think the majority of them are justified as being negative, as they either only list a few small nitpicks and completely disregard all the great things in this game, or just say things that I flat out disagree with. For example, I see people complaining about a softlock which alone brings their review to a negative, or I see people complaining about clunky movement, which it may seem like when you first start up, but if you play a few runs you'll find it to be quite the opposite. Honestly, what I think is happening is that when these people saw Dig was going to be on mobile, they immediately assumed it would be super easy because "mobile games are easy" and got frustrated when they found this "easy" game to be difficult. Sure, they did simplify down the moveset a bit to work with phones, but it is still a very tight and challenging experience. If you liked original Shovel Knight, this is similar to that but with a more arcade-style feel. Not as good as the original, but it lives up to the Shovel Knight name well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is shovel knight same moves*, same awesome soundtrack, and... wait, what's that hole over ther-SHOVEL KNIGHT DIG! instead of a high quality precision platformer that is the original, with DIG you have an ok semi-random vertical platformer version of shovel knight that is frustrating within 15 minutes. You see, the game is designed around going downward (digging into the earth literally, clever), this was done by outright forcing you to go down as quick as possible by making the jump forcibly break platforms, and a screen crush if you take too long in a stage. When you die you go back to the start of the world (3 levels a world, with a bunch of variant levels branching from the start of a "run") and spend your gems in a shop for a myriad of items both useful and not that you can find randomly in the levels below, and some stat upgrades that are permanent. Some of these items are keys that let you go to special rooms and paths that can take you to more treasure, item shops, or relic rooms when you take them to the specific door without getting hit. The problem with this? Every challenging section of this game is built on throwing digging machines at you that have spikes sticking out the side or a platform challenge that you can fail because:- You automatically dig down by jumping. - While being forced to play the game quickly. - And you can't get hit. - And the stages aren't guaranteed to have the key or door in any specific area.It's frustrating to say the least, and I only played it for 25 minutes. It's a good game that is so frustrating that I don't want to even play it. So I refunded it, I wouldn't bother with it if you were hoping for more Shovel Knight, because it's an entirely different game in execution. I like every single idea this game has, but the execution is a bit spotty, and I have enough games in the backlog to just not bother with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Most roguelites extend replayability with lots of variety in character builds (Dead Cells), giving the player permanent upgrades that can be set against increasing challenges (Enter the Gungeon), and ongoing character development (Hades does all three)This has none of that and gets dull FAST. There are a few tweaks but you're basically descending the same cavern with a shovel every time, and it quickly gets stale. As with other roguelikes, procedural map generation doesn't really create variety.Stark contrast from Shovel Knight, where the amazing DLC gave players wildly new and interesting experiences. I do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Grindy, overly-pressured, and kinda weird. I'd really call it more of an arcade game than a roguelike, just because of how much the game seems to push you to move quickly, and how low-impact most of the power-ups are.So far, I've seen a total of four sources of metaprogression:1. A relic-shop which unlocks relics for you to find in-run (but doesn't start you with them). None of the relics are really inspiring; it's all stuff like 'ignore damage from bombs' or 'jump higher'.2. A merchant who sells keys that unlock challenge areas, which, when completed, unlock active items. The merchant also sells inventory capacity, although the price rapidly skyrockets.3. A gravestone with achievements on it, which unlocks extra inventory for one extremely rare merchant encounter.4. Shortcuts. Who even uses shortcuts in roguelikes? If people actually feel a need to use the shortcuts, then you've done something wrong.There's also a spot for an armorer, once you find him, but I doubt he's any more interesting.Honestly speaking, I was expecting something like Steamworld Dig based on the title and what I saw of the mechanics, but it's, really just 'go downwards and fight stuff'. There's no subtlety, no strategy, and nothing really interesting. There's little to no variance between runs at all.To the good, the actual platforming feels solid, but that's probably just because it's built on the same engine as the other Shovel Knight games. And... that's about all I can say that's good about it. The bits that were re-used from the original Shovel Knight games are good. Everything that /wasn't/ reused from those games is... lackluster. It feels like neither Yacht Club nor Nitrome bothered to try and understand what makes a roguelike good or bad, instead just assuming that they could toss a bunch of their existing IP into a big pot with some procedural generation.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really needs a 'Meh' recommendation.As expected for Shovel Knight, great music and visuals, but it doesn't really work as a roguelike/lite in its current form.Maybe could be salvaged with more areas and a lot more relic/modifiers that much much much more substantially affect the gameplay but as is, it's not really worth the price. One of the best parts of roguelikes is getting modifiers that synthesize or otherwise start to break the game's systems, but this doesn't seem to reach that critical mass at any point. Maybe it does much later, but if so it's a different problem that it requires so much of a grind to get there.Update: Just finished the game. Same opinion. Ran into some more bugs, which was annoying, one of which soft-locked me after beating a boss. Also, I grew to dislike the lack of maneuverability more and more as the game went on, which made it all the more frustrating each time I missed a jump by a tiny bit and missed out on getting a gear. Also, I get that it's random but it was really annoying to so often find keys right after passing locked doors or eggs just after passing nest rooms (and then not seeing another of either for such a long time later).As before, I think it would be a lot better with more levels/artifacts/modifiers/etc, and if some of the current per-run modifiers were moved over to a progression system (e.g., higher jump). Or keep them as they are but allow the player to equip some subset before starting a run. As is, it's less challenging and just more annoying. I just don't think Shovel Knight's brand of platforming really lends itself well to this style of game. Alright overall, but still much too short (especially for the price point) and too light on the "rogue" to really recommend as a roguelike/lite. Would love to revisit if some more meat was added.Update update: Just saw that this game is also on mobile. That explains a looot (and I think dashes any hopes of them fixing the things I don't like). Good on them for making and selling an actual game on mobile, but it's too bad that it's probably a good mobile game instead of a great game, period.
