_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic graphics. Good controls. Nicely design semi-random levels. Cleverly indicated secret paths that are just tricky enough to spot with the fast paced gameplay. The digging mechanism feels like a throwback to the games with focused concepts of old (e.g. Bubble Bobble, Qwak, Ice Climber), though it plays more like a normal platformer than those games, but with a unique touch.Difficulty-wise, I think it feels like the game is fair, though some hitboxes could maybe be a bit more generous in the players favor (e.g. some spikes at edges etc).I see many reviews complain about the short length, luckily I seem to suck a bit at the game.I think I may have reached the last stage at 9 hours, which might be a bit weak on my part. There are alternate paths (e.g. inspired choices like the fire world or water world etc.), giving some variety on repeated runs. I guess a  may keep playing past completion for leaderboards etc.It's been too long since I played the original to compare them fairly, but I'm starting to grow a bit tired of regular retro platformers, so for me the change of style was definitely a good thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be a no-brainer buy at $14 (and I would change my review if it switched to that price), but they've managed to find a price point that makes the game not feel good to buy. Within my first run, I immediately started keeping track of the refund window because I felt uncertain. In my time playing, I beat the first boss and got pretty far into two areas that came after, but I just felt like I was neither making enough meta progression to give this game a stronger narrative vibe nor was I enjoying runs enough to really get sucked into the "one more run" mindset too heavily. When I first heard the title for the game, I was hoping it would be slightly more "Mr. Driller," but it ends up feeling like a very terrestrial Downwell. Downwell does a good job of keeping you moving with a challenge, but this game doesn't really know if it wants to leverage its verticality all that seriously and doesn't balance the overall "staging" of each level's progression. It's almost like a platformer rogue like where each room is below the next, but it also wants you to think it's a vertical digging game. The problem is that it makes both combat and digging not feel as fun as they should be.

_childDocuments_.review: So a lot of the negative reviews for the game are due to this game being very different from Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove. If you are expecting another indie platformer, you will be disappointed. I know I was at first. But if you can appreciate the game for what it is, it's a lot of fun, with some drawbacks. The graphics are great, the music is great, and the gameplay is great. The magic system has changed for the better, where the relic you are using has a maximum number of uses that is displayed rather than each relic having a different cost to use. I think the levels are a lot of fun and the boss levels are challenging but not impossible. My recommendation for the easiest route is Spore Knight -> Tinker Knight -> Hive Knight. The new knights are also a lot of fun. I do think, however, that the game lacks the same replayability as I was hoping. I beat the game once, and the prospect of finding all the armor schematics and purchasing all the upgrades isn't as exciting to me as it was in Treasure Trove. Overall, I think this game is a good addition to the Shovel Knight series, but I'm looking forward more to a direct/proper sequel to Treasure Trove in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die-hard Shovel Knight fan and a strong roguelike fan, the game often feels overly punishing. Not in a satisfying difficulty way, in a clumsy frustrating 'shut the game off and play something else' kinda way. Which... is a shame.Admitted, I've barely gotten through the game but I don't really have the drive to see it through either, and I think that speaks volumes of a greater issue. Shovel Knight as a series has always been punishing to some degree, it's ingrained in it's old school platforming DNA, but when paired with Dig's roguelike approach and a lack of tangible progress, restarting runs can feel both disheartening and demotivating, all of your momentum essentially has been lost.I don't think there's any way to improve your starting layout, only purchase options and different items to encounter, though I have no real desire to find out if I'm wrong about that. I'd feel at least some motivation if I had a goal to work towards with permanent upgrades and gold. I'm ashamed to admit I even had to enable the health difficulty handicap for more consistent runs and progress.Lastly, and I noticed this almost immediately in my first hour, but by the game's philosophy of downwards progression a lot of the enemies will generally force you to move down to avoid them, which in a bubble is good game design, but in practice when combined with precision platforming and a lack of upwards swing or any shovel range, combat against enemies in my opinion feels one sided as flying enemies can easily rush you down and put you in a position where you're either forced to take platforming damage or enemy damage. It just doesn't ever feel good. I can't express enough how badly I want to say I "dig" Shovel Knight Dig, Shovel Knight Treasure Trove is probably my favourite game and Dig's art direction and music is as good as ever, but the gameplay, the most important part? I personally can't get behind it. If I were to summarize how it feels to play Dig, imagine you're playing a modern platformer but almost every quality of life change we've made in the past 10 years has been functionally removed and then added as a purchasable upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: Review by Unam Shovel Knight: Dig is a spin-off of the original shovel knight. This is most relevantly seen with the art style, as this game chooses to adopt a 16-bit style over the original's 8-bit. This may lead the player to believe that this is an evolution of the series, but it's not. Although I liked the game it has some flaws that keep it from being great. Unlike the original games, Shovel Knight: Dig is more of a Roguelike than a platformer. I like the shift in the genre, it's not often that an established series switches gameplay genre, and I welcome the change. The gameplay revolves around going digging down to rescue your treasure. Along your journey, you'll visit five different areas with different dangers, where each room appears to be randomly generated. Along your journey, you'll meet NPCs that can give you items to aid in your expedition or abilities that make things easier in a specific situation. In each room, you'll be able to collect three gears which are usually in a tricky spot, but if you manage to get all of them you'll be able to choose between refilling your health or obtaining a free ability, which pushes the player to explore the world. After completing three rooms of an area, you'll have to fight a boss, which is not particularly hard. Like any other Roguelike, it's not expected that the player beats the game on their first try, as the experience gets easier the more you play the game, as there are some permanent unlocks that can make certain scenarios easier. If you're not exploring the caves then you'll probably be talking to NPCs or buying stuff. There is not much to do up there apart from talking and buying, so there is that. The graphics are really pretty. Shovel Knight: Dig looks the best out of any in the series, and it still retains its characteristic trait and is pulled off to an excellent degree. Again, if you like the other games or any Roguelike games, you'll find something to enjoy here, but...The game is not flawless. For its price, there is not much to do here. Like I said, It took me 5 hours to beat the game, which for a Roguelike is fine, however, my biggest problem is that there is not much replay value. Sure, you can go down again and unlock everything, but there is no incentive to do so. The rooms can start to be redundant you'll start to get bored of the game, which is against the principles of a Roguelike. For a successful Roguelike, the player should be able to keep enjoying the game even after having three hundred hours or having everything unlocked, which is something that does not apply to the game. The game itself is semi-cheap, so it doesn't hurt you that much if you want to try it. As previously stated, Shovel Knight: Dig is a new step for the series. I enjoyed my time with it, and I like the new art style as it retains the charm of the original games. It has a few flaws, most prominent is the boring gameplay loop, but for a few hours, the game is a lot of fun.  I give Shovel Knight: Dig a...

But in the best interest of any potential buyers, I'll try.This is *NOT* anything like Shovel of Hope.  This felt more like an attempt to deliver as many hours of game play, regardless of how stale they feel, per dollar as they possibly can.  Levels are randomly generated, frustrating, and annoying.  The level design polish that made other Shovel Knight games truly shine, is entirely absent.  Don't get me wrong, the artwork and animation are top notch.  However, they entirely missed the mark on the *feel* of the game by substituting interesting levels with this "hamster wheel crap" so ubiquitous in video games these days.Buyer beware, this is not Shovel Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's balancing is frankly terrible. From other reviews, it seems like difficulty is all over the place. Some people say they beat the game stupid quickly, meanwhile I'm over 25 hours in as of the time of this review and STILL haven't been able to beat the game at all, regardless of which ending.First off, having 0 real permanent unlocks is lame as ♥♥♥♥. I know it's a roguelike but no unlockables other than a few sets of useless armors deincentivizes a good bit of replayability. The only armor that I even bother with is the one that provides more durability and allows you to hold one item after defeat, but even that's imperfect because it only allows you to pick an item out of 3 options in your inventory regardless of how many items you've accumulated, it's just lame.The feature to skip to certain levels in the main plaza is, similarly to most of the aforementioned armor, useless. You don't get to enter with any items and it'll pretty much not allow you to get the true ending if you decide you wanna go to too far in of a level.Also besides all that, there's just some real cheap design. Sometimes enemies will just appear out of f*cking nowhere and hurt you, some offshoots you expect to have shops or chests will have useless NPCs that don't give you anything, or even worse, NPCs that will turn randomly into enemies. It's bs and entirely up to RNG, when these shouldn't even be here to begin with. It's cheap design, simply put.On the brightside, there's a good bit to love here. Dig controls even better than Shovel of Hope in my opinion. The basic shovel swing can be repeated faster, Shovel Knight feels just a tad less slippery, and everything is just super tight. Just be sure to turn off the auto-shovel bounce in options.Music is fantastic as always courtesy of Jake Kaufman, the goat who did Shantae's music (My fav work of his) and unlike Treasure Trove, he doesn't gotta limit his music to chiptune here, really let loose and it slaps.The graphics are more 32-bit Sega Saturn-y this time around in style than 8-bit like Treasure Trove which is, again, like the music, an upgrade in my opinion. Ngl the updated visual style is actually why I checked this game out b4 Shovel of Hope.Story is good too. A prequel to Shovel of Hope that connects well and is just comfy, made Shield Knight my fav character lmao. Too bad the story is so hard to fully experience firsthand cuz of the unfair RNG and sending the player ALL the way back to the start of the game if they die :/All that said, for every thing Dig does right, it does 2 things wrong. If you want a more rewarding roguelike from the series, go play Shovel Knight: Pocket Dungeon. Shame this game is only ok, cuz an action roguelike with Shovel Knight platforming gameplay sounds brilliant on paper.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight tries its hand at being a roguelike, and it's pretty fun!  If you're skilled at platformers, you'll probably be able to get your first clear in under 3 hours, which isn't bad at all, although it will probably take you somewhere between 10 and 15 hours before you've gotten the true ending and seen everything.I fear that Shovel Knight Dig is getting mixed reviews because it occupies something of a niche space and doesn't appeal strongly to any one specific audience.  Rogue fans may be a bit disappointed because the game features very little meta-progression; you can unlock new accessories and abilities to find in the dungeon, and you can also unlock a handful of different suits of armor that you can start with, but otherwise there is very little powering-up that you can do between runs.  Player skill and knowledge makes all the difference here.  On the other hand, for more traditional Roguelike fans, they may be a little disappointed in the lack of variety.  After you've played through the game a few times, you'll probably have experienced all of the different types of enemies and traps the game can throw at you; it may vary things up a little bit, but it will rarely surprise you with anything unexpected.  And finally, for Shovel Knight fans and fans of traditional side-scrolling platformers, you'll probably be disappointed by the capricious nature of the game and the relatively short length if your goal is just to complete it once and then be done with it.If you're looking for a game that is somewhere in the middle of all those, though, you'll be pleased to find a solidly-crafted roguelike platformer with some very light elements of progression that don't massively or permanently alter the difficulty, and it has gorgeous graphics and great music to boot.  There's enough randomness to keep you on your toes, but with patience, you can learn the right way to handle any situation.  Compared to the older Shovel Knight games, there are new characters, new enemies, new abilities, and a cute story that gives a few more details about Shovel Knight and Shield Knight's history together.  If that sounds at all interesting to you, it's at least worth trying it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a genuinely upsetting game to me. The original was incredible because it was one of the best traditional platformers the genre had seen in years. The incredibly careful curation of the level design stuck it out like a six-foot tall sore thumb in a crowd that already wasn't very big to begin with. It sat as proof that a well-designed platformer will always beat the roguelike genre in moment-to-moment game-play, filling your time with a rewarding experience that respects the player by having an ending. I was so excited for the follow up to the Treasure Trove, as since it's release the roguelike genre has bloated the platformer scene. It was gonna be really nice to get a new game that wasn't bloody procedurally genreated.And then the press release showed the next in the series would be a roguelite platformer with castlevania items, biomes and semi-permanent upgrades.I didn't touch it for over a year for that reason. Curiousity got the better of me though, and I found a key for it on ♥♥♥. And I tried to like it, I really did, but the components of this game make the entire vision of it feel AI-generated. it's exactly like Spelunky, it's exactly like dead cells, it's painfully similar to Noita, and Exit the Gungeon, and all the other popular roguelike sidescrollers. They all blend together because you don't finish a roguelike, you burn out from it. The original Shovel Knight knew this and ignored the roguelike concept for that very reason. Shovel Knight Dig isn't a bad roguelike, it's a familiar one. It's the entry that made Shovel Knight a series, and frustratingly it's the first in the series to alienate the core concepts that make it compelling. If you like roguelikes, you'll probably like this one. I'm not sure how many times a developer can put a new coat of paint on what is essentially the videogame equivalent of Sisyphus, but Shovel Knight is now one of those coats of paint. Please, for the love of god, don't buy this, unless you really want studios to crank out more of these bloody procedurally generated games. that was one hell of a stream of consciousness.

_childDocuments_.review: The team seem to have forgotten everything fun about shovel knight. The fundamental mechanics are setup in such a way as to make the game feel frustrating and not fun. In Shovel Knight once you had a powerup it was there with you forever, and as a result you felt like you were progressing with each run. In this dungheap however, the mechanics serve to make you feel crappy for ever caring enough to play the game. I'm sure the team put real effort into this one, but the roguelike randomly generated rooms feel uninspired and repetitive, and very often situations will arise that are impossible to avoid damage from. Again compare this to the sharp well designed levels of shovel knight and you start to think their mechanic designer doesn't understand how to make enjoyable games anymore. It just doesn't feel good to play this game, and I suspect Yaught Club now has more money than talent in the studio, and it's killed their creativity.

I've purchased most of their games, and I dont regret supporting them in the least, as everything they do is unique and interesting to me, but none have held my attention for long. _childDocuments_.review: I won this game during Yacht Club Gaming's Shovel Knight 10th Anniversary stream, and I must say, I adore it. The art, music, and gameplay are phenomenal. While I understand the game launched with some bugs, my experience was completely smooth with not a single technical fault. However, that doesn't mean there aren't areas for improvement. The gameplay is just as challenging as the Shovel Knight Treasure Trove, with even higher stakes. You can spend 20 minutes on a run, only to be sent back to the beginning by one false move. Additionally, there's no substantial way to make your character more powerful over time, aside from some armor and adding variety to the Well. There are numerous options to increase the game's difficulty, though. I'm proud to say I've completed everything the game has to offer and enjoyed it despite these criticisms.The biggest flaw, however, is the 'true ending.' It involves a significant amount of RNG, and the run itself is more than twice as long as a traditional run. You can spend almost an hour on it, only to stumble at the last second, which is infuriating. Hopefully, the upcoming DLC will address this.For fans of Shovel Knight and those seeking a challenge, I can't recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointment.  This game is deliberate in it's unbalanced design.  It is unbalanced to conceal it's low replay ability and how short the game is.  That might have worked for SNES era games, but should not be the case in a Roguelite.By deliberate,  I mean the game is "well-designed" (not scuffed) in it's traps and baits, and in creating situations in which you will get damaged no matter what, but I am using the word deliberate because I do not think it's good game design.  For instance, hidden walls you blow up will hide enemies or high damaging spikes which defies game logic.   Deliberate platforming traps that effectively one-shot your character and make you throw a complete run.   You use a low health weak character that you cannot upgrade, and the game has deliberate instant situations designed to damage you.   In a fire area sometimes there are multiple missile spewing enemies out of hit range that will burn complete section.  It is baffling how  many times you can see miles away you're getting damaged and you can do nothing about it but take it.  This game demands precision but does not reward it.   In terms of game progression, there are no permanent upgrades. Shovel Knight usually learn multiple moves, but in here, you forget them on death.  All artifacts or skills you find in runs are inconsequential and you lose them.  No perm health upgrade.  Other than unlocking this is not really a rogue-like.   So all the money and unlocks except for armors are a waste of time.  The game loop simply involves Vanilla runs from the start and praying that you do not get bad RNG with enemy placement and if you do, that you are able to collect all 3 cogs so you can fully heal.The exception being the red slash armor.  This gives you more damage, takes half your HP when you get damage but it's scuffed when you finish a section it autoheals the HP it took.  So once unlocked, this is the armor you will always use as you do more damage if unharmed and heal a bit upon ending the run. What is frustrating here is that the game has a great foundation and deliberate designs,  it is obvious the devs could have made a  great game.  Instead of doing more content, more stages, more instances,  and do a better game they decided to deliberately inflate game hours by making this unfair and cheap to play deliberate design.At $20 plus, you're better off playing any goood rouguelite below that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like Downwell and Shovel Knight (2014) had a baby. It's a really good Roguelike, and I highly recommend it.Most of the reviews I'm reading remind me of that one game reporter that had to review a Roguelike for a company, only to complain in their review about all the aspects of what makes a Roguelike a Roguelike (probably because they hadn't played one before). Roguelikes are unforgiving, just taking too long on a puzzle/segment in this game alone kills you. You're gonna die in this game a lot... but that's sorta the point. You're supposed to die a lot (every time you die you complete a "run"). You earn in-game currency every run, which helps you unlock temporary/permanent power-ups so that you can get a little farther on consecutive runs. That's the game-play loop of this and most other Roguelikes. Unlike the original 2D-Platform game this Roguelike draws some of its inspiration from, this game focuses more on vertical scrolling movement wherein going back up isn't an option.Some folk out there do not enjoy having a character with several power-ups, weapons, and helpers die to a flimsy mistake on the third level of a game, only to have to start over from scratch with nothing. I'm not one of those folk(s), and if you aren't either then: this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an option to vote maybe instead of either yes or no 'cuz Shovel Knight Dig is a VERY interesting game, but it's also a flawed experience, as someone who really enjoys the original Treasure Trove saga and is a massive sidescroller rogue-like addict.I was initially hyped for this game upon its first announcement back in early 2022, and was anticipating its release date. I got the game on Switch at launch initially (due to portability at the time), but only decided to get the PC port recently due to certain features that the Switch version apparently lacks the extra gameplay features + the extra song (for some reason), which I don't get why. I dunno if other console ports lacked these things, but it's something that kinda irks me the wrong way when that happens.I think the overall structure is really neat, and I do enjoy the more old-school hardcore approach to this rogue-like compared to other sidescroller rogue-likes of this type, but it's VERY luck heavy and unforgiving. Also, the camera can sometimes be a li'l ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with enemies sometimes appearing from the top *stares deeply at the white flying things in Mushroom Mines*. Even combat is finicky as Shovel Knight has knock-back anytime he swings his shovel at an enemy, which is not only weird since it never was like that in Shovel Of Hope, but it makes fighting enemies a bit awkward.Also, the Mushroom Mines is surprisingly one of the more difficult stages in the game, and it's the first one you go through. Even the Secret Fountain and Smeltworks are much easier to digest in comparison. I'm not just talking about the room with the massive drills, the white flying things, the spike placement, etc. Only thing that could make it arguably easier than the 2nd wave of stages is the boss.The main reason why I still play this game and was willing to get it twice in spite of its flaws is because I enjoy the gameplay loop and digging through dirt in the right fashion is always satisfying, especially when you're rewarded with gems after digging in a certain way. I honestly think it's a fun Shovel Knight game on its own, but it's not a particularly great rogue like. Not bad, but definitely could've been better executed.P.S. Jake Kaufman can take my money any day 'cuz my god, he went at it again with this one. Shoutouts to the Secret Fountain theme.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love Shovel Knight and love what this game tries to do, it just isn't for me. The pixel art is gorgeous, the relics are neat and the gameplay can be satisfying and fun at times. But it's just so difficult for no reason, the first level has so many hazards that don't deserve to be there, hell, I feel like there are more enemies in it than Drill Knight's Castle Stage. There's also some problems where enemies appear, in the Smeltworks, an enemy can spawn right on top of you and there's nothing you can do about it. Enemies will spawn off screen and hit you without you even being able to react. And honestly, Shovel Knight just feels weak as well, even with upgrades to his attacks, he just doesn't feel strong enough to go one on one with certain enemies and I get it, it's an uphill battle because it's a roguelite but it's just so overtuned for no reason in the slightest. Most of the hitboxes don't even make sense either, with the spiral air slash that you can purchase, it only ever attacks in front of you. It's a game of luck and you're always bound to be screwed over at some point in your run, most of the time leading to you losing because you made one tiny mistake. I'll still continue to play it and try to complete it but it is just not good.

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelikes are some of my favorite games, and among the many roguelikes I own, Shovel Knight Dig is absolutely one of the best I've played. If you've played the original Shovel Knight: Shovel of Hope game, you'll quickly find your footing, as the gameplay is quite similar, only you're going down instead of sideways, like in Downwell. Descending through the six (or seven?) levels the game offers, you'll collect gems, relics and items to help you in your quest. I think the name of the game is satisfaction: digging through dirt is quick, snappy and instantly rewarding, same for collecting gems, the sound design of which enhances the experience tenfold. You'll be left with that "One More Run" feeling after every failed attempt that truly sets good roguelikes aside from the others. To put it simply, it's as if a classic game like Mega Man or Castlevania was remade to fit in a roguelike setting, and it's definitely an incredibly experience. Cannot recommend this enough!PS: I also own this game on Switch, which is a testament to how captivating the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: This "recommended" comes with a lot of major caveats. Let's get one thing out of the way first. Calling this game a Rogue-lite is misleading. There's nothing "lite" about the rogue elements of this game. When you die, no progress on levels is saved and you lose all of the loot that you gained in the level save for money and a few collectibles. There are very few permanent upgrades to make runs easier, and what is there mostly just adds more items to the pool of accessories you can get or acts as a modifier to make runs feel different. The items that you find in the dungeon itself often have very limited utility, so progressing further into the game mostly involves learning the levels, learning what items are useful, and gitting gud. There are some accessibility options to make things a bit easier, but that may or may not lessen some of the more frustrating aspects of the game. Levels are randomly generated, with all of the good and bad that comes with that. Every run is different, and even after many runs I'm still seeing new layouts in the various biomes, but that randomness also means that sometimes the game just feels like screwing you over with bad loot and shop positions. In short this is a Shovel-Knight flavored rogue-like. If everything that I've written above hasn't scared you off yet, then this game might be for you.Good points: As expected of Shovel Knight, the presentation is beautiful in terms of graphics, music and story. The levels themselves are fun to play through, hiding secret treasures, weapons, and even pets in every nook and cranny. The new biomes and bosses feel right at home in the shovel knight world, and the gameplay feels a lot like what fans of the original game have come to expect, but with a rogue-like twist as mentioned above. I'm personally not fond of procedurally generated levels as a rule, but these do a pretty good job of making each section feel fun to play, even if I think hand-crafted levels would have been better.Bad points: A lot of the items that you can buy to add to the dungeon pool seem useless except as fodder. One would think that the more useful items should have been saved for the shop as something to work toward, but it feels like they did it backwards, giving most of the really useful items to us right up front. The game also seems a bit buggy still. While I haven't noticed as many bugs and soft-locks as other users (which hopefully means they've been fixed) I did have a true-end run or two messed up by some glitches involving the items needed to get said ending. The true-ending itself is very cryptic, tedious and stupidly frustrating to get, and it can be really frustrating having a run go bad 3/4ths of the way in because of a small mistake. I've lost count of how many true end runs I've missed due to one misstep.  In short, the game does a lot of things right and a few things wrong, but overall may not be for everyone due to the nature of the genre. For people who are fans of a more difficult style of game with a side of frustration, I'd say give it a shot, but those expecting a more tailored experience similar to the original may want to think twice.

_childDocuments_.review: As of recent, I have found myself playing this game more and more as of late, both due to my own enjoyment of the base game and due to the recent QoL improvement option you can opt into. If you don't feel like reading all I have to say, I still think Shovel Knight Dig is another good entry in the Shovel Knight franchise, but with plenty of room to grow and expand in future updates. As for why, let's start with the positives.Starting off, the gameplay and level design is just as solid as ever from Yacht Club Games' titles. Teaching without pop-up tutorials, simple and satisfying controls, a tough-but-fair experience, etc. If you've played Shovel of Hope especially, you know much of what to expect in this prequel. Furthermore, the art style and music is the stuff of dreams, standing as my favorite style of Shovel Knight so far even almost a year since the game first launched, something future installments will have a difficult time topping down the line. The story, while relatively simple, is charming all the same, with a simple goal to retrieve your stolen money from the dastardly Drill Knight, with it clearly leading into the original Treasure Trove package should you face the True Ending, something I recommend anyone do, especially thanks to recent improvements to lighten the stress of getting it. The characters are incredibly memorable and expressive, from returning classics such as Chester and Tinker Knight, to those new to this title, such as Drill Knight himself and the Gastronomole. In all, this is a must-get for any Shovel Knight fan, with hours of fun and replayability baked in.That said, despite all that praise I just gave, this game isn't perfect in my eyes. Though, these can definitely be seen as nitpicks as I love this franchise to death and have played every title countless times. Firstly, the items you collect in this game run out relatively fast, with the only real purchasables being accessories, armors, and relic keys. Once you get all those, that's it and you begin amassing this massive mountain of cash that kind of just lingers on and on. On top of this, the same 6 worlds become familiar to the point where they feel much less exciting to explore and conquer. While sometimes I do see a generated room new to me, for the most part, the game does feel like it kind of...runs out of new content to share. Sure, this is inevitable in all titles, but in the end, I find myself wanting more. More items to throw in some powers, risk and reward, and uniqueness in my runs. I want new worlds to plunge into and learn top to bottom. All in all, I just want more to do, more to spend, more to experiment with. I do know that this game will be receiving future DLC updates to bring more content, though I will admit, the first one did leave a bitter taste in my and many other peoples' mouths.The dreaded Knightmare Challenges, only unlockable after you beat the True Ending and visit all 6 Worlds in one glorious run. Here, Black Knight from previous titles shows up and taunts you to face 10 difficult and challenging runs, each adding one more brutal challenge on top of the last til the finale serves as the ultimate challenge on if you've mastered the game or not. When I played it upon initial release however, I found them very RNG-dependant with a dread that the reward would not be worth it. At the time, we had a secret boss fight only at the end of Knightmare 10 with a reused boss theme and a lackluster reward. Since then, in the QoL preview, they have since eased some of the more unfair parts of the Knightmares and provided a truly good reward for putting yourself through hell and back. However, the reused track still remains and with how I remember this dreaded challenge, I may never enter the Knightmares ever again, something I'm not sure the devs intended.In conclusion, do I think Shovel Knight Dig is worth your time? Yes, of course. But, I can't help but want more from this game than any other title. Treasure Trove is complete, Pocket Dungeon already has a huge mountain of content, but Dig? I just want to see more from it all around. Something I hope the devs will provide in future updates. For now though, I recommend this mostly to returning players from Treasure Trove. If you're considering getting this as your first title, I recommend the original first and foremost.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Shovel Knight and rogue-likes both, this has been a very fun game to dig into. It feels like a mix of Dead Cells and Steamworld Dig with the Shovel Knight aesthetic and familiarity thrown onto it, so if you enjoyed those games or are a true fan of our sapphire spade-wielder, then this is right up your alley.It may seem a little difficult at first, but what rogue-like isn't? It's about building up your progression bit by bit and working towards that full potential run. Thankfully, some armor upgrades and accessory unlocks can help the game be a bit more forgiving.If I had any one complaint, it's that the "True Story" starter didn't seem too obvious to me at first. I knew I could interact with it a bit in a cute way, but I had no idea about nudging it in the right direction... Not until I looked things up elsewhere. Though perhaps one could also argue that's the nature of the beast, intended to reward inquisitive minds and the first forays into discovering this game being a  to the Treasure Trove saga.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is certainly a fun game! It has addicting roguelike gameplay, lovable familiar and new characters, and even a dope secret ending (more on that later, but don’t worry I won’t spoil it). However, though I enjoy this game greatly, there are some nitpicks I have with it.THE GOOD PARTS	Everything this game has to offer is very fun! I really enjoyed using the armourer’s hints to unlock new gear, the relic keys to find new challenge rooms, and putting together everything I learned from playing into unlocking the true ending!	Speaking of the true ending, wow it is good. I was a little upset when first playing, because going through only four areas and skipping two of the hexcavators made runs feel too short. But going through every area all in one run, and even having to do special challenges in each area felt way more in line with what I like in a roguelike. The extra lore bits were appreciated as well.	As far as general gameplay goes, it feels good! Controls are responsive, Shovel Knight moves like I would expect him to, and the digging is very satisfying. Having different levels of keys and eggs makes it genuinely feel important to not get hit sometimes!THE BAD PARTS	Unfortunately, I can’t exactly say this is an AMAZING game. My big issues are that the game is too easy, and IT DOESN’T HAVE ENOUGH CONTENT TO BE WORTH 25 DOLLARS. Don’t get me wrong, as I said before it is still very fun, but…25 dollars? For what is essentially a glorified mobile game? Nitrome has made plenty of FREE mobile games before that were just as fun as Shovel Knight Dig, so why does this one have to be so expensive?	As far as difficulty goes, ehhh. I beat everything the game had to offer in roughly 7 hours. That’s not a lot of time for a roguelike that’s been being hyped up for a few years now. Most runs can be completely cheesed by some of the relics. War horn does four damage, covers a MASSIVE part of the screen, clears out dirt, makes gears and gems fall to the floor, and magic isn’t even hard to refill. On one of my runs, I managed to get 70 war horn blasts stocked up, making the game a total pushover. Even the true ending path isn’t very hard, with the exception of maybe the bomb puzzle (which doesn’t even feel hard due to real skill, often times it came down to whether or not I got a good room/enemy layout).CONCLUSION	All in all, I still recommend this game. Just try to get it when it’s on sale for at least half off. As I said, it is a very fun game, but without very much content to offer, I don’t think it’s worth more than 10 or 15 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, man, I really had high hopes for this. Shovel Knight with roguelike elements? Right up my alley. However, for a game about digging there's not much depth….sorry. And honestly, most of the relics and other items are rather useless. The only purpose I found for the money was for unlocking a shortcut to get to the end quicker, which happened waaaay too quickly for the price of this game, especially compared to games like Hades that have so much more to offer. I will say the graphics and music are great, but this is a total let down for fans of Shovel Knight or anyone looking for a roguelike fix after Rogue Legacy 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a very good rougelike game, and an excellent addition to the Shovel knight series.Shovel Knight Dig's game play is a downward moving rougelike platformer, in which shovel knight digs down to the bottom of drill knights mining expadition, to save his bag and the collapse of the earth!Pros:-The game is quite fun-There is lots of content per run, leading to many different runs with very different outcomes-The randomly generated nature of the game leads the game to not get old-The games art and music is incredibleCons:-If you are good at rougelikes this game can be beaten quite quickly without as much challenge-There are only 3 new knights out of the 6 (not including mole knights new fish design)-Some of the hints for different parts of the game can be a bit too cryptic,(There are more pros and cons but want to keep review short)Overall I would reccomend this game for shovel knight, and rougelike fans.

_childDocuments_.review: The only word I have for this is disappointing. Far, far too difficult, and not for fun reasons. Not least of all the fact that the true ending is a massive, convoluted mess to get, and not even remotely worth your time.As a prequel to Shovel Knight, it's alright, and if you like brutally frustrating roguelikes it's your thing, I suppose, but as someone who has loved all of Yacht Club Games' catalogue so far, this is just depressing.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight Dig is a solid platformer with amazing visuals, sounds, and boss fights. However, there are some major issues that prevent me from really enjoying this game.The original Shovel Knight has a "shovel drop" move that allows you to bounce off enemies and dirt while jumping, and Shovel Knight dig builds the entire gameplay experience around this mechanic; every jump results in a shovel drop. This is problematic  because it forces you to bounce off any dirt or enemies you collide with, which results in you taking damage from enemies that are chasing you from above. This problem is also made worse with another mechanic in the game: a giant drill that chases you from above if you are moving too slowly.The giant drill is a creative mechanic that applies pressure in an otherwise relaxed situation; it forces you to make decisions quickly on where to go and what to grab and allows you to become a better decision-maker in the process. However, since the drill comes from above, any enemies or dirt below you will often bounce you right into the drill, resulting in your death. These deaths feel unfair as you cannot prevent these bounces from occurring.I've also encountered some issues in the first area where drills spawn from the sides of the stage in such a way that they are unavoidable. Either I have no method of getting above them, digging below them, or there is an entire wall of drills that results in a forced hit. I've also encountered a teleporting mage that appears in the "forge" area of the game (one of the second areas) that teleports exactly on the spot I was on, also resulting in forced hits.Every issue I have with Shovel Knight Dig boils down to hits I was forced to take. The original Shovel Knight was designed in such a way that any damage or death received felt like  fault rather than the game's. If these issues are fixed, then Shovel Knight will be an amazing experience. I've loved coming across secrets and events that I hadn't seen in previous runs, and I've enjoyed every run feeling fresh from the random generation of levels. The soundtrack is also amazing, as expected from the great Jake Kaufman.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that put a ridiculous amount of hours into the original SK, the idea of a Shovel Knight roguelike really appealed to me. I'm glad to say that, at least in my opinion, Dig most definitely delivers on almost all fronts. The controls are as smooth as ever, the levels themselves are full of creative traps and set pieces (my personal highlight was Hive Knight's zone), the game is gorgeous to look at and beautifully animated, the bosses are all very fun and getting to see Shovel Knight and Shield Knight working together was really cool. I would have liked to see a lot more accessories, as there are currently way too few of them, and I would have liked there to be more upgrades/sidegrades available (Perphaps bring back the relic upgrading system from SoT?). In addition, the insta kill death saw apears a bit to quickly. The run time is also quite short (the in-game clock says I got the true ending at around 10 hours, while the steam one says roughly 15 hours, which is odd), though I'm personally not bothered with smaller roguelikes (Going Under took me around the same time to complete and I adore that game).Overall though, I had a blast playing this game. It is now my go-to "game to play while listening to a podcast in the background for hours".
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: I hate roguelikes. I hate roguelikes. I have played so many roguelikes and it's the singular genre of video game that I straight up just do not like. Shovel Knight is my favorite series of video game ever. I say this so you know my biases, and so it's known that I was absolutely crushed when I found out this game was going to be a rougelite. But, I have maybe a bit too much trust for Yacht Club, and I liked Pocket Dungeon (which was a puzzle-roguelike), so I got Dig anyway. I threw myself at the wall a bunch of times, got mad, screamed, cried, yelled, and then put the game down. I'm not the best at video games, but I've heard this game is also just kinda hard, so I wasn't getting very far, and the roguelike aspect was discouraging on top of that."Ok Juno then why is this review recommending the game" Well after I screamed and cried and pissed my pants about the game (I did actually cry for a little irl) I did two things: First, I watched a playthrough of the game, both the regular and true endings. This got me to not only see what someone actually good at this game played like and gave me some of my confidence back, but, and maybe more importantly, I got to watch the story. I love Shovel Knight for the story (yes I'm one of those guys) and Dig has got to be one of my favorite games YCG has ever put out based on the story alone, second only to Specter of Torment- but it's like, a close second. I won't spoil anything, but as someone who had anticipated this game for its entire development span, the story is almost everything I could have wanted out of a new SK game.The other thing I did, after reinvigorating myself in the game and taking the night off from playing it, was go back to the game, and give myself a bunch of extra health in the accessibility settings. Is this cheating? Probably not. Would it be unnecessary if this game was a little more balanced in how it generates enemies and terrain? Maybe, but I don't know or care enough about that aspect of the game to speak on it. All that matters to me is that I'm having way more fun with the game now. Maybe that's a dealbreaker for you, but also consider that I suck at games and you'll probably do way better than me on the default settings lmaoI also think it's worth pointing out how damn good the art is in this game. I love the art in this game so much it's unreal. It's so expressive and fun to look at, the characters all have great designs and even some old characters have been squashed and stretched into Dig's new style and it's absolutely delightful. The writing is also funny, creative, entertaining. I love seeing the interactions and relationships between characters, both between the bosses in the game and the NPCs in your campsite. I think this is the most alive the Shovel Knight world has felt, and I'm so here for it. And I'd be a fool to not mention Jake Kaufman's fantastic work on the soundtrack yet again, he never misses.TL;DR/Should you get this game?: If you're coming from the original SK games expecting this to be a regular platformer, or if you're like me and hate roguelikes, you should be very aware of what you're getting into before you get the game. I would honestly recommend watching someone else's gameplay (it doesn't have to be all the way through) before you make a decision if you're on the fence, just to see if it's your thing. And if you're still undecided after that, you can never go wrong waiting until a sale- plus, the wait will give you even more time to think! I do think that there's some growing pains with this game, both on the player side and the developer side, but I also trust YCG and Nitrome to make patches and updates that will greatly improve this game in the future. Once I got used to the gameplay, I personally really enjoyed it, and it's one of my favorite Shovel Knight games now. It's just up to you to decide if you feel like taking the time to get used to it like I did, I guess!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not liking other games like Binding of Isaac that have similar mechanics to Shovel Knight Dig, this game is the first of its genre I can definitely say that I love. It's not a traditional platforming adventure, instead opting to be an arcade-type experience best played in short bursts. I had high hopes for it before release and it did not disappoint - it's got an addicting, exhilarating mix of platforming and roguelike elements that I can't get enough of.+ Wonderfully detailed sprites that greatly enhance the character and monster designs from the original game.+ Catchy and upbeat Sega Genesis-styled soundtrack - not quite as good as the original, but still a solid evolution of what was previously there.+ Gameplay that is all about tight platforming and quick decision-making. By the end of a run you're above and beyond in terms of power thanks to the numerous amount of upgrades you can pick between as you go.+ Accessibility options are excellent for introducing the game to new players and easing them into the mechanics.- Controls require some adjustment, as certain details have been changed from the original game and some hitboxes are deceiving.- Depending on the random layout a player gets, the difficulty can zig-zag between extremely easy or hard.- Pretty short length overall (around 3 hours until my first successful run).

Also like the OG Shovel Knight games, its most certainly not very forgiving when it comes to combat and platforming, which has been the cause of me yelling at my PC a few times over clipped hitboxes, but all the same it's all in good fun.For any fan of our little blue earth mover and ambassador of the code of Shovelry, this is a wonderful addition to any library, and a very good time-killer for sure!FOR SHOVELRY!

_childDocuments_.review: Yacht Club Games and Nitrome come together to create a fun adventure with plenty of challenge, fun characters to encounter, and a ton of visual and audio charm for Shovel Knight and Roguelike fans to enjoy. Some say it is short or lacks content for the price but I don't agree. There's all the achievements to go after, new relics to unlock behind challenge stages, blueprints to new armor hidden away in stages, shovel blade techniques hidden behind their own gameplay challenges, and a True Ending! What content is there has clearly got the polish one would expect from a Yacht Club Games product. Plus, there's even talks of DLC in the works, which given their track record is sure to add a bunch of high quality content as well. I would strongly urge people to give this game a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a good game, but I wouldn't say it's a great game; I enjoy it and I want to keep playing it because I enjoy Shovel Knight games. If you want it, you might want to wait until a sale. Otherwise I'd say it's nothing special and if you're introducing yourself Shovel Knight, you should def play the OG and I think the OG is worth full price. If you're looking to get into the roguelike/roguelite genre I can say I've played better ones with cheaper prices. The game just came out but I hope the devs tweak the game more because this game could be better.I've beaten the game and it hurts a bit to give this game a thumbs down but I personally still find it enjoyable and will keep playing it here and there to get 100%. Overall I'm really happy to have another Shovel Knight game to play, the game is beautiful, music is great but it leaves a lot to be desired. The game is short and relies on replay-ability to prolong the gameplay with you starting every run at functionally level 0 (there are some caveats) and sometimes getting stronger throughout the run. This is not a bad thing and is the nature of most roguelike/rougelites but there's not much of a sense of progression because most upgrades/unlockables are just a chance to find them in your next run. I must give props that they have an accessability settings adjuster so you can make the game as easy or as hard as you like, I think that is just fantastic because easy and hard is subjective.  PROS:  - It's a Shovel Knight game and it's nice to have more content about the Shovel Knight world  - Graphics are amazing, spite animations and backgrounds are beautiful to look while you're playing the game  - Music is awesome, Jake Kaufman did an excellent job with the soundtrack  - Lots of secrets to explore, adding high variability between each run based on what you find  - Controls handle very well  - Permanent upgrades from armor, each change the way your run will go  - Ability to unlock more power-ups, items, and attacks  - Ability to unlock and skip to lower parts of the game, comes with increase to your health too  - Every level feels like it's own unique place with different enemies and different hazards  - Boss fights are solid  - Accessability settings: make the game as hard or as easy as you want!  CONS:  - Items, power-ups, and attacks unlocked give you a CHANCE to find them in your later runs  - Few power-ups are good and I don't find many of the items that crucial/helpful  - Due to the level layout I don't find myself using the unlocked horizontal attacks much  - Virtually no ability to make a build like other Rougelikes/Rougelites  - The high variability does come at a cost, sometimes the game is really hard, sometimes really easy, sometimes you're rich with no shops to spend money or all the shops and no money, all the keys and no doors to unlock, all the locks but no keys, etc...  - Not much of a sense of progress outside of the unlocking the chance for new items and going deeper  - I have played runs without getting any power-ups/items and not because I choose to avoid themRecommendations to the Developers: - Allow permanent upgrades/ability to make builds before going in - Ability to pay for health/magic increases before you start the run - Create synergies between attacks, armors, items, and power-ups - Reduce the variability in regards to keys and eggs so that if there's doors/nest, there's increase drop chance for the key/egg - Get some kind of healing, wealth, item/power-up at the end of boss fights whether its a choice or get all 3 - You get a Gem at the end of each boss fight, why not make it contribute to the run (buffs/wealth)I give this game a thumbs down because although I love Shovel Knight, it's not the game I can sink my teeth into like I had hoped. As the game stands right now, I think it has room for improvement, and it would serve the game really well to add some patches and new content into Shovel Knight Dig to build it up more and allow some more customization before each run so it feels like the things you unlock last run are more helpful in the next run. Shovel Knight Dig is a complete game, but it needs some refinement.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Shovel Knight. It's a great platformer with a lot of original ideas, fun bosses, and a large world that rewards exploration. I was very excited when this game was released; unfortunately, Shovel Knight Dig is not even close to the same caliber of game.There are some good points, and I'll highlight those first. If you enjoyed the mechanics of Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove, you will enjoy the mechanics here. The movement is not identical, but it is similar and feels very good. Moving, jumping, digging, attacking, and taking damage all feel very fun and fair. The platform elements are also pretty cool, and some rooms/stages make good use of the gimmicks. The music and art style is also very good, you know what to expect here if you've played Shovel Knight.Now for the bad. The first thing I noticed is that the upgrades are almost entirely uninteresting. There are attacking relics where you can spam projectiles (there are variations on how these work, but it's pretty much irrelevant). There are accessories that do small things for you; a few of them seem interesting, like immunity to spikes, but most of them you will never notice. There are four upgrades for your shovel, and I didn't find any of them helpful or interesting for stages or bosses. Then there are a few upgrades that ruin things in the other direction. The propeller relic lets you float upwards for a mega jump, which ruins some potentially challenging stages. The health upgrades make bosses free: with 6 health, all you need to do is get close and spam attack.Then there's the big one. This game is short. Like, 2-5 hours to beat the main game. I got stuck on the second stage a few times, and then I got a good build. I was feeling good, like "I'll make some progress, this will be a fun run!" and then that was it, the game was over. I blew through the bosses I hadn't seen, flew through the stages, it was just free. This wouldn't be a big deal if there was a lot of post game replayability that has been a staple of rouguelike games, but there is basically none. The main game is done and there seems to be no point continuing. It feels more like a short platformer with a lot of RNG than a fully developed rougelike game.If you are a huge Yacht Club Games fan and you know that you NEED to play this, do what you have to. But if that isn't the case, wait for this game to fall to $10, or just skip it and replay Shovel Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for an hour some things really stuck out to me about this game:1. There is no tutorial. It's very common that you will die or be confused the first handful of times you enter a new area, HOWEVER this is a rougelike and dying is part of the genre. Stick to it and you'll have a fun time learning and exploring2. There is a massive drill that will show up if you take too long in an area. It seems like this will OHKO you anytime you come into contact with it. The time for exploration comes AFTER getting comfortable with the room layouts. Personally, I enjoy this because it gives the game a longer shelf-life with more replay ability.3. The game is puzzling. Again, dying is a part of the process, so don't be upset if you get stuck in a room. The enemies are almost always going to be used to navigate the screen (like the first game) so start bouncin' on those bad boys. 4. The game is beautiful and rewarding. The graphics for this are the best I've seen from a pixel-based title. The colors are exciting as well as the movement of the enemies, NPCs, Bosses, and Shovel Knight himself! This game stays fresh not only from the rouglike RNG levels, but from the stylish GBA-inspired look.5. Don't get too caught up in some of the games complexities. Have fun! At the end of the day, this will always be about a knight swingin' a shovel for valor, vigor, and victory.Steel Thy Shovel!

Again, the only criticism I possibly have is that it should be $15, maybe $20. $25 is a bit overboard.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game! Very fast-paced roguelite full of gems, dirt and baddies. The artstyle and soundtrack are incredible and full of character, character movement and diggging feel as they should. The only negative I've noticed so far is that there doesn't seem to be a huge variety of room layouts, and they started repeating within the first hour of play, which is a pretty bad sign for a roguelite where you'll be seeing the first world in particular a whole lot. Let's hope they will add more of those like Dodge Roll did with Enter The Gungeon, else I fear the level designs will become boring rather quickly.Still worth checking out for fast runs and gem gathering!
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: "Shovel Knight Dig" is my first time playing a Shovel Knight game. Simple, enjoyable, and wonderful retro vibe. The other Shovel Knight games intrigue me in the light of this, but that's a topic for another debate. It works well on the Steam Deck! It is simple to learn and has easy controls, yet it can be challenging. Suddenly, I am motivated to dig and now researching to buy a shovel online.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not worth the price. It feels pretty clunky at times, especially when falling because the game automatically performs a shovel drop so you'll constantly be bouncing and hitting enemies or spikes above. The game also seems pretty shallow, at least from the first two areas I've played, and apparently a full run of the game only takes 45 minutes. I'd recommend waiting for a big sale before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Dig

_childDocuments_.review: When Drill Knight and his dastardly digging crew blast apart Shovel Knight's peaceful campsite and steal his loot, he grabs his trusty Shovel Blade and starts tunnelling after them. Meet new friends and foes, visit strange lands, and outfit yourself in your quest to keep the entire land from collapsing underfoot! Jump, slash, and dig your way down an ever-changing chasm of mystery in Shovel Knight Dig, an all-new Shovel Knight adventure!
